_childDocuments_.review: Not for me, maybe for you.This game is more... dark souls than collect and craft.The combat system is....swing and miss and get hit by over powered attacks from enemies because there are no advances combat techniques like....dodge...You have an extremely limited stamina Pool which gets smaller and smaller because the the scarcity of food items to consume to increase it.You have to have stamina to Run, you have to have stamina to "Evade attacks", you have to have stamina to sleep...There are no starting recipes and everything is trial by discovery, which is fine if you had a semi-functional combat system...while trying to collect ingredients...Then there is the storm of death corruption that comes out of nowhere and kills you because there is no warning system in this game and very limited Camera angle.Items break very, very, very quickly.Also, gold in the early game appears to be useless.If you want a collection crafting game where you die a lot in pursuit of making potions for meaningless gold, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a great game, but an enjoyable one. Some game play mechanics seem pretty simple like the combat, and luckily I didn't experience any bugs. For myself, it was jarring for a short while, but I didn't find it overwhelmingly too much. _childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this with the fact that I got this from humble bundle monthly.7 Hours of staying in the same exact area with very little progression. Like many others say. The game is overall just a chore. I enjoyed it for a while but the frustration of your AI companions having basic coding where they only function best as pack mules. And even then they'll get attacked and probably killed in a fight they get in.Hitboxes can be awful sometimes, if you're too close to an enemy you'll outright miss them especially on the smaller enemies like rats and chickens. Also you can only hit one singular enemy per swing of your weapon, same with potions.Something else that's unknown to the player is if you purify the first "boss" of the game, and then are late getting out of the storm when it arrives in the first area. The boss can be CORRUPTED again. 120 health enemy which means you're gonna need to hit it 18 times (with the sword) while it only needs to hit you like 4-5 times in total (it deals 8 damage). I understand gearing the player towards using potions to keep out of danger but the weight limit is too low for how much you're gonna be expected to need to gather what is needed. Shovels are 3 pounds, Axes 5, swords 7, torches (lit and unlit) 4, and each potion you craft is .5 pounds each. You're already using over 15 pounds just carrying around basic equipment.If the weight limit was lifted for our player character (and not reduced upon transformation into other animals) then maybe the game would be more enjoyable. Maybe it's part of the difficulty, but it's not fun to play as is right now for me. TL;DR AI is terrible, weight limit is annoying, gathering is slow and tedious, great concept and aesthetic with poor execution.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.An alchemy scavenging game.The Serpent Rogue has players start as a plague doctor named The Warden as they try to fight back against an approaching corruption.  Players will forage for items, brew potions, and use that to fight back against the evil of the land.   As a concept, it sounds intriguing and the graphics are good. Battling the evil forces makes the player wonder what they’ll find. The problem is The Serpent Rogue runs into a couple of rather big problems.  The first is that without any tutorial it can be hard for players to understand what they are doing, and even once that’s understood, how to use many items is kept from the player.  Even just understanding how to use a potion correctly can confuse new players.  The second problem is that maps don’t appear to reset, so if a large boss or a strong enemy chases you to the exit, returning through that same portal will immediately put you against that same enemy.  There’s possibly a way, but again, there’s nothing to tell you how to deal with that. A final issue is that I’ve heard that this game can be rather short, and while there’s a lot to explore the main story is only a handful of hours. Pick this up if you want an obtuse survival game.   It has traces of Don’t Starve in it, but ultimately, I couldn’t enjoy this game and I couldn’t even begin to understand it.  This is a game where you are better off turning to a walkthrough or a guide before you even start, and that’s not a good experience in my opinion.  If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend you skip this game due to the layers of frustration I encountered.The stamina system is really bad. You get a couple of seconds of sprint, and to re-sprint you have to release your sprint button and re-press it. The minimap is too small to see anything and there's no local map so there's lots of running around looking for stuff. I found this especially unnecessary in the safe areas with their spread out stations. Stamina capacity also decays quickly requiring the constant intake of food.The other major pain point is the storms. At the start of the game there is literally nothing else to do other than go into the wilderness and forage. But if a storm comes, you have no choice but to sit in town and do nothing. Sleeping burns stamina cap so even that isn't a good option. Other offenses abound like wasting resources to find valid recipes, requiring the player to press and hold a key to perform simple actions, the sometimes problematic camera with no controls, etc. Hell the multiple launch splash screens are unskippable and pause when you alt-tab.These frustrations are generally part of the core gameplay loop, thus I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Serpent Rogue is a 3D rendered hybrid crafting, exploration, RPG, combat game... which, really, should be a slam dunk because everyone likes those kinds of games, right?  So why is this handheld (Switch) ported game not a slam dunk?  Well, good ideas don't turn into great games without exceptional implementation, and The Serpent Rogue does not have that. Despite not being in Steam Early Access (where this arguably belongs), the game is missing features and is apparently incomplete.  Due to the lack of meaningful progress from the developer, it's unlikely the game will be completed at all, yet the developers reprehensively have their hand out for money for an incomplete game.  This is a good reason for gamers to avoid this.  It's not polished, it's not fun, it's got a lot of bugs... it was just implemented badly.On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.Another defect in the game caused by the console-peasant-centric design is the intolerably bad camera controls.  There's no effective mouselook, and control of the viewing angles is deliberately outside of reasonable control from the user.This defect springs from the limitations of inferior console peasant children's toy gamepads, but on PC we don't have this limitation due to KB+M controls... however, the developer deliberately chose to arrogantly foist this handicap onto PC gamers.  Out of spite, or laziness, it's unclear, regardless, once more console peasants and console devs have made gaming worse for everyone.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The Serpent Rogue didn't appeal much to the people who own a copy of the game, either.  It has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game didn't really capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for finding the location of the Undertaker, trivial to get, but less than 18 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  Hardly a success story, gamers just weren't all that interested in the game.Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this game was with players reveals a surprise... there's a modest spike in player counts for the game.  But this only happened once, and isn't consistent with the achievement stats, that show less than 18 percent of players bothered playing the game for any reasonable amount of time.  How is it possible for this game to have so many concurrent players who didn't bother engaging with this game?  Trading cards.  People will use card idling software to collect the cards and sell them, but this won't trigger any achievements in-game.That tells us people only really bought this game for trading cards, and that's a damning indictment of the woeful quality.  A closer look at the numbers shows the game just has a couple of players every week running up the game and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with little merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?The Serpent Rogue has the almost unethical price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "The Elder Scrolls Online", "Rust" or "Grand Theft Auto V".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this, I wanted to like this game. The art style, the narrative, it all felt like it had a lot of great potential. Getting into the game, I felt the movement was a little clunky, but I could get used to it. Most aspects of the game were a bit different than what I might have expected, but not in ways that were a detriment, just unique. Unfortunately, this was not true of everything.The storytelling was fine, but the rest of the flow of information seemed designed to emphasize that your character had only just been born into this in-between world, and thus knew nothing, and had to learn it all the hard way. By itself, that wouldn't be enough to get me to drop a game, but when this ignorance extends to aspects of the GUI, it makes things a lot harder to accept. What few NPCs you run into at the beginning give you almost no information, aside from your mentor who serves as a very brief, and very limited, tutorial. So when I went into the very first zone with enemies in it and succeeded in nothing more than breaking my axe (the only one in the game so far with no way to replace it yet) and suffering my first death (quite ignominiously), I was forced to run back to retrieve my belongings having gained nothing from the ordeal. Except, that is, for having run up the percentage displayed in a little diamond at the top of the screen which, even now, I have absolutely no idea what it is meant to indicate. I feel as though there is something on that area of the map you are meant to do in a very limited amount of time, but as things stand, I would have no way to do anything but fail at that. Between that, having had to 'waste' every bit of several items I had collected in the name of 'research' only to discover after using it all up that that batch in particular was *supposed* to be used for something else, and what felt like a rather abrupt stop to any narrative delivery after the minuscule tutorial, I felt myself just as abruptly lose any further interest in trying to find out what that percentage in the diamond was about, or anything else in the game for that matter. Whatever it was, I was probably doing it wrong. But how was I to know? I never got a chance to learn how I was supposed to do it right.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of roguelike games, I must say this game has quite an interesting mechanics.I love the mechanic of discovering the effects of ingredients and discovering how to put them together to create something.If you are a fan of constantly finding and farming ingredients to craft an get stronger, then this game is definitely for you.The corrupted storm mechanics to "change" the make is a unique way of roguelike.You can enter the same place and the loots and enemies respawn without needing you to actually die to go to a next cycle.The follower system is a fun touch too, where you can get followers in a few different ways.Fun game with a decent amount of play time depending on how well you play to progress in the game.Game could also do with some QOL especially with the craftingThe game does have some bugs here and there which some can be easily fixed by just restarting the game.Had one gamebreaking bug where I was clipped through the ground and got stucked then killed by the boss I was fighting.But the worst most game breaking bug made me unable to do most of the important mechanics like using certain potions, can't guard, can't aim and throw.This bug caused me to not be able to beat the final boss and wasted 10 hours of play time.I do enjoy the game a lot but the bug just put me off a lot.Buy this game knowing the risk of the bug I experienced.P.S. The price of the game may be a bit steep for the amount of hours so if you are not up for it then I recommend getting it on sales or go sub January 2023 Humble Choice and get this game along with many other fun titles.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - For me this one's an easy 8/10 for the graphics, but no better than a 2/10 for the rest so I suggest you avoid this like the plague.After buying this game yesterday and playing for about 30 minutes I decided not to keep the game.  When my axe broke within 5 minutes of acquiring it and could not be repaired I began to question the game mechanics.  Whey my character was absolutely starving within the first 10 minutes with no explanation why they were so hungry so quickly I started to ask myself why this game had such good reviews from several publications and professional reviewers.  When I noticed that sprinting was awfully slow and barely faster than walking, that combat was poorly designed and very boring, that crafting wasn't really interesting or fun, that your character's items wear out quickly, and that you spend a lot of time holding the E key to collect things but not actually doing anything interesting or fun I was pretty sure I wouldn't be keeping the game.  I was even annoyed when any written dialogue was occurring because it comes in at a slow enough pace that I can read it faster than it shows up, and it's accompanied by some annoying gibberish noises that I assume are supposed to be speech.The main problem is that there was nothing in the first half hour that made me feel like this game was worth playing or worth more of my time.  I see why there were mixed reviews.  The overall concept and artwork are both great but the actual gameplay, inventory and UI system, game mechanics, and primary game loop are all lacking.  It falls flat within the first half hour and that's when the game should be grabbing a new player and making them excited to see what else the game has in store for them not promising them a lot of boring harvesting and lackluster combat.I know I didn't play for a long time but I really didn't want to keep playing, I actually decided to stop because it wasn't fun.  When I sat down to play a few games today I really didn't want to start playing this again.  That's the bottom line.  It wasn't fun, I had no interest in playing it again, and that means it's not worth keeping nor does it deserve a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: Serpent Rogue is a "discover the mechanics" game.  Little or nothing is directly explained and the player is left to learn by exploration and experimentation. In the hands of a lesser dev team it's really just a recipe for needless and pointless frustration.  Regrettably, this dev team is  in the latter group.  There may be something here but I have neither the patience nor tolerance to find out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with an awesome alchemical brewing system, an atmospheric setting and decent gameplay. I really like the world and the ways you can interact with monsters/characters/items. It's also a very cool feature that you can see what's happening on other maps while you're not there.Although the main story is pretty short, the game offers a lot of fun achievement you can work on.However, I chose to say "good" instead of great or awesome, because it sure has it's flaws. I'll point out some of them, in case of the devs reading this review, because I really like the game and want it to be the best it can be.- the inventory weight limit is way too small. maybe increase it by 5 or 10 after each main mission?- the balance of where and how many ingredients you find could use some adjusting. e.g.: it was way easier for me to get good amounts of fish bones before I even got enough shells to research them, only to find out that they are way weaker than bones. And at the point where i completed the story I've never even had done a potion with claws.- even after completing the game I couldn't find out what Mavka's forest song thing was for. Some things in the game could use a better explanation or more useful journal entries. this might also apply to the creatures entries. I understood that you can use the rat to crawl through holes, I randomly found out that the toad is to get objects from afar, but there's a lot of transformations I couldn't find out what to use them on or where to use them.- I don't know if this was the case just for me, but there are some bugged achievements. Like the one where you have to steal from multiple people - I stole from a lot, but it just didn't count.- at the start of the last bossfight it's really unclear that you have to slay the tentacle that spawns in the light cone. within my first few tries I was close to the boss, trying to throw my sword at him and I didn't see that there spawned a tentacle somewhere way out of sight.

_childDocuments_.review: it is an entertaining game with compelling premise and simplistic, but intereting combat style (for better or for worse). name: Curse of the Sea Rats
detailed_description: Curse of the Sea Rats is a ‘ratoidvania’ platform adventure with lovingly crafted, hand-drawn animations. Embark on the epic journey of four prisoners of the British empire, transformed into rats by the notorious pirate witch, Flora Burn. To regain their human bodies, they will have to fight dangerous bosses, uncover the secrets of the vast Irish coast, and ultimately capture the witch who cursed them. Beautiful 2D, hand-drawn animation breathes life into the game's cast of characters - inspired by classic animated films and reminiscent of the golden age of 2D platforming. These animations combine seamlessly with detailed 3D environments enhanced by light and shadow effects to create a 2.5D platforming experience of incredible quality. Chart your progress through a huge, non-linear world as you attempt to track down the pirate witch who cursed you. Shipwrecked on the coast of Ireland in the 18th Century, you'll need more than just your swashbuckling skills to forge your path to freedom. Discover four playable characters – David Douglas, Buffalo Calf, Bussa, and Akane Yamakawa. Each character brings their unique fighting style to help you overcome the challenges posed by enemies and the environment! Play alone or with up to three friends in local co-op mode. Each character has strengths and weaknesses. You'll be able to improve their abilities as your adventure progresses - unlocking new special skills, boosting your offence and defence, or learning powerful magics! A labyrinthine network of hundreds of pathways, rooms and discoveries lie ahead, in a substantial quest with over 12 hours of content. Can you master each character’s playstyle, find all the hidden secrets, and unlock each of the game’s multiple endings? PLEASE NOTE: Multiple controllers are required for local multiplayer mode Many thanks to everyone who has supported us so far. We look forward to updating you on our development progress. In the meantime we would welcome any feedback in the community - and don't forget to Wishlist if you'd like to be kept up to date on any upcoming news!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I want to love this game. The graphics, the animation, the music, they're all just dripping with charm. I adore them. Watch them. Listen to them. But don't come here looking for a fun game.After falling to my death three times in a row in the wind level because I didn't quite grab a ledge and tog insta-killed, enough is enough. Neither Metroidvanias nor Ratoidvanias should have instant pit deaths that require you to lose half your stuff and spend countless time backtracking. (And if you thought you could do a corpse run to get your stuff back, maybe you can, maybe you can't; half the time your lost resources are inaccessible.) Not every darned game under the sun needs to be "Dark Souls Hard" where you lose half your crap and are punished by loss of your time because of one mis-timed button press, meandering through empty levels to make one more attempt at a jump to progress.It doesn't stop there in terms of the gameplay, the black mark on what could have been a great game. The levels are big and empty with only one or two enemies each that kill you in one or two hits. Health items are rare. Power-ups don't feel meaningful other than the one vampire skill that David gets. Oh hey, you have the key item for this cut scene room you found... oh, you just lost all your money. But you won't care because money isn't really useful anyway, and the item shop has bonkers pricing, if you can even access it at all.I hate, hate, hate, giving this game a thumbs-down because it should have been so much more. It *could* be so much more. I hope beyond hope that they find a way to patch this, because I can imagine that so many people worked so hard on this product. But at the end of the day, this product is a game, and as a game, it suffers, and I'm not sure I can even bring myself to keep playing to finish out the map, much as I want to experience what the art team produced.I'll be pouring out some rum for what could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Sea Rats has been jokingly dubbing itself as a ‘ratoidvania’, and one of the weirdest parts about rolling credits is realizing how complete that moniker is. Because this sure is a metroidvania with rats alright; beautifully hand drawn rats for sure, but otherwise its a game that’s a very paint by numbers implementation of its genre that probably doesn’t execute with a high enough level of quality to warrant that safety.Extremely easy combat up to and including its final moments make the game frictionless and its bosses unmemorable, cementing Curse of the Sea Rats as an animation showcase first and a worthwhile metroidvania second.4 Player Co-Op is a fun inclusion, but the restriction to make it local only and some negative implications it has on progression systems make it a haphazard implementation at best…Ultimately, Curse of the Sea Rats can at times be a beautiful and even entertaining addition to the genre, but its never a truly essential one.Curse of the Sea Rats unquestionably nails… the rats. Each of the four characters is beautifully hand drawn and glides across the screen in unique ways, usually aligned to their elemental property. You can see this animation focus as early as its kickstarter; Walt Disney and Don Bluth are both named inspirations, and the ‘handcraftedness’ of this ordeal makes up a large percent of the campaign… maybe disproportionately so.Because the game is successful in this area, the characters and enemies are beautiful; and watching all these animations play out is arguably the reason to play. But it's in trying to elegantly weave these animations into gameplay where Curse of the Sea Rats fails, and its cardinal sin is a big one: it just doesn’t feel very good.Turns out showing off all those beautiful attack animations demands a lot of frames, making each swing this giant, slow commitment. It goes beyond the point of deliberateness and into the territory of clunky and awkward, and it gets exacerbated by the fact that enemies deal damage with their bodies not just with their abilities.So you have to get real up close and personal, plant your feet, then start swinging… all the while even brushing up against your foe will disrupt that rhythm entirely. Each character TECHNICALLY has a running slash but they always bring you to a complete stop anyway.  It almost feels like youre playing as a turret, with the full stop requirement and long animations for every ability. Each button input is more like a micro cutscene playing out before you rather than an extension of your character that you have full control over.Defensively you do have a parry, but between its stiff animation and lack of feedback its sometimes hard to tell when it worked.Some of this does get slightly mitigated with the introduction of the dash and double jump, letting you avoid damage in ways that the base toolkit doesn’t support. Funny enough you avoid the plant your feet problem in the air because you can move and swing while you’re airborne, so most of my combat footage has me doing these weird little bunnyhops every second so I can stay nimble and on the offensive.But no amount of cheesing this system will get around the combat and movements inherent jankiness. It looks great, it trailers great, but it doesn’t play great… and it negatively colors almost all other aspects of the game.Off the coast of late 18th century Ireland, the Admirals Son has been kidnapped! As a prisoner to the British navy you can earn your freedom if you defeat the piratey big bad and save him. Doing so necessitates doing your metroidvania staples of getting double jumps and super jumps and reaching previously unreachable parts of the map.The character you pick is largely irrelevant to that progression. You can play as any of them with the differences between them being statistics and combat abilities, rather than exploration changes. You can stick to a single one for your whole adventure if you like and, in fact, that might actually be the correct play…. at least at first.Because although the level ups are shared among all characters, the skill progression tree points are not. So if you’re switching up between characters and progressing them all simultaneously, you’re not maximizing the potential of any singular character.This extends to co-op as well, rather than balancing Co-Op with aggressive scaling on your opponents, it does so with lack of scaling on you. Because the same currency must now be shared between two or more characters instead of just one, usually resulting in your progression feeling a little gimped.More balanced as it may be it does prolong the acquisition of new abilities, and it can be a little deflating needing to make decisions on which party members get new abilities rather than letting everyone do so.There’s a lot of weird little idiosyncrasies like that co-op or otherwise, decisions that it makes and features that it borrows from other games without really understanding why.It’s got a soulsy idea of death in the sense that there’s no game overs and you can make runs back to your corpse to reclaim lost currency. But it doesn’t take in the same lessons that Souls made when going from Demon to Dark in that, without persistent replenishing healing items, each walk of shame back to the boss is also going to be coupled with a grind for more healing consumables before you get to try again.Then again it doesn’t really matter because you won’t be dying. Between the skill tree and the stats on level up, you will very quickly invalidate every challenge curse of the sea rats throws at you. My only combat deaths were on the first boss as I was learning how the combat worked and a mid-game boss that caught me off guard with an instakill pitfall. Aside from that they’re all pretty effortless stat checks, whose mechanics can almost all be entirely ignored assuming you come with healing items because there’s no heal animation, you can just pop into your inventory and click away consequence free.Even enemy spawns are awkward, they reset every time you leave the room which can be frustrating both because of how small these rooms are and how often you’re supposed to go back and forth between them by the very exploration driven nature of this genre.There are times that when, despite its failings, Curse of the Sea Rats is enjoyable. Clunky, awkward, and unceremonious as it may be; it still benefits from the intrinsic satisfaction of unlocking a key new move and going back to see which metaphorical doors that key unlocks. But without any core gameplay ingredients to call its own, and without tight execution of existing genre tenants: it’s relying almost wholly on its presentation to be a differentiating feature, and even then, that presentation’s quality only extends as far as the characters and not to the sometimes ugly 3D backgrounds.There are worse ways to spend 10 hours especially if you’ve got some friends, but I suspect that the footprint ‘Curse of the Sea Rats’ will leave on the metroidvania genre, will be a size befitting its main characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A metroidvania with decent visuals is always a game I love to play. This one looks good, and it refers to itself as ratroidvania, because everyone is a rat. Lets see if it is as good (and hard) as Tails of Iron. The unique feature is of course it's local 4-player option. You can play alone, but for fun play with a friend, and for chaos play with three friends. There are not too many similar and good games out there, the last one I remember was Bravery and Greed. You can choose between four characters, all play rather differently. They have an inventory screen, differet stats (attack, defense, magic,...) and all play unique. They have skill trees to upgrade (requires spiritual energy from slain foes). Playing with a friend is easier than playing alone, because you can revive each other.The game features the expected metroidvania mechanics - there is an automatic map, you can smash and plunder chests, Ancestral Doors allow you to quick travel, when you leave and re-enter a room (often accidentally) all enemies are revived, when you die you can retrieve your collected spiritual energy from the place of death. Touch an enemy and you lose health. The maps are full of hidden chests. The quatermasters sells you stuff, other crew members help you if you bring them certain items, and a ghostly Chinese mentor named Wun Yu promises to make you human again if you bring him a mighty amulet. Collect enough spiritual energy and you can improve your skills with his help, he also heals you and you can switch characters when you meet him. Defeat bosses to get new abilities like the double jump.You are a pirate, caught by the British crown and brought home to face trial and execution, when a witch transforms everyone on board the ship into a rat and then kidnaps the admiral's son. The ship crashes against a rock on the notoriously dangerous Irish coast, probably the rats could not operate the large sailing ship too well. Seems most members of the crew survived, and the admiral offers to clear you of all charges if you bring him the witch (dead or alive) and his son (alive). This is certainly one of the worst introduction stories I ever encountered in a game... or maybe not, if I think about it. Who cares? You are a rat, your friends are rats, and you have to platform and kill the witch and her army of monsters. Gamepad works fine, the animations are amazing (it looks like a Don Bluth cartoon), but combat feels a bit off. Health loss whenever you touch an enemy, leaving the room when you near the edges, a strange dash ability, health potions require two button presses... I dunno, while I love exploring the locations, the combat was not my favoite. The first boss is slightly overpowered if you encounter him at the beginning, but after you have gained a few levels and bought the first ability upgrades he isn't so tough anymore.  Metroidvania for up to four local players, best played at least in two player mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Many have the tag metroidvania which most (atleast i) compare to Castlevania or Bloodstained, while often they fail.But Curse of the Sea Rats succeeds in that, you got this big map, you got all sorts upgrades, level ups, everything a true metroid/ratvania should have, set in a nicely animated cartoony atmosphere.I could not find myself in most of the negative reviews (and i have no idea if things have been altered since some played in a beta phase), the enemies are easy, sometimes too easy because you can either just duck and attack them or jump on them and attack them, most won't be able to hit you, i never had to block or parry anything.As with Castlevania, in this game you can you also grind to the limit if you want to do so, be it orbs for upgrades or just leveling up and get more HP (both go hand in hand) combined with a few healing items, many to all bosses will be easy as 1,2,3.The wind level with the ledges can be annoying (especially the birds) but if you got a beefed up character with enough hp, and good upgrades, you will eventually get past it with ease.Also the controls were fine to me and i never experienced having to dash very much to such precision, i don't think this game deserves much of the critique (anymore).Minor spoiler ahead, there are 4 endings, mind that you can unintentionally skip one needed for an achievement, and if you miss that you have to play the whole game over again.8/10

We had a blast playing this game.A fine story, wrapped into beautiful art style that resembles the nostalgic feeling of classic Disney titles.Some of the minor issues/remarks:The good stuff:All this considered, Curse of the Sea Rats is a must have to anyone who is looking for a great co-op adventure. Give it some time, as you get stronger and better equipped, things will get more and more fun. The game deserves it's place right next to the great ones, such as Guacamelee and Sundered in the niche world of co-op metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for about 5 hours in the alpha/beta phases.About 2 hours into the launch release.I provided some feedback regarding sound and controls that don't appear to have been fixed or resolved since reporting it and between launch. The controls aren't nearly as tight for the time they've been developing it since crowdfunding. I hope there are some post updates and considerations from the larger audience since the launch date.The animations have improved and the over-all voice acting is better. The story struggles a bit and the opening intro is a bit jarring and quick to understand the primary cast of characters.I really want to enjoy the game, but it doesn't cut it on mechanics and controls that are more polished in similar indie titles with similar studio sizes. Attack controls are sloppy or unresponsive. Move controls lack finesse. Some sound effects could use softening, like those in breaking objects; repetitive sounds like the grunting in jumping and attacking could be less frequent or more varied. A simple woosh or jump sound could replace some of the grunts. I enjoyed playing it better without the soundtrack and sound effects.@Petoons Studio, we all want to enjoy the game, but the lack of community input based on your crowdfunding campaign has shown you're not taking some constructive criticism. Ultimately it's your game, but we all want to help make it as fun and enjoyable as possible. _childDocuments_.review: The game is beautifully rendered, I'll give it that much.The controls definitely leave something to be desired with an overcomplicated blocking feature that is challenging to figure out the timing of let alone figuring out the timing of enemy strikes to perfectly align the block in the middle of combat where combination swings leave you trapped in motion and open to enemy attack too often. There are too many instances of dash+ double jump that have to be perfectly executed again and again and again to advance on the map. It lead me to endless looping of the same room until death, which then reset me halfway across the map with no quick way back to the room to retry.The voice acting is alright. Some of it just has very muddled accents where it sounded like they were confused about what to be going for. The scripting is baaaad. There are cutscenes that add nothing to the game content and just drag on far far too long if you're streaming & avoiding skipping through the audio. The hero quips back to the villains before the boss battles largely fall flat and make the villains look more sly than dumb. They played it way too safe and boring with the dialogue in this game.This game is also guilty of having a mostly useless multiplayer option and too much long backtracking through empty rooms on the map that just lengthen the game unnecessarily. I'd wait for this one to go on sale before jumping into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game pretty to look at it? Yes.Is it fun? Kinda.Does it succeed as a metroidvania? Nope.These days, if you're going to design a game of this type then you need to recognize you are building it on the shoulders of games that came before it - games that excelled at the mechanics and tropes that now define the genre.Unfortunately, Curse of the Sea Rats leaves many of those mechanics unpolished or ignored: unbalanced skill trees and characters (is there any reason NOT to play as David?), sluggish movement and combat, a map heavily lacking in information, no quest / objective list or guide... The list goes on.Most of your time will be spent running around trying to figure out where you should go or what to do, fighting random bosses you stumble upon, while shrugging at a narrative thread so scant your next steps are never made clear past the first 3 minutes.At $20 USD it's not a lot out of pocket, and there is some fun to be had for awhile. But expect frustration and boredom to set in as you lose track of why you're playing, and once you have David's 30% health boost with every attack it's doldrums galore.Let this one be, and set sail in search of brighter seas.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, so good - I liked what I played during the first hour give or take. Nice graphics and music, good-enough characters & story for the genre, and most importantly (for me) a fresh, interesting setting. Honestly, as much as I love Dark Souls and Hollow Knight, it can get tiring when almost every metroidvania nowadays follows the same template: destroyed kingdoms, punishing deaths, super-vague story and all. Gameplay here is not the snappiest but perfectly serviceable so far, especially once you unlock double jump. Just don't get too greedy during fights, since you are animation-locked into attacks. There are also several sidequests you can stumble upon, multiple endings (as far as I've heard), plus skill trees for each character. I noticed there's a purchasable item for respeccing your skill points, which is great if you want to try out another character without bothering to level them all up in parallel.I might update this review once I'm further in the game, but as of now I am enjoying my time with the sea rats.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to get straight to the point. Curse of the Sea Rats is a by the numbers Metroidvania that brings absolutely nothing to the genre. The map layout and design is as basic as they come, with barely any fun secrets to discover and not that exciting to traverse through. Combat also is extremely basic, you have a set of well... basic attacks and you stay with them start to finish. Even though you unlock a couple of spells/special attacks they are barely worth the trouble and after a bit of leveling your basic attacks will do way more damage. The existing skill tree is pretty basic, boosting your skills, unlocking the special moves mentioned above but nothing interesting or game changing. Not only that, if you stick with only one character (you unlock their skills separately) you will unlock everything on the skill tree before reaching the mid point of the game, depending how often you lose. You get money from killing enemies but there's barely anything to spend it on. You get the basic potions and some helpful items but like the XP points, by the half point I have so much money that even if I kept everything in my inventory maxed out, my wallet barely felt it. Not only that, you get way better healing items if you just explore the map, making the things you get from the merchant almost irrelevant. Presentation wise, Curse of the Sea Rats is a mixed bag. The hand drawn stuff is great, it's obvious a lot of effort and care were put into designing the characters. The 3D assets though are extremely bland, like not a single screen in the game is anything to write home about. The backgrounds are for the most part lifeless and unimaginative, animations are usually reduced to badly animated waves. There was an area with a waterfall that wasn't even rendered properly to flow downwards, left only to flicker pretending there was animation (maybe a glitch but who knows). Music is nice but you will probably forget it the moment you finished the video game. Still, not bad at all. Voice overs though, are all over the place. Some actors did a pretty good job, others not that great, and a couple seem to have trouble keeping their supposed accent and the quality of their work changes throughout the game (mostly the Japanese character). So I left writing about the core gameplay experience for last. And that's because there aren't that many things to write about. As I said at the beginning of my review, the game is a Metroidvania so by the numbers it is actually impressive. Like, it plays it so safe, I am actually impressed. That means if you just want another title of this genre, you will probably have fun but everything will leave your memory the day after you complete the campaign. There are no cool weapons to seek after, no amazing new abiltiies, no combos, no deep buried secrets hidden around the map. At least the controls are pretty decent when you don't fight enemies. Platforming is fluid and when you unlock moves like high jump, double jump and dash you can flow across the map in pretty decent speeds. When in combat though, things aren't as good though. There's a weird delay in your attacks and parry that need some time to get use to. Also attacking makes you stay in place which also doesn't feel right, especially when you consider that mashing at the attack button triggers a 3 hit combo (only one in the game unfortunately) that lets you completely open to attacks. It can get kind of annoying early on but then you realize that as long as you hit the enemies first, they get stun locked and you can kill them pretty easily. Not only that after leveling up a bit and unlock most skills, most enemies become mostly a nuisance than an actual threat. The funny part is that this is even more of a case with the bosses. After the 2nd or 3rd boss, I never had issues with any boss, in fact I would dare say they were easier than most common enemies. You can hit then 2-3 times with each attack, most of them end up being critical hits, so you can drain their life bar in a matter of seconds. On the other hand for some reason, most of their attacks don't really damage you that much, to the point that, except maybe for the final boss that has three different phases, I  barely bothered avoiding their attacks, I was just getting near them and jump attack them (which hits them with 2-3 attacks every time, usually them being critical hits). So to summarize an already long review that probably no one will ever bother reading, we have a by the numbers Metroidvania that takes zero risks or makes any attempts to add something to the genre, with decent music, cool hand drawn characters, bland environments, slightly problematic controls, after a point barely any challenge. If there was a  choice between positive and negative score on Steam, I would've chosen that one. But I will recommend this just because it plays fine, it never crashed or glitched on me, and even though it's extremely basic it's still a fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I randomly bought this on release and finished it then (albeit one of the bad endings) but put it on the backburner to see how the game would mature with future patches. I was pleasantly surprised to see it had quite a bit in the ensuing three months or so.  At launch, it had some questionable design decisions that were at odds with what one would expect from a metroidvania such as pitfalls that resulted in game over, attacks that overcommitted as you couldn't cancel the animation, and a bizarre decision to force backtracking in the endgame while permanently blocking certain routes.  Thankfully, much of this has been addressed and the game feels quite at home in the genre now. There are still minor quibbles with character balancing, boss balancing, and so on but the devs seem committed enough that I'm certain the end product will be something they can be proud of and something that'll be quite fun for anyone picking this up. I figure I'll be back for more in the future between wrapping up achievements or simply finishing the game with the other two characters I hadn't used yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but there's several problems. Namely, the combat is really hard, -but- doesn't give you a way to dodge roll, seemingly never gives you I-frames, and you get hurt just by touching an enemy, even if that doesn't make any sense given the enemy. (For example, why should the enemy whose entire moveset is to throw bombs damage you by proximity? By that logic why don't we damage them by proximity?) It's also unreasonably hard to jump over enemies. Oh, and speaking of jumping, the platforming is very floaty and imprecise, making parkour sections borderline unbearable.I would love to get back and play more of this game if they were to just make the controls a bit tighter and up the combat mechanics to be more playable. As it stands it's a deeply frustrating experience to play. (Also, please, let me turn off the snarky comments every time I respawn -- it gets old fast!)

_childDocuments_.review: 15h+ 4/10 1 with savescum, otherwise multiple Not yet. I made a start for a map guide, just to help others get through it and maybe build further on it. you can find it  No Yes, multiple. It doesn't help that after fighting the last boss you are stuck around that area and can't go back exploring. But even without that, there are achievements for multiple endings. Not really, you'll have leveled up all the characters around the ending which is the most grindy achievement No No No No No difficulty settings in the game, except that the game is easier with multiple players because you can resurrect each other NoI have a bit of a hard time writing this. I think Curse of the Sea Rats is a good game and it is quite addictive as I came back to it. Although in the period before the release, there were quite some bugs and it seems that the development team was a bit thin-spread with a local gaming fair the week before and also having to ship the physical Kickstarter copies themself. I understand that with a small team, there is only so much that you can do in a short amount of time,  but I hope the team will be able to fix the bugs found by the community. There were some things that made my playthrough less enjoyable:- Something with a sidequest with a bone that can screw you up quite badly, can't say much more because of spoilers- The gold chests give a food item that can heal you a  little bit, this felt quite underwhelming for a chest item, and being able to buy better items in the shop - The spirit that helps you during the game is such a grumpy grandpa, I wanted to ignore him but after dying for the X amount of time in a short time and him telling me how much I suck didn't help- And last but not least, the wind area is such a challenging area when playing solo, because getting blown off a platform, or getting attacked by the penguin birds and getting thrown off the platform is instant death, while in multiplayer you have a chance that the other player can revive youHowever, even having experienced already quite a few of the things above in the beginning, I kept coming back to the game to play more. So it was quite an addictive game and I'm glad I played through it. And as written above, to make it a bit worse is that you can't go back to explore the map further after defeating the last boss. I do recommend Curse of the Sea Rats if you enjoy metroidvania and especially if you want to play with others through it. _childDocuments_.review: I'm in complete disbelief as to how a game this amazing has such poor reviews... And to think i almost missed out on this absolute treasure of a game because of it. Now i'm aware that there were some issues at launch, especially with character controls relating to combat. But even if we ignore the combat there's still so many great things about this game that i just find it hart to believe how people could've been so harsh on what is for all intents and purposes a bloody great game. All of the problems have been fixed with the 3 post launch patches so what remains is a highly enjoyable experience from start to finish. Now it isn't perfect, the game has some issues mostly relating to balance and subtitles being wrong sometimes, but other than that there's literally nothing wrong with this. I wish i could do more to crank up the score to the blue numbers but alas one review will have to do... If you're on the fence like i was, and would like to go in a bit better informed i'll elaborate on some of the things that i loved about this game. The thing that stands out the most is the exploration and how fun it is to gradually uncover the map. The map and level design is great, there's a good flow to it. The map is hugely interconnected with shortcuts everywhere and each zone bordering on at least two others if not more. There's a large variety of environments, from shorelines to caves, forests and even crypts! The transitions between the biomes are also very well done, with rooms that blend the two together. The map design also makes sense, with the lighthouse on the side of the shores, at the highest point on the cliff. Or the trees that you climb with branching paths from the central stem. And caves that lie below the plains. I also must add that the visuals are absolutely gorgeous, there's so many beautiful vistas and backdrops with tons of variety. My personal favorites were the snowy forest, the underground shimmering pools and the autumnal forest. But even the most 'boring' zones, like the shoreline still look jawdroppingly pretty.Not only the environments are beautiful but the characters themselves too. Each character design is bursting with personality and animated to perfection. The store page brings this up but it's really amazing how smooth the animations look, and make the game feel. Each of the four characters you can play is highly different from the rest visually but also gameplay wise. They each have their own moveset and skilltree! While there's a lot of passive effects in there there's also several unique moves for each character. I played the whole game exclusively as the indian woman as she appealed to me the most with twin daggers, but i'm looking forward to playing as the others too. The japanese woman with her nage yari also looks super fun, as does the bouncer looking guy that loves to smash foes with his fists. Only the american gunslinger doesn't intrigue me the same way but each character also has unique voicelines throughout the story. This even further increases replayability and i'm excited to come back to this in a few years when i've forgotten most of the story.Speaking of story the game has an entertaining narrative that while not groundbreaking or indepth, still does a great job pulling you in. There's some comedy sprinkled in between that didn't always land, but did manage to make me chuckly a few times. Every interaction is also FULLY VOICED, which is mindboggling for an indie game. The voice acting varies from decent to very good and each character sounds quite different. Speaking of sounds the game has great sound effects but an even greater soundtrack. I'm happy that i picked it up with the bundle as the ost is amazing. No really, from the typical shanties you'd expect to serena soundtracks as you run through beautiful fields. This OST transported me into the world and i'll for sure listen to the amazing ost some more the coming weeks. Performance was also great and i didn't have any crashes and only one bug where i couldn't input any more controls and had to force quit the game, losing a tiny bit of progress in the process. The game is wel made and up until now mostly positives, however there are a few negatives that i'd also like to adress.The game starts of REALLY difficult, with most enemies and bosses two or three shotting you. This felt demotivating as i still have a huge backlog with plenty of hard games, so i'll take any easier one i can get. However as i gained some levels things quickly started becoming doable, easy even by the end. This isn't only due to gaining levels but also the healing consumables that are quite sparse at the start but by the end you have dozens of them. Late game bosses were more of an endurance test rather than a display of skill, although you could always challenge yourself to a hitless attempt. For healing i still prefer either the flask approach (blasphemous) or the spell aproach (Ori) but at least this game wasn't stingey with the consumables. The bosses themselves despite their inbalance were still very enjoyable due to their variety in designs and attacks. Everything is well telegraphed and apart from one late game boss that has a bottomless killpit, none of them feel BS. I really liked the bosses, enemies and combat in general in this game. It's smooth, fair and responsive now so even though it's basic it was still fun. What wasn't fun though was the the ghost companion taunting me after EVERY SINGLE death. However that and a few subtitle quirks are all that i can really fault this game with. So i think curse of the sea rats is a great game for pretty much anyone. Wether you like nice visuals, great metroidvania exploration or fun bosses. It's going into my libraries favorites and i can't wait to play it again at a later date. Now please give it a shot, you'll find it oozing with charm. And when the game has convinced you it's worth a shot, do your due dilligence by providing this gem of a game with a thumbs up. Help right one wrong in the world by giving this game the respect it deserves!

_childDocuments_.review: Updated for Patch 1.3.7 on 23rd June 2023.Game is in a much better place than it was at launch. A lot of work has been done to fix up the combat which, while still simplistic, has more speed and snappiness than it used to.My earlier criticisms about map progression and the removal of fast travel after a point in the game have also been fixed, as while it does still happen, it is now temporary — although you do have to be going for the "true" ending to unlock it.The team have worked hard and taken onboard community feedback in a solid way, thus I'll be changing my recommendation. While I still think it is, generally speaking, a somewhat mediocre metroidvania experience, it is a damned sight better than it was and that is worthy of praise. It may be good fun in co-op — certainly a lot of the people I've seen on the discord or forums who have been having a blast with it mention that they've been playing it with their partner and/or kids — so that's worthy of consideration!-----------------------ORIGINAL REVIEWS FOLLOW------------------------Updated for Patch 1.1.2: (28th April 2023)The below critique about blocking various pathways has been alleviated by now just being able to destroy the blocking boulders if you approach them from the correct side, which kinda destroys the purpose of them being a thing in the first place. While it is a change for the better, the removal of fast travel is still there making you run the entire length of the game world in the endgame to do any kind of cleanup.A Note on Playtime:There are always people who say "why play so much of the game if you didn't like it"?I make maps of metroidvanias. These require time and effort. Probably 50% of my game time in metroidvania games is map stuff or, in the case of Sea Rats, trying to figure out whether mechanics are bugged or just working weirdly. (In Sea Rats case, they were bugged. Quite a lot.)Original Review from v.1 of the game (Early April 2023)The last 10% of the game has you trek across the entire width of the map having removed your ability to fast travel AND blocking off various pathways to artificially lengthen the route. It pads out the game in the most frustrating way possible, at the time in a metroidvania where you should have the most options for traversal and exploration. Sadly the developers have made trying to 100% this map an absolute chore.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on Kickstarter in 2020 and followed the development over the years, because I was excited for the self-proclaimed 'ratoid-vania' and the art style drew me in. Now that it's finally here, I've gotten through one playthrough and it's fair to say the wait was questionable. First of all, the game's main difficulty curve relies on you being able to react quickly to flying enemies that can tank half your health no matter how much health you have or whatever level you are. I appreciate a little challenge but in this game it is a bit inconsistent. I struggled with the first boss, but pretty much steamrolled every other boss after that. I honestly died to the puffins in the Cliffs more than anything else. I appreciate what the devs were going for with this game but the plot fell flat with nonsense. The fully voiced characters were a nice surprise even though some of the dialogue was a bit underwhelming. Do I recommend this game? Yes, it deserves a playthrough or two, to see the alternate endings. If you enjoy metroidvanias, this game is at least worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing game and probably the game of the year of its genre. A really nice surprise despite all the negative feelings from others, which I do not understand and do not share. I really regret that I didn't manage to become a backer on Kickstarter and contribute more. The game could easily be 3x more expensive and it's really worth the money for current price. So I just hope that I will be able to make a KS pledge for the sequel...Amazing and careful craftsmanship, hand-drawn cute graphics and excellent gameplay supported by an above-average playing time makes this game great and funny. I definitely recommend it.The only thing that really surprised me was the difficulty. The game has only one and can not be changed or tweaked. I don't like very hard bosses in games in general, because it is often very hard to beat them for me and the only result is I am so frustrated durng playing. So I appreciate easy bosses, but it was suspiciously unbalanced here I think. Defeating Fatso required a bit of exping at first, but once I improved my character, I beat almost all the other bosses in the first 1-3 tries with a simple attack (with absolutely no cover and minimal use of magic). Personally this difficulty perfect fits to me, but it's a bit of a shame for other hardcore players, that it makes the gameplay monotonous or "uniform" during main battles. It's a pitty, when each boss is beautifully animated and has different types of attacks. The only exception was Murat Reis and especially the Necromant (but that was more about the jumping skill).In any case, finally a game that can fully compete the legendary Captain Claw. (1997)

_childDocuments_.review: Like others, I wanted to enjoy this game as it is actually full of charm, however, the controls are stiff and unsatisfying, everything does unnecessary large and unbalanced amounts of damage, and speaking of damage, there is something about the contact damage in this game, I can't quite put my finger on it, but it's really annoying, I think it's the fact that there is no knock back and there are very few frames of invincibility after taking damage, which causes you to sometimes sit inside an enemy taking a lot of damage before you can pull yourself together and move away from them. Hollow knight has set a new standard for Metroidvanias, and this game unfortunately does not come close in terms of controllability. For the sake of honesty I have to state that I took advantage of the refund time window, so yes I did not play too much of it, but what I did play was enough to know the amount of frustration that would be awaiting me in the future with this game, but I might come back for it in the future if the game gets cheaper and/or gets improved, but as it is right now I couldn't recommend it.Edit: I forgot to say that this game seems to not record the state your character and their inventory where in when you save in the save rooms, it just saves your position in the map, if you go, for example, into a Bossfight, use healing items and die, those healing items are not given back to you when you respawn in the save room, so you’re gonna have to grind for money to buy them again, and that’s unforgivable, if you’re going for a dark souls death mechanic, in a Metroidvania you need to give us an estus flasks, or at least have the game record everything I had on my inventory before death.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited about this game, but also worried when the reviews came out, since the most important part of a good metroidvania for me is good, fun controls. After having played the full game, I can happily say, whether due to patching or my own personal taste, I found the gameplay to be just fine. It's not good enough to make me want to play again just to play it like Hollow Knight or Metroid Dread, but it is good enough to not be a distraction, and that's really all this game needs it to be.The reason I say that is simply because everything else about this game is worth it. It is visually beautiful, with a much better variety of location and visuals than I was expecting. And as someone who owns rats, seeing a positive representation of rats in this beautiful style is wonderful.As for the metroidvania elements, it's a mixed bag, but mostly on the good side. The map is absolutely massive, and there's a lot of paths you can take, which makes exploration feel rewarding. The pace of acquiring new movement feels a bit imbalanced, with most of the movement given to you early, and late game it's mostly just keys, which feel disappointing in comparison.As for combat, I'm torn. The first difficulty spike is too early, and too high, which I imagine throws a lot of people off. Also, the retrieval of xp can sometimes be inconvenient, and would be better served if it was always left outside the boss zone. I would actually compare it pretty closely to Shantae games, so if you enjoy those games, once you get past the first difficulty spike you should be fine.On the whole, I was very happy with this game. I had fun, and I'm looking forward to playing again with another character and also getting my wife to play as well. If you have the patience to get past the early difficulty spike, I think you will greatly enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of the Sea Rat is a audio-visually solid handrawn 2D metroidvania platformer for genre newbies which misses (like Itorah) the chance to really stand out from a game mechanical point of view.Difficulty ★★★★☆☆☆☆☆☆ (very fair mechanics except of contact damage)Updated for v1.3.7* absolutely awesome character and world design (especially Flora Burn, she is a blast)* cool artstyle* handdrawn cutscenes (I do love this)* lovely details and a lot of camos or homage appearances of other game or movie character* 4 game coop (this is unique for a Metroidvania)* good soundtrack (I have about 3-4 tunes I totally love)* a lot of funny dialogues, especially with David Douglas* we still wait for some interesting KS stretchgoals* Petoons are still overworking things* insta-deaths when falling off is removed (v1.3.7; except in boss fights)* Petoons listened to the critics and changed the endgame mechanics (portals and world can be free roamed and used again)* handdrawn cutscenes could have been made better (more details and frames) * fight system is a little bit clunky (later more on this)* hitboxes of dangerous environment is sometimes off* no new game+* no difficulty settings (this especially is annoying when playing in coop)* I do not like the voice acting of Bussa at all* Ressurection ring can't be recharged properly. The dull version just disappears* you can virtually kill yourself to 0 HP by switching characters with low health points (ring needed)* false color, shadow or whirling bushes bug will be trigger somewhere in Erius and Banba Forest on longer playthroughs (day 1 problem)* coop mode: if player 2-4 will trigger a cutscene, it can happen the wrong voiceover is used for some dialogue lines (eg. Akane with Bussa voice)* coop mode: if you come from the right side to the spider mini boss player 2-4 get stuck outside screen* coop mode: if you die and get revived it can happen that souls and money collected get temporarily stuck on your face reloading or restarting the game is often a solution to fix persistent misbehaviour of the game.While the hitbox system got a little bit fixed during combat, hitboxes with environment and contact damage are still a little bit weird. Also only David and Akane have a good aerial control due to the multi boucne and floating dash ability they can unlock. Also there is absolutely no difficulty settings. You can only switch to a inferior character and limit yourself in some things (no item or magic use, no upgrading) to make it more interesting. There is no adaptice difficulty behaviour for coop mode, like +50% enemy HP for every player joining. Also a new game+ or boss rush would be pretty nice. But we still miss some KS stretchgoals, so let's stay tuned for that. I must admit that as a Kickstarter backer I am not totally free of some preconception. I backed this project because I totally loved Petoons idea, design and handdrawn concepts from the very beginning. The final result is still pretty well, especially after the first two patches. They are on the right way.Personally I do enjoy the game and played it multiple times through with different characters and friends together. Even with all the little 'edges' here and there I have a blast playing it. Some people on Steam are going too harsh on the devs if you ask me. This game gets better the more polishing Petoons does, and I see forward what will come next. And I also will be on their next kickstarter project as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The hitboxes of this game are horrible. You visually strike the enemy (your weapon visually goes through the enemy), but the hit is not registered. The art is fine, but the combat is infuriating. I don't understand why the devs couldn't fix these weird hit boxes after so long and so many complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy Metroidvanias?If so, you're going to like this game.It's a competently put together Metroidvania that'll give you everything you enjoy from them, but it won't blow your mind. It's good, but not great.Pros: The art is beautifulThe music is fantasticAnimations are fluid and greatRunning and jumping feels nice and fluid.Cons:Stage design is... Just OK.Combat doesn't feel as fluid as it could have done. Whenever you swing your weapon, your character comes to a full stop, which feels somewhat yanky.Hazards aren't as obvious as they could be. I've run right into spikes because they just haven't been visible enough.The story is, quite frankly, bad and uninteresting. Which is impressive for a story about pirate rats. It tries to be funny. Sadly, it usually fails.Save locations are awful. Many times they lead to a Lot of annoying backtracking. Usually because of dying at a boss and the save location requires moving through multiple screens, often including a teleporter, just to get back. It makes trying again on a boss tedious.Some bosses feel cheap due to instant death falls.Worst part of the experience:At one point you go into a dark location that require a lamp you can purchase.The lamp break when you die.In the dark location there's a boss.Dying to the boss means you respawn in a light area without your lamp.Forcing you to run to a shopkeeper and buy a new lamp before running back.It just... Feels awful.A lot of negatives, but I still give it a thumbs up. Why? Because it's a Good game. Not a great game. Not a fantastic game. Not one everyone ever should play.But if you enjoy metroidvanias, you'll have fun. Not as fun as if you played Cave Story, Metroid, Symphony of the Night or Hollow Knight. But still. It's not a bad game, just not perfect. And that's fine too.

_childDocuments_.review: This is about a 7/10. It's good! Not great, but good. The game absolutely does not deserve a "Mostly Negative" review. So I am making one to discuss my honest opinion. It is certainly not a must buy, but it is good! It deserves a reasonable chance. It works, I have not had any major glitches in my 7 hours of play so far. I have not beaten the game but have cleared around 70% of the map.I played co-op with a person remotely without any issues. Which is nice. It is a functional metroidvania style of game and I found it very fun as a multiplayer experience. The characters all have good designs and a different sort of build you'll end up with as you level them up. Each fits a certain archetype and you can sort of tell by looking at their skill tree. You will unlock a dash later which is also different depending on your character. Characters are beautifully animated. Environments are good, but not quite as gorgeous. The environments are varied enough and have distinct zones which makes traversal interesting.General enemies are varied and not too hard to manage. None have felt overly unfair or repetitive. I do think some of them are very small scale critters but it has a certain charm to it. They sometimes throw a mini gauntlet at you which is fun. I think it helps sell the world a bit better like this so I am happy with the variety.Combat is really fun but I do think there are some issues. One is character who can parry seem to be unable to parry many boss attacks. It rarely makes sense to bother with trying to parry over just doing damage. There are characters who can just block and I have to test if that works on bosses. Either way it is not well communicated what can or can not be parried. The timing is very generous on normal enemies and can be somewhat useful there. Maybe there is stricter timing on bosses but this frustrated me. Combat could certainly feel more fluid but I found I adapted in time and it felt much better. This game does commit the major sin of contact damage. It is very annoying with some abilities. It really should only be attached to an enemy which is charging forward or doing an attack in said direction. The bosses are all different and try to vary up how you're playing.  They are creative and have a lot of character behind them. I will say that at the start they felt much more powerful, but by mid game some did become a bit too easy. This is mostly because you have options, more healing resources, and enough health to take a few hits later. It's not bad to have games which are a bit easier but it does feel like the game wanted to be a little more challenging. Especially since the early game has them feeling more dangerous. I am not sure it would benefit from becoming a slog though so it is not a terrible thing. They are fun for what they are, but if you are looking for a crazy challenge this will not offer that to you. The world hides lots of references and funny item descriptions. Side quests seem okay though one is very punishing for no good reason and it can be unclear if there is a followup or not for others. There is one quest where you only have 3 chances to do it which was annoying but no others like it which i've seen. Voice work is decent. It is nothing you'll be blow away by but I found it tolerable. Some of it certainly seemed less professional. I appreciate that they did voice most characters though and it adds to the feel of the world. Ultimately I think this is a great game to play with a friend or great for someone hungry for metrioidvanias. It is not the best out there but it isn't a busted or bad time at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 2 3/4 hours, give or take a few minutes. I've been looking forward to this game since I first caught wind of it, a couple of years ago, I think. Damaging spots on spikes seems inconsistent; there were times where I passed through a spike and didn't take damage, and other times where I didn't quite touch them and took damage anyway. The attacking animation stops my character dead in place. They teach you to block/retaliate early in the game, but from all I could tell from the first boss, it doesn't work on bosses, so I stopped trying that tactic.This is all in sharp contrast to the gorgeous artwork and fun characters. I appreciate that the cast of playable characters is actually pretty diverse, instead of "another generic white guy #3562", too. But none of that will matter if the game isn't fun to play.I will own up to the fact that I'm not good at games like these, so I do my best not to let my lack of skill color my interpretation or enjoyment, but after almost three hours of this, I just don't care for it that much. _childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty interesting game overall, it's a slight recommend for me because it does have some issues that could be off-putting to some players.  First, the art and style of the game ooze charm as you can tell a lot of love was poured into this game.  Full voice acting on all characters in the game and the vibrant style really make this game come to life well.As a metroidvania, the map is decently sized, but there are not a ton of "upgrades" in the sense that you see in other games of the genre.  Fairly early on you will get double jump, and shortly after that you get the dash (which can be used in the air in combo with double jump).  At this point the movement in the game feels pretty good, and from this point on, you are not really unlocking much in the way of new exploration powers.  I actually played the entire game and missed the "super jump" until right near the end when I stumbled across a boss I had missed. It was not needed to clear the game at all, and the game does open up a bit and give you a lot of freedom in terms of where to go next.  The rest of the time, progression will be blocked by locked doors requiring keys, or quest related items scattered around the games sizable map.  You get to pick a character at the start of the game with no information on their talent trees, but you can switch characters at any save point and keep your levels, but talents for each much be leveled separately by using the souls-like currency that drops a percentage of when you die.  The lost currency can be regained by going back to where you died, and it was super easy to farm it if you want to as it's dropped fairly liberally compared to the cost of upgrading.I did get the true ending I would say, and my playtime is shorter than advertised.  This is in large part because the character I ended up sticking with, David the sword user rat, has a life-stealing ability that was bonkers broken to the point where it was very hard to die once I unlocked it.  Falling into some pits still results in an instant death, but these are not too common outside of one or two areas.  I steamrolled pretty hard with this and its probably why my playtime of 6 hours clocks in less than other players who may be using other characters.   There are no difficulty settings, but if you don't want to be challenged you can play this character as I did and sail through the game if you are a casual player.The controls can be remapped once you are in the game, but not from the options on the title screen, and the gameplay is not super responsive for combat, but movement generally felt really nice with dash and double jump.  There is a "point of no return" late in the game, and its not telegraphed ahead of time, so you may be missing on out achievements and such on a single play if you end up crossing this point and save before you are ready.All this being said, I enjoyed the game for what it was, and it oozes charm with a lot of funny references through the story and cast of characters and bosses who are fully voice acted from start to end, even with some nice cut scenes sprinkled in there.  I played on keyboard and had no issues at all once I found out how to remap the controls.  I recommend this but it may not be everyone depending on what you are looking for in a metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review:
Curse of the Sea Rats is a 'ratoidvania' platform adventure with lovingly crafted, hand-drawn animations.

Embark on the epic journey of four prisoners of the British empire, transformed into rats by the notorious pirate witch, Flora Burn. To regain their human bodies, they will have to fight dangerous bosses, uncover the secrets of the vast Irish coast, and ultimately capture the witch who cursed them.

A labyrinthine network of hundreds of pathways, rooms and discoveries lie ahead, in a substantial quest with over 12 hours of content.

Can you master each character's playstyle, find all the hidden secrets, and unlock each of the game's multiple endings?
