detailed_description: Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box This title is included in Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box! New tales from the Borderlands: Deluxe Edition Control your corner of the universe with New Tales from the Borderlands - Deluxe Edition! This Edition includes: The PC version of New Tales from the Borderlands. Tales from the Borderlands Full Game: Play as Rhys and Fiona in this hilarious, heart-wrenching story set on the desert world of Pandora About the Game Take a stand against ruthless corporate overlords in this narrative-driven adventure! Within the perpetually war-torn metropolis of Promethea, you'll control Anu, Octavio, and Fran on the worst day of their lives. Help these three lovable losers as they endeavor to change the world (and maybe even save it)! Face down a planetary invasion, vicious vault monster, and cold-hearted capitalist in this cinematic thrill ride where what happens next is up to you! Meet a motley cast full of misfits, assassin bots, and talking guns in this race to the top! It's time to fight back against exploitation and corporate greed. It's time to make Mayhem your business. THE UNDERDOG STORY OF THREE LOVABLE NOBODIES Decide the fates of altruistic scientist Anu, her ambitious, 'streetwise' brother Octavio, and the fierce, frogurt-slinging Fran. With nothing left to lose and everything to gain, you'll claw and con your way through this thrilling five-part story full of gun-toting goons, otherworldly beasts, and delicious tacos. AN EXTRAORDINARY CINEMATIC ADVENTURE The Borderlands aren't just home to Vault Hunters, psychos, and weapons-corp CEOs—they're full of downtrodden, intrepid civilians just trying to get by. With a host of returning and fresh faces, including an assassin bot with comedic aspirations and a less-murderous-than-usual bandit, this unforgettable tale is sure to delight fans new and old. YOUR CHOICES SHAPE THE OUTCOME The decisions you make determine how your story ends. Whether it's Anu's vision of a universe that markets more than weapons, Octavio's dreams of fame and fortune, or Fran's frosty plot for revenge—their success or failure depends on you.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the  franchise who played everything it has to offer (even the now defunct  on iOS), I really wanted to like this game. Telltale’s  (2014-2015) is my personal favorite of the franchise (sorry !) and when a (spiritual) successor was announced, I had high hopes – even if the new game would be developed by Gearbox Studio Quebec instead of the old Telltale team. Sure, the writing of  wasn’t great () and  did only  in that regard. But for the sake of the old , I just had to take the chance.Now, as you already know from the headline of this review and the “not recommended” status, I unfortunately did not have the experience I hoped for – in fact, it was even worse than I feared. And I’ll tell you why in a minute, but first, I want to highlight the fact that the development of this game was . For example, motion capturing had to be done with far less people involved than originally planned, which resulted in story rewrites. No one can say if the game would’ve turned out better if the development went as planned, of course – but I still feel like this might be one of the reasons why the game turned out as bad as it did.The first disappointment for fans of the original  is going to be fact that this new game is not connected to the old one at all, save for some very, very few cameo moments. Even though the original game ended on a cliffhanger that was only partially resolved during , everyone hoping for some well-deserved returns of certain characters is going to be disappointed:  is an entirely new story with new protagonists instead.To quote this: “We want to make [the game] entirely contained and different so that people, whether they're returning fans or new players, can fully enjoy the game without having to worry too much about what came before“. In my personal opinion, this is already a weird decision, as the  franchise has so many established characters and plot points well-deserving of more story involvement, that a self-contained story featuring entirely new characters just seems unnecessary.But even apart from the question if a self-contained new story was the right direction to take the franchise in, the promise of new players being able to  enjoy the game without previous knowledge doesn’t work out. While the main story should still be understandable, many  concepts, like the Vaults, Eridium or Sirens, are playing a part in this new story – without being explained at all. As such, I wonder if players unfamiliar with the franchise would really be able to  enjoy this game – apart from the fact that the rest of the game itself is far from enjoyable. is a story-driven game focusing on three protagonists acting as a team. It’s all told in five episodes for some reason, even if they all released at the same time as part of a package. In fact, the episodic formula doesn’t even add anything to the game narratively. Each episode starts off with an opening song and intro, but they don’t even come close to the  of the original  – a shame.Probably the biggest narrative problem of  is the aforementioned protagonist trio. They’re advertised as “underdogs” we’re supposed to root for but frankly, they’re annoying, unlikeable and downright frustrating to deal with sometimes. This feels especially weird to me since the  franchise is filled to the brim with “unusual” characters who are still likeable. But here, the main characters all act like idiots to the point where I just desperately wanted to force-quit. A character literally dies because one of the protagonists doesn’t manage to open a door (pushing instead of pulling), for example, while another protagonist manages to turn the final reward of an entire episode (!) into nothingness in mere minutes.Initially I hoped for some type of character development, something that would make me sympathize with the protagonists – but to no avail, the characters would continue to be unlikeable morons. The game tries to sell you some character arcs during the last episodes, but they’re a) really, really forced and b) don’t change anything. The protagonist trio remains insufferable with no regard to anything except themselves. Frankly, during the last hour of my playthrough I was just hoping they ended up with such a small role that later games in the  franchise could simply ignore their existence.Apart from the protagonists, the game features a few side characters, but most of them are only seen for mere minutes – which is a shame since they’re already way more interesting and likeable than the protagonists during these few minutes (e.g. Stapleface, Phuong). Considering how little they show up, it’s even more baffling that  tries to pull off an emotional moment with one of these side characters – which of course fails simply because we never got to really know them.Speaking of emotional moments,  consequently manages to eliminate any potential feelings of suspense, tragedy and whatnot thanks to its sense of humor. No matter the situation, there’s always an unfitting, dumb joke around the corner to prevent this game from having any impact at all. Even the final battle, the climax of five episodes, is far from a glorious and suspenseful ending – instead it’s an extremely awkward fight thanks to ill-fitting attempts at humor.That said, apart from having no emotional impact whatsoever, the overall plot is way too long for what it actually ends up saying. The antagonist only shows up a few times and is frankly wasted on a story like this, turning from a villain I would’ve loved to see in  to a joke thanks to the final episode. Actually, the beginning and the end of  are the only parts that actually matter, the entire middle part feels like pointless filler with few consequences. also offers very, very few locations to visit, which makes the game feel even smaller – and makes its length even worse. There’s only a handful of areas you can walk around in for a few minutes until you’re mostly reduced to QTEs and dialogue options in the exact same locations again. The most gameplay comes from a forced sidegame called Vaultlanders, which amounts to pressing an attack button a lot and a directional button every 20 seconds. That’s it. I have no idea why it’s even a thing.The only good thing I can say about  would be its engine working better than the old Telltale engine did. But apart from that, this entire game is just a frustrating experience for even the most devoted  fans. Unless you absolutely need to know every piece of lore of this universe, I can’t recommend playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: as a long time HUGE fan of Tales from the Borderlands, which is an exceptionally moving game and beautiful story, and a fan of the whole borderlands franchise as well , this game is terrible .Tales from the Borderlands was BEAUTIFUL game about growing as a person, recovery, and love . the messages and the character growth and the love between the characters was incredible and really struck the heartstrings. what the game did best other than the concept, was the pacing and execution. what Tales gets right that New Tales completely fails at, is pacing. Tales knew exactly when to make a joke and when to allow tonal shift, saving the jokes for inbetween banter and triumphant moments after the sad. NEW TALES IS ENTIRELY JOKES . NOT 20 SECONDS CAN PASS BEFORE A TERRIBLE SELF AWARE JOKE IS MADE . AND ITS JUST SO BAD . there is NO emotional value in this game whatsoever, and that would be fine given that this is supposed to be a comedy or something, if only it was actually funny . Tales from the Borderlands is one if not THE MOST charming games ive ever played in my entire life, and this does it no justice . Tales is a timeless masterpiece that shook me to my core, if you for some reason havent already , GO PLAY TALES FROM THE BORDERLANDS. TLDR : i finished the whole game and i regret it sooo much . it was not worth the money or energy playing for hours to maybe get to "the good bit " that never came . its not funny , its not particularly well written at all, just. if you like Tales from the Borderlands or even any borderlands game you wont like this onePLEASE dont waste your money on this game it isnt worth it i promise, go play the original Tales.and even if i was to simply play this game ignoring the rest of the franchise, i would still HATE this dumpsterfire sorry

_childDocuments_.review: I love Borderlands and I especially loved Tales from the Borderlands. It's one of my favorite games ever and I actually just replayed it over the last few days in anticipation of this sequel.I could not be more disappointed. After 90 minutes, it is officially the first game I have ever requested a refund for. I've bought and played many dozens of games for just a short time that didn't really hook me but never once did I consider a refund because maybe one day I'll come back. But with New Tales I didn't even hesitate. It's just that bad.- The writing is awful and pure cringe. Some of the things the characters say don't even make sense. I groaned and/or rolled my eyes a dozen times.- The characters are annoying and over-act every line. - The controls are clunky, the QTEs are on really short timers, and the characters walk awkwardly fast like they're on one of those airport moving walkways. - It doesn't really look or feel anything like the Borderlands universe.- Rhys was turned into a psychopathic violence-merchant, completely disrespecting his character development and personality from the original Tales and BL3. This was seemingly done to fit the "everything corporate is evil and bad" theme that permeated every single scene that I played . Which brings me to the last point...- There is a distinct sense that the people who made this game cared more about injecting their personal ideologies at every possible moment rather than making a fun game with good characters and story-telling.+ Literally nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: I love borderlands- definitely more than most people. I'm autistic, and this game series/franchise is my special interest- has been since I was introduced to the Borderlands Universe with the original Tales from the Borderlands in 2015. I own every borderlands game, every DLC, and copious amounts of merchandise, and have not regretted a thing-- until this game. I regret buying it. I uninstalled it as soon as I completed my first, and last, play-through. I thought I knew what to expect with this game, but I was wrong. I was completely blind-sided by how confusing and bad this game was.  There is no consistent plot- when one thing is established, a completely different thing sidetracks the original or contradicts it entirely. There are situations in the game that Make No Sense in the context of the greater Borderlands Universe, and the characters acted in unexpected/nonsensical ways that left me going, "huh?" I actually found myself asking, out loud to no one, "What the ♥♥♥♥ is this?" numerous times throughout the game. It was like watching a failed group project, where everyone had different ideas and the teacher felt bad telling anyone no, so all the ideas and elements were mashed into one game- regardless of whether it made sense or made for a good story. Characters that Should Not have been present in this game, especially in the context they were presented in, were there. I had to pause a number of times and walk away from my computer to process what I'd just watched. Mechanically, this game is a mess. In the original Tales from the Borderlands, your choices had tangible, visible consequences and actively changed the story. In this game, your choices had little to no impact on the story. The system for measuring team cohesion/compatibility makes no sense, and despite my best efforts I was unable to actually Do Anything. The quick time events also had little to no effect. There were a few situations where not completing the tasks in time had consequences, but I had many moments throughout the game were I asked why the event was even happening- it'd be nonsensical or feel poorly placed. There was also no clear way to tell What the quick time events actually did- there was one quick time event that, after I failed it, I realized I would have made the character shoot himself had I succeeded the event. The only part of this game that I genuinely enjoyed and had fun were the Vaultlanders Battles. At least with those I felt like I had some semblance of choice or agency in the game. TL;DR This game gave me headaches, left me with more questions than I thought possible, and I am incredibly disappointed. Do not buy this game- and if you have to buy it, only do so when it's on sale.

My review isn't even that funny and it will probably get more laughs than a single joke told in this schlock fest.  This game feels insecure. Not in its build but in the way that it's trying way too hard. Borderlands has always had a solid character base with cynical humor sprangled in. These are the flattest most corporate characters (ironically) that I have ever encountered in a video game. I feel like every time they speak they turn and they wink into the camera.I feel like I'm constantly waiting for a "well that just happened" or a "let me guess, he's right behind me isn't he?". Like even bad marvel writing isn't this bad.  I have no idea how I achieved the playtime that I have with this. I must have left this on in the background at some point because I can't imagine I finished this at any point. Who knows? Perhaps this game is genuinely so bad that I blocked it out. Don't waste your time or money even if you get it on a bundle. This game is so terribly written that gearbox should be paying people to play it

_childDocuments_.review: NTales is as bad as it looked on the tin, after fully completing this game, I can confirm the lack of marketing isn't a company oversight, it's so the game's absolutely abysmal quality doesn't cause a bunch of video game reviewer youtubers to bring negative traction to it like they did for BL3 and further sink Gearbox's awful reputation. This might be a bit scatterbrained because it's just really hard to conveniently describe the many ways this game fails to me.So, to address the most pressing issue, dialogue in this game feels like it was written by a person who has never interacted with a single human being in their life. People really under-appreciate how well Telltale nailed the whole "guiding you through choices and conversations" thing. In Telltale, I could easily follow how characters felt, what they were talking about, and the meaning behind why I am getting the choice to expose specific dialogue when presented. In NTales, I frequently have problems trying to track what the ♥♥♥♥ characters are talking about, because no joke, so much of the dialogue is just repetitive filler that goes nowhere. Tacked onto a "team score" system that seemingly has no actual relation to each other, this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare for tracking your team score and character-relationship score because it's never very clear what raises or decreases it. The game is uh "nice enough" to have Telltale's ! checkmark system that warns you an event happened because of your choices, but not nice enough to at least tell you how your score changes with each dialogue choice making everything about the presentation a lot more confused.Adding onto that, each character has a different "icon" for whose making the dialogue decision but no customized UI like OG Tales to help instantly clarify whose making this choice, quite frequently leading me to make a decision I did not want on a character. (Being rude w/ Octavio rather than Fran because I didn't notice the Octavio icon mid scene) Some QTE's in the game are also choices being presented as QTEs that you have to intentionally miss to make the choice, rather than actually clarifying what will happen if you don't hit the QTE like Telltale does. There's also no icon for character-specific QTE's, so I also had a less common issue with the wrong character doing something I would rather they not, such as Octavio shooting someone.Because of the lack of clarity on what the point of choices were, and why the game recorded them, when the episode choice recap appeared at the end of an episode, I quite frequently found myself unable to recall what choices the game was even referring to. I have literally never played a Telltale game where I couldn't recall the big choices the game tracked, but in New Tales a bunch of random dialogue choices are tracked and even big choices fall to the wayside of your mind for how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring and un-interesting the game is.These characters spend most of the game talking about literally nothing in circles in ONE singular room for 30 minutes with little to no action or interesting thought attached. Meanwhile OGTales, everyone was on a slow paced but constantly progressing adventure, they were interacting with each other while advancing towards the vault, and fighting for their lives to prove they were goofballs but capable of working together to get to that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ vault. It's frustrating, and by Episode 4, most of the game is rendered pointless and we haven't at all made progress as a company, we've just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ around doing nothing in the least endearing way ever. So by the time you get to the finale where the game acts like these characters have changed and grown as people, all you can think about is how the game wasted 4 whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ episodes of character development time to force it at the last possible second of E5 and then act like it was worked upon the whole game. The ONLY character I can say had a somewhat of an actual arc was Anu.Speaking of the characters, the main three are all mostly unlikable. I found myself surprised by how great Fran was only for her to be devolved to a really gross sex-pest that immediately killed my interest in the character. Sorry but having her constantly hit on everyone and the more creepy ♥♥♥♥ she says and reacts with in the game pretty easily made me not like her, I really hate sex-pest dialogue, it's not funny, it's really creepy and uncomfortable. If that was just removed from her character and she was treated as an actual person, I think she would be the best character in this game of garbage because her voice acting is great, and a lot of her dialogue is good. Octavio is just, the worst. So much unnecessary melodrama in this game is caused by this character and instead of blaming Octavio for what is obviously a lack of intellect and seriousness in dangerous situations, the game instead wants you to empathize with his stupidity and understand he's... "DOING HIS BEST???" I genuinely don't understand how anyone thought this was logical when this character does nothing but harm this game with his inconsistent character and inconsistent stupidity. He literally negates half of Episode 3's plot because of a dumb decision you can't control that even HE wouldn't make. His voice acting is terrible and he constantly delivers lines in the worst way humanly possible (no offense to the VA), and his dialogue is so SO exhausting. A lot of times Octavio's comments actively sidetrack you from the actual conversation, or have nothing to do with it. It's a lot of meaningless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thats just there to waste time, and a more insidious thing the game does is that whenever Octavio does something insanely stupid, YOU are in control of HIS dialogue instead of the person mad at him. Meaning you literally can't even directly chastize Octavio for his stupidity in game, you have to ♥♥♥♥ on the people who are mad for VERY VALID REASONS.Anu is just confusing, she starts off as the worst character in the game but does get better as her VA delivers lines in a way that makes me feel like I want to scream and not in a good way, I don't know how to describe it but I think they were trying to portray her as neurotic and anxious but the delivery, idk, it leaves a lot to be desired. She was easily the character I wanted to play the least and actively felt dread getting thrown into a segment with her. Throughout the story she's honestly the most determined to actually progressing the plot which is respectable but she's always whining which makes her very tiring to listen to. That and she takes way too long to notice the worlds most obvious things, the amount of melodrama that comes out of characters getting injured when she has a <spoiler> that should always be at the forefront of her mind is ridiculous and unbelievable. Throughout the game, she does become more confident and less whiney, but again, happens way too late, actual progress as a character should be present throughout everything, not just changing entirely at the last possible moment. Overall, NTales is more of a cringe endurance test than a new borderlands narrative game experience. I was sick of it about 10 minutes into the game and had to make it about 10 hours while my brain melted with each new experience. I will admit to laughing from time to time, I had about 2 laughs per episode but a big problem was that when I finally gave the game credit for it's humor, it would hit me with a joke so unfunny, I'd pause the game and just think about how so much of this cringe dialogue got into the final product. It's ridiculous that NTales released in this state and was allowed to just, be such a blight on the Tales series. Tales wasn't a masterpiece, but it was definitely a good game and deserved more than whatever the hell this was.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Telltale Games and the Borderlands series. The original Tales from the Borderlands is one of my favorite narrative games period. So it's very disappointing that this game ended up being so bad. Here's a list of things I didn't like:Freakish, twitchy, and uncanny character animations (especially when they're 'dancing', yuck). Of course Telltale animations were stilted and awkward, but damn if they didn't know how to play it up for comedic effect. Here the characters wriggle and writhe like lake leeches.Voice acting is very amateur with only a few exceptions. Feels like high school drama department a lot of the times. Out of the main 3 I liked Fran the most but even she is prone to delivering her lines with a thick, syrupy texture like she's on stage or in a radio booth. Octavio was by far the worst of the 3 and sounded like it was his initial line read. Anu was ... okay.Obnoxious loud = funny characters. Timm-E, Stapleface, Brock, the list goes on. Even  has a character screaming at you. Pack your earplugs.Underutilizing actually interesting characters, like Diamond, Radon, Pierre, and Phuong.  Pierre in particular got a few good laughs from me and I was hoping he'd end up as a business rival of sorts, maybe this game's answer to Vasquez? Instead the game decided to devote more time to the screamers and to the Badass Superfan, whose gimmick ran dry after 2 encounters and never did anything interesting.Lou13's general incompetence and uselessness. And unfunniness. So, so, so many jokes fall flat. Tacos galore and immature sex jokes are the order of the day. Not like hanging out with your friends but with friends of your friends' friends. Technical issues like stuttering, hitching, and texture pop-ins. Also had an amusing bug of Fran's arms staying up in a shrug after observing things while playing as her but that was funny.The music is so weak and noiselike, both the score and the montage-intros. Not an earworm to be found, whereas the original Tales and other Borderlands games had plenty of fun tunes in the intros and as background music.EVERY action scene has NO room to breathe. Like seriously, let the action play out without pausing every slight movement to make a weak quip or joke. It's like a Marvel movie that doesn't know when to quit but dialed up to 11. The choreography is also incredibly sluggish, Characters stand around during cutscenes and just let things happen, which is the same problem that BL3 had. This could've been Gearbox's chance to satirically address it but, aside from one tiny joke about waiting for a slow machine arm to finish moving, they just continued doing it. Example: Pacing is so, so slow and greatly harms the storytelling. Conversations last way too long and I definitely had the feeling of "why are they still standing around talking?" more often than not. Dialogue also has trouble ending without 3-5 extra seconds of the camera lingering on a person's face for no reason. Of course this is sometimes used for comedic effect, but the majority of the time it simply doesn't pull away quickly enough.They really had no idea what to do with Rhys, personality and story-wise. He's a whiny coward and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just like he was in BL3, further doing away with his development in the original Tales. Plot holes and contrivances. Here's some right off the top of my head: I never felt like my choices really mattered, Common complaint about Telltale-style games, I know, but here it was especially bad. This was due in large part to side characters that you have an impact on not affecting the story significantly.And finally, my BIGGEST gripe with the game is its team rating system. You are actively discouraged from making silly choices/choices that the characters themselves would make because it will ruin your team dynamic as well as lock you out of the best ending. Lou13 will also berate you with out of place remarks about how shoddy your teamwork is and your team's negative "vibe" mere seconds after the team has finished high-fiving and congratulating each other on a job well done. In any narrative game, railroading sucks. But in a choose-your-own-adventure game? It's a cardinal sin. What kind of comedic-focused narrative game tries to steer you away from the comedy? It's just fundamentally messed up.Some things I did like: Juniper and the Shard Spirit are cute. Episode 3 is the best of the bunch and I genuinely laughed a few times there. Cosmetic options are cool, if jarring to see on a first playthrough. I like the Vaultlanders announcer in a sort of ironic way and how he's halfway between trying and not trying.In all honesty, New Tales is how I expected the original Tales from the Borderlands to be based on the writing quality of the Borderlands series: obnoxious, dull, and sluggish. Fortunately, all those years ago I was happy to be proven wrong by the talented team at Telltale. But now with Gearbox writers at the helm, you can see the sex-joke addicted chickens have finally come to roost in their rotting coop, and New Tales suffers for it. I only paid $4.50 as part of the Pandora's Box bundle and I feel really bad for people who trusted Gearbox and paid full price at launch. As Fran would say: "I'm not angry, just disappointed."

_childDocuments_.review: so, new tales from the borderlands was ... something! i was really excited going into it, and i can say it was moderately enjoyable. it was not worth $40-50 at all, esp. with the preorder which included three skins in all grey!! woohoo!! that was super cool!!!in comparison to the original tales from the borderlands, the game shines in some aspects. the mocapping is wonderfully done. a lot of people are saying its awkward and weird, and at some times, it definitely can be. its not an entirely perfect system but it shows a good amount of emotion. with the funding of telltale’s tftbl, it was clear where they were lacking. odd cuts, janky animations, etc.the gameplay of new tales is definitely more polished. there were a few things that were odd and not well done and some segments were definitely dragged out a lot more than they shouldve been. i wish there were more interactable events in the world b/c i did enjoy exploring. vaultlanders was a unique addition, though overall felt very lacking and didnt make sense in terms of the storyline. it couldve done without it, and im 99% sure this was only added for replay value (collectables?)they brought in some other new things i didnt necessarily enjoy. the entire system that was created for rating the group dynamic also did not care in terms of the game. i had about two scenarios where it did.i didnt even know what was changing my group dynamic or how characters felt about one another. i didnt even know if they were on good terms by the ending of the game -- it wasnt made clear by gameplay. my only indication were a few popups stating “fran doesnt respect octavio” (yeah, i wouldnt either) and it was annoying. lou13 has an entire point in the beginning of the game stating teamwork would make the process easier to survive, and yet this didnt reflect one in the entire game. not where i saw, at least.holy. ♥♥♥♥. they bombed hard with the music choices. one of the BIG big aspects of tales, what made it shine, was the introduction and intros. they were well done, crisp, perfectly timed. its difficult for me to pick a favourite intro from any episode of tales because theyre all so well done -- from a stylish crash onto pandora to “busy earning” by jungle, to the somber crash onto pandora to “retrograde” by james blake. it was clear every song in tales was carefully chosen and the intros were framed around them.whereas in new tales, its... weird. the introductions to the episodes are odd, weirdly timed and dont expand upon much. it felt like they were trying too hard to mimic the bonding the tales team went through -- but that was natural in comparison to this. even then, there wasnt a single introduction i enjoyed. episode 5′s introduction was the best out of the bunch but even then, the music choice was odd and it felt like there was nothing happening. it wasnt worth watching. whereas in tales, it would hook you and keep you there the entire time.the name cards are also very oddly timed. a lot of them dont appear when theyre supposed to. typically in borderlands, we get a line or two before a character’s name is revealed. i found multiple times, either name cards did not appear for characters that would be reoccurring, or would just be flat out poorly timed. it didnt feel like borderlands, which is known for the flash of the cards and the catchy one-liners to accompany them.i think episodes 2-3 were quite literally worthless and provided nothing. i dont think i even remember what happened in those episodes. the ones that really captured me, were the last two. its where the spirit of the game (quite literally) came out to reveal itself. i didnt expect myself to get emotional but episode four did make me cry, and then immediately sober up in confusion when it jumped to a retro 90s fighting style game with fran.some of the jokes dont hit quite right and a lot of episode four is... odd. between the std’s joke, the spiderant, so on... it felt unnecessary. the running gag of lou13 “data sharing” (aka having sex) was uncomfortable to watch.and there were a lot of inconsistencies with the writing, as is usual with the borderlands universe, but:- anu creates a device to replicate siren technology, which is disregarded after episode 1 and never brought back up again- octavio’s idiocy goes beyond being an idiot and quite literally just having no brain for the sake of “humour”, which just comes off as frustrating- characters just stand out in open hallways and get shot and die. its seen as emotional and heartbreaking in game, and incredibly stupid as the player of said game. why the hell did stapleface die from a gunshot to the shoulder? why couldnt anu heal her? who knows, there is absolutely no explanation for it- when the characters are going on a gameshow and stopped by a bouncer, he says “all contestants are accounted for” and then when you get into the area, there is literally. a single person. and its not a sake of others going before said person -- they literally begin the gameshow, starting with that person, a moment later.- rhys calls anu to ask her help to stop tediore from opening the vault, and then, never follows up. literally. he is not seen from again for like five chapters or something ridiculous and when he does return, its for a completely separate reason and its never brought up again.i really liked anu and i resonated with her. although a little irritating at times, i could appreciate her as a character. it was a real breath of fresh air in comparison to the other borderlands characters we typically receive. octavio was... octavio. i did enjoy fran, but the consistent horniess was overdone after about the second episode.a lot of the side characters that were introduced just, dont get brought back in. youre introduced to a big group of characters in the first episode by octavio, and then you barely see any of them for the rest of the game. (justice for diamond danielle) its a waste and once again, one of the biggest complaints i have about borderlands games is wasted potential.now we have an additional cast of characters we’re most likely never going to see again, who were introduced as important to one of our protagonists and then never expanded upon. (the fact we saw a literal talking gun more than any of his closest friends was weird)where loaderbot in the original tales shines, lou13 fails in every. single. category. from personality, to likability, to personal sacrifices for our protagonists... its all lackluster, disappointing, and i could not care less about this character.anyway, we’re never going to see about 99% of those introduction characters again and while its annoying, im fine with it if it means more room for other, already established characters who deserve some more time in the spotlight.going back-- we finally saw katagawa senior! they copied katagawa jr’s model entirely, and put a beard on him. fantastic, great work everyone. take a day off, you guys deserve it. mustve been really difficult to come up with that one, especially considering the art we see for him in the next episode is literally not the same man.if you go into this expecting tales from the borderlands, you’ll be disappointed.if you go into this expecting good writing, you’ll be disappointed.5/10 i just want the telltale writing team back

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is just cringe. One of the main characters is a whiny manchild just expecting the world to serve him riches on a silver platter despite lacking any actual idea or product to warrant it, and another is a whiny nonviolent womanchild who somehow comes across as having less personality. Fran was the only interesting one, because she seemed to be the only taking initiative or control over her own life and having a flawed character dealing with temper problems and a restaurant in decline rather than no character at all. Rhys and Fiona were characters who acted, you know, actively got ♥♥♥♥ done. They had dreams and ambitions they actively pursued by any means. They had charm and wit beyond sarcasm or cringing. Anu and Octavio just talk and whine while the rest of the universe pushes the plot along and drops opportunity in their laps. The story was written by Gearbox rather than Telltale, so I already knew the plot was just going to be loud and obnoxious in a vain attempt at being funny (i.e. traditional Gearbox writing) compared to the first Tales written by Telltale (which WAS actually funny), but I didn't expect this game to be so eye-rollingly bland. Borderlands was never actually funny, but it was at least unique if not intriguing; I would be more into the series if not for the absurd excuses for interruptions of the main story that don't actually contribute to plot progression. New Tales doesn't even have that defense. It's just boring, cringe, and unimaginative.I get writing is hard, but there's really no justification for charging a game like this for $40. Even the $20 sale I bought it for wasn't really worth it. I finished the first episode and immediately decided I didn't want to play any more of it. It just isn't fun. I would continue complaining, but I refuse to put in more effort than New Tales' writers did.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 2 is and may always be my favorite game of all time. I loved Borderlands 1, the original Tales from the Borderlands, even the Pre-Sequel had some very good moments. It just seems like everything Gearbox is doing is structured solely to piss me off. Borderlands 3 had some of the tightest gameplay of any game I've played recently, but that was all undermined by the complete ♥♥♥♥ show that was the story. When I saw that they were making a new Tales from the Borderlands game that was developed completely in house I knew that it was going to consist only of the parts I hate of every modern Borderlands game. Unfortunately, I still decided to give it a shot. Maybe this would be different. Maybe this would be Gearbox's redemption. It was not. In the past week or two I played this game during most of my downtime, getting progressively more and more frustrated the longer it went on. The only characters that I found remotely interesting were the ones you spent maybe 1/9 of the story interacting with.The ONLY good thing that I can say about this absolute dumpster fire is the fact that it ran on my Steam Deck day 1. There were a few minor graphical errors. Stuff not showing up on screens, or certain minor segments being invisible to me, but honestly that might have been doing me a favor. Just don't buy this and if you do, wait until it's like 5 dollars and EVEN then flip a coin to determine whether or not you should really get it. I just don't understand how something like this can get published. Who thought any of this was a good idea? I'm gonna go forget that this ever existed and I hope that nobody else will have to go through what I just did.

I do like how  All parts that involved the Tediore soldier who Vaultlander battled you were funny, or at least not irritating- as well as most of the dialogue from the Tediore guards.At about a halfway point through Episode 4, the game started to really show it's flaws.The main 3 are split up and taken to The card at the beginning of the game warns you about violence and classism but does not warn you about the  This is something that's both not new to the Borderlands universe examples being  What is different is that this is the first thing in the borderlands universe that lasts several minutes on screen to someone who isnt doing it to themselves (correct me if im wrong) and it definitely made me go "yeesh." To someone who isn't used to the borderlands games, I feel like they might want a heads up for that??Anyways, ep5 really felt like they wanted to tell their own story and were sick of having be in the borderlands universe with borderlands lore and borderlands rules. _childDocuments_.review: “NEW” Tales from the Borderlands, is a game that exists.I finished the “NEW” Tales from the Borderlands about fifteen hours ago, that would be 48 hours-ish after its release. And man, I had low expectations but this… creation. This collection of narrative three-week-old soup managed to do worse than I could’ve ever expected.I just wanna preface this by saying a few things: One: I’m painfully aware that a lot of passion went into this game despite my feelings on the matter. I know game development takes a lot of time and work, so part of me still can’t completely hate this game. Even if it’s for the models or art of it.Two: I’m an original fan of Tales. Tales and the Pre-Sequel are the two games that pulled me into the franchise completely. I am a fan of what some consider to be the ‘lesser loved’ games, nevertheless though, ones that have a lot of heart behind them. As well as very loyal and passionate fans for those instalments specifically.All that being said? What the hell did I just play and spend 10 hours of my time witnessing.“NEW” Tales from the Borderlands aims to ride off the original’s niche and well-loved success, only to take a huge dump on everything the original established and created. The usage of any Tales characters is purely to appease fans like myself, and I can’t say I didn’t fall for some of it. I love Rhys, I really do. He’s one of my favourite characters of the series along with Fiona and they manage to shove in every reference they can to the original Tales whenever Rhys  appear. But hey, at least they fixed the ungodly creation of 3’s Rhys model. While the new one may not be perfect—and unfortunately reminds me too much of a certain pilot—it at least fixes a few of the issues I had with his ‘new’ model. Rhys looks aged, but still is identifiable as Rhys himself. He has a few moments too where I recognise him for Tales Rhys, but apart from the physical acting, the similarities stop about there.There are a few “sequences” of dialogue that eerily make Rhys either sound or come off like Jack is still in his head. Forget the whole “I don’t want to ever be like Jack” narrative arc that Rhys experienced and his original trauma. This new Rhys seems to relish in being a pretty rude CEO of Atlas with nothing but money on his mid. The Atlas “slogan” comes way too close to something Jack would come up with, for my own comfort, frankly. While the new VA tries their best to meet the pitchy lovableness of Troy, I can’t say with the deeper undertones that it really doesn’t sell to me that Jack is somehow still in Rhys’ subsystems.And while all these present criticisms have been about Rhys, I think it sets the tone for how the rest of the game plays and presents itself. Cuz the fact that they can’t even get Rhys right, really does reflect on how poorly they pulled off the ‘Tales’ formula as a whole.Within the first five minutes of the game, I could see all the flaws that would repeat for the rest of my playthrough. If it wasn’t characterization, it was the presentation of the intro cards or the music intros.So, to start, the iconic Borderlands splash intros are such a key part of the franchise. But somehow they screw the basics up on that. One or two of the intro cards had the right timing, but most of them were delayed for way too long and didn’t immediately pop in upon character introduction. We’d get them after a full flow of dialogue instead of immediately on meeting the new character and hearing their name.As for the base of the Tales formula itself? The “X will remember that” pop ups were non-existent. Most of the direction over choices felt vague or completely lacking in the iconic Tales interaction department. The ‘Tales’ formula mostly felt like an aesthetic slapped on top of a game that has no real idea how to use many of the features of the original instalments of any Telltales game.The biggest issue though? The characters. Y’know. The thing that’s MEANT TO CARRY A TELLTALES GAME.In under a minute of initial gameplay, it became rapidly clear to me that I wasn’t going to like Anu. Anu is meant to be the character we’re rooting for, but she comes off as clumsy and somehow unintelligent despite the game insisting to us that she’s a scientist. The presentation of the main characters leaves a lot to be desired. Octavio is the only character I can say that I found to be anything semblant of a Borderlands character, Fran following behind that before they utterly destroy her character by Episode 2. But even then, that’s stretching it. They’re just trying WAY too hard to capture the original dynamic of Rhys, Fiona, Vaughn, Sasha and LB, instead of going with something unique and new.I have my gripes elsewhere with Octavio and Fran. Fran’s development is an issue in itself as we go from a very respectable portrayal of a pan individual to 90% of her dialogue being horny or about her libido. Many of the comments making me really really uncomfortable at times as they were borderline inappropriate or just in poor taste. It felt like my choices didn’t matter, or in some cases, offered misleading choices and the characters would come out with something I wasn’t picturing at all. And yes, while the original games did that as well, they were done in good taste and with humour. Here, however? I feel like I’m being punished for not playing the game EXACTLY how the devs want me to. I enjoy a neutral playthrough and yet the game does everything in its power to make you feel guilty for not choosing the “good” and “kind” options. For y’know… A BORDERLANDS GAME WHERE EVERYONE’S IN SOME WAY A BAD GUY. Aka the KEY overarching narrative of many of the prior instalments to the franchise with both Fiona vs Rhys, or how Jack became Jack in the first place.The pacing in itself and presentation of the characters was a painful playthrough, with the only redeeming characters being Lou13 whom I begged to stay on screen longer most of the time. The same with Stapleface.  I’m just saying, it says a lot when I’m more excited to interact with the Tediore ‘Vaultlander’ NPC, than I am to interact with the rest of the game.Good god, I am not looking forward to the implication of a season 2 All in all? I’m probably only going to replay this game to reach 100% completion, or perhaps to see Rhys again since the physical acting was, admittedly, funny. I don’t intend to ever replay it beyond that, unlike the original Tales that I’ve replayed through once every year since it’s completion. I don’t recommend it for Borderlands fans, or Tales fans. Especially original Tales fans.If you’ve never played the original Tales and this is your first taste of Tales as a Borderlands fan? Please don’t let this game give you the wrong impression. It is by no means ANYTHING like the original. I do highly encourage you to pick up and play through the first two episodes of the original game if you can, it really is a game with heart. This “NEW” Tales reeks of cooperate which is pretty ironic considering its narrative. So let the original speak for itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Another in a long line of embarrassments populating this ever-crumbling franchise. Awful writing and characters, painfully unfunny dialogue, and it spits in the face of long-running established game lore and characters. It's a pathetic excuse for a canon game and the people who worked on this should honestly be ashamed of themselves. There are some neat ideas here and there, ones that could be explored more (pacification of enemies over murder, the evolution and brain patterns of psychos, a corporation being unable to kill its targets due to legal loopholes in their own company code) but so far this game has proven itself to be an absolute waste of time and money. Only reason I bought it was because it was 90% off in Pandora's Box collection, and it's the only title I didn't own. Though even then I still would have rather spent my £3.50 on some protein bars or something lol.Another annoying thing about this devolution for the franchise is this game features a content warning. In a Borderlands title. You can really tell the devs have changed hands, huh. Also, Fran is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ creep - if you write a male lead like that nowadays, you're gonna be in deep ♥♥♥♥ and your company ruined, so good job for your drive for equality Gearbox (no I'm not going to use the term 'woke' bc it's silly, but there are definitely double standards present in recent Borderlands titles regarding dialogue, characters and thematic elements).The only things worth praising are the decent sound design, cinematography and environments. Optimisation is fine too, even if for some reason it bricked my computer on start-up and when I tried to stream it. The voice acting is also very good, much like Borderlands 3's; it's just a shame none of the characters are endearing or interesting. The performances are good but they're certainly not fun to listen to. I don't want to blindly hate on this game because clearly some amount of effort was put into its presentation, but this is another example of the exact avenue NOT to take a beloved franchise. Borderlands used to mean so much to me, and I've invested lots of time and energy into these characters and experiences, as have millions of other players. But game after game Gearbox is destroying everything they built over the last decade, and they don't seem to care at all. What is happening?

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even start? New Tales from the Borderlands is a..... game, to say the most. The characters are each.... "unique" in their own ways. Let's start off with Dr. Dhar. She is a gun-hating, science-loving pacifist whose whole spew from the get-go is how much she hates working for a mega weapons manufacturer, yet she still chooses to work there so she can make "devices" that don't hurt but rather help (and as I am half way there, yes, 5.6 hours is only half way). She still hasn't changed in the slightest, even though, as we all know, in the universe of the Borderlands, not all problems can be solved with kindness, yet after certain events unfold in the game, she still likes to spew her insipid no violence rule and apply it to everyone else. Next up is the brother Octavio (yes, another sibling team in the same style as the first game). He's just basic, nothing new or innovative; he's an idiot whose wants fame and sometimes has good ideas during the game. That's it, just basic character design. Now for the worst of the three, the "bruiser" (lack of a better term), Fran, who is just an insult to anyone that falls into these groups, she is a woman who is in a wheelchair, overweight, and pansexual. None of those things, separate or together, would be an issue. Borderlands has always had gay, trans, bi, and so many more people that are a part of the LGBTQ+ community; it's never been an issue until they used Fran's character design as an agenda filler. The whole character is about filling a quota, nothing more, and definitely not to represent anyone. Fran is constantly making sex jokes, being an absolute horny perv with an extreme temper, and who gets off by killing people when she gets too angry. You are constantly reminded how brutal and sexually repressed she is, very off-putting and very disrespectful to those she is meant to "represent." And the worst but best part of EVERY OTHER character is amzing funny or just downright badass. Now with all that out of the way, the actual game play feels awful, and you might be asking what gameplay it's a narrative-driven stroy game. Well, just as in the first, you "control" the characters actions or reactions to save help or otherwise impeed others throught the story, yet the game feels nothing like the first, where you had timed actions to help or save another character in New Tales from Borderlands; it feels like one of those crappy "interactive" ads for bad mobile games. There are some moments in the game that you do feel like you are a part of or helping when you complete the actions, but aside from that, it's very minimal, to say the least, and the story so far is not compelling; it lacks a real badguy. Yes, there is the tediore corp, but they hardly do anything after the first encounter; they feel like a background enemy type, nothing major. last but most definitely least, the time to play this game. Yes, I like taking my time and I enjoy long-form content, but with the 10 hours of this game, the story is so drawn out it could have been later than the first, but not a big deal. But after 10 hours, you fell so drained, and at the time of this review, I was only 5 hours in, but I was falling asleep, and, oh god, the music they used for this is like a bad joke of a music game. The sound track is awful, and thats after comparing it to all of the other Borderlands games. If you somehow read this far, then you know this: I got it for free. Practically, it came with a huge bundle for all the other Borderlands games, so I got a huge discount on anyways, so either wait till its a dollar or go watch someone else play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the overwhelming negative reviews I still wanted to judge it for myself since it is a story-based choice game which I love. I thought most people were disappointed because this one doesn't include the same cast of characters from the previous game, which I would have been fine with so long as it topped or at least matched the quality of the first game. Unfortunately, it did not. New Tales From The Borderlands lacks everything that made the first one great. Amazing side characters that each bring something to the story, an interesting villain, a plot that hooks you from start to finish, comedy that's actually funny, and iconic songs each episode...it was supposed to build upon the strengths its predecessor offered but nope, it's just so mediocre and those minigames/vaultlander battles weren’t helping. With these type of games I like to replay and do an evil/hero route but the choices didn’t feel meaningful so I have no desire to play this game again. Most of the time it was more like picking between a choice that was cringe or less cringey. I pick a dialogue choice that I think will sound cool but the character's delivery on the line was far from it. I get it, one of the main characters is a nerd, but what's the excuse for the other two playable characters? I'm trying to find the pros with this one but the only thing I can think of is the visuals/facial animations.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw some other reviews before playing saying it was bad but wanted to make my own opinion, which ended up being: it’s really bad.The characters are horrible, they are all unlikable, annoying, unfunny try-hards with a strong Netflix vibe (thinking especially of Resident Evil, I expected Anu to start dancing to Dua Lipa at any moment). The only good character was LOU13 and there were maybe some minor interactions with the guards and Brock (the gun) during the later episodes that were amusing, I guess. The obviously motion-captured animations were interesting, though even they felt a bit out of place sometimes.The main story, while the premise is not entirely bad if condensed, is practically non-existing throughout the game, or rather ignored until the final episode. It is constantly being sidetracked with long stretched out boring segments in which nothing happens. After the first 3 or so hours (episode 1) they just about managed to introduce the characters and barely touched the main plot. Then they spend multiple episodes trying to accomplish nothing in particular while just fooling around with unfunny, boring scenes, until they finally focused on the plot in the last episode or so. Which is pathetic compared to what Telltale managed to do in even just their first episode.Then comes the gameplay. If you’re used to Telltale you already know there typically isn’t that much interaction but, in this game (which is not by Telltale to be clear) there is so little interaction that my controller just turned off by itself at one point. This is especially noticeable early on in the game. There is also this weird little mini-game that shows up sometimes in which you fight with collectable figurines but even that lacks any depth. Just smash A until dead, you have to be asleep to take damage and the only thing that differs the characters is the final blow. No voice lines or anything like that.That takes us to my final point before I fall asleep (it’s 3:30), basically none of the previous characters are really there. Marcus narrates between episodes, Rhys shows up at the very beginning for a moment, some characters from other BL games appear as a hologram without dialog for a second and then at the very end Fiona says a word or two. Nobody talks about anything that has happened after the last interactive game (like what happened in the vault or with Sasha) or even the main-line games. It is much less connected to the Borderlands games compared to the original Tales from the Borderlands.TL;DR: Don’t play it, it’s bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Look this isn't the best game in the franchise. Far from it. And it's not helped by the fact naming it "New Tales from the Borderlands" sets up expectations that this game could have done without. The story's okay-ish, not great, but it's serviceable. Three idiots trying to make a name for themselves while getting entangled in a corporate plot. Pretty simple. The main cast is at their core, pretty good, but their interactions with each other can be grinding at times. Especially the humor that is a contention point for this game. It's over the top, absurd, stupid and I personally loved it, but it's absolutely not the universal experience.Some of the secondary characters are tragically underutilised, like Diamond Danielle, Lor, and others, but especially, ESPECIALLY Stapleface. Oh and L0U13 is quite literally useless, for a front cover character. Sad.The graphics are virtually identical to Borderlands 3's, which isn't a bad thing in my opinion. The game looks good.The gameplay is typical Telltale (cutscenes, QTEs), but sadly Gearbox failed to fully replicate what made those games awesome, mainly in the explorable environments, there's simply not enough of them here.The main cast's gameplay gimmicks are ridiculously unimportant. Fran's is just "punch ♥♥♥♥", Anu's goggles are just a mean to make you work a little more to advance in the story, and Octavio's echodex is the most used one, but also paradoxally just as bad as the others: his hacking minigame is unnecessary and ridiculously easy, the wiki feature is useless, and the call feature is literally used only once in the story.Vaultlanders is on the other end of the spectrum, the best idea of this game. It's a huge love letter to nerd culture and I really want a fully fledged standalone Vaultlanders game with fully developed mechanics.Music-wise, the game has few licensed songs but they're nearly all awesome picks.Now my biggest gripe with the game, but also my hope for the future of the franchise: the Lore.Right from the start the game reworks the lore regarding Sirens, and removes the exclusivity of their powers by introducing us to Anu's device that replicates the Siren's abilities. Ouch. Also, how is Atlas, the corporate underdog that gets constantly bullied by other corporations, the one that spawns this thing? This "ultimate" weapon that would be coveted by every company would make more sense if it was made by another of the companies that are far more advanced and powerful. I mean, Dahl, the company of all sins, is right there as the prime candidate.Then towards the end we're introduced to a new thing: "shards", , resulting in an entirely new and interesting character. They are a very pertinent character who poses interesting questions and seems to have pretty clear cut opinions on things like murder, the opposition of good against bad. I like it's input into the often crazy and out of control universe of Borderlands. Sadly, they don't have much screen time and leave to god knows where.  All we know is that it looks like a big deal that they're here, and seems to be teasing things for the future of the franchise's storyline.  Is all of this linked to the big war teased in The Pre-Sequel? So many questions!Overall, the game's issues looks like a reflection of Gearbox itself. It doesn't know how it wants to approach things and ends up stuck in a flood of jokes to hide the problems. You shouldn't pay for this game, it's unnecessary. If you really want to keep up with the lore and story of the franchise, you're better off watching a game movie on YouTube.

_childDocuments_.review: - Graphics and art style are pretty cool. Add a new depth to the Borderlands feel and IMO was nice     - Voice acting all around was pretty solid      - Story was weak, derivative, boring, and nonsensical      - Most of the main characters are extremely unlikable throughout the entire story     - Character development is nearly non existent      - Not a direct sequel to Tales from the Borderlands (not a surprise, but some of the characters from that         make an appearance and they even ruin those     - Story pacing is some of the worst I've seen, manages to start too slow and then get too fast and then         suddenly be too slow again. Never felt like it was moving at a proper speed     - Somehow has less gameplay than these types of games normally do, which is incredible since that's         normally minimal     - Borderlands comedy is here but horribly mixed with the dramatic elements. It never knows if it wants to         be serious or funny, often mixing both in awful ways.I really wanted to like this game coming into it, and I thought the negative reviews couldn't really be right. Sadly it really wasn't great at all, frankly it felt pretty terrible. The story wasn't good, the characters felt awful and were easy to not like, and somehow in a game where I was expecting little gameplay, there was even less than that.I normally really enjoy these types of games, so it was extremely disappointing to feel like I had to drag myself to the finish line for this one. Especially when the ending was absolutely not worth the time put in. Overall I can't recommend this, even to a die hard Borderlands fan, this just seems to be a huge misstep and can definitely be avoided if you've been on the fence about it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... okay. After going in with expectations to be completely disappointed, I wasn't entirely? The only things this game does better than the original Tales from the Borderlands is on the technical side, most of the time the mocap and facial animations are actually really good? But other times they're creepy and some characters have stiff faces. Otherwise, the first Tales is by far the superior game and story.There is some good in this game, there were some actually kinda funny moments and some cool story ideas. There is still a lot of bad in the writing, people have been saying it's about as bad as Borderlands 3's, but I'd say it just has an equal amount of bad, but more spread out with okay or even good stuff in between. The blow is softened a bit, or maybe I've unfortunately become too desensitized to it all haha.The main characters are, also, okay. Anu is probably the least interesting and doesn't change all that much in personality to really make me feel attached to her. I hated Octavio with a passion in the trailers but found out Gearbox used only his most annoying moments in the marketing, in the game he's much more tolerable and I honestly felt very sympathetic towards him near the end. Fran is probably my favorite overall, great acting mixed with their surprisingly good facial animations, but the writers focused way too hard on the "she wants to have sex with everything" joke, she makes horny comments at horribly inappropriate times and makes a lot of serious moments uncomfortable in a failed attempt to be funny or lighten the mood. It clashes with a lot of the choices you're given for her that are very personal and caring actions to the other two characters.The story itself is serviceable, after a very slow first episode things finally start to pick up and seem to go somewhere interesting, but it all starts to go downhill pretty quick and doesn't really feel like it goes anywhere. There are many "convenient" plot-holes and contradictions to force moments that just did not need to happen, and they seem to use up all their seriousness in the second to last episode, reducing the villain, who up to that point was actually really great and genuinely scary, down to an absolute joke and causing the climax to have so little weight to it.While I'd recommend the original Tales to anyone, even people that have no interest in Borderlands, I can't really recommend this game to anyone except for hardcore Borderlands fans and people that absolutely love this genre of game. Ultimately, I don't think this was a tale that needed to be told, but I can't in good conscience say this is a bad game with the overall amount of enjoyment I got from it, it's just okay.

_childDocuments_.review: So, you want to hear a story, eh? Then watch a Let's Play or wait for this to go on sale; unless you really liked the way that Borderlands 3 was written.✪ QTEs were expected in a game like this, but mercy absolutely wasn't. Without adjusting any settings, my fat fingers have slipped up and pressed the wrong prompt several times. Instead of failing the instance immediately, as I would in literally any other game, I was always given a chance to right my wrongs. There are also quite a few settings that let you tweak the QTEs, from their difficulty, to some quality of life features like warnings, interaction time and input method adjustments.✪ This game phenomenally establishes the fact that real, livable worlds exist in the Borderlands universe. Tales from the Borderlands did this to a degree, but we solemnly saw communities and mostly got to see what it was like within corporations. New Tales from the Borderlands, at least in its first half, is full of life beyond the main characters on both sides, and I hope we get more of this down the line.✪ Comedy will always be a subjective topic, with very little being able to constantly tickle the funny bone of every critic. New Tales from the Borderlands got me to laugh just as much as every other entry did, for what it's worth—which isn't much, but when it got me, it got me pretty good.✘ I'm not quite sure what's going on with the writing for these games, or if the writers are even mentally well. Since Borderlands 2, the need to tell cohesive, point A to B stories was shelved in favor of padding the main plot line with meta humor, questionable edge, and building up lovable characters, just to kill them off in ways that don't make much sense according to everything else that's happened. New Tales from the Borderlands is no exception to this, and though it's full of great ideas, their execution often falls short because of some weird, nonsensical writing decisions leading up to them. ✘ I get that this is meant to be a take on Telltale's formula, but I recall actually being able to play the majority of those for a decent amount of time. In New Tales from the Borderlands, I only *actually* got to play for about 2 of the 10 hours in its runtime. We do a *lot* of listening in this game, with the cast standing around in the same room and little going on around them for the vast majority of it. There are times when nothing happens for well over an hour, and the burn is so slow that you feel as if the game is longer than it is. If not for the mini-games that broke up the slog, despite being simplistic button mashes, I don't think I'd be able to make it to the end.✘ At the time of writing, there is no way to skip or fast forward lines of dialogue, which is a pain for folks (like me) who constantly have things come up while they're gaming. There were a couple times I had to quit the game, with each of them making me repeat a dialogue heavy section with no way to speed through what I've already heard or picked up. What's worse about this is that I swore I quit after seeing the autosave icon, but I guess it didn't count for some reason. So after the second time it happened, I just left the game running when I had to step away.✘ Even when taking the kind of game it is into consideration, the surprising lack of standard PC settings is disappointing. The visual sub-menus sole options are; Brightness, Display Mode, Resolution, Vertical Sync, Graphics Quality and Anti-Aliasing—with the last 2 being limited to three settings, each. Graphics Quality can only be set to Low, Medium and High presets, with Anti-Aliasing being either None, FXAA or TAA. I don't usually mind that icky "console port" feeling, but since prior games at least put forth some effort, I can't help but be a little miffed.• There is a joke in Episode 5, involving a door, that was so baffling to me that I actually, for the first time in this entire series, got a headache from frustration. Not only is it a really bad joke that goes on for way too long, but it leads to a situation that I'd very much prefer didn't happen, and could have been avoided if not for Edgy McKilljoy being handed the keyboard for the game's writing.• Despite previous Borderlands games being able to recognize when I was using a PlayStation controller, this game forces all controller users to sport Xbox face buttons. Just about every game I've played in recent memory, including Borderlands 2 and 3, allowed me to have PlayStation face buttons when I felt like using a controller. Kinda weird how this one doesn't.New Tales from the Borderlands is the start of something that I hope gets better, but I'm not sure it can. If you're interested, wait for a sale or watch a Let's Play. If not, you're not missing much. Everything important that happened here will absolutely be recapped in Borderlands 4 anyways.■ Playtime: About 10 hours (+3 hours idle time)■ Visuals: Pretty good, minus the occasional texture pop-ins.■ Story: Not good. Full of great ideas with poor executions. ■ Post-Story Free Roam: No■ Chapter/Mission Select: Yes■ New Game+: Sort of?■ DLC: None at the moment.■ Photo Mode: No■ Optional Content: Collectibles ■ Update Frequency: No updates at the time of writing (one day after launch)■ Accessibility Options: A few; mostly in the form of various Gameplay settings that can make the experience a bit more comfortable.■ Plan to 100%: Sure, why not?

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, I'm easy when it comes to story based games. I really am. All I want is a decent plot, characters that are engaging enough to not actively detract from the game, and either some form of comedy, drama or mystery (or at least a narrative arc that makes you want to finish the story) - this game has neither. The bar is literally on the floor, and New Tales from the Borderlands rolls up against it and whines annoyingly. And then makes you fail a QTE. That's the gist of it. None of the characters are likeable, which isn't necessarily a bad thing; terrible people can be interesting and fun in a fictional setting. Unfortunately, they are also annoying, unsympathetic, unrelatable and possibly worst of all: Unrealistic. Not in the sense that people like them would be unlikely to exist (it's a satirical, semi-realistic setting, after all) but in the sense that human beings don't act, think or speak like this. Moreover, their personalities, traits, and even looks seem to have been ran through a randomizer. It's telling that you can choose different skins for each character that make them look like completely different people, with no running theme - they're just soul-less vehicles for spouting unfunny dialog. Speaking of which, the writing and "jokes" are unfunny at best, offensive at worst. Just... wow. Please don't think "how bad can it be", like I did. Trust the reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: A dull, unintelligent and sad excuse of a Borderlands game. Cringefest at its finestThere might be a high chance you will like this game, if you were a big fan of Borderlands 3 and its writing.If you love the first 2 Borderlands games (+TPS) and/or Tales from the Borderlands then stay away from it.This game is a bad joke.Would this be any other franchise, I would completely ignore this entry. But it is Borderlands. A game known for its brutality, insanity, dark/potty humour, over the top presentation and eccentric, original, crazy characters. It is big and loud.This game on the other hand already shows you a screen at the start, WARNING you about the display of violence and inequality, almost apologizing for even putting any "disturbing" themes into this game. It makes sure that you know it's 2022.At any given moment you will be reminded that "woke" culture is a big thing now and its ideology has to be followed through which shows in choices, that are only varieties of the same answer. If they aren't, on very rare occassions, the game tries to make you feel guilty for making a choice that doesn't fit into the way the developers wanted you to play it.I've seen a robot dab, heard "Slay Queen", "problematic" and "The sauce" way too much and it maskes me feel like I have become too old for this. The main characters are beyond cringe. Intelligence or logic does simply not exist for them, even though one of the characters is supposed to be a scientist. From time to time the game feels more like a 'Dora The Explorer' episode and you want to scream at the screen, because their idiocy will stop them from finding a quick solution or causing the problem in the first place. It seems like the most important thing in the development was to force in jokes every 2 minutes, just for the sake of it. The timing was off every single time and ruined multiple, dare I say, every single scene. Not a single soldier felt like a threat and they all seemed to be in relationships with each other. For example telling each other "I love you" in tense scenes which destroyed the atmosphere. Completely misplaced. Not just once - it was a running gag.Halfway through the game the jokes become almost only of the sexual kind. They probably ran out of bad jokes, so they decided to make even worse ones.The music choices feel like those of an average teenager that just hit puberty and experiences their first existential crisis.The messages, mostly ethical and political, feel forced and pushed onto you. Friendship is magic is the motto and EVERY PROBLEM can be solved by a hug OR teamwork. Yes, you heard right. Friendship is the way to success. Otherwise you get punished by scenes that would end up in the characters not working together and having a "bad" outcome". The game does not warn you about this, and you have no idea which choice is meaningful and which one gets you closer to your "found family", as the game calls it.It physically hurt me to play through scenes that had such an obvious solution to it, yet the characters were completely oblivious, naive and unexperienced to realize the situation they are in. The second-hand embarrassment was over the charts. What could've almost been a parody, missed that exit and tortures the player with nonsense and stretched out conversations of pure stupidity.One of the characters danced out of cover in an extremely dangerous situation, barely dodging a lethal attack at the last moment, because he heard music. Twice. The danger and seriousness of the situation were tranformed into a joke. This game spits on the previous games and reimagines it for the target audience of Netflix writing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sounds like a fine enough story on paper, but the writing and characters really just sours the entire experience. Like, it's really just abysmal at times, especially in the final episode. Really, there's a lot wrong with it, but it can be seen primarily in the three main characters.Anu is the main character of this game. It's not a three way split between the three, like how the main characters in Tales 1 were both Rhys AND Fiona. Anu is the clear standout of the group, as we follow her more thoroughly. She's an anxiety ridden character who seems to have been written by someone who doesn't have anxiety, but thinks, "Ah, she's quirky, you see? Look at her have an anxiety attack. Are you laughing at how quirky anxiety is?" Aside from that, she's bland. She's somewhat believably anxious at times but it always feels hollow at best and forced at worse. She has a semi touching story about learning to not be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but it's very bare bones.Fran is the best of the main three. She fits the setting of the game (Borderlands) pretty decently. She's rage filled, but trying to control her anger, and really horny. Like, REALLY horny. All of these are things are what I come to expect from Borderlands, and her attitude, ego, and overall bombastic character plays well off the stupidity of Octavio, and whatever Anu is doing. All she wants is to beat up the antagonist, it's not overly preachy or anything, she just wants to punch a ♥♥♥♥♥.Octavio is just the worst. This franchise has had some stinky characters, but man, he's written like one person in the office looked at a reddit meme about how millennials are all obsessed with tacos and made that his entire personality. He's seemingly supposed to be the haha funny guy of the group, but he's just annoying.Genuinely the best character in the game is the face of the game, LOU13. His cold responses to things can be genuinely funny at times, and he seems more grounded than the three main characters with his trying to find a place in the world arc. I can see why they shoved him on the box art.Side characters and even main characters have their moments where I'd chuckle a bit, but then it's right back to business as usual.The humor is bad, and this story relies on it too much. Even when a moment is supposed to be serious or somber, they throw some haha quirkiness into it. Episode 5 is filled to the brim with moments where you're just sitting there wondering what is even going on. Which is REALLY sad because the ending of episode 4 is when they actually had me interested in it. Only to go back to bad jokes and tone deaf interruptions to the current situation they're in. Tales 1 had a few moments like that, but they were very few and far between and the humor felt better paced 9 times out of 10. Don't play this game. I would recommend just watching a run on Youtube or just reading a Wiki page if you really want to know what happens. I played through it twice and got the good ending both times, and both times I just sat back and groaned more often than not.To this game's credit, it's visually really well done. The camera work, models, animations, lighting and environments all look like direct upgrades from Borderlands 3.
