_childDocuments_.review: So, yeah. The entire point of this lengthy introduction is to make it obvious that I am invested in the Borderland’s universe and its characters. Especially the characters. Speaking of whichThe ones from the NewTales are embarrassing. The team’s bruiser moves inches per hour, has no shield, is extraordinarily irritating. She is exactly the kind of a character that would have died within the first two minutes of any respectable Borderlands game right after the intro and yet, in NewTales, everyone including the villains becomes inexplicably scared the moment she frowns. Well okay, the Borderlands’ universe is slowly running out of the evil supercorps and this time around the main antagonist is Tediore, so maybe they would be scared. Nonetheless.Coming back to said character. Despite having no long range weapons, shields, moving at a snail pace, and generally having no positive traits whatsoever, she constantly manages to mow down legions of enemy soldiers, regardless of the fact how mind-numbingly ridiculous it may look. Unless the plot needs her to be disarmed and confined by the two of exactly same grunts she’d been obliterating by the dozen  few minutes earlier. Then there’s a rebellious woman who is a top-tier scientist, the brain of our team, a pacifist to the point of releasing the caged animals on a – let me make a point here – space station. Finally, there’s her brother, a butt of every joke and the punching bag for the rest of the crew. Right behind the playable characters, there’s an assassin droid. Who, despite being an obvious clone of every previous ‘you are being rescued, please don’t resist’ zero-empathy deadpan sink, had a potential to be an interesting character. He becomes absolutely bothersome quite soon and as if that was not enough on its own, remains so useless throughout the entire campaign that the plot makes him vanish and then reappear on a whim, without providing any good reason for it.    And, since I’ve already mentioned the story, there is absolutely no reason for the NewTales to exist in the first place. While this is a highly subjective opinion, I would like to assume the selling point of a Tales’ sequel would be to explain the Fiona’s fate. No such thing happens here. Furthermore, hardly any characters from the main games appear in NewTales, and even if they do, it’s a split-second cameo. Remember how the first Tales had Zero, Jack or that very meaningful scene with Scooter? There are moments when this game would have been made infinitely more enjoyable by letting one of the old characters on the stage. Yet, the authors decided against it. Furthermore, the entire script feels as if written by an AI or someone with absolutely no understanding of either Borderlands lore or sci-fi world-building in general.  The authors seem to know the components of a narrative but could neither properly write nor join them together. The pacing for the most part is horrendous, there is a common disregard for any logic, and the dialogues are painful to listen to.  The chemistry between the main trio is INSUFFERABLE. The authors aim for playful banter but lack the skill in writing, which results in most of the dialogues between the protagonists feeling mean-spirited or plain spiteful.At least, unlike the movie, they’ve kept Marcus as a narrator. Chapter four is maybe not exactly good by the standards of gaming in general but in comparison with what happened up to that point, it actually makes an unexpected amount of sense and reaches some character development. And then there’s chapter five. And that, somewhere 10 hours plus in, is where this game finally starts making sense. Even a joke or two manages to land, some actually heartfelt events  take place, there is a successful callback to previous events and finally some proper stakes are introduced. There are scenes that made me want Anu and the crew to be part of Borderlands canon. The problem is, without the context of the previous chapters it’s all completely worthless, and the earlier story is plain not worth going through just to witness the final hour or two. New Tales matured like a slice of rotting pizza with pineapple and anchovies in times of plague, warfare and anguished starvation. You’re still probably going to need some sizable servings of liquor to numb your common sense down or a group of friends doing the MST3K somewhere in the background. Preferably both. But let’s face it. After Borderlands movie and the recent narration in the cinema in general, NewTales have grown to become almost barely palatable if you get it by mistake while buying Pandora pack.Still, even if you get this one for free, there is one currency simply not worth spending here: your time. It is a demanding task to actually find a story that is told with less skill or style than NewTales, and consequently if you are not a hardcore fan of Borderlands’ lore you can absolutely skip it. And if you are such a fan, you should avoid NewTales like a plague. In the endYou’ve already spent more time than you should with NewTales just by reading this piece, so as alwaysI swear, I’m not a particularly proud person but I feel this review is written better than the game, and that means something.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this by saying I think the title of this game does it some harm in terms of what to expect from it. It's neither a sequel to Tales From the Borderlands really or the next incarnation of Borderlands as a looter shooter RPG. What it is is the casual gaming equivalent of a DLC story centered on people who exist on the sidelines within the universe. More so than the original Tales, as that had more of a tighter correlation with the main stories of Borderlands. But such is marketing, and it technically lives up to its title.Did I laugh at this game? Not really. It got a few chuckles out of me. Nothing that wasn't more of a curt laugh. But I don't mind that. I'm happy to be simply amused. Other people might find it annoying. The story and characters, on the other hand, definitely grew on me over time. Episode 1 was just okay. I was pretty invested in the side characters, things were better written than I anticipated, and it was decently paced. Episode 2 was...ehhh. It really doesn't pick up until toward the end. By the beginning of the third ep, however, something just clicked about these characters and their interactions. I was invested from that point on until the end of the game. It was more like reading a book or watching a series, where it takes time to get to know the characters and their motives and see how it affects the bigger picture. Not really a flaw in my opinion, just slower than maybe anticipated. Some of the tense beats and moments could have stood to be higher and tenser. That unfortunately works against the game at parts. It's not much of an issue in the later episodes. But it's a bit too persistent in the early parts. 'That could have been done better or cooler' crossed my mind more than it should have. Also, I think it should have ditched the episodes entirely and told one streamlined story to make it more even, as it didn't really feel like the episodes were divided all that much. But that might not bug some people as much as it did me.The high points of the story I found really high, though, and pretty emotional and often solid from a strictly human standpoint. They're engaging in the right way. Also kudos to this game for really hammering in the point of dynamic storytelling, much more than the original Tales did. People in my household played the game simultaneously and got wildly different scenarios and endings. That's definitely a positive for me.  I don't really recommend this if you only like the main Borderlands games and don't care too much for the lore of the universe or whatnot. I maybe recommend it to fans of the original Tales wanting to see storytelling more in that vein, but probably at a discount. And for casual gamers who like character-driven stuff and don't mind a little cringe humor mixed in, sure, go for it. It's not mind-blowing, and it won't change your life and enlighten you, but it has some occasional solid stuff and can be measured by its own merits. Again, there are some moments that might have been done better, or better explained and/or shown. But the overall impact is still there. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR (YES THIS REVIEW GOT WAY TOO LONG IM SORRY)gameplay/looks = good/ enjoyablestory/ Writing/ Characters = filled with cliché boring jokes that never land, terrible writing, unlikeable superficial predictible annoying characters, comedic relief every two seconds (although you needed relief from the comedic relief), no suspense or drama at all, you basically want all the protagonists to just shut up, MIND NUMBINGDisclamer: This will be in no way a comprehensive review, im just going by my own feelings I have right now after just finishing the game. I have never played a "tales" type game and after this I don´t think i ever will again.Let´s start with what i liked about the game though:GRAPHICS/ATMOSPHERE/PERFORMANCE/GAMEPLAYI think the game looks great. I´ve always been a huge fan of the comic style look Borderlands had since I started playing it in 2012 on my Dads account. The atmosphere is great as well I think every location looks and feels nice and I don´t really have any complains about that at all, the music in most parts is nice too (i did not quite like it in the 3 or 4 "montage" scenes you had in the game (hopefully you know what I mean) but I did not mind it as much as other things). I have a decentily up to date system so the game ran great at 144fps the whole time with only like one or two hiccups or instinces of tearing or whatever i can´t even remember. Since this was my first experience with a "Choose your own adventure" type game i did not have anything to compare the gameplay to but it was still enjoyable at most parts. The QTE events for the most part were alright although a bit too easy sometimes (I played on normal difficulty) The dialogue choices for the most part felt good with great variety in the availabe answers and making you feel like it really mattered what you said to another character. Only small complaint i would issue with this would be the joke answers, which I did not like at all. For example giving Ock the chance to say "I like Tacos" what felt like everywhere. This was easy to ignore though since you still had three different answers left (duh) so I did not mind it as much and did not want to include it in my criticism.Sadly that is but all of the positive things i can say about this game.ALL OF THE REST (SPOILERS)This part will be a mish mash of all the things I just want to get off my chest so please bear with me and try to piece together this mess.Lets start with the CHARACTERS, our main Protagonists could be very simply be broken down like this:Octavio = oh he´s really stupid that´s why he´s funny he always does the wrong decision you guys he´s so goofyAnu = Oh my god she has anxiety what a pity but she is so good at self reflection (at the end)Fran = guys did you know the fat lady in the wheelchair can be horny too (oh and she is very angry)L0U13 = robot (he analyses things not very human like and breaks every emotion down even for the dumbest player)And sadly there really is nothing more to them, the game tries to get into a deeper connection to the characters by putting a broad message out that is applyable to the real world (like Anu with self reflection, Fran with anger management etc.) but all these messages are so "on the nose" in every case that I could not help but not take it serious because it was always (at the big reveal of the message) like: DUH! no ♥♥♥♥ it would help to manage your anger or yeah sure time heals all wounds we can all agree with that, but a Borderlands game is simply not the place I want to have my mind changed. I know this is a story based game and therefore it has to rely on those points instead of gameplay. So basically it just boils down to which character can you personally really relate to, since i could not relate (or frankly didnt like) anyone the characters and all of their dialogue was just boring and annoying to me and left me wondering what stupid crap they are gonna say next with even more disappointment when they actually say it.Next lets get to the WRITING and or STORY TELLING and my god. (Disclamer: I dont know how many versions of this story or how many different endings exist if any at all so im going off the story and ending i played as if that is everyones experience)I am guessing no one really expects a Borderlands game (after Borderlands 3) to have somewhat decent writing but this really takes the cake. Every. Single. Line. Is a terrible joke that NEVER lands because it is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ predictable that not even a first grader could laugh about it. Every time the tiniest smidge of suspense or action is build up, it is completely destroyed by some dumbass thing Ock had to say or some stupid dance he had to break out (YES HE DABS AND MILLIE ROCKS IN THIS GAME IN 2022) or Fran just being mindnumbingly horny and angry or L0U13 breaking down  the situation in "robot terms" or Anu having another panic/ anxiety attack OR my personal favourite: Tediore soldiers being literal 10 IQ degenerates making dumb and dumber jokes by every minute and not seeming to get anything right EVER (it is obvious they are treated like clone troopers in the Star Wars franchise even mentioning that they never hit anything but it just doesnt work here at all because of the 4th wall being broken so often). Look i know the Borderlands serious is known for its "silliness" or not taking itself very serious but this is just too much. Let me give an example: Handsome Jack. He, mostly, when he communicates with you in the game says some outlandish ♥♥♥♥ basically just "flexing" on the player or straight up insulting you. BUT in contrast to all of the characters in this game, he has moments of actual suspense and villainy and just overall deepness to his character that makes you go: "holy hell this guy is a real ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥". For example the scene after defeating Bunker and freeing Angel when he kills Roland. The whole scene is just beautifully terrifying and TAKEN SERIOUSLY and only AFTER the scene is over he goes back to being the guy we know over the ECHO just insulting and playing with the protagonists. This game just does not have that at all. All the dramatic or action scenes are just constantly interrupted by some dumb jokes or dances that just make you cringe every single time without fail. Let me give an example as well. In the final fight with Susan when she merged with the shards. Ock keeps on calling the Tediore IT service for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason and just dancing and goofing all over the place, while being shot at by Susan although Fran is just hovering next to her at all times. It just never feels like the characters are ever in real danger because there isn´t a single scene i can remember in the entire game that was taken seriously 100%. And i know it is supposed to feel this way since the story focuses on them being "losers" but it just does not work at all since all the jokes are just regurgitated BS that frankly, I dont see anyone finding funny even in the slightest. Also in that end scene i described Susan gets pushed into the beam device or whatever by Frans wheelchair alone without any help. SO: what you are telling me is that the combination of the Shards, THE MOST POWERFUL AND RARE OBJECTS IN THE KNOWN UNIVERSE (as Susan reiterates so many times), an alien source of power, making the merged vessel actually invincible and capable of death rays desintigrating people with a single hit....got overwhelmed buy an overweight ladys hovering wheelchair. I could really go into more detail with examples and such why i didnt enjoy the game at all but im running out of space. In conclusion: If you have too much money and want to know where Borderlands 4 could possibly start at, play this game and be disappointed. For everyone else i truly would never recommend this game, save yourself the money and the hope a good Borderlands game will come out again some day. Thanks for reading if you got this far.+2/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, some of things were fun and made me laugh my ass off, but as a casual fan of Borderlands since playing the original Borderlands on the PS3, can't recommend. This game doesn't hold any candle to the original Tales From The Borderlands. TWO MAIN REASONS WHYThis game doe not take place on Pandora, instead it takes place on Promethea in a very much thriving city despite the planet becoming under siege. Its not really Borderlands if its not taking place at the edge of civilization. Pandora : wild west / mad max , Promethea : Los Angeles / New York. Yeah, the reoccurring theme of big corporations screwing over the common man is in this game, so I will give it credit for that. It just doesn't have that Borderlands feel. I really do not like Dr. Dhar. She is a pacifist scientist preaching about making the world a better place free from violence, but violence is often glorified and accepted in this universe to a logical conclusion. She spent much of the game believing that her gun, sorry I mean her device, can change the world. However, her approach to things have often led her to just pissing people off or her being taken advantaged of. She is a scientist, but she has no street smarts or people skills, In effect, she is not actually smart or considerate as she likes to believe. Near the end when she addresses this issue, it doesn't feel like she actually learned a thing. Honestly, the game would be ten times better if it just stuck with and focused on Octavio and Fran. They had a pretty good dynamic going on, and their own personal character arcs were more intriguing and fulfilling than Anu's. All of the game's best moments came from these two characters, like I was laughing my ass off to some of those scenes. Honestly, just watch those clips on Youtube and it will be a far better experience than actually playing the game. Oh, And the way they bastardized Rhys in this game is just unacceptable. It feels like his own personal story from the original was thrown in the trash. Just disgusting. Friendly reminder that Borderlands peaked and died with Handsome Jack. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of the Borderlands Series, I cannot in good conscience recommend this title to anyone. Let me explain why.First off the Motion Capture. How could A Triple A company like Gearbox say the mo-cap for Octavia was fine? There were times I sat there stunned thinking GearBox went out of its way to make fun of Children/Adults with Downs Syndrome, or even people with buck teeth. Yes, the animation for him was that bad.While I am at it, how can you have a game with trigger warnings like "inequality" and "emotional distress" but then have a character like staple face which makes fun of people with mental health issues? Oh right, that character is classified "a psycho" so that is fine for sliding under the wire. No, I am not offended by it, not even in the least. I just think if a game is going to pander to the thin skins then they need to go all in on it.Lastly, the game play. I am baffled at how this can be a QTE like game; but you are given very little time to complete actions, yet when you have a choice of actions which are (A) and (B) the game gives you two minutes to decide. Also this is the first game I ever saw that gives you a QTE Mini Game with an option to have the game do it for you, not to mention that most of the time, it does not matter if you press the buttons to do an action as the game will pretend you did.Oh, and if you are wondering if this ties into the Older Original Tales from the Borderlands, it sure does. No, not because of Rhys as his whole thing was retconned in Borderlands 3. No, at the very end of the game you get a 5 second reference.Save your money and pass on this game then go to play Borderlands 2, maybe even three with the handsome jackpot DLC, you will have way more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm partway through Episode 2 and I am just so done; I'm gonna need a stiff drink and probably something requiring a needle to get through the rest of it. This has to be one of the most poorly paced, poorly written, poorly acted – poorly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ EVERYTHING – stories I've ever experienced. Cringe-worthy dialogue punctuated with awkward pauses (completely sandbagging what passes for jokes in this game); scenes that drag on and on yet still somehow end abruptly; pacing so languorous it's practically nonexistent; and actors whose only direction seemingly was to act silly and shout their lines. (If they'd been properly directed, someone might have told Anu's actress to dial back on the weird and wild gesticulating she is always doing, and Octavio's actor to lower the volume). Don't even get me started on the meandering plot. Right when it seems the characters are finally given a purpose and a goal to achieve, the game cuts immediately to a montage of our heroes... sitting around... doing nothing... waiting for... something. Like I said, the pacing is practically nonexistent. Individual scenes feel like they were written in a vacuum and then mushed together at the last minute; no flow, no through line, no oversight by a head writer or director.Nothing that made the first Tales so brilliant and beloved is present and accounted for here (not even the slick episode intros with the kickass licensed music). It's bland, it's incompetent, it's lazy. Avoid this abortion at all costs and play the first game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game is suffering, and I'm only playing it for the lore. I'm a Star Wars fan; I watched the Acolyte to see the lore; I’m used to this suffering. The three main characters are poorly written. The wheelchair lady, in my opinion, is the only redeemable if at that because of her desperation for love being mentioned in the wrong moments; also her past is kind of cool - would be a good vault hunter at the least. All of the characters are all awkward and seem to have more idle motions than necessary. I cringe at these pauses and in-between moments because of their execution. There personalities are also just generally atrocious. There are inconsistencies in the story; . The characters do things that are unnatural for a person for the purposes of progressing the story. Things that borderlands citizens wouldn't do, let alone people in the real world; . I feel like people would also show more effort in resisting and actively attacking someone rather than wait to react after they've been trapped or arrested. Several times, the characters just wait for the bad guy to trap them and then resist being trapped once they're in a cage, and even then, they resist poorly. There are relationships between characters to achieve... the good ending? Haven't gotten there yet so I'm not sure of the relevance. Regardless, the character development per each person seems forced to achieve the overall sync between them all. That is, I don't think someone who is prone to be angry all the time would choose peace and sympathy over revenge so suddenly at any given point. It's something that's recognized and thought about before being accepted and ready for such a change. There are some animations that are cut. I've noticed you see the camera up close to the character's face and at different angles while they're talking, but they're animated in a way so they're not talking to anyone in particular so they're just talking aloud in a room by themselves (they're talking on the phone); I understand the cost cutting and saving money by not animating people, but it's just unnatural in the execution; throw a .gif on a tv screen and look at it occasionally. They also have someone describe the action instead of showing it; . In episode 5, there seems to be a swap of character models. They used the finalized design of a guard that you see throughout the entire game, and during a walk with the characters near the end of the game, they used a different design that's actually interchanged during the cut scene. Or someone is wading through a water substance at waist level, only to be walking on top after a cut scene. There are two minigames that I've found. Fighting with Amiibos by smacking them until someone wins, but it's turn based so one person hits, then you have the option to dodge the incoming attack from the NPC. It's more time consuming than actually fun. I will admit the character you face to get some of the Skylander figures has a certain comedic aspect but it borders on cringe. The type of super nerd that would wait outside of a building for a new figure he preordered months ago. It has an appeal for some, so it isn't all that bad. The second minigame is "hacking." Standard minigame for a visual novel: mash buttons. My gripe is with the second part of this minigame, where you have to wait for numbers to appear. When it rotates through the numbers 0 through 9, you typically press the button halfway between two numbers, to get the second number that you wanted. In this minigame, you need to push the button when it's clearly on the number before the one you want. It's mostly annoying than anything else. The humor is... awful. 90% of the jokes they made have been bad on setup, delivery, and follow through. There are only three jokes, thus far, I've actually chuckled at.   . The humor would hit maybe 20 year ago but nowadays it falls short. I will admit that there are some good things though. I think the big bad villain is cool; how they carry themselves, their plan for domination, and their imperfections being seen.  I also like a few of the side characters, like the psycho girl seen occasionally (Stapleface), the robot posing as the game's thumbnail (Lou13), and the robot assistant you see at the beginning of the game (TIMM-E). In a normal Borderlands game, I would love these characters; they're cute, funny, and annoying in their unique ways. I got this game from probably the Handsome Jack bundle where you get every single borderlands game and DLC for cheap. That’s the only time I would buy this game - when you can't remove it from the cart.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a massive Borderlands fan and this game is, sadly, completely and utterly terrible. The story's themes feel crammed into the final episode, the characters are unevenly written and make bizarre choices, the game design makes pivotal choices feel unclear leading to unsatisfying endings, and the new lore is poorly executed. There are a few laughs, but this was the first Borderlands game I have ever wished I hadn't bought. It brings me no pleasure to say this game is bad because I know a lot of work goes into making games and I love this franchise. Still, the game just doesn't land in any way and is one of the biggest gaming disappointments I have had.If I had to give it a score, I'd give it a 2/10 and only for the first episode, which I found to be an intriguing and enjoyable start. I also think Rhys was written well in his limited appearances, and the supporting cast is endearing but don't have enough time in the game. I really don't want to be harsh, but there's just nothing else to recommend here. The game is entirely story, after all, and sadly the story here is one of the worst in the series. Even without comparing it to the original Tales, this game fails entirely. With that said, if you're craving a Borderlands story, you should just play the original Tales.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the characters. There are three main characters you control: Fran, Octavio and Anu. Anu is by far the most interesting character, she's socially awkward with a lot of movements/gestures that show how she's feeling and has an actual moral compass, but most importantly she has a no kill rule (kinda) which makes her more interesting. Octavio is very bland. He's a stereotypical happy go lucky guy who cares about his image too much and is a coward, what makes it worse is that he has nothing else to go with it. Unlike Anu he has no moral compass, he has little to no affection to those around him and is genuinely easy to forget. Fran is much worse. Fran is much like Octavio in that she's bland and has no moral compass. She's a fat angry frozen yogurt worker who instead of having a character just tends to be comedic relief as well as a "beat 'em up" type character, she's got an angry side and a "trying not to be angry side" which honestly was a good dynamic except it was thrown to the wind in the second chapter. The story itself is bland as well. Since the characters aren't vault hunter material the story has to adapt by dumbing down literally everything else around it. Enemies have no braincells and instead of having serious talks/action scenes the story opts for pure comedic relief. I despise how the vault monster was slow and done absolutely nothing. The characters could stand there talking, screaming even without the monster batting an eye. The ONLY redeemable thing I see in this game is the side characters, Louise is a good comedic relief character with satisfying predictability and good design, Rhys was especially good here since he had a more stable background (the only character with one at all tbh) and Stapleface was cool to see. It sucks to see how the tales from the borderlands fell off, the first one was really good for what it was. The characters in that game were so much better, the story was good and the scenery was great. TLDR: This game is like the first one, but with bland characters, no story, no pleasing visuals and is just 99% family guy comedic relief with only like three good characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so... let me start this review out by saying that I LOVE the Borderlands franchise and I've been a fan of these games since I was twelve. I grew up with these titles and I remember how in love I was with Tales From The Borderlands way back in 2016.That being said, I went into New Tales From The Borderlands with a completely open mind, having recently finished Borderlands 3 (and finding its story okay) and other titles from the series. I ignored the negative reviews, watched no commentary videos on the game, read nothing about the plot or premise, and decided to just give New Tales a genuine, positive try!And honestly? I found the game alright during and after the first two episodes. Nothing groundbreaking, but nothing awful either. Then, episodes three and four had me REALLY intrigued and hooked with episode 4 probably being the best of them all, despite some glaring plot holes and major inconsistencies with the Borderlands universe.In fact, let me note some things I DID like about the game. I think Anu is a well written character. I liked her a lot, found her funny (if a bit annoying at times) and she was definitely my favorite protagonist of all 3. I also liked the execution of quick time events, with a prompt coming on screen before every one of them helping you to get ready. I liked that Rhys came back (with his personality quite botched and contradicting his development in the old Tales, but still very much Rhys-y), and I loved Vaultlanders!But then episode 5 came to erase everything I liked about New Tales. Oh,..my...GOD. Episode 5 was a snoozefest. A complete, total snoozefest with no redeeming qualities. I was bored out of my mind during this game's grand finale. The pacing was terrible. There was TOO MUCH COMEDY at ALL the wrong moments. There was no tension, no buildup, no thrill, no intrigue or hope. It was just a hollow shell of a story hemorrhaging horrible, out of touch jokes at every step. The ending was not satisfying, yet it was still weirdly impressive because of how overdone yet completely bland it was. I was truly willing to give this game a thumbs up BEFORE I finished it. The final episode took every nitpick that I had about the previous episodes and amplified it to the maximum. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Telltale Games for ten years now. Like many who probably played this game, I am a HUGE fan of the original Tales from the Borderlands. Just because this game has VERY LITTLE in common with Tales 1, doesn't mean it's a bad game. In fact, I enjoyed this second game quite a lot! The three main characters all have VERY distinct and fun personalities (Although I can definitely see Fran's excessive horniness becoming grading for some players.) L0U13 is a GEM in this game, and the dynamics and much more personal stakes in this story make it stand out distinctively from every other Borderlands story. While some of the potty humor from BL3 does popup in this game, I didn't find it distracting at all, save for the final fight in Episode 5 that felt just a bit too dragged out. In addition to that, the only real con I had is how underutilized the side characters in this game are. In episode 1, there are almost half a dozen characters you get to meet who are REALLY cool, but with the exception of like two of them, the rest don't really show up for the majority of the story. It's rather disappointing, but the main cast is still REALLY strong to carry this game on their own. Anu was absolutely my favorite!I haven't seen all 5 of this game's endings, but the amount of different characters who can live or die in this game makes the game open for TONS of replayability. Even if you don't care about these new characters and only wanted to see more of Rhys and Fiona, PLEASE just try and give these new characters a chance. I truly think this game has some very big implications for the rest of the Borderlands franchise!Final score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is a huge waste of time, calling it a game is a bit generous.DO NOT pick it up on sale. Don't even play it if it was free. That is ALL you really need to know. Just watch a Lets Play if you really need to experience this.DO NOT PLAY.But if you are like me and is a glutton for punishment you can continue reading this review.This "game" feels like it was made as a torture method to force confessions out of you. The review will contain spoilers, but who cares?So who was this game written for? Is it satire? A parody? None of the "jokes" connect at all, it is never funny, emotional or convey a message of any kind. The characters are so uncanny, their facial animations feel broken because their upper lip seems to be non-existent on the majority of characters making them look like automatronics. Was this written by an AI? Aliens who made an attempt to write how they think humans behave? Whenever a character smiles their mouth move in a unnatural way. At points the lip-sync is completely off.The Quick-Time Events are so oddly placed. Calling it a "Quick" time event is wrong, it's a slow time event. You can literally never fail it. Even if you let the timer run out, it will just ignore it and play a slightly clumsy animation anyway and the end result is the same. Only a few times does a failure end in a actual fail-state and you have to replay that short section.The QTE Promts show up waaaay too early and since the timer is 5 seconds to react the whole game grinds to a halt and it feels so weird, like you hit the pause menu in the middle of an event and then resume it. Everyone just stands there waiting for you. Doesn't matter how long you time you take, the end result is the same. Everyone freezes.There is hardly even any type of moving around and exploring, there hardly is any game-play. It could just be a constant moving "movie" with a few dialogue options really. Not that you get to pick the dialogue options that often anyway.The Vaultlanders mini-game is impossible to lose. All you do is mash the attack button during your turn, the dodge the opponents attacks by moving the stick on your controller in any direct the game tells you to, and you have such a long time to react. It takes no skill, there's no stakes and why it was even included is beyond me. It adds nothing, it doesn't feel rewarding either. You can't lose. All of the so called "game-play" mechanics are made in such a way you really can't lose. Remove them from the game and just keep the dialogue options and nothing would be lost.So who is the target audience with this writing and game-play? And they do nothing.The game was so annoying, and it just drags on and on and on, Kinda like this review. So often I just want the characters to shut up, nothing they say matters. It's a constant failed joke and you're sitting there waiting for a laugh track to kick in, because it pauses constantly like in a sitcom waiting for the audience to react.Within the first minutes of the game, a character does an accent and one of the main-characters reacts to it and calls it a "problematic accent" However the game contradict itself later on by having other main-characters and playable characters do various different accents, and actually make a mockery out of them in a mean-spirited way. So how is that okay? You immediately say "problematic accents are bad" only to later do them yourself and say "isn't that funny? That's a funny accent and mocking it so funny though!"Major mixed signals there. Is it 'problematic' or not? Or are only some characters allowed to mock others? What is the message here?If Borderlands 4 will be written in the same style then I am almost certain it will be the last Borderlands game we will ever get. I hope the writing will be more in line with Borderlands 1 and 2, Hell even Borderlands 3 wasn't that bad. It had a few meh moments in the writing but all in all I had no real issues with it in Borderlands 3.Last Warning.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant when I saw the negative rating of this game; having played the first Telltale Borderlands, I wondered why the new game gained a low rating. I genuinely enjoyed this one! And to be clear, I never played any Borderlands original games, Only the Telltale one, so I won't compare it to the original game. You are introduced to three characters:The story is about a scientist, Anu, who creates a device that can eliminate evils instead of killing them; she introduces it to her boss, who is displeased by it and fires her. She left Atlas and returned to her brother, who lives in Promethea, only to find him in Fran's broken frogurt shop. The three of them decided to work together and fight against Tediore. There were many funny moments; I laughed and enjoyed the game. The quick time events were quite tricky, and I'm glad there is an option to stop the timer so you can enjoy the game with no stress from pressing random buttons.  Most of the gameplay is about choices and a couple of scenes where you explore and pick up items or search for things. The action is all during the cutscenes and QTE. The artwork is exquisite; I liked the areas and characters so much; the character's personalities and development are great; you need to work on the relationships between them to get various endings, five in total. The total of 'skateboard' determines the team's bond, and each of the two characters' responses to each other determines their ending and reaction to each other. Choose wisely. You can always go back to the main menu and choose the episode you want to restart and change your choices; each episode has multiple chapters to start from.Pros:+Great artwork.+Interesting story.+Good voiceovers.+Good soundtracks.+Good character animation.+Lots of funny moments.+Funny Tediore guards.+Brock+Fighting Mini game.+Collectables. +Multiple endings (Depends on character's relationships and team score)Cons:-Too many sexual references from Fran.-If you restart a chapter, you can't skip the scenes.-No manual save.I'd start the game with Octavio instead of Anu. I wouldn't say I liked her very much, and her awkwardness doesn't represent the game well in the first half-hour. I didn't like the constant sexual references from Fran; I like her, but not when she acts weird. If you enjoy narrative games, give it a go; it is a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Fine narrative, characters, and writing, sucky gameplay, awful finale, great epilogue (probably depending on the ending you get).In true telltale fashion, by purchasing this game, you are essentially paying 40+ dollars for a movie with a couple button presses thrown in there for good measure.That being said, you could do a lot worse than this.CHAPTER 1:Everyone had their doubts from the minimal (and abysmal) marketing for this game, and after giving the first chapter a fair shake, this is showing some potential. In my opinion, this is the best that the borderlands writing has been since bl2, not that the bar has been super high as of late. While there are still plenty of "how do you do, fellow kids" dialogue moments, the dialogue, for the most part, seems much more real and character driven, aside from JUST trying to get a laugh out of the audience.The only major gripes that I have so far are the monotonous qte's and the fact that all of the side characters are infinitely more interesting than 2 out of the 3 playable characters.Nevertheless, I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy the first couple of hours of what this had to offer.CHAPTERS 2-4:The in-between chapters of the game had some fantastic moments, but there was more than a fair share of forgettable filler. It was at this point that I had realized that the game was going for a much more silly-than-serious, please-do-not-take-this-seriously kind of approach, which works in most aspects of the game, but falls completely flat in others.Again, my most prevalent gripes are with the main characters, and the fact that they are not nearly as interesting as the various side characters that have been introduced, despite dwarfing all of them in terms of screentime.Other than that, the story has kept my attention pretty well, the writing is, while still fairly cringeworthy, ANYTHING but bland, and the characters feel very human. OH BOY, CHAPTER 5:Chapter 5 is bar-none the weakest of all the chapters in the game. At this point, the writers couldn't seem to settle on whether or not they wanted to go for a more comical or serious approach, because writing and character moments are all over the damn place. I suppose everyone had to learn a lesson of some sort, which led to the final chapter being chock positively full of hamfisted character arcs that feel wholly undeserved. Not to mention minor characters kicking the bucket left and right for no reason other than "let's wrap this up." Everything leading up to the ending was bland, forced, and worst of all, monotonous to try to slog through. Fortunately though, the ending (that I got, anyway) wasn't all bad, and did a fairly good job of wrapping everything up, while leaving room for a future installation in some capacity.CONCLUSION:I enjoyed my time with New Tales From the Borderlands. Despite being plagued by more than its fair share of problems, the writing was some of the best that I've seen out of borderlands in a bit, and the character development and worldbuilding in the game were fantastic, save for some schlocky moments.Liked it up until the end, maybe skip if you don't like narrative driven games, wait for a sale anyway:5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is a nice interactive movie. Some ppl might be disappointed by the story, though. It is not as crazy as you migtht expect from a Borderlands game, even boring sometimes. If you're not interested in sitting back and enjoying the story, you won't be able to do much with the game. You shouldn't switch off too much, though, because the need to make decisions pops up suddenly again and again (and they have to be made under time pressure), and the QTEs also come without warning and relatively often. In contrast to As Dusk Falls (which was quite good in terms of its story), where the QTEs were all very similar and thus soon absolutely boring, in New Tales from the Borderlands there are very different activities to complete under time pressure. Of course, they aren't complexity monsters, but you have to dodge in the right direction, press the right buttons, hold buttons down, hammer on buttons, release buttons at the right time, aim with the gamepad... so the QTE sequences don't get monotonous too quickly. Besides these actions that pop up directly from the story, you'll also have to explore smaller environments or solve simple puzzles.You take on the roles of three characters - all three pretty much losers. Loveable, but at times so dumb it almost hurts. There's the genius scientist Anu. She works for the ATLAS corporation - which actually makes nothing but deadly weapons. That's not necessarily Anu's goal in life, though; she's developed a device that lets you just beam things (or people) away without killing anyone. However, she has no idea where the things or people are beamed to, nor how to get them back. So her device is not yet fully developed and ready for mass production, but her boss doesn't care. He does care, however, that Anu has just freed all those poor lab animals from their cages again... Anu wears goggles that allow her to scan the environment.Then we play Anu's brother, the wannabe corporate tycoon Octavio, whose pride and joy is a special watch on his wrist. With the watch, he can go into the Darknet and retrieve special information. It also works as a phone and for hacking various electrical devices. He dreams of his economic success while struggling through life with petty crime. By his side is his friend Lou13, a killer droid. Octavio gets potential targets to reveal their names, whereupon they are eliminated by Lou13. His other friends, a taco stand owner with strange pets and a dwarf who blows everything up, are also a bit unusual - but helpful in combat.And finally, we play Fran, who is in a hoverchair, selling the best frozen yogurt in town in her store and waiting (forever, of course) for the insurance company to finally pay her the insurance money for her store, which was badly damaged in an accident. She can upgrade her hoverchair to perform all sorts of additional functions. She's actually quite nice, but she's tended a bit towards excessive violence in her previous life....Anu is fired by her boss, Fran disposes of her protection racketeer, and Octavio once again assists his killer friend on a mission when an invasion of the planet by enemy forces occurs - and the adventure of the three begins. We play the three of them in turn, several times in each episode. At special booths (Change-O-Mate) we can improve their equipment (glasses, watch, hoverchair) and buy them new clothes, if we have enough money. We can find this lying around in various containers in many places in the environment. Already a little better hidden we can also find Vaultlander game pieces, which we will also need later for a mini strategy game.Actually, our three characters aren't as extremely wacky as we would expect from the Borderlands universe. They're just weird guys making their way through life. The really crazy characters and creatures do exist, though, and we encounter them throughout the game. Whether that's enough for you, or if it makes the game too un-Borderlands-like, you'll have to decide for yourself. In any case, it's not quite as over-the-top a story as in the first part.An adventure game in the style of the old Telltale games - you explore the (manageably large) environment, listen to long conversations and make a number of decisions under time pressure, while repeatedly proving your skill with QTEs. The story offers a good mix of really silly humor and serious decisions, but it still didn't win me over across the board. In parts it was a bit drawn out, and in parts I was expecting a bit more loopy and over-the-top Borderlands humor. Not bad, but not on the extremely high quality level of part 1.

_childDocuments_.review: It was extremely boring: It's essentially a game where the point is to be as inoffensive as possible and try to develop the relationship between three protagonists in the most seeker-sensitive way possible. So it's pretty much the opposite of what I expected out of borderlands. I expected blood, gore, violence, and very gritty humour. Unfortunately, if this is what you're after, don't bother with this game. It's starts off with a little bit of violence, but devolves into how the three protagonists feel about each other. That's the game: make each of the players really like each other. So it should have been labeled "BlanderLands", because it has almost no thematic harmony with early borderlands and by trying not to offend anyone, it's seriously bland. I pushed through and finished it, but I could only take about 20-30mins/day before literally falling asleep. In fact, the main benefit of the game is an alternative to counting sheep: if you need a new way to fall asleep -> try this game!Also important: you can't skip any of the boring dialogue, because that's that game. If you could skip the dialogue, it'd pretty much take about 3mins to complete. There are a few options you can make thoughout the game, but they showed up usually when I was nodding off.  Lastly, the humour failed because the entire f-ing game was focused on feelings, so it felt like every part of it was vetted so a 13yo wouldn't be upset by violent words/actions.All in all, the story is just plain boring. and I wish I had quite it earlier, but I get more sleep on the days I played this game, so there's that.This might be the way Borderlands series is going: boring, seeker-sensitive, purile, with an extreme desire to not offend anyone. I hope this is not the direction or the series creators turn it around, because I have very much enjoyed almost all the borderlands games. I even liked BL3 (though a bit purile).

_childDocuments_.review: I love Borderlands and its lore and Tales from the Borderlands is in extension probably my favorite Telltale game because of that.I appreciate Gearbox trying to produce content for those who wanted a sequel, but this was just too far off the mark.The main cast has flaws. And not in the way of 'Look at our flawed protagonists! Let's see them struggle through five episodes!'. These characters are all constants.In one corner we have Anu, an anti-social scientist trying to make the world a better place. She is in a constant state of awkward, cringe inducing panic attacks and bumbling through every scene with another humanoid, making you wonder how she made it through an intake to get to such a position.Then there is Octavio, a walking embodiment of self-pity and idiocracy. He is a constant bickering manchild sprinkled with a pinch of narcissism surrounded by 'friends' who appear as quickly on screen as they will dissapear.And lastly, we have Fran, which I think anyone would mention last as she seems to just be along for the ride. What started off as a half-interesting character, stuck in a dead-end job and dealing with anger-issues, quickly turns into a contant grumpy background character who tip-toes between backhanded comments that are either overtly aggressive or overtly sexualized. Even her character defining backstory, mentioned here-and-there throughout the story with the same intense slowzoom, gets build up massively at a certain point before being reduced to an out of place minigame, shoehorned into an almost static still frame. This character, ironically the one I can review with more details than her two counterparts, to me still seemed the most interesting, which says a lot about Anu and Octo.And while the main cast was leaving something to desire for me, I have to give credit where it is due.Some of the side-characters made me chuckle for a moment, especially the first few encounters with the Tediore soldiers, mostly identical nobodies who play off eachother in a way that made me feel like they should get their own Tales, even if some moments (particularly in the later episodes) were hit-and-miss.What I mostly missed in this story, aside from a good main cast, was a good side-cast.Where the original game used the Borderlands property in amazing fashion, reacquainting you with characters from the main series (Zero, Handsome Jack) and DLC (Athena (sorta DLC), Shade), the title cards were this time around mostly reserved for one-scene/two-scene characters, like Hans, a icepick wielding maniac, Stapleface, the most obnoxious bandit you've met so far and ... Sexy Free Labour Intern? who admittedly had good moves.Lastly, I want to emphasize the story, something I have yet to mention.Remember in Tales 1 where the first episode was structured in a way the first half of the game you meet one main character and their (in my opinion charming) clique, taking you approximately 15 minutes between the cold open of their story to them clearly having a goal and touching base on Pandora?Get ready to now deal with 3 characters with loose ties taking upwards to an episode to get to an unestablished goal, all the while switching between their stories in ad-hoc manner.The pacing is all over the place. For instance; Episode 1 switches around 6 times between the main cast and enviroments, including 3 hubs to interact with characters and surroundings, before Episode 2 then constists of a well-counted three enviroments, one being the same location 1/3th of Episode 1 took place, a sewer/cave (counting them as one, as they both function as a hallway) and third enviroment I won't mention due to spoiler's sake. To top that off, In this whole episode the player gets one hub to freely walk through with 4 interactables. The rest of this episode is a one hour long movie.During episode 4 and nearing the end of the game in Episode 5 where one character starts to dance (TWICE) during the ultimate bossfight, I realized myself something. This game is not really just wacky adventure. This game is a series of fever-dream scenario's where characters try to compete for who can look the most incompetent and slap-stick comedic at any given time. Conclusion: I got this game on release (October 21st) and finished it 2 weeks later (November 5th) after forgetting about it for 1,5 weeks to clear more space on my computer. Good moments; Bad... a lot. P.S. The musical intro's... I can forgive a lot, but what this game has shown me in that regard... it just hurts. #NotBusyEarnin'

_childDocuments_.review: I am honestly disappointed in this game as a whole. Jumping from the original to New Tales from the Borderlands was quite a bit of a screeching halt from what Tales of the Borderlands used to be. I usually give a benefit of the doubt with most games, but this... this is just... underwhelming... and honestly boring. Just in my first hour alone I knew that the magic of what the original had was not going to be in here at all. Plus, with doing some research on this game, I saw that Telltale had practically no fingerprints on this game due to them closing as a studio.If you are expecting the same flair and comedy that was present in the original, it is practically nonexistent, save for L0U13. There are recurring characters from the original, but from what I mostly played, they are... extremely watered down if not changed over completely.The jokes in this game are either mid at their very best, cringe-inducing most of the time, or do not land whatsoever.It seems that they opted to use more visual comedy than anything else, as the most jarring aspect of this game is their use of motion capture. It seemed that they shifted focus onto that more than anything else in this game.The game-play itself was also a bit jarring as it goes a little bit into the exploring aspect, but the camera setup was completely different as well. It seemed like they were trying to go more of an ambitious "Open World" aspect, and I am using that term extremely loosely, but it seemed to be a scrapped idea at the most part.I do not see myself finishing this game, nor do I recommend anyone buying this game standalone. I got this game through the Pandora"s Box Collection when it was discounted quite heavily. If at all possible, I would recommend fans of the Borderlands series and those who are fans of Telltale games to steer away from this game entirely.I do not recommend this game at all as a standalone. If anything, get this game with the Pandora's Box Collection when it is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: [3/10] New Tales is Gearbox’s attempt at making a narrative game like the previous entry developed by Telltale. It takes the gameplay of a Telltale game and mixes it with the writing of BL3. That is to say it is lacking in both aspects. The gameplay is simple and is a small departure of the Telltale style. Due to this lack of gameplay beyond quick time events and dialogue trees the writing must be main focus but it is bad. The three main characters you play as are all unlikable and don’t have meaningful character arcs. In addition these arcs happen in the last episode. Playing this game makes you feel secondhand embarrassment watching the characters behave like idiots in all situations. There are a few redeeming side characters that we’re enjoyable but only one is explored. The main characters spend most of the plot messing about and instead of overcoming any real obstacles. The main obstacle to plot progression is them goofing off. There is a few funny moments and good scenes that make the game decent and not a miserable waste of 9 hours. It is an alright game and has its moments.It is an alright game and should be considered a bonus to the pandora’s box collection but I don’t recommend buying this game as a standalone. Only time will tell if the events of this game will effect the mainline Borderlands titles but if it is the case it is likely better consumed through a recap than a full playthrough.

For background; I avoided reading all of the negative comments because I like to go into something new and un-phased with my own judgement about something. I absolutely love the Borderlands series because of both nostalgia and I love the writing, characters, lore, story, EVERYTHING about it. I have played every BL game (only made it halfway through the 1st because for some reason it triggers my motion sickness playing that one). With that being said.....New Tales from the Borderlands was terribly written. Anu was extremely annoying and her animations were over the top and not needed (she looked like she was tweeking half the time). Octavio was pretty funny, but also annoying at the same time. L0u13 was probably my only favorite character in the game...and he really didn't do anything. Fran was obnoxious and they tried to make her likable and bada**, but she also didn't do much with the main focus being Anu and Octavio even though you make decisions for her as well. I'm very disappointed Stapleface and Phuong had ZERO time in the game and had very minor parts; they were the most interesting characters tbh.  The story itself was all over the place and half thrown together. It never really dove too deep into anything other than the siblings' relationship with each other..which even then was choppy at best. New Tales doesn’t do anything for the Borderlands lore other than throw in a few big names  I have no hate towards trying to take the series in a new direction, but this wasn’t it. I wanted to rip my eyes out and smash the exit to desktop button halfway through the story, but I continued on purely to see how it was going to end and continue with what was being added to the lore. Apparently, there are multiple different endings which all suck regardless of if you get the Good, Neutral, or Bad ending. Neutral is supposed to be canon with Good requiring you to look up a guide on choices to make. I got the Bad Ending  That’s the other thing….the ending was so bad. So quickly written just to end the story….reminds me of GOT tbh. And after all of that…the main characters don’t even do anything worthwhile. Like…what?This game pushes the envelope of, “average people doing heroic things just to go back to average, normal lives again”, which is wild because isn’t that what Anu and Octavio wanted to avoid? Hm. Let's talk about the other characters which were more interesting to me than the main characters… Diamond Danielle and Radon…you could even throw Paco in there. They seemed so much more interesting and I wanted to know them more than what the game gives you. You get 1 scene with them…and then little cuts of them doing something and that's it, but they seemed like they all had more depth than the main cast. I guess what I’m getting at is this…side characters had more interest to me than the main cast did (other than L0u13 and even though he was “a main character” he was shoved to the side 95% of the time…mostly just reacting to what’s going on). I will praise the graphics, music/sound, and smoothness of gameplay, but that’s literally it. I truly do not care to replay this dumpster fire of a story just to see the other “endings”  You can unlock skins as you slowly progress through the story and use money you get to buy them (they were terribly hideous…Fran had zero good skins, Octavio had 1 decent skin, and Anu had 2…but that was it). All in all…. 2 out of 5 stars. Even if you have this game as part of your bundle, I wouldn’t recommend playing it. You can quickly get a 2 minute read on what happens and how insignificant this game is to the rest of the series. If you DO choose to play it then get ready for a snooze fest that forces pacifism in a GORY SLAUGHTER FILLED GAME. Terrible, over the top acting and main characters that were extremely uninteresting whereas the side characters barely get any notice and they seemed way more interesting. They even acted like you were going to need them and they would help you…but no. You use their help once and never see them again.

_childDocuments_.review: New Tales from the Borderlands is pretty much your usual Telltale game but set in the Borderlands universe. The game continues after the events of Borderlands 3 so you might get spoiled with some stuff if you haven't played Borderlands 3. The game introduces 3 new characters that we take control of. One of the unique things about these 3 characters is unlike Fiona and Rhys from the previous Tales from the Borderlands game, Anu, Octavio and Fran are mostly together on one screen and will have to interact with each other a lot. When I started playing the game, some of these new characters were rather annoying to me but they all ended up growing on me and eventually, I ended up likeing each of them. But still, my favorite characters are the unplayable ones such as L0U13, Brock and Phuong.In terms of gameplay, it's your usual Telltale play-style however, unlike any other telltale game, this one actually has multiple endings and those endings rely on the choices you make and how high each character's relationship level with each other. I'm also glad the devs finally included the option to rebind your controls so you won't be stuck using the WASD format if you're not used to it.In terms of game length, it's not very long and it took me around 10-11 hours to clear my first play-through and that's me really taking my time.For the story, it's decent enough for me but what made me enjoy it the most is just the usual Borderlands humor that I have always liked. It's kind of disappointing though that instead of continuing Fiona and Rhy's story, they had to introduce new characters instead.Overall, I really enjoyed this game from the characters to the comedic skits between them to the hilarious trolling I did to Brock (Yeah, that talking gun really got on my nerves). But despite all of that, I only recommend this game if you're craving for more Borderlands stuff and you really enjoy the Telltale gameplay formula or else, you should just wait for the game to go on sale as I don't think many players would find the full price to be justifiable for the game's length.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I could add much more to this conversation than what's already been said. It's just a lousy followup to Tales From The Borderlands (and all of Borderlands in general). Ideas that could have been good are buried under layers and layers of plot holes, wasted potential, and a desperate need to crack jokes at all costs, even at the expense of mood and character development. I don't think the writers could decide if they wanted the game to be like a wacky space sitcom or a serious drama about everyday human struggles, and I think that identity crisis is what ultimately crippled this game. Now I only have experience with the Tales games and don't have knowledge of Borderlands otherwise, so I didn't pick up on some of the inconsistencies with the lore of the other games until I read other reviews (like the whole thing with Katagawa Sr. or the fact that Tediore was never written as a serious corporation in other games), so I guess I wasn't as outraged as some other players. Regardless, if poorly written plots frustrate you, you should stay away from this one.Oddly enough, I kind of enjoyed myself a little though? Maybe knowing it's going to be a stupid mess beforehand dulls the pain and just lets you enjoy the ride. The game definitely knows how to create spectacle, so maybe that's what did it.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game with extremely low expectations. As someone who was a big fan of Borderlands 1, 2 & Tales but not a big fan of 3, I was concerned this was going to be more of what I didn't like in 3. Although I did thoroughly enjoy Tiny Tina (outside of the additional content/endgame stuff), I was still pretty concerned.NTFTB is a mixed bag. The beginning is a bit of a slow burn as they try to introduce the characters in the funniest fashion they can. This creates many moments of "try hard" comedy, where you can tell they are really reaching for a laugh. In some cases, it falls completely flat. In others, it's a double whammy as they take an un-funny joke and extended it WAY beyond it's welcome. It's definitely a bit rough.However, at some point along the run, some of the characters really began to grow on me. Especially the non-lead characters. There ARE many hilarious moments that I feel make this game enjoyable. From the throwback references here and there to reoccuring side characters starting to shine, there is a lot in here that is actually really good. Yes, even throughout the entire game, there are misses, the hits start to outweigh them as you get closer to the end. Although I was sponsored for about 4 hours of the run, I dove back in and finished the game with an additional five and thoroughly enjoyed myself. Although I really enjoyed the main case of Tales incredibly more, the side characters and situations in NTFTB made it something that I had a really good time playing by the end. It won't be for everyone, but if you can take a little cringe humor with the good stuff, you may really enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, boy. I usually never write a review for games, but after seeing so many bad reviews that are just plain and simple unfair and/or wrong, I decided to write a review for this game.Is it a Telltale game? No. Is it still a great story that got me hooked from the beginning until the end with a very lovable group of playable characters and sometimes even better non-playable characters? Definitely!The game is NOT woke as people claim it. Nothing gets weirdly forced/pushed onto you. Nothing feels out of place... Well, as much as you can say that about a Borderlands game of course.I saw many people complain about the fact that they changed the main characters for this game. Guys, you never played a Borderlands game before then, right? Every game has a different set of playable characters!The humor of the game is as it should be expected for a Borderlands game. Don't expect the deepest thought-trains. There are other games for that. But I had a great time, laughed rather often and just enjoyed the almost 10 hours of gameplay.And of course there is the "gameplay" that gets criticized often as non-existent... This game is a "tales" game which uses the essence of the Tales from the Borderlands game of 2014. Which is a Telltale game. Which means those are pretty much playable movies where you just make some key decisions, sprinkled with some quick time events. Why do people act so surprised that New Tales also has such a gameplay? It was VERY much expected to be that way. If you don't like those kinds of games then don't buy em and complain afterwards that you don't like it. Seriously...Anyway, it is ALMOST as good as the first Tales from the Borderlands, which was one of the best Telltale games in my opinion, and it is FAR better than Borderlands 3 which I had to stop after a few hours because I just didn't like it while I loved 1, 2 and even the Pre-Sequel.So if you like Telltale like games, like Borderlands, like some campy humor... Then this is the right game for you. Don't listen to reviews of people that either didn't play the game or managed to put in "0.2 hours" before their review which just says "Sucks". Or reviews of people that are just sad because Gearbox didn't make a game just like they wanted it to be.Now grab your SHINIEST MEATBICYCLE and explore the planet of Promethia with Anu, Octavio and Fran in New Tales from the Borderlands :)

I think a lot of the negative criticism is unfair, my only criticism is the story-telling was clunky and awkward only a few times, but thats expected with every game at some point. Overall, a fun time with fun characters that I whole-heartedly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to review this as despite the mixed reviews, I personally quite enjoyed the game. Now, as a longtime borderlands enjoyer (the series has been a favourite for close to ten years now), I can see why people who fell for the charms of say, one and two, might not enjoy this instalment so much - it deviates quite a bit and, aside from the art style, company names & some familiar characters in the form of vaultlanders, there's not much that links to the series roots. However, I'd say at it's core it still very much represents the themes of the series!Pros: + Really liked the dynamic of the main characters. Adopted siblings who really truly care about each other and try to overcome their flaws together,  the found family aspect with Fran and L0U13. I'm a total sucker for these things! Overall, they were all really charming too - albeit, sometimes their character traits were pushed a little too much in favour of jokes.+ The story brings in some interesting concepts such as anahatium. Would love to know where the heck this thing comes from, and what it's doing as of the end of the game!! (I haven't gone through every ending yet, so the one that I did play has left me with a bunch of questions :D) + Personal appreciation for both a main character in a wheelchair, who's seen as a total badass by those around her, and getting to see Lor's transition from 3!! The series has always been great for its inclusion, which i'll always adore it for.+ I really liked most of the humour! Some of it could've been toned down at times when there was meant to be tension (ie. Susan Coldwell's office, ch5.) But things like the recurring gag of the superfan, L0U13 chasing the laser pointer, or Octavio holding himself hostage were all really fun.+ Choices!! A lot of choice games can struggle with making you feel like you actually have an impact- but I think this game did a pretty good job on that front. There were actually times where I was wondering "Oh damn, how different would this have played out if I hadn't done this thing a couple chapters ago?" - The end of chapter summaries too would sometimes mention something that I didn't see /at all/ which piqued my intrigue :D+ Cosmetics. Not much to say, just always nice to have!!Cons: - Vaultlanders. Don't get me wrong, I like the concept! This is a soft-negative at most, mainly because it's just hit button over and over. However, I totally get that this is an optional sidegame and there were probably external circumstances that made it difficult to explore this concept further. - [CH5 SPOILERS] Stapleface's death :( She gets shot and bleeds out, all the while Anu's goofing off with an enhance feature instead of using the obvious door handle. As a scientist. :( This is one of the jokes I feel went too long, and really made the scene a little frustrating as SF was a very sweet character. The fact that the healing crystal just suddenly stopped working for this scene, too, was very confusing. Overall, my recommendation is a tentative yes. I'd say if you enjoyed Tales, BL3 or TTW, you're more likely to find something you enjoy about this game. The price for value is also something that'd maybe scare a lot of potential customers away, as the total playtime for one entire run through (checking every interractable in the world & vaultlanders included) took me about 10 hours total. For a game that's mainly dialogue-heavy and some QTE's, 34.99 may be a bit steep for a lot of people, or drive those away that are on the fence about trying this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a neutral rating I would as I think a negative one might be a bit too unfair. The game is ok, although the writing can be flawed, especially in terms of inconsistencies.It also gets a bit preachy and cliché at certain points which can be a bit annoying. I found myself rolling my eyes a couple times throughout the game.Surprisingly I think some of the jokes landed well which is a positive considering the lack of good jokes has been a reoccurring complaint over the last couple games in the Borderlands franchise. That doesn't mean though that there aren't bad and/or cringy jokes, because there are, plenty as to be expected, but it's nice to see that the writers haven't quite fully lost their touch.What I found the most annoying about this game is that the developers decided to take away some quality of life features present in the previous Tales from the Borderlands game made by Telltale. For example, they added missable achievements. Also, the achievement(s) to get all endings has been quite annoying, because not only there are 5 endings, it isn't clear exactly how you're affecting them. If you research online, you'll be able to find out what metrics the game uses to determine what ending you'll get, the problem is that you only get to see those metrics at the end of each episode, so it's hard to keep track of them while in game and make choices accordingly.To add up to that, if you're trying to go for all endings, that obviously means playing sections of the game again, but that's simply tedious as they removed the option to skip dialog, so you're forced to sit through scenes that by certain point you already watched a few times just so that you can get to a choice and select something different.I'm trying to go for all achievements, but I'm considering giving up as I already replayed the final episode about 4 or 5 times and yet I still only got 2 of the 5 endings.

_childDocuments_.review: After watching some of the trailers I had my own reservations about the new characters and about how the old characters would be handled. However, I did give it a try. And I was not dissapointed.First of, about the new characters:You may find some of them to be one-dimensional at first, but that is what the story wants you to think. Going forward you will discover that each of the characters have a lot more to their personalities. So, don't give up on them so easily.Now, about the old characters:If you're worried that the old characters treatment is bad, don't be. Sure, they don't have a lot of screen time, but when they do, you will find that they still have that which made them them.About the story:The events you go through may not be as glorious as they were in the previous game, but still it is quite fun and enjoyable.The plot of the first game was driven much by Handsome Jack, and yes, there is no Handsome Jack here. However, having three main characters this time makes up for it. The interactions between the team is what's moving the plot forward, and it is quite a ride.About the gameplay:Yes, this is still an interactive movie. But, it has some new additions: minigames. On your playthrough you will stubmle across quite a number of different minigames. Some of them are repetative and may seem boring, in that case there is a skip button for it. The main minigame (Vaultlanders fights) is present across the whole game IF you are discovering most of the playable territories. If not, however, there are only two mandatory fights that you have to play. There are also miniagames that you will encounter only once, but that expirience will be worthwhile.My personal score for the game:7.5/10
