_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzle games, I highly recommend giving this one a shot. I'm the kind of person who can't just sit down and watch something without doing other things as well, so this game was perfect for me. It is fun enough that I can play while I'm watching a tv show or YouTube videos, but not so engaging that I can't maintain focus on my other screen. The first few times that I played, I had fun solely focusing on this game but once you've played it a handful of times, I could see it becoming repetitive. Again, for me it's still fun because I play while watching/listening to other things but if I didn't do that, I probably wouldn't have sank in so many hours. If you love puzzles and peaceful scenic music, then I'm sure you'll love this. And if you're someone like me who needs to have something to do while watching something, then I think you'll enjoy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: looks like a good team of developers, really wanted to support them with a recommendation, but i just can't. I got the game to chill but ended up being bored as hell. The Art is amazing, Music is so chilling. but still there is a huge lack of content i feel like there's no goal, like i'm not asking for a complicated long missions, just give me a goal to feel that i'm accomplishing something. again this game is not bad it just needs some more work in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. The calming music, the charming sound effects, and the cozy visuals make for a soothing experience. The game is lightly challenging like a traditional puzzle while having missions and achievements that spice everything up. This is my go to game for quiet evenings or fifteen-minute breaks. It's something that can be picked up and dropped easily without losing any sense of focus or progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fairly intuitive puzzle game that feels like a single player version of Settlers of Cataan or Carcassonne. The only enemy is the randomness of the stack, and of course your own lack of forethought. Very fun game, worth about ten bucks, which I think is what I paid for during a sale. Definitely a spiritual successor to Townscaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It is addictive... Almost so much that it becomes stressful xD Well I love when everything fits and you get this "Perfect +60". So if thats not happening I get sad. But thats literally the only thing that makes me mad about this game and arguably its my own skill and patience while placing tiles that causes it. Now really.. This is a great game! So simple yet so much potential to replay again. It seems like there are some hidden tiles that you can unlock throughout the gameplay which is awesome. Personally I hope there will be some nice additions. I mean, mountains would be a nice thing, maybe with mines.But anyhow nice game, would recommend every day, especially for this Early Access prize!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece of a game, and it still isn't even finished yet!Games like these, to me at least, are rare specialties that I only come across once or twice a year. I cannot physically describe how calming and fun playing this is. I've played about 12 games now and none of my villages have ever looked similar to one another. My only complaint would be that, so far, the variety of pieces is kind of low. I would love to see more hexagon variants. Also, I'd love to see an infinite mode where the game plays the same but without the tile limit. Overall, definitely pick this up, especially if it's in your wishlist. It's $10 and it's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovely and relaxing game. The colors, music and sounds make it very easy to sit back and relax while playing Dorf Romantik. While the concept of the game is very easy it's quite challenging to make it past 10k points as a starter, it takes time to get familiar with the game's scoring system. For me this makes sure that the game stays interesting to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Once you get the hang of the game, it’s going to be really easy to lose track of time while playing this. It’s such a simple concept that has been well executed and will have you saying “one more time” after each game. I’m quite anxious to see where they take this title. It has so much potential and is already loved in Early Access. Just really well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? The game is beautiful.  Both the music and the graphics are gorgeous.  The gameplay is chill, relaxing, almost meditative.  It is easy to play, but also challenging, but not in a stressful way.I love watching my landscape grow as I build it out.  Finding the best way to match the tiles, fulfilling quests, getting a "Perfect", all to see how long I can keep going as the longer I can go, the bigger my landscape is.  And the better I match, the better my landscape looks.  And I love there is a creative mode where you can just build to your heart's content. I highly recommend this game.  Simple, but fun.  Great just before bed or after a stressful day.  Can't go wrong with getting this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: They claim it is a relaxing little world builder type game. They lie.After you learn how to place the tiles in a short tutorial covering 98% of the game play,they toss you into a digitally addictive universe.Soothing melodies play in the background driving your rage meter into low gear as you attempt to beat your own high score and build a wonderful little utopia.Random tile generation will have you mildly frantic as you try to complete the micro quests and replenish your stack of chips.I made the mistake of showing this game to my wife, and now I have freedom like I never imagined, except I use it to play this game along side of her...
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Quiet and relaxing. Watch the little trains zoom around! Take a deep breath of that ocean air! Is that a village? Hell yeah its a village, make it a city! Did you run out of tiles? No biggie, try again and get better. Want a stress free creative landmass sculptor? WE HAVE THAT TOO. Very enjoyable, zen type game. Please buy and support the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Game was not what I was hoping it would be. It is incredibly frustrating for me to play; an experience I would compare to trying to assemble a jigsaw puzzle with random pieces from a collection of multiple puzzles. Sometimes things fit together well. Sometimes a few edges fit, but create issues elsewhere. Most of the time it is trying to assemble something that doesn't look like anything. I was hoping it would be relaxing and I have tried to get into it. But it is simply not working for me. Very disappointing, but it is probably my own fault for taking a chance on a game based on reviews alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Really absorbing, simple to play, challenging to complete, several modes to suit many preferences, the interface and game design are intuitive and consistentCons: Not a lot of depth to unlock, all the goal rewards are purely cosmetic, and the prettiness of the map doesn't hold up very well beyond a certain size. Larger developments don't evolve into anything more interesting like some sim/builder games, they just sprawl. The edge-compatibility highlights don't show up well for every kind of terrain.Still a high recommend. Many hours of enjoyment, worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This beautiful tile-based map-building game is exactly what I needed. It can't help but be relaxing as you scroll through the game, placing tiles with a delightful *click* as birds chirp and quiet music plays in the background. It is simple to understand, difficult to master, and everything I could want in a an idle, zone-out game. In addition to building strategies to get ever higher scores, you also cultivate peace and quiet while you play. The perfect game for a busy mind that needs to be engaged and challenged but in a stress-free way.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: So much more than meets the eye.  Addictive gameplay, strategic thinking, clever, aesthetically pleasing and most importantly: so much fun!  But beware: I was not, repeat, NOT joking about the addictive part.Now get a drink, settle into your hovel and watch the hours drift by as you obsessively try to place tiles perfectly for bonus points.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so zen and is a true time sink!!! One of the best games in my library by far. Really easy to dip in and out of and a no pressure way of playing. You can up your strategy or just make pretty towns, forests, railways, fields or rivers. The background music and atmospheric sounds add to the calming experience
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a lovely puzzle game. I bought it and instantly couldn't put it down. The concept is simple...place tiles that have matching edges to form clusters. Tiles can be placed anywhere though, matching is optional but encouraged! The amount of tiles you start with counts down each time you place one. Earn more tiles by completing quests to form certain clusters with certain amounts of trees or fields, etc. On my second attempt I let my board get a little leggy, making the tiles I needed more and more complex. On this 3rd try however - I'd like to keep things tight. Anyways, it's saturday morning and I've just made my coffee. Time for puzzle catan ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Aaaaaaaaaaaaand relaaaaax.Lovely relaxing time filler for when you want to zen out for a bit.Very easy to pick up because you wanted something to do for 20 minutes and subsequently lose a couple of hours to.No time limits, very little pressure unless you want to min/max every tile placement, and even when you do run out of tiles you can continue in free play mode to polish off that river or complete that train line.If you like Mini Metros/Motorways and wanted a peril free alternative this could be for you.If you like Mini Metros
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is as relaxing as it is addictive!  Definitely has that "just one more round" feeling.Every game is different and there are even various game modes and scenarios to play.I would highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a chilled out tile matching type game with enough challenge to keep you diving back in.10/10.  Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Its not as simple as it looks, not not be deceived lol. Its a casual puzzle game but it will get tricky to break certain point based thresholds. Its akin to Islanders in my opinion which is a good thing. It will keep you entertained especially if you want to chase higher achievements for tracks and rivers!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Single player, easy to play, colourful, relaxing music and sounds, gently animated, cute animals, no time limit, quests, unlockables, seasons, progressive achievements, can save multiple sessions, creative mode, all ages.Cons: No kitties :(A friend gifted me this game last July when we were between lockdowns here.. took me 3 weeks to get all 47 achievements and I thought to write a review... but then the latest patch added 37 more so a couple hundred hours later, here we are lol. Easily my favourite go-to game. I love puzzles and problem-solving, matching, colours... and I really love that the songs are instrumental. Perfect game if you want to chill for an hour (or ten! I've reined it in though) and literally create your own little paradise tile by tile :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very very very good Relaxation Board Game.You just listen to some music and place tiles and chill. Even at its current state having a quick 15-20 min session is super enjoyable and a great time killer.Once they release creative mode so we can mess around with world building it would be even better!Its super cheap and totally worth it (because i imagine on full release they would increase the price a bit)
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game. Really surprised by all the great reviews. At first, this game is interesting, but after an hour or so it becomes mind numbing not relaxing. It just isn't fun. Unfortunately, because of all the good reviews, I kept playing thinking it would get better until it was too late to refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful relaxing game! This game makes me pass hours without realizing it. You just start building something nice, then you want to get your score up and unlock more tiles and maybe go after some quests...after some hours you start saying "just one more tile" but the next after that one is the one you were waiting for and keep spending another hour buildingSimple, Innovative and Fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: While I refunded the game, it was fun while I played it. However, I refunded it because I bought the game through Steam, but due to some glitch the game got removed from my library. Since Valve wasn't able to help. I just refunded it. Maybe I'll buy it again later, but after the hours of hassle, I'll wait for another sale.That said, while Valve was supremely unhelpful, Toukana reached out to me personally to see what they could do. Ultimately, the problem is on Valve's side, and since I bought the game through Steam, Toukana couldn't really do anything.The reason for the positive review is honestly because the devs at Toukana actually cared to respond, and didn't just ignore the problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: GRADE: A all the way. It earns its A rating because it is a super fun puzzle game that delivers exactly what it advertises and if this looks at all like something you would be interested in then it is well worth your time and money to give it a try. Wow, Dorfromantik is way more than I expected! It's like a zen garden in a game, with these adorable little tiles you can place to build your own landscape. Matching the edges? Super satisfying! And the longer you play, the deeper it gets. I swear, I've spent hours just chilling and creating these elaborate maps.For $10, this game is a total steal. It's perfect for quick bursts of fun or those days you just want to zone out and build something beautiful. Highly recommend checking it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't really have flaws in a traditional sense. It's fulfilled its quirky little goal of being an adorable puzzle game perfectly. Seriously, by this game if you like adorable indie games; the art style is cartoonish and beautiful; the mechanics are intuitive and inviting, while still remaining a do-able challenge.Toukana, you may be a couple of fellas from Berlin now, but I really can't wait to see what the future titles of this company look like. This game is adorable, intuitive, and a fantastic time-killer that challenges you in a very fun way that somehow avoids getting too frustrated. The only 11/10 I'll ever give to any game goes to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable, casual, peaceful game. The regular gameplay mode has great mini quests to chase and completionist goals that unlock special tiles. The sandbox mode allows you to set with sliders the kinds of tiles you want to be in your infinite pool of resources to skip or delete as they arrive on your stack to build your dream map. The visuals are pleasing, the music and ambiance are immersive and happily zen. The controls are intuitive once you get going and allow your mind to flit creatively across your ever expanding world to find the right places for each tile. If you love casual, mildly challenging, world building games - this one is for you! Even if you're a hardcore gamer, this is a great game to cool down and relax in.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: To clarify, I can't recommend the game *at full price*.It's not a bad game. Similar vibes to Mini-Metro, it's essentially a puzzle game. It's relaxing but I would struggle to get my money's worth of playtime out of it.I try to get a dollar/hour out of games at a minimum. And I, personally, can't imagine that I'll play for 15 hours. So my "no" recommendation comes with the caveat that if you can catch it on sale it would be worth it.

But actually no, this game is great, I love it, its cute, its satisfying...its probably not a good idea to put this on a work computer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing! highly recommend this game, easy to understand yet challenging, depends a lot of your observational skills and also a bit of luck for the tiles you get. I suggest to keep track of time, very addictive :PI'd love to have some bridge tiles to connect railways or house tiles over rivers it might make it more dynamic!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I love it! There was a bit of a learning curve, but after playing a bunch of games where I didn't know what I was doing, I cannot seem to lose my current game. Neither of those things is a complaint. Very meditative and soothing, I turn the in-game sound and music off and listen to my own music while I play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like nothing else I have played. It is a no-pressure tile laying board game essentially. You build out villages, wheat fields, train tracks, etc. You earn points for completing quests and matching tiles together with other like tiles. The art is beautiful, the soundtrack is lovely, very relaxing. There is no time limit pressure. If you play the standard mode, your goal is essentially to beat your own high score. Otherwise there is a creative mode where you can just build for fun. If you like board games, or if you need a game that you can just unwind and relax with, then this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to figure out what this game reminded me of, but eventually it hit me- it's like Carcassone, on a hex grid, and single-player. I was about to say "non-competitive" but that's not actually true; you get a score at the end of each round, so you can compare that with your friends if you want. But I don't want to. This isn't a game I want to play to dominate people. This is a game to solve emergent puzzles and to meditate. It's been a ♥♥♥♥ year. This game is bringing some peace into my life and for that I am ever so grateful.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I have already been sucked into this game. The art style is great, the music is really relaxing, and the game as a whole is very "Zen" Its a little discouraging to run out of tiles but starting over and seeing what you can make next time is part of the fun. And if you're really attached to one of your worlds you get the option to continue building in a creative mode. Its very satisfying when all the pieces come together perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: "The perfect is the enemy of the good."  -Some guy in a wigBut that sort of sums up the crux of this game.  Do you spend the time to slot each hex perfectly or just click away to try to unlock the tasks presented as fast as possible? Which one will keep you alive longer or could you do both?Here we have a casual puzzle game. Crafting a model train (and boat) world one terrain hex at a time. Each hex is some combination of fields, fallow land, forest, or town. Some hexes have water or a railroad section. place them to have all their sides match and you get a "perfect" and another tile. Make contiguous spaces to meet challenges and you get five tiles. Expand and find hidden challenges that give you more ways to score. Don't spend more tiles then you earn or you lose.Good low stress game.  Good music and nice graphics. A pleasant experience.Not at all exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. Saw RTGaming playing it and immediately decided that I should get it.The simplicity of the game mechanics coupled with its peaceful ambiance is the perfect combination for a game to just start up and relax. There is something just so satisfying about find the perfect place for each piece to fit.Also, having always something cool to discover and unlock adds to the entertainment and replay-ability.The menu could use a bit of polishing, but it is hardly important, and most of your time you'll spend it in the actual game. Also, it would be nice if it could become a bit more visually apparent when a piece is not a perfect fit, as it sometimes gets hidden behind the surrounding piece's or pop-up goal notices.Overall, a very enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game; it's mostly relaxing with some challenge to meet goals, but it's not painful to accomplish a lot in this game. It's still early access as I write this, but I've not encountered bugs or problems with play. I've had a lovely time playing this somewhat open ended puzzle.The only things I would wish for would be creative mode and more tile types. It'd be more fun with more pieces to play with! Fortunately, this seems to jibe with the developers' plans. The only thing I'd like would be a flower or garden tile- the forests and fields are lovely, but flowers would be even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Great but not good for minmaxers.Great relaxing game you can make other people happy with, by gifting it to them. Me as a minmaxer found myself resetting the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ playset over and over because the game gets progressively harder with more complex tilesets added to your pool through achieving milestones. (without rewarding you with more points or anything with increasing complexity) However that increases the RNG basis of the game and you find yourself starting over and over and over to reach new highscores. In the beginning you will have a smooth relaxing walk in the park discovering all the nice perks and cards and rules (that are not all really obvious or explained, most basic are, rest is trial and error). Anyway if you play this game a little bit and enjoy the smooth ride...it's great. If you are a stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minmaxing moron like i am? Pffffft....smooth ride my ass. Reload puzzle hell and for some reason i cannot stop ;-) Choose wisely...
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a truely beautiful game in the truest sense of the word. I love the visual style and all game mechanics. A great idle game to play while not using your mind too much. BUT you can also get really intense with this game and try your hardest for the best store. Especially for the frequent sale price i can only recommend diving in!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Oof. I really wanted to love this game- the art is so pretty and cute, and the tile placement thing seemed like such a neat twist on city builders, which I *love*. Before We Leave had a similar hex-based aesthetic, which I thought worked really well.However, the game is extremely rigid, lacking even the flexibility of solitaire: you can't reshuffle your tiles or use anything other than your top tile. And you can only place tiles directly adjacent to other tiles, making it basically impossible to plan routes for things like rivers and railroads.Overall, while I liked the aesthetic, I realized after about an hour and a half it was tedious and frustrating more than fun and relaxing.The music fits the vibe really well and the controls are easy enough to pick up, and I'd give it a pass for how the different land types do not blend well at all, but the gameplay just isn't enjoyable.F+
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to play Carcassonne and either were unhappy with not having friends to play it with or that the tiles lacked the proper number of sides? If so then Dorfromantik is very much for you. Dorfromantik is a calm relaxing game where you piece together a world and complete small challenges to get more tiles, rinse and repeat. A very good game to chill out with.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect little game. It really strikes the balance between relaxing and tactical. You get extra points for perfect tiles which really boost your highscore so shooting for these feels very rewarding but you can also just try to just create an aestetic landscape. Now I will go back to playing and unlocking more sweet special tiles!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Chill, relaxing, engaging without being stressful, great soundtrack.  I kind of wish there was just a bit more dynamic elements, like having a slot to set aside a tile, or being able to put a tile on the bottom of the stack if you want to use it later, or having little perks unlock every 5k points or something like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The most relaxing way to stretch your brain muscles. Just engaging enough to be able to multitask while playing, or chose to be swallowed into a world of vibrant colors and some of the best music in a game out today. A simple set of rules gets you started, and from there you can chose to let your imagination run wild, or chase after the high score mark. Whether you're into the city building or puzzle aspect, this game is money absolutely well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun and chill the music is amazing and its just so fun to watch a huge lake come together, a HUGE forest be built with houses here and there, or a really cute village come together no matter what you wont ever get a village like what you built before and thats what makes most of the fun
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: deeply relaxing little city builder that still has a good amount of strategy. while the soundtrack is absolutely fantastic, this is also a great game to play with the soundtrack muted with your own music playing over the top of it. Dorfromantik is the sort of thing that, like driving, allows you to really appreciate music bc its all-encompassing but not so much so that you can't get absorbed by a new release or old favorite. Aestethically this game is also beautiful, and its fun to imagine navigating around the little worlds you create. strongly worth the early access price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and sound are very conducive of a chill experience (full marks for that), but I _do_ find myself obsessing a bit over getting a higher score and unlocking the many, many achievements. A lot of these achievements come freely as you play the game more, so that's satisfying. I look forward to arriving at a point where I feel accomplished and simply build tidy little settlements. Thank you for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a German game designer made a game that uses haxagonal tiles and is not dull!All joking aside, though, the game is lovely, beautiful to look at and very charming.The mix of pure ambiance / just building and puzzle mechanics is great and there will be a creative mode in the final release, so you will be able to just make the arrangements you want.Easy thumbs up, especially given the price.Creative mode just adds more value.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most relaxing and chill gaming experiences I've found, and one so engaging and straightforward that my littlest one begs to play it, too! Far from being frustrating on any level, it feels like you're empowered to create your own little landscape the way you want even if you don't always care about maximizing your score. At full price it's worth it, so if you catch it on sale it should be an instabuy.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Entering this game is to turn your entire brain into hexagons. There is no outside world, only hexagon tiles.There are no loved ones in your world, only hexagon tiles. There is no need nor want for subsistence, only hexagon tiles. There is no concept of time nor space, only hexagon tiles. 10/10 this game is definitely worth it. If you play it with your sole focus on the game, you will enter a trance like state and levitate through the power of hexagon tiles (or maybe this is just a personal experience and others don't get this). I tried to be funny, hope this made you smile.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly excellent way to pass the hours when you don't feel like putting in a lot of effort. I've described Dorfromantik as Carcassonne-singleplayer, but better. The gradual progress through unlocking tiles and expanding your deck based on scoring is delightfully involving; the artstyle is almost soothing in t simplicity; and there is never a point of frustration or boredom.Great little addition to anyone's collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly simple, relaxing gameplay. The strategy aspect of it is easy to understand and work with, but at the same time there is a high skill ceiling to it that gives the game a lot of replayability and difficulty.The colorful visuals, ambient fun music, and sound design are also incredible. These are what really make the game relaxing and stress-relieving.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes you need a game that lets you sit down, relax, and listen to some peaceful music. Dorfromantik nails those points but also has high scores for people who want a little more competitiveness in their games. You receive more points for matching tiles perfectly together, for example a tile has a blank side, a forest side, and a town side. You then are rewarded for placing a new tile that matches the side it is connected to. This quickly becomes complicated because each tile has 6 sides and you are trying to perfectly fit together hundreds of tiles.This game has a limited amount of tiles you place and you complete quests to add more tiles to your stack, for example a quest might ask to have 50 trees in a forest. You would then combine your tiles with trees into a long chain to make a forest and complete the quest. You can also receive 1 extra tile for making a "perfect" tile, this is a tile that is surrounded by 6 other tiles and all sides match each other. One of the nicer additions to come out of early access for me was the option to play without the limited tiles in creative mode. This truly makes the game one of the most relaxing I have played with no worries about the puzzle aspect, you are just combining tiles to make a neat little map.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, peaceful game that has just the right amount of thinking and planning needed to make it feel like you're moving towards a goal while letting you feel like you're moving at your own pace without any sense of being pressured. It's very meditative and calming, I recommend it if you want something to zone out to and relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games that is easy to pick up and hard to master. I have 100s of hours, mainly because of the no time limit and working from home. You can just leave it on in the background and come back to it whenever. The devs are still working on it, and adding new challenges and tiles, but it's definitely more than playable.Placing a perfectly placed tile is very satisfying. Be prepared to lose hours of your life, to one more tile.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I think I'm at a point where I can give this a fair review now.So what is it? It's probably best described as a tile-laying board game but specifically designed to be played digitally, and solo. You get a stack of hexagonal tiles and place them on a board, trying to connect fields/woods/plains/villages/rivers/railroads. The placement rules are relaxed except for rivers and railroads, which HAVE to connect. However, if you want a higher score, you're going to want to place tiles that connect correctly on most or all sides. There are also dynamic quests attached  to some tiles (e.g. connect a woods area with X amount of trees) that reward you with more tiles if completed.The game is excellent, but it certainly won't be for everyone. If you're playing for a high score, a single match could easily take you 1-2 hours or beyond. And it's only really excellent when you're tackling it that way. Its good casual fun otherwise, but you would probably get bored after the first handful of games if you don't enjoy the challenge.The good thing is, you can go at your own pace, the music is zen and its a nice relaxing but thoughtful session. If you like solo board games, or have the patience for jigsaws, or love a bit of sudoku for some brain exersize, the chances are you will really appreciate this game.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, soothing tile placement and deeply satisfying puzzle experience. Trying to beat the highscore, you'll have to constantly find the balance between waiting for perfect placements and finishing quests. There's always a reason to start another round - beating your highscore, trying to unlock something new, or just building for beauty and relaxation. Great visuals and sound overall, great community and responsive developers with a clear roadmap, highly valuing player feedback. What more do you want from early access? For this price, it's a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying to play. The difficulty of placing tiles with matching sides and getting objectives completed to keep the tiles rolling in is very well balanced, it never feels like its difficult to complete the objectives, only that you made a mistake earlier that has gotten you into a tough postion.Great to play while chatting with friends or listening to a podcast, good vibes for sure. The aesthetics are very charming and its surprising how exciting it is to get a new skin or tile type to spice up your landscapes.Overall I highly recomend this game if your looking for a very lite puzzle game to pass the time and relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game manages the fine line between being challenging and relaxing, giving its players goals to strive for without making them feel like they have to "win". It is definitely a game that you could just use to unwind after a long day and enjoy how you grow the countryside and cities as you place the tiles. However, it can be just as fun to see how high your score can get by strategic placement.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of my new favourites. If you're looking for something low key that's simple and easy to play but still has its challenges and achievements while being mildly addictive, look no further. I saw someone playing the demo version of this game on youtube and was immediately intrigued. I'm so glad I decided to pick it up! I immediately got lost in it. I can tell this will be my new go to for winding down before bed. I would play it on work breaks but it's so addicting I wouldn't be able to tear myself away!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice, relaxing game that's easy to pick up yet hard to master. The pace is fairly quick, so it has that 'just one more turn' vibe going for it as well. Pros:- pleasing, colorful aesthetic- satisfying audio as you rotate pieces around, and click them into place- colors/seasons gradually shift in different regions as your puzzle grows - you'll never build the same puzzle twiceCons:- my achievements/progress got reset after opening the game today (I had to start all over), which leads me to my next point:- the game does not list new objectives once you complete the 3 milestones listed in the upper corner of your screen (I assume the devs don't think it's likely you'll complete all three in one game)- sometimes the background will quickly flash different colors as I move about the puzzle, which can be jarring- I'd like to have options for different themes when I start a new game (mountains, desert, fantasy, spooky, etc.)
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is as relaxed or strategic as you would like it to be. The music is intermittent and nonintrusive. The art is gorgeous on zoom-in as well as from a distance. The sounds are satisfying. I found the changing sky colors (background) to be beautiful but triggered a headache, so I appreciate the option to turn them off. The addition of monthly competitive challenges and creative mode has really turned this game into a gem. If you enjoy strategy tile games or would like something engaging without stress, check out Dorfromantik.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The concept and aesthetics are fantastic, however, after some hours there's a kind of repetition to the gameplay that begins to become tedious. The game either needs more game modes, or some more mechanical complexity to keep things interesting.Seeing only 3 tiles in advance also feels like an artificial impediment to strategic planning. there has been many sessions where, had I seen the next 5 or 6 tiles, I could have planned adequately to complete some quests before running out of tiles.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A zen game where you create, tile after tile, a colorful and cozy "dutch" landscape, with fields, towns, sprawling forests and rivers. Isn't exactly full relax, as high-score and challenges keep you hoping to get THAT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TILE TO COMPLETE!! But if you want go full relax, there is the sandbox mode, where you can unleash you creativity.The game keep getting little updates here and there, filling the map allow you to discover and unlock more "decorative" tiles and new challenge.Still hoping for "urban train station" and "railway river crossing" tiles (but perhaps I have yet to discover them), or a workshop, so people can add their own tiles or colo palettes.For me, it's a solid 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is made with love. You can really tell how much effort the developers put into this game. I love puzzle games and this one is super relaxing and fun! Really helps me with my own anxiety. Matching tiles to make perfect placements is such a satisfying feeling and completing quests adds to that! The creative mode continues to get better and better! I find myself getting lost for hours making unique little town designs. All in all, this game is super worth playing and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants a fun and casual game play experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an adorable and fun puzzle game. Not incredibly complex, but it's really enjoyable and I have been playing it while I queue for other online games. It's just very soothing seeing this world come together as you place pieces. I really enjoy watching games that slowly generate a random map, like Dwarf Fortress or Loop Hero and this gives a similar vibe.My big wish for when this reaches full release is a button to 'finish the map.' Sometimes I run out of pieces before I get a satisfying map shape and I would love to see a button alongside "Game Over" that turns off your score but turns of creative mode. I would love to just get a nice finished map that I could screenshot for a computer background or a reference map for an tabletop RPG. Also a feature to hide the UI for screenshots (though that might exist, I haven't found it yet)
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik (may we shorten it to "Dorf") is simultaneously relaxing and frustrating. Like most tile games, it combines strategy with luck. The tile in Dorf is more than pleasing to look at, and I have on several occasions ended a game to only continue in creative mode to finish fleshing out my landscape. I feel they could make minor changes to the game for playability, such as more significant rewards for completing more difficult missions (like seven new tiles than the standard 5). You will finish a game, get frustrated, and yet, find yourself right back to starting all over again. If they keep producing new tiles and tweaking the game, this is a long term winner. I find it my goto when I need a break from RimWorld or my other RPG games. Relaxing, artistic, and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a fun game to just sit back and relax after work with.I can just sit down and play for 40 minutes and calm right down.Recommend it greatly.>The Music is calming, and beautiful.> it's a great casual game, great for boomers.> You can take it seriously enough, and create some beautiful boards, and rack up a high score for all to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A marriage between world building and solving an endless jigsaw puzzle, bundled with cozy ink texture graphics and a gorgeous soundtrack. Has something for the cozy game lovers, the strategy-loving challenge seekers, and the casual gamer who wants to try something new. Endless replay value. It's like drinking a warm cup of tea after a tedious day out in the cold. One of the most original games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of this game, i think is based on the board game "Carcasonne". The difference here is, Carcasonne is played with square tiles, "Dorfromantik" is played with hexagon tiles. you have tiles fortrain, crop, house, forest, waterways, grasYou try to combine the tile borders to achieve greater connected areas of the same tile type. So every time the game is played, the map you build looks different.During the time of the release and a some time afterwards, i improved my placing skills of the tiles and at some point not only unlocked some special tiles, i also reached a high score of 10k. At this time i looked forward to increase my highscore but the downside, was i never again since the patching of game started. in other words, when the patching of the game started, the score dropped to 50% at best.So i observed and tried to identify what changed:reason #1:currently for me, their are two starting conditions. one is, that at start i have all special tiles with numbers on it. which is a pain to start with. yes, the starting special tiles, do not have high conditions to met, but all 6 of them at the start, well not my favorite situation to start with.reason #2:the total opposite of getting any special tiles. up to 4 straight waterways or 4 crop fields in a row. this maybe sound easy but when you get 4 straight waterways and the suddenly 4 curved or 4 intersections of waterways in a row, this can ruin quickly every attempt to even make some nice layout. the worst round i had so far, was when i got 12 crop tiles in a row.To put it simple, the shuffle system was altered in an unknown way, which puts the player, me at a disadvantage from the very beginning or at some point during the game, were the end is clearly at hand.Sometimes also the fact, you get a special tile, for example to build a forest and the rest of the cards you receive are only crop tile fields. so you have no chance to finish the task without a fair chance.To put in numbers, you have for example 25 tiles left, you place a tile which requires 48 crop tiles connected and 50% of the left tiles represent anything else, but not enough crop tiles. Before the patching of the game startet, i was able to reach one time a highscore of 10k points, took my some time, but now if i am lucky, i reach a score about 4-5k at best. so the shuffling and some game mechanics appear to be altered to totally disadvantage situation for the player.So what did i change, i now play the game in the morning, 1-2 rounds and the evening 1-2 rounds, nothing more. even when i try currently i cannot reach the point, where i would say "that was a close one".
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game a near hour. It's a great game. it's calm, relaxing and simplistic. it can be played to just create a fun, beautifull world, or you can go big brain strategy mode and plan your world ahead to create the biggest world and unlock the most tiles. and, while I came to the conclusion that this game is not for me, I cannot deny it's a great game and would highly recommend it for anyone who wants this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A casual tile-placing puzzle game where the objective is to go for the high score and optional challenges. The player gets a stack of random hexagonal tiles and is asked to place them on the map. You get points based off placing tiles next to other tiles with matching edges, and for completing some in-game quests to, for example, create a contiguous group of farms with 14 fields. Completing the quest will reward points and additional five tiles. Perfect tile placements (where all six sides match adjacent tiles) will also reward one additional tile. Closing off certain groups of completed quests will also award five additional tiles.+ Easy to pick up, but still has some depth if you want to go for the high scores.+ The quests keep gameplay engaging.+ There's a creative mode.+ Calming soundscape.+ Mobile controls- Placed a few hexagonal tiles, placed them all. Don't expect anything more complex than tile placing.Ultimately, you just need to ask yourself: "do I want to play a hex-tile-placer puzzle game?" Boy, did I. Placed those tiles real good. Got a bunch of perfect placements. Made a big looping railroad track that went nowhere. And a big forest. Yeah, this game's alright.  .
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game, love building my little worlds with my choo-choo trains and boats rumbling around. Lots of game modes for whatever type of experience you are looking, either challenging or chill. My only nitpick is that unlocking things in the game is tied to the main play mode, would like to be able to build without worrying about running out of tiles and have the chance to unlock things that way. I have been exploring the other playmodes and those are a lot of fun too.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very subtle. It's appears as a cute match the tiles game but after a while you discover it's nefarious side when it gives you a railroad and river piece. How am I supposed to place that when I have my river on the right side of the map and all my railroads on the left? I end up having to build my railroad and river network toward the middle. Ugh!My point is you get lost in building the tiles and forget you are supposed to be matching as many sides as possible not just making the largest railroads/rivers/towns possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik has charming visuals and a core mechanic that is satisfying in the way snapping two lego bricks together is. Unfortunately, I found the actual gameplay loop mildly irritating. Occasionally you find just the right tile to complete a region and that's satisfying but most moves you are given the option of settling for a near match where 1 or 2 sides are incorrect or extending your overall map wider and wider. The former case feels unsettlingly suboptimal (a feeling validated by the score track) and the latter case runs headlong into the games sluggish camera controls. The result is that I played a single, hour long run where I achieved a reasonably high score and more or less have not touched it since.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a relaxing and highly accessible puzzle game that revolves around city building, carefully placing tiles and losing hours of your day in the blink of an eye. The devs have created something special with this title - the art is stylized in such a way that the sprawling coastal villages peppered with Autumn trees you'll often end up creating make you feel like you're creating somewhere familiar and comfortable. The gameplay is simple enough that just about anyone can pick it up, young or old. I'm really looking forward to the creative mode and any future updates.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game with a good idea: building a map, with a focus on aesthetics, relaxation and peaceful country life, rather than war and conquest. What I liked: it's quite relaxing. Good controls. Soothing music.What I think could be improved: A) the graphics are OK, but could be a little more detailed, forests and fields in particular look very stylized. B) The game tends to starve you of tiles. You get one extra tile for a perfect placement and five for a quest, but perfect placements are not so common, and completing a quest will take you more than five tiles on average once you've progressed beyond a certain stage. Watching your stack of tiles slowly run out and being unable to do much about it is frustrating, not relaxing. C) Clearer indication of open borders for "close group borders" quests, they're difficult to see right now.What the game is missing: A) a creative mode. That's promised. B) An undo button. Sometimes you misplace a tile and want to undo that. Would be nice to have an "Allow undo" option, at least. C) An "Add extra tiles" button would be nice - one that, when clicked, will give you an extra five, for free. Think of it as taking a mulligan. (And again, this could be an option.)Overall: a good effort that I don't regret picking up. It'll be interesting to follow this game's further developments.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game that is sneakily addictive and satisfying. Very calming, and was even able to enchant a partner who rarely touches the world of video games.  Wonderful interactions and performance with well crafted visuals and design all under the influence of a calming and satisfying soundtrack. I would recommend for a broad range of gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely loving this game so far. I definitely need to practice, but it's the most soothing game I've ever played. My hope is that they'll keep adding achievements, biomes, etc. This could be a lifetime favourite if they keep this going. For early access, it sure does feel polished. Love this!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I've only owned this for a day and already I know it is going to be a classic for me. I can focus and care about my moves as little or as much as I want. I can play carefree and just focus on aesthetics, or I can try to maximize my tile placement for the best score I can get. I love how this game plays in that regard, a perfect addition to my collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that is very definition of "easy to learn, hard to master."  It seems simple enough... matching tiles with different landscape types to make a pretty vista.  But there's some deeper gameplay here, and while you can just have a fun time slamming down tiles, you'll hit a wall until you unlearn some bad habits and assumptions.  Bigger isn't always better, and attempting to make every goal are two issues of mine that often led to me running out tiles early and prevented me from getting bigger scores.I think if I had one main issue, it's that the need to connect the outlying quest tiles to unlock new goals and eventually tile types wasn't made very clear.  I kept wondering why I had clearly made a forest of 500+ trees on several occasions but didn't get the achievement until I re-read some stuff about the game.  I may have missed something somewhere in the tutorial, but it would be nice if this was made a bit more clear up front.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: As a gamer who cant stay fixated on a game too long, this game piqued my interest. The moment I started playing, I was instantly hooked and most importantly relaxed. The game lets you play a simple "puzzle" style city builder but lets you be absolutely creative and build out a little landscape how you like while matching up pieces to make it a cohesive building experience. I love the music, soft visuals and the care put into this fun game. If you play this game high like I did, youll REALLY enjoy it.Blaze on <3
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Getting my Girlfriend to play a game is very hard. She will usually say things like , this game is too complicated, or too violent, or too easy, or not interesting. This game really got her sucked in. I never thought I'd see her sit for 4 hours at the computer playing a game on the computer. Well since I showed her this game she's been playing it everyday and she loves it. Not too mention I'm addicted as well. Its perfect and amazing. Throw on a audiobook or podcast and play for hours. worth every penny
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really peaceful game, meant to represent the charm of rural landscapes of towns, farms, rivers, and forests. You rotate hexagonal pieces of terrain to match sides with what you already have placed to earn points. Earning points gives you more pieces to place, and completing various goals unlocks different varied tiles for future rounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing puzzler with nice art and chill music. Try and complete the simpler tasks or spend more time setting up spaces that will allow you to place 'perfect' tiles to go for longer games.Enjoyable to see the map grow and fulfilling to unlock new tiles.If the trailer makes it seem like something you'd like then you probably will. It's definitely the right price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing peaceful game. However, there is some management and limited resources aspect towards the end of each game, so if you find that really stressful it might not be ideal for you. For me it's a fun calm challenge and I love it. I got this after a stressful week and it was bliss to unwind for even an hour on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is soothing to play and a lovely logic game that requires just enough thought to keep the brain occupied without ever becoming a stressor in its own right. The music is calming, the graphics are charming, and no matter how you lay down your tiles, your little landscape will always be gorgeous. And when you inevitably run out of tiles (usually without even realizing it), you get to start all over again!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely relaxing puzzle game. Place tiles on the hex grid to try and build terrain, and earn more points by accomplishing goals of making certain sized areas that pieces will give you. It's thoughtful, but not in a stressful way, and the presentation is very soothing. The perfect game for taking your mind off stuff for a little bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: My main frustration with this game is all the missed opportunities to create game dynamics that would enhance play. I mean it's ok to potter around and place tiles until it gets a bit meh, but I can't help but feel it lacks the ability to really give players any real game mechanics that allow greater creativity and beauty.If this game had babies with chip chain then I can imagine they might be better.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most relaxing city builder games that I have ever played. The music is gentle and there is something satisfying about placing the tiles and watching the world come to life. The more you play the more the world opens up and the more biomes you can unlock. And if you don't want the restriction in the regular gameplay, you can always play in creative mode and build to your heart's content. Highly recommended.Updating months later: As this game continues to grow and change it still continues hold my attention. It is equally challenging as it is relaxing. And the addition of the new music and biomes continues to enhance the experience. It continues to be one of my favorite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so chill and relaxing. I bought a copy for my brother almost immediately after playing it, to share the love, and he's played so many more hours than I have. The music is great. You get lots of bursts of serotonin with the quests and expanding your creation. It reminds me of Carcassonne, but less stressful since I'm not worrying about other people since it's not competitive. Peaceful city-building is where it's at!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, relaxing, satisfying. Love it. I wonder if the developers read the comments, but I would suggest adding more quests and objectives. Maybe some campaign. Also I would love to see living things interacting with the landscapes. For example: people settling in the cities. Maybe a big enough city may have a mayor, which brings some benefits. Bigger lake may house fishes, ducks. The forests may have animals in it. This can be expanded vastly. Maybe these things may allow you to build up on already placed tiles and stuff. I realize this is long term expansion of the game, but Im just throwing wild ideas in case it can provide some inspiration.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The art in this game is fantastic, underneath the cuteness is a tile laying game with some solid strategy.  Completing objectives extends your play just like in the old school arcade racing games.  Thinking about how to best use the landscape types on the tile will make you question your choices after you have run out!   There is lots of discover and unlock in this game and I find myself constantly drawn back to try to beat my high score.  Overall a very relaxing game with great music and its a good way to unwind after more intense games.   I am looking forward to see what Creative mode has in store in the future.  So far this game is a beautiful village romance!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems simple, but it can make your simple brain works too. I mean, if you wish to have a bit of tiny calculation & strategy to place the tiles (hexagon) then this game is for you. But if you wish to bombard other nations, deploy military and win a war, this game is NOT for you.A chill game, non-violent 'board games-vibe' like DORFROMANTIK is always needed during this stressful times (because of pandemic and hectic life quests). Thank you developers for creating this and having a humble attitude as well. Plus, you're listening to community suggestions to create the CREATIVE MODE in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I'll admit it took a little while for me to properly grasp the mechanics but once I did I was pretty much hooked.Dorfromanktik hits the perfect balance for being both relaxing and engaging. Whilst the gameplay requires quite a bit of thought and planning; the pressure is minimal and accompanied by a peaceful understated soundtrack to create a very chilled atmosphere. It definitely has that 'one more attempt' appeal even after multiple game overs it's easy to simply jump back in and try a new strategy with multiple little incentives to keep you coming back.Quite a few commented on how much they enjoyed watching during stream too so it's definitely been added to my list of games for me and my audience to wind down with.In terms of criticism, one thing I would love is an undo button for your last placed tile. There have been a few times where i've mis-clicked and wrongly placed a tile ruining my progress which was a little upsetting.Besides that I'm having a great time and I'm super grateful to have been sent this to try out as it feels like one of those games specifically made for me. Can't wait to see how things progress moving forward!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: There's not enough here for me. And I get that simplicity is at the core of this game but it just needs a little more to it imo. One idea, for example, would be special tiles which you can accumulate as quest rewards or whatever and they are available at any time to play. These would obviously be rare but could fill a specific need on demand. I'm looking for a little more control over what I'm able to do. I also think there should be some economy type bonuses such as connecting a large urban area with a large field area or connecting two urban areas. This would simulate trade and tourism.I played for a few hours and it was alright but there's zero urge to play any further so I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not been playing this game for very long at the time of writing this, but so far I've found it very chill and addicting.I love the combination of town/village building and puzzling, and what's great is each town you build will be unique so it feels fresh each session.For an early access game, it's super stable and feels mostly complete as it is.2 things I'd love to see implemented into the game being;-The ability to save a town if you reach the end of a session, and can view it in some sort of gallery.-An endless mode and / or a mode where you can freely build what you want.I know this isn't strictly a town builder game, but it would be cool if there was a separate mode where we could free build without relying on random chance tiles, and minus the puzzle element.Please don't get me wrong though, absolutely love this game as it is so far. The suggestions I made would just be an awesome addition.-UPDATE-After reaching out to Toukana on Twitter, they confirmed that they are currently working on an endless mode. Sweet!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A low-key, very relaxing flavor of puzzle game that also manages to be surprisingly compelling for how simple the core loop is.The premise is simple: -You have a finite stack of hexagons to put onto a grid next to one another.-The more edges match, the more points you get for the placement.-If all six of a tile's edges match after a placement, you get bonus points and an additional tile.-As you play, you get challenged to compete certain specific objectives for more tiles.-Once you run out of tiles, the game ends.There really isn't much else to say; everything works appropriately, the music is pleasant and fits the pastoral quality of the scenery you'll be constructing, the sound design is unobtrusive...  If this looks like the kind of puzzle you'd like to put together I can only recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game by a friend and it turned out to be one of the best gifts I have every received.  I simply love the simple complexity of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly well made.It is a relatively simple puzzle/strategy game with a lot of depth.+ Very easy to learn+ Intuitive controls+ Very smooth learning curve to reach mastery. By the time you master one element of the game, the next element is ready for you as soon as you feel ready to make the jump+ Very player friendly. Someone at the door? Answer it, you don't even have to pause your game. Baby crying? Go clean that diaper. The game will wait.+ Relaxing sound track+ There is a strong strategic element that adds a lot of excitement. Playing as perfectly and balanced as possible; finishing small quests, making perfect plays and trying to unlock new tiles by reaching and completing bigger quests.So I think this game is pretty much as good as perfect, but there is still room for:- There's not a lot of music in the soundtrack, I haven't reached to point yet where the soundtrack annoys me because the tracks are very relaxing and subtle. But some extra tracks won't hurt.- In some cases it hard to figure out which part of a tile is which type of landscape (especially with forests) you will eventually figure this out with experience and by that time it is no longer an issue, but here's some room for minor improvement here. Mainly aimed at new players.- I'm nitpicking here, but sometimes zooming in out out can be a bit of a hassle because the controls are very similar to the controls that turn a tile. It's nice and intuitive to have these controls so similar, it makes the gameplay simpler. But sometimes I wish there was a key (like ctrl) I could use to zoom in situations where otherwise I'd be turning a tile (and the other way around).
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The very definition of chill. There is a tactile feeling to tile laying games that translated extremely well to the digital media and as a puzzle it is genuinely satisfying. The pastoral setting is lovely but I can see how this could be easily modified to suit whatever theme you prefer (gimme my Warhammer Old World setting dammit!). The lazy landscape is serene and the music soothing and there is nothing more satisfying than puzzling together a huge dark forest and vividly imagining the horrors that lurk within ready to terrorize the local town if their greedy inhabitants ever get too close to the woods stringing up their bones like chimes in the trees as a testament to the might of the Horned King!Or maybe that is just me..

_childDocuments_.review: Experience the euphoria of creation in this high-octane, top-down build-'em-up. Contend with the ever-more-extreme demands of the Brandenburg Rural Development Committee for yet more lush wheatfields, serene forests, and cozy woodland hamlets, all to feed the insatiable hunger of the German peace machine. Deploy the hexagon, nature's perfect shape, to construct a sprawling network of countryside fixtures. Erect dread monuments to your terrible might, such as the Maze of Endless Maize and the Three-Tile Circular Railroad To Absolutely Nowhere. Learn to fear and respect the hidden power of the otherwise-innocuous river, as its conniving curves and bewildering bends ruin round after round after raging, tearful round. Experience the nail-biting thrill of wondering if the tile you need for that one spot you've left vacant for the entire game even exists in the first place. Realise that it doesn't. Lose. Quit the game in childish fury. Come back for more.This game has it all. If you don't buy it, then your brain is stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Review at Patch: "10th of February"Hours Clocked: 6Considering this is the second copy of Dorfromantik I own, I other being on the Nintendo Switch, I do recommend it.The game is straightforward, you place hexagonal tiles adjacent to others, build a scene and continue going until you run out of tiles to put down. They can be rotated to match sides for bonuses. Simple enough, but the hook is keeping your pile of tiles flowing.While you can simply go for making a pretty scene, there is something satisfying about using lots of tiles to make a large diorama of your own design. Getting more tiles through completion of challenges, and perfect matches does not impede the relaxing style either.As you play, you will unlock new tiles like a Beaver Dam, or Old Tree that can crop up in you your tiles for more variety. On top of that, you will unlock new themes like Enchanted or Fjords which you can toggle for extra appeal or flavor. They can all be on at the same time too, so you can get a whole cornucopia of variety if you so choose.When your game ends, you can continue it in Creative Mode if you really liked how it turned out, or you can start a again. You can also save your maps that you might have taken a liking to, so even if you can't add anything else to it, you can show it off or just admire the boats, trains and nature sounds.Overall my recommendation of Dorfromantik is Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is barely a game... it's a console (Switch) game that should probably have been a mobile app.  It's selling point is that it's "casual" which means "incredibly shallow" in terms of gameplay.  The idea is that you create an idyllic village scene by placing various tiles around.  In an attempt to make some kind of game out of this objectiveless sandbox, there's a few limits to what you can and can't do... you can run out of tiles, and you've given what seem to be procedurally generated "quests" that just involve specific arrangements of tiles (like placing three tiles with "forest" edges together, how challenging).  You might as well play dominos with only one player, that's pretty much what we're dealing with here, only slightly more visually appealing.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard, there's some minor technical foibles that aren't helping.The game features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the mid 2000s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.Because this is a console game, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.This looks and feels like a mobile app, but it doesn't seem to have made it to the app stores.  It's unclear why this was put on Steam/Nintendo Switch instead of the app stores it seems to have been designed for.  Maybe it was removed, maybe it was rejected by Apple and Google (they do have more rigorous quality standards than Valve does for Steam, after all).Regardless, for all intents and purposes "Dorfromantik" might as well be a mobile app, it has the same limitations and dumbed down qualities.  It's impossible to recommend such a game to PC gamers.  We don't spend all this money building gaming rigs so we can pretend they're iPhones and play games that might as well be mobile apps.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Another unusual point, the software contains stock/store assets and other packages, but the "developer" here hasn't credited the people who actually did the work for the software (a scarecrow asset, a number of Unity packages for UI and graphical effects and so on).  While this isn't necessarily against the license for the use of those assets, and it's not an unusual practice for this kind of code reuse, claiming the work of others as your own without crediting them (I checked the credits) is highly unethical.All of that might be forgiven, but the pricing can't be.  Dorfromantik has the almost comically optimistic (if it wasn't so sad) price of $14 USD (plus TWO soundtrack DLC's for $6, making this games true cost a whopping $28 USD, near AAA pricing), for which you could easily get any number of recent AAA games.  The developer seems to genuinely think this is a better game and thus should cost more than the entire Mass Effect trilogy, The Witcher 3, Subnautica, Deep Rock Galactic, the list goes on.  I know, right?You wanna talk about city building?  This costs more than Cities: Skylines!!!This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this massively overpriced product.  Given the defects and quality issues with the software, coupled with the unrealistic price, and the questionable ethical nature of the developer and/or their associates (as outlined above), this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a wonderful little puzzle game that's somewhat reminiscent of both the board game Carcassone and the Xbox Live Arcade game Hexic HD. Your job is to place tiles with matching edges onto a hexagonal grid and fill the board. Seems simple enough... but there's a good amount of depth to it.To start, your tile stack isn't infinite and will deplete at a fairly steady rate unless you complete quests along the way. These quests come up fairly often and rely on you making a connection of either exactly X amount of a resource, or surpassing X amount in one group. Certain versions of those quests will drop a flag in their resource pool once completed. To grab the flag and accumulate even more tiles, you must close the entire resource pool. There's a nice amount of strategy in deciding when it's better to continue expanding a forest to complete quests that might require a large amount of trees, or starting a new forest and picking up more tiles so the round doesn't end. There's other ways to grab more tiles, such as making a "perfect" hex, by matching the patterns on every side of one hexagon piece. Managing both of these factors well will help you go far.But, if you're not as concerned with the score there's a creative mode too. Upon finishing any round, you're able to continue playing and placing tiles as you wish with no pressure whatsoever.At it's core, Dorfromantik is a puzzle game that's easy to learn, hard to master, and will have you fixated for hours. Whether you're looking to paint a scenic landscape with beautiful designs or seeking the challenge of making a perfectly aligned grid with nothing out of place, Dorfromantik is definitely worth your time.
