_childDocuments_.review: Created and published by Toukana Interactive, Dorfromantik is a casual strategy puzzle game that allows players to build their own picturesque countryside one piece at a time. Based in Germany, Toukana Interactive was founded in early 2020 by four game design students attending HTW Berlin. Their second venture, Dorfromantik, showcases their whimsical disposition and talent for crafting games that keep the player coming back for more.GRAPHICS 8.5/10Dorfromantik draws you in with tranquil landscapes and keeps you hooked with tricky gameplay. Quaint and colorful, this game has a cute, cel-shaded style that instantly catches the eye. Red-shingled houses and trees have a hand-drawn quality, and natural features like plains and lakes are filled in with rough strokes of color, giving the appearance of an oil painting. Changing seasons are represented by gradual variegation across the board, fields of green and purple slowly bleeding into warmer hues of russet and gold. Deer wander through woodland meadows, windmills turn in a gentle breeze, and plumes of white smoke drift up from chimneys, adding movement and life to an otherwise stationary landscape. As a gamer drawn first and foremost to visuals, I find the art direction of Dorfromantik one of many shrewd moves in Toukana Interactive’s already blossoming career.SOUND QUALITY 9.5/10Drift along on a current of calming music as you expand your world. Dorfromantik’s soundtrack is curated by Laryssa Okada and Pygoscelis. Only a handful of musical tracks provide a backdrop for the game, but their relaxing atmosphere pairs perfectly with its leisurely pace. One particular track bears an uncanny resemblance to Yoko Kanno’s song “Green Bird” from the anime Cowboy Bebop; another employs the ethereal notes of a piano à la film composer Thomas Newman. The additional sounds of roosters, cows, and horses accentuate the game’s country vibes, while boats and trains chug along their highways and birdsong trickles up from the treetops. There’s also an adorable little pop whenever you lay down a tile (and what sounds like a low note on a glass jug when your placement is invalid). Altogether, the combination of music and sound effects is soothing and transportive.GAMEPLAY 9.5/10Although one could literally play this game single-handed (a fact I relish when my cat falls asleep in my arms), that doesn’t mean it’s mindless.Like any good tabletop sim worth its salt, Dorfromantik is easy to learn but difficult to master. Even after watching the tutorial, it took a few sessions to really wrap my head around how to get the most out of each turn. However, once I finally understood how my actions either promoted or kiboshed a biome’s ability to expand, my high score began to increase by leaps and bounds. The goal of Dorfromantik is deceptively simple: build outward from a central tile and connect matching biomes to earn as many points as possible before you run out of tiles. Each tile is a hexagon that contains one or more natural or manmade features: village, plain, farm, water, railroad, and forest. Each turn can net you between ten and sixty points depending on how well you align your current tile’s edges with the existing board. The more landscape types you match up, the more points you earn. This wasn’t specifically pointed out in the game’s tutorial for some reason; I discovered it by accident through a combination of trial and error (emphasis on the error part) and online research. The main focus of Dorfromantik is the quest tiles, which require linking a prescribed number of matching biomes to complete. Fulfilling a quest tile rewards you with bonus points and—more importantly—extra tiles, which are essential to the continuation of your game. Biomes light up when connected to each other, giving you a nice little visual hint about the effectiveness of your placement. Much like chess, surveying the whole board before making your next move is essential. The number of linking biomes required to complete new quest tiles increases the longer you play, so leaving large stretches of farms, rivers, or towns open-ended is definitely a wise move. However, you may choose to ignore a new quest if it means completing another when you’re short on tiles. One tile is drawn from the stack with each turn, and once you run out, it’s game over. See how long you can keep your session going—the longer you play, the higher your score!OVERALL 9/10Toukana Interactive’s Dorfromantik ticks all the right boxes for a peaceful yet engaging game. The beautiful landscapes, clever mechanics, and constant desire to beat your high score will have you saying ‘Just one more game!’ like it's nine o’clock on a school night. Every session is unique and culminates in a new map that’s just as beautiful and organic as the last, resulting in a very high replay value. The combination of strategic puzzle solving and creative worldbuilding is also downright addictive. It’s just the right amount of challenging and relaxing, and when mixed with a bird’s-eye view of the halcyon world emerging almost as an afterthought of your game, it evokes a satisfying sense of productivity and serenity. I can already tell that Dorfromantik is one of those games I’ll be coming back to again and again for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun hex puzzle game. You will get pretty good at building out the maps and unlocking new hex tiles, though some of these unique hex tiles seem to unlock multiple times. The game seems to usually stall out between 15k and 20k points as finishing the quests becomes more and more difficult. _childDocuments_.review: The depth of strategy takes an interesting approach here. Making you Intuit the coming situations. Why not just keep making one huge forest? Well because you will eventually need two as forest quests emerge from the stack. Then ultimately merge those two forests together to complete even more quests that "might" come. Try not to split up your "Outs" with rivers or tracks. Create a couple zones of each type with planned lines on where you hope to eventually merge. You may have only one giant city with 100 buildings and then receive quest for a city with 75 buildings! You cant add it to the Huge 100 building city without failing its quest. Forcing you build up to 75 from scratch! It's a new way of thinking that is super chill with a bowl and a cup of coffee. Lol!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty relaxing game, hours of chill fun (I had no idea I'd already played so many hours of this game). It's easy to play, challenging when you're ready to be challenged, but never tense. Just peaceful. The best part is settling into the "flow state", getting in The Zone, and just laying down tiles and building endlessly. The worst part is running out of tiles and having to stop. I hope there will be additional features to make it easier to keep going and going.Some possible examples:1. A game mode where you just don't run out of tiles (but maybe then you can't unlock any new secret tiles - or the game mode is unlocked after you have unlocked all the secret tiles). Maybe this is what the proposed "Creative Mode" will be?2. UNDO. A single undo, or even destroy a tile would be great for those mis-click moments where you put something down where you didn't want to.3. The ability to set aside one or more tiles to use later (or draw multiple tiles like a "hand" and choose which order to lay them down), because sometimes you get a piece you don't need NOW but will need SOON.4. Or, the ability to trash or reshuffle the current tile.5. The ability to mulligan/reshuffle the entire stack, when just nothing is looking good.6. The ability to buy a specific tile you need - maybe chosen from a few specific ones rather than selecting ALL possible tiles (like, a station, a full water tile, a full forest, full field, and so on).Features like that would be nice amenities, but aren't necessities. To be clear, I'm having plenty of fun with the game exactly as it is! After all, my suggestions are all ways to continue playing the game, specifically to prolong the flow state.Even if it stays as it is, it's a work of art! Absolutely worth it. Thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state I wouldn't recommend it, but in hopes of it getting some changes to make it way less frustrating I will keep the thumbs up. The concept is there, just the execution isn't on par with it yet.In general I like it, it's a cute game, chill, relaxing, fitting music and I enjoyed my time with it, mostly, but it's also an absolutely frustrating mess. It is way to random.What this game needs is a better weigthed randomness that favours what you are trying to accomplish with quests you have and or better mitigation for it in form of either wild cards and/ or 2-3 options per drawn tile to choose from.It is absolutly no fun seeing yourself getting 5 quests for a trainline that grew exorbitantly large and no way to finish any of the quests, I have gone, in that situation, with 30 tiles without a single trainline, you are just stuck at that point with no way of getting those quest tiles. Especially trainlines and rivers are a mess. You can't forcibly close them and sacrifice these quests to hope for something that is doable at that point. At some point, no matter what, you NEED a very specific tile to either close the loop or put a stop to it. I like the IDEA of a balance act of trying to fit tiles perfectly together vs sacrificing some quests or perfects to keep the run going, but the reality is that you are just too much at the mercy of the random tiles to even dare call it a balancing act.After 26 hours of learning what tiles are possible and doing the math behind it, the chances to get any kind of tile you want is abysmal. To many variables in to many configurations. You can go very long without any kind of tile you would need to work on a quest you have, NOT TO MENTION any tile that fits the surrounding of said quest.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I try to put in at least 20 hours before reviewing a game but I make an exception in this case...  is a wonderful and casual puzzle-type game that delightfully blends a "city builder" with simple puzzle elements.  . A truly relaxing and enjoyable game while still providing a satisfying sense of accomplishment.You will enjoy challenging yourself to do better and learn from your own mistakes while improving over time with experience. I will say it is well worth its purchase price as-is (mind you, I missed the 'Early Access price by a single day and have no regret!). I highly recommend and I would be very surprised if this game would disappoint anyone whom genuinely enjoys this genre or any puzzle-type games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: DorfRomantik is a puzzle game that is very easy to sink a lot of hours into; starting a new game after finishing off of a deck of map tiles is extremely tempting. Theoretically, the game has the potential to be an endless puzzle, though I'm sure that there are engine limitations for the amount of tiles.The soundtrack is calming, the art style is simple but very pleasing to the eye, and the gameplay is simple enough to grasp but challenging to master. Well worth the price as an Early Access Game, with a lot of growth potential down the line. I also appreciate the clear lines of communication with the developers, which is always great to see among a small game design team. I'm looking forward to seeing what sorts of new tiles will be presented, and how the creative mode will be introduced. I could see some interesting potential with exporting tile maps for tabletop purposes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a single player Carcassonne with missions. There are currently two modes: High score and creative. In high score mode, you earn tiles by completing missions (link over 30 houses together, create a forest with over 200 trees, close off a set of fields, etc). Your score depends on the placement of these tiles (10 points for each edge matched, for instance. There is no time limit so you can take it easy, placing the tiles until you eventually run out giving a score at the end. As you progress you also unlock more tile types to add variation the better you get.Creative mode has unlimited tiles and you can change which ones are most likely to appear next. Both modes are relaxing, unless you get obsessed about beating your high score :D Personally, I play one game and quit, do something else then feel a desire to come back for another game. It's not a game I can play for hours in one sitting, but this isn't a criticism. It's one I just want to keep coming back to with a more adrenaline inducing game in between sessions.Update: Works absolutely perfectly on Steam Deck using both touch controls and joysticks.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Where sometimes you get a great board game adapted for a PC, this is a puzzle game adapted into a board game. The simple mechanics of matching types keeps this from ever feeling like anything other than a delightful brain tickler. I love the addition of other modes as well, the Monthly Challenge ensures that you'll be coming back to this to work on improving your score and unlocking new tiles.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and wonderful game but I don't play it often because it opens part of my mind that I am not necessarily comfortable exploring on a frequent basis. Paired with the ambient, peaceful music, it invokes some REALLY deep thinking where I find myself reflecting on my life, who I am as a person and the impact I have on the lives of others. All while I'm just placing little tiles around the map and watching little boats and trains move along them slowly without any care or urgency. Hard to adequately explain but it's probably the most calming experience in the world outside of any mind altering drugs. For me, it's even more powerful than any meditation I've ever done. Super recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill, easy to learn hard to master kind of game, feels like a very forgiving puzzle, as you get more points for more edges matching, but it will let you place as long as at least one matches. Some of the UI needs a bit more explanation, like the challenges that are exact versus +, but for early access it's good fun
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely likeable game - slow paced with relaxing music but fiendishly difficult (for me at least) to get to any sort of a score over 6000. I'm not sure I want to read the strategy guides out there to place my tiles correctly because I'd like to think I can 'win' a higher score. Dorfromantik is not for anyone with a trigger finger, or is an  adrenaline junkie or requires something visceral to thrash themselves against. This is a strategic game which you can play just for the soothing music and devilish decisions on tile placement. I'll dip into it on and off though i don't suspect it will ever be my 'go to' game when all else fails.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo, and now the full game, of Dorfromantik for a good few too many hours I can undoubtedly say this has been the most relaxing and engaging game experience I have had in years. The concept is simple yet extremely entertaining, perfect for relaxing after a stressful day or for whenever you just need a small break from work. Overall a perfectly well made game 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This is my go-to game for calming my brain. The music is soothing, the tiles are pretty (and have variety), and the various achievements give me something to work toward without feeling pressure to race against a clock or other players. And if you happen to like the little world you're building, you can enter creative mode in order to continue with infinite tiles (albeit without accumulating points). It's a fun and chill little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: You want a dose of digital endorphin? Here you go. That's what you'll get with Dorfromantik.If that doesn't sell you, maybe this will: Dorfromantik is basically a single player version of Carcassonne. Get a big stack of beautiful hex tiles, then place them down to form wonderful, unique, peaceful countryscapes. Some tiles come with attached quests: attach this piece to pieces that contain more than 130 trees by lining up edges correctly, and you'll get more tiles, more points, more relaxation.And that's all there is. I have never played a game that is as relaxing and easygoing as Dorfromantik, and considering the state of the world we live in, that's a very nice thing for a game to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Lord I hadn't realized how much time I have played this. Great little puzzle game to mess with while watching, listening to, or doing stuff. While it is relaxing it is not nearly as simple as it may seem on the surface. To get higher and higher scores takes planning and patience. Pay attention to where you place tiles, try to recognize the future tiles that would fit into your already placed tiles. Make sure to abuse that undo button and try different solutions to maximize perfect tiles. Or you could just zone out and place stuff to look nice... that's also fun.So simple, addicting, and engaging. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a super cute and chill game. Thoroughly enjoyed my hexagonal tile placing experience! Will place more tiles again! The little train and boats were super cool, I want to be able to build a massive rail way... someday. Even though the music is super calming and the game is chill, each round does take quite a while. In the 4.5 hours I have played, I have only done 3 maps - it is very easy to lose yourself and time in this game. DO RECOMMEND! Chat & I give this game 8 / 10, breezy said it was B*ITCHIN! _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you can sit back, relax, and casually build up a nice and unique map.You can control the entire game using only your mouse, which is fantastic!I can easily see myself booting this up in the background whilst I wait for something else, like a queue time.Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very relaxing and easy to play. The music is soothing, the designs are lovely, and I love seeing the moving pieces as they are so cute. I love how peaceful things are and I look forward to seeing what they add in the future. I also love creative mode. It's so much fun to custom build tiled maps to how you want. Unlocking new tiles and skins makes me feel so pleased hearing that sound and seeing what I got. _childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: it's a simple game, or, rather, a toy. The graphics is lovely and objectives are simple, but the gameplay is too straight forward: you pull a hexagonal tile from the top of a limited stack, place it on the board, connecting trees to trees, fields to fields to extra tiles in the stack as a bonus . But ultimately (and too soon for me) you run out of it and it's game over and start over. After 4 runs I put it back in the box and slid it under the bed: it gave me no sense of satisfaction but rather a slight disappointment of failure.I imagine if there were some challenge like connecting to a railway station tile to run a train or building a city of certain population in a designated space would give me that satisfaction that I missed, and without it there is no real motivation to play it again

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea what Dorfromantik means. Anyway, I won't repeat what everyone has already told you about this puzzle game. _childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This aesthetic puzzle game is easy to lose yourself in. Enjoy placing hexagonal tiles to build a unique, randomly generated world. Earn tiles with perfect placements and build continuous networks of homes, waterways, railroads and more. I like that there are so many things to unlock to add flair to your map- skins and special pieces like a beaver damn for your rivers- and that there are different color schemes. This game is easy to play and difficult to master, offering vast replay-ability. The soundtrack is nice, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunningly beautiful with a cardboard/toy box aesthetic to an astounding detail with every single map you build looking gorgeous and like an actual small world which genuinely feels really satisfying. The games can take quite a long time to play, on average I'd say about an hour but I still play a little too hastily so assume a little longer, for example a youtuber called SB took about 4 hours but was an exceptional run, highly reccommend it for getting into the game. However the games are saved and can be quit at any point completely seamlessly.So the gameplay itself is as simple as putting hexagons down and connecting them together to earn points, simple. However the complexity is in attaining a high score by trying to maximise your efficiency, as you have a set amount of tiles to place which are increased by "Perfect" tiles (when all 6 edges of a tile are matching another tiles edge) or more commonly by completing quests on certain tiles, by getting a big enough biome, getting a specific size biome or even specific and then closing it in! Plenty to think about and it encourages thought into where to have a "Main" forest for example and where to place ones to be small and closed in.Once you reach out you'll notice hexagons in the distance which, when reached, will reveal a tile with a quest and an aesthetic you wont have seen on any of your own tiles. Complete the quest and you unlock a new challenge. Each game you start gives you 3 challenges out of your current pool, and completing said challenge will give you a new tile, such as Deer on some forest tiles, moving trains on railroads that will travel along, or beautiful flowing fountains on town tiles! These moving pieces truly remind you how much love went into this game made by 4 STUDENTS! It's insane! The soundtrack is beautiful and calming as is the aesthetic, they're planning on adding more features notably a creative mode for those who want to build beautiful worlds but are focusing on the gameplay and features to ensure the product is worth, and good lord is it beyond its worth. Absolutely a steal and an incredible game for those who want a soft, relaxing yet just thought provoking enough to not be boring and with fantastic replayability.And to the devs if you happen to notice this, a feature I would love is the ability at game over to look over the map, I'd love when I lose to be able to zoom in and admire the world I bought, screenshot it and just admire what I managed, I think it would really be wonderful.  Also I have only ever done around 3 reviews I think, and never even a quarter this length so, take that as you will. It's absolutely brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly relaxing game, but can also be deceptively challenging. Whether you're just in the mood to build and add tiles without caring much past aesthetics and decompressing after a long day, that's fine. If you want to try to keep your streak going and unlock more tiles towards a higher score, that's fine, too.  If you just want to build a lovely countryside, you can keep on playing even after your tiles run out (though your score won't increase. The art is absolutely lovely, with the different looks available from different "biomes" keeping things fresh. The music, art, and simple gameplay all come together to make this an enjoyable game indeed. If you're looking for a relaxing change to add to your gaming library, put this game at the top of your list. I can't wait to see what Toukana adds next!EDIT: Nominated for "Labor of Love" for this year's Steam Awards. Keep up the great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is the ultimate procrastination tool masquerading as a game. It's a digital version of adult coloring books, a puzzle on steroids, a black hole of tile-matching goodness that sucks you in and never lets you go.A virtual puzzle but instead of just fitting them together, you get the satisfaction of creating a unique new world.It's like meditation but with less incense and more pixels.If you're looking for a stress-reliever, a  zone out or just something to kill time, give Dorfromantik a try. The only downside is that you might find yourself neglecting your responsibilities to play this game.Just don't blame me when you realize you've spent the entire day trying to get perfect tiles instead of doing work.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: A visually pleasing, highly addictive puzzle game. Quite a bit of strategy is needed and you need to meticulously place every piece to go for higher and higher scores.That said, this game isn`t for everyone and gets repetitive rather quickly. At some point your score is so high and you have so many tiles placed that you need a couple of minutes just to figure out where to place your next tile. Apart from the achievements/challenges there is nothing noteworthy to strive for. They reward you with new skins for your biomes which makes your game look even more aesthetically pleasing.A minor gripe I have is with the unnecessary grindy achievement "play 50 games with a score of 5k or higher".
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME. Every evening after work I relax by playing a round of this. :) Easy to pick up and go and super nice to listen to a podcast or audio book while playing!The music is calming and chill as well! :) Cannot wait for more updates!! :) Definitely recommend to anyone that needs something to relax and process your day - especially if you need something mindless to keep your eyes busy (ADHD).
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: While it won't knock your pants off, it's not trying to.  It does well what it sets out to do, which is provide a chill tile placement  puzzle game that offers mild challenge and enough direction to help you set goals to achieve.  The tutorial could be a little more thorough about all aspects of score counting, but I'm just here for a light snack game and some achievements to work towards.  Totally worth the 10$ asking price.  The preview videos show you precisely what you get, no surprises.  There's not a lot to this game, and that's just what I wanted from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: The nice thing about this game is that you really can't go wrong with your choices. It's chill, giving you a vibe like you're playing a game made by Bob Ross, making your own world full of happy little trees (and houses, and lakes, and rivers, and fields.) But there's reward if you want to put out the effort to make your choices to maximize score. Going for that perfect on a tile? Great! Just putting it where you think it looks pretty regardless if it matches the surrounding tiles? Great! This scratches an itch in that I feel like I'm being productive by creating a beautiful world and unlocking new things as I go along, all with the cozy atmosphere that is perfect for relaxing after work, having a cup of tea, and listening to an audio book or podcast. I can't wait to relax with so much more of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like city builders? Do you like puzzle games? You'll probably like this. It's a very simple and relaxing game where the object is to optimize placement of tiles to keep the session going. There's enough engagement and challenge to keep you invested, but it's definitely more a game to unwind to.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Really a wonderfully simple and relaxing game. Endless replayability potential and the whole vibe of it is really soothing and adorable. Mild puzzle "solving" mechanics that drive a very satisfying experience and it doesn't need anything more to be something I can see myself easily sinking unknown amounts of time in to.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: When I play for too long I forget what even is the meaning of life. I rarely boot the game for just an hour, I admit. By far one of my favorite game, they tweaked the balance til it's just right, the multiple game modes are great and you will find the one that works best for you. Good game to keep my eyes and hands busy when I need to follow some audio. In case you are hesitating between switch and steam version, the fluidity of the mouse for steam makes it so that you can play fast / too fast, but the slower tile placement on switch actually allows the players to focus more and not play bad placement too fast, Both versions are great, and definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very laid-back city builder.  It has more in common with a board game than a big daunting sim, with just enough complexity to be engaging but not overwhelm you with systemsYou're dealt random tiles to place on a hexagonal grid, with each tile containing terrain that you can link together, like trees, houses, train tracks, etc. The focus is on short-term goals rather than something like balancing supply and demand or planning traffic flow. Sessions last until you run out of tiles. My sessions are typically an hour or soIt becomes a light puzzle game when you get a tile with a "quest" attached to it. The quests net you big points for linking a specified number of a terrain-type together, like a 25-house village or 200+ tree forest. Since tiles can have different resources on each side, this creates some decision-making for how to best arrange them when you have multiple quests in play and try to keep layouts open enough to accommodate tiles you might get in the future, especially if you also want things to look cohesive and make sense (not required for points, just for fashion)I really enjoy it! You get the satisfaction of growing a town without the intimidation of it being too involved. The art style and music are very cute and it's fun to see little environments come together
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my first hour or two with Dorfromantik, but after that I found it to be repetitive and irritating. You are given a set of randomly generated tiles with rivers, trees, houses and fields on them. In order to keep gaining new tiles and avoid a game over, you need to make bigger and bigger sets of matching tiles (a line of 20 river tiles, or a group of 30 houses etc). The problem is that the game wants to be both a relaxing casual game and an addictive puzzle game, but doesn't really excel at either. You can't just relax and make a beautiful countryside scene because you are forced to constantly hit your goals, i.e. you might want to put a cute little forest next to your hamlet, but you have a goal to make a group of 400 trees, so you are forced to just keep expanding this one great big forest you have. If you don't hit these goals you won't get any new tiles and will get a game over. You also can't play it solely as a puzzle game because there's not enough substance. You are literally just making big groups of matching tiles - there's not really much strategy to it. A few times I tried to plan ahead and just never got the right tiles I needed to create the design I wanted. You are at the mercy of RNG - if you need 10 more trees to hit your next goal and you just get 10 field tiles that are useless to you, you're just out of luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I watched RTgame play this. He did everything so poorly it enraged me to the point that I bought the game myself just to prove I can do better. This is a lovely city building/puzzle game that is perfect to relax to. You get to play at your own pace. There are no timers. The game also does not simulate citizens like true city builders so that is one less stress factor. Not getting a perfect tile is really of no consequence. There is a nice variety of tiles which results in a different city every time you play. This game is chill, easy to play, and only as challenging as you want it to be. Its also very pretty to look at and can be satisfying if you actually tried to make aesthetically pleasing city.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Zen yet so addicting. I've found myself moire than once sitting up until 4 AM (yup... 4 AM) playing. Totally lost track of time. I love unlocking the special tiles, and I love the skins for the world. I hope there are more coming. I also love the music. So peaceful and works so well with the animal sounds above it. I do wish there was more info re the monthly events and what all we can hope to find as we progress in the game involving more critters, skins, and other fun treats. All in all, if you want some good, happy (yet absolutely challenging) gaming, this is the world builder to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: logical godsim with nordic vibedifficulty: 7/10 if u want to win challenges, but u can just play at ease and have fungraphic: 8/10 everything here looks a bit like a comic book, but that's a real charm. bioms naturally connects with each other, creating an eye-catching color palettesound: 7/10 just relaxing and regulation is possibleirritation: 0/10 really chill and heartwarming - personally my comfort gameOVERALL: 8/10just wish for more options (especially new bioms) in future, i feel a bit of void playing it nowbtw i don't reccomend playing on touchpad
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I do love this game. This is very relaxing, creative and strategic. I do recommend it to anyone who loves games such as Cities Skylines or Townscaper, it is new, original, and you can find some similarities. GO FOR IT, THIS IS VERY COOL <3DEV NOTE (remarks and improvements): - the train logic is too chaotic; to many deviations, too many turns. If you are trying to play the points you will get something very ugly and messy.- water train stations.... okay why not, but let's go for ground train stations aswell no?- BRIDGES for trains... because having 50 water train stations is not so beautiful xD- maybe wagons with the train?- roads & cars?- more things! great game! Go for it! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful, relaxing game. On first sight it seems to be simple, but the quests become more difficult over time. Dorfromantik is the "just one more round" type of game. It has a unique and neat art style and the relaxing music makes it perfect. This game doesn't feel like any other Early Access game I ever played. The gameplay and overall quality feels - in its simplistic way - much more polished.I'm still curious though and looking forward to the further development and additions the devs have in mind. For now, I can definitely already recommend it. It's really nice to see what a small group of young game developers can accomplish.Toukana Interactive, you have my respect, and I'm also looking forward to see the other games you'll make. Thank you for releasing this game earlier than planned in a time like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to play Carcassone but without all those pesky friends messing up your village?This game is a beautiful relaxing time-eater. It's as challenging as you want it to be. You could obsess over maxing the value of every move like I do. Or you could just try to make the biggest forest and the game will be just as happy to come along with you.The biggest praise I can give though is that it feels totally finished here in 0.1.2 early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I love all the different types of tiles that you can match together, and all the different terrain. The water is probably my favorite type of tile because there is a lot of different shapes and sizes that you can make into amazing landscapes. The only thing I don't like about the game is that the fields look like rocks, so they look kind of tacky. They don't even match up that well. But otherwise, everything in the game is pretty amazingly relaxing. I would say 4 1/2 out of 5 stars. Overall, SUPER good!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Great, very relaxing game, with a very simple premise and a lot of strategies to learn if you want to push your score higher and higher. If you looked at the trailer and it seems interesting, I couldn't recommend it more. I love playing this for a few minutes or an hour or so, always gets me relaxed when I'm feeling stressed. Had this game since it came out in early access, and I'm glad it's near to a full release now!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a beautiful game build around an interesting idea. You create an idyllic landscape out of hexes, trying to fit the next elements to the rest. It is fun, short, and casual. It can be relaxing, and it stimulates your mind to some degree.Personally, I do not think the game like this, that is built around casual fun, should have levels, unlocking and any kind of grind. It is not a problem, but a feature that does not fit to the overall atmosphere.The replay value of the game is rather low. After learning the rules and gaining some experience you will begin to see how much the game depends on the random factor. From my experience, puzzles designed by human generally provide a better experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Not even a full hour into playing this game and it's truly something else.While it might not be the super hard, mind boggling puzzles you'd see sometimes, this game is definitely a top of the list for me. It makes everything so perfectly soothing and calming to look at, the atmosphere is relaxing, and the gameplay is super simple and easy to understand, but can still call for complexity when you need it. It's a perfect balance of a fun, casual, simple, and amazing Strategy/Puzzle game. Good work developers!Definitely a 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game has become the one that I play to have some me time, to relax and to do things I love. It's as challenging as you want it to be with the different options there are within the game. Even if you challenge yourself by playing it with a limit, you can always continue your map in the creative mode, which gives it a gorgeous twist on being creative in your own way. Wether you play this every day or decide to not look at it for a while, it will always be a game that will relax you in a way that it doesn't give you any pressure to achieve things. However, the achievements do make you think twice about placing something and only adds creativity in your brain.As you can hear, I'm hooked. I can only hope you'll like this as much as I do :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It's chill and you can get lost in it and forget that you're supposed to clear quests to keep getting tiles or else you run out and have to start over. That's not a bad thing though, because you get to use new things you've unlocked in your last playthrough. Replayability is what this game is about. It's very relaxing if you only have a few minutes or don't feel like getting into anything heavy for an hour while you drink your morning coffee  or afternoon coca-cola. Have fun and be well. Stress is bad. Play Dorfromantik
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is such a nice game. Just being able to chill and take my time, all while trying to find the best placement of the next piece is quite interesting. Watching the beautiful landscape evolve, all while trying to get max points and still making it look nice and natural. quite the mental exercise :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing and Challenging at the same time. The unlockable hex variants give you a reason to keep coming back without it feeling to grindy, and make each session feel new and different. Charming visual aesthetic, and the addition of the quick and creative modes make this humble game the complete package.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game like you wouldn't believe. It acts all friendly like it's some sort of relaxing chill hex game but it's just a visage to slowly grind away your sanity in what ultimately amounts to a massive waste of the minutes you have left in your life.Oh, Dorf Romantik, you sly, deceiving little devil, luring me in with your adorable hand-painted graphics and soothing soundtrack. How could I ever resist? But just as I let my guard down, you unleash the hidden beast within.You claim to be a "relaxing building strategy and puzzle game," but what you really are is a tactical mastermind that feasts upon my feeble attempts at creating idyllic landscapes. Yes, I see through your ruse, Dorf Romantik. You're not fooling me any longer.Sure, the game starts off easy enough, lulling me into a false sense of accomplishment as I place tiles, creating quaint little villages and serene forests. But then, out of nowhere, you hit me with these so-called "quests" – the windmill that demands six grain fields or the deer that wants a 50-tree forest. Well, guess what, Dorf Romantik? I don't negotiate with terrorists.And let's talk about those "unlockable tiles and biomes," shall we? Oh, how exciting it must be to discover new lands, filled with new challenges! Except, you know what I don't need? More challenges. I have enough of those in my life already. If I wanted to feel the crushing weight of my own inadequacy, I'd just check my bank account or try to assemble IKEA furniture.Oh, and don't even get me started on the high score system. You mean to tell me that not only do I have to suffer through this relentless hexagonal hellscape, but I also have to compete against others for the highest score? What kind of sick, twisted game are you playing, Dorf Romantik?But perhaps the most egregious sin of all is the undo button and rotating the last tile to not lose. Yeah instead of losing my mind over the placement of a stupid lake tile, I could just enter creative mode but again there's the score I have to worry about.In conclusion, Dorf Romantik is a heartless, diabolical game that masquerades as a calm, peaceful retreat from the chaos of life. But don't be fooled, my friends. It's a hex-shaped nightmare that will slowly, mercilessly grind your sanity into dust. You have been warned.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend Dorfromantik. The art style and sound design are amazing and give a great sense of tactility when placing tiles. There are plenty of game modes and themes to choose from. The game is simple and easy to learn while giving almost unlimited play-ability. Even when not on sale this game is totally worth it, the developers continue to update and add new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill until your score starts getting and the walls start metaphorically closing in around you. Dorfromantik is cute and comfy from the presentation, graphics, and music. My only gripe is that I personally have a hard time seeing the indicators when you mouse over flags. More of a nitpick is that I wish something more grand and cool would happen when you close something off like how it happens in Carcassonne... which also gives a visual cue to the player that the thing is completed.Anyway. I would definitely recommend Dorfromantik to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just the most ridiculously lovely and satisfying game I think I have ever played.Think classic euro board games like Carcasonne, but designed for a satisfying single player experience.it's beautiful, it's relaxing and it puts a huge smile on my face.Highly recommended, just go buy it, what have you got to lose?

My favorite thing about the board game Carcassonne is placing the tiles and seeing the "world" come together, I rarely actually care about "winning". This game brings that to life in video game form and throws in little quests to finish that award you with fun little tile upgrades. I absolutely love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very nice game when you just want to relax and not think too much. The tasks are relatively easy, and the challenges aren't too hard either, especially the first two-three tiers. I mostly bought this game because of the visuals - it was so pretty when I looked at the screenshots - but then I started playing it and it turned out to be quite addicting as well.Now to the not so great aspects. I had a small issue with it crashing on me in the first few days, particularly when I played it for about 4 hours (or more) straight, but it doesn't seem to be the case anymore. Also, the one problem I have with it consistently since I first installed it, is that the game has a tendency to freeze when I try to exit, and I have to force it to close. But other than that it works well, so I can let this slide.Overall I would definitely recommend Dorfromantik, I have fun with creating the landscapes and the issues do not affect the gameplay itself, even if they can be irritating.

_childDocuments_.review: The Early Access release of  comes almost a year after the April 2020 pandemic-inspired release of , which was a mere day before the start of Ludum Dare 46, the 72-hour game jam at which four Berlin-based game design students built the  for . At first glance, it might indeed look like  to players, but  and it's certainly not a clone.To continue the comparison, think of the road and city building of Carcassonne, but expanded in complexity. The six edges of each hex can have individual trees, fields, or houses, which you connect to form tile groups. Instead of roads, there are winding railroad tracks and rivers that  against matching sides of other tiles – constraining your designs. You start with a stack of 40 tiles and always place whichever is on top. When you're out of hexes, it's game over. Tiles can spawn a quest to connect either a specific or minimum number of its matching map feature together, like 100 trees or 25 houses. Occasionally that's followed by an additional quest to close off the tile group to further connections of that type. On each quest completion, you're given five more tiles, letting you play for longer. You score points for connecting edges that match each other, so that playing perfectly would result in a beautiful map. Of course, as the game goes on, filling map holes with the perfect hex becomes more difficult.The game picks three progression challenges you can work towards during your playthrough, like 25 sequential flawless tile connections (on all touching hex sides) or building an ultra-long river of 50 tiles; there are also special quest tiles on the outskirts of the map with a unique crown symbol that represent regular quests at a larger-than-usual scale. Both will reward you with new tile biomes, new tile types, and alternative reskins of tiles.Considering it's a permadeath procedural survival* puzzler and the meta-goals are making it through as many turns as possible, scoring high, and unlocking new content for future runs, I'm tempted to label it a . Of course, nobody forces you to, uhh, run. You can just hang back and watch birds fly by, or build new paths for your tiny little boat and your tiny little steam train. In , I often felt at the mercy of the available buildings, and obsessed over getting the maximum amount of points, which even meant remembering the best order for placing specific buildings. I had to plan ahead so often that I longed for blueprint outlines of future buildings. Here, I instead just focus on juggling my quest tasks, and scoring is more of a side effect of that.While  looks like it should be a deceptively simple matter of arranging hexagonal tiles to score said points, it's far from under-designed. That you're not under any immediate pressure to act doesn't mean you won't be racking your brains to optimize the arrangement of your last few tiles, desperate to complete quests and delay the inevitable end with another five or ten chips to play. The game logic that deals your cards is more of a reactive  than a 'dumb' random number generator. At the game over screen I usually know  which one or two tiles I should have used more wisely to reach another round of five, and the feeling that I cannot win with the tools I'm given hasn't really come up. In my best game, I made it through a handful of sequential  situations, finishing a quest or closing a tile group with one of the last two moves. Each time I was sure the end is near, yet just as sure that focusing and taking it slow could well get me another set of tiles to play. Good enough for #4 in the pre-release leaderboards, and only short  random railroad tile – of which I of course had at least one in the minutes before. Mea culpa!On the other hand, nobody forces you to play to win, to strive towards unlocks, or to go conquer online highscore leaderboards, either. With its mellow, calm music and pleasing aesthetics, the game lends itself to being played simply for idle relaxation, and that will be built upon with a Creative Mode the developers already announced for a future release. I've read numerous posts on social media where people express an interest in this game for  of goal-driven gaming. Usually I'm the type to focus on quests and securing unlocks for the next playthrough, but a few times I was so engrossed working on a mini-project that I lost track of the upcoming end and got caught completely off guard by it.To convey the titular atmosphere – the German word "Dorfromantik" channels something like an idyllic village life, free of worries and pollution – the developers have tried their hardest to keep UI clutter to a minimum. Unneeded complexity and feature creep are things they're very much wary of, hence they haven't implemented popular user suggestions like a joker tile (that connects with everything), the choice to keep a tile as a reserve for later, a limited-use undo button, or a UI popup showing exactly how many points you would score in the current cursor location. Adding everything but the kitchen sink would sure ruin the delicate balance they have maintained a year of careful tweaks.Expect to see more biomes and tiles added throughout Early Access. If you would prefer this game with a gamepad or touchscreen, it might be worth waiting for support to be added.Speaking of , it seems so many people ask the dev team to turn it into an economy management game / city builder, a 4X title, or to add multiplayer, that they even clarify on the Steam Store page that these won't happen. As someone who counts 4X multiplayer to my most favourite game genres, I totally get where those requests are coming from. The great visual style development studio Toukana's graphics guys came up with would be an amazing fit for a deep strategy/simulation/4X game. Other things you won't find here at least for the Early Access release that might put you off are that there are no campaign levels or pre-set scenarios with expected goals ("get three star rating"), there is no endless mode (playing to relax, without the sandbox freedom a true  implies), and it's not the kind of puzzle game where you can blaze through the progression tree / Steam Achievements (they're the same) in 2–5 hours and call it a day. In ten hours, I've barely collected a quarter, and those likely are the easiest ones to boot. While I definitely get a strong  feeling from the game, for me it's more something to play for an hour at a time than something to sink hour and hours into without a break.Unless you strongly dislike the very idea of procedural game worlds, of survival* puzzling, of needing to unlock content, or of only being able to progress towards a limited amount of goals at the same time, there's little reason to refrain from recommending this game.*: No, I wouldn't tag it a "survival" game on the Steam Store.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gives me the feeling of having left a puzzle on the living room table, but where there's no 'right' way for the pieces to all fit. There's a definite satisfaction is putting the pieces together perfectly, but there's another satisfaction in just laying everything down where it seems nice, and seeing what comes together over the course of the game. It saves frequently, so it's easy to pick up and put down at leisure, but I find for myself that I can get lost in it for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, it is a zen/methodically paced puzzle game involves you matching similar sides/types to other pieces. The game rewards you for building maps with as many perfect matches as possible while also fulfilling challenges such as X piece wanting to be apart of a 200+ house section, or a 400+ tree forest. I personally enjoy playing the game in the evenings or quiet weekend afternoons as a way to relax while having something to do (a lot of ADHD and ASD people struggle to actually relax or meditate, and for me this is really relaxing as it gives me dopamine for achievements, doesn't leave me alone with my thoughts, and provides flow-state). The music is pretty ambient, but there is no big sound cues other than those for achievements and perfect matches, so you can put on your own music of choice and not miss anything. The achievements are pretty in-depth and skill focused, so while the skill floor to play the game is low, it has a higher skill ceiling, which I like. On that note, there are creative modes, quick modes, harder modes, as well as a monthly mode with leader-board. Technically all the modes have leader-boards, but I find the monthly to be the most enjoyable and rewarding competitively as you are limited in space vs the hard mode which is just harder challenges. TLDR if you are looking for a cozy relaxing game, and enjoy the task of matching or sorting things for fun, doing puzzles, or other sorts of spacial strategy games, I would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

Strong one-more-turn-ness when I was on limited time wasn't helping.It's visually quite beautiful but the presentation is otherwise kind of bland. _childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a fun little building strategy and puzzle game. You place a bunch of hexagonal cards from your stack to build up a village. The game is over when you don't have any cards left in your stack otherwise it's endless.Let's say you have 60 cards in your stack. You're just able to play the first one but can see two more. To get more cards in your stack, you need to do little quests like connecting 20+ trees, houses, etc.Aside from that, you can do challenges like getting a high score of XXX, etc. to unlock new cards. Right now there are 10 cards to unlock and 3 different biomes. The main goal of Dorfromantik is to mindlessly play a relaxing game OR to beat your old high score and get a new one. Dorfromantik for sure is a fun strategy game. The graphics are nice and the music is relaxing. It's a game to cool down, play a short session here and there or while watching something. Without something to work for (unlocking something, scenarios to do, etc.) I can't pretend it's more. But that's not a bad thing. Dorfromantik is in Early Access and pretty cheap, so if you're looking for a cheap, relaxing, building strategy game - go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: Chill Game, No Real Point, Music Is nice but repetitive, Purchase while on sale.Long Version:Pros: It's a relaxing tile puzzle game. It is easy to understand the concepts and difficult to get good at. As you can see by the hours I've played it, I've put a lot of time into it, but frankly I'm not trying to be good at the game. It has a lot to offer for those who want to be able to take their time with choices they make. There's not a rush to get it done, and as such, I've accidentally left it on for an hour or two before realizing it once already. If you quit, you can simply pick it back up where you left off, or start up a new game. This is not a graphically intense game, so you should be able to play on lower end machines as well. Cons: If you want a game with a story, this is not for you. That I recall, there isn't even a semblance of a story to be had. The music also tends to get repetitive after a bit, and there isn't really any winning to it. While I don't mind this type of game, some people do seem to enjoy a more driven experience, so I felt it useful to put that here.Conclusion: Frankly, if there was a "maybe" for recommendations, that's what I would have put. It really depends on the factors I laid out in the cons section, but if you do get it, I recommend waiting on a sale, as there isn't a whole lot to the game to warrant full price purchasing. If you do buy at full price, it's okay, but it's better if you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: This indie game is more like a puzzle activity. You have hex tiles with meadow, fields, forests, and houses. You quickly unlock rivers and rails which increases the difficulty. Tiles can have "quests" which ask you to connect multiple tiles of the same kind. If you complete a quest (or finish of flagged areas) you will get more tiles to play with. Your play is limited by the remaining tiles you have.As you play you will get little notifications (easy to miss) to "grow" your tiles out towards. If you do, these become quests tiles for that session. If you complete that quest you get a challenge. Challenges cannot be selected, but you are given three to work on each game, from what you've unlocked. The challenges, when met, will give you powerful tiles that will always request a quest. Example: you may need to grow out to a white hex, reveals itself to be a tower in a city. That city then wants X houses around it. If completed you get a challenge. The towers want you to get perfect placements in a row (where common edges match other common edges). If you do this challenge in a game, you will get tower tiles added to your pool. Towers always ask for more houses around them, so they become a great tile to get bigger cities.Between the random tiles you are dealt, the challenges you aim to meet each session, and the charming aesthetic this game is a delight and will entertain you for blissful hours. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Don’t let the simplicity of this game fool you. You start out thinking it’s simply point, spin a tile and place it. Think again…. because with every tile you place, you take a step deeper into committing what you’re going to build next! Hidden behind the clean interface, and ease of use is a great little “thinking” game. The four students who created this game should be commended for identifying and building a game that hits a niche market. That is, a game that makes you think, gives room for creativity and best of all stays true to wholesome gaming, bypassing the insanity of constant combat, starving people or racing against the clock. Bravo!The game has goals, which are actually attainable and achievements come at a satisfying rate. Even better, there is “creative” mode (think sandbox) that lets you just go at it and build out a map larger than you would think possible. Is this game going to be for everyone? No. But, for those who want a game that’s challenging yet relaxing, you should give it a try. I look forward to the developers continuing to add on to this game, while staying true to its theme.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this genre of city builder lite and puzzle to unwind and relax, and Dorfromantik has quickly become my favorite in it. I enjoyed Islanders a lot too, but lost interest after there ended up not being much longevity to the gameplay. Dorfromantik gives you special tiles to build towards and unlock, different biomes to build through, and progressive unlocks to help gameplay not feel as repetitive, and so far it is working for me. Plus it's beautiful to look at even when your tiles aren't perfect.I'm looking forward to seeing more tile options and what else is added, but it's still worth it as is.Edit: Updates have added a lot more options to gameplay types and fixed any issues I had! Enjoying the new features added as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: In need of a really nice chill game? This game is for you.It is not a game you would play end to end in a sitting. It is one you would play it over multiple sessions when you just want to relax. GameplayIn the beginning, you start with a stack of random tiles. The idea is to match as many as you can together to expand your playing field. You will be challenged to keep the groups together to reap the rewards of more tiles for you stack to keep you playing further. The challenge then is do you close out a group, or risk it for further rewards. Also occasionally in game play, you will extend you tiles outwards and a greyed out special tile will appear approx 10 tiles from the current edge of your tiled map. If you build to these before your tile stack diminishes you will be given a new tile type.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game - its basically a flashy puzzle.  The shapes look like hexes but they work like puzzle pieces.  The game play is chill - it's got a sort of like solitaire card game vibe, where there is some strategy but its real mild and you're more so playing to waste time till work is over. ...BUT in the same vein, it can also invoke a bit of like minesweeper angst/rage when you get bored of playing it.This game does feel like an odd ball investment.  IMHO $10 feels steep for what amounts to a 2D puzzle, but I guess I have surprisingly extracted 38+ hours out of it... part of that might be idle time when I had to actually do work... IDK.Whether or not you will like this game probably boils down to how minimalist you like your games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a beautiful, slightly luck based, slightly strategic, challenging game. I only have good things to say about it, in all honesty.  This is not a game you will want to play if you are a person that goes for easy/fast achievements - I didn't get a score above 8k during my first 10 games.  The game has only become better as they have pushed updates, added content, and have made it even more of a challenge. I typically play this game once or twice every couple of months, casually. Its the type of game where you can put down and pick it back up without needing a refresher on how to play.There are very challenging mechanics such as absolutely zero undo function for accidental/less ideal tile placement, and also no way of seeing exactly how to line up a tile for a perfect fit unless you really just have experience playing and have learned what the different pieces are. It forces you to take your time, to be patient, and to focus. These key components make up part of why I find it to be such an enjoyable game. If you're someone who doesn't like these types of challenging qualities in a game, then this game is not for you. If you get frustrated easily, do not buy this game - you won't enjoy it. But for everyone else, I absolutely recommend this game. Its just fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting game about creating landscapes.You just jam the board full of pieces that have bits & pieces of forest, town & river pieces & after a bit of playing you get to look at the landscape you created & go "wow, did i make that?".Very replayable as you'll just keep trying to beat your own highscore, great time sink.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally soothing to me. I play this before bed and it actually helps to calm my mind. I suffer from bad insomnia, to the point where I'll just lay there staring at the ceiling. I learned of this game from watching DF and I'm just thankful it exists. Absolutely recommend this if you love puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: a really beautifully designed puzzler. very relaxed, no pressure play style. well done developers! it gets more challenging to find the correct tiles to fit to the present ones when the tiles dwindle and the goal to get new ones are at the edge of the possible - will the correct tiles appear to finish the quest?it's nice to see a student game at such a polished state and was a pleasant surprise to me. so far it's a really nice game and I think this is something that I can play for a loooong time again and again for calm evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It is an incredibly chill and relaxing puzzle game with lovely graphic.The goal is quite simple - you have to score as many points as possible by placing down hexagonal tiles while trying to match their edges and complete quests which gives you more tiles to place. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it.Works without any issues on Linux with Proton (9.0-2).
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Normally if I said a game put me to sleep, that'd be a bad thing.  But here is a game so peaceful, relaxing, and calm that it puts me in a tranquil state in which I'm okay with being a bit drowsy.  I dunno, maybe I play too many high intensity games.  It's a nice change of pace to just chill out with a game, have it give me a couple of goals, get some cool new tiles to place down, and just play for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like puzzles? Do you have OCD, and need things to line up?Do you love Carcassone, but sometimes wish you could get away from your over-competitive board game buddies?Do yourself a favor and get this game. It's an incredibly relaxing single-player puzzle game with dead simple rules. Match stuff up and make big cities, dense forest, vast farmlands, and long river and rail lines. To top it off, listen to some calming ambient music while you play. Absolutely recommended if the above sounds like your jam.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relaxing game and all, but as is so often the case with games like this, sometimes that's not enough for me. It's fascinating and fun to lay the tiles at first, but eventually, you get tired of it.I would like to see more different quests. There are basically two quest types, a) build exactly or b) build more. In addition, over time, the quests also become unmanageable because the requirements increase too much. That's okay, but especially in this later part of the game, you have practically no tasks left except! Very tedious searching for perfect spots.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple, fun and so very addictive, it's almost terrifying. It's also really easy to learn and to just jump into. Strangely enough, it can be relaxing  brain-wracking at the same time, which makes for something of a unique experience. The point, very briefly explained, is to place six-sided tiles on the map and try to get them to match with the tiles you will place next to them. You get points based on how well you achieve this. The more you play and more points you earn, the more special tiles you unlock, keeping things interesting. You also get to decide the pace. You can spend hours and hours creating that perfect landscape in the creative mode or you can choose to go for the more challenging game modes (which, admittedly, can still take hours). After a couple of days of playing, I'm quite certain this will become my go-to game whenever I need to scratch that itch to build or create something. Considering this game's immense replay value and low price, I would say it's quite a steal. Get yours now!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so. I love boardgames. Yes, the ones you play on the table with your real life friends, touching real life thingies and rolling real life dice. One of the games is carcassonne. But my friends don't really like it that much, also corona. I could spend hours placing tiles and making my own world maps. And this game allows you to do that. Endless (if u are smart) map making without the need of friends! Make a river, make a forest, build a city! Yay
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. A very pleasant diversion. Challenging, but not the kind that stresses you out. Just the thing to unwind with after a stressful day at work.Highly recommended if you like CIV or other building games (but without the conflict).I can't help but imagining that the towns are population by characters that look like Tim Conway's Dorf character. _childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a tremendous source of relaxation and joy since I got it. It straddles a very fine edge between being mellow enough that you don't feel bad for failing but addictive enough that you want to keep going. While I received my copy during a dev stream giveaway back during early access, I've since bought it for other friends because I love it so much and think everyone should try it out. Watching the small incremental improvements (undo button, my beloved) has been really great too. There have been many times now where I've said to myself "I'm just going to play for a little bit, I have things to do" and then before I know it, an hour or more has passed. It's so easy to get sucked in and just see if you can finish one more quest or clear one more flag. Random things I appreciate:- how the tiles fall into place as if they were real cardboard tiles- the animals!!! when the bear is sitting down it looks so cute- when you have several windmills close together and you get them to all point in the same direction- changing the biome options to match my mood- vaguely making up stories about the world that I end up with as I'm playing
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: What can you say about Dorfromantik that hasn't been said. Who knew such a weird name for a game, would work. It feels and looks like a classic video game or board game, but Toukana Interactive hits it out of the park with its simplistic entry. PROSPresentation: Beautiful animation that holds up in its simplicity and layoutRules: My kids loved it, simple and easy on the surface that can get away from you super fast.Control: Easy that a child can do it. Classic: This is as obsessive as any game I have seen in a while. Innovative: The simple rules are innovative as many card games struggle to do today.Future: Interesting to see how the build on this entry. What can you add to make it better.CONSRng: Can be frustrating in the necessity of getting what you need when you need it. Architect: My five year old knows how to build a lake better than I do. Ooi...Careful: I am not sure if Adults will enjoy this more than kids in the long run of replay ability, but I sure did. The con here is they can add to something that I believe does not need it. OVERALLI have to say, few games surprise me, but this one was a lot of fun. All three of my kids played it for a long while. It has a lot of positives and most important, no stress. There is not world to conquer, or faction or boat to save, just good clean puzzle fun. A steal. Toukana executed it wonderfully and you would find the price of admission well worth many of the classic board games in any store. A wonderful game. My final Score 4.3 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the most addictive and coziest strategy game right now. For puzzle lovers, landscape design lovers, low stakes strategy game lovers,. The soundtrack completed transported me into a meditative, focused and relaxed state (highly suggest using headphones). When I first saw this game come out, I was hesitant because I was afraid it would be repetitive like Townscaper. But I was easily hooked on this game as I continued to learn how to play the game through different strategies for increasing your deck throughout your build and unlocking beautiful biomes and skins. _childDocuments_.review: At first glance, Dorfromantik seems pretty basic. You place tiny hexagons on an infinite board, and you can get more tiles to place by following the game's rule set. Though after just a few minutes of screwing around, you start to realize there is a lot of thought and organizing, that has to go into your playstyle, if you want to achieve a higher score. It's weirdly challenging and relaxing at the same time.When putting every single tile perfectly, you can even go on without ever getting a game over. Here and there some small gaps start showing up, for which you haven't been getting the right tile yet, and I gotta say it's honestly so satisfying to get that specific one, you've been waiting for your entire run to finally fill in the gap.Though even, if you don't put a lot of effort in, you can still have a great time, building a cute village. Alternatively, you're also free to just build tiny cities in creative mode to go full Zen, and just construct a beautiful landscape or play a quick round with a limited amount of tiles.The soundtrack is just beautiful, perfect to relax or drift off for a little while.I'm very glad, I got this, when it released in Early Access, because of how cool it was to watch this game evolve to what it is now on 1.0 release.Highly recommended for anyone that just wants to wind down in these strange times that we live in.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: You might want to check the "Serene City-Builder Bundle", as it features quite a few quality products. Islanders has been a favorite of mine for some time, and while Dorfromantik doesn't reach the same great heights, it's nevertheless a really, really nice rogue-like tile-building game. You like the board game Carcassonne? Well, this could be the solo video game version. The art style, the chill vibe, the *fantastic* soundtrack, I can picture myself coming back to this once in a while. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a game developed and published by Toukana InteractiveThe game offers some nice graphics and environments, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the same and has a really great aestheticDorfromantik overall, however, is a fun game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a good casual puzzle game and to play in short bursts

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful, cozy, relaxing puzzle-sim game from Toukana. For the achievement hoarders, there is plenty to enjoy - whether it is the immediate numbers initiative (assimilate a pile of 500+ trees into a forest) that adds more tiles to your stack, the high score for each completed game, or the passive progress that carries over multiple games and unlocks new tile types and biomes, there is plenty to enjoy on varying levels. But when the numbers fall away, you are creating a little world for imaginary inhabitants to enjoy, and there is something cheerful about watching the subtle animations as trains and boats traverse the environment. The inevitable "is it on Switch" question will probably continue to plague Toukana Interactive over the next few months. Maybe they will embrace the challenge, or maybe they will just continue with small updates to the PC version for now. Either way, I'm curious to see what is next!
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik is a simple but beautiful game. You place hexagonal tiles to build your world. You can build for style, or you can follow the strategic side of things and see where it leads you. The strategy involves pairing similar tiles to earn points and satisfy requirements, such as having 12 water tiles connected, or 400 trees.It's so relaxing when placing these little tiles perfectly and building the greatest wooded area, perfectly formed railways and rivers and then… the demo ran out. So I played it again… and again and then I grabbed the game when it came out in EA. The art style is gorgeous and the easy play style allows you to effortlessly lose plenty of time to this game.100% recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most chill and laid back games I've played. You can play to push your puzzle skills and see how far your land can sprawl with limited tiles, or get creative and build whatever you like the look of in this tile laying landscape game. Even when the tiles don't go in your favour, the relaxing music keeps you nice and calm.

_childDocuments_.review: Meditative and interesting it still managed to grow into something both kinda dull and overwhelmingly big after a bit for me. _childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: Dorfromantik may be one of the most peaceful and relaxing games I have played in a very long time. The art style and the music blend well and help aid to its overall atmosphere.In terms of gameplay, it is very simple and easy to pickup/understand. You start each game with a procedurally generated set of hexagonal tiles and you earn points each time one is placed. Once you run out of tiles, the game will end.Each edge of these hexagonal tiles are tied to a specific biome: Forest, farm, field, town, river, or railway. Matching the edges of these biomes to other biomes of the same type will earn you more points.As you draw tiles, some may have large numbers on them that indicate they are a quest tile. These quests are tied to specific biomes and requires that you connect them to other related biome tiles. The number on the quest tile indicates how many connecting biome tiles are required to complete the quest. Successfully completing the quest will generate more tiles into your stack allowing you to continue to play longer and gain more points in the long run.I don't see myself playing this game super often as I usually find myself playing longform RPG's and grand strategy games but this is one I will always keep in my favorites list if I am ever in the need of something short and sweet to wind down or relax to.
_childDocuments_.name: Dorfromantik

_childDocuments_.review: For early access, it has a good amount of challenges and the right kind of pacing. If the dev team can keep adding this sort of meta-game, then this will become a nice high-score chase. Has all the joy of tile-placement board games and brings with it a good mix of strategy and chance. Highly replayable.
