_childDocuments_.review: i played the demo for 5 hours debating on if i should get this gameeventually i caved and decided to buyi will be refunding it.TLDR: its a passable time waster but for the pricetag its not worth it, 6/10Pros:1. its not yet another rhythm shooter that takes place in hell (seriously, can we pick somewhere else?)2. the gunplay is really nice3. decent base soundtrack, not great but fine4. abilities feel cool with the exception of the movement based ones which i'll get into in cons5. custom music is something you dont realize you want until you have it6. the art is really goodCons:1. enemies feel copy pasted or made artificially difficult through a gimmick2. bosses are pathetic and dont feel like they pose any danger to me3. dual weapons is pointless until you get a card that specializes in it or until you get a weapon that complements your primary4. (this is a big one) the movement is entirely pointlessyou can slide, dash, double jump, wall jump, wall run, grind on rails, use a grapple hook, teleport, ground pound, and ground pound into a jump to get a boost (likely missed some but thats all i can think of as of writing)you will use literally none of these and exclusively stick to double jumps and dashingthe movement is completely pointless because there isnt a reason to move like thisenemies will not require more than a dash to dodge from or a double jump to move above themit feels like they saw what ultrakill did and didnt realize WHY ultrakill has such deep and varied movement but shoved it into this game regardless5. (another big one) the custom music system is infuriatingthe ai that adds bpm will change is mind on a dime despite the song having had a consistent bpm for the past 2 minuteswant to tweak the bpm yourself? eat it. you have to manually decide when the bpm should start. dont have machine like precision to figure out exactly where it should go down to the millisecond? eat it. the bpm will slowly drift off beat.you cant even hear bpm changes via the metronome feature unless you save changes, confirm the track, then enter back into the track editorif the ai cannot figure out what the bpm is on its own just completely ditch adding the song because it will be completely unplayablethe only good thing i can say about the custom songs feature is that when it works (rarely) its addicting as all hell6. stages feel identicaleven if they technically arent every room blends together in a way that makes you feel like you arent making progressthis can almost certainly be chalked up to stages have a single uniform pallet7. you're either extremely underpowered at one moment or literally so unstoppable its boring in anotherif you can manage to find a good high level gun early on you've basically already wonbut if you dont then you're gonna be slogging through stages dealing with miserable kill times8. you unlock things via the dead cells unlocking systemthis is not a good thing.dead cells did not cook with this.dont do this.9. parrying feels forcedi dont parry when i actually need to, i parry when i'm told tomuch like the movement, the parry system feels like it was taped on because "idk man ultrakill does it and people like ultrakill so we should do it too"i like the idea of it giving bonus damage or some kinda special affect like it does right now but its just not enough justification to have it in10. this game feels like a campaign based game mangled into a rougelikethe rougelike mechanics feel extremely forced, as if to fill a checklisti wish i could explain why i feel the way i do about this point like i do with the others but this one is more of a gut feeling that i cant really pin down properlythis game has so much potential yet when i play it i constantly feel like something is just missingits charming, somewhat fun, i can listen to biscuit funk for 3 hours and still not get sick of ityet in a sea of rougelikes and rhythm games this game stands out in neither crowdi'll likely still play the demo as an excuse to listen to the songs i like while killing time shooting goobers, but the full game is a hard pass for me6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately too repetitive to keep my attention. Fantastic concept for a game, but the execution is lacking. $20 for 3-4 hours of gameplay just ain't it.>80% of the weapon and perk/upgrade roster is useless. Melee weapons are unusable because they lazily slapped contact damage on every enemy. Not only does contact damage take the flow out of the game, it's also lazy as heck and makes close-range weapons downright self-destructive to use. Most enemies HAVE melee attacks, why do they also need to do contact damage??Unlocking things takes too long. You can beat the game in a couple hours, and at that point you will only have unlocked 3-4 weapons out of however many there are in the game. However, most weapons are bad so you are griefing yourself by unlocking them anyway. They just blindly copypasted the Dead Cells system (which is a bad thing!), but then without the "scrubbing" mechanic that DC has, so if you unlock something bad you're just stuck with it forever.There is custom music, but the custom music creator is basically unusable. I'm willing to bet the devs have not tried using this one at all, ever. Seriously, don't even try making your own. The mixtape system and the track switcher are good, but actually trying to edit the BPM for a track is torture. Speaking of mixtapes, why do they just end without looping or cycling, and leave you quite literally dead in the water unable to fight back?Enemy and boss variety is low and uninspired. Most bosses are bullet sponges with the same basic attack pattern repeated 30 times. There are not many regular enemy types in the game, and most of them just feel annoying. For instance, the robot that turns into a homing missile when shot curves too aggressively so you can't juke it.There are only a few things affected by the beat, which is "parrying" SOME attacks, not all (actually just a quicktime event and not a real parry at all), and when the game will let you shoot. That's it. Your movement, enemy movement or enemy attacks are not bound to the beat at all. This makes the rhythm aspect feel disjointed.No builtin latency calibration tool, so god help you if you suffer from audio or video latency. My desktop setup has very little of this - others are probably not so lucky. I actually can't play this game on my laptop or TV, and I'm not even gonna TRY this one on the Deck.There is basically no tutorial. The tutorial tells you "Move with WASD, Shoot with mouse, jump with spacebar". Yeah no kidding game, but what does the door with a lightning bolt on it mean? How do I slide and keep momentum? Do I even need to? (the answer is "No", the copypasted Ultrakill movement tech in this game is literally useless, just dash and jump is all you need). How does a track's BPM influence the game's difficulty? Why is this kills reward door closed and won't open when it says I got 38 out of 25? Is that a bug or some hidden feature? Why do I need to join some random guy's Discord server and complete an entire "onboarding process" to get answers to any of these questions?tl;dr: this game is basically slop, taking elements from different games and mushing them together. There's actually a decent amount of effort into it, but the mechanics just don't mesh well with each other. I'm 50/50 on giving this game a positive or negative rating, but in the end I'm gonna have to put this one as Not Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, I can turn on the soundtrack to MGR:R in a game that doesn't suckBut really, this game is exactly what the rhythm shooter genre needed, its strengths aren't even necessarily because of good design (even if it IS well designed) it's just because the alternatives are just, not great?BPM is too kit-bashed with random assets and in general lacks a lot of quality from weapons to flat soundtrack to dull rooms to not very fun boss fights.Hellsinger is a close contender, but has a few problems of its own, the multiplier punishing you for getting hit runs in contrary to the enemy design that spams you with projectiles that can be hard to make out, the soundtrack's genre doesn't make it easy enough to stick to the rhythms, and good GOD does the game crash a lot, making you restart an ENTIRE LEVEL.but ROBOBEAT? It's cut to the chase, with a strong enough weapon roster shown off right at the beginning, focusing on the basics and how stats can be tweaked to make that feel better and full of variety without re-inventing the wheel or forcing you to use clunky unfun garbage, there's a lot of movement, but the game doesn't box you into spamming dashes or parries and also invites you to try and manipulate your movement in other ways like the wall/ground parry and recoil momentum.There's good sound and visual design that makes each hit punch, seeing and hearing enemy attacks is pretty easy, but the feedback to getting hit probably should be a bit sharper with the audio, and I personally recommend replacing the blinding static effect with a directional hurt indicator.Levels and enemy design go together pretty fluidly, never feels like you don't have enough space or have too much, or that the enemies don't work with the area you're in.The soundtrack is a bit simple, but unlike BPM it doesn't work against the genre, with the style and simplicity fitting the more electronic style.The worst I can say is that it's a bit easy, and that I personally don't like boss fights in any FPS game, and there's some criticisms to the custom track maker needing a few more features and a better way to detect beats, unless I didn't notice, there's not even a "tapper" to try and manually set the BPM of a track, but instead a clunky menu to add beats manually on the graph for the audio, which is hard to navigate through when it's confusing on how you're supposed to rewind the audio in the first placeEDIT: Apparently according to the developer response, there are options to have a "tapper" but it just wasn't very clear at first, so this isn't as big of a problem, and shortly enough might not even be a problem at all.Wall jumping can get annoying just trying to back up into a corner and now you're sticking to a wall, could there be an option to change the behaviour to only stick to walls while holding space or not at all for walls behind you? Can't say I cared for the story either, but it's at the very least a bit vague so you can kind of just skip past it and think about it again if I ever decide to care about it.And to any of the devs, if you're reading this, fix the jump so that you can add momentum to it, you can jump and then shoot with boosted recoil to launch yourself in the air, but not jump and shoot at the same time as you won't gain any momentum, it's a minor thing but it makes it feel very "natural" like it's Rocket Jumping.Also, I don't know if anything like this gets introduced later on (probably not), so I'll just mention it for now, if it doesn't exist, how about some two-handed weapons? maybe variants of existing guns but stronger and/or with a unique gimmick, for the folks who don't like the dual-wielding, or just some stuff that would work better with it, like a sniper that reloads every other beat, penetrates targets, and/or has an alternate fire mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Robobeat is super fun, being able to import your own music is really cool especially if you make your own. The music included in the game itself is also really good, but I'm sure you'll spend most of your time listening to your own tracks. So don't be afraid to give some of the in game songs a listen and see if they'll fit into any of your custom playlists.Gameplay: The movement is silky smooth, the strafe jumping feels amazing especially with the air control upgrade you can come across which I definitely would advise you pick up every chance you get (just don't double up on it unless you want to buzz around like a discombobulated mosquito). The guns are fun and varied, and while I don't personally like weapons like the ping pong and the cosmic, others main those weapons. So I can say with confidence there's already enough variation to suit many different people's needs when it comes to blasting bots.         The variation between rooms is pretty good too, with parkour, timed target shots, and others it gives you more to do with the good feeling gameplay than just shoot bots over and over again, which keeps it from getting stale.Overall if you like games like ultrakill, and you love music, you'll love this game. I can't really give it a fair rating since I haven't beaten it yet, but it's been keeping me coming back and I really enjoy it

_childDocuments_.review: If you like to take "blasting some music" a bit more literally, check this game out. Custom songs can be a bit tricky, and even annoying to get the mp3 files for, as well as get used to their tempos, as the game typically utilizes the overall beats per minute, or backbeat; but once you're past that, the game shines beyond golden. Tricks, stunts and showmanship earn extra score and some rewards, while still not being extensively necessary to play, allowing you to lean into more stylish yet hardcore gameplay over time; not to say even tonedeaf playing is easy, either.Legitimately one of the best games I have ever played, even with only this few hours clocked - if they continue to update the game, or add new content and features like more options and ways to decal, remix and design your cassettes and mixtapes, I'm going to lose my mind it's just that good already.Feel the beat.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game can be considered a musical shooter, its combat actually has depth and complexity that is only surpassed by swap heavy movement shooters like Ultrakill. Once you figure out the combo system, you will be clearing rooms in a single shot.  The sound track is top notch! However the fact that you import any music you have into this games it infinitely re-playable. I play Ultrakill A LOT, but I can't play it on my SteamDeck. Not because it won't run, but simply put the game is too complex for a controller. ROBOBEAT manages to keep the combat on part, but eliminates the swap combos for a static arsenal chain combos.  Making this the perfect controller game for those who are wanting a movement shooter on the go.This game comes with my highest recommendation!!

_childDocuments_.review: In game tracks are good enough for getting a hang of things but the real charm is the custom tracks and in that regard its hit or miss. Some tracks need just a bit of polish by using site to analize the bpm and then chosing the right beat (i would change "first beat" to the "chose first FIRE beat" as it was kinda confusing at least for me at the start) and then you can vibe to whatever you wanna as long as its mostly consistant  Its good, after 9h and beating the game i feel i still have space to grow and at the same time i have enough skills that i can adapt to things quickly. Some enemies are wacky (green turrets...) and parrying them is challenge on its own but some like the timer throwers or balls on death ones are where the mechanics shine. Melee enemies on the other hell could be deleted and i wouldn't cry. Sometimes you  want to parry and you miss, either because they missed you or you just were a bit away from their range. Utility is also great, hooks, teleports, airbone beams, nukes, finishers, its all usefull. I came here and saw dev live, (ngl, you rock.) But stage 3 and 2 revolvers was pretty much what i expected. Its not "jack of all trades, master of none" its "master of all trades". Aimbot, dps, solid dps, easy to use.From the weapons i unlocked and played with, only revolvers, this crit in air laser and spiny blade seem unique enough that when i see them with good passives i feel i am in god run. And even then i wish spiny blade had some combos and that more guns had 4 combos like revolver. Melee is... melee. Health is precious, on 4th difficulty level you dont even have a way to heal before boss and melee is just a wack. I tried to make it work but everytime i do i take chip dmg from enemies, idk if they hit me with punches or maybe colision is enough to take my hp away but it just isn't right. Why melee when you can kill a room in 3 shots with right build. Utilities are great but there is 1 issue - %dmg reductionThis stat makes me take even the most useless unitality if it has %dr. with two of them you can have in theory 140hp and 35hp heals. Add 15% dr card and its 155 and 40hp heals. Solutions:Make other guns either stronger in their game or more unique. How about making   - inheret enemy projectile and then you can use it against them?   – make enemies pick up the balls from the floor and amplify explosion and dmg based on amount of shots on enemy  – make them shock enemies (dmg delay tradeoff) and be like mines for a 10sek if you plant them on the floor  – charged shots make it bounce 10 times, increase base bounces to 3-5 and widen the beam so it hits easier. Also dmg multi per bounce. Make it fun, not tedious.   – each successful shot hits 1 additional enemy, charge 2 times to let hits hit the same enemy if there is no other enemies around.   – DMG. Make it oneshot with charge green turrets even if its 4 th stage and its level 2 gun. Its supposed to be a shotgun, it feels like a worse revolver.  – idk if each bullet deals dmg or if single bullet deals dmg (I hope it’s the first case), but dmg isn’t enough compared to other weapons. Also its just shotgun. Make it fire for 3 beats automatically after using it. It could make it a support weapon. Also you could make additional aliment – acid (like that one card) , that It would apply. – I love the design on it, I just wish it had combos like charged = charged shots of the weapon that hits it. Block = puts it in front of you to shot a gun with. Block+charge = spins to 2 enemies with huge dps and freezes them.   – Its just… wacky? On fast songs it removes beat, on slow its pain, it feels like it needs some kind of rework all together. Make it maybe fire as long as you are hiting beats and the longer you keep combo the faster it fires? Then block could be insta max firerate and charge would be a quick series of shots.   – honestly its alright, aoe, dmg good, fire application. Charge charge/block charge = next shot makes a puddle of fire would be neat  – decent, tho idk what shock does. Similar to flare gun with puddle of shock.  – Remove penalty. 15hp for one mistake is enough to make you wanna ditch it after 2 misses. Make charge + one beat = explode, charge + 3 beats = explode + pierce. Block+ 3 beats = explode 3 times on enemy (bosses) ALL MELEE GET +2-5 HP PER HIT/KILL. I don’t know what to change, knife throw seems a bit wacky but I guess with melee build it could be good.. but again too glasscanon for not enough gain. They are fine, wouldn’t mind more unique ones (double shot but 30% less dmg, charge after kill, killstreak bonus, remove dmg taken from 0.5% hp gain, remove +dmg% if 25% hp (if you want to be glasscanon there are dmg for dmg taken already), dmg in air, auto charge if not fired for x sec, empower other gun after x shots, next attack shocks/burns/freezes enemies after x shots from other weapon etc. dmg reduction is king. Make it baseline form 0 at t0 to 20% on t5. It will make you think about upgrading them while also reduces rng. Add more unique stuff to them like Freeze = enemies frozen by that explode/freeze last 10 sek/ killing frozen enemies reduces cd/+x targets etc.Hookshot = stuned enemies explode/additional stock/ longer reach/ grabs enemies towards youheartstopper = move normally during slowmo/invincibility but cd longer/ last longer/ killing during it heals youEtc.Some of them are perfect (bounce, dmg reduction for killing, burn on everything, both gun use) some of them are good (15% dmg reduction, dmg up) some of them are fine (movement speed, slow on slide) and some are awfull (walljump duration, freeze when hit, explode when hit, puddle of acid) I would focus on more of each except awfull. Also some kind of reroll reward in enemy rooms would be nice. Stuff like +jump, 30% crit chance, slow after parry kill, shops pre boss, repair radio, 1% dmg up per killsteak, A tier combos charge your weapon, upgrade your weapons by 1 tier, shock on hit, enemies are 20% slower, 0.5sek longer window for parry. Also allow us to chose which categories we want before draw.  Less melee or different placement. Make them deal less dmg or slower, idk. I wish it would be more about 1v1 with melee enemies. I wouldn’t mind a miniboss rooms where you have those melee enemies but with 3-4x hp but its 1v1 with you. When 3 guys with swords run behind you you don’t really want to risk 1/2hp to parry. Focus on stuff like timed parry enemies, orbs on death ones, make some enemy attacks more visible with some kind of alert right before shot for snipers. Or what I think would be nice – timer but not as forgiving. For example, green turret wants to shot – you get green shield alert and you have to LOOK AT THEM to parry their attack. It makes it more skillbased and less about running around and praying you kill them before they kill you. With all the changes I wrote game would be braindead easy – ye kindaBut ngl, with it I wouldn’t mind having them tankier, having some mods that you can chose on them at the beginning of stage like “attack set you on fire” “each attack you get increases dmg dealt to you by 10% for rest of stage” “reduced dmg after getting hit” “enemies disable you for 2sek after hit” “more enemies” Adding some elites wouldn’t be bad too with some kind of “releases orb after death”, “50% less dmg to other enemies” “faster” “throws timed balls” etc. Stuff like this will make every run unique, weapons would be unique and worth trying out, utilities focused on their ups and downs

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hell this is good. They took BPM and just improved every aspect. - Incredible shooting mechanics. Tons of movement options. Weapons that all have their gimmick and play differently. When you manage to overcome a difficult situation you feel amazing. It is quite difficult and chaotic though so not for everyone. I will say though that not all weapons are born equal. Some don't feel great to use, and seem very weak compared to the others.- Roguelite meta progression similar to Deadcells. You progressively buy weapons and upgrades over multiple runs and unlock them for subsequent runs.)- During a run you find weapons and active spells with better stats and different perks. The increase in power during a run doesn't seem as strong as in other roguelites, but I feel there might be some pretty insane combos I haven't discovered. - Cool music with some variety that you can change at any time depending on if you want to play with a faster or slower beat (the faster the beat, the faster you shoot, but the faster the ennemies act). Cherry on top, you can import your own music and play with your favorite tracks, so if you don't like the game's music you can play with the genre you want.The importing can be a bit tedious. The game tries to automatically recognize the beat in the song you import, but sometimes it doesn't work correctly and you must create the beatmap by hand. It's not too hard or long to do.- Interesting story and tons of secrets hidden around the map. The game rewards exploration with lore and new music to play with. The game also oozes styleOverall I give it a solid 9/10, this is truly a gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Wowowow. Where to start...So I've never really played modern-day boomer shooters besides a bit of Ultrakill (also a blast), but I'm a big fan of roguelike/lites and rhythm games. I was genuinely surprised at how this game blends the genres together. There was a bit of a learning curve for me to progress but with enough runs, I kept getting better, and it was a blast to play through each run. The custom song feature is surprisingly very fleshed out. The game's ability to auto detect BPM for custom songs is pretty darn good, considering. I'm on the final path at the point of writing this review, and the biggest concern I have is "what do I do once I beat the final path (presumably the game)?" I think there's enough replay value for me here to go back and keep playing either way, but it'll be disappointing to "beat" the game in my eyes, given how much fun I've had.

_childDocuments_.review: Not just is the gameplay loop solid AF, the ability to import my own mp3's and map them so extremely easy is a stroke of genius. What I absolutely adore is that all of the tracks are shown in the form of cassettes you put into a walkman. I don't know what it is, but it is immensely satisfying to add my own tracks and increase the size of my cassette collection.A small wish I'd had for the game would be to be able to set the bpm to visible for custom songs. I like seeing the bpm for the base songs, why not be able to show the bpm for custom songs in the cassette menu?Search for a bpm tapper online and tap the beat of your song. Then you have a bpm you can input for the song if the automatic function fails you. Or you let the song run in the editor and tap the 'b' button to the beat on your keyboard for the whole song.Do yourself a favor and don't miss this gem.

The in-game track editor is simple yet intuitive. Most of the time the auto-bpm function works like a charm! _childDocuments_.review: Still working through this one, got one more run to complete, but I feel pretty good about putting a review here.Outside of wishing that the custom track tool was more user-friendly (being able to manually set beats by just clicking along with the song would be cool), this game is stellar. It's a movement shooter in the vein of ULTRAKILL but with the rhythm system of Metal Hellsinger.If you're not good at rhythm games, don't worry, it's generally more lenient than those games since it rewards performing activities on-beat with a looser score system than Hellsinger. It's a roguelite, but clearing a run isn't dependent on your build at all. Enemies telegraph their attacks very, very clearly but still quickly enough that it feels challenging and fair. You could probably succeed with the starter kit if you're good enough, and upgrades along the way are just a bonus.The base game's varying flavors of EDM are great across the board, I haven't had any trouble recognizing the beat of any track even during hectic combat. If that genre isn't your speed though, you might chafe against the custom song tool since it struggles with songs that don't have a consistent BPM, and the interface for editing tracks is unfortunately tedious to use. The automated system is great when it works, but for when it doesn't, I hope the manual process is improved with updates.The visual design is like ULTRAKILL: minimalist but still stylist. The weapons all have a fantastic punchiness to their audiovisual design, there's a serious attention to gamefeel here that sometimes exceeds its inspirations. In particular, I love how it incorporates slow-mo and hitstop to sell the impact of parries and heavy weaponry. There isn't a lot of story, but what's there has a bit of charming campiness.Outside of the track editor nitpick, this one gets a big recommendation. It's a total blast to play, the design is well-considered all around, and it uses a bunch of stock Source sound effects. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Game very good, track editor needs more toolsThis game is incredibly fun, I've been seeing way more games incorporate rhythm into other genres recently and It's definitely the most fun I've had in recent years. The gameplay feels nice and the only real gripe I have with it is the massive lack of being able to restore health outside of clearing a specific room type or clearing an entire area (It just feels strange the way health is balanced). You always land on 1hp before the next hit kills which makes it feel both more fair and very intense.The soundtrack is also very nice and exceptionally varied, being able to switch tracks on the fly and go through every song you collect keeps the soundtrack from getting repetitive. That's not even including the fact you can add your own music to the game as long as you install the mp3 on your computer.There's just a few gripes I have with the editor that I want to voice, first being unable to change the beat mid track and having to manually add the tempo change. Secondly the note slider doesn't have a snapping tool making it harder to get things exactly on beat, and finally when you actually fix the song and it works normally, the tempo change is just so sudden you miss a combo or parry because of it.I already mentioned this in a discussion somewhere, but I'd really like to propose the idea of- Automating BPM (probably with the pre existing bpm set tool by drag selecting a section of the song to then only apply the automation to that section)- Grid snapping (to make all notes snap in the right place depending on a user set bpm based from the first beat of a song song)- Being able to add a count in on specific portions if there's a tempo change (similar to the Rhythm Heaven games and Rhythm Doctor)Even if these ideas aren't added the game is still a blast, if you're interested definitely give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best rhythm shooter I have ever played by far. 1) It is incredibly easy to add custom music. All you need is an mp.3 file of the song you want, and the game's built in cassette maker does the rest for you. You can put in you're desired BPM, so you can have you're song as fast or slow as you want. On top of that, you can make mix-tapes so if you want all of you're fast or slow songs grouped together you can do that without needing to switch songs mid-combat. 2) The community is already great. The discord server for this game already has many user-made cassettes that you just need to download, ready to play with. 3) The flow of movement is very nice, and I rarely get myself stuck in a corner or unable to move, movement is pretty much constant if you wish it to be. 4) The general mechanics go very well with this game. I love the game play loop with the upgrades you gradually obtain as you play. 5) The weapons are dope. I love spending time with each one of them learning their mechanics individually, slowly becoming with each one (my favorite is the bouncy one). 6) If you get a good mix-tape on, whether origonally from Robobeat or one you made yourself, if you get the BPM just right it feels amazing. I found the sweet spot the be around 170 BPM as my personal preference, but really anything consistent works very well. 7) I don't know how long the beta was available to play but from day 1 of the full game being released it's very polished and I can't say I have noticed any bugs in my 5 hours of playtime thus far.Overall, I'd personally give this game an easy 10/10. The progression of both my own skill/understanding of the mechanics and unlocking new areas/items is really fun to see. Definitely a game I will keep coming back to, can't wait to see what gets added in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally. This is the one.A couple of years ago I was introduced to a new game genre called rhythm shooter. I must've tried all of them and, to my surprise, there weren't all that many of them. On top of that only a few were somewhat popular like BPM or Hellsinger. Don't get me wrong these games were an absolute blast to play, making you feel like a bad-ass while shooting enemies in the face, on the beat while listening to some sick tunes. But for me there was always something missing.BPM, absolutely amazing but the graphics were a bit off-putting, I'm talking about the color scheme. Later on they added a way to add custom songs, it wasn't that straightforward but it was possible.Hellsinger had some really good graphics although if you weren't into metal, the music could be off-putting especially when there was only 1 song available per mission. Adding custom songs was a nightmare, to me at least. And again don't get me wrong it is still an amazing game. These are just some flaws I found while playing these games.Now Robobeat. Holy brother in Christ, this one has everything. All the flaws from the other games, not there. The game not only makes you feel like a bad-ass, you feel like a G O D.The music is top tier. There's so many tracks to choose from, you can change the song during play AND you can add custom music which is very straightforward, works surprisingly well.There's so many different weapons, abilities and perks that completely change the way you play, absolutely mental.and many more things...Anyways, a big thanks to Simon and everyone that's working on this game for showing us what the genre is really all about.Also why are all these previous rhythm games not more popular? I'm guessing feeling like a bad-ass is overrated or people are too busy modding their anime catgirls into Skyrim.I really do hope this game will receive all the attention and praise it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: I found the demo for ElecHead, I believe thanks to a Twitter post, back in early 2021, and was immediately smitten with it. The short experience was perfection, so I was very excited with the possibilities of a full release. The core mechanic is really brilliant! It creates for a lot of great puzzle platforming, with rooms ranging from straight-forward to alright-I-gotta-think-about-this-for-a-minute-because-it-seems-impossible. With a runtime of around 2 hours, it explores the fun concept without overstaying its welcome, but I can't help but say that I was hoping for more: more puzzles, more mechanics, more of that feeling I got when I played the demo. That's not to say ElecHead is bad by any stretch of the imagination. What it sets out to do, it does extremely well!  Figuring things out and exploring is always satisfying, and the presentation is enjoyable throughout, so it is well worth your time.
