_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant puzzle platformer with incredibly simple mechanics and a beautifully restrained four color aesthetic. You play as a small robot character with the ability to electrically charge platforms and obstacles by touching them, and shortly after gain the ability to throw your head in three different directions, allowing for shockingly diverse level design possibilities. Developer Nama Takahashi constantly iterates on established concepts in brilliant ways, and never ceases to make the player rethink every screen encountered until the obstacles are viewed in a different light, leading to a steady loop of satisfaction.However, there's also some minor flaws. For one, there are many transitional segments that force you to run through simple corridors that go on for far too long. There was also a questionably hidden (though not required) ability, as well as a long backtracking segment near the end that was oddly ill-conceived compared to the rest of the game. However, it stands as a fantastic experiment in effortless, effective game design.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: While I had an overall good time with ElecHead and I do give it a positive vote, I don't think it's for everyone. It's an adorable and clever game with plenty of unique puzzles, none of which are excruciatingly difficult, though a couple do ask for some precision and timing. If you watch the trailer and look at the screenshots and think, "I've got to get this game," your instinct is probably correct. For $10 or less, this is an adorable bite-sized adventure that lasted me nearly three hours to finish and another hour to fully complete.What I'm going to focus on here are the points that would make this a mixed review for me, and that potential players should be aware of. My main issues with ElecHead are issues that I tend to see from a lot of really small games like this: a game-changing feature is very hidden and impossible to know about without a guide; the game's collectibles that you'll backtrack for require redoing a lot of the puzzles you already did; and the options menu is overly simplistic to the point that it doesn't make a whole lot of sense.The game-changing feature I'm talking about is something that isn't shown in the trailer or anywhere else officially, so I'm hiding it behind spoilers.  This feature is not required to finish the game with its standard ending, but if you want to get all of the collectibles and/or see the secret ending, you  this ability because at least one of the collectibles requires its use. It also makes a couple of the puzzles I found to be particularly annoying a lot more tolerable, which makes me question why such a big thing was hidden away for only the completionists to find.ElecHead is a Metroidvania, which means you will end up backtracking through earlier parts of the game but with new abilities that unlock new areas. It's required to complete the game, regardless of which ending you get. This isn't a big deal and I'm a big, big fan of Metroidvanias, so totally fine by me, but the problem is the optional backtracking for the collectibles. There are 20 chips you need to collect for the secret ending and an achievement, and I missed half of them on my first run since I didn't want to spoil myself with a guide for my first time through. That was a mistake, because when I went back to get the ones I missed, I ended up doing a bunch of the puzzles again. I get why the fast travel system is set up the way it is in the game, but it does lend to problems with the idea of collecting everything without following a perfect route on your first time.The options menu is, quite honestly, really bad. There's no words. You read that right, no Latin characters anywhere. It's all iconography that you have to be able to decipher. Don't recognize a symbol? Don't understand what this specific symbol is trying to indicate? Too bad, there's no guidance, no descriptions, no labels, nothing. Just icons. Accessibility is a big thing the video game industry needs to work on; having a clear and easy-to-read options menu that anyone can understand is a huge part of that.That all said, these issues don't overshadow the game's incredible charm, awesome chiptune soundtrack, and clever puzzle design. Overall, I do recommend it, but it's definitely a rough package. I hope the developers will take lessons from this game and apply it to future work; they've clearly got the talent, it just needs refining.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Elec Head is a bit short (I beat it in 2 hours and took another 2 or so hours to find everything), but its very good. The puzzles are clever, the game feels really nice to play (meaning the action-y bits aren't too difficult) , and the art seems simple but it can be really quite beautiful. The soundtrack is also somehow simultaneously nonintrusive, but also rocks. It would come and go, but when the music would kick in I got really into it.There is one puzzle I wasn't the biggest fan of (because it relies on you stumbling across something really difficult to stumble across) but it was optional.Still, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels just right, no filler whatsoever, nothing wasted as every possible puzzles are explored in this game. Everything works well, had a ton of fun figuring out how to solve the levels. There is a moment when I had to repeat my actions couple of times thinking it was the solution, turns out the solution is completely different.Was not thinking enjoying puzzle platformer yet again. But here I am, first game I finished 100% since long time.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and clever puzzle platformer. The presentation and graphics is stylish and serve the gameplay well, and I especially liked how the game had no written text whatsoever (even the menu options are all icons).The difficulty is not too high, so you don't need to be a puzzle expert to beat it (but some of the puzzles for optional collectibles still forced me to stop and think outside the box).Time to beat was about 1 hour and 30 minutes for me, and a little over 2 hours to find all tracked collectibles and unlock all achievements, but there are some well-hidden super secrets I still haven't found.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best puzzle platformer I've played in YEARS, possibly ever (though it's hard to compete with Celeste and VVVVVV, but this is certainly in that tier).  The mechanics are simple in the sense of what you can do, but that concept is  with a few meta tricks thrown in to keep things fresh.  There's a collection element for those who like fully exploring the entire game, in addition to some other extras for the diligent. I had a blast from start to finish, there was never a "I want to stop playing this right now and do something else" moment.A couple of quick notes to wrap this up:
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games are a form of conversation between player and designer.My brain starts to picture these sorts of exchanges whenever a puzzler gets interesting. This is important, because ElecHead is the most intellectually dense conversation I've had with a puzzle game.Like most of the "puzzle greats" ElecHead is an extraordinarily simple premise: you conduct electricity through anything you touch. At first it's deceptively basic, but screen-by-screen the twists keep coming. The sheer number of interesting puzzles Nama Takahashi was able to create with such a narrow toolset is a testament to his creativity as a designer. The game might "just" be 2 hours long but every puzzle finds new ways to test, surprise and delight you. ElecHead is a conversation that doesn't waste a single word.ElecHead also has sprite graphics and chiptune music that seem simple on the surface but there is a surprising level of detail and great talent on display in these self-imposed limitations.It all crescendos to an ending sequence that you'll find yourself replaying over-and-over in your head – like any good heart-to-heart.The delightful irony of all this? ElecHead doesn't actually contain a single word.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely charming little adventure with lots of puzzles and secrets. I'd definitely recommend it, even for those who aren't as into puzzle games.While I appreciate them committing to the bit, the settings being textless can cause problems, specially the video settings. For anyone else who may be interested in playing: 4th option is fullscreen or not, 5th option is pixel scaling.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a joyous puzzle platformer and one of the best hybrid puzzle games I've ever played. It's an incredible demonstration of hiding things in plain sight - I especially love how most platforms have visual gaps in between them that the character can't fit through, to make the actual hidden passageways stand out less. If you are super observant, you are rewarded greatly - and if you aren't, or don't care to look for things right away, you aren't punished. As for the puzzles, it's all quite easy, but no less creative or interesting than if it were harder - and the difficulty ceiling prevents frustration. Some rooms near the end of the game (or for the super secrets) are genuinely awesome little enigmas.The music is wonderful, and contributes to the flow of playing the game, even when backtracking in an empty room or while retrying a platforming challenge.In short, it feels like a flash puzzle game from the golden age, fully fleshed out and with grown wings.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little indie puzzle platformer. After more than a decade of playing all sorts of puzzlers it is hard to find innovative and original games. I heard only good things about this game but I was surprised by the quality of puzzle design in ElecHead. it is short but it introduces so many fresh ideas and it doesn't waste your time by repeating same puzzles often.You can also find some optional secrets but even that has it's purpose and that is a second ending.I like the retro look and the music is very well made. I would recommend this great game to every puzzle game fan.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformer. My biggest critique would be that the game is too short. The difficulty ramps up well, and the solutions are satisfying when you figure them out, but for seasoned puzzle-platform lovers, this game may leave you wanting more. I would purchase a sequel in an instant. Also, I recommend playing with a controller rather than a keyboard, as the movement with the primary game mechanic (no spoilers) was more intuitive that way. Another nitpick is that the menu is a tad confusing, though the design choice does avoid any need to translate! Would recommend this game and I am excited for whatever game Nama Takahashi comes out with next!Edit: Also checked out the developer's itch.io page and really enjoyed the other two games I found there, if you're as into this developer as I am!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Nice short game with cool puzzles. What I noticed is this game is really good at pushing you towards the solution with its level design and making you feel smart, introducing things just in the right way and making the sections very clutter free. The art style and OST is nice, nothing more than it needs to be.One unfortunate thing is, the secret that allows you to 100% the game is either something you'll find by accident or miss. It's a cool secret but there's no clear visual hint or really anything apparently that could let me find it. Unlike the collectables, you cannot see what 'chapter' the secret is in, so you cannot narrow down the place to search for it as easily. It's not fun to just bump into walls for hours.It also looks like apparently everyone I saw play or talk about this game gets confused by the lack of text in this game and the use of only iconography for the UI, specifically around deletion of the save file VS leaving the game. It looks like several people will just accidentally delete their save file.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is the new gold standard for Puzzle Platformers. Every puzzle is just so meticulously crafted. They're bold, smart, creative, and most importantly, fun. Add to the package a stellar soundtrack and multiple endings, and you have a masterpiece here, future puzzle platformers are going to have to measure up to the new king here.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly short, but quite enjoyable puzzle platformer with a neat core gameplay idea. It did felt a bit underwhelming in player ability department, but it does a good use out of mechanics that are present. However 100% achievements of it is a bit... frustrating. Due to the 35 score minigame achievement, as that minigame is pure RNG, hence you can luck out (like me) and get it fairly fast, or spend an unreasonable amount of time trying to reach that score.Overall worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Best puzzle platformer I have ever played.  Better than Braid, Limbo, Inside, VVVVVV, Thomas Was Alone, Fez, anything you can think of. The levels are incredibly elegantly designed, but if that's all it was it would be worse than Braid.  It is every indie dev's dream to make a game this focused and clever.  Nay, clever is not the right word.  Genius is the only word befitting of such a perfect game.I will say that I didn't think it was this good at the very start, but I also didn't think Undertale was this good at the very start.  ElecHead eventually gives you everything you could want.10/10, perfect game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Elechead is almost all puzzle-platformer killer, almost no filler. You play as a cute robot that can electrically charge everything you touch and everything those things connect to. After a brief tutorial showcasing many of the tools and hazards and how they’re affected by you, you get the ability to detach and throw your charged head while your discharged body is able to run around freely (within a time limit). From there the game does as you’d expect by mixing, matching, and tweaking all of its elements into puzzle rooms, but Elechead deserves praise for being easy to parse thanks to its simple visuals and limited color palette. Combined with strong puzzle design, I would hesitate to say I never felt stumped while playing, it was almost always me going “What?” *beat* “Oh!” the way through. If there’s any real flaw with the game, it’s that if you miss any of its secret collectibles (that are actually required for the ending), you’ll have to backtrack through at least some puzzle rooms, but thankfully very few of them are laborious to redo. A more subjective problem is that you can easily finish the game in less than 3 hours, but to me that just means that it doesn’t wear out its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game! Masterfully crafted puzzle platformer, highest class in game design, simplicity and visual communication.I highly recommend it to you if you like puzzle platformers - or everyone who values incredible tight crafted games.I'm looking forward to the next game the developer makes <3
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a minimalist indie puzzler with such a smart central mechanic used in novel ways throughout.I like to imagine ElecHead is a Mega Man boss getting his own adventure, and the 4-color almost game-boy art style of the sprites and tilesets suggests maybe the creators were cheekily thinking the same.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Very neat and tightly-designed puzzle platformer with emphasis on both the puzzle and the platformer, just the way I like it. Definitely feels a bit short but everything that is there is really damn good, so I can't complain. I think some of the super optional special secret palettes are hidden in dumb  ways but you can get 100% achievements without them so whatever, the way the game is structured and the mechanics and the polish and all that are all there in spades and it's definitely worth your time to check out, maybe on sale if you must but, play it, yeah
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid puzzle platformer, following the template that I enjoy a lot: One main gameplay gimmick (your head electrifies any platform it touches, and any that touches, and so on), a few puzzle elements that interact with it (blocks appear or move, or lasers fire), and then some clever explorations of that gimmick without overstaying its welcome. The graphics are cute and easy to read (and extra palettes are always a nice touch) and the chirpy music is fun too.The regular game was quick but satisfying, with clever and unexpected use of its own mechanics, and took me about an hour and a half. Finding the alternate ending took about that long again (my play time is inflated by leaving the game open while I ate lunch), and was definitely more challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: its definitely on the short end (my 97 minutes elapsed was enough to play the game start to finish, albeit not 100%ing), but this game has some fantastically clever and unique puzzles, especially near the end. 100% worth it. nice pixel art, fun music and great sound design too! my only complaint is that the lack of any words extends to things like the settings menu, which makes it a little hard to understand- however, the game itself is a great experience!(edit: after writing this review and looking online, it appears that there may be even more extra puzzles/etc than i had assumed- others seem to estimate 2-5 hours of playtime, so i'll definitely be going back to look for more!)
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This game totally took me by surprise. I was recommended by an Indie channel and it just blew me away in every regard. The pixel art is beautiful, the chip tune soundtrack does a great job of building on the familiar melody, the puzzles are so well crafted and so fun to figure out that I never once thought to look up a solution even when I got stuck a couple times. The only gripe at all with the game is the length, I 100%'d it in about 2 and a half hours and gladly would've taken more. Can't wait to see what this dev does next.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little puzzle game. Not super complex but not a cake walk. Every puzzle is unique or a twist of other puzzles, which keeps the game fresh until the very end. 100% completion is not needed to finish the game, but the quest for 100% will make you discover secrets and puzzles that are separate from the main path, adding an exploration element to the game. The story is super simple, kinda interesting but not super deep.My only complaint is the need to abuse broken game mechanics to get that 100% completion, especially because you'd never discover these exploits by playing the game normally.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have much to say besides the fact that this is a VERY clever game with clever design all around so that the player has fun. The game is pretty short but ALL of its content is very very good.The music was very good as well as literally all the art and design and I can't recommend it enough.If you like little puzzle platformers I beg you to try this one!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely appealing puzzle platformer with a pleasing aesthetic and a banging soundtrack. The game really succeeds in executing novel puzzles that make me feel clever -- even as someone who plays a lot of puzzle games -- while remaining a sensory treat at the same time.  The only nitpicks I can put against this game are its strict adherence to icon based user interface and one frustrating puzzle solution. As to the first point, as you will likely see in other reviews around this one, there is a reset save icon that many people mistake for an 'exit' button, especially since it is the final icon on the game's menu. When the icons do work, and they do for the vast majority of the time,  they contribute to the game's significant charm quite well, but it could be smoothed out in places especially with the reset button, perhaps by changing the button to be different or to take the 'save reset' functionality and put it into the environment where it could be better explained though the game's screens or context clues what your action would do. As for the one mechanical qualm I have with the game it would be a mechanic involving  This mechanic wouldn't have irked me so much if it were hinted at better environmentally  Still, this was not a necessary screen for progression but it did lead to me trying to invent movement techniques for longer than I'd like to admit. These are small nitpicks that don't take away from an incredible and well-polished, although short, experience that I would recommend to everyone. Easily worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: As a quick summary, I completely and wholeheartedly recommend ElecHead. I think it’s worth the price of entry and if your video games tastes are anything like mine, you’ll have a lot of fun with the game.To get a bit more detailed, ElecHead is short, sweet, and feels like a callback to a style of game that I don’t see as much of anymore. I saw someone else compare the game to VVVVVV (6 Vs), and I think it’s a pretty apt comparison, but they’re still quite dissimilar in a lot of ways. ElecHead’s emphasis is on platforming and puzzles, without any semblance of a story. You’re a robot. You need to go forwards. That’s all you need.This is just my personal preference, but I think the limited color palette and near complete lack of text makes for a very endearing atmosphere. Throughout the game you’ll unlock different color palettes to choose from as well, which I think is always a bonus.I didn’t 100% the game, I might in the future, but I experienced the bulk of the content and it took me about 2 and a half hours. I think for the price that’s a fair deal, and the bonus content can probably give the game another half hour or so, maybe another hour max.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful bite sized puzzle platformer. Elechead has intuitive puzzles that are tricky but not terribly difficult. The music and sound design are also top notch. The ability of the game to teach the player how to solve puzzles by showing rather than telling was unparalleled and the best aspect of this game. Of note, It took me around 3 hours to beat it blind with most of the collectibles and messing around with a minigame. Players who are more interested in just completing the game or are more clever than me (not difficult) will likely beat it in less. This said, there is very little filler in this game and it was a lovely experience start to end. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is the smartest platformer I have ever played. The main mechanic is used in tons of different ways and the level design is top notch. Every time I figured out a puzzle, I felt pretty clever after it. Searching for all the collectibles was fun too, because they were always hidden in a way that you only saw them, if you paid attention. I adored the 2-Bit art style, the pixelart animations and loooooved the chiptune music! The game is put together very well and inspired me to do something similiar in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best finds of last year - a perfect puzzle platformer! The simple movement is responsive, putting me in control so any missed jumps always felt like my fault and not the game . The collectibles added the right whimsy and additional challenge. I wanted a lazy Sunday puzzle game, and this knocked it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Absoultely love Elechead. Originally played the demon on itch and the full version doesn't disappoint. Ingenious puzzle platformer where you play a little dude/dudette with a battery for a head. Everytime he touches something he infuses it will electrical charge which can be used to open doors, fire flames etc. You can also detach his head and lob it for max shennaningans. Deserves to be mentioned in same breath as Stuffed Wombat's "Qomp" and Nifflas' "Ynglet" as stand out micro-indies this year.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: + Minimalistic+ Very clever exploiting this minimalism+ Very tight puzzling, no filler, no overstaying his welcome+ Some really really good "a-ha" moments- To me, not as memorable as other puzzle contenders, like Patrick's Parabox or Baba is You- Almost zero replayability after finishing it Definitely, absolutely buy it... but wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle platformer with a neat central mechanic.  It is a little bare bones visually (what you see in the screenshots is what you get in terms of art) but still aesthetically pleasing, and the soundtrack and sfx are well done.It took me only 33 minutes to reach the ending, but I think I found it way earlier than expected, since I still had over half of the base game that I hadn't explored yet.  After finishing up the rest of the base game content + getting all the collectibles required for the bonus ending I clocked in at a little under 4 hours in game time.  So about the right length for the price point, although I could see a non-completionist run finishing in around 2 hours or less.Some of the options in the pause menu are a little confusing since the game sticks to a "no text" philosophy.  Specifically it should be noted that the last option in the pause menu is "delete your save", so don't pick that one accidentally.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Although short, this is an awesome puzzler with simple but nice visuals and some really clever uses of its straightforward mechanic. The secrets are well hidden enough without being too hard to find, the "aha" moments of solving some of the later puzzles are really satisfying, and it's just a great game across the board. If you don't like how short it is, get it on sale, but otherwise I'd highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: The mark of a quality, efficient puzzle platformer is how limited a tool set it can provide while still offering up a plethora of "Oh, THAT's how I solve this!" moments and a minimum of frustrations. Elechead is a legitimately perfect game by this criteria - you play as a robot with a head full of elec, charging any surface you touch and any machinery connected to it with electricity. There is approximately one (1) upgrade you receive early on allowing you to displace your head from your body. The verbs are run, jump, and toss and despite those restrictions it doesn't recycle a single puzzle over the few hours needed to complete it 100%, even as it moves recursively through itself to present challenging new rooms tucked just behind the old. Can't recommend it enough.(Don't mind my long-ish playtime - this was a perfect game to play while uhhhh definitely on the job and not often swapping to its window to solve another room or two.)
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is a pretty (and) fun puzzle game. There are many different paths you can take wherever you are in the game, some hidden, some only apparent as you play through the game and unlock more abilities. There's even an ending that you can only unlock if you completed everything else.That being said, the game is very short (2 to 5 hours to complete 100%). Wait until it goes on sale to buy. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I got interested in the mechanic and wanted to try it out, but turns out the game was also all-around really polished and wonderful! The puzzles are really clever, it's fun to play, and the visuals and music are spot-on. I recommend warmly, it's a great game!The only thing is that while I appreciate the attempt to create non-textual menus, I *did* accidentally delete my save data when I wanted to just close the game, just literally seconds after completing everything 100%. Didn't matter for me much, but I recommend being careful with the menu!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome puzzle platform game. The gameplay is super smooth and fun, and the levels are clever. The game has a cool hidden secret you can access near the end of the game. Maybe there are more secrets that I missed?My only complaint is that the game is way too short. It's like a tiny taste of what could have been an epic adventure. I wished there were more levels to dive into and enjoy. Overall, this game gives you a memorable experience. If only it was longer, it would have been a masterpiece. But still, it's a must-play for anyone who loves platform/puzzle games. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions are pretty negative - mostly centred around the interface. The interface depends on cryptic icons, including an icon that wipes out your save file - the meaning of which I only discovered after wiping out my save game.The puzzles are mostly okay but too arcade like for me. At times I knew exactly what I wanted to do but it took me ages to execute the controls with exactly the right timing. I should have paid more attention to the action label.I got about 3/4 of the way through the game and got stuck. I lost interest at that point, which I almost never do when I am that close to finishing a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Elechead is the best puzzle platformer I've ever played, full stop.The super simple rules are very intuitive but lead to such an incredible depth of possible mechanics. I found myself cackling at so many of the puzzle solutions from the very start.It's nothing short of innovative. Do not sleep on this.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A simple puzzle platformer with novel mechanics. It's short (I completed main story and most collectables in ~2hrs), but I'm much happier with short-and-varied than long-with-filler. Overall it was too easy for me, but unlike most times I say that, I still quite enjoyed it: most solutions to the puzzles can be executed in just a few seconds once you figure them out, so even if many are too easy it doesn't feel like they're wasting your time in between the harder ones. I'd thus recommend this to genre aficionados of all experience levels.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: The game has six levels, lasts around three hours or so, and it follows two very simple mechanics to create some fairly clever puzzles; basically, your head has electricity and everything around you is a conductor, so you have to figure out what to power on -or off-, in order to get past a lot of the puzzles and obstacles.Up until the last room of the last world: the sixth one; I had loved the game, but then, the developer thought of doing something different for the conclusion of the game. You get two endings, one requires you to collect every cartirdge available in each level; there are about 20 or so in total; the other ending, requires you to backtrack to the first level whilst going through a multitude of different hidden pathways.I checked guides, forum posts, and about the only one I found to be useful, was one where people where vaguely talking about not understanding if their game was broken, or if this ending design was a deliberate choice: I don't understand why game devs do this, in an attempt to trying to make their game more cryptic and special, they ended up turning it into a slog for me; as an end result, I ended up refunding the title. It's a shame too, because other than this, it was a nice game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.user: neizod ネイゾッヅ 黒猫
_childDocuments_.review: The core idea & mechanic of the puzzle is really good. However, I think the implementation is somewhat to one the extreme that makes the game unenjoyable sooner or later.Many puzzles are timing puzzles. That's fine. But the implementation require almost exact timing. Like, do this in 10s or die, but traversing the puzzle already take 9s. At this close, it'll be too blur line between "I know how to solve it, I just misjump!", and "should the puzzle really must be solve this way?". This issue is worsen in later harder puzzles where they're intentionally designed to deceive the players to go with the first solution, but the correct way is to re-evaluate the whole situation instead.This game also like to deceive players in other aspects. Like having a lot of hidden walls, which is not a bad idea if implemented correctly. But hidden walls for the main quest??? I think it starts to smells fishy.Another annoying part, comes in three-folds, is the navigation. The first fold is that the inter-level design doesn't allow backtracking. Complete some level and the door will shut behind you. To play previous levels, the player have to teleport to the teleport hub. But then, the second fold, is that although this game doesn't have an intertwine map like the metroidvania genre, it still have branching paths to the secret. So if the player make a wrong decision on which path to take, they will miss the secret and forced to progress the main quest. Which bring to the third-fold, the teleport hub. There are too few and too scattered. If the player miss a secret at the very end of the subarea, then they have to redo the whole subarea from beginning, without anyway to skip the previously solved puzzles.But the most unforgivable part is that the developer name the first encountered teleport hub as the "teleport no. 2".  Seeing that, one instinct might be trying backtrack to find the teleport no. 1 (don't forget that the game have branching path, not a linear path that confirm there's nothing to miss). But we can't go back far since the door is lock already. And we can't teleport to the start of the game either since it is not a teleport hub. Turns out that the teleport no. 1 is behind a hidden wall right after the start room, which can actually be backtrack from teleport no. 2 when you learn about hidden wall in later area of the game.I try to assume good faith from people. But, as I've seen too many wickedly crafted deceptions in a game this short, my conclusion is that the developer is just a troll. Which will not only result in a thumb down from me, but also a withdrawal to support these kind of indie developer in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: While the gameplay is really clever, I just hate when: - you have to headbutt every single wall looking for "hidden passages" that are mandatory for progressing in the game - the game makes me scramble through the entire map multiple times to collect all (in this case 20) "trinkets" needed to actually finish the gameI unfortunately don't have this much time to spare and I really hate that I would have to go through the map several times looking for hidden passages. The idea is very clever, but these are just unnecessary gimmicks.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a 10/10 for me:-Nice puzzles that are not hardcore nor too easy-Some precision platforming that is not infuriating-Controls are smooth/fluid-Music is excellent-Reasonable amount of secrets to discover, it's nice that the game shows how many are left on each level-Love the pixel art, minimalistic but beautiful - It's like you are playing a great NES game, specially if  you turn on the CRT effect.I want more of this!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: 🔳 Essential - buy it NOW☑️ 🔳 Avoid Time to finish – 5 hours to 100% on Steam DeckAny technical problems? NoneWorth revisiting? No✔️Some of the solutions are very clever but not too obtuse, so as they are still solvable without a guide.❌Game feels a little too short. I was ready for a couple more levels at least.Overall – Cool little puzzle game with clean graphics and a catchy soundtrack. Throw in some fun to get collectables and the odd minigame and ElecHead is a great time, if a little short.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is a unique puzzle-platformer that explores the consequences of having an electric-powered head and how it can save the world! Generally, I found that the puzzles can be solved after a few seconds of thought or a few tries. However, the most compelling aspect of the game was finding all of the secret rooms. They are hidden throughout the game and the map gives slight hints for their existence; The game demands thinking outside of the box for 100%-ers. The game is short, although I enjoyed the length. No aspect of the game overstayed its welcome and fresh, unique puzzles await at each room. Extremely happy to have found this game and played it through.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Watching the gameplay trailer for Elechead had me really excited. However it wasn't the puzzle game I thought it was. Instead it's a very short game that starts off feeling linear but you quickly lose sight of the end goal. There is very little info on what to do, and the player is left trying to wander around finding 20 chips without any real direction. The menus in the game are made up of only symbols and it's difficult to tell what you are navigating without trial and error. To beat the game requires you to wander aimlessly looking for hidden passages, walls that are not really walls, and floors that you can fall through to get to other areas. I did manage to complete the game due mostly to my hard headedness and determination to get my $8 worth of enjoyment but it required finding a map posted online and watching a few bits of a youtube guide. If the game had a map, some direction, and more of the puzzles to solve it would be wonderful. As it stands now it just isn't what I thought I was buying and I wouldn't consider it a game worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to recommend this game for its mechanics and puzzles,but then I remembered I saw this nasty image:Game has more such screens:What's even worse there is an achievement for finding all tu*d rooms/screens:That's why I don`t recommend this game.ib4: "These rooms are taunting you" and/or "something you need to figure out."1) Poup is not funny2) Mega Man 1-6 managed to be a good platformer without such "funny" screen. Crash Bandicoot™ N. Sane Trilogy also did not have to resort to toilet humor.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent little platformer. A deceptively limited moveset is revealed to be more layered than you could imagine, with clever, intuitive puzzles made more impressive by the fact that there is no dialogue, exposition, or anything except a few visual pointers on the control scheme. The sheer number of secrets and collectibles are well-hidden, respecting your intelligence and awareness without ever feeling unfair. Top it off with a wonderful soundtrack, charming graphics and a running time that doesn't overstay its welcome and you have a very worthy adventure to bring back the light.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: While simple at it's core, ElecHead gets a surprising amount of depth out of its main mechanic, and those "a-ha" moments were plentiful throughout. It's not the longest game (only about 2-3 hours) so that may be something to consider when deciding whether to purchase, but I never felt like anything the game was trying to waste my time. Sometimes short and to the point is exactly what you're looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the most elegantly charming indie games I have ever played. An easy-to-understand, yet impressively flexible gameplay premise that goes a much longer way than you would expect it to as well as having a surprising amount of secrets and collectibles, all while without telling a single word.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much. It's very charming, the challenge of the puzzles feels just right, finding secrets feels extremely rewarding. It's short and sweet and I promise you you'll enjoy playing this while you get cozy. To say anything else would be to spoil this game for you. I'd argue this game is very much for everyone.Play ElecHead, its a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: , cute little game, that’s it, it’s perfect.After a planet-wide blackout you take control of Elec, a cute lil’ robot with the ability to power up machinery with touch in this strange metallic world.The main gimmick of this puzzle game is that Elec is a living battery, powering up everything that it touches to interact with the various game elements as you’ll traverse each level towards the ending.The selling point is how simple and effective the graphics and aesthetics are, one color to indicate what has been powered and another when at rest.But the real selling point is how damn clever this little title is with the implementation of its main mechanic and how many times it can subvert itself to stay fresh without being complex save for the more “secret” levels where you’ll have to really work for that extra ending.Maybe too little content, and no story other than what the steam store gives you.But on the other hand, adding more would make the game feel needlessly bloated, so this is a non-complaint.Short, simple, clever, good.That’s ElecHead for you!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I probably spent way too long playing this game, which is much more complex that it seems. In ElecHead, you are a cute little battery-headed character that solves fairly simple platform puzzles to advance through 7 areas of the game. I'm not sure I would have ever completed this game if it wasn't for the help of the guides on Steam. The power-ups are well-hidden, so congrats to you if you managed to find them without assistance.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I am not what you would consider a gamer.  I like to play 20 minutes at a time, casually, every few days to pass the time.  This game, however, changed all that.  As soon as I started playing, I was hooked.  I played it for 6 hours and completed it in one day.The puzzles are brilliant, the control is as smooth as intuitive as it can be, the game world sucks you in, doesn't waste your time, doesn't go into deep cutscenes that nobody cares about, doesn't have a plot.It's just solid gold gameplay that has you thinking outside the box at times, challenging you at every turn with brilliant game design.The polish is surprising, this game knows exactly what it wants to be and executes it to perfection.Some reviewers treated its "short" length as a downside, I think it's a huge plus.  I hate games that take too much of your time.  If it's gonna be this good and this addictive, I like it that it can end in 15 hours or less.  I really wish they made more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did. The main mechanic is honestly pretty clever, and the game has a strong start and a great soundtrack!But first impressions can be deceiving.The puzzles at the end of the game are such a chore to solve with how incredibly esoteric they are, and I had to look up a guide on how to solve them. And when I did, I didn't feel stupid for not figuring it out, I felt dumbfounded, wondering how someone's supposed to solve them without resorting to tedious guesswork. That's never a good sign. Also, some of the late game platforming sections get frustratingly difficult to the point where I start to wonder if the reward for going for 100% completion is even worth it.It was not worth it. There are better puzzle platformers out there, skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Short fun puzzle game. Takes about 4 hours to "100%". I put that in quotes because for some reason there isn't an achievement for getting all the visual filter collectibles that tend to be harder to find than the base collectibles. A lot of the puzzles have really creative solutions.The only thing I didn't really like about the game was finding secret areas that were impossible to beat without a secret power-up (which you get no indication of how to find, you kinda just slap your head against walls until you happen upon it). One of them is technically possible to beat without it and since I didn't know about it at the time I tried doing the super precise timing on it for like 15 minutes before giving up. I think areas like this should've been given a specific symbol so you'd know not to bother. Backtracking for secrets can also be fairly annoying since you'll typically have to restart that zone from the beginning. Though this isn't the worst thing as zones are fairly short when you already know all the solutions.Also in case it wasn't already clear, this game has a limitation placed upon itself where it cannot use words at any point in the game other than the title of the game and credits. This isn't really an issue at any point though, but I could see some players erroneously selecting the trash can icon in the main menu to delete their save by accident, though the game makes it fairly clear what it does.By the way I hope you like seeing turd screens, because the dev is a certified troll.TL;DR 4 hour cute puzzle game with some annoying parts, personally would wait for sale before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Found this game to be highly fun to play and it stands out from other puzzle platformers by being fast as well as clever.  It is not all action or all puzzle but both fused together intriguingly. It also has unusual mechanics I've never seen before in a 2D platformer which is icing on top of the cake.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much to be said of ElecHead really. It's a short, decently paced, somewhat tricky puzzle platformer. Once again I find myself frustrated at the blatant padding that is making you replay whole sections of the game to find a collectible you walked past the first time, but at this point that's basically standard in these games. I want to like the little twist at the end, it's a cute idea that plays with non-linearity more than puzzle games usually do, but it honestly left me feeling really dumb for a good half an hour, thinking I'd made a completely pointless excursion when I was on the critical path. As much as I admire the desire to make a "pure" puzzle game with no text, sometimes it's just obnoxious. When you refuse to put words in your options menu (I'm not kidding), then maybe you've taken it too far.Frustrations aside, it's still a cute game that does a pretty good job of intuitively teaching you its mechanics then bending them to their logical endpoint. Some dodgy moments aside, ElecHead is a fun way to spend an evening.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I think I really enjoyed this game. And I had been looking forward to buying and playing it ever since I saw the initial trailer for the game concept. The achievements are fairly easy to get all of them and exploring the mechanics. And playing through the game was really fun. I would really love to see more levels from this game. Especially ones that are more difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It's a perfect balance between puzzle and platforming. Sometimes puzzle platformers become "I know the solution but the execution is tedious and difficult." Elechead never does that, at least for me it didn't. The ability to throw your head around as a power source leads to a lot of surprising moments and mobility. I would love to play more of this.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a seemingly simple game with a creative mechanic. But the level design is very well done. It shows you how a simple mechanic can create so many puzzles and makes you think differently. It's full of secrets, and small bits and pieces that make you smile. I can see a lot of thought and heart went into designing this. If you like puzzle games, I'd say this is a small tasty snack.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is an incredible game. It utilises its simple moveset in a myriad of different ways, and builds the player up to the more advanced puzzles. A lot of out-of-the-box thinking here. It's definitely short (I got all achievements in 4.4 hours) but if it were longer it would probably risk overstaying its welcome. The game executes its concept long enough to fully explore it without it becoming tired or repetitive. This game has some of the best level design I've seen this decade. Although, one small negative is that it also has the worst option menu UI I've seen this decade as well. The game's minimalism is nice but it didn't need to continue into the settings.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the best games that I have ever played. It's able to deliver incredibly satisfying, rewarding, and challenging puzzles without telling the player a single word! The art style, music, and sound design are all the same great quality as the puzzles. I cannot recommend this masterpiece enough.UPDATE: After finding every single collectible in the game, I can say that some of the color pallets are a bit *too* well-hidden as the player isn't really given a visual indicator when, say, a color palette is hidden behind a wall. I really wish there was a count for how many color pallets you had collected, as well as a corresponding achievement to help those who want to collect everything blind.My review still stands, though just be prepared to look up a guide if you truly want to 100% the game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: An ingenious puzzle platformer that, like all of the greats, is devilishly simple in its premise but iterates upon just a couple of mechanics to deliver a truly unique experience. Some players deride the short length, but for me the two hour playtime is the sweet spot. Sure, there could have been a couple of more mechanics, a boss fight or two, or a little story to flesh out what's happening. But sometimes, for me, idea and the aesthetic of a game are enough. And for that, Elec Head delivered.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty freaking awesome game. Most of the puzzles get the noggin joggin and are very satisfying to solve. This game is pretty short, but I'd say it's worth $10 I got both endings after 4.4 hours and I'm only missing a few cosmetic items.                 <<<<<<  !!!
