_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent little game! It has a very good mechanic idea (the head of the character activates electric systems), and the game uses it in so different and astonishing ways, that's incredible! The riddles are full of good ideas, even using the off-screen! But I won't tell you more to not spoil you.And last but not least, the game knows when to stop, and doesn't try to be artificially longer.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very charming ittle puzzle game. If you take anything from this review, it should be that. It has great art, great music and sound effects, and good puzzles, albeit puzzles that are a tad on the easy side of things.That said, the puzzles on offer are still very well designed, you will feel stumped for brief moments before grasping the solution, and a wide variety of different mechanical concepts are explored throughout the game.I find this game very easy to recommend, both to long term fans of puzzle games, but also (and perhaps especially) to newcomers in the genre. This game appears to be extremely friendly to people who might not really play puzzle games, and while still providing a decent challenge.I only have two complaints. The first is that I thought there could have easily been more hard puzzles at the end of the game. All of the puzzles are well designed, and I wouldn't remove or change any of them (except one, which is my second complaint). But it feels like there were a few mechanics that were under-explored. I feel like the game needs an additional 15% or so of content to really fully utilize all of it's mechanics.My second complaint is that there is one puzzle in the game that I found to be very frustrating. The actual puzzle is very cool and interesting, but executing the solution requires very precise platforming that I ended up retrying over and over again, long after I had actually "solved" the puzzle. Thankfully, this puzzle isn't required for anything in the game, and completing it only rewards the player with an additional color palette option, so it's not that bad.Expect around 2-3 hours to complete the game (depending on how good you are at puzzle games) and an additional hour or so for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool concept for a puzzle game! The execution was really good too, everything felt properly tutorialized and built up, with a solid difficulty. I wish this was a bigger game.I feel like the game could probably use a map, back tracking for collectibles was kinda confusing.But I really loved the fact that I had to backtrack, a side scroller puzzle game is something I wanna see more.I didn't go back for the filters I missed since they didn't count for completion and there was no marker for which area they were in, which is a little upsetting.The super Secret clip out of bounds area was kind of silly, wish there was a reasonable way for the player to find it on their own and if the mechanic there was utilized longer, it made the game feel unfinished with that added in, showing what more it could be. But solid game regardless.The credits music BANGED.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually one for puzzles, but this game is truly fantastic. It's a very simple game, but it's also one that masterfully maximizes its core mechanic. The complexity builds throughout the game, but never abruptly. The player will be presented with a very simple design of a new twist, and then things escalate. You never are thrown into a complex situation while being completely clueless and uneducated on what the game wants from you.As far as collectibles are concerned, there is one type that is used to unlock a secret ending and there is another type that is purely cosmetic. The cosmetic collectibles are significantly more difficult to both locate and obtain, in my opinion, and probably are only of interest for completionists.I did not ever need to view a guide for a standard puzzle that stood in the way of progression to the ending, and I did manage to find all of the basic collectibles on my own, but I did need guidance to find the "secret upgrade" (which is, unfortunately extremely obscure and also mandatory for the alternate ending, as far as I can tell) and I also used a guide to locate the general locations of the cosmetic upgrades that I missed on my initial playthrough.One of the downsides of this game is that, inherently, it is tedious to travel throughout the map in post-game or completionist efforts simply because virtually every room is a puzzle, and you have to therefore solve previously-solved puzzles again repeatedly to search for secret rooms you missed the first time through the area. The "secret upgrade" can be used to cut down on the time demands of many puzzles, but it still is far from just sprinting from room to room like you would in many games.Overall, despite the inconveniences associated with 100% completion, I can't recommend this game highly enough for anyone even remotely interested in puzzle platforming. It truly is a masterpiece in the genre as far as I'm concerned.Oh, and yeah, it's short. If you manage to beat it in under 2 hours, don't be a scumbag and refund it after you had a good time. If you didn't like it, that's one thing, but if you did, it earned your few bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A very well-done puzzle platformer with an open map.  Several of the main blocks that prevent you from going to later areas too early are only a lack of knowledge of how to proceed, knowledge that the game teaches you very skillfully.  It's just fantastic game design.  I beat it in two hours, and I'm no speedrunner.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I remember actively following the development of Elec Head through the developer's twitter, and loved the concept. It was nice finally getting around to playing itI love how the puzzles really make you think outside the box, and make you pay attention to even the smallest mechanics of the game, there isn't much variety to the puzzle elements introduced but the game uses the ones it does have to their max which is always fun. I do wish the puzzles were a bit more difficult thoughWhile a lot of people compare it to VVVVVV due to how nostalgic the music and more simplistic art style, it reminds me a lot more of the puzzle flash games I grew up on then the Atari era design V was based on. The music is good, the art is too but it gets a little dull after a while, it would've been nice to see more mechanical details like the dead Elec Heads laying around, or a backdrop for the different areas, it might've helped build up what story there was a little better tooIt's a lovely little gem for anyone who enjoys puzzle platformers. As many others will point out the game is short, it takes about 2-3 hours to 100%, which doesn't bother me but at $9.99 it might not be worth it unless it's on sale. But if you do pick it up, I doubt you'll regret it
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming little puzzle platforming with a rare case of creating both interesting challenge on a execution and puzzle level. Excellent endgame, though a second ending is locked behind a secret I really have no idea how you are supposed to have the instinct to look for on a blind playthrough. Still a very excellent, short time though, a real treat.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: is an ingenious retro puzzle platformer with a simple hook and deceptively simple design. It's a strangely addictive time with an inspired high contrast aesthetic akin to another indie, . Although, these games have their defining differences. Mostly in the fact  is through and through, first and foremost, a puzzler. Simple at times, complex at others. You're given a rather simple move set, and small set of rules. You conduct electricity, and that powers whatever you stand on or more specifically whatever your electric head touches. You can throw it, and even super secretly you can give it a rocket boost. But that's all you can do really. But somehow, each problem requires a solution that ends up feeling spontaneous, and at times, miraculous. Allowing you the buckets of gratification even if it really was the only way of doing it. It's smart, but not defeating, or overwhelming. You're eased into things before you're let loose again. All signs of intelligent game design that most tend to get wildly wrong, but not this game. A really good puzzler and simply put, a great time. I only wish there was more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is a quintessential puzzle platformer with a stylish presentation and minimalist storytelling. The puzzles along the main path are largely about execution rather than brain-burning complexity. However, after a couple hours the game starts becoming extremely secret oriented which is really not my preferred style. That said, this game is unique and exceptionally well-executed.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun short game.Every room is a unique puzzle with a fresh solution or fun twist, with using the same simple mechanics but solving it in hundreds of different ways.There's like, zero texts in this game to explain anything whatsoever. You kinda just go along with the game and it's great that way. Not that it's confusing or anything.It is like REALLY short though, even 100%-ing the game only took like 3 hours.Honestly I don't know if I wish it's longer or not, I think the length is great given that the base mechanic doesn't change too much. Maybe it is better this way for it being this short.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game as a fun little gimmick, with good audio and visuals to boot. The electricity mechanic was fun to solve puzzles with but started to get stale by the end of the game. There are also enough secrets and other unlockables to keep you playing for awhile, but I'm happy with the 2-ish hours that I spent on it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformer. I liked the way the puzzles were designed, the solutions always felt satisfying. The platforming was only tied to the puzzles and was never tied to difficulty in execution. I did not however enjoy that secrets, and sometimes even progression, was tied to hidden things without anything pointing towards them.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A bit short for its price but still very fun and engaging puzzle platformer. Each puzzle room has its own unique implementation of the game's main mechanics and feels very thought out. There was only one room that really stumped me, and it was because I was misinterpreting a hint that feels obvious in hindsight. The game is designed in such a way that even if you're stumped, you're likely to eventually find the solution by just screwing around if you don't figure it out yourself - which happened to me a few times.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: With so many puzzle-platformers on the market, it's hard to find one that feels genuinely fresh these days, and yet ElecHead somehow manages the feat. This is a genuinely excellent puzzle game with a unique mechanic I haven't seen before; the electric head that you throw to activate platforms and other devices.The difficulty is fairly moderate; it might take a few minutes to figure out a solution, but there's mostly nothing here that feels frustrating. Overall, excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun puzzle platformer that I had a lot of fun with. There are 2 endings, the first is more straightforward, but he later is harder because some of the late puzzles to get the unlocks get REALLY hard and require some real out of the box thinking so just... keep that in mind before picking this up. If you're a more casual puzzle game player you may need a guide or assistance as they require some really out of the box thinking, the last one I needed to beat the game had me stumped for like a half hour.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles were fun.I got my $10 of fun from this game, but it's definitely not polished.  Very lazy programming.  The menu is just a bunch of confusing icons with no text descriptions.  I got to what looks like the end of the game, but I'm not even sure if I beat it or not.  The sound track is just as lazy as the rest of the game and sounds like what they call "Earth Music" in that Rick and Morty episode.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game but way, way, way too short and simple. Most of the puzzles are very straightforward and simplistic which leaves you wanting more by the end. I think I only actually had to stop and work out a solution two or three times in the whole game. If the game was like $3 then sure it would be fine, but definitely didn't feel like it was worth the full price or even half off.Really wish the game had a lot more going on. Both with new mechanisms and challenges and so much more. The general concept is great, but it is sadly too straightforward and simplistic in the end. Rating would absolutely change if they added more content and maybe a level editor. But as it is now I'd say just go for a different puzzle platformer.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Really tight puzzle platformer with a a great mechanic that's pushed to the limit. Some of the secrets in post-game can get a little obscure and exhausting, but I think the main part of the game is where it really shines. Great level design and fun puzzles, definitely very worth it! If you like VVVVVV or Celeste, I think you'll like this game a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Would buy Elechead on sale ($7 or less). Elechead will teach you how to do something, and then make every possible puzzle off of it. Its design is very economical by doing a lot with a very simple concept; it will milk every possible mechanic in every way it can think of, leading to very minimalist, satisfying ideas. I found myself being surprised at a lot of the puzzles in this game, and it's pretty surprising how this game seemingly isn't reviewed by many. I can't fully recommend it at full price because I think it's too small of a game, but it's still worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played in a very long time. Things that I liked: My only complaint about this game is that there isn't more of it. I beat the main game in about 2 hours and got 100% completion in about 3. I recommend this to not only fans of puzzle games but literally anyone who wouldn't feel disappointed by the length to price ratio.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Only one real complaint, and that's 100%'ing this game is rather cryptic. pretty much all of the game's puzzles don't require any sort of walkthrough. But trying to go for all secret chips required a quick trip to YouTube. BUT, other than that one bit, I must say, this was a satisfying little puzzle platformer! It utilizes it's mechanics quite well, and was delightful from start to finish. It's a fun little bite sized adventure. And I recommend this to any puzzle/platformering fans.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformer. The visual presentation is great, and the palette swap is something I wish more games could include (Downwell is a great example of this). It sounds great, and the controls feel great. It reminds me a lot of the old Nitrome games I used to play when Flash was a thing. I like that some of the actual platforming provides a challenge. Sometimes these types of games lean too far into the puzzle aspect while neglecting the platforming aspect. The game was a little bit shorter than I anticipated, but it was a good time while it lasted.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully done! It's incredible that after nearly 40 years a developer can still create a game in this genre that feels fresh and takes on an identity of its own.Each room presents a challenge, with puzzle-platforming that left a player like me who has played this type of game for decades unsure of how to proceed. To manage all of this while only introducing one upgrade in the late game demonstrates how fleshed out the concept is. Though not quite as long, and lacking in story, I hold this in high regard with the original Shovel Knight campaign in terms of 2D quality, albeit a much different style of platformer. Highly recommended and great value!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game with a good mechanic that it keeps building off of. It never quite explains everything so you’re forced to figure things out on your own, but it’s never too difficult. If you get “stuck” it might just mean you need to try a different tactic or something later will help you. Visuals reminded me of NES Mega Man with more contrast. Movement, animations, SFX, and music… all good! Enjoyed playing! Thanks for making it!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Immaculate. Underappreciated. A video game in the purest sense. I found myself smiling and laughing as I played through each of the just difficult enough puzzles - many times going "There is no way I'm solving this" to "Holy crap I did it!!" in a matter of minutes. Though I believe the dev pushes the full limit of the electrifying aspect of the puzzles in this, I'd love to see an expansion on the idea in a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Solid little puzzle platformer where your head (unsurprisingly) generates electricity.The levels are cleverly designed around your body/head powering anything you touch with a head throw thrown in to add to the complexity. Overall it's short and sweet with some added secrets here and there and a neat soundtrack too. A masterclass in its genre. If only it were a little longer!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A short and simple platformer game with a unique concept, it may not be much stuff but ElecHead nails the definition of a good, short platformer perfectly.The gameplay is, as I said, unique. Your head is a power of electricity that can be collided with walls and platforms to progress through levels. A couple additions will add your control to the next level, or should I say, just ahead. There are no levels, a few checkpoints to warp to and simple endings that even a baby could understand. What I also like about this is that this game doesn't rely on text, like at all. Everything has a unique symbol so literally everyone can understand. And also, this game is super completionist-friendly, You can complete this in a single session, it's easy but not too easy, and it makes you think just that little amount. A PERFECT GAME for those who like platforming and want a short and simple game to pass time.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun, brisk game that is worth the price. The puzzles were usually pretty creative and gave me a satisfactory “aha!” when I figured them out. The color schemes and pixel art were perfectly simple and pleasing to look at. It worked perfectly on the Steam Deck!(Ignore my playtime as I played the first 4+ levels at 30 FPS without realizing it… I just thought Elec was meant to move that slow lol)
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead has a brilliant core conceit to its puzzles which I haven't seen done anywhere else, where your character's body acts as a power source for everything it touches (which can both help and hinder you). It's short and sweet, but still gets the most out of this concept, regularly bringing in new power-ups which change the way you interact with the world. Regularly challenging yet not frustratingly so, the difficulty of the game's puzzles was the perfect sweet spot for me.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: That was a really fun, simple yet challenging puzzle metroidvania game.Taking the electric conductivity mechanic to its fullest, you have to make your way through different obstacles that will make you ponder for a while about your positioning and timing while going back and forward. Each one of them teaches you about a different mechanic and without making use of a single word. Not even the achievements nor the menus have them, yet they convey all they need in a sufficient manner.Regarding the presentation, it might not look like much but it delivers what it proposes to do in its pixel art fashion, mostly in the few instances the background gets the spotlight. The soundtrack is also something to be noted, but in a more subtle way, having a few variations here and there while also staying mute in very particular rooms. No worries about the few colors offered as there are some palettes to be discovered around the map... in quite the obscure locations but still.In short, if you have a few bucks at your disposal and are in a puzzle/metroidvania crave in a bite sized package, here’s an enticing choice.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: a fun little puzzle platformer with very creative solutions to its puzzles and a touch of metroidvania-like level design, but a little short in length for the price. i beat the game's main story in an 1h44m, and after finding all the collectibles, only clocked in at 3h33m. there are also the optional pallet swap collectibles, but as of writing this review, i have not gotten them.a pretty nice short title reminiscent of games like Tower of Heaven. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle design, clean presentation, and a nice length that doesn't outstay its welcome.It's easy to think you know what you're getting into from looking at the pics but the game always managed to pull a surprising spin just when I'd start to get comfortable.A classic indie game through and through.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game! It's a very neat puzzle platformer that has simple controls but uses them in unique ways for the many puzzle rooms. I only got stuck one time (3rd or 4th to last puzzle) that I had to look up and go "How was I supposed to figure THAT out?!" The music is a treat as well. It definitely gave me some VVVVVV vibes, definitely worth a playthrough!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting mechanic which is explored to the fullest. Tightly designed puzzles which slowly reveal the possibility space of the main mechanic. Lots of delicious "aha!" moments. A showcase of expert puzzle-action design.Clean, minimal and attractive graphics. Nothing feels superfluous. Almost everything interacts with your abilities.Smart icon-based, text-less UI.Reactive ambient soundtrack which was very much to my taste.3 - 5 hours of playtime, depending on whether you want to find everything.Shockingly good!
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best designed puzzle platformer I've seen in a while. I can only think of a couple puzzles that were kind of bs, and they were hidden side areas to get optional color swaps for the game. Besides those, the game has a super smooth progression. The game wrings an amazing amount of complexity out of a simple set of mechanics, as each room makes you really think about how the electricity and head throwing mechanics actually work. Just pure puzzle platforming fun the whole way through
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Masterpiece, made by basically two people.Short with not much replay value but I'm happy to pay for this game and piece of art.WARNING: this game is tough as both a platformer and a puzzle game.WARNING: literally impossible to beat without walkthroughs/guides.This is because of secrets and not just fake walls (of which there quite a few).At 4 hours I basically beat the game outside of the "impossible to deduce" secrets I mentioned.Walkthrough playtime is about half an hour including all collectibles and endings.I expected a more casual game with a few easy puzzles, and despite being wrong in the worst possible way, I enjoyed the process of making progress.Not counting the impossible secrets, this game has some of the best puzzles I've seen in a game because they are logical and clever rather than just throwing a million things for you to calculate or being braindead, they are nicely in the middle.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game during the Indie Nintendo Direct the other day and was surprise to see it on steam. Snatched it up this morning and its fantastic. Good yet not too hard puzzles, controls are great, sound track is amazing as well. Lots of good shovel knight vibes as well. If you just want a platform puzzle game this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely entertaining puzzle platformer with one of the coolest mechanics I've ever seen. Puzzles start off simple enough, but by the end there were some that genuinely had me stumped for a bit. However, those "AH-HA" moments when you figured a puzzle out were very satisfying. The soundtrack also bumps super hard which is always a win. My only criticism, if you can call it that, is I wish it was longer because I enjoyed it so much. The fact that this came from a one-man dev team is amazing and I hope he makes more games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: One brilliant puzzle mechanic, perhaps not completely wrung out for everything it's worth, but widely and cleverly used and finely sharpened to a razor's edge. It's not long unfortunately, but at the same time it's not a game that's meant to be. An absolute masterclass in level and puzzle design, teaching through play. It rewards you for learning, for noticing, for applying, and for thinking outside the box. Though it's not a metroidvania, between the aesthetic and main mechanic, it has major Gato Roboto vibes, another short and sweet gem. I wouldn't be surprised if someone on the dev team previously came across that title.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this! ElecHead is short, but crams in an enormous amount over its two hour gameplay time. Its visuals are crisp and clear and the concept keeps developing steadily to keep you entertained all the way through.Plus, the level design! Quite exceptional at its very best. A sequel would be more than welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mindful that I might end up writing something that takes longer to write and/or read than it would take a person to just play the entirety of the game in question, so, short and snappy. Here goes!ElecHead! It's a puzzle-platformer which establishes a tiny handful of core mechanics in the first, like, 4 minutes, pats you on the back and throws you at a series of challenges which are solved through the clever use of electricity. I really like this style of game design: nothing against the alternatives, of course, but I really enjoy games which hand you a small number of central mechanics at the start and test your growing understanding and mastery of them over time by only changing the environment in which they are challenged, rather than serving you a slowly expanding set of skills.Nama, the game's developer and designer, clearly established the central mechanics available to the player early on, because it's really impressive how incredibly well designed the challenge in this game is. The game is given a genuinely satisfying and enjoyable difficulty curve through level design alone, gently introducing new environmental hazards and mechanics at a pretty even pace, which all tie in to the central electricity mechanic that the player has direct influence over.ElecHead is really a masterclass in how to do so, so, so much with so little; I felt like I was still learning more and more about the game right up until the finish, and having an absolutely wonderful time with the process of learning the entire time. Also, it needs mentioning, Nama has a really delightful sense of humour that comes across in the mechanics and some of the smaller details of the game (including one particularly devious puzzle that I won't spoil).There's some really nice environmental narrative stuff going on, and a particularly entertaining secret ending that's a reward for some fairly enjoyable secret hunting. The soundtrack is really nicely composed, and complements well with the process of thinking your way through some of the trickier puzzles that might have you stumped for a little bit; but it's never a tiresome experience, overall. There's even some leaning into some interesting meta-mechanics which I feel were used sparingly, and really show an interesting lens on game design. It all comes together and, in a sentence, produces a really interesting and compelling gameplay experience with so little chaff and a huge amount to love!Nama is absolutely a game designer you ought to keep your eye on.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Elechead was a tightly designed experience with difficult, but not impossible, puzzles that always seem to come together in a satisfying way. Despite leaning on the short side, I enjoyed my time with Elechead and felt the game had quite a few creative ideas.Elechead is a fairly short game, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. I think oftentimes puzzle-platformers can drag on a bit and run out of creative level-design late in the game, but Elechead left me feeling satisfied with no boring lulls in the game; however, I think they could've done just a bit more given how versatile the game's central electricity mechanics are.My only real issues with the game involve the late game. Without spoiling, the way to progress in the final stretch feels overly cryptic, and I had to use a guide for the first time in what was, up-to that point, a very understandable and straightforward experience. Some of the collectibles were also a bit obnoxiously out of the way, but that complaint only applies to completionists.I would definitely recommend Elechead to anyone looking for a fun, brain-teasing puzzle platformer that won't take forever to beat. That said, my play-through in which I got every collectible and did everything there was to do, only took me 2.8 hours, and I was able to beat the game (without focusing on collectibles) in about 1.5 hours. Knowing that, I think $10 is a bit steep, and would recommend wish-listing the game and waiting for a price drop if you're interested.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. ElecHead is an exceptionally well-designed platformer with plenty of old-school charm. Don't let the simple mechanics fool you - the levels are full of variety due to the sheer creativity of the developer. The game has just enough story to tie it all together, but don't expect much more than that. Fun, challenging and full of creativity, ElecHead is a breath of fresh air for platforming mechanics and level design.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, and i've obviously given it a positive rating, but the fact the game doesn't tell you anything and an extremely needed powerup is totally hidden in an area that makes zero sense to traverse too is a bit bad game design.I'm all up for not pointing the player in an obvious direction, but in this case, maybe make it a bit easier? also tell us that we need to get all the collectables.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect little puzzle platformer: polished, beautiful, smart, and focused. Challenging but not punishing. As in all the best puzzle games, one simple central mechanic — electrifying surfaces by touching them — is complicated bit by bit and cleverly worked out in all its possibilities. Wonderful sound and art (the jump and landing sounds alone are worth the price of admission). Secrets are generously indicated to the player and fun to search for.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is a must-have for puzzle game lovers. It scratches the same itch as games like Braid, VVVVVV, The Swapper,  and Limbo. The puzzles revolve around a simple mechanic; any surface you touch becomes electrified, which powers on each of the game's obstacles, causing them to behave in various ways. The puzzles manage to be challenging while only having a few moving parts, with the challenge coming from the counter-intuitive consequences of this mechanic. The game design is perfect, in that everything is communicated to you wordlessly. You learn by playing, not through heavy-handed tutorials.This is a PUZZLE-platformer, with a strong emphasis on puzzles. While some sections have to be completed within a time window, you do not have to have very fast reflexes or super precise jumping to beat this game. However, getting all of the games secrets does involve some skill.The aesthetic is perfect! The protagonist is cute and expressive, and the environment details are minimal to emphasize exactly what you need to see. There is a little bit of plot to be inferred from the scenery and the ending cutscene, and the twist at the end definitely got an audible "woah!" from me.This game nails secret hunting. There are two tiers of secrets. One tier is explicitly sign-posted, and is needed to get an alternate ending of the game.  As long as you pay close attention to your surroundings, you will be able to get this ending. The second tier of secrets is not hinted at, and is gated behind the trickiest hiding spots, hardest puzzles, and most difficult platforming. This is the right way to do secret hunting, IMO, since it gives something for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: An easy recommendation. Absolutely fantastic concept. I almost didn't grab it for whatever reason, maybe I was slightly turned off by the super old school art style which I didn't care for much before playing but I actually grew to really appreciate it. So many of the reviews were so adamant to just stop reading and get it so I did!My only complaint is regarding the end of the game. The concept that was used I personally just wasn't a fan of. It felt disjointed from how tight and fun the main part of the game was. And the main part was so solid. No filler. Just good puzzles one after another. Do not that at all turn you away from this absolute gem though. You may actually like it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: If you like little indie puzzle-platformers at all, I STRONGLY recommend Elechead. It perfectly executes on the ideas it's built on. There's some puzzles based on its unique mechanic, some platforming exactly as challenging as is warranted by the context, some secrets, some even-more-secrets, some surprises, some great music. A whole little arc of fun times and discovery and feeling clever, packed into a package that I 100%ed in under 4 hours. You could as well, +/- 2, or you could just do the core of it in even less. There is absolutely no cruft, no less-perfect extra junk thrown in out of insecurity.I always urge people to value short videogames. Time is something you spend, and if you can spend less of it and still get a complete package, that's amazing. This game is amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: You can finish it in just one sitting. The puzzles are not overwhelming but at the same time some of them require more time. Overall, it is great. One thing that might've been done differently is the ending. I must say I was quite confused, I didn't know where to go, but later it turned out that i somehow had missed the second ability and because of this I was not able to move one. I needed to check it on the Internet. But still, it was fun.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: An expertly designed puzzle platformer, the mechanics are simple but they never wear they welcome, with very creative and clever level design, even the trollish scenarios (you know what I mean) make the player pay attantion to their surroundings to find a way to progress. The puzzles are hard, but I never felt like I needed to consult a guide to progress, everything feels strategically placed and nothing feels haphazard. This is definitely one of the best puzzle platformers I've ever played, and if you're a fan of the genre, you must play this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short game, and really well done. Puzzle platformer that introduces new puzzles at a great rate. Quick enough to keep you guessing, but not too fast to completely stump you. I found myself saying "wow that's a clever twist" about how to solve the platforming several time. I would definitely recommend. Music and graphics are just my style too.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Simple yet superb game! The puzzle platforming is what really shines and it really makes you think hard about how to use all the tools you are given but also WHAT tools you have been given... It's due to the excellent level design that all the tools have to be used in many different ways and it is pretty challenging at times. The pixel art is comfortable and the movement feels just right. I think the game is just long enough to present all that the game can give you! It never becomes stale or boring and every level (room) is refreshing. Super tight game :)
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: ElecHead is a short (~3h) platform/puzzle game greatly inspired by VVVVVV, in which you control a robot leaking electricity through its head. That electricity is conducted through whatever it touches, activating mechanisms such as moving platforms. This central mechanic is simple and very easy to understand, yet interesting enough for the game to build multiple intricate puzzles on it. The game design and level design are excellent and manage to fully exploit the central mechanic in a concise way.Compared to VVVVVV, the platforming aspect is much easier, and the focus lies more on the puzzles, which are clever but not very difficult to solve.Getting to the end of the game and collecting all the main collectibles feels mostly fair (it involves a few hidden passages, but they can easily be found once you start looking for them).There are also a few other secret unlockables, which do not all feel as “fair” to get (hidden passages with no hints, one or two game mechanics that are not obvious and only used for one secret, ...)Overall it's a really great and enjoyable game that will not get boring due to its excellent design and short length.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool idea that is executed really well. Do be mindful that you need to have one of the special video-game-puzzle brains, be willing to refer to discussion boards/Reddit, or look at guides or YouTube videos to be able to solve some of the trickier puzzles. I don't have that kind of brain, and I still got through perhaps 90-95% of the game's puzzles by myself. Can't fault the controls or the way it plays, can't fault the graphics, and can't fault the music/sound either. For me and the way my brain works, a couple of elements were a little too esoteric, in that I would never have thought of the solution, at all, with some help. But that doesn't make this a bad game! Far from it. It's perhaps one of the better puzzle/platformers of recent times. Just... You know... Be really mindful of how well you/your brain goes with more 'adventure-y' puzzle/puzzle platformers, like The Pedestrian or The Swapper. Love those? Then I'd wager you'll also love ElecHead.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many bright and positive things I can say about ElecHead, a tight puzzle platformer based around the mechanic of manipulating your electricity-charged head to power platforms and objects to navigate the world. Standing at a confident four hours long, it manages to pack an immense set of skills and tricks that all stem from its primary two-button control scheme. After obtaining the ability to throw your head, that's it, and it is because of this simplicity that not only do all the puzzles seem fair and within reach, but are critical to how well-designed every asset of ElecHead is. The core adventure of the titular robot won't give too much pause, it consistenly challenges the player by presenting new obstacles and ways to shake up your existing knowledge. Talking any more about the puzzles themselves would be robbing the game of its best solves, so instead I will say constantly be thinking about everything the game has told you and try everything. It was a joy to see everything ElecHead has to offer and I hope a new game or more levels will grace us in the future.Also, the music is incredible. Put it on the maximum setting.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty short (I reached the end in a little over 2 hours), but also among the most delightfully satisfying puzzle platformers I've played. You play as ElecHead, a power-generating robot who supplies electricity to machines to which you are connected by metal, and use this ability to progress through each screen. As a twist on this basic ability, you are able to detach your head from your body, allowing it to power something while you navigate elsewhere.The level design thoroughly explores the potential of this limited ability set, but best of all leaves it to you to figure it out. There is no time wasted on heavy-handed tutorials - in fact, there is a clear design choice to have as little text in the game as possible. Between the title screen and the end credits, I was not shown any text aside from minimal one-time prompts indicating the available controls. The game is divided into a number of "areas" where you are guided toward identifying a new "trick" for interacting with the world, and then challenged with puzzles that iterate on the theme, requiring you to exercise this technique in new ways, and in combination with others previously learned, often challenging assumptions you may have developed as a player.There are some interesting and challenging puzzles in this game, some of which stumped me for a matter of minutes, but nothing of the brain-breaking, show-stopping variety found in other games like Baba is You or Stephen's Sausage Roll. ElecHead strikes a balance that makes you stop and think without killing the momentum of the experience.There are apparently a number of secrets that I missed, and the game is so good that I might actually go back and look for them. If you like puzzle platformers at all, definitely check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Very good puzzle platformer that has some neat ideas about electricity. Most of the puzzles are pretty straightforward and only need a little trial and error to figure it out. However, there are bonus rooms with harder versions of similar puzzles that give you extra collectables and different colour palettes. My only complaint is that the pause/options screen only has images so it's a little confusing.I finished the main ending (3hrs 40mins) although I only collected about the half the 'chips' required for 100% completion.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastically creative minimalist puzzle design. Hard to believe the number ways the game's creator found to combine a tiny number of verbs into surprising and thought-provoking puzzle mechanics.This game respects your time and your intelligence. I 100%'d it in just shy of four hours, which felt like the perfect length for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: it's very polished all around, and you can refer to the other reviews for specifics.i guess i should just mention that there's a black and white color palette, which is... kinda a meme (both primary and secondary colors are white, so it's harder to tell what's activated and what isn't since the only indicator is now the sparks that surround the active platforms, and the screens all become pure white)(more importantly: black and white not recommended, it's supposedly bad for your eyes - you can (normally) see a halo around the white parts)
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun easy but complex puzzle platformer. Everything in this game is thought through. The game feels complete and polished. All the puzzles are unike and often have a fun twist. The game teaches you mechanics that often has more then one use. Thats what I like. Its pretty straight forward how the mechanic works but its still very deep. Loved this game, really recomend it. One of my favorite puzzler.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Lateral thinking puzzle about conduction. You only recieve one powerup throughout the entire game.Since many of the game's secrets rely on knowledge the game drip-feeds you over time (or stumble into), when you reach the end, you'll easily be able to figure out where all the secrets are.If you are a fan of puzzle platformers that force you to think and recall far more than execute tight sequences, this is up your alley!There are some secrets that are so out of the way, they don't even contribute to your macguffin-collectible counter! Instead, you are given extra color palettes. I - and Elechead (If you die too much on one area, he gets upset) - got VERY annoyed by the Tower of Heaven one, because I could perform single-frame jumps to reach it, instead of discovering a sneaky mechanic for it and it alone that asks for patience.Additionally, do NOT try and bind a button to the star thingy on the bottom of keyboard controls, that (as of November 10th, 2021) crashes the game if you try to bind it yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely tightly and cleverly designed puzzle platformer. It's designed around a single (or two, depending how you consider it/them) mechanic that is constantly re-contextualized throughout the run of the game. The way it constantly forces you to think creatively and reapply the mechanic in new ways is extremely satisfying and, at least for me and my brain, paced pretty much perfectly. As soon as you grasp a new way you can use it, you're made to figure out a new twist on it. Highly recommended if you enjoy the genre at all
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great puzzle platformer. The design is really solid from the mechanics to the level layout to the actual puzzles. It's all very clever and satisfying.Took me about 6 hours to finish it (most of the time on record was being paused overnight in menus etc).Recommended if you like puzzle platformers at all. This one is expertly crafted.There were a couple of spots at the end or later in the game where I had to resort to video walkthroughs or a map layout.I have no idea how people finished this game in 2 hours without cheating ;)
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool puzzle platformer, I really appreciate the retro style and the concept behind the game. The level design is excellent and the puzzle are smart without being obtuse and overstaying their  welcome sadly it's also it's a little bit it's downfall, it won't be much of a challenge for puzzle veterans and you will probably crave for more but only because what you get is so fun. _childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice puzzle game with simple controls, and good puzzles. The hidden unlockables have especially good puzzles locking them. It is fairly short, however, although I would say still worth it at $10, although if thats a bit much for you for only a few hours of gameplay at most, then definitely get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformer, reminiscent of the old flash games in which you had one mechanic that is really polished: your head is electric, and your body is conductive. There are things that are conductive in the world too and you can enable this things by powering them with your head. That's it, that's the game.Sounds simple but it is really well thought out and polished. Super recommended!The only drawback is that in order to get 100% you need to get an optional ability that is way off the beaten path and you can only access it via a glitch (the floor looks normal but you can fall through). I was racking my brain trying to get a collectible that it wasn't possible without it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome puzzle game, with some neat platform aspects. The music is fantastic and really adds to the adventure. What the game may lack in complex mechanics it makes up for several times over with creative puzzles that keep you thinking until the end. The secrets and extra color palettes and an extra layer of challenge for those who what more. Perfect for a lazy weekend or to play in few short sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet puzzle platformer that you can knock out in a single sitting. Solutions are built around the main mechanic of powering things that your head touches, a mechanic that is pushed to the limit and makes the game surprisingly deep. It features secret collectibles and two endings, meaning it has some degree of replayability if you're up to find them all. It's not really a Metroidvania (it features exactly one permanent upgrade at the time of writing), but if you enjoy that genre you will enjoy this one. Some of the puzzles were very very clever and a joy to solve. Overall I would say it is comparable to VVVVVV in that is a platformer with a very unique and fun mechanic that, once you've learned all the tricks, can be beaten very quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle-platformer. Good music, clever puzzle design, crisp aesthetic, tight controls, so the fundamentals are all there. I think where the game shines most, though, is the world design. I don't want to spoil too much, but it's in that design where the whole game is made of rooms of the same size all stitched together. I'm a little biased towards this style, but I still think this game does it objectively well, with all sorts of fun secrets like 20 hidden collectibles (wonder where they got that from). These make ElecHead feel a lot longer than it is, which is exactly what you want in a puzzle-platformer. You don't want to dwell on one for too long, but you want the experience to be satisfying, so it's fantastic that this game knows that.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformerIf you have patience and are clever this game can be awesome. The atmosphere drips of early 8-bit nostalgia and the graphics and music fits well. The platforming part feels fair and there are few places which require pixel perfect jumps. Most puzzles are fairly obvious but will require a few retries. Then there are a few rooms that are real head scratchers. The game grinds to a halt and I grew frustrated. Sooner or later, you will figure it out. Everything to solve the room is in the room… in most cases. But the worst part are the hidden rooms that are just there. No markings on the wall. You will end up grinding against every wall.Overall it was still a great game that was short enough to not grow tired of it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Great simple gameplay!The game is short and sweet. As I played through this a phew things stuck to mind. 1. the sound design is amazingly put together; i could tell what the character was interacting with simply by what little sounds i heard.2. the gameplay was tightly designed; while going through the levels, you have nearly everything at the start (except for the head throw). All puzzles are then based off of using the few items at hard to the fullest of their abilities.3. the OST was amazing; the songs were great and utilized to give the play the maximum amount of impact to the scene they are in.Great game, i hope it gets more popular9/10, easy to pick up and stop, or return to when you have a hour or two...
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: Elec Head is an excellent little pixel puzzle platformer. I'm not the hugest fan of puzzle platformers because I often feel the platformer aspect of them becomes, in a sense, irrelevant to the puzzle solving. Elec Head never feels like it lets down the platformer medium in its mission. The character controls great and the animation is fluid and polished.The basic mechanics are simple. Your character's head conducts electricity either through the body and down to the floor below you, or by being thrown and conducting from a distance. The electric charge interacts with the environment in a few ways, mostly by causing platforms to move and activating hazards. It's pretty impressive how many different puzzles developer Nama Takahashi manages to create out of so few elements. Not once during the journey did I feel like a particular puzzle was redundant or not worth my time.The game takes place across one large, mostly linear, map. There's one power-up in the game, the afore-mentioned head-throwing ability, and it does allow for access to new parts of the map, but this is not a metroidvania. In addition, there are also 20 hidden microchips (Or maybe they're keycards? The game refreshingly contains almost zero text outside of the title screen and credits.) These chips allow access to the true ending, although it's almost identical to the standard ending and neither is anything grand, this is okay though, since Elec Head, like any good game, is more about the journey than the destination. There are also larger chips that are even harder to find that unlock new color palettes. If you've played similar limited-palette indy games like Downwell, which the creator has said he was inspired by, these types of bonus palette will be familiar. Personally, I quite enjoy different vibes different color palettes give off.The music is great too. Elec Head has a nice retro style platformer OST to jam out to.I only wish the game were longer and had some tougher, optional, sections to conquer. It took me about three hours to finish the game with most of the hidden chips, another 45 minutes to find the last remaining ones, and I still have yet to find all the hidden color palettes. There're only a small number of puzzles that I found exceptionally challenging, and those were the ones that focused more on reflexes than puzzle solving. A custom level designer and a way for players to share their own maps would be another great way to extend the game's playtime. As it stands, it's a short game that doesn't strike me as having a whole lot of replay value, although I think it would be a great game for speedrunners to spend time honing skills at.Despite the short length, this is a definite recommend from me, and probably the best puzzle platformer I've experienced.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent puzzle platform game with a unique mechanic. The controls are simply left, right, jump and (shortly after starting) throw your head which doubles as a power supply. Each room represents a new challenge and a new way to combine these actions. It really needs to be experienced.It is a very short game, I completed it quite naturally in just over 2 hours while collecting half of the secrets. For me I prefer high-quality over length, and there is zero padding in this game. The designer has implemented some really clever variations on the genre which subvert expectations. None of the puzzles were so difficult that they became frustrating and there's a balance between platforming skill and working out the "trick".I paid full price for this the day after launch and I don't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the demo for this on ich.io like 3 or 4 years ago and loving it and then just kind of forgetting about it for a while, a number of months ago I researched to see what the progress was with no luck and then a week or so ago found the game was finally releasing! And it was so worth the wait, this game is delightful.The puzzle mechanics are unique and plentiful considering how minimal the controls actually are. You only use two face buttons and d pad/stick (or arrow keys plus 2 keys if you use K+M), and the signature mechanic of the game is that your robot head conducts electricity on different surfaces and you can throw your head forwards or upwards to solve puzzles. And in spite of that simplicity, there are still many unique mechanics aside from just that, including some precise timing and other things like that.Visually the game has a simple color palette and a soundtrack that doesn't have much to it but more than gets the job done. The sprite work is all fantastic and the minimalist color usage makes sure you never get confused about what's happening on screen. The levels are all super fun to play and I would say the difficulty in this game on a scale from 1-10 would probably be around a fair 5 or 6, maybe going up to a 7 near the ending parts. There's no hub world and instead you sort of warp back to areas if you want to, aside from that you just finish one screen and keep moving forward.Just a fantastic little game that I've been waiting a while for and I'm so glad it's finally here, the only complaint I have is that it's a bit short, depending on how good you are at puzzle games you'll probably beat the game in somewhere between 3 and 4 hours. But it's more than worth it for the $10 price tag and I highly recommend this game and hope for more from this developer in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

_childDocuments_.review:
In a world enshrouded by darkness, deep inside a factory, the light of hope still shines.

ElecHead has you play as Elec, a small robot on a mission to bring light back to the world.

When Elec touches walls, floors, platforms, switches, and more, he makes electricity run through them, activating them.

He can also detach and throw his head to trigger things remotely, but be careful: if he doesn't get his head back within ten seconds, he will shut down.

Elec will have to use his head, literally and figuratively, to find a way out of the trap-ridden factory.
_childDocuments_.name: ElecHead

name: Taxi Chaos
detailed_description: RUSH THROUGH THE CITY TO DELIVER YOUR CRAZY CUSTOMERS! Get behind the wheel and get ready for a brand-new taxi experience! Drive around the city as the seasoned cab driver Vinny or the self-proclaimed ‘influencer’ Cleo, and pick up the craziest of customers! Power through midtown in a strong muscle car, race past all parks in an exotic supercar or drift around the business area in a Japanese tuner taxi. Whicher you choose - your challenge is to deliver your passengers on time! At least, if you want to make any money. Navigate through crowded streets, dodge pedestrians across sidewalks or even defy the laws of gravity by jumping over rooftops! Nothing is too extreme when it comes to delivering your passengers on time! Discover the best shortcuts and get to know New Yellow City (NYC), as well as your passengers, like the back of your hand. Are you ready for this crazy and chaotic ride? • A completely fresh and modern take on the old-school classic taxi games! 🚕 • Explore and master the streets of the immense and vibrant New Yellow City. • Discover the best routes to speed up and maximize your fares! • Go hard! Go crazy! The more risk you take and the crazier you drive, the higher your rewards! • Break the rules in seven extreme rides: from the iconic yellow cab to a full-blown muscle car! Earn enough to complete your collection. • Get to know your bizarre passengers through hilarious and fully voiced conversations! Pick up a hipster, plumber, rockstar, an alien and many more! • Smash through mailboxes, streetlights, fire hydrants or everything else that is in your way! The city is your playground. • Test your driving skills in three distinct game modes! Enjoy the classic Arcade Mode, cruise around in Freeroam or step up for a real challenge in Pro Mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Not what I was expecting. Since Crazy Taxi is one of the only comparable game in this genre, I'll be using that as a basis.For starts, everything about this game is a watered down version of Crazy Taxi, even to the original. The game isn't nearly as chaotic or fast paced. The environment is based of of NYC and isn't nearly as fun or dynamic to traverse as the other Crazy Taxi games. Because it's NYC and as a flat as a board, the game is built around having to jump like an Italian plumber to even get a good time if you can find the spots to do that, that is. The controls for the car are very lacking from what I've found. Can't drift the car (at least from what I found, correct me if I'm wrong here). Boosting the car is only valuable when you pick someone up since you can only boost when at a stop (again, correct me if I'm wrong...). And a key to get high combos is to just do small bunny-hops down the street. Nothing really challenging...The dialogue between the cabbies and customers seems too relaxed for what you are doing in the game, and very limited so it gets old fast.In all, this game doesn't compare to even the original Crazy Taxi.  The only thing this game does that I was Crazy Taxi did is the Free Roam. But like I said earlier, the environment isn't as fun to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: We all know the good old classic 'Crazy Taxi' and boy did we have a lot of fun with it,Taxi Chaos makes an attempt to give us this experience again in 2021/2022.Taxi Chaos Gameplay: To give a direct clarification, the game is close to Crazy Taxi but nowhere near the expectations we get from watching the Taxi Chaos trailer,A strong advantage is that the gameplay is almost identical to that of Crazy Taxi,you have to pick up passengers according to the difficulty of the ride which you can determine by the color that hangs around the passenger,you have a general timer that expires and every time you pick up or drop off a passenger there will be some time added to this timer,using the jump function (yes, your cars can jump to avoid traffic) and also using the many shortcuts the city has to offer will also determine the number of extra seconds you get on your timer. if you can serve enough passengers, you can unlock other vehicles that move faster and more efficiently.This is an addictive style of gameplay but despite this I didn't get the feeling that I want to unlock all the vehicles glued to my monitor.There is only 1 city, and the soundtrack is far from as stimulating as songs like the offspring and also the audio dialogues of the characters are a sequence of a number of different recordings that you will hear several times during 1 session,after a few sessions you will soon get tired of the sound part of the game.Also, there are only 2 characters available, a male and female, so you will not be able to choose a character based on style and looks, but according to gender, which is a major limitation in character favorites.Graphically I can't say it's wrong, the game gives a nice picture of how the experience of this type of game used to feel and excelled, although the entertaining factors of the rest of the game are very limited and feel free to add some more content , especially when you look at the current price of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: No sir, I don't like it. You would think it would be easy to do a good Crazy Taxi clone twenty years after the game was first released, but clearly this is not the case. Taxi Chaos has terrible controls (keyboard of controller), a limited at best camera and voice acting that gives me a headache. The conversation is recorded multiple times verbatim but by different actors. It makes 90s sports game commentary look verbose and stimnulating. In theory, this should be fun, especially the free roam mode where you have fetch quests and storylines, but trying to find most of these "collectibles" is pretty hard as they don't generate unless you are directly on top of them. The limitations of the camera hurt and hinder this aspect of the game as well, making it more frustration than anything resembling fun. The controls though? Yuck. Not only does the game sometime ignore that you are pressing to brake, but drifting is non-existent and invisible walls seem to come and go at the whims of the game. I'll be trying to do a stunt or jump and suddenly there will be an invisible wall there that wasn't the other six times I tried it. Scoring is nonsensical too. I borked up a ride and got there with a second to spare? FOUR STARS. Then another time I took all the super short cuts and had almost a full time left with a run. two stars - despite all the jumps and shortcut bonuses. I wish i could understand the scoring logic, but after 4+ hours it just seems to be beyond me. if you like Crazy Taxi, just stick to that. I just did not have fun with this at all, and believe I tried to find something about the game that I could be positive about.
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Why does stuff like this get made? True fans of Crazy Taxi surely would have taken more care to incorporate the best parts of the game they're paying homage to into their title. But that's not what happened here. This is a generic, stripped-down, mind-numbingly boring version of a much, much better game.The taxis are slow and lack a lot of the more advanced driving mechanics (crazy drift, crazy stop, limiter cut, etc), the map is almost totally flat, the passengers keep rehashing the same three canned conversations ad nauseam, the game's visuals are beyond bland and look even worse because the contrast is cranked way too high for some reason, and the music is just dull light rock. It's bad. Cheap cash-in bad...
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Taxi Chaos isn't actively bad, but it's also distinctly not good. The art design is respectable, but there's none of that Crazy Taxi flare and the gameplay loop is just tepid. The jumping and weaving you see in the screenshots is not typical. Mostly you've traveling straight lines between light traffic. Normally I'd shrug at a lackluster tribute to one of gaming's classics, there's plenty of that on Steam, but having the audacity to charge $24.99 for an underwhelming time waster when you can buy the original Crazy Taxi for $7.99 is absurd. I'd love to see a proper successor. This isn't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: 🔶  🔶  The graphics are good, all based on a city with many cars and building to avoid, and a little park to explore, but there only 1 main atmosphere. The arcade gameplay is simple to learn, but too much simple, drive a car with a jump function and a boost launch when you burn out your stationary car, pretty like the same as Crazy Taxi, but without any penalty when you runs into other cars.Each run starts with a 90-second timer, you save extra time by dropping customers off at their destinations.3 Main game mode in the main menu :Normal is the base game when you have a GPS for helping you dropping customers off at their destinations.Pro is the same as Normal mode, but without the GPS for helping you, so almost impossible to know where to go except by learning the city map for hours.Free Run is the same as Normal, but with infinite time to run in the city and explore it.So all 3 Main game mode are almost the same gameplay.7 differents cars in the gameAll 6 others cars need to be unlock, (finish 5 runs / get 5-star at the end of a run …), but all cars drive the same way, and need multiples hours for unlocking them. Game cost 25 euros, all game mode are the same and the game take maximum 1 hour to see the main content of the gameplay, no career or mission mode, cost way to much. No story in the game, but that ok because that a racing game.Music is ok, but really repetitive.Really bad optimization, take 5 minutes for loading if installed on Disk Space (the game only take 3 Go), and required to be installed on a SSD for loading properly.Some freeze during gameplay, especially on first game on a section (played on i5 / 2 Go VRAM / 8 Go RAM)Also no graphics configuration in the game. 🔶  🔶 💚💚💚 :- Graphics are ok- The main arcade gameplay is playable …❌❌❌ :- … but literally the same as Crazy Taxi but in worse- The High price for a really poor content- All cars are almost the same with any car customization- Need to be installed on a SSD card.
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome, very close to sega's crazy taxi which was out in the late 90s.  That version is available on steam but Taxi Chaos is more modern with better graphics!Has a sense of humour with driver/passenger chat and so on.  You only have a few moments to deliver a passenger to his or her destination then you simply move on to your next customer.  Each customer asks to go to a different location which can be long or short distance.  Long distance gives you more points but short distance takes less time so you can move on to your next customer more quickly and boost your time limit counter.A good sense of replay value is here.  Even though the game play itself lasts for around 3-4 minutes, the more you play the more you unlock extra features.  For example, there are 6 or 7 different styles of taxi cars to unlock  which you can unlock by completing various requirements such as play 5 games of arcade mode.Worth every penny!  Fun to play with perfect car handling physics and you will get that feeling of oh, maybe just one more go!

_childDocuments_.review: This game runs pretty well on the Steam Deck, so if you only want to play it there, you might think it's worth it for a cheap price.  On my desktop PC on my 4k tv however, the game is horrible. There are barely any configuration options.  You cannot adjust anything about the resolution, texture quality, or any display settings at all.  There's barely any other customization options beside that.  So, it looks absolutely terrible on my TV.  It looks like it's running at 720p, and the performance is very sluggish with tons of stutter.Even the load times on my pc are bad.  It's installed to an ssd, but it seemed to take maybe 30secs to a minute to load the level after I pressed the Arcade Mode button.You're much better off skipping this and getting Crazy Taxi instead, but if you want to try it on the Steam Deck, you might be satisfied if it's a decent price.

_childDocuments_.review: Taxi Chaos is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.  It's a ripoff of Crazy Taxi, and despite being much newer and having better graphics, it's worse in all other respects.  Usually games are awful because the developers didn't bother with graphics, despite knowing that video games are a visual medium.  Here, it's just about really poor gameplay and really poor console porting.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 5 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Taxi Chaos has the completely unrealistic cash grab price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Cities: Skylines", "Far Cry 5" or "Bioshock Infinite".  Heck, this costs more than GTA:V, which has taxi missions in it, as part of a much, much larger game.  Where are you going to spend your money?  More wisely than on games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10Wow, Team 6 Game Studios finally made a decent game. With that being said though, some serious work has to be done to make this a worthy successor to the Crazy Taxi series. But considering that I love Crazy Taxi and Crazy Taxi 3: High Roller, I couldn't help but enjoy this, especially since aside from The Simpsons: Road Rage, there are hardly any Crazy Taxi-like games. But if you aren't a fan of Crazy Taxi, you can give this a pass or hold off for now and try the games that inspired it.+ Decent replay value.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.+ Rewards you for doing certain tricks like jumps and near misses.+ Decent soundtrack. With that being said, I still recommend playing Crazy Taxi sounding music.- No mini-games.- Repetitive dialogue.- No graphics settings.- There's no way to cancel mid-engine jump start.- Scoring system makes no sense. I earn $17,000, I get 4/5 stars. But when I earn $8,000, I get 5/5 stars?
_childDocuments_.name: Taxi Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: What could have been a solid spiritual successor to SEGA's popular Crazy Taxi series turns out to be a sluggish, boring, and misguided turd of a title. The taxi drives too slow, the handling sucks, the dialogue is bad, the audio quality is poor, the actual voice-acting is amateurish, the graphics are bad, the compass barely works, the music is annoying, etc., etc., etc. You name an aspect of this game and its quality is subpar at best.I think my biggest gripe with this game though is that the city is too difficult to learn. There's a "pro mode" that turns the compass off and it borders on impossible. Too much of the city looks identical, with entire blocks made up of copy-pasted assets. The unique drop-off points are supposed to serve as landmarks, but they're nearly indistinguishable from everything around them. Crazy Taxi had clearly defined routes with very obvious landmarks that help orient you within its city, and this game just lacks that entirely.Oh, the $25 price tag is straight robbery as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Taxi Chaos  is a casual arcade racing game where you select one of a wide range of unlockable cabs, each of whom has different attributes: the strong muscle car, the superfast exotic supercar, the corner-drifting Japanese tuner, an American classic from the ‘60s and more: Taxi Mayhem has them all. Your goal is to try and earn big cab fares, by picking up any customers and dropping them off at their destination spots as fast as possible before you run out of time! However, beware: most customers are a little crazy.

name: Cozy Grove
detailed_description: Welcome to Cozy Grove , a life-sim game about camping on a haunted, ever-changing island. As a Spirit Scout, you'll wander the island's forest each day, finding new hidden secrets and helping soothe the local ghosts. With a little time and a lot of crafting, you'll bring color and joy back to Cozy Grove! Features: Beautiful, dynamic, hand-drawn landscapes that come alive when you help a spirit in need. Dozens of memorable characters and spirits for you to find and befriend. Each spirit has a unique, extensive story for you to unravel over time. Collect spirit animals, craft decorations, go fishing and more! 40+ hour campaign filled with side quests, designed to span months of playtime. Like Animal Crossing, Cozy Grove is synced to real world time , and provides 30-60 minutes of new quest content each day. After that, you can fish, craft and decorate to your heart's content!
