_childDocuments_.review: I should preface this by saying that this is not a game for everyone. The real-time days passing is kinda a take it or leave it thing: if you're into things like Animal Crossing or even just the concept of Daily Tasks in various mobile or online games, you'll probably be fine with that part of the game. If you want to get a game done in a weekend, then no, you can't really do that. There's no penalty for not logging in multiple days in a row, so it's just that things like quests reset at 5 AM your local time. That being said, I don't want to make the claim that "this game saved my mental health" or anything, but it did give me a sense of routine while dealing with a disability that prevented me from doing a lot of things. The daily quests gave me An Activity To Do, and it made me feel like I was actually making progress on something in my life after completing a story quest, even if that "something" is a mostly silly video game. There's criticisms to be leveled against the game to be sure, but they're kind of par for the course for the genre. The NPCs will repeat dialogue, if you want to complete the collection some of the RNG is really bad, etc. (although for people who enjoy 100%ing games, completing the collection is not an achievement, both in-game and on steam). The game does have some really good characters though, and I'll stand by that. I think my favorite bears are Olivia Cubbins and Allison Fisher but I'm also biased. They all are distinct, and that's including the DLC bears. Overall I think if you know what you're getting into it's something that can be really nice, but if any part of it, especially the real time gameplay scares you off then it's probably not your thing anyway.(For those with some triggers, the bears, being ghosts, are all dead. At one point in their story, they'll describe their deaths, but you have a dialogue option before that where they ask if you want to hear it. That doesn't avoid all possibly triggering content, but if you know there's a specific thing that would get to you, I'd recommend asking someone who has been through the story about it.)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is charming!! The artwork and the music are just beautiful.As someone who played Animal Crossing religiously last year, this game is definitely a homage to it, but with a few different aspects.The limitations of quests per day keep you from burning out like in Animal Crossing, and the prospect of continuing to expand your space and capabilities is a nice goal to work towards!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is indeed very cozy. If you like small bites of gameplay and don't mind playing around ~1hr max per day, this is the game for you! It starts off super slow but does build up. The game never feels stressful or pushy in any way, and is a great game to just wind down and relax to.I like the customization options as well, it's cute how the clothing and hair options switch up every day. I only wish I could stock up on hair options instead of having to lose my previous hairstyle each time I get a cut. With that being said, it's obviously not game breaking and just a personal preference because I am indecisive af!I like the quality of life updates that have been pushed out since release- I think they have helped dramatically and I also just like knowing that the devs are responding to players' critiques and actively working on patching the game up.edit: I'm now 10 more hours into the game and still adore it. I really love the time gating, personally, because it really makes me look forward to the hour I play it. It's nice to make it a short daily ritual to do my quests and all. Still super happy with all of the quality of life updates that have been pushed out! If the devs ever release DLC I would definitely purchase it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: , a very chill experience, strangely punctuated by some dark humor that hits you like a bowling ball.The main draw of the game starts with the exploration of this mysterious and haunted island and rapidly becomes some sort of fetch quest for the various villagers.One of its main mechanics, besides crafting and harvesting, is the fact that once the daily tasks are over there is nothing much to do, finding a good alternative to incentivize you to play just a little everyday, without making it a mania.Even if after a while it becomes somewhat repetitive, like the title implies it's a very "cozy" game, one to be played without rushing and simply used to start the day in a better way or unwind after a particularly stressful one.A heavy criticism must be had about the "late" game, since the combination between limited resources spawned to advance the story and knowing the island like your pockets makes this a chore, and the point where you should be done with it even if you did not complete the story.I suggest it if you like the graphics and are a fan of the genre, otherwise you could find this quite boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for 120 hours at this point, so it's definitely worth the money I've spent on it. It's a bit like Animal Crossing, but very few games reach the level of polish that Nintendo games are known for. This isn't a perfect game, but I've enjoyed it and I'll probably dump even more hours into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm also going to complain about the time gating that goes on in this game.  And I'm giving it a negative review because the only way around this time-gating that they specifically tell you about if you complain to them may corrupt your save file.  So rather than just include an option in the game to disable time-gating, they would rather the users risk corrupting their save files to achieve the same thing.  There are multiple better ways to do this.  Like a forum only patch that disables the time gating if you specifically look for it.  An obscure config file in the system folder you can change an option in.  Or just a normal in-game option.  I don't care, just don't ask me to risk corrupting my save file because of your "artistic vision"Update:  Played several days worth of the game now.  I'd call it a 7/10.  Obviously, this is a hidden object game.  The ghosts have lost things or need you to collect materials from around the island.  In exchange, they will train you in skills and advance the storyline by giving you logs.  Something I don't care for with this style of hidden object is that the objects are hidden in more and more obscure locations.  At the start, it's just find a bunch of feathers.  Then it's look under stuff.  Then they're hidden inside of a breakable that you've never seen before.  And the time gating actually gets worse as the game goes on.  So later you'll encounter timed quests where if you don't complete them within 12 hours, something happens.  I assume you don't get the optional reward.  And these also progress.  I just completed one where I had 12 hours to complete the quest and the only way to get the items for the quest was to wait an hour for them to be mailed to me.  Meaning people on tight schedules are really screwed.The art is absolutely gorgeous and the detail is what drew me to this game in the first place.  There is a rather bad "collect every item in the game" feature.  I feel like they were trying to copy Stardew Valley here, but it's just not the same.  Stardew Valley was a neat and organized set of collections.  You knew what you had left to collect and you knew what you'd be getting.  This is just collection vomit.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is lovely, and while the quests are a bit boring and simplistic, it's the real time aspect that tanks this for me. I would have happily sat down to play this game for hours, losing myself in helping the bears pass on - but instead a choice was made to enact "real time" into the gameplay loop. It was a very poor choice, in my opinion. Some people may have a lot of free time to sink into waiting for this, but I don't. Would not recommend buying if you're looking for a game you can progress through quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a quaint, peaceful game about helping the deceased move on. While it does have time-related mechanics (ie: having to wait a day between quests), it's nothing I've found has negatively impacted my gameplay. The game itself is intended for short, daily play to give you a break from the bustle of everyday life. On average, I personally find myself going for around an hour a day. I'm going to explain some of the game aspects that people don't like, and how to work around them.While the stacks for most items are fairly low, things that you personally drop on the ground do not disappear! At least not for 24 hours, I've yet to personally test further. Anything you can bake or craft generally doesn't need the items to be in your inventory, either. They can be stored in your tent, through your campfire, and still be accessed in the recipe menu. This saves a lot of time running back and forth, and that precious inventory space!Something I've had problems with but can be avoided by more careful planning is if you toss food to imps and there's some nearby, all of the imps will try and grab it. If you're trying to feed a specific one, this can make it difficult. However, it's not a necessary aspect of the game to feed the imps as you can get imp essence from breaking your tools through constant use, because that is one of the mechanics! However, they're very cheap to fix, usually only needing 3-6 charred fishbones so far (you get those from burning fish!).But my favorite part of the game has to be the characters themselves. You only get a small bit of their story every day, but if you really pay attention, you'll find yourself caring for these funky little spirits. You'll come visit them day after day to learn their story and help them out, and maybe you'll find some secrets on the island as you go! The game is still very young, and I'm really looking forward to seeing where it goes from here! I'd love to see the crew fix up inventory and storage issues as well, but there are ways to work around it already. Tl;dr? I highly recommend this game, despite the time and storage issues that can be worked around still. Get this game if you want to spend about an hour a day helping out and getting to know the spirits better!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It has a unique story that unravels as you help the residence on the island. If you enjoy Animal Crossing you'll enjoy this game. Its got fishing, bug catching, trees (and other types of plants) harvesting, and doing quests for the residents. I really love that you can decorate not only your own campsite but you can place stuff all over the island. Keep in mind that anything placed outside your campsite runs the risk of disappearing due to the layout in some places change. The game does use your IRL date and time to determine seasons, day of the week, and time of day but if you miss a few days the residents don't act any differently. So if you're the kind of person that would put Animal Crossing down for a week and then got too stressed about the villagers reacting there is no need to worry here!  All-in-all, it is a very relaxing game to play with a beautiful art style.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that Cozy Grove is a must for everyone who enjoys relaxing games. This game perfectly balances elements of comfort and challenge.If you're familiar with Animal Crossing, you'll notice a lot of similarities between the two games, like fishing and house building.What I loved most about Cozy Grove is its smooth introduction. The game gives you the right amount of time and space to adapt to the routine with the spirits, missions, and the bonfire. It doesn’t restrict your exploration at any point, allowing you to gradually get used to common elements in the grove, as well as the recommended actions related to them, such as selling flowers or donating every new item you discover. The bond you develop with each spirit and bird also makes the experience feel very comforting, something that’s further enhanced by the absolutely perfect soundtrack.The mechanics are very simple and easy, with basic clicks to access your bag, missions and interact with items around. Something that could be enhanced is the item selection whenever we are close to more than one item, which turns out to be common after we populate the environment with more elements and we might end up clicking another item that was not the intended one. Regarding pricing, I bought it on sale for R$14, and I definitely consider it worth the price—it’s given me more than I expected.I would wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone interested in casual and cozy experiences, and I’ve been doing so ever since I started playing it. It’s the perfect combo of relaxation and the satisfying feeling of accomplishment!

_childDocuments_.review: Great music, smooth controls, absolutely breathtaking artwork, and an extremely lovable cast of characters. It's simple without being boring, and in-depth without being overwhelmingThe best way I could describe this game is somewhat of a mix between Animal Crossing: New Horizons and Cult of the Lamb. If that sounds appealing to you, then I'd highly recommend this game; especially if you're mostly a fan of simple, daily quests and actually building relationships with charactersI'd also add that this game has many QOL improvements over similar games of this genre, such as ACNH. Bulk crafting is available from the beginning, as are bulk donations. Smaller things like bug catching and fishing also feel more fun and satisfying, since more control is given to the player with how you do themThe only big things I would warn people about when it comes to whether or not they'd enjoy this are that the daily quests most often just boil down to fetch quests, which may get repetitive and boring/frustrating for some players. This game also follows your real-world clock, meaning that timegating is absolutely present here, and that may be annoying for some players who would rather progress at a faster pace. The game is slow in terms of its gameplay, and that can be a positive or a negative depending on what you specifically are wanting out of a game like thisOverall, I'd absolutely recommend this game to people who enjoy other games of this genre. However, if you're someone who's annoyed by fetch quests, timegating, and slow gameplay, you may not get much out of this, and may be better skipping out on it completely

_childDocuments_.review: When I started playing Cozy Grove I honestly loved it.- The characters were cute and kinda fun.- The aesthetic was beautiful and just up my alley.- Music is chill.- The game mechanics are simple but fun enough to keep me engaged.But after a few days of coming back to it and playing as it was intended I started to get really annoyed with it, to the point of regretting picking it up all together. Everyone keeps saying that it's like Animal Crossing but on PC. No, it isn't. Far from it. One of the caveats of Animal Crossing was having to play in real time due to there being little to do each day, but it was always possible to time travel and progress the game at your desired pace. This game has far less content and features than AC and it actively rids you of any control and forbids you from playing more despite being very grindy:- Time-travelling (changing the time on your PC to progress) could break your game and thus is heavily discouraged.- Daily quests don't stack and if you can't complete it today, you won't get a new quest tomorrow after finishing the current quest.- Resources are needed in large quantities but it's impossible to gather them in one sitting due to them not spawning quickly enough.- Some quest items' spawn is entirely RNG based and due to your incapability to force-spawn or wait around for them to spawn, some quests could remain incomplete for days.- Game requires a copious amount of items that you need to gather and manage (including all the quest items!!), but you have barely any inventory space or storage, forcing you to litter all around your island and run back and forth a lot.- Some animations (catching fish, learning new recipes, cheering after completing a thing, receiving items) are very slow and annoying due to you having to wait for them every time.- There are sooooo many middlemen in this game, which forces you to run all around the island, back and forth to do something. In of itself it's not bad, but in combination with a small inventory and a myriad of slow animations at every step, this gets really frustrating.- Most story quests are fetch-quests which forces you to run around looking for various items, which gets repetitive and boring. I didn't personally mind it that much though simply because the authors seemingly couldn't come up with any other fun ways to progress the game and character stories.- Although the sprites for environment objects are pretty, it's really difficult to tell what you can interact with and when you want to do that you have to position your character correctly to even be able to do so. (E.g. I could not figure out what to do with a machete because no-one tells you that and the cut-able bushes don't stand out enough.)- The variety seems purely superficial. After playing for a longer time and completing some collections, I realised that most collectibles like fish, critters and flowers are just variations of each other in different colours. Of course there are different species, but there are a lot of different colour variations of each one (which is especially bad with flowers) and it just seems like they wanted to inflate the total collection to stretch out your play time.- The "Likes" and "Dislikes" mechanic makes the game seem very cluttered and stressful. I can't be the only one who plops my animals into the spot I think they'll like and do the same with similar preferences, ending up with a whole horde of animals and potted flowers in the middle of my camp. I'd say "I wish there was more variety in their preferences" but then I'd also have to say "I wish there was more space to accommodate all my plants and animals", and so on.This game is not Animal Crossing! It obviously tried to replicate its success but with more adult themes (death and afterlife) and cozy 2D graphics. But it also took its shortcomings such as annoying animations and daily 1-2 hours of play. At the same time, it barely has any content to it and doesn't even let you grind for resources which you need a lot of. Animal Crossing targets kids and manages to entertain adults, while Cozy Grove targets adults and treats them like children.I would only recommend it to people who - 1. Have low standards; 2. Have nothing better to do with their time; 3. Are desperate for an Animal Crossing experience but have absolutely no way of actually playing it.Otherwise, save your money and time - it's not worth it in the long run.I did think that it might seem strange that I'd still play this after finding it thoroughly annoying at times, lmao. And yet, my review still stands. I continue only because I have nothing better to do and I'm a dum ol' completionist when I deem it possible. That is exactly why I said I regretted getting this because now I HAVE TO spend more time to get as many achievements as I can because at this point it's a sunk cost so I might as well get my money's worth.Tell you what though, after this much more time playing Cozy Grove I finally began to see a semblance of a story. I am honestly ecstatic to find something I genuinely like this far into the game (because so far the story seems pretty interesting), but it's just so ironic that I had to spend almost 50 hours playing as intended to find it. And this proves my point even further. In the first hours (or rather days) of playing, all there is to do is grind for resources and complete fetch quests, aka playing an AC ripoff on PC, with practically no story to differentiate itself. Who' d play this if not someone who has low standards, has nothing better to do with their time and is desperate for an Animal Crossing experience?All in all, it's not a terrible game and I'm not here to spew hate. Just sharing my experience and everyone should decide whether they want to play this for themselves. Wish developers all the best in their future endeavors o/

_childDocuments_.review: If you plan to play this on a PC, I recommend you're fine with timegating. I imagine timetravelling to be extremely tedious on a PC, opposed to a Switch or such, and, really, personally I enjoy the day-sized bites the game offers me as an intended experience. The routine of playing this only for a certain amount of time before running out of quests to do per day can be frustrating for some people and I understand it - but it's honestly part of the charm for me. But, again, if that is a game mechanic you do not enjoy, I'd recommend you do not buy that game."Cozy" really is the perfect way to describe this game. For me, it hits the absolute sweet spot between Animal Crossing Foraging, Stardew Valley character bonding, both of those games' relaxingness and something very uniquely its own.The bears you meet are all very different and very unique, their personalities and histories offer so many different experiences. Some are more frustrating, some are more engaging, but all of them are incredibly endearing. And their backgrounds tend to deal with some heavy stuff as well! Also, you can get hugs from those bears and, really, that's all my frayed nerves crave at the end of a rough day. Joking aside, this is not only a great casual game, but also a fantastic comfort game. Fantastic to wind down or just relax.The soundtrack is beautiful, the artstyle is unique and very cute, caring for all the animals and baking/cooking goods is very satisfying and the customisation options are pretty varied. Not to mention the decorating! One major flaw is the layering of optics. You can walk behind pretty much everything and it will get see-through/disappear. Behind those objects you might find quest items. It can be a bit frustrating to try and find them, from time to time. But, honestly, if you've invested just a bit of time, you should be able to afford the quest item hints, which at first seem kind of expensive if used regularly but quickly turn out to be laughably cheap.8/10 I demand a portion of the game where I can personally fistfight a foodcritic

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a wonderful camping adventure. An errand based system, it works with the number of days played to progress the story. This can be frustrating when you have missions that need rewards from NPCs, as some days they won't have a task for you or you've run out of tasks and just have to wait.Over all, Cozy Grove is just as it says: cozy. Gameplay can be compared to Animal Crossing mixed with Don't Starve. An overall fun experience, no matter how much time you put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure at first if I'd like the game because of the limited daily progression, but it turns out it's quite soothing. You don't get penalties for skipping a day. Story line quests have no time limit and sometimes you won't be able to complete them for a few days. If you've finished all daily quests and want to play more you can start decorating or work on your fish/bug/shell collection. I really like it as a daily part of my life. The stories of the individual bears are also quite touching at times.Also, the dev team is quite active on discord. They're still working on new features (and some small bugs) and they really listen to feedback from the community. I realize this game and it's slow pace won't be everyone's cup of tea. The execution and polish is on point though.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a relaxing game after a stressful day and it is probably my favorite game right now. I've played every single day since I bought it! Like the game states, you can get 1-2 hours of gameplay before you're left to just farm or decorate, but I like that because it doesn't get tiring. I'm the type who needs to complete my collection, so I love finding stuff to donate to the captain. I like that you get rewarded with items that you don't have to buy. The controls can be a bit weird at first, but you get used to it. It can cost a lot for upgrades, and I find myself running out of space fast. The island also expands relatively fast, so I feel like I can't keep up with placing enough lamps. Resources can also be hard to come by. It can also be hard to find some items for the quests, so I buy clues often. I assume these things will get easier the more I play.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this! The main gameplay is fairly simple - talk to npcs for quests, feed logs to your fire to expand the map, chain lanterns to bring color back to the island, and collect a wide variety of resources using the tools you'll gradually acquire. Over time, you'll also be able to craft furniture to decorate with, cook food, plant flowers and fruit-bearing plants, raise several different kinds of animals, rescue lovelorn imps, buy clothes for your character, fill out your item archive, and take part in festive events. There is absolutely nothing challenging or taxing about these tasks, so I find it a very soothing way to wrap up my evening, or to de-stress when I'm feeling anxious. Very much OG Animal Crossing vibes with a ghostly twist.The game is specifically crafted for shorter play sessions of 1-3 hours/day, so it's great for both older kids and busy adults. It took about 3.5 months of daily play to complete all the story elements, and now I am cozily continuing to manage my island, experience the seasonal changes, and hunt down elusive bugs and fish. The date and day/night cycles in-game are synced with your computer clock, so it will take at least a year to see everything the game has to offer. I love each eccentric resident of the island, and I love that uncovering more about them requires investing the time and energy over several weeks to become friends with them. Through regular interactions, you get just enough incremental details to piece together what happened to each of them while they were alive, as well as what led to their deaths. It's not an immersive or epic storytelling style, but it's highly effective - allowing their bittersweet stories to unfold organically, and forcing you to get to know them before having your heart break for them. The game doesn't shy away from sad or difficult topics; however, it always leans into the mundane humanity of them, making each character's struggles and mistakes feel impactful specifically because they are so relatable or common. The tough subjects are also balanced out by humorous dialogue and flavor text that keep the game from ever sitting too long in a dark place.In terms of overall production values, the art is adorable, and the soundtrack is still relaxing even after 343 hours of playtime. While I do have some minor gripes about how cluttered the decor can feel, how hard it can sometimes be to click on the one specific thing you want, and how finicky the heartbroken imps can be, the gameplay has on the whole felt very polished and intuitive.I appreciate that the developers are highly receptive to player feedback, and are continuing to put out updates with new gameplay features, quality of life enhancements, and necessary patches. The latest update added cats, bunnies, and AoE farming via accordion playing, so if that's not quality content I don't know what is!I bought the game on sale, but it is worth the full asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play this game if you're looking to binge multiple hours or progress quickly, because it won't let you do that. It is time-gated, similar to animal crossing, but there are only X amount of things to do each day until you're forced to log off. That being said, I'm into this type of game since I can play 30 minutes each day and feel like I'm progressing towards multiple goals. There are a ton of things to collect and badges to earn. I'm literally only an hour in but I get the gist of it and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a super chill game you can play for an hour or so each day, this is the game for you. It's like an Animal Crossing/Spiritfarer hybrid.Be aware - this game IS time-gated, which means that after you've helped the spirits with the quests for the day, no more are available until the next day. This is intended - it gives you something to look forward to each day, and lets you progress the story in real time over months. A lot of people are unhappy with this but if you've played any AC you know how well this system works. It's a peaceful, chill game - not something that should be binged in a week. That being said, after the quests are done, it's not like the game locks you out - you can still craft, forage, fish, buy/sell etc. And as more spirits are unlocked daily you'll have more to do as each bear  has their own requests.I'm definitely looking forward to playing this each day. And I appreciate the QoL improvements over ACNL - it tells you which items haven't been added to the encylopedia yet, it's easy to make money, you don't have to swap between all your tools when you want to dig/mine (the game just figures it out when I click places and you don't need to have all your materials ON YOU when you to craft.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've put about 38 hours into this game so far. It's a very chill, casual game that's good for taking my mind off of things for a while. Because the tasks are daily and finite, I don't find myself getting lost playing for too long, and I also appreciate that the game does not punish you for not playing for a while, so you can pick it back up and play for a few minutes, an hour, whenever. It definitely lives up to its name as well, the furniture items, bears, and pets are all very cute, and the atmosphere or the game is very cozy and cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: "Cozy" is the right word to describe this game! I love the graphics and the characters; I also appreciate how you can keep coming back to find new collectables, and take your time with the quests and the missions. It's so relaxing playing this game, and I love gathering supplies to decorate the island and buy new outfits. The story is very heartfelt too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The important thing to know going into this game is that it's all about patience. You can't marathon through the story & you can't play for 6 hours straight, all by design. This game is a fantastic clone of animal crossing with a lot of tweaks on those mechanics to make it easier and more pleasant to play (hello fishing that doesn't make me die on the inside), and it actually has a plot! A plot involving a host of lovely ghost bears with unfinished business.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best game like Animal crossing thats not Animal Crossing out there. This is meant to be played slowly.... a little bit everyday... as you discover new 'villagers' and items. It feels great to discover a bit more bout each character as they slowly remember who they were. The dialogues are awesome, and the art really fits the theme. There's a ton of content here. A lot of materials for crafting, recipes, fish, insects, clothes.... If you like collecting stuff, you will love this. Really relaxing experience, a must play to any lovers of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you are looking for something relaxing that uses a real-time clock. After finishing the quests the bears give (which range from 3 to 5 depending on the day), I like to fish, collect shells, and catch bugs. It has become part of a morning ritual for me. I drink coffee and play this game until I need to get ready for work. It's a nice and relaxing way to start a day. Sometimes I even play after work.New fish, shells, and items seem to appear pretty regularly. Overall, a nice relaxing time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect little game to relax and just sink into the world it offers! It is very similar to Animal Crossing in its gameplay and Spiritfarer in its story (so if you like those, you will love Cozy Grove!), going after your real time and setting up events and content you might need to wait a day for and finding old spirits and helping them. The game offers great gameplay for about 1-2 hours a day and is nice for whenever you are bored or just want to relax.The music, artstyle and its characters are incredible nice and lovely designed, you will enjoy your first foot you step onto the island immediatly and feel invested into story and the spirits housing on the island. This is not for people who expect a action or survival game, similar to Don't Starve or others, so keep in mind that Cozy Grove is really more for your own relaxation and good times. I am very interested to see where the story is going and how my upcoming days on the island will look like! Only sad thing I can see for now is that there is no multiplayer, but on the same hand, there is not much multiplayer content as of right now anyway and everything is more tailored to just yourself - which is absolutely not bad at all! Big recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Am I one of the few people that have actually stuck around to see the end game credits? :)The game is very soothing, music and sound is superb if you need to clean your head after a stressful day.  The artwork is amazing, I really like the style! Story of ghosts is interesting, only downside would be that you actually need to spend some to unlock the storyline
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of reviews comparing Cozy Grove to Animal Crossing and while I can see how people could draw similarities in aesthetics the game is far more comparable to Farmville. Yes, a lot of Cozy Grove is time gated-- and it's not necessarily a bad thing. Often times I will play for about 1-1.5 hours a day before I exhaust spirit logs (what you need to expand the island) and quests and I'm told to come back another day. Nodes are exhausted after a certain point, and I've found as the island expands and your tools are upgraded nodes appear far more frequently. Bugs and fish respawn infinitely. I do have a love-hate relationship with fishing as the animations are slower than bug catching and the crafting chain requires you to recycle most of your fish for bones making it the more tedious of the two. Personally, I've sunken a lot of time into games up front and gotten bored of them or burned out. The nice thing about Cozy Grove is it's very relaxing and I always feel like I'm progressing. Badges and achievements are easy to achieve and obtained simply by exploring the world and doing daily tasks. Everything you do gives you reward currency to buy custom items and creatures to decorate your island. You get recipes quite frequently for foods and furniture as well as a chance to buy what you don't have. I really like that they don't give you duplicate recipes for things (like a game we all know and love). The story so far is cute, dark, and wonderful. Kudos to the devs for continuing to give the game updates. I look forward to playing the DLC when it is released this spring!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've played 25 hours, and I haven't come to the end of anyone's story yet. It's chill and laid back, think Animal Crossing. You need to do what you can do and then maybe come back the next day. I will say it gets a bit grindy the further you get into it, people will want you to collect things that could take multiple days or even weeks to get. The option to have it perpetually daytime has been a lifesaver for me, as I find I have a lot of trouble finding items when the game is in evening/nighttime. The art style is beautiful, and I appreciate being able to see what is behind most things really easily. The only thing I would change are the amount of coins it costs to upgrade your storage, as I find I'm out of storage really easily even with multiple upgrades because I simply can't afford it. Pro-tip though, you can just drop items in your tent (especially useful when you have a second room) and they will remain there.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It is the first game I booted up on my steam deck and it met all of my expectations of what I define as "cozy". The art-style, music, characters, quests - all is contributing to a relaxing and wholesome atmosphere! The only complain I have is that I cannot play for longer than 2 hours/day due to lack of quests, however, that is not a big deal for me. Recommend for everyone who is looking for a relaxing and cute game for the evening)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game already. And I love it so much that it drives me bonkers about the optimized play time, haha. I can appreciate that it helps with maximizing game time and can help with not sitting in front of the computer all day, but my poor hyper fixation head and heart can't take it. xD I love the graphics, music and story line so far and I can't wait to help more bear spirits on Cozy Grove Island!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxed game with soothing music and little tasks for you to do to pass time.  The game is intended for you to play EVERY day for a short amount of time ala Animal Crossing.  The game forces this action, by only allowing you to complete so many tasks each day before it tells you to go do some fishing or collect seashells in the meantime.  So technically, you could play for longer, but I can't imagine fishing and collecting seashells is going to hold your interest for very long on it's own.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love Animal Crossing?Do you love Bears?Well boy do I have the game for me!Cozy Grove is a charming and lighthearted game where you get to make your own little camp and decorate a home like you would in animal crossing while helping the spirit bears of Cozy Grove find peace by helping them with daily quests which are on a real time clock, so players with limited time a day to play don't miss out by not having 4+ hours a day to grind.It's important to note that the game as you progress will handle subjects of grief and loss which may be a lot for some people, while the character will ask you if you're sure you want to hear about their last day I felt I should add this to my review(most importantly you can hug all the bears). would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: There's only so much that you can do in a day, but it's made that way. It's for playing like 40minutes - an hour a day, not for long sessions. I enjoy that there's only so much I can do, because it gives me back the rest of my day. It also gives me something to look forward to every day--I have to check in on my bears & buy new clothes!It's also just a cute little game with great art & the dialogue is cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I'd really like to recommend this game.It's very relaxing and the art style and music is just top notch!Unfortunately though the pacing and progression really destroys this game.At first it didn't seem like a problem to be time-gated with how much things you can do each real-life day.But when you have quests that take you a few days to complete and just very annoying RNG it starts to get really really frustrating because there just isn't anything to do each day.I get it that the devs want you to take time playing the game and don't feel like you are missing out just because you can only play for half an hour every day.But as it stands right now it just does not feel rewarding or joyful to play at all.So sadly, as it currently stands, I can not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game to play with a really unique story, smooth stylized graphics, and a relaxing style of game play. In many ways the game can be similar to that of animal crossing by doing quests for animals, living on a island, and real time play. However it offers a lot more secrets to discover! Personally my favorite part is having the multi coloured pet birds all around my camp site!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set on a comfy and slightly creepy island that reshapes itself a bit each day. You're a little scout helping the spirits of this island. The graphics are great, the writing is quirky, and the audio/music is very chill. There's crafting, cooking, fishing, gardening, raising animals, collecting, and designing your island/camp. The mechanic of lighting up the world through your actions is cool.The game wants you to play a little bit each day and I think it is really effective and fun during that time. The developer is really responsive - putting out some quality updates with a real ear to player issues. Some people may view the gameplay as time-gated progress and fetch quests. If so it is not the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to Animal Crossing but different in a way that keeps you motivated and understand there's no pressure to check in every day. If you're unable to play during daylight hours, there's a daylight setting so you don't have to constantly play in the dark - something I definitely appreciated! I got this game on sale but it's well worth more than the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love Cozy Grove soo much. It's design is super cute and gameplay is fun. I have this game on 2 different devices and love it on both systems. The soundtrack is lo-fi goodness. Even though that the game "Limits gameplay" it was designed as something you play for a short time every day and I love that about it. It takes the pressure off of a casual game and it doesn't shame you if you are away from it for more than a couple of days, like other games I know of.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, it was my fault to not read up on the game so in short words: The Game Is Time Gated: it is 1-2 hours of content every 24 hour period.Without the time gate I would recommend the game.I had other gripes aside of the time gate: the UI is terribly colored, hard to read. The game is beautiful but the daylight is too bright, night is a bit too blue. Tho at this point I'm just nitpicking...
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Animal Crossing New Horizons, then boy howdy do I have a game for you. There is foraging, adorable spirit bears, a blathers knockoff that is a seagull, the list goes on. It's meant to be played for about 30 minutes a day, very akin to ACNH, with different quests that help build up the community. I could honestly say that this is one of my favorite indie games of 2021.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game but I honestly never finished the main story because... Well, way too much fetch quests. And some of them are so long to complete, it's really frustrating to start the game on a new day knowing that all you'll do will be fetching random stuff and talking to NPCs who will give you even more fetching quests. Also it prevented me from crafting furnitures and things that I really wanted for my camp, I almost never dared to use my materials in case it would be useful on another quest. This got tiresome after some time. Another thing that bothered me was the animals: to have all the essence I needed or had to fetch, I had to adopt a TON of them. For real. I didn't even get that attached to them in the end, they just became cattle. The thing is, to get essence, you need to feed them what they want, and to cook the food you also need specifics essences. And there I was, stuck, being unable to complete some quests because I didn't manage to have the good essence, the only way was to miraculously fish some or that the store would have ONE. I mainly recommend it though, because of the art, the NPCs who are really funny, the soothing music and the bunch of personnalisation from your clothes, to you surroundings with furnitures, flower and plants, and all the cute animals you can adopt. But I think it isn't well balanced enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely little fetch game. I really enjoy it and the fact that one runs out of things to do without having to play for hours is honestly kind of nice. It's relaxing (for the most part, photography quests can get a tad difficult) and also forces you to calm down in the playing as the game requires you to play for multiple real time days rather than having a faster in game clock. There are a bunch of customization options for the character and while it does have some sad elements to it (sad memories from spirits and more) it's really sweet. Give this a go if you like calm fetch games with some fishing, digging, taking care of animals, that sort of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a darker and sadder Animal Crossing. So if you're looking to scratch that particular itch with some daily tasks and befriending your ghostly neighbors, then definitely pick up this game! The game includes fishing, bug catching, crafting, baking, as well as hidden items to hunt for and neighbors to talk to and help solve their problems. Even if it's not on sale, it's an amazing deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Since getting this game almost a month ago, I have played every morning. It scratches that Animal Crossing itch like no other game has been able to do. It takes about an hour a day to do everything that I can do, but that's fine with me, it's one of the things I like about this game. I love the weird, cute looking animals you can collect, feed, and level up. I love talking to every bear every day even if they do repeat what they say. I love collecting things and decorating my little spot on the island. I love when I unlock a new bear and find out what kind of bear they are. I love how the island changes - like the post office is there one day, gone the next, and back again the day after that - almost like the island itself is alive.Really looking forward to the changing seasons and I can see myself playing daily for at least a year just to see the different stuff each season brings.Rated 9/10 - because I do not like the in-game camera that you use to take pictures to complete some quests. Actually, the camera itself isn't bad - it's the quests for specific pictures that I could do without.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Its a "must to chill" game cuz sometimes, when all the quests done then you must stop pushing yourself then just do some fishing and catching bugs...The animations and musics are good enough to sooth yourself.Its pretty much fun when u reach the next season (from spring to summer, from summer to autumn, etc) cuz more and more things to do and discover. If not, sometimes, it quite like doing some homeworks that the bears give you daily.Take time, with no pressure, go collect stuffs and earn badges. The amount of collections and clothes, trees, birds, deers, badges, decorations are huge then you will slowly finish them with joy.Tons of things for decoration, and the kittyy meow meow are sooooo cute.Love the stories behind each soul, also the drawings. Spry Fox team people are also really nice and kind.Take it easy to enjoy the game ;)Appreciated!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot! It's cute, simple, and a very good alternative to Animal Crossing on Nintendo Switch. A lot of people complain about the "real-time system", and you can't really progress without waiting and taking a day at a time. It's important to be aware of that, but it isn't necessarily a bad thing. Good for learning some patience! I should also mention that Animal Crossing, New Horizon  also has the same system, but nobody seems to mind. Although, it would be nice to have it as an option instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good wholesome fun. You help the bear ghosts on the island, harvest fruits and flowers, fish, catch bugs and care for spirit animals. I enjoy all of the little side parts of the game like collecting flowers, reuniting separated imps and making food as much as I do interacting and helping the bears. The game play is simple, but satisfying, and I enjoy the limited daily game play. Sometimes the search and retrive tasks can be a little tedious, but if you run out of patience you can always ask the ranger bear for directions to the hidden objects. I really enjoyed the little ducklings that followed you around at the begining of the game, even with them sometimes getting in the way of fishing. Very cute! I would have loved to have them back. Ultimately all round a really good cosy game, would definitely recommend to anyone who loves a wholesome game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of cozy games, Cozy Grove is a game where you play a spirit scout who, after getting stranded on an island, is tasked with helping the spirits of the island recover their memories. Requirements for such quests include gathering items scattered throughout the island. It is very relaxing and fun to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute and it's relaxing, and it's way less annoying than Animal Crossing, but ultimately I think it's a waste of your time. I don't have an drop-in replacement alternative in mind for you since I'm not into Animal Crossing-type games, but if you want to:- Feel chill cozy summer camp island vibes: Try A Short Hike- Think about helping dead folks: Try Spiritfarer- Feel like you're outside in a Boy/Girl/Enby Scout-type way: Try Firewatch- Need to do a fishing minigame: Hoo boy. Try Hades, not because it has the best minigame, but because it's a way better way to sink your time than this game, and it *does* have a fishing minigame. Or I guess Stardew Valley.- Just do easy stuff day after day just because: Try brushing your teeth
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the type of game that I would like. And I tried really, really hard, but I couldn't get into it because:The game stretches itself out on purpose. You can't just sit down and keep playing and accomplish all the goals. Some goals you can't progress except by coming back to play tomorrow, collect the item, check in the next day, etc. At several places I felt really lost at what to do next. A few quests devolve into waiting for new digging spots to spawn, hoping it has the items you need. Everything else about it, I loved. The graphics. The color vs greyscale. The music. The little forest creatures. Loved it. But because of the progression/ stuck-ness issues I don't feel this game is worth $15 as it is right now. Maybe I don't want to be forced into only being able to spend 10 productive minutes in the game a day. Maybe some days I want to put in an hour or two. It should be my choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:♡ Great casual life-sim gameplay loop♡ Time gate is perfect for short sessions♡ Charming art style and hand-drawn visuals♡ Daily gradual progression always gives players something to do♡ Characters with meaningful backstoriesCons:♡ General lack of depth in gameplay.♡ furnitures don't have any interactable elements.♡ Daily progression restriction can become a major hindrance.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Review being written after just a few days in. Will update if anything larger crops up as I uncover things.Something I'm sorely missing from this game is having more non-quest-related reasons to check back occasionally within the day, whenever I have small pockets of time. In AC, there are villagers with varying personalities moving about doing their own things, who would at times interrupt you to ask for a favor or simply talk to you. You could enter their houses and see what they're up to, nab a recipe from them, cure them if they're sick, etc. While there isn't always something going on, there's always that possibility that something MIGHT, and it makes the game feel that much more alive. There's no such thing here—you have a fixed set of bears that reside in the island and your task is to gradually uncover them. They don't really do much outside of their own specific functions (baker bear, postal bear, etc.). So once you've got that 20 to 30 minutes of gaming done, that's about it. All that's left is gathering, which feels especially tedious when the environment feels like it's missing some dynamism. Apart from that, this is a fairly sweet, comforting game that won't be for everyone. The art style is charming, the music relaxing. I find myself not really caring about the characters much at the moment. I wish fishing felt more satisfying, as it's one of my favorite activities in games in general. Not so much here.I'm curious to see what else the game offers as I uncover more things, and if Spryfox has plans to expand the game beyond that, but as of now, it fills a niche market that I appreciate.Update: Checking out this game again after taking a long break, quite a number of QOL stuff added and the Fall season looks super charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Very repetitive. I didn't mind the real time gate keeping progress. But what little gameplay you can do a day is very boring, uninspired, .You search for X amount of things scattered around the map. Find me 7 leaves. Find 5 lost mails. Look for 8 bugs.Every single day it's like that.Imagine the dullest fetch quests you've seen from an Ubisoft title. Now build a game around that.It's sad because I really liked the art style, but a good art style can only carry your game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to say I enjoyed this game and I did, but there wasn't enough of it. As much as I like the gameplay I can't get over the fact that it only offers a small amount of the story each day. I would preffer to get more things to do in a day than just a couple missions and foraging. There is only enough content daily for an hour of playing after which there is nothing at all to do than walking aroudn the island and swapping between fishing and foraging.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, casual game for a surprising amount of heart. I love the aspect of helping the ghost bears of the island finding peace. And a good collect-a-thon is right up my alley. It's adorable, I love the pace of it (so laid-back), and the seasonal updates keep things fresh. Easily one of my favorite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I started this game a few weeks ago and considered quitting after a few in-game 'days'. I didn't like the forced pacing, which requires you to complete a few tasks a day and then leaves you at a loose end (unless you time-travel), making you wait until the next 'day' to complete similar, slightly more difficult tasks with quite repetitive dialogue.And then after the worst work week I've had in a while, I sat down and just relaxed with it. I suddenly found the deliberately slow pacing calming instead of irritating, and felt really pleased once I'd crossed off all my little tasks for the day. After a bit longer playing it, I've decided Cozy Grove is actually the perfect game to slow my life down for a short while in the evenings, and gives me the headspace to zone out on a fun, spooky island.I'd recommend this game if you're looking for something slower, more chill and with some cute characters to brighten up the experience. The game looks and feels very cozy and the music fits this vibe too. The dialogue *does* get a bit repetitive and there's only so much you can do in a day, but if your work-life balance could do with a bit of reset (like mine!), I'd definitely buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Update: In this current state the game is borderline infuriating. I just tried to fix it effing up 4 days of progress for me by alt+f4 and of course it didn't work. Here's the thing: randomized games are fine. It helps create more content without more work. But ONLY when this randomization is SUFFICIENTLY CONTROLLED. I am on day 10, I have 2 quests that I wasn't able to complete for 4 days and these aren't the first ones. One asks me to burn 4 relics, which you only get 1 per day- and of course I only find new types that I bring to the collection, not burn, so no luck here. Then I have spent 4 days looking for a poisonous mushroom, 14 eggs and some other ingredients for godawful quest for the bird. I finally had everything, cooked and ready. And on the way to give these to the bird I met another villager who asked for ANY cooked food. "Hey" I thought " I have tofu and jam and salad and candy in my storage, easy money". So I give him ANY food. AND THIS MF TAKES THE DISH THAT I TRIED TO MAKE FOR THE BIRD FOR 4 DAYS. F O U R  D A Y S. REAL HUMAN DAYS.Before that I was gonna write how the developers listen to the feedback, how they compressed first 5 days into 3, expanded storage (here I have another wonderfully infuriating story about needing to upgrade Mr Kit's store instead of storage which I didn't know and the money is real tight in the beginning, so another quest on first week took me 4 days).And after 10 days the constant searching for objects is REALLY tiring. Sure, Charlotte can help for 100g, but I want to play the game, not check boxes. And the baker that takes hours to do anything (which additionally isn't visible anywhere, I just noticed that it says estimate on the bottom after ordering 5 dishes. And the game really overestimates how willing I am to come back in a few hours)So yeah, for now I'm done. The fkg bird egg tea broke me. I don't have any eggs and I'm not willing to give this game any more of my time before I know that it's gonna be worth it. Because right now I'm tired of fighting it to have fun.Oh man, I really want to like this game, but so far I played for 3 days and it took me an hour each to run out of things to do.I have to say- I did not realise this was the same real-time bs as Animal Crossing is. I know some people like it and it is relaxing for them, but that is the reason I don't play either AC I have anymore- I don't like it feeling like a chore. Today I may want to play for 5 hours and tomorrow I might not have time or energy at all.And still- I played AC for 100+ hours each, since every day it opened up more and more activities, you could remake your whole village/island if you wanted to, hang out with real friends, etc. Here activities so far are gathering and fishing, remaking the grove is not an oprion and there is obviously no multiplayer (which on it's own is not a bad thing, I prefer singleplayer, but it doesn't help with creeping up boredom). Besides, it really surprised me here that on day 3 you don't get enough logs for a new ghost- makes me really think how much more time consuming it's gonna get each time.One of the main things I love about the game is the artstyle, but the way it's implimented is really irritating. There is no way to rotate the world like in similar "2d in 3d" Don't Starve, so things can get hidden or obscured by anything, let alone simply blend into surrounding because of the amount of sprites per m^2. And considering that most of the quests so far are fetching and most activities is collecting it really turns into "Where's Waldo" trying and spot collectable shells among decorative ones, collectable leaf piles among non-collectable shrubs and hoping the one ore stone is not hidden by other non-ore stones.I know I sound exhasperated after only 3 hours of play and that should tell you something.And again- I REALLY want to like this game and I will play more hoping there is something ahead after the hump, but with how little time, energy and patience I have after this year I can't recommend it thus far.

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for little time only, but so far the game is everything it promised would be. But be warned - this isn't a game to speed-run, your daily progress is limited. This is the game you casually play to relax, you collect items, complete quests, craft and cook, and decorate your camp while soothing music plays in the background. The art style is adorable and magical. The Bears are very cute as well, and I love it that you can freely hug the bears and pet your animals whenever you want, there is no limit. Overall it's just an extremely cozy (how fitting) and relaxing game suitable for anyone who wants to just chill and not worry about grinding to develop their character and competing with other players or NPC. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game. I am like 110 days in and I don't think I've missed many days since first starting. The art style is extremely cute. There is a surprising amount of clothes so you can have a whole new look every day. You can get adorable pet cats and feed various animals that you have around your island. I'm basically addicted to this game and view it as part of my day now. The story in the game can get quite dark at times too for such a childish looking game. I love it so much.My only gripe is sometimes I wish I could do more than fish or catch bugs once I exhaust the daily tasks.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute! The mechanics are pretty intuitive and the characters are all super charming, it's easy to keep coming back just to learn more about them. It's also pretty easy to earn enough money to keep ahead of quests, whether through collection rewards or selling or recycling. I do wish there was a way to automate harvesting, at least in the player's little clearings (though maybe there is and I just haven't played far enough to unlock that!). To me, at least, that's easily the most tedious part of playing, but farming large-scale is also optional, so I'm willing to forgive it either way. The biggest thing is the characters, and they're all just wonderful. Learning about their histories and the tragedies that tie them all together is heartbreaking, but their presence also brings bundles of new joy. I love it

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and Cons... This is a nice wholesome cute game and I love the art style and how relaxing it is to play but I will say this. The game goes based on real time so for example some goods come in the mail and you have to wait hours for them in real time. I don't like how you can only help so many ghosts a day before the game cuts you off saying you can't do any more for that day but I do like that it leaves you with free time to explore and collect items in the game and craft and decorate the place without having to worry about quests. I still overall recommend this game though because it is delightful to play you just can't really play it for long periods of times.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: One more edit here, I'll try to keep it short. Unfortunately I will change my recommendation back to "no". The patch to enlarge inventory really only helped for a few days. Once again my camp is littered with items I can't store. I don't farm resources, it's just from collecting what I see while doing tasks. Additionally, this game requires you to hold quest items for days at a time so right now I have 6 or 7 quest items that I can't use. You either throw them on the ground or have them take 7 spots in storage. One other thing, this is just preference but after 22 hours I am finding the game boring. The only thing to do in this game is to collect resources and take them to NPC's. Progression in Cozy Grove isn't satisfying. You get one more bear to do tasks for and a small section of the island unlocks. The art is good, the music is good but it's always the same. Their are a bunch of different types of furniture and decorations in the game but the map is so small and cluttered there isn't anywhere to put stuff. This game needs a lot of work. It needs more variety than just fetch tasks, it needs to give you the ability to move things and customize your island. I hope to see better updates in the future but for now I will say bye to Cozy Grove.EDIT: I am revising my review since the update but leaving the old one in. I am very pleased with the devs. They really listened to the community and the most recent patch solved most of the complaints I had. Stack sizes have increased and there was a free storage upgrade which is significant. Another thing I notice is if you are given a quest it takes the item from storage without needing to return, really helpful. The only thing I would still like to see is a search/sort function for items. There are A LOT of items in this game and I still think it is difficult to find certain things. So happy for this update!So far I actually enjoy Cozy Grove overall, but it has one huge problem, resource management. Not good for a game centered around gathering resources. I am very early game and already majorly annoyed by resource management. One problem is stack size. The stacks are really small, it's dependent on the item but, for example, "leafy greens. This is a very common resource, you can get around 6 from on harvest and there will be multiple bushes on the map. The stack size is only 10 for this item, so in two days I had like 5 slots of inventory filled with leafy greens. This is just from casually harvesting as I do the daily quests, I ended up just throwing them on the ground, will they disappear? Can I get them easily later? We'll see. The spirits will also give you quest items you need later. So you are obligated to use storage to hold them for days. I can't even imagine how annoying this will be later. I have found recipes that require 50 of X resource but the stack size is significantly smaller than that so to craft one thing it will take ~20% of your inventory. Consequently you are constantly having to drop things and run back and forth to storage, which brings me to my next problem. I am on day 5, and have already upgraded storage twice, it's full and the storage upgrades are pretty expensive. The stack sizes are the same so those 50 leafy greens from my inventory also take 5 spots in my storage. Another issue is there is no way to sort the inventory or storage. Many things look similar so if you need to take something out you have to look at every little thing. The bigger problem is adding things. If you want to add something from your inventory to storage you need check that it is there checking everything and then manually adding it. Again, many things look the same, there are multiple golden colored colored fruits; come to think of it, I think every fruit I have is a nearly identical gold color, there are two red mushrooms, multiple potatoes etc...This also compounds the time gate feature. Maybe you need a specific resource but you don't have it because you literally couldn't collect it because no inventory, if you can't find it, sorry, come back later. For example, right now I have two quests. One is to get an item for one of the spirits that can only be obtained from helping the others. The other is to get salt for a different one, the salt has to be bought from the store but to do this the store has to upgraded, which takes one day so I am blocked on two quests. All this makes it to where you are constantly having to drop things and run back and forth to your camp. Then you don't have things you need because no space. You're constantly being told you can't do something now, come back for this later, or you can't carry this thing you need, it makes the relaxing and cozy vibe this game wants to provide fade to annoyance. What I would personally think the devs can do is increase stack size and inventory size and put in sorting functions: search, sort by type, alphabetically etc... I really do think they way items are grouped should be altered as well. There is a lot of content, a lot of resources, this is good but if I don't have the inventory to save the things I find it doesn't matter. The 7 or 8 fish I have found on day 5 shouldn't consume 20% of my storage.I will keep playing and look forward to updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is one of the best relaxing games that I've come across in a while. From the music to the beautiful art style and concepts, this game is worth every single penny. Pros: This game is very similar to Animal Crossing in that you end up stranded on an island, taking care of and providing for the individuals who happen to reside there. However, this comparison falls short in quite a few ways (negative and positive). Unlike Animal Crossing, there is a story component that really draws you in to the game. You're helping restless spirits from a wide range of personalities and backgrounds come to terms with their death/past. Talking about the NPCs, they're all wonderful if a bit cold in the beginning. Some of their quests are a bit tedious (especially the postal runs), but the dialogue and "heart events" make up for it. There's a lot of diversity in personal struggles that these characters go through, such as: relationship/family issues; memory loss; as well as discussions of the effects of disability/being a disabled individual in society. Overall, the concept of being a Spirit Scout is very wholesome and fulfilling.  Cons:Like I mentioned, a lot of the quests are repetitive and tedious, especially given the overcrowded nature of the island's layout. There's a lot of things that you can't move (trees, monuments, etc), which can be frustrating when you're trying to decorate and/or any of the resources. Despite being one of it's marketing points, it doesn't really have as much custom-ability as you'd think (for those who really care), which can grate on the nerves of those who like to keep things organized/a certain theme in areas. Obviously, I can live with these cons and the potential cons of only being able to do a few tasks a day/having to wait multiple days to get items. This aspect of waiting really helps create a mellow environment in which you're able to just spend an hour or two each day going through a little to-do list, unlike the "sand-boxy, spend hours playing at a time," nature of Animal Crossing. Despite all of these comparisons, Cozy Grove is a game that will likely become a well known name like SV and ACNH given it's originality and the talent that went into making it. Overall, Cozy Grove is a lovely game that will quickly become a part of your down-time routine.

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh... I'm so disappointed. What have you become, Spry Fox?I really wanted to like Cozy Grove. In theory, it has so much I love in a game: slow but steady progression, collecting and harvesting, decorations. It's one of the few games that borrows from Animal Crossing in which it's in real time, and you're rewarded for playing every day in it. On paper, it seemed like a mix of Animal Crossing, Spiritfarer and Story of Seasons. You get pets! You have sets to decorate your house and town with! You can cook! All the while helping the Grove's spirits and learning more about their backstory.The theory is great. The execution... Not so much. It's an okay game, but it's stretched thin and meant to be played for 100+ days, when the endgame is painfully empty. And none of the features I talked about are very rewarding. I'll get to it.I had a great time in the first 10 hours or so. So much, I got excited, I bought the DLC. I'm now sitting at 80 hours gameplay and have not been able to start it, as the dlc only starts once the main quests have been done. All well, I don't mind putting a lot of hours in a game, as long as it's enjoyable. And here, it's just not the case.As I said, the game is designed and there's hardly anything to do after day 30 or so... It becomes a drag, you keep on farming but there is nothing else to do. I guess feeding the bird again to get your 432nd essence. What you're really waiting for, though, is the story. But even then, it feels like the bears are just stalling to say anything meaningful. They'll ask for you to catch 5 rare fish for the 10th time (their quests are also repetitive) so they'll tell you their story. What do they say? Quote one of the characters (spoilers ahead!):Hardly a soul survived the accident. Not even mine.Huh? Ye want me to continue my story, do ye?Arr, I see. One good line isn't enough.Well then. I'll tell ye the next part... soon.That's all you get. One line. Want to hear more? You'll need to wait a few days. All stories are painfully stretched thin, stalled and worked up when there's not much content really. I caught myself skipping dialogues more often than not -- something I NEVER do in games! The other features are not much fun either. Cooking is pretty simple, gathering resources has awfully long animations (no, I don't want to see my character and all of her pets dance after I've plucked my 597th flower), the fish and bugs in the game are also artificially made more varied: 4-5 bugs will have exactly the same design, the same description but different colors. I'd much rather have 20 original species than 20+80 reskins...Well, at least you get to decorate your home and town, right? Not so fast... Your pets and cats have opinions and will love you based on what you used to decorate. Both my home and the Grove became a haphazard clutterfest and any decorating projects I might have end up becoming too convoluted for me to even start. Long story short, this game tries to get inspiration from animal crossing, but in all the wrong way. Due to many of their game design choices, it ends up feeling more like a lazy free-to-play mobile or facebook game than anything else. It made me wonder if the devs even played their own game to the end. That being said, there still are a lot of people who love and enjoy it as it is. I think it's enjoyable if you don't mind playing it for 20 hours or so and then dropping it when it inevitably becomes dull and chore-y.For the completionists like me, even if you enjoy the genre... Don't. Trust me. You're going to have a bad time.
