_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game with interesting new ideas, stymied by poor design decisions that make it a chore. If you like Stardew Valley type games, and don't mind the restrictions usually found on mobile, it could be for you.Good:- Interesting characters, a slow burn unravelling of their stories- A nice 'illumination' mechanic whereby helping spirits each day lights up the area and enables resource harvesting. Feels rewarding and like you're making progress.- Lots of outfits and recipes to collect for collector / crafter types- A mysterious shifting island, where the surroundings of the ghosts you help gradually come into existence and organise themselves more and more as days go by, forming a beautiful little hamlet you can appreciate walking through.Bad:- Wants you to grind out vast item requirements, except has no grind mechanic but to keep logging in each day.- Far too many items to handle. Even with the game's generous base camp storage and backpack, you run out of space repeatedly. Even worse, while it gives hundreds of decor / furniture options, there's almost nowhere to put anything outside of inside your own tent, which even when expanded is poky. The game does eventually reveal some open-spaces it calls something like orchards, but these are far from your base and by default are not illuminated - so you won't be able to harvest them without doing daily quests.- Outfitting the tent needs a dedicated interface to be viable. - Huge array of crafting items but no apparent way to preview them when at the crafting station. Also, why can't I have my own crafting station? Walking 30 seconds left to the crafter just discourages me from bothering to outfit my tent.- Super-annoying delays on most tasks like burning items in the campfire or harvesting resources. If the game let you keep moving while these happened - or if it at least streamline things by pushing them to your backpack without animating every single item, it would feel much less cumbersome.  Items that are harvested also fail to 'jump' into your backpack if you move too soon, meaning every time you harvest something you have to hover around until it's definitely picked up.- Clunky interface for specific things like putting items into storage. While you can click a bunch of items to store them by double-clicking the last, if you happen to click-and-drag, everything gets deselected! Infuriating when you're already annoyed by the need to make space. - Quest items shouldn't appear in your bag at all; or at least they should not take up slots. A fairly transparent mobile-style 'upgrading' mechanic as well; 5 mixed greens make one fancy green, 5 fancy greens make 1 deluxe green, and some recipes requiring many deluxe greens... you see where this is going? And that of itself would be fine - if you could only grind things. But your only choice is to wander the island and hope those items are available today. - Very, very Timegated. You can only make so much progress with the spirits each day, requiring you to come back day after day to keep unlocking the stories and expanding the island. While the game does seem to 'bank' a couple of days of progress if you can't play for a few days, it caps out at one quest per spirit, I think. I don't mind that every day isn't necessarily a story quest, but I don't feel encouraged to come back to the game specifically because I know I don't get to control the flow of events.  And as an older gamer, my time isn't always available daily - I rather get things done in blocks when I have the opportunity. And no, you can't change your system clock if that's your plan - the game even warns you that will break things. - Huuuuuge problems with layering of visuals. The layout is crowded making this more of a problem than you might think. Most of the daily quests are fetch quests; go look for this near a something something. But there's no way to expose the items behind others than walking very close to them. The game desperately needs a few keys to do the following: 1) Hide/fade out any un-interactable elements. Yes, the trees and terrain are beautiful, but the fetch quests just end up being skipped by talking to the NPC who will give you a marker - except every time you want to invoke that, you need to go back to NPC. So much time wasted running back and forth. Give us this mechanic as a base ability, Spry Fox... 2) Toggle interactive items to be 'on top'. Frequently you'll have pets wandering behind bushes, and you want to interact with them except the foreground blocks you - and so you just don't even bother.I want to love Cozy Grove - I feel like it could be another Stardew-style game with its own niche. But it just works against you so often, that you don't even want to keep playing. -spoiler tag- * one caveat : There is an item that can be used to harvest all nearby nodes - but you still have to hang around for everything to attract itself into your backpack. Close but not enough IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Within the hour and a half I played at first, I already knew I liked it that little bit more than Animal Crossing.My 'neighbors', as one ethereal bear calls them, are ghosts that need help moving on.As many have pointed out (mostly negatively), it is a real-time game.In the beginning, there isn't much to do until the next day.I don't know what people are expecting of this game but for those of you who have played AC, I'll tell you this:- There is no debts. Your coins are yours.- There is a 24/7 store. (With a variety of stock.)- That looming feeling of having to decide whether to donate or sell that fish? Gone.- The daunting feeling of having to save coins for a debt over buying new things? Gone.Most people said they finished the tutorial and the '1st day' in half an hour.If you're familiar with AC, that happened as well and picked up pace the following days.It's a simpler AC with a cute soundtrack, lovely art style and a bittersweet story of passing on.EDIT: Still enjoying this game even more after the updates. What AC still has issues with (e.g. multi-crafting) these guys fixed in a few updates. It's the only game I own that genuinely soothes my anxiety.

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is cute and I want to care about the story but it falls flat for me. The game play is much of the same fishing and catch bugs that you can get elsewhere and most of the bugs and fish are re-colors of the same model so not a whole lot of uniqueness to it. My biggest problem with it is that it uses real time and the story locks up until you wait a day in real life. You can technically change the time on your PC but that is a huge pain for a failing of the game itself. I wish I listened to my gut and stopped playing earlier so I could request a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the main story content and greatly enjoyed this game. I think it could use a new game+ feature where you can restart the story but keep you stuff and upgrades or maybe DLC where you start a new island and magically bring your stuff, but that's more work for the devs than a simple new game+. Either would help keep me playing more now that the story is done. I stay focused better with some long term goals.  It's very worth the money and time as is though. I was hesitant because I'd never played a game that is real time{time gated} and that is the main reason most don't like it or don't get it. I actually wound up liking this about it. It's nice and relaxing to just log in for an hour or 2 or less each day, do the story then mess about fishing and collecting things and be done.Some of the achievements are long term goals like play in every season or break excessive amounts of tools. So if you are a completionist, who needs to get them all, this might be frustrating for you. I do not see that as a main goal for the game though so it might not be the game for you if that's your thing. Most people who enjoy the game play it to relax for awhile not trying to min max and do it all fast.It looks nice and charming, it has a few mysteries and surprises to uncover. The story is fun and the music is very enjoyable and relaxing. The seasonal events have been good as well.There's no downsides to the game to me other than my wanting more.

Your job is to help the spirit bears with their final task on earth and help them accept what has happened. _childDocuments_.review: I like pretty much everything about this game. It's super cute, the story is amazing, I love the creative manners of resource farming and the way in which you can decorate the island. I would recommend anyone give this game a try: However, I have one problem with it.The story is not self paced.This wouldn't be so much of an issue because I like resource farming and decorating in itself, however you can't do a lot of decorating/resource farming of certain (many) items until you complete the quest allowing you to collect those things. The issue is you're only allowed to complete a certain number of quests in a day, at which point the game tells you "sorry, come back tomorrow to advance some more". You can still resource farm to your hearts content, but since the quests are directly linked to certain functionalities in the game, you're really just wandering the island in circles gathering leaf piles. You're only allowed about 1 or 1.5 hours of actual story gameplay per physical 24 hour day, which is super annoying to me. If it were open world exploration, it might be considerably less stifling, but you're on a little island (that you can only expand through the story quests). It's so annoying that it's honestly killing my enjoyment and I'm considering messing with my laptop clock just so I can progress a little. I have such little time to play games that I like to progress as much as possible in the time I do have, but this game expressly forbids that, or if it has an option to turn off the waiting period, I haven't found it yet.All that being said, it's still a really fun game and worth the price. Just be warned that if you also have little time/patience like me and prefer instant gratification in your video games, this may be a little annoying for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, and if you like games like Animal Crossing you will probably like it too.It is a cute little game which allows you to help out ghosts by fulfilling the tasks they give you.You also build a camp for yourself, take care of animals, harvest plants and flowers, decorate the island etc.Everyday you get a few tasks and some things you can harvest, but after those are done you may have to wait till tomorrow to get new ones, so the game is more of a gradual story and a slow burn (which I like a lot because I do not have the time for major games at the moment).If you want a cute little game to play from time to time for relaxation's sake, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: There are multiple types of games. First person shooters like Doom, fighters like Mortal Kombat, rogue-likes like Darkest Dungeon. They are all cool on their own, yet completely different from each other by their gameplay. Some you may like, some you won't, matter of taste and to each their own, blah blah blah. Most of negative reviews for this game I've read were like "Good-nice-okay game, but not my type of game, RHEEEE~" or "It's a time-gated hidden object game, I HATE HIDDEN OBJECT!"I remember people crying about Dark Souls and it's difficulty when it was it's main feature... is not for the people who wants to complete it in 10h, uninstall and forget. It is  to be played slowly, relaxing way. It expects from you to play it a couple of hours, then leave it to do other stuff in your life, play other games and so on. Perfect for small sessions before going to work-university or sleep.Visually the game is amazing, music is nice and cozy, the art style is appealing, the whole idea of coloring the haunted world with light and bringing peace to animal spirits in their afterlife in such cute, nice way.Gameplay-wise it's simple and nothing really special, one of the many games based on collecting-crafting lots of stuff and decorating your camp. Then again - there are lots of popular relaxing games like this and this one in particular - is nice on its own. Good for kids and grown-up men, tired of everyday stress and depressing emptiness of their hollow lives.I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a super chill and cute collectathon. My only problem with it is that it's timegated (like Animal Crossing for example). There's around 30 minutes of content each day. After that, you can still fish, collect materials on the ground and craft but you can't progress the story further until the next day. It's slightly annoying. For some reason, cooking is also timegated. You go to an NPC, order food and have to wait at least 1h for it arrive.Apart from that it's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Chill, real-time life sim game like Animal Crossing that doesn't rely on gacha for random neighbors and also doesn't shame you for skipping days -- ghost bears are always there for you if you wanna just fish a little or whatever and you don't gotta worry about it. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. But there are a few things people should know before buying1) it is extremely new and therefore does not have the most content2 )it is more of a story than it is a game. the entire point of this game (imo) is to teach you that life's greatest joys can't be achieved in one day. the game teaches you this by forcing you to come back each day and help regain the memories of the Cozy Grove residents bit by bit. patience is important 3) You are not supposed to play much more than an hour a day, If you are looking for a fast paced game where you can min max until the sun explodes, this is not the game for you. that being said, this is one of my favorite games. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an experience similar to Animal Crossing, this is not the game.  I read about this game before buying and would see posts/videos with people saying things like "OMG AC FOR PC" or that its an Animal Crossing but in a ghost world, it is neither.There are similarities with Animal Crossing such as fishing, decorating the island and the game running with real time.  Decorating is not as interesting and doesn't serve much purpose other than making your "pets" and trees happy to gather more resources from them and to expand the light to unlock additional gathering nodes.Cozy Grove is not a bad game by any means but if you are looking for something to sink a lot of hours in to, this again is not the game.  I find myself playing no more than 1 hour 30 mins max each day to complete all of the available quests and sometimes spend extra time fishing.  New content is gated behind real time and each day you are limited to how many quests and upgrade resources (spirit wood) you can collect.  When new areas are unlocked, new fish, materials and ghost NPC's become available.It is a game that you play for a short burst then come back and check the next day.

_childDocuments_.review: The question isn't if I like the game, the question is if I recommend the game. I like the game a lot, its really cute, and is nice, simple fun. But do I recommend it? Not really, unless you want a game for reasons such as:You have issues controlling your amount of gaming time on your own, often over play to your detriment and want to learn how to control that. Or...You have children who want to play games, and you want them to play a game that basically runs out of things to do in an hour so that its easier to control how much they play.This game does say in the description that it really only is for 1-2 hours of gameplay a day. I just wish that it wasn't that way, and honestly feel like the game would be better if it wasn't. It feels like the game was almost made as if it were a mobile game, which I really dislike. Being forced to wait for content to give the game an illusion of being long and rich isn't really my thing, but I wanted to give this game a chance anyway. Its a calm and relaxing game that plays like Animal Crossing and looks like Don't Starve. You bring light to different areas of the map by helping ghosts (which look a lot like the bears from Alphabears...) and placing lanterns. There's lots of clothes, creatures and plants to collect and decorate with, as well as many wild creatures, fish and cooking recipes to collect. I like it a lot, but I think I would recommend it more if they lifted the forced lack of content. Regardless, it would be wonderful if there were an option to be able to just play it as you wish, with or without content restriction. I would love that a whole lot better. Give people a choice and I think it would be even more widely received.One other minor gripe I have is that so many creatures look alike, they're just simply a different color. I wish they all looked different than each other so it was easier to see which ones you don't already have even in non lit areas.

_childDocuments_.review: As the cool, autumn wind whistles through the trees and you feel the warmth of the campfire, you find yourself engrossed in a wonderfully quaint and emotional video game. Welcome to the world of Cozy Grove! From the creators of Spry Fox, this whimsical and heartwarming game invites you to embark on a journey of ghostly adventures and discoveries of hidden treasures. So why is Cozy Grove worth playing? This thoughtfully crafted game not only offers charming, hand-drawn visuals, but also presents a story centered around empathy, connection, and resilience.1. Cozy Grove is primarily about exploration and gathering. As you wander through the beautifully illustrated environments, you'll collect resources ranging from wood to crafting materials. These are essential for progressing through the game and assisting the ghostly inhabitants with their problems.2. The game revolves around a series of quests and missions. Some tasks are simple - like finding lost items, while others involve more complex puzzles. Each day brings new missions, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging.3. Crafting and customization play a big role in Cozy Grove. You can craft a myriad of items - from tools to decorations, adding a personal touch to your island camp. Additionally, the game's day and night cycle affects the resources available and the quests you can undertake, adding another layer of depth to the gameplay mechanics.Cozy Grove is more than just an adventure game – it’s a beautiful narrative that explores a wide range of themes and messages. One of the significant themes is the emphasis on community and helping others. As a Spirit Scout, your role is to lend a helping hand to the ghostly inhabitants, strengthening bonds and building a sense of community.Dealing with grief and loss is another prevalent theme in the game. The spirits you encounter are dealing with unresolved issues from their past, presenting a thoughtful exploration of loss and the process of healing. These poignant experiences add a depth and emotional resonance to the game, making it more than just a casual play.Moreover, Cozy Grove promotes the importance of self-care and mental health. It shows us that it’s okay to take things slow, to take time out for ourselves, and to take care of our emotional well-being. Along the journey, you also experience meaningful relationships and connections. From establishing friendships to empathizing with the characters’ situations, the game beautifully encapsulates the essence of human connection.For more of this review and to watch some of my gameplay visit  my profile for link

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a wonderful and compelling game filled with calming tunes, a sweet atmosphere, and lovable characters to tug at your heartstrings. I found some of the best storytelling in gaming in this game, and some of the quotes from these bears will stay with me for a long time. It was a lot of fun learning more about each bear as the days went on, like unraveling the different layers of their stories that hurt so good. I cannot praise its dialogue and its story progression enough. With that, once you finish the main story, the slog to 100% is a bit painful. The achievement requirements seem like they were chosen by a random number generator rather than an actual human who had played the game, and by the time I finished with this one (at almost 150 hours in), I was very tired of the monotony. The gameplay itself could use some polish and a lot of quality of life updates, but it was great to see the creators continue to work on it and push out so many updates over the past year. Cozy Grove is an easy recommendation for me--as long as you are not going for completionism.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I have way more hours on Switch. I bought it again for PC.This is like animal crossing, but more self aware, dark, and with actual story and quests. Time-gating: If you don't like games like animal crossing, don't play. You aren't meant to binge this game until you can't anymore. This game is meant to be played slow, at your own pace, for short periods of time each day. It allows you to slow down and enjoy the little things more. If you don't like that, don't get it. This feature does not mean it's a bad game that deserves negative reviews, it just means it's a relaxing and slow game and that that isn't the cut of your jib.Animal Crossing Relations:- "Museum" to donate to like Blathers- Collect sea shells and fish to farm money- You earn badges much like Nook miles achievements- "Villagers"- DecoratingGameplay: - You can decorate to your hearts content, farm crops and pet animals, and uncover a dark story about ghosts all in one. All cool items (furniture, pets, recipes) you get are randomized for each player each day, making it a unique experience. If you start a new character, you may get cool rare furniture on your first day you never saw before or it may take you longer to buy a pet deer than before.- You have to uncover these spirit bear's stories one day at a time. Every time you complete a quest, they add colour to their portion of the grove. Every morning you'll have to do their quest and add colour again until their hearts are complete and their story is finished. Colour allows you to harvest crops, keep your pet animals alive, and it just looks cuter. There are specifications to furniture and items. Rarities, likes and dislikes... You have to keep your plants and animals happy to be able to harvest enough resources from them.- The quests are Hidden Object quests (like the tag on Steam indicates). With having to re-colour the world (without colour everything is the same shade) and having hidden objects, if you are colour blind this may be a challenge and a half. You can purchase hints in the game that show you where things are, though. Your quest inventory will also give clues.- Some players find it frustrating finding ingredients and items for quests and other things because you can only collect so many resources a day and people usually sell and use them all immediately. Once you learn the way this game works, you'll understand how to manage your resources better. I don't see it as a fault. Most games have frustrating areas that just need learning. Everything may be confusing at first (saving resources, fishing, re-colouring the world) and therefore frustrate some people... This is because this is a new and different game attempting to make its own scene in the world of games. All you have to do is understand how the game operates. There is no instant gratification or ability to cheat (yet).- Once you get the ball rolling and establish your camp, like with most video games, there will be more to do.Nothing about this game confused me, frustrated me, or made me want to quit. I love it and come back to it every morning, waiting for the day to reset at 6am. I can't wait to progress through the story, grow my island, and decorate more.There is a Cozy Grove discord where the developers are active, replying to players, and hearing out suggestions and bug issues. They are listening and aim to improve an already adorable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Animal Crossing, but with missions/quests to keep you engaged in the game. It feels like there is a reason to come back each day and adding to your island isn't daunting. The art style is adorable, the characters are cute, and the music is incredibly relaxing. There's a little bit of something for everyone - crafting, cooking, collecting, and I'm sure more I haven't unlocked yet. I do wish there was a little more to do on day one as the game takes place in real-time, but each subsequent day adds more and more to do. It wasn't immediately apparent that the game was in real-time or that it was time gated, so I was a little disappointed at that. Day one took maybe 20-30 minutes to complete all my tasks, which was a bit of a let down. I do wish there was a little more to do on day one to sink your teeth into and get you hooked, but I still really enjoyed the game. Once I completed my day one tasks, I focused on collecting resources, making money, and getting upgrades (some of which, like AC, take a day to go into effect after you buy them). I actually ended up creating a second file as well and found that each island is a little different and the items you receive are different, too. Day 2 took around 60-90 minutes to complete my missions/quests, though I wasn't rushing through them. More tools have been unlocked and more things you can do other than just collecting resources once you've finished missions/quests for the day. I found Day 2 even more satisfying and I'm glad I was patient.If you're looking for a game to sink your teeth into and grind away at, this might not be for you. If you're looking for a more satisfying Animal Crossing complete with cute ghosts, missions and quests, and shops that don't close at night, then this is definitely the game you're looking for. I'm recovering from major knee surgery and this game has been my zen. So glad I found it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough. The music and sounds are so calming. I really like the idea of helping these spirits move on and us doing our best to assist them! I also really appreciate how the game limits playtime to only a couple hours a day because I would definitely play this non stop (just like I did with animal crossing). While the time limit can be a bit frustrating (I've been playing for over 2 weeks and don't even half half hearts with any of the bears), I can appreciate taking things at a slower pace. That being said, this game has its flaws and won't be for everyone. It's basically solely fetch quests, which I enjoy, but I know they can get very repetitive and boring for some people. The pet management can get a bit frustrating at times... I feel like my camp is infested with birds lol. Though, that could just be me not knowing how to properly set them up. I also think that decorating your campsite is more tedious than it should be (how do I make all these birds happy!?)Despite its flaws, it's a wonderful little game with an excellent story. The gameplay is easy to learn, and it's pretty intuitive. It can get very repetitive, but if that doesn't bother you then it's worth checking out!  I got it for myself, played a couple hours, and then immediately bought it for my friend too! It's a pleasant little mix of Don't Starve and Animal Crossing :)

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love Cozy Grove! The charming and relaxing atmosphere of the island, combined with the beautiful hand-drawn art style and peaceful soundtrack, make it a joy to play. The game play is fun and engaging, with a good balance of resource gathering, crafting, and questing.But what really sets Cozy Grove apart is its focus on storytelling and character development. Each ghost on the island has their own unique personality and back story, and interacting with them to learn more about their lives and help them move on to the afterlife is a truly rewarding experience.Overall, I highly recommend Cozy Grove to anyone looking for a cute and enjoyable life simulation game. It's the perfect escape from the stresses of daily life and I find myself coming back to it time and time again.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Warhammer avatar guy likes colorful, cute, zen video game.Cozy Grove is a zen game with a lovely art style and soundtrack that doesn't take too much of your time, since it gives you a limited amount of activities that progress its stories each day. It's not a good fit if you're looking to play longer sessions and can be a slow burn at times. Nevertheless, I've had fun slowly growing my collection of trees, animals, and deer, gathering materials, cooking meals, and discovering the story of the NPCs on the island. The only "challenge" comes from the occasional quest objective that may require lots of resources/meals that you can't quite get/make yet, but patience will eventually see you completing them. Post-launch updates have also fixed some of the game's more annoying elements while adding new content, like decorating the interior of your tent and pet cats.I've heard it compared with Animal Crossing but can't confirm how similar they are, since it's not a series I played so far. On it's own, it's a neat little game that was clearly made with lots of love. Just be aware of how it limits content, since that seems to be a deal-breaker for some people.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. It feels like Animal Crossing x Stardew Valley x Don't Starve. You get to do quests, craft furniture, collect clothes and other items, fish, all the good stuff! The only downside is that it runs in real time, but there is a notice for that when you buy the game. It said it is optimized for one to two hours of daily play and that's certainly true. It's a cute and very relaxing game. I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's beautiful and has adorable characters you get to learn more about every time you play. It really helps you not play for your entire days with having a finite amount of quests you can do for NPCs at a time which I really appreciate, it makes this game stay as a stress relieving cozy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I play this game nearly every day. I love that it's real-time but also doesn't have the pressure of FOMO like other real-time games. There's a completion aspect to each day so you can play and feel accomplished. The creepy-cute art style combined with the hide & seek gameplay is a great combination. Activities like fishing are fun, not annoying. I hate to fish in games and I will sit and fish in Cozy Grove for hours because it's relaxing to do. Characters are endearing and have personalities that are enjoyable to interact with. Completing badges and collections are another fun aspect to the game.Cozy Grove is cute, funny, and relaxing to play while still offering a meaningful challenge. I've recommended it more times than I can count and I love to stream the game on Twitch.Edited to Add: I play have this game nearly every day for while now. I'm on day 68 and I just need to say: YOU CAN HUG THE BEARS NOW! Also the storytelling is absolutely beautiful. So many feels. New game updates have kept it fresh and added new challenges. I highly recommend this game. Buy it and play it now.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game allows you to play at your own pace, but doesn't allow you to do much in a day. I would say it was an annoying tactic for game longevity as you have to come back the next day if you want to unlock the complete story of the bears.I would recommend it for players who love stories and lore, and couldn't play too much daily due to irl stuff. Solid characters and lovely music, with an art style that doesn't cause eyesores.Overall, decent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Don't Starve and Animal Crossing had a baby. The occasional creepy twist to the cuteness and the sometimes dark humor are right up my alley, and the casual hidden object mechanic is unique. Also, it's nice not to feel pressured to finish a game or to put massive hours into it -- you play for like an hour a day and then you're just done until tomorrow. I'm into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If I could mark this neutral I would, however I requested a refund for this game which leans towards not.I do not hate this game. I actually really wanted to like this game. However as someone who played a lot of animal crossing AND don't starve (the 2 games everyone compares this to) and this game just feels too bare bones. I would of played it a bit more before refunding but steam has that 2 hour policy so I felt forced to either like the game in the first hour and a half or not. I guess I just don't see myself being interested enough to go through the game all year round. I already have animal crossing for that and it seems to do it better. In this game the bears are all in one spot and it seemed like a like of fetch quests. I liked the art but that's also the ONLY thing remotely like don't starve in this game. Nothing else about it is like don't starve. I also don't like that I didn't have a tent or a home like in animal crossing. yea you can upgrade the little tent by the spirit fire but can you go inside? not even sure. There bears also have little places that look like homes or work places but you cant go inside I guess? You walk around this one very small island that grows as you do the quests for the bears. I like the idea that the colors come back to the island as you do quests but the quests itself seemed just, bland?unfortunately I couldn't play more to see if it gets better without risking my refund so I guess I wont know.I can see how some might like it. Its cute that's for sure, but not for me I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It was really boring and felt like I was having my hand held the entire time on a small island with only chores to do. This looks like a Don't starve, Animal crossing, Spiritfarer, Mix that lacks the core of what makes those games so fun. The aesthetic has the potential of being cute but its not functional game play wise.    Don't starve art/lineart works well for itself because there's sparse objects around to clutter everything up. Theres too many trees and bushes I can't interact with and it makes everything seem cluttered and unfocused. In Don't starve there's a ground texture and a few objects to interact with so as not to confuse the player.       Meanwhile this game has tons of objects around you CAN'T interact with that clutter the screen and makes it hard to focus on what i'm doing. I have to actively squint and try to focus on my cursor in order to understand "Is this an intractable bush? No? Then how about the tree? No? what about this random object on the floor that looks like I could pick it up for safe keeping... No? Then why is it here. For aesthetics? I can't tell what i'm supposed to grab. My cursor is white and so is the background."Its frustrating and makes me feel like there's so many items I want to interact with but I can't because ether it doesn't matter or I haven't unlocked a shovel that can clear the area of bushes so I can see what i'm doing.   The aspects of AnimalCrossing and why its fun; The customization of the character and as well as the world around you, As well as random villagers with cute aesthetics and personalities. Some of the core aspects of the game (Specifically new horizons) is starting with likable characters (That are random so its like a gacha on who you get and what the town looks like) So it feels special and unique to your specific character/you and your play through. It Feels like you randomly made a new best friend or a random neighbor or what have you. Meanwhile the characters in this game aren't as charming and likable.       Spiritfarer has you going from place to place in a boat (which allows for more views of different places so the fact you're with only one individual at a time doesn't get tedious or boring)If I were stuck with a character I didn't like very much at the very least I got to go out and see the world. This game makes it so i'm stuck on an island with a character I find boring, Skipping through dialog so I can get my next chore to do so I can progress farther but it just feels like one long tutorial and its incredibly boring to slog through. I shouldn't have to slog through a games tutorial for an hour just to hold on long enough to get to the good part.       Animalcrossing is colorful with basic shapes and less details making it feel like a cute doll house where you're the doll, and the neighbors are stuffed animals and a simplified world where there's little room to ♥♥♥♥ up. It has few lines and when it does the darker lines help guide the eye to an area you need to pay attention to while the colored line work blends what you don't need to focus on.      Don't starves dark scratchy and gritty lines make everything look similar to some of Tim Burtons art work to set a dark and scary world where you don't know whats going to happen but you know nature is out to get you.      SpiritFarer has straight thin linework with soft colors for the background that allow the player to focus on the rounded out player character (as well as what they're interacting with) due to them being ether darker or brighter than the back drop; Allowing them to stand out. Over all i'd give it a 4.5 out of 10Its tutorial is wAy too long and it feels unnecessary. I should be given starter tools in a bag from my boat and interact with the world in order to learn as I go (Similar to don't starve)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fixer? Do people come to you for advice? Would you like to play a ghost-assisting Girl or Boy Scout and give advice to a bunch of ghost bears who have all made such monumental mistakes that they literally can't go to the afterlife?Cozy Grove is a a sweet, comfortable, cute game. There are seasonal events, you can decorate the whole island, there's a bunch of built-in animals to take care of *other* than the bears, you can dress in pretty much any style you can think of (including head-to-toe in armor)... It's a really sweet game with lots to do. If you're the kind of person willing to log on for a few minutes a day to run around and talk to your ghosts, it'll break and warm your heart in equal parts. My roommate hasn't played it, but got so attached to a character via *my* playthrough that I wound up reading every one of his conversations with me aloud so they could hear what happened to him.The casual way that the diversity in this game is treated deserves its own paragraph. When I began playing, I didn't know it, but I had been experiencing the symptoms of fibromyalgia for at least four years. Even before I was diagnosed (and really accepted that I'm disabled; I was still destroying myself by pushing myself too far), the handling of the disability representation made me really happy. I'm being vague so I won't spoil anything, but to this day, I think fondly about that specific character. Queer representation is also there, entirely casual, without making a big deal about it. I love that. It made—and makes—me so happy.The most beautiful thing about this game is that every character is flawed. Some seem kind and aren't; some seem like they have bad intentions but don't. It's not something I know how to put succinctly, but it's lovely.The New Neighbears DLC is more than worth it: it adds several new characters, and by the time I had unlocked them, it very seriously doubled my playtime. That's a wonderful thing, although it took me almost two years to beat. I can definitely see myself checking in now and then, even after I've gotten everyone's stories finished.All of that to say, I can't suggest it enough. It's a very slow game, and not the kind you can just grind away at, and it's a nice reminder that not everything has to be as fast or as efficient as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, perfect for a relaxing game play. The graphics are so cute and love discovering more of the island. Only downside with the way the graphics are it's sometimes hard to find the objects. But, it's a game that definitely keeps you coming back since you can only do so many quests in a day.

That's alright. We have to help the people at the pace they are willing to be helped..." blah blah COME BACK TOMORROW. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This one is adorable! I do not compare it to Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley type games. It is very much like Animal Crossing, though. I like the premise of the stories of each character and the game play is unique. The graphics are charming and unique as well. The tasks you are given can be done in a single day, and new ones come along the next day. Some people complain about this but I've no problem with it as the time between can be used to collect resources, craft items, fish, and make coins. If you've ever wanted Animal Crossing for PC, this one very closely fits the bill. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely ADORE this game, however, if you have bad eyesight like me, it can be really frustrating to look for the small objects. There is an option to zoom in, but that makes it a little bit more frustrating to look because you only have a small screen to look at and you miss other things that way. I highly recommend it though, it's adorable!!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: The game has a real time daily task pace like in Animal Crossing. If you do not like this, then this game might not be for you.Cozy Grove is an incredibly relaxing and soothing game with a beautiful art style, lovely characters and a ton of things to do. I'm usually very critical with the games I play but somehow Cozy Grove is so heartwarming and offers so much to do (daily quests, fishing, crafting, bird pets to care for, a lot of characters) for such an incredibly low price. I don't want to sound as if I got bought or something, but I am really rooting for this game, because you can see how much care and effort the developers put into it. In my opinion Cozy Grove is for you if you want a nice and beautiful game you can play daily to relax, forget the issues of real life and feel cozy. Also, I want to mention there is a lot of content there. I mean, there are 180 fish, over 150 plants at least, things to cook, so many craftables and every bear (there are at least 20 from what I know) has a unique story and some personal problems you can easily help them with (their stories so far were not depressing per se, more like funny quirky weirdly relatable). The first days might be a bit slow, since there isn't that much to do (still like 30-60 mins gameplay), but after let's say... day 3, there's really a lot to do every day.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that will take you time because it works in real-time like Animal Crossing. The sheer advantage with this version is that you can advance time if you need to (or if you're impatient). With regular updates and seasonal visits from certain Bears, the game is constantly improved upon; However, once you get past the core 13 bears to ascend, it becomes a rather dull slogfest of collecting seasonal fish/flowers/foods.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a cute and cozy game. In Cozy Grove, you are a Spirit Scout helping spirits (bears) to make peace with their lives. The game is beautifully written and the bears are easy to get attached to. Every day the spirits will give you quests to complete and progress their stories. Next to the amazing storytelling, you can also do the following things:Note that Cozy Grove is . This means that you get new quests daily and you have about one to two hours of playtime each day. This doesn't bother me at all. It's very nice to login everyday and check on the spirits, farm a little, cook a little and buy and craft new decorations. It is relaxing. Cozy Grove gives me a warm and cozy feeling every time I play it. I recommend this game! It quickly became one of my favorite games. 10/10 for me :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while. At first I was excited. It's a really nice game, the problem is You are artificially blocked from moving the main story. I enjoyed that for the first 2 months. I treated this game like an 1 hour break. You can't really play any longer, not after 2 months. It became a chore, with additional chores inside. You go in, You wake up, You collect all plants, You make fetch missions, You get a mission with item that You might get in a few days, or weeks... You gather staff, and I am not sure why I was doing it. The cooking is so annoying, You can't cook many dishes at once, You need to click through the whole conversation to make one dish. 51 hours... divided into more than 3 months. Its like a mobile game where You go online, collect Your earnings, harvest, plant new plants and log off. I can walk around the map with my eyes closed at this point.  Those missions are boring, fetch this, chase that, gather this. In the first 2 months the map was expanding, I had new stuff to do, it was all new, but now... Nothing. Lots of items to collect, too bad most of them look the same. they are just in different colours.Some only show in particular time of the year, which some people might find exciting, I don't.I really wished I could finish this game, I even got myself DLC. but unfortunately the story is stretched so much, it's simply becomes boring. There should be an option for people who do not wish to play this game for another year , to be able to advance the story faster, or like me, turn it on, when the fun ends, so at least we can finish this game.This game has it's perks and is different than others, but is it really worth playing a year? No.Don't get me wrong, I played 51 hours. Definitely worth the money... But would I recommend? No. Why? Because I couldn't finish the game, so I had that very bad after taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you burned out on Animal Crossing like I did and want another Stardew Valley-esque game, this is the game for you. This game does only offer about 1 - 2 hours of gameplay per day, but I think this is a good thing so players don't burn out on the game before they can finish the full story and discover all there is to uncover. As someone who still hasn't discovered everything, I think that the time cap is a good way to stay invested every day without the fear of burnout. + Beautiful graphics in a cute and unique art-style+ Wonderful characters with great background stories to be discovered+ The music is incredibly relaxing+ Offers a lot to be discovered+ / - Can't grind the game for hours every day
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't have enough going on to be interesting. It's basically a seek-and-find where most quests boiled down to "find this thing for me" or "find thing to make a thing for me" rinse and repeat. Whats worse is, like animal crossing, the game operates on a real date & time system and only will allow you to do a few quests before it STOPS YOU and tells you to come back another day. It's even worst when the game tries to high road stalling its own lack of content by telling you to "have patience" when you're upset that you were only able to squeeze an hour of game play out of it each day. I really wanted to like this game but I just CANNOT recommend it at all. Every time I play I get so bored I start nodding off. So if you're looking for a sleep aid then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people are not going to enjoy the restraint of set amount of quests per day, but this is perfect for me. I lost my abuelita, and this game is really one of the things that helps me get out of bed in the morning to do something casually and quietly. It's not so much that I have to spend hours upon hours on it. And it wakes me up and puts me in a positive mindset. So cozy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: While some people might find the game being in real time a drag, I actually really enjoy it. Especially when I have had a long stressful day, I love coming into this relaxing, happy game to say hi to the spirits and explore the island. The art style and music are lovely, and I don't feel pressured by time to get stuff done. There are more than enough high-stakes games out there, so it's a nice change of pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable and fun but also makes me cry because I care so much about these bears. I love the art and the island management style and the way there is so much to do. However, the best part is piecing together the stories of the ghosts of Cozy Grove as they slowly share them with you. It gets to me in all the best ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Many souls of the dead cannot leave the earthly world, due to various unfinished business. And only ghostly scouts are able to help them - having dealt with matters and releasing their souls to the next world.In the role of one of these scouts - the player must help several ghosts to rest on a small island "Cozy Grove"Pretty cute "Farm Frenzy" - in which the player must carry out the tasks of the ghost bears day after day, and in his free time go fishing, search for shells and garbage in the fallen leaves. Along the way, decorating the island with a variety of luxury items and breeding a zoo of ghostly animals.We've seen this in hundreds of games, but unfortunately this game decided to limit the player's time. And he gives strictly one task from the characters, after which you can continue the story only the next day.And if at the beginning of the game you really can spend only an hour on tasks and then collect ingredients, then the further you advance in the story, the more daily tasks you will open. And the longer you will need to play.In addition, there are too many tasks for collecting resources in the game. Resources that do not just appear on the island in the amount you need, so that you go around it and collect everything at once. Not! You will run in circles around the island hundreds of times, as items will appear after you pick up the previous one. And that means running around the island, looking under every bush, finding a feather - and going on a second round-the-island adventure. And so on until you collect all 10/20/100 pieces!Yes, there is a "hint" in the game where to find the desired item. But she's pretty vague. So "I saw an object near the skull" - in any case, it will make you run around the whole island, even if this skull is the only object on the whole island!I would also like to note that against the backdrop of LGBT and other topics - the authors of the game decided to make a "strong and independent girl" a hero - without offering a choice of gender for the player. I usually don't care who to play - but in this case, I was a little confused by the desire of the developer to send a little girl to a haunted island without any help or contact from adults. In the case of a boy - I would consider such a move - a kind of "growing up".The game is cute, sometimes interesting. But finding items daily and having to log into it daily makes it unplayable for me.I held on as best I could, but I only lasted a week.I recommend this game to children, office workers - who have nothing to do at work and girls. Why I don't recommend this game to guys? Because it seems to me that they will not sit in it, just like me because of the monotony and boredom.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute game that has too many downsides right now to recommend. The biggest issues I had with the game is RNG quests. Get unlucky enough and you will have many quests asking for the same items that only appear once a day. This can stall a player for more than a week.Another issue I have is the in the very nature of the story progression. (light spoiler warning) Starting up the game and everything is white with black ink outlines. Progression fills in the color but only for that day. Pretty neat mechanism until you realize that you are item hunting in a sea of black lines. I always felt like I was squinting at the screen to find items. Lastly, tying to the last complaint. The clutter OH THE CLUTTER.  Plants and decorations abound as the default and that means not a lot of room for doing your own thing. Trying to item hunt? Have fun clicking on everything to see if you can interact with it or not. Trying to place items? Have fun either getting your stuff lost behind natural decor or having to cycle through the "next item" button to get to the thing you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Animal Crossing! Not sure why people keep repeating this.I didn't enjoy the game as much as I thought I would... There's a lot of quests and text, which I'm sure some people will enjoy! But I bought the game thinking that it would be like Animal Crossing, and well, not.It allows you to be super creative and if you are into really rich story games, then this is definitely for you. Also, kudos to the design team, the game is super cute!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the game is cute, but that's more or less where the positive side ends. Also, in all fairness: I was looking for a game that was similar to Spiritfarer, so the expectations might have been a bit high (if you haven't played that yet, I highly recommend!).Pro:+ Graphics are cute+ It's peaceful+ Limits the time you can play it (in case you have a problem with doing that yourself)Con:- It is very boring: You pretty much just walk around the island for hours, looking for whatever the bears conveniently lost that day- It is repetitive: The only task you get is to look for x in y quantities- It is frustrating: The game gives you clues on where to look for, but in most cases that means looking behind EVERY object and that gets very frustrating after a while- You don't really get much of a story: The bears will tell you a bit, but not enough to bond with themThere are other sides to it as well, such as fishing, collecting critters/shells and building stuff on the island to maximize e.g. production of fruittrees. However, I don't really want to through the hassle of doing the collection-quests every day to level up the bears/stories and the building part wasn't enough to keep me on the game.Tl;dr:It is a cute game that does not offer a lot of variety and gets very repetitive and boring quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's the perfect game to relax with and chill out to. There is only a limited amount of stuff you can do in each day, but that just keeps me coming back. It's almost like a little happy ritual of visiting cozy grove at the end of each day for me, play an hour plus, then go on to do something else. I have missed multiple days in between too, and there is no penalty when you do, which is a plus for a busy mom like me! There is no stress here, so fish, bug-catch, cook and quest to your hearts desire. Exploring is fun, and searching for items is entertaining. When it gets tedious or I get stuck looking for something, I can always buy a hint which helps. I love collecting stuff, so this is perfect for completionists like me. I love that each spirit has their own personality, and story, and you are helping everybody whilst getting to know them. Very positive game. Highly recommend it to others in search of cozy, light-hearted games to unwind with.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A halfhearted thumbs up. I am completely split in how I feel about how game play is parsed out in a few minutes a day. On one hand I like how it reminds me of doing Dailies on Neopets back in the day, or my routine in Animal Crossing - it makes game play feel rewarding within those moments, a fast little dopamine hit. On the other hand however I don't feel connected to the story or game as a whole as it feels a lot like a mobile game for me. Once I've found everything I needed for the day I just log off. "Oh, but Rachel, there are so many cute decor items!" Yes. And the decoration mechanic is a nightmare. I can't stand how messy the game is lol. I understand it's necessary for the Where's Waldo element but it's just awful to look at and navigate for me. The parts of decor that are movable feel clunky and annoying to deal with. I feel like a lot could be solved by having the move mechanic toggled off and on so you could mass edit all the decor on the screen but as it stands moving my character to exactly where I want to put the item, opening my inventory, selecting the item, selecting that I'd like to place the item, oh no it's slightly off, let me back out of the inventory, let me step back so the item is no longer see through from my proximity to it, now I will select it, select move, AND NOW I get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cursor to fine tune the placement. It's insufferable.But I'm still playing so I must be having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I absolutely love this game!! It's similar to AC:NH, but I enjoy the general storyline a lot more. As someone who juggles a lot of games that do take a lot of commitment, I appreciate that the intent is to only play this one for 1-2 hours, which allows me to unwind and relax a bit after work. That being said, I've only been playing for about a week, so I may change my mind in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is the ultimate chill game.  It's perfect for just switching your mind off and vibing at the end of a busy day.  Note: I do time jump!  Its not recommended by the developer but when I wanna have a long play session I just push my computer clock forward a day.  I keep track of my last played date on a post it.  Remember, you can go forward in time but not back!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Charming casual game with adorable gothic art. Gameplay is limited each day, so next day login is required to forward the plot. But the collections and minigames like fishing, skipping stones, and catching bugs are always available and good for killing time or keeping your hands busy while watching TV. Good for all ages, plus or minus concepts of death.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: As one would expect from the title, this game is nice and relaxing. It feels more guided than a game like Stardew Valley, but has a similar soundtrack and set of activities. Cozy Grove also feels similar to Animal Crossing: New Horizons, but it has significantly more story. It also has a nice feature that makes it easy to find a stopping point each day, encouraging me to game for a bit and then take a break. I think it would be great for kids because it feels much less addictive, almost encouraging me to play for no more than an hour each day.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: really cute, as the name suggests cozy, the music is calming and I wanna find out more about the story and play more.Cons: I think this game is better suited for nintendo switch because you can only play once every day (???) like.... why? The time in the game is the same time as in real life, so basically you can play only half to one hour a day with actual progress, and then you can keep playing just for the cozy music and the art style, but you can't really do anything to see more of the story.So, overall I liked the game and would recommend it BUT I would have liked it better if you could play however long you want and I have to tell you that if you think about buying this game to actually play - you should consider getting a different one.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game in itself, just don't expect to be doing a lot on a daily basis. It's definitely limited compared to Animal Crossing, but also great for starting your day or ending it while relaxing. Also, I truly loved the graphics of Don't Starve (Together) and Oxygen Not Included and Cozy Grove reminds me of them, which is a plus for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really do love this game.  I keep wanting to come back to play it each day.  I don't mind the time limit on things or the story progression being slower.  It gives me a little bit of time each day to decompress but not so long that I can't get on with other tasks.Overall a great game.  My thoughts/ramblings below:I do feel like the game logic is a little skewed in that some of the items I am being requested to provide are not available.  They are not feasible at that stage in the game.  I'm on Day 9 as of this writing and feel like I need to sell all of my otherworldly possessions just to get enough coin to upgrade so I can get the things I need.  Instead of throwing all of the item requests at us when it isn't feasible for me to even have some of them, they might have been better off to limit the requests until say, Day 12 or what have you so you have had time to gather items.  The "random" requests I understand but if they changed the percentage of random it might help.  Technically, if I can only buy one egg a day and I'm on Day 9 - I can't possibly have enough eggs unless by random chance to feed the darn bird.  Can't feed the bird, can't get essence - circles infinite.Also, if I hadn't googled how to do some things I'd have no clue.  Sure I maybe could have figured it out.  But the tutorial from one of the bears came two days after the requests showed up....so I googled how before the bear was even prompted to tell me how.  Maybe I'm just not an "ignore until it's needed" person.  But I don't like those limitations.  If it's there for me to see, I should be able to progress and complete that task.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: i really, REALLY want to like this game more than i do. i play on a steam family with my boyfriend, so we take turns each playing for about an hour or so a day, comparing notes about our progress and trying to flesh out our collections, which is where my main gripe about cozy grove comes into play. the time-gating wasn't a huge issue - a little annoying, sure, as many MANY people have already stated, but after about an hour of playing i'm naturally about over getting cozy in the grove for the day anyway, so i wasn't bothered by that being as much time as it would allow me to play, usually. my main gripe is this: if you want to time-gate everything, if you want me to only play for an hour or two a day, and there's only so many resources, and the things in my collection are locked to certain months, WHY do you make me grind for things that are out of my control? take the seashells, for example. i'm on day 40-something at the time of writing this, and i have not completed either the march OR the april seashells, both of which i can collect at this time. in fact, i haven't even SEEN a single one of the 'crystal' shells. this is entirely out of my control, as only 20 seashells spawn a day, and they spawn at set intervals apart, so i am forced to run around looking for them, wait, run around looking again, wait, and HOPE that it might be one of the ones that i need. i can't close the game during this time either, as resources don't recharge while the game is closed, other than via the day progressing.additionally, the game's more than a little clunky, between the weird hit-boxes of everything, the rock-skipping mini-game that you can't get good at no matter how hard you try, and the obnoxious way of cooking or crafting ( having to slog through a bunch of dialogue screens to get allison to make me an ingredient that i'll get in five minutes, which i can use to slog through more dialogue screens and make another thing, which will be delivered to me in another five minutes ), but i'm able to work around these issues, mostly by just.... not doing those things, which is certainly one way to handle it! there's also so much in the WAY, mostly in the sense of visual clutter, random bushes and trees and rocks and other detritus, which i understand is vital if the fetch quests are meant to be even a little bit challenging, but that doesn't make it less bothersome that i can't ever clean it up around here. also, i am constantly running into and getting stuck on the corner of things that i couldn't see, as they went transparent before i noticed they were there. this is especially apparent in arjun's area, as he has a lot of tents and little posts and things on the ground, and they always seem to catch me. you can't plan for where they're going to be, either, as the island tends to rearrange itself overnight, which is charming as a plot point but a nightmare logistically. it's hard to plan your decorations when things will be somewhere else entirely tomorrow, and even harder to plan when you have to check the likes and dislikes of every pet, flower, and tree in the area against the tags on your desired furniture. i've taken to just putting the decorations i like into storage to maybe use someday when i'm further along, in the hopes that the island rearranging itself will settle down as i progress, and it also was relatively easy to get my house to the highest level by recycling the ample quartz i receive from working on my collection and getting the subsequent achievements from crafting x amount or catching y amount of z, so i have the storage space for it. i also don't bother lighting up the place, as all of the lights give a piddly amount of light, and you have to get lucky with a recipe that a. you like and b. you can afford to make A LOT of, in order to really get anywhere with it.i'm also not entirely sure who the intended audience of the game is meant to be, age-wise? from the mature topics covered, some of the references made, and the way the game is clearly meant to be fit into a busier schedule, i would say that it is intended for adults who are looking for a way to unwind, but if that is the case, why does the game insist on handholding me through everything, as though i am actually a child, and not just playing one? i don't need to see a fishing tutorial every single time i mess it up, i KNOW i messed it up, and i know how, even! the quests are almost painfully easy, even without checking the hints for where you can find things, and charlotte, in her endeavours to be helpful to a more inexperienced scout, just comes across as patronising in her dialogue, with how she wants to explain every small thing i should know. (sssssiiiiiippppp)all in all... i wish there were a 'ymmv' option for recommending. despite my frustrations with cozy grove, i enjoy playing the game for a little bit of time a day. the music can be repetitive, but the art style is so cute, and i don't even mind having to fetch stuff over and over, except for the 20 screens of dialogue i've already seen. yes, yes, patrice, the imps stole the mail again, i KNOW. can we wrap this up so arjun can tell me how he needs some sandpaper that jeremy left near one of the stones with the smiley face on it again? i like the characters, well... for the most part, but i'm sure some of them are meant to grow on you over time - though at this point i have my suspicions that at least one of them never will, since i'm about,,, maybe halfway through her story, and i still do not like her - and their stories are interesting, when they're not incredibly slow moving. i just wanna collect all the stuff available in a month in that month, man. this game's got enough longevity from the daily time limit of quests without making me have to play for multiple years just to finish my collection. please just let me collect everything before i have to wait until 2025 to get it bvhfbvalso, as a random side-note, i love the names and descriptions of the different things, they're very charming, and i enjoy trying to figure out how they relate to each other or what they are a reference to, but 'kpop antifan' has actual ( very bad !! like "attempted to take an idol's life" bad !! ) connotations within the kpop community, and does not mean what you think it means, given that the description of the critter implies it's someone who prefers metal music instead. #notallmetalfans /lh

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is refreshingly wholesome. I check in on it first thing after I wake up and I look forward to it all day if I'm at work. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: reminds me of animal crossing as there is a collection feature, and tasks to fulfill, and day and night cycle that follows your actual time, the difference is you are helping bring back color to the island you reside on, and there is a continuous storyline with this game. and there are no villagers but ghost inhibiting here. but that's all the more interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorable and heartwarming game. The music is lovely and the designs are delightfully cute. The characters you meet are endearing and I just love everyone I meet in this.My biggest "criticism" is you can really get lost doing the dailies. I launch the game and suddenly it's been two hours. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this game out a while back, thought it was cute, but wasn't at a place where I was interested in consistently checking into a game every day for progression, as I'd gotten my fill of that with Animal Crossing. But more recently, I'd found myself really wanting something I could visit for just a little while every morning. A ritual where I can help others, collect items, craft things, and just exist in a very cozy space for a little bit of time each day. Cozy Grove is a perfect game for someone who doesn't want to, or have time to, spend hours in one sitting trying to progress to something. Here, you can take your time, you only have roughly an hour of tasks you can make progress towards each day, but you can spend whatever time you'd like fishing, catching bugs, and listening to chill music and moving your little decorations around. You can make this island your own, you can enjoy something well crafted in bite sized moments, watch seasons change, and work towards collecting everything in a way that feels unhurried. Come to Cozy Grove to earn your Spirit Badges, and stay to feed the animals, catch a bunch of cute little bugs and fish, and burn just about everything in your bonfire. Burn. E v e r y t h i n g. Oh, and wear cute hats. Don't forget about the cute hats.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A friend gifted this to me; this is the best cozy game I've got. If you are looking for a calm game that you can come back from time to time and do not want to trouble yourself that much about grinding stuff, this is the game for you. Cute ghost bears and cute magical creatures are just a plus and you can make your character wear different cute clothes every day!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relaxing little game. Very chilled and the stories of the bears are, so far, all quite interesting. I actually quite like the time-gating - there's sufficient to do for 30-60 minutes or so a day, which fits nicely for me. One minor gripe would be that sometimes it's difficult to target the item you're after, especially if it's next to something else, but other than that, a very nice, relaxed "play for a little while" to help wind down after work!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: ✿ PROS- the game is chill and cozy- cute and charming art- you get to dress up and be the most fashionable spirit scout ever- ability to decorate your base or...the whole island if you're up for it- you get to hunt around for things for your neighbears (basically a hidden object game with hints)- beautiful music- funny/silly item names- touching story✿ CONS- while using the controller: trying to harvest fruits/flowers when they are next to other harvestable plants/trees is a pain. it would take you several tries to get to the tree/plant you want to select because the place gets crowded. getting the accordion from the game shop for this job is the best purchase ever. so yes, harvesting is easier if you use the mouse.✿ RATING: 3.5/5// i understand that this isn't everyone's cup of tea since this game is slow-paced and very chill. i actually fell asleep while playing it at one point. however, i think it's the whole point of the game. it's not going to let you play longer than 2 hours. it's basically something you'll pick up in order to take a break from a busy schedule and relax. the game is a mix of farming, fishing, decorating, and hidden-object game all in one so it's not that there's nothing to do in it. you'll also find yourself chuckling at the in-game names some times. the thing i like the most, aside from the dress up and decorating, are the stories you get to learn from each neighbears. some are sad, some are fun, but it makes you wonder about life. if you're into these stuff, i highly recommend the game. otherwise, skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cute game! I am loving it so much. It plays similar to animal crossing in that there are only a small number of 'goals' to complete each day and it runs in real time. You are a spirit scout sent to cozy grove when your boat floats away, now stuck you are tasked with helping a variety of bears to 'asend'by unlocking their memories of their lives by completing tasks for them. It's very heartwarming and each bear has a different personality that makes them unique with different outlooks on their lives and deaths. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It is a cute game where you are upgrading and decorating an island and at the same time helping bear spirits that are on it. The game limits how much you can play daily by not giving you more than one quest per bear per day. I don't really mind it that but at least in my experience the one to two hour per day claimed in the store page is only really true for the first few days of playtime. After a short while it would be 15 minutes or so, rarely more unless you get a bigger quest to do.As for the quests you have 17 bears in the base game that will give you quests almost daily. Sometimes the quests will progress the story and sometimes they wont. The problem with them is that the quests are incredibly incredibly repetitive and you are doing the same thing over and over again each day. They are all either go find these XY items around the island based on the same clues or give the bear XY items that you can also collect or craft around the island. It really really needs a bigger variety of quests and things to do, otherwise it gets really boring before you even get close to beating the game.Works without issue with Proton (played on versions Proton 6.3-8 to 7.0-4).
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: i bought this on a whim. read the top few reviews, and figured what the heck, we'll give it a go. and the top reviews, both positive and negative, are quite accurate.unfortunately for me, while i enjoy the game, the time gating is a deal breaker. this is very much a game for a person who doesn't have a lot of time to play every day, but does has a little time to play consistently every day. i am not that person. i'll go weeks with zero play time, then have an entire day where i can kill 10 hours just video gaming. i'd love to spend that 10 hours chilling in cozy grove, but cozy grove doesn't want me to spend 10 hours in cozy grove.sure, sure, i could time travel. but that's just obnoxious. if the time gating is so important to the developers they might consider making this a mobile game. logging in and poking it for 10 minutes here and there throughout the day would be possible if it were a mobile game.as it stands, i uninstalled it because i'm not going to spend 5 years trying to progress a single bear's story, no matter how charming i find the art style, or how interested i actually am in the bears' character development and learning about their story.

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove
