_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who often struggles with a fixation on one game at a time, and struggles with maintaining play on Life Simulators over extended periods of time, I initially thought that Cozy Grove was something I wouldn't vibe with at all, expecting to dump it within a few days and be done with it.But here I am, nearly 3 months later and very pleasantly surprised and happy at how my experience has been.Cozy Grove is a Life Sim that manages to make very short bursts of gameplay feel very rewarding and very full of content, even if you only play for an hour or so a day. The amount of things you can do, your quests or activities such as resource gathering, all take the perfect amount of time as to still feel like you're committing yourself to doing it, but not that you're wasting too much time/effort on them.It's, as the name suggests, incredibly "Cozy". The atmosphere, the art, the music, it all comes together beautifully. Nothing feels forced upon you, and just moving around and doing all of your silly little tasks is a great time killer that really helps you take a step back and just relax for a while. It's absolutely gorgeous, its art style something directly out of a picturebook, and the designs for the characters is something I enjoyed as well. Though yes, all of the bears use the same base shape, I like that it's then up to their accessories and surroundings to help distinguish them. Plus they look perfect for hugging.The game's world, narrative and characters are also splendid. The story gives you enough explanation as to your existence within the world, and how the spirits operate and how you help as a Spirit Scout, but doesn't overwhelm you with too many of the nitty gritty details. The stories of the spirit bears in particular are often quite powerful, and as you unravel more and more about who they are (and who they were), you find yourself becoming enraptured in their stories, and wanting to see what happens next. And once you reach the end of one of their stories, the sheer satisfaction you get from both a gameplay and narrative standpoint is phenomenal.It's definitely got a few issues here and there. Selecting the correct item when something is in the way gets annoying, and needing to wait until a bear has given you everything before you can move again feels like it's wasting time, but I think the rest of the game more than makes up for these flaws.Otherwise, this is absolutely a game I recommend if you like life sims and are looking for something new to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so chill and relaxed. A perfect game for my relaxed streams, and fits very well with my campground theme. I wish I could play it for longer than a couple of hours a day, but it's still nice to be able to chill and relax with this game. The music fits so perfectly with the game too. I love listening to the music so much that I bought the soundtrack so I can listen to it even if I'm not playing the game. I have recommended this game to many people. Personal review...10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: oh nooo, this game is incredible!! THIS is the new animal crossing. Gorgeous art, so smooth, lovely music, LOVELY story and characters. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The big talk of this game is the time restraints. In my belief it creates a very healthy relationship between you and the game. It also certainly lives up to the name "Cozy Grove." Apart from the part where you suffocate fish and burn them as a resource... I never understand that with these games. But I guess they run out of ideas.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little hesitant at first about the real-time aspect of the game, but it's actually one of my favorite things about it now! It manages to be completely chill, with no pressure to stay in the game for hours until you're burnt out. No quest, even the daily ones that expire, seems urgent. It's somehow more chill and relaxing than Stardew Valley, with the calm bittersweetness of Spiritfarer. 100/10 recommend for a couple of hours of mentally restful downtime every day.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very cute game. Love the art style and the small details.Because the game runs in real time i really enjoy doing small ingame tasks each day so it's not overwhelming. It lowkey reminds me on Animal crossing. Overall defiantly recommend cozy Grove for people that love a cozy and relaxing game and for Everyone with a small time span to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game and I love that I don't have to waste my whole day to feel that I got everything out of it each day. There is plenty to do in terms of gathering and fishing and arranging your decorations to keep my occupied after the main quests are done if I want to spend more time in game. Seriously I wish people would learn how to read and stop leaving negative reviews when the game never HID the fact that it has a time lock. Additionally, it is possible, for those who want to, to change system time and keep playing so I don't get all the negative reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this for 9 hours so far across 4 days and it's all I think about. I actually like that you can't binge the game for hours and hours on end as quests are limited each day. As my friend said, it's nice that the game kind of forces a game-life balance. I'm making it a point to play it a bit in the daytime and a bit at night as I love how the game's clock follows your actual clock. So if it's daytime IRL, it's also daytime in Cozy Grove. I love it. I just really love it. As someone who missed out on the Animal Crossing craze (the two have similarities), I love love LOVE this game! The music is awesome! It's really so calming and cozy. The art is beautiful. All I do is gush about how pretty the game is. I love the concept! Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you play a spirit scout on a haunted island, helping the ghost bears there resolve their issues. It's cute, but the daily tasks are the same every day - wander around the island and collect items.  It's chill and relaxing at first but ended up feeling like a chore after three weeks of doing the same thing ever day.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: My new favorite way to start my day :) Gives me many wholesome and happy vibes. And I love how you can get help to any quest if you need to- no judgement. And the daily play element works very well for me. Sometimes I wish I could play for longer, but I actually end up looking forward to play more the next day and get progress. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Having now played over 50 days of this game, I can confidently say if the world and scenario of Cozy Grove is what draws you in AND you're willing to work through a slow start, it really begins to shine around 20 or so days and only goes up from there. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you really want to play Animal Crossing but don't want to shell out for it and/or a whole ass Switch, please get this game. You know what? Get this game anyway. It's a tad slow going at first, but goodness me it doesn't take long to pick up and now I can spend my precious sleep time doing this instead, and I know we all love that.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute game! Has a similar feel to Animal Crossing in the way that it runs in real time, you help out your neighbours, catch bugs and fish, collect foragables to cook with and furniture to place anywhere you'd like. Art style reminds me of a cuter version of Don't Starve (also a great game if you like survival). You can purchase some incredibly adorable and glowy animals and surround them with things they like which is always appreciated. TL,DR: You can feed and pet cute animals and give your quirky bear-neighbours big hugs, 10/10 you will love  this game if you love collecting everything.

_childDocuments_.review: This game provides something uncommon in this type of gaming (in my experience, at least), which initially turned me off the game until I decided to come back, and now I find it comforting and enjoyable. This might not be for every cozy gamer. First, a few tips: - When you start the game, don't be disappointed in the size of the island - it expands as your character levels up, more or less. - If you find the options lacking in Kit's store, look around at your other neighbears and see if they're selling something, a lot of them are, but they're usually specialized to the type of bear they are. This took me *forever* to realize. - If you care about achievements, I will say they can be a bit grueling, but they are all ones from the scout badges in-game, and it doesn't have to suck to get them all, you can still keep it low stakes. So if you care about the scout badges, I recommend starting them early in your game play, be consistent and spread out how you manage them. For example, every game play I try to make sure I feed a few animals, chop a few bushes, buy a few flowers, grab a few shells, sell a few things, buy a few things, etc. instead of stressing about getting every animal every single game play and then once that badge has been reached, switching to another badge. - If you're stuck trying to find something: you can ask the bear between your tent and Kit (Charlotte, I think?), and she'll tell you where it is for 100 gold.- If you get stuck low on money, remember Francesca will recycle your quartz for gold at quite a high conversion. Now, for the uncommon feature mentioned above. This game is intended to be played in short-ish bursts, consistently over long periods of time. Comparatively, when Disney Dreamlight came out, with a similar overall game play type, I played it for 5+ hours a day for the first few weeks and then haven't picked it up in a while just because I felt kind of burnt out on it (still highly recommend it if you like these types of games, though). I have a similar length of gameplay as I do on Cozy Grove.  But, Cozy Grove I got 9 months ago, and I play ~15-30 minutes a day.  The game seems engineered to throttle your game play options after a certain amount of time, forcing you off organically when you find yourself bored and without tasks to complete. I've grown to enjoy this and find it actually makes it feel cozier than something like Disney Dreamlight, which can be overwhelming sometimes and start to feel like a chore to keep up with, which is the opposite of the point of cozy/low stakes game play. I have a bad habit of skipping over text bubbles in some games, and I've rarely read the conversations in this game so I can't speak to the quality or enjoyment of the story in that way. Awful of me, I know. From what I do catch as the words fly by, they all seem to be kind and sweet conversations from a variation of viewpoints and identities/abilities. Seems kid friendly but can't be 100% as, again, I never actually read them much beyond the first few words.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a lot of really cool ideas, such as being able to craft without having the item in your inventory, as long as it's either in your storage or in your backpack. But it doesn't work for recycling or collections which I think is weird. It's also very cute and I love the idea of each bear having their own storylines. I also don't mind games that are only meant to be played for an hour or two a day, so this review is not based off of that.That being said, I think the game has a few flaws that are very hard to overlook. The daily tasks are about 90% of the gameplay and they are very repetitive and boring. It's fetch quests. "Go find this item with a vague description of what it is or where it is." Every day you have to "relight" areas of your island by helping your bears but it makes finding things very hard. Everything is just a few shades of grey until it gets relit. They allow you to pay a currency to have the location handed to you, but it's not fun either way. Once you give a bear their item, they might give you the item you need to progress the stories, they might not. I don't mind daily tasks, but I mind that these ones are never a fun thing to do and there is not nearly enough variety in the kinds of tasks you are asked to do. Another problem I have is that although the game really wants to be Animal Crossing and appeal to that demographic, it's missing a key element that games like that have, which is the ability to customize your island. Your island has a LOT of clutter in the form of trees, bushes, lanterns, etc. that CANNOT be moved or cut down, etc. I understand why they did that, they are used as hints for the fetch quests, BUT it's very frustrating. It's particularly even more frustrating because I don't mind the pets and harvestables having preferences of decor, but it's so hard to enjoy decorating with all of the other clutter in the way. You can't make this island your own and I think that's a big part of why people play games like Animal Crossing. I really wanted more from this game and I think they have some good ideas, but I don't think the game is actually fun to play which makes it hard to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a family friendly game. It has elements of Animal Crossing to it but this game is really dark. It hits to close with actual traumatizing situations with ALL of the bears backstories. And if you don't know ahead of time (which the game description never mentions that the undertones are so dark so I didn't know) it can be actually triggering. I got to a point where I shut down the game and walked away trying not to breakdown. If you have underlying trauma this game is not for you. These are not slightly sad or heartwarming backstories to help them then move on. And the time gating just draws out the traumas to where even if it were to get better as you help them move on I wouldn't last another 40+ hrs trying to get there. Shame on the creators for not being clear about their games direction. I will not be continuing to play this game.Though if you like dark games then by all means pick it up. _childDocuments_.review: It's a little like Animal Crossing, only all the villagers have tragic backstories and there's an awful lot of skulls all over the island. Some players don't like the slow pace and time-gating (you can time travel forward only, if this really bothers you), but it's a game that very much rewards taking your time with it. I found the pacing perfect for absorbing the sometimes very heavy story beats. It’s got beautiful art, a bittersweet and soothing soundtrack, and excellent sound design and lighting effects. The gameplay itself is smooth enough. The classic Nintendo-style fishing mechanic is improved here with a visual guide to help you know where you’re casting your line. Farming is slowed down, but not painfully so. The decorating system is a little clunky - I’d like to turn some of my furniture in more directions than available, and moving it around without a preview is a little vague. Getting the whole island kitted out with lamps is satisfying, especially as you unlock more lamp styles and can fit the light to the location theme better. The quests all tie in nicely with the characters, rather than feeling arbitrary. The gameplay loop is meditative, and I appreciate that I can take as long as I need to complete various tasks. If it takes me a week to catch enough fish to complete a story quest, the bears don’t mind and the game will not punish me for it. The accessibility is pretty high on this title, though there's room for improvement here and there. One of the bears provides a hint function for hidden objects, so low-vision players can fulfill quests without dealing with zooming and lighting effects. There's a “perpetual daylight” mode I found very helpful as well. Thanks to the inked line watercolor art style, color blind players should be able to see most things, and nothing requires distinguishing colors. Very little in the game requires quick reflexes, although some of the critters can pose a problem there. Aiming the net can be tricky when you’re in a hurry. The game has basically no penalties and no deadlines, it's all very low-pressure. There is no voice over, so reading is required, although the text is only presented one or two sentences at a time, with no more than three lines of text on the screen at any time. And I know it drives some people crazy, but I absolutely love that the day resets at 5 am, so this nightowl can play when it suits me best.Disclaimer: I received the DLC for free as part of a volunteer testing group. My review was written before that time.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point of writing this, I have ~60h ingame playtime and have played from early summer to early fall. Some weeks every day, some weeks I skipped.The reviews who compare it to the most comfortable and forgiving aspects of Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are correct. I want to clear up some criticisms from negative reviews with mine though.In the beginning, you unlock more and more bears on the island who offer different functions that add a lot of things to do aside from the quests those bears give you. You get different tools to search and harvest different materials, you get fishing, you slowly get more items to purchase in the shop, you get more and more recipes to cook. You have a collection to fulfill, similar to the museum in Animal Crossing. You can buy a lot of pets you can pet and feed, bushes and trees to harvest. The cook times of the recipes have already been reduced from 1 hour to 5 minutes and the items you cooked during those initial 5 minute timer are usually delivered together, so you do not even have to wait a full 5 minutes for each item you cook. You can use these for the museum, for the pets, and to maximize sale value (Roasted fruit -> Jam -> Fruit tincture!). You keep finding recipes to craft a ton of furniture, which you can also personalize through crafting dyes. You can upgrade and decorate your tent, which with time gets more and more rooms.What I want to say with this is - you can stoically do the daily quests and be done within 30 minutes, or you can set your own personal goals and grinds just as you would in any other game, like RDR, Skyrim, WoW etc. The design, the furniture, outside decor etc is beautiful and you get major areas on the map to decorate as you please. It is very, very inviting to gather materials (and still easy enough!), process them to fill your museum, feed your pets, get quests done, furniture your home and decorate your island, and keep enough of each material in your storage for upcoming quests, broken tools, or in case a new item you want to craft. 99% of the days I play Cozy Grove, I am busy for at least 4 hours. I know this might not be attractive for teens, but working people with other responsibilities will be thankful for that.I have to say, Cozy Grove is extremely forgiving in this regard. I am playing in early fall right now, and I am easily still finding tons of legendary fish that spawn in summer. It is not as strictly locked as people here make it seem. This is way, way more forgiving than the dailies and weeklies from battlepasses of multiplayers that lock skins behind ingame currency you have to grind for or miss out on forever. The items in Cozy Grove always return, always. Yes, it might require you to check in with the game every few weeks, or at least a few times each season, but that is a very low commitment. I remember when being a completionist was about exactly that - the commitment, the effort, the grind, the satisfaction of having it all despite that taking a long time. Why do we have "completionists" now who only call themselves that because they're "OCD" about a number on their gaming profile? It's true, you will not get a 100% within 20 hours of playing this. But I have played 60 hours, and I have over half the badges, and a lot of the item collection at Captain Billweather is already finished or close to 50%, without me trying to 100% it. Despite the large amounts of shell and flowers in this game, I believe it is relatively easy to complete, especially when the events are announced so you can get those Halloween fish, peas etc. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a slow game. Keep that in mind when picking it up. It's not meant for "the grind," as the collecting, gathering, crafting, and decorating are all a cascade of getting parts 1, 2, and 3 which can take a few "days" or hours to do. This is a great game to help focus away from anxiety, stress, and gives you goals with generous time limits so that you 1) are all manageable and possible given time, and 2) with long time limits so that, in case you don't finish, you don't feel overwhelmed with a list of unfinished requests from the bears. The stories are good, cute, and somewhat dark, with some cute customization to your island, your avatar, and your tent. I definitely enjoy logging into this game every day to get the "daily quests" done, as well as spending an hour or more after those quests are finished to do random collecting, "gardening" and chatting with the bears. Would highly recommend if you just need a nice, cozy game to fill the time and still get that reward serotonin going.
