_childDocuments_.review: I'll agree that it's a lovely game, but if you're planning on streaming it maybe make it a super short stream, or the first like hour or so of a longer one. Played it for the first time on stream and it was about an hour and a half until the game was like "there's nothing else to do today go fish," which I wasn't going to just, sit and fish lol. I enjoy it anyway but I'll be making this a game for "me time" instead of streaming, I think, as I want to play it every day because I love it, and it isn't something I can confine just to streams.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a sweet, cozy, gentle experience. I love that it isn't harsh, there's no violence, it's all about love and redemption and kindness. I love that there's quests, but also tasks to complete outside of questing--fishing, collecting, crafting, DECORATING! The art and overall stylistics are beautiful and again, sweet and cozy. I really have no down-sides to offer. It's a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels reminiscent of Animal Crossing meets House in the Cerulean Sea. My main gripe with animal crossing has always been that it feels too overwhelming. Too broad. Cozy Grove feels like a sweet middle spot. It's something I can sink some time into, but not feel like I have to spend my entire day grinding at to make progress. Yes I know there are gripes about it being run on real time. But I'm a busy person. If I want to repeatedly come back to a game, I don't want to feel overwhelmed by all that there is to do. If you like a reprieve in your busy day with spirits that have interesting little problems and feed some animals. This is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't a huge fan of Animal Crossing, so when I saw people comparing this game to AC I wasn't sure I would like it, but I bought it on a sale anyway. I have spent 40 hours so far on this game and I will be spending more. I love the vibes, the art, the music, and the content. It really gives you just enough to do per day to avoid burn out, but be enough. I joke that I am doing my daily chores, but I look forward to the days I am able to play this after work. The only tiny complaint I have about the game is that I have to be in front of an object to interact with it, and it is a little clunky sometimes. I had to dig deep to find that complaint though.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove has been a part of my ritual since I got it 2 weeks ago. I log in to do my daily tasks (it's time-gated to real-time, like Animal Crossing). The tasks force me to slow down and diversify my time in a way that's not frustrating - but rather reassuring. "The game will be here for me tomorrow, please get everything else done that you need to." The music is soothing, the dialogue is cute and you can progress your story.It's got completionist goals, it's got cute decorating and crafting, it's got cute spooks, it's got pets. It's kind of everything I want in a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty relaxing. I enjoy it on my off days from work to just have a chill time. The artwork is interesting and very cute. The game runs smooth and has no weird dialogue that takes to long to get through. It's a pretty straight forward game you can enjoy when you don't want to hop on more focused games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly one of my favourite game I've ever played! The art is just so cute and beautiful. Even tho you only have 1-2 hours of game play per day (doing the quests), there's just so much to do. I've already put 32 hours into the game but I can tell you that there's a lot more to come. It's just so relaxing to play. I can say that Cozy Grove really helped me with my anxiety.If you love cozy games, this one's for you. You have no rush, you play at your own pace and that's just one of the many other great things about Cozy Grove. If you like collecting things, that's a great option too. You have fishes, insects, sea shells and a lot of other things to collect to complete your collection. If you love animals, I'm sure you'll fall in love with the game since you can have a lot of animals with you at your camp that you can interact with everyday.Those great things are just scratching the surface of the potential of the game.It's 100% worth the money. I can't even explain how I love the game, it's just crazy. ♡
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: What instantly attracted me to the game is the adorable art style and similar game place as Animal Crossing. The game play is pretty fun. And I appreciate the work the devs are doing to improve the game. Aside from fun game play are the diverse cast of Ghostly Bears you must help. Each one is unique and full of personality. The relation ships between the residential spirits of Cozy Grove is so intriguing to learn.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game, for me, has been lovely. As other reviews state, it's time-gated, so even on a day where there is tons to do, it's probably a maximum of 40 minutes of playtime. Nearing the end of the story, I am only popping on for a few minutes a day.Things I thought were particularly strong were...- Art style- Dialogue writing, many of the bears you get attached to and I found the writing really refreshing and funny, you really do feel like these bears' lives are realistic in the sense that they're multi-dimensional characters, many of whom have made morally gray decisions. I did not expect to have my heart strings tugged as much as I did!- Music (although I agree that it gets repetitive)- Game flow from around day 20-60; there's enough to do without it being too much, you feel like grinding a little bit is worthwhile as you will likely need the resources later, and it's still fun to spend 10 minutes fishing- Updates from developers have been responsive to feedback and add exciting elements- No penalty for missing daysThings I thought could be improved...- Diversity of quest types; the game is essentially only fetch quests, though the developers are trying to make them a little more interesting.- Spacing of the story - for example I am at day 100something and I've completed the main story quest, but there are still 3 bears whose 'personal' stories I'd like to finish, but I have over 1,000,000 coins and tons of resources so I don't really feel a desire to do anything other than check if there are updates with the 3 bears (often there aren't) and then log off. There is enough content that it could probably be timed a little better to make all the endings hit less than a week apart.Overall I really enjoyed this game as an after-work activity to mentally transition into home time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, as advertised, extremely cozy! I could gather mushrooms and fish for days. The cute take on macabre humor on a haunted island from which your predecessors have not returned is delightful. Gamepad support is stellar. The stories of the ghosts are a nice balance of silly and bittersweet, and I don't think I'm even halfway through. I have this game with my morning coffee, and you should too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: So, my love for this Game goes so deep that I finally bring myself to writing a review, that consists from more than a "good".Cozy Grove, eventhough it's artstyle might remind you a bit of Don't Starve, is the little, more storydriven, twin of animal crossing. You arrive on an empty island, which after further inspection is not even close to empty, but filled with ghosts which all need your help to find their peace. Every day you play (this game runs in real time), you get a small portion of story and a few quests, that consist of crafting, searching things or, since one of the newer updates, taking photographs for the spectral population of the island. Next to this you can plant trees, flowers and bushes, hunt bugs, fish, decorate your island (and your home), have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of pets and try to finish your collection of all of the above. Now that I described the gameplay, I want to tell you why I like this game, maybe even a bit more that the better known releases in this genre. 1. The pacing is just right. I have enough to do in a day to not be overwhelmed neither is there to few chores. My progress is just about right to keep me excited to start the game every day, and the day after and the day after that and after...Plus there's enough variation to keep you entertained. I really am curios every day to see what new things I will learn about the ghosts stories, which leads to our next point:2. The characters. Every Ghost or non Ghost character in this game has a character and is not just a hollow shell. I love to see them progress through their stories and warm up to the player's character. The progress the ghosts make also opens up new shops and more.3. The Details. I just want to mention one little example, or my review would get waaaaaay to long. Whenever you finished talking to a ghost for the day you have the option to ask them if they want a hug, that alone would be incredibly cute and a nice little detail, but no there are ghosts that will refuse your hugs until you have earned their sympathy. The hugs don't do anything in the game besides being a small thing that makes me smile whenever I hug one of my ghosts - which already is part of:4. This game is relaxing and makes me happy. No explanation needed.In conclusion: When you want 1-2h of storyprogression and animal crossing-esque gameplay and that over a long period of time, with a nice artstyle, well written characters and a lot of personalization options and that every day, cozy grove is a game you might want to look into.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I'm afraid I just can't get behind the limited gameplay per day. I'm 3 days in, and yet I have all these inventory items I don't understand, not enough space, and I basically can't do anything for anyone every day and they all become ghosts again.Unfortunately, for me, it feels like a chore to play this game and that I'm making absolutely no progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game already say it clear that you only need to play 1 - 2 hours a day.This is the reason:You need to talk to the spirit bear (or we call it NPC), they will give you a quest (the spirit bear can only give one quest each day - sometimes few spirit bears doesn't have quest), the quest is either you need to seek some items (this item only appear when you have the quest) or collecting natural object (we can collect this items even without the quest - wood, fish, critter) and sometimes they also ask for cooking itemsFor me this is a fun and relaxing game, you can finish the quest slowly and if there is no quests left you can just collecting the natural object like fishing and catch the critter or cooking, you can donate every new items you have found it to NPC
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I MIGHT recommend this game. I've had fun. Even if you don't find the time issue acceptable, you can get around it by changing it manually (although it's not the greatest experience). Expect maybe 15-30 min of daily gameplay. It looks cute, kind of like a colorful version of 'Don't Starve'. The clothing options are fun, my favorite is a hat that makes you look like a sunflower. The music and the effects are satisfying as well, and I love the part of fulfilling quests that colors the island. The NPCs are quirky and interesting.What makes me hesitant with this game is how repetitive everything is, and how it feels stressful mixed with boring trying to come up with enough materials to finish feeding your animals and fulfilling quests every day. Materials are limited in spawning and frankly it's very bothersome to just wait and search all the time. There is also a 1 hour wait time on cooking.Everything gets more and more cluttery and it's harder to find quest items and materials through all of the furniture and whatnot. Also, targeting things in a more congested area is really hard, whether you click or go closest to your target to use the E key it's set on not picking out what you want. I don't regret buying it, since I've gotten 30 hours out of it so far, but I am aware that some people probably would.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and music are lovely, the bears are so fun and the game as a whole is super relaxing. As someone with a busy schedule, being able to play around 1h/day without getting feelings of missing time is so great. It might be a bad thing if you intend to play this game only and tryhard it by farming a lot, but for people looking for a good everyday break I highly recommend trying Cozy Grove.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Cozy Grove!Cozy is definitely the right word. I personally loved that it's in real time, as it forces you to pace yourself and not burn yourself out of the game :') The stories are actually really interesting and touching, I was not expecting that! There are tons of decorations if you enjoy playing around  with those. At first I was annoyed at having to decorate around the Bear's own decorations, but I ended up liking the challenge of addind stuff around theirs :) For people who like their achievements, some of them are ridiculously long if you don't actively work on them from the beginning (looking at you ''break 150 tools). Super happy I got to play this game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I buy this game because I searched a alternative for animal crossing. And this is the .It is very relaxing and helps you to get off the day and get involved creatively in your own world.The artwork is more gorgeous as other life-simulations and the world grows bigger and more colorful with every advance. So you always have something new to discover.Every day you become new quests of the villagers. That the game is optimized for one to two hours of daily play is also a plus point for me (I get lost easily in endless games.). When you have your daily quests finished you can close the game and wait for the next day or you can do some everyday tasks like fishing, grinding, harvest, crafting, decorate etc.The gameplay is also good. I have some trouble with the controller and play with keyboard and mouse. Its my personal taste. But the gameplay and the keyboard layout is very intuitive.I love the game, the story in the background (the story is not the most important thing, nor is it the most present in the game), the characters, the gameplay - i love the whole game and I can only recommend it to others.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I have played 64 hours to get the first story of a bear complete and it was a disappointment to say the least. Lost and found quests are repetitive and take longer and longer. The first heart of a bear is easy but instead of getting exponentially more challenging or more fun it just takes longer and longer to complete quests. Ofcourse it's highly addictive and i kept playing to see what would happen if all the hearts of a bear got filled. But now after having one finished I am deleting the game. Don't play this if you don't want to waste your time. If you do, be my guest.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure you've heard that it's like Animal Crossing and Don't Starve mixed together - and that is very correct. It's a very fun, relaxing game. The only down fall is you can only do so much in a day. I'd like to be able to get as much spirit wood as Flamey can consume!!! Also, I've found everyone's game is a little different. Some people get some recipes and some get others. You have to find your own way in the game and I think that's pretty neat. It's a game I look forward to playing everyday!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy grove is really cute and relaxing, its the perfect game to just sit down and chill with during a break. The limited daily quests also are nice because sometimes I get too burnt out on a game after playing it for hours on end every day but with cozy grove I end each day ready to come back and play again the next and see what new stuff is waiting for me simply because it's not possible to grind for hours. For some the restriction might be annoying but I think it's nice
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The word 'Cozy' is the perfect way to describe this game, it'll leave you feeling warm inside and calm! I didn't think I would put so many hours in to this game when I first purchased it but something keeps pulling me back in for more.I would highly recommend as a slow paced and easy going game, that you can dip in to at anytime.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It can be a little glitchy with the drawings and placement of items, but that's harmless. Stories are cute. It's a nice little game I like to relax with. Contrary to some other opinions, I do like that there is a limited number of goals you have each day. 1. It gives me a feeling of accomplishment. 2. It gives me a reasonable stopping point so I don't get sucked into playing for 48 hours straight.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a charming, relaxing, kinda addictive and very slightly irritating game. During the summer holidays, it's become a part of my daily routine, and it just makes me feel good. It is, indeed, cozy. I've always wanted to own Animal Crossing, but am not willing to spend so much on a suitable console, but Cozy Grove triggers fond childhood memories of playing Animal Crossing with my friend. The art style is very different of course, but the realistic, honest, dark, and humorous dialogue is sort-of similar. Yet where AC is more about the harsh realities of debt, CG is more about the harsh realities of death. Which makes it way more peaceful.Things I enjoy:- the dialogue and storytelling, which somehow manages to be genuinely touching and thought-provoking (for some bears moreso than for others)- the way the game gently forces you to set your own desire for control second to the needs of those around you, not only in helping out the bears and going along with some fairly outrageous requests, but also by just having to live near the MESS that is Dennings' home,
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautifully made. I like the idea of bringing color into the after live of this ghosts. The game somehow paces down my day. I know too many games where you just binge and grind until there is no soul left inside you. It is therefore relaxing not being able to brute force the story line. It is like in real life, traumatic or sad experiences take time to get over and it needs patience do deal with the hurt ones. I will for sure invest some more time into this pretty little gem.There is still room for improvements: the inventory has no sort button and it is only possible to craft one or possible max amount of goods. But then again, the game is not about winning as fast as possible or being perfectly efficient. You play a little scout, how could it be perfectly organised...I rate it 4/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Its a lot of finding materials or items within the woods to restore the bear spirits. Theres only so much you can do in a day and it runs on a real world clock, so that may be a deterrent for those that just want to grind through a game. Highly recommend it, super chill and low stress.Edit: I'm on day 77, and I've transcended a few bears, and worked hard to build the trust for these bears. A few of them after transcendence, disappear entirely when the dlc kicks over. I was so excited to show Clyde that I made it, and I couldn't have done it without him and he was gone. On top of that, the personalities of the bears is completely stripped from them after they transcend.. And thats utterly heartbreaking as well. I still love the game, and am invested in the story and each of these bears lives. I just wish there was some follow through with after transcendence.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It is sooo cute and relaxing! I love the puns. Characters are adorable. I'm not into games with lots of decoration assets and in Cozy Grove you need furniture to get some buffs therefore my island is a mess and it gets a bit hard to select stuff that are behind other stuff and I think I lost some chickens, but apart from that it is a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: this game is SO cute and wholesome. it's limited to one to two hours a day, which was strange to get used to, but that's only for the main storyline quests. you can spend as much time doing whatever you want, like collecting, decorating, etc. helping the bears is really satisfying and i just love how chill it is to play in the morning with coffee. pick it up on sale!!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: We all have to eat crow sometime, and today is my day. I reviewed this game poorly just yesterday, stating it was in serious need of QoL improvements and massive rebalancing, and while I stand by what I said, apparently those things were also already on the minds of the developers at Spry Fox LLC as an update was released less than 10 hours later.. It’s clear the developers of this title are attuned to the community that’s growing around it, as they even posted a polite request to give the game another try after I updated. Personal touches, such as polite or tactful comments on reviews and acting upon suggestions from the community, really shine a positive light on this development team. There’s a difference between acting like you listen to what your audience is saying, and addressing those complaints head on, which is what they’ve done here and then some. Reading through the patch notes was like breathing a sigh of relief or getting a trill excitement at each point. It’s rare for me to be so excited over an update, but they’ve carefully addressed the major economic and resource imbalances, added a “craft multiple” option (which is fantastic, thank you devs.) hint location refinement, and so much more in this most recent update.After playing the update on a new save file and completing the first day’s worth of quests, I found myself satisfied with the amount of content provided. I was able to relax and enjoy the tranquil music and complete the handful of quests without frustration, coming to what felt like a natural stopping place (in part thanks to new dialog from Flamey which I enjoyed immensely). I’m now excited to see what other updates the developers may have planned in the future, and look forward to really unraveling this story!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot in common with several other survival crafting games. The critical difference with this one is that it happens in real-time, so you are only *supposed* to play for a little time each day - but for days and days and days in a row. I hate games that try to tell the player that they are playing the game wrong. In this game, you run out of things to do each day in about an hour. After that, you have to wait (or change your computer clock). I opted to race my computer clock ahead so that I could try actually enjoying playing the game for a bit (doing a few days in each session). Once I got to day 6 or 7, I realized that this game was missing a critical piece for any game. The game is cute, and has some interesting mechanics that it took a minute to sort. But, the game doesn't have joy. I don't feel like I am actually working towards something -- just that I am grinding. I guess their hope was that the daily time limit would hide the lack of joy and grind.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to have something to play to relax for a few minutes every day after work or college. Being forced to wait for resources to refresh stops me from grinding through the game and getting burnt-out like I would with Stardew Valley etc. I think it's super cute and worth the price I paid for it (^-^)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game had me in a CHOKEHOLD!! I will say I kind of trailed off playing after a while because it can get super monotonous. Regardless, it's a great quest-based game with tons of customization and lots of fun to be had!! You can get a lotttttt of hours out of this one! I think I just convinced myself to play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: 20 days in and I'm on the fence about how much I like this game, but if you specifically love collecting items, don't mind a load of inventory management, and are prepared to approach the game with patience, it makes a reasonably enjoyable calm gameplay experience.I think my biggest frustration comes from a mix of a UI design problem and my own love of packing items into a space-efficient configuration.  I'm constantly wanting to harvest a bunch of flowers from pots I put down 1-2 spaces away from each other, and it is a HUGE pain to try to target individual flowers or other harvestable items placed so close to each other.  (Especially with a controller -- mouse isn't great but controller is 4x worse.)  I don't love the idea of rearranging flowerpots to spread them out farther, because placed items also interfere with targeting random collectibles, and also, new ghosts keep popping up in what I thought were safe places to expand my garden, with new accompanying decorative scenery that gets mixed right in with the stuff I deliberately laid out.Anyway, if you can tolerate a bit of chaos, or if you are willing to put in the work to reorganize your decorations as you discover any issues with your first attempt, you may have a better time with this aspect of the game.  These problems also may be subject to change in the future, since it seems like devs are still tweaking the UI for the better as time passes.I do enjoy the spirit dialogue.  Humorous tone with a little underlying tragedy in many (most? all?) cases.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Steam kept recommending this to me. It was near the top of compatible matches and it was on sale, so I thought I'd give it a try. Page said it was a play 1-2 hours a day thing, which sounded doable for a slow progress gamer like me. And the name itself says "Cozy" which made me think it'd be relaxing. I was unprepared for how much story content there is. When it's tagged with "story rich" it absolutely means it.To be clear, I don't generally care about story content. I opted not to get the expansion because a review said it's mostly more story content.The game is generous in that it has a skip function, but the amount of times I had to use it in order to keep interacting with mechanics wore me out on the first attempt. After a minimalist character creation and a long feeling intro scene I washed up on the island. There were a number of speech bubbles before I could actually do anything, so as soon as I could actually start playing I quit. I'd seen the art style which is like Don't Starve (not a good thing for me), but more cute, and interacted with the flow of the game (which is that there will be a little bit of user interaction and then a fixed camera moment followed by speech bubble after speech bubble of story content). I was ready to return the game, but I had to be fair and give it another try; actually play a bit.My time was limited if I wasn't sure about keeping this, so I decided to check out the guides to see what I'd be dealing with if I really dedicated my time to this game. Instant intimidation: Time gates, meta strategies about how to get around time gates, what things to ignore or not focus on, benefits tied to cosmetics and decorating, a bunch of food recipes for quests, achievements you can only get at certain times of the IRL year. I told myself that none of that is necessarily bad. It's probably many small things to do over a long span of time. Just give it a try. So I got to the camp site. Cut scene, more speech bubbles, leave cut sceene, more speech bubbles. Can't actually do anything, so I have to go talk to somebody. Around this time I realized I was in a mandatory tutorial phase where I'm expected to get emotionally invested in the characters. The skip function is there, but I'm not sure if they're going to actually be telling me something useful or if it's just a bunch of story. As it happens, the answer is both. The characters tell you how to use the game mechanic the same way a blog gives a recipe: they tell you their life story and then tell you how to do things. I unlocked some of the people nearby the camp site. Ran in circles a bit because I didn't understand how to check quest progress, dug some holes, scattered some leaves, skipped a lot of dialog. Things didn't seem like they were changing up or going somewhere more, so I called it there and finalized the return. The game feels like a visual novel with some farming sim mechanics thrown in. People who like story rich RPGs will probably have more fun with it, since a lot of the things I'm complaining about are things they would enjoy. I don't have any constructive criticism to offer because I didn't get far enough to find anything wrong with the game; it's just not a game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. I love the art style. I love the spooky theme. I love the bears. I love the decoration items. I love the pets. I love having a game that I can't sink too much time into in a given day. And I do find it cozy and relaxing... up until a certain point.It is not as relaxing as I had expected. That's ok, but I do think it is worth noting for potential buyers. It is a fairly grindy and resource based game, and on top of that the core mechanic is essentially an I Spy game in which finding very obscured tiny items is needed to progress. There is a hint system, and a pay-to-find-it system, but even with that there are moments of frustration for me personally. Also, it requires a lot of patience, with some quests spanning days. I wouldn't say this is a problem for me, but I could see it being a problem for someone else.So, yes, I recommend it. I'm still playing it every day. But I would be lying if I said it was as relaxing as Animal Crossing or Stardew Valley, for example.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite cozy game! It's mainly a hidden object game to find objects for spirits on the island. There are other activities like fishing, planting flowers/trees, catching bugs, and collecting a cute wardrobe. Most objectives can be completed in just an hour and do not refresh until the next real world day, so this is a great game to chill out and enjoy, but not get sucked into for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Well... it's cozy enough i guess. The game has a peaceful vibe yet undertone about death to it, you can't binge play it though the game is restricted to real life time and things could be done so much in one single day, to boost the game length i guess. The game itself doesn't rush you to do anything and there's no competition so no hurry?? Oh.. and there's no farming no romancing so it's not a harvest moon type game it's more like animal crossing according to my friend. In conclusion if you want a slow-paced chill game Cozy Grove might be cozy enough for u.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: As you can see I've only played for 5 hours. Here's the thing, I've played 5 days > 1hr/day because I couldn't find something to do in order to play more.  I love relaxing games but this is just something beautiful to look at and... I wanted to play. Because it's a game. Before getting this I was 100% sure I'd give it all the positive recommendations possible but I just simply can't, it's kind of an empty game. One thing I'm sure of, I will never ever believe the hype, marketing and reviews of a game...
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit that what at first was just a cute exploring endevour quickly shifted into hugging souls and hearing our their stories, one by one. The stories are curiously drawing you in, and while you fish, gather flowers or shells, like i many such games, do not be fooled! There is a deeper story underneath. The detailed graphics stole my heart and the BGM music soothes my heart. Please, give Cozy Grove a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It seemed really interesting - I watched a video or two, it was on sale. I kept waiting for it to get less annoying, but it just got more so.  The art style along with the hunt down hidden items in uncolored areas. Oh that little bush that doesn't disappear - the black squiggle line/leaf is hidden behind it....  Oh and tomorrow we're going to move everything around so when they ask you to find something vaguely near a stick - you have to go hunt down the new hiding place for the stick.That there's no way to make any real money. Ingredients seem annoyingly rare. No, no storage unless you have 400,000 gold - but Mr AH bear is going to want a particular item tomorrow which won't spawn tomorrow. The only thing in any quantity is fish, but fish sell for 50 gold, you can turn fish into 1+ fish bones and then turn fishbones into furniture, and get maybe 250 gold - but no I'm not kidding about the 400,000.  Oh hey - something is asking for this and this requires a deviled egg which requires 8 boiled eggs, but to make a boiled egg you need 12 eggs, and you might get 1-2 eggs a day.There's a ton of pets, but no place to really put them unless they are all on top of each other and the same with trees. Then you can have as many cats as you want, so long as it's only one or two. You start off with things that don't like rustic or common and when you start off - you only get rustic and common. Oh and spooky and I have yet to find a single thing that liked spooky. And then I didn't even like the characters - I'm supposed to want to help these bears move on and I just kinda thought maybe that wasn't going fast enough because I still have to deal with them. Then the notes from the scout leader who basically sends you letters everyday going, LOL FU
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It's very similar to Animal Crossing, except you can only play between 1-2 hours a day which is pretty nice as I always look forward to it. It works in real time, so you can complete some quests each day, then you have to wait for the next ones to progress the story. It's very pretty, very relaxing and very cute. Highly recommended :)Activities include:* Fishing* Hide and seek for lost items* Crafting* Decorating* Digging and finding treasures
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute and amazing. I played for hours straight and I would play even more if it wasn't for the quest system. In fact, this is the problem with the game for me: you can play only for a few hours daily, because there's a limit of quests you can do every day since it follows the real time. For me, it is a problem because I'm the type of player that doesn't have much free time and, when I have a free day in my schedule, I'd like to play as much as I wish. But in this game you can't, then I'm forced to stop playing it because there's nothing else to do on that day. Since I don't have time to play every single day, I'm also forced to wait until I have another free time to play it again and sometimes it takes too looooong for me to have that kind of day. And, well, I'd like to play others games in my free days too, 'cause I love games and I have a loooooooong list of games I wanna play when I finally have a free time!Well, that said, let's go to the recommendation!If you like games like Animal Crossing, for example, you're going to LOVE this one! It's cute, it has a nice story and the quests aren't difficult. The villagers are adorable, there are collections for the ones who like to explore and collect things. You're going to craft, you're going to learn about the villagers, you're going to buy cute clothes and accessories. Also have easy achievements to get! You just need to play and do the quests. It's casual and calming, so if you're looking for a game to play and distract yourself from the world out there, it's is perfect for you! You'll probably forget about every single problem and worry only about your new ghost friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes charm with its artistic style, simple gameplay, and excellent soundtrack. It's exactly what I want to play when unwinding. The criticism about the lack of things to do are valid and I hope it is addressed going forward via new activities and expanded decoration opportunities. But for me, it offers enough and the price point is low enough I still feel confident in recommending it. I'm not looking for a game to grind out multiple hours a day. I have like 20 games-as-a-service I play for that already. Cozy Grove is a neat little package capable of scratching that itch of casual, relaxing enjoyment. My play time as of writing this is my first day playing. I took my time to enjoy the scenery and read all of the dialogue available, dug up some holes, mined some ore, and jumped in any pile of leaves I could find. That's how I play games. If you play games similarly and are looking for a nice little romp in a charming forest after getting stomped in your competitive game of choice, I think you'll like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Great music and superb art!!! I usually play this before work or during my breaks to unwind. Super fun and chill game if you're already burned out with Animal Crossing but still have that itch to play a social/crafting simulation game. It's very fulfilling to play! The game is also generous with quest rewards ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute game! Its fun and the fact that there are storylines to progress with each bear is nice, but its very annoying how the game doesn't really let you play on your own terms. Its so sad every time you hit a wall in things you can do, even if you don't really care about making progress. Its very nice and fun but you can't expect to get as much out of it as it seems at first glance.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The devs were kind enough to give me a copy of this cute little game and I'm really enjoying it so far!Like the other comments say, this isn't a game you can play for hours on end in one sitting. This is a game much like Animal Crossing in that there are only so many things you can do/complete within a day. I actually don't mind this aspect!The art style is stunning (reminds me of Don't Starve but cuter) and the sound effects for everything in the game is super satisfying. Only played a little bit of Cozy Grove but it has left a really good impression on me and I would recommend it to others who also enjoy Animal Crossing!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very relaxing game that's very simple to play but also very fun. Most similar to Animal Crossing though not an exact copy in a good way. I enjoy waking up and completing all of my little tasks for an hour or so as it's not very intensive though a nice game if you're not looking to be stunned by complex mechanics
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove feels like a charming combination of Animal Crossing and Don't Starve, and keeps you coming back each day for more.You begin the game as a Spirit Scout on an island with an enchanted talking campfire, and your new home, a tent. As you wander the island you discover different resources and collectibles, along with a handful of ghost bears. You are able to fish, catch bugs, cook, and raise different kinds of supernatural animals. Like Animal Crossing, there are different quests, events, and objectives to complete for your bear acquaintances each day, although slightly more in depth or extensive at times.  Even once you run out of quests to do each day, there is still plenty of content to explore. You can turn many items into a "collection", where they are catalogued, and receive rewards for them. *Be warned, do not time travel (particularly back in time) as this can corrupt your save file and you will lose all of your progress.* Over time, your island slowly expands as you build rapport and friendship with your spectral neighbors, and unlock old forgotten memories of theirs.Cozy Grove is a fun game that provides a truly cozy environment, and becomes difficult to walk away from.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy grove is cute and fun game to play when you want to relax. First I didn't realize that you have only certain amount missions per day when you play. Didn't read the description of the game that well but it's okay since I like this system. This game has a lot of things to collect and there is many achievements which I like. Story of the game is nice and interesting. I haven't finished the game yet but I don't see my mind changing about the game that much. I wished there was more skill to fishing but otherwise I like the game. I can totally recommend this to people who like cute games with nice story and likes to collect things in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is very relaxing and peaceful. Each bear's story is unique and enjoyable. This is a game I can pick up every day or after setting it down for a few weeks; there's always something to do, and a lot of achievements to keep you busy and working toward goals.The art style is probably my favorite part of the game. There are so many items, characters, and parts of the environment and they all mesh very well together. The large array of items also gives you a lot of opportunity to create the aesthetic you want to have at your campsite.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Played for almost a full hour, about 56 minutes. Honestly I thought I would like this game since I love games like Animal Crossing. But it's repetitive right at the start, it is ENDLESS fetch quests, it's a glorified point and click finder game with walking.It has a crafting system, and seems like it can offer hours upon hours of endless idle daily chore game play. There seems to be some sort of pet system but I wasn't able to accomplish that due to having to wait 14 real hours to receive food through the post system in-game. Like I just mentioned, the game does rely on real time, which is how the developers intended it to be played and I think there's nothing wrong with that.The main goal of the game seems to be leveling up your relationship with the spirits that reside in Cozy Grove (The island you are on / title of the game), to learn about them and their backstory as well as helping them "pass on" (may be wrong about the passing on). Sometimes this can be as simple as crafting an item you probably already have the resources for, to tediously looking at the grayish background of non-populated areas of the island for multiple biscuits that blend in with the background and are behind bushes and other objects. (Note: the gray areas can become colored either by helping a spirit for the first time around that area or by extended reach with lantern crafting and placing early in the game). You can expand the island by raising your relationship status with the spirits and using a unique item on your main campfire that they give you (not always) after completing a task for them. This opens up areas for you to explore and it seems in most cases it also introduces another spirit for you to care for. This would be interesting if this wasn't just a fetch me an item and progress the story sort of game, which if it isn't, they don't do a job of making it known whatsoever. The only thing I did in the first hour of the game was fetch items and expand the island before I was done with the monotony. The spirits have some nice dialogue to share with you, (decent writing, a nice joke or pun here and there)  but it seems empty and lacks the depth you would expect from a game that the entire focus of is helping the quest givers. It's maybe three or four lines and it's on to the next fetching.I see the nice pictures of what people have created with the crafting and placement system, but honestly the game is just an idle time passer if anything. The ability to place objects in the world is just an added bonus and gives you another thing to strive for, seemingly to compensate for the lack of depth this game has with the "story".Other than the actual game play, the world itself is nice and beautifully crafted, my only gripe graphically would be the gray areas.I think this game would be wonderful for the correct audience, of which I was not.When I saw footage of this game before it came out, it seemed different and more "immersive" than just fetch quests and clicking on a bush to harvest mushrooms and branches.PLEASE realize, I played this game for 56 minutes like I said at the beginning. The repetitive nature of the game reveals itself very early on, and it was all I needed to see to realize that I made a mistake in purchasing this game. Everyone will have their own unique experience with this game, if you are interested in this game, then try it out or look at other people playing the game first before making a decision.This is my OPINION.-Picked up game on "sale" for $9.89 -which is leaning more towards what it should actually be priced at, seems like a mobile game if anything.-Received Refund-Do Not Recommend unless you like this sort of thing, look at game play videos before making the purchase if you are unsure.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: it's such a nice game to play after you've had a busy weekday (talking as a student worker!!!!!) i've been playing for over a month and i still love it. the "time lock" system might not be for everyone, but personally it helps to have a low stress game where i don't feel pressured to go through the entire thing in a few days. the environment customization options are really varied but imo not enough that they become overwhelming, same goes for your character, who always looks cute as hell!!!! the bears are absolutely lovely, most of their stories almost made me tear up, i can 100% fix clyde and valentina and i will.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy slower paced games in general and I find Cozy Grove is a great slow, life sim. The art is beautiful, the details are wonderful (I laugh quite a bit), and I don't mind how long it takes to get through. I can see why having only 30 minutes to an hour of game play per day bothers people. I happily hop around the island resource gathering or checking recipes when I've done main story and timed daily quests. I am not a fan of the photo quests or skipping rocks so I give those a pass. Some people will find the ever changing landscape on the island a frustrating experience but I've found there's a few key features that don't move around. All in all I definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The premise for the game is cool. The first couple days i loved it (you only play like 40 minutes or so a day) but after a while it's just so grindy. It can take days to accomplish one single goal and that just isn't fun. Getting some stuff seems rng based and making no progress in this game for days at a time is just a bad time. Everything feels like a free to play phone game mission (why does it take 12 eggs to make 1 boiled egg?). Maybe with future updates the game will be worth playing but for right now it's more hassle than it's worth. Pity too, this is one of my favorite genre of games. I was looking forward to a spooky animal crossing. But this aint it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun Animal Crossing-like game. There is tons of stuff to collect and there's always something to do every day. I love the little stories you follow with each of the ghost bears. It starts off slow but about a week in it really picks up. If you want to play Animal Crossing on Steam this is probably the closest thing you can get. 9/10 Really fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice art, atmosphere and idea but this gameplay is a nightmare. If only this game could afford basic non-daily gameplay I would be happy to collect the feathers, leaves and whatever else even if it's repetitive and casual. I just want to spend a good time playing, not to get a second job. That's sad cause the other aspects of the game like music, characters, badges etc are very cute and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a calming experience, with just enough to do every day to keep you busy, but without pressure to play every single day. The graphics are very heart-warming and the characters are lovely to interact with. For that price I would ABSOLUTELY recommend, if you like games like Stardew Valley, or Animal Crossing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the closest thing to Animal Crossing in terms of completing daily quests within days before being locked from progression. It's not a bad thing per say. It's cute, relaxing, and spooky sometimes. Can't believe it's from the same studio that made the Alpha Bear on mobile back when I played it in high school. The characters and their memories are cute and witty. It's just wholesome, what else can I say?
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, cozy, time gated game - If you're looking for something casual that requires only a few minutes a day to show time progression and a deeper story progression while being able to fish, craft, garden and cook Cozy Grove is for you! I wish there was more of it - I spend a long time in the game daily not just idling but wandering around and fishing, catching bugs, collecting shells... There are so many still left for me to find and I've already spent so many hours in game that I'm sure this one is going to be super rich with content. Fair warning, it's like a daily grind so if you don't like that kind of thing then this won't be for you but I've been having tons of fun with it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, chill game, which is kind of what I need right now. At first I was a little frustrated with the real-time day limits, but I think it's trying to make a statement about helping people on THEIR own time--you can't help someone until THEY are ready, and I appreciate it in that sense. I also appreciate the slightly off-kilter humor of the characters (and the Scout Master's letters, LOL). So far the story has been fine (and on the warm, but sad side), which is sort of what I think I expected, because it's meant to be chill and relaxing without some crazy dramatic and gripping stuff, right?
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: To me, this is a much better version of Animal Crossing. It might not be for everyone but the writing is touching and great. The long burn isn't due to "grinding" but the opposite, intentionally enabling small gameplay sessions to give you meaningful progress. I do wish the various economies were less opaque, it's hard to know (without looking up a guide) whether something is worth spending money on or selling, what the best use is for various things, etc. because if you use up materials on furniture "just because", it can stunt your progress elsewhere for a time (not forever, of course, but maybe longer than you'd like).
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a charming game with lots of things to do. With cute graphics and simple gameplay mechanics, this game is perfect for all ages. The tasks are varied and can range from collecting critters and resources to fishing. The controls are easy to pick up and the game has a fun, lighthearted tone that will keep you entertained. Overall, Cozy Grove is a must-try for fans of cute, casual games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this, you've probably played, or have been interested in games like Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing. Cozy Grove possesses elements of both games aforementioned, but can hold it's own. For me, the thing Cozy Grove does better than other games in this genre is its ability to encourage healthy playtime. Like most games I enjoy (especially simulation games), I can spend hours at a time questing away. I don't think this is an inherently bad thing, but I do occasionally have moments of regret when I realize how poorly I've managed my time. Cozy Grove has a finite amount of things you can harvest and quests you can complete in a given day. While you could spend hours fishing for new species to add to the archive, it's never been something I've felt I absolutely needed to do *today*. Admittedly, I was a little turned off to this approach when I initially purchased the game; but, after giving it another try, I've come back to it every day and I intend to continue doing so until I've completed the game. I really think Cozy Grove has improved the way I approach gaming in general. I feel like it has taught me a good lesson in restraint!! I realize this methodology isn't for everyone, but I really think it's worth giving a try. You might not have much to do on day one, but I assure you -- day by day this game will blossom in to something you will really cherish!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just adorable! I love the art style and the story concept. There is plenty to do in this game, all based on finding, collecting, and crafting items to expand and help the Spirits of Cozy Grove. I also personally love that there is a limit to what you can do each day you play, giving you that break from the game to come back tomorrow and play again! You can also personalize your island with things that you craft, as well as your character's outfit and look.This is such a relaxing and cute game, I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The most important things to know about this game are:*It is time gated*. You are not in charge of how much of it you play, inasmuch as advancing the storyline. You will be told repeatedly to "Come back another day" and NPCs will give you lines about being "patient" because this is probably the core ethos. It's ultimately why I stopped playing. For people who have very limited time to play games in the first place (whether you have a demanding job, children, health issues, etc), the game telling me on my day off that I simply can't enjoy the storyline any further and that I should just exercise patience? Very irritating. Especially because...*The game is just a loop of the same activities.* It's very cute to look at, but be prepared to do the exact same task over and over.. and over.. and over.. and over. With your upgrades/access to equipment also being (you guessed it) time gated. Feel like you made any progress the last time you played with lighting up your island? Congrats, the NPCs are now uncolored again and it's time to essentially start over. I don't have a lot of life to waste, and honestly, this felt like frustration more than fun. This is from someone who generally enjoys collection gameplay.The artwork is adorable. I was very much hoping to enjoy it. And I'm sure I would.. if I had the time and inclination to live on the game's schedule instead of my own.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface first that it's inaccurate imo to compare this to Animal Crossing. This is more of a hidden object game, which is not a genre I enjoy, but I am enjoying this one nonetheless. It's pretty cute and chill. It's not a game you play for multiple hours at a time. Once a day every character has new dialog, will give you some sort of quest, and once completed advance their story.Beyond that there's crafting and cooking (possibly more I haven't unlocked at the time of writing) which I found very boring, unfortunately. I have no reason to try that stuff besides completing quests or improving harvesting. I'm not enjoying decorating the island either. Placing furniture is a bit clunky at the moment, and the island is densely filled with trees and stones and imps that I feel adding furniture only makes it worse.Lastly, there are stuff to collect. Neither the stuff nor the rewards are engaging so I never go out of my way to collect stuff, just pick up whatever is on my way. The game is VERY generous with the material you harvest, which quickly fills up your storage. Because I don't craft much I usually just sell it all and harvest whenever needed.These are all small inconveniences, and would have been incredibly annoying/disappointing if the game sessions weren't short. And so in conclusion, it's a nice game to play for an hour every day while listing to some podcast or music (the game ost is very good too). Just don't expect it to be anything like Animal Crossing, or to play for multiple hours at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute! You do tasks every day in real time to help the ghosts of Cozy Grove move on. You meet ghosts one-by-one and your island grows each time you do. You dig, fish, forage, and craft. There are birds and deer and imps you can care for. This game will take a long time to finish; as of right now i'm 70 hours in and haven't saved a SINGLE GHOST. It's a unique game and I absolutely love it. I absolutely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A very very kind game so far, gentle and perfect for what I like when it comes to games. I especially love that there's no time limit on some of the quests, because it doesn't feel stressful to have a real life AND enjoy the game at the same time. There are some anti frustration features that fix what irritate me about some games, too- things like harvested materials NOT falling into the water, or being told where hidden objects are. But the game also doesn't feel too hand holdy or coddling to me, which I very much enjoy. 10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Animal crossing or any other laid back games then this one is for you. This game is a lot more like the GameCube Animal crossing where you are sent on tasks by the locals. Such a cute game, nice cozy music, and all the elements you are looking for in a chill easygoing game. It's tricky in different ways than you are expecting
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. The art style is lovely, the story is *chef's kiss*, and the pacing is surprisingly good. At first I was a bit apprehensive because the reviews said that you can only achieve so much progress each day, but I actually really like this. If you're doing uni or work or school and want to play something adorable and relaxing during your breaks, then this game would be a great fit for you. I don't have any major trifles with this game (or minor ones really), the only thing I get frustrated with is when I can't find items - but hints from Charlotte Pine are cheap anyways so I don't mind. The customisation options are fantastic, both for your character and tent. In my honest opinion, it's totally worth the price. Flamey is love, Flamey is life ^3^
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 5/5Artstyle is very beautiful. Probably this game's biggest draw honestly.Sound: 3/5The music goes for a very rustic vibe, which I do enjoy. However, the limited amount of tracks, plus the fact that there's no distinct track for certain parts of the game (Title screen, weather change, etc) makes the music get tiring far quicker than I expected.Gameplay: 2/5Probably the thing I least liked about it; Cozy Grove encourages to help out your ghost furballs and progress their story on a literal day-by-day basis; The other aspects of the game felt to me like a secondary feature. As such, minor annoyances that popped for me such as unable to organize tasks, very janky item placement and blindly looking around for items with no indication that they're available sometimes (ex: Was told to find roots, couldn't find a single root even after hunting around) detered my experience with this game.Difficulty: N/ALike with other life sims there really isn't a challenge level. This is a game where you go about your own pace.BOTTOM LINE: 3/5Cozy Grove is a pretty chill game but it's shortcomings really made the game feel a bit too annoying for me to love it. Still, for the price, I say it's worth a purchase to see if it's shortcomings are something you can get past, especially if the visuals and music already pull you in.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is a relaxing game where you run around trying to help the spirits you find. If you like Animal Crossing this has a similar feel. I have very much enjoyed the game. It has an interesting setting and story line. Though its a little sad once some of story lines complete and characters no longer interact with you in the way they did before.  Even so the characters and art are charming, If you like cozy games you may want to check this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It's such an endearing, sweet game - I love that you can give the bears hugs and pet your little animal friends. I do wish the furnishings didn't require quite so many materials to make. While gathering is something I love and have plenty of the basic materials, I feel like really being able to decorate more would be nice as part of the early game.This game is also perfect for those of us who don't own a console and wish we could play ACNH
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I like that you get a set of tasks to do and that you don't feel like you need to keep going and going. You can collect items around the island if you have completed the tasks, and want to continue playing, but I don't feel like I need to keep going and going. It's very relaxing and so friggin cute. I like that the date and time are displayed in the corner because if it isn't then I have a hard time keeping track of time (the fact that each day has a set amount of tasks also helps me spend an appropriate amount of time for my lifestyle and needs). Also- I broke my wrist and there was a lot off stuff I couldn't do for a heckin while. I was able to play this game with one hand on my laptop which helped me pass the boring days while I was healing. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a chill game with adorable graphics. Love that it's chill but that I don't get sucked in for longer than I want to spend on it. It kinda feels like a chiller version of Stardew Valley for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game that you could spend hours on at a time if it let you, but much like animal crossing it works in real time and gives you a certain number of tasks to do per day before you've done all you can for the day. The beauty of this game is that you want to keep coming back to play for about an hour each day and visit your new bear friends to help them out.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: As long as you read the description of the game and it sounds appealing, then you most probably will like the game. Weirdly enough, the usually frustrating time-gated content in the Cosy Grove feels right. It's a chilled game that is not intended to be binged until finished. You should consider this a semi-regular meetup between you and your scout to unwind from the day and answer to your collection addiction.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing game that involves finding items, gathering items for recipes and crafting, farming, and harvesting. Although I am super anxious at the idea of death, this game brings comfort. I also enjoy the soundtrack and the story lines. I have not finished the game, however, I feel that it will have unlimited play ability.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: One of the cutest games i have ever played!! The spirit bears are so cute!The art style is phenomenal 10/10The soundtrack? Stunning and so calming 10/10The character design? Amazing, incredible 10/10Cozy Grove is one of those games i couldn't recommend more! It's stylized and funky! love the daily tasks! I'm thoroughly enjoying the story at the moment!! Can't wait to play more! I recommend this game! support the amazing creators behind this adorable game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game but i have to give it a down vote, there is not enough to do in one day, the games story is locked with you only able to progress so far each day in real time, for example i am on day five in game and in real life with playing this yet i have only clocked 4.3 hours of play time. It feel like it is far too lax in its playablity, and though i like it, i can see myself getting bored with it and not playing for the story through due to its poor time management.I understand the developer wants to slow it down a little but it feels too slow, if they made it so you could say break for an hour and come back for more quests then cool but waiting till the next irl day to continue with a game is just a little bit frustrating in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and how it is designed to fit into people's lives. It is a beautiful game designed thoughtfully to minimise the risk of people getting addicted to it. This game has a limited number of tasks to be completed daily and it displays the time in a non-obtrusive manner on the bottom right of the screen. I appreciate all these elements as I am someone who gets easily addicted to games and play hours (nights) on end...until I invariably have to uninstall the game so that I can get along with other aspects of life. This game has allowed me to enjoy gaming in a regulated and balanced manner. I find it a refreshing daily getaway activity to engage in, and I wish more games will learn from this one. There is a lot to find satisfying and fulfilling in this game. I find that I get more and more proficient at completing the tasks everyday, you start capturing rarer creatures, and I am much more efficient at locating hidden objects as I learn the layout of the land and I intuitively know where things are placed. I particularly love raising my spirit animals and watching them evolve, and growing my area (and my funds).Besides this, the game is beautiful and has many elements that make it feel very homey and welcoming. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I've never left a review on a game before! Not for any reason other than I've always been the reader of such reviews. This game is awesome, if you're into games that use time as a large element of it. Dunno if you've ever heard of The Longing (game based on a swedish myth about waiting 400 days for the king to awaken) but this uses time in a smaller, but still very impactful, way. Oftentimes when I see people harp on and on about how boring resource-gathering or completing tedious missions are, but the thing is that this game isn't meant to be the most interesting or engaging game you've ever played. To me, this game is about mindfulness. You choose to log on when you're ready to just kind of let your mind wander with the help of something to keep your hands busy. If you have ADHD, I think you can see what I mean. For example, I personally spend so much of my life thinking and planning and preparing for every step of the day (can you say ANXIETY???) and where I used to spend that time thinking in the background of TikTok videos (that frankly made the process 10x longer and more exhaustive) I now do it alongside the gorgeous art style, fluid + satisfying animation, immersive soundtrack, and cute, reliable characters of Cozy Grove. So, if you're ready to just spend a bit of every day tending to your growing campfire to spread your light to every corner of the island or helping out the newest lost ghost with their daily "repetitive" tasks please get this game! You won't regret it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and very chill game. Become a Spirit Scout and help out the ghosts who all have a story to tell. Has tons of decorations you can buy or learn to make to decorate the whole island. Lots of wardrobe items you can purchase and you can even redo your whole character look. Has a nice n easy fishing system and a more challenging rock skipping mechanic. Super cute touches to the characters; when you do some things like catch a fish, they dance! Even the imps and animals celebrate and dance! I am somewhat addicted to it now :DUpdate: Loving the seasonal events! Halloween was so fun as I was able to get a ton of scary costume hats and wardrobes and am looking forward to the winter / Christmas event and more fun clothing
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This has been a favorite game of mine since I purchased it. In the beginning of the game there is not a lot to do and it can be frustrating having to play each day to advance to a point where the game is finally unlocked (you can fish all variety of fish, you have all your tools, and you have actual content to play for a while). If you can hang in for around 8-10 days and do all story quests to advance your fire/island, the game gets very enjoyable in my opinion. The collection aspect is very fun and I love getting new items to donate. Three quick tips that can make your experience better and I wish I knew:1. The island will rearrange itself.  Anything not in the designated zones could get hard to find and may have the items around it move around and change. 2. In the beginning it's hard to populate your area but that changes very quickly, as will you available areas to place items. Don't be afraid to move stuff around to new spots.3. Try to keep harvestable items (flower pots, berry bushes, trees, etc...) close together. Once you get the store upgraded and can purchase the harmonica, you can harvest everything in an area with it. t's helpful to have things close to get maximum use from it.I recommend for people looking to play a couple hours daily. It's relaxing and there are a lot of items to collect. Decorating is fun and the character options (clothing, hair, etc...) are great if you enjoy being able to look a variety of ways. The bear stories are interesting and I feel there are actual lessons to be learned from the scout master letters, the bears stories, and just in having patience to continue the journey every day.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, enjoyable, and calming. On my PC it autosaves every 10 mins or so, and I can also save it manually in the options, which is amazing for when I get passed a big story mode quest that took a while to complete. I also like that it goes by my timezone, and has a paced gameplay, where you have to wit until the next day to complete new quests!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I like it overall, but I have a couple of specific issues.A. There's tons of furniture but it does not facilitate organization, actual interior/exterior design choice, or functionality in the slightest. Let me explain. There are 4ish main "types" of furniture e.g. rustic, spooky, etc. Then there are several rarities from common to legendary. You want to put this stuff in organized areas so it can benefit stuff. Oh, these bushes like Cozy stuff, etc. Except, this deer hates common stuff, so he needs his own extra-special Bustling area. Oh, that bird hates deer, so he needs his own patch of Rustic area and flowerpots to facilitate his needs. This is bad because it just leads to patchiness in the landscape I design. No organization. Just patches of this and that everywhere. It looks terrible. My island looks awful. B: The characters are just so boring. I'm coming back to this every day, right? I want to see some serious development in these souls and some real revelation. I played Spiritfarer. I want some Spiritfarer-types up in here. These characters just feel uninspired and like they were all written in the same day by the same person. I don't have to care about this. It's just something I want to care about, and don't.So you get certain Animal Crossing vibes by playing it daily and sort of building on the previous day with your relationships, decoration, and chores. I like that. I mean, every quest is pretty much fetch this or find that. Idk if that can really be helped. But you come back to it, like you would with Animal Crossing. But in AC, you can actually design a really cool island, and populate it with the villagers you think are just the coolest. It's an extremely 7/10 game. It's good, but falls short of great.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The developers are wonderful at reviewing player feedback and implementing quick changes and updates! The community is wonderful over on Reddit and Discord. This game is meant to be played for a short time every day. It is NOT a game where you binge play, so please be aware of that. I am the type that loves to binge play games, but this game really helped ground me and I actually love that it limits how much I play a day. I typically spend 2-4 hours on it a day, to be honest, but I know others spend as little as 30 minutes a day. There is no punishment for not playing or not finishing a quest that same day. It's a super cute game that is improving itself continuously with quality of life updates. I highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: All the Cs. Super cute, casual and calming. It similar to Animal Crossing in its daily cycle and a few of the mechanics like fishing, bug catching and item collecting. Like Animal Crossing you can run out of things to do, I'd say I get an average of 1 hour gameplay a day out of it. It was the perfect game to play after work to wind down. I adored the near chaotic nature of the island and the stories that you get from the characters are ridiculous, wholesome and occasionally kick you in the feels. I'd recommend this to anyone who plays games to relax. If you want something to stimulate and challenge you, yeah no this isn't for you. But if you just want to veg out for an hour, enjoy a calming soundtrack and do some favours for dead bear people then I think you'd enjoy this a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so adorable it makes me tear up. Love the art style, the quirky humour and the music.I also enjoy the pacing. With e.g. Graveyard Keeper and Stardew Valley, I felt like I binged and then ran out of things to do.I've only been playing 3.5 hours but I like that game time is linked to real time, and to progress you often have to come back later -- in real time. There is still stuff to grind and collect, but the story only progresses and new items only become available gradually.I also am not much of a base builder, but the decor collections, and harvesting from certain items that like to be near some collections but not near others feels more like a puzzle than base building.It's also a great sign that patches are coming out so quickly (although I hadn't run into any trouble yet at this point).If you like cuteness and casual gaming, then definitely pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic casual game, if a touch sad. Similar to games like Stardew valley but with more focus on crafting and story. Each bear has a story to tell and they get surprisingly melancholy. Still, I'm almost sixty hours in at this point and have no plans on stopping. One nice thing about the game is that there are some limits to how much you can progress the story each day. This makes the game bite-sized - perfect for tired people who want to play games but also sleep.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this spooky cute game. It has all the charm of a cozy farming game paired with the bittersweet knowledge that your character is there to help folks come to terms with their life and afterlife. The character customization and the seasonal events are spectacular. The game also has the helpful feature that gently lets you know that you've completed everything you need to for the day and that its ok to log off. Its quirky, cute, lightly spooky, and makes you fall in love with your neighbears. I love this game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of all the loud, hard-hitting, gore splattery gun fire with demon guts? Tired of taking down waves of slobbering aliens with your bombs and throwing battle axes? Do you just wanna kick back, pop open a cream soda and relax with a cute little story? If you're looking for a zen kind of experience with adorable spirit animals, soft, lilting music and interesting backstories, then I think you'll enjoy Cozy Grove.You play as a Spirit Scout given the task to stay on this wooded island and aid the spirit animals who inhabit the woods. The spirits give you various little jobs here and there, which earn the animals' trust. The more tasks you complete the more the spirit critters they open up to you, as well as open up new areas to explore on the island. It's got everything an eager Spirit Scout needs: cooking, fishing, collecting, planting, buying pet birds to give you company, even a relatively expansive wardrobe!The game is just that: Cute, Warm and Cozy. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I have now collected a few more hours of play and have therefore updated the review a bit.I still think it's a super cosy game, perfect for the daily grind. Nevertheless, I have noticed a few things that I would like to share with you.Pro's:- you have different quests every day- each character is unique and individually designed and has different functions/tasks- the graphics of the game are cuddly and pleasant for the eyes even after playing for a long time (day and night adapt to the real day and night times)- you have many different options (for example, you can raise animals or take care of flowers, trees and plants)Con's:- On some days you only have 3 quests and on others up to 9, it can be stressful / exhausting, as some are also timed, if you don't have the time you lose the quest.- in some quests you have to search for 10 items and that can be quite exhausting with a map that is constantly expanding / as well as other side tasksMaybe there could be a regulator to make sure you don't have too many tasks in a day.
