_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good Animal Crossing knock-off, but much like Animal Crossing, you'll find yourself looking for reasons to continue 2 or so months from now. Do you like Animal Crossing? Were you a gamer in 2020 who wasn't able to get your hands on the newest Animal Crossing because the world went to ♥♥♥♥, and those humanoid cockroaches known as scalpers made getting a Nintendo Switch pain unending? Then, you might like Cozy Grove. From the makers of Alphabear comes a slice of life, hidden object, fetch-quest-a-palooza that's so relaxed, it might get a little boring. You play as a Spirit Scout, trapped on a deserted island... well, deserted in that you're the only living person there. But don't misunderstand: you are not alone; the island is inhabited by dead BEARS!!... And, bears who think they're not bears (for plot reasons). The long of the short of it is: talk to the bears, do fetch quests, solve their problems, and help them move on, as is your duty as a Spirit Scout.There isn't much to do in a day (each play session can last up to an hour). As the island grows, you're running to more and more places while helping an ever-growing cast of socially and emotionally off bears, hearing their stories and working out why they can't or won't move on. Everyone has a story, and being dead jumbles it up; your job is to slowly draw it out, with emphasis on SLOW: I've played for 57 hours, and I'm on day 53 in-game. There's no (apparent) consequence for skipping days (although the longest I've skipped was 4 days). The game's clock runs on the same system clock your computer does, but you're warned not to fiddle with it or you'll corrupt your save data (everything and everyone runs on a set schedule, even if the bears don't ever wander from their little places on the island). It can get tedious fast, so pace yourself. I have yet to completely help any of the bears, but I'm close with some. Guess I'll stick around to see what happens. :P

_childDocuments_.review: Cute bears and items in game, nice bg music.Not a fan of the real-time element implemented. Characters unlocked give out only 1 quest everyday, play time around 30mins and then there's seemingly no more to do.Wished there could be an option to change that in game.Limited resources, limited quests per day. Quests type is rather mundane, they become repetitive after day 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Having put an additional 100 hours into the game, I'm going to go ahead and change my review from Recommended to not recommended.  I was waiting for the summer update to drop and now, having played it, I'm about finished with the game. First things first.  This is what the game is billed as (per the purchase page).  My responses in bold."Cozy Grove is synced to real world time,  and provides 30-60 minutes of new quest content each day . After that, you can fish , craft  and decorate  to your heart's content!Features:• Beautiful, dynamic, hand-drawn landscapes that come alive when you help a spirit in need. • Dozens of memorable characters and spirits for you to find and befriend. Each spirit has a unique, extensive story for you to unravel over time. • Collect spirit animals, craft decorations, go fishing and more! • 40+ hour campaign filled with side quests, designed to span months of playtime. Here's the thing with Cozy Grove.  It is a beautiful game with very interesting (for the most part) characters with very interesting stories that is so insanely tedious that after over 100 hours I'm left wondering why I ever started playing.This is the only game I've ever played that you have to clear 2 grind fests to get to the third and fourth grind fests.They claim you can craft to your hearts content, but they take great care to limit materials and storage.  They also make it so that in order to progress, you need massive amounts of materials for individual quests.  The same materials you use for crafting ....In order to progress you have to grind for money to grind for storage to grind for materials to grind for quests to grind for recipes to grind for crafting.   It's grinding all the way down and it isn't fun.The recent update added .... extra things to grind for!  It also reduced the amount of materials you can get in a sitting and didn't increase storage.  They want you to grind even harder.TLDR: Cozy Grove is a beautiful interesting game that goes out of its way to make you dislike it.

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Have to start of by mentioning the fantastic cozy art style. It's both aesthetic and spooky - the perfect combo!Lots of exploring options and unique characters.Plenty of quests and side quests.I though it was indeed adorable how the developers gave the player the pets feature which i totally exploited. You can also name your pet by clicking the ''name your pet'' button after going up to your pet. Was a bit surprised that they didn't give you the option of giving your pet whatever name you wrote, but instead you have to select from the ones given. Although the variety of names isn't lacking - I mean, I kept scrolling for solid 10 minutes through the list of names and it still kept giving me new name choices. Props to them for putting in the game so many pet names, must have taken them forever. Almost forgot - there's also a fishing feature. At one point (no spoilers) you get a fishing rod and can fish anywhere near the shore. Can't say it's surprising that more and more games these days add this feature, but when it comes to it - in this game in particular, the feature isn't so bad.I also noticed some creepy crawlies and spirits roaming about which gave that spooky vibe. Enjoyed the unique and genius idea of the color expanding with every time you expand your island and meet more of the islands inhabitants.The animation is smooth, art style cozy as the title implies and overall my experience was satisfactory. Would absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: **WARNING: Do NOT progress your game too fast. There is an achievement involving lovesick imps that can be irreversibly made infinitely more difficult to obtain - if not impossible, as I've not been able to make any progress in nearly 2 weeks - due to how the game is coded. Since the devs are working solely on the sequel, you're out of luck if it happens to you. When you get access to lovesick imps, take the time to complete its achievements before proceeding in the game.**That aside, since it's the only bug that is potentially game breaking, this game is a genuine delight to play and has helped me be more sensitive and patient with myself and my problems due to it. It's a very easy recommend from me, especially if you're going through some hard times and just need something you can make a rhythmic part of your day and give you some sense of stability.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Think "Mystical Animal Crossing". Very atmospheric. Upbeat and gentle music. Cute characters with REALISTIC back stories you slowly uncover- like a mystery! I wholeheartedly recommend for a calm, peaceful gaming experience. No rushing around, no "do that thing or DIE" stress.The only thing I would change are tweaking the user interfaces a little bit for a smoother experience. For example, the Inventory screen: you can't click outside of it to close it, you have to click the X button to minimize it. The other example is when you bake/craft things: you can't select multiple recipes to bake/craft at once. You have to craft them all one. at. a. time. and get a chat dialog every time you do. To be honest, that's just me being nit-picky though, other than the above, the controls are intuitive and certainly won't deter you from wanting to play.I'd still say "buy it". If you remotely enjoyed games like Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing or Harvest Moon I promise you'll like this. I look forward to getting on just to listen to the music! So yeah, I'd recommend this game. 10 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and fun to play! I love the aesthetics and the music is very nice. A very comfy game. Also, for a person with adhd who tends to hyperfixate and spend hours at a time on games without taking breaks, I appreciate that the game runs in real time and will stop giving you stuff to do after a while until the next day, forcing you to take a break, get up, and give you time to remember that you might've forgotten to eat while you were so deep in playing. Whoops! I'm really enjoying Cozy Grove so far, and I can't wait to play it again tomorrow! I'm gonna grab a snack now.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great one for anyone who liked the "help your neighbors" and collecting vibes of Animal Crossing, but didn't care/weren't motivated about the interior decorating as much. There's a lot of clothing options and decorating you can do around the island, and likely the longer I play the more interior furniture I'll collect. (I'm 7 days in and have only received 3 interior items and at least 10x that for exterior, for context)Because of how the game is set up to have you play a little each day, there's a finite amount of neighbor quests you can do each day. Although you could theoretically gather almost endlessly, you'd get bored. I can play for 1-2 hours and easily knock out all my quests and a few gathering loops. Some quests are harder than others, and some quests spread over a few days which gives a nice variety to the game.Recommended for kids or adults who enjoy a little bit of whimsy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: the game is good if you are okay with playing the game just 30 minutes - 1 hour every day. Also, the attitude displayed by the devs made me confident in recommending this game to others.I must point out, though, this game has some UI/QoL issues that may frustrate new players. Players familiar with games similar to Cozy Grove might also notice the unfair economy and quests. Expect a harsh first week in this game because most of the content (valuable/rare items, recipes, food) are locked during early game, which lead you to being poor and unable to buy nice things to decorate your grove with. Some quests also felt harder because of this. For these reasons I left Cozy Grove...I was so frustrated that I decided to join the Cozy Grove Discord and write a suggestion. In a matter of weeks a new patch was deployed and most of the crucial problems the community pointed out was solved! In weeks! This attitude is rare to see in the industry nowadays, and is what made me decided to give Cozy Grove a second chance. The game finally felt fair. And fun. What made me stayed afterwards was a new intriguing story line you are rewarded with each time you progress. Progress more story line, and you are rewarded with a new character. Unlock a new character, and you are rewarded with more things to do! I am stuck with this endless loop and I can't stop looking forward to everything the game has to offer, even if it meant just playing 30 minutes - 1 hour every day.I do hope they will add multiplayer (we can visit other people's grove), events, and NPC to NPC interaction, but through the attitude that has been displayed by the devs I can confidently say that they know what they are doing and put my trust to their decisions for the future of Cozy Grove. There's going to be a huge update this summer, if I'm not mistaken? I'm excited for it!

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game. I have put in over 70 hours and have run into for the second time an issue where a char wants an item from a char that I haven't unlocked yet. But, the final straw is that I finally realized that there are like 4 different resources in the game and all the npcs want these resources for their quests. every once in a while one of the npcs will want like several days worth of these resources and i mean saving every last one for several days. What has happened in my game is I now have so many npcs wanting these resources that I cant make any progress toward satisfying the npc that wants several days worth of resources.        I ran a very successful RPG PVP PVE server where we had to script out all the interactions and what not. So I know what it feels like to think you have made it perfect and other people to point out all your mistakes, but I have just run across too many game breaking mistakes and problems to with a good conscience be able to suggest this game to others. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The game is, first and foremost, extremely slow and repetitive to the point of boredom. I really tried to give a chance for it and play it through, but this doesn't get any better towards the endgame.Collectables are time-gated, meaning that as the seasons change, so do your fruits, shells and fishes. If you want to collect everything, you have to put in the hours, every day. If you somehow missed something in that month, or you simply were busy and couldn't put in the effort, congratulations, you can wait a year to acquire it.UI design is not user-friendly. Crafting (furniture and cooking) is tedious as each time you select an item, the window closes, so you have to talk to the NPC again, select the option for crafting, search for the item you want to craft and once again - your window will close and you can start all over.The terrain keeps changing unpredictably, rendering decorating your island pointless - what looks good today might be blocked by a huge chunk of ore tomorrow (oh yes, resources migrate too).Finances are off balance. You need a tremendous amount of money at the beginning to afford items from the shop, backpack and vault upgrades. You literally have to scrape it all together. By the time you have the means to generate a bigger income, you will most likely have acquired what can be bought with money and thus renders it useless.Backpack and vault are extremely tiny at the beginning, and since you have no idea what resources are important so you are frantically leaving piles of random items around, cluttering your island.Events and special features are not explained properly so you are left wondering what a certain item does or weather it'll be useful to you or not. New features are not tested properly and often bug up ie. in the spring, little ducks followed you around and often block you from casting your fishing rod or photo quests bug out even if you meet the requirements.All in all, the game wants to be a sweet, slow paced relaxation but ends up being a tedious, repetitive chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Update (38.6 Hours Played):This is still a lovely game, but it didn't have the longevity for me that I had hoped for.  I stopped playing this regularly after a few weeks because the story progression slowed down to a crawl.  There's usually only a couple hours worth of things to do each day and there are many fetch quests to fill out the time.  This is great if you just want something to play a little aimlessly.  I don't mind that.  But I lost interest and it was hard to keep coming back when it would take progressively longer to open up more areas of the island.  It takes more and more logs to expand the range of the fire each time which is a fine mechanic, but there are too many filler quests, some of which don't reward you with logs.  There's also a log that becomes available for purchase most days in the store which lowers the value of the item for me.  It's not as satisfying to buy it as it is to be rewarded for helping someone.  I haven't quite broken the economy yet, but it's kind of becoming a money/item collection game without much else.  The preference requirements for furniture/item placement ruins the decorating aspect for me because my brain doesn't like keeping track of who likes what and I don't enjoy it.  The farming for fruit and flowers isn't all that interesting and it feels more like work.  Talking to the bears is only for quests and maybe a follow up comment.Original Review (4.8 Hours Played): This game is so appropriately titled as "Cozy."  Super chill and charming.  It's a relaxed way to spend a couple hours a day collecting things.  I really enjoy games with an inventory and crafting system.  Bonus for having a collection to fill out.  The sound design is pleasing and the numerous achievements are satisfying to collect. If you're looking for something to play for hours, this probably won't scratch that itch.  Like the description says on the store page, it doesn't have enough to do for more than an hour or two a day unless you want to do laps of the island and grind for items. I only have a couple critiques:1. Due to the washed out nature of the landscape when it's not lit, I find it difficult to find items, especially if they're needed for quests.  The visual design is lovely, but a bit cluttered.  But it's easy to talk to one of the bears to get a clue to finding things which is a nice feature.  I shamelessly use it frequently because I want to enjoy my time in Cozy grove, not search aimlessly for something my eyes don't register.2. It took a while to figure out how to throw things and use the fishing pole.  The mechanic isn't bad, just took some getting used to.  But there was no tutorial and I couldn't find control instructions to tell me how to do it.  I don't need a game to hold my hand, but I got a little frustrated while playing trial and error to figure it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure that other reviews will comment on how relaxing this casual game is however,  :I had the same worries.  I couldn't get into Animal Crossing because I didn't like the consistent IRL time pressure.  However, while Cozy Grove does have the IRL passage of time, if I understand correctly, the game only progresses 1 day for each day that you actually go into the save file.  (For example, if I start Day 1 on December 1st, and I don't play again until December 3rd, then I would be on Day 2 of the game, not Day 3.)  THIS IS A HUGE GAMECHANGER!  Now I don't feel compelled to constantly be on the game if I don't have the time.  It's not a huge commitment, and that flexibility makes me  to actually play.Is the game time-gated?  Yes.  There is only so much you can do each day; the first day has an hour, more or less, of gameplay, though!  But honestly, each day is like a good cup of tea that makes the gameplay...well...cozy.

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove: The game that should have been a graphic novel.(Or what happens when creatives who don't know how to code try to design a game.)This game has been praised for its writing and art. If that were all it was, it would be fantastic, however (and it must be put down to the developers' inexperience and not malice), playing this game feels like being in an abusive relationship: The breadcrumbing, gaslighting, stinginess, and broken promises ultimately add up to a frustrating, disappointing, heartbreaking waste of time.The game design was flawed from its very inception. It should have been obvious to anyone working on Cozy Grove at any stage that the math did not work and the balancing would be horribly wrong. These problems are now so entrenched that there is no way for the programmers to fix them. Sadly, the player won't find this out until having sunk far too many hours into the game.Although it has been billed as a relaxing, slow-paced game that won't eat up your time, nothing can be further from the truth. A player could spend real-time years in Cozy Grove and never make progress on collections and achievements, due to the aforementioned balancing and RNG problems.Cozy Grove ultimately feels like a game in early access, full of bugs and bad choices, however, given that it has been out for over a year and there was no change in course during the most recent update and DLC, one must conclude that there won't be.I wanted to love Cozy Grove and, for a time, I thought I did, but it is a game that will never live up to its great potential. My hope is that this review will save you, dear reader, from experiencing what I suffered. What a waste and what a shame.Update: SpryFox has announced a sequel to Cozy Grove. This is confirmation that Cozy Grove will not be fixed. But get this: The developers think the thing that is wrong with Cozy Grove is that the territory isn't big enough and there aren't puppies, not the dysfunctional interface and RNG system. Skip this game and skip that one, too.

_childDocuments_.review: The only way I can describe this game as is "Disappointing"I don't dislike it, but the game makes you do the same exact thing every day.Turn it on, walk  to bears, receive fetch quest, get item, make area full of colour.I bought this cause I was expecting a cute animal crossing esque game I can play from day to day but while Animal Crossing New Horizons didn't respect my time for the first week in terms of progression, you still had stuff to do when you finished your main thing, cozy grove comes to an unsettling stop once you finish all your quests for the day.There's not much variety in dropped items, quests, or what you can even make/buy until I suppose end game, but to get to end game is going to take days/weeks because once you did what you had to do, the game literally tells you there's nothing left to do.You can fish, you can give imps things. That's it.And that's why it's disappointing because the artstyle is adorable, it's right up my alley, but there's genuinely nothing to do, once you've played it for 3 days, that's pretty much everything.You don't have an actual house, you don't get to purchase many things and they all fall into about 6 categories, you can't go into the bears houses (when they actually have some) and there's not variety in bears, everyone will always have the same bears.I know some of this is a bit much to ask for from a small indie studio for the price they're asking, but the price they're asking for feels more for all the beautiful art, and less for a fun game.If this game got an indoors update, or even some cheap expansion/DLC I'd love to give this another try but otherwise all I got was a cute game that tries to be animal crossing without any sort of the longevity that makes me love animal crossing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable and there are a lot of things to love about it. That being said, it needs a lot of improvement. If you have endless patience and don't mind waiting a great deal of real world time to achieve small little slivers of progress then this is the game for you. Unlike some of the reviewers I understood that, like animal crossing, this game was the type I would play for 30 mins a day while drinking my coffee. Inventory space is limited and upgrade purchases only satiate your space needs for a short period of time. Need to cook something to satisfy an imp? Spend 10 minutes juggling inventory in order to gather the supplies to cook the item. Then wait an hour to receive said item. Come back in an hour and use the item on the imp. It gives you an essence that you don't have room in your pockets or inventory for. Repeat this each day. Need a rare fish? Fishing takes a long time because they often 'poke' at your line four times before biting. You'll be running back and forth catching and selling fish for 20+ minutes. Need to feed a brokenhearted imp a bon bon? Wait two days for all the ingredients. Cook 20 bon bon's and wait an hour. Get bon bons and toss them at the imps to bring them together so they "meet" and reward you with an essence. Spend all 20 bon bons to bring them together. They never never "meet" - they are just standing next to each other, a mere 1/2 inch apart....crying. Sorry, but this games cuteness doesn't excuse it's frustrations. I'm bummed that I played too long for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, if you like games like Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley you will enjoy this game!*May contain spoilers*The game is cute, cozy, relaxing and incredibly wholesome. Each day is unique with various task to complete accompanied by character stories for each bear. Foraging opportunities bring you items that you can use, sell, or donate to your collection for rewards. Initially I was frustrated when I realised that the game was limited on what you can achieve in one day. I quickly came to enjoy this feature as it made me slow down to truly appreciate the games qualities and focus on other aspects like island customisation and collection completion. I've found that despite this limitation my daily gameplay time has increase as I've unlocked more, and I can easily spend 1-3 hours on the game. If completing tasks for bears is the only aspect of the game you focus on, you will get incredibly bored as these are mostly find object tasks. Have patience while the island unlocks and the stories to develop, it's worth it. After completing your daily tasks, you can focus on designing your island with various colour customisable decor. Find, buy, or craft the items. Decor items have various tags that you can group together to create themes which could be beneficial for your animals and plants.------2024 UpdateDevastated that Cozy Grove: Camp Spirit is a Netflix exclusive. _childDocuments_.review: Summary: There are a few minor bugs, but overall  is a fun game that's perfect for lovers of games like .I was looking for a laid-back, relaxing game, and this did not disappoint. I found the art style cute, and I loved the subtle differences in character design between ghosts and their memories. The characters are engaging and it's easy to get invested in helping the spirits find peace. Even the letters your scout leader sends are so entertaining to read.When I get into a new game, it can be easy to spend hours upon hours playing. Since  has a limited amount of plot-progressing tasks each day, it's easy to hop on and play for a bit without getting sucked in for several hours on a work night. It's a nice way to unwind without accidentally spending my whole evening gaming.There are some bugs in the game. When feeding spirit animals, the animation can sometimes take a while to kick in, so you're stuck standing there until the animation starts. Similarly, when you learn a new recipe, you can get stuck in place while the recipe is displayed even if you try to click out/exit the recipe. I use a controller to play, and there were times when the select option in menus/my inventory would disappear. I'd have to exit out of the menu/inventory and reenter to select the option/item I wanted. I also notice that when fishing or bug hunting, there were moments where the net/fishing pole would get stuck, and I'd have to release the button and re-press it to get it to work. If two items were close together, it could be hard to select the right one. For example, if I stood right in front of my fire and pressed A, my character would walk a few feet over, and the menu for a nearby spirit animal would open, as if I'd selected it instead. I don't know if these issues are specific to the controller or also happen when using a keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: Whyyyyy all the time-gating. I really REALLY wanted to recommend this game and even went into it telling myself to be patient, but... I can't recommend it. It's really adorable, the art and the characters are lovely, but I it feels like a chore to have to log in daily to get anything done. This isn't a F2P mobile game, it's a PC game and the time-gating makes no sense. I was even okay with waiting a day to unlock quests, but cooking? Do the developers seriously expect me to play, wait an hour and then turn the game back on? I don't have that kind of time in my life. Sorry. If the time-gating gets reduced a bit (the cooking in particular is ridiculous), I may try it again, but as it is, I can't recommend it, although the concept and gameplay otherwise are really adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I saddens me to say I don't recommend this game. I really want to like it; the art style is super cute and the music is amazing. However, the gameplay itself is super repetitive and downright frustrating.As a Spirit Guide, you help ghosts move on by exploring their stories. Every day you walk up to the ghosts and they'll give you a task. 90% of the time this is to fetch something for them, sometimes multiple items (say for example letters) but only 1 spawns at a time so you're just wandering around and around and around waiting to see if there's a new letter to be found at the same spot as the last one. After you're done the ghost will give you a reward.Sadly, often it will be a decorative item instead of Spirit Wood (which you need to collect to unlock new ghosts) and what's worse is that often the task won't even progress their stories; which already goes very slow. When this is over there's simply nothing to do anymore so you're looking at 30 minutes a day of incredibly repetitive gameplay, without any reward, per day at the max. You can fish and catch bugs like in Animal Crossing but there's no way to tell if there's more species to collect at this time of year or if you've had them all so you're just getting the same ones every day.Money is hard to come by; items you need to craft for some tasks don't always have a set source so you're grinding to feed your birds every day but they won't give you the 1 egg you need to bake something for a ghost who asked you to do so half a week ago. It's just infuriating.I love a farm/life sim like no-other and I usually quite enjoy doing the same things every day but without reward it gets so annoying.You won't spend much time decorating either. Many items have tags that influence the things around you (for example those birds!) so you find yourself placing down random items in the middle of nowhere just to increase the chance of getting that single egg and then still not getting it day after day after day.Since these are such fundamental parts of the game I also don't see a point in being like "I'd recommend it if they'd change x". So sadly, this game gets a massive SKIP from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be completely relaxing. The dialogue is very cute and funny and the graphics are very beautiful. I find myself thinking about this game a lot and wondering about the expansive stories of each of the spirits. A lot of folks are saying that it gets very repetitive after a while, but it feels very much like Animal Crossing in that way and I don't mind it at all. The Cozy Grove 'lore,' if you will, is very interesting to me and I find myself really wanting to open up new areas and find new spirits to talk to. At this time I think have like 12 spirits to go, and I'm not sure how much more of the game there is from there, but I'm hoping there will still be stuff to do after a few more days of playing this, hopefully :')It's a really cute game, I'd recommend it to folks wanting a nice, cozy and wholesome little game with bears and cute characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I play once a day in the morning and have been enjoying it. It's a nice casual game, similar to Animal Crossing. I enjoy the stories you unlock from each of the NPCs. I love that you don't have to keep your crafting supplies on you, as long as they are in your storage. Would recommend to anyone that enjoys games like Animal Crossing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I'm gonna be fair, this game is being updated and supported to add new content and QOL updates to the point where it's worth a purchase to support devs who care about their games and actually update them. If you're into New Horizons and want some more, similar gameplay with some limitations, check out a video review and decide for yourself. It's not a bad game but it's nothing crazy. Just something fun to do to pass the time, or decorate if you're into that kind of thing.Review (about 10 hours in): The game is fun so far. Similar to Animal Crossing but a little more like pocket camp than new horizons. You do quests for spirits that are on your island in return for new items and features. You're limited to how much you can interact with them per day, progressing your friendship (hearts) with them like in pocket camp. There are no micro-transactions though and this is why the game is paid. If it were like pocket camp in that sense, I wouldn't have purchased it. Once you've completed your quests, you can fish, harvest and collect items. This is rather boring for the most part but does give you something to do, especially since these items can be used to craft items and decorate the island, or sell for some coins. There are badges as well which help give you something else to do, and they give you coins as a reward. Quite a bit actually (at least it seems that way so far). Overall this game is pretty fun and addicting, but after an hour or so you'll find yourself bored with not much to do since it's like animal crossing and you're limited to how much you can do per day. I'd give it a 7/10, but with updates and added content/features I could easily see that being upped to an 8.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great alternative for ACNH fans who are looking for something new, but similar. The characters are lovable and have nice storylines with good pacing as well as difficulty for the progression level, the quests are simple and aren't particularly time-consuming, and the atmosphere is extremely relaxing. 13/10 would recommend to anyone looking for a cozy game and vibe. Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: To me this game is just fine, but I wouldn't recommend it to someone. I'll probably try it for a few more days since I paid for it but generally I find there's more things I dislike about it than things I like.The vibe is nice, I really do like the idea of it and I rather enjoy the aspect of coming back to it each day. That's what the premise of the game is and so I don't think negative reviews critiquing it for that are quite fair. However, as a game, there are several features that are real misses for me. I really like the idea of the world being colourless and then becoming more colourful as you help the ghosts, but the way it is you help a ghost and a big area around them gets coloured, but then it's colourless again the next day. To me it really removes what could have been a really cool way to get a sense of progression by adding colour bit by bit. This just feels like each day, you do your chores, and everything is all messy again the next day as if nothing happened. You can extend the range of colour with lamps and stuff, but I just don't find that satisfying at all.Another thing that I really dislike is that the furniture has all these different tags or modifiers and that certain plants and animals prefer to be near certain tags and dislike others. I found this overwhelming, the tags aren't coloured or visualised (not even bullet points! just a list!) and it seems absolutely tedious to have to constantly go click on all your furniture to try and puzzle this out. It also feels like it would force you into decorating a certain way and prevent creative freedom to some extent. Together with the colour thing, these totally remove any joy I would have in decorating my island. Maybe the interactions with the bear ghosts will eventually pay off, but it currently feels like I don't care all that much about their superficial ramblings and Where's Waldo-style fetch quests.Also, while the art is quite lovely, it's so busy looking I find it so hard to tell what is important and what is just backdrop. It makes the repeated fetch quests even more of a chore to me. I wouldn't say it's all that similar to animal crossing (it only wants to be), and I bought it thinking it was, but considering that it even mentions animal crossing in the description, I feel a bit annoyed and misled by that. I really want to like it, I've come back a few days excited to try again but it just isn't doing it for me like the other games it's trying to emulate.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I won’t be original if I say that this game takes the best, easiest, and most comfortable sides of Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing, but that’s the way it is.And a hook with a couple of hours of play per day removes that feeling when you can’t tear yourself away from the game, although it’s time to.PS also, the story turned out to be very sentimental and deep.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I'm really enjoying getting to know the characters and the island, and I can spend hours harvesting and fishing after the 30-60 minutes of active gameplay. There's much more to the game than just completing quests, you can craft, sell items or donate them to the museum, buy clothes or camp decorations, and feed your animals/imps. I'm actually kind of grateful that the game doesn't allow me to spend all day running around on the island because I can't burn myself out. It's a chance to slow down and really enjoy the small victories in-game, and I know it will be there for me tomorrow. Also, the little gems of dark and dirty humor that are sprinkled here and there are *chef kiss*.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game, and for the first few days I definitely did. But the game very quickly turns into a grind typical of F2P mobile games looking to try and get you to pay money for shortcuts. All of the tiered items are an absolute slog to obtain, especially if they are items where you need to wait for a respawn, and the cost of upgrading the things necessary to craft some of the requested items is absurd. (200,000 for the shop upgrade to be able to buy cocoa beans for a cake my bird has been asking me for since day 4 is absurd, especially when the only reliable way to make money is to recycle your quartz..which locks you out of other items that you may want.) The "achievement"/badge system helps only so much, especially when the monetary awards are usually quite small.The game encourages you to take it in small chunks, but it only takes a few in-game days for that mechanic to betray itself if you want to feel like you're making any meaningful progress. I love the characters, I love the aesthetic, but I can't see myself recommending this to anyone. I was very excited for this game. Very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a fun, quirky game. Gorgeous art style, fun gameplay, relaxing pace, charming NPCs. I find myself reading every item description because it can be creepy and hilarious all at once. It's apparent to me that this is a labour of love. I look forward to playing it every day because I enjoy making happy discoveries and new spirit and pet friends. To see my island come alive with colour is a very satisfying thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Animal Crossing (more so the older versions) and Stardew Valley you'll probably like this game. It's very similar to Animal Crossing but a few things stand out to me. Firstly, when you craft things or need to give someone an item for a quest, you luckily don't need to have the items in your backpack in order to craft something/complete an item quest. It pulls from your storage as well as your backpack. Another plus is that bugs and fish don't get scared and despawn if you accidentally run past them. Fishing is also incredibly easy in this game. With most fish you only need to get the bobber close to them, even if the bobber isn't right in front of them sometimes they'll completely turn around and start biting. Some fish are a little harder to catch and in most cases you can tell by their shadow shape the level of difficulty. A couple things I dislike though are that 1) a lot of the bugs do not have a unique design, only a different color of the same design. Like 3 different bugs can have the exact same design but come in red, green, and blue and are considered different species. It can be sort of difficult to remember what you've caught already because of this, especially in sections of the map that aren't lit up and are therefore in black & white, since it will not look like a different bug. 2) there's not really an encyclopedia of bugs and fish you've caught. Your inventory does tell you when you have something that hasn't been donated to The Collection yet, and the Captain keeps track of what you've donated as well, but The Collection is sorted by the order you donated the items and not organized by the season or type of critter. There are subcategories of things like shells, fish, bugs, food, etc. so it's not entirely random, however I think it could be better set up to keep things more organized. A plus side that differs from the AC museum collection is the donation system gives you rewards like coins and gems, and sometimes other more rare items like recipes or metals, so you actually get things in return when you donate.Something else I love is that your fishing rod and bug net NEVER BREAK! Your other tools will eventually break, BUT the durability lasts much longer than ACNH tools, and when they do break, you get crafting resources from them. Tools also don't need to be entirely remade, you simply take them to the crafting bear and repair them.The bears are reeeeally cute and all have super unique and interesting back stories, personalities, and character designs. I wish there were more pet types. I believe there are only birds and deer (I haven't even unlocked deer yet) and I think it would be fun to have maybe squirrels or mice or something added. You will run out of things to do in this game after probably less than 2 hours per day. It's similar to old Animal Crossing titles in that way, you're meant to complete a few quests, do some shopping, explore for resources and be done. You can keep fishing and catching bugs for hours if you'd like, but any substantial gameplay will be completed in about an hour. I think I'm only on day 11ish of playtime so it may slow down even more the further into the story you get.The music is really nice, I just wish there was more of it.Overall, there are a lot of things I like, and nothing I truly dislike, only aspects I personally think could be designed a little better. It is really relaxing and definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you've been looking for a fun, relaxing life-sim style game, then Cozy Grove is the game for you. I splurged, as I do almost every year, during Steam's Winter Sale, grabbing a few odd, yet fun games to try. This year, Cozy Grove was one of them. After sitting on my wish list since the game released in April of 2021, I decided it was time to give it a try. There are many things I love about this game, but the things that keep me coming back are the ease of play, the characters and branching storyline, and the beautifully done artwork. Much like Animal Crossings, it's set in real time and ideal for roughly 1-2 hours of play per day. In this way, the game is peaceful. You aren't caught up for hours, or even days, in a never-ending quest than leads from one thing to the next until you're completely burnt out. Most quests last roughly 15 to 45 minutes, allowing for instant gratification, while others need to brew a bit and are active over a few days. You're rewarded for exploring the island to find new treasures and adventures in many ways, from merit style badges to Captain Billweather Snout's Book of Secrets. I personally love to loot everything when gaming, so this collection style gameplay appeals highly to me. Add in camping, crafting, and upgrading and you've hooked me for life. Plus, Cozy Grove's menagerie of creatures on the island are all friendly, so I don't have to fight anything or anyone to get what I want. This simplicity helps me relax at the end of a long day. Whereas if I'm playing Borderlands, I'm certainly looting everything, but I'm also fighting my way through scores of characters and challenges to get there. It's still super fun, but it puts me in a much more active mindset. It's a different playstyle, is all, and it depends on my mood as to which of the two I'd choose to play at any given time.Cozy Grove's characters are lovable, whether they be a spirit bear, animal, or imp, and its story is unique. All of the spirits you can befriend on the island are found one by one, each with their own storyline, setting up a campaign that could easily give you weeks of game time. Your focus as a Spirit Scout is helping said spirits remember their lives by fulfilling quests that will eventually allow them to find peace. You're basically an adorable ghost psychiatrist who helps them relive their sometimes not so great memories, in turn giving you a history lesson about the island and why it's so haunted. On top of the seventeen spirit bears you befriend, you'll also meet merchant and seasonal bears who bring interesting and sometimes necessary wares to the island. This is also very similar to Animal Crossings' set-up. Again, both games sync to real-time. So, each bear has their specialty, their specific days and times to be on the island, and for some, the festivals that come with them. You'll also notices several imps as you wander the island, which are odd little critters that tend to disappear as quickly as you spotted them. Although small, they are important to the island as a whole, from being a part of quests to feeding them and mending their broken imp hearts. Plus, during the winter festival, snow ball fights with the imps are plentiful, much like my real life in the Northwest. Some reality built into video games is healthy. Just a pinch of a reminder, you know?The pets of Cozy Grove could be a whole other post. Think Pokémon, kind of. Or maybe there's more of a Neopets vibe going on since they respond to décor and evolve or mature due to being fed. Either way, it's a fun addition to the Cozy Grove universe, and I want to collect them all. I also want them to all be friends, but I guess that's not happening thanks to the cats. Typical. As an artist myself, I must say the art and design throughout the game is absolutely wonderful. The beautifully drawn, dynamic landscape literally comes to life before your eyes as you complete pieces of the storyline. Even when colors are muted before lighting up certain areas, the game's style is simply exquisite. Each character has their own unique look to match their personality and quests, making them all very unique individuals. I found myself excited to unearth each new spirit bear, since I never knew what the designers had in store for me. You can also decorate the island and your tent, as well as change your clothing to mold the universe as you see fit. Cozy Grove's crafting feature opens up a whole slew of options in that respect, thanks to maker-bear extraordinaire, Jeremy Gruffle. Crafting and Cooking recipes can be found around the island, the developers once again showing off their well-known influences.All told, it's one of those games you just have to play to see what I mean. It's simple, it's fun, and it's a great way to spend a couple of hours of your day away from all of the overwhelming things life sometimes presents. It's even better than Animal Crossings in my opinion, mostly because the inhabitants of my thriving little island tend of guilt trip me each time I'm away for too long. If you're anything like me, who tends to get distracted easily, you know what I mean. I don't need too much reality in my video games, okay? I'm sorry I was away for exactly 294 days and that you want to move to another island now. Life happens. My spirit bear friends don't judge me!Anyway… If I haven't convinced you to give Cozy Grove a try by now, this game is probably not the one for you. But, if you're at least intrigued by the notion, it's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and, yes, cozy game that wants to be your newest long term commitment. You get a short list of things to do each day, and more and more unlocks as you play, expecting that you will still be coming backs months after starting. Which isn't really a bad thing, just something to be aware of. You can't really binge this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute and relaxing! It does deal with a little bit of real time mechanics, so that is something to be aware of, but I kinda like that feature to a degree. It helps to stretch the game out, but does limit play time per day. You can still forage and fish, but I do wish that a little more story material was available per day. Overall, so far it is awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game! Normally I tend to munch through games, so it's a nice change of pace to savour it over a long period. There's also more to do the longer you've played so I wouldn't worry about the quest limit. I'm about two weeks in and the artwork, the music, characters, gameplay - it's just so charming and soulful. I think the critiques I read in the reviews before purchasing were too harsh. I have thoroughly enjoyed it for the time I've played - I don't mind hunting for the items, and I'm still interested in the story lines. I love the attention to detail, and it feels polished and well rounded and I haven't encountered any bugs.I highly recommend it, and if you aren't convinced - you can pet/hug all the animals! I would really like it if they added more to the soundtrack, as much as I like the tracks, it can get a little bit repetitive as it's a long game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game for people who like casual but immersive worlds. Lots of adorable character customization options that are actually fun to discover, and always plenty to do. The updates are always packed with new items and things to do (rock skipping! bug catching!) which is such a nice surprise. And the stories are funny and easy to follow.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly dull. Maybe okay for children but I cannot recommend this game for adults.What this game offers as the main feature are side activities in other games.The good:- the graphics are cute- the music is relaxing (the American pathfinder vibe was hit pretty well)The bad:- I'm not sure if I even want to call this a game because it lacks any complexity to make it interesting. You simply run around the (eventually expanding) island and try to spot randomly spawned nodes to harvest resources (to sell, to craft, to add to a collection). With a shovel, with a fisherman's rod, sometimes simply something to click on (like bushes and leaf piles), etc.- base building is not interesting at all. There is hardly an incentive to do it. It just felt pointless and tedious to me (collect random items from harvest nodes, buy recipes, craft with random items, place object near your campfire).- there is literally nothing else to this game- oh and you can only do a few quests every day which effectively limits progression to mask the lack of content (quests expand the island, unlock new recipes and new havest nodes to click on)I bought this on a sale and still feel like I paid too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I love it. I just got the game and it is already one of my new favorites. It is like Animal Crossing and Don't Starve had a beautiful baby, both of which are also favorites of mine. It is without question easy for me to recommend, especially for the price. You will still have to pay $60 for Animal Crossing on Switch. (I did so gladly, but that is 4x the price.)However, you know you. Can you stand to pick up and put down a game for a little bit every day? I can and have (and have also just put hours in grinding resources, events, and multiple saves when I haven't...) and will with this. I feel it is rather disingenuous to call it the F2P problem when it does not sell you time savers for real money, but I digress.All in all, it is fun. Just not in a hurry up and complete the plot in a night sort of way.

Logging on every day to see all the colors gone again is very unsatisfying to say the least, but again that's just my opinion. If you like these kinds of games, you'll definitely like Cozy Grove.

_childDocuments_.review: This game quickly got added to my daily routine, playing it for a couple of hours every morning before moving onto something else. _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A bit of a slow start, but really grows on you quickly! It's nice to have a game with limits to how much you can play in a day in my library. It's so cute and loving the "spooky" aesthetic. I also love games with lots of resource gathering and crafting so this is really hitting a lot of what I like in a game altogether! _childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, prefacing this review with I'm only a few hours in and I received it for free, yada yada yada. Do you need a cute game that you can't endlessly grind? Do you need a game that's got cute as heck bears that somehow will also make you cry when you unveil their memories? Do you want a game with an amazing soundtrack and art style? If your answer is yes to any of those questions, Cozy Grove is for you. Here's the thing - I'm 2 weeks into this game and you have to play it IN REAL TIME. Every day I go back and do my "dailies," and get my bear quests, pick my flowers, feed my birds, and try to make my adorable little bears happier. It's roughly an hour or two a day so you can't just grind and grind and grind to get through the story. I've done a little over 50 story quests in my short playtime to give an idea of what you're looking at time-wise. Now that being said, there's a lot to do in CG. You can simply search for resources, do daily quests to quite literally light up your bear's homes, craft/bake, pluck flowers, hunt for seashells, fish, and they just added a big update that brought in skipping stones, catching bugs, and hugging the bears. Spoiler alert: you're going to want to hug the bears. If you're comfy coming back days on end to help your grove and progress your story, this is the game for you. Patience is key with Cozy Grove. Your logins will essentially turn into dailies and there's quite a bit of repetitiveness. On the flip side though - they've already started adding more content and they seem very open to feedback in their Discord! I'd wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who likes a simple, relaxing game with a good story - you just have to be patient. P.S. If you cry easily, this may not be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely in love with this game. However, this game made me realize that I do enjoy binging games. I wish I could do more in a day than just 1-2 hours. Everyday I am looking forward to continuing the story line and seeing what I can do that day.I definitely recommend this game for all the cozy game lovers out there.

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is quickly becoming my favorite game.  It's so chill, and though it has the supernatural element of spirits/ghosts in it, is great for anxiety management.  It's not a scary supernatural game, but rather one where you want to (and can) hug the NPCs.Pros:-Excellent soundtrack; the music creates a cozy, calm atmosphere-Great visuals; the style is perfect for the game, and the NPCs are adorable-Relaxing and fairly easy to use; I rarely got frustrated over using any tool and repairing them is easy-Character customization is available (though not too extensive for hair), and there's a ton of optional clothing you can collect and wear-There are still things to do after finishing the daily quests, as bugs and fish still spawn-If you're having trouble finding an object for a quest, you can ask for a "hint" (it'll actually point to exactly where it is) for only 100 coins-Upgrading your storage (aka, upgrading the tent) is quick and fairly cheap to do for the first few times, which is a relief since you'll very quickly find yourself short of inventory space-You can place any decoration item anywhere on the island and inside your tent (after upgrading)-You can get spirit animals (11 days in, and I have thus far only been able to get birds and cats) who are adorable (and provide resources if you keep them happy and can feed them what they request)-Crafting is simple and easy to do, and you can find recipes all over the place to make new things-There are two types of currency:  coins and gems.  As you'll amass a vast amount of quartz gems, this is a great thing in order to balance out your purchases so you can afford other thingsCons:-You can't upgrade your backpack for a while (not to mention it's costly and doesn't give you many more spaces), so you might have to constantly run back to camp to put things in storage or to Kit to sell things in order to clear up space-There is a limit to the amount of shells which spawn per day, so you can't just keep grabbing them when you're done with quests (I believe it's somewhere around 20)-Mining ores is frustratingly long.  While other resources are plentiful, ores take a long time to be able to mine again and don't give you as much materials (which can impede quests and make them take longer; I've had one quest for about two days now for the golden shovel upgrade)-Fish aren't worth selling to Kit unless you catch a rare fish.  If you haven't already donated it, best thing to do is burn them for fishbones since that's a common crafting material-Skipping stones are frustrating; oftentimes the stones will land on the sand just one or two pixels away from the clam and not count, but when I adjust to throw the stone just a tiny bit harder it'll lose at least two skips (giving me a rather lackluster reward)-Since many resources don't respawn over the course of the day (ore rocks, bramble bushes, and the limit on shells) there is little to do after you finish questing aside from fishing, catching bugs, and jumping in leaf piles-The cooking mechanic, while interesting, often needs a ton of a certain resources-To harvest materials from a spirit animal, you need to feed it the item it is requesting in its thought bubble.  Already, there have been days where I couldn't do this due to a lack of resources which made it impossible to craft the cooking item-Decor items have themes to them; trees, plants, and spirit animals have likes and dislikes when it comes to these themes (and sometimes to other animals), and it can be a bit confusing to manage it all.  While this isn't a bad concept, and this part might be more of a "neutral" than a "con", it can just be a bit confusingOverall, I would absolutely recommend this game.  I hear a sequel/second game is in the works and am super excited for that even though I still have tons of things left to do in this game.  That's how good it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It's just a grind, and it's not a fun one.It feels like a animal crossing wanna be.The characters, the residents of this town, the people i should care about made me feel nothing. Not happy to see them, not intrigued by how they died, nothing, they just feel like quest npc's.The game part of the game is just kinda tediousCollecting resources feels awful. Fishing was somehow made not fun.Decorating like you want is barely an option, because of the deco sets it just doesn't feel rewarding if you aren't getting anything out of them.i'll keep playing to see if perhaps updates or times change my opinion, but right now I wouldn't recommend this game.Go play stardew valley.Edit:After playing for 17 days doing missions and whatever i've come to the conclussion that yes, there's really no point in continuing.I really tried to like this game but i just could not.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a wonderful taste of what Animal Crossing could have been if it had been developed by folks with any sense of fun. I hate Animal Crossing due to all the tedium; thankfully, Cozy Grove fixes a lot of what went wrong in ACNH.***Updated 7/15/2021: The game, overall, is a win. I have sunk many many hours into this game, so it is worth the basic price tag.I am still keeping an eye on Spryfox for MTX. Some of the mechanics in the game (such as waiting an entire day for stuff to be delivered) still reek of a premium currency that is on the way.I can recommend in the current state, however there are some things that need major work before I can say YES BUY NOW.1. Fishing: I hate to say it, because I can tell the developers want fishing to be a fun minigame, however, they pretty much took every crappy element of fishing that I hate about every other game and slammed it into one!Do you hate having to control cast? This game has it!Do you hate it when fish flee if you land the bobber too close? This game has it!Do you hate it when you land the perfect cast, only to have it ruined by lower-tiered fish? This game has it!Fishing is the least fun thing in this game, and there's a LOT of fishing :(2. Microtransactions: Spry Fox has a history of developing mobile games. They better not be using microtransactions in the future of this game, or I instantly take back any positive words in this review.3. Dayslong mission items: I hate this. It's not fun. Get rid of missions which 'may take a few days'.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet, calming game set on a charming island filled with ghosts that you have to help. Patience is fundamental to progressing the story; you can only collect so many resources in one day, and with the game progressing in real-time you may need to come back a few days in a row in order to complete quests. It's not a game designed to be binged, and that's what I love about it. Login for an hour, then get off and go on with your day. Highly recommend for those who like games like Animal Crossing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: CONFUSING GROVE! - This game is a mess. A cute, colourful mess with great music, that bombards you with tasks that somehow don't feel like they are linked to any progression. Calling it an isometric Spiritfarer is a reasonable general comparison but it lacks Spiritfarer's overall sense of getting things done. It also has a mechanic that sort of resets your progress every day which is a bewildering design choice. If the developers were trying to create a game that felt like putting on warm slippers in front of a gently crackling fire it hasn't worked. These would be slippers made of bees in front of an angry fire that won't stop asking for logs.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The game is similar to Animal Crossing, sure. But I think the unique story elements, animal husbandry, and art are worth purchasing this game. It's very soothing and relaxing and you can really make the world your own. Just about everything is customizable and I really enjoy playing it! AND THE SOUNDTRACK - I wish it were on Spotify because I could fall asleep to it every night as it is sooooo soothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The game has an interesting story line. I like that there is only so much that you can do in the game each day so that you don't finish the game quickly. That can also be a bit annoying sometimes because you want to know what happens next in the story. This game does require patience when acquiring resources to make things, which can sometimes slow game progress. Overall, I think it's a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very cozy and the atmosphere is great. I also like the time-gating mechanic that rewards patience and playing a little every day. However, the inventory management is needlessly cumbersome, the majority of the game's quests are boring/frustrating fetch quests (find X objects hidden in this area), I didn't find the characters that interesting, and I didn't really want to play the decoration minigame for optimizing my island, as there was a lot of debris all around the island. Overall, I think I've enjoyed cozy games with more... game to them (Stardew Valley, Spiritfarer)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is only meant to be played for at most like 2 hours a day. Its a slower paced animal crossing with deep emotional story lines for the bears you meet. I would only say get this game if you are on the fence about it IF you like slow no stress cozy games that you can't play for hours and hours. I play this game first thing in the morning get my dailies and then go on with my day and that is the perfect way to play. Also if you get this game I HIGHLY suggest looking at money making guides cause you need a lot of money to do upgrades to your tent, backpack, storage, and shop.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy Grove is one of those games that you can't really spend the entire day playing; there's a limit of logs you can acquire, and Flamey literally tells you to come again tomorrow. But! For some reason, I find myself lingering despite the fact. I love every bear in the game, and the stories are sometimes so heartbreaking that I can't stop thinking about them. I can't speak highly enough about the game. It has quickly become one of my absolute favorites, and the only real negative for me is that I really wish there was a way to get the bears that you've helped ascend back! I miss you, Arjun!! All in all, highly recommend if you are truly looking for a cozy time, cute graphics, and a little bit of sadness. Yano, as a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played this every day for over a month now, and it's become a little ritual that I look forward to. After work, or when all the chores are done, I'll open it and chill out. I love collectathon games, and there's a lot of things to find. While it's true that the daily quests might not take up more than half an hour, I don't think I've ever played for less than 90 minutes each time. Once the quests are done there's fishing, crafting, things to find, and an inventory to manage. I can't wait till the seasons change, but I feel I might well have 'completed' the story before we get too far into the year. However, I'm very glad I picked it up and hope the developers will continue to add new content for a while to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, long time fan of this developer. I was so excited for this game to launch. I started playing this game on launch day on Switch, and then after about a month started a new game on PC. I haven't missed a day yet since restarting on PC. It's part of my daily ritual and I love visiting Cozy Grove every day to see what progress can be made. I'm also VERY impressed with the first big update.Everything about this game is so beautifully done. If you like casual sim games, you need this one. It's one that gives purpose to coming back day after day.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Animal Crossing? Do you want it to be a bit more.... Spoopy? Then Cozy Grove is the game for you. With an art style similar to Don't Starve, this charming game tasks you with getting badges for helping your fellow ghost citizens. Pros:Gorgeous musicBeautiful art styleAmazing atmosphereGreat storylineStoryline you might be saying. Yes, this game has a storyline. This game is less open ended than AC, but it's a welcome change. Cons:The controls for throwing things can sometimes be a little borked where my character will run off instead of throwing the thingOverall, fantastic game~
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I like that it isn't rushed or pack full of action. Sometimes I just want a cozy game with no pressure. The art is lovely and the music very calming. One thing I would have liked is in game days instead of realtime. Right now I have to wait for tomorrow to get new missions and I don(t want to stop yet. If there were in game days I could just go to sleep and go to the next day. But that's only a minor annoyance.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little bit scared to try out this game after reading so many reviews about it being boring, but I decided to give it a try anyways and I must say this game truly is worth it, however I think it does reach a certain audience better than others.  This game is a bit repetitive. (But in Cozy Grove's defense so are most games in this genre.) Most of your tasks include the same gathering of materials, finding hidden objects and there is a limit on how much you can really do in a day because as I've noticed, you even run out of how many materials you can forge in a day before it resets (which in all honesty does suck) but this game was a good fit for me. After a long day of work or school I find it quite relaxing to sit and do mind numbing tasks for some cute bears with a visually pleasing art style and chill music. It is the true definition of a "Cozy game"Putting in an hour after work to calm down after being yelled at all day at my customer service job is pretty nice and this game does a good job at giving that comfy atmosphere. If that's your sort of thing I would definitely recommend Cozy Grove.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how I've put over 8 hours into this game already since getting it, but if you're a fan of Animal Crossing I hope you'll feel the same. Very cute concept overall, plenty to do but still time gated similarly to AC (which is good, this isn't a game to race to the end!). Fishing, critter catching, crafting, cooking, and all of it helps little bear people. Wouldn't recommend for small kids, there is just a good bit of long story reading and some of the situations described are a bit heavy. Teenagers and adults though, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game before the DLC, and then restarted it once the New Neighbears update was released. Its a charming game and became my "ritual grind and chill" I love the writing, I love the characters and this is one of those games where I want to keep playing/talking to the bears. The game is a bit grim in tone, but i love how affirming it gets to be. I just really love how the Spry Fox team dealt with the topics and the backstory reveals. I would recommend giving this game a shot if you want something casual and a bit dark but also heartwarming. Thank you for such a great game! (Now to 100% the achievements...)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable! Although it is synced in with real time it has become a daily routine in my life. You are only meant to play a little at a time until the next day resets and then there are new quests and such. There's so much that you can earn and unlock. You play as a spirit scout and help (fetch quests) the spirits on the island of Cozy Grove which are mainly adorable bears! Each spirit has their own story and role. You unlock badges for doing different things such as meeting more spirits, fishing, bug catching, skipping stones into ocean clams, owning and minding your animals that you can buy with the in game coins that you earn, you can decorate with items that you earn or craft, you can harvest flowers/ fruit/ nuts, you can ask the camp fire "Flamey" to smelt burn the iron/ gold ore that you mine from rocks and other things that you can forage for. You earn and unlock crafting and food recipes. Your character dose not need to eat in the game but you can make food for your animals when they want something, for some quests I believe and also turn them into the collection spirit for a reward, you can help these little guys called imps when they want a mushroom/ potato or whatever and they will also give you a reward. Pretty much any Item that you obtain you can turn in once to the eagle bird spirit who keeps a collection for rewards and some new recipes he gives. There are different outfits that you can acquire and wear by doing quests or buying them with in game coins that you earn. You have a tent that you can go into and decorate as well as the outside and you can also upgrade your tent at times and this will also give you more inventory space which I love. You can unlock new spirits to help when you feed Flamey the fire a certain amount of spirit logs that you earn from doing quests. There's a shop run by a fox with a mouse on his head lol! that you can buy items or sell your items. You can play this game at your own leisure with a mouse, keyboard or controller which I also love that there is a controller option. I've been going back in forth between my mouse and my controller, I find it's smoother to run around the island with my xbox controller but easier to skip stones and things with my pc mouse. The graphics art is super cute and the music is relaxing with country wilderness camp vibes. There is so much to this game that I know I probably didn't mention every single thing but I'm enjoying my time playing it, it's super relaxing. The more relaxing games in my life the better, since having depression and anxiety games like this help. I don't have to worry about dying a million times lol! These are my only gripes: I wish every quest wasn't the same at times so it would keep things more fresh and new and I wish you could keep cat pets in the same room with other cat pets. Loving the game so far, great job devs :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect little game to fit into a busy schedule. With some games you return after a long day start to play them and after awhile look at the clock and its 2am and you need to get up at 6am.With this game its more just 30 mins to an hour running around doing fetch quests and after you're done for the day, this time limitation really helps the game not to become monotonous or too repetitive. I like the stories each bear brings, its fun to interact with them and the graphics are adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game! I bought it not too long ago while on sale and have been playing almost daily for about 10 days or so. I have already discovered quite a few of the spirits, there are consistent tasks every day for the spirits you've found and that number grows regularly. Each of the spirits has its own story to be discovered and tasks specially tailored to them. The art style is absolutely adorable, there are so many little details and features that just tie the whole experience together to make it very wholesome and enjoyable. It's honestly really fun and I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a chill, adorable game! I was looking for an alternative to Animal Crossing and stumbled upon a beautiful and relaxing life-sim with daily tasks and plenty of collectibles! 500/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It is so incredibly relaxing. If you want a cozy game I cannot recommend this enough. One of my favorite aspects of this game is that it is not designed to have you play for hours and hours a day. This game is designed to keep you paced, playing only an hour or two per day. I love this idea because it keeps me from over-playing and getting burnt out like I did with animal crossing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: an excellent game that could can load up and play for a few hours with your morning coffee everyday. i love the fact that the game can't really be "grinded" or rushed. the story telling is captivating and the actual game play is adorable. there's something so satisfying with earning all your badges and helping out others along the way. it's become a part of my morning routine and i recommend it entirely!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: i like this game a lot :) people are right when they say the quests repetitive, but i think that's fine for what the game is. it's fun and easy to play and i like having a game that i can sink half an hour or an hour into daily or abandon for weeks/months without feeling lost. the art is also very cute and i like the bears a lot. aesthetic-wise, this game honestly beats animal crossing for me...very cute game. well worth the money if you're a fan of the style & gameplay loop. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasant game, relaxing, slow-paced, a bit of grindy but quests are nicely spaced between real-life days. The only issue I have with the gameplay is that when you are stacking trees/bushes on each other, it's hard to see when trees/bushes in the background are ripe and ready to harvest.
