_childDocuments_.review: A super laid back and calming game - designed for rainy days or a hour away from the real world.A fantastical cross between Animal Crossing mechanics and a whimsical take on Don't Stare Together artwork this games brings the best of the two games together. Help the other ghostly inhabitants of your personal Island while collection items, crafting, gathering memories and scoring scout badges. I would highly recommend for people who enjoyed either of the above mentioned games or who just want to gather and enjoy some fantastic music along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, interesting and well paced game that avoids the usual pitfall of titles like these - its not generic and bland. The story unveiling in Cozy Grove isn't as straightforward as you think and I'm very invested to see how it progresses. The newly added mechanics in the summer upgrade like catching bugs make the game feel fresh and interesting even after me playing it for over 50 days every single day. The art style is original and beautiful to look at, the character customization is fun and has a lot of variety (the in game shop has something new every day, hairstyles, clothes, accessories etc). I have noticed that this game has became a part of my daily routine, doing your quests while eating breakfast is relaxing and fun. I would happily pay more for this game, the price is a steal, honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game daily for a couple of weeks and I'm hooked! This is not a game in which you can spend long hours at in a short period of time, it's a game to have short sessions on each day. It takes off the preassure of farming and progressing quickly, making it a really nice and relaxing game.I love checking out everyday the new thingies that have popped out in my island. The bears and animals are quite charming too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice and chilled game, do not play if you want to progress immediately.  From what I have seen, the game is meant to be played casually on a daily or as often as possibly basis.  The day/night cycle is 5am till 5am IRL time.  It's not like Stardew Valley where you can go sleep and wake up the next day.  You go sleep IRL and then it's a new day in game as well.  Once you've gotten all your spirit wood available for the day, there is still foraging, stone skipping and fishing to do, but I haven't felt a need to grind anything yet.  I can literally play for a few hours, then move onto something else and not feel like I'm loosing time to grind.I also love the graphics, etc. super cute, can't wait to see what they do for Christmas! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game so far. All of the characters are so cute and the artwork in this game is phenomenal. I love the spawn rate on items such as fish and leaf piles. I am also extremely fond of the fact that you cannot grind in this game. Each day has a certain amount of quests you can fulfill, which is great for someone like me who can and will get sucked into a game for hours on end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy both Don't Starve Together and Animal Crossing, you'll definitely enjoy this game. It's very cute with a VERY mild creepy undertone. Most of the "creepiness" is just the fact that you're dealing with ghosts and you need to learn about their past lives and help them move on. I'm not a fan of creepy games and I love this one so I'd definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable and so much fun, I'm already hooked. The interesting thing is that it's not a binge kind of game. You can't play for hours without end. Eventually, the game tells you you're done for the day. A good thing that keeps you coming back but also sad because I wish I could play forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: The game is perfect for if you want to play an animal crossing type game, but without the stress of trying to move forward too fast. People say this is "time gated" which I guess it is, but its not punishing. you can collect and sell all night (which is what i do for fun to decorate and dress up) to pass the time between missions. It is slow, fair warning, but on day two it feels a bit better. Just be aware that if you don't enjoy slow games, this game isn't for you. It is a commitment but not a punishing one.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is primarily fetch quests with a lot of geomancy. But also, from the X's in the ground, to the silhouette fish, down to the triangle noses, this is Animal Crossing. Nothing wrong with that if you love Animal Crossing, I just wish it wasn't so blatant about it.I'm refunding it because I already own Animal Crossing. But also because there's too much Feng Shui/geomancy to worry about (e.g. this chair you're about to place is RUSTIC, Tommy the Crow does not like RUSTIC furniture, but Jimmy the Plant does! Either move Tommy away from the chair or put this next to Jimmy!), and the furniture doesn't do anything/nobody can come see the work you're putting in.That said, it is very much trying to get the cozy mechanics down and it is very charming, just a little off the mark for my tastes. I would recommend Spiritfarer, Animal Crossing, or Stardew Valley over this. If you've already played all of those and just want more to tide you over, by all means get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I got it on sale for $12 but it's more than worth the full price of $15 (it's on sale for $7.49 right now). It's a cute game where I go on little errands for these adorable ghost bears on a drab island. It's extremely charming and I look forward to coming back everyday. I'm on Day 30 and I definitely play each day more than I need to (I fish and bug hunt and stuff). It's very relaxing and I think the characters are well thought out and I like how it gives you little tidbits at a time. I love decorating my house, giving my character little outfits, and staging little scenes around the bears. I think the art style and object themes are beautiful. If you're looking for something light and cute to occupy your time or an hour or two a day while watching TV, definitely get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely loving this game so far. The best way that I can describe it is Spiritfarer meets Animal Crossing..if you enjoyed those two games, you're bound to enjoy this one.The characters are adorable and unique, I love how they are themed (as an example, the mail bear looking like a parcel!) and I am so excited to meet more of them and build my relationship with the spirits I have already met. The art and overall aesthetic of the game is..to die for.Totally recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Lol at the people bashing a 15$ game that's about being chill and taking it slow.It's a good game if you like Animal Crossing-esque time gated kind of games. What is "time gated" ? That you can't just sit down one afternoon and complete the game, it's about logging in 10-40 mins every other day or few times a day you feel like roaming on the island and talking to your spirit friends --- while also progressing the story. It is an animal crossing esque game in that way , there's also clothes, tons of fetch quests and personalization for your "cozy grove" placeable items, craftables, shop expansions, expanding the island ect. Its a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game on sale because I'd heard good things about it, but didn't really understand the premise. I like games like Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing, and figured this would be something new to try out. It's a really cute game (the "perpetual daylight" setting is a lifesaver if you can only play at night). The controls are a little difficult/slippery at first, but after a few hours I had them figured out. The directions aren't always super clear, but it's more of an exploration and decoration game instead of completing goals as fast as you can. Charlotte Pine, one of the first bear spirits you help, can also point you in the direction of various quest items so you will never be truly lost. There are so many things to collect in this game that it seems overwhelming at first, but go slow. There's only about 30 minutes of "new" content in the game per day if you only have a few bear spirits unlocked, but as you go on and unlock more spirits, your daily quests expand. You can also spend hours just decorating the island.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. Very peaceful and relaxing. There is enough things for me to do in a day and not feel rushed to get it done. The artwork is just lovely. It's a very good game to keep my anxiety down and allows me to not have to get everything done right away. I look forward to future Bears and adventures in Cozy Grove.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Soundtrack = 10/10, no stress about it, very cozy and relaxing.Gameplay = 10/10, also no stress, a little bit of story here and there and you get attached to all kinds of cute bear spirits.You also get to fish, rummage around bushes, dig for treasures, decorate around the island, while also summoning cute little pets.I've "only" played 5 hours on steam, but I also have a little bit of time on my switch.10/10 do recommend this game for a "break" in your every day life, and also in between other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Game is not ready, its still in Beta. Your NPC can have only quest at a time, and you can't reject them for any reason. You get quests you cant' solver because the Npc is not yet unlocked or the resources, or the quest needs 8,10,12 of a resources when you are on day 3. For a game that you have to come back each an every day for resources and Npc quests, the bugs make you not want to come back.	I like the special  sauce of coming  back each day, not being able to finish the game in one sit down, that is not the issue. Quest you can't reject because you don't the the ability to solve, and lock up progression, or locks up one or more Npc's for a week long quest is not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% Cozy game! Relaxing and beautiful. ♥♥♥ Played after recommended by ETA Sept 2024: I can't believe I have been solidly playing this game since Jan 2023 and still at a 50/70 game achievement. _childDocuments_.review: Pros: - cute af - the art style is adorable - relaxing soundtrack - the things these spirit bears say are an absolute trip - giant fox demi-god shopkeeper?? YESCons - not a game you can get lost in for hours (but also not the point of the game) - not many quests to do at first - quests are time-locked - mostly fishing or catching bugs to get moneyCozy Grove takes after Animal Crossing in the sense of developing an island from your own little campground out and helping the island's ghostly residents, and--like Animal Crossing--after you've completed your quests for the day, the game is 80% fishing and catching bugs. If you're a fan of AC, this probably won't bother you too much. If casual gaming isn't your bag, this will drive you up the wall. The biggest criticism for the game would be that there isn't a whole lot of main-quest content per day and its daily quests are time-locked, and that bites most as a new player when you're excited to sink an entire weekend into the game (and you can't... unless you've got an audiobook or anime queued up alongside and are fine spending the vast majority of said weekend fishing). HOWEVER,  and this is stated multiple times throughout both the game's description and first few hours of gameplay and if you somehow missed that... that's on you. The point is to gradually develop relationships with the spirits you encounter and help them resolve their issues to (presumably) move onto the great Bear-yond or something equally punny. As you complete more quests and uncover more of the island, you get more daily quests from the spirits you've met and more ground to explore (and more bugs to catch and more fish to fish lol). I do wish there was an option to bind hotkeys for tools kept in the hotbar, but after expressing this to a friend, was informed that "this game is not for sweaty gamers" and I'm not even that sweaty, so keep that in mind.Cozy Grove is adorable and a great casual gaming experience, but if you're looking for a game where you can get lost in and oops it's 4am and you have work tomorrow, it's likely not the game you're looking for. Maybe check out The Wild at Heart or Kari instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game lets you explore and collect materials for as long as you'd like, but once you collect all the spirit wood for the day, you're done. I think that's my favourite part because of how overwhelmed I was in animal crossing. I just feel so relaxed running around and getting to know these hilarious and adorable creatures. I definitely recommend if you like cozy, chill games.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really amazing! At the beginning you still have a small island so there isn't alot to do in the day, but as your island gets bigger and bigger you have more and more to do and I'm now at the point where I can play for several hours until I've exhausted all the things I can do in a day (my island still isn't fully expanded). Granted, having little to do at the beginning did help with not playing this game obsessively, which I actually didn't mind. It is a cozy game for sure but with the struggles that you help the bears with, it's actually also a game that makes you think and you really grow a bond with the bears so sometimes it can also get a little emotional lol. The customisation in the game is also really nice, you can decorate your island (although mostly the space around your tent and the orchards, but that is quite alot) and you can customize your little character with a ton of hair and clothes options! Overall I just really recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing little game in isometric 2D sprites style that is a definite homage to Animal Crossing.Similar to Animal Crossing, the game follows the actual time setting of your PC and the world adjusts accordingly, with many objectives in the game designed to span multiple days (some being forced, some being because of requiring gathering limited resources so a little bit RNG). [PROS]+ Interesting premise & a charming art style+ Likeable characters that have individual stories that unravel as you interact with them and assist them+ Game world expands at certain progress milestones, making your island larger over time+ Collection system that rewards you for cataloging things like fish, bugs, materials, cooked foods, etc. Items that you haven't submitted yet helpfully say that they can be submitted in their tooltip, and this disappears if you've already turned in that item before+ Can place most things anywhere you want+ Plants and animals have an interesting system of Likes / Dislikes, where each has a different combo of both using tags that are on placeable environment objects like furniture and the animals and plants themselves+ Progress on the first two days or so has a nice little kickstart to get you up to speed before it starts slowing down a little, letting you get set up pretty quickly[CONS]- Item collection from randomly appearing nodes (dowsing spots, dig spots, leaf piles, overgrown shrubs) seems to have some kind of "soft-cap" in that once you've used a certain amount of them in a given time frame (or possibly an entire day) the spawning of them slows down . This limits your gain of certain types of resource each day somewhat, though it seems bug and fish spawns are not capped in this way--- Mining nodes, Trees, Bushes, Spirit Animals, and Flowers are even more restricted than the above, having what appears to be a definite daily hard-cap of only one harvest per day, per node. Additionally, for Spirit Animals to produce anything, they have to be fed; from my experience, they do not always want to be fed all at once or at the same time daily; the most animals in the same area that have required feeding within a many-hour-long span of time was only 3 (out of a whopping 10), thus making it difficult to make sure you get the harvest from each of them each day unless you check multiple times per day--- There's a definite amount of grind and tedium through the crafting system for rarer and higher tier furniture and objects (and the resources to make them). Most resources have tiers, with the next tier being rarely available on its own, or otherwise has to be made via "compressing" many of the previous tier into only  of the next tier. This means some "simple" recipes becoming exceedingly expensive and massive time sinks. As an example, you have the wood materials; Branches, Softwood, and Hardwood. All three are available at different drop-rates from trees and leaf piles, and you can make the higher tiers using the lower tiers. But the exchange rate is abysmal. 10 branches > 1 softwood, and 10 softwood > 1 hardwood; making 1 hardwood equivalent to 100 branches. Hardwood naturally has the lowest drop rate as well- Music becomes grating over time; I've started having to mute the music and play my own or put on Youtube videos in the background as it legitimately feels like the game only has two music tracks (I don't know how many it actually has). When playing for an hour or two at a time, it makes me feel like I'm going insane from the lack of variation, as the tracks don't have that good looping quality that Animal Crossing hourly tracks doTL;DR: It's a good game and well worth the price of admission (despite my gripes) if you like chill and more relaxed paced games like Animal Crossing. If you're expecting to make progress fast, steer clear, as this game will most definitely not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The art is beautiful, I love how the game looks, and the characters are wonderful. The premise is cool too, but it just gets really boring over time. And the fact that you can only do so many things a day just makes you feel like you HAVE to play or else you're wasting progress that you cannot get back. If the quests were different maybe it would be a bit more fun to play but this just feels like a good idea that was badly executed :(
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: It is indeed a cozy game, where you try to help out the spirits and light things up, bringing the island back to life. Game certainly teaches patience, because you can't just rush it through. There are limitations how much you can push the story forward during the day, but little by little it comes together. Would recommend for player, who like sweet, wholesome gaming experience and isn't in any rush.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I was interested in this game after reading an article that it is like Animal Crossing with less capitalism. This is an enjoyable game to relax to, the atmosphere of Cozy Grove is calming even with ghosts running around. They're all friendly and adorable and I enjoy interacting with the characters and helping them out. You can do many of the same things you do in Animal Crossing- befriend the villagers, run errands, harvest and collect resources to sell or use in crafting, and buy clothes and items to decorate your campsite. Only thing missing is the shady raccoon and his mortgage. Some people don't like how the game limits how much you can do in a day, but for me, who has limited time for video games, it fits perfectly to allow for me to play a little each day to slowly unravel the story. I think that's part of the unique charm of the game, is unfolding the story at a slow and steady pace. I'm a person who does not like for a good game to be over so quickly, so I appreciate the fact that this game forces you to slow down and enjoy the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games to chill to. I finished it on Switch and wanted to play through it again on another platform to get achievements. It's so relaxing, and one of the few games I actually want the soundtrack to. The bears are all unique and it's fun to explore the layers of their stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable and super calming! I love this game because it reminds me a bit of Animal Crossing and Don't Starve if they had a baby. Even though it's only about two hours of play a day, it helps you start or end your day with a smile on your face. I absolutely love all the characters and their dialogues. You can choose to be sassy, or polite depending on the day and it makes me giggle every time. Highly recommend if you're in need of a cute game or just want to be relaxed.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: You know that feeling when you're watching Bob Ross and you feel so comfy and at peace? This whole game is like a Bob Ross painting - in fact, it feels like you're actively living inside a Bob Ross painting.This game is often linked and compared to Animal Crossing, and for a couple of points, I would agree; however, I think that Cozy Grove stands up entirely on its own as a incredibly comfy, wholesome, and mindful game about connecting with some lost souls (no pun intended) and appreciating every day. I love waking up in the mornings and having a cup of coffee and tea with my Cozy Grove. For me, when I really enjoy a game, I can get incredibly fixated and hyper-focused to the point of burn out but the game's mechanics of giving a fixed amount of quests per day to be effective in combating that. I always feel satisfied by the end of my daily runs and feel excited to return the next time. I'm sure I've only just barely scraped the top of the barrel so far, but I can't wait to see how my Island looks a month+ from now. I would highly recommend this game for folks looking for a rewarding, comfy, slow-burn that can be incorporated into any schedule, especially busier ones!
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME. the soundtrack is so soothing and the art style is adorable. The characters and the backstory along with the cute outfits, pets, and decorations really make this game beautiful and one of a kind. If u like AC u will definitely love this game. I wish we could color the walls of our tents ⛺️ but thats really the only complaint I have. Amazing job!

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I purchased Cozy Grove because I wanted a competent clone to fill the Animal Crossing sized hole in my life. Like nearly everyone, I played AC religiously in the early days of the lockdown. 200+ hours later, when I realized there was no real progression to speak of, no more to unlock, no one new to meet, nothing really to do.. I regretfully put my island to rest. Rarely, if ever, to be seen again.Cozy Grove was on my radar as soon as it released and.. Hey, it's about being stranded on an island! You can fish! and decorate! There's a whole cast of neighbors to meet! I was intrigued to say the least, this game sells itself as New Horizons But Spooky, and that couldn't be more in my wheelhouse. So, within a few weeks I gave into temptation and purchased the game at full price.Immediately, I was in love. The game has the same time-gated progression as AC, meaning there's only about an hours worth of gameplay each day before you have to wait again. I seem to be the minority, but I really enjoy games like this. Popping in for 30 minutes to an hour each day, hearing a little bit more of each of the island resident's stories and slowly expanding and changing the game world was extremely satisfying. I was raising live stock, planting trees, decorating my camp and playing for 2 hours or more each day until every ounce of content had been thoroughly exhausted. I couldn't get enough of the sad but sweet stories of the NPCs (who are all bears.. and ghosts) and the game's dry, millennial sense of humor. After 30 or so (real and in-game) days of playing this way, I began to better focus my efforts. Decorating wasn't really clicking for me, raising the animals likewise turned out to be more trouble than it was worth, but I was still having a blast upgrading everything, meeting new bears, and continuing the stories of the old ones.The bloom was off the rose a little around 60 or 70 days in. The game was very grindy and slow in the beginning (something they have fixed a lot with post-release patches) and I lost interest. Eventually, when I returned, it was to play for around 20 minutes each day to do that day's story related quests. I was still enjoying the game, but I was ready to move on. At this point, I still hadn't reached the "end" of the game or any of the bear's stories. So I kept playing, 20 to 30 minutes a day. They added bugs to catch, but I was never really interested in doing that. A handful of times, I was given a quest that required a heroic amount of grinding and those would take a week or more of extra tedious hunting, but that was mostly because my stockpile of resources from the early days of playing had finally depleted and I hadn't been refilling them.Finally now, after over 100 in game days, I have completed all of the story content and it left me feeling a little underwhelmed. None of the bears' individual stories really blew me away like I was hoping they might. They weren't bad by any means.. just a little simple and repetitive. The main theme can be summarized as "people are sometimes shortsighted about their own faults and insecurities, but we should be more open and honest about them because that is what makes us human." It drives that point so rigorously that it left me feeling a little numb by the end.. as much as I agree. I kept telling myself that I would go back after completing the stories to finish up all the collecting and decorating, but then I helped my final ghost bear and felt an overwhelming sense of closure. I really enjoyed my time with Cozy Grove. It wasn't everything I expected it to be, but it's not without it's strengths. It's exceedingly charming and it has a few actual jokes. The gameplay is a lot of simple pointing and clicking and fetching, but the act of bringing color to a literal black and white ghost town is forever satisfying. It's ok that I liked what I liked and didn't like what I didn't like. It's fine to put it to rest

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE cozy grove. It's like animal crossing's little goth sister. I've been obsessed to play it every day since I got it. I love how the game runs in real time and how it gives you enough content daily (about an hour and a half of game play daily). The characters and their stories/background are so fleshed out. There is something to do and learn every day. This game is fun to play at a slow pace. This game has cured my animal crossing burnout.  Not to mention, the art style of the game is also soooo cute! Very pleasing and warm and it is very fun to explore around the island. I 10/10 recommend this game, especially for people looking for a cozy game to wind down to :)
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★☆☆3/5 Overall the game is fun. However, claimed that the game providing only 30-60 minutes of quest for player to play for a day, to change the play style of the animal-crossing genre game.Yep I agree with this for the first few days, but at the later days will find out that "Nope, this is still the usual game we played, that thought grinding, will help for better gaming experience." "Game level" that bump up too much : The moment I unlocked the chef bear, my bird straight forward to ask for a chocolate cake. But, I don't even know where to find a coco bean for that. I can only find that to upgrade the shop which spend ton of money to it.Recipe is asking too much material : Cooking one boiled egg I need 12 eggs? Where the other 11 went? I gave them to the freaking bear for free?Btw, instead of using the name of Animal-Crossing, the game is more like a "Where's Wally" for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sort of game you play to kill time. Similar to animal crossing in that you wander around, you fish you collect things you build relationships with the locals. In game time is the same as real life and there is only so many things you can do in a day, espcially in the beginning. But its a nice change, its relaxing and stress free, I like all the locals. They are all diffrent and I want to help all of them.Game play has the typical fish, collect, farm (by way of putting down the plants, no watering necessary) later on you can get an item that helps with group collect instead of individually going from plant to plant or tree to tree. Animals want you to cook diffrent food items sometimes and like diffrent objects so you find yourself juggling and re organizing areas to make them more optimal. Seek and find items for the villagers can be a lot more challenging then you expect but if its not your jam Charlotte can be bribed to tell you where it is.  Its not a game to stress over, its a game to enjoy. I bought it on sale but will buy any sequels they bless us with as they come out. I've definitely taken long breaks from it only to come back and find that I missed the locals and enjoyed visiting them and playing some more. Its nice to have a game I don't feel pressured to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. For ages, this was an absolute staple for me, opening it up every single day to complete a couple quests, catch some bugs and fish, etc etc. Now Cozy Grove 2 is in development, and I'm looking forward to it. It is a nice relaxing game. Yes, it is time gated, but in my personal opinion, time gating is only an issue in subscription-based games, where time-gating directly equates to costing you more money. This game's only monetization beyond the Steam purchase of the game is the singular DLC (€5,69), adding multiple new characters and concepts to the game.If you want a chill game with animals and interesting backstories, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend it.This tries to be an Animal Crossing competitor, but it doesn't understand what makes Animal Crossing likable. It's not the daily chores or the real time nuances; it's the villagers, who are generally happy and pleasant. This game has villagers that are all dead and unhappy. In general, I found these Cozy Grove residents a strange combination of uninteresting and depressing. No endearing personality; just a sob story to compel game progression.Gameplay generally involves hidden-object fetch quests. If you struggle with eyesight (as I do), the quests are somewhat stressful — especially at the onset when everything is white and monochromatic, causing everything to blend in together. Additionally, this game suffers from some of the same setbacks as early Animal Crossing installations did as well; namely, the daily limitation of activities. As others have said, your first day only lasts about 30 minutes. I spent 32, and I struggled with several quests as well as spent a few extra moments looking for something to do. Not a great first impression.Not a happy getaway, not interesting gameplay, unsettling NPCs, and nothing "new" or unique to set it apart. If you're looking for something great, this is definitely a title you can pass on.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this cozy game- it literally has Cozy in the title. It's basically a series of search and find quests. It's fun for awhile but then it's the same mechanics over and over. The only reason I have so many hours is because I'd leave the game open after running around the map looking for the item that was requested in a quest. I just got bored once I realized there was no real progression and no mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game! Wasn't expecting to get hooked (if you like fishing, you'll like the fishing in this one) but I did. Has a nice pace, pretty relaxed, progress feels well paced so far. I really like the cartoon style of the game too (I feel it has that don't starve vibe). Over all definitely a win win for me. This is one you can pick up any time you want to relax. don't mind a little bit of farming and looks like it has plenty of challenges the more you play and progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Cozy Grove

_childDocuments_.review:
Welcome to Cozy Grove, a life-sim game about camping on a haunted, ever-changing island. As a Spirit Scout, you'll wander the island's forest each day, finding new hidden secrets and helping soothe the local ghosts. With a little time and a lot of crafting, you'll bring color and joy back to Cozy Grove!

Features:

* Beautiful, dynamic, hand-drawn landscapes that come alive when you help a spirit in need.
* Dozens of memorable characters and spirits for you to find and befriend. Each spirit has a unique, extensive story for you to unravel over time.
* Collect spirit animals, craft decorations, go fishing and more!
* 40+ hour campaign filled with side quests, designed to span months of playtime.

name: Pacific Drive
detailed_description: Deluxe Edition Get ready to blast off with the Pacific Drive: Deluxe Edition ! This bundle includes the game plus an additional items pack themed around space exploration, that you can use to customize your station wagon. About the Game Pacific Drive is a first-person driving survival game with your car as your only companion. Navigate a surreal reimagining of the Pacific Northwest, and face supernatural dangers as you venture into the Olympic Exclusion Zone. Each excursion into the wilderness brings unique and strange challenges as you restore and upgrade your car from an abandoned garage that acts as your home base. Gather precious resources and investigate what’s been left behind in the Zone; unravel a long-forgotten mystery while learning exactly what it takes to survive in this unpredictable, hostile environment. Features Outrun the storm while facing strange perils in a world that shifts with every journey into the Zone Your car, your way – scavenge resources to craft new equipment and configure your wagon how you want. Experiment with different mods and car parts to navigate a treacherous landscape, and look good doing it Unravel the mystery of the Olympic Exclusion Zone, an abandoned research site in an anomaly-filled version of the Pacific Northwest Original score by Wilbert Roget, II and featuring 20+ licensed songs DRIVE TO SURVIVE It’s you and your station wagon against an unforgiving, vicious world. It’ll take more than a fresh set of tires to keep you alive, on and off the road. Your faithful wagon can be upgraded and reinforced to protect you, but the car is going to take a beating. Keep your gas tank filled and your panels intact to withstand the radiation permeating the Zone. You’ll be pushed to your limit - making repairs on the fly, scavenging materials wherever you can, and adapting your rolling fortress to tackle the many life-threatening dangers that lurk in the shadows. INVESTIGATE THE ZONE The experimental leftovers of the secretive ARDA organization remain scattered across the Zone, and finding answers won’t be easy. Everywhere you look you’ll find anomalies, surreal forces of a twisted nature that make your journey more difficult... or more interesting. Silhouettes in the dark, rolling piles of scrap metal, and towering pillars of earth - each trip is packed with otherworldly hazards. As terrifying as those may be, nothing compares to the overwhelming power of a Zone Storm. Stomp on the gas and outrun it if you can - these rolling maelstroms rend the landscape and obliterate anything that sticks around too long. Don’t let that be you. REPEAT Check the map, pack some gear for the trip, and hit the road. Gather resources and collect data as you go, there’s all sorts of useful stuff inside the walls of the Zone. Make it back safely and use the contents of your trunk to improve your car and garage. Every time you venture out, new trials await: bizarre weather, unforgiving landscapes, and experimental remnants. The golden rule in the Zone is ‘nothing ventured, nothing gained’ — some materials can only be found in the most dangerous places. Be smart out there, and don’t waste time — it’s going to be a long haul.

short_description: Face the supernatural dangers of the Olympic Exclusion Zone with a car as your only lifeline in this driving survival adventure! Scavenge resources, load up your trusty station wagon, and drive like hell to make it through alive.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a fair amount to take in but what matters is quality rather than quantity and the learning process for this is a joy.  I only wish my dad were still around to play, he grew up in the Pacific Northwest and it was a tossup whether he enjoyed the hikes more or the drives to them.  Would have been right up his alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up to be fair to the developers. The game is not bad but didn't find it fun. Fortunately there are a lot of play options to make it easier to play as the default settings are quite difficult and frustrating. I kept thinking before I played it,  if I was going to have enough time to finish a mission or not before I had to leave, and this turned me off of the game.  The average round in my play through was not 30 min but closer to an hour. Not for me sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow, an optimized My Summer Car set in the PNW, but also crossed over with spooky STALKER monsters, works really, really well.  The atmosphere is simultaneously tense but dreamy, driving around the winding mountain roads of the Olympic peninsula.  Stop to take in the beautiful mountain sights! Or because an explosive statue is standing in the road and you need to find a way around it.I envision spending many hours with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of the film Annihilation but with some sort of Ghostbusters type station wagon. A unique gaming experience, at times quite frustrating but also fun. Optimisation needs some work, DLSS doesn't seem to be working properly, the game suffers significant FPS drops and occasional stutter, also the shadow quality kills the performance on higher settings and makes the game look a bit dark.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I love playing this game. It's a great survival game, with a lot in common (spiritually) with Raft, Green Hell, and Subnautica.You go out in your car, into medium-sized maps, where you collect resources from ruins while avoiding semi-intelligent dangers. Each run culminates with a suspenseful race to the exit, while the world collapses around you. You start off afraid of everything, then as you learn the limitations of the dangers, learn to avoid them and move efficiently. You're always in a race against the clock and the condition of your vehicle, and the core loop is extremely satisfying.From a design perspective, I really admire how the devs worked within their budget and technological constraints. Like Raft and Subnautica, they don't spend money populating the world with other NPCs and complex models, instead they spent all their time making really good design and aesthetic choices, plus lots of clever easter eggs and winks in the customizations and upgrades you can build for your 'base'.Play this game -- it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is interesting, it feels close to Subnautica on land, though the story does not expand.You cannot trust all Sounds to be a cue that something is happening, radio chatter is just random stories of no notice and game is widely covered in secrecy, which you can slowly unveil by collecting excessively short radio recordings. As we encounter Anomalies they all receive a brief story upon scanning, some explain exacly what to expect, some, leave you questioning what you just red, the unknown, exploration and the feeling of driving like its 90's again. scavenging resources, crafting upgrades to collect more efficiently, to carry more, to be safer. Begining of the game is brutal, as we have almost nothing and can barely keep the car in one piece, midgame (~20h) mark i was feeling good about my progress, i was stocked up on all Tier 1 and 2 materials, just didn't had access to Tier 3 materials, moving forward with story changed alot, suddenly corrupted anchors are no longer an issue, but Tier 2 and 3 Resources suddenly become an issue once again. Game has alot of weird bugs as of this review date 29.02.2024, teleported my car up a hill (max range is 25m), drained the battery (As it doesn't explain that it consumes 20 points of battery charge anywhere), and physics went wonky launching my car 300 meters into forest, landing it on its back, so i had to teleport it again. Random texture clippings sometimes, shadows of crosshair in some well lit zones causing weird tearing on screen and squares (Happened only once but still), assests loading late and being all over the place in garage, missclicks can result in trashing all of your gear, and well, you never know how much resources you will receive from trashing an item, as some give you nothing. Story is not bad, but i mostly enjoyed the driving around, music on the radio sadly is very limited, so after 20 hours, you will be getting tired of all the tunes. From what i saw, weaker systems encounter way more game breaking issues.I hope that over time the wikipedias for this game will grow and more will be known, so more casual players can also enjoy what this game has to offer at full game's potential, try-hards can enjoy what this game has to offer for them as it is right now (Wearing off parts, swelling battery destroying your doors over time, worn out storage dropping items as you drive, etc).But once you build that mix of parts of a car, and find how you enjoy playing, the game becomes quiet nice. Some anomalies are useful, some are annoying, some make you regret actually discovering them (I'm talking about you blacksmith), Story ending is kind of abrupt, and might lead most of players to drop the game afterwards. Hopefully some further update will come out that will provide additional content.Attempting to complete high end recipies is currently nearly impossible, as the olympic resource is ultra rare and you simply have to get lucky to find any, so final grind is excessive, hopefully this will be adressed with future patches....TL;DRExploration: 8/10Driving: 7/10Story: 5/10In-game Music: 8/10Is it in playable state? 5/10 (One crash, 3 zones with weird graphic rendering).Time to beat? 20-40 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently I have started to really appreciate games that take steps to take a real action, like playing golf or driving a car, and adding seemingly unnecessary extra steps to make the experience more realistically immersive. A itchio horror golfing game I played recently, Greener Grass Awaits, forces you to place down your golf bag, take out the correct driver, and when you are done shooting, pick it back up and carry it to the ball before placing it down once again. It's a small, unnecessary touch that grants a piece of almost tedious realism to the act of golfing, but it also isn't tedious at all, considering it only requires a single button press, and it feels natural to do.Pacific drive toes the exact same line between tedium and immersion with its driving mechanics. Physically turning the key by hold clicking on the key, and disengaging the parking brake by actually moving the lever. Flipping on the windshield wipers with the actual wipers stick on the steering wheel, turning the radio off and on, etc. It's deeply simplified: there is no gear shift, no blinker, no air conditioning. you can't roll down your windows or lock your car. But it's enough to feel real while not overdoing it with unrelated systems. Everything you can do can and will affect your gameplay, and everything missing is entirely irrelevant. There is no need to lock your car in a deserted wasteland, for example, but when it rains ingame, having windshield wipers is greatly appreciated. This focus on the car and its systems also extends to the way it moves. The momentum from turning and accelerating, the way the car reacts to bumps in the road, the light of your headlights perfectly illuminating the area in front of you... the car is perfect. I personally think the gameplay is a bit lacking? It's definitely engaging, and I had an incredibly amount of fun vibing to the ingame radio for hours on the road, but it does get a bit repetitive. It's a looter game, so that is to be expected I suppose, and with the procedurally generated landscapes and landmarks you start seeing the same things over and over again. Luckily if you follow the story through the intended gameplay path (instead of spending hours ignoring the story like myself) it does switch it up enough to keep it fresh.Overall, I think this game is fantastic. I personally wanted more intentional environments, but I think that's just a personal thing, as I can't think of any better way to make this game than the way they did it.Definitely worth the 30 bucks if you think you'll enjoy vibing in a car at night in the forest listening to fantastic music and dodging supernatural anomalies.soo apparently the story is also really good

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a certified classic. I love it to bits, and it deserves more recognition. A nice 30$ price tag, for a not-so-short but definitely sweet experience. For one, I think they did a Superb job with the car and all of the mechanics surrounding it.        The swapping out and upgrading car parts, the upgrading and modules you can attach, and the decals and detailing you can do, It's all great. I really like that there's all of these different kinds of damage the car can incur that you'll need to fix with several different types of repair kits that you'll need to store in the car.     Another thing I really like is the danger aspect. There's all of these different 'Anomalies' along the road, but they're never out-right trying to kill you. Instead, they all act to sabotage you and your car, acting as obstacles in your way rather than direct threats, which I thought was a very good way of doing it. The anomalies themselves are super cool looking, and they all do various different things that can throw off your drive in various ways.    The last thing I will mention is the world and the characters. I really like what they were going for with the aesthetic, and I think they nailed it. It perfectly fits what I would envision an SCP road trip game being like. The characters are are all great, you'll be listening to three voices over the radio helping you out as the game progresses, and you get to see how your relationship with them grows, as well as their relationships with each other. The VA's did a phenomenal job making these characters entertaining and fun to listen to.        I do have some nitpicks, like the Quirks system. I do not think it's a bad inclusion at all, but it did need some more time in the oven. Overall though, If I had a tierlist, this game is going into A tier. For an indie studio, they smashed this out of the park, and I really cannot wait to see what they do with this game going forward, or their future projects in general. Very highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a tremendous survival game that draws healthy comparison to some of the best in the genre. The focus on the station wagon helps to set it apart, with many useful upgrades and customization options. Quirks give the car personality and gadgets improve reliability. Widespread randomization means that every trip plays out differently and there is great reward for planning and executing long drives across an unpredictable region. There is also a fantastic sense of discovery, thanks to weird anomalies and other oddities, in a world that has a suitably creepy atmosphere. With careful preparation and apt driving skill, the next deadly storm will have you singing along with the car’s radio, even though it switched on by itself.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression of Pacific Drive was positive. It is unlike any game I have ever played, and I considered it worth playing for that reason alone. That it sticks the landing as well as it does made me play it for as long as I did. Nonetheless, I stopped playing it about 3/4 of the way through, and do not intend to complete it. (Total play time is about 30 hours.)Pacific Drive is unique: It owes an obvious debt to Boris and Arkady Strugatsky's novel Roadside Picnic (indeed, I bought the game the same day I finished reading the novel) and, perhaps to a lesser degree, the Stalker games, which are more explicitly based on the novel. It is a game about discovery, and it rewards exploration (with caveats; more on this later). Your opponents are so-called anomalies, not humans, and these too can be discovered, analyzed, and added to an ever-updating database. It includes a plethora of upgrades to your character and to your car, in the style of survival games. And it is, after a fashion, a light car mechanic simulator. Ironwood Studios has woven these elements together seamlessly.The game I wanted and expected is one in which you gradually begin to tame your environment, with the aid of upgrades, until your crappy little car becomes an offroad beast (as opposed to "slightly less crappy") and aspects of exploration that were stressful at the beginning, including dealing with certain anomalies, slowly become distant memories.There are elements of the above, to be sure. But that is not the game that Ironwood Studios wants to provide, and it is not the story the devs want to tell. By design, you are constantly on the edge of losing control, of your vehicle and of your environment. In many areas the game has much more in common with a roguelike (and indeed some reviews label the game a roguelite), in which you are pushing against a time limit and taking calculated risks to extract as much from the zone as you can without taking one risk too many and losing it all. While some of the early zones and many (all?) of the story-mission zones have an aspect called perpetual stability, most of the remaining zones have an instability to them that makes it deadly to linger for too long. Get in, explore for as long as you dare, and then get the hell out. This makes for a fast-paced game that is not about lingering but about optimization of movement and prioritization of targets. For me personally, this aspect of the gameplay is a poor companion to the game's sense of discovery and wonder, with exploration becoming a means to an end rather than the end itself.I say "wants to" to make it clear that this is not the game being broken but rather intentional design, and is therefore not a flaw as such. It becomes a question of taste, and is likely a large reason Pacific Drive is labeled a divisive game by some reviewers. The other half of the game is the garage. This is very much a game about preparation, and there is a deliberateness about this portion that I found deeply satisfying. However, it is the exploration of the zones that gives the garage any meaning, so the above issues do impact the gameplay here, albeit indirectly.To Ironwood Studios's credit, they do give in-game options to tweak the game's parameters. You can disable car damage, disable player damage, and make other tasks easier or simpler. But why would you want to? It would just nullify the impact of many of your upgrades and make the game that much hollower.One thing that should be pointed out is the dialogue and music. The dialogue will instantly thrill any fan of Car Talk (for reasons that will be obvious to fans) and the songs on the jukebox are nothing short of fantastic. Much better that anything you are likely to hear on an actual radio. However, they do become repetitive after a while. It's about a single album's worth, and no one wants to listen to the same album for 30+ hours.There are a few issues which I feel are actual flaws, bugs, or design oversights, rather than a question of taste:• Most damningly, and the main reason I quit the game early, is that there is a game-breaking bug that completely breaks literally every single component and upgrade of your car (not "damages" but "breaks," making it necessary to replace that part entirely). All doors, all panels, all side attachments, both roof attachments, both bumper attachments, both backseat upgrades, your battery, and your engine. All of them. The breakage happened all at once: no storm in sight, and I was next to my car when it happened, so I could witness all three batteries bursting at the same time, for example. This is obviously a bug, and yes I reported it, but it was not even acknowledged by the devs, so I think they don't have the first clue how to reproduce let alone fix it. People on the forums repeat numerous other bugs that make me think the game could have used more time in the oven, but this was the most damning one, and ended the game for me.• The UI is less than intuitive, menus are occasionally buggy (Esc won't let you leave certain menus; you have to switch to a different menu and then press Esc again), and map legends are sometimes incomplete. The map system is not intuitive and is poorly explained. Some of the descriptions and dialogue are misleading or outright wrong (such as that of one of the most important bumper upgrades later in the game). The game's failure to communicate adequately with the player is a complaint that I noticed comes up repeatedly on the community forum. Many of the descriptions that get automatically added to your in-game database tell you about lore but no gameplay-specific information. This issue is subjective, but when enough people say things like "why didn't the game tell me this???" you might want to rethink things like affordances, tutorials, UI design, and/or textual content that is provided to the player.• There is a graphics bug (geometry) I encounter sometimes in the garage, but restarting the game fixes it. No biggie.• When you install a cosmetic item, subsequent items are shown in the UI as already installed, preventing you from installing more than one item at a time. The only workaround is to exit the Detailing Station and re-enter after every new installation of a cosmetic. (This is no longer an issue once everything is installed.)• About 90% of the items I collected during my play time consisted of basic building blocks: mostly metal, plastic, rubber, or cloth. Clicking on the 5–10 container objects per building to collect primarily these objects began to feel like busywork by the second map. The vapidity of the exercise reminded me of the worst aspects of Starfield and similar games. Enduring that gameplay dynamic for 30+ hours is a true test of patience.• A few other miscellaneous bugs that should have been caught during play-testing because they are easy to discover and reproduce, but this review has gone on long enough.I really wanted to like and recommend this game. It was clearly a labor of love. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend Pacific Drive in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had an absolute blast with this game! At 40 hours I've reached the end of the story but I'm still itching to get back into the zone and complete all the upgrades and finish collecting the "Mystery Podcast" style audio tapes.Some people complain that you can't save during a drive but I feel that mechanic really makes you really feel like you're going on an expedition, motivating you to prepare as much as you can. This sort of thing is my jam, preparing, risk assessing, sometimes getting out of a deep zone gate by the skin of my teeth because I got to greedy and stuck around too long, the feeling of getting back to your garage with your car just about limping.My only complaint is there isn't more of it! I'd love to see an expansion that advances the story. I feel like even though the character's stories have come to an end, when it comes to discoveries in the zone we've barely scratched the surface. Maybe an even deeper "inter dimensional" zone past The Well that needs exploring. I'd buy that!Overall I'd say if this even slightly piques your interest, go for it! You can't go wrong for the price!

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface, Pacific Drive is a cute survival game. However, it is run-based, and if you can’t complete a run in a single sitting, you won’t be able to progress. There is the option to pause the game when you’re in the menus, and it saves when you move to a new area. If you like to feel alone in survival games, Pacific Drive is also not for you, as supporting characters will talk to you very frequently. Disappointingly, about 2-4 hours in this game introduces references to racism, paedophilia, genital mutilation, self-harm and suicide. This shattered my escapism and immersion; others have complained to the developers about including such themes, and the developers have regrettably stated they’re proud to include these topics and advocate for them. The car also does not have a cup holder.

Just finished the excellent story and its all around a great game! It needs more love!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Okay... this is a weird game because the more I play it, the less I want too. So, do I recommend the game? Yes, out of the hours I have played, I think it's worth the price, if it was more expensive, I would not give it a thumps up, but it's the perfect prices for the experience.I have yet to finish the game but I think there isn't gonna be much change to the game play when I am 17 hours into the game. Short review/OverallI enjoy the game, it's worth the money but the longer you play, the more it just becomes a game about picking up stuff and not about explore cool places. I would recommend to new players, to keep pushing towards the middle and not spend hours exploring the small places to the sides, once you have been to three places, within one of the walls, you have seen most of it and scanned most of it. The Good-This game speaks to me, I am always a hoarder in videogames, and this game is perfect for me. Just let me pack the car full of stuff for no other reason that "You might need them". -The driving is good, same with how you deal with taking care of it.-Crafting, pretty good. A bit to dense for my taste, but still enjoyed it for the first 10 hours without complaint.-The voice actors are top notch, wish they were a bit more personal tho, like it feels like they are talking to a recorder and not to a person. The Bad-Everything breaks to fast, like armor, windows, tires and so on. It all breaks a lot faster than it should in my opinion. I almost fully upgraded car and yet, ♥♥♥♥ break way to easy and in the long run. It's almost cheaper to have mid tier armor and just replace it when it fully break than high tier armor.The UglyThe more you play, the less it becomes a fun exploring game and more a chore of picking up resources. There was times where I was driving and I saw a resources I needed and instead of thinking: "Ohh yes!" I just sign, stooped and picked up the resources. Once you have done it for over 15 hours, it's just boring and I wish there was a better way once you are in late game. Like I am still running around and picking up steal scrap 15 hours into the game. Feels like I should have gone past that now.

_childDocuments_.review: Many games were inspired by Roadside Picnic. The sub-genre of 'forbidden zone' stories has exploded and been influenced by the work. You can see it in this game.I've played S.T.A.L.K.E.R, metro, and I think a few others I can't remember the names of. Nothing really quite gets it. Definitely worth a read if you enjoy games like this.On the game: there is a balance between the mundane and supernatural that I don't think any of the others quite gets right. This one comes close.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: First impression: High On Life with a car. a game by and for a generation that thinks the quirkier and more chaotic the better, but with a lot of redeeming qualities.My major gripe with the game is that the graphics, user interface and overall visual experience is a chaotic, cartoony, sometimes too dark convoluted mess designed by someone whom i guess has ADHD, which requires a lot of time and effort to get used to.You can only save the game when you're at home and during checkpoints, and not on the road doing a mission. A design choice thats understandable but annoying at the same time. Even though i'm mentioning this, it shouldn't be changed because it would undermine the whole prepare-and-explore loop and allow savescumming. (If you're a entitled dad with 32 jobs and 4357 kids and can only play 3 seconds a month this simply isn't the game for you, so stop complaining about it. Last but not least,  the system requirements are too high for a game that looks and performs mediocre at best. Tested on a Nvidia 3070 @ 1440p and even with DLSS on "performance", around 55 FPS. Now for the good: It's an original, gripping and fun game to play that has the potential to go down in history as a cult hit,It has the rare ability to make you zone out and forget everything else around you, and that's a good thing.The loop of preparing, exploring, looting and upgrading your car and garage is addictive and the weirdness, excitement and amazing atmosphere really grows on you. also kudos for the soundtrack.If the devs add a few more lights to the garage, optimize the game so it also runs on non-NASA hardware and iron out the little bugs currently present, i'll raise my thumb a little higher in the air.One footnote: the first decals you get for your car are a bazillion (completely optional) woke decals, just why? Games are escapisms from a world that's getting more insane by the day. Don't put wokeism, and for that matter, any form of political agenda or activism in them.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a looter/driving roguelite that serves as the perfect example of the journey being far better than the destination. I won't spoil anything. I'll just say that you shouldn't rush this game unless you're a dedicated speedrunner. Just enjoy the drive, take good care of your ride, and don't crash. My personal biggest gripe is that several upgrades earned with late game energy points should have been unlocks for the midgame, not endgame. Most players could beat the game without maxing everything out which is too bad since some of the upgrades are fun and add lots of QoL improvements that make the regular game loop much more enjoyable overall.Special mention to the radio tunes included. Holy Mystery and Turn the Page were my personal favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: The game overall *was* really fun, but there are a lot of issues atm that considerably mitigate any fun to be has.The saving system in particular needs A LOT of work (some missions can bug out and softlock, requiring you to lose 2-3 hours of progress). The lighting system, especially on 'Medium' or 'Low' settings for Post-processing, will either be WAY too dark or WAY WAY too light, and won't really be able to make up it's mind. The RNG can be a bit brutal, but not in a way that you can learn or benefit from- just in a 'wasting your time' kind of way. Aside from that, there are a handful of bugs that haven't been sorted yet, that are either frustrating or downright game ruining (i.e., a lot of physics-based achievements like 'keep the car airborne for x amount of time' or 'go y speed in the car' will be given to you randomly in loading screens as the physics seems to bug out there, the forementioned softlocks, the map sometimes freezes the whole game and requires you to alt-F4, running in DX12 will sometimes BSOD your entire PC after about ~20 minutes of gameplay, etc. - these are just the bugs I personally have found). I personally enjoyed the game a lot, and would recommend it if it didn't have these issues. However, after the sixth run in a row that didn't count at all (about 4-5 hours down the drain) because either the game didn't save correctly, the game crashed, or the game crashed my computer, I kind of lost interest in the game and didn't want to play anymore.

_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a unique take on the survival crafting genre. Game play consists of collecting, crafting, driving and panicking. In Pacific Drive it's you and your station wagon which is the main thing keeping you alive. As you travel around looking for cars to scrap and buildings to loot things progressively devolve into chaos. Forcing you to jump in the wagon and haul arse towards a beam of light while you do your best to avoid hitting the numerous obstacles in your way.Your character is a silent protagonist much like Gordan Freeman from Half Life. Story is told by listening to some other people who are also in the zone via radio. On some occasion your radio may pick up some other interesting broadcasts. You're not quite alone because you have 3 companions to keep you company on the radio. If you have every played Firewatch, it's similar to that. I really enjoyed the voice actors work in this game. They are the driving force behind the story and they do a very good job of setting the atmosphere for this mysterious and dangerous place you've been thrown into.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game for about 5 hours now as of writing this, so beware.I discovered PD around a month ago when I accidentally stumbled upon it by pure chance from a twitter post talking about it. Considering 80's 90's era Sci-Fi and "Le driving game" in "Le Alan Wake" and "Le stalker" place I knew there was something neat under the hood. So I pre-ordered the game and as of so far I'm very positively impressed by the quality and polish of the game.The driving feels is satisfying, you can almost feel every bump, rock and pothole you drive across during expeditions into the Zone. The atmosphere and ambiance is THICC and masterfully crafted- the visual elements compliment the audio-design and vice versa. one moment you're just minding your own business, it's sunny out and overall peaceful, a gentle wind can be heard complimenting your tasks when out and about- and then in just a few short minutes a fog so thick, you could cut it with a knife sets in and the wind is gone, all you can hear is yourself, and if you're unlucky something rustling in a nearby bush or a deep bellow from just close enough to make you feel tense- and paranoid. I don't think the game is trying to be a horror game but it did scare me on numerous occasions and made me feel almost constantly paranoid that something might jump from behind me, especially after a nasty encounter with some.. tourists- you'll know what i mean when you manage to encounter them yourself if you decide to pick the game up.as for the problems, I really can't think of many? i guess the quirks system is one, but it's less the quirks fault than the Tinker machine being infuriating to work on. I get that the game want's to make the player feel connected to the car, but why can't i get my guess if what i'm seeing and thinking is the correct answer gives me only 1/2 correct guesses but then kicks me in my ass when i get the other 2 guesses wrong. it's so hyper-specific. Why can't a specific quirk have multiple correct answers? sure it makes the game easier, but I shouldn't be picking up more quirks each time i go on an expedition only to be unable to correctly diagnose the quirk when i think it's what's happening. in short, the car is haunted but the machine to fix it is total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and is pretty much like gambling. and you only get 6 tries before the machine boots you out of making anymore. I'd get having limited tries if the machine could already automatically do some of the guesswork for you, and it can, but only with an upgrade which you have to grind for and SURPRISE you need to go out INTO THE ZONE with your QUIRK and run the chance of getting ANOTHER QUIRK when go out to gather resources to upgrade the damn machine. In short, apart from personal PC specs not running the game as smoothly as I want it to run, that is my only criticism at the game.Now, as far as launch goes, PD has had a really good launch so far- but not without some controversy. In the game you can build a customization station which let's you store stickers and other little doodads you collect on your expeditions on the zone to customize your car. now AFAIK (since I haven't unlocked it yet) it comes with LGBTQ+ related material like pride stickers and whatnot. For something so relatively harmless people seem to have cooked up a hailstorm on the forums ranging from "why is there gay things in MY video game!!" to "THE DEVS ARE GAY GLOBALIST COMMIES WHO EAT CHILDREN" (I'm not exaggerating).In short, Personally I don't think it's a big deal, a little immersion breaking since, the game takes place in 1998 when gay-culture was relatively under-the-radar and not so prominent as it is today. but overall I'm not against it, just a heads up so that anyone that might be sensitive to such topics don't get whiplash from it.Inclusivity is a genuinely difficult subject to discuss as it is one of those topics that someone will inevitably take close to heart. whether you're against it or for it. To me, having anything to do with pride feels mostly like a checkbox, like those stereotypically gay people you see in media, which are horrible representations of gay people, and the only people that do find them remotely appealing are specifically those same people that behave as if being gay is a personality trait. Either way, if you don't like anything remotely to do with that sort of stuff then don't get this game, though I do think it would be a shame if you choose not to specifically for that reason. if you choose to interact on the forums for PD then- please don't bring up the topic, people have made enough noise about it already and it's taking away from actual discussions about the game with people going back and forth making ad hominem, antagonizing arguments or genuine insulting without any kind of sane contributions to the discussion. There is place to criticize the game but making a big point about the flags and how "you don't like them" or "you don't like the people not liking the flags" subtracts away from more important conversations.either way great game, a hard 9/10. has some performance issues (but that just might be on my end) and the tinker machine is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but the Driving, Vibe and Atmosphere make up for all of it's issues.

Hood started opening every time I was reversing, thought it's another dumb bug. Realized after ~2 hours that hood thingy was actually something that can happen. Now I'm not certain that visual artifacts weren't intended...Way to gaslight me, game. Well played!UPD: Hahahaha, screw you game! I spent like 7 hours thinking that radio is wonky, just to realize it randomly changed volume when I turned left and that was intentional. I genuinely feel like I'm going insane, because EVERYTHING that happens in the game does something weird, so I never know when it's just a temporary effect, or something I have to actively fix!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Looks good- Has spooky atmosphere (although nothing actually spooky is happening)- High production value (graphics, UI)- Has accessibility features (which help to mitigate some of the shortcomings of the game).Cons:- Boring. Oh my god this game is boring- And annoying. I never played a more annoying game. - You drive in a slow and hard to manouver car, every 50 meters or so there is an obstacle on the road which you have to drive around, avoiding trees on the side of the road. From time to time you stop at a cabin or shipping container sized "lab" and loot the chests and lockers in there for resources. (Feels nice for about 30 minutes and tedious afterwards.)- Don't forget to put your car in park *every single time* otherwise it rolls away. Also don't foget to put it back in drive when you return. There is an achievement for when you forget to put the car in drive for the 20th time. Because you will. And it's not fun. (After some 15 hours of gameplay you can research an upgrade that will automatically put the car in park when you get out.)- The "enemeis" in this game are called "anomalies", which for example are bollards that come up from the ground every 10 seconds or so and my flip your car if you happen to be on their spot. Yes, this is the kind of enemies we are talking about. Other anoamlies are swirling things that controls your car for 10 seconds or so (and usually drives it into a tree) if you drive into them. Or there is an abduction thing that pulls up your car and usually rams it into a tree. And so on. The challenge is to drive around those menaces. If you get caught in or by one of them the only consequence is that your car may get damaged. Which you will later repair in your garage. But there is no proper (i.e. fun) repair mechanic.- There is some Fortnite-like border thingy that after some minutes closes in on you, damaging your car if it reaches you. You have to hurry to some exit point, which may be far away and not reachable in time. If you don't manage to do this your car will be destroyed. Or you will die, which essentially damages your car and removes most of your collected resources. (Always a fun mechanic.). Neither repairing nor collecting resources is a fun mechanic for some weird reason. You can also trigger this Fortnite-thingy yourself. Escaping your death is the only exciting thing about this game. "Exciting". Not fun, though. This mechanic is also annoying as f... Am I emphasizing enough how annoying this game is?- And, my god, this game is dark. It is dark dark. Have you ever played a dark game? Make it two times darker and you have Pacific Drive. This game looks nice for 10% of the time when there is daylight, the rest of the time it's nighttime and you see nothing. And it rains a lot, oftentimes combined with a nice thunderstorm. Ever drove your car at night during a thunderstorm? Then you know how annoying this is. Welcome to 50% of the driving part of the game.- You want to see something at night during a storm and want to turn on your car's light?! Tough luck. It drains your battery, which lasts for 10 minutes or so. You may(!) find some recharching station, but probably not. Not sure what happens if you run out of battery. But as starting your car also uses battery power I guess you will no longer be able to start your car. (You can build a starter cable, though, which will probably help.)- You have to find "power orbs" to be able to leave an area, which also acts as research points, which can be used to upgrade your car or garage. Actually the most fun part of the game. The upgrade meachnic. Not the power orb collection mechanic, of course. To collect orbs you get out of your car, walk to an orb, the game then triggers some "danger", like electrical sparks or pollars or radioactivity or something, which you avoid but directly running back to your car without looking back. You don't even have to avoid this stuff. In short: You run to the orb in a straight line, take it and run straight back to your car. That's it. Fun gameplay. Not.- And, wow, this game is underexplained. There are a lot of edgy texts for all kind of items or "anomalies" which however do not explain what they are and what they do. Take for example this "power orbs are used to leave the level AND as resource for research"? The first part is kind of explained in the game, the latter is not. I have never had to search the web this much to understand how a game works, because it explains basically nothing ingame.- I could go on, but everything else was probably said already in a thousand other negative reviews.- If you consider buying this game *please* watch a gameplay video and realize that this game is boring and annoying before wasting your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying the game so far. When you go on a run with thick fog that could make you think you're entering Silent Hill or a dark night with loads of tourist anomalies, the game hits just right in terms of atmosphere. Only just started working on getting blueprints and manufacturing improvements to my gear and car and I will say the game could've explained that portion just a bit better. If you like to just go through menus though I'm sure you'll find everything quickly enough, and there are enough unlock trees to draw me in just to see what my car and gear will look like in the long run. Performance has been great on my almost six year old machine at this point so I can't speak for others claiming performance issues. Only real complaint I have is the same as most of the negative reviews about the lack of a save function mid-run through the zone, but at least so far every run has been about 30-45 minutes max so I don't find it too bad so far. Difficulty has also not really been an issue. As long as you stay aware of your surroundings it is fairly easy to avoid enemies and harm, minus the occasional shifting environmental damage.TLDR: So far a personal 8/10 that I can see going higher or lower depending on how the story and later locations feel to me as well as hopefully patching in at the very least an exit save function mid-run.
