_childDocuments_.review: So the skeleton of Pacific Drive is survival-crafting games ala Grounded, The Forest, Minecraft, and so on. You wander around and get resources and use the resources to make a bigger backpack and ♥♥♥♥. It distinguishes itself from its peers in two ways:  1.  By emphasizing environmental hazards 2. Formalizing the base->expedition loop. Every Pacific Drive expedition ends with you arriving back at the Garage, where you can refuel and recharge for free, and conduct repairs and upgrades in peace. Then you venture out into procedurally generated levels in the Zone full of roguelike modifiers. Then it's a race against time both in an economic sense (Fuel, HP, and battery will typically dwindle as you explore) and in a literal sense (Each area has a timer after which it becomes uninhabitable and you must flee.) Many hazards are variations on a simple setup: A small, easily visible zone of pain. Bubbling pools of acid or lightning in the middle of the road that you'll want to drive around. A few are more mobile, or actively seek the player. All of them serve primarily to apply pressure or exacerbate each other- If you're fleeing a storm of deadly acid rain at 60 mph, you're going to struggle to weave between obstacles, and if you pop a flat tire, you're going to struggle to outrun the storm. Overall, it's a very thoughtfully constructed game that's an absolute delight to play!

_childDocuments_.review: The description of this game and it's tags do not completely hammer home that this is a rougelike (lite?). You will collect resources, gather information and upgrade your car as the main game loop. If you are a fan of rougelikes, then this is a great game for you. The survival aspects vary by the map, its modifiers, and its depth in the zone. Some maps are a cake walk, others have you on your toes, and others will put you through the meat grinder. The basic menu, icons and general UI did take some getting used to, but I was able to eventually figure out how to navigate menus and find out how to unlock the various upgrades. If you buy, take time to learn the menus and displays, especially the in-car display of health and damaged parts when you are driving. The in-game radio music is amazing and very atmospheric, but is also limited. I find the same songs coming on quite often. Great songs though!The voice acting is well done and made me feel like I had people rooting for me and trying to explain the world to me. Each voice acted character is integral to the story and I found myself excited anytime one of them spoke through my radio or headset. Environmental sound design is the highlight of this game for me mainly because you are out in the forest completely alone. But what's that distant siren? Did I hear an abductor? And why did it sound like something was moving in the trees right next to me? All these questions and more will freak you out and prompt you to stay close to your car. It's your best form of protection and escape. It's also important to note the crazy amount of customization options to make the game easier or harder on yourself. While I have not changed any of the customization to make it easier to survive, I did set lootable items to the maximum highlight, and made nights brighter. I find both make the experience more positive and stop me from stumbling blindly through maps like I am wasting my time. And it should be noted that neither of those settings make the in-game light sources useless. Headlights, floodlights, flares and lamps are still necessary at certain points. Overall a great game for a great price. I still haven't finished the story and don't plan to anytime soon!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely happy with my purchase, I've sunken many hours into not only finishing the story, but also doing a completionist run after the fact. The characters are amazingly well written and not once was I hoping for anyone in particular to stop talking. In fact with the solitude you get used to in this game, I was hoping the characters interacted with me more. I only had two things that I wished were in the game, and they recently just added one of them with the most recent update, Functionality for custom audio tracks to play in the radios, so any file you may want to listen to in-game can simply be put into a directory under AppData and it'll be played.Truly the only other thing that I wish this game had was VR support, it's the perfect game for it, as it's atmosphere and "feel" (Especially with the great audio work done) would've been immaculate in a true "first person."

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a creative game, which blends some novel action and RPG elements in a way that don't seem overly derivative. As other reviews have noted, the 'portal back to home base' sequence manages to really grab you every time and the game's visuals are well done. The only real issue is the difficulty balancing at mid-game, when your car is essentially broken or on the verge of giving out almost the whole time. I think the devs thought this would add an element of suspense and force players to be careful but it ends up being mostly tedious because the way that saves and mission structures are setup is that as soon as you head out, you don't have the option to head home to refit and such, you either make it by the skin of your teeth or you "die" and lose basically everything.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe this game in terms of comps, I'd say it's like if STALKER and Jalopy had a kid, and then that kid watched a lot of Gravity Falls.  It's got a lot of creativity in it, a lot of cool ideas, and there are moments when the visuals are absurdly cool in a way that other games just don't give you.Also, the mechanics aren't too stressful, and the process of meticulously looting, driving, and then retrofitting your car back at the garage, kind becomes a very zen loop.  I like it.That said, I think the ending of this game is the most disappointed I've been with a story in a while.  It's not even BAD, it just... ends two missions before it should, it feels like?  But if the worst I can say about a game is that I wish there was more of it, it's probably not that bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool idea, a combat-less looter raid game (PG Stalker) but most of the game feels very artificially controlled/managed by the AI in a bad way. Successfully navigate the wasteland and got your car through the world with minimal damage? Here's a homing speed rabbit that launches you off a cliff with no way to avoid damage. And now that you've lost everything, here's some "random" gear and spawns that will get you back on the path. Dying and losing all your stuff feels completely separate to any of your decisions, the same way that pulling off a run successfully with lots of loot also lacks any sense of achievement. Leaving my car far from any anomalies while i harvest materials to repair the vehicle, only to have random spawns rip off my panels/door, scatter my possessions and flip my car doesn't feel like "this is a skill issue I need to improve on in the future", it's just the game stripping any reward from playing safely... just because.The crafting/looting has some creativity, the radio characters will grow on you, and the soundtrack is decent, but the biggest sin seems to be the serious lack of speed while driving.The racing aspect shown in the trailer really only happens the last 60 seconds of a level, most of the time you are either carefully navigating 10ft hitbox electricity bands/acid balls or moving your car from house to house because the resources you actually need to lot are behind 2 locked doors. Something that chases you (the abductors move 3 times as fast as you and give up after 20 feet, playing stealth red-light/green-light is not fun behind the wheel) would have really added something because at the end of the day I'm on the brakes (or trapped in a character animation) more than the gas.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and unique game, Need more games like this that get out of the mainstream mold.Only downside is you only have one car. Would have been fun to have small Jeep or other cars to unlock over time, Mayby have multiple space in a parking lot to store cars. Anyway, still a great game TBH and plenty to keep you busy!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This perfectly represents what is is like to drive around in Washington, I should know I live there. The only things it is missing is the little reflective turtles on our roads for when the rain completely obscures your vision and the rain that completely obscures your vision! Other than that this game nailed how it feels to drive 30 minutes to town to go grocery shopping.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, unique experience that has a perfect balance of tension, frustration and calm.It has an interesting story, great art style, fantastic sound design, VA, music, and most importantly;  Fun gameplay.This type of game isn't usually my go to, but this was fantastic. Cannot recommend it enough. My only gripe is the UI is a bit janky and takes some getting used to. By the end though, you'll be using it with muscle memory.Also please give auto-handbrake its own slot. Please. Please, I beg you Ironwood.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I don't love it.This isn't terrible at all. The graphics are nice, the story is coming from a good place and most of the bits and bobs of a decent game are there. But I found it pretty boring and the gameplay loop isn't fun for me. Doing a half hour mission only for random occurrences to destroy most of your car (again) only so you can fix it up (again) just wasn't fun for me and most of the car "upgrades" I installed broke just as easily as the previous ones I had. The game just feels very indifferent to your enjoyment.A good idea but just rather unsatisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun! The world building is super fun, and the rogue-like in a car is super fun. It's sort of like Jalopy, but really well done. It's a little like The Long Drive, except it's actually game lol.You don't need to know anything about cars to play this game, it's a super fun scavenge and craft game, with some really unique and fun mechanics. Honestly, this is the first fun and unique game I've seen in years.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Interested in anomalies, beautiful and strange scenery, exploring the unknown and roaming trough abandoned places for scraps like some raccoon while driving your dumpster wagon with your precious loot off a cliff because the car decided to take a wild ride with you behind the wheel praying for your life?10/10 would recommendGood story, Progression with character and a car with personality.Music is atmospheric and well made.& no AAA-studio BS, just a good game to enjoy or fight the anomalies.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Really wish I can give it a thumbs up, I really do, but the game performance is so bad, the everything is choppy when looking around, walking and driving even tho I am getting around 90-110fps doesn't seem to be smooth at all. _childDocuments_.user: Esti de porte lourde du calisse
_childDocuments_.review: This game throws you into a zone where strange phenomena occurs and you have to cruise your way out one mission area at a time. During missions you scavenge for resources and use them to craft tools, car parts and other materials to upgrade your garage once you make it back. The loop is simple but satisfying with great risk/rewards for venturing long periods of times in your mission areas.The atmosphere is very eerie. Strange sound occurs all the time with some being cues for dangers incoming sending chills down your spine. At night it gets very dark, and a light source is needed to find your way forward. The game's ost is very good at setting the tone of mystery and of... "Haul ass outta there". There's also a unique radio music track with some of them not only being very fitting with the game atmosphere but are also some very good piece of music ("Conjuring Hell" by Smokey Brights and "Train Song" by Ilene Dracott)The story hasn't got to me yet but the voice acting is very good.I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes rogue-likes/lite, Stalker and the "Roadside Picnic" book. I think you'd feel at home playing this game. It's also very cheap and i think its worth grabbing and give it a shot
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: So, I finished the game, and I really enjoyed it. It was very interesting to explore and drive through the zone with good music and a perfect atmosphere. I do recommend this game a lot. It has a unique feel, and the gameplay feels like something new!Forty-three hours of enjoyable gameplay, and all the achievements unlocked.

The game has about 10ish PRO LGBTQ?!? flags/stickers, BLM flag/stickers yet, has no country flags/stickers which is divisive. if you can over look the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.... Great concept, Fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the game for about 12 hours now and DAMN does it live up to my expectations. When I first saw the trailer for the game I was convinced I had to get a PS5, this game was almost going to be the sole cause for me to get the console because I thought it was an exclusive. I've always had a soft spot for sh*tboxes, This was probably THE reason I was so excited about the game. The moment I stepped into the demo,I fell in love with our lovely wagon.  There can't be a better choice for navigating the post-apocalyptic landscape, especially in a survival-looter game. Design of the car? it's absolutely spot-on. You can almost feel the soul of that little old car as it chugs along. Quirks mechanic also add so much character, making it one of the standout mechanics I've encountered in the recent games i've played. Diagnosing and having the option to fix them is great. The driving experience is smooth as butter, and it manages to feel smooth without feeling "heavy".  I would love to have the option to have a manual transmission tho (i know it would probably suck while scavenging).The upgrade and crafting mechanics are quite satisfying. It feels unbelievable building up your vehicle. Stumbling upon higher-tier parts from scavenged vehicles earlier than you're supposed to just adds more to that feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a gem. The atmosphere is amazing. The environments are varied. The story/voiceovers are expertly done. It's a joy to drive around listening to the game's radio and do your thing.The main gameplay loop is go on runs and gather stuff you need while avoiding anomalies and other dangers. You'll gather a lot of resources and craft and upgrade stuff. Runs can take from 20 minutes to an hour or even more, depending on how many zones you visit and how much time you spend on each zone gather stuff. The game is pretty forgiving. It autosaves when you first enter a zone/map, so you can't save mid-zone and continue.If you enjoy exploration, driving and that resource gathering-crafting-upgrading loop, you'll love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into survival games with a heavy dose of mystery and tension, Pacific Drive is definitely worth a spin. Later trips in the game require some planning ahead, especially when combining car upgrades to handle what you're about to face. The grind is moderate compared to other survival games, it was enough to keep me engaged without being overwhelming. Plus, the story is pretty cool, with lots of mysterious elements you uncover as you explore, adding depth to the eerie, atmospheric world.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: The game runs smooth as butter, and cruising around was a blast. But man, when I hit that last zone, I couldn't help but feel like I hit a speed bump.Like, don't get me wrong, they hyped up this last area big time, making it sound like the ultimate challenge. But when I got there, it was like, "That's it?" The missions were few and far between, and it felt like they ran out of gas on the budget or something.And the ending? Pfft, talk about a letdown. It was like they took a page out of the "Lost" playbook, leaving me scratching my head more than feeling satisfied. I mean, come on, throw us a bone here! I wanted closure, not more questions.But hey, despite the bumpy finish, I still had a good time with Pacific Drive. It's like cruising down a scenic route with a few potholes along the way. So yeah, if you're down for a laid-back ride with a few bumps in the road, give it a spin. Just don't expect the last stretch to be as thrilling as the rest of the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much. I think partly it's just one of those thing where the concept is incredibly appealing to me personally. But it's also just such a well put together experience in every way. The car building is very tactile and feels great, even something like how you swap out parts and repair them feels tactile and it's obvious a lot of thought has been put down into small details like this. The UI design is so consistent and commited to this beautiful 8-bit style, it really reminds me of industrial computers and car diagnosis tools. (which is probably what they were going for)The world i beautiful, the textures might be considered "low fidelity" but they are deliberately made in this kind of "oil-painting" dishonored style which looks great. The voice acting is great! And i think the actors did a great job. Regarding the world structure, how it's hub based with some randomization over an open world. This is something other people have critizised, and while i kind of agree. I do think that the run based gameplay is actually quite fun, and like everything else in this game it meshes very well with all the rest of the gameplay elements. However yes, i would still have preferred an open world. However i'm guessing that a run based game is a lot less resource intensive to create, and an open world might have been too ambitious. Maybe this is something for the sequel which i so desperately hope they will make.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is an enjoyable nice fusion of Car Mechanic Simulator, Interstate 76, Fallout and Stalker. I like fiddling with the car and looting abandoned villages, and I also like that the interface is fiddly. There's a nice feeling of mild panic as you run back to your car when an anomaly storm is coming in, and you're frantically trying to turn the key and slam it into gear.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 3 days and finished it in 29.4 hours of playtime and lemme tell you that this game is the most average, average game I have played in a while...This review contains no spoilers!If you are strapped for time, go to the bottom and read the conclusionPros. - Amazing artwork and aesthetics in-game, It really captures the 1980~ period of time the game is trying (I think) to be set in. - Decent car driving mechanics with upgrades and add-ons being very noticeable. Traction and how the car feels when driving around is pretty good.- Great game atmosphere and weather mechanics really make the game-play experience so immersive. - Lots of car customization (both aesthetically and mechanically) making the car really feel like your own- The true feeling of panic when things are going wrong (and trust me, they will go wrong fast if u are not careful)- Great game world and enemy/creature design (except for the Tourists, I f***ing hate their mechanics but I think that is more my personal opinion) which really adds to the immersion and strangeness of the Olympic Exclusion Zone- Likeable narrated "main" characters- Fun driving on straight(er) clear stretches of road- Inventory management is complex and forces you to think when putting stuff in your backpack or in your car when scavenging.Cons. (this game could have been so so SO good)- Bugs, There are a bunch of bugs, both small and very large such as:  - Certain objects (rocks and other junk) spawning inside loot like anchors.  - Being able to clip through walls  - The final mission bugged out on me and forced me to complete it twice to "finish" the game. Once with   dialog, once without...- The driving. There are also some large issues with driving. Your car can be fast in this game, you can even put nitro (a boost) on your car to speed it up much much more BUT, each time I drive I ask "why should I go fast?" In this game, your car has a health bar, determined by the health of all the body panels on your car. The problem is that the panels take damage when you hit something (very realistic I know!). The problem is that there is so much garbage (rocks, landslides, wreck piles, etc.) blocking (like fully blocking) the road that going fast means that your going to slide and damage your car, meaning that you intern will have to repair your car and may die when on a drive. There are ramps and boosted ramps, but there is little reason to use them (unless there is no other way forward) because when you land, the car is very difficult to control meaning that you will crash, and because your car's suspension is not stiff enough, your cars front will always end up taking damage.The part I do like is towards the end of the game. The last sector has few of these obstructions allowing for faster speed driving, and the obstructions only partially cover the road or drive-able areas making me feel really good swerving and weaving between them.- Your car needs so dam many repairs with your wheels popping every 4 feet (towards the later zones) and needing so much repair putty or blowtorches (which are really expensive material wise) that micromanaging your cars repairs and supplies to repair your car start becoming extremely essential in the start and middle of the game.- The story. I found the story a little bit difficult to understand and a bit shallow. All the story missions entail you driving to Pos A or just flipping a switch or just driving around to certain locations. The ending also kinda sucks with a lot of running, except for the driving part which is really good but maybe could have been a bit longer and used some improvements. - Kinda strange overall map mechanic with junctions skipping over the "Walls"- Pretty bad looting system. Loot and supplies only spawns in 4~ places, Inside boxes or locked containers, scrapped items inside buildings, out of dead enemies and small nodes/boxes out in the landscape. This is not great, It means that when you enter a building, the only things you are looking for are things to scrap (like electronics) and boxes. There is no loose loot or anything hidden in the corner of the room(beyond maybe a box thats behind a bathroom door) for you to grab. This makes looting feel extremely repetitive and boring once u have done it a bunch.- The characters on the radio feel very detached from the story and feel very distant. There are 2 points in the game I felt that my actions really impacted the people guiding you on the radio and even then, it still felt like it didn't have the impact it deservedREAD THIS FOR TLDR REVIEW!! <----------------------------In conclusion:Overall, I feel like this game is lacking something. Its almost a great game, but isn't quite there yet. The game has good driving mechanics but feels like it doesn't want you to use them to their fullest potential. The game has decent looting mechanics but they get really boring after figuring out there are no secrets or hidden items. The characters also feel distant when you hear them asking you to do things. Overall I feel this game has some amazing ideas and features but implemented them without their strengths. With the game like this, I cannot whole heartily recommend this game to a friendAlso please let us close the garage door!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

Do you just like working on cars and unlocking a tech tree? Maybe you like gazing upon anomalies?  How about taking in some  levels of radiation? _childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good! Enjoying it a lot. Had one bug so far - don't use an anchor before they tell you to.Atmospheric, lots of upgrades, should be good to play for a while.Beware - you cannot save when you go out on a run. Its extraction shooter-y in that you need to leave with your gear or you won't get any loot. Some of the story missions are quite long though. Builds some great suspense, but make sure you have time when you head out.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, my experience with this game was lukewarm at best. The storyline took its time to unfold, which didn't bother me much as I was more interested in the driving and car customization aspects. The real excitement kicked in with the open-world exploration for scrapping and gathering materials. However, upon returning to my base loaded with hundreds of metal pieces, I found the game lacking in what to do with my haul. This was a letdown until I progressed further in the story and unlocked more of the crafting menu, which significantly enhanced my gameplay experience. Fixing up my car and seeing my progress became immensely satisfying. I'll admit, there was a moment around the two-hour mark where I nearly gave up on the game entirely. Yet, I persisted, and I'm thankful I did. This game turned out to be a unique and rewarding experience, blending slow progression and seemingly mundane tasks into something special. If you have the patience for gradual development and enjoy simple pleasures in gaming, this title might just be up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's a very solid, cohesive single-player experience.My biggest critique is that the mini-game of "zone-weirdness or visual glitch" does get old when you have to re-load your save 3 times because the garage has a new concrete floor that is 4 feet higher than the regular floor. This doesn't happen every time, and I have yet to have my gameplay impacted by visual glitches.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Fully finished the game, and whoa boy was that an experience. I loved the game from start to finish, even if there were some elements that were rough around the edges. Menu management with a controller is rough, and the UI has some parts that aren't as clear as they should be (I lost 2 hours of progress to the darn vacuum!) But really, I can't recommend this game enough. The soundtrack fits the vibe, the visuals are spot on for the feel of the game, the voice acting is all great, and just the story too... Something you wouldn't expect with a game like this, at all, but there it is and it hits hard. The ending in particular, the last 3rd overall, is just incredible. I loved it start to finish and will likely come back to play more of it further on down the road. Rare a game nowadays leaves me craving more after over 40 hours, but this one left me wanting a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a really good game. It's really well made and the art style is gorgeous! I didn't like the car quirks as in my opinion the car should be a reliable safe haven amidst the eerie, spooky landscape but, that being said they do give you the option to turn those off and I enjoyed the game far more with that feature being disabled. The outer zone is my favourite as tbh, the mid and deep zones become too chaotic to reliably park up anywhere and scavenge anything without be messed with by anomalies which in my opinion could maybe use more balancing? The anomalies can actually be quite annoying and can be far too much when they all pile on top of each other in zone 2 and 3. Like actual fists of frustration form beyond zone one haha. The work these guys have put into driving/maintaining the car though really is top tier. I wonder if I would've liked the game more as a whole if you drove about investigating anomalies, uncovering an unravelling paranormal mystery Outer Wilds style with survival/crafting mechanics as opposed to constantly battling with the environments. I would've like more peace to really take in the visuals of a world expertly crafted by the team. Anyways 6.5 - 7/10 for me, worth a go but maybe on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Roadside Picnic and The Southern Reach Trilogy I am way, way into this game.  It's all about the atmosphere and the lore. You like all those things, you'll probably like this game.Edit: Completed the main story and my love for the game has only increased. The soundtrack is top notch. The voice acting is very well done and effective. The lore satiates my curiosity enough to where I enjoy making connections and theories that aren't necessarily all there - and that is definitely a big plus for me in and of itself. If there is one thing I'm disappointed about with Pacific Drive it is the complete lack of living creatures/anomalies, even just in the background. No Bigfoot or mutant raccoons or the Grey Thing from peoples' dreams. Would have at least been nice to see things like tracks or things peeking around distant corners or up in trees.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: The little touches are what really shine in this game. Ex, your car has the potential to pick up little quirks, like when you activate the wipers, it also wipes the fuel gauge back and forth, or turning on the dome light every time you open a door. All the quirks are fixable but they really give the game character.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the most unique survival/crafting game I've ever played. Combining a super interesting story with a very unique spin to the crafting genre by putting all your efforts into one singular thing (a car) instead of your full base or buildings was a stroke of genius. This game is hitting all the right buttons for me, and I cannot wait to play more. Survival game fans, LOOK HERE.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game does a great job when it comes to art and environment. Its not to the level of Subnautica which disappoints me, but to me it makes it worth recommending. It was a fun 24 hours to beat the game, but I don't see any reason to do it again or continue. But to be honest, most of the game is just average or slightly above average. If you are expecting something revolutionary, you will be disappointed. I was hoping for more unique anomalies and meaningful upgrades for my car. The type of game where you explore new things and get surprised by them, but instead it felt like I was encountering the same things and the upgrades were pointless. I would have loved to customize more, but your paint and decals don't tend to stay when you destroy your parts or swap them out.I feel largely what the game needs is more resource sinks that isn't your car. By the time you beat the game, you may not even have the great stuff for your car. So at the point near beating the game you have to ask yourself if its worth grinding late game resources for upgrades you realistically don't need but would be really nice to have. Would have loved a better engine but never could have afforded it. Same with upgrades to repairing.In short, this is a complete experience from start to end, but don't expect anything grand content-wise like Celeste or Hollow Knight. Its gameplay is average and its story is average, but its art really carries it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: each mission can take hours (you will want to explore and gather as much as possible) but you can't save mid mission, and the default setting for quitting mid mission is to lose the items you gathered and suffer car damage (alternate setting just sends you back to your base without damage)they will probably fix that in a future patch, so wait for thatI would have loved the game if not for that
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game was good, but not great. I was looking for something to fill the void left by The Outer Wilds, this game did not fill that void. Nonetheless, this game does absolutely nail some aspects, primarily the driving experience. The sound of rain on the car roof is so well done it gives me chills every time. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Although there was some frustration at the beginning, I ended up having a pretty good time with this one. Story is interesting, the characters are well acted, and the areas are cool (especially the ones deeper in the Zone). A lot of the game's systems are not explained, you have to learn by experiencing them. Not too bad when spaced out, but if you progress too fast early on it can be annoying, so slow down and enjoy the ride (until the zone storm spawns, then get the hell out of there!)
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:This game has issues. IF you want a smooth game with great driving mechanics and a cozy feel of driving between adrenaline boosting sci-fantasy storms, look elsewhere.Average time to complete a run with two areas while collecting most of the items in the map is over an hour. This is extremely long. Loot can just disappear from your car. Particular early game pieces of loot, ceramics in particular are extremely rare. Ceramics are used to repair your car. So, you had better not be a new player who isn't good at the game yet. Two runs, each with three stops, three of the six stops were "rich". I got 10 ceramics. That was in total. It took me over four hours and I ended the run with less ceramics than I had started. (Dumpster pearls are the best way to get ceramics. One game me 8 ceramics!)The main problem with the game is the vibe/feel of driving. It doesn't "feel" good to me. It is not one thing, it's the package. How would I improve the vibe? Instead of instantly teleporting to a stop, have a long relatively straight highway with almost no points of interest. I want to spend time driving in a game based around a car. Instead, I feel like the car is fighting me at every turn.Looking back at my original review, I highlighted the tutorial, JUST driving through Washington was GREAT! You can teleport back to the garage through the glowing pillars, sure. I don't mind, that's fine. Every moment that I'm in my car, I'm looking for POI that will take me out of my car; instead, give me 2~5 minutes of JUST driving per run, compress the maps a little so that instead of 25-30 minutes to clear a single stop run, I am instead spending ~20 minutes per stop. There are other problems, anomalies have weird hit boxes. Some have hit boxes that are insanely small. Driving beneath them does not trigger them. While others have hit boxes which are 1.5~2.5x their visual size. Lightning transformers will follow you for an oddly long distance. continuing to appear beneath your car. Spike traps have a near perfect depiction to their hit area. (Still bugged. I ran over a spike trap with my right wheels, both were punctured. When I got out of the car, My front let wheel was punctured, the right wheels were no longer punctured.) Original Review:This game started well, the tutorial was great! I really loved the initial moments of the game, driving was fun, the sound and rain were both great!Having to hold R2 for 3 seconds is annoying when you are trying to scrap multiple objects.Things went downhill at the end of the first mission. The game does not explain things well. I was told to collect a glowing orange orb. I did that. Set it up, and the game just decided that it didn't want to work. Had to abandon the trip. Repeated the mission. Now, it says drive into the portal, provides you with a waypoint on the map, and sends you off. I went to the waypoint, but that was not the correct location, so I died. Honestly, losing an entire hour of progress because of a poorly designed game is annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I took out my AMP engine, finally replaced it with LIM-Chipped engine, closed the hood. Blowtorched everything, checked that nothing is worn and that mural decals look amazing on her. Checked everything one more time. I think I've read enough flavour text pieces about tardigrades, collected enough stickers and chose the best bartender decoration. I think I experienced enough of Peninsula and I need to rest. I think I finished this game. I checked everything again, blowtorched everything, recharged her and quit, knowing I'm leaving her for a while. I cried a little that evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Exploring Pacific Drive: A Thrilling Adventure GamePacific Drive is an exhilarating adventure game that takes players on a captivating journey through stunning landscapes and challenging obstacles. With its immersive gameplay and breathtaking visuals, Pacific Drive offers an unparalleled gaming experience that keeps players engaged for hours on end. In this article, we delve into the world of Pacific Drive, exploring its key features, gameplay mechanics, and what sets it apart from other adventure games.Unveiling the World of Pacific DrivePacific Drive transports players to a mesmerizing world filled with lush forests, treacherous mountains, and mysterious caves. The game's stunning graphics and attention to detail create a truly immersive environment, allowing players to feel fully immersed in the game's world. As players navigate through the diverse landscapes, they encounter a myriad of challenges and puzzles that test their skills and wit, keeping them on the edge of their seats throughout the game.Engaging Gameplay MechanicsOne of the standout features of Pacific Drive is its dynamic gameplay mechanics. The game seamlessly integrates platforming, puzzle-solving, and exploration, offering a well-rounded gaming experience that caters to a wide range of players.The game's intuitive controls and responsive mechanics ensure that players can navigate through the terrain with precision and fluidity, enhancing the overall gaming experience. _childDocuments_.review: "Local man infiltrates the Exclusion zone, steals a car and squats at a mechanic shop filled with illegal and questionable machinery. Local man now known as "Driver" drives the stolen car throughout the Exclusion zone stealing and breaking Government property to mod his already illegal car into a health hazard on wheels and somehow survives all the Deadly anomalies that has killed countless Government officials. Intercepted Radio chatter coming from the Zone indicates that the Driver is recieving instructions from known conspiracy nuts, more as the situation develops."Pacific drive isnt a game for everyone, if you enjoyed the gameplay loop of Jalopy then this game will be up in your alley so to speak, but in short all you do is, built parts, drive, fart and scrap stuff for materials. And no you dont have your uncle to keep your company, but you do have a radio. NOTE THAT I HAVENT COMPLETED THE GAME YET.The levels are beutifully crafted with hazards that will mess your car up if you cant dodge them, the game isnt an "open world" but is divided up into large levels you have to traverse with your blinged out car, scattered throughout the levels are houses and car wrecks which you can loot and which you can scrap parts to gain material.The car you stole can be upgraded from a hunk of junk on wheels to an armored beast that'll make most militias and third world militaries jelous, with fun gadgets you can install. like a wind generator that powers your batteries mounted on a side rack, or storage unit for more stolen property and junk. You can also customize the paint and add small things like that tree thing you hang on your backview mirror to make the car smell nice.Driving feels really good and i love the small things you can interact with like park brake and keys for the first person view of the drivers seat. countless times have i forgotten to unlock the parking brake after i've hoppen in or to put the car into park when looking at my huge GPS.Checkpoints and saves are HORRIBLE, ATLEAST PUT A SAVE ON LEVEL TRANSITIONS. As it is right now, you can only save at the mechanic shop, making long drives a risk of wasted time if something would happen, if youre willing to play this game then clear your schedule and plan your playtime, because when you're out in the zone you cant save.I hope to see more content for this game in the future, if there is anything planned.

_childDocuments_.review: Where is my drive?The game is advertised as a driving game with survival elements and some scavenging for car upgrades. Even the game's name suggests a strong focus on driving.However, in reality, driving makes up the smallest part of the gameplay. The player spends 90% of the time ON FOOT, gathering resources or building car parts in the garage. The free driving through the Zone, as shown in the trailers, is impossible because the game world consists of multiple very small maps, densely packed with points of interest and scattered resources. You need to scavenge a lot of resources to progress in the game. Instead of DRIVING between these tiny maps, you actually fast-travel. The car is essentially just a backpack on wheels that requires constant maintenance.There's also no free saving system, not even a Save+Exit option. In 2024!Pros: On ultra settings, the visuals are stunning, and the atmosphere of the Zone is very immersive. The sound design is excellent too!Cons: Everything else.Refund requested.

_childDocuments_.review: If $10-$15, I'd recommend trying it. I would not buy at full price.The first 10 or so hours of the game is refreshing and unique, but it does eventually lose steam by the time you start getting near the "inner zone" (the final area ~15-20 hours in). Also, your game saves are inconvenient. You must either be in the garage, or at the start of each new map transition. Amazing sound design, great soundtrack.Details:-Voice Acting: Highly polished, but the story is mediocre-Sounds: Limited songs, but all very high quality, professionally produced (CHECK OUT THE SOUND TRACK!). Environmental sound design is top notch-Visuals: Consistent, atmospheric, stylized, low poly.-Atmosphere: Pacific north west. Dark nights, frequent storms, spooky atmosphere and sound design.-Gameplay: Very fun in the beginning, but will probably lose appeal by the mid to late game. The missions are pretty bland, the environment loses it's intimidation, and the majority of the "anomalies" (similar to STALKER) can't be interacted with or utilized as a resource, which feels like a missed opportunity for a survival craft game. Overall the gameplay is an awesome proof of concept, but is missing enough depth to cover the final portion of the game. Building nearly any of the final tier of items means you'll be delaying the end of the game by a couple of hours, and it doesn't feel worth it at that point. The ending feels rushed, and pacing starts to drag. The lack of a save anywhere/anytime makes it a commitment to finish an entire route. You do autosave at the start of each new zone, however, that does not help at all if you need to leave half way through a zone. (There are usually many zones per route, generally at least 3 by mid game.)

_childDocuments_.review: For 30€ the Journey is worth it. I really digged the exploration aspect to it. Do not expect anything to be chasing you to kill you, but think of it just phenomena that will put you into situations you do not want to be in that may get you killed: There is a lot of see, and alot of weird anomalies that will damage your car.You will have to maintain the damage on the car, and the main mechanic comes around to swapping parts that need repairing with fresh parts and continuously cycling through parts with ones repair furniture. This saves a lot on materials: So a new players priority would be 1 Get more storage for parts, and 2 get more raw materials for spare parts.After about 30 hours  of play, I think I at-least covered 80% of the things to see, and will someday return to complete my log book fully. The first starting hours are a bit of a slog, as you have a mission to complete and gives you infinite amount of time to complete them. Some may take this as a mistake that every single run is gonna be like that.... Its not. Zones can remain stable anywhere between 5-15 minutes or be infinitely stable. But if starting out, do reserve 2 hours at-least for the initial bump. After that its a lot faster.Sometimes you may want to just keep moving through a junction just to survive to your final destination; but that's the game, its the Journey to somewhere. The game saves between Junctions but you cant really save a run unless you have passed a threshold to another junction or returned to the base.The story falls a bit flat by the end of it (felt a bit rushed, there was no build up to the resolutions on reasons for some of the main characters, and the ending walking flashback sequence felt off and drawn out), but otherwise a solid game and I enjoyed my time with it. Customization is quite good.  I would have loved to have some ability to clone some of the stuff, as quite alot of the paint/vinyl cosmetics are very transitional and will be gone as soon as one swaps the parts. There is a very minor gripe about some of the free stickers included from the get go when unlocking customization that feel abit out of time for something supposively set in the 1999's (alternative) timeline, but eh, accuracy goes out of the window what ever there is scifi stuff weird ♥♥♥♥ with zone anyway, and representation matters to some folks alot.The quirk system also felt a bit off, since I barely every had anything but some very specific quirks with my car that i kept of repeatedly repairing out. Not sure if subsequent runs will solve this issue, but I never hard quirks that removed parts of my car forexample. Usually it was just my wiper causing the lights to toggle when going right among other "annoyances".

_childDocuments_.review: You can operate the windshield wipers. 10/10 game of the year.If you get out of the car and don't put it in park, the engine keeps running and the car may roll away. Nice and realistic if occasionally alarming.For a game with hardly any enemies (at least so far), it can be tense or even terrifying. I had some sort of radioactive storm hitting me and I was down to 20% health when I managed to escape back to the garage. What a rush!The resources grind isn't too bad. The blueprint unlock rate is reasonable. The tools degrade faster than I'd like but that's not uncommon for this sort of game. The car itself is exactly the sort of rusted-through wreck you'd expect to find in this environment, and restoring it to a better condition (or even upgrading it) feels rewarding. All in all, it is worth it to me at this price point, but I almost put it off until a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this one. There's a LOT to like here... it has that whole Control/Alan Wake/Remedy vibe going on, which I ADORE. It's got chill, it's got tension, it's got WTFOMGBBQ... it should be an easy recommendation, right?Well, for some people... yes.I expected a game about a journey... a long drive to find your way out of the situation you've been pulled into... but that is NOT this game. No, this is basically a roguelike with a car. You have a base of operations, you pick a destination, and then you get a procgen area to scavenge for resources.After that, you return to your base, upgrade your tech tree, upgrade your your car... and then you scavenging again... repeat... repeat... repeat...This game got it's hooks in me immediately because I am a sucker for moody, atmospheric, immersive games... but after a few short outings, the repetition was already wearing out it's welcome. I do want to see where the story goes and I want to dig more into the lore... but I am just not into this gameplay loop.Look, if you think the concept sounds amazing and you are a fan of "scavenge -> craft -> scavenge -> craft" gameplay, you are going to LOVE this. It's... unfortunately... just not for me. I need to feel more of a sense of progression... and this is just too roguelike in it's core loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a piece of art and I could not recommend it enough. This is a phenomenal offering that uniquely blends genres such as roguelite (progression), soulslikes (exploration), extraction-based survival (mechanics), and simulation (base building, inventory management), then packages it in a gorgeous and immersive driver (not driving) experience that just sucks you in. As the *driver* you bond with your UGLY A$$ car. Because the game is so tactile (especially when played with DualSense), it does not take too long for you to "feel" that something is not right with your Ectomobile. You learn to love it with all its imperfections. Your knowledge of the twisted world you're in grows stronger with each run, encouraging you do "one last run," then you realize it's midnight again. Driving feels great, especially in late-game. Sound design is also well executed. Not only in the context of immersion and intense build-up moments, but also the amount of indicators that compliment the UI elements of this game. These intentional UX design decisions were clearly made to encourage that "tactile" experience I mentioned where you're invited to interact with the game at any given moment. Linking to a gateway and rushing through the massive pillar of light at 88mph (or even better, mid-air) never gets old! Voice acting and story telling is great. You can hear all kinds of Twin Peaks influences in this game. It's not because the story takes place in the PNW, but mostly due to the mystery and humor that's incorporated into the writing of this narrative. It's quirky. It's weird. And I freaking love it.Devs: you all are amazing! I hope there's more planned for this title!Save-game-worriers: I highly recommend giving this a shot! You can manually save the game at any moment and load up multiple saves. The game also auto-saves by overwriting your current save each time you proceed to the next location or junction. As others have already pointed out, you will always have the option to end your run early if you so choose.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo as I was intrigued by the unique game design and wasn't sure what to expect. After playing the demo I wanted more but again was unsure if they could keep my interest with this type of driving game. It's safe to say that this is one of the most unique, interesting, zany and original driving games (or any type of game) that I have enjoyed.        I often get tired of crafting games as they always seem to imitate each other with the same structure and they always seem to try urn into an collection exercise. This is not the case with Pacific Drive. You are itching to get your car ready and prepared for your next adventure trip into what can only be described as a dimensional gear shift into a colourful works of weird and wonderful yet bizarre discovery. As you travel picking up more information about the dimensional desturbences that are plaguing the land and collecting more and more unusual and useful artifacts or components for your vehicles array of gadgetry and mechanics. All the whole upgrading both garage and vehicles equipment for the next trip. The car is the most mundane of vehicle's but packed with an gizmos and tech and resembling the interior of a familiar deloreon from another psifi adventure. In short I love the car. It's fully upgradable, customisable and will be your companion , albeit a little bit rebellious at times , full of quirks but all this adds to its charm.In a game that.defines the expression "it's all about the journey" this suits perfectly, the controls are simple and fun , the graphics visions and occurrences are beautifully crafted and my hat comes off to the Devs for an original , fun and in my must play game. Never before has there been a driving game with so much crazy enjoyable but exciting fun. Got to go am of to "breach" another trip to see where it all ends up. Can't wait !!! Trust me if you like to play behind a wheel your in for a treat. 9/10 thus far . Already want a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: There is only one reason this game does not have Overwhelmingly Positive reviews, and that is simply the collective intelligence of some reviewers. Just scrolling through, I have seen several asinine comments trying to justify a poor review, and i will attempt to address most of them here so you can then go ahead and choose to buy the game based on its merits, and not based on the overly dramatic crying from a select couple neanderthals.1) "THE MISSIONS ARE TOO LONG AND NO SAVE MID GAME" -I guess you haven't played a Souls game before. Dumb reason to rip a game.2) "THIS GAME IS NOT FOR ANYONE WITH A LIFE" -If you cant justify sitting down to game for 1-2 hours when you want to game, then you should a] settle on one game to play per session, b] look at a lifestyle change if you're so unable to do what you want, or c] realize at that point maybe gaming isn't that important to you, move on to something else/game with less time demand, and take notice that's a YOU problem, not a problem with the game. A lot of people like a long session of unbroken immersion, which this game has in spades.3) "DON'T BUY IF YOU HAVE A JOB OR KIDS" -Probably the dumbest one on here. i work six days a week, 50 hours a week, and I just had myself a reasonable 90 minute session before bed. Got plenty done, advanced the story and upgraded my Wagon a good bit. Dumb, dumb, dumb- refer back to #2.4) "YOU LOSE EVERYTHING EVERY TIME YOU DIE NOT WORTH IT" -Nevermind, THIS is the dumbest one on here. This game, along with damn near every game of this genre nowadays, has a toggle for that. Actually, its THREE settings. Lose All, Lose Some, or Keep All. Which, by the way, its defaulted to Lose Some and not Lose All, so not only did these troglodytes not have the wherewithal or common sense to simply open the settings menu, but the entire basis of their gripe wasn't even fully enabled to begin with, and with the least effort possible could have been disabled completely. As can your car damage.This is a wonderfully unique title that has so far lived up to my expectations. I've been waiting for quite a few months for this to drop, and it's a gorgeous title indeed. Working on an apocalyptic family hauler while listening to obscure Seattle sound 90's bands from a radio in the corner is oddly zen-like, and i imagine myself doing it for many hours in the coming months. Do your own research, watch some gameplay on Twitch or youtube, and roundly ignore any of the complaints I mentioned above. From there, you'll be able to decide pretty quickly whether or not it's for you- but my initial impressions are extremely high.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Welcome to Nightvale you will love this. If you love this you might like Welcome to Nightvale.It's a wonderful game with an immersive world to get lost in. It really picks up at around 5 hours when you have the freedom to completely explore the game on your own, learn about the world and upgrade your car.I recommend not listening to the snowflakes with over 20 hours in the game that give a bad review because a simple flag manages to ruin their game. If you understand the story it does make sense, but I don't need to tell you they're not bringing that up for 'realism' sake. The music is incredibly comfy, the mix of intense and calm moments is very nice. It's not really scary, the world manages to feel more mysterious than hostile. Still hostile enough to cover your car in lead while not being scared of the anomalies on foot. The aesthetic is coherent and fits the game. Can't wait to get more immersed in this and it's already one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it not saying it in the tags, the reason you cannot save mid-map is because this game is a rogue-lite. Great game, great story. Wish it was a little longer, but overall still worth the experience. The mechanics are solid and the controls and feeling of the car are well done, which makes the initial experience, and the replayability all the better
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded after an hour playtime. I like the concept, the setting and gameplay was fine, but I simply cannot stand for a game that punishes you for not having hours to spend completing a mission. So you played for 40 minutes but need to go do some real life work? Too bad, all mission progress and items looted are now forefeit. Come back and try again when you have more free time. No mid mission saves, no checkpoints, nothing. You either set aside the time needed to finish a mission completely, or don't play at all.I have little enough time for games nowadays as it is, so playing one that demands you spend however long it mandates to complete a mission rather than have a save anywhere, or even mid-mission checkpoints, absolutely sucks.Not to mention the fact that the game is buried under about 5 million menus and the worlds worst UI means this is an easy refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly can't recommend this game, its an example of a game that has very satisfying mechanics but without a gameplay loop to keep it interesting. Maintaining your vehicle and scavenging fuel/power is not a big part of the game as far as I played.  Instead the main thing I needed to do was loot in order to progress, and simply walking through the same 5 building templates to loot the same containers was not enough to keep me engaged. This game could have been 8 hours long and would have been a great experience, but expecting the player to put in 20+ hours of a loot treadmill to get to the end is just not realistic.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game feels like it was made by a team that knows what gamers want. The upgrades and unlockables are usually very worthwhile. Lots of QoL features for any kind of player, Responsive and intuitive controls imo and has just the right amount of realism while still letting you get immersed in this mysterious world. The sound design is awesome, it can make things feel tense and everything sounds satisfying. It looks perfect for the style it's going for and the obstacles you can encounter feel pretty fair and reasonable but can still give a nice challenge. The prep work before each run feels nice and important and satisfying to see very tangible progress in what you can and have accomplished. Love it and definitely recommend anyone remotely interested in this game to check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game amazing.It's been fun playing around with it-although, I want to say I think the Vac was annoying to find out by myself that it DELETED your stuff instead of storing it. Especially when it spits out your trunk after collecting it-I lost a lot of metal and stuff for thinking I could just rapidly dismantle things and collect it all convienently.I've heard that people have lost hours worth of material for this mistake as well.But the devs are seemingly resonsive so hopefully these things will be clarified or fixed, small issues like not being able to close the garage door in the autoshop, and smaller other things don't diminish too much from the overall experience of travelling, maintaining, assessing, and working with what materials you got. It's a real ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the coolest games to come out in recent years. Highly stylistic and incredibly fun. The game is a roguelite, with missions being relegated to procedurally-generated levels that provide different challenges and resources, as well as a persistent upgrade system that can be utilized between runs. That being said, death is heavily punished. The cool part is that most of the gameplay is customizable. If you don't want to lose items when you die, turn it off in the settings menu. Don't want to bother with the quirks system? Make it easier with an option in the settings menu. If there's a gameplay function that you don't like, chances are you can turn it off in the settings.Overall, this game is super unique and knows exactly what it wants to be and pulls it off extremely well. Definitely worth the price and definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever had a beater of a car you've given a name, pieced back together, gone on road trips with, and told stories about, this may be the game for you. If you love weird atmospheres and the PNW, too? Yes please. I felt like this game was a love letter to those piece of ♥♥♥♥ cars and the weirdos who drive them. I really expected this to be a horror game going in, but alas. Soundtrack is excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit hesitant at first reading through the reviews of this game and after watching some streamers play it, but i did end up getting it and i have to say for someone who hasn't really played many single player games in a while i gotta say this is low key one of the most chill laid back but also a bit tense at times combo i have played like only got it yesterday and already had me hooked in for more then 5 hours so far and I've barely even scratched the surface of the story...
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Early game feels a bit basic, and I almost went for the refund button, but glad I didn't.By basic I mean:- crappy old car- no resources to upgrade anything- a feeling of low control over anything- no clear idea what the hell you're supposed to be doing- limited world at base locationIt was starting to feel like there wasn't really much to this game.But once you get past some of the quirky, weird aspects, heading out on a few trips & start learning what the actual hell is going on, the game really starts to come to life.  I've played through to the (very obvious) mid point of the game now, where the tech tree starts getting interesting and you really feel like you have a fighting chance, rather than just barely making it through.If you like games with exploration, driving, upgrading/tech trees, resource gathering and a good atmosphere, then well worth the money.  The graphics aint bad either!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even gonna lie, this is the best game I have ever played. I'm not a fan of cars, but oh my god this game is amazing. The visuals are gorgeous, the story is enthralling, and the gameplay loop still manages to be interesting and fun well after finishing the game. Pat yourselves on the back, Ironwood Studios since this is genuinely the most fun I've had in months.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept, but almost everything about this game is just 15 degrees off. Nothing feels "right". The controls, the UI, the crafting and questing, ar fine on the surface, but don't feel great. That coupled with the crashes every time I complete a zone makes me suggest giving this one a pass until they either improve some of this stuff, or it goes into the discount bin.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I was 13 hours in and the game was fine. But in a later level the game crashed and deleted my save file. this is not a game that you want to replay the first part of. Its a very slow burn to have a save file lost. I was enjoying myself but i cant see myself playing the game ever again for this reason. I'm extremely frustrated because this game is good but not good enough to drive and loot for 10 hours again to get even come close to the meat and potatoes of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying it for the time being, although a bit stressfull at times it makes up for it with an extremely engaging gameplay loop, haven't died yet too, came really close to it on a couple of ocassions, it does feel great when you come back full of new resources from a trip in the zone with 5% health remaining, altough seeing how hard staying alive can sometimes be if you're aiming for better loot I do think dying will be very much an anger inducing situation. Hopefully the story is as good as the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought I would actually complete this game as I found it rather challenging at times, but I did manage to do so (which is apparently rarified air as less than 10% of owners have actually done so). It was actually a lot of fun. Half the game is high stress, and the other half (in the garage) is relaxing. Luckily you don't have to unlock all of the upgrades to make your car viable for the final missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of best games i've played in the last decade!A Cool mix of survival, crafting and level progression always with the "environment" in the back pushing you further. But you have the save haven of the garage after every exploration.The grafic design and effects are gorgous, the atmosphere is immersive and the soundtrack is awesome!The only "downside" is, that the game is over now, but 40 hours to completion is quite a task anyways. :-)I really enjoyed playing Pacific Drive and you definitively can count me in for potential DLC or even part two! :-)Greetings OPTi
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I spend most of my time in other games exploring every crook and nanny before progressing and this game is meant for people like that. I also get frustrated with games like No Man's Sky and Subnautica because you're meant to build a nice base AND explore and I'd rather explore so the base is a messy wasted nothing. This game is also for people like that.People whining about the save options are half casual. My favorite moments playing were because of the stress caused by not being able to save mid run. It's not supposed to be easy . Plenty of amazing games have this mechanic. I agree we need to be able to close the garage though. I wasn't raised in a barn.Edit: Can close garage door now, 10/10. My opinion has not changed on saving. Anyone who is casual enough to be butthurt over the save system is playing the wrong game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems really fun but unfortunately the save system is a non-starter for me and I had to refund. You basically have to complete every level (which can take an hour of dedicated play or more if you want to explore every bit of the level) to be able to save progress. Have a child or simply want to call it a night? Too bad. Keep hate-playing until you reach a checkpoint or redo everything you just did next time you come back to the game.I'll pick it up again and revisit this review once I see they implement a sane save system.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. Tarkov but single player, PVE, and a mysterious hostile world to explore. My only complaint is how short the main game is. While it took me well over 30 hours to complete it feels like there is nothing to do afterward besides customizing your car to go into the places you've already been. I'd love to see an expansion that gives us more places to explore and a reason to go back out into the zone. The game play loop is extremely fun and always keeps you engaged. I love the car's mechanics and how it develops quirks as you play. It gives the car personality and allows you to personify it while you are out traveling alone. The fact that the game doesn't outright tell you everything is really nice in a world saturated with games that will give you a tutorial for every little thing. Just play this game. It's worth every penny and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: If S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and Jalopy had a child... except it's kinda clunky, overwhelming, hasty, and not really enjoyable because everything around you is just made to keep you from progressing. Game feels like a passion project, and definitely worth it to buy and try it. Somehow, after ten hours this game left me with dissapointment and lack of will to go on with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

Anomalies than being on the road with the average ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Western Washington DriverBut honestly the game is really damn good and captures the evergreen climate really wellmy only gripe I got is the ass ton of Pride Flag stickers in the decal station I KNOW they added last minutelike idk what the hell a Abrosexual is but I doubt they need validation from this game, let alone will receive validation from this gamelike hell there's a Christian Song in the OST and every single thing except the pride flags fit the time periodbut that's just a very minor gripe and it's super easy to ignore honestlyThe only thing I feel missing from the game is Workshop support with the ability to easily mod in new songs to the radiocause I do like the music selection (besides Puzzle Pieces that song is like a jack hammer to my skull) but the selection is small and repetitive
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Finally finished the main story today and enjoyed the experience enough I figured I would share my thoughts on the game.Ironwood Studios has created a truly unique experience here. After 35 hours I can say that I thoroughly enjoyed myself throughout the entire journey aside from a single crash to desktop and a small handful of annoying but not gamebreaking bugs. So not only did they deliver an interesting and enjoyable game, but also a very solidly performing one, which in itself feels all too rare these days.There is a clear sense of vision and care present in basically every aspect of the game. From the driving, to the survival mechanics and the sound design. My only complaint would be that the UI can be slightly fiddly to use at first and has a slight learning curve to it before you will likely feel comfortable fully navigating it.The driving feels tactile, especially with a controller and you can read a lot of how your car is fairing just from how it handles and sounds vefore even checking the dashboard UI.The Zone itself is interesting but also somewhat familiar of you have ever played games like Stalker, although this one does enough to be unique in its own right. It is an alien landscape that has a constant sense mystery and slight hostility to it. You almost always feel as if you are being watched in some way.The survival mechanics are overall quite excellent in how you maintain and upgrade your car. Maintain fuel levels, battery charge and just the general integrity of it is an engaging experience that had me merrily tinkering away and always looking forward to the next upgrade or chance to perform repairs.The story is interesting but can become a bit confusing if you don't pay attention to what is being said. All of the voice acting seems top notch and I genuinely liked the small handful of characters you are able to hear over the radio.Overall just an excellent and unique game different from anything else I have played. I look forward to seeing if this ever receives future content or a sequel of some kind. Absolutely worth the price as it is though.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad I took a chance on this game. The atmosphere, the gameplay, the characters, the writing are all amazing. I love driving hell-for-leather towards a rift as the world breaks apart around me. I love cruising through the fog and rain watching the ghosts of houses pass by around me. The only gripe I have is that I wish the garage had an upgrade that let you influence the weather. I especially love driving in the rain and this game really hits that sweet spot for me and I wish I could make it so that it rains a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. Good execution, fun & good characters, encountered not a single bug, and it's pretty. Some personal critiques are that the game gets relatively repetitive (at least early on, idk about late game) and a lot of the time is just repairing the car just good enough to go back out, just to repair it again. Again, it's a good game but not for me.oh yeah, biggest flaw is that you can't save. it's repetitive and you HAVE to commit to runs that might take a long, long time just to get there and back for some stuff. It's hard to pick up the game since it can be so repetitive just to have to commit HARD because of there being no save button. Again, very good characters, good execution, pretty and trees making me gush, very little frame drop, good controls whatever, just repetitive & no saves.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe grab it when it's on sale but I played it to the end hoping it would become better but it didn't. _childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: So, the basics of Pacific Drive is a nice little drive-and-loot-and-craft your way through a few zones of weirdness and a story with a startlingly effective cast of characters, for all that you only ever hear them through the radio.It's a fun and enjoyable romp, with some very good music to listen to on the way. _childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing beats the experience of getting lost in the world and scrapping for resources, and then suddenly you get caught out, and now you're trying to outrun the storm, your car is breaking down and your health is draining, and your racing through the woods whilst avoiding enemies to get to the exit - there is always something new about this game to experience. The experience of the car and taking care of it makes the game feel a lot more organic as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of driving, a lot of scrapping, and lot of smearing repair paste on your car.  But so far at least, not a lot of fun.  At least for me.  It kind of feels like you're playing minecraft and punching trees repeatedly.  Driving the car itself is a bit of a pain, turn the key, move to drive, open the door, leave the car.  Over and over to go scrap every panel from other cars.  It just gets old.And the save system is AWFUL.  No game should have me out collecting stuff and unable to save for fear of losing half an hour of game play in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, it runs well on my old machine. If you like to explore, loot, craft & survive in dangerous environments, PVE only. Then this will be up your alley. I enjoy that things do break on the car & that you can fix them.However if you're short on time, you can still hobble along with a flat tyre,broken door & shorted out headlights to get home! There are aspects that are a little bit of a grind at times, but that's exactly what you sign up for if you're into a gather/loot to craft kind of game. The more you loot & gather, The more things you can craft to make your missions easier. The story is good, I do wish there was more story content past the "ending". After I had finished with the story, I didn't feel like exploring the zones past that.If they ever plan DLC with story, i'd be happy to play that!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique game. It's a bit like a more polished version of The Long Drive, important to note is that the world is not seamless, though. You hop from junction to junction via a fast-travel system. The demo (which encompasses the tutorial level) does suggest that there is less driving than there actually is a lot of the time. The demo is dense with buildings to search and the map is relatively small. Later areas are larger and you will often have longer driving segments between sites to explore. Do play the demo, though, as it otherwise represents the overall gameplay loop, atmosphere and story very well. The latter is pretty intriguing and the game can get downright creepy a lot of the time
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems really cool. Unfortunately the performance leaves a lot to be desired, the graphics menu doesn't quite seem to work as intended (DLSS always switching back to auto) and there's a thunder sound in the game that, while potentially being intentional, had a nasty static tone to it that was abusing my ears, I could not stand it.
