_childDocuments_.review: ------ i gave a thumbs up to this game first, now it's a thumbs down. I didn't want to finish it and forced myself to play the 5 to  10 last hours ---------it is a very meh game. You will find in other reviews what the game is about, what follows is the felling when i was at the end credits : the lack of variety in the anomalies is atroucious : with the setting of lim it could have been anything, and what do we have : aoe of elemental damage, walking elemental damage, moving aoe of elemental damage, standing elemental damage .........lack of variety in the musiclack of variey of the biomesyou can skip half of the upgrades because lots of them are useless, and most of them costing way too much ressources, and thus, runs and time to make them.lots of useless mechanics (i'm looking at you, transmuters)The anomaly system on the car could have been super fun, but it's usually tedious.you can skip half the intersection because the only good direction is north westthe game is wayyyyyyyyyyyyyy too long considering what it has to offer.despite being way too long, it's a hassle to find all the audio log nonethelessthe story is kinda bland and not well told, with secondary characters struggling to convey any sense of danger or narrative tensionthis game contains enough fun things for 20h max, and by that time you're far from the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. A couple of issues initially with bugs and optimizations, but so much fun and such a cool story. The atmosphere, the voice acting, the gameplay, all amazing. Just when you think you've seen it all and can't be creeped out anymore, some new anomaly or condition shows up and shows you wrong. They never rely on cheap jumpscares, in fact, I don't think I've had one all game, except maybe the tourists showing up.Absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, this one is a "yeah, no" for me.Main issues are pacing, the saving system, the UI, narrative and lighting.Pacing - every time you want to reach a mid or late game location, you have to go through all the early game locations required to get there. This is fun the first, second, maybe third time - after that, it's just a chore. If you're starting a mission, you could spend an hour getting to the location the mission is set in - who thought this was a good idea? The grind is bad enough without it.Saving system - related to pacing above. You can't save "mid-drive" - once you leave your garage, that's it, you either finish the mission or lose all progress if you exit the game. I believe the devs said this is a technical limitation they can't fix - you gotta give them credit for admitting to have a skill issue.UI - seriously, who designed this? Idk about controller, but on kbm it's barely usable. Some actions are hold-input, others a button press - for no reason. The upgrade menu (fabricator) is worse than DOS (seriously, is the default resolution of that screen 24x24 pixels?).Narrative - does anybody actually care about the 3 losers who constantly Skype call you while you play? Ugh.Also, what is wrong with the lighting system? Is my character going bling? If you don't crank the brightness setting to the moon, you can't see anything in the dark (which for whatever reason is most of the time, the game has an in-game clock but somehow 80% of my drives are in pitch black). This is not how being in nighttime works, maybe if the devs ever got outside for a bit they'd figure it out.I've found that the music is great, graphics are pleasing. But that's not enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Game completed. Overall a good game. Voice acting is high tier and the story is interesting enough. Difficulty ramp is mostly good and the anomalies scale in a way that helps keep them intimidating. You never feel fully safe and in context of the zone, you shouldn't. A few places that it falls down:Parts "wearing out" makes some thematic sense but there isn't a way to predict when something is getting close to worn out so you can't take steps to avoid problems. On the very last mission of the game I started with a tire that was at full health, two zones in it goes to bald, blows out the next zone. This is symptomatic of the game's weakest point, a fair amount of breakdowns and challenges you deal with feel completely arbitrary. Very much an "f you, that's why" sort of vibe. The result is, especially towards the end game, a sense of futility and a grind that doesn't pace will with the rest of the game. If that's something that will really bother you, this isn't for you. If it's something to forgive, this is a good 25-40 hour romp.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting over 3 and a half years for this amazing game. Arcade driving at it's best. Love the visuals and damn please fix the high and ultra shadow options. I drop half my frames.Every single sound effect in this game is masterfully crafted to make you jump back in your car and scramble for the exit junction. This game offers true immersive alone-ness. Nobody is here to save you but that damn car.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific drive is a fun, atmospheric, and oh so creepy game that's definitely worth your time. You play as a driver who finds themselves stuck in a quarantine zone with no way out, scavenging equipment and dodging creepy anomalies in the dark. The only tool to help you get through this? A haunted car. The game loop consists of going out for drives as short or as long as you'd like them to be. You stop by landmarks to college salvage, trying not to destroy your car by the many hazards on (and off) the road, then teleporting back in a race against time. Use materials to upgrade your base and vehicle, craft new equipment, fix any damaged parts, and off you go further than you could before. It's satisfying and it was easy to progress through the technology tree. It was somewhat difficult to understand the UI and controls at first, but once you figure it out it's fine. It makes sense, just isn't very intuitive. What this game really has going for it is its atmosphere. Pacific Drive isn't "difficult" by any sense of the word - the difficulty is all in your head, conjured by the fear of the numerous anomalies you encounter on the road. Once you understand them you eventually realise that there was never any reason to be scared in the first place. This right there constitutes exceptionally good game design to me.All of this is accompanied by an average and frankly overused story about technology gone wrong. It's good enough to keep you going, but never really feels closed, complete, or shocking. The various story fragments you collect and scan across the world are written well and often entertaining.All in all, a game well worth its price tag and your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This hits the spot in terms of unique games. Imagine driving through Gravity Falls during weirdmagedon, or if 'Welcome to Nightvale' took place in the northwest part of the U.S.. Things are strange, deadly, and unpredictable. The whole "not being able to save the game in the middle of a mission" is really a non-issue seeing that this is a rogue-like game. the fact that you can save your game when you go back to the garage is a saving grace, but not being able to save out in the field adds to the challenge. it's unique, brilliant, and the music is really good. Welcome back to the 90's, now DRIVE.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Very neat paranormal angle and the setting has a flavor not unlike Portal 2. Wild stuff abounds, both spooky and amazing. Visuals are wonderful, aiming more towards style than realism and doing it in a fantastic way. There's a little grindiness to it, but the act of simply exploring should give you plenty of time out in the world to get everything you actually need, there's only a couple items that would need some real grinding.The game loop is pretty straightforward. Equip car, explore map, come back, research/repair/rebuild, and repeat. There's enough customization to get you attached to your car, but not so much that it's a chore to deal with the system. The Quirk system adds in little oddities that any driver of an older vehicle has encountered, ranging from everything like misbehaving headlights to your car trying to drive itself away from you.Great balance of tension and action. Different map modifiers make you more or less hesitant to explore certain things. One run can be leisurely and fruitful, another run can be a constant race against storms and anomalies. The overall game ran longer than I was expecting, but didn't overstay it's welcome. About the time you've seen everything is when it wraps up.There are also good story themes. The campaign has a story, but there are also bits and pieces of atmospheric story you pick out of the environment via audio files. Overall a great mid-budget game. Plenty of bang for the buck, looks great, plays great, sounds great.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Generally, it's a decent game. A game has to be entertaining for me to pick it back up after it has failed to grip me in the tutorial segment, especially if I then continue to play it for another 53 hours.Not spoiling anything, even though there's not much to spoil. Don't expect any advanced plot twists or anything, I definitely wouldn't buy this game for the story. The characters are fine to listen to but also very trope-y, you got your old annoyed lady, a charismatic optimistic daredevil and a shy introverted scientist. Nothing you haven't heard before. I really wish they'd have made more about the plot because at the end I literally felt nothing about it.Pretty decent and kinda addictive. Maintaining your car is nice and the game itself has a decent loop for it. There's many options to make this game more accessible, even though none of these options really make sense to you unless you play the game for a few hours. At the start of it I changed some things I thought were good, but at the end, for a rogue like game, I only failed like two or so runs.  It was more of a breeze to play through. Towards the end, driving through the same old junctions and layouts was getting kinda boring, even if it was randomized to a degree.The tutorial is (as I said) relatively long and the game "runs" themselves are also relatively long, which is why I didn't pick this game up again for several weeks. I didn't wanna commit to something where I can't exit a run within 30 mins or so. Expect to spend anything between 45 to 60 mins per run.Overall the gameplay itself is the strongest selling point of this game, if maintaining your car, foraging for supplies and driving through a wasteland/exclusion zone is your kinda deal. Not for people with motion sickness, though.Game was running okay, I was playing on 1440p with a Vega 64, a 5800X and 32 GB RAM and had everything between 50-85 fps on medium settings. I wish the game would be running better, especially given that the artstyle is kinda simplistic.Graphics themselves are fine and atmospheric, although it really felt like the focus was on the darker sections of the game, I rarely got to play during "daytime". With my settings the aliasing with the jagged edges was noticeable, but I got accustomed to it.Buy this game if you enjoy driving in a wasteland and foraging and exploring, don't buy it for the story. Overall a well made game that I spent a good enough time in it. I'd wait for a sale, but its def worth the time. Unless you want some big story to come out of this, which, uh, rather don't buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love a lot of things about the game of what I've played so far: the voice acting, the lore, the crafting system, the sweet station wagon On the game loop, you explore areas to progress the story, gather crafting ingredients and before you leave each zone you need to gather a particular resource that allows you to warp back to your home base. This resource is also used for using the upgrade station (on top of the crafting ingredients) The world is scary and you do feel you and your car are fighting for your life some times if the right random anomalous conditions are rolled. The upgrade tree which includes upgrades to you (e.g. backpack size), your car (paneling, engines, new abilities), and your base (machines to make servicing your car easier or breaking down old parts) can be a little overwhelming at first but it's a lot of fun on the old style computers you find in the game. Having a blast with it, big recommend. Try the demo as it captures quite a large chunk of the game loop.

_childDocuments_.review: The game simply isn't what I thought it was going to be. As of writing this review, I have just finished the storyline.From the promotional material on the Steam page, I was imagining a procedurally generated open world and lots of driving, with the occasional stop to loot a point of interest.Unfortunately, the maps do not seem randomised, although they are sometimes rotated, and while the exact loot found and the exact dangers present do vary from visit to visit - the fact that I say "maps" is another disappointment of mine. The game is open world in the sense that you can visit any of the dozens of unique locations any time you want, and they are connected on a road and highway grid in an even larger map that you traverse by selecting a location and fast travelling to it.There's little reason to venture outside your car when things are going well, and when things are going poorly, there's every reason to simply get home and recover. Most resources are beyond abundant if you get out to loot every few hours of playtime, and the ones that aren't abundant then form a very narrow funnel for your activities that make it feel like you have much less freedom than intended.A strong linear narrative pervades the entire game and provides a direction to follow. To me, this simply reduced my desire to explore outside the 'given' path, as it seems every location within the three 'zones' can have that zone's resources - so not going for the quest path is simply slowing your progress most of the time.The dangers present in the game are not particularly grand, and unless your car itself develops an unfortunate quirk, there's not a lot to fear. In my playthrough, I almost died twice, once to a bug in the end sequence, and once because my car's quirk opened the driver's seat door and an anomaly nearly killed me during a forced-damage segment of the game. Most of the quirks developed are benign or unimportant, like making your window wipers move faster or slower, or turning on the cabin light, fiddling with your radio or dashboard, etc.Finally, I was looking for a driving game with survival mechanics, but it seems I purchased another mid-budget linear narrative game with driving mechanics and a crafting system. The only 'survival' present is that you have a health bar, and that your car can be damaged to a point where you take damage instead. There is no need for food or water. The car has ample supplies of power and fuel so there's little risk of stranding yourself, and there is no way to save while outside your safehouse, so even if the game had larger locations and more driving segments to lean into driving and exploration more - you would be forced to do so in a single sitting, without the ability to save and come back after dinner.TLDR; Wanted driving game, got narrative game. Emergent gameplay from survival and difficulty is lacklustre.

_childDocuments_.review: The game says I spent about 45 hours in it, while Steam says it was closer to 60. Regardless, this is one of the more tricky to review games. I kinda don't like it. But I found myself coming back to it. Allow me to try to explain.The game is centered around a mystery. There's a section of the extreme NW of the USA that's been walled off from the rest of the world. You, as The Driver, have somehow gotten through the walls and made friends with some scientists and a station wagon, and now you're off to unravel the mystery. It is your job to repair and upgrade your trusty steed while exploring the alienated world of the Olympic Peninsula after its weird little apocalypse.I was immediately swamped. The designers seemed to feel like having a mystery as the story was just a start. You also needed to be punished with a mystery of user-interfaces and obscure diagetic exposition. There are indicators on the dashboard of your car that I still can't explain. If you notice something anomalous out in the world, and you're quick enough to step out of the car and scan it, you'll get the basic information -- the name of the anomaly, the type of damage it does, and where you found it -- plus a little snippet of text log that's along the lines of "Joe-bob found one of these in his lunch box last week. Seemed to take a liking to his donuts. We're calling it Tubby."That's great and all, but ... what? Nowhere does it tell you to hit it with a stick. I understand that might actually be the point. There is some joy in discovery, but I mostly just found it annoying. Even after my 60 hours, I'm still not sure if I'm missing something about these big glowing orange balls.  You can scan them, but it doesn't really say anything. My first couple of hours sucked. The game loop is this: From the garage, pick a location on a map, get hints on what might be there. Go there. Get totally wasted by the environment that hates you, pick up a few resources, then finally push the big button when the environment REALLY starts to hate you. Then, you have to bust ass to the exit point before the environment finally kills you.  If you make It back to the garage, you can now use what you collected to repair all the new damage you made.  It wasn't until I was probably 15 hours in before it finally hit me: this is a Rogue-like. You're *supposed* to roll a random experience that is *supposed* to be punishing. But this game seems poorly balanced, and I quickly began to feel put-upon. Everything gets damaged, everything wears out, repairs and upgrades are expensive, and if you can't afford them, you're stuck going out into the world unprotected. It felt a little like Death Stranding in that respect, especially when there's a bout of acid rain going on.The developers know their game balance is a problem, though, and they put in the ability to set the game into a gentler mode. I took advantage of this, and immediately started to actually enjoy the game. I put in another couple of hours and started exploring deeper into the zone. But before long the lack of resources and the unfortunate timing of required upgrades coupled with a failed run left me softlocked again and I was about to abandon game.Then, just this month, the developers released MORE difficulty adjustments, and this allowed me to put the game into full baby-mode. This finally allowed me to enjoy some of the exploration, drive into the deepest parts of the zone, and complete the story. Some of the excitement of the game was gone, yes, but it was either that or abandon the game.The ending was not at all worth it, by the way. I can't say the mystery has been solved, nor has the Zone been fixed. Also, I'm usually very susceptible to games that create analogs of places I've been. I'm currently a resident of the PNW. I can almost see the Olympic Peninsula from my house, and I have literally done the Pacific Drive. But the world the game presents has been so alienated from reality that I have absolutely no feeling of "I CAN SEE MY HOUSE FROM HERE!!" in this game.So I don't know what to say. There are probably people out there who enjoy this torture. Better, the game now supports a more exploration-focused configuration so people who are not masochists might also be able to enjoy the game. I found it diverting enough for me to come back to, twice. I think if you let yourself use the difficulty configs, you might enjoy your drive.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately disappointing. Really cool general vibe. Some of the driving and exploration is cool. Some of the music fits really well. Escaping with a sliver of health feels great the first few times. The outer zone looks beautiful most of the time. But the story sucks, narrative progression is completely disconnected from general progression, some of the final upgrades are just pointless. Anomalies are just annoying things to drive around. Difficulty is too low, there's no real danger (I never died in the 60 hours), and yet you have a timer that doesn't let you explore at your own pace. The drive-not-like-an-idiot-for-2-minutes missions are trash, the final mission is mega trash. Car upgrade balance is off too: no point upgrading the engine past the first upgrade after you get nitro, no point upgrading shielding after limshield and ion shield. There's a much better game in there somewhere that got lost along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Was slightly disappointed at first as I thought it would be more open-world focused, but pretty quickly adjusted to the setup and enjoyed it just as much, if not more, than if it were open world! I do agree with others that being able to save during runs would be nice, but I understand the principle behind why you can only save on-demand at the base / autosave at the start of a junction. It raises the stakes and prevents you from just mindlessly reloading the second things start to go wrong, and I enjoy that. It's frustrating to lose everything, but that's kind of the point. I don't have much in the way of complaints, though I do have a few things I wish could be implemented. First would be more biome types, though I understand the current limitations on that. Second would be the ability to change up the body of the car a bit more! I had entered this game w/ the impression that I'd be able to beef up the car, and have been a little disappointed on the limited selection of parts and addons. That said though, I absolutely love this game!!! The story and characters are delightful, and the car controls really well :D

_childDocuments_.review: 16 hour edit: Things get even more interesting (and creepy) as you settle into the meat of the game beyond the tutorial. Night time during heavy rain will have you on the edge of your seat and some of the environmental modifiers are absolutely brutal. I love it! I've only found a couple more bugs and all of them are still minor, like a stretched texture occasionally flickering in the air. These bugs are rare though and don't really get in the way at all. It's still a big thumbs up from me!_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _Pacific Drive is a great game, and pretty much what it says on the tin. Your car is like a mobile base that you drive around the zone, collecting scrap to fabricate upgrades and equipment, while dodging STALKER style anomalies. It's lots of fun so far and I'm excited to play more!Everything works properly and performs well for me. I've encountered only one little UI bug that doesn't affect gameplay at all, that's it. Just the wrong prompt displaying at the wrong time. Pretty impressive for a game that's only hours old and hasn't received any patches yet these days.Before you launch the game you should make sure whatever sort of surround sound you use is properly set up. It really works well here. Then turn off the lights, turn up the volume, and enjoy the drive!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy this, but the cool, creepy atmosphere quickly gives way  to boredom when you realize that there are no serious threats, and therefore no tension.  What threats do exist are, frankly, more annoying than scary / cool, at least so far as I've seen.  Also, you can only save at certain points, and on more than one occasion now I've gotten my vehicle stuck due to the wonky controls and had to reload, losing 30-45 minutes of progress.  That might not be a big deal if it was 30-45 minutes of repeating gameplay that I'd actually enjoy, but I just can't bring myself to go back and redo 30-45 minutes of stumbling / skidding around in the dark, bored and annoyed, only to probably get stuck again.  I think I stuck with the game as long as I did because I really like the aesthetic, the backstory, and whole post-apoc genre generally.  it got old fast, though, and mostly just reminded me of other, better games of the same type that I'd rather be playing.  On the fence as to whether I'll give it another try, but right now I just don't have it in me to further play, or to recommend, this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good concept, TERRIBLE execution. Over the course of my playtime I gradually grew more and irritated with the game, going from minor gripes, to actually just bee-lining missions to finish. Save yourself the money and boredom. I'd much rather have used my money and time on something else more engaging/exciting. They stuck the landing about as well as your car does, and apparently it has no shocks at all. And I cannot in good conscience be silent either about certain inflammatory "woke" items added to the game, which I will discuss later after more egregious issues (as well as to also avoid any knee-jerk reactions). Right off the bat, the "currency" you use with anchors to purchase tech quickly go from the MOST "rare" being valuable to the MOST USELESS, as all other tech, scans of your cars quirks, etc. all require STABLE energy which only shows up in the boring starter zones with zero other valuable resources than can be found elsewhere, but also the late game or CORRUPTED/UNSTABLE energy turns out to be utterly useless as it cannot be used for anything but the limited amount of tech trees. In layman's terms it'd be like if legendary rarity ingredients dropped all the time but common level rarity items dropped only 1/10 in a MMO. Oh you want to use a scanner? Well too bad there's no map outside your car, and the item you need to scan for resources is locked in the highest tree and takes up the essential roof space which you can only fit two.My biggest gripes is how mid-end level resources are almost impossible find, with the latter very well may as well be. I'm in the very last mission and have only seen olypium resource occur ONCE, and its utterly almost indistinguishable from the regular boulders of the zone. AND ITS NOT SCARCE IN THE GOOD WAY, especially considering HOW MANY RECIPES REQUIRE IT. In addition the utterly cluttered car interior has so many doo-dads and gizmos inside it makes the DeLorean look bare. I get they're trying to go with the whole "70's mad scientist" vibe but it seems really far to cluttered compared to the neatness of Long Drive or Summer Car (both of which were produced at a 1/10th of this games budget) where you can tell stuff from a glance. Even outside the car your HUD still completely is obscured by all kinds of text that completely spoils the atmosphere of nature, and I checked if there was any opacity. So the store screenshots are completely misleading, which has that taking a big dip in my rating, as I do not appreciate dishonesty. This lack of clarity is even further evidenced with the devs dancing around the issue of being able to save or even suspend your game during a mission. 80% of the anomalies are either tepid in design or annoying in game, without ever really seeming like a threat. Also all the ramps and jumps have solid rails that make you crash and grind into them rather than actually be helpful, and the fuel can is constantly leaking and next to useless compared to upgraded fuel can.Also they seem to have rearannged and nerfed some anomalies from the press-release demo PARTICULARILY the healing anomoly which was supposed to be in the first area, which further shows more dishonesty. By the 3/4 mark the game gets embarrassingly melodramatic with cliches of "I've gotta do thing!" "No it's too dangerous don't do thing!" "I'm gonna do the thing!" "No please don't do the thing!" "Come in dude! Please, dude respond!" "Take care of protaganist for me...I love you forever dude" "no dude! nooooo!" Followed by sad music twangs when you get back to the garage, all of which I felt nothing for which further undermined the sense of silliness. I don't honestly know how they wrote that part with a complete straight face, especially compared to the rest of the writing which seems at least passable if not interesting most of the time. I'm wondering if its a case of another writer filling or just running out of steam. And the ending is a embarassing lore dumb hallway, which seems even more sloppilly written especially since the hallway lasts twice as long as the audio recordings. And the "ghost" popping up was predictable too, and your reward for dragging the bobblehead all the way towards them is just a single sentence saying "oh cool". Now onto the most tenative issue:Unlike most, the gay couple were well written enough and their relationship not shone with a spotlight for once (like how paranorman  wrote gay charecters), which gives them some credit in my book, instead of it being their only defining character trait like most AAA writers try these days with LGBTQ characters). However I built a decal station to install a funny wizard on my mirror and got dumped with  pride flag paint jobs  because it couldn't fit all of them in one notification (even including some politically inflammatory controversial flags to boot, in case it wasn't "woke" enough). Its fine if you want to include these as a mod (or gosh forbid, a DLC) but you really shouldn't jam these things in a place where people are just trying to have fun. Not to mention is completely immersion breaking to see a LGBTQ  (just a decade before homophobia  reached its peak in 1980).Also the basketball minigame is poorly programmed and nearly impossible to get it into the ring without it bouncing off the rims. Even a game like half life that came out 20 YEARS AGO had a functioning enough engine to do basketball. come on people.Yes i'm just dumping all my gripes as I go along now i'm just so annoyed at this game. Its not even BAD bad, just mid as possible, which is the worst possible line to land in.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique spin on survival games. I loved maintaining and upgrading my car in the auto shop, readying it for the next expedition into the Zone, doing quick patch jobs in the field and siphoning gas from wherever I could while the deadly Instability was breathing down my neck as I floored it to the nearest Gateway, praying that my car makes it back with all four wheels still on. Aside from functional upgrades and modifications to your car, there are also tons of cosmetics you can add ranging from paint jobs, decals, stickers, and more. The save function may be a turn off for some players. You can only save whenever you go into a new junction, or if you're in the Auto Shop. If you manually save while in the middle of a run, you abandon your drive and get penalized. Personally, I've never done this, so I can't give you details as to what these penalties entail. All in all, it's a fun game that I highly recommend. Especially if you've ever wondered what it would be like to go through a S.T.Al.K.E.R.-like setting with a car.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, this is my first ever Steam review and I recommend this game to everyone who enjoys challenging, creative and atmospheric indie games. If this is likely to be an issue for you, just wait for further updates or play around with the available difficulty settings, there's plenty of features and game mechanics to tweak to make it less difficult and cozier. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly brilliant!Really fun gameplay loop, wonderful atmosphere, good music and an interesting zone to explore!10 hours in and I barely saw them go by!Performance can be a bit hit or miss but I found that by reducing shadows to medium my fps shot right up! The game actually saves every time you exit a level, the devs recently put out a very lengthy news post covering just that. So that removes any problems I have with the save system to be honest!All in all, a hearty recommend if you like 'being alone in a beautiful yet dangerous zone'.I suppose if you like S.T.A.L.K.E.R, Death Stranding or Into the Radius, you will like this.Although Pacific Drive has no guns/combat as far as I can tell.Personally I want more games centred around your vehicle like in this one! _childDocuments_.review: Q: Is this game fun? Is it a good game overall?A: Yes and Yes.Q: Is this a must buy, masterpiece level game?A: Definately not. But it is quite a unique experience.Q: Are there any bugs?A: You can find just a few if you really try, but nothing major, noteworthy or gamebreaking.Q: Is it system hungry? Will i need to buy a top tier PC to run it?A: Nope. Its optimised well and runs just fine even on outdated rigs.Q: Is this a long session game?A: Yes. And it does require you to dedicate time to it. Because it only allows you to either manually save inbetween missions. Or it autosaves on checkpoints during missions. And those checkpoints might easily be up to 1-2 hours apart. Depending on your playstyle and mission conditions.Q: Is there really a minorities propaganda ingame?A: Unfortunately yes. Both in story and some cosmetics. Not a deal breaker just yet, but definately a thing to consider.Q: Is the Deluxe Edition worth buying?A: Its totally optional. You wont miss out if you skip it. However, unlike most other ingame cosmetics those DLC items glow in the dark. And since more than half of the game time its spent in the dark, having those actually helps sometimes. So if you have extra coin, might be worth it for you.Q: Is the game worth full price?A: I'd say yes it is. Its a good product overall, and if you can spare time for it, chances are you wont regret it. But if you ever see it on a sweet fat discount then its definately a must buy.GL HF

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend, solid 7.5/10The visuals, atmosphere and the oppressive nature of the Exclusion Zone are almost the stars of the show, they did a standout job making it dangerous, ominous and interesting. The various hazards and threats look unique and are really a thrill to encounter for the first time. When you do your first few portals back home the impending collapse of the area is fantastic, its a visually interesting mechanic that creates tension and excitement. Its almost more fun when a run goes wrong, things can quickly domino spectacularly and it keeps you on you toes.I really enjoyed narrative presented - spooky science experiments gone wrong, not ground breaking but done well. Its simple, effective and doesnt rely on grand setups or exposition. You get what information you need from the few other characters you interact with over radio and the flavour so to speak is from notes/logs etc. The car itself, your life line and main reason to exist looks fantastic, as do all the little upgrades and doodads you make for it. It nice to control, simple with a touch of realism in interaction. Caring for it is simple enough in execution but can require a bit of leg work and repeated grinding of areas to get what you need. The garage (your home base) is really nifty, it looks great all upgraded and has a cosiness to it i appreciated. The process of fixing and upgrading the car and garage, for me, was overall very enjoyable and often cathartic/relaxing which is a great contrast to trips into the zone. The core gameplay loop is, head out, get materials and or head to story quest marker then back to base to repair/upgrade/restock car. Again i found a lot of this stuff quite relaxing and some runs can be fun and frantic but it can end up being the weakest point of the game. I also didnt care for some of the random generation, namely the debris on the roads, why is there a random barrel or traffic cone and barrier combo every 100 metersHeading out to get materials is a given, at first its all novel and even exciting but once you have encountered all the various anomalies/hazards and know how to counter/avoid them, it  can get a touch annoying - The ones that cant be combated or avoided become frustrating. That plus the fact you start from the same spot each trip means you have to go through the same areas over and over each run getting longer and longer, with certain paths basically becoming a no go for a time. It can all wear a bit thin and waters down a often unique and thrilling experience. I will point out that due to recent updates you can now tweak a bunch of settings to increase or decrease your difficulty, however too easy and youll end up with a short game with little thrill. As i said Its visually great in many respects but that being said there are some issues with the shaders, and setting the shadows to high tanks my fps but medium or lower the shadows are a flickering blobby mess. Still it runs fine enough but could be better. Sound wise excellent bar the atmospheric sounds which are great albeit a bit loud at times,  voice acting was really good i think.Really a great game in many respects, i think it could be better with less repetition and if the world was more open and you didnt need to backtrack so much i believe it would be outstanding.

_childDocuments_.review: I am SO MAD about all those negative reviews which are complete lies.1. THE GAME  SAVE BETWEEN RUNS, STOP LYING. It takes literally max 5 minutes to go to the next section or back to the garage. If you don't have that much time for a game, just stop buying and playing games completly.2. People are complaining that the game is too hard. You can turn off everything in the settings that makes the game harder. You have so many different options. And then they complain that the game is too boring without the difficulty.... The timer is there for a reason. There are even zones without a timer. You are supposed to go out multiple times to farm materials. The game wants you to hear the sirens of the storm and then get stressed. If you dont like it, turn it off. Just like losing items on death, just turn it off if it's so frustrating. Adding to that: It's not that easy to die.3. To address some other reviews: You dont have to install a pride flag, flags dont hurt you. Read what the game is before you buy it and then leave a bad review, because it is not what you imagined. Yes you get a lag spike sometimes when a new shader loads in, it lasts for like 1 second and only for the first time it loads in. The game itself runs perfectly fine on mid settings on my GTX 1060 6gb and it still looks absolutely awesome. There was 1 bug for me now, but completly exiting the game and re-entering fixed it. It's still a new game from a small team. Takes a bit to fix all the bugs, submit a report if you find one (it's right on the main menu screen). And no, the storm definetly doesnt instantly kill you, you have enough time to loot and drive back. If there is a region with fast storm, rush through it.Now for the main gameplay loop:You got your car and your garage. In the garage you have all the time you need and many different tools to upgrade and customize your car. Then there are zones when you drive out of your hub. You drive out there, loot things and see many different anomalies (things that make your looting bit harder and can be scary, especially the sounds), storm comes, you drive either to the next section or warp back to the garage to fix and upgrade. In my opinion it could count as a horror game, the maps can be really dark and the sounds and visuals of anomalies can be scary, but you get used to them as you explore the world. Yes I've been frustrated too once, but got back to the garage, fixed my car and lost some materials, farmed them again and everything was fine again. Got bullied really hard from many different anomalies at once.Great game, love the idea and the looks.Also a little help with the tinkering station because that's the only thing not really explained to you:(Your car can develop random quirks, like when you drive backwards, your hood opens up, etc)You select it like this:What part has to do something - What exactly does have to happen with the part - What other part gets affected - What exactly happens with the affected part.As with my example:Car - drives backwards - hood - opensAfter you diagnosed the right thing (all smilies), you can switch over to another menu with [E] to fix the quirk.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Fun survival-scavenger-with-a-car game. Plot is meh, Stalker-roadtripping vibe is cool. Decent if short soundtrack also! It's not for everyone but worth getting on sale. Quirky, interesting but rough around the edges and a tad undercooked 7.7/10In detail: If you like scavenger games and like doing it through a haunted but helpful car in an arena that is reminiscent (a little bit) of Chernobyl from the Stalker games then try this game out. I liked the concept of the game when I saw the trailer and what's shown in the trailer is basically the game. The story is lacklustre, the protagonist is mute and bland. There are some cringe current day politics inserted in the game but which can be wholly ignored and there is a distinct lack of any endgame unless you are really hooked to the game loop.Positives: The car mechanics are fun. Looking after it and boosting its qualities is fun. As is going into the anomalous zone and scavenging for materials. The base building is fun as well though it does become tedious towards the end game. The soundtrack is surprisingly good. It definitely could have more songs in it. After a few hours you will start hearing your favourites a bit too much and skipping past the more forgettable ones. The story is ok. Didn't pull me in.The voice acting is good, it's just a shame that the protagonist is silent. The game can get a tiny bit spooky at times which adds to the immersion. Although there's nothing to really creep you out properly.Satisfyingly challenging. you feel horrible when a trip ends in failure. There are features you can tweak to make the game easier if you're struggling, though some of them will deactivate achievements. Negatives. The plot is boring. I thought the whole point was to escape but in the end you don't even have that as an option. The post-endgame is just you back in the garage. If you love the gameplay loop then fair enough, you can continue scavenging for crafting materials, but other than doing it for the sheer love of the loop, there's no narrative incentive to do it. The protagonist doesn't talk or even have limbs! I tried looking down and couldn't see any legs or arms, so (for me personally obviously) this broke the immersion at times as I imagined my character was just a floating camera lol. The story in general is told through the fun medium of....collecting text and audio logs. Boring! There are some instances of VERY BAD explanation of what things do (car upgrades) or even how the quirk detector works. You just have to figure it out with trial and error. Again, not the worst thing, but I think it's a design flaw more than an intended game feature. Unnecessary current day political inserts: The game is based in 1998. BLM and all the various alphabet genders do not exist. And yet, when you unlock the station to decorate your car with stickers, I noticed that the game gave me 25 stickers for free, "oh nice" thought I. I open my station and see BLM stickers as well as the 23 different stickers for all the various menu of genders that blue states in the US allow you to be now. It's cringe, it's immersion breaking and it's unnecessary. Make it optional DLC or better yet don't have it! I'm trying to survive an anomalous, radioactive zone in 1998 and yet it's necessary that instead of a funny 'how's my driving ?' sticker I get a sticker that represents something that didn't exist in 1998. Stupid! Very very stupid. The "enemies" lack depth. You basically encounter a set number of enemies in the beginning and as you advance you just meet the same but stronger. They missed out on the opportunity to make this game scary by adding more creepy enemies or even have a 'entity' that can stalk you.

_childDocuments_.review: Driving through the wilderness inside of my car. Everything was grand -- until I get sucked into a world full of danger, intensity, and unknown. Pacific Drive is incredible: from it's beautiful scenery to its treacherous journeys, the game has lots of twist and turns (in the roads of course)! When I stepped into the world of Pacific Drive I was greeted with an unforgettable experience.I don't write reviews often, and there's a ton of positive traits that I love about this game. So I made a list of brief pinpoints below on things that I REALLY enjoyed about Pacific Drive: The gameplay of Pacific Drive was very nice. At first, the game seemed very complicated on how to do things such as crafting materials, interacting with objects, stuff like that. I don't tend to play games with a lot of controls because I get confused easily, but in Pacific Drive I got the hang of it very quickly. Some other things I liked about the gameplay was the mechanics. I love that you're able to customize your car to your preference. It made it feel like I had an opportunity to be myself in the game. For example, you can paint your car, add stickers, etc. I'll be honest, I am not very good with lore and this game is pretty built on it. Even though that learning lore isn't my strongest forte, I think the devs made it very easy for players to understand all the events that happened in the game. As you're driving around, you are able to get audio logs and other important information as you explore the game's world. They made it simple for you to be able to reexamine the pieces of lore if you're wanting to look back at incidents that have happened. I also really liked the writing of the game too. The graphics of the game were really incredible. There were times in Pacific Drive I wish I was just transported there to be in that moment. Seriously, what a very beautiful game. The sounds of the game were just as good. The music was great and the sounds in the forest really put me on edge. Sadly, everything has pros and cons. I do not have very many cons at all, but they are there. So I wanted to get over one I can think of: graphical issues. It hasn't happened very often, but there were times in the game where the graphics just glitched. I don't know if it's just my computer or the game itself, but when I am at the auto shop there were graphical issues. Getting off and reloading the game fixes it for me, so it's not too big of a deal but it's there. Pretty much that's all, I did however get stuck in the corner of a house before while exploring on foot and couldn't jump out to free myself.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------So my conclusion is, Pacific Drive is such a gem of a game. If you love driving a car, going on journeys, learning lore, crafting, doing tasks, try to survive, etc. then this game is definitely for you. After watching my favorite YouTuber 8-BitRyan play this game I knew I was in for a treat. Overall, an amazing game, thrilling, beautiful, life threatening, I will definitely be playing this incredible game again.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I received a review copy for my job.  The part where I shill the game:Pacific Drive scratched an itch for "road-likes" I didn't know I had. Eerie atmosphere, fascinating SCP Foundation-esque lore, well-written characters, and an addictive gameplay loop makes Pacific Drive a memorable experience. It's not open-world, more like a huge map with expansive hubs, but that doesn't make it any less fun to explore. The devs built Pacific Drive's controls around WASD driving, and it's definitely the best WASD driving I've experienced in any game.  I realized that the reason why the car felt like trash in the demo was because it WAS trash. Hella satisfying to turn the hunk of junk into a speed demon.  My biggest reason for replaying will be to fill out my upgrades and logbook. I must have missed so many anomalies focusing on the main story. Even at the climax, Pacific Drive kept surprising me with new stuff.The part where I complain: My one bit of advice is save twice at the garage before any important mission. I encountered two soft-locks in 36 hours of play, but that's nothing I couldn't recover from.  I would appreciate a toggle for the UI in a future update too, because it's honestly a bit immersion-breaking seeing so much text on-screen for the game's beautiful moments. I also felt some difficulty spikes necessitated a bit of grinding on my part that I didn't like. Of course, that could 100% be a skill issue on my end, lol. There are performance issues on the highest graphical settings, so you're probably better off sitting on high or medium for the best experience.Final ThoughtsGame good, need patch for minor fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: In most cases, I’m not really a fan of survival games. Horror games are even less appealing to me. From my initial observations, Pacific Drive seemed to be a combination of both of those things. However, after giving it a shot I realized that it doesn’t entirely fit into the archetype of either one. It delivers something familiar but provides a unique world full of mystery and surprises that lets you explore it in the coolest piece of junk I’ve ever been metaphysically bound to.Abbreviated Review: Pacific Drive takes place in the Pacific Northwest, specifically on the Olympic Peninsula. An elevated coastal area of the country that is densely forested and crisscrossed by a handful of winding roads navigating its mountainous tree-covered stretches. Within the game, this is represented extremely well with the atmosphere and general aesthetic of the area captured throughout the accelerated day-night and weather cycles. Yet, within its natural beauty lurks several dangers that will make you forget the views.Taking a page from the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series, the world in which you find yourself is filled with various types of anomalies that have manifested within and warped the partially radioactive environment. However, rather than wielding a machine gun and battling your way through them, you’re supposed to hop into your soul-bound station wagon and haul ass to a less dangerous location. A location that you will then meticulously search to find every possible useable piece of scrap and/or trash to schlep back to your hatchback and store in your trunk for later use. This is the cornerstone of the foundation that is Pacific Drive’s gameplay. Collecting items, avoiding anomalies that either want to inconvenience or kill you and keeping your rolling rust bucket of a vehicle going down the road.While you don’t necessarily live inside of your garbage-collecting station wagon, it is your sole lifeline for your on-and-offroad adventure. Not only does it allow you to get where you need to go faster and allow you to move between the regions, but it also protects you from all of the radioactive, electrical, and physical elements trying to halt your progress. It’s the place where you can keep the spoils of each of your runs into the Exclusion Zone and provides a platform upon which you can build some interesting makeshift technological marvels that make you a little more productive in the process.When you first warp back to your garage respite after a dramatic sky-beam portal escape, you’ll be able to deposit everything you’ve collected in boxes and cabinets scattered around the garage. You can use the raw materials to craft more parts for your vehicle including replacements for its missing body panels and bumpers. You’ll also gain access to a fabrication machine that lets you craft blueprints to learn how to build newer and better parts like lead-lined doors that protect you from radiation and larger fuel tanks to get you further without scavenging for gas.Just as important as crafting car parts, you can build out your garage base to give you handy tools like a repository that repairs broken parts while you’re on your next run or a deconstructor that lets you break down dysfunctional items into their core crafting components. You’ll even get a special machine that lets you apply various cosmetic features to your car like decorative steering wheels and hood ornaments. The mechanics around repairing and upgrading your perpetually breaking conveyance are just as much a part of the core gameplay as the exploration of the world you find yourself within.While you never at any point directly encounter a living creature in Pacific Drive (unless you account for apparently sentient anomalies), you will always have three individuals buzzing in your ears about the tasks you need to complete. The story that they convey, despite being centered entirely around your actions, feels like a secondary element that you are only participating in. The voice actors do a great job and the fairly extensive text and audio lore you discover is well-made, but it was hard for me to feel much attachment to it when it makes up such a small percentage of the overall game. Most of my 25 hours were spent either scavenging for items or trying to maximize my car’s capabilities. Then, many of the moments they did actually feed me exposition, I wasn’t able to focus on listening since I was running for my life or hopping in and out of menus to try to make the most of my trash heap.Though it does take a while for Pacific Drive’s story to come together in a somewhat disjointed way, it never really felt like a major detriment. Yet, there were some anomalies in the overall experience. The most obvious one is the repetition of going out, exploring similar areas, avoiding the same sorts of anomalies, and finding a lot of the same materials. It was compelling for about 10 or 15 hours, but as you cruise into 20+ hours, it starts feeling a bit “samey.” Even the fantastic radio soundtrack starts to get a little old. There’s also been some contentious thoughts on the save system that only saves runs when you enter a new map – which can easily stretch up to half an hour of progress that won’t be saved without moving on. I personally never had any issues with this system though and tried to block out enough time to do at least an entire run (which can stretch 90 minutes or more) each time I booted it up.Quirks aside, even with the clunky “Quirk” system, Pacific Drive is well worth checking out. Though I wasn’t a fan of the scarier aspects, I never had that persistent tingly feeling of existential threats I typically get because most anomalies in the game are environmental. What it did create was a great connection with my vehicle as I made it more functional and capable while being tailored exactly to what I wanted. Swapping parts in and out was satisfying and keeping it all in one piece on the fly was an engaging part of the fun. When you combine that with navigating across the paved, dirt, and non-existent roads of the zone while trying to find everything you need, it culminates in a fantastic experience. Just one that I think I’ve had my fill of… for now… unless there’s some DLC…

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game stretched way too thin.This game wears it's inspirations on it sleeves. Roguelites, survival crafting, driving, extraction. And it does it mostly well. The problem comes from the grind, the pacing, and the resulting stress. It has all the hardships of its inspirations, it has loss on death, everything has pitiful durability, there's timers everywhere you go. And revisiting an area you've been too recently just makes that area harder.What I'm left with is feeling like every trip has only a smidge of progress. Or a serious risk of catastrophic backslide. I had to plan a trip to the far end of the map just for a single rare resource I need a ton of. I spend 30 minutes just getting there, have 5-10 minutes to find and grab what I need, everything on my car broke from the drive this far, and everything finishes falling apart when I have to make the mad dash home.I want to see what's next, but I'm just too burnt out.

_childDocuments_.review: The driver (MC) will eventually realize that station wagon (secondary protagonist, also known as Car chan) is the only character that truly cares about them. Most of the human characters range from "only interests in their own business" to "down right being a jerk to the driver". On the other hand, Car chan is the one that save your ars multiple times, protect you from the unforgiving environment, and accompany you throughout the whole journey even that there are no real benefit for Car chan to help the driver (if it's not true love, I don't know what is).  I think this is where the developer do well. Even though station wagon doesn't speak, you can somewhat grasp their personality. A mixture of yandere and tsundere. Car chan is... well, extremely obsessed with you, if that is not obvious enough. They will also show their tsun side by throwing some tantrum at you... and you know it's Car chan begging for more of your attention, just like a common romantic relationship. Through multiple expeditions, every fix, every upgrade, the driver and station wagon's bond strengthen. Heck, it even become very funny that other human characters tried to gaslight you into believe that Car chan is the reason that the driver was stuck in this hellhole in the first place. Station wagon cannot defend themselves verbally, they can only show with their action, and the driver DO understand.It's a little disappointing that very little information is given about the station wagon despite we spent all of our play time with them, maybe the devs want Car chan to remain this mysterious figure. Or maybe they are saving it for the DLCs, which I will definitely buy. Great car dating sims game, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: God i want to recommend this, there are so many thing great about it but.. i just cant. If a game doesn't respect your time, why would i respect the game. Devs, you have so many things in this game that seem to be at odds with each other, lets start with the fundamental bugs (and why this game feels like early access to me) 1. the optimization is in desperate need of help, the skitters and the frame dragging can be terrible in some places, 2. The settings of the game - minus display settings don't save one exiting the game, meaning you have to change your personalized settings every time you play- for a game that's both Jalopy (not my summer car) and STALKER- you should literally know better. Nothing worse then being on a 4 hr run just to have the game crash out or second part of this- aspects of the game that fight each other-1. Exploration vs time vs no save plus invincible enemies - i felt like i was playing outlast in a car! and if you have no save function it means you have to abandon run which i couldn't help but notice you punish ppl for doing that;  your car is trashed and u don't even have enough in your garage to make another manageable run meaning hey time to start the game over- 8 hrs of progress- GONE. 2. item collecting starts feeling like a job simulator instead of an aspect of Exploration, 3. i cant both play this game and work at my job- look ill be honest devs, no save on exit function means your game is going to fall off even with the good reviews bc ppl will go to games that respect their time. I tried to defend you guys in the discussion topic vehemently, But the more i played this game, the more i started to agree with most of the discussion. I get you're trying to make a rogue like and if a single run didn't take so long-then i wouldn't be giving this a negative review, look at Hades for how to make runs feel fulfilling instead of feeling like im back working in retail  doing the same thing to get items over and over and over again. If you devs are able to do a save on exit function- (if Returnal can do it so can you also i know way to much about UNREAL so i know you can) i will rewrite this thing, i will still have complaints - but at least i dont have to worry about my life getting in the way of playing a game that i can tell you worked hard on- even if it was a bit shortsighted. And love for what was clearly a passion project.(also for the jester reward sry i hurt your sensitive little feelings bro - i know this may seem hard to believe video games are not made for everyone and are rarely made perfectly. )

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up not thinking how much I would enjoy it. I started it up for the first time, three hours went by, maybe 5 hours. Very interesting game and very unique in a few ways. I spent a lot of time gathering and exploring (as much as one could). Graphics look great, very smooth to play. A large tip for this game: Take your time gathering when you can, and read and go through your logbook, it is a very good resource and I overlooked it for the longest time. Would have saved me a lot of time in the beginning. A few things I will like below that I will list that would be good improvements to the game. It took me about ~30 hours to complete the game. Just a warning, I will mention some spoilers below, but some of them will help a lot when you start the game so you have in the back of your head and will not ruin any of the story.Possible Improvements:- Re-balencing a lot of the skills/blueprints you learn, how late in the game you get them, how difficult it is to get materials with the limited time and the inability you have to go back to areas to gather and build up resources and materials.- Make the anchors one click to pickup...- Make shifting, ignition default one click.- Make quarks more easily diagnose-able and less frequent. It seemed they come back every run, and some of them are SUPER annoying. A few of the times, for a certain quark I c never solve even though it seemed like I had put in the correct guesses. Never saw that particular one online either. It is still unsolved even after using my perks/skills to guess. It is the only one that is still an issue. After a while, you just give in to the quarks and stop bothering. It is not even worth it.- I ran into an issue twice where a certain geyser would spawn right under my driver door in the later levels and make it almost impossible to enter my car after grabbing an anchor. It got in such a spot where it would not throw my car in the air but anytime I tried to click my door to get in (and be protected by my car) it would toss me into the air before I was able to, over and over. Even kicking the car did not work, nor did punching my desk. Just make the spawn of these near your car a bit more forgiving, as this can ruin a 30-45 minute run instantly.- Would be nice to have you guys say something or some kind of prompt when a new anomaly is near or on your screen to scan it. Especially at the beginning of the game, it is difficult to realize how important scanning all of them are to progress.- Can we make the other tires other than the off-road tires more useful? Seems like they are the only useful ones by far.- Is there a way to have some areas with perpetual stability in each zone that people can use to gather resources and scan missing anomalies?- Make markers a little more detailed on what you need to do, some of the later missions have you lost and you are on a time limit, I will not list them here, but it is on the last 1/3 of the levels.- Allow some of the utilities in your garage to be unlocked in earlier parts of the game (I will not list the names here), or to increase the usefulness of repair items, especially on tires.Other than those QOL improvements and small balancing, this game is both beautiful, and very enjoyable to play. My favorite part is building and upgrading your base, and upgrading you car, just wish they were a bit more balanced. I feel I spent a ton of time gathering as much as I could, but still had lower level stuff that would have been very useful earlier on. I would highly recommend this game. But would watch a could videos on some tips since it can feel like a lot at the start of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: What I wanted:- Immersive driving exploration game with survival elements. - Rushes of exhilaration while speeding through the unknown.- Big areas to explore, no invisible walls, no loading screens.----------------------What I got:1. Uncomfortable driving experience, feels like you're a giant in a toy car with the child-sized roof blocking over half of your sight. Even with the FOV maxed out you can't really see out the side windows in your peripheral.I don't remember any feeling of shifting gears, felt like very simplistic driving model.2. Tightly scripted corridor levels. You wanna go out and drive? Select a mission from your garage and watch a load screen and get plopped in a little corridor area with invisible walls and a few procedural loot/enemy areas. Then enjoy the load screen at the end of the corridor when you're ready to go back to base.3. Time-wasting repetitive tutorial and gameplay elements. The tutorial starts with some really boring driving for nearly 15 minutes. Then you get about 10 tasks in the garage where the flow for each is something like:push a button to open the cartoon locker, push a button on each thing in the cartoon locker to put it into your backpack, push a button to open your backpack, push a button to equip that new thing, push a button to close the backpack, hold a button to use that thing on your car while waiting 10 seconds, push a button to open your backpack, push a button to unequip that new thing, push a button to equip that other thing, push a button to close the backpack, hold a button to use that thing on your car while waiting 10 seconds, push a button to open the backpack, push a button to unequip the other thing, push a button to close your backpack. Then you get out in the open world and the process to loot anything is pretty much the same as above ^This is the kind of repetitive pattern task that I train my dog to do as punishment, it's not fun guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine "The Long Drive" with more of a direction: add some elements of scientific paranormal (think SCP), and a gameplay loop of drive, explore, loot, escape before the radiation kills you, beef up your car, slap on some paint and decals you found in the zone you visited, repeat. Along the way, you encounter anomalies like the ground shifting, strange robots, unsettling setpieces, stuff flinging itself on the road, friendly dumpsters that somehow give you what you need, stuff falling from the sky for no reason... a bit unsettling, a bit wacky, and always a bit of a different experience every time you go for a drive through the exclusion zone in the pacific north west.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game and very fun, but - and it's a small nitpick - it still falls into the "inclusive" fallacy.In the cosmetics crafting bench - the detailing station - you have approx. 20 different flags in support of various sexual identities, and even BLM (the same guys who beat people on the street and looted stores during riots), but one flag is curiously missing; The Heterosexual, or Straight flag.Considering the majority of players would be of that sexuality by weight of statistics alone, this is rather UN-inclusive.Moreover, you'd expect a game taking place in america to have an american flag - but that is also missing.All in all, it feels like a cheap pandering effort.Again, it's a great game and this is nitpicking, but since nitpicking is the fashion nowadays, I shall permit myself that privilege.

Doing a twenty minute (or more!) junction and then getting bricked out of finishing multiple times- twice literally on the way to extraction- is absolutely a killer and pretty much completely the reason for the negative review. _childDocuments_.review: A fun and enjoyable game with a fantastic loop, but it struggles with an overall weak story that occasionally suffers from questionable exposition decisions that lack cohesion and polish to the point that character interactions between the main cast can feel 'out of character' when compared to later conversations, and the story itself leaves plenty of loose ends that appear relevant at the time, but ultimately go nowhere and are rarely, if ever, mentioned again. Additionally there are some general design issues with a few menus and descriptions within that lack clarity, particularly with the upgrades in the auto shop. Ultimately these issues cause Pacific Drive to fall a bit short of the game that it desires to be.The game could (and likely will) benefit from a few patches to smooth out some of the rough edges it has. It could also greatly benefit from a hardcore difficulty setting for those who would like to squeeze a little more fun out of replays with the extra challenge.

Buuttt... There is 23 heavily political stickers, all catering to a minority that push their political ideology on the majority, flags that did not exist prior to the 2010's. Supposedly, it is "not to exclude anyone", but they could easily have been made part a free DLC, and no one would have been excluded. However, since modern political symbols, are placed in an era which they were never present, never existed, shows it to be a deliberate underhanded choice, to push modern politics on players that play games to have a breather, a break, from all the deranged modern political nonsense------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Besides politics forced on the player, in games that are played to have a breather from all the heavily political deranged nonsense, the game is okay.The game is somewhat similar to an extraction shooter, that was popularized by Escape From Tarkov (Interesting but loosing the gear you worked for is a hard nope), you enter an area and gather loot, navigating various anomalies, and trying to reach an exit.The driving physics is more on the arcade side, with some aspects being somewhat reminiscent of what is realistic. _childDocuments_.review: Great little game, took me 20hish to enjoy the full story, with a healthy mix of farm and main quests.Pros :+ great concept and fun gameplay loop with the car+ tight-knit moments when you zoom out of zone, clutching a difficult extract+ damage feels progressive and balanced, you can clearly feel if you're greeding out or not+ you're free to play to play a high-risk, fast-paced game, or chill out, farm junctions and go out early so not to die+ large array of tools and freedom to pimp and repair car+ great atmopshere and visuals+ polished and well finished (no bug encountered, except for the garage radio volume that can't be changed)+ exceptional voice acting and nice dialogues+ good radio songs+ thank god the character you play remains silent and background-less, please don't do the same mistake as Subnautica 2 and its unsufferable main protagonistCons:- the gameplay has little to no evolution towards the end, anomalies don't get much more interesting- highway junctions should not require an upgrade to skip, and should not be a thing at all ; they slow down pace, eat up more resources than they often give and defeat their original purpose of going fast- crafting curve needs to be a little eased up, or end-game items need to be crafted with mid-zone reagents ; I did not bother acquiring any end-game upgrade as I was already on the end of story when zone 3 mats became available ; that may just be me going too fast with the campaign though- some main missions clearly lack a proper soundtrack (passing the second wall being the biggest one)- let us close that garage door, and let us put custom songs in the game folder for the in-game radioA well-crafted and concise game, that lacks very little gameplay additions to become fully enjoyable to farm and repeat as a proper roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. The concept is excellent, creepy circumstances, a compelling game loop, lots of intrigue, really cool setting, etc. Here is the rub, it has forced me to replay the tutorial section of the game several times due to unrelated issues and wasted so much of my time:1st attempt: Played the opening cinematic and tutorial at the garage, which took a solid 45 minutes because I was trying to learn as much as possible with less than stellar instructions. Set out on the first mission and played for about 45 minutes more before I ran out of time and needed to go to bed. I looked for a save option and surprise, you cant save during missions. I had no choice but the quit and lose all of that progress. Apparently, you can only save at the garage unless it auto saves for whatever cryptic reason.2nd attempt: Played the opening cinematic again, and re-started the tutorial section. I already knew what to do so I started prepping the vehicle ahead of the prompts. Got the the part where it requires some specialized parts from a cabinet, but for some reason they weren't there. These parts are necessary to complete the tutorial so I waste a ton of time trying everything I could think of looking for them and a workaround. Eventually, I googled it and found out that it is a known bug and there is no fix. No choice but to restart.3rd attempt: Played through the opening cinematic, and through the tutorial again, following the prompts exactly. Once the tutorial was done, I saved the game so I wouldn't have to go through that again. At that point I called it a night since it was too late to keep playing. The next day, finally ready to start the first mission, with plenty of gaming time ahead of me, snack nearby, and a good bit of motivation. I play through the first mission, collecting everything it says to collect, crafting everything it says to craft, and going through all of the steps. Finally some real game play. I get to the end of the mission and the lady in the radio directs me to drive into a pillar of light, so I head towards what I think that is referring to, apparently I misunderstood the directive and promptly died. OK, so what happens when you die? Back to the garage you go, but with an empty inventory. 4th attempt:  I had read that you can head back out to where you died and pick up you lost items. Fine,I set out to do that, but it wont let you simply go again, you have to repair the car all over again, and go through a huge checklist of busywork before it lets you head out. I get to work, still motivated to get back out there, unfortunately, I couldn't complete the checklist because my inventory was empty. I scoured the entire area for supplies but came up short. There simply isn't any obvious way to complete the checklist if your inventory is empty upon arrival at the garage and you already used the contents of the cabinet in the garage, (including the contents of the helpful dumpster, so don't think I missed that.)OK, at this point I was getting irritated, but I thought no big deal, I'll just reload that post tutorial save and redo the first mission again...  THE F%!#ing save was overwritten when I died! The only choice at that point would be to start all over again. How could the devs let a player go for 7 friggen hours and not give them a path forward if they die. I am not going to try again. No Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique and fun game. Gives me stalker vibes. I will say, the gameplay can be a bit repetitive, and the quirk system really kills the experience in some ways. For those who dont know, your car itself is an anomaly, so with that comes these "quirks." Essentially, its issues with your vehicle, like the horn honking when you shut a door or the windshield wipers turning on when you open the hood. From what I can tell, its completely random. You can fix these quirks by going to a station and fixing it, but there can be an unlimited number of these quirks present at once, and if you fix one, another can pop up. This in itself is kind of cool, but its problematic to the gameplay because you have to be VERY specific about what is wrong and what happens when you do what. For instance, one of my issues is that the car horn is honked whenever the trunk closes. Very obvious issue and easily described. However, the game will not give you hints if you're guess is close, and for some reason, that isnt whats happening. I cannot replicate the issue doing anything else with the car, and its very obviously happening when I close the trunk, but its telling me thats not the issue so I have no idea. That in itself is not a huge issue, just a funny problem with the car, but what is actually impacting the gameplay is that the right rear door will just open for no reason. Like I can literally walk away from the car and it will open. So theres no way for me to know what is causing this and you cant just infinitely guess into oblivion, because there's a limit of 8 guesses. So 8 guesses and once you go out of the garage again, you get 8 more guesses. As well as the fact that it would take thousands of guesses to go through all the combinations of issues to just fix one problem. However I currently have something like 4 or 5 quirks on my car. Another quirk that is pretty impactful on the gameplay is that the headlights go on when the steering wheel is turned 100% to the right or the left. Again, i just described the issue to you perfectly, however when I go to the quirk-fixing station, this isnt a correct description of the problem, and the issue cannot be fixed. This system is really annoying and the rear door opening is seriously making me not want to play the game. Its a cute feature and reminds me of those "customer states" videos on YouTube, but its a mechanic that adds nothing to the game and only takes away from the already slightly repetitive gameplay.I think this is a brilliant game but I hope some of these little weird features get fixed, or outright removed. I only want this game to get better because its really unique and fun to play!
