_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on the 'extraction looter' genre, with some cool mechanics and great atmosphere. The driving is weighty and feels great, with some lovely rumble feedback if you play on controller. It really puts you in the vehicle and makes you feel any broken part or terrain change. Your car is responsive, fun to drive, and reacts to damage and mechanical issues believably. From the way the car handles, the controller rumble feedback, and the noises the car makes, you can usually work out the issue before even looking at the damaged part. There are some minor physics glitches every now and again but each patch they release lowers their number and severity which is great sign from the developers (I've only had a couple items dropping through the ground, small jiggling when parked and a few little hops, nothing game breaking or run ending). The mechanic portion of the game is great too, with you slowly upgrading your garage and car with little QoL changes run after run. The customisation is varied, with pretty much total freedom on what parts, upgrades, or visuals you want to focus on, and the little baubles and trinkets you find in the world for your car are always a nice little bonus to a run, with lots of paints, decals, stickers, shifters, hood ornaments, steering wheels and more to find littered throughout the boxes and bags you dig through every run.Each run has great choice for how you want to play it, with different paths to take through the map. Do you want a leisurely drive with a few towns to loot and explore? You can do that. Do you want a crazy race through acid rain and lightning bolts where venturing outside the car leads to almost certain death? Pick a route through a storm zone. The game allows you to pick your route and customise the difficulty to your heart's desire. Most of the locations aren't overly different (at least within each area) but the driving and anomalies within them keeps everything fresh and interesting. The story is sparse, with most of it being delivered through little radio chats, with a lot left up to you to find audio logs, diaries, scan locations and anomalies for information on how the zone got so messed up. There are a few 'story missions' where you have to go to a few locations within a run and activate some machines or find some files but you choose when you want to complete the objectives, and you can back out at any time. I prefer this method of storytelling, leaving more up to the player instead of forcing it down your throat and I found the radio conversations engaging and funny, and the mystery of the zone kept me heading out to learn more. The looting is quick and rewarding, with a few accessibility options to make thing easier if you so desire, and finding an armoured truck or roadside cache is always fun and exciting.All in all a great game with solid driving physics, great customisation, and a mysterious world that draws you in, making every run rewarding and different. You really feel attached to your car (oh god the remnant has it's claws in me), adding your own personal touches and slowly upgrading it run after run. It is very rewarding to feel the improvements of new wheels, or an engine upgrade, allowing you to go further every run, learning more about the crazy world full of danger and mystery, and how the zone got to the way it is now. Hoping this 'looter tooter' keeps getting updates because it's a great merging of 2 vastly different genres and I can only see it getting better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game for those who love weird ♥♥♥♥ and figuring out how things work. _childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a very hard game to review, as it takes an incredibly simple game loop, and somehow manages to keep it interesting with a fresh new breath of life every expedition. The game loop consists of driving around to find resources or an objectives. You then drive like hell to get away from anomalies, or escaping the catastrophic destabilization of your zone, returning home to your garage to upgrade your vehicle, rinse and repeat progressing further into the Olympic Exclusion Zone.What really stood out to me about this game is how incredibly immersive and astounding the atmosphere of pacific drive is. Combined with the stellar music and sound design leads to a jaw dropping level of world building that I can't possibly put into words for this review. I also really enjoyed the variety of ways to play this game, their are so many various upgrades and strategies you can use to survive and thrive in this game. Ex: you can decide to step away from using gas to power your car and completely swap to an electric engine which will drastically effect how you play. Every early to mid game upgrade felt incredibly impactful on the way you play and could make the difference between life and death. However, I will say that the "end game" upgrades were ludicrously expensive and overall not at all worth the effort as I beat the game using zero "corrupted energy parts" which are the final zones rewards, without a single failed run through any point in this game. Which brings me to my next critique of this game, I went into this game completely blind without any prior knowledge or research and as I played I had a total of ZERO failed runs. Not to say I didn't have any close calls, as I can think of several instances were I was panicking as the feeling of death rapidly approached my character. But I feel as though that was more due to the incredible atmosphere as mentioned earlier. I almost wish there was some sort of difficulty slider OTHER then just a harsher death penalty.In conclusion, this game was incredibly fun, and I definitely recommend purchasing this game. The game play loop may have been repetitive, but the large variety of anomaly's, weather hazards, quirks, and zone factors spiced each expedition up immensely making boredom near impossible. Additionally the story was rather intriguing, and definitely served its purpose to drive you forward into the chaos of the Olympic Exclusion Zone. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a great game, with an interesting and engaging story, characters that you want to learn more about and a world inhabited with weird and wacky things around every corner. Making each trip into this sem-rough-lite feel new and interesting. I really do love the world of Pacific Drive, the strange and mysterious place filled with anomalies and makes the mind wonder about their creation and purpose. It combines the feeling of a drive through the scenic wilderness with the world of SCP. The only downside to the game is the more repetitive gameplay, outside of discovering new anomalies / resources or building a new tool there is very new and engaging gameplay within each run. So if you aren’t a fan of more grindy, resource gathering games then this might not be for you. But that honestly is the only downside of the game for me, I still had a lot of fun with the game and no game has ever been more attached to a car in a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: (About halfway through the game at the time of review)I really, really like this game. It is very immersive, the story got me hooked, the gameplay loop is completly my style of survival games, and for a game that requires a lot of crafting/inventory managment, the Quality of Life is very polished.I enjoy a lot some of the game design decisions. Few examples:- At first I feared that the game would be very grindy, farming basic resources over. But the game has a system where each trip can only end in a given zone ONCE. Which means if you play slow and keep planning trips to safe areas from the start, you will later on be forced into the more dangerous areas later anyway. (And each zone has a hidden timer before the storms closes in, so even if the player has a good amount of time to farm, it's not an infinite amount of time, and I find that nuance important)- If a craft requires intermediate products, those can be crafted on the same page. Even complex recipes can be crafted in a few seconds, and the required resources can be anywhere (on you, in the car, in the garage...)- It is (mostly) not the same resources to craft new car parts and to repair existing parts, and the resources given back when deconstructing a part at the garage is quite generous. This means that designing your car before a trip and maintaining it during the trip are two independant skills, and getting good at each of them is very rewarding.I'm writing all of this because I'm sad this game isn't getting as much recognition as I feel it should. I suspect that survival game enjoyers didn't look at this game because the game looks like it is a lot about cars from the outside, and story enjoyers or car enjoyers are turned off by the survival/crafting aspects being too overwhelming for them.But if you're a survival game enjoyer, please give this game a chance, it is very polished and well refined.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rogue lite looting, crafting, survival, sci-fi game. You are stuck in an abandoned experimental zone where strange sci-fi phenomenon happen and you have to get out. You drive around in a station wagon and walk around looting materials to craft new tools and upgrades for the car. The biggest problem with the game is it is prone to crashing and relies on an auto save system. So of course I crashed and lost an HOUR of progress. This was only 94 minutes into my playtime. So I stopped playing the game, because that is the most irritating design decision I have seen in a looter crafter. My rating = 5/10 The game has a cool atmosphere and ideas behind it that make it stick out in the crowded field of survival crafting games, but awful design decisions around saves and the game being unstable make the actual play experience frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: *SPOILERS AHEAD*Overall, not a bad game. Interesting mechanic, and it plays well for the first 10-15 hours, then the enemies, the storms, and the gameplay itself starts to get repetitive and boring. The outer zone is very well fleshed out, but the middle and deep zones are well... boring to put it simply. The story was immensely disappointing, starts off with some great mysteries (what is LIM tech, how does it work, what are the forces behind it, what went wrong, what caused the mass hallucination, etc?) that really pull in your interest, but then it falls flat in every way when it comes to developing these points/actually explaining these things. The character development also was really weak, you start to sympathize with/connect with the characters in the beginning, but your interactions/them talking to you become much less frequent, and you find yourself not really caring so much. I didn't even really bother with the other news clips and other bits of info that you get, it just really didn't grab me. The other instances of remnants affecting others were barely touched on, would have made for some neat side quests to learn more about those instances.The ending is probably the most unforgivable part of this, The Well, which was hyped up to be this crazy spot where it appears most of these anomalies originated from, turns out to be so plain and boring, Big Cappy was much more interesting. The end sequence made no sense, having the driver walk though an area full of random objects with some flashbacks from events he never experienced? Then to just walk out to the car, in an area that is supposedly so full of Gamma radiation that you'd cook practically instantly and drive away? And after all of the regret and the desire to fix the Olympic Peninsula, Oppy just tosses it away, basically saying "Ah well, all of my lifes work here, but I'm going to leave, bye!" and leaves Francis and the Driver to fix what damage her project created? I get her following her husbands advice, but couldn't this have happened after the damage was fixed? Would have tied that off better.Frankly, I think if they would have spent as much effort on the story and the character development as they did with their "inclusive" efforts (i.e. the litany of flags that gets puked in your face the second you build the detailing station, etc, etc), this would have been a FAR better game. Shame, as it showed so much promise in the start. Developers, please, stop with the inclusive nonsense, just make good games. Please.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst thing about Car Mechanic Simulator is that, while the core game loop is quite interesting, beyond that, it's a bit of a shallow grind as you just end up doing the same jobs over and over again.  Which feels like a job, so, uh, well done, Car Mechanic Simulator.  But this doesn't have very long term, lasting appeal for gamers. So, what if we took Car Mechanic Simulator and married it to a horror/crafting/supernatural game where you need to drive around a spooky area affected by a great and mysterious supernatural phenomenon?  Now you have great game mechanics and a reason to play the game!  And that's what they did with Pacific Drive.  Fantastic concept, delivered well.  From a technical standpoint, all the basic optimisation and customisation features are there.  Professional quality delivery plus a great game concept turns this into a game I can gladly suggest people consider buying.$30 is a little steep, but not insultingly so.  As usual, there's better value for money if you grab this on sale, so keep an eye out for bundles or discounts.  You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This genre mish-mash is one of the more unique and interesting games I've played in a bit. I have massive respect for developers that try and do something original and unique, and they really did that here.Even though the game arguably has some minor performance issues, its good sides vastly outnumber the bad ones. The graphics are pretty decent. The voice acting and writing in general are great. The story is peculiar, bizarre, and interesting to explore.The gameplay itself keeps you on edge. This game's atmosphere can be really, really unsettling, and puts some real pressure on you sometimes. I love the attention to detail in the garage, the myriad of ways you can customize your car, and all the cool stuff you can install and play with. The garage mechanics are outstanding. I love the quirk removal tool.If you don't mind driving a car and want to experience something truly unique that is obviously put together by people who are passionate about gaming and love this project, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Survival Game where your base is a garage and your means of travel a car, that's also an entity and bound to your character. You quicktravel over a map, explore new areas, find stuff for upgrades for your car and your garage and continue towards the center of the anomaly.You can also walk around on foot, which you will be doing alot. Exploring, dismantling items, fixing your car and doing everything you can't do from inside of a car.Seems to be very story-driven, and not really open world, as you travel to specific zones and then teleport back to the garage.Overall interesting idea, fun gameplay and a fair price, if you ask me. Definitely worth if you like these type of games and can get over the condescending jerk treating everyone like crap on the radio.Well, sometime's she's nice, to be fair. But she quickly makes it up by being a jerk again. And, of course, everyone loves her, because people love getting treated like crap. It's a backpack manager with exploration, and your trusty car.The story (So far for me, I'm only 6 hours in) is good. Albeit a bit railroaded.The first few hours are very unintuitive, I died a few times because I had no idea what I was doing. _childDocuments_.review: This is a love story between a boy (at least in my case) and his pos car.  I don't know if you're like me but I HATE station wagons.  Well I used to.  Damn, if this game doesn't have me looking at them now.  You are NOT driving around in a formula one racer, not even at the end.  But that doesn't matter.  You realize pretty quickly that your car is your lifeline and vice versa.  Treat it well and it'll keep you alive.  Treat it poorly and you likely won't survive to see another day.  The devs have done a fantastic job of pacing the progression of the car, the mechanic shop with which you fix and upgrade your car, and the zones you need to traverse in your car in order to find parts and resources to upgrade and progress through the story.  I was deeply concerned about the pacing, but it's so well balanced!  The story may not win any awards, but it shouldn't be overlooked.  It serves its purpose to drive the player forward into new zones and greater challenges.  In essence, it helps control the pacing.  I cannot recommend Pacific Drive enough.  In a time when so many great games have come out, this is the one that sucked me in, and that I needed to finish before moving back to any others.  Seriously, I started up Palworld, Enshrouded, Last Epoch, and Sons of the Forest, and all have been really good!  ...But this was the one that drew me in and wouldn't let go.

_childDocuments_.review: You might look at my hours and think, they must like the game! Yes, yes I do! That's exactly why, in it's current state, I cannot recommend it yet.The story is really good and I like the voice actors, it slowly unfolds and you get dragged in until you're in too deep. This brings me to my first complaint, the story is so good that I WANT to pay attention to it. However, you have to pay attention to the game while playing otherwise your car could end up in ruins. I was never able to fully pay attention to either sadly. The game tells you that you can reorganise lore fragments at the fax machine but the way this is done is abysmal, you can either take them out or click on them to drop to the bottom of the list. There is no 'sorting'.  Now, your car, oh boy, here we go, where do I even start. The concept of upgrading your car all the time, getting new attachments, paints and decals is cool! What isn't cool is that your panels/doors/wheels/attachments can just randomly get an unfixable debuff after one run that makes them completely useless. At least you can throw them into the scrapper which gives you back a decent amount of materials. Now, back to upgrading. A lot of the upgraded car parts feel rather lackluster. I don't see a single reason to ever get the electric engine for example; you would have to modify your entire car just to accommodate for the electric engine and lose out on a lot of attachments. Most of the damage types in this game are avoidable, electricity being harder to avoid which results in just using the specific doors/panels that are resistant to electricity (plus they got more durability compared to anti-radiation for example). The same goes for upgraded tools, half of them do not feel worth upgrading because the materials required to craft them are very late game and hard to get. While on the other hand you'll be drowning in other low tier materials so why not constantly craft the cheaper tools. (I'm a loot goblin)Now, almost everything you encounter in the game, you can scan. But instead of giving you actual useful information... it's just lore and you have to figure out what it does yourself? Now, most the anomalies are self explanatory but not all of them. Ah and of course, quirks. The concept of your car having quirks is fun, they can sometimes even benefit you! My car would get a burst of speed if I honked my horn for example. But some of the quirks are really hard to identify and can ruin your ongoing ruin (which you can solve with upgrades and spending energy on it).I like collecting little cosmetics, once you own one, you own it forever which is nice. The free to use pride stickers are a nice touch. However, the decals have a limited amount of uses sooooo if you have to replace any part of your car and don't have a spare decal? Too bad, same goes for the paint. The collection of music in the game? Splendid! I love listening to the in-game radio.Two weird bugs I encountered:1. I loaded my game and the entire garage was tilted at a 45 ° angle? -> This was fixed by restarting my game.2. Half my map didn't seem to load, it was just a blue void? -> This was fixed once I drove into the part that didn't load.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels impossible to move forward without disabling damage entirely. All RNG. There's no guarantee that you'll find the materials you need and the amount of damage your car regularly sustains is immense, even if you do everything right and are very careful and observant. Also, you can't save your game outside of the garage, which makes it terribly inaccessible for ppl with busy lives and you might lose hours of progress due to a brief loss of your internet.Apart from that, the overall atmosphere in the game is horribly lonely and isolated. Even the NPCs who speak to you over the radio only pipe up for a few seconds here and there when you're not doing the main "quest." Moreso than other survival games, the sense of anxiety and dread I felt at all times was so terrible I could rarely stand to play for more than a few hours at a time, and I rarely felt good or victorious upon making it back to the garage. I only felt relieved when I closed the game, which I think speaks volumes.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 A great experience with the game opening with Ghost on the Road to the ending with more cool stuff happening (no spoilers). The music throughout the game was amazing, the atmosphere was on point, the anomalies were interesting and the upgrading was a lot of fun. The game is labeled a survival horror game but don't let that scare you off. I would say at most it is more atmospheric than horror.  I would also recommend to anyone who wants to simply enjoy themselves to play with punishments off. :)This game had a few bugs unfortunately though none impacted the final score or overall enjoyment of the game. DirectX12 would crash on launch so playing on DirectX11 fixed it and allowed me to play with no problems. When you exit the car by towers there is the chance to be teleported to the top of the tower. I had this teleporting bug happen twice and each time I had to fall down but the game only dropped my health to 1% each time. The garage radio will be off but play music on returning to it. Some ideas for the game. An upgrade that puts speakers outside the garage base so you can still jam out while getting scrap or looking through lockers out there. The quirk-fixing machine is very hard to read with black on orange the way that it is. Maybe some credit music, unless it was a bug when I hit credits no music played and with a game full of great soundtracks it was surprising. I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a game to vibe to.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play a ton of survival or crafting type games, but I really like this one. _childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere and intriguing setting. Voice acting is very good and the story is for the most part intriguing enough to keep you engaged in the game's world. If you like survival games and picking every item not nailed to the ground, highly recommend picking this game up.That said.About 80% of the way through the game, it feels like the devs run out of money/ideas. Late game progression is horrible. Upgrades are essentially pointless because you have barely any missions left to do and resource requirements for these upgrades compared to how quickly you can gather them is ridiculous. You can continue playing after completing the story, but what's really the point?The ending is really, really bad. There’s some subtle hints here and there what’s at play in the zone, but the game doesn’t take this anywhere. I honestly can't recall an ending this unsatisfying and disappointing. It might be a simple case of sequel-baiting tho.Also, the game doesn’t run very well, especially for how it looks. There are small, annoying bugs like not being able to close menus while browsing logs and bigger bugs like the settings menu not working properly.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will contain end-of-game spoilers for the game.During the drive in which you're meant to cross the deep zone's wall, if you arrive at the map without a LIM-Shield, you are soft locked unless you manage out of bounds clips after which you can escape. This took me around two hours to figure out and accomplish. I've read forum posts that indicate it's possible to still proceed with the mission without the required item, but the game gives you no hints on how to progress, and I haven't verified this.The second bug occurred during the ending sequence- I jumped out of the TV corridor after reaching the centre of the deep zone and after falling into the void for a minute I was dumped into the end-game sequence. After I cleared this, the game entered a permanent, unplayable state with strange, large-font prompts that I was unable to reset with load-games or restarting the program, effectively destroying my save file as I was unable to leave the garage.It's a charming game, but as I'd like to see attention to these issues and I will not be playing through the latter half of the game again in order to reach end-game, I will mark this as negative to hopefully see attention brought to this to improve the game's state.

_childDocuments_.review: Practically all the tags for this game I consider to be BS. This is a timed extraction game.You go into a map that has a time limit before deadly 'something' comes and kills you. You have to gather a set amount of energy to create a teleport to leave and go back to your garage. There are also buildings that can be looted for crafting. Do you go looting or just get the energy and leave? All the tension in this game comes from the time limit. If there was no time limit, then this would just be a game where you drive your car to avoid objects and gather resources to progress through the crafting tree.You can drive on the roads, where anomalies will literally, just spawn out of the ground right in front of you. Or you can drive off road, taking massive damage driving through trees and hitting rocks. Either way, they both pissed me off. The roads are inefficient routes with cheap game mechanics and driving off road avoids the cheap mechanics, but then you have to spend time and resources on repairing the some 15 parts your car has.I didn't find the driving enjoyable. The game seems to even do things to literally make it not enjoyable. Like having the ignition where a stereo normally is, with a giant hit box that causes you to turn the key when you mean to hit the gear shift. Or just the fact that I'm driving this crappy station wagon having to either, avoid things popping out of the ground right in front of me, or go off roading through the woods. Maybe if I had some fast car, driving fast, then simply avoiding objects as gameplay may be fun. But driving a slow crappy car avoiding objects, I didn't find fun. The crafting is interesting, but all very gamey. Why does your scanner only have 3 charges? Because you can upgrade it. Why is your gas tank small? So you can upgrade it. Why do you take so much damage? Because you can upgrade your car doors and panels. Why is my trunk so small? Because you can upgrade it. There are some interesting tools, like the pile driver and scrapper, but the upgrade tree is massive with mostly gamey things to make your crappy car better. It's interesting on the surface, but when you realise it's mostly stat upgrades and not new things is when I lost interest in it.One that killed me, literally, was not having this energy detector. At this point, the energy always showed on my map, so I'm thinking, why do I need this detecter? So I didn't craft it. And then the next map I played had a debuff on it that causes the energy to not show on the map. I couldn't find the energy to create the teleport and died. Which is a massive resource loss. Not only do you lose the resources you gathered on the map, but you also lose a portion of the things you brought with you, as well as having to repair damage on your car.I like the atmosphere and that is the only thing that has kept me going. The driving is boring. Game mechanics feel cheap, there is no combat and it just ended up feeling like a boring grind game to me. Drive my car, avoiding objects to get resources, under a time limit so I can extract with my goodies and do it again until the game says I've reached the end.Usually, I would just move on. But this game got hyped, along with all the BS tags it has on Steam makes me feel like I've been deceived on what this game really is. It's an extraction game. Which if I knew that originally, I would have never have purchased it.

I spent over 60 hours in this game and 100% recommend this if you enjoy Raft or Subnautica. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game way more than makes sense.The core gameplay loop is shockingly engaging, and the eerie vibes are *chef's kiss*. I get why the grindy criticism exists, and I detest grind, but the way the game pokes and prods you with different challenges and encourages self-driven (get it?) learning about the way its mechanics, world, and lore works sucks you right in.Diverging from just doing the story-driven sorties pays back in spades in this regard. Getting out to different areas of the zone and exploring is really awesome, for the resources, landscapes, and unique scenarios you end up getting yourself into. The more you do this, the more customization you can do to your station wagon, which in turn feeds right back into more tactical decision making in the gameplay loop. Also, visual customization is more fun than it should be (maybe because you sometimes have to weigh picking up these items against carrying more crafting resources) and can actually serve a gameplay purpose (i.e. visibility of the vehicle in the environment).I do get the criticism of the save system, because sometimes a drive/sortie can be hours long. I do, however, appreciate how effectively the gameplay benefits from forcing you in this way to engage with it in a free-flowing manner; save scumming would destroy a lot of the fun in the gameplay loop. I have a few suggestions for how to approach the game with the save system in mind if you have limited time to play:- Speed through in-between areas with minimal looting. Take advantage of grabbing easily accessible energy anchors in stable areas to be able to have the charge you need to open a portal when they are available.- Upgrade to get more scanner charges. You can choose several available "nodes" on the map this way to have the ability to open portals back to the garage somewhere closer, if you can't make it all the way to your furthest objective.- You can modify your gameplay settings on the fly to abandon a drive without loosing your gathered items.- Pause the game and leave it running in the background 🤷‍♂️It *might* be possible for the devs to make a save-scumming avoidant save system that would allow for a bit more flexibility. A few thoughts for them to maybe think about: During a drive, make the only way to save be a save and close. Maybe only when no danger is present. Maybe forcing a restart of the given area.I'll conclude by paraphrasing another review:Hit myself in the head with my trunk door and lost 2% health. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: While rough on the edges few games capture the eerie vibes as good as Pacific Drive. I love driving and roadtriping around the PNW. The Olympic Peninsula is a beautiful place full of awe inspiring vistas and lonely roads. I've had weird experiences over those roads driving in the night. I love it.This game makes use of this setting and beautiful places and mixes it with the eeriness of an alien world. Sprinkle some roguelite, crafting and extraction mechanics and you have a game where every run feels slightly different, there's always that feeling of wanting to see more of this beautiful yet uncanny world but also feeling the rush of knowing the nature is against you, that you're insignificant to this perilous world.As a game the mechanics are force you to take hard choices of prioritization, same as your battle against time or wondery. Should you take this harsh path to get faster or take the scenic road. Should you focus on the resources or the energy or just trying to make it? Each trip takes a long time to get there, but also takes a lot of time of preparation. In this aspect it truly captures the nature of roadtrips. It forces you to plan your route, study each stage and pack your car accordingly. There will always be unexpected things along the road but you can (and should) try to anticipate for things. At the beginning this can be overwhelming, there's so much data and so many things to explore and learn about. Every time you find an anomaly it remains mysterious about what effects it can have on you and your car. You always feel brittle against this world, always trying to make the best out of the trip. Isn't this what every road trip is like? Making the best out of getting to a new place?I think no other game captures the awe and experience of roadtrip as well as this one. I love cars. I love the PNW. I love the feeling of wonder at every corner in the exclusion zone. Even though this game is full of bugs and performance is atrocious and there's so much downtime crafting things and managing inventory this game just feels great!You'll like this if you like games like: Subnautica, Control, Outer Wilds.The Best: So much to explore, such eerie vibes but not scary. You're always in between planning your route and time yet managing your time and resources.The Bad: Performance is really bad, you'll need a beefy PC to run this beautifully and performant. Many bugs (annoying but not breaking ones). This would be great in the Steam Deck but performance isn't there.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I still have to complete the storyline but I played enough for a review. This game gives me the same vibes as Subnautica, but with less crafting and faster gameplay. The graphics are good, the setting is great, the plot is well written. You get really attached to the car, you feel safe when inside, you don't want to walk too far away and you care if it get damaged. It really grows into you and it fits perfectly with how the story develops.And having loved Alan Wake and Control, I think the developers set this game in the same universe, without ever explicitly saying it. There are so many things in common that it can't be otherwise, and I love it.Pros:- Great setting- Great visual and sound direction- Nice crafting system, not too complicated and it impacts gameplay meaningfully but without being frustrating- The game doesn't guide you too much in terms of what you should craft and when, and I like it (Minecraft vibes)- Love the gameplay loop (go out of your base, loot/follow the story mission, get energy from anchors to open a gateway back to base, activate gateway and rush to it as the level collapse into chaos) and the difficulty is well thoughtCons:- Mirrors destroy your fps, bring all the mirror settings to the minimum to double your fps, they aren't that useful gameplay-wise or noticeable graphics-wise- Sometimes you get too many levels without gateways to your base and you are forced to do a few more levels just to find a gateway and exit- Inventory management of the different resources at the base should be improved with a better auto sorting, higher stacks and shared space between the different storages

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely fun and well made survival game. It takes the fun, tense parts of rougelikes and extraction games and applies it to a fun loop of exploration and gathering that feels impactful. There's a few maps that you can tell are repeated, but with the other elements of the map being randomized and how different each run can be, it never really feels like you're repeating the content over and over unless you spend a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend Pacific Drive.If:- You enjoy exploring, setting-based storytelling (similar to a walking sim with much more to do)- You enjoy extraction games - or like the idea of them, without enemies shooting at you constantly- You like crafting, upgrading, unlocking abilities, dense customization- You are a fan of scanning, plotting paths, planning loadouts leading to every contingency counted for- You like Simon Stalenhag and wished his books were a PC game.I've spent about 58 hours in Pacific Drive, as of the time of writing this. Probably could have finished it in 40 if I was really rushing. And I really, really enjoyed the journey. It's a slow burn, meditative game. You can play for 20 minutes and feel fairly satisfied, but a session can easily last hours. The process of prepping for a trip, crafting, customizing, upgrading, plotting the course, and departing is methodical, but each time I came back I was making new lore discoveries, bringing back new scans, new materials to upgrade the garage or car with, or a new mission to try to make it deeper in the Zone.Trips into the Zone are eerie, but this is not a survival horror game. It is full of the Odd. Anomalies that don't care who you are - you're never stalked or hunted. The Zone is an eco-system, and while it would have been easy to include enemies with dense AI the setting is so good at establishing mood that I think I would have felt discouraged from exploring if there was greater risk. Things are already unsettling when anomalies can pop up behind you without notice. Your radio can randomly tune in to eerie frequencies without warning. I feel like this was the perfect balance. There are still Anomalies you interact with - behaviors that you can learn and interact with. But this isn't Outlast, at most it's Jurassic Park. This game is gorgeous. Taking off for a trip in the night in deep fog, anomalies and lights from buildings setting a gentle glow, the horizon turning deep reds and yellows, sometimes from the sun rising or setting, sometimes from the Zone itself. Even without a photo mode I was constantly stopping to take screenshots.I really enjoyed the loop of collecting materials. Building tools to enable you to collect more, methodically picking apart the safer maps, upgrading your car's storage to take more next time, really fun. If anything I think they could have upped the default difficulty a bit - if you're a pack rat and you're smart about your approach, and take notes about where certain resources are always found, you will probably never really be hurting for car parts, repair putty, and anything but the rarest deep zone materials. The game does allow extensive accessibility options - ease of access and tweakable difficulty mean you'll likely be able to find the perfect balance for your playstyle - I'm looking forward to replaying in the future with the difficulty cranked up as hard as I can.I've been making games for ten years now, and I can tell the folks that make Pacific Drive poured a lot of experience into this. The story of the game is ultimately about humanity - about sacrificing personal goals for work. About love and commitment. About learning when to let go. The Zone is a lovely backdrop, but it's a vessel for the rest of the story - there's no shortage of anecdotes, tapes, collectibles, and other things about the Olympic Exclusion Zone to keep you busy, and feel immersed in the world, but keep in mind that ultimately that won't be the focus end-of-game. I would love to see more about the mysteries of the Zone in the future. I've had a few performance hiccups, mostly solved by turning of DLSS. Otherwise the game has run great. I walk away from the game satisfied, but hoping for more. And even though I've finished the story, I'm still looking forward to my next run.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this is for everyone. but it's for me. It's lonely, slow paced, kinda repetitive, and the radio hits just right. It's got that sad kinda limbo feel that I love about post-disaster / post-apocalyptic game worlds. It's just you and your ride exploring the beauty and hazards of the exclusion zone.EDIT: The devs listened to the players and made it so we can close the garage door. 11/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This is a roguelite game. I've never seen it mentioned anywhere (not that I looked), but had I known that's the type of game this is, I probably wouldn't have purchased it. I generally prefer open world games. The game loop is: go through a portal, get through the area as quickly as possible, find the way out, spend currency at the shop to upgrade things, rinse and repeat. If you die, you lose everything from the run. To me that's the definition of a roguelite. This missed expectation is on me. I'm not NOT recommending this because of that. I just think people should know before buying.The game is fun and has interesting mechanics and looting. The way the exploring works means you have to rush through exploration to make it out alive. I am the type that likes to slowly explore every little pixel... and you really can't here. When I tried to do that I failed and wasted like 45 minutes of looting. It really takes away from what they've built here. I'm sure the hard core folks love it... but that ain't me. Too much anxiety to get out, not enough creepy-chill exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: About 15 hours in. I quite like this, its an interesting game. Recommended, though I don't know how much replay ability it has, I have certainly gotten my moneys worth (And no where near finished the game yet).People are whinging a bit about not being able to save in missions, I get that but think it makes the stakes of the game a bit higher though with the length of some missions I wish it was available to save mid point at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: So far I enjoy the game and I'm only 3 hours in. For starters, it doesn't take hundreds of gigabytes of space so that's a plus. There's been plenty of action while I've been getting used to the pace. I'm definitely not disappointed. And the graphics are decent, and the game runs well on my system. And it's only been 3 hours but I haven't encountered any bugs. This is refreshing compared to my other games that might randomly crash. The world needs better games like this one
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I did not realize upon purchase that this is essentially a roguelite -- which I absolutely adore. I really enjoy the gameplay loop.I think my favorite thing is the quirk system. Feeling like your car is haunted, and carefully examining its quirks so you can diagnose them successfully was immensely satisfying for me.The upgrades for your vehicle are incredible, and the car really feels like my own. There's an in-world explanation for why you feel so attached to the car, but it really parallels how I feel about it while playing. And the mood is unmatched. With the amount of unlockable crafting recipes, customization, building and scavenging there's a lot here to enjoy.The radio has some absolute bangers. Cruising through decaying forests at night listening to my favorite station just scratches an itch no other game has.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: The car parts&upgrades system is simple and easy to learn, but at the same time it is advanced enough to “feel like mechanic” and spend 15-20 minutes repairing car after a tough expedition. The basic kit of any open world - several different biomes, each with its own resource. Nothing special.Anomalies annoy you enough to avoid them, but do not punish much for mistakes. They are . It seems to me that the developers squeezed out everything possible in this setting.Definitely not boring, pretty good for this genre.Good balance between routine and fun. You'll have to loot a lot if you want to explore everything the game has to offer, but you won't need to haul loot (and science points) in trucks to complete the game. I didn't meet a single one in 20 hours. Good job 😊As you move deeper into the zone, tension within the expedition will increase. First biomes are pretty friendly and peaceful, but during mid/lategame trips you  feel safe out in the zone. I had two close calls during my playthrough and . There were moments when, after a long expedition, I, pumped with adrenaline in a completely wrecked car, returned to the garage and stared at the steering wheel for a couple of minutes, catching my breath. Definitely a strong point of the game.Pacific drive is well thought, well balanced and fun experience. Definitely will keep an eye on Ironwood <3Below are some remarks and suggestions for devs that I have come up with during my playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Cannot recommend it enough, it's great. The devs have found a really good balance where the car isn't too annoying to have to babysit, and as long as you take care of it it'll take care of you. There's so many good options for customization, and the game design is solid and tight and focused. Bit buggy (several pages in the logbook are basically unusable due to some sort of glitch, for example) and the intro sequence could probably use some tweaks but everything else is so solid I can forgive it. There's also a massive amount of customization of difficulty, which I think more games should have and I always appreciate devs that go that extra mile, because difficulty customization and accessibility go hand in hand.Also massive bonus points for the absurd (in a good way) number of pride stickers it gives you as options to stick on your trunk hatch when you first unlock that customization. Thank you devs for that!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Updated the review after a second game session:First i need to warn about this game expecting you to sit for 2h+ in a row to finish an expedition.You cannot quit and save the game when in expedition, so if you have less than 2h at a time to play, you might want to wait until this issue is addressed.That said, so far the game is incredible (i have 5h of actual playtime so far, the other hours is my letting my PC on all night since my first expedition took too long to finish.)
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I was in hope that a game made after one of my favorite books, Roadside Picnic, will be worthy of the book. Unfortunately it wasn't. Though the game is not completely bad, there are some nice mechanics and ideas, but unfortunately there are even more bad decisions.The Good:- Crafting, research, car and garage upgrades.- Good way of story telling, good voice acting.The Bad:- There is no open-world, only a number of similar not so large areas with loading screen between.- No saves in the middle of really long (1-2 hours) trips, only in garage and autosaves at loading to next area.- Trips are repetitive: drive to some place, collect stability anchors, open portal, reach the portal out, get teleported back to garage, repeat.- Not much to explore, very few types of buildings, nothing to do inside but to loot few containers and go.- Forced diversity. I've had enough of this crap in real life, now it came into a computer game. Very frustrating.- A bit cartoonish looking world.- Pretty long unskippable intro screens at each start, at least easily fixable by deleting the clips.- Weak ending that has not much sense.- Poor optimization
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Immensely engaging roguelike with immaculate vibes.  Yes, there's a heavy focus on scavenging and crafting, but there's also a wide selection of difficulty options to remove a number of mechanics.On the subject of long runs - you can quit the game mid run and you will load back in as you were at the beginning of that location.  The game doesn't draw attention to this (presumably because you could use it to save scum), but each run is not the full commitment it appears to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent example of how far work put into immersion can go. I would be the first to admit that I am not a fan of cars in games but Pacific drive is an excellent example of how it can be done well.I would describe Pacific drive as something akin to STALKER but with you managing a car to protect you from the harsh elements instead of shooting your way through everything. The atmosphere is fantastic along with all the immersive design decisions around the balance of the player and their car.If I had one complaint it would be a lack of building variety particularly when it comes to the assortment of buildings that you cannot go in but simply have to walk around looking for lootables. Despite this gripe I look forward to what this game will possibly add or improve in a sequel or dlc. Also I would like to request radio mod support so I could put my own music into the car radio. I for one think the death stranding music would go great with the vibe this game creates.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game and went in blind (apart from watching the trailer on Steam) and was positively surprised!Pacific Drive is a game with a lot of atmosphere, suspense, tension and car tinkering.When your car tire explode and suddenly you have to find a car wreck somewhere close by to steal its car parts to fix your own car, all while a dangerous storm is closing in and you really have to go: That's when the game shines!Weather, day/night-cycle and paranormal phenomenon all contribute to an eerie, but strangely cozy experience.I recommend if you like car driving games, want to tinker on a car, collect resources and upgrades and so on, all while things feel a bit spooky!
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Having looked forward to this game for a while I was super excited to finally play it.  I was initially a bit conflicted by the whole not being able to save mid-session or just save problems in general.However, I said screw it, put the game in drive, smashed the pedal to the metal, and didn't look back... and I'm so glad I didn't.  I’ve played a LOT of games over the years, but nothing quite like this one and I enjoyed every mile I put into it!So, if you love cars, science fiction, compact narratives, environmental storytelling, exploration, looting, risk, chaos, and you are somewhat skilled at time management, then don't hesitate to get behind the wheel of this amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly my GOTY!I worked delivery in the PNW for almost a decade, and this game hooks with all the beautiful magical mysterious vibes that delivery driving invokes. And the variations in game difficulty was also a very wise choice, I definitely set it low at times so I could just enjoy the beauty of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game because I like spooky games and i absolutely LOVE road trips.  But this game seems to priorities the "get out alive" aspect of the plot to the exclusion of nearly everything else.  It punishes you for doing nearly everything and if you make one wrong move and run into any of the anomalies (an easy thing to do given how bad hard the car is to control) your basically dead because everything on the car breaks and your left just wanting to restart a level (which you can't)If you enjoy punishing yourself with games like Tarkov or its ilk, this might be for you.  But if you were looking for any sort of casually enjoyable experience, forget it!

_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been this immersed in a game since Valheim came out. I absolutely loved it. The effects, though, yup, they are worth it. The storm is something to behold! Not to mention all those effects through fog - nice one, devs!I would even say it´s a bit better than Chernobylite. _childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. I really enjoyed my time with it. It was an interesting and fun take on a "survival" style extraction game. Exploring and looting while trying to keep your car intact, upgrading your car and kitting it out with supplies you need for runs was great. The progression system in my opinion was perfect. I never felt stuck or lost. They put a lot of love into this game and it shows. It punches WAY above it's $30 price tag... worth double that for sure...
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: This game has awesome mechanics! The quirk system is by far the most innovative mechanic I've seen in ages, I spent an hour finding out what was causing my car door to open at times and it was an awesome hour of troubleshooting and setting up tests to find the cause. The gameplay itself is incredibly fun, creepy and interesting, but I find myself taking it in doses. More optimization is required as I'm only getting 45fps in the garage on a 3070,My two gripes are that descriptions of items and anomalies are often just some sort of story about them that rarely describes what the thing I'm scanning actually does. The other is the save system, I don't know if it's some sort of roguelike mechanic or some sort of engine issue, but in 2024 with gamers who have jobs and families, there is no reason for me not to be able to save and quit at any time for any reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: You go on collecting things/missions in your car that you gradually upgrade, as well as your base, the garage. The game has a great atmosphere, and despite being eerie or even unsettling, it definitely isn't like a horror; there are no jump scares, fighing or anything frightening really, but it did keep me on edge sometimes. I liked the concept, the characters, the story and the gameplay. With some casual hoarding, it is over 40+ hours of fun I had with it, well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: games amazing. one of the best games i think ive ever played perchance. shame the story was so short and the ending felt rushed. i hope now that theres some more budget we'll get a side story or maybe a story extension to help oppy instead or something comes around with updates . i also went through a pipe that had a ramp on it to get through to the other side of an elevated road and the pipe just lead to the underside of the map so i fell and got stuck in a void of nothingness so there are a fiew bugs. but other than that 10/10 worth money
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: A solid survival game with enjoyable driving, satisfying car maintenance between expeditions and an engaging story elevated by absolutely stellar dialogue and voice acting. The things that will stick with me from this game are the gun-it moments racing against disaster, the quiet moments afterwards as you patiently patch up yourself and your loyal steed in the safety of the garage, and the peanut gallery trio of voiced characters who accompany you on the radio through the whole affair.Not a terribly long game, but that also means it doesn't overstay its welcome. Pacific Drive is something very different in the survival game genre and well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Pacific Drive

_childDocuments_.review: A really excellent game that's not for me purchased against my better judgement. Full disclosure: I despise survival craft games and most roguelikes - uh oh, that's what Pacific Drive is. That said, I think this is the best version of those mechanics I've encountered so far.Pacific Drive is a beautiful game. I love the atmosphere, visuals, story, concepts, and a lot of its mechanics. The mystery is so strong, and it can be so relaxing to drive and enjoy the music as rain washes over the windshield. To be honest, I find it difficult to say much of anything negative here other than the fact the game gets pretty repetitive pretty quickly. In another life, this is probably one of my all time favorites, but collecting materials to craft parts over and over just really isn't my thing.I have to give Pacific Drive the benefit of the doubt, though, because I really believe it's an excellent game and I think it's tragic that I can't enjoy it more.

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive will take you roughly 25-40 hours to complete depending on how thorough you want to be at exploring versus doing only what is required to reasonably succeed on the story missions. The game also has ultra-wide resolution support, and ran smooth even during the busiest moments. So I was very impressed.I had a lot of fun playing this game. It felt like an X-Files miniseries turned into a video game. There's some jank with regards to driving and car physics, but after a couple of "whoops" reloads I knew enough to reliably avoid putting myself in those situations. The game isn't overly punishing, even in the event of fail states, so it's worth taking risks while exploring, more often than not.

_childDocuments_.review: Pacific Drive is a brilliant game which is absolutely terrible at explaining it's mechanics. Horrible, really. There's an initial onslaught of systems and context which can feel immensely overwhelming. Some games do this, no big deal. One could argue it makes sense for the situation the protagonist finds himself in.But it doesn't end there. There are mechanics - some of which are absolutely core to your success in the game - which are so poorly explained, or worse, never explained at all. I'll give you a perfect example. Towards the latter half of the game, you'll need to craft a specific item which allows you to progress deeper into The Zone. Once crafted, the game prompts you to store said item in your trunk and set out for a drive. I completed the mission without ever equipping the item, because A) the game never explained its purpose, and B) never prompted me to equip it. It was only through Googling the item did I figure out what I should have done, and it turns out a whole bunch of other players were just as perplexed as I was. I could list other examples of these communication issues, but you get the gist.Don't get me wrong - the game is brilliant. And I'm completely addicted to the core loop and all it entails. But none of these opaque communication issues enhance the game in any way. They feel like poor design choices rather than game enhancing ones. And when The Zone is already throwing everything it has at you, understanding how to best survive shouldn't involve scouring threads on the internet for peer support.Having finally reached the Inner Zone, I'm seeing story trophies pop at 15% and less. That says a lot. The vast majority of players tapped out well before finishing. This seems pretty rare for such a popular game, and I'm hoping it tells a story for the devs which they'll factor into whatever they choose to do next. Immersive, addictive, and sometimes deeply frustrating. All told, 2 out of 3 ain't bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Pacific Drive for ~10 hours over the weekend and I thought there would be more driving.Summary: 6/10- Not what I was looking for.  Repetitive.  Bad voice acting.  “Meh” story.  Good soundtrack.  Good visual effects and style. My take:  So I loaded up Pacific Drive and spent some time with it over the weekend.  There have been a number of performance related complaints regarding the game in the forums, but I did not experience any issues.  My system is pretty robust though, so your ymmv.  First off- the intro made me think the game was going to be *exactly* what I had anticipated.  A cross state/region driving simulation with survival and crafting mixed in.  That’s really not the case.  Shortly after the intro, you escape an approaching “instability storm” and make your way to “The Garage”, where you will spend significant time touching up your car, crafting things, and listening to tunes.  You also meet the three primary narrators.  They offer insight via badly written and badly voice acted exchanges.  These don’t really get any deeper or any more interesting.  At least not in my 9  or 10 hours of playtime. I experienced a glitch during the tutorial in the garage and had to resort to the Internet to overcome it.  Apparently there are a number or progress hindering glitches related to tool tips, the UI and quest progression.  Some users have reported having to restart entirely.  This didn’t happen to me, but it was a frustrating 45 minutes while I tried to figure out why the second tutorial instruction was trapped on my screen and what I needed to do next to advance the storyline to where I could once again resume playing.  This reinforces my belief that in-game tutorials are cancer.Once the game kicked off I realized that it really isn’t much of a driving simulator.  You plot a route from the Garage and exit by driving down a short path and turning left.  You then “port” from the Garage Gateway to your selected zone.  The zone is an instance of modest size that contains a few points of interest: mostly cars and structures to loot/scavenge and some “anchors”.  When you’re ready to leave or are forced to leave by an approaching storm, you collect enough anchors to fill an energy meter in your car and then Drive just ahead of the triggered Instability to a Gateway back to the Garage.  For “reasons” you have to be a certain distance away from the exit gateway to trigger the charge in your car.  While this ensures you have an exciting exit drive, it struck me as kind of stupid.  The zones are filled with anomalies and radiation that will mess you and/or your car up.  The basic loop is- Enter the zone-check your map- mark a cluster of points of interest-drive there, get out, loot, return to car-drive to the next point.  You dodge “anomalies” which range from glowing buzzsaw-esque ground effects and flying masses of angry traffic lights to creepy exploding mannequins and clusters of bent rebar that magnetically fix to your car disrupt your controls and electronics.  The anomalies are reasonably varied and fairly interesting. Aside from watching your fuel and battery gauges (why oh why does a car battery deplete so quickly when being driven?),the anomalies and the oft-accompanying radiation are the primary source of survival pressure in the game. The zones are small enough that there isn’t any real sense of distance and you will do all of your looting on foot.  You have a scrapper (looks like an angle grinder) for scavenging from cars, a trusty crowbar for stuck doors, an electronic kit for keypads, a pneumatic hammer for certain plasma containing objects, and a few other tools of looting.  Mostly they are a means of resource depletion and gameplay extension- as they break down fairly quickly during use and must be replaced.Similarly, your car is damaged or loses panels, doors, or internal parts and must be replaced/repaired.  Various upgrades from “steel” doors to “armored” panels and additional storage racks can be added to aid in your looting and scavving.  Each trip ends with a return to the garage, repairs and upgrades, and then it is time to plan the next route.  For me, there was no real sense of travel or relying on my car.  The sense of driving and surviving were sort of muted by the almost rogue-lite feel of bamfing from the garage to a zone, doing my looting, and then bamfing back.  There is some metaplot about a DARPA like organization called ARDA and mysterious LMP technology that maybe/probably Philadelphia Experimented a chunk of Washington before getting walled off.  Maybe some allusions to the narrators being in a not-quite-alive or “normal’ state.  Not sure about the latter.  Mostly a vibe.  But anyway, it wasn’t presented in a particularly engaging or interesting way.Like travel in Starfield, the going and coming of Pacific Drive felt disconnected.  I wasn’t really “Driving” nearly enough for a game with the word in the title and the mystique of a long highway haul in a strange and forbidding landscape was lost.  I was hoping for Kerouac in The Zone, but mostly found a heavily instanced survival-crafter with mediocre narrative elements and a very repetitive gameplay loop.  It isn’t awful.  It isn’t even “bad”.  But it probably isn’t worth your dollars.

detailed_description: FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE is a bold reimagining of the original FINAL FANTASY VII, originally released in 1997, developed under the guidance of the original key developers. This critically-acclaimed game, which mixes traditional command-based combat and real-time action, makes its Steam debut along with FF7R EPISODE INTERmission─a new story arc featuring Yuffie Kisaragi. ■STORY By exploiting mako, the life-blood of the planet, through their mako reactors, the Shinra Electric Power Company has all but seized control of the entire world. A ragtag group of idealists, known as Avalanche, are one of the last bastions of resistance. Cloud, an elite SOLDIER operative-turned-mercenary takes part in an Avalanche operation to destroy Mako Reactor 1 in the city of Midgar. The bombing plunges the city into fiery chaos, and Cloud is tormented by visions of a bitter enemy long thought dead. Once more begins a story that will shape the destiny of an entire world. * This game is a remake of FINAL FANTASY VII, first released in 1997. The first title in a multi-part series, it is based on the story from the original game, up to the escape from Midgar, adding in new elements. ■FF7R EPISODE INTERmission (New episode featuring Yuffie Kisaragi) FF7R EPISODE INTERmission is a brand-new adventure in the world of FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE. Play as Wutaian ninja Yuffie Kisaragi as she infiltrates Midgar and conspires with Avalanche HQ to steal the ultimate materia from the Shinra Electric Power Company. ■Content included in this product FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE contains the following content: - FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE full game - DLC 'FF7R EPISODE INTERmission' (New episode featuring Yuffie Kisaragi) - Weapon: Cacstar - Armor: Midgar Bangle - Armor: Shinra Bangle - Armor: Corneo Armlet - Accessory: Superstar Belt - Accessory: Mako Crystal - Accessory: Seraphic Earrings - Summon materia: Carbuncle - Summon materia: Chocobo Chick - Summon materia: Cactuar *The additional weapons, armor, accessories and summon materia can be obtained from the Gift Box on the main menu. *The weapon 'Cacstar' can only be used in FF7R EPISODE INTERmission (Yuffie episode)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing remake. You do not need to play the original but I would recommend it so you can either appreciate the "updated" story and gameplay.By updated story, I am talking about the dozens of hours put into the game which would take you like 3 hours on the original game. That's right, this whole game is about 3 hours of the original game. So there is a lot of new stuff to do and explore.It also touches on things in the original that you could only speculate on, and this game outright shows you more of the backstory. Which is great, but I think the next part might suffer in terms of being a "faithful" remake.Without going into spoilers, this game is obviously not a one for one remake. That's fine, and is probably a good thing. The original story line wasn't very good but the adventure was. While the dialogue and cutscenes are odd, I do think the story is overall better so far. The way this game sets up the next game makes me believe that this will be a different story all together with the same events, and more then likely a different conclusion to the story.Gameplay for the most part is set up very well. I like how they modernized the game, but it does suffer from the fact that the characters you do not control don't really do anything. That might be a good thing since the game is very easy once you get the hang of it. I don't think there was a single instance I had to reload from a death, and I only had a character down a handful of times.Because of the gameplay, there were a few fights that had to change. So the elevator fight in the original is now a lobby fight. Being vague on purpose. However it would have added more complexity to a unique fight in the original.I do not know if the free form of the combat changed so much in terms of difficulties in battles but I do not think I used a single item in a fight outside of a phoenix down once or twice. Again this game was very easy on normal, and the only "difficult" fights were just people who were sponges that just took it so it was a time sink more than anything.I look forward to replaying this on hard mode, and I definitely look forward to the future parts. I don't know if this game is worth $70 or any game for that matter. It's worth a playthrough if you played the original or just like the Final Fantasy series.

As I embarked on this journey, the city of 🌆 Midgar dazzled me with its breathtaking visuals, a testament to the sorcery of modern-day .Walking through the streets, the  whispered tales of old, echoing the memories of the original saga. The world felt alive, with every nook and cranny telling a story, the  meticulously crafted with love and attention.But, as with every epic, there were trials to face.I found myself trapped in a labyrinth of , a seemingly endless parade of scenes that often felt like detours on my quest. New faces appeared,  whose tales felt out of place in this grand narrative. And then there was . Oh, Barrett. His voice, once filled with passion and fire, now seemed off, not quite capturing the spirit of the leader I once knew.My journey was further tested by the challenges of the . The port seemed to have been crafted by a novice mage, with limited graphic spells, a disdain for the ultrawide scrolls, and a bizarre choice of incantations (or should I say, keys). And the final blow? The realization that this was but a chapter, an  with a treasure chest price tag.This tale of Midgar, while visually stunning and mostly true to its roots, is marred by unnecessary diversions and challenges that test even the most patient of adventurers. Would I embark on this journey again? Perhaps. But with caution and a lighter coin purse.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say right off the bat that this game isn't like the original FF7 on PS1 (and on Steam) - though that's probably well-known by now.For what it is, the first part in a trilogy, the game is surprisingly decent fun; sure, it's not my favourite JRPG (it's no Xenoblade Chronicles or Chrono Trigger DS or whatnot), but it's still well worth my time. It's no longer fully turn-based, instead going for a mix between that and action combat, where you can attack freely in order to build up your ATB gauges, allowing for the usage of spells, items, or skills. Frankly, I don't mind this change; it's not as wildly, and off-puttingly, different as FF15's combat, and still pays tribute to the original FF7's combat.In order to pad the relatively-short Midgar section of the original FF7 out into a full-sized game, some areas are made larger; I understand why this had to be done, and I don't "hate" it, but...eh. It's something.However...Square Enix, WHY DID YOU CHANGE YOUNG TIFA IN THE LATEST SURPRISE UPDATE? For those that aren't aware, in the latest update (a surprise drop alongside FF7 Rebirth's release on PS5) one cutscene was modified - it's a flashback to Cloud's youth, where Tifa wore a cowgirl outfit. In previous games, and originally in this game as well, she wore a white top with nothing underneath, which was fine as nothing explicit was shown (of course not).Now, the cutscene was modified so that Tifa's wearing a black bra underneath the top. It's a minor change, but if it's so "immodest" and abhorrent for her to be braless...why not change it earlier, huh? Squeenix was clearly fine with the original for years, only for it to be changed in Rebirth, and thus had to be altered in Remake as well.
