_childDocuments_.review: Note: Played the full game on PS4, replaying now on Steam.I'll state up-front that I don't have a problem with this being just part one of a remake. It felt like it had enough to warrant the full price tag to me. So, if that is your only concern, you can buy without worry. But if you're interested to hear whether or not the game is good, read on for further detail.I still have my original black back discs and jewel case. Some parts of the Remake game carried for me on pure nostalgia. Others were not so good. Others still were so awful that I have no idea how any adult making the game could have examined them and thought, "yes, this is good, this should go in our game."I'll start with the good stuff. Some parts of the Final Fantasy VII Remake are really exceptional. Number one is that it starts off amazingly well, and feeds fans of the original tons of fan service and nostalgia right off the bat. A tear came to my eye playing the opening few hours. The new combat system, although far different from the ATB of the original, is pretty fun! Animation is amazing- really stunning, and that extends from combat, to NPCs, to cutscenes. Great soundtrack, of course, as the original was fantastic as well. And the art direction is fantastic. Now on PC and with updated graphics, Midgar has come alive for me. It looks phenomenal and feels like the city in the original game did. There's also an exceptional level of polish here. There are very few bugs and there's a deep attention to detail in every part of Midgar.However, a lot of the game is a complete mess narratively whenever it's not re-creating scenes from the original.The only time the writing was hitting for me and felt good was when depicting the original characters. Square Enix has a lot of character designers from the original working on this team, and it shows. Not once did the characters say a single line of dialogue that felt out of character for them. The writers clearly still know these characters deeply, and the voice actors nail every single one of them and are cast perfectly.But that's where the good stuff ends. I won't spoil the game here, but suffice it to say that almost all of the new content added to flesh out the original story is bad. It's full of inconsistent rules and plot holes (being stuck in the area in Chapter 17 after falling and having to spend the entire chapter climbing back up, and then just next chapter watching Cloud jump literal hundreds of feet), full of MacGuffins (Chapter 4 is guilty of this, along with Chapter 13 which makes zero sense whatsoever, and Chapter 14 which could have been cut completely and the game would have lost nothing), and rampant use of deus ex machina for anything and everything whenever the ghosts show up, culminating in an event near to the end of the game that made me roll my eyes and literally groan aloud because of how awful it was.The real problem with all of the stuff they've added is that it completely torpedoes the pace of the Midgar portion of the original game. I expected this bloat to be represented by the side quests, but those were actually fine. This bloat shows itself in the main quest, which I did not expect. Entire chapters of this game feel like a complete waste of time, and a lot of the writing in these new chapters is so amateur as to feel like fan-fiction. The moment-to-moment scenarios are often just cornball video game nonsense that's impossible to take seriously, eg. "monster stole the key, go chase him down", or "this bridge you are crossing just fell down, now you have to go through this entire level, routed through conspicuous combat rooms with enemies". Lots of random nonsense to move the plot forward that feels contrived and unnecessary and impossible to care about. Compare this to modern story-driven games like Witcher 3, Red Dead Redemption 2, or God of War (2018) which are using every single moment, every single line of dialogue, either to tell a compelling story or develop their characters further. Final Fantasy VII Remake feels bloated with tons of fatty, disposable content when you compare it to other titles that strive for great storytelling. It's extremely disappointing, because I consider the original Final Fantasy VII to be fantastic at storytelling, tone, timely comic relief, and pacing. And the Remake fails in all of these aspects.Despite how good this game tends to look, a lot of these failures make it feel old and outdated, which is ironic, of course, because it's a remake of an old game! These are the exact problems the remake was supposed to fix! But these arise not just because it's a remake, because this flaw primarily exhibits itself in the new stuff. The classic scenes from the original game which are re-created here are as timeless as ever and work really well. But the structure of the new portions they have added for the remake feel like they've been designed by a bunch of guys who are stuck with '90s video game design philosophies—Everything feels way too gamey and arbitrary, put in place by a developer's decision rather than organically arising from the story and characters, and because of this it becomes impossible to take seriously and fails to have the emotional heft that good storytelling often does. Look, I don't mind if you make me chase a MacGuffin every once in a while, but it has to serve either to develop the mechanics of the game and teach me something new, or develop the core characters or story further, or even lead to a relevant, spectacular set-piece. Too many of the pitfalls of Remake lead to none of this, and the game feels like it spends half its length spinning its wheels as a result.So a lot of this game is a mess and inconsistent from moment to moment with what it wants to be, whether it wants to be a faithful remake head nodding to its original fans, or a new story all its own. I thought they executed on the former very well, the latter was pretty disposable, standard video gamey stuff. This is very relevant to the game's ending, which I won't spoil here, but suffice it to say that the ending was the culmination of this kind of poor writing, as it seems to go completely off the rails with the most obvious, heavy-handed pseudo-artistic statement to the point where I'm not even really interested to continue playing the next episode. I've heard that Nomura is famous for this kind of stuff, which does no favors for his talents as a director and a writer in my eyes. I really hate disliking the ending because I just know people are going to rag on anyone who doesn't like it for being perpetually angry gamers or whatever, but it's seriously bad. Think Game of Thrones Season 8 bad. I honestly cannot believe that the game got out the door with this ending. Someone high up at Square Enix needed to tell whomever was responsible for writing this ending that it was not going to work. It's a failure of epic proportions.All of the best stuff is from when they re-create the original scenes, most of the stuff I didn't like was new writing injected into the framework of the story which already exists. So if they're going to tell their own story now with these characters, from here on forward, I'm really not interested in that, because I don't find their storytelling up to par in most cases and the bombastic, campy style with which they tell it is really not for me.It's neat that this thing even exists, and it's got a lot of polish. But it starts off well and ends poorly, and it's very inconsistent throughout. I'm surprised it's been so well-received both critically and among fans new and old. Nevertheless, if you were a fan of the original, it's still probably worth playing—warts and all.

_childDocuments_.review: FFVII REMAKE is a game that aims for an immersion through realistic graphics, sound design, and controls, while bringing a sense of fantasy through it's combat, story, and the other classic RPG elements such as augmenting and upgrades.The combat is quite fun and challenging, while still holding some of those turn-based battle elements through the abilities and magic. Overall I enjoy the battles I come across and actively seek out more of them.The world is beautiful and dystopian, but textured and structured so well that you have to believe this is a real story about some time in the future. The characters are very well done and the story behind each one helps you to feel like they are real.The story itself is straight-forward, and kind of a classic tale. There is an evil force that is harming people, but is accepted as the standard way of life, until you come along and defy it. But it's done in a way that makes you feel the impact of defying the "norm" to a deeper level, with some quite emotional moments. Overall, I really enjoy the game and would recommend it to anybody who has a powerful enough PC to run it!

_childDocuments_.review: I had a weird time with that one. I never had a PlayStation growing up, the only exposure I had to FFVII was my best friend narrating the entire story to me when we were kids, to a point where it almost felt like I had watched him play.I was genuinely excited about this port, getting to finally experience this legendary game was something that had been on my bucket list for quite a while.The thing is - and that is my very own opinion - that I found the overall experience to be boring.The story is interesting, but not captivating. And I know this is only a third of what the whole plot is supposed to be, but I felt cheated of how much money it cost me to experience this. It's messy, rushed, voice acting felt soulless, the gameplay is stiff and repetitive, and the dungeons are tedious and forgettable. I ended up trying to rush to the end of the game just so I could put it past me, still while trying to get all the quests done (another low point of the game IMO).I'll give the Yuffie DLC part the commendation it deserves. THIS was fun. Characters made me feel things, I felt the excitement, the grief and the determination of the main character, moreso than with the main cast.Maybe it's a "you had to be there" kind of experience? I wasn't, and I suspect a significant amount of players weren't either - and my experience with this game was disappointing, it was like watching a group of people have all sorts of inside jokes and pretending you're not here.This is not my first Final Fantasy game. Far from it. Yet I wonder if I would have explored more of their catalog had I started with this release. If you've loved the original title, you'll probably marvel at what this game has to offer. If you haven't played it back in the 90s, chances are you won't enjoy your experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game in and of itself. However, I can't overlook the fact that Square Enix did everything they could to artificially extend its playtime to make a "full-length" game out of the first third of the original game.I can't overlook the fact that the story feels incredibly drawn out as a result of the absurd amount of filler content that was inserted into the plot.I can't overlook the fact that most areas that you travel through are so massive and filled with generic riddles that it takes you hours just to get from A to B.I can't overlook the fact that almost all bossfights follow the same scheme, where you destroy their arms/legs/horns/wheels/etc. to make them vulnerable for a few seconds, and then attack them as much as possible during that time, only to repeat that process again until the fight is over. On top of getting old quite quickly, this concept also does not work very well in many cases, because enemies frequently reset their stagger bar (for example when transitioning to the next phase), erasing all your previous progress.I can't overlook the fact that this PC version of the game still has technical issues like stuttering and poor optimization that have been present ever since the day it was launched for PC (originally as an Epic Games exclusive) in 2021. Crisis Core: Reunion did that MUCH better.I can't overlook how long it will take until we will be able to finish the game (as in, all three parts of it). Maybe you've watched the trailer for FF7 Rebirth (aka. part two of the remake) that was recently shown at Summer Game Fest (like me). Maybe you've never finished the original FF7 so you're even more excited how the story will continue (like me). Well guess what. I hope you're prepared to wait for YEARS untila) Square Enix has finished developing and releasing two additional "full" AAA titles,BUT ALSOb) we as PC gamers will graciously be blessed by their release for our platform, which (assuming the timeline will be similar to how the first part was released) will take at least another year on top of that.But the worst thing about all this is still the unused potential that this game had. It's not like these negative points completely ruined the game for me. It's not like I had a bad time when I played it - it was just underwhelming. There were some great moments in the story, and watching the trailer for FF7: Rebirth made me genuinely excited to play that, too. The issue I have with this game is just that this kind of excitement is quickly forgotten when you spend hours solving riddles or doing sidequests, only to finally be rewarded with the next tiny portion of story, which will be followed by more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly, an epic action (J)RPG -  this game REMAKES the beginning of Final Fantasy VII (one of the greatest games of all time) - and serves as the first part of a trilogy. A brilliant, beautiful slightly flawed masterpiece - that is of exceptional AAA quality, abolutely stunning visually, features FUN & engaging polished combat, incredible sound-design & lustrous score, full of rich characters, an engrossing & compelling albeit confusing story - the game is an awe-inspiring immersive experience that only suffers from some pacing & padding issues. Time to buy another PS5 for Rebirth in February! Twenty years ago at the age of twelve, I was on a family trip to the local retail store - I was allotted the opportunity for ONE game. I dug through the bin of PC games and stumbled across a dull blue box with grey trimming. On the cover was a blonde haired man, he held a giant sword - the imagery was simple but powerful, and just below him was the striking iconic teal meteor with the words Final Fantasy VII. After inspection, I could tell the game would not impress me visually but ultimately I decided to take a chance on it. It would be my first Final Fantasy experience, and little did I know that it would be one of the most powerful, resonant, and transformative pieces of art I'd ever experience. A video game whose rich world, narrative, themes, and characters would continue to capture my imagination even twenty years later...and if I'm being honest, Final Fantasy VII is my personal favorite story across any artistic medium - including film, television, and literature. Hironobu Sakaguchi once said he was excited having Yoshinori Kitase to direct the original Final Fantasy VII, because Kitase was formerly a filmmaker - and in his visual presentation of his games he wanted them to surpass feature films. And, that is exactly the level of scope & production that Final Fantasy VII REMAKE has - it feels like an incredibly quality, polished cinematic presentation of the video-game so many people love.Final Fantasy VII & REMAKE is a game that is so rich thematically, and covers so many wide-ranging topics that are still culturally relevant (if not moreso today) from classism, corporate greed, corruption, environmentalism, mental illness, trauma, loss, death etc. - a lot of the topics are dark & mature, which is always unexpected for some given the aesthetic & playful additions to the games like the colorful chocobos. That's what made Final Fantasy VII so original - it's weird, it's quirky, it's playful - but there is so much depth & meaning to it's characters & story/themes that are incredibly human & resonant.However, REMAKE is an incredibly bold, reimagining of the story - that so many hold dear & love. The game serves far more as a sequel or continuation of sorts with it's constant hints, references, & allusions to the original, and even Advent Children. Beat for beat though the game follows a similar structure of the beginning of the first game - but with NEW, ALTERED, & MYSTERIOUS events too. The themes of  are heavily featured now and the narrative is far more complex, possibly convoluted with multiple timelines, and possibly time travel (certain characters) - but definitely mysterious. The major revelations will come in the sequel stories of this trilogy. But, for all it's changes to the original at it's core it's the same beloved & memorable characters (a ragtag group of misfits & outcasts) all coming together and embarking on a journey far greater than themselves, and far greater than they could imagine. And the main theme of the original game  - or rather how precious and valuable life is - how beautiful, but painful, how fleeting LIFE is - and how LIFE is to be protected...that core theme is reverberating all throughout this game. In that regard, the REMAKE is just as faithful as the original.The one topic of the game, I find most significant are the characters. One of the main reasons the original Final Fantasy VII is so fondly remembered is because of it's brilliant writing & development of it's characters. The core cast of characters are beloved, unique, and diverse - each with their own desires, arcs, growth, and shared sense of loss. If there's one aspect the REMAKE exceeds the original it's in it's showcasing of it's characters and their development. Square manages to masterfully reintroduce players to these iconic characters - in a level of detail unseen before. To see these characters beautifully reimagined in a modern 3D AAA context is incredible, the sheer amount of detail - the expressions in their face, the clothing, the weapons, the hair, the sounds of their voices (brilliantly voice-acted) - no more reading dialogue bubbles! Long gone are the days of the polygonal figures of the PlayStation 1 era. However, the upgrade is not just in it's graphical presentation with visuals & aesthetics, or even just in it's audio presentation with voice-acting - but it's in taking the time to develop these characters. Take for example Jessie - a tertiary character - the young, rambunctious biker girl member of Avalanche (who's incredibly thirsty for Cloud) - her character is given so much more room here to breathe, so much more depth, and context -  We learn about Jessie's childhood, her ambitions as a theater performer, etc. We also learn about Jessie's father, a once hard-working, honest man trying to provide for his family - who was left permanently bed-ridden in a vegetative state after being forcibly overworked at the local Mako Reactor by Shinra. The next character I'll mention is Tifa - I have to say in the original for me...Tifa was overshadowed by Aertih - who was the embodiment of good, light, and holy (literally the Holy materia). But in the REMAKE Tifa fully realized - more expressive, and voice-acted you can tell she is the concsience of the group. She is constantly questioning all of their actions & the ramifications it will have, she is consistently expressing concern & care for the others. She's not just a capable bad-ass fighter, she's also incredibly kind, caring, and compassionate - and I think benefited so much more from the REMAKE. Lastly, I'll touch on Barrett - the loud, boisterous, larger than life personality - he's incredibly blunt, and has a fiery passionate contempt for Shinra, and is hellbent on saving the planet. But, beneath that harsh rough exterior is a father who's desperate to improve the quality of life & material conditions for his daughter - in a world that is unfair, brutal, and unforgiving.Overall, this game is brimming with passion - quite a number of the key original devs worked on this game - there is so much careful thought & intention behind every character, each line of dialogue, and the iconic imagery. Honestly it's a miracle it even exists, and it's of such exceptional quality. I didn't get a chance to discuss the music of the game - which itself is a beautiful reimagining of Nobuo Uematsu's masterful score. Hearing the iconic of the game genuinely gave me chills. Nor discuss the incredibly FUN tight polished combat, action (J)RPG perfected! I haven't even played the DLC...'INTERMISSION' with Yuffie's story yet! To any passionate fans of the original, who haven't played the REMAKE yet - and to any curious newcomers to the series, I say God-bless and enjoy the ride. I truly, cannot recommend this game enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning: This review is going to be potentially VERY LONG.So, let me start out with my thoughts on on gameplay, mechanics, and sidestory content before i begin talking about the main story because that's gonna be a micro-biography in itself...Gameplay: Combat systemI remember the very first time i saw gameplay preview footage waay back in I think it was 2018 or somewhere around that time, I was appalled by how drastically they changed the combat system feeling as though they had already ruined the game before it was even finished.  Having beaten the game, I no longer harbor those thoughts.It was a nice blend of the old and the new but classic mode supposedly being geared towards those who prefer classic FF7 gameplay is a down right shame. The AI stands around for ages doing absolutely nothing, dragging out battles unnecessarily.  It's clear this was added as an afterthought rather than a focus to appeal to classic fans but the combat system was obviously designed with a more fast paced combat style in mind as when you take manual control of the characters and attack, the battles feel more alive and natural instead of stagnant and drawn out. If there was one thing I disliked about the combat system though, it was the enemy AI's annoying tendency to time its interrupting attacks at critical moments when I was about to claim victory or stagger a boss only to have the battle be needlessly drawn out by another 30 seconds or more because my ATB gauge was wasted due to the interrupt. Often times this would result in me missing a critical window causing me to be forced to wait or repeat battle mechanics, i felt these "conveniently timed interrupts" were a cheap gimmick programmed into the game's AI to add an layer of unnecessary artificial difficulty to battles.On a final note, the "disabling attacks" left characters unable to act for far too long in my opinion.Gameplay: MenusFor the most part, I found this to be pretty faithful to the original game but the weapon upgrade system felt unnecessary at the least and an unwanted gimmick at its worst.  Most of the "upgrades" were down right useless in fact the only useful ones i often found were the attack up, MP up, and materia slot adding upgrades. Everything else looked like the guy programming this upgrade system went: "Uhhhh, crap, i'm out of ideas! Hey random fellow dev! What stats should I throw in here to fill the gaps?" and just pooled random suggestions. Gameplay: MateriaHow can I put this...I found it satisfactory but also lacking?  Of course they made sure to include many of the major ones, fire, ice, lighting, time, ect but then you got ones that just baffle me at their use making Materia like the "stagger boost" highly situational.  Most of the materia just sat in my inventory unused because of how situational most of it was.  In fact, in my whole playthrough I think I may have used some of these materia for maybe 2 or 3 battles before swapping them out for Time, Healing, or one of the elemental materia.The summon materia turned out to be the biggest disappointment of them all however, I can see why they gave players those bonus summon materia in gift box now because otherwise I would have used summon materia maybe...5...or 6 times in my entire 40hr playthrough?  Gameplay: Motorcycle sectionsBy far one of the most irritating things to sit through in this entire game. The first one was just filler content(will get into that can of worms soon) and had these forced dodging segments following by holding in the accelerate key to catch up, deal some damage and then repeat the process.The second one was a trial in aggravation.  The boss on the highway was so annoying to deal with that if not for me being LITERALLY AT THE END OF THE GAME and felt as though i needed to push through for the sake of finishing, I would of uninstalled then and there as this boss was so frustrating to deal with and not to mention was just a freaking tank with way too much health.Story and side story content:I'll start with the sidequests as once i get into my thoughts on the main story everyone who actully loved this game will immediately click away...The sidequests felt completely unnecessary in my opinion, sure some of them gave some decent rewards but most of them were a giant waste of time and made me regret walking into this game blind. I spent 10mins on a single quest to get a freaking useless bangle or piece of junk as a reward on most quests. Looking back, I could have shaved off probly 10hrs if i had only done the ones that gave decent rewards and moved on.The Main storyWhoo-boy...here we go... Okay so to start off when the main story beats where going on, the game was awesome beyond words but then following nearly every single one or just before, I was slapped in the face with nothing less than what I could call "Filler content" It's clear the devs knew that if they gave us the story beats and nothing more, this game would barely break 20hours(if you skipped all sidequests) so they added this filler conent.Some of it was a welcome addition, for example, going back to sector seven, i could totally see cloud and co doing that BUT THEN we got bulcrap filler like the underground lab section under sector 7 or the completely unnecessary and drawn out filler in Wall Market. There's so much filler content that I can't even recall it all and it makes up a staggering 50% of the game!  There's so little original FF7 content in this game, you'd wonder if they weren't trying to make a brand new FF7 and toss the old one in the recycling bin...Too soon?Well here comes the spoiler alert tag:THAT'S EXACTLY WHAT THEY'RE DOING!Filler content withstanding, up until you reach Shinra HQ, the original story is more or less maintained and intact but once you get there, its like the writer took the original plot, tossed it in the shredder, salvaged scraps of it and then rewrote EVERYTHING ELSE. I'm not one of those "FF7 purists" who grew up with the game (FF6 was my childhood game) but this rewrite nearly made me ragequit the game.Not only do you fight Sephiroth(There's an innuendo here about "exploding too early" to put it in the most PG terms) at the end but they pretty much retconned the ENTIRE REMAINDER OF THE ORIGINAL FF7 GAME by having cloud and co defeat the "harbinger of fate".On that note, the whispers by far are the most lazy plot device I've seen in a video game since the overly used "paradox" plot device used in F13-2. These "whispers" serve one purpose and one purpose only:  To give the writers a narrative "way out" when they either wrote themselves into a corner(aka: killing barret) or to ensure the characters can not intervene with core events from the original FF7 when they CLEARLY HAD THE MEANS TO DO SO.If you're gonna retcon 90% of the damned game, why bother keeping the original plot intact at all?Closing thoughts:Despite my issues with them retconning the original plot of FF7, I did have fun playing the game for the most part even though some battles were outright frustrating.(looking at you sahagin and your jump spam!) With that said, if your a fan of the original FF7, prepare to be enraged by the retconning BUT if your not a FF7 purist or are okay with remakes taking liberities like this game obviously did, then I can recommend giving this game a try.As long as you view this game as its own standalone Final Fantasy entry and do your best to not associate it with the original FF7, you're in for a fun time and an overall enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The story digs a bit deeper than the original and manages to stretch the first 10 or so hours of the game into 30 hours. There's a lot of padding in the dungeon design too, but without random encounters that is to be expected to bring even some amount of combat to the game.The combat system falls a bit short compared to other action JRPGs, like Tales series. To me it feels like it would have been better to stick with purely timer based system or completely free system. This mishmash of different mechanics is just confusing and doesn't work.Graphically it's nothing to write home about. Passable in most places, but especially texture resolution leaves a lot to be desired and especially skybox textures are at times extremely pixelated. Overall it looks like a game made for a 10-year-old console, because that's what it is. You can hang it on the lazy port too, maybe those faults would not be so noticeable at lower resolutions from viewing distances typical to TVs. Speaking of the port quality, most glaring fault is the lack of any meaningful graphics settings, although those should be built-in for any Unreal Engine 4 game. I also had glitchy controller inputs where my xbox one x pad buttons did not conform to the input prompts. At best the controls are unintuitive with keyboard and mouse, at worst he game is almost unplayable. For example, good luck with the darts minigame with digital keyboard inputs.Basically the whole package is a throughly mediocre game that tries to cash in on the nostalgia for one of the greatest JRPGs ever made. If the regular price was 30€ and it went for sale it could be a good deal, but no matter how you look at it, there's just no way this game is worth 80€. Especially when this is a lazy port of a 3 years old console game made for a console of the previous generation. For holding it from PC gamers for 2 years and then another year before it was released on Steam, the price should have been seriously discounted as well. And I don't know about regular prices on PS4, but If I had paid 80€ for this, brand new on the console, I would have felt ripped off.Overall I could almost recommend the game to a true FF7 fan that is willing to overlook the technical faults but the pricing is the piss-marinaded cherry on top of a cake with poop icing. Even considering that this game includes the yuffie dlc that was sold separately on PS4, that only adds about 3 hours of gameplay tops and adds nothing to the story. And if the game isn't that good to begin with...

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 4.5 | Narrative: 4.5 | Graphics: 5 | Soundtrack: 5 | X-Factor: 5Call me a milf cause man, i love Final Fantasy.GAMEPLAY:FF7R was my first JRPG that I've played that had real time turn based combat. I know it's not a new concept, but as my introduction to this type of format, wow. I was blown away. I cannot stress this enough, but the combat is so cool. Being able to slow-mode a skill menu, while actually hack and slashing outside of that window gave a perfect balance between rapid-fire action and remaining faithful to a "turn-based" system. Need a breather to take a moment and think about your option select? Open the combat menu mid-fight. Don't need to? Mash the inputs that'll get you to the skill you want to select and the battle flow remains uninterrupted. The quick-swap character system allows you to swap between Cloud, Tifa, and Barret (and sometimes Aerith), allowing you to min-max your damage output and change up the pace of the game if you so desired. Every character boasts their own unique movesets, with Cloud having his signature buster sword, Tifa being an up-close and personal brawler, Barret being a machine gun simulator, and Aerith specializing in magic. While you select one of the playable characters, your other team members are controlled by AI. Admittedly, this system isn't perfect, as the damage is not optimized, nor do you have full control of your party at all times. Thankfully, your autonomy as the player is more than enough to clear any difficult battle, and there aren't any consequences for rapidly swapping between your roster.The game also gives you plenty of autonomy with building your characters, and the skill tree system is near-perfect, allowing you to truly polish the skills you value the most. Do you value survivability? Raw damage output? Speed? Being able to have more accessories equipped? The game gives you full control of what you want to invest in. Me personally, I'm a numbers kind of guy so I appreciated the game allowing me to just become as powerful as possible <3The gameplay outside of combat consists of going from Point A to Point B in the world, and the occasional odd mini-game. Exploration is present in this game, but is not a core part of the gameplay as the game is pretty linear in structure and has limited movement options apart from walking, running, and climbing up ladders. I'd love to see a greater emphasis on exploration, and movement options catered for it in the future games of this trilogy (please Square Enix at least give us a jump button)!Also I need to address the motorcycle riding sequence in the game. This is personal. WOW. It sure was surprising to see when I first experienced it in game, and it was so cool. It was one of the moments during my playthrough that made me realize that what I was playing was truly something special. It's not even a significant concept in the game, as it only appears twice, but it's one of so many small aspects that make the whole of the game that FF7R is so amazing. That one motorcycle boss fight near the end of the game sucked, though. LOL.NARRATIVE:You'll hear this about a lot of Final Fantasy games, but it's because it's true. The story is in fact, quite amazing! As this game is part one out of three games, you can't actually talk about the entire narrative here. But what Square Enix has done with Midgar from the original FF7 game is astounding. The game devs have breathed so much life into this remake, and the segment of a game that used to be Midgar has become fully fleshed out, and feels like a real and believable world in a fantasy universe. One key difference in the remake is that the game allows you to get to know more about the side characters, such as Jesse and Biggs. The characters all feel real, so when something happens, you FEEL something. The story and character writing is phenomenal, and the beautiful and compelling setting of the game exponentially builds upon that.GRAPHICS:Cloud Strife is hot. Oh wait, um, I meant that the graphics are gorgeous. This is without a doubt, one of the most aesthetically pleasing games I've ever had the privilege of playing through. Just LOOK at the game. And the in-game cutscenes of the game are on a whole other level. When a cutscene played, it felt like I went from playing a video game to watching a cinematic experience at the theatres. I've never described a cutscene like that before (and this is HIGH praise), and I honestly never thought I would. But here we are! The game also had brilliant moments of transitioning between gameplay segments and cutscenes. There's a point in the game where you're playing as Cloud, fighting off a bunch of soldiers, and upon defeating them you realize that they've called backup. There are simply too many enemies for Cloud to fight, and you transition to a cutscene where he jumps off the side to land on top of a moving train. It's one thing for the game to be cool, but it also makes you feel cool for simply playing the game. W game.SOUNDTRACK:The amazing graphics, combat, and narrative all breathe life into this game. And the cherry on top of all this is the music. This game already made me feel things, and the music only made that worse <3. I could go on and on, but I'll just leave it at that. IT'S REALLY GOOD. I PROMISE.OVERALL: 5/5GOD I love this game. Final Fantasy 7 Remake's very existence is a privilege in itself, and if you aren't playing the game when you COULD be playing this game, I don't know what to tell ya. You probably like pineapples on pizza?

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second time with FF7R, I played it on launch on the PS4 pro. It has for sure shown its age after over 2 decades, gameplay wise and graphics wise, but the story is still incredibly well done with a beautiful soundtrack. And I think you should play the original before this one.Now, about the remake. This game is really, really good, FF7 fan or not. I think anyone can enjoy it just for the incredible graphics, gameplay, and great story. The game just does so much justice to the original and makes it 100x more impactful with it's key moments. The fully orchestrated soundtrack, the sort of cheesy in a good way voice acting, there's a lot to love about this game. Now, there's alot of contention over the ending and the potential direction for rebirth and the final remake game, however I was personally fine with it. I don't think the ending is necessarily bad, and for the most part is not problematic based on some of the recent comments from the developers on the future of the series. Overall I would strongly recommend this game after the original, and do not be discouraged from what you may have heard about the ending.HOWEVER, this port... yeah. It's definitely not the best. First off, I had a world of problems with voice acting in cutscenes being jank due to some poor audio support. The game lags in the cutscenes sometimes, even with my 3060 i7-11700k. They fixed the dualshock support issues, thankfully. It's 70 dollars, and there are virtually NO upgrades to this version. The only graphical improvements you can use are slightly better textures (and I really do mean slight) and HDR settings. Even if we had graphical improvements, the game would probably lag because of how much it struggles even on up to date hardware. It is almost unacceptable, considering God of War on PC is only $50, and often on sale for less, with a whole slew of graphics options and other settings. Still recommending this game, because apart from the poor port management, it is really well done. Game might be better on a PS5 if you somehow have that.

_childDocuments_.review: An ok remake that was made with a lot of love but no sense of pacing and some blunders story-wise.If you never played the original FF7, go play that first (maybe get it on Switch; ~30 hours?). After OG FF7, you could do Crisis Core Reunion (on Steam, ~30 hours), and then go for this Remake (~40 hours in Normal if you don't rush it).The great:- Midgar is full of life, and eavesdropping on people on the street is quite fun.- The environments are beautiful (except for some mazes full of bland corridors)- The characters look great, sound great (at least for the Japanese VA), and are much more fleshed out. It's a pleasure to see the interactions between everybody in the group. Aerith in particular is so likeable.- The story roughly follows the same beats.- Some great remastered tracks.The good:- Combat is fine. The Normal difficulty feels fair: it is challenging, and bosses are not too bullet-spongy (although some really are, and some are more annoying than challenging).The mid:- Maybe a bit too much materia is given us for free, which cheapens it.- Moggle Medals  are lame. You get them randomly (?) when breaking crates, but anyways you can just farm them on a 2 minutes timer at some point of the game. They unlock some rewards, but that doesn't make them more interesting. They shouldn't have included them in the game.- The random HP/MP/Moogle Medal drops (at least I think it is?) from breakable boxes on the map. They feel like an after thought.- The English translation makes sense and is grammatically correct at all times (OG FF7 was at least a bit weird in the French version). But there are differences when comparing the English text to the Japanese audio. Those differences don't alter the story, but can change the mood of some scenes or even the personality of some characters. I preferred the JP version by a lot, it's much more nuanced. Also it makes it harder to try to follow both text and audio at the same time, but that's a niche problem.The bad:- The pacing. It's just so slow at times, with some big fillers. Depending on the section of the game, this can be:  - a brand new low-stakes story block (which does help connect with side-characters a bit better)  - boring side-quests including finding lost cats (which do make the slums a bit livelier)  - mandatory slow walking or crawling in some part of the game (which is just annoying)  - expanded dungeons (only one of which I felt was designed well-enough, the one before Reactor 2)  - very long cutscenes (which look great, but take a lot of time from gameplay)  - And the last section of the game lasts forever (half of it could have be cut off, it's just a chore)- If we compare with OG FF7: OG's pacing is miles better. We (almost) never get bored, (mostly) always have something exciting to do. The tone can be inconsistent throughout the story (looking at you, Hojo on the beach), but the pacing is very good. In the Remake, the tone is much more consistent, but the pacing is not great, we lose momentum at every step of the game, and while that works on some level (gives us frequent breathers to look around us and enjoy the environments), it is also preventing us from appreciating the main story.- Navigating the menu can be very slow, and even the simple action of opening the menu might fail by just triggering a pause, if you don't time it right (for example if you tried opening the menu a bit too soon after Cloud stood up from his bench).- The last section of the game is bad, they botched it imo. The ending in particular: I know Squix likes to end its games with big abstract enemies, but one important thing that makes the Midgar section of OG FF7 work is how grounded it is. In this Remake they go into crazy nonsense that 1) is explicitly targeted at players of OG FF7 + Crisis Core Reunion, 2) due to its enormous scale diminishes the impact of everything that would come before or after that, 3) gives a very unsatisfying ending, 4) makes me very sceptical about the reworked storyline in Rebirth (although everybody raves about that one so I'm cautiously optimistic), 5) is just gibberish with flashy animations.Now trying to go through the Yuffie section. (edit: I gave up, no motivation to go through that one)

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade is a quality single player experience which borrows heavily on the original. Where this game deviates from the original's story and environments is where it suffers, luckily for the majority of the game it does follow along. The Yuffie DLC story which is included in the base game is all original but fills in gaps in the original lore. This game does require the user have a base understanding of the original, and playing it without such knowledge would likely be highly confusing as much of the content expects you to be familiar with both the original FFVII as well as the spin off games like FFVII Crisis Core.All that said, its still a moving experience that as an OG FFVII gamer moved me emotionally in ways few games in this modern era have. Its has its best girl simulator aspects (comment your favourite), despite being censored from the originals. The combat is great too, although nothing original. And most critically they have no Denuvo malware bundled with the game. So the verdict, full recommend! (Disclaimer: you should probably play Final Fantasy VII the original game before playing this)

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 "Square-Enix used Cash Grab! It's super effective!"*slow clap* So this is what we've been waiting for. Really?This game has ISSUES, and it tells of that story throughout the game. The often MMO-like fetch/kill quests are insanely boring when you have such an interesting world that could be explored instead. We are presented with small and often lifeless dioramas that represent the fantastical world of FF7. Each town is  linearly crafted into corridors upon corridors. The town music... lacks immersion at times.And then you run out of content. Huh? With how linear it's been going, it should have been relatively easy to have more, right? What a strange way to deliver content these days. And speaking of delivering content, there is no forgiveness for treating PC players as second class. I have refunded the game because I have already played it, don't support how PC players were treated, and think the asking price is insane for what we got (and how long PC players had to wait to get it).It's crazy that this is the best they can come up with. We're not talking about a new franchise, but a very well-established and insanely popular one. The original literally CEMENTED Square-Enix in place as a AAA developer for all time (and space), so it's too bad that a few chefs somehow managed to spoil the entire dish even though they were already using a legendary and award-winning recipe.How do you even **** it up this badly? I don't even know. Does it make sense that you are tasked to venture out into the (limited and bland) wastes to complete quests when you could be doing them in one of the coolest cities in RPG history instead? Does it make sense that there are extremely high flying enemies that make their chosen combat system feel super janky and frustrating? How about giving the remake the green light to strip out the living and breathing world that the original PSX version was able to portray, replacing it for lifeless dioramas? There are so many cool ideas that the remake could have used to move the story along, but instead we revert back to FF13's corridor-based system. None of this makes sense, but I can tell you what does: They chose to make a quick buck off of a legendary brand.During its development hell, Square did mention the necessity to cut elements of the game to make producing it manageable... but that does not make it okay to do a half-***ed job in the elements that we do get to play. It's so half-***ed that even the minigames feel off! It's not that the mechanics used in them are too old to be used in the 2020s, but rather the overall feel of each one feels scuffed. Like eating food from a microwave. That kind of feeling. But I suppose that's how it should be, considering the entire game feels like you never left the train ride. Just one long corridor to explore... Until you reach the point where they're charging you to get into the next several train cars. And you'll wait while they get everything ready because SURELY it'll be worth it. Right PC players? The defacto biggest gaming faction? Surely no one would be stupid enough to **** with you, right?Ultimately, you'll have to play the original to understand how big of a game FF7 was at its release, compared to its competitors. This title should be enjoyed for what it is, a mediocre episodic "cash grab" with some weird immersion breaks in the story that completely ruin the pacing. But SURELY they'll do the franchise justice with the next few episodes, right? This one was just a test, and now they can make the next episode way better! And they definitely won't use any excuse to delay the PC version on release... Oh yeah, they'll definitely avoid ****ing with the biggest gaming faction this time... SURELY...It's surprising to see even the biggest names in Square-Enix allowing this to happen, given that they felt passing on this project to a new generation wouldn't feel right. Completely understandable... except now it's probably better to let the new generation make things right. The ones who grew up with the game won't be so out of touch like you suits were... of that much I'm absolutely certain.FF7 Remake is one of the biggest disappointments simply due to missed opportunities and the excessive amount of cutting corners. It is simply unfathomable on how anyone in charge could have okay'ed this mess... unless it was, of course, to milk their die-hard fan base once more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only an hour or so in, thus this review is simply first impressions. I absolutely adore FF7. The original has been in my top 5 of all time since about '98. When they dropped the initial reveal trailer for this reboot, I was over the moon. It's why I went out and got a PS4, which is hilarious since I do not actually own a copy on PS4. Anyway, I've gotten through the first section and gotten a feel for the updated combat mechanics and here's what I got to say so far:Graphics: It's gorgeous. This is what I always wanted the original to look like and they more than delivered. Animation is a bit choppy at times, but that's probably thanks to my mid-level PC and crappy internet connection.Sound: It's a Final Fantasy game. The soundtrack is excellent. I also love the voice acting, though Barret's voice doesn't fit his dialogue as well as the other characters (in my opinion anyway).Controls: I'm using mouse and keyboard and it's obviously meant to be played with a gamepad. It's a bit clunky, but it's fine. I'd use a controller, but I'm lazy and the controller is all the way on the other side of the room--probably ain't gonna happen.Gameplay: This ain't your granddad's FF7. Combat is faster, more fluid, and a lot more satisfying than it was back in the day. Don't get me wrong, I love some good turn-based combat, but this feels so much better. It's more strategic and more thrilling. Putting it all simply: this is, from what I can tell, the same game that well all (presumably) know and love, just with a much nicer coat of paint. It feels like the game they had in mind all those years ago but could never have been able to deliver due to, ya know, technology being what it was then vs now. It feels familiar while also feeling like a fresh experience. Exactly what was needed.

_childDocuments_.review: IN MY OPINION, THIS IS THE BEST GAME I'VE PLAYED IN YEARS AS WELL AS MY FAVOURITE GAME AS AN ADULT!!!This game was an amazing experience. I have played the original Final Fantasy VII and while the remake is not 100% true to the original when it comes to story, it exceeded my expectations in what it delivers as a whole. Some may complain that you are not getting the entire game as Square Enix has mentioned that this is part 1 of several episodes but Final Fantasy VII Remake will give you 40 to 50 hours of gameplay (minimum not counting extra post game content) and after you see what content was put into this game you will understand why Square needs to expand the game into separate parts. This game alone is 2 blue-rays long!Graphics- 9.5/10: This may be the best looking PC/Console game I have ever played. Square used the unreal engine 4 giving character models and environments the royal treatment. I could clearly see the texture of main character Clouds purple turtleneck. Very beautiful game.Characters- 10/10: Square did an exceptional job with its characters and their developments. It felt like they were real with real emotions and heart. Chemistry and interactions between characters were as good as top notch movies. We got to know the characters to their core like never before. Most character's voice actors and actresses were also right on target!Story- 9/10: For the most part FF7R stayed true to its roots and expanded on some of the characters, environments and storylines that the world fell in love with in 1997. However, there were some expansion of story that I find questionable especially in the latter parts of the game. Gameplay- 9.25/10: I was worried that I would not like the battle system. Even after playing the demo I wasn't truly convinced. It is a hybrid of action and turn based. As I progressed through the game I appreciated it more and more. Now I can honestly say I love it! The new battle system might be my favourite of all Final Fantasy games. It is not perfect as aerial combat is not perfected and camera angles get messed up every once in a great while but the foundation of what it demonstrates is amazing. Aside from gameplay the game is very linear but I didn't mind it as the original was linear during the Midgar portion as well. Combat System- 9.8/10: Combat is amazing, boss fights are epic, story and characters truly lived up to my expectations (I also loved how they brought life to characters like Jessie, Biggs, Wedge, along with a few new faces), and I felt the materia system was truly a next generation approach to one of the things I loved most about FF7. I liked how all the classic area we all loved in FF7 (for me, wall market, shinra HQ, Aerith's church, climbing the wall, and train yard) still made an appearance, and in a lot of ways even better in FF7R. One of the best things about FF7R is the replay value, beating the game on hard, getting the bonus items/gear, and watching mechanics for some boss fights evolve truly made the game feel so rewarding once completed.Music- 10/10: This could be the best soundtrack I have ever heard. Square brought back Uematsu (legendary composer). The music brings boss fights to full adrenaline rush as well as sets the mood of the narrative of each scene. The music itself was worth the purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game hoping this would be a remake that would honor the original game. It does not. I played through the whole game so i can ♥♥♥♥ on it. So here it goes.Graphics: Amazing! Stunning! Cutscenes, in-game, you name it.Sound: Amazing. 10/10. The music the voice acting, everything.And that's the good stuff. Let's see what's bad.The combat system is something new and not that great. You can even roll like dark souls, but you don't get invincibility frames, so if you roll and something gets you, it gets you. You control on of three characters. AI almost immediately focuses on the character you control ignoring the others. This can be exploited. The original game had a basic, solid combat system. Now it's more of a mashing attack button festival most of the times, except boss fights that you need to exploit the AI.Is this a full game? Yes it is. The worst part of this game is how slow it is. It is painfully slow. This game is about 30-40 hours to complete in order to achieve a fraction of the original game's plot. You just get out of midgar. In the original game the sabotage of the reactors and getting out of Midgar takes about 10 - 15 hours max. So in order to have a fully fledged game and ask for a full price they have overstuffed this "episode" of the game with mini games, INFINITE cutscenes and dialogues and CORRIDORS. LOTS OF CORRIDORS WHERE YOU HAVE TO SLOWLY walk through. You just sit and watch as your character squeezes through various obtastacles, BUT SLOWLY. The Materia system: It was perfect in the original. Now it's even more complicated. The all materia you could link with other materia in the original, in order to target all enemies or allies, has now been substituted by the magnify materia, which is colored blue. So the game gives you LOTS of materia early on, but none of the good stuff. Combine this with the new upgrade weapons system and you get a whole new thing to invest time on. Each weapon can be leveled up and through leveling materia slots can be added. It is kind of nice in a way, but it is yet more stuff to spend time on.  The party system. Pretty bad. You don't get to choose your party. Even during times when you have 5 members available, the three characters that engange in fights are determined by the game. This makes no sense. Choosing your own party and gearing them accordingly is a feature since the first games of the series.This game even has fetch quests. What a shame. Because by today's standards this is a good game, but not something great or special. The original game was HUGE, absolute masterpiece for the time it released. It was a big deal. This on right here is just another AAA that don't stand out among the abundance of similar games that get released nowadays. You could also play assassin's creed or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the product of a wish upon a monkey's paw. I enjoyed the first couple of hours of the gameplay, and the soundtrack was fantastic for the most part, but a lot of small issues compounded over time. Gameplay - Final Fantasy XIII's stagger system makes its unwanted return, making characters who should be powerful feel anemic more often than not. It plays like Final Fantasy XV, post DLC, which would have been great if it wasn't for this awful, awful stagger system. On Normal, higher level enemies and bosses take a lot of damage with very little positive feedback, making the combat really tedious at times. What's worse is how many bosses are multi-stage which makes the game feel like it's trying to draw itself out and makes a tedious experience frustrating. One of the New Game + benefits is the ability to skip the motorcycle mini-games and frankly I wish I could have done that from the beginning given how unfriendly that (and other mini-games) are for players who primarily use the keyboard and mouse to play. Even with a controller though, the motorcycle segments of the game aren't intuitive and fairly frustrating. Story - It's not the original story. The original has been superfluously tampered with in ways that somewhat make sense for the sake of fitting in the canon of other Final Fantasy VII media like Dirge of Cerberus and Crisis Core. In other ways though, the plot of Final Fantasy VII has been compromised in a way that seems very mean spirited. It's almost as though the current writers wanted to upset the people who like the original story. When Final Fantasy VII is allowed to be itself, it's nice to revisit familiar set pieces, and watch familiar interactions. Square Enix: DO NOT DO THIS TO FINAL FANTASY IX. DO NOT DO THIS TO FINAL FANTASY IX. DO NOT DO THIS TO FINAL FANTASY IX.

_childDocuments_.review: Props must be given to the graphics. This game features an awesome recreation of Shinra and Midgar to look at. The main cast is great as you would expect, but the sidecast is weirdly underdesigned by comparison. The story is faithful and the chapter oriented structure makes sense. Overall, this is a cinematic masterpiece.Gameplay is where most things go wrong. The progression is slowed down by constant crawling through tight spaces and sidetracking for treasure boxes hidden in corners. The battle system is a weird mixture of attack chains/abilities/blocking/dodging that feels more punishing than rewarding. Most of the time one's missing crucial materia or party members, since the story loves to shuffle the party around. The human bossfights are designed around waiting for gaps and counterattacking, and they get progressively more annoying because Cloud does not have the speed to match. Fights with flying enemies with melee is inconsistent, some attacks teleport-jump you and others just whiff. While in the air, you can only continue your combo or wait to get knocked down to the ground. The intermission gameplay changes things around to fix some of the issues. Yuffie has a much nicer moveset, can perform some actions in the air, and does not need to use elemental materia. But this is added on top of a flawed system and just shows the lack of direction from the start. The battle system, while cinematic, needed more time to develop, making the 50 hrs gameplay feel like a demo of what they hopefully expand on in the following games.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this straight, the game excels in production values, and as a fan of the original, it's fantastic to see this reinterpretation of a classic, revisiting enemies, locations and characters that are loved till this day.Graphics and music are a real treat, can't even complain about the framerate focused experience either, as it allows for a smoothly running game. Voice acting is top notch as well, however the default mix drowns out the excellent music, so make sure to lower the volume of voices significantly.While we're on the topic of music: The remasters are great, but, are remasters nonetheless. The original tunes are brilliant in their composition, always able to perfectly convey the mood and atmosphere, telling a story of their own, on their own. As well written and technically well done these remixes are, they are remixes still, offering a great throwback to the original tunes at times, but lacking in emotion due to their overuse of additional layers of bombast.This criticism goes for the entire game: The original FF7 was a masterclass of epic world-building and cinematics on PSX. FF7r attempts to one-up the original in every single way, but whilst doing so, fails to live up for the simple fact that it offers a whole lot of style over substance. In order to add substance, the world is padded out with significant padding ranging from from dull fedex sidequests, to downright dull filler dungeons. What remains is a reimagining of a game that has its highs dilluted by an over-abundance of sub-par padding severely disrupting the pacing of the game, which was something the original did exceptionally well.Play this if you want to experience Final Fantasy 7 in a 2023 cinematic fashion and find PSX graphics and mechanics distracting you from enjoying the original experience.Play the original if you, like me, are in it for the story, value a properly paced classic RPG experience and are able to appreciate a story told, and find voice acting, set pieces and triple-controlled action RPG-mechanics a nuisance, rather than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Remake is an extremely fun RPG. This game doesn't look or play like the original 97' version. That being said, the story is 90% accurate to the original. One major change is the addition of these time traveling ghosts that interrupt the characters. Other than that It's basically the same classic story we all remember with additional characters, subplots, and updated game mechanics.I wanted to talk about my gaming experience. I've put in over 300+ hours into this game on the PS5. It looks and plays great on console. On PC has some minor issues that might bother some folks. After playing a few hours I noticed frame drops and issues with visual quality. (I only seemed to notice this once I got to the sector 7 slums in chapter 3). You can play with the settings but nothing will fix the issues 100% without maybe installing some mods. I'm also playing this on the Steam Deck and I've been playing on lower settings. It's still playable so it's not to bad and didn't hinder my enjoyment of the game.Now I want to get into the gameplay and story. This is only the Midgar portion of the story. Which only covers about 5% of the original's story but this game has A LOT to offer! All the parts of Midgar that we remember from OG are here! The original cast is back and they are the best they've ever been. New characters and dialogue were added. The city is so big and the graphics are beautiful! In the slums section of the game you can hear NPCs talking about their lives and struggles. They also update you on current events if you stop to listen to them which is cool. One of the best parts of the game is Wall Market. Depending on which conversations you have (or don't have) with certain characters can dramatically change the outcome of some quests. There's so much to do you couldn't finish it all in one playthrough. Side quests are also not mandatory which is nice!Most of the scenes from OG 7 are still here.The only scene that was censored was the hallway scene in the Shinra building which I think is kinda silly.The music kicks butt. Not only did Square manage to add every Midgar track from OG. They improved upon them and even added some new ones which I appreciate. Square really went above and beyond with this one. It if goes on sale I'd recommend picking it up if you haven't already. The DLC is worth playing to so check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: There's probably little that could be said about FF7 that hasn't already been better said somewhere else. As an FF newbie, I came into this knowing little more than Internet memes and a few unfortunate spoilers. (Yes, especially *THAT* one.) While we have a copy of the original game ported to another console, I didn't really want to play that, since I didn't feel the need to look at 27+ year old blocky graphics and annoying chip-tune music. When I heard about the "remake trilogy" coming out, I felt this was finally my chance to dive in. Since then, I've been waiting anxiously for Remake to be ported to a platform I own (since I'm not going to by a PS5 just for one game), and once I acquired a Steam Deck, it was one of the first games I purchased.The story, naturally, does not disappoint. Quarter-century-old spoilers aside, I was immediately drawn in. The graphics are stunning as well, and far superior to the original. The Yuffie "INTERmission" bonus story was also a nice add-on with obviously sequel hooks for the second game in the trilogy. Everything from beginning to end feels epic, and it's hard to imagine how the second and third installments can build upon them given the high bar already raised. (Naturally, I already know they will, given how Remake covers barely the first quarter--if not less--of the original's scope.)The only place I will ding this game is its Steam Deck compatibility. Technically, it works very well on the Steam Deck 97% of the time. It's that remaining 3% that keep it from being perfect. There are a few spots where the game suddenly and unexpected drags to a crawl and the entire Deck becomes sluggish and unresponsive. It can take several minutes--and a lot of patience--to navigate the nearly-frozen menus to exit the game and let the Deck recover. Then the game can be restarted with relative ease. Fortunately, I am an obsessive saver from my old PC RPG days, so I rarely lost any significant progress because of this, but it could be frustrating for someone not so inclined. I eventually set the textures and shadows to low in the graphics settings (they default to high) and this appears to fix things, but I only discovered late in the INTERmission quest so it might not be a silver bullet.I am now anxiously awaiting for Rebirth to be ported to PC and, presumably, the Steam Deck will shortly follow.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VII Remake took me by surprise. It’s got all the reasons not to work: young adult dialogue, the usual Japanese-style “gasps and sighs,” a weird setting, a pared-down version of the original story, and a semi-turn-based combat system. Yet, despite all that, it’s incredibly hard to put down. The challenging combat and unique progression system keep things interesting as you learn to exploit enemy weaknesses. Even by today’s standards, the setting feels refreshingly unique. And yes, the characters have their “cringe” moments, but they’re somehow charming and really grew on me. In the end, FFVII Remake actually feels like a true Final Fantasy game.The soundtrack? Outstanding, no question about it.Then there’s Final Fantasy XVI. On paper, it seemed perfect for me: mature, westernized dialogue, combat from the Devil May Cry producer, a medieval fantasy setting, epic moments, and a fantastic score by Soken. But, somehow, it doesn’t quite hit the mark. It honestly feels like they slapped the Final Fantasy logo onto a different game entirely.That said, both games have killer music and solid protagonists. But FFVII Remake? That one’s the real winner for me.And now, I honestly can’t wait for Final Fantasy VII Rebirth to drop on PC. If FF7 Remake is any indication, this team knows how to handle a true remake: taking a classic and bringing it to life in a way that feels fresh, exciting, and true to its roots. FF7 Remake is proof of how remakes should work—breathing new life into a game that actually needed it, instead of redoing titles that already look fantastic (looking at you, Sony). Here's hoping Rebirth takes everything that made Remake great and dials it up even further, when it finally comes out on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VII: Remake Steam Edition brings a fresh wave of nostalgia and awe-inspiring beauty to one of gaming's most beloved classics. Square Enix has masterfully reimagined the iconic 1997 title, and the result is nothing short of spectacular.Graphically, Final Fantasy VII: Remake on Steam is a visual masterpiece. The character models are incredibly detailed, capturing the essence of each character in a way that enhances rather than alters their original designs. The city of Midgar, now rendered with stunning realism, is a breathtaking spectacle with its towering skyscrapers, neon lights, and gritty industrial zones, which breathes life into the futuristic Cyber/Steam Punk city.One of the standout features of this Steam Edition is the improved optimization for PC, although not without glitches here and there. The game runs smoothly, even on mid-range systems, and offers a plethora of customizable graphics settings.The only minor downside is the episodic nature of the remake, as this edition only covers the Midgar portion of the original game's storyline. With this, it feels like unnecessary 'filler' content was added to add to the tale of Midgar, leaving you to painfully wander around The Slums and Wall Market for much longer than you should. How it can be slow, it does expand on the original Final Fantasy VII tale with content not in the original 1997 version.Final Fantasy VII: Remake Steam Edition is an absolute triumph. Square Enix has not only successfully resurrected a classic but has elevated it to new heights. Whether you're a longtime fan of the series or a newcomer to the world of Final Fantasy, this game is a must-play for anyone who appreciates masterful storytelling, stunning visuals, and captivating gameplay.I don't know if I say this too early?. But really this is one of the games I like the most out of all the games. The remade character is very beautiful. The setting is ultimately peaceful and simple. I must say the graphics are amazing. I love it

Too few pc settings available to tailor the experience to your systems capabilities. No options to enable/disable settings that have been standard in all PC games for decades. Wanna remap run for your keyboard? Nope. Wanna turn on/off Vsync? Nope. Turn off DSR? Nope. Uncap FPS? Nope. 4k? Nope.On top of the lackluster settings options, the game runs terribly on most systems due to horribly optimized engine settings which often require playing on low settings on a RTX 3080 Ti and it STILL STUTTERS!What's truly sad is that many of the issues seem to be the result of the DRM. Meaning that only the people who pay for the game get the crappy experience.I've played this on PS4, PS5, and 2 different PCs. I own no less than 4 copies of this game and I choose to play none of those because Square Enix has decided to handicap their own work with terrible decisions that punish only their legitimate customers.I'll be seriously considering whether or not I buy the next title based on whether they continue to insert horrible Denuvo DRM crippling the experience for paying customers.If there's one thing I want the developers to take from this it's this, Denuvo makes your game worse, punishing your paying customers and teaching them that they can save $70 and have a better experience by NOT buying your product?You want my money? _childDocuments_.review: Tbh I was pretty skeptical of this game since I havent really played much of the Final Fantasy series outside of some of the old DS games.  My buddy bought me FF7R and insisted that I would enjoy it.  Well he was one hundred percent right.  Now I obviously never played the old one so I do not have any real attachments to the old game or story and am essentially viewing this game with completely fresh eyes.  I know some things about the story have changed but its mostly of no consequence to me.Despite my tentativeness I found myself quickly engaged with the story's narrative and the characters which are admittedly very trope heavy.  The game really goes all over the place from serious, to light-hearted, to dark, to zany, with a healthy dose of being anime as ♥♥♥♥ in a good way.  The voice acting is all pretty well done despite some clunky dialogue with Barrett being my personal favorite character.The story is basically all about Avalance, and eco-terrorist group who probably all carry pocket copies of Industrial Society and Its Future, going up against the evil mega-corp Shinra who is killing the planet.  The main character Cloud is an edgy emoboi merc who ends up tangled up in the Shinra conflict with Barrett, Tifa, and Aerith while he chases after the BBEG Sephiroth.This game is downright gorgeous although it suffers from typical stutter issues that could easily be corrected by allowing us to precompile shaders.  The combat is interesting and harkens back to the JRPG roots in a way that feels good.  Lots of over-the-top boss fights as is typical of the genre.  The soundtrack is probably the real standout of the game as every last song and track is just phenomenal and really blew me away.  The story is pretty entertaining and keeps you sucked into the mystery and tension of the narrative.  Quite a few emotional moments which is always a plus for me.Overall Im glad I played it and cant wait for the next installment of the game to see what happens next.  Its probably a 9/10 game but due to some pretty awful stutter, I have to give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: No doubt this game will go down as one of the finest games in its decade, yet I don't say that without caveats. I started Final Fantasy Remake Intergrade (FF7R from now on) with no experience in any other Final Fantasy title, and less than a dozen hours into the original 90's game. Coincidentally, I stopped almost exactly right where this remake ends, so I have a fresh frame of mind to analyze it. I'll approach this review from the standpoint of those who don't have nostalgia or memories connected to it. I worried this game wouldn't stand on its own when I learned it actually splits the original story into 3 parts (two yet to be released) and one prequel. Pretty important for a game of this price ($40 on sale)! Thankfully, the remake fleshes out the scant story from barebones to a massive 40 hour adventure, and I never felt it was either lazily contrived, departing from the original ideas, or wasting my time. FF7R is hands down the way FF7 was always meant to be played. I can see the intentions of the original staff coming to fruition 20+ years later in an exciting way.  This is the type of RPG that tells a story instead of letting you write your own. You make very little important decisions in this game, I think about 3, and even these had to do with whether you advance a plot rather than changing it. It plays out like a 40 hour movie where you control the action but the writers control everything else. You will be watching a lot of cutscenes, a LOT of cutscenes, and for a very long time. But I would say 70% of them are spot on, 20% are welcome but you itch to jump to the action, and 10% are boring; ranging from plot-necessities to "obviously only there to keep the game from being janky". Thankfully, this 10% is spaced throughout the whole game, so there are almost no sections that you have no choice but just suffer with silence. As an avid fan of Star Wars: Knight of the Old Republic, FF7R gives me a lot of hope in what a KOTOR remake could play like. The combat is a fluid and natural mix between hitbox-response time combat like an action game and turn-based combat like a classic RPG. The trick is the ingenious ATP system, which works by having regular, real time attacks, successful blocks and patient waiting charge up a 2 part meter called ATP.  ATP is necessary for abilities, like: healing, calling down lightning/fire/ice, buffing offense or defense etc., if it's more than moving or attacking, it uses ATP. This way, FF7R benefits from the adrenaline pumping experience of a Souls-Like without sacrificing the calculated, strength vs. weakness, ability vs. counter gameplay. "Waiting your turn" is a real part, yet in the meantime you aren't totally helpless to the wiles of the enemy. The combat doesn't get "old"; plentiful and varied enemy design (especially in the boss department) keeps you moving, thinking, and adapting, not just spamming buttons. Yet within a section of the story (in side quests especially), you are liable to feel mush after killing sewer rats the for the 100th time.  The original game suffered with this, too, but to a MUCH higher degree. FF7R handles this issue pretty well, yet without the complete polish of something like Jedi Fallen Order.  The story is charming in many ways. I love how the characters branch out in tangible, rewarding ways. It's really refreshing. But often, the female character design can detract from the characters themselves. How they dress and how they behave (Tifa especially) seem pretty different. Mods solved a lot of this issue for me. After all, modest is hottest. Yet don't take me as a prude when I say the developers may have been thinking with the wrong head in some of the production decisions.As a potential buyer, I would consider these things:+Fantastic Steam Deck game+Great story, like a 40 hour long Oscar Nominee+Well worth its price in content+Satisfying combat+One in a Series (it's not done here!)but also...-This game wrapped itself up in such a nice bow by the ending I don't feel any need to go back for any post game content like achievements, collectibles et cetera. Once it's done it's pretty much done.-Along the same lines it's not extremely re-playable, unless you're the type to re-watch your favorite movie 4x a month-It's part of a 3 part series, and its already pretty pricey on sale. If you want the whole experience you could potentially be set back $200, albeit over the next 5 or so years. It's a large investment of time and money considering the whole 3 game FF7 Remake could take around 120+ hours to complete, not even including the prequel Crisis Core.  All in all, I would give it an 8/10. A long game with much to come but not much to return to.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, another day, another game that fails to live up to its name. Don't even think about buying this 1/3 of a game, folks.
