_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, as a fan of the series and this game being one of my favorites, I'm quite disappointed in the remake. The visuals are absolutely stunning, and a few of the cutscenes bring back fantastic memories, however... the dialogue leaves a lot to be desired. I know the dialogue in the original wasn't that great, but they seemed to have doubled down on it with this game. It's abrasive to me, like trying to rub my brain with a cheese grater. The lack of random encounters is also disappointing. I'm hoping with part 2 they give you a little more exploration and stay a little more true to the original FF7 formula. The side quests also leave much to be desired. Most of the side quests in the original had something to do with world building, character development, etc. The side quests in the remake seem to be simple cookie cutter rpg nonsense, like fetch quests. They don't add much other than something to sink your time and get a little extra experience.As far as positives go, the movement in the game is super crisp. The transition between types of movement, like climbing a ladder and running are a lot more fluid and not as jarring as the original. I like that the movement is also incorporated into the battle sequences. Fighting the scorpion in the intro and having to hide from its laser was wonderfully immersive by comparison. The animation sequences and the art are right up with the Advent Children movie, which was exactly what I was hoping for.Do I recommend the game? Absolutely. If you're a fan of the series, then it's worth the trip down nostalgia lane to see what they're capable of. Is it a good game? Not really. For all the visual polishing, they left a lot to be desired from the actual content.

_childDocuments_.review: Big props for everything except the combat and all the forced walking bits.But seriously, this is a very pretty game with great music, as expected. I respect the big swing with the story and whether or not it pays off in the second and third game I don't even care. But the combat...it's trying to split the difference between an action game and the classic turn-based Final Fantasy game and the result is still subpar on both ends despite being the best attempt at this in a Final Fantasy game.My dodge isn't even a dodge. It's a roll with no i-frames. It's only effective if I happen to roll out of range of an enemy, and if I get hit, ever, then I'm stunlocked for the entire combo, however long it may be. I'm clearly expected to swap party members often, which is fine, except doing so is jarring and flow-breaking and my other party members are often in weird and stupid places like out of range or not even in line of sight.The summons? They may as well not have exist they're such an afterthought, and it's the same with the limit breaks. The stagger system? Like oh so many others it's punishing instead of rewarding. Good stagger systems don't let you deal damage, they let you crit.

The execution is phenomenal is some aspects and horrific in others. The story is good and the direction is superb, the visuals are great but very stuttery and not well optimized for PC. The design of the villains is pretty cartoony and cringy, probably my least favorite thing about the story. And honestly these chapters of side quests in between the chapters where things actually happen are SUCH FILLER. The side quests in this game are some of the worst, most tedious fetch quests I've seen since whatever the last ♥♥♥♥♥♥ MMO released was.WIth that out of the way, this is the single worst action game I have ever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ played. I have never in my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ life played an action game where I spent so much time twiddling my thumbs, hands not even on the controller, waiting to play the game. In combat, you are disabled 80%+ of the time, it only gets worse the farther you go. The game cancels everything you do. It stuns you for LITERALLY 30 seconds at a time, your entire team, doesn't matter. Doing a limit breaker? cutscene cancels it. See a big attack coming? There's not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing you can do about it. _childDocuments_.review: Conclusion: This is a game that could've been 15 hours long but they decided to make it 25-30 hours long. Try out the original FF7 and see if you can get past its age, if you can't then play this one. Played up until the Shinra building.There is a dance section in the Honeybee inn when you're invited by Andrea, make sure your parents don't walk in on that one.Everything that was in the OG Final Fantasy 7 is great. Some of the added scenes work very well too, mostly the Tifa stuff,The Sephiroth scenes suck. All of them do. It just ruins the initial mystery of his character that original FF7 kept until you reached Nibelheim. I guess not having Sephiroth in the first game was too much to ask for Tetsuya Nomura ¯\_(ツ)_/¯, in fact it was too much to ask for Sephiroth to be out of the screen for more than 2-3 hours. You'll be seeing Sephiroth's face at points and think "Not again", I started getting a similar reaction with the ghosts. It's like you're enjoying a fine story that's standing on its own two legs and you can just see Nomura's hand reaching in and telling you that he's there and directing the game so stuff is gonna get convoluted and weird.WHY show the plushy cat (Cait) during one of the most emotional scenes of the game? He shows up out of nowhere so you suddenly see a goofy cartoon cat that you know nothing of feeling dejected and sad about what's happening, instead of focusing on the characters we do know who are ziplining for their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lives.The side content is nothing, mostly walking around finding stuff in town or killing a few monsters. The dialogue in these would be their only saving grace if it were good, but it's just generic throwaway lines.A lot of the scenes and conversations added don't do much since they can't progress the story, they're trying to pad out a 6-8 hour story into a 20-30 hour one and it shows when you listen to it.There is a lot of padding. A LOT. Here's a few examples:- Constant wall shimmys, seriously. You will be surprised how often the game makes you shimmy. It slows you down so a 4-5 second walk turns into a 10-20 second slog. Yes, Cloud's biceps are very detailed and shiny, I've seen them two dozen times up close already, thank you.- Small sections of the original game turned into giant ones in this, but providing more or less the same content. So what was 3-4 screens in FF7 is now this giant sprawling dungeon in Remake with almost no enemy variety and constant running through halls and into battle arenas. (I see you, 10% player drop during Aerith's first section, who the ♥♥♥♥ came up with the hand crane puzzles?)- Ladders everywhere.- Some scripted battles go on for way too long, usually because of huge HP pools for bosses. You should technically come in prepared but you have no way to change materia mid-battle and you can't know a boss' weaknesses beforehand. So yeah, go and die once if you don't wanna spend 30 minutes fighting it with unprepared characters. You could also look up a guide online but having to do that is not a good show for a game like this. - Chests with some really inane objects thrown around on dead ends. Those precious few seconds you spend going through the hall, opening the chest, getting the item and going back to the main path add up. It's tiresome, it's nothing, it ruins what FF7 can provide to you as a well-crafted storytelling game so you get the big shiny headline that says your game is 40 hours long when released. I hope they move away from this in the next game and actually provide the original story with meaningful new content.

_childDocuments_.review: I've rarely if ever seen a game more preoccupied with getting in its own way than FFVII-R, but occasionally, some fun manages to squeeze its' way awkwardly through the gaps in its design. It's slathered in modern AAA gaming sludge and baked in sugary, coma-inducing Tetsuya Nomura nonsense. Still, the original script that it attempts, for a while, to vaguely recreate, as well as the combat, which I think is lifted from FFXV, are essentially solid.I don't like Tetsuya Nomura. I don't like his writing, or his character designs, or what he seems to want to accomplish with the stories he tells. His constant drive to shove cosmic-tier threats into simple stories makes everything he creates seem vapid, boring, and empty. I'm sorry for this. I know that many of you love the guy, but I think he's like the Michael Bay of Final Fantasy. I acknowledge his contribution to the original FFVII, which is basically the last of the series I'm able to take seriously, but it was very evident to me from the excruciating early-game motorcycle sequence that he had much more influence here, and increasingly so as the story strayed into sugary drivel and the worst Advent Children-tier excess that forces my brain to stop caring.At its best, I can say that R instilled in me the wonder of exploring those fascinating pre-rendered environments that enthralled me in junior high in full 3D, and that while it told the story of a cold, rootless mercenary finding a place for himself, I was along for the ride. This is interrupted both by a ceaseless and frustrating obsession with procedural traversal animations, I suppose to hide level loading, and jarred to a halt by the game either slowing the pace at which Cloud moves for mostly arbitrary reasons, or literally pulling you away from exploration and back onto the rails of the plot.I would still give a recommendation based on the fun I managed to have if the ending weren't so disgusting. In what I suppose to be a misguided effort to ensure that a pointless remake would not be a pointless remake, Nomura went far beyond injecting his mind-numbing brand of action into the narrative, and essentially guarantees us that in future installments, he absolutely was going to **** this up. I recommend this game as much as I recommend vomiting.Thank you, good night.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR game isnt bad, just disappointing how iconic and important to the community this particular final fantasy is. Feels like a better version of 13. I dont think someone would be able to enjoy and finish this game without nostalgia lens.PROS- Beautiful, the graphics definitely do the game justice considering how important this particular game is to FF lovers and gamers in general- Everything audio about this game is just mind numbingly good, from the voice overs to the music, both thematic and environment- The characters are amazingly well written and all extremely entertaining on screen-Alot of good systems in the game: menus, materia, weapons, summons, stagger, limits etcCONSPacing- this is a big one and it impacts almost everything in the game so theres going to be multiple points. Too much of the game feels like theyre trying to stretch out the experience just so they could say players spent X+ amount of hours. We know theyre going to split the original game into parts, but the sheer amount of filler content that just isnt engaging is pretty rediculous- SO MANY UNNECESSARY CUTSCENES, you climb a ladder, or you kill a mob, and it launches into a cutscene just so they can say "we did it!", everything in this game needs an associated cutscene and can be pretty infuriating. To be fair, you can skip a good portion of it, but then it just feels very inorganic. Plus alot of these lines and interactions can just happen as youre moving around....- how picky doing interactions could be, hitboxes are pretty small when it comes to interacting with anything, so you'll often times run past, then double back then double back again. So if youre running around and you run into a button, or a merchant or a ladder, youre forced to slow down and line yourself up instead of interacting with it when youre within a certain area. Very annoying if you are trying to move through an area quickly, I found myself running around the chest/ladder I want to use alot because on top of being in the right position the game also takes a second to register that and for the promp to come up. Slows the game down ALOT- Enemies are weirdly very spongy, some of them just take too much damage for how difficult the fight itself is, and some of the bosses just feel like youre beating a sandbag for half an hour without doing anything technical or dynamic- narrative pacing is a little bit weird. Minor spoiler alert. In one of the first missions you end up in a motorcycle fight where you trash the other characters bike on your way to a mission, within the SAME night the guy gets it fixed and finds you again for a rematch. Not to mention when he does you're supposedly in hostile territory with a bunch of enemies and they all just stop so you can fight this random guy instead??? I understand back in the day games were limited by the hardware you played on, but narratives like this just feels weird and very out of place, and it happens alot in this game. Combat- I honestly hate the combat. I have nothing against action combat per se, the animations look good and the skills hit well.... but its not combo based so you're just spamming attack until your gauge fills up for you to use a skill. The game feels like it should still be tactical turn based with the way you play it. Literally just feels like a better version of FF13, and you know what they say about polishing trash...doesnt matter how shiny it gets its still trash-Being able to switch characters is a cool idea except all the characters end up playing the same. Its even worse if youre playing Cloud or Tifa since theyre melee characters, you have to be within melee range and attacking (to fill your gauge) to do ANYTHING (items, spells, abilities) and because enemies move pretty dynamically (which is great in an action game) if you use an ability and it misses, it feels even worse. Its also annoying how the mobs will always go after the character youre playing, which makes sense to a degree, but you can never just take a step back or stay on a boss's flank - target lock isnt very good either, because the enemy can literally move off your screen and your character isnt forced to be facing them so there will be times where you attack nothing, or use your melee skills into nothing even though you have target "lock"- Aerial combat, is atrocious, its cool to see your character jump up in the air and attack, very anime 10/10, but sometimes the aerial enemy is just out of reach, like beyond a hand rail, and youre just sitting there waiting for your gauge to fill so you can cast a spell- summon system is REALLY FREAKING COOL, but disappointing. You can only call on the summon when you fight a "hard" enemy. But its pretty arbitrary what the game determines as a "hard" enemy. Multiple times the summon started triggering and counting down when the boss was about to die that I killed the boss before I could get the summon out. Sometimes in relation to the point I made above about aerial enemies, it would start triggering just because the fight drags on so long because I cant hit the enemy. Also never have been able to get multiple summons out in a single fight- the stagger/limit system is good just seems pointless 90% of the time. Oftentimes the mob will die before you get to stagger them, which means even more rare you get to build up your limit to do that ultimate move, even on some bosses I killed them without ever getting a limit break off.- switching materia around is pretty cool, but outside of your basic offensive spells and heal spell, the majority of them just go unused because theyre just not impactful enough. Eventually regardless of proficiency, every character turns into this hybrid spell casting but most of the time spamming attack kind of characterTo sum upThe game is playable 100% and at the time of writing I'm almost done myself, but I'm finishing the game more because of loyalty and im definitely intentionally skipping content in the back half of the game just to get it over with faster. Too much of it is just meh, and outside of a couple of really well rendered cutscenes, theres not much thats very memorable about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This remake sits in a weird place. It's graphics, main story, motion capture and animations are clearly big budget. But it shows signs of troubled development and lingering ideas that needed to be cut entirely or sharply rewritten and reconsidered. The start of the game pretty much has no fluff, the first few chapters are the best this game can offer. Significant development, little padding. As soon as you get to Seventh Heaven that changes. Side quests turn into killing rats, finding cats, finding children, killing small mobs again. Cutscenes show pointless ♥♥♥♥. Walking somewhere, Sighs for no apparent reason followed by 3 seconds of silence into a response. Sections are entirely made up on the spot because some dude went "Soo...yeah dude, the game's about half way but it's only been 15 hours so I mean, we could write it better bro but I mean, just make Tifa or Aerith fall down this thing and let Cloud save them by doing this pointless section and that's about 30 minutes". Put 3 robot hands here and make them do this 3 times because ay? Mad? Invade SHINRA HQ and eh... let them climb 59 floors, let Tifa do some climbing section where the players holds W and make it take 15 minutes cus she falls down, she's so cute isn't she hi hi. If all else fails use the tried and true press stick forward and follow slowly gameplay... and some CEO goes "Write that down you idiots, this is the creative integrity we need, DOES NO ONE LIKE UBISOFT AROUND HERE???". The game is stained by these Side quests, it's stained by these sighs and pauses, theses padded out sections that are clear filler content only a Monke ( hi hi ) wouldn't be able to see. It's a disgrace that they call this a Remake for what almost certainly could be called a Demake. Every genuinely amazing step it takes forward, they take 3 steps back into the PS 3 console generation and poor game design.  They took a 10/10 or 9/10 game and created a jumbled mess of ideas, slapping the writers into a corner and telling them to make ♥♥♥♥ up or they won't get paid this month and staining a experience that was clearly made to be nothing but love for the original.As much as I ♥♥♥♥ on this game and give you objective information with no biases I still DID enjoy the game a lot. What I wrote above should be considered by everyone trying to buy the game but this section below is my love for FF 7. I ended up really caring about the story and characters. That's why I HATED the padded out Aerith section after meeting her again, it felt like an eternity to get back to the main story. I hated how poorly Wedge was used later in the game. Especially what happens to Jesse and Biggs. I was invested in blowing up the Reactors and how the game juggled it's politics but It all just kinda fell to the wayside.I love the combat of the game and how satisfying it feels to control Cloud. I loved finding weapons for him and the whole cast, giving them equipment and customizing their abilities. I love controlling each character in battles. The bosses were so fun to fight, not hard at all, but it was enjoyable watching them. Watching how they made them animate and fight you. I loved the dancing "rhythm section" with Andrea. The ending fight was an underwhelming mess but I was still hyped. SEPHIROTH, SEPHIROTH boss theme was soooo cool. I've never played the original game but that one is probably where you should go if you actually want to experience the story. This game is only a 3rd of the original one, padded out for more runtime while it desperately clinged to have less. Parts that kill the enjoyment exist and It feels like a lot of the Final Fantasy fans are blind to it out of nostalgia reasons. Instead of being an actual Remake It can easily be considered a Demake with a beautify effect on the camera lens. Cya.

_childDocuments_.review: The fonts in Final Fantasy VII Remake are way too small. Everything from the context-sensitive descriptions of various items in the Options menu to the ATB bars to all the abilities and their descriptions in the Fight menu—it's all way too small.Here is a screenshot showing "Adjusted various graphics-related settings" at the very bottom of the screen. That is the in-game font size used for many things when playing the game at 2160p. Above that is a font layer I added to the screenshot that is properly scaled. This is the minimum font size I would have chosen if I were doing UX on FF7R. And above that line is another font layer I added that shows what it could have looked like at 80px.And another:Generally, the issue with readable fonts is a solved problem, so when a AAA studio includes very small, anti-consumer fonts, it's very frustrating. The solution has been implemented in games and operating systems for over 15 years now. A simple formula is:Scaled Font Size = (Resolution / 480p) * 12pxFollowing this formula, you will get the scaled font size for any resolution. For example, at 4k, the minimum font size should be 56px. Dialogue, health numbers, headers, and other elements would typically need an additional 150-200% of this amount as well.What is important is the relative font size to the screen. If you solve for that, you can ensure the game is playable on the Steam Deck, desktops, and for people playing several feet away from a TV on their couch. But when it's too small like this, you're going to have at least 30% of your audience straining or squinting. It's unacceptable.What's worse is that Square already had a great example of appropriate font sizes in Final Fantasy XII: The Zodiac Age. Just compare—it looks so beautiful at 4k and is very easy to read. Dragon Quest XI is also very easy to read. So why did the devs of FF7 Remake go so wrong if Square knew how to do this internally?For this reason, I can't recommend the game. At this point, it's anti-consumer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game satisfied my expectations, full stop. I spent 46 hours with this (I didn't even spend the full time with everything they give you because hard-mode offers replayability + extra stuff to do for example: More side-quests, after-story stuff etc.) and if you are a fan, you'll enjoy it! As a game loved by many, they had a tall order to fulfil and everything from character interactions, voice acting, harnessing colloquialisms, music, capturing the charm of the story, it all worked. It's a beautiful game and very worthwhile.It is heavily story-oriented, and it left me wanting for more gameplay to be released into the world. The original game had this portion of the story very on rails as well, so the scope of the game was detrimental to this specific entry. That being said, they were able to add small elements of freedom, which was very bite-sized and wasn't completely satisfying. Their reuse of the areas was creative but again seemed a bit like spreading a little butter over too much bread. The game is basically how I expected Final Fantasy XIII to be (same linearity but with the same combat and FFXIII would've been amazing!).All things considered, the game is remarkably beautiful, fully polished and true to a remake. The boss fights were tough (especially if the wrong materia are equipped), varied and interesting (even though later on in the game it feels more of a "boss rush"). There were a lot of ways to build your characters. I found the gameplay very interesting, though there is room for improvement. My main gripe with the battle system is that it felt a bit too messy sometimes– I couldn't properly use abilities, spells, items because the actions took too long to animate. It basically took out the element of skill and planning: An enemy can jump across the screen and immediately stop you (sewer turtles..). This is supposed to make it more challenging, but I found it was often hard to tell when that was going to happen.I hope the rest of the game is less on rails... I loved the open-world aspect of the original and am very excited to see the next iteration.✔️ Best version so far, if you’re willing to do a few minor tweaks on your own (FF7 Hook to fix stutter, Modding, ReShade etc.)✔️ Excellent combat that reimagines FFVII’s ATB system in a modern way. It also caters to those who never want to use a menu with shortcuts.✔️ Excellent mod support day one✔️ Great remastered soundtrack that adds depth to the original.✔️ Superb retelling of the Midgar Arc with some plot changes that, while a bit daunting, end up fleshing out the world that much more and leaves us with anticipation for the next part.❌ Not everyone will like the changes the story does. Purists will probably hate them (?)❌ It has some padding in some sections. Perhaps five hours too long.❌ Dungeons have these slow-downs on the linear path to go under an object etc - some of these animations are completely unnecessary and it could be faster while moving out of combat.❌ Yuffie DLC feels out of place since it re-used sector 7 instead of any other one from the 8 (missed potential), and the "carnival" aspect and turtle show feel completely out of place.❌ Why is the lightning in this game so awful? Walking around in a house, leaving it and it feels like the game purposely tries to make me blind. Lighting in this game absolutely sucks.❌ You’ll want Part 2 right away.A fantastic remake now available for PC. Includes the DLC and DLC episode. It does have some technical issues but that is so easy to fix that I don’t feel the need to deduct a point from it. There is padding. Stretching a 30 minute section into a three-hour one is meh, BUT it's not really that bad when the rest of the game is this fantastic. I highly recommend it. It’s not perfect but it is a remake that was made with passion for the original game and it shows. If you already own the PS5 version, you can skip it BUT if you've never played it or lack a PS5 and don't mind a few tweaks, it's worth it.If you have never played FF7 and don't want to spend that much money as a "first-timer" and can ignore old-style graphics - check out the original:Costs only 6,49€ and you can check the story from the original without spending that much on the Remake and check for yourself why so many people loved FF7 in their childhood - just like me ♥CPU: i9 9900k @3,60Ghz (STOCK)GPU: RTX 2080 Ti MSIRAM: DDR4 32 GB RAM @2667MHzOS: Win10Resolution: 1440p 32" locked @60FPS

Then you can interact with the console, then you can go back to the door with another press and hold switch.Enjoy this 40 second dialogue cutscene, broken up with a forced slow walk to a short ladder that's followed by another dialogue cutscene.Welcome to town! You want a side quest? Go look for a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cats. Found them all? Now go play hide and seek with a bunch of kids.There's a really fun combat system (with its own faults) and a beautiful world that's so grossly padded out with ugly hallways, lots of backtracking through linear paths, cutscenes and forced slow walking and a million "let's make this take longer than it needs to" buttons and switches and animations.They really took what was a five ish hour section of the original game and padded it out to 30 hours.I'm on my fourth attempt of playing the game, just at the point of no return final act. I've played through the original upwards of eight times. Every time I try FF7R I find myself asking "why did the devs put this in the game? Do they actually think this is fun?".FF7R feels like a beautiful game that rarely ever let's me actually play it. There's just so much watching and waiting and walking.

_childDocuments_.review: This being my first Final Fantasy game, it certainly met my expectations. There are numerous cinematic scenes throughout each chapter, following Cloud's story as he teams up with Avalanche to fight against Shinra. Although Yuffie's storyline is shorter, it still introduces two new characters you'll easily grow attached to.The soundtrack was astonishing and beautiful, adding to the overall experience. There are three difficulty levels available: easy, normal, and hard, with hard mode only being unlocked after finishing your first playthrough. While easy and normal modes allow you to progress without frequently switching your materia, hard mode requires a significant amount of patience in each battle and demands frequent loadout adjustments for each character as you progress through the chapters.Overall, this game is a masterpiece, and I'm eagerly looking forward to playing part 2 when it releases.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, I've never played any other FF games (including the OG) before FF7 Remake. I took multiple screenshots throughout my second run on hard mode. Playing on the highest settings really allowed me to appreciate the details of the environments and characters.The OST went crazy! The OG tracks were enhanced to suit the atmosphere and intensity of key moments. The new soundtracks were also valid. Personnally, The Airbuster boss OST is my favourite. Voice acting was also very nice.For the story, I am aware that this game is more of a reimagining than a fateful remake but I'm not entirely a fan of how it's been handled. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a huge tragedy of a series of mistakes that started back in 2001 when Square fired Sakaguchi. The Tao Te Ching says "When the Sage's work is done, he forgets it: that is why it lasts forever." Sakaguchi got that--which is why he let every FF be it's own world and story, and moreover why he didn't put all the eggs in the FF basket. He didn't keep trying to rest on his laurels. He was taking bold risks. And sometimes when you take bold risks, you fail--which is what happened with Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within, an honest swing and a miss. But at least you can say about Spirits Within that it was original, that it wasn't padded with drivel. (I really think the only reason Spirits Within flopped was because it was called Final Fantasy when no one expected that a Final Fantasy would look like post apocalyptic sci-fi New York. It's a pretty darn good movie--It just isn't an FF at all.)With that said, it is not simply a mistake that Square decided to remake this franchise. It is fatal. They will not survive the next ten years, primarily because of this decision. Look people, we know they pay off the reviewers and we know that every platform can and does put their thumb on the scale of likes to dislikes if paid properly. FF7 is too big to fail, Square is no longer above doing shady things to gaslight people into buying their product for reasons other than it's an awesome game. And quite frankly, too many fans wanted this so bad that they are too primed to like it that they can't see or admit how this game is a complete flop.But really people, 12 half sucked, 13 was complete garbage--yes all three of them, 15 was basically all the worst elements of every western RPG slapped together in a world that was waaay too big with a story that was waaaay to small with a gameplay that was so convoluted and unforgiving that the game just literally asks you if you want to cut out huge swafts mechanics that were completely functional but complete BS. At least 13 kinda looked like a game that resembled other Final Fantasies and had gameplay that was actual ATB (which believe it or not, FF fans all really love ATB.) But 13's combat design was the most restrictive. So they decided with 15 to make a game that was so open that you literally get decision paralysis. It's a consistent principle of all successful games--and was consistent in all FFs. Give the player freedom, but a directed freedom. The Crystarium was completely linear with very meaningless suggestions of choice in character development. In FF10 you could go off the rails with character development but only at a certain point and in certain, meaningful ways. 15 is seriously mechanics upon mechanics, and none of it ever felt like it mattered that much. Original FF7 was the perfect balance of open and restriction. I never felt like there was decision paralysis. I could for the most part walk away from the main story and explore for secrets. The sidequests were few and varied and never tried to derail you from the main story. Battles were usually less than a minute. Bosses were usually less than 5 minutes. The game seriously respected your time while still being challenging and compelling. The mechanics for character customization feature possibly the most interesting example of emergent gameplay and interaction between mechanics we have seen in a JRPG--materia. The dungeons tend to be on the small side--usually 2 to 5 maps--and the save points are frequent--again respecting your time. The pacing of the story is perfect, although there are some amateurish moments in the writing (like why didn't Barret let President Shinra talk so much? Why wouldn't he just shoot him?), the mistakes can be forgiven because the characters are bright and fun and the plot has a lot of mystery. This is basically the opposite of everything about FF7R.So the plot is completely broken because there are no stakes because FF7R has entered the multiverse. They're now fighting the arbiters of fate, which come across as increasingly unconvincing since they are very selective about what things that were supposed to happen that they care about making sure happen. Not only are there no stakes, people are constantly falling and catching a ledge by one hand and constantly getting fatally wounded. Why do they keep padding the cutscenes with this garbage? I know that no one is supposed to die in the sewer in chapter 4 (or whatever), why would anyone other than a 5 year old find that suspenseful? By the way why don't we make this for adults first since it's adults who have the money, who are competent enough to play it and are probably the only ones playing it since to like this game you would have had to like the original already. (there's nothing here for new fans). Not only does it feel like FF7R now exists in a kind of Disney world where all the good guys are perfect angels and all the bad guys are puppy-eating child-snatchers, and no matter what happens all the good guys are gonna live and all the bad guys are gonna get their butts slapped. AVALANCHE, the eco TERRORIST organization are now so good that their bomb in reactor one was only supposed to be a little bitty one, but Shinra saw the bomb and decided to make it a 1000% bigger by hitting the self destruct button on the reactor. This is the case even though the people in the slums were so fed up with Shinra and the people living on the plate that they wouldn't care about killing people up there. And seriously, no NPCs die when the plate falls? Aerith evacuated all the people!? What is this Hallmark Channel B movie writing doing in this game? Why can't the Honeybee Inn be a brothel!? There's already supposed to be terrorists in this game, we can have some other flower girls too.! And yes, I saved it for last because everyone already said it, and also because you're supposed to save it for last--ENOUGH WITH SEPHIROTH ALREADY!!!!!--give me some flippin foreplay before you put it in, daddy! for the love of god, Buddha and the spaghetti monster!You guys at Square really had the ability to make the definitive version of FF7--just don't change it's story too much and modernize the gameplay. But instead you didn't jump the shark, YOU JUMPED THE SIN. It's not just the tedious, mandatory and frequent minigames. It's not just the painfully tedious platforming sections. It's not just the bloated character customization system with basically meaningless choices. It's not just the 15+ minute boss battles. It's not just that every little secret in the game is detailed in the menu with where to find every missable and how to unlock every door just handed to you. It's not just that the gameplay thinks it needs to be Dark Souls, despite the fact that Nier should have taught them a lesson about what people really want out of an easy, blockbuster, anime hack-n-slasher, It's literally everything about this game.I'm seriously at the point that I'm convinced the panderverse is a conspiracy, that the CIA has been going to every studio and insisting that they make garbage remakes of their most popular franchises. How come none of these remakes and reboots ever hit the mark? This game is so bad that they actually have to be trying to make it bad. And you could say that about countless other remakes. And you can be sure they're lying about the sales and the reception. It's like a conspiracy to make us hate the nerd stuff we grew up with and go outside or something. Who the heck would wanna do that!?And by the way, Crisis Core was also bloated slop. The dungeons were too big, there were tons of filler arcs that I'm embarrassed today to think that I played through them. The Gakt character was stupid, he needed to shut up about the goddess.

_childDocuments_.review: there is a version of this game that is my absolute favourite thing in the world! there are so many moments within this that show me the creators truly understand what made the original FF7's world so charming. it's not JUST cloud's backstory, and his beef with sephiroth, its all the weird and goofy ♥♥♥♥. it's squatting in the gym, its crossdressing, its fighting a giant house. this game even introduces new bits, like darts! seeing i could play darts made me over the moon happy! combat is similar and dissimilar enough to feel fresh while also making sense; materia works in the same way, ATB is still there, i think the did a really good job at modernising the way it worked back in 1997. the characters are spot on, and with more thought to its localisation each character gets more flavour, aerith in particular, feels infinitely more alive than she ever has. when she says "I'm not some princess who needs to be coddled, y'know... ♥♥♥♥!" I fell in love with her. graphically its stunning of course, and midgar is so amazingly realised too! each slum town feels rich and deep, wallmarket in particular as this home of debauchery and vice, i love it. i love what they did to midgar so much. the original music and revised music is all great; Underneath the Rotting Pizza is and incredible rearangement and yet Collapsed Expressway is an amazing original piece! there is so much here to love, SO much. fighting big bosses feels great most of the time, airbuster is awesome, the Turks are great, and each character's unique style makes them fun and exciting. the weapon system itself is cool, allowing for customisation thats more interesting and exciting that the original game. being able to play the whole game with the Buster Sword if you want, but also having the variety! wow!but nothing is perfect, especially if tetsuya nomura has had his grubby little mitts on it. i'm not saying the man can't write a good story, and for as bizarre as some of his stuff comes across, he does have rules for his stories. but i don't think this story needed destiny, or arbiters of fate, and while i appreciate we delete destiny at teh end of the game, we certainly dont need to add in extra plot twists like Zack and Biggs surviving; it just isnt necessary. i think its all red herring material personall,y, i think by the end of the trilogy both Zack and Aerith will have died, regardless of how its looking. we'll see! i could be wrong! also barret shouldnt have sunglasses, they suck. another bad thing is the filler, or at least some of it. i get that they wanted midgar to be its own game, and i even agree with that decision if the result is a midgar this fleshed out, but there are filler chapters that are genuinely awful. every side quest chapter is worthless, boring, unoriginal drivle. there isnt a single good sidequest in this game. do better next time, please. also, leslie and the sewer sequence feels tacked on and bad. i think they couldve done SOMETHING better than that too. there could have been a bit more on the plate i feel like, like on the way to the shinra building maybe we have another chapter, like chapter 2, where we're going through the streets of the plate to get to the tower, and so on. Hojo's lab is absolutely awful. i love a secret lab for the lore implications, but the story is nonexistent at that point and the manouvering is frustrating and weird. do better!looking forward to part 2 :)

_childDocuments_.review: Really wish I could give a review other than Yes/No.I enjoy the game when I'm actually playing it. The story isn't bad either. Unfortunately, the gaps between the enemy fights and actual story progression is filled with some of the most unbelievably annoying content that could possibly exist. There's also a weird paradox where the transition areas are so beautiful and detailed, but they're also hella tedious to navigate.I want to make it clear:- Holding a button to do something is not gameplay.- Climbing up and down ladders is not gameplay.- Forcing players to walk back and forth to press buttons is not gameplay.It's like the game developers had some mandatory quota for the above things for EVERY playable area, and it got to the point where I just got frustrated at the amount of "nothing" I was doing.The epitome of my personal experience was one (spoiler-free, don't worry) part where the characters need to urgently head to a certain destination. After an hour of navigating the area, holding down buttons to open doors, climbing ladders, and moving obstacles, my boredom *slowly* turned into frustration. But you know what? I told myself: Midgar is a trash heap - there are going to be obstacles, understandably.It was when the mini cut scenes started playing I had to turn the game off for a bit and chill. The characters would stop for 10-15 seconds, comment about something, then talk about how they're in a rush to their destination. Repeat this about 5 to 6 times. Maybe I'm less patient than I thought I was? Or maybe it was THAT egregious.Please. Trim down the fat of the game. I'd rather have a better experience over 15-20 hours than a mediocre 30-35. And "mediocre" is generous for how god-awful some of the pacing is.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Square didn't learn a damn thing from Final Fantasy 13; long drawn out linear hallways with literal zero input or impact from the player makes a very bad . Ten hours into the game and I don't think I've made any decision yet. Every "major" combat encounter is scripted to a T. You can't damage a boss more than a certain amount before a cutscene happens, summons are only allowed when the game says they're allowed, and limit breaks seem to only be available when the game has decided that combat is wrapping up. It's not a game- it's just a walking simulator with a story attached. No, honestly, that's all it is. There's no random encounters, there's no deviating paths, there's... Nothing. It's so boring.The thing is that this remake tries to take what the original game did in ten hours (at best) and turns it into a 40+ hour game. And that original ten hour experience was jam packed full of action and iconic moments- this game? It's just characters fawning over Cloud as if he's a literal god while winding through hallways and  having combat...Oh, and the combat, if you can call it that, is so bad. Everything is tied to a slowly generating ATB gauge, which is how the original was- but, the original was turn based, so it made sense. This? Why do I have to wait for the gauge to fill, choose a spell, wait for the spell to cast, wait for the spell to hit the target, while still having to expend MP? Like, what? Either have an MP cost on demand or have a gauge cost- having both just bogs everything down. And, jesus, didn't everyone collective agree that Final Fantasy 13 was , and yet the stagger mechanic is back. Doing no damage for awhile just to "stagger" a foe so you can have a burst window where you actually do damage is so tiring. Who thought that was fun? Oh, yeah, and every enemy has a stun-lock mechanic that is poorly telegraphed. The game is like, "Oh, you're in melee range? Here, let me stun-lock you while doing almost instant-kill damage." And there's no grinding to become more powerful, so it's just a question of wiping and slogging through the encounter again.The writing is also really bad. The original game made caricatures of the characters, because the game was already spread across four discs so there wasn't a lot of space to flesh out characters. In this game? So much character "development," and yet everyone is still a caricature without much depth. Yeah, having characters dialogue at you while leading you by the hand to the next chapter isn't character development- it's Fi from Skyward Sword. "Oh, you found a keycard, what can that be used for, Cloud?" I don't know, maybe it will unlock the ability for me to punt you out of the party so I never have to hear your whiny nonsense again, Tifa and Barret. And it's so nice of Square to make Barret just Samuel L. Jackson cosplaying as Captain Planet- sooooo much depth and nuance in that.There was so much Square could have done with FFVII, but this isn't it. They honestly should have just made a 1:1 remake with graphical upgrades and some quality of life improvements. This? Hot garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the game is gorgeous, and has a compelling story. It is more or less the same story as the original '97 version of the game but more fleshed out.The boss fights are unnecessarily long and tedious. The cut scenes have a tendency to last too long. I'm all for story driven narratives, but good lord, dial it back. I've probably seen what feels like 3 hours of cut scenes at this point.The new fight system has a steeeeeep leaning curve, and is easily the worst part of the game (for me) at this point. I'm more than 15 hours into this game and still struggling with the fight system. Maybe it'll get better. And maybe the combat system is the new norm for this genre, I don't know, but it kinda blows. The last time I played this genre was FFX. In any case, I would have preferred the classic combat system. Not this new "classic" combat system which also kinda sucks. The new "classic" combat mode just means that offense and defense is done for you (sort of) so you can use spells, items, and abilities -- IF available. _childDocuments_.review: I consider FF7 (1997) the greatest game of all time. I've been playing games since Spectrum, NES etc. Back when FF7 came out, GTA was a quirky top down arcady game. Since then GTA has come a long way. But at that time, FF7 took gaming to new heights. Unprecedented story depth that surpassed the Legend of Zelda, and a tactical and strategical combat system that allowed you to wisely customize and massively boost the power of your squad through wise between battle decisions. The open world was perhaps unlike seen before, albeit I have yet to play FF6, which I intend to. The characters and plot were deeply portrayed and there was a strong sense of mystery. The capacity to explore was huge, and there were incredible encounters and secrets that were beyond the main story and completely hidden and optional. The scope of the game was unprecedented and delivered on 3 separate but continuous PlayStation disks of sprawling content. The cutscenes were revolutionary, as was the incredible soundtrack that continues to win awards. In totality, FF7 (1997) offered a true sense of transcendence.So how does the Remake stand up to this? I consider the Remake to have revolutionary CGI. The CGI graphics are spectacular and do justice to the original. Despite decades since I beat FF7 (1997), the script seemed to stay true to the original, although I think there might have been some early reveals, which I am not sure were appropriate. The story continues to be excellent and evocative. The characters were portrayed excellently, true to the original. Probably I am too experienced, but the combat was much too easy for me, but still fun overall. Perhaps hard mode could have been available from the start? Having replayed the Midgar section of FF7 (1997) I can confirm that there are new, quite substantial, story embellishes in the Remake that are quite unusual compared to the original. Also, I would consider it to have inappropriate boss encounters if staying true to the original game and story flow, which violates the lore and mystery of the original game.While more amenable to button basher fans the combat veered towards Bayonetta-esque gameplay, but I think it was an intelligent balance nevertheless. I should say that for the truest fans of the original, this is a slightly questionable outcome, as the combat now shifted from strategical to a lot of evasion and button bashing. However, perhaps I played it too effectively, and I think newcomers probably found the system challenging and hence exciting. The strategical combat layer (with materia) was still rewarding and fun. Now that I am replaying FF7 (1997) after decades, I realize that they stayed true to the leveling up of materia, which I thought was an additional feature. The soundtrack was better than ever, but stayed true to the gorgeous original soundtrack. However, I wonder if some of the songs were delivered a bit early considering the original script.Indeed, a weakness of the Remake is its desire to rush the story of FF7, likely for profitability. I won't lie, the Yuffie expansion is pretty fun, and I like the strategy mini-game. However, I have to question the use of Yuffie compared to the original, again rushing FF7 story, but hopefully it is compatible and true to the original script. You see, I want to learn more about FF7, not see it re-scripted. The worst terminator movie (5) was because of an effort to give an alternate future to the original movie, and it worked out horribly wrong, not least due to the horrible casting (especially of Kyle Reese). So, please stick to the tried and true for an epic like FF7, especially after 20+ years when we have all forgotten the amazing original story anyway, probably because we were kids, because we still remember it enough to know if you are butchering it. You can split it up, add embellishes, improve the overall polish, but please stay true to the beloved story.As for the expanse of the game, this is the Remake's biggest downfall. This game contains only the intro section of FF7 (1997), which was always more restrictive than the rest of the game, but still provided for over 50 hours of game play so far. Perhaps I should be grateful that Square went to such an effort to portray this section of the original game, but I am concerned about the continuity of the game play with successive installments. How does my progress in this game connect to the next? What about my materia and upgrades? So that is an issue because the first game had total continuity through its epic, open world adventure. This game is a fraction of that adventure, and does not even come close to the scope. I understand from a marketing and business perspective they might have not had much choice; but how can I compare this to the original FF7, there is no comparison. FF7 (1997) was a continuous, sprawling, open world epic, and the developers went out of their way to deliver revolutionary scope. This game is very much modernized, stunning, but much more restrictive and only a fraction of the original story, with strong efforts in the CGI department, but less so in the efforts to deliver truly revolutionary RPG scope like the first.Definitely recommend this game anyway, and wish Square continued success. I will be playing the other installments also.Summary: Amazing sound, animations and graphics. Good game-play with some variety, adapted but reasonably true to the original game. Quite linear considering the genre and a small fraction of the scope of FF7 (1997). Excellent, inspiring story but cut short.EDIT: After decades I am now playing through my favorite game, FF7 (1997) and I can say that the Midgar section and the overall experience is very faithfully reproduced by the Remake, and so I am increasingly appreciative of these efforts, including the effort to give more depth to the story. Although, the concerns about continuity still stand in terms of leveling the character and such between future installments. Having finished 1997 again completely, I can say that FF7 back in 1997 was not only dramatically more expansive, but actually took me longer to finish than the 2020 edition. That speaks volumes for the 1997 production value, but also says something about Square's intent to embellish the Midgar section in 2020. 1997 has to be considered the superior game at a fraction of the price, if you can get past the dated technology.The Yuffie expansion is also worth playing, and has stunning visuals and good gameplay. The best part of the Yuffie campaign is surely the ending, which shouldn't be missed, especially for FF7 fans.

_childDocuments_.review: The PC port of the remake is just a mess. Do not get confused by the first hour as all the linear corridors only mask the game´s true problem - the stuttering in open areas. Due to Square´s amateurish programmers who clearly are not able to work with UE4 properly the game has problems with the streaming of textures. This causes the stuttering. It is funny when you realise this is happening despite the fact that the vast majority of textures are simple, low-res and awful looking PLUS object meshes are so low poly as well. Just take a look at this:  .Final Fantasy VII Remake as a game is a good one, nothing to die for at all, but it can be fun. The combat system is enjoyable, the extended Materia system deepens the original Materia system allowing the players to "role-play" more. The design of the environments is mostly good, sometimes very good. There are plenty of minigames, a colloseum to beat, the fantastic interactive Cloud dressing scene, the motocycle scene is now much longer and much better designed. I like how Square deepened the original story and also gave life to many characters from the AVALANCHE group. They have a much bigger role now which is great not only for the bigger role´s sakes, but because Square handled it really good. Yeah, there are loads of good things.On the other hand there are equally as many bad things. I mentioned the average looking graphics (except the main characters that look top notch, tho common NPCs are so shallow), but the the artstyle is very nice, so that is why the game does not look bad at first sight. The more you look at the graphics, the more you dont like it. The game takes place only in the beginning Midgar part which in the original game last like 5 hours. The remake took those 5 hours and extended them to 50 hours adding a filler content, boring fetch quests and tons of cutscenes. The game can also be very limiting as it "guards" your path very often and does not allow you go where you want which you´ll know for the WARNING sign warning you that you are leaving the mission area. Yes, that WARNING as if this was a COD game. And yeah, Square, since this is a PC game, can you add the mouse cursor support in the main menu? I am a k+m player and I am sick of using arrows when browsing the menu. + the reorchestrated musical score+ the added depth to some AVALANCHE members+ the main characters look beautiful+ the extended Materia system (you can focus on Magic and be a magician, or a raw power and be a warrior; tho nothing else regarding traditional role-playing classes)+ the combat system is fun, but Classic Mode sucks+ bossfights are great+ the game gets better in the second half+ INTERGRADE is a welcome addition which deepens the story of REMAKE+ the story has a nice twist to the original game allowing Square to get rid of their ties to the original story and make a completely new story in Rebirth and the final third game of the remake saga+ the Arbiters of Fate story addition+ minigames are great and fun+ the expanded dungeons are nicely designed - the graphics of the environment is just so bad (bland and low res textures, low poly mesh objects, bad lighting, ugly NPCs with strange movements, pre-rendered backgrounds look horrible because of their low resolution)- tons of typical fetch quests that can be found in MMORPG (nothing unique, average content, boring execution, lifeless quest givers)- stuttering in the open areas is sometimes unbearable- annoying invisible walls (many times you cannot explore environments because a WARNING sign appears and turns your character back which is so limiting and stupid)- many times the game forces you to do something or go somewhere which is frustrating (for example, Tifa is waiting for you in front of your apartment and the game literally pushes you to her and does not allow you to explore the surroundings)- handholding (sometimes the game explains everything in so much detail that you may feel like a complete idiot - for example the crane puzzle)- missing the mouse cursor support Final Fantasy VII Remake is a good game tho it is clear that the game definitely does not reach the quality of the original game. It is because instead of a worth new content the game rather focuses on empty boring fetch quests (sometimes it is even a mandatory thing for the story to continue which is not good). The combat system is really great and it is fun to to play as Barret or Tifa. I absolutely adore the new story feature - the Arbiters of Fate - which I consider to be a really clever twist that not only fits the Final Fantasy VII world but, which is more important, basically allows Square to come up with original ideas in the next two games of the remake saga that can be implemented to the story without breaking the original story. Fantastic!! The Intergrade expansion is a content worth playing not only because has great bossfights and level design but also because it contains an additional ending cutscene which just cannot be missed by anyone who cares about the story and cannot wait for Final Fantasy VII Rebirth.

_childDocuments_.review: This one has it's issues. Without nitpicking, they boil down to three, massive problems.1) The stuttering issue has not been fixed, although there are workaround that help, they  aren't perfect. I have seen that  this has been an issue since it first launched on PC TWO YEARS AGO.2) Being incomplete. The "Remake" ends at a point that is not even a third of the original  game, which means that there are at least 2 more coming, just to cover one games remake.3) The price. This one, despite being incomplete, wants you to pay 70$ for it. Not only is the  game not whole, the price is a  departure from the standard 60$ for a AAA game that we have had for 20+ years. One might  think, 'hey, its just 10 more  bucks, that's not so bad.' And if this were the only game to do so, you might be correct. It  won't be though. Other  companies will look at this, and then charge 70 bucks for THEIR game, because hey, it  worked for this one. And then 80$  games will start appearing. Such will continue until games STOP getting sold, and at that  point the QUALITY will suffer BEFORE the price drops.This one ALSO has its upsides.1) The game looks, really good. There are some fairly obvious areas where the appearance is  clearly subpar compared to  the rest of the game, but those parts aren't truly important. The characters, playable, npcs,  enemies, and especially the cut-scenes all look great.2) The game play is fun, and engaging enough to be entertaining, even if your companions  aren't quite aggressive enough.3) Outside of the stuttering during cut-scenes, the game runs great on my upper mid-tier  laptop.And its more neutral aspects.For me this really is only the added story elements. They are a bit too kingdom hearts for me. They are neither good, nor bad.Ultimately, I only bought this one due to the launch sale, and already having enough cash in my steam wallet to cover the rest. Otherwise I would not recommend purchasing without a 50% sale at bare minimum.

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal reimagining of Part/Disc 1 from the original game. I genuinely think I have zero complaints or criticisms. The studio shifted to real-time combat similar to Crisis Core or FF15 and it feels very tight. The weapon systems are different than the original and add a nice level of customization that didn't exist in the original. The story is excellent and really fleshes out all of the characters from Part 1, adding depth that the original couldn't. The soundtrack is amazing and pays homage to much of the original score. The graphics are gorgeous throughout. The team really poured themselves into this and it shows in the quality of the game.A couple key differences are: the number of independent (less) and support (more) materia; how summon materia function; and the number of limit breaks. I think these are take-or-leave differences that don't impact the quality of the game, but some might disagree. Highly recommend to any fan of FF7 and to anyone looking for a solid JRPG.

Without wanting to spoil anything: It is unclear what exactly causes most of the divergences from the original timeline and I doubt any of it will ever be explained, did  fart after he did whatever he did, causing a ripple through time and space that somehow explains why the ♥♥♥♥ some of the differences exist? Probably not, it's probably all just a cheap excuse to have the dementors appear on screen.The story is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ embarrassment, not only did they stretch a 6-8 hour story out to 30-35 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hours, they also butchered everything that the original stood for and then spat on it. The final chapter is basically just that, an insult to the fans of the original, a cheap attempt at meta commentary that is supposed to seem deep and meaningful but ultimately fails because of how badly it has been written and because of how unnecessary it is in the first place.Gameplay is mediocre at best, the combat system feels unrefined and not well thought out. They should have either committed to a more turn based system or a more action based system. I didn't mind the command aspect too much, what I did mind though is that there is more unavoidable damage in the game than there is avoidable damage, it feels cheap; seldom did I actually feel like I was killed because I made a mistake, more often I just got stun locked upon entering combat and just watched my health bar disappear into nothingness as though it had never been there in the first place. Who the ♥♥♥♥ balanced this ♥♥♥♥? A first grader? I did eventually beat the game on Hard mode which was far easier than expected but god was it frustrating. There was absolutely no challenge in this game, only frustration, frustration that made me even less interested in the absolutely butchered version of a story that I remember being quite fond of when I played the original a few years back. I may not have grown up with it but I do faintly remember that I played through the game a few years ago.The cherry on top of all this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the atrocious level design solely centered around padding out the run time of the game for as long as possible cause you gotta get a few dozen hours of game time out of this absolute dumpster fire. A dumpster fire that costs 80 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ €, I feel ripped off and I bought this game during a sale for like 40€. Final Fantasy VII Remake doesn't respect your time and money, nor is it worth either of those.The side story is much better than the main game. It doesn't overstay its welcome with an overly padded out story, it has unique combat mechanics that actually give some level of fun to the combat and it has an awesome mini game. I was actually a little disappointed at how quickly this side story ended since I would have loved to see more and experience more of the combat. The synergy system is amazing, it's fun. Honestly had they included it in the main game I might not have disliked the combat quite as much as I ended up doing.Sadly Intermission suffers from similar problems as the main game, namely ♥♥♥♥ level design. But it did fix the clunky traversal mechanics from the main game, for example climbing actually feels fluid now and not like it was designed solely around making you play the game just a few minutes longer.

_childDocuments_.review: I always like to break these games down with a pros and cons list. The following is why I think this game is utter trash and why I am saddened at watching the downfall of Square-Enix as they continue to pump out garbage in the hopes of making money while exploiting what was an amazing franchise.Pros:*The cinematic in this game are top tier. If there was anything that they invested into the game it was making the kids look adorable, and making the animation of the characters crisp. There is even a couple cinematics that I would consider best animation quality top 10 of the decade. *Materia that is equipped, showing up on weapons was very cool. It gave you just a slight feel of impacting the game.Cons:*The Voice Acting/Scripting. Especially for Barrett, was obnoxious and ridiculous. I felt ashamed and embarrassed for black people every where at how obnoxious they animated Barrett. I have lived in Japan for close to a decade, so I know that a lot of these voice acting absurdities come from legitimate bias in the Japanese culture. *Destiny Ghosts. WTF I mean really WTF. A bunch of magical ghosts somewhat/mostly/who knows controlled by Sephirorth (our new cosplay femboy character, nothing like the original) that serve no purpose other than to annoy the crap out of you......*Plot Armor. Because they decided to not remake full game and instead just made a whole game about Midgar (im sure based on making more profit on selling part 2s and part 3s down the road), they had to develop new plot lines they couldn't just parasite off of the original FF7. When they deviated off of the original game to add content it was obvious, plot/scripting was dumb, chapter/quests were tedious, character cut scenes were annoying and boring take your pick. Where it really annoyed me is when they tried to add plot surprises. Just FYI if you're walking on a pipe above sleeping monsters, the pipe will break and you'll fall into the monsters. If you need to be stealthy, Barrett will start yelling and you'll get into a fight with shinra troops. These are just a few examples of the constant tropes you experience in this game.*RPG. Look, I am glad that Square-Enix thinks that their new fighting model versus the old turn based system is better. I however, disagree. I think its dumb and stupid. If you're going to impose a remake of an old game, give us the option to play under the old game style.  I cannot mention how many fights i got in where I didn't have the right materia equipped because the fight required spell counters to be won. Ide end up assessing mobs then letting them kill me so i could restart fight with right materia equipped. Nothing worse than having an elemental attack equipped that heals enemy so all you can do with that one character is sit out of fight....*Macros/autocasting. In the whole game there is only one materia, and when I say 1 i mean there is only 1 of its kind and only 1 available in the whole of the game that auto-casts. Of course its a low tier cure that doesn't even upgrade...... Why can I not just set up my characters to auto-attack, block, and auto use abilities/spells in a fight versus having to cycle through them in the most annoying fashion while simultaneously engaging in a real time fight. *Lack of open world. The whole game is scripted to the point of nausea. There is almost no ability to roam off on your own and farm mobs or upgrade materia outside of the plot. Its a lock step, follow-the-path, game that is in direct betrayal of what made all the original Final Fantasies so good. Players loved the original final fantasies for their open world experiences. We loved that there were hidden quests to complete and locations to explore, and hidden items/weapons to attain.*Items. Collecting the music was dumb.....The mogul store was dumb and annoying to get to, collecting weapons was often just as simple as buying them at weapons shop, potions were dumb and ineffectual, none of the gear other than weapons that you equipped on your character changes their look, and there was only three gear item equip slots.......Don't get me started on how dumb the materia and upgrading weapons sections are. This materia use process was about as imbecilic as when they tried the whole "clothes materia" in FF12.  They turned materia into the meta balance of the game and side lined armor. I mean Cloud  is still rocking the same stupid looking shoulder plate with bolts that he is in chapter 1. *3 Person Teams. In keeping with their continued attempt to ruin FF7 they made sure that you were restricted to no more than 3 person per team fight. Now this got very annoying because if you specc'd your team with Barrett being support and Cloud being more of a tank counter, and then the next fight Tifa and Aerith are matched up together, then enjoy replaying last battle 5 time before you finally get lucky enough to pop off enough spells/abilities to stay alive. *Falling. For some reason, in the game, they were obsessed with having characters fall ridiculously high places and survive but the characters cant even jump down from 3rd to second floor in Jenova chamber......another slapstick plot armor mechanism that makes the game even less enjoyable.In conclusion, this game is an utter betrayal of its original and this abomination should have never happened. This is just one of a long line of mistake Square-Enix has made in the pursuit of money over actually granting the player base what they desire. Once again another game is made in an attempt to "attract younger players" that does nothing more than insult the original players. If I could give this game more than one thumbs down I would.

_childDocuments_.review: Like so many I grew up with FF7 being one of the hallmark experiences of my gaming childhood. When I heard they were remaking FF7 I was excited but disappointed it was going to be a PS exclusive. I only recently became aware they ported the game to PC and was excited to learn this, picked it up quickly.Like a fool, I didn't seize the opportunity immediately to try the game out for defects, like a fool, I let the refund window elapse before I'd even known what I'd gotten myself into...Okay, in all fairness, the game isn't that bad. It isn't perfect, but it's a decent recreation of the first disk of FF7. The combat system is different, it's much more akin to crisis core or FFXV, which isn't bad, but it does make for a dramatically different experience. Even the "classic mode" which has the game input basic commands for you while you are focusing on planning your spells and ability uses was rather limited. The friendly AI was pretty good considering at not getting plastered by bosses with raid style mechanics ("dont stand in the fire" etc) so for the most part you do just have to only worry about the actions of a single character. It would've been beneficial however to have more automated AI behaviour as has been seen in some other games like FF12 and 13.The story was created with great visual fidelity to the original, there are scenes they had to take liberties on, others told and shown in greater context, and the occasional event that doesn't quite exactly follow the storyline of the original, leaving you always guessing what's happening next. It seems as though this is FF7 as seen in some other timeline, yet much like in the series Loki featuring multiple timelines, there seems to be some force trying to constrict events to a certain outcome. Interesting enough twist to keep people who've played the original still feeling like there's more to see than just some new polish.Okay, so why is this a flat out negative review? Well, if you haven't realized yet, like SO, SO many of Squeenix's ports, the attention to care and quality control of this port is absolute gutter trash. There are several major bugs that are essentially unavoidable no matter how much work you spend trying to fix them, namely the game audio in this version somehow constantly dies when the audio engine is even remotely taxed, causing the whole game to sound like you just grabbed your speakers and jumped into a pool with them. It's probably the worst audio issue I've ever encountered in any game ever. The only way to combat this is to turn the volume in game settings down to 1 in every category and then crank your speakers to the max and even then you can barely heard the game. The second you get an outside notification not from the game say goodbye to your ear drums. This is an absolutely debilitating issue for this game and you might as well accept that the game is going to sound like whispers or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if you're going to choose to play with any audio at all.The second issue pertains to cutscenes. For some reason, the game is not capable of displaying or processing certain cutscenes, many of which are pretty critical to understanding and following the story. When this issue occurs the screen freezes frame and dialogue audio continues while all other sound elements are removed from context often leaving you staring in silence at a still frame for what feels like an eternity. Apparently there's a community "fix" for this that requires you to individually download each and every video file one by one and replace them all, every cutscene file in the game which they hosted as separate individual files just to make it as nightmarishly tedious as possible. But jesus christ why is it up to the community to make the game just playable as it was meant to be played? I should've learned my lesson by now and you should learn it from me too, don't trust Squeenix PC releases to not be bug ridden pieces of ♥♥♥♥ that should never have been released and that will never be patched.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally finished the game today. Looking at the steam achievements, less than 1/3 of the people who own this game have actually beaten it. It's not a long game. You can probably beat it in about 30 hours. I took closer to 50 hours because for a time I attempted to get Bahamut, before I decided to just beat it to see the story.  I played the original Final Fantasy 7 when I was a teenager, about 14 I think. It was a massive chunk of a game with a huge world to explore, tons of different enemies, a variety of minigames, a convoluted plotline, tragedy, heroism, and a bittersweet ending. At the end of what had to be more than 70 hours of necessary gameplay, you finally descend into north crater and have a final epic showdown with Sephiroth. This game felt to me like it was simply a cash grab that cheapened any of the actual drama and plotline of the original. This game is pretty, and it has a decent battle system. However, you get all the materia you're going to need before you leave the slums and go to the Shinra Building. That means for the last 1/2 or maybe 1/3 of the game, there is nothing you find that is needed and none of the Materia is new.  The final battle tried SOO hard to convince me that it was an epic showdown with a villain I should care about, but I just didn't care, because it's not earned. Sephiroth exists merely as a shadow of his reputation from other games, but they threw him into the game anyway. The last battle is all about 'fighting destiny' and I'm here thinking, but I liked the way the original game played out. Aerith's death was necessary for the plotline to achieve the gravitus and emotion that it had. If you take it away, then things are just too easy. So, my conclusion is that this game is mostly entertaining for about the first half of the game, and then after that, they begin cheapening the original plotline while making the plot of this game weak. I doubt I'll purchase the sequel.PS There are flashbacks which appear to be literally grainy video from the original final fantasy 7. I can't tell if this is a homage or a show of phenomenal laziness. I also saw a complete rehash of the battle zone from Final Fantasy 7: Advent Children which I also wonder if they used as recycled assets.
