_childDocuments_.review: I am sure you are questioning yourself, do i need the dlcs for the game being playable ? Actually not, vanilla game has in total 67 playable vehicles which 26 out of it are dlcs.With 9 different Regions which contain 26 different maps, 14 of those are dlcs.That sounds like quite alot, but it's not a big deal.Game is actually a very playable even without having a single dlc.If you are a coop player, you will love this game, if you think you wont be able to play with your friend due to not having all the dlcs? don't worry if he has all the dlcs and you not a single one, you can still play with him all day long. _childDocuments_.review: I will say "yes" -- but it's not for the faint of heart.  (See TL;DR in SUMMARY at the bottom)Only bother with this game if you are masochistic and/or have plenty of perseverance.  I'm typically an even-tempered person but this game can easily throw me into a bit of a rage.  The game designers are unforgivingly evil in what they have created.  Oh yes, it is very purposeful to work against the player all the way throughout, even at the very end of a mission after hours of work, they will throw a curveball at you that you won't expect and it will topple your truck in an instant before you even realize what the hell happened.And, yet, the frickin' game must have something subliminal in it, because I am addicted to coming back for more punishment, over and over.- Sounds are some of the best I've heard in a vehicle/truck game.  No cheesy horns, or electronic engine revving.  Lots of variety all sound realistic.  It's a pleasure to start the bigger guys up, just to hear it - and turn them off too- (Overall) physics are pretty good.  Particularly the "cockpit mode" is great, complete with all the bouncing & leaning that would come along with it- Given the level of challenge, when you do accomplish something, you definitely feel accomplished, because it _actually_ took a crap-ton of work and skill to do it!- Certainly better than SpinTires/MudRunner; lots varied missions that make a little more sense, and have rewards; plenty of vehicles available in the base game (Which is great bc I despise having to purchase overpriced DLCs)- The bigger trucks (much much later in the game) are actually fun to operate!  Armored scout is (a little slow but) fantastic, after finally getting that- Graphics are reasonably good.- Accessories & customizations are nice features (though I wasn't really able to spend money on them through most of the game)- It may teach you virtues like: humility, patience, perseverance, how to deal with painful mistakes, & calm in the face of utter frustration- Steering wheel support was pretty iffy in earlier releases; later, took some initial pains to figure out how to get it working w/the game- No "true" manual shifting (unlike in previous ST/MR).  Sad point. However, was able to config my shifter to switch some gear modes that  made it feel like shifting. Clutch use is meaningless.- Modulation of gas pedal was not very effective; tiniest pressure and the wheels start moving as if it's half depressed!  By 1/4 way, it's full-power.  Not ideal for easing out of mud & snow!  Rather, must rely on choosing a gear --  you have advanced enough to have that- Sometimes mud dead-stops a truck at high speed as if it hit a brick wall; and despite being what should be a high-torque rev, the engine will stall. It's their way of saying "use a lower gear" but doesn't feel natural.- Unlike most games, this starts out super-hard, and gets (a little) easier as you go.  Be ready for a rough time until you learn and progress more!- I can't multi-mash the horn (No honk-honk possible!)  Once horn sounds, you can't stop it by letting go, and it must sound completely before another one. Not a big deal, but oddly I find the horn one of the more enjoyable things about this game.  Hah!- Gas seems to burn off too quick -- even when simply idling!- Some vehicles just didn't perform as well as I'd expect; excited to get the Hummer, but turned out to be an unusable piece of garbage, even after upgrades!- Level designs don't really make realistic sense a lot of times- Camera system SUCKS many times.  Forces you to remain zoomed in close to your vehicle (unless you constantly spin your mousewheel).  Walls, watchtowers, and buildings make the view freak out and flip-flop between looking straight-down and the view you're really wanting.  Highly disorienting!- Annoying mission system mechanics: 1) Despite being at a (visible, even) turn-in point, you must switch to the mission before it lets you turn it in.  2) You must hitch a trailer and its load to be able to turn it in, or use the repair supplies on it, even though it's literally sitting right where it needs to go, it does not count until you bring a truck with the right hitch and attach it -- DUMB!- It may teach you anti-virtures like: anger, rage, and loss of faith-   Do NOT go that way!  Take what *appears* to be the long way.  True, almost without fail through the whole game.- There is no shame in using Recover- Get big Mud tires as soon as able- Be creative, even if it feels unrealistic.- Config keys/buttons to use quick-winch & release quickly & easily- Keep your path so its near large winchable objects; it will save you.- Monitor fuel gauge & get good at estimating what you can do- Use back/forth steering, along w/winch if possible, and lower gears, slowly pulling you out of deeper terrain.- Turn off engine when studying the map or waiting un-paused- Don't go into deep mud & water zones until later in the game! That truck sitting out there is a trick.- In regular mode, selling vehicles gives back as much as it costs to buy, so you won't lose money by selling them back. Extra trailers you find can also be sold.- Put on a podcast or show, then just go at missions w/a measured pace.  Me?  I pretty much caught up on all the Critical Role episodes by firing them up every time I went to play this game.  :D- It would be great if you could have trucks or equipment that could actually *repair* roads.  Then, it would be players choice if they wanted to take the time to get through the muck and mire and boulders everywhere, or if they wanted to take the time to clean-up and build a proper road.  Then, at least, the highway tires and vehicles might actually be able to be used.- A toned-down mode of the game might be useful, until you get used to its mechanics and want to tackle the normal and hard modes afterward.  I'm sure I lost a couple years off my (real!) life from the frustration I felt from playing it.  Games are supposed to be fun... right?- More true utility from modulation of the gas and clutch pedals.- Return to proper manual shifting, like in previous SpinTires/MudRuner.- Being able to get out of the vehicle in some situations would be useful / fun / realistic.- Having an autonomous winch in the "Slope" Trial sure would be nice.  But, evil designers aren't nice.- I also wish evil designers were at least occasionally nice.Since a lot of the detail above is more just me getting my rants out of my system after 200+ hours of play, this is the TL;DR:If you're looking for a casual game.  This is NOT it.  This requires work.  If you're looking for a true challenge, or just enjoy big trucks and romping around in the mud (at slower pace, not monster truck stuff) and can deal with the games vein-popping experiences, then this is the game for you!Remember, though, the first part of the game takes the most effort, IMO.  So, get through that, and then you will start to be rewarded.  It still doesn't let up on the challenges - ever - but you will at least have proper equipment for the job, and a variety of things to do or choose from.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I bought SR I refunded it. I kinda thought its cool but like every new player I thought it was hard and frustrating and I could'nt understand where the fun/reward is or whats fun and rewarding about going slower than a granny on a stick through endless puddles of mud, snow and water. It's worth mentioning that Iam by no means someone who likes hard games. And I have almost no patience when it comes to video games.But it kinda lived in my head. I wanted to like it, I knew there had to be something to it. All the positive reviews just could'nt lie. So, I bought it again. A guy that hates simulations, has no interest in cars or trucks and the only "driving" games he played were GTA and mario kart.And while I played through the tutorial a friend of mine, that has even less interest in games like SR, watched me play it and bought it because of the coop.And then another friend who has also no interest in racing/car games and cars or trucks in general also bought it.And for the next month or two we were roleplaying truckers, doing contracts, hauled cargo, checked out watchtowers, collected upgrades and customized our favourite trucks.It's been over a hundret hours now and while the others kinda went on and barely play SR anymore, I'm still into it very much and even bought lots of the dlc's.Every simulation nerd will scream that this is not a simulation. And while there are still moments where I fight for every inch in a sea of mud or snow, there are almost no more moments where I dont know whats wrong, why Im moving in slowMo all of a sudden or what to do about it.SR rocks!tl;drTrant ist Schuld das ich SR spiele

_childDocuments_.review: Snow runner is the much anticipated sequel to Mud runner, the third game in the spintires off road simulation series, and this new installment takes the spintires concept from being a curious toy to a full fledged game.  Quite a monumental leap to say the least.  I won't be covering many of the things that stayed the same from mud runner, as I already made a review of it.It does this mainly by adding a new progression system.  Trucks and upgrades are now earned through money, an XP level system, and scavenged from the maps as you play.  In some ways, this makes the game into a bit of a metroidvania type of ordeal.  There are many areas starting out that you simply cannot reach with your current equipment.  And that can be rather frustrating to someone unfamiliar with spintires.  Your biggest enemy is yourself if you don't know what your trucks can and cannot do.  Many judgement calls will have to be made.  Especially when doing a super heavy haul contract with early game equipment.That being said, another big change to the spintires formula is the kind of work you will be doing in this game.  Before it was simply hauling logs from the yard to the lumber mills.  And while those jobs still exist in snow runner, you'll also have to haul a variety of different cargoes and the super heavy trailers mentioned before.  As well as vehicle recovery operations.  You can pick and choose what jobs to do for the most part, but some are required to complete to unlock others.  And this brings the biggest change to the game, the new open world maps.The base game is split into three regions.  Michigan, Wisconsin, and the Tamir river Siberia.  So two of the three games are in America now.  And these three regions are split into four maps each that are linked together through tunnels or checkpoints.  The maps are like your typical spintires maps.  You need to get to watch towers to clear up your own 3D map you have, and find gas stations, repair hubs, garages and resource points.  Some of which need deliveries to get running.  Bridges may also need to be built and rock slides cleared through deliveries as well.  All of these maps have a main goal in mind that usually amounts to finishing a megaproject.  A new oil derrick or pipeline being built to show you made a difference in the world.So now we have the trucks themselves.  There's a massive variety of them this time, and nearly all of the western trucks are licensed by the companies that make them.  The first person cockpit view is now faithfully detailed with functioning gauges and dashboards for every truck in the game.  Horns are now different for each vehicle and engine sounds are unique as well.  All vehicles feature not only a slew of modules for different jobs, but also a massive variety of cosmetics as well.  Light bars, bull bars and bumpers, fenders, flashing lights, roll cages, visors, you name it.  As well as stickers for the outside and inside.  And inside you can get bobbleheads, fuzzy dice, air fresheners, and curtains.  The vast majority of them are actually not even paid DLC.  With many being unlocked through the trial modes.There's a new damage model as well.  And its...  Alright.  Vehicle components now have their own hit points, which is good in practice, but this also means that the cabin is free to take fatal high speed impacts with trees that would total your truck in a previous game with no damage suffered.  And in my personal opinion the components have too much health.  Out of all the hours I've played I've never destroyed my engine, fuel tank, suspension, or gear box.  I've only punctured a tire three or four times, and that's usually the result of the damage system glitching when mounting a hard object like a curb or rock at a funny angle.  The suspension will also constantly be taking 1 or 2 points of damage as you drive along a road for some reason.  But its so tanky you never need to worry about it actually breaking.  If I were to change anything, it would be cutting vehicle hit points in half to be honest.And the last thing I have to add is that the flavortext in this game is something else.All in all, if you were a fan of any of the other games in the series, this one goes above and beyond those before it.  Its eurotruck only the road hates you, the cargo hates you, and the truck hates you.  And I can't get enough of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the first game in the Series Mudrunner, Snowrunner follows the same basic gameplay, Transport things however you see fit from A to B, or C, sometimes D, and “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ why is this street flooded and I am stuck in the mud to my headlights??”  Saying the gameplay is simple is an understatement and not what Snowrunner aims for. While on the base, the gameplay is transport goods from A to B however you want, there is much much more to it. You Start out with a single truck, and earn money through your first easier jobs, but very soon you will get in contact with one of the main aspects and one of the big selling points of the game. The Physics Engine. I think it is fair to say, that still, Snowrunner has one of the best Physics simulations on the marked. The game simulates the inertia of the each of the many vehicles you can obtain individually, and how they affect the mud, dirt, snow and ice you displace (or get stuck in) when you drive through it and saves the state of it. Which is impressive on its own in my opinion. And this is where the great appeal of the game lies. Each transport is a challenge on its own. Which route to take, do you have enough fuel? Can your current vehicle conquer the terrain with the added weight of the goods you want to transport, or can you take this route with a long trailer behind you? Maybe go for the longer route or risk the shortcut and potentially become stuck? But don’t worry, if you get stuck, you can either try to rescue your vehicle with another one from your fleet, or let it be transported to the nearest Garage.  Snowrunner also features a detailed damage system and much more.There are countless upgrades all over the world to find for your vehicles to modify/tune them in your garages!  The different objectives also offer a good variety of challenges and hey, maybe you can find a new vehicle stuck in some swamp at the corner of a map? And must figure out how you can rescue it? It’s for you to discover.  -Great Physic Simulation-Huge Map-Lots of Vehicles, upgrades-Many different goals and challenges-Detailed damage simulation    I play these kinds of game very rarely, but Snowrunner really captured me. Playing around with the different vehicles and upgrades and dragging yourself through deep mud and snow combined with the amazing physics simulation is just way too much fun. If you are into Simulation/Transport games, Snowrunner is a must play.  And if you rarely or never play these games, but think “hey this could be fun” its absolutely worth to give this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it for everyone, only a niche audience. Don't get me wrong SnowRunner has a few things it does very well. It's easily the best off-roading sim I've seen. The environmental physics are great, mud, water, ice etc. The graphics are great and the models are well detailed. What bothers me is the fact that after a while of playing you'll just get bored. There's not another soul in this game, no npc's, not even an image of one when you take on a mission. Just bland text, and not even much of it. You'll spend HOURS hauling cargo across the map only to get a one sentence thank you and a few bucks.I think one of the biggest let-downs for me is that this game is SOLELY about the driving and NOTHING else. You make virtually no impact on the map, I was hoping that there would be more missions to clear rubble from the road, pave muddy areas, and transform the map as you complete objectives. Sure there's a bridge here or there you can repair but that's it. There's an entire class of Highway trucks and Highway tires and Highway customization you can do.......useless. There is no road in this game that is just pavement, and you'll never change that. So it negates the whole point of those. No story, no people to help out, no real hook that actually gives you a rewarding experience for all the work you do. Sure you unlock a new truck, maybe a new upgrade. After a while they just start blending together. After about 100 hours it's just mind numbing and dull. There is SO MUCH potential here for a game like this to be so much more. It needs more purpose and reward. This game really nails the off-road part, but it's the only trick this pony has to offer. It wears off.

_childDocuments_.review: Hauling cargo over long distances, on almost impossible to conquer terrain. Dragging your wheels in neck deep mud, snow or water. Cursing life itself whenever your truck flips to its side just a few meters away from the destination because you drove over a pebble. Any of these sentences got your blood pumping? Oh boy, this is the game for you!SnowRunner is packed with content. It's not for everyone, sure, but even if you aren't into driving/racing games you should have a try. It is something different. The game runs well even on a toaster, sounds nice and most trucks/cars handles relatively well. If you have some sucke- I mean buddies willing to play with you, the gameplay is even better, there is genuine incentive to help each other out. Winching your buddies out of a pinch, transporting multiple sets of cargos over long distances as a unit will speed up game progression drastically. Even in coop you can sink tens to hundreds of hours into just the base game. Also there are three years worth of additional content, granted some of the seasons are a lot better than others. Oh and did I mention it has modding support?My advice is to try this somewhere (or if you have played mudrunner before, imagine that game on steroids), then if you like it, grab the base game itself. You can grab the year passes later on, when you have most of the stuff unlocked in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this game fills a niche of needing just enough attention to not get bored, but also enough to be really fun and interesting. Its a very specific sweet spot that allows me to have fun with a game and also watch videos on another monitor. Don't get me wrong, its still fun to play this game by itself. Pros:-Very addictive gameplay loop-Loads of content in the base game alone, and DLC adds a ton more-Excellent graphics and soundtrack-Great terrain simulation-Variety of trucks, upgrades, and customization. All well detailed-Tons of mods to add more contentCons:-Vehicle drivetrain simulation is lacking (transmissions never shift down; low gears sometimes feel like they don't give you much torque multiplication; weird H (high) gear that feels like a crutch to get around the downshifting issue, but can also sometimes send your truck rocketing forward depending on the setup)-Asphalt grip is actually non-existent at "high" (35+ mph) speed, even with highway tires. -Hard mode has some unnecessary handicaps. Not being able to sell trailers and fuel costing WAY too much. Recommend making your own hard mode with new game+. -A few tasks/contracts can be really tedious because they require you to drive the exact same route multiple times in a row. Not many of these, though. -Mods seem to be restricted to adding content and making edits to existing content. No way to change core gameplay features (ex. can't allow trucks to use diff lock when not in low, cannot have more than one winch, etc.) A few modders have done some great work making new mechanics within the existing framework, but there's only so much they can do. These cons aren't dealbreakers IMO, just stuff to be aware of beforehand.

Wrong, you are an honest trucker and you will earn them through honest work. The ghosts grant you "xp" and you gain levels, which grants you access to additional much more powerful trucks. Then, you can use the Ghost Bucks™ you earned through the ghost quests to buy them.It's a great journey across terrible roads doing stuff for needy ghosts. It's very relaxing until your truck falls over and all your logs spill out.

_childDocuments_.review: SnowRunner is like Death Stranding trucker edition, except instead of the developers putting BTs in your path once you find a promising route, they put a tree across the road or a broken bridge.  Okay maybe it's not like Death Stranding other than the fact it's a beautiful looking game about delivering things in disaster struck areas.  The base game has three maps each with 4 large, connected areas in Michigan, Alaska, and Russia.  The Year One pass adds an additional four maps, each with multiple areas and is completely out.  The Year Two pass just released it's second map.  There are also additional trucks available to owners of the DLC passes.  I would suggest getting the Premium Edition with the Year One pass as it's a decent price, especially on sale, and decide after playing if you want the Year Two pass.  I played for a week and decided to get the Year Two pass.The game starts off slow.  You don't have many truck options, and you are limited on upgrades for what you have until you rank up enough to be able to buy them.  While the progress is slow, it's steady until you get up to around rank 12 or 13 when you can buy mud tires for your larger vehicles.  Until then, you will hate the game if you try to take on every task without proper planning because above all else, SnowRunner is about planning.  You need to know the limitations of your vehicles, you need to know what routes you can take with your vehicles, and you always need to have a backup plan.  Sometimes proper planning means strategic placement of extra vehicles, fuel trailers, or repair trailers.  Some of the most enjoyable moments are pulling your truck out of the mud or righting it after flipping it.The game also has a good modder community.  Some recreate real world vehicles, some add more options to vehicles in game, some create vehicles that just flat up break the game, and some make beautiful maps that can extend your game play indefinitely, although with the Year One and Two passes I have >200 hours and plenty of content left.  I would highly suggest not using the modded vehicles that break the game early on as it will ruin the experience.  I just installed some mods for the first time prior to writing this review to see what was out there prior to writing a review.  They were entertaining, but I've turned them back off for now as delivering a fully loaded convoy over a treacherous, snow covered mountain pass is strangely rewarding.Multiplayer is also a a lot of fun, whether is just helping explore a map to find upgrades, jumping in to rescue a friend, or making a large convoy to deliver cargo for missions.  I haven't spent too much time in multiplayer (<12 hours), but I've not had any connection issues.  There are some bugs, such as losing fuel when trying to partially refuel a vehicle, but it seems like refueling works if you press and hold the refuel button to fully refuel a vehicle.  Winching and cranes also seem to not work properly with someone in the vehicle you are trying to connect to.  The cranes don't do anything, and getting too far away will cause a winch to snap, so you just need to have someone swap to a different vehicle temporarily.  Other than those issues, it has been fun planning with friends.  As the person with the best trucks and most skill out of my friends, I generally hop into a truck with a crane to provide support, so they get the main experience, and I just help them out of a bind.  We've had many humorous moments on rescue missions and playing bumper cars.  Playing in someone else's game also gives you money when completing tasks, so you can also play truck rental service by pulling out some good vehicles to let other players use them while you lounge around and collect money from their work.You will get frustrated; you will curse the game, but if you stick with it you will learn to love it and appreciate the beautiful worlds created by both the developers and the modding community.

name: The Sundew
detailed_description: Shibukawa, capital of Japan, 2054. Water drips from the cracked ceiling onto the edge of your bed as the incessant rain masks the whine of a refrigerator and the neon hum of the city outside. You don’t recognise the heavy breath in your ear nor the warmth of the body lying next to you... The world’s gone to hell, and it’s taking you down with it. Welcome to Shibukawa. You are Anna Isobe, a cybernetically enhanced cop in a world that’s left you behind. Once a shining hope for the future, cyborgs have become taboo, replaced by drones and automata that make even your heightened abilities obsolete. Stuck in a thankless job surrounded by indifferent eyes you still have a duty to protect and serve, and that’s just what you’re going to do. The Sundew is a dark adventure game set in the aftermath of a devastating future war, where the world as we know it was twisted by flames into a terrifying new dystopia. What begins as a normal day quickly becomes something else, and soon a lonely beat cop will hold the fate of the world in her hands. The Sundew pays homage to classic adventure games of old while reflecting contemporary issues and gameplay. Beautifully drawn pixel-art and stunning sound design brings this dark future to life and grounds you in a vision of humanity’s progress that is both alien and strangely familiar... Japan lies in ruins, save for the bustling haven of Shibukawa. Guide Anna through this new megalopolis and beyond in her search for the mystery behind a growing conspiracy. Travel from the backstreets of the city to far-flung isles, and the most notorious prison this side of the Steppe. Alongside classic point-and-click gameplay The Sundew will ask you to make decisions that will change the future of humanity. Playing off contemporary issues, the choices offered are never black and white. Where do you believe mankind’s interests lie, and what means are acceptable to achieve them? Features Guide Anna Isobe, a cyborg cop with a dark past, through the unravelling of a global conspiracy. Experience a diverse cast of characters, each with their own secrets and history. Explore Shibukawa and the remnants of the old world. Make decisions that will change the fate of humanity, for better or worse. REVIEW 'The Sundew is an unrivalled modernisation of the point-and-click genre. It’s stunning, engaging – and best of all, feels like it might just usher in a subgenre renaissance.' That Film Blog •

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this, but I just can't despite getting all(?) three endings.The main reason I can't is because the story just... is... uhm... hang on, It feels like the story is trying to go three different directions, then picks direction four as it's path. I still couldn't say why the main character goes along with the second half of the game, There's also quite a few bugs:- Some scenes are triggerable multiple times.- One scene won't start unless you have a specific item but the game will force you to the scene trigger and won't tell you why it's not working. At the same time you can't leave the building you're in... unless you use the map and teleport away (though you can't progress the story that way and have to go back to the building to do so).- In a different area you need to hit a specific hotspot to have a scene play out, otherwise you'll be told you don't have the correct item... despite there being literally one item in the area, and it working after the scene has played out.- Not sure this is a bug or intended, but there's an effect that changes the aspect ratio when you move up and down certain screens... and it's super jarring.And finally there's a way to crash the game 100% of the time right at the end, which I found out by accident. Thankfully the game autosaves often so it was only a few minutes to get back to the same spot.I realize it sounds like I disliked everything, but the game wasn't a complete disaster. It starts out fantastic, loved the opening scene. It has an okay help system. Graphically it hits my sweet spot. Sound and music are great. It just needed someone to look over the story and a bunch of bug fixes to be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I really love cyberpunk stories. As such, i was hooked right away by the game's premise and setting.The atmosphere is really unique and backdrops are gorgeous. The art is top notch and helps immerse you in the game.Some puzzles were a bit tricky but overall they are fairly logical and do not require pixel hunting (thank god ! I still have nightmares about some old Lucasarts or Sierra titles because of that).The story begins as a simple "get to work" mission but end up much more interesting after a bit.I haven't finished it yet but i'm eager to find out what happens at the end.Overall: A really good point'n'click adventure game. I'd give it a 9/10. To me, it's on par with Wadjet Eye's games and some others and definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: is a nice-looking point & click adventure set in japan in 2054, with the expected amount of neon-fueled depression and a cyborg cop called anna as protagonist. you are forced to work on a sunday after a cyber attack on the police station and while getting prepped for your next job, something weird happens, followed by more weirdness. hard to talk about the story without spoilers, so I won't, I'll just say I didn't find it particularly interesting and the writing is iffy as well.controls are mostly fine, largely mouse-based in the usual left click to do stuff and skip dialog, double-click to run, right click to look at stuff fashion. there's some keyboard functionality as well, the inventory is on the top of the screen, there's a map for fast travel, you keep notes about current goings-on and things to do, and the intercom can be used to call people. , as it should, and there are .the game says f1-f5 are for help/hints, but I figured it'd be more like a built-in walkthrough or hints on what to do, maybe more and more helpful or something. 5 keys for it seemed like overkill (and it is), but only tried them after finishing the game. turns out, they are for items to pick up, stuff to interact with, characters to talk to, exits and even collectibles. would've saved me from a lot of unnecessary and annoying pixel-hunting, though I'd still prefer a single button for all of them. since collectibles are optional and purposefully hidden, not showing them wouldn't even be an issue (don't care about them anyway, though the fixing of signs and stuff is a pretty neat idea implemented well and there aren't many of them).good pixel art and audio, separate volume settings, a few languages and an autosave toggle for  with a not exactly discreet pop-up saying so. wouldn't mind if it was just an icon or 'saving...', but  over 11 slots as well. you can name them and they show the date and time by default.it's okay overall, nothing especially memorable, though obviously a great effort from a small team, and some might even be wowed or moderately impressed by the story (kinda hard with so many forgettable characters). it  and there are a couple of choices, one meaningless, the other influences the 3 endings somewhat. since it didn't manage to hook me completely, I'd say  for your next cyberpunk fix. and don't panic if you don't see the load option after finishing the game, saves aren't gone, it's just a bug and restarting will let you load them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I like cyberpunk settings. And I like point&click adventures. So I should really have enjoyed this game very much, but... nope. The game feels partially unfinished and partially just broken.For starters, there are plenty of in-world objects that are labelled when you move the mouse over them but you cannot even "look" at them. They serve no purpose at all. I mean, not everything is required to have a purpose, but why hint at something that your character will not even comment on it?Then there's this bug. Yes, just one. But it is such a huge glaring one that I have no idea how anyone could have missed it. In many areas your character's size is just way off. About twice as big as she is supposed to be, maybe more.Next up, invisible walls. Eg. the "story" tells you to go place B, but the game will not let you. Without any in-world explanation it keeps you in place A until you are "done" there before it lets you progress, even though you are told that you urgently need to go on. Or when you interact with a certain object, you cannot pick it up, until the game decides that the time is right (again, no in-world explanation why she should pick the item up then and not earlier).The characters just are not relatable. Most NPCs only make an appearance in one place and do not matter in later stages of the game anyway. They are just there to push the "plot" forward, but have very little personality. Sadly, the lack of personality also applies to the player's character to quite an unpleasant extent.And then there's the *sigh* plot... holes. I do not mind when a plot has some blanks for the audience to fill in, or puzzle pieces to be put together. But not like this. Putting plot fragments and tropes in a blender and throwing the result into someone's face is not how you tell a story. This game was developed for the most part by just one person and that deserves some respect despite all its flaws. I hope that her next game (if there ever is one) will do away with the mistakes that were made here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this moody cyberpunk point-and-click. The pixel graphics are nice, the music and ambience is atmospheric, and there are some cool and intriguing ideas in there. Sadly, the writing is quite hopeless, with overworked, heavy-handed dialog, a hard to follow plot with paper thin characters and some weird tone shifts that doesn't really work within the otherwise serious story. I get the feeling that the creators wanted to "make a cyberpunk game" more than they had an axtual story to tell. (Something that becomes even more obvious when you compare TS to other (and better) "cyberpunky" point-and-clicks, such as Technobabylon or Gemini Rue.) Puzzle-wise the game is ok. There are some obtuse old-school adventure game stumpers that can be quite easy to lose track of, but luckily the game has a good built-in list of objectives that is really helpful. Overall I would say that The Sundew is decent but flawed. Not something I would recommend outside of the hardcore adventure game/point and click completionists or cyberpunk fans who has played everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thrilled to finally be able to play The Sundew, an impressive effort from solo French developer Agnès Vuillaume.  I've been rooting for this project for several years.  I know the project has faced some heartbreaking setbacks and some high hurdles in its path, so it's wonderful to see that the developer was able to so gracefully overcome those obstacles and release such an enjoyable, polished game.In The Sundew, we follow Anna, elite cybercop, who undertakes an unusual mission.  After an escalating series of twists and turns, Anna experiences a major revelation that has seismic implications for her personal life.  She has no time to process this before she is framed for a crime and shipped to prison.  However, she escapes, and now must investigate the conspiracy from the fringes of society where she now lives.  The game is set in a neo-Japan, takes us from an urban Tokyo-like city to the snowy ruins of Hokkaido, and features a top-notch aesthetic that had me oohing and aahing every other screen.I've had a major soft spot for the cyberpunk genre ever since 2015's Technobabylon, which is the game that really introduced me to the adventure genre, and since then, I've practically played them all, from ENCODYA and Neofeud to Blade Runner and VirtuaVerse.  The Sundew is classic cyberpunk; it's telling a familiar story, but the story is told well, hitting all of the right beats from start to end.  Gameplay and art-wise, The Sundew feels most similar to the Tex Murphy games, and fans of that series will feel very at home here.Even though The Sundew has these classic cyberpunk elements, it brings plenty of new things to the table.  The game's title and plot are both references to Drosera flytrap plants, which make a number of appropriately symbolic appearances throughout the game, adding a refreshingly botanical flair to the futuristic hellscape.  The art is well-thought out, at times literary in its execution.While not difficult, this game does not hold your hand, either.  It does feature modern conveniences such as autosave and a well-implemented objectives checklist that can keep you on track if you get lost.  Paying attention to dialogues is important, as well as fully exploring scenes.  It's not nearly as pixel-hunty as "the classics", and the art is incredibly clear and readable despite the resolution, but there is a small amount of hunting around for things (including a fun optional objective to find hidden space invader sprites in most scenes).Even though it just came out, The Sundew is already something of a cult classic in some forums I frequent.  I am not finished the game as of this writing, and plan to revisit this review later, but I want to congratulate the developer on this wonderful game, and encourage anyone who visits this store page to please buy it.  This is art worth supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Indie cyberpunk point’n’click. Pleasant, if stereotypical experience for those who want a dose of the trendy genre in their life.Anna is a cyborg cop with a disdain for the rules and a somewhat self-destructing side. Woken up on Sunday morning after a night of fun by her boss, she’s being sent on a mission to shoot a mysterious target. During pre-mission physical check something goes awry in the police station; not knowing what is exactly going on, Anna decides to proceed with a mission first and deal with the rest later. “The rest” will include an array of topics typical for this set-up such as “man vs machine”, ”man vs AI”, “man vs the system” and some strange botany – essentially, everything that is expected from an adventure in CP style.The game starts in substantially “cyberpunked” Japanese city (Tokyo has been destroyed by an unknown force) and involves solving a mystery that sits appropriately within the lines of this genre narrative without stepping outside of usual.  While story is decently pieced together, it does suffer from sudden info dumps that seem to come out of nowhere to add a layer of complexity, however, due to rather abrupt way they are introduced, they only bring the feeling of being forced on the player in hopes to give a brisk backstory and some conclusions. It would have been much more satisfying to learn bits and pieces throughout the entire game and let it slow burn into a player’s heart instead of suddenly informing about the reason to go through everything in the first place, all the while leaving some story threads purposeless in a head-scratching way.  Anna is trope-y yet likable enough to continue explore the mystery; and the writing, just like everything else, is floating at “middle-of-the-road”, average mark (few translation issues included). Nothing to write home about (ha!) but fitting well with the rest of the elements to make progression effortless and pleasant enough to follow it through the end.Puzzle element in “Sundew” is of a classic point’n’click variety (mostly of an inventory manipulation sub-category) and is an easy-breezy business even for those who doesn’t play adventures all that often. Some of the solutions will raise an eyebrow (still easy but just… bit silly), and one particular moment will be a pain in the neck simply due to unintuitive placement of an item; but overall,  it’s a brisk “go, go, go” pace that won’t really stump the player. There will be a few decisions that will ultimately lead to different outcomes (the rest of the dialogue choices won’t affect much at all), so saving manually is a great idea despite autosave doing its job if there’s a desire to see all endings – drastically different in theory, but a bit anticlimactic in execution. And there are collectibles throughout the game for those who are into it, plus achievements to hunt down  - a fairly standard set with a “light” tag hanging on it.The visuals are, just to follow the overall pattern, exactly what cyberpunk PNCs tend to look like in their textbook variety. A retro, dark, noir-ish pixelated look. It’s done well here and even has a few imaginative takes on modes of transportation which were kinda cool. Of course, mandatory city skyline with neon lights and dark alleys are included in the setting. Can’t really be cyberpunk if those aren’t present, so nothing to worry about here – stylishly blurry bodies of NPCs will be animated in all the appropriate backdrops.There isn’t a voice-over here (apart hilarious glitch where Anna starts speaking French for a few seconds), but it works. As always – on a tight budget it’s usually better without one than with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ one. Music is very sporadic, and whenever it is present it’s a rather “unmemorable but nice” sort of techno deal. The game is mostly built on sound effects, and they do a good job of relaying the atmosphere of the situation with occasional over-the-top moments. Essentially, yet another component that is good enough to make an enjoyable but a tad run-of-the-mill experience.“Sundew” won’t be blowing anyone's socks off, as the game is as “standard cyberpunk point’n’click” as it gets, with all the tropes it ensues. It has a rather rushed, but interesting enough plot and easy puzzle element that will prompt a player to continue through this just under 5-hour mark adventure. The game will work best for those who likes anything with a cyberpunk tag – you will get the classic, safe set of your favorite things, or those who, for some unexplained reason, are running out of things to play and have a point’n’click itch they need to scratch – this rather new, a bit stereotypical but still entertaining adventure can help out with that. Now… to battle, or not to battle the AI, that is the question.

_childDocuments_.review: Full review: On one hand, you have a spirited, ambitious attempt to create the next sweeping epic the likes people can latch onto and discuss for years to come. On the other, you have a relatively short game that does not afford the story time to develop to get to that emotional boiling point. While a pretty solid Point & Click adventure with intuitive puzzles and a neat I Spy side-hunt, The Sundew will always be marred by its own insistence with telling a five-hour story in two hours. I appreciate the attempt; it just didn't land as intended.+ Puzzles are consistently logical and only occasionally odd+ Completely effective in showcasing a retro Point & Click+ Finding Space Invaders aliens is fun- Story is too large in scope for the short runtime- Characters are generally underwhelming- A few puzzles have very unclear instructions
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Of the few cyberpunk themed games that I've played, I ended up liking this one best.  The atmosphere is a bit more interesting and unique than some others.  The setting is a futuristic version of Japan, with traditional and advanced elements combined in an interesting way.  The main character is edgy as you'd expect, but not outright obnoxious.  The puzzles are pretty standard for a point and click game but that's not really why you play this type of game after all.  The dialogues are not too long and the game doesn't overstay its welcome, taking only a few hours to finish.  There is just enough character development but not so much that you want to skip it.  It feels like a chapter in a series, and I would enjoy seeing more games set in this world with these characters.  Also there's a character who seems to have vitiligo which is a condition I've not seen included in a game character before.The first part of the game takes place in a crowded, humid city.  The second part is in a cold, desolate abandoned town.  Its a nice contrast, and not overdone.  The 'choice' in the middle of the game only changes a few dialogues.  The ending sequence is in a different kind of environment which I won't spoil.  There are three endings with a short sequence each, and its easy to save near the end to see all three.There are hidden objects to find, about one per screen, as well as a few places in the game where you can clean up graffiti to collect an achievement.I could complain about things that I haven't liked in other cyberpunk games that I've played or watched videos of, but it's all down to personal taste with a genre that is so steeped in atmosphere.  I just happened to really like this one and found it had the right tone and world-building for my tastes.  YMMV of course.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this point and click adventure game very much.  The story was interesting and very well done.  I enjoyed how the writers gradually and naturally gave you information about your character and the game world as you played instead of a data dump of sorts at the beginning or everything at the end.  I thought the challenge level was just right.  Moving on in the game was logical, fair, and fit with the story, but wasn’t too easy that I got bored.  There are optional collectibles that were creative and fun to collect with their captions in the scenes.  No voiceovers,, but that didn’t bother me at all.  Manual saves which are always nice.It took me 6 hours to play and I had a lot of fun with this game.  I recommend to point and click adventure fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I'm hitting thumbs up for the great artwork and for the things the game attempts -- it has a bunch of issues though:   Weird and picky puzzle triggers  (eg, leave a location and come back), some very barebones characters and writing throughout (but then other stuff is weirdly detailed), and some translation issues...   These all gave it some artificial difficulty and gives the whole game a surreal haze.   I did think the strange choices on where to put details, unexplained events, and the quirky puzzles gave the game a lot of personality though.  It reminded me of the early 90s French adventure games, and helped form some weird mental bond with the dev -- so even if it was somewhat bewildering, I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful and amazing point'n'click ! Everything is there : cyberpunk city, easter eggs, a strong heroine, the fight for the truth, sassy jokes & references... Above all, clever puzzles which don't require silly logic on the contrary of lots of games of the genre.  The game has definitely potential . It is about 4 hours (looked only twice to the walkthrough), the story could have been way more developed without being dull.For reference, I'm a sucker for cyberpunk atmosphere and pixelised point'n'click (Wadget Eye is da best). The Sundew has clearly the top level quality needed to be a instant classic :) Most of all, I am pleased to see such a good game coming from a fellow citizen from the North of France!I would be delighted to support any future game from the dev. She is a beast : doing almost everything all alone is definitely amazing. Arigato for this awesome game!Agnès, vous jouez clairement dans la cour des grands. C'est un plaisir de voir que vous faites honneur à la scène vidéolique francaise. Découvrir votre univers a été une joie et je n'en demande que plus :D
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I really hope the devs are still working on improving the puzzles and adding a little more polish to The Sundew because it's loaded with potential. If you get stuck I recommend using the guide; some puzzles are a little convoluted but the story and art's worth your time.The Sundew is a decent modern point and click; it has the potential to be amazing but needs a little more TLC. The pixels are stunning, story's intriguing, writing's decent but puzzles need some work.For more niche curation, follow me at:
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: The Sundew nails all the important parts of a good classic point&click adventure game.An engaging story, interesting characters, nice artwork, a workable game interface that doesn't get in the way, a great soundtrack and a game world with a lot of potential.That being said, the game does have some weak moments. It's relatively short (maybe ~4-6 hours to get most endings?), and there are a some areas that require pixel hunting. I also remember needing to find one particular item that is crucial for progress, but without any logical connection to the circumstances. I suppose this wouldn't bother players who mindlessly pick up all items they can carry anyway, but I prefer to have an actual reason to do so. Especially if certain items are somewhat hard to miss.I'd recommend this with a 3/5 or maybe a 4/5 if you have a particular craving for cyberpunk point&click games.Definitely a developer to watch - I'll be looking forward to a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: A very good point & click adventure game.With a very interesting story, atmospheric art and a few choices along the way as well.The only real downsides are:- It's fairly short (makes sense for a mostly-solo project, of course)- A few bugs (mostly graphical glitches, none major)- Some puzzles require you to leave a screen and come back without any indication that you actually did something, pretty awkward.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid game. A warm comeback to the era of point'n'click adventures. You control a female cyborg in a cyberpunk world and have to unveil the conspiracy . Usually you have quite a few tasks at hand, but thankfully there's always a to-do list to keep you in the loop even after breaks.I particularly enjoyed the system of collectables. I missed a few, but I liked the little endorsements in every one of those.To the fans of the genre and those who like a good short indie game, this is definitely worth playing.Now, to the negative reviewers... This game is made by a solo developer. She had the guts, the expertise, the inspiration and the will power to create an entire game single-handedly. And then she gets judged by the same standards big corpos do? This is exactly why we can't have nice things.Please understand that a review is a very powerful tool. You shouldn't give a thumbs down just because a game "could be better". Yeah, there are some bugs and inconsistencies here and there, yes, the game does feel rushed in the second half, but... Sometimes you should vote for the potential. Just a few too strict thumb downs can make a difference between a promising start with possible sequels improving on every aspect of the original, and the game dev career cut short. I do hope this is still the former case, and we'll get to see more of Agnes' work.Thank you for pulling this off, Agnes. Looking forward to your next game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: It does feel incomplete, rushed perhaps, as though segments were missing. But it's definitely recommendable. The fundamentals are all there and you can sense the backstory & worldbuilding are well-realised even if the finished product doesn't really do them justice. The design is excellent, with interesting & inventive scenes, and a characterful handcrafted quality. Puzzles were tricksy in that way less modern point & clicks can be, and I really enjoyed that. In itself it's a fairly good game; moreover it oozes promise and I'd be excited to try something from this developer in future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game and story. No pixel hunting or "try every combination" type of puzzles. It eliminate most of the frustration from traditional point-and-click and enable you to fully enjoy the story line. I think one of the key element of this game his its overall atmosphere, supported by its graphic design and sound track.The sound track, in particular, is quite immersive. I would strongly recommend to play it with your best sound system. I did play part of the game with an over-hear gaming headset and part with a regular so-so one, and that make a huge difference. Sometimes, you really have the impression it's raining outside. Borrow an headset to one of your friend if needed, I think you would really miss something if you don't have the right audio setup!
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Cool art-style- Cool cyberpunk world, good world building, lots of lore and very imersive.- Interesting locations and characters. Lots of points of interaction.- Mostly playable with just the mouse.- Interesting mechanic with the EYEphone.- Story was okay, it kept me interested. Arguably the ending felt a bit rushed.- Auto-save (which can be turned of if that's your preference.) Manual saves are also supported regardless with a generous number of slots.- Mostly solid point and click puzzle design and the character occasionally gives some useful prompts. There was a few odd choices for item combinations etc but overall I felt the game ticked along quite well without getting majorly stuck.- There does seem to be some choice built into the game but I'm not to sure if it has any real effect.Cons- Frame-limited and screen tearing. No proper v-sync implementation.- Weird hot-spot reveal implementation that uses keys F1-F4 to separately show different kinds of hot-spots e.g. items you can pick up or characters you can speak to. Not sure why it was done this way. Something like a hold left click to show all hot-spots at once would have been preferable. Also the hot-spot remains for items that have been removed from the scene.- Quite short.- Some hot-spots are just the tool tip with the item description i.e. they have no dialog or function what so ever. Felt a bit strange to me.- No voice acting.Overall its a decent cyberpunk point and click. Interestingly the opening sequence of the game is identical to another cyberpunk point and click "Born Punk" not sure who took inspiration from who or was it just coincidence.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I had been looking forward to playing it for quite some time since I saw the trailer a few months ago. It has a great look and feel to everything, and it was a really cool world to explore. The puzzles in general were solid, though I will say some were quite annoying and required some overly specific solutions which made them at times frustrating, but which adventure game don't have their share of have those? The hint system was perfectly done though. The few times I needed it, it didn't over share information, so was ideally balanced. I will say that I feel like I only scratched the surface with this game though. Such an interesting character, job, city and story. I definitely wanted more, so I really hope that we can get a Sundew part 2, or just another adventure with Anna Isobe that is longer and with more depth, because I think there is so much more to explore here. She's a really fascinating protagonist and what's not to love about being in a cyberpunk future Japan?Amazing that the majority of this game was made by a one person team. An incredible effort that I really enjoyed my time with. Definitely reccommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand other negative feedbacks, but I love this game very much. A little game jewel that deserves to be more known to more gamers, especially retro adventure game lovers! The graphic is very beautiful! The game is very unique and creatively made! I would love to see more games of the same developer Agnes! There were some pixel that had wrong color or missing in the graphic, but there were very few of them, because the game wholly is awesome. I just made it to one of three (or four) possible endings, and I wish the game had more content so I could play longer! This must be bought and played!!! 10 of 10 stars!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly mediocre, but fine enough to get on sale for point & cick enthusiasts. Story feels like it's been told a few times too many already and it has a few problems with the game only progressing after performing specific actions with no indication for what those are or why you're stuck. It's also short, which is fair for the price, but still, it's over before you could really get into it, while also letting you spend the larger middle portion of the game on plotwise unimportant stuff. Puzzles are either banal or completely obtuse with nothing in between, but still decent enough. I could see this developer progressing to make far better games, but it's not a bad start.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: It saddens me to give this game a negative review. It held promise... and that's precisely what makes it disappointing.At first, the game is really quite decent. The setting's nice, the atmosphere's good, the art's not bad, the main character's fairly cool and the plot seems reasonably interesting.Then a twist happens... and after that, the pace of the story quickens too much and the game becomes less and less enjoyable. The things we discover and the answers we get are all deeply unsatisfying. The ending is incredibly rushed and disappointing.It barely took me more than four hours to reach the end. The game would need to be at least twice as long in order for its story to reach its full potential.The puzzles are not the worst I've ever seen, but most of them are not especially memorable either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Meh, it’s okay. Biggest pro is the setting and art style. The longest chapter in the game is set in a very cool, snowy, dilapidated urban landscape. Wish we would have seen more of that.Problem is that the longest chapter in the game is also pretty useless in terms of storytelling. The whole plot gets resolved basically entirely during a massive lore-dump carried through a poorly written conversation at the end of the game.Puzzles are mostly fine, not sure what people are referring to when they complain about moon logic. Just put the damn scrambler on the stupid little table, and everything else is a breeze :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful pixel art game, beautiful to look at, scene after scene, and quite challenging to play. It contains a lot of  original ideas, bringing a surprise at almost every "click"! You get involved in the story and can't wait trying to progress, risking to loose all the funny side "bonuses" and the irony of many dialogues. Luckily you can save and go back, so you can enjoy it multiple times! Thanks for this superb creation, and congratulations!
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: The Sundew is a great little sci-fi point and click adventure that appears to have fallen under the radar somewhat. The pixel graphics are moody and atmospheric. The music is a blend of neat chip tunes and classic arpeggiated synth stuff. The puzzles are at a comfortable level of difficulty, and the dialog gets the job done. Unfortunately it's hard to feel a connection with the characters because the protagonist is a bit mean and the plot moves forward at a pace that doesn't allow us to get to know anyone else.If you've played any other cyberpunk adventures, the overall story here is not bringing anything new to the table, but that's fine. It's got megacorps, cyberspace, rain, noodles, neon, all that jazz. Aside from the wink-wink nudge-nudge references to present day western pop culture, this one feels pointedly set in Japan, which is something that makes it stand out from the more nondescript pan-Asian sprawl settings we sometimes get. I feel like if the story and characters had been given a bit more breathing room this could've been even better, but as it is it's still a decent few hours of story that anyone who dug Beneath a Steel Sky, Gemini Rue etc should enjoy playing through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, old school point-and-click - just like how they used to make 'em! Pixelated goodness and nice, big blocky text - just like we're used to of recent for this fayre. It's not cyberpunk per se - more post-apocalyptic in nature to be honest, but still a little tech noir flavour going on. If you like games like Technobabylon, the old Blade Runner point-and-click and Lacuna then this should prove an enjoyable addition to your library. The Sundew has a great story and while the only real character developed is your own, the others are interesting enough in their own right to make for an engaging gaming experience. The main character, Anna, is very fun to play - sardonic, witty and an all round badass with a great mohawk! Puzzles are for the most part doable without using a walkthrough - but if you need one ( I did once or twice) then there's an excellent, concise, spoiler-free one in the Steam forums for the game. For me, the game lasted around 5 - 6 hours so plenty of bang for your buck, especially if you grab it during a sale. A definite recommend from me. I very much enjoyed it and hope the dev continues to make more games of this ilk.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning aesthetic, a throbbing soundtrack, and a neon soaked future Japan to puzzle around in.The puzzles are intuitive and the game is very friendly with solves.The writing is fairly solid and the protagonist has personality.Definitely worth checking out for fans of cyberpunk stories and/or point and click adventures.Very, very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I love cyberpunk. I love pixel art graphics. I love interactive fiction--specially point and click. Pretty much can't go wrong with this one for me. I find this game an interesting specimen because the retro aspects of the game really hold up. Certainly there's more to cyberpunk than can be contained in a sparkly cinematic, no, cyberpunk is a serenade to the materialistic techno culture with layers of apathy. Yeah, that's all here, and yet it's not too heavy really. I think this is a really intelligent interpretation and I highly recommend to fans of these genres! P.S. I've made a walkthrough video for the first apartment area while I share a few more thoughts on this one. Check out the link in this review.Intro Walkthrough:
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: I get worried every time I open yet another pixel art Point&Click without voice acting because it's impossible to tell when it's a stylistic decision, a budget constraint or lack of effort. This one is a pleasant surprise. There are isolated weak parts where the game locks into expecting a very specific sequence of triggers and fails to telegraph it properly or the chain of events is built more around the puzzle than vice versa, but the rest of the time the game is solid with well designed puzzles and a transparent goal system. The art is heavy on background details without becoming muddy and makes good use of the limited palette. The story is obtuse at times, but in a very traditionally cyberpunk manner where it contributes to the paranoid conspiratorial atmosphere. Overall the single dev is showing a good handle on the genre and I can't wait to see what follows this good first step.
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant enough point-and-click cyberpunk adventure.  You play a hard-bitten cop who has been treated poorly by society, set against a shadowy megacorp whose influence reaches into government.  Your choices affect the ending of the game.This game feels like a solid first attempt at a point-and-click adventure: the elements are all there, and with some more experience I think this game would be very engaging.Spoilers past this pointStrengths: fun puzzles, good worldbuilding, I cared about the main character.Weaknesses: there's some Chekhov's Guns lying around that are never fired e.g. Jimmy hacking the intercom never comes back; Donna's walkie-talkie gun never comes back; the lab-bot says Karin has an ulterior motive which is never explored (...and why was she arrested, again?).  There's a choice of endings that needs slightly more flesh e.g. if you could take control of Isobe after she's made her choice, even if it's just one or two clicks, that would make the experience more immersive.  The shadowy figures remain shadowy...Overall, leaving me wanting more is a good result from a game.  I hope the creator makes more games, and I'll be sure to subscribe to them to see what they create next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Sundew

_childDocuments_.review:
You are Anna Isobe, a cyborg cop abandoned by progress and thrust into the midst of a global conspiracy. Experience classic point and click gameplay as you travel across the dark future. Shibukawa, capital of Japan, 2054. Water drips from the cracked ceiling onto the edge of your bed as the incessant rain masks the whine of a refrigerator and the neon hum of the city outside. You don’t recognise the heavy breath in your ear nor the warmth of the body lying next to you... The world’s gone to hell, and it’s taking you down with it.

Welcome to Shibukawa

name: Last Train Home
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition! Get the full Legionnaires experience with the 'Last Train Home Digital Deluxe Edition' including the major DLC 'Last Train Home - Legion Tales', the digital Artbook and the atmospherical Soundtrack. About the Game Embark on a desperate mission through the depths of a war-torn wasteland. Your goal is to guide Czechoslovak soldiers back home onboard an armored train, but the path ahead is fraught with peril. Caught in the middle of a brutal civil war between Russia's Red and White Armies, your unit must remain in fighting shape, managing what little resources you have and maintaining morale at all costs. Venture through the bleak and unforgiving landscape of Siberia, where the freezing cold and the merciless environment will push you to your very limit. Resources are scarce and your crew is exhausted, but you must keep pushing forward. As you journey through the heart of the conflict, the horrors of war will surround you. The fate of your legion rests on the actions of a few key soldiers, as you engage in real-time battles that will determine the outcome of your mission. You must choose your tactics wisely, using every skill at your disposal to safeguard your troops and complete your mission. With careful training and development, your squads will become a seasoned legion of comrades, brothers and sisters, ready to face any challenge that comes their way. The decisions you make along the journey will determine the fate of your comrades. Inspired by historical events, of the Czechoslovak Legion and their determination to return to their newly formed republic following The Great War, this mission will test your courage and your will to survive. The Last Train Home is in your hands. PICK YOUR BATTLES: Deploy your squad and complete diverse objectives in a series of real-time missions where specialist combat skills, planning, and superior tactics will lead you to victory. EQUIP YOUR SOLDIERS: Level up your men by unlocking new skills and gathering better equipment – discover their stories, assign medals, and help them rise up through the ranks. MANAGE YOUR CREW: Direct your soldiers in their non-combat roles onboard the train. Craft items, heal your wounded, and restore morale for the arduous journey home. UPGRADE YOUR TRAIN: Unlock your armored train’s full potential by upgrading the carriages and locomotive and oversee important maintenance work to keep it running. JOURNEY THROUGH SIBERIA: Stockpile and trade supplies, make new allies, and overcome crisis after crisis as civil war rages across the vast snowfields of Siberia. BASED ON HISTORICAL EVENTS: Last Train Home, is a compelling narrative that portrays the experiences of the Czechoslovak Legion and their valiant fight on behalf of the Entente powers during World War I.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I'm going to support this game because its made by a smaller studio. They nailed the music, storytelling, and cutscenes. The animations between missions and the live-action filming is impressive. And I enjoyed the overworld gameplay doing missions and managing resources.Now where this game loses points for me.The RTS component is very bad. Its very clunky and frusterating. I've played similar style RTS games like this and it always ends up the same, just a clunky mess. The pathfinding for infantry and vehicles is attrocious. The stealth mechanic isn't that good.This game would have been better off doing an Xcom style turn-based combat gameplay instead of this messy RTS thing they tried to do.It was a very close thumbs up for me. I can easily put a thumbs down for this. The missions seem mostly the same (kill a bunch of Soviets). By the end I had so many resources and I was just blobbing the whole map.Be wary, this game could be not for you. If you look passed the imperfections you might find some fun here.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Unique story- Excellent setting- Gameplay loop is a ton of fun, pretty addicting - Visuals are on the border between passable and good- Resource management feels meaningful - I love the live action cutscenes, even if they are a little cheesyCons:- UI could be better in some places- Some missions are frustratingly long and overstay their welcome, especially if it is on your second or third attempt- No way to tell units to hold fire and move at full speed a the same time, you can only hold fire while taking the movement speed penalty of stealth- AI is dumb enough to be cheesed/kited/baited pretty easily and has less memory than a Skyrim guard8/10

When the enemies ring the alarm bell it doesn't seem to do much other than alert the three guards that were already heading towards it. Every other enemy is just chilling like before. Make me want to play Xcom 2...which I think I'll after writing this. The train management is alright I guess. Honestly just kind of a boring game.

_childDocuments_.review: The epic adventures of the badass Czechoslovak legion in an armored train on the journey through Russia during the civil war, done as a great semi-historically-accurate strategy/management game that's challenging and captivating. Definitely better than expected, I enjoyed the entire playthrough which lasted an impressive 33 hours. If you like top-down strategy war games and games like Frostpunk or This War of Mine, give this one a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely worth your time. There is clearly room for improvement in the combat, character management, and story, but all of these aspects are still highly engaging on their own. Of course, the setting and premise of this game is what ties everything together perfectly and elevates this game to the next level. While this game is not super realistic (who wants realism in an rts anyway?) it is highly immersive and draws you into its world completely.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. Not a GREAT game, but - worth the cost. The novelty alone grabbed my attention. It's a good story, good music, solid art. I only briefly felt any sort of supply pinch, even at max difficulty. The early game is the only game. You won't get to make massive history changing choices, unfortunately. You can't bring the McDuffin family to the port with you. You can't steal any of the gold for your soldiers. You can't bring any villagers with you. You can't betray the rich man, even once you learn he has zero claim to his supposed 'inheritance'. You can't target and destroy aircraft on the runways. You can't pull up track behind you for supply, nor put down track ahead of you to create alternate routes. You can't feed the dogs and/or adopt them. You're insanely limited in how much supply you're allowed to give people, which also has zero effect on the game. Your sniper rifles and pistols have the same range unless your sniper does a special little dance and locks down in place. Sniper rifles alone are sufficient to destroy armored cars and tanks. Your soldiers can't go on their bellies or low crawl. You can't go up or down unless stairs- no ramps or ladders or climbing. CERTAINLY now scrambling over terrain. Incredibly bad path finding, especially for veterans of the great war. There's freak-en 'out of bounds' areas that USUALLY goes right up to the main objective, essentially making every stage a railroad event. Not nearly enough time actually in the train. Train travel constantly interrupted by WAY too many available opportunities for free supply. Soldiers are apparently unable to use their enhanced winter uniforms while inside the train, and gain no benefit from its warmth except when on mission. Sleeping bags are somehow expended, like fuel, despite the team having a few hour mission - ENTIRELY DURING THE DAY.  Flowers and herbs heal your soldiers from gaping chest wounds in about 6 hours. You're not allowed to post security or establish a perimeter when your train is stopped. Just... a lot. There were a lot of choices made, which I vehemently dislike. Frankly, it was a slog and a chore by the end. But! I'm glad I finished it and would recommend it, just roll with the frustration and have a good time! Ultimately? Pretty easy game. Wasn't at challenging in the ways I was hoping to be challenged. Not even a little bit.Would recommend! Not everyone is a military historian VFW with additional logistics background; *I* am not the target audience. Was pretty fun. I know I'll do a 'fast as possible' run and a 'big money' run eventually, but not for a year or 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Legionaries!!!I still much enjoy this great game and for the price this is just incredible.I am 3/4 of the main campaign and still got much to discovers, if you played carefully and well-timed your actions, this game is just next levels. Almost of what I would have wish of "Company of Heroes 3".So far;It's really nice, kind of multiple mix of game. ;I can feel the control are much similar to ''Alien Dark Descent'' and you also have resources management same as ''IXION'', ''Frostpunk'' or ''AOE''.For folks who did played ''Metros Exodus'' you might feel the same country side immersion which is Great!! Same for the locomotive, which you have the chance to make it more effective and armed thru the game.Really nice GAME who shown multiple new mechanics and follow some based events of the Czech armed forces stuck in the middle of Russia Civil War.Plus the current discount 10/10!!
