_childDocuments_.review: I first tried this as a demo in next-fest. This is why we need demos because that led to me finding my favourite game of 2023! This game is like a combination of Xcom and Command & Conquer with resource gathering and survival added to the mix. The story and aesthetic is beautiful and tragic with a real sense of the hopelessness and struggle of war. It's fun of course but not the usual glorification of combat that you see in games. The sense that you are desperately just trying to keep your soldiers alive and get them home is palpable.It's a complex game with the need to constantly monitor stats and resources, and try to allocate soldiers with the right skills for the right task.Then you have the battle decisions. Do you take the experienced soldiers with their improved skills or the newbies to get them levelled up. You also have to balance which types of soldiers you use. Scouts for visibility and ranged kills, grenadiers for vehicles or large groups, and how many medics will you need?!The difficulty settings, very cleverly, let you make different parts of the game easier or harder. If you like the challenge of the combat but not so into the resource management, you can balance the game that way, or vice versa.Personally I found the defaults offer a good level of challenge, especially in the later game where resources become scarce and the oppressive cold is a constant threat.The voice acting is first class. I love the "immersive" option which is all in Czech and Russian (but with subtitles) as it really IS immersive. On my second play-through I chose English which makes it easier to follow and the voice acting is also fantastic, but it feels less natural.It's clear that a huge amount of love and attention to detail has been put into this game. There are decision points which give some replay-ability, particularly one where you choose to go North or South and you get entirely different missions and points of interest.I'm just about to try the DLC then I'll probably go for my third full play-through! I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Excellent historical setting that is under-rated and under-utilized. The Bolshevik Revolution was gnarly at best and few understand how this even changed the world. Additionally, the overmap for inventory and resource management, even if it is clunky. The armored train is fun to work on, upgrade and maintain. Lots of options, and getting a new rail car feels awesome 'cause it dramatically expands your abilities.Also, the story is pretty decent. Also an RTS, which are rare these days.Cons: Playing. This game is very, very janky. Starting with stealth. Stealth is there, and there is basic stealth mechanics. You go into "silent mode" (stealth), and then creep around, going into bushes and cover to block sight with your soldiers. However, to see enemy vision, and plan your approach, you must mouse over an enemy. Not a bad system, but the controls are super jank and you must pause, then come out of pause, to effectively change targets. In addition, there's a delay between you ordering and your characters acting. Something like a third to a quarter of a second. Enough for your characters to ♥♥♥♥ up the order, especially if someone comes into vision all of a sudden. But what about classes designed to take advantage of this?All the relevant abilities are locked at high tier. For example, the Scout's distract ability is key to any successful stealth attempts and is arguably the single best ability in the game, but it's unlocked at level three. A base scout then, isn't that useful, even if he can remove parts of the fog of war. This is complicated by the system of perma death and tight supplies, which means often stealth is the best way to deal with enemies so you don't lose characters, but, due to needing to level up your characters, and needing to not expose them to unnecessary danger, it means that if you want to play well, the game becomes a complete, TIME CONSUMING SLOG. Not kidding, some of these missions can last an hour. ♥♥♥♥ gets boring real fast.But you can fight! Right? Yes, and it's a terrible idea. You will likely expend more munitions that you can gather if you get into several fights on mission, so you either stealth (see previous problem), or, you avoid the soldiers. Avoidance is not a bad idea, but the (enemies) wander about and there is no way to see their patterns, not even get intel on their routes, so you will often bump into them at random. Not to mention that the enemies are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crack shots and somehow WAY faster than your guys! Like, the Reds can just run down your troops. No sweat. It's stupid how accurate and tough they are. Literally no room for error.Lastly, there are cool items and power ups on the map, like armored cars and tanks. But guess what? They get melted by enemies, because your characters use their guns so slowly, and and the enemies almost never miss! Even regular rifles chip down your metal pretty fast, even on tanks, TANKS, which really defeats the purpose of them. Your almost better ignoring them on most maps.THere's so many other small things that piss me off, but you get the point. The core mechancis are not tight, not responsive, and hard to manage. If your going to get this game, play on easy mode. You'll get a chance to enjoy the game for what it is. As much as I want to love this game, I can't, because it's not a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had my eyes set on this title right after its release. But since I had a few other games to play, LTH went to the Steam wishlist and I waited for the discount. Finally, after finishing most of the games played from the end of last year, I was tempted by the summer discount and bought the straight edition including DLC. And I certainly don't regret it. In short, it is an RTS in the style of Commandos combined with other strategic elements from, for example, the game XCOM. The primary goal is to get a group of legionnaires back to the newly formed Czechoslovak Republic. But there is a catch. Due to developments on the front, there is no going back west, but you will have to cross all the way east across Russia to Vladivostok for the last ferry to take you home. All this accompanied by Captain Langer, played by the Czech actor Karel Dobrý, known for example from the role of Adalbert in the medieval film In the Name of the King. The game is a tribute to the Czechoslovak legionnaires, although the processing is not completely historically accurate.You start on a path not far from Moscow, which we could already try in the demo version of the game. In addition to individual missions, you will also have to take care of your train. Here the authors really won and incorporated all sorts of twists and turns into the game. During the game, you will not only be able to improve your locomotive, for example, or exchange it somewhere in the station depot, but you will also be able to supplement the train with, for example, a medical wagon, a kitchen wagon, or even an artillery one. In each of the given wagons, your legionnaires will be able to perform the given work according to the type of wagon. Treat wounded and sick colleagues in the medical room, cook food in the kitchen room, and shoot at enemies in the artillery room as an artillery support mission. Infantry wagons are a chapter unto themselves. You need to have enough of these and upgrade them to maximum capacity as soon as possible so that you have enough reserve to load all the legionnaires you meet. I underestimated this in the beginning and had to restart the game from the beginning. Not to mention the insulation of the wagons. This must also be done in advance, otherwise your passage through Siberia will become impossible. Another factor is the collection of material and components. It is possible to buy these from a merchant from time to time, but at a very disadvantageous rate. Either way, it will sometimes be necessary to buy something and sell other components. Fortunately, during the journey, there are so-called points of interest near the track, where, according to their types, the material is located. However, since the expedition is under time pressure, you will also have to decide which points of interest you will visit. In addition, there are built-in algorithms in the game, where your sent squad can find either an above-standard number plus more, but rather take the minimum and sometimes nothing at all. This can be influenced by the beneficial properties of some soldiers and, conversely, negatively. A soldier may get injured, be attacked by a pig, or catch a disease. Soldiers improve in combat and learn new skills. They are then more versatile and can help where the shoe is currently pushing you. The more versatility, the better. The game is really detailed in this.The sound system and especially the dubbing is of course at a very high level. The legionnaires were lent their voices by well-known Czech and Slovak dubbers, and the sound system is extremely authentic depending on the situation. Opponents speak Russian, of course. The period music was also well done, both during the train journey and in the missions. The music in them changes according to the current situation, where at first it is calm, but as the battle progresses, the music becomes faster and more dramatic. Likewise, the sound effects of gunfire, driving cars and the like sound like real guns and cars and not comical. It goes without saying that you and your enemies are covered behind certain obstacles. Then the firefights become longer, and in order not to waste too much ammo, I recommend using a grenade as an argument against enemies. The journey is divided into several chapters in which you will complete a number of interesting missions. Here you will help the local farmers against the Reds, who will plunder their village, save the cathedral, destroy enemy factories, artillery positions, fortresses and more. From time to time, a tree will fall onto your tracks and it's up to you to punch through it or remove it and keep the wood. Interactions will also occur at points of interest, and from time to time you will have to make decisions that will affect the morale of your soldiers. Sometimes you will be faced with bad decisions and have to choose the less bad one. To replenish the morale of the soldiers to high, which is necessary to avoid desertion, you can drink in station pubs or individually replenish the morale of each member of the expedition with consumables. So is the lack of fitness. Micromanaging your quest will play an absolutely crucial role during your journey back home. As you progress, the opponent will become more and more aggressive against you and the threat factor will appear. If it exceeds a certain limit, it will become a reality and the enemy will attack you with planes, for example. Fortunately, the game can be slowed down or stopped completely during hectic micromanagement passages so that you don't waste precious time and think everything through.Unfortunately, we come to what disappointed me, and it wasn't enough. I found a major bug in the game where at the end of the third chapter the grenade kill didn't work for me after entering the railway bridge. Of the group of soldiers, only their commander died in the explosion, while nothing happened to the subordinates. Another bug is the game crashing when loading saved positions. Six crashes in about sixty hours isn't too much, but I'm of the opinion that a well-optimized game definitely shouldn't crash like that. Not to mention the absence of a Quickload key, how could the creators forget such an important element of the game?! I was also struck by the unrealistic artificial intelligence, which completely ignores dead colleagues on the ground and reacts strangely to, for example, your revelation. I would expect comrades from the wider area to flock to you and start combing the area like for example in the first Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive. All you have to do is run 100 meters, hide in the bushes, and within a few seconds there is peace. To reinforce the enemy's patrols, the alarm must be raised by the enemy himself. I found the difficulty of the game incredibly easy except for the last mission. And please, I played the Commander. It was enough to lure one by one to the bush with the explorer's stone and then peck them. I usually knocked out the patrols with grenades and dogs with a bayonet lunge. Rather, there is a chance that you will get stuck because you run out of fuel on the train or because of underestimating the situation you will end up without food or freeze. Train management is annoying especially when deploying squads and taking care of specific legionnaires. In the windows, it is necessary to move using the sliders, whenever you send two or more squads into the field and if you need to improve, heal or supplement a specific legionnaire with blue and yellow bars. It would be enough to increase the size of the main windows of the platoon management and reduce the size of the panes, so that you can fit three platoons in the main window without having to scroll the window down. You will curse this especially towards the end of the game, when you will easily send 4 or more platoons into the field and improve dozens of soldiers. Unfortunately, the game in all of this falls down unnecessarily in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: A review in brief, if you are coming originally from Czechia or Slovakia - buy this game.If you like strategy games where you can manage every soldier - buy this game.You also get to ride a train, so that`s a fat plus too.Also, this game has a nice demo version, which gives an accurate representation of the game. Get it first, if you are not sure about the purchase.Tips for the folks that will buy it:1) You need to get the infantry wagons first, if you do not later in the game you will be forced to leave some legionnaires behind. You don't get any new soldiers in the late game. Ideally, you need to have 3 infantry wagons with maxed out capacity status.2) Early in the game you will have a choice of either picking the kitchen wagon or a workshop wagon. My advice - go for the kitchen one, with it you should not experience food shortage for the rest of the game. Moreover, you might that so much food at one point that you will be able to trade it off for something else. You will have a chance to get a workshop wagon later in the mid game, I would advise to get it at one point as the upgrades from it will help to get through the late game more easily.3) You can acquire (for free) an artillery wagon. When you will get it, unless you got a workshop instead of the kitchen wagon, it will be useless as it will have no ammunition. In the mid game, via story quests and side quests you can get around 18 shells for it. In my personal experience, I only started to use the wagon in the late game. With all of that being said, just keep in mind that it is a long-term investment which can pay off faster, depending on your gameplay.4) Try to visit as many points of interest on the map as possible in the early and mid game, in the late game you will most have not time for that. Try to avoid the villages where you can only trade there, unless you really need to trade.5) There are some negative traits that cannot be taken away from the soldiers, I am mainly talking about "agitated" trait. A soldier can get it if he was down during the mission. Thus, try to be careful with the soldiers. Soldiers who got wounded and got "injured" or "gravely injured" traits will eventually heal if they rest enough. "Agitated" so far cannot be healed from what I could see, and it gives unpleasant permanent debuffs.6) Be extra careful with tanks and armoured vehicles, it`s hard to fight them as they have the chance to almost one-shot your soliders.7) "One-shot" ability which the snipers will later have can destroy the armoured vehicles in 3 hits.8) Cover is important in this game, and soldiers who are in full cover are well protected from any enemies, apart from the tanks. Or the enemies who flanked them.9) No coal - game over, no wood - game over. Give priority to the coal first. Metal is also important as any good upgrade in this game needs it. Cloths is important early in the game to improve the infantry wagons, in the mid and late game you will probably not use it, thus you can sell most of it. However, it can be used in mid and late game in order to keep the soldiers warm when they are on the missions, so try to keep around 100-200 of it or so, just in case.10) If you are getting overwhelmed with the action during the fight, just press "space" for the pause, you can turn this game into an "X-COM" kind of game if you wish.11) Storage. Early in the game, you will have a chance to change the locomotive. I did not change it, as the default one consumes the least coal. I did have a lot of coal throughout my run, but I ran out of storage and I was foroced to get another storage wagon. One of the locomotives offers a lot of storage and the possibility to add more wagons to the train, however it consumes a lot of coal. I did switch to it later in the game, but it did not matter at that point. Do as you see fit in this situation, but know that storage in this game is also a resource, in a way and if you do not have enough of it you would later need to think of which things you need to get rid off.Good luck and have fun with this game, I have had great experience with it.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10I got it for $20 and it feels like a $20 - $25 title. It's like a budget version of Partisan 1941. For example, imagine your relatives whom you haven't seen for years are coming over for Christmas. You decide to have fried chicken with the family. normally you would buy fresh chicken, clean for any feathers and cut into parts, marinate and soak in buttermilk the previous night so it can sit overnight, make a fry mix with 5 or more different herbs and spices, and deep fry it in olive oil.Instead, you bought walmart or costco chicken and sprinkled some bread crumbs over it.That is Last Train Home. It's also the Last time your family comes to visit.You play as lost soldiers, trying to go back home with barely anything. In-game you kill dozens of enemies but loot nothing off of them. No inventory system.You have stealth, but it's Partisan 1941's distant cousin that's weird and likes eating glue.You have to grind train class soldiers and level them up so they can fight or participate in battle. Classes seem like they are important, till you realize a single soldier can have 5 classes.Cover system is the glue sniffing cousin of smarter kids like Company of Heroes. Even Dawn of War, a title from 20 years ago, does a better job.Last Train Home forgot buildings can be used as cover.Your "Legionaires" forgot to attend the "How to move a howitzer or relocate a machine gun" class.I can go on but that would just make the game a meme.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this wish-listed since forever, so I was really looking forward to it, I was hoping for Snowpiercer meets Aliens Dark Descent / Shadow Tactics / Desperados III. Ultimately it gets a thumbs down.1 Major letdown:The tactical combat. Its really awful imo, especially after chapter 1 in which it was fine. The stealth system doesn't really work, the red army camp in chapter 2 is a massive mess (you can place explosives to blow up trucks but whoever you instruct wont move after placing explosives blowing themselves up). It feels very janky. F5 is probably my most used button due to very strange controlled unit behavior. You can't capture objectives while stealthed - so you need to unstealth, but there isn't a hold fire button, so one of your guys might randomly start shooting at some distant enemy. Its just weird.1 large issue: The train UI/UX. You can't sort by perks which becomes problematic. The whole assigning people to various tasks without seeing what they are actually good at unless you click into their portrait screen is quite frustrating. I'd love to be able to let an off duty soldier work on a train upgrade - is this possible? No - you need to remove them from their squad, and even more annoyingly, put them back after the upgrade is complete - otherwise they'll sit in that upgrade slot for all time. Workers assigned to upgrade a train part will stay assigned even when it completes. Its micro management to a really silly degree.The redeeming feature: If you manage to get to terms with how to manage the train, the concept and train management parts are actually quite fun and novel.The demo is sadly not representative of the full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I bought the game on release and immediately fell in love with it. RTS and Management sounded great, and it was, for the starting part. The first 1/3 of the game was exciting, what would await in the far reaches of Russia, what MORE would there be? Maybe a wicked twist for the story, or maybe some of your soldiers would fight each other on some occasions (because of different beliefs). Slight spoiler: . The closer I got to the end, the more I felt the urge to just end the game because it was getting boring. The same type of stealth-missions, same type of enemies, same kind of rewards. As many others pointed out in the "negative" comment section, the story feels bland. Good guys vs bad guys and so on. Missions often were not challenging, just tedious to complete because of some dude not entering stealth mode after a takedown. In short: Good game, very cool combination of a RTS and management-game, nice theme, but needs more variety and content, because after 20 hours, you have seen it all.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good historical game about the birth of Czechoslovakia and its troop's evacuation by train. _childDocuments_.review: A solid RTS title that unfortunately declines in quality over time. The management layer is simple and initially interesting, but does not meaningfully increase in depth or complexity over time, while UI issues make it increasingly cumbersome as you get further into the story. For example, the job slot selection UI only shows 4 potential workers at a time, while your roster can grow to over 30 in the mid-late game, with a dozen train job positions that constantly need assignment and re-assignment based on the situation. Meanwhile, the tactical layer suffers from almost non-existent enemy AI, which is only capable of moving along simple patrol paths, responding to noise, or (rarely) following a clearly scripted path during events. This means that as the game progresses, the only way that difficulty increases is through larger numbers and higher stats. While hostiles do have classes and skills, you will never see these in use unless you make a mistake, and their impact is often minimal.Most concerning, the game has received no patches since launch ~2 weeks ago, and still has quite a number of bugs. From cover positions that can't actually be taken, to mission objectives that trigger at incorrect times, to hostile patrols that can spawn in and shoot you from outside of the map, the game can be quite frustrating with inflicting 'undeserved' losses. This is made much worse by the decision to not allow mid-mission saves. While this would be an interesting source of tension and consequences in a well-polished title, it's a deal breaker here, forcing you to replay missions that can take up to an hour in a long campaign that already overstays its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Combination of strategic resource management and tactical command. You take command of a group of unique individuals with different skills, traits, backgrounds and even portraits. You assign roles based on characters skills and the needs of your train, from engineers to riflemen. While the story is fairly linear (you are on a train after all), you do get to make many choices affecting the condition of your crew, the missions you take on, and the rewards farther down the track. A great game. I want more of these.

_childDocuments_.review: While I applaud the attempt to refocus from their strength into tactical game, it came out as, well, studio's first foray into tactical games. Example is where you set up overwatch with your MG on open stretch of a field, and watch it manage to do nothing, while your random soldier with a rifle, firing from cover, absolutely wrecks open enemy after another.Or then you go to attack someone in high cover, by the time tutorial finished explaining to me why and how should I bayonet charge that position, my rifleman sniped the opponent already.The stealth is just best not mentioned. There was clear inspiration from Commandos series here, if you only saw that series from a moving car.It's a shame, as the game looks stunning, and the story seems interesting, but I don't want to pain through game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! In short, it's a challenging tactics, survival and management game. These three individual aspects combined make the game a great and challenging experience. After 50 hours of play I can give you an overview: The only thing I have to hold against the game is: it's a great game, one of the most exciting tactical games for me in recent years, but an incredible amount of wasted potential. I'll try to summarize the individual points:1. storyhere you get a (!attention) historically based story, which is beautifully written and divided into individual clear chapters. every now and then you can make decisions, some of which affect you or unlock new missions. The presentation is down-to-earth oldschool but brings its own charm. Characters are written normally, definitely fitting and authentic in the setting. the only thing is that the legionnaires are all "too perfect". Especially in the beginning it is shown that these soldiers would never do anything wrong and - yes. the other side is clearly evil. here you could have brought more shades of gray and moral decisions at the beginning that are really serious. Because as we all know: war, war never changes.-more opportunities for random encounters throughout the game would be desirable, especially to increase the replay value.2. management, survival and mapManaging the train is a lot of fun and gets trickier as you go along. do i ration from the start so that i have more later on? do i invest in insulation early on or do i wait and run the risk of not having the materials later on? would you rather have a workshop, kitchen or ambulance? everything fits together well and important raw materials are in short supply. but this is where you could have done a bit more in terms of narrative and gameplay as described above to develop the full potential. similar with the roles and squads on the map: role allocation makes sense and is exciting, you always think about whether to send the squad out, whether the soldiers are tired, who is working on the train, etc. - but what would it have been like if a squad ran out of energy and therefore couldn't return? If they had to have rations and sleeping bags with them to generate energy? and if they don't have that, do you have to consider leaving the soldier who has no energy behind or sending a second one and hoping they can somehow make it back on their own without seeing anything on the map? Or a splitted railroad and i need to think about which way? the way with the forrest and woodstack? or the other one with the ruins/villages?3. battlesthe battles are really fun. they are challenging, the classes fit together well. they are really well balanced and those who have mastered the mechanics can give full rein to their tactical genius.and here i come, even if it is the game's greatest strength and it is far ahead of other titles, to the greatest weakness, the potential:some mechanicen do not make sense, e. g. mines do not resume, bayonet attacks with two soldiers on two soldiers, who then attack only one. but these are little things that do nothing to counteract the fun of the game.more importantly, I'd like to have more trouble. more settings about ki, search history of opponents, communication of opponents, ki strengthens, how far shots are audible. Also here, what if you make a shot and know that half the card is going to attack you? Yes I know, not everyone wants that, but I want to have the option that this happens and then the opponents are in alert readiness, have a bigger field of view and discover me faster. suddenly deviate from their routes or new two-trupps appear patrolling?What I unfortunately don't like at all is the implementation of guns, vehicles and tanks. The animations aren't nice, the behavior unfortunately leaves a lot to be desired and especially when I take a gun I can let the whole map come to me and kill everyone. The AI ​​should be better here, not go into the radius or flank with two squads. I don't really understand the cover system either. I think cover is cover. no matter whether it's a wooden board, clothesline or stone. whether from the front, the side or the back. Tactical gameplay is lost here because it is not profitable to flank a position. This is only worthwhile if I catch opponents outside of cover AND can get into cover myself.also that soldiers cannot shoot when they are running. So not at all? Medics only have one pistol and a grenadier can also shoot with a short-barreled weapon. And the gunners only run after them when they are out of the radius. It would be cool if they stopped quickly and shot, with a greatly reduced hit rate. here could be moreI want a second part of the game!-the game ABSOLUTELY needs modsupport, so resourceful people might be able to make a total conversion, in the starwars universe or whatever, so the community just gets bigger and bigger. -it need more settings or a hardcore tactical mode.-a steamworkshop,-maybe a rougelite mode witch random maps? really, the game is awesome but could be my dream-game.You see. sooo much potential! dear deavs, make a second one, again a train or a convoy? maybe the WW2, Vietnam? maybe you know the series "the last ship"? But thank u for a great game!The bottom line is, the game gets from me 95/100 points.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is very interesting conceptually but rudimentary in execution. The game is not bad and actually hits its stride in the latter half as the snow starts falling and your legion's situation truly starts to deteriorate. The tension from this, pressing home the notion that getting out of this war torn country is an ever more pressing issue. During this phase of the game the diversity of the missions expands and your legionaries  truly start to feel more powerful as they hit the level cap.  This is the high point of the game and while I Enjoyed it, getting there  through the earlier sections of track was painful. There were also chronic issues that persisted for the whole ride that ultimately contributed to this thumbs down.  This game is held back by many of it's systems being very basic both mechanically and in terms of the writing. To provide an example on the strategic level, you have to send out search parties to gather resources. There are random events at the collection points that can impact the resources received.  The problem is there's only a handful of outcomes that actually happen and after a 55 hour play-through you have most of them memorized. If I had a bag of coal for every time somebody got mauled by a boar searching an abandoned settlement id have never needed to worry if the train would make it. The overarching writing of the story is not better, though voice work in the legion's native tongue is awesome. The reds are bad, the whites are incompetent, and we are the good guys. I would have liked more moral ambiguity playing off the fact that we are desperately trying to escape a civil war we have no part in. For the RTS elements, again, everything here is basic and the enemy AI is about as smart as a bag of rocks. Most levels regardless of difficulty can be completed with a single scout, said bag of rocks, and access to an assortment of bushes around the level.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely worth the money. Below are my few points on great game that could have been excellent, but isnt:Positives:-Beautiful area graphics, train etc.-Storyline and concept-ImmersiveNegatives:-Not optimized graphics. If you want top graphics settings and decent FPS you need to have a serious gaming rig-Various small bugs and ambiguities (coal consumption mechanics are nonsese, train that is supposed to consume a lot of coal isnt really consuming a lot etc., soldiers getting stuck while moving, grenade throwing, doing critical shot)-not balanced well - you are supposed to be forced to make hard decisions on coal and food, but even on commander level these are pretty ok and no challenge at all.-AI of enemies - Enemies are simply retarded. _childDocuments_.review: A very decent game that merges both management and RTS style mechanics. The game options allow you some degree of flexibility in how you'd like to approach the game with tweaking things to both the management and RTS so if you have a preference you can lean more into the difficulty of those genres. As a history buff the game shines a light on a relatively lesser known event so for that reason I enjoyed it, the main story is told mainly through text events and the narration of your adviser, which I must admit his VA has done a great job. Your soldiers are more X-COM than developed personalities although the traits system of both RNG and your actions/events allow a decent amount of variety within your cadre of soldiers. The game is not perfect, some things are a little unbalanced in favour of a player who is familiar with RTS mechanics as the ai does seem to struggle a little bit countering Stealth - but even that is a testament that you have options to play the game guns blazing and sneaking about. The UI of your squad management takes a little while to get used to but as you play and remember what soldiers you have assigned to certain roles you can get a grasp of things rather quickly. Overall, having just completed a first playthrough as a leisurely pace of around 30 hours, this game is worth your time. A fun mix of RTS and management, with a historical flair and a smattering of moral choices to make along the way. Last Train Home is a game that may have one or two diversions but firmly stays on track.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a pretty cool game and I'm inclined to recommend it but the QoL problems are severe. If the devs do a patch update that solve them, I will change my review. I haven't been writing down everything but here's two examples:-There's a mission in Penza where you find a group of prisoners and if you didn't find a specific civilian earlier in the mission, you have to spend a lot of time backtracking, trying to figure out what you missed. The game should mark the approximate key location on the map as soon as you find the prisoners. In general, this design decision that wastes players' time should be reversed.-The UI for managing characters is terrible. I threw my hands in the air when I had to decide what soldiers to leave behind because at that point, there were no sort options whatsoever. This applies elsewhere too though. It takes too many steps to understand your roster.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and then had to pick it up.  This is very evocative of the old "Commandos" series I played when I was young.  The premise of the game is cool and the mechanics are interesting.  This is definitely worth your time.Pros: 1) The train! 2) The setting is something I wasn't familiar with and it's actually astonishing what these guys had to go through.  3) You will get attached to your characters, and the leveling system is satisfying. 4) Great voice-overs. 5) Compelling gameplay loop.Cons: 1) Not very high replay value.  I played through once, very much enjoyed it, and might come back a second time to look at some decisions I could have made differently, but that's about it.  2) Train management can get fiddly.  This is both a strength and a weakness.  My main gripe is that it can take a minute to find specific people or skills for certain missions or jobs.  3) There are a few moments of tonal discordance.  Once, I won a mission without anyone getting shot, and the next cutscene acted like half my troops had died or fallen ill.  Neutral: 1) There were a few bugs in the first week of launch, but nothing I wasn't able to work around.  By now, these are mostly completely resolved. 2) A couple of quest lines seem to have imprecise triggers, some decisions don't always play out with satisfying results. 3) Stealth can be very satisfying, but also slightly inconsistent.  You'll just have to learn the rules around how it works through experimentation.  4) Understandably, this story is told from a standpoint of Checkslovakian nationalism - but it can seem a bit like propaganda at times (for a country that no longer exists in a conflict with factions that no longer exist)Again, I had a great time with this game, and I recommend it as worth it's value.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: The story is truly fantastic, there are things that seem very repetitive but these are kept interesting via other events, you can always skip them as well if desired. _childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliantly crafted game set in 1918 with an immersive storyline! The plot is rooted in real historical foundations, thanks to thorough research, and takes place during a dramatic period: the Czechoslovak Legions' journey through Russia during the civil war, amidst the rise of communism. The game authentically captures the haunting atmosphere of the time, reflecting the turmoil after the near destruction of the Tsar's family. Gameplay is smooth and balanced, with the train-upgrade feature adding a unique touch—it becomes both a mobile fortress and a home, just as it was historically. Highly recommended for an unforgettable experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Good story, good gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: "Last Train Home" is like managing a rowdy road trip through Siberia with the Czech Legion post-WWI, but in game form. You'll juggle resources, plot strategic routes, and try to keep your squad from falling apart—both literally and figuratively.This top-down adventure throws you into the boots of a resource manager extraordinaire. Picture this: you're desperately trying to balance food, ammo, and morale while your squad explores the wilds of Siberia. It's like a high-stakes game of chess, but instead of kings and queens, you've got Czech soldiers and the occasional vodka break.The graphics? They're actually not too shabby for a top-down game. It's retro-cool, like a historical comic book come to life. You'll guide your pixelated troops through snowy landscapes, dodging bandits and Bolsheviks like a boss.Overall, "Last Train Home" is a compact, challenging experience that'll test your resource management skills and strategic wit. Just remember: pack extra socks, keep the vodka flowing (for morale, of course), and pray that your train doesn't get stuck in a snowdrift. Na zdraví!(provided by ChatGPT)

_childDocuments_.review: Great all around, except for the combat imo. First off, the main point of the game, which is resource management. You control a train, and have several different resources such as fuel, food, ammo, people, and things like metal for upgrades. The whole resource management part of this game is very simple yet very engaging. Send your soldiers out for supply runs as your train powers across the country side on a gorgeous overworld map. This section is a little reminiscent of The Wandering Village visually, which I really enjoy. Although, the part where this game starts to shine is its harsh choices. Can you spare food to a war-orphaned child, or do you keep it for your men as your limited supplies dwindle? A bit like more depressing games such as This War of Mine. Most of the time though, making the "good guy choice" isn't actually that costly, and so there isn't much incentive to be a bastard constantly even on the harder difficulties.The part I dislike about this game is the other half of it. The combat. Its simple and straight forward, which is fine, but the game acts as if you're able to conduct grand strategies that could rival a general. You cannot. Put your guys behind cover and hope they hit their targets. Its fine, and admittedly satisfying, but its SO costly in ammo and medical supplies that you are forced to use stealth a majority of the time, which sucks. And yet, they base so much of the game around it. The stealth in this game reminds me of old flash games, as you literally spend maybe 90 percent of it avoiding HUGE enemy vision cones. Your options include sneaking (which makes you move silently but does not conceal you at all even behind cover), throwing a rock to distract a guy (which is what I spend a majority of the time doing), and using binoculars to see beyond your vision cone. The only thing that really counts as stealth in this game is the fact you can hide in bushes. Every single combat encounter I get into, I groan, roll my eyes, and consider closing this game. If they had ONE more stealth feature, the ability to hide undetected behind cover, I would seriously consider this game a masterpiece. I know this seems like such an odd reason to stop short of giving this game that title, but if you try the combat for yourself, you'll see what I mean. Imagine playing Metal Gear Solid and Solid Snake cant crouch, lie down, hide behind cover, or use any stealth gadgets but the game still focuses HEAVILY on stealth, because thats how this feels. I would argue that maybe 10 of my total hours have literally been cheesing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ stealth systems in this game. All in all, this game is VERY solid. A definite 8/10. If you can look past my one complaint, its wonderful and beautiful. It deserves at least a try from anyone who gives it a passing glance.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable experience which takes obvious inspirations from Frostpunk. _childDocuments_.review: After 4 hours, I can tell this will be a good game.Highest difficulty.It combines the "home front" decision making of This War of Mine or State of Decay with the combat of Dawn of War 2 or Company of Heroes.  All told during a period of time that will make any fan of the World Wars era happy.Something Last Train Home adds that I wish Dawn of War 2 had was an "active pause" where you can survey cover, use abilities, and give orders during stop time.  For a tactical game, this is a must.  On highest difficulty, soldiers out of cover pretty much get hit every time a shot is fired.  I think most soldiers can take 4 hits before dying, but even one hit has implications on the strategy map when bullets aren't flying.If I have one complaint, it is that the UI is a little clunky with the day/night shifts and identifying which soldiers are working which job.  But this happens when the game is paused and is not a significant issue.Graphical quality is average and will probably work on older computers built after 2020.  I can run this game 1440p on an AMD 5600 XT which  benchmarks at "too powerful for 1080p, not powerful enough for 1440p"

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is neat. The voice acting is excellent, the cinematics are very high quality, and I absolutely love the illustrative cinematics as Captain Langer recounts the events. The game is split into two major sections, a resource management section where you drive your train across the frozen wastes of Siberia, and RTS-style missions where you control your squad through beautiful, well crafted maps. In the overworld section, you drive your train across all of Russia, with villages, lumberyards, and more along the way to scavenge resources from. As the game progresses, and you venture further into Siberia, the risk/reward of exploring missions becomes an active decision that you have to make when you pass points of interest. You could stop for everything, but is it worth stopping the train for it? Now, for the other half of the game: the missions. Each mission throughout the game is on a beautiful map, set in cities, countrysides, factories, and more. Most maps start very small, but expand as you progressive through objectives, and the minimap changes as it adjusts to the newly expanded maps. Each mission is littered with resources to supplement your journey. The weather changes as you advance, and the map design reflects those changes. My absolute favorite part of the combat is that units actually go where you tell them to go. If you have multiple selected, they'll arrive at their location in a formation, but if they'll snap to cover whenever possible. My only critique with this movement is that a lot of bushes that you would hide in near fences will end up snapping you to the fence when you move close, which might be out of hiding.  Overall, a very enjoyable game. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: AS promised, I have taken my criticism down. Devs follow up was impressive and the bug that was breaking the game, in my opinion, is gone. The main missions are really good fun and reward patience and thinking through. You get fond of your soldiers and seek to preserve them. Great work Devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I've read good things about this The Last Train Home so after seeing it on sale I decided to give it a go. At first I thought I had picked up a real bargain. I liked the concept of the game, the story was starting to seem interesting and the train management system and resource management all seem really well done.However, upon reaching the Moscow mission, my opinion has quickly changed. The combat is appalling and has completely ruined the game for me. The snipers are useless. Aside from the binoculars I don't see the difference between them and the rifleman. Even with a good vantage point and clear line of site if you attack an enemy they just run right up to within shooting distance if them before firing a shot. It's the stealth gameplay though that really stinks in this game though. The so called "Silent Mode" is pointless. All it does is make your squad move really slowly and not open fire, even if their team mates are being shot at. Also, setting up any kind of ambush feels impossible. Even if you hide soldiers behind a solid stone wall in "Silent Mode" an enemy patrol will always spot your soldiers the second their cone of vision reaches where your soldiers are positioned. I really wanted to like this game and with better combat it could be a very good game but unfortunately the lack of tactics just spoils things too much for me. Back to JA3 I go.

_childDocuments_.review: THQNordic hit it out of the park with this. There's replayability. There's an engaging story. There's RNG that's *actually* random (as in restarting from a save game can literally be the flip of a coin on success vs failure). The graphics are awesome as well. The only complaint I have about this is that at times, the RNG can completely screw you over (artillery strikes that wipe out all the heavy equipment, for example; reload and no artillery strikes screws you over). It can be a little draining and frustrating sometimes, but the awesome thing is that it's completely RNG, so simply reloading from an earlier checkpoint can "reset" things and get you RNG that's not as back-breaking. Although the opposite is true and at times a reload can get you RNG that causes you to be squashed in the blink of an eye. Either way, I just started my second play through to experience the different paths that can be taken. I'm guessing it'll be as awesome as the first play through.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely lovingly crafted game, by a passionate development team. It has been an honor to help out testing this gem (and getting the finished product as compensation, which was a nice surprise after months of testing...) , and I hope Ashborne Games sticks around for more titles.LTH is a blend of managing resources, nurturing the individuals under your care, and solving complex moving puzzles. It's a squad-based skirmisher, a strategic game that can be paused to stop & think, and every mission is unique. A lot of energy went into making every fight, every engagement stand on its own rather than being repetitive. Secondary goals spice things up. I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone even tangentially interested in strategy games, be it in XCom, Jagged Alliance, Battletech, etc. pp. - this game will scratch those itches. You even get a tiny bit of Frostpunk with managing your moving train in the cold. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Best way to describe this game is to say that it is a combination of "This War of Mine" with some RTS like either XCOM or Command and Conquer where your goal is to get a legion of soldiers out of Civil War Russia by piloting a hijacked train eastward through Siberia. Its fairly similar to This War of Mine in that you have a 'base' to upgrade and manage resources for in this case a train, while at other parts of the game you are participating in RTS combat scenarios with your troops from a top-down view. The train/base management part I love. You need to keep track of mainly 5-6 different resources to keep your train moving as well as to upgrade parts of your train for better buffs or acquiring specialized train cars as the story progresses. Soldiers themselves meanwhile can unlock different roles (5 combat related ones, 4 non-combat related ones) and you can set aside a chunk of time trying to big brain which roles pair well with each other so you can really maximize your soldiers to their best potential. Soldiers also have certain buffs and debuffs in terms of personality that might make them great for some missions and an absolute liability in other missions... You do also have to be careful with how you allocate resources because you most likely will NOT be able to fully max out your train and all soldiers unless you really tweak the settings.  The RTS aspect i'm less a fan of, but that's just because of my nature in general and not the fault of the game. Missions set you into a map and a maximum of 10 troops complete objectives as they work their way through the map. UTILIZE THE QUICKSAVE BUTTON TO SAVE YOURSELF FROM HEADACHES. I invented a few different swear words after one of my troops randomly opened fire on a squad of soldiers I was trying to sneak past, and some of the missions at the very end of the campaign really throw a lot at you. All of that though is pretty part for the course for RTS games though so just be advised that it is a part of the game. Overall I enjoyed the hell out of the 60 hours I spent playing the game. I did manage to get it on sale for 50% off which also swayed my opinion a fair amount, and I had to start the campaign over from scratch after I realized how to actually assign roles and stuff properly, but there is still marginal replayability to this game. I didnt find out until right before the last mission that I had to manually select which guns for soldiers to use to bring into battle (meaning all the level 3 guns I had been acquiring up to that point were being used as wall decor) and troops were using level 1 guns the entire time... I also leaned pretty hard into sniper/scout tactics to get through missions, but people who prefer to go with more heavy-handed strategies with machine guns and grenades can fit their squads accordingly too. All in all this is a really solid game for anyone who:1 - Has a touch of the tism or slightly undiagnosed adhd 2 - Like trains 3 - Like killing communists 4 - Likes games that occasionally go on sale for 50% off

_childDocuments_.review: A game steeped in history, but lacking in gameplay. It has the worst worlds of RTS and Squad-based tactical games. Most of combat is looking at russian detection cones and putting your soldiers away from them. Even that is annoying as cover and concealment are poorly telegraphed. Load times are a huge bugger. Solders level up, but most abilities you get from levels have no satisfying impact, with a few game-breaking exceptions like the Critical Shot. There's no reason not to field a team of scouts, 1 grenadier and maybe 1 medic. The whole thing is boring and tedious.But that's no problem, right? You can just set the combat difficulty to low and breeze through the boring parts! But wait, that makes battles big gifts of free resources, making the supply and train management part of the game much less difficult. There might be some balance of difficulty sliders to make the game fun, but after 34 hours I haven't found it yet.Still, the atmosphere was top notch, and the premise and storytelling was enough to pull me to the end. I wish the encyclopedia entries had more meat to  them. Characters had traits, but aside from the looting related ones it was impossible to know which one would trigger where. I don't regret my purchase, but I don't think its worth buying. The studio has my interest for their next game. Just pick between RTS and Squad Based Tactics, please. This mushy inbetween style is awful and most buttons just don't feel good to press, and the passives are so low-impact I don't feel them at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is an easy recommend. I completed the game in 90 hours but played very slowly in the first half, and raced through the second half.There are two main parts to the game. The management of a train that transports troops through Russia, and battle stages where you control squads of men selected from your train to fight various battles in RTS which reminds me very much of sniper elite, but the sniping is only 3rd person view.Like any game that tries to incorporate what could be separated into two games in one, players will likely find that they prefer one aspect over the other. Personally, I liked that I had to gather wood, metal, food, etc to upgrade my train, and feed and care for my men, however, the actual management of the train I felt was a little tedious- constantly having to disband squads because they had to drive the train and stoke the engine wasn't fun. In fact, I never had one squad that wasn't disbanded when they got back to the train. II liked that each soldier was an individual character who could level up and develop skills throughout the game. I enjoyed the vehicles and heavy guns which my soldiers could take control of, and the purchasing and upgrading of weapons and skills.Some areas that could be improved: snipers are greatly overpowered. On the battlefield they provide unlimited ability to use binoculars at no cost to detect enemy. They have instant kill shot when they level up, and also have zone of death which means they can have extended range damage and accuracy in a small arc that you select. While the fact that you have to select an arc could be a limitation, you can easily select a new arc and set up in 1 second. Because of these advantages, a group of 2-3 snipers with little or no support can often complete a mission. You have little chance of getting hit because you can use your special abilities to see all enemies before they see you. Snipers also have the stealth ability, so they can easily hide, and even when spotted easily disappear. Enemy troops that spot you move towards you for a few steps then if they can't see you, which is almost always the case, they then act like they didn't see you. I played on the recommended difficulty. When the battle has a recommended squad size of 8 and you can complete it with 3 men, snipers are probably overpowered.While you can't save during firefights, due to the high value of individual troops, I soon found myself saving every 5-10 minutes and as a result could play more carelessly with no penalty. If someone important died, I could simply load. That isn't how the game is supposed to be played but players will be strongly motivated to play in this way.I would suggest reducing the ability of snipers to use binoculars because binoculars effectively remove the mist of war. While a cool down on binoculars might seem unrealistic, it is no more unrealistic that binoculars seeing what is happening on the other side of large buildings. Once per minute or two would be better. I might have three snipers, so once per minute would still be a lot.This would force me to use some lesser value troops to explore and take more casualties.Secondly, while this may be the case on higher difficulties, I would recommend no saving during battles, only saving at key moments, or having a limited number of saves, 2 or 3 per battle. Players can restart if they are unhappy with the outcome, and should not be getting to the end of the game with a train full of level 5 soldiers as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok first i want to say, i overall enjoyed the experience, especially at the the start. _childDocuments_.review: Spectacular blend of tactical strategy, management, RPG and story. The game's systems all complement each other perfectly. On the train map, you deal with events, resource management and planning. In the tactical maps, you deal with unit placement, ability use and stealth. It is odd to have a stealth system in an RTS/RTT game, but this one is intuitive and extremely rewarding. Getting the drop on an entire enemy squad because you had your movement timing down is such a rush, and seeing your troops progress and become more versatile over the course of the game adds a fantastic sense of progression. Personally, this is now one of my favorite games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: LTH is not very easy to recommend, but except a lot of mechanics playing on your nerves it's a lot of fun - with very interesting topic and a lot of great ideas. If you're not Czech or Slovak, it will be better to wait for 50 % sale. (8 or 9/10 reviews are biased nonsense.)LTH is screaming "We wanted to add everything but we didn't have enough resources". I'm sorry for them because it could be one of the best Czech games ever. Biggest issue here is everything in the game is halfway done. I'm not going to make a list, because it's really EVERYTHING. And since Ashborne Games are not CDProject, I don't believe they're able to finish the game post-release.Next big issue is game's relentless pursuit of a depressed mood often leading to funny moments. You can capture 2 tanks + 4 trucks and singlehandedly annihilate every enemy in the mission, but mission debriefing is in the spirit of "we've barely made it". Your people could be happy and warm, but according to intermezzos they are "starving and freezing to death". Why? Just why?I could get over all of this, but I cannot handle HDD era loading times (on NVMe)... and squad management - you cannot seamlessly transfer soldiers between work in the train and battle squad. You need to remove them from work manually and then they're available for battle. And it's nerve wrecking that squad aren't customisable groups of soldiers usable for different occasions. No. Every soldier can be in one and only squad, so if your main soldier is a hunter as well, you need to remove him from battle squad and only then you can add him to hunting squad and send him hunting. Now imagine you need the same soldier for missions, hunting and looting so you need to rework your squads before every task. This makes no sense in game!Should be fixed: Barbora Hlavatá is something like Emma Smetana? I don't have her in the train, but she's still commenting events in missions :-DI recommend anyway, but be prepared to swear a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: One level, Last Train Home is a very competent strategic resource management and tactical combat game. But as an immersive historical experience, it's one of the best I've ever played. Where it shines most is in the character-building. During the game you will take on around 40 individual soldiers, who you get to know only through a painted portrait and story interactions. And yet with these bare ingredients, by the end of the game you will know and care about every single one of them.There was Maximilian the sniper, who would always bring back game when he went hunting. Magdalena the medic, who would brighten up everyone's day with a smile, and who was tragically killed in the final battle. Kamil the taciturn grenadier, never seen without a rolled-up cigarette, and whose motto was "Captain say, Kamil do". Ondrej the train driver, who could be persuaded, if reluctantly, to pick up a rifle when a squad was short-handed.The final touch that will make this game stay with me is that at the end of your journey the game gives you a 'where are they now' summary for each of your survivors. It made me genuinely sad that there was no 'where are they now' for the ones we lost.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I almost, ALMOST uninstalled this game and was going to ask for a refund. But then I decided to start over after reading some gamer tips online. The tips really helped out.Post WWI. There's a Civil War in Russia. Between the Red Army and the White Army.  Neither are to be trusted. But the White Army seems to be less brutal. I finally passed the learning curve. Now. I. Am. Hooked.  This is one of the best games since the original, legendary, Rome Total War. It has a long overdue and fresh theme to it. Just like game, Rome Total War. It requires a lot of micromanagement, planning and strategy. With a lot of Battle Tactics. Logistics and TIME!  The map is HUGE. Even though you're following a narrative and have to stay within the confines of the narrative. You are always given choices, like mini crossroads. With each decision at each crossroads determining the future outcome of your future experiences.  For instance. There are two main West to East train Routes that you can choose from. The Northern Route and the Southern Route. Both have their advantages and disadvantages. Some Missions you can chose to bypass. Others are mandatory. Like whenever the enemy blocks the tracks and set's up a blockade. You have to clear the blockade.The Train is so much more than your temporary home. It is your life. Surrounded in an immense World of Death & Destruction. It offers a chance to survive two back to back Wars. For you and whoever is lucky enough to join you along the way. It is your sanctuary. Therefore.  It is paramount that you consistently maintain and upgrade the Steam Machine as best you can. For me. The Hallmark of a great game. Seems to be the way in which it can devour your time like a hungry wolf.  Not time though frustration. But rather, through being intensely immersed and hypnotized. So much so. That you become  Total Warly.   " OMG, it's 4 in the morning! I have to get up early.!"  LOL  Yeah. It's that type of a game.The level of detail on the maps is fantastic. Beautiful Lakes, Rivers, Mountains, Streams, Villages leading to Towns and Cities.As for a Battle Tip? Try to emphasize on Snipers (Scouts) to quietly and slowly remove threats vs frontal confrontations. That is perhaps the BIG SECRET to this game.  It really makes a difference. In my next battle. I may even experiment by forming a team of snipers with perhaps one Machine Gunner and one Grenadier. That would REALLY be interesting to use Navy Seal Style Tactics. Caution. You may enter another realm and lose yourself in this one. But isn't that the whole purpose of entertainment?Try the Demo. Put your phone on Airplane Mode. Get comfortable and join us.  There's 9,000 miles of Russian Wilderness, Towns and War Torn Cities between here and our homeland in  Czechoslovakia.  The Russians are a very unpredictable people. One day they are a friend of the Czechs the next day, an enemy. They are who they are. We are not them. This is THEIR Country. We are strangers here and must leave. But along the way. The Russians, both Red and White Armies. Seem to  respect those who show strength, courage and endurance.   "Comrade".
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: If you are into strategy games such as company of heroes or men of war, you'll love this one. Truly is an amazing game, it is not the most challenging in the standard difficulty, but it does not need to be. I wish I could have paid more attention and understand all the mechanics before the end of Chapter 1 but it is a journey worth taking, the tactical pause you can make to move your troops around is a game changer for any narrative RTS experience where making decisions in real time is not really mandatory, the feature makes for some great moments as it allows you to play it more like a turn based strategy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Combat is fun, stealth not so much it can get tedious and I feel like there is not enough depth to the stealth system to keep the stealth fresh for longer periods of time. Train/soldier management is fun aswell, but I feel like UI leaves something to be desired, finding out which of your soldiers is occupied with what requires you to hover above specific place in UI to show you the information, it gets bit annoying after while.I have played about 5 hours and I have made it past chapter 2 with plenty to go, so I expect the game length to be beyond satisfactory. Voice acting (playing in Czech mind you and somehow I have hunch this might not be the case for english version) is mixed bag. Intonation during mission briefings seems to change alot for no reason as if the voice lines are stitched together. Some lines in missions to me sound like they are from a b-movie and are overacted, but that might be deliberate choice. Other than gameplay I have to mention the art/artwork and great story/premise of the game. The game itself oozes love for the subject matter and you can tell developers put their passion in making this. Even though I may seem critical in my review I wholeheartedly recommend the game, it is indeed something special even though it is not perfect. Also, according to other comments it makes commies butthurt so that is also something that warms my heart.

_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of a a modern/updated WWI themed Oregon Trail. Managing and upgrading the train while in the overview screen has some elements of a cozy game, able to upgrade and take care of your troops. Then the combat aspect is really fun to play. After watching The Pacific and Band of Brothers, it makes you really fell like a military commander, assessing each situation and taking precautions on capturing objectives. The storytelling is deep and the cut scenes with live action make this game all the better. Every choice you make has an impact and you can get yourself into some tough situations. It does take a bit to understand the mechanics, but it tries its best to walk you through in the tutorial. One thing I had to learn on my own was how to upgrade the train. Highly recommend upgrading the troop capacity. I didn't realize this by the time I got to a Point of No Return and when I finished the final mission of the area I didn't have enough space for the new troops and had to reload an old save. That's part of learning though, make mistakes and learn from them. All in all I don't play a whole lot of RTS games, but this one is a win for me. A lot of content for the the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Train Home reminds me the most of Company of Heroes combined with Commandos in terms of the RTS part (more players probably mention that), and I think Ashborne games managed to combine the best of these games. Both of these series are huge favorites of mine and after playing the demo of The Last Train Home I knew it was the game for me. Moreover, within the framework of the game's processed historical period, it is an original subject - a chapter of Czechoslovak history, about which many people do not know many details (even in Czech republic). The story of the Czechoslovak legionnaires and their pilgrimage through the ravaged Russia during the First World War (or right after it) is very nicely handled within the RTS genre.I was afraid of the management part, because I only play sporadically when it comes to management strategies (warehouses, weapons, ammunition, food, materials, etc.). Fortunately, I got into it very quickly and the principle of taking care of the soldiers and the train in general is without problems.Summary:+ caring for individual soldiers+ sound effects+ great Czech/Slovak dubbing (I didn't try English)+ feature films/scenes+ music+ artworks during loading+ overall design of the game user interface+ weather effects, especially in the rain+ random side missions+ train management (wagons, locomotives, upgrades)- sometimes soldiers get stuck on each other or some obstacle and you have to help themGreat game from Czech meadows and groves. My rating 8/10 (not far from a nine)

This will bring it in line with titles like Divinity and make navigation generally easier! Keep up the great work by the way- I played through the entire demo and loved it, been waiting for this game for months!)

_childDocuments_.review: For those who like RTS games; This is brilliant. TL;DR? It's similar to Frostpunk, not just because the game takes place in a semi frozen landscape, but also due to having to manage the needs of your people, ensuring they survive. The difference between Frostpunk and LTH is that there is the capacity for combat, and this aspect is very reminiscent of the Commandos series of games from the late 90's and Noughties. Both the asset/manpower management and combat aspects of the game gel to provide a very rewarding and enjoyable experience.You are part of a team trying to get home, but can only do so by travelling inside Russia, from the west to the east. As the storyline progresses alongside your train, the game's functionality is gradually introduced in a manner that is quite a moderate learning curve in comparison to other games (Frostpunk included) thus I'd bet not only will it suit experienced RTS gamers but also new ones. Areas of control and that require attention in game:- Locomotive (You will have the option during the middle of the game to change to a different locomotive. I recommend the towing bull as it has the highest car capacity and speed is not an issue) - Train cars (each car has a role, can be upgraded, has heating options that are manually selected and I recommend you prioritise heating and comfort)- Soldiers (training, roles, skill point allocations and morale management)- Routes to take to Vladivostok (each route will bring different challenges and additions to the story)Audio:- Voiceovers - You can opt for either your primary language or the native language of your soldiers, with voice quality that is near perfect- Sound effects - [INSERT 'TERRI CREWS EXPLOSIONS' MEME HERE] Very good quality albeit a little lacklustre when artillery rains down on the target. A little more bass would be nice.- Music - Oh wow, it is sombre, depressing, and fits perfectly with the vibe of the game. But also, it provides a beautiful contrast at times when you finally do get a win (eg: searching for food, raiding unoccupied residences, hunting etc) and such wins seem to illicit a greater sense of satisfaction and relief as the death of your soldiers has been delayed, even just for a few days.Graphics:- On max settings, 4k resolution and DLSS enabled, it will be a picturesque vista laid before you with very detailed graphics and it won't tax your system too much, unlike Cyberpunk. They really did a good job on this side of things! Also, lowering the settings is a breeze and still provides an enjoyable experience at the expense of the quality of visuals. Interface:- Ok, I will admit, it has its moments where the interface seems clunky, but overall, if you know what to look for, you'll get there. And there is plenty of guidance provided in tutorial pop ups.Lastly, a few tips:- If you take the towing bull, you get up to 9 cars of which I recommend you take the following - 1x each of artillery, stock, hospital, kitchen and workshop cars, with 4x infantry cars. This will give you freedom to craft everything (except vodka and cigarettes) that you may need as well as house up to 48 soldiers that you slowly add to in the game.- The first car you are offered free of charge should be the workshop car. Being able to craft ammo will be a godsend and that leads me to my next point- If at all possible, use stealth kills and save ammo. Then, craft ammo with your workshop car, selling ONLY to merchants that are not on the track or at depots you stop at. Merchants you send squads to visit give higher sale prices.- Scouts - The best unit (IMHO) in the game. I take 5 along on each mission and they do the majority of the grunt work and killing, with support from machine gunners and grenadiers when you face waves in a mission. Get them levelled up and add to their roles medic or grenadier to make use of the trait that comes with those roles, and they will then become Rambo. The ultimate in-game killing machines.- Check the traits of each soldier, as some may be prone to accidents, or may not be suited to working in the train but have bonuses for combat/squad runs, so it is important to apply their skills accordingly or suffer the consequences.- Unless you know you have WAY more resources than is needed and need the space later down the line, don't sell your primary resources (coal, wood, metal etc) as these will not fetch as much as finished items at merchants. Instead craft items and then sell these; by doing so you level up your soldiers, making them more efficient whilst making a profit.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Last Train Home is -so far- an excellent game for those who enjoy the resource management of Frostpunk, Airborne Kingdom, and styled like Foxhole, but with RTS combat elements that, while not ground-breaking in its genre, work well and are engaging enough to those who aren't too sweaty about it. Resources are scarce, but an on-the-fly difficulty adjustment means for those of you afraid of losing like myself, this game can be prevented from giving you gray hair; but you'll always be working hard to scrounge up something to get your train just a few towns further down the line.The visuals are nice and watching your train roll through the country is quite fun. The voices are well done and the story of having to traverse the entirety of Russia to get home is a compelling one.Some reviews have mentioned wonky unit actions during RTS segments, and that it worsens as the game goes on. I have encountered one or two strange moments for sure, but I was able to salvage the moment. Some balance patches and bugfixes for these niche moments may be in order.Strangely enough, every item has the same range unless you count actions, so snipers have the same range as a handgun medic. Odd. I'd like to see that change.Last Train Home is not a game I have completed. But, so far, I am enjoying it quite a lot, and have no major complaints other than niche moments where balancing or weird unit behavior have broken immersion.Also, for those of you thinking of buying, do NOT let soldiers run out of stamina! :)

_childDocuments_.review: I love playing strategy games such as the legendary Desperado's, Shadow Tactics, and Commandos. This game is somewhere in between of those with a pretty unique style which I loved as well, however some things I did not like about this game:1. Shadowing the whole map except the area where you have a crew member. (This can be accepted in a hardcore game mode, but playing normal mode should be normal).2. The game graphics is below average.3- The loading a saved game takes long time compared to the average in similar game. I mean I understand this for loading for the first time, but having to wait this long every time you get killed it's frustrating.4- Sometimes you need to fix the view cone of a particular enemy to be able to move around them or do something, but you can't do that and you need to hover your pointer on them while they are moving which makes it a bit difficult and annoying.Apart from the above, the game is pretty fun and enjoyable.
