_childDocuments_.review: From the gameplay perspective, Last Train Home provides very good combination of resource/base(train)/people management part (in this regards, it has some 11bit games like Frostpunk and This War of Mine vibes) and tactical RTS (kind of Company of Heroes, but with 3-10 soldier squad). Each of this part is entertaining by itself, but constant switching between them helps you fight with the inevitable feeling of genre saturation (something you can avoid by not playing it in one week like someone).Of course there are things that could be slightly better. For example AI of enemies is sometimes.. lets say questionable, . But it is not necesserily an issue, it more feels like some compromise to make the game "feel-good-to-play" and allows you to aproach missions in stealth as well.For technical quality, I am kind of impressed what Ashborne Games studio did just in three years. Game looks beautiful. The maps where RTS missions takes place are huge,  still unique and filled with beatifully modelled landscapes, buildings and vegetation.It is also good to mention, that during whole game I encountered only one bug, where mission goal was not triggered and I needed to restart mission. It was little annoying, but nothing terrible. Also keep in mind that I have start playing right after release, so facing only one issued feels almost like miracle.Of course I also have to mention the story. It is wotrh to mention that I was born in Czechoslovakia, so it was touching for me to listen to (well.. actually kind of be a part of) this chapter of history preceding forming our independent state. Of course, it is not a documentary and some dramatization and shortcuts were needed, still Last Train Home tells a strong story that is a good derivate of these terrible journeys on railroads. I also apreciate that you can readlittle  more about some events that happens in game in encyclopedia that is included in the game. There is also very good sound design and music that supports the overall mood of the game.I can only recommend you to buy this game. And if you are not sure if the game is for you, you can try demo - I am sure you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of Partisans 1941, Last Train Home is clearly a labor of love meant to share an important historical and cultural story. Despite some technical issues and a handful of half-baked systems, I enjoyed my time with it.The good: front and center is of course, the story. While not incredibly deep or immersive, it's an important tale nonetheless and the narrative conveys all the perils one would expect while steaming through a post-WWI country in the midst of yet another war. Secondly, the combat is FUN above all else, even if it is fairly simplistic in terms of tactics and weaponry. The control scheme is intuitive and while stealth is somewhat necessary in some parts, throwing your troops into battle and letting them do their thing is also perfectly viable. As long as the cover system is utilized, there are some epic battles to be had that are paced very well.The bad: the gameplay systems are a mile wide but an inch deep (more on that later). The map progress is linear as one would expect of a train, but after the first few hours there wasn't much variety to keep things fresh. Next, I had a number of technical issues ranging from vehicles wigging out and freezing, to troops ignoring commands. It was nothing too egregious - particularly for an indie game - but it was frustrating. Finally, the loading screens were atrocious. Playing on an SSD, each quick-load consisted of 2 different loading screens that spanned 25-30 seconds every single time. The worst: even on Challenging difficulty which is the highest preset (outside of custom difficulty settings), the game was just too easy. I'm saying that as someone who has always been painfully mediocre at RTS games. Both the combat and especially the management systems left much to be desired. After the tutorial area, I never ran low on supplies again for the rest of the my 35-hour playthrough. An abundance of fuel meant I could blast through the map at full speed and a surplus of food meant I basically didn't have to worry about rationing food. All of that is a real shame because tight resource management is half the fun in games like this. In summary, Last Train Home is a solid title. it has a fair number of issues but ultimately it accomplishes what it set out to do. It's a fun, casual experience that offers a good amount of content, even if that content does get a bit repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: This is a thumbs "meh", not "up".The combat and mission design is good, evoking both Commandos and old school Red Alert. The presentation and main story is polished, and I enjoyed all the non-english voices too.But the train management is very dull and feels like a souped up mobile game. There are constant popups and level ups and so on, most of which don't matter at all and just add a few % of improvement. This is so distracting it took me until 3/4th through the game to realize I had gotten essential skills like "camouflage" and "critical shot", which completely changed the combat.You pretty much see all the possible train encounters in chapter 1, and then you just repeat them verbatim for the entire game. Upgrading the train is just a tedious exercise in gathering resources, reassigning people, and then assigning them back to their regular job a minute later. This can lead to dumb mistakes, like leaving the artillery unmanned during an important mission. This should've been handled by having upgrades be a temporary job instead of a permanent reassignment.It's also an odd choice that the official "story cast" does not appear on the train at all. There is no "officer car" or anything, but you constantly see their portraits, and they do most of the talking on important missions. This adds to the feeling of playing several disconnected games.There are also quality of life issues that can ruin the longer combat missions. Save scumming is both necessary and tedious, and there is no auto-save even though the missions have clear arcs. Some more examples:- It's hard to tell who is selected, because the portraits just move up/down a little bit. When a group is selected, one 'main' character does all the actions, instead of e.g. the nearest squad member.- Pathfinding can be erratic and you don't see the path they will follow. Many attempts were ruined because a character went the wrong way and you constantly have to babysit their moves. When moving groups, it doesn't show you their formation at the destination. When moving a group into a bush, the game doesn't even ensure they end up _inside_ the bush.- "Silent mode" combines both "sneak", "stealth kill" and "don't shoot". If you want your soldiers to run they will also auto-shoot. If you want to hurry someone into a bush, and there is an enemy in range, they stop like an idiot and start aiming. If you are in the middle of a battle and someone is still on "silent mode", clicking the "shoot" button will cause them to crawl out and try a stealth kill. It's so very retarded in practice, this should've been different buttons. Stealth kills are also glitchy near fences and other obstacles, which adds to the problem.- No decent ambush mechanic. Soldiers will run out of cover like idiots if the target is too far instead of just waiting a few seconds. The shooting range indicator is vague and never explained, and it's confusing whether it's showing you your range or theirs.- The binoculars encourage you to scout ahead of time, but this can trigger timed events early when your characters are still too far away. This could've been fixed by just warning the player that they need to hurry, and delaying the event until they actually get close.All in all, it's a good combat game with some UX issues, combined with a dull management game that overstays its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: First the standard note: Last Train Home is a game that I consider to be a successful mix of "Frostpunk" (survival aspect), "Jagged Alliance" (squad management) and "X-Com" (home base expansion), combined with occasional real-time battles and a light "Commandos" vibe. All wrapped up in a World War I based scenario. A setting that is wonderfully fresh and works brilliantly with the game mechanics.   A solid recommendation if you can overlook the weaker battles. If you're looking for a C&C game, you've come to the wrong place. But if you can get along with a shallower Jagged Alliance-like game that convinces with its setting and strong atmosphere, this AA title offers a great adventure for a more than reasonable price.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the movie "Dr Zhivago" (David Lean's 1965 masterpiece starring Omar Sharif, Julie Christie, and Geraldine Chaplin) and one of my favorite sequences in the movie is when they are travelling by train through the steppe to relocate due to the Russian Civil War; while traveling, Zhivago meets one of his old acquaintances, Pasha Antipov, better known as Strelnikov (superbly played by Tom Courtenay), a ruthless Red Army Commissar, who could execute him, but decides to let him go. That whole adventure on the train, surrounded by wilderness and peril both from Reds and Whites, always fascinated me. I must say that this game brings me back to that masterpiece, with a little known episode of the end of World War I involving the Czech Legion, formed by former Austro-Hungarian POWs that fought for the Allies in exchange for guarantees from Czar Nicholas II to allow the creation of Czechoslovakia after the war. The Legion was a neutral unit in the Russian Civil War and was to cross Siberia to reach Vladivostok and there board a boat that would take them back home ("to go West, you must go East"). This game brings back this historical episode to life, and is similar to Frostpunk and This War of Mine (in the gathering of resources) with some squad-based combat. The train management part is pretty good; for the combat part, I would have preferred a turn-based combat, but that's a personal preference, since I do not like RTS fighting. A bonus is that you get to kill Bolsheviks and (almost) save the Russian imperial family, Do yourself a favor and immerse yourself in this great episode of Russian History. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: This game is solid all the way around. It's very friendly to people who may be getting into the genre for the first time, having both an in-game difficulty slider you can use at any point in time if you're being overwhelmed, and a pause system in place during the combat portion of the game(to let you properly plan out and place your units for mission and it's objectives). There are very few bugs I ran into during my play-through, and some of them have already been addressed and fixed. The Dev team for this game are clearly invested beyond just making a game, and aiming more for creating a full experience. The most annoying bug I ran into was dead soldiers still being registered as live soldiers, losing all their morale and deserting, causing the morale of my entire train to plummet. This bug did not break the game for me as I still managed to keep morale pretty high at all times. The story is amazingly done, I'm not a historian, so I'm not going to comment on the authenticity of the story, but I know the game definitely nailed the WW1 vibe, allowing for a pretty immersible experience( I actually felt bad for my crew as more and more things happened). This is definitely one of its strongest feature, the story rich, roller coaster this game can put you on is worth experiencing all on its own but the combat and resource management of the game add a very good layer that keeps you engaged in real time decisions. I don't write reviews very often but this game struck me as one that I really wanted to on. Amazing game, Amazing Experience, Amazing work by the devs. Hats off to the whole team, you did a phenomenal job and I will keep and eye for games coming from them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Little bit of a learning curve to understand some of the management scheme....but after an hour and maybe a fresh restart 3 hours in to learn from mistakes makes a huge difference. The combat is good once you also learn how best to work with your squad. Cover, concealment and setting up kill zones with machine gunners can be very rewarding if done correctly. _childDocuments_.review: I'm really glad I bought the game and plan to buy the DLC as well. If you don't know if the game is your cup of tea, try the free DEMO, which is long enough to find out. The only downside was that after buying the full game I had to replay all the missions from the trial version.I really like the theme and the time in which the game is set. The execution of the game is in the manner of Company of Heroes in terms of combat. Then there is the element of taking care of your train which you must not run or it will affect the abilities of your crew which must be taken care of. She may be incapacitated due to fatigue or poor morale, injured, or some members you just need on the train. A very strong element that I recommend to follow are the abilities and characteristics of the crew, which are really worth using because they can strongly influence, for example, prices in trading or provide a bonus when finding raw materials.When playing, it's really not worth rushing and completing missions by fighting. Over time, the game increases in difficulty and will show you that using the stealth method (which is really primitive) pays off. Not only will you save a lot of health for the crew, but you can also get some good ingredients thanks to it.If you expose the crew to frequent damage, what happens is that the crew member gets a marked status that cannot be healed and has reduced abilities until the end of the game and is practically disadvantageous to you. I also recommend investing resources in the thermal insulation and heating of the train from the beginning of the game, because as the game progresses, cold becomes a big problem and you don't have so much material to upgrade later on.+ Original theme+ Gameplay+ Story and Voice acting+ Graphics + Train management+ Multiple ways to complete mission+ Crew atributes and perks which are worth using+ Stealth mode + The possibility of using cannons, tanks and vehicles+ Reasonable price+ Variety of missions- Stealth mode is very simple - Enemies are quite dumb

_childDocuments_.review: Everything, from the presentation to the gameplay is exceptional. It is easily one of the best single player RTS experiences in the past decade. I do have a couple of not so minor complaints though:1) The post tutorial difficulty spike. To put it bluntly, the developers heavily over corrected when it comes to the difficulty. After you reach the city of Penza, the game abruptly gets significantly more challenging. Whereas preciously you would at most be dealing with groups of a dozen or so schmucks with bolt action rifles, you are now forced to regularly contend with groups of up to 30, with about half of them typically being specialists.2) Riflemen are too weak. To put it bluntly, the riflemen become obsolete incredibly fast. They have some neat abilities, but broadly speaking, they are outclassed in every way by other roles. Medics can provide a roughly comparable amount of damage output at a lower cost, while simultaneously making nearby units harder to hit. Grenadiers can do much the same, while doing more damage and providing anti armour capabilities. Machine gunners can force entire groups of enemies to hunker down at will, as well as providing as much fire support as three riflemen. Lastly, scouts are just as capable at stealthily eliminating targets as the riflemen, while also being able to instakill any infantry unit without even leaving cover. As it stands, they are quite literally just a temporary steping stone to other classes, with almost zero mid-late game viability.3)  ”Hmm? ...Must have been the wind”. In case you don't get it, the stealth is insanely janky. It is not only possible, but exceedingly easy to wipe out entire group of enemies one by one simply by sitting in a bush and repeatedly stabbing anyone that comes to investigate the death throes of your prior victims. 4) The game tends to break its own rules. A lot of combat encounters go South out of nowhere because the game just sorta wants them to. A particular example would be a minor mission near the start of the post tutorial area. After ambushing some soldiers that were digging a mass grave, one of them shouted something about not letting the squad get away. The encounter played out fairly normally, until suddenly, a large group of enemies seemingly materialised behind the squad. Apparently, that voice line triggered a sizeable patrol that would have normally been nowhere near close enough to notice the gunfire, leading to me taking several injuries whereas I really shouldn't have. The game is very good, but it definitely has some rough edges.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An enjoyable (albeit conservative) mix of genres that leaves the source material to do a lot of the heavy lifting.If you are interested in or intrigued by the topic, you will get a lot more mileage out of this game than someone who is here purely for the gameplay.As a whole, the game feels more wide than deep. The systems (train resource management, soldier level progression, real time battles, research etc.) are rather simple on their own, though when combined, there is a lot moving parts to manage – some of which are rather cumbersome. The game rarely tries anything particularly original or surprising. On the other hand, it looks nice, sounds great and runs okay.The real time battles feel like a more polished and streamlined version of Men of War minus the jank (well, most of it anyway).If you are looking for a game that excels at a particular thing, be it resource management, tactical battles or anything between, there are likely better options. That said, Last Train Home does a little bit of everything just about well enough to keep your attention until the end of its story.

_childDocuments_.review: Without writing an essay, this game feels like a beta. AI, combat, management, and many other aspects all seem half baked. You have to fight the menus to organise your men, manually moving people around and reassigning them far more than you should have to. Combat is super lackluster, and no one can hit the broad side of a barn. When they do manage to land a shot, the target just tanks it. I don't know what's expected when you're fighting wolves, because you can't really shoot on the run, and your characters just stand there and get mauled to death, so you end up swapping out who's taking the damage since they can't act on their own. Again, everything looks and feels very wooden. Each firearm is locked into specific roles, so you can't just hand them out freely, which seems wrong for the type of game this tries to be. You can't rename the train cars to organise things to your liking, like having a better labelled infantry cart just for the squads.Don't get me wrong; the game seems fine enough, but it's these small things and many others that turn me off and make it hard to recommend. If the game goes on sale for 75% off or more, maybe it's worth it if you don't mind looking past the imperfections.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun historical fiction! This game is part X-COM RTS tactics, part resource management, part RPG story. Set in the beginning of the Russian Civil War, in the closing days of WWI, you play a Czechoslovakian commander, leading the Czechoslovak Legion. Look up this group if you haven't, they're a historical entity from this time period. To summarize immensely, they're ethnic Czechs and Slovaks who rose up and fought with the Entente in WWI and the White Army in the Russian Civil War. They commanded the Trans-Siberian Railway, and that's where this game takes place: on the railroad.You command your train through Siberia, trying to reach the Pacific coast of Russia to sail away to safety (heading west into Europe is a no-go, as there are effectively two wars being fought between Moscow and Prague). You must manage food, fuel, and other resources to keep your Legionaries alive. The game is split into roughly two sections. The first is the resource management aspect of the train as a whole. The second part is the RTS missions. You can send your soldiers of different classes on missions for resources (and there's a fair amount of required story missions). This is a classic top-down RTS troop-movement tactics game.The best part is that you can change the difficulty for each of these parts individually, meaning you can have difficult RTS but easier resource management, or vice versa.One issue I have with the game overall is that, for being a fairly-accurate piece of historical fiction, it does portray the Red Army as the "orcs," the unequivocal bad guys. Which is a bit one-sided but as this is from the prospective of White Army allies, it kinda makes sense.Your soldiers all have character traits that affect dialogue and rewards (and consequences) from random events, giving a fun character connection with each of your soldiers. Overall, this games strikes a great balance of gameplay, difficulty, story, and entertainment. It also tackles some pretty serious and dark events/scenarios, as this is a game about the Russian Civil War after all. I definitely recommend picking this up if you have any interest in WWI historical fiction combined with strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very novel game, almost deserving of its own genre. Set in Russia during the Bolshevik revolution, this game shines a light on history that is typically eclipsed in our media by the more well-known Western front during the same era. If I could describe this game in one sentence, I would say it's Frostpunk: Train Edition smashed together with diet CommandosI played the demo before release and I just had to get this game. Why then, don't I recommend this title? It's because at about 10 hours this game becomes boring and repetitive. The demo covers very well what the game is like, but this means that beyond that there's nothing more to explore. There are two major points I want to highlight that made me quit playing. The first is centered on combat, the second has to do with points of interest on the grand strategy campaign map.The combat is like the commandos/desperadoes series, in that it's basically a real time tactics game with an emphasis on stealth. Enemies have a view cone that you have to avoid in order not to be detected. Stealth is important because you want to keep your squad healthy and you can get the most resources this way. So what's the issue here? Well unlike the games I mentioned previously, it doesn't have the same intricacies, depth and refinement. The AI behaves in a completely immersion-breaking way, the only way to kill somebody stealtily is with a melee attack, enemy view cones can sometimes view through multiple layers of trees and bushes, if you bayonet a howitzer or a machine gun it magically explodes and much more. It's unfair to expect it to be as good or expansive as the games marketed as real time tactics, but they didn't improve upon the concept since they released the demo. Which is a major fail in my book because this game is almost six months old.The best way to quickly play this without having to do the chore that is stealth, is simply get a guy who can run real fast to alert all of the enemies, then try to kite them into a killzone. The thing is... if you run away the enemies sort of forget it ever happened and continue doing whatever they were doing. Another way to play it, but requires a bit more micro, is to load your team with 1 medic, 1 grenadier and fill the rest up completely with riflemen, then just overload your enemies. They still need like 5 seconds to see that there's 12 angry Czechs charging at them, so you can just abuse the AI that way. The only obstace at that stage are entrenched machine guns, and you can deal with those by throwing grenades at them or just avoiding them. Thing is, missions tire out your men fast, and soon your crew will be as tired as you are from having to play these missions. Because yes, some missions are avoidable, but most are not.So imagine my reaction when during a particular mission, I spotted an empty armored car with not one, but TWO machine guns. Yes I could occupy it it! Finally I thought; I could use this vehicle to kill some scummy Red commisar on the other end of the map... only to discover it functions basically like a reskinned static machine gun, even down to how it fires. Seeing an armored car pivot on the spot like a merry-go-round was hilarious initially, until I learned that I can't actually drive the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing from point A to point B. Or better yet, take it with me on a separate train cart for future missions. Wasted potential.As should be obvious from what I've written above, the combat roles are also restrictive. There are about two abilities per role, with 5 roles in total. So you have your medic, your riflemen, your sniper, your grenadier and your machine gunner. The machine gunner is a waste, because of how much ammo he consumes and how much time he needs to set up. Medics have obvious uses. Grenadier is good but grenades are in limited supply... so that leaves about two classes that are always useful, the sniper and the riflemen. The riflemen because he has... wel a rifle, that is actually the best and most ammo-efficient weapon. And he can instagib enemies with a bayonet charge. The sniper because he can use his binoculars to reveal an area in the fog of war, and additionally he can throw stones to distract enemies... Which made me think: Why don't other classes have this ability? And why can't I bonk-bonk a stone on somebody's head and take them out in a stealthy-sneaky manner from range? Also why doesn't he have sniper shot ability in the first place? I thought the point of having a sniper rifle was to take targets out from afar. Instead it functions like a slower-firing carbine, with a slightly higher range. Aside from the actual combat, I also take issues with the grand campaign map. The actual train sim is fine, moving the train about is fun and there's strategical decisionmaking involved. Stopping the train is dangerous because the Red Army is out on a hunt for you, so if you do have to stop, you'd want to use that precious time to upgrade your train, like outfitting your infantry carts with heating to warm your soldiers or applying armor plates to your locomotive. The bad part is scouring for resources. Sure it's fun for the first 10 hours, but after that you realize that almost every point of interest is the same, with the same copy-pasted text and an x amount of resources that you get. There are only a handful of points of interest that have an extra narrative, but it's mostly one of the following few scenarios1. A forest that you can scout for food and wood2. An abondoned Russian ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you can scour for fuel and cloth3. A lake in which you can fish4. A town with a merchant (either a food merchant or a gun merchant)5. A larger town/city (typically with a merchant / train depot / maybe a pub)The points of interest are typically resolved by sending a squad there, who then either have to solve a dilemma or need time to scavenge (sometimes both) If they had wanted to keep my interest, they need to have drastically increased the amount of different PoI this game has to offer, with more dilemmas, images and flavour texts. When, completing chapter 3, I entered a new map with an even longer train track, dotted entirely with the exact same PoIs i had explored a dozen times before at that stage, I decided I've had enough. I was 10 hours in and had completed maybe 20% of my journey: No thanks. So yes, extremely promising game, but quite a let down in the end. I would have at least expected that they fixed combat by this point, but they didn't. That would have made the rest of the game bearable at least. Since they don't seem to be doing that, and that they have already released a DLC for this game, means that it doesn't get a recommend out of me. It's a real shame too, because I tried hard liking this game and they certainly put in effort when it comes to the presentation, I mean the real life footage of the trains and soldiers is magnificent.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game since it was announced, it looked great and I love the time period.And yet I can't bring myself to like it. What follows is my longest review to date and one big rant, you've been warned.TLDR Stategy layer 7/10, tactical layer 0/10 = 3.5/10 in total, just let me skip the combatThe goodTrain management, artstyle and the mapThe bad: The game wants you to stealth (cause injuries and using ammo is bad) and so despite the combat being good (although it would seem that directional cover is not working cause a soldier wide open to a flank is somehow dodging every shot) you are practically forced to stealth. Which revolves around sitting in a bush and stabbing every bypasser. The characters lack any stealth abilities and AI is extremely unaware, not that there is anything to be aware of cause I guess legionnaires send every dead enemy to the other dimension leaving no body behind. So instead of fun combat you are left with a half-baked chore of a system. (If you want tactics with guns may I suggest Partisans 1941 stealth there is WAY better): Bit of a mixed bag: Czechs are voiced ok-good, enemies might have as well been voiced by google translate: I love the Legion and hate the reds, yet even for me the game was so black and white that it seems like an understatement. Cause LITERALLY every Russian you meet is either a grieveng mother/grandma or the most punch-able person ever, while the Czechs might as well be saints. Like I get it, CURRENT EVENTS, but it's a history game ffs.: The game has no idea what to be, it tries to show that it's gritty and dark with it's plot, yet missions are written with jokes and banter straight out of a B-movie. It honestly just feels in bad taste.: Mixed point again: love the backstories and portraits, but can't bring myself to care, which I really expected from this game. There are too many characters with them being different in stats and perks only.  I get the necessity for scale so can't really blame the devs here.: Almost forgot and I really can't. The game has perks that are needed for events, right? So you should make a squad with people with these perks, right? So it should be EASY to find them, right? WRONG, you have to click through EVERY SINGLE ONE OF YOUR SOLDIERS TO FIND THE PERKS YOU NEED, WHY? (almost lost my cool): Now I don't want to say it's on purpose but you are properly introduced to stealth around 2+ hours into the game and it REALLY makes me think first of all thanks, second the game has potential but the stuff above is so fundamentally buggered there is no hope :(PS Steam pls be merciful and give me a refund

_childDocuments_.review: My wife's great-grandfather was a member of the Czechoslovak Legion. He made the trip to Vladivostok which this game is about. He kept a diary, over 250 pages of it. From what I've read, I can attest that: the Bolsheviks (Red Army) were utter savages. They pillaged, looted, raped, murdered. They were also very stupid in their military tactics. Because they never valued human life, even of their own, they would undertake absurd and suicidal missions that made no sense. They got obliterated by the Legion on many occasions because of it. Brainwashed Russians can't swallow the truth even today. During the Soviet period they created a massive disinformation campaign to discredit the Legion. But make no mistake, this game is historically very accurate.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. It tells a often forgotten story of the Czechoslovak Legion. Its a fascinating game with a great story line. Just be ready because this game is brutal. Its frostpunk but with combat. The combat is generally engaging but the stealth portion is broken as enemies (realistically) change their patrol patterns. While realistic this is unsuitable to a game as its impossible to be stealthy for really any period of time as its impossible to plan your movement. One moment a guard walks around a building and the next they change the pattern and retrace their steps out of nowhere thus seeing you soldier sneaking up on them. It makes stealth frustrating. Combat itself is fine except for machine gun emplacements. They are extremely difficult to deal with. While realistic, having enemies like that that knock your troops down in a single burst while also having them out range all of your troops means its just a slog where you will lose most of your troops to one machine gun. Its just impossible to "use tactics" against such enemies as the bayonet charge just hits the gun itself not the enemy controlling it, your handheld machine guns dont have the range, and your grenades cant be thrown long enough. Even with the combat issues and stealth issues the game is a solid choice especially for its price

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal, one of my first RTS games and I absolutely adore it. I brought them to the edge of the zone we were defending, and with only seconds left in the assault I had them hold their positions under tank fire to prevent red infantry from capturing. _childDocuments_.review: My great-grandparents fled Bohemia just prior to WWI - so, this game was, to me, a fascinating look at those who stayed behind in what would eventually become a most tumultuous period in the Czech and Slovak history.  Playing it was a personal gift, but for you?  I still think Last Train Home is worth the ride.It isn't for EVERYONE, naturally - so, what is it?  This game is a well-thought-out and engaging "city builder", in that you have to manage the condition and upgrades of your train cars, development of your soldiers, and even toggle their responsibilities between military roles, and the train-related jobs found such as engineers, workers (shoveling coal and maintenance), doctors, and cooks.  Resource management is essential, giving this title a survival angle that works perfectly in context with the subject matter.  Often, you'll be stopping your train to send out military sorties in hopes of making a trade, or scavenging off the land for additional food, coal, or lumber.Then, there's combat.  It is real-time with a pause mechanic, but frontal assaults rarely work, and this doesn't play like an RTS.  Instead, each military map feels like a puzzle to solve.  Honestly, more of the DNA of Last Train Home's combat comes from turn-based titles such as X-Com.  Challenging, but not enervating.The story is exciting - your troops want to go home, but are stuck in the middle of a civil war between the remnants of the provisional Russian government (the White Guard) and the budding Soviet revolutionaries (the "Reds").  Neutrality isn't honored, the Reds see you as a dangerous armed adversary, and hence, the concept of the game emerges - your train needs to travel across the entirety of Russia, all the way to the coast of Vladivostok, to take a boat back west.  To your young home, Czechoslovakia.In short, I think this game is a keeper.  Hats off to Ashborne Studios.  I'll be watching their next project with interest.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game on sale for $25 and that is the highest price I could recommend the game at.This game suffers from some serious issues in terms of the combat. Fundamentally, your soldiers are just pawns on the board and they will attack whatever happens to enter their combat range. They have abilities they can use based on their class and will unlock a few new ones as they level up, though I've found that trying to use their abilities generally gets them killed faster than if they simply free fire at enemies. The cover system in this game is offensively unpolished. You can't get into cover behind buildings or around the corner of one. Buildings also cannot be entered which is a confusing omission. You can only use something waist high as cover, like a fence or pile of logs. This presents a bit of an issue as you can rarely get a squad of more than 3 people into cover near each other to where they can all hit the enemies you are in combat with.The aggro range of enemies is also very very short. If they are outside the fog of war, they usually won't get alerted to your position and continue their patrol. This makes fights rather boring as you won't have to hold a position or move soldiers as more enemies enter the fight. Just move your guys and let them shoot until the fight is over. Reveal the map using the scout's binocular ability, rinse and repeat until the mission is over.The missions are pretty hit or miss as well. They're generally just a large map with some enemies sparsely sprinkled around. It gets tiring if objectives want you to run back and forth over a large area. You'll have a main objective and some optional side objectives. The optional objectives usually just boil down to fetch quests. Not very interesting or inspired. The train management is fine, nothing to write home about. Just some very basic resource management and random events. It works for what it is, not sure how to make it better but it feels one note for what was marketed as a key aspect of the game.All in all, for $25 it's fine. Try it out if you're curious, but don't expect a super polished or engaging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it a lot. the game is very entertaining so far and it seems there is still a lot ahead. Within its single components, as for instance the real time tactic map (with its battle and stealth elements), base building (the train), rpg elements (i.e. leveling soldiers and workers), overall strategic map and decision making are all good not great. The combination of each element and the interesting overall story make sit a great game for me. I am not sure about the long run, if it will be still similar fun and entertaining the next 20 hours or so (I assume thats the amount of time i will need to finish my first game). I also cannot say anything about replayability yet - there is some chance for alternate approaches and decisions, so a second run might be possible. On the negative side: The game ask you to do mainly stealth runs in the tactical battles...for me its fine and a challenging fun. Anyhow, it is a bit strange that killed enemies are just disappearing and based on that there is a low risk of other living enemies sounding an alarm (unless they see you) --- this is a bit far away from the reality. there shopuld be a need to remove the dead bodies. For hardcore rts/stealth players (not me), this might be a real issue. So far I only experienced a grafic error/bug once, but nothing dramatic. The game is running smooth without any disturbance yet. Awesome game, i can recommend to buy it if you love the above described game components.

_childDocuments_.review: I am Czech. I am a history buff and I love this game. Right up my alley with the mood, theme, gameplay and everything. The live action scenes are absolutely superb and completely absorb you into the story. You will create a relationship with your soldiers over time and the story that unfolds is an amazing experience. Congratulations to Ashborne for creating such an amazing piece of art and game. There are of course some things I would love to see changed or improved. Firstly, the vertical fighting doesn't work well - I got into situations where enemies could shoot me from below, but my soldiers couldn't shoot down from a bridge. Next up are some little inconsistencies with breaking sneaking mode. Sometimes a stealth kill puts you out of stealth, sometimes it won't break it. Same goes with synced shots. Probably my biggest complaint would be the speed of or rather the absence of quick load. The game is sometimes very complex and I just wanna try if something works and load the game quickly if it doesn't. Loading the game takes quite some time. I would also like to rename squads or at least colour them or change icons.This game is definitely worth your time and money even if you're not really into the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10.This game has a very enjoyable story and if you enjoy the gameplay of Desperado's III, you will enjoy LTH's gameplay. The train management is a cool aspect along with all the solider management. However, I do feel like it can be a bit too "micro" management for my liking. I'm ~10 hours in and I still feel like I don't understand some of the soldier management stuff. Also, the actual gameplay feels...unrealistic? Why it takes 8 rank 3+ soldiers ~5+ seconds to kill one person standing the open 10 feet away is beyond me. Not a perfect game but it is very enjoyable and the maps are very well thought out and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first got this game a lot of people seemed to compare it to Frostpunk. I don't think this comparison is fair at all. I mean not to say this game is bad, it isn't I'll get to that.The Frostpunk angle seems to be brought up repeatedly for it's comparrisons to "bleakness" and "cold" obviously. But while Frostpunk is a fictional game about surviving the big freeze, Last Train Home is a fictional WW1 inspired story about a desperate escape.If I were to compare it to anything... It'd be a sorta Company of Heroes (The first one) meets This War of Mine.The RTS side of things might not be SUPER in depths compared to some other games. But the whole vibe, feel and emotion it gets across in it's story is a major factor for this game. Based on that alone, if it's at all the sorta thing you're in to, buy it. For a story focussed RTS it's the best thing to come out in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where we try to lead Czech legions from Moscow to Vladivostok while managing resources and people. Since we will be using the Trans-Siberian railroad, the game reminds us of Frostpunk with its harsh road conditions.  The fact that each soldier in the game has a character reminded me of Oxygen Not Included. Soldiers have jobs that they are predisposed to, some are more inclined to be laborers, while others have the skills needed to fight. We can say that our structure of using soldiers in missions is similar to games like comandos and desparados. At the end of the day, we can call it a game where we collect resources, improve our train and fight enemies on our way to Vladivostok to avoid problems in Siberia.If I count the good things about the game, for those who like games like desparados, comandos, etc., the game is fun to throw a stone and attack secretly behind the enemy. People who will not get bored even if they play hours of tactical play should buy this game. This is the strongest part of the game.If I count the negative aspects of the game, Siberia will be cold, resources are important tension is created. But you realize how unnecessary this tension is during the journey. The Trans-Siberian railroad is about 9000 km. I reached half of the way in 25-30 days. When I reached half of the way, I had about 40 days of food.  Although I didn't try to collect any food supplies in the last 2 chapters, I had enough food for 60 days by giving full meals to the soldiers.  That's why I didn't stop at places where food could be found anymore.Another important resource is coal, which you need both for heating and to keep the train moving. When I arrived in Siberia I had so much coal that I could have traveled from Moscow to Vladivostok without ever collecting coal again.In general, the tension that Siberia is cold and we need food and coal was pointless.The artificial intelligence of the enemies we fought in missions was very bad, there were enemies that did not react even though the enemy in their field of view was killed.I played the game on normal difficulty, I would like to point this out. If I knew it would be this easy, I would have played it on a harder setting. But I'm not sure if I'll play it a second time in a short time.Although it was less challenging, I enjoyed playing it due to its tactical aspect.Thank you to everyone who contributed. I hope you achieve greater success in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Although I am still pretty much at the beginning (only 3 combat missions played), I really love how atmospheric the game is so far. It also covers a very interesting part of history that I was personally only little aware of and that I am now starting to read more about, i.e., the Czechoslovak Legion and corresponding events after the revolution in Russia in October / November 1917.We are the commander of a small group of legionnaires, traveling east on an armored train towards Vladivostok. All of the legionnaires have their own personalities and desires, and we need to try to keep up morale, while violence increasingly erupts during the journey. We must also take more and more tough decisions, e.g., whether we should take (or even steal) food from civilians who barely have enough themselves to survive.The game is superb in illustrating the poverty, the sorrows, and despair during these times and as such is similar to titles like 'This war of mine'. From a tactical-combat and management  perspective, I would say that it is also somewhat similar to the 'Jagged Alliance' series. Thus, if you like this type of genre, rich storytelling, and a setting that appears to be largely inspired by historic events, 'Last Train Home' might be a great fit. Obviously, it still has some flaws though. For instance, in one mission, the Red Army receives reinforcements, and from an animation standpoint, it does not look like that the troops are actually moving their feet, but are more being pulled forward on an imaginary line. Soldiers periodically also collide with invisible objects and get stuck. All in all though, the game runs very stable, and I have not faced any crashes yet either.In sum, I think the developers really did an amazing job, and it feels like a lot of love was invested into the game. The art is fantastic in my opinion. Really, kudos from my side!
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Train Home is not just a video game; it's an immersive experience that seamlessly blends captivating storytelling, stellar voice acting, and innovative game mechanics to create a truly unforgettable journey.First and foremost, the voice acting in The Last Train Home is nothing short of exceptional. Every character's voice is not just a reflection of their personality but a conduit that draws players deeper into the game's rich narrative. The emotional nuances conveyed through the voices add a layer of authenticity that elevates the gaming experience to new heights. The cast's performances are so convincing that you'll find yourself emotionally invested in their fates, creating a profound connection that lingers long after the game is over.The storytelling in The Last Train Home is a masterclass in narrative design. The game weaves a complex and intriguing plot that keeps players on the edge of their seats from start to finish. The pacing is impeccable, offering a perfect balance between suspenseful moments and quieter, character-driven scenes that allow players to connect with the protagonists on a personal level. The narrative unfolds organically, revealing twists and turns that will leave you gasping in awe and eagerly anticipating what happens next.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying this game and can recommend it.On the overworld map it is squad management game with mobile base (upgrade the train, select abilities for soldiers), and within missions it feels like commandos with slightly worse QoL features (compared to games like shadow tactics - there is little information about partial cover visibility, distance to which one's steps can be heard or enemy alertness timing).However, it is in marrying of these multiple layers where this game truly shines - material captured and bullets spent in tactical maps have implications on the management/base upgrade layer.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A very good survival RTS where you take a journey across Siberia post WW1 during the Russian Revolution and the rise of the Soviets. Very difficult with the resource management. However, there are several difficulty settings that can make the game easier, including a story mode if you just want the story. The voice acting is in the native tongue and I recommend it and you can have subtitles in multiple languages of your choosing.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I had written a positive review after being half way through the game that had a lot of caveats (and would have been a neutral one, if steam allowed for that). However after finishing the game I have to change my recommendation to a "thumbs-down".The game is by no means a rip-off, it is priced fairly. But the only thing that carries this game is the scenario, because gameplay-wise it doesn't offer enough. Playing on the highest difficulty neither the tactical missions nor the strategical train management offer any challenge. In the beginning you think both things will get harder, but the opposite is true:Tactical missions: After your soldiers level up you will find that you can just sprint across the map and shoot everybody without stealthing or even taking cover (apart from very few choke points, but you have artillery strikes for those). I've dreaded the tactical missions in the last third of the game, because even though the game creators tried to mix up the mission design, the limited gameplay makes every mission feel the same.Strategy layer: In the beginning it is really exciting to prepare for Siberia, because you always ask yourself: Am I truly ready for the hardest stretch? That is until you realize that even on the hardest diffculty there is no survival aspect at all. If you do your tactical missions and harvest the ressource notes on the map you will have literally more ressources than your train can carry when entering siberia. My train arrived in Vladivostok with enough fuel, food, weapons and money to win the war in Europe - not once was there a dicy situation while managing the train. Unfortunately the game really falls short of what it could have been and comes apart after you figure out that there are very little things you truly need to consider.. I really wanted to love this game, but there just isn't enough there.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A neat game in a rather niche setting. A mix between a "settlement" management sim and an RTS, without going too deep into either. Engaging story with some replayability value, plus there's a Legion Tales DLC that gives you separate missions with lots of challenges to try. Mild historical inaccuracies but nothing that would irk me too much. Fortunately, both Reds and Whites are being shown here as the backstabbing evil they actually were so I'm content on this. The game has good art, good music, authentic voiceovers in Czech as well, I enjoyed playing with that on. Sometimes there were small bugs like bad pathfinding or soldiers getting stuck in cover or a tree - but it's all minor stuff.But overall I recommend Last Train Home if you like the "road movie" kind of stories and are interested in the WW1 setting. Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem that has flown under a lot of people's radars (and really has for the past month since its release). The management of your train and soldiers in/out of battle is a comfortable blend that tests your skills as a commander of a Legion making their way across a war-divided landscape of Russia that keeps your attention locked in without feeling overbearing about any one particular thing. Just now about halfway through Chapter 3 and the plot is getting interesting with all of the choices I have made so far. Interested to see what the team will release in the upcoming future with their "Tales of the Legion" announcement
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I´ve done two plays,  one playthrough and combining the management of the train ride and the tactical of the combat scenarios is a fun mix. Although on "normal" difficulty not that taxing. Most combat can be done by sneeking around with a sniper once it is good enough to get the distracting stone. And the hardest part of the train ride was the cold of Sibiera, I´m glad I had that idea from the start even if other things was more interesting at the time to upgrade.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Skvělá strategie z naší historieNice strategy with great story inspired by real eventPlays bit like mix of Frostpunk, Banner Saga and Dawn of War. Some lines sound bit flat and some hillarious but audio is great, so is 2D art, 3D is okay for RTS. Most of negative reviews is because of all factions being somewhat questionable and Reds playing antagonist in story or AI being dumber than average Russian. With bugs (dec2023) it's bit russian roulette. For me it was just some failing achievements and funny frames, some had easy sailing and some had crashes or serious bugs needing troubleshooting. It's still shortly after release and devs seem to be interested in fixing it.Also some tips for you:
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly Good combat, feels like what a good realtime XCOM would feel if it had a baby with early Company of Heroes and a little pinch of Men of War. The game is highly customizable to your liking and pretty much everything from the enemy difficulty to resource management can be adjusted to your liking. The voice acting is very authentic for all three languages involved. That being said. naming your narrator thr "Historian" and then starting the first hour of the game demonizing the soviets for wanting to disarm you when you started this whole conflict by starting an armed assault on Hungarian POW's and then storming a Soviet headquarters after some of your men got arrested is just plain silly. But you wouldn't know that if your only source of history is this game, they much preferred the Company of Heroes 2 approach of depicting Soviets murdering civilians for ABSOLUTELY no reason instead. Overall I highly recommenf it's been one of the most surprising games this year!
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: So far, seems to be a fantastic entry in the squad-based RTSwP genre. Great story, wonderful VO work, gorgeous environments and solid action. It's like a mix of Frostpunk meets Company of Heroes meets Men of War or Iron Harvest. Having a great time so far and the detailed mechanics of taking care of soldiers, the train AND trying to stay alive and finding out if I'm' going to actually make a difference in these lives is wonderfully entertaining and historically accurate for the most part. Looking forward to finishing this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about the Czechslovakian Brigade trapped in Russia during the civil war and having to escape to Vladivostok by train across Siberia from history. This wonderful game captures that experience. It has that slavic esthetic, which I have come to enjoy. I liked that I could listen to the dialogue in Czech/Slavokian with English subtitles. The game is based on a novel written by the second-in-command of the Brigade.There was a good balance between collecting resources, improving the train, and combat situations. I improved all the cars by building the best heating available. I was dismayed that almost everyone became ill when the cold came. I forgot to turn the heat on! The battle missions are interesting as one can choose what specialists you want on your team. The game is quite linear, going from west to east, though there are two detour choices. I would play it again, anyway. I can't think of anything negative about it. 90/100
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A solid survival strategy with a rogue-like feel, with the combat missions feeling like a light version of Company of Heroes.The train feels limiting at first but carefully managing your resources and having constant pressure to move in one direction - wherever the tracks take you - is somewhat the point!It's truly great to learn about the more hidden corners of history through a genuinely rich and engaging experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Fighting battles knowing that the injuries your soldiers take will affect the rest of your run for the rest of the game makes the combat significantly more intense than it would be otherwise, especially with how easy it is for soldiers to get downed in this game. It also makes collecting resources for your troops and train feel substantial and rewarding instead of tedious. Not even 1/3 through the game but this is shaping up to be one of my favorite RTS games. Also the setting is really cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: If you like This War of Mine, Aliens Dark Descent, and other survival / resource management games, you'll probably like this. The story is very good. Combat with the ability to pause to queue up squad actions is nice. I haven't found it too repetitive as some reviewers have said--not any moreso than most games are after you play for a long time.Probable the games biggest weakness is that the UI and menus are not very user friendly or intuitive. I find myself clicking around more than should be necessary to see the necessary info. But that's a minor complaint, and the game is very fun overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: For a strategy game I'm quite happy with how it plays. This is what I have to report after 12 hours of gameplay.It's got a nice card-based strategy element to keeping your characters alive, happy and rested. It gives useful perks to keeping my crew alive and getting more, as appose to culling them to get an ideal crew. This trade off leads to more food to feed and less cabin to store them in, but more opportunities.  The stealth could use some work. The "huh what's that" stealth is fine, I guess, but it leads to me weaving my troop in and out of an enemies line of sight to move him out of position instead of something more creative. The combat is fine. Position your troops so they get a competitive advantage and use limited resources to get an edge in combat, like machine gun volley, or grenades. And some other problems...-Grenadiers randomly will decide not to throw their grenade if they travel a few feet to throw it. I've had this happen twice, and it's gotten them killed by firing at the enemy instead of throwing the grenade. -Troops who have enemies slightly out of their range and are targeted to said enemies will move out of their cover to target that enemy. Is it so hard for them to just, shoot at the enemy with less accuracy? Why didn't anybody think of that for this strategy-cover based game? Especially when all troops have very similar para scopes, I find it useless putting my scouts behind my other troops because they straight up won't shoot despite having rifles. -Bayonet charge won't work on a turret if it turns. If it turns around, your bayonet charge will simply slice at air and die to the machine gunner. Why was this in the tutorial if it isn't going to work as intended?-Characters who are stealth mode won't move away from enemies line of sight, instead choosing the fastest route to get somewhere. I can understand this, but why would you have them move outside of the bushes to get to another spot in the bushes? It's super counter intuitive.-Cant tell when a character is in melee or shooting. I've had characters straight up kissing the opponent and I'll mark him to attack, he'll reload his gun in front of the enemy, and get shot in the process. -Camera zoom is very limiting. I don't have to only see my troops 24/7, what if I want to periscope out to move them somewhere else, or have a better job seeing all the way around my troops instead of being so zoomed in. You'd think this would be a fine workaround but sometimes you'll be facing enemies on both ends, and pausing constantly on each end to time abilities and movement is super time consuming. -Characters randomly won't stealth kill in tall grass. They'll walk up to the enemy, stare at him in the face, (spamming to stab kill now....) and then they'll be found and killed.Anyway, good game so far. I hope the combat and keeping people alive simulator doesn't get repetitive. And that I don't lose any more 30 minute battles to stupid bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: >your superior commanders "we must remain neutral in this conflict">literally 5 minutes later "okay now kill an entire village full of red soldiers and cripple their logistics by artillery shelling their trucks"also story:>"oh no the red army is taking food from those farmers">we just literally looted the same burning building of food and left the old lady to starveI expected this to show the horrors of war and maintain a the neutral stance about the conflict, but the game seems to lean  on portraying the Red army as the Big Bad of the story, especially since your Nemesis is a comically evil looking smug Red Army commander who looks more like a star wars antagonist and follows you throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A more polished, and in some ways easier version of Partisans 1941, which itself was... wait for it... a real time with tactical pause RTT/S, with an XCOM base/day system, Commandos inspired stealth, and Company of Heroes combat. It's a mish mash and it's very ambitious. It plays well, it's cozy, there are consequences, but for seasoned players, it might be at times too easy even on the hardest difficulty with DEFAULT modifiers, you can make it super unfair if you desire. The traits for scavenging and combat are cool, but I do kinda miss the tech tree from Partisans, tech trees seem to mostly be for train upgrades, I also dearly miss the inventory jenga inspired by Commandos/Diablo/Silent Storm etc. but that's okay (what's less okay is there seems to be less indoors gameplay :( ). I have finished chapter 1 which apparently only 68% of players managed to do and I assume the gameplay loop is BASICALLY established, it's just, spread out over the course of however many hours with unique resource management challenges, choices and maps to tackle. If this somehow sounds appealing I suggest buying the main game, uncertain on the DLC, it kinda looks like Last Train Home but without the train :)). One TINY complaint, the mouse camera control is floaty so you might need to resort to WASD/arrow keys for camera movement, it's not the most fast paced game out there but it can be so it is a shame, but it's less janky than I am describing by comparison to other games. It's very fun and playable. I installed the game on a crappy external hard drive and I love to quicksave/quick load, the times on it are a little slow but nothing too scary. I was a bit surprised by the FPS performance being in the 60s on ultra settings, I actually have the same GPU recommended and above the CPU requirement, but at least FPS does seem to go up if using FSR or lowering settings so that's good, but 60 is very playable. Buy it, we don't see REAL TIME XCOMs too often, it's a real gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat simplistic, the onward train is rudimentary in resolution, the trips to adventures is boring. The notion is effective, but details are not up to date or well thought out.  Not to mention, my computer freezes invariably after about 1/2 hour of play, especially when reloading a saved position.  Attempts at resolution of this problem by running in "administrator" mode or "compatibility" mode, were entirely unsuccessful.  Apart from this, though, I find the game not worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: A good game at a fair price point, it hits all metrics and scratches the RTS and simulation itch overall 8/10. Story (9/10) is superb drawing from historical events while putting its own spin on things. Game-play (8/10) is split into managing your people on the train as they navigate a harsh world trying to claw together resources in order to survive, the second part is controlling your squad in missions. A reasonable purchase at the $40 price point, I picked it up at a 25% discount. The game is good, I cannot imagine if it cooked just a little longer what the developer could have achieved.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished my first run of last train home, I have to say the game grew on me but a few sore aspects refrain me from recommending it full heartedly. In short, I feel the RTS segments should have been dropped. Its not that they are bad and some missions were genuinly fun but it feels dated. like something from a couple of years ago.   on the other hand what I feel could have been developped more; is the whole train and people management segment. What is there is good and engaging but just sits on the border of greatness. If the RTS missions had been designed as narrative questions influenced by whom you sent, that would have made it better. Like fors instance if you bring a burglar in a city mission, he notices a sneaky back alley way your other soldiers would have missed. Stuff like that to influence the mission outcome. Story wise, well the march of the legion is one of the greatest stories of tragedy and heroism in the early 20th century and I never fail to tell it to anyone i can; so I do find it a bit weird to have it seem as if all of it took place in 20 days.  Likewise, while not as clear cut anti communist as some have made it out to be; by having only the bolsjeviks as your enemy is a bit limiting. i would have loved some local bandits or outlaws in the mix, local partisans who don't trust you; stuff like that. In conclusion I had a good time with last train home but I can't shake the feeling that it could have been even better. A solid 7 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Its a mixture of resource management and RTS.The game balance is abit off so once you got the basic stuff running, it gets easy even on hardest diffculty.Most of the time, the gameplay will be about travelling hence, it tends to get repetitive with gathering items,but the sudden RTS combat missions are fun.Surprisingly, there's voice lines and live cinematic cut scene.The story is decent as its an unexplored theme/history.Overall, its enough to last you around 30 hours, not much replayability though.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but this a game that definetly deserves it. Do not expect the most complex or indeepth mechanics but they are solid and work as you would expect: stealth, vehicles, manning guns, economy, side missions... A solid 9 with plenty of hours to enjoy in just your first run (mine took around 40 hours, although most people could probably finish it faster). I just hope the developers won't stop with this game and that they will try to replicate and improve the formula in a new environment.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and the demo definitely sold me on it, but I'm not motivated to play it much more after a few chapters. Unfortunately, the demo really shows everything the game has to offer and it never evolves past the demo.My biggest problem with the game is that everything's too shallow. After the intro, the player has a small train with nothing but a couple of passenger cars. I now have around 32 soldiers, as well as a workshop, kitchen, medical car, and artillery train. But what's actually changed? Erm... it's not really clear. Managing the train consists of assigning soldiers to roles, upgrading various train cars when the train is stationary, and sometimes selecting different crafting recipes. Things like an FTL-style 'gotta go fast' meter emerge later, as well as the cold, but they're too easy to stay ahead of. I had max insulation in every train car before the cold mechanic was even enabled.There's also some nodes around the map which give resources, shops, and occasionally a scripted text event. These felt okay for one map, but they're a bit too formulaic and predictable to be interesting. I even found myself skipping some of them a few chapters in just because I couldn't be bothered to get the resources, and I still felt like I had an excess of supplies.And that's pretty much it for the train layer. It sounds okay on paper, but in practice I haven't interacted with any facet of my train for an entire chapter and it's still running smoothly with an excess of resources. I don't need 8 people cooking or doing medical duties when 2-4 can handle it easily. I'm not even looking at my characters stats or levels, because increasing stat points (of which you only get 4 or 5 total, per character) give a ONE PERCENT efficiency boost. I'm not micromanaging my characters by switching roles to minmax stats, because there's not enough work for the characters to level up in other roles. It's a neat concept, but for something which encompasses 50% of playtime it just hasn't worked for me.The tactical combat felt okay initially, but after a few missions I realised they all play out the same way. As many other reviews mention, just stack a group of snipers and you really can't lose. It's ammo/resource efficient, it takes the RNG out of combat, and it's borderline impossible for the AI to counter. Every mission is a stealth mission, so there's not much reason to take other roles outside of maybe 1 grenadier for vehicle booming. I've played 10, maybe 15 tactical missions, and the same strategy unfortunately solves all of them. There's some extremely expensive gear upgrades available to purchase, but I can't see why I would when the sniper has a 1 hit kill skill on fast recharge. There's also very little connection between the train and the combat phases. Soldier skills and health carry over between the two, naturally, but that's about it? The roles I've assigned on the train don't matter for the combat, the engine or cars I've acquired don't matter. All the missions are premade scenarios that you teleport to for combat, and then teleport away from afterwards. I get why it's made this way, but it ended up feeling very detached, especially as characters would regularly talk in missions despite not being there (e.g. the omniscient second-in-command).Overall it's a bit too flawed for me to finish it. A neat concept executed in a very safe manner that didn't really offer anything new and didn't do anything particularly amazingly well.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda made me nostagic towards the old Commando's games. i found it pretty fun to play.Level your scout/snipers to 5 asap to get the insta kill and fast silent walking. Get them to have level 1 in grenadier or medic to get the grenade/heal pack perk and equip the level 5 scout with heal packs. Use grenades and stones to lure groups of enemies to one spot and BOOM. all while remain hidden
_childDocuments_.name: Last Train Home

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a joy and a breath of fresh air! Compare to the insuferable load of soulless crap that the gaming industry is pumping out these days, this is a little gem!Story and Atmosphere - 10/10I absolutely love the atmosphere of this game and the care and attention put towards being historically authentic. It has a pretty grounded and mature story given the circumstances of the legion's trip and battle for survival against nature and human adversaries. It's no witcher 3 but it does give you choices with consequences and so on.But by far the thing it does best, it makes you care about the humans you are bringing to the destination. The way it feeds you little narration snippets throughout both live action acting, game cutscenes and text events along your journey is done really well. You actually start caring a bit about the people you are guiding and after a while start remembering their personalities. Makes you feel like being part of the real life dash across the warring Russian countryside more than 100 years ago.Graphics -  8.5/10Loved the attention to detail on the train elements, and it is by no means a bad looking game. There are nice variations and detailed buildings/landmarks on the maps as well.The only detractors are that the UI is not as good as it could be, and overall it doesn't bring anything ground-breaking in terms of graphics.Sound - 9/10Found nothing to complain here. The gameplay sounds are good and immersive, and the voice acting is excellent (I'm playing on the czech/slovak/russian voice and german subtitles). Gameplay - 8/10The missions itself are quite fun and challenging and it can get frustrating in some places if you do not bring the right tools for the job. There is a bit of a learning curve to it, which roles are good for that situations, it definitely makes you earn it. Which I like. This ain't no company of heroes, people die super quick and a simple grenade can wipe out half of your squad, so you have to take care. There are still some little bit unpolished stuff like when you drive in the armoured car it's hilariously bad how it steers, and I also led to a suspension of disbelief moment where enemies can only spot it from the same range as a soldier despite being literally a metal barn on wheels. But its more hilarious than detracting from the game haha. The train and travelling part can get a bit boring and tedious after a while as I would like more types of locations to be able to interact with along the way. Verdict - almost a must-have in my collection, and hopefully it opens the door to more games like this!
