_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, I really did, I saw it's charm and silly premise and really wanted to immerse myself in a gameboy-esque world filled with colorful characters and a fantastical story. Little did I know what I was getting into wasn't just a game that would look like a gameboy release, but also feel like one, all the jankiness and sometimes downright hostile design included as was customary for that era. Seriously, If you had given me this game with no context whatsoever the only thing that would've tipped me off about it not actually being an authentic gameboy release is the fact that the character sprites don't actually follow pixel grids and the main character's jump physics let him slide up corners to make otherwise impossible jumps, so really I must commend the dev's dedication on going all in on the theme.The story is... fine. The general concept and ideas I liked a lot, but it's when it comes to the execution that a lot was left to be desired. Now it's important to mention: I played this game in english, which I can tell is not the original language of the game, so it's possible that there were some things lost in translation or perhaps the translator just wasn't very good at conveying the original message in an elegant way (there are some minor spelling/grammar mistakes here and there so it really wouldn't surprise me if that were the case). However, as it stands I must report that dialogue in english was written in an incredibly stiff and artificial way. None of the characters feel like actual people, they're mostly just tropes and one-dimensional plot devices, and they stay very simple even when the story attempts to develop them beyond that. This would honestly be fine if the game was more self-aware and tongue-in-cheek, and while it DOES have moments that are more humorous which work far better imo, those are honestly quite rare. For a game called "Save me Mr Tako!" which is centered around a conflict between humans and a race of sentient octopuses (that's what the game calls them, don't yell at me for not using 'octopi') the tone is weirdly serious throughout, and it does not work in the game's favour as most of the dramatic moments really fall flat. There are also some minor inconsistencies in the worldbuilding as well as characters sometimes not making the most logical decisions or other plot contrivances, but honestly if you get into the headspace of this being an actual gameboy-era game this stops bothering you as such things were par for the course in most older games as well.The gameplay is... nothing special. Really, I would almost call it boring, but it did manage to keep me mildly entertained for about six hours so that would be somewhat disingenuous. The game has two main mechanics going for it: shooting ink to immobilize enemies, letting you jump on them to do platforming that would be otherwise impossible and hats that alter your shooting style. The first mechanic is what really carries this game, without it this would be a plain 'ole regular platformer that would probably feel even blander, however the game really fails to utilize this mechanic in new and exciting ways. Once you've beaten World 2 you've pretty much seen everything there is to it and the only things that will change are how many times you actually need to shoot an enemy to properly immobilize them, which does nothing to enhance the gameplay and only serves as an annoyance. In fact, this game has a lot of annoyances, like the fact that every time you die you lose the hat you're currently wearing and the only way to get it back is to take it from a checkpoint (you can only recover one hat this way btw.) or finish the stage you're currently in to go into another stage and get it from the hat NPC. Not to mention there is always only one checkpoint per level and dying in a pit doesn't always leave you in a good position to run all the way back to it. Seriously, why? Why couldn't you just let the players have all the hats in their "inventory" and freely swap between them or something of that sort? This is less bad in the beginning of the game, as most hats basically just have the same effect but make you shoot different looking objects or make your shots have different trajectories, 99% of which are so insanely gimmicky you will never actually find them useful in any situation whatsoever. Legitimately, the default shot your character has is the best in the game by far, there is absolutely no reason to put on like 90% of the hats beause they will either do nothing or actually hinder your gameplay. The only hats that are even worth paying attention to are literally the first one you get, which grants you one extra hit before death, and the upgraded version of that which gives you two hits.  Still, like I said before this wouldn't be so bad if you didn't actually need any hats to progress in the game, and for the most part when you DO need a hat the game is kind enough to not take it away after a death... provided it gives it to you in the first place. Sometimes, however, you'll be faced with challanges in stages where you're not provided with the right hat for the job, meaning you'll have to actually carry it throughout the level to the place where you need it, hoping you don't get hit on the way there because if you do you'll have to run all the way back to the checkpoint (if possible) and then hope you don't get hit again when running back where you were heading in the first place. It's tedious and unfun, and most of the time you WILL get hit either because of the janky hitboxes, unexpected enemy behaviour, or simply because you've started being so fed up with the game you started being sloppy which will just make you even more frustrated. This game really is not that hard, I've been playing on the medium difficulty where you only get one hit by default and I've never gotten stuck on a section for longer than around 5-7 lives. However, while not hard, the game does like to throw just barely avoidable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at you like fish and birds jumping at you off the edge of the screen, or jumps that look deceptively easy but will actually throw you into spikes because you bumped your head on a corner. I don't consider that difficulty, it's just another annoyance. Speaking of annoyances, here's another hat-related one: the button the game tells you "swaps" your active and stored hats doesn't actually do that, in fact it only discards your active hat and makes your stored hat your new active, but then when you pick up the discarded hat it becomes the active one again. That means that whenever you actually want to swap your hats, you need to discard them both, then make sure to pick up the one you DON'T want first, then finally pick up the one you actually want. Fun.Lastly, the level design is... bland. There's just no way around saying that, the levels feel very repetitive and same-y. None of them really stand out in my memory and a lot of them just blend together into a blur. The only exceptions might be the "special" levels signified by the castle doorways on the world map, but even then those usually go for long enough that parts of the level start to blend in with themselves. Generally, I think this game could actually gain a lot by "trimming the fat" so to speak. There are a lot of levels where nothing interesting happens at all, you just move from point A to point B in the exact same enviorment you were in the level prior, with the exact same platforming challanges, just in different places or with slight variations and not even the story gets progressed in any way at all. Those kinds of levels you could completely cut out of the game and nothing would be lost, in fact I'd argue that it would improve the game by letting the other, actually meaningful levels stand out more instead of being sandwiched between complete filler that shares the same coat of paint.All in all, I wish the best to the developers, but this just ain't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: When taking a first glance at Save me Mr Tako, it is hard to not to have a feeling of sheer nostalgia, considering that the game very much harkens back to the "oldschool" gameboy /monochrome graphics /color palettes, which may or may not a turnoff for some people. But for me personally, it very scratched that itch of mine (having grew up in the late 90-s)The story of the game is a rather standard affair: A war is being waged between humans and octopuses (yes, really)  with our main character Tako who is trying his best to bring peace between the two rivalry factions, despite his entourage highly disappproving of his efforts.  While the storyline isnt likely to beat the writing of The Witcher series, it doesnt have to: it does helps to bring context into an already well-rounded platformer and giving a goal for our protagonist to work for.Gameplay wise, Mr Tako definitely borrowed a bit from games such as Super Mario Land series, Kirby, a Hat in Time and many others:  You are plopped into a hubworld in which you are free to explore to your heart content, talk with other octopuses, visit shops and its also from here that you will acces the level portals (with new levels being unlocked along the way).  Most of the time you will go from level to level, collecting feathers and inks while also dodging and neutralising enemies with your ink. Dont let the cutesy artstyle fool you though, as the game does not kid around with difficulty: one hit and you are out. Mercifully though, there are checkpoints scattered around levels and the hats will also help making your life all that easier And yes, hats are also a thing in this game, which, just like in Hat in Time, will give you various power-ups ranging from special projectiles to use to other perks that will make your life all that easy, such as giving you an additional hit you can survive before you drop dead.In terms of music, the game keeps in line with its retro/ gameboy sound design and it provides a rather mellow and pleasant vibe that goes along nicely with the overall gameplay (and dare I say, its also that kind of music which i would love to listen to off-game as well).So how would I rate my gameplay experience so far? While Im admittedly nowhere near even finished yet, from what I have experienced so far it is without a doubt a very competent title, even if a bit less forgiving than most platformers of that genre.  Aesthetically speaking, its very pleasant to look at and it has a good amount of gameplay both for casual and for the completionists out there, definitely would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off well being a cute, Kirby-like gameboy platformer. The combat however you realize early on has next to no variety. You use hats to change your equipped ability, but most of them tend to be useless or actively a hindrance to your progress. Most of the stages feel fine enough, however when you get into some of the later dungeons they suddenly are *extremely* easy to get lost in. The game expects you to remember what every location is called without any indicator on the world map screens so you find yourself just wandering around until you finally stumble on the correct one again. For the kind of game it is, it goes on way too long as well. I expected to be done with it far sooner than it was and as time went on it was evident that I was not having fun anymore. Everything felt like a chore by that point. Sad this didn't quite get where I wanted it, maybe it's good for others. It's not terrible by any means, but it's also not good enough that I could recommend it in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed what bits of the story I experienced, the humdrum level design and character art really took me out of it. _childDocuments_.review: Did not particularly like the story or find the levels that interesting.   Also more than a few levels that are mazes with no in game map of any sort. It's very easy to get lost if you stop the game for a bit and come back to it later, especially in act 3 where you're expected to go back and forth between the areas.It's very easy to get stuck for a while somewhere and have no idea what the game expects you to do and have to wander around until you stumble on whatever you actually have to do to progress.  I'm just done with it now.  Doesn't help that I can't seem to find any walkthroughs or playthroughs around that aren't speedruns.edit: loulou's hints become almost useless in act 3, where loulou's hints become stuff like "you have to visit the 3 temples", when the next thing I have to do is go back to some sewers with a key.  Even before that, I have trouble remembering which places are named what, and names don't show up unless entering an area.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice Gameboy aesthetic retro platformer 2D pixel art game that revives Trip World / Kirby / Clash At Demonhead game style.  It has good art and half-decent feel, and I'm going to check out any future game by these developers, but I have to give this one a harsh review.  The problem is:0) Over-written like so many indy games.  Way too many textboxes and few of them are good.  You might expect some funny quirky textboxes, when you consider the title is "Save me Mr. [Octopus]", but the text was almost like irrelevant strings of boredom.  It seems that many indy game designers are self-absorbed and want to cram as many (bland) textboxes into the player's face as possible.  That's not gameplay, people.  It's mediocre, it's intrusive, it's irritating to constantly click through.  This isn't High School English Class personal fiction sharing time.1) Bland level designs.  You jump here and there, but it's boring and uninteresting compared to the good classic platformers.  The geometry doesn't feel like a place and isn't cool to travel through.2) Tedious annoying bad-feeling structure.  As you go along, the game switches back and forth at seemingly random points.  One moment you're in a town apparently talking to people and seeing unclear textboxes about hats or mini-games, the next moment you're in a standard Kirby/Mario level area.  Unlike other games that have both safe and normal/dangerous areas, this one was incoherent and neither part felt quite right.3)  General Uncreativity.  At one point, two octopuses sing a song which they say is their special octopus song (or something like that).  You would expect some kind of interesting not-perfectly-human-sapien melody and harmony chiptune here right?  Nope.  It's the most generic "castle king trumpet" tune ever in history.  Why bother?  How can octopuses in a goofy octopus game have a bland cliche human tune?It's worse than all the games it pays tribute to.  I played it for 30 minutes, it's fine as a thing, I'm not mad I paid for it, and I will stlil follow these devs to see what else they do, but I don't want to load it up ever again.
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really say whats putting me off after finishing the 1st of (I assume) three acts.Maybe it's the grafics, even though I grew up with the Game Boy.Maybe it's the levels, which feel similar, even though they very in location and enemy types.Maybe it's the ever changing colour pallet, often fitting the area, but sometimes just looking weird.Maybe it's the story, which is suprisingly serious and dark for the setting (A pacifist octopus trying to same the world from a war between his kind and humans)Maybe it's the powerup system (using different hats), which feels unrewarding as most do not feel like an actual upgrade, despite having wastly varying effects.The game is not bad, unenjoyable or even unplayable. But maybe you know this feeling: You are playing a game and you wish it would be over faster so you can play something else. Every cutscene is annoying, because it stops the game from ending. That is me here.I don't regret spending 5€ on this and encourage you to try it, if you miss games like they were on the original GameBoy. I probably do less than I thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: A game about a cute little octopus in 8 bit style. Whats not to like? Wont lie, I can't be bothered to write my own review, but seeing how few reviews are on this game I want to help its review score a bit. Heres someone elses review which summarises it perfectly (source Hardcore Gamer):It’s hard to describe just how enjoyable Save Me Mr Tako is. It seems so simple and quaint from the outside, but contains a meaningful adventure that won’t soon be forgotten. The original release left many little things to be desired, but the Definitive Edition comes back in full force and ready to give Tako another change in the limelight so he can prove his eight tentacles aren’t just for show. Anyone who likes platforming, good adventures or just that classic Game Boy vibe should not miss out on one of the most enjoyable little indie titles ever made with Save Me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition.
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on the Switch, and got it here to support the developer. If you like platformers or had an original Gameboy, this game is a must.The story is grandiose and emotional, and the characters are fun and memorable, and you get very attached to them by the end.Gameplay is varied thanks to the “hats” mechanic, and it never gets boring. Some hats like the ones summoning cats and dogs are a particular standout. It is a challenging game, but with the new “heart” difficulty on the definitive edition, it should be at anyone’s reach.If you are a fan of classic platformers, I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This little octopus combines so much that’s wonderful and intriguing about what we once believed games could be, into a long and loving experience. In Save Me, Mr. Tako you play as Tako and his several allies and rivals, caught up in a narrative about war, trials, and family issues of Fire Emblem proportions. While that setting is mixed with platforming exploration levels in a world crafted in the style of Kirby’s Adventure, don’t be fooled since this isn’t your bargain bin “Love Letter” indie game. Save Me, Mr. Tako is as modern and complex as any of the greats.
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I had bought the original version back in 2018 since the concept of this game peaked my interest greatly (Gameboy inspired platformer with a plot that stars octopuses, which are my favorite sea animals) and I had a lot of fun with it so I was more than happy to double dip for the definite edition! I really enjoyed the plot and it's message of learning to love and accept others regardless of differences they can't control and I really appreciate there is now a mode that will let players who mainly want to enjoy the story have an easier time. The platforming and difficulty was fairly balanced and when it got tough it didn't feel unfair to me. The soundtrack was great to listen to and it sounds like music that was made for an actual Gameboy game. The hat gimmick was creative and while I few felt samey (the Piolos Babies and Diane's Shield for example) they were really fun to find and figure out which hat I needed to discover stuff.I don't have any complaints since the definitive edition fixed the issues I had with the original game so I would give a solid recommendation to anyone who has any interest in this lovely game! Do it for Tako!
_childDocuments_.name: Save me Mr Tako: Definitive Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Dive into a great adventure in the Game Boy era! Tako will travel the world, explore mysterious dungeons and fight tenacious bosses on his quest to end the war between the octopus kingdom and the human realm. name: No Place Like Home
detailed_description: Welcome to No Place Like Home! No Place Like Home is a cute and relaxing sim where you play as Ellen Newland. A girl who decides to visit her grandfather, on Earth, for the very last time before she moves to Mars. However, she soon discovers that her grandpa is missing and that his farm was recently destroyed. With questions on her mind and adventure in her heart, Ellen intends to save the environment, help the community, find her grandpa, and rescue the animals missing from his farm! Clean the world, destroy mountains of trash, vacuum all the rubbish, and recycle resources to build your very own dream farm! Everything you need can be found and recycled from trash, and if you befriend local neighbours, they may prove very helpful during your farming and adventuring endeavours. Find seeds, become a farmer, and use your produce to cook delicious dishes that can be traded for useful items! There are tons of plants, fruits, vegetables, flowers and trees to find and grow. You can also make honey, jams, mayo, and lots of other preserves to spice up the farming fantasy. Explore and go on adventures through many diversified zones. Trek through the wonderous Lonely Hills region and restore the damage done by its poisonous gasses. Save animals from icy weather in Frozen Peaks and fix the leak from an old factory that has turned the local flora into giant mushrooms. Break the giant dam and release the river to bring nature back to the desert. Find, rescue and befriend farm animals that have gotten lost throughout the valley. If you gain their trust and take good care of them, you can be sure that they will return the favour. Once you are ready, you can show off your fun side by giving them funky hats and throwing them awesome parties! Rebuild, refurbish and decorate your house into a cosy place of perfection. Find awesome decorations and items across the world and use them to personalize your abode. After all, there is No Place Like Home!! If you wish to relax and enjoy some time with your animal companions after a hard day at work, then look no further! Join us now and start your adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: I have only been able to play this very sporadically during the Alpha but that actually opened my eyes to how much has changed and improved during that time.I can honestly say the game is very enjoyable. A completely different approach to the farming genre.Never thought I would find "sucking up garbage with a vacuum" would be so satisfying but here we are. I find myself clearing every area I go to completely and not getting bored of it at all.It doesn't have much "intense" game play at all but I really enjoy this. No need to befriend villagers by remembering their birthdays, no need to stress over seasons ending and crops dying etc. Just enjoy your time and clean up the mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first play through of this game and REALLY enjoyed it! The quests are straightforward enough while still making you think, and the combat is easy enough that the game is still relaxing to me. The clean-up will either become meditative or repetitive depending on your own personality.  My main advice is to not go crazy with building farm buildings. You're going to want to build more than one chicken coop, pigsty, etc. but there is no easy way to keep up with gathering those materials (it's still manual, even when you're equipment is totally advanced) so keep it to one building each for easy management.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one, but...I think right now it's a no. I like the game fine enough. Building out my farm is sort of fun and discovering all the zones is interesting. The story is bad, but I don't care about the story, so I don't necessarily count it among the negative aspects of the game. However, the game overall is just too buggy and riddled with things that common sense says should not exist. Examples: If you're standing too close to a patch of trash, anything at your feet won't get sucked up without moving away from it. Somehow the vac's programming lacks the ability to get stuff that's so close, which is ludicrous. When you're finished with a quest, the extra quest items that may be in your inventory don't go away, and you can't get rid of them with the trash can, so your only option is to let them clutter up space in your inventory or storage. There are a couple of quests that I've run into where if you don't do the quests in a specific order not spelled out by the quest log (or anywhere other than the forums), further quests in the chain won't be available to you without emailing support and letting them tweak your save file somehow. Unless I do that, I won't be able to finish the game, because for whatever indiscernible reason, the interaction with the NPC needed to move on to the next area isn't an option when speaking to her. So I'm stuck.For as long as this game was in early access, these things are just not acceptable in full release. It's perhaps fun ENOUGH for a $20 game, but ultimately the problems are too aggravating to get me to recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loathe to leave this game a bad review, because at one point, I really felt like it had a lot of potential. I played in early access, and while it was definitely still a work in progress back then, it felt like it had more to offer in early access than it does now. For a game that has been fully released, there are quite a lot of bugs, typos, places to get stuck, etc. I have quests in my quest log that have all objectives checked off, but are still marked as incomplete. I've found numerous small piles of trash that can't be sucked up from any angle. Major complaints and cons:- Dialog feels very unnatural and clunky. - Farming is very basic. Plant, water, harvest, repeat. No other mechanics such as different harvest times for different crops, fertilization, scarecrows, etc. Don't buy this expecting the farming to be a particularly interesting aspect, despite food rations being the main currency in the game.- The map feels somewhat limited, which isn't a major issue, but it feels like it takes a lot of grinding to get what you need to unlock certain areas.- Combat is very clunky and overall very annoying.- Fast travel system really doesn't make a lot of sense lore-wise anymore. Early access had fast travel points that were via a sewer system; now there's just a big room with themed doors that magically take you to wildly different areas of the map.- The story and lore is very weak and doesn't get explained more as you progress.- No inventory management or sorting.Overall, it feels like the final release just removed a lot of what made this game unique, stripped it down to its bare essentials, and didn't even really improve those essentials. At its current state and price point, I really can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is easy going, fairly addictive and collectors will most likely enjoy!Has a similar feel to slime rancher and is a good alternative if you run out of things to do in that game.Pros:> Nice art style> Decent length game with a fair price. All the better if you get it in a sale. It's not game of the year material but you will likely have some fun with it.> Between the relaxing gameplay and the silly story, it doesn't take itself too seriously> Straight forward progression based farming with plenty of options to maximise profits.> Upgrade and improve your gear and most buildings/machines you can make.> Decent number of areas to explore and re-explore to complete sidequests. Interesting to see how places change with gameplay.> Build almost anywhere and add as many decorations as you like.> Satisfying sounds and vacuum ability that will be a dream for anyone who likes cleaning/makeover simulators.> You can put a banana hat on a chicken or a piggy hat on a pig. That sets the theme for the entire game, really.Cons:> Not much challenge and you just start the next day when you die. If you want a game with cool combat, this isn't it.> Buggy graphics at times. Sometimes objects disappear from a certain camera angle or randomly pop in. Not game-breaking, but does ruin the otherwise charming graphics a bit.> The map isn't great and it's fairly easy to get lost if you don't pay attention to the landmarks.> Frequent (albeit not too long) loading screens are a pain. It seems to take the same time for a tiny house to load as a sprawling forest.> Farming/placement controls could be a lot more intuitive and satisfying. They work, but they're not really anywhere as good as other similar titles. The item stacks can seem a bit silly too, since a machine will take 12 veggies... but all veggies stack to 10 and so on. Chests are small, identical, unlabelled and fill up fast (they are cheap to make though).> The last zone is over far too quickly and the ending can be a bit abrupt. Think of it as a bonus scene and the true gameplay in the getting there.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relaxing game. There's no punishment for getting knocked out and no need to eat and drink or constantly check in at the farm. That said, there are a lot of issues. After the first chapter, you become suddenly incredibly wealthy and are only waiting on the next seed packet to drop to unlock the next upgrade. There's very little text, but there are many typos. The world has been chopped up into many small zones with loading screens between each that drastically slows down what should be an open world. Many zones are cut up with invisible walls that get in the way of navigating the world, keeping you from walking up or downhill or preventing you from jumping down a platform from one side but not the other. At the end of the game with no warning, you're handed a super gun that replaces your watering hose that beats the level for you. I did not even realize there was a boss battle until the boss surrendered. It looks like there was once one fast travel mode via a cave under your farm, but maybe a second one added later via the minimap with many more points, but not the points in the cave, which is kind of clunky.Some of these issues may be fixable. Certainly it should get a proofread and have the typos fixed. Mid and high level upgrades should be made much more expensive, or preserved food (the in game currency) should take longer to make. Maybe a few fences could be placed along the more awkward invisible walls so there's some indication we're not supposed to walk in those directions. The fast travel cave could probably just be done away with, since the minimap seems to have already replaced it. As for the super gun, maybe only give it to the player at the boss fight and also not have it one-shot the boss.So if you want a relaxing, pretty game, this is fun, but it's not really that well made.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey all, Don't expect much and it'll be a good game. I absolutely loved cleaning up the trash and I enjoyed most of the story line. There are funny moments, and some that make you groan in a "What just happened?" kind of way. Took about 25ish hours to complete, so it does take up some time. That's about it for the good. For the irritations: Bugs. SO MANY BUGS. Goodness forbid one of the animals you need to complete a quest glitches off screen. Better restart or figure out how to spawn in an animal. There will be many times where instructions were unclear, or you swear you did what it asked and nothing happened.  The biggest disappointment was the ending. It preps you for an awesome ending. I was looking forward to it. Instead it gives you one of the most rushed, lackluster, and horrible written endings. I hate the rating system because it's about a 50/50 for me. If you like little things and can deal with a lot of bugs go for it. Otherwise, steer clear!

Or it was fun but a little to monotonous after the first couple of hours. I'm hoping as the game develops this will change.Pros:- Unique way of collecting resources by drilling and vacuuming up trash- Currency is food a player has to cook from crops and livestock resources- Different NPC you meet as you explore teach you new recipes- Relaxing game musicCons:- No camera zoom in or out. If you plant trees they'll obstruct your view A LOT!- Invisible walls in some livestock coops, making it hard to interact with animals- Day cycle too short.- There is no sprinting, jumping or mounts so getting from point A to point B will take most of your in game day- To many resources and not enough things to do with them.- No way to regain health except to sleep.- Can't rotate camera when place item down so you have to be facing exactly the direction you need to in order to see where you are placing items.- Can't access storage when crafting so you have to make sure you pull everything you need from storage before crafting.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who tried No Place Like Home while it was in early access, it definitely improved on the gameplay side.Now onto the review. No Place Like Home is a relaxing game where the farming is easy to work with, lots of trash to pick up, and a bit of story to make the world building somewhat interesting. After completing the game, here are my thoughts:Pros:- Plenty of collectables and in game achievements to keep me engaged;- Customising my house and farm is very flexible and make it easy to make the place my own;- Upgrading feels rewarding, helping me out through the exploration of the game;- Having things for the animals to do other than walk around is a nice change of pace for farming sims (gathering for a picnic or dancing);- The currency in the game (preserves) is very easy to come by;- Nothing in the game makes the player feel that something unfair happened;Cons:- Only the crop soil can be placed using a grid. Makes having a unique layout easy, but planting trees is hard to tell if it is in a good position or not;- Enemy machines are a little easy, didn't lose all my health once during my full game playthrough;- Animals tend to overcrowd corners and get stuck, making gathering material from them, a bit tricky/near impossible;- Speaking of animals, there are no penalties to not tending to the animals after long periods of time.- There doesn't seem to be many NPCs, making the world exploring a bit empty. Even with that, I wish there was an easy way to know their names;There might be more cons than pros, but I still feel like this game is worth a try, considering it is a first for the developer. Completing the game in a little over 20 hours and still having some things to do, it is a good time waster.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I can't recommend it in the state it's in right now, which is a shame. It's a cool concept, but poorly implemented at the moment. Settings are wonky, controls feel sluggish, there's some serious problems with seeing the attack zones of enemies (and I'm not color blind, so if I'm struggling with it people who are red/green colorblind are going to have huge issues), quests seemed to trigger out of order, and one I was on refused to finish. I hope these issues get addressed, and I will definitely be checking in at a later date, but for now it's very much "early access."The good: It's cute. Everything about it is cute, and it has a decent sense of humor without reaching an "oh god why" level. The music is pretty good, and the sounds fit what you're doing. I consider it a good thing when I can turn off the music and not feel the rest of the soundscape is distracting.The meh: The gameplay (at least as far as I got) seems very shallow. Plant crops, water them, harvest. Befriend animal, wait, harvest from it, fill whatever need it has, then wait again. Drill pile of junk, suck up loose trash, put into recycler and wait. Use the currency you get from that to build new buildings. Buy new buildings with food preserved from what you grew. The foundation for a simple but enjoyable gameplay loop is there, it's just unpolished and maybe unfinished. Expect your first few days to fairly slow on the "getting stuff done" front. (And be sure to go into the house to sleep away the night. That wasn't explained to me, I stumbled on it after walking past the stairs and seeing them light up.)The bad: Pacing is off - I either encountered things far earlier than I was introduced to them, or discovered things long before the quest meant to tell me they existed, and some things just outright were not explained to me at all. I don't mind a game that lets me just go explore, but it didn't set itself up as such through the quest system. The moment you enter the farm area, you're told to talk to an NPC and begin their quest line, with no hint that nothing is (as far as I could tell) locked behind finishing it, and all the implication that you need to do this before you can do anything else. Controls are sluggish at times and you WILL need to fix the mouse sensitivity as soon as you load up the game - it doesn't default to 1 for some reason.End TLDRControls: It feels like it's optimized for controller right now, but it defaults to mouse and keyboard even with a controller plugged in. Mouse sensitivity is set incredibly low, and it's split between the X and Y axis. For some reason I started out with both X and Y set to 0.3, and I ended up feeling ok with 1.5 but probably could have taken it to 2.0 for better results. Unfortunately, mouse sensitivity does nothing for movement controls. All of that is thrown out the window when you activate your drill, though - tank controls engage, including incredibly slow movement. Reach of the drill is *just* short enough you can't finish off a junk pile without moving, and there's *just* enough of a delay between letting up and it actually turning off that quick reactions to get out of the way of an enemy attack is spotty at best. That assumes you can see the attack icons, though - I had things set to Medium and they all blended into the ground, even the red icon. I only spotted the green icon when I knew there was an attack coming and where I should be looking for it - there's no way I would have seen it otherwise. I feel for anyone who is red/green colorblind and trying to play this game.The default keybind mapping is odd and threw me off at first, then just annoyed me. The only standard keybinds are M for the map, and 1-0 for your hotbar. There is no jump, but instead of leaving spacebar unbound it's defaulted to "vacuum" instead. Your mileage may vary, but I was ready to change the bind by the end of my 1.5 hours because I kept doing my usual "jump when I'm walking somewhere" thing and annoying myself with the sound. Both E and R are used for very common actions, but I didn't notice Q doing anything for some reason. Tab is your menu key, but annoyingly messes with the Shift + Tab bind to bring up the Steam overlay. I had a few times where it cancelled the overlay and only brought up my menu, which was not what I wanted.Oh and the mouse cursor is captive to the screen in all window settings, at least when I played. I didn't see a way to turn that off, and so needed the Steam overlay to escape the window without alt tabbing completely. Hopefully this QOL bit will change at some point, but it's common enough I don't really think it's a deal breaker, just something worth mentioning.Pacing: A good portion of what is a deal breaker to me is the pacing. When you start, you find a ton of junk that is very satisfying to clean up, but you have very little direction to do so. Your first quest is to put down a chicken coop and befriend 5 chickens. Nothing is said about the potatoes you can plant, or how you'll want to get those going early on so you have 5 potatoes to befriend said chickens. Likewise, nothing is said about the piles of junk or any of the obviously special crafting materials you'll be getting from cleaning them up. Turns out most (all?) of those are quest items for later! While it's good that you can get them even before getting the quest to collect them, I have to wonder why you are required to clean up so much of the junk just to find all the chickens if you're going to be getting quests for these items later. Quest items jumping ahead of the quest feels... odd.I also completed a quest to put a hat on a chicken before receiving it - and got the "quest finished" dialogue pop up, which confused me because I had thought I'd just discovered a cute cosmetic mechanic. Thankfully doing so didn't break the quest chain, despite 'turning in' that quest before being told to go do it.The quest that did break, and that finally frustrated me enough to just quit, was the "bring proof you've befriended a chicken" quest. I have eggs, I have a chicken feather, but neither of them in any combination will complete the quest. There is zero help for what else you might need to do, even when you go back and ask for a reminder or hint. The quest log didn't have anything useful, either. So either it's broken here, or so vague about a specific that I just couldn't find what it wanted from me. Either one is not good.I'll be watching to see where this goes, but there's enough small issues adding up to keep me from enjoying it overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game a few months ago when it was on sale and didn't play because I wasn't sure if I would like it or not. Yesterday, I decided to boot it up. For 2 and a half hours straight I vacuumed trash off my farm, planted so many seeds, tamed chickens (and robots?) and met a few townspeople. After that, I knew that this game was going to suck away a lot of my time. I loved how satisfying it was to clean up the farm! I played Island Saver (a free recycling game that teaches kids about banking) even though I definitely wasn't the target audience. This game combined what I liked about that game and added in farming, house decorating, ranching, and more exploration!The new update added in even more rooms to your treehouse. Did I mention that you get to live in a TREEHOUSE in this game?? I'm wary about decorating for now as I'm not sure how limited my resources will be, but I have seen in the community sector what some people have done with their homes. I know that I will end up spending a lot of time decorating my house and farm in the end-game. _childDocuments_.review: Game is very relaxing. Its the only game ive purposely set out to 100% on Steam. Some tips I can offer? _childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I really enjoyed my 39ish hours playing No Place Like Home.  I am a fan of these types of farming/crafting/exploring games and this game added the unique (to me) twist of cleaning up trash.... which I found very satisfying.  The graphics are great and ran smoothly up until end game.  This game was fun to play but did have a few issues.  I found that there wasn't a reason for a lot of stuff... I never had a need for eating food, wool from sheep, money played a very small part in it and I ended the game with so much extra.  There are so many extra quest items that sometime I felt like I was missing parts of the story?  Quests were often times out of order or completed before I was even given one. _childDocuments_.review: Overall:I recommend this game to all exploring-building-farming-(cleaning)-friends. I like - no - I LOVE this game. Graphics and music are nice. For the action aspect there are some bad robots you have to "fight", and fighting is really not my kind of thing, but I can get rid of them fast. Even after the first Major Upgrade with new "harder" enemies, I struggle only when there is a bunch of them in one place. But with a little strategy and learning about the opponent's weak points, it works quite well.For the management aspect, you really don't have time for everything in one in-game-day, even the longer day after the upgrade.My focus lies in exploring and cleaning, but this is my gaming-style. There is no need to feed/water/farm every day and I like that. -------------------------------------------------Notes in tests:Edit 8 -> more Content (@162+ playtime): Another new area, animals, NPC and Seeds and no need to start a new game *happy*Edit 7 -> Major Upgrade (@150+ playtime): 2nd second tier area and more is life! <3 <3Although some items are missig, some spots where I stucked in and 2-3 floating trashpiles, it is possible to complete all quests, if you start a new game.Edit 6 -> Major Upgrade (@80h playtime): 1st second tier area and more is life! <3A lot of functions have been completely redesigned: tutorial, journal, tools, crafting, cooking, puzzles and even the village. New plants, new animals, new enemies, camping tents, Lonely Hills and sewer dungeons has been added, and the in-game day is longer now. Through the sewers you can travel faster across the map. The additional camping tents serve as save (like the bed at home) and respawn points, making exploring more fun.Since there are some bugs with quests, I wasn't able to complete them in this playthrough. And I'm not done with cleaning everything yet ^^ (after 25h!!) As expected: in the new areas are some "old" bugs like floating trash piles, stucking areas, spelling errors and bad performance. Now even my laptop ends in overheating, but I've got the same issues with all Unity Engine games. _childDocuments_.review: So I was unsure how to review this game at first. I read through others reviews and found myself agreeing but also disagreeing. I want to preface by saying I genuinely do love this game. I haven't put as many hours into yet, but I find myself thinking about this little game all the time when I'm not playing. So, now for my review.Please scroll to the bottom of this review for my personal note to the developersThis game is good. I'm a lover of games like Animal Crossing, Sims, Stardew Valley, etc. This game fits nicely into the same kind of category. Its not a perfect fit, but its a fit. Please remember before you buy or play, this is an indie game. Even though it is the full release, it still has its issues. I didn't realize I picked this game up only a handful of days after the full release, literally like 5 days after. Go in with low expectations and let the game show you what it has. Some things to considerController play: I dont play with controller, but I tried and I was unhappy with the lack of support even though other reviews say it was supposed to work with controller. That is something that needs fixed in my opinion, as they said it would be a feature and it has not been nicely implemented yet. Motion Sickness: I dont have motion sickness, so I can't really comment on it, but I can very much see how it could be an issue with this game. There are some motion sickness options in the settings, but again, im not sure how effective these are as it isn't an issue I struggle with. So if you have motion sickness issues, please approach with caution. The graphics: So my game started with graphics and everything being on performance mode and I rather like them on that setting. I play on a 300$ cheap laptop so too high of graphics really messes with my computer. Im not unhappy with the graphics as I like the cutesy look, but if that isn't your thing, then that may be a problem for you. The gameplay: So I haven't gotten myself unfixably stuck yet, but I did have a brief second of "Oh god, what do I do?" Good news, there is a quest tab! Bad news, past the beginning that shows you the basic controls, there isn't much else for a tutorial on what to do or where to go. There isn't a huge online presence telling you how things do and don't work like many games have, but there are some youtube videos that I've found slightly helpful. I am not displeased nor pleased about this as I do like that go your own pace feel to it and the feeling of freedom within the game. Now, I know some players don't like this as some machines and some parts of the game have little explanation on how it works (though they aren't hard to figure out with some tinkering), so keep that in mind before you buy. The gameplay can be seen as clunky as well, I get that. Personally, I do like that, but if you are going in expecting a smooth and slick gameplay experience, you may be disappointed as some things feel a little unfleshed out at the moment if you were expecting more. Combat: I like hitting the robots with the drill. Its cute. Its fun to just spam the button and whack them over and over again. The little area that pops up for there attacks can be hard to see and may not always tell you where the attacks are coming from (in the case of the spitter robots), I haven't found it overly difficult. NOTE: The attacks the robots do pop up a little grid of where it will hit that are red/green. If you are colorblind or are visually impaired, you may struggle to see it as it may blend into the ground. Plot: I have not found myself being rushed, but I also haven't felt like there is no reason to progress. You are a young girl looking for her missing grandpa on an earth that has been flooded with trash. You must pick up the earth and restore the farm to help all the little animals of the world. I like it, its very cute and cozy feeling. Theres the underlying mystery of where grandpa went or what the big trash flood was caused by, so you may get sucked into that. Overall, pretty cute plot. Price: For 20$, it could be so much worse. I was happy with the price and am happy with the amount of things I've gotten done in game to say I, personally, think I paid a good price for it. I'm very used to the strategy of EA and the Sims 4, where I've paid twice the amount of this game for half the gameplay. If you are struggling with funds and can't excuse the expense, don't worry about it. But if you like these kinds of games and have the extra money, giving it a try won't hurt. Overall: While I see where others may dislike the game, I personally have enjoyed the game enough that I feel it would be dishonest to say I could not recommend it. There are caveats as with any game, but I genuinely think this game could turn into something really cool and fun and even if it does not progress past this point, its a cute little game to sink some time into on a Saturday and can help you unwind after a long day. Please read other reviews as well, as I'm not a professional reviewer (Though I'd love to be) and these are just my personal thoughts and feelings. Those used to more mainstream games may find themselves displeased with this game, but you if are willing to set aside all expectations and just take this game at face value, letting it show you its cute little things and cute little niches, then you can have a pretty good time.Developers: You have made a very good, very cute game. This is something that the cozy gaming crowd online would really love and with continued support and improvements from you, No Place Like Home can become a great game and attract a lot of players that like these kinds of games. I beg you not to fall into the trap that EA has with Sims 4. As much as I love that game, they just release content that sometimes does not work just to make money. Listen to the community you have created and most of all, don't abandon this game. I'm genuinely in love with this game and can not wait to see what else you will do with it. You have some wonderful potential here and I want you to know that I'm so grateful that this little game has taken up space on my hard drive.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played Fresh Start and loved it. I went looking at other games by the same developer and found No Place Like Home. The trick seems to be turning the mouse sensativity up to something like 300% and then it plays normal. This time around I played through the entire storyline and really enjoyed it. At one point, I had to completely start the game over because quest items didn't appear in my inventory after I collected them and I would occasionally need to save and quit and restart the game because it would get glitchty. I realized that it seemed to get buggy more if I stayed up all night in game and was awake when the new day started. I found that if I went to sleep even an hour before 7 am in-game and allowed the game to do it day resets with the sleep setting the bugs were significantly reduced. I also feel like it needs a little balancing. The upgrades / items up front took a long time to get to and then came really fast towards the end so I didn't get much chance to use the higher end upgrades because the game was almost over. Shifting the progress up a little would make the game more enjoyable. Overall, though, the game is relaxing with the satisfaction of the farming aspect. It is a fun, cozy game. _childDocuments_.review: If you're certain kind of person - you know the type - that enjoys doing domestic tasks in video games immensely but are allergic to them in real life then you have come to the right place my person. You will drown in trash, be trash, embrace trash and then you will destroy it into little pieces and vacuum it up and you will do it for 90% of this game. So if this is your jam, then I do suggest you get it and try it out.However, despite having put in hours into the game and although I have had my fun with it and fully intend to finish it, I cannot recommend it in its current state. It's janky. Like, one of my biggest irritations is the combat. What is the point of it? You swing your drill and evil robots go boom. They are annoying and they await you around every corner. I see no point to them. They are not even the main antagonists, the trash is, yet you have to deal with them. I wish the developers had left the damn things out.Ugh and do not even get me started on the NPCs. Mass Effect's husks have more personality than these people. They just stand there, like statues, and only occasional move. It's jarring. Like, it would have made far more sense to have the talking animals be the NPCs instead of bothering with human beings that provide no valuable aesthetic to the game, they just detract from it. Have Cornelius the chicken run the farm store and Napoleon the pig the general store. It would be far more pleasing because at least the animals are more animated. Then we get to the world itself, now as mentioned, every damn corner is filled with heaps of trash so you are gong to be drilling and vacuuming until you are blue in the face. The world is dead and do mean that from a literal and environment point. You need to fix the world. Okay good, nice. But your actions do not always lead to enough reward. Not to mention there are very little game effects present in the game, like for example you have to melt large blocks of ice with bonfires but instead of there being a melting animation, the blocks just... disappear. Bruh, I know coding is hard, I am a developer myself but come on? This is just lazy on another level. There are so many graphical glitches like the sky flashing black, the distant stuff being super wobbly and just the placement of the assets in general. Some of them clip in each other or clip through the ground. The doorways do not always touch the ground and just breaks immersion. It really feels like the developers closed their eyes and did a quick job of the terraforming of the world and then just copy pasted all the assets in, moved them around a bit and called a day. There is so much more you could have done but nah.Lastly, the economic system. I do like the concept of food being the most valuable resources and turning your meals into lasting products is a nice touch but that is where it ends. You cannot sell anything you collect. There are some conversion machines to turn fruit into jam and milk into cheese but all this is for is unlocking recipes and cooking. That is it. The game is just too easy. You don't really have to work for it. You just move from area to area and suck up trash and hey look, the pumpkin seeds I needed to unlock recipe B6. The quests where you have to collect things you just collect them hand them in to the lifeless NPCs and get your reward. Oh and you don't even have to look for these collectibles very hard because there is usually 2-3 extras in the world just in case you thought that maybe you'd have to work juuuust a little harder.Oh and inventory management is nightmare and your stacks are tiny. Something players absolutely love beyond a doubt.Hey, at least you can upgrade your movement speed and move superrr fast.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a hard choice between whether or not to recommend this game, but I ended up deciding on "Not unless it's on sale and then only if you're realistic with your expectations."It's cute. The art within the game is really nice, the actual assets don't quite reflect that though. The concept and gameplay are both simple and enjoyable but lacks any real amount of depth. That's not necessarily a bad thing though. I really enjoyed the cleaning aspect.It never really felt like I was changing the world. Sure the mess was gone (except for some that was bugged and unreachable... or bugged and kept reappearing) but most zones just stay kinda ugly. The combat could use some work. The first time I got to a pair of enemies I couldn't reach with melee, I left assuming I didn't have a ranged attack. I don't remember learning that the hose could be used for that in the tutorial. Speaking of which, I ended up having to google to find out how to do some things (like rotating objects) because the tutorial is VERY simple/minimal.I don't know anything about the Devs but I'm just going to assume English isn't their first language. Either way they really need to hire someone to proof read through pretty much everything in the game. I'm not too fussed about a spelling mistake or two, it happens, but daaaaaaaaaang, it got bad. Plus I think one character had a name change at some point during development because one character is referred to by two names (and I'm not referring to Honestly, I've usually got pretty low standards for games. I don't mind if a game is bad as long as it's fun, and I think this was definitely the case, however the ending really left a sour taste in my mouth. The ending  I can't really be bothered opening the game again to just finish everything out of boredom... so yeah, it's cute and kinda fun, but I don't really recommend it.

I don't even know if I can really count some of these as bugs as it looks like the game was just left in an incomplete state near the end.- The game explains only part of the details. It doesn't explain that you can make more pet food at once by just tossing random stuff into the kitchens, it doesn't explain that you can suck in debris while using the laser, and it doesn't tell you that when you're using one of your tools (the water hose, the vaccuum or the laser), you can move your Left Stick/Mouse and make it aim higher or lower, which is super useful for some of those water buttons you have to press later in the game.- Sometimes after you get rid of a dirt pile or rock, the game will still act like it's there and won't let you around it. Leaving the area and coming back sometimes fixes this.- Your invincibility frames when hit are limited, if they exist at all. When you fall down, you have a slightly longer bit of protection, but if you're fighting several enemies at once, it's easy to get smacked around.- A large number of the items are worthless except for a single instance. In example there is no reason to grow flowers in this game unless you want to put them in a flower pot: you cannot sell them, you cannot turn them into other products and when you harvest them, you simply get more seeds than what you harvested. You need Wool for a quest, but after that, there's nothing to do with it but turn it into Yarn, which neither of them can be sold or turned into anything else.- You will probably start/finish questlines without realizing that you're doing it. There's been so many times I was cleaning out an area and accidentally started a new quest before I was even finished with the ones before it. It's not necessarily a big deal, but it can be confusing.- There is an item called Glue Waste that you can only get in the final area of the game. In order to get all the achievements associated with it, you'll need 100 pieces of it. The problem is that the area is glitched and sometimes it won't actually collect part/all of the Glue Waste there. Saving before going there and reloading if you don't get enough is the only way to get the 100 Glue Waste achievement.- You only really need to go to the Labyrinth if you're looking for Cornelius. Everything else down there is scrap, recipes, and decoratives.Again I can't say I didn't enjoy the game, but with all these issues it's hard to really give it a positive view.

At about the mid point of the game you spend about 1/3 - 1/2 of your day on upkeep.Third, third there are places where you're "supposed" access but are VERY tricky to get it since you can't jump. _childDocuments_.review: No Place Like Home has charm, but it still feels like an Early Access game.The tutorial is one of the most lazy on-boarding experiences I've had in recent memory.There's a bunch of little things that need polish; animals clipping into buildings, seeing parts of the map when entering your home before the loading screen pops up. Combat is really stiff and hit boxes are jank. The general feel of mining + vacuuming up the trash doesn't feel satisfying and lacks any and all feedback. The farming aspect is fine and passable. Using the watering function on the vacuum is really weird and off centre and water sometimes fails to dampen soil. Placing down seeds/plants could also use some polish.There's also massive frame drops in areas where there really shouldn't be any, and I have shadows set to low since it's a memory hog.I'd give this game a pass, maybe pick it up on sale just to kill a few hours, but there's better farming sims on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: In a lot of ways, this game is pretty decent, but the more I play the game, the less likely I am to ever recommend it to anyone. In fact, at this point, unless it's free, it ain't worth your money and support at all right now. It's that bad.It has a lot of issues (nothing game breaking, but still a lot of problems) and a lot of logic and fun factor issues. Getting stuck simply because there's no jump mechanic is weird to me, but invisible barriers in places where there really shouldn't be any are really annoying. Food is used as a one time market / upgrade thing and nothing else... so having a large farm is completely pointless as you only ever use each food item once (twice max). There's no way to heal yourself aside from sleeping it off. I don't feel like health upgrades and movement speed upgrades do anything at all, there's not even a visual indication that it does anything. Water tank upgrades and well is a pointless addition to the game as not once have I ever felt like I needed those. Recycling / preserving also seems pointless as you really don't need much of it in the game. There's no motivation to doing anything in the game since the payoff is always either nothing at all or nothing of actual importance / value. Getting that first door unlocked in the tree house was incredibly annoying as it rewarded you with literally a small hallway with a lot more doors to unlock. Finally getting a room door opened just offers empty space which is completely not needed at all, I assume all the other rooms are the same. There's no balance in the game at all, even the stacks make no sense. Controls and UI could be improved but are tolerable, graphics and sounds are pretty good for the kind of game it is, music is repetitive like most games which is why I always disable it. Oh, and I only just realized that I can use the water on those blue buttons to unlock stuff. There was no guidance at all to indicate that's what was needed to be done to them.I definitely don't see the point of giving us all these new locations to explore if there's no motivation / rewards to grinding our way to those locations. Why should I clean all these locations? Why should I saves the animals from the cages? Why build a home for the foxes and feed them? Why build a home for the deer and feed them? Why filter out the pollution in the water? Why neutralize the gas, especially since it does nothing at all to me despite the quest need for herbs which also has no effect at all? Why re-plant the trees? etc... There's no reason to do any of those things and so many others I forgot about. All these quests give you nothing at all as reward.Also, is it just me or is this game a bit sexist? NPCs (mostly male) do literally nothing while being arrogant like they know everything. The main character (a female) cleans everything including the NPCs yard and does all the cooking for them, etc. Why is there not even an option to make a male playable character? Just seems a bit sketchy to me.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: An ambitious farming sim with a twist ends up a lack-luster, ultimately boring, buggy,  and repetitive experience while the devs release two more uninspired games and ignore their first mess, No Place Like Home. Don't believe me? The majority of positive reviews have caveats and complaints so do yourself a favor and really read the reviews before wasting money and time on this game.Full Review:This game had so much promise in Early Access. So what happened?They wasted so much time listening to the small number of players on their Discord server that every time they made a change, so many of their actual customers disliked it that the devs had to go back and rework it. The largest of these changes was when they removed the underground area because their Discord fan boys didn't like it. It turned out the majority of their customers either really enjoyed it for resource gathering or it was their favorite part of the game.So they said they were adding it back in, released into 1.0 without fixing any of the quality issues or fleshing out the story because they made poor choices by not involving their entire customer base in decisions, had to drop things like fishing, and tried to compensate for all of this with chicken hats. This game should serve as a cautionary tale for developers who release in early access on Steam then mistake their Discord server for their customers. No Place Like Home could have been one of the best in the genre. Now it's another lack-luster farming sim full of glitches, a bland story, and wasted potential.Add to that they've been teasing fishing for a year but instead of adding fishing, they've made two more games that don't bring anything new or inspired to their respective genres. But, apparently, fishing is still coming... yeah... maybe by the end of 2023. It still wouldn't be enough to save this game from being a mediocre farm sim.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really relaxing and fun addition to the farming sim genre. There are a few things that are rough around the edges due to the nature of the game being in early access, but all in all if you enjoy Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, etc. you are almost guaranteed to like this game. I also find it really relaxing to clean up all the trash :) There is a small issue that the game has no currency sink so there's not really an incentive to take care of your animals or farm after you've completed the quest, but I've seen it raised so perhaps the devs are working on fixing it and it doesn't detract from my overall enjoyment of the game. There aren't too many NPCs and no romance options, which is the notable difference from other farming sims, but it fits within the story of the game. There is also no season/weather change - you can grow any crops whenever you want. There is some combat element with robots but it's not often difficult. There are fun decoration options and the art is gorgeous, as well as a pretty expansive world to explore (and clean up.) Would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Only about three hours in- but it feels like a stripped down casual "My Time at Portia"; The aesthetic, concept, and exploration elements seem on point; and while the gameplay is grindy it is sort of to be expected. I solved my own frustration with the vac system by learning that you can actually run BOTH the drill and the vac if you start drilling and then press the vac key. Totally an exploited bug, but doing that made the whole game much more fun and reasonable vs clearing out a space, vacing a space- over and over and over.The main place this game falls down is one place that I don't think it ever intended to be good at- character development. While I am currently only early into the game, I have already felt the problems outlined in some of the other reviews. The cast of NPCs while FINE- don't have any kind of relationship system common to farming games like this. Not having any form of way of learning more about these NPCs, talking to them, befriending them, etc is a big disappointment. Now, I am not going to rate this down based on this- in fact, I still think on balance this is a good game- I just know what I like and I like to get to know people.Another thing I do wish this game had (but I understand why it doesn't) is some form of voice acting. Not only does it give some personality to a title, it also pushes it from casual farming/cleaning game to something where the characters are more likely to come alive. Once more, I don't think it was ever intended nor do I rate it down for this but still.Overall, No Place Like Home is a chill experience which I do look forward to seeing develop more. Right now it feels like a really good game to play alongside children- who may be wanting that visceral exploration, bashing things, etc- but don't need the deeper gameplay and plot progress. Also, I love all the chickens. Woo.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok Ok OK! I hated this game at first, however once I sorted out the mouse pointer speed and could actually move the camera without having to strain my wrist I really started to love it. the world is vibrant and colourful and I never thought picking up trash could be so satisfying. there are some problems however. like having some resources cap their stack size at 10 while others are in the thousands, which is just stupid. so much inventory space is wasted. the Game is terrible at giving you some sort of idea of what to do. literally like no instructions at all. if like me you suck at interpreting what one vague icon means without any text or written instruction (I'm looking at YOU tutorial maker) you might get put off of this game like I was very quickly at first. stick with it though and by the time you get your chicken party you will have got a decent enough idea of how it all works. the world itself is nice, some voice acting would have been nice, the game play is fun and relaxing but there definitely is a need for a little more improvement. all in all it is a pretty decent game that I've accidentally stayed up until 9am playing... the story line, though I haven't finished yet, seems pretty good. The farming sim is lovely and well implemented I particularly enjoy watering my crops but if you arent into it (what's wrong with you, it's so much fun to use a glorified super soaker to water plants) there is a sprinkler that is very easy to unlock. I do wish there was a little more customisation for my character but you can put a frog hat on a chicken and if THAT isn't enough to sell you on it you can adopt dogs too. all in all, I really like this game but now I REALLY need to go to bed.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game - there is a LOT to do - interesting to explore. I would recommend it but there are just one or two points that need to be mentioned. I was going to mention this in their discord but it won't let me in so I can't leave any constructive feedback to help the appeal or development of the game (hopefully they might read this). These are just my opinions of course and most people probably wouldn't agree but the developer's blurb for the game (I might have missed it of course) doesn't mention the need to destroy dozens and dozens and dozens of robots in the areas where you have to collect the trash both underground and on the surface. The advertisements for the game give the impression that it is just a farming-type game and doesn't really mention the constant battles you have to engage in. I accept that many people won't mind this  - I just think there are a few too many unfriendly robots in some areas and it's sometimes a bit overwhelming and the game becomes more of a shoot-em-up rather than a farming/exploring game. The fact that every time you get killed or "fall asleep" as the game puts it (????) you end up back at the house which means having to travel back to the same area to complete what you were doing - this gets REALLY tedious very quickly.  If they were to put some other points where you could re-spawn to after you are put to sleep (killed?) it would be better (maybe somewhere near where you were when you "fell asleep" - it would save a lot of tedious travelling which makes the game boring to just constantly have to repeat these journeys. Before anyone says "learn to deal with the robots" I am doing this but there are just so many of them - I don't even mind being put to sleep by them - you expect to lose some of the fights - it's just the going back to the house and re-starting every time - it's so annoying. That gripe aside, I have played nearly 30 hours on this game and do enjoy it apart from the problem mentioned. I would recommend it to anyone who likes farming-type games just be aware there is a lot of shoot-em-up element in the game. I am looking forward to further exploring the map as there seems to be a lot still to accomplish in the game. One more thing I should mention is that I found the tutorial very difficult to follow - it could be my computer screen of course but I just found the images on the boards very hard to follow and I felt they weren't explanatory enough. I had tried to start the game on a number of previous occasions and just gave up because I couldn't understand the tutorial. Finally I decided to give it one more try and enlisted my daughter's help with the tutorial and I was glad I did. Once I finally got into the game I've really enjoyed it despite the annoying bits I've already mentioned. This is not in any way intended to be a negative review - I would definitely recommend this game and even more so if they did something about the tedious bits I've mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game for about 30  two days. So you can certainly assume it has some interesting features even though it is far from being perfect. While – at last for me – it had no game breaking bugs or crashes you will have to accept a few imperfections:-	You sometimes can press buttons through walls and therefore access areas you should not yet be able to-	The Inventory sometimes fixes the cursor on first slot when trying to move objects from/to a chest while you are unable to move it to the chest. To solve this you have to click on the first slot in your inventory once and then can move cursor to target inventory-	I’ve played on a UHD monitor and you can see that the loading screen is actually just a picture on top and you can see the game loading the content on the left and right side-	You regularly get a small recalculation and redraw of the ground based on view angle or how far away you are-	The quest symbol disappears over the head of the NPCs-	The AI is not the smartest (you can basically stand behind an enemy and they do nothing until you attackBesides those things I felt very entertained, the crafting and farming elements are nice and follow an easy-to-understand logic.

_childDocuments_.review: The positive review is very tentative - I finished the game, and so would feel dishonest saying it can't be enjoyed, but that's basically the whole reason it's not a negative one. There's a lack of polish in this game that can't be excused even from a small, inexperienced team. I won't say there should have been more complex economy, or more animations, or branhing questlines or whatever - this was obviously not within the team's scope. But sitting down and fixing typos and dropped interpunction? Making sure that the "you fell asleep" screen pops up *after* the fainting animaiton plays? Adding an ending slide after choosing the option to continue playing after the final quest? Small things matter for presentation, and they're achieveable for even a small, part-time dev team. This release feels like a late internal milestone build, not a finished game. On the upside - there's a lot of charm here, too. The cleaning mechanic is simple, but satisfying. Putting hats on animals is 10/10, no complaints here. The occasional easter eggs made me smile (like what happens when you put a UFO hat on a cow). The 2D artwork is very cute (shout out to the UI artist, the icons and other ui illustrations are adorable!), and in general - I can't recommend it at full price, but at a discount? Sure, why not. I hope that this dev team makes something more polished in the future.
