_childDocuments_.review: I finished it over 3 days, NPLH is a great game, similar to My Time at Portia and Stardew Valley but without the relationship growth. The basic gist of the game is to clean the area of trash which is absolutely everywhere and rebuild your granddads farm. Its easy to play, with good exploration and puzzles within the dungeon. The farming an crafting side is extremely simple, the hardest thing to do is grind to find the materials for each recipe. The enemies you defeat are extremely easy to defeat, there was not much of a challenge regarding them.I finished the main quests (except 1) and did as much as i could within 25 hrs, the last few hrs was just back tracking in case i missed anything. Only thing is I am stuck on is the house key quest as I cannot find the last keys, not sure if I've missed them somewhere in hidden places or they just are not all available in the current open areas or if its glitched out, after checking online i still cannot find the the last key. I have also run out of components for upgrading my equipment as i have collected as much if the trash as i possibly can.As far as a map system, there is nothing, its essentially a photo of the "world", there is no interactive capacity at all. you can create camps in designated areas but there's also no fast travel aspect so half the time you are running from one place to another and it gets quiet repetitive and boring.There is no penalty for losing health or passing out, you just begin a new day as the last camp you actively slept at. There is also no energy system like Stardew or Portia which i think is fantastic, but the hours of the day are just shorter and you pass out at 10 pm.I'm impressed with the graphics as my laptop can somehow handle it, was a little glitchy if i didn't let it load enough.  Only main problems I had was it taking forever to actually quit the game. A reoccurring problem was having trouble with trash heaps sitting above ground level and my vacuum not being able to suck it up even though it was in front of me. Again no sure if its the actual games issue or just my dinosaur of a computer system/ GPU. After a while storage becomes an issue as there is nothing to do with all the materials you collect so you just end up with chests everywhere filled with crafting materials. Food jars become meaningless as there is nothing to spend them on. I'm hoping for some sort of exchange system where you can get rid of all the unnecessary excess materials. Also will there be a way to sell the animals you collect (pigs, chickens, etc) as there are an abundance of them. Overall the game is cute, fun and extremely enjoyable, if not calming and I can wait for the rest of it to be released.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Release Review:Ok, so I finished this game and yeah, I'll still recommend it.  It's a VERY LINEAR GAME.  Don't expect some kind of fun "open world" (ha!!) game.  So one of my complaints in the early access was that I was getting lost. Well, I never got lost in the final release.  Not once.  There is literally a path that shows you exactly where to go. All. The. Time. There was no underground anymore (not worth talking about at least) and you can't get lost.The game is also "front heavy."  You reach a point where resources are plentiful and have little continued purpose. It gets easy honestly, and I'm not a "dark souls" level gamer. I'm kind of a filthy casual. I like the combat, though I wish there was one more level of challenge by the end of the game.  I like that the different enemies have different strengths and weaknesses.  I _like_ that I can get tools to make combat easier so it isn't the be-all-end-all of the game. I like that I can focus on the story.I still wish there was more purpose to the farming. They added in buffs (combat, health, sprint, etc.) for cooking which was a HUGE improvement from the "cook it once and never again" but it meant for everything that wasn't a recipe I wanted to make, I just tossed the extra seeds in a chest and ignored it.I left my early access review because a good bit of it would have just been "copy pasta" up here.  NPC's aren't as deep as I'd like, The plot is really fun and I'm glad I played it.  It's not a farming game.____________Early Access Review:I'm recommending this game, but with some strong caveats. It is a lot of fun and the premise feels unique.  The "clean up the trash" element which defines the main character's goal is something I feel like is new and different.  It is very satisfying to get ALL THE TRASH.  Like, I wish I got this kind of dopamine from doing the dishes.  But dishes come back.I think one of my most preferred things in the game is the combat. This is a weird one, but the combat in this game is simple but satisfying.  It is not so common as to overwhelm the story or other gameplay, but definitely produces a sense of threat and excitement when it appears.  The challenge honestly makes me go seek out the pockets of monsters I don't HAVE TO defeat, but I want to finish cleaning the entire area.Now for some of my issues. And I actually have a lot of issues.  My first is that this game is marketed as "farming game" like Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon - but the farming is one of the least important aspects of the game.  You will plant things and water them, and.... once you've used them they are pretty much useless.  You can cook, but each recipe will generally by used ONCE in order to upgrade your equipment or farm and then you will never use that recipe again. And If you accidentally make something you've used before (damnit mashed potatoes!!!)..... there is no use for it.  You throw it away.  There is no purpose to learning to make complicated dishes."Money" (scrap and preserves) are too easy to get or make.  Once I cleaned the basic stuff off my farm, I already had enough to make sure I NEVER needed to worry about funds again.  The conversion of trash into "money" takes time, but nothing a farming simulator player would even be bothered by.  The "return occasionally to run the next set" is no big deal, and after the first 2 days, I only did it to either clean up my inventory or when it was convenient.Speaking of cleaning inventory - the underground.  Filled with trash and theoretically needed to help you "refill" if you need it.  Why would I need it when I am overflowing with EVERYTHING and I've only entered the 3rd section/chapter?  Mostly, it just seems to be a good way to get back home.... oh wait there are even faster travel options with the literal fast-travel-hub.  So it's... I don't know.  It isn't a randomized dungeon, it can be mapped out and never changes. Basically, the game is linear.  It isn't a survival challenge because you don't need to eat or sleep - all the food is useless, remember? There isn't a penalty for dying.  You aren't trying to make money (you don't sell those crops you grow, you use them to make each food once or for some other quest and that's it).  The animals are honestly more annoying them helpful. The raccoon LOVES getting in the way of a path like bridges or doorways until I moved it's house out of my farm down by the beach.  Out of the way and out of my path.Even the NPC's are.... ok.  There is this cool glimmer of great dialogue, but... after about the 3rd time you click on someone you know 100% of what they will ever say.  Ever.  A challenge for all game designers, but still something I found disappointing.I am enjoying this game. I want to finish the plot/story and see what happens. The graphics are fun and enjoyable, the pigs are some of the cutest characters in the game (the cat behavior is also great).  The landscape does actually feel relatively big despite actually being limited (you know, it isn't minecraft infinite generation).  I will probably play through it, uninstall it, and never play it again though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a post-1.0 update to a previous "recommended" review. In early access this game showed some real promise, albeit with a few excusable warts. Unfortunately, those warts (and bugs) remain after the full release. The development process was a wild ride, as the developers clearly felt the need to attempt to capitulate to all received criticism simultaneously. The result is an un-focused, un-finished pile of compromises and glitches. Instead of focusing on fixing real bugs and graphical errors, the development team wasted time re-balancing and re-factoring nearly every system in the game, at times with seemingly random approaches. Also the main story upon release is basically the tonal opposite of what it was in earlier builds, which ruins any message the game once kind-of had and leaves me personally with a feeling of "so, then why am I motivated to do any of this?" Very disappointing for what felt like a refreshing start.

You can do as much or as little as you like and I really enjoy that its not farming orientated, so doesn't feel like a grind like other similar games.You're left to figure out how to accomplish tasks. how to navigate the wolds by yourself and other aspects, so it keeps it interesting as you figure out how to interact with quests/objects etc.Its Early Access so there are bugs and changes happening, but the devs are very responsive on the community forums and respond to players request for updates and fixes. _childDocuments_.review: Long story short: This would be an incredibly fun game to me, IF it were finished. 6/10.Short story long: This game has a fun premise, especially for someone that enjoys collection and quest based games that are light on combat and action. There are however several glitches and problems, some of which could be gamebreaking. At least once, my progress was not saved and I had to replay a large portion of the game. Another glitch allows you to pick up items, but does not place them in your inventory. If you are picking up limited quest items, this permanently removes them from the game and makes it impossible to finish. Grammatical and spelling errors are common in dialogue, I'm guessing because of localization/translation issues. Several game functions, like maps and controls, are difficult to get a hang on because of poor instructions/labels. Conflicting character art makes the game feel like it's still in testing, not finished. I completed the main story at a very leisurely pace (and repeating some sections) in 32 hours, and while I mainly enjoyed it, I think most people would find the gameplay lacking or tedious, as well as too short for its cost.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? Yes. But do I rate it highly? No. I give it 3.5 stars out of 5, with the stipulation that aside from its issues, it is very FUN. And I keep coming back to playing it. However, I do have some issues with certain aspects, and I would love to see these get patched:1. The navmeshes are not great, especially in the Lonely Hills areas. Sometimes you simply can't move anywhere because the navmeshes aren't connected well, so you are just stuck and have to fast travel to get out of the tiny spot you got yourself stuck in. These aren't like hills or anything you're getting stuck on, but just flat ground that you SHOULD be able to walk over. 2. There is no quest marker system to help you with quests. It asks you if you want to track a quest, but then there is nothing on the map to indicate where to go or what to do. You just have to explore and hope you find the pieces you need. I wish there were quest markers at least on the map indicating where they pieces of things be found, with a tally that says something like "3/5 house pieces found" or something. 3. Fruit Trees. Where the heck can you plant them? It seems like you're supposed to get them pretty early on. You get like 100 seeds for fruit trees just cleaning trash, and you need the fruit for upgrades. But you can't plant them anywhere that I can find? There needs to be a better method for this, or some kind of tutorial help. But there is nothing, and the internet has given me literally nothing to work with. I guess I'll just keep playing and hope that eventually, I will find a place to plant a fruit tree.4. The graphics look unfinished. I understand that it's a simple graphics kind of game, but I find myself wishing there was a bit more than there is. It has a feeling of being an incomplete game, and I was surprised to learn that this version IS the graphics updated version. It's not something that HAS to get fixed, but I do wish for a bit more. This game would be so much better if it was just a bit prettier. If it were prettier to look at, I would want to spend more time playing, and it would be more rewarding when I clean up an area and restore nature.5. The stack size of items. Why is it different for different items? Wood and rubble have a stack of 100, seeds have a stack of 50, batteries have a stack of 40, and food items only 10. Why not just make it all 100? This frustrates me and makes storing items irritating.Now onto things I absolutely LOVE about this game: 1. There is no feeling of being rushed, you can really go at your own pace. You can stay up all night long if you want to, but there is something nice about it only growing dark at near midnight, so you know it's time to head back to the farm and stash the stuff you found. I don't feel stressed while playing, it's very relaxing. 2. I love that you can drill and vacuum at the same time. Makes getting through mountains of trash so much easier! 3. I LOVE the way the sprinklers work! They can be set IN BETWEEN the plots where you plant stuff! This is such a novel concept and I love it, it makes me wish other games had this feature. Thank you for making such an awesome sprinkler system!!4. The stamina wheel is nice, because you get a sprint boost for a bit, but there is no penalty for using up the stamina. You don't suddenly slow down when you use it up, you just use it, then wait for it to recharge, and use it again. I only wish it had a bit longer boost!4. The game is addicting and fun. Cleaning up trash, clearing out an area, restoring nature, these all have a very cathartic feel that makes the game rewarding to play, and I keep coming back to it despite the things I don't like. I wish this game was available on PS4 or Switch as well. I would probably buy it on all platforms if it was on more than one, which says a lot to me about whether a game is worth playing. It's just fun. There are probably more things I love, and more things that frustrate me, but I feel like this is a good list. TLDR; it's fun despite little issues it has, and I recommend it. Worth the price of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: is the sort of game that looks great on paper, but the more you play it, the more it looks like they used toilet paper.On the surface, NPLH looks like your typical, casual farming sim: planting, watering and harvesting crops, managing domesticated livestock, collecting resources, placing buildings, etc.  The story even starts out kind of interesting: Everyone is leaving Earth for Mars because the planet is covered in garbage.  Like, literally covered.  Miles and miles of piles and piles of garbage.  Your character loses contact with her grandfather, who remained behind, so she decides to take her trusty super vacuum cleaner and gigantic drill and pop down to the surface to find dear old gramps.  And thus begins the cleaning sim.I'll admit, this aspect of the game certainly scratches a fine itch: Clean and rebuild all the things!  It is quite satisfying to see chunks of garbage whisked away, leaving large, open swathes of land for you to later fill up with more garbage, like comically over-sized tea sets and ridiculously tiny paintings.  So far, so good.  There are even some cute touches like being able to name each individual animal AND place comical hats on their heads!But, that's where the fun ends, and the frustration starts.From the moment you land, it's apparent the developers couldn't decide what kind of game they wanted this to be: is it a farm-sim? Is it an open-world exploration? Is it a combat game? Is it a puzzle game? Are robots good guys or bad guys?  At least one thing it is not: a Romance sim. There are absolutely no social aspects in this game: No romance plots, no birthdays to track, no gifts to give. Sorry Portia and Stardew lovers, this game is NOT for you.  The very first character you encounter is a talking chicken.  No explanation of why it talks, but you have no choice but to start following its instructions in rebuilding the farm, rather than immediately seeking your missing grandfather.  Which pretty much sets the theme for the rest of the game:  Meet someone, do a large series of unreasonable tasks, only for them to tell you "sorry, your grandfather is in another castle," go to the next zone, lather, rinse, repeat. Once you finally do find him, the game inexplicably changes into a shooter game powered by... the talking chicken from chapter one, who is now a super chicken that you can launch (), destroying everything in its path, making that final level utterly pointless in the first place.   I'd spoil the ending for you... except there really isn't one.  Much like the rest of the game, it doesn't appear that the developers were able to figure out where they wanted to go, so they just kind of... stopped writing.  I've seen better plots in triple-x movies. More satisfying, too.  Still a better love story than Twilight, though.The entire game is plagued with more typos than I've seen since the first Pokemon article appeared on Wikipedia.  I get that the developers are Polish and English isn't their native language, but if they paid for localization, the least they could have done was paid someone literate to do it.  Even using Google translate would have worked better than whatever they did.While the bugs in the game are few (beyond the typos), those that exist are pretty nasty, and potentially, could destroy your hardware.  Simple things like duplication bugs (which sometimes overwrite existing items), or accidental destruction of mandatory quest items exist, as well as the more serious achievements-running-backwards, and let's not forget the tiny "If you set your graphics too high, your video card might burst into flames" problem.  That these bugs and typos still exist months after release while the developers are pushing out new games is exceedingly disappointing.While not bugs, per se, the inconsistencies of the game magnify that frustration considerably: Why do characters and quest items change names with no explanation? Why can I stack 50 jars of preserved fruit, but only 10 stacks of the fruit I'm preserving it from?  And why is it that pet food can be carried in any amount?  Why can't I make an omelet with a duck egg?  Why can't I make cheese and goat cheese in the same device?  If jars of food are the currency(?!), why aren't fruit preserves considered jars of food?!?! Is the game playable?  Yes, I managed to complete it, as well as all 158 achievements.  Was it enjoyable?  At first, but that dropped off faster than a roller coaster.  This is a game that had immense amounts of potential, but was failed by developers who didn't take the time to polish() this very rough stone.2.5 out of 5 stacks of garbage.  In this case, fewer would be better.

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential. I don't usually do reviews, but I thought this game deserved it. I've been wanting to play this game for a while now and I finally got it.There are some good things (like the character's art and little pictures that show up <3, so gorgeous!) but I was expecting so much more... I played almost 2 hours so I can't say for sure how the story goes but there were many little things bothering me during the short amount of time I played that I'm not sure I want to get back to it... I'll try to list them all here:1. I'll start with the graphics. From the store images, you can see that the game is fairly simple, but what bothered me was the how dark the game is. And at the same time, when it's night, it's not dark at all, it just feels like the brightness of my monitor was lowered (no color changes, etc). If I turn the brightness of the graphics all the way up, the outside areas look great but inside the house, it feels like the sun came for a visit. The walls SHINE.2. Sound design: the music is okay, and the noises were meh. It feels like there wasn't much thought put into it. Also, while in the tutorial area, I felt like there were two songs playing at the same time? Speaking of tutorial area, it was kinda meh as well.3. It feels like a game for kids. Not sure how to explain this but it just felt strangely (poorly) simple. That wouldn't be a problem if it weren't for some specific things such as at some point I just "fell asleep" and was transported back home. No explanation why, no warnings, no nothing. I figured it was because I died from the robot attacks?4. Lack of consistency in the gathering of items: some you need to use the vacuum, some you need to interact with, some just come to you...5. The characters you meet feel fairly shallow. Also, why aren't they cleaning the trash? D: they are in the middle of huge piles of trash... which also makes me think ... why is humanity leaving the earth behind and moving to Mars since one single person with a vacuum could clean a bunch of stuff (and don't tell me they don't know how to do that machine because they sell upgrades for the stuff that you have)6. It has a few bugs - materials that take forever to come to you or don't came at all, visual bugs when you are in higher places, etc.7. It's HARD on the computer. Look, I don't have a pc that's worth that much but it's still pretty good. It runs V Rising, Baldur's Gate and few other heavy games on max graphics with no problem... but this game, I had to put on Medium, otherwise I could play using print-screens that it would feel smoother.Overall, I'm not sure I would recommend this game. Actually, I don't. Unfortunately.I think the idea behind it had so much potential, and I had a feeling that it would be a casual chill game... but now I feel it's just forgettable.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely cosy farm game with a unique eco twist. As you try to find your Grandad, you must clear rubbish from the world by breaking it down with your drill, then sucking it up to recycle it with your vac. Plant and harvest crops to trade for perks, equipment and upgrades for your tools. You can also raise animals and collect their produce.As you clear the dirt and debris from the land, new areas become accessible for you to explore. You can also craft items and decorate your home on the farm.It's a fairly easy game to attain 100% achievements too, very satisfying and relaxing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only steam game I've ever requested a refund for in having an account for over 17 years.What seemed like a charming casual clone of the beloved stardew valley, or other similar games turned out to be not so much.  Playing the tutorial made me realize how "early" this early access title actually is.  The water mechanism (right click) sometimes took several tries, or distances to the plants to figure out, making it frustrating.  Placing objects like the wooden box to collect the loot was not placing correctly, again frustrating. Collecting my items from the recycler made them clip past the fence and thus was unable to collect them.  Right clicking on plants does not harvest them as the sign next to them says, you have to click E -this is clearly just a bug, but contributed to the overall decision IMO that this game is very-very early access, and not worth the 75% off price tag... Getting into the world after completing the tutorial, and the frame rate cutting in half immediately, shows the optimization levels of the game are also vastly underwhelming.  I'll wait til this gets a full 1.0 release and then read the reviews and watch youtube videos to determine if the state of the game has improved enough to warrant buying it again.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game!Destroying, vacuuming up, and recycling trash is really satisfying, as once it's gone it never respawns. Slowly but surely, the game world gets cleaned up.Lots of animals of different species to help, lots of crops to cultivate and harvest, lots of map to explore, and lots of stuff to collect.Even on the hardest difficulty, it is quite easy to have more than enough of everything, especially Jars (game currency). However, farming, animal husbandry, and cooking makes for fun and relaxing gameplay.Combat is simple and straightforward, and enemies are not complicated or difficult to defeat.Spiders are the most common enemy type, which may be a problem if you suffer from arachnophobia, despite the spiders being robots.The game is easy, so if you're looking for a challenge you won't find one here. If, however, you're looking for something casual and relaxing, you probably will like this game.I haven't run into any bugs apart from enemies and trash piles becoming invulnerable, and those are easy to solve by closing and relaunching the game.Many if not most of the achievements have punny names, which in my book is a definite bonus.

_childDocuments_.review: The most recent update has changed the game and not for the better. I now have issues with framerates causing the game to jitter and lag and lock up. I have issues with severe motion sickness with how the character moves. The screens arent loading properly, crops and eggs and such arent loading in so they remain invisible in the game. The position of the crafting station has things catching at the top and not falling into my inventory. I then have to move into the house, sleep and reload and then HOPE they'll let me vacuum the item up. It doesn't always work so I have to try multiple times. Animals are walking on water where you cant reach to tame them for your farm. I can't even get the dog because he keeps glitching into a wall/rock. Sometimes the load ins cause issues like your honey being available to collect infinitely or the eggs just being available non stop. Which same may think is good but it's still an issue all the same. Overall what was a wonderful game to pass the time and enjoy myself relaxing in now makes me motion sick, lock up in certain zones and unable to do the activities properly. Maybe they'll fix all these issues but they've had a few hot fixes since the big patch causing these issues and things haven't changed.

_childDocuments_.review: 2nd Edit: The quest issues have been fixed to my knowledge and I was able to progress.The hitbox collision is still an issue, but the game is back to being finishable. The game gets kind of buggy as you progress, animal pathing preventing you from building things anywhere they step, piles of junk not disappearing when you vacuum them up, or they disappear but their collision box is still there and remains there post-restart. The combat is not pleasant, and the fanfare of progressing is almost non-existent. I feel like the story could have gone harder with the whole 'rebuilding town' idea and bringing all the distant villagers back together to collaborate on saving their home. The vacuuming and animal care has gotten better over time and is rather satisfying now. I think I've vacuumed almost everything away at this point. Honestly the vacuuming drives the plot forward far more than grandpa does, as basically nobody has heard of him for months except the last person you meet. I think more story moments would add a lot of value to the characters and the player to really flesh out this Wall-E-like planet.I love that every character has a unique reason to stay on Earth, I just wish the story did more with them after their 1 or 2 personal questions are answered.---------------------------A good game that needs some story re-organizing, combat needs improving (but is serviceable), and some QoL fixes. I love digging through the stacks of trash. I think there's a good 'buried stuff to trash pile' ratio. I think the game would benefit from the story being introduced in a shorter manner. The first questions you're going to the farm to answer is "where is my grandpa" and "is he okay?" to which for the last 4 hours I've been met with 'I'll explain whether or not your grandpa is even alive after you do this long laundry list of tasks'. Then the next guy you meet wants you to make the chickens love you before he's willing to tell you if your grandads even alive either. I feel like I'm being prevented from even starting the story! It feels like they're all pulling a huge ♥♥♥♥-move against this girl who came all the way back from their coveted station-placement to make sure her last living family member is still alive. I'd compare the feeling to waiting at the airport. You get the quest item they wanted and suddenly you need to do another task for them before they'll tell you anything, then they just keep pulling the rug out from under you. Ffs chicken! Let me play the game! You've got such an impactful setup to the story, but you won't let me explore it until the chickens adore me! (this happens on several occasions btw)Other than that frustration I'm still having a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: First of, my setup:GPU: GTX 3070CPU: Ryzen 7 5800X @ 3.8GHzMemory: 16Gb DDR4 3600MHz 16-16-16-36OS: Win 10 Pro (build 19042)Why you should not buy this game:-Game suffers from extremely poor FPS, no matter what settings.-Camera speed is extremely inconsistent, not only does it force some very weird and laggy mouse acceleration, but the speed of the camera also very inconsistent.-Forced MSAA, everything looks just a little more blurry then it has to be, even when disabling all other effects.-Combat, Gathering, Planting.... everything is extremely clunky and inconsistent.-Audio is all over the place. sometimes there is audio, other timed its only left channel, or only right, sometimes there is no audio at all. except for the music, you will hear the same ~10sec looped music all the time....-Little to no animations, just basic animations.-Movement on terrain is extremely inconsistent. you can walk up some trees, but if there is a light slope then its up to the gods if you can manage to traverse it.-No jumping. This wouldn't be a problem, but because of how inconsistent the terrain movement is in the game you will find yourself swearing over how there is no jump mechanic in the game all the time.There are so many other things wrong with the game you could write a 100 page essay.This game might be OK in a year or two. but TBH, when the devs cant even nail the feel of _ONE_ core mechanic of the game, then you know you have some really bad devs.The only thing nice about the game is the art direction. props to whoever is responsible for that.But the game coding is down the dumpster. its a mess...TL:DR. wait until 2022 to play/buy the game.There is no fun here at this moment to be had, just frustration.

I love the idea of cleaning up the land and re-building it, it makes me feel accomplished in what progress I make in the game. It sets a pretty lonely tone pretty well since there's like 6 humans (so far) in total and majority of the land is just animals and robots. I truly enjoy the self-pace of the game and as someone who gets antsy with fighting, I truly enjoy the fact that the robots don't re-spawn, it gives me less stress and more opportunities to explore the map and take in the scenery without having to fight for my life every five seconds. _childDocuments_.review: Pros: This game has a lot of character and spirit. The look of the game is appealing, the content is fun, and the farming is fulfilling. The animals are cute and petable and the main character collects so many adorable little pets. You get cute little robot friends as well! You are flooded with resources throughout the game, giving players plenty to do and build what they want and alter their home with new furnishings and such. The game feels unfinished, which is to be expected, but everything that is currently there is beautiful. Reminds me of some of my favorite farm sims, from My Time at Portia to Animal Crossing and Story of Seasons, but without the romance options. This game is both peaceful and familiar and strange all at once. Love it.Cons: There are still LOADS of problems with this game. - Some weird visual glitches and settings basically have to be all the way down not to fry your machine. The game is not designed to run on a typical home gaming PC at all. This game needs some serious updating to take care of the lag, the visual glitches, and the way it runs. And my laptop is brand new with an SSD!- Combat feels like it was added as an afterthought. The enemies are the same all throughout the game and are mostly more annoying than dangerous.- There is no hint system for finding your way around, which is good for me (I like getting lost looking for things) but might be annoying to newer video game players or younger players.- One of the most necessary components of upgrades is a very limited resource. In fact, it's so limited that players cannot build all of the upgrades in the game. This is incredibly frustrating, as I can no longer build the upgrades to the decorations bench to make more furniture and decorations for my house. That made me incredibly sad. - Some of the quests bug out.- Some of the interact-able items are too high or low for the MC to reach which is super super frustrating. - Some other small visual and other things that are more annoyances, but can still annoy me a lot, like the fact that the deer you can get as pets run really fast, and I'm just like WTF, let me catch you and pet you, you ungrateful four-legged moron. I can't FEED you if I can't CATCH you. Overall worth playing, but keep in mind it's got a long way to go to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I really love this game! There is something high satisfying about vacuuming up rubbish and recycling it!. It has robot mobs to fight which helps break up the time with some action. I do find having to buy the recipes in one area and build the corresponding item in another a bit tedious but its not a big deal. I also find the underground area to be very maze like with door locked by finding "buttons". Its an annoying area IMO but again its just part of the game. For me the game is relaxing and time consuming. There are some minor nuances as with most early access games but nothing major. The glitches are not to bad and the menu screen allows you to "unstuck" whenever you need to. Placing items as others have noted does have its challenges but I am hopeful that will be fixed at some point.   I high recommend if you just want a semi easy relaxing way to pass the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game which has so much potential, so much hope and promise and possibility.  But it falls short in almost every way.  The theming seems great.  A post-apocalyptic farming sim where you restore nature to the world and have fun adventures along the way.  Kinda like My Time at Portia but with more of an Eco Focus right? _childDocuments_.review: The world, music, soundscape and concept are quite delightful and I've spent quite a few hours playing already. Unfortunately bugs and design choices that make the game less fun and relaxing than it could be. The nearly all the issues I've had relate to either the reticle, inventory management or navigation.1. When you've opened a chest, the first item in the inventory is targeted and stays stuck there regardless of where you point the mouse. Unsticks eventually, but can't find a reliable way besides multiple clicks and often accidentally picking up the first item in inventory.2. Reticle aim has little to nothing to do with which structure, object or animal you're aiming at. This is true for trying to select a chest to open, an animal to feed or picking up a placed structure with R.3. After pressing R on a structure to pick it up you have to use the mouse to confirm. This clunky kind of confirmation is used in other places in the game too. A hold-press to pick up or press once to pick up and second time to confirm would be much more user friendly.4. Reticle targeting for the water hose. By all means, make the arc of the water a thing so you have to aim higher to get it further away. But if I need to aim 2cm higher AND 2cm to the left to hit a water bucket switch then there's something wrong.5. The reticle is placed well above the character's head so for aiming purposes I tend to land up with the camera sitting 45 to 50 degrees above the character. This becomes troublesome indoors or going under trees as your view gets blocked. Sometimes objects near the camera will disappear from view, an expected mechanic, but not always.6. Vacuum targeting. I get that you can upgrade it, but even upgraded the targeting of the vacuum is pretty bad. The vacuum will just miss things if you're facing down a slope, even if you point the camera as far down as you can. Which of course is not great for a game where you're almost constantly moving.7. The farm is incredibly small for the amount of stuff you can build. And with animals wandering wherever they want and blocking the placing of building, this is incredibly frustrating. You can't get them to move either.8. Not sure if the expectation is that you build all over the map, but having everything all over the place is already annoying. Already noticed this in the case of the second llama shack that's somewhere random with no map marker, so I'm expected to remember where it is. Similarly for the fox sanctuary. Not sure if the boar sanctuary is also a source of something.9. Quest and normal navigation. The map is mostly useless in this regard. There are so many things to find and places you need to revisit as you upgrade gear to be able to reach new locations. There really needs to be markers on the maps for things you've found, be that boars, buildings/caves etc that you can enter or structures like the llama shack that isn't at the farm. If possible also some sort of completion stats for buildings and areas as you eventually lose track of which buildings and structures you've visited and cleared out. I'm pretty sure there's still a room accessible by a manhole cover that I couldn't clear early on but cannot find again.10. Inventory management is pretty terrible, especially later in the game when you start collecting a lot of stuff. Objects do not always autostack so you land up with more than one incomplete stack of an item. Unstackable decoration items (like the chicken decoration) just take up unnecessary space. Addition of a "sort" button on chests and the inventory would help, as would putting the chest and inventory side by side so there's less scrolling needed.[Update] Noticed you can disable the reticle which leads to me naturally keeping the camera lower. Which suggests that it should be moved down. On a 38" monitor at 3840x1600 it sits about 2cm above the characters head and would be better just above their head. The character could also be moved slightly to the right (or left, but I think right works nicer since the waterhose is in your right hand) but keep the endpoint of the stream of water from the hose at the center of the screen. This might make the aiming feel less clunky and prevent the character from blocking your view of whatever you're aiming at.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one. I enjoyed it enough to finish, but it is so flawed and buggy that I would have a hard time recommending it to anyone else. It only feels fair to give a thumbs up but think long and hard before buying.I spent over 60% of my playtime just mindlessly drilling and vacuuming. Dozens of hours. I never would have finished this game without shows/movies going at the same time.I enjoyed building up my farm and unlocking new crops, animals, and buildings. Clearing trash did have a zen like quality to it, it's just that there was way too much of it and very little of it felt optional. Quests were decent enough to give me some sort of goal.Unfortunately turning in the quests was awful. The map lacks markers for where important NPCs are and nothing shows which way the player is facing, making navigating the world needlessly difficult. Additionally quest objectives frequently do not have a directional arrow in the quest tracker.And now for a long list of bugs, none game-breaking but there's so many they really add up:  - Transferring items out of storage is broken unless you first mouse over your inventory on the bottom half of the screen.- Animals stack up on top of eachother and targeting is buggy making them incredibly difficult to tend manually.- Animal gathering automation frequently bugs out and stops while mostly empty, leaving animals untended.- Key items can drop through the ground if picked up while your inventory is full.- There are areas you can walk out of bounds or fall through the world.- Some animals can bring you currency which gets stuck in your inventory with no way to get it properly in the currency storage.Tons of mindless repetition, bad map/quest UI, lots of frustrating medium/minor bugs. I had a decent enough time with the aid of something else keeping my mind occupied, but buyer beware.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: This had the potential to be a good game. It still does, honestly. There are parts that are interesting. The farming could be fun. The cleaning could be fun. But there are just so many little problems that just add up to it just - not being fun.There is no inventory sort option. This makes managing your inventory incredibly obnoxious. Using objects in the world is sometimes overly precise which makes everything annoying. Want to talk to an NPC? Harvest a crop? Pet your dog? Hope your camera is pointed in  the right direction and you're standing in exactly the right spot.Quests are buggy. You'd assume quest items would despawn once the quest is complete. They do not. This leaves you with a slowly increasing pile of junk you can't do anything with as you can't discard quest items. (You can, thankfully, store them, but you can't throw them out or drop them.) There are reports of quests glitching out if you do them in the wrong order - I can't personally confirm this, but I did encounter a quest NPC before I was supposed to, and while this didn't break everything, it did require me to backtrack to do a thing I was intended to do earlier before the NPC worked.There's still a chance that the game may come together in the future as it updates, but in its present state, I wouldn't recommend it.

Field squares? Stacks of ten. Food? Stacks of ten. Seeds? Stacks of 50. Barely a third of the way through the game I'm having to juggle a dozen treasure chests. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim back when it was $5 because the screenshots reminded me of My Time at Portia, a game that I quite enjoyed. I decided to wait until the first major update before going in and seeing how the game played. After 5 hours, I cannot fathom how low standards for video games people have that the current aggregate user score on Steam is "very positive". I can excuse the bugs, lag, and overall jank, but this game commits what I consider to be the worst cardinal sin one can make in the games industry; It isn't fun.Throughout the entire 5 hours session I had, 90% of my time was spent holding down left click to destroy garbage, and then holding down space to vacuum it up. I am not exaggerating. All of the farming, crafting, and building is just a paper-thin veneer over the egregious monotony that is actually less fun than doing your taxes.I encountered a huge number of bugs, but I won't mention them here. I also won't mention the handful of English errors, since that also will probably be ironed out. Instead, I will mention things that I think are game-ruining if not addressed.1. The lag. This is one of the worst optimized games I have ever played. To my memory, the only worse game I've played is Subnautica. The frame rate slows down to a crawl most of the time, which I first thought to be because of the piles and piles of trash the game had to account for, but it even happens in areas already cleared of trash.2. There are too many items, and half of the existing items either don't have a use, or don't have enough uses. This one I think will be fixed with time, but the category of item I can't ignore here is food. Aside from the ingredients to make one dish one time, there is literally no reason to farm. At all. Food can be used to preserve for currency, but I had 2000+ before leaving the first area, which is hundreds more than every upgrade in the game requires. Food can't be used for anything by itself, which I think is a gigantic fatal flaw for a farming game. You make big farming plots, put sprinklers, build coops, and pig stys, only to realize that after one or two harvests, there's literally no reason to use them anymore.3. Recipes are the only reward for exploring. Recipes are what you need to cook dishes to trade for upgrades, and these are the only non-renewable resource that's given for exploration. This doesn't seem terrible until you realize that the dishes can be cooked without the recipes by experimenting with ingredients. This means that if you look up a recipe guide, you can, in essence, skip the entire game's progression the second you pick up the necessary ingredients. The underground in its entirety becomes redundant if you do this, and it's a shame since that's the only area with good level design.4. The game is lacking even the basics of player options. There is no sprint, no jump, no block, and no dodge. You can't name your character or customize them in any way. There is no way to heal outside of sleeping. The game won't let you pick up any item when your inventory is full, even if the item in question would fit into an existing stack. Passing out at 22:00 doesn't incur any penalty. The buttons and "puzzles" scattered about don't have any reason for existing. When the button for a gate is two feet away in plain sight, it makes you wonder why they even bothered to include them.I could still keep going, but this rant is long enough. In time, I hope the devs can make something actually good here, but this needs some serious work before it can become anything I can even remotely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: As long as you mix up the exploration with the farming you can find a nice balance to the game play. If you explore until you can't get any further you'll have just spent a very long time drilling and vacuuming only to now be stuck on the farm until you make enough preserves to get the tool upgrades you need to go further... so grindfest to grindfest. I recommend making yourself go back to the farm regularly to keep things moving along. Plant your trees early as they take a while to grow but can then be harvested daily and require no care. Easy money makers once you can make preserves. There is a lot to craft and the game is very cute. The NPCs are quirky which was nice. You do end up on 'fetch quests' and 'make this quests' but why not make the pig-crazy man happy?If the controls feel wonky double check the mouse sensitivity settings. I have no idea why mine were on the lowest setting when I started, but that was awful. Easily fixed though.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cleaning up the clutter then this is for you. You will grind a ton of garbage in order to clean the place up. For me, it's fun. Still needs a lot of improvement but I can see this as a fun game for those who like farming, crafting, and the post-apocalyptic theme. What needs to be fixed:-Being able to move the camera when planting seeds (If it can be done when watering the plants or when gathering, it should be capable to do for planting)-Same goes for plotting crafts like the coop and storage, need to be able to move the camera whilst doing it and to be able to rotate them-To be able to pick up crafts after making room in inventory. Not sure if it's just me but I couldn't pick up the coop when I had full inventory when I made room for it. It was just sitting next to the workshop. When I clicked "e" to try to pick it up, it kept putting me in the workshop menu. I tried "r" and spacebar, didn't work either. I had to quit the game without saving to redo it.-Wish we could dodge when fighting the robots as well as to be able to jump.-Wish we could drop inventory instead of throwing it in the trash to make room (unless I didn't know there was an option to drop)-Need to polish up some of the story writing. For example, in the quest called "Preserves Needed," it said "Before I can do that however someone needs to teach me how to do that. Grandpa told me about a nice shopkeeper living close downhill, he might just help me." The sentence could've simply said, "Before I can do that someone needs to teach me how. I remember Grandpa told me there's a nice shopkeeper living downhill, who could help me."-They should add achievements as well as cards to craft them into a badge that we can show off on our profiles :DOverall, it has beautiful artwork and a nice soundtrack. It's fun and I look forward to when it all comes together! P.S. I really dig their loading screen, I'd like it as a background for my pc or steam account. Maybe even have steam chat emotes/stickers!

_childDocuments_.review: At first you feel like Wall-E cleaning up the world. Then you realize that's all you do and it gets boring. This game feels like it wasn't completed and the dev got bored and decided to ship the game. The controls are very clunky and very hard to get used to. Combat is underwhelming and stiff. Farming is an absolute chore. And the story is very bland. It's not all bad, the visuals are really nice and you can build a nice house if you take the time. The music was also top notch. I beat it and even got all the achievements but even on sale I don't think I would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: So far I really like this game. It's very simple and relaxing. For $5 I feel it really is worth it.Pros: -Farm and ranching is very easy-The game is very pretty in its... waste land ascetic -Controller users can easily learn to play this on a keyboard-Great time killer -Music is nice Cons: -Clipping issues with the terrain. Mostly ascetic, but still a bit annoying-Getting stuck on terrain you really shouldn't be getting stuck on. I'm getting stuck on the edge of a lump or grass/dirt or at the very corner or a rock I'm not even touching. I end up not being able to run away or move out of the way of an enemy attack. -Watering. It was great for a while. I started collecting apple seeds and all of a sudden I cant water my crops. The action doesn't work at all. -No way to heal. I'm not sure if that's the point, so maybe this is just a personal opinion. It would be nice to have a way to heal. Maybe food or a spa. I know you heal when you sleep, but I would like to heal while I'm out roaming and collecting. -Everything is TOO easy to buy. I usually like easy relaxing games, but being able to buy everything upgrades you so fast there's just no challenge at all. -When I try to pet/clean live stock and bots, sometimes the action doesn't work. -No jumping. I enjoy jumping. So this is probably just a personal preference. But it's really odd to find a game in this style that you can't jump in. -Screen tearing and frame rate. Turning on VSync did help a bit. -No controller support. -NPC? Ive been playing for 4 hours and have only found 1 NPC; the guy by the store (don't remember his name). I'm not including the NPC by your home when you finish the tutorial. All in all I do enjoy this game. I look forward to updates as we go and really hope these bugs are fixed soon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun concept, but I ended up refunding because inventory management is unbearable. There's no sort function of any kind, and if you want to move multiple stacks of items -- which you'll end up with a lot of very quickly -- it requires clicking and dragging each one, one by one (vs. what most other games that use shift + click or something to automatically move items).I'll probably revisit this game when it's finished.

_childDocuments_.review: Was enjoying it but the game allows you to recycle quest items when no longer needed so I trusted it when it told me I can recycle something, I still needed some of the item (quality wood) and now cannot complete that particular quest line as far as I can tell as I now do not have enough of said item.A lot of invisible object remaining after removing trash piles which gets annoying,Inventory is also annoying after a while as you can quickly get a huge pile of items and the chests just aren't big enough for my playstyle of gathering everything.Farming is interesting in that you don't buy seeds to sell produce so much in this game as you find seeds to plant and then turn into food jars (either raw or processed) that you use to buy upgrades and I find the farming side to honestly be bad as you can get so much items and have little use for it especially after upgrades no longer need said item as getting money is easy with little to no effort really.Honestly would have given a positive review if I didn't come across the bug that allowed me to recycle an item I still needed. Think it happened because I found them before the quest was given or something.Destroying the trash piles is oddly satisfying but inventory getting filled fast at the beginning ruined that satisfaction a bit, Need to balance trash clearance and farming to properly upgrade gear to make that better so my fault to some extent.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game, so sometimes a bit too buggy for my liking.This game has been on my wishlist for a while, then it sat in my library for a while and now I have finally found some time to try it.I have to admit that I love the idea (living in a world full of human trash that has to be removed and recyled. I also like the mechanic with the vacuum (reminds me of slime rancher) and the graphic style. There is not much of a story but you find quest as you discover the map.There is also a good amount of stuff to do: taming animals and robots, fighting weird lawnmower machines, restoring the environment, recycling, building etc.Now on to the problems of the game:- the resolution is not the best, in the tutorial the instructions are a struggle to read because of this (really blurry)- watering plants only works half the time, honestly the thing that annoys me most- day-night cycle is a bit aprupt (it gets darker from one moment to the next) and at 10pm you just faint (to be fair you just faint and wake up at home without losing any stuff but it's still weird because it happens without any warning)- sometimes walking is a chore because the ground is not even, hence you sometimes get stuck n stuff and have to wiggle around until you are free again- combat is not really fun. it's not bad but it doesn't add much to the game especially since there is no explanation for why these machines are "bad"? (you can kill then with like 4 hits usually, but there is no dodge, you have to move out of the way with WASD and that is way too slow)- sometimes I feel that there are instructions missing. it really takes a while to understand what you have to do and hwo to do it (progress wise)- at least one area is really laggy (the area with the shop)- the map is abolutely useless, I NEVER know where I amThe game is only out for half a year so I think they will still work on fixing most of these issues. I enjoyed the few hours I have spent with this game so far, so I'll give this a recommendation. Just know that it's far from perfect before you buy.EDIT: Now, after finishing the game, I thought I'd add a few more things I noticed in the later areas. - First of all, the one area that was laggy stayed laggy even after removing EVERYTHING (trash, animals, ect) from it, sadly and it was a pain everytime I had to pass it. The other areas were fine, mostly, sometimes a bit slower but not as bad as the store part.- The game was very slow throughout and very repetetive, I personally enjoyed it but it might not be everyone's cup of tea. There were three doors that I could not open no matter how much I looked for ways to them, Idk if they are supposed to be added in an update. There are also bridges that you can walk along but they don't seem to go anywhere?- There are 3 'chapters' with their individual quests. I finished all of them but one quest is not finsihed because I did one quest part before talking to a certain person.- Some trashpiles are floating and you can't remove them for some reason and it's really unsatisfying to walk through an otherwise clean world but have these random pieces of trash everywhere you can't get ridd of.- After cleaning everything that is removable and collecting all of the treasure boxes, I was not able to get all the updates because I was missing upgrade parts, very annoying.- The map got more and more annoying the more I discovered, especially the underground is almost impossible to use as "Short cuts" as it is supposed to because you just get lost.- the farm area is way too small, there is no place to fit all the animal pens, fields and trees there.- there are a lot of ressources that you just don't need, they just clogg up your inventory
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very relaxed. There is no time pressure, combat is simple, farming is simple, most quests are simple. I like the idea of cleaning up the landscape to progress. It takes some time to do, but does not feel like that endless grinding you have to do to progress in some games. It feels like a simpler and laid back 'My Time at Portia' .The new control system introduced on April 29 is much more intuitive and easy to use than the original one.    My only complaint is the view is third person only. I prefer first person games, because the third person view can make me dizzy after watching the spinning landscape.    i would recommend this to anyone who likes casual building/crafting/farming games.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: I see lots of potential, but the beginning feels very lacking, and there seems to be no way to sprint or jump. _childDocuments_.review: Genuinely an amazing game, I am super excited to see how it plays upon full release. _childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that should be bought a year from now. It's core game loop is very solid, you will find it very soothing to clean up garbage but it's held back by the lack of polish and obvious bugs.Don't expect Stardew Valley, or Harvest Moon depth to the farming sim parts - this isn't that kind of game. That being said, this game does deliver some of the implementation on the planting mechanic I've seen in a 3D game.Getting food for your animals is my biggest gripe, you can't bulk craft them which means you're standing around for 15 minutes shaving away at your potato supply while you play crafting station whack-a-mole.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like games with "lets clean this place" concept. So i bought this game on the first day of full release, but it's still feels really unfinished :(Pro: - The trash mining/vacuuming was really fun core gameplay mechanic for me. - The artworks for illustrations (for example in the quest book) are really nice. (animals in hats are super cool :D ) - the 3D modelled animals are also cute. - The amount of content seems good for me but...Contra: - ...it's needs to be polished. Really. - The battle feels like "Ok. But why?" The battle mechanics are just a little above minimal. - The quest mechanics are also unfinished / unpolished :(For example when you spray some water on the toxic piles and they just pop out from the exisence. Or when you place campfires to melt the ice for wheat, when you alredy can grow as much wheat on the farm, as you want... - I've got the feeling, that the game encourages you to farm more, and more, but for what? The upgrades seemed pretty cheap after one point. -  If you like the concept, wait for a few monts, and check the roadmap.But if you like what the developers alredy done, and would like to support them, buy it.Overall it's a fun game, so I'll chek the updates sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my honest review, and I will mention the good and the bad; let's start off with my initial experience that many people would benefit from knowing prior to buying this game.TLDR: I highly recommend it; please do not go in expecting a very clean game without buggy features. It is a super relaxing small game, the story is easily completable in under 20 hours, and I'm pretty sure it is completable even in under 12 hours. Many improvements are needed to make the game much better plus more enjoyable.I started off with the tutorial (I normally skip anything related to tutorials in essentially almost all games), and right off the bat, I was unsure if I was going to like it. The tutorial is straightforward for the MOST part, but it became a little confusing towards the end, and I was unsure whether or not I was fully done with the end sections, such as the process of feeding the chickens, etc.I was also slightly disappointed with not being able to take off this hideous outfit on my character; I was slightly under the impression that from the depicted banner, I could look like that or have that choice. This was not the case.I reached the end of the tutorial slightly confused, and then I decided to travel further into the map to my area. It then started to get interesting.  I was greeted by the main character throughout the story, a chicken that initially guided you in what you needed to do and how to "move forward". Your place was infested with complete trash, and for someone like me, I like to have a very clean area, and everything must be cleared prior to moving forward. The controls are pretty straightforward, and I was surprised that I didn't really find someone to immediately suggest the mouse sensitivity because the start mouse sensitivity for looking around is horrendously slow. I learned something later on for personal preference, and now this isn't the achievement I hoped it would be, which would be to clean each area spotlessly. If you want to do it, I suggest holding down your vacuum button (if you're keyboard and mouse) and then holding down the button to drill through everything. This helps suction a lot of the trash WHILE you're drilling through so much trash. I played this game at a pretty slow pace and how I wanted, which the game allowed you to do so.Gameplay overall, it was a very relaxing game, and the ending came quickly. It was slightly anti-climatic because there was no actual cutscene.... **SPOILER**You are given a choice to go to Mars or stay on Earth, which the options mean that you can still do whatever you want in the game without exiting or ending the game by going to Mars (now I only read this through Reddit forums; I selected to stay on Earth because it clearly implied that I didn't want to end my play session).This is by no means a clear, clean game without bugs. The recent update to this game to add automation is really nice for farming and planting for you. However, my MOST DISLIKED part of the game is inventory stacking with the number of seeds you obtain; planting apple trees, peach trees, etc., was ABSOLUTELY annoying. You could not neatly stack them closely together or even a decent length away. The game will not allow you to do this as they grow to a decent size, but I felt like it ruined a lot of my plots to be placed down and my ability to add more trees. Yes, the game provides you with many different zones, but I do NOT like the constant zone loading screens, so I try to do ease of access, which is my farm. Another thing I hope to see is increasing the stacks of everything, ESPECIALLY of the veggies + fruits past 10; they take so much space and make you run into inventory space. The bots that collect from animals + harvest do not have very much space, nor are they upgradeable to have a bigger inventory space. It would be cool to see an upgrade to all storage, including the robots. The robots I noticed GLITCH VERY EASILY and would stop actually working or eventually stand still and "harvest" that way but seem to fail to deliver the stuff into their chests. It would be really cool to decide where they could drop off the items in another storage space. Our animals, such as the dog, cat, and raccoon, would have been cooler to allow them to follow you on trips + select the type of breed or collect more. I have not fully investigated this completely.Another issue I ran into was decorating my house, my main room when placing wallpaper; the wall is also painted on the other side, which is the hallway. I try to repaint this, but it ends up repainting my room's wall, too. It was also a hassle to even paint any hallways with wallpaper that required sides of the hallways. I have yet to try the sandbox version of this game. I will put in a review when I do the test after my 100% completion of achievements. PS: I feel like my fully upgraded drill/vacuum hardly made a huge difference. However, GO FOR RANK 3 VACUUM AS SOON AS POSSIBLE.Thanks for reading if you got this far. Lmk if any questions xoxo

_childDocuments_.review: A nice cute game with it's ups and downs. I finished the main story and almost all side quests in 23h. As a total review it's somewhat in middle (maybe towards positive).Positive:- Satisfaction when you clean those huge amount of trash and get to see the landscape clean!- Improving the landscape via quests to make it cleaner/prettier.- Several buildings, upgrades, animals, crops etc..- Pet animals :)Neutral:- Currency is somewhat weird.- Transportation. Although there is a form of fast travel you still have to walk a lot which is getting annoying in big areas you cleared and you have to backtrack several times.- Building space. It would be a lot better to have a big flat area to build as you like. You still have enough space though to get the job down.- Story & Characters. Nothing great there.- Graphics are cute and simple but could have been better. Same goes for level design which is very bad in certain areas.- Enemies. Could have had more variation but still it's plenty to get the job done.Negative:- Several bugs, nothing big but still annoying.- Inventory! Super annoying right of the start. It only has 1 chest with very limited space. Could have been fixed very easily by introducing either bigger containers or larger stacks for items since after a while you end up having tons of chests and managing is just annoying. Best solution currently is to upgrade player's inventory.- It gets very tedious especially in later game. This could have been fixed if there was more automation and more (& cheaper upgrades).- Flowers. Not a single user apart from the looks.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence about this game because of the reviews that said there were a lot of bugs and glitches. I thought I could deal with a few little bugs, so went ahead and bought it, and did manage to get a few dozen hours of decent game play in with only some annoyances, but then, indeed, ran into a huge game-breaking bug.The final zone of the game - what I think was meant to be the climax of the story - didn't load when I re-entered it. Permanently. It's just an empty map now, so I don't know what was there, what was supposed to happen, or what the end of the game is.At the same time, all the animals back on my farm and all of their associated buildings disappeared. I tried reloading several times, but it's all just gone, so I can't continue or complete the game.There are also a few quests that are just broken and impossible to complete, even if the elements of your game don't suddenly fall into the void.So, yeah, don't buy this game. Not sure why it's been "fully released," because it's clearly not ready. Bugs/glitches range from small and irritating to you cannot continue, full stop.Aside from that, although the premise is kind of interesting, there's just a whole lot of potential that was left on the table. The story is pretty basic and shallow. The controls could have been better designed. The hit boxes are a mess. Game play feels both messy and tedious.I explored all of every zone, except the last one since it choked, and the world is pretty empty. You're left wondering if it was really worth cleaning up the garbage at all.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game and the progression seems well thought out, the actual layout of the map, over-abundance of trash (and uselessness of it), and the "doors" as the puzzle-solver component being almost _everywhere_ is just not well thought out.  The designers would do well pushing this more as a "clean up the world and make it nicer" game instead of a "trash everywhere is an obstacle you can push through, and you're just supposed to try to get point A to B".  Also, the piles of garbage in the middle of the dungeon feels just like a new developer thinking "hey  this pile is a pretty pattern, let's just put it here to make the design less empty" instead of any sort of strategic planning.Anyway, I'm putting the game down until it's not early-access.  I was really motivated to level up parts and meet the people, but that is like 5% of this game.  I'm generally disappointed and would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphic is nice, Stardew Valley feelings come up, even though the game definitively is very low content vise. You feel the early access vibe but it works better and seems all in all much rounder then many other early access games. Future areas are already visible and I clearly have the feeling that the developement is very well structured and it does not look like it is going to be abandoned soon.Some Bugs occure but they are not Gamebreaking.The added cleanup feeling and the cute 3D-graphics are something that differs it (in my opiinion positively) from just a stardew valley clone. (Nothing against SV)Story is practically not existing and at the moment the main focus are further areas to be added I have the feeling.The resource and building system is extremely simple, personally I would like some more mechanics that dive deeper in the recycling idea, at the moment there is trash --> usefull material--> buy your stuff at the shop with that and that is it. It would be interesting to see some real live techniques that are used to recycle and separate plastics, metals and electronics, but this could eventually take away the relaxing gameplay...All in all the game is relaxing, nice to view at, the fields and garden objects are beautiful, just the right thing after a long, stress full day if you want just to turn off your brain and get the feeling of doing something useful, before you go to sleep and actually do something useful the next day. Like Viscera Cleanup simulater without the cynicism and dark humor. Looking forward to the new areas.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: I have played many hours of No Place Like Home and completed all of the achievements.  The game has an amazing amount of potential.  It is made up of 4 sections, each providing new animals to add to our farm and new plants to grow and harvest.  The progression is the perfect balance to create a smooth progression.The problem comes in that it feels like an unfinished game.  Almost like it is still in early release.  I initially stay away from early release titles, because I do not enjoy playing half games.  Let me explain and give examples.  In the third area you get access to sheep, and need to do a few of the more complex quests to unlock them.  After doing so you are able to gather wool.  I immediately made the needed upgrades to my farm to allow 10 sheep, the needed amount for an achievement.  Then started gathering the wool.  There are two or three upgrades/objects that can be purchased with wool, one of them being the loom.  The loom turns wool into yarn.  Seeing this I started producing yarn in large amounts, only to find out there is ZERO use for it in the game.  This feels like an entire portion of the game is missing.  This is repeated with flower seeds and gardens.  And seen again in the later plants, olives and cranberries.This leads to another glaring issue, cooking.  At first it does not seem to be a huge issue, but when you realize that cooking is the primary use for all of the farming it becomes so.  This became apparent when I realized that most of my farmed plants went right into the food preserver.  The major issue with cooking is that there is no major benefit to making more complex meals.  Example Sunny Side up, two eggs found early on and easy to make early on.  After eating allows you to sprint without confusing stamina.  Other foods give this same bonus and there are some complicated recipes that do so; however there is no benefit to using a more complicated recipe.  SO through out the entire game I just used eggs, and for healing just baked apples.  No reason to ever cook anything else.  Once again feeling unfinished.Conclusion : The last half of the unlocks add nothing to the play experience leaving the last half of the game feeling incomplete.  The cooking mechanics also feel highly incomplete.This is not about lacking polish, but lacking completeness.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: Good little game, fun, relaxing, easy, kind of like a mix of Stardew Valley & PowerWash Simulator in that you clean the world & build a farm. It does however have a few bugs, quests can break & the ending is kind of a let down (the last zone feels like the devs kind of just gave up & wanted the game done). It is worth having in your library for when you're looking to kill some time just building a little farm with crops & animals, making some produce, planting trees, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: No Place Like Home is a really cute farm game about finding your grandpa and building back up the farm in his absence. NPLH still has a lot of bugs with trash piles that can't be picked up, typos, performance issues, stuttering, fps drops in random spots throughout each map, and clunky building placement and movement controls. However, even with all of these flaws, it is a really relaxing game to play and turn your brain off if you enjoy creating and managing your own farm. I hope the developers continue to add content, optimize the game more and squash bugs since it was a really fun time. Overall, NPLH is a game I recommend but with caution due to it still being a bit rough around the edges and that may turn some people off that would otherwise enjoy the game and its cute art style, 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: Clocked almost 22 hours on the game and managed to finish perhaps 95% of what the early access version has to offer. First impression: reminds me of My Time In Portia minus relationship and town building aspect, instead of mining, you're essentially getting rid of landfills and battling evil bots in exchange for resources while restoring the green in your environment, and that is super satisfying in my opinion.Pros: I see whole lot of potential with the game, the artwork is beautiful and the expansive world is an ambitious feat. There's plenty of resources to be had, in fact too much that I was wondering whether it would make sense in the long run. Cons: The camera movement can be frustrating a tad nauseating. Since the world is quite huge, I find my character walking around a whole lot especially when I'm in the middle of a quest and the time runs out, the grind starts again tomorrow having to 'walk' to the destination. Would be nice to have some kind of transportation upgrade! All in all, love the concept of the game, perfect for OCDs like myself who also loves a farming resource management type of game. Looking forward to the full version!
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: After 30 hours I have all the achievements. I don't see any reason to replay it to be honest. _childDocuments_.review: I started playing the game when it first came out and I have enjoyed the game a lot, but I couldn't play it for a little while and then another update came and the intro was a lot different. I like the change in  the way the controls were explained. I also really like the way it looks. this game is fun.  Not to challenging but challenging enough. nicely  balanced. _childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable, low-impact game ala Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia.While there are small residual issues (more below), No Place Like Home is a unique, well-designed, and caringly-crafted game that will enjoyably occupy a few dozen hours of your time.The great: the backstory, while somewhat derivative, is sculpted into a truly unique form of gameplay. The mechanics are simple and easy to learn, but still allow for leveling both in RPG and player terms. Enemies require some thought and experiementation to overcome, but are not a serious enough of an obstacle to move the gameplay outside of casual. The tech tree is straightforward, and even the most complex items have few prerequisites.The average: While some quests are unique and engaging, too many are similar to each other and begin to feel grindy near the end of the game. The in-game map and fast-travel are designed tightly around the quest chain, but the gameplay isn't that linear, so moving through the world can be tedious and frustrating. The wide variety of crops and animals seems only to exist to feed a few grindy quests. The quest log is quite brief, requiring you to both pay close attention to the easily-skipped dialog and remember across game sessions.The Bad: There are still clearly early-access bugs: several maps are clearly less polished and allow for unintended clipping or getting stuck. The targeting system is abysmal: the hit box for some animals seems infintessimal, and all targeting seems to depend too much on elevation--leading to resources in a depression being un-minable. The simple mechanics stay simple throughout the game, and so by area 2 or 3, you've mastered the technical aspects.Overall, it's an enjoyable game, but it's not for everyone. Even for completionists, there is only about 30 hours of gameplay and 5-6 hours of that will be a grind. However, for those who need a low-impact escape to another world, this game satisfies.
