_childDocuments_.review: Okay. This game is Excellent so far. The trouble with Reviewing a game like this, is finding a way to explain it without making it sound completely dumb. But I shall try. First, Whoever reviewed this game before me, that called it Wall-E: the game, Essentially you're right. This game is the ultimate game for people like myself. I am a part of a strange group of people that enjoyed the Monotony of digging out massive holes and terra-forming in games like Minecraft. I find that to be incredibly satisfying and I cannot put into words how relaxing and rewarding it is. That said, this is a world, filled with junk piles and remnants of the old world, and it's ultimately your job to clean it up. Basic premise, fantastic execution. There is a progression system that relies on building your way up from nothing, or with basic machines, in order to buy recipes from vendors/Barterers, to build even more. Honestly, this game reminds me of My Time At Portia, quite a bit in that regard, (Minus the Town-building, and relationship aspects.) The game does have a "Day to Day" system, much like games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, meaning, your day is saved when you either got to bed, or pass out, and the next day begins. Farming and animal husbandry is very similar as well, but in this case, it's a mix between Robots and Living Creatures. Gathering is tiered to progression, as a game like this should be. Certain blocks cannot be broken unless you have the proper tools. In the same Vein, some areas are quest dependent, and progressing through each one sometimes requires that you complete a part of restoring the zone, in order to move on. (This isn't super intrusive, it's just there, and the way it's done is tasteful.)Farming is similar to tool progression, in the form of, "The Farther you go in the game, The more you unlock, and those items are needed for more recipes." I know that I've said it before but the way that this game builds upon itself is amazing, and I absolutely adore a progression system that isn't "grindy" or forced. This game has just that. Movement. The hard thing about this game is the movement, I feel like it's the only drawback and honestly, it's barely worth griping about, but hear me out. Traditionally, I cannot stand a game that doesn't allow you to jump. This game... you've guessed it.. Does not allow you to jump. This is fine, because it keeps you from fast-tracking through areas that you shouldn't, but it's also annoying when you get hung up on a piece of terrain or an object that really shouldn't be stopping you from moving. The game, however, has an "Unstuck" feature in the game menu, accessible by pressing the ESC key, which, is okay and at least makes it so that you're not wasting a day stuck on a rock. Also, to note, the camera is kind of clunky. It's not horrible, but the camera and targeting systems are not the best. Having an indicator or something of that nature when watering would be insanely helpful, especially since I'm having an issue where farm plots glitch out and cannot be watered unless you find the "Sweet Spot" to water then from. Combat also suffers from this issue. You can swing at an enemy, well within range, but sometimes you miss because of differing elevations, that you cannot seem to notice, or crappy hitboxes, I'm not sure. Combat isn't a main focus of this game, so it's not a huge deal, but... It's a thing. Overall, I adore this game. It being very early access, there's more than enough here for you to be intrigued and want to keep playing. This is a rare thing for an Early Access game these days, and I'll say it now, for $10 it's well worth it. In fact, I'd call it a gem. This has to be the most rewarding game that I've played in a long time. You've seen screenshots, if you're reading this. You know what this game is supposed to be. If you're looking for something similar to Farming sim games, or building, or just laid back, chill games, this one will be perfect for you. Quit thinking about it, it's more than worth the price. ;) Grade-A, devs, excellent job so far, keep up the great work!

_childDocuments_.review: In NPLH you'll play as Ellen, an aspiring Mars colonist that decides to go back to an ecologically-ruined Earth and start a new life, trying to set things right instead of abandoning the planet, alongside her grandfather. Turns out the old man disappeared, so you'll have to help out the few locals that chose staying behind like him, and understand what happened to him. Heaps of trash and crazed robots dominate most landscapes, a result of mankind's outrageous conduct; despite the premise, the settings aren't bleak at all between cute animals (sometimes sentient, for a dash of fantasy...) and bright colors. If this is the post-apocalypse, it doesn't look too grim;  lore and writing feel rather generic, as none of the characters or quests will stick in your mind or really hook players at any point - mostly uneventful.You'll be doing mainly two things in this title: clearing each area from trash using your industrial drills and vacuum, and manage the farm. Despite the biome variations, each area plays out exactly in the same way: (slowly) clear trash, collect everything that drops, open chests, push buttons to open gates, bash robots that attack you... always the same two types, slow, weak, badly animated and with death having no penalty whatsoever. There's no variety, be it in the first or last areas, except the occasional timed buttons or mini puzzle: highly-unusual findings. Quests for NPCs mainly consist in gathering X amount of a resource, going from point A to point B or helping X amount of animals by feeding or herding them - also in this case, missions feel too similar and have no interesting variations at any point.A good number of upgrades like increased vacuum range, drills potency, etc. can be purchased using Preserved Food (currency) alongside specific resources (mostly farm products) - they're marginal improvements that aren't really needed given how miserable enemies are; they won't make the cleaning ops much faster either, except when they allow breaking harder mounds of trash, which is mandatory to progress past some areas.Most farming sims have relations or even romance options with the various characters, other than activities to do alongside them; let's take the famous Stardew Valley, or My Time at Portia as references, to name a couple. Here there is none of that: NPCs act as glorified, static quest "dispensers" with some random dialogue options for lore's sake, and integrated shops for new machines / facilities for the farm. This completely cuts out any attachment the player may hope to develop towards the characters, and makes the story as a whole, a glorified series of chores.While it's initially satisfying to set up your own farm freely, or renovating gramps' old house with furniture, wall paper and other amenities, soon the farming side of things will take an annoying, bleak turn indeed. with the locations divided in "compartments" instead of a smooth open-world, you'll end up without space for facilities end crops, thus develop your farm over several "sections" of the world with a loading screen between each. The normal quality-of-life basic systems such as auto-sorting or auto-stacking are absent, chests can't be marked or named, animals clip into each other and have to be manually harvested for resources - very fun when you have 45 chickens and 30 pigs in five square meters. This all amounts to a tremendous slog of fidgeting with interfaces half the time, misclicks and general annoyance.The farm isn't even that engaging to take care of: crops won't die if you forget to water them, rather not grow. Animals are self-feeding and immortal; automatic systems to water everything are unlocked soon enough, so you can stay away for days without caring, and just go back to dump loot when your backpack is full. Cooking is completely useless, as processing raw materials is just faster to gain Preserved Food, while Trash to recycle is ever-abundant - you won't need the various buffs (speed, damage etc.) food gives anyway, given how easy combat is. The various Tier 2 and 3 machines, expensive and locked behind blueprints, are just redundant and not worth the hassle, as you can build five Tier 1 machines, recyclers to name one, and get the same (or better in some cases) efficiency for half the total cost. Once you set up fields, facilities and everything, even just Tier 1, you are already as good as done with the farm, no more meaningful evolution from that point onward... just redundancies.You can see the lines between the various "tiles" that compose the map. Fall through the map itself at times, get stuck in collisions and have to fast-travel back to fix yourself. Animations? What are those? Better make that gate just disappear as soon as the button is pressed, same for huge blocks of ice, boulders or you-name-it. Break enough trash in an area and see your FPS plummet even with a high-end GPU, as each bit of trash is a standalone physics-enabled object, all with Playstation 2-era graphics, amazing! Did I mention the main quest broke permanently, barring me from finishing the game? Yeah, that should give you the idea of this "1.0" release's state.

_childDocuments_.review: Well! I had a whole review typed out until Steam nuked it, that'll learn me. Let me try again lol.At the time of writing this, I have finished all of the currently available content in No Place Like Home.No Place Like Home is a mostly calm game that features farming, cleaning up the world by drilling and hoovering trash, and occasionally beating up some robots. Cleaning up the world is a large part of it. Seriously. You are going to be clearing a lot of trash. If you think you will get bored by that, don't buy this game. Personally, I enjoyed clearing the trash: It's incredibly satisfying to get rid of it and clear area after area, discovering new seeds and resources as you go.Beyond that, the layout of the trash is not always the same, so there is variety there anyways. And while drilling, you will find robots (who are kind of the ones hoarding the trash) to beat up as well. If you are looking for - or expecting -  complicated puzzles to solve, hard enemies to beat, and maybe a husband or wife à la Stardew Valley or My Time At Portia, this is not the game for you -- you hardly interact with people, and there's certainly no romance to be had.  Equally, although there are "puzzles" of a kind, they aren't particularly complicated, and the enemies aren't tricky to beat, although they do increase in difficulty. Generally, the game is pretty calm and simple. It doesn't introduce any wild mechanics or hugely break from the norm (except in its base idea). The wildest thing is that you can get a pet raccoon WITHOUT acquiring brain worms (look them up. they are real).That sounds a little negative, maybe, but I would still recommend the game. Like I said earlier, it was fun to clear the trash. Beyond that, farming itself is also fun - and it is incredibly satisfying to advance there too, to acquire chickens and then maybe some pigs, to plant higher value crops, etc.Unfortunately, the game is in Early Access, and it shows.Particularly height is a problem in game. You can only interact with things that are exactly at your height - anything that is lower is not interactable with, and anything that is higher you can also not interact with. This is fine in the first areas of the game, but in the current last area, which is hilly, it becomes problematic, because unfortunately, the height levels there aren't adjusted properly. This means you have enemies sinking through the floor of mountains before popping back up when coding kicks in, and enemies that are accidentally not on your height level, which means you can't damage them - but they can damage you. Fortunately, it's usually pretty easy to lure enemies to flat ground and then kill them. The height issues also mean that there are a few - maybe five or six - trash piles that are impossible to get rid of, because they hover slightly above the ground and therefore aren't at the same height as the player. There are also perhaps ten or so trash pillars hovering midair that the player cannot destroy because they're too far up, which is unfortunate. Thankfully, these trash piles and pillars are mostly out of the way in the "highest level" area, so it's not too awful.Apart from that, pets/animals also have problems with height, and occasionally will get stuck on little bumps on your farm, which is a little unfortunate.And I think that we can all be glad that most of the game is spent not talking to the other humans that are left on earth, because what dialogue there is... is full of grammatical and spelling errors. It's certainly still easy enough to understand what's going on, but it does get kind of annoying, and I'm not someone who complains about spelling errors, usually. However, all in all, the bugs that a common player will encounter are NOT game breaking, they're just a little annoying. There is no death in the game, you just fall asleep, so even if you get a little extra damage from an enemy because they are too low for you to hit, it's not that terrible, and like I said earlier, it's easy enough to kite them somewhere that's flat and kill them there. Generally: You will not get a perfect, polished game, but it is worth the money nevertheless. It's calm, mostly relaxing, and pretty satisfying, and I look forward to the new content that is coming.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; fun, but unfortunately very buggy. Might be nice to play on creative, or if you just wanna explore, bonk enemies, and have a cute farm to tend to without caring about the story, then knock yourself out. But honestly? The amount of bugs outweigh the cost of the game so, if you still want it? The amount of times I've had robots clip into walls... we shall not speak of those. Also, I was not aware that if you fast travel right after triggering the repair for the architect's house, it will not count as completed- even though it should be. I've already explored the majority of Lonely Hills and part of Frozen Woods before discovering this, and needless to say, it's given me a reason to drop the game completely.Yes, the game is a nice way for you to turn off your brain for a while and run around drilling, vacuuming trash. You can befriend animals and give them fun little hats, but for some reason, I can't give them to my dog and cat? Disappointing, to be honest. _childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little game. I wish there had been more, especially with the gardening and the decorating of your new house. Maybe more things you could interact with. The fridge was smaller than the counters, that sort of thing.The farm animals were cute, I did love the disco balls lol. The gardening was easy, not much of a challenge so long as you ensure that you remember to save some veggies and fruits for seeds. I played for around 30 hours and beat the game. What little bugs I encountered (except for the one I'll mention below) were insignificant.The cleaning of all the garbage became a little tedious, I won't lie, but it was nice to see that all that effort and time was rewarded. The fast travel wasn't perfect, you always had to run through a few more 'sections' to get to where you really wanted to go.My only real issue - the CAMERA. God it gave me headaches. I was constantly fighting to get it to reorient so I could see where I was going and what was around me. It was infuriating. It never STAYED where I wanted it to point. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fantastic. I've enjoyed the ability to farm, craft, explore, and generally clean up the world to visible effects when done - and it's fun to be helping various other villagers with fetch quests/research/what have you. If you liked Stardew Valley, you'll probably enjoy this game. TL;DR at bottom.Pros: -beautiful setting and sounds-great world-building, real sense of accomplishment as you clean and fix areas-lots of things to do and even more places to explore!-good variety of seeds/crops, animals, and recipes - each recipe learned does feel like a significant achievement and offers great progression-variety of areas to choose from, all with (fairly) simple puzzles-combat ranging from simple to hard enough to kill you a time or two-relaxing atmosphere with no real consequences for time takenCons:-TURN IT ON PERFORMANCE GRAPHICS. It won't make a difference visually, but you WILL overheat your computer on anything else. I'd love to see this fixed, as it's a little concerning when the computer overheats to the point of shutdown.-Long, confusing routes in the tunnels and a poor fast-travel system leads to simple quests taking days and days before it's efficient to go home-Placement system for buildings and trees is wonky, needs to be less restrictive (as part of the game does involve some measure of customizing your farm! Would be nicer if it could be a pretty farm, too)-Time taken to care for animals is costly; they all keep running and moving into areas you can't access, especially if they want a bath-(It seems like this has been fixed, but the number of typos and grammatical errors I was encountering in this game even yesterday was incredibly disappointing)-Game-breaking bugs, most of which could be resolved with the simple ability to jump What I'd love to see:-Minimap of some sort, or even a compass, or barring that, maybe even signs (esp in the tunnels)?-Some means of caring for animals faster/better pathing for animals-Better ability to place trees/buildings, some sort of idea on how closely they can be placed to other buildings at minimumTL;DR: Game is fantastic even in its early-access state and is worth getting. It's relaxing, but has bugs (to be expected at this stage, to be clear) that are occasionally game- or computer-breaking [[PLAY ON PERFORMANCE MODE]], as well as quests that can be somewhat unclear. Still lots of fun, satisfying, and immersive otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: Does the game have potential? - Absolutely.Is it worth even 25% of its price right now? - No, unless you deliberately want to support the dev.I trust the dev, and I do want to see what will happen to the game, therefore I won't refund or something.BUT, I won't recommend to buy the game until:1. Visible range will change or become configurable. Right now it affects the game so much that even on GTX 1060 you have to look down to get decent fps.2. Vertical gameplay will change in some way. It just HAS to change, because the game has a lot of verticality, while right now the controls are made for absolutely flat top-down gameplay.These are the two things that kill all the fun right now. Until then, the game is nothing more than a tech-demo, only released to gather the feedback.After that, well, there will be at least something to thoughtfully support.The game already has a decent amount of content, but it lacks the way to play that content.Now it's more playable, thanks to graphics settings and battle/interaction tweaks. I think, after the global optimization patch, it may happen that I would even "recommend" the game.And, thanks to less lags, I think I start to understand the vertical stuff: you should ascend by a ladder and then fall to platforms in a correct way... _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 3/31/22Now that I've gone back to play this game after the full release, I'm happy to say I give it a positive recommendation. Seems they've worked hard to solve those gamebreaking bugs and continue to improve the game in good ways and actively seek out feedback from the player base.Although the game is certainly not completely bug free, it is definitely fun to play and has me smiling at times instead of cursing out of frustration and disappointment. In order to give it a fair assessment and see all the changes that may have been made, I did start with a new game so that there would be no corruption from any former saves.Let's start with the Pros:     - Lots of space to explore and things to collect     - Funny and cute little animal animations and noises      - Some nice environment and building designs     - Fun and unique little touches for your farm and it's inhabitants     - Cleaning up the environment with a vaccum device which I found to be oddly satisfying         and fun in itself     - Music is chill but upbeat and changes with different environments     - Different modes like Creative, Adventure and there's talk of adding a Hard Mode soonI'd like to add under this "Pro" section that the devs are working hard trying to improve the game and fix bugs as quickly as possible. Knowing how difficult it is to prioritize those things and keep players happy, I think they're doing a good job handling both right now. So on to the Cons:     - Some quests still seem disconnected and this can make it difficult to know what you need        to do in order to progress.      - Only partial controller support right now which is fine but would like to see that changed        to full in the near future. Having to switch back and forth between controller and mouse is        very awkward and annoying.     - Hitboxes, esp on animals, are still causing issues with harvesting etc when using a con-       troller     - Cooking needs to have some way to do large batches esp in mid- and end-game. Not        sure why they chose to give every other piece of equipment on the farm that option but       the cooking station so could be in the works for a later update?     - Some areas still have bugs and collision issues but aren't game breaking at least for me       and this last playthrough     - Ending needs some work. Very short and anti-climactic.Those are the major points that need some work imho and there's some other smaller issues like chests needing the ability to be labeled, stacks of crops could have higher limits etc. Those are just QoLs and can be added later if enough people request them. Overall the game has seen great improvement and so I wanted to come back and change my review to reflect that and tell you that I think it's worth a buy right now just don't expect a "perfect" game. Still needs some fixing and polishing which is still happening but it won't stop you from having lots of fun just exploring and cleaning up the world one trash pile at a time. :)The following is the original review posted on Feb 18, 2022:Buggy mess. Don't buy it until the full release and they sort things out if they ever do. Examples of things that can and did go wrong:-Your entire farm disappearing after hours of work put into it-Quests being unable to complete because you can't get a certain item because (insert any number of reasons here)-Animals that have been befriended never showing up to your farm therefore sometimes stalling quests and upgrades-Floating unreachable trash piles-The hit boxes for some things makes it nerve-wrackingly difficult to harvest etc.-and the list goes on....I do give credit to the devs for trying to listen to us players and they have made some changes that made things a little easier but something is definitely wrong with the coding and they just seem to keep releasing tons of patches just to placate all the complaining instead of actually really fixing anything.So just don't buy it yet, folks. It's a wait and see.UPDATED ABOVE ON March 31th

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that is pretty relaxing to play, especially if you enjoy farming games. Achievements are pretty easy to get and most are obtained through just farming and exploring the world. I had ~60% of them about halfway through the quests. Controls on PC with mouse/keyboard work just fine, and I haven't played with a controller so I can't speak on that. Some minor bugs in the game, but nothing game breaking and will be listed below. I noticed that if you're crafting food, and you want the achievement for crafting 200 dishes, you need to do so one by one. I.E. If you queue up 10 dishes, it still only counts as one dish made towards the achievement. I've tried making multiple different dishes to see if maybe the lower end dishes count for less but even the higher end dishes with multiple ingredients still only count as one when crafting multiple at a time. I like that there is an in game achievement tracker that matches the achievements for Steam, and some of the posters you get are super cute. I will say, the story is a bit short though, and I felt like there could have been so much more that the devs could have done with the game to extend the play time without making it feel so rushed. There also appears to be some areas that look like they should be able to be explored but there's no way of reaching them due to the entrances being blocked off. I also don't like that you can't really zoom in so trying to angle your camera for placement or exploration is a little annoying. I also feel as if there are some items, specifically the storage chests, that should also have upgrades available for purchase. Overall, I'd recommend the game though.Minor Bugs:- Trees often float a little bit above the ground.- Hit boxes are a bit annoying when you're trying to befriend an animal, harvest their produce, or show affection towards them.- There are a ton of invisible walls all over the place. The worst I've found is in the Frozen Peaks.- Upon destroying trash, sometimes the trash pile or mountain still shows that it's there, or creates said invisible wall.

_childDocuments_.review: No Place Like Home is a peculiar game. I loved it, but I would hesitate to recommend it. Let me explain. The gameplay is fairly repetitive, with some optimization issues, and a huge (and I mean HUGE) dose of jankyness. However, it seems the devs keep working on it (in fact they released a huge update with some major QoL improvements just after I finished 100% the game). I had a lot of fun playing the game, and found the main garbage-cleaning mechanic to be extremely relaxing. My biggest complain would actually be the economy/item-balance. It is unbalanced, with most items having almost no use at all, or you getting 10x the amount of items that you would actually need to do everything in the game, which means you end up hoarding a boatload of virtually useless resources.If you like games with low stakes, no time pressure, a lot of grind and routinary gameplay, and have a high tolerance for low budget games, then please try this one! But otherwise, avoid it, because you will only get very frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: A tentative recommend, with a few caveats.Before I begin I would like to state that I don’t…really consider NPLH to be a farming sim. I mean, it is, but in my opinion it’s not a very good one. However, this is still a very fun game for other reasons. The farming is actually incredibly unimportant save for growing a token amount of certain produce in order to unlock new skills and recipes.I have a slightly complicated relationship with this game. I got it back in early access because I saw my spouse playing it, and thought the garbage cleaning mechanic looked super fun.I like the game, and would recommend it to people, but only as long as they know what they’re getting into. If you want a farming game, a game with memorable and fun NPCs, or a charming cottagecore farmer life story, you won’t find it here. If you like zoning out for hours while you tear down giant piles of debris so you can suck up all the trash with a totally not magical, high-sci-fi vacuum, then this is probably your game.To be completely clear, you aren’t actually required to clean up everything. There’s a few quests here and there that involve cleaning specific things (such as chopping down diseased trees and replanting them) or rebuilding structures, but you’re never forced to say, clean an area in its entirety before moving on.The quests can be a bit unclear in their objectives and have kinda poor tracking, and it’s possible to sequence break and mess up some of the quests for a bit. The story is basic. Super basic. It’s not bad that it’s basic, it’s all the setup you need for the kind of game it is, but there’s no big time story happening, just looking for your absent grandpa who foisted his trash heap farm onto you. The dialogue is nothing special save for a few jokes and references here and there.It’s also not super well optimized and is a little bit laggy. Might have something to do with the sheer number of objects loading in due to all of the trash you need to clean up.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but I've really been enjoying this game, it's very relaxing and a go at your own pace kind of game. It feels like a combination of games that I've played, such as: Slime Rancher, I am Future, Animal Crossing, and Stardew Valley. While it can get a bit repetitive, its been satisfying in the same way that Powerwash Simulator is satisfying. There is just something about cleaning this place up that gives me all the dopamine. I also like that you are able to proactively complete most quests, rather than having to find the NPC character to get the quest first for the quest's items to spawn. I also really like that I don't have to go chasing after the animals either, I can go back to where I found them later on once I have the right resources. Although, I wish there was the ability to mark locations on my map, since it can get confusing which "collectible" (for lack of a better word) I have found and which I haven't. As well as the ability to click into map areas already visited and view the local map, rather than having to fast travel there to see the map.However, the game does start lagging when you have a lot of animals, it isn't unbearable, and you aren't limited to only the starting area for your farm. So it is possible to spread out and make specific locations for animals, rather than cramming them all in, which helps save of frames. The same goes for farming areas, when you start harvesting a massive amount of crops at once, your frames might take a significant hit until you've picked everything up. I also really wish that the stacks were larger, while some, like resources go up to 100 in a stack, crops typically max out at 10. Which is a huge hassle when you really expand your farm, and are getting well over 100+ crops, but that means at least 10 inventory slots get taken up, making it difficult to move things in 1 trip. I also feel that the chests are much too small, or at least should be given an upgrade to increase their capacity. There are also some obvious issues with NPC pathing, such as the robots getting stuck on doorways, or enemies not detecting you when you are directly in front of them. It is also possible for the player to get stuck, but that is easily solved with fast travelling, and you will not lose any items when doing so. I also would say the story line is fairly predictable, but maybe I've just played too many of these games... anyways, the fact of the matter is, it is very easy to break the immersion, especially if you explore areas fully before talking to certain characters (like I did... oops). Decorating can also be a bit frustrating, as it isn't possible for you to place objects, like a lamp or planter, onto a table at all. There is also very little variety in decor, which really leaves me feel like it's pointless to do any interior decorating, especially because most of the objects aren't able to be interacted with.Overall, this game is very good, and could use a bit more polishing, perhaps in a patch, especially for the issues with AI pathing, storage capacity, and object/decoration placement.In summary:Gameplay: 7/10 - Relaxing go at your own pace, can get quickly repetitive, and there are some bugs and other issues, but they haven't been game breaking for me. If you like casual games, I'd give it a try.Graphics: 8/10 - I have all my settings set to ultra, and I consistently get 120-144 fps when I'm in areas without a lot of drops, animals, or robots in one location. When I am in these crowded spaces my frames can drop to 40-60 fps, until all the items are picked up into my inventory.Story line: 4/10 - Predictable especially if you've played games like this before, and not really essential to the gameplay. it just keeps the player wanting to progress through the map, but does not really immerse you into the story itself, as the game can break the timeline very easily, if you "over explore" and clear out entire areas before taking a quest from an NPC.Full Price or Sale: Sale - I mean who wouldn't want to save money, but also some of the game just feels to be lacking polish, and I don't think I'd be able to justify to myself paying $20 for this game, unless there were some updates to the game, refining it.Overall: (7/10)+ (8/10)+ (4/10) = (19/30) + 6 points for 60% off sale = 25/30 so yea it gets a pass for me, as long as you pick it up sale, I'm sure you'll really enjoy this game too. Geez I'm such a nerd, okay have a great day byeeeeeeee!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game that can itch that OCD need to clean up every single piece of garbage around.However a few notes1: Storage - This can become an issue and I wish they had handled it a bit better. If you go hog wild and really build a large farm you are going to end up having to have dozens of chests to store everything, so larger chests as an upgrade would have been nice. You also probably only need 2 of each tree (minus oak, you will get more than enough acorns  from garbage piles) and perhaps one of each of the animal buildings, fully upgraded. Now that being said you may need to do a bit more in the beginning of the game just to get things going "money" wise, however about half way through you should have more than enough prepared meals (money) that you dont really need any more3: Cooking - Aside from mashed potatoes for healing you probably dont need anything else and those are the easiest things to make, so just stock up on potatoes and you should be good for the entire game4: House decorating - This just seems like a complete after thought and I did not really put any effort into it because it was a little clunky and it seemed unnecessary to expand your house beyond the first one, which was brought to you via a quest.5: Controller support - It says full controller support, however rotating the camera around so you can see goes so slow with the controller that makes the use of a controller null so just stick with keyboard and mouse.Still though this was a cute and mostly fun game that I would recommend, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute game with a LOT of potential but lets be very clear IT IS EARLY ACCESS. Even with moderately decent farming mechanics at this point it feels a little more like one of those "pressure washing" or "unpacking" games. You play as a young woman named Ellen cleaning up and helping to revitalise a valley in post apocalypse Earth. I found drilling away dirt piles and vacuuming them into my inventory to be very relaxing which is good because there is a lot to clean up, and it is because it was relaxing that I have tentatively put a positive recommendation. Other than the cleaning up I really enjoy the animal taming and caring for features. Having varying needs of feeding, washing, or giving affection to animals each day to ensure production takes away the monotony some farming/life sims can have while doing similar upkeep. You can fill your days with exploring, trash clearing, or farming duties without ever feeling like you're rushing something, and it is meditative in a way that I've seen other people claim Stardew Valley can be but has never quite been for me. That being said it is pretty directionless so if you like having a little bit of structure imposed to nudge you along in your games maybe check back in like a year, because while you do get quests you get next to know guidance on how to complete them, and most feel like they'll be achieved organically by just plodding along rather than being something you have to put any particular effort into achieving. As I said at the beginning it is Early access and there are MANY improvements that could be made. I am going to list the big ones that I have noticed with just a few hours of play, so you can decide if you're willing to put up with them or if you'd rather wait until the game is fully completed. As of 3rd of Jan 2022:1. You cannot split item stacks - this is incredibly annoying for cooking as you have no choice but to put a lot more of an item than the recipe requires to create your meal and you don't get the excess back or multiple foods. 2. The Map is just a picture and not particularly proportioned, there is no player maker and certainly no landmark markers to help you get back to people or points of interest. This makes trying to figure out where anything beyond your farm is something of a pain as it is so simple as to not even show you were paths to other areas are, only that the areas do/are going to exists somewhere.3. Items in your hotbar don't highlight when selected - this would be less of an issue if some items like seeds didn't require you to open and close your inventory to deselect them. 4. You loose the ability to rotate your camera while preparing to place an object. 4.5 I had to google how to rotate a held object - I genuinely can't remember if it ever came up in the tutorial (which was actually quite good and raised a little nostalgia for some much older games with how straight forward and simple it was) but it isn't in you encyclopedia with the rest of the button reminders. [Press E while holding an object to rotate it btw]5. Despite the interesting futuristic setting and an uncustomisable MC there is no notable plot. There is no intro telling you who you are, what the state of the world is, or why you're in this Valley, there is an assumption that you read the game description and that's all you need to know. The quests offer some very limited world building in their descriptions as do the few bits of NPC dialogue. They are just enough to show a lot of thought has gone into the world building, we just don't really have access to any full lore. Speaking of NPC dialogue, extremely limited as it is, some of it (particularly in a convo with a certain fowl) had notable misspellings that did not appear to be stylised/creative choices, and probably could have been run through a word processor before being inserted into the game. So yeah those are my current big issues. On a more positive note, the art style is cute. There are many save slots which I'm sure will become useful as more content is added and more diverse play styles become available. The little interaction you have with NPCs does give them and the player some interesting hints of personality and hints towards some good world building. The robots add a cool fresh dimension to your farming. You can tell your neighbours dog that he is a good boi. While it very obviously has a long way to go it's current form is still pretty ok for just chilling out, it'd probably be really good for those moods where you wanna game, but not wanna game game.(edited 26/01/22 to add how to rotate an object to point 4.5)

_childDocuments_.review: So I completed this game, more or less, in about 26 hours.  I did not finish all the quests, but I did the final area, which you can access without doing all the quests.  So overall, cute game, the controls are a little iffy and it can sometimes be a pain lining up directly with an item to interact with it.  You can't move everything around on the farm and it's a weird layout so you don't have a ton of room, but it's manageable.  I like the little spider bots that you can make to help with collecting crops and animal products.  They're expensive but worth it in my opinion.So now the cons: the game froze a bit here and there as I progressed, the quest tracker doesn't work (or it didn't work for me) and so it was a little hard to figure out where to go.  The lighting in the game could be toned down a bit, especially in the house, the desert, and the frozen area.  It's a short game, doesn't take a long time to finish it and if you decided to stay on Earth it's just farming, caring for animals, and finishing quests/clearing trash.I would recommend getting the game on sale, it's not bad, but there's just not a ton there, but it's a nice little cozy game that has some customization to it that I think most people would enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: I absolutely love this game so far. For a small price you get access to a decent amount of content; albeit with a few bugs and performance issues which I am sure will be fixed.Long version below:No Place Like Home is one part adventure, one part farming sim and one part casual play. It's roots lie within such games My Time at Portia and Stardew Valley, it is currently in early access with the road-map stating the game will be fully released this year. The premise is Earth has been abandoned by the majority of humanity for Mars, only few remain here on Earth. A lot of rubbish/trash has been left in its wake; this sets up the player to clean up using a trusty vacuum and drilling tools to run your farm. You can tame pets, grow your gardens and decorate your farm. The game loop is relaxing and I thoroughly enjoy cleaning up and growing the farm, such as being able to build chicken coops, cute robotic helper coops and so on. Building these coops and outbuilding such as a kitchen/recycle machine help you to farm resources.The aesthetic of the game is lovely, the colours and the cuteness of the animals make it a great game to look at, there are a few performance issues tied to the graphical settings, I am sure they will be fixed soon as the developers seem passionate about their game and community feedback.Overall, I am enjoying this game a lot, it has a unique premise and look, which helps it to stand out alongside the other popular farming sims out there. For the small price currently, I wholeheartedly recommend picking this game up. I am excited to see where the further development goes.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: No Place Like Home is a cute and relaxing farming and ranching sim. The style is very whimsical and there's a chicken knight in there named Cornelius the Brave. How cute is that? The setting is post apocalyptic where the world is covered in garbage. Your main goal is to clean it up while you're looking for your grandfather. Cleaning up each area and restoring it is very cathartic and relaxing. However...Cons:I honestly thought this was in early access while I was playing. The quest system is a catastrophe. It's easy to get quest items before you're actually on the quest. Or get quest items after a quest had been completed. Quest lists are buried with very little information about where you're supposed to go.There's no reference for what each NPC is named. So if you have a quest to speak to "Mark", you have no idea who Mark is, where he is, or what he looks like.I read other reviews that mention invisible weird collision elements that folks run into. I had that too, but realized that there's a graphic setting for that. Turn on foliage and it will reveal tree stumps, branches, etc. I have no idea why a setting would hide an object but not the collision aspect. If the foliage is disabled, you'll run into invisible collision things on flat surfaces and it can be really challenging to get around.The farming aspect is fun and relaxing, but very -very- poorly balanced. You can cook meals which will give you three different effects. Healing, running speed, or throwing a chicken grenade (don't ask). However, once you upgrade the kitchen to a higher level and make more complicated meals... they still give you the same effects in the same amount as the cheaper, easier to cook meals. Really, the only reason to have any crops and animals at all is to upgrade your tools and have a handful of meals to heal and such. There's a greenhouse, but you get it at the very end of the game. And by then, you've already unlocked everything, so what's the point? Greenhouses are better for farming sims that have seasons, but this doesn't have seasons. Battle is also very poorly balanced. When you finally fight the lass boss fight, it's entirely possible you'll miss it because it's just any other fight. It took me a second to realize "oh there's a dude sitting on this robot, this must be the boss fight". My graphic settings are set to as high as they would go, and as I run around, the terrain still shifts around as if it was a level of detail, which is usually in the distance. This shifts around right under the feet and I can't figure out why.All in all, I did play it all the way through, but this game still needs some serious work.
_childDocuments_.name: No Place Like Home

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a nice concept and has nice graphics. BUT, as an indie game dev myself, I found some game design flaws. These are not in any specific order and I hope the devs read reviews- Too easy to kill enemies. You can hold left mouse button to use the drill and just stand in front of the enemy and it will get stuck getting damage- Farm puzzle doesn't need a solution. There's a simple puzzle inside the farm, next to the river, where you need to put a box to get to the other side. OR just get close to the case and grab it with E- Loading screens are not anchored to full screen. My display resolution is 1824x1014 so I could see to the sides a gap and see through it the game changing scenes- Conversation with Rudy doesn't take you back to the speech options. If you talk to Rudy, you can choose a dialogue. when that dialogue is finished, it just closes the conversation and you need to interact with him again. I didn't talk to more people, so I don't know if this is a bug or the conversation system. But it should take you back to the options so you can choose another one- No falling animation. Even if the game doesn't have a jump system, you should have a falling animation. The character looks like it drops down because it needs to be stuck to the floor- Camera clips through walls. Inside a house you can see what's on the other side of a locked door. kinda ruining the "what's behind?" feel. It works good with fences though, since it would be annoying if the camera just springs everytime you hit a fence- Music doesn't loop while talking to someone. I noticed when you are talking to someone, music just stops and everything is silent until the end of the conversation, where the music starts again- Dialogue skips when you click continue when they are speaking. It should complete the dialogue and then, if clicked again, it should take you to the next one- You can drill + vacuum through walls- If you die, the game restarts fast. There is a dialogue box telling you you died and you respawn, but there is no death animation so it just feels so sudden- Stamina drains way too fast. Maybe there is an upgrade later in the game, if that's the case it's ok. But if the stamina is the same for the whole game, you just run for a couple of seconds before draining it completelyThese are just some little flaws I found. It's not unplayable, it just feels like some rookie mistakes everyone (including me, I'm not a dev god) does when making their first games. Keep up the good work :)

_childDocuments_.review: I like No Place Like Home a lot, as you can probably guess by the amount of time I've been playing. _childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little game which is only 25% complete.But for 3,99 there is nothing you can do wrong.It is rough around the edges, no doubt about that, but you can already play around 10-12 hours without greater problems.There are a few bugs and glitches, like falling through the floor after a big robot jumps you, but it is not fatal, because at the end of the day (literally the game-day) you spawn back in your home.There are also a few issues with reaching some areas on hills or small obstacles like small stones you cannot walk over etc. nothing major.But that is about all that i did notice in my 14 hours of playing this game.At the moment the 3,99 are worth the gameplay you are getting NOW, without waiting for the whole game.The roadmap states that every quarter of 2021 the dev will add one new area to the game.If this holds true the game should be "complete" at the end of 2021 or first quarter 2022 if you add a few delays.If you like these small building, farming and animal husbandry-games, this should be right up your alley for very little money.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, but what happened to this game? I was waiting for this update and was happy seeing it appear in the downloads. Then I read the patchnotes and was actually excited. I rarely allow myself that, due to my experience with promises made in the gaming industry about computer games in the last couple of years. Massive changes to adjust for loads of more content... well,... I can confirm the first half of that statement.But somehow they forgot to say how much they have removed from the game in the wake of the update as well. Here are some examples:The interconnection of the areas with one special portal to the central hub close to your farm ist still there, although it has been moved. But all the other caves and tunnels are no longer connected, no more vast underground network to explore and no more puzzles and little parcours to open passages. That is all gone. Every cave or tunnel is now just a small hole in the ground with some trash and a few hostile robots.And speaking of robots, you remember the non-hostile ones? The little shy and nervous guys that you could clean up, tame and build a shelter for and keep them as farm pets? Those are gone too, along with their building. Only the robot lamas remained. But that is a good thing, no? You need the place for more crops. See, you remember when the npcs would only trade with you if you had preserved food jars AND a certain dish for an item on sale? The original story in short was, that currency was no longer an important thing in the game worlds future and quality cooking became a more valuable method to strike a deal. Well, that's kind of out of the window. The prizes on items in the shops are now preserved meal jars only. And they went up quite a bit. I completed the village and most of the lonely hills so far, since the update and I didn't need to use my basic cooking station for anything else than occasionally coooking pet food, to maintain the flow of eggs, truffles and such. All my other produce went into the preserver for jars or the birdhouses for new seeds. Collecting cooking recipes is now a hobby on the side, you don't really need them anymore.The npcs also sold upgrades for your vac tool, particularly Rudy, remember? You could purchase a blueprint for an upgrade to mine through a new type of trash or more range or more impact. Then you would go to your workstation and build the upgrade, given you owned the required upgrade materials. That was obviously way to inconvenient. Now you buy the actual upgrade... and that's it. The npc even installs it for you immediately and you're good to go.That saves you time, wich is, again, a good thing. Since something else they removed is a couple of shortcuts. The bridge across the river in the village is gone. Until you can open the door to the shop on the beach side, you have to walk around the lake every time you need to get to the other side. The shortcut on the beach via ladder to Rudy's post on your farm... also gone. In the lonely hills the paths have been modified even worse, it feels like you have to do a lot more walking in the game now.I don't know if I can continue to play, since I am stuck with the quest for the toxic piles in lonely hills. I have sprayed all of them with my new and clearly not improved integrated mini-Bulbulator and they stopped glowing, but my questlog doesn't register them als done. I encounterd a few bugs that haven't been there before the update, none of them were game stoppers until now. But that is enough anyway. There is more, but it doesn't get any better. This was an absulute thumbs up previous to the update. But the "great new patch" definitely feels more like a massive downgrade.I will monitor the development of this game and I still hope this is some sort of an accident. But my hopes for a nice release in just a month are severely cooled down. P.S. WTF did they think when they turned the doghouse into a "kennel"? Not only takes it up way to much space now, according to the story I adopted the doggo so it is taken care of and has a good life on my farm, roaming around as he pleases. Yes, he did get in the way every once in a while, sitting right in front of a chest I wanted to access. Kinda like a real pet. But now he is confined to a spot that is smaller then the chicken coop. They might as well put a chain on him. I haven't gotten to the cat or the raccoon, but my guess is, they "fixed" them  the same way. I have to end this now, it's getting frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game that is difficult to learn, has deep resource management chains and a complex storyline, this is not the game for you.  This game is more for just wasting a few hours without the monotony of an idle clicker game.  In No Place Like Home, you play the character Ellen Newland who has postponed her relocation to Mars in order to visit her grandfather one last time.  Upon reaching his farm she discovers mountains of trash and pollution and… a talking chicken named Cornelius who gives her no information about the location of her missing grandfather, but rather, sends her on her first quest: find a tome he has written about farming for dummies.  The game seems to be more about raising the alarm about humans being terrible stewards of our planet than anything else.  Which is fine, I guess, as we ARE terrible stewards of our planet.  Ellen’s job is to clean up the waste, recycle what she can to use for building items she will need to run the farm, make upgrades to her equipment and perform quests for NPC’s she encounters in the game.  Along the way she learns that there is an evil scientist who is responsible for the mountains of trash which appeared in the region overnight.  As the storyline progresses, she learns that the evil scientist is her grandfather’s twin brother.  The story builds you up to expect a grand finale showdown but lets you down with an anti-cathartic and, honestly, really dumb ending.  This game has three modes to it.  Adventure mode, which is the easiest mode.  Then there is the challenge mode which is the same as Adventure mode except you need coffee, the robots are harder to destroy and everything costs more food and recycled materials to build or purchase.  Finally, there is a creative mode where everything is free.  This game has a lot of problems, the main being tessellation.  There are too many places where things simply don’t work correctly as frames don’t tesselate properly.  For example, there are areas where you cannot place growing plots on the land because, for whatever reason, the game believes there is an elevation change at that point and your farming plots end up in the air where you cannot use them or remove them.  They are stuck there forever like little floating square islands.  Additionally, there are many places where your avatar should be able to traverse unhindered but there seems to be an invisible wall preventing her from doing so.  Conversely, there are also places where she should not be able to traverse but can, like walking through walls in the underground areas of the map.  Speaking of the underground, why?  I mean, it adds absolutely no value to the game.  If you are going to have an underground, at least make some sort of mystery out of it or have some sort of purpose to it.  Other than being a place to get resources you can get anywhere it really serves no purpose.  Overall, I have to admit, even with the giant chicken, I am underwhelmed by this game.  It appears as if the devs were in a rush to put out a game and didn’t take the time to smooth out the rough spots or do the little things to make the game enjoyable.  Maybe I am expecting too much.  After all, Chicken Launcher does bill it as a relaxing game.  And, if that is all you are after, then it lives up to its billing.  But, with the broken English and poor grammar, the tessellation issues, poor story line, minimal resource chains and myriad other problems, I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this game.  It is a cute game.  If the devs can fix the problems with it, then I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Presently I don't recommend it for everyone, but it does have an audience for some fantasy wish fulfillment.I had this game on my wish list for a while and nabbed it on the summer sale.  Let's start with the pros.This is the only farming game I've ever played where you can throw down animal pens outside your main farm. This is so nice to someone like me who didn't want a bunch of robots running around my farm making my computer lag, but still wants to house every stray animal I come across. My computer isn't very powerful, so I appreciate that- in the post apocalypse- I don't have to worry about where I put my pigs.Satisfaction simulator: I will clean everything.While the types of crops are somewhat limited, I'm not trying to do the mental math scheduling harvest and replanting because all the plants grow at the same rate. This might annoy someone else, but I'm enjoying having a single mass planting day and then exploration and cleaning.Fast travel exists. As far as I can tell the travel time is immediate and you can get to most NPCs with it so far.Now onto the cons:The largest con  for me is the map. The map is absolutely USELESS for manual exploration. You don't have an arrow showing direction, the only things marked are NPCs, and determining where you are, where you're going, where was that quest at, which animal is where, and if there is actually a pathway up that hillside- ALL of this is a trail-and-error MESS. They desperately need trails marked- either by default or by lighting it up as you explore. Quest areas could marked or highlighted . I'd love animal icons, of course, and for underground especially knowing which doors I have and have not activated or which trails are still blocked would have saved me LITERAL REAL TIME DAYS of BS.The underground areas are a frustrating maze of space. I know this is partially because there are multiple entrances and you have to go down ALL OF THEM to fully open the path ways, and per point 1, a functional MAP would be literally game changing.Once you hit the second "zone" of the map you start running into invisible walls while cleaning. This makes navigation very difficult, as you might imagine, and will result in you getting RECKED by robots you COULD have run away from if you weren't suddenly smacked into thin air and put at a dead stop.Enemies will clip through walls, making it literally impossible to find and kill them, as if the invisible wall thing wasn't annoying before. Similarly I have clipped through at least 1 garbage pile, since I was already in combat it's hard to say whether the enemy or the clipping damaged me, but based on the speed and amount of damage- I am assuming I got killed by the garbage.Now, I can admit I haven't finished playing. I'm still enjoying the game right now, it's basically wish fulfillment to have a bunch of space to myself and all I have to do is clean it? Sign me up! But the bugs seem to be getting worse as I get deeper into the game which has me rather worried about completion. They aren't SUPER game breaking right now- as death is just waking up the next day- no item loss, no lasting damage- it's just super annoying to me specifically to die from a dumb glitch. So, your mileage will vary depending on wish fulfillment, specific bug tolerance, and your desire to have a good map. So I can't recommend it for everyone, but it certainly has an audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is a cute, relaxing fantasy farming game in Early Access. Start either with everything available from the start, or in adventure mode with easy and casual gameplay. So, where IS the challenge mode? I guess there is none, this is not that kind of game. So what is it? Well, you run around with an enormous tool. Kind of a vacuum claener, water hose and jack-hammer in one. You break up stuff, suck it into your inventory and put it in a recycler to build new stuff. You befriend animals to receive eggs, and find blueprints to craft new things. Your aim is to build and run a farm. Or a zen garden. Everything is full of trash, so you have to collect trash, recycle it, craft tons of items, cook food, plant seeds and water them... kind of a survival game without the survival part. Talk with animals, kill hostile (battery-run) animals, construct new buildings and furniture. You'll soon dicover new areas, all completely destroyed by humanity. Your goal is to restore them back to their original beauty, without trash and poison around. Wish this would be so easy in real life.  Casual, zen-like farming and building game. Collect trash and rebuild a world trashed and destroyed by humanity.

Yet, I still found this a lot of fun to play.  On the bright side, it is a very chill game.  You can happily waste hours on end just going around doing things and completing the quest line.  The graphics are great.  The music is very calming.HOWEVERThe story/premise makes no sense once you get in the game.  The world was abandoned because we trashed the planet, but with no effort at all you can clean it up and solve all the problems?  Threats are not threats, just an annoyance, really.  Even at the basic level of production, you produce more wealth than can ever possibly be spent making most activities in the game completely pointless beyond the first use of each item.  There are base building elements.  But, there is absolutely no point to them at all.  Other than being able to build and place furniture and household appliances, there is no reason to do it.  You cannot use them at all, other than your bed...which the game gives you.The puzzles are not puzzles, or challenging. If you are willing to put up with all of that, this can be a very fun and enjoyable game to play.  If you can't...save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, how I wanted to like this game.I dig the nurturing vibe in games, having an impact on the setting and making it visibly and unequivocally better over time. So when a game crossed a farming sim (a genre that usually ticks those boxes fairly well on its own) with an eco-friendly clean-up-the-joint vibe, I was quite intrigued.Unfortunately, No Place Like Home was probably ambitious beyond what the skill set of its tiny studio could deliver well. A word of advice gleaned from far too many hours (and years) playing games: when a game wants to diverge from/iterate upon/otherwise tweak core elements of a genre, and particularly when it wants to lean into said changes as part of its core identity, those elements had better darn well be polished to a mirror shine.Fans of farming sims will likely scratch their heads when I say that you can't just till the earth to plant crops--no, you find little panes of dirt embedded in garbage heaps (as a random drop), which you can then slap down anywhere the game will let you. On the plus side: farming wherever you want it! (Or at least wherever the inscrutable terrain mapping algorithms will permit it.) On the minus side: you start out with not having nearly enough farming space no matter what you do, and then later end up with stacks and stacks of dirt squares with nowhere practical to put them.Unlike most farming sims, every single upgrade requires one or more of a single farmed product (many of which are themselves dependent upon upgrades)--in addition to the crafting materials, etc. required to build the utilities and fixtures to make those possible. Players of farming sims past will thus understand why the decision to not have a reliable external source of any given crop seeds (save potatoes) at any point in the game is truly baffling.Literally every resource you need either comes directly from the garbage, or from things you make/upgrade/otherwise are gatekept by the garbage . What that fundamentally means--and which even non-farming-sim-experienced players can glean--is that this game is , in its heart of hearts, a farming sim. It is a garbage-clearing game that uses an anemic and possibly leprous farming sim as a speed bump in the progression curve. To be fair, there is a certain dopaminergic, meditative quality to maneuvering Ellen and her drill--vacuum backpack through piles of trash as you demolish them and hoover up their scattered remains. And you'll do a lot of that, boy howdy. However, the game seems to have suffered from development by whimsy: all of the farm animals have a host of tiny hats you can place upon them (except the cats, dogs, and raccoons, which for some reason lost out), yet there's only two fundamental types of enemy in the whole game, with a few occasional tweaks to them in terms of size, color, and durability. There's about 5 types of piles of trash, endlessly pasted through maps which will look varying amounts of different (aside from uncluttered) when you're done with them, due to static landscape elements you can't affect, and a host of collectibles strewn about which may or may not be important (unfortunately, you are permitted to destroy some of the important ones, making some quests un-finish-able--yet the quests are coded so sloppily that you can still to a great extent work around that). There's a huge array of decorative things they made for you to (ostensibly) build and put in your home (some of which require blueprints scattered around the world to be obtained first), yet none of them do anything meaningful or useful, and you don't even need the house space (or its upgrades) for any practical purposes. Would that they had perhaps focused their development time and guttering ingenuity on more of the game's actual meat and potatoes.The NPCs are immobile, pointless speed bumps as well, sending you on quests that are poorly-written (both in terms of dialog  in terms of coding) and typically utterly pointless, as well as completely unrelated to anything you or they should care about in the slightest. Several of them are apparently quantized, in that they exist simultaneously in two places, yet their dialogue options remain entirely the same in either place. (This becomes particularly baffling, e.g., when the lone architect demands you repair his home... which is in an entirely different part of the world, and you never once see him there.)The ending is strange, lazy, unfulfilling, and abrupt. I finished the game feeling legitimately angry at it, as well as the fact that I spent 20 hours of my life hoping the game would somehow pull itself out of its death spiral at some point. I also, quasi-tangentially, desperately hope that the one guy they put on the game's English translation (from the team's native Polish) was a volunteer, because--speaking as someone who does proofreading as part of his professional work--he did a terrible job. (Though, in the spirit of fairness, you can only spit-shine a coprolite so much; he may not have had anything good to work with from the get-go.)I'd played NPLH during Early Access, and wrote off many of its flaws at that time as being byproducts of a game in early development. I cannot in good conscience, however, excuse that any more, now that the game has had its self-avowed "Full Release." I've played countless Early Access games powers better than this nominally-"complete" one, and with less development time behind them to boot. While perhaps the only likely way for the studio to improve is to have enough funding to embark on bigger and better projects (i.e. practice making something more like perfect), I don't know that this studio is one which should be given the chance to fail so thoroughly again. Consider other uses for your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun adventure/farming game i have lost many hours to playing it and I am still not bored. There are a few bugs still but the developers are working hard to fix them and make everyone as happy as possible. You play as Ellen, the grand daughter of a farmer/inventor who has gone missing. Following the trashing of the earth you work your way through the levels cleaning up, rescuing animals, planting crops and helping people to try and find your grandpa. _childDocuments_.review: No Place Like Home is similar to many of the other farming sims out there. This version has light combat and a larger world where you are not restricted in just putting things only on your farm. The interaction with your farm animals is cute, and I enjoyed the first Disco-rave on my farm. The house-decorating is mediocre, not a whole lot of furniture to choose from, and the rooms are larger than what you can fill them with. Things don't snap together (like kitchen counters) which really drove me inside trying to line things up the best I could. There were still a few bugs; most of them were no big deal because you wouldn't encounter them more than once, but there is one inventory bug that you'll run into a lot. The story was a little corny and ended abruptly, in my opinion. But I don't generally play these for the amazing story-telling.Overall, I enjoyed the game and would recommend it to fellow farming-sim enthusiasts.

_childDocuments_.review: No Place Like Home is a life/building simulator similar to the likes of My Time at Portia but focuses on a trashed environment to clean, repair and maintain.The visuals are quite good looking with pretty (as far as literal garbage can be pretty) cartoony styled graphics and quite a lot of attention to detail in for example foliage, trees and creatures. As for the mechanics in No Place Like Home you wield a shovel (and later upgrades), vacuum cleaner and water sprayer to clean up whatever is in your way. Most notably, there is no jump or dash!The immediate first thing I noticed is that there is no running or jumping in this game which felt really weird and made collectibles hidden behind piles of garbage a chore to get to. That said I don't mind it much as that's sorta the whole deal of the game! Besides that the gameplay feels a bit cumbersome, things like picking up structures is finicky and you can't pick up anything because you  use the vacuum to do that and with everything going flying when you hit it a wild goose chase happens every time. And if your inventory is full you do pay for an item in the shop but don't get it, kinda annoying you need to check that. That said this game does perfectly satisfy that itch of taking care of a big task and just 'mindlessly' going at it bit by bit while listening to relaxing music (and getting to grab items you shouldn't be able to because the vacuum is stronger than the barriers). As a small minus I'd say that the combat is absolutely terrible, you're wielding a long huge shovel, yet your range is 0, you have to touch the enemy to hit them. Lastly I'm impressed at how big the world already is, how many decorating options there are and how unique and fleshed out the upgrade trees are even in this early state.The soundtrack to No Place Like Home is quite calming and relaxing but it doesn't feel all that unique or especially varied, it absolutely functions for what it needs to do but it does get stale quite quickly. As for the sound design I like what they've done so far, the sounds of whacking dirt piles or vacuuming isn't annoying and just straight up satisfying.So to sum it all up, would I recommend you to get No Place Like Home? For now a careful yes with a high amount of concern for others that don't have a beefy computer to handle this amount of (ab)use. Sure the game is unpolished and unfinished, yes the guidance of what and how you're supposed to do things isn't quite there yet and yes it is unoptimized but the things that are there like a highlight for relevant items, quick planting, all of the options for progression and all the things it does right absolutely make up for it. And for the discounted price at early access this will be a super bargain for when it's finished. And I'd like to take the time to properly and on it's own say, P.S. One major bug I found is that if you go to place something and press escape it gets permanently stuck to your mouse cursor and you can't place it or get rid of it. (trying to then sleep to fix it also had the weird effect of my save data saying "day 2")P.P.S. After the January 2021 patch the game runs extremely better making the usage go down to 35% CPU / 1,5 GB RAM / 40% GPU. The patch did however introduce a lot of small bugs. The cat just lies dead on the ground sliding around. The Mayo Maker and Ultra Kitchen can't be interacted with nor picked up to reset it. Boxes don't always get vacuumed up. The vacuum itself gets stuck every now and then until you use your shovel. The sprinklers I had didn't work on the first few days and some of the cube bots are now in the ground.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is boring.No Place Like Home is boring.I picked this game up because I adore the message it's trying to send. Unfortunately, once I actually played it, I had to force myself to continue, because it is deeply, incredibly, boring. I managed eight hours by telling myself "all right, you need to play some more so you can post a properly informed review," and then I found myself splurging on other games so I would have an excuse not to play any more.My generous assumption is that it is intended for children-which the art style supports-and it is certainly inoffensive enough-but for anyone above the age of 12 looking for something engaging, pass this by.On top of that, its ecological messenging runs headfirst into gameplay conceits, and both come off the worse for it. I would assume the intent of this game is to educate as much as entertain-but it manages neither.The primary resource you harvest throughout most of the game is garbage. This is represented in-world by Wall-E-like rectangular prisms that break down into Plastic Bags, Water Bottles, Pizza Boxes, and Nonspecific Blobs. Upon collection, you throw all of these into a ~magical~ Recyling Machine that then spits out a pile of girders and roofing sheets, forming the resource necessary for trade, construction, and crafting, Building Materials.This is lazy, but it's a game for kids, so some handwaves are to be expected.It's much less egregious than your next tier up, Electronic Waste. A primarily blue mass of wiring, CDs, CRT monitors and less identifiable scrap, E-waste is used to make...Beehives. And mayonnaise mixers.Do you know how many heavy metals are in e-waste? Lead and cadmium, just for a start, and while lead is nasty enough, cadmium is *significantly* worse. And our happy-go-lucky protagonist is just weaving wire into primitive beehives that require destruction to harvest (not modeled, obviously).This would be much more excusable if you were trading these reclaimed materials to NPCs who, presumably, have the facilities necessary for processing these items into usable forms (or can just use microprocessors, batteries and CRTs directly!) but using them as crafting material sends a bad message.Cleaning up the various areas in the game is held up as your character's highest calling, and this is laudable-but only in one area is it even vaguely realistic. By cleaning up water, replanting "polluted" trees, and destroying bear traps, the protagonist returns foxes to the second area-who show their gratitude by giving you seeds, which are otherwise a nonrenewable resource. This is reasonably well-handled, so I won't beat on it too hard.Except for one aspect.The "polluted" trees are depicted covered in plastic bags, used tires...and glowing blue mushrooms, which are fully capable of breaking down both. Yet our protagonist merely chops them down and replaces them with new ones. Rather than being used as a foundation for long-term compost, the trees simply break down into Old Wood and a variable amount of Garbage, which you turn into Building Material.Ugh.Where exactly do you think soil comes from?Piles of garbage, evidently! Every time you break down one of the large Garbage Piles-mechanically separate from the rectangular prisms of garbage cubes-you have a chance to get a Farm Plot, which will produce endlessly forever with no breaks, no remediation, and no fertilization. On top of that, the Farm Plots are mechanically considered buildings-and they're not even raised beds. You pick them up and move them with the same interface used for beehives, chicken coops, and pig pens. If you're going to consider "farmable soil" to be a movable building, at least commit to the bit.This is where I gave up, because clearly this game was not intended for me. It was not intended to genuinely educate; everything in the game is either handwaved or glossed over. It rounds off every corner it can find in the hopes of not confusing children, and then the actual gameplay would put most children to sleep.Now-there's a lot of room in permaculture and soil remediation for interesting gameplay. Cleaning up the soil-ensuring it's free of toxic heavy metals, microplastics, and the like-can still be engaging, and building from Toxic Dirt to Poor Soil and eventually to Rich Loam would be deeply satisfying. Start out with raised beds, then slowly graduate up to better and better soils that grow faster and deliver greater yields, rather than making "greater yields" a generic upgrade bought with Building Material.For example-You show up on Earth, and inform Mark that you're setting up on your grandfather's old farm. Mark nods, acknowledges your grandfather did good work with the starting farming area, but that the plot of land he bought sight unseen from Mars was heavily, heavily contaminated. He spent the last few years of his life getting that patch of dirt plantable, and he finally managed it before he passed away.Hey, he left all his equipment for finding microplastics, sequestering heavy metals, and building soil behind. I see you've got one of those reclaiming rigs, maybe you can finish his work?And so, you plant mushrooms, sunflowers, and leafy greens on Toxic Dirt, from which you get Contaminated Produce, which you feed to a Decontaminator to get Organic Material. Having done so, you mix it into the Toxic Dirt and repeat a couple more times until you have Poor Soil.The garbage you collect can be turned into Organic Material as well as Building Material-the Organic Material is used to make Compost or mixed straight into the soil, depending on how much time you want to spend.And so forth, and so on.Instead, you have...the thing I listed above.Oh yeah, and the combat sucks.Wait for My Time at Sandrock instead. God, I wish I could refund this turd.
