_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun waste of time, but the game could use a lot of improvement.From the start it feels like a weird farming/clean-up game. There are some characters to meet, some hints of quirky storylines that lead to nowhere in the end and a lot of animals to take care of. And in the end you get to find your grandpa and go to mars... or not.Gameplay is very repetitive and the controls are very edgy. Let me explain: You get to a new area that is filled with trash. You use your drill or whip to dismantle solif piles and your vacuum to suck up lose piles. There are evil robots you need to destroy and items to find so you can complete some objectives. Repeat.sound good enough until you discover that you can save a ton of time if you run around with your vaccum AND drill activated all the time. if you come across a robot it will be stunned by the vaccum and damaged by the drill. you only have to deactivate the vaccum to deal more damage. Next.These robots come in 2 variants and each in 2 sizes. You have the jumper, that can't jump if you just stand in front of it and the spitter that can't spit it you just stand right in front of it.You see, where this is going.After all areas have been cleaned you get to got to the Sunken City to save Gramps. The cit has some new kind of trash piles you have to first hit with your whip, that you never used throughout the game, because why would you? And now there are much larger groups of robots that make your life a bit more difficult. But they still work the same.The farming part is an annoyance to say the least. You will end up lacking storage and inventory slots to put all the stuff you need to grow in order to get upgrades equipment to drive the story. on top of that there is house building and decoration that you can either build or get as rewards ... and you have to store that away as well. That would be OK, if your only storage was a chest with not a lot of item slots and the item stack sizes weren't tiny and wildly varying. Most items stack at 10, some at 50 or 100. I could live with the last to but all produce from your farm only stack at 10 and you have to grow a lot of produce to get anywhere.The further your progress the more trouble your inventory makes. even after all inventory upgrades. This should be the other way around. The lack of auto-sorting and stacks not filling up before a new stack is created do not help either.In the end I'm glad, I made it through the game but it didn't feel like an achievement. More like a chore. In the End two old white men agree that the girl was always right... yay.

_childDocuments_.review: Earth is nearly abandoned.  A few people remain among the toxic waste and trash piles covering the land.  Having ruined the entire planet, most folks have moved to Mars.  No, I'm not talking about Elon Musk's recurring dream, this is the setting for No Place Like Home.Ellen Newland, played by you, is about to head off to Mars as well, but decides to visit her grandfather one last time.  But gramps is nowhere to be found, so at the urging of a talking chicken with a penchant for disco, Ellen has a Lorax moment, and sets about cleaning up the world with what has to be the highest capacity vacuum cleaner ever created.I'll tell ya, if you like games with cleaning, farming, crafting, cooking, or just walking around petting things, No Place Like Home has you covered.  Think Portia, but you can forget about the fence around your property.  Here, you can put things anywhere in the world!  Want an apple orchard in that zone you just cleaned up?  Well, go ahead and plant one.  Don't want pigs stinking up your farm?  Build their house on a snowy mountain!Now, I write this having read some of the negative reviews, and I don't know why my experience is so dramatically different, but I can say that the only thing I dislike at all is that the water hose is hard to aim, but once you can build sprinklers for your crops, that becomes much less of an issue.  Other than that, I simply adore this game, and am on my second playthrough, which is something I rarely do, as I have plenty of games I never played through once.I know there aren't as many jokes in this review as usual.  I didn't say, oh, this is a retelling of the classic fairytale "The Bishop and the Prostitute", or that if you rearrange the letters in Ellen Newland, you get "Lewd Nan Nelle".  But I was trying to make a point, which is something else I rarely do.  This is a fine game to play, and I suggest it to people who do that. Crinoline Otter lets you look like a bell, and is a .

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Recommended for fans of farm/life sim type games. If you can deal with lag, somewhat shallow content currently, and grinding, then I'd say buy it now. Otherwise I would recommend waiting until its full release.Playing No Place Like Home reminded me of playing My Time At Portia when it was still a small demo on some indie site. Meaning that it was a lot of fun, has a *ton* of potential, and has plenty of issues that need to be fixed. But being early access, I have high hopes that a lot of the criticisms will be addressed - most notably the lag and collision detection - as the game nears full release.The gameplay itself is pretty fun, if a bit grindy at times. You spend a lot of time destroying garbage blocks and sucking them up with your vacuum. You then use the trash to help you construct your home area. You can farm, cook, get a few critters, etc. The map so far is relatively large, though a bit hard to navigate at times. The "quick" way to navigate is through underground tunnels which can get horribly confusing at first, but can get you to far away locations a bit faster than walking on the surface. Things like crafting recipes are obtained by giving the various NPCs certain items - most notably food, which is the currency of the game. The crafting itself is pretty basic in that you select whatever it is you want to craft from your crafting table and so long as you have the materials, you can quickly make it. However, upgrading the various equipment does take some time. As for making actual items with your equipment, most of it is "insert X amount of items and wait." For example - to make mayonnaise, you put five eggs into the maker and after sometime it will be ready. As for more negative aspects of the game:It can be grindy sometimes.Lag and subpar optimization.Camera needs work, especially when planting or decorating.Collision detection needs work, enemies can easily disappear into the mountainside.Quality of life improvements - better item stacking, proper map system, etc.The quests/story content are relatively shallow currently.There are probably a few other negative aspects that I just can't recall at the moment. Overall, aside from the grindy aspect (which is the nature of the beast in these kind of games), I think the developers will make some headway with the others. So far they seem committed, are patching often, have a road map laid out, etc.Overall I would definitely recommend this to people who are into the farm and life simulation type games. But if you're hesitant or concerned about some of the negatives, then by all means - wait until the full release.

I do not enjoy the grind.Personally, I don't really care about putting hats on chickens and dancing with them but I guess other people will love it. Unfortunately, the hats are useless loot that clogs your inventory. Speaking of which, the inventory could use an overhaul imho. Not a fan of having to open the inventory to put things I need into the hotbar all the time.That said, there are some really cute ideas in this. I really wish this was at the quality level of Stardew Valley but it just simply isn't. Glad I bought it on sale, at least.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun to play, but also it's frustrating. It is quite unfinished in my opinion.Let me start with pros:- It's pretty colorful. - The main plot is simple, but enough to go through.- The premise of cleaning the world is great.- Animals are fun.- It's enjoyable when you want to chill.On the crossroad:- Difficulty - it's easy enough for new players/gamers, so they won't get annoyed or won't bounce off of the game. On the other hand, the final battle is too easy, it's easier than other encounters. There's a new hard mode now, but I didn't check it. This game could have no fighting at all and still be fun.- Tons of trash - lots of trash means lots of resources. It also means tedious work.Technical cons:- Invisible walls - it's not even walls, it's more like poles or stones. In many places, you can get stuck on a flat plane by an invisible obstacle which you have to walk around. It's especially frustrating during battles.- Level related collisions - when you are a bit higher than an object (trash, treasure box, enemy) you are unable to have any interaction with it.- Inventory quick stack - when you open a chest and want to grab something from it using quick stack (rmb by default) it doesn't work, because it puts your object from first backpack slot into the chest. Very annoying.- Placing buildings - you can't place a building where an animal is standing. Fine. You can't move the animal. Bad. How am I supposed to place things where I want, when there are unmovable obstacles.- Quest items - there are more quest items in the world for each quest than needed. When you finish a quest, quest items (those left after finishing) are marked with recycling icon. This is nice, but it also happened with one particular quest I did not finish. While doing the bulbulator quest, you have to help some deers. You find logs (quality wood) in the area which are needed in 3rd part of deer house fix. Unfortunately, I found logs before the quest, because I wanted to clear some trash first. When I was cleaning up my inventory, I recycled all quest items marked with recycle icon. The logs were also marked. I had 10 of them, and they were described with something like "Frank uses them to build stuff". I already did quests for Frank, and the deer quest is from Harold! Well, I recycled logs, and couldn't continue with bulbulator quest, so I had to start the game from the beginning. OMG!Other cons:- There is lots of stuff that is unused, like some kind of placeholders. Wool balls for example are totally useless (only for achievement). Most of the stuff is generally used only for unlocking some recipes or buildings. After that, you can use it in cooking, but with better recipes unlocked, most of this stuff is obsolete and useless. So is loom (needed to create wool balls from wool), greenhouse (late game building, too late and too small inside).- better food effect doesn't seem to last longer than basic food (might be wrong on that).- Moving coop (probably other buildings too, didn't check) makes your poultry homeless, and you have to befriend them again.- Flowers are uselessIn the end, I can't recommend this game, at least not at full price. It looks to me more like an early access game than a polished product.For me, it is a meh game.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind, I have an i7-5930k, 16gb RAM, and an Nvidia 1080.This game does not, under any circumstances, run well. On the highest graphics settings, frames are perhaps 10 FPS at best. Lowest settings, 30-35. At some points I felt nauseous while playing and eventually developed a headache. While I understand that this is an early access game, there is no optimization to be seen. Beware if you're sensitive to stuttering frames.Story, from what little I played, is not addressed. You're thrown directly into the game with no idea as to who you are, what you're doing, or what your goal is. You start up and the first thing you see is a sign that might as well say, "These are your controls - have fun." You then see heaps of trash all over the place. You remember the sign that told you how to suck up trash. And you do this until you go to bed, then rinse and repeat. If you're lucky, you'll notice a sign that says "Shop" and follow it down a poorly constructed hill that the character has trouble maneuvering down. Once in this "shop," you'll find that words are difficult. So difficult that you're presented with pictures showing you how to upgrade your items - of which you aren't sure of their purpose. You're told what the items are, but not how they work or what they're used for. I'm not asking for my hand to be held by any means, but even a little bit of direction would be nice.Finally, this game is riddled with bugs. I had countless piles of garbage that were left floating in the air once they exploded and they would not come down. I would frequently get stuck on these piles and could not suck them up. They were stuck, as was I. Another bug I experienced was with the little corral for the robots. I placed the robot coop, befriended a couple robots, then went to bed. Upon waking up the next morning, the robots were all glitched into the top of the coop and would not come down, nor could I harvest the resources from them.Luckily, I was able to get a refund for this game. It is most definitely not ready for any sort of public access and I feel sorry for those that have had the misfortune of enduring it. Please take this as a warning to WAIT. Wait for it to be polished and playable. It is not even worth it's current $5USD price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I'v played this game for quite some time.  Started when the game was officially released in full form without the tag of early access.  The game does have a story you can explore, and the premise of going down to the trashed planet to find your grandfather is pretty interesting and fun.  Defiantly an interesting group of characters and the animal models are all really adorable. This game gives me Slime rancher vibes with the sucking and water mechanics with a dash of harvest-moon/stardew valley vibes. Would I recommend this game? Yes. With its current mode of just story and creative you can finish the game in less than 20 to 30 hours oh so. It dose have a decent house decoration stuff, same with decor for the farm. One thing I didn't know till I started experimenting that you can place farm building and other items in different areas other than your farm. Including the fruit trees. There are some minor cons. They give you excess amounts of quest items other than the one singular book.  By the time you get to the end you will have a chest full of items you can not through out or delete.  *update, just notices there is an update that you can now recycle them.If you try putting all the animal buildings in one area, it will lag out that area. I know my rig isn't the beefiest, but its not from the bottom of the line. For visuals, in some areas you can see where the bots were placed via a blue ring clipping through the ground. Once defeated the rings stay. There is some weird tree collisions with the bore home and trees when you try to collect seeds from them compared to the dear and foxes. The dear also clip through the mountains and vanishes from time to time.When you meet Harold (the pig guy, I just call him that) at the second location hes at, after completing his quest there and you go talk to him. He will thank you for the other npc that joins him when you free it in the next area even though you haven't done that yet.Now, I've played this game many ways. From speeding through the story, clearing and recycling all trash and debris material, from not eating a single drop of food. But one run that you can not do and finish the game is not opening the suitcases scattered around the map. When you get to the area with the ice wall you need the fire logs to melt the ice. I tried using the old wood and the other type you could freely collect from other mission items you don't need but it would not except them. Even in creative mode going the back way through the desert, there is another ice wall along the path the the radio tower. 9/10, vary chill game. Will continue to play. Would love to see what the moders will do with this. Hope this helps those who ponder if they want this game or not.

_childDocuments_.review: So I saw this game had a full release, so I re-installed it to give it a go.This is not a complete game. This game feels like it was just given up on and dropped. There are invisible barriers everywhere, the terrain completely shifts as you move the camera around/walk around, there are things like wool you can spin into yarn that the tooltip says is a crafting item but it serves no purpose at all.In fact, this feels worse than the first optimization patch back in 0.16. There's also just not enough flat space to properly do any farming. The workaround for that seems to be farming bots that can get crops and such for you, but they're rather difficult to actually control. As an example, you can't set one to just pick up potatoes. If you're a bit on the strict organization side of things, it's highly frustrating that you can't sort chicken and geese into separate coops very easily, and that basically all other farm animals except pigs just get lumped into the cowshed.So sad to see this be the "complete" version of the game.Updated review!With the 0.16 patch, we have been granted glorious optimization and now we can enjoy full framerate even in wide open areas with a lot of stuff. The game is fun. Nothing crazy in-depth, just a fun little explore/do some quests/cleanup an abandoned trashworld game. The one thing I would add are more fast-travel options or maybe a way to set up camp. After a while half of my gametime was going back to where I was at the end of the previous day to resume what I was working on, which was a long trek even with the existing fast-travel tunnels. This is made worse with my ADHD where in the downtime of waking back up, going outside, refilling recyclers and sorting crops, goldfish brain would kick in and I'd forget what I was doing.Overall a cute, enjoyable game. I am looking forward to what else they're going to add to it.Previous review below:Recommended with a caveat: it is NOT optimized.This is going to be a fun game someday, as long as they optimize it to run on current-gen PCs. It's a cute game with a good premise. I have a GTX 970 and get 7fps in wide open areas, but 60 in enclosed spaces or close to and facing walls. Changing your settings doesn't have any effect on framerate.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore games like this and really like the potential here, but it is NOT a polished game and the annoyances outweigh the actual fun by a long shot.   If you have any hand, wrist or ergo issues, pass this game buy.  My hands and wrists are aching and I use an ergonomic trackball.  Issues include, 1. mouse sensitivity fluctuating to the point you can't hardly move at times, and at best you'd need to slide 3 times just to turn around.  2. There is no way to tell when you're tired, so you'll randomly pass-out and be transported to your house, you wake up, but there is no indication if it saved or not.  It's an mechanic meant to limit game-play for no good reason.3. Time moves at an unreasonable pace, with no way to adjust or even pause.  I used the escape menu as a test, but no, time keep moving and if you take too long while in the menu, you'll pass-out and wake up at home as soon as you press 'resume'4. Progression even for a exploration game is too slow, especially when you literally pass out on a regular basis trying to find your way around.Additional movement problems, but they have an unstuck feature which is very nice.  This game is lovely and I think it has the potential to be the best of Harvest Moonesque / Deiland put together, but at this point, it's just painful, mentally and physically instead of fun to play.   I'm gonna keep this, because I hope the developers will continue to improve.

_childDocuments_.review: OKAY. I like this game! Let me make that  I plan to play MORE! BUT IT IS very,   in development! This game starts out with the most BASIC tutorial ever - to the point where I didn't even know it was a tutorial - I walked forward and realised 'wait a minute'. After that, the controls started to kind of make sense, so I was able to play quite a bit afterwards! This game has an amazing idea. I love it, it's not super original but it's fun! You start on a farm which needs rebuilding. It's absolutely covered in TRASH. The earth is covered in trash and it's up to you to clean it up. This consists of 'breaking' trash blocks, and sucking up the pizza boxes, empty water bottles, bin bags, all of it, with your vacuum. The vacuum has a big range, so actually it can suck up things easily, no effort really. Then you put what you've sucked up into a machine (you can buy loads of them) to recycle the parts into pieces you can use to build. The machines take time, so I really recommend building a few to get yourself going.- Farming! The farming is super easy. You break trash, sometimes you find seeds buried there, you plant em, water them super quickly, (like, within a few seconds you can water your field of 30+ plants), and then either make the crops into food, or use them to trade with your animals for items (see below).- Ranching! Ranching is exactly what it is. I cleared space in my yard/farm area, and made a chicken coop, and tamed a few wild chickens. They really like potatoes, and I had an abundance of them. Each day a chicken will give you an egg if you give them a potato in exchange. They also hang around wherever you put the coop. There are also other animals, like cats, dogs, pigs, and robots.- Robot Ranching! This part is like, not as cool? But still cool. It's a cool idea, it just needs expanding on. You can find wild robots that aren't ...evil ... buried in the trash, once you help them out, you can choose to take them home by giving them some batteries. Like chickens, they are 1 battery per ...however long. It may be one per day, or one per week, I didn't actually see. Batteries come from fighting bad robots, so I'm a bit worried I will run out to be honest. But robots give you 50 recycled parts at the cost of 1 battery, so it seems like a good trade, if the batteries are easy to come by? I'm not sure yet.- Easy to get other crops & water: Watering your plants is easy, you can just suck up water from anywhere with your vacuum, even through fences, which I'm not sure the developer was going for, but I love it. I'm super lazy, so that works for me. Crops are the same. You don't buy them from the shop. You find seeds in the trash. Mostly. You can also feed birds a potato to get potato seeds. I'd like to see this made into any seed, or feed them 1 (x) for 1 (x) seed, etc. You can also suck these up through fences lol.Take these with a grain of salt. This is just a part of being early development. I'm sure these will be fixed/added. (Er, I am HOPING the developer will see these reviews and be able to fix/add these concepts!)- No controller support. This is hit and miss. I'm able to play with my keyboard, but when I see games like this, I automatically assume I can use my controller. I plug my pc in, and for some reason I AM able to walk around! But it doesn't work if I try and use actions.- Watering plants is a hit and miss, literally: I can't figure out what I'm doing. I just spray chaotically and hope I hit a potato. This works, but I want it to be easier. I'd like a constant spray instead maybe. Yeah I'd run out of water sometime but I have no idea what I'm doing most mornings. Watering/washing animals is my least favourite thing to do.- The characters are all the same: lol, this is ...uh, placeholders, right? Probably. So don't worry too much here. The shop holder is the same as the guy you meet in the tutorial/outside your house, haha.- I hate using 0-9 on my top keys to do things: I am 100% already using a keyboard, please allow numpad support for this. Pressing 5 on my numpad is much faster than pressing 5 on the top for me. This is obvs. a preference.- Rotating doesnt make sense: So actions are 'E'. I am putting down my kitchen/chicken coop/ whatever building, and I struggled to find how to rotate anything. It's not , or . It's not < or >, or []. What could it be? Oh, after going back to tutorial, I find out it's E. That was terrifying because I was worried I place it facing backwards. Does this make sense? Why is E the action button, but also rotate?

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I'm giving a positive recommendation only because yes, it's entertaining, and it's fun, and it's enjoyable, but that's going to come with some caveats that are so ridiculous and massive that you could land aircraft on them.GAME ENGINE: The game is..... Mostly okay. Like, there're problems with it, but it's serviceable. There are some small bugs here and there, but ultimately nothing that makes the game completely unusable. Aside from maybe the camera controls. They're awful. Genuinely. I don't know why the camera moves so stupidly slow compared to your look speed, which causes a hilarious issue where you massively overshoot while looking, and if you're vaccuuming and have broken a LOT of stuff, you create a huge lag spike a the game tries to figure out how to suck up a full 360 degree arc of mess all at once. Also the conversation menus are a bit buggy, with highlighting not properly happening on options you're holding your mouse over. And speaking of the mouse, being unable to see a cursor or a cursor crosshair while removing things or planting things? Is a remarkably bad decision. Fix this.MAP: The map is expansive and fun, though it does suffer a bit from some dreariness issues. And when the game starts getting dark, the map becomes grossly muddy to look at. So maybe give us some controls to boost the game brightness in darker scenes, or maybe even brighten those levels up with a nightfall/moonlight effect. Also there are some hilarious geometry issues with the map, from floating trash that you can't destroy in the Frozen area(specifically the power plant area), to a seemingly intentional way to get out of the map in the desert where you can go through a hole in the canal wall, fall to the bottom of the canal, and since you can't get back OUT of the canal without fast traveling, you can just.... walk all the way down it to where you're outside of the actual map, and in a wide open space of nothing. Which is amusing because there IS a way to get out of the canal once you get there. But it still doesn't get you back into the map.GAMEPLAY: The gameplay is alright. Nothing feels unfair, or WAY too grindy, though there is a slight sense of butting your head against a wall. There's a distinct feeling, however, that they reached a deadline and/or ran out of ideas, as the last part of the game ends up being a Half-Life 2 esque "Blow everything up with a god gun" romp that ends in a somewhat boring and really quickly resolved conversation. Which, again, wouldn't be SUPER annoying were it not for the fact that so much of the rest of the game feels genuinely unfinished. Like, one of the characters is in several places at once. In fact, a few of them are, while another character has you build him a house that he then just... doesn't go to. Several houses are still mostly destroyed, even after yet another character moves in and repairs one himself with no help from you(which is odd considering everyone else wants me to do their building for them), which has him existing in THREE places in the game at the same time. A robot you have to do a bunch of stuff with ends on a dialogue note asking him to go visit someone..... and he never does.... Several in-game items just don't have higher tiers at all(which I get, there's no point at that stage since they don't offer advancement opportunities), several crops have no use at all, and I can't help but think that some serious balancing needs to be done in terms of how much pet feed you want us to give to animals. Also let us multi-craft recipes. I know you can cheese the game engine into doing it with pet feed, but everything else gets confused and just doesn't do it. Fix that. Additionally, farming can feel a bit... I dunno, grindy? And while one of the later game lines talks about doing things with your own hands, it would be nice if there were options for automation, i.e. a later stage for the Robot house that lets you tell them to automatically harvest fields and put the results in a box, or even at a third stage, lets you set fields as "Plant This crop, harvest when ready, turn enough crops back into seed to replant and store the rest". In the meantime, Llamas are.... useless. They're neat, they're cool, and hilariously, there are more of them on the map than you can store, which is weird, but you get So much resources from just... clearing things out... that there's no real point in them existing. Maybe if they would venture out and slowly clear trash over time in random places all over the world or something, bringing back the trash and contents to storage, they'd be useful? As an aside, I never once put the building decoration stuff to use. My house is barren, in part because the space feels so ridiculously small with the camera issues that I don't wanna try fighting with it to decorate rooms that already feel a teensy bit claustrophobic. A gridded top-down organization mode would not go amiss(same with the outside space, to be honest, being able to move or rotate buildings without having to re-friend all my animals would be nice). There's a lot to like here. It's a cute game, it's sweet, it's amusing, but it's also a right pain in the butt with how it does stuff that just... doesn't work? I really hope they fix those parts soon, and continue to flesh out the world building just a touch, maybe with more house repairs, more water cleanup and environment cleanup, maybe even with getting the rail system back up to where it should be. Or at the absolute very least, don't have a door to one of the areas missing its door frame(Village to the oceanside space), or don't have there be a door that's chained up in the oceanside space that can't be interacted with even when you can interact with every single other door in the game. Do I recommend it? Yes. But ONLY if the developers continue to fix and improve this.Edit: Okay, honestly, I have to kick this back down to Not Recommended. The bugs are... plentiful... and while I did recently discover a workaround to the pet food shortage, the game has now rolled back my save not once but twice. And that's right about when I decide that enough is enough. I cannot recommend buying this game until they put significant effort into fixing the game bugs, and until the save rollback problem goes away permanently.

_childDocuments_.review: No Place Like Home is a very casual farming/cleaning simulator, and I think the devs did a decent job in making it light and simple. Combat isn't stressful and the progression is self-paced. The sounds were really satisfying to break down rubble and vacuum it back up, and the graphics were cute and fun. The music was a bit repetitive, especially if you've played their other cleaning sim, Fresh Start. All-in-all, this game was relaxing and fun, with a few caveats:-The water is difficult to direct. The aiming looks right, but I had to turn my character this way and that to get it to actually hit my target.-The story and characters were interesting, but the ending is very lackluster (though Cornelius was perfection).-There are materials in the game that appear to have no purpose -- flowers, wool/yarn, glue and the extra pieces from quests that you are sent to acquire. I'm not sure if these things were meant to do something and were just forgotten, but they take up precious inventory space and aren't worth keeping around as far as I can tell.If you want a casual gaming experience, I'd say you've found it in No Place Like Home. It took me about 26 hours to fully complete the game (achievements and all), and I do think it's worth the price, but I'd recommend getting it on sale simply because it's a bit unpolished.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a farming sim with fun NPCs to get to know, you will be disappointed. If you like farming sims, but you also like games like Lawnmower simulator or Power Washer Simulator, this game can be quite fun. The best part of the gameplay is sucking up the trash; if you play it like a farming sim you will be drowning in resources so quickly you won't be able to progress (I found myself drowning in money and resources and had to shift my game play style because I wasn't making any actual progression). The NPCs are 2 dimensional to the extreme; their dialogue is always the same, (Unless you've completed a quest) even if they're in a different location. However, you have to return quests to the iteration of the NPC that gave it to you, making it feel like they're not even the same person. The game feels like it's early access, even though it's fully released. TLDR; this is lawn mower/power washer simulator with extra steps. If you play it expecting that, you'll have a good time. The animals and their hats are hella cute.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched a couple of people play this on Youtube and found it interesting enough to play myself. I am not a gamer in any sense of the word. I do love farming and cooking games so this was right up my alley. What I didn't know when starting the game was that it was still in Beta. Not a bad thing, just never been a part of the formation of a game while playing it. There are still some glitches and some things are funky but overall at the time of writing this review, I love the game. Cleaning up the earth after humanity trashed it and let for another plant. You begin to clean up starting with your grandfathers old farm and branch out from there. You plant crops, tame and gather animals (don't do all of the animals cause you won't have room on your farm for anything else.) Just do 5 to 10 of each animal and you'll be fine. You find these little robots that are covered in trash and have to get the trash off of them and tame them. They will give you resources. They remind me of hyper puppies. Don't do more than 10 of these. Trust, more than 10 and you'll not have room for anything else. You find others who need your help and give you recipes for items you need on your farm. One hint while traveling through areas, your garbage collector will fill up fast. I choose to cut down all the piles of rubble in the area that I visit so that I know I've been through there already. Especially in the underground where you can go in circles finding your way. Look for golden suitcases which gives you recipes. The enemy robots are not really difficult to kill, some of the higher ones need you to vacuum while drilling and some need water to electrocute. Take your time, give each area a good once over before you leave and always, always search the bushes for suitcases. Can't wait for the finished product of this game. I may play through it once or twice again before the final launch, just to see if my time to complete it can do better.

For example:-Several simple grammar and spelling mistakes-My sprint stopped working randomly (a restart *did* fix it)-Base stamina is too quick to deplete compared to recharge time- sprinting 5 steps isn't great-Vacuuming up the trash you break down is an integral part of game play and the Vac does not reflect that- I have to make several passes to get everything up-Instructions aren't the clearest at times-Map design was definitely...a choice- paired with the hyper limited sprint, it's mildly infuriating at times-No way to see where your cursor is, which in a third person viewpoint makes placing/watering a guessing game-Game defaulted to 720x480 and performance mode, which made it look like it'd been lifted straight from PS2 era (not that major but definitely surprising)TL;DR Could be a very nice game, just feels like it should still be in Alpha with the amount of polish it currently has. name: Flock
detailed_description: Flock is a multiplayer co-op game where players take on the role of flying shepherds, each tending to their own unique herd of adorable flying creatures. The game is an ode to the joy of flight and discovery. Starting with a small herd of hover-sheep, you nurture and fly them toward fresh, untouched pastures. Along the way, you will discover the secrets of the beautiful uplands and its wild creatures. Weird flying creatures. Are they fish? Birds? Snakes? It’s a real mystery. They are mostly friendly though, and with a bit of skill you can charm them to join your flock. As your flock grows and your sheep get woolier, you can use the wool you shear from them for hats, cardigans, even socks! Will you find all the creatures? Even the super rare and elusive ones? Will you keep them to yourself or share them with your friends? Will you knit the longest scarf ever seen? Will you find all the hidden treasures stolen by the pesky Burgling Bewls?

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been an absolute blast so far to play. The overall mechanics are simple - fly around, identify new species, and charm them if you have the right tool (which you 'unlock' by finding them) - but the game itself is adorable and charming. I'm about two hours in and haven't charmed even 10% of the species in game. Species vary based on habitat and time of day, and also exhibit unique behaviors for the species too! As someone really into biology and ecology, this game's likely to keep me entertained for a while. It's also got little side missions and a few challenges that you can get out in the field too! 10/10 recommend if you're looking for a chill and charming game!
_childDocuments_.name: Flock

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re into creature collector games, this is a great addition to the genre! It has a cute, simple story with likeable characters and a neat gameplay loop. Play solo or online with a friend, fly around and seek a variety of beautiful creatures to add to your flock. The map is surprisingly big, featuring many unique zones which house 60+ creatures in total for you to find. Locate whistles to be able to charm new species by using an awesome distance style minigame that feels fluid and easy to master. Some creatures can only be found by using a zoom mechanic while you fly around, and they are hidden well! Traverse the map by coasting or hit wind gusts to quickly get to your destination. Mark areas with map markers to help keep up where you need to go in order to fill your creature guide. Achievements aren’t too bad of a grind, but you will need to charm every creature in the game, and then catch enough of each species to become an expert catcher. The outfit customization is amazing, and the art style is a joy to look at for hour after hour. You find yourself starting with a small herd of flock, then before you know it, you gather a horde of elusive creatures to accompany you on your journey. Great indie game that was a joy to play through!Achievement Count: 45Time to 100%: ~12hrsDifficulty: ★★✩✩✩Genre of Game: Creature Collector, Casual, AdventureFun Rating: 7/10Checkout my YT video review or my

_childDocuments_.review: The first few hours of the game are fun, (when the story is rolling), but then it becomes an impossible grindy slog post-game to reach max bars with everyone. Especially certain 'rarer' species. The spawn rate of the big white ones patrolling the marsh are still abysmal and will take irl hours of searching, even after the reluctant adjustment made by the devs. There's very sparse customization if you were looking foward to that in this game. The starting birds are all there is, and there's very few (sometimes only 2) clothing items to pick from, despite the sheep wool being the only collectible in the game you can continue to harvest indefinitely.  The post game is also bare and unfinished. There's no rewards for completing your collection besides making that species glow, no new cutscenes and barely a scrap of dialog about it; but given the forced camera angles and your flock liking to get between you and the camera while you're trying to do something in a lot of areas, it's a huge hindrance and not a reward as the glow makes it even harder to see.I don't know if the devs just want to artificially boost hours played or what, but the spawn rates of some of these creatures makes this game unenjoyable and more like a chore. 20$ is pretty steep for a 2-3 hour game, which is how long the story takes, I don't recommend buying it off sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Flock, overall, makes for a fun and relaxing game that's a joy to get lost in for a couple of hours each session. It's always fun to find new creatures and for the most part there's a good mix of common spawns combined with slightly more elusive creatures that need a keener eye to catch. The multiplayer is also fun to use for the purpose of playing with friends, though to be honest this feature also seems to be the roughest.Creature design is bright and colourful and you're bound to find at least a couple of favourites in a given species. Variants also mean catching multiple of certain species can be a fun hobby, and the sound design for the various creatures makes listening out for some of them a viable and valid tactic for hunting them down. (You might also discover a favourite creature based more on how it sounds than how it looks, since you can always sing to your flock with Y and see which of them answer.)Unfortunately, Flock is not without flaws. Most noticeably, for a completionist, the game overstays its welcome due to having criminally rare spawns, with no real way to improve the odds of finding those missing creatures you need. This seems especially odd given that a feature unlocked towards the end of the game - the Feed Bag - lets you place food in feeders to generate three random creatures native to that area. I'm frankly baffled why the developers didn't decide to include an option to trade Wool for a "Rare Feed Bag" from Jane, which you could then use on a feeder in a given location that increases the chance of rarer spawns. This would not only make feeding my sheep still worthwhile after I have all the fashion I want, keeping Wool a resource worth collecting, but would also help the game avoid dragging on by a  of hours to the point the fun experience turns into a teeth-grindingly frustrating one.Honestly, I love this game. I've had fun with it! And I do intend to try and complete it.But the Expert system feels wasted - there's little reason to be an expert save for completionist's sake and you're better just farming the same most common creature of a species instead of hunting down rare ones for more points - and the rarest of the game's spawns are so rare that you could be spending three, four to even five hours at a time not seeing what you need. And  if you're co-operatively playing with friends, you could be spending five hours for only one single spawn that only  of you can actually charm.So while I can recommend this game for casual players, I would offer a word of caution to completionists that this game will probably become a frustrating experience instead of a fun one, as the gameplay loop simply doesn't justify how rare those final elusive spawns can be and how much time you will feel like you're simply wasting, praying on a good spawn.

_childDocuments_.review: too short, too buggy, at least for the price.the style of this game is adorable and the premisse of finding and collecting creatures is interesting,however, theres some issues with this game that sour the experience quite a bit.first of all the game constantly interrupts your doing and yanks your camera away for every interaction, which happens a lot and becomes annoying quickly. In a game where fluent movement is ever present, a sudden stop like that feels like you're crashing.I also found some minor bugs. We got some innocent clipping through objects, which is better than colliding i guess.But then we also have a camera issue. Every 5 minutes the camera janks around 90 or 180° and when i happen to be in movement at this microsecond, i completely change course.That is annoying bc it happens a lot, but it's not exactly game breaking.What is gamebreaking is the spawnrates of some of these creatures.Some spawn one a day on the entire map and only for a few minutes.Which gets frustrating in the end rather than joyful collecting.if the devs fix camera and spawning (or even add some mechanic to make creatures spawn on demand) then this game could be very decent.even then this is a short and rather shallow experience.I played a fair share of indis that are only a couple of hours long but those usually have some sort of story arc and a satisfying ending. Flock does not. You find creatures and then you dont find creatures.So even while I enjoyed this for the time being, its too bugged to complete and became frustrating to keep trying.And call me picky but I think games should not be frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Flock is a cozy game centered around traversing beautiful and surreal landscapes and attracting various flying creatures to join your...well, flock. You play as an unnamed character who is a denizen of one of the prettiest and strangest openworld sandboxes I have experienced. You fly on a bird and with the help of your relatives you fill out a field guide to the various fauna of the land. The various flying creatures come in a variety of shapes, sizes and families. Attracting a new creature requires the right whistle for that creature's family and triggers a mini game where you can encourage the creature to join you on your adventure. The creature designs are varied and striking. Clearly a lot of work and love was put into their artwork. Another thing done well was the layout and landmarks of the open world. Usually I get overwhelmed and hopelessly lost in games featuring a large overworked but the landmarks and layout made for easy orientation. There is a map you can use but I found myself using it less and less. The serenity of flying around the map just for the sake of exploring is so sublime. Other than Dredge, no other recent game has made me feel so at peace with the world while exploring. There are a few ruffled feathers here. I was a little let down by the mini game that you play to attract a new creature was largely the same for each and every species. I was expecting something a bit more varied like the mini games in Dredge. While this did not make me dislike the mini game,  it makes me feel like there was a bit of missed potential. Speaking of missed potential, there really is not much in the way of a story explaining the world or how the various characters came to be in it. That said, there is a bit of beauty in the slice of life presentation. Over my 6 hours of gameplay,  I have found most of the species and anticipate it will take about 6 more hours to find the remainder and grind for a few of the achievements. Flock has been a lovely experience so far and I would love to see more games like this that create strange new worlds to lose yourself in. I very much encourage you to join the Flock.

_childDocuments_.review: Flock has a very cozy and beautiful world you fly through on the back of your bird in search of mostly bean-shaped and some eel-shaped colorful creatures and sheep. They all have different behaviours, sounds and habitats. Once you find them you can play a little tune to make them join your growing flock. Some of them are harder to find than others, so you'll need a bit of patience and willingness to just fly around at different times of day and try your luck in order to collect them all.One of my favourite parts of the game are the sheep which you can set down to graze on specific mounds, and once they've eaten enough you can shear them for wool and it has the best animation and sound design. It's also a delight to find a new one and get to name it. At first I was not convinced but after a bit I started to love the dialogue in the game as well. The clothing items also have humorous descriptions.The UI, drawings and sound design are beautiful and made me realize this game is from the same people who made Wilmot's Warehouse!I'm not done with the game yet but I wanted to leave a review anyway because I love it so much and I'm kind of saving the rest of the game for when I don't feel well again. I very much hope they will make more games like this in the future and I can't believe this feel-good gem doesn't have more reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game has been love at first flight.*hold for applause and uproarious laughter*For real though this may already qualify as one of the most charming, delightful and relaxing games I've ever played. You explore a big open world that expands as you progress, discovering and identifying different creatures and eventually earning the ability to charm them into joining your flock. I'd say it's just barely challenging enough to keep you on your toes, while still being a low-stakes and immensely relaxing experience (with easy-mode options for little kids or people who want even less of a challenge).You should absolutely get this game if you enjoy exploration, creature-collecting, fun traversal mechanics, and a vibrant, quirky aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game up until my save file got deleted in less than 2 seconds because there is no confirmation for deleting your save file. I play on controller and because of how my buttons are laid out, when I went to grab my controller to start playing, the button to delete your save file was held for a very brief period of time in which my whole save was deleted. No confirmation, no reasonably longer period of time to make sure that the user is really sure they want to do this. All of my progress gone in a game that is all about steadily building progress and spending time relaxing. I will not recommend a game that prioritizes "cool and quirky" UI decisions like hold to confirm over keeping the player's save data intact. It's a simple thing and doesn't need to be hard to implement. Why a game like this would assume that you are deleting your save files so regularly that it needs to be done in a snap is beyond me. Please just add an extra "are you sure you want to delete your save file" prompt.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, but janky. The automatic height while flying was very annoying at times, especially when I was too high in the air and had to fly around for a while to come back down. The camera was often too close to my character, and sometimes my character would be beneath the screen entirely.Co-op worked fine for two hours and then dropped unexpectedly. My partner was unable to reconnect to my game until they restarted theirs, at which point they reconnected and both of our games froze and crashed. There's not really much of a point in this being co-op anyway since each player has their own progression. We didn't notice any activities we could specifically do together, except for exploring the map.I believe I got about halfway through the game in the two hours I played, with most of the achievements being unlocked at the end (complete all of this, find all of that, etc.), so there's not much here anyway. Might be fun for kids, but I wouldn't recommend it to adults, especially not at the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, YES I would recommend this game. It's beautiful in its simplicity, colorful, with fantastic audio. The creature's chirping and environment music is delightful. The actual gameplay, travel, and charming system was easy to understand and master after a bit of practice. Flying around was an absolute pleasure, and my partner and I frequently logged in to just soar around the forest and enjoy the scenery. I also frequently chirped to hear my flock's response just for the pleasure of it! The audio team did a fantastic job here.I really admire that the devs decided that 'taming' isn't aggressive or forced. You 'charm' the creatures with love and music, and the creature voluntarily joins your flock without force. Its a refreshing change from so many games that trap/knockout/leash the creatures you acquire.There are a few notable issues I found during solo/co-op play. As enjoyable as this game would be to play with many friends in one session, some parts of co-op gameplay were frustrating.But if you want a cozy, colorful world to relax in and enjoy the sights and sounds, this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Flock

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of the day, I would definitely recommend Flock. I enjoyed my time playing and loved a lot of the features the game had to offer. It was cute, relaxing, and had a lot of charm to it. That being said, there were a few things that felt a bit lacking, and someone looking to purchase the game might want to take them into consideration.Here's what I enjoyed the most about Flock:The visuals were very pleasant, especially during the sunset and sunrise. The distinct style helped add even more cuteness to the land and critters. There was a decent variety in the creatures that can be found, as well as several different biomes to roam and explore.Some of the creatures had more unique mechanics behind charming them than others. I really liked this and it made it a bit more challenging to find some of them. Some you can only find at specific times of day, while others camouflage themselves and require a closer look. A few involve short puzzles that stand out, too.I also liked that you can easily manage your flock and make it to your liking. You can favorite creatures so they don't get replaced with newly charmed ones and just as easily swap out creatures when you're ready. You also don't lose any creatures, even if they leave your flock. You can call them back at any time. Flocks are also expandable to allow even more buddies to accompany you.Now here's a few things I didn't enjoy so much:The biggest complaint I have is how short the game is. It took me around four hours to complete the main story, and that was with taking my time. I'm sure if someone were to rush it, they could finish it within two or so hours. Even four hours isn't very much playtime considering the price. I was having a great time and didn't want to end things yet, so I kept on playing to unlock all the achievements. Doing this gave me an additional eight-ish hours. I still had a good time playing in those eight hours, but I had already seen everything there was to see. All I did was search the same few areas for specific creatures to become an expert in charming them.Speaking of becoming an expert in charming, I think the reward for it was a little disappointing. I mostly did it for the achievements and to one hundred percent the game, so I wasn't necessarily after the reward. Even so, something more unique would have been nice. Maybe a special accessory/bird color that can only be unlocked through becoming an expert? Or a bonus creature for each species that you can only find and charm by being an expert?I honestly don't know that I see a lot of replayability, either. It might be nice to return to once in a while just to fly around, take in the sights, and relax after a long day. Other than that, though, once you've seen everything the game has to offer, that's about it. For me personally, it's more of a game that I would return to after a few years to experience again.Multiplayer also felt quite lacking. I played solo the whole time, but still hopped in a public lobby briefly just to see if anything new was offered. Everyone progresses individually. You could have all the cloud levels lowered, and your friend would still only have two lowered. You can't help each other with quests or charming. I honestly don't even see a point in having multiplayer as an option when it works in this way. All you can really do together is explore, and even that is dependent on your story progress. It would have been neat if they had some creatures that were multiplayer specific and required teamwork to charm, or a different main story that accounted for multiple players and involved them working together.In spite of the few minor gripes I had throughout playing, I still had a fun time. I loved soaring through the sky, dashing under rocks, and collecting adorable creatures along the way. I have no idea if there are any plans for it, but I would love to see some future updates that add even more creatures to find and more areas to explore. :) .

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE collection games, and no matter what I always gravitate toward filling up the books and museums, rather than finishing the main story, even if it's not the point of the game. Whether it's catching bugs and fish in the Animal Crossing games, discovering the logs of monsters in Lethal Company, or doing it as the song says and catching them all in each new Pokemon generation, I just can't get enough!So you can expect my pure, unfiltered JOY when in the not-not-so distant past of 2022, I saw the reveal trailer for Flock and realized that not only was there a game that would scratch my collection and identification itch, but also one that looks AMAZING!?! AND some of the creatures look like NOODLES!?!?!Suffice to say I was hooked from the very beginning and I was going to wait for however lo- I forgot the game existed for almost 2 years...Anyway, in early June I rediscovered the game through it's release date trailer, and as if nothing happened, I was once again absolutely hooked on the game, chomping at the bit waiting for it to release.And that leads us to present day, and what do I think about it?...Now THIS is just what I needed.First of all, I definitely don't think this is even close to being game of the year, but if you want a beautiful, tranquil, cute, satisfying, collecting experience, this is the game for you and it won't disappoint. (+ noodles)P.S. If you prefer scores-> (9/10) = Dopamine in a cute flying capsule.

_childDocuments_.review: A proper old school shooter. Not a Treasure ripoff or some anime-bullet-hell-nonsense. This is the best new shooter I have played for as long as I can remember, the kind of lost treasure you would need an emulator for. It really evokes the feeling of the golden age of shmups from my childhood. It might not be a huge challenge if you are into these kind of games, but they do not make them like this anymore. If you should find it too difficult, there is a huge range of upgrades that mitigates the difficulty. The game starts with the developer thanking you for buying the game. I would like to thank them for making it.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and approachable shoot'em up. I normally don't like these games because I find them too difficult and not worth the effort to get good at. But Hybroxia 2 settles you into the difficulty nicely. First few levels are easy, then the difficulty gradually increases. By the time I was at the end of new game plus I was dodging screens full of bullets having a great time.If you want a nice little "My first shoot'em up" that doesn't overstay it's welcome, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: A game like this is tricky to review in terms of a strict recommendation versus not, mostly because it's so reliant of the history of the player who is picking it up, and how specific their needs/wants are from a SHMUP like this. To be frank, if there was a sideways thumb on this, I'd be giving it that rating.There's nothing wrong on the surface of Habroxia 2: it's movement and gunplay is solid, having a reasonable secondary weapon system that can lead to some interesting ship configurations and can produce some challenge in the early going. Its directional aiming system on the 2D plane is a little bit different in the genre and helps it feel a little bit special compared to others on the mid-tier SHMUP genre. The game's upgrade system does help in allowing newer or less skilled players in the genre to be able to complete the game, despite not having strict difficulty settings.With all that said, higher skilled SHMUP players will find the game's bullet patterns and boss designs to be lacking, feeling a bit repetitive over the long haul. Level design isn't entirely inspired in about half the levels, as even the claustrophobic caves start to feel the same when it's the 4th cave you've done in a row. The upgrade system starts to backfire on the game as even mid level shot power can absolutely destroy bosses in short fashion (not even when grinding for points), and for a game that's designed to be short and repetitious, you start to feel a lack of creativity over time. Enemy designs lack pizzaz and in particular, boss encounters almost feel like mini-boss counters over the long haul. There's a lack of oompf for a lot of elements from the game, as things like the music feel too generic to really get your heart pumping for the missions at hand. While the game does have a very basic story, it's on par with Arcade/early NES games, which may have been the design choice, but it still feels underwhelming especially when you get absolutely no reason/idea what's going at the mid-game.It's really a game for those who want an easier experience and a solid but not overwhelming entry into the genre for the price point. It's good, but not great.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my Habroxia 2 review, this time around Habroxia 2 is a Twin-Stick Shooter that makes the gameplay even more fun, let's get into the positives about this game.The story mode they have is pretty cool once you beat the game they have NG+ modes that raise the difficulty of each stage, level designs are way better than the first game and the boss fights are well put together as well, the upgrades are also better this time around and allow you to do more overall with your ship.There's also a few extra modes you can unlock that adds more to the overall experience, if you like Habroxia then you'll like this one as well.The only negative I have to say about this game is final boss was kind of a let down other than that it's still an enjoyable experience and I hope they eventually make Habroxia 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Watch my review here:Having not played the first Habroxia, I was pleasantly surprised by this sequel! If you're expecting a bullet hell shooter, this isn't it. It's an old school style SHMUP game that has nice retro graphics and music, many different types of bosses, branching pathways to find secret levels, lots of upgrades and abilities and it's a lot of fun! _childDocuments_.review: "Habroxia 2" is a shoot'em up game; not a bullet hell. A classic arcade game with improvements. You can upgrade using currency earned while playing or choose not to, for additional difficulty. It has a few fun tricks up its sleeve, like shooting at different directions. It's not revolutionary for its genre but it holds the fort just fine!It came to steam before "Habroxia" and it is harder, more fast paced and crazier than it!With many upgrades, different loadouts, cool bosses, branching paths and tons of action, there won't be a dull moment! It isn't very lenghty but it has an NG+ mode to keep you busy longer. And let's not forget the "Boss Rush" mode! The storyline of the game is a nice breather from all the action!It will take some time to make all the upgrades and you won't be able to bring them with you in every available mode. Decent controlling, fair difficulty and enough variety in enemies and modes to keep you entertained for a few hours! Unless you want to complete everything, that requires some extra playtime.For more reviews, follow my curator

_childDocuments_.review: Decent shoot’em up with same-looking stages and easy gameplay.There are two modes available, although it is recommended that you start with campaign because arcade has a bit harder difficulty.The gameplay is very typical of a space shooter. The biggest twist is that your main gun follows a twin-shooter mechanic that can fire in either direction. However, if you prefer the old arcade mechanic, you may enable it in the controls settings.The ship has a secondary attack that takes a few seconds to recharge. Weapons that are frequently used as primary weapons in similar games can be found here. Some of the possibilities are Vulcan gun, scatter shot, and missiles. Most of it is unavailable when you begin, therefore you must battle bosses to obtain new equipment. Another great feature is that the weapon may be fired forward or backward, and you can have a different weapon in each direction. Boost is another ability that uses secondary weapon energy, however it is used only very rarely to destroy small rocks and obstructions.Although enemies drop a lot of items, these little rocks frequently hide the best items. You can collect credits, health, or one of the special weapons like bombs or lasers. You can only carry one, so keep it for when you truly need it. Stages are nothing that hasn’t been seen before. It can become repetitive after a while because they look so similar with the same enemies. The objective is to avoid obstacles and kill as many enemies as possible, but the game keeps things interesting by mixing side-scrolling and vertical stages. A huge plus is branching campaign. There is, of course, a boss fight at the end. Stages have a couple of extras that urge you to replay them; bounty on a marked enemy and a missing astronaut that needs to be collected. Everything can be upgraded with credits found throughout the stages. The first stages can be a bit difficult because you’re so weak, but you will soon blast through everything when you upgrade the main gun. You only need to replay the first stages a few times and you shouldn’t have any trouble later.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing I noticed about Habroxia 2 was the unique weapons and the way they worked.   Normally these games rely on a primary weapon that fires forward and several secondary gadgets that clear the area with their own distinct fire patterns.  In this game your primary multi-directional weapon is controlled by the right stick, essentially giving you a twin-stick shooter integrated into a traditional forward-moving space shooter while your secondary weapons typically fire forward and behind with much more powerful effect but also with a short cooldown period between uses.  Ultimately, finding the perfect weapons setup is critical for beating certain levels, but weapons can also factor into a player’s personal playstyle.Much of the difficulty rests within the weapons and upgrade system, as the game never fluctuates from its mindlessly repetitive level design, enemy placement, and bullet patterns.   There is definitely some try-die-repeat gameplay here, but once you finally figure out that perfect combo of weapons and learn the levels like the back of your hand Habroxia 2 can become almost too easy near the end.  If you’re looking for another mindless space shooter with a charming retro design then give this a shot, but there are plenty of flashier and better constructed games out there just like this.Full review at

_childDocuments_.review: After as transcendent and fresh an experience as Elden Ring, playing a video game-ass video game like Ghostwire felt somehow refreshing. The story leaves plenty to be desired, kicking off with bland-man Akito and his vaguely tragic past being spared death by the unquiet spirit of paranormal investigator KK, a brusque and rough individual who takes up residence in Akito’s head, giving him supernatural spellslinging powers to tackle a masked menace who has banished Shibuya’s population to the spirit realm and kidnapped Mari’s sister. It doesn’t really go anywhere particularly interesting and the baddie never elevates beyond a monologue maniac but the interplay of Akito and KK is fun – they’re not at odds but are very much an odd couple with a fun dynamic. The gameplay itself is an interestingly paced FPS, nested into a compact and beautifully detailed open world Tokyo. Instead of guns, Akito fires off spiritual bullets that roughly correlate to a pistol, shotgun, and sniper rifle, with a little accompaniment from a super-powered bow. His movement is relatively slow compared to the hordes of faceless ghostly visitors he fights, meaning a lot of back and sidestepping or parrying attacks to jockey for positioning while revealing enemy cores to dispel in a brilliant shower of light and particles. It’s not the deepest combat but it has its moments of incredible satisfaction when one well-placed attack does away with multiple enemies. A lot of it takes place in the open streets, where stealth plays a part – crouch up behind an enemy and you can dispel it instantly. Traversal is somewhat limited but feels great. The player can zip from streets to rooftops via an amusing grapple system that becomes unlimited later in the game, then glide across alleyways and streets to stay up above the sprawl of Shibuya. I found myself much more taken with Ghostwire’s open world than much of its combat. There’s a degree of self-consciousness here for providing a relatively compact experience that could take only 10-15 hours, so the developers have absolutely packed the world with collectibles. There’s reports of KK’s paranormal investigations, hidden treasures to be traded to nekomata that come packed with bits of Japanese history and culture, and most staggeringly 240,000 spirits set loose in Shibuya to capture and ferry out of the cursed city via phonebooths refitted with DIY supernatural tech. The spirit collecting, I had cause to belief, affected the ending. As far as I can tell it did not, and I would caution anyone from pursuing this goal unless they’re really in love with the world of the game. Which I was, truly. It’s gorgeous and fascinating in very specific ways. Akito’s hands, for example, are the most well-rendered I’ve seen in a game, tendons and veins flexing along with fingers, knuckles going white with effort. The rain-slick streets reflecting Shibuya’s endless neon is the most taken I’ve been with raytracing since it became a buzzword, the foggy rainy be-spirited city taking on an incredible amount of shifting, scintillating color. It goes beyond urban Tokyo to smaller outlying suburbs for a bit, where modernization rams up against tradition in fascinating ways. The culture itself is a tremendous draw – each landmark, collectible treasure, and Yokai encounter comes with a corresponding lore entry reflecting on centuries of fascinating history. It feels like a major missed opportunity that the story is held separate from this, and I think in summary the game sounds less interesting than in practice. Where it triumphs most is having an overwhelming notion of its themes and setting and fully embracing them at every turn.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game but the review is for the update.They added an update, Spiderweb, and after it I hated this game. And it's not because of quests where you need to walk through all levels without a hit, but the random maps where you need to get one or another item for quests. And these maps are increadibly rare. I spent HUGE amount of time and still didn't get last items just because I couldn't get the right maps. So these update is an absolute waste of time. The quests on the maps are exact as in the game, just put on a small piece of map. And because the randomizer is so broken, it gets boring instantly. I wish I hadn't wasted my time on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire Tokyo Is a really cool looking game made by a bunch of artists who want to show you some cool sites, take in some interesting vibes, listen to some neat tracks they made on an ingame music player, and kill a bunch of ghosts in some really simple, but very flashy combat. It's not super complicated, it's not particularly revolutionary in its gameplay, and in many ways is "generic open world formula" with lots of collectables to collect, sidequests to do, and areas to clear... The story is fine (although in terms of storytelling really steps it up in the last couple of missions), the characters have some fun dialogue to listen to as you go around, but it's definitely the atmosphere that steals the show, the game's never aggressively trying to be scary, but it's got a general spooky paranormal feel that ends up as this bizarre mix of both occasionally unnerving and, after a while, weirdly relaxing. But what's oddly great about it is that Ghostwire Tokyo avoids a mistake that so many other open world games make and it is so refreshing: it doesn't overstay its welcome. I beat the game, did some exploring, finished all the sidequests, and it took me just less that 20 hours, and that felt right. it never stuck around long enough to get boring, it didn't demand that I dedicate my entire life to it, it was a game that let me see some sights, had some fun, and felt satisfied upon completion as opposed to relieved that it was finally over. And in an age of open world games that never end, having one that did before it ever became boring or annoying just felt really nice.So yeah, I will be remembering my time with Ghostwire Tokyo fondly and, especially in the current climate of this type of open world game, that's more than enough :)

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this game is worth 10$-20$ at most.It is such a short game, the only reason I got around 24 hrs game time is, because I went for some of the very boring achievements which at some point I also stopped, since it got too boring. Main Story:The story is unbelievably short for a 60$ game (I think if you only do the main story, you'll be done in 3 hrs).The story itself was very uninteresting which at some point made me just skip all the cutscenes and get done with the game.Combat:At the start of the game, I though wow this is going to be fun but later I realised, the combat doesn't really progress through the game, you literally do the same things from the start to the end, no real new techniques or enemies which would make the whole combat experience more fun.Skill system:There is a leveling and skill system which is very minimal, you can power up some of your abilities a bit and then learn 2 new executables and the rest is more like whatever, it doesn't really add to the whole combat progress, to make it more entertaining.The thing what I really enjoyed was the design of the city, it really felt good to walk around and look at things, I must say, it was very detailed and by far the only thing I enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Gameplay was fun with a variety of weapons, parrying, and quick purge.- Visuals (especially towards the later chapters) are very creative - Side missions were interesting and not too tedious- Animations of the combat and general interactions were satisfyingCons:- I played on the hardest difficulty and disabling the ability to gain xp which increases your synergy level and gives you skill points prohibits you from making upgrades on the skill tree. Seems like an artificial way to add difficulty.- Boss fights weren't that hard or innovative- Personally, I found the story somewhat interesting, but it is clearly the weakest aspect of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!A great action title, but in my opinion the game shines the brightest through it's story and the world that it created. I love the attention to small details around the world and for the Japanese culture.The hybrid between the modern age and Japanese culture is amazing although a bit too unclear in some parts, but from what I understood that's the intention of the developers, to let our imagination do some work. The story also has some unclarities if you are really after the details from the same reason.The story is great, but it can feel that the main objective is sometimes a bit out of focus.Combat feels great and is interesting with the mechanics it has and I love the fact that you can go however you want in the game, go loud or be sneaky. There is a great variation of enemies with different sets of moves and abilities so the combat won't get boring.The two main characters are a great pair that made me love them. The antagonist is also great with an interesting background and story.I don't feels like the game is horror, but it certainly has it's moments that would get your heart pumping. Especially through it's atmosphere that the devs just nailed it.For the achievement hunters out there, the 100% is not that hard to get and not even that boring since the game has different systems and mechanics to help you track collectibles. You can finish the game and then go back on the same save and clear all the achievements, and that I love. The only problem I had with the 100% wast The Spider Thread. ST is a rogue-like approach of the game and it feels nice for the people that just want a bit more out of the game, but for the achievements hunters it's hell. It's nothing too hard but it's looong and fells like a literal chore to finish. So the hardest achievement is certainly Catalog Conqueror.In conclusion, I would highly recommend this game to anyone especially if you love the Japanese culture and traditions since it has plenty of.Good luck and have a nice one!

_childDocuments_.review: I know this is a Bethesda game because I'm avoiding the main story, all combat devolves to spamming left click and healing items, most of the good content is in the side missions, and most of the fun is in the environment and exploring it.I really want to like this game. I'm a weeb who enjoys collectathons and the supernatural. But I don't, it's just not interesting.Even ignoring the dull combat(every other review is right about it, so I won't cover it), my main issue is that the collectathon portion doesn't feel rewarding or challenging. The rewards for collecting most things is money which is mostly useless, and XP which does let me level up to get through combat faster I guess. And rarely am I doing something interesting to get the collectible, it just happens to be on a roof or behind a rock or something but I can hold tab, spot it instantly, and go get it with minimal effort. The ones you can't just turn on wallhack for are a little more interesting but beyond being neat items in their own right, are only good for money. The fundamental issue here, I think, is that the game is very committed to being a realistic city, and cities are mostly boring buildings. This is why the side missions are so good: it leans on the supernatural to make the boring building interesting, but outside of those set pieces the apartment building the ghost is on top of is just a rectangular apartment building like the all the others.I can't be asked to care about the plot, there appears to be some intrigue but it is painfully clear who the bad guy is despite the game trying to make you doubt your ghost life-partner. The rest is figuring out the mystery team's story and that just doesn't motivate me to watch cutscenes that I could just skip. Also your sister is trapped by the baddie, which really just makes this weeb Banjo-Kazooie.All in all, I am 5 hours into the game, and all I can think is: do I want to spend another 15 holding right click on ghosts while occasionally progressing the plot? Not really.
