_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it, though the Far Cry-ish open world felt like it dragged in the middle. Totally my own fault since it was far from mandatory. Side quests in that part were mostly samey or simple, but there were memorable ones like the school (added in the Spider's Thread update) and finding TP for the poor soul stuck on the can. As for the story, it was a big ol' whatever. Standard fare and nothing to write home about, but it was fine. Akito and KK grew into a good duo, and Hannya was sufficiently hammy for a big bad.The game also looks amazingly detailed, and I spent more time than I should have walking around exploring the area. I did spend the first few hours messing with the config file to tone down the overbearing blurriness of the TXAA and some other effects, but I was surprised how well it ran on my poor old i5 4670K and GTX 1070. Overall, I enjoyed my time with the game, even if the open world felt like a bit too much.Oh, and don't use the English voices. Just don't.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit that I've put 32 hours in this game reaching some of the rare achievements. I normally don't do that. I don't care about chievos. I don't collect "feathers", neither I run from corner to corner of a huge virtual city without at least minimally interesting errands.In Ghostwire I almost felt ashamed spending hours searching stupid objects and selling them to cute floating cats. Damn I did that! And I kinda liked it, because I felt some strange tranquillity when rummaging across streets of "Tokyo", yet spending my time pointlessly. I think this tranquillity came from such factors as charming graphics, almost total lack of challenge (including counter-based) and Tokyo stylistics itself (and I must say it's perhaps the best Tokyo implementation in video games so far). Or maybe I was simply in the mood...... Because this game was clearly driven by marketing dept. of Bethesda. Instead of filling the game with interesting (and long!) side quests, NPCs worth talking to (ah, same marketing from recent Fallouts?), and meaningful "object search", we do collect here:- emotes- music- outfits- rendering styles- what else hmm... ah yes, the most important bit - ♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera stickers!!!Please tell me why or why would I ever need all of that virtual crap? I really want to bang my head at my desk because I cannot explain how in 2020s game companies still think that they can create dozens of hours of gameplay, which rewards gamers in non-gaming experience? How bold a person from marketing should be thinking that the game of this genre will capture a person's time not only for 100% completionism, but also for... replayability? Seriously? Do they think I will replay another 32 hours so I can collect ALL STICKERS? Sigh.Well I'm almost OK that I spent this time because of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tranquil evenings which gave me quite a decent nostalgia for Tokyo. I'll go get now BG3 or Starfield and spend virtual time with much more quality and less regrets. If there's a plan for Ghostwire 2 of any kind, I only wish for it to reconsider the gameplay, making it either less open or filling it with more content worth looking for.But gosh, this marketing department is really good, made me collect "feathers" again.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on a whim when i was deciding what game to play during my short break from playing the entire Yakuza series. I was wanting a game that involved collecting things and doing tasks in an open world and I already had this downloaded, so i thought i might as well give it a try. Thankfully, this game met my expectations and more! After a few days of consistently playing it, I have beaten the main story. I did a very hefty amount of side content and i thoroughly enjoyed every moment. I loved the side content and how it matched exactly what I wanted, with their being tons of yokai, tanuki, statues, and more to collect during my time in Shibuya. The main characters and their story had just the right amount of edginess to match the setting and tone of the rest of the game. The visuals in this game are so consistently interesting that it really feels like another world has bled over. Ive heard people say that the combat wasn't the best, but i disagree. I enjoyed the combat until the very end, and as much as i may have stuck to a couple tactics too much, it always felt energetic and responsive. I never felt like i was overly strong or overly weak, just that i was working through it as i was supposed to. I was consistently satisfied with the difficulty (I played on Normal) but i can see it getting a lot more frustrating if i was on a higher difficulty. Also, something that cannot be understated is just how cool it feels to see all the locations of shibuya, the yokai, all the random objects you find, and all the stuff my american brain hasnt had the chance to explore before. All in all i felt very positively towards this game and i would highly recommend anyone who enjoys open world games with cool visuals and an emphasis on collecting and light horror elements.

_childDocuments_.review: A mysterious fog falls down on Tokyo and people that touches it vanishes. You play as Akito a young man who watch over her sick sister when she is kidnapped to serve as a vessel for a ritual and pretty much dies defending her. Now a spiritual being know as KK will partly take over his body giving him supernatural powers to help get rid of ghost plaguing the city and to rescue your sister. Acquire offensive power of air, fire and water to fight along the ability to glide and a variety of other gained by points when you level up.Tokyo is absolutely beautiful and feel devoid of life with only ghost and animals lefts. The combat system is interesting but will get repetitive really quickly, this would be a major problem if the abilities were not numerous and for the about 30 types of ghost roaming the city creating at least some diversity. There is many items hidden on this large map to hunt and a few Easter eggs.By the end of the game if you picked up everything you will nearly be invincible defeating all enemies in a few hit. The ending is the most unsatisfying I have seen in years, it vaguely resolve the plot while giving a "life lesson" about living to your fullest with some of major inconsistencies.Now the DLC is a major problem switching style completely to a rogue like game. Complete various puzzle levels with random objectives. Earn ethereal cash to improve your abilities and spend it quickly because if you die you loose all your items and money making it extremely hard and unsatisfying.get only if you are a dying fan of this game and like challenges.Is it good, yes ! Could it been better story-wise, definitely ...

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly hard to write about this game, it's an interesting or weird one depending on how you look at it and what are your expectations, I'm loving it myself, if you enjoyed Bethesda's other action games I'd say give this a try, I would say it's similar yet so different.The gameplay by itself is not that advanced, you got three abilities and a bow as the primary weapons and I get the criticism about how it could get boring after a while by itself, if you're going for the 100% yeah some of the side missions are pretty much the same and collecting the spirits will absolutely get repetitive, also the game is very easy, I'm going through (by accident) on the hardest difficulty and didn't even notice until i checked the menu 17 hours in which also completely disables leveling which I don't even know what it does and playing on controller which I suck at yet I still basically only ever died to frame drops, so if you looking for a challenge this ain't it.However if you just wanna go through the story, do the more interesting side missions like the setting and the atmosphere you'll have a good time with this game. Developers deserve the support for taking the risk to make something actually unique, a rarity these days.Also it's recommended you exceed the recommended system requirements if you wanna turn up the graphics and even then there still will be frame drops sometimes and crashes too. The single patch that was release didn't fix anything, still plays like the pre-load build, there wasn't a day one patch either.

_childDocuments_.review: How to put this... It's not Mirror's Edge, not Dying Light, not Far Cry, not Doctor Strange, not Harry Porter, but perhaps it's all of the above, and more.There aren't much games out there, less open world, that depicts locations in Asia, but this game does, and it NAILS it.The size of the open world, combined it with the compactness of Tokyo's infrastructure, as well as the vertical manoeuvrability of this game, makes it the best open world I've ever experienced. And it provides details that you would otherwise not expect from its peers. (I don't recall the last open world game has actual functioning escalators) Explore-able in door areas are peppered throughout the world, from free roam, to side quests.The amount of player customisation, including first person view, has way more than you'd expect from a first person game. Decent sized skill trees, solid, and satisfying combat. Oh. Did I mention you can not only feed and pet dogs, but also converse with dogs and cats?TL:DR;If you aren't the type to read through notes, take your time to explore, and immerse yourself into the world the game crafted and provides for you, you may not enjoy this game as much as you would otherwise. This game heavily rewards you for ♥♥♥♥ around and find out.At the time of this review (7 hours), I'm only at Chapter 2. Tackling all side quests and collecting everything I came across.Updated Review:With the recent updated content (New skills, new missions).Ghost Wire: Tokyo started off as more of an action oriented with Japanese Occult themed game. But not anymore, introducing a new area with 2 part mission. The horror is full on. While the horror aspects are pretty much a cliche, the execution is none the less perfect. Compound that with accurate Japanese school setting, it easily sent chills up my spine.And the updated skill tree, made the already satisfying combat, even better.This is one of the games that I did not regret not getting it on sale, it was worth every single penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: So I am kind of torn with this game.  I was a pretty large fan of previous projects from them IE The Evil Within.  And during the game I was almost completely convinced they were connected from all the weird digital distortion effects.  But you are in fact not connected to a STEM computer (as of this time of writing).  The story is kinda very generic but it does tug on your heartstrings a bit.  I don't want to talk about the story too much so lets move on to the gameplay and gameplay loop.Combat can be pretty thrilling and visually very cool!  But combat after a while is repetitive.  You have three basic "ammo" types.  And they create a charged attack or a regular attack.  Wind is semi auto pistol ammo, water is shotty ammo, fire is rocket.  I had upgraded all the combat skills and while it was nice, they don't feel impactful at all.But lets talk about monsters and fighting.  The combat early on is great.  Enemies are creepy, ammo is not super plentiful unless you know what to look for.  It felt tense and exciting.  While they do introduce more monster types to fight and they all have their own looks and patterns after a while they feel brain dead to fight against.But I digress.  This game is not bad by any means.  The visuals of this game are really insane.  The reflections, particles, everything.  Enemies look fantastic.  Combat looks fantastic.  I just feel like for an open world game it just needed more oomph.  Maybe NPCs that make sense in the world.  Random events that occur within?  The open world kind of feels very unalive while it makes sense in the game it feels weird.  Overall despite its weaknesses I give it a strong 7.  This developer has a good record for me and I feel like this can be made a lot better in the future.  This would have been a 10/10 for a PS3/Xbox 360 game IMO.Pick it up on sale and I think it will be worth your while.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: It's a above average game, the plot of the game has some missing cuts of which leads the player to wonder "Wait what happened to this one guy or wait wasn't he just here how did he end up here...". The combat is great, however the melee in this game is underrated and should deserve equal love as the range attacks.Overall, it's a good fun game with easy controls that'll learn quick. _childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Very intense and deep story. Graphics and game play are fun, but it gets very, very redundant fast.It's open sandbox collecting souls and feeding dogs. This game has so much more potential than what it ended up actually being. Had the Story not been so rich and interesting I wouldn't have recommended it. The Boss fights were unique, nothing out of this world difficult at normal difficulty. Didn't have much trouble at all to be honest., This game is different from other games being it's a Japanese title and i'm American so the culture differences and such were more interesting to me because of it. This game would be a good choice when it's on sale. If you want a game that you can mindlessly collect souls hopping from rooftop to rooftop and opening gates to open new areas, then this is your game. If that doesn't sound like something you're interested in, then don't bother.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: I almost missed this game due to the marketing. Even the cover-art makes it look like some over-styled laser-whipping, neon-lit game where you pull off cool move after cool move without stopping until it is over.Well, I'm very happy I bought it eventually as part of a bundle, because it's absolutely the opposite.Yes, there's plenty of neon signs, Yes, there's a sort of whip to collect spirits, but the effect is entirely different from what the marketing suggests. It's not exciting, it's not action-packed; All of it serves an entirely different purpose: Making you feel lonely and abandoned... Even the primary antagonist which you'll see on any poster advertising this game is very rarely present... mostly he does speeches to ... no one in particular.The result is disturbing. The world is as it should be with millions of people present, but there's nobody home. It's a bit like World of Warcraft but rather than the quests being connected, they're just that: quests for you to do without any real meaning other than helping these tiny, unimportant souls, which really are lost anyway and whose lives didn't really have any meaning even before the events put in motions by the before-mentioned antagonist.Even the enemies are meaningless. They are repeating shadows of real-life archetypes like the greedy banker, the soulless worker and so on. Nothing about them is any way exciting. And there's not a lot of them anyway. And they aren't dangerous either.This games is absolutely tedious. What makes it a great game for me is that it doesn't apologize for it. This game absolutely drives home the point that the world is gone and what's left behind is a soulless wasteland.The controls are a little wonky if you don't use a controller, but it's acceptable. In fact in ties in rather well with the tedious nature of the game. The graphics are not technically top-notch, but they are coherent and believable, which in my opinion is much more important than technical prowess. The city depicted here really feels like it has been alive at some point, which is important in that really makes it feel abandoned now.The primary story-line is pretty straight forward and told in pretty nice cutscenes (mostly, but not entirely ingame): Brother tries to save sister who has been abducted by bad guy who has succeeded in in turning everybody into spirits. by teaming up with spirit of former demon-hunter. Sometimes (towards the end) it's a bit cliché but effective.I haven't tried the English version, and I suggest you don't either. This game is very much designed to make you feel out of place and having to read subtitles absolutely helps.I know this isn't really a review, but more of a story telling you how this game surprised me. Long story short, if you like a game with a great scenario, event if that scenario effectively means bad gameplay, give this one a try ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: The game was boring and it took me like an hour to figure out how to continue with one quest and every so often when i would right click the cursor would go off of the game and i would have to spam click in order to get the cursor back on the game. it would happen all the time in combat and outside combat because right click is used for a ton of things
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: the new update includes DENUVO DRM.Not sure if Bethesda or Tango is to blame.But this is definitely weird - sometimes, some JP games come with some sort of DRM on launch, but there's a chance they remove it later on. For Ghostwire, the game has been out for a while and now they randomly decide to put DRM on it. This DRM only hurts legit players (there's enough proof that Denuvo will affect game performance and at worst, make the game unplayable for lower spec rigs) and if you need an explanation why this won't prevent piracy or actually 'protect' the game, you'll need to do some outside reading since I'm not going to get into that.I'm just glad I'm not affected since I finished the game months ago and have long since uninstalled it. DRM certainly the reason why I wont bother to check what the new content is. BUT if I still had my game installed, and it auto-updated, and DENUVO was installed without my consent, that would be a completely different story.---As for the actual game, personally, I enjoyed it. Its really NOT for everyone thanks its gameplay and delivery. Feels like an oldschool, early-PS3 JP title back when Japanese game devs were still open to trying out new things in games instead of being forced by their corporate overlords to just follow whatever AAA trend is selling. The only thing modern about the game is the visuals, which looks very much in line with the quality of late-stage PS4 era games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun, stylistic game that really dragged me in. Throughout my run of this game I was still finding myself enjoying the unsettling and spooky nature of the game. I could not have loved the soundtrack, ambience, and exploration any more than I already did. While the combat and story weren't standout they were still a joy to partake in. A definite recommend from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: I have always been a fan of large open-world games, so I enjoyed playing Ghostwire a lot. The visuals and gameplay are astonishing. It can get repetitive at some point. Still, it has its moments and is worth a shot.Personally, I love the interaction between KK and Akito. The banter and teasing between them make them sound like brothers. Their relationship makes the game better for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: I already knew from the moment I seen a trailer for this game that I'd love the game and I was right. THE best game ever. I normally like a lot of chill relaxing and cute games that aren't stressful at all, but this game really tops all of them.You can tell the amount of effort and love the team put into this game. The environment for this game was so immersive and so detailed, I enjoyed standing next to this shop that had such an addicting store song and I'd occasionally pass different stores and just stop for a bit to listen to the stores music. Sitting on top of a building and seeing nothing but abandoned cars and buildings, items and clothes worn from the people that were taken all strewn on the ground, the silence of people but the continuing music of all the shops buildings, billboards, animals, nature, and running vehicles left behind felt so powerful in a way. Don't get me started on the traffic lights turning red during fight scenes and the rain not being rain drops but being tiny little rain kanji. It was really amazing to see and feel the effort the team put into this game. Sometimes I wish this game had the nap options like Stray (LOOVE that game) because how pretty the environment was and just sit there and take it in. The visitors were so fun and unique (except for two of them, y'know which ones I'm talking ab that keep popping up out of the air). I just wish there were more to the random yokai other than them being used to obtain magatama and some side missions, esp my favorite cute Nurikabe. I also think I really loved all the really really unique side missions more than the main mission (well not always, KK I won't forgive you for making me cry man). The gripe people have saying its a collectathon and saying they dislike that part of the game doesn't make sense to me because you can literally just ignore it esp since a lot of it is rewards if you want your skill tree to be 100% unlocked and just random fun. I was actually surprised so many people didn't even finish the second chapter of the game just because they were overwhelmed over stuff they could just ignore, I just genuinely don't understand how they could drop such a pretty and cool game.I loved the game so much that I decided to 100% it before I even finished chapter 4 (also because I really wanted the tanuki suit because it was so cute and cursed). I honestly don't have the patience for collecting stuff or grinding in games but this game made it so fun to do, I did it all really as I hit new areas so it was never overwhelming having to tp back and forth to different areas except for the odd few achievements where I couldn't find all the tanuki, artifacts, or spirit photos (ok the daikyo achievement was the only sucky one which took like 3 hrs to get because I was so unlucky but the feeling of finally being on the brink of death because I got it gave me so much happiness).The only real gripe I have with the game is that it would of been better if we could also feed all the cats like we can with the dogs and get an achievement for feeding all the cats and dogs in the game, but upon starting Spiders Thread I forgave it because its all focused on cats which is so adorable and reminds me of when I played Monster Hunter Rise with my bf. Oh and also a really cool chance they missed out on is somehow making the giant stand nearby the tokyo tower and you looking up seeing it looking down at you since you always see it in the distance looming near the tower. There were actually a lot of achievements they could of made as well, like the graffiti stickers and getting everything for the photo mode unlocked which I used a lot and maybe a special simple mission like the tanuki one for unlocking and finishing all the nekomatta missions since they're all so cute. Also the amount of spirit photos we had to do was crazy lol, prob could of toned it down a bit. OH also I was so salty (not really) that once I finished the game they gave you OP prayer beads that let you go thru the game collecting spirits and the side achievements so much easier than what I had to deal with lol.Anyways, there's really a lot I could fangirl over this game but I'll keep it "short." When I heard the news about Tango (still crying I will never get a second game or any other new games, curse you money grubbing Microsoft) I immediately went back to the fan art building they dedicated a whole area just for their fans amazing art and just took in all the art and love this game received from their fans. I hope they know that despite the sucky situation that happened, they created games that they should be proud of for the rest of their lives. Thank you Tango Gameworks for your hard work. Thank you Ghostwire Tokyo for such an unforgettable and fun experience.Now to get the 100% achievement because Spiders Thread is kicking my ass
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo is a good game but some may struggle to find as much enjoyment as others.I think the most important thing to think about when deciding whether you're going to spend money on this game is to determine what's important to you in a game.If you're looking for a deep combat system or a story with incredible depth I would suggest you look elsewhere.On the contrary if you're looking for a game with an visually stunning world and satisfying collectible's I think you may just find yourself sunk into the beauty of this games rendition of Shibuya for a solid amount of time. 15ish hours if you rush the story and do some side content. 30 hours if you're looking to 100% the main game, and 40-45ish hours if you're looking to get 100% of the steam achievements including those in the games alternate rouge-like mode which is totally free and okay.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't remember the last time a games ending/ending sequence made me choke up and cry. But this is the most recent example. Maybe im just a sensitive baby ♥♥♥♥♥ but, the way life and death is portrayed as beautiful, and how that translates into the way the end plays out just made the story all the more touching. The music during cutscenes, gameplay and that oh so gorgeous ending is S tier. The game itself is just as beautiful as the story, Unreal Engine 5 is no joke. The combination of abandoned neon streets with the fascinating backdrop of Japanese folklore, all wrapped up into the streets of Shibuya. _childDocuments_.review: I had some high expectations from this game knowing it was a part of the Sony-exclusive story-driven game, but it was a letdown.Just researching that the game is based on Japanese mythology, you would think it should be interesting, but it is not. The story initially feels exciting but wears off after a few hours. The English voice acting is very average. I played the entire game in the Japanese dub with English subtitles, which made the game much more enjoyable.Many things happen in the plot that have no explanation. One thing happens after another, playing like a sob story.The one good thing about the game is its graphics. Man, are they beautiful? It gave a good run for its money to my 4090, which looks very pretty in some places. However, the character models ( humans and animals ) look old and dated. However, some monsters look fabulous ( especially the scissor lady ).The gameplay is good but needs to be more challenging; even when playing on the second-hardest difficulty, I hardly died while playing it. The gameplay is passable. The game needed to do more to keep me hooked on the story or its side activities. It was an okay game.

_childDocuments_.review: + you can pet cats and dogs+ cool enemy design+ good gameplay / combat+ lot's of stuff to collect & interesting places to explore- lot's of stuff to collect (I hope you like collecting)I recommend playing this, if you're interested in japanese culture - all the items have interesting back stories, there's a lot of stories from daily life and folklore, etc... if you're just looking for a cool fighting / horror game, this one might have a bit too much lore / collectibles.edit: also, I got this on sale for 20 bucks - for that price, it's really good. _childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it. This game reminds me of Infamous, Bioshock and on some elements a Far Cry game. Some might not like that it has the same format as a Far Cry game (capturing outposts over and over again), but that is something I have always found to be fun.It can get repetitive. As I said, you have to capture 'outposts' (toriis) and the side-quests are somewhat tedious. I know that that is not everyone's cup of tea so just putting it out there.Otherwise, the game has had a lot of love put into it. The detail in the buildings, character designs, side-quests - it is amazing. It is hard to put into words but the details are crazy-good.  The dynamic between the 2 main characters was also very fun. Pretty sure I mainly liked the game because of those two - because of their relationship.  If I had to evaluate the characters individually, I think I would not have liked either of them.The plot didn't interest me that much. As I said, the 2 main characters' dynamic was what kept me being drawn in. The plot seemed to only be a way to keep a story going forward. I never felt really invested or immersed in the plot. Even if the cons seem to affect the main points of a Video Game, I still felt like the game was worth my money and time and that the game is fun. I definitely don't recommend that the player plays the game in one sitting, as it can get very tedious that way, but the game is definitely worth playing.TL;DR  -  Can get tedious and boring - still liked it because of the love put into it and because of the two main characters and their dynamic.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: If you have any interest in Japanese mythology, and want a different take on open world gaming, I think this is just the thing. As someone who is VERY tired of open world games where you run for 15 minutes through empty landscapes only to shoot 3 guys in the head and hoist a flag, I'm happy to see Tango essentially said "but what if its Tokyo, so 100x more Japanese?" It does have fights and collectibles, but you fight faceless ghouls with you elemental powers, and collect the spiritual remains of weasels with sickles for arms. Climb towers? Try lassoing a flying tengu. Fetch quest? Yea, but for a ghost on the toilet who needs more TP. Forced stealth? Sure, but only because this kappa won't eat a cucumber if he thinks I'm watching. It doesn't break the mold, so much as applies that mold to a more condensed/focused world, and with a folklore twist. Instead of running through empty landscapes, its running the incredibly detailed streets of Tokyo, or gliding over their rooftops in spectral form, looking for souls to cleanse. I will say I don't know that I'd recommend this at 60$, but on sale for any less its a no-brainer for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo is an intriguing game that blends elements of action and horror in a supernatural urban setting. With a compelling plot, impressive graphics, and unique combat mechanics based on mystical abilities, the game delivers a visually captivating experience. However, some players may find a lack of depth in the narrative and yearn for more variety in missions, just like I do! Overall, it stands out for its unique atmosphere and innovative gameplay mechanics!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun so far. If you like simple combat that evolves through abilities then you'll enjoy the action. The game is vibrant and and well designed from a graphical standpoint. You'll find yourself gliding from rooftop to rooftop before dropping behind an enemy to rip there core out. Enemy damage is high and the parrying feels just forgiving enough that it is hard to master but easy to learn, while the new abilities you earn will have you trying out new attack combinations for more efficient kills. I find myself crowd managing often, setting up 2 or 3 enemies in there weakened state before multi killing them. I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: It won't bother everyone though, because it didn't really bother me. The flaw is Tokyo. You're playing in Tokyo and as you can imagine, there aren't a lot of different looking places within any large city, so even though there's a lot to explore, it all takes place inside a concrete jungle. The scenery can get old. There are A LOT of power ups to discover and collect so if you want to be strong you don't really have a choice but to traverse the map. I imagine that aspect coupled with the repetitive scenery will bother some more than others. I have a feeling JRPG players, grinders, and most importantly....weebs, are going to be far more welcoming and forgiving of this game than others. I won't lie, the Japanese lore and culture in the game is pretty interesting/fascinating.There's a lot of good though. The graphics, the combat is fun (weaving hand signs never gets old to me), the game mechanics, I liked the cast and the story is decent (it gets better as you draw nearer to the end). It's not really a scary game but there was one side mission that got me. Had resident evil feels to it lol. Some of the side missions are really good, others are fetch quests, but you can't tell which is which. Mixed bag. The game is also kinda easy. I played on Hard difficulty and didn't break a sweat at any point in the game. Game runs well. 130fps 1440p native ultra settings with minor dips in certain areas. Game crashed once. It's solid.In the end, it's a good game man. What can I say? I don't regret my purchase....though it was 67% off. Delicious lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Ghostwire Tokyo is a great game. Initially when I heard about the game, I was hoping the devs would focus more on the horror aspect; they did not. (Mind you, the game does have horror elements, but it's not the focus.) However, what they crafted is extremely fun, and I am happy with (and prefer, even) the direction they chose. I plan to do another playthrough on the hardest difficulty once I upgrade my PC.I wanted to mention some downsides.Optimization - Of course all new games seem to have these issues. (My CPU is minimum spec, while everything else is recommended+.) When I would start a play session, my FPS would start at around 120 and drop over time, eventually reaching less than 30. A save and exit to main menu, followed by hitting continue always fixed this problem. Some of the cutscenes would lag and my FPS would tank. However, most of the time it would recover fairly quickly. It wasn't a smooth experience, but it didn't really take away from the story, for me.Hyakki Yako - I wanted to 100% this game off of the get go, and now I have. However, I would have completed the game at around 38 hours, if not for this random event. In the beginning of the game, you're prompted to hide from the Hyakki Yako. This taught me (and others, I assume) that I should hide from them when they appear, fearing what may happen if they catch me. I avoided them all throughout the game and when hunting the last of the spirits and wondering why I haven't hit 100%, I realized after a google search... There are spirits trapped within the Hyakki Yako. While it may make sense for spirits to be trapped within, I really think the game should have told you somehow. (I am aware it is on the minimap, however it did not display 'Hyakki Yako Spirits' until I had completed the event for the first time. Seeing as I avoided the Hyakki Yako for the whole game... You get the picture.) Having to spend an extra 4 hours running around between 4 teleport locations to try and force spawn them was tedious and frustrating. Do not play this game without an SSD. I moved the game files to my hard drive as I realized my SSD was getting full; this was a big mistake.Little nitpicks; No FoV slider. I would've liked slightly more UI customization. (I couldn't split interaction icons from mission icons. I played the game with minimal HUD to be further immersed in the game, I only kept the ammo information on screen in the bottom right.) Voice logs don't play when you pick them up; I think they should. (I do actually think a couple of them do, but not all.) I didn't get to listening to a majority of these until after I had completed the game and was doing completionist stuff. Additionally, voice logs should continue to play when you swap tabs in the menu, or close the interface. Finally, when attempting to complete the food checklist for the achievement, I found that the consumables tab was not listed in any discernable order.Thanks for reading, and I hope this helped inform your purchase of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo oozes style. Its world is incredibly detailed, gorgeous, and enjoyable to explore, with Japanese folklore to learn about and immerse yourself in.If you have Ubisoft-fatigue i.e., open worlds that require you to perform mundane tasks to check off objective markers on the map, then either its gameplay loop will be offputting to you or you may have to overlook it. Its combat is overall simple and can be repetitive at times.After its initial release, a roguelite mode was added that is as fun as any game dedicated to its genre, and it is completely free on top of the base game.I will admit, for me, this game is style over substance. Had this game not sold its world so well, had it been another setting, it might not have been as enjoyable. But because it is so immersive as an experience, its vibes so immaculate, I am willing to say it is an actually good and underrated game.It is a shame that Tango Gameworks is no more. I can only hope the developers of this game are able to pour their creativity and hard work into other projects in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: So far not many glitches other than I did get caught between a wall and a bike and the bike wouldn't move. There are some occasional frame loss but I am playing on highest settings minus RTX (was using it and didn't like the performance loss) with DLSS set to quality. Will test on my older PC to see how well it runs. Story is fun as is gameplay. You can pet and feed the dogs of the game as well as pet the cats (haven't had the option to feed despite owning canned fish). The tone is very serious and the world building is amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo isn't a perfect game, and the control scheme can feel kinda funny at times(right click for interact/aim), but the game is well worth a play-through for the atmosphere alone. Pros:Shibuya is an incredible environment to explore and just take in. There is just enough unease in the lack of people filling the streets to never fully take away that slight on edge feeling you get while roaming around. The Visitors are well designed and uncanny though there aren't too many varieties of them. The folklore and inspirations behind many of the quests, collectibles, yokai, and enemies is all really nice as well. There's not much horror to be found throughout, and the few moments there is some it is pretty effective.The story is engaging enough, and emotionally resonant at the end.The paranormal/tech aesthetic is really damn cool.Cons:As mentioned before the control scheme can be a little odd sometimes, and the lack of a dodge can make combat feel clunky at times, but the perfect block is satisfying when it's pulled off.If you're looking for a horror heavy experience you're not gonna find it. This is an action game with horror inspirations and themes.The game suffers from most typical open world game problems particularly in it's collectibles. Many repeated events for the Magatama and the copious amount of souls to collect could be off putting to some. The game does give you tools to track down some of these collectibles easier though.The game get's pretty easy once you've hit max level and have the bead power ups which made the final bosses feel a bit underwhelming.I doubt I'll ever go completionist on this game, but in the 27 hours I did put in I was able to accomplish a fair bit of the collecting, and enjoyed the story and combat quite a lot. The game is worth a play though(especially if you get it on sale), and I enjoyed my time with the game greatly!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Yes it could be seen as a time sink; the combat was not really challenging, enemies were repetitive, and it wasn't really in the horror genre though there were certain horror elements in some parts. But I had a boat load of fun. The gameplay was top notch, the Japanese voice acting was great, and Tokyo was beautiful. I didn't have to think or try too hard, everything was straightforward - just the right kind of game for a casual gamer like me.

_childDocuments_.review: Tango games are kinda odd. Evil Within 1 and 2 are great fun on the first play through but the shifting environments, focus on stealth and especially the obtuse narratives always overwhelm when I think about firing them up again.Time will tell if I ever feel like running through Ghostwire: Tokyo again, but I really loved it and was almost feverishly compelled to 100% it.PROS+ Tokyo is quite something to run around and explore.+ Atmosphere is top notch.+ The side quests are fun and charming.+ Combat's a little simplistic and on normal mode the talismans feel like fluff, but I never got tired of it.+ Well paced open world stuff along with a satisfying level up system.+ The eeriness without jump scares works much better than Evil Within's tWiStEd NiGhTmArEZ.+ Raytraced reflections occasionally astounded me and are the first time I bothered with RTX.+ Collectathon could have been a negative, but it's all cool Japanese lore and lovingly done.CONS- Story is pretty basic and the villain is disappointing, but it's an improvement over how bogged down things get in the Evil Within games.- Things occasionally feel empty in the bad way. - Performance is wonky. Restarts always had me at a smooth 60 fps and it felt like FPS gradually slipped the longer I played.Loved this game but it's not for everyone. If you're interested it's worth picking up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: To the developer: Please let me disable the rain. Tokyo Ghostwire's rain system is by far the most frustrating, and immersion ruining weather system in any game I've ever played. It's loud as hell, blocks your entire vision, takes forever to stop, and when it does stop, it's back within minutes.Besides rain: While Tokyo Ghostwire's world is a nice walk though Japan simulator, the game itself is a victim of it's own success as the world feels like a grindy wild goose chase, and the story suffers as a result. While the first few hours were really exciting, after killing my thousandth ghost, and collecting yet another set of souls the gameplay loop started to feel meaningless and boring. Call it ADD or something, but I've tried so many times to get on with the story, but I keep forgetting what I was doing, or why I'm even supposed to be invested in the game at all and I just can't seem to finish it. While the visuals are beautiful, the game has a severe lack of depth in my opinion. If I could describe what it feels like my first word would be "dead" (which if you think of it is quite in-theme, but that's beside the point). The game is dead quiet, there's barely any atmospheric music, and the only time there's any playing is during combat.

_childDocuments_.review: A really repetitive game that gives a nice break from all the try/hard games out there. Because of how hard it is to actually die, or how easy it is to stay alive, this games allows you to explore endlessly and gather souvenirs and souls for hours on hours! _childDocuments_.review: This is some initial impressions, I am far from completing the game.The game did not try to detect the OS resolution and started in 1080p. Furthermore, it has 90s style resolution selection in the menus: you have to click through every possible resolution to finally reach 2160p. The arrows that accommodate that change - or any other setting adjustement for that matter - have a very tiny hit box and are easy to miss with a mouse. The menu experience is not as bad as Elden Ring but up there.I started the game and saw the first part of the opening cinematic (this is rendered in real-time) and then the game gave me a warning about missing video codecs (this is where they cheaply start a pre-rendered part of the opening cinematic). First of all, the game does not have the required codec bundled-in, unlike so many other games on Steam, which have everything required installed on the initial launch. Furthermore, why didn't the game warn me about the missing codec when I started it? Why did it do literally in the middle of the opening cinematic? On a side note, I've already played that same game on PS5, and the whole real-time cinematic-to-pre-rendered-cinematic-switch is done very poorly - you immediately see color change and frame-rate change (I've had the game in Performance mode and the pre-rendered cinematic runs at 30 FPS), furthermore, pre-rendered cinematic there has full-on RT while the Performance mode does not.The game runs great at max settings on my machine but there are often stutters when traversing the level (without even much else happening, you can move forward and every now and then stutters will follow). These are not present on PS5 and is probably the same reason for stutters are found in most of the mediocre console ports - shader compilation is done on the go (and it's pre-cooked on the consoles; some decent ports - like HZD - do this pre-cooking as well, by the way, although at expense of slower initial launch).Otherwise, even though the art is great - hands down - the game does not sport any impressive visual tech. Despite some use of RT, the light/shadows don't look as realistic as in Dying Light 2 - very far from it. Everything is either too shiny/too much reflection or too dark. The light does not bounce around the room in any realistic way.Some negative highlights:- Too many pre-rendered cutscenes right in the middle of real-time rendered cutscenes. The former run at noticeably lower quality and it breaks the immersion- Mouse controls are not too precise and most of the settings I've seen for acceleration/sensitivity are for controller exclusively- Constant micro-stutters while moving around, no matter what the graphic settings are- Loading times are fast but I am sure in 2022 it would have been possible to stream going in and out the building without a loading indicator (sometimes it's a very prolonged black screen, sometimes an actual loading indicator)...- Even with all RT on, it doesn't look very next-gen (when compared to several games that were released as far as a year ago even)- "Corridor" open-world. You can re-visit anything but the levels are very narrow corridors in essence and as such don't give the depth of, say, Dark Souls games, which were also "corridor" open-world (and Elden Ring is full-blown open-world)- Rain looks really bad. In fact, it's the worst-looking rain I have ever seen. It looks ugly and It also freely pours through concrete roofs- Extremely repetitiveSome positive highlights:- Great art- Slightly fresh perspective on the FPS- Has F.E.A.R. vibes (the hospital scenes almost look stolen from that masterpiece of a game)- No missable achievements- Aside from micro-stutters, runs really well with everything to max (and looks noticeably better than PS5 version event on Quality)- Still better played with a mouse (this is more when comparing to the PS5 version where mouse is not an option)My verdictI was super-excited by this game prior to actually playing it, but now I don't think it's worth its full price. Maybe it's not worth playing at all. This game got repetitive super-fast, even when not trying to do all the side content. You get new skills, new equipment, but it doesn't change pretty much anything. One hour in the game feels almost exactly as at the beginning. I recently spent over 100 hours on Elden Ring and, wanting for me, I finally got to playing Dark Souls 3. Every time I played these games, I couldn't stop, as they kept and kept on giving new interesting content. Ghostwire stops giving about 15 minutes in.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire Tokyo is an excellent game.The controls are immersive. There are many different attacks each with their own style, and there are SO many different ways to approach when an enemy wave is approaching. The story (so far) is well made and interesting. Furthermore the atmosphere is incredible, I could easily imagine myself spend an evening just exploring Tokyo to enjoy the atmosphere of it.The cutscenes could easily look like something from a movie, they're so high quality and the sound and cinematography is perfect.On the negative side it can quickly get repetetive and boring to 100% and get all the achievements on, but the main story and even side missions are a pleasure to play. Some of the side missions could be a story of their own and the visuals are just as good as the main story visuals.The normal difficulty is a little easy too, so I'd recommend to play on hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo is a beautiful and eerie jaunt through the streets of Japan, coming face to face with lore and legend while fighting for your own quest and purpose. With seamless gameplay and fighting mechanics, 40 hours of exploration will seem like no time has gone by and it will leave you wanting more time running the glistening streets of Shibuya.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo was pretty enjoyable to me. I like the visuals a lot, and the gameplay was pretty good in my own opinion. I would say its a solid 15 hour game if you're like me and not looking to 100% everything. I really do like the environment of the game, just going around looking at stuff is really cool. And some of the designs of the enemies are very cool as well. Though only one really made uncomfortable in a good way. And I actually like the combat in this game, I think its pretty fleshed out and have no complaints. Feels pretty unique. I hope to see if they could use this system in a different game somehow in the future. My two biggest issues with the game aren't huge. I think the story could have had a bit more to it. Not that the story is bad, but since that was most of the game to me I'd give it a solid B. Maybe it could have been a little longer as well, the final half of the game feels a bit fast. My other nitpick is that the sidequests could be a little more interesting, there are some cool ones, but a good amount feel samey. There's collectibles and stuff but I'm not gonna comment on those since I didn't dedicate myself to actively trying to get all of them. I think now in 2023 and onwards, if you are looking for a cool experience that you could probably go through in a week or two, I'd recommend grabbing this on a sale. Overall, I'd give it a B+!

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game both aesthetically, and with fun gameplay that is exhilarating and addicting.  It is very rare for me to do sidequests over the main story, and this game sucks you into it so nicely.  There is always something to do when running around from quest to quest, and just taking in the environment and colours of the world.  The story is a bit iffy and confusing to follow, but overrall it has a good message and sucks you into the feet of Akito pretty nicely.  Highly recommend, and will probably try to 100% it if I get a better computer.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun, interesting, keeps you moving through the game because you want to know more/or discover whats next, its well balanced in difficulty and there are moments where you get stranded without abilities and end up with no arrows or magic, but thats because YOU played incorrectly and now you will punished for it. _childDocuments_.review: I would say I enjoyed it for the first 10 hrs and then looked forward to finishing it. That's not to say I did not enjoy the rest, but more like well, rest was OK. If you have read the other reviews, the reason is obvious. The number and type of enemies you encounter, the type of activities are kinda in a loop.So, you start the game with elemental magic power of win, add water and fire. The power of elements are also in that order. You get about 12 casts of fire, 25 water and 60 wind when you unlock all the jizo shrines relevant to each one. Wind is meh dmg but abundant. Water is kinda aoe, allows getting through defenses (umbrellas) on some tougher bosses, but fire is the real deal. Of course fire is also what you dont usually have access to much most of the game.Talismans and beats are very useful in some situations. Sneaking, especially from higher ground to one-shot strong *but not strongest* mobs works well and I would advice to do so. To unlock some higher versions of spells, you need magatama, yet another collectible from some activities or sometimes you have to buy (expensive) from vendors. I think going for movement related higher spells, like flying for 5secs served me well (played on hard difficulty). Having access to more arrows is also good b/c well, arrows are powerful especially if you can headshot but nothing stays in place long, so if your reflexes are not great, you waster some :) Oh also, they drop after a certain distance so you have to target above the head based on distance.As game is kinda open-world, albeit you need to unlock torii gates to clear the deadly fog to be able to explore more and more of the map, you need to travel on the ground and on the roof. So, I prioritized skills that help you with that. In terms of skills, some you unlock by gaining XP via killing ghosts, doing side and main quests or by finding stuff. The most important gain of skill XP comes from finding the investigation notes of KK, the ghost that possesses you. Of course, you can run around and use keep scanning, use shrines and praying for finding stuff or well, you can use mapgenie.io :)You gain HP by eating various food you find or buy but even when you reach top level, 55, you still get 3-shot at most if you don't heal. Somehow, gaining more xp does not seem to make you too strong. Oh healing is on cooldown and I think the max healing item I saw heals you for 150 while at the end of the game I think I had close to 400. Most heals you for 85 to 130, a few secs cooldown where you need to avoid dmg and you can top off.Graphics were good. The attention to detail in incredible. You go into someone's house and just look around, it has so much detail. Oh don't bother opening up 'bathroom doors'. There are zillions of them, and 99% does not have anything. There are other things you can interact and open with nothing to see. Just use your scanning/senses.Story, eh name implies it. It's weird, this is not like Final Fantasy juggernaut we are talking about, dont expect anything really, it is more about exploration and gameplay which after a certain point is more of the same. If you want to learn about Japanese culture, there are lots of tidbits there in the database. This is not a game you will remember for ages, there is not anything that is extra good but then again nothing extra bad either. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD: The music, the atmosphere, the attention to detail, and the setting.THE BAD: The combat variety, the finicky traversal systems, and the lack of trading cards.THE BOTTOM LINE: Ghostwire Tokyo is a love letter to Japanese music, culture, and lore. The game is layered with all sorts of interesting facts and tidbits about just about every aspect of Japan, from its historical artifacts to its food. The story is straightforward and earnest in presentation. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys thoroughly exploring a map and reading up on the neat things they find.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as full of horror as I wanted, really not scary at all, but still fun.  I didn't come in expecting a spook-fest, but because of that I had fun.  The combat is interesting but simple, and the side quests are hit or miss, but I am enjoying my time.  A good between game for those big boys like Elden Ring and Horizon: Forbidden West.  Check it out on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: What do you mean Joe?-  Ethereal Weaving  is pretty fun... for about the first dozen times. Then you realize it's only three spells with a single shot attack and a charge attack. No mixing, no flowing. Simply that. Three spells with a single shot or charged shot. -  You get a bow, but it is the most flat, none impactful bow you will ever shoot. You also get some talismans: one stuns them , a BUSH talisman  and a distraction talisman . I believe there are a few others but I hadn't unlock whatever it is yet.-  Running the game on high at 1440p the game looks pretty good. Performance holds pretty well at over 60 fps too. Not running RTX. - : The combat is the most fun with ethereal weaving, but it ends there. The fights themselves are boring. Enemy variety after 7 hours consisted of ~6 enemies total? Enemies are easily kited and movement for your character and the enemy are just slow and clunky. - : The crazy thing is, the trailer I watched had absolute BANGERS. When I get into the game and start fighting, there is NOTHING. No music, nothing getting you pumped during the fight. It's flat. In one "boss" fight, I heard some solid beats, but it was drowned out by the enemies moaning the entire time.  Outside of the fight though, nothing. Just flatness. Your character uses the same voice lines over and over again. Feed the dog? ONE LINE OF DIALOG. Spend money? ONE LINE OF DIALOG.The crazy thing is Tango Gameworks made The Evil Within and The Evil Within 2. Both amazing games that hold up to this day. Ghostwire: Tokyo feels like a step backwards. The game is just full of busy work, with boring side quests and boring rewards. They often give you "skins" as rewards but the thing is, you can't see those skins outside of their photo mode. It's just shoehorned in there. They hook you with this cool magic weaving and then just stopped there. This could have been something amazing, and instead I'm left with regret.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of very interesting visuals and has a nice game play loop. The main story line is pretty cool and has some really neat spectacles in the boss fights. _childDocuments_.review: Really great game with an innovative and fun combat mechanic.  Beautiful world too, especially if you have been to Shibuya and Tokyo before.If you are experiencing frame drops, try setting "Level Streaming Distance" to "1" and "Texture Streaming Quality" to "Auto" (all the way left), this helped immensely and only got me one instance of framerate tanking during 5 hours of play.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought this game would be super boring, so it took me a long time to pick it up. In the end I really enjoyed it, but I still think that it could be very easy to burn out on (for some people at least).The main thing that made me enjoy the game is probably my inner completionist. The game by default would be very short but there are a lot of fun side quests, collectibles and such.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a pretty good game inspired by Japanese urban legends. The game puts players in the character's first-person perspective to get the most realistic view. The combat scenes when casting magic are also very high quality and quite skillful. What impressed me the most is probably the game's background which is quite detailed, it can be said to be a realistic sketch of a real-life Tokyo city. In particular, the game's plot is not seamless and the connection to create highlights is not as expected. Overall, if you don't put too much emphasis on the plot, Ghostwire Tokyo is still a perfect choice for those who love the Japanese horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: If low FOV and no option to change it bothers you, don't bother with this.  Editing the INI files with the usual FOV fixes for Unreal Engine games doesn't even work, it's hard-coded to ignore that, as far as I can tell.Also dips in framerate every time something new appears on screen (which is often), and this is coming from someone who's only trying to maintain a solid 60 on reasonable settings and 1080p, nothing more.  Its also coming from someone who has 70+ hours in Elden Ring and rarely experiences that game's infamous stutters and performance drops.Might be a great game, but I can't recommend based on those technical factors.

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell:  "The triumph of style over substance"...  aka "What I've come to expect from Bethesda products"I'm 14 hours into a game I bought on a sale forever ago.  On Halloween, I decided that, in the dark, I would finally play it to knock it off my "To-Do List".  I'm enjoying it......enough.  However, one thing is clear to me that may not be apparent to all within the measly 2-hour refund window you get on Steam:This is a game of "busywork" and "getting high off of itself".  The style is good......like REALLY good.  I dig it a lot.  The atmosphere is solid.  The design and graphics are excellent.  But, much like a date with a vapid fashion model, there isn't much there once you start relying on anything beyond what your eyes see.  I find myself already wondering, less than 20 hours in, if I will be able to give enough of a crap about any of it to slog through to a "100% completion".  I may.  At the very least I see myself saying, "Screw it.  Let's wrap up the campaign.  To hell with all the collectibles and side quests."  However, for an open-world filled with ghosts, you'd hope that the "busy work would be worth it".  I just don't think it will be.I spent $20.  For that price, I'm ok with it.  For that price, YOU would probably be ok with it.  However, temper your expectations here.  It's "middling gaming" at its "middling best".  It's average.  It's "fine".  It's "a decent time suck".  It will not change your life.  It's not one of those games you "excitedly tell your friends about".  You'll play it.  It will tick away your finite life as well as the next game.  If that is all you want or expect, prepare yourself for the "plain oatmeal" of gaming experiences.However, if you want a game featuring two protagonists merged in order to overcome a great evil....you may want to check out Middle Earth: Shadow of Mordor, instead.  At least there is substance and innovation there with solid gameplay.  That being said, if you already played it......I suppose you could give this a try.  Just buy it on the best sale you can and DO NOT buy the deluxe version.  The only other "market" I can think of is that sub-group of gamers who are, to be as polite as possible, "Japanophiles".  I like Japan, though.  I find the culture fascinating.....and I am exhausting all the interest I have just to push through this.  You're going to have to have something more pushing you through than that...or just have a MUCH higher "appreciation" than me.  Even as a "tour of Tokyo"...there are better, more engaging games.  Persona 5 and Akiba's Trip come to mind....the latter not even being all that great either, but with a LOT more character.All in all, the final score is a whopping "meh" out of 10.  Even now, as I write this, I am trying to decide whether it gets a "thumbs up" or a "thumbs down".  I have decided I will toss a coin.  That's how average this is...I can't even be bothered to decide on my own whether I'll recommend this or not.  "Tails" it is....sorry Tango.  On the upside, that was one of the more exciting moments I've had with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had saw this game on a facebook ad and I told my husband, "oh yeah i have a new game to play." Then i forgot the name after telling him and i was so upset, but thankfully i saw another ad on facebook. Added it to my steam wishlist and a friend ended up buying it for me because i was gushing how great it looked. I knew i was going to like this game, but didn't think it would turn into me playing it for the past four to five days non-stop...The combat system, the graphics, the interactions with side quests, the way the environment changes to stay relevant to the story, and just everything else that is a feature in this game is so breath taking, and amazing. The way it also incorporates Japanese culture and spirit lore is amazing. It sometimes does feel grindy finding the spirits to transfer, but other than that; it's a completionist's dream and you can still focus on the main story line without missing anything. 100/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game through proton on Linux.Graphics - Beautiful. It's gorgeous. Environments could have been a little more varied, but each area at least has a distinct flavor. I had minor performance issues with when red explosions were present until I turned ON ray-tracing. Weird.Gameplay - Fun. A few warts. There are some weapons and items I rarely used. But generally I liked the movement. The character's actions feel a little slow at first but it fits thematically and mechanically with the of the rest of the world. The game takes your powers a few times, but it has specially crafted encounters for those moments.Story - Cohesive theme. A little bit tropey. I liked it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some fun things in it and can be enjoyed. Running around a video game Tokyo is super refreshing and the detail in the world is something to be enjoyed. Walking into houses and apartments is super cool and I love all the yokai they included. Caveat: big glaring open world-itis problems. Not a lot of enemy variety. Try to cull your play thru to picking only 3 or 4 skills you want to spec up completely. The rest definitely don't need that much. You want the real, proper ending? Watch it on youtube. Don't save all those spirits. Definitely much better with a keyboard and mouse.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: There was a lot of criticism towards this game regarding it's gameplay and lack of variety. But that is an oversimplification of what is really going on. You have several skills to your disposal that often need to be combined or switched up. Sure you can play it like a shooter but when you switch up you will get so much satisfaction out of this game. And yes, it does take a little while for the game to be challenging. However slowly but surely you will encounter some enemies who you can't dispose of so quickly. And no, this isn't a horror game. But make no mistake, there are missions that do embrace the creepiness. Still. in essence this is an action adventure with focus on the adventure and that is simply is top notch. I like the world that has been created and certainly wouldn't mind a sequel where atmospheric horror will be the focus. It would definitely enhance the gaming experience. Overall I am having a lot of fun even when there are too many collectibles in the game.Edit 06/06/2022: I platinumed this game, meaning I got all the trophies and did all what the game had to offer. Some trophies were questionable and frustrating but keep at them and you will get them. If you are a little intimidated with collecting all the spirits then there are ways the game helps you out. There is a special grapple move that makes it possible to summon a Tengu and then get on places that are hard to get to. There also is a set of prayer beads that points out the spirits. Plus you get some spirits released when you dive into the demon parades and defeat the enemies who are trying to catch the spirits in cubes. I stand by what I said, I had a lot of fun playing this game and definitely is one I can recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Conclusion: So generic and bland you'll be bored of it after a short hour and half. I'm in my mid 40's and I've been gaming since the Atari 2600. I'm going to need a damn good game to stay interested. This is NOT it. The gameplay feels like your standard 'open world but not quite' ubisoft - it's FarCry, Japan edition but with dumber enemies that just stand there. Marrying old and new Japan is neat, but gets old quick. The story is as generic as the sequence of buttons you need to press over and over again to win  - to a 'hold left, click right and hold middle from time to time'. As for the "side missions" - I didn't expect skyrim, I didn't expect fetching rolls of TP either.. Does it look good? No, it looks GREAT. The graphics are on par with Observer: System Redux and at times beat it , but the budgets are different evidently . So to demo your new rig? Defo the 'wow factor'. Running the game on max Ray Tracing with all options set to cinematic will require a 30xx series GPU however. With a 2080 + i9900 combo, you can count on a solid 60fps running  RT on medium, all options default and DLSS to performance. Add adaptive sync or similar and you're in business. And it's worth it - the stunning location in Shibuya look life-like at 32:9 on a SUW monitor (i use a G9) @ 5k. Gorgeous, especailly as HDR is handled well and configurable to 2000 nits (if suppported). Gorgeously boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game at full price.The default settings are not optimized at all and look grainy/fuzzy and the camera settings are very hard on the eyes. After about an hour of researching how to fix the camera settings (google some presets and turn off VSync), I had to then load the game through my nVidia experience app to optimize the graphics settings. Finally the game is playable and looks gorgeous.....but its empty.The whole city is empty with very few enemies around and the ones you do find are so easy to defeat. The combat is extremely basic and is the same for the entire game. I only played 9 hours and I have all the combat abilities unlocked and its the same one shot firing system that's very lacklustre and uninspiring. You also get a bow.....that doesnt do much or even do serious damage at all -  and when you actually need it later on, its useless. You just have to stealth kill your way out, which isn't a play style that is super fun in this game.Its not even worth it to run around town fighting the few enemies that are there because the real leveling in this game is gliding across rooftops to absorb spirits and then using the phone to turn them into EXP. I leveled up to fast like this and unfortunately that's the whole game. Basic and boring combat, in a mostly empty city and leveling through rooftop gliding to absorb spirits - with a hint of story in there too.I'm sure the story is good, but I just cant bring myself to finish this when I'm running around by myself just doing random stuff without any sense of real urgency or purpose. And the "boss" fights.......What a huge let down. I was so excited to see this menacing enemy about to cleave me in two; only to find out that I use the same basic combat to take them down exactly the same way as every other enemy in the game. The fight ended so quickly and ruined the great introduction and promise that it had.The trailers for this game look so good, and it has so much potential; but unfortunately it falls flat in every area that matters. I paid $80 but this content isn't worth anything over $20.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a thumbs sideways,The good things I liked about this: the graphics are great, I love the aesthetics, the setting is neat, and the dynamic between Akito and KK was fun. And the only thing this grants you is money (which I found worthless in this game) and xp (which you will cap out on long before you collect everything). _childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo was a game that I was very excited to play since it was debuted at E3 2019. I'm an enormous fan of Shinji Mikami, he's an icon of the survival horror industry, and I loved what Tango Gameworks has put out so far with The Evil Within 1 and 2. I was expecting a horror-themed adventure where I would need to pick my battles carefully, know exactly what I was going up against, and plan out what resources I'll be using in the fights ahead for what I could not easily circumvent. The game was far more straightforward than anticipated. The combat has amazingly fluid animations, exposing a Visitor's core and ripping them out feels so visceral and satisfying, much like the Glory Kills in the latest Doom titles, and weaving between Wind, Water, and Fire attacks to handle different situations always did feel fun. However, that is the entirety of the combat of Ghostwire: Tokyo. Once you have all three elements and the bow and arrow, it never develops any further than that, and aside from bosses, enemy diversity is sorely lacking. Traversal is monotonous until fully upgrading your glide and Tenku summoning capability, which is an enormous investment of 7 Magatama tokens and 40+ skill points. And unless you're playing on Hard like I was, the combat is almost never threatening or tense. Once I'd learned the timing on every enemy's attacks (which did not take long given how few enemy types there are in the game), most encounters were a breeze, and quickly became tedious. The characters and story also leave a lot to be desired. The villain is a one-note megalomaniac with little to no development or characterization beyond being a BBEG with a motivation that makes perfect sense to him alone. The banter between Akito and KK is entertaining at first, but their dynamic barely changes from Chapter 1 to Chapter 6, the end of the game, and unless you are reading supplementary files or listening to recorded voice lines, you lose out on a great deal of characterization and motivations. The world is beautiful to behold, painstaking efforts were taken to render photorealistic streets of the Shibuya District of Tokyo, and it feels vibrant, real, and incredible to explore. Though there is little reason to do so unless you feel like doing every side quest, collecting every relic, and collecting every soul in the city. Due to the nature of the game's premise, there are no NPCs in the game to interact with, the streets are quite literally a ghost town, which I think greatly hurt the game and its atmosphere. Ultimately, I feel disappointed with the end result. It does not feel like any other game that Shinji Mikami has worked on. I was hoping for something in the vein of Resident Evil, or The Evil Within 2, but this feels too much like your typical run of the mill open world sandbox Ubisoft copy-paste title. The side-quests and hunting down yokai felt so much more fun than the actual main story, and I wish the game was more like that instead. Investigating spiritual disturbances, finding out what their grievances are, and either making them happy so they leave on their own accord or battling and exorcising them oftentimes felt much more fulfilling of a gameplay experience. At the end of the day, 5/10. Not offensive, not great, but it felt like it was sorely missing a lot of substance. I would not recommend this game at the full price of $60, but I would suggest picking it up when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Ghostwire pretty cold, not knowing really all that much about it. And my expectations were entirely off. I expected a somewhat slow paced and horror oriented game. What I got was a first person action-adventure game that revolved around spirits and dead people but in no way was creepy or horrific. This didn't make it bad, just not what I at all was expecting. As things go, Ghostwire is a solid game, but the only thing it really excels at is looking fantastic. The story, the gameplay, the audio, all just kind of falls into the "it's not bad, but it's not exciting" category. There are some interesting elements, like being exposed to so much of Japanese folklore and spirits, but it's also let down by a lot of grindy and repetitive gameplay. Collecting 240,000 spirits, even if you're getting at least 100 at a time, is a lot. Over 100 relics. 50+ statues to find. 25 tanuki uncover. Plenty of yokai to find and engage in their mini-quests with. Lots of side quests. You get the idea. They don't change a lot and rapidly become tedious. Once you've gotten a megatama from an oni or kodama, you will do the exact same thing for every subsequent one. Similarly, the enemy variety leaves a lot to be desired too. You'll be seeing some of the same enemies throughout the entire game and only occasionally will you have new ones that appear. They look good and fit the overall game theme but after you see the same faceless guy in a suit with an umbrella for the thousandth time and with so many other enemies looking very similar, you just want something new. The bosses look cool and not *all* of the enemies are exactly the same, but it's not enough to overcome the general feeling that you're fighting the same few enemies over and over again. Complaints aside there are really good parts to the game. The controls are good and traversing the Shibuya area in Tokyo is fun, especially once you can latch onto Tengu (or summon your own). Combat plays well, even if it's not tremendously difficult. Your different combat options feel fun and meaningful whether you go around sniping people with a bow, sneaking up and stealth killing, or just going in to kill stuff with some spirit powers. As mentioned before, the game does look really good with lots of fun detail and animations. I did quite like the characters even if they're not tremendously deep and they don't have a big or interesting character arc. The voice acting (I played with Japanese voices) helped bring them to life rather well. When you put it all together, Ghostwire: Tokyo is a game that did some things right, but dropped the ball in plenty of other ways. It would be interesting to see a sequel that refines the game and brings out more of the enjoyable parts while removing a lot of the grinding and adding in a lot more enemy variety. I'd personally like to see a greater focus on the horror and less on the action, but that's not specifically an indictment of this game. Just a preference. Overall it's an above average game that is fun, but I can't recommend getting it at full price at all.
