_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo is a game about supernatural forces and a "boy" that gets possessed to save his sisterm unravel the truth behind the disappearance of the city and save Tokyo. The game isn't really anything else but that. From the things I do not like about the game and the things I did, I feel like Ghostwire: Tokyo has/had potential but squandered it on making the city feel as realistic as possible while ignoring the STORY, COMBAT and OPEN WORLD. Below I will state my opinions on this and what I liked about the game.EDIT: I REALLY wish I could give this a NEUTRAL response but sadly STEAM does not allow you to do that so I am forced to make it POSITIVE but it was a mixed bag of emotions for me so it should have been a NEUTRAL review.⚫OPEN WORLD #1: The open world is littered with "SOULS", MUSIC, YOKAI, PHONE LOGS, JIZO STATUES and more... why is this a bad thing you might ask? It just feels like a chore. You do not get rewarded by doing... ANY of it.⚫OPEN WORLD #2: The open world was pretty boring if anything and had little incentive to explore unless you want to collect all the souls... that was it. ⚫SOULS #1: There is no way to track the "SOULS", apart from the beads that can track them in 200m and to get 100% you have to MANUALLY run around and collect all 240k+ souls. This got stupidly tedious on top of doing the other collectables.⚫SOULS #2: As someone that is colourblind I had issues seeing the souls when I pressed TAB to do the little scan. Yes there are colourblind options but it did not change the colour of the scan. The cars, bins, streetlights, souls, enemies... all of it meshed together to create a frustrating game-play loop for me.⚫Animations/SOULS #3: A good amount of souls require you to do a HAND "minigame" to actually be able to pick them up. I felt so bored using these. Yeah you can get KK to do them but I still need to HOLD IN TAB. Then you have to use ANOTHER animation to pick up the souls and then ANOTHER animation to deposit the souls... all to get meaningless "MONEY" and "XP"? You can CAP out on XP WAAAAAAAY before you collect all the souls... which has more or less next to no use. (for me at least). They added in a new branch in your SKILL tree to speed this up... I wonder why.⚫The story was not very... memorable. It felt very forgettable once I finished it. I felt a sigh of relief once I had finished it.⚫The combat is VERY lacklustre. Boring. Repetitive. Probably some of the worst I have had to do in a long time.⚫The ending boss fight, or boss fights in general, are terrible. Forgettable. Easy. No challenge. Specially the ending boss.⚫I encountered 2 crashes, caused by Denuvo DRM (apparently), something about SNOW or something like that on the error log.⚫I got given "clothes"and masks as rewards from missions. I never get to see them if i am not in a cut-scene. What a useless reward in an FPS game like this⚫There was side missions in the game that BLEW me away. It was the school side missions where you had to put a stop to HANAKO-SAN. The creepy mannequin following you about... the kids in the hallway, the atmosphere... all of this is what I was craving coming to this game.⚫Side missions are what make this game good, in my opinion anyway. Some of them are just so heartwarming and almost bring a tear to your eye.⚫The details of Shibuya are astonishing. I felt like I was actually in the city. Exploring each and every corner, nook and cranny... it was just filled with detail. What an amount of love and passion was put into creating this gorgeous city.⚫The graphics are great and the aesthetics are on point at times.⚫The dynamic between KK and Akito as the story goes on was great to witness. The jokes, the quips and the fighting... man... that is what makes a character.⚫You can use an interactive map online to track all your collectables, that is what I done and I managed to find them all within 30 hours and achieve my 100%.⚫Plenty of content IN GAME to keep you busy for a long time, I presume, if you do not use an interactive map like me.After all is said and done, the game was terrible at the start. Combat was a joke and the performance was horrendous. Coming to it now, in 2023 onward, I finally got to play the game. They released a "COMBAT" update to try and make the combat better, did it? Oh hell yes it did. With how much detail they have put into the city and for how much content this game has to offer (NO DLC of course), this game is worth it, on sale. I would NOT recommend buying it for £50. I would LOVE to see what they do with the next "GHOSTWIRE: Tokyo" game. If they do it right, they can have a SERIES on their hands, imagine it... GHOSTWIRE: New York. GHOSTWIRE: Scotland. GHOSTWIRE: Russia. Just some examples of what they could do.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. I am not a person who really cares for how amazing a game looks but this was such a pretty game. You can just look at the screen shots to see what I mean but it really felt like a real world. The tiny details of the kanji symbols in the rain or being able to pet various shiba dogs and their eyes have the glow of the city lights reflecting on them was just cool to me. And you can't beat a game that lets you pet dogs AND cats (although the cats can be little jerks and refuse you!)Combat was fun for me, I know it can be "boring" to some but I enjoyed it. You can be stealthy or you can just go in elements a-blazing or just use your bow for some ranged combat. I mixed it up and had no problems with being bored!There were plenty of side quests, achievement hunting and ghost busting to keep me playing for over 60 hrs. I got my money's worth and now that I have unlocked all the beads, another play through will be in my future :)Overall, if you love Japanese mythology, urban legends, or want to visit the Shibuya district someday, then I think you would enjoy this game

_childDocuments_.review: I've always wanted to play this game since I last saw the release trailer for the PS5 (but didn't want to buy it due to the price...and it was also a PS5/4 exclusive for a while). Since I got the game at a decent (discounted) price, I decided to play it - and I wasn't that disappointed in the game at all. Here's my review.Scenery/Ambiance:I'm pretty much a giant ♥♥♥♥♥ when It comes to games with a creepy/eerie ambiance (not cause its scary, but cause i'm very easily startled) and honestly, this game's ambiance at times can be quite scary. some parts have dark/moody lighting and some parts have melancholic lighting - if its moody, then its moody, but if its melancholic, its melancholic. Shibuya and some parts of Tokyo are very pretty to look at, but some parts are extremely creepy, making you look over your shoulders at times, hoping there isn't a ghost popping up near you. The scariest part for me would be just right before you fix the bike. i'd give the ambiance about an 8/10Graphically:The graphics are pretty nice, but there are some parts I absolutely despise, actually let me correct that, there's one thing I absolutely despised in this game (graphically). Its the rain...the rain looks like absolute dog ♥♥♥♥♥. I mean, the raindrops are absolutely massive; once it rains, it makes the game look clunky and you can't really see much. Besides that, the graphic is visually stunning, The magic looks amazing as-well (it's almost like a doctor strange simulator.I'd give the Graphics about a 7/10 (the rain ruins this score)Combat:The combat is REALLLLY fun for me, although I've heard some people talking about how it gets really repetitive. For me, personally, it wasn't too repetitive, mostly due to the fact that I was switching it up a lot (I assume the people writing about the repetitiveness of the combat are mostly just using wind-form) by choosing the perfect elements for each fight (and i was playing on the hardest mode): fire is good at penetration (when it comes to the umbrellas or staggering bosses) and water is good for a wide area when you're being surrounded; wind is just good in general for spamming at mobs (although I recommend leveling up the attack speed of the element). The bow is kind of lackluster, I don't really find myself using it too often, especially when you can just replenish mana by smacking mobs with you fists or aiming for perfect parries. Sadly, even though I enjoy the combat, there are definitely some improvements to be made, for example: having to replenish mana to fight is a little annoying, It makes it so that you don't really want to waste mana fighting small mobs all the time - its just not worth it; and a plethora of other improvements (not ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to talk about it)Combat would be about a 6/10 (some weapons are kind of useless)Enemy Variation:You could probably count the amount of enemy types on two hands (which isn't exactly a good thing), There's: Hanako, schoolkids (two variants, but the same thing), the rain doll, Ice ghost (which I've only seen once during my whole main story play-through), Fat boy, police man, skinny boy, female that shoots red coom at you, a child that you never fight, Scissor lady (kinda hot), oh yeah, and finally the generic white/grey cloth ghosts. The bosses don't count, you only fight them once anyways. The mobs aren't even that strong, even at the hardest game mode, some of them are just kinda tanky; extremely easy to just stay far away from them and spam.variation of enemies is about a 4/10Boss fights:The bosses are kinda lackluster, and weird. The bosses just pop up at weird points in the story, not really spread out properly (especially near the end, u just have a back to back boss fight). the only boss I found slightly difficult to fight was the spider ♥♥♥♥♥, cause she actually had a mechanic (in-some-way), but the rest of the bosses just require you to dodge; its like fighting the other mobs, just re-skinned (the wolf/fox boss doesn't count, all you do is pull its tail out, it's not really a fight)Boss fights I give about a 4/10 (hella boring, besides the spider)Story:The story is kinda of interesting? Idk, you're required to play the prequel if you want to understand some parts of the story a bit, or understand where KK comes from, and the prequel doesn't even look to interesting (and its super long), so most people won't bother playing the prequel. Some parts of the story is kind-of stupid; how and why is Mira (the MC's sister) chosen for selection to be sacrificed. Idk, the story is really boring at some points, its just running around and doing small things. Although, i'd have to say, I quite enjoyed the company of KK, but it is weird that KK and the MC got along really fast (since they were fighting for control in the beginning), I felt like they could have explored the idea of them slowly getting used to each other and building trust near the end, but they kinda just said "oh well, we good now"I'd give the story about a 5/10Artistic intention:This game is artistically beautiful, the game could almost get away with being called an art exhibit simulator. Some parts are gorgeous and a the game includes a-lot of imagery, for example the ending imagery with the flowers (red spider lily) wilting away, symbolizing death. Its gorgeous. This game is an art student's wet dream, that's all I can say. If you want to understand what I mean, then play the game.I'd give artistic intentions about a 9/10Equipment:Equipment is an L...Mid...Dog-water...whatever else adjectives I could use to describe it. Most equipment is useless. I haven't used the decoy or the bush talismans at all, there's no need. The stunning talisman is useless on bosses. the weakness is also useless on bosses; normal mobs are already weak enough, which doesn't incentivize the use of the weakness talisman. The bow, as I already said, is trash.not a lot of equipment, not a lot of useful ones, so its a 3/10.To sum it all up, the game is fun, but some polishing is needed. A final score of 5.75/10its good, just not worth paying full price. Would be more if the rain was decent.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR; Do not buy this game at full price, get it at half price.Now let's start with the good stuff.The setting is nice, the game looks good (mostly) and combat seems fine.The story is alright, I guess. Nothing special and nothing annoying. Which I don't mind at all if the game is more about gameplay.The graphics are all over the place. Some scenes look really good. While others broke any immersion that might have been there. As long as you move you're likely not gonna see much of the bad stuff. Stopping at the wrong place shows the not so nice parts. There are sometimes textures similiar to the door in Final Fantasy VII Remake (for those that do not know...it was PS1 bad). Alot of reused assets. Which for me wasn't that big of a deal since most of the rooms looked kinda like someone actually lived there. And sometimes the placement of objects could have been better.Still a solid look. With some more polish for some of the not so important locations it would be even nicer.Now to the bad part. Open World and Combat.This game should not have been Open World. It feels like a shallow copy of your typical UbiSoft OpenWorld. You have your "towers" (Tori gates), your useless collectibles (at least they contain some lore about japan), your useless loot (I was swiming in everything not too far in the game) and of course alot of mostly boring side quests. There was zero need to make this Open World.Now of course you can just ignore most of that stuff and just focus on the story. I did most of the side quests since I'm usually try to do all the content. All that took me about 19h. Now I did not go for all the collectibles.What really annoyed me was combat. You have your 3 "spells" which you can charge. You have a bow (which I hardly ever used outside of special missions). You can parry. And you kinda should do that. There is no dodge. That means you either block/parry or run. This did not feel good. You never really have mich ammo and I don't really know why. Since you pretty much always have an option to generate ammo wherever you have to fight. This felt kinda useless and awkward, Combat was too shallow and didn't really evolve much.It is sad that they didn't care more for the combat. This game has some really nice scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Great experience, the city is absolutely beautiful and a joy to explore, the amount of attention to detail is nuts and it provides for a very immersive Tokyo experience.At first I really liked what they were cooking, lots of unique elements which made it feel like something I haven't experienced before, after some time you start to get the gist of it, it stops offering new stuff to do resulting in your typical open-world style game with a funky combat system that gets pretty good after you've acquired some upgrades as you lack damage at the start.Side quests are barely worth mentioning aside from the high school horror questline which was great, every side quest is basically a fetch quest over and over again.Still one of the prettiest experiences I've had, it's worth playing alone from the visuals.It ran great, it's buttery smooth when you put it on windowed fullscreen, no crashes and just generally very polished.Recommended.

Action and exploration, but it's in the ward Shibuya in Tokyo so even the exploration isn't really all that fun; it's an urban landscape that just all blends together. It just doesn't feel like a complete, cohesive game. Now, maybe it gets better further in but, honestly, really disappointed I bought this. It's just a mediocre game, neither great nor bad, just average. The combat has nice visuals but it's very basic and there are way too many controls and keybinds. Good luck successfully rebinding actions though since you can only have 1 action per key even though the default keybinds double up on certain keys. I would honestly say this would maybe be worth $15, possibly up to $20 but absolutely no more than that. If they want this to become a series, their next game better understand what it wants to be from the beginning and dive further in to the horror aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to rate. I can't say I wouldn't recommend it, because there are definitely people I would recommend it to, but I wasn't one of those people. To summarize it, it feels like Ghostwire Tokyo was an alright linear game and then someone up top said "let's make this an open world exploration game with side quests because the run time isn't long enough". ----The Pros: The world design is generally nice, and there are for sure some spots where they do fun stuff with the visuals and setting. The monster design is good, the detail on random objects (such as in a store) are good, the sound design is spot on, and the story is alright. ----The Cons: It keeps going. I'm fine with repetitive games but something about the core loop of Ghostwire Tokyo just got old and stale HARD after doing a few side quests. It's a game where you level, but by the end of the game you are fighting the same monsters and they are taking about as long as they ever did to beat up, which becomes WAY TOO LONG after enough encounters. It's a game that feels like it should be a horror experience.... and it isn't really? That's not a hard negative but it's something to note. The enemy designs are good... but there really aren't that many of them? I'd say there are like, 5 categories of enemies you will see over, and over, and over again which is such a waste because when you get a new enemy they are always really well done designs! The game seems to stumble over itself a lot where it will have a neat idea but the execution is just the most lame version of it or it gets overused to the point where it is rote. There is a neat moment where you are largely powerless and need to sneak behind a well designed spooky enemy to take their tails off to weaken it. Good concept! But actually doing it doesn't reward carefully sneaking up on the creature, it just really rewards cheaply hiding in a hole and popping out right after it passes you. If you TRY to do it the fun way and take too long, KK will constantly remind you what you are supposed to be doing, as if you've forgotten the task you've already done 2/3 times. ----All in all, the game is a collectathon at heart and if you LIKE that, YOU are the person I would recommend this game to. There are so many spirits to find, statues to find, objects to find, Yokai to find, etc. If you want substantial rewards from each item you find though, go somewhere else. I feel like if you just blitz the main story that's the way to go, and then do the side quests later if you are hankering for more.

Performance was solid, even tho I run an RTX 3090, i barely had any fps drops with everything maxed out + ray tracing (no dips below 60fps). Tried both controller aim and M&K and if you have to pick between them, for the love of god, stick with M&K.Overall an 8.5, worth full price if you're into japanese culture, repetitive activities and good story. maybe not worth full price if you want deep combat mechanics or complex open world design.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for a long time as you can see. For those people who say the main story isn't that long, I don't understand what they are talking about. I am not going out and collecting every tiny thing, but I am doing side quests, and making sure my skills are (hopefully) enough to handle the end of the game.   This game has gone beyond my expectations, these people have done all the right things. The story is engaging, learning what is going on as you go through the whole thing, they aren't handing you all the answers at once.  The fights aren't that difficult, you can even avoid them if you want to and the map is extensive.  It's a nice mixtur of creepy, sci-fi and action with some cute and funny elements mixed in so it's not all doom and gloom.  I will say, as a player of horror games, I didn't find the game all that scary until the 4th chapter with this one specific side mission... not to give anything away... but to the Devs.... that was cruel and mean. It's been a while since a game has made me scream, let alone three times. _childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo is overall a really good game. The storyline for the main questline and side quests are extremely well done. The graphics and combat are great and beautiful. The world overall, quests, atmosphere, and vibe are absolutely gorgeous and amazing. The mythology of the Japanese yokai and the like are awesome, although they don't include a lot of them (such as the kitsune). The storyline is also very deep and sad at some points.The bad parts of the game is that there are SO many collectables. Between the jizo statues, the spirits, matagama, relics, voice recordings, investigation notes, AND tanukis. There are 240,000 spirits you have to collect to get them all, and to make it worse, the statues give you more ammo, the spirits give you a ton of experience and money (killing enemies is pretty bad for xp), matagamas are needed to upgrade your abilities in the skill tree, and voice recordings / investigation notes give you skill points. Because of this, collecting these things are almost necessary. You don't NEED to collect all of them, but unless you want to be extremely weak by the end of the game, you need to collect enough to be able to upgrade your abilities, etc. The actual storyline / side quests is pretty short at that. Most of the game is spent collecting things.... I don't think it's worth the 60$ price tag AT ALL. Definitely something to get on a sale though. It's worth playing and beautiful and the storyline is great, but not enough to pay 60$ for such a short game.Pros:Great graphicsGood combatGreat storylineGood atmosphereNice side questsJapanese yokaiCons:Jumping is atrociousWay too many 'collectables'Price for game is too high for what's givenToo many situations with flashing lights, explosions, etc.TLDR; The actual storyline / side quests is pretty short at that. Most of the game is spent collecting things.... I don't think it's worth the 60$ price tag AT ALL. Definitely something to get on a sale though. It's worth playing and beautiful and the storyline is great, but not enough to pay 60$ for such a short game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire: Tokyo is delightfully strange and oozing with style. It's a stunningly beautiful world to be immersed in. I admittedly don't know much about the Japanese folklore and urban legends that this game is based around, but that constant sense of the unknown lurking around every corner hooked me right in. It's a much more "chill" game than the Evil Within series, but you can always turn up the difficulty if you want a challenge (there are four difficulties total). It's pretty clear that they wanted everyone to be able to get through the whole game this time around. Stealth sections are rare and forgiving enough, and resources are everywhere.The open world is a bit Ubisoft-esque - cleanse Torii gates to unlock more of the map, collect a bunch of stuff, level up, build out your skill tree, rinse, repeat. While I agree with some critics that the gameplay loop gets a bit repetitive, you constantly feel like you're propelling the story forward, and there's some really great set pieces and sections where the world is literally morphing around you with unsettling imagery. The main story missions will give you the tools you need to get through the game, so you won't necessarily need to grind the sidequests and collectibles to progress.It's essentially an FPS, but using magic instead of guns. It feels oddly like a modern spiritual successor to the Heretics and Hexens of the past, while throwing in their own take on Doom 2016's glory kills for good measure. It's not a particularly difficult game, and in turn it can make the enemies seem like less of a threat overall, but it still manages to make me feel uneasy when I turn a corner and see a group of them waiting for me. Bethesda continues to be one of the few publishers to encourage creativity and innovation through their new IPs. Tango delivers a breath of fresh air in a world of games that are sequelized to death.Edit: The main story isn't really fulfilling, but it's fine and you'll get your moneys worth on sale. I've gone back to work my way through the sidequests and they're actually pretty great. I'd recommend at least giving them a fair shot. A lot of them are similar in how they play out, but the little stories are pretty good. There's some truly heartbreaking and messed up scenarios.I like that these sidequests really lean into you being a paranormal investigator and helping spirits move on by solving their problems. Makes me think this game may have worked out a bit better as a Phoenix Wright-like paranormal detective game. Some of these sidequests even have similarly interesting and spooooky set pieces as the main game. It's worth some extra grind after you finish the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game that plays a lot like Cyberpunk. Surprisingly weird-in-a-good-way typically Japanese storyline - something you would never expect from a Bethesda game. Ignore the "soulslike" tag. This is not a game where you die over and over just to be annoying. And seems to have been given this tag simply because it has "souls" in it. It's a graded (through areas initially being blocked off by a ghost fog that will kill you if you wander into it for more than a few seconds before hitting the cleansing points) open world where you run around unlocking new areas by cleansing shrines and increasing your powers through side quests using a "Rockstar Radar" approach. Whilst opponents are very varied and the ways of dealing with them also become varied the more you progress and level up it isn't anywhere near as customisable AS cyberpunk in terms of available approach and some might find it a bit repetitive or grindy for this reason. Personally I'm having a lot of fun with it and I find the bizarre story quite refreshing. It's certainly worth dipping into.

_childDocuments_.review: Far Cry and Control had a Japanese kid. I'm addicted to this game, but I understand that is not for everyone. Buy it only of you have high tolerance to repetition, as it repeat the Far Cry formula to the bone. Combat is simple but effective. Basically, you have a semi auto rifle (wind), a shotgun (water), a grenade launcher (fire) and a sniper rifle (a bow). I like the progression system, as every skill leveled up feels substantial. The setting is great, Tokyo looks outstanding at night, but I wish there was more variations, as a day/night cycle and different weather conditions. First person camera works well, but a 3rd person camera to see the different outfits would have been great. It's a very formulaic game, but what it does, it does quite well. A plus for being a extremely polished game. Didn't encountered not even a glitch in 20 hours. It also has no online features (a plus for me) and no MTX. It's pure single player. I know it's blasphemy for many, but I recommend playing with a controller, as the rumble adds a lot to the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start this review by saying that I enjoyed this game, I just can't recommend it for one huge reason. That reason being, the combat is terrible. The combat really just boils down to left click spamming enemies and then holding right click. There's very little actual strategy involved, it really is just "shoot enemies until they die." There's no weak point system, there's no elemental damage (Despite the fact that your attacks are elements), there's a perfect block mechanic that I used a grand total of one time because it's risky and barely useful at all. The only thing that somewhat saves the combat is the stun talismans, which open up most enemies to where you can instakill them (Which can be very useful on some of the spongey enemies). The exploration and world is what really made me enjoy this game, and the side quests were actually pretty well written and fun, but the combat plays such a large role in this game that it is hard to overlook. So as much as I enjoyed this game, I really can't recommend it unless you're willing to overlook the combat and play the game for its exploration and story.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a lovely game and I regret not getting it sooner. The reason that I didn't is that I heard some things about it which put me off, but having played the game myself I feel they were a bit misleading so I thought I'd adress them too.Repetitive gameplay - Yes, but in the same sense that Assassin's Creed has repetitive gameplay. You go through the same motions in different settings. I enjoy this type of gameplay.Empty world - Yes, in the sense that it feels abandoned by humans. It's not devoid of life. There's the eerie feeling of everyone just having up and left, like dishes of food still set out on a table, but there's nobody there to eat it. The world is still vibrant, with sound and clutter. There's other living things, even though humans are largely missing. This also builds a certain tension whenever you see a human form, because they're not supposed to be there. I think it sets the stage very well for the story experience.No quests - There is a big story arc, but a lot of the other content is entirely optional. That is true. For a completionist with a sandbox mindset it's great. I realise this is not for everyone, but it's absolutely my jam and I'm having a lot of fun with all the side activities.Not english - I thought voice lines in japanese would be more of a hurdle than it really was. It actually helps with the immersive feel of the game to me. It seems more natural in this Tokyo setting than if they'd been speaking english. The voice acting is good, it's the same feeling as watching a really good anime. Not knowing the language isn't a problem, it adds to the flavour.So I get that this game won't be everyone's cup of tea, but some of the things reported as negatives might be a roundabout positive to someone else. I've not experienced any lag, bugs or glitches, despite running the game on a potato, which in and of itself is refreshing. Just smooth and immersive gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a damn tour of Shibuya, Tokyo, Japan at this point. Also, remember this was supposed to be Evil Within 3 before they changed it.Also note, that this is an open-world game! That means there are collectibles galore. Honestly, I have never found this to be a problem. Apparently, some people do. Now a solution to this is, just to ignore it... It's pretty easy to do. The prizes aren't really game-changing.The graphics are the greatest strength of this game. The atmosphere/visuals are very evil within and they look beautiful. The devs made nighttime Shibuya really stand out.The character design looks really good. All the visitors (enemy AI) all have some type of backstory that fits their style of appearances such as an exhausted salaryman, a greeter that is tired of putting on a fake smile all day, and the typical kid that's been abused throughout their whole life and will summon other enemies to protect them (Kind of like a screamer that attracts zombies in Left 4 Dead). Though throughout the game, you will most likely be fighting the same 3 or 4 enemies.Storywise, it's pretty simple honestly. The main character, Akito, gets into an accident, gets possessed, whole town turns into spirits and Akito must save everyone including his sister, Mari. I would go deeper, but I ain't spoiling. It gets pretty emotional is all I can say.Now of course the main downside was the combat. There is stealth and not stealth combat... Though to utilize the stealth more, I really needed to use a skill that makes you move while crouching faster because by the time you sneak up to anybody, they somehow use their "back at the head" eyes, and you get ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Good job Akito for damn near crawling to the enemies instead. *clapping* (End of rant). At first, I thought this whole using Naruto psychic hand ability is an interesting and fresh idea. It was for the first few hours. As you get stronger and get more hand weapons, I only found it necessary to use just one hand ability, but that's just me and maybe that's why the combat got pretty repetitive. Still, I got my enjoyment out of it.As you explore around Shibuya, you might see where devs forgot to add stairs such as this,But, just some minor thing that's understandable.There is character customization, though it's just cosmetics. You cannot change gender or alter your appearance of Akito.As for the price, I paid $30 for this game. I would either pay around the range of $35 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: After 20 hours straight I can say I'm addicted to this game, but I can also say I wont get through a second playthrough right after im done with it and yes, I'm already saying that without being done once. The reason I am addicted to this game is its setting and the Tokyo map., both are something new to me. It's so much fun to learn all the new things about the gameplay, the story and everything else and it's a lot of fun to explore this city which is really like a real city after you clear the fog. Talking about this harmful fog, I first thought that this game is about running through narrow streets surrounded by this fog that will never go away. I was so wrong, you clear almost everything off it and then you can explore most parts of the city. I've never seen so much verticality in exploration in a game. Until I played the this game I thought The Division 2 has the most complex modern city map, but this one tops it in my opinion, at least wehne it comes to the fun of exploring it. But at least I think there is a downside for some players as well. Because this map has so many things to collect, at some point I said to myself: “This is going to take your whole life.” Of course, this is complete nonsense, I think after 20-50 hours you should be done with everything. But yeah, that's going to be a lot of clicking activations, collecting, climbing, and so much more than any other game I've played before. It's like walking 5 meters and you can collect 5 different things and after another 5 meters you get another 5 different things, that's crazy. I mean, you don't have to collect or activate everything, but if you're a completer like me with Fomo in exploration, it can be daunting and really annoying at first.That's why I say: after finishing this game I'll let it rest for a long time before doing another run, that's for sure ;-)Still, I think this game is absolutely worth checking out. You should try it for at least two hours and don't forget, the longer you play, the more this fog will clear. This introductory/tutorial sequence doesn't reflect the late game very well in my opinion. To be honest, I had a completely different impression of the game at first, so please keep that in mind ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: First person shooter with a supernatural storyline and a Tokyo setting (but you guessed the latter already from the game's title, didn't you?). While the combat mechanics are not exceptionally thrilling for my taste, the atmosphere, story and abundance of references to Japanese pop culture and tradition more than make up for that in my case. With lots of items to collect, it's easy to lose the track of time while exploring the city looking for something: this is actually pretty relaxing, but probably boring for anyone looking for more action.Taking the time to complete secondary missions and look for collectibles considerably lengthens the duration of the game, but it looks like a fairly quick game if you just go straight through the main storyline. From the technical point of view, the game (as originally released) ran smoothly on an i7-6700K and GTX1080 @1920x1080 with high settings. Loading times on a mechanical HDD are acceptable with a perceptible delay only when loading a savegame on start up.Completionists and anyone with a love for Japan will be more pleased with this title that those players looking just for the adrenaline rush of combat.UPDATE: by the time I completed the game, I warmed up to the combat mechanics, thanks to unlocking more powers/talismans that give a wider range of options to fight Visitors. I thoroughly enjoyed the game and my only (minor) complaint is that it was not really straightforward that the "save 100% of souls" achievement requires completing a number of encounters with the "Hyakki Yako".UPDATE POST SPIDER'S THREAD DLC: Loved the content introduced with the Spider's Thread DLC, the amount of stuff added with a free DLC is quite remarkable. The new area/quest for the main campaign was fun to explore/play, the further enemies add some variety, while the Spider's Thread mode - with its roguelite gameplay - gives some longevity to the game. All in all, 50+ hours went into playing the DLC content, most of those in ST mode (finding all the lost cats and beating ST without taking a single hit took a while). The only downside of the update was the introduction of Denuvo, but I like the game too much and decided to make an exception to my "no games with Denuvo" rule. Can't say whether Denuvo had any real performance impact, since in the meantime I have upgraded my hardware and that might be covering any effect of Denuvo on performance.

_childDocuments_.review: I slept on writing a review for the game, but I think this is my new favorite comfort game. It's not particularly frightening, but that's not the point; there's a wonderful amount of detail in the setting for you to explore, and while the quests aren't especially challenging, this is open world done right. Meeting and engaging with the variety of animals throughout and finding/recognizing new tidbits of folklore is rewarding in and of itself, something you won't find in any other game of this kind. I really enjoy the RPG elements as well; although nothing revolutionary, they add layers of strategy to combat that incentivize the various systems in place for leveling up and enhancing elements for new playstyles. The narrative works well as a motivator for exploration, but the additional justification in the form of world building is excellent. This is a game that has substance in the whole of its design rather than what wheels it chooses to reinvent, so I would absolutely suggest giving it a try. The setting and artistry alone make it worth the time, but its heart and enjoyable experience make it one of my new favorites of the past few years.

_childDocuments_.review: I pretty much completed everything the game had to offer. It took me about 35 hours to collect more than half of the Spirits, do most of the side quests except 1 or 2, complete the main story, and grind a frick-ton. Since I don't play many open world games, it was a blast to really get immersed in the environments & just take it all in. The graphics are absolutely stunning, with excellent Ray-Tracing implementation, effects, models, and a great art direction to boot. The various spirits, hostile & friendly, all have fantastic designs. Not to mention, the cats & dogs that roam the streets are the best. I mean you can literally read their thoughts and give them head rubs, it's the dream.   Now moving onto the gameplay, It has it's highs & lows. Exploration is fun and satisfying, but combat can get really bland and annoying at times. It's pretty basic, only having 3 types of powers, and a few items like a stun, and debuff to enemies. The rest of your loadout is used for stealth, consisting of a magically enhanced bow, an auditory distraction, and cover to block enemies vision. There are also multiple skills, and buffs you can acquire. It's basic, but with the sound & visual design, you feel like a bad-ass when you pull it off.   The story is really good, with a great cast of characters, that are well fleshed out. Pretty much everyone except the main antagonist, has a great amount of depth, and charm to them. Sadly the antagonist falls flat, having a very generic super-villain personality, and not having much screen-time. He just wasn't as fleshed out as the other characters, and was just forgettable. Though his design is extremely cool, as for all the other characters & creatures. Except for him, Ghostwire Tokyo has a very strong, and very touching story, that must have had a lot of love and care put into it.  Most of the side quests were surprisingly good. All having touching stories, and a lot of care put into them. While some were better than others, the ones that hit, hit hard! Like, some of these stories were equally as touching as the main plot.    This whole world that was created was just filled with personality and life! A lot of other open world games can feel lifeless, but Ghostwire Tokyo isn't one of them. Overall I'd highly recommend this game! It's a solid 7.5 out of ten, flawed, but fun.

_childDocuments_.review: In my 46 hours of gameplay at Hard I've collected 90% of the spirits all but 1 Tanuki and 1 jizo statue and all the Nekomata relics and side missions in addition to beating the game. I mention this because much of the game is a tedious scavenger hunt. Cutting this out would mean the side missions and main story would only take about 15 hours if not less. Unfortunately, these scavenger items end up playing a role in building out your skills and while you could skip them it would put you at a disadvantage at harder levels. Each time you enter a new area or collect a relic you get a bit of Japanese history which is interesting but also a bit distracting from the ongoing narrative. Though the map may be laid out similar to Tokyo outside a few specific areas generic assets are reused over and over. This results in seeing the exact same layouts of various features like parking lots and gas stations and stores. Despite the map being rather large this makes it feel very repetitive. Overall a lot of the game feels really padded out. It can still be enjoyable but I would have rather had a short, leaned down version that focused more on the story and possibly even had a smaller, but more detailed and less repetitive map. Combat is ok, but often feels clunky to me. Playing at Hard never really felt Hard it was more about getting stuck in the sometimes cluttered environments that was more of a risk than the enemies usually. Graphically the character models look very good, but you mostly only see them in cutscenes. The city looks good also but doesn't have that next gen depth to it. However, the game runs very well on a 1080 Ti at 1440p at max settings. I only encountered one bug where the screen stayed red after damage but only until I cycled a menu. There are roughly 5 main characters, though you never see one of them and your interaction with other characters, outside of enemies, occurs almost solely in cutscenes. You trigger some missions by talking to ethereal spirits but otherwise thats it.  So is this an $80 game? Definitely not. Absolutely not. I don't want to undermine the hard work that game developers do but compared to many other works out there that are priced lower but still new, 80$ for the Deluxe version and $60 for the normal just seems quite high. This is a mid level game that if you ignore the tedious scavenger aspect you will burn through in well under 20 hours or less with no replayability options.  TIPSBow is the strongest single enemy weapon in the game. Though there are enemies that it will bounce off of and others that will charge you making it less efficient. When searching for relics listen to the sound, when you do the ghost whisper they make a funny little sound when you discover them and then they add a yellow pawn type symbol to the map. I ended the game with over $1 Million meica so don't worry about spending it on Nekomata emotes and clothes or even the seemingly expensive detective notes. I bought everything and still ended up over a million. Donate at the temples and they can mark Tanuki, jizo statues, and other items on your map for you. The Tengu summon skill is expensive but can really speed up navigation, especially if you want to collect spirits. However, it doesn't work very well. You'll often find you can't get a Tengu to summon in many places.

_childDocuments_.review: Well it lets you run around Tokyo (Shibuya specifically) without all the people. However there's a dangerous fog blocking your path. So much for the Japan travelogue you were hoping for. Despite being a safe country, Japan does have a creepy vibe to it in places - especially at night time - so this game is unique in the fact that it brings it to the fore.Getting around a reasonably accurate Tokyo is also disorientating - just like the actual place itself! I lived near Shibuya for a good number of years so it was fun to revisit some of the well known landmarks.The game works better as an exploration game where you can find lots of things to loot and collect, plus plenty of ghostly weirdness and Japanese yokai lore to keep it from being too boring. If you like hunting for secrets then this is your game. If not then understand that this is the main focus.The combat is not much of a challenge and it's quite easy, if repetitive. I didn't really find it too challenging. In fact you start out pretty underpowered, and it only gets fun later on. Problem is, you may not persist with the game long enough to get to the more enjoyable bits - so this one is a slow burner. Again, "Ghostwire: Tokyo" is more of a collect-a-thon than an FPS.As an experience you can sort of chill out to without feeling too stressed out - it's not too bad. It's just not particularly great in my opinion. Has more missed opportunities than Japan's lost decade.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy the aesthetic of Tokyo or Japanese folklore, you won't be disappointed by this game. It's gorgeous, and you can feel the love put into crafting every location and environment. This is the first game I have ever completed with 100% achievements. I loved it.The gameplay and story started slowly at first, but the environment was enough to lure me into continuing. And I am very glad I did; the game designers were . It is an open world game, but it doesn't overwhelm you with every possibility at the start but perfectly reveals more of the map at the right moments, until you are let loose to expand the terrain and explore for yourself. I never felt limited in my experience nor confused about how to progress.  to advance the main story, and as you clear the map, a few side quests pop up for you to complete. . Everything looks so fantastic and colorful, and very engaging. Let's be honest: this IS the game's selling point - the reason you're here - but they really knock it out of the park. I truly felt like I was in Shibuya, in Tokyo, and was very immersed. , and I never once felt like a location or environment was stale or that assets were reused. Every pocket of the city feels like a different place.Of course, anything so great can dull with over-exposure.  to frequently break you out of the loop it crafts for you. Many of the story quests and side quests utilize the ether-based nature of the overall story  which are totally different from the city environment you find yourself in most of the game.As you progress through the quests and explore,  of Japan. Due to the nature of the game, you will find yourself passing through some areas a few times, so you have multiple chances to pick up any relics along the way. It doesn't feel like a total collect-a-thon. Every new Yokai you catch and relic you pick up is interesting and tells you about some Japanese folklore, which I though was very cool.The gameplay really begins to open up after you gain additional attack abilities. At first, it did feel somewhat slow, but once you get a few additional abilities, there's more ways to handle enemy encounters. Again, like the map and the environments, the game grants additional abilities to you at just the right pace, once you get started. , and personally I prefer this as the combat is engaging and interesting but not overburdening to detract from the game's shining points, namely, the environments and world-building. . The schoolgirls act giddy and sporadic, never stopping in one place for too long. The big guys with the red heads notice you faster and are more tanky. The game scales the difficulty properly with the player, never being oppressive nor boring. I can see how some could say the combat can become a bit repetitive, but in my opinion, the question needs to be asked of how complex it needs to be to be engaging, and I think they firmly hit this mark without overburdening the player. The story was well crafted, clear and involved enough to hold my interest the entire time. The voice acting is great, and the characters felt alive. No characters feel confusing or under-developed. . Some of the cutscenes were just straight bad***. I probably took way too many screenshots.This is one of my favorite games now, and if any points resonate with you, I really think you should give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An interesting and fun idea with several flaws. Stylized, but not for everybody. Overall enjoyable but not worth full price.Steam can use this review as more data to support adding a middle thumbs button to their review system. I have very conflicting feelings about this game. I feel that I had a genuinely fun time playing the game, but struggled to enjoy a lot of aspects that would have really would have given it a *wow* factor for me. The world was decently done and very atmospheric, but I would hardly call this horror. Honestly nothing about this game was scary. The visuals were satisfying and at times unique and impressive. The combat is unique yet simplistic, but I can see how some players wouldn't care for it.The unfortunate major downsides of Ghostwire: Tokyo lie in the writing and repetitiveness. Throughout, I felt that the story was unclear and confusing. The English voice acting is absolutely horrendous but I personally had to deal with it because I found it difficult to play the game and focus on subtitles when keeping the audio in Japanese. The writing and characterization was bizarre and disorganized. Some of the deeper themes of the story felt like awkward and poorly placed "life lessons." The game does get repetitive and towards the end became mildly tedious. Some side content felt lazily tacked on. There are also a lot of unnecessary features in the game (e.g. photo mode and outfit customization). This being said, the game stays just over the line of being a fun experience.I don't think I could ever recommend that someone pick this game up at full price. It does not live up to the $60 price tag. All in all, Ghostwire: Tokyo is a great idea that could have been done better in many many ways, but still offers fun gameplay that is worth a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game pretty much feels like a typical Ubisoft game with tons of (mostly pointless) collectibles scattered throughout the game world, but without any non-enemy NPCs, so it gets quite lonely. The first three or four hours of the game are quite interesting, because the game continuously introduces new enemies, attacks and demon-related side quest. However, the (in my case) remaining 25 hours are just really repetitive and grow continously boring. You only have three types of attack (wind, water, fire) as well as a bow throughout the whole game, so you barely feel any progress during the remainder of the game. Also, the game introduces prettty much all enemy types throughout the first three or four hours and most of the basic enemies have pretty much the same attacks, so the fighting gets very repetitive, however, there are also a few bosses (around 5?) in the game, which are actually quite cool. The game also contains a skill system, however, in my opinion pretty much the only skills worth investing are the attack skills. There is also some currency in the game that enables you to buy items (mostly food) in various stores led by hovering cats, but I don't remember buying anything throughout the final 25 hours of my playthrough, because the game world is stuffed full of food lying around, so I had millions of unspent Yen (or whatever the currency in the game is called) at the end.Unfortunately, I have to say that I didn't really like the story, which is apparently meant to be the core of this game: Akito tries to save this sister who has been kidnapped by some occult maniac to use her for some ritual, but the game failed completely to build up any empathy for the girl -- even up to the final minutes of the game I did't really care what happens to her and I'm definitely not a psychopat. Moreover, the two main charakters Akito (the human) and KK (the ghost) are kind of annoying: KK tries really hard play a "bad cop" character throughout the game, but he doesn't really bring the right feeling over, especially when he gets excited when Akito has leveled up, so I just stopped listening to his rambling after a short time.This is definitely not one of the worst games I have ever played, but I really don't think that it deserves a recommendation: it simply too empty or too shallow and the repitition of tasks in the last 75% of the game simply don't justify a thumbs up.Finally, I have to admit that Japanese lore is not really my thing, so I cannot judge whether any of that demon stuff is actually related to it, but if you're actually intro Japanese demon lore, then your might actually give it a try when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: -You can pet the cats and dogs-You can read the thoughts of the cats and dogs-You can give a nekomata a japanese lion mask for a quest, then he wears it!!!10/10In seriousness:If you're interested in Japanese culture, cuisine, architecture, etc. this is a very cool immersive experience in terms of touring some of Japan. Feels kind of like being immersed in an actually good live-action anime. (I know, that's not a real thing)Graphically it looks insane, and I'm managing 4k, low ray tracing, medium settings with dlss on with a 3070 and i7 10700F. It still looked amazing before I even turned RT on.Gameplay, it's an open world first person shooter with a supernatural coat of paint that feels pretty unique compared to some of the other games of a similar genre on offer out there.Just a warning: The tutorial of the game is rotund to put it mildly, and you'll be introduced to the world with a slooow burn over the course of a couple of hours. If long tutorials are a deal breaker, stay away.Otherwise this gets my seal of approval. I think it's an under-appreciated gem that got a bad rap, and unnecessary amount of hate when it first launched.Actual score so far: 8.5/1045+ Hour update:I've taken a few breaks from the game to prevent burnout, but I'm still going, and still having a blast every time I play. Also I feel I should add that I picked hard mode, and am very happy with the balance on it. I don't think i'd be quite as engaged if I had've picked something easier. The game has been enticing to 100%, or at least for the relics, since they're all educational tidbits about Japanese culture and history. I reiterate: if your'e into Japanese culture, this game is awesome. If you don't care about it, you might be disappointed with what's on offer. Updated score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire Tokyo is best summed up as Doctor Strange meets Japanese Folklore with a twist of FPS game in it, or John Constantine for that matter. That aside, the game is pretty plain with side quests and collectibles taking up more time than the main story. The story itself is fine, it isn't the greatest but it isn't the worst either. It might be tedious for some people as this game is pretty similar to Ubisoft, in a sense that your entire map will be polluted with collectibles and side quests. It is up to you whether to complete it or not but some area are a necessity to clear in order for you to progress the main story. Now the gameplay isn't bad, it just gets really dull and tedious after a few hours. There's basically no combo to be done, you either hold or spam your mouse for attacks. Besides that, you can also use sneak attack or talisman to supplement your fight to make it more interesting. It isn't ground breaking but it isn't bad either. It just works will be the best analogy to it. The controls for the game are also abit janky. For the record, I'm referring to the climbing part of the game which I think is really poor compare to the first Dying Light game. Sometimes the climbing animation is just skipped entirely, not sure what's the reason behind it but other than that it is fine.Now, I will give credit where credit's due. In terms of recreating Japanese Folklore, the boss and the monster actually felt quite a breath of fresh air instead of your typical NPC enemy. Yes there's slender man and there's weird student without head. But I'm not talking about those, I'm talking about the bosses you encounter throughout the story. I think their design is really nice and matches the tone of the game. Heck, even some of the side quests Yokai looks really inspiring. As for the character's voice actor, I believe they did a great job. I play the game in Japanese dub so it is quite a blast to have Kakashi talking to me but that is besides the point. Main point is, the did a great job. The OST is also good. It is another aspect that I will praise about the game. It supplement each quest perfectly, eerie but not too much.In conclusion, the game is alright. New concept with old style of gameplay. It works, but is it worth the asking price? That is for you to decide. I would highly suggest for a sale before picking up this game unless you really have to for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good action-adventure title from Tango and Bethesda! Some of them have cool backstories but others feel meaningless- Fairly short main story. If you solely focus on the main questline, you can easily beat the game in about 5-6 hours. For a $60 title, it seems a little too short.- Some bugs with movement. When gliding, the auto mantle system occasionally doesn't work properly. I can't count the amount of times I have fallen off a building due to my character not grabbing a ledge. Also trying to jump multiple times in succession sometimes doesn't register. A few enemies have ground AOE's you need to jump over and the buggy jumping has killed me a few times.- SPOILER: I would give the game a solid 7/10. Hoping for The Evil Within 3 next!

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostwire Tokyo was a love at first sight thing for me. Im a huge fan of Japanese folklore and I was excited by that alone. First the good. The graphics are nice and the particle effects light up the screen constantly. I love all of the different yokai and monster designs. Moving around Tokyo can be really fun once you upgrade your movement abilities. The story lags a little bit and I believe a good chunk of emotional investment is lost by not playing the prelude unfortunately but it does pay off in the end in my opinion. The not so good. The charm did sustain me for the first half but by the second half the flaws started to show through that charming sheen. Ghostwire Tokyo is a game that follows what modern western design has been doing for well over a decade now. Large worlds with way to much to do and collect with very little substance to any of it. Seeing new Yokai to interact with was cool until it was the same handful over and over again. Finding tanuki was cute the first few times. Absorbing souls started as a fun way of encouraging me to explore but quickly turned into a massive errand. Combat never evolved past block and shoot. Side quests can be interesting but they all amount to brief distractions sometimes they only amount to fighting a group of enemies that end up rewarding you with little more then exp and money.All in all I do recommend the game but if your not big into the subject matter or your currently burned out on open world gameplay design then maybe wait for a sale. Ghostwire Tokyo is a very charming game but its almost as if it lost its passion part way through.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free Review:Combat is very fun and eye candy though so far the enemies I have faced are very linear. I've set the game on Hard and it's honestly not as challenging for what I gathered. I only died once, enemies aren't very aggressive and playing zoner can be very cheesy. Parrying does rather feel satisfying to execute and rewarding, and I hope in a future patch they make the enemies abit more aggressive. I could be wrong, given that I'm only 4 hours into this game and so far I'm enjoying it myself.Map and visuals: Being set in Shibuya, honestly it's jaw dropping how pretty the game is, and it's honestly the open world game I look forward to see set in dense cities. I would say that this is on par with Ghost of Tsushima level of visual fidelity. I'm running on a RX 6600 and setting it to Low Raytracing with FSR 1.0 on in Ultra Quality is surprisingly playable, however even without Raytracing the game look stunningly beautiful that even if you turn of Raytracing I really wouldn't notice at all.Side Content: If you are expecting hard puzzle solving quest, then I suggest lowering your expectations because most quest that I've done are very handholding and cookie cutter, like most side quest is a spirit asking you to collect something inside a house, do some hand movement to break a seal and that's it. sometimes there are a few waves of enemies but that's it. Exploration: This game does have some parkour but it's janky but servicible at best. sometimes a I like to walk around streets, but these bird things that you can latch on to get on the roof quicker are obnoxious to listen when you just want to roam around. and you can't really shoot them or anything so you have to hear their annoying "RuaaaAA"RuaaaaAA"RuaaaaAA"Overall it's a very good game, not something that I would believe is a Game of the Year contender, but it's very decent.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, look, I finished the game; that means a lot, honestly, so pardon my following harsh comments.Ghostwire is the best bad example of telling other developers that you cannot rely on good scenery and graphics solely when making a game, and it does not compensate for the lack of gameplay.I think the scenery is excellent; I would love to traverse Tokyo collecting all the collectibles for Neko yokai; the problem is the base combat system is so bland and nasty every time I get into a fight; I want to quit the game. The upgrading system is fragile, you get some game-altering abilities, and that's it. No dodging improvement, no new combos, most of them are just stats increasing upgrades, so leveling up is not exciting.Enemies are very repetitive, there are only 4 base type enemies and others are reskins. Especially considering the massive yokai roster from Japanese folk lores. Enemies also respond weakly to your attacks, I originally expected to have real time damages but nop, they "shatter" randomly and not entirely based on the damage.Even if I enjoyed doing collectibles, I am still pissed that there are so few rewards from all the chores. The talismans are just stats boosters, and you get them pretty middle to late game. One Neko only rewards you three items for 12 items collected, clothes are only rewards and you can't buy them. The main story is really short, it basically has 4 chapters, 6 chapters in total but last 2 chapters were just weak boss fights. There are a lot to dive into, such as KK's team and the learning process of ghostwire martial arts, but not, just jumped straight in.Overall nothing else to say, very disappointing. Only recommend if you just want to play some games to kill time, but perhaps getting a game pass is the better option.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished the main story of Ghostwire: Tokyo the only way to describe the game comes in mind is a colossal disappointment.That being said, lets start with what the game gets right: Art and level designers have outdone themselves, from the authentic looking environment, interesting enemy designs to some visually outstanding set pieces. Likewise on the audio side you have some excellent work with various enemy and ambient sounds as well as the music.Unfortunately every other aspect of the game falls flat: Main story is not only paper thin but it is also pretty terrible in overall, it does not help that characters are bland and despite the games best efforts it is difficult to care about any of them.Combat is very basic: You furiously wag your elemental finger gun at the enemies shooting either wind, fire or water spells at them until your finger runs out of juice. At that point you either switch to your bow or go find some blinking objects in the environment that you can bash to replenish your finger juice. While the game features mechanics such as blocking and perfect blocking, various talismans and an "ultimate" ability you charge by using finishers on enemies - none of those had a place in the combat loop and were never really needed on the hard difficulty due to the poor enemy mechanics.Regular enemies can be divided to 3 categories melee, ranged and flying. While this may seem like a very broad strokes division, it is fairly accurate due to how barebones the combat is mechanically. You fight every enemy of a type in a same way - sure their models might be a little different or they might shoot 5 projectiles instead of 2, but does it really matter when you either walk backwards or strafe while shooting and avoid every single attack?Bosses in similar manner are fairly basic, either having a specific gimmick or weak points you need to shoot while avoiding 1 or 2 main mechanics (generally jump over something).Main bulk of the game is its open world structure which takes after the all too common Ubisoft open world formula. You liberate some outpos... I mean cleanse Torii gates which allows you to unlock new story and side missions, you despair at the amount of generic collectibles the map is littered with and then more than likely get bored and rush the main story.As might be apparent from the review, I really disliked the game and as such I very quickly decided to focus on rushing the main story. Out of my ~9 hours played, roughly 3 hours was spent doing side activities in the open world and 6 was the main story.All in all, I personally did not get much of enjoyment out of the game and definitely would not recommend it at the full price. For those wanting to jump in regardless - I would recommend waiting for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I saw Ghostwire: Tokyo I really thought this game was the survival horror Tango Gameworks were well-known for, but set in Japan. When I finally get my hands on it, well, let`s just say the experience is quite different than my initial thoughts. It is not a bad game. In fact, Ghostwire: Tokyo has, in my opinion, best open world design after Elden Ring and Witcher 3. The animation is smooth and satisfying to watch. And the core gameplay has that vibe of classic survival horror Shinji Mikami made in the past. Yet, lacking a defining theme and being too conservative are the two reason that put the game in an awkward situation. It is hard to say the game is bad, and it is also hard to say it is a must-play either.I am still amazed at the game's open world design. The level of detail is insane, an almost one to one rendition of Shibuya according to my sisiter. Simply taking a stoll down the street constantly fills me with wonder. No scenes has been copy-pasted blatantly. Every part of this city has its own special sense of style, which make exploration really great in Ghostwire: Tokyo. The experience only elevates with the ability Spectral Vision, a radar-like skill which highlights items and enemies around you. Pick a direction, drop the Spectral Vision, and go forth at your leisure. You would be surprised how much secrets you can uncover from  doing this. It also serves as a great reminder if the density of the city may be too overwhelming.Ghostwire: Tokyo does a great job at portraying the spiritual belief of east-asia, in the form of side quests. Classic yokai like Zashiki-warashi, Nekomata, and more make their appearances in game. Several side quests paint a clear vision of how obessesion can cause serious trouble to one`s mental and physical health state. And my favorite parts: the game`s rendition of urban legends. Two of them stand out the most. Kuchisake and Kisaragi Station are the highlight of my playthrough. Not only the atmosphere is horrifyingly superb, but also their presentation leave quite a impact, really making me wish this game is a full on horror.→Sound cue is really distinguished and well-done. →Hand gesture animation is smooth and satisfying to watch.→Using cats' thought as hint is a interesting idea.I always view upgrade system as evolution for the core gamplay, branching paths for players to customize their playstyle. So I am really disappointed to find out the upgrade system is rather conservative. It never goes beyond offering you minor convenience like faster casting, crouch-walking speed increase, etc. The spell upgrades just make you fire faster, wider, and bigger. It`s a shame because there are so many potentials the dev can put in, ideas like implementing elemental damage instead of just visual indicators, fusing two of the three spells to create either unique attacks, buffs or debuffs, or even something for Wired-in that can create a doppelganger mirroring the protagonist.Another main problem of Ghostwire: Tokyo is that it`s hard to pinpoint what the game is trying to be. My first impression of the game is "Evil Within-like sets in modern Japan", so I am really fixated on regarding this game as survival horror. Unfortunately, Ghostwire: Tokyo fails to meet both. Survival is never a problem considering the abundant resource scattering around the city. In fact it`s pretty hard to run out of resource in this game. The horror part, on the other hand, comes really close to great, if they can stretch it to the full game. Like I said before, the side quests involving urban legends have some of the best setup for horror. Horrifying atmosphere, terrifying yet mesmerizing visuals and a suitable difficulty. It pains me to see that the dev doesn`t bring that level of horror buildup to the whole game.→The later parts of the story feel rushed.→Boss fights are disappointingly easy despite their striking visuals.→Wish there are more yokai introduced.中文小簡評→一款有點難定義、推也不是、不推也不行的陰陽師模擬遊戲。→一比一還原澀谷區，以及我第二喜歡的開放世界設計。→支線充滿經典妖怪、都市傳說及靈異小說橋段。→各個音效簡潔有力且分明。→各種手勢動畫非常流暢。→讀貓狗的心思找線索是一個非常有趣的設定。→升級系統太過於保守，以至於玩法變化不大。→真心希望這遊戲可以往恐怖遊戲發展，很多支線設計得令人膽戰心驚，不解製作團隊為何不投入同樣心血在開放世界裡。→後半的故事感覺想匆匆了事。→Boss看起來很有威嚇力，打起來令人失望地簡單。→如果能看到更多妖怪或都市傳說就好了。

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, got all spirits, and needless to say I really enjoyed my time with this game. Here's Good/Bad breakdown:Good: - The open hub/open world they made is incredible. Really breathtaking just being in such a finely detailed model of Japan. Makes navigating the environment really good, and seeing as most of the game is a collect-a-thon, it does well in encouraging people to wander the world.- Movement and traversal after getting a few upgrades is very solid. Feels effortless to hop around, and a lot of options to fast-travel as well.- If you're a fan of ghost folklore, and especially that of Japan, this game has a lot to introduce you to. Stories that are told through Japan and their versions of ghosts most common in those stories. Yokai, Tengu, Yurei, Kappa, Oni, Kasa-Obake. It's cool to play through a game and learn more of japanese culture in the way they run through it.- Combat is very flashy, but gets shallow as the game progresses. More on combat's weaknesses in Bad.- Story & Dialogue. Story is engaging enough to bring me in, and dialogue between the main characters transforms very well as the game goes on. Felt like even after 15-20 hours of traversing the world and getting into fights, I was consistently running into new dialogue between main characters.- All of the Dreamlike and Haunting sequences are really fun to explore, though they are limited.- Music/Soundtrack- For being a collect-a-thon, the game presents a lot of helpful tools you can use to track most of the main things you'll be collecting.- Graphics/RaytracingBad:- Biggest issue is with rewarding the player for their efforts. A lot of what you can do will result in very little, and some upgrades you'll unlock are almost meaningless (Upgrading glide time from 2 seconds to 3 seconds). Sometimes the only reward is a steam achievement. If there is a sequel, they really need to address this.- Combat is not very deep. You will unlock abilities within the first couple of hours and they won't change very much. Some of the combat mechanics, such as losing your powers temporarily, are introduced and are rarely used.- You will most likely hit max level far earlier than you'd expect. I hit level 50 and went another 7-10 hours in the game without levelling up again.- Photo Mode doesn't pause gameplay. If you want to take a picture when enemies are present, you'll get knocked out of it. Occasionally this also crashes the game.- If you aren't into collect-a-thon's, the main story is rather short.- Small complaint: Critical dialogue during combat is an issue. I'm typically too focused on combat to read the subtitles.

_childDocuments_.review: "TAKE MY MONEY!" That's what I said after seeing the trailer. I have many experiences with a few games (not mentioning names), this is not. Elden Ring and Ghostwire Tokyo were released 1 month apart from each other, and because I live in Japan, Steam games are twice as expensive. I chose the latter without any hesitation, and my thought? My money is well-spent. With the amount of attention Elden Ring has, I feel like Ghostwire Tokyo is underrated. It is rare that any of the games I have pre-ordered, this is the only one game I am super proud of my own choice. Gameplay is fantastic, the environment is breathtaking, super realistic (because I live just outside of Shibuya, I go there every 2 weeks for work). This game pays extreme attention to details. 10 stars? How about a million stars? Storyline: captivating, and even though yes, there are grinding in this game but they are limited. You want a horror game that has action, adventure and super powers to fight those scary Yokais? This game covers it all. What are the chances of me running around Tokyo with NOBODY? Well, it is possible with this game. Of course games are games, you can't go around politically correcting people saying "This game has zero accuracy on the map!" of course not, duh! If you are thinking about running to Harajuku or Shinjuku in this map, perhaps you should stick to Google Map. _childDocuments_.review: Tokyo Ghostwire is a good game, if you really like Japanese culture. There are a few negatives in this game that I will need to address. First off the combat of this game is good. People really complain about it, because it is so simple. To their defense, it does get very repetitive. That is the problem with this game, repetitive game-play. When I started out in Tokyo Ghostwire, I was really enjoying the environment, story and even the combat. After a while you get very bored, This whole game is a grind fest. I got to chapter 5 of the story and there is a big block of text that states "make sure you are ready, there is no going back". I spent hours collecting statues, Tanuki, and worst of all SPIRITS. There are too many spirits to collect in this game. I am only at 70 percent spirits and I have spent hours collecting them. I am bored and tired of collecting and grinding in this game. I reached max level in the game, which is 50.  I didn't finish it yet, because I am an achievement hunter. One of the achievements is "collect all spirits before completing the story". This one achievement is making me bang my head against the wall. If you don't care about collecting and achievements, then this is a fantastic game. The lore of this game is amazing. Every collectible has back story. The side missions are very good and interesting, but they are just fetch quests essentially. Make sure you have a really good RIG to play this game, CPU is very demanding. All in all I do recommend this game, despite its flaws.
