_childDocuments_.review: I have never felt more conflicted about a game.On one hand this game has great presentation, story and some pretty fun open world activities.On the other hand the game is short, the combat is repetitive, and the other half of the open world activities are very grindy.The worst about all of it is the performance, played the game with an RTX 4080 and an i9 9900k and still I couldn't get above the 100 fps.Basically I wish I liked this game more than I did because I love japanese folklore and mythology. Sadly this great concept for a game hasn't been executed well. If they ever make a sequel I hope they make the combat more fun and maybe ditch the entire open world thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: It's not really a combat-heavy FPS / shooter type game, although there is periodic combat gameplay. The encounters are fairly spread out.While it is a spooky game, it's not really a terrifying horror game either. As far as spook levels go, you should expect something about on par with Alan Wake, maybe even a little bit below that. It's got a spooky atmosphere for sure, but it's not gonna make you sweat with dread. Not even close.A lot of the gameplay is frankly just exploring the eerie, abandoned, rain-slick streets of night-time Tokyo, where you appear to be the only human still in existence (everyone else vanished in a sort of "evil rapture" event). You help nice ghosts, you beat up evil ghosts, you feed dogs, you collect traditional japanese artifacts, and you hunt yokai. It's more of a slow, exploration-oriented experience than you might have envisioned. In a lot of ways, it's a high budget collect-a-thon.Only real complaint I have is that, as far as the platforming controls go, your character's feet feel a little bit too slippery/bouncy when it comes to platforming on the rooftops. The edge grab feels like it works somewhat inconsistently, and when you try to land on / climb onto certain edges or objects, you just slide or bounce right off, which sometimes throws you off the roof and leaves you searching for another way to get back up, which can be irritating. But it's a relatively minor annoyance overall.If you're looking for a primarily combat-centered experience, you ARE going to get bored. The combat is.... slow... and clumsy... and sluggish... and simplistic. Sometimes it's as deep as just standing in front of an enemy and the two of you slapping each other until one of you dies. The combat is PS4 flashy with N64 gameplay. In fact, the combat seems to sometimes be deliberately annoying. If you are locked onto an enemy (which locks you into aim assist if you're on controller) and repeatedly hitting them with blow after blow, the enemy will "stumble" to the left or right which---FOR SOME REASON---causes your lock-on to black, forcing you to miss and requiring you to move the cursor and relock. It seems to do this so that combat isn't too easy, but it mostly just feels a bit irritating to be honest.If you're looking for some absolutely terrifying horror, then this isn't gonna fulfill your masochistic needs. Some of the enemies have interesting or even creepy designs, but you'll see them copy/pasted so much that they lose all sense of spookiness at all after a while and are about as scary as a Skyrim goblin.I'll be frank with you that the gameplay is a little shallow. It's very exciting for the first ten hours or so, but by the time you're getting to the end of this game, you'll definitely find that there really aren't a lot of ideas going on. If you blast through the main story, the game will be over shockingly soon. If you're a completionist, you'll find that all you're really doing is engaging with excessive padding in the form of doo-dad collection.But hey: if you love japan, you love to explore open maps, you love to collect, you love spooky vibes but not crapping your pants with dread, and you enjoy sometimes occasionally getting into a fight, then you're gonna have an okay time. It may not be quite what you were expecting when you saw the trailers, but it's an interesting game in its own way. I'm not sure if I'd recommend buying it at a full $60---and I definitely wouldn't recommend buying it more than that---but for $40 or below I feel like it's pretty alright. If you're gonna get it, though, expect more of a "chill" game than an "intense" game.

_childDocuments_.review: Tango Gameworks is a really interesting and creative output . I really enjoyed the Evil Within series despite their numerous cons, and I think that their games are fun if sometimes a bit janky. Unfortunately, Ghostwire Tokyo has a lot of neat ideas that didn't quite come together for me. Tokyo and its Yokai residents are incredibly fun to look at, but slow movement, tedious combat, boring sidequests and a pretty bland plot didn't make it for me. The lore and atmosphere are incredible though, and there is a pretty cool game hidden in there if you just want to wander around a haunted Tokyo.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this alot - kinda feels like Dying Light with traditional/modern japanese culture. This aspect of culture was one of my favorite parts because it felt unique and original even though now there are plenty of games of this genre. Main story is a bit short for my liking but its filled with creativity and originality all the way through. side missions are fun and interesting though like collecting spirits, I'd never do them again. To me there really isnt any reason to play through it again despite it being an awesome initial run. The filler/repetitive tasks are samey and hardly worth doing more than once or twice. Overall great game for a 30 hour binge with its biggest weaknesses being no replayability and repetitive side content.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostwire: Tokyo

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the great visuals, Japanese culture, and depressingly wholesome story. I wish I took advantage of the camera more since the game is so beautiful and you get these clothes and emotes that are only useful for photos.Main story itself is way too short, but there's a lot to do if you go through the side quests and try to collect all the relics and spirits. It's not really challenging and the bosses are too easy, but I still enjoyed the combat style even when it gets a lil repetitive.

name: Godstrike
detailed_description: Godstrike is a 3D boss rush bullet hell where time is your health and currency. Face and defeat powerful bosses before time runs out. Taking damage and using abilities drains your remaining combat time, so watch out! SKILLS Unlock over 40 unique abilities by defeating bosses. Customize Talaal’s loadout before each battle to create powerful combos, ability synergies, and a playstyle that’s entirely your own! STORY In Godstrike you are the embodiment of Talaal, the last of God’s seven masks. Talaal finds her bearer just in time to fight against its siblings who hunt her in an attempt to absorb the power within the mask. The bearer is now trapped in a war that does not belong to her, a cycle that seems impossible to break. FEATURES Customizable ability loadouts, allowing the players to optimize their game style. Competition focused gameplay so you can challenge your friends and beat the highscores. Multiple game modes, including Roguelite-style mode! Twitch compatibility allowing viewers to affect the game, upgrading and refreshing the game experience. Full gamepad and controller support.

_childDocuments_.review: The game overall is pretty good, but I have one huge issue. And the huge issue is the balancing, Some boss phases are very easy but immediatly after that the difficulty gets cranked up 200% with patterns that are almost unmemorizable and projectiles that make the game feel more luck based than skill based. Another thing is that the abilities need reworking, Some of the abilities are overall weak and put you in more danger than you were previously. But congradulations to the devs, you guys did an excellent job with this game. Solid 6.5/10Edit: Having now beat the final boss i would like to change my rating, from a 6.5/10 to a 7.5/10this game blew me away in the second half, The bosses quailty improved and the game opened up more and i ended up really enjoying systems that i previously didn't like.All i have to say, is good job devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting concept, and definitely fun at points (Sentiel and Cindeal being standouts), but disappointingly poorly built. Here's a bunch of problems and generally weird things I ran across in no particular order:- Hit boxes are inconsistent at best and always favor the boss hitting you or avoiding your attacks- Your hitbox feels like it stretches further away from your perspective than it looks like it should- Hurt boxes regularly get sent out before animations start- Very few attacks are telegraphed- A lot of attacks change randomly and have a strange tendency to try to appear right on top of you or way out of your range if it spawns something- You have no invincibility frames, so you can easily lose most of your time from one attack if that attack persist (the final boss is very guilty of this, and the previous point)- The dash ability feels like it gives you i-frames inconsistently so you can throw yourself into damage pretty easily, and I'm not even sure if it does give you i-frames and I just slipped between attacks a lot- Your character blends into the background and has the same general shape as your protective abilities so it's very easy to lose track of where you're at if you're focusing on hitting shots- Honestly it's much easier to tell what's going on when the color scheme changes and the contrast heightens when you run out of time, there really should be a way to make the game always look like that instead of putting yourself into one shot rangeHopefully the dev team irons out these kinds of problems if they ever make a game like this one again. I could see it being a serious contender for games like Furi, but the execution on this game is really rough.
_childDocuments_.name: Godstrike

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love boss rush games I can not recommend Godstrike. It is not horrible, and some people might enjoy it, but it is very average in every aspect and there is nothing really to be hooked at. Enemy design is mediocre. Game is kinda like Fury but all bosses in Fury were unique and memorable, I still remember them all very well after almost 4 years of playing. As for Godstrike – I played it just recently and already forgot how many bosses were there. You fight a giant worm, giant beetle, giant robot… all the most generic stuff you could imagine. Visuals are so-so, music is pretty bad etc.Game is centered around an original mechanic that is your HP = timer, but while it sounds good in theory, in practice it gets annoying very soon, it is very common that you run out of time at the very end of the fight and lose because of that despite doing pretty good overall. It also makes it nearly impossible to play carefully and thoughtful, as I would like to. Either you rush or time runs out and you die.  What ruined the game completely for me is the final boss fight. His last form clearly was not tested as at least one of his attacks is all about RNG that is usually not in your favor and the only real way to beat him is some cheesy ability combos. Game also seems abandoned, it was not updated since launch, leaderboard seems to be broken and I don’t think devs even care about it anymore.Can’t recommend, unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Godstrike is a twinstick bullet hell bosh rush roguelite arena shooter by OverPowered Team. It was previously released on Steam as Profane but taken down. It has been updated and released under its new name. I was already following the game as Profane and keeping an eye on it. When there was a demo contest I jumped on the opportunity to win a free game key.It can be played with a dual stick controller but personally I think it's best played with the mouse either in combination with an one handed controller or with the keyboard. Using the mouse lets you simply put the reticle on your target allowing you to concentrate on dodging bullets. I prefer playing with a PS3 move navigation controller (in combination with a mouse), you could achieve the same with a Switch Joy Con or an analog joystick. Certain mouse drivers let you remap your buttons which is very useful for Godstrike. I've set up a mouse profile so I can map active abilities to the mouse buttons. You can use <m> to make the reticle show permanently. Alternatively you can use a draw tablet instead of the mouse.Time is your health, currency and your score. To beat each boss you're given a certain amount of time. You can use this time to spend on active abilities while passive abilities are free. You can choose up to four of each. When you get hit you lose time. When your time is up you can continue but any hit will finish you. In Arena Mode the time left after beating a boss goes onto the leaderboard.To activate an active ability you first have to collect souls the bosses release after being hit. The souls are collected for all actives at the same time. E.g. if you have two active that require resp. 4 and 5 souls, at 5 collected souls both are ready for use.Each boss has multiple stages with different attack modes. Some bosses can take quite some practice before you can defeat them.Story ModeThis might be the best mode to start the game with. Here you'll be told the background story and you get to battle all the bosses one by one in order of difficulty. You start with one active and one passive ability. You'll earn more by defeating bosses. After losing a battle you can retry as often as you'd like, however after a few attempts you can also choose to try to clear it on easy. Clearing a boss on easy will take you to the next one so if you want to beat all bosses on normal ignore the easy option.Arena ModeIn this mode you can choose which boss to battle with any of the abilities available in the game. This mode will let you earn scores for the leaderboards.Challenge ModeThis mode is procedurally generated and plays differently every time unless you chose the seed. Every time you play you get different abilities and different bosses to battle with different conditions. You only have to beat 5 bosses but once you lose a battle it's over. When you've lost you have to start over with a random seed or enter one.Daily ChallengeThis mode is the same as Challenge Mode but you only get one go a day and can't choose your seed.I think the game is great and I can recommend it if you like twinstick shooters and enjoy bullet hell. I play a lot of shmups with only bit of bullet hell and the occasional twin stick shooter, for me this game was pretty challenging but I can beat all the bosses on normal after enough tries. If you're new to these genres you might be in for a big challenge.Technically you could clear the Story Mode in 60-90mins if you're good enough but you can spend hours on each boss to get a good score on the leaderboard in Arena Mode. The Challenge Modes are really hard and might not be as much fun until you can clear all bosses on normal in one go. I'm not there yet :)At first it can be a bit unclear how to hit bosses but you just have to make sure to aim at the height of your bullets, usually the lower part of the boss.Since actives load at the same time it may be helpful to use combos e.g. Arcane Shield and Overload. Then if you activate both you can safely unleash spread fire up close.Recording of the demo run that won me a free Godstrike key:

_childDocuments_.review: I went back and forth thinking if Godstrike is recommendation worthy. This is a nieche title. The game is short and quite difficult. 	In short, Godstrike is a boss rush game leaning heavily into bullet hell territory. It offers some replayability with it's Challenge mode based around roguelike mechanics and daily challenges. The story is negligible. 	Unfortunately there are also some problems with camera work which might frustrate some players. Graphics and music are not impressive, but they don't have to be. This is an indie game. A title developed with a certain nieche in mind: People who like challenges and tough bossfights. In that narrow nieche it works really well. Fortunately for me, this is exactly what I was searching for. There are only 10 bosses but the encounters offer variety and challenge. For me that's enough.	This is a positive review as I really liked being tested by various bosses in Godstrike. For most players it's a skippable title, but for those few devoted bossfight enthusiasts it's a recommendation.If you are interested in a full video review, then check out my yt video:

_childDocuments_.review: This game consists of 10 boss fights, each lasting a few minutes.  Its design closely mirrors Furi; however, the game's primary focus is bullet hell + dual stick shooter.  Bosses are designed to be played multiple times and I won't get into the time = life mechanic, which is fine but doesn't necessarily increase enjoyment of the game.With some more development time, this game could've been polished into something really nice.  Unfortunately, with minimal patches since launch, we're left with some balance problems.  I beat half the bosses on my frist attempt and the other half required 1+ hours of practice.  I quite liked the overall challenge but the inconsistency of the fights was painful and bosses will superficially increase or decrease their aggression in the later half of battles, to the point where it feels like the devs are just trying to force a slog.And the hitboxes.  Oh the hitboxes.  They are oh so inconsistent.  Some monsters have hit boxes where their shadow is and others in the mid section.  Also, bullet speed is very slow by design requiring you to lead shots.  The combination of this plus the poor hit boxes almost made me put down the game at one point.I can only recommend this game to someone who is looking for a bullet hell challenge and willing to work through some slight mechanical issues.  It's definitely worth the price and a lot of polish went into it.  Hoping the dev will take another round at this formula for perhaps a more polished sequel.  Great idea for a game overall!

_childDocuments_.review: When checking out the trailer for Godstrike (GS), I was intrigued by a system where a timer would serve as my health bar. Boss fights can be the best part of a game, so I was all too happy to take on this challenge, and strike down the gods! That overconfidence may have been unfounded though.There are four game modes available in GS: Story, Arena, Daily Challenge, and Challenge. Story Mode doesn't have much of a story, as you don't even find out anything about each boss as you fight them, aside from their name. However, it gives a structured progression to playing GS, with each victory unlocking a passive skill, an active ability, and extending your time limit. Arena lets you fight against any boss, with any combination of the active and passive skills available in the game. The Daily Challenge is a random battle against one of the bosses with some condition in play. However, you only get one chance to beat it, so if you lose, you'll have to wait until tomorrow to try the next one. Challenge is somewhat similar, as it pits you against five boss fights, though you start each one with a clean start. Losing any of the fights means that you've failed to clear the mode though, and have to start over from the first fight.No matter which mode you try, the gameplay is the same for all of them. Before jumping into the fray, you're able to select from the skills you have unlocked. You can take four of either skill type, but passive skills cost nothing to equip or utilize. Active skills, on the other hand, both take away some of your time limit, and require you to pick up souls the boss drops in order to activate them. If you fail to beat the boss a few times in a row, you'll be able to switch to Easy Mode. The only thing this changes is how much time you lose when hit, cutting the amount in half, as the boss itself will behave the exact same.The developers suggest playing GS with a controller, which I was all too happy to do, especially since this is a twin stick shooter. Your projectiles have a limited reach, so you can't cower at the extreme edge from the boss. Depending on which skills you set, they can be activated with any of the four 'shoulder buttons,' based on how you assign them. If you use any of them often, it'd be prudent to keep them in a consistent place. Although there's an opening cutscene explaining the origins of the world, it really doesn't establish a clear foundation for what's going on. The long and short of it is an incredibly powerful being gave the world life, split into segments, which fought amongst themselves and were lost to time, and that was for the best anyways because it led to thousands of years of peace. Then some evil force pops in from places unknown, wrecks the entire continent, and leaves an island of people alone for a few centuries. When that place starts getting screwed with, a hopeless gal heads out for a solution, finds the long-forgotten herald... and you go into the tutorial.Admittedly, part of what caught my eye about GS was its aesthetic, as it reminded me of Furi's style. Each boss has a simple arena as a backdrop, there's some neon touches on their projectiles, and even the overhead perspective has a similar angle and distance. A recurring problem I noticed stems from the varying sizes of the arenas. The camera adjusts its perspective based on the character's relation to the boss, and what's occurring on screen, slightly zooming in and out to accommodate the action. This movement can be somewhat disorienting when trying to dodge everything on screen. Most of the time I wasn't listening to the music in the slightest, but when I paid attention, I noticed that it has a somewhat primal vibe to it. There's an emphasis on percussion, with sounds like drums and clangs making up the forefront of the track. It fits a combat tone well enough, and even seems fitting for some of the bosses you fight against. However, although each boss has its own music, I don't think they all paired up incredibly well, and they don't sound that different from one another. The sound effects seemed a good match for what was happening on screen, so I had no complaint there.  🌟 Conceptually, GS has a novel approach on a boss gauntlet format.🌟 Each boss fight feels unique.❌ The difficulty of the bosses seems to fluctuate significantly. I can't beat one of them even when attempting it on Easy Mode several times, while I have one-shot others. Similarly, how long it takes to dwindle their health bars seems very inconsistent, as I've seen a few melt away rapidly, while a couple of them seem to take forever to chip away at.❌ Some attacks lurch at you suddenly and too fast for you to avoid, particularly with how random the movements can be. I don't know a reliable way to dodge certain phases due to this matter.❌ There aren't nearly as many bosses to fight as I was expecting. Since the store page mentioned there were 40 skills, I expected a boss count close to that.🔍 Some of the phases seem to be hard-wired to follow a specific path, as long as you act similarly each attempt. For instance, on my many attempts at Garodal, I noticed that his 1st phase follows a very set route if you take an optimal approach to decimate his health.🔍 Getting your aim just right can be a nuisance at certain angles, so when possible, find places to easily maintain consecutive hits on the boss.Although I was intrigued by the idea behind GS, I don't think it works out well in practice. A timer on a boss fight can be an arbitrary way of making it more difficult, and if the balance isn't set well, it can ruin the experience. By getting rid of a traditional health bar and blending it with the timer, this forces players into a situation where they have to be mindful of how much damage they're doing to the boss throughout the fight. After all, if they're playing too defensively, the timer will deplete regardless of whether they take damage or not. For the bosses that gave me the most trouble, the difficulty stemmed primarily from how hard it was to consistently hit them with my attacks, as their hit boxes were smaller, and they were highly mobile. Not being able to hit the opponent, when they keep blasting you and exploiting your puny invincibility frames, makes for fights that aren't fun to engage in. Considering how much time I've spent trying to beat the same boss, and that all the game modes don't sufficiently change up the gameplay, I don't think GS has much to offer. At the very least, I can say for certain this isn't for casual players, but I don't recommend it overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Godstrike is the bullet-hell, twin stick shooter from The Overpowered Team, and Freedom Games. The player will face off against evil deities in order to lead the protagonist through the story and weed out the corruption that has poisoned the world.Talaal, the player-controlled hero, can be augmented with a huge variety of spells and passives. Abilities that create weapons that will automatically attack the boss the player is fighting, abilities that augment your natural shooting ability, ones that will defend the player and destroy projectiles. The sheer level of combinations that are possible between the abilities to choose from, combined with the passives to choose from, is mindbogglingly huge.  These are our MGN Impressions of the masked-god driven story that is Godstrike. Our experience with the game is based on the PC, Steam version, played with a control pad. As such, if you’re playing the switch version, or playing via steam with a keyboard and mouse, your experience might be different from ours.  The MGN Impressions are broken down into four different but equal parts: Story Sound Gameplay X-Factor The X-Factor for our impressions will change from game to game, and for Godstrike we’ve decided to go with accessibility. Will the game be accessible enough for players who are new to the genre, or aren’t fans of bullet-hell games in general? Want to find out? Stick with us, and you will.  Story 9/10The thorn in the paw of most bullet-hell games is that there is very little purpose to them beside from the base-level gameplay. You evade the boss, and you deal damage. You progress through, and that’s about it. Where Godstrike marks is difference from the other entries in the genre, is that it has a genuinely well-crafted story.  Without giving too much away I will say that the introductory cinematic gives enough purpose and interest to the player, that they are loathe to skip any later implications of lore. This is really good drawing point, not only are you here for the gameplay, or from your curiosity of what you’ve seen about Godstrike online – you’re given enough early to be invested in seeing it through.  Sound 7/10First off, let me just sound that the soundtrack fits the game so well. It’s harrowing and foreboding in places where it fits, and is exhilarating in moments where you expect to feel that rush. The lack of a 10/10 rating has absolutely nothing to do with the soundtrack. It’s of the highest quality and execution, and has made for excellent background noise whilst writing and recording this review. You can look it up on YouTube, give it a listen, even if you’re not a huge fan of listening to game soundtracks as background noise or as an experience in general, I highly recommend it.  What lets the sound department is the quality of that open cinematic. It’s incredibly well done, but the lack of an appropriate voice to match the text, is a let-down. My mind is immediately drawn to a voice like Galadriel, narrating the opening exposition. The addition of that hauntingly beautiful smooth voice, would bring the cinematic to life and would give the sound the quality to match the video and the story. Gameplay 10/10My instant impression is of the game is that it delivers what it promises. It delivers what you’re expecting it to. There is no mistaking that Godstrike is a bullet-hell game. You don’t have to wean yourself in, or get a feel for the game, you get what you’re expecting and this makes the same so simple to pick up. That’s a pass mark for gameplay for us. So, what takes Godstrike from a pass mark to a 10/10? A few things. First, the tutorial room is a great idea. The player can experiment with abilities, ability set ups, the game mechanics like souls, and more. That’s a great gameplay decision from the developer.  Next, the shear level of different ways you can play the game. The ability and passive set ups that are possible are of a ridiculous level, and provide so much variety in how you can play the game from attempt to attempt. That’s going to keep you coming back again, and again.  Next, the health is timer, and timer is health gimmick. It provides something different, and gives the player a fresh experience even if they play bullet-hell games often. And that’s a very good thing, because if you’re heavily experienced with games like this, it can be hard to feel like you’re playing a different game each time you try and buy something new. But here, you do – there’s a point of difference and that’s great.X-Factor 8/10The X factor for Godstrike is accessibility. How easy is the game to pick up, if you’re inexperienced with bullet-hell games, or are just not a fan of the genre in general.  What would I say? Very accessible. How can I say this? Because bullet-hell games aren’t in my top three favourite genres, nor do I have a huge amount of experience with them, but I find myself wanting to play more and more Godstrike.  Wanting to play the game in my own personal time, without recording, or preparing for an article? That means the draw and the accessibility is there for people like me, and perhaps you too. So, if you’re on the fence because you’re not the biggest fan of the genre, or you don’t have much experience trying them, give Godstrike a go. You might be very pleasantly surprised.  I hope you enjoyed our first impressions Review of Godstrike.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of game design this game makes everything wrong a developer can make wrong:-The very first level (introduced as tutorial boss) is already somewhat difficult-The 3D side view makes it difficult to judge if an projectile or enemy will hit you.-Often you don't know if something hit you, because there is no feedback.-No checkpoints of any kind. Every time you die you have to start from the first phase of the boss. -Most bosses are faster than you and you are usually only a tiny bit faster than the bullets. This makes dodging awkward and you cannot retreat into an advantageous area.-Almost EVERYTHING is randomized. Not that randomization is something bad in general, but in this case it means that there are no patterns to learn and you will often end up in bad situations without it being your fault. -Bullets don't have generous hit-boxes, which means you get "what, that did hit me?"-moments instead of "oh, that was close"-moments. -The power-ups, on the other hand, must be hit dead-center to collect and they disappear absurdly fast. -The visual contrast between bullets and background is not high enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I streamed this game on twitch the moment it became available. From the start, I was having a ton of fun! The first four bosses were defeated with 0:00 on the clock which means you can't be hit again or you'll die, so this definitely led to some heart pounding moments! There are different abilities you can use to overcome the boss, but these abilities come with a cost, time. If you choose a dash ability, that subtracts 15 seconds from your overall start time to defeat the boss. There are passive abilities which do not effect time, and these abilities can help with attack speed, movement speed, damage negation, or even help with picking up shards to power your abilities. During my stream, two members of the development team stopped by, gifted subscriptions to my channel, and were overall extremely friendly. I have truly enjoyed this game and for somewhere between $10-15, I think its a great deal for a great game. Cheers all!

_childDocuments_.review: Godstrike is yet another of literally hundreds 2D retro top-down shooter/brawlers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  This one is 3D rendered at least, but with as little effort as possible, with quasi-minimalist 3D low poly "art" (chosen purely for the aesthetic and not at all because doing the graphics properly is hard!).  So what about the gameplay?  First up there's some degree of polish here, this isn't exactly shovelware (but close).  Nice tight controls help.  Unfortunately the core game design has problems, a lot of them.  The hitboxing isn't quite right... it might take a long time playing to be able to adjust to the deficiencies there.  And this is a "boss rush" game, so the encounter design is half-baked... you just fight a variety of bosses without the usual interesting filler, but that's to do with the defective concept of using procgen instead of the difficult but necessary job of hand building levels and content for a video game.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The game assets are far from bleeding edge, with lowish polygon counts and somewhat low resolution textures, making this look like it's at least 10 years old.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks poor in comparison to more professionally produced games as a result of their decisions.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.Godstrike has the laughable, eye-watering price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Deep Rock Galactic", "Monster Hunter World" or "Grand Theft Auto V".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, Godstrike is one of the better looking twin-sticks I've played, with a very stylistic graphical approach and some pretty good enemy designs. Given that you'll be spending the balance of the game fighting bosses, that certainly counts for something. An added effect is that when the game gets visually busy (and it certainly will), it's usually to pick out the protagonist from the masses of bullets filling the screen.I would call Godstrike a middle-difficulty game, at least as far as games like this go, but the difficulty curve can be pretty savage. Sage use of active powers is the key to beating the later bosses in a timely fashion, and in fact the right combination of abilities played at the right time can ruin a boss in short order. The key is to get it to a rhythm: Activate a suite of damage powers, wait until the screen is filled with souls from the carnage, then turn on a defensive power and scoop up those souls to start the process over again. The impact is more than worth the handful of seconds shaved off the timer.Overall, I would recommend Godstrike for aficionados of twin-stick and bullet hell games. It could even serve as an entry point for beginners to the style, though be prepared for the game to let go of your hand after a few stages.

_childDocuments_.review: And there I was, playing another bullet hell twin stick shooter.  Thinking I was just over and done with the genre, I decided to pick up Godstrike.  I was so angry...when I found out I was enjoying myself.  Godstrike the sort of challenging and addictive title that is an easy recommendation for those who enjoy games like Furi.  The twist being your health is actually your time bank, which after it gets depleted leaves you with one last hit.  It certainly causes an adrenaline kick that could be confused with panic.  Along the way, you develop new abilities and perks that you can mix and match according to your play style.  So. that's definitely really slick.  And while it art design isn't setting the bar for modern gaming, it's vibrant color palette and synth soundtrack fits nicely.  Godstrike was one of those impulse purchases I certainly don't regret.

name: Unknown 9: Awakening
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Digital Deluxe Edition of Unknown 9: Awakening includes: - The Mercenary cosmetic pack - The Shadow cosmetic pack - The Aviator cosmetic pack Each pack contains an added unique Haroona skin with two additional color and texture options, a supplementary skin for Haroona’s journal and two extra, alternative, combat animations. About the Game Delve into the mysterious world of the Unknown 9, and uncover mysteries hidden in plain sight. You are Haroona, a Quaestor born with the ability to venture into a mysterious dimension that overlaps our own, known only as the Fold. On her quest for powerful hidden knowledge, Haroona will learn to master her unique connection to the Fold, which allows her to channel its powers into our world... But such power does not go unnoticed and Haroona quickly becomes the target of a splinter faction calling themselves the Ascendants, who want to use the Fold to alter the course of human history. Become Haroona - Play as a young and courageous woman who has the ability to dive into and channel powers from a parallel dimension known as the Fold. Master the Fold - Leverage your mastery of the Fold and choose your own playstyle. Step into your enemies to control them, dodge bullets, vanish in plain sight, hurl Umbric energy at your opponents, and more. Journey across the world - From the sands of Mauritania and perilous Indian jungles to the gothic landscapes of 19th century Portugal, discover some of the most mysterious locations the world has to offer. Discover the Unknown 9 universe - Unknown 9: Awakening lies at the heart of intertwining stories, unfolding through a multitude of Unknown 9 products whose events and characters make up a much larger Storyworld.

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I can ignore glaring tech issues if the gameplay is fun enough (heck, I like Sonic 06). But while the core gameplay loop is very fun here--think Hitman meets Uncharted with Doctor Strange powers--the surrounding game can't save itself.The story:You've seen it all before; classic "cocky upstart loses mentor, goes on journey to become less annoying" plot. The main villain is a lazy Jordan Peterson caricature written by people who'd struggle to be political cartoonists for Buzzfeed. Sweet Baby Inc. Enough said.The glitches:Your character constantly gets caught on textures (forcing a checkpoint reload), characters clip through the ground during cutscenes, facial animations often look alien and broken, certain mechanics can be triggered in such an order that they cancel out their own actions (body possessing), etc. This is not AAA or even AA.The gameplay:Combat encounters are terribly unbalanced, randomly spiking in difficulty with opponents that are not well-suited to the gameplay mechanics (gearhead!). Worse, upgrades spread across three mutually exclusive paths (stealth, crowd combat, duel combat), meaning in order to adequately upgrade yourself for one type of enemy encounter, you'll be left naked and afraid during the others. And this isn't a choose-your-playstyle title; you will be forced to engage with all action types, even the ones you're barred from prepping for. It's bad game design. There's no mid-game difficulty switcher, meaning if you overestimate your ability to handle Unknown 9's jank at the beginning, then late-game, you're in for a bad time.The good:The combat really is stellar *when it works.* It's AC/Hitman-style stealth but you can snatch souls out of bodies, possess people, trigger remote explosives, force-push goons, and do these things in sequences that look incredibly stylish and cinematic. And, to really zero in on Unknown 9's cinematic efforts, the game borrows liberally from Uncharted, trying to capture that brand of excitement in its platforming, camera angles, globe-trotting plot, etc. When the game works, it's obvious what the development team was shooting for. And for brief moments, you get that golden experience. There's a genuine attempt at adventure-genre innovation here, and I love the ideas. They're just buried under a lot of rough execution.I don't know what the nail in the coffin was for this project. Rookie dev team with amateur coders and hack-fraud creatives/writers? Lack of budget? Publisher-accelerated deadlines? Or some combo of all three? Whatever the case, I would like to see these fellows make another title, but I worry the team's issues are too fundamental to ever produce greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game a fair chance, and it ultimately disappointed me. I can't recommend it. However, unlike many who leave negative reviews after only a few minutes of playtime, I did complete the game.I feel like this could have been a decent game with a better story and more compelling characters. I can overlook clunky controls and subpar graphics, but a game needs to tell an interesting story with well-defined characters to be truly engaging. This game has somewhat interesting lore and a good setting, but the story itself is terribly mediocre and predictable. In addition to the weak storytelling, the characters are entirely forgettable. Despite listening to every line of dialogue spoken aboard The Morning Star, I couldn't bring myself to care about any of them. Haroona, the main character, is particularly disappointing. She lacks charm, personality, and emotional depth—just another typical "strong female character" without anything unique to offer.The combat, with a few exceptions, is heavily focused on stealth and features some interesting mechanics. However, the AI is incredibly simplistic, and there's little enemy variety. I found myself exploiting the same tactic repeatedly: using Shroud next to an enemy, performing a takedown, and then repeating the process on the next few enemies in the area.Bugs were also a frequent nuisance. I had to restart from the last checkpoint several times because I got stuck in combat, preventing story cutscenes from triggering, or encountered enemies that glitched and became invincible. The "Quaestor's Grace" skill upgrade, which seemingly went untested by QA, grants temporary invulnerability and makes it far too easy to break the game by going out of bounds.Is this the worst game ever made? No, there are definitely worse games out there. But after finishing it, I couldn't help but wish I had spent my time playing something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t even know where to begin with this game—everything about it feels fundamentally broken, like very little thought or effort went into its creation. From the moment I started playing, it was clear that this was one of those games that probably came together over a weekend with someone idly messing around in Unreal Engine 5. The world feels empty, lifeless, and incomplete, as if they simply clicked a few assets together without any real vision or design behind it.The audio and music are a disaster. It’s almost insulting how bad it is, as though it was slapped together as an afterthought. There’s no atmosphere, no immersion, and certainly nothing enjoyable about listening to it. In fact, I often found myself muting the game because the sound design was that grating.And the mechanics? They’re pointless. Nothing about the gameplay makes you feel clever or engaged; it’s just a string of bland interactions that serve no real purpose. The few mechanics the game has feel tacked on, as if the developers thought, “Well, I guess we need something for players to do,” but they never stopped to ask themselves why those mechanics matter. It’s an exercise in frustration, not fun.The writing is equally terrible—abstract, nonsensical, and completely non-tangible. It’s as if the developers were trying too hard to be "deep" or "artistic," but it just ends up being a confusing mess that lacks any emotional connection. It’s impossible to invest in the story or characters because there’s no substance there.And I really can’t stand when people try to defend this game by saying it just needs a bit of polish. Let’s be honest: a bit of polish isn’t going to fix something that’s broken at its core. The problems here are too deep to be solved with a few tweaks. Anyone who says otherwise is either lying to themselves or just wants to be a contrarian. This game is a waste of time, plain and simple.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you folks love reviews that start with "I really wanted to like this game" and whatever? I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ don't.So, I'll go with: "Our expectations for you were low, but holy ♥♥♥♥!"And here comes possibly one of the most aggressive reviews I've written here on Steam. Good job on making an aggressively bad game. It's not like I tried to be patient, you see my playtime. I'll skip short the part everyone already knows: I got the game for free with an AMD promotion and thought, "I already installed it, so why not give it a shot?"I have a thing for bad games. I like to find something in these, to see things with my very own eyes. And no, I’m not talking about underperformers like Atlas Fallen, Immortals of Aveum, or Styx. I’m talking about the real stiff stuff that simply doesn’t know how to execute its ideas, janky as ♥♥♥♥. Balan Wonderworld, Wanted: Dead, Redfall. And guess what? I finished them all.Unknown 9 is a truly terrible ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess. I don’t even know where to begin. I can list at least one good-ish thing about the aforementioned games, but Unknown 9? Hell nah. I couldn’t bring myself to finish it and dropped it after seeing I was asked to solve the exact same puzzle for the third time. I must mention briefly that the game had a 28gb patch out of nowhere where I finished up with it for the first time.The game starts as pseudo-stealth and then... forces you into close-quarters combat, as it often sends waves of enemies into arena-like areas. That’s when the game truly exposes its weaknesses. The combat is janky as ♥♥♥♥, and when you think there couldn’t be worse enemy designs, the game never fails to surprise you. Your abilities are basically R1+R2 spam. R2 fills a bar that lets you TKO your enemies, and R1 is your classic light attack. Everything else simply does not work. As far as I am concerned you need to clear out all the enemies before you proceed to the next area to unlock certain doors/gates. Perhaps it's because I iniated combat somewhere. I really hope so otherwise it's plain ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if the game simply does not let you skip enemies. Btw you cannot upgrade your abilities in combat. Why not? Why is this arbitrary? If at that time I notice I am missing out on something and I have enough resources, I better make a use of them, no? The whole gimmick (the experimental area, so to speak) is being able to tap into your enemies and have them turn on their friends, but all you can do is make some enemies stick to others' asses and do either a ranged attack or some shockwave slam sort of ♥♥♥♥. It’s not like you have a bunch of gadgets that can immobilize your targets or whatever. It’s nothing exciting. At best you can make an use of the enviromental damage. And I must admit you can at least link some creative combos by using those but in games like these you should be able to abuse your powers to their limits. The game already screams "I am a budget title," but man... they played it overly safe with every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic. There’s nothing inspired. You can already possess targets in Dishonored and Styx. If there is nothing game changing about this said ability (like using character specific gadgets to solve puzzles or clear out areas) then it simply means devs ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up so bad. Yet another instance, Remember Me actually had some bold ideas going on despite the janky combat. There are your classic action-adventure sequences. Walking on a plank while the protag mumbles about being cautious. Does it give her a character? No. It's a classic trope and it does not work. Why? Because you are barely 6ft away from the ground and a fall could barely injure you. How can a studio lack this much of a common sense? As a game of unknowns, it has its fair share of bugs. Moonwalking enemies when you tap into them, AI getting frozen, an enemy somehow pushing itself outside the area’s bounds, and even hilarious animation bugs when Haroona (the MC) was supposed to hold a mounted gun, but I could see her in a supposed-to-be FPS sequence rather than the flying planes so I patiently waited to die but all I knew I was suffering.And all this DEI stuff? I frankly don’t care to discuss any of that. I just want to let people know there are characters with Indian ancestry. Chloe Frazer, PoP's Farah, Symmetra—not only one of OW’s OG 12, but also has a lot of people simping after her. Are not these characters somewhat loved across the globe? Make your own judgments. A game like this works better when it’s humorous or at least can justify its own mysteries. Unknown 9 is neither. Sure, there are some banters between the protagonist and her companions, but none of them are at Indiana Jones/Uncharted level, so it was bound to be doomed from the get-go. And then, the alleged mystery about the mysterious dimension, "The Fold," didn’t ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unfold enough. I’ve finished over 60% of the game and still don’t know what its exact point is.There are only two bosses, and both are recycled later on. Both are incredibly dull, and your second encounter is seemingly the exact same, so that’s another reason to drop the game quickly. Bosses, you can't tap into. You need to drain their shield first to do damage. You can't really use environment either. As if they tried to create the most boring design ever. The puzzles are nothing clever; they’re your usual “redirect the beam” type of ♥♥♥♥, and you feel like a monkey trying to fit some shapes in. Why are these sequences even in this game? You only have two rotations to begin with. Seriously, what the ♥♥♥♥? Is the bar that low? Luckily, the optimization is fairly good, but well, the MC can’t even do justice to Anya Chalotra. The opening sequence of the game is all-time meme-worthy. The faces look bleh, and I can live with that, but they look absolutely irredeemable when they are in The Fold. The Fold has a total pile-of-♥♥♥♥ color pattern, and the facial expressions and lip sync are not quite crisp. Imagine how hairs would look like yourself. Most of the scene compositions are plain bad, so when Haroona was running out in tears after our “villain” told her to do so, I was bursting out in laughter where the scene was supposed to be emotional.I don’t know what’s the story behind the game, but I am severely disinterested in hearing it. All I know is, it allegedly had a problematic development, and well, as a debut game, this does nothing for Bandai Namco and severely hurts Reflector. A game that should have been delayed further or even shelved is now released, and they were expecting what? To sell this piece of jank? For real? A YouTuber who longplays this is likely to earn more than what this game grosses.It's also interesting that 62 reviews that have counted towards the average score are 45% positive while all the 217 reviews combined are only 25%. Is it a mere coping mechanism of the players who actually bought this game? Who knows? But the data is here, and Unknown 9 is not only one of the worst games of this year but also of all time(39% of the players traversed the Charadrius in Metaphor:ReFantazio and that's about 30 hours in, I know most ATLUS fans are bunch of no lifers but only 41% finished the first chapter of Unknown 9 which is merely the first hour)★½✩☆☆☆

_childDocuments_.review: My original review of this game was 7,556 characters too long, so I had to cut out about half!  Thanks, Steam! (sarcasm)Bandai Namco requires you forfeit your rights and agree to forced arbitration AND a class action waiver to install the game if in the US.  The fact that they'll do this to anyone means they should be avoided in their entirety.  It doesn't matter why the provisions are there, THEY SHOULD NOT BE THERE TO BEGIN WITH!  You must also agree in the game, meaning you're required to forfeit your rights TWICE.  DO NOT ACCEPT THIS!With that said, I received this game for free when I purchased my 7900 XTX GPU, so at least I didn't have to pay for it.This game does almost everything wrong.  All it does right is world design, when excluding the tacked-on gameplay elements, and some lighting from Unreal Engine 5.  The game lacks ALL options for depth of field and chromatic aberration, so you can't turn them off or change them.  There's no zoom or FOV control, so you'll be stuck with a camera that's too close and can sometimes be EVEN CLOSER during combat, like when the bottom of Haroona's, being the character you play as, shoulder blades were at the bottom of the screen.  WHY ARE THESE SETTINGS MISSING WHEN THE ENGINE SUPPORTS THEM?!Target locking only locks the camera on enemies, but Haroona will REPEATEDLY strike the air because she fails to actually aim for the enemy you're trying to attack.  There's NO combat target locking, nor any ability to make Haroona attack in the direction of the enemy via the left thumbstick, played with a controller; she will ONLY strike in the direction she's facing.Camera controls are sometimes restricted or removed.  Inputs are delayed to such a degree that just to start walking takes almost A FULL SECOND before ANY motion is made after the input.  This is an issue with combat, as trying to get through the enemy blocking, wherein they can block every attack you use, other than a heavy attack, by raising their arms to their chest, doesn't work half the time.  Because of the delay and enemies having none, you'll find yourself commonly hit out of your attacks before you're able to use them.  It doesn't matter if you're actively striking the enemy, you'll frequently be hit and staggered.  Your combos are very short, enemies' are longer.Enemies almost never respond to being hit: punch them in the face, and they'll ignore it and hit you back.  Being hit will be enough to stagger you and force you to wait for your character to stop stumbling.  That staggered state can be extended by other enemies, which may lead to a chain that drops your health almost to 0.  During staggered states, you can't block, dodge, or heal.  Unlike enemies, blocking drains your energy and your shield can be broken, forcing you into a stagger.The energy to use the shield is also for some attacks and healing.  The only ways to restore that energy is to avoid your enemies while it slowly restores, being be shot at and chased during this, or by punching them.  You can also unlock skills to help, but it doesn't make much difference.  Restoring the energy in fights isn't a big deal, but it is annoying that you can't heal unless you're practically standing still.  Enemies can do more damage with one hit than what you heal, and you'll need to heal a few times to restore all your health.  Stealth is a laughably pointless joke, and you'll be FORCED to take out every enemy in an area before you can progress.The game is FAR too linear.  There's nothing wrong with linear games, but there is a point at which it can be a problem.  The ONLY way to obtain skills is to find the skill points around the world, but because of this game's linearity, if you happen to go the way to progress through the game, you can't go back and get anything you missed!  Climbing or jumping up, down, or to something sometimes prevents you from retracing your steps to explore areas you'd missed.  You can also sometimes reach a cutscene which changes your location.  Part of this issue could've been mitigated with a map, minimap, and waypoint system, but this game has none of those.  You have to guess which path is correct, then hope it doesn't trigger something that prevents you from going back.  Since skills are obtained from this exploration, missing too many could be detrimental later in the game.For the story, I couldn't figure what was going on from the very start.  I don't care for stories in games, but I try figuring out what's going on in new ones; I had to stop trying with this one.  You start with some old lady and kill random people in your path.  The lady gets killed by someone who pulls the evil villain cliche of allowing you to live, so you later return and fight him.For another cliche, after losing the fight against him, he's randomly distracted by the zeppelin your friends are on as they fly it behind him.  He suddenly forgets he can force-grab and pull you, and that he was holding a loaded gun he was about to shoot you with, and allows you run away and jump onto the zeppelin, making your escape!  This means there's a final battle against him at the end of the game, where you finally defeat him, if you can deal with his nonstop attacks that make your limited dodges and shield tedious.  He's a damage tank wrapped in a sponge.  The only way to hurt him is with perfect dodges, followed by strikes with energy to build a scripted combo attack.After a few scripted combos, you beat him and exit the realm you were in, finding yourself surrounded by enemies you can't reach.  You can't possess them, they shoot at you from a distance, and you can't cross the gap to get to them for combat.  Instead, you can suddenly insta-kill them by force-pulling or pushing them, which wasn't previously possible.  The rest is a slow travel through an earlier area of the game until you reach the end and have the credits roll.Almost all of this game will remove your ability to run, forcing you to move at the slow jog you usually default to, or force you to walk.  Some balance-beam sections are also laughable, as they'll be about 2 feet wide, but Haroona will creep along them as if they're only 4 inches wide.  Some balance-beam sections are created by breaking a tree with your abilities which just so happen to be the exact right size to be a perfect bridge for you to walk across.  Those trees are identical and in areas that make no sense, such as in a cave.  Again, gameplay elements ruin the world design.The people who designed the game's world did good, the others are incompetent and use ideas that were dated 15 years ago.  The areas of the game largely seem natural, but every aspect of the gameplay ruins it.The game has raytracing (RT), but only from the light from Haroona's bracers, and only when in the dark.  There are times when the game has you wandering through the dark because it forgets those bracers can glow!  I suggest leaving RT off, regardless, as it can reduce your framerate by about half when not present.  When present, even in a tiny cave you have to crouch through, the light was able to drive my framerate down to 27fps at 1440p.  Some settings require you relaunch the game to get them to apply.  It doesn't inform you which setting requires this until AFTER you change it, nor should they require such to begin with if properly programmed.  The glow from the bracers without RT looks like there was no effort involved, but RT on them only is the most brain-dead implementation ever, making it stupidly pointless.Bugs: loading into a cutscene played a barrage of collision impacts on repeat with every frame that ended just as I watched Haroona fall into an abyss and say I died.  The cutscene load caused it, as when I reloaded the autosave it made at that same point, I loaded into that cutscene, without needing to redo the fight.  Another cutscene froze the game and forced me to kill the process from the background with Task Manager.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Has potential but not worth the full price. Your $50 are better spent on the new Red Dead: Redemption PC port.SPOILER WARNINGS for Chapter 1 and 2.This is a AA game, but it's fair to judge because it still cannot compete with modern AA releases.My hopes were high for this game as an Uncharted-like game with some East-Asian influence. All I want is a good single-player, linear, cinematic, story-driven game with a good narrative, compelling characters, and fun gameplay.And yes, I played this game on a controller because this is what it was designed for. I also played on a high-end computer.I have played halfway through Chapter 2 until I unfortunately lost interest.This combat system reminds me of Dishonored. The gameplay puts heavy emphasis on stealth, combining supernatural abilities with a melee-focused attacks just like Dishonored does.Where Dishonored succeeds, Unknown 9 unfortunately fails. Dishonored has fluent and more gameplay whereas Unknown 9 feels clunky and less meaningul. The combat system offers a much greater challenge thus reward for players who have mastered it.Am regenerates too fast. This results in an extremely repetitive combat, mostly made of button/ability mashing or chaining.Yes, there are the basic strategies such as pushing enemies into dynamite and causing them to die, which can be rewarding and fun to pull off. However, it's very much overused in this game, making it too convenient.But the real power is when you can leverage certain ability chains to win every single combat encounter with minimal effort and similarly low reward. Stepping and shade are way too easy to abuse. Am regenerates so fast and can be used for OP abilities. You can always repeat the game loop of "shade/hide, stealth kill, shade/hide, stealth kill", and if you need an exit plan, reserve your "Stepping" token for any emergency that comes in your way.It is fun to discover such strategies and to apply them, but it becomes tedious at some point. Combat feels like it's forced and unnatural, not an end in itself.I don't mind a shallow combat system though. I have played many games with bad combat systems but at least they had great story with great writing.One major issue I have with the combat is that this is a stealth game emphasizing player choice in different confrontations, yet the game requires you to kill every single enemy around. You cannot simply sneak past them in Chapter 2 as you could in Chapter 1.Outside combat, Unknown 9 behaves a lot like Uncharted, only the parkour is much simpler and pretty much almost risk free.The riddles are basic and not very time-consuming. Parkour is also 100% safe and there is little challenge or reward in jumping the right way.Unknown 9 also overuses narrow passages that you have to press Y to fit between. I remember it happening over 5 times just in the first 30 minutes of gameplay, which is a bit too much.As a reminder, I ran this game on a high-end PC by today by contemporary standards: RTX 4090, Intel i9 14th Gen, over 64 GB DDR5 RAM.Loading new regions results in a significant stuttering, i.e. severe framerate drop. This is especially noticeable in the beginning of cinematic cutscenes.Enemies say "she" without even knowing the enemy is a single, female person. That happened in Chapter 1, even before the Ascendents were actively looking for her, as well as in Chapter 2, where she is not the only wanted fugitive. Luther is one of them.The graphics look very, very dated. I have compared this game to Dishonored, and yet Dishonored doesn't feel old due to good graphics quality and the unique art style.Facial animations are rather poor for a AA game, and animations are not up to standards. Now, again, some of this wouldn't be a problem if Unknown 9 didn't have a realistic graphics style and had chosen something more stylized.The story's premise is that civilizations will always be destroyed, paving the way to their own destruction and the next civilization's rise. One civilization, the Sahin, sought to break the cycle. Realizing their own destruction's inevitability, they chose to give immortality to nine of them, the Unknown 9.A magical realm coexists with our real world, called The Fold. It works similarly to the Force in Star Wars or The Fade in Dragon Age. Some people are gifted with a special ability to travel the Fold, they are called Quaestors.In the modern civilization, some have realized the nature of civilizations, that their own is also going to end one day. In the modern day, some of them led by a man named Vincent wish to use mystical powers to break the cycle. These people seem critical of Quaestors and are persecuting them.Great Unfortunately, the writing is the dealbreaker for me in this game.Reika is a great character, the only one I take no issue with. She is seemingly killed in Chapter 1.Vincent is not a very convincing villain. He sounds very insecure, he stutters as he talks, he sounds like he's scared of the spotlight. He lacks the charisma. He is bland. He is not somebody that I actually believe to be a cult leader. He also lets Haroona go in Chapter 1, only to change his mind and decide that she should be persecuted. He is indecisive and incompetent.The protagonist should be one of the most well-written characters, but Haroona thus far not. After losing her mentor Reika to Vincent, Haroona becomes bitter and vengeful. However, the transition from her personality in Chapter 1 to Chapter 2 is not only too rapid, it is also barely showcased in any notable way. It feels unatural, it feels like the plot needed her to be vengeful and bitter.The enemies - why exactly do they hate us? Why is Vincent a bad guy? We have the answers from the story - Vincent leads a weird cult that blindly obeys him, he kills Reika, and he dabbles with powers beyond his own control that could spill doom for humanity. Vincent and Reika symbolize a sort of good and evil dynamic and there is great potential in this story.But does it sound believable based on what we actually see, the writing and the animations? Not at all. The dialog is unbelievable, sanitized, and unrealistic, and Vincent comes across as that weird Reddit moderator who was bullied too much in school and is now on a power trip.Unknown 9 has lots of potential, some great ideas but terrible execution. The protagonist is not compelling or likeable, dialog is bad, and I cannot take the characters or their motivations very seriously. The gameplay is nothing special either, it's too easy and unsatisfying, unrewarding. I have played many games with bad gameplay but a good story, and unfortunately, a $50 Steam game with the "Story Rich" and "Lore Rich" tags should have better writing than this.If an action adventure game cannot persuade critics through gameplay, then perhaps it should through storytelling and amazing characters and humor. This is not the case here, unfortunately. No humor, no entertainment, not so relatable characters.This game isn't the return to amazing linear Uncharted-like games that I had been looking forward to. I don't think it's worth $50. Recommending only on sale if you are into story-driven games and you're completely out of options.Here are some recommendations so that you're not:- Dishonored: AA stealth-based games with a great story and amazing, fluid gameplay- Life is Strange 1: AA game with great story and characters, a timeless stylized look, and magical abilities. If you like a female protagonist, this is one of the best games out there.- Uncharted: Unknown 9 but better- Quantum Break: Linear, cinematic AAA game with time manipulation abilities and an amazing story- Black Myth: Wukong: Great melee-based AA game if you want a challenge

_childDocuments_.review: The positive things first: It's a functional game that actually looks quite nice, even without ray tracing. The implementation of keyboard and mouse is surprisingly good for a console port.Overall, there are only a few noticeable bugs like texture streaming occasionally dropping the frame rate when using ray tracing (it's fine w/o RT), or the hair and cloth physics often being weird.The litany of negative things:- The story revolves around being some sort of "chosen one" chasing a McGuffin. That wouldn't be too bad in itself, but since the game takes itself too serious and tries to be too bombastic, the story telling often feels quite comical and out of place.- The game fails to engage the player during the tutorial chapter. You only get a few combat abilities while listening to the verbal diarrhea from your companion, trying to squeeze the world building into a series of voice-overs.- After the cliffhanger, you are thrown into an adventure that lacks any side stories. Over time, you will gain more abilities and encounter more variants of bad guys, but the overall combat feels repetitive and quite boring.- Generally, moving through the mostly linear areas often gets interrupted by cutscenes and exploration isn't really a thing, except for some "hidden" room or dead-end path with a collection item.- Progress doesn't really feel rewarding. I made it through about a third of the game and the amount of collections, tidbits of lore and skill points is nice, but it didn't really feel like I was making much progress in the story and getting more backstory didn't help to feel engaged either.- The world in general feels quite disjointed. On the one side, you learn ancient magic tricks to fight through the armies of bad guys like a discount-Jedi, on the other hand, colonial pre-WWI India is depicted as some sort of Indiana Jones inspired steampunk world.To me, it looks more like your typical €20 early access game from a dev that is more focused on a potential Netflix miniseries inspired by the game than the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I got a key for this and Space Marines 2 with my 7950x3d from BestBuy. Space Marines 2 is actually insane competition for this game most people who got the keys probably just played that only.4/10 if generous, extremely mediocre. I finished the entire game in 8.8 hours and got at least 75% of the collectibles on normal difficulty. It would literally be INSANE to pay $50 for this. There is basically no reason to buy it, but if you really wanted to maybe $10 is a fair price but even at that price point it is lacking compared to other games.I don't really have an eye for graphics but they aren't great. PS2 is a little exaggerating maybe xbox 360 level.But even then Far Cry 4 looked better and that was on the 360. The graphics are not charming in any way. I couldn't help but to notice the climbable walls are literally a flat texture of stones and that the character's hands actually float over them instead of touching it. For a 2024 game that is genuinely insane. And it's just the same repeating texture every single time. The level design is also somewhat squandered with stupid one way gates that act like loading screens and little caves you need to shimmy through. Only unlike God Of Wars implementation of this idea it seems pretty unnatural and the gate is literally the same old red painted one with a crate leaning against it even if doesn't make sense for the location.  Everything you can jump on also white paint on it. The character design is also extremely bland and offers no free customization except for 2 they just added in the first update which are actually worse than the default ones.In pretty much every cut scene I felt like I could see the character's animations resetting or pop in. Even during normal gameplay animations would glitch out frequently and especially the npcs. In the early segment of the game there are a lot of motionless npcs standing everywhere and you literally cannot interact with them in any way. Talk about cutting edge. The named npcs don’t even look at you when you initiate dialogue. Regarding the 30G update that I downloaded for this game because I took so long to finish after getting my key I did not notice any improvement in performance or animations or anything at all so I'm not sure what it even did aside from add 2 cosmetics. The story is pretty much nothing, it says nothing it does nothing. It has no value in my opinion. I did not really care about any of the characters and the development seems forced. The only interesting plot point is related to the revelation achievement and I guess the ending slightly. If there was music in this game it literally left no impression on me.I see in the positive reviews that some people enjoyed the combat system. The only combat ability worth mentioning is stepping into the bodies of enemies. It's slightly unique but it's slow and pretty much just the same thing over and over. A lot of the enemies felt like damage sponges and the combat is more mediocrity. I don't see too much to enjoy.About 7 hours into this game there is a cut scene where you escape from enemies by turning a lever that moves an angle before a running enemy can reach it. I noticed that as it cut back to the running guy his position got reset or he would've actually made it on the bridge on time. Even then he probably still could've just jumped onto the bridge it wasn't that far. The enemies also could've just went around the bridge and jumped on it from a position that they easily could've reached but that was it. I think this scene is emblematic of the whole game.One strength of the game is that it's inspired from eastern ideas like karma and stuff. That could make the lore a little interesting.I don't see any obvious ways in which DEI manifests here outside of the ethniticies or sexes of the characters. It makes sense for the main character to be Indian because it's set in India and uses the eastern ideas. Maybe just the bad writing?It is a bad look for AMD to put their name on this game. Maybe Space Marines 2 cancels it out though. Also worth mentioning is the insane greed to put up cosmetic dlc for $5 each. Nobody has even rated them within the first day of their release so clearly nobody is going to buy that trash. You would've already got scammed into getting those if you got the deluxe edition.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wondered what it would be like to play a game that feels like a nostalgic trip back to 2005 while simultaneously running so much worse than Space Marine 2, which is supposed to be an AMD sponsored tile, then Unknown 9: Awakening is your ticket to disappointment. Visually, the game looks like it time-traveled from the era of the original Space Marine 1. It’s like they took the graphics engine from a decade ago, dusted it off, and slapped on some new textures that still manage to look outdated. The performance? Let’s just say I've seen smoother gameplay on a potato, you see the FPS at 85 but the 1% lows at 10. Frame rates drop more often than my hopes for this game, making combat feel like an awkward dance where nobody knows the steps.Now, let’s talk about the characters. Or rather, let’s talk about their lack of character. The facial animations are so lifeless that it feels like I’m interacting with mannequins. The characters’ eyes just stare straight ahead, giving me the distinct impression that they’re plotting something sinister—or maybe they’re just as bored as I am.In summary, Unknown 9: Awakening is an experience that leaves you questioning your life choices. It’s a game that aspires to be ambitious but ends up feeling like a relic of the past—one that you’d rather forget. If you’re looking for something fresh and engaging, keep scrolling past this one. Save your time and sanity; there are better ways to spend your gaming hours than staring into the void of this game’s soulless eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels a bit like Assassin's Creed but worse.Feels a bit like Tomb Raider but worse.Performance is terrible considering that the visuals aren't that great to begin with. Graphics settings are lackluster. For example, they did include upscaling tech - but only FSR 2.3 (iirc) - and they did include RayTracing - but it only applies to very specific light sources. Games should at least run well if they don't look good but this does neither.Haven't played much yet so take this with a grain of salt, but the characters so far feel flat and one-dimensional. With the way the writing sounds I don't have much hope for any real development in the depth of story or characters.The game seems to consist of tiny, narrow encounters chained onto each other where you can do stealth takedowns, use your abilities and fight enemies. Neither of these options is well executed, though. It's basically a miniature-scale Tomb Raider game. Only that stealth is finicky because enemies might spin around randomly, go slow-mo and walk in place for no reason or see you behind an obstacle. And melee is incredibly repetitive even when mixing it up with abilities (so far, maybe there's way more variety later).The main ability of stepping into enemies is basically just an extra attack using the borrowed enemy's weapon to strike / shoot another enemy just to go back to bad melee combat. Later you can chain-step into multiple foes for more special attacks, extra damage to the last stepped-in enemy and so on. None of these sound remotely appealing enough to give me hope for a turn-around into a fun gameplay loop.It's not a terrible game. But it's not a good one, either. It's more of a "if you have nothing else to play and it's on a deep sale (50€ is waaaaaay overpriced) and there are no interesting upcoming releases in the near future" recommendation. But as long as you have anything else to do - now or relatively soon - I'd advise you to steer clear.
