_childDocuments_.review: I've got this game bundled with my AMD GPU and thought gonna try it out. I now have finished the prelude story/tutorial part. Story seems ok so far, tho the antagonists felt too much cliche. The skill mechanics are interesting and it has stealth in it that I'm fan of. NPC enemy ai doesn't feel too special, but isn't terrible either for now.My main gripe and why I can't recommend the game for now is the performance. For the not so pretty graphical quality the game provides on high setting, it has constant hick ups for me, sometimes it even freezes for 1-2 seconds. That needs to be addressed, because it keeps pulling me out of the game. It's very annoying.I ran it on 1080p ultrawide, have an RX7800XT, 32GB ram, SSD, only my cpu is a bit weaker, but I had rarely problems like this with other games that ran on Unreal Engine 5 and those had better graphic quality. Not to mention it runs Cyberpunk 2077 on max quality without RT pretty flawlessly.When the issues got solved in a patch, I will probably come back and play it to see the rest of the story/gameplay and judge it more by that.Update: AMD released a few hours ago a new driver which includes improvement to this game. The big stutters are gone and I only see small ones sometimes that aren't as bothersome.Okay, now that I have finished the game I can properly give a review.First a shorter tl;dr. The game is okay, I would recommend it maybe on a sale, but you have to get through the first two levels to really getting any hook for the game.The good:- Story is ok with some highs in it.- Combat will be more challenging and fun later, you can't just heavy attack spam like at the start. For example you can use your skill in different fun ways like pushing/pulling enemies into a pit.- VA is good.- Graphics looks a bit dated even on epic, but as you get further into the game there are some nice level designs. I liked the airship's interior in it too.- Enemy AI is decent if it doesn't get buggy, better than SW:Outlaws for sure :)- Boss fights were okThe bad:- Outdated level design. The levels are pretty narrow, tunnel like with some more open fields, pretty old school level design. Reminds me of the oldest Uncharted-like games, but less cinematic. Lots of cliff crevices you have to go through in cutscenes. I think this game had like 30+, every level had like 4-5, same animation. It's getting boring very fast. Same with the cutscenes of going through closed doors. Lots of doors...- I personally didn't like that "skill points" are hidden in the levels, but after you finished the game you can replay the maps and find the rest of the collectibles. Also companion trying to rush me forward while I search for hidden items.- Animations aren't too good. Face animations are not the worst it's a bit better than what Bethesda does. Lots of bugs.- What puzzles it has, it can be barely called puzzles.- Cinematic cutscenes still have some bugs after the first patch. Sometimes Haroona goes knee deep into the ground while it plays the cutscene and when you get back the control she pops back having her feet on the ground again. Also the letterboxing on ultrawide is annoying.- Companion AI as like in most of the games I've played feels annoying, is in the way in stealth gameplay.- For the graphical quality it has, it doesn't have too good performance. On epic quality without RT, no scaling I had 60fps average on 2560x1080p.Also I know SBI is a hot topic here for people and I don't like it either if artificially and unnaturally some agenda is pushed in a game like in Suicide Squad. So I've paid close attention to it here and I have to say it's perfectly fine at least story wise. I haven't read all written lore tho.

_childDocuments_.review: - Disappointing. Not really any woke vibes but basic story, bland characters, plenty of game breaking issues, graphics are unimpressive, tedious world exploration, poor combat, and extremely novice-minded game design and programming choices (examples below). I don't really take time to try new games but this one seemed interesting so I gave it a shot. I thought it would have the fun factor typical of these types of games.However, it does have game-breaking bugs such as a part where you knock down a tree to use as a bridge with Lucian, except the tree doesn't trigger the game action to make the path crossable (bad programming) so the story can't be continued. It's a linear game so whenever a path breaks it's over. There are no alternative routes here.The story from before the game broke was about ancient dimensional beings in history along with the villain trying to end their world's form of Samsara (life and death cycle of reincarnation in Hinduism) that is also somehow ending their version of the world to make the next one.There have been no real motives provided to justify the protagonist going on a mystical murder spree of these individuals, the soldiers are just villains from the get-go. As far as I can tell you're playing as the villain who keeps on separating the souls of mortals from their bodies and having their comrades kill each other just because everyone in this world (including you) are mean and violent.There isn't really any "wokeness"/DEI. The characters are  and most of the enemies look like Indian male and female soldier models with British voices. Up to the point I reached, the only white males I've seen appear are the main villain (Victor or Vincent) and an American (Lucian).The majority of the issues with the game are just from bad programming and novice-level game design principles with apparently no QA team. -Talk scenes turn head in wrong direction. The tutorial intended you to be on the left, the NPC can't track you on the right.-When walking there are conversations. These cutoff abruptly if you reach a specific new event spot.-Follower often gets stuck, and of course they never help you.-Followers can be standing but are not seen by enemies.-Enemies can be impacted by storm effects when no storm present, making them vulnerable to attack (error is no storm in that area).-Cutscenes can have a subtitle of a sentence that appears in the next conversation-There are many women soldier voices when most areas are mainly men. Some all-men areas have women voices.-Doors get magically locked until enemies defeated, limiting stealth options-NPCs are sometimes facing a direction where they're talking to no one-Enemy AI patterns can get stuck, so their cross-routes get messed up and you have to work around itThat is just some of what I noticed from 2 hours in just trying to setup and enjoy the game, and what I could reasonably fit into a review. The developers themselves are a subsidiary of Bandai-Namco which is why they had high production for this game as their first project. They are not indie devs and the team consisted of some established industry experts, so I don't see how any of these problems got by them.The graphics and scenery are dull. You don't feel like you're in India because of how boxed and unalive everything is. It's not artistic in any way, it's just untextured and bland. NPCs have a few repeating animations in town and there is no sense of oppression or interactions. Only Haroona is really targeted by the "bad guys" and they're all just mean for no reason other than plot purposes (their conversations imply that they want money and power even though the villain states early on that it's not about power).Most of the gameplay is spent pushing you forward through game design elements like walkways, climbing, and finding the next path/door forward which is more annoying than anything. Then the combat is pretty bad, there's no flow to it and no real rewards or penalties to keep it engaging. They wanted something like Batman and Dishonored with the limitations of Assassin's Creed but nothing is really responsive or fun. You learn that bad guys really like to hang around conveniently placed explosive tanks and other hazards.They also took other elements from Arkham games where they wanted you to use direction buttons to perform specific things like see-through vision and stealthing (Batman's smoke, but this time a cloaking spell).You have to unlock the fun gameplay elements (combat/specials) with skill points that you can miss, requiring you to constantly keep an eye out for the glowing orbs. And not all basic abilities are unlocked during the initial tutorial even though Haroona is supposed to have them at that point (e.g. the shield).In the end I'm mostly just disappointed. I'm sure they may try to at least fix some bugs, but even if it was completely bug-free the game design choices (gameplay, levels, animations) are not fun. They meet the company's checkboxes (e.g. "Make this wooden platform here to cross over") but they do so just for the purpose of making the player stay on a level longer and not to enhance the game or that area. The same goes for the combat, the action is not any fun and is a slower-paced mishmash of things everyone has seen before. They were unable to capture the essence of the trailers.They tried to throw too many different elements into the mix and missed out on the opportunity to craft their own identity. I think of all of the disappointments here, that one is the biggest of them all. The end result is that it will probably make for a better movie or show than what they attempted as a game.

Actually, I somehow read some discussions here on Steam before starting it for the first time, so I was more on the 'if it sucks I just uninstall it and haven't really lost anything' side.Played through it once (around 10 hours) and it was 'okay' more on the good side. So as I have to make a choice between recommend / do not recommend I say: recommend. It's by no means a 'must play', far from it. Also, if you are even slightly interested in this game wait for a 40% sale. In the end you will not have missed much if you didn't play this game, but if you somehow gain access to this game you might as well try it out.The gameplay develops nicely through the game as you unlock more skills and it actually shifts from 'be as stealthy as possible and delete enemies one by one' to 'jump right in the middle and alert everyone and then use all your skills to rip 'em apart while they come to you'. But you should do some light sidetracking / exploring, as unlocking skills requires a certain item which you won't collect automatically on your main path a lot of the time.Also: chapter 12 (of 13) is waaaaaaaaaay too long and a typical symptom of 'we need an hour more playtime for the statistics' without any other purpose or delivering anything new. The final boss fight is bad. Like, really really bad. Learn to dodge the same 4 or 5 attack patterns that he has and then use a certain attack when there is an opening and then repeat this for 5-7 minutes. Other than that I was enjoying most of the game, as the 'stepping' into enemies is an interesting and fun combat system.Of course the game isn't perfect. But it's also not trash. And despite what people say... it's not 'woke'. Yes, your main character doesn't look 'hot', but that's about it. No woke propaganda is pushed upon you (looking at you DA:TV), men are men, women are women and one of the more sympathetic characters from early in the game is an literally 'old white man'.7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an enjoyable, albeit clunky, stealth/fantasy adventure game. It is a Double AA game, so set your expectations accordingly. The graphics & cut scenes are *mid*, there are random (infrequent) frame rate dips, and sometimes the camera angle/perspective will completely cut off the character's head while they're speaking in some scenes. All that said, I actually had a lot of fun playing this game. The balance between stealth/supernatural powers is done well, and the ability upgrade tree is satisfying. Invisibility, shields, telekinesis, phasing, mind control, etc... all are really cool new additions to the stealth genre, and it was nice switching between all out offensive play styles, or a more stealthy approach ala Violet Parr from the Incredibles. While the graphics are pretty basic, certain parts look next-gen (ish) in the right lighting. The game looks better in fast paced combat than in exploration/cutscenes. I have a 4070 Super and was able to get it playing at 4K DLSS Quality, Ultra graphics, ray tracing enabled, and keep it mostly at 120FPS with the occasional frame dip/loading. On Steam Deck, it plays around 30 fps locked at low graphics/ balanced FSR, and 35-40 FPS on DLSS Performance. Still need to tinker to get a stable 40 fps setting.As it's a double AA game, I think the price should be closer to $29.99, but I've enjoyed my time with it so far despite it's shortcomings. Signed,-- not a weirdo from 4-Chan

_childDocuments_.review: Thought the game was pretty good overall. The combat and stealth are fun, though by the time you're about halfway through you'll probably be able to brawl through most encounters. The levels are fairly straightforward with room for some light exploration so you can find collectibles and things to upgrade your skills with, so it's worth taking time to go off the beaten path.When you're in fights or sneaking around, you can possess people for a short time and use them to attack other enemies or destroy generators connected to hazards that can make things harder for you. That stuff was really neat!The story was alright. It's might not be the most amazing one to be told, but it's decent and entertaining enough. There were parts of it that seemed like it didn't give us enough time with certain characters so that players could grow attached to them. That said, there are parts where the game lets you choose whether or not to go talk to some them, so some development can be missed if you're not careful.Do be prepared for some tough boss fights though. In a couple of them, it can feel like the game doesn't make it clear how you're supposed to beat them. Attacks are telegraphed and there's time to dodge them, but what to do when you have an opening wasn't always clear. So some of those, one in particular, you might find frustrating. Biggest gripe I've had is mainly in the animation department. The characters' faces don't seem very expressive/have too subtle expressions most of the time, with a weird "snap back" thing that happens in certain cutscenes. It doesn't kill the game for me, but it did take me out of it a little.If this game goes on sale, get it. It's a pretty decent single player game that can be challenging in certain places. And the mind control/possession mechanic is fun to play around with also.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is an honest review. I'm apparently one of only 6% that have actually finished the game, so at least I'm not totally full of bs. I think the game is decent enough to merit a playthrough. It does contain a few  unique game mechanics that you've never seen before (like the stepping ability that allows you to control enemies in a time warped state) and this is really neat. This is basically the main reason I would recommend the game. It's the same level of innovation that F.E.A.R brought with the slow-mo attack. Unfortunately, the developers missed a golden opportunity here since the enemies you'll encounter, and their "abilities" are very limited. As an example, what you can actually do on these stepped enemies are either hit the ground, flash forward with a spear or shoot one or a few rounds of pea-bullets that make the same amout of damage no matter where you hit. The feature is cool but it gets old very quickly since you'll end up doing the EXACT same thing over and over again, and since the enemies take so little damage from shooting each other, you'll more ofthen than not just use this ability to soften them up.Now, the main issue with the game is the linearity. And I'm not talking about the story or it not being open world here, I love games like Tomb Raider or Uncharted or any story driven FPS like Metro or what have you. But this game just does not give you any options. You MUST kill off all enemies in a certain area before you can move on, and you must face them with your fists. Because, who needs weapons when you can punch...Sneaking is heavily discouraged by all areas having alarms everywhere and even the innovative step feature is actively being hindered with most of the areas being blocked from it's use. This is sad as the game would have been so much more fun if we as players had the freedom to sneak around wherever (and not only in the 10% designated area) and if we could actually use our abilities. Oh and of course you can't step into an enemy currently taking damage (and it will cost you that stepping stone just because you tried).Another main issue with the game is the forced hand-to-hand combat. Your enemies will often have ranged weapons, but you'll be forced to attack them head on, with your fists. Even more absurd is the fact that some of the heavy-type enemies will explode upon death causing you to die or be at 1% HP in the process. I stopped counting the amount of times that after killing of 15 enemies, I died after killing the last heavy, since it exploded, and had to redo the entire scene AGAIN. A crazy design flaw imho.I'll also have to complain on the overall difficulty. My biggest misstake was obviously that I did not chose the story mode, because I've struggled A LOT with my survivability. I've had to replay certain areas ten to 15 times, as your character will die by 1-2 hits from a heavy and once your stepping stones are out and your "am" (ability to block and heal) is out, you're basically dead as your enemies will easily block any ordinary punch you throw at them. A possibility to change difficulty in game would have been nice, and saved me 6+ hours of replaying the same thing over and over... I might also add that I did use a controller for the entire playthrough, as that was "mandated" at game start. It's actually the first time I've used a controller on a PC game, as I'm not a console guy... And why do they have a save option in the menu? Because no matter when you save the game, you'll always just end up from the last autosave-checkpoint, which sometimes are far between and on weird locations. The companion characters are useless in combat. They will not draw any enemies and they will only do like 1% damage per 30 seconds on any enemy... Why?On two occations I was unable to progress from a certain area because the game bugged (eg companion character got stuck and was unable to move), and had to reload from last check point, but other than that no game breaking bugs that I noticed.Playing on epic graphics setting, the graphics is acceptable, but nothing more. It's far from top notch, and the quality can sometimes be on par with 2010 era games (water and foliage are REALLY bad at some places).The story was for me rather uninspiring and incoherent. To be honest, I don't get the setting or the characters or the enemies or the abilities and the other dimension. It's just a weird mess. And whenever the mandatory area fights are over, your companion will instantly nag you that you need to hurry up. Stray away from the path for five seconds and again, they will tell you to hurry up, we don't have time.TL;DRPlay it to experience some innovative cool mechanics, but beware of eventual boredom because of uninspiring story, forced linear gameplay (with the most boring puzzles you'll ever solve) with few options or exploration opportunities and overly hard difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh the glory of the "double A" game, the bizarre world of jank, graphical fidelity that feels a generation or 2 behind, and weird gameplay ideas that, while not always perfect or fully explored to their potential, still don't fail to give some enjoyment. This is a world of hidden gems; that said I'm not going to be hyperbolic here, Unknown 9 isn't necessarily a hidden gem but at the same time I would so far genuinely hesitate in calling it bad either.As I write this I want to add the context for the future that this game is this week's punching bag; it's not reviewing particularly well and there's also this bizarre hate campaign surrounding it for some silly reasons I won't get into, but I want it said that my enjoyment and recommendation of this game so far is not one that stems from a reactionary place; a lot of my growing up happened on the Xbox 360 and this style of linear single-player adventure with a bit of stealth, a bit of action, and a cool gameplay gimmick or 2 to spice things up was very common. I have a distinct nostalgia for that kind of game; stuff like Enslaved Odyssey to the West and Remember me; they weren't perfect and they were very much of a certain outdated era of design but there's a comfort in them. Unknown 9, for better and for worse, feels like it was plucked straight out of that era.Now let's just get this out of the way, graphically but especially in character models and facial animation, this game leaves a bad first impression; in motion during gameplay it's not that bad but the face rigs animate in a way that just feels off, I wouldn't normally care that much but the game opens on arguably one of the worst examples of this and it's just a bit odd of an initial moment to start the game on. But give the game a minute and a classic "walk behind your mentor as they teach you the basics" kind of opening and very quickly the game gets you your toolkit and into the flow of things. Now combat and stealth isn't the smoothest experience, you can feel a bit of stiffness to all of it but the tools the game gives you to enhance both combat and stealth is admittedly quite fun. Pushing and pulling enemies with powers is always fun in games, no exception to that here, and jumping into enemies to take over them and set up traps is also a nice novel edition that spices things up a bit. Add to that your basic distraction move, invisibility, a shield that can parry, a dodge button, and some basic melee combat and you've got a serviceable system with some fun gimmicks. It's not exceptional but being mid fight and suddenly pushing enemies into explosives and traps while taking over people to run them towards said traps to make them even more deadly... That's genuinely good fun.Now I've been playing this on the hardest difficulty and... I'm surprised this is the hardest, normally the hardest difficulty in these games is full of unbearably tanky enemies and one hit kills on you but it's shockingly balanced in a way that actually keeps me engaged and using all the tools at my disposal... I don't know what the other difficulties are like but I'm surprised this is the hardest because I can only presume that the other difficulties wouldn't have me feeling like I need to use all the tools in my arsenal like this one does; it's a surprisingly balanced difficulty so far and I actually recommend if you do play this to consider giving it a go, you will die but, at least so far it's felt really fair and honestly has for me opened up the game to being more fun by forcing me to engage with it properly.Still, it's early days for me, I'm about 5 hours in and, while I am having fun, the danger of giving me all my tools so early is potential repetition, I don't know how much this game will suffer from that but it is a strong possibility for any game like this, but I have been seeing the occasional new enemy type so, we'll see. As for the story to carry me through... It's fine, some of the writing is genuinely witty and snappy but overall, so far, it's nothing more than okay, I'm not massively compelled by it but I'm not skipping cutscenes either, it's not a particular highlight but some character interactions are fun so, it's okay.Now at full price I can see this game being a hard sell, I don't regret it so far but I got strong 360 era nostalgia and a budget that allows for it, it probably won't be worth full price for most people though but, on a sale, I honestly don't think it's that bad at all, it's definitely outdated. Its design and overall feel really does feel like it comes from over a decade ago but, honestly, it's nice to see a game like that appear again. These kind of linear single player stealth/action adventure games are a lost art, and while I'm sure some would say that that art was lost for a reason, it's not for me. I've been smiling my way through this one so far, the occasional jank ragdoll from pulling a sniper from a ledge just adding to the charm. I'm not going to tell you this is some great game but I would be lying if I called it a bad one so far. I enjoy it, imperfections and all, and sometimes that's all one can ask for.An addendum upon game completion:Yeah, nothing really to contradict here, the game stayed fun, didn't outstay it's welcome, higher difficulties definitely seem like the way to go, can lead to some minor frustrations but it forces you to use the mechanics to their fullest which is nice. That said the game never really rises above its own "okayness", there are hints and moments of level designs or fights that show that there is some more potential to be mined here but, for now, this is what we have and what we have is reasonable even if not exceptional.Honestly it's a shame that this game's sales and reviews are low because this is honestly the kind of game that I think needs sequels more than most, a sequel that can iron out the issues and really go for it and push the game forward even more mechanically, in the world we live in though I'd be very surprised, which is a shame, there's potential here that absolutely can be mined, and sadly this game only touches the surface of it.That said, on a sale, and/or if you have a bit of nostalgia/miss that old 360 experience, even if it brings the jank with it, I think there's an enjoyable experience to be had here; nothing exceptional but there are moments where it feels like there's another world out there where with more time this all comes together a bit more. But, maybe partially because of it's weird little awkward state it's in, I can't deny I was charmed by it and would be more than happy to see and play as Haroona again one day :)

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my entire review (& more!) here: Unknown 9 offers players a unique blend of stealth gameplay and supernatural powers in a mysterious early 1900s setting. You play as Haroona, a “Quaestor” able to manipulate Shade and travel through the mysterious Fold, tasked with stopping the Ascendants, a group meddling with forces that could doom humanity.The game’s core shines in its stealth and Shade mechanics. Players can sneak past enemies, use Shade abilities to control foes, and employ combat skills to survive. The Shade powers offer a refreshing twist, making for engaging encounters that feel reminiscent of Assassin's Creed and Star Wars. The skill tree offers meaningful upgrades across combat, stealth, and Shade abilities, giving flexibility in playstyle.While the environments are visually impressive, character animations and expressions feel dated, which detracts from immersion. Controls are mostly responsive, though some minor inconsistencies, like unintended movements during stealth, can be frustrating.With around ten hours of gameplay and limited replayability, Unknown 9 is an enjoyable but straightforward experience best suited for fans of supernatural stealth. It’s worth checking out—perhaps when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Not nearly as bad as Many of the reviews seem to want it to be.  looks alright most of the time, and spend the rest of the time either breathtaking or terrible. Hair shaders need some patches in general but the landscapes look gorgeous with some really cool set-pieces. seems to have a fair amount of cut content and definitely feels like some upper office meddling occurred. But overall it's solid and I enjoyed seeing it through.Pacing's quite bad and makes the whole progression of Haroona's arc and relationships to the other characters feel very rushed. Still ended up growing more attached to everyone than I expected though.Worldbuilding is stunning and intriguing.Only critique is that The Fold needs to be even weirder and less comprehensible then it already is. It's an unknowable place beyond time and space where all that is, could be and was is all happening at once. Confusing architecture should be the least of it. is fun but gets a bit repetitive towards the end. Much of the game is comprised of finding an area of enemies, sneaking in and taking down two or three of the most dangerous you can get close to, before getting caught and having to fight your way through the rest of them. There's enough enemy variety that you can get through the whole game before it starts becoming a problem. Combat it self is varied with an array of ranged or close attacks as well as plenty of environmental options for eliminating foes.The Stepping system that allows you to take control of enemies and use their unique ability's against each other is really cool and allows for much more diversity in your rampaging. You can use it to drag a group of enemy's together next to an explosive and then detonate it with another enemy's ground pound while a sharpshooter walks into the explosion and chips off some health of a target you couldn't get in the explosion. Then you just step back into your own body and watch the carnage. Great mechanic. Very fun all on it's own. Slightly horrifying lore implications since we later learn the person being stepped into is fully conscious and aware of what's happening while they're being stepped into.  Fun :) not worth the current full price, but good if you want to to spend 10-12 hours exploring and fighting your way though a beautiful world with a nice story and fun powers.

_childDocuments_.review: There are pros and cons - for me, the pros outweigh the cons by a significant bit - especially considering this is a AA studio, not a AAA studio. It reminded me a lot of Greedfall in that the story is really good but the character animation and cut scenes are meh (not in content, just visually).If you play games for the story - you'll probably really enjoy this one. If you play for the combat? Same thing. Pros - I really enjoyed the voice acting, the different play styles available (stealth and  combat), and the story. The story was interesting and, while it had some similarities to other games, had a fresh take on some old tropes which I really enjoyed. I love the characters - especially Luther. The world is gorgeous and it doesn't feel repetitive. I really enjoy hunting for the collectibles, too.Cons - Animation can get a bit wonky in cut scenes so the game can feel older than it is. The body models can behave oddly while standing or in cut scenes, and there are a few weird bugs (like my character being half in the ground multiple times during cut scenes). There's also a rendering thing in cut scenes for widescreen monitors where they "shrink" the scene to "fit" but it doesn't help - everything's still extra wide which can look odd at times. And OMG, Haroona's eyes are consistently wonky and creepy. It's frustrating because Luther and Mila are really well done - so I know the game company is capable.I finished the game last night. Here's the final take:Aside from some (minor) stuttering happening when coming out of cut scenes (I'm on epic quality) and 1 crash to desktop (I didn't have to repeat anything I'd just done - which was nice), and a couple weird moments where characters were half in the ground - I didn't have any technical issues or bugs. I was pleasantly surprised.I love the combat. I like being sneaky - and I really love that there's a way to fight...without actually fighting. Getting to turn bad guys on each other? Yes please. I had a blast blowing stuff up, having the baddies turn on each other, and generally just annoying the crap out of the masses sent to make Haroona's life hard.Each "DLC" outfit has a slightly different skin on top of having different clothes and hair - and the small picture doesn't do the outfits justice - at all. I ran around in the 20's style outfit for my game (Haroona's skin is disturbingly smooth for that one - but I like the clothes a lot) but I'm now rocking the Merc gear (looks fantastic and Haroona has the muscles to back the gear up which is cool). Low-key having fun switching the looks up now.I've seen a lot of feedback about the game being "woke" and it's really not? Unless you count different sexes and races simply existing as being "woke." Diversity is just part of the game but it's not a topic IN the game. As far as Haroona not being "hot" like Anya. Well, no. She's not - but that doesn't bug me anymore than Geralt, Kratos, Senua, etc not being hot made any difference in the games they were a part of. Aside from the weirdly wide-eyed stare, she's a normal person with average looks. I can tell Anya was the face model (there's a resemblance there), but they're definitely not twins. Overall, I'd give the game a 6.5 or 7 rating. Definitely worth playing - just not the game you take time of work to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly decent sim game, but it's lacking in many ways. $30 is steep for the state of this game and the lack of content. Probably the most disappointing part of this game is the progression. This is a broad overview of the types of progression you can make in this game. Probably the most disappointing part of the game. More expensive mowers don't equal more efficient mowing. The most expensive mowers are larger and can be more of a pain to operate than just going with a cheaper Zero Turn. All mowers also suffer from the cutting blades being bogged down by thick patches of grass. Even though you have this heavy duty mower at your disposal, it still gets bogged down just as often as the basic mowers. They have more speed which is more of a curse than a benefit in most cases. Better be light with the throttle or you'll unrealistically damage your engine and leave patches of grass.More like a menu simulator than an actual HQ. You can't visit this place, but you can purchase better HQ's which grant more bays to store your mowers. You can also upgrade your HQ to have more bays before purchasing the next tier of HQ that has even more bays.At the time of review, you can have up to 4 employees. You assign them before you tackle your own job and they complete their work at the same time you do. You can also train each employee (at a cost) to upgrade their stats to make them more efficient. I personally have not seen much benefit in upgrading their stats, because as you level them up, their pay increases, but previous jobs you have done stay at the same rate. Doesn't seem to scale very well unless you're always getting the higher paying jobs queued up.This is your reputation. This levels up as you complete jobs, spend money on Marketing, and also stacks with employees completing jobs. As your reputation increases, the more valuable jobs start popping up. Big oof here. The biggest problem is the lack of sensitivity sliders and button mapping. It's 2021, there's no excuse for not having the ability to customize my controls. The lack of Thrustmaster Wheel support is also a big letdown. I specifically went with a Thrustmaster wheel because of the belt-driven drive which is far superior to the Logitech gear-driven drives. My other issue is also the lack of TrackIR support in a sim like this. Some mechanics that I just don't like or need improvement. This could probably be avoided if I had a weed whacker for trimming. Since I don't, I have to slam my tractor into various obstacles that probably have bigger hit boxes than they should. Some of the more complicated yards have more objects to collide with too. Some bushes even act as a solid wall and behave like a metal barrier. Each collision also counts as a penalty and decreases the value of the contract. I can usually offset this by doing the Ground Check quickly, but that's not how this should be done. Keep in mind, collisions are more of an issue with the more complex jobs that have more obstacles. Trees are the lesser issue for me, except for some of the bigger tractors that collide with the branches. These jobs really have no place in this game. You'll get a job worth a laughable £30 and all you do is pick up some garbage. The job also won't leave your queue until you complete it either. Some jobs require you to get a perfect stripe rating to get the full value of the job. This is just way too high considering the very sensitive controls. You also need a specific mower that has a stripe attachment to complete. I've only noticed a couple Zero Turns with this ability. I was able to complete a few of these jobs with a 97%-98% rating, but got docked £10. This isn't much off the contract, but lets be real, is a human going to dock my pay because my lines were 2%-3% from being perfect? This happens way too often. There is no visual indicator that I need to control my speed, there's just a meter around your speed that indicates the grass is thick. The grass looks the same as every other patch, but I need this meter just to let me know it's thicker. Not a fan of this mechanic at ALL.As of writing, this was added to Mouse and Keyboard controls, but not a controller. This is a giant pain when cutting thicker grass patches since this bogs down your mower and also leaves patches of uncut grass behind you. This isn't a bad sim game, but it needs polish. There's hardly any graphics options and the performance is a little weak for a game of this scale. In my opinion, this is still an Early Access game. I put time in this game, and I'm not seeking a refund, but I wish I would have waited for more updates before jumping in.

_childDocuments_.review: This is possibly one of the poorest attempts at an authentic simulator I've ever had the misfortune of experiencing. I'm biased as a professional lawnmower, but that only makes it painfully obvious that the developers of this game have never as much as touched a lawnmower in their lives, perhaps even grass. The game's design is poor and unoptimized, and the DLC is uninspired and gimmicky. But let's talk about the positive parts of the game first. ...Now that that's out of the way - The controls are absolute garbage: I understand that this game is intended for use with a controller or gamepad of some kind, but the m&k keybindings are low effort at BEST. The camera is incredibly wonky and sits on a hair trigger, requiring constant monitoring so that your camera won't find itself 6 inches into a flower bed. The movement controls are similar, while clearly designed for an analog joystick, you're either moving at full speed or not at all. The menus suck: settings are impossible to navigate, nothing is labelled, and the way settings are applied makes it way too easy to screw up your settings with no way to know which ones are screwed up. The settings typically governed by a slider are instead essentially a list of 5 or 6 increments of which there are no intermediate steps. Don't want your camera sensitivity at 60%? here's 70%, take it or leave it. The grass... isn't grass? I can understand the need for a simple grass texture from a resource-economy perspective, but the grass in the game doesn't look even close to real grass, nor does it behave as such. In the real world, grass will lay down, changing its shade depending on how the sun reflects off it (this is what creates the nice satisfying stripe patterns), but in game, there are certain things that attempt to mimic this behavior, but it's rare and inconsistent when it does attempt do use this effect.The lawnmowers kinda suck: the models are cool, don't get me wrong, but they simply do not operate the way real lawnmowers do. Their motors will intermittently overload for . Throttle is all-or-nothing, and grass discharge methods don't behave realistically. You can damage blades by engaging them on a flat surface? Not sure where that one came from. The selection is poor: There are only a few options for lawnmowers, and even fewer trimmers. While there are cool options, there are countless other professional brands that are completely unrepresented, which seems like an unfortunate circumstance considering the game offers a "career" mode which appears to emulate a larger scale professional operation. In my opinion, this game should be titled something more fitting, such as Lawnmowing Simulator Simulator, because all the mowing you do is in name only. If you want a satisfying simulator game with good mechanics and a better experience, go play PowerWash Sim. I'm not a professional power washer by any stretch of the imagination, but at least the game feels good to play. I regret every second of the thirty minutes I spent on this game. If it receives heavy overhauls to basically every core system of gameplay, I'll consider playing again, but as for now, the game is LEAGUES away from being a good , much less a good lawn mowing game.

The way the mowers bog down when going through thick grass is awesome! You have to slow the mower just like in real life!-Damage is on point too. Running over flowers, yup that happens for real when mowing. Bumping into objects that cause damage to your mower, yup again on point.-Garbage picks, oh man this is how I start a job for real with my company.-Employees that call in sick or go on vacation unexpected. This is all stuff a landscaping company deals with all the time. -Equipment maintenance. Keep your mowers in top condition and cuts will go much smoother. Is this a sim or is it real? Hmmm?I am very happy with how the game works, but it definitely could use a few improvements. The devs seem to have a roadmap laid out that will bring in string trimmers and backpack blowers. I'm looking forward to these additions as they should bring in a variety of new jobs. Leaf cleanups I hope!One feature that I hope will be introduced later is possibly being able to drive to the job site. As this is a big part of a landscapers day. Travelling back and forth from job site to the shop would be greatly welcomed.So in conclusion, if you are a landscaper this game is pretty satisfying. As a casual gamer who's looking for excitement. Prob not so much. This is a simulation of running a lawn cutting business. In real life it can be very repetitive, much like this game. P.S. Get the SCAG Turf Tiger II mower.

_childDocuments_.review: Would not recommend this game, it lacks a lot of depth. Jobs are samey, with no real variation between maps. There is little motivation to work your way through the jobs short of getting better mowers. By the end I had a couple of workers and would just assign them to mowing jobs while taking the "trash collection" jobs myself just so I could progress without having to sit and mow myself -- at that stage I'd realised the novelty of the game had worn thin.There is just not a lot to do in this game; the business management side is lacking, there is no other stuff to do like weed whackers/blowers, etc. and it would benefit greatly from more interesting jobs (e.g., cut a golf course with specialist equipment needed and different cut heights, etc.). You also don't have a truck/trailer or drive to any jobs, you just accept a contract and you're magically teleported somewhere -- lots of missed opportunities to actually make a good game. Feels a lot like I'm playing a "Steam Workshop" game that's currently in alpha with 90% of the features missing.I will also say, for a game that is literally based on mowing a lawn, the textures/graphics for the grass are terrible. There is no ability to see different grass heights short of cut/not cut and it's not very satisfying to look at cut grass. Have a look at some screenshots and you'll see what I mean. There are no graphics around grass being thrown from a mower or stuck on wheels or anything either.In terms of skill/progression -- the only variation or challenge in this game is needing to modulate the forward-speed on your mower so you don't "bog" it on long grass (in reality this is tedious, and not fun). Why they can't set cruise-control or a maximum speed is beyond me.Note1: I played this "off-Steam" for around 8 hours or so before getting the game on Steam so I could access the latest patch, so the 90 minutes played is not entirely accurate. I have since refunded on Steam.Note2: Looks like they've just released a roadmap which includes some of this complaints, but I feel like it's too little, too late. These should have been in the game from launch whilst the novelty of playing was still fresh.

_childDocuments_.review: Lawn Mowing Simulator is the first game of its kind I've tried. You mow lawns. That's it. There's no race against the clock, no battle mechanic, no necessary missions or need to complete anything. There are challenges there if you want them, and a business-running side of things that was an interesting touch. But you don't really feel the stress of running that business. There are no contract completion deadlines or angry clients that get in your face when you accidentally back into a fence or run over a flower. There's no stress to this game - at all.And that's what I love about it. There's something about the take-it-easy vibe of this game that I really enjoy, even when you're just starting the lawn-mowing business. There are multiple mowers you can unlock just through playing the game (earn enough money, buy the mower), which I like a lot more than having mowers as DLC. And of course, each yard, lawn, and park is beautifully rendered. This is a good game to play when you're just looking to relax. Put some music on in the background and mow away!

_childDocuments_.review: I like a lot of simulator games, even ones that take on routine, boring tasks.  I drove back and forth over wheat fields in Farming Simulator for hours and hours and there's kind of a zen relaxation about the whole thing.  I know some people get that same simple enjoyment out of mowing their lawn so I figured that might translate well to a game.Well it might.  But it doesn't.  At least not here.  The controls and camera make that experience impossible, you're far too busy trying to fiddle around with everything to ever drop into that relaxing "zone."  Watch the play throughs, not only are they steering but they're constantly moving the camera around in a frantic two stick dance that rivals a dual stick shooter game.  (The weed whacker is even more of a nightmare.)  But the one thing that's most unforgivable for me is that they didn't get the grass right.  In a lawn mowing simulator.  Anyone who enjoys mowing their lawn will tell you they like that OCD thing of making nice, neat little patterns in the cut grass and this doesn't have that.  In fact, it doesn't even give you that satisfaction of a job well done because the lawns actually look worse after they've been mowed than they did before you started.  When you show up to a job it looks like grass.  When you're done it looks like little yellow hair stubble on a giant dirt face.I got this as part of a bundle but if you're considering it as a straight buy, I recommend a pass.  Go out and mow some real grass.  It'll be way more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, but I actually have very mixed feelings about it because it was not what I anticipated.First, cruise control is not explained in the tutorial / test drives.  Without it, you'll have to mow at the speed of a NASCAR qualifier, which will result in damage to your equipment and the area you are mowing.  On a keyboard, cruise control is activated with TAB.  Then use W and S to increase / decrease your speed.  In order to not start cruise control at max speed, press W and then immediately press TAB - if done quickly, you can get cruise control turned on without it being at maximum speed.  I found this out by reading comments from other players and then experimenting.  Something this important should be explained in game.    Second, I personally find some aspects of the game to be challenging for no reason - such as being given a short time limit to find and remove things you wouldn't want to hit with a lawnmower.  As if a homeowner would come out with a stopwatch and give me short amount of time to prepare to mow . . . If this happened, in real life, I would tell the ba$t4rd to mow their own grass.  Since this time limit is a feature of the game, I must tolerate it or skip this step and lose out on money and experience points.  I expected to have some sort of schedule, an in 'mow this lawn on Tuesday,' not prepare in less than five minutes and finish the job in 23 minutes.  I can't imagine a world in which a homeowner, or anyone, would care whether it took me 23 minutes or 45 minutes, so for me, it would improve the game if we could do away with the timer.  If I am to finish some job in less than an hour, why can I only do one job per day?You can highlight the areas where you haven't mowed yet if you hold down the Ctrl key for a moment, but this doesn't work while you are walking or driving, unless cruise control is activated.  Then there are times, early game, when you are offered only 'eco' contracts but the player has no way of getting 'eco friendly' equipment.  I read other players experiences with this and it seems that the solution is to dump your game, start a new one, and mow better this time - and in this game, better usually means faster, not neater.  Neatness counts for little in this game, when I would argue that one of the main reasons for mowing is to maintain a neat and tidy appearance.  Speed seems to be the main focus in this game.Another thing that makes me scratch my head:  I am fined for damage to flowers.  I have no problem with there being a penalty for damage, but a 'fine?'  What sort of city flower authority is issuing these fines?  I suppose it could be an HOA or something, but it just doesn't make sense to me.  It would make more sense if I had to discount my services, or I didn't get a tip, or some other form of penalty.  Each time I see a "fine" penalty on the screen, I imagine the flower police taking me to court.Perhaps I'm just not computer savvy, or perhaps the game controls aren't very intuitive, but I had to google how to exit the game.  The menu does not make it clear to me.I do like mowing the yards.  The equipment itself looks good.  I like maintaining the equipment as well, as it needs to be fueled, repaired, charged, etc, and these aspects are included in a way that adds to the game and isn't the least bit tedious.  I like being able to hire others and assign jobs to them.  It was a nice touch that the devs included a bit of personality for the job applicants.  The scenery is nice.  Since I already bought the game and it's refund time expired, I'll keep playing, but I honestly would not have purchased it had I known more about it.  Some players like a challenge and would find a game boring without it - if that's you, the things I've mentioned are 'features, not bugs' but if you are looking for a casual game where you can zone out and immerse yourself in mowing, I would say that this isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.  I really enjoyed power wash simulator so I thought I would enjoy this game as well but there are a few things that make this un-enjoyable.1) The Electric Mower thing.  I saw this comment in other reviews before I purchased and thought people were just whiny because they didn't like the update, a mower had negative stats,  or they were ideologically against all things electric motors for political reasons.    My issue is none of these things.  In fact I never got to use the electric mowers but instead after just 3 yards my campaign became soft locked because I was offered only yards that 'required' an electric mower to complete.    I couldn't buy an electric mower because my garage didn't have space, I couldn't sell my existing mower to buy one because it prevents me from selling my only mower.   I clicked to expand my garage but it takes some sort of in-game time which I guess only passes when mowing lawns for your garage to be upgraded.   I started to down the path of creating a new campaign and figured that I would just select an electric mower as my first mower and avoid this problem entirely but It wouldn't let me select that as a first mower. I think Electric Mowers could have been done well.  They could have offered a different type of mower with different pros/cons.  Perhaps it is cheaper to run (no gas, less maintenance).  But using it might bother customers because of noise or you have to spend time to recharge it needing to switch mowers.  Having lawns be electric only was really bad idea especially when it can soft-lock the campaign.2) No Saving mid-lawn.   This is a major drawback is you can't stop and save your progress on a lawn and come back and play again later to finish up.   This is just another thing that takes away from the casual nature I hoped this game would have.3) Business management is too much in-the-weeds.  I can appreciate some level of business management but this just goes over the top in what I was hoping to be a causal game.- Garage space (don't like it, would rather infinite all the time)- Advertising (don't want to think about that, just want to select from a list of jobs)- Loans ( would rather just have expensive items be unavailable in campaign until you save up for it)- Employees ( what is this an automation game? _childDocuments_.review: Having played for over 11 hours of the game, I can honestly give a fair review on it. For the price you pay, and for the type of game, its not bad overall. There are a few niggling issues which need to be addressed especially in the beginning phases of the game. Think of this game as repetitive, a start up business working the same client over and over again, where you can do the same gardens numerous times as you level up. My biggest issue with the game is the ability to control your acceleration of the mowers. In fact, you cant control it as everything works at one speed. This is where in the problem lies. The engines overload very quickly regardless of the type of mower you are using. Its extremely frustrating to move, slow down, move, slow down in order to prevent your engine overheating. When you earn next to nothing, but end up having to pay so much for repairs and maintenance, all you're actually earning is RP. It takes the "fun" out of the game entirely. The other thing is that you as the player will always be cutting, and the only way to assign contracts, requires you (the player) cutting with an employee, instead of just sending the employee (whom you can level up) to the contract to complete. I dont see then why levelling up is necessary, albeit to ensure less wear and tear on your equipment, and increase RP and cash. Yes, thats enough, but as a businessman, surely you could send your employees out on their own?PRO: Fun in the beginning; Growing your "Empire"; Vehicle selectionsCON: Too repetitive, especially in the beginning; Acceleration cannot be adjusted; Engine overload saps the fun out of the game; No option to send employees on contracts solo without you doing it like a real simulator should doOverall, for what you pay, you get it. But is it worth it? No, not really. The farm simulator, city simulators offer so much more than this. Ive only done 11 hours, and I just dont want to play anymore, because the frustration of the engine overloading so easily, makes me stop contracts anyhow minimising my income and RP. I think if this were addressed by the developers, I may play again.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game overall, with a few gripes.+ Mowing is genuinely fun. It feels great and the sense of accomplishment is real.+ Varied, colorful, detailed, and realistic environments. Variety could be better but there’s enough.+ Great machines! Using real brands helps with immersion.+ Maintenance management is fun, and career mode as a whole is fairly well done.- The engine damage is a fun killer. With no way to manage throttle (either max or off), you have to severely reduce speed to avoid damage. This makes mowing a LOT more of a chore than it should be. The option to turn this off would be so much welcome, especially when you want all the chill from mowing with NONE of the tension.- Lackluster physics. _childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a lawn mowing simulator. NO riding lawnmower in the world works the way the ones in this game do. Because the engine will overheat after 1-2 seconds of use, you have to drive 1-2 feet, then stop for 2 seconds to wait for the engine heat to come down, then drive another 1-2 feet, then stop for 2 seconds, etc. Repeat 500 times. If you try to just drive for longer than 1-2 seconds, the engine heat will go into the red, and the mower will shut down, damaging the engine. Since the throttle only has 2 settings - all the way up, or all the way down (which means you can't engage the mower), you can't set it at, say, half, and mow continuously with the engine at a lower heat level. It's all or nothing. And all the way up means the engine overheats every 1-2 seconds of mowing. Absolutely infuriating trying to mow a huge lawn when you can only drive for a foot before having to stop and wait for 2 seconds for the engine to cool down. Takes forever. And because it takes so long to mow a lawn with this start-stop-start-stop method, you burn through a tank of gas mowing one lawn (and probably damage your engine), so after you get paid, you burn up half your earning in repairs and refueling. Now imagine doing this for 10-20 lawns. Ugh. NO fun whatsoever. The British designers of this game have apparently never ridden a REAL riding lawnmower, made in the U.S., where you can actually turn it on, lower the blades, and actually DRIVE the thing continuously and mow an entire lawn without having to STOP the vehicle every foot or two without the engine "overheating." No such thing in a real lawnmower.  If this is how British lawnmowers are made, I imagine most Brits don't bother mowing their lawns, or they just buy some sheep or goats to keep the grass short. Would NOT recommend this, unless you enjoy wasting a lot of time starting and stopping every 1-2 feet. All it did for me was tick me off.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this game, YET. Bugs:The game is full of bugs that needs to be fixed before you can play it properly. There are controls on the steering wheel though I can't find a way to see them. Steering wheel:I'm really glad that steering wheels got added however it seems like they have just binded the wheel keys with the keyboard controls. in the Stiga it makes the steering  indirect meaning that if you turn the wheel 90° the in game wheel wont turn 90° and it reacts much slower. As per the Knight its literly undrivable. it's really hard to explain but when you turn the wheel to the left its like clicking A and when youre not moving the wheel even if its turned its like not clicking any button so it straightens itself up. _childDocuments_.review: 4.9/10I REEEEAAAALLLY want to give this game a 8/10. It's enjoyable, mellow, the graphics are decent, the controls are fairly clean, but the one factor that really drags this down is that there's just SO LITTLE content.The NPC helpers all look nearly identical. There's only a few locations. Not much difference in the mowers. Very few peripherals. Finally, the controls aren't flexible enough to allow for fine controlling your speed. I only ever use one mower because I never NEED to actually use anything else. Even if the game recommends a smaller mower, it doesn't matter because the entry to the lawn is wide enough for the big mower. I got down some basic patterns and now I burn through every yard with minimal effort, not that there's many yards to begin with.When I used the my dad's riding mower as a kid, it had 5 gears, reverse, AND you could control the speed and go as slow as you need to do precision steering. That mower was built in 1978. How is it that in this game modern riding mowers can't do that? On a game pad!On top of all of that, there's really no peripherals to include. Like, what about mow and perforate? What about upgrading your bag collector to a bagging trailer? What about a fertilizing trailer? What about pulling ACTUAL weeds?Finally, the game lacks playable content and even the expansion only adds a little more material. I was hoping for loads more yards, really challenging yards on sloping surfaces or mowing a hedge maze or some silly stuff like trying to mow a dinosaur exhibit where the dinos are real and you have to avoid them or they'll knock you off and damage your mower (won't hurt you, just slow your process down).There's so much more and so many fun things that could be done in this game that the devs just chose not to do and it's just flat out disappointing. I like the game, I really want to recommend it to friends and others, but at this time...no...not yet.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of games like House Flipper and PowerWash Simulator, I was looking forward to trying this one! It did not exceed my expectations. In fact, it barely met them. Getting one of those two games is worth more than paying for this one. Only buy this game if you're in the mood for a semi-tedious gaming experience with no real payoff. If you want decoration, get House Flipper. If you want to make something clean, get PWS. There are quite a few other sims out there that are pretty fun, but this one is not...all that great. It's also not that bad. It's a solid middle-of-the-road type game as long as you go into it thinking you'll be disappointed.This game is entertaining enough if it's the type of thing you're looking for, but for my money, I'd go power wash instead. If you've already finished PWS and you're in the mood for something sort of similar but not as satisfying, this is a good replacement, but don't spend too much or you'll regret it.Since I only have a binary choice of thumbs up or thumbs down with my review, I am going to put a thumbs up. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for July 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. Watching the progress bar slowly tick up, trying to perfect each lawn and avoid damaging the grass, or flowers, and watching the lawn slowly get cut by each subsequent pass entertains me. _childDocuments_.review: So, I bought this game not really expecting much. I figured it was just another simulator game wanting to get in now with other simulators being popular. I figured I'd try it, and I'd most likely end up refunding it. I was pleasantly surprised to find that this game actually holds up. There are some good, and some bad. I enjoy the gameplay loop this game offers. It's simple, yet enough to keep me wanting to come back. You simply go from job to job, mowing lawns, and avoiding the flowers. You earn money, then spend it on upgrading equipment, hiring employees, and upgrading your garage. This gameplay loop is very similar to other simulator games, so nothing too shocking there. The mowers do actually handle like real mowers, at least the couple I've used. Stopping very quick without any throttle applied, and getting up to speed quick. The sound design I feel could use some work, as sometimes it's not the best. It's not bad either, just needs some improvement to be on the level of the likes of ETS2. I'm not a big fan of having the mowers condition constantly on screen, but I am a fan of minimal UI in simulators, so others may not mind this as much, I'm also not the biggest fan of the time bonus stuff. I feel this system could be traded out for a skill tree instead. Being timed for cleaning the yard/lawn, and then the time bonus for mowing faster just isn't for me, and I think a skill tree would make the game just that little bit more fun for me. Overall though, this is a solid game. If you're on the fence about it, I would recommend giving the game a go. It's a relaxing game, with something to make you actually want to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, but ultimately not sustainable. This is not good game design - PowerWash Sim has a button you can tap for constant spray. That is much better, and there is no reason why it isn't implemented here. Additionally, the devs seem to only care about sales and profit. They have released paid dlc since the base game came out, but have not delivered on promised content expansions for base game. The controller comment I had above could be easily fixed, but dev presence on their discord is nonexistent. Their known issues list has not been updated since August 2021, this is unacceptable. I am saddened that I can't recommend this, because it is a fun game, but suffers from poor design and lack of follow-through.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. Lawn Mowing Simulator Review. Here goes. You start by choosing an avatar for your gender male or female. After this, you name your company. Then you name your player.  After that you can choose to dual colour your T-Shirt, the main part and the stripes. You can colour your hat. You can choose from a list of Logos to place on either front only, back only or both on your T-Shirt. Unfortunately you can not change the colour of your trousers, add jackets or gloves or change any clothing to different ones. To enjoy the simulation of driving fully you really need to use a Joypad or gamepad controller, preferably Xbox controller. It will be so much easier and less frustrating when it comes to throttle control and steering. PC keyboard is not ideal. I have been using a Xbox Elite V2 and its so much more controllable and comfortable.You start next to your trailer with the tractor you chose to test drive on the trailer. and pick-up truck. Next the game asks you to do a test drive in the first and cheapest Stiga yellow tractor with or without a tutorial at your choice. After you do a bit of mowing you don't have to complete the job. You are taken back to a menu where you can buy the Stiga or test drive or buy another tractor. I think there is a choice of 3 mowers you can demo.Simulation is very good. The Stiga is like the cheapest first tractor which has a 33cm cutting blade and its pretty quick. Throttle control is either idle or max rpm which you control with d pad. You also control the Cutting blade height with the d pad too. Left Joystick for steering. A to get on tractor. X to start the tractor and x again to start cutting blade. LT for brake and RT for accelerate. A to empty bag. The first task is a ground check. You have a set timer in which to check the garden for littering objects. After this the main timer starts your job and the time is an amount of reasonable time it should take to do that particular garden. Each job is different, with a different garden. different pay, different obstacles. There are penalties and fines for destroying flower / beds, bumping walls, gates, buildings and also if you turn too fast you can damage the grass and mark it by scraping marks of mud. You will be charged off of your wage and loose RP reputation points for damages. You can over rev your mower,, strain and damage the engine, run low on fuel, damage the cutting blades. After each job you can perform maintenance with fuel fill up, blade replacement, engine repair. You can also run out of fuel on a job and i think you are just required to pay more for quick repair or replacement of anything.Unfortunately time is wasted when you have to keep making a trip to empty the grass bag. But this can make the practice and exercise of the challenge of the time and duration of the job. It's something you can improve on by finding quicker routines. The camera is like a moving camera, there are 1st person and 3rd person cameras aswell and a chase camera which i'm not so keen on as it moves rather than staying fixed view.Back in the menu, you can shop for a new mower, advertise to hire new employees for your business, upgrade your headquarters, add more garages. There is a challenges menu where you will probably be required to complete objectives and tasks to beat the timer clock as you rank up with each job that you do, more challenges will be added. I think the game can easily be made better. It is both fun and rewarding and relaxing though. I would definitely give this game a 5 star for being very satisfying and relaxing. This type of game is very good for when you want to lay back with something simple and easy to enjoy without too much concentration but have fun.Overall i am very positively engaged in this kind of game and i really only have good things to say about the game. If i could say anything, it would be what the developer could do in the future, You know if there is a LMS2 at some point. My ideas for a next game would be one with a more of an open world type feel, where you can customise your character more uniquely and buy a vehicle or trailer and drive yourself to homes or business or your own headquarters. I am sure there is a ton of ideas from other players feedback in the community. I look forward to new DLC, additions and updates to the current game and i am very happy with the direction they have started in.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 9/12/2022:  Originally I said "not recommended" but a recent update smoothed out the GAMEPAD controls a little bit... just enough that the game is actually playable.  Still super twitchy on the steering and throttle though.  But not as bad as it was, I mean originally it was IMPOSSIBLE to drive in a straight line, kept overheating the engine from accidentally giving it too much gas, crashing into walls and flower beds constantly.  Recent update patch improved it... but still twitchy.  And still HORRIBLE on keyboard controls.TL;DR bottom line: so USE A GAMEPAD.  Even gamepad has really twitchy throttle and steering and camera angles, so get into the "Controller Configuration" from the Steam Library and tweak the sensitivities and such, it's the only way to make it possible to drive the mower without murdering hundreds of flowers or crashing into all the walls.  For the love of god, DO NOT PLAY ON KEYBOARD.Full review:Gonna split this review into three sections - first will be general description of the game, second will be what I LIKE about it, and finally will be what I DISLIKE about it.  Three game modes to choose from:Career Mode - build your own lawn mowing company.  Hire employees, take jobs to earn cash, and level-up to unlock the mowers and job sites for use in Free Mow plus unlock new Challenge Mode jobs.Challenge Mode - Mow a lawn, but there are special rules.  Some have limited fuel for your mower, some have a time limit, some have different rules.Free Mow - pick a mower, pick a job site, and just mow.  No pressure, no time limit, no economy or financial reports to worry about.As a concept, this game had a GOOD IDEA.  It's kind of relaxing to just kick back and drive a lawn mower.  Visually this game LOOKS GOOD.  You won't see most of it because you're focused on the grass under your feet, but the background art is actually really cool.  There are hot air balloons, neighbors walking around, even police cars driving by sometimes.  And the actual scenery - the fields and little towns you can see beyond the fence - look nice.Sound design is great.  The mower makes an actual lawn mower noise.  The blades have a separate sound effect layered over that when you turn on the mower deck.  The engine will rev up and even stall out if you run too fast through thick grass.  The weed trimmer has its own set of sound effects.  Even when you crash into something, the sound effects are SOLID - you'll wince when you ram the neighbor's car and say to yourself "Oh, that'll leave a mark."  Music is less than awesome, but not terrible.  Utterly forgettable, but not intrusive upon the gameplay.There are even ambient sounds like birds, dogs barking, neighbors hammering things... it sounds like the world is actually alive around you.The entire play style here is "casual."  There are no winners or losers, no hidden secrets that you need to find to unlock ultimate weapons or whatever.  Just kick back and cut the grass.Career Mode is not too difficult, it's nearly impossible to fail.  You really have to try to lose.  But at the same time, it takes a long time to succeed in terms of being able to afford the next HQ upgrades and bigger lawn mower machines.  It's a nice balance.Free Mow - is just totally zen.Challenge Mode is like Free Mow, but with some added level of difficulty because of the special conditions.  It's not "impossibly hard" but you really have to strategize and work for it if you want to clear a challenge.Each job will last anywhere from 30 minutes to 3 hours.  And you CANNOT SAVE YOUR GAME in the middle of a job.  So if you are going to play this game, plan ahead and make sure you have NOTHING TO DO for a few hours.The camera angles are crap.  The 3rd person camera keeps getting stuck behind trees so you can't see what you're doing, or it glitches to weird angles that make it impossible to see if your mower is actually hitting the right spot on the grass.  The first person camera isn't useful at all either, because you can't see the edges of your mower deck - which you NEED TO SEE THAT in order to aim your mower such that you don't leave any mohawk stripes of tall grass behind you between laps.The controls... are just... TERRIBLE.  Steering is so sensitive, the mower likes to snap to certain angles and you can't make smaller course adjustments.  Which means you're going to crash into a lot of things and run over a lot of flowers, both of which will add FINES to your end of mission score, reduce the money you earn in career mode, and make you fail certain challenge missions.  This is also the case when walking around with the trimmer, trying to do small areas and get around edges of flower beds so you don't accidentally murder all the flowers with your mower... the controls are so jumpy you end up killing more flowers with the trimmer than with the mower.  And the accelerator on the mower is super glitchy.  Sometimes you put the pedal to the metal and only do 1 mph.  Other times you put feather-light pressure on it and you shoot off like a rocket.  It's hard to steer with the three smallest mowers in the beginning of the game.  Unlocking bigger and faster mowers makes the problems 100x worse, it just becomes practically impossible to play.  Seriously, this game has the twitchiest controls I've ever encountered.  It's like the main character is trying to be a landscaper but he has both epilepsy and Parkinson's disease, and he's a psychopath.   This can be SOMEWHAT fixed by going into the controller config from the Steam Library and changing the sensitivity and response curves for the L-stick, R-stick, and RT buttons... but you'll never get it perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game isn't that terrible, but I would still classify it as "beta" or "early access" level of polish. I also wish there were more precise speed controls.The balance for career mode could use some tweaking.  The game has a whole system for basically running your own lawn care company, hiring employees, managing equipment, and setting up multiple jobs/contracts each day.  Unfortunately it forces you to mow each day just to progress time, and if you are looking forward to more of the management style of game play you still have to take the time to mow yourself; could be a turn-off for some.  Ultimately if you can get this game on sale it isn't the worst way to spend your money if you enjoy these types of zen games, but it does appear as if the developers have stopped supporting the game, and as such I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from PowerWash Simulator, there's some things about this game that immediately stand out like a sore thumb. I understand maintenance is a large part of using any equipment, but what I liked about PowerWash Simulator is they ignored the aspects about actual power washing in real life that aren't fun. That's the whole point of making games - to make it fun. This game misses the mark on that note, and it ruined the experience for me entirely.My engine constantly overheats and it's surprisingly more boring than I initially thought to cut grass because it lacks depth. In PowerWash Simulator, you have different equipment for different purposes, and there's a lot of depth of dirt that requires extra attention. Here, however, you simply set your cut height and go. It doesn't matter what equipment you use as it doesn't even require that you use a weed eater at the end of every job if you managed to get most of the grass in the open with a riding lawn mower. I never even touched a weed eater despite it being a required piece of equipment for every contract.Ultimately, the lack of importance in equipment, the overbearing maintenance of your equipment, and lack of depth in cutting grass ultimately make this an extremely repetitive and boring experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently tried out Lawn Mowing Simulator on Steam, hoping for a relaxing and immersive experience that would transport me to a peaceful virtual garden. However, what I encountered was nothing short of a frustrating and mind-numbing ordeal.From the very beginning, it became apparent that this game lacks any form of excitement or engaging mechanics. The concept of mowing lawns may sound relaxing on the surface, but Lawn Mowing Simulator fails to capture the essence of this experience. Instead, it turns the simple act of lawn care into a repetitive and monotonous task that quickly becomes a tiresome chore.The game's mechanics are a major source of frustration. The controls feel clunky and unresponsive, making it difficult to maneuver the lawnmower precisely. Something as basic as cutting grass should be intuitive and smooth, but Lawn Mowing Simulator manages to make it an arduous and aggravating endeavor. It feels like battling with the controls is more of a challenge than the actual task of mowing the lawn itself.Furthermore, the lack of variety in gameplay becomes painfully apparent after only a few minutes of playing. You're essentially doing the same repetitive task over and over again, without any meaningful progression or rewarding moments. The absence of diverse environments, tools, or even a semblance of a storyline further contributes to the game's mind-numbing nature.Graphically, Lawn Mowing Simulator falls short of expectations as well. The visuals are lackluster and uninspiring, failing to capture the lushness and vibrancy of a real garden. It's disheartening when you realize that even the virtual lawns you're tending to lack any sort of visual charm or attention to detail.The audio design is another letdown. Instead of providing a soothing soundscape to accompany the supposed relaxation of mowing lawns, the audio elements are bland and repetitive. The absence of a well-crafted soundtrack or ambient nature sounds only exacerbates the tedium of the gameplay.In conclusion, Lawn Mowing Simulator is a prime example of a game that promises relaxation but ultimately delivers nothing but frustration and boredom. The lackluster mechanics, repetitive gameplay, and underwhelming visuals make it a tedious chore rather than an enjoyable escape. If you're seeking a genuinely relaxing experience or any semblance of excitement, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. Save your time and money for a game that actually delivers on its promises.
