I am hopeful more wheels are supported soon, but I have heard that its not very well done and there is little to no force feedback from the start.2. Only riding mowers. While I love riding mowers, and love the zero turns in this game, as well as the satisfaction they provide, they really could have and should have added weed whackers (edge trimmers) and push mowers.3. Multiplayer. As with almost any sim game, multiplayer would have sent this game's replay value through the roof. It would be amazing, even if it was just simply having a buddy hop on a mower and help you out. Think about farming simulator when you are running combines on a field with a friend vs alone. its so much more fun with a friend.4. More variety in the landscape. I get its a residential / a few parks, paddocks and orchards type of business, but everyone I have talked to asks "can you mow a golf course?" Things like this would have been such a bonus. Or think about mowing the side of a highway with cars and trucks flying past you. Adding more variety in jobs would be great. Don't get me wrong, after the first few levels it does get better, but not quite where we want it to be.5. Let's be real, the cut grass looks awful. The uncut grass looks great. I think going back to the drawing board on the cut grass would be a good idea.Other than those things, this game does a lot of things right. The graphics are stunning, the scenery is super detailed even close up and looks great. The atmosphere and lighting are wonderful. The player animations in 3rd person view are great and its generally a fun game to waste some time in. Is it worth it? yes. Could it be so much more? oh my goodness yes.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is fairly simple and straightforward overall. This is both good and bad, as there really isn't much to do other than drive a mower and try not to miss any spots, damage the ground (even on concrete/gravel), or hit a flower. All of which are fairly simple things to avoid after about 5 minutes in. While I do recognize that the title is clearly "Lawn Mower Simulator", and not "Landscaping Simulator", there seems to be a missed opportunity to add in additional tools and equipment to help with the lawn side of things. This makes the game rather one dimensional overall, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but also not necessarily a good thing. There seems to be issues with the game remembering your settings, and only applying them when you go into the settings menu to change them back. An example is audio, despite turning off the music previously the game starts with it at full blast. Once I go into the setting menu and click the audio tab it instantly applies my previous settings. Additionally, there are control issues. Being unable to remap keys is a bit of an issue but manageable, however the fact that the look inversion and look sensitivity is different between first person and driving a mower, without there being individual settings for these perspectives, is frustrating. It means that you have to adjust the inversion and sensitivity when in first person, then once you jump on the mower go back into settings to change them again. And as of yet I have been unable to find where the save and preferences files are at locally to see if some settings can be adjusted there.  Add in that there doesn't seem to be any form of advanced graphics options and you're left scratching your head on how the "Normal" preset is still only about 40 FPS on the smaller maps with plenty of stuttering. While the game looks decent enough, and I'd even go so far as calling it pretty, there really isn't that much going on where my Ryzen 2990WX and RTX 2080 Super should have trouble hitting 100+ FPS with no stutter, which indicates some potential for optimization. There is potential here, and the devs have built something that could go far, but this feels more like a beta release to iron out bugs and features, rather than a full 1.0 release. I hope the devs take a moment to reevaluate the state of the game and make some adjustments in gameplay, stability, controls, and other general quality of life areas.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I like this weird type of "simulator" games, I really have to say: jesus christ, this game is boring on a whole new level...In contrast to the various farming simulators out there, this game only offers drawbacks: you don't actually see what you're doing because there is very little visual difference between mowed grass and still-to-be-mowed grass. It is very difficult to actually mow precisely, because the cutting part of your vehicle is under the driver's butt instead of being at the front of the machine, so you always leave some little unmowed grass spots -- which is especially annoying because the game forces you to mow the grass almost perfectly to be able to finish the mission (kind of a "zero tolerance" mentality here). Furthermore, there is actually only one machine that you use in a single mission that may take way over half an hour to finish, which gets very boring very quickly.Some other reviewers write that this game is relaxing, but in my opinion, it is just utterly boring. Going to attempt a refund, it's not playable as is.Edit 2: While arguing with steam about the arbitrary 2 hour refund period. Some fixes I tried that pushed me over the 2 hour window while troubleshooting. a. Updating my video drivers, rolling back my video drivers, and updating again. Same result across the board. b. Tried taking a panel off to increase cooling, even though it wasn't overheating beforehand. No change. c. Tried validating game integrity files, no issues found and no change. d. Tried forcing the game to run on my APU (Ryzen 5 5600H) instead of my 3060. No change, crashes persisted.e. Monitored memory usage and verified it's not a RAM issue causing the crashes.Edit 3: I don't know how it happened, but my APU was kicking in and taking over duties from the GPU. _childDocuments_.review: The game looks nice. Somebody put some work in those flower assets. Also the trees look quite realistic. And the mowers look crisp and realistic. Can't be expected any more these days so.. yay!I like the scenes! They look nice, natural, as you could expect them to be somewhere. I feel immersed.TL;DR: The Accessibility update is useless!, the game is mostly unplayable with mouse/keyboard and the game file it  for downloading, the install is even bigger! The entire game is made on the use of four meaningless buttons and an analogue stick. I mean did you use a controller to program the game? Would explain a lot. Imagine, dear devs, there is at least the alphabet and numbers from 0 to 9 present on any keyboard following even remotely any standards. That are at least 30 keys you can map.  a little secret here just for you: most gaming and office mice also have additional buttons to map. Mostly 2 additional ones, but more for MMO and other mice. AND, AND, AND uhh wait for it, there is more! I am so excited to tell you: A r-click is present even on apple mice.But yes, I know I know... what to do with the controllers, you ask. If you have so many buttons you can  (imagine!? blasphemy!) map on a keyboard and would even allow for mouse buttons to be mapped, how can controller compete with that. Quite simple, really! Not? And how can we resolve conflicts with mapping soooo many keys and mouse buttons and EVEN r-click for exiting back to the previous screen instead of taking the hand off the mouse just to hit backspace, you ask! Uhm... you are game devs, right?A word on game file size: Too big! (But I still like the assets!)A word on the game using 3 physical (so 6 threads) out of my 12 physical cores at 100% (i.e. 5.2GHz): This is an absolutely ridiculous not optimized game!Say one would want to map throttle on keys 1 and 3. Yes? No? Probably too intuitive. Ok, another one: Not having to hold a key for 2 seconds to start the engine also is an option if you can afford more keys than just 4 you have to somehow avoid being hit accidentally. Sounds cool? I like it at any rate! So there's this peripheral device, called a mouse. So, strange concept here: You have at least one of your hands on that mouse about 99.9999999% of the time playing most of the pc games today. And - as mentioned - there's a r-click and (usually) 2 more buttons on a mouse, which are incredibly convenient to map to very repeating button presses like throttle up and down on mouse1 and mouse2 respectively. Or return to previous screen on r-click. Frankly, personally I don't care if you let me map a key to what I want or not, because I just make macros to detect button press as analog stick input and have that on my mouse1 and mouse2 forwarded to software function keys F26 and F28, which are mapped in the game as throttle up and down for my imaginary controller. So yes, I already have what I am asking for here, but a lot of other people don't. And this is where paying attention to community feedback suddenly is a big part of developing a good game.Cheers! (hope you had fun reading! I had fun writing at any rate!)

_childDocuments_.review: I like this simulator but I can't recommend it. All the other reviews are pretty spot on, this "game" lacks a lot. It kinda had me feeling like it was going to be like farming simulator (17) but the lawn mower version. I guess that's my fault since no other simulator has come close IMO. Either way the graphics are good and bad, the mowers look ok, but the grass is terrible. There are bugs with the character wanting to always run backwards so I have to keep nudging the joystick forward. the price is pretty high for what you get, this feels like a $5-$10 game. I'm going to assume they had to pay royalties for using name brands. The game play also lacks a lot. Upgrading tractors seems too easy and contracts are boring. You pick a contract and then go mow, if you have employees you can do multiple jobs at once. You make way too much money and the jobs are kinda drawn out. The first thing you do in career mode is name your company but you don't get to manage your company in the way of hiring employees and sending them to complete contracts. you can only assign them to a contract and then you have to also work on a contract at the same time.  Also you should be able to assign multiple employees to one contract to complete it faster. you pay the worker a set amount each week so part of the strategy should be deciding how you use there labor. You should be able to put 1-2 ai workers on your contract to help reduce the time. As it is you assign an ai worker and yourself to separate contracts and bank thousands, that's super unrealistic and really lowers the amount of time and effort it takes to upgrade and eventually stop playing due to maxing everything out. I get that its a "lawn mowing" simulator but since they added a "company" aspect there should be more to it. I hope they update the game and add more to it but I wouldn't be surprised if this is the way they left it since it's not in early access. Also I'm kinda having a hard time thinking this isn't a joke between (developer) friends. _childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I DO NOT NORMALLY REVIEW/RATE THIS EARLY, BUT I FELT I NEEDED TO SPEAK UP - AT TIME OF POSTING, I HAVE PLAYED 1 MONTH ~19 HOURSUPDATE 5/26/22: Wheels are still broken. Must turn 105 degrees before game registers it. Play only with controllers I guess. Bad devs rather pump out paid DLC then fix a basic feature. This game is not finished. I am very disappointed in the developers. You should be ashamed of yourselves. You create a niche game, and do not flush out the game content and mechanics prior to release. You are releasing additional "free DLC" before the core game has been finished. Tsk, tsk, tsk...CAMPAIGN: There are a fair amount of "maps" and for the beginning of the game, I've only done "General Cuts" since that's all that been available so far. I've seen at least one other type of contract "Striping" which requires a roller. First off, the money made from contracts is next to nothing. I mean, I wasn't expecting $10,000 from cutting a freakin lawn but COME ON... In the first month, I earned $14,637.27, but after expenses (wages, building upgrade, wages, penalties, vehicle purchases, maintenance, building maintenance, bank loan repayments) I made $1,262. So $13k in expenses. Ok, fine, I thought the 2nd month would get better, I hired a 2nd worker, trained them to level 3 in the different areas, and found out that the next building upgrade is $160,000!!!! So...If I earn $1,300 per month, it would only take me 10 in-game years to get that much. Additionally, you can ONLY hire 2 employees so this means only 3 contracts can be completed PER DAY. I have 5 available! Why can't I hire 2 more employees???? The devs also did NOT implement wheel support completely, which means while the wheel "works" its super inconsistent and annoying tbh. Gamepad works much better - but this is a simulator, I shouldn't have to use a gamepad. Well, I paid for the game, and certainly past refund time, but if I had done that I would have left a remark to call me when its done. I played the beta and enjoyed it, but did not expect this. The "business" aspect of the game is sadly very poorly done and not finished. Please stop adding "free dlc" if you have not finished the core mechanics. I'm going to keep my eye on this, and if things improve I'll be happy to change to a YES, I recommend. But at this time....No, I do NOT recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs a buyer beware, this game was built for console/mobile players, not PC gamers.  PS4 or Xbox is the only real way to enjoy this game.  They only recently added support for five driving wheels:  G920, G29, G923 (Playstation), G923 (Xbox Version), LOGITECH FARM SIMULATOR.  If you have anything else, you're stuck driving with a keyboard.  There is silence about any plans to add more wheels or backwards compatibility with other logitech devices, so I think this is it.  There is silence about any future plans at all, any new features, user requests, new maps, expansion, etc.  There is no published roadmap, no Trello, no Github, no news about the future, so no idea where this game intends to go.Lots of secrecy here, not much communication.This means the game, as gorgeous as it is, is quite limited and you have perhaps 11 hours of gameplay before you're done with it.  And driving with a keyboard when this could be oh such glorious fun with a wheel and pedals...is frustrating.  The publisher needs to look at titles like ATS/ETS/Asseto/Tourist Bus Simulator and hopefully some lightbulbs will go off about what this game could be, what market they could capture, but it's not happened yet.There are some strange decisions made.  For example, they didn't aim for realism with the mowers, they're just pretend mowers.  The "challenge" is don't go too fast or the engine will get damage hit points - but you cannot set the speed.   And driving with your limited device, good luck doing anything with precision.  I wonder if the intended audience was children and they're surprised by all this adult attention?  I dunno.I say wait and watch this space, don't buy just yet, especially if you don't have one of the five supported wheels.  The secrecy is a bit of a red flag.  I think this might just be all we ever see of this game, just maybe 20 different lawns and some challenges like striping, but no more.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, I was looking forward to it so much. Though the game is relaxing, semi-enjoyable, and extremely satisfying, it is almost entirely unplayable on PC without either a controller or wheel/pedal setup. The controls on PC are par at best. There's simply no keyboard support. The controls are unchangeable and spread out all over the keys. Throttle control just does not exist. It's either max throttle or you don't move at all. Start moving forward and you reach max speed quickly. Once at max speed, if you do not let go of the key briefly which is just annoying to do every 10 seconds, a prompt will appear that you have damaged your lawn mower, damaged the lawn itself which decreases money & XP, mower bogs down and you do not cut the crass you had just ran over. Not to mention the horrendous customization for your business and character, no support for ultra-wide resolutions, no other lawn care things your typical business would offer such as weed-eating, edging, gardening, and maybe tree trimming just to name a few. I do believe this game has a lot of potential but right now, it is far from what should be publicly released. I do NOT recommend this game whatsoever and will be immediately requesting a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 game. Absolutely the best thing I can get for 25€.Well since I've seen some horrible written reviews, here are some pros and cons:Pros:Realistic and runs very well (30 fps for max settings on a 1050 Ti, graphics include  ambient noises, people walking by on the sidewalks, cars driving by, etc.)Progression is quite nice, the adverts make leveling up not a nightmareMowers are amazing, well made, look good, quite a few options (My favourite is the Knight OFT or Stiga Park Pro 540)Quite a few maps, includes both houses and parks, also stuff like Manors, castles, generally interesting things.You don't just make turns and cut, you have to think about stuff like the engine overloading and not fully cutting, grass collectors getting full, etc.Relaxing and satisfying.Cons:Maybe a bit too much repetition in the maps, but that's not an issue for me.Lack of a free cut with unlimited everything mode, but that's fine as you can get all mowers and a high enough rank in career and get all the maps and mowers.Nothing else, really.Overall rating:10/10. Game is fun, relaxing, you can relax after a hard day of mowing outside (joke intended). If it's raining, you can still cut in game.Highly recommend it, if you can, get it. If not, save up and get it. As soon as you get it, the better it is, as the price is too low for this game. It's a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: After having sunk 15 hours in less than 2 days, I can say this game overall is highly enjoyable and relaxing. The graphics for a game like this are good, would like to see some improvement on the grass texture though. Here is some things I would love to see added that would really make the game worth the $30 price tag, as right now I think it should be in the $15-$20 range- Add the ability to change the currency from EUR to USD (I mean hell you can change every other aspect such as from the metric system to imperial, so why wasn't this included on launch?)- Keybinding options for players to change keybinds around whether on controller or KB&M- More mowers such as Exmark, Wright, Gravely, Ventrac etc. (Im sure the licensing to have these is expensive so I understand why it may not be in yet). Also adding more variety such as weed eaters, blowers (especially since you can blow grass into beds), and walk-behind mowers- Larger properties. I feel like I've beat the game and all properties are now repeats which will definitely get repetitive - Commercial properties. It would be awesome to have the option to mow more than just residential and farms, mowing various businesses with islands in a parking lot for example would add some more challenge to the players as well as add a new option to prop your mower over curbs to get to an island with no access point.- Increase fine amounts as well as overall mower maintenance. It is wayyy too cheap to repair your mower (My $15k mower should cost a few hundred to repair or even a thousand if really damaged) and the fines you get for running over flowers / not blowing out grass clippings is so minor that I don't even bother cleaning / driving carefully around beds- Ability to purchase new tires for mowers to increase stability or potentially have to get new tires because there was a nail in the yard causing you to get a flat.- If objects aren't cleared before mowing they shouldn't automatically disappear but instead should stay on the land and cause potential damage to the mower- And finally the ability to drive to job sites instead of being instantly teleported. This would just add to the immersion of the game and would allow the player to purchase various trucks and trailers that can handle different sizes of mowersThere's a lot more I could see added to this game but I would be here forever. Overall, it's a very enjoyable game and a good choice to clear your mind from other more competitive games, but I definitely think the price is too steep for what is offered at this moment in time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great, chill zen game to play while catching up on podcasts or TV shows. The core aspect of the game, mowing, is done very well. I enjoy the variety of mowers available and the ways certain mowers change the way you mow (e.g. being mindful where you blow grass if your mower doesn't mulch or collect grass clippings).  There is steering wheel support, which I was both surprised and thrilled to discover. I use the Logitech G920 and it was plug and play, without needing to change any settings or calibrate. The accelerator goes forward, the brake pedal does reverse (which on most real-life tractor-style mowers is accurate). Unfortunately there is not currently support for customizing button layouts, but it works well as is. The UI could use a little more polish, it sometimes gets slightly confusing when you start out. Some have complained that there's no way to pause the game while on a job, and therefore can't change settings in game, but I discovered if you tab out of the game it will pause. Not sure if that's a bug or not, but it's a minor issue. I have only just hired my first employee and just short of buying a second mower for them to use, so I can't speak too much on the management aspect of the game. It looks promising. Overall, I played for 6 hours straight today and had a great time, encountered zero bugs that blocked or changed gameplay, and would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys monotonous, zen-type games like this. I will definitely be getting my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I've already clocked in over 50 hours into this game and I absolutely love it. Granted, there are a few bugs here and there, and there is currently a cap for being able to hire workers, but regardless of these things, this game is an absolute must have if you are into simulation driving and managing games.I work as a professional lawn maintenance worker, and I'm constantly using all kinds of equipment in that job. Ranging from small, push mowers to 72" zero turn riders. I wish there was a little more diversity when it comes to mowers, as well as more features, such as being able to bring more than one mower with you at a time to make smaller spaces easier, but its still fun to try and complete the challenge regardless.There aren't a whole lot of contracts right now, and the selection of mowers is also relatively small, but there's still plenty of diversity. The one thing I don't think I ever thought I'd see in this game, (or in general life) is central pivot mowers. These types of mowers make going around flower beds really easy, as well as being able to get those tight corners where a zero turn makes it a little more difficult to get. The very last Toro you can get has some really nice purchasables as well, including a flail mower, which makes tall grass seem like nothing.If you're someone who wants to just get an experience with equipment, this is an amazing game for you. If you do the same thing that I do, this is still a really good game to play, as it can help you learn how each piece of equipment works, what to use, and where to use it. You can play this game realistically, doing one lap round and then back and fourths, or, you can just go in circles.Unfortunately, there isn't any in-game modding support, or multiplayer. I personally think both things would make this game 10 times better than it already is. The amount of tools you would be able to find would be incredible, and it would be amazing to be able to play with your fellow mowers on bigger, longer winded jobs.At the end of the day, if you want a good, chill time with a simulator, this is a great choice to make. And I'm confident that soon the developers will take it even further. The sky is the limit with the possibilities that this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Be advised; this game is designed for "controller" (analog input) play.The core mechanics are solid.  The career mode and challenges are standard.  There's a lot of repetition.  LMS is a good game of relaxation.At this time I cannot recommend this game based of it lack of input options.  Key commands cannot even be rebound.  Actions are hard locked and, speaking plainly, I don't believe KB+M was ever taken into consideration.  Although LMS shows "Full controller support", it should indicate minimal KB+M support.Either an oversight, short sighted, or intentional the developers decided that movement is limited to "W,A,S,D" on a keyboard.  Why?  As most KBs are basically switches.  The input is received as either 0% or 100%, there's no in between.  This is a game of finesse.  I've found I'm unable to complete higher level challenges simply because I cannot control (micro adjustments) my mower accurately enough.So, rather than complain, I have solutions, and they are relatively simple.  It SHOULD be possible to bind left/right mower turning to HOLD LMB + Mouse movement (think of highlight text).  This would provide just as much analog input as any controller.The next change should be made to cruise control.  Quite honestly, the inability to set an exact cruise control speed is the biggest detriment to failing challenges.  In LMS, as your mower passes over longer grass, your mower becomes less effective and does damage to the engine.  With inconsistent pressing of "W" and "D", cruise control can jump by as much as 4+ MPH.  IT's not uncommon for me to find a sweet spot at 5.4 MPH, only to hit a deep patch of grass, lower the speed, but it jumps down to 2.2, now I'm losing time, I try to tap by speed back up to 5.4, but I jump all over it and rarely get back.  Solution;  simply bind the cruise control speed to the mouse wheel with increments.  It would be nice to see an option to set increments of .1, .3, and .5.  As such every wheel click up/down would change speed by .1, .3, or .5.At the end of the day, it's not a bad game, just very limited for KB+M.  to me, it's a deal breaker...meaning IF I had known before purchase what I know now, I would not have purchased LMS.  I think, at this point, I'm just playing out of spite to get my $30 worth.  However, I'm pretty sure the game is "winning" though, as most gameplay sessions are more frustrating than they are relaxing...and tthe salt in the wound is that it's completely unnecessary.My current KB is the ROG Strix Scope RX (which is very sensitive) which might seem like and advantage, but it's sensitivity only serves to exacerbate the jerky movements.  My current mouse is the Logitic G502 Lightspeed wireless.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing to note: This game absolutely requires a controller instead of the mouse and keyboard. There's no way to manage your speed to not overload your mower engine in thicker grass with the mouse/keyboard setup. You can "pulse" forward by tapping/releasing the W key, but that makes for an awkward, jerky experience.With the controller, things are alright, but I've tried a few different controllers and noticed the mower direction seems to have a mind of its own. Very well could be my controllers, but I wouldn't image this would be the first time I've experienced this issue with them. The camera angle makes it challenging to line up the mower in third person view, especially when rounding corners or going under trees. Going up a slight incline causes the mower direction to change drastically and I had to fight a bit just to try and keep a semi-straight line going at all times.The graphics are great. Not very impressed with the grass quality but I'm assuming this is the best that can be done as it's really making my graphics card work for it.Overall, I bought this game to kick back and enjoy cutting some grass but I keep walking away from this game frustrated at the controls. There's no string trimming or edging around sidewalks. No tutorials (that I've seen) to show you how the game expects you to mow or how to improve. Mowing is a timed experience. I really wanted to like this game but I'll just go back to Farming Simulator instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to play this game after playing the demo. It seemed to be right up my alley in the fact that I enjoy sims (varying in levels of quality and polish). This game ain't it though. Firstly, the crashing. This game crashes constantly on my machine, so much so that it's hard to actually finish longer mowing sessions. There's no way to save mid contract either. I'm unsure why it crashes but it's probably due to the fact that it's using 100% GPU. Yes, 100% GPU of a 2070 Super for lawn mower simulator. The game doesn't even look that great. And yes, I turned the settings as low as they could go. It still uses 100%. Also, the FPS is trash. Good lucky even hitting 60 without decreasing resolution.Second, the grind. I have only played for 6 hours but it's shaping up to be one hell of a grind just to get an upgrade HQ so I can get a third mower. Maybe I'm wrong here and the pace at which you make money increases but it's looking pretty bad right now.Third, you literally cut grass and that's it. Yes, it's a lawn mower simulator and there's no false advertising there. You cut grass BUT it would be nice if you could maybe do some different things like string trimming for example. There's no variety here; it's straight up boring.Fourth, and ties a bit in with number three. You can't bring 2 mowers to a job (as far as I've seen). Some jobs you need a smaller mower (push mower might be good if it was in the game). You're stuck with either a mower that's too big to get into some places or a mower too small that will make the job take forever. Also the collision physics are laughable. You touch something and your mower springs back 2 feet like you hit a wall doing 15 mph.In summary, I like the concept but the execution is just bad. Also, FIX THE OPTIMIZATION

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys satisfaction based simulators, such as powerwash simulator. However, I do think there are some (mostly) minor quality of life changes that could be made to the game to really make it live up to its potential.Pros first:I have had no performance issues and the game has ran great. Haven't encountered any bugs. It is satisfying and an enjoyable game to relax with. I've had a good time with it for the most part so far. The maps are fun and have different challenges to find a solution to.Cons:By far the most major issue I have with this game is the overloading engine mechanic. At the very least I feel this should be optional for players who want more of a challenge. The game doesn't do a very good job at explaining why exactly your engine is getting overloaded or how to fix it. At one point I got annoyed enough to just take the extra time and cut a majority of the grass with the trimmer. It's not a fun mechanic to work around, avoiding the flowers for example is  fun mechanic to work around. The engine overloading is just frustrating and the game doesn't tell you how to solve the problem other than "raise your cut height or slow down". Raising your cut height isn't always possible.To move on to a related point, the game doesn't tell you it has a cruise control option, which would be beneficial to know to avoid the previous engine overloading. Additionally, if you're playing on controller and partially hold down the trigger to go a slower MPH, when you hit the cruise control button it shoots you up to top speed. If I'm partially holding down the trigger to go 3 MPH, it should stay 3 MPH when I press the cruise control button, not shoot me up to full speed.Another mechanic the game doesn't tell you about is that you can change the camera angle, which can be really helpful.  However, in all camera modes, tree branches can really obstruct your view and cause you to run over flowers easily. This could be easily solved with transparency through the branches while they're directly in your camera view. The timer for cleaning up trash at the beginning of the level should be optional. There's no time to appreciate the map and look around at what you'll be spending your time on because you're forced to run as fast as you can while staring at the ground to find all the trash before the timer runs out. I also don't think there should be such a push to complete the map as fast as you can in general, I'm glad that there's no penalty for going beyond the recommended time, but I think with games like this a lot of players would prefer to take their time and enjoy the experience rather than having a timer shoved in their face. It would be nice to disable the timer from the HUD while mowing.There's a pro-view mechanic, which shows you the grass you've missed and still needs cut. This is great, however you can only use it when you're completely still and not moving. This seems counter intuitive when the majority of the time you're sitting on a moving lawn mower.The menu for beginning a new game is very confusing and there's no effort to explain what button to press or what you're hovering over on controller. Overall these are minor quality of life improvements that I feel could really make the game live up to its potential. I'm still having a good time with the game and will continue playing it, and in general would still recommend this game to any player that enjoys satisfaction based simulator games.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I got a controller and have been playing with that. Night and day difference. I'm still leaving this as a "no" but that's still a "wait and see". If you have a controller and can look past the performance issues, the overheating/overworking of your mower is still incredibly annoying but it's a significantly more enjoyable game. Do not play this without a controller or you'll rage quit in its current version. I think if they fix the performance (I regularly drop down to ~45 fps and crazy stutter on at least 1 or 2 parts of each location with a 5700xt, 5900x, 64GB ram, SSD), fix the camera controls, and fix the trees and buildings constantly messing up your ability to see, I'd move this to a "yes" recommendation. I'd rather play with keyboard but even without that, fix those issues and it goes to a "yes" with a controller for me.One more thing - I wish you could send out your employees for the day without having to go out yourself. Sometimes I'd rather just send them, focus on their training and more of the business side of the game, and not have to spend ~20-30 minutes on each location mowing myself. Original: This is a strong "wait and see". I've played an hour and a half so far and it's unbelievably frustrating due to the bugs. Mouse and keyboard support is an afterthought and the devs response has been it was designed for a controller. It shows. The throttle is on or off. When on and cutting, your mower overheats every few seconds and gives you a message you should slow down (you can't due to throttle being on/off) or raise your mower height (I can't because it won't let me go any higher). So instead you hit W for 2 seconds, let go, wait half a second, hit W for 2 more seconds, and just repeat that. Every yard is "I can't wait for this to be done". Congratulations, you've made me hate mowing more than I already do. The performance needs a lot of work. If I look at a "busy" part of the yard in first person view, I get super stutter/choppy. I have to switch into first person because the other views have their up/down reversed from what any normal human would expect and the trees are constantly blocking your ability to see anything. You can't change the Y axis for just one view, it's all or nothing -- if you invert it then one type of view works but the rest are wonky. Same if you don't invert it. The jobs in the game pay low and the HQ upgrades are high. This wouldn't be a problem if the game was fun to play, but it's not. I spend most of the time angry because I'm fighting the game. So, again, wait and see. If you like these types of simulator games then it could be a lot of fun in the future. Right now it's extremely over-priced and the bugs and weird dev decisions make it really frustrating to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of simulation, not much game. If you are into hardcore simulation this game might be for you, during campaign mode you have to manage multiple factors such as gas consumption (or charge for electric machines), speed, engine strain, blade wear, cut height, turn radius, and making sure you dont damage client property.Not all of that this game does well, engine strain for instance jumps without warning and there is no way to determine if or when you will overload your engine so all you an do is stop for a moment costing you time which costs you "money", property damage is also hit and miss as turning to tight will cause damage (unrealistic) and the hitbox on the tractor makes it very easy to run into flower beds and forcing you to stay away and then come back with your trimmer.Your trimmer, this is another area that is forcibly "realistic", you have to nearly look straight down or else the trimmer isnt touching the ground and doesnt cut anything.All in all Im sure someone really into lawn mowing or simulation may like this game but I cant recommend this to the gaming audience as a whole, hell I like PowerWashing Simulator and I dont like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind that this is a very early review, only considering the very first mower and not covering any of the management aspects of the game. I am mentioning this, because judging by playtime, that is what close to every review published by now should type before making comments on the overall quality of the game.And before i move on, i want to share an experience that i had with this game. I was looking for a relaxing title to just turn my brain off and forget about my struggles at work. So on release day, i bought it, downloaded it and started playing. And while i was on my third mission, just mowing away, i thought to myself: "aw man, the birds a crazy loud outside, i should probably close the window to hear the game better. And then i realized that not only was my window closed, there were also no birds outside since it was pitch black since it was nighttime. Which to me was crazy, since i legit felt warm as i thought i was being grilled by the summer sun, mowing my lawn.What i'm trying to say is: the game is extremely good to pull you into it, if you let it. Is mowing lawn super boring? For some people it defenitly is, so think twice about getting it. I have OCD and can only say that it's extremely satisfying to watch the grass shader disappear, Speaking of which: the game looks great and the landscapes are fairly realistic.But before i finish, i want to touch on some negatives as well:1. The cut grass looks bland. It does a very good job of destinguishing it from the normal grass to make it very clear where you still have to cut, and the pressed down lanes from my mower tires make it look pretty decent, but it is very apparent that it is just a green plane with little going on.2. I was a bit disappointed to see that there were no advanced tools. The lawn usually stops at the edges, giving enough space to mow everything with a mover, which wouldn`t be the case in real life. I would have loved to toy with the idea of having a hand mover for the edges or maybe cut more than just the grass on the ground but some of the scenery too.But as it stands, it's a very relaxing game to me, so i can only recommend it IF you're into it and thinking about buying it. If not, i wouldn`t blame you to skip this either. The choice is, as always, yours.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not terrible, but it's not good. It's a game about mowing lawns, which is fine if that's not your thing, but if you're LOOKING for that...The biggest problem is that the game doesn't give you adequate auditory feedback of how close the mower is to overloading. There is a gauge, but for 80% of that gauge the sound is the same, so there's no hint you're getting close. And the grass density changes often, and VERY quickly (which is also unrealistic to real-life). Visual indication of this in the grass itself is not enough to tell the difference.This means you have to either spend most of your time going slower than you could get away with, OR you're spending all of your time with your eyes glued to the gauge in the lower right corner and are not able to look where you're actually driving the lawnmower. They could have easily made the mower sound scale more accurately, which would have made the game much more realistic AND playable, but they haven't.Controller support is mid; there's an option to adjust dead zone, but it appears to affect all axis of steering, looking, and throttle/brake at once, so to get decent responsiveness on the throttle has my view slowly drifting off to the side.In addition the mower seems to maintain an unpredictable amount of momentum, so letting off the gas stops you instantly at a low speed, but you need to let off the gas almost entirely to stop quickly from a high speed, which you need to do frequently due to the frequent and sudden changes in grass density. So driving through the grass is a constant, herky-jerky, frustrating task, rather than being something calming you can entirely zone out to.And sometimes the mower will just suddenly SHOOT forward at top speed, slamming you into things, often when it's going over irregular ground.And would it really be too much to add that familiar "gravel getting up into the blades and pinging all over the place" sound effect when you go over paths and such? You know, some audio indication of the damage that's happening to your mower?It's not horrible, but I wouldn't recommend it. I'm glad I waited until it was seventy percent off, and didn't buy the extra dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆Lawnmower Sim provides a unique and surprisingly enjoyable experience centered around the mundane task of mowing lawns. While it may not sound like the most thrilling concept, the game manages to capture the simple joys of maintaining a well-groomed lawn and offers a surprisingly relaxing and therapeutic experience.One of the standout features of Lawnmower Sim is its attention to detail in replicating the intricacies of lawn maintenance. The game offers a variety of realistic lawnmowers, each with its own handling characteristics and cutting abilities. From push mowers to ride-on mowers, the game provides a range of options that allow players to choose their preferred method of grass cutting. The controls are intuitive, and the physics simulation adds a satisfying level of realism as the grass is neatly trimmed and tidied.The game's graphics and audio design contribute to the immersive experience. The environments are well-rendered, featuring lush grass, vibrant flora, and picturesque settings. The sound effects, from the hum of the lawnmower engine to the gentle rustling of grass, add to the sense of immersion and create a soothing ambience that can be quite relaxing.Lawnmower Sim offers a range of challenges and scenarios to keep players engaged. From timed mowing events to obstacle courses and precision cutting tasks, the game provides a variety of objectives that test your lawn maintenance skills. These challenges add a layer of gameplay depth and keep the experience from becoming monotonous.Furthermore, Lawnmower Sim provides a welcome escape from the fast-paced and action-packed nature of many other games. Its calm and leisurely pace offers a unique form of stress relief and can be a pleasant way to unwind after a long day. The game's simplicity and lack of complex mechanics make it accessible to players of all ages and skill levels.However, it is worth noting that Lawnmower Sim may not appeal to those seeking adrenaline-pumping action or deep gameplay mechanics. While it succeeds in delivering a relaxing and therapeutic experience, some players may find the concept too niche or lacking in long-term replayability.In conclusion, Lawnmower Sim is a surprisingly enjoyable and relaxing game that captures the simple pleasure of maintaining a well-manicured lawn. Its attention to detail, immersive graphics, and soothing gameplay make it a unique and therapeutic experience for those seeking a break from the usual fast-paced gaming fare. While it may not have the broad appeal of other genres, Lawnmower Sim delivers on its premise and provides a satisfying and calming gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as complex as Farming Simulator and not as satisfying as Powerwash Simulator but if you really like simulator or lawnmowers I think it is a decent but limited option. Instead of a Yes or No I would give it a Maybe if it was an option.I got the game with Humble Choice and gave it a try even though I had no interest. The tutorial was a bit flat but I got curious and pushed through a couple jobs. If you can get past the early slow mowers with almost no pay it actually turn into a game.The game lock the maps to your Career rank so it is very repetitive early on. There are also not that many mowers so progression is painful. Buying new mowers is what got me to "the end" ( There is no end, but biggest HQ and Max employees. ) because they get bigger, faster and also drive differently from one another. The progression curve is also a bit weird because when you can hire your first employee and get a second mower you'll make almost double the money, as long as you get lucky with the random jobs choices. When an employee ask only 500$ a week and it can do a 1000-2000$ job 5 time a week it is very lucrative.Graphics are surprisingly good, nice environments and very detailed mowers. Where it can be hit or miss is the grass/lawn itself. It does not look realistic at all to me but it has pretty realistic physic where you'll see your mowers wheel marks, including in which direction you pushed down the grass for example. There are hills, rougher spot where your mower will shake and maybe swerve a bit and length and amount of grass will affect your mower.My biggest gripe with the game, beside the progression curve, is the employees. They don't really exist. You'll pay them and they'll make you money but you can't watch them work or have them on the same job as you to help and finish faster. You'll have some random civilians walking on the sidewalk and random sounds but it would have made things more lively.

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs some work, but it isn't awful.I wouldn't classify this game as a simulator as it isn't an accurate representation of mowing in real life. The lack of smaller equipment in this game requires you to shove your mower into tight spaces, this damages your mower and induces fines. I would love to see other lawn care items such as weed trimmers and smaller mowers.One of my biggest issues with this game is the lack of optimization. Running on 4K Normal settings my 3070Ti can barely keep a steady 60FPS with the game frequently dipping and staying at 40FPS. In contrast, RDR2 (one of my favorite titles) can easily run at 4K 60FPS on a mix between high and ultra settings. I have also encountered a large number of bugs in just my 4 hours of playtime. These include: issues not being able to walk properly at the beginning of the levels, bad collisions which cause you to hit things you are nowhere near, and issues with the menu freezing or not working properly.The controls in this game are unintuitive and overall poorly set up. There is no way to change this. Additionally, the game is very limiting on other settings that can be changed. One big thing I was happy to see was wheel support. I of course was immediately saddened when I learned it was only for 5 wheels. Most games don't provide official wheel support for every wheel which isn't an issue because you can configure the wheel and its controls in the settings. However, in this game you can't use non-officially supported wheels even if you wanted to.Overall this game isn't bad, I just wish it had gotten more attention before release. I watched the developers stream right after the game had launched. It's obvious they are passionate about their game, so I hope they continue to work on it and improve it. I was super excited about this release and I hope this review helps improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing to consider is that even though they have "simulator" in the title this is by no means a proper simulator. For starters your only tools are mowers - no push mowing to start as you go from rags to riches and very un-worldly payouts for completing a job. Protecting flowers is difficult at best when you only have a big mower and there is no way to really ensure you are going to protect them all - this is the purpose of a weed eater... fine control over what you cut and don't, but of course this is also missing from the game.Some of the mowers are just stupid fast. Doing the first challenge was NOT a joy as the mower they provide you goes from 0 to 10 mph in and instant and there absolutely no way to run it slower unless you want to tap W and move it forward that way. After some additional reading it seems a PC game was made with controllers in mind... I call BS to that. You made an Xbox/Playstation game and tried to pass it off as a PC game. Shame on you... and no you did not make it clear that this was your focus so don't comment and say so. Don't drop a PC game on a PC gaming platform (Steam) and then act so surprised PC players are upset that the mower using mouse/keyboard is totally broke.  I've got too much time played to refund - this alone make the game unplayable for mouse/keyboard players. Shame on you.Camera movement is a sick joke and setting up the camera for first person does NOT carry over to 3rd and there is no way to set them independently.My biggest worry is how the game displays. I don't know what it is about the quality of motion, but the game displays like its running at ~20 FPS although throughout my entire 2.5 hours of playing my FPS counter never dropped below 45 FPS. _childDocuments_.review: Tonkatsu Ramen RecipeIngredients:3 pounds pig trotters, split lengthwise or cut crosswise into 1-inch disks (ask your butcher to do this for you)2 pounds chicken backs and carcasses, skin and excess fat removed2 tablespoons vegetable oil1 large onion, skin on, roughly chopped12 garlic clovesOne 3-inch knob ginger, roughly chopped2 whole leeks, washed and roughly chopped2 dozen scallions, white parts only (reserve greens and light green parts for garnishing finished soup)6 ounces whole mushrooms or mushroom scraps1 pound slab pork fat backDirections1) Place pork and chicken bones in a large stockpot and cover with cold water. Place on a burner over high heat and bring to a boil. Remove from heat as soon as boil is reached.2) While pot is heating, heat vegetable oil in a medium cast iron or non-stick skillet over high heat until lightly smoking. Add onions, garlic, and ginger. Cook, tossing occasionally until deeply charred on most sides, about 15 minutes total. Set aside.3)Once pot has come to a boil, dump water down the drain. Carefully wash all bones under cold running water, removing any bits of dark marrow or coagulated blood. Bones should be uniform grey/white after you've scrubbed them. Use a chopstick to help remove small bits of dark marrow from inside the trotters or near the chicken's spines.4) Return bones to pot along with charred vegetables, leeks, scallion whites, mushrooms, and pork fatback. Top up with cold water. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, skimming off any scum that appears (this should stop appearing within the first 20 minutes or so). Use a clean sponge or moist paper towels to wipe any black or gray scum off from around the rim of the pot. Reduce heat to a bare simmer and place a heavy lid on top.5) Once the lid is on, check the pot after 15 minutes. It should be at a slow rolling boil. If not, increase or decrease heat slightly to adjust boiling speed. Boil broth until pork fatback is completely tender, about 4 hours. Carefully remove pork fat with a slotted spatula. Transfer fatback to a sealed container and refrigerate until step 7. Return lid to pot and continue cooking until broth is opaque with the texture of light cream, about 6 to 8 hours longer, topping up as necessary to keep bones submerged at all times. If you must leave the pot unattended for an extended period of time, top up the pot and reduce the heat to the lowest setting while you are gone. Return to a boil when you come back and continue cooking, topping up with more water as necessary.6) Once broth is ready, cook over high heat until reduced to around 3 quarts. Strain through a fine mesh strainer into a clean pot. Discard solids. For an even cleaner soup, strain again through a chinois or a fine mesh strainer lined with several layers of cheese cloth. Skim liquid fat from top with a ladle and discard.7) Finely chop cooked pork fatback and whisk into finished broth. To serve, season broth with condiments of your choice (salt, soy sauce, miso, sesame paste, grated fresh garlic, chili oil or a mixture of all, for instance) and serve with cooked ramen noodles and toppings as desired.

_childDocuments_.review: A lawn mower (also known as mower, grass cutter or lawnmower) is a machine utilizing one or more revolving blades to cut a grass surface to an even height. The height of the cut grass may be fixed by the design of the mower, but generally is adjustable by the operator, typically by a single master lever, or by a lever or nut and bolt on each of the machine's wheels.  The blades may be powered by manual force, with wheels mechanically connected to the cutting blades so that when the mower is pushed forward, the blades spin or the machine may have a battery-powered or plug-in electric motor. The most common self-contained power source for lawn mowers is a small (typically one cylinder) internal combustion engine. Smaller mowers often lack any form of propulsion, requiring human power to move over a surface; "walk-behind" mowers are self-propelled, requiring a human only to walk behind and guide them. Larger lawn mowers are usually either self-propelled "walk-behind" types or more often, are "ride-on" mowers, equipped so the operator can ride on the mower and control it. A robotic lawn mower ("lawn-mowing bot", "mowbot", etc.) is designed to operate either entirely on its own or less commonly by an operator by remote control.Two main styles of blades are used in lawn mowers. Lawn mowers employing a single blade that rotates about a single vertical axis are known as rotary mowers, while those employing a cutting bar and multiple blade assembly that rotates about a single horizontal axis are known as cylinder or reel mowers (although in some versions, the cutting bar is the only blade, and the rotating assembly consists of flat metal pieces which force the blades of grass against the sharp cutting bar).There are several types of mowers, each suited to a particular scale and purpose. The smallest types, non-powered push mowers, are suitable for small residential lawns and gardens. Electrical or piston engine-powered push-mowers are used for larger residential lawns (although there is some overlap). Riding mowers, which sometimes resemble small tractors, are larger than push mowers and are suitable for large lawns, although commercial riding lawn mowers (such as zero-turn mowers) can be "stand-on" types, and often bear little resemblance to residential lawn tractors, being designed to mow large areas at high speed in the shortest time possible. The largest multi-gang (multi-blade) mowers are mounted on tractors and are designed for large expanses of grass such as golf courses and municipal parks, although they are ill-suited for complex terrain.

_childDocuments_.review: Lawn Mowing Simulator: A Surprisingly Zen Experience (But Maybe Not for Everyone)Lawn Mowing Simulator isn't your typical video game.  Instead of slaying dragons or winning championships, you take on the serene (or mundane, depending on your perspective) task of mowing lawns. Here's a breakdown to help you decide if this unique sim is for you:The Grass is Greener on Your Side (of the Screen):Relaxation Station: Lawn Mowing Simulator offers a surprisingly relaxing and meditative experience. The gentle hum of the engine, the sound of the blades cutting through grass, and the picturesque British countryside all contribute to a calming atmosphere.Attention to Detail: The game boasts impressive realism when it comes to mowing mechanics. You'll need to factor in factors like blade height, ground speed, and fuel consumption for optimal results.Building Your Business Empire: The career mode lets you build your own lawn mowing business. You'll take on contracts, purchase and upgrade mowers, and manage your finances. There's a surprising layer of strategy to it.Not Quite a Walk in the Park:Slow and Steady Wins the Race: Gameplay can be slow-paced, especially for those who crave fast-paced action or high-stakes challenges.Repetitive Nature of the Beast: Mowing lawns, while oddly therapeutic, can become repetitive after a while.Limited Scope: Don't expect a sprawling open world or a ton of variety in objectives. The core gameplay loop revolves around mowing lawns.Overall:Lawn Mowing Simulator is a niche game, but it caters to that niche exceptionally well. If you're looking for a relaxing and oddly satisfying experience, and you don't mind the slow pace, then this game might surprise you.  However, if you crave constant action or a deep and engaging story, you might want to look elsewhere.Recommendation:For fans of simulation games and those seeking a relaxing experience: Absolutely give it a try!For those who crave action, adventure, or a complex narrative: This might not be your cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Lawn Mowing Simulator is exactly what it says on the box.  You run a lawn mowing business and you get to ride on a number of authentic, real world lawnmowers.  For all the obsessive compulsives out there, you can enjoy the deeply satisfying process of mowing a lawn until it's neat as a pin.  Well, that's the idea anyway.The graphics are top notch here as well as the lawnmower models.  The game concept is fine, too.  You've got a fun business management game punctuated by lawnmowing escapades... what's not to love?The problem here, and it's a big one, the lawnmower handling and camera controls in this game are just utter garbage.  You need to press obscure buttons to adjust the mower throttle, blade height, lower the mowing cage... all keybound.  You're going to spend more time hunt and pecking the keyboard than actually mowing lawns.  Why couldn't they have just had some interactive mouse controls?  Oh yeah, because consoles.  Once you do get started, that's when the crappy Playstation port camera controls come into the picture.  You can change the camera angle with the mouse, but it's inverted and wobbles all over the place.   Playing this game is frustrating and annoying due to the clumsy, hamfisted console control scheme, and that's a crying shame.  For the whopping, eye watering $20 USD price tag on this game you would think the developer might have had a budget for playtesting this on PC.  But it's evident based on the sloppy controls in the game that they never bothered.   If they can't be bothered testing their game and making sure it feels good to play, you shouldn't bother buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Much as you'd expect, this game involves lawn mowers and simulating their effect on grass of varying heights and locations. After completing 30-some hours, I decided to compare the experience to mowing my parents' lawn. Without having several thousand dollars (or GBP) to spend on getting a riding/standing mower, I elected to use the push-mower found in the "garden shed" location. Already things are different, but perhaps importantly I am still dealing with spinning blades mere inches from the ground. So far so good.Once I got the mower into position (pleased to not have to dismiss a notification present in the game if you elect to employ someone without having sufficient 'strimmers' (string trimmers).Here's where using legs I control natively is superior to the PS5 DualShock controller I was using in the game. I found cornering much more intuitive, and handling uneven ground was much easier in reality with my fleshly legs (notably, in my simulator plays, hilly terrain would often send my mower into rocket mode). I also found much less detritus in the lawn (particularly absent were standing bottles and full sheets of newsprint).I enjoy making real grass shorter, and removing excess digital length in digital lawns is also satisfying, though not in the same way. This isn't power-washing, let's not kid ourselves, but if you want to hear some birds and occasional car alarms and the gentle whirr-whirr of digital lawn mowery, then this may will scratch that itch.I will continue making lawns shorter in the, er, what, 6 locations (?) for a while now. And sometimes picking up trash for reasons beyond my ken.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one for those that want to use a wheel. I do like the game and have enjoyed watch many play it online. I recently go it and was eager to get into it with my wheel, but the game only "supports" five wheels.. I will give it a proper college try once more support is added.The good:It can be very fun and relaxing to play. Interesting locations, nice graphics, good at scratching that itch everyone has to mow a virtual lawn.The bad:TLDR: I'm disappointed that the wheel support is lacking. It can detect that I are using a wheel, but there is a lack of detection actual input. The wheel in question is a PXN V10. I know there are "Supported Wheels," but that just tells me that I need to buy different hardware to enjoy your game.It automatically detects that I have a wheel plugged in, PXN V10, but doesn't allow me to actually set it up. I've tried both Dinput and Xinput modes to see if that had any effect, but it didn't. Usually that does the trick if it's a more controller based system. For example. it asks me to turn my wheel, I do and nothing happens. It ask me to press my accelerator, I do and it does detect that a button is pressed, but there is not pressure sensitivity at all.. It's extremely unfortunate that there is only support for specific wheels and not a system that can detect generic output. Only having five wheels supported limits the players that want to play. I know each wheel setup is different, but I have managed to even get my setup to work well with Disney Speedstorm, and that's not even a game that supports wheels. The simulator community is built on people who want to expand their control of a game to more express to it's IRL counterpart. Even though this game is seen more of a meme to most people, I would hope in the future there are systems put in place to better enhance the experience of the player base who bought and want to enjoy your game. Yes, all this may sound like a broken record, but it's repeating for a reason.My conclusion:I do recommend this to anyone who doesn't have a wheel, has one that is supported, or doesn't care either way and just want's to have fun. But I don't recommend this if you have intended to use your wheel and is unable to use it. I will still try to find a way to emulate a wheel, possibly through JoyToKey or something like that. If anyone has solutions, I and others would greatly appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: It seems kinda strange to mow digital lawns but if you think it over it is pretty much like shooting digital tanks or slaying digital dragons - the result is nothing, the process is everything. The four-wheeled lawn mower is loud and agile and the lawn is basically your rally track with its own speed limit, lap time and of course big cash prize at the end. This strangely entertaining and unexpectedly satisfying activity is spoiled only by developer's name 'Skyhook Games' which is a synonym to 'cheap and crappy' so the engine overheating mechanics is annoying, controls are awkward and graphics optimisation is absent. The game doesn't have gamepad settings so you will play with max sensitivity and good luck with it. There are quite a few British-themed lawn areas plus a pair of DLCs for those who want more. The scenery looks outdated but kinda nice and mowers (15 of them - all licensed) look and sound realistic.Verdict: it's a strange fun but fun nevertheless.P.S. And you don't have to kill anyone which is quite rare for modern games.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this game, unfortunately a few things kept it from being enjoyable. Such as: Not the best, not the worst. It's mostly icons, but you get used to what's what. The issue comes from scrolling the bar for picking a mower for example. Move mouse left-right to scroll, but it is way too sensitive so you have to jerk your mouse back to stop scrolling. That bar also starts moving when you're only slightly off-center, not when you're near screen edges. Or I should say, lack of. Typically when mowing sound plays a HUGE role for letting you know what's happening with the mower. Typically it is a few distinct tones: sound of the engine, whine of hydraulics, whirring of the blades, and few lesser ones. Still, each sound changes depending on what's happening. Cutting a heavier spot? Whirring of the blades gets muted a bit, engine sound gradually changes to lower frequency more "powerful" roar. Going up a hill? Hydraulics whine a little louder. Meanwhile here it's "two distinct sounds for blades and everything else is just *noise* ", not to mention that all mowers literally sound the same. Additionally, there is no soundtrack to speak of, just one song that loops over and over. At least it feels that way. "Look down to cut" but are you really cutting? You don't know! The "trimmer" seems to be just an image overlay on top of everything else, so cutting around bushes and such it looks like you're lifting the trimmer over them instead of reaching under. And in general there is no real visual effect to show when the grass is being cut, so it ends up being "walk two steps, turn around to see if you've cut anything, walk two more steps". And perhaps my biggest issue:  May be my colourblindness, but often it is really difficult to see if you've missed a spot. There's "Pro vision" that highlights uncut grass nicely, but it goes away as soon as you move. IRL there is usually a nice dark shadow from taller grass as well as a distinctly different texture and that makes it obvious as to what has and has not been cut. In this game blades of grass are far enough apart where this color/texture change is often times not visible.Lawn Mowing Sim used to have a demo, but it has been taken down for some reason. Shame really. Would have saved me some time and them a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it is definitely a game for fanatics of the subject, who at the same time are fine with arcade controls. It's a baffling sim game that carried me through some longer videos and podcasts, but after seeing repeating locations and no significant changes in the gameplay, it doesn't feel worth it for any more than a dollar, which is about the price I had it for in a bundle.The look of tire tracks and accurately lowering grass height is a simple satisfaction that can carry you for a few hours of mindless time sinking, while you pay attention to actually mentally stimulating content in the background. Unfortunately the game falls short and becomes so ungodly dull that all the time spent on it ends up feeling somewhat wasted. A shame since it does seem to be made by guys at least somewhat passionate about this mundane subject.Every map starts with few minutes of running around, fishing for "f to pick up garbage" prompts, then hopping onto a driveable mower, making straight and curved lines most efficiently, finishing with a hand mower around flowers and walkways, and lastly picking up bits of grass that flew beyond the lawn area.Driving feels ok, but there is only one way to achieve your goal sensibly, hand mowing is instantly tedious, making you squint at the minimal height differences, and aiming for the unreasonably high completion % required, while parts required to get mowed down are not easily highlighted or shown on any kind of minimap.After you get bored and notice that upgrading your mower still makes the game play the same, but with higher pay, you can try the business mechanics, which are actually just idle game things, of slowly investing into making employees do most of the work for you. You can see what the biggest or fastest models feel like to drive, but there is still no novelty, you have the same levels, same routine, similar visuals, monotone sounds, and no flavor details, besides ugly looking pedestrians beyond the fence sometimes.I had it for almost nothing from a bundle and I am still not happy, I could only recommend it to the subject fanatics, who care more so about the technical and light business aspect, rather than super a**istic level of accurate simulation. At least part of my playtime is having the game idly open.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and relaxing but the experience is ruined somewhat by business management elements that don't really add anything to the game. The game gets a recommendation, but with caveats.So I heard about this game after seeing several ASMR Youtubers post about it so I thought I would give it a go. The execution of the core concept of mowing and cutting the grass itself is great, but unfortunately the developers took this bizarre decision to incorporate some convoluted campaign mode that sees you trying to build some kind of grass cutting empire, and it really detracts from the main concept of the game.So to the main action in the game. Cutting grass. It's well executed and sitting on top of your mower chugging along and cutting the grass is really relaxing. The graphics and mechanics are well done and functional and it's easy to see the effect your having. If you find you can't quite locate the last bit of grass the game helpfully gives you an option to highlight it in white so you can go and find it, so it never gets frustrating. You also get a strimmer for doing edges and little bits of areas that you can't get your ride on mower into. It's enjoyable and relaxing and if your a fan of power washing games and others that simulate relaxing tasks, you will find this to have the same kind of vibe.The actual mowing of the lawns themselves is the games strength and I don't really have much to complain about in this regard, but if I had to really think of complaints about the actual grass cutting portion, it would be that the levels all tend to begin to feel the same after a little while. Also, the approach you take is really quite fixed. Big mower first, then strimmer to tidy. You basically work in a circle inwards or outwards every time, and the idea you might use the strimmer for than the odd missing bits of grass here and there just isn't a mechanic you can employ. However I am really reaching here, and in the end you won't find it to be a big deal.Where the game really begins to fall down is the business management element the developers have incorporated that allows you to take out business loans, grow your grass cutting business, hire employees and buy new and better mowers and headquarters to work from.I get that the developers probably wanted to add more depth to what on the face of it would otherwise have been a fairly simple game but unfortunately the relaxing element of cutting grass and the chore of managing a business just completely clash. The business management side of the game just serves as an object to frustrate your progress more than anything else.As an example, to purchase more than one mower type, you need to purchase or upgrade a headquarters. So you have to save for this before you can purchase another mower. It's frustrating as hell because you just want to get a different mower. Likewise, the game gives you an option to hire employees to do contracts and make more money. Why on earth you would want to do this when you want to mow the lawns yourself? It's just completely pointless faff that gets in the way of the enjoyable bit of the game which is mowing the lawns.I think even if you enjoy business management type of games, you will find this aspect of the game is not particularly satisfying because ultimately aside from being able to purchase other equipment, the business management is fairly inconsequential and just hampers your ability to just get on with the task of mowing.Ultimately I feel the developers would have been better off just giving us straight purchase and upgrade options for new equipment as you earn money rather than trying to get too in depth into running a grass cutting empire. There is another game that follows the "Relaxing task" formula called Power Washing Simulator and while not quite the same activity, you basically follow the same formula of going to different jobs to power wash different things. The developers of that particular game clearly understood people don't want to be managing a business, they just want to power wash crap and so the upgrades and purchases option is extremely straight forward with no business management faff to get in the way. It's an approach that would have worked well in Lawn Mowing Simulator had they decided to go that way. Alas, we got the annoying business management aspect instead.Speaking of purchasing new equipment, the game includes a large collection of ride along mowers and strimmers for you to purchase. They can vary in quite a few features ranging from power train (Electric or petrol), cutting width, steering types and a few other features. However frustratingly they are locked away to a degree by the needs to expand some elements of the business management aspect, like getting a HQ that can store more than one mower.The mowers are all well designed and riding them feels authentic. They do tend to all feel the same though and there are only a few aspects that sets some of them apart as a reason why you might want to purchase a new one. Drive type is one. Some jobs demand that you use an eco friendly mower so you must have an electric powered one for certain jobs, while in others you want a petrol powered one to give you more endurance. The ability for the mower to take a collection box for the grass cuttings is another as having to pick up disposed grass cuttings can get annoying. Some mowers have a lawn roller to give you that striped lawn look. Finally some mowers are able to turn more tightly than others and some can turn on the spot, making these mowers more useful in tighter areas.Outside of these particular aspects though, there's very little difference between the mowers other than visual appearance and as long as you have one electric mower and one petrol powered motor both with zero turning circles, the ability to add a collection box and roller, there's not much reason to try and get anything else. The strimmers are exactly the same. They all mostly work the same and there's very little to choose from between them.Overall the game does what it says on the tin and you will find the core game play of mowing a lawn satisfying, and for that reason I do recommend it. It's just unfortunate the developers decided to bog down this game play with business management aspects that just frustrate the experience rather than compliment it.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review by saying this  a bad game, and I wish there was an neutral rating as there are things I both like and dislike about Lawn Mowing Simulator.I like the sound and looks of the mowers themselves, the graphics overall, and the fact it is considerably better optimised since I played the original 2021 NextFest demo. The "Lawnmowing" portion of this simulator I mostly like. It's also refreshing to have this set in Britain, as most games/simulators are exclusively set in the United States; so it is refreshing!The main issue I have is the this simulator is leaning towards more realism then some others I played, most notably PowerWash Simulator. I don't like the whole "company management" side of things, an aspect that turn me off on many other simulators. There's also the pre-requisite tasks you need to do and can't just go lawnmowing immediately. Freeplay is better then Career mode in this aspect, but it's still a thing to note. The fines and having to maintain equipment are also an issue for me personally. What I like about PWS is that it is a simulator, but it does take a few liberties to make it more fun for a casual player. Lawn Mowing Simulator isn't one of those type of simulators.In conclusion, this isn't a bad game, and there is room in the market for simulators that is ultra-realistic! No doubt other people will love the whole company management game mechanic and the fact it's really realistic - right down to damaging the ground for doing a U-turn for too long. For me though - this isn't what I hoped it would be and I'm glad I picked this up when it was on sale!

THERE, and OMG WHERE AM I LOOKING?   I also have this game on Xbox, which is considerably better because the controller allows far greater precision control.
