_childDocuments_.review: This is interesting.  I like the mechanics so far, and I am not bothered by what most people complain about.The mower overloading is a real life thing, and it happens in this game.  I do wish the implementation was a little easier to "feel" than having to watch your speedometer constantly, and maybe a little easier to see visually when you're hitting some high grass (like have difficult sections visually display the grass going to seed).The grass cutting looks fine to me - both pre-cut and post-cut.  I have graphics cranked though, so maybe that's why.  Could it be better?  Sure.  All graphics could improve no matter how good they are.  Are they good enough to give a satisfying cutting experience that you can look at when you're done with satisfaction?  Yep.The number one thing I'd improve on is the ability to save mid-mow.  I got 25% done with a mow after just over 30 minutes tonight.  Having a family I frequently can't devote 2 hours to a single play session.  I had to lose half hour of progress just because the devs haven't implemented a seemingly basic feature that's been requested since at least 2021.  I just can't fathom why this would not be implemented (Seems the game already has to store your cut pattern as you're mowing, so just offload that data to a save location, but I'm no game dev).  Some say quick save would be cheating.  I'm not sure exactly why, but ok let's address that.  At very least, allow the game to save its state and exit the game.  No quick load, no problem for the anti-quick-save crowd.  The only thing I can imagine they're worried about is reloading to avoid mower damage or flower damage.  The fines are so incredibly small I just can't see caring enough to reload and redo a section of grass.  On top of that, it's not like this is an e-sports tournament.  We own the game.  If we want to cheat/exploit to make it easier, does that negatively impact your playing experience?  No, it does not.  Am I cheating?  No.  Do I care?  No.All in all, it's exactly what I was hoping for, minus the ability to save mid mow.  I can relax and enjoy the relative monotony, which is something that stands in contrast to my professional career and family.  Just give me the ability to escape on my time without punishing me for not having more.Edit at 32 hours:I'll add that while I still enjoy it quite a bit, there are some notable flaws.  For one, the controls are really twitchy on the zero turn mowers.  And to make matters worse, there are many locations where the geometry of the land causes the mower to act erratically - slowing down only to bolt forward with no warning, or literally cause the mower to catch air and miss a section of grass entirely.  Also, the view controls in first person locking your head to a small cone looking forward is also annoying.  In real life we look behind us, and in third person your avatar also looks behind themselves when backing up - this should be allowed in first person.  Next, even with mid-tier powerful mowers like the SCAG Turf Tiger II, you frequently run into overloading.  Couple that with the fact that you can mow so fast and things get out of control really quickly.It's certainly not all bad - as I said, I enjoy the game quite a bit and play regularly.  I do have some suggestions that I'm hoping are helpful.1.  I wonder what it would be like to use the two analog sticks to control the zero turn mowers' control sticks like they behave in real life.2.  Smooth out the terrain so mowers don't experience unintended movement.3.  Maybe allow multiple workers on each job - one edging, one trimming, one mowing.4.  Allow Pro-View to toggle - let us choose when it's visible and when not5.  Give us a button to restore all tools at once - repair blades, engines, refuel, etc.  Or at least a button to fully restore each tool, maybe unlocked at a certain experience level.6.  Show charge/fuel remaining for trimmers in the menu similar to the mowers (I have to guess which ones need recharging/refueling)7.  Allow attachments for the trimmers, like bush hogs and the likes to tackle more overgrown stuff easier.8.  Allow us to toggle the icon to collect grass clippings.  It's annoying when I go to trim at the end of a job where no collection/mulching is required and there are tons of grass clipping notifications flashing by as I move around.9.  Have more open areas to mow where you aren't overloading the mower.  Sometimes it's just nice to pin the accelerator and get into a rhythm without worrying about the overload meter.10.  Give us a way to acquire customers and procure contracts so you can mow their lawn once per week.  The first mow of a contract may be overgrown and nasty, but as you continue to maintain their yard it gets easier to maintain and looks better.11.  Include some of the other portions of a lawn mowing business like leaf blowing, edging, and maybe even landscaping.12.  Allow us to physically see our headquarters instead of it just being an icon and having the knowledge of how many slots one has.  Give us a visual reward for upgrading.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, but has three major flaws that keep it from being replayable.First, the good. It's a pleasant relaxation game. I really enjoyed most of the maps. Most of the maps which had modes which I wouldn't consider really "my thing" (strimmer-only areas, overgrown, or rain) were a nice change of pace and the frequency they appear matches that. There was a good mix of cottage-style twisty gardens, tight-in spaces, and big rectangular lawns. Graphics are very good given the price, but the required performance matches... don't expect to run it on a potato.Now the drawbacks. They're fairly major.I really do like this game, but the last two bullets above are keeping me from playing any farther or buying either of the DLC.I'd really love to see them add a feature where you take an employee or two with you to the job site and have them either clear cut the large areas of the lawn while you undercut the tight corners or walk around with a strimmer and clean up behind you. Also, larger mowers and matching content (like a Hustler Super 104), or a double or triple butterfly mower (like a EXTRA 687T or 690T BX).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I didn't know I needed. I love relaxing games and simulator games and this one scratches a lot of those itches. From building your business and managing/training employees and profit with maintenance/fuel costs and loan payments to the pure satisfaction of being out in nature listening to the birds while you sit on pure gas powered rotating blades of freedom. _childDocuments_.review: Not keyboard and mouse friendly, yes you can play with them but it feels as if it was a after thought, even lightly taping a direction steers the machine widely. You are also unable to adjust how quickly steering responds ether.Also using mouse to look around was sickeningly fast however you could adjust that down, for myself 60% was fine but do think if the game started with the default at 60-70& and allowing players to go higher would have been the better option.Menu options trying to exit are also vague as you need to "back" out to the main menu to finally quit.If you play using controller it would likely be more enjoyable as you should be able to finely tune how it steers. Using a keyboard you ether will be leaving swaths of grass or wasting time by only using 1/2 the cutting area.I'm a fan of simulator games and this one did interest me and I was lucky a friend got a copy he did not want and gifted it to me, but as I'm a old school lover of playing mouse and keyboard this game fails to appeal to my playing style.This limited review is based on how I play my games of PC for any who play similar to myself so they understand the challenges it will offer.I cannot comment on game progression or long term play due to quick loss of interest based on my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I had my first child when I was 17. After years of schooling, I worked as a lawyer before I was forced to resign. The local government corruption fell to the hands of gangs. I wouldn't work FOR them so I was seen as a liability. I had to go back to working in my uncle's auto shop with shame hanging over my head. Just when I thought things couldn't get any worse, my wife was pregnant again.I knew I had to make a change. I loved my family but there simply wasn't enough money to provide. I saved up enough for a plane ticket and left with nothing other than the clothes on my back. I tried to renew my license to practice law but the fees would set me back too far. All the mechanic jobs have gone to locals and those with more experience than me. I was lost.On my way home from another failed job interview. I stumbled across a house with an old man struggling to limp to his lawn mower. He fell over and I yelled, "Sir, are you okay?! Can I help you?" He didn't answer. I didn't want to go on his property but I had no choice. I rushed to his side and asked again if he was okay. He gently whispers, "my....lawn...needs..." He didn't need to finish, I knew what must be done.I put on my trusty baseball cap and hopped on the machine of grassy death. I murdered any weeds that dared disrespect the lawn of this nice old man. I fought valiantly with nature until it cried, "mommy!" When the battle was finished, I marveled at my creation. The old man says, "here's 5 dollars." But I knew what he meant, this was my calling. My purpose. My destiny.My name is The American Dream.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of things that I could waste my time critiquing, but there's one make-or-break issue plaguing this game being the controls.  To put it bluntly, they're absolutely terrible.  The keyboard controls feel like they were included as an after thought and suffer as a result.  With that said, obviously it was intended for a gamepad, right?  Surely those controls are at least passable, RIGHT!?!?  I don't even have the energy to tell you you're wrong.  The best way to describe these controls is they're either ON or OFF.  You either get 100% speed or 0%.  As a result, your trimmer (which is terrible in it's own right) will often find itself plunged into a flower bed at the slightest twitch of a joystick.  Oh yeah, you're penalized monetarily for damaging plants and other items, so precision is demanded but not provided.Overall, it feels horrible to play.  Just save your money and stare at a brick wall.  You'll both be a bit richer and have a more enriching experience.

_childDocuments_.review: After 70 hours I feel I have beat Lawn Mowing Simulator. This is really a game where I can just kick back and relax and enjoy the satisfaction of it. This relaxation doesn't come without complaints though. First of all, I feel like after doing all of the properties multiple times, there is not enough variety in gameplay. This could be solved simply by releasing more DLC, possible outside of Great Britain. Second, "Beating" Lawn Mowing Simulator so early makes me feel cut short and like it should've taken longer. I don't like how after I bought my final garage with unlimited bays, I was limited to 4 employees and told I was at my max when I attempted to hire more. I believe for Skyhook, simply not setting a max number of employees and number of jobs at once would prolong playtime of a lot of players. Third, running a small lawn care business in real life, I feel this is not realistic enough. Yes, "It's just a game", but it is here to simulate mowing and running a mowing business. In real life the first step for most is a push mower and I think this would be a great addition to Lawn Mowing Simulator. This would also add much needed variety to the game in the different types of mowers. In Lawn Mowing Simulator as I type, there is 13 sit-on mowers and 1 stand-on mower. They could add 21' honda mowers, 21'-30' toro push mowers, and more options for stand-ons than just the Scag V-Ride 2. Still, Skyhook continues to maintain this incredibly relaxing, and great game, I just hope you can release more content and updates in the future to satisfy your player-base.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what the name suggests, a Lawn mower simulator. Starting with yourself and a small budget you build a garden care company up from the bottom using a variety of mowers and line strimmers to help you on your way. Luscious landscape graphics set in the British countryside await the player, from houses in the country to city parks each with varying levels of difficulty, whilst the backdrops are super i fear/feel the grass texture lets the game down.  I get that the programming and variables in grass are a massive challenge and the dev's have done an excellent job in the execution but in some cases the grass does not react in the way you would expect, IRL grass would spring back up slightly after being driven over, in game the grass goes down and stays down whilst it has no effect (or appears to) on completion visually it can be annoying. Flowers IRL flower density would be greater but that's neither here nor there.  Ground damage is achieved by tight turns, high speed and stupid driving its a nice touch even if a little senstive in some places. The strimmer will damage plants so watch out.Collisions, some of the clipping of in game objects could use some adjustments, you quickly learn how close to  structures and in some cases paths you can get before you incure fines whilst elsewhere driving across paths incures no fines for collisions. Controls are simple nothing to complicated the machines respond as expected, note that weather plays an effect in the game so grass becomes slippy, easier to damage, etc. ect. worth noting that I play with a controller, I understand it can be played with a keyboard, I don't know about a steering wheel set.Ground Check is an annoying addition that can be skipped but provides a bonus if completed though objects can be exceptionally difficult to find in some cases. a simple menu driven interface that is easy enough to use though it could use a better tutorial, some work could also be done to give better machinery descriptions given not all mowers can have a roller fitted (needed) for a later levels.Overall its a great game though, prepare for it becoming repeative, this won't appeal to people looking for action that said it provides a refreshing challenge and a sense of satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brilliant, cathartic escapism. I recommend without pause.Why would you want to mow virtual lawns I hear you say?Mowing's a chore, why would you play a game like this?It's hard to answer these questions without actually playing the game, but let me say...The game taps in to something about you as a gamer. Call it O.C.D, anal retentive, completionist addict or just escapist nerd.As you mow, you are in pretty countrysides, Manors and Smaller Suburban Mansions - you get to take in this life.Its just so..relaxing. There's enough game here to require your attention and skill (and the challenges if you're really into it will kick your ass!), but the general career is accessible, fun and infinite. Your business can keep running as long as you want your career to prosper.The Devs are honest and have always been clear about what was going to be and not going to be part of this game. Its a 20-Dev studio, and quite simply, with the polish and look of this title - they have outdone themselves.The game has had a few bugs here and there that have since been squashed and it is heavier on the specs compared to say the old Farming Sim Games, but this one's a keeper.Finally, the game is also a great "second-screen game". If you like to relax and have a TV show or film on a 2nd screen, this game is great for this. In terms of Sims, its up there with Euro Truck Sim and Flight Sim in it's accessbillity and relaxing demeanor. But there is something raw, more grounded. More close to home with lawn mowing, that I just cant stop playing.300Hrs and still loving this game. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I love mowing lawns but I live in Utah where it's snowy for half the year. When I saw this I thought it could be cool, but also could be a very budget-style creation. I was right the first time. this game is amazing. They are still adding some functions like trimmers and blowers at the time of the review, but it doesn't detract from the gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Mowing my lawn is something I look forward to for de-stressing, and for the most part this game scratches the itch.  If I had any complaints about the game, it is way too easy to hit things, the throttle controls are very sensitive on a controller (no desire to buy a Microsoft Elite where I can adjust this outside of a game), and instead of one transmission gear - I'd like to see multiple.  They did try to mitigate the throttle issue for keyboard players by implementing a 'cruise control' feature which made things easier when not using a controller, but it's main flaw IMHO is that it cannot be easily incremented.  Tap the gas and it will increase the speed by a varying degree, same for tapping the brake.  Also, when cutting grass to the required length - the end result looks like my yard after a drought.  Not deal breakers at all.  The graphics are good, the game is relaxing, and I look forward to updates.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and relaxing simulation game.  simple enough mechanics. can be a little repetitive at times but thats to be expected.  A good number of mowers to buy and use, all with different handling stats and accessories to buy.  the AI needs some work, so far i have never seen any of my workers get a time bonus and they crash into things alot but still making money.biggest gripe for me is the overload system, the mowers lose something here, its way to sensitive and despite having good speeds available you are forced in lots of cases to drive half speed or even slower while only cutting a tires width of grass.no key binding remapping offered as yet, hoping that comes in at some point though.other than that, the game is fun and entertaining and worth a look, just dont take it super serious.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get the obvious out of the way: this is just a lawn mowing simulator, not a landscaping similar. If you expect trimming, weeding, or blowing, you have the wrong expectations.As a lawn mowing simulator, this game scratches the itch. There's something calming and restorative about carefully mowing these pristine lawns, listening only to the hum of the motor, the birds, and passing traffic. (Though I also enjoy pairing the game with a good audio podcast). Graphics exceeded expectations. The settings are pleasant and have nice touches of realism beyond the yard you're cutting. I do find the business aspect a bit basic, and it's not a huge motivator for me. If you're looking for a reliable game you can pick up and mentally tune-out, this should do it. Oh, and make sure you have a controller.

I LEGITIMATELY DO NOT UNDERSTAND! How do you only add cruise control for ONE method and not the other? _childDocuments_.review: Update:I decided to come back to this game after not having played for a long time. My progress has been completely wiped, and I have to start over from scratch if I want to play. No thank you.Original Review:I really, really wanted to recommend this game considering how much time I spent in it, and would like to spend in it. However, it's a $30 game that plays worse than some early access games. You can't "pause" a contract and close the game. If you need to abandon the game for some reason (life happens), you have to forfeit the contract you're working on completely and start over. To avoid this, I once left my game running for no more than 30 minutes "paused" (the timer pauses so I could come back), and my entire PC locked up. I couldn't even pull up task manager (running 32 GB of RAM and a Ryzen 7 3700X CPU). "The game is fairly intensive on resources." There's more minor annoying quality of life things that I hope they improve as people report bugs (another reason why the game should be classified as early access). The throttle isn't really adjustable. It's either on at full RPMs or off. Adjusting this would make many jobs easier when the motor is so easily overloaded against tall grass. Even on a controller, reducing speed is not easy, as you use right trigger for the gas pedal vs using a joystick. The mouse sensitivity is super high. I have to lower my sens on my mouse to 400 dpi in order to not get motion sickness. There's also no edgers / trimmers, though devs have said they are in the works with no ETA. And there was an issue with steam achievements completely resetting every time the game launched, though the devs did manage to fix that within a week or so. Overall, I'm excited to see where the game goes, but I cannot recommend it for a fully released game for $30.

_childDocuments_.review: I am seeing other reviews saying there should be more to the game, that there's no string trimming or edging, etc. But I am confused because the name of the game could not be more literal as to what you get. _childDocuments_.review: Before you read any further just realize that this game is exactly as described on the tin. If you don't like mowing in real life then this won't be for you. I happen to be one of the people who find lawn mowing quite soothing.Things start easy enough with a simple rider. You can choose from a collector or a mulcher. Both are perfectly fine for the starting contracts and you'll be able to afford new mowers and hire employees soon enough. Managing your company also seems to come pretty easy and includes training your employees and advertising.The downsides to this game are that there aren't any walk behinds or weed whackers. In real life I wouldn't use a rider for detailed mowing around flower beds like you have to in this game. The other downside is that the texture used for the cut grass is almost worse than the long grass. It looks like you're scalping the lawn.One last good thing I will say though is that the dev team seem super committed to the game. They have a pretty active discord where they look for bugs and have even stated they are going to fix the cut grass texture as well as add weed whackers. Overall i'm quite impressed and only see this game improving from here!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game so far because similar to other "mundane task simulators" this one is also weirdly satisfying and enjoyable for me especially with the lite business management parts in the campaign but there are a few technical things that could easily be fixed in a patch.1: 2: Separate camera sensitivity for when you're on the mower and when on foot, I find that the sensitivity for the camera when in the mower is a bit low.3: Rebindable controls, why does a simulation game like this not have the ability to change your bindings? if it were a joke game along the lines of Surgeon Sim or Goat Sim I'd be more understanding but it looks like a lot of effort was put in here to make it more akin to Farming Sim or Flight Sim so why are there no options for either controller or keyboard and mouse users to change the bindings?4: This one is a bit more on the optional side because of Steam having deadzone settings but having deadzone settings would be nice for controller users, I'm finding that the deadzone is so tiny that I can occasionally get my controller to start drifting even though my controller is in good condition.5: Why is there 2 separate wide camera modes that have different Y axis ranges? just combine them into one.Other than that this game is exactly as expected and I'm probably gonna spend a crazy amount of time on it lol.Edit: the 1st issue I listed with the camera axis has since been fixed :D

_childDocuments_.review: First off, if you're into sim type games this will tickle your fancy.Coming from a decently long play time in many other sim type games, this game seems to do what you would expect. There's a couple things that's missing but I'm sure will come at a later date, I've viewed the discussion forums and the community hub and the devs seems to be pretty on point with customer relations.Quick and dirty: The first two lawn mowers aren't worth a damn. They get bogged down in very low height grass (I've seen others complain about this, and I have a decent understanding of how these types of mowers work in real life).The first 2 mowers need to be looked at with the bogging problems, other than that the other commercial mowers seem to do really well, I've stuck mainly with Baggers/mulchers and zero turn mowers only (that's just my preference).There are things that definitely need to be added. I would like to see more mower brands, and eventually I would like push mowers to be added too. I also think it would be really nice to have some older "retro" if you will, mowers be added in to the game.Right now, I don't think the throttle system is working 100% because you can only choose between high and off, you can't select mid-ranges or any other range..that's not how mowers in real life work.I'll be dumping many hours into this game, I can already see that. The biggest problems right now are the throttle control and bogging problems in the lower tier mowers (I know they're lower tier for a reason, but the bogging mechanics seem to be tuned way too high for those).You'll notice I didn't say anything about graphics etc.The graphics are good, some hiccups but everything seems to run just fine with everything on high. I'm running a GTX 1070 - 8gb card if anyone is wondering.Overall, the game is a solid 7.5/10 right out of the box, this could be improved upon by what was stated previously.P.S.RETRO MOWERS WOULD BE AWESOME. (I really want retro mowers) :D

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I am totally glad I decided to purchase this game. At first I was nervous, about things like the controls for PC but having played with controller, I think it plays perfectly with them. Things that I would love to eventually see for this game would be as other players stated, and I don't mean to sound like a broken record however. Firstly, Push Mowers would be a great addition for early game, as you are just starting your business, you will be doing more smaller properties like houses that only really have a small front yard and a fenced in backward  or something like that. This would help delay the player from getting mid tier mowers right off the bat. Secondly, Blowers whether it is a hand held one like stihl for the first one and then have an upgrade for a backpack blower for players that are farther in than first time players. These could be useful for players that use a chute instead of mulching or bagging, as if they do happen to get grass clippings on pavement etc. Finally, would be a weed eater or edgers of course, and mainly speaks for itself. To get all the grass away from walls, landscaping and so on.  this would be more of a final touch to a property where the progress bar wont be fully completed until they would trim after mowing everything. Overall, it's a must buy if you find mowing satisfying or just love mowing in general!

Basically, the the gameplay loop sees sees you setting out on a yard cutting business in which you'll take on agreements, update and work on your HQ, keep up with and purchase more vehicles and representatives, and at last increment your benefits and notoriety until you're landing the most esteemed positions. The entirety of this happens inside an essential menu structure, so don't expect anything too top to bottom, however it does an OK enough occupation in the change time frame between yard to grass. The management side of things is truly a pardon to keep you cutting however many yards as could reasonably be expected, however, and this is shockingly lovely pleasant practically speaking. You get on your cutter, you turn on the edges, you ensure the cutting stature is right and you've exhausted your grass clippings, and you set off attempting to cut the ideal example so you can be done as fast and productively as could really be expected. The objective is to keep away from harm, accomplish a specific degree of accuracy and complete your positions inside a set measure of time to get a pleasant reward. There are a good number of licensed mowers you can buy, and just over 30 different types of yards to cut. And in terms of gameplay, the vehicles generally handle well and are easy to get to grips with, ensuring that even if you've never touched a lawn in your life, you'll get the hang of it pretty quickly. It truly is the kind of game that radiates a helpful energy, as you thoughtlessly remove while paying attention to something like a iTunes pobcast behind the scenes. Visually, it's not awful at all either, particularly as far as the detailed characters, mowers and environments surrounding the gardens. The actual yards are OK as well — the only issue manifests when you're attempting to discover patches you've missed, and once in a while shadows and bad quality surfaces don't make those patches as clear as they ought to be. I am hoping to one day start my own company too! No White New Balances needed to play this wonderful game! Although they do help that's for sure. Now I can sit in AC while mowing the lawn! _childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to play this game. Unfortunately it was very disappointing, graphics were meh, even on ultra with a 3070. _childDocuments_.review: This game caught my eye when I saw it in the store. If you like to mow grass and whatnot, go ahead a get it, but don't expect 100+ fps at 1080p or 1440p. Depending on what hardware you have and what graphical settings you play at you may get 100+ fps on this game.Im running on a r5 2600 cpu, 16gb, 3000 mhz ram, and a rx 580 8gb and i get 25-30 fps when looking straight forward and 50 fps and above when looking up in the air (obviously it's not having to process a lot of textures). Edit: i have upgraded to an rx 6700xt and the game runs flawlessly!Overall, it's still a good/playable game. I recommend it for anyone who likes to mow lawn.
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid simulator for cutting grass. It has its bugs but it falls into the same chill simulator vibe as PowerWash Simulator which I've had a ton of chill fun with.Pros:1) There's a decent sense of progression and way more areas to mow than I thought.2) Mower upgrades are awesome and feels rewarding after finally upgrading to a better mower.3) Being able to offload tedious work to employees while you pick up litter is pretty hilarious and the fastest way to progress.4) The physics are actually really well done and it's actually hard in some instances to go fast. I've done so many poor jobs and striping is pretty difficult to do fast. But it shows how much better I can do and learn compared to some people in the discord doing crazy cuts.5) The developers are VERY responsive on Discord and reviews and have an awesome presence and just want to make their game work great, eventually.Cons (really, the bugs):1) There's an issue with the camera where the Y Axis flip gets reset if you're in third person or something, it's unfortunately easier to deal with if you just play with default controls.2) I personally get issues where I have to restart the game after every mission else I get 100% usage on my 3080 and choppy inputs. This isn't so bad since you can set up everything, back out and a restart is very quick.3) There's only 2 employees so you hit a productivity ceiling pretty early on. You get 5 jobs eventually in the upper ranks and it feels unfortunate to have to really choose what you want to prioritize (money or RP) every 'day'.4) I think early game progression is a little too long, since the early jobs don't pay much and it can be really tedious to invest 20-30 minutes to each mow on the early mowers. Then you get to a point where you can rain money and RP in when you have 2 employees, do litter jobs that take a literal minute to do then you get the instant benefits of those 10-15 minute cuts since the employees do an ok job. I think this needs to be balanced, it's nice when you get there... but getting there is painful.5) There's (in my opinion) too small of a gap between HQ upgrades and the costs. I think it would be good to add an extra employee with the last one or some other perks and maybe raise the costs?6) The UI is quick to navigate once you've learn it but it has some issues. The attachment system is confusing since it relies on vague UI and physically modeled the attachments on the mower. If you don't know what everything looks like and own the same types of mowers this can be a little unclear. I have done circles around figuring out and relearning how to fire an employee. If you drill into the hiring menu, you have to back out and it doesn't reset when you navigate to it again. Not sure if resetting to the top level when you enter a tab is the best experience or not. I also wish there was a way to fix all of your parts on the mower fast. Right now you have to drill into each mower's menu, go to Maintenance, click on all 4-5 of the tabs, then hit Full Repair or whatever. Multiply that by the amount of mowers you have. I'd love a quick Repair All to Max button on the first page. I don't particularly like the bottom options menu since they take up a lot of space without providing a lot of functionality due to all the sub menus. I get it helps for consoles that need large UI but I think it could be improved by adding better optimized options.Overall it's a great game, looks decently pretty for an indie Unity game (Not knocking that, I love Unity) very chill or challenging depending on playstyle and the mechanics are way more thought out than you'd expect. Many locations, only 3 types of modes for now but the amount of maps make all the cuts so different. Awesome dev team, which is the #1 thing to me, this game is solid and decently fun right now and I imagine in time it'll be an amazing chill gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there are a few glitches and bugs to be hammered out. That being said, overall, I feel that this game is worth the current price as long as the developers continue to optimize and release new content for the game. Currently, there seems to be some serious optimization issues with the game, that causes stuttering with even 2xxx or 3xxx Nvidia GPUs. Alongside this, there are some minor other issues, such as key bindings or unsported wheel input devices. Despite these things, I am inclined to give this game a positive review. I quick pop into the official discord shows that the developers are aware of the current issues, and they are even planning for future expansions of the game, including hand mowers and trimmers. This game does not appear to be a quick "cash grab", but rather something that they hope to further refine and expand upon. That being said, if you want to avoid some minor headaches and optimization issues, I would advise you avoid purchasing this game until these issues are resolved. Otherwise, this game is a fantastic time burner and excels at being a landscaping company simulation.

_childDocuments_.review: Strangely addicitive. I am compelled to keep playing. Three contracts (lawns)  done and I feel a sense of accomplishment and pride in my work. Overall extremely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy mowing my lawn and looked forward to playing this game just to see what it was like. As it's name suggest sit's a lawn mowing simulator. There are other aspects that goes into taking a care of a lawn but at least for now the game is focused on mowing which is fine by me. Overall it's a relaxing sim that doesn't require a lot of thought. One of the most enjoyable aspects of lawn care is the relaxing nature of it and I think the game accomplishes this. ProsStriping is fun and I'm glad they included this in the gameAs stated earlier very relaxingI guess my graphics card is better than most but the graphics look just fine to me (GTX 3070)Controls are easy to navigate (may require some tweaking in the settings)Love the before and after shots Cons:In the future it would be nice to see different grass types as they have different mowing heights and requirements. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:Controller seems to work fine now, no more issues.First, sorry for my English.Second, I’m leaving thumps up for now since there is no option for a mixed thump, hope to see it improve.Definitely has potential to be a great Sim game... but still needs optimization work.The environment looks really great.If everything works, it's actually pretty relaxing(even better with music of your choice) like ETS2 cruising level relaxing.Buttons, levers, and pedals are animated.(Unfortunately, there's no first-person body)Vehicle Maintenance, blades, engine, fuel.Controls..well controls.... you can not change keybindings(minor issue).1.)Fixed with Cruise Control.  2.)More Graphic options and optimization. Between Normal and Very High there doesn't seem to be much of a difference, my gpu either way runs at over 90% with occasional frame drops.(40-60 with rtx2060 at 1440p)(Well, more just more... mowers, missions and locations lol)Definitely some hand mowers, for more delicate work. And other stuff you need for mowing?A first person body would be nice.More environment sounds.Better looking end result grass. The grass looks great just after cutting it doesnt look that good anymore. Or maybe I'm just nature-loving lolMaybe change the ground check mechanic. The timer is somewhat annoying, and it would be fun if there would be some remaining stuff in the grass for added challenge.Mod support.
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Has Potential if i could rate it neutral i would and would recommend once they fix a few things.I play all the sim games cars, trucks, trains, planes, boats, tractors, so this is my kind of game and it is decent but has some flaws.UI: Menu alot of the time the back button on the controller or keyboard doesn't work and i have to use the mouse to click back.As people have said settings are very limited cant change keybinds, no ultrawide resoultions. While my logitech wheel does work some what, the turning is incredibly stiff, feels like fighting against the force feedback of the wheel so i decided to just use a controller instead.Very difficult to exit the game took me a moment to figure it out.Gameplay:Most part it is good camera views i find to be nice and easy to manage, cutting of the grass is satisfying.Some issues however:Throttle why even bother if its 0 or 100, i would replace throttle with gears slow to fast as is the case with most lawn mowers they run at a constant RPM but you select the gear you want there fore the speed you travel this will help with the next issue.Going down hills, slight down hill no matter how lightly i press the trigger the mower over speeds so to get down hills is stop start, problem could be resolved with the gear selection as mentioned, that will also help with people playing using keyboard.Scoring system needs reworking, you get a $20 bonus for sprinting around the yard picking up objects, but only $1-2 bonus for completing under time and no bonus for cutting 100% of the grass. Once you reach the % target its in your best interest to just go back to the trailer even if that means leaving a big patch of uncut grass. Too much emphasis on the time it takes you, yes maybe you get penalised if you take a really long time but most people play these kind of games because they are relaxing not to try and do things as quickly as possible.Sure people have mentioned more tools weed whackers hand mowers etc and yes if these were introduced would take it to another level but i did get this game knowing it was lawnmower simulator, not garden maintenance simulator.Customisation: Has your standard options which is fine. However company logo selection you cant change the colour so unless you want a uniform that goes with green you have to not display your company logo on shirt.I'm writing this review because i see the devs responding and just wanted to give some honest feedback. I enjoy the game but because of a few of these issues and for the price and wouldn't currently recommend. If they fix the problems particularly the UI side of it i would be happy to edit this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game so far. Using a keyboard is hell on your hand, so it is best to your a controller. With that being said, there are some issues with controller support, namely the game wouldn't let me pause with the controller during a contract. Game has room to grow and I am excited to see where the devs take it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The joy of cutting grass on a ride on mower and the feeling of accomplishment, without the hassle or heat or real mowing. One critique is they need to add a freshly trimmed grass smell feature - that would be bliss. EDIT: After playing for over 24 hours, I still enjoy the game, but there are some major issues. Super expensive mowers that can't mow 8 inches of grass without the engine breaking down - which is some unrealistic nonsense. That and you are only allowed 2 employees, who are very easy to max out, as well as a ton of repeat jobs and lack of diversity. This game is NOT early access, yet it has all the missing pieces of an EA game. It needs work and updates, and it should have been done before release. I cannot recommend this game in its current form..

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always down for a relaxing game that has content.  So far I am hooked, I get to start off as just a single guy with a single mower, and I get to grow a business through hard work.  I used to move semi professionally and this is really taking me back.  I'm really looking forward to seeing what the community does with mods (hopefully they are allowed).  This could a be an even better game/sim than it already is.
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is pretty addictive. However, with that being said, the game is still bugged as if it were a Beta still. When turning on pavement, bricks, or another surface besides grass, you can still get fined for destroying the yard. The menu is bugged, you can't go back to previous screens after you select an option. The RPM is all or nothing, you can't selected a specific range. The aspect of the multiple contracts, good range of mowers, and overall good quality graphics. This game could be a major simulator with some tweeks. Look forward to more mowing!
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: First few 'missions' down and the game is pretty good. Relaxing. But it is definitely lacking some polish in the UI department.- I really struggled to get it to recognize my XBOX controller, which it finally did, without explanation, after a few minutes of leaving the game open and in the menu screen.- There is no pause button. So once you start mowing, you can't stop! Don't even think about changing game settings once you start mowing because there is no way to access any of the menus once you start.- Many of the controller buttons on the menu screens don't work (start button for options, 'B' button for back, etc). I have to use the keyboard buttons which then change my control settings from controller to mouse/keyboard.- The game lacks any additional tools for your lawn care company. Miss a tight spot near a garden, curb or fence? Unless you can get your mower deck in there, you're out of luck. It would be nice to have other implements (Weed Whacker, hand mower, etc). Sounds and graphics are decent and the game runs reasonably smooth. I haven't tried it with a wheel (I can barely get the controller to work). If you are looking for a relaxing excuse to avoid mowing your real lawn, or you want to fantasize about owning a ride-on mower instead of using your legs like a peasant, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lawn Mowing Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Experience the beauty and detail of mowing the Great British countryside in Lawn Mowing Simulator, the only simulator that allows you to ride an authentic and expansive roster of real-world licensed lawn mowers from prestigious manufacturers; Toro, SCAG and STIGA as you manage your mowing business.

name: Demeo
detailed_description: Adventurers, it’s time to unite! A dark force has taken over the underworld in the RPG dungeon crawler, Demeo, and it’s a world you’re not likely to survive alone. Demeo is a cross-platform cooperative adventure for up to four players that recreates all of the magic and camaraderie of gathering around a tabletop with friends to do battle against the forces of evil. Assume the role of the eagle-eyed hunter, mystical sorcerer, deadly assassin, protective guardian, melodic bard, powerful warlock or boisterous barbarian. But choose your heroes wisely in this cooperative adventure, for once players have accepted their quest, they must work together to vanquish the unholy force that corrupts everything... or die trying. Our story originated inside the Elven Necropolis — but that was just a mere overture! Following the first Demeo adventure, The Black Sarcophagus, players have already explored the Realm of the Rat King and Roots of Evil — and with our latest adventure, Reign of Madness, they’ll venture into the town of Ends for the first time and meet Demeo’s newest playable character Uhrak, the Barbarian who is never more than a grappling hook’s throw away from the action. Gathering friends for a night of casting spells, rolling dice, and moving miniatures are some of your fondest memories -- and now you can have this same experience with players from anywhere in the world! Demeo recreates all the fun of tabletop dungeon crawling in the digital space by connecting players for table talk, treasure hunts, and plenty of turn-based action with infinite replayability. It’s dangerous to go alone! Grab your friends and assemble a party, because exploring the depths of Demeo requires strategy, cunning, and teamwork. Every character has their own unique approach to managing magic and monsters — and they’ll need to work together if they want to survive! Take the mantle of the hunter, sorcerer, assassin, guardian, bard, warlock or barbarian, all with their own unique abilities and skills, and use them wisely if you are ever to vanquish the darkness that is Rackarn and Alfaragh. Join your fellow adventurers in Heroes’ Hangout (VR only), a social space where players can meet and share their stories of treacherous quests and tantalizing encounters. Come together with new friends to start your next Demeo adventure together, or pal around as you play archery and arcade mini-games, paint miniatures, learn tips, listen to cassettes on the boombox, customize your avatar and more. Take your battle against the forces of evil with you wherever you go! Demeo: PC Edition has been optimized for Steam Deck, bringing the game’s native controller support to Valve’s popular handheld device. It’s never been easier to jump into a game of Demeo with friends right in the very same room. Go on an adventure with friends no matter which device they play on! Demeo supports cross-play multiplayer across its entire ecosystem. Form your party with players on Steam, PlayStation 5, PS VR2, Quest, Pico, and more!

It’s never been easier to jump into a game of Demeo with friends right in the very same room. Go on an adventure with friends no matter which device they play on! Demeo supports cross-play multiplayer across its entire ecosystem. Form your party with players on Steam, PlayStation 5, PS VR2, Quest, Pico, and more!
short_description: Adventurers, it’s time to unite! Gather your friends and battle the dark forces that have overtaken the world of Resolution Games' award-winning RPG dungeon crawler, Demeo. The next generation of tabletop adventure has arrived!

_childDocuments_.review: I would absolutely recommend this game, but there's PROs and CONs to this.PROs: - this is a very challenging game that requires collaborative teamwork among the party of characters you choose whether you're doing single player or playing with others if you are going to survive. Having someone go rogue only leads to pain and suffering - such as jumping into the fray without backup/support, or opening doors when the team isn't ready yet - leading to more aggro'd baddies.- The challenge makes completing each floor very satisfying- The visuals look fantastic. The level of detail in the design was really well done!- Despite the difficulty of the game, the challenge keeps it interesting. However, once you figure out what works, it's hard to stray from that...making replayability not the greatest.CONs:- There's really no reason this came out in VR first. Sure, it looks cool - but it took me a while to realize I can use the joysticks to TILT THE TABLE so my neck doesn't suffer from looking down for so long.- The balance of characters is a little off. The sorcerer and bard are 100% support units, but need a little more offensive capability - especially the bard- The balance of enemies needs improvement. After about turn #3, you're constantly under attack - especially after you complete the first floor. New enemies can spawn anywhere in a spot where your party doesn't have vision, which also includes the starting point you spawned. So while you're trying to push forward, and maybe earn a break to regroup, you've also got enemies behind you ambushing you.- There's little chance to get a breather and regroup especially after the first floorWhat I'd like to see in future updates:- ***If you play multiplayer but don't have all 4 spots filled, it'd be nice to still be able to run 4 heroes- Playable custom maps from the community- Build your own character -> attributes, abilities, and cards...could be fun!- Enemies not as aggressive - or at least slow the respawn rate - especially when not in sight (or at least within a certain range of the characters) so players can potentially have a turn to heal & regroupOverall, it's a great game. I definitely do not regret buying it. There's still room for improvement, just like most games :)

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game is fun and polished. The problem is, there is no variety or progression. Maybe in a few months it will be worth the money, but it isn't right now. And that's what's holding this back from being a enthusiastic thumbs up. Here is how the game goes:You jump into a multiplayer game (or start your own) and pick a character: wizard, knight, archer, or assassin. Each is different and fun in its way. You then jump into a randomly generated 3D dungeon. Problem is, even though they are randomly generated, they feel identical to the last one you played. They are cool and detailed, but also grey. No color, no change of scenery, just a randomly generated dungeon map that feels just like the last one you played. You and your team fight your way to the guy with the key and kill him. then you take the key to the gate to finish the level.You then visit a store to buy and sell cards with the gold you found in piles in various location on the dungeon floor. Then you go to level two. Level two is a slightly larger randomly generated dungeon that looks practically the same as level one. You kill the guy with the key, find the gate, and go back to the store.The third floor is always exactly the same. It's the smallest and always has the same monsters and the Elf Hag Queen. Kill her and you immediately win. But, after the first time it loses its luster. Sure you get XP and can unlock a new mask or dice color. But, that's it.The graphics are very nice, the game play is fun and intuitive, the game has very few technical issues and runs very well. The problem is, after playing for seven hours and beating it by myself once and with a group of others twice, I'm getting bored of it. Now, in the Summer a free expansion is coming. What that includes I have no idea. There will be no progression yet, but there will be new classes. A/so, hopefully, new maps, new cards, and new bosses. Maybe if they opened it up for modding then others could add some variety while we wait for expansions.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most fun I've had in VR, and that's saying something. Brings a convincing sense of being in the same room with a group of friends playing a fantasy board game, without the hassle of setting everything up or having to retrieve the dice from behind the sofa. In fact it's difficult to emphasise just how big of a deal it is having that sense of presence here. The game itself is compelling stuff. It's not particularly complicated to play, but there's plenty of depth available. The main criticism I've seen is that there's only one campaign, which is true at the time of writing (more are coming), but I've played through it five times in the past couple of days and each one felt unique. Dungeon layout, monsters and items are randomised, and it plays out very differently each time. In fact, each new situation feels unique, giving plenty of room for different tactical approaches that keep replayability fresh. What the game does particularly well is that sense of being overwhelmed at times but being able to pull everyone through using your tactical genius! The visual and sound effects are very well done, the pieces feel like hand-painted models, and there's a real sense of quality to the entire game. Jumping in and out of games, setting up games, it's all handled with ease. It is easily one of the best VR games I've played.There are a few issues right now, although nothing major. There's no mid-campaign save at all, which means you better have 2 hour plus set aside! This is being addressed soon though according to the devs. Each of the four characters is interesting and has pros and cons, but the mage probably needs some tweaking; really, just more to do particularly in the early game. Mages rely on cards for their power, but without them their tactical options are limited. There may be a few minor bugs as well, but we didn't really notice anything serious. But I have confidence that the devs will fix and improve this game based on their track record.So yeah, an excellent game and don't be afraid to jump right in and start having a blast. There's more content coming soon, but if you're worried about replayability I'd say there's plenty to be had already if you have a group of players enjoying themselves. The game plays fine solo as well, where you take on the roles of all the characters, but there's no doubt it's much better in a group.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish you could choose something between thumbs up and down, let me tell you why!First of the game is a lot of fun, both solo and multiplayer! You get to play a classic type of table top rpg but in vr where everything is animated and and spells have pretty effects and it all looks great! The game is also quite challenging which I'm totally cool with but I can understand if people would like some difficulty settings.You get to play through 3 levels, 2 of which have a random layout but they all have the same theme (grey, dark dungeon) and the last one seems to be the same since it's the boss room.Which brings us to my biggest gripe with the game; that's it, that's all you get.. there is only 1 boss as of now which would be fine if this was a $10-15 game but it's 30 buckeroonos which feels pretty steep for a game you can play through in a little over an hour. There are also plenty of bugs, especially when playing multiplayer, like getting stuck in the loading screen and eventually just getting stuck in a black void, not being able to open doors and enemies sometimes being able to target you when there is no way they have line of sight (through walls and closed doors) just to name a few.They will be releasing more adventures and new bosses later on and the bugs can get patched but right now this is essentially an early access game for $30 marketed as a full game which is kind of a bummer because I was really looking forward to it.TLDR; what's here is fun but really bareboned for the price (1-3 hours of content) and the multiplayer has a bunch of glitches atm.

_childDocuments_.review: Demeo is a fantastic game and a D&D fanboy's wetdream. The game looks, sounds and plays fantastic, but I'm going to have to not recommend it for now, since I've yet to finish a single full game. I've had 3 hard crashes mid game and a game where the key glitched and would not let us complete the level. It's super frustrating to be invested in a game and with random friends you found online, just for the game to crash and not be able to join again.  The game finder is lackluster, the only way to play with randoms is either creating a game and waiting for someone to hopefully join you or doing a "quick match" which 80% of the time will join you with a party that lost a member due to a crash. The game also only has 1 campaign at the moment, ONE. So you have probably a couple of hours of fresh, awesome content and then, well, nothing. They've already announced they're releasing a new campaign this summer, but to have the balls to release a game as a full release (it's not early access), have such a limited amount of content and no custom campaigns is kind of insulting. Hopefully we get more content and a fix for all the crashes and bugs, because the game is a lot of fun, I hope I get to finish a full game some day.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of potential, but it needs some kind of progression besides cosmetics. Maybe a custom deck for each class that you could earn stronger cards for. Useful unlocks help keep your playerbase engaged.  It feels like a really good start for a VR tabletop rpg, but not quite a whole game yet. Online can be tons of fun, but the whole experience is ruined with p2p networking. No servers means no way to browse available matches by latency or region, and with a time investment per match of 1.5 to 3 hours, it can be very frustrating to make it all the way to the end only to get disconnected due to someones poor internet. It's also real annoying how enemies always know where you are and move through the fog of war to hunt you down. It's not really a dungeon crawler so much as zergfest that you try and survive until the guy with the key comes to you. It really limits your ability to play tactically and clear rooms as a group. The fact that you can never truly clear a floor because enemies constantly spawn in any dark areas of the map you can see only add to this problem. Devs priorities are all over the place as well. Biggest new thing coming up is the 2D version. Unless they plan on giving the 2D version away for free to increase the playerbase, I don't really see the point. There is not nearly enough content is this game to play it outside of VR. It's too bad, it really feels like one of those games that is just one or two good design choices away from being a huge hit.

_childDocuments_.review: Demeo is a Co-Op, turn based, dungeon-crawler. Play solo or with up to 4 players, hunt down the key, find the door and escape to the next floor. The 3rd and final floor is where a fairly upset Boss resides. Take'em out, win the game. Sounds simple, right? Well, that depends on you and your crew.The game itself is loosely D&D-esque but without the D&D b.s. [...and to each their own] No numbers and time spent building characters, and dialogue .... ugh, not here, just pick a Hero and start playing.   There currently are 5 Adventures/Books in this Eleven King Saga to play. [Hopefully more after they complete the Official D&D game Hasbro tapped them to do, but no official word from Demeo on more content] Each Adventure feels unique and has a unique Boss to battle as well. The first Book, Black Sarcophagus, is considered to be a good one to start for new players compared to the other 4. The 2nd, Rat King, is arguably the hardest. With the 5th Book as the conclusion, sort of speak. There are 7 Champions to choose from, each with their own strengths. The Guardian, Mage, Assassin, Hunter, Bard, Warlock, and Barbarian.I had just recently bought this again for Steam so I have ~45 hrs. in the game here but ~3k total hours on Quest 2/PC Edition. Most of the negative reviews I see are from players that don't "understand" the game. Opinions are fine, but judging because of ignorance is, ignorant. In this game you may actually die and not win, lol. And that should be okay. It is in failing that you try and play again, but with the knowledge from last matches "mistakes/lessons". There isn't a carry over Leveling System (and that turns some ppl off) but the Heroes can 'Level Up' throughout a match. I enjoy it that way. The only difference between players is the knowledge of the game from multiple play-throughs and not Levels, otherwise my Level 853 Hunter doesn't need your Level 5 Bard, lol. This game when it's all said and done is a very large Chess Match. Once the enemies actions are learned and "accounted for", it's nothing more than Chess: Demeo Edition. In Demeo the enemies will spawn from the darkness within each dungeon. So therefore, it is best to keep moving if possible. Meaning that you can't "clear" a floor of mobs. (Again, may turn some ppl off) but it's with the 'danger of dying' that ushers you to move, find the Key and go to the Door. Demeo can punish those that get greedy. Staying together is another good idea. If you get Downed, it is nice to be within reach of a team mate to be helped back up. The best part is ... it's in all in glorious VR, where you can 'be on the board', pickup most pieces in the game read/learn their attributes, etc. The Co-Op aspect is also something special as well. Demeo is crossplay, so you can play with other platforms as well as from other countries. Language barrier, problems? Nope. You can draw. Which, doesn't sound like much but is HUGE. You can usually figure out what someone is "saying" by drawing lines to enemies, chests, etc. Communication really helps in this game. It is nice to 'talk through a scenario' before acting to make sure "we're on the same page", BUT ultimately, it is your turn, however you'd like to take it.No VR? no problem. If you purchase it on Steam or Quest (Meta, yuck) you get the PC Edition FREE or vice versa. With PC Edition you can zoom in and such and it looks super clear and crisp and it does have it's pros but in VR the game really does pop but after a year and a half of having a 3lbs device strapped to my face ... I'm good. I enjoy the PC Edition just as much as the VR version. The VR versions (not PS5) also have Heroes' Hangout where players can meet up, set up a game, play a retro arcade game, jump into the painting room, shoot some arrows and more.It is turn based, so it can sometimes take a minute or so to formulate a plan and execute. The first Book usually takes about an hour on average with the other Books taking sometimes much longer. Depending on various thing: The Adventure being played, player knowledge, number of mobs, number of players, roll of the die, etc. Most plays are 1 to 2hrs. give or take. The longest match I've had was ~4.5 hrs. with 3 new players on the 4th Book .... and we lost, LOL. BUT even though you may lose a match or so, you'll of had a GOOD TIME PLAYING. And that's rare in games today. When a player loses, most times it feels bad and you'd get mad or upset and although it doesn't feel 'good', not ever once was I upset with the playing of the game itself as opposed to the decisions that led up to our timely demise. This game feels fun, even when you lose and with more knowledge comes quicker/better solutions.And remember, this game is not a rushed type of scenario. Relax. Tilt the board to your liking. Stand up, Sit back or Lay down .... and Roll the die. Happy Hunting Champions.

_childDocuments_.review: (Full Review video below!)Demeo is a breath of fresh air for veteran VR players and a wonderful game for everyone that's just getting into VR. It's a VR RPG Board Game Dungeon Crawler (1-4 players) where you can choose from 4 different characters and complete dungeon crawling campaigns. With the ability to cross-play with EVERYONE (Steam & Oculus currently with plans to bring it to Rift in 2ish weeks and EVENTUALLY to PC) this will be a juggernaut of a game in the next few years with a ton of content.The graphics and atmosphere truly make you feel like you are sitting around with your friends playing a good old dnd board game. The incredible thing being done here is the AUTOMATION via AI and ANIMATION of taking any action during your turn. It's a blast to move your character and watch them attack or cast spells and really brings the game to life.The camera controls combined with the ability to play this game literally ANYWHERE on a wireless headset makes this game a slam dunk addition to ANY VR library for everyone of all ages.The gameplay is engaging and really forces you to cooperate with other players (single player you get 3 characters so you can beat it alone!) and strategize with them to really make every move and attack count!The main drawback currently is it's SHORT on content. This isn't necessarily a bad thing because Resolution Games has a long history of delivering fresh content to many of their older games and they already have plans to bring a ton of FREE content (starting this Summer!) to Demeo.Buy this game and support a great company!
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Demeo is quite fun! They recently added a 2-player co-op mode (where each player controls two characters), as well as a non-VR version, and I think they're working on additional content, so it's great to see the game being supported.In terms of gameplay, the game has some flaws. Enemies route towards the players (and will open doors getting to you), and new enemies will spawn in, so in the process of clearing a dungeon floor it never feels like you're ever done. In fact, it seems that the biggest difficulty is supposed to come from the fact that if you're too slow (and not killing enemies fast enough), you will get swarmed, so, the pressure always feels high. I really wish the game relied less on swarms and more on deeper combat mechanics that require more strategizing, tactical and co-operative play. Ideally, a bit of both worlds would be great.All in all, the game is very enjoyable, and luckily the community has made some mods available that allow you to turn off monster respawning and routing, more can be found here:

_childDocuments_.review: Great coop DnD style dungeon crawler. Much more fun than I expected. The gameplay, controls and graphics are very nicely polished. I found it extremely fun to play with a friend and, in a positive way, very addictive. The game is only lacking a save feature and more content. Both is being worked on. Currently there is only one campaign consisting of three randomly generated levels and 4 character classes to play. After 17 hours we've beaten the campaign several times over with every character combination, so now we're desperately waiting for new levels and characters to be released which are promised for free for summer 2021.Also the balancing will need a bit of tweaking. The tank and assassin are way way stronger than the hunter and especially the wizard. And eg a healing card for one character costs 50 gold and one for 4 characters costs 500. Nothing game breaking but there is lots of room for optimisation.It takes us about 3 hours to finish the 3 levels and you cannot save in between so we ended up letting the game run idle for hours when we needed to take a break. Which sometimes resulted in in laggy performance and graphics bugs which we never encountered during regular gameplay. It's a great game and I appreciate the developers decision to release a very polished base game with little content instead of the other way around. It's much easier to add content than to polish a game after release. I also appreciate that additional free content is coming.It's it worth 25€ in its current state? Absolutely!
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Lets talk about some problems with the game really quick.Yeah, there's only one dungeon right now. You'd think this would be a problem, but Resolution did a great job of randomizing some aspects to make each run feel a little different than the last.Is the default view kinda painful? Yeah, but you can press up on the left thumb stick to change your angle of view. Is Archer OP? Yes, now stop talking about it before you ruin everything for me!!!OFC, there are some weird glitches, some latency issues, disconnects, etc. Have Faith. Resolution will address these things sooner rather than later, this only came out a little bit ago after all.And yes, you can spawn enough friendly pets to literally pin yourself in the spawn, unable to escape, pinned in by spiders and rats and other nasties. And that sucks, I don't have anything positive to say about it, it's just a lame way to end a run.That all aside, this game tickles all the right parts for me. I'm a gigantic DND nerd. Been playing since 3.5. When I first saw the trailer for this, I knew I had to get it, no question. And Man, am I glad I did. The detail in the environments, the models, the player tokens... phenomenal.The gameplay is great single player (archer solo ftw) but it's absolutely better with more players. The amount of fun just grows with each player you add, and the weird stuff that I've seen other player's pull has been hilarious.BBG coming in to punch the archer? Pin him in the corner with some barricades and throw some poison gas at him is exactly what I'd expect my players to do if I was DMing and it's beautiful. Running around as all archers is even funnier, because honest to god, that endless army of pets is just broken!And of course, being a dice goblin by trade, being able to unlock shiny, new clicky clacky rocks is perfect. tl;dr, do you like TTRPG's? Pick this up.I cannot wait for the next dungeon! HYPED!

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a lot to make me write a review, and even more for a positive. This is one of the best vr experiences I’ve had and that’s saying something. Does it need more content? Yes! However the groundwork for something epic is here. If the devs really do drop content like they have announced then I can see replay ability here. _childDocuments_.review: I did not get this game for free but I did buy it in a multi-game bundle that was for a Black Friday sale. Despite that, even at full price, this game in VR is significantly worth it's bang for its buck. When I saw what I believe to be a simple board game in VR I figured I'd maybe get a dozen hours out of it at best.But I was wrong. Very wrong. I've logged about 42 hours into this game and can finally say that I've truly finished all of the online portion of it. There is indeed an entire figure painting and portrait painting system within this game that I have not touched but I'm also not interested in. And you can also play every single one of the five campaigns in a single player Lobby if you do not wish to deal with other people. Personally, I feel like that defeats the purpose of buying this for online but to each their own.With that said, the community in this game is absolutely fantastic. I have never at any point in time stumbled Upon A group of people arguing or fighting in any capacity nor did I hear any awful racial comments or anything like that. Everybody has been extremely kind and everyone seems more than willing to teach each other through new campaigns and mechanics. The community is absolutely one of the best I've encountered.Now let's get to the game itself. At the time that I'm writing this, there are five campaigns. The first campaign is so crazy easy that it feels like you would be playing that more for the social aspect or while you're learning. The second campaign, the rat king, can be extremely annoying especially if you have people who don't know what they're doing. The third campaign, the roots of evil, is personally the one I feel is the best. There are no crazy annoying mechanics and there are no hard to understand concepts for new players. Whether you end up in an experienced group or a new group, you're pretty guaranteed to have a good time. The fourth campaign, some sort of desert serpents, it has an annoying mechanic but all in all can be quite enjoyable in a lot of fun. Honestly, out of every campaign this one is probably my favorite as far as the two levels leading up to the boss fight. My only issue with this particular campaign is that despite trying multiple multiple times I could never seem to find a group who was willing to actually play the boss correctly. Every single group I got paired with always wanted to cheat and glitch the boss to death which completely killed all the fun of this campaign. Which is a real shame because this one is definitely one of the best ones. The newest campaign that just came out on December 15th 2022, some evil Elven King, this campaign can be incredibly painfully annoying especially if you end up in a group of people who don't know or don't care to play the mechanic. In this one, in both levels leading up to the boss there is a mob that will spawn portals that will then spawn continuous moms and if they are left unchecked, you will become overrun and lose the campaign. It slows progress significantly to do this correctly but every time I get placed in a game with kids or people who have never played it before and just want to ignore the mechanics always ends up as a failed group and a waste of my time. But this fifth campaign's final boss is probably the most fun final boss in the entire game. I truly enjoy every moment with this final boss but even after just playing at three times I feel like I've played through every campaign on every character class that I'm interested in and I just don't have the will to continue playing it. But don't take this as a bad thing. This game was so incredibly enjoyable that I was able to get way more value out of my money on this product than any game I've purchased in quite a long time.You will without a doubt enjoy this game if you're a fan of tabletop RPG games and just lack people to play it with in real life. Imagine having a tabletop game where every time you felt like playing it you could just instantly teleport your friends to your location to play. This is some of the best VR use I've seen in quite some time.The game is great, the community is great, the challenge is definitely there, and there are multiple ways to play the game in both online and solo. Although I'm personally done playing it, it's definitely a game with a lot of replay value and it certainly has everything you would need to keep coming back
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: So I have now played the 2nd episode (Realm of the Rat King) for 5-6 hours. And somehow it's very unfun. Let's review:* The dungeons are now "dark" - instead of line of sight visibility, you have 2 tiles of visibility. Sure, you can waste time and money putting down a couple torches, but it feels like they tried to nerf the archer with a much less fun game mechanic. Playing in a dark dungeon feels like stumbling around in the dark - you won't be able to see enemies until they're right next to you.* Something is wonky with the RNG. One game, we had crit after crit. The next game we had miss after miss. If there ever is a time to play with the RNG to make it feel more "fair", this would be it. A game session where 1/3 of your rolls are misses is not a fun session.* On most turns in the dark dungeon, the dice usually vanishes as soon as I throw it and the game lags for a second. Physics bug? Is this also why my game started lagging behind my friend's game by 3-5 seconds? Who knows?* They must have heard people complaining about how easy the first episode is, and cranked up the difficulty by... spawning tons of grunts? It has become a slog fighting through a gazillion spiders, rats, slimes, and more rats. And there still is no adjustment of difficulty based on team size, so they solved the problem of being too easy for 2 players by making it hard enough to require 4 players.=== ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW ===Wait to buy this game.In its current state, Demeo is a very short game. It consists of 3 dungeon levels, and is beaten in about 2-3 hours. Once you beat it, you can of course replay the game over and over, but there are only 4 classes and you will see the same randomized monsters and item cards from your previous runs.The game balance also seems a little wonky. There doesn't seem to be any difficulty adjustment based on number of players (2 players will face the same number of monsters as 4 players), yet it's easy enough to win with just 2 players of the same class. More mechanics that give different classes synergies would be appreciated, along with some sort of difficulty adjustment.It's also one of those games that doesn't really need to be in VR. Yes, it's fun zooming in and looking at the nice art - like playing with intricately painted miniatures. But the core gameplay is clicking and dragging things, and indeed they are promising a non-VR version of the game "soon". (Will it be a separate purchase? Unclear.)The developer is promising additional adventures, but I would hold off on purchasing until they follow through with the promise. They have also promised a Rift version for the Oculus store (unclear why it's not released, but the Steam version supports Rift anyways) and a non-VR PC version.
