_childDocuments_.review: Not (currently) for me. The game can be pretty fun for a while, but it falls short in some important areas in my opinion and I think the content on offer for the price is lacking, though that part may change as they add new campaigns.I have 2 main issues with the game beyond the amount of content. The first will hopefully be fixed--the amount of bugs and lag. I played through the campaign with a few friends and the first floor worked pretty much exactly as expected. Once we got to the second floor, however, everything slowed down. We'd have up to a minute between turns, by which I mean we'd use the first half of a character's turn, then the second would be unresponsive for at least 30 seconds before it would allow us to move or play a card. This happened on every single turn until we got fed up and closed the game. I imagine this will be fixed over time, so it's not a major concern for me, though the ability to save your progress on a run would be very appreciated for situations like that one as I imagine a restart would have corrected the issue.The second issue I have is with the design of the game, so I doubt it will be addressed, and if it is, it will likely take longer. I felt that there was very little depth to the actual gameplay. Coming from more involved tabletop and turn based games, the options available to the player, especially in co-op where you may only control one character, are very limited. You can interact with the environment in very shallow ways and the cards you get that would expand your abilities in any significant way are best held for moments when they're needed which are few and far between. The result is that each turn tends to be using the same ability or abilities as the previous turn, occasionally substituting movement instead. So basically, you wait for your friends to go through their turns, knowing exactly what you'll be doing when your turn comes around and rarely having to adapt or think on your toes. It gets repetitive quickly and the difficulty just isn't there to keep things interesting in my opinion. More classes may help, or maybe a leveling system that has your character gain new permanent abilities, but as it currently works, it's just not particularly fun.These gripes aside, the game is very well made and still pretty enjoyable, at least for a single play through (if you don't get bugged out like we did). There's potential here for the game to become something really cool and the presentation is great. If I see that the new content comes out and changes are made to make things more strategic, I'd happily pick the game up again to give it another shot, but I think the current amount of content and the issues I've mentioned make the asking price of $30 too high. $15-20 and an early access tag would make a lot more sense in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Sega Demo Disk?It’s a game about optimizing Tabletop Simulator’s VR mode specifically to do one thing, lying to yourself and saying you’re going to play one “quick” game, hoarding money, making choices, making mistakes, wishing the enemies stopped blowing each other, and the good ol’ fashioned joy of playing Tabletop RPG combat with friends.The game plays like an RPG tabletop simulator, where you are given a randomly-picked/generated map with random POI, enemy spawns, and gold spawns. POI’s consist of treasure chests, health fountains, and other ♥♥♥♥ I’m sure I haven’t discovered or will be updated later. Enemies are divided into five categories by my observations: Spawn Enemies, Floor Enemies, Summoners, Muscles, and Bosses.You and your team, or you and incredibly good luck, will need to find the enemy with the key on your floor, kill them, and proceed to the next level. There are three levels in total (for now) and the floor plan/layout seems to change each run. While incredibly rewarding to beat all three waves and win, I have some big news and a suggestion: No one thinks it makes sense to earn the same amount of Experience Points regardless of if you win or lose. 1000XP, flat, per run. My guess is that if you really want the cosmetics, you should just play like an idiot for about 50 matches, and ascend madly.While this sucks, the only things you can unlock are cosmetic, and all characters and content is available without any paywall…yet.There’s talk about a non-VR compatible release of this title, and while I’d like that, I’d also like more content. This is fun, but it’s not fun enough to make you want to play rounds back-to-back unless a friend wasn’t available to join last time. Classes, skills, and combat are, to some extent, relatively perfect.My only suggestion is that I wish I could cancel literally any action. If you pick up a card you often must ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ commit, so imagine it like playing Chess with an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who won’t let you take back a move regardless of whether your hand remained on the piece. Sure, it teaches you to commit to responsibility and consequence, but more often than not it’s straight consequence.Die throwing can be iffy, unless you don’t really care, in which case it’s fun yeeting your dice into space and getting it to suddenly decide a face value.I wish the figures had idle animations when they weren’t attacking, otherwise it feels like the equivalent of Harry potter’s Wizard’s Chess. You move inanimate piece which stays inanimate, and then it suddenly moves when it wants to commit violence.A fun time with a friend, better with a group of friends. It has the makings of a perfect VR game, and I’d recommend it to anyone I know who likes tabletop RPG’s, RPGs, and having fun with friends.4/5 – Can’t wait for the non-VR compatible title/functionality!

_childDocuments_.review: : If you have friends to play with, get this game, it's worth it.I've been playing this game with two other people, we played the first level over and over with every combination of 3 heroes possible. We were clamoring for the new map and then it dropped. We were able to barely squeak out a victory against the rat king the first time. Every single time after that we've been absolutely destroyed by the mechanics and various bugs. While we are happy that the game got harder, we just wish a couple of the mechanics were tweaked or that each pack has a difficulty rating. The rat king one being extra hard.I guess let's start with the darkness mechanic: As you delve deeper into the sewers (great visuals btw) it gets harder to see. You start to only see 2 blocks in front of you. The mobs can see across the map like it's pure daylight; I've been shot from across the map a frustrating amount of times. The devs added a card to handle this, the torch. The torch would be a great mechanic IF it didn't die, basically the mobs seem to prioritize the torch, killing it in 3 hits therefor making 2 of the 4 classes useless in this pack. I would say to fix this issue: make it so mobs don't have better sight than the player or fix the torches to not die from damage but rather just time out instead of both.Hit and run: The hit and run mechanic was a pain in the first pack but too deadly in the 2nd pack where there are way more rats. I've walked into a room as the tank with 10 health and 5 armor and got downed because of the number of rats running it to hit and running away with one bigger mob to do the killing blow. It's not fun to be a tank and have to worry about being completely pounded into the ground by lesser mobs if you open the wrong door. Rats have this and so do dogs which do more damage and really don't make sense to have it. To fix this I would say make it so mobs can't pass through each other or limit this mechanic to weak hitters so swarms are still dangerous but a couple dogs and some ranged guys wouldn't down a fully healed up tank in one turn.Berserk: This new mechanic is where larger mobs hit harder and hit twice when they get low on health. The devs need to mark this on the mobs that have it and beyond that it seems like there should be a down side to it. The mob can hit harder and hit twice but SHOULD take more damage as a result. A tank can be downed by one tough mob that goes berserk.The Rat King: He is too much. He spawns rats, he has berserk, he can heal himself, and does hit and run. Plus the adds come as a ranged attack and he can see through the dark. He is an amalgamation of everything bad about the new pack. Take one of these mechanics away or nerf it and it would still be super hard but at least doable.All that said, the game is super fun if you play the first game pack where you can see. I hope the devs take some times to adjust the difficulty of the 2nd pack. My friends and I had to play the first pack at the end of the night to get a win and not feel terrible after getting our asses kicked by the hard and sometimes unfair mechanics. We look forward to more levels, monsters, cards and heroes to play with. We just might take a break until new content comes out or the sewers aren't as tough.

_childDocuments_.review: If I only had one word to describe this game, it would be... wow!This is on my list of best VR games of all time.  It is very similar to some of the D&D-based board games. You control a miniature and you get two actions per turn --- move, attack, play card (although some cards can be played without using an action).  You can be one of four classes.  While the game mechanics are simple, game play requires strategic thinking (and cooperation when playing multiplayer).  Game difficulty is just right.  It's challenging.  This is not an easy game and you can definitely get yourself into a bad spot, but it's not impossible.  AI is pretty simple.  It seems like for the most part it attacks the closest character within sight, but has a chance to do something unexpected which forces you to change your strategy and keeps the game interesting.  This game is fun in single player, but really shines in multiplayer.  Enemy difficulty is scaled for the number of players.  Experience and loot --- gold and chests --- are given equally to each member of the party, so there is no fighting over who gets to open a chest or who picks up a gold pile.   Graphics are gorgeous and the game atmosphere is fantastic.  Sounds and music are excellent as well.  I also have to say this game has the best tutorial of any game I ever played.  It is engaging and not patronizing.  The camera is really well done as well.  You can move it so you have an overhead view or you can zoom in and place your view right next to the action!  I think my only critique here would be that because of how you rotate and zoom, sometimes it is easy to change the zoom when you are only trying to rotate and vice versa.  I got a little better at this as the game went on and it ceased to be that much of a problem, and honestly, I don't have suggestions for how to improve this.  It is not a game breaking thing by any means, but something I noted while I was playing.  I am kind of neutral on this one.  I guess I will say that camera control takes a bit of practice, but you pick it up pretty quick.  The only real critique I really have is the lack of ability to save a game.  Let's say (hypothetically of course) that someone bought the game and had a blast playing with a few friends last night.  The trio of friends beat the game and the someone in question decided to try a single player game because they wanted to keep playing but their friends had to log off.  That someone started a single player game and after a bit realized it was 11:30 PM and they needed to go to bed.  They would have liked to come back to their game, but there is no save option....  Some suggestions.The ability to change your character before the game starts.  We had s situation last night where two of us accidentally picked the assassin.  One of us wanted to change because the game had not started, but once you choose your character you are stuck even though the game has not started and you are still waiting for other players.  The game saves your data, which is nice if you get kicked because your character is still there, but that means that our idea of leaving and coming back so you could re-choose your character failed.  The same can be said of the card shop.  As long as some players have not selected ready and others have, there is no reason not to let players toggle between ready and unready (for example, we had a player who noticed after he had hit ready that he could aford another card, but it was too late).Difficulty modes.  I think the monster level is perfect and you don't want to alter that to make it easier or harder, but it would be cool to be able to turn off the points of interest so you don't even know where those are unless you enter the room and then the little marker can pop up.  Also it's be cool if you could pick between 3, 4, or even a 5 level dungeons.  Campaign mode!  It would be awesome if there were like 5-7 different dungeons/areas and you had to defeat them all to beat some kind of story mode in the game.  This of course would require the savegame mentioned above.After you beat a game in multiplayer, your only option is to leave.  A restart button is needed here.  Overall, great game!  It is a little pricy, but it sounds like the devs will continue to update and add content and it looks like they put a lot of love and effort into this game already so I doubt they would just abandon it.  The replayability factor is high and so I think it is definitely a worthwhile purchase, even at full price.  If you love fantasy, D&D, tabletop gaming, and strategy games, this one is definitely for you!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I really, truly do not understand why the reviews are "very positive". The game itself has a very nice interface, it's pretty intuitive and the tabletop feels alright to use. The gameplay feels okay, its acceptable, its not the best tabletop experience in vr (tabletop simulator takes that award). There is no object manipulation beyond characters and enemies on the board, the cards aren't very tactile, etc. it just feels very bare bones in that regard. Beyond that, the entire game feels incredibly bare bones. Hit animations aren't that great, the boards look very meh, and the worst, most important part: there is no content. There are 2 campaigns of 3 randomly generated levels with no enemy variety, there is no real deck building to speak of, no carry over progression, and barely any progression during the campaigns themselves because they are so short. The only "progression" is a battlepass style skin unlocker as you get exp from playing. So what's the point? Why keep playing the randomly generated levels when nothing changes and there is nothing to work forward to?For 30 dollars I think it is very reasonable to expect more than what there is. This game in it's current state is not worth playing at all. This is a game that I really don't think anyone would buy if it were not in vr, as everyone is thirsting for good vr content and this is one of a few options that exist if you are looking for a tabletop/rpg. Save your money and buy tabletop simulator with your friends instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as i want to recommend this game, i'd highly recommend to wait on your purchase unless atleast one of the two following things happen:1. Roadmap for the game is made public and/or the game already received all of it's (hopefully) upcoming updates2. This game receives Workshop support or tools for creating custom content.For now, the current content is very bare, so the game would benefit hugely by allowing players to create custom content like campaigns, models, classes, spellcards etc. . I'd easily recommend the game if it has workshop support.Both campaigns right now feature 3 randomly generated dungeons, the last one being the bosses lair. That makes 6 total levels to play through, easily finished under 4 hours if you use your spells carefully or don't plan on replaying the campaigns a bunch. So, there isn't much content for 25€ for me to recommend this when there are so many other games that offer better value for the amount of content given. It is a fun experience and i can see myself playing it more, but it really does need custom content to truly turn into something that can last for the years to come.One of the only things that is bothering me about the gameplay is that monsters spawn in the fog of war, so a room you previously cleared and missed 1-2 turns of vision on could suddenly spawn some monsters to mess up your playthrough. I wish there was a better solution to respawning enemies into the dungeon.Another one is the existence of the roadmap that apparently exists. Neither is the game marked as early access nor is the roadmap of coming content posted  , apart from a small mention of it's existence in the games description. It's not accessible to the public.

Progression is through cosmetics and in roguelike fashion otherwise limited to the skills and experience you gain as a player.The stock balance is toward the side of very challenging in a way that's liable to grind you down with the sheer number of enemies, but the  to prevent enemies from respawning in rooms you've cleared and from opening doors entirely fixes that for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it.  For starters it's NOTHING like DnD, let alone ANY dungeon crawler.  It's more like a spastic rampage board game that's 100% combat focused.- There is no character leveling up, NONE.  You gain cosmetics only.- There is no character MAKING.- There is no card customization.- There are no campaigns.  Each "Book" is just an RNG tileset.  No story, no exploration.- You are instantly overwhelmed with 10-15 enemies all running for you from across the map.- The difficulty comes from the bad design, not the mechanics.- Enemies are infinite and are randomly placed in ALL non-sighted areas and this INCLUDES spawners.- The view / movement controls are disgusting.  Just let us use the thumbsticks to move the camera.  I don't know why this is in VR honestly.  There is no benefit or immersion enhancement.This makes the meta to just beeline the keyboss while you have your two starter cards and pray for RNG.  No matter what you do, you will be seen across the map instantly and all mobs will beeline you.  There is no resting, no regrouping.  It may as well be a tower defense game skin.Has potential, but the design is attrocious for what it's trying and claiming to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the game was great when it first came out. Wish it was more of a dungeons and dragons type free roam adventure but its still good none the less. I had played the first dungeon quite a bit and put the game down while waiting the new Rat King dungeon. Upon updating yesterday and checking the new update out, I logged in to find myself forced into the tutorial, which I found odd, and after skipping the tutorial, found myself looking at an experience bar of 0% at lvl 0... I lost all my initial progress, all my items... Which is quite frustrating. After playing a bit, and asking other players, I quickly found 2 others it happened to. Is this going to be a recurring issue? Is every update going to lead to the possibly of some of the player base loosing all their progress? I've observed other glitches as well since the update, but this is the biggest reason as to why i am giving this a - review at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: As nicely put together as this game is, it kinda went way below my expectations.It is a very comfy game, you can kinda just lay there while playing, it doesnt ask too much effort out of you.My main issue is mostly with what they give you, you get cards and such as spells and tools to use to defeat monsters, but most of those cards are consumable, and playing as a wizard i just had consistently 2 spells, so most of the time i felt like there wasn't that much interesting stuff to do, furthermore when you get a new card via the "level up" you don't get to choose it or choose from a group, you just get a random one, so by the RNG you could get really useful cards or very mid ones.Furthermore after reaching the first boss, you realise that they spawn more units, that defend her, but that's not like "at half health for a phase transition" its whenever she wants, so your resources get drained greatly, and it kinda feels like a waste of time.. like we've already lost, theres two giant spiders, 5 small dudes, and a boss with 30+ hp and all i can cast is zap..This game is kinda like a deck builder without the building aspect, just a deck..Honestly i bet some people could enjoy this game much more than i am! But i feel like it's a little lacklustre, maybe at some point someone will mod the game to be more like what a player like me likes?

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying my first 5 hours despite it not being quite what I expectedI watched a couple of videos but didn't really get a true sense of the gameplay.  It would be easy to mistake this (if you don't do your research monkey boy lol) for a Vandal Hearts / Hero Quest / Xcom esq dungeon crawler. It's not, the game wants you to get a wiggle on due to the enemy knowing exactly were you are when it comes to re-spawns.  There's no clearing of the map but a mad dash for the exit whilst tactically maximising the elements of each room along the way.  At this early stage it's not brutal but I found this out the hard way after wasting time and good cards on the continuous onslaught (in waves).  My new tactic is to avoid points of interest and bee line to the exit.  Cards are your super power not character progression as there isn't any.Take this with a pinch of salt as I kinda like feeling in the dark so don't research thing to the nth degree to keep some surprises so there's a chance I've missed something.All in all deffo worth a purchase and glad I bought it!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has issues with dice rolling being in favour of misses for the players usually getting between 2 to 5 per 10 rolls. _childDocuments_.review: GREAT game, LOTS of potential.It plays really well! Camera movement is smooth, everything around atmosphere, sound/visual design, characters and gameplay is top level. The zooming function is just genius. Just the fact that you literally sit in the Stranger Things basement, where they always meet to play D&D. This game is FANTASTIC.Some minor problems:The rotating table might be offputting at first, but is really nessassary so that my neck won't literally die.The game does not have a save-function in between levels, so you basically have to sit through 2/3 hours of gameplay.Maybe a bit too easy for my taste.I can't really commend on classes and their individual power YET, since my friend and I played just one game, but I've seen people mentioning the balancing. I thought the two classes we played were fine in that regard. Just so you know. Really nothing big that ruined the fun we had.This game is hands down the best turnbased stategy experience I've ever had, not just in VR, but in general!HOWEVER:At this state, I just cannot recommend this game due to the lack of content, and it hurts me do give this a negative review.I've beaten this game with a friend first try. Fairly easily aswell. We took a lot of time to explore and play around aswell, and even then we were done in ~2 hours. I don't see a huge replay value aswell.In a world where this game has more content aswell as STEAM SUPPORT, this would truly be a one-of-a-kind game you should NOT skip on.Heads held high, the Developers will add more content and a PC-Version just this summer. This game is still in it's baby days after all. Once more content rolls around, I'll make sure to update this review!Edit: I feel like this does not deserve the negative review anymore. I didn't find the time to play the new updates yet, but there is clearly more content added frequently. GJ Devs!

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:  Realm of the Rat King is killing this game.  The first module (The Black Sarcophagus) was moderately easy to complete.  Some might say almost too east.  The newest module (Realm of the Rat King) seeks to change that... but like most game designers, they've gone too far.  The levels are not just more challenging, they're damn near impossible.Just to lay out some "features" of this new module...1 - Your sight is limited to just two squares around you, unless you have a torch in the room or attached to a hero.  Torches only last for 8 rounds of play though, so be sure you have TONS of them, which then limits your ability to carry other cards.2 - Creatures run in, attack you, and then run out of your visual range without a torch... making it impossible to him them without wasting one action point just to find them again.3 - Creature difficulty is SIGNIFICANTLY ramped up. Many larger creatures spawn in the second level, and many of them have healing capabilities, rending them much harder to take down. A lot are also immune to being stunned so your Sorcerer's viability just got smashed to the ground.4 - Map issues are no help either.  The levels of Realm of the Rat King are more cramped and often cause "blockages" with spider eggs, spore fungi, and rats nests literally blocking the only path of attack.  Plus, the corridors now often are a single space wide instead of two... making it harder to maneuver around enemies for the Assassin... or just in general.With these difficulties and extremely high skill requirement now, I'm changing my recommendation from "yes, buy it" to "no, avoid it" until some kind of difficulty system is implemented, or the monsters are re-balanced more in line with the heroes' skills.ORIGINAL REVIEW: This game is AMAZING.  What a great use of VR... bringing table top RPG games to life.  They just released a new module (for free) as I write this... with more on the way.I'm hoping they continue to release modules.  However, if I have one criticism, it's that they've missed the opportunity for community-created content.  Utilizing the Steam Worship, having a tool that would allow people to create their own campaigns to be played by the community would be INCREDIBLE!Hopefully, they'll do that in the future. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and even talked some friends who share my love of D&D into purchasing it so we could learn the game together. None of us has any experience with the board game, and perhaps that is the problem. Let me explain.The interface is beautiful, stable, intuitive and innovative. Being able to pick up your figures and use their actual orientation in relation to the baddies/environment is simple and very effective - and then watching them animate in response is awesome. The game also seems to have been inspired by shows like Stranger Things in terms of what the board is surrounded by - kind of scratched my 80's nostalgia itch. Other VR titles should seek to be inspired by how they are getting the players to interact with the board.BUT...The lack of story and character development completely subverts my willingness to invest myself or to endure some of the games difficulty. The game is always the same. Random generated 3 level dungeon, Same baddies and very limited cards with which to deal with them. But the feature that completely defeats me and has now caused me to uninstall this game is the infinite spawns that continually rush you, including from areas that you have "cleared". This is not fun or strategic in any way - the games devolves into a mad rush to find the key carrying monster and get out of the exit before you are completely swarmed by endless monsters - that is it. The only goal in EVERY LEVEL of EVERY GAME.Having never played the board game, perhaps this is true to the way it is designed and thus the creators of Demeo are obliged to adhere to that mechanic. I don't know. But assuming that the people who wish to play this game are also D&D fans, removing strategic/tactical progression through a dungeon, and having no character progression/development AT ALL completely undermines what I believed was going to be a wonderful simulation of nights of D&D with my friends. It is just not fun to run, fight the same things and see no change to characters or game as you play.Sorry Demeo - I really thought this was going to be a winner

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely need more VR games like this one! it's great being able to chat with friends, plan your moves and then feel the anticipation of the dice roll.It's a great mix of chilled turn based flow and intense sudden surprises. Pop your head around a corner at the end of your move only to see 5 beasties waiting for you brings me back to some of my fav games, like XCOM.I highly recommend it for tactical and social game fans.Can't wait for the FREE DLC... gotta love Free DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: So far Demeo is THE best VR game I have played.Controls are very intuitive and easy to move your PoV around the Board.Being allowed to get right down to eye level with the models and watch their animations up close is awesome.The graphics are very nice, with well balanced colour and blended effects that are very impressive (love the Bard's Hurricane Anthem!).The PC version is also very nice, but of course not as immersive as VR.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a thumbs up with the admission that there is definitely a bit of work to be done before I'd suggest paying full price for it.It's a lot of fun, don't get me wrong- I've enjoyed playing- but the content is limited at the moment with only two main storylines (which don't take long to complete). It would be great to see some more storylines introduced to the game down the road.Some other things I'd like to see:More character optionsMore flexible difficulty scaling for smaller groups (as it is now, the game is almost impossible to beat without a group of 4, which for most people is not feasible).Support for mods/Steam workshop contentCustom campaigns, map editor, etc.That being said, I love this game. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, the animations look really cool, and just the fact that you can zoom in and see the characters from up close is really great. However, in terms of recommendations/ideas : * The ability to create our own levels : The community you'll build doing that can be MASSIVE* Different level of difficulties : Yeah you can fail, but even though sometimes it's a close call, if you're careful you can't really fail. So that's good to begin the game, but having different difficulties will give the game a higher playable time for more advanced players* Optimize the game : I'm playing this game on steam using a quest 2 and an oculus link, and boy it lags a lot. _childDocuments_.review: Updating my review after playing multiplayer and realizing there is no content...After playing a couple rounds of multiplayer I think I am switching my opinion to a thumbs down until there are more adventure modules. Right now there is 1 adventure. So there's about 2 hours of content and then the game expects you to repeat that 45 times to unlock all the cosmetic unlocks in a battle pass like progression system. I'm not going to grind out the same exact adventure for 90 hours just for some cosmetics. I struggle to be content spending $30 for just one adventure. Once more adventures are added with more bosses and more enemy variations $30 will be more than reasonable. Until then, the price is just too high for what's available atm.---Original Review Below---A great, if not a little simplistic, tabletop experience.That's not necessarily a bad thing. DnD can get very overwhelming with its rules and math. Keeping the game simple makes it very easy to pick up and get into and IMO emphasizes the social aspect of the game more than the technical bits.This does mean that hardcore tabletop gamers might feel the game is a little shallow. The game does a good job at throwing wave after wave of enemies and never really giving you a second to breath. This does kinda feel like a bandaid for depth but it works out allright.There are definitely some quality of life improvements to be had. Selecting characters wasn't always as responsive as I would have likedI'm not a fan of that opening movie starting as soon as the game starts. Not everyone has their headset on and ready to go as soon as the game starts. Also that audio volume was sooo loud at the start. Give me a chance to address those things before bombarding me with a 5 minute story time...Overall those are minor issues that can be addressed easily enough. I'm definitely looking forward to getting some MP time in with the game.This will be a thumbs up from me as it delivers exactly what it promises with very few flaws. Will definitely see this streamed in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I just bought this game the other day and I am so addicted. It's simple in it's core, random floors / random mob spawns but always 3 floors per quest/adventure. Even so, I am loving this game and everything about it. The immersion is great being able to move around the table to see the board from any direction, the people that play this game for the most part are chatty/friendly and coming from someone who often sticks to his own pack of friends, this game has me branching out to meet new people to play with! There are currently 2 Adventures and 4 Heroes with an update coming soon (Dec 12th or 16th (not sure of exact date)) that is adding a 3rd adventure and a 5th hero class! (Bard). If the developers continue to add adventures and hero's and maybe even open this game to the steam workshop this game will surely explode on steam, especially with the non-vr / vr cross-play (*not yet available for non-vr )and crossplatform between steam/oculus store.This game is a tabletop boardgame/card game mix. You do have cards that consist of abilities and items, but you also have movement and "basic attack" that is controlled by you manually picking up your piece and moving it across the board. Each hero has a "refresh ability" card that is always available and can be used once per turn or once it has refreshed (cooldown). All other items/abilities are one time use. You gain cards by either killing mobs or looting chests and can hold 10 cards in your hand. There is also a revive system, when you reach 0 hp you are downed, on your turn if you have a healing potion you can revive yourself, or an ally can bring you back up on their turn if they are able to reach your body/token. You have a limited amount of times you can be downed before you just outright die though, which I believe is 3 lives, on the 4th down you are fully dead.To conclude, I feel most DnD fans and board/card game fans can find a common ground in this game and enjoy it. Even with the small content it has right now it's still very well done and simple enough to be able to do the quick tutorial and jump right into the game feeling like you are at least somewhat prepared. I am excited to see this game grow and look forward to playing this with my friends and trying to conquer each adventure! (Rat king be super stupid hard lol but I enjoy the challenge). 12/10

_childDocuments_.review: I havent gotten very far into Demeo but I've enjoyed what I've played so far. The game is a top down dungeon crawler with a light story where you and up to 3 other friends play a scenario to complete objectives and win a 3-level randomly generated campaign. If you're into games like Gloomhaven, Hero Quest or Descent, this is like a VR version of that sort of adventureThe game has a lot going for it:- The soundtrack is simple but nice- The environments are detailed and easy to sink into- The background is cute- The story isn't anything to write home about; a simple DnD-esque campaign complete with a 'GM' narrator- Combat is tightly tuned making almost every point of damage and healing valuable- Controls are pretty intuitive and easy to use once you learn themHowever, Demeo is far from perfect and has a couple issues that keeps it from shining:- The angle of the play board is uncomfortable to interact with for long play sessions necessitating either tilting the table which kinda breaks a lot of the immersive fun of 'being there' or just looking away at the wall to rest your neck.- There is not a lot of variety. Each class has its own set of unique ability cards but there are a lot more 'generic' cards that everyone has access to. I would have preferred the ration of unique to generic to be reversed.- The game doesn't explain most of its own rules so the players just have to do a bunch of trial and error to figure out what everything is and does. Some objects you can pick up and get a brief description for but often critical information is left out (such as the detonation area of a bomb or that you can't teleport onto revealed gold to collect it). This lack of information has caused some disagreement between players when one person experienced one thing and another experienced something else with the same object/effect and its difficult to make a call with this incomplete info at a critical juncture of a run.Some other notes/thoughts about the game:- It's not hard for the most experienced player to start quarterbacking the game. Sometimes this is valuable but it can become annoying when one player just starts telling the others what to do. Leadership is valuable but the game lacks enough variety to keep one person from being able to understand and make calls for everyone.- Line of sight can be difficult to sus out when you're trying to line up for ability. This hasn’t caused any catastrophic damage in my runs but it does feel bad to be a square shy of being able to use an ability because you weren’t sure if x-thing was in the way.- It’s a bit too easy to accidentally move your unit. When you're trying to figure out the line of sight for an ability, if you loosen your grip or are viewing your unit and it becomes your turn, you can find yourself moved with no way to 'undo'. I would love a config option to have a confirmation dialogue before committing to a move. Bonus points if it had the added benefit of being able to move your unit somewhere and, before you commit, could pull out an ability to check the range before committing.- Progression is really slow. Maybe you get a big bonus for finishing a campaign but I've done 5 floors in three run and haven’t unlocked the first cosmetic.Overall though, I'm quite enjoying the game and look forward to future content. Worth a buy if you've got some VR friends to play with (and non-VR friends supposedly coming in a future update).

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of VR, of action figure collecting, and of Gauntlet/fantasy in general, this is a dream come true. It's basically a 3D-VR turn based Gauntlet with co-op for 4 players. Definitely scratches that tabletop fantasy itch. I do have plenty of hopes and suggestions for the game, and although it is a bit light on content for the price, I am appreciative that the devs have communicated their intention to continue to supply the game with more free content. As far as criticisms, I think the main one concerns some light neck strain just from the nature of how you look down at the table. The table can be adjusted so that it's more tilted towards the viewer, but that can itself be a little disorienting. Other than that, I would like for even more character creation and depth of gameplay, along with dialog choices to make a more true RPG experience. As it is, the gameplay is on the basic side and strategy becomes more a thing of utilizing abilities and placement of characters, etc. My hope is that in time the gameplay is made even more robust as we see more of the content come in. First new adventure is slated for Summer of this year and I can't wait. If you're a fan of tabletop fantasy games, definitely dive in, you're not going to regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential but feels like an early access title, especially for 30$.  This is not just due to balance issues, the assassin and mage are squishy and lackluster.   It is more due a severe lack of content, only one board design and not that many monsters.  Furthermore the game does not seem to scale for less players.  The VR implementation is pretty good, but if they had play tested their game for any length of time they would have realized that playing a game looking down with a VR headset is a recipe for a sore neck and headache.  You can tilt the board 90* but it doesn't seem right.  Perhaps better rotation control would help.  Anyways if they release more content and balance the classes this would be a fantastic game even with the sore neck.Update:So there is quite a bit of content now!  That was my biggest issue and seeing the devs release a lot of new stuff has been great.  The difficulty still seems a bit absurd but I guess giving you the ability to change the difficulty would make it too easy.  Also considering this is a card game it would be nice to see more cards and you could choose your card loadout depending on the hero you were playing.  Balance for small groups is still an issue and even with 4 players someone always has to play the tank which can get kind of old.  Despite this the game is in a much better spot and I feel like a thumbs up is deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: I have this game on the Oculus platform but also purchased it via Steam for testing purposes with mods and the like so disregard the play time as I have oodles of hours played at Rank 60.This game is a wonderful creation of co-operative strategy board gaming. It is meant to be played with a group as if you were pulling a board game off the shelf for game night. While having inspiration from fantasy games and the 80s theme the game is not a straight RPG or pen&paper tool so temper those expectations. There is no individual progression beyond Ranks for cosmetic unlocks but the game isn't about an individual it is focused on the group aspect.What you have here is a simple to learn but complex game that can provide hours of fun, with the addition of mods you can change up the game entirely. With a regular group your can game while having a social meeting or gathering all in a VR space.The other great thing about the game is that despite being a year old development and content has been released without additional costs. When so many developers nickel and dime you it is a relief to find one that seems to want to work with their community and continue to improve their product without putting the costs squarely on their players.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing core product!  I simply can't wait for the DLC's to come.  I'd give this a 9.8 out of 10.  It comes in a time where I want to play a dungeon crawl (e.g. D&D or Shadows and Brimestone style) without the trouble of actually meeting with people in these weird times.  The graphics are beautifully done, the animations are very cool, and the audio is engaging.There is room for improvement or some bells and whistles with visual/functional options.  Button toggle for microphone muting would be great.  Table tilting is available, but is rigid in application.  Rotating on axis while tilted to define what angle the tilt occurs would be spectacular.  Ability to make co-op players masks and hands a variable degree of transparency would be fabulous.  Currently, the core game is a three level with end boss.  As the product grows, I'm hoping the dungeons can be stitched together in the host's chosen order with the ability to save progress (with choice of continuing without all players present if one can't make it).  Right now the game will reset without ability to save if ended, which isn't a big issue due to the dungeon size, but loss of cards gathered before getting to the next floor is a bummer.  My Oculus Q2 streaming PC had a glitch visually so I, as the game host, unplugged my headset and restarted it, SteamVR, and launched back into the game with the Room number I started.  To my pleasant surprise, the game was very graceful in handing off the hosting and let me back in with my chosen character and card set I had before I dropped.  This is great stuff, well done.  Thank you for making such a great product!  We seriously can't wait for more content, maybe another character to chose (my recommendation would be a berserker or shape-shifter), and lots more bad guys!  Add in character building a la Dungeons and Dragons or Shadows and Brimestone styling, and I would ask you to kindly take my money!

_childDocuments_.review: I only have a few hours into Demeo so far. But, I think this game has so much potential. I bought it at full price because I want to support this game and show there is a market for games like this. You are able to zoom out if you want it to look like you are playing with small minis, or you can zoom way in so you can see all of the action. No matter how you play, it looks great. The rules are simple and easy to learn. It also isn't a breeze. You can get overwhelmed with enemies or have a few bad dice rolls that hurt. So far, it hasn't felt like a cheap gimmick to me like some games that just pile on the bad dice rolls to simulate difficulty. There is so much room for this to grow. I have only played solo so far, but I think it will be even more fun with friends. If you like tabletop games, I think this is worth it. I'll still play tabletop games. But, with this, there is no setup or take down, no getting your minis painted (which I enjoy), or building terrain. Its also easy to learn so you don't have to explain the rules. I'll come back to this review at some point in the future. I hope it does well as there is so much room for this game to grow. It is good as it is, the base is great. But, this team had a good vision and they were able to implement that perfectly!

I generally wait for sales, but I wanted to support the concept. I'm not sorry that I did; they did a great job.UPDATE- There are a few bugs encountered at this point. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great game, seriously ;)All the little graphics details, the characters even have little stamps with "made in sweden" at the bottom.The developers really put love into this project and you can see and feel it.Was the first VR game for me where I played and talked to other people and had ton of fun with it.I hope there will be a little more content in the future (maybe even other game modes e.g. where someone is the game master or something like a map editor) but for now this is already a really solid, funny, very special game.There are a few minor things I would like to see improved (e.g. maybe a faster camera-movement/sensitivity settings for it) and maybe an game-internal friendlist, because I can't stay in touch with the people who play on oculus, since I don't have a facebook account) but overall it's very polished.10/10, definitely worth the money if you like "real old school games" you maybe played when you were a child. ;)Can't wait to play another round with the people I met there.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun way to play with friends for a table top experience that is easy to pick up, but also very challenging. The enemies are relentless, as they should be! I've never had a whole lot of time to spend to pick up a game of Dungeons and Dragons. Demeo throws you right into the heat of everything so you can focus on the core dungeon exploration, combat, and socializing without having to make an all day campaign of it all. It's pretty bare bones for the content, but everything is well polished, from what I understand there are planned content updates later, including desktop play may be in the works. I'm looking forward to see how this game develops!
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is some kind of DnD style dice & card kind that simplifies too many things in a very clunky way to be fun to play.In General the games performance seems good which is no surprise given it's simplistic graphics.The Performance in VR is kind of ok even though in a Rift CV1 roation and zoom tend to stutter a bit on more than good enough hardware.This is propably to to lack of optimization for the specific platform or maybe even Steam VR.I had te opportunity to look at the game with Playstation VR2 and it had different issues (the whole field was wobbling around all the time).Looking around and moving your characters is working fine and the whole concept with the cards in your hands is kind of interesting.Playing those cards is super annoying because you can't just select the card and then a character or enemy you have to drag  the card onto them. While this seems like a nice idea it is implemented very poorly.Moving your character implemented in the similar way. You have to be very accurate in order to move your character to a position or attack an enemy (by dropping your character on it). This often resulted in wrong actions for me, especially in non VR.The game also lacks convenience features - to name a few:- you can't just double click a field to move you character there- you can't click on a character portrait and have the camera moved there- you can't move all your characters together except for through doors to the next dungeon level.I also don't understand why you are in turn based mode the moment you enter the dungeon. I would expect to be able to move freely until I encounter an enemy but that isn't possible.Fighting and moving around is super slow and not fun at all. Enemies seem to make more damage and have more HP than your heroes. But most importantly they don't drop stuff and spawn endlessly upto the point where I didn't bother continuing to play.Demeo seemed like a good idea until I started playing it. The moment you enter the dungeon it openly displays all it's weaknesses.Starting at the lack of platform optimization and control issues and going over to missing convenience features and ending at super slow and boring gameplay.I mananged to play roughly and hour until I removed it from my disk and will propably never touch it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a "git gud" player? If so, this game is for you! If you're not a toxic fanboy of this extremely unbalanced game, then keep reading.This looks a lot like DND, which is cool.It's a board game, which is cool.You can play it in VR or on desktop, which is cool.....That's it.The enemies CONTINUALLY SPAWN. This means if you cannot keep up with action economy, then your party is doomed.Healing is limited. This means you can get outnumbered/out DPS'd, and your party is doomed.The devs, realizing that 2 people CANNOT play this game and win, enabled each player to play 2 tokens! So 4 people can play 4 tokens (a "full game") - but if you have 3 players, you're boned. You only get 3.The game is supposed to scale with your party. I found no such scaling present - if it was present, it was to such a small extent that I didn't even notice it.I played 3 of the 5 currently available maps. First map, we won by the skin of our teeth, it was exciting to think we did so poorly but still won! Second map we got hammered in Area 1. We tried second map again, and again got hammered in Area 1. We tried a different map, and literally wiped the floor with everything, it was great. We kept that same party composition and tried the "second map" again (the one we had so much trouble with) and made it all the way to the end boss, where they literally spawned TONS of creatures every round.Look. The devs tried, they really did, and you're going to find players who have gamed the system in order to come out on top, but this - this is not fun. Endless enemies that spawn (you will NEVER clear a map, NEVER, there will ALWAYS be spawning enemies), "level ups" that are purely cosmetic (you will always be as weak as you were when you started, unless you get lucky and get a potion to increase health/speed/damage - but those reset when the map is won or lost, so it's not permanent).....this game is just a disappointing mess compared to what I thought it was.My mistake. I thought this was a well balanced, finished product that truly makes the world of VR shine. Instead, it's hot garbage. Even the modding community has taken it upon themselves to try to make the game easier because the Devs don't want to fix their hot garbage game.Fun factor on this started at a 10 and over the course of a few games with friends turned into a 0. This is a crash and burn - and it's mostly because the Devs aren't catering to both the hardcore players, as well as the players, like my friends and I, who find the game to be insanely challenging.Artificial difficulty, I think, is the biggest kicker here. That's a cardinal sin.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: This is a one of the best VR in the last few years. A great dungeon crawler that will make any D&D fan fall in love. It's one of the smoothest VR games I have played. Everything just works and cross play is simple and works with no issues. Typically I think $30 is too much for a VR game, but with the upcoming new content coming this summer, this is without a doubt a great deal that I highly recommend it.*Updated* The new Adventure is out and its well done. They continue to update and add improvements, a must buy for anyone into this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing the VR version with friends.  My goodness the game goes long but we can't stop until the final boss is dead.  We have one more book to do and then we have plans for re-doing campaigns with different characters (who is up for the all-Bard battle?)This game is over-the-top polished in VR.  The Heroes Hangout miniature painting room is already good enough to be its own experience, and it's just kinda thrown in there for funsies.  While you wait for your buddy to figure out his VR mic you can explore the room and read monster manuals, appreciate the comic book references, pick a new shirt, check out the discord chat on the projector, or shoot arrows.The game itself is also simple and yet leads to complex gameplay.  Classes are interesting and you'll want to try them all, but you will find a favorite.  I'm a fan of the barbarian. Each "book" can be replayed as the layout and enemy locations are procedural.  Still, I find myself wanting more content and look forward to updates.The game feels difficult, your characters are always about to die and make it through by the skin of their teeth.  The game is pretty well balanced.  Some cards, enemies, or powers aren't well-explained (we had to look up what the blank barbarian card was for, for example) but learning the powers and enemies is part of the fun.I tried the desktop version and the gameplay is the same but I vastly prefer the VR version for the ability to see more of the board and choose a viewpoint more easily.  Desktop feels too limiting, especially the camera control, if you've been in VR.  Overall a strong recommend, best with friends but also worth doing solo.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I played this game quite a bit solo, and had a really fun time.I lost interest overtime as none of my friends had VR to join in the fun.Once the flat version came out, this game got a new life.I am really enjoying working through it with friends.With 4 campaigns out at this time, there is plenty of variety in the game to keep you entertained for hours on end. That said, I'm always looking forward to more classes, missions, and features. Overall a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: This seems like it could be a fun game, but I really hate the controls.You have to squeeze the controllers to "grab" the table/air, then push/pull in order to simply move or turn around, which is extremely cumbersome. The map is 3D, so you do need to move/turn/zoom around a lot to see everything, and after an hour or so my neck hurts and my wrists hurt.Why not just allow the option of using the analog sticks for movement/turning, since the game doesn't use them?The game seems polished, but there's not really a lot of depth to the gameplay, and it's also currently lacking in content. I guess it's okay if you're looking for a "lite" dungeon crawler, but not for $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games I've played yet! Having a relaxed, simple, and fun strategy game to play friends was something I felt the VR realm was lacking and Demeo did a great job filling that void.Is there room to grow? Absolutely! Hopefully they continue to expand the game with new dungeon layouts, heroes, and enemies! _childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the game so far. While the content is shallow, every game is different and each party has its strengths and weaknesses. Potential to be a cult game, if the devs address some things:- More content; maps, quests, characters, monsters etc.- Push to talk- Coin flip death/kill- Redesign the last level. It is too easy right now. The level should force the group to use cards. At the moment you can save all your cards until the queen becomes vulnerable- Option to enter at certain levels would be great in quickplay. 1, 2, 3.- Make the quest completion more rewarding. Exp is fine, but maybe unique skins or money towards a shop would be more motivating- Would like to see a harder game in general. _childDocuments_.review: I normally try to have more game time before reviewing a game, but I will make an exception for Demeo has I've completed my first run throught the game in ... very little time. The core mechanics of the game are very nice. I'm a dnd player and this definitly showcases how VR could offer some very interesting options for tabletop RPG in the future. I would not recommend this game sonely because of its lenght and lack of progression element. At the time I'm writing this review, there's only one three level (floor mission) and my friend and I, completed it within 3 hours of game time (learning and all). Obviously me and my friend can still replay the game a few more time, but it feels a lot like an early (very early) access game. _childDocuments_.review: From my initial 90 minutes, there's a lot to appreciate: the graphics, originality, sound, gameplay, nice card design, etc.I tried two skirmish runs and found that time flies by. I died in both; it seems weighted toward difficult overall. Perhaps with a 4th person, it might balance the odds. You think you have an area pretty clear and suddenly, more spawns and monsters can quickly overwhelm your party.A couple things I didn't like as much:1) the potentially friendly-fire on a miss; I think I'd rather have it miss everyone including enemies.2) dice rolling directly on the board is a bit awkward. It might be nicer to have a 3-walled room slightly above the board to throw the dice into.Overall, I can see this being quite a bit of fun with VR friends. I give the current incarnation 8 of 10, but temper it with needing more review and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Researched the game like mad and was pretty sure it would be good, but damn... wow.  Don't let the play time affect things, this game will be played extensively...This game I dare say is what VR was made for.Technical info people might want to know: HTC Vive and Oculus 2 Quest controllers recognized when running the game with the different hardware.  Playing the game via the Oculus 2 with Virtual Desktop allows you to run the program wirelessly and it's sweet, but on the Vive, the experience felt more solid and in control. No performance issues.I will probably still be buying the Oculus 2 version specifically so I can play with multiple family members.  I strongly recommend this for anyone who likes any form of D&D or strategic dungeon adventures and especially if you like playing with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The content is very limited in its current state, so much so that I felt it necessary to refund before I even played it for a couple hours. Graphically it's a gorgeous game, but the gameplay is extremely repetitive and there's hardly any story to speak of. There are unlockable cosmetics via exp in game, and while this isn't bad, it's a shame they opted for cosmetics before adding a good amount of variety to the game. The game does have a lot of potential, but until they either add mod support or release a significant amount of additional content, I don't think it's worth its current price. That being said, I will end up buying it again if they ever add more content / mod support. If you're looking to play a DnD type game with friends, I recommend Tabletop Simulator over Demeo in its current state. It's much cheaper (frequently on sale for 10 dollars, just 20 without), and while its not as graphically impressive as Demeo, it's massively customizable and has workshop / mod support, with endless amounts of content including full stories (not just assets) already made for you right from the get-go if you don't want to make your own.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and has great mechanics, which makes it all the more sad that there is no progression. If at each level up you had a chance to gain a new card or you could build up currency with each play-through to purchase a random card out of different tiers- that would make the game mint imo. As it is I haven't even completed a game (couldn't defeat the boss on the first try). Once I found out that leveling up only gives cosmetics, all of my initial enthusiasm and getting sucked into this game vanished.It needs some addictive progression like some of the card-collecting games (hearthstone for example). You don't even need tons of card like most of them have. They should cut out half the cards that you start with, turn them into un-lockables; and add a few new ones with each major update that have different rarities. You can unlock them with currency collected from playing the game, with bonuses from doing well and defeating bosses etc. Then either directly purchase the cards (just to get the chance for them to appear in a play-through) at different prices depending on rarity, or even better imo would be that you can pay to unlock a random card at different price/rarity tiers. Then if you get extras you don't need, you could either trade them back in for cash or sacrifice two or more for a higher tier card. Maybe even trade them with other players! Make some of them really hard to get or costly. That way you can always be working towards getting that last epic card you want in your collection, even if it takes ten or twenty play-throughs. At least there would be a purpose. Then think how cool it would feel playing with a few friends, and you use a card out of nowhere that none of them have seen that saves you all from otherwise guaranteed doom!I believe this type of progression would also make the upcoming pvp even better, and not destroy it like other forms of progression could. Other strictly card-based pvp games have the same random card collection system that works great (though some can get too p2w).I also think a slow/grindy stat-boosting like in rogue-lites would be great as well. Maybe just keep it out of pvp. Leave it in co-op for sure. Not huge boosts, but just enough to give you a sense you didn't waste the last 3 hours playing...If none of this is possible, then at least make the cosmetics more unique to each player. As it is, the same ones unlock for each player at the same levels which is boring. Not sure this would be enough to bring me back in, but it would be better than nothing for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Look I am going to be completely honest. I am not a huge fan of D&D, never have been. In fact I was tempted to not buy this game even though my friends wanted me to. After playing JUST ONE GAME RUN, which by the way one of the boys had to get off for school and the other had to go to which only left me and my other friend who were both bards (healer/support) so sadly we had to end. Although that alone was 1.6 hrs. If we had continued all night it probably would have been 3+ hrs. _childDocuments_.review: I game is a lot of fun!  It is truly a lot of fun.  I love the strategy that you must use with others or alone.  Its fun and reminds me of sitting around a table with friends and talking it out. There are only a few problems that I have with the game.  Being a VR game, it has the potential of triggering your motion sickness, but this one is pretty bad.  It is a bit shaky.  Motion Sickness is possible with this game due to the quick jerks and shakiness of the camera when you turn your head even slightly.  You wouldn't think that a board game would get you sick, but I couldn't really play more than 20-30 mins without needing a long break.  There are no controls other than the ability to turn off the back ground and just see the game, but it doesn't help much with the movement.  There isn't a way to drop the difficulty and the game is pretty hard.  Moving from dungeon to dungeon, you keep the same health.  The way to heal is a card that you may find or buy, or 1 healing well per level that you may not be able to get to.  Monsters continue to pop even though you may think that you have killed them all. Overall, the game is fun and I would recommend it, but you may want to wait until the bugs are fixed or the price goes down.  There is only 1 adventure to play in the game with "more to come".  I am not sure if you will have to purchase them or not, but can't wait to see what this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Like HeroQuest or a simplified version of D&D, except with nothing going for it.You can't customize your decks. Some of the cards don't tell you what they do. Every time you make an attack—which is once or twice per character's turn (i.e. all the time)—the game forces you to pick a target (even when the attack has no options, like the spinning slash), pick up the die, toss it, wait for the result, wait for the animation, then wait for the attack resolution. What should take three seconds instead takes ten or fifteen.The game wastes your time and makes itself obnoxious at every single step of the journey, and doesn't offer the mechanical complexity or meaningful decision-making to make the time and pain worthwhile. _childDocuments_.review: The Game itself is genuinely a good game but I don't believe the price of this game is reasonable at all.Demeo is a game where a group of up to four people go in and hack and slash to the third floor which has the sinister and evil boss residing in once you defeat that boss, you win The End.Gameplay: The general idea is you will fight enemies with your team with cards or simply dragging and dropping your character onto an enemy you then roll a die it will land and depending on the face of the die it may hit, miss, or crit onto a enemy.As you kill enemies you will gain xp when you level you get a new card this card will not be renewable but everyone in the party will get a card. Which is a slight problem for me as it do's not seem worthwhile to fight enemies if there is no permanent bonus aside from a card. As you delve through the dungeon you will find chests which will hold a card for you to use or gold which can be used when going to a shop which is at the end of every level. Now the key is a item you need to go to the next area but it is guarded by a semi powerful enemy you have to defeat and then after defeating find the exit to leave as well as defeat any enemies guarding said gate.  Once going through the  gate you will be greeted by the shop it can let you buy permanent bonuses or cards. Afterwards you go to the next level, and then finally the boss.  The boss is brutal as it is immune to almost all status effects so it is not hard for it to kill you it also spawns with two mini bosses (from the previous levels the ones who held the key at least that was the case for me.)Overall the game is fun with friends and can be quite chaotic with the hero combos you can have my main gripes with the game is its price i don't recommend paying 40$ for the game as it is rather short and there is not much of a gameplay loop it will get to feel like the same run after some time. Levels don't feel like a power spike as there are no real permanent bonus so speedrunning to the end is kind of required as the more items you use on a level the less prepared you are for the boss. It is also very short as there is only 2 levels and then the boss.  The game is fun and unique but it feels very limited.I also would not be as against this game if it was Early Access but this game is not which is why I sincerely hope they add more to this game like longer runs or more unique effects or something that can change the run on its head as it is I don't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: New Edit: People keep comparing this game to D&D, it's a deck building, tactical board game. The mechanics are very basic and the only thing that makes it challenging is the endless mobs. Descent is more like D&D, this game is more like HeroQuest. To anyone who thinks this is a good game, go try out Descent 2nd Edition on Table Top Sim and discover what a GOOD RPG style board game is like.Realm of the Rat King: The new campaign is identical to the first. Trudge through an endless horde of monsters, get to level 3 and kill the boss. No variation, only like 3ish new monsters and cards.This game just feels awful to play now. You are constantly horded by a never ending stream of monsters. You will often get mobbed repeatedly by high level monsters surrounded by lots of small creatures. Getting past level 1 has gone from a challenge to gruelingly dull due to just being trounced by mobs and being forced to waste every card you get. Trying to thin numbers is a waste of time. Archers can shoot you through walls, ffs and monster archers have longer range than the hero archer. So they can shoot you from across a large room and you can't shoot them back. Monsters have vastly superior numbers, hit points, immunities and do more damage than you. I just feel like the devs have done it's best to make it as hard as possible to advance. They've stripped all fun from the game to satisfy their few players that want it to be stupidly hard.What is funny, mods are coming. We already have mods in the works that can change difficulty in all sorts of ways, by nerfing monsters in various ways and lowering spawn count. This is good news because while the devs shut off a great deal of their playerbase by making the game stupidly hard, modders will make the game more accessible, customizable and maybe even make it into a proper RPG. There is already a mod in the works that has an AI narrating every move. The modders are going to make this game greater than the devs ever will. I predict that the next campaign is going to be paid and possibly cosmetics, cards and characters will start to cost money as well.But I also predict modders will allow you to import models, add new hero types or even allow you to make your own hero. Like a lot of other games, this will be GREAT with mods, but in the end will lose its shine in vanilla. The vanilla servers will die out, but what I also imagine will happen, the game will get an update that blocks mods from multiplayer games.So now, I don't recommend buying this game at all. It's cool that it's in VR, but that's where it ends. Any similar genre game on TTS is just superior, play Mansions of Madness, Descent, Kingdom Death: Monster or Gloomhaven. These are vastly superior games with great balance. They are challenging, but still very fun. Some of them even have RPG elements and proper length campaigns, unlike this game.Maybe in the future, a year or two, this game will either find it's balance or mods will blow up and make it great despite the devs. But until then, the VR gimmik doesn't make the game better than anything you can find on TTS.First Edit: First thing I want to say for new people, this is NOT an RPG. There is NO character progression as far as stats or skills. The deck building is very weak and limited. There just aren't that many cards per hero. There is only 1 campaign which is 3 levels and there are a small number of enemies. Also, only the main characters are animated.This is NOT like D&D in any fashion. It is a board game, much like Heroquest.Original review: The game is fun, but I wanted more. Skipped the tutorial and spent a lot of time goofing around. We had 2 players and we beat the campaign in 1.5 hours. As fun as it was, I was left wanting. I understand that there is more coming out, but I am not sure it's worth the price for this small amount of content.Everything was really well done. Game felt really polished, no noticeable bugs. It felt like a challenge without being TOO hard. I play a lot of these kinds of games, so it felt like it could be good for both newbies and pros. Animations on the champions were fun. Most cards felt good and in general the system felt fine.My biggest gripes (beyond the lack of content) are that I would like for summons to be controlled, otherwise they feel kinda nerfed. I wish tilting was smoother (tilt x with left stick, z with right) or was chosen on a slider. The way it is designed is a bit unintuitive and awkward. Another idea would be to put a knob on the board you can turn to tilt. Lastly, the enemies need animations like the main character. That part of it feels inconsistent.In short, more free content (no paid DLC yet), let us control summons, make tilting more intuitive and more animations.I would not recommend buying this until it has more content with the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love Demeo.It hosts a great online community of friendly players. Its one of the beautiful things about being a non PvP title - it bring players together and generally avoids the negative behaviours on display in mainstream competitive games.The rules of the game are relatively simple but there is plenty of crunch. The randomness of both the dice rolls and card draws is set just right so that I always feel I have agency but that I will regularly have to react and reevaluate my plans. In addition, there are several fun mechanics/interactions in the game which are left to discover via experimentation and sharing of knowledge with other players. This is a clever implementation that really encourages the group to talk - the game never feels like a solitary experience even when playing with complete strangers. All these factors keep the game interesting despite the limited amount of content......I feel that the game needs more content, or far better still an ability for the community to create their own dungeons/scenarios/house rules and share them easily, without having to resort to mods (and whilst fun are quite limited in what they do). I understand the work and infrastructure involved for such an addition would be immense, but I'm pretty convinced it would propel the longevity of this game many decades into the future (think AoE2 and the like).I have played the majority in VR (Quest 1), which is definitely the way I would recommend you play if you have the hardware. Since the recent patch where I can no longer cross-play with the community at large and only with other Quest 1 users, the servers are understandably empty and its hard to find a game. I have since moved over to playing on PC whilst I await the Quest 3 launch. I have enjoyed the PC version though I feel my situational awareness is worsened by my restricted view of the dungeon. Not a big complaint really, its still my favourite game to play.If you like a relaxed atmosphere, a friendly community and a fun game full of 80s basement nerd vibes, this ones going to rock your socks. DELARNIER!

_childDocuments_.review: I am basing my Thumbs Up/Down recommendation based on whether or not this game is for me. It is not. I can see that this game is very much for other types of people, and I will list my impression of this game from why it is not for me. If these things work for you, then charge on.The game is a game within a game. You're moving pieces across a board and playing cards as of it is a board game. This is obvious in the preview, but I thought it would be bother me less than it does. I lose immersion because of this.The spawns are endless. They just keep coming in. There is no victory in a dungeon. There is only escape. You can escape after looting chests, or escape with less loot. There are very few encounter varieties. Wolf, rat, etc, and once you know one, you can codify your approach to it. It will not be long before you have formulated every possible conflict. For me, less than 8 hours.Everyone does identical damage. Armor and weapon type are irrelevant. There is only the skill cards and that is all that separates anything. If you see the big heavy knight and throw her out in front as a tank to protect your mage, you've made a mistake and she is going to die. Also the mage bonking something with his stick does the exact same damage as her sword, which is the same damage a half-dead dehydrated bard would do if he dropped his hand with half intent casually on an enemy's shoulder (this does not exist, but the game mechanics make the statement true if it did exist). Overall: Low immersion, unimpressive combat stats, and repetitive. However if you look for board games with endless conflict and would treat this as a standalone game that has unique function to adapt to, then have at it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a new player, I immediately found myself at a disadvantage due to a severe lack of information during game play. Power cards give poor or misleading descriptions, conditions give no descriptions whatsoever. You might find yourself tagged with a condition and there is no way to know what it actually does, so you can't adjust your tactics accordingly. The sheer volume of enemies swarming you in the first dungeon alone leaves you in a nearly hopeless situation. You need huge amounts of healing to survive yet you are allowed only the most minuscule amount. The d12 dice results in a cripplingly high percentage of friendly-fire attacks. I only played halfway through the second level of the first adventure (book? chapter?) and I killed my own party members TWICE due to "skull" (natural 1) rolls. The special abilities available to each class are far too rare to offer any real chance of survival. I'm a veteran player of turn-based RPGs and this game, while possessing potential, still needs a lot of work before I would recommend it. Although, if you don't care about surviving the dungeons or about effective combat choices, I suppose you could still have fun losing to the AI while laughing with your friends.
