_childDocuments_.review: I'm making a change to the recommendation, because they have released a "PC" version that allows you to play the game without VR. Probably just as well because VR just isn't getting popular enough to entice more players. The PC version is quite good, and suffers none of the problems I mention below. I haven't followed up to see if they ever fixed the VR issues, so I won't hold that against them anymore.=========================== Original VR Review ========================I like the game, but the Windows Mixed Reality VR is a Mixed blessing. The table top looks great, and the animations of the character models are all fantastic. I love the immersion of being in a game room with a full miniatures tabletop setting that you can play on and manipulate at will.Game play is very intuitive and I like the use of the VR hand controllers for manipulating pieces, table and the dice roll.However, here is the problem: The table can be adjusted with the controllers. Zoom in, Zoom out, rotate, raise, lower, etc. But the game will just suddenly move to different position without touching the controls. In the middle of playing a game, boom, I'm looking at a wall instead of the table. As the game continues, this situation seems to get worse and worse until the game is completely unplayable. In fact I've been unable to complete the first level of a dungeon because of this problem. At times, when the game is playing perfectly fine, it will suddenly throw up a black screen saying "resetting your position in 2 seconds." Then it moves the table off to the side and far away. I have to spend several minutes getting the table back to where I can see it. Then often it resets the view again.What is particularly frustrating is that whenever the game "Automatically" resets the view, it always places me looking AWAY from the table. It seems perfectly random. One minute I'm playing the game, and the next second I'm looking at a wall in the virtual "basement."Hopefully this will get ironed out, but given how long the game has been out, I suspect It's just broken beyond repair.

_childDocuments_.review: Issues:Enemies respawn constantly in rooms already cleared. This allows them to constantly flank the player. It gets so ridiculous that you cannot kill enemies faster than they spawn around you. Not really any progression. The game gives no incentive to loot chests or gold or anything really. Because all loot from chests or gold are really just cards that are 1 time use why would anyone waste a 1 time use card just to make it to a chest to get another? Some cards are not strictly "1 time use" but they are in all practicality. You only get to reuse cards from deck after a level which is obtained by x amount of XP. So levels dont even progress the player, they just allow them to use a card they have in the deck. This game really encourages you to rush through the (very small) amount of levels to the end avoiding exploration and fighting. This is compounded by the fact that enemies continuously spawn but yet experience yields no real permanent character progression. Not enough content for 30$. Sure there are lots of grand promises for EA but I prefer not to be at the devs mercy and refund until more content is added.Positives:A way to play a tabletop game with remote friends. This is not a unique benefit to this game but the VR aspect makes it different than many of the others.Unfortunately I have put in a request for refund. This game simply does not offer anywhere close to 30$ worth of fun/value for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this by saying: If you have a dedicated group of friends to consistently play this with, or don't mind playing with total randoms, then I totally recommend this game (assuming the rest of my review doesn't run you off).As it stands, the reason I don't recommend the game is two fold. First, single player. It's the same gameplay as it is with a group, with the same number of enemies, and same difficulty...except playing solo you have a 3-man party instead of 4. While this doesn't appear to be a huge problem at first, this makes getting overwhelmed while playing solo pretty much guaranteed. I'd have more fun drafting up my own solo DnD campaign or listening to nails on a chalkboard than trying to play this game by myself one more time. Enemies constantly spawn in areas where you don't have vision and one less player character means less vision which results in more enemies overall. This also means less damage and less AoE to clear out enemies. So yes, the map can fill up FAST.The second reason I wouldn't recommend it right now, is there's a single campaign (more to be released) and only 4 playabale characters. For 30$, the content and variety isn't there right now in my opinion.Overall I find it to be a fun DnD-esque game to play with friends, but not something I think most of the casual players will find enjoyment in playing solo.Sidenote: I haven't tried the matchmaking (yet) as I'm not typically a fan of random players in games with voice chat. But for the sake of an updated review later, I'll try it and see how the community behaves. When I played with my friends though, the game was a blast! Still just challenging enough to play through and thinking you're not going to make it, but it's SO much more enjoyable with a 4-man team - especially when you work together well.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very rough and I highly recommend you avoid getting it as it currently is with how unfair the game is, if you have a friend you can do co-op mode (2 heroes per player) which is what the game feels balanced around, you can have a good time but it's still stressful.Gonna just leave a simplified list of problems/complaints:Bosses: Boss room/fights are just brutal too much trash filling the rooms on top of questionable design choices for mechanics (newest boss can spawn 4 hands that attack you on top of being able to spawn 6 mini bosses, overkill) Did I mention the bosses get to enter an enrage where they can attack upwards of 4 times a single turn with x2 dmg, yea sounds fun right?Trash mobs: There is too much period, every room is just full of mobs everywhere it's again overkill. Obviously your not meant to clean the entire floor and you should keep moving but the fog of war prevents repositioning safely since you'll move into a hidden space occupied by 7 other mobs. Mobs also spawn endlessly, there is no floor clearing you will be swarmed eventually.Fog of War: Your heroes are legally blind, no that isn't a joke you're unable to see spaces that you absolutely should be able, even if the angle they're in or the elevation they're at should logically show you the tile it won't and it's infuriating.Ai: The ai will literally shoot you through walls and at angles that shouldn't be possible, to add salt the wound if the enemy is ranged and can hit you at their current spot there's a very good chance your hero can't because they're blind.Health: You get 10 hp per hero and are expected to go through 3 floors of trash mobs with insane amount of density and a lot of potential map hazards, yes you can get healing items and fountains but its completely rng, you get one healing potion a hero after that your banking on getting lucky coming across a fountain or another potion in a chest otherwise you have to survive with the hp you came in with to be able to buy a potion from the vendorDice: ♥♥♥♥ the dice, there is 1 side for missing and 1 side for a crit. I swear to god the game intentionally makes me miss when the attack matters the most I have bad luck but the amount of missing I get for it taking a single spot of a dice is too damn high to be a coincidence.Cards: Card descriptions absolutely do not tell you what a card does, it's super vague and sometimes down right misleading (example being a card saying it does dmg to only enemies but in fact can hurt allies too, another being a card says it does 1 dmg in an 3x3 aoe thats it what it doesn't mention is the fact the 3x3 aoe is also a knockback/knockup which is a major bit of information)Pvp: I don't really care about the pvp I have no idea how they even intend to balance it considering how jank the balance is in the pve mode but they're really pushing for it so much in fact that they've decided it needed to be it's own standalone game pulling a complete bait and switch on users who may have gotten it for that or were looking forward to it (in other words a scam unless they offer it for free to current user which they should if they have any respect for their playerbase)Store merge: The only reason I can think of a store merge was a way to hide reviews such as mine criticizing their poor management of this game, so that's scummyTldr: Games fun with a friend but there was clearly no balancing done at any point of release (Also the game has been out well over a year since it released as a vr game first so there is no excuse for how poorly it's balanced) (Devs can't be trusted)

But then any game is fun if you play with the right online players. Reminds me of when I played them properly for real.It's pretty easy to get the hang of and quite simple.In fact a bit too simple. There isn't that much to the game, 3 levels that are semi random and only 4 characters to choose with very limited customisation. It's also heavy over-female represented. You get a Knight (female), an archer (female), an Assassin (maybe female can't tell) and a wizard which is the ONLY male.Seriously? What the hell? It's MALES that are mostly into this kind of thing evident by the fact that in the 5 games I've played they were all male. So why are females so heavily represented esoecially in roles that would be male (as in the Knight). At least give us a male alternative like used to be the case in games!Oh well. that's how it is, I guess. But I have to say. I wanted to play a knight and didn't want to sound like a girl while doing it. Need more choice and more male-representative characters. Also I noticed not one black guy. Why?Not worth full price.I'll keep playing for now and see if it gets better, if it does I'll change the rating.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Demeo in VR which really was nice on the visuals and make you feel like you are really inside that dungeon.The Voiceover is nice and using the cards strategical is fun.But it has quite some issues.For one, the Levels are randomly generated and relatively bland at that. You play through it once, you have seen everything from that level. There are five different layouts. Hardly any story at all. There is a progress system that doesn't feel like progress but just gives different skins.There is an endless spawning of enemies, and they all always know where you are while you can't see them. So you always have to rush to the keybearing monster and then rush to the exit. A bit steep for a 38,99 € game, still steep for 23,99 that I paid in sale. But it is fun to play.The most glaring issue is the save system. You *can not* save during a level of a dungeon. A level can take between 15 minutes and one hour. You can make a pause save between two levels, but as soon as you return to the game, the save is deleted. So if you notice after 5 minutes that your batterie is low or you get a phone call or you don't have that amount of time after all, then you are out of luck. As long as this game don't have a savesystem that doesn't make sense I can not recommend it. Even though playing it really is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic addition to anyone's VR game collection if you like D&D type games. You can zoom right in on characters and the detail is awesome.  There are always games running you can join and I have found the people in the public lobbies to be largely friendly and fun to have a game with - not one rage quit in 70 hours of playing by any team member so that is much better than most games!You have to be clever with your goes, it takes a little bit to master a character, games take about an hour or even a little bit more to go from start of level 1 to the end of a boss fight, but when you join a public game you often as not come in half way through a game.Definitely on my favourites list

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for casual D&D like dungeon crawling. Adventures are split in 3 levels, and the whole adventure takes roughly 3 hours if you're new to the game. Great for people with not a lot of free time but still ache to RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played board and PC/Video games for 25+ years this is one of the best board games on PC I have ever played. I hope they add more adventures, mechanics, and heroes but as it stands EASILY worth the price with an easy hundred-plus hours of replay-ability. This is a must have for PC or VR. _childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: My hours are short on here, but its because I play it mostly on the Oculus. I can play it stand alone or pc. I love being able to take my games with me without lugging around a computer. Also, This game works great on the Steam Deck. I haven't played it online with the Steam Deck, but if I am not playing it in VR, I'm playing it on Steam Deck. Works amazing on it.I would have to say this game is a cross between Dungeons & Dragons and a standard tabletop game. It's a dungeon crawler where you and your opponent take turns. You start the game entering the dungeon and depending on what character you choose you have a limited amount of moves. You get two actions per turn where you can either use both actions to move twice or attack twice. You can even move once and attack once in the same turn. Your powers come in the form of cards which you can collect throughout playing and raising your XP bar. Most of these cards will cost you one action but there are some, like the healing potion, that don't cost an action to use.Whether you play this on your PC or your VR, it's a fantastic game which is constantly being updated with new DLC and characters which are free so far. It can be played with up to four players, you could join random people online if you choose or you can go at it yourself. The more you play, the more XP you gain, in turn which unlocks cosmetics such as different colored dice or costumes for your characters, etc. I've played other games like Gloomhaven which I enjoyed quite a bit, but for some reason this game just scratches that itch a lot better. Maybe because you can customize the way you want to play, or because there are unlocks to work towards. Either way I highly recommend this game. It is one of my favorites and you can cross-play between the standard PC version and the VR version so play it how you like.0 Comments  Subscribe to thread (?)

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the fun I've had with this, I would say that you can do a lot better elsewhere in a game with ANY actual RPG mechanics, without them this just doesn't land for me, although I did have some fun with it. In a world where baldur's gate 3 exists...why would you ever play a game like this? Unless you just really aren't looking for an RPG.Mechanically this feels very much like simplified DnD, if you played it before you will immediately recognize a lot of the aesthetics. If you are an experienced dungeon master you will appreciate what it feels like to play a multi-character party by yourself, likewise DnD players will find a lot of familiarity here and you can even play co-op with a friend and each manage one or two party members.. Where it is not like Dnd is in terms of it's social atmosphere and role playing. There is really none of that here, but that isn't the experience this game is trying to be. Story telling is also pretty much non existent despite the DnD like atmosphere. This is a tactical turn based action rpg combat game. Careful positioning, attacking, interacting with objects, and using abilities are all that will be required of you to survive.It's a decent dungeon delving, mechanical table top feeling adventure game. There is some fun to be had in picking your party, battling monsters and learning their abilities and searching for treasure and loot.It does everything a TTRPG dungeon crawling simulator should do. Lots of tactics in combat and the game can also be quite challenging. Now for the negative thingsI really hate that it lets you save between floors but if you want to exit in the middle of a session you literally lose all progress. Why have this? Atleast let me start over at the beginning of the floor. As it stands it seems like it wipes your entire save file.The RPG aspects of this game are all roguelike. And there doesn't seem to be any permanent progression for your heroes. Don't expect to be allocating skill points or finding a cool new piece of armor or weapon to use on your characters. There is none of that here. Special ability cards carry over between floors but not between missions. Many of the abilities could use better descriptons and/or tooltips. Certain abilities or status effects you will no clue what they do except through trial and error.The game doesn't have a lot of variety. Trying out the different classes and exploring dungeons is fun, but there is not much more to it than that. It is a rogue lite and things are procedural generated it seems, but you will still being doing exactly the same thing every time you play. There is a very barebones meta progression system that takes forever to level up and mainly only gives cosmetic items. I'm not against such a system, it works great in deep rock galactic, but it feels more like an afterthought than anything well fleshed out or exciting.Overall the game lacks depth but doesn't feel like a casual game either, just highly diluted table top strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must have for anyone who likes VR and turn based combat. It is incredibly well done. There are multiple campaigns and heroes which play out differently and use procedural levels, so no two playthroughs ever feel the same. The interaction in VR is top notch and being able to play "in person" just feels so much more fun and natural than pancake multiplayer games. The levels and models are very detailed and well textured. The classes all feel totally different and have their own strengths and weaknesses without any of them being overpowered or weak. Content is continually being added and there is even a hangout area where you can go while you wait for friends to join the lobby. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I think stating the positive first is best then note the negatives. The negatives are not meant to be criticism, more suggestions as I believe and hope there is much more to come with this game. Firstly, this is the best experience I have ever had in a video game. The game in VR is one reason, the other is that they have done everything so well to make this a magical experience. The details in the models, voice acting, making it feel like you are playing a board game with super cool components. The dice has a cardboard texture that looks slightly worn from gameplay. The animations are great. The base gameplay is also very well done. The game is super fun to play, and very well designed. If you want to enjoy a very fun tactical fantasy board game in a beautiful imagined world this is a must buy in VR. It will blow you away. There are some quirks. The tutorial is good and gets you going easy enough, but some card descriptions are vague. +1 movement permanent or just one turn? I believe some cards are one turn others not, but not clear until you play the card to find out. Not a big deal but did effect strategy first/second playthrough. Sometimes you will set up an attack and then find you moved your hand slightly and it was just a move. There is no undo in that case. I now very carefully ensure I have surgery hands when doing an attack. This game would be so much better if there was more cards per class to pick from. Maybe some neutral cards that can be used by all classes that can be bought in the store between levels. I really hope this game keeps going and more content like cards, characters, and levels. There still is a lot of game here already though that will entertain you for a good amount of time.  Game is superawesomegood! :)

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, but it has some caveats.First of all, this is not D&D. It's a tactical dungeon-crawling board game, closer to Descent or Gloomhaven. This may seem like a nitpick to most people, but you must think tactically at all times and cannot pull any punches. The lack of any difficulty settings is sorely missed, but I'm glad they added the Doubles mode, to allow two players to control two characters each. This game is brutal without a full party and hard to recommend playing with any less.That being said, you absolutely need to look up the House Rules mod for this game. It adds options to make this game easier (or harder) in ways you can customize based on your preferences.  It absolutely improved my experience across the board.While the game is out of early-access, they are still adding content. It's come a long way since release. New maps with new monsters and new classes have added a lot of variety to the game. It can still feel repetitive, especially since the only progression is for cosmetic skins (and I kinda feel they're too expensive), but I haven't even seen everything yet, 12 hours in. The earlier reviews saying they completed the game in 1.5 hours must be woefully out of date--my most recent session was 3 hours, and that was just the single  campaign.I did like the Hangout mode, but not being able to keep your custom paints for the main game is a bit silly. Surely that feature is coming later, right? Right?Playing in VR is a lot of fun, and while there have been some tracking issues (which are more on my end than Demeo's), my only real grip is that the tilt options could be improved.  Let the tilt angles be customizable--I never seem to be able to get quite the right angle I want.I sound down on this game, but at the end of the day, it's become one of my favorite VR experiences. The level of detail rivals the best of the real-life Dwarven Forge tabletop tilesets, and being able to zoom in on the map provides the kind of experience I've dreamed of since first playing these kinds of games. The card-based combat is simple but provides enough options to where you're not just using your basic attack every round. I'm excited to see what new stuff is added in the future (like, say, the aforementioned House rules mod).

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a lot of fun for me and is currently one of my favorite VR games.  The game is simple by design, but thanks to the randomly generated maps and encounters remains a new experience every time you play.  The social aspect of the game is even better.  The game allows you to play by yourself or privately with friends, or join up with any number of super friendly people in the community, depending on your mood at the moment.  The campy humor of the game being played in a basement also isn't lost on a person that grew up playing fantasy games with friends in the basements of childhood homes. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute delight.  It reignites feelings of playing the HeroQuest (1989) board game, which I adored as a kid and continue to dust off from time to time.Getting in and out of the game is a breeze and, likewise, getting hooked up with friends is easy enough for quick setup.  The adventuring classes all feel unique and offer the gameplay options one would expect from a dungeon crawl RPG like Demeo.  Much like similar games, each adventure is broken into several areas, and you have the option to collect gold and use it to refill your hand of cards between them.  While you do regain random cards throughout each stage by performing actions or unlocking treasure chests, you do have to make strategic decisions about what cards to hold or play.All in all, I am super stoked about the upcoming crossplay with PC players, as I really need to play more with friends who don't have a VR setup.  I would strongly recommend this game to anyone who likes the idea of a classic dungeon crawl RPG, if only to experience the satisfaction of its bone-crunching critical hits.

_childDocuments_.review: Make no mistake this game is really good and worth it ! I'm really impressed by its experience and the visuals look amazing even on a next-gen headset like the Varjo Aero ! I simply have to applaud the people @ Resolution games in charge of graphics and textures. Equal to the people in charge of moving the board around, zooming in etc. These functionalities form the basics of the game but they we take those for granted so easily we forget how well the devs handled this part.Gamewise it plays very nice as well. After learning all the rules and getting used to them through 30 hours of play you start to  realize this is like a game of chess with alot more options and a large randomness factor to it as well as human interaction because lots of good strategic group decisions are required to complete these missions. As for the negatives:There are really only 3 major settings (with each their own amount of submaps) but you quickly get acustomed to the same settings somewhat which induces a feeling of repetitiveness. Not a problem though.A major room for improvement on the other hand are the characters and their abilities. I've been playing for instance the Bard alot and even though his buffing abilitiy makes him a valuable party member, playing him first hand feels really like a waste of time because every single turn you waste your 2 action points on first moving into a place where you can actually buff your running teammates and then actually renew that buff and that's it :( This feels like you get nothing meaningful do to as a bard nor having options to choose from. To fix it I suggest not assigning an action point to the bard buff. This way the bard could still move and do an action on top of keeping up the buff. This sort of gameplay would feel ALOT more gratifying because it will feel like you actually have a choice to make when playing a bard.Besides that it feels kind of futile (and too hard of a challenge) that no matter how well you group up and bundle your forces the enemy just keeps spawning endless more armies in the dark that eventually overrun you. This makes you feel like tactics don't matter much at all since you'll get overrun no matter what you do. This should be tuned down a bit honestly so that people can really (almost?) CLEAR a certain part of the map and regain their strength before venturing on.All by all GREAT GREAT game of which I'm sure all remaining issues will be improved or ironed out. The foundations are already here so elevating the gameplay to perfection should only be a matter of time.

_childDocuments_.review: A gem. So let's skip to ideas for how to get the most out of it.You CAN tilt the table so that looking straight ahead is looking "down" on the board; for me it's by thumbstick forward. Switch which hand you look at cards in; give your neck and hands variety in what they do, so they tire a lot less. Shorter visibility in Rat King does NOT mean you can't have strategy. I play w. 3 chars: Guardian,Sorcerer,Hunter, in that order. Pick your chars/order for reasons that make sense to you. Guardian can open a door AND block entrance to shield your other chars ... if there's a mob or big-bad over there. (And ... if you stay put, does G get attacked, or not so much?) Look close on monster turn, for glimpses of enemies in stealth, for arrow paths (back to shooter), for where poison or other damage is (floating red numbers, briefly) ... ALSO for range attacks you can see in the dark SOMETHING is on a square (when you hover your range attack card over that square) and deduce what it may be (does it move next turn? did you see what ran into the dark near there? is it immune to Stunned? is it still there after taking the first arrow you can shoot?). You can find out if a Point of Interest in the dark is a chest or a fountain by hovering over it before actually moving there. That's a lot of visibility! Plus Torches and Reveal Enemies when available (note that finding a lack of monsters is just as useful as finding a bunch; either one informs your strategy). Plus Reveal Path and Hunter's Mark for seeing individual big baddies in the dark. Play with and notice what exactly blocks the way for enemies (surprise: spider's nests). The advantage of Magic Wall: Notice the range on placement(!) compared to other blocks like a Barrier. Attack as enemies pile up behind a block, or go the other way while they're stuck. A stunned or panicked enemy will not attack you for that turn, so don't underestimate the advantage there, and clobber other enemies or make some safety for yourself with the breathing room. Count how far enemies can move, add 1 (attack reach), go one more space further away, and that way use being-just-out-of-reach as one defense. Kill creatures that move further/are-closer first. Notice which things will stay dormant if NOT attacked; pick your time to attack them, and maybe never do. Notice when what might seem a minor attack sends something BACK to dormant (instead of, say, activating in 2 turns).An idea: At the beginning of each character's turn, notice if they have a means to restore health, and notice if the card hand is full. Play more defensively if you have run out of health options. Skipping using an action can be much better than moving to be more exposed. Waiting ... is also warfare! Free up a lot on playing SOME card if your card hand is full (or maybe even when only 1 away from being full if your blue card-like points meter is nearly full or a big fight is about to happen AND a treasure chest is nearby). A time like that is your moment to experiment! If nothing else, it may be better to discard a card of lesser value (to you!) of your choice onto the blue meter, to get credit for it, rather than miss out on cards when the meter completely fills. Spend cards to kill enemies; get cards more rapidly. Be wise but not too conservative; it's a balance.TRUST YOURSELF AND TRUST THE GAME. You can figure this out. And the game looks stupidly overwhelming at times, but when you get a feel for it, especially on how to limit your HP damage and spread out or block your enemies, it isn't. It IS a reasonable game; just unforgiving, and not a pushover. In my view this is BATTLE CHESS. And how well you do on levels 1 and 2 sets you up strong (or leaves you crippled) for level 3. Just before you leave a level, play any remaining summon-creatures cards -- they'll be with you next level, and they won't take up a card slot. Strength and Swiftness cards' effects also stay through future level(s). Don't assume the goal is (or isn't) to kill as many as possible; think about what the most effective goal is, for the level. Every time an enemy surprises you, you become a better player, now knowing that trick they have. The ONLY bug I've found is once when 1 of my party moved through 2 others of my party in a doorway ... it showed I can move beyond but in fact it didn't let me; and other times it did let me in that circumstance. A wolf can move through a downed member of your party, but neither other characters nor enemies can.There IS a way to beat the Rat King; don't look online and rob yourself of figuring it out yourself. Notice combination effects ... like (fairly obvious, and not my favorite unless strategically placed) a Lure next to a Cannon. I like that the game saves, and even saves the Shop choices you were dealt, and that it is more limited in layouts and has a fixed set of types of enemies. For me, a chessboard that changes too radically game to game would negate my hard won experience. I like playing a similar thing (but random starting positions) again to see if I can beat it this time. If you exit the game via Steam system menu BEFORE YOUR WHOLE PARTY IS DOWN (when that looks inevitable), you can replay from the last save.I zoom in and reach toward a piece before I pick it up; which makes moving it and dropping it where I want harder to goof up. Hover over gold, THEN drop on top of an adjacent enemy to both get the gold and attack the enemy in one move. I have both zoomed across the board (carefully!), and holed up with a Healing Ward and ways to block the entrance(s) of the room I'm in to do away with many enemies. Shooting arrows through characters does no damage to friendlies. Piercing Throw does. Lamps block as well as serving their obvious function ... without acting like a Lure(!) ... subject to the risk of some enthusiastic elven archer. The Tutorial is very good, and good to revisit after a few games.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.  So much fun with friends.  With some minor exceptions, it is balanced really well also.  It may not seem like it the first few times you play through, but as you get better at the game, you start to see that it is.  Highly recommended!!I have to keep editing my review because this game just keeps crawling up the ladder to be one of my favorites.  My first review was "Game is meh..."  Second review is above.  Now - I have to add to it to say that this game has given me the BEST dungeon crawling experiences I have ever had in ANY RPG....  EVER.  Several times we've gotten that critical hit, right at the right time....  or that critical miss!  So many "you played that card at the right time, at the exact right spot".  So much fun.  Also - I take back my statements of it having some minor balance exceptions.  It's all in knowing the true strength of your characters and playing them correctly. _childDocuments_.review: Demeo is an ok rogue-lite turn turn based dungeon crawler but it still could use more content. Online multiplayer is what really elevates it and makes worth buying.Tactical gameplay is minimalistic but fun, with minimum reading necessary as it was designed for VR. Pacing is really good especially for a turn based title: enemy AI takes very little time to make its moves and there are enough monsters to make every turn matter. Difficulty is just right to be satisfying, but could use some optional tougher challenges. Since having different difficulty levels might disrupt matchmaking, adding some Pandora's boxes or sealed rooms with most dangerous monsters could have been the best solution IMHO.Enemy and skill-cards variety is a bit lacking: after beating both campaigns ones you will experience pretty much everything this game has to offer in terms of content. I still enjoyed playing the game a few times after finishing campaigns, thanks to very well implemented online coop and decent player base. Demeo has enough replayability for a VR game, but can't really compete with flat-screen TBS juggernauts like Into the Breach.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun tabletop experience in VR with 4 distinct character classes, interesting sets of abilities, and a limited but interesting number of enemy types. If you're playing in a group, it's best played with a complete party of 4. The game doesn't appear to scale the difficulty based on number of active players so running a session with only 3 people can be challenging and just 2 people nearly impossible. If you're looking for a single player journey there's a skirmish mode that allows you to control all 4 characters. Unfortunately, in multiplayer, you're limited to controlling one character per player. The runs can be kind of long and as best I can tell there's no way to save mid-run and resume later (2-3 hours each). There's no real experience progression or character development. It would have been interesting to allow people to develop a character type and for the game's difficulty to scale based on group composition and experience. Instead, each round starts with the same base character types and stat sheets. Experience does unlock some fun aesthetic upgrades for each character as well as different die types.

And even with a full party, the realm of the rat king is still decently hard!)

_childDocuments_.review: After about 10 hours of play time, the replayability of the game is one of the best I've experienced out of most of today's games.Pros:The game is fun and engaging. The strategy aspect of it really gets you into feeling like decisions you make, can make or break the run, and personally I enjoy that. The deck building aspect is also a nice touch to the strategy. And like i said before even with there only being two levels right now, I still feel like I wanna go back and play again and again due to the randomness of each different play through.Cons:Not many to be honest, but some of the friendly AI decisions kind of make you scratch your head. So personally I would like to see an IQ increase of a little. And to be honest the only complaint I really have is enemies having lines of sight the players do not. If a ranger shoots me, but i can't see him to retaliate to stop that damage, it puts a slight unfair tilt towards the enemies.All in all it's a great game, I can not wait to see what else is in store for the game, but I would make a few QOL changes (if it were me).1. Make a non VR port to the game. VR is a great way to play the game, but sometimes VR isn't an option and the drive to play the game is still there. I.E. Babysitting children. Or after a few hours of VR headaches. I'm no Game Designer or engineer so I really can't say how difficult it would be, but I feel like using the arrow keys to move the camera around, Right click to move around the table. Scroll wheel to zoom in and out. You could make it to where your hand always shows at the bottom of your screen in the UI, and having Left click do everything else is Pheasable. Not sure though. Just a thought.2. Make the ally AI a little smarter. Not overpowered, but maybe if they attack a monster and it's Immune, then the next turn they'll focus on another mob. Instead of just keep attacking the immune monster over and over, wasting their life.3. Instead of letting the ranged monsters get free damage on the party, if you pick the archer or have the archer in your party, maybe make it to where if the goblin is out of LOS or just out of view he shows up just for the archer, giving the archer the chance to stop the free damage. I understand that may actually be of game design to make the game a bit more difficult. but some monsters do way to much damage to not be able to fight back or try and use moves to go find them and get LOS.4. The sorcerer feels very under powered. His damage is not really there, and while he dose bring some utility, I don't feel his stun is really all that helpful. It helps with the small adds that for the most part can be one shot, but most of the dangerous adds are all immune to the CCs. So I would either make less of the big guys immune or give him a bit more damage to make up for it.5. In the future I would like to see a cleric style class added to the game. Not one to overpowered, maybe mid damage/ mid heals. or no Damage and focuses solely on heals. That would make a great addition to the game.All in all, I can say for the price it's really worth the price. I would recommend the game to anyone that enjoys the fantasy style turn bases Strategy deck builder!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't consider this to be my final review, as this game is still in it's early stages. I enjoy the game a lot, you'll spend a minimum 1hr 30min playing through 3 dungeons if you're in a party of 4. So make sure you made time before getting started. You have 4 classes, Wizard, Archer, Warrior, Assassin. Each class has their own unique abilities/cards. If it's your first time playing, you'll find the game a bit difficult at first. But once you've played a couple of rounds, it's rare that you'll lose at any point. I do believe they should provide a difficulty option, as I understand it the game difficulty scales with the amount of players, but I find this not to be enough of a challenge when you're in a party of experienced players. At first I thought I would get bored with playing the same dungeon over and over again, but since they are all randomly generated, the experience is fresh each time. If you don't mind grinding through the same dungeon, love DnD style games, want more VR games, then I'd definitely give this game a shot. If you think playing a single dungeon over and over again is a bit boring, then I'd wait until they've made more dungeons, which I do believe the next dungeon is coming next month for free.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game last night, and I have to say it is really fun. The ways that you can manipulate the game board (shifting it, resizing it, tilting it) make for a very comfortable and immersive experience. I do have a couple of gripes with the game however:1. This game is too easy. Now, I am certainly not a noob when it comes to turn-based dungeon crawlers. I've played DnD many a time, and I'm used to strategizing with other players. However, all three parties that I have run so far have ended in victory. Heck, you don't even need a diverse party to win. My last party last night started out with 4 sorcerers, then after one left, we picked up a rogue. Our one sorcerer was pretty reckless, and basically attempted to confront the final boss on his own. Even with having to cover for his mistakes and rolling an enormous amount of misses in a party full of melee squishes, we won pretty handily. I think this is a far cry from what the Demeo trailer advertises.2. Lack of certain protections from trolls, lone wolves, etc. Now, I know that the host can kick people, that's great. However, there is one situation where a lot of power is vested in one person and where this power can be used to screw over the whole party: acquiring the key. In order to open the door to the next floor, only the person with the key has to get to the door and open it. The other players, even if they want to get the rest of the gold on the floor or open the rest of the treasure chests, are powerless to stop that one character. Moving on to the next floor should be something that the majority of the party needs to agree on, or there should at least be an option to toggle a vote in order to move on.I would go on about how the game lacks content, but others have already done so, and the development team is already planning new adventures. Hopefully the rapid growth of the Demeo community inspires the devs to keep churning out new content.If you are thinking about purchasing this game, I would probably take the plunge now before they add more content. The atmosphere is great, the animations are great, the card-acquiring system, while unorthodox, is also great. There are enough people online to find a game pretty reliably and quickly, and I would certainly recommend this game to any fan of turn-based strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game this is! i am not into Dungeon Crawlers in real life but i do play board games here and there. The only real downside of Demeo is that  it only has 1 campaign right now (more to come). However, the levels are randomly generated so if you like the game there is a huge replayability waiting for you!The online commutity you play with is really good. _childDocuments_.review: So much potential!!!This game is great so far! Disregard the negative reviews about not enough content. They are already announced more content coming this summer. Plus there are tons of skins and dice to unlock. The character models and animations are awesome. I do with the enemy tokens had animations as well but that's something they can add later I suppose. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of VR content out there is garbage, but this is decidedly an exception. I would rank this as one of my top 3 VR titles to date.  It's a great game that is worth the price.  The VR experience is smooth, intuitive, and engaging.  Multiplayer matchmaking works well and mostly glitch free.  The game is tough, but not too tough  to be fun. If you like turn based tactics games and have a VR headset, this is the game for you.  The only downside is that its still lacking in content.  I played about 20 hours and feel like I'm done with the experience. I realize that more content is on the way, and as that comes out I will be sure to play it.  My congrats to the developers.  This is a great game that capitalizes on the enormous potential of VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Take Diablo and mix it with this holo-chess from the star wars movie - thats Demeo.Most fun if you have friends to play with, just exploring dungeons with randomized monster/treasure placement, thats enough to trigger some addiction. It is also super relaxed, as you can play it seated, which i highly recommend, as standing and looking down on the tabletop will give you a sour back after some hours.Of course the game is not perfect, so many possibilities to enhance it still, but the devs are active and the community is positive, cheers.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocre. As many others have said, the amount of content is rather pitiful. This does not only apply to there only being one "adventure", but also to the very low variety of enemies and cards. Because of that, replayability is very low.The core combat system is also rather limited. You only have two actions every turn, and a somewhat limited amount of cards, so the tactical options are not very broad either.Finally, I don't really see what this game gains from being VR. All of the mechanics would play and feel better on a flat screen, and the choice of visuals does not justify it either.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Good sound with music you can turn down to a less-than-deafening level.+ Fun card/ability mechanics.  Decent variety for different classes/characters.+ Graphics!  Wow!  Love the way it looks!+ Fair price for a very nicely polished VR game.+ Continued content updates (if they push them out at a decent rate).  Replayability skyrockets with more maps.Cons:- Not really /enough/ characters.  I also HATE being gender-locked.  Let me choose a male Archer or a female Wizard.- Voices.  I'm not sure if they just don't fit the character models in my head or if they're just... not good.  Especially Rogue.- An occasional weird glitch with microphones.  No other game I play has this problem.  It just... stops working.- Cosmetic rewards (maybe?) that reward you for replaying... except that there's only ONE 'module'.  Grind-fest maximus.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is in it's infancy, it provides a badass VR experience. I cant wait for more characters with unique decks (please add a brewmaster). I have been trying to encourage my friends to get this game as I think it's something we could potentially spend hours playing together. A few things that I think may need some tweaking are the following:========================================================================*COIN FLIP (Rogue Card)  -The Rogue class gets a card called Coin Flip. It's an extremely cool card where you flip a coin, and if heads is flipped, the mob you target is instantly killed. In my very first boss encounter while playing a skirmish, I used coin flip on the Elf Queen and one shot her. I felt that the scenario was very anti climactic and was expecting to have my work cut out for me.*LINE OF SIGHT/TARGETING   -There were a  couple instances where an enemy archer shot me through a wall which made no sense whatsoever. This doesn't seem like it was intended to be a part of the game since the Paladin/Warrior class thing has a nice Line of Sight mechanic for it's lancer throw.========================================================================I am not trying to complain, but highlight issues I have encountered thus far.The game is listed at $30 which may seem a bit high. I am in defense of the price point and think that it is reasonable. If you are someone who adores these types of table top games, this is a great project to back. Like I stated before, I can't wait for more classes dungeons.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: IT HAS CROSS PLAY!!!!I have played two games now and i am super hooked. It is so fun to be able to play a table top game like this with strangers all over the world. The best part is that its all cross play and it does not matter if you are on the Quest 2 or Steam. I cannot wait to see what comes of this game because it is such a great idea that can be expanded on A LOT!!! I was worried about having to look down the whole time but you can tilt the board so you can look straight ahead and still get the same view if you are looking down at the board.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a perfect tech demo of things to come with VR.The map movement, ability useage, and how you can pick anything up is absolutely next level.It's an incredible experience. This is one of the few times that I will suggest you purchase a game that I can't even come to play anymore. The issue is that it only has 1 map right now, and it only lasts about an hour and a half. The only reason to replay the level is to get new skins for your dice and characters, which is wonderful, but not enough to keep me coming back every day to play.They will be releasing new content over time, and so long as they don't require you to pay for it like DLC, I will always suggest this game. However, the 1 single map is absolutely not worth 30$, so if they start asking for more money per newly added map, I'll have to change this to a negative review.I hope other companies look at how Demeo made all of it's systems work and use that as a framework for the next generation of VR games. An XCom game in this style would be absolutely amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't get enthusiastic about games set in sword and sorcery style settings. My friends played Dungeons and Dragons in real life, so i got in on the games to be sociable. This VR game, takes the best parts of the D&D tabletop game experience and simplifies the rule set. Even if you don't like magic and sword fighting games, There is lots to enjoy with this VR title. Game runs great on even lower end hardware but my experience was with a 5800x and 6800xt. Fluid animations, no hiccups during gameplay. I hope the developer increases the number of classes and characters that are playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: So far i'm 4 hours in and i'm absolutely loving it. The polish to this game is amazing. I love the fact that you can zoom in and be face to face with creatures and other players. The fact that the world around you has life to it is also awesome. This game has so much potential and i REALLY hope to see this game grows to the next D&D style game. Yes, there are bugs, connection issues, and other annoyances that i would hope to see fixed. Even with the issues there are this game is more than worth 30dollars. I hope that content comes in a steady stream and i would also hope they open up mod support. Join me in supporting what could be the best VR TTRPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: I've played single player only for about an hour, and I'm enjoying the game.  I'll definitely be trying out MP soon.* Tutorial is quick and to the point. * Camera controls seem natural (think Minority Report -esque).* I liked the seated gameplay.* Long game sessions didn't give me vertigo/ motion sickness(Rift CV1)
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well polished and high quality game in terms of assets, sounds, voiceovers, and etc. Currently only has 1 campaign that is fairly short (1hr-2hrs to complete) but I still consider the purchase worth it for the enjoyment it gave and the future potential it will have. There are no difficulty settings currently. The procedural generation can sometimes create wildly easy or sometimes somewhat difficult fights. It's also not clear how mobs spawn, we cleared an entire dungeon one time and had to just wait for new spawns, which I think is an awkward and not immersive mechanic (better to just spawn the dungeon with all encounters already).Overall I think this presents what the potential of VR should look more like nowadays - high quality social gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: It's great to play at the beginning and fun with friends. The best experience for me is to played it with 3 other friends. The talk and coordination becomes natural and similar to pen and paper rounds.For now there is very little content that you can play which is a shame. There is also very little narrative play, character progression, story evolution, and similar elements that i am missing from standard RPGs. VR leans itself well to be this kind of tabletop combat simulator. Don't forget to adjust the angle of your view with the right thumb stick to avoid looking down all the time.Several months after the release and there are still some blocking bugs that can kill a gaming session.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great for the art style selected. The gameplay is good, except for some glitches. Hopefully that will be addressed soon.Is it worth $30 ? Yes and no.Yes, it's fun to play. Friends would be great to game with (up to 4 players). PUG's are even fun with the right group and mentality. No, there is only one dungeon, in which to play. Yes, it re-arranges parts of the levels to look different, but it's the same parts. It really doesn't matter much, as the levels are small, especially the 3rd level. Why does it take 1.5 hours to over 2 hours to play? Well, there are a few reasons. The game is still new to most players and they just haven't gotten the hang of it yet. There are "quirks" and sometimes it makes things a little harder to do the things you need to do. And there can be a fair amount of fun being had by the group.This game looks like fun and it is. This game looks easy and it is... and it isn't. I've been in groups that lost. Failed throws, misused spells, bad cards from chests and bad play can hurt the group. Critical hits (Crits) can save the group. Usually everyone experiences both during the games.Having an experienced player in the group, is good for the group. There is much to learn.Since Resolution Games is providing additional content this summer ('21), I would have to give this a "recommend", even at $30.

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody brilliant.Since it's turn-based combat, it ends up being a very chilled, social game - perfect for me to play with friends who live on the other side of the world. It's simple enough to pick up, even for somebody with little tabletop RPG experience, but there's plenty of strategy and tactics to explore. The graphics and animations are great - some of the enemies like the big slimes look fantastic! The controls are OK - I'd rather be able to control the camera/zoom/etc. with the joysticks as well as with motion controls - to move a long distance to scout out a room or zoom all the way in/out or whatever, you really have to "swim" quite far with the controllers. Also sometimes it's a little annoying to drop your counter on a particular enemy/tile without repositioning your view or reaching forward an uncomfortable distance.The dungeon layouts and enemies are randomly generated, but right now like others have said the content is quite limited for a game at this price. I really hope that the devs continue to add more content into the base game, rather than splitting everything off into paid DLCs. At the moment there is enough content for a good few hours of fun, but with more maps, enemies, character classes, cards/spells, bosses, etc. this could be a truly groundbreaking VR game. I think that the high price is justified, so long as they continue to add more free content to flesh it out. What's already there is very well done and polished to a sheen, but it feels like a very generous demo rather than a full price VR title.It would also be great if there was some kind of progression system that impacted your character within each run, rather than just an overall level up system to unlock cosmetics. For example, being able to increase your HP pool, damage, armour, poison/frost resistances; or give you specialisations that give you extra damage against certain enemy classes. etc. Perhaps after completing a map you're given the choice of a single upgrade to help you for the rest of the run, so you can build out your character differently each run.Opening this up to Steam Workshop so modders can make their own maps, enemies, etc. would be a huge boon to the game and instantly counter any complaints about the lack of content in the game as it stands.I also hope that this ends up being a mixed VR/pancake experience, so people without VR can join in. This game doesn't really *need* to be in VR - don't get me wrong, it works pretty well in VR, but it's just a tabletop game, VR doesn't give you any extra immersion or interesting controls, but it definitely does vastly improve the social experience. being able to point out features and indicate them to your friends directly rather than via pings makes everything so much more tangible, but I feel like the game would also work great with a mixture of VR and 2D (and obviously massively increase the potential audience).Besides Walkabout VR Golf, this is probably the best VR multiplayer experience I've had. Definitely worth a buy if you're at all into tabletop RPGs and have a few friends you can play with. They've done a fantastic job with this and I can quite safely say that unless you're really hard up for cash, you can ignore the negative reviews on here. When the biggest complaint about a game is "it's great but we want more of it", and the devs have promised to deliver frequent content updates... you might as well get on it now.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure I would like this game. I am old school D&D. I like choices. I like SO MANY choices. This game doesn't really give you a ton of choices in terms of character selection/creation or selecting your own starting spells, etc... In the skirmish that I played, you don't get to have 2 mages or 2 fighters or whatever. That is already decided. All that said, this was so much fun! The 3 hours I played my first skirmish before my party died a horrible and ignoble death really just flew by. I was worried I would get motion sick with the movement of the table as I zoomed in and out, but I didn't have a problem with it (although it was giving me a headache when I watched someone else stream it - so I agree with other watchers that having a streaming option that makes it stay in one place would be desirable). I enjoyed zooming the table in and out to see different vantage points, turning the table as needed to be able to see better or get closer to my targets.  The environment really worked well for me.  Learning the controls was very easy. Using them - same - very easy. I also thought the artwork was well done. It's a very distinctive style and cohesive. You do have opportunities to select things later. There definitely is a learning curve on how to deal with certain circumstances and how to best use all you have been given to meet your objectives.  I'm looking forward to playing it again. My wish list? I'd like to be able to customize my character and select starting spells/weapons. (More like D&D that way.) I'd like to be able to play with all 4 characters in skirmish mode. And in a perfect world, I'd like to be able to play mixed VR/non-VR so I can play with more friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game, but I also do recommend waiting a bit for them to actually release a full module/campaign as I'm sure lots of other reviews will have said, the game currently just features 1 boss that spawns in the same boss room, and 2 randomly generated maps One small one larger and thats ya lot for levels. But once you get the basics of the game down there isn't a huge amount of challenge or variation.I've done five runs so far, once solo, once with two of us, and three times with four players which there was no comms as it was quick play and haven't lost a game yet. _childDocuments_.review: It is games like this that raise the bar of expectation for gaming (in this case VR gaming). There are others that you already almost certainly know about. As usual, it isn't something particularly new as a concept. It is mostly the thoughtful and careful execution, that takes it to that level.  This is a surprisingly good start for a table-top RPG implementation.  Its an easy game to play. If not, perhaps, not so easy to succeed at - at least at first. The environment is well thought out and no doubt will be improved upon. The graphics are good, but with engaging game-play, not as important as one might think. And 'think' you will have to.Whilst Single player 'Skirmish' is satisfying, Multiplayer turn's this into an enjoyable social experience and the mechanics of the interface do not get in the way - which is something of an achievement in itself.There are undertones of 'Hearthstone' in the card play mechanics and some of the presentation, that knit together with a table-top, cosy room atmosphere in the game that will let hours spin away and batteries drain. Yes, this game is very likely to keep you engaged long enough to have to worry about battery life...I am genuinely surprised just how well this rather obvious take on table-top gaming works in VR. I am fascinated to see where the developers take this as they explore the possibilities it offers.If you have any interest in this 'genre' of gaming at all and own a suitable VR headset, I would, at the very least, recommend a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this is definitely the start of a great game. As it stands there is only one adventure with 1-2 hours of gameplay but you can play through that 4 times with each of the unique classes which stretches that to a slightly better amount of extra gameplay. That time is thoroughly enjoyable though because the only major problem with this game is its lack of content which is a good problem to have assuming they add levels and mechanics at a good pace.In my opinion this is an early access game, as it stands its a very simplistic and short game as you can move, attack and use ability cards. Theres no armor, weapons, or even character levels. The ability cards are cool and all but there really aren't that many to spice the game up. What I'm seeing is a strong foundation of a game that if added to regularly could become the Beat Saber of tabletop games for VR. I definitely recommend picking up this game to both enjoy it for yourself now and encourage the devs to add more quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Demeo

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice VR tabletop dungeon crawler that came out of nowhere from my perspective. Enjoy the graphics, animations and overall esthetic...it's funny to get immersed in the details of the dungeon with it's monsters, layout and such only to come back to remembering that in this title you are playing the dungeon "table" in a VR basement...but the REAL reality is that you are playing it in your living room in a VR basement in a VR dungeon. Inception anyone?Kidding aside this game looks good and gladly also plays very good too. It was very intuitive on how to control the world, play your characters and cards and evolve throughout the game. There is also a encyclopedia of controls/tips and simple feedback explaining both the gameplay and game elements but it's real easy to pick up.It is short as many have expressed. Three levels in the solo skirmish. Have not played multiplayer yet to see if there are differences. I fully expect that this game will be successful and should warrant the producers to generate future added scenarios to flush it out more. Ideally a editor or workshop inclusion would be a great future goal for this title too as then a community could bring it's collective abilities to purpose. Even with it's short initial campaign/mission though it seems the general layout and seeding of monsters/chests/healing statues etc are all procedural so there is lots of replayability. There also appears to be some player/character progression that occurs but I haven't played enough yet to see how that further develops.Overal, very glad I got this and would certainly recommend it as one of better VR titles in recent memory and seems like it will be ripe for further development.Final Though...This also smacks of Gloomhaven like play although it is not a straight clone of said game, so if you like that idea of strategy/puzzle like dungeon crawlers...this VR title is the most immersive I have seen yet!

_childDocuments_.review: the only problem so far is how long the animation time is when you miss, other than that the game is fun and challenging. _childDocuments_.review: Remember back in the days when playing Hero Quest with friends - or more recently Gloomhaven? Finally we have something similar in VR and it is just as good as one would expect. If you love board games this will hit the spot.The game play works amazingly well. Granted there are bugs here and there but overall I did not hit that many (blocking) problems during the first 3 hours of game play. It took some attempts to find a game but after the game was found the experience was great.Then to the price and content. Sadly the amount of content lasts just about 1 hour - it is literally 3 maps and that is it. You have choice of 4 different character types so the game will definitely stay interesting for some replays but in the end the game is just screaming for some longer campaign (like in Gloomhaven). There is a note from the developer that two more "books" will be added later on (for free if I understood correctly) but have to say even with the added content it is quite little what you get for your money at least time wise.Giving thumps up for this one even with the high price point - it is the best board gaming experience you can get in VR right now and I would highly recommend at least supporting it. This is one of the fields where VR really shines and I have been puzzled that it took so long someone to fill this gap.

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now I have played two matches, a skirmish (solo mode where you control 3 heroes) and a co op with a friend. There's something intense about you using your body to block a door from a swarm of monsters while a friend chucks spells over your head.As it stands right now, it's essentially a virtual board game with no expansions but with more content (and mouse and keyboard support) on the horizon, I'm excited to see where this goes.

New modules will make it even better,

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly great (with minor gripes) review.There are a lot of really good things about this game. I love the presentation of it all, being in a 'stranger things' style basement playing with three other people on a living board game - It just feels good to play...The animated board is amazing. Spells flying everywhere, characters reacting to incoming attacks, the ever-growing poisoned areas. It all feels very interactive and exciting.However, a couple of things stop this slightly short of greatness on day one of release. Moving around the board is a bit awkward. I found myself looking at odd angles most of the time at the map and it took me ages to work out the controls for tilting the camera.Secondly, it feels a bit lacking in content right now (I know, I know. It only just came out but it should feel deeper than it does at this point). I know some more things will be coming  but I was hoping for a full on campaign, like the Descent boardgame. I hope this comes, along with more maps and heroes, etc.But these things are not game changers for me. Day one of playing and I love it so far. Good interaction in multiplayer and a good gaming experience overall.  I would recommend buying this if you love board games or fantasy rpgs. I can see potential for player created maps, mods, and tons of possibilities built on this solid system they have. I know this is literally the same day that the game came out, but I have a few ideas/gripes. 1. Clearing a floor can take a little while, let alone doing all 3! The biggest miss of this game so far is not having a save option! I had to abandon our long fought 2-player clearing of a floor, and we'll have to start over next time. Having a save button is essential!2. Somehow when you open the first door, it's like you've aggro'd the whole floor. i.e. enemies will keep pouring from the halls while you're fighting. detailed_description: Hoa is a beautiful puzzle-platforming game that features breathtaking hand-painted art, lovely music, and a peaceful, relaxing atmosphere. Experience the magic of nature and imagination as you play the main character, Hoa, on her journey through breathtaking environments back to where it all began. Breathtaking hand-painted art Step into a painting that lives - explore a vast world of meticulously crafted sceneries of stunning hand-painted art. Outstanding original soundtrack Captivatingly story-telling and emotionally-charged, Hoa's exceptional score, originally composed and live-recorded, brings its world to life with a touch of nostalgia. Lovely creatures Keep an eye out for delightful magical creatures along the way. Most of them want to be friends, some might even tell you a little story or two. Cuteness guaranteed. Gentle, yet compelling flow Navigate with a keen eye and solve exploration-based puzzles. Relax to the organic rhythm of subtle storytelling while being intrigued by endless little wonders. Be a child - it's easier and harder than it may seem.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually this is not a bad game, but to be honest, it's not a great game either. "Hoa" will easily impress people with its art style, which is heavily inspired by Ghibli anime. The soundtrack is another good thing, though there is a problem with the way they used the music. Throughout the game, there is just one song is played in the background, with a little tune with certain area. You may feel intriguing with the music, but soon, after 2 or 3 areas of the game, you'll find it boring to listen to the same melody over and over again.The story is short, easy to understand and follows the theme of fairy tales, but also tells the message about the environment. The gameplay is kind off matched with the theme, at least in the concept. The game's pacing has problems when allocating time between regions is relatively uneven and inconsistent. "Hoa" brings no sense of danger, too serene for its own good. Hoa also does not bring the feeling of wanting to explore. As soon as you enter a new area, a map pops up and just show you where every item is located, and most of the game follows a predictable pattern. Level design is okay, not entirely bad, but also not good and clearly not memorable. The same thing can be said with the puzzles. The chasing sequence is a huge chance for player to test every skills they learned, but Hoa wasted it by transforming it into a cutscene. The final level of the game is something standouts as the most creative part of the game. The mechanics of this level grow to be so counterintuitive that someone may find it bizarre and obnoxious, but clearly this is the most memorable level. "Hoa" has made a certain effort in creating a relatively consistent and quite pleasant experience. Although the movement mechanics, puzzles, and level design lack depth and have certain pacing problems, in the end the experience can still be considered okay. I will recommend this game, but only if those who intend to play it already had a mindset of going to play an above average game. "Hoa" is not bad, but also not very good, and not really memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is a breathtakingly gorgeous and non-violent platformer. Featuring simple puzzles and an abundance of cuteness, all whilst being wrapped up in a relaxing yet captivating atmosphere. It may have short playtime, but it is a standout experience from start to finish, and one I wholeheartedly recommend to fans of the genre.There are few words in Hoa, and although there is some readable text with a handful of characters, most of the context is given through the detailed surroundings. You play as a little creature named Hoa  (I believe this is Vietnamese for flower). Hoa instantly begins her journey with almost no explanation as to her goals. She traverses across fields, oceans, dark caves and more. Meeting wise creatures along the way who remember her past and help guide her on her mysterious journey. Hoa's story is completely explained through a poignant final cutscene, which puts the whole adventure into perspective. Until this moment, it is not clear who any of the characters are, or what their significance is, including the protagonist. Being a 2-4 hour game, this approach does not bother me, and instead I found it impactful. Telling a short story through art alone, worked well for my engagement. The story is not complex, in fact, nothing about Hoa is necessarily complex, but all the pieces come together with such finesse to create a memorable experience.Hoa is a 2D platformer and as stated previously, it is not difficult, nor is it violent. You cannot die or become injured in any way. Time your jump wrong? You’ll be transported just a few seconds back. Run into a robot, and you will only get a slight kick, serving as an annoyance as opposed to a hindrance in any way. Players eventually acquire simple abilities allowing Hoa to double jump, smash, push and fly/hover. Puzzles are only exploration based, almost always consisting of locating five butterflies to proceed. Each area is beautifully distinct and has a nifty little map to help players if needed. Each of the areas features a character that is connected to the protagonist in some way, and Hoa must first awaken them, and then gather the five butterflies to be taught a new skill to proceed.Hoa truly was such a relaxing experience. From the moment I launched it, I felt my mood improve. From the beautiful, bright art, to the loud yet uplifting instrumental soundtrack, I was already impressed from the first few opening minutes. Fortunately, the game only continued to impress and matched these feelings of serenity with its gameplay elements. Although each level follows the same formula, explore, wake up the creature, collect butterflies, repeat. It never felt repetitive, potentially due to how short it was, but also how different the levels were, visually. Yet, without mentioning any spoilers. The last level completely changed things, focusing on gravity-based puzzles which unfortunately do make me feel quite sick, completely opposing all previous chapters. It is still of simple nature, but for me, it was a bit of a sour note to end on.Games with beautiful screenshots on its store page lure me in every time. Hoa was no different, and it is its stunning hand-crafted art that makes it what it is. With a strong focus on nature and vivid patterns, I couldn't help but see resemblance with Studio Ghibli. Seeing flowers bloom as you jump on them, the cutest rhinoceros beetles, the impeccable colour palette, it all brings Hoa's natural and stunning world to life. Another strong point is the accompanying original soundtrack. Full of zest and exuberance, the instrumental score oozes positivity and wonderfully compliments the adorable surroundings. Without much dialogue, and without any voice actors, the importance of the soundtrack should not be underestimated in its ability to tell a story, and here it succeeds fantastically. Approx. 4 hours, however the game can be completed in 2. Yes, but keyboard is also supported  None, it is a linear story. I have 100% achievements, few are missable but are very easy to gain in just one playthrough, or through chapter select.A simple, gorgeous and truly delightful little platformer. Its relaxing atmosphere drew me in from the beginning and combined with its Studio Ghibli aesthetic, it was a pleasure to play. It is on the shorter side, but if you are not bothered about simple gameplay and the art appeals to you, I highly recommend picking this one up.
