_childDocuments_.review: One day after a hard day at work, I was seeking a stress-free game, and Hoa came across my recommendations. Although there are flaws with the game, it was the game that I was looking for to relax. The art design makes you feel like you're running through a world straight out of a Ghibli animation. The vibrant colors, whimsical creatures, and relaxing soundscapes throw you into an anime-inspired world that is a treat to navigate. The gameplay is very stress-free. Unlike most modern platformers, death is impossible since nothing can kill you, and falling is forgiving, so you don't have hard segments to repeat. The flow of the game is simple. Players take the role of a fairy, slowly discovering what happened to her after being kidnapped. You were able to escape with the assistance of the forest creatures and a mysterious being. In each area, you will meet an individual and piece together what happened to you. Right at the start of each site, you are given a map with two types of symbols on it. Aside from the final area, you have to collect five stars in each location and activate a few emblems to wake up the animal there. Once they are awake and the five stars are collected, they will teach you a new ability to progress. The game's climax plays differently, adding more puzzle elements and a navigational bit involving screen rotation. The story does an excellent job of compelling the player to figure out what happened to them but, unfortunately, fails to deliver a satisfying ending. The last segment of the game was a bit disorienting to me with all the screen rotation, but I still felt satisfied solving the puzzles in that stretch of the game. In the end, the way the developers wrapped up the story just wasn't worth it to me since I still had unanswered questions. The game clocks in a little short, which makes the price vs. content feel a bit steep. There isn't much replay value since there aren't any hidden secrets, extra whimsical characters, or dialogue to discover. Having everything laid out for you on the map to start makes exploration non-existent, so you always know where exactly you are going, which shortens subsequent plays. The only other real gripe I had was with the music design. The choice of music was a fantastic and mood-setting element that fit the environment and helped add to the world. However, there are issues with the overall design. Short songs will replay in the same area several times, which causes you to hear the same songs often. Approaching emblems will stop the main music from playing and play something different when activating the symbol. After lighting it up and walking away, the previous song that was playing turns back on. It feels like someone hits the pause button on the soundtracks when you get near the emblems and the play button when you walk away. For me, the soundtrack drives the environment and tone, and this stop and go with the somewhat short songs made the soundtrack, while fitting, feel poorly designed. I did enjoy this experience. It's relaxing, cute, and for the most part, stress-free. While the story wrap-up didn't have as strong of a drive as its initial opening, it's still got enough there to keep you interested. The overall game took me a little under two hours to beat. I ended up going through again to pick up a missed achievement. Hoa is an excellent game for a rainy day or a day you want to escape from stress. It may be short, but it's enjoyable. I'd say wait for a decent sale and grab it for one of those particular escapism-type days.  *nominated for 2021 Outstanding Visual Style𝕀𝕗 𝕐𝕠𝕦 𝔼𝕟𝕛𝕠𝕪 𝕋𝕙𝕚𝕤 𝕋𝕣𝕪

_childDocuments_.review: "Hoa" in Vietnamese means Flower, and just like the name suggests, Hoa is an absolutely beautiful game.Pros: - The visual is stunning. I love the Studio Ghibli inspired artworks and the multi-layered magical forest they created. Right when I watched the short opening, seeing our lovely hand-drawn fairy floating on a leaf-raft while adventurous melody played in the background, the tone was set immediately. It almost felt like ideal setting for an evening of peaceful, chilled-out gaming. And it did. - The soundtracks are amazing as well. - Gameplay-wise, Hoa is a puzzle-platformer similar to the like of Limbo or Little Nightmares, but with a much simpler set of mechanics and a mild, almost zen-like theme as it features no combat or major threat. To me, it's a pro because it fits with the setup theme. Cons: - The Vietnamese language pack needs adjustments, specifically wordings. For instance, while most names are common Vietnamese words, some names are left in English (Bouncy) or translated into pairs of Han-originated words (Linh Tự) that are hardly ever used and created inconsistencies.- I noticed some input lag here and there (e.g. sometime Hoa kept moving for 0.5 sec after input stop). They are rare so didn't hurt the experience, but worth mentioning.- I know it was never the selling point for this genre, but there are platformers that benefit greatly from having compelling story-telling elements. Seeing Hoa's outstanding world make me wish there were more of those elements here, like hidden lores, secrets or just...more interesting NPCs (NPC designs are great, but they just have very little to interact with).Overall, I really think this is one of those games we should play now and then, just to treat our eyes some candies and our tired brain a tropical cocktail of happiness.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is a pretty game for sure, with nice music. However, that's the only thing really going for it. The gameplay leaves much to be desired, and so does the story. The platforming is fairly boring, and the story really doesn't do anything except build on a premise that you really are given no reason to care about. I finished the game solely to see if there was any payoff. There wasn't. I wrote this review as a sort of catharsis.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I've played more than half of  and I think that is my cap for this game. It's absolutely not a bad game and is actually quite pleasant overall. But a couple things about it made me feel like my time was better spent elsewhere. Anyway, let's dive in.First, I want to talk about some positives. This game is, as mentioned above, quite pleasant. Actually, in a way, it completely radiates positivity. And it is definitely a child friendly platformer with a story best suited to children. The maps have a kind of Metroidvania inspiration, but they aren't vast enough for it to really qualify as such IMO. The backtracking is also fairly minimal overall. The artwork is super pleasing to the eye, and the most likely reason why people say this game is casual and relaxing. I mean, it is fairly casual, so I don't really disagree with that. I also think the puzzle designs are clever. They aren't particularly difficult, but clever? Yes. I especially enjoyed the big spiderweb one, and the kicking robots are kind of funny.Your basic goal in each area is to find five butterflies and however many glyphs are present. The glyphs unlock what I'm going to call area bosses, although realistically, you don't fight them. Instead, you give them your five butterflies and they teach you a new gameplay mechanic such as being able to move blocks, double jumping, turbo jumps, and so on. They will also universally act like they both recognize you (despite you having been shuttled out of the area while you were a child) and are glad you are now back. They will give you a musing about the situation that led to your family fleeing and will also tell you which area and boss to go to next.So, that's all good stuff. However, this game is not really relaxing as advertised by a fair few previous players. It can be relaxing at times, but there are too many instances where the nature of the controls and the control sensitivity mixed with what seems like invisible gaps on certain platforms, such as the edge of leaves for example, lend themselves to a bit of frustration. And that becomes especially noteworthy once you start having to combine ladybug platforming with swinging vines. The vines are already fickle enough with regards to when they register that you should actually be grabbing them. It becomes a bit tedious when combining that with the ladybugs. Additionally, the double jump doesn't always register once you've unlocked it. And that all leads to unnecessary do overs that become tedious. Will you overcome these things? Of course. The game is not really difficult at all. But I don't really enjoy the gameplay design fighting you along the way. Additionally, the story itself is not really engaging. Family is exiled. Child grows up and returns to reclaim 'x'. The people (or bugs and other things, as it were) who were left behind celebrate your return. Hooray!!! At some point, I just realized I was actually kind of bored and didn't really want to have to deal with the game's shortcomings any longer despite the game only being a couple hours long (like three at most). Part of that is my own relative lack of enjoyment when it comes to platformers I imagine, but the issues I outlined were the largest contributing factor. However, that doesn't mean this is actually a bad game. Like I say, it's definitely not. More like a meh game. And it's just not a game made for me, making ignoring its issues something I don't feel like doing.I got this game as part of the NSPCC Charity Bundle on Fanatical, and that was perfect in my estimation, as it allowed me to try it out without having any regrets from, say, having paid $14.99 for it. I definitely would not have appreciated that price point, and realistically, it's a bit steep for the amount and quality of content in general, in my opinion. But bundled....it is definitely worth a look then. I'm giving this a positive rating, although, had there been a neutral option, I would have selected that.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is a delightful, enchanting platform game with a gorgeous handpainted backdrop.It is a gentle, simple game which I note that many reviewers on other sites trashed because of its simplicity and nonviolence.  It would be a pity if these sort of games vanish because they're not grittily realistic.  I feel mankind would lose part of his soul, if we cease to delight in the mundane and the simple joys of life.  As both Plato and St Augustine said: The beautiful is the pure manifestation of the good.   I'll get off my soapbox now!Hoa means flower/blossom in Chinese and she does look like an inverted flower.  Hoa is a fairy who washes ashore with no memory of her past or who she is.  She restores the land as she trots along and we are propelled into the macro world of insects and other creatures....but it is never scary because the insects are so darn cute!The pace is peaceful and relaxing, however the platforming is quite precise.   There is a part where you swing on bluebells 3 times and if you miss, you go back to the beginning.  Experienced platform players got through this in 2 to 4 hours, but those who are very uncoordinated like me will take much longer!  I played with mouse and keyboard and my fingers got in a tangle having to hit so many keys at once!Each level introduces a new skill granted by a major character.  You are given the ability to push boxes, double jump, extra powerful bouncy jump and flying.  All of them will be necessary to complete the game with the aid of beetles who give an extra boost, ladybirds will form a bridge, larva will give you extra bounce, jellyfish and fish will act as bridges and the masochist robots will give you a kick in the butt!Each level also introduces a different natural environment including amongst the treetops, underwater, in a mechanical world and in caves (where I got lost!).  So the final level was a bit of a surprise as it was in black and white and more difficult and austere than previously.  This is accompanied by a sumptuously gorgeous soundtrack which is very evocative and uplifting with natural sounds like the tinkling of the bluebells as you swing on them.  Just delightful.At the heart of this game is a community being unified in making sure Hoa reaches her goal....and at the end, the true story of her past is enacted in a lengthy cutscene.  The ending is a bit ambiguous and open to interpretation.Hoa is game where you become like a child delighting in the magical world of nature.  Befriending the cute Rhinoceros beetle was a highlight.  As the game progresses, you become invested in Hoa's destination.  Highly recommend for all ages.  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dime in a dozen overly cutesy platformer that tried a bit too hard to tug at the heartstrings with no rhyme or reason. The end result is quite soulless and a bit emotionally manipulative, just stuffs looking cute for the sake of being cute. The music can also get grating after a while with just a few piano strings repeating itself.Game also has some inconsistent visual cues and parallax background items, some pieces look like they can be jumped onto due to shading/lighting but they're actually background. Level design is a bit nauseating to follow as everything looks the same and the game never make quite clear when you need to backtrack. It seems to want you to rely more on the map rather than the environment, and since moment to moment gameplay itself is nothing to write home about, the game went from being a chill and serene experience to something dull and unremarkable.

_childDocuments_.review: By the time I wrote this review, my feeling for this product is rather conflicting because on one hand, this is basically a VNese product and as a VNese, I appreciated what the developers try to accomplish with this game. However, and I know there would be a however, the product's quality does not justify the price that this product demands. Let's just get to the bottom of this:* Positives:- The graphic is gorgeous as hell, as this product is heavily inspired by Ghibli movies, especially My Neighbor Totoro- The Soundtrack is amazing, for the sheer value alone, the soundtrack is the MVP of this game as it carries the whole narrative and story.And... that's it, now to the hellscape that is:* Negatives:- The core design of this game is too simplistic to the point sometimes it's just non-existence. The main character is basically invincible as there is no actual threat in this game so that the whole game feels like a boring side walk, which leads to another issue- No gameplay situation to use all the skill set player acquired throughout the game. This issue alone can kill off the pacing of any AAA game, let alone a small indie game like HOA. Speaking of killing off the game...- Way too short + No replay value, literately. One thing that the developer should have done is giving players the ability to choose completed chapters to replay, but of course this didn't happen. On top of that, the game is only 2 hour long, which is not really a problem to me, but combining with what I mentioned earlier and people can sse just how waste of a opportunity this game is. Another thing that is wasted is...- Story (or at least what the game tried to tell you through the paper-thinned context) the message is clear - saving the environment, but it is poorly executed as hell. In the end, I don't really care about the story of the game- Bonus point: Metal town cutscene and the following chapter: Total bullshot, instead of giving player the control of MC to escape the robot, it is a cutscene. But wait, THERE'S MORE!!! The ending chapter design can be snashed into a wall to pieces, take those pieces and boil them to dust without loss of value because that level gave me diarrhea of level design and camera design.-> Critical score: 5/10, only buy this game on sale or when you are obsessed with Ghibli artstyle     Reviewer score: 6/10, has potential but wasted too much on the face value (Graphic, Soundtrack)

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game both by myself, and with my 5-year old child. The first five levels of Hoa are amazingly beautiful and peaceful. If it had been just that part of the game, I would have recommended this game unreservedly to those seeking an atmospheric easy game. The music, the artwork, the intuitive gameplay, all of it is on point. The levels are a bit puzzly, the controls get a bit more interesting with every level, and everything is just so pleasing and charming. Don't get me wrong, this game is not challenging at all for adult gamers, but as a relaxing casual game it hit just the spot for me and my daughter.However, from the water level onward I kept encountering problems. First, some foreground elements of that level wouldn´t load, no matter what I tried. Those elements are needed to make sense of where you are able to go and not go. In the end, I reinstalled the game, and that seems to have done the trick. I also did not enjoy the dark maze element of that level. It wasn´t fun, and I missed the beautiful graphics. The little snippets of dialogue seemed to become rather uninspired by then as well.In the factory level, the tone of the game suddenly shifted hard. No more relaxing natural charm, suddenly we were in a factory, offering some relatively bland gameplay, and ending with a fully automated chase scene. The level was boring to me, and scary for my daughter. The final dream level proved our undoing. My daughter found the black-and-white aesthetic too scary, so I finished that level on my own. I don't really mind that this level reused a lot of assets from previous levels. It was done in an interesting and thematic way. And switching around the world and the controls was a fun literal twist on what came before. However, those controls were extremely janky, meaning I had to restart certain bits a couple of times to get my little gnome to move at all. Then, when the final cut scenes started, I saw nothing but a white void. I could hear the music, but didn't see anything. From youtube I know that there was supposed to be a cinematic ending. The game did not respond at all anymore, and I had to shut the game down completely to get it to stop. When I tried to continue, I had to start over at the same point of the level where I had so much trouble with the controls. So I decided to leave it there for now, and maybe somewhere in the future I'll feel the motivation to give it another go.So I can recommend this game for players who want an easy beautiful game, and who are either happy with just those earlier levels, or who can deal with some jankiness later on.I can also recommend part of this game to parents wanting to play this with their (even very small) children. It's sweet, relatively easy, and so much fun to play together. However, do not go beyond the first six levels. Also, there is no happy ending. From youtube I now know that the cutscenes at the end of the final level show a dramatic flashback of how Hoa's home got destroyed by the robots, and how she was left all alone. That's it. No happy reunion with anyone after that.So not suitable at all for kids. And whereas adults are probably supposed to feel a vague hope that all will become well in the future, or maybe a sweet melancholy, I found it all rather bleak. Especially considering how the game presents itself up front and in the first levels. I don't know why game designers feel the need to do this. Either make a bleak game, or a happy one, no need to surprise players with a cheap gotcha halfway through the game.I admire the makers of this game for what they have created. The visuals, the music, the levels, all of it has been so lovingly crafted. And I really and honestly thank them for that. My daughter and I have had a lot of joy with this game, and will likely do so again and again in the future. However, I felt it necessary to let other players know that the latter part of the game is very different from the first levels. To me, the game is still very much worth the buy. But I would have appreciated this knowledge up front.

_childDocuments_.review: (Updated this review slightly after my second playthrough)Absolutely beautiful game. Gorgeous watercolour art, a phenomenal soundtrack, and one of the best underwater levels in any game. If you love Studio Ghibli movies (especially Castle in the Sky) or are a fan of games like GRIS and ABZÛ, you'll probably enjoy this too.That said, I do have one major criticism for an otherwise perfect game: the controls.There is no way to remap your controller/change key bindings in the options menu. This can make the final level EXTREMELY frustrating and challenging for some players. Towards the end of the game, there are parts you have to platform upside down and at an angle, essentially reversing with the controls and was VERY hard for me to get through (especially with a controller), which tainted an otherwise relaxing and soothing experience. The final level in general can be very disorientating for some players, since there is an entire section where you have to play with reversed controls in a darkened area. If you're a player that needs to customise their controls or has trouble with any of the above gameplay elements, think carefully if this is a game you want to purchase. Otherwise, this game is a fantastic showcase of Vietnamese talent and worth supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta be honest I thought this was going to be a game where you walk around the neighborhood giving people tickets for having the wrong type of tree in their yard or having a house number in the wrong font……Hoa is a very calm and chill game thats the complete opposite of an actual homeowners association though. Hoa is a game filled with childhood imagination.Bought the game based on its Studio Ghibli feel alone. Breathtakingly beautiful animation. It was very pretty, but also very very very easy. And very repetitive. And not particularly clever. But really pretty.The story felt like a collection of trope fairy tales and finishing the game left me wondering if there was more to it or if I’m just a bit slow on the head. Slow relaxing game, very shallow mechanics and almost zero progression. Classic platformer with no big surprises.Jumping, the main thing you do could be more tight. Imagine playing mario on ice level but you slide a little less. It suit the dream feel of the game but became irritating on tricky platforming parts ruining the zen of the game.The art is really the highlight of the game. Nothing truly special but it hold very well. On the negative side, some of the visuals do not complement the gameplay very well. Innacurate map, entrances and exits are sometimes unclear and elements from the background can look like valid platforms so you just fall through. Minor setback but still frustrating.The game diffculty is balanced and some would probably like it harder but it’s not exactly the point of the game. Sometimes, you just feel like chillin. It’s extremely relaxing, extremely beautiful, and sadly extremely short.  That said, I don’t regret buying it. I recommend it if, you are not tight on money or you can get it on sale. If you enjoy snack bite experiences and don't play for the challenge but mainly for getting some light escapism then this is the game for you.6/10 Because the grass in these levels look way too overgrown for the HOA to approve.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is a game where spectical and whismy take the forefront of the experience: and if those things don't matter to you, then it's probably not a game for you. It's not trying to be an interesting platformer in any sort of way. Sure, the mechanics here work and the controls are responsive enough, but many of the elements act as a minor challenge at best despite some puzzling have to be done. But that's not what the game is trying to really test: it's taking you on an adventure for you to get lost in the beautiful visuals, the environment that tells a story in each area, and the ultimately uplifting story that will make you feel your troubles melt away for that day.The detail in the drawings in both the fore and background is pretty impressive, giving layers and a sense of depth in the world that you end up paying a lot of attention to, not realizing that you're not even doing anything at that point. You get lost in the soundtrack that's both epic and mysterious, you get lost in the subtle sound design like bells playing out of a bell like plant. It's a game that emphasizes a world that you're trying to piece a story from, and there are certain levels (like the last one) that can really change your perspective and really leave an impact on you.Is it anything special gameplay wise? No. It doesn't want to complicate the experience with overly done mechanics, and I appreciate that. It's just a relaxing time that let's you calm down, and enjoy the view.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is a charming indie puzzle platformer by Skrollcat Studio that immerses players in a beautifully hand-painted world. You play as Hoa, a tiny fairy on a journey to reconnect with her homeland. The game features stunning visuals reminiscent of Studio Ghibli films and a soothing musical score. Gameplay focuses on gentle puzzles and platforming challenges. The controls are intuitive and forgiving; there's no health bar or fall damage, allowing players to focus on the exploration rather than combat. The gameplay primarily revolves around jumping and using abilities learned from friendly creatures encountered along the way. The narrative explores themes of growth and environmental awareness, enhanced by interactions with some whimsical creatures. Overall, Hoa is a short but sweet adventure that can be completed in about two to four hours. It's perfect for casual gamers or anyone looking for a relaxing gaming experience. With its enchanting visuals, calming soundtrack, and heartfelt story, Hoa stands out as a cozy gem in the indie gaming landscape.

_childDocuments_.review: both art and soundtrack are good but the game itself is short and disappointing, a little bit over 2 hours of gameplay and it already started feeling repetitive.story is uninteresting, the level design and platforming are lacking, i felt like i was playing a demo for a bigger game - nothing in this game has made me curious about the universe or the characters, it all feels very bland, cute but bland. The characters you meet throughout the game will tell you the backstory of your character and at the end you get to watch a cutscene that tells the same story, again. _childDocuments_.review: During the intro you watch a tiny little boat - made out of a leaf - reaching a shore during what could be described only as one of the Ghibliest days of all the Ghibli days possible. When the protagonist steps out the shore starts blooming.   About 25 seconds in and there already are at least two important points to note. First of all, the game looks, sounds and feels like a work of Hayao Miyazaki, Joe Hisaishi and Co. And while graphics or music are relatively easy to emulate ~ Well, no they aren't. We're talking studio Ghibli tier of superiority here, so no, that's not a simple undertaking to mimic those. Still, the Skrollcat Studio somehow managed. AND (and it's one of those splendid, impressive, all capital letters AND) this game does not look like it was Ghibli inspired. It could actually be put right next to the Miyazaki movies and stand its ground with that tiny, red leaf wizard thing of a protagonist holding his* head high. Slightly blushing probably though, he* is so cute.There had been another thing here I wished to mention, but while writing that first part I've actually forgotten what it was all about. Ah! Yes .. The game gives you achievements for basically everything. The point being, it's a short game. Two hours and some, maybe three. It's an extremely buggy game but in a good way. Bugs deserve more attention. Stag beetles and rhinoceroses (rhinoceri?), butterflies, caterpillars, bees and then more stag beetles. And they are all absolutely pleasant to look at, staring back with their huge, round eyes, tip-tapping while they follow, buzzing and fluttering as they fly by. HOA is definitely, 132% NOT Hollow Knight, no Sir or Madam, no way. The leaves and mushrooms, just like that shore from the intro, grow and bloom as the protagonist passes them by.The game is basically a tiny little Nausicaä meets Totoro. It's (mostly) green and (completely) safe and cozy. There are no fail states and the worst thing that can happen to the protagonist is being pushed a few steps back by, for example, a charging Frenzied Rhinoceros Beetle. But he looks so wonderful that you won't even be mad at him**.Hoa is a metrovania - lite. Meaning, it's a simple platformer involving some very basic exploration puzzles. Each location requires the protagonist to collect 5 butterflies in order to unlock a skill that allows progressing further. Each of those locations is extremely short, just four or five rooms in total, but it's also filled up with moments that make you smile and think something along the lines of "Oh, no. They didn't!" But yes, indeed, they did. I won't spoil anything since Hoa is short and you best discover everything on your own, but there are those little things that make you smile and feel that pleasant warmth somewhere inside. Pleasant, I've said, so no, not a heartburn, I’m looking at you, Death. You don’t even have a heart to burn so there’s that.Listen to me (metaphorically of course, since you basically can't. 'Read me' just does not sound as significant). This game made me feel more affection toward a box I used to jump onto a higher ledge, than I have for a reasonable 76% of humanity. Which, as I am well aware, may nowadays not be a bar set particularly high, but it was a %#^&&@ box. Every single one of them. In chapter three. Take as much time as you need to process this information.  There is a forge level that only lacks living soot balls. And there are those robots that actually look quite familiar as well. But above all else, despite the fact that every single character that the protagonist meets wishes him* well and supports him* on his* way towards this story’s conclusion, there is this sense of something melancholic lingering. There is a dark cloud behind the silver lining. There is basically a Ghibli movie: the Gamelite. Because. All in all, you can’t just appear out of the thin air and create a Miyazaki – tier masterpiece. It’s impossible according to the laws of physics, rules of reality and forces of narration. You can never get as serious as Lady Eboshi killing a god or as miraculously full of hope as Totoro growing the garden. But Skrollcat gets so damn near. Closer than Ni No Kunis if you ask me. And if you’re reading this far, you do. So, go ahead. Run with the stag beetles tonight (quite far, outside the suburbia). It will be a lovely, three hours short, little run.    And in the meantime, as always, try to have a great life. * I don't exactly know if the protagonist of Hoa is a "he" but the person behind the controller was, hence. Mileage may vary. ** I'm pretty sure this time around. Due to my observation of certain tell-tale measurements of the said beetle's physique, I am quite convinced he was a male.

_childDocuments_.review: GRAPHICS / AESTHETIC : 20/10 PLAYTIME (2-5 hours ): 4/10MUSIC : 20/10STORY: 6.5/10GAMEPLAY: 4/10PRICE: 10/10 (I know it might seem like a high price for a short game but you need to remember that this is an indie studio and I believe the price reflects the healthy payment the artists would receive for the time they spent pouring love and detail into every crevice)should you get this game? YES! I think everyone should experience a game of this beauty. But if you're someone who strictly wants to get a new game for the game elements, this might not be for you, if you like the aestheic and are okay playing something for the story and experience then definitely get this game!!THE THINGS I LOVED: Absolutely incredible visually i've never seen a game with this much incredible artistry and detail, even the smallest details in the back have so much life and character. the characters in the game and so loveable and amazing and the things you use to solve puzzles and excell through the levels are really unique and challenging at some points! The music is incredible if you like anything by studio ghibili you'll adore the art and music in this game, it reminded me most of howls moving castleThe things that I think could have been improved or built upon: Let me preface this bu saying that i LOVE this game and I highly recommend anyone play it!.... but there's just so much missed opportunity. I understand that the devs wrote this as a short story game but This could easily be a full length game with replay ability, adding simple combat would have added so much to the game, collectable items more levels ect. The way this game plays is that you arrive at an island, play through about 7-8 or so dungeons to unlock powers then you solve a final puzzle and the game essentially ends.  while unlocking powers you're vaguely told about your life before coming to the island and why you came back. At the end of the game before the credits you're shown a series of beautiful art showing what happened in detail. Honestly this threw me off a little bit, most of the game i found it hard to be motivated to continue through the levels, because beyond beauty i didn't feel much reason to finish the game. after seeing the credits I wonder if showing this scene at the start of the game would have been more beneficial to players, giving them a reason to want to continue the game. as when i approached the end i didn't understand why the game had really led to the point it did and even tho it was explained, it was hard to really savour that because the game had already ended. I think that if they started with this world building scene, allowed the character to unlock skills and then have a series of levels at the end and in between that involved some simple combat or collectable finding and even some more hints at things from the past, leading up to the final event in the game,then this would have been far more enjoyable as an actual game and also turning it from a 2-5 hr game to a 50 or so hour game. am i saying they had to do this for it to be worth buying? HELL NO! it's amazing as is! Im just saying they could have done more with it The things i hated:you can't edit keybindings, the given keybindings are very random and hard to remember, keybindings for powers could have been easily simplified also, i wondered alot whether some keys or powers were even necessary had it just been planned out better. I don't think this game runs well on a computer - I will be transparent and say that i use a recent laptop, but i'll also say that i can play games like the witcher 3 on here without issue. - Hoa crashed many times, and sometimes the game would auto save when my character was stuck in the sky or something and i'd open the game and couldn't do anything. There's also no windowed settings. The most epic part of the game it autoplays the character for you, I understand why they did this as they wanted a certain outcome and timing for things, but it could have easily been made into a playable part and I think that was a missed opportunity and made me sad realising I just had to sit back and watch the most exciting part of the game

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I am not a platform player and in general, jumping puzzles can be difficult for me. I have a low skill level and what I appreciated about Hoa is that I wasn't punished for it. When I would make a mistake, it wouldn't undo hours of progress or have to restart the level after a certain number of tries. There's no dying so I was able to relax in a positive environment that encouraged me to keep progressing. This is probably the first game where I 1) understood how double jump works and 2) felt a sense of accomplishment after trying, failing, and succeeding. Thank you to the developers for making a beautiful game that helped progress my own skill level in a tranquil environment and for methodically introducing new mechanics in a thoughtful manner. Hoa has replayability for myself, because of being closer to my own skill level and being a gentle, learning environment.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is....a game I have mixed feelings about. As you can tell from my playlog, it's not that long, and if it was just 30 minutes shorter, it would be short enough to get a refund. Not that this is always bad--Abzu is one of my favorites and it barely cracked 2 hours. So...the good, bad, and bittersweet...Good: AMAZING graphicsGreat musicPlatforming is simple in a way that works for the way it's supposed to beBad: The actual gameplay can be too simple beyond the platformingFelt like the story had no real punch to itSome iffy collision detection on objects you're supposed to interact withBittersweet: The last 2 chapters are much better than the first six, to the point where if the entire game was as good as those last two, it would be incredible. As it is, it's frustrating that it's not until the very end that things fire on all cylinders. I actually have no idea if I'd recommend this game or not, and I picked Yes because there were more things I liked than didn't. The best litmus test is to watch the trailer and see if the tone appeals to you or not. If so, yeah, you'll like it. If not, pass, because a lot of the game's appeal rides on its tone. Just understand that if you get it, it's not too long of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable characters, gorgeous visuals, and a decent plot. The story is a learn-as-you-go type of thing.If you're looking for a game that is aesthetically pleasing to the eyes and ears with little or no brain power required, this is the game. For the price, I find that you're paying mainly for the beautifully intricate visuals and soothing music, and the game aspect is an added bonus that bumps it up to its price, which I'm completely fine with since my main preference lies with game aesthetics. That being said, it's fair to say that it's not outrageously priced if you take that all into account.The only con I would mention but will acknowledge that's totally not the game's fault is that it's sort of glitchy and may crash towards the end, but I noticed that it's actually dependent on your PC specs or that the quality setting is on high but your device isn't sufficient to support the game since it gets a bit more fast-paced towards the end.All in all, I can see myself revisiting this game every so often because it's just too beautiful to leave it stashed away in my library. I look forward to seeing what new games the studios have in store for the future. I would like to add that I love that the name Hoa is extra meaningful to the character and game as it's also the Vietnamese translation for 'flower'.

_childDocuments_.review: When I firt started to play this game, it enamoured me with its beauty. A lover of Disney animation as a child, this title reminded me of classics like Lion King and 101 Dalmations, though with a crisp modern digital touch. The classical score also added to that atmosphere, weaving a story that had me wondering until the climax....and then just not caring anymore.The game is simple. You play as a fairy who floats to an island on a leaf, and as the story progresses you learn you were saved when "they" came. Your parents were kidnapped, but you wish to find the person responsible for your escape. You must find one-three sigils (the more the deeper in you get) while collecting five butterflies to give to the larger animals that helped with your evacuation. Each one (save for the last in the water level) give you basic moves like double jump, short flight, and ground pound.Honestly, I did enjoy my time for the most part. I used a controller and sometimes my character would not move (a real pain at the end of the game), or just keep moving when holding the analog stick in the opposite direction. Given how many times you're scaling tall areas, randomly walking off a leaf or ledge when you're not even pushing a direction can set you back a bit.However, the main reason I cannot recomend the game is with one simple question: Have you ever been so invested in a movie or tv series to have the ending be so bad it literally ruins the entire experience? Well, that was Hoa for me. After about two hours I finally got to the climax, only to have the final confrontation be an animated running scenario that anyone would have loved the opportunity to at least jump a la Sonic the Hedgehog or some kind of Sega CD FMV. Instead you just watch the ending play out, come to a conclusion that basically voids everyone's sacrifices to keep you safe, and end with a labyrinth of every stage you ran withreverse controls and camera ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that might make some sick, all for one last animation.Yes, the ending was that bad. While I outlined everything, I didn't spoil anything incase for some reason you wish to pay $14.99 ($12.74 at launch) for a title that takes two hours, and maybe one-and-a-half of it being enjoyable until the shoddy ending makes you regret buying it in the first place. And yes, I have pushing four hours in because I played again due to missing one achievement in the last stage. I knew what it was, but just completely forgot to do it.So if you enjoy a visually beautiful gamer with equally as enjoyable classical musical pieces you may be able to justiy the price for such a short game. Truthfully, if the ending didn't ruin the whole experience for me, I would have recommended it. Sadly, with no payoff to the time you put in, an ending that was so bad it ruins everything you did [yes, I got the point of what your deeds accomplish and purposely avoided it here due to spoilers], and a final section that feels tacked on for no reason other than to hit the two hour mark to avoid refunds? No, I cannot suggest this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa starts as a very basic platformer, but also dazzles right away with its amazingly cute graphics. The game is a visual (and audio) work of art. Just as I started playing it I had a feeling I should be doing it outside in a more natural environment.It starts out simple, and very slowly the game builds up the story and adds some mechanics - this game has one of the smoothest learning curves I've seen. Even if it's not the most challenging game for experienced platform gamers, it's shaped in a way that makes it perfect for new-to-the-genre players to pick up and get used to the tradicional mechanics. Also, it's perfect for kids, but still enjoyable for "any" aged players and animation fans.I can't really fault it anywhere... well... except when I got stuck on the furnace puzzle because of some weird bug and before that, in the underwater level, where I was unable to go into an area because the camera would not follow me. Still, those are minor issues that I believe should be fixed soon so, I can only recommend it to anyone willing to take a break from more action packed games and instead rest their eyes and ears - while still having fun - with this gorgeous game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game would be great for children, but otherwise will be rather bland and disappointing. Don't buy at full price.Hoa is a simple game. It's mechanics are restricted to wasd, as well as 3 simple mechanics you pick up within the first hour. The music would be rather pleasant, however the fact it does loop with little variation the whole 2 hours ish of playtime gets one sick of it too soon, as well as other audio cues will be harshly and jarringly swapped from left to right ear and vice versa, without much of a fade in or out. The music can cut out randomly, not returning until the next chapter is loaded, giving an eerie "Is this where the boss music kicks in?" but you are never in any danger in the game.The most climactic and the only potentially dangerous moment is stolen from you to be viewed as a cinematic, and runs for longer than I would've liked.The following chapter is disorienting and very little is newly introduced before its back to the same mechanics, the controls get flipped and the camera twists, which can induce headaches and the like.The story overall is okay. Its charming, the art style contributing heavily to the ghibli-esque theme, however it is both incredibly vague and bland until the game is complete and you get the final cutscene explaining things for you, even then I wouldn't say its anything special. This seems like a game that had a lot of promise, but fell quite a bit short in the end. A lot of time and money was obviously sunken into it, but overall I wouldn't say its worth the purchase, at least not at the full price (At the time this is roughly 15usd). Still, I've given it its full run in hopes things might get better, and I'm not the sort of person to request a refund if I've finished the game, even if it wasn't what was expected. I personally find the very positive overall review to be a bit misleading, and would at best give it a positive score.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.Minor non-story spoilers ahead.Hoa is a hand painted and linear puzzle-platforming game that tells the story of a faerie and her journey through different worlds. It has a few puzzles to solve but they are all easy, and even a young child can figure them out and the patforming parts aren’t very challenging, except for the final level.The game looks like it was made by Studio Ghibli itself: the characters and background are beautiful and very well drawn, and the animations and effects look great, even movie quality good. Unfortunately the game doesn’t scale to 4K, the native resolution seems to be far lower. The music sounds great and helps create a relaxing environment. The theme songs seem to be heavily inspired by , and overall the songs work very well with each of the different levels.As mentioned the gameplay, puzzles and platforming, are simple, but in each of the worlds you visit you gain a new ability that adds a bit of complexity to the gameplay, but still it’s simple abilities like being able to push objects and the double jump feature. In the final level, the difficulty increases sharply when SPOILER . This was the only level that required a few tries and where I spent more time.  18 Achievements. Around 2,5 hours, without any help. Easy, but gets slightly harder in the end. Easy, most are story related and can’t be missed.There are a few other easy ones that require completing certain tasks 10 times like SPOILER . Still, there is a chapter select option and you can go back and complete them later. Hoa is a very beautiful puzzle-platforming game, with easy gameplay and a simple story. The visuals alone make a memorable experience, the game Studio Ghibli never released, but since the game is a bit short, the price is still a bit high at the moment (I bought it for 5 EUR with store credit on Humble just a few weeks ago.)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little disappointed with this title to be quite honest.The game is perfectly fine for anyone genuinely interested in Hoa. I casually played along & I made a handful of mistakes along the way, so this isn't some perfect run time but rather an average session with all achievements completed to top it off. If Hoa had at a minimum 4 hours of game-play, I think they could justify the current price of £10 but for just under 2 hours... It's not worth it at the current full value. I am currently considering a refund for this title because I expected a lot more from it. 100% wait for a sale if you are planning to buy this title.(Not enough game-play to justify the price but what is there, is really cute.)

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this and what an absolutely beautiful game! Try not to expect some hard core platforming here. I really enjoyed the art and the music. It felt very much like a toned down Hollow Knight type game. I think where the game lacks in deep story telling and pacing issues it makes up for in it's attention to detail in the art and animation. It's simple, rewarding as most of the achievements are acquired as you play (don't forget to move the arms of the shackled robot 10 times...LOL!) relaxing and a grade A introduction to anyone looking to get into platformer games. It's short and sweet so don't go in expecting typical platformer excitement. I give Hoa an 8 out of 10 Definitely worth a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable game for what it is. I went into this expecting something beautiful and atmospheric, which means I got exactly what I expected, and just a little bit extra on top. The gameplay is not challenging, so if that's what you're looking for, this is not it. But if you're looking to relax completely, and if you like Ghibli movies (the music could be taken straight from one tbh), 2D animation, and have a few hours to spare, this could be a good pick. The story is simple and straight forward, falls a little flat due to storytelling at the very end, but I liked it. Would recommend warmly to anyone who's new to gaming, or just looking to relax!If you buy it, I highly recommend buying it with the soundtrack.I had some intermediate lag problems all throughout playing, but that might just be my computer being sick of me. Finished in 2.7 hours according to Steam (all achievements).Semi-spoilers:The story could be structured differently in my opinion, without much extra content added, and it would have a much bigger impact. Especially the ending. Adding in some creatures/characters to encounter during the walk through Land of the Spirits for example, and getting the cut scene in pieces, instead of in one go at the very end, would do a lot for the storytelling. And to be honest, I got frustrated during the inverted controls section, which impacted my feelings about the ending significantly. It could have been a feature earlier in the game as a challenge, instead of affecting the ending (which was supposed to be sentimental to some degree). I was also very diappointed to realize I had no control over the main character during the chase sequence.I fell in love with the world quickly, and I sorely missed more world building features, such as storytelling from creatures along the way. The world they have created is so visually stunning, I would have loved some more exploring and collectibles. I got all Steam achievements on my first playthough, so this, sadly, has little replay value for me.Can't wait to see what else this studio can do!

The two main cutscenes were also glitching out hard for me.Story and characters are pretty minimal.Get this on sale if you want to chill for a bit with some light platforming, Ghibli-inspired eye candy, and nice overall vibes.Solid 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem of a game. It's Journey mixed with Gris presented with the art, music, and charm of a Ghibli production. It's the little details that make this game super endearing. The ivy leaves that are platforms will give a little bounce when the player lands on them. The sound of flittering wings when you encounter a beetle just gives that extra sense of a living, breathing world. And, of course, there's the cuteness element. For example, when the player learns the double-jump skill, the little toon performs a twirl in the air. CUTE!The game is short but it is worth a replay just to be immersed in the art and music again. If you're like me, a person who sometimes want to play a casual low-stress game to unwind, definitely give Hoa a go. There is zero violence. There isn't fall damage either. Everything is wholesome. The developers put so much love, care, and attention into this work of art and it definitely shows. Please support the developers by purchasing this game and hope they make more games like Hoa!

_childDocuments_.review: Barely recommending.Hoa is a cute platformer that starts out as a tedious chore with delightful graphics and ends with two rather great levels.The game seems to be a bankrupt vision that has been resurrected or saved to be shipped.There's a cut chase level that has been repurposed into a cutscene. There are a few graphical elements that seem to be glorified placeholders. The game teaches both keyboard and controller regardless of which you are using. The voiceover text seems to have been cut. There are a few effects that play on top of the level (sparkles) or don't fit the art (robot sparklies in the last level). The achievement art is placeholders.My only true and non-nitpicky gripe is that the controller has input issues: sometimes movement can get stuck -- It seems that left-right side switch creates a tiny delay during which input is not received which in turn seems to break jumps from swinging.That said, the game delivers on atmosphere and price. For around 10€ the 4 hours and ending were worth it. Level design is rather good in teaching the game and whilst some of the levels suffer from time-sinking problems the overall sense of achievement is present.Miyazaki meets .. deadlines.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoa is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.  And that's one of the kickers here, this is a really badly done Nintendo Switch port. But first it has to be acknowledged that the visuals and sound design here are quite good.  While I normally find that games are unrecommendable due to lazy/bad visuals and sound design, here, that's not the case.  Unfortunately, and this is something that should have been completely avoidable, the console port sucks. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Hoa has the almost comically optimistic (if it wasn't so sad) price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Alien: Isolation", "Wolfenstein - The New Order" or "Metro Exodus".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.This is just far too highly priced for such a lazy console port.  PC gamers deserve better than lazy compromises from developers who think the Nintendo Switch is the pinnacle of gaming hardware. Unfortunately Steam reviewers aren't presented with a "Maybe" option... if they did, that's what I'd choose.  This isn't a completely bad game, but it's also not one of the best.  As always, if you read my review and you can overlook the negatives I've called out, or they just aren't important to you, then by all means go ahead and buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it ironic that this tree hugger propaganda is coded on and meant to be played on a computer. But seriously, these minimalistic, immersive visual short adventures are right up my alley. They are meant to give you something to think about and evoke some emotions. So I expected a lot from HOA, yet it just did not deliver. The controls are super simple, the puzzles are the equivalent of "there is a fork in the road, a star points left and a skull and bones points right. which eay would you go?" It just underprforms nad underdelivers. I ended up sympathising more with the robot that had some emotion instead of the protagonist fairy who we were supposed to like because...plot said so? Games like this need to be made wit ha lot of heart and should focus on storytelling. This one lacks the storytelling aspect, so it ends up feeling like something you would play in an afternoon with your 5 year old while waiting for mom to get home.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the graphics are beautiful it's not worth the price for less than an hour of game-play. I've played more in depth, longer platform games for free on sites like Jayisgames or Newgrounds. It looks like it wants to be some sprawling epic but it's just a short time killer. The soundtrack is way over the top and trying way too hard. The inability to change key bindings is inconvenient. Pressing K and L is unintuitive. Let me decide if I want to use WASD or arrows. Let me decide if I want to use space to jump (I don't). As for story...? Meh? There's a prologue as an epilogue that fills in all the details at the end. But it feels like an afterthought. Honestly, save your money or grab this when it's 90% off.Oh, and unskippable credits. At least have a montage of the beautiful artwork or something interesting to look at while we're waiting.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. Just WOW.That is but one word to sum this game up. The artwork, the music, the story is so cute and so pretty! As a "weeb" AND a lover of platformers - this title takes my breath away. It kinda reminds me of the art style that Studio Ghibli used, especially in movies such as "My Neighbour Totoro" and "Arriety". I actually uploaded screenshots, and added quotes form Totoro in top make it seem a little nostalgic for those who have not played the game yet, and it is still so fitting.Honestly, if you are a lover of platformers - and you enjoyed the beauty and serenity of Ori and the Blind Forest - BUY THIS GAME NOW. It will be money well spent - and your soul will be happy! It isn't as difficult and complicated as Hollow Knight, so this is a nice game to just relax to and take in the scenery and beauty.Honestly, I am in love and it is totally worth it. _childDocuments_.review: This game could've been so much more, yet it's a generic boring platformer, get x to unlock x. Not to mention the art that draw me in is not present in the game. Poster has nothing to do with the graphics which are awful. The game is not even challenging, the only challenging part is the awful controls. The developers do a great job helping you understand the story and then throwing in that ending really ties it together in a way that I did not expect to get so emotional over. The art is beautiful in a similar way to glibly, the music is calm and fantastic in setting the tone for whichever section you're in. Mechanics are smooth (though those blue bells slightly got on my nerves) and its a pretty easy platforming game overall. I will say its a pretty short game for 15$ but for the clear effort and quality that went into this? Definitely worth it imo. Don't tryhard the game because you'll finish it pretty soon anyways and enjoy the music and gameplay of this casual game.One last thing, if you are prone to vertigo this game might not be the best for you, or at least the last section might not be. _childDocuments_.review: This game is short, like my above 2.3 hour playtime single sitting was when I beat it short (I only glanced at a guide to make sure of whether there were missable achievements). Upside, it's a nice little platform puzzle game, very casual. Downside, controls got wonky a few times (most notably on those stupid flying ladybugs, also be aware there is a late segment that includes reversed controls and even a part where the camera slowly slants including all the way to upside-down while leaving your controls the same as you control your character who is now on the top of the screen among other things), and the ending credits do not let you escape easily (I alt-f4'd myself, although I almost sat it out for the music, debating on the soundtrack tbh I think I'll wishlist it and I almost never even do that much). Oh, and if you care about the achievements, one requires you let yourself get kicked by the robots 10 times (possible to get this by accident but also possible to miss), one requires that during the 2nd treetop section you try to jump onto the back of the red stag beetle you encounter after encountering a couple of blue stag beetles that you can ride (you cannot miss where this beetle is, don't worry it's not in some hidey-hole, and as you need to get past it for a butterfly it's possible to get this by accident anyways), and the last involves moving the arms in the factory 10 times (given that technically you only need to move them a grand total of 2 times, this makes this very missable). Other achievements are either progression-based or one for jumping on the bouncy caterpillars which is literally impossible to miss as you will definitely bounce far more than 10 times.NGL I got this cheap and am kinda glad I didn't pay full price...

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a peaceful, cozy game to play for a few hours. The art style, nature sound effects, THE MUSIC. What I read about the music in this game was my biggest motivator to wishlist and purchase, and it did not disappoint — I've already re-listened multiple times on Spotify since finishing the game. The story is told in bits and pieces as you go, and while I would have liked more to it, I still cared and found myself very emotional after the final montage as the credits rolled. It's been a LONG time since I've played a game whose puzzles revolved around game mechanics dexterity and navigating the environment successfully, so this was a great re-introduction to that kind of gaming. _childDocuments_.review: - Hoa's most distinguishing positive quality is the beauty of its artwork. Whether you're racing through a sunny flowered field, drifting among the ocean's depths with jellyfish, or winding through the smoking machinery of a clanging factory, you'll be delighted by the amount of detail poured into the watercolored backdrops. This is clearly a Ghibli-inspired game, and the Hoa pulls off the look very well- I was curious about the name, but apparently "Hoa" is an anglicized form of the Vietnamese word for "flowers". As you might expect if you've looked at the screenshots, they factor quite prominently into the game's visuals- I'm particularly pleased by the lack of an interface. There's no health bar, powerups, mission markers, or other sundries making your screen untidy. You get full, unadulterated, and unobscured views of the game's art at all times, which I really appreciated- This will likely sound reductive, but until I play a game like this that thwarts my expectations, I'll cling to believing this stereotype: You can look at any artsy platformer and immediately guess what it's soundtrack will be. Piano, strings and woodwinds. Mostly playful and light in the early going, perhaps even a waltz. Towards the middle, it becomes more mysterious and austere, probably implying the existance of a water or ice level. It then proceeds to a darker tone as the game hits its the culmination of its central conflict and the composer maybe throws a little synth in there or maybe even throws an effect on the piano or strings if they're feeling frisky. We then return to a variation of the game's opening theme- This isn't to imply that the music in this game is bad. It's not. I liked it! But there's so much opportunity for a composer to do something unique in a game like this that I feel like yet another game with an airy classical soundtrack that borrows too many notes from Vivaldi- The story for this one is a little strange. Not because the plot is weird or hard to understand, mind you. It's only because the entirety of the narrative is backstory explaining what happened to the main character as a baby with only a minimal connection to the events of the game.- The backstory, I've learned, is a bit inspired by Vietnamese folklore. Although the plot can be summarized in a sentence or two (an exercise I'll forgo to avoid spoilers), it's nice to get a small glimpse into another culture's mythology- Vibewise, this is as peaceful as a game can be. With all the pretty art, upbeat classical music, and complete void of difficulty or danger, you'll be up to your neck in the warm fuzzies. Well, most of the time. Hoa is not a frustration-free experience- Oh dear. Here's where things start to fall apart- Having played more puzzle platformers than anyone really ought to, I'm disappointed to report that the platforing controls in Hoa felt particularly grim- Normally, receiving a double jump in a game is a nice upgrade that allows you to access new areas and generally move around the world a little more easily. Unfortunately, Hoa features the most annoying implementation of this feature that has ever been committed to code. I don't know why, but changing direction while double jumping seems to work only 50% of the time you try to do it. If there's a window for it, I wasn't able to figure it out in the game's brief runtime. It felt unresponsive and iffy throughout the entire game- The jump wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the swinging vine segments. For reasons I don't completely understand, the physics for these require an inordinate amount of precision. You need to build just the right amount of momentum, jump at exactly the right moment, and grab the exact part of the next vine the game wants you to grab, or else you'll fall and have to start all over. You can't rely on your double-jump to save you on these either due to the iffy momentum; most times you try, you'll just sail off in the opposite direction like an idiot- The puzzles as a whole are barebones. Really, they're more like slight obstructions like getting a beetle to follow you so you can make a jump or working your way through a spiderweb maze. Your brain won't be taxed, but your patience might- Even when the game tries to mix up its formula in the last chapter, it falls flat on its face. The shift in artstyle, perspective, and controls is really cool and effective visually, but it just compounds the issues with the platforming. Those really frustrating vine jumps? Those sucked, so now try doing them upside-down and with reversed controls. The worst part of my experience was that after struggling through the artificially-inflated difficulty of this section and making it to the final cutscene, the game just ♥♥♥♥ itself and crashed. And where was my autosave? That's right. At the very beginning of the section- The duality of this game is hard to square. On one hand, it's beautiful and calming in its best moments, but a complete mess at its worst. The awkward jumping physics and the presence of game-crashing bugs really put a damper on what could have been a much better experience- I'm unsure if my crash had to do with the fact that I was playing on the Steam Deck, but that little green "verified" checkmark made me feel confident that I wouldn't run into any major problems. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case. Just like my dad used to say, I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed. It's worth trying for the art if you really like what you see in the screenshots, but maybe temper your expectations of the gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: One of my first reviews, thought I'd start with this game since its a rather under the radar indie that I feel I enjoyed a lot more than I thought I would, so I want to talk about it a bit.This game is a great, relaxing, simple but fun experience. The atmosphere is undoubtedly the best part about this game, as it does a great job at making the otherwise relatively simple gameplay enjoyable. The mechanics of the gameplay are not new or innovative, mainly doing the standard song and dance for platformers, but the beautiful art and the captivating music really make it worthwhile, and honestly this game held my attention better than some Triple A games in my library (not hard but I thought it would be worth mentioning). A small detail that I noticed is how some simple mechanics are changed slightly in order to better fit the atmosphere. A good example of this is the start of the game, where you have to move platforms, and instead of pushing or pulling it, it is a beetle that will simply follow you wherever you guide it. Again, it is a small detail, but one that I greatly appreciate.On the topic of criticisms, I find it quite hard to mention them without compromising the tone of the review. The actual jumping is rough around the sides, the story is generic, and like 2 parts of the game were more frustrating then I thought they needed to be, but I don't feel like any of these compromise the games quality. There are 2 major criticisms I did want to bring up thought, and that I don't feel can be swept under the rug. The first being this game's inability to change keybinds. I had decided to take a break playing this game for about 2 weeks, and I did so right after I had learned to fly. Naturally, I had forgotten how to fly when I got back. Because the game didn't allow me to change keybinds, or even go over the skills I had learned, I had to spend a roughly 2 hour period looking up details about the controls of this game (which was made even worse by the fact most people play this on controller!). My other big criticism of this game is the dialogue, which is incredibly poorly written, and that detracts from the story pretty much anywhere it pops up.However, despite my criticisms, I do not want to seem as if I hated this game. It was very fun for what it was, surprisingly so, like I said at the start. Playing this game made me feel like a kid again, and made me nostalgic even though I had never played this game before. And it warms my heart to know that even though I've played countless games, many of which are far more mechanically advanced than this one, that I can still be impressed and thoroughly enjoy a under the radar indie like this. And while I don't think the game is a must buy, I do think it was worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has watched some ghibli movies, I got really intrigued by the design and style of this game that resembled the aforementioned part of visual entertainment. This game provides a short yet beautiful story in a setting that is equally if not more beautiful than the plot itself. The gameplay is nothing hard to get a hand of and with its simplicity will provide a relaxing adventure that will perhaps make you tear up. This canapé is definitely worth the money and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short "peaceful, relaxing" indie 2D platformer with visuals that nicely combine hand-drawn 2D backgrounds with cel-shaded 3D models. Unfortunately, the level design isn't particularly interesting, and the platforming and general control feel awfully clunky, which becomes a bigger and bigger problem as timing-based elements take greater precedence further in; this isn't exactly Celeste, to be sure, but it's frustrating in ways I can't imagine the developers intended, and is more than enough to keep me from finishing this one. try it on deep discount, maybe

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty short game. Finished it in 2 hours, but for real, the soundtrack and design really giving me Studio Ghibli vibes, and i love it. I can't get enough of the soundtrack, that is AMAZING. Story wise there some things they don't give you much lore, but they give you the basis of what happened and its really nice. _childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ok. In general, I'm a little torn on if this is suppose to be a recommend or not, but my experience playing this on the SteamDeck was not great.In terms of gameplay, the game is slow-paced, linear, and presents no challenge. While these qualities aren't inherently problematic, I did not feel like the gameplay or exploration was particularly rewarding or ambitious. The movement was not as smooth as I would've liked. It's apparent that the intention is for the artwork and music to carry the game. Having played this on the SteamDeck, there are significant bugs with the cutscenes and music. A couple of the cutscenes had stuttering issues, forcing me to close out of the game. I also had issues with the music sometimes randomly becoming blown out.
_childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful animation, relaxing background sounds. That's where the good sides end.Sometimes the game was too difficult for me. Once I left the game waiting for a better moment for so long that when I came back I realized I couldn't remember all the controls anymore. There were no instructions in the game or on the internet, so I had to start from the beginning.The music is sometimes too reminiscent of certain works by Joe Hisaishi.The ending is too open for a game that explains things in detail along the way. Suddenly, the player has to figure out for himself what the ending really means. I don't like open endings, they're frustrating. Especially when you have to work a lot for them. All in all, a nice experience, but I wouldn't play again.P.S.  After the harmony of nature you suddenly end up in some urban factory with robots, rust, oil, flashing lights, etc. It's like playing something completely different. If I had known about such a twist, I would not have bought the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: This Studio Ghibli-inspired cozy platformer is adorable, beautiful and nicely emotional. There's not much to say about it, as it's extremely simple, and incredibly short, even by the standards of a tiny indie platformer like this. I can say however that if you're looking for a quick shot of feel-good energy, Hoa definitely delivers. I'm excited to see what comes next from its promising developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute platforming game, beautiful scenery and relaxing music. Many have said it gives a sort of studio Ghibli feel, and I would agree. The story is very basic, so do not expect much detail, although it was enjoyable. The main focus is definitely the music, scenery, and platforming. Highly recommend, and it only takes about 2.5 hours to beat it if you have any platforming experience (so consider getting it on sale if you cannot justify spending the full price for 2.5 hours of game-play). A controller may be more suited, but I played on keyboard.As a spoiler free warning, the last level can be difficult and disorienting (potentially even nauseating). Do not let it stop you from giving the game a go though, unless you are very sensitive to disorientation in games. It is manageable with a little extra focus and you will get used to it. And as a side note, you cannot use a mouse at all when using a keyboard, not even for menu select. There is no controls page, so you have to remember if you take a break from the game. For keyboard, classic A and D movement, SPACE for jump, M for map, K for flight, and S for a ground-pound. L is object interaction.
_childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: - This is a relatively short story about the last fairy of a kind and its journey to uncover a catastrophe of the past.- Visuals are stunning and music is outstanding. Controls feel more than good enough for this type of game, and mechanics, albeit needless, offer some degree of variation to the gameplay, which is always nice.· Most people I've seen talking about Hoa mention "Studio Ghibli vibes", and I can clearly see where that's coming from. Beautiful aesthetic.- There are 2 trophies which consist of repeating certain actions 10 times. In my opinion, these are completely out of place in such a game.· I forgot to do one of those 2 and was dreading I would have to do a rerun to 100% it for such an absurd trophy. THANK GOD THE GAME HAS A CHAPTER SELECTION.- Nothing outstandingly bad in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: Very short and relaxing 2D platformer. Nothing new but beautiful in art style, music, story. No combat, just easy puzzles and jumping/pushing/double-jumping/floating and evading some not too scary enemies.I found the last section with inverted controls and rotating camera rather annoying, but the rest was great. Very short, took me less than 3 hours to finish. That's fine, it did not overstay its welcome. I am looking forward to their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hoa

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game to start the new year with.  Great music and art.  This could totally be a Studio Ghibli film!  It's a fun short relaxing game.  The only thing that I didn't really enjoy was near the end, as it was hard to relearn some of the controls.  I understand why they did it though.  I hope they make a Hoa 2.
