_childDocuments_.review: So, lets get this down, I love this game, if nothing else for the fact that if for the last 10 years you asked me "what is the game you would like to play" I would say this. It has it's problems but not nearly enough to lower my enjoyment of this.So I would just like to thank the Developers for this game before I go further into this.The simple fact that you made this in RPG Maker VX Ace is incredible to me, if it wasn't for the small peaces of artwork from the RTP you kept, I would have never noticed.Good Points:> Fire Emblem mixed with Ogre Battle combat, to me the ideal combat system.> Good Army customisation options, with multiple classes, traits and artefacts that really affect your units.> Good Difficulty options, I tried Warlord but honestly it was too hard for me in a first play-through but so I bumped it down and restarted but overall Commander felt very good.> Great pixel art (I have a very weak spot for pixel art in this style)> Good Main story, nor perfect, but good I enjoyed itI cant say there is anything I would really call bad in this game but some stuff could really use some improvements, in this or the sequel. See these more as suggestions that mention some of the points I found a bit lacking. In no way are these dependant of my current enjoyment of the game.To Improve Points:> Linear story- There isn't much of a branching narrative from what I could tell. Except for a decision at the very end of the game it mostly plays out very linearly, there are only very few side-missions after mid-game, 5 I believe, that do give you some context about what is happening and have reward like a new minor character or power.> Not saying that the game NEEDS a branching story or a lot of side content, but I would like there to be more.- More Interactions between characters> At the end of the game I had about 40ish total conversations in my archives, they were all for the most part a good read and I found them interesting, but that means of the cast of 14 characters some only talked once, and a few never spoke to each other- UX> Although I use a controller and the problems mentioned by most people using mouse and keyboard dont really affect me, the main thing that did was the ways menus and list were laid out requiring me to go trough a lot of menus to. Or how when adding a unit to the squad there is no visual indication if you can add them or not due to CP costs. I'm by no standards a UI expert but it feels to me like it needs some work.> The combat has no indication of the possible outcome, this isn't a complete need in most cases but I really felt like I needed this in Warlord playing with Permadeath, you eventually get a feeling to how each squad is going to react in a fight, causalities, who will die to what etc, but that's something you can't really afford and don't know how would this be implemented in all do honestyLastly, Incredible Minor Nitpicks:- Some characters have Generic Class Sprites> I know why this is done, these characters can change classes unlike the custom sprite ones, but seeing my boy Jules as a lowly archer all the time made me a bit sad. (I started working on a little custom sprite for him, he killed the final boss, he deserves it)- Correction: Ranger tiny sprites look too similar to Skirmisher sprites> Just that, so much so I thought there were no ranger sprites in this game, I had to change the review.Overall Amazing Game, I cant wait for SoW 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking at this page, you've probably heard that this game is like Fire Emblem and Ogre Battle combined. It is, in a way. But it also improves on and modernizes those formulas. Unfun mechanics from those games, like sitting units next to each other to grind affinity in Fire Emblems, and the alignments and chaos frame from Ogre Battle are consciously done away with.But once again, that doesn't seem to do justice to this game. Symphony of War is also a very clean game that just shows quality and attention to detail in everything it does. It is difficult to quantify or describe exactly how, but one this game's best qualities is that its tuning is very tight. I've often been surprised by this game's ability to give you missions that feel hard, but fair at every stage of the campaign. Even if you find yourself in a powerful position for where you are in the campaign due to lucky rolls or good strategy, the game provides you with optional objectives, from finishing before certain turn limits for increased rewards to forcing enemies to surrender rather than killing them outright for you to be able to challenge yourself. Furthermore, the army management part of the game provides a lot of interesting options at every turn. You choose whether to settle for mediocre new units or keep paying gold to roll for new ones. You choose among a large number of classes to promote your units into that all have their own unique purposes. You choose which artifacts to buy that can greatly change the performance of your squads.All in all, 10/10, would buy again.No, seriously.Give me a sequel, Dancing Dragon!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic Fire Emblem style game with plenty of its own ideas. So good I played through twice!Gameplay: If you have played Fire Emblem or Final Fantasy Tactics, you will be right at home with the grid based strategy map structure of the game. What really makes Symphony of War stand out is the squad system. Instead of just controlling 10 or so individual characters, you control a bunch of different squads consisting of multiple units. The game opens up quickly and allows the player to experiment with different squad compositions to fit their own playstyle. Want a tanky squad that never dies? Slap some sentinels on the front line and put a few healers behind them! Want to erase enemies from the face of the planet before they can counterattack? Put a bunch of mages or siege cannons in a squad! How about a mounted squad that can weaken an enemy and retreat to safety? You can do that too!Over my two playthroughs, I experimented with tons of different squad compositions and had tons of fun refining and tweaking them over the course of the game.I would suggest avoiding the permanent death option, though. My first playthrough was on the normal difficulty setting with permanent death on for the entire playthrough, and it really felt like the game wasn't balanced around it. It felt less like the old Fire Emblem games which were balanced around losing units forever and more like a Pokemon Nuzlocke challenge. Possible, but not the intended way to experience the game.Story: The story is pretty typical for this genre of game. There isn't anything you haven't seen before, but some moments are done really well. The story felt a bit rushed in the final few chapters, but it was never actively bad or a drag to read.DLC:The game has paid DLC as well. My first playthrough was done without the DLC, and it was excellent. With the DLC you will get eight new chapters and a handful of new classes to experiment with. The new maps flesh out the stories of some of the side characters and provide access to some of the new classes and artifacts. While not required to enjoy the gameplay or the story, some of the new classes are really fun to play around with, especially the necromancer and risen classes. If you aren't on a budget, I would recommend picking up the DLC as well.Overall a fantastic game, and I can't wait to see what the sequel has to offer!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd really like to recommend this game and, for casual players, you will probably truly enjoy this. The game mechanics are great. If you have experience with strategy games, and play on above normal difficulty levels, you will not be challenged here, even on the highest, Warlord, difficulty level. Even without save scumming, I've just breezed through the missions up to 10, typically losing no units at all... only on occasion did I even have one casualty.I'm really hoping for an actual challenging difficulty level. If they do this, then I'll be very pleased with this game. Until then, I can't recommend this except to casual players.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most underrated and underhyped game I've played. It is very obvious that the developers has put in significant time, effort and love in making the gameplay very enjoyable. - If you love Fire Emblem you're gonna enjoy this game. Imagine Fire Emblem but with much in depth game mechanics and RPG style customization. - Cheap price. It's a steal if it's on sales, which happens quite often.- Decent graphic and animation with nostalgic feels.- Decent BGM and SFX. Voice-over is repetitive and cringey at times but fortunately you can easily turn it off.- Easy to learn. In game tutorial/glossary is comprehensive enough so long you have the patience to read them- Controller compatibility. There is even a built in speed up button. Very much like playing Fire Emblem on emulator.- Huge variety of classes and items which promotes customization and creative builds- Despite a lot of people complaining that the menu sucks and lack QOL, I love it very much. Simplicity, less is more. Perhaps kids nowadays have things too easy for them. - DLC is a must get. It adds significant contents such as new side quests, new class, new items, new traits etc.  - Each playthrough takes around 30-40 hours+ which is quite long and definitely value for money. - Replayability. There's 100 states if you wish to replay it over and over.- NG+ (DLC) offers significant customization which allows player to pick the best option for their playstyle and expectation. It's like a mini built in modding tool.- Small cannons, field cannons,  - Similar to Fire Emblem (or most strategy games), AI are pretty dumb. Suggest to add more surprise element such as fog, enemies pegging from behind, or simply bullsh-t mechanics just to f-ck with the player. I am a masochist I know. - Almost all the victory condition is to defeat everything or capture something. Would be great if there are more variety to this.- Some units are way too overpowered.  - Some units are way too underpowered.  - Quality of life. I'm sure people are already asking for filter function as well as other better ways to navigate the menu.- LB/RB on controller should rotate between squads instead of acting like left and right button. Also that start and select button are useless and should be used for other QOL purposes. - There should also be a deploy all option. Would be better if players can choose whether cavalry goes in the front or back.- Add character portrait on battle map. Also, all story characters should have unique sprite/class. - Base game and DLC are a must get on sales. Soundtrack and guide are optional and get those only if you want to support the developers.- Like all strategy games, enemies are either dumb AI or it's artificial difficulty in your face. But it doesn't really matter. What matter most is that I had tons of fun with Symphony of Wars.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mash up of Fire Emblem and Tactics Ogre.Lots of customization in how you handle your army, can go all in on dedicated units of heavy infantry or light cavalry, or you can make an army that's made up entirely of mixed unit type squads. The use of a leadership stat to limit how many soldiers can fit in a squad works pretty will, it keeps you from steam rolling the enemy by putting everything good you got into one full size squad and shows how you're progressing over the course of the game, getting to fit another guy into a squad makes a big difference. Theres traits you can slap on individual soldiers and items that you can attach to squads that really lets you get into the fine detail of how you want a squad to work. The battles themselves are pretty great to watch, the art, sound, and animations make it punchy, unless an attack is deflected you can hear the impact. You can see how the game handles different unit types and their speeds in combat by when they attack, which helps you learn how it all works.Story is mostly what you'd expect for something like this, with a couple of interesting twists, but beyond that nothing that blew my socks off. There's also a relationship system where characters can have conversations between missions and you can learn a little bit about them and the world that they live in.The game is pretty good, there's only a few things that hold it back. Some of the unit traits you can give dudes seem pretty pointless, like "No movement or combat penalties in desert/snow" sounds pretty good until you realize that only covers like three or four missions and you'd be better served with something else. The whole relationship thing can get that same problem that Fire Emblem has, where two nerds hang out like twice and go "Hey, I love you now", or how one voiced character is barely fleshed out and only has one conversation with another, more developed character. Generally that part of it feels a little half baked, it might be fine if you're not looking for more interesting interpersonal relationships in the plot. Also parts of the game are very "HELLO, THIS WAS MADE IN RPG MAKER". Nothing that keeps the game from not being fun, just stuff to be aware of.Overall, I'd give this 8 squads surrendering in terror because their morale is at "Shattered" out of 10, if you like strategy and tactical stuff maybe check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: A very thorough indie game. Well balanced enough that you can most likely clear it without grinding, but the option is always there for those who want it. In this game you have actual battles, which play out like Fire Emblem, but with squads, however I spent almost as much, if not more time, in the army organisation menu trying to balance out all of my squads to get the most bang for my buck. They've done a great job of making it hard to perfectly balance between adding units to a squad and kitting it out with gear. Quality of Story and balance actually are slightly inverse. The story begins very lukewarm to the point of wanting to skip dialogue and the battle difficulty and balance is challenging but good. That gradually inverts as the story warms up and (if you've done arenas especially) your own army's power outstrips the opponent's which makes balance worse and is less fun (so best not to grind much). Overall a very good indie game that doesn't cut corners.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say enough on how good, no... fun, wait... just surprisingly enjoyable this game is. I'm not a review-writer but I like to make exceptions in special cases (either very good or very bad). And this game is VERY good. Symphony of War: TNS hits that very difficult spot to hit where the player feels empowered but not coddled, challenged but not oppressed, and free but not aimless. It's just an enjoyable experience. I'll admit... I bought SoW:TNS once before, played about 2 minutes and said, "This is not for me." and promptly refunded it. As I continued to see the spectacular reviews pop up I decided to give it another chance and, as they say, I'm glad I did.If you're considering this game then you likely know the concept... Build an army, engage in warfare on a top-down map where battles take place in small cut-scenes, and defeat the bad guy by achieving the victory conditions. The game advances over a couple dozen and a half set story missions each one preceded by an "organization and planning" stage. Sounds straightforward right? Well it is, mostly. But take all this and add in the ridiculous number of different unit types and silly number of squad unit combinations, and THAT is what sets the game apart from it's ilk. I can honestly say that I'm not certain whether I enjoyed the battles or the planning stage more. There 's just so much fun to be had in designing your squads and planning your army that Symphony of War is almost in a class of it's own in this respect. The game goes even further in customization with an army skill tree and unit equipment/upgrades. At one point it almost becomes too daunting, but it doesn't take long before the player is creating and experimenting with relative comfort. I'd also like to add that this game does not fall in to the common trap of missions becoming a puzzle game... where specific moves are needed at specific places at specific times. Almost all missions are winnable using various strategies.I do have a few gripes with the game. The battle sprite artwork is fantastic, but I thought the character portraits were amateurish and also didn't blend well with the rest of the retro style. There are no hover-over tool-tips for attributes and skills (At least not in the build I played) so be prepared to reference the interwebs or in-game resources for help. I'd like to see a more diverse skill tree because by the end I had unlocked every skill available. And finally, I will recommend that if you  are a veteran of these types of games to crank up the difficulty a notch, because normal can be a tad on the easy side. But don't be fooled! SoW isn't perfect but it's faults do nothing to detract from the enjoyable experience.I highly recommend this game if you like this style of tactical strategy game. I'm hoping this is the first in a series of Symphony of Wars because this game is FIIIIIIRE... :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you like tactical role-playing games, like Langrisser, Final Fantasy tactics, or Fire Emblem, then you'll most definitely enjoy this game. It's very story driven, the lore is easy to reference if you're lost, the characters grow on you, and it does have a relationship/bonded feature (not quite like Fire Emblem as I have yet to see bonded statuses mentioned after they've established and there is no dialogue options). There's a good few challenges and multiple ways to handle each stage and each unit. That and having restarted stages, it's nice to see that not every unit against unit outcome is the same. Additionally, it's nice to see strategy play out during a fight (watching the fights helps you determine if your medic, mage, etc. are in good spots where they won't insta-KO). The plot in and of itself is really good thus far. I'm to chapter 20 after trying at S-ranking all or most missions, and so far each twist and turn of the plot has had me cheering, frustrated, and sad for both the characters and the land that SoW focuses on. The only con that I have is that when you are in a stage with a bunch of enemies, you have to wait till their "AI" makes a move. Every single enemy. Despite this (as it's a minor con), I look forward to finishing it and replying it to grab those missions that I couldn't S-rank. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Scratches that itch for the old school Disciples 2 formation based tactics, while also delivering a very easy to learn and understand tactical map view very similar to Fire Emblem. The game works, I didn't really experience very many bugs, or any that I can recall, it took me a little bit to learn some of the ins and outs, like how to increase leadership, and I still don't know how to ambush properly, but that's okay. The story is the story, I liked it enough to keep going, I don't like Abigail's voice though, it bothered me the entire game. It feels... very forced, almost insultingly. And that second form for Diana... A little cringe my friends. The tactics gameplay is amazing, I learned a lot from watching the opponent decimate some of my forces, and it always feels really good to wipe out a regiment of musket bearing units before they have a chance to blow me away. I loved how absolutely broken artillery is though, if I could figure out a good way to make that a light cav unit without feeling like I wasted 5 horses on the deal, I would have. Barnabus was my favorite squad, heavy cav was the best, saved me time and time again. I would have preferred there to be no choice in gender if the final scene was going to disregard it and the ending show the female one anyway though. Overall, Really good game, 4.5/5, I'll probably come back and replay the story and try to get all the achievements. See if the beginning choices make any difference. Buy it if you liked Fire emblem, or the old Disciples 2 games, its a blast. If you don't, buy it anyway, the gameplay is really excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: okay , so i've obviously played this to the end , so in truth the game is not garbage per se. Let;s see....ill talk about gameplay , art , and story. I'll start with gameplay first , since i'm assuming most people care about this most.1. The gameplay itself is alright.1.a  Combat It;s not that hard honeslty , with the most glaring issue being balance. Unit balance is ....terrible. I was expecting some rock/paper/scissors , but in truth there are some units that are simply better then others in all aspects. 1.b  Another issue in terms of gameplay that i've seen is imo the tech tree. U can easily obtain every upgrade in the game like....60ish % in the game , which imo is not that satisfying since it just means there is no meaningful choice that will alter your gameplay in any way......tho , to be completly fair , its almost pointless whatever you pick one or another since for the most part ....they won't radically change your gaming experience , which is sad because it takes away from your agency as a player to make meaningful alterations to your army. Jut make the upgrades better , and increase the cost so your players can't power farm all of them.1.c All the main missions and sidequests also have almost no party restrictions - there are actually squad limits , but i am talking about npc limitations - meaning u can almost always just use your strongest 2-3 squads to mow everything down. Imo , having different missions in different regions involve different npcs and therefore armies will force players to use  different strategies , while also introduing an element of challenge to gameplay. It would also increase imersion a bit....since it makes more sense to have different commanders taking care of different theaters of wars.1.d That being said , i've found the bonds and player choices (which aren't many mind you) to be largely meaningless. Bonds give some morale bonus , and....honestly.....after finishing the game....i still have no clue whatsoever what morale does for your own armies. I know that low morale on the enemy teams give you the option to make the enemies surrender (which leads to more gold since u can ransom them) , but i haave no ideea whatsoever what low or high morale does for your own squad. There might be an explanation in the game's encyclopedia , but i couldn't care less , since it  never affected my gameplay.1.e The AI is incredibly stupid. Like....very much so. I've had maps in which ive killed half the enemy;s forces by putting my best team in the middle of the map and letting the enemy attack me. For all intents and purposes that should be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful tactical decision....but in this game....the enemy will just leeeroy jenkins into you for the most part.There are some other flaws to the game  (like the battles being incredibly boring and stat checky. The only actually interesting fight being the very last , and at that point your armies are so strong that you can legitimatly finish it in one turn before u can even see some of its mechanics at play.  All in all , gameplay is serviceable if the devs decide to improve the ai and unit balance for the most part.2. ART - the art is .....so and so. The chibis are cute if you like that style , but the actual character portraits are pretty rough. It;s serviceable  , but it could be a lot better honestly. The change from the cute chibis to the portraits in the conversation is pretty noticeable tho , and it always breaks immersion for me and just makes me think that it would have been much better if either the portraits just followed the general aesthetic of the game (and just use cute chibis) or just straight up be of higher quality.3. STORY - this is the main offender for me. More then gameplay ....i care for a good story , and the game lacks .....masively in this department. It has some good idees (cliche for the most part , but hey...some elements can work even if cliche) , but sadly the devs have a hard time writting a cohesive storyline ...with some "plot twists" being painfully obvious while others being straight up ass pulls without any setting whatsoever.It also feels like it starts to drag a bit too long in the last couple chapters...and the ending slides also leave a lot to be desired. For example , right at the end of the game your character has to make a decision.....which is never fully explained not before ...and not after with an ending slide. I legit have no ideea what my character did or what happened with him after he took said decision because there is no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending slide that explains that decision.Now....i know this dragged on a bit....but i really felt the need to explain why i gave this a NO , so people don't just call me a blind hater.  While i went pretty hard on the game , the fact is that it still kept me playing it to the end , so as i said ...its not completly garbage. It has some good elements, and some of the bad ones can be patched out (the stupid AI and unit balance for example) ,  but the lackluster story , terribly written character conversations (seriously , at some point in the story ....1 character will simply talk about how women like badboys more then good guys. how cringe is that ?) ,  and mediocre art kinda kept breaking the immersion for me over and over.Overall , my score for this game is probably a 6.5-7 at best. Would i recomand others to play this game ? Sure....it can be relatively enjoyable if u like strategy games (especially if the devs do take the time to patch it in the future).Would i recomand u buy it at full price? No. In it's curent state , i don't think the game is worth the price tag attached to it.  Maybe buy it if you're really into this style of game or if it's on reduction....otherwise no.Hope this helps , and sorry for the wall of text.

_childDocuments_.review: Symphony of war is an immersive 100 experience! It really makes you feel like you are in a symphony of war.Tactical strategy -> definitely can get your brain juices pumping.Story -> acceptableCharacter dating sim -> well, not really here for it, but it was there I guess...But the real reason I was hooked on this game was the direct and straight forward preemptive strategy component of the game, or the REAL game as I thought of it. That being SQUAD COMPOSITION. This was where I spent most of my time in the game. I had a great time playing Warlord difficulty and making a 3 sentinel squad with artifacts that granted extra ranged damage reduction and the everlasting potion (free healing). This led to what felt like an innovation in war being the decoy squad which could usually be used to hide squads that would have died if they were attacked by the enemy units but instead the decoy squad would take the blow and leave the battle with but a scratch. For this reason, I really liked this game.Some actual critiques of the game were that I didn't exactly know how damage worked and I didn't know if damage% reductions for specific types of damage happened before or after the armor reduction to the damage. I think more clarity on how the mechanics of the game worked would have improved my experience. This games squad formation reminded me of one of my favorite parts of Star Sector, which is one of my favorite games of all time.Thus, this game gets a 10/10 from IGN because there is a little something for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: First 10-15 hours is great, but they give you so many cheap shots in their battles that I just can't bear to keep playing anymore. They let the story and their enforcement of the plot, which as you see in other reviews isn't very good anyway, override their good battle mechanics and excellent unit development mechanics - and don't get me wrong, those last two things are great.Like there's one battle where you're designed to get wiped out as part of the story. OK, if you want to advance the plot and split the players army up then that's doable. Just tell me that's what happened and move on. Why make me spend 20 minutes getting my butt whipped against impossible odds? How does that experience improve anyone's enjoyment of the game?That's just one battle and not ragequit worthy in and of itself. But there's another thing that the devs seem to love: having enemy units show up out of nowhere in the middle of the battle, units that weren't on the board, and surprise your units. Worse yet, in at least two of those battles (there's likely more but I binned the game after the second time) the enemy unit is literally unkillable. It will wipe out whatever it encounters in one attack and you can't harm it. They do tell you that this unit is showing up, but they don't tell you when or where, which doesn't do you much good.My thing is, play fair. If you want difficulty give me more enemies. If you want to set time limits (which I don't like either, but OK), then just set a f**king time limit and tell me what it is. Don't resort to that.It's not even about winning or losing. Likely I would still have won that last battle. The point is that with the unit development system you spend a lot of time working on your squads and promoting characters. Killing them off with cheap tactics like that is, to me, a lack of respect for my time. You don't want to have the impression that you're working harder than the devs did.Based on the game score most people don't mind the above. But I just can't stand that kind of stuff. At all. To me this game isn't worth the space on my hard drive, much less the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game definitely has it's moments and there's clear love and passion put into almost every facet of the story, world and design. I think it does unique things with the strategy rpg genre that I've been looking for awhile now. The use of gameplay story integration being a clear priority put into the development which I highly appreciate. However, I feel it's lacking in alot of places, mainly polish in it's presentation and some of it's writing. The portraits are fairly inconsistent in size and position, creating weird combinations with the UI, artifacts definitely need a UI rework and a sort button navigating it was really bad experience, alot of the dialogue feels clunky and unnatural, deciding to go for exposition over characterisation often. Alot of the art was oddly low resolution or inconsistent, Diana's portrait is scary in her proportions, Stefan's mouth has a line that feels overly thick, barnaby has an uncanny almost open eye when he closes them, a general lack of polish made the experience feel cheaper than it took to make.I actually really find most of the cast enjoyable and despite some people most likely saying they feel bland, I prefer a more grounded realistic take on cast design over other srpg's that will give every character a different hair style, the realistic art for characters like Stefan look excellent and the artist deserves alot of credit despite my complaints above.Some characters are bland and uninteresting though, never being given conversations or screentime to properly develop and others can just feel like a blank void of characterisation, the worst example being Jules who contributed nothing to the plot while feeling like an awkward void of bland-ness. I wish there was a dialogue log so I could reread dialogue I might've missed, it doesn't help that sometimes the text speed can feel awkward and stutter in an attempt to emulate speech pacing. There's alot of scenes I actually like in the game but there's this awkward feeling that looms over the game's story, I hope if the other games continue to be made, they can focus on making the characters feel more natural in the way they speak whilst still expanding on the world. I really liked the theme they were going for of the characters creating their own mythos that would be carried down and i'm excited to see how they'd handle it in the sequels. Besides those issues this game is pretty cool,. the mechanics are well thought out, well established and well utilised, most maps felt neat and permadeath wasn't overdone or underdone, it felt just right and establishing connections and stories with my own personal handmade squads was really fun. i think some mechanics need more signposting, walls were super confusing with what units could or couldn't shoot over them, when did archers double and when didn't they when attacking from range, stuff like siege cannons preventing a squad from being light infantry. All these things are things I feel could've been explained better though the tutorial log was pretty helpful, though some parts of the catalogue unlock at certain points and create spoilers for the game's own story such as how the powers tutorial spoils a character. I think there's alot of cool memorable moments that do make the experience worth it overall, and i think getting on sale was definitely a good decision, There is alot of love and care put into this game and I admire the devs for truly making a game they should be proud of, despite some of it's shortcomings.  I hope this game or it's sequels continue to expand on it's writing flow and quality of life to become something that could even rival the greats.edit: Also the controller support was perfect, everything felt great, just wanted to throw appreciation out for that.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect mix of Fire Emblem and Ogre Tactics. Squad micromanagement in this game is a very interesting way to pace the action between battles. The lack lack of experience and materials grinding through much of the game felt like a double edged sword: limiting the number and types of units you're able to train up in your army, but this also makes your unit comp decisions feel like they matter and you can't spam the best units. Mercifully, the game is very lenient in refunding materials should you decide to respec units or adopt a different strategy later in your game.This game is truly a diamond in the rough. There's definitely some balancing issues that need to be addressed as of version 1.0a when I finished my first playthrough, but the devs seem to be on it as the patch notes for 1.0b seem to be packed with needed changes.

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding turn based strategy game, glad I took a chance on it.I've played a lot of TBS games, but not one where you set up squads under single entity characters. I feel like being able to change and experiment with different squad make ups and combinations was almost as fun as playing the game itself.It was a bonus to come out of a mission looking forwards to what new items I could equip, what characters I could class change, or what new mercenaries were available for recruitment.The turn based portion itself is good, but certainly not outstandingly difficult. The AI is for the most part competent and will try to attack your weakest units as long as it has a path to them.I did notice a few instances where the AI seemingly wasn't playing by the same rules as me, with one particularly annoying example experienced several times. I had a situation where enemy class 2 archer units, with a range of 2 tiles, were attacking me from 3 tiles away. This can normally be achieved if they are on a hill or a bastion. They were not, however. They were on flat, green plains. They were certainly not the third class archers which indeed have 3 tile range either.This happened in several scenarios and was kind of annoying. Luckily archers are rather weak and it was never a threat, but having them not playing by the rules I had to abide by was unfortunate to see.Other than that I didn't run into any bugs or crashes, no text errors. Everything seems to be good there.The story wasn't bad, but it wasn't outstanding either. It served well enough to tie the battles together and give you a general motivation to accomplish things.One play through took me about 35 hours, and I can easily see this being a game that can be replayed multiple times to try out all the different unit combinations.Overall I'm really pleased with Symphony of War. I think it's absolutely worth the low asking price and would recommend it to anyone with an interest in fantasy turn based strategy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: It has a very similar look and feel to the Fire Emblem (FE) series, both in story and in gameplay. However, it differs from the FE series in one of the core features of the game, which is the implementation of squads and troop types. This, to me, adds more depth and complexity to the game, and it makes battles and skirmishes feel more realistic and strategic. The fact that you can have squads specialized in certain combat types and be able to maneuver them freely to gain the tactical advantage gives the impression that you are an actual tactician/general. Not only that, but the morale of the squads can be affected depending on the outcome of each battle, for both the ally and enemy squads. You can even have enemies surrender if their morale is low enough. I find this feature is interesting and more immersive in my gameplay. Playing with permadeath on adds in to the realism even more and makes you really consider each move more carefully.Although I haven't played through the entire game yet, I would highly recommend this game if you enjoy the FE series and want something similar to it but also a little different.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I had found this game years ago. When I was a wee lad, I fell in love with a game called Ogre Battle: March of the Black Queen (SNES). The game has been a favorite of mine for years and I will regularly download the rom and emulator just to play that game. Since then, I have not found another game like it. There was an Ogre Battle for the N64, but it seemed too cartoony and dumbed down. So I was pretty disappointed... Until this game came into my recommendations. This is that game that is like Ogre Battle. Two dimensional graphics where you move your units around the board, gather resources, auto battle the baddies, and (my favorite part) change the classes of your units. I loved that aspect of Ogre Battle and it's here in this game. I am only into the second battle, but I can already tell that I am going to love the rest of the game. If you want a game close to Ogre Battle, this is it. Buy it... Buy it now!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I did not expect to enjoy this game as much as I did. Do not let the 32-bit 90's graphics fool you.Imagine a game with the team customization of Ogre Battle, the between-battle configuration of Super Robot Wars and the rock-scissors-paper combat flow of Fire Emblem.  That's this game.  And wow does it work well.On top of that the character portrait art is gorgeous and the music score is professionally done.  My only gripe is the story and writing are nothing special, but for an indie game this game is punching way above its weight class.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, very nostalgic. The cinematic graphics feel a bit off compared to the rest of the game's graphics which look awesome but its forgivable since it doesnt look bad. The various mechanics that remind of old games such as Ogre Battle, Fire Emblem and maybe Warsong work very well together and are easy to understand. The customization is insane, from the main character to the squads compositions and items everything feels unique to the player and the story has a lot of twists and turns to keep you entertained for hours and hours, well worth its price. I would, however, like if the game provided more choices when it comes to the story and the path we wish to take. When dialogues happen the player has no input and everything the main character says is predetermined (perhaps by the initial character creation questions?) it would be cool to have some options of things to say or do that could impact the story somehow, besides choosing to do or not the side quests near mid/late game, but since the team behind this game is quite small i can see why some things are limited. I can only compare the dedication of the team to provide a good game to something like the FTL dev team or Factorio dev team, something rare nowadays and very much appreciated. 100% recommended

_childDocuments_.review: The Bad: -The story is full of the usual epic fantasy tropes. The twists can be seen a mile off and the game doesn't really bring anything new to the genre. A great evil has arisen, best friends from childhood are torn apart, chosen ones are to fulfill prophecies of destiny, yadda-yadda-yadda.   (C+)-The dialogue is pretty horrendous at times. Especially for the main character. And even more especially during any "romance" dialogues. The speech in this game often feels childish or out of place for the fantasy setting. (D)The Good:+The game has an excellent game-play loop. Organizing troupes, upgrading them, assigning weapon and armor bonuses, etc. are all good. The auto-battling system itself is really well done and enjoyable. Though, once the game really picks up and you're fighting many more larger-scale battles, you'll likely want to turn up the battle-speed in the option menu, or spend a loooong time waiting for 35 small battles to take place.  (A-)Last mention: I didn't play on the hardest difficulty, but the one under it. Once you have a strong set of 3 or 4 characters, they pretty much do all of the heavy-lifting. If you have an adept healer or two, your squads can almost never die. I felt powerful, but also kind of purposeless, as the challenge is whittled down to almost nil. Overall, I really did enjoy playing the game. This type of game-play style is pretty rare, and rarely well done. Despite the story and dialogue, the rest of the game holds up quite well. I give it a: (B-)

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but I have really enjoyed it so far.I know that the negatives will be more than the positives but the latter are so great, they win over the former in the end, in my opinion.The bad things first.The story gets a weird turn after a dozen chapters and this is the reason why I stopped playing for a couple of days. And in general, the story is not that great and the characters are not that memorable. Also, I had the notion that the protagonist could create relationships with the other npcs, but besides some basic chatting and befriending some of them, without any benefits, I haven't seen anything substantial on this matter yet.The UI for the squad management is not very controller friendly and not informative in general.I wish I could see in a glance my squads' power, artifacts etc., without having to get in and out of the menus the way they are made. It makes it too time consuming and tiring to see what each of my squad needs and therefore I haven't even equipped many of my artifacts or my skills for that reason.And that comes to the next point, which is the difficulty.I know that I can change it to hard or whatever, but I always try to play the games in normal, in the sense that this was the way it was made and meant to be played.And in normal, the game feels sometimes too easy. There were a couple of fights were I had to sacrifice a squad or two due to my mistakes mostly. But there was no fight were I felt I barely managed to win. Especially Diane is too powerful and mostly one-shots the rest of the game so far.Now the good thing(s).Well, as you may already know, the squad mechanics is the most interesting part of the game and is very well made and very enjoyable. I spend a lot of time in between battles to manage my squads and I have never felt I wasted my time there. Only if the menus were better made as I said before..I like the graphics because the remind me of Shining Force on Mega Drive, so I appreciate the nostalgia.The character art is.. of an acquired taste I would say, although you get used to it pretty quickly.Music is fine. Not bad but nothing memorable.As you see there is only one really good thing about this game so far and a few bad ones.Still, they are not so bad to make you not want to play this game. And the good is so good that it makes you not mind the bad ones.I wish they get a lot of support from this game, so they can make another, more improved in the future.I will be looking forward for it. And that is why I give a positive review in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle to write positive reviews because I'm the kind of person that demands perfection in an imperfect world. I have so much feedback about this game, things I'd like to see improved or changed, but at the end of the day, none of that really matters. The truth is, I could not put this game down until it was finished. As a gamer in my thirties, I was overwhelmed with nostalgia as I played Symphony of War (SoW). The music, the character design, the political intrigue, all of this melded together to deliver an experience that I've been missing for more than a decade. This game stands on the shoulders of titans like Ogre Battle, Final Fantasy Tactics, and Fire Emblem, but it is no clone. SoW builds on the systems of its forebearers and threatens to establish a whole new genre. SoW is expected to be the first in a series, and the next installment cannot come soon enough. I'll be anxiously waiting to devour the next installment, or any DLC that comes our way.Thank you to the team at Dancing Dragon Games for a truly delightful experience. Nothing could have prepared me for this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so awesome.  I have not finished it yet, but I made significant progress in the game at the least to be breath's away from unlocking final tier in the perk/passive tree thingy.  It's got that ogre battle feel that you long for and it's in pure turn-based combat.  There's no special magic cards to help you in battle, but there's many unit types, many strategic ways to destroy the enemy and there are 3 difficulty settings you can pick at start of game.  The sounds and music are nice, especially the music.  If you played any of Phil's other games, you will pick up on what kind of music to expect.  For a rpg maker game, it's definitely S tier.  If you think back on how you customized your squads in the old Ogre games, you will probably feel right at home here as messing around with that and equipping them with artifacts (kinda like gear for the squad) is fun.  One thing I remind you though is you actually speed up the animations and the game itself with holding a button down and it's really really fast.  Also keep eye out for tents on certain missions as they easy to miss and have better loot/recruits in them than u would get in between missions.Dev also plans to add more cool things to the game like new modes as mentioned on discord so I'm excited for that.  He also fairly active and fun to talk with along anyone else there.  I highly recommend this game to fans of turn-based combat and tactical rpgs alike.  The story gets really really interesting too.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really recommend this, as much as I want to.  There's a foundation here that I would want the team to build on and look forward to their next outing, but the game here just isn't enough to justify the time.  The story and writing are bad, the UI is annoying (e.g., I can't see at a glance what levels and leadership my units have), and the gameplay is just too easy (on Captain).  Doom squads are just too easy to create, and they'll carry you through multiple maps.  I shouldn't have to lack any fear of my squad's health after being attacked by 4-5 enemy squads; that should be a tactical error that should cost me, but it doesn't, except in XP distribution.  The units are greatly unbalanced (dragons are too good, light infantry are real bad), so once you figure out what's good, there's no real incentive to make a balanced squad.  Also, the maps are too small/linear to justify having 15-20 squad maps.  By the end, I usually left half my team idling just to speed it up, especially since, as stated above, you don't need more than 1-2 squads to chew through the enemy ranks.  It also really didn't help that my final impression of the game is that the game bugged during the ending, so I don't even know how the story ends, although I think I'm fine with it.Too flawed, too much filler, too much fiddliness to really recommend, but still looking forward to how any potential sequel shapes up.  I mean, heck, I finished the game, so it's not like I didn't enjoy myself, but at some point, it was just out of completionist obligation rather than any sort of desire to push on.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you're a fan of Fire Emblem, Ogre Battle, Advance Wars, or Final Fantasy Tactics, pick this game up!As a kid, I grew up playing some of the classic SRPGs. Sadly, they don't seem to get made that often today. Yes, Fire Emblem is still putting out new games, but aside from that, there hasn't been much effort put into the genre lately. This Indie game, made by just two people, seeks to remedy that.On it's surface, the game looks a lot like an older Fire Emblem game. The pixel-sprites remind me of Super Nintendo (in a good way!) and I find most units "stand out" which is also a plus.The gameplay is extremely similar to Fire Emblem, but with a twist borrowed from Ogre Battle 64: You can add multiple weaker units into your heroes "squad" to assist them in combat. This adds quite a nice layer of customization, as these weaker units can grow into a variety of more advanced classes. It should also serve to keep replayability high, as your army may look vastly different from one playthrough to another.Sadly you *cannot* customize each units weapons/armor, but I understand why this choice was made, as many would find managing the equipment of a hundred soldiers overwhelming (I would personally enjoy it though). The only way to customize a squad other than via its membership, is via held items. These affect the whole squad, and there are only a maximum of three slots per squad. The items seems pretty well balanced, and it's often a hard choice in terms of which to use.Overall, the batles are very satisfying, as is the unit growth/customization. Now, on to some things I didn't quite like as much.....The story is a bit generic (at least so far, haven't finished my first run yet) and there is a lot of dialog. And if I'm being honest, the dialog is one of the games weaker points. I would reccomend hiring an outside writer for a sequel.The only other complaint I have is the character portraits. In a vacuum, I am simply not a fan, but taken with the rest of the games art, they seem out of place, like they don't fit in. I would also reccomend outsourcing these for a sequel.I cannot comment on the music/sound as I mostly play on mute.Taken as a whole, this is an AMAZING game with a few notable weak spots. It was made by people who very clearly have a passion for the genre, and it definitely shows. Not only am I excited for any future updates, but I really hope there is a sequel some day as well. Anything new this company puts out will likely be a day 1 buy for me. Don't let the character portraits put you off. Do yourself a favor and play this game!8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game was a lot of fun for a while, the story had some interesting twists and turns, about halfway through I was really surprised that a tactical rpg that was entirely reliant on power leveling specific units would do this or that thing to make the early battles chaotic and keep you from just relying on one or two overpowered units.  And money was tight so I couldn't just buy whatever overpowered thing I found. I started recommending it to friends and clocked like 30 hours in a single week.I was enjoying it so much that halfway through the game  I even started doing a second run to try and doing one of the really hard achievements, where you have to defeat a completely overwhelming force, and so I tried to create an army specifically for that one stage. But then in the second half of the game the story falls apart, the twists stop being interesting, and it stops doing things to force you to mix up your troops and you no longer need to worry about money. And once you've developed a decent sized army the challenge just falls off a cliff.  It actually becomes a better strategy to just have five or six units battle over and over to overlevel and become unstoppable, than it does to try and juggle all the characters and unit types.  I had a lot of fun with the game overall and couldn't stop playing for the first 30 or so hours... but it was a real struggle to get through to the end because it just became dull and it stopped being about juggling unit types and rock/paper/scissors combat and more about the enemy having sheer raw numbers. It took me a couple week to get around to doing the last handful of stages because the game just fell off hard near the end.Still recomended though! If you're going to play it, play it on hard mode, consider turning perma-death on, and don't overlevel.  Don't play it on easy, there's just no point, and normal is pretty breezy.

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to some other reviews, this one gets a BARELY RECOMMENDED rating from me.Symphony of War isn't a great game overall. It is a good game, where the strengths largely outweigh the weaknesses, and a reasonable price point gives it a good gameplay to price value (at least as of being around halfway through the game ans ~20 hours in).Pros:- Good strategic army potential- I can see the potential for some strong synergies later in the game (although I may have missed a lot of opportunity to build towards some of those)- Decent character artwork- Clean sprites (although many look like RPG Maker)Cons:- Very little explanation of systems, units, and effective planning tools- Story and dialogue are quite mediocre and all over the place (at least around halfway through)- Very limited ability to level up additional units outside of the story (I got one arena "token" so far halfway through the game, and no ability to "respec"?- UI has some very odd choices on how to manage units, items, etc, especially when trying to interact with units in armies vs. those in reserve. Far too many "clicks" needed to do simple things - should have been caught in testing and optimized by now.The largest draw to this type of game is the construction of your army units. Something that is very poorly explained overall, giving you little real guidance on what you should aim for. Should you combine infantry and calvary? Archers and mages?  Some of this is a bit of common sense, but since you are playing in a system heavily influenced by which unit types are strong against others (not to mention a barely visible elemental affinity system), how do you defend weaker units, and how do to keep units alive and well, this is barely covered and minimal guidance is given.I've found the battles to grow longer and longer, but not really more fun. Instead of feeling like I have more tools in my arsenal and more options to use them, I seem to be relying on the same strongest units as others can only chip away at enemies versus almost destroying them in a turn. I am sure there are ways to build better unit combinations, but I don't know them and don't see myself doing another play through as I'm already dragging my feet - but I do intend to try to finish the game in case more of this tightens up as we get later into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say that my experience with SoW was mostly positive, but with some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ here and there that really got on my nerves towards the tail end of things.This game is impressive to me, the developer make good use of RPGmaker in a lot of aspects. And not well enough in others, but I'd still say it's overall a great effort.There's fun to be had in creating armies, forming squads, and upgrading units into whatever you want them to be to make a balanced squad or make someone dedicated to one role. The old fire emblem weapon system of stuff breaking isn't here, thank christ. Instead we have sort of an armor/weaponry circle? It's a little hard to explain but it's easy to understand the offense and defense benefits.My biggest complaints though is that, for most of my playthrough, I was only really motivated enough to form 3-4 independent squads that did not come from a plot relevant character. Most of the time those important characters already come with their own armies, and even if you make a ton of troops you probably won't get far without the benefits from one of the default leaders, whether you buy stronger ones at a marketplace or not being irrelevant. And it's only really in the last couple of chapters that you get to deploy upward of 20 squads, though for me I was rolling with 17 at the end of my first playthrough.Guns are annoying. I was fascinated with them at first, but then I realized they were cheap shots to destroy everything with only one unit being able to really survive a full volley, and that's the sentinel. Of course this is before they start throwing rows of 4-6 gunmen at you, and if it's the enemy that goes first then you may as well mark that squad off as KIA for all it's worth because the enemy guns tend to have 2 shots whereas yours only get 1 until a late end game tech tree becomes available.There are several priority targets and strategic approaches you can take when attacking. For me though I wish I could've had an order that said "Ignore the healers you minges." because seeing 5-7 people dogpile one healer in the center and wasting their turn instead of the row of magic tossers in the back is very VERY aggravating.I also advice against playing with permadeath mode on. Cause it felt more arduous than it was worth. The plot wasn't really incredibly deep, and the characters are pretty one note. Honestly though, sometimes a straight forward nice time is a good thing instead of a ton of complex twists and turns that make you go "Oh sh!t" every 5 seconds. The game also does great at one point when your resources feel like they're dwindling, I won't go into detail but it matches up with how the plot was up and til that moment and it felt great to build it back up.It's a good game for the most part with some pretty big red flags, but overall as something to lay back and relax with the challenge felt pretty fair, especially if you try to S rank chapters, though I do not recall any option to replay previous chapters unless you got a save for then, but if you're like me you save before each chapter anyway.I look forward to whatever this team does next and probably will be investigating their previous products as well.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10I loved this game. If you like turn based strategy, custom squads, and beautiful pixel art, then you'll enjoy this game. I only played through the campaign once. I do not think I would play through the ENTIRE campaign again just to do higher difficulties. It would be nice if there was a skirmish mode (beyond the Arena), or some way to replay previous missions on higher difficulties. Edit: After writing this I found that "Endurance Training" is on the roadmap, which kind of addresses this a bit.I don't have any complaints about this game, but there are improvement opportunities in areas related to some of the writing and voice line quality/direction. I thought the premise of the story was fine and the main cast well written with motivations and personal conflicts. However some points of the story just felt "thin". That's the best word I can think of for it. I wasn't expecting stellar voice acting, but there is wide variance in the quality of the actual audio quality for some of the characters (Raskuja in particular).I like that there is a permadeath option so that people who enjoy that kind of gameplay can opt-into it, but I am not one of those people. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Excellent throwback, bringing modern language to a worthy parody of older fantasy army management /tactics games (gameplay is basically the exact same as the Ogre Battle series).Pros:○ Replayable if you want to experience variations on the story (relationship building) or try different army/tech builds.○ Most achievements actually feel like achievements. These can be obtained in under 100 hours played (guides say 60-80) but i spent 110 because i'm a masochistic perfectionist who has to play on the hardest difficulty. If you aren't me you'll probably like this even more.○ MANY different ways to build your army, and depending on how you build early will affect who has what later on... so your experience is actually your own experience. The missions are linear, but the progress through them and the resulting army will be different every time.○ Excellent music. I'll admit to spending probably 5 hours just listening to the music... was there a music pack? I should probably go buy that...○ Mechanically perfect for the genre. Hits have weight, dodges feel important, and having a full squad of archers hit your heavy armor soldier line for 0 damage 20 times in 1 second is a great feeling.Neutral:○ The characters are obviously parody, but not silly. Standard tropes apply. Well written and the Main Character (you) get some of the funniest lines as it directly contrasts the older trope styles of the other characters. It isn't for everyone maybe, but it's well done.○ The story is predictable. Since everyone is a trope if you've spent any amount of time in related genres you'll see what's coming long before it presents itself on screen. This isn't bad, but not necessarily good either. I do have to admit I love that the story stuck to its path and didn't "ha, gotcha" with a twist that didn't make sense as many other games and movies have begun doing recently.○ The tactics are important, but you'll probably spend more time (re)building your army. I personally enjoy this. Managing the resources for class upgrades, selectively equipping artifacts, early on deciding whether to make a single super-powered squad or spreading the powerful characters out to make multiple 'slightly better than average' squads... lots of options.○ "The AI is stupid". well yeah, very minor spoiler but you start off in an academy where you can assume that your character has learned all the tactics that they would throw at you. I feel this story line decision was based on the fact that the AI is simplistic (another throwback in the genre). It's not 100% structured responses but it's close enough that it's easy to figure out how to bait them into attacking things they have no chance against. I feel it's reasonable AI, and the difficulty is more based on your ability to plan multiple moves ahead (or use a lot of restarts if that's your thing).○ bunch of other stuff I probably forgot to focus on.Cons:○ Nothing hidden in the map; no easter egg type stuff (as a comparison ogre battle had special item finds for searching specific squares, random popup fights which you could sometimes get them to join you a-la march of the black queen for unique units, pumpkin head and ghost specialty halloween units) ... maybe this should go in neutral but missing the opportunity was disappointing for me. ○ No multiplayer. Okay seriously that's kind of obvious for this type of title. Having multiplayer wouldn't really provide any extra benefit beyond a gimmick that would be quickly forgotten by 99% of the playerbase. You don't play longform tactics army management games to have/make friends.○ umm... it took 20 years to get a decent Ogre Battle replacement? Seriously if the items above aren't to your liking pretend I put them here. Overall great game. Maybe not in my top 5 of all time, but definitely up there (note i have over 700 games just on Steam as of this review). Highly recommended to anyone who enjoys tactics, strategy, and/or min-maxing / efficiency management.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quality game. If you're looking for grid based turn based strategy, this'll scratch that itch for sure. It's not perfect, and it can be pretty short (I'm not calling 88 hours short, I just kept accidentally alt tabbing out of the game instead of closing it). There are 30 story chapters and 5 optional chapters.The good: -The gameplay mechanics are unique enough to be interesting, yet simple enough to not be confusing-You very tangibly become more powerful as the game progresses, there is a lot of cool ways to progress and train and expand your army. You actually feel like you started as a regular soldier and ended up as a once in a generation set of killing machines that can tear through full armies-The level designs are usually pretty fun, there are a few more mundane ones, but the layouts of the maps are usually pretty interesting-The dialogue (with some exceptions *ahem* lysander *ahem*) is pretty great! It's engaging, it's fun, it never tells instead of showing, it's informative without being exposition dump. It makes you care about the characters. I will say though, that many characters fall to the wayside. New characters come in and shove the old ones out of the spotlight, and you never hear from the old ones again. Barnabus is literally the main character's adoptive father figure and after a certain point, he basically never says a word again until the endThe bad:-The story starts out really good and then just veers off the rails at the end. I'm still very confused by many things in the ending, a pivotal character, I'll call him "the hand" to not spoil anything, is just never explained even remotely, and he plays a very pivotal part in the story-This game does not hand hold at all, which is great, but there are some things that should have been made way clearer, like how to read how traits work, and things that are just never explained, like what influences whether or not a character gets a free action-Every difficulty except warlord (the hardest one, and the only mode with permadeath) becomes a cakewalk. My first playthrough, on the normal difficulty, not even the easy one, I beat the final chapter, killing the final boss, a literal god, in two turns. You really have to intentionally handicap yourself so as not to steamroll the second half of the gameOverview:I grew up on Shining Force and Shining Force 2. This game is exactly what people who like FF Tactics, or Dark Deity, or Fire Emblem would enjoy, a game that follows the tried and true method, but adds enough new mechanics to keep it fresh. The story gets confusing and is a bit lacking towards the end, and honestly has some weird things to say about religion, and colonialism, and conquest and all that, but through and through an engaging, fun game. Just be ready for every character to totally switch up and change personalities after a certain pivotal point.

_childDocuments_.review: The last game I reviewed was Dark Deity. It was a promising game but ultimately pushed me away because of gameplay decisions I felt got in the way of the overall experience. A little over 20 hours and a credit scroll later I can safely say that is not the case with Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga.From a gameplay perspective- as with Dark Deity, Symphony of War takes heavy inspiration from the Fire Emblem franchise. Specifically, Fire Emblem: Genealogy of the Holy War. Maps are large but filled with side objectives, checkpoints, chests, and a lot of enemies. To not overwhelm the player, you're given a lot of tools to handle the obstacles in your way with customizable squads; units made up of story as well as self appointed leaders with troops that dictate your movement type as well as how your squads attack. This allows you to tailor your roster to better complete each map as well as their side objectives and earn the oh so glorious S rank at the end of the mission.Why should you work towards fully completing each map? Well, they answer that in two ways. 1 being the Merit system, which allows you to unlock better troops and items throughout the game and the other being resources. Some units will require more than just feeding them enemy soldiers and as your army grows the more resources are needed to keep your army up to task.Where I can say the game fell short for me was the story. It's... okay. It serves its purpose to keep you engaged but often times it feels like the gameplay can not express the tone of the story. Often times plot points happen with very little build up and twists feel like they happen for shock factor instead of something where you could follow the train after thinking on it for a moment.Overall, I had a lot of fun. Minor nit picks aside it was well worth my money and I'm looking forward to what the devs cook up next. I'd give the game a ten but there's no farming or fishing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. It's completely unrecognizable from the RPG maker box that it comes from and combines this really fascinating mix of Fire Emblem as well as Advanced Wars.If you don't know the difference, Fire Emblem focuses around controlling individual units while advanced wars strives for more an RTS feel (building armies, capturing resources, etc). Each game tends to have their weaknesses and strengths and Symphony of War doesn't JUST try to take the best of both worlds and mash things together willy nilly. They take strengths and CERTAIN weaknesses to provide a completely fresh experience since, realistically, both games have their own feels and rather than haphazardly combining things OR simply copying without improving/iterating on the past, they decide to create something new. Gone are single units per "stack" and in their place are ever evolving squads of units. Your main character is one of two characters in this game with unique classes with other story units turned into beefed up versions of existing classes.Typically, you usually make each story unit their own squad, but you can additionally create squads of non-story important units either from mercenaries you train/hire or sometimes units that are given to you throughout the campaign. There's a couple of them, but not going to say what they are because they might be spoilers.With this system, you get this sort of interesting usage of units since rather than singular units, you are managing a squad. This means that you can build some squads to be completely all out offensive or have a mix of healers, defenders, and attackers. Because of this, the game forgoes the weapon triangle. Instead, they have a more ambiguous advantage and disadvantage system like how magic ignores armored class defenses (aside from the paladin class) and how ranged units are vulnerable in close range. This also means that as squads take damage and units die, the squad that loses combat effectiveness in a much more satisfying way than either Fire Emblem or Advanced Wars. In Fire Emblem, a 1 hp unit dealt the same amount of damage as a 100 hp unit, thus forcing developers to create systems of chance to determine the success of an attack. In Advanced wars, the entirety of the squad's hp is considered a singular whole and when the squad takes damage, you lose units in terms of the percentage of hp (20 percent hp lost = 20 percent of squad lost = 20 percent of squad fire power lost). Symphony of war lets you play something more satisfying than both systems where you CAN create situations where you cripple your opponent while also having defensive minded squads that can even out damage and heal against poke - rewarding both Offensive squad building and defensive squad building.Now, aside from the great gameplay, there's also the fantastic story. What a rollercoaster - classic war epic with lots of drama, high stakes, and great characters. While the main character is a bit flat, I do at least want to KICK THE LIVING ♥♥♥♥ OUT OF THAT MOTHA-♥♥♥♥♥♥' GARBAGE THAT TRIES TO ♥♥♥♥ WITH HIM/ME. It's simple, it's sweet, and it's a whole lotta fun. I do feel there are some cutscenes that are missing towards the 3rd or 4th last mission, but it nothing world breaking. Now, if only there were a way to ask to get one's hands on their source code because holy hell, I wanna make a game with this system now.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Fire Emblem with guns and actual army, now on your PC - a big YES.It has everything from Fire Emblem and more, from the good, the bad, to the not-so-appealing.Gameplay-wise, it's very fun. It's well thought and well put together, very solid. The progression is great, it started out slow and simple and gradually gives us more options. The combat is complex (in a good way,) backed by the customization that is so free yet balanced. Can clearly see the dev loves the genre. No weapon triangle, btw.The story and the writing are all alright. But since it's inspired by FE, it met with the same pros and cons of FE storytelling.Then there is the art. Like most FE games before FE 13, it suffers from being generic and uninspired, and cobbling 3 extremely different art styles together made them hold themselves worse than the Veridia Empire. Still, it's a really nice and fun game from the gameplay perspective. Don't let the art discourage you like it did to me for a very long time.Edit: though the customization is fun, it's also kinda pain. Wish it's made easier or utilize being on PC more, an ability to hover the cursor over units to see their status instead of the needs to use the menu would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard about the PC launch of Tactics Ogre: Reborn I felt the urge to play a Tactical RPG immediately. That’s when I found Symphony of War and decided to give it a try. I'm glad I did.If Fire Emblem and Ogre Battle had a baby, this game would be a possible offspring. The inspiration is evident right from the start with the blue-haired main character (Marth) and the tarot reading when you start a new game.Gameplay is essentially FE but, like in OB, combat is carried out automatically by squads that can range from 1 to 9 units. It’s possible to fast forward combat by holding the left trigger, which is great. Units are not locked onto a certain path once you evolve them. It’s possible to conveniently devolve units and get a full refund on the materials. There’s no need to backtrack to a prior save so you don’t get stuck with a unit you don’t like.Even though the writing and the menu’s UI/UX could be improved, it’s not enough to justify a thumbs down. If you are itching for some Tactical RPG time, SoW is a solid, budget pick that will run on your kitchen toaster and will keep you entertained for dozens of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy game to spend a few evenings with. I really enjoyed it, it took me back to simpler times, and the art style is charming. The difficulty was never unmanageable, it gets a little too easy towards the end if you don't play with permadeath, but at the same time, it probably becomes a lot more stressful if you do and one of the best things for me was how relaxing it was. I had a few that were in my headcanon, but they really weren't that different from the average unit.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Extremely enjoyable squad builder and a great amount of customization. Between types of units, upgrades for those individual units, artifacts that affect whole squads, and designing the squads themselves the amount of choices you can make regarding your army is wide enough to have you spending more time designing your team than actually fighting with them. For me, this makes it all the more satisfying when my squads absolutely annihilate everything in their path as a result of my meticulous tinkering.-Decent levels of strategy, especially early on. Strategy becomes less important later as squad building becomes more of an option.-Story was alright, no major plot holes for me but also not many huge winning moments. In the end it makes sense and came with a few fun twists. The conversation system between characters felt sporadic and random though, and if there was some way to bring those about through in-game efforts that would be better in my opinion.-The resource system and occupiable map objectives added another layer of thought into your army that was a welcome addition and made you take into consideration who needed upgrades more than others. The amount of resources you received in the first half felt barely adequate and kept me on my toes(good). Soon after that I ended up with 15-20 of nearly every resource(except iron, darn you iron) and already rocking 15 squads of t3 units, could do with a little less to keep up the challenge if you ask me(captain difficulty here)-Throwback graphics when done in this style are always great. Brings me back to my FE: Shadow Dragon days.-The balancing of the units and their respective counters felt very well designed. Nearly everything in the game has some sort of strength and weakness, whether that be glass cannon rifleman who can burst down nearly any enemy front-line but lack a second attack(for most the game) and have little to no defensive capability or sentinels who come as the best defensive option against rifleman but lack attacking power and are weak still to magic. This game does what many hope to achieve where instead of a rock-paper-scissor triangle we have a dynamic system filled with multiple options. Do you want to make a squad that is enormously tanky and capable of inhaling constant damage? It can be done. Do you want to make a squad of only artillery canons where they can one shot any army at distance? Have at it.Cons:-Will suck up your time.-Needs more missions, especially side missions. I was hoping once we reached the chapter where we first encountered side missions they would become common. I was very disappointed when they did not.-Difficulty is a bit sporadic. I feel personally that for the first half of the campaign, it is in uphill battle where every resource objective is essential and fights require more countering and strategy. Once you reach a certain part in the campaign where main characters start getting upgrades and you have artifacts overflowing in your inventory, a single squad can conceivable wipe half of a stage on their own without any effort. While I don't necessarily hate myself, I do enjoy a challenge and it would be great to see the enemy having an escalating amount of resistance/intelligence as you increase in power as well. I mean, twice I was faced with a "run from the super boss and escape the map" and instead I just turned and killed him both times.-To build on the point above, having a skip option for the enemy turn is needed. Spend a bunch of time watching the enemy army plotting.-The enemy AI could do with a slight buff. Much of the time they are easy to fool and consistently will only attack whatever they register as the lowest "threat" rather than what they might counter, the bigger threat that will likely one shot them next turn they are standing next to or a one person squad on the edge of death but still has a higher threat count. It makes it so I can bring suicide squads and just sacrifice them to save my main squads or distract enemies while I kill them freely.-AddictiveOverall, a well thought out and developed game. If you are looking to play a squad builder that comes with a fire emblem interface, you're in the right place.
