_childDocuments_.review: Short version first. If you enjoy Final Fantasy Tactics, Ogre Battle, Battle for Wesnoth, and/or Fire Emblem, you'll likely enjoy this. Does it clear the Threshold of Badassery? No. Not if it stays like this. Could it? Oh so very YES. With some love and growth. 6.5/10, maybe an 8 or 9 depending on developer plans.If this is the final version of the game and the developers intend to do nothing more than fix bugs, I'm sorely disappointed in them and have to give this a 6.5/10. IF this is just a first iteration, which I SO hope, it jumps to 8.5 easy. Worth one play through? Absolutely. Revisit? Maybe after some expansion work. Ok, long version. First, 30 + missions, each nicely variable. There are a few points on a second run through where I would do things MAJORLY differently, like when you temporarily lose units or making sure I have dragon riders for a certain mission. You'll know both when you get there. Otherwise, solid. Captain difficulty engages the mind without being an exercise in frustrating resource management. On higher difficulties it can be very difficult having to permanently sacrifice units you've taken pains to develop. 8/10, could use some polish but pretty sweet anyway.Second, the story. The bones already in place are good, sturdy bones. But they need MORE. More character development between cut scenes, more exposition on lesser items. As an example, they make a big deal on a side mission about dragon broods being controlled or destroyed by the baddies, then only mention "Show them the might of the Red Dragon Brood" after you've saved the Blues. (Suck it Red!) they totally could have made that more of a thing in the blue rescue mission, or in other places. A good starting point with lots of potential, BUT, and this is BIG, please, please, please, PUT SOME MEAT ON THEM BONES.5/10, good start.Third. Units and Mechanics. It all makes sense and works well together. I wish there was less cross over between upgrade paths for the recruits, aside for a tiny handful of possibilities, it doesn't really matter which type you recruit so long as it is the right gender. Other than that, no complaints really. A good balance between ranges, melee vs mage vs archer. Archer and gunner and nicely distinct despite both being ranged, technically, and crossbowman is a nice middle ground between the two. A couple interesting combo units and some specialty units. And a couple useless types.The useless types (in my opinion) are the fire mage and the cannon. They have potential, but end up kinda meh unless you have a very specific unit formation. For the magi, the fire attacks an entire row (max 3), the lightning an entire column (max 5) and ice does a kind of burst centered on one, so max 9 maybe? The Ice is the most versatile and the lightning is always nice. The fire tends to hit the front row and unless upgraded in the tech tree, goes on the second turn so not so useful. The cannon is slow and only attacks on offense, so you kinda have to build your entire army around three or four units stuffed with these to really make use of them except on the defense. Which happens exactly ONCE. When you don't have the tech to build them.7/10. Needs a little love.What I would love to see them add in is a page or three from Battle for Wesnoth and give the community a map editor function. Let them build their own scenarios and campaigns, and do multiplayer maps, and SHARE THEM. I HOPE they are moving in that direction (in addition to building upon the story) because that would take a solid and satisfactory game and boot it up into the Realms of Badassery. So in review. Worth a play? Yes. 6.5 if this is where it stops, if growth is planned this jumps to an 8 with potential to go even higher depending on what they do with the potential this title has.

_childDocuments_.review: As has often been described for this game, it is basically a fusion of Fire Emblem and old school Ogre battle thanks to the small teams of units.I just completed the game+ Gaiden chapters so bear that in mind from his short review.Pros- Good animation/sound effects, pretty surprising since I think this game was built on the RPG maker engine or something similar. - Unique blend of tactical RPG thanks to the way you can build your units, having say a blended unit with infantry and getting cavalry movement was very cool and features such as the ambush mechanic to keep things interesting. - A decent cast of likeable named characters, gave me a chuckle or two with some of the witty banter and kept the plot at an even pace. Cons- Mid to late game gets rather tedious, not from lack of enemy variety bu lack of environments. I understand they wanted to have a large scale game with many units on screen but it wouldn't have hurt to vary them every so often, far too many open planes gets boring after a while.- Some unit types just felt too one sided, defensively or offensively (more specifically firearms and mages), so while you can build around that with specific items and teams It felt a bit ham fisted. Why can't my mages and firearm users hit from more than 1 range!- Strange difficulty spikes for some missions, more or less forcing you to turtle to survive lest you risk losing or sacrificing units you should not have.- Feels like it Is not as replayable as has been said, yes some items and units available will be different per mission but it still didn't feel organic enough to make it interesting (instead of say branching routes like some other Strategy RPGs can do). - The music gets incredibly repetitive between missions, it would have been nice to have some small variety when entering into battle as that's where it was most noticeable to me.  Tl;drIf you enjoy a Strategy RPG with a good amount of depth, decent unit variety and a few unique mechanics while not destroying your wallet, pick up this game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played in a long time. Of all the many many Fire Emblem clones I've played, this one is the best for sure. It's squad innovation is so much better than the double-unit innovation that more recent FE games have introduced so I daresay this is actually better than FE. The squad system where heroes command squads that can each level up and branch into different classes is complex enough to satisfy tactical and RPG itches while simple enough not to get you too caught up on administrative work. Despite running 10+ squads each with 6+ units, I still find it less stressful and more enjoyable to manage than the endless class changing in more recent FE games. I'd say this is the true spiritual successor to FE and what FE should've evolved to. This game has a lot of heart - it's obvious the devs really love the genre and crafted something they enjoyed. The game does get repetitive towards the end. It took me 60 hrs but really should've ended at 40 - once most of the squads got upgraded to end class units and the tech tree filled out, it became kind of a slog to continue for so many chapters more just to finish the story. Sometimes less is more. There are also lot of quality of life improvements that can be made, like toggling enemy move on/off (maybe there was a hotkey for that but I never found it).But for the most part, you would not regret getting this game if you have any interest in tactical RPGs. Bravo to the team that made this!

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of hard to put into words just how much character is in this game. I love the Fire Emblem games that came out on Famicom, the feeling of size and scale, compared to later entries in the series. A lot of people will probably end up comparing this to the gba games, but I think it has a lot of the heart and soul from games such as Fire Emblem 4 and Thracia 776. Speaking of the latter, the second you feel content, thinking that the game is pretty much going to be a breeze, there is a bit of a rude awakening, if you are not prepared. Without getting into spoilers, I felt the same sense of ascending dread as some of the characters end up doing.It is fair to say I ran into a minor bug (that actually worked out in my favor, but a bug is a bug) in which I reported to the discord, wherein I both got advice in what to do to have an easier time with the level as to not run into the same situation that led to the bug, and a direct contact to explain it to one of the developers. The community is quite welcoming and kind, which is particularly relevant to the review because the game has a link to the discord in the menu. People are playing all sorts of bizarre challenge builds, finding success in the deeper mechanics that most people probably don't need to deal with.This is a kind of game I didn't know I needed, until I got it. There's a couple of small things that could be changed for the sequel, such as better spacing out the gaiden chapters, but as it turns out my other gripe with the game is being addressed sometime within this week. Future players will appreciate the infinite arena mode, and it will make a secondary playthrough all the more fun. I have had a lot of fun with this, and will be playing it again soon.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute must-play for fans of classic Fire Emblem games, this game mixes the visuals and mission structure of early FE with the squad-building mechanics of Ogre Battle 64, and it largely succeeds.Gameplay: Again, very normal turn-based tactics fare. The missions had interesting twists that kept me engaged from start to finish. The squad customization was extremely fun and I spent many hours just tweaking my units and trying to build the strongest squads. I like that the simple mission based structure kept the focus on the gameplay and there wasn't any running around to  gather crafting materials or anything like that. Everything happens on the field or in the menus in between missions, and that's perfect in my book.Story/writing: This was somewhat hit or miss for me. At times the story and dialogue and support conversations struck me with how interesting or funny they were. At times things felt rushed or under-explained, especially in the final act of the story. I still can't really fully explain what happened at the end. However, because this aspect is such a small part of the overall experience, I wouldn't let it dissuade anyone. One thing it thankfully does not have is a bunch of cringe, one-note anime trope characters. While the writing didn't always work for me, I do appreciate that a lot of care and love went into each member of the cast.Other comments: I recommend that tactics veterans start with the higher difficulty. I chose Normal and my units were so strong after a certain point that I absolutely bulldozed over the last third of the game. That's without looking up any kind of optimal builds or strategies online. Overall score: 4.5/5. An easy recommendation to any tactics fans, especially if you love the likes of old Fire Emblem, Final Fantasy Tactics, Tactics Ogre/Ogre Battle, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been keeping my eye on the game for a while so I was READY when it dropped on us unexpectedly. Within the first week, I logged 40 hours. I took my time, reading all the dialogue, experimenting with the mechanics, and generally immersing myself. I was immediately impressed. The music somehow manages to be nostalgic, yet new. The characters are immediately fun, the character art is refreshing in a sea of anime-esque designs (not that that's an aesthetic I dislike, being a massive Fire Emblem fan)  the pixel art for both the maps AND in battle sprites is INSANE, and the combat mechanics add depth and complexity that really felt like a breath of fresh air. Amazingly, none of this ever changed. From the time I started my game to the point I finished it last night, I was engaged in everything the game had to offer. In particular, I greatly enjoyed the squad mechanics. I've heard that this is something that was inspired by Ogre Battle, but I unfortunately haven't played it so I don't know how true this is. Regardless, being able to fully customize squads however I chose was a HUGE draw of the game, and I loved the spectacle of large groups battling it out. There's nothing quite so satisfying as fully upgrading an entire squad of Paladins and Templars and other such units to ride in to battle with Diana, garbed in gold. I played on Warlord, which I feel was the right decision. I've played a ton of strategy games over the years and this challenged me just enough, without feeling like BS at times. This was aided by unit permadeath being on, and the squad system. Permadeath in something like Fire Emblem feels like such a make or break system, and while I like it, it can be annoying at times. Here, with the number of generic units you have, it feels more like a tactical decision when you decide to move on after losing some men. I also very much enjoyed the ability to choose different attack types, like aggressive or cautious. Feeling like I had the ability to give proper orders to my squads was CHOICE. Although I will say, even on Warlord, by the end of the game all I really chose was Aggressive or Force Surrender. Very rarely I chose cautious, but the majority of the time I was all blitz all day. Not inherently a bad thing, but it is something I noticed. I almost never targeted the leader or attacked normally. Something that surprised me the most about the game was just how invested I became in the story, and the world. It's hard to convey in a way that gives the positive vibe I intend, but the writing was "simple" in a way that was very satisfying. The story beats weren't anything out of left field in the best way possible. The characters make sense, the story makes sense, and the world makes sense, while still being interesting. And even having said that, there were still aspects of the world that were unique and cool, such as the Donnari (sp?) order and the nature of the paladins as an all female order. I won't go into it her for spoilers but that was COMPELLING justification for the design of the order, I loved it.There are only two negatives I can really bring against the game. One, is the dissonance between the art styles. The design of story cutscenes, with characters walking around and talking to each other, clashed with the design of the combat map and (in my opinion) with the character art as well. However taken on its own, I think the art and design of the story cutscenes was fine, and I'm unsure of how to balance those differences. It's just what stuck out to me. I also began to get slightly tired of loop near the very end of the game (chapters 26-30.) I feel like my squads largely were complete by chapter 25 or so, and I think that kinda killed my motivation to continue a little. Fortunately, I did continue, as I wanted to see the end of the story. I also appreciated some of the varied mission structure near the end of the game, that helped keep things fresh.Overall, I loved my time with the game. I want to thank Phil and the rest of the team from the bottom of my heart. A few years ago, my nerdly little heart never would have dared to dream of seeing an indie strategy rpg be released, let alone one of this quality. Yet here we are. I can't wait to see what else you guys do, I'll certainly be telling people about the game, and I think I may do a more in-depth analysis of the game as well in a video. You all are great, and I'm glad I got to experience what you've made. 😄

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this one.  And, here's a quick take.  I'll add more later too.Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga surely has taken some queues from some of its old school predecessors like Ogre Battle, Tactics Ogre, Advance Wars, Langrisser, and many others.  You get your standard grid based maps where you can capture strategic points for money and supplies.  Battle is turn based.  You move your troops first and then the enemy moves.  It's a bit different than most games in the genre in that you fight with squads which consist of an assortment of units.  You can configure these any way you like as well.  Battles remind me of Advance wars, with you on one side and the enemy on the other.  Each unit in the squad takes a turn until they're all done.  Combat is quick and there's a good amount of strategy.  After maps, you can recruit new troops, edit squads, and do some sort of relationship interaction.  Sort of like Fire Emblem.  Aside from the occasional grammatical issue, it's graphically serviceable (you cannot resize the window either).  I'm sure it shines on smaller screens.  Not my 5120x1440 monitor.  And, the same static pictures do show its indie roots.  Some pics with different expressions would have added a lot.  The music pretty good as well.Cons:Way too many clicks to do thingsSave are difficult to differentiate from one another.Right now, it's interesting and engaging.  The customization seems pretty deep and it has three skill trees for the commander (this is army-wide).  The more I play, the more I'll know, but so far it's enjoyable and I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Think Fire Emblem, but you can assign every leader a squad to complement their abilities.Symphony of War was a very fun experience. The squad-building element makes it feel fairly unique among tactical games and gives a lot of extra variety. There's a large number of units you can bundle together and experiment with, as well as a wide array of items and character perks to really let you customize your units. Finding a squad that works for its given role feels satisfying as heck! The difficulty level feels about right (with permadeath on feeling like a solid challenge and permadeath off feeling leisurely without becoming dull). The story even takes a few interesting turns.I have some knits I could pick: The portraits look really out of place with the rest of the game's art style; you get used to them, but these weirdly detailed renders sporting thousand-yard stares are a bit eerie for the first few chapters. I'm a little disppointed by the lack of direction you really have over your named character - them carrying your name of choice is more to make you feel affection toward them than to make them "your character". The 'tutorial' section, while better than whole wikis for many games, mis-explains the unit-typing a bit; it briefly explains that the most plentiful unit type will usually determine squad type and talks about priority, but fails to mention that light vs. heavy and cavalry vs. infantry are actually determined separately for this. You can, in fact, have a light cavalry squad with only a single light cavalry unit, provided it was a tie between light infantry and heavy cavalry broken by that light cavalry. And on unit gripes, in spite of the wide variety of units, there's only a single 'kind' of flying type, and several of its qualities make flying type squad design extremely limiting.And again, these are all knits. Most can be easily ignored or gotten used to.I highly recommend this game to fans of tactics rpgs. You will have a wonderful time. I'd also recommend it, though less-so, to fans of grand strategy - the squad-building element will probably delight you the same way hand-crafting an army composition would.

_childDocuments_.review: The closest indie game to the Fire Emblem series I have yet played. The game ended up being much better then I expected. The maps and challenges feel much more involved (in a good way) compared to typical FE games. Animations are fairly well made, tech tree makes sense (for the most part), and there are a ton of different accessories throughout the game. For an indie game, the story was entertaining and I look forward to sequels. A must buy for any FE fan!Gripes: I was not a big fan of the character art personally, sprite graphics were great. As mentioned in other reviews, the UI/UX needs some big improvements (playing it with a controller worked fairly well overall). One thing I'd love to see in the future is a list of units (irrespective of what squad) that you can sort on the different attributes and ability to favorite. For those of you who really enjoyed the squad management system, I highly recommend looking up Bahamut Lagoon

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a veritable diamond in the rough and doesn't get enough attention. If you're a fan of grid-based strategy games like Fire Emblem, Langrisser, etc you will feel right at home with this game. It  brings to the table some interesting new features like the ability to endlessly customize your various squads' composition; instead of being static units that never change, you have a real sense of progression as you fill out the 3x3 squad grids with interesting and varied unit types. It adds a whole new element to the strategy of preparation in addition to what you do on the battlefield. I never felt like the difficulty was unreasonable, and it ramped up at a modest pace as you gradually improve your team. I particularly loved that you can create squads from scratch from units you can buy, so you can have quite the large army - and the best part is they usually don't restrict you too badly in terms of max units - a lot of the mid to late game missions allow you to have 20 squads, which is enough to allow you to give everyone a chance to fight.The characters are interesting, the plot was surprisingly deep and easy enough to follow, the music is pleasant to listen to, and above all I always had the sense that this dev team cares about their game. A lot of love and care went into this, so if you're looking for something to scratch that grid-based strategy itch, give this game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Fire Emblem fan, this is an absolute buy. Don't expect polish or QOL features.  But the tactical combat and squad customization gameplay are delectable.  A lot of care was put into the missions in this game. They are challenging without being overwhelming, and never feel cheap. There are multiple difficulty levels, so if you want to play with permadeath on for your units, you can, but you aren't forced to. The story is fairly boilerplate, but the writing isn't bad. But again, if you buy this game, you're buying it for the super crunchy tactics gameplay, and the highly customizable squad mechanics. There are multiple unit types and you have complete freedom on how you arrange them in your squads. You can do highly specialized squads with the same unit types, or mixed units that have more utility and survivability. You can equip each squad with magic items that affect the whole squad, and each unit can have custom traits equipped that let you go even more granular. Over time, your ability to field more units per squad will increase, and there is a lot of min-maxing to optimize each squad.  It's great fun to spend a while getting your squads built up and then turn them loose on the battlefield to see the results. Downsides are the UI is utter garbage, clumsy, and annoying to use, but not so annoying it interferes with my overall enjoyment. No voice acting, mostly static character portraits, but that's what you get with a super indie like this. _childDocuments_.review: A solid recommendation for anyone who loved the Fire Emblem / Advance Wars / Yggdra Union games from the Gameboy Advance. If you are familiar with those games the Symphony of War will be instantly familiar and while they mostly nailed the game play there are a few issues which bring the experience down for me.Lacks a skirmish modeA minor gripe because the balancing is pretty good, but I would have liked a way to build and test unit combinations outside of story levels.Level designAbout level 10 the opponent starts fielding massive numbers of units, this slows turns down to a crawl, long enough to go make a barista style coffee and drink it. There is an option to speed up enemy animations but better design would have eliminated the need for it entirely.There is also an escort mission, the bad kind, the only kind, if there is anything the devs need to be ashamed of, this is it.Story and CharactersI liked almost all of the characters, most are relatable and occasionally funny. The story itself is okay, unfortunately the way the devs chose to tell the story could have been better. The cartoonish pixel graphics don't suit the tone and there are levels that are either impossible or brain numbingly simple to accommodate the story. I also felt many of the characters had very little presence or agency within the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game so far. Definitely inspired by Tactics Ogre, Advance wars, Heroes of Might and Magic. Alot of homages to the Tactical games and RPGS from the early 2000s to 2010s. But I feel the difficulty is lacking.Maybe Its because I'm only 10 missions in so i should update this when i get further in. Appreicate the thought of a turbo mode for those that like the feel of fast moving pieces. The Unit customisation and class system is a sick throwback to the Tactics series. The  visualizations of the units are very fluid. Really like the class variety and its synergy with the squad system.I'd reccomend playing this with  permadeath on. Alot of older tactics games had this mechanic as a mainstay, really lifts the experience but is challenging. Reccomended

_childDocuments_.review: If you've wished for another Ogre Battle style game, stop reading and buy now.  It scratches that itch like no other since the SNES ogre battle game. For the rest: It's a fun variation of a turn-based strategy game similar to Fire Emblem and other SNES/GBA/Genesis era games.  There's a bit more complexity with the ability to make squads of up to 9 individual units that fights as a group on the game map, and there is a lot of fun to be found with fiddling with these squads and then unleashing them on the enemies.  With a little bit of forethought, the game is fairly easy, and the story could have used a few editorial passes, but it's an indie company and you should make allowances for the story being a little on the weak side.  So far the Devs seem responsive, so I have hopes that there will be higher difficulty settings to add in updates, and I have hopes for future games in the formation fighting style.   As for this one, I'm pretty sure I'm going to play again with fun class restriction challenges like "Bros only" to restrict healing on the battle map and other gimmick runs.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Yes BUT.Without spoiling things, I am on Chapter 26, but I don't know if I can bring myself to beat this game. For the first ten hours, I was blown away. This is a great modernization of concepts used in Ogre Battle : March of the Black Queen and I love it for that. Each of the main characters felt interesting and developed (if tropey) and I didn't dislike any of them, which is rare. Combat felt rewarding and challenging without being obtuse.Halfway through the game everything sort of fell apart. Between not having access to critical resources I'd spent a long time cultivating for many missions in a row, the plot losing a lot of its charm and the character interactions beginning to feel like they were put on the back burner, and the fact that all of my units except my dragons were already maxed out, I slowly stopped having fun with the core gameplay loop. I trudged on well after I hit the wall hoping it would get better, but so close to the end I can't imagine anything is going to suddenly occur to make the game interesting again.But I do recommend it at the end of the day, because I had at least 25 hours of a great time. These are fixable issues. Fewer missions (I can think of a few in specific to cut), more late-stage units or greater resource milestones to getting them, more unit diversity in general, challenges that encourage you to build extra squads or shake up your squads more, etc. etc. I would be willing to check out the forthcoming DLC (which has more units!) to see if it alleviates some of these annoyances, and I'd especially be interested in another game from these same folks.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually like turned based combat. I don't usually like RPG maker games. This game however, took both genres and pushed them to their potential. I really enjoyed the game start to finish. The story was pretty good, I don't know why people think it's bad. It's not going to win any awards, but the plot was still enjoyable. My favorite part of this game was getting units, forming squads, leveling them up, giving them items to make them stronger, to make the strongest squads that you manage. Then playing with them, especially in arena mode (although arena did get kind of repetitive) was super fun. On the normal difficulty, the game isn't all that difficult, although there are some levels that can be tricky. But it didn't need to be difficult to be super fun. Warlord difficulty however, is a different story. If you want a challenging experience, then play it on that difficulty. People complaining how easy and normal are too easy, when they don't even try warlord kind of makes their arguments fall flat. This game is a super fun turn based strategy game with really addicting level up mechanics that can be enjoyed from the start of the game until the end. Highly recommend. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished this game, i can safely say that I've not felt this level of nostalgia in ages. It feels good to have played this game; to dive into its systems and truly learn how to run through it with well-executed strategies. I whittled away entire days figuring out how to properly pull off a mission, and even now i look back with new knowledge i'd bring to a new play through with zero hesitation.Symphony of War is a love letter to those of us who played Ogre Battle, Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics, pitting you, your army consisting of squads of customised units against a varied selection of enemies. Thinking things through pays off, and you can customise your difficulty from the get-go, meaning if you're new to this kind of game you're not facing a massive skill wall.I mentioned customised units: Well, let me paint you a picture of my roster: I had a squad of mages linked with bodyguards running around. Almost all of them were units i myself recruited from the market,  trained and turned into whichever class i wanted. Unit doesn't have something you want? There's items to customise them. From units, we go to squads: Each squad has 9 spaces. Only one unit doesn't take up 1 space, and that's the DRAGON. It takes up two. To continue: There's one leader, and up to 8 units accompanying said leader. As you'd expect, you've got a bevy of units, ranging from a large selection of staples a la knights, rogues, swordsmen and women, and paladins, to the ranged selection, with bows, early firearms and artillery cannons also making an appearance.Despite the presence of units that seem powerful, it's all balanced to an excellent degree: Cannons preparing to decimate your line? If you have a cavalry unit able to hit them, or a squad of rogues ready to flank them, you can decimate the cannon units without them firing a shot in return. Got a massive cavalry charge headed your way? Spears, magic and other means can be used to melt them.And melt them you will: The developers of this game did an amazing job with the effects, though some can be a bit underwhelming..which is the nature of the beast: You can't make everything as glamorous as a rain of fire, or an artillery barrage.When it comes to map variety, i am also pleased, though there is one gripe i have: As there are traits for fighting in multiple map types, i had hoped to encounter said types a bit more often than i actually did, making said traits not that useful. Otherwise, the inclusion of weather  (which can MESS UP your gunpowder units) and night time missions means you have to adapt to all manner of circumstances.The story is gloriously nineties, as many of us who've played this can attest: It feels like a plot you'd play on one of the older consoles, but doesn't feel outdated in the least, even if some of the twists can be seen a mile out.All in all, for a game i played for 50 hours at the time of writing this? I think it is money well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: So, not gonna lie its got some low budget Indie jank to it. The games got 4 different art styles, and two of them actually work together. IDK why, but one of them is just random RPG maker graphics for the cutscenes? It really takes you out of it, mostly because none of the gameplay looks like that at all. Overall, the visual STYLE just feels like an asset dump. That said, the sprite work for the actual gameplay as well as the combat animations is charming and works well, and the portraits are well done even if they kind of feel like they came from a mobile visual novel or something.The music is overall good but not terribly memorable. We have Hitoshi Sakimoto at home type stuff. The vast majority of it fits, every once in awhile there'll be a song that just doesn't match the mood of the story being told, but none of its bad and I USUALLY mute the music in games and just put on my own. I didn't with this one, so take from that what you will. It DOES do the annoying thing Shining Force does, where it'll switch to a different song for the attack animations and then restart the battle music over and over again, but it didn't bug me as much in this because at least the attack music is decent, and the animations are a bit longer. Sound FX all work well and aren't too jarring, and the small amount of voice work in combat all adds character.The writing and story is generally generic fantasy chosen one stuff with some grim dark political intrigue thrown on top. Its generally decent for what it is, despite some awkward dialogue. This is a game that wears its influences on its sleeve, and its very much "you got ogre battle in my fire emblem." The writing is exactly what you'd expect the writing in that game to be, and it does the job.The gameplay.... hoooboy. So, yah know how I mentioned "you got ogre battle in my fire emblem"? Yeah, turns out that was a really good idea. You get the grid based strategic unit control you've come to love from games like fire emblem and shining forces, along with branching class promotions and learnable traits for unit customization, but you're assembling them into synergistic parties of up to 9 (depending on the squad leaders leadership stat and some other skills and traits.) It works incredibly well and makes for extremely rewarding and deep gameplay. It doesn't hurt that the map design and enemy balance is also top notch, and they actually included setups and classes that punish some unit placements and combinations. It does feel a little stingy with the light orbs, but its also possible the devs just think I'm using WAY too many paladins, templar and mages. IDK.Sooooo... people like numbers I guess?Graphics: 5/10. They would be a solid 8/10 if they just got rid of the portraits and rpg maker cutscenes tho. To be clear, nothing that is here is bad art, there's just no art direction.Music: 7/10. Its pretty good, fits the mood.SFX: 8/10. They all do exactly what they should do.Story: 6/10. It does the job, its more good then it is bad but overall kinda meh.Gameplay: 9.5/10. There's some minor Indie style UX Jank holding it back from being perfect, but its damned good.Overall: 8/10. It's REALLY Fun. I'd bump it up if the graphics where more consistent and the plot was less generic and more engaging but still def worth playing. Would recommend, especially if you really dont care about graphics and are cool with it looking like an asset dump because of the wildly different art styles.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy strategy RPG games, there's a lot to like here in terms of gameplay.  The writing/dialogue (with the exception of the narration parts in between chapters) is on the weak(er) side, but the gameplay elements of creating your squads, leveling your units, promoting them to a higher tier class, and further customizing how your squad plays by using artifacts (items that confer stat bonuses/special abilities) is a really fun gameplay loop.I personally wasn't sure about the autobattling mechanics, as I came from strategy games where either your one unit was the one you controlled (Fire Emblem, Final Fantasy Tactics, etc), or where you had your squad and could equip items to the leader and designate each unit's attack (Disciples, etc).  I got used to it very quickly and the rest of the gameplay mechanics definitely outweigh any sense of a loss of control there.The bottom line is, if you're looking for an engrossing, well written story, you're probably going to be disappointed, but if you value the strategy and gameplay elements more, it's basically a must-buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This kinds of games are extremely my ♥♥♥♥, so I was interested on it when I saw a trailer for it a few years back, and now, after 100 hours of playtime I can say it is a fun game worth a try if you like the genre. 7/10.I dream of getting a game in this genre that nails everything I want and while this game is not it, it did give me some glances at it. But for every thing it does right, it kinda fumbles another. -I like that there's 3 tiers of classes for units, but the pacing in changing between them is all over the place.-I like the squad system for the most part, but having 2 rounds of attack per combat just makes everything too volatile, you either destroy your opponent or they destroy you in most cases, which then makes permadeath a very frustrating option to go with (and one I believe should be a must in this kinds of games)-I like certain parts of the story like the middle part (won't say more for spoilers) but there's also a lot that is predictable and kind of badly presented, like what happens before the final boss.-I like the DLC in general, but last map is incredibly unbalanced because of the DLC units it has, which are also pretty unbalanced both for and against you. -I like the support system and convos, but just like every other game in this genre, it doesn't go hard enough on them to really make them feel organic and make the characters bloom. -I like how many options of units you have by the end of the game, but I wish there was more detailed information in the tutorial manual.I could go on, but essentially, it's a messy rollercoaster ride. Would love to see a sequel or something that learns from this one and just goes hard on fixing the problems it has. Oh, and the Visual Update is great, good job guys.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is solid and has good mechanics.  Units are well-balanced with only a few being too weak and a few being too strong.  This is pretty surprising given how many classes there are.  Squad management is a fun and rewarding experience.  One of the best turn based strategy games to come out in a long while.Some complaints:The game is a bit too easy and a bit too forgiving.  I think the change to retain upgrade materials from dead units on the permadeath mode was a mistake.  Story squad leaders being immune to permadeath means that you don't have to care if they live or die.  The consequences of losing a unit is actually pretty minimal, and zero if a story unit dies in combat as they will just come back for the next chapter.  It would be nice if story units that fall in combat were removed from your roster like generics on permadeath so I'm not incentivized to treat them like immortal meat shields.  The game needs a harder difficulty and some updates to the AI.  For example, cavalry squads aren't abusing their movement to reposition after attacking the player.  Archery squads that use warbows and samurai will only attack at 3 range meaning they lose all the potential damage from the samurais which can attack at 1-2 range.  I've also seen some squads with a single cannon choose to attack at 3 range with the lone cannon instead of at 1 range which would have used 8 melee units + the lone cannon.The story is serviceable.  Nothing special, but it isn't bad.  It provides context for the events that are occurring on the screen which is good enough.  My only complaint storywise is that quite a few chapters are thrown away for the sake of the story.  For example, a series of chapters removes the squad management and shop mechanics.  Because you don't have access to squad management or the shops, the difficulty is heavily toned down turning these few chapters into a snooze fest.  There are a couple other instances of chapters sacrificing gameplay for the sake of the story.I think the arenas were a mistake.  When you add arenas or a way to grind in turn based strategy games, they tend to just be abused to break the game.  It happens in Fire Emblem, and you can do it here as well.  I know they were slightly nerfed, but I don't know if it was anything more than that they cannot be indefinitely spammed in the endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: Very very very fun game.  Its gameplay is absolutely a blast.  Its not the deepest strategy game, but it has good breadth (lots of fun and distinct classes and unit combinations).  The maps are decent, not too memorable but not frustrating either. I also appreciate it doesn't unit cap you as harshly as Fire Emblem or Unicorn Overlord does.  It has trait and artifact options that can lead to some really interesting tactics.The story is alright if a little too straightforward.  The characters are alright too, the dialogue isn't corny but its rather uninvolved at the same time.  The music was good (kinda reminded me of Fire Emblem Awakening), the art was... interesting.  The new character models are nice, the battle sprites are really well done, but the old models and the RPG moments are rather... awkward to put it nicely.Overall its a great game when it comes on sale.  8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say, the first thing that attracted me to this game was the pixel art.  I absolutely loved the look and style of the old Ogre Battle games, and this matched it up well.  Just watching all the unit animations was a joy for me and I never got sick of it.  The story is a fairly straightforward jrpg affair, the main characters have enough optional interactions to flesh them out, but they don't get very deep in most cases.  It does the job well enough and I had fun, but I do feel like some of the character interactions needed to be a little better rounded out.  The relationship mechanic is extremely simple, and is really just a matter of deciding who of the bachelor/bachelorettes you want to pair up.  All in all, I enjoyed the story and characters well enough, but the pixel art and gameplay are what really make the game.The gameplay can differ depending on the difficulty you choose.  There's an option for perma-death for any soldier who dies in battle, which would have made the game more difficult, but I'm not a masochist.  Looking at the discussion boards and you'll find challenge seekers who still find hard mode and perma-death too easy, but I went with normal difficulty and no perma-death.  It started with a bit of a challenge but was definitely a cakewalk at the end since all my superpowered units were always surviving.  I always appreciate steady power growth and love to feel like a badass at the end, so it worked out well for me.  You'll need some decent tactics to start out but about halfway through you get additional options that turn tactics into "don't do anything extremely stupid and you'll be fine."  Your army layout is mostly going to depend on your tech tree advancement at the beginning and whatever units you can scrape together, so you may go firearms or magic dependent, but at the end you'll have more than enough tech advancement to get everything unlocked. The one thing I might gripe about it is the army organization ui.  It's fairly counter-intuitive and took some time to get used to.  It's not terrible, but considering I spent the majority of my time organizing my army, I would have appreciated some better options for display. Like an option to view a list of all units so I didn't have to go through 3 menu options to go from overall army, to squad, to individual unit each time I wanted to use an item or upgrade.  All the same I enjoyed fine-tuning my army so it didn't impede my enjoyment of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I probably won't finish the game. I might not actually play it again. It's absolutely great at what it attempts to do, and I do really like the game. It's just not different enough for me to care. I've played too many tactical rpgs. It's still worth playing though if you just want more examples of a good tactical rpg.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent strategy game. I lost myself for hours and hours trying to perfect my squads. Definitely would recommend to purchase. Best $14 I've spent in a long while. _childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I would have to agree with many of the really positive reviews of this game. I have about 25 hours in the game so far and I have thoroughly enjoyed the ability to customize both each squad as well as the various items the game has to offer to further allow you to build things the way you want. The upgrade system is very good and you do have to make some choices, especially early on, on how to spend your limited resources.I would also agree that the interface can be cumbersome at times, but honestly it has not taken away from my enjoyment of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game assuming that it would lack polish, it was the battle system and unit customization that sold it for me. The soundtrack is surprisingly good too. This game has a lot of potential. I consider my purchase to be an investment, to encourage Dancing Dragon Games to create a better sequel, with improved graphics, story and system.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I still think the story was a touch generic. I could kind of tell where most of the plot twists toward the end were going. One or two surprised me, but the game's story was at its peak toward the climax in the middle. I was on the edge of my seat for all of that.Gameplay-wise it was awesome. I've only ever played a couple of Fire Emblem games, but fans of that series are going to adore this.Aside from the rather generic storyline (in my opinion), the only other thing that felt a little weak were the social aspects. Friendships and romances developing between the characters were very brief and didn't really feel like they mattered save for a few words spoken in some cutscenes. It wasn't enough to make me dislike the time I spent with the game, but I was hoping for a little more.Overall, loved this game. Might play the DLC one day!
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: An fantastic throwback to the Tactical RPGs of the golden era. At the most base level, I could describe this as Fire Emblem meets Battle Chess, but it definitely gave me overarching vibes of games like FFT and Tactics Ogre. The amazing pixel art gives it that nostalgic feel, but with little of the clunkiness that plagued early TRPGs. The soundtrack was good, and of course the gameplay was great.Instead of just deploying characters, you deploy squads, each with multiple units (up to 9 by the end of the game). You can tweak each unit, promote them, teach them skills, and equip the units with gear that can drastically change how they perform in combat.A great love letter to the classics and a testament of what is possible in RPG Maker. Kudos to the devs, I had a blast playing this!
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of turn based RPG games with good story, this is a great game to try out. I have played many fire emblem games and others like it. This is a great spin on tactic RPG Style. Highly recommend this game so far being 9 chapters. The game does have some minor things it can improve on as the menu system can be a bit annoying sometimes. Other than that the game play is great. Making unique squads are neat and you can do a fair bit of tinkering. For 20 bucks this is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: The good: The game play is phenomenal. Fire Emblem on steroids. It's really freaking good, and enough to justify getting the game all by itself. If you're a fan of the genre, of this kind of game play, you will like the way this game plays.The bad: The story is... not great. It certainly exists, but that's about all I can say for it. It's incoherent at times, with a reliance on unexplained deus ex machina. It's possible that a sequel will fill in some of the gaps, but right now, as a standalone title, I spent far too much time wondering what the heck the characters were thinking.The ugly: Remember how I said the game play was phenomenal? Well... there's a catch. It IS phenomenal, but only when the story isn't stepping in to mess it up. The entire point of this genre is to get attached to your units, but how am I supposed to do that when every few missions half my party vanishes due to plot, new characters I've never met show up, and I have to rebuild my army all over again? This does eventually settle down, but for the first half of the game, expect units to come and go almost at random. INCLUDING YOUR MAIN CHARACTER UNIT. Which admittedly makes sense, given the plot, but personally I can't view that decision as anything other than a bad idea.The mildly warty: There is virtually no game play that isn't part of the story. Yes, there's the arena missions, but those are attached to the story by way of needing specific items found in the campaign to do a mission. Verdict: This is an amazing game let down and even sabotaged at times by a below-average story. Definitely worth playing, because yes, it is that good, but temper your expectations accordingly. And, unfortunately, there's nothing you can do with the game that doesn't involve the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Indie games have really grown on me over the last few years. As an older gamer who was there when the Nintendo first came on to the scene, I have seen alot of games, and alot of franchises come into glory and fade to dust. I am pretty picky, though. I tend to only play traditional RPGS (eastern and western) Strategy games, and tactical RPGs. Mainly turn based, but I make exceptions here and there. So understanding what I like is a context one should take into consideration with any recommendation I make. I am biased, and I dont deny it.With indie games, I understand that developers usually work within their means with limited assets and resources. I take that into consideration when I do or dont choose to give them a shot. Once in a while, you strike gold though, mining for a great game. You find developers who take those limited resources and assets and forge them into a true work of art. I can point to a handful of such titles among 100s of them. And now one more has joined that list.Symphony of war could be called a "love letter" to, and spiritual successor of a few titles. Taking the idea's of classics and melding them together perfectly, while side stepping alot of the faults those classic games may have had. This title wasnt crafted by commercial developers out for a cash grab. Its a creation you can tell was made by fans, for the fans.I went into this blind, going on a few screen shots, and I think that is the best way to experience a game. So I will keep this short and just say this- If you are a fan of ANY of these classic games-Ogre BattleDark WizardFire EmblemShining Force (originals)Tactics OgreFinal Fantasy TacticsVandal HeartsThen this game was made with YOU in mind.  This is a great game, and what is more...Play 10 or so hours into it and then ask yourselves what such a team could do with expanded assets and resources? VERY MUCH the kind of developers the gaming scene has been lacking. Indie developers have more heart in their creations than do commercial developers imo. THESE are the titles we should be supporting. These are the kinds of people we want running the industry and crafting our hobby. By backing developers like the creators of Symphony of War, we make the future of gaming a bit more secure. Yes, the game is that good. Try it and youll see :)
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game for $20.The writing is sub par. It's a bummer that there aren't more special unit types.  But if you are a fan of Fire emblem, Tactics ogre, Ogre Battle 64, or Final Fantasy Tactics, then this game is a must have buy.  I had a blast with this game.  I started over around chapter 10 once i understood fully how unit affinity types worked but the campaign itself was a solid 35 hours ish.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Strongly reminds me of the Fire Emblem games for the GBA. Story is very interesting, although with some childish dialouges here and there, but could be due to the localization. Troopmanagement outside combat is atrocious, every single action like moving units, show their stats, change their classes, or use an item has its own submenu. You're forced to constantly switch between those menus to customize a single unit which you can have up to 9 in one troop instead of making changes on the fly.Other than that, combat in engaging and keeps you motivated even after 45+ Hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, it's okay.  I've gotten my money's worth and I would recommend buying it on sale.  The story isn't the greatest.  Overall, it is not a difficult game.  In fact, even on the hardest difficulty, it is not hard at all unless you are playing with permadeath and/or going for only S ranks.  Without permadeath, S ranks are still pretty easy.It is a very linear game.  The squad system is okay but you pretty quickly realize which squads are worth making so there isn't much to it.  The formations also don't really matter because your squad is always facing front in battle so unless you are facing assassins, your front line guys always need to be tanks and that's about it.  The game would be more complex with directional attacks added in.  I also found the grand strategy layer to be lacking.  There is no choices so the game is pretty much linear reducing replayability.  I'd really like if the map layer actually let me make strategic decisions.Overall, I'd still recommend it.  It's a good first game.  They can and definitely should make a lot of improvements for any sequels though.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on a whim because I wanted something turn based and tactical. I did NOT expect what is probably my leader in the clubhouse (as of now) for GOTY 2022. If you are at all into tactical combat and management of squads to use in combat, this is a no-brainer.Pros:-Tons of ways to customize your army-Story is better and more engaging than I expected-Super responsive developers (constantly talking to people in Discord)-Satisfying combat (fights are autobattled but you can manage around this to an extent and be smart about the fights)Cons:-Clunky UI and navigation. This is by far the biggest con. If you forget something, want to look something up, remember how your squad is made up, etc, you are constantly going into and out of menus.-Some things need better explanations-Even though the story is engaging, most of it was fairly predictablePlaying through the main story will take 30-ish hours or so. _childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to finish the game before leaving a review. It's a great game, not quite as good as a classic like Fire Emblem 4, but not far off and with many quality of life tweaks to make it a pleasure to play rather than a chore. The basic system if great, just the right amount of micro-managing and not clunky in any way. There's a nice progression from foot soldier up to dragon rider and many choices from archers, melee units, mages, etc.The story isn't amazing, but it's not awful and it's just the right length. Maybe one or two extra side missions would have been nice, but I definitely felt like I had reached the end about the right time. Some of the maps were a little "samey", but the game is fun enough for that to not really matter much. It would have been nice to have a few "infiltration" missions and maybe some different objectives more often than "kill everything" or "claim the castle".Tactics-wise is also good, but could do with a few tweaks to make it perfect. I never felt like there was any real equivalent of a weapons triangle. Sure, some damage types worked better on certain units than others, but it never felt enough of a difference. Also, most formations boil down to improving loyalty of the troops and the leadership of the leader to add to the number of troops allowed. Seeing the leadership score go up for a non-leader troop seemed a waste most of the time, but this is what came up most often. Also, the items system was a bit lacking, but these are minor grumbles really.I guess the only thing I really didn't like was some of the character portraits, actually almost all of them. They just didn't fit the art-style of the rest of the game particularly well. Lots of primary colours in big swathes with little shading or artistry. Maybe they would have worked better if they had been shrunk down to hide their very simple and basic style?I would definitely play a sequel, or even an expansion. This is the best new tactics game I have played in years, and I've played a lot of them!

_childDocuments_.review: I just did a first time run-through, not really knowing what to expect. So here are my first impressions and thoughts after beating the game on the medium difficulty.So lets start with the story. I liked the simplicity of it, everything done was classic war fantasy. The relationships were straight forward and pleasant enough. I do wish there were more avenues to explore each character. For example, I thought the side battle that involved one of the main characters was very cool - I wish there had been more of that. It would have improved the attachment to the characters and added another battle to do. I felt the characters were like-able overall, but as I said, I wish there was...more depth added. As for the battles, I felt they were the best part of the game by far. They were challenging enough, but not overly so in the medium difficulty. I hardly needed to micromanage the resources. I imagine on the hardest difficulty, I would actually have to calculate every move. Managing the army was also easy, but there were times when I wish I could do more battles. BUT I understand why this is the case, it would be very easy to over prepare the later stages and take the challenge out of the game. I feel the game has some replay-ability. I look forward to seeing if the choices in the beginning mean anything, and I also will definitely play the game on the hardest difficulty to test myself. Hope there's a sequel! Good job.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, lets write a real review here shall we?  13 hours played, which is the game beat.  There only really seems to be one path, so replay value is rather low.  That said it was a rather entertaining 13 hours though the story near the end seemed to get a bit fuzzy.It plays a lot like a mix of Ogre Battle and Langrisser Hikari.  The squad formations, promotions, battles, all clearly heavily Ogre Battle influenced but it doesn't have the real-time over world mapping, giving it a bit more of a Langrisser feel when actually in the Scenarios.If it was a $60 game I would be rather disappointed in the length and lack of branching, but for a $15 game it was a great way to spend a weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game if you are into games such as fire emblem.  There is quite a bit of customization you can do with your units, picking different troop types to add to a unit, giving them gear (which provides bonuses to the entire unit) and giving them additional traits. _childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Fire Emblem is probably my favourite franchise.  Some I love, some I don't but to date, I have never liked an FE alike.I've only just started this but my first impressions usually last with games.1.  Unlike 99% of games out there, the characters and dialogue aren't annoying.2.  Great music.  OST is one of the biggest selling points for me in a game.3.  The story has already shown signs of movement after just 1 map.4.  The mechanics work and it plays nicely.5.  It's nice to have a squad that mixes up the way you have to think about how you play.  I have seen this implemented badly in other games where I had to move every single character in each squad, so to have the team move as a whole, works well.  6.  The game looks really nice.  It's an RPG maker style game and feels like a fusion of old Fire Emblem and Ara Fell.  The portraits are nice too.I don't care much about individual elements in games.  They just need to work together and it feels like they do here.  It all seems to gel together to make a very polished overall feel that makes me want to play on.  Like I say, just first impressions but can't fault it so far and it looks very promising.  I'm looking forward to carrying on with this.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game on sale and I have to say that I have had a great time playing it.  It has everything I like about fire emblem but extends it with a full squad consisting of 5-9 units depending on what units you put into it. The class systems are simple, and each class is very interesting. From melee, to magic, to cavalry every unit performs really well. The tech trees make your units go from normal to really really good. I've put over 20 hours into this game so far and have been having a great time with it. If you want to watch gameplay you can check out my youtube channel under fatalis entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: I had the pleasure of being invited to play this during the closed beta phase, and luckily I was able to finish it on medium difficulty. Gotta admit, I was EAGER to see this publically released and throw money at it as soon as possible XDI've always been a huge fan of RPGs, including SRPGs. While I love titles like Final Fantasy Tactics and the Fire Emblem series, at the same time it's become a bit stale to me to see every other indie SRPG thread the same ground. Symphony of War however plays more similarly to Ogre Battle and Soul Nomad, a style of gameplay I rarely see, and overall inproves on the precedent set by those games too. Battles are REALLY fun and can be REALLY challenging, but at the same time it's intuitive enough that the player can learn how it works by practice. Heck, I think half my playtime was spent on the Squad screen, assigning groups, improving units and adding artifacts, creating squads just became part of the fun to me!As for the story, it does seem like a throwback to the "Chosen One" narrative, similar to older Fire Emblem titles... At first. The game does great at setting up the world and plot before kicking off the real meat of the story with some amazing twists. I REALLY loved the midpoint of the story, without mentioning spoilers it makes for fantastic story drama and offers some of the best emotional payoffs. The characters are charming too, and while the gameplay limitations mean that not all of them get many chances to shine, the Support system helps mitigate this, and may even reveal some interesting, heartwarming or funny depths of each character's personality (shipping too!). Ultimately, yes, it IS a story about Good vs Evil, with the tone of an Heroic Fantasy story, but it does a great job at making it its own thing, building over the bases of the genre and creating a lore-rich world with likeable characters.Overall I REALLY recommend this game, especially to RPG / SRPG fans who may be wanting something different from the FFT / FE / Advance Wars experience. It offers something different, inspired but at the same time unique, and I really hope this game becomes the starting point of a new series or an inspiration to future SRPGs.P.S: You may find me in the game as a cute Witch unit ;) Pls put me in the same team as Diana, Stefan or Lysander, I love them <3
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a treat.  I've been gaming for 33 or so years.  This game reminds me of Ogre Battle Tactics from the PS1.  If you have any interest in games such as Fire Emblem or Tactics Ogre this game will not disappoint.  Anything this dev releases I will buy without question.  Not only that but they are even adding more content to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: This game has scratched every itch I've had for a Fire Emblem type tactics game. But it's not "just another Fire Emblem." It actually adds new and interesting mechanics. Instead of just having a unit on the field, each "unit" is actually a squad of units that you get to assemble and customize as you see fit. Could be a squad of nothing but archers. Or maybe you're more into mixed unit tactics.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: this is a 7/10 tactics game with a lot of promise, but ultimately it underdelivers. first off is the lack of polish- the game was clearly made in rpg maker and the menus are a mess, particularly when deploying units. as far as the game goes, there are 30 chapters and the first 12 are very strong both gameplay and story-wise. however, the story goes off the rails for the end of act 2 and beginning of act 3 until giving a fairly decent ending.gameplay-wise, the mid and end game are terrible. the computer AI isn't good, and the game compensates by mobbing you with 2-4x times the number of units. worst is that units will routinely spawn partway through the mission, and in a few instances infinitely. this doesn't feel like good design, it feels cheap. the final boss in particular was terrible as it felt more of a stat-check vs. a tactical battle.still, there is fun to be had for at least half the game. it's worth checking out, but keep your expectations low.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent tactical RPG. The battles are consistently fun and engaging, the squad management and class progression is well done and enjoyable, and the overall game feels really good. The story is a little vanilla and some of the dialogue feels a little "off", but is pretty good as a complete package. Combine a decent story with excellent gameplay and you're got a great game.TL;DR - If you like Tactical RPGs, you're going to love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended! While there are quite a few Fire Emblem-like games on the market, it's a pity that I haven't seen any Orge Battle-like games for years... So if you are a SRPG fan, Symphony of War is a great game to try. Hopefully the development team will continue to make fan games like this. Some recommendations for the dev team:1. Overall art work could be better;2. more unique units, polish the combat system, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: Deeper than fire emblem.  Each unit is a squad of characters.  There are lots of units so you will spend less time worrying about RNG. Some units will be better some worse.  If you play max difficulty with permadeath then be ready to replace some expendables unless you like save scrum.  But the game is pretty generous later with handing out tier 2 units with a tech tree upgrade.  Even on the highest difficulty the game seems to get easier as you progress if you start to get ahead of the difficulty curve.  Once you are able to force lots of the enemy to surrender you get more faction level and money, unlocking more upgrades and recruit better units allowing you to get even more surrenders the next map... it snowballs pretty quick.The power system also contributes to the snowball nature of the fight.  Deal more damage charge up (some) powers then use those to snowball harder.Overall it is pretty fun, but the difficulty curve needs adjustment.  I'm 2/3 through the campaign but have already unlocked all the tech tree and maxed out my squads.
_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.name: Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. To be honest, from the title and the cover art, I almost bounced off this game, but I'm glad I stuck around.To me, the core but that separates this from other turn-based tactics games is that it adds just the right amount of crunchiness and customization. That each "unit" on the battlefield is actually a set of units that you choose adds a ton. In some ways it almost feels like a deck builder, constructing the right combination of units to fill the specific niches on the battlefield. And there's even more depth for those who want it, with individual unit affinities, traits, and stat bonuses, but I never felt that I HAD to interact with those systems if I didn't want to.There are some issues; I wish there was a way to filter across all units, including those in squads, I'm not crazy about the artwork even though I'm generally a pixel art fan, the last few missions have too many units involved and can be a bit of a slog, but none of those seriously detract from the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Am amazing homage to (among other things) the outstanding GBA Fire Emblems, with a greater focus on force customization and preparing the right squads for the right situation. Good buy at full price, no brainer on sale. The good: satisfying force customization and gameplay, fun little characters, and a broad and highly flexible class change and promotion system that lets you bring the right tools to solve the game’s tactical problems. The bad: nothing, honestly. Outstanding turn based strategy game. The details:1. Great little cheesy fantasy plot that meshes well with the gameplay. It’s good fun, and a solid backdrop to the various missions. I would characterize it  as a YA fantasy novel. 2. Awesome focus on squad building and customization. The main characters come with examples of how to put squads together, but most of the missions have space to bring more squads that you can build up from minor/filler soldiers. Taking advantage of this can help fill gaps in your army, or let you load up on certain strengths, e.g. a cavalry heavy force, or extra heavy infantry squads to rank the enemy. There’s decent odds you’ll want to tweak your squads mission to mission, depending on the situation. 3. Decent variety in maps and missions, with the environment and enemy types demanding some thoughtful deployment and use of your forces.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid 6.5 out of 10 game. The bones are here for a really fun time, and leveling up and gearing out units is a real blast.Where this game suffers is with the most boring story trope and the general feeling that what you do doesn't matter. Characters are shallow copy pastes from every generic old DnD campaign: Chosen one has to defeat the evil Chancellor. Get thrown in prison and escape? Turns out you still have all the gear you went in and all the units you went in with too so there doesn't feel like any connection between the story and actual game play. Unit gets wiped out in combat? They return next mission with no negative effects so there is no reason to play conservatively.Also enemy AI only does one thing: attacks your lowest HP unit in range. This behavior is so predictable that you either end up having to ignore it or exploit it, but the AI will literally NEVER do anything else.The unit sprawl is a bit of a turn off too, there's no real reason to not max out the number of units you can deploy which ends up being quite a lot of sprites to move each turn. There never feels like high stakes outnumbered element to this game, at worst you might not move a unit far enough to get a bonus objective in time or something.With those MAJOR negatives this is still a thumbs up because the care mechanics are just fun, and the between missions unit adjusting scratches the strategy itch. Relationship mechanics feel like a waste of time though, mostly just because the characters are all so boring.If someone can do a full conversion mod for this game giving it a real story and more "impactful" results of your game choices this could be a really great turn based strategy tactics game. Right now it feels like the most vanilla of vanilla templates pasted over a terrific game engine.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys the Fire Emblem and Ogre Battle games, this game is amazing. Squad building and challenge missions altogether with the amazing sprite work of the classes/units makes this game very pleasing to play/look at. The devs did an great job putting this together and I'm very grateful that a game like this was made with passion.The game is a love letter to FE and OB franchises and the movement/battle system is heavily inspired by them (and I'm glad that movement isn't done like OB, so yay!)The RNG aspect of which unit will attack which unit --- this might sound bad to someone, but I always loved RNG in games like this, it creates suspense and tension. Also, it's not entirely RNG, there's a lot of player influence as soon as you figure out and understand which unit attacks which row/line and the cover mechanic for heavy units, also not to mention ambush, shock and daze/stun effects from siren/sorceress.There are a lot of classes (which is a giant plus in my book) with different movement types, unique skills and attack patterns, you just need to dive into the game and learn them.Squad building is my favorite thing here. Multiple choices for everything. You want a full mage squad - you got it, but here's 5 movement and you're very susceptible to enemy engages. Want a full cavalry squad - here's a lot of movement but good luck pushing through the heavy enemy front lines, also here's canto so have fun. And there's many, many more. Overworld positioning is also very important. Hills, forests, walls all come into play for ranged units and light infantry which make them have a lot of impact against certain units. I've never used Ranger class, I would always choose Assassins over them, until I saw the power of  the Precise Shot ability and the burst that comes with it is what makes this class amazing. Pair that with a forest tile and these units will dodge almost everything. Very nice addition and the overall concept of "light infantry" is great!There are a lot more mechanics like morale, surrender, objective capturing, leadership, etc... but I won't "spoil" everything so that the new players can learn this themselves.For storytelling, I have really high standards and if it doesn't touch my soul then I consider it meh overall and there are only a few games where I really love the storytelling. That being said, the story is ok, it's not great but it's not bad as well. I won't talk about it because I need to go into detail and it will contain spoilers. But, what I will mention is that I love when the story interferes as events in chapters, don't want to spoil them, but there were some great moments and in one instance a very terrifying moment when you get overwhelmed... great chapter :)I beat the game on normal difficulty. Early and late game were the most interesting, mid game was very easy and one or two chapters were just straightforward (do this in an obvious certain order to win), these were the weakest chapters imo.I plan to play again on hard as soon as the game receives an update for unit name changing :)tl;dr --- Awesome game, go play it ! :)
