_childDocuments_.review: It's a very pretty game but it's so short. I'm glad that I got it through a bundle because it's not worth the price they're asking for it. I understand that people need to make money to produce niche games like this but you need to make it worth it to your audience. What I was hoping for was a game that dealt with trying to find hard to find ingredients for their food and dealing with trying to use alternatives in cooking. Raising a kid in Canada during the early nineties.   I know that the devs wanted to leave the game on a high note but I was more frustrated and left wanting more than they were willing to give. Relying on context clues to figure out the Tamil words and some of the plot points in the game made me annoyed more than intrigued. I don't mind googling to learn new things but sometimes, it doesn't work. It's not fun to be left in the dark to stumble along while everyone else in the know knows what's going on. I can understand the choice that the devs made but they should have thought about who their audience was before doing that. My question Is their audience the people that share their culture or is it everyone who speaks English looking for the next cozy game? My opinion is that the devs are trying to appeal to both but fail on both accounts due to lacking a Tamil language Option for the game and leaving English speakers in the dark.  I'll admit that I loved the art stye of the game and learning about Tamil cooking was interesting enough that I might try to make some of these at home if I can.  I don't really have anything else to say besides, get it on sale when it's at 75 percent or so. Or get it through a bundle like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art, beautiful story, short but fun gameplay. I love this game and what it stand for. I highly recommend the experience of playing this one. Played on the steam deck and it runned fine. It is more of a mouse game than controler, imo, so the control were a bit tideous, but not like unplayable.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: As an immigrant who moved to America with her parents, I felt so much in the shoes of Kavin. Everything from the lunch, to the translating on the phone. I almost felt furious at Kavin because I had felt and almost done what he had. But I see my parents almost every weekend, I only speak our language with them and my family, and I do everything to cook our recipes. This game has me choked up and I'm so glad I finally got to play it. I wish I could bring this game to the masses, this is something someone needs to feel. The visuals and game play were also so gorgeous and fun! I can't wait to try these recipes too!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could say I loved this game, but to me the gameplay and story fell short, specially for the price. I understand that creating a game atkes a lot of effort and time but an hour long seems too short for the price. I feel like the gameplay was a tad too simple and straightforward, for a puzzle game it was way to easy to solve the recipes.On the story side I fount it moving and beautiful but it needed more "capters", even then it still made me tear up.Every other aspect of the game is beautiful from the visual art to the sound design, it creates a very complelling style that  aids the story perfectly.I still support this game because you can tell the love the creators put into it. I hope they continue to build on this idea.PS:this game made me hungy even when I had just eaten dinner.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: its a great game - it has a really good story and the actual gameplay is really fun too.it is really short, you can honestly finish it in like an hour and a half - i'm glad that the story doesn't overstay its welcome and is pretty concise without feeling rushed but it also means that maybe id suggest buying this game on a sale or as part of a bundle if you are tryna get more gameplay for ur money8/10 game fr
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot express how much I love this game. It's artistic graphics are refreshing and the gameplay, while simple, is still challenging. The storytelling is clear and touching. I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a game that is more story than game, enjoys game artwork, and loves cooking. Maybe especially if you love cooking because that will help a lot when it comes to gameplay.  The only con I have is that my wife and I were able to sit down and play this game together in one sitting. I could stand for it to be a lot longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful storytelling, linking food to memories and leaving simple clues to piece it all together in a natural conversation later down the line. The art was lovely as well, great uses of colour to make those food pop as much as the music! A down to earth experience for immigrants living in Canada and being first generation Canadian which resonated with me. Despite the difference in culture, I felt similarities when balancing traditional culture,  blending into Canadian values with a dash of parenthood. Thank you for the wonderful experience and I look forward to the cookbook!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The only game where you'll end up crying over spilled curry—and loving every minute of it. Imagine trying to cook your mom's best dishes from memory, but with a narrative twist that tugs at your heartstrings harder than a sad Bollywood movie. This game is part cooking sim, part emotional rollercoaster, and 100% a recipe for success. Just be warned: playing Venba will leave you hungry, homesick, and possibly Googling 'how to cook dosa' at 2 a.m. If you think food brings people together, wait until this game whips up your feelings into a perfectly spiced emotional stew!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I've been waiting ages for this game... and it did not disappoint ! As someone who loves to cook... this game is a work of art. I could smell some of the dishes, I swear. And the sound effects ! The sizzling and steam are auditory gems, and I really loved how Venba jingled when she moved, it's such a heartfelt detail. The story itself is one of cultural identity and I think it's portrayed masterfully, in a way that's relatable but also true to the Tamil culture, without alienating players who aren't familiar with it. All I know is I'd love it if I had a Venba to show me how to cook these dishes.A lot of love, sweat, tears, and good food went into this game and it shows. Absolutely outstanding, my compliments to the chef(s)!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking through the reviews to figure out you should buy this game, my answer is to do it without hesitation; buy it at full price if you can! I can tell that the devs put a LOT of love and care into this game, and it really shows.Initially I bought this game after finding out about it through TikTok, thinking it was a cooking-based puzzle game.Full honesty, there isn't as much cooking as I expected, but I still learned a decent bit about South Indian cuisine nonetheless. The real charm of Venba comes from the story the game tells, and how it uses the act of cooking to give insight into the experience of being an immigrant in a foreign country, mainly the struggle between keeping your culture alive and adapting to your new home.I won't spoil too much about the specific events in the story itself, the circumstances surrounding my family are incredibly similar to the one presented in Venba, and by the end of the story I was holding back tears. Is the story itself not that long? Yes, but the fact that the story itself was so poignant in a short amount of time is a testament to the ability of the devs, and I would give anything to play this again for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a review for a game before this. I also haven't heard of Venba before I purchased it randomly when looking for a casual cooking game. I saw the visuals and skimmed a few reviews and figured, why not? First off, the visuals are stunning. Secondly, the soundtrack is done so well. But most of all, the story is what really got me. I am not Indian but I am a first generation Vietnamese American and this story really touched me. I felt seen when playing this game. I was so moved that i actually called my own mother on the phone after that one scene (iykyk). By the end of the game I shed a few tears. Please support Venba, it was a beautiful and emotionally moving game! Short and sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who had a big wet sob during Domee Shi's "Bao," I found that this also fell firmly into the camp of "stories about about food and love and Canada and the Asian diaspora and being a mom and having a son and navigating culture and identity." Which is to say: get out the tissues. Venba is a beautiful little game - in writing, in visuals, in sounds and music. I've done a couple of rounds now, and during each playthrough I catch something new to admire, whether it's in a frenzy of gameplay in the kitchen and a lingering pause, a practiced hand versus a shaky pour of oil, or a single word highlighted in a line of dialogue. In short, I've had a wonderful time with Venba. And I get the sense that I'll be returning again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It packs an emotional punch, but it is a very short game, I spent about 1.5hrs for a single playthrough. It is also much more story than actual gameplay. But a fantastic story at that. It knows exactly which heartstrings to tug at.Playing on the deck was all touchscreen interface.Because I was using touch input on the Deck, I did get stuck in some of the content that unlocks after the game is complete, but it was not a big deal.The length is a little disappointing, the story, the art and music, and the recipes all left me hungry for more. But I feel like it was a fair price, considering I bought it on sale.Also bought a copy for a friend who I expect to enjoy it as much or even more than me :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely mini game about an immigrant family moving from India to Canada and looking to find a better future for their child, and remembering where they come from through food.I need to emphasize that it is a mini game, as I got just over an hour of playtime out of it on my first play through. However if you need to get all the achievements it may take another play through or two, as I wanted my first play of the game to be without spoilers.The art is gorgeous and the music is very catchy. After originally playing the demo back in June 2023, I realised I needed to buy the game. The only downside is that I wished it went on a little longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game since they announced it at the Wholesome Direct. Story and the artwork is really amazing and I say this as designer myself. I wish this game was longer though. I'd really appreciate if there was an option to view the actual recipes to make them at home. The only con I have about this game is the price and it is purely just PERSONAL. As a broke student the 1 hr gameplay does not really justify the exorbitant price of this game. But I do understand and appreciate the amount of effort that went into this. Best of luck to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wholesome, endearing and beautiful game! The graphics were comforting, the music was a continuous vibe, the story line was emotional and the food made me hungry without any question. I was in tears by the end of it. This game is gold dust to South Asians and the sense of representation that it gives cannot be put into simple words. Truly appreciating the many themes of love, family, loss and culture that it brought up within a short span of time. Couldn't recommend Venba enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: My parents moved from India to America a little over 3 decades ago. I bought this game to play with my mom and it became a very unique experience. We're from South India, as the family in Venba. It was funny and silly to almost ignore the game's tutorial, because my mom cooks these various dishes all the time at home.Equally, it was interesting to talk about the topics the game presented. My older brothers and I experienced a similar disconnect to Indian culture, because despite wanting to appreciate it, we also had to deal with the negatives that come with being 'Different' in the western world. My brothers experienced bullying, being compared to those stereotypes of Indian characters in TV and I found myself being a spectacle every time I brought Indian food to school or decided to wear something from India. We didn't get to learn Malayalam properly, because schools discouraged that, since it 'made us unable to communicate' with them. We were mostly alone as the only South Indians in the area, so we didn't get to celebrate holidays in the same way as if we were in India.There's a balance to appreciating the culture you come from and embracing the culture you're within. This game made both my mom and I tear up. To see Venba try so hard, to see Kavin pull away, to see how difficult it can be.This was an amazing game and it was worth every penny spent on it. This may have been just about the message of the game, but it was fun to play, with every loving detail put in and to read and just feel how accurate it was to the conversations my family has had.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I'm half Tamil and moved countries, and now playing this game made me ugly cry and want to call home. This game is loaded with nostalgia - especially its absolutely beautiful soundtrack. I know and make the food featured in this game and I could smell every step of each recipe. It was also a great feeling to see the Tamil script on screen in a video game! I can't believe this is on Steam and the world gets to see it!! Please buy this game and support the creators. They've created something so wonderful and homely, and I pray they keep making more.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with incredible music. Visually appealing (although perhaps a bit more work can be done on diversifying the animation, as well as fixing a few artefacts).A DETAILED RECIPE BOOK OF ALL THE FEATURED RECIPES IS PROVIDED AT THE END!! Something I hope to remember if ever the cooking whizz in me wakes up.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous, salivated a lot, teared up a lot, too. I totally want a game mode where I just make food in this style. Thank you for making this and sharing this story. I think that art speaks volumes and can really inspire people to care and better understand what is happening in the world or in their local area. I wish art was more important to the world because of this alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: i didnt expect to tear up today ;-; what a beautiful game and story !!! <3 the music and sounds emerges you in the game you can almost smell the food, it made me so hungry xD i loved the bright colors and art too <3immigrant parents really sacrifice everything for their children the least we can do is honor their culture and keep it a part of their life as it is part of us. going to hug my mom and tell her im sorry hahahaha if you have an immigrant parent/parents im sure we all been through this, dont be consumed with guilt just become better to them before its too late <3333
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

You can feel that the developers put their own life stories into the game, and with every minute, you get more immersed. -> You should play Venba if you love real-life stories packed with emotions, all wrapped up in a great, cozy art style!P.S. _childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo for this back in nextfest. Took me a little bit to buy the game but I finally did and I'm wondering why I hadn't done so sooner. The story of this game touched my heart. I'm just your average nothing special person with no real identity. I feel I got to see a different side of things and I loved every minute of this experience. One of my viewers related to it a bit because of their own culture (though they are not Tamil but still live in two worlds). Another was like I need to call my mom now. Just play the game. _childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: it's a short game with a very simple yet amazing storyline and a loot of cooking puzzles. it has it's own unique style which i personally never have seen before which gives it its own unique touch. despite all those aspects; would i pay the full price? nah, i would wait for a sale and then enjoy it, for me personally it's not really worth the full price
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Too little cooking, control of the cooking and generally just a bit too short.And the "situation" of the story was just annoying since there was no "real" attempt at communication between the kid and the parents. Doesn't matter if it happened or is based on a true story if it doesn't capture you and bad communication is just tragic not interesting.So pretty much an unsatisfying story with too little game in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very beautiful. I wished it was longer because the cooking parts and story were nice but I appreciated what was made. It doesn't touch on things super deeply but still tells enough of the story so people can understand the feelings of the characters in the game. Overall, I quite enjoyed it and it was money well spent!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a gorgeous game with a poignant story. It is about a South Indian couple that immigrates to Canada in search of a better life. The story is told in mostly Venba's perspective as she cooks traditional South Indian dishes. She is left with her mother's old cookbook, but it is falling apart and missing some key sections. The goal is to figure out each of the recipes given some limited clues from the book, and then cook them successfully. I cried quite a bit playing this game. As a Desi American who immigrated with her family as a young child, some parts of the story hit too close to home. The immigrant struggle is portrayed very well in this game. Some of the dialogue was reminiscent of conversations my parents had when I was younger, and they evoked some strong feelings. The concept of sacrifice is especially important in this game. I replayed some chapters to get all the achievements, and seeing the little details in the artwork and music made me enjoy it that much more. This game is short but sweet, depicting the struggles of trying to balance two cultures while trying to fit in.I am not South Indian, so some of the recipes were new to me. It was fun to try and figure out not just the ingredients, but also how to prepare the food. However, I was excited when one of my favorite dishes from my native country was featured as a dish!! It also felt special to see a family on screen that not only looked like me and my family, but shared the same experiences as well.The art style is beautiful and reminded me of a children's story book!! And I love the proverbs at the beginning of the chapter. I highly recommend this game if you like cooking games, puzzles, and touching stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, great soundtrack. My favorite track is Thulludhadi Valasu. Contrary to the other reviews, i think that this game is a perfect length and i'd willingly replay it multiple times. Cooking feels fun, the story is painfully relatable if you're 2nd+ generation immigrant who feels disconnected from their ethnic background, and playing it gave me an appreciation for my circumstances that I didn't really have before.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This narrative game wraps a very moving story and a small (but oh so smart) cooking system to take us through the life of a family of immigrants from India to Canada.It's short, it's beautiful, it's very well crafted, big kuddos to everyone involved in this work. Thank you Visai Games !Now to get some Indian food.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game should last 15 minutes longer (a chapter longer). It just felt to me that there's a missing story beat somewhere. Other than that, it's pretty much perfect. The art direction for this game is really unique and I appreciate that. It even gave us free recipe book! Made me want to make my first homemade briyani. But the best part about this game is its powerful message. I don't think any game ever prompt me to call my mom. Definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The second the installation was completed I called my mom over, who was confused when I turned the monitor toward her and showed familiar letters, and when Venba was spelled out in Tamil her face lit up and nodded when I asked her to play it together with me. She started reading out the dialogue, stumbling over a few of the English words as I nudged her along, but she was so fixed on the dialogue that she didn't want to stop. She was fired up when the cooking levels began, ignoring the recipe book I was trying to decipher and telling me the order in how to cook the dishes. We both laughed in excitement when Venba brought up Puddu- because really, when is that ever brought up in everyday life?- and looked forward to reading the Thirukkural, the texts of wisdom that is centered under the calendar at the start of each chapter. And then the roles were flipped and I read the Tamil lines my mom nodded as I tried to translate the words. It's honestly wild to see a game this personal (and calling me out) come to life. Thank you for creating this moment for me to bond with my Amma. We already planned on launching some rockets tomorrow.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: -  I think the less you know about it beforehand the better. -  This game will make you hungry for food and teach you how to make it!- . Only takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes and I think it has the perfect length. The gameplay doesn't outstay its welcome and shifts in different ways while the story leads you wondering what is going to happen next. It’s probably even faster if you are a decent cook.-  Thematic and the right tempo for the scene. -  I like the different ways of omitting information that challenges you with the cooking. - , ingredients fall over and become clumsy when someone less experienced is cooking.-  - Not all the controls are great on pc. Maybe better with controller. Especially when I need to rotate on the screen.- Is this a cutscene or do I need to click. Cinematic borders would have helped. Sometimes you are also looking at a still image that can make you think the game has crashed.This is a fantastic little game that I can recommend to anyone. It’s easy enough and will probably teach you something new about cooking, and if not, it will teach you something about what it means to be human.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Endearing, bittersweet, and beautiful. This story shares the struggles that come with being first-generation immigrant Indian parents, raising children who drift from their roots, and recognizing each other's experiences in this unique dynamic. I definitely resonate with the experience of taking educated risks in life, exploring the horizons, hoping for the best, and that it's okay if things don't turn out how you planned. Despite the struggles, there is family who loves you, near and far, and happiness when you get to enjoy delicious homemade meals together. Ideally, you cook them together too. ;)Through puzzles designed around limited information (the cookbook is damaged!), you are taught helpful cooking techniques. As someone who cooks often, I actually did not know many of these tips! And as a third-gen Mexican-American who loves Indian cuisine but has no idea how to cook it, I appreciate the care that went into sharing these recipes in a way that is easy for someone like me to learn. The colorful and textured food and sound design in this game makes me very hungry! I'm eager to try these recipes out soon. Beautiful game!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Man I hate leaving negative reviews for indie games but the bottom line is its just too short and doesn't even have much game play at that. I finished the game in 73 minutes and I even messed up on a few recipes, and most of the recipes pretty much just involves clicking and dragging thing in different orders. The story while touching and super relatable to me, felt like it didn't really have depth because of the short game length.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant bittersweet story about family connection over food. Less than two hours long, and fairly simple in nature, I'm not sure I would recommend it at its current full price. Definitely one to pick up on sale if it's the sort of story you're interested in. It also contains a detailed recipe book with the dishes from the game, which is a pretty neat and valuable addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Very wholesome visual novel about Venba, who emigrates from India to Canada with her husband. Through 7 chapters you explore different points in their lives. It's mostly a narrative-based game with each chapter having a small interactive part where you cook different dishes. This game is very short (it took me <2 hours) but the story is genuine and touching (not to mention really sad at parts) and is perhaps my favourite visual novel that I've played so far. While the price is high for the hours of gameplay that you get, it's clear that the developers have put so much care and effort into this story and for that reason, I think this game is absolutely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a game where you will be filling your screen with lots of food presented in charming colors, dazzling cooking sounds, and a whole lot of virtual flavors you could swear you could almost taste through the screen (although screen tasting doesn't yet exist as a technology so you can only wish for it!)But Venba is much more than that.In its short running time Venba tells this story about a family that comes from India to make a better life for themselves on the new continent,Cooking is this fragile spirit that permeates many moments in this family life and while it doesn't always succeeds it does come time and time again to connect them and save them.Venba is one of those stories that reminds us the power of food and the unique path that we can travel if we let ourselves be carried away by our senses.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game along with my mother. It was a an unspoken two way conversation for hopefully both of us. Beautiful portrayal of complexities of parent-child relationship. Emotions have been seamlessly woven into dishes. The Chicken rasam (i make for my toddler when he falls sick) hit very close to home for me. This game brought a very calming experience. Loved the conversations. The mask that keeps changing expressions was a cute touch. Highly recommended :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing the user reviews noting Venba takes roughly an hour (took me around one and a half hours myself), I approached it more like an interactive movie or storybook than a video game (if only because the majority of the games I play have dozens of hours of content, and I made sure to distance myself from that attitude here). With that angle, I really liked this! I'm not Indian but I had a couple childhood friends who are, and my parents spent a large part of their lives in India, so recognizing a few of the dishes were fun (ah, biryani is so delicious and it looks good here too)!The story itself (more specifically, Kavin's perspective later on) really resonated with me as someone who wanted to be more closer to the other kids I grew up with rather than my family or history, and while I've already made up my mind on reconnecting with my roots, this has definitely reinforced my decision.I don't normally write reviews but I felt like making an exception to this lovely short story, especially since this is an indie game. I won't lie, the art style is what drew me in at first, but it didn't take long for my heart to empathize with the family. Would wholeheartedly recommend if the other positive reviews resonate with you!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. Touches very well on the immigrant experience in a non-imposing way. I especially loved how the storytelling came through the meals as opposed to direct actions. Just overall so great and so worth the investment of money and time. I really wish this game gets out to more people cause its just so touching.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A tender and wholesome visual novel about a Tamil expat couple and their story. It's indeed a visual novel but food and cooking are a fundamental part of it, and it's up to us to actually cook ^^I have to admit playing this game just before dinner made me super hungry :)On a more serious tone, as an expat myself i understand the delights and the sadness of living far away.. impossible not to shed a tear playing this.Expat or not, you should play it too.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A short, bittersweet story about the Indian cuisine, being a parent and hardships as an immigrant.Even as a person who has near zero interest in food I found the dishes depicted ingame looked pretty tasty, and the accompanying soundtrack makes it all better. Only downside of this game is that it's very, very short. it's just about an hour long to achieve 100%(which requires you to replay at least 1 chapter). I know they literally said it out loud in their store page how it's short, and I'm aware of the fact that not all games should be subjected to a dollar-per-hour rule but paying $15 for just one hour worth of experience is hard to justify in 2023. Otherwise, good game. It tells a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A well written, short and to the point story about family, growing up and trying to fit in, all told around the main mechanic of making indian food. Although I personally don't have faced the same struggles as the characters and am not very familiar with the culture, the story and all the details felt authentic and I was way more invested than I thought I would be. I'm pretty sure the creators know what they are presenting really well. The art style stands out and is pretty and colourfull, while the music choices are fun and fitting. I also highly appreciate the additon of an actual cookbook with the recipes you make during the game! Some people may find the price tag a bit high for the duration (1-2 hours), but you should still consider Venba, at least during a sale if you don't feel the full price, as it is a sincere, unique, well crafted experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for ages and it didn't disappoint. The story is wonderfully written with some of the most beautiful and delicious artwork I've seen, it made me genuinely hungry to try all of these dishes (not that I have the skills for that). It was also really wholesome to see a genuine look at the struggles and happiness of trying to raise a family in a different country with different cultures, navigating the difference between a parents upbringing and their child's, but doing so with love and understanding.The cooking ended up being more interesting/harder puzzles than I was expecting from the demo, which were fun to work out and while I think they are easier with more cooking knowledge (eg what kind of ingredients might be added when) they were still very accessible.The only downside I had was that the game was as short as it was, I would have loved to play more and discover more recipes, and I'm already hoping for some DLC. At first I had thought this would be closer to cooking mama in the number of recipes and the focus, but instead the cooking is incorporated really well into the primary visual novel of the game as an act of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really sweet! You learn how to cook Tamil food and the story is deeply moving and natural. I like how you get to see things from Venba and Paavalan's eyes, and then see their son Kavin growing up. All of the characters change and you get to see why they feel and think the way they do. I loved learning about Tamil culture, and it was eye opening learning about the struggles Venba and Paavalan faced moving from India to Canada. I'm really glad Kavin learned to be proud of his culture and that he apologised to his mum for not supporting her. We need more games and stories like this! Keep up the great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to recommend this game, but not at its full price. Unfortunately, this game is SHORT, as in less than an hour short, maybe 2 if you want to collect the achievements. I want to like this game, and for the most part, I do. I wish the story were a lot longer because all the hardships our family faces are so brief, that they lost the opportunity to be much more meaningful.Otherwise, I appreciate the unique art style and the family cooking aspect, the puzzles were fun and the story was decent. If you enjoy wholesome games I think there's a lot to enjoy about this game, it has a nice soundtrack and includes recipes for real-life use which is a charming touch and may inspire players' interest in Indian food in their own kitchen.Because of how incredibly short it is I encourage you to buy it on sale, as much as I appreciate smaller creators and indie games, it is just too short.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The incredible visual design was obvious going in, but I was surprised & impressed by the depth & ambivalence of the story, especially given the quick pace of the game. Cooking interactions are simple but satisfying and beautifully conceptualized. Great jams too! Played w my partner over a couple hours, enjoyed every minute. Wish there was more (not for the price; just because it was lots of fun), but video games are impossible to make, so I get it. This is a v good one!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I had such high hopes for this game, played the demo which gave me an excellent idea of what to expect, and was practically counting down the hours to the full release last night Australian time. And man, it did not disappoint at all. If anything, it was far more emotional and nuanced than I expected. I got so choked up at several points, the intergenerational perspectives were so thoughtful and deep, and the insights of being caught between two cultures were spot on. Made me realise I was super lucky that I got sent to school with horrible cheese sandwiches instead of desi food though now I wonder if I would have gone "You people are all idiots, my desi scrambled eggs are the only way to make scrambled eggs. SCREW YOU GUYS!" But maybe not.What I really admired was the careful balance of story and gameplay. I don't like too much story in my games, I want to be actually doing something. So even though there was probably a little more story in this than I usually tolerate, it was still told well enough that I wanted to know that stuff and was still delighted when it came time to make a thing. There was also a real elegance in life events withheld which resulted in me going "Wait, what happened? Where are we now? We are? Omg."  Gameplay wise, I really liked how the recipes got more intuitive as the game progressed, less instructions and more guesswork. To my delight, I found my own instincts kicking in and going "No, wait, yaar, you bhagar the seeds first" and "oh wait, I know the layering in biryani goes!" For a desi who lives to eat but refuses to cook, I fully impressed myself. And it was indescribably exciting to successfully make biryani and dosa and rasam even virtually. I used the hints less and less the longer I played and no doubt soon I will replay without using any hints.A really beautifully made game with such wonderful attention to sound and visual detail. I loved the texture of the art style and that the controls were still smooth enough that I could play this without any controllers or keys, just the touchpad on my laptop. Thank you so much for making that possible. And thank you for representing Tamil food and making Tamil stories! I didn't want this to end!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about Venba from TGA 2023, it was really fun to complete and I believe the story has more to offer than the cooking itself. While yes, the cooking and figuring out how to make each dish was fun, the story and a peek into another culture and the issue of self acceptance was worth more in this game. Thank you for bringing light to your culture and life in one beautiful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet game about generational differences. While it might be up there in price considering it takes about an hour to play through the story, it really is worth it. The visuals and art style are gorgeous, and the storytelling really drives home the struggle of immigrating parents and raising a child in a completely different country. I teared up at times but the ending was very sweet and its just all round a really nice comfort game to play. Some of the dishes look fantastic, and I can't wait to get the official cookbook to maybe try some of them!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so pleasing and easy going. The story is beautiful and you feel for the characters. Even though I come from a different culture, cooking is also always so prevalent, so this was somewhat familiar to me. A bit short, could have some different mechanics to extend the gameplay and let you explore, but it is marketed as a short narrative, so 😅 Like someone else said, be careful, it will leave you feeling hungry!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Heartwarming Culinary Tale! "Venba" delivers a captivating short story, despite its linear nature. The game's lovely graphics and soulful soundtrack create an immersive experience that tugs at your heartstrings.One aspect that pleasantly surprised me was the cooking "puzzling" element. It seamlessly blended into the narrative, adding a delightful twist without becoming annoying or distracting. In fact, it complemented the story beautifully, enhancing the overall experience.As I journeyed through the game, I was delighted to discover that "Venba" had more to offer than just entertainment. It provided an opportunity to learn something about cooking, making the experience not only enjoyable but also educational.In conclusion, "Venba" is a heartwarming gem that enchants players with its touching story, delightful graphics, and harmonious soundtrack. The unique integration of cooking as a puzzle mechanic adds a delightful layer to the game, making it a truly enriching experience. Don't miss this memorable culinary adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it being a bit short, it was really an amazing game. From the art style, to the music, to the writing, I absolutely loved it! I've seen some people saying it's not worth it unless you have a connection to the culture, but as some random american-latino i think it's definitely worth buying. It's such a touching story, and the game play is really fun too! I do wish it was a bit longer but I still have no regrets, and will be recommending the hell out of this to my friends. Also despite not being the best cook I'm definitely going to try and make some of these recipes when I have the time, they all looked and sounded so tasty!! Overall great game, definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The game tells a pretty plain story about Asian immigrants, about family and identity. The story is really short and it doesn't really feature much gameplay. But it is still a great game for me because I can relate so much and I also happen to have a Tamil best friend. I hope there is a sequel or expansion.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: As a non Indian, the food look amazing. The gameplay is point and click, it sometimes lose my interest but the story kick in and I'm motivated to go at it again. The game end pretty quickly, I can even refund it after finishing it but I won't.Overall, a short cute game with a tear jerking story about immigrants family. Worth a buy and worth to keep in your library.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very beautiful, very short bittersweet experience. And I do want to emphasize on that last part. It is a marvelous experience and I HIGHLY recommend it, but just know that if what youre looking is a puzzle cooking game, this isn't it. Your gameplay interactions arent that many, but I dont think this game needs it. Like I said, it's more about the experience this little story makes you feel.Had been following the development for quite a while, and I bought it on release, and I have no regrets. Thank you devs for this product of love <3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The visual style, music and the methods of strorytelling (what we're directly told by characters and what is implied by what we see) are all magnificent.Went into this expecting to feel sad and yeah that happened, but also now I'm REALLY hungry. Genuinely gonna have to try atleast one of these recipes.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game for sure, good direction ( art, programming, audio, story ).The gameplay is simple and satisfying. You definitely learn how to cook a cultural food. Recommended ( First thing I remembered was the game called Cooking Mama )Every scene touches you deeply, the story is very good so far. Very sentimental I think, a little emotional... ( it depends on your life, experiences and culture I think )For everyone that is looking for a short story with cooking gameplay. It will be a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: So beautiful and touching all around! Wonderful story (well paced too), gorgeous art, music, and sound design - you can really hear everything cooking. I felt so emotionally connected to the characters right away. You'll definitely feel very hungry! I want to try to make some of the recipes (which are written out on the game's main page).
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting this game to make me cry, but boy, was I wrong. This game is very beautifully made and the ending is very sweet. My grandfather was Indian, and he had two children, one being my mother and the other my uncle. I've heard a lot about how they got picked on for being Indian and for embracing the culture, and as I notice generations of my family continue, I notice how culture seems to get watered down the younger the kids are. In a mixed family, I'm the eldest of my siblings and I hold my cultures very dear to my heart. I notice, however, that they often don't seem nearly as interested in any of our cultures, which is very disheartening for me and my parents, and it feels like it creates a rift between us. I just feel like this game really nailed these topics so well and it brought me to tears by the end of it.My only complaint for this game is that it's short -- on one hand being because I wanted to play so much more of it, haha. But on the other hand, I did feel it was a tad bit expensive for a game of it's length. I was able to finish the game in the span of about 2 hours, which I feel is a very short amount of game for 15 dollars. I can't be too upset about that though, as there was obviously just so much love and effort put into this game. I can see myself playing it again every now and again just because it's so bittersweet of a story. I genuinely loved this so much. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Great story telling! Very emotional, was crying a lot - it was so heart touching and well designed. The game is very short though, I needed 2 hours for a first playthrough - but feeling like having to play it again for 100%ing the game, so it might end up with being 4 hours for me.The music is very catchy as well, there is also a Venba inspired playlist on spotify if you are interested btw =)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba ... O Venba... O Venba !!!!! Such a short sweet and emotional game. Thank you Steam for having it in your platform. This just resonates so much with every Asian kid's life and their bonding with their parents. O my word, this game narrates the story of Indian parents migrating to Canada and are coming to terms with a number of challenges from language to job and several other issues on the way. Kavin, the son born to this beautiful family, is the apple of their eye and who acts his own part which gels well with the whole story. The spectacle of this game are the number of recipes being cooked giving you that breath of fresh air emanating with Indian goodness. The music fits really well with the gameplay being so creative yet a bit challenging if you havent cooked certain dishes in real life. I do not want to add more to this as the game is short and I do not intend to spoil the ending in any way. Great game for anyone wanting to have a chilled out and family atmospheric game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a beautiful game that tells its story and connects us to it, through the universal love of food. The art style aids that journey but its asmr levels of sound design and on theme music shines perhaps even more so. Your only desire and wish is that you could eat and smell the dishes. The puzzles aren't too difficult and lends itself to an overall cozier type of gaming experience.My only criticism of the game is its length. The devs are honest about the amount of content the game offers, so that's a plus in terms of transparency. I knew I was in for about 1-2 hours of game play before my purchase. At the end I felt it lacked just a little more time to really let it all truly sink in. As you experience the ups and downs of the story, you might not leave as touched as the team might've intended (and you might've hoped). For context I finished the game with all achievements, as well as explored the differences in which the dialog choices made to the conversations, in 115 min. I would also not consider the game to be particularly replayable. IN CONCLUSION this game gives you a calm and touching experience, that you can finish in one sitting. You can feel the love and thought put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game that breaks both out of common game design concepts as well as cultural topics defined by Western standards. Having an immigrant family story with all its protagonist's struggles of raising a kid in a foreign country mixed with cool cooking is such an unusal hybrid of good storytelling and an easygoing but worthwhile type of gameplay. It also has a "serious" flavor (!) to it as you will get inspired to cook yourself for real after having played this. (Trust me when I say this, as the writer of these lines isn't a great cook himself.)In terms of presentation Venba shines as well: The artwork is as pretty as it is unique, and the sound design is downright amazing. I loved all the sizzles and frizzles, and of course all the Indian songs as well as those little instrument sounds which are perfectly placed throughout the storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely beautiful game with a very real and heartwarming (and at times heartbreaking) story. stunning artstyle, incredibly fun soundtrack and overall very good vibes. I only wish it were longer because of how happy playing it made me. as a child of immigrant parents, i could see my family and myself in this and it made it a very emotional journey. one i enjoyed very much
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is less a game and more interactive storytelling and is done with a beautiful art style and music. That said its really well done and struck a lot of chords with me as my spouse is first gen immigrant to US and the thoughts and worries for our two children having an appreciation for both eastern and western cultures and heritage.100% recommend if you, your partner or parents were first generation immigrants to another country.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: What brought me to the game was the cooking aspect however what I am enjoying even more is the story behind the food!  If you have the means please purchase this game. The art is beautiful and the food  looks so good you can practically smell it.  I  am also enjoying learning about an identity outside of my own. Venba and her families story is one that is though different from mine is one I can relate to. I am hoping you will pick this title up so you may see for yourself. It's not that expensive so it's not like your breaking the bank!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could mark this down as a "yes, BUT" recommendation. The game is great, it's absolutely beautiful, the atmosphere is fantastic, it made me weepy and reminded me to call my mom.HOWEVER, it is very, VERY short, with only one ending and limited replayability unless you just REALLY want to get a perfect score on every recipe - and even that shouldn't take too long to do, once you've figured out the trick to them once. I recommend playing this game... But maybe not at full price. $15 for a game that's barely over an hour long is rough, even if that's a really solid hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short game (I got through it in maybe 2 hours tops) but the gameplay was enjoyable and relaxing and the story resonated a lot with me emotionally. The cooking sections were well balanced and I liked the ways cooking and food were woven throughout the story with feelings, memories and culture.A real gem. I waited for this one to come out and was even more excited for it after the demo, and I am not disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know much about this game before downloading, I just came here looking for a fun little cooking game. I was drawn to this with it's focus on deshi cooking. And now I'm an emotional wreck and I need to call my mom.Thank you to the devs, I didn't expect to be hit with these feelings on a tuesday night.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Although I liked this game, it's more of a shot story about a cuisine than a game.  The theme is cooking Indian food, but the game play is just simple point and click with no real challenge.  There are only a handful of recipes, and only about 15 minutes of cooking game play.It's heart warming, and worth it for the story and exposure to a culture, and a small insight into an immigrant's perspective, . . . but not really a "game" about cooking.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A truly beautiful game in style, story and gameplay.I loved the soundtrack and visuals, i think the game looks and sounds absolutely wonderfun. The two hours it took me to complete it were very enjoyable! The game managed to tell a story about family, being foreign in a new country, having your child grow up very differently and not beeing able to fully enbrace their "home culture". Even tho i am not tamil, i felt for the parents and the child, their problems and constantly feeling misunderstood. The gam portraied these issues very nicely and in a way everyone can follow. The gameplay is simple but fun non the less, you recreate different indian recipes with a slight puzzle mechanic in the levels. You cannot really go wrong (if you do you can start that step over). This kind of cooking was very relaxing and fun and made me want to start cooking the dishes in real life too :DThe only small issue i have with Venba is that is it quite short (2.4 hours to 100%, maybe 1,8 for one playthrough). I personally don't mind, especially because i got the game in a bundle, but this might be relevant for others. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: was a unique experience. The sound design and music is incredible, like actually INCREDIBLE. Yes, it is short, but I don't think that matters too much. It doesn't overstay it's welcome and gets a wonderful message across while showing such wonderfully crafted meals. Crying so much from this one. Sorry mom I was an a**hole teenager lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, with vibrant colors, distinctive art style and wonderful music. It made me reflect on my the immigration stories of my family and also want to hug and call my mother. It's touching, it's unique, it's absolutely worth playing. This is mostly a story driven game, but it did encourage me to cook some Tamil recipes. Thank you to the creators for a wonderful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: If Roger Ebert's infamous claim that games are not art wasn't already debunked, this work of interactive art definitely puts it to rest once and for all. This is emotionally powerful art that gives us believably flawed characters who will make you laugh and cry. You'll definitely want to plan ahead for some Indian food right after you're done playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game was everything I hoped it would be. I laughed 🤣, I cried 😭, I felt all the feels 🥰. The story is beautiful and heartfelt. The artwork is stunning. The puzzles can be difficult, but were not so impossible that they were frustrating. The music is outstanding. Love, love, love this game. I wish it was longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: this game was short, detailed, and satisfying to play. above all though, it was extremely heart wrenching. I can see this resonating with many people of different backgrounds, especially those who have immigrated or are second gen. this story was beautifully written and very touching. it felt very familiar to me but also introduced such a beautiful culture in an accessible way. food and cuisine plays such a huge role in identity and is something that connects us all as people. i would highly recommend purchasing this game to experience yourself. my only complaint was that I wish that there were more chapters or even dlc, but even so, the game feels complete. it's more so just my own desire that craves more gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. I got it on humble bundle so for full price I am not sure I would have personally been satisfied. It is only about an hour and a half and not as much game play as I was anticipating. The puzzles are also easy and there aren't that many of them so it is really less of a game and more a visual novel. It is an absolutely gorgeous game and the music is awesome as well. I love visual novels too but as someone with no personal ties to a story about culture and immigration it was interesting but I wasn't as invested in the story especially with how fast paced it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Short point and click game, with a sad story about an unappreciative kid, who learns too late about valuing his parents. Felt that it was too simplistic, as was the cooking puzzles. It included a "cookbook" but only as in-game menu, with tiny font. Struggled to play this through to the end, despite the easy gameplay. We wanted to learn about Indian culture and cuisine, but left disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A short narrative-driven game where every mechanic is utilized so efficiently and seamlessly to compliment each narrative beat. The love for South Indian food is infectious for someone who is not part of the Indian culture. A touching story that comments on the theme of immigration, culture and parenting. A big recommendation from me for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I think I loved everything about this game. It's not full of joy all the time, it's actually pretty sad most of the way. But it taught me something. It gives a better, more profound, understanding of what it can be like to be an immigrant and have hopes and fears for your life and family. Food is such a good focal point for this story. The gameplay is fluid and easy, I would have loved to cook more but still, it's okay. Now I want to try all the recipes I learned there. Thank you for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: As an Indian person born in the U.S., I felt so connected to Kavin and his story.  I related to so many of his struggles being brought up in a different culture and traditions than your parents were brought up in.  Venba helped me realize how a different environment can affect your cultural practices and how my family language and traditions are slowly being pushed out as a result of it.  I just want to say a thank you to the developers for creating this amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and touching little game that unites culture, heritage and cooking. The art style, the storytelling and the music are all very sensitive and made me wonder and tear up at times. As a parent of a young kid who was not born in the same country I was, this game speaks to me in a deep level. The dilemmas, the worries, the joys and the pain all feel very real, very authentic.But you don't need to be in a similar situation to appreciate this little gem. As long as you appreciate story-rich games, I believe you'll find something enjoyable in the experience, as it's very carefully crafted and well-written.And if you're curious about the southern Indian/Tamil culture, even better! I played this game with my phone on my hand, looking up different recipes and cultural references the characters dropped. I might give it a try to that Hyderabadi biryani at some point...
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Venba and it’s such a heartfelt game. The story is touching, exploring family, identity, and heritage, and the visuals and music are absolutely stunning.  If you enjoy emotional stories and cultural experiences, I’d definitely recommend giving Venba a try!I want to point out that I thought it was a bit short (about 1-2 hours), could have been more fun to try more recipes!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It is very short, even after I read everything. I am actually shocked at this, because in my imagination telling a story about a foreign family in a strange land, mixing in foreign cooking with unfamiliar ingredients, can be dragged to the point of boring people by just explaining stuffs. In fact, I was actually quite excited at thinking I was going to learn a ton about a foreign culture. But NOPE. Here, I cooked things I still have no idea about, from ingredients to finished product, and learned things I already knew, since myself and my parents are immigrants. For example, I don't understand why can't this game tell me what ghee is. Is it supposed to be common knowledge for everyone in the world? Do I not deserve to know what it is unless I am willing to google it after I close the game?  If cooking is being advertise as an aspect of the game, I totally expect to learn about what the heck I am using IN GAME. There were like 6 cooking sessions in this game, and only the last 2 were slightly interesting, cause I finally got some info about what I was messing with.Story is very short and simple, The kind you can guess where it is going from the first chapter. Though I don't know why there's a lack of the kid's point of view through out the story, which is supposed to be about parent/kid relationship, until the very end. By then I find it hard to see from his viewpoint anymore and it makes the ending a bit shallow. All in all, while it is not bad, I do not think it is worth what it is charging. It could have been much better with a little effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: the story is so deep and engaging, i love the full game play making necessary stops at each stage and kept me more involved. this game is around 2hours. but it doesnt feel so , it felt so short but interesting. I gifted this to my friend and they felt so great playing it. hope they bring more games like this
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Rarely are the struggles and sacrifices of parenthood conveyed better than they are in Venba.I found myself reflecting on the choice I've made to not become a parent and that details touched upon in Venba tell many reasons why. To bring someone into this world and only want success and happiness for them - how much do you nag and pressure them to make certain choices? Do you leave them be to make mistakes and find their own way? Every interaction with them leaves an impression. Will they still love you regardless of which way you flip the switch? The answer is like the recipe books you see in Venba. You may get some hints on how to do things from previous generations, but you'll mostly be met by smudges and have to improvise to try your best. And if you couldn't tell, this game isn't cozy - it's full of emotion. I cried more than once. It's an experience I'll remember for a long time.Now excuse me while I text amma and appa that I love them.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a short but sweet game. It's about 1,5 hours. I really liked the soft artstyle, story telling, music and cooking recipes. I'm definitely going to cook some of these dishes! Having said that, you should not play the game on an empty stomach. Please buy the game and support the creators, It's worth the money and you get a relaxing experience whilst following the love and struggles of a family trying to find their place in the world and eachothers hearts.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I cried. Some of the text conversations were almost exactly on-point for old conversations I had with my mom when I first started college. I immediately went to give her a hug after I played. Some of the cooking mini games aren't even really games for all the "effort" you put into it (rotate your mouse), but it's more about the story than the cooking, anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: More of a story than a game, but what a good story. Was thrilling to play a game where the main character is a Tamil mother who grows older through the story. A rarity (or even a first?) in this industry, and I loved it. And making the food was a great way to show how food connects (and sometimes disconnects) people. I was left hungry! I will fire this up again, I'm sure.Some are complaining about the price, but considering how beautifully crafted this game is, I think it's worth it. Just note before you purchase that it's short, but meaningful. Maybe give it a try, even if you have no connection to this culture or life experience.One last thing: the music is 🔥
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The story, visuals and music are beautiful. However, I find the cooking parts to be really frustrating.For example, I'm totally stuck on the "layering" part of the biryani recipe, where the directions are almost entirely crossed out. It feels like the game expects me to be able to figure out how to make it, but I can't, so I'm just trying every permutation of ingredients in the hopes that I'll eventually get it right. I have no idea how to continue, short of searching for a guide or walkthrough.I really want to recommend this game, because of the obvious care that went into its creation, but I'm stuck and don't know how I can recommend it to anyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A moving story of struggle, regret, and loss from a perspective of a immigrant.Venba weaves a tight emotional journey by capturing the struggles that define moving to a new place and making a living there. Strongly recommend.We should encourage game creators to create such powerful narratives without being bound by the constraint of keeping the game long.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is an extremely beautiful game with stellar art direction and music and sound design. However, a single play through takes about a hour and a half and the story feels a bit too spread apart. To give a little context, you will do a chapter and then time will jump forward 1 year or sometimes up to 5 or 10 at once! I personally would have liked smaller time skips and to be able to enjoy more meals and more interactions between the family. Maybe even a single instance of Kavin experiencing a meal in another home so we could explore his feelings more as a child.The experience is enough for me to say that the game was worth it and I know I'll definitely come back and do another play through down the line, but would have definitely loved even more.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me want to call my dad and tell him how much I appreciate what my parents went through so that I can have a life in Canada.Prepare for an emotional roller coaster, and perhaps a heavy metaphorical blanket of grief and regret, especially if you're born from first-generation immigrants in North America.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: In  you play as Venba, an Indian woman newly come to Canada with her husband to start a new life while trying to hold onto your roots. Venba has moved to Canada with her husband Paavalan to start a new life. Shortly into the game Venba is pregnant with their first child, a son named Kavin. The core game play centers around Venba, trying to keep her Tamil culture alive by recreating old recipes her mother used to make through the use of her mothers very worn and damaged old cookbook. The recipes play out as puzzles that you create by following along with the cookbook and Venba’s memories to help fill in the missing instructions in the book. Woven throughout is the story and struggles that Venba and Paavalan encounter while trying to settle into their new life in Canada. The new language, job prospects, and wondering if they made a mistake in moving to Canada. Told through chapters as the years pass Venba tries to teach her son as he grows up about his Tamil culture but struggles to connect with him as he tries to shy away from anything that makes him different. Later in life Kavin tries to reconnect to his family through the use of food. In Venba you recreate recipes from reading what is still legible from Venba’s mothers old worn recipe book and Venba’s memories. Most recipes (the ones that have multi-stages) have checkpoints that save so if you fail you do not need to redo the whole puzzle. Also there are hints available if you need them and background information on what you are cooking. The art of Venba is colourful, hand-drawn and has a storybook style to it. The music is wonderful, before starting to cook Venba will turn on the radio and listen to music before cooking. Something I do in my life too when I spend the day in the kitchen cooking and baking. The Tamil tunes are lively and add so much atmosphere to the game while you're cooking. The ambient sounds in the game really bring the art of cooking to life. You can hear the food sizzle when it hits the hot oil, the blender blending away, the crank of the tools as you pipe out dough. They did a phenomenal job of capturing the sounds of the kitchen as you cook. You can almost smell the food cooking when it is sizzling in the frying pan or simmering on the stovetop. This game admittedly made me hungry. I love Indian food, some of the most flavourful cuisine I have been blessed to experience. This game has a lot of love and heart to it. It is respectful of the subject matter and not afraid to embrace the sensitive issues. The cooking puzzles are simple but not repetitive and the gameplay is secondary to the narrative as they move the story along at a nice pace while teaching you about Indian culture and their tasty cuisine. 🥘
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot explain how this game came out of left field. Just absolutely amazingly done. It is such a touching story about growing up, love, loss, family. It touched my heart and had me in tears at the end. I lost my father at a young age, and he also read me bedtime stories that he made up. I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Those tiny little details like the sound of Venba's anklets whenever she walks. Kavin's recklessness can be shown on the animation of the cooking ingredients after he used it. Venba always wipes little Kavin's mouth after she feeds him. I just love Paavalan as a father. The dishes animation and graphic... girl.. SLAPSSSSSS HARDDD. Great story with great message. Always call and text your parents guys, whenever and wherever you are.One more thing, I LOVE how interactive their phone screen is, it's like we're also playing as the character itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Really gorgeous game, clearly the developers put a lot of love into the story and the game! _childDocuments_.review: Been looking foreword to playing this ever since I finished the demo. It's a very short but very sweet playthrough. I've always been interested in learning more about Indian food outside of curries and this was a very wonderful segway into researching Tamil foods to make! And along the way I felt very deeply for all the characters here. I'm the daughter of a first-gen Filipina immigrant myself. Just a great game, fun cooking puzzles, a heartfelt story with a moral of gratitude. Highly recommend! <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game tore my heart out. I cried several times and loved trying to figure out the recipes and put the cookbook back together. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Thought I was getting Indian cooking mama, ended up crying at least four times. 10/10 would recommend.The story of Venba's family is deeply moving. _childDocuments_.review: Venba is a game that tells a story of cultural identity through traditional cooking. It speaks on the difficulties faced by immigrants as well as the split identity their children often struggle with, being torn between tradition/heritage and fitting in to the culture of their new home. It's short, sweet, and beautiful. You can tell there is a lot of love poured into this game and it's something you can enjoy regardless of your own cultural identity.The story follows Venba and her husband Paavalan, immigrants from Tamil Nadu, as they do their best to raise their son Kavin in Canada while still instilling traditional values in him. The story will hold a lot of meaning for the children of first generation immigrants as it touches on struggling with one's own identity and rejecting one's history in order to fit in. The story is emotional, it's sad, but it's also really hopeful and beautiful.I think the saddest moment in the game for me was The gameplay is fairly simple, it's a mix of visual novel with some cooking scenes. The cooking itself is presented mostly as a puzzle. Venba has her mother's old cookbook but since it is worse for wear she had to work on restoring it through her own memory of the recipes. There is no real fail state, if you make a mistake the scene will reset and you can continue trying again with ease. There are also hints if you are struggling, but I find the puzzles simple enough that it's unlikely most people would need to use this. Each recipe also has some optional flavour text that gives more information on the meal being prepared and the character's thoughts at the time -- I thought this was a really nice touch.The visuals for this game are gorgeous. While the art style is simple in the way it is stylised, it's visually appealing and a feast for the eyes. All the food looks delicious, I even found myself looking up some recipes as I was playing to see how the food looked in comparison and I must say they did a really good job getting it spot on.Oh and the music is phenomenal too. I've always enjoyed music from other cultures and Venba has been a gateway into me discovering more cool music.The game is short though. You can finish it in under 2 hours, and if you missed any achievements it's not hard to go back and mop them up in under 3 hours of total gameplay. I still really recommend the game for anyone who wants a lovely narrative driven journey that they can wrap up in a single play session. I can't wait to see what else these devs will put out in the future, we need more stories like this and cultural representation in the gaming world.I'm really hungry now.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a wonderful and heartwarming game! <3 Next week i'm going to be making all these recipes, because damn.... it made my mouth water! And also my eyes... I cried. Ugly tears. The story is heartbreaking, wholesome and authentic, just like the food. Don't play this game on an empty stomach. Also, Play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is beautiful and thought-provoking, though very short. it touches on certain issues of racism, classism, and the immigrant experience -- and leaves it at that, without further exploration or a lingering message. at the end of the day the game is about Venba and her family, though they experience and go through certain events that make commentary on the treatment of immigrants in Canada overall. still, i'm really glad a game like this was made for the sheer experience of understanding the small ways it can be difficult to adjust to a country and culture. the artstyle is beautiful and deceptively cosy; i wasn't expecting to feel as sad as i did in some parts of the game. the cooking mechanic is a bit iffy, though that could be because i played with mouse and keyboard. it seems like it was designed with a controller in mind for sure. just an overall lovely game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim because I like cooking games and this one was on sale. I did not expect such an emotional and uplifting story. I recommend everyone play this game as it is not only a calming gameplay but a relatable and beautiful message.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is the kind of cooking game I love, one which goes through the cooking process in detail, so you feel like you're really making/learning something. It also strikes a good balance in terms of cooking knowledge: if you don't know what you're doing, it's fun to work it out, but if you do know, it's fun to steer things the right way. The game was short, and while I would have enjoyed more time with it, the story rounds out just fine, and the mechanics have their own arc as well. It's just a nice, compact, 1+ hour game.It's hard to talk about the story without spoiling something, given its length, but I found it enjoyable and enriching (pun intended).
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is, at its core, a simple cooking game but it is wrapped in layers of the Indian (Tamilian) socio-cultural experiences of an immigrant family. The gameplay is to a small extent, a visual novel and to a larger extent, a trial and error puzzle. You try to decipher the missing parts of a cookbook that has been given to Venba by her mother, thus, trying to strengthen her roots.What follows is a story across many phases of their life while maintaining the cooking puzzle gameplay. The story is truly heart-warming with themes of immigration, motherhood, marriage, and cultural propagation & fealty. Visual design is stylish and makes animated images of food look truly delicious. Soundtrack is another highlight with my favourite song being Chellakutty - Alpha Something ft. Deva. I think this game is a remarkable effort and I hope to see more from them!Feel free to join my group and follow my Steam Curator for more reviews that focus on indie games & Indian themes.
