I knew there would be a story surrounding it but it wasn't a major interest of mine when I bought the game but I quickly fell head first into the story as soon as I started playing and had my emotions tugged in all different directions.The use of the food as a way of storytelling was incredibly well done. Genuinely made me cry at the end.I would love to see DLC of more recipes done with Venba and Kavin in india.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much looking forward to it and I'm not disappointed!Simple but extremely touching, straight to the point and generous in the way it tells you this story. I'm still sobbing tbhThe gameplay is fun and very satisfying (along with the sound design!). The music are AMAZING omg.So, this game is fantastic, although a little short. I wouldn't have minded 20 to 30 more minutes added to the game. But considering the love put in this game and the size of the team that worked on it for 3 years, I only can be very satisfied by the experience that I just went through. <3<3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a video game; it's a story with some cute, pretty puzzles in it. It almost feels like the modern equivalent of a popup picture book, narrative with sudden burst of interactivity in it. Don't let any of above sound like I'm trying to detract though. It's a very moving story and the art design, sound design and direction are all incredibly well done. If you are like for an enjoyable, film length experience, I highly recommend Venba.A complaint I have (that also ventures into spoilers, stop here if you want to go in untainted) is that the plot could have focused just a little more on Kavin's motivations. Lots of second generation kids have valid reasons for putting distance between themselves and their parents, but Kavin's parents are nothing but sweet, supporting and understanding (if a touch pushy), and it comes off like Kavin is simply acting like an ass for no reason. There was an opportunity for real nuance that is just ever so gently missed.Other than that though, it's a very fun experience, and I would love to try out some of the recipes!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: What a masterpiece of a game. For anyone studying how to tell compelling video games stories, this is a must play. Took me 1.5hrs to complete, played casually in one sitting. I am not Indian nor Canadian, nor do I think you need to be. Though I would imagine if you are either, you'll likely find some wonderful details that would only enrich your experience. #familyportraitThis game could have gone in so many directions that would have made sense from a gameplay perspective. But I'm so glad the team held back and focused on the core of the message. This is a brilliant example of being specifically simple. This is a touching, intimate story that should be experienced in one sitting. Truly a masterclass and masterpiece. What I'd give to work on a game like this. Congratulations to Visai Games! I cannot wait to experience your next story.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The story telling, music, appreciation of recipes and life stories are very well done in this game and I even found myself looking up recipes throughout the game to make a few for my family!While I do recommend the game, there are some fixes that should be addressed prior to anyone purchasing. The game play (in my opinion) was not worth the cost (full play through was a little over an hour) and an skip button would be very useful (cut scenes drag on and while trying to finish achievements).
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Came for a cooking simulator; and finished with tears in my eyes. Venba is absolutely packed full of soul. It does a lot with very little, using the medium of cooking to convey the larger plight of the immigrant story and the sort of half-way-in story that comes for children who feel like they never really fit in. If this were just a visual novel, I'm not sure it would work as well as it does. The choice to make it a game, where you're trying to figure out the recipes; and taking the actions of cooking things does a stellar job of making the story beats impactful. I really appreciate that they tried to come at this from the angle of Venba and her son, as opposed to just focusing everything on one person's perspective. I would so heartily recommend playing this... And then maybe give your folks a call afterwards if you can.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Felt like the game was holding a mirror up to my own life, with almost the exact same conversations I've had with my family. Never did I think a short one hour game would make me cry so much. Definitely worth the price, a beautiful and heart-breaking game depicting the struggles of 1st and 2nd gen immigrants straddling between two cultures.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this experience. Very simple gameplay and a very simple story, but carrying an incredible amount of heartfelt depth if you pay attention.As an Indian immigrant myself, with a father who untimely passed away recently, and an aging mother, this hit very close to home. I'm not gonna lie, I had to stop myself and wipe away some tears when I saw a lot of myself in Kavin, relating to my own childhood and wanting to "fit in" due to all the bullying and embarrassment I faced, but in doing so giving up my roots and distancing myself from my family and my culture.Eventually I did come full circle, reconnecting with my family and heritage, and am now proud of my identity and origins. However now, as an adult who has since migrated again to a different part of the world, I also see a lot of myself in both Venba and Paavalan, striving to adapt to a foreign environment and trying to make ends meet.I know it's a short game (only about 2h, maybe less) and I understand the concerns about "value for money" that other comments have shared, but I certainly got great value out of this game and I would heartily recommend it to anyone.PS:  Call your parents. They miss you.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game while I played it. But it ended up not being for me. A big thing for me was how trying to open the options menu froze the game. As well as the ability to not skip cutscenes. (tho this could be an option in the options menu but idk) I did end up returning the game but I would still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A really short and sweet narrative game.The colours are vibrant, music is catchy and if you like cooking asmr, you're in for a treat.I think its nice that they have also given the recipes for the dishes you cook in-game, in case you want to cook it irl.I would recommend getting this game on sale, I don't think there enough content for the full price though
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game brought me to tears, it's so true to the challenges immigrants face. The inner and outer struggle for authenticity is something many children of immigrants can relate to. Telling that story through recipes was brilliant, I felt so immersed and was invested from start to finish. I can tell a lot of heart went into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I cant not love such a well thought out story that knows how much time it needs to make a point. Caught myself getting way more emotional than I'm used to with a game, probably with how close to home the story came. If I had to make a criticism, it would honestly be that it made me WAY too hungry for food right out of my reach, but in turn inspired me to dig deeper into all they offered. If you can, please give it a go through, worth the money n time.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you're into cozy puzzle games. The music is fun to listen to and the story has a small element of choice. The recipes are fun to make and it does take a bit of logic to figure them out.My only complaint is that I have a grand total of 88 minutes of gameplay and that was enough to finish the whole game. It may have some replayability for the puzzle aspect, but the story parts I've found so far to be unskippable (though you can speed up dialogue a bit) which can get repetitive once you've already played it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it's just cooking and a story, Venba is a simple yet fun game. There are quite a few layers of emotional storytelling that make you think about your choices. Even when you think it's the right choice, it might be wrong. Or they could all be wrong. It's definitely worth playing, even if it's just under 2 hours.Vegetarian Warning: Digital fish were harmed in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: That's a great game!The cooking puzzles are excellent and engaging. Solving them shouldn't take more than a few minutes, but it still leaves a feeling of victory.The story is quite simple but yet so well done (and kinda relatable) that made me emotive a few times.The game itself is kinda short but the experience was good to me all the time, if you're interested I recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I always love cooking games and Venba is no exception. It was so lovely that after I beat it on Steam, I bought it for PS5 and played it with my partner so she could experience the story as well. I loved everything about the game: the setting, story, sound design, art style, music, cooking mechanics, and more. It’s also jam-packed with lots of subtle details that really elevate the immersion and world-building of the game. Fantastic job Visai Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on a whim and I'm so glad I did. It's a very tightly told story with well made cooking mechanics that do a surprisingly good job drawing you in emotionally and not just being speed bumps to the next bit of story delivery. I was holding back the tears, trying not to look crazy in an airport by the end of my short, sweet experience with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best game I've played to date. It was such an emotional journey, one that I'm sure many first generation or diaspora kids can relate to. The game play was calming, reading through their dialogue, cooking traditional South Indian recipes.It all felt very organic, a shared experience of many children of immigrant parents. Being Indo-Canadian I also want to learn from my mom's recipes and feel more connected to my parents regardless of our differences. The story hit hard.I'll be recommending this to all my friends regardless of their ethnicity. There's something here for everyone. Thank you to the developers, the representation was much needed.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: how was this so good😭😭 It was so heartfelt and moving. felt so good when making those delicious foods and music is so fun. I love the characters and their story so much!!! it portrayed struggle of immigration so well and you know where they are coming from exactly. cried at the end I want more of this beautifully made game that is full of passion
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting this game to be more focused on the cooking, but it's mostly a narrative game where you happen to cook in between the story beats.You explore the story of an immigrant family raising their child and the struggle between their home culture and where they emigrated to. While the story spans 20 something years and big events happen, it's generally surface level things.While you have a few cooking puzzles to solve, they aren't that complex. The longest cooking session ends up being towards the end of the story where the mother already knows how to cook well so it's just boils down to "click highlighted things, you can't mess this up" which is just boring and long.I finished it in about 75 minutes. I wouldn't call it a transformative gaming experience, but it's nice that more stories like this are being told. You don't see many games focused on first generation immigrant culture, fitting in, children feeling like outsiders to both where they live and where they parents came from and so on.I hope the developers make more interesting games in the future with a bigger scope!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Super short, very sweet, expect to tear up or cry, especially if you have a tenuous relationship with your own family. Now this contains the recipes as free DLC too, and I can't wait to try making them! It's more like a visual novel with some interactive portions interspersed, but totally worth the play time! If you're on the fence, think of the time you'd spend at a theatre and the cost of a ticket. Now compare that to this and know you're getting a really heartfelt experience made by a team who wants to share an experience, particularly one that might be common for children of immigrant parents.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a game that unironically feeds the soul. As someone who also left friends and family behind to pursue a better life in a different country, it felt strange but also good to see some of my struggles being represented by characters in a game. I saw my struggles with holding on to my culture while still adapting to a new environment; to see my struggles encapsulated by Kavin's realizations at the end of the game was like a lightbulb in my head. It perfectly encapsulates Indian culture, as well as the symbolism of food and family ties in that culture. To cook and feed your loved ones is one of the most profound ways to show your love for your family. This game is one that strums your heartstrings like a guitar, and is one that is able to have it's plot and themes felt deeply by all of its players. I'm so happy that I was able to encounter this game in this lifetime.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game especially touches the heart of immigrant children and our parents, but will surely reach beyond that. The story of Venba is told through the player's attempts to perfect and create their own versions of legacy recipes, bringing out the family's worries, failures, and importantly, their attempts to connect with one another. Playing this made my heart yearn, and I thought of my parents' own legacy recipes and their hope for my better future. This short and hopeful game will touch you, and I sincerely hope everyone plays it!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the gameplay, art, sounds and the music, but the story was the best for me <3 Even if I have never switched cultures, I can still relate to Venba and her relationship with her son. My family was just me and my parents, but they split when I was a young teen and got new partners. Our relationship was not good in the beginning, but it became worse and worse. I have almost no contact with my mom, even though I lived with her (and I also worked under her when I moved out) and meet my dad only every other weekend. I have tried staying connected to them but it never clicked. But now, when I'm 30, my dad is actually trying. It's a bit hard because he lives on the other side of the earth from me, but I'm very happy that he is doing his best and caring about my interests and feelings.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a beautiful game that the moment I finished it, I fired it back up again. I wanted to get the achievements but I also wanted to go back and read all the flavor texts and other dialogue options too. Venba really filled my heart with the love of culture, even though my culture is not the same, I understand wanting to extend the lifeline of your heritage. I also understand where Kavin said he felt like a "tourist" too and that really struck a chord. This is a beautiful game and defines the term "cozy" as to me, there is nothing more comforting than the sound of your parent cooking in the kitchen and looking over their shoulder. It also made me crave Indian food which I had the pleasure of having for the very first time recently and it was absolutely incredible. Venba makes me want to try everything on the menu and I hope everyone votes for this game at the Steam Awards for Outstanding Story-Rich Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a touching visual novel of a family of immigrants in Canada. It's short and sweet but you see how it is going to go from miles away.The food mini-games are of 2 types: two or three where you need to correctly choose how to make certain foods, the others where you just need to click when prompted.There are dialogues where you need to choose between two options without change to the story either way. Kinda pointless.I got the game for cheap in a bundle - that is the only way this is worth purchasing. I can see the thought and love that went into it, but it is just an interactive story that doesn't even last that long. Completed in less than 2 hrs and I was pausing it to do chores around the house.I wouldn't recommend it at full price, kinda nice with a big discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting months for this game! And I can't wait to go back and get all the little achievements. The storytelling in this game was so nuanced and this is what I think visual novels should be like. It really tugs on your heart strings plus now I want to try a lot of new dishes. I also enjoyed that this game took place in Canada.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Venba is a short indie cooking game where you have to cook several different tamil dishes as an indian immigrant in Canada, struggling to fit in during the 1980’s. The story has many touching moments and overall seems authentic and touching. It’s divided in just 7 different chapters each of them is set in a different time in the life of the characters and can have a few different dishes you have to cook together.The game’s graphics are very artistic and very colorful and some of the illustrations seem to have been made with crayons (or imitations of that look) judging by the fuzzy and irregular edges of the drawings. The characters, dishes and ingredients have a stylized and cartoonish look that works very well with the vibrant colors. The music brings up and works well with the Indian heritage of the characters and is enjoyable.Regarding gameplay, the game takes a very casual approach that’s very different from many other games that require quick thinking and mental agility, while adding a sort of puzzle element. Your focus is figuring out the recipe by following clues and not doing the steps necessary quickly. You can take your time and the food won’t burn and if you fail you can just restart with no consequences.The dialogue options, on the other hand, didn't seem to affect the story very much.  15 Achievements. Maybe 1 to 3 hours. Did one run with no guide, but later I had some trouble finding out a few dialogues for the final achievements and replayed the game 3 times. With a guide, 1 hour is probably enough. Easy. The dishes can be restarted as many times as you need Easy, but you need to pay some attention. The achievement that took me more time was  After beating the game once, you can use the chapter select to go to specific levels and it seems to work for the  Venba is a short story driven indie casual cooking game that anyone can play with likable characters and a touching story and colorful illustrations. Figuring out the recipes is fun and the dishes look very appetizing after you finish cooking them.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is both a heart-warming and heart-breaking tale, and is told in a beautiful way. The cooking puzzles are fun and add an interactive element to the narrative, and audio and visual art within the game is phenomenal. I also really like that the devs included the recipes for the meals and information about the music. I did enjoy playing this one, but it is quite short, so for that I think the price can be considered a bit steep. However, it's an experience that I highly recommend if you like games involving food and stories that pull at your heart strings.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful game. I mean this as a compliment - I never imagined such a short game could make me feel so much emotion. I cried sad tears. I cried happy tears. I was truly touched.Genuinely would recommend to anyone who has an evening or afternoon to spare. The artwork was beautiful, the sound design was lovely, the gameplay was fun and satisfying, and I’ve already said how I felt about the story. Thank you to the writer and team behind this game for sharing.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game. A storybook-like game that has its own little activities to do in between, which is a nice touch. Wonderful music, and great sound effects too. The game has a very good UX/UI as well (hints aren't spoon fed, and there's a nice dialogue around what could help you without exactly being a giveaway-hint vs a critical thinking hint). The story was nice as well, with a good delivery and without the unnecessary exposition that a lot of games have nowadays. Instead, the game has you visually infer what's going on in the silence between dialogue. But I found it was a little short and could've been expanded on a little more in certain areas.  I think $15 is a little steep, since the game is less than 3 hours long. I bought it on the summer sale, so the game justified the price with the DLC cookbook. Then again, I've paid much more for much worse, so I will say the price shouldn't push you away from a lovely game. There's a lot of love in it, and that's to be very respected. That being said, I will recommend the game regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: As a first-gen East Asian American, I'm always more in the camp of telling diverse stories that don't always involve not fitting in/cultural assimilation, not because they're untrue, but because there is more to the diaspora than that. However, this game was still very heartfelt and felt special because it was from Venba's POV. I also felt immersed in the game and really appreciated how they meshed the elements of the cooking sim part of the game with how the characters were feeling. It's quite short (a little over an hour, potentially less if you're a really quick reader + good at solving the simple cooking puzzles), but it felt about right given the story they were trying to tell. That might be an issue for some, but I thought it was worth the price- I did get it during the launch sale, though. I definitely teared up a bit a couple of times!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: While I really enjoyed the experience, this is not what I expectedI expected a cooking sim game.And while recipes ARE used as plot tools, the game is actually more of an interactive cartoon.A pleasant interactive cartoon. With sweet characters, and an insight about immigration in general.The Art style is very pleasant as well, same with the music.But again, this is an interactive cartoon. With minimal interactivity.If you want more than an interactive cartoon, you should NOT buy it.If you are ok with an interactive cartoon, focusing on delicious recipes, you may go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with a rich art style, beautiful and absorbing music, thoughtful story and fun cooking mini-games.Overall I enjoyed this game and the story took me on an emotional journey. The way the narrative is presented works well to convey the emotions at the time.The cooking aspect of the game is cute and enjoyable, there are some slight puzzle elements to it but nothing major.The game is mostly a relaxing, interactive story-book with some mini-games, which I enjoyed. Sadly though I was slightly disappointed by how quickly the game progressed and how few of the cooking mini-games there were but that would be more due to my expectations of the game being a bit longer. Highly recommended as an fun, emotional short story game you can play in one night.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but very sweet and at times heartbreaking game about Tamil culture and cuisine combined with the topic of generational differences and the depiction of immigrant parents witnessing their child grow up in/prefer Western culture as well as the POV of the immigrant child itself - something I could deeply relate with, since I grew up with two cultures and felt/still feel "ashamed" about my actual heritage and therefore lean more towards the culture of the country I was born in.I really enjoyed learning about Tamil cuisine - the procedure and ways of cooking it - something I wasn't really aware of prior. Many tidbits in the game that I was already wondering about, but I didn't have to google at all c: Easy to tell how much love was put into this game, the art style is really cute too and while it was a short game, I think the characters were amazingly portrayed and the dialogue was on point as well. The story itself inspired me to think about my own experiences and especially those of my parents more too. Go hug your immigrant parents if you can!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Short but beautiful game, all these recipes take me back to when i was a kid and I would get picky about all the things my parents would make. I loved every minute of my time playing, being an immigrant I feel a lot of the painful things Venba and Paavalan dealt with but this makes me love tamil culture even more fiercely and I even got to practice reading Tamil again after so many years.If I have any criticisms, its that this game makes me so nostalgic to the point that I'm homesick!!! I miss the sounds of Chennai the most, thanks for the capturing that essence as well with the music <3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely albeit rather short game about what it's like to be the child of an immigrant or an immigrant who has a child in a home far away from your native land. Very touching and emotional, I cried several times being an immigrant myself. In the midst of my gardenGrows a palm-tree;Born in the West,Away from the country of palm-trees. I cried: You are like me,For you resemble meIn wandering and peregrination,And the long separation from kith and kin. You alsoGrew up on a foreign soil;Like me,You are far from the country of your birth. May the fertilizing clouds of morningWater you in exile,May the beneficent rains besought by the poorNever forsake you.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a lovely narrative game with very accessible puzzles. I just completed it and have big feelings about it. I enjoyed everything. The attention to details in the art, the music and the sound effects is incredible. A beautiful immersive and emotional game which touches the heart. It is short but worth it in my opinion. As someone who expresses love through food, this game really stroke a chord in my soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Chanced upon this game's demo during Next Fest and was smitten with the writing and dialogue. While it is a short game and wished it was longer, it still managed to make me feel attached to the characters really quickly and tug at my heartstrings throughout.I am not Indian nor an immigrant hence I couldn't really relate as much in those aspects, but putting you in the shoes of Venba really shows you what being a parent is like and what they go through. As children, we may sometimes think of our parents' actions as excessive, but most of the time... it just comes from a place of love.Other than that, music and art were great, the food looked so delicious I wish I could grab the food through the screen..
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: An amazingly relatable and earnest game/story/experience that shows and tells everything it needs in its short runtime, then lingers on long afterwards. Warning: you might want to call your parents afterwards if you haven't done so in a while, and are in a position to.The puzzles rely mostly on visual comprehension/recomposition logic, with very few trial and error bits (mostly during the first one, arguably the hardest in the game). The puzzles are very entertaining to play through and definitely translate the feeling of figuring out a recipe, despite the abstraction of many steps and processes. The main feature is the narrative and aesthetic experience however, with special care given to the sound design (the sounds of the kitchen and the different dishes, oh my). The passage of time, life, relationships, cultural mixing are all broached tactfully and with just enough ellipses that we understand the weight of everything, despite living through it all in a matter of hours. It's masterful, it's probably one of the better crafted games of this kind in recent years delving into complex emotions both foreign and familiar, and it's worth your time, money, thoughts and care. We need more games like Venba, much like we need more people like Venba and her family.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet but needed to take a break to wipe away some tears.This is extremely relatable to play as an indian immigrant. The art is beautiful and the story is very authentically written.Play this if you like short narrative games. Thank you so much to the developers for making this.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a bittersweet but adorable game about Indian culture and being an immigrant, as well as being a second-generation immigrant. It would have been nice to dive deeper into such topics, but the game might've become too text-heavy if that was the case.Venba is short, and drawn in a cute crayon-like artstyle, which supports the narrative. The narrative is simple yet very impactful, and even brought tears to my friend's eyes. It's a great game that lets you relate if you're in a similar situation, and alternatively it's a great way to gain some insight into how life can be, growing up with clashing cultures.The soundtrack is absolutely awesome, and really immerses you in the culture, I highly recommend Venba!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a shame that a game with such a peculiar artstyle and story like  isn’t more well known, but I can only say the nomination for best debut indie game of 2023 is fully deserved!Cook traditional Indian dishes simply by dragging and dropping elements on screen as the semi-torn cookbook says, with minor deduction work when filling in the blanks for missing or ruined pages.You follow the story of Venba, Indian mother who deals with family raising and culture shock of being in another country for better opportunities.Despite how clearly of a tearjerker story this is going to get it is also very well written and the thematic of family and fear of losing the roots of your culture can be universally applied everywhere.With a good story, short length, simple gameplay and lovely graphics, this game is the perfect introduction to more narrative-driven games Maybe some pacing problems here and there, this was the perfect setup to start as a purely culinary game that started to sneak in more and more on the daily life and happenings between each dish, instead the game features some lengthy story sections between dishes to the point of that being the focus of the game instead of how it is marketed as.People could also find the asking price quite steep for the length of the game clocking in between 1 and 2 hours, but this isn't an issue depending how you see it.I liked it, think of it as a movie you can play for an 8$ ticket on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following Venba for quite a while since I first saw a tweet about the game long long ago and I've been waiting for the release day! I knew it was going to be good because of the love and care being put in to the work but I was really blown away by all the detail and tremendous amount of care and craftsmanship put into all the details, the animations, effects, interactions, sound fx and amazing music. It is also such a heartfelt tale that brought tears to my eyes both as a son of parents who are getting older and as a father of a 9 yo who I feel, like Kavin, is growing up too fast in a very different world. It is a beautiful experience that captures a culture, its heart and aspirations through such nuanced storytelling; while every other element adds flavours beautifully around it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: If you love a heavy story type game this game is for you. The mechanics and gameplay in itself is easy and you get into the game quite quickly. I played the game using only my computer mouse and there were fun movements you got to do to make the recipes. I recommend this to anyone that wants to try something new and deep and make sure you have some tissues nearby just incase of some tears! No spoilers but this is a bit more indepth. I found myself sobbing over the story multiple times, the art style is fantastic and really works for this game. The food looks amazing and I had to eat something after playing it. The game is fairly short, it took me almost two hours to complete but I think it is great for this type of emotional game. I wish there were more levels of the cooking in between some of the heavier storytelling elements but you could easily just pause in between levels. More cooking levels would be fun overall because of how it makes you think and try to figure out things. The music and soundscape is also sooooooooo good that I would want to sit with just the sound of oil frying things for hours. Love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about the length of a feature film (I platinumed it in barely over two hours) but it packs a LOT of emotion into those couple hours. If you want a recommendation about whether you should buy and play this, unqualified YES to both. Get the soundtrack too, it's great.*sigh*Food is something immigrant communities carry with them wherever they go, and often it is the one thing that ties both the immigrants themselves and subsequent generations to their ethnicity and culture.This one sentence is Venba's thesis statement, and it discusses it thoroughly. It's short, but sweet. I want to write more, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really amazing and extremely relatable for me growing up as a second generation Eelam Tamil in Toronto. It helped me understand the struggle and sacrifices that my parents went through as well as challenging how I viewed my culture throughout my life. Definitely made me cut onions for sure and communicate more with my family afterwards as well as embrace my culture more especially our diverse food dishes. Fully recommend this game to everyone and hope it inspires people to explore Tamil cuisine as well as culture! I'm definitely going to try making this recipes with my family for sure! நன்றி! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much that I bought it without the soundtrack, but soon regretted it! The story is touching, and so are the characters, even with such a "simple" design. The visual style of the game is unique. And incredible music to go with it!!!I love the noise Venba makes when she walks, very bling bling.The overall length of the game surprised me: I wish it had been longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful narrative game that uses food and cooking as the thread that ties each time period together that this family goes through. Even though the story is very short, about the length of watching a movie, the care and attention to detail that went into every aspect of the game (sound design, music, art direction, UI elements, etc.) goes above and beyond most indie games I've played. It also made me very hungry for dosa, but that was to be expected :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: That was just amazing, I am not from India and this is a good game to learn at least a good bit of Indian culture, that was very good and beautiful. I want see more games like this, learn and appreciate other cultures in such good, wholesome and perfect way. Best game I played for a while! <3 Also, the characters, amazing, keep up with those. Gotta love all of them!!! The details!! Ah I can't express all I think of this game in just one comment. Just made my day. Recommend 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful game! Growing up with a Tamil best friend, the story of this game comes from a place of authenticity and heart. And as a child of an immigrant into North America myself, there were so many lived experiences that I was able to relate to. Now I wish there was an actual recipe book that came out of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that tells the story of Indian family that deals with the challenges of immigrating to Canada in the 80s. The narrative is intertwined with various authentic Indian dishes that the player needs to prepare by following clues and hints provided by the game . It reminded me a bit of Strange Horticulture; definitely a passion project that tells a short but impactful story.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good game, I first got it for the cooking and the art style but as i played the game I focused more on the story. I usually don't cry from any media, especially games but Venba made me sob hysterically. Pretty quick gameplay and not that much recipes, if thats not your thing then this might not be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I just played Venba, a game that tells a short story about Tamil immigrants living in Canada and how their family evolves of the years, all tied together by the mother's cooking.It's a sweet story that brought tears to my eyes and makes me want to learn to cook south Indian food! This is the kind of game I want to make.  A short story told in game form.Definitely recommended!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Embark on a heartwarming journey with this game, where delightful recipes and a compelling storyline evoke strong emotions. Explore Venba's life as she relocates to Canada with her family, re-discovering her mother's various Indian recipes along the way. A word of caution: playing this game on an empty stomach is not recommended, as the charming cooking sessions are sure to leave you craving Indian food!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Everything from the recipes to the sound design is great. Short story worth a play.  Play is pretty easy for a puzzle game but it's more of a very interactive visual novel if you want a better description of gameplay. Bonus owning the game is getting some recipes (after completing the coresponding level) that you can actually make at home that I plan on trying.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited when I realized I was making idli, dosa, chakli, I was fearful for their family, I was punched right in the gut thinking of the traditions and family members I may never see or experience again. I felt seen in a way no other videogame has made me feel seen. Thank you Visai, this game is so special.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I cried, I cried in a 70-minute duration game. It really hit close to home, and all the conversations are on point. I felt so connected with Venba and the family, and it reminded me of who I was when I was a teenager. The cooking mechanics are also fun and visually appetizing. The general art style is great, and the music is amazing too. It's like a small present box with a variety of nice trinkets inside. Totally a well-deserved Games for Impact award for TGA 2023. I'm glad that I played this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆Venba is a sweet and short game with a ton of references to the food, language, design and music of the southern most state of India, Tamil Nadu. The art style is vibrant and cute, the music is lovely and unique, the gameplay is simple and minimal. The gameplay is part visual-novel, where you can make a few dialogue choices, and, part cooking-sim, which is really fun and has tiny puzzle elements. Venba is a really short game but one that is enchanting and entertaining from start to finish. For me, the base price is a bit expensive, but I would highly recommend getting this game during a sale!It is true that this game does not tackle all the complexities faced by Indian immigrants but that doesn't make it a bad game entirely, the primary story it focuses on is the relationship between a mother and her son, and I think it was done beautifully. Including the actual recipes for the 12 dishes and the OSTs in-game is a nice bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It's terrific, but I wouldn't get it unless it were on sale. The art is beautiful, the music is amazing, which is saying a lot since I usually mute BGM. However, it took roughly two hours to complete the game, despite taking it slow and trying everything, reading every text and dialogue options. I hope to see a future DLC or update that could really turn Venba into the game it has the potential to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: So so so cute, I love the artstyle and the music. As the tags say, this is a story game, you can't change what happens but you do get to choose dialogue a few times. I played the whole game in 2.9 hours, I understand not wanting to pay 15€ for that, but keep in mind this is an indie developer/publisher! Very easy achievements, mostly just played the game and got them. The game includes a cook book with actual recipes, which I think is pretty cool! Solid game, loved it even cried a little<3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful short and sweet story. It almost makes me feel guilty that i bought it on sale, granted, it's only 1 hour long. But it tells such a beautiful story with a beautiful meaning and i loved the cooking sounds and gameplay. It just tugs at your heartstrings in all the right ways. Yea.. Short and sweet is really just the perfect way to describe this. Definitely worth it if you can afford it ^-^
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It's very rare I buy a game on release day, but this sold me instantly. As someone who has a parent from the middle-east but grew up in Britain, I could very much relate to the story (mainly from the point of view of the son), including all the twists and turns that happened during his life in-game, and my life in the real world. I've never found any other game to be as relatable as this one.But personal viewpoints aside, it really is a beautiful game. The visuals are lovely, and the food has made me want to try some of the recipes myself! The story has a lot of twists and turns for a game so short, and the story was very emotional in a very real way, that you know it's the story of thousands of families across the world. The music is also wonderful.I feel that games like this, where stories are told and we can learn about other cultures are very important, and we need to encourage more indie developers to tell their stories. Of course, not all games need to tell stories, it's perfectly fine for some escapism into fantasy worlds from time to time, but I'm very glad this game exists and I hope more like it will follow.Now, the game is pretty short (I finished the main playthrough in around 1 hour, then played through most of it again to clean up achievements), so if that puts you off then be warned. That said, I'm 100% happy to have paid the introductory price, but I would understand why some might not want to for the short playtime.tl;dr buy the game, support the devs, and enjoy your time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This was a beautiful game with a touching story and fun gameplay. The puzzles aren't too challenging and by the end of the game you'll have a real craving for Indian food (but they give you the recipes to make them!).It is pretty sad, though. Like, I was not expecting how sad I felt while playing this game. I just finished Resident Evil 8 and that game was happier than this.Still highly highly recommend though!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The story is sweet and presented beautifully. There's a bittersweet something from start to finish that makes it feel realistic, but also a lot of warmth.The cooking is fun, makes you figure out some small stuff by yourself and the recipes are very different from each other so the steps aren't the same everytime.It's very short, but it's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Good things- soundtrack is great. individually.- the UI transition is creative- artstyle is great- The gameplay mechanics is fun. (except the day that doesn't have the instruction)Bad things- the story is kinda short. even though i play it slowly, i still finish it with 70 minutes.- For me, the gameplay can't make me immerse into the main point of game that much.- it can't convince me with the main point of this game that want players to love their culture. (it is a great concept to play around tho). IMO it lacks the scenes that tell about how struggle the main character is.- The soundtrack doesn't suits many scenes.i enjoy this game. but I'm not recommend buying this game if you have to choose from many interesting game in your wishlist. maybe it is a little bit overprice.If this is the only thing in your wishlist, buy it then.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The story is beautiful but too much less gameplay for the price. Not much recipies, not much figuring out. Its a linear story and even the story is too short. Not to say this game is terrible. I am only comparing the price for the gameplay. Else the music, issues and style is quite good. If it explored the food aspect a little deeper, it would have been satisfying,
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend for the story, it's short and sweet.Also beautiful art style and the music goes well into the mix.The cooking portion while somehow fun it doesn't really punish you, if you do a mistake you only redo the step you did wrong, there's no game over.My biggest nitpicks should be that the story is very linear and dialog choices don't impact anything, it might change a few lines of dialog but that's it... there's no replay value because of that.Overall, the game is extremely casual with no real challenge and you can beat in 1 hour and half... but it was a good experience for me at least.As a bonus you have the list of recipes with the steps for you to cook them in real life.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a short, thoughtful visual novel about emigration and family.It's often described as "that cooking game", but there are maybe 4 little cooking puzzles in the whole thing? It's also often billed as "cozy" (I think I actually got my copy in a bundle of "cozy" games), but it's pretty real about the trials of emigration and the difficulty of visibly being an immigrant in a wealthy country. Overall, I enjoyed it, and it was the perfect game for lying sick on the couch with zero energy. it includes actual recipes for the dishes you make in the game! (not that I have the chops to make any of them)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really short and sweet game, beat the whole thing in about 70 minutes. The story pulls at your heartstrings just right so that you aren't left sobbing but you feel sympathetic to the characters in a way that keeps you thinking about them after you've already shut the game off and gone to do something else.I'm a born and raised white american who has never really seen the world outside of my state so I'm not exactly an expert on this topic, but I've heard so many stories not unlike this one in real life from others online and this really adds a whole new layer of perspective to it. Thousands, probably millions of families have experienced this exact story in real life. To me, it's a game with cute visuals, but to some people this is how they grew up.I wouldn't say this game has that much replay value, but if you consider the price worth an hour long story with a really pretty art style and an emotional story then you should definitely play this. Just note that the game is like 70% dialogue and 30% cooking so if reading isn't your thing you may be a little let down. It's a 10/10 from me though. My only real exposure to Indian food has been butter chicken from a restaurant I stopped at on a trip, but I think I'm gonna have to look up some recipes and try them out in real life.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanna like it, but I can't. You play as a newly-wed wife coming from a Tamil background. The game consists of chapters of different stages of her life, only involving her family. It took me less than 1,5 hours to play it entirely.And that's just the problem. All problems she faces as a woman, mother, immigrant and wife are so lightly touched upon that it just never matters. Throw in a random cooking puzzle here and there and a forced teary eyed end. It just does nothing justice really.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The game talks about some hard stuff, like racism, fitting in, and finding yourself.The cooking part is cool and chill. You just drag and drop stuff on a board to match the recipe. The game gives you some tips and facts about Tamil food and culture. The game looks and sounds great too. It makes you feel warm and cozy.bawled my eyes out while I made biryani in the game. In that part, Venba told her mom she would come back soon, but she didn't. And the recipe book her mom gave her was all messed up and she never asked her mom how to restore it. wondered if her mom passed away or something.I felt for her because I'm Asian too and I have a different culture from North Americans. The game shows the gap between the second generation immigrant and their parents, those kids refuses literally anything about where they from. I saw a movie called  that was like this game. It was a good movie that also showed these problems.When I was a kid, I didn't care about my parents or how they felt. But now I get where they're coming from. I felt bad for the dad in this game. He did his best to take care of his family and get used to the new place, but he also had a lot of troubles and stress.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is an simple, yet an incredibly rewarding experience. The gameplay is simple yet engaging, asking you to recreate recipes and fill in the gaps where the recipe book has worn out. In that way, it's best described as a narrative-driven puzzle game. What shines most in Venba is the heart warming narrative. It follow the story of Venba and her son Kavin, facing the troubles of being a family that feels so culturally out of place in a new country.It's about a 1-2 hour experience for a single play-through and closer to 3 hours to 100%. It's worth every cent in my opinion. You also get a free recipe book :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to buy Venba at first considering it's short playtime, but it's heartwarming story and immersive visuals are sure to stick with you far longer than the 70 minute playtime. The love and passion put into this visual novel is evident. I decided to play it twice to unlock all the achievements. Although my second run-through was quite repetitive, I noticed tiny details that enhanced the story. Picking different dialogue options still led the main narrative along, while offering more insight on the family. Details such as text color to represent English vs. Tamil, and the speed of the text from each character made the novel all the more immersive. The work put into this short game definitely pays off.I believe individuals of any cultural and ethnic background will be able to enjoy Venba. I am not South Indian, but as a Filipino-American with two immigrant parents, the story was painfully relatable. Venba explores themes of parenthood and growing up that would resonate with any person. Overall, I would strongly recommend Venba to anyone, and I'll be sure to pester my friends and family to try it out. Though its game play is short, it's a beautiful love letter to South Indian culture, and is most definitely worth a shot if you're interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start the review saying this the game is beautiful and the story can make you cry. BUT those are all the compliments I can give this GAME. Just look at the playtime i couldn't even milk 2 hours out of this game. The game mechanics are basically non existent and the ones that are somewhat interesting don't come back.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Biryani was easier to make than soft fluffy Idlis 10/10 for realism. If you're Indian especially south Indian this game might make you bawl your eyes out and call your parents. The music is great the food looks awesome and the sound design will make you smell the spices frying in oil. There's a lot of love that's gone into this game and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game, at least about its description. It's extremely short, I finished it in 45 minutes. And at least 5 of those minutes were sitting through a 'click the next highlighted object.' The story is great, I love the theme, the conversation it's having. But honestly I could hardly call this a game. It's 95% story. The first two game sections were cool, and I thought I'd get more puzzles. But there is a total of 4 or 5 of the cooking 'games' and they are so short.  And then we get to the part where you're cooking something and it is literally just 5+ minutes of clicking and dragging or clicking and flipping with no story or puzzle or any engagement aside from waiting for the next highlight to pop up. If you want to try this game just know what you're getting into. If you want a short, story based "game" with excellent storytelling but very little gameplay, it's for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This was a unique and cozy game. Not only was the story interesting and heart warming. I also felt like I could smell the wonderful cooking just by seeing the beautiful illustrations. Now I feel inspired to cook more! I recommend this game to anyone that wants to play a cozy game without it taking up too much time.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: An important story, beautifully told- a must-play even if you don't share the experiences with the characters that have brought so many other players to tears. It's short but it has a big impact that lasts well beyond its runtime.Part of that is the included recipe book- which is both well written and contains recipes that taste great!(I can personally recommend the chicken rasam.)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I will say that the game is incredibly short (I finished it in 1.4 hours) but the artwork/animation is beautiful, everything feels complete, and it has an in game cookbook/all the songs so that makes up for the lack of length for me. I knew how the story was gonna play out yet I still got emotional, 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a simple game, it is short, and that is more than fine, and the story is well more than worth the price.It is a sweet, loving game telling a story of self, of culture, and identity and it does so masterfully. It pulls you in quickly, and keeps you with it. It's bittersweet in the ways that all good stories are, and was clearly made with love. I highly recommend playing this game, and settling in for a cozy time that will somehow make you miss home, even when you're in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game got me really hungry :P Amazing art style, it's difficult to make food in art look appealing but this certainly made my mouth water. The game is short and sweet and emotional. It's a peek into the life of an immigrant family, inbetween two cultures, trying to make it all work. The cooking minigames were like a little interactive puzzle, the rest is mostly a visual novel. And a stunning one at that. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game showing how food is tied to your memories and your family.  A story about leaving your home, making a life in a new country, the struggles, what is gained, what is lost and what can still be found no matter what time has passed if you reach out to learn.  I enjoyed my time and learned something.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and I don't remember feeling so many emotions while playing a video game in only a span of 1-2 hours. It's a heartwarming story of immigrants in a new city trying their best to make ends meet to raise their child. This one felt close to home, literally.Please play this game while you learn some delicious recipes with wonderful music playing in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, Idk why it says I played for 8 hours, the game def doesn't take that long. But besides that, omfg this game is so well made, the art is beautiful and the writing and story is amazing. I was so hungry playing Venba, I could practically smell and taste all the dishes. I'm really excited to see what else this wonderful team of creators will make!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is one of those games that remind you what video games as an art form are capable of. As an interactive media, games can tell stories and help us experience them in an immersive manner. Venba does this beautifully by properly utilizing story, emotions, sound design, visual design and raw inspiration. As someone from south India, and with the same name as the lead developer of this game, I cannot deny that it hit me hard. Venba delivers a heart felt story about immigration, culture, and cuisine in the package of a wholesome and colorful video game. This is a love letter to videgames as an art-form that will really hit you hard, especially if you resonate with the culture or the story in general.Thanks for making this team Visai, this is truly magnificent. I highly recommend this game, but beware it might make you leak from your eyes and/or your mouth.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome short narrative game that really gets what makes cooking fun. I'd say I wish it was longer but honestly it felt like the perfect length for the simplicity of the cooking puzzles/mechanics and any added challenge would get in the way of the story and excellent atmosphere.The soundtrack, sound design, and art direction in particular are stellar. The story really captures the mundane pain and joy of Venba's life.Also, it made me call my mom.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and the story it told. I really felt for the characters and the situations they were going through. I could relate to some of the issues that come from being part of a group that isn't part of a dominant culture in the place you reside in. It was very heartwarming and had it's somber moments, but I'm very glad I got to experience it. Figuring out the recipes and making them gave me a thrill that I didn't expect. I would recommend this game to anyone that enjoys cooking in games and/or the story alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a lovely and charming game! I think it's important to set expectations that it is a short game, so you should consider that when deciding to buy it. Otherwise, I felt it was just the perfect length. It's a refreshing and sincere perspective on being an immigrant, growing up and family. It's very hard not to feel connected to the story at the end of the game.Also, I felt so hungry throughout the whole game! I could almost smell the dishes, the art was so beautiful and full of detail. I didn't find the recipe mini-game that obvious for me, but the game has a nice hint system to unblock you whenever you are unsure of the next steps.Beautiful art, soundtrack and sound design (I cried quite a lot at the end). I recommend this game to anyone looking to immerse themselves into something deep and sincere :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I'll begin by addressing the elephant in the room: Venba is one of the more expensive games you'll have played when priced per hour. You shouldn't resent that. Adding length to it would probably have served merely to bloat, and the level of care in every aspect of its presentation justifies the cost for me - even better on sale.I'll also note that you don't need any personal connection to its themes to be deeply affected by its plot. My family tree has about as much geographical diversity as the Galapagian tortoise. If anything, I benefited more from playing the game: while I had academic knowledge of some of the social and cultural difficulties that can exist for families of immigrants, I feel I now have some level of understanding which I didn't before.The gameplay itself is simple. My mum could probably work it out without instructions. However, what elevates it above a visual novel is the satisfaction of inference: successfully 'solving' how to make a recipe is much like the feeling of entering an answer in a crossword, but with an overlay of the colours of the cooking on your screen and the smells in your mind's eye (mind's nose?).However, it's clear that the gameplay wouldn't stand on its own. The story is what we're all here for. It's tough to say much without spoiling things. I'll try to do so with a clumsy metaphor. Work out the values you hold so dear as to not need to think about them. Remind yourself of the person you love the most. What if the two of those were inconsistent with each other?The final thing: today a 'DLC' was added of a virtual cookbook containing English-language instructions for making some of the dishes you make in the game. I think I'll have to try.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a parent or an immigrant but I lived far from my parents and moved from one city to another several times. Sometimes it is quite difficult for me to survive and adapt to a new environment, culture, heritage, food. In the past, my communication was a little lacking with my parents. Even though I don't really feel the story of this game in its entirety, yet it feels close and relatable for me. This game truly depicts the difficulties of living abroad and successfully delivers a journey through the lives of parents and children during difficult times until in the end everyone lives happily with each other only with the context of food and their native culture that unites them. BEAUTIFULLY WRITTEN. This game will always have a place in my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: "Venba" is a perfect combination of cooking puzzles and a wholesome story all in one short game. I've been following the production of this game for a while and instantly bought it when it went live on Steam. From the music to the storyline, I would be lying if I didn't say I got emotional during some parts. I also want to highlight that the game is very educational, and I am excited to learn more about the culture. (I would also love it if there was a collection of the recipes featured in the game)So I would love to recommend this game to anyone who wants a short and sweet game, with amazing visuals, music, and storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I ended up refunding it.While the story was incredible and deeply relatable—especially as an immigrant in Canada, I connected with the main characters— there is basically no gameplay.I was very excited when I saw cooking simulator, but there were very few recipes to cook, and the pacing felt rushed toward the end. You quickly went through a handful of recipes, and that was it.While other $5 games offer 3-9 hours of content, this game feels too overpriced.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is another game where it's hard to determine if it is "worth the price" So let's get the things that might determine that for a person out of the way.1) The game is short. I finished the story in 94 minutes. So just under an hour and a half. That's without me having a few achievements to go back for. One of which I'm gonna have to play through the whole game again for I think. Not that I mind, because I enjoyed it. Point is. No matter what a game contains, is a game with 1.5 hours of gameplay (depending on how quickly you figure things out and achievement hunting) worth $15 for you? If the answer is no.... well maybe way for it to be on sale and ask again. If it's still no... this game might disappoint you.2) I originally wanted this game because it reminded me of Cooking Mama and I want to say it did scratch that itch. The way you cook in this game is not quite the same, but similar enough that if you enjoyed Cooking Mama you'll probably enjoy the mechanics here. The thing though is that not a whole lot of the game is cooking. There is more story unfolding than there is cooking. The cooking is fun. The puzzles of figuring out the recipes is fun and of mild difficulty. If you are wanting a Cooking Mama like game though where the majority of the game is cooking, this won't be it and you will be disappointed if that's all you want.Still here? Okay. Let's go on then.Venba is a beautiful story of passing down culture to your children, with a focus of passing it on down through food. That's the surface level though. More specifically it's the struggle of passing down your culture as an immigrant and dealing with the divide that can happen when you are wholly part of your culture and your child is growing into the norms around them. There's also the aspect of your child being bullied for being "different" by those who fall into the social norms. Them feeling as if they need to seperate themselves form their culture to fit in.On a level that I think will fit anyone who is a parent though... it's a story of just struggling to raise your kid the way you want. Struggling with what you want to pass on and teach. Your morals, your values, your culture.... and trying to make it fit with the kind of life YOUR CHILD wants to live. A story of trying to not be overbearing, of realizing when you as a parent need to step back. Then the struggle that persists through the entire story no matter how it shifts. The importance of family, giving up things for your child, worrying about if you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it all up, and living with some of the regrets you might have as a parent.This story was really touching. I'm not an immigrant. I'm a white woman in Kansas. I don't exactly have a lot of culture to pass down to my kid either. There are some things I try to pass on to him though. Struggles I see as my kid grows and his interests change as he grows obsessed with what is popular. Meanwhile I'm just trying to help him stay himself and be true to himself and that he doesn't have to follow the crowd on what is "cool". Something I know will just be harder as he gets older.So I can relate with the story here, despite my heritage and no being able to relate to Venba on a cultural level. I do relate with her though on the mother level. On the parent level.This game depicts that struggle that we all have as parents in such a beautiful and amazing way. Probably one of the most realistic depictions of this kind of struggle I've seen in a game.So on the story alone I recommend this game. Especially if you are a parent, or if you are a kid that has struggled with identifying or not with how you were raised.I also have to say that I love that so much of this story is told through my favorite language. The language of food. So much can be learned about a culture and your heritage through food. I love that.On a game play level, as I said it gives Cooking Mama vibes. Not exactly the same, but still pretty close. I wish so much there was more cooking. I'd love if there was eventually a DLC with Venba teaching Kavin more recipes. Just so we can do the cooking more.But what exactly is the cooking gameplay? You are cooking from Venba's mothers recipe book. Sadly Venba hasn't been able to use it a ton when we first start the game. Assumingly because she can't find the ingredients in Canada. The cookbook is damaged with pages torn and water stains. So part of the recipes are missing and you have to use Venba's memories of watching her mom cook, context clues from the recipe book, and logic to determine what you are supposed to do. It was really interesting as someone who knows nothing about Indian cooking. I would assume this would be easier for people who know the dishes? Since you'll at least know the order of things, but I could be very wrong.Also the food looks delicious! They announced they are making a cookbook and I can't wait to get it and try some recipes.But seeing all the cool dishes has me more interested in Indian cooking and I really enjoyed how everything was presented.Down to the more technical stuff.Performance was great. I had zero issues. Art style is absolutely beautiful! Again the food looks delicious and has me intrigued! The soundtrack is AMAZING!!! I've never listened to Indian music really (maybe a few songs here and there), but I really want to get the soundtrack for this game cause it is SO good!Overall Venba is a game for people who don't mind pay a bit for a short experience that will still be fun to replay if you are the kind who like to replay a story simply because you liked it and want to experience it again. It hits you in the feels and makes your tummy growl.100% recommend.Now.... Off I go to achievement hunt!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a nice game, but it was not what I wanted it to be. The story is heartfelt and sad, but I wish the gameplay was a little more than just clicking through dialogue. I was most interested in this game for the cooking aspect, which unfortunately makes up only a very small portion of it. If you're interested in a short story about heritage and family, this could be for you. If you're interested in a cooking game, this will probably be a little disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game but really short. Very much love into the game but i wish there was more "cooking" mechanics in the game. More into the story than the cooking and I wish there was more story as well to connect with the characters. Also would love more recipes to make or added as a reward when completing the game for players to try and make irl.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Sort of an interactive novel with cooking puzzles. You may get hungry playing this, because I know I did.You're gonna finish this in half an hour if you can do most of the cooking tasks correctly or with little error. If you have difficultly, clock in about two hours. Three hours max. This might be a deterrent for some players so keep that in mind. But keep in mind that a book can be about $14-$20 USD so if you think about how you get some puzzles out of this, it might change your mind. Or it might not and you'll opt for a book.There's not much replayability unless you want to get all the achievements. That's not a huge draw for me, though these achievements will give you a bit more feel for the story being told. And that story is a very emotional one. It's one of coming to a new country for opportunity, acceptance, and trying to fit in. It's your child rejecting their identity in an attempt to fit in and seem less "weird". It's love and loss. A lot of loss. A lot of love. It's told through cooking.You don't have to be Tamil to find this story speaking to you, I promise.There's an option to turn off head bobbing and screen shaking, so the devs have my love for that. From the bottom of my heart, I thank you very much for that. The kindness shown when this was asked for is why I purchased the game. I was already interested as it was, but seeing how this was handled was really why I was confident in purchasing. So I don't have to worry about getting nauseated while playing. Which is great, considering I should be focusing on that food and story! I don't have to worry about my health. Nothing scary I have to address.I wish the game was longer. I wish Venba could talk more about her family, falling in love, and had more flashbacks to what she had fought against so I could get a sense of Kavin having a journey to be proud of his heritage and everything his parents fought for. I wanted to see a little more of Paavalan's writing career or even his bedtime stories he once told to Kavin. I feel like there could have been places to introduce more cuisine (or even Venba's distaste of Westernized homogenized cuisine). The flashback with the soup is perhaps one of the strongest parts and I wish we could have had more flashbacks, like Venba showing us just why her mother's dosa recipe is so special and not because the recipe is superior. We know recipes from our parents and grandparents have something special to them, so it would have been nice to see this go further and then eventually segue into Kavin's memories of his upbringing.However this is a small studio. This is a small budget. This doesn't say anything wrong happened. If anything, I was so lost in the story I wanted more. Everything was so very right that I needed more of the story. I'm a glutton and I was being given "fine dining" in the form of a good story and it ended all too soon.While I'll stand by that there needed to be more, I'm still satisfied with recommending it with the warning that you may feel a little dissatisfied that you didn't see more. Venba transports you to a specific time and will conjure up specific feelings, potentially because you may have experienced this in your life and you'll desperately want to see more. Or you'll just appreciate the story that you're screaming that this can't be it and you need more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write a lot of reviews for games, but for this I had to make an exception. Venba was the first game in a very long time to make me cry.  The art style is gorgeous and feels so homely in way that's both fresh yet familiar, the music was spot-on (my family doesn't speak Tamil but blasting old Marathi and Hindi music while cooking is close enough lol), and the gameplay was delicious! But what hits me hardest by far was the story... it feels so cathartic experiencing a piece of media that Understands what it's like to be a 1st and 2nd gen immigrant, the joys of cooking food your family makes, and the struggles of juggling multiple identities. The length of the game is just enough to give us that catharsis, but I do wish there were more recipes in the game! Hats off to the team for a solid debut and I look forward to more games they make in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The art is beautiful, the music is great, and the story was very touching. However, I found the game disappointing, as it didn't offer much as a puzzle game. Not all the recipes were puzzles, and the ones that were puzzles were extremely straight-forward.  I would still recommend the game because I did enjoy it for what it was, and I want to support this South Indian cooking game in the hopes of its success promoting future South Indian cooking games :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re on the fence but think this game might be for you please take the leap. I promise you won’t regret it. This game has my whole heart, an instant new favourite. The soundtrack, the art, the story, the mechanics… everything was perfection. Yes, it is a short game but that makes it all the more beautiful and memorable. I recommend carving out a few hours, putting on your headphones and emerging yourself completely.Thank you to the devs for this unique heartwarming game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Verba was a good cozy game with a great story-line. It tells the story of a family that has immigrated to Canada and decide to raise their child in this foreign place for the hopes of a better life and opportunities. The soundtrack was great and I appreciated the art style. This game only has a handful of puzzles that are pretty simple to solve. I would recommend this game if you are looking for a good story, but not if you are looking for a challenging set of puzzles to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Great indie (jaja) with innovative gameplay and implicated developers. The cooking is easy, the story hits deep and make you feel like living there with the characters. All in all, a ten out of ten experience. Games like this, good in every way and sensible with culture is what videogames are for.Spoilers: The story narrates frankly what a family of a second generation born goes through.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed both the story and the cooking interactive aspects of this visual novel. I love this kind of story that talks about real life problems and lets people see into a way of being that they might never have otherwise. I'm super happy I bought this and would love if it were expanded with some further recipes/background chapters etc.It took me 80 minutes to play through, and while some may say it's expensive for that, it's very normal to pay this amount for a cinema ticket or something similar, and these sorts of games don't have the ability to scale up/bring in funding from other parts of the company, like massive 100+ hour games do. Thank you to the team for making this game and I look forward to future stories!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A short little game about the Southeast Asian diaspora told through cooking. I am not from India, nor do I speak or read Tamil, but the experiences told here are similar to my own. The music is wonderful to listen to as you figure out how to make Tamil dishes from a cookbook passed down from generation to generation; furthermore, the game also provides some delicious flavor text on how some of these dishes are traditionally prepared and served. A cozy title for sure! Now if you'll excuse me, I think I'll be heading out to eat some goat biryani...
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: What an emotional punch in a fairly simple concept. This game is not long, but that means the cadence of the story needs to be told with just the correct rhythm.
