And it succeeds there. It tugs at the heartstrings, but not overtly so. At the end, it feels like an honest, raw telling where it's obvious a lot of attention went into detail. Short form of it makes it more demanding, IMO, and in the end, this is a gorgeous little package that should be savoured even if one's not jotting down the recipes for later.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: As an immigrant, I appreciate seeing stories that portray what it's like to create a new life away from your country of origin. And experiencing the good and bad things from it. Beyond that, the fact that this game shares that POV using cooking mechanics is fantastic. I hope to see more games like this -and with the same recognition that Venba received!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game and it left me a bit emotional. I liked the concept of it all and the meaning behind it. However, I think it's really overpriced for what you get. I hate to say that because I love supporting indie developers, but for a game that falls at 1.3 hours of play time with little actual gameplay... It's not worth the price. I would wait until it's on sale like I did (I got it for about $7).
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly neat and cosy game, but I do have some issues with it (as a South Indian whose family has moved overseas a few decades ago).1. (Neutral) The game seems to be written from the POV of the "child", which is alright but it misses a lot of the core issues immigrants face. Towards the end, it did feel like they were trying to make up for it by introducing more issues in a little cringey way. I do understand that its hard to really portray the experiences to someone who hasn't been in those shoes, so I won't judge the narrative harshly for that.2. (Positive) The game mechanics are alright, trying to get you to think about ingredients and how the order would work.3. (Negative) The game's way of calculating achievements is terrible. One minor misclick and your entire run is spoiled. If you forget <insert thing on every level> on one of the levels, you need to replay the entire game (an hour-ish) just to be able to get that <secret achievement>. This also isn't helped by the fact that the text progresses at weird intervals and there's no "fast forward" or "skip seen text" like with many other VNs, making getting the 100% completion hard unless you follow a guide from the start... which would spoil the experience of the game. All in all, I still do recommend playing this game, though you might want to wait for a sale because its kind of high priced. Then again, its an indie game with a nice concept, so I don't mind recommending it for full price if you're really interested in supporting the developers. Playing this game reminded me that I have a limited time with my elders, and a lot of these recipes and culture will be lost over time if I do nothing... so I'll try my best to learn recipes from my grandma as much as possible from now on... and document it as properly as I can so that I can pass it down to my kids (if I ever have some), or to my friends' kids... or just random neighbours in my community.I do hope to see more from the studio... I'm fairly sure they have interesting stories and experiences that would be wonderfully expressed in the form of a VN, because there were so many minor things throughout the VN that portrays the passing of time (like changing cultures, especially for people who identify strongly with more than one culture over their life).
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one the main reasons I bought this was for the recipes-I love Indian food! That being said, it's a really sweet little game that really makes you care about the characters. I did find the recipes a bit hard to follow now and again, but there are very helpful hints when you get stuck. All in all, well worth the $8.99. Okay, gonna go cook some biryani now.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I went back and forth on how to rate this. I went in expecting a cooking game, and wound up enjoying a puzzle game with a story that made me cry more than once. I wish it was a bit longer, but it never overstayed its welcome. A definite buy, if you love a good story and some simple, satisfying puzzles based on cuisine most folks aren't familiar with.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Want to cook some South Indian food and cry? Have I got a game for you!Seriously, this game is great, and the writing is really sharp. It's tough to write a drama without having a "villain" (or at least an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) to get the plot moving, but they nailed it; there's no bad guys here, just good people struggling to communicate. You don't have to come from the same background to empathize with Venba and her family, and without getting into spoilers, it's heartbreaking to watch at points since you can't help but root for everyone involved.So yeah, it's great. If you're interested enough to be looking at the reviews, you'll probably enjoy it. (Just don't play it when hungry, lol)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, and I have been waiting for the launch. I even checked my steam every 30 minutes on July 31st, and it was justified! I love how, even though I do not relate to the family's struggles, or the culture, it still had a strong grasp of my emotion! Beautiful story telling, delicious looking food, intuitive game play, and overall it's just so lovely!The game is pretty short, but it was fun, and it did not get old when you're playing it again and again! super wholesome, super lovely! it's truly amazing! Now i'm off to learn how to make the dishes in real life.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a beautiful story, but some buyers may find the price unjustified for the game's length. I haven't replayed it but  there are a number of secret achievement to unlock that might justify doing so. I didn't find the puzzles to be particularly challenging, but many were engaging, requiring some thought to figure, and neither break the immersion of recreating a recipe with incomplete information nor distract from the narrative. I think this game is an excellent example of storytelling in the medium, I wasn't expecting to cry but I sure did. If you can afford to spend $13 on what may only be an hour long experience then I would strongly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game. The visuals were great and the food made me hungry to look at. I will say this game is the shortest game I've played at a 15$ price. I expected it to be somewhat short when I bought it but this took me like an hour and half to play though. I would buy this game if you are looking to appreciate the art and food but not if you are looking for hours and hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The food you make in-game looks gorgeous, I really want to get some Indian food right now...The game in general looks amazing, especially the characters.I really liked the story and music, the gameplay is like a cooking puzzle game, but the cooking could have been a bit more fleshed out and detailed in what you need to do before you finish a recipe (like cutting or washing ingredients first). 4 out of 5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: short and bittersweet. my parents were immigrants so kavin gave me mixed feelings.. mostly because i saw myself in him, recognized those conflicting desires to fit in and be "normal" versus enjoying things provided by my parents. beautiful game that has a lovely cookbook, and made me want to cry at some parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, you can play the entire game BEFORE THE REFUND PERIOD CLOSES without rushing through it.So, if you have the spare money I highly suggest playing the game, don't rush take it slow and enjoy it.and if you don't enjoy it... just refund it! Trust me you'll have the spare time. I got stuck on some puzzles for a while and even took a small break to get a snack and had 40 minutes left before the refund window closed.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a heartwarming, gutwrenching, and incredibly beautiful game. I loved the synergy between the cooking puzzles and the narrative elements. Many details within the game felt deeply personal to me as I grew up in a part-Telugu, part-Bangla household. But, even if you're someone who is unfamiliar with South Indian food, culture, and themes... there is something incredible for you to experience here. We've all experienced the love language of food, and this game is a celebration of that universal, shared  experience.(I also have to bow down to the sound design and the music in this game. It is PHENOMENAL. When they said "hear what you can't taste", they REALLY meant it. The OST is also beautifully composed and produced. I'll be listening to it on loop these next few weeks!)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: While I consider myself a connoisseur of independent games, I have to admit that when I started Venba I had doubts on how much I could get into it given that I'm not Tamil, an immigrant, or a mother. But two hours later I was openly sobbing as I played. The game just does such a good job putting you into the shoes of the protagonist in a way that makes some parts of the game legitimately heartbreaking.While 15 dollars could be said to be a bit much for such a short experience (and one without too much gameplay), I've always believed in quality over quantity of game time. And I can say I felt more emotion and catharsis playing 2 hours of Venba than I did playing 60 hours of most AAA games.If I want to impart anything, it's that even if this game seems like something that just "isn't for you", I implore you to give it a shot. It may surprise you in just how moving it can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a wonderful go at your own pace slice of life cooking game that has you puzzle solving the recipes much like Venba and her family do with their lives. This is truly about family, love, and loss. Keeping memories close while making new ones. It does get sad at times, but much like life the game helps you keep going and see this family's story to a contented ending. It is a quick play through so good for if you want something calming to do for a few hours. The music and recipe book are added bonuses. As someone who is not of Indian culture I am looking forward to exploring the recipes in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba was a long awaited game, and experiencing it will be a very significant memory with all its story, music, and artwork. The plot is driven by an immigrant Indian, already a unique yet resonating background, and through cooking minigames and narrative the game takes you through the family's life. Colorful artwork and creative use of level design bring a realistic take on Indian 1st and 2nd generation immigrants' lives into a simple, short, but emotional game. While the game length and amount of "play" can be surprising, the emotional quality, dedication to depicting extra authentic culture in game, and the charm make it an incredible title all its own and one I know many kids will be sharing with their friends and family instantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals are pretty, but the game is way too short for the price. Cooking is very linear and generally you don't get rewarded for completing/mastering any of the mechanics.The story itself has some potential, however it feels predictable and it skims over any and all deep topics that it tried to present.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: this is such a beautiful game. i don't even know how to express it; the stories of grief and culture and identity are so wonderfully done. it was an honor to learn about this section of indian culture and food as i grew up in a very ethnically homogeneous area in wisconsin. my only complaint that it wasn't longer! i suppose, however, that i'll just have to do my own research and even try to find some of these recipes to try myself. thank you for making this game and spreading such a lovely message! 10/10 :D
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't a ton of interactions, it is more an interactive storytelling experience. The story is so real, so sincere and so beautifully constructed. There is something truly genuine about having the player interact with the culture of the protagonists through food. It's a great way to engage with the player and continue the main story with nice details in the background. Also the main story feels very real because it touches such a wide range of emotions from happiness, family, struggle, immigration and xenophobia but do it so subtly. Definitely recommend, if you like story driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A game about cooking and family life.The art style is unique.The story was wholesome with a few serious tones in between. The Cooking parts are like a puzzle game and aren't to hard to solve when making each dish.Game is short and to the point, and the dishes in this are also based on real Indian recipes. It's a thumbs up for this one for sure, and i would highly recommend giving this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is an impressively handled short story. It centers around a small family, two parents trying to raise a child in a place and culture that is very different from what they grew up with. And so it artfully explores each member's perspective and approach to handling this cultural clash, and how that impacts their relationships with each other.Food is a one of the defining features of any culture and this game cleverly incorporates that fact into a set of simple, but yet oddly satisfying puzzles that push you to complete the recipes from a damaged cookbook.This touching narrative is wrapped with in a colorful 2D art style that is a pleasure to see and served with some wonderful music on the side (honestly there were times I just stopped to jam).Venba also happens to explore a culture I am not personally very familiar with. I won't pretend that I now know how to speak Tamil or could cook any of the interesting recipes on display myself, but it's nice to get a taste of something different, even it is just an appetizer ;)The game is fairly short, about an hour or so. I wouldn't have minded if it was longer, but it made use of its time wisely and didn't overstay its welcome. I can respect and appreciate that (in fact I've become partial to shorter games lately to be honest) <3Get it. Play it. Enjoy it. And then uh.... let's maybe give our parents a call eh?
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the cooking mechanics here - they actually felt like the process of learning a new recipe. And the integration with the story and the way cooking intersects with life and memories was great too. The story was pretty heavily tragic and it was interesting how it balances that with the lighter aspects of life!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I beat Venba in less than two hours. I'd say I wish it were longer but it never really wore out its welcomeand it hit me in a place very very few games can. It's one thing to see a game or book or something about the story of blackness in the states, or east Asian immigration ot the west, or other stories about the immigrants from global south to the West. It's another thing entirely to have a game entirely devoted to your experience of straddling two worlds. To see someone who looks like you and has the same feelings, fears and hangups and it to be on a different side of that battle....it's evocative and heart-wrenching.I know exactly what's going to happen not because I know these tropes or because I've read media that follow this format. I know each line and what's going to happen because I have lived it and I can see the choices I made...the statements said, and not said. Venba hit because it turned a mirror onto me, and said "look at you. This is hte life you've lived. The lives your parents did. What are you going to do with it?" It doesn't feel trite because it's real and feels like it was written by someone who experienced it and who was molded by it. There was never a slur on screen and never an overt act of racial violence but all of the little microaggressions and othering elements were almost painfully fronted in the way those acts often are.  I am a Kavin; this game was a dagger through my heart and it was great. I'll never be the same. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, relaxing and fantastic game that touches on real issues. I found myself teary eyed while playing this game due to the hardships the family faced. Food and their culture always brought their family together. This game emphasizes wonderfully on the importance of culture and the lengths that families will go through to ensure their children have a better life.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game punched me in the throat, broke my heart, drove me to the hospital, and lovingly stayed by my side the whole time.  Wow wow wow. Seriously, wow. But really, uber seriously, this game was amazing. The story-line, the different perspectives of Amma and Kavin, their reconciliation. Beautifully told. I only wish that we got to repair more recipes.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a short and heartfelt game about the power of food to bring people together. I've been playing video games all my life, and this has been the only game that's made me cry. The experiences of the immigrant characters and their trials in a new world and balancing their two cultures while raising a child felt so authentic that it was instantly relatable to me. I saw my own childhood in this game, and I never knew I needed that part of me to be seen. The art style and sound design were immersive and charming, and its length felt perfect for what it was. I really enjoyed learning about foods from a culture I admittedly know little about, and everything looked so delicious. This has easily become one of my favorite storytelling experiences, and I'll be recommending it to everyone I can.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a sweet game.  The story was short and straight to the point but have so much emotion and love put into it. I adored the art style and was so pleasing to look at. Just a little over an hour and I wish it was a little longer but the story doesn't need to tell more so I understand. If you have a bit of free time and $15 I would definitely recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, I was hoping for more of this game. I do not know much about other cultures and I was hoping this would sort of launch a game that helped me learn and appreciate more of the culture. I feel like it missed its mark, at least for me who has never had Indian food before and doesn't understand how the Tamil life is. The game is also incredibly short so even on sale it would be hard to recommend since the storytelling itself felt lacking. I wish they would have gone into more detail not only with the story but the cooking itself. When they made the dinner spread I had NO idea what was going on and that's probably around the time I realized the game just wasn't for me, but I did want to at least finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A cautious recommendation but because of the story but the game lacks gameplay oomph.The game really highlights the struggle of moving to a new country, the uncertainty and financial anxiety of the move, and the sense of loss as your children grow up in a culture that isn’t your own. It’s understandable and approachable to folks who have been through and folks who haven’t. If you have been through it, the extra details like  hit like a brick to the gut. The game really captures the subtle details right (). I also appreciated that the game didn’t feel the need to explain every event and let you figure out things via just the visuals. However, the game length did feel a bit short especially since you only see one perspective.The gameplay is kinda lacking. Cooking is fun and it feels like an adventure game where you have mini puzzles needing logic to make some recipes but you only do it a handful of times. The rest of the time, there’s just one path. I would have appreciated more complexity here but I’m not sure how they could have incorporated it in. Florence, a very similar game in terms of gameplay, had a much better balance of this but even that game struggled with incorporating complex gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 stars overall! While it was pretty short, this was an absolutely lovely game. Though I'm not Indian, I can absolutely relate to so many of the themes in the game. The sacrifices Venba and her husband made for their children ring true of so many families of color, and the embarrassment Kavin felt towards his background and the food his mother made (pushing him away from his culture) is also so relatable and real. I love the art style of the game, and the care and heart that was put into it. The soundtrack is authentic and enjoyable, and the story itself is very moving. I definitely recommend this as a story and an experience, more so than a game. In that regard, I wish there more recipes you could cook, maybe in a DLC or something in an 'arcade' mode. But the game is still very cute and heartwarming.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this game! It is a beautiful story of the process of life and the differences and hardships faced by first and second generation immigrants. The art style is so beautiful and the puzzles are fun and new every time with different levels of complexity. My only complaint is that it's so short! I want to do more recipe puzzles! But it definitely feels complete and enriching. I would absolutely recommend this game if you like puzzles and grounded stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: very moving and personal story - beautyful artstyle great music gameplay was suitable for a cooking game.I had to pause and stop playing because it hit me right in the feels .. this game is truly special and extremely well designed from the story telling perspective a lot is shown - silent moments that say so much very movie like experience made me feel like I wanna try out all of these dishes ♥TLDR: GET THIS GAME !
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, very cute and kinda emotionally heavy! It's a great story and I feel would be a wonderful game to show relatable struggle for those who are 1st or 2nd generation immigrants. My only complaint is that its short and there isn't as much cooking as I thought there would be, I did buy this mainly for that. But I'd still give it a positive review due to the storytelling and art style. Worth the play through 16/10 would read the flavor text again.Also remember to call your mom!  :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Game saved me before I even played it. I didn't realize I lost my credit card at a Ramen shop yesterday and Steam didn't have my new credit card info. So when I went to buy Venba, I couldn't and luckily discovered that my credit card was missing10/10Seriously though - while short, Venba is an incredible and touching story that'll bring you to tears. The cooking puzzles are simple and relaxing and would highly recommend a playthrough for a relaxing evening!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. I didn't get anything more out of this being a game than if it had been any other non-interactive media. I enjoyed the music the most. If you're the type who likes being told stories through games then this might be a good pick for you, but since the choices are meaningless and the puzzles are a matter of trial and error for the most part, no part of the game felt satisfying to play or complete for me.I want to see games do different things like this though, so even if I didn't enjoy the game it's still worth recommending.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game was beautiful and hit home so many times. Well done to the creators for making a game that really highlighted the NRI life from both perspectives. I was crying far too many times while reading the conversations, remembering my childhood, relating to the many things Kavin either said or did as a kid. The cooking was a great touch, I absolutely need to play this game with my parents. Loved it so much
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little game. It's light on gameplay but that makes it a very calming way to spend a couple hours, and the narrative is very personal and rich. It gave me a glimpse into what it's like moving to another country with a different culture, letting me see a perspective I didn't really have in real life - which makes it a wonderful story. There's a lot of attention to detail to convey the characters, and to celebrate Tamil culture.I also really really want to taste as many types of dosa possible now.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of my absolute favorites so far this year, and it was very well worth the wait! Firstly, the art style is so lovingly done, the characters and their designs are spot on and the food looks so amazing in this non-realistic style that you'll still get hungry. The music is an absolute bop and the cooking mechanics, puzzles?, I'm not sure but they're fun and rewarding. However, above all else, the story, oml. This has to be one of THE BEST stories of an indie game I've ever had the delight of playing! An immigration story, finding purpose, the fear of new things, and regret all played key moments in this games narrative. It made you mad at characters, sad for others, and ffs someone give Venba a mf hug! I had an immense joy playing this game, and I will absolutely love making a review of it! WOULD VERY MUCH RECOMMEND!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: this is a short and sweet game that will inevitably make you tear up and want to hug your mother. im not south indian, im actually bangladeshi, but the struggles that the son goes through are so incredibly relatable, and yet, the way which the mother responded to him made my heart ache. the texting scenes especially made me feel a bit miserable. its a great, heartwarming (and heartbreaking) game for anyone who's willing to spend a bit more than an hour of their time on it
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A short game about a woman making food for her husband and child using her own mothers recipe book. The game is tender and sweet, but also a little sad. Makes you realize how fast time flies. It was fun for me, however I wish you were able to skip the cut scenes because I was trying to 100% the achievements and it just took too long. Would recommend if you were looking for something quick to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba was a really great experience. It really captures a feeling of distance and loss for the hope of opportunity... sometimes opportunity that doesn't develop for everyone. In this game you play as Venba she's a young immigrant living in Canada with her husband Paavalan.On the first morning she isn't feeling well and wants to cook a meal for Paavalan and herself before they start their day.She retrieves a cookbook her mother had made for her before she left from India because she wants to have a taste of home to calm her symptoms. When she opens the cookbook she finds that a lot of the pages are damaged. Venba wants to repair her mothers cookbook.The rest of the game you follow Venba and her family through conversations and scenarios as Venba and Kavin try to repair the cookbook.I think that this is more of a story driven experience than a "cooking mama" style game, that being said, I would love to see a DLC for more recipes someday. Maybe Kavin has Venba on a video call for instructions and he and his friends make some and enjoy some of the meals all together. I think the art style is so vibrant and pretty. This is one of those games where if it catches you at the right moment it can bring you back to memories of people and places that you might have forgotten about. I would recommend giving Venba a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba tells and interesting and empathetic story in a shorter time than many games get through their tutorials. You play as an Indian woman, the titular Venba, who has immigrated to Canada with her husband. Through the course of the game, you cook several Tamil dishes which basically work as the game's puzzles because the instructions are sometimes vague, obscured, or missing. Beyond the gameplay that these recipes bring, the recipes also tie into the narrative and allow the game to ask big questions around culture. Are you who you are because of where you're from? Or because of who your family is? Or is it both or neither?Video games allow you to inhabit someone else's shoes better than any other type of media. You see through a character's eyes, act through their hands, and empathize with their experiences. Venba is a wonderful example of this unique ability, helping you learn more about and appreciate things that you may never have had any exposure to or personal experience with. And it does it in a fun way! It's really great and I'm really happy this game exists.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if the Devs will ever see this, but I had to provide feedback after picking up this game. I was introduced to this game by a youtube play-through. I have never picked up a game BEFORE the play-through was complete, let alone finish it before the Finale was posted. Yet this game hit me at a deeper level than I every thought possible. I work with a lot of transplants from India, and my wife works with newly arrived refuges to help them integrate into our society. But this story of the loneliness and isolation that can come about not just from society, but from watching your children assimilate to that society in a way that you can't - it just hit me to the core. I am having problems thinking of another book, movie, story, or game that hit me this hard. This is an amazing game, and as soon as I finished, I immediately made my wife play it as well. We had a long discussion after playing this on how we can better help those we work with, or at least how we can be more understanding to them. Thank you so much for making this game. I am changed for the better because of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short game but it's all about the story more so than the gameplay itself. It's a chance to not only explore food of Tamil culture but also learn about the difficult experience of immigrating to another country and all the ups and downs that come with it. The art style is cute. Story is well written. All in all it is a cozy game to tug on your heart strings (and make you hungry). I understand the price point given the work that went into it but personally, $15 for a game that lasts most users about 2 hours feels like a bit much so I'd catch it on a sale or in a bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Short yet sweet story-driven game. I never had an opinion or point of view with Indian-of-Origin Individuals, I seldom encounter them irl. After experiencing this game, I feel like I can connect to the struggle they go through and I can see them as just more than "another type of person"I know that sounds bad, and I don't have too much of an excuse. At least I cab finally sympathize...Its made me want to reconnect with my own heritage, Thai of origin. My dad still makes those meals for big parties despite being American Born (semi-reverse Kavin scenario?) But anyway, you're not here for my life story.The only complaint I have is the amount of cooking there is - there isn't enough! I wanna cook more with those satisfying sounds & recipe decoding! The story makes up for it though. Overall, 8/10 I need more
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a beautiful little indie game about the immigrant experience, telling a really heartfelt story about family and heritage through the act of cooking and recovering family recipes. Even though it's a really small little game, I cried multiple times. I cannot recommend this more. (Warning: If you're expecting complex puzzles and a playtime of more than 1 hour, you'll be dissapointed!)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a charming and heartwarming game that beautifully blends cooking with storytelling. Playing as an Indian mom trying to reconnect with her roots through food, you get to explore authentic recipes while uncovering a touching narrative about family and culture. The visuals are vibrant, the music is soothing, and the cooking mechanics are simple yet engaging. It's a short but memorable experience with a cultural twist that leaves you craving more.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is more than a game, it's an experience! I played the game twice the day it came out, made me cry both times. The story is rich and touching. You are invested in what happens to the characters. And as a white person it gave me a small glimpse into what the experience of immigrants can be like. All the struggles they deal with and how resilient they are.The food sections are beautiful, music is lovely, the art style is very original and engaging. Special shoutout to the sfx that really helps make you feel like you're cooking yourself. Loved to learn about Tamil and the food and language from the region as wellA must play!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy, short, cooking game that's just noticeably more involved than an interactive novel. I think this is perfect for an afternoon where on just wants to play a cozy game. It is short, easily finished in an hour and a half, but it tells a compelling, well paced narrative during that time, I did not mind it's shorter length. I'm white and not first gen, so I cannot speak to authenticity of the story. I did, personally, find it compelling and stuck with me. Though, I imagine this may be more emotionally charged for folks with those identities.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, and brought back a lot of memories for me too! It hit quite close to home even though I come from a different country/culture. The food in this game looks amazing, and the almost puzzle-like nature is quite fun to figure out! The little game design and art elements to denote the level of cooking experience of each character in different stages of life was something I really loved as well.All in all, this game made me want to cook, maybe I'll even tackle making layered biryani again and hopefully, the next time I do it won't be as disastrous! (My housemate and I once attempted to make some using her mom's recipe and well.... let's just say it didn't go super well with two inexperienced cooks ^^;  )Other than that, the art direction, the music, as well as the writing was all superb! I felt for the characters, and I truly learnt to care for them as I play through the game. It also mirrored a lot of my experiences, having lived in another country for a few years, and being disconnected from my culture. All in all a wonderful experience. The game was obviously made with lots of love, and it tries its very best to make you love it too.You know it's a good game when the only thing that you wish for is for it to be longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: (Slight Spoiler Warning)Living in Kuwait growing up, I watched A lot of cartoons and that led me to speak more English than Arabic.. It got to a point where I was disappointed to hear that the cartoons on certain channels were in Arabic rather than English, I wasn't very interested in Arabic Classes in school or certain Arabic or Kuwaiti foods that I ate, It even dreamed of Studying College overseas. Now, as a fourteen year old and first playing this game was a huge eye opener for me. Hearing Venba and her Family's story touched my heart and how she was afraid that Kavin might have been distancing himself from his culture. I somewhat saw myself in Kavin's shoes, and though she never really said anything I felt that my own mother felt the same way about me, if not, adjacent to it. It felt like a slap to the face about how your culture is important to you and how it tells a story about who you are and where you came from. When I finished the game and it cut to the credits, I called my mom and told her that when I start going back to school again that I'll try harder to Learn more Arabic, I feel that this game is was a wake up call for me. would really recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I think everyone should play Venba. It somehow delivers a fun AND informative cooking game within a truly touching story. It has empathy without shying away from difficult situations/life moments, and shows food as the important cultural and social connection it is. This game tells a beautiful story, is well animated, has an excellent soundtrack (going to keep listening to it for sure) and has satisfying problems to solve similar to Some Assembly Required.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development for Venba for a while now and I so so excited when the release date finally came! I also decided against playing the demo so that I could have a brand new experience when it was complete.Now for my thoughts:Venba is an absolutely beautiful game. The sounds, the music, the art and the story, all of it is very very beautiful. You experience the story bit by bit, with short scenes of dialogue between Venba and her family while immersing yourself into her culture through the preparation and eating of food. Each recipe feels very personal, laced with small memories of Venba and her mother, or sometimes with just genuine love and care for family. As someone who has immigrant parents, I couldn't help but feel deeply touched by each of the struggles that Venba, her husband, and her child all uniquely face as people who stand out in their community. Even with struggles that were not distinctly said, it was easy to imagine and reflect on what my own family had been through.It was a story that hit close to home and had me in tears. In my opinion, though the game was not particularly long, it was well worth the price for an experience that is so full of love and detail.Just wish there was a cookbook embedded in the game to refer to make these delicious recipes in real life..!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a heartwarming game. It is very well made and the soundtrack is great. Venba is a point-and-click narrative game with a couple of puzzles. Nothing challenging and the "branching paths" are pretty limited, there's not much change to the results, if any, but the selling point is the narrative. My only real complaint about the game is that it's 1.5 hours long and costs $15. IMHO, it's just a little too costly for the game's length.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the artwork and story-telling aspect of this game. Colours are gorgeous, cultural elements interlaced with cooking too, and the gameplay is fun!I do wish this game was longer though. It's about two hours of game, in which a lot of it is dialogue, and some of it is game. I would still recommend you buy iut, but maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Though I'm not Tamil, I'm still very much a child of immigrant parents and this resonated with me very much and like the other players stated, I felt called out and I'm ok with it. I'm perfectly ok with a game being short, I just hope that there's a future expansion with Kavin flying back to India to visit his mom, maybe he starts a family of his own and introduces his mom to his family. Maybe his children get to experience Grandma Venba's recipe. Just my imagination running wild with this cute game. If there's a future expansion, I definitely will be onboard with supporting this!!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short game with actual gameplay -- making food -- being an even shorter part of the whole experience. In order not to make the gameplay sections feel completely scripted (you're following a recipe book, after all) the recipes are often missing crucial information and some experimentation will be required. I would even call the gameplay the weakest part of the game if it wasn't for the absolutely joyous background music accompanying the preparation of each meal. When the radio gets turned up, you know it's time to celebrate.Venba is really an analysis about trying to raise your family in a foreign country with a foreign culture. How much of your own culture will you be able to retain while  attempting to fit into another society? Great writing and a distinctive visual style with bold, vibrant colors. A little bit sweet and sour, the game will take you through a range of emotions in just a couple of hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: ( this definitely reads more as a journal entry than anything else because of how much this game reminded me of my own life, so if you'd rather skip through all that -- its a solid 9.5/10 -- just wish it was longer. )i'm usually not one to review games because i simply forget about it. but for this one, i feel like i must. as a first generation immigrant to canada -- especially an only kid who moved for uni in search of a better life, and perhaps a little bit of soul-searching and to detach myself from my parents, this hit me hard. in my family, food is a love language that supersedes almost everything else. so to see the story narrated via Venba's kitchen was really special. when they were sending Kavin off to uni, i was in tears, because it reminded me of my own parents -- they must have struggled to see me leave so abruptly, to live in a place half the world away all on my own. i didn't think much of it then, but seeing it from Venba's perspective made me want to jump on a flight to india just to hug my mother, and to lay my head in her lap.i related to Kavin a lot, but also to Venba. being a first-gen immigrant is confusing -- my culture is so deeply rooted in me because of all the years i spent back home, but the need to fit in to a new culture, the fear of revealing too much of yourself in case they ridicule it is something i know all too well. i'm always afraid i'll forget my mother tongue, or how to write it. on a personal level, this resonated with me a lot, but the art, the storytelling and the game design were all so stunning as well. its such a wonderful game to play on a slow saturday afternoon when you need something to distract yourself from the looming dread of having to figure out life after uni -- it was a beautiful reminder that despite everything i can always go home.it's been an hour since i finished the game and it's already become one that's really close to my heart. i do wish it was longer but i appreciate how it made me feel less alone, and for reminding me that if the homesickness gets too bad, i can always go to my kitchen and make some rasam and rice. :) thank you to the dev team for this wonderful game. i truly appreciate yall so much.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This has been one of the few games to bring a tear to my eye.The art is beautiful, the music is catchy and the game play loop is well made and adds a good amount of challenge. I adored it covering the culture and couldn't tear my eyes away from the amazing story. If you have even the slightest want to purchase this game, please do. It is a short but enjoyable experience and it is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A short narrative game about the immigrant family experience through making South Indian cuisine. It’s got beautiful visuals that really sell the food while you experiment and try and figure out how, exactly, you’re supposed to make it. Notably, the narrative is through the eyes of the eponymous Venba, the immigrant mother, rather than her child. She’s an eminently sympathetic and interior character, and her struggles, along with the rest of the family’s, are felt clearly. The story, while at a faster clip than I expected, is intimate and grounded in its heartbreaks and hurdles while still remaining hopeful.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: The sweetest game, heartwarming and realistic. I've heard many similar stories from old friends growing up. Our lives were very different, I had the privilege of not experiencing some of the discrimination this game touched upon. But it was nice to see something that felt so honest. Sometimes we don't have the chance to say something before its too late, sometimes we make the wrong decisions, sometimes there is no right decision available, we are all just learning to grow. Our ways of growing will always be different, this game really showed the differences in cultures and how it can create barriers. Yet love and support can still bring children and parents back together in the end. This game is by far my favorite, it just made me want to cry in a good way. As for the game play, it was short and sweet. I found it to be quite fun and relaxing, although I ended up extremely hungry afterwards! Please play it if you can!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a really beautiful and fun narrative cooking game. As a player who isn't that familiar with Indian culture, this game was really nice and a great learning experience about what its like, and the beauty of the culture. I loved the art-style and the music, and the story. It was a 10/10 experience. I loved it, its a really beautiful game. Definitely had a few moments that I almost cried. In a good way. I recommend this to everyone :)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game after 1 hour and 20 minutes, I can say that this game is my favorite I have played in his kind of genre (of a casual short game with a few puzzles) so far. What had me initially interested in this game was the unique setup and wonderful art style; right after getting the notification in my mailbox I decided to purchase and try this game. After all I had waited a little while already to see this game finished.Whereas Florence had also a sweet art style and interesting puzzles, its story bored me quite a lot personally. It was just quite chewed out already, meet-cute before a break up (I still recommended it, because this is just my personal taste). When the past was around also had a similar feel to Florence. It is hard to compare any of these games after all, because they are all completely different stories, yet they did not manage to pick me up where I was, as much as Venba did. Venba gave me all those emotions that were lacking before. I really thought that maybe I just did not like that genre.However Venba, excited me with its puzzles in which you cook traditional recipes; they were not too hard and simultaneously not too easy. The game gives you pointers where to go, but at times you have to find the solution yourself. Not to mention, the recipes were beautifully drawn and during the process I could almost smell the delicacies sizzling in the pan.The aspect which trumps it all, the interesting puzzles and the stunning art style, was the story itself. It was engaging to be able to choose dialogue options, I did not even care whether it would influence the story at all, because choosing dialogue was not about changing the story, but finding out more about the characters. I think this story is a masterpiece, it made me sad at times and smile at others - simple as that. This story broke my heart in a good and wholesome way, and I think that is its strongest suit absolutely. I am sure this game will reach a lot of peoples' hearts. Also, it really makes me want to call my parents. If you like short narration games, emotional dialogue, with some puzzles sprinkled in: well, this is a must-have. Do you recommend this game? A thousand times yes. Thank you Visai Games for this absolute masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: i've had this game on my wishlist for a while before it got released. went into it expecting to cry and it was like even more emotional than i imagined. it has really beautiful and well-done art, storytelling, music, and sound effects. it might be short (1-2 hours depending on if you want to 100%) but it packs a lot of production value into that time. a great example of why i love indie games, 11/10also fyi it works great on steam deck, except that i can't seem to make it the full 1280x800 resolution, it gets letterboxed into 1280x720 even if i select 1280x800 in the steam game properties. the letterboxing is not a huge deal though
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a short but sweet narrative cooking game and OMG it hit me in all the feels. Experience saddness, happiness, disappointment, loss; it's relatable on so many levels. The food all looks so delicious. This game made me hungry and want to call my mum.I just wish it was longer and there was more cooking. I feel like we just got to see glimpses of their life, jumping ahead in time, it would have been lovely to spend more time with the family, possibly exploring more in-depth storylines or just seeing more of their everyday life.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I cried like a baby playing this. This short game manages to really hit you in the feels with it's well crafted relationships between characters and delivery of the story. I really felt like I could feel the same emotional turmoil the characters were experiencing- and the game pulls off a great 'show, don't tell' delivery. No hand holding here. I loved the cooking, I finished this game feeling so hungry and really keen to try some of the recipes. The art style is gorgeous and you really feel as though you can almost smell the food. The music is also incredible and really adds to the experience.I think this will be one of my top favourite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not crying you're crying.This game genuinely brought me to tears. Gives a true telling of how hard it is to transition to a foreign land as an Indian and how staying true to one's roots can conflict with what is normal around you. After living in Chennai for a while and coming back to America there is a level of yearning for this cooking and familial love that it is indescribable. Abhi thank you for making a game that touched my heart
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a beautiful game that carries you through the lives of a family, while teaching you their traditional family meals. It's gorgeous to look at, heartwarming, and is definitely a game worth playing if family is important to you.My grandparents immigrated to the United States in the 60s, and there were many parts of Venba that really hit home -- it brought me almost to tears a couple times, too.I'm excited to hunt for all the achievements, and can't wait to see what other stories and adventures these artists have in store for us in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Truly beautiful slice of life game with intuitive cooking gameplay, amazing design and very interesting storytelling (like letting you scroll through the text, having the text be displayed slower when Kavin speaks in Tamil translated english because he's new to the language or story important memory being used in the cooking puzzles). There's a lot of very meaningful details with the ways the music are implemented too. And the cooking puzzles are pretty fun and engaging. The food looks lovely and it made me want to get more into cooking. It's a really well told story about immigration and culture and all the subtle implications of it. Only problem is that it's SO SHORT. It went by really fast and when it ended I was left with a "that's it moment". It was still a great end and an amazing story but I would have loved to follow Venba thorough the rest of her life. What about when Kavin gets a kid, how will their relationships with cooking takes its form. I think there's a lot more story that could have been said. And with this format I honestly could go on forever, I'll eat it up. It's a bit of a shame that it's short but it's literally the only complain I have. It was a great experience. And if there's a sequel or even another visual novel of the sort using the same concept & mechanics I will definitely play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who's a kid of immigrant south indian parents, this video game tugged at my heartstrings so much. i first heard about this game in 2020 and was so excited for the release and am so happy to finally play this game!! and this game met every single one of my expectations, the music, the art, the story, it's all so beautiful!! all the recipes in this story, i've grown up with, the dosa, the idlis, the rasam, the dal, and the biryani!! all the little details made me so warm like my family have the same hing/asafoetida container venba does! my mom's recipes are similar to hers, which helped me with figuring out the recipes tbh, and just, i adore this game so much!! the tug and pull between kavin and his parents is a struggle i know all too well as a kid who wants to spread her wings, but also cares for her parents at the same time. i relate to the feeling embarrassed growing up of being indian and wanting to fit in. thank you visai games for creating such a beautiful game that makes me feel so seen!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: I've never really felt compelled to review a game before, but this is such a beautiful story. It gave me access to a perspective I wouldn't have otherwise. If you're on the fence about buying this game, just buy it already. Although it's short, I can tell the creators put their soul into this game. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is an absolutely wonderful short narrative game. I really didn't expect this to get me as emotional as it did, but the writing really hit a chord with me (tears were definitely shed ;v;). Seeing how culture and familial themes are handled from the different perspectives of the three characters and how they all had very unique yet universal struggles with immigrant life really made me empathize with them despite the short run time of the game. The cooking puzzles/mechanics are simple yet different enough that it never felt like a slog (you also get to unlock the actual recipes which is a great touch!). Not to mention the art and music are just wonderful in their own right! A lovely experience to go through in an evening where you aren't quite sure what you want to play - definitely was a pleasant surprise for me! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is a wonderful cozy/narrative game. The story is about an indian family who did imigrate in Canada. Discover indian culture and cook various delicious recipes throught simply puzzles. The graphics are really beautiful and the soundtrack is relaxing. I really enjoyed this game, I highly recommend it!!!! 🍛🧡
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful, the cooking ties in so well to the story and I love how it develops with the characters. The music and art fits perfectly and the game even incorporates the sounds of the kitchen making me feel at home when I play. Amazing game, I'm definitely going to replay this and get all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba interweaves some excellent cooking puzzles with an unflinching set of vignettes that cut right to the heart of the most difficult conversations human beings can have, and all done with a lovingly detailed art style that excellently conveys both the food and the people involved. Venba's emotional real-ness gives it an impact you just don't see in many other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: They were not kidding when they said short, I want more! Venba packs a big punch for such a short game though, with a beautiful art style it opens a small window into the challenges of 2 parents living and raising a child in a foreign country with a culture different to their own. We see the complexities of the relationship between parent and child as the child is growing and trying to gain independence, and an identity separate to their parents while trying to find where they fit in the world. At the same time we see the parent struggling to watch their child reject their culture and in a sense rejecting themselves, while also trying to respect their child's desire to become their own person as they transition into adulthood.TLDR; I paid these people to make me cry.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba was a beautiful experience - from the immigrant story to the cooking mechanics to the soundtrack. I love that the game is short and doesn't overstay it's welcome, and the mechanics are simple. It manages to tell a full story about culture through the food, and I can highly recommend. It made me hungry - and wanting to learn to cook the recipes!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable game! Makes me want to make and try South Indian food. And the story is very gravitating as well!My only feedback is that there's very long sections of dialogue, with very few interruptions of cooking in between. A lot of reading following by very little gameplay tends to be boring, but coming from a tiny indie studio I completely understand. The art, the story, the music more than makes up for it! There's a lot of soul in this little game. Looking forward to more endeavors by Visai Games in the future! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Just played this for my channel. That was a very cute, heartfelt and interesting adventure told through and alongside indian cooking. Not gonna lie, I've picked out three recipes already to cook. Who knew even pixelated food could look so tasty. The story was really nicely told and had a good pacing. Some was just hinted or needed to be figured out between the lines, I love that. Don't need to spell out everything.The music complemented the whole package and I love how little details in the interface gel with the story beats. Keep on knocking those spices over, my boy!Would recommend this to my friends!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game.. It's rare that a game gives a new perspective into my own life, but this did that, and amazingly. The music and art style were full of character, and the gameplay light but engaging, tying in seamlessly with the storytelling. i can't find anything negative to say even if I try! The symbols and subtleties were also delightful to notice and added to the richness of the story.And to top it off, for me this is the first time seeing genuine Tamil and Indian culture manifesting in the game medium. I was honestly a little apprehensive to see how our culture would be portrayed to the world, but this game blew my mind!Though the story is based on Tamil culture, sometimes it feels like the story is actually playing with which, between Tamil and North American (to be generic), is the familiar and unfamiliar culture. And something makes me wonder that perhaps the gamemakers intend that every player also may find the two cultures and conflicting worlds familiar and unfamiliar in different ways! I'm very curious to know others' experiences of the game on this point.Overall, I just loved the game, and respect to the creators!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba's been on my wishlist for a while and I'm glad I bought it during the spring sale.As a South Indian, the breakfast recipes were easy to figure out and fun to make. I've watched my mother make them so many times that even if I make them differently, I could do what she does and that was the solution.I don't think a game has made me cry in a long time. Really well made. I wouldn't mind being able to cook more dishes or having a lengthier storyline, but this was quite perfect too.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Very short (took me around 1hr to complete) and sweet. More like a visual novel than a game. I could relate to it as a 2nd gen American (though not Indian). Has some well used tropes of the immigrant experience but still hits you in the feels. If it sounds like you would like this game, you probably will (and vice versa).
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: It was a beautiful, emotional and deeply personal story, I had a blast playing it and highly recommend it just for the sound track alone. It held my attention for the whole game which is pretty hard to do! The art is unique and vibrant with a graphic yet homemade quality. Overall, I adored it. My only complaint is that its too short! It would be really fun if they added more levels with different recipes, almost like a free play mode I guess? I don't mind spending the 15 dollars because this is such a great piece of art, I just want to play more!
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely made me cry at multiple points, all in under 2 hours of gameplay. Really hit home even as a grandchild of immigrants; the stories and connections that can be made and told through traditional cooking can be expressed through generations if given a chance. Incredibly beautiful and thoughtful, will be thinking about this game for quite a long time
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: short and simple enough to 100% in under two hours and kinda overpriced for that amount of content, but the storys sweet and the recipes are nice i guessof course i wont be able to relate to the experience of immigration and emigration and being a POC in canada so it didnt strike that much of a chord with me, but the other half of the game was pretty nice (i wish there was a way to skip story sections when just going through chapters to do the minigames, wouldve made one of the achievements easier to do)
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short but sweet game! It was fun to play through it and read the story and the fact that a lot of it is told through food makes it all the better. There is not much game-play, but it's a great story. I really enjoyed the art; I haven't played or seen anything like it before, it's pointillism but animated, which was really interesting! It only takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to complete, and about that if you want all the achievements. I went back and played out some different dialogue options. They don't really impact the story but it was fun to see. Also, it has a really cool soundtrack!They announced that they are planning a digital cook book and oh MAN do I want it! As I was playing it really made me want to learn more about the culture and the food. I can't wait to try some of the recipes when their book comes out!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: A heart warming and at the same time heart wrenching tale that anyone who has had to uproot and emigrate far from the familiar home would emphatise with. The struggle in trying to maintain one's culture, identity, language and food taste while constantly going against the pressure to conform and assimilate with the adoptive society. This story is more poignant when a couple from India decided to start anew in Canada, a country often said to be a model on multiculturalism and acceptance, and yet the struggles are still hard at times. Learning a new language while maintaining your own, bringing up a child who will always face a tug of war between history and culture and their adoptive country, securing a job as newcomers, of choosing between a dosai or pizza, or being afraid of being the odd one out as kids, of changing your name because its easier for your froiends to pronounce,  the food that you felt are alien to others and being ostracised because of that. A changing of family values between the parents and their kids, of which normal childhood itself is hard enough but a multicultural one being more so. It hits hardest when the growing distance between parent and child, the disappointment, misunderstandings, loss opportunities and before we realise its too late.Venba elicits a lot of the above to anyone playing it, it's essence brings out what many of us would have gone through if not as an immigrant in foreign lands, at least in our relationship with our parents. It's also a story about generations and how food brings us closer and ties us to our past and to our loved ones. The recipes depiction makes itself felt so vividly as i played and salivate, dang the briyani makes me yearns to head out and get one now.Good+ Rich story telling enfolds through its food themed gameplay mechanics.+ The atmospheric music and soundtrack that provides the backdrop to the mood.+ Superb introduction to Tamil recipes+ The emotional gut punch it can leave you in the end, the game has heart.+ Simple yet effective puzzler game play.+ The graphics shows that you don't need 4k resolutions to make a great game.+ A superb narrative take on the trails and issues of immigrants and maintaining your identity, culture and heritage as a households in a foreign land.Bad- Nothing really, except perhaps its too short and you'd wish you had more, as well as more recipes.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Venba is pure poetry. This short, story driven cooking game encapsulates so much raw emotion and depth surrounding an Indian family's immigration to Canada and bond with one another and their culture on a journey of self-acceptance. I love the additional facts that you can explore about each dish and the way the food fuels the story with each authentic dish, made challenging through the need to interpret various parts of the recipe book that have been lost with time (and the hint system and very forgiving nature of the game that allows you to explore and make mistakes). This is an absolutely gorgeously drawn, true labor of love. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game ! As a white european person, this allowed me to better understand the complexity of what it is to live as an immigrant, or an immigrant's son or daughter, in countries where their culture is not always welcome. How it must feel to want to belong and keep your own culture at the same time.The game was beautifully made, visually, musically and everyone should play it, it's not long, and you won't forget these few hours spent with Venba.And I wonder... Why am I so hungry all of a sudden ?
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me sob so many tears. I resonate with the characters so much, the emotions and hurdles they face and how this game connects the recipes is so special. It healed the inner child in me and made me grateful for all the cooking my mom has done for me. Beautiful character design and sound design as well! have been following this game for a while so really happy I was able to play through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Venba

_childDocuments_.review:
Cook delicious South-Indian food and experience the journey of an immigrant family in Venba! Venba is a narrative cooking game where you play as an Indian mom who immigrates to Canada with her family in the 1980s. Players will cook various dishes and restore lost recipes, hold branching conversations and explore in this story about family, love, loss and more.

Cook Mouth Watering Dishes
Venba's recipe book gets damaged when she moves to Canada. Restore the lost recipes to cook delicious, mouth-watering dishes that serve as a connection to the home left behind.

Explore, Converse, Experience
Get to know the family well, hold branching conversations, and explore as you face the challenges that arise from day to day life.

Features:
- Cook authentic and delicious recipes handpicked from regional South-Indian cuisine
- Hold branching conversations and explore different narrative beats
- Beautiful visuals and animations
Unique soundtrack inspired by Indian musicals

name: Sker Ritual
detailed_description: JOIN OUR DISCORD 📢 POST-LAUNCH ROADMAP About the Game An intense, round-based, zombie horror shooter by indie developers at Wales Interactive. Play solo or up-to 4-players online, facing relentless waves of Quiet Ones whilst solving mysterious missions, uncovering Easter Eggs, upgrading steampunk weapons and obtaining Miracles — a vast network of Celtic God powers. It’s 1914, and Elisabeth Williams has conquered Sker Island, now seeking domination with a broadcast of the Siren’s Song. Arianwen, her daughter, has opposed her, and after being mysteriously awakened, you must join her mission to thwart the broadcast and save the world from descending into hell. Sker Ritual is not a direct sequel, but an FPS spin-off from the award-winning British indie horror game, Maid of Sker! • Old-school round-based FPS action • Play solo or up-to 4-players online • Story continued from Maid of Sker ‘evil’ ending • Optional objectives & hidden Easter Eggs • Supercharged ‘Elites’ with unique abilities • Collect and enhance 'Miracle' powers • Explore free reward systems ‘Dread Levels’ and ‘Sker Pass’ TEAM TACTICS OR SHOOT SOLO? Designed for playing solo, or up-to 4-players online. Short of a teammate? No worries, the intensity of Sker Island’s hordes scale to the number of players. You could always find-a-friend over on the official . SKER ENEMIES The Quiet Ones have returned and they are not alone. Sker Island has recruited new elites, each with a unique set of abilities that will force you to change-up your playstyle, change your location, or enlist the help of your teammates! Old enemies aren't the only ones to curse the lands of Sker, we have many more new faces — even some without faces — that want to destroy you. IT'S A MIRACLE Killing enemies offer a chance to drop powerful Miracles . Look out for these, you’ll need them. A Miracle drop offers a choice of three random upgradable powers that buff or alter your shooting, melee, grenade and healing. A fifth slot is reserved for your Ultimate , a chargeable powerful action to save up for those sticky situations. Each Miracle is bound to a Celtic God and come in many forms including rarity, core attributes and power. MASKS, QUIPS AND MORE Collect and induce fear on Sker’s inhabitants with interchangeable masks inspired by all forms of horror; folk, gothic, zombie, science fiction to the supernatural and more. Taunt your teammates with unique voice lines and switch out your dynamic menu scene environments from the Island. THE LAUGHING POLICEMAN Get your guns, ammo, and more at The Laughing Policeman’s booth at locations around the maps. Buy stock munitions or gamble on a randomly picked weapon with a chance of gaining a higher base level. Climb the weapon ranks with unique upgrades courtesy of The Laughing Policeman’s SUPER CHARGER for bonus buffs and visible steam-punk inspired enhancements.

_childDocuments_.review: CoD Zombies without egregious business practices. There is some jank, but overall I believe there is a lot of charm. The developers seem to be rather keen on supporting this game with new content. The extensive list of DLC is *not* for any actual fundamental gameplay features such as missions or weapons. They are entirely cosmetic. Overall, I would pick this up. Do keep in mind though, you will likely not be able to play with randoms, unless you organize with people through the publisher Discord. However, there is an offline mode for solo play.

We're expected to get to level 500 and even on higher difficulties it just seems far too much of a grind. customisation could be better aswell instead of just masks and a few background menus.

_childDocuments_.review: Once you die in game, you are perma ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Playing with a full squad turns into a single player game cause your friends will die, and never be able to contribute again. Since the respawn tokens scale in price with how often you die, and since there is no picking up of downed players, there is no coming back from a single death. Do you use your 5k for a gun upgrade or re spawn token? if you get a better gun you can do more damage, but the second you get pinned in place by the zombies youre dead and have to rely on a teammate to buy you back. If you buy the token instead you wont be able to do any damage, ensuring you never make money to buy a gun upgrade, leading to your inevitable death again. Throw in undersized hitboxes on zombies for when you shoot them (some dont seem to even have a hitbox from the side) but oversized hitboxes for when youre trying to run past, points only being awarded for kills and assist, with some mini bosses not even rewarding you for beating them, and terrible dsync, this game could certainly be good at some point and i understand this is early access, but ive played better early access free games, and i payed 10 dollars for this

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for round based zombies like CoD zombies this is a decent alternative that has some objectives that doesnt take away from the round based gameplay. Weapon selection isnt bad just it have much to offer for variety.The mystery box in this game is a dog in a dog house named lucky.Mini-bosses are also included with the normal enemy types just on certain rounds.This game has a ton of potential but is limited due to the 5 man studio but that doesnt take away what from what has already been provided and what could be in future updates. If you enjoy a game that you can sit back relax from your normal competitive game this would be a great game to look into! Overall 7/10 for what the game has to offer as of right now but that could change in the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: Way too many flaws and just not good enough to recommend.-COD Zombies, Squad, wave shooter but the only way to win is to do the all the objectives. Killing zombies progresses to the next wave and things keep getting harder, the only way too keep up is too keep upgrading your gun, the cost to do this keeps doubling and the enemies quickly outscale you because the cost of upgrading becomes too astronomically high. This means the best way to play is stupid, just leave the last zombie alive and keep doing the objectives. GGEZ. - You can hold 2 guns but the other gun is useless since you can only afford to keep upgrading 1 gun. Every mission has 1 unique gun that you will need to use to do the objective, if you play solo your other slot is solely for this gun.- Game just sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game perfectly captures what made COD Zombies so incredible in the first place, my only complaints are the story and maps don't really have a lot of connective tissue, it feels like you just show up at new place to do a thing and it makes the journey feel less important.I'd also love a challenge map similar to Town or The Giant where you can just go for high rounds and don't have to do any quests.Either way this game has massive potential, also free DLC maps are amazing, thank you Devs
_childDocuments_.name: Sker Ritual

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual takes what made COD: Zombies great and piles on loads of cool stuff. It's a ton of fun, challenging, and super replayable. Despite the dip in player numbers in the past couple of months, the devs STILL keep grinding and keep giving us great updates with brand-new mechanics to dive into. I'm surprised at how this gem doesn't get the attention it deserves. I'm usually pretty picky about where I spend my cash, but this game is worth every penny, unlike most titles on Steam.Definitely recommend it, one of the best co-op zombie shooter!

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game on YouTube, looked like a pretty cool alternative to Call of Duty Zombies. It feels really dated though. I can get past the 10 year old graphics, but it plays like someone modded CoD:WWII zombies into CoD:WaW zombies, clunky controls with terrible gunplay. There are also only about 8 weapons. Maybe it would be worth it on sale, but definitely not full price. Try HuniePop instead
_childDocuments_.name: Sker Ritual

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay and reward system needs tweaks for multiplayer. Points are not shared between team members and only one person gets points for killing enemies. If you die with your team and become underpowered because you didnt get enough points, while your teammates are doing better, you will never be able to catch up because enemy difficulty means your under powered weapons will not be able to keep up and you will continue to fall further and further behind. This make the whole team completely unbalanced and the teammates with the most upgrades ends carrying the whole team. Fix this major issue and this game will actually be worth playing with others.
_childDocuments_.name: Sker Ritual

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly enjoyable round based zombie game similar to COD Zombies. That being said I really only suggest this game if you intend to play solo as multiplayer (if you can find a multiplayer game) lags to the point that it ruins the fun of the game. If multiplayer is fixed this game would be a strong recommendation any day.

_childDocuments_.review: Really hard to recommend something that every time I've tried to find a group, literally no one is playing this game. It's super rare that a game is dead on arrival, but....When you do get a game, it's basically the same Zombie Survival game that CoD has established, except this time there are little quests in between.After trying games for days and using the developers discord, no one is playing this game. The discord is dead, the game is dead on arrival.The developers responded below and while I respect their opinion, imagine believing that a healthy game means you have to trawl Discord groups to find people that actually want to play this game, and that ALL of those people in this discord are playing other games.So to answer you devs, this IS the Sker Ritual Experience, which is, a game that absolutely no one wants to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, its good for all players. If you are experienced max out that difficultly. if you are newer, hit the lower settings. It can be played solo or co-op. Even playing solo reminds me of the days of when COD zombies was good. They also have a good road map. Buy or sale either is a good option
