_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is something you should play if you like Call Of Duty Zombies and want to support indie devs. This game doesn't take itself too seriously and knows how to have fun with itself. While the game is a bit bland, I think there's something to love here and I hope that this game gets the care it deserves in early access. It definitely feels like an early access game, so there are a few gripes I have with it. Most notably, I feel like the sound design (or in some cases lack there of) can make the levels feel a little bland, the gun play is kind of lacking (it's not bad, but some guns need more kickback), and I think the point system is a bit flawed (you get points per kill, vs. in COD where you get points per shot). I feel like if they changed the point system to match COD, it would make weapons like the fully automatic guns worth using, but atm, any strong AoE weapons or shotguns are pretty much superior. Outside of that, the battle pass system is not great either but it's also free as well as the current 4 maps, so it's more something cool to get, but really the fun is in the maps. I also want to highlight both the art design and map design. While some parts do feel a little bland, the maps are super detail and well thought out. The puzzles are engaging and some change per run so it's always making you think. I really enjoy this about the game. Overall, I recommend it and hope you support these devs. This game with enough care can really be a game to remember.
_childDocuments_.name: Sker Ritual

_childDocuments_.review: Game is honestly really fun, if you can look past the animations and sounds not being the greatest at times (which i personally haven't noticed beyond some animations), its a really fun game! it reminds you of mixing a rogue-lite a little, various parts from BO4, BO3, BO2, and probably other COD zombie games, aswell as having some elements of KF2, the game doesnt force you to solely play through the story of the maps either, you can simply choose to play normal zombies if you wish! Currently there is no text or VC features so that is a downside, but i imagine in future updates we will.
_childDocuments_.name: Sker Ritual

_childDocuments_.review: I have thoroughly enjoyed this game, alone, with friends, and with random people in matchmaking, it's a great new twist to the old-school Call of duty zombies and I would recommend this game to those with patience.the reason I say this is because sadly it is still an early release of the game and I feel there is a lot of work to be done on the game to get it to its full potential.The game has bugs, I've run into too many to list here but some of them are game-breaking, and some of them are funny.the weapons we do have are awesome and fun to use and look at, sadly there is a small selection compared to what could be.the collectibles, Easter eggs, and extra objectives are fun and make the game fun to replay and the achievements range from simple to do to exciting and head-scratching.the game does punish you for dying too much which adds a bit of spice to the game but might be tough to newcomers to the genre of game.the customising options are fun as well, but like the weapons are limited at the moment of writing this, hope to see more in the future.a bit more control on the matchmaking would be nice too but its ok.all in all a fun game, worth a go, sadly the bugs are a little annoying but dont let that stop you from having fun with this.i know im sending mixed signals with this review but i enjoy this game, if any of the devs want a list of the bugs and problems id be happy to go through them.
_childDocuments_.name: Sker Ritual

_childDocuments_.review: Very very similar to OG call of duty zombies. The game literally takes every good thing about the varies call of duty games and makes its amazingly fun. The easter eggs are doable for players who arnt hard core, yet there are tons of extra eggs that seasoned veterans will love. The map designs are mostly good with solid camping spots on most maps. Only three down sides to this game that i can see is 1. No split screen option for local couch gaming, 2. No in game lobby voice chat capabilities, and 3. there needs to be more weapons. The game play can get pretty stale without some more options. The game is a solid 9/10 and for the price it cant be beat. Definitely would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: the game is slowly getting worse with each and every update by adding ridiculous enemies and bosses. the two newest maps are very small and close quarters making them very stressful and difficult to enjoy. most of the new weapons are underwhelming and locked behind quests on said new maps. and dont even get me started on the insane amount of DLC cosmetics that cost way too much. i was an advocate for this game before it even came out and it had $20 dlc packs when it was in alpha (not even out yet). save your money and wait till some legit improvements happen.

Only have 4 hours played atm and happened 3 times already which is really frustrating, also sometimes hitboxes feel off. The game itself is  conceptually good and fun but needs a bit more polishing when it comes to mechanichs and bugfixes for a smooth player experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty decent if you want to chase the feeling of black ops 1 zombies. As an early access game, the bugs I've encountered have been minor (one powerup doesn't work [the "shock nearby enemies while reloading" one]). The most difficult thing is finding a game with other players. Often the queue is so long that once you get ONE random in your lobby, it will start. If you do end up waiting for a third and fourth, the second person is 90% of the time now afk because you both waited 5 minutes for a game. Obviously this will be improved if the playerbase increases, but for now, expect to get your best games if you and three friends decide to play together.I'd also love to see even more variety in the tasks you complete, and I'm sure that's something that's on the roadmap.Overall, fun game, but don't rely on the random matchmaking for 3+ players unless you invite some friends

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game. My 2 biggest issues with it are that it's online only with no option for a single player offline experience. And the other being that the EULA spells out in front of you that do not own the game, nor a copy. You simply buy a license to be able to access the service, which is a huge ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ red flag to consumers. As far as gameplay goes, it's just round based zombies with objectives, that's it. Nothing all that revolutionary if I'm being honest. If you really want to play, I recommend waiting for a sale and be wary that the game can be ripped away from you at any point as I stated earlier that you are not buying a copy of the game, simply the rights to access the content. So if they go bust or shut the server down, you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review, this is a bare bones nazi zombies. Bare bones because there's only 2 maps, but otherwise, id say this game has more potential than nazi zombies. The bugs, for the most part, arent game breaking. There are a couple places where i got physically caught on the terrain and when i tried to jump, i glitched out and either a) got stuck floating in mid air, helpless as can be, or b) for some reason teleported to first spawn. There is fps drop in later rounds, but it remains playable when it occurs. So far, the absolute worst thing to happen to me was when i was about to beat the first boss, Abraham, the game just straight up crashed. _childDocuments_.review: On sale, I think the game is fine.There are four stages, each one has puzzles you have to solve while facing waves of more and more stronger enemies, culminating in a final boss fight at the end of each stage.  Each stage then has bonus objectives, which are similar to the puzzles you solved earlier, except these don't come with objective markers telling you where to go, or what to do.  Kinda like Myst.Matchmaking was a nightmare.  It's not a popular game, so not a lot of games to join.  If the server host leaves, whoever it is, everyone gets kicked.The game also has a few annoying parts to it.  Like there are these random events where you have to accomplish a task within a set amount of time.  But by the time you get there, half the time is gone.  Then you need to kill enemies or something, and if there are no enemies, you fail.  I don't like how I get punished for things outside my control.  If it's a DPS check I failed, sure, whatever, that's on me.  If I need to kill 30 enemies in an area, but enemies aren't spawning, why do I get penalized for that?The weapons are also an annoyance.  You'll find that only 2-3 weapons are actually usable, and the rest are trash.  That really hinders build diversity.  The powers are also kinda boring, like just a flat +% damage increase, or a damage over time effect.  Nothing transformative.  All this means that replay value is minimal after you beat each level.

_childDocuments_.review: A Refreshing Departure for Zombie Veterans: Sker Ritual ReviewAs a seasoned player of Call of Duty Zombies, stepping into the world of Sker Ritual felt like a much-needed breath of fresh air. This game offers a departure from the familiar, injecting new life into the zombie survival genre with its unique mechanics and challenges.Our group of three, all veterans of the undead onslaught, found ourselves pleasantly surprised by the fresh take Sker Ritual brings to the table. From the moment we dove into the game, it was evident that this was not just another run-of-the-mill zombie shooter. The developers have clearly put thought and innovation into every aspect of the gameplay.### Feedback:**Sewers of the Dead:**- Opening doors with the plague pistol sometimes resulted in them being permanently locked for others.- Certain doors remained closed for some players, requiring multiple purchases.- The plague pistol felt underpowered compared to other wonder weapons.**Deadly Lover's Fortress:**- A glitch occurred where a siren teleporting at a player caused them to lose their weapons and rendered them unable to interact with any prompts or inputs.### Improvements:**Plague Pistol (Sewers of the Dead):**- Add a lingering AOE effect to enhance its effectiveness, such as dealing damage to zombies passing through for a brief duration.**Sword (Deadly Lover's Fortress):**- Make upgrades unavailable before forging, or ensure that any upgrades transfer once forged for smoother progression.Despite these minor setbacks, Sker Ritual remains a standout experience for zombie enthusiasts. Its unique mechanics, immersive environments, and challenging gameplay offer a refreshing departure from the norm. Despite encountering a few glitches and areas for improvement, our group thoroughly enjoyed our time with the game and would highly recommend it to anyone seeking a fresh take on the zombie survival genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I just had the game for like an hour or two but I already think it's fantastic. Still needs some tweaks tho.The there's mostly 5 things I'd like to see improved.1- Gameplay is great, but there's too much "silence": I don't know how it is in multiplayer cause I haven't tried it. But at least in solo, the player character doesn't say anything at all. It would be nice to have some voicelines when you get a weapon, buy a perk... random voicelines when you kill regular enemies, mini bosses... Kinda like in CoD, because yeah, everyone is going to compare this to CoD let's be honest, and that's not a bad thing. And in multiplayer, different characters could react to each other voicelines and respond.2- Walking animation: Maybe it's just me, but I find it a bit weird when I move and there's no headbob when walking, only when sprinting.3- Upgrading animation, the first time I've upgraded a weapon was a bit confusing, you see the weapon being put into the machine, and at the same time, you get the upgraded version in your hands instantly and I didn't knew where it came from. Coming from CoD I expected it to work like the PaP machine, you put your weapon there (and your character switches to your seccond weapon), wait a few seconds, weapon comes out, and you have to pick it up. Either do that, or do a "lightning" animation or something IN your hands and transform the weapon right there, in front of my eyes, because as of right now, it looks a bit janky, seeing the weapon in the machine and then "POP" almost instantly it is in your hands already upgraded.3.5- Steming from the previous point. Lucky animations also could get a rework. Monkey brain likes seeing the weapons spin before getting the prize like, again, in CoD, but here Lucky just spits a weapon in front of you and that's it.4- Scaling / Points, getting points only on kills makes it really hard to get points in higher rounds, it may be too hard to keep upgrading weapons at that point. So I'd either add a health cap for the enemies, or grant points for damage aswell not just for kills.5- Mo' Weapons baby.I get that the game just came out, the team is small and further improvements are bound to come in the future, but I wanted to give some feedback to help imrove the weak aspects that I've found. Specially because I'm really enjoying the game, it has great potential, and I haven't read any other comment on this matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting into things I want to say that I've played every map and done its story and hidden story objectives on the normal difficulty. I do like this game, it scratches that itch for a good round based COD zombies without it actually being COD zombies. I just have a few issues that I think it hold it back from being better. Objectives: I don't mind the objectives, I think every map has something unique going on for the main story and it's pretty straightforward what you need to do, there are maybe 3 or so puzzle/code related steps but it's nothing challenging. For the most part I would say the MAIN story objectives are solid, but I have an issue with the hidden objectives for each map. You aren't told what to do for them (which is good, it's nice that people can hunt for stuff and it feels like an Easter egg) and 90% of the time you are doing the same objectives for each HS (hidden story). Each HS starts off with the same objective of shooting a character in 4 random spots on the map, at first I thought it was okay but found it tedious after having to do it so many times.  I also wish that there was a little more to the HS objectives, they tend to be about the same length as the main story for each level, but for it being the hidden no hand holding stuff they were really tame with what they make you do. I guess you could say that I am biased as I internally compare this to something like BO2 or BO3 which may not be a fair comparison I admit, but I was left wanting a little more. Overall I would say that for the story and objectives they aren't hard and are fine on a first run through, they are the same every time. Gameplay: Seeing other comments, I have not tried playing online with other people so I'm unsure if the disconnection issues are really that bad but I have not had any crashes. The gameplay and feel is fine, it's a little clunky in some departments but nothing too bad. I think that the miracle powers are alright and spice things up enough to allow for "builds" and combos that work together. The main issue I had was with the guns. They feel fine to use but the damage starts to drop off really quick. With how expensive buying things can get you will fly through rounds fairly quickly and find that by round 10 some guns start to feel like you're shooting peas at your enemies. Of course you can upgrade them or "pack-a-punch" them but I find the system to be flawed mostly due to how many points it costs to upgrade. The first upgrade (on normal difficulty) costs around 5k, which if you've played zombies is fairly normal, but it doesn't upgrade your damage by a crazy amount which is fine. However, with the next upgrade costing 15k, then 30k, 45k, and finally 60k you end up just upgrading one weapon and hoping that it'll hold. I don't think this would be so bad, but anything that isn't considered a "wonder weapon" (COD zombies term) isn't holding up to any high rounds or bosses.  I found myself usually just getting the wonder weapon for the map and upgrading that because it was the only reliable source of damage, but even then this only really applies to 2/4 maps currently in the game. For CC I found that the thunderbolt and howler were pretty good, the plague is a good single target weapon, and the shattered edge just felt like a wet napkin slap (although I didn't upgrade it that much, again because over 100k to fully upgrade). I think the reward for doing all of the HS is good though, it allows for easier runs later on once you've gotten it and is fulfilling to get. If you want the tldr, it's a good game, if you want to play a round based game similar to some COD zombies then I would recommend. There are just a few issues that hold it back from being amazing. I'm hoping that some of the future content will be of the same quality or even better.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, if you're looking for a fix for CoD zombies, this game has pretty much all of that. Gameplay is pretty ight, perks, PaP, perk upgrade system, mystery box. It's sort of a reskinned zombies, new names and whatnot, though they do have their own mechanics, special enemies are very common, like the one that bursts into flames when it dies, or the one that shoots a laser beam at you. The bosses feel a bit uninspired though, they're tall, tough, and have a couple attack patters, once you get them down though, the bosses become trivial due to their slow speed. I will say though, failing to complete certain objectives around the map can lead to spawning some pretty beefy and fast enemies that are much more of a challenge. Only played solo so far, and haven't completed any of the quests yet, but they are there, and I kinda just found myself doing them, could be due to the quest marker system in place. They do also capture the atmosphere pretty well. Particularly on the second map, it feels claustrophobic, and you can find yourself in a position where you have to use your special ability just to escape. Unfortunately, as rounds progress, the weapon upgrade system doesn't seem to mean much, as even the special weapons on maps when upgraded do very little damage, which can lead to mid game feeling boring because everything is just a bullet sponge. Overall, give the game a 6/10 so far, it captures the spirit of zombies, and would say it's more engaging than cold war zombies, especially with the in-game progression system adding a bit of dynamacy game to game. Wouldn't say it's anything too impressive, but is an enjoyable experience, and definitely fits that roundbased niche, even if the story is handed to you, but I mean, it's fun.(I hear the servers are unstable, but I can't say, have only played solo so far.)Not too stoked about a battlepass for each map, granted, it's free so it's more like a progression system, but the progress is slow. A lot of the game just feels a bit slow like that. Progression, mid game zombies kill times, stuff like that.Edit:Also, little disappointed there aren't character interactions or anything like that. Of course voice acting can get sendy so I get it, but it would be nice to have voiced characters beyond taunts and stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Sker Ritual is a solid COD zombies alternative with its own unique aspects and aesthetics with the same round-based zombies features most would come to expect. With four solid maps each with their own questlines/easter eggs, this game is worth the asking price in my opinion.Here's a more comprehensive breakdown of some pros and cons from my one 90 min session on the first map, in which I completed the main easter egg and reached round 25:~Pros~>The game's atmosphere makes it feel different from Treyarch zombies. Imo, this game feels like a cross between CoD WW2 zombies and Infinite Warfare zombies, which might sound like a red flag to some people but i think it works. The upgraded weapons are given this bioshock, tesla-coil type look, and a lot of the first map looks like a post cold war era research lab underneath a little farm village.>The narrative was passable, it wasn't very in-your-face or over the top, and you definitely can play and choose not to care about it. Still, there seems to be some lore here and the easter egg steps match the vibes of the narrative well.>There is a 5 scale difficulty range, making this game suitable for complete nooblets or zombie vets alike. I played my match on normal and didn't have too much trouble, but the difficulty does spike hard into the later rounds.>The game has made some improvements on the classic zombies formula: Zombies don't windmill attack, it is much more difficult for them to trap you in corners/hallways, and they get stunned if you shoot them past 50% hp, depending on the weapon. That being said, clutch moments are definitely still possible, since a good amount of the zombie varieties are ranged/aoe.>The map size was sizable and the easter egg steps were paced well, with a fair boss fight to close. There are extra secrets and collectibles to find, as well as side and bonus easter eggs to complete that are unguided.>Most of all, the game was a lot of fun! The zombie variety was handled well, the g-slide tech allows for quick doge-like movement, and the dog being the mystery box which was a nice surprise.~Cons~>The game's biggest weakness lies in its engine, which I assume is Unity, and the assets/animations used. This would be excusable if it was still in early access, but its fully released. Enemies visually look narrow, like im playing on the wrong resolution, and the animations for running and being stunned (comically spinning around) felt cheap. This applies for the weapon animations as well, and the view models take up way too much of the screen! >Weapon upgrades felt generally uninteresting. Sure each weapon gets a new look, but I used half the roster and all the upgrade does is bump the damage and that's it.>The perks feel pretty weak, especially since their flavor text shows exactly how much % increase in the upgrade you're getting for buying them. Most of them felt like nerfed versions of some original zombies perks, which may be due to the additional strengths provided by the utility system and secondary perk system.>The secondary perk system felt a bit off and weak. Essentially, every few rounds you can use a "miracle point" to take an upgrade for one of your "utilities" (gun damage, health potion, grenade, melee, and ultimate). At first the game gives you several options to choose from, however once you pick one of these options, you can only upgrade it as the game goes on. It would be nice to experiment with different upgrades for the same equipment slot in the same match.>The game difficulty on normal spiked HARD on round 24-25. The game was almost trivial up until this point, especially when you are given a 30 sec cooldown health potion that insta heals you after a 1 sec animation. Guns feel like they do no damage maxed out at round 25, and with a lot of zombies being ranged/aoe at this point in the match, it started to get a bit stale fast.Ultimately this game is in a solid state right now, and while I will probably continue to wait for gulf war/custom zombies chronicles 2, I hope this game will continue to improve in order to foster some real competition in the round-based zombies market, which is desperately needed after the garbage activision has produced over the past few years.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting 10 hours in on my main account and around an hour and a half into this account I can affirm that Sker Ritual is a good game with a few flaws i would love to see fixed by the developers.The Good:The music is enjoyable and fits the tone of the gameThere is a good weapon varietyIts a fun addition that the random box can give you weapons higher than tier 0The gunplay is enjoyable right from the start and the weapons have good sound effects and have the proper impact when firing.The different enemy types and abilities displayed by them make for enjoyable combat.The missions, while maybe too often containing fetch quests, are enjoyable and engaging for the player.The miracle and boost systems add an enjoyable progression to gameplay.The atmosphere is spot on.The Bad:The enemies in the game have health that scales up too high in the later rounds (This has never led to me dying as you can run past almost any enemy if you understand the games mobility system well enough)The weapon damage does not seem to scale enough in the later tiers, ie 3+The hit detection in game is weird when firing at enemies moving sideways.Hit detection is 50/50 if you aren't the host, even in private games.There are enemies that will teleport to you/spawn on you the moment you are alone, remving any sense of town time from the game, in turn reducing the tension in game.Short term changes that would make a long term addition to the game:have enemy health scale more slowly as rounds increase and instead opt for a larger quantity of enemies (I find myself almost never dying unless in a very narrow hallway because there's never enough enemies to body block me even later in the game)Increase weapon damage in later weapon tiers (The guns feel under-powered in the lategame which leads to me almost ignoring combat to focus on objectives because it feels like there's no point in firing 1-2 magazines to kill a single monster, I also feel no desire to upgrade the weapons to the next tier for 30,000-60.000 points because I know the damage gain isn't really worth it)Stop allowing for mobs to spawn/teleport on the player non stop (games like this are fun because of the tension that ebbs and flows when you're being chased by a mod and then find a moment of respite just to have that mob reappear. In this game i never have the moment of respite, I just keep moving because if i lose the mobs they'll spawn on me, so the tension is gone.)(This teleport/spawn issue also makes it so that the strategy late game is to just run the mobs in a circle until there's only a few of them before doing objectives instead of trying to use those small moments of respite to try and pull off an objective, which again adds to tension)Boss health is pretty spot on in my opinion, so i would make sure to upscale boss HP with the damage increase as to not make bosses too easy to kill. They could also use a damage increase as they're currently and inconvenience rather than a threat.Current rating is a 7/10potential to be a solid 9/10 with those few changes.Note that in my 11-12 hours of playing the game I have only lost once and that was because a mob teleported to me while i was leaving the map and i thought I could tank the damage. (This was my own error and purely a skill issue lol) The game is not overly difficult in anyway, it is honestly more tedious late game than anything and just needs balancing changes to make it a more enjoyable and challenging experience instead of tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual is an atmospheric co-op survival shooter that builds on classic wave-based gameplay, reminiscent of titles like Call of Duty Zombies and Killing Floor. With its eerie setting and the engaging miracle system, it offers a fun and engaging experience, especially when played with friends. However, some bugs and minor issues hold it back from its full potential.Gameplay and Mechanics: 8/10Sker Ritual successfully captures the tense, adrenaline-pumping action typical of wave-based survival shooters. The core mechanics focus on surviving increasingly difficult waves of enemies while using an array of weapons and the game's signature miracle system, which introduces supernatural abilities to help turn the tide. The mix of firearms and supernatural elements keeps combat engaging and adds layers of strategy to each round. The game also allows players to team up and coordinate, which shines particularly in multiplayer sessions. Playing with friends is a highlight, as communication and teamwork become essential for survival.The gameplay is fast-paced, and while it borrows heavily from established titles like Call of Duty Zombies and Killing Floor, it manages to carve out its own identity through its horror elements and the use of miracles. However, bugs like bosses wandering outside their designated arena can disrupt the experience, making it impossible to progress through waves—a frustrating issue that detracts from the otherwise intense action.Atmosphere and Visuals: 7/10Sker Ritual excels in building a creepy, oppressive atmosphere. The game's setting and visual design effectively convey a sense of dread, pulling players into its haunted world. The dark and foreboding environments create a tense backdrop for the action, enhancing the feeling of fighting to survive against overwhelming odds. While the game doesn't boast cutting-edge graphics, the visual style is consistent and suits the horror theme well, maintaining immersion.However, there are occasional visual bugs, such as enemies clipping through objects or getting stuck in the environment, which break the immersion. While these issues are not game-breaking, they are noticeable and suggest that the game could benefit from further polish.Sound Design and Music: 8/10The sound design is a strong point of Sker Ritual, helping to build tension and enhance the overall atmosphere. The eerie ambient noises, enemy sounds, and weapon effects all contribute to a sense of urgency and fear. The soundtrack complements the action and horror elements, heightening the intensity of combat sequences and moments of suspense. Playing with friends while navigating the tense, dark environment becomes an immersive experience, thanks in part to the well-crafted audio.Replayability and Content: 7/10Sker Ritual offers solid replayability through its wave-based structure and cooperative gameplay. The variety of weapons, the miracle mechanic, and different maps keep the experience engaging for multiple sessions, especially with friends. However, the lack of content updates and the presence of bugs, such as bosses wandering outside their arenas, can limit the long-term appeal. The game captures the essence of what made classics like Call of Duty Zombies so beloved, but it needs more variety and polish to maintain player interest over time.Bugs and Technical Issues: 5/10The most significant drawback of Sker Ritual is the presence of bugs and technical issues. While the overall gameplay is fun, encounters with boss fights can be disrupted by bugs, such as the boss wandering out of its designated area, making it impossible for players to defeat it. These issues can be frustrating and break the otherwise tense flow of the game. A few patches could potentially resolve these bugs, but in its current state, they are a notable detractor from the experience.ConclusionSker Ritual is a fun and atmospheric survival shooter that captures the thrill of wave-based combat with a horror twist. The cooperative gameplay and unique miracle system shine, particularly when playing with friends, making it a great title for group sessions. Its atmosphere, sound design, and gameplay mechanics create an immersive experience that fans of the genre will appreciate.However, the presence of bugs, especially those that impact boss fights and progression, detracts from the experience. The game needs further polish and additional content to elevate it from a solid but flawed entry to a standout in the genre. For players who enjoy cooperative survival shooters and can overlook a few technical issues, Sker Ritual is a worthwhile experience, but it may not hold long-term appeal without future updates.Score: 72/100

_childDocuments_.review: Finally after being apart of this game so long I have finally decided to write this review! lets get to the meat of this shiny albeit a bit unpolished gem!Sker Ritual is a fantastic horror FPS based around the ideas of Wales Interactive's previous title Maid of Sker, and the games they've casually played in their off-time, specifically Call of Duty Zombies! It's gameplay formula is most similar to Cod WW2's Nazi Zombies mode with both a guided quest for you to follow and then the ability to do a more difficult unguided easter egg along with a small variety of weapons including your usual shotguns, rifles, smgs and more including some more funky weapons that fulfill the games wonder weapon role. I will now list an extensive amount of things this game does right, wrong, and just okay.  (Can be worked on but is still alright)While an extremely fun game it can be a mixed bag for certain people expecting a lot more compared to call of duty's usual round based zombies experience. I personally love this game but objectively there can be quite bit to note on the more mundane or bad side, making this game quite unpolished compared to most shooters on the market. From stiff janky view-models reminiscent of the early 2010's to net-code problems that might make matchmaking a nightmare. There thankfully is a lot to love about this game and it fits right in for me as an almost nostalgic feeling horde shooter made by a lovely indie dev team who I am very happy to have helped with during early access.

_childDocuments_.review: second game review,Feels good, better then current cod zombies for sure, while I have a couple gripes with mechanics I definitely think would be relevant if this title was $60, at $20 this game is well worth the price if you like cod zombies.The gripesTHE DLC SELECTION OMGThe dlc selection is a problem, I felt the need to tab through every single dlc because the game was more then twice the price with them included, turns out each dlc is just a skin for your character but it feels awful to have the game have a barrier to entry of reading through all those pages, this problem is more on steam then the dev, but if dev could slap a "cosmetic" label on the splash art for the dlc that are cosmetic I think you would get more first time buyers.I dislike having difficulty selection, I understand it being important for the game to be accessable but the game feels significantly easier then the cod version on almost every setting, I think a few difficulties could be eliminated with just having a difficulty where you press a button to start the next round but maintaining the enemy damage and hp so you can practice the easter eggs.melee feels weird, quick melee has an odd delay between swings, I understand the balancing effect here but it just feels bad. I would rather have it do less damage and have less delay then the other way around.I still do not understand how miracles work, particularly the ones that seem like they would be passive, do the new miracles replace the old ones if you dont use them? are they stackable? what actually causes you to gain a miracle point?I dislike tiered "pack a punch" type mechanics, while it is inoffensive here and allows for weapons to scale to lategame better I would prefer that the tiers be devided into different machines or something else to give more of a feeling of each tier being special besides the first and last tier.Edit: 5th game, the wonder weapons are a further gripe (I have been grinding the first map, will do other maps once I clear the boss) both the plague and the thunderbolt feel less like "wonderweapons" and more like what cod ww2 special pack a punches were, the same weapon with some additional particle effects and a little bit of AOE, while they are way better then standard weapons numerically (un upgraded they do similar dps to tier 2) I do not think they do enough to feel special compared to standard weapons.Lastly: honorable soduku. I understand the feeling that you need to balance people extending rounds to do challenges, but honestly, let us just run zombies in circles if we want, dont make them explode for no reason after 5 minutes, its dumb.

_childDocuments_.review: Just got done 100%ing the current map. This game is pretty much literally a copy combination of killing floor 2 and cod zombies but honestly I don't mind that much, I love both of them. A few things I've noticed. -The enemy health multiplier needs to be nerfed or the guns buffed basically every gun except the Remington fails to do any significant damage at all past maybe round 25 including the wonder weapon which even after spending almost 100000 points on it which is another thing-The prices for pack a punch and life tokens are way to high especially when mixed with the fact that most of the guns do such a little amount of damage the prices for pack a punch should be dropped to at least 5000 per use instead of a constant multiplier and the life tokens should be halved down to 2500.-Enemies attacks are too slow and they're too quiet, its not difficult to train zombies because of the multiple wide open areas in the map but if the last zombies dies while your trying to do the riddle in the library it can be close to game ending.-Should be some sort of difficulty slider, I think its a good idea to make the game easy enough for all kinds of player to be able to complete but I do wish it was a bit harder to make it more interesting. -Not as much as a con as I just thought it was weird, the gun names do not match the guns in the game, I'm assuming this is for some copyright related reason however the names the guns currently have are also real names of older guns (the Kalashnikov is called the Fedorov Avtomat and the M14 is the Cei Rigotti) again not like it  needs to be changed its just kinda weird.-The game is a nice representation of the standard welsh countryside on a regular Friday evening.-The map looks great and is fairly large for a first map which gives the player a lot of options with a mix of deadly close quarters corridors and open areas to train enemies. Its never too hard to train zombies however some of the main story steps take place in these close quarters areas making it somewhat harder to progress (which is a good thing it, the story is not too easy and not too hard)-The elites look nice and it feels like just the right amount of them are in the game, not too many so where its like black ops 4 but just enough to keep it interesting (side note: please remove the banshee she makes me want to commit rope neck)-For a game that entered early access 3 days ago its certainly of a somewhat higher quality than most even if it has ideas stolen from cod zombies and killing floor. I kind of feel that it has just enough in common with cod zombies that activision or treyarch or whoever could potentially pursue legal action if the game isn't changed however at the same time it might be just different enough to get away with it. As long as they keep the game updated and keep adding maps, guns, perks, miracles, and other new features I could definitely see myself playing this more.

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game is alright, but there are some pretty big issues in my opinion. The game has great potential but I feel like it could use a bit more polishing as all the small  shortcuts build up to a point of taking me out of the game and making the story far less interesting as I have a much harder time actually getting immersed in the game due to most animations being pre-made or not having any animations at all. The dog is the greatest offender as the lack of any animation makes the dog feel like an object instead of a friend. If I could give a mid rating I would, because the game could get to be amazing but these little things here and there keep it from reaching its full potential.(also like the most mediocre music ever, and the dog doesn't go into his dog house to grab your guns(also also, the lighting is pretty flat in most of the areas in the game, some more exaggerated lighting would be wonderful to help build a dark atmosphere instead of having everything slightly shaded blue and dull)).Edit: The atmosphere is still just so mid man, I want to feel something when I play a horror shooter, not just feel like I'm going through the motions.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- You aint killing Zombies, but I find the Silent a very interesting and original concept- THERE IS ACTUALLY A STORY AND THEY GIVE YOU TELL YOU WHAT YOU NEED TO DO WITHOUT HOLDING YOUR HAND!! Definitely something I feel CoDZ Lacked was the incorporation of a story. Yeah, it had one, but it wasnt prominent. I played a lot of CoDZ and I only know bits and pieces of the lore from watching videos, not from playing the game itself.- Shooting and killing the Silent actually feels really fluid and well designed and the gunfire and reload sounds feel crisp and clean.- I love there is a tier system for the upgrades, like perks and whatnot and I also love you can buy ammo for guns at a reasonable price if you run dry.- The revival tokens are definitely a nice addition cuz at least you dont have to sit out for the rest of the round and can get back up. PLUS, you keep all of your stuff (guns, perks, etc) so it doesnt feel like you are back at square one each time you die- I genuinely love the healthbars so you dont have to guess how much longer a certain enemy will last and the minibosses and world events were a great addition to keep you on your toes.Cons:- I havent ever had a chance to revive my co-op partners because of how short of a timer it is. You have too many hostiles to deal with and you really dont get a chance to revive and if you dont have any revive tokens, your out for the round without being given a chance.- The guns feel underleveled the further you go. Because of how fast the rounds are, the hostiles get stronger a lot quicker and if you dont have the points, you cant upgrade them in time to keep on par with the level- In CoDZ, shooting a zombie will give you 10 points. Its why some people can have over 20k points midgame. I think if they had something where it would give you 1 point or 1 point per like X effective hits, it would combat some of the recursive buys in the game, like the weapon upgrade systemOverall:I really love the design of this game and I do hope to see it being developed more and I am IMMENSELY enjoying it so far. I also am holding out hope for a PS5 release w/ crossplay cuz I have friends who are on Playstation and are sad they cant join groups of friends in games who are on Xbox/PC cuz they cant afford switching platform. This game is fun and its a not a bad way to kick back after a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ workday with some friends. As of this review, I have 2.6 hours in the game and I gotta say absolutely AMAZING work for a team of only 5 developers!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game in a while that has brought back the memories of playing COD Zombies with friends. I think Wales Interactive has a good foundation for Sker Ritual, and with improvements over time, this could be a real competitor for Activision. The developers care and are constantly listening to community feedback and suggestions to improve the game. Plus, the developers offer a free DLC road map for new maps and weapons. I really enjoy the innovative take on the COD Zombies approach to a round-based game. I think the varying enemy types are awesome, the maps are amazing, the Easter eggs are super fun, and the miracle system allows for a new experience every game. The only con for the game is that it doesn't feel as polished as COD Zombies, but this is understandable given the size of the team and doesn't take away from the experience. If you want an innovative take on the round based COD Zombies genre or are sick of the lack of effort from Activision and looking for something to fill that itch, then this is it. Plus, you can't beat the price of $20–25.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I had hoped it would be and more. I see a lot of reviews mentioning crashing and bugs, I have yet to crash and sometimes do run into random things around some parts of the maps but never anything that would hurt the playability.In terms of customization and replayability this game has that and more. Plenty of different levels, perk upgrades, guided easter egg quests, hidden easter egg quests, maps, and weapons. Try not to go into it with the mindset of it being COD Zombies, while it's similar and you will compare the two, it is very much its own game and it is an amazing game and take on a round based survival shooter! It's better than any zombies rendition following Infinite Warfare honestly!To the developers: Thank you guys for such a fun game, made me feel like a kid again chasing objectives and high rounds! One thing I will ask, if you can change the spawn rate for the zombies on normal mode as rounds get higher. _childDocuments_.review: The problem is, all of this cosmetic content are variations of the same few things.Masks, background, audio lines, icons. That's effectively it. I think my major gripe with this is that you can only wear 1 mask at a time. So even though I own all the cosmetic DLCs, and have a dozen+ masks, I can only use 1 at a time. So I really don't care about unlocking more. If the different weapon tier skins were unlockables in the same way as masks, and instead different tiers were color, VFX, and sounds variants, progression would feel a lot more satisfying. Not trying to make this sound as if it's easy, but from my perspective this would be worthwhile. I'll be looking at a gun the entire time I'm playing the game, while I will almost never see my own mask.The problem is, half the time you will only find Lucky/Mystery Box in the later half of the game, and every map just gives you access to buy the same few guns and garbage melee weapons that don't scale effectively. Lucky has some great weapons to offer, and I love that you can get different tier weapons from him. But why do I have to wait until I beat the first 3 mini-bosses in map 4 to see him? Please let me waste all of my points on him earlier in the game.Featuring some really great game-breaking bugs causing hard-stops in quest progression. For QA, this has happened to me on maps 2 and 3. Map 2 was saying we'd only placed 2 canisters, even though I'd just placed the third. I placed the third one in the starting room with the difficulty changing rock. Map 3 was finding keys, I grabbed one of the keys and all of the indicators disappeared, so we looked up a guide and couldn't find keys at the locations in the guide.Ultimately, because I've actually really still enjoyed playing the game, and it has so much going for it. With the content planned the price-tag seems pretty fair as well. I just hope there's time for refinement, and that these buggy patches are just a symptom of adapting to a live-release format (I will edit this review if they're more permanent). To me, 4 maps is great, but only if I can replay them in different ways, and they aren't breaking. Meaning maybe Lucky spawns in random dog houses, we get more weapon options (This probably doesn't align with the game's current goals, but even if this meant less visual variation in the tiered weapon models/textures, this would make an incredible difference imho), a more generic survival mode without puzzles, or . All in all, I've enjoyed this game so far. Maps 1 and 4 are fantastic, I love the feeling of upgrading my guns (sword is great too, but general melee doesn't feel worthwhile after a few rounds), I love the perks and meta-game upgrades. It just needs some more love!The road-map for this year looks excellent, and if it comes with bug fixes and general polish, I'm sure I'll be back to update this review. I know it's gonna seem counter-intuitive, but I still recommend you try it. If you run into bugs on your first play-through, refund it, or do what I'll do and sit tight for future stability and content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like to leave reviews. But I could not ignore doing this one.I loved playing this game for the time I did. Even when I got stuck for no reason on the second map. It has a lot it needs to work on. But that's not the reason for my review.I am a concept artist. And from mine and other concept art perspectives. Their conceptual artwork for the miracles and dragon designs from the notes you collect in game are very fishy. They have the same mistakes that AI art generators would make. E.g. Brigid- Her pupils clip over the eyelids and her hand is just a wrist with fingers attached to it. There is no palm.Morrigan- The crow rested at the bottom is very misshapen. it's wing looks like it's been broken from its body and one to the upper right looks like its merging with her hair.Draig- On one design it has 3 claws, and on another on the same page it has 5 claws, it is missing an arm on the bottom concept and its missing parts of its wings.These are not all of the found mistakes either. Just a small portion of them.Even at a basic level beginner artists would notice these mistakes. These aren't the sort of mistakes humans would make. Most know a western dragon (excluding the wyvern and wyrm) would have 4 arms. Even if it didn't. it would have a clear indication that it is missing an arm. It is inconsistent with the other concept of it since that dragon has all 4 limbs attached. So why does this one have a missing arm in one of its designs? Another tell tale sign is the hands. The way they are in the notes does not make sense. AI commonly struggles portraying hands and a lot of the concepts that have visible hands and arms have them misshapen, merged into other body parts or just two arms attached together.

_childDocuments_.review: I fundamentally do not understand why Call of Duty refuses to give us a traditional round-based zombies experience. I’ve got a feeling it’s due to the fact they cannot find a way to over-monetize zombies like they do with WZ & MP.Nonetheless, this game is a decent pickup, especially since 10 year old cod games are STILL $60!?I nearly beat the first level with my brother on the first try, and I have some things to say. Overall, I enjoy the game…. But there are some serious flaws.First, there is cross play, my brother played on his series x and I was on my pc, but there are some wild networking bugs. His internet is worse than mine so we thought I should host, but whenever I did I was stuck infinitely at “waiting for other players” while he had already loaded into the game? Also, cross play just doesn’t work. So instead of being able to directly invite each other to a party, we have to match make in a public session at the same time & on the same map and wait till we see each other, then one of us can invite the other to a party to play private matches. Yikes.The gameplay is pretty great, however I think the first few rounds go by WAY too quickly. Additionally, there needs to be a way to make a crawler so we can explore without being chased down by full speed zombies. Also, why do the zombies have ranged attacks..? I’m not a huge fan of that. Like if occasionally a ranged zombie spawned that would be cool, but the diver that shoots lasers and the flame throwing zed spawn very often. Also, the revive tokens are a cool concept, but they are too expensive. Players should respawn at the end of a round with no gear and full points.Lastly, while we’ve only played the first map, we were 99% done with it. But the boss fight with Abraham is just not fun. Idk if this was a networking bug, but Abraham had an attack where he tossed something at you to pull you towards him. But there is NO INDICATION THAT ITS ABOUT TO HAPPEN. There absolutely needs to be a unique anamation and audio queue before you just get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ yoinked away from where you are and towards a massive boss, who is sometimes surrounded by zombies who all hit you at the same time and kill you before you can even do anything about it. That’s how we failed. Absolutely pissed me off because there isn’t a way to know when you’re gonna get yoinked away.However, with all that being said, it’s an early access game, so jank is to be expected. Since Activision refuses to give us a traditional cod zombies experience, this works well. And some things like “triple points” made me laugh out loud. It’s pretty fun after spending 10min trying to play a private match via cross play lol

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual does some great things and really helps scratch the itch to play a round based zombies mode. The game at whole plays pretty similarly and they still use creative differences to make the game wholly separate.Things the Game Does Well: - Fun and easy main objectives with hidden easter eggs to follow that are still doable without too much stress - Unique wonder weapons - Cool take on the mystery box with Lucky the Dog - Straightforward gameplayThings the Game Does Not Do Well - Hit indicator is sometimes hard to track (personal preference) - Game can be a bit dark unless you turn up brightness (also personal preference) - Poor optimization          - The optimization seems to be there but it struggles at times. In comparable games I run settings on ultra and have no issue pushing 200+ fps to ensure I make the most of my 165hz monitor. In Sker Ritual, it constantly bounces between ~120-170 dependent on whats going on.Overall I think the game is worth playing and I definitely think that the optimization issues are outweighed by the game being good all around. I would like to see new weapons and perks come sooner than later to keep gameplay fresh. However, if you are a fan of these kinds of games, you'll enjoy Sker Ritual.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, not to go on and on, but...(Apparently, this is a port of a console game)1) Movement is a pig:You have to press shift AFTER pressing W in order to run.Otherwise, you get to walk away from the zombie hoard. Nice.Why isn't the character running by default? There's zombies outside O_oRunning up stairs? Sometimes works.Running through doors? Sometimes works.Resuming running while ever shift is pressed because you stopped running for some reason. Nah.2) The zombies can wall you in so you can't get away.  I especially LOVE that mechanic.3) Gameplay is so painfully mismatched. Just feels like they didn't test the gameplay properly, or enough.  Also, the animations are sooo ssssllllooooowwwwww for someone trying to kill zombies in a hurry lol4) Revive mechanism is a dog:You get shown where to revive, even if you have no revive token.A... ONE... Single revive token!Apparently there are glitches to do with this, but I haven't played it for long enough to see much else.5) All the zombies on the map will run towards you even when they can't see you.Yeah. Makes sense. O.oIt's so much fun after respawning... with no bullets. And the worst melee mechanism I have ever had the misfortune to encounter:6) The melee attack is, well, ridiculous;I think you attack on the order of 5 times a minute.  Exactly what you'd expect from someone trying to kill zombies.It does feel unfinished, unbalanced and clunky.  The map I played on is replete with glitches and awkwardness. Like you're fighting against the developer's code and not working with it - Fighting the game and not the zombies.I know the dev team is small, but it is a shame that they couldn't play test it more before releasing it.  The movement, weapon dynamics and the unbalanced gameplay just makes it feel confusing, futile and ultimately not enjoyable.  It has a lot of potential, though, if they could just sort out the movement bugs and add a proper weapons/interaction interface.It's not often that I say the game is in the way of it being played, but this seems to be the time.Lastly, navigating and reading the in-game's interface doesn't pause the game. So much fun.Refund requested.It's just not that enjoyable and I couldn't 'get into' it.  I could barely even play it lolGood to hear so many other people might have it on their favourites list, though.Adding new content when the gameplay is still broken? -1 point.Releasing the game when gameplay is still broken? -5 point.Adding bugs whilst fixing bugs? -10 points.The crosshairs are enormous and CAN'T BE CHANGED!  You can customise your guns, but not your HUD O_o Again... Wha...??! -4 points.The running SFX sound like your legs are about 20cm long, it's totally hilarious. -1 points.Map design is chaotic.  The revive mechanic... Going back to the beginning of the level is just g**s. -6 points.You can end up in an untenable position where you can't actually do anything and just die. -7 points.You die randomly without it being obvious that you were actually hit. -10 points.Not much satisfaction from shooting.I can't, in good conscience, recommend this game in it's current state given the lack of enjoyment I have experienced.  You may like it, but you also may end up stuck with it with no chance of a refund.A lot of people have compared it to a game called 'COD Zombies', which I have no experience of playing.  Although, if it is anything like this clone, I probably wouldn't enjoy that game either lolI am not a fan of getting stuck on scenery (SE4!!!); underpowered, slow or inappropriate weapons; sssssllllooooowwww player animations in a fast-paced, frantic hoard game - especially when using weaponry - break up the flow and makes for a disjointed and jarring playthrough.Some mechanics seem to have been purposefully introduced in place of proper gameplay mechanics and events and that's what's get me the most.  It makes the dev(s) seem (for want of a better word) lazy, like their heart isn't in the result; their end vision cannot be reached; or their end vision is incomplete.  The amount of attention paid to how the mechanics affect the player, the game and the task/scenario needs to be looked at.A lot of potential, but there seem to be missing steps in the planning and development phases of this game which are leaving holes in the gameplay and some mechanics.I highly recommend that the dev(s) write out a more exhaustive chart of the game, focus on the details and how they fit together and stick to that, maybe develop an extensible game framework to build the game around to make it more consistent and easier to change/modify the mechanics in future.Idk, I'm just some random guy on the Internet.

_childDocuments_.review: I could make a whole essay on the good and the bad of this game but here is a simple and quick review of the game after a little over an hour in the title as someone who just happened to stumble upon this game thinking that it might be something to get a little enjoyment out of.The Good:- Concept (has the ground working of something interesting but flawed execution) - Graphics/Design workThe Bad:- Gameplay (very similar to cod zombies without much too make it stand out in the genre)- Runtime per map (In terms of completing a main story in the map)- Fast paced combat and movement with very slow, tedious missions and mission objectives sometimes take too much of your attention away from the horde that is constantly coming with little to no wiggle room too work with in and in-between rounds- Pushes lots of lore too quickly too where it can be easily forgotten or overlooked especially when dealing with hordes of zombies grabbing your attention- Weapons and weapon feel are lacking in the feeling of power as you can find a new weapon later into a map and it will deal similar or weaker damage to what you might've had before- Way to much enemies way too quickly (Zombie waves get way too large way too quickly)Overall the game still needs a lot of work put into it too make it feel worth the hassle of getting through the story with its current game play problems and actually being able to involve yourself with the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels terribly close to a janky early access title. I've played CoD zombies before, the original - from WaW, and this definitely has its moments for sure. It's not devoid of fun, but you'll have to put up with so much just to get the most out of this game.The main thing that's extremely infuriating to deal with right now is the annoyingly inconsistent hit-registration. It happens once the game ramps up the enemy spawns, everything starts teleporting and suddenly your shots and melee hits will appear to connect, but never actually do anything. You will, however, take a lot of damage, and it's already a huge fustercluck so you can't do anything about it.Using your abilities during the supposedly more exciting waves have a large amount of delay, when it usually doesn't. There's also a universal lack of feedback, it doesn't help that invisible and actually-telegraphed teleporting enemies are spammed - some of them are purposefully quiet which adds to frustration.Look, objectives are fun, I like 'em, it adds variety and makes me feel like I'm doing a small 4-man raid with friends. The problem is that sometimes you'll have to carry around an objective weapon; This alone isn't a huge issue, it's just that sometimes there are objectives where you need to deposit an item. The prompt to deposit and replace on-hand weapon is the same. Let's say you have a tier 5 weapon, in the heat of battle and protecting your team, but you also need to deposit, but suddenly it just replaces your tier 5 weapon, and now you can't kill anything. Nice.The above mentioned problem wouldn't be such a huge issue if upgrades weren't so painfully slow, especially for first-time runs, when you're still figuring out the objectives while surviving waves. For the most part my most used weapon is the knife, and the axe, because shooting feels so awkward, and I've played so many shooters - this has the weirdest and floatiest feeling.Enough rambling. Is this game fun? It's possible to have fun, yes. I like the art style of the gear, especially the Bioshock-esque weapon upgrades. I also like the abilities, I think they're fun - though poison is kind of useless. Unfortunately there's just so many problems that take away from the experience that I can't recommend this, not even with friends. Maybe when the issues get ironed out, get it on a discount, otherwise it's a pass for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel obligated to offset the somehow positive reviews of this game with my one pointless review.I've played CoD Zombies for as long as I can remember, and this game is a disservice to the niche genre. It clearly has some effort put in, but it's just seriously lacking in fundamental ways that matter.Just some of my issues in no particular order:No FOV setting.Dedicated servers instead of p2p—40 minutes into my first match the servers simply decided that my friend and I could no longer shoot zombies or do basic actions. Also, there is a baseline level of lag on all zombies and players even at low ping. Coupled with poor lag compensation, multiplayer matches just feel terrible.Extreme lack of weapon balance—some of the weapons are clear winners.Lack of weapon variety—I used the mystery box equivalent and got the following. Baseball bat, crossbow, baseball bat, fire axe, baseball bat, hunting rifle, crossbow, double barrel. Make of that what you will. The 'wall-buy' weapons appear to be at least half of the weapons available in the box besides medieval weaponry. I really have no idea what direction the devs were taking the weapons in. It's pretty pathetic considering how much character weapons have in CoD Zombies.Obvious quality of life issues that simply aren't thought of. For example, there's a teleporter on the second map. If you take it and there happens to be a few zombies on the other side, you simply die. CoD Zombies had the forethought to simply ragdoll those zombies or have them respawn elsewhere on the map.Lower-than-average performance on RTX 3070, i5-13600k. No stutters, but 60-70 fps at 1440p.Poor input handling/buffering. Sliding is almost useless because you cannot continue your sprint afterward without spamming the sprint key in an effort to get the game to recognize that you don't want to be crouched.Almost every feature in the game feels hastily implemented and like an obvious effort to take advantage of a lull in CoD Zombies content, rather than pay homage while improving the niche. It would take an absurd amount of overhauling to get this game to a playable state in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Is it perfect? no. But the game is fun. For how small the dev team is, its a great game. Like some of the other reviews I've seen, this is sorta what Zombies players have been asking for, a standalone zombies experience. Its beyond me how CoD hasnt figured that out yet, but these guys did, so kudos.  The "rogue-like" elements with the gods makes the game super re-playable as well. There probably will be some balance with them in coming patches ( some are ridiculously OP), but most of them feel pretty good. Weapons are fairly balanced early, and actually feel really good on later rounds (as long as you keep pace with upgrading them), which is more than you can say for any of the other recent zombies iterations.The EE's are fun, and much like WW2 or Cold War, are guided. But then there are secret EE's as well after you complete the main stories, which personally I still havent really found anything about. Aside from a couple steps on 2 of the 4 maps. All and all, good game from an Indie studio that has taken advantage of the gap in  a competent CoD zombies experience. I dont know if there are really any maps or other content on the horizons, but for now the 4 maps on release are quite fun, and still have some mystery to them.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this writing Sker Ritual is still very much a work in progress, but also one that shows a lot of promise. The gameplay draws heavy inspiration from the various Call of Duty Zombies mode iterations (accruing points by killing enemies, using those points to unlock doors and purchase weapons/upgrades, fighting through waves of increasing difficulty, etc.) while also very much doing its own thing with its spooky Lovecraftian setting and enemies. Sker Ritual also has a much more forgiving learning/difficulty curve than CoD Zombies, if you want you can just grind waves and see how far you make it, or there's a main quest you can work through by completing various objectives around the map (and even a boss fight at the end). Unlike the more intricate/obtuse "main easer eggs" in CoD Zombies, the Sker Ritual main quest (at least the one for the single map that's currently in the game) can be completed in its entirely without much difficulty even if you're playing solo. I appreciate this lower difficulty curve, but I'm hopeful that future maps will increase the challenge just a smidge (or that developer Wales Interactive has plans to implement formal difficulty levels) since right now it's just a little too easy to trivialize the difficulty by upgrading the pump shotgun a few tiers and going ham.That being said, I much prefer a game like this be just a little too easy than too hard. The current 'Sker Pass' of unlockable cosmetics still feels a tad too grindy, even after the most recent patch which reduced XP requirements for leveling up, but I get that Wales Interactive doesn't want players to burn through all 50 tiers too quickly since it's currently the game's only form of progression. Again I'm hopeful that Wales has plans to implement new progression systems and unlock categories (my assumption is that we'll eventually get stuff like weapon skins and character avatar outfits), but all good things in due time.For now, it's best to look at Sker Ritual as an investment purchase. What's currently there likely won't hold your interest for too long (though, as always, it helps if you have a few friends to blast monsters with), but like I said before, there's a lot of promise, and Wales has already released an early roadmap of upcoming content additions to look forward to. Hopefully we won't have to wait too long to play those additions for ourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend this game in spite of the lackluster zombies that Call Of Duty has given us the past however many years but this game is definitely not ready to compete. Fundamentally i enjoy this game a lot and i hope it eventually succeeds and surpasses COD, but it still has many flaws. I will preface these by saying I played multiplayer and cannot speak on the single player experience, if that changes my criticisms at all.1. Performance: you can FEEL the performance on this game. Me and my friends all experienced the game feeling and looking extremely choppy or just general not smooth gameplay when playing this game even with some of us having 150+ frames. Running off a 3070 and 5800x I would expect the gameplay to feel more smooth.2. Hud/Aesthetics: What I mean more so than aesthetics is just how some information is presented. The hud itself is messy and feels pretty cluttered; simplification could definitely assist a little bit in this aspect. But there are quite a few areas where the visuals are just messy; such as the visual clutter of shooting zombies with pack-a-punch weapons and having a crazy amount of text popping up and cluttering your screen.3. Engine: Now this one can be seen as more of a preference or nitpick but I'm curious how other people feel about this. The game physics feels like you are a roblox character and not a person in the same way cod made you feel like you have weight. When you jump it just feels like you being teleported higher and then dropping, not like a human dropping. I cant exactly explain it in words other than just saying it doesnt feel like you are a human and it more so feels like you are a roblox or gmod character.Again I don't dislike this game and I really hope for it to succeed but at the current moment I cant in good faith recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual is a great example of the Treyarch COD Zombies formula executed and done right with the twists needed to make the game different where it needs to be. This game scratches the itch that I've had since BO3 zombies, now the maps aint no Der Eisendrache, but some of them are very comparable to some older maps in the series. The one thing Sker Ritual needs to do to really cement itself as another Zombies game one needs to have if they enjoy the genre is, map variety, gun variety, and craftable traps and weapons. The current game and flow is great but I cannot see myself playing the hundreds of hours of Zombies ive played in BO3 let alone the rest of the franchise. Dont let this discourage you though, this is fresh new Zombies for anyone who enjoys Treyarch Zombies and needs some good gameplay. Its amazing to see a small studio giving a go at something thats been essentially monopolized for no other reason than, no one could make something as fun and enjoyable as Treyarch Zombies, and its safe to say Sker Ritual does that. Im no where near done with the 4 current maps and easter eggs but im excited to see whats to come from Sker Ritual.

_childDocuments_.review: I am revising my review from negative to positive... I gave this game a second chance and it got its hooks into me, proving to be an excellent experience! My initial impression of the game was extremely bad due the cons I have listed below in my original (negative) review.I never played COD Zombies (from which this game is based), so I really didn't know the meta. Once I got a bit of map knowledge, I found the objectives to be (mostly) a lot of fun (still, f*** the labyrinth/goat maze in the Hotel map). Going for high rounds is a blast, the weapons feel punchy and varied, the enemies are well varied, the bosses are fun, and adjustable difficulty allows you to play it at exactly the level you want to play (and you can adjust it mid-round). As mentioned below, while a bit different, it reminded me of "Unloved", another favorite of mine. Evading and killing the hordes is hella fun. Though I stand by the cons I listed in my original review, and they do mar the experience a bit for me, overall I'd say I really enjoyed the game.One recommendation I would make for new players, or for those like me who haven't played COD Zombies, don't be discouraged if you can't "finish" the map objectives. COD Zombies actually called them "Easter Eggs". The original goal was really just to see how long you could survive. If the objectives are not fun, going for high rounds definitely still is!The game is well polished, well balanced, looks great, feels great, and once you get a feel for the mechanics, is challenging and fun. It was made by an enthusiast indie dev team with a lot of love (which inspired me to take a second look), and boy, am I glad I did.Original review (cons):Two game in a row this weekend with the same problem: Run around lost and look for little things that are easy to miss. Maps are way to maze-like, corridors are too narrow, objectives are nebulous, multiplayer has janky bugs, upgrades are too expensive... I could go on.Perhaps the biggest problem is that this game relies heavily on three mechanics which are almost universally despised by most gamers: Escort missions, timers, and mazes. If you want an action/zombie game that is more focused on the action and less focused on getting lost and escorting lambs, pick up "Unloved" instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not your daddy's FPS Horde Shooter. There have been a lot of negative remarks and postings from people who haven't even played the game or sat for 3 minutes at EGX and made assumptions. Let's give you a more informed and detailed review so you can get the full story.With 5 hours of solid game play in at review time, I can offer better answers to your questions.First, let's remember this is still in Early Access (Day 1, actually). If you don't want to deal with some slight issues or possible bugs, wait for full release (Scheduled for early 2023). As for my game play, there were only small control issues and some stuck points the devs are already aware of and fixing.Controller or Mouse and Keyboard? Both! And they are hot-swap capable. This means you can try your mouse and keyboard then plug in your controller and take over the game play right away. Unlike other shooters you don't need the controller plugged in before you load the game (or unplugged) and which ever you use for control, that is what will work.Is this a sequel to Maid of Sker? No. It is not. It does use the characters from that game. The Horde is made up of the Quiet Ones and they are out to get you, each type with special abilities. Add in the mini bosses (Banshee, Abraham, Phantom, etc) and Level Bosses for each map and you have a lot to shoot at.Is this game slow? Absolutely not. It is a round based horde shooter. So yes, the first few rounds are going to be a little slower. Depending on the number of players, your first few hordes can be quite small. (Did I mention the horde size scales to the number of players in your party? Yeah, they do!)How many maps are there? In total there will be at least 4 maps. Early Release contains one. It is MASSIVE. Just like most other games, you won't have access to all of it right from the start. and THIS is where Sker Ritual starts to become different from the rest.You start with a basic weapon, have the opportunity to buy new ones (in game, on the fly) and upgrade them to more powerful versions as you progress. Random enemies will drop "power ups" which are time based (5 to 20 seconds) powers such as area effects, 1-shot kills, refill ammunition and more.You also earn "Miracles," one-use or semi-permanent buffs to your weapons, melee attack or abilities. You get to choose from 3 Miracles at each level up. Just be quick, the horde doesn't stop while you make a decision.When you kill enemies you get points, and those points are used to unlock doors around the map, giving you access to more and more areas. You don't just shoot to kill, though.While you are unlocking map areas and being chased by hundreds of Quiet Ones and bosses, you have to also maintain ammunition levels, power up your health and endurance, and solve little puzzles. All at the same time.What? You didn't think it was JUST an FPS did you? You will need to complete objectives to get through the entire map. Crossing back to areas you have already been and finding new doors or access points to areas you didn't even know where there. As the horde size grows and gets faster, they become better suited to match your abilities and can easily overwhelm you. You also need to figure out how to perform certain actions, when, and where those actions need to be completed.If you think you are just going to shoot "zombies" and rack up points, think again. You must think on your feet, escape trouble, stay alive and use your brain to find the next path, which is rarely easily found.Action, Adventure, Zombie Shooter, FPS, Puzzle Solver, Horror Co-Op, Round Based, Fast Paced and a LOT of fun. I don't know many games that can offer all of that, but Sker Ritual does. It may not be everyone's cup of tea, but it is a lot more than you are expecting, I can promise you that.8/10 from me, with promises of improving as Full Release comes closer.

_childDocuments_.review: So I have about 40+ hours on this game so i think its time for a review. the game overall is a 7/10 imo. Sker does many Things well and many things not so well. Pros : Good atmosphere and overall map designs. fun classic round based horde shooter. relatively easy main Easter eggs and fun hidden Easter eggs.  decent boss fights and good variety of enemies/guns. A Good perk selection with no perk limit. a sick selection of masks and best of all free DLC maps/ weapons. cons : laggy servers (anyone who is not the host). mini bosses who don't pose much of a threat and are just annoying bullet sponges at times. the point system inst the greatest. you almost have to pick a single gun and dump all your points into it in order to be able to kill anything. the game almost punishes you for trying new guns during the match. upgrading weapons don't change at all and only give you extra ammo in your reserve. If I spend 155,000 points to fully upgrade a weapon i should at least have more that 20 bullets in the gun. some of the miracle skill trees are absolutely awful and feel like a waste of money/points. somethings I would like to see : giving the bosses/ mini bosses a little more character. maybe giving them voice lines or there own music when they spawn. decrees how much xp is required to unlock camos or change it to required tasks like kills/head shot kills. make upgrading guns feel more rewarding like increased mag sizes or alternate fire modes (make starting pistol full auto for example). be a little more involved with the community. I had to do an update today and I have no idea what it was for. overall the game has its strengths and weaknesses but it adds to the charm. I wouldn't go as far to say its the next cod zombies killer buts its defiantly a fun game to play solo or with friends.  The devs seem to be working hard on this game and it shows. I know it takes time to perfect a game especially for a small team. I sincerely enjoy the game and I hope it has a good life cycle. If you had any doubts if you should get the game I say you should just don't expect the game to be perfect. its not a perfect game but thats ok. you cant rush perfection.
