_childDocuments_.review: Even though the game is in very early access and lacks alot of polish and content, what there is is pretty solid. You can beat the main objective of the first, and currently only, mission in about 25-30 rounds and I've done so twice. The game is good so far but I've noticed a few problems, which is expected in an early access title.Nitpicks:1. the first one is graphical, the weapons and many of the textures look very bland and unpolished. I imagine this will be updated as time goes on but your guns won't look very eye pleasing. 2. The design of the weapons are fairly bland but change as you upgrade them. However the Thunderbolt NEEDs and overhaul, when you ADS the barrel isn't lined up where you fire, and it lacks an iron sight. The gun is fairly decent but how it feels to fire is attrocious. Problems: The only real problems i've had with the game so far is how imbalanced the weapons feel, the pump action shotgun is objectively the strongest weapon once you start upgrading it without equal, and alot of weapons you'd expect to be very solid options, the Hunting rifle and assault rifle, are extremely lackluster in terms of damage and over all usability.The other problem being the poor explanation of your abilities and how you level up. everyone has 5 default ability, 3 active and 2 passive. When you get a miracle you can decide to branch your active differently then other by leveling them up.  It sounds good but you don't actually have much time to sit and reach each option when you level up, giving some extra time between rounds to read and process what choices you have would be nice.Bugs: I've only ran into two bugs so far, one fairly minor and the other actually unenjoyable. The first being that every time I throw a grenade, theres a 1/4 chance it clips through the floor or detonates without an effect. This is mostly an annoyance but nothing I lost sleep over. The second being the final boss. When me and my friends go to fight him, after his first few attacks he just stands still, and given you can 7 hit kill him with a tier 3 pump action shotgun it makes him kind of a cake walk. All of these are entirely due to a lack of polish, which is to be expected for a game that was released 3 days ago. The game is playable and is fairly fun despite the current issues and lack of content, i'd recommend this game but also say that waiting for the game to be in a slightly more polished state before picking it up is 100% understandable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this from someone who loves the Call of Duty Zombies franchise from the bottom of my heart. I've played all the zombies maps from CoD since day 1, and have been consistently playing every release with the inclusion of the semi-frequent custom zombies map. I want to love this game. I want to dearly recommend this game to anyone that likes the CoD zombies franchise... But I can't. Now I have high expectations for this game, which might be unfair to the devs as they're a small team, but I have to be honest for anyone expecting the same level of quality coming from a CoD zombies game. The core mechanics, and soul of the game are definitely there in the game itself... But. This is a real diamond in the rough kind of game. It needs a crap-ton of polish before it starts to feel like a suitable replacement to the CoD Zombies formula. Before I continue with the Pros, and Cons. I understand there's a roadmap which hopefully means more updates and changes, so if my problems are fixed with updates, I'll change my review to suit.My biggest gripe, and hardest to change, is again. Map layout. Pack-a-Punch is usually situated in a location that has great meaning to the map and is often a reward for fighting through hordes, and or completing parts of the map. Such as the O.G Der Riese, where you finally earn the power to upgrade your guns after teleporting 3 times. Moon, where you reach the teleporter and go back to Earth. Shadows of Evil where you complete various tasks, and finally reach the seedy under-belly to complete a ritual to earn the Pack, etc., etc. In this game, Pack feels like it’s randomly thrown in. Whether it’s placed in the corner of a corridor, the exact next side room of spawn, or just in a random room far away from spawn. Even finding the pack-a-punch feels like a chore. Unlike Cold War, there is no mini-map to help you navigate the level, and if you want to use the older CoD maps as a comparison, it fails in that regard, since the older maps had a blackboard-esque map guide to help you through the levels. Even further, it’s so confusing to find Lucky for the same reason. In zombies, you want to know where the Mystery Box is? Look up. There’s a bright blue beam, and if you can’t see it, ala Kino der Toten where the majority takes place indoors, the blackboard lights up to help you find it. In Sker, good ‘luck’ finding Lucky. Sometimes zombie doors look incredibly similar to walkthrough door, making it confusing on where to go next. And all that can be honestly forgiven, if not for the most egregious problem. Every map feels like it’s a maze of horribly tight corridors with no breathing room. A usually good zombie map consists of a medium-sized spawn room that leads into 2 choices of doors that lead into an often bigger room, branching off into different choices of corridors with inclusions of rooms to run around in, so you never feel trapped. In Sker… It feels like every map is “Oops, All Corridors” with a few small rooms to breathe in. The maps feel too big, yet constricting in their size. Like a pool that’s too deep. Sometimes a smaller, yet detailed map is better, than a spread-too-thin map that tries way too hard to be a “final” level map. There’s a reason why Shadows of Evil, Der Riese, Kino der Toten, Mob of the Dead, and Ascension are all so beloved. Again the main, and core mechanics are all there. I sincerely hope with all my heart that the game only gets better, and better.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised. I tried out the demo and showed it to two of my friends, and we spent a night just running the game. Very old-school Zombies vibe, the controls are very close with some Roguelite elements tied in to the perks system. I will say that the netcode needs a little uplift and/or the option to just peer to peer could be nice. Playing on 113ms and it's still a little janky as it feels like animations slow down a little on higher ping, I can see this being more as a hindrance for matchmaking if the lobby host isn't local or near you but It's not that much of an issue when you're having a blast.Enemy types are pretty unique, I loved the early introduction of the blazeslingers, ranged zombies are cool. We get 4 campaigns to play and each are pretty unique, the writing/story telling could be a bit more cohesive however it's still very well done for an indie game.I will admit, I mainly looked into this as it's developed in my home country. (DEWCH I GYMRU!!) and this game definitely hits all the classic Zombies feels whilst giving it some nice QoL and new mechanics that don't detract from the actual game play.For the price it's worth it, especially if you want a game to play with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is, as one of my friends called it "a little crusty." However, it is quite fun. I've only tried two of the maps thus far, but I like what I've played. If you like CoD Zombies, it's very similar to that style of game. There's less weapons, but just as much fun and easter eggs/hidden endings. Guns can get upgraded, you can get more masks akin to Payday. There's 4 free "passes" that have cosmetics and masks to unlock that are based on the maps. There are also random buildcrafting abilities "miracles" that you can choose as you play each map that changes the gameplay each time you load in. This makes gameplay fresh each time. Definitely worth a try if you like Zombies and have always wanted a CoD Zombies standalone. There are some frame rate issues and bugs, but these devs seem fairly small and very responsive. Looking forward to the future of the game and I might check out their other game Maid of Sker for lore purposes (as Sker Ritual takes place within that universe).Verdict: 8/10 Fun, replayable, especially fun with friends, dig the lore and ambiance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a foot in the door for competition in this dry-land genre pretty much exclusively ran by Activision. The guns and their animations FEEL like your character is genuinely using them, the unique rouge-lite abilities every game along with the varied and unique weapon designs leave a fun feel to the gunplay and survival. The music fits each moment and intensifies the encounter, monster designs are detailed and varied, even in the casual "zombie". Although intro and end cut scenes are clearly very amateur, there is also very clear love and detail put into the game.Clearly borrowing a lot from CoD Zombies, especially Cold War, but solving a lot of those games's issues. Each map having unique mobs of its own to deal with, and mechanics exclusive to it, keeping things fresh each map. In the future if this game gets continued support, I only request 5 things, a few more maps and weapons, a couple of balance tweaks (buff autos PLEASE), patch the rare but intrusive bugs (randomly doing no dmg on high rounds), add in easter egg music, come on, it is a staple of the genre now, and finally, add a workshop, adding a workshop and letting players make mods for the game to the degree BO3 has, would very much expand this game, and actually put a little fear into Activision if the mod patcher the devs made actually works well.However, this is a indie publisher, and with that comes and indie budget, as of the time of this review, it is a little buggy, some minor issues with balancing, and weaker connections get booted all the time on online matches. Though the developers are rolling out patches for the minor issues constantly, this game at the sale price of $20 dollars is well worth it, the base price of $25 would be just barely pushing it in my opinion. This is by far my longest review and I felt this game deserves it. This game holds the potential to do what competition does. Innovate. With a little more work, this game will reignite the genre or in the very least, take the genre away from it's creators who clearly no longer understand it. If you have been looking for a new Round-Based Survival game similar to CoD Zombies, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good copy of CoD Zombie. It looks nice, feels decent. The atmosphere is honestly quite good, outside of the non-existent music. The diversity of weapons is satisfying, though not greatly balanced. Pricing on most things seem decent, outside of the revive token that are incredibly expensive and scale up.It definitely has its set of issues.Dying is an enormous setback, incredibly expensive, and your teammates can't revive you. So if you die, you're sent into a negative loop since you lose the money to get the upgrades. You kind of end up locked out of participating and slogging behind until you eventually die again since you can't kill the zombies fast enough. Hits don't have any impact, which means you don't really feel like you're dying when you are.There's definitely too many special enemies that are hp bags and not very fun. At least one of them is gonna get stuck behind a spawner and you'll have to go through the whole map to find it. And the escort quests are incredibly boring. To add onto this, I'd say there is a networking issue, most of the time playing multiplayer, even with high grade fiber, you have a lot of desync issues. In its current state I'd say it's somewhat worth it for a few hours of fun, but that's it. It definitely, definitely has the potential to become a really good game, but right now I'd say it's not there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual is the first time that i've truly felt like an outside developer from the call of duty series has captured what made the COD Zombies formula successful. Tension in it's kiting/training. Point Economy and Map Knowledge. It's downright one of the most underrated of it's genre. I've seen nobody talk about this game, i've seen nobody discuss how true it is to that original formula. How it brings a fun aesthetic and wears it's inspirations on it's sleeve. It's a modest game at that as well, the budget and price acknowledges that. If you're not a big fan of the original, i think you're not gonna be won over but ultimately this feels very specifically aimed for people who want that formula. If you are, then this is an absolute recommendation! The game keeps it simple. Your mission is to stop an evil ritual from spreading throughout the world by destroying cultic radio transmissions corrupting the same inhabitants of the island. There is lore but i best keep it there. It also takes a deeply unique take on it's horror, relying on celtic folklore. Welsh folklore at that. The game screams "made in wales", if you've ever been there. Seen it's sights, you'll know it's straight out of a fairytale or fantasy novel at points and it works perfectly for the horror cult tone the game is going for and also fits perfectly for a "Zombies" style game. The art style really really helps make this game look leagues ahead of others trying to ape the genre. It realised what it wanted to be but also wanted to stand on it's own feet aesthetically. This also is true mechanically.There are currently 4 maps in the game, which is pretty low as most games go but they are true "zombies" maps. The fun of the game is exploring them, piecing the main story easter egg together, solving puzzles that for the most part are fun to execute on! The map design isn't half bad either! The first one is a great opener but is easily the easiest of the lot, don't expect a soft ride if you're not a veteran. You will "not get" things but i encourage you to keep your eyes open! Each map as far as i can tell has it's own unique boss and even multiple specials which adds a lot of personality to the map! Gunplay is really solid, it's not exceptional but for an indie developer of this size. It's incredibly impressive that someone has nailed the gunplay so well. Most do not manage to get it right!! You've got double barreled shotguns booming, hunting rifles popping heads off, more exotic weaponry have a definite flair to them. I also have to talk about other game mechanics, at least compared to what it's really inspired by. Grenades in the COD Zombies of past have ranged from being fairly useless mid game and relatively solid loadout options. Sker makes it relevant at all points of the game, this extends to the rest of the kit you would usually expect. Your knive can be upgraded, to the point that it can consistently reach midgame or even later as long as you give it the attention it desires meaning you can always seal an easy close range kill and extra points to boot. Not just in damage either, there are many modifiers you can add to your knife AND your grenades. Your "Ultimate" ability isn't the flashiest but it can be built to do so much as the game goes on. Through an ingame build system (think a bit more like roguelikes). It's like someone took bits and pieces of what they liked of each game and fitted them in to see what worked well for the vision they had for their own version of that particular system. It means it's a lot more of a focused gameplay loop. Your arsenal is rarely invalidated at certain points and if you fall behind, it's because you made too many mistakes or you didnt exploit the point economy. Point Economy is sker is harsh, you use it to buy doors, perks, revives and self revives and weapons. It makes executing enemies with headshots and knives a bit more important than in the past, yes you can dispatch your enemies in easier and lazier ways but do that too much and you'll find yourself slugging along a lot slower than you might want with your upgrades as to which there are i think around 6 full weapon upgrades. All adding a new visual element to your gun model (think bioshock), a really nice touch that isn't just another animated camo fixed to your gun. Sker is pretty accessible, if you've never even heard of what a cod zombies is then you'll have a really good starting point to deal with everything. Plenty of instructions to get the information you need to complete the maps. Plenty to understand the mechanics. There are multiple difficulty options, if you're a vet then go at least to hard. I found it just too easy on normal. If you're new then give normal a shot. You can tweak difficulty inside the map itself if you want to give yourself an easier time with the exception of the nightmare difficulty as far as i can tell. Which boosts the enemies to around what people would expect from around round 50 if you've played cod zombies in speed. If you die in Sker, you'll lose a life and need to get another revive token if you want to not game over the next time you die. This costs quite a pretty penny, so above all else emphasis staying alive. Don't get stuck in a corner, always be moving. Never ever stop moving.Overall Sker Ritual is meant for a very specific type of player, the kind that time has forgotten. It invites newer players to try out the formula that was started all the way back with the Nazi Zombies mode back in COD: World at War. As we get the formula more and more diluted and the COD series forgets what made the originals so fun, i am glad that Wales Interactive took up the mantle to give it a shot, understood exactly what it wanted to be and executed with that understanding on all levels and didn't rest on it's laurels by giving it a unique take on the genre. I want to see more people do this, make people realise we never needed the AAA glitz and glamour to get back to that core fun. So do i recommend this game for people who have zero idea what "a call of duty zombies" is? If you're a fan of survival horror horde shooters with an emphasis on coop, i can see you having a good time with this and it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cheap for what it is! If you don't like wave survival period like the more distant relatives of Killing Floor then i can't recommend it for you, it is what it is. If you're a diehard easter egg destroying vet, you might blow through the content really quickly comparatively to other people but that's fine to me considering the incredibly modest price point, it's just a really great time if you're suited for it. It's an overwhelming recommendation for me, this game is a truly hidden gem!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot going on. If you're looking for a wave-based shooter similar to COD zombies this has the bare bones reminiscent of that: wall weapons, a mystery box, special "hound-esque" intermediary rounds, etc. But then there's the rest where the issues lie imo. Playing this game solo is too difficult. You must complete various tasks around the map to progress on in order to eventually face the respective level's boss... allthewhile getting shot at by skeletons firing electric arcs, fat dudes throwing fireballs, and energy beams fired by a Dollar Tree version of the Big Daddy from BioShock. These "special" units prove to be the most frustrating. There's also your typical various melee combatants smacking you from every direction with all this going on. Bottom line: If you have 3 other willing friends then I can see this game being more manageable, but it is not solo-friendly. It's also difficult to find players online, having found no matches in over five minutes. With more optimization and combatant-balancing it has potential. The dev's are passionate about making this game a success, reviewing feedback and making alterations, and that in itself is admirable. Worth the peep.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I want to say that this game is a better version of the zombies mode from CoD, even with all of the issues I am going to mention. It feels like there is a lot of heart here, but it is definitely not executed to the extent of a released game. The game recently hit 1.0, but seems like it would benefit from significant improvements to several systems. First off, the movement in a game like this needs to be smooth, feel good to the player, and above all its needs to be consistent. When a major part of your gameplay involves kiting zombies around you really need to make sure the player feels like their character is responding well to inputs, which this game currently doesn't do. Often you will be sprinting only to hit some unseen chunk of the scenery and abruptly be walking, some doors and corners have larger hitboxes than they appear to, and sometimes one zombie will block you into a hallway where there should clearly be enough room to escape. In addition, your character feels clunky and slow, which adds to the already present issues with movement to make moving around the large maps (which you will need to run all over to complete objectives) very tiresome. This is the main reason I am refunding this game. There are several secondary issues which could be addressed to polish this game, such as massive hit registration problems in multiplayer, matchmaking being extremely inconsistent, point acquisition and weapon damage scaling poorly with higher waves, and bugs (I encountered one wherein I upgraded a gun only to find it no longer even fired projectiles despite sounding like it was). In addition, respawning needs to be reworked in a major way. When you get to a high enough level in a multiplayer game and die, it is impossible to recover much of the time, largely due to the game taking one of your weapons upon death during a wave. This can be the gun you spent an insane amount of points to upgrade, and it is replaced with the measly starting pistol. This not only feels bad, it is unreasonable in a game which can kill you simply due to poor level geometry or bugs removing your ability to defend yourself. Lastly, this game can be brutal on a middle-of-the-road PC like I have. I wouldn't say my computer is bad by any means, I am able to run titles like Destiny 2 on upper level graphics with no issues despite literal hordes of enemies and projectiles on my screen. This may be an unfair contrast due to budgetary differences of the developers, but it still highlights the issue. In later waves, the density of zombies and effects leads to frame dropping, which combined with the problems with movement, gun function, and punishing respawns introduce a level of chaos that make this game very frustrating to play. I would say the most frustrating thing about this game is that I really want to keep playing. I love the lore, the care that obviously went into the game, and the sense of humor the developers put into the cosmetics, among many other things. Unfortunately, that brightness is tarnished by the unfortunate drawbacks I have mentioned to a degree that makes it feel like a slog to play. I really hope future patches fix some of the issues here, or I don't think I can re-download it in good faith.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played CoD zombies consistently since Black Ops 1 and has stuck with it through all of its entries (even the awful ones), this game is the real deal. Not only does it do justice to this type of game mode, it also does enough different and new that it is able to distinguish itself to the point that I feel bad having to mention zombies as a reference point for this review. The miracles system is amazing and offers a new layer of rogue-like gameplay on top of the usual formula of perks, weapon upgrades, and random weapons. The fact that the game guides you through parts of its quest is great, as I never saw the appeal of needing a guide or video open to complete an easter egg. The enemy design is a lot of fun and has significant diversity, breaking up the  same-ness that can come up with this type of game. I wasn't sure about the flow of the maps at first (and there is room for improvement) but as you play them more you start to see the logic behind their design. As for changes I would like to see: an armory system allowing us to customize our weapons (camos, attachments, etc.) and level them up over time. It's a major point of progression that feels absent. The game does have an issue with weapon and perk variety which will hopefully be solved in post-launch support. It's just not exciting to try for a random weapon when all weapon are available from the vendor and when there are only 8 regular weapons in the rotation on the first map. Additionally, many weapons feel unbalanced in terms of being too weak and some elements seem superfluous like the safeguard powerup that reduces the damage taken ( maybe this should give temporary health instead that's not attached to a timer, similar to armor). Tldr: Good game with a lot of potential. Hopefully they follow through on making it all it can be. Buy it if you like this sort of game design.

Bullet Sponges  After roughly round 20-25, the enemies become very bullet spongy, with even triple packed AKs barely doing much. 3. Performance  To be fair, my PC is probably just terrible, but the game starts to lag on later rounds and has issues keeping a smooth framerate due to the amount of enemies. 4. Small simple map  I think it would be nice to just have a small map that you can just survive on. The first map does it okay, but a map similar to that of the giant would be nice, very easy to navigate and easy to unlock upgrade areas.5. Workshop  I know this is a tall ask, but the workshop is the reason Black Ops 3 is still played and popular. Adding a workshop for custom maps would vastly increase the game's lifespan. Overall, Sker is a fun game that I would recommend, but it needs some extra bits to really make it great.

So it becomes super frustrating really quick.If there are some future patches that can balance out the upgrade cost vs power/damage levels that would be something to look forward to. Playing on easy through the 4 maps got me nearly all the main menu upgrades, I was only missing the 5th level so It wasn't like I was under leveled. And I wouldn't say I'm bad at shooters (i'm not amazing but not bad)... either way someone should be able to play through the game without being perfect especially on EASY. Last straw was playing with 2 people, starting on normal, both got down twice because of getting stuck between enemies because of the teleporting dudes, we switched to easy in the match and continued to struggle with killing, getting stuck in the terrain and running out of ammo. _childDocuments_.review: As it stands this game is a disaster, at least for me.It's easy to get caught up and stuck on uneven geometry. This has been an issue since launch and it seems that nothing has been done about it (in fact, I think it's gotten worse since the last time I attempted to play it).Enemies are already pretty tough to deal with at the lower levels (even on the easier difficulty that they've since rolled out since launch) but trying to get everything a single map requires you to do whilst also fighting endless, ever increasingly difficult waves of enemies, really drains the fun. Enemies take too many shots, do too much damage, and can lock you into a corner.Movement is slow and stiff and lots of things cause your running to come to a halt (meaning you have to activate the run again.) If there's some kind of stamina meter, it's not prominent enough for me to have noticed it and I don't recall seeing one whilst in observation mode while waiting to or attempting to revive.Speaking of, reviving is made unnecessarily difficult and punishing. Being killed really feels like an end to any progress and the cost progression of the life tokens is ridiculous. It starts at 5000 and doubles from there. Being able to revive, I get, is somewhat of a privilege in a horde game like this, but your allies should either have some way of reviving you beyond the revival chambers or, perhaps, you should still be able to purchase life tokens even in ghost form. As it stands, the moment you die, especially if in the midst of a key moment, everything feels like it becomes impossible.You get an achievement for visiting every place in a map. This would be fine if not for the fact that you basically have to visit every part of the map in order to complete all the various tasks that the level asks of you. And to be clear, these are not particularly fun tasks to complete. Most of it is stand in this designated area and then kill a bunch of enemies until the game feels satisfied. In the meantime, more and more waves of enemies are approaching, whilst you either take them out to clear paths or ignore them entirely to find the next goal point (which is likely on the complete opposite side of the map). If the game were linear (say like Left 4 Dead) it wouldn't be such an ordeal to complete so many different things but because it's an open sandbox, you are running in circles just desperately trying not to get lost.The difficulty itself, isn't inherently an issue. But the problems are so numerous that you truly are not fighting the enemies, or the challenge of the game, but rather you're up against the game itself. It's not even particularly horror inducing as the horror elements feel like they were just random, various ideas thrown at a dart board and then mish-mashed together in order to fill some kind of quota. "We must have zombies! And also insert the obligatory Resident Evil reference to Mr. X! Oh, also throw in banshees! Their screaming definitely won't get annoying as it endlessly fills the players ears! Also they should teleport! Oh, put in invisible enemies as well! Nothing screams horror like barely visible variants of only one kind of enemy!"The game isn't scary or challenging; it's just poorly made.

_childDocuments_.review: Your player character will get caught on random pebbles on the ground and be unable to move, and some rooms are super small with props everywhere, so enemies will swarm you there, and between their bodies and the props all around, it becomes impossible to move. Most of my deaths are just getting stuck in between enemies and props in small corridors while trying to complete an objective. Speaking of objectives, they're all the same. I played 3 of the 4 available maps so far, and it's pretty much just: Kill enemies -> Buy door -> Kill enemies -> Stand in area and wait for progress bar to load -> Kill enemies -> Buy door -> Repeat. There are some puzzles, but since there's so much time pressure and you're constantly only 2 feet from a new enemy, there's no way for the puzzles to be brain teasers, most of them are just "point the thing in the right direction" or "Memorise this code and put it in the machine"Certain objectives are timed, and if you die and revive yourself, your progress is reset, but your timer doesn't, so you end up just having to wait 30 seconds for the timer to reset and then do the objective all over again. Some objectives will have you running across the entire map searching for 4 randomly placed items to pick up/destroy, and most of the time there are no objective markers on them, so you'll likely just spend 30 mins wandering around looking for them and by the time you do their quest, so much time has passed that the enemies are now too strong to keep up with.Gunplay isn't bad, but most guns are pretty useless and you'll only be using a select few. You can upgrade the guns with money as the game goes on, but upgrading costs a ton, I usually only upgrade 3 times per game, and by around wave 25 and above, a level 3 gun does not do ♥♥♥♥. Basic enemies take a whole mag to the head before dying. But upgrading is too steep. You can keep up by using other abilities, but when the guns are the most fun part, not being able to use them sucks.As you go through a run, you'll get to upgrade yourself with "Miracles" which are basically just passive buffs. There's a couple that are good and then the rest are just plain trash. Most are just stuff like "Do 4% more damage" not even joking. Of course, you can upgrade these buffs and they get stronger, but most of the time going for more nuanced abilities like poison, stun or auto aim just end up biting you in the ass later, so the only real strategy is just getting the generic explosion around you ability everytime.Bosses are tedious at best, and brain numbing at worst. They're just bullet sponges with very easy to dodge attacks. Most of the time, the only real danger is the swarms of enemy spawning around them.Story exists, but I couldn't care less. cosmetics looks pretty basic and mid.Overall, the game is just tedious and gets old really quickly. It was fun for the first 5-6 hours, but it's definitely not worth it's price point for me. I'd say complete the first level of the demo three times, and you'll have basically experienced everything in this game

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual is, literally, it's own take on COD Zombies and I genuinely feel they've taken the best of the mechanics from each respective COD Zombies game, the Environments are very interesting to me, I like the maps and the direction they've taken with it - especially with the game being tied to an Indie game which I have no experience in but this makes me want to play that indie title to understand more of the story at large.My friend group and me have played COD Zombies since WAW and one of my friends who I bought a copy of the game for enjoys the game a lot. He feels there is some collision problems at certain spots of the map, expresses he's "Gotten Stuck" hugging corners on walls before the enemy even grabs him, but I've had little amounts of that problem. Perhaps there are some collision maps on some of the levels that are not directly to the physical wall but beyond it with the mapping?The only thing I personally have a bit of a gripe for is the weapon models...It takes place in... Estimate 1890 - 1915, but there IS an AK model that looks more like a modern AK then, say, the weapon it is named after, that being the Federov Avtomat. I am not sure if this is a licensing issue, copyright, or otherwise.Alongside an AK 12-esque weapon that looks a little *Too* modern for the setting, at least from what I've seen of it, there is also an H and K MP5 style firearm, which I feel would have been a cut in for an MP 40 or, more close to date, an MP 18I have found very little things that actually bother me with Sker Ritual regarding the gameplay - the puzzles are confusing, especially the first match I played where a player that knew what they were doing decided not to do any of the puzzle and watch me and another newbie bonk heads together - I eventually figured it out the pattern for (Draining blood) and got through that specific puzzle to continue the map along, but we were at wave 25 by then. It's best to kite zombies around to do the objectivesbut I also feel what I'm bringing up as my *only* gripe regarding weapons is nowhere near a priority for the team to worry about - especially when some weapons only intend to have that weapon as a fill in to represent a weapon *group* for the sake of NOT making endless models of guns that all functionally do the same thing and take up weapon spots for, say, Lucky (Which is the mystery box).(Such as the Hunting Rifle is a stand-in for all the bolt action rifles anyone can imagine, and has twenty two rounds in the magazine over having, say, four rifles like the Mosin, Enfield, Mauser and Springfield with historical clip sizes and damage rates. The one hunting rifle does the same as all four to begin with and all four would arguably operate the same way between one another regardless of magazine size)I feel a GREAT idea, if the concept of changing weapons models could be a thought for the dev team later down the line, could maybe be to create interchangeable weapon models. Changing the hunting rifle to whatever other weapon the team would want to add to the game and letting the players decide what they'd like to have for said weapons appearance. It's just a weapon model swap like a customization item for the player.The game, for my rig, runs smoothly - I've taken to using a revolver and melee build! (I do feel that the quick melee should be allowed an upgrade, like with how Black Ops Two let the players have a Bowie Knife. I'd LOVE to see a quick melee upgrade that is a Welsh Blade and cosmetic items that could be inspired from WW1, such as gas masks and other such things if they aren't already present and I haven't seen them.As for the direct melee weapons like the Pioneer axe, I feel they feel lack-luster and believe, maybe, they could have a combo of some sort when they are upgraded to higher tiers - a tier two axe you can swing twice in succession, for example.This is a solid title for the gameplay the team was envisioning. The Levels and story as I've played so far are interesting and I'm confident there are tie ins to the horror game it is based from. The gameplay is fun and scales up in difficulty considerably between waves 20~ - 30. I'd have no problem recommending the game as it is, especially if you have a friend group that likes to play COD Zombies or played WAW Zombies

_childDocuments_.review: The best in the genre of round based fps survival horror despite not "inventing it". It feels well balanced. At first, Normal difficulty feels too easy, but it climbs and ramps up quickly in pace and intensity. I do wish there were more guns available rather than being left to utilizing Lucky to give you random guns, most of which seemed mediocre. I love the aesthetics and atmosphere as well. If you're a fan of COD Zombies this is a must play for you!! I have not come across any bugs or glitches yet, and it runs beautifully on my PC. I love that there's cross-play. I do think that you should be given more XP, or lower XP needed to level up. I feel like I really progressed in the game, but just missed the mark to level up which didn't feel very rewarding. This game is better with teammates, as Normal mode gets a bit more chaotic than expected. I would recommend Easy mode for solo play. The game really pushes on using strategy in a positive way. I know it may be a smaller developer but I would have liked to see playable characters be different from each other with personality, rather than just a customized character. I really hope this game gets the love and attention it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like CoD Zombies meets KillingFloor 2 meets Left 4 Dead 2.  Interesting Story line, very cool monster design, smooth gun play, very well designed maps.  My only complaint is that since it's an "always online" game and not running locally or on a local dedicated server (and I don't see why it couldn't), there can be lag that kills the flow.  Sometimes your melee strikes wont register if the enemy is too close and once in a while, gunshots don't register which can REALLY be a problem.Now, had I know this next part, I would have passed on this game.  There is NO dedicated server or local multiplayer support.  The devs (as of the time I'm writting this) have no plans for it either.  That means, when they inevitably shutdown the servers, you're stuck on single player (cause that's offline) and that's it.  The game is basically bricked when they turn off their servers.  God Forbid a dev gives the players the tools or capability to enhance the game's longevity past when the devs run out of money and have to shutdown the game.  Games as a live service are CANCER.  They are killing the industry.  TF2 still has a player base.  CAUSE THE COMMUNITY KEEPS IT ALIVE.  If we can't host our own servers, there is no community.  There is only the devs and it dies with them so I wouldn't sink too much money into this game.  Get it on sale for at least 50% off and don't buy skins.  Not until we get dedicated, private run servers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first in depth review, and I am happy to write this.I am really enjoying this game and see why it is being called the “COD ZOMBIES KILLER” by many who enjoyed the zombies mode.I have played CoD zombies since WaW and I really enjoy Sker for it’s detail and feels like the developers of Sker are fellow players trying to provide what the zombies community wants in a round based fps.I experienced a few bugs that can be avoided or patched later, one being that at random I was stuck in place and had to reset my game. A little disappointing because I was at round 20 BUT it still saved my progress and rewards so it wasn’t all for nothing. COD DOES NOT DO THIS IN MY EXPERIENCES.The game also provides tutorials, keeps track of stats, has easter eggs on every map and different difficulties, can upgrade your perks so they are more effective in matches (like juggernog for example can be upgraded from 20% boost to 100% boost after the last upgrade).The upgrades are permanent and make it easier for you to play harder difficulties.Completing easter eggs reward you with cosmetics so there are permanent rewards for doing them.The game comes with a few maps to play and they are big with lots of detail!My only complaints so far are:- There is no split screen yet- There is no crossplay yet for PS5 to join PC/XBOX players and vice versa- There is no in game friends list yet- No weapon customization yet- Paid dlc is cosmetics only (PLEASE MAKE MORE MAPS)These may be patched in the future at some time, and I hope that the developers do because I am happy to support this game, as they clearly care about making a fun and quality game.I highly recommend this game to those who are looking for something like CoD zombies but want something different than the mainstream.I play this on my 512gb LCD STEAM DECK, and it works great!Highly recommend, even not on sale because it is THAT good!

_childDocuments_.review: It is just like a lower tier cod zombies. There are about a dozen guns with some being map specific but they can be acquired through a dog/mystery box named lucky. Even ranked up weapons can spawn using him so it can be worth it.Each map has a story that progresses when you follow the objectives and ends with a boss fight. It is weird but the boss is an "easter egg" and the boss after the secret objectives is the "hardcore easter egg". The match only ends when the host uses the exit portal or everyone gets downed. Everyone has 1 extra life that can be used to res someone else or res them-self at a machine while in "ghost mode". Lives are not used up if you can make it to the body and res them before it disappears. More lives can be purchased by using a machine but it is not available on the hardest difficulty. Each match boils down to opening up areas until the weapon you want is available, finding the weapon upgrade machine, choosing to do the story or not, opening the rest of the map and buying the perks, upgrading your weapon, earning the "mystic power" perks every couple rounds, and lastly either survive as long as you can or leave after beating the boss.Solo play and offline mode is available and it offers difficulty choices that make it easy to just do the story. Multiplayer for 4 people is also here, which makes the harder difficulties easier. My only cons so far is the multiplayer connectivity in matchmaking isn't very good. If the host leaves or disconnects the game ends and it gives you the bare minimum exp.I recommend this game and would like to see where else it can go.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be teling you about the single-player Sker Ritual experience.As a "Zombies" mode game, Sker Ritual is tons of fun for playing both solo or with friends (I assume, as I could convince my friends to play with me ;-;). The guns feel great, the perks are great, there's a progression system, the levels are mostly extremely solid (did not care for the hotel as I got trapped multiple times in corners).The primary issues I have with the game come from its UI and level progression. My longest runs all ended up being roughly 90 minutes long, whether I died or won in the end. This is because a good portion of those 90 minutes is spent running around trying to complete objectives that the game does not give you ALL the information for. In one mission, I had to acquire a lamp and use it to find symbols for a code. The lamp takes a weapon slot and isn't itself a weapon. It seems that in these cases, the game may allow you to have 3 items: A primary, a secondary and an objective gun/item. But that was not made clear in the UI. There's no symbol for the weapon slots you may have.Worse of all is the game gives you a marker, which you follow, and it leads you to where the code has to placed. However, the game doesn't tell you where to look for the code info with the lantern. There's no area of search radius on a map, and the objective only leads you to the puzzle you're solving.  There are target objectives ("shoot these targets"), but no indicator of where they are, so you run around the entire map blindly for 10 minutes.  This ends up making the maps feel long and repetitive because you're looking for something that some players will find in 10 seconds and others will take 15 minutes, all while under attack by enemies.I have a blast with this game and thoroughly enjoy it. I hope steps are taken to smooth out some of that map search time so you feel like you're progressing steadily. Perhaps an indicator can come up after a certain amount of time or waves has been cleared since the objective was placed. It's clear that the objectives want players to work together to accomplish tasks, splitting up to look for clues or have a dedicated "lamp person" to explore, but as a solo experience, it just makes the runs a slog that I feel could be cut down to a full 30-60 minutes of just solid gunplay.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a $25 indie game that strives to be Call of Duty Zombies as a standalone experience, taking inspiration from Call of Duty: WW2 and Call of Duty: Cold War primarily, with Bioshock vibes intertwined.For the price point, it's hard to beat, especially with the prices of the actual games. Unfortunately, although it is early access and only just released, the gameplay is very lacking and clunky. I think this will change with time, but the perk upgrades are extremely boring numerical bonuses, unlike Cold War and WW2. Even Bioshock had a better upgrade system than this.I'm also not a huge fan of just how much is going on in each map. _childDocuments_.review: While the core loop is fun, it gets old and cheap really quick.Enemy health scales with waves.  And you're going to be dealing with a *LOT* of waves.  You CAN upgrade your weapons, but the cost scales (which makes sense), as does buying ammo and life refills.  Unfortunately, towards higher level waves, you barely do any damage unless you have been able to upgrade your weapons.  It feels like a major slog, and you don't really feel like you're growing in power as you play the game.  The perks are nice, but since the enemy health starts to scale wildly, there will come a point where they don't feel that powerful.  30 ticks of poison is nice on a shot when a basic enemy has 100 health.  It's pointless on an enemy with 2,000+ health.  I do want to give the game a chance, but my refund window is closing.  While there is a passive upgrade system, I just don't  think it will be enough to change my opinion of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, if Treyarch won't do it, someone will.This game captures a lot of what I loved about COD Zombies pre Cold War, and I think it's totally worth the price. _childDocuments_.review: INTENSE IN DEPTH Review (Making sure you get the moneys worth and hoping creators see this)7/10 rn, but potential is 9.5/10If you like Cod Zombies, this one is a $15 buy. It has a lot of potential and for what it is now, it is very good. But I do have a lot of issues with it, but those issues can be fixed pretty easily. I played only one match and it lasted 2.6 hours. I also already did every puzzle, tested every gun when fully upgraded, got every perk, and beat the final boss. I will we writing what I like about it, the problems, and what glitches I already encountered. Note that there is only 1 map rn out of 4, so assume everything about this review, is about the first map. I will be giving my thoughts on what could fix this game for the better. I played solo as wellWhat I liked:1)First I noticed that was kinda rad, was that the fact it was more of a thriller/horror game. I got jumpscared by so many zombies that I did not expect to be behind me, to my right or any random direction. They did a great jump making it so you have to constantly be aware of your surroundings. You would think you could listen to their groans or footsteps, but most the time they quietly sneak up on you and then start groaning and yelling2)The map provides thriller/horror stress as some puzzle spots like the small wheat field and fog goat land (though I think your visibility should be shorten more in the fog).3)The point system is based on kills rather than hot many shots you put in. This makes it kinda nice so you can't abuse point grinding, making it a little harder4)The gun upgrade machine costs more each upgrade5)The puzzles were actually very cool and It took me a couple minutes to figure 2 out, but they are easy enough for you to figure out on your own6)The areas around the map can actually provide you with a lot of stress when figuring out puzzles (unless your the type to leave one alive and train constantly)7)There are abilities, but it's not like they are something you can excessively abuse. For instance, the main ability thats just does an AoE around you, usually will kill everything, but it takes a considerable amount of recharge. Same with the grenades, but you can throw only 1 every 30 seconds while the main is based off how much damage8)There's a mechanic in the game called "Miracles". These are simple upgrade point to passively upgrade your guy. When opening up the upgrades too, it acts like a rouge-like and gives you 3 random choices. These Miracles can also upgrade if you see them in the shop again, and I believe that can upgrade 2 more times after the first time you get it9)The hp bar system was something that concerned me at first, but it turned out to be a really really important factor. Unlike CoD, these zombies REALLY increase their hp over time. This can definitely make the game harder at times10)A lot of close quartered areas so make it more fun and harder, but of course each puzzle area has sorta a massive space so you can run and try to figure out the puzzle (A little too massive for each area I think, especially the fog goat area)11)The zombies are just fast enough always to be a distraction so you have the option of course to keep just 1 and try to figure out the puzzle OR kill it and notice that the start of each round has a 15 second break for you to do literally whatever12)Oh forgot to mention it's a huge map and the boss zombie is basically George Romero (without the enrage though) from Call of the Dead in Black Ops 113)There are ammo stations to buy ammo around the map, but I didn't see a need for it since I used the shotgun and it never runs out14)Can buy your teammate in mid round. Costs more each time15)Battle Pass FREE.Problems:1)Both the double barrel and regular shotgun are the only things viable after round 20. Reason being that every other gun just doesn't clear the zombies fast enough. The shotguns one tap till like round 39.2)Shotguns never run out of ammo period. They will ALWAYS have like 100+ shells by the time you get another max ammo3)Zombies were terrible at attacking. I literally was just walking pass them and their animation to hit was way too slow. They miss every time. 4)The enemy with the laser never hits. Left one alive to see how accurate it was and the prediction of it knowing where to shoot it pretty bad.5)Trains in this game is beyond easy in big spaces6)The actual final boss felt way to easy. It was just him with a single minion zombie coming out like every minute, I also think that may have been a glitch, since they were coming from the entrance where I ran from zombies at the start of round 407)You can buy literally weapon from weapon shops around the map, one is in the STARTING ROOM. Like are you kidding me there, I can just buy the most OP weapon at the start and just fly through without difficulty. That ruins the fun a lot. 8)The dog (mystery box) only gives the weapons from the weapon shop (which lets me assume there will be more guns, but there is ZERO point of using it rn. (I used it 9 times just getting weapon shop items so I confirmed it for sure)9)Boss zombie is ZERO threat. Even when you fight him again as the "final boss" where they add more mechanics to him. I never got hit once. Don't know if can one tap you or something. 10)Is there supposed to be a story at some point or is it just do objectives till you win? I legit don't know since there was never really anything being explained, just a checklist of what to do11)Getting the lantern puzzle made me think I broke it. I grabbed the lantern and immediately switch to my shotgun. NOWHERE on the UI did it say it equipped to the "3rd" weapon slot. I only figured out I had it since I started buying guns and it randomly switched my 2nd weapon slot and 3rd weapon slot. The switch was probably a glitch, but that glitched saved me from restarting12)Sometimes the checklist objectives were very vague. The Lantern one really screwed with me since when I found each symbol, and ordering them from one start of the area to the other didn't solve the puzzle. In the end I had to guess what order they went in. Same with the very last one, just says to kill Abraham after destroying the communications room. I sat there killing hordes for like 10 minutes waiting for the boss to spawn in that room (it was totally big enough to be a boss room). It wasn't until I looked up someones quick gameplay online to see that they left the room to find a door was now open. So please put in a way point right after destroying communications13)Communications room realizing it now is a huge waste of space/time. You run in, destroy 4 things then leave for the final bossGlitches:1)Bought a Dog gun and it transferred my current guns rank to the gun I just bought. I tested it 2 more times and on the 2nd one I lost the upgrade so I have zero idea if the it was supposed to transfer the upgrade or not. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: It has been really great to see this game develop onto a full product since it's early access stage, near 3 years in development and the result is well worth the wait. With new features of crossplay between XBOX and Steam, soon on PlayStation. New weapons too! Also secret easter eggs to do which unlocks a super weapon. Game also has free a battle pass with plenty of unlocks, which don't cost any extra money. Excited to see what's to come from Wales Interactive and happy to support them!Set in the 20th century and based on old Welsh folklore, "Sker Ritual" features terrifying demonic creatures and a wide range of upgradable weapons to send these creatures back to where they came from. Additionally, players have the opportunity to team up with three strangers (or friends) to vanquish the evil that plagues Sker. Each map offers different enemy types to battle, unique "wonder-weapons" specific to each map, and bosses from the Maid of Sker world. The game employs various mechanics to keep the gameplay fresh and distinguish itself from CoD:Zombies, such as the Miracle Points system, which adds a roguelike element to the game giving you different special abilities or buffs to choose from.The gameplay loop is highly entertaining, allowing players to either test their luck and see how far they can progress through higher waves or complete objectives to reach the final boss of each level. Personally, what truly sets this game apart and keeps me coming back for more is its meticulously designed setting, artistic choices, music, and well-crafted enemies.For those seeking a refreshing wave shooter experience, "Sker Ritual" comes highly recommended. See you soon on Sker Island, stranger!

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really need to add a "somewhat recommend" button.This game has some great potential, it just needs a little bit more time spent on it to iron out some kinks. Such as:To me, a lot of the weapons all sound the same. Some of the sound effects, such as the red vase you need to collect for the second mission just sound like a guy ripping a bong - seriously! Go listen for yourself. And at times, the ambience seems a bit dull. Glass shattering when you throw a bottle/grenade doesn't really have much of an impact, yet, it can do quite a bit of damage. While I've enjoyed the game as a whole, like the way they've used inspiration from Call of Duty: Cold War, they need to just change a few things that would make it a bit more immersive. For example, have some sort of visual/audible effect when interaction with the dog for a random weapon, it's just bland. The animation for crouching screams poor effort. Have some pride in your work, not just snapping the capsule half height to a set value. ADD MORE WEAPONS! Maybe I'm missing something, but I've only found a pump shotgun, a double-barrel, 2 maybe 3 pistols, a bolt action, an M14 and a couple of mission weapons. That's it. In some areas, the game lacks effort, but in others it exceeds expectations and is actually fun. The devs are fairly active, so I have no doubt that they'll be making improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of CoD Zombies, but hate having to follow video guides for the easter eggs, then I highly recommend you check this game out. It plays similarly, with some slight changes:- 5 difficulty settings so you can tune the challenge to your liking- Each map has a quest (like an Easter egg), although the objectives are given to you via the UI- Miracle system letting you select different powers for each of your equipment;your gun (ex: bullets slow enemies, or deal more crit damage, or fire faster), melee, grenade, healing elixir, and ultimate ability (ex: invincible for X seconds, AOE damage around you, AOE stun, etc)The game currently has 4 well put together maps and 4 free battle passes, definitely worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Just wanted to start this review by saying this game is amazing and super fun all around, but I would like to offer some feedback on some small issues I found in multiplayer while playing with my friends, as well as three things to improve the game.Starting with the issues on the maps, we had problems with...1. Sewers of the Dead: Using the Plague Wonder Weapon would not open doors in multiplayer. Additionally, some doors would have to be bought again by some of the other players, even after already being bought by one of them.2. Deadly Lover's Fortress:  we found a bug with the siren enemies where they take your guns and don't give them back, which breaks the player character coding and doesn't let them use items or interact with anything. Dying doesn't revert the glitch. We found this in multiplayer as well. next is some improvements to some wonder weapons as well as an addition to the game i and my friends would love to see.1.  An improvement to the Plague Wonder Weapon could be to add a lingering effect that lasts for about 2-5 seconds for additional damage. Whether it's on contact or ground damage would be up to you, the devs.2. Deadly Lover's Fortress: Upon getting the Sword Wonder Weapon from the box after first unlocking it, the weapon can be upgraded. But when transforming the sword to the new, more powerful version, the upgrade does not transfer to the newly acquired sword. Thus, you are forced to re-upgrade using points all over again, and it's very tedious, making the sword not feel worth it due to this small feature of the upgrade not transferring. would be nice to see the upgrade transfer to the new sword...3. would love to see an enemy/zombie counter that can be toggled on and off in the interface settings so that you know how many enemies are left during the rounds if this inst to hard to add.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is just incredible. It's everything I've wanted out of a COD Zombies style wave-based shooter. It has perks available at stations around each map, mystery weapons, upgrading guns, but it also adds a miracle system of passive perks that you can build each run in a rouge-like style that work in synergy with each other; as well as the ability to upgrade your guns multiple times, not just once. But that only begins to brush the surface of the overall progression system that you have for completing each map- which yes, you can complete because it has actual quests with puzzles that you do during the game. 4 Maps currently, all with unique quests that end in a boss fight (but does it really end the first time you kill the boss?)I think this game is fantastic, and a few of my friends and I were fully convinced to buy the game just after the first few rounds of playing the demo. You can certainly rest assured with your purchase of Sker Ritual, I cannot sing its praises enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Sker: Ritual combines intense zombie survival with solid shooting mechanics, making it a must-try for fans of Call of Duty Zombies. Here’s what you need to know:Gameplay Mechanics:Sker: Ritual offers an intense round-based zombie survival experience.Face relentless waves of vicious horrors, upgrade steampunk weapons, and collect Celtic God powers.High-octane objectives keep you engaged as you battle the Quiet Ones.Recent Updates:A major patch (v.0.5.8) has significantly improved the game:UI Animations: The user interface now feels smoother and more responsive.Audio Enhancement: Post-game summaries now include audio cues.Playerbase Surge: The game has seen a substantial increase in players, making it far from a dead game.In summary, Sker: Ritual is back in action, and the recent updates have breathed new life into this zombie-infested world. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The ONLY thing holding this game back is the smol player base, besides that the game is an 8/10 and just lacks some polish, the adjective not the people.The gunplay is fantastic, there is a somewhat limited gunpool but you can upgrade (pack a punch) each weapon 3 times. You can stumble zombies by running into them, so rarely do you get trapped in a corner and get outright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths. The game is far more intense than zombies though, due to it having killing floor like mobs where each one is somewhat unique and can either teleport, be invisible, explode (hurting other mobs or you), or have long range attacks. The (from what I have been told) cod WW2 zombies like progression has upgrades for: your heal bottle. your grenade, your knife, and your 'ultimate". Each of these function like MOBA hero's abilities where they have a cool down, but with the miracle system, you get to choose a random active/passive to affect these abilities that really changes gunplay on each subsequent playthrough. Theres 4 maps and 1 easter eggs per map and most importantly they're ALL WAY-POINTED (you know, the most annoying part of cod zombies is having to look up tutorials?) They're also a blast to do.You can tell the game was made my a small team due to its lack of polish, but I'm sure now that the core of the game is finished, they'll polish this into a shiny diamond. Can't wait for this game to blow up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not horrible, but after playing it with my friend who I have played 1000s of hours of COD zombies with, this game just feels a lot like a chore instead of an actual game. I do not think this game feels good anywhere in terms of development and is at worst irritating. Pros:-Decent UI, its nothing too much for the eyes and keeps everything simple.-enemy variety, has something beyond the normal zombie and tries to diversify.-Self-revive tokens are nice, can definitely be useful as to not end up losing to a screw up.Cons:-The guns feel terrible for the most part, ESPECIALLY on CO-OP, hit-reg and damage wise later on.-Most of the $2000 guns you get via Easter Egg steps feel weak and somewhat pointless-Lots of stuff is re-used, same Easter Egg mechanics, same map feel, and even the same bosses / their skeletons (Rat King / Abomination).-Pack a Punch (or whatever this game calls it) is terrible, barely upgrades guns at all, you are better off using the dog (box) as it can quad pack guns for $900 vs. $20,000+-The easter eggs is for me like 70% of the reason for playing, and they aren't very good. I could never see myself playing the maps as a basic "survival".-The sound design is all over the place, half the time the enemies are so loud you want them to shut up and stop stomping, and then the other half you can't even hear yourself getting stabbed or electrocuted during bosses.-Boss spawns on the maps are indifferent at best, just bullet sponges that annoy you and don't really do much.TLDR; I tried to be very positive towards this game when i was trying it out myself, but wow I literally cannot think of anything this game improves on with regards to the COD zombies formula, I wouldn't even put these maps above World at War maps and those I don't have the best memory of playing. I cheer these devs on in trying their own but it honestly comes off as a extremely sub-par re-invention of COD zombies.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 0/5*To be honest, I don't care about the story. If gameplay was good, I'd take notice, but no.Gameplay: 0/51) The Quiet Ones have bad animation (they attack faster than their slow animation).2) Half-Price becomes mandatory at later rounds, point gain is same for harder rounds.3) Maps are too dark, even if the map has proper lighting or not (like I get that it's part of the story/mood of the game, but I'd rather see where I am going).4) Low walls don't let damage through (yes I tried shooting over hand rails and no damage) or don't let you jump over (I also tried, you might as well disable jumping altogether).5) Maps are too tight quartered, not spacious enough to get through The Quiet Ones.6) The Quiet Ones have a huge collision box, but small and inconsistent hit box, you get easily mobbed, but you can't get out quickly enough.7) Ultimate skill charging is slow, it's fine for earlier levels, but later levels no.8) Grenades and skills don't do squat even on higher rarities.9) Levelling outside the game is a chore, so much hard work for so little reward.Sound: 1/5*1) Weapon and throwable sounds have a delay (like the kind of delay that if you play a soundless video and an audio clip in succession). The feeling is that the game is just merely playing the sound clip.2) Annoying voice chatter from NPCs in the game, so unnecessary, except for just one voice line, when aiming for the hidden easter egg.NOTE: I disabled the music, so unnecessary for me in this regard.Online: 1/51) At least it lets you connect online, but at higher rounds, you get unexplainable lag. If this game P2P, then (probably) the netcode is bad. If this is dedicated, then the servers are bad.2) No reconnection when you get kicked from the party gameTotal Average Score: 0.5/5There's no way, even a smidge, that I can give this as a recommendation. CoD Zombies Killer? Dream on. CoD Zombies (the MWIII open-world one) may be bad, but it's not as worse as this.

Comes with all the QoL changes that Cold War brought, and adds its own little intricacies to set it apart.If you like CoD's round-based zombies and you just want more of it, this game will provide in grand fashion.

_childDocuments_.review: I could go in-depth about what I think is good and bad about this game, but I want to keep things simple and say that Sker Ritual feels like the kind of game we need more of, and that's passion projects. The easy comparison to make here is that it's similar to CoD Zombies and that's clearly the inspiration for this. I think Sker Ritual really captures the spirit of CoD Zombies while trying to differentiate itself and give it's own take on the formula. For a small indie developer I think it's really cool how well they've captured that same feeling as CoD's Zombies mode and they've managed to keep from feeling like a copycat. The best way I can describe Sker Ritual is that it feels like someone made a passion project inspired by CoD Zombies. It feels familiar and has that arcadey fun that's easy to pick up and play, but it's not trying to be or replace CoD Zombies. I think the only thing I can really criticize the game on is that the $25 price tag feels a bit steep. I grabbed this on sale and think I got it for like $10, and am happy having paid that, but I know I'd have a hard time trying to get some friends on a $25 indie game. I do think they need a bit more polish to lift the game up and make it worthy of that price tag, particularly with animations. Hopefully we'll see the player count grow in the future, the developers are definitely trying their best to make this a smooth, fun experience for everyone What's really impressed me about this game though is that the developers have continued to work on the game and have continued to fix, update, and add things to it at a steady pace, for free! I recently learned that this game was made by just 5 developers so the rough spots make sense and I think they're definitely something that can be smoothed out in the future if they're able to continue working on this; it's admirable how much work they've already been putting into the game post release with free updates. If any of them happen to see this review I'd actually love to know if this was a planned sequel or started as someone's passion project!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 (I only played Solo)Lots of tedious missions if you want to do the story. Each map I tried was a "collect these 4 things" where i either had to escort a bunch or hold a spot for a time period. It heavily encourages speedrunning the missions in the early waves since they go against the flow of training hordes. You can just leave one zombie alive, but that only increases the tedium of some of the escort missions. These are the types of missions that were also heavily criticized in later COD zombie games. It just got irritating by the third map and i lost interest in it. The worst part is, to even continue past some of the early stages of the map you are required to do it.The gameplay is ok, feels almost like Cod World at War since the graphics and clunkiness almost makes it feel like im playing a PS3 game. The hit reg for the knife is really bad, but most of the guns felt ok. The gun options to choose from were extremely standard and so were the perks. You got juggarnaut, mule kick, speed cola, and double tap plus something similar to quick revive. Not a really good or a bad thing, you could even say its being more faithful to the earlier CODs with this simplified perk system. The rougelike build system was there, but it didn't really change my experience too much between games and how I played.  The maps are also a sprawled out spiders nest of corridors, they were fine but nothing interesting thematically. I think my biggest issue right now with the game is that it pretty much is the same thing as the older Cod zombies plus extremely generic predictable additions that don't actually add much to the experience. Its ok for scratching an itch, but it doesn't bring much more with it and I wouldn't even say its better than just playing Cod zombie.If there is one thing going for this game is that its not created by activision, so it has potential for its future. Im curious to see where it goes, so ill give it a hesitant thumbs up for now.Wishlist:- magic box (dog)  should show the animation of the guns spinning like a slot machine. Not only is it more enjoyable, ill also get to see what potential options there are- gun buy points should be more spread out. It sucks that like 3 or 4 guns are grouped next to eachother in a cart in 1 or 2 areas rather than having them spread out across all areas- would appreciate some cosmetic differences in the base zombie per map. I was disappointed going to the doll map and finding out that it was still just the same zombies- dismemberment and maybe even crawlers- limited number of self revive in solo, having unlimited makes later rounds too easy- point scaling in later rounds, the number of points for higher tier guns becomes extremely grindy and the pay off once you do pick up a tier 3 gun isn't that substantial. A tier 4 gun is about 49500 in hard mode and a zombie kill gives about 90-100 points regardless of wave. Thats 495 zombies I have to kill, and these zombies are super spongey late game. They take 20 headshots with a tier 3 gun. And that doesn't even factor in the cost of buying ammo in between. Its unreasonable the cost vs how much you getBugs- sometimes the end game screen wont load so i have to quit the game and lose all the rewards I got- fire dot damage is considered an enemy assist and does not count towards your kill count. At waves 30+, most of your kills will be from dot so it practically takes away half your kills from the stats

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like you have to go out of your way to go down in this. The zombies are far to slow, deal way to little damage, and generally pretty ignorable. The special ones don't make it any better either, most of them miss their attacks anyways. The guns themselves aren't terrible, but they lack a certain "oompfh", could definitely use some sound and visual polish.The grenade is like a party streamer grenade, it just shoots out a bunch of silly string, it's kind of pathetic visually.This game feels like the dev desperately wanted to make a COD Zombies competitor, but likes KF way to much.Way to much player HP + On the go heal? The reason KF's difficulty works is because they throw SO much at you and their AI is smart, they grab you, go around you, cut you off, aim ahead of you to catch you. KF's difficulty is so precisely made that it makes it work despite how much HP and healing they give you access to.This games zombies are like always round 1 COD zombies that take 10 hits to down you, they don't slow you when they hit you in any capacity, and you can literally rub your skull against their belly and not get attacked cause their so slow.The map I played on felt "ok". I mostly did a quick run to just get a feel for the games mechanics, the map is inoffensive I suppose.The miracles mechanic is interesting, I like the idea its going for, although it feels a bit flat. I did poison in my run, and it's really just "my guns deal DOT damage, my grenade does DOT damage, my knife does DOT damage.", nothing else. I don't imagine the other elements are that much different, probably also just extra dot damage with no real gameplay mechanics. Could definitely use some fleshing out.I think the dev's here have passion, and I think they could make a decent game, but for goodness sake they need to make a choice on what they want their game to be, KF or COD Zombies. You can try combining them, but that's gunna require so much elbow grease that you'd be shooting yourself in the foot and hand. I wanna see this game make waves and achieve something, but as it stands right now, it feels like KF on easy mode with worse AI. Fix the difficulty before anything, please. The guns are "fine", the maps are "fine", the visuals are "fine", the mechanics are "fine". The difficulty isn't. (OH YEAH, AUTOMATIC WEAPONS ARE USELESS. NO POINT BUILD-UP ON HIT, ONLY ON KILL. JUST USE SHOT GUNS.)Make zombies faster -> let zombies grab/slow the player on hit -> make their pathfinding/tracking better -> make the ones that need to aim at you properly AIM at you -> remove the cool down on the knife and lower it's damage (it 1 hit ko's at round 8 like what?) -> make all the guns GOOD, not just shotguns -> choose, either player has lower HP and goes down faster (more tense), or make the zombies more effective at holding the player down and swarming the player (more action).ONCE you've done those things, THEN you can look into improving the already decent things and maybe adding more things like more guns. I will make this review positive despite this wall of criticism, I do think this is actually a good base and they COULD really make something great here, so I want these dev's to know that they've got GOLD, clean it up and make it shine like a diamond. 🧡🐝🌸

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice little game, visual pleasing, not special but good enough for a guy like me who is sick and tired of the cartoonish graphics in video games. Technology have made so much progress and for whatever reason (lazy, no imagination, no abilities and so on) studios choose to develop games with graphics from windows 95 era. At least this one didn't go this path and I am glad about it!It still has some bugs and glitches, the most annoying one is that I get stuck when I am near objects, not every time but it happens way too often to bring in uncomfortable situation and to mention it here.The game doesn't offer any assistance in what to do with the missions, ok it tells you do that but not where it is or how. If you see youtube videos from other people who have done it, you can continue, otherwise you get stuck.I was gifted this game from a friend, he also couldn't figure out what to do next. I have gifted this game to 2 people, none of them knew what to do with the missions. You see...we can't all be rtrds...something else is the problem!The gameplay is fun! I enjoy playing this game either solo or with friends!But playing with friends means less money for all, the game doesn't seem to scale up/down depending on the amount of people in it. Also the discount drop is super rare and without it playing with a group it is next to impossible to level up the weapons!Last game, we got the half prize at wave 2 and then at wave 32... and after wave 20 if you do not have a weapon level 4 at least, the game becomes very hard! Still can be done but much much harder!There are some super annoying enemies that teleport constantly, those if we do not have the sudden death drop...they can drag the wave for too long! Those enemies need adjustment A.S.A.P.Another problem I have seen is with miracles, those that affect the "Q" skill with the scull, if you do not pay attention, due to Isaac or enemies etc, they can faq you up really bad! The default as is, is a super nice AOE skill. I haven't found any other "miracle" that improves it and the replacement for buffs are basically garbage!So you have been warned! Try to avoid replacing the default one with rtrd buffs!All in all the game is a solid 7/10
