_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoy this game, it is a fantastic Treyarch-like zombies mode utilizing round based gameplay with features such as pack-a-punch, a "mystery box" and perks.But I do have some criticisms which I hope are someday addressedCall me old school but I don't like the points on kill system which is similar to Black Ops: Cold War. The Issue I find with this system is how it heavily hinders progression, due to the way the tiered upgrade system for weapons work, if memory serves it starts at 5k jumps to 15k and so on, but you only make around 130 points per critical kill, even less for non critical kills, this I think can be fixed by doubling the amount of points you receive in general or swapping over to a points per hit system.Another issue I find is enemies are slow at hitting, I find myself rarely getting hit by melee enemies throughout the runs I have done, another issue is ranged enemies at far too easy to dodge their attacks. I feel for a player to get hit by an enemy they really have to try to get hit, I think if the Devs increase the speed of enemy attacks it would be great. While I am on the topic of enemies I don't like that they only feel stronger every 10 or so rounds, and I feel they take too much damage from the melee attack which is effective for a hot bit which while you can say it's risk vs reward, I don't feel a knife should kill in one hit past round 5, yes it allows us as the player to quickly garner points, but I would like a better points making method over relying upon the knife for more than 5 rounds.Outside of that I think a lot of the game is great. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but the bullet hit registration is really poor when fire rate gets too high. It makes it so an entire tree that increases fire rate needs to be avoided to ensure that your bullets can register correctly or they don't do any damage. Enemies tend to be bullet sponges past round 20,The point system needs some work because at higher rounds most of the guns feel like your shooting paint balls at the zombies, and you just don't get enough points to keep your weapons relevant.The maps need A LOT of work, mostof them are incredibly janky. Boss mechanics also are incredibly bad at times to be honest. Bosses spam pull you close to them into fire, and a horde of zombies they freshly spawned so you get stuck in a circle jerk and die instantly.The amalgamations teleport all around the place when they run, there are "invisible" enemies that you can see, however there are a lot of instances that I take damage from actual invisible sources. It's fun for about 2-3 hours and then you see the late mechanics are very spammy, unavoidable AOE damage, 8-10 amalgamations spawning at a time. Overall though, the game has tremendous potential and I hope the devs can release some updates to make it more enjoyable.EDIT: 5/19 It seems like the game has taken several steps backwards since the last time I played. Random crashes, if lots of enemies spawn in frame rates drop so low your game freezes (running Ryzen 7 7700X, 4070 TI, 32GB 5600MHz RAM).

_childDocuments_.review: 4 maps (only 2 are out now), but this is a fully featured cod zombies experience with less polish coming in at only $15. _childDocuments_.review: Fans seeking a direct Call of Duty: Zombies replacement may want to consider other options. While this game draws clear inspiration from the CoD formula, it offers a distinctly different gameplay feel.  The pacing, particularly the player's footstep sounds and relatively small maps combined with enemy speed, created a disorienting experience for me.Don't make the mistake I did of buying it immediately. The demo offers a great opportunity to experience these gameplay elements firsthand and see if they're a good fit for you.Perhaps this game will improve with further development, but at its current 1.0 version, it may be worth waiting to see if future updates address the balance and pacing that would create a smoother experience.Obviosuly I want to see this kind of gamemode out of the hands of Activision, but this sadly isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't honestly write reviews ever.But as playing CoD Zombies as a child with my brother was a big part of my childhood, I felt obligated.If you are looking for a game reminiscent of all the old CoD zombies mixed in with some of the more recent ones like BO3, this is the game for you. Infinite waves, Easter egg-like objectives.Story, although not as intricate as a telltale game etc, it's very fun for a zombie wave shooter.Fun enemies that keep the game-play challenging if that's what you're looking for you can change the difficulty, and if you think you want to change it without quitting the match? You can do it in game which is such a great feature.Upgrade your character with rewards from completing the story objective and completing higher waves.The upgrades serve as permanent perk buys for your character, so you actually get rewarded for playing the game, whilst you can still buy on the wall perks.The downsides of this game so far? Hitches in frame-rate being quite frequent, but it is on track to be fixed.The AI for the enemies are a little dumb, but honesty? Its a zombie game, they aren't meant to be super intelligent, however it is a little hilarious on wave 50 I can wipe everything out by making a blazefinger kill it's buddies without shooting a bullet.There aren't a lot of guns at all.Various bugs that when not game breaking can still be frustrating, example: final zombie of a round not spawning and taking 5+ minutes to end the round.Sometimes when pressing F to pick up an object it doesn't always detect input, causing you to thinking you picked it up, and having to go back and actually pick it up.With all this being said, it is a brand new game being exactly 4 days old as of this review, and I would implore all my CoD zombie enthusiasts the get this game as it will serve as the better replacement for something we have wanted for a long while. This game is 100% worth getting. The devs care, and they do a great job.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend the game in the stage that its currently in, poor networking issues mixed with a horribly unbalanced rogue like element called miracles, on top of a whole lot of other issues.Prices for upgrading guns, getting more revives and even refreshing your "miracle" options all become more expensive the more times you use/do it, granted the guns costing more makes sense, but when an unleveled weapon takes half an hour to kill a single zombie at wave 20 you are force to save every bit of cash you get and hope you get a decent weapon early on that you can level up... On a side not I think the perks you can buy from wall machines are pretty balanced price wise, you should only ever pick up at most 4 of them though as the rest of them are a waste of money.Refreshing your miracles should not scale in prices, it starts off at 2k then 4k into 6k, it probably goes higher but i never bother to refresh them after a certain point, its a ridiculous money sink and if you have a general idea of what you want you may end up not having any cash left at all.And then revives... first off it takes way too long to revive a teammate, even with a maxed out revive speed perk... The maxed out revive speed perk should be the baseline speed at which you revive teammates.And the pricing on the revives goes up way too high, starting off at 5k is fine, but use it more than once and it scales so high that if you buy another one you wont be able to afford upgrading your weapon, BUT if you dont revive your teammate before the end of the wave, guess what? They loose all their weapons (as they should), but in practice you are forced to buy them no matter what, making dying not a point of failure but frustration at the games mechanics.Also, I CANT SEE JACK ALL in this game, unless i blast my gamma settings to max and then turn my screen half gray with the brightness setting, the flashlight does barely anything to help when its max distance is half a meter in front of your face.Finally, the biggest multiplayer issue that i have found so far is netcode, heres a short list of things that have happened due to it:1. _childDocuments_.review: Many will notice that the game probably inspired by Cod zombie mode, this one's just have its own unique game-play to it, so far i have played it solo to see how far things can go, and there are few things i noticed, and will be mentioned below.Game-play wise it is a game where it is easy to understand, kill enemies, get rewarded with money, use the money to buy weapons, buffs, upgrades.performance wise, only had 2 tiny micro stutters within almost 2 hours of gameplay otherwise it is 144 fps for me indoors, and as low as 90 when it is full of enemies, special effects etc, and all of this on max settings.difficulty, might be easier early on, but as you progress the enemies become bullet sponge even with upgraded weapons, to the point that you feel upgrading is not worth it anymore.upgrading, weapon upgrading is good up to tier 2 or 3, but after that the cost is a whooping 50k, basically it goes from 5k to 15k to 30k, then 50k, you can try your luck with half price enemy drop ( similar to max ammo, nuke, etc  in cod drops ), yet what are the chances to get it or not? so i couldn't get to tier 4 to see if there is any higher upgrade, and at this point i don't think it is possible, or even worth it unless it was extremely powerful to justify the price of the upgrade. IMO it should be toned down by half at least.Weapons, there isn't that much added yet, i assume it is due to being EA still so either ideas not there, or they have some ideas of weapons to add but for future updates.Special effects, needs to be toned down a bit, late waves you get blazers (group of them) where if they fire either together or simultaneously it will fill the screen, and probably cause eye strain easily, it can also be bad or flashy for those who have issue with such things.Shock when reloading doesn't seem to work, it was a buff iirc, didn't seem like it dealt any damage at all, since i have damage shown when i attack enemies, so probably the devs need to look into it.overall the game is really fun in solo, and it will be 4 times fun in co-op with full team, happy that i noticed this game, and hope to see more from the dev, along with more weapons, and tbh it is optimized more than many triple A games out there for how much it throw at you and still remain at high fps.my rig is a laptop:i7 11800h, RTX 3070 ( max-p 140 tgp), 16gb ram, the game is also installed on external HDD, not SSD, loading wasn't an issue at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I am glad someone is actually trying to use this genre other than Treyarch. I have been wanting a standalone zombie wave survival in the similar style of COD zombies since they started slowly ruining it over the past few years. So far in the hour I have been playing I am pretty satisfied in the game. Its not a AAA title by no means, but they defiantly put the work in to make it a decent game. For a price of 19.99 at the time I bought it you cant beat it. Things that could use improvement, smoothness of animations, cut scenes, and maybe the zombie count/difficulty scaling. The game does scaling okay, but it could be better, I made it to round 17 easily on normal difficulty on my first play through on a map I had not even seen game play of. Even at round 17 I didn't die I just closed the game. The difficulty system honestly could go away and I would be happy, A wave survival game shouldn't have difficulties, its all about how far along you can get in the rounds based off skill. It takes away from the competitive factor that was the biggest thing about zombies pre black ops 2 before all the easter eggs/story line. Do not get me wrong the easter eggs/story line are fun, but after you do all of them, if the game doesn't have a competitive leader board it will slowly die, and in my honest opinion the option to select difficulties ruins that. Everyone should be playing on the same difficulty, with it slowly getting more and more difficult.Overall the game is great for 20 bucks, Its fun. As long as the developers keep working to make it better this game could be something great one day.Also there needs to be a leaderboard, at the time of this review I dont see one.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think the game has a good skeleton of what can be done with a system like this. It hearkens back to those classic round-based zombies games I used to play, but with some modernized elements that I think are for the best. If you want a direct comparison, it's kind of like Call of Duty: Cold War's zombies mode but with a bit more lean into the traditional types of zombies that you might be more familiar with. The maps are diverse enough with interesting elements to enjoy. Each map also has a unique "wonder weapon"-like thing tied to its main story which is a nice touch and encourages you to be more involved with the story than I think other games are. I do also appreciate that the main story is guided so you don't need a degree in esoteric schizophrenia to understand what to do next, while also leaving the bigger secrets hidden for you to figure out on your own.Everything you unlock is unlocked by playing the game, and that's a refreshing thing to see in a sea of awful microtransaction hellscapes. I hope it stays like that. The actual gameplay loop is exactly what you expect and delivers as a zombie format. No arduous gimmicks, just exactly what you want. The perks are varied enough, if a tad uninspired (I'd be interested to see if a 6th perk could be added that plays more with your Miracles). Weapons, while only being a small pool, feel good and I don't think there's anything particularly underpowered.The cutscenes for some of these story beats are REALLY clunky.I wish there was more weapon variety. Not including the special weapons, I think there's maybe 9 or so unique weapons, but I wish there were more.Various animations feel way too stiff for both the player characters and the enemies, especially on several of the secret bosses.Some minor quality of life features feel unfinished or missing (i.e., proper party system that isn't prone to kicking people?, sharing weapons from Rex, proper statistics tracking and more visible weapon stats, and a few others), and I hope that can be ironed out later.I think the game is worth its price tag for a round-based zombies game. It has enough content to have kept me entertained and the story beats were engaging enough to encourage me to see it to the main story's end (I have yet to do the secret beats, but I hope to change that soon). I do think the finale is a little goofy, but I blame a lot of that on the stiff animations. There's a lot of positives, but there are some glaring negatives that I can primarily point to being lack of polish. This game has a great bit of potential, and I look forward to seeing what'll be done in the future. If you're one of those people who like scores:

_childDocuments_.review: Sker Ritual is one of those hidden gems made by Indie developers that never seems to get the attention or hype it deserves. If you're like me and love the Call of Duty Zombies formula, but found the latest iterations to be a mess (looking at you Vanguard!), then you'll love this game.Now keep in mind, this is in early access and the odd bug will occur, but I haven't had anything game breaking, the worst I've had is the main boss getting stuck from their spawn and not moving, making the encounter so easy. The devs seem keen to get this all ironed out though, and their CM FluffyClouds seems to be making the rounds to take all feedback on board!So what is Sker Ritual? Well, its a wave based, point mechanic FPS with objectives and a main story to complete. Headshot kills earn more points that body shots, doors need to be bought to proceed in the map, guns can be randomly rolled for from the Lucky Dog, you have a molotov grenade and a healing potion to help out with any troublesome moments you face. What makes Sker unique is the Miracle system, a form of levelling granted at the end of rounds allowing you to upgrade parts of your kit from 3 randomly generated options. Bullets, healing potion, melee, molotovs and a special ability can all be chosen, and future Miracles allow you to improve their rarity, boosting their effects. And yes, this does allow you to make builds in the game! Want poison bullets so enemiss hit take some damage over time? There's an option for that. Want to turn invisible from a press of a key, if you're lucky enough it's possible. But the real decision come from synergising all of your kit to take down enemies, like some bullets do more damage to slowed enemies, so spec your grenade, potion, melee and ability into slowing hordes for the big DPS increase. We don't even know the full list of combos just yet, but there's a lot of depth to it!We also get a roadmap, stating another 3 maps are coming, and additional features to be released. You also get a free "battlepass" feature in game, allowing periodic unlocks as you progress for masks and voicelines.The fact this game is £10 on sale, or about £12-13 when not is an absolute steal for the content in this and what's to come. I highly recommend you pick this up and try for yourself. After one game, you'll be hooked!

After a maps main quest line has been completed you can start the secret quest line for that map.In some of the maps even the end cutscene changed when both are completed.The fifth map was good but lacked the core story of the first four. It did tie up loose ends between characters. The map starts you in a small broken house which you must fix. It feels good to play and a throwback to a claustrophobic zombie fighting.Then there is Tides of Terror which is a 2/10….Every other objective is killing enemies in X circle. Two simple shipwrecks with 20 doors you need to spend points opening. And a sub-boss that has it’s sound turned up to 500%. Only in this map did I get instant killed at least once on most runs due to that thing. The new enemy is a crab that mostly sits there staring at you.Based on the four starting maps I was expecting steps that required me to think and explore. One of the steps in the fourth map has you solving mathematical questions, to create a monster. However, they are written in symbols and therefore I had to think to solve it. Diamond, Square, Triangle, Square, for example.The special weapon is a minigun which is nice. However, it is easy to miss because it is not part of the main quest. The special weapons of the first four maps are. They play a part in solving the quest, not just a killing tool. From ripping hearts out of the dead to powering metal scarecrow.I was hoping for the start of a new threaded quest line. The main quest about killing godly / mythical legends. The hidden question line being focusing on harvesting their power. I hope they go back to a story driven game. The lore based on real myths and history really sets this game apart. I could write about the combat and other mechanics, but I will leave it there. This review is already long enough.Overall, an 8/10.20 + hours of what I am going to call a story campaign.I recommend buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: As it is, right now I honestly don't recommend this game. Don't misunderstand me, the concept and idea is great and I love the fact that this is sort of a L4D/Killing floor type of game, but if any of you were to buy this game as it is I'm pretty sure that the boredom will come crawling pretty quickly.It's fine for a couple of games, or you can even test your patience and reach ten matches but at the eleventh one you'll probably start searching for another game to kill some time while this gets updated with any new content. If you also count that there are two achievements in which you have to stay alive for 35 rounds and 50 rounds, I even wonder who actually did these two (surely friends because solo's I doubt). I honestly tried it, so hard, but after reaching the 21 round every time I just simply quit because I get bored. Just sitting there, waiting, killing, repeating.. you know by now that yes, after a while it gets boring (after repeating this so many times).The problem lies also in the fact that the grind is real, the normal difficulty for this game it's not rewarding at all because for doing at least one level of the "sker pass" you have to play at least two times or if things gets worse, even three times, doing the same and only available map, same objectives and so on. The only thing that can make a difference and  make everything more interesting, is the fact that right at the start of the match you can choose to increase the difficulty of the level and raise the bar really high. There's also another level, expert I assume but I didn't try it because the hard mode indeed was already challenging for me. Still, it's not enough and I doubt you want to start already at hard mode (but if you're a masochist go ahead, it's great).I just hope that they will bring new content soon and rework the overall grind because it's not really great.------------------------------Honestly speaking, I still don't recommend this game at all. Of all of the things I asked kindly to the developers like adding more exp for those who play the game solo (moreso because the game is technically dead. Hell, it was DOA all along to be fair and I'm not surprised that you take a lot of time to even find a lobby if you decide to go co-op), they totally ignored it. Sure, you can get more but only if you play ad Hard or Nightmare and I'm not a tryharder kind of player and if I have to repeat the same level at normal with just one single level for the account and one level for the sker pass for each map, yeah no. It takes an  to even reach half of the pass, so imagine grinding over and over and over on the same map, same objectives, same monsters and so on. It's not fun, it's a huge chore.Also the too many puzzles. I get for the hidden easter egg that you need to do quite a few tasks, but the puzzle in each level it's really boring. It's not something interesting at all.It's really a shame because I see that the devs plans in adding two more maps in the future but I'll definitely won't be playing it. They really should've made another standalone title and not a co-op like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Theres a lot to like about this game, but I cant really recommend it. There are a lot of strong decisions that make this game feel like a successor to early cod zombies, but a lot holds it backPros:Gunplay is fun, and skillful usage of guns/abilities is rewardingTheres ammo deposits all around that dont just cost your guns cost, which is goodUpgraded guns can be restored if you dieThe objectives are earnestly interesting and aren't just "shoot the thing" or "defend another thing"Story seems uniqueCons:No character. Cod Zombies had a lot of strong characters, which this game lacks. The bag on head being customizable is a funny way to do this, but there's no personality besides the narrator. At higher levels, zombies become damage sponges which isn't as interactive as it seems. This is a problem that stacks with the next one, as wellYou only earn points upon killing zombies. This makes the games economy weird because there is simply a point where you can't advance further. If you were the player that opened up the map and passed on weapon upgrades to do so, it is miserable to play catchup with 3 other players who can actually do damage and take a majority of the points for kills.Finally, what got me to stop playing: the graphics. I had everything on their defaults and I got to a round in the theater where I was doing laps to avoid zombies while trying to complete objectives, and doing so made me physically ill. The motion blur from swinging and running and attack blur from the ranged zombies, combined with the grimdark color scheme made my head hurt and made me nauseous. I was defeated not by zombies, but by throwing up. Overall, I think this is a neat game made by a small studio, so I dont regret buying it, but holy do I wish the game was brighter and more friendly on my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed zombies mode in COD BO2, BO3, Infinite Warfare and etc... This game just about nails it. For starters, I feel everything has been improved upon to really justify sinking hundreds of hours into this. You earn cosmetic items as well as the ability to upgrade the perk machines between matches. In game is very fun, the variety of enemy types, the appearance of mini bosses, more optional objectives than I know what to do with. This game is almost perfect. The only department I find lacking is the gunplay and melee feel a bit loose. It definitely doesn't feel as tight and fine tuned but this is something I can forgive easily considering the amount of fun the game already is.Pros: Life Token system, Difficulty Selection, Character Unlocks, Perk Upgrades, Interesting Maps, Music, Guns, Health Potions, Miracle System, molotovs, and much more.Cons: Gunplay feels loose, like you don't get that sayisfying snap when you use iron sights. Also the melee is a bit wonky. You kind of blindly swing in front slowly and there's no lock on to the closest enemy either. You'll miss a lot until you figure out to time melee strikes ahead. Though the upside is that one swing aimed correctly can take out at least three to four mobs instead of only damaging one.Oh one more con, no splitscreen. I didn't subtract points, but that option would have made this even better. All in all, if you liked Zombies, you'll like this a lot. If you don't like this, I have a suspicion you don't like much of anything.

_childDocuments_.review: It does a lot right, but a few major things wrong.The maps are fun with multiple paths, the quests are inventive and encourage cooperative participation, and the upgrades were cool. However, the wrong makes it difficult to enjoy.Players earn points to spend on weapons, upgrades, and resources by killing hordes, but points are primarily awarded to the player that does the killing blow, so often times point distribution is skewed. For example, if one player spends earlier rounds fending off the hordes so another player can complete objectives, then the objective-player will have no functional points. This is burdensome during later waves, when upgrades are absolutely required to stay ahead of the bloating health pools. Ability upgrades don't clearly indicate if they'll overwrite previous ability upgrades or how they'll change abilities if they change how a ability functions entirely. For example, adding a healing element to molotov/grenade completely removes its ability to damage, which is a rough thing to find out in the heat of battle.Weapon purchases only effect the current held weapon. Gun and melee weapon purchases overwrite the currently held weapon. Ammo refills require points to buy, but only refill the weapon in the player's hand at the time of purchase, not all weapons the player carries. The game doesn't give any indication of this in advance. The player can carry, at most, two (2) ammo-using weapons.Quest objects may replace the player's weapons entirely without any clear indication that they will and the weapon is never returned; the player will have to repurchase the weapon and re-upgrade it.Killed hordes have a chance to drop temporary buffs (Infinite Ammo, Half-Price for purchases, etc.) but the drop odds are such that temporary buffs usually drop once a horde has been wiped out, rendering most buffs useless as there are no enemies to use these benefits on and the buffs don't last long enough to be useful at the start of the next wave.This isn't exhaustive, but in short: the game structure is cooperative, but the mechanics are not. This seems like it'd be an enjoyable game for someone who likes arbitrarily difficult games and only has a surface interest in cooperative gameplay. Not for me, but it's for someone.

name: Asterix & Obelix: Slap them All!
detailed_description: A double helping of slaps! The Romans and all other enemies better watch out! About the Game The year is 50 B.C. Gaul is entirely occupied by the Romans. Well, not entirely... One small village of indomitable Gauls still holds out against the invaders. Everything is falling apart! Our two heroes will travel all around the world to fight the Roman Empire in a 2D horizontal scrolling Beat Them Up game, completely hand-drawn and made in the purest tradition of the genre. Enemies and wild boars will have to be cautious! Asterix and Obelix are back… And it's going to be another great fight! Play as Asterix and Obelix in cooperation (local multiplayer mode) with family or friends! Slap thousands of Romans away with a wide range of moves and unique combos to each character! The Adventure mode chapters are based on existing Asterix & Obelix albums. The game also features an exclusive chapter that was created specifically for the game. Alongside the main adventure, discover mini-games to complete the feast of our Gaulish friends! Enjoy hand-drawn designs faithful to the original comic books series and animations created especially for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fortunately, I wasn't influenced by all the negative reviews at the beginning. As soon as I saw the first pictures, I was thrilled. This is how a game about Asterix & Obelix should be!I think the biggest mistake you can make here is comparing this game to the XXL series. I've played these games too, but I'm not exactly a huge fan of the games. Why this? Because they remind me very little of the old comics. Some of the figures look very exaggerated and I find it completely absurd that the magic potion can conjure up a tornado. The XXL series is okay as a video game, but for me it is definitely not the measure of all things.Asterix & Obelix Slap Them All! is completely based on the old comics and the old stories, the good old art style from back then is also taken up. The graphic designers really did a great job here. The music is great, the voices (at least in the German voice output) are good. The medium level of difficulty offers a certain challenge, but can be mastered. We also have everything a good story needs to have about the two gallic heroes: wild boars, pirates time and again, bandits, prison breakouts, lions and of course... Romans without end. Sure, at some point the opponents repeat themselves, but it was no different for comparable games from the past. This was criticized in some review, not really understandable for me. Elsewhere it was criticized that the game was too short. I don't think so, after ten hours I already had the feeling that the end could come, although I had a lot of fun. It's one of those games that you start all over again after the first play through to improve your score, as it was in the 1990s or before. I feel very much reminded of the days of good old Super Nintendo, as the Asterix games were sometimes very similar.On my part, there is at best one point of criticism: I would have liked to have had more mini-games. At Asterix & Obelix on the SNES, for example, you had the opportunity to take part in the rugby game in Britain. Such and similar moments are neglected here.Conclusion: I can only say that I am having fun and I am grateful for this wonderful game about the two gallic heroes. So far the most successful of all games for me next to the old SNES classic Asterix & Obelix. I would be very happy about a second part of this wonderful game with more stories from the legendary comic series.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe the ratings for this game.  This is a really great game!  And that's coming from a beat-em-up expert.  I've been playing beat-em-ups since Double Dragon I for NES.  I have every major beat-em-up released on Steam (that I know of, suggest them if I'm missing any important ones).  People seem to be fixating on the lack of Options and deadpanning the game because of it.  Would it have been nice to have the option to change resolution, controls, and audio?  Yes, of course.  Is it a flaw in the game that they are missing?  Yes, of course.  Does it ruin this otherwise excellent beat-em-up?  No, of course not!  This game is super fun, well-balanced, has some of the best (if not THE best) artwork I've ever seen in this type of game, and it avoids all of the most annoying pitfalls that beat-em-ups typically suffer from.  Let me give you some examples.  You know what this game doesn't do?  This game doesn't do player stun-locks, it doesn't let you get hit from enemies off screen, it almost never gives enemies invincible frames in their attacks, it doesn't make bosses into bullet sponges, it doesn't make levels last so long you start wishing they'd just be over.  The combat system is well designed, giving both playable characters their own unique feel and move set and making both equally fun to play with.  My girlfriend and I were able to casually play through Act I and II and part of III on medium difficulty in just around 3 hours.  One level we had to retry a couple times, and several we only scraped by with a little health, telling us that the difficulty level was extremely well balanced.  We had an alarm set for an hour and a half in case we needed to return the game but when the alarm went off we were both still having a great time and agreed the game was definitely a keeper.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick impression:  I don't know Man... I think the game is freaking awesome \m/ :) \m/ ! Note: I come from the Arcade era, and I know the small kid version of Me would be freaking out if He saw this back in the day.I just finished the first level with the big Man Obelix since I always roll with the big dudes in brawlers like broseph's: Haggar, Goah, Max, Floyo, Major Dutch Schaefer and many others.Basically feels good Man, this is an old school Arcade brawler through and through there is no question about it this is what We played back in the day. What is pimp the game has been furnished in 2D HD art at the level of Cuphead, just not the same exact style of course but that type of quality.Other than that there is a large move set, you got your super bar, you pick up stuff, can switch between Asterix & Obelix in SP(this is cool), there are a lot of different enemies and they all look awesome and are animated really well. The background art is ACE and the rest of the game looks amazing.The game automatically saves the last level you are at so you don't have to re-play the levels. There are four difficulties, so if you are hard core there is a mode for you. The game looks insane at 4K!!!!!! To make sure the game was running at 4K I right clicked on the the EXE picked properties -> Compatibility tab -> Change high DPI settings -> check mark on : Override High DPI scaling -> drop down : Application . I do this with all My games since I have a 4K screen, it may work in 4K out of the box I never tired it just as is. This trick forces the rez that your screen is set to.I don't know what else to say, I enjoyed the little I played and would of stayed and cram quarters in it if it was a cabinet at the local Arcade(when We had them). There even is a cool storey transition between levels and at the start of the game which I enjoyed(nice touch). Also if you watched the cartoon the style and art is on point, good job!Personally I don't feel the game deserves the hate but rather praise, having said that I am a OG and come from the Arcades and C64 days so maybe I think differently as to what is expected.100% worth getting in My opinion if you like Arcade brawlers and currently Streets of Rage 4 is My jam(10/10).

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the game is not good. It is mostly very repetitive and the overall gameplay feels weird and gets boring after a while. Enemy types repeat all the time and those that are different still feel really similar to the others and none of them really change the way you have to play against them. Higher difficulty seems to only increase the damage of opponents. Bosses are, just like regular enemies, punching bags - at least the first 2 that I encountered in my short play time - and the fights did not feel special at all. The story is a mixup of Asterix comics as far as I can tell, which is okay I guess, but the way it is told is not engaging at all.The visuals are nice, but they often feel quite lifeless, because they are only partly animated and nothing is going on in the backgrounds. The music is just meh, in my opinion.What is also unacceptable is that there are no graphics or audio options. I understand that this appears to be a port of the console version, but still..Overall, I am very disappointed. If this is on sale for a few bucks at some point, it could be an okay buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didnt get this game because of all the haters with no clue. if you are even a slight fan of Asterix comics, or classic side scrolling beat-em-ups, then this game is an essential. the animations capture the feel of the comics soooo well with some classic moves you will love, such as Asterix picking up a roman and swinging him over his head to knock down others, or Obelix picking up a roman and slapping him silly then punching him into the sky leaving his roman sandals behind. there are lots of references and play throughs of several of the comic stories ive seen so far. Dogmatix even follows Obelix around, though to the best of my knowledge he doesnt attack or anything. the people hating on this game are clueless. there are people hating on this game because it doesnt have video options like playing in windowed mode, or alt languages, which btw, it does have alt languages, I changed mine to French to feel more official. who gives a game a bad review because you cant play in windowed mode? this person doesnt like gaming, they just like Windows 10 and programs they can use to open more windows in Windows 10.there are people hating on it because the enemies are repetitive. ignoring the fact that most of these whiners barely have an hour in the game to see if the enemies change, I can assure you that they do. ive clobbered romans, pirates, vikings, gladiators, highwaymen and im only in chapter 3 so far. further, its Asterix and Obelix, if you know anything about them or are even a slight fan you know that a lot of romans get clobbered, and this game is no different. im not sure what they thought happens in Asterix comics. another group of whiners complains that there aren't powers or gear to unlock to make you more powerful. that is correct in my experience so far, however it seems they have no idea of what a side scroller beat-em-up is. Streets of Rage, Final Fight, TMNT, x-men, Simpsons are some of the best beat-em-ups ever and none of them have ways to level up your character other than the original old school way your character gets better, by playing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game and getting good at it. I guess some of them let you pick up a lead pipe to clobber someone with, in this game you can pick up a roman and clobber people..another person complained that its just a mash X simulator. sure, you can play the game and just mash X (light hit), but there is a block, grab, hard hit and jump button you can use too, and mixing them up gets you different combos and attacks. I assume the same complainer is giving Forza racing game a ♥♥♥♥ review calling it a holding X simulator. visually this game is perfect, as even the haters have to admit, and technically this game plays very well. responsive controls, lots of moves and I havent even figured out how to do the special moves yet. the enemy AI is impressive too, when youre clobbering romans, they actually try roman tactics, stick in a group and throw spears, if you knock them around they will gradually migrate back into formation. the romans are simple to beat up, however if you let them group up and throw spears it can be tricky. overall I find it has a lot of advanced AI tactics that work quite well and I havent seen ANY other beat-em-up compare, im very impressed. as well its nothing to have 15-20 characters on the screen and it doesnt lag or cause any issues. in some cases the enemies moves end up being timed in a way that if they surround you, it can be hard to get back on your feet, but I find that is rare and once you know, you can avoid it fairly easily. if I had to complain, I would mention that if you get too close to an enemy, it will register your are facing wrong direction and not hit the enemy. its a classic issue in beat-em-ups, they all have it but this one its a bit more pronounced, as well it can be a bit slow to change facing direction, especially if you hit an attack button, but I must add these are small issues. I also find that the game more than makes up for it by having other moves giving generously easy hits. I guess the regular price is slightly up there, im not saying its not worth the $30 but after playing it $20 and buying this is a no-brainer, steam sale has it for $13 which is easily worth it. overall this is a solid beat-em-up, probably in the top of the genre  with the other titles I mentioned, with some of the best AI, and true to the source material graphics. I would say you dont need to know anything about Asterix to love this game if you are a fan of classic beat-em-ups. If you are a fan of Asterix and Obelix at all you should have stopped reading this and bought the game after the first couple sentences. especially if its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An Asterix themed slap-em all and it looks great too, yum. I didn't need more to be interested, but the stars had also aligned. The game is Steam Deck verified and looked like the kind of game that would be good to play on the go. Perfect for a trip I had planned at the time. So it didn't take long for the game to find its way to my library.The game puts you in the middle of some classic Asterix tales, like Asterix and the Normans or Asterix in Spain and features tons of familiar faces. Granted the stories are hyper-condensed and people that don't already know them will barely be able to follow them, much less appreciate them. But for those that do know the tales, the game will make you feel like you really are in one of those good old comic books. This adds a fair bit of weight to the nostalgia factor. It helps that the art is truly gorgeous and very faithful. Obelix in particular is a treat to watch. Sorry Asterix, but this is about beating folks up and nobody does that better than our resident roast boar afficionado. As far as I am concerned the game delivered. Is it the best beat'em up ever made? Not even close, as it's dogged by rather poor and clunky controls. Often enough a dealbreaker in this genre. It also lacks proper customisation options. For example, on an ultra-wide screen it will actually stretch. As if it's a game from 20 years ago. Be that as it may, it still plays great on the Deck and, as an Asterix fan, I found it reasonably entertaining. All in all, a good purchase.For the fans, I repeat, for the fans, this is fun romp and I can recommend it. Twice so if you want something quick to play every now and then on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another failed Asterix game. The visuals are superb, the music is OK, but the rest really doesn't stand up. The storytelling is horrible, with the actual levels doing nothing to advance the story, which is a dumbed down version of the comics, and appear as cutscenes, to make the game even more tedious. The combat is quite meh to begin with, and there is no development, no new elements, just new enemies who do the same basic stuff with a few extra attacks thrown in here and there. Interestingly, some general mobs do more damage than Obelix, which is quite anti-lore, to say the least. But what did me in were the boss fights, usually at the end of long grinding levels. They are not particularly hard, but it's easy to get caught in attack chains with one character, and if you accidentally die, then you have to suffer through the pre-boss part of the level. I mean, what's the point?And unfortunately, this last question is quite appropriate for the entire game...

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks and feels absolutely beautiful. The animations are perfect—but that's where the good stuff ends. I understand it's a beat 'em up side-scrolling game with mindless punching, but it could have been so much more.The story and static cut-scenes are a huge "nothing". They literally go like this: "Our heroes are going into the woods. Our heroes are climbing the ship. They're getting off the ship. They meet an X. They come back. They are going to location X. They come to location X. They are going back..." For what? That's not a story; that's just a descriptive filler, that serves no purpose. There are so many great Asterix adventures they could have used to craft a compelling narrative.There are no collectibles to distract you from the monotony you'll feel after playing for more than an hour. It quickly becomes so boring that you forget you are playing it while playing it. That's how your mind can go away. I need to remind myself that I am playing a game. The old arcade games at least had secrets and some variety—like pulling up a rope or something. But here? Nothing. The decision to mix all enemy types across all levels not only makes no sense but adds to the monotony. Pirates in town, Romans on ships—why not assign enemies to specific locations?With just a bit more effort, this game could have easily been a 10/10. But I'm afraid to even look at Slap Them All 2—from what I've seen, they haven’t fixed anything. Maybe they've added a few new moves, but that's not worth buying the game over.I'd give this game a 10/10 for the first minute of gameplay, then decrease the score every half hour of play. I've put in about 4 hours over the two years I’ve had this game installed, and I really hate that I’m a completionist because I just want to get it over with. But it's so boring, I can't even bother. So, 2/10.But damn, it still looks beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: The year is 50 B.C. Gaul is being entirely occupied by the Roman Empire, but a small village still holds out against the invaders. Led by Asterix and Obelix and thanks to a miraculous potion, the village rebels against the enemies, in a classic adventure inspired by the comic books that brings our protagonists all around the world.Upon starting a level, you will be required to choose if you want to play as Asterix or Obelix, but you can also swap them any time in the middle of the game, which is good if one of them starts to run low on health. They both share the same move-set though: punches, kicks, jumps and combos, they are pretty much the same in terms of effects and damage dealt, with the only difference being the hold button, which can generate a few different attacks (such as slapping or throwing enemies against others). Overall, combat feels pretty basic and repetitive, requiring spamming the same few buttons, with no power-up or upgrade. As a typical brawler, you move in one direction until you reach the end of the level, fighting multiple waves of enemies. A few bonus stages will instead require you to race and destroy any object on-screen within a time limit. On the top left of the screen there is a classic energy bar used for parries and special moves; it recharges over time or when you hit enemies with standard attacks. The vital bar can be easily recharged by eating food found inside barrels, which are also full of money that increases your level score. Unfortunately, this score doesn’t have any effect on gameplay and since there are no collectables or extras to unlock, it feels completely useless. There is no tutorial in-game, but you can find a short list of commands in a separate menu (and you can’t rebind them). There are no graphics or sound options either, which is rather disappointing to see.There are only two game modes: Adventure and Free Play. The campaign longevity is decent enough, but there are many recycled assets, stages and enemies (romans, gladiators, pirates and bandits) which, paired with the simple combat, ruin the fun and make the gameplay extremely repetitive. Unfortunately there is no online co-op, so you can only rely on local multiplayer or Steam remote play together. The “problem” is that the gameplay is clearly designed for co-op, with enemies often appearing on both sides of the screen, so you really need to have someone watching your back. There are four difficulties, but even at medium difficulty the game can be harder if played alone and I often found myself overwhelmed by a great number of enemies spawing everywhere (like in a sort of 2D musou). This is why, as a single player, it can become very frustrating. Boss fights are rather disappointing too in term of design and variety, and I found them to be even easier than some enemy hordes.The art style is 100% faithful to the comic book, both in-game and during the short cutscenes in-between levels. Environments feature beautiful coloured backgrounds and it feels like being inside the comic book. Characters have some pretty nice animations, with many popping “puff!” and “bong!” icons appearing when smashing enemies. Music and sounds are mostly coherent with the comics visuals, but Asterix and Obelix will often repeat the same few lines, which can become tiring in the long run.At a first glance, Asterix & Obelix Slap Them All! seems really funny, but the beauty of environments and characters is soon washed out by some tedious gameplay and repetitive use of the same assets. The game lacks many mandatory features for this genre, with the progression and difficulty mostly balanced for two players, while proving to be a far less enjoyable single player experience. A missed opportunity, for a game that artistically is completely faithful to the comic’s style and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: So much better than I thought it would be.The controls are extremely responsive, with zero latency and fast and fluid animations. The moves for Astérix and Obélix are different enough that playing as either character feels distinct, but they are also well-balanced and both characters have all the tools they need.The music is energetic and uplifting and very catchy! It sounds just a little bit more like a cartoon movie score than an arcade classic of old, yet not entirely so and it sounds right at home. You'll be humming along for sure.Finally, the visuals are BEAUTIFUL and I don't really think I need to describe them since that's plain for all to see on the trailers and screenshots. It looks almost exactly like the comics and cartoons.A few words about the PC port:- It runs flawlessly at 60fps with no bugs to speak of. I'm currently running a laptop RTX 3080 with 140W TDP (performs approximately like a desktop 3070) but it doesn't seem to be using it heavily, so it should run fine on a wide array of configurations.- It defaults to exclusive full screen- There are no options whatsoever. None. I have to assume the language is auto-selected according to your system language as there isn't even an option to change it (that means I'm stuck with the English dub, whereas I would like to use the French dub along with English text.- That also means there are no graphics options, including no setting for resolution or refresh rate. It seems to default to your desktop resolution with a 60fps v-sync (as there is no screen tearing).- There are also no controller customization options. I'm not sure non-xinput controllers work natively, but xinput controllers (such as the Xbox One/Series controller do) and non-xinput controllers should work with no issues if Steam Input is enabled. Controls cannot be remapped natively in-game, but you can freely remap the buttons via Steam Input. The default configuration should work fine for most people, however.- According to the developers, a patch is coming soon that will add options to the game such as resolution and language selection. This patch was announced in December 2021.

detailed_description: When a pandemic puts the lockdown on a blooming relationship, will the new couple keep the romance alive, or will distance pull them apart? Cozy up with their quarantine story and see if they’ll find a way to stay connected in the weirdest of times in this new episode of the Half Past Fate story. Features: Learn to love from afar through the charismatic 2.5D pixel-art style of Half Past Fate Enjoy a charming and honest slice-of-life story set in all-too-familiar circumstances Play from both sides of the new relationship and see how each of your lives have changed Judge (or admire) each other’s home decor, peculiar roommates, and musical tastes Explore in endearing detail the intimate environs of each other’s quarantined lives Maybe figure out what the heck “defragging” does
about_the_game: When a pandemic puts the lockdown on a blooming relationship, will the new couple keep the romance alive, or will distance pull them apart? Cozy up with their quarantine story and see if they’ll find a way to stay connected in the weirdest of times in this new episode of the Half Past Fate story. Features: Learn to love from afar through the charismatic 2.5D pixel-art style of Half Past Fate Enjoy a charming and honest slice-of-life story set in all-too-familiar circumstances Play from both sides of the new relationship and see how each of your lives have changed Judge (or admire) each other’s home decor, peculiar roommates, and musical tastes Explore in endearing detail the intimate environs of each other’s quarantined lives Maybe figure out what the heck “defragging” does
short_description: Finding true love is hard enough when it’s in person! Build a relationship through the screen as a couple copes with lockdown life by staying connected online! Will their love be loud and clear, or will their signals fade away?

_childDocuments_.review: Back last year, I found and played a game called Half Past Fate which instantly grabbed me with the cute art style and that it’s a rom-com slice-of-life adventure where you follow six people as they cross paths with their destined soulmate and eventually get together as you jump through time and switch between perspectives. , but I quite enjoyed it and it surpassed what I was expecting from it going in. Fast forward to this year, and we’re now having another chapter added onto the Half Past Fate universe that I doubt many people would have predicted.Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing is basically adding in another couple to the original cast, but this takes place after the events of the original game rather than intertwining this within the original timeline. First of all, the original storylines didn’t have a lockdown going on, this does have a short mention of an event that took place in the original, and there were changes to the town starting. Anyway, this time around we’re only following one couple. If you played Half Past Fate, you may have a faint recognition (or outright remember depending on when you played) of who these two are.We’ll be following the cashier of ElectriCity, Robin, who was not at all interested in interacting with customers and the Swole Tea guy from the Tea Festival who we learn is Stephen. Their paths have not crossed at all until now, when Stephen needs some help. He doesn’t exactly know anything about computers and his isn’t doing so well, so he ends up going to his local electronics store (which I don’t think he goes in at all). Though, today is his lucky day as the Nerd Force nerd that’s meant to help fix electronics decided to skip out on work. This causes Robin to see if there’s anything she can do, which in turn puts down her barrier, and they hit it off really quickly. To the point where they’re making plans to see a concert. Though, as you guessed correctly based on what this game is about, these plans are dashed as the virus has started spreading and the state this game takes place in is put into lockdown. Luckily, with technology and that they did exchange phone numbers, they can still talk and hang out through their screens. Giving us a look into how cute they are even when they’re apart, only seeing the highlights, as the weeks go on. And on. And on until the end of lockdown and being safe from catching the virus doesn’t seem so in sight anymore.I’ll stop here, as I don’t want to go into too much considering that this is a short game. Although, I will say that there are two different endings which is only determined by the last choice you’ll have. Depending on your choice, you’ll see how this relationship will end up and if it’ll survive or even continue when everything calms down.I’m a little bit disappointed in this title to be honest. I did know going in that it’ll most likely be a short little story, but I couldn’t help from desiring a little bit more. I would have loved to see more of Robin and Stephen’s relationship blooming, as it did feel like it was going a little too fast despite how well they hit it off the first day. Or perhaps even revisit the couples from the original game to see how they were doing and how they’d deal with navigating a relationship during the pandemic. However, this doesn’t mean it isn’t as charming. The art style is still cute as ever, we get to see a snapshot on what’s happening in this city after the original game as well as two new houses, get to know new characters both before the pandemic and how they changed due to it, the transition between both Robin and Stephen’s house was nice, and it still has interactions with various people and things you can opt to see (though, of course, not as much).I may have wanted more out of Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing, but it still has what made Half Past Fate as great as it was. It’s just that it’s a smaller game that focuses on one couple rather than multiple. It serves a purpose of telling how a rom-com possibly could go if plans were suddenly dashed due to lockdowns and it does it well. I’m also sure many people are going to relate as while there are people okay with seeing friends or loved ones through the screen, there are those that missed out on plans and hanging out in person. I’d recommend picking up Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing to anyone that loved Half Past Fate and has an hour to spare to complete this short side story nonetheless, but you're not missing much if you opt not to.

_childDocuments_.review: This was barely a game. It was about 30 minutes long and what feels like a half-finished story. _childDocuments_.review: I came across  a while back when randomly browsing for something a little different which might appeal to me, with no idea that there had been a predecessor, which does not appear to be available on Steam.After consigning it to the “huge backlog, I'll get to it whenever” pile, I finally found a chance to pick up something which would not take long to run through, and other reviewer play times told me that this was the game in my library which would fit the bill.Here we have the story of Stephen and Robin who meet at the start of the covid pandemic, and therefore, despite finding each other attractive and getting along very well, they are forced to try and build a relationship via electronic means at a distance.  As this game was released during the time of lockdowns, the question, surely, is does it still stand up as a relevant story and piece of entertainment now that it is no longer topical?We get to play the parts of both lead characters, who are depicted by controllable pixel-graphic sprites and also displayed as more detailed portraits during conversations which are presented in a visual novel format at the bottom of the screen.My initial reaction to finding that I had to move the characters about with either the WASD or arrow keys was one of horror.  No mouse control (or, in the case of a laptop, no trackpad) at all; which immediately felt clunky and uncomfortable, though I'd add that I'm used to playing VNs more than anything else, so this was simply unexpected rather than a real burden, and after getting over the surprise, it was pretty easy to adapt quickly.Every so often we get a choice of what the leads will say to each other, though the only really important choice comes last, leading us directly to one of two possible outcomes to the budding romance.- The narrative is beautifully written, creating believable characters in a realistic scenario which the huge majority of us will be able to relate to.- Keyboard controls, after originally throwing me, are pretty straightforward and also detailed from the menu.- Character movement is smooth and there are also resolution and other graphic options available.- Ideal short game for those one-free-session evenings.  - You can complete one ending, and upon returning to the start menu, select “Continue” to play  in order to see the alternative end.  No need to replay the whole story.- Zero mouse control, strictly keyboard only, non-adjustable.- Automatic saves only.  Due to the overall length, not a huge problem, but be aware, no manual save.- Text speed is auto-set and is slow.  Each caption can be forced to complete instantly by pressing the space bar, but this means you have to press space twice for every caption to move conversations along at an acceptable pace.  This is unnecessarily burdensome.To answer my earlier question, yes this is still an enjoyable ride along with a new relationship struggling to maintain during a period where the protagonists cannot share physical time together, and this is not diluted by the change in situation since the pandemic's threat subsided.The speed of text progress was a little irritating at times when I seemed to be space bar bashing just to get anywhere, but otherwise the storytelling held up well enough to make this an overall positive experience.My initial play through took 1.2 hours, then approximately another 10 minutes after making the other available final choice.  At a price (UK) of £4.79, this is quite cheap on a per-hour basis against any other form of entertainment; but when compared directly with its peers, it could be considered to be priced a touch on the high side.  I suspect most people who might enjoy this, would also feel less enamoured if purchased at full price.Nonetheless, if you enjoy easy going, well written, visual novel-esque role-play type romance story games, you're probably going to find this a satisfying hour or so of leisure time.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's short, but that's not a bad thing per se in my book. It only really makes sense to play this if you've played the original Half Past Fate, though - it expands on the world and pairs up two characters who were in the background, but visible. And it does it... adequately.I mean, let's not beat around the bush. It's not as good as the original. The charm of Half Past Fate came from the mixture of will-they-or-won't-they, weird shenanigans that the characters go through for a chance of romance, and general emotional warmth coming from the interconnectedness of all stories. Romantic distancing has only one element of that: the will-they-or-won't-they. And it's okay. There were two moments where I might've squealed a bit at the cuteness, but that's about it. Oh, and it ends way too early.If you ask me, the formula of Half Past Fate simply does not translate well to depicting an online romance. It's less about showing the contents of (arguably rather cute) zoom calls, and more about depicting two online lives that sort of come together; Chat logs, social media posts, games played together... anyone who's ever had a relationship like this knows what I'm talking about. And Romantic Distancing simply does none of these things.I'm still recommending it if you liked Half Past Fate, purely because it's, well, more of Half Past Fate, just a little different and somewhat less good. It's a snack at best, but I can think of plenty of worse ways to spend 40 minutes of your life.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original Half Past Fate this was an extremely fun little adventure that brought back some of the characters, sights, and themes from the main game. Although short the love story between Robin and Stephen feels authentic and relatable (especially with a lot of us still in lock down / quarantine). If you want to spend some more time in the world of Half Past Fate, or you just want to take an hour to absorb a cute little love story, definitely give Romantic Distancing a try!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who hasn't played the original Half Past Fate yet, but planning on it, I was a little disappointed in Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing. The game was really short and didn't really offer much on gameplay and story.The story is of Stephen and Robin, who meet at a computer repair shop when Stephen's laptop needs fixing. They find a lot of common interests and decide to plan a date to a live music show. Sadly their plans are halted because quarantine begins. The story continues on there with them doing dates through video chatting and having small hurdles along the way.The story is a great idea in theory, but they didn't really expand on it properly with the game. It was still enjoyable enough, but I wouldn't recommend the game, especially with the current price of it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you think it's like the other HLP game then I can tell you - ❥ Great graphics, cute story and lovely details.❥ A story-based game, not a lot of freedom of choice. ❥ Playing time: ~ 50 minIt tells a beautiful love story that tries to develop during the pandemic. It addresses problems, refers to safety and awarness, but shows the nice side too.A repesentation of what effort it takes, but also shows ideas on what you're able to do in order to get closer to someone even in a situation like this.Although the story could've been deeper and longer.❥ Would I recommend this game to you? Yes. It's a well made short game.❥

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played Half Past Fate (the original game), but I bought it because it was on sale and it looked cute af. It was really short (around an hr or so) but it really made me feel all the highs and lows of their relationship - a huge smile on my face in their sweetest moments and a pain in my stomach whenever they fought over the same fears we know so well during this awful year. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Half Past Fate (which I did enjoy), I decided to give this sequel-of-sorts a go. But to be completely honest, it feels unfinished and barely worth mentioning. I'd recommend Half Past Fate, but not this spin-off. It's EXTREMELY short, and I feel like it cuts off without offering any meaningful story or message. Robin's struggle with dating through a pandemic isn't explored and even their time apart isn't shown. Then they just... continue online dating anyway, and that's happily ever after? It really lacked meaning, to me.The ending was abrupt, I totally expected to see them on the other side of the pandemic tbh. There's also way less interactive elements, not even any achievements... You just watch a subpar story unfold for 30-40 minutes, and that's the whole game. I enjoy the characters but just wish there was more depth, overall. Nothing to do, no secret objectives, no achievements/easter eggs, seemingly no cameos or references to the original game (beyond asset re-use, I guess).
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing

_childDocuments_.review: Played this after the first Half Past Fate game and caught me off guard how short it is compared the first one. That aside, this spin-off features the same gorgeous art style, good writing, and down to earth and relatable characters. I recommend it if you've finished HPF and want to explore some other aspects of the world and get to know more characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Half Past Fate: Romantic Distancing

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Half Past Fate and absolutely adored it so it was obvious I'd cop this one as well. As everyone else, the game is fairly short. However, its an experience I still enjoyed. It was very bittersweet and as someone who dated online, dealt with heartbreak over circumstances that couldn't be controlled, I felt the feelings of the two characters on a personal level.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely breathtaking. The art-style, the colour choices, the music, the dialogue, everything about this game is so nice and so comforting. I played the game on stream and chat and I absolutely fell in love with this beautiful little game. It's not a long game, but the story definitely melts your heart. There is nothing to fault. The game design is seamless and my favourite part (aside from the music) was the way each scene transitions into the next, specifically when you walk into different rooms. This game was so beautiful and I'm so, SO thankful to the Devs for creating such a sweet little experience for us all to enjoy. 10/10 rubber chickens.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game with a small rebate (about 4$ US) ,i loved the subject,with everything going on right now,i decide to give it a shot.I find in easy to relate to Stephen(one of the caracter),also the SNES feel is great,music is nice...remind me of sone NES and SNES music,that bring's a lot of memories.It's not a dating sim per say,it's more like a story driven game.This game definitly deserve more attention.If you love story driven games,this is a nice 4 bucks who make you forget your miserable empty life like mine...The only downside,it's pretty short(just over 90 minutes) and there's not much of a replay value8/10

name: The Pathless
detailed_description: ARCHERY AND FALCONRY Become the Hunter, a master archer who travels to a mystical island to dispel a curse of darkness that grips the world. Soar through the air and forge a connection with your eagle companion. Perform fluid acrobatics and execute awesome trick shots with a unique archery system that allows effortless shooting while moving at high speeds. The Godslayer won’t rest until the world is destroyed. Your bond with your eagle and the fate of the world hang in the balance. EXPLORE AN OPEN WORLD With no map to guide you, shape your own path through ancient lands filled with secrets. Traverse lush meadows and snowy tundras, ascend mountaintops and glide over misty forests as you soar to new heights on the wings of your eagle. Discover the dark history of the island as you solve puzzles in ancient ruins and unearth long-forgotten lore. Peer through the veil of reality as you use your spirit sight to uncover the secrets of the past and find your path through this pathless land. FREE THE ANCESTRAL SPIRITS Giant corrupted spirits stalk their domains. Hunt them down with your trusty bow and a little help from your eagle companion-- but be cautious, or the Hunter could become the hunted. Engage in epic boss battles against the cursed beasts to restore light to the land. Dust yourself off and get ready to try again if you fail–The Pathless doesn’t punish you with permanent damage or death. AWARD WINNING SOUNDTRACK Immerse yourself in an interactive music system with one of the most expressive scores ever written by industry legend Austin Wintory. Featuring traditional Tuvan throat singing from the fabulous Alash Ensemble. Game Audio Network Guild Awards, 'Best Music for an Indie Game' Annual Game Music Awards, “Score of the Year, Traditional / Acoustic” Annual Game Music Awards, “Audio of the Year, In-Game Music” Annual Game Music Awards, “Audio of the Year, Main Theme” STUNNING LANDSCAPES Explore a beautiful and captivating world from the mind of Journey and ABZÛ visionary Matt Nava . In the ruins of an ancient civilization reclaimed by the wilds, verdant forests border massive cliff faces with snow-capped peaks. Navigate crumbling temples and towering spires in your quest to bring the light back to this cursed land. STORIED VOICE ACTING Set out to stop The Godslayer, voiced by Troy Baker ( The Last of Us, Arkham Origins, Bioshock Infinite ), as The Hunter, voiced by Laura Bailey ( The Legend of Vox Machina, Last of Us 2, Gears of War ).

_childDocuments_.review: For those who are running Linux and wondering whether to purchase. It is working flawlessly so far with Proton GE and Experimental. Playing with controller and keyboard. Zero issues so far.Only played for a short while, but if you loved ABZÛ, Flower, Journey, Gris, Rime, or AER Memories of Old, this game will not disappoint, and is absolutely gorgeous to look at. Speed running by shooting arrows around is truly unique and adds another layer of possibilities to the game, and it is tremendous fun by just gliding along the landscape, completely forgetting about your next destination and goal. Game-play wise definitely much faster than any of the aforementioned games. Cannot wait for the next Giant Squid offering.Edit: Finished the game, almost thirty hours of play time so far, zero issues or crashes with Proton under Linux. Really enjoyed the diverse boss fights, the connection with ABZÛ (super secret), and the extended ending. Hopefully there will be some DLC for this.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game.On one hand, the things it does well, it does VERY well. The movement is fluid and satisfying, the art style and environments are gorgeous, The boss fights are a spectacle, and of course the soundtrack is beautiful and the highlight of the game. Unfortunately, the game is let down somewhat by some pretty glaring flaws.First, the puzzles (which take up a significant chunk of gameplay) are rather repetitive and most if not all of them are braindead easy, making them more tedious than fun.Second, the navigation system SUCKS. Your only means of navigation is a pulse which puts a red glow on any unexplored points of interest. The problem is that this glow is both quite faint and doesn't show through terrain. I once spent a good 40 minutes searching for the last collectible in an area because it was tucked away in a corner where you couldn't see the glow.It's a decent game, but I can only recommend it if its on sale, and even then id think carefully about it.Hope this helps

_childDocuments_.review: For as serene and intriguing as The Pathless can be, the game was far less impactful and enjoyable than I had planned it to be.I love the idea of complex and diverse movement in open-world games. Whenever game's with expansive landscapes make traversal entertaining, it turns the world into one big skatepark and helps to justify the scale of the environment. The Pathless tries to apply this concept and manages to look stylish while doing so, yet the process feels terribly automated. Lock-on aiming cripples the level of involvement needed to cross vast distances. The speed at which you move doesn't change the fact that you're still primarily holding 'up' (and 'LT') and moving in straight lines. Wide-open fields do very little to challenge you and the game hardly ever demands or allows for creative movement.The major upgrades you receive are uninspiring stat boosts that lack a strong impact on the game. These moments of triumph were missed opportunities to introduce a new skill to master.  Essentially, the game’s beginning plays nearly identically to its end. This draining lack of evolution also applies to The Pathless' stereotypical adventure-game puzzles.The many puzzles of The Pathless have a severe quantity-over-quality issue. Even those found later in the game fail to surpass the basic limits of 'light the torches' or 'align the circles'. I was often disappointed to venture to an eye-catching landmark only to be greeted with another stale 'crates and buttons' problem. They’re overly-intuitive and no ingenuity is required to get the solution once you've scouted out all of the puzzle's required pieces. There's also a handful of mini-puzzles that are reused ad nauseam. If you've made it through a dungeon or two of any other adventure game before, you've probably played fifty percent of The Pathless.Aside from the art and music, The Pathless fails to distinguish itself. Very little happens to the game's feel from start to finish. In some ways, the game subverts the expectations of an open-world game yet it still stumbles into the genre's same old pitfalls. Excluding a map is bold, but the game still scatters dozens of meaningless side objectives into each area. Deepening the puzzles or expanding the movement could've saved the experience and the extent of what’s available comes off as restrained. The game seems afraid to innovate upon itself. It acts as if maintaining simplicity in its core is integral to its artistic tone. This is a scenario where avoiding 'game-y' progression for the sake of a mystical setting ended up undermining how well the game engages with the player.It doesn't feel right to say this much about a game with so much artistic appeal. The superb music that accompanies the journey carried the experience and occupied me during long trips. Views from the top of hills were worth more than whatever feeble extrinsic XP reward had been placed there. Boss fights offered bombastic scripted sequences that were a welcome and exciting contrast from the boredom of puzzles or gliding. For me, The Pathless was a private concert with some good screenshots and cinematic bosses sprinkled in. For you, The Pathless could be something more. Just remember to adjust your expectations based on how you feel about minimalistic open-worlds and recycled RPG puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔵The game is not optimized very well, so expect to use high TDP to hit consistent fps.To fix resolution problem change the "high DPI settings" of the game executable:- Find the game executable Pathless.exe on your system (manage > browse local files).- Right-click the executable, then select Properties.- Switch to the Compatibility tab and click on Change high DPI settings, under "Settings".- On the new window, under "High DPI scaling override", activate the checkbox: [✓].- Select Application from the dropdown menu and confirm with OK.- Click Apply, then OK on the Properties window.- Launch the game.Tested on: OnexPlayer Mini Pro 6800U
