_childDocuments_.review: Now, on to the review;The Pathless is, as I’ve said earlier, feels like Shadow of the Colossus, except the MC can run around, jump and fly very quickly, all rendered in the beautiful art style TGCompany is known for. It is not made by the same studio, but from what I’ve gathered some developers who left the original studio and found their new one. The game has unfortunately flew below everyone’s radar for years because it launched exclusively on PS5 & Epic Games Store, but has since late 2021 been made available on this storefront.In this game the gameplay follows a very simple but engaging iteration; you are thrown in the ruins of a lost civilization. You are provided with very basic visual cues and explanations on what happened. You play as the heroine, an adventurer with almost no background, who arrives on the shores of this destroyed world. The heroine is armed with nothing but a bow, and soon after she meets an eagle who will be her companion in this odyssey. Her bow, eagle and legs are so to speak the main gameplay vectors in the game.The heroine can run around the world at very, very fast speed. This dashing is limited by her stamina, but therein is one of the main interactions of the game; around the world are many talismans floating everywhere. You can aim and shoot these to restore some stamina and boost your dashing speed temporarily. This loop comes naturally and intuitively as you play, and makes for an exhilarating and impressive experience of fantasy, euphoria and wanderlust as the heroine strides with verve over vast steppes and plains provided that she will, with great constancy, hit the talismans along her path that will reinvigorate her. The camera is one of the things I love most about this game. It is very drawn a-back; the character is lost in the world. Yet there are no issues with readability or visual clarity; the game’s art style is built around bright, saturated hues that present everything with radiant clarity, combined with the heroine’s brightly coloured red suit. The eagle gives the heroine the ability to fly. It can carry her around the world. It can either glide (losing altitude over time) or flap (the equivalent of a mid-air jump). Its flaps are tied to the number of crystals you collect around the world. There are many optional collectibles around the world, often locked behind puzzles or exploration, that can upgrade the heroine and the eagle’s abilities.Shooting the bow consists of holding the button. The rectangle starts wide, but narrows over a short period of time until it is perfectly enclosed; at that point the arrow loosened will be guaranteed to find its mark. An arrow loosened too early will often stray in a wide arc around a target, without much confidence in a positive outcome.The Pathless’ world is huge and ethereally beautiful. Its great expanse will be made small by the heroine’s rapid strides and the eagle’s ability to carry her in its skies. There are 4 plateuas in the game, each with its respective guardian spirit taking shape in a fantastical animal form. Each spirit is corrupted, and roams its world, surrounded by a tornado-like inferno, resembling a mobile hurricane or a natural disaster that is visible from a long distance. Getting caught in this inferno before you have weakened the spirit by destroying the totems of the godslayer that corrupt the spirit will mean that you will have to undergo a small but intense encounter with the spirit, in which you must stealthily avoid moving its gaze and find your eagle - who is very skittish around the dark energy corrupting the world. These sections will remind those who played Journey of those levels in that game, in which you have to sneak past those large ribbons who will try to tear your cloth. After fulfilling some prerequisites (purifying the totems of the spirit in towers around its world), the spirit will immediately attempt to flee to a large structure in its world. There, reader, the hunt begins. You will embroil on an intense chase with the spirit, in which you will have to loosen your arrows repeatedly on its legs in order to bring about its downfall bring its retreat to heel. Once the spirit breaks its rout, a vicious battle culminates between the heroine and the spirit. You will have to time your dodges accordingly to avoid its attacks and hit its weak points. These battles are often intense and are the culmination of a long period of peaceful exploration. This is how the Pathless proceeds; a long silence, a shrill howl, much like Shadow of the Colossus. This will be repeated for 4 times until the final fight with the main enemy of the game; the one responsible for corrupting the lands and its spirits. Once a corrupted spirit is defeated, it will bestow you some of its power. The world in which it had inhabited will be restored to some of its former luster and purify the lands in which this spirit has once inhabited. As mentioned before, the worlds of the game are large. It does not feel tedious at all to traverse them thanks to the speed in which you are able to move and the ability of flight. I was inclined more than once to make the long trek from the highest, final world to the lowest one. The sense of wanderlust in this game is near unparalleled. Its world is empty of a liminal sense. There is no map, and there needs not be. Each plateau is finely designed. Almost every structure will have something. You will have to guide yourself by its landmarks and orienting yourself with your surroundings, those sorts who do not heed much attention to their surroundings will be lost here. There are some places you’d be surprised to know you can travel to. There is this one mountain shadowing the world, overlooking what seems to be the end of the world, sitting in the clouds. I noticed a castle at its crest. The journey to this mountain was an adventure of its own. After a long trek up the mountain, with some difficult platforming, I made it to the top and searched the ruins. Then I looked back down on the extreme distance from which I’ve climbed up. It is moments like those which cemented The Pathless as an unforgettable experience to me. The world is truly open. I have nothing to say yet on PC because I have not yet tried the game here, but on PS5 the game ran adequately well with a 60 FPS locked performance mode, and a 30 FPS native 4K mode which looked gorgeous. I have not ran into any glitches or bugs that I remember. The game is one of those, like Journey, which are not needy for hardware, but will captivate any eye that searches for beauty.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is an open-zone world with a cool movement mechanic. It's very well polished and has some Zelda-ish vibes going for it, but runs a little too long given the depth of the mechanics. My experience with the 2nd and 3rd zones felt almost identical to the 1st, and the puzzles begin to feel like busy work a little too quickly. The art is beautiful however and the story simple but atmospheric. The music pleasant but unmemorable.Overall I'd recommend this game to anyone looking for a short open-world action-adventure game. If you have already played BotW, A Short Hike, Journey, Abzu and Spider-man, this game may be a little less exciting, but given the care taken with its presentation, it's still worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: + Vibrant, stylized graphics that create a very immersive atmosphere+ Traversal and bow mechanics are fairly simple but fluid+ Pure raw exploration (no fast travel and no map)+ The eagle acts naturally and the interactions with it are adorable. You can also pet the eagle (whoa~!)+ The eagle can mimic your whistling pattern (use arrow keys to whistle. Hold to whistle longer)+ Many achievements to hunt AND an achievement about getting all other achievements (I love those)+ Many secrets and lore texts to find (world-building and lore is interesting as well)+ Camera movement is really well-made (you rarely have to fight the camera, if at all)+ I don't have enough words in my vocabulary to describe how magnificent and fitting the music is as a whole+ Unique and thrilling boss fights+ Has a perfect ending+/- Characters talk in a fictional language. I personally love this because the emotions behind the words are still there+/- It's a little hard to change direction or stop when sprinting (takes a little while to get used to the controls, but it's not a big deal)+/- No DRM or other bloatware (unless you count Steam, I guess)+/- There is no world map, but you don't really need it+/- Game is perfectly playable either with a controller or KB&M+/- You can't rebind controls (not a personal issue, but worth mentioning)+/- Minor graphical glitches (very rare)- It was an Epic Games Store exclusive for an entire year (originally released in 12th of November 2020)- Talismans sometimes drift and phase into solid objects (like trees or the ground), which makes them impossible to shoot- Graphics options can only be changed in the main menu (a bit of a hassle when you are trying to find what option is causing massive frame drops) and most options require a full restart of the game to change/apply- Effects are a gigantic performance hog on High and Ultra- Post Processing has obnoxious amounts of DoF on Ultra- Some finer details about specific mechanics are never explainedMSI GTX 1060 Gaming X 6 GBAMD Ryzen 5 2600X at 4.00 GHz16 GB DDR4 RAM at 2933 MHzEverything is cranked up to Ultra except Effects (which is at Low). Current settings yield 80 to 100 FPS without any significant or noticeable performance drops. Resolution is at 100%. Vertical Sync is OFF (not like I need it anyway, since no tearing). Post processing is at Low as well due to the obnoxious Depth of Field it introduces at higher settings (which makes EVERYTHING blurry if it's even remotely far).Mind that the game's graphical settings only have Low, High and Ultra options (for some reason).-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------You can always pet the eagle when you are bored/sad/whatever to cheer yourself up. You can also whistle at it to make it mimic you!I'm not against competition, but Epic Exclusivity is making things worse for the honest folk. I actually acquired a shady copy of this game like 8 months ago to test how the game is. Played a little and then patiently waited for it to get released on Steam, so I can buy it the day it gets re-released. Good thing I can wait. I waited like 8 years to play Journey on Steam, so 1 year is basically nothing when compared.I'm still wondering why Effects on Ultra cause such a huge performance drop. Maybe it's bosses' red dome that is present on the map to show where they are hanging around at (before you defeat it and cleanse it, of course).Just when you think you are fully done with a puzzle/section, you discover more lore text and/or more stuff to do, given that you return to it to investigate or explore further after solving the main puzzle.Spirit Vision lets you see more than unexplored areas. It also marks the ground you walked on, so you can tell if you have been in or near a monument before.If you are about to get caught by a red storm, you can actually go to the main menu and continue to prevent it. Honestly, it's fun for the first 5 times or so but gets stale fast, especially when the boss decides to move close enough to catch you. The only downside of this is the weather changing, so you might end up having less visibility if the weather rolls a storm.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless by Giant Squid tasks you, Usane "Soo-Nyung" Bolt, and your newfound eagle partner, with the herculean task of freeing the beast gods corrupted by "The Pathfinder", and in doing so, bringing light back to the region each beast god governs.Justifying the pricetag are the game's extraordinary setpieces and incredibly evocative score. The music firmly fits the scene of exploring the remains of the island-nation the game takes place on, as well as fighting tooth-and-claw with the bosses the game throws at you.The bosses really are a standout act I feel. A standard fight mainly consists of dodging attacks until you're presented with a juicy target in the form of a glowing red eyeball, but the build-up to the fight as well as the pacing of the fight itself is handled expertly. You spend your time in each region almost like prey, fleeing from objective to objective, weakening the beast so that you can strike back in gloriously cathartic fashion.The movement system seems promising at first, and is good, but could be great provided a bit more flexibility. If you don't plan your path two steps ahead you may see yourself face-planting into cliff-faces more often than you'd like.Shooting arrows works with an auto-targeting system so you can pay more attention to the environment, visuals, and avoiding obstacles, rather than hyperfocusing on striking an apple 100 meters away while moving at mach 5. I think the system could use some tweaking however, as I would often find the game not targeting what I expect it to target. For example, the game would often place priority on targets close to me, rather than one further away but almost in the center of my viewport. The game locks your orbit camera while charging an arrow as well, which feels quite awkward sometimes. Provided you hit what you wanted to hit though, the feedback is immediately satisfying. I don't think I ever tired of loosing an arrow into a talisman and the burst of speed that came with it.On the other side of the coin are the puzzles, which provide a relaxing contrast. Barring one featured puzzle in each region, the puzzles quickly get repetitive however. The overworld puzzles are similar in nature and solution to the Korok Seed puzzles in Breath of the Wild. I don't think there are so much that it will get tiresome though, even for a completionist. You will be rewarded for your efforts, and there are some pleasant surprises if you're curious when exploring the world.World building is done very well. A lot of detail is put into the lore surrounding each beast god and the relationship they had with the people. The messages of those people long-passed also provide a saddening lens to which you can piece together the recent history of this island and its tragic conflict.The Pathless would have been a standout favourite of mine if not for a couple of gripes I had with the gameplay mechanics. None-the-less, it is still an awesome title and a great step for Giant Squid that I hope a lot more people give a go!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Take Journey and Abzu, add a lot of rather simple, but mostly fun puzzles to a surprisingly big world, a very fun movement system and impressive and cinematic boss fights and you get The Pathless!Visuals: 10/10, nothing super realistic or with perfect physics, just beautiful as it isMusic and sound design: 10/10, music composed by Austin Wintory, who also made the music for Journey, Abzu, The Banner Saga trilogy, AC:Syndicate, Absolver and many more. Absolutely fantastic and epic when needed.Movement: 10/10, Sliding, gliding, flying, jumping and running is a pure joy with the "stamina" bar and the simple-to-use bow/arrow mechanicPuzzles: 9/10, they weren't overly complicated, so you likely won't be stuck for more than a couple minutes at any given puzzle. There could be a bit more variety, but they were still enjoyable and fun to solve. There are a lot of puzzles of various sizes scattered throughout the world.Story: 10/10, mysterious and cryptic and interesting, told only through ancient glyphs on tablets, the last thoughts of corpses that you can listen to and the environment itself.Combat: 9/10, non-existent for 90% of the game, but during the other 10% it's kept rather simple, yet very enjoyable and cinematic. There is a small part where you have to be stealthy and the boss fights offer a lot of fun at a rather easy difficulty (you'll likely only need a few tries max per boss). There are more than enough games with challenging combat out there, this one is accessible to even the biggest noobs while still offering solid entertainment to more experienced gamers in my opinion.Collectibles: 10/10, Next to puzzles another big part of the game. It's kept simple enough to not feel like work or tediousness and the spirit vision highlights points of interest and where you have and haven't been in a generous radius around you. There's no map or quest trackers, just go to a spot high up, look at your surroundings through spirit vision and keep relevant locations in mind. I'm rarely a completionist in games, but here I just felt like fully clearing every area and getting 100% in ~17h.You're also being rewarded for finding all the stuff in an area., which motivates you even more.Bonus points: You have an eagle as a companion and you can (and have to) pet it. You can also "tame" wild animals, so they'll follow you for a while. Pretty cool having a small armee of wolves running around with you.Conclusion: 9,7/10, If you want to explore a beautiful world with fluid movement and simple, but satisfying puzzles and combat to a fantastic soundtrack, buy this game. The price tag is a little steep for an indie game, but considering how much longer it is than e.g. Journey or Abzu and how smoothly it runs, I'd say it is worth it even without a sale. I bought it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game but really repetitive.Unless you're REALLY dedicated to 100%'ing games, I would definitely recommend playing through only the main portion of the game and avoid trying to collect and complete everything or it will certainly get stale.All of the following statements ring true if you avoid doing EVERYTHING:PROS:Fun and interesting main movement mechanicSolid advancement/progression for upgrading your movement and abilitiesBeautiful graphicsInteresting story set in an original universeCONS:The bosses can be annoying when they're roaming, forcing you into repetitive stealth encountersPuzzle diversity is lacking a bit (even worse when trying to 100%)Aiming at the correct object when there are many target-able things on screen can be fidgety.I would say, buy this on sale. This game is overall pretty solid, but I think the 40$ price point REALLY hammered this game down. It's just a liiiiiitttlleee too pricey for what it is. I would pay 20$ or less for this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It's very pretty and performance was great on my system. Running around the world is really fun and easily the best part, but most of the content disappointingly makes no use of the movement mechanics.The majority of the game is made up of basic "non-puzzles" that feel ripped out of the first dungeon of a 3D Zelda game. Find a bunch of torches, fire an arrow from one to the next until they're all lit. Carry a weight onto a button, fire an arrow through these loops to hit a switch, they're all the same.The first phase of each boss is great. They start with a chase sequence which makes good use of the traversal system, but the rest takes place in closed arenas where it slows to a crawl. You can't die during these so it results in a stale battle of attrition where you inevitably win regardless of how well you play.There's this red storm-cloud which moves around the map and will chase you if you get close, and running from this is tense and exciting, but getting caught forces you into a slow stealth section.A lot of the design decisions seem at odds with each other, and I think the main part of it is fact you can't die. If you're gonna make a game about fast paced movement, I don't wanna stop to solve puzzles and read lore every 2 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, The Legend of Journey: Breath of the BirdIt feels like a mix between Rime and Shadow of the Colossus.I really really love The Pathless. It's a little repetitive, but it's short and sweet, and I find the movement so satisfying and the world and bosses to be so well crafted. The game is so heart warming. The journey is amazing and the story is incredible and very beautiful. This game has a special place in my heart.I just beat the main story and I just have to say, this game is so much more than I expected. It is visually stunning both in its native mode and in its slightly lower res mode, and switching between the two is so quick and seamless. I enjoyed the Resolution mode for cutscenes and Performance for almost everything else. As a game, there’s nothing else quite like it. It definitely reminds me of BOTW but this game literally has no map, and no fast travel option. It is open world, kinda. The areas are kinda broken up but you can go back and forth to every area you've been to once you beat it. There’s basically no HUD either. It feels like such an immersive exploration game and it’s simply so fun to traverse.The story is great . If you've played games like Abzu, Rime or Journey, it has that kind of minimal storytelling vibe. Ultimately satisfying. I loved the rhythm/momentum based flow this game has non stop. It's so addictive and beautiful. The scenery is out of this world. The puzzles are thought provoking (sometimes not always) and they do a really good job! There’s some very excellent platforming based boss fights.It's around the 9 hour mark give or take, depending on if you have difficulty or not. Can be a lot shorter if you don't. It’s not super long because the traversal is fast but the game felt like a lot of content and it feels like a huge world. I highly recommend it if you enjoy puzzles and traversal, but not if you need combat and death in all of your games. There’s enough hate in the world. Enjoy this relaxing game as it is. Really don’t sleep on this game. People who ignore all indie games like this one unfortunately ignore a big part of what makes video games the best and most variable form of art and storytelling.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The Pathless is a very simple and relaxing game, bringing some fun into the relaxation hours. It's about 10 hours of content if you run all achievements, so I suggest picking it up on sale. 7/10, if you liked Abzu or Journey you'll like this.The Pathless is one of the most mindless games I've played in a while, but honestly that's a good thing here. The main appeal here is the fluid movement paired with the nice graphics. It's very easy to turn your brain off and have fun with this title. Assuming you take your time and explore rather than speedrun the ending, you'll get 10 hours here, and that's about a full week of relaxation time for me.The actual gameplay boils down to exploring beautiful scenery to try and stop a corruption. The boss fights are fine, maybe even a little too easy. No challenge will be presented here as it's more about the journey than the destination. This game may as well be the final piece in the spiritual trilogy alongside Journey and Abzu, and it fits the niche of calming exploration very well.The story is fine, nothing special. It has a simple and effective method of portraying the message, despite that message being a bit on the nose. The overall moral is true but when the moral is explained explicitly at the end it makes you wonder if the devs thought that it was able to be missed.My main issue with the game is the complete lack of innovation. If you liked Abzu, it's Abzu with a bow and running. If you liked Journey, it's Journey with a bow and running. Don't get me wrong here, I still think this is a game worth playing, just don't go in expecting to be blow away. I recommend picking this up while on sale as a 40 dollar price tag is a bit steep. I think 25 is fair and anything below that is a good deal.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and when I saw the trailer I was very excited, however when I played the game I didn't feel as if my expectations were at all met. The trailer seemed to advertise an interesting and innovative experience similar to Journey and Abzu, but in practice mostly just feels like the repetitive tower capture elements of Farcry with less steps and a cool art style. I personally played through the first area and was already getting bored as I neared the end of it, and as I made it to the second area I began to notice that the formula wasn't changing or evolving in any way. Basically, I don't think it's fair to charge $60 for this game when it feels like the first level has been copy-pasted four more times in order to extend the game and justify the price tag, and I honestly would not have bought it if I had realised what the gameplay would actually be. To be fair there are some occasional puzzles and small activities to engage with in the sparse environment but they aren't difficult or interesting enough on their own to warrant the effort to find them and complete them, and the small exp reward is far to meagre and feels kinda stingy. I did still enjoy my time with the game somewhat, but mostly for the first hour and a half, past that I started to quickly get bored.In my opinion it feels like the devs should have made a shorter game so they could have focused on making it more unique and fleshed out, rather than making a world that feels empty with repetitive and over-simplified challenges. TLDR beautiful art style and world, but main content is fairly repetitive and side content is kinda boring.

_childDocuments_.review: The first impressions of this game are about what you might expect, namely, another excellent product from Giant Squid — with much the same team behind them: Matt Nava, Austin Wintory, and others.  The game runs smooth (assuming you have sufficient specs), plays well with either KB&M or controller, and there are fairly flexible options should you, say, suffer from motion sickness or the like.  One small downside so far is that there is no place to rebind controls, but the default controls work well enough to let it slide....and now I have completed and nearly 100%ed the game.  There are influences abound, and you'll probably be reminded of something similar you saw or played.  For me, I saw similarities to Journey/ABZÛ (no surprise there at all), AER: Memories of Old, Bokida: Heartfelt Reunion, RiME, and even a touch of Samurai Jack; as well as lots of central and east Asian influences in the art and the music (which by the way features yo' boi Austin Wintory playing Bass Kazoo!  This, in addition to dozens of other exotic instruments: A Nyckelharpa, Xiao/Dizi (i.e. Chinese bamboo flutes), Taiko, frame drum, and the Alash ensemble!).As in Matt Nava's previous games, movement and speed are of the essence, and the more you interact with the game, the faster it will let you go.  In particular, the more secret stuff you find (and believe me, there's well over 50 of them), the more freely you can move (I don't want to spoil the exact mechanic, but it allows you to go higher).  Note that, unlike Journey and ABZÛ, you cannot meditate by sitting.  However if you stand still, the music will shift to accommodate that.The gameplay is simple: shoot the talismans to keep up your speed, and find stuff.  There are tougher bits in this game, but fear not, for this is not a game you can die in (again, like Journey and ABZÛ) — only get temporarily hurt.  No particularly fast reflexes are needed to have a comfortable experience.  There are also light puzzles that are easy to solve with their own little rewards.  All are present, yet not all are mandatory, allowing you the freedom to forge your own path.  After all, this game is not called "The Pathless" for nothing.  When there is no Path, you are free.  The game wants you to be free, to explore, to seek out its secrets, to hunt down its lore depicted in its departed spirits and steles.  There is no Path, but there is a path — your path.  Enjoy it at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: 80% of the time spent in the game is wandering around, finding, platforming, solving mini puzzles and collecting stuffs to unleash 3 towers in every map (there are 4 such maps). It gets pretty repetitive and boring even though the travel mechanism is unique and fun in general. I didn't enjoy doing this grind, unlike in some other games. There is no map or HUD, its a simple game focused on the experience. Story was fully predictable, but nice.The main highlights of the game are Boss fights, music, and visual. They all are good but Boss fights are great. In fact, every single fight in this game is a boss fight, total 5. There are no general enemies.If challenge is something you are looking for, this game will disappoint you since you can't die. Judge your purchase decision and price accordingly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless was a fun experience for a few hours, but the novelty wore off quickly and innovation stagnated in the middle of the game. If the game was streamlined to its best moments, it would be as good as ABZÛ, but as it is there is a lot of filler. The visuals and audio are beautiful, and when exploring areas and concepts that are novel that is where the game really shines. The boss fights, although easy, were fun spectacles, and you got to pet a cute bird. What is not to love about that?Unfortunately, the movement mechanics were shallow and the environments were nowhere near as diverse as they were in ABZÛ. This unfortunately made exploration a chore rather than something to be excited for. Ironically you spend a lot of time stuck to paths (else you are cursed to slow-walk your way to your destination)In each segment of the game, there is a mechanic involving darkness and corruption. In the first area, a dark circle randomly appears around the map and then moves slowly. If caught by this circle, you enter a stealth escape segment which can be pretty interesting for the first time. I was hoping the mechanic would change for each corrupted beast, but unfortunately it stayed the same throughout.The finale was very fun and a good ending to the game. I appreciated seeing an area very similar to a favourite of mine from ABZÛ during the final sequence. The boss fight had a fun moveset, but it was too lenient for my tastes.They say you should expect to pay $1 per hour of gametime to determine the worth of a game, but I got a lot more out of my 2 and a half hours in ABZÛ than 10+ hours in Pathless - I would rather the game have been condensed to its 2.5 hours of best moments rather than have all the padding!I really enjoyed ABZÛ, so I expected to really like this game. At first, it was a lot of fun, but the game was littered with so many pointless collectables that rehash the same mechanics and ideas over and over that I burnt out hard before finishing the game. I had to take a 10 month break before coming back and finishing. I wish I could give an "informational" review rather than "not recommended" because I think this game still has a lot of value for other people, but if you are like me and like to go in blind and try to complete everything - you may be in for a nasty burnout!If you haven't already, go play ABZÛ, and if you enjoy that game and still want to play The Pathless I urge you to do the bare minimum to progress so the game stays fresh the whole way through. Hopefully your experience will be better than mine!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a sort of middle recommend option, I would do that. The Pathless is a pretty cool game that I think some people will like or even love, but others will probably hate. I'll start off with the good things. The art design is beautiful, the areas you traverse are filled with history and sights. Its cool. The movement is great, you shoot your arrows at these booster things that boost you forward with speed, plus you have your bird you can fly with. You can also pet the bird. The scale of the boss fights are great, it feels huge and awesome. The whole thing is just really atmospheric and I think they nailed it.Now for what I don't like, and what will be a deal-breaker for most. As I said, the art design is pretty, but the whole point of the game is to bring the light back to the land that was taken over by evil; essentially meaning the whole world is a drab dark grey until after you clear the clouds, but after you clear it there is no incentive to stick around unless you want to 100% the game. That's not a huge deal though, it still looks cool even though it's a little drab. Another issue is that the movement isn't really utilized very well in my opinion. I don't think the mechanics are all that practical and in the end it just leaves you wanting more out of it. I still had fun with it, but it had potential to be much better if you ask me.Those things are whatever, they could have been better, but the real thing is the gameplay. I personally was not bothered by it too much considering that the game is on the shorter side, but along with the price tag... Let me explain. It's basically Far Cry gameplay, without the 20-40 hour playtime. what I mean by this is, in Far Cry, you go clear outposts, turn on radio towers, take the area, do it again. In The Pathless, you solve puzzles (fairly simple ones at that), activate the light towers, fight the boss, take the area, do it again. It has a few more steps to it but its basically the same. Again, the boss fights are cool and with the whole package, it didn't bother me all too much, but it is LITERALLY rinse and repeat gameplay. So yeah, that's kind of it. If I had paid the retail $40 I think I would be going a bit harder on this game but I got it on sale for $20. I think that is a perfect price. If you can buy The Pathless for somewhere around $20, you are okay with the simple repetitive gameplay and short playtime, and are interested in what it all has to offer, go for it. Otherwise I just would not recommend this to you. I enjoyed it though, so that's why I'm recommending and not giving it a thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: For a lot of multi-boss games the first boss is usually more impressive to encourage the player to continue the game. This game however is one of the fewer games that I've played, that each boss is unique. With that being said this game is incredible, the story line is rich, and enthralling. So much time and attention was put into this game and it truly shows. Fully clearing each plateau was extremely rewarding, and made me pay attention to a lot of the small details. The movement in this game is fluid and it becomes satisfying to zoom around the map. Not once was I disappointed with this game. I found it was hard to shut my computer off and go to bed each night. I HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone who loves adventures. This game is truly one of a kind, and is certainly a hidden gem on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Eyeball Conditions Hot-take:Who is this for? Folks who get vertigo from motion blur, hate glitch filters for good reason, can't physically handle some camera types, migraine conditions, muscular eye conditions, and all sorts of things that aren't epilepsy but do exist in the video game player world.Giving this a Preliminary: Ok Due to Granular Settings!Text in game: Scales well to resolution and uses a very legible sans-serif font. No straining to read what little there was to read in-game or menu text. They kept it simple and it works.Camera type: Third person, controller right stick controls the camera, speed is adjustable and follow "stickiness" is adjustable from Speedy to None. Is the Camera fast? So fast I'll puke? Hey you control this. My muscular eye condition doesn't handle fast follow and I used the "lazy" setting with gentle touches on right stick and I did not send myself into a fit of nausea. The controls are well tuned.Update: The game does encourage Moving quickly but that is focused on your character and I personally found this very grounding for the parkour-y elements that you can be doing at times. But there is more than one way to skin a cat and traverse the land without getting yourself motion sick I have found so far.3rd person but how far out? Pretty darn far out so far. Have not encountered enclosed areas but footage indicates the game is very Open Spaces conceptually so I don't expect Crash Zoom moments entering small building which plague 3rd person cameras in the modern era. Update: It does tighten at moments but never at an overly speedy crash zoom effect (esp with shake and blur off) and you want it to tighten during the dashing parts so your pov is wider. Honestly the tutorial island as I like to call it is a great place to test out this function and see if it makes you sick. I found it fun once I got used to it and my eyes were not straining to see but rather my brain was simply learning that dash mode as it has some tricks I won't spoil.Blur? Shakey? Motion Blur is actually a slider instead of on/off. Crazy. But yes, toggle it to zero and poof. Camera shake? Same deal. Check and check.  See above on how vital this is.Filter Removal? No "turn off eyeball melting filters" options but from the footage I made sure to check before even I purchased and the gameplay I tested so far... the game is beautiful and not trying to glitch effect or flash bomb our eyes. The aesthetic is very easy on the eyes and not going for realism or a vaporwave video. Watch some video yourself to make sure it isn't a strain trigger for your own specific conditions.Update: A mechanic I had NOT gotten to and is pretty key to this game is the ability to see 2nd reality/the veil/2nd plane of existence whatever you want to call it. It has 2 buttons dedicated to it, that is how important this mode is. (one toggle one hold) This vision mode with blur etc off mostly is a color tint with other objects revealed or made translucent. NOT A BIGGIE IF YOU ARE LOOKING BRIEFLY HEAD ON... BUT.....BUT... what IS A BIGGIE? There is a slight bending at the corners of the camera. Like a concave lens that was mostly flattened but all the edges are still a bit fish eye. This definitely gives me eyestrain/tweaks my muscular eye issues towards migraine land. So leaving this mode on persistently for me is a big nono.My best comparison for it is... The camera in Outer Wilds. Most people do not notice it has a fish eye curve all the way around it that bends plants, everything at about a 20% radius when you start the game. Made me heckin' sick to walk around. Couldn't play. Bummed.Am I pushing through this Veil Mode? Yes. How? Flipping it on briefly for short moments and looking straight at the middle on a big honking screen avoiding moving too much and seeing those curvey edges. Do I experience pain anyway after an hour of play? You betcha as an Alaskan once said. Will this be a gamebreaker for some eye conditions? OH YES IT WILL.Graphics in general? I tested on ultra and on very high. Granted, I have a medium-high end rig. The game held up well and gave me solid fps at 2k resolution and 120hz, no issues. No fps flutter or screen tear even without vsync. But some games can't even have stable frame rate even on a high end rig so kudos. Low end rigs Opinion Warning: The spec requirements and research shows this game allegedly can run on almost a tin can. I would not recommend that though because the high end settings are more the "as intended" game. You can play it on lower settings, but I think you will miss out on a big part of what makes this game compelling to me aka feast for the eyes. (ain't that funny) But seriously, this isnt a 50+ hour RTS. It is a 10-15 hour adventure. Visuals is a key factor.That is it on the eyeball hot take. I will update... oh here it is:Addendum because of my updates on 11/27: The veil mode and the bending edge camera is decidedly going to be painful for some eye conditions. I cannot judge until you experience it yourself. Or try and find some FULL SCREEN high fps footage of it with the edges and all the crap. As I like to say, muscular vs neuro we got a lot of different eye issues out there, your milage may vary. If you have suffered this entire eyeball hot take and you have a non-epilepsy eye condition that is sensitive to the things I talked about and you still want to try the game... you will get the mask that gives you the vision well before the steam 2 hour mark. You can try it, see if you puke, and request a refund.For me this game is super delightful... except that effin' camera filter in the Veil mode. Someone tell Annapurna to stop encouraging studios it publishes to stop curving their cameras. It ain't funny for our eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a third-person, semi-open world action game that has you playing as a lone archer fighting against an evil force corrupting the land. Together with your pet eagle, you must traverse multiple plateaus, fight massive beasts and uncover the secret history of how the world came to be the way it is.The game has an emotionally resonant story that follows a relatively simple structure, but the way it is delivered is at a really high standard. The interactions between the main character and God Slayer, the antagonist, are intense and really well-written. The God Slayer may be evil, but there's a bigger picture to his backstory that makes him a lot more nuanced.Like I said before, it's a semi-open world game. What I mean by that is that it's split into multiple zones or plateaus. Each one has its own objective, and you cannot progress to the next one until you have finished where you are. Nevertheless, each zone is filled with interesting locations and pieces of worldbuilding to get invested in.As for the gameplay, it's incredibly fast-paced. You move very quickly, making travelling quite satisfying sometimes. Using your bow and arrow, you can shoot at sigils which boost your speed and propel you forward. The boss fights were some of my favourite moments in the game thanks to their intensity and variety. There's plenty to like about The Pathless. My only major criticism is that it can feel repetitive. Looking past that, however, you have a really captivating experience that I can easily recommend to anyone.If you would like to see a more detailed version of this review, be sure to check out my video review for the game here:   (Game was gifted by a friend)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: At first the concept was interesting, running around and shooting the talismans to move, but after doing it for 3 hours and realizing that that's 90% of the game it feels a little stale.The concept of the game is run around, do very basic puzzles, fight boss, do that 4 times, fight one more boss. After defeating the 3rd boss, i thought I would get to the ending of the game, but it was revealed to me that there is a 4th spirit to aid, at which point i just gave up on the game not wanting to repeat the same running around and doing the mediocre puzzles. for another half of an hour or so.Furthermore, the optional puzzles which grant you more eagle flaps feel pointless, as never have i found myself in a situation where i thought to myself "I wish my eagle could take me even higher". In fact the majority of the game I spent on the ground and what I would have loved to see more is perhaps more movement speed buffs besides the one granted by that one spirit.It's not all bad however, the visuals are nice in general and it is a pretty charming game. The only visual aspect that I did not like was the boss fights which, while visually unique and very entertaining, relied too much on the color red to the point where it was sometimes confusing what's red because it's just red or what's red because it means danger. The aiming indicator is also red on red which made it unclear when it would pop-up. Overall I'd give the game a 6/10, but I would not recommend it due to it getting boring and repetitive down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't so impressed with The Pathless when I first began playing. Well worth picking up, and another home-run from Annapurna Interactive and Giant Squid.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game isn't a "total flop" or isn't worth playing at all, but I think it fails to deliver on so many fronts that it becomes disappointing, and some decisions within the game are outright baffling. For its full price I would really struggle to recommend this game. It's incredibly short (I've 100%ed it in 11 hours) which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I struggle to see how The Pathless can justify its price for such a short playtime coupled with its incredibly shallow story and repetitive puzzles (which is a hefty chunk of the game's content).The visuals are absolutely the game's most striking and defining feature and I applaud the style and scale. Reaching high places or finding hidden nooks and crannies felt personally rewarding as the visual spectacle was really nice. However, it's pretty meaningless when there's no substance within that world: sparse information about the world is drip-fed in textboxes that fail to create any intrigue and are ultimately pretty forgettable. The only interesting storyline in the game () is barely developed and in the climax of the game amounts to a pretty underwhelming and vapid exchange. There are no connections to be substantially made with any area or character in the game beyond looking pretty and it's super disappointing considering how much potential the story has. Given how the protagonist also barely has any motivations, development or characterisation herself, its pretty hard to get invested in such a surface-level story. The puzzles are fine but nothing deep or interesting, just a matter of looking for where a weight for a pressure plate is, or for what angle to shoot an arrow through a torch is, and it applies to pretty much every puzzle in the game (you'll be able to identify the "category" of puzzle pretty quickly). This didn't bother me personally but it didn't really invoke any "aha, I did it" or "man I'm stupid" feelings, it just feels like completing yet another puzzle for a stepping stone to clear the current area. The most baffling decision for me was the choice to stop playing the music in each plateau after you've cleansed them of the curse and beat the boss in each area. With little reason to explore the world already, no music just made it even worse, and I fail to see any reason why it shouldn't continue to play the music given how good it is (unless my game was bugged somehow?)I bought the game discounted and whilst I don't necessarily regret it, I just wish the game did more and spent more time properly developing its world, characters and setting so people can actually be invested beyond "game looks nice", and for its price it really needs more going for it than that, otherwise its basically just a sandbox to come back to that doesn't even play its fantastic music again when you beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love The Pathless.  It has a great art style, and I am sucker for bow games and a sucker for games where you have an animal pal, so it seemed like it was right in my wheelhouse.  The Pathless is a game where you explore an empty landscape looking to solve puzzles and fight bosses.The landscape is expansive.  You travel around by running or gliding.  You have a turbo meter, and regain it by shooting talismans that are dispersed around the world.  You can't really miss, as long as you hold fire down long enough to fully target the talisman.   There is also a skill shot, you can let go when the target meter is exactly halfway.  Sadly, having to have the talismans EVERYWHERE, so that travel isn't too much of a chore, ends up ruining the beauty of the landscape.  You have a bird pal, but all you really use it for is gliding and jumping.  As you progress through the game, you gain the ability to boost yourself in the air more and more using the bird.  As you gain more boosts, traversing the landscape vertically becomes trivial, and in a game with very little to do, taking away one of the few challenges is a negative.You see, in the Pathless there is very little to do.  You run across puzzles that when completed either let you:a.  Activate a toweror b.  Gain some points towards earning more bird boostsThats it.  There is nothing else to collect, no other upgrades, etc etc.  The puzzles are decent at best.  Most of the puzzles in the game are similar to one another and involve the same sorts of solutions.   Then, when you have activated enough towers in the region you are in you get to fight the boss.  The boss battles are very cool and pretty epic.  First you chase the boss while trying to shoot targets on its body while it flings fire at you in various ways.  Then it shifts to more of an arena battle, where you are dodging attacks and shooting targets.The game just never really excited me that much.  It is very nice looking, although much of that is ruined by the talismans everywhere, and by the fact that you frequently travel with "detective vision" on, because it is extremely difficult to find objectives without it.  By the end, the game because somewhat of a chore, and I had to force myself to finish it, just to finish it.  4/10

_childDocuments_.review: (2020) is my first serious contender for  I cannot remember the last time I had as much fun playing a game instead of just being entertained by it. Every individual element, from the music to the art, the animations to the character design, the sound effects to the level design, feels masterfully done by veteran professionals who love what they do. The gameplay feels so natural and fluid that you forget you are playing in a way I can most easily describe as magic.I tend to gravitate toward games whose worlds I want to live in and explore, and in that sense  offers almost unlimited access through its vast seasonal biomes. Except for the familiar towers with their birds-eye views of the sprawling hills around them, everything in the vibrant game world feels unique, with every excursion into its ruins worthwhile. Everything you do in the game world, from climbing massive ancient bones of a long dead beast to floating down a lazy river, feels meaningful. I was reminded many times of  (2019) and  (2017) in the shared sense of total player freedom.Behind the curtain a little bit, the experienced team at Giant Squid used impressive technical tricks to keep gameplay feeling smooth and even across all skill levels. Dynamic asset loading, zero explicit tutorials, no texture pop-ins, invisible target locking, quiet auto saving, thoughtful dynamic lighting, intelligent companion pathfinding, and an illusory "health" system are just some of the many thoughtful mechanics behind the scenes that yield space for the player to entirely immerse themselves with a confidence rarely found in other games.Despite all the systems working for it,  is sadly not a perfect game. Not allowing players to rebind controls is a giant no-no for accessibility, and the inevitable community demand for an option to disable the UI for a game made to be screenshotted show that even professional teams can still make obvious mistakes. I found some of the boss fights, forgiving as they were, to be overly complex and too difficult such that in a traditional game I would not have been able to complete them at all. Originally a year-long Epic exclusive, that the game has not seen a single update since releasing on Steam near the end of 2021 feels indicative of its future as Annapurna rarely makes changes to  games.I will continue looking forward to more from Giant Squid, whose work so far has proven reliable to surprise and delight.

_childDocuments_.review: i cannot emphasize enough how much i love this game. For bigger things: the boss fights are enthralling, with each one having unique elements about them. it's so much fun to run around, shootings the targets and just goin fast. The interactions with your bird are heartwarming too. pathfinding for your bird works really well, I can count on one hand when it got stuck, and even then it only took a few seconds for it get to me again. it has high replayability, what with how fun thr puzzles are and how many small details there are to find. the atmosphere, the ambiance, the sound design, and the art style, it's all wonderfully made.As for the smaller details i noticed. even the backs of mirrors are pretty. i like how your bird will sit on a corpse's head or on a weapon that brought an end to a life. the story's details can get heavy yet that small thing this bird does dampens the blow somehow. and i love running with animals.From the big important parts of gameplay to the small details in atmosphere, this game covers all the bases. it provides a relaxing experience with no health, no huge setbacks, and a relaxed pace. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that promises exploration, it sure doesn't really want you to explore. Everything to do on the map is in very obvious POIs either marked by glowing yellow or in the mask overlay. Everywhere else is just empty terrain. A big red storm will randomly teleport around the map and sometimes follow you, forcing you to be constantly looking over your shoulder to make sure it doesn't kill you. This seriously detracts from the exploration, making it very stressful. Sometimes the storm will just teleport on top of the place you were going to, so now you have to go somewhere else. Oh, and if it catches you, you lose a bunch of things you were collecting.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful game. Running and combat flows well, the story is lovely, and the world is vast and interesting with elements left up to your interpretation. You're rewarded for poking around in areas, and for observation. There are many optional puzzles and challenges you can logically work through. A small warning: there are some minor jump scares, if that's something that might bother you.My only criticisms:1. I think the game would be even stronger if there was less narration. The story was completely clear without it, which is a testament to the set pieces and animation. Hearing voices after an hour of ambient sounds, bird calls and monster music could be jarring at times. 2. The momentum can be a little fiddly. I never quite managed to do any of the butterfly challenges as I wasn't accurate enough. I seemed to overshoot constantly when doing a string of talisman jumps. This may well just be me lacking the finite skill for it, but I had a great time otherwise with movement so this was the outlier in my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: What initially drew me to this game was the art style. I loved the bold color choices and the "Breath of the Wild" vibe of the environments. Visually, I give this game an A+ in terms of style and execution.The story, however, is pretty basic. There’s a big bad guy destroying the world with his evil influence, and you have to stop him. Along the way, you save some "Gods" who are under his control. It’s nothing particularly remarkable in terms of plot.As for the gameplay, it’s fun but quickly becomes repetitive. Let me explain—with some minor spoilers to clarify the mechanics. (These spoilers won’t ruin the plot but will help illustrate the gameplay loop.)In conclusion, the game is enjoyable, but it could definitely be shorter and cheaper. The visuals are striking and help the game stand out, but I believe the base price is too high for what’s offered. I’d recommend picking it up during a sale, ideally in the $20–25 range, but it’s not worth paying much more than that.*Review edited for relevancy, clarity, and spelling.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played some of the other games by Giant Squid and ThatGameCompany then I definitely recommend this, not just because of the decent quality you can expect but also because of a fundamentally different experience that The Pathless is. Now while I wouldn't necessarily describe this game as phenomenal or innovative as potentially opposed to some of the other games, Each part is still decent and compelling. The story though executed through written text and speech is still gripping and filled with little nuances that add to the big picture. The level design, art style, landscape and atmosphere are all excellent. The actual gameplay is almost flawless, with a few questionable choices. You can adjust the sound unlike Abzu but you still can't really change much in the way of graphics, which could make gameplay a bit stuttery or slow on lower end platforms. Also in all of the boss fights the camera will automatically adjust and usually lock to a position at certain moments, which in some cases makes it hard to tell if that feature was meant to be useful. For example in the 3rd boss fight the camera locks when you're in the last phase which makes calculating your jumps needlessly hard. Aside from those small issues, definitely worth a test if it looks loike your thing, and definitely if you've played some of the other games I mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: This is so much fun, and would be even more without the boss battles. I've done the first one and it was very frustrating. I just like exploring, collecting, finding bits of the story and solving puzzles. The puzzles are fairly simple, just a question of figuring out the right order and/or finding the required items, which are nearby. And no timers, at least so far. In the second area, I realized I can move to the next area without doing the battle, so I guess that's what I'll be doing, and then handling the bosses last, if I feel like finishing the game. Although there are some extra abilities you get for clearing an entire area, so maybe the bosses would be worth it at this point (I'm in the third area). I paid around 9 euros for this on sale with an extra bundle discount as I already had Abzu, and I think that was a good price. Also, since I'm always complaining about it, no motion sickness at all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: In contrast to ,  is as top notch but has higher highs and lower lows for me.When you time it just right, the flow of shooting arrows and boosting continuously, feels uniquely satisfying. The transition from open world exploration to blood pumping boss chases to spectacular boss fights is amazingly effective and engrossing. It is waves more ambitious than ABZU while delivering the same if not higher caliber of gorgeous jaw dropping art style, direction and animations.But at the same time being a bigger game with a different structure it ended up with a few drawbacks:The basic running and gliding at times feel painfully slow (especially late game) but aren't precise enough for meticulous platforming.Biomes are differentiated with colorful flora and fauna and striking architecture but the non-linear structure doesn't make it easy understanding where you are in relation to the world (a map, even rudimentary one, with just one icon showing where the player is, would alleviate this). This isn't helped by the shorter than typical open worlds runtime of the game, which is a plus overall, but hasn't left me with a mental map of where which sights are or with a sense of place. I enjoyed the exploration but I did not enjoy getting lost multiple times.There are lots and lots of different types of puzzles, some of which might not land for everyone (like the sound puzzles that thankfully you don't need to do for 100%ing).Last little bit of personal annoyance is there is no Photo Mode.You can finish this in about 7-8 hours. 12-13 if you wanna 100% it, which wasn't as bad as I was expecting but definitely accentuated some of its problems.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a 'neutral' recommendation from me. Despite my downvote, there's nothing inherently wrong with the game. The game is responsive, the controls work just fine, the world is pretty and the story is good enough. Unfortunately it's just not very fun or engaging. The Pathless is an open exploration game with mild puzzle elements, a couple things to collect and some boss fights.The world is neat but a bit samey. Unlike most games where world-is-toy, The Pathless doesn't do a good job encouraging exploration and, instead, points the player at points of interest with a radar system and little else. Visual elements get mudded very easily since you're often in dense biome that shrouds all the points of interest (hence the radar system).After 4 hours, movement throughout the world had hardly evolved and is done mainly through dashing about and shooting respawning spirit targets to refresh your dash meter. This is kinda fun at first but becomes tedious and downright frustrating when you want to explore an area that doesn't have any/enough targets to refresh your sprint, just requiring you to walk until you get back on the main path. Its not engaging either and is mostly just holding down the fire button until one gets auto-targeted, then release the button to rinse and repeat at infinium.The puzzles are okay but nothing particularly challenging. There is only so much challenge that can be offered when everything in the world you can interact with highlights and auto-targets. Most puzzles were very obviously marked and telegraphed exactly what you needed to do so it was less problem solving and more going through the motions.Lastly; there doesn't seem to be a way to fail. You don’t seem to be able to die in the game and, at most, if you do something wrong the character just gets knocked to the side, you stand back up and just do the same action again only slightly better this time. It was particularly disappointing for the boss fight once I realized there was no consequence for failure. Whether I avoided the balls of fire slamming into my face or not didn’t really make any difference to the end result; with no incentive to do well or drawback for doing worse, the victory felt extremely hollow.That’s not to say it’s a bad game and you wouldn't be remiss for trying it. But its got so little depth and gameplay, I cant really  it persay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an action game. You have boss fights, but they are as the rest of the game: they test your timing, not your strategy. Most of the bosses can be brute-forced, because death doesn't exist in this game: most attacks only push you back a little. If that's your type of game, welcome, it's a really nice puzzle platformer!Mastering the movement was quite fun, although I wish there was more metroid-vania-like progress, where you can discover places only after getting more abilities. Most puzzles are easy and short, which makes it the ideal bite-sized game session after work, for me personally. In my opinion, it's not a deep lore masterpiece like Hollow Knight or Rain World, but I still enjoyed playing it, very much so. I'm going to get 100% achievements just for the sake of it, it's just that kind of game that you'd want to 100%.Things I didn't understand without the Internet:- you're not supposed to run into the storm, you stupid. It looks beautiful and all, but it's supposed to be scary. You can avoid the Tall One once you're caught within the Storm, but it won't get you anything (except for an achievement), so better avoid going into it.- the first ending is not the only ending, go and visit the boss arenas once again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a BEAUTIFUL game, much as Abzu is in its own way. The graphics are deliciously simple yet breathtaking, and the music is its own gorgeous set piece. The story is simple yet so profound and there seems to be a lot of lore in the game that you can find through the aura whispers and various lore stones.I can really recommend this game for those who enjoy the relaxation of simple enough puzzles and figuring out your own path in this beautiful game (just realised how apt that is! Nice one, Giant Squid). At some point I did feel a bit like it was much the same, but honestly, that faded so quickly with the game's story and music and gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I wishlisted this game after playing games Like Journey, Abzu, and Aer Memories of Old, all of which I have enjoyed immensely. The game does not disappoint. The game mechanics are smooth and easy to both use and understand, the gameplay is exactly as fast-paced as you would like to make it, and the boss fights are extremely fun and satisfying. Exploration of the world is also great, with ways for both slow and methodical, and fast players to scale obstacles, find collectibles, etc.I absolutely recommend this game, alongside the studio/publisher's full library.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: its .... quite boring sorry, i really really try to enjoy the game, but i truly couldn'tThe movement mechanics are really nice and simple, movement in general flows really well, the art and the environement is very nice (although if you already played games like ABZU and Journey, there isn't going to be much new for you)bosses are ........ very linear, i personnaly didn't liked it because i though that fights would be less linear and scripted, but i can see people enjoying fight against bossesnow for the main issue and problem ..... is it really an adventure exploration games ? because most of the time you will do puzzles, let me explainthe game loop goes like this :- you enter a zone, to access the boss you must activate X towers and to activate those towers you must gather X numbers of talisman, and to acquire those talisman you must find ruins and resolve puzzles- you wander, searching for ruins (aren't very hard to find, easy to navigate in the field, you just have to avoid the red cloud, even then it doesn't impact you as much as you think if you get caught)- you find the ruin, solve a basic ubisoft type puzzle- repeat the process until you have enough talismant to fight the boss, go to the next zone and repeat.If it isn't clear, the main mechanics of the game (movement, exploration) are quite secondary, puzzle, being the main activity since apart from puzzle ruins there is pretty much nothing to do .... and the puzzle are not interesting at all, its the AAA "we put a puzzle here to fill the void in our level design, otherwise the player will be bored" type of puzzles the kind that can get really annoying, its pretty devastating to see that the main mechanics (movement) are totally in desync with the main activities (puzzles), when i entered the third zone and the game asked me to do even more boring puzzle, i was done.overall there is quite a difference on how the game is presented and how it plays, if you have doubt about buying pathless but still want to play a fast paced game with striking environment, i would much rather recommend Solar Ash, its funny because it has very similar mechanics (in movement and explorations, not bow stuff tho) Solar Ash mechanics and activities work perfectly hands in hands, where pathless activities feel more like a desperate way to fill a void around the main game mechanics, quite sad.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Got all the achievement in the game just under 10 hours in one sitting. Reminds me of GRIS and the journey with less of a emotional story from GRIS and takes alot of the world building from games like the Journey. this game has more fluidity and movement which is fast and fun. Boss Fights are cool but not hard which leads to the game being easy, however the game is obviously design this way when you are playing it. with its Relaxing, engaging and fluid game design. id give this game a 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a clear evolution of the ABZU formula, and is an absolute joy to play. Make no mistake, this is an actual game whereas I would categorize ABZU as an experience, but not a game. Having said that, The Pathless proves that you do not need to have tons encounters or combat in order to create an enjoyable game. The puzzles are not terribly difficult, but they are fun. Exploration is effortless and showcases the world with a beautifully intuitive and simple control scheme. Story is interesting and well written without excessive monologues or cut scenes. Much of it is communicated through body language and historical notes found throughout the world.Make no mistake, there IS combat in the form of some pretty epic boss battles, on a scale similar to Shadow of the Colossus and Praey for the Gods. What I can say is, the combat is well done and just as intuitive as the movement/exploration system.Interestingly enough, there is no world map! Minimal HUD as well. However, there are ways to track where you've gone and what is left to explore. Honestly, it is so well done that I wish more games adopted a system like the one in The Pathless.I would recommend this to anyone that loves open world adventure games and wants to enjoy a game at their own pace without the need for grinding out endless battles to level up.It's a bit short, but what is there is very enjoyable and fleshed out. Runs smooth as butter on my 3700X and 6800.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Most developers don't get puzzle platformers right, particularly because they either get the platforming wrong, the controls wrong or the puzzle wrong. This is even more pronounced when you do a 3D platformer. Giant Squid however, got all the things right just enough to make something innovative and fun. What you get here are something of a cross between old-school Tomb Raider puzzle and exploration, coupled with racing-style traversal and chase sequences, as well as Shadow-Of-The-Colossus-Lite boss fights. And, Giant Squid has put just enough polish in all 3 aspects to make each of it a compelling part of the gameplay. The downside is, it doesn't offer the challenge of old-school Tomb Raider puzzle or it's depth of exploration, it doesn't quite capture the thrill of speed you get in (for example) Forza Horizon, and it doesn't capture the breathtaking spectacle and experience of defeating a boss in Shadow of the Colossus. But, The Pathless a definite proof of concept. And a very good one. Recommended. Let’s get the fundamentals out of the way. Graphics and artwork of The Pathless is minimalist but it looks good and the game runs well. The colors are vibrant and high contrast, with good use of light and shadow. The controls are also good; it’s got minimal jank, the camera work is also helpful and doesn’t get in the way of the player. The speed is addictive, making you want to always fill up your spirit bar. One criticism I have is that while jumping/gliding/dropping, there is an input delay and it can some times dampen the flow of your movement. The world is divided into what I believe is 5 stages, and there are huge. Lots of vertical and horizontal spaces to traverse which aids the thrill of speeding your way across the land. There is no map system or a overlay user interface, the game doesn’t lead or handhold you, rather you are left to discover and figure things out for yourself. This could’ve been bad but Giant Squid’s simple but thoughtful game design ensures that players are able to form reasonable deductions with simple observations. This is very old-school, and very rewarding and I can’t commend this enough. Puzzles are unsophisticated but again, because the game doesn’t handhold you, you’re left to figure out for yourself the nature of the puzzle and how to solve them like old-school Tomb Raider. You really get a sense of achievement when you solve these puzzles, and the reward for solving these puzzles is worthwhile. The boss fights  - which are the only combat in the game - are not dissimilar to many 3D platformer bosses, where they have multiple stages that you need to overcome. What’s great is that you get to use your movement mechanics to take down these bosses, including a chase sequence. There is no death in the game which I think works in the game’s favor and it doesn’t detract from the experience one bit. The lore and world-building is done well. Many writers of platformer games make the mistake of putting a lot of exposition which slows down the game play significantly. Here, Giant Squid wisely spaces out the lore throughout the map and in small concise anecdotes from the dead as well as monoliths. This allow players time to soak in savor the information, letting the players form their own opinion and thoughts regarding what is going on. This is how lore should be conveyed. A bonus point is that you get to pet an eagle. And petting the eagle is surprisingly endearing. Don’t get me wrong, each feature of The Pathless – the puzzle, the traversal and the boss fight - is good and done well enough. It does feel lacking however. The puzzles could have been more elaborate, the traversal controls could’ve been tighter and the boss fights could’ve been more epic. It is understandable though; the worse thing a game studio could do is to bite off more than it can chew and here, Giant Squid did just enough on all fronts to make The Pathless a solid game without any noticeable flaws. The Pathless is a good game. It falls just inches short of being an outstanding game. But we have here is evidence of great things to come. As it is, I have no problems recommending The Pathless for any Puzzle or 3D platformer players.
