_childDocuments_.review: Game is not exactly bad. It's a nice indie game, but I still give it a negative review over positive. Reasons are:- This game is too repetitive, I get bored after 30 minutes. - The tutorial is not clear enough, before explaining game objective, I feel extremely frustrating with the cliff in the beginning area.- Price is too high, even with 50% discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The design philosophy here is really great! The point of the game is to run around an island doing puzzles and purifying corrupted areas so the dev team went out of their way to make the system of travel from A to B as enjoyable as possible. A simple or slightly challenging (skillshots) timing system is used to increase and maintain high speed while running through the plateaus. Great atmospherics and music also make the travel from A to B feel like a proper journey in real life; You don't feel like you're pointlessly wasting time until the next actual piece of content. The content and meat of the game is all around you! Time spent travelling feels well spent.The puzzles are generally simple, but still fun and challenging just as in games such as Breath of the Wild. I found the plot and the in-game lore pieces to be quite interesting to read and uncover. The story's not revolutionary, but is still well executed. The red cloud can get annoying at times, but creates great in-game moments where the devs can repeatedly produce flow-state while you try and run away. This adds another side to the movement system. The boss-fights can be hit or miss, but I can assure you the final fight is properly epic.I would recommend buying on sale though; I would probably pay $25 or slightly more for this title which I suppose is a big statement because I'm quite stingy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked interesting and relaxing up on first glance on the store. I finally picked it up and immediately got the biggest smile after hearing the arrow sound effects, and figuring out the stamina mechanics(shooting the tailismens give you stamina back and a burst of speed). It does not take long to get sucked into this game, and it's very well made, reminds me a lot of how older adventure games were structured out, you have your starting area, then multiple progressively more difficult levels or areas, and then the final boss area. Plenty of collectibles or upgrades scattered about too. This game is so simple but so much fun as well! It's definitely an A+ from me and I just got to the first real level/area outside what you would call the tutorial. If a game makes that big of an impression on you THAT early, you know it's worth every cent!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is superb when measured by virtually every metric. Well, except for length. But you know what they say, size doesn't matter. Despite only taking about 6 hours to complete, The Pathless finds a way to be impactful. The game achieves this primarily through its atmosphere. It just oozes beauty. Every pan of the camera and note of music fills the player with that hard-to-describe "wow" feeling. I found a few mechanics slightly mundane but was captivated by the surprisingly rich story and satisfying movement system. I highly recommend The Pathless.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely gorgeous game; the aesthetics, music, and world-building are simply fantastic.Unfortunately, the gameplay just doesn't live up to the excellent presentation. The gameplay consists of nothing more than tedious token-finding and puzzle-solving. The only other thing you do is even worse: poorly designed encounters with bosses (where you have to avoid being seen) and utterly obnoxious boss fights that are either too easy or too hard.For most of the game, the beautiful environments were enough to make up for the intrinsically lackluster gameplay, but after a while, I realized that I just wasn't enjoying the ride anymore. The story was good enough that it motivated me to keep going to see the ending...but I can just watch that online without suffering through a game that I don't actually enjoy playing.EDIT: Wow, just looked it up and it turns out that the game doesn't even have a satisfying ending. You just get a split-second cutscene after the final boss fight, and that's it. If you get *every single item in the game* (every light stone and every spiritual gift), you get an extra 5 seconds after the credits.(sigh)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Journey and ABZU, this game was a letdown for me in many ways:-This game lacks the artistic approach to game design found in the previous games. It doesn't possess the same "beautiful" aesthetic as Journey and ABZU. Instead, it is just a generic game where the story is conveyed through basic dialogues, opposed to the abstract storytelling of the earlier titles. -The gameplay is EXTREMELY repetitive. I believe this is the game's primary issue. If it were a 2-hour game, it might offer a better experience, but Giant Squid decided to add unnecessary hours to the game by forcing the player to engage in tedious walks and fights and stretching the gameplay to 6 hours.- The "Boss Fights" are plain boring."The "Puzzles" are excessively easy. If you're making puzzles this simple, why not remove them entirely? Every puzzle feels like a speedbump where the game is just forcing you to wait.The Good:+ The Talisman/Speedbost mechanic makes running quite fun. + The music. Just don't expect Journey level of emotions.If you're looking for a game similar to Journey and ABZU, this is NOT the game for you. However, if you're looking for a chill game, it might be a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game gives me the impression that it was a labour of love, and clearly means a lot to its developers.I loved the story, and the bond you build between you and your bird. I'm trying to seek out the last few achievements, but I am genuinely sad to have finished the game. I'll now have to play it again on my tablet. ;)Despite its high quality, I feel that because it's not a particularly long game it should be cheaper. Perhaps the £15-20 mark? Worth a play though, but perhaps grab it on a sale if you can.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I need to preface this review by saying that on Steam deck, this game's performance is not great. Only sometimes was I able to to get a consisent 30 fps, but most times the game played at 25 fps or lower. I don't know the same can be said on a regular gaming PC. Overall, this game was decent, i think it is the weakest of the games in the lineage of Flower, Journey, and Abzu. While adding the unique movement and pseudo combat of bow & arrow = run fast was novel, I didn't find the world design or art direction to be as inspiring as the studio's (or devs for that matter) previous works. I also thought the theme of "there is no one way truth" to be silly and not really represented well by the game itself. I did like the spectacle of the boss battles, though. Those were pretty cool. Overall, I can't recommend this game on steam deck, but if you have a decent pc it might be a fun and quick experience to pass the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Pathless is in some regards a fairly pretty game, but there is just far too much Less and not enough Path. There is no map, no quest log, and while the game thus goes 'exploration!' the end result is just tedious. The environments are very similar, and the only true landmarks are the gigantic pillars you need to cleanse - all of which look identical. While there are ruins and cliffs and puzzles to solve, most of those are up on cliffs, and the game loves painting everything in the environment in the same dark colours.Sure, those same dark colours help make the "locate towers" button's thing about highlighting all landmarks in yellow more easy to see, but in turn makes traversal more difficult than it needs to be. And, between the difficulties of controlling the Hunter for the more precise platforming segments, the focus on shooting talismans to maintain speed, and the inability to actually see where you're going thank to the terrain, Pathless ends up committing the gaming sin of just not being fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I would just like to say that I'm completely speechless. I really enjoyed the story. It was both relaxing and action-packed story. The art style of this game is just.. wow. It's more like a cartoon rather that something realistic, but that is the magic of it. Most of the time, when I was exploring this world I've felt like I was running in those mountains and I could almost feel the air whistling around me. The atmosphere of this game just completely drew me in and I couldn't resist. If you have option to spare some euros, just do yourself a favor and buy this game, so you could experience it as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Pathless is satisfactory rehash of the Breath of the Wild formula:    -Chill exploration (adding some interesting new takes on world traversal that make it perhaps more engaging).    -Finding collectibles to increase your power (directly related to your ability to traverse the terrain, no new weapons).   -Occasional puzzles and boss battles (which are, admitedly, on the very easy side, you can't die in this game).   -True and tested (and boring) story of good versus evil, with cool stylized visuals for both the protagonist and antagonists.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe this game in one word it would be "Simple". The core mechanics are quite simple to get a grasp of, the puzzles are pretty simple, gameplay loop is simple and overall quite a simplistic experience.Yes the game is pretty simple but that doesn't mean it's a bad thing. Visual presentation & the soundtrack are beautifully executed & go extremely well with each other in creating an enthralling experience. The movement is the best thing about it. What starts of as a simple shoot the talismans to gain speed boosts soon turns into combining all your aerial & ground mobility options to zip around the map and it is here where the game is at is best, just zipping around from here to there. Puzzles are plentiful and are not that difficult, this game encourages plenty of exploration as you have to collect lightstones to progress, lanterns for upgrading your eagly & messages to discover the lore (Also for achievements). Combat is extremely sparse and is only during boss fights. The boss fights all have two phases the first is an excellent chase sequence where you have to utilize all your movement options to chase the boss and deal damage while avoiding their attacks and the second the fight is in a more closed space which plays out more slow. Each boss has a unique feel to them but ultimately has a similar pattern to them. The story starts of slow and intriguing, you get bits and pieces here & there and ultimately has a very satisfying ending.My only gripes with game is that the mobility which is fantastic is not really implemented on other areas of the game aside from exploration. For example, during the first phase of the boss fights you're using your mobility options to chase down and deal damage to the boss which is fun and fantastic but then in the second phase you come to a screeching halt and play it out like any regular platformer, you jump,run, avoid attacks & hit the boss when they're vulnerable. Would've much prefer if the first phase was more expanded upon. Moreover, the puzzles also slow you down where you shoot from different angles to light or hit objects to solve the puzzle. Would've liked to see puzzles which utilize this game's fantastic movement options. The worst part about this game is probably the stealth sections where you are limited to slowly moving around. This can be avoided and I get that it is meant to be avoided but  firstly it could've been made more exciting and secondly the clouds sometimes pop out of nowhere forcing you to enter stealth sections.Overall, despite the simplistic nature there is something addictive about this game and I have enjoyed it a lot. From the interesting story, satisfying although a little repetitive gameplay loop and fantastic video & audio presentation. Definitely a slow burn in the beginning & probably not for everyone but I can wholeheartedly recommend everyone to at least give this a shot despite it's flaws, who knows you might enjoy it more than you expect like I have.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most concise and well executed movement and open world design in any game i've ever played. Every aspect of this game is in service of eachother. Exploration makes movement better and movement makes exploration better. Art direction, music, sound design, graphics, story, atmosphere, it's all 10/10. My only criticism of the game is the fact that i can't fight the bosses again unless i boot up an old save-file. which is more of a compliment than anything. This game is seriously underappreciated and underdiscussed
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Pathless is a pretty unique game in my opinion, it has a very distinct gameplay loop that I don't think I've experienced before, the environment is beautiful and varied, the sound is satisfying (especially the whistling sound of the arrows), the music is fitting and the whole game feels like a fairy tale come to life, albeit a slightly childish one but still decently amusing. I don't have much to really say about the story, however I can state that exploring/platforming felt smooth, some of the puzzles were decent and the bosses looked and felt epic. On the other hand, I do think the game lacks the variety and creativity a little bit with the puzzles. I think it started to feel a little stale after first couple of portions of the game, it would have benefited the game much more if there had been more unique puzzles (unique to the appropriate area, relevant to style, location and context). I also think it's quite jarring how the game is not really handholdy but for some reason the boss fight are, and extremely so which means there is no sense of reward for beating them really. And I also think the "storm" mechanic or the general danger of every zone should have been different and that would have made each of the locations more interesting.Overall, I think Pathless is some decent fun but it definitely gets repetitive, especially near the end. Therefore, I would understand if people were to dislike this game, however I personally had quite some fun with the game and most importantly due to its traversal mechanics so I am going to give this a thumbs up. Get this game on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: it's like somebody played Breath Of The Wild, stripped it down to just the elements that made it compelling, built a concept around those and then rendered it in the most beautiful color pallettes you've ever seen. Highly highly recommend for any fans of exploration, secrets, dead worlds, Beasts and the power of friendship - Do be aware though, that much like Abzu this is definitely an ART GAME. It's telling you a story and showing you a beautiful world to accompany it. There's enough problem-solving in its' puzzles and excitement in its' boss sequences to feel like you're playing a game, but if you're looking for something to truly challenge you, innovate on itself or offer opportunities for creativity and out-of-the-box thinking, you may be happier playing something else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, it feels like someone took the things I liked about breath of the wild and made a more focused experience about them.It really is all about exploration, the world is vast and as you make your way around it you'll find places holding simple puzzles which reward you with emblems that allow you to unlock the next areas. Traversal is fast and fun which really helps with the usual boredom of moving across an open world (you go faster by hitting targets scattered across the map). The game also has overall straight amazing presentation (which was to be expected from the abzu devs) with epic spectacle bosses, great mongolian soundtrack and while the story is kept simple it still gets good emotional moments especially since it does such a great job of making you connect with your eagle companion (game has actual petting mechanics).My only gripe with it really is that the puzzles can get pretty repetitive after a while, and I imagine that would be even worse if you go for 100% (although I believe the game isn't intended at all for that). Also the price tag seems a little high for a game that takes about ~6 hours to finish, so grab it on sale if you can.I had a lot of fun with it and recommend it to pretty much anyone as long as you like open world exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Another amazing game from Giant Squid! At first, the area felt a bit overwhelming because there was so much to do everywhere and I wasn't sure where to start...but little by little, I got more used to the flow and just took my time exploring the area. The building puzzles weren't too hard, but spotting environmental puzzles was even harder, which I liked. There were even some that made go "Ha, smart."I liked the story, and the cinematography behind it was a real highlight for me. Every cutscene perfectly laid out, wallpaper material! Actually, everywhere you look is beautiful since the game shares a similar art style to Abzu. Bosses were another highlight, every fight was very invigorating and cool. Nimue/Snake god boss and her whole plateau was probably one of my favorites.Some downsides, besides overwhelming map (but this is subjective), were that sometimes arrows wouldn't recognize the targets, even when standing right next to one. But for some reason, I only had that problem in the first big area. Dense tree areas can be a bit too dark for exploration if you haven't cleansed the area yet. Lastly, the game can feel short and a bit pricey for an open-world game if you only follow the main objective. So, I recommend waiting for the sale.And if you're buying this game mostly for the eagle, that's valid too. Either way, 11/10 birbs from me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game so charming and beautiful that I purchased it twice (PlayStation 5 & Steam). It implements a mechanic where you run and shoot targets and you pick up speed as you hit consecutive targets. The main objective is to cleanse the land of evil. My only regret is that the game is relatively short. It also gets a tad repetitive, but because the game is short, you don't really notice. If you are looking for an easy and relaxing game, "look no further fella, you found him."
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I first played this game on PlayStation and when I found out it was getting a Steam release I wasted no time in buying it a second time. A beautiful game with a richly detailed, expansive open world, filled with secrets and lore, accompanied by a fantastic score by Austin Wintory. The Eagle companion is adorable as all hell and the bond between it and the Hunter is really sweet and makes the game truly compelling. Please give this game a chance, it's really good. We need more open world games that encourage exploration and taking your time rather than just completing tasks/side quests.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning designs from its environment to architecture to characters. The game doesn't complicate things for you but it has it's own challenges, which are easy to pass through. It's one of those games where you'd like to take a break from games with long playtimes and enjoy a solid <10 hours of gameplay.Annapurna is really nailing it by publishing these games, and let's not forget the amazing work of the development team at Giant Squid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this game, unless you don't mind running around solving puzzles. I got around half way through the game before i just didn't care about finishing it.The puzzles are not that difficult, but it gets tedious at times, having to do 2 puzzles for each tower. It's just not my kind of game, just gets boring. If you do like solving puzzles go for it. It's not a bad game, i just prefer to play something other than this.If you have played the game, and you enjoyed it, good for you, i'm glad you did.Maybe i'll come back for it later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a formidable journey through beautiful and well-crafted environments, sublime landscapes, under an hypnotic music.It has poetry, it has mystery, it has charm and melody.I especially enjoyed the boss battles and the multitude of hidden yellow gems that you can unlock through various environmental puzzles. The game could be a bit more difficult, though that is not specifically the point.It was a complete and intense experience that I cannot recommend enough if you enjoy small open-worlds and exploration.Thank you for this.P.S: You can pet the eagle. I spent 30 min doing so, the first time. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it very much. I'm pretty garbage at platforming, yet the puzzles weren't too frustrating. Navigating and traveling around the maps was a joy with the music and scenery. Pacing was good and it didn't feel repetitive at all even after getting all the animal light token thingies.Sometimes it gets difficult to see the callouts in a boss fight when everything is on fire. White and red flashing on orange. Might be a problem for some people to see. Not sure if there's color settings.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a very good game for people who like to explore. The environments are huge with lots of verticality, the platforming and action elements are light and not too hard, and the puzzles are not very hard either, but do require paying keen attention to the environment around you, which is perfect in my book.There's no map, but you can switch into a radar-like view where ruins/structures/places with things left to do glow red against a cool blue. This gives a great overview that's still grounded in looking at the world itself. And the red glows aren't necessarily visible if obscured by a hill or structure, so you still have to move around and try to get to high places to be able to spot everything. I think this strikes a great balance that supports the focus on exploration without making it unmanageable to find things.The primary weakness of the game is a lack of variety in the environments. The game has four major areas and the three first felt virtually the same to me, apart from the trees being red in the second and the grass being yellow in the third. The things you have to do in the four areas also follow the exact same formula each time. That said, the environments are beautiful, and each area is filled with interesting ruins and structures, many of which are quite unique, so the moment to moment gameplay kept being engaging to me. Add to that that your abilities to run fast and fly high gradually get stronger and the later environments are tailored to that.Progressing the story requires solving less than half the puzzles in each area, but this is one of the rare games where I felt like doing them all (which also grants minor extra abilities). If you like exploration, chances are good you'll enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game is absolutely gorgeous. Giant Squid has stepped up their environment creation and design while still holding onto their signature look, with several nods to ABZU throughout. The story is nothing super innovative but it is done well, and it can easily be pieced together with a bit of exploring. You can pet the eagle, so really that makes up for everything. The music is by Austin Wintory, and so it is phenomenal. Need I say more?Yes, the main gameplay loop is rather repetitive. If it's your cup of tea, there are collectibles that reward you with upgrades should you find them all. Otherwise, it's a "collect seal, break barrier, defeat boss, rinse, repeat" sort of deal. However, in my opinion this isn't a terrible thing for this game. Had GS tried to shoehorn in a bunch of other mechanics to try and fluff it out, there would be half-dangling strings of ideas left everywhere with no conclusion. The way the game is, is concise with a main mechanic that it does really well. The bosses are what really shines. Each has a common theme between them, but they are all still unique in ways that keeps each section engaging and force you to pay attention lest you be caught unawares. The auto-targeting system is very intuitive and quick to allow for that build-up of speed. The only issues I seemed to run across was my character not wanting to fire her bow from time to time. If I was in a rhythm it didn't seem to crop up, but if I was knocked out of it sometimes the Hunter would simply refuse to fire for a few seconds. Nothing major, but it did get irritating in those little in-between moments. I did manage to sequence break this game, despite it being "open-world". I had traveled up the side of the mountain (in a way I apparently was very much not supposed to do), and accidentally came back down onto the wrong plateau. I was summarily accosted by a boss I had not triggered any cutscenes for, nor ever encountered before. I then had to reload a previous save, losing about 15 minutes of progress, to be able to return to the correct plateau that I had not been able to find in my panic. So do be aware that it can be quite easy to make the game go squirrel-y if you explore a bit to well.Overall, the game seems to be optimized really well and that's with the highest visual settings on. The only lag I ever noticed was during the transitions into cutscenes, never during the gameplay which is a plus given how much speed you can gather and how fast-paced the boss fights can become. It took a little under 12 hours to 100% the game, so it's a nice little adventure. Is it $40 grade? Not so much. However, if you can catch it in a sale I would definitely recommend you pick up this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love The Pathless. I really like Giant Squid games and I had a surreal and almost religious experience with their previous game, Abzu. It was breathtaking and very memorable. When I saw some of the art style and the same magic in trailers and reviews for The Pathless, I couldn't wait to get my hands on it. I watched countless of videos about it, trailers, and read all of the positive reviews about it. I knew for a fact that I would love it. ... and, then I didn't. This game was nowhere near as memorable as previous games by this developer. The diamond shapes littering the beautiful and lush scenery take you out of the immersion. It somehow started reminding me of games that I would play in the early days of elementary school, where I would get rewarded for correctly pressing on a shape or number. The reward in this case is a stackable boost of stamina that would allow you to move faster, but... that's it. The bird is a cute touch, and as others have pointed out, you do get to pet it. However, I found that this game had very little going for it. The music wasn't very memorable and neither were the puzzles. The puzzles were somewhat tedious and very similar to one another. It felt as though you had no real goal. I didn't feel much of a connection with the protagonist. I was going through the motions of shooting the comically out of place diamond shapes to gain stamina, and I solved very pedestrian puzzles which were all so similar to one another, but I didn't feel a motivational force to keep me doing these things or going on. With Abzu, for example, I was so enamored with it that I finished it in one sitting years ago and I still dwell on how lovely this was. This, on the other hand, I didn't find memorable or captivating. Even when I was finding myself slightly captivated by the scenery, those cut and pasted looking diamond shapes are there to make me feel as though I am playing a game that perhaps my ten year old self might have appreciated slightly more. All in all, I wish that I loved it but I never warmed up to it. This should have been exactly my cup of tea but it was far from it.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like somewhere between this, Sable and Outer Wilds, there exists a "perfect" rendition of this formula and narrative, but that isn't to say the game isn't good. It's fun, the art style is fantastic and the gameplay feels smooth. Austin Wintory nails the score just like he did on Journey. Loved the choice to opt for timing based movement and combat versus aim. Definitely would've made shooting talisman a little more annoying ha.That said, this is an open world game and while that inherently doesn't have to be a bad thing, Indeed, players can enjoy the fact there is no map, no markers no quest log, no npcs dishing out fetch quests etc. As an Outer Wilds... fanatic (I did see that Kelsey Beachum did some narrative work on this, something that made total sense given how non linear all was), of course I want more games to be like this so, of course, this is a massive plus. However. Each plateau doesn't innovate and build enough on the existing formula. I don't feel like I'm making progress beyond the change in biome and landscape, which for the first three are mostly all flat anyway. The puzzles do get a little more tricky but I would've appreciated less, more complex puzzles as opposed to checking off the same nine locations in exchange for an extra ability. Getting to the third one really made me wonder if I was treading water, as opposed to making progress. Each level has 3 obelisks, there's some lore strewn about but none of it really impacts your play - in Outer Wilds, your understanding of the universe is what powers your exploration and puzzle solving. Here it's a side of greens, healthy, but overlooked by most as the game doesn't need you to understand any of it if you don't want to. A missed opportunity perhaps, seeing as the movement really allows you to explore things both close up but also cover massive distances very quickly - perfect for finding hidden secrets or finding a piece of lore that could be the key to unlocking the next obelisk.It's simple, it's enjoyable and the bossfights are definitely the highlights, though the hydra one was pain. I like that the storms are basically a timer to complete the obelisks quickly, though again, maybe more depth here with how to evade them could've been nice.Beyond mild nitpicks about ongoing open world trends, it's a fun sandbox, you can fly, shoot and generally do cool things in a large, lush landscape. Pick it up on sale, keep your play sessions short and you'll make the most of it. Especially if you're after a break from the "Ubisoft" open world design.

The music and sound design chiming in at all the right times and leaving me wanting more. Outstanding game, strongly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've given a thumbs up to worse games than this....  FINE!  But its kinda boring.  The plot is the same lone player fights back the darkness to restore a land now corrupted. That leaves the art and gameplay to carry the weight.  The art is beautiful but the locations are all the same.  Been to one pull tab tower been to em all.  All the ruins look the same there's no map so you just sort of run to the glows.Mobility is the biggest complaint.  The game would have been worth finishing had the traversal been fun.  The problem is sprinting is done by firing arrows at randomly placed targets and your double jump is your eagle which means you latch then flap up then glide.  It works but the result is kind of clunky.  Its this whole song and dance to make dash and double jump less fun then they would be in just about any other game.Secrets gave a meager reward and were littered all over the place,  which meant secret hunting was tedious for the slightest of rewards.  Puzzles were fine, they would have been serviceable but they were at best okay which meant that I was going from okay puzzle to tedious traversal to another samey indistinguishable location.   It was beautiful but it was boring and I've just played too many other games that are more fun than this under similar setups.Look you can see all the talent on display here.  I'm not gonna downvote a dev that I know will be making more things I want to see in the future (ABZU was amazing). _childDocuments_.review: This game will sweep you off your feet with the visuals, wow you with its sense of speed, and captivate you with its music. I played The Pathless on a large TV and the colours, the beautiful cel-shaded graphics pop like nothing else. You zoom through the world at lightning speed, wind whipping past; you soar through the sky and see the entire map stretch before you, towers rising into the sky and ruined temples obscured by fog.There are multiple biomes, each rich with their own bright colours and terrain, and interesting puzzles. The game isn't difficult by any means, you can't die or anything, so you're free to enjoy the striking visuals and score without interruption. There's more content in the game than I completed, but it's not required to advance in the game, which i appreciated.The story is pretty barebones, but it doesn't really need to be anything more than that. It focuses all your attention on the parts that matter: the beautiful sights and sounds, the sense of speed, and wide open map that's free to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: An open-world exploration game built around a fun and unique movement system. Interesting premise, great aesthetic, and engaging gameplay that greatly rewards thorough exploration the whole way through. The only threat you face is underwhelming, the bosses can be a chore, and it's rather pricey for only 9-13 hours of content; but if you want a novel take on the open-world genre, give it a try next time it goes on sale.  is an open-world exploration game about a master archer called the Hunter, who travels to an ancient island at the end of the sea to break a curse that threatens to corrupt the gods and destroy the world. Accompanied by an eagle companion, you must combine your abilities of archery and flight to seek out the remaining gods and free them from the grasp of the mysterious and powerful Godslayer. Much of the story beyond that is told to you piecemeal by exploring the ruins you find along your journey, so it's best I let you discover the rest by yourself.Excluding the tutorial zone, the game is divided up into four regions, each larger in scale than the last. The core gameplay loop is the same in each one: explore a vast open area in search of lightstones to restore power to three obelisks that will weaken the corrupted god in that area, giving you the opportunity to defeat them in combat and release them from their curse. There's no minimap to tell you where to go, asking you instead to rely on a skill called "Spirit Vision" that will reveal hidden objects and highlight locations of interest on the map. These locations hold self-contained puzzles in varying forms, some rewarding you with the lightstones you need to progress while others offer crystals that improve your eagle's ability to fly. You're not given explicit instructions on how to solve any of these puzzles, or told what kinds of puzzles there are, and sometimes there's no clear indication that something even  a puzzle, so you'll need to have a keen eye and be willing to mess around with anything that looks unusual.  Nothing revolutionary, but the experience would be far more boring without them breaking up the travel sections.Speaking of travel, the whole game's design is built around a rather interesting movement system. Your walking speed is incredibly slow (at least in relation to the size of the map), and your ability to sprint is very limited on its own. Scattered around the island are a bunch of floating red talismans, and shooting one with your bow will replenish some of your stamina gauge; and if you're sprinting while you shoot one, you'll also gain a burst of speed. The idea is to chain talisman shots as you run to maintain a high momentum, allowing you to travel between locations in a fraction of the time you would otherwise--something that even works when flying with your eagle. I've played a bunch of games that force an annoyingly slow pace in order to try and manufacture a "relaxing" experience; yet the flow state I'd slip into as I rhythmically fired shot after shot to dash across these sprawling landscapes as fast as I could was somehow more relaxing for me than any of those games ever were. There's not much in the way of danger to be found while exploring--no enemies, no traps, not even fall damage to discourage risky behavior, so you're given a lot of freedom to wander around and experiment with the movement system. There's only one threat you'll run into in each region, but I use "threat" very loosely here. As you work to free a corrupted god, it travels inside this massive red storm cloud that teleports around the map and can chase after you if you get too close. Getting caught in the storm triggers a stealth segment in which you have to rescue your eagle, who's fallen a moderate distance away, without getting seen as the god tries to hunt you down. Hiding from the god just means not moving when you're in its cone of vision, so it's more like a sudden game of Red Light Green Light than an actual stealth segment. Evidently if you get caught, your punishment is losing some of those crystals you've been picking up from puzzles, but these segments were so easy that the thought of failing them never even crossed my mind. After my first bout with them, , only there to waste my time whenever they landed in a section of the map I was trying to get into.After restoring the three obelisks in an area, the storm gets locked to the center of the region, and entering it begins a multi-phase fight to free the god from the Godslayer's control. : a chase sequence that has you sprinting after them across an open field until you can get close enough to shoot at its weak points. They so quickly that it leaves very little room for error when chaining your talisman shots, made worse by an array of obstacles that clutter your screen as you run and stop you cold if you bump into them. This segment can take a frustratingly long time, and the boss will randomly start to outpace you once you get close just to pad out the sequence even further. , each incorporating different game mechanics to make a unique fight that mostly makes up for the annoyance of their first phase. After a successful fight, you're provided a substantial upgrade to your movement and are free to explore the region uninterrupted, with the god's storm cleared away and the path to the next one opening up for you to progress at your leisure.Boss battles aren't the only way to get upgrades, however, and sticking around after freeing the god can give you the opportunity to improve yourself even further before moving on. Each region holds more lightstones than you actually need to trigger the battle, but finding all of them will offer you an additional character upgrade, often related to the one you earned from the boss and always just as useful. The other collectible outside of lightstones are the aforementioned crystals, and collecting enough of these gives your eagle additional flaps while flying, affording you greater vertical movement as well as more gliding capability. Upgrading flaps starts out slow, but picks up speed pretty quickly as later regions offer more frequent and larger crystal bonuses; and diligent players will eventually get enough of them to ensure that nowhere on the island is off-limits. Since the regions kept getting bigger as I got better at traversing them, --which is good, because you'll want to spend as much time exploring as you can to get the most out of your purchase., with my post-game achievement hunting putting my total playtime closer to 13 and change. It was a fun time overall and the problems I had with it were minor in the grand scheme of things, but I do feel like it was a little lacking given its high price tag. Maybe I'm just spoiled, but $40 feels a little steep for how much content I got out of it, even when taking into account 100% completion; so you may want to consider waiting for a sale before picking this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Abzu, I knew that I had to get this game and play it at some point. I'm very glad I did.  The gameplay is quite a bit different here, but both games have a theme of healing the world. Unlike Abzu, this game has quite a bit of text and dialogue. You find corpses throughout and can read the final thoughts of some of them. At first I wasn't too interested in them but by the end I really grew to appreciate the worldbuilding and lore that was going on. Finding out about the events of the world through these sources was something I absolutely loved and added so much to the game for me. Though I still do love the silent approach of Abzu as well. The score is also really great (as to be expected) and the game is very beautiful visually. The boss encounters are large in scale and very visually impressive, though at times they could feel a tad clunky. The main gameplay consists of going around the wilderness, finding statues, temples, and other structures which house Lightstones. Sometimes you'll have to solve puzzles in order to get them, and thankfully none of the puzzles ever felt annoyingly hard. That being said, sometimes they could be a bit too easy, but I understand the reasoning behind that. Overall it was a great game, and I'm super excited to play whatever Giant Squid releases next.
