This turns into a satisfying experience of rhythmically shooting at targets to keep moving quickly. Lastly, the soundtrack is amazing and fits the mood of the game very well. I heavily recommend playing both The Pathless and Abzu and I will continue to keep an eye on Giant Squid's future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly loved this game. Everything about it just worked very well. Its beautiful, has a great soundtrack, the lore is interesting but not too deep, and it's FUN. The movement feels very fluid and the soft puzzles are interesting to figure out while not being too challenging. If I had to offer a criticism for it, it would only be that the game feels a little too easy across the board. Some harder puzzles and combat would have pretty significant impact. Overall I really enjoyed it. Most importantly: you can pet the bird.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and atmospheric exploration-puzzle game which plays like a love child of Shadow of the Colossus and the puzzle sections of Breath of the Wild.The Pathless is a very nice and chill journey through a big fantasy open world with interesting land marks, a simple but engaging story and some organically designed but fairly easy puzzles, which is occasionally interrupted by a cool and cinematic boss fight.If you are here for a puzzle game that you need to rack your brain to get through, this is not it, and if you want it for a cool and challenging boss rush then it's probably not a good choice either. This game is all about the flow, the simple joy of using a very fluid and engaging movement system while exploring a visually stunning environment and the occasional puzzle, exploration task or boss fight is just the icing on the cake. The music, the visuals and the gameplay all blend together seamlessly into a very well made mix of escapism.Oh and you can pet the bird.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant since they're the ones that made Abzu, and Abzu nearly put me to sleep. This game does a good job of reexamining mechanical tropes in games that really don't serve a purpose in every title, the most advertised as which being their 'shoot targets to sprint' function. How often have you been trying to get from point A to point B in a game and you might as well just hit the numlock key and doze off? This makes traversal more engaging without just watching your character parkour. with minimal inputs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: A breathtakingly beautiful game with a simple gameplay concept. With the help of your eagle companion, you explore the mysterious island of the gods to try to save the world from "The Godslayer." You learn about the world by exploring it and interacting with ruins and souls of the departed, as well as the spirits of nature.Some things that really stood out to me about this game were just how visually beautiful and compelling the environment and character designs were. The eagle is one of the cutest companions ever, and it never stops being adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless' title ties to both the theme of the story and the gameplay.I have never felt so free in any video game ever like The Pathless. There is no one dedicated path for you to follow to reach an area or travel to the next. You can reach them in whatever way you wish.If you're a fan of Breath of the Wild or Shadow of the Colossus, this game is for you. There's clear inspiration, and yet it isn't a shameless copy. It's unique between the two.The only bad thing about this game is that there is no photo mode, with all the amazing sights you can see in the game.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's particularly my kind of game, but this is (with one major area and presumably a boss fight left) 10/10 for me. It's pretty, the music is good, it's got great flow, and wonderful gamefeel. The excellent gamefeel elevates the puzzles and the collectathon elements, as does the wonderful art style and flow. Many of the "secrets" are much better versions of the Korok seeds from Breath of the Wild, and the puzzles have a way of not irritating me like puzzles in games over do. The boss battles are giant set pieces that have yet to let me down.Overall, I don't think I can say enough good things. No bugs, no glitches, no complaints from me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and have waited for Journey 2, well. The Pathless is the closest we've gotten to. It's a rather large open world and easy game, so it passed the vibe check. You get a cloth based main character with an owl you can pet, yes you can pet it at anytime and sometimes required. 10/10 right there. You use your pet to help glide around this large world when you're not using the weird movement system where you auto-aim targets that boost your speed like a rhythm game. It becomes pretty epic towards the end. Speaking of epic, the soundtrack is made by Austin Wintory, so you're ears will thank you for getting this game. The other surprise I didn't expect is while the bosses aren't that hard, the spectacle they offer is something that feels both intense and memorizing despite it's simple auto-aiming arrow based combat. You probably didn't make it this far and bought it once you found out about the owl petting. I don't blame you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing! The presence of an immersive and gloriously isolated open world combined with a forgiving combat/traversal  mechanic is intriguing and it kept me hooked for the entire play-through. I loved finding all the puzzles and facing off against wicked bosses (with a final boss that's nothing short of awe-inspiring). It was an exhilarating and moving experience and I look forward to playing it again in the future (I miss my eagle friend already). Kudos to Giant Squid for developing such a unique and beautifully executed game, and to Annapurna for consistently publishing some of the best titles out there!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless was made by Giant Squid, a studio led by former members of thatgamecompany, the people behind Journey. If that brings to mind atmospheric adventure games, then you're on the right track. However, I think a more apt comparison is Shadow of the Colossus.I think this game might be better.Before the pitchforks come out, keep in mind I didn't beat SotC until the PS3 remaster, and I've also finished the remake for PS4. It's a solid game. But one of the greatest games of all time? Eh...The Pathless provides a beautiful environment to roam around in. The general flow of sliding and shooting can be picked up in minutes, and as you complete puzzles and glide with your eagle, you're treated to gorgeous vistas that turn into natural wonderlands as you purge areas of the Godslayer's corruption. You'll run with deer across the plains, slide on your knees, and hit a target in midair while leaping over a rushing river. It's good stuff.People praise SotC for its minimalist structure, but I was really looking for more context as I rode Agro across barren wastelands punctuated with the occasional lake, beach, or forest. Why was the land cursed? Where did the colossi come from? These questions go unanswered. In contrast, The Pathless provides just enough lore to keep you engaged while maintaining an air of mystery. Through snippets of text, you learn about the gods you're fighting while lighting torches and bouncing arrows off mirrors. These give appropriate reasoning as to why you're on the island and what you're up against.I don't know what black magic the developers used to make the colors so vibrant, but I can't emphasize enough how great this game looks. The soundtrack has a nice mix of folk instruments and the occasional vocals of a fictional language that sounds similar to Mongolian. You're rewarded for going off the beaten path, and there's no minimap, but you don't need it. Areas pulse red if there's something to collect, just use your eyes. Aren't we all pro gamers anyway?If you're rushing, you might finish the five bosses in less than 10 hours. Getting everything will take a few hours more, so it might be best to wait for a sale. Either way, I really enjoyed this game and appreciated that it didn't have fifteen samey areas just to pad out the length, but instead four well-designed ones. I can appreciate a game not overstaying its welcome and providing collectibles that are seamlessly woven into the core gameplay loop.In SotC, I would just find, like, a lizard or something. Riveting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is an excellent game that executes its visual presentation and art direction at an elite level. An intriguing and straightforward plot helps drive the player forward as they push their way through the island using a well thought out movement system that feels rewarding and fluid. The combat sections are robust and dynamic, and show off a veritably refreshing approach to fighting a boss.The first pitfall present here is a lack of evolution in some of the core mechanics. The movement and exploration is engaging for the most part, but after a certain amount of time it loses some of its appeal. The second is the stealth mechanic present in each area. It desperately needed to either be varied by zone, or have a more engaging core mechanic.Overall, it is a game more than worth your time if you enjoy single player games that focus on a sense of exploration and visual appeal. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Aquaspace for the Nintendo WiiWare but with a bird and a bow. Banger music and impressive visuals as always. I kinda wish it wasn't a pain to travel everywhere, what with the map being large.Even with 15 hours, the game still felt short somehow. However, I really enjoyed the cutscenes and lore, which the previous giant squid game did not divulge explicitly.Over all, a good game for a few evenings.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The joy of movement! The joy of Exploration! This game is a great example on how to  from others (namely Shadow of Collossus) without blatantly copying their ideas. It's more of a relaxing/girlfriend/listening to a podcast type of game where there are almost no punishments for mistakes and the "puzzles" are really simple and give you instant gratification. All of the "secrets" are revealed to you via a sonar-type power, so there's as much exploration as you want without cryptic stuff getting in the way.The bad part is that, albeit there are only a few fights, they are pretty similar and I really hate how the color pallet turns into all kinds of red and you just can't tell things apart. It's a visual spectacle, but fails to be engaging, because it isn't clear what to do and special effects get in the way too much. Still, the epic fights are just there to be epic and you are only punished with a couple seconds of boredom if you get slapped too many times, so the unclear nature of it all is easy to forgive.Fans of Sony games like Shadow of Collossus, Journey and Death Stranding (I think the boring stealth sections are inspired by it) will feel at home. Action lovers be catious.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! If you have played Abzu and enjoyed that game you will love this. It feels like a mini Breath of the Wild game but less frustrating as there is no health bar.  I'm currently halfway through and wish it was a longer game. It's more about the puzzles and having fun, it's the right amount of difficulty in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingIt got me hooked after 5min.The gameplay is simple and the puzzles are fun to do.It's the first game after years of gaming that i really enjoy trying to get the max out of the ingame world.Worth mentioning is the cinematic soundtrack which is really beautiful.Can't wait for a sequel or the next game from these developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime: 9 hours to get true endingBasically a more linear Breath of the Wild. You have open world exploration, but are locked to completing regions in a specified order (although why frankly doesn't make sense to me since it'd have little to no impact on the story or progression).Same issues I have with BotW, the exploration is great but the things you do in the world get very repetitive with little variation as the game progresses. You have the equivalent of Korok seeds for minigames and sheikah shrines for your puzzle/dungeon. I wish the game had explored more elements to the puzzles, as often the ruins were just the same block/torch setup in a new environment. And unlike BotW where you have a wide toolkit and physics engine that can let you create your own solutions, your limited options keep you restrained to the developer intended answer most of the time.While pretty, this just didn't give me that same kick that I got from going through ABZU's immensely lush environments. Nothing about the landscape I was exploring in Pathless felt all that engaging or unique outside of some of the more exotic architecture. That said I did enjoy the subtle storytelling and world-building. Coming across the tablets and spirit messages to get a better understanding of the lore were a big plus.The storm mechanic was interesting but a flawed execution. Since there's no serious consequence to getting caught, it just becomes annoying at worst than actually suspenseful. Not to mention half the time I felt like the monster would just blink into existence and immediately catch me in an open area where I'd have had no time to hide.The moments when this game shined was when I was just chaining a long series of speed boosts and sprinting across the world. Especially later when you unlock more options for terrain traversal. However, going into the endgame this feels pointless as optimal world movement quickly shifts to using the eagle to hover as far as possible. I wish the game had just kept me on the ground so I could enjoy more of what I was looking at up close, and just using more of the blue talismans for vertical elevation. Keep the eagle hover and maybe two or three jump boosts, but limit it at that. It's comparable to how revali's gale completely invalidates the need for climbing in BotW. It robs the game of a unique core mechanic that should have been explored more instead of replaced.Didn't run into any bugs that I recall, although at times I found trying to line up a shot on a target when there were a few options on screen at once to be really finicky but that was really only a problem with the bell puzzles.Soundtrack is absolutely fantastic, but with Austin Wintory behind it you're going to get a masterpiece. That man is the Hans Zimmer of video game OST's.Ultimately I would recommend a playthrough. It did feel rote at parts but there was enough interest to keep me invested to the end. That said this game is a one and done for me, I don't see any value in a replay. Get it, but at 20$.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: As good as Journey and Abzû, but in an open world! And this change is very well managed. What a pleasure to explore this island and discover all its secrets and puzzles! The boss sequences are nice too, and very challenging, even if we can't die. The musics are always excellent, and I like the fact they adapt to the situation. Besides, the mechanics of run and boost and eagle fly are really pleasant.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is noice! Buy it. I just recently defeated the first boss and was amazed at it, so much so I have replayed it over 10 times now. I am really looking forward to take on the others. I've been doing a lot of running around, enjoying the fluid movement mechanics, and completing challenges and finding things in the beautiful world. If you have taste in games like I do you'll enjoy it. Support the devs :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Austin Wintory and Giant Squid do it again. This game is a feast for the eyes and ears, and the movement feels excellent (which is a big plus, since it's 99% of what you're going to be doing here). Fans of Journey or ABZU are obviously going to enjoy this, but I would hazard that people who enjoy the aesthetics of games like Dark Souls will appreciate the atmosphere all the same.Nice combat encounters, very cinematic, the rest of the gameplay feels a bit like if Nintendo tried to make Korok hunting actually fun. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I bought his game at 75% off and still feel like I paid too much. I will concede that it is a beautiful game and the sprinting system has its' feels good moments but each zone felt nearly identical to every other zone,. The boss fights, puzzles and exploration became stale quickly and never meaningfully changed over the course of the game. Once you've played the 1st quarter of the game, you've played the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what i call wasted potential. There is so much they could have done with the unique mechanics in this game. All in all its a gorgeous game and it looks like they put a lot of work into the design and everything, but i beat the game in 5.4 hours. And honestly there were fun bits but it was more of a chore tbh. if the game focused on more of those scenes when your fighting the bosses and applied those ideas to the actual gameplasy of the rest of it it would be great. If they had more action adventure type scenes like for instance like in Prince of persia when you are running from the dahaka,, EVEN for solving the puzzles JUST ANYTHING.  something that added more skill and time and enjoyment to the gameplay then it would be worth it. But it only if it is on sale imo would i say purchase this game. 52.99 is a joke for a 5 hour game
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant and captivating game. It makes travelling and exploring very fun, and rewards players for checking out all the hidden ruins and secret caves. You get a companion eagle, and petting the eagle is part of the game, which is delightful! Reading the various monoliths and the memories of the dead provides a compelling story. Some of the ghost memories are especially tragic, if you take the time to read them. Some of the landscapes and music feel a bit like Journey, and some of the puzzles have a bit of a Legend of Zelda vibe, but overall there are enough new concepts that it doesn't feel too derivative. I completed the story in about 23 hours, getting a good number of achievements.The only cons are that some of the elements are a bit repetitive. You find light stones, light up some towers, chase down and fight a fiery boss, several times. I didn't mind it, but I can see how others might. Also, once the whole map has been freed of the curse, I would love to explore around it more, but I haven't found a way to continue exploring post final-boss.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Only 4 hours in, but this game is beautiful with music and visuals. It's very fun and easy to travel around the world with out feeling bogged down and too slow during the start. The controls are very tight, movement is a bit floaty which works most of the time, but so far is a struggle for anything requiring really precise landing (those dang time challenge yellow butterflies). I suggest you play this with a controller not a keyboard and mouse. The game doesn't outright tell you where to go but uses a lot of visuals to help direct you, for how massive the map feels I don't feel lost and the landmarks are easy to follow. It's everything I expect from this company and more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda torn on whether to recommend this or not. On one hand I did enjoy the game, but if I had paid full price and not the 15$ for a key that I did I likely would have felt scammed. What is good in The Pathless is really good. The art direction and music really carry the experience, however the puzzles are very samey from start to finish (they are all some variant of light these torches, shoot through these hoops, and place that weight on this button) and while the movement can feel good at times I found that it quickly grows tedious. The auto aim takes any sort of skill away for the most part and you never truly feel fast as the speed boosts quickly taper out, often before the next talisman leaving you slowly meandering towards your next boost.I enjoyed the visual spectacle of the bosses especially as it broke up the monotony of the rest of the puzzles-n-shoot game play, but ultimately was left unsatisfied by them. There are no consequences in this game. Getting hit just means the boss takes slightly longer, no health bars or anything. I get that they're trying to be artsy, but it really takes me out of the moment when I get slammed by a meteor and remember "oh yeah none of this matters".By far the worst part of the game is the big red globes the bosses move around in through each zone before you beat them. These globes will try and spawn directly where you want to go and when touched teleport you to the world's laziest stealth section. I failed one on purpose just to see if there was any actual punishment to be had and all that changes is some flight gems get knocked out of you, but you can just pick them up sonic style. By the last zone I would just get caught on purpose as it was far fast than playing out the entire sequence and I already had 12+ flaps so any loss I did incur felt meaningless.Overall This game is okay at best, but gets caught up in being an art project rather than a video game far too much. I wouldn't pay more than 15$ for it and certainly not the ludicrous asking price of 40$.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The price for this game is WAY too much. The most this game should be is $15, and thats being generous. I went for a completion of all the achievements, and while I don't have that due to something ill discuss later, i still only managed to have about 13 hours of playtime. I didn't even know what I was doing for the majority of the game until around the second boss, and by then i already had about 2 hours. The game is simple and pretty, the gameplay is a decent, but short. its very repetitive too, the creators of the game did try to balance the repeating puzzles but there still ended up being a few dozen of the same puzzles. Really this game had nothing to blow me away, and thats extremely disappointing considering how nice it looked. Now about the achievements, they are currently glitched, a lot of them wont be given to you despite you completing them multiple times. This is very frustrating when it comes to 100% runs too. But whats more frustrating is the disconnect between the creators and the fanbase. Myself and many others have gone to their discord, which is where you're meant to contact them on, and have complained about an issue. Despite the developers being online, multiple infact at all hours of the day, they dont get back to anyone. So no, dont buy this game, its very overpriced and repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Abzu, Journey, or Flower, then this game is obviously a must buy.The Pathless is simple, beautiful, broad, and is a lot more mechanically engaging than a similar game such as Abzu. The puzzles are usually pretty straightforward, the mask shows you where you haven't been, the game is entirely at your own pace, but it never felt boring to me. It's like a really long hike through the most beautiful forest/plateau/steppe/tundra/whatever you've been on, and while the story was a big motivation to keep moving forward, I ended up going and exploring every inch of the map just for fun.Also the bossfights were awesome and intense.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly philosophical message in the final dialogue! Very unique game. Relaxing visuals, novel movement mechanics. The relationships feel indigenous-inspired and align with positive land-stewardship. Highly recommend if you are looking for a low pressure puzzler that is reminiscent of Princess Mononoke. 10/10 would pet my golden eagle again
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- A lot to explore. Comparing this to BotW, you get 4 (better) divine beasts, 5 (better) bosses, about 40 shrine puzzles, something like 100 korok seed puzzles, 6-8 areas worth of interesting places compressed into 4 areas, always active Rivali's Gale (the updraft ability), and a paraglider.- The atmosphere is awesome with the normally dark calm setting ... and the next moment the forest is on fire and a giant animal thing is shooting lasers and fireballs at you.- There's a lot of focus on verticality and the upgrades to the bird make it more fun to explore later on, when you can just fly all the way up, scan for what areas you haven't explored yet, and glide down to them.- I basically did a reverse boss order playthrough, just because halfway through the first area I was curious if I could climb that mountain all the way to the top. And I could. It was challenging, but I did it, and it felt great.Neutal:- Running fast while shooting targets seems fun on paper, but the targets are nothing more than a mana bar refill to keep you running fast. You don't even have to aim and now there are floating squares everywhere, even in the sky. Sometimes tho, they are placed strategically so you can chain jumps or speed boosts in a satisfying way.- The sphere of doom is constantly chasing you around the areas, and you actually have to be careful because getting caught by the beast inside means losing some XP permanently. The world feels more dangerous and immersive that way, but it's also a pretty lengthy sequence whenever you get in there accidentally.Negatives:- It's 2021 and you can't get away with gibberish voice acting because it's a "foreign mysterious langugage". It sounds silly and plain english voiceover would have been a lot better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: first off, this game is worth every penny of it's full price.  it is an amazing game, i would highly recommend it.  to set expectations straight, this game is an adventure puzzle game.  there is no "combat" in the game in the traditional sense beyond boss fights.  this comes as a surprise to most people, as you are given a bow, but no one to shoot at.  the correct way to look at it is thinking of the bow as a tool rather than a weapon.  however, that is not to say that there aren't things to shoot at.  talismans are scattered all over the island, and shooting them will increase your sprint speed for a short time.  this makes for a fluid traversal experience, and one that i greatly enjoy.  90% of the game is spent exploring an island that has been corrupted by a mad spirit.  you discover lore, secrets, and spirit tokens to progress the game and the story.  the game is not hard, not at all.  but you do not play this game for it's difficulty, you play it for it's story.  boss fights in this game are a spectacle to be sure, and while they are not hard, they are amazing to experience.  i will not spoil the story here, but it is a really interesting one that delves into human psychology and one's purpose in life.  this is a massive improvement over giant squid's last game "ABZU" which while it was a great game, lacked the depth and lore that this game abundantly provides.  in terms of performance, i got away with running this game on a 1050Ti, but it was much better when i ran it on a 1650.  overall this is a great game, and one that i would recommend to anyone who likes exploration puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy exploring the world and learning about the past, and the overall plot. The traversing is nice when I get to take in this vast land that has a nice history.As with other critiques, the puzzles do seem rather lacking at times, but I still enjoy the roaming aspect.Also, you get to pet da bird.I got this 80% off so I'd say that it was worth that much, but I could not justify getting it full price. I recommend it for the narrative and discovery elements, and the occasional boss purging, that stuff is pretty epic when you're chasing them down in a fiery cosmos.Final rating: 7.5/10 I could get lost in this world, no cap.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Giant Squid, like always, makes great games and this one isn't the exception either. The Pathless is one of the great adventures that captivates with It's breathtaking semi-open worlds and fun gameplay. The fluid movement which is mostly running and gaining speed by shooting talismans and flying with your eagle fella makes exploration a joy. Mix it with very nice soundtrack and captivating story which has deep meaning and you got a great game that will make AAA studios and their games look like a piece of garbage compared to this one. Altough movement was nice to control what really impressed me was how the worlds are big and yet so minimalistic to the point They can tell a lore behind all of them. The worlds have bunch of puzzles which use your archery skills and can get you talismans to light up the towers to experience which will upgrade your eagle's ability to fly even more but beware the storms that can put you in stealth sequences and you can loose some of your experience If you get caught. Each world has also boss fights which aren't really punishing like in other games cause you can't die in the game. I must say It's really nice game and If you especially like open world games you should try this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, you can compare it to Breath of the Wild, getting that out of the way right away. However, the former exclusivity period has turned The Pathless into a true hidden gem of a game and one I would recommend.It cleverly trades a map for a radar system showing you the landmarks you've been to and where you still have yet to see. The world feels like a watercolor painting brought to life and it's one of the best examples of natural biomes I've experienced in a video game. Once you've beaten the boss of an area, it becomes fun and engaging to just run and fly around. Despite the Hunter being the only recognizable alive human in the world, the world does not feel empty.While I personally believe it was worth its full launch price, I can see why some may feel that it's overpriced. It's somewhat short for an open world game, I effectively 100 percented the game (less a few achievements) in twelve hours. But it's definitely a game I would come back to for a de-stresser.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Game Is extremely well made. Like very very well made. Every bit is polished and there is not much to fault in the execution of the games mechanics. However, the most novel thing the game does is petting the eagle. It's the best part of the game, which is not ideal. I found the movement too simplistic, where it boiled down to a rhythm of holding left trigger and pulling right trigger occasionally as the game chooses for you what to shoot. I would have loved to see an option for a more challenging aiming system (I didn't know about the half full timing thing until after I beat the game). The ruins you visit are interesting but ultimately empty. yes the room on the hill is cool until you realize that all that is inside is a dead guy and 3 barrels. You collect yellow gems to increase the amount of flaps your eagle can do, which was useful, but nowhere near useful enough to incentivise me trying to level my flaps up. Not to mention, that you need so many of these little gems that through the course of the entire game i managed to get 1 extra flap which made an indistinguishable impact on my game play. Also, there's extremely simple sneaking bits that seem to only interrupt the rest of the game. the sneaking bits are good to introduce the bosses, but then why do I have to deal with them multiple times? On the flip side, the music is incredible and beautifully supports the Mongolian themes of the game and the art direction hits its mark in every facet of the games world. To me it was too much style and not enough gamey substance to hold my attention. It is in absolutely no regards even close to a bad game. It just really did not appeal to me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The game has unfortunately not much to offer. The story and world design are super basic and the gameloop is: solve easy puzzle, get object that allows to activate 1/3 towers, fight boss (that are almost all the same, although I must say I stopped after the second boss). The only thing that really distinguishes this game from others is the movement mechanic which is really neat. BUT: the choice of a open world is really bad for this. The world has not been designed for specific movement combos like a linear world would have been and so, often the most efficient way of moving is repeating the same movement over and over again. Strangely, the parts where linear movement is required are badly designed and you loose all your speed since they require you to recharge for a few seconds. The concept is interesting, but concept demos are only worth it if you have a lot of time or if they are on a huge sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not Early Access, yet it has an issue with resolution selection that requires a workaround and no ability to rebind controls (for which I didn't readily find a workaround).  Refunding for now, but it looks great and I look forward to trying back a little later when it's had some bug fixes and updates.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: So, originally got the game on my computer, and found it entirely unplayable due to my extremely low framerate.However, since refunding it and buying it for the same price on console, I can undoubtedly say it is definitely worth a try. I've gotten about 8 hrs in this game so far, and it's been a joy for almost the whole time.Some things I love, definitely, about the game is the sheer speed at which your character moves around in the semi-wide open spaces provided. Everything is spaced out so you even have an excuse to go absolutely buckwild sonic fast towards your destination (or away from the absolutely massively ominous red cloud gaining behind you that appeared out of nowhere and interrupted the last 2 puzzles).The bossfights are also really fun to experience, because although the formula is the same (at least for the first 4), it manages to spice it up with solidly different attacks, patterns, and strategies for the second and third phases (and we can't forget how cool they all look, and how well the special effects appear). Speaking of how cool things look, the environment is absolutely gorgeous, with each area having little things that make sense (lots more water features in a previously flooded area, land generation in a forest vs a cold mountain vs a hardwood forest, etc.)For critique, I'd say the tutorials could use a little work, as they can be difficult to decipher, as well as just communicating as a whole what to do a tad better (I spent a while clearing red clouds before realizing they were an obstacle and not a task). There's still a specific kind of puzzle I can't figure out how to do because try as I might, I really just can't figure them out (I recognize these complaints might also just be me, so take them with a grain of salt).There's also the topic of the red clouds that appear. Actually getting caught by them isn't so bad, and even can be fun, but oh my word is it terrifying to see the giant red mass looming behind you because you looked away for too long while doing a puzzle. These clouds almost make it a horror game. I look over my shoulder more times during this game than a dark alley irl.Overall, the issues really depend more on the person playing it than the game, as I haven't seen any major glitches or bugs since I started (besides crashing in Nimue's fight, I think I saw somebody else get that too).
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad by any means, but for its base price, I'd definitely have felt a lot more deflated by what it offers (which makes me glad I got it on a sale for 21 bucks).The Pathless is easily compared to Breath of the Wild in terms of its explorative, nonlinear gameplay. However, this game focuses almost exclusively on the exploration, and light puzzle elements, and leaves combat extremely sparse, and trivial. You can't even die. Taking damage just trips you up a little bit, and is more of an inconvenience. This made boss encounters feel pretty weak, and unsatisfying. I didn't feel a need to get better at dodging their attacks because I could just shrug it off, and wait for the next opening, which you could argue makes it approachable to people newer to video games, but at that point, I'd rather there be a sort of assist mode that can be toggled.It's a pretty game, with a simple story that to be honest, has no real surprises, and is laden with tropes and cliches, but I don't think that was the point. You're meant to take in the sights of the world around you, and uncover the history of the land you're saving. The music is fantastic. which is unsurprising, since it was composed by Austin Wintory, who also made the music for ABZU, and Journey previously, both of which I thoroughly enjoyed.Unfortunately, that kinda makes my relative indifference towards The Pathless sting a little bit more. I really wish I could say the game was better, but it's pretty one-note, and it kinda got stale, with little to spice up the gameplay, especially when going for all achievements. I'd be a fool to not mention, however, that you can pet the eagle at any time. That's the best feature of the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: With action-packed boss fights, amazing music, and a fun and fast movement system, this game was a blast to play start to finish. I was especially impressed with the Eagle companion AI, as she's very easy to control during puzzles. The idle animation is pretty cute, not to mention you can pet her. The puzzles themselves aren't particularly difficult, but are still fun to complete, keeping the fast pace of the game in my opinion. My only real complaint is that I wish there was a world map or some kind of fast-travel system for added convenience. (and maybe some cool map art) But this is a minor nickpick that didn't take away from my enjoyment of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game.At the moment a bit more than 11 hours in, but about only 2 hours are actual game play. For every hour, you spend at least 90% of just looking aroud, trying to find your next destination. Need only one more idol to fill up the bonus tower? If you are lucky it only takes 2 hours to find it, and then you solve the puzzle in 3 minutes.Spend over a hour trying to find the last one on this level. Don't think i will continue playing this anymore.If you like mindless searching, repeating types of puzzles, and anoying boss fights This game is for you.Developers of this game (and almost every other game these days) seem to think that a long boss fight makes a simple boss hard. No, it's still easy, but they try to make as much chaos on screen as possible, so you will miss the marks when to shoot. _childDocuments_.review: This game was really nice. The visuals were really pretty, it ran really well, the music was amazing (choirs and orchestras all over), the concept was simple but compelling, there was plenty to discover and explore, and the conclusion was satisfying. The puzzles where a nice range of difficulty and all well thought out, and I really appreciated how I could skip some if I wasn't understanding them and move to another and still progress. The gameplay with the bow and arrow was new and interesting, making you use the bow a majority of the time for dashing and jumping rather than fighting. The movement was really smooth, and really where this game shined. It was really fun getting into zen-like groove moments and just flowing through the landscape with the controls. The game isn't as good as Journey or even Abzu, but I still think it's a good game in its own respect. When you make amazing games, they aren't all going to better than the previous ones, but they can still be good. The 3rd boss was not my favorite thing at all, I thought some of the timing required for it was a little awkward, but otherwise I struggle to really think of any criticisms. This is a great game all around that does not overstay its welcome. If it looks interesting to you, you'll probably enjoy it!If you wanna watch someone else play it, I did it on twitch @crustyoldhuman

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a simple game that makes the absolute most of it's mechanics. It's movement is fluid, it's set pieces entertaining, and it's exploration is addictive. _childDocuments_.review: I found "The Pathless" boring and frustrating to play."Journey" is one of my favorite games. I have played through it many times. "The Pathless" was made by Giant Squid, which was founded by some of the staff behind "Journey". Giant Squid also previously made "Abzu". Unfortunately neither "Abzu" nor "The Pathless" come close to the quality of "Journey."Giant Squid seems to have a fetish for making you hold down the trigger buttons. In "Abzu" you had to hold the trigger to swim forward, and in "The Pathless" you have to hold the trigger to run. Luckily unlike "Abzu" they did include in-game settings in "The Pathless" to change it so you can toggle run rather than having to hold down the trigger. However, I still just don't like having to shoot randomly floating crystals to run. Just... why? There is a reason we haven't seen this kind of feature in other games.The music in "The Pathless" just doesn't resonate with me. It doesn't elevate the gameplay. Because "The Pathless" is an open-world design it has to use more general-purpose soundtracks rather than soundtracks that are more specific. For example, the soundtrack in "Journey" is amazing, and it elevated the game in "Journey." However, "Journey" was not open world; "Journey" was a linear game broken down into levels. This meant "Journey" could have specific soundtracks lined up with specific sections of the game unlike "The Pathless." I will never listen to the soundtrack of "The Pathless" outside of playing the game.As for the graphics design, I will give "The Pathless" credit in that the bosses look amazing. However, there are only a handful of bosses and the rest of the game is just bland and boring. Everywhere you look just looks the same. It is all just a standard forested/nature area. Why is "The Pathless" designed to be an open world game but there aren't any interesting or unique locations to discover.The game gives you a mask you can put on that gives you an alternate vision in which some things are highlighted, but it won't let you run while you have the mask on. WHY!?!?!? So you have to run and stop, run and stop, run and... just to use the stupid mask. And even when you use the mask it doesn't even work the way you would expect; like, it applies a subtle red aura around places of interests, but when you get relatively close to the place of interest is stops showing the aura. This is confusing when the aura stops appearing because you ran all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way over there and now you have to spend multiple minutes searching for whatever the hell you were led here to find. and if you often won't find it and thus you just wasted a bunch of time which isn't fun.This game is much more puzzle focuesd than either Abzu or Journey, and I like the idea of them adding more puzzles, however I hate the puzzles in this game. This is where I find the game extremely frustrating. First off, finding where to go is an absolute pain due to the issues mentioned about the mask vision. However, once you find the puzzles they are bad too. Some puzzles are in relatively large rooms/areas, and it takes more time to just find all the stupid switches you need to press than it does actually solving the puzzle. Other puzzles are scripted in specific ways. Like one puzzle you have to shoot bells hanging from a tree in a specific sequence, which is extremely easy, but it took me multiple tries. Why did it take me multiple tries? I have no idea. I shot the stupid bells 10+ times in the right order in various ways, but it would never trigger the win condition; my only guess is that you have to stand on a circle while shooting the bells and because I have have taken a small baby step between shots it may have canceled my sequence. But that is the problem: the game doesn't tell you what you are doing wrong. The game does so little to help guide you and that just isn't good game design. Another thing that sucks about the puzzles is the arrow physics; there were multiple times where when I was shooting at a fire my arrow when one direction, but when I moved this other thing and shot an arrow from the same spot my arrow went in a completely different direction. What I mean is that the game forces your arrows to act like it wants them to act. It doesn't give you a mechanic to tinker with. It gives you a mechanic and says, "this can only be used in this way in this specific puzzle."The shooting is terrible... It auto aims every arrow. If there is no valid target in range then you can't even shoot an arrow. This just makes no sense. It is extremely frustrating because you don't have a good way to pick a target. You have to position your camera angle in non-intuitive ways to try to get the game to cooperate. But the worst thing about the shooting is that you can ready and/or fire two arrows at the same target. The game should not allow this. Once you shoot an arrow at a target the game will know if that arrow will hit the target, and if it will, then it should change targets so you can fire another arrow at another target. It is hard to explain without just experiencing it for yourself, but yeah, the arrow targeting is terrible.I gave "Abzu" a negative review, but I enjoyed "Abzu" more than "The Pathless". That is sad. I hope Giant Squid makes another game that will win me over, but having two disappointments since "Journey" I don't have a lot of faith in that happening.

_childDocuments_.review: if anything perhaps a little Too attuned to my tastes for my current liking (im somewhat in the mood to be Aesthetically Challenged recently) but i wont be ungrateful to something that so specifically seeks to please me. more of Everything should take place in forests, more games should experiment with movement beyond just button combinations, more games should have spiritual aspirations in their thematics, more games should be unafraid of the Ritual...the gameplay loop here is a strange sense of Ritualized Freedom, finding your own way and adapting within a prexisting repetitious structure...really really does feel like a Pilgrimage. like many of these kinds of games, the texture fills in the blanks left by the simple narrative, and as didactic as the main theme is, as someone who left the authoritarian constraints of monotheism and only rediscovered my deep need for spirituality in more Multiplicitous and Esoteric places, i cant say i didnt feel seen, or didnt find a balming beauty. giant squid's (and ofc by extention thatgamecompany's) approach to "artsy" games is something i might have been inclined to scoff at as insubstantial or too eager to explain itself previously, and maybe i can see the argument for that, but the Populism they bring is something im currently in a place to admire a lot i think. more of Everything should take place in forests.

_childDocuments_.review: Casual game of puzzles and exploration, featuring amazing mobility and a few "boss" fights.It's a unique experience, so it gets my recommendation.I can't say I love anything in particular about visuals, sound or design individually, but they all combine into something resembling a masterpiece that I think will age quite well.The world is lacking detail, yet it never feels empty or dead (something I can't say about most open world games).Music and sounds are just okay on their own, but they add to the atmosphere and the world.I loved the animations too. Characters feel lively, and the world has (mostly) subtle animations, like effects of wind, animals and particles.Story is kind of generic, but because it's presented through some key points (rather than full narration) and is given very little focus it ends up feeling almost like an open-ended and philosophical debate.Mechanically this game is very barebones. All you can do is move(including jumps and glides), shoot bow (that is auto-aimed for you) at nearby targets and in very rare cases interact with stuff like switches. If it sounds boring it's because you are being deceived by the devs.A huge chunk of this game is world exploration and mobility in this game makes it delightful. While moving normally you are fairly slow and clunky. The moment you shoot one of many targets in the world, you gain momentum and move like the wind (I recommend watching a video for this). I would compare mobility to open-world Spiderman games.This game has no map (something I've loved in Ghost of Tsushima and I love it here too), so you can finally look at the world rather than focusing on minimap. It does however have a scanner tool, which makes it feel more like other open-world games, where you scan the area to see where to go and run there without thinking much. I think this is a good way to do story, if you don't have a good story to tell.Puzzles make up another massive chunk of the game. Puzzles fairly short and easy. I don't know when this became a praise, but puzzles test your wit and not your reflexes/muscle memory (i.e. no solutions require some perfect-input action to solve). Puzzles are a mix of unique (where each one needs its own solution) and generic (once you know how they work, you just go through the motions).A great example of achievements being achievements and not playtime padding. They never felt like a chore list or a massive grind, which I can't believe I have to complement. I played the game, explored as much as I could, beat the game and by that time I got most of them naturally. I read the remaining achievements and could figure out what's expected of me without having to look up a 20min video guide.There is one achievement (lore collection) that can be annoying, as you can be missing 1 item and have to run around most of the world. With that said, if you explore thoroughly you will probably get it done without going out of your way.The game DOES have 1 obscure optional challenge, but it's not linked to achievements, nor does it give any real benefits in game. It's more of a hidden lore thing.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect game for those who enjoy titles such as Journey, Abzû, Shadow of Colossus and The Last Guardian. A very enjoyable experience from start to finish, which never becomes too hard or too boring, since luckily no part of it overstays its welcome.[TL/DR] 🏃The Pathless provides a fluid movement system, interesting puzzle design and a gorgeous presentation, both visually and auditorily. The soundtrack is often very soothing, until the tension starts building up and both the imagery and sound accompany this build up beautifully. It's an incredibly solid and pleasant experience, even in it's short playtime, which is worthy of game of the year accolades.[VISUALS] 🦅Much like it's predecessor Abzû, this game was very well designed. I could see visual influences from eurasian nomads (mongolia, russia, etc) in character's clothing, themes of falconry and in its soundtrack, several egyptian influences when it came to stone carvings on walls and 2D representations of people and deities in decorative banners, as well as aztec influences in terms of statue design.Given the immense amount of visual diversity present here, you'd think it would become a mess, but rather it combines to create a very strong and unique aesthetic which adding to its immense scale, made me want to explore every corner of its world.Matthew Nava is an extremely talented artist and director, since this game is the fourth I've played with him at the helm of either Art Direction, Creative Direction or both, and all four of those games - Flower, Journey, Abzû and The Pathless, back my claim. I even own the book "The Art of Journey"  (signed by him and Jenova Chen) which he wrote and designed about the creation of the game, and it's one of my most prized possessions. I highly recommend grabbing a copy of it, if you can find one.[AUDIO] 🎼As I stated previously, the game draws heavily on eurasian steppe's music for their signature sound, which originated in southern Siberia as well as western Mongolia, commonly known as throatsinging. The soundtrack was composed by the amazing Austin Wintory of Journey fame, who managed to secure two BAFTA awards in 2013 for his work on one of 2012's best titles.It's a remarkable soundtrack, one that grabs hold of you and never lets go, one that manages to both intrigue and excite, one of the main pillars of the this game's appeal and more than enough reason to buy this game and support these incredible artists. It's so good, in fact, that you'll most likely be listening to it long after you finish the game, since its uniqueness is not easily replaced elsewhere. Another banger from Austin, and certainly the best soundtrack in 2020.[GAMEPLAY] 🏹The game is made up of two main types of gameplay, puzzle solving and exploration. Each of these is supplemented by a movement system which is quite unique to the game, and that will have you running, jumping and gliding across grassy plains, dense forests, flowing rivers and snowy mountaintops with immense ease and an incredible sense of speed.Puzzles are intuitive and while they frequently reutilize their mechanics, they do so in fresh contexts to create somewhat unique head-scratchers that fortunately never feel too hard nor too easy (excluding the bell puzzles which could have had more complex patterns to follow - they're far too easy). Every puzzle type demanded at least a good analysis of the surrounding environment, which always felt fun.Most puzzles are complex enough to make you spend a few hours in each of the game's four main areas, and although I do wish some would have made me think on their solutions for a while longer, the truth is the current difficulty adds enough intentionality and reward to the gameplay as it stands. This also means you'll never have to consult an online guide to finish anything in this game, if you think things through and look around for clues, you'll solve everything rather quickly.There are also several hidden puzzles, rooms and currency throughout the world to be discovered, which repay close attention to your surroundings and always left me with the thought of how well designed everything looked and felt. If you enjoy exploring open worlds and finding interesting things to look at, you'll really appreciate what Giant Squid have made here.The game has a minimalist yet interesting world to explore, and the tidbits of lore scattered across the map allow players to discover what the ideology and life of its inhabitants was before their demise, which also helps make exploration fun, engaging and the world feel more fleshed out.[BOSS BATTLES] 💀Each main area ends with a boss fight which functions as a puzzle itself, and they all felt interesting, but were not in any way groundbreaking. The outcome of the fights felt rewarding as well, as did 100%ing every area which rewards you with a special mechanical boost to help you along the journey.[FINAL WORDS] 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟I highly recommend 100% completing the game, the achievements are approachable and excluding 2 of them, I did every single one on my own basically on my first and only run of the game.It took me about 11 hours to see everything and 100% the game, I feel this was a fair amount of hours and one of those cases where more playtime would actually detract from the experience, so I'm glad the developers knew when to end the journey and keep it cohesive.If this playtime seems short to you, just get the game on sale but make sure you pick it up because games as unique, well-designed and enjoyable as this don't come along everyday and we should support developers making worthwhile experiences on a small budget. If you can, consider picking it up at full price, because you won't regret it and the developers surely deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: Before mentioning anything else: there is a button that let's you PET THE BIRD AND IT IS AMAZINGOther than that god-tier piece of game design, The Pathless is a cross between Breath of the Wild and Shadow of the Colossus mixed with a vibrant, awe-inspiring, art style and a fluid movement system that will have you feeling so agile. The lore is not thrust into your face but scattered about the map, leaving the job of piecing everything together to the player if they choose to. I chose to and had a much more deep and enjoyable experience for it. The puzzles are simple and satisfying while the boss fights are interesting and dynamic. This is a perfect chill game that won't have you spending the next 80 hours of your life working on it, it's a short and extremely enjoyable experience. I would love to see more of this world if there are more stories to write.

_childDocuments_.review: Set in a beautiful and expansive landscape full of ruins and relics of a mysterious past, the environment of 'The Pathless' is quite intriguing. You are first introduced to a 'special' eagle that becomes of great assistance and companionship throughout your journey. Whether you are sliding across the tundra, bobbing and weaving through trees in a dense forest, or gliding over the peaks of snow capped mountains, the feeling of constant speed and forward motion is tremendously enjoyable. Throughout the game you are tasked with solving puzzles/obstacles and hunting the occasional colossal astral beast. Giant Squid Studios has released yet another thoroughly beautiful and powerful story of companionship and bravery... The truth is a pathless land!
