_childDocuments_.review: I loved Journey, it is one of my all time favourite games. I loved ABZU and the different tone that brought to the table. This game is like those, but not the same. The locomotion in the game feels good, and gets better as you progress and more skills unlock. The visual stylings are great. The soundtrack is another great one from Austin Wintory. The general game play is: go to area, solve six puzzles, unlock the boss, defeat boss, unlock skill, go to next area. Repeat. The bosses are great, with each one having its own feel. The final boss is great, and the ending is absolutely satisfying. I can see myself going back to solve the additional puzzle littered about the fairly expansive world when I want something satisfying but not too taxing.,
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It has some ups and down. It's really pretty, there are some nice ideas for moving fast in large open world areas and a lot of things to collect all around. My problem with it is that it become very repetitive, very fast, with most puzzles being quite similar and puzzles themselves far apart in an ocean of running around the plains.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Although the environment is repetetive, that is the only downside I experienced to the game.The puzzles are of various degree of difficulty and the secrets are very rewarding to find.For as you progress you gain enhanced ways of traversing the lands and the environmental storytelling is very interesting, I found myself deeply engaged with the unfolding story from start to finish.The music is bautiful, the style attractive, the bosses got unique twists and the finale was phenomenal!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh! Just loved it. So smooth, so fun, so beautiful, so simple yet effective. I want to say the only criticism would be that each plateau gets a bit repetitive with the number of talismans to collect (there are a lot) but for me to 100% the game and nearly get every achievement only took me a casual 18hrs so it isn't as long as something like 'Immortals Fenyx Rising' but something about it felt a little stretched just for content bulk. On the note of puzzles to solve for talismans, I commented to myself a few times that I was impressed by the amount of variety in puzzles the devs came up with considering it is always a bow and arrow puzzle. Props!Anyway, LOVED THIS GAME and highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Giant Squid has delivered yet another masterpiece with The Pathless! This captivating game follows an archer and her loyal eagle as they embark on a quest to restore balance to the world of the Tall Ones. Every element—from the enchanting story to the breathtaking graphics and mesmerizing soundtrack—feels like a true work of art. The main storyline can be completed in around 4-6 hours, with full completion taking closer to 10-12 hours. If you're reading this, stop now and go experience it for yourself—you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This is an S-tier indie game.The views are gorgeous, color of the fire is especially vibrant, overall environment is beautiful and interesting to explore.The movement is smooth and fast and has a unique way of putting you in a sense of constant flow.Boss battles are a spectacle in itself with multiple phases, each one of them feels epic.The puzzles aren't very difficult if you are used to such games, reminded me of the puzzles in "Immortals: Fenyx Rising", they are fun to figure out and a nice change of pace between traversing the wilderness.The length of the game is also just right, I've completed it in under 11 hours.10/10 definitely worth playing
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another gorgeous game from Giant Squid with a beautiful minimalist design and a serene atmosphere. Running, jumping and flying around varying nature is so fun and satisfying. Puzzles aren't that hard, but there's many of them to be found.Also, you can pet the eagle AND it's an important part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Even if this isn't your kind of game, I would still highly recommend purely from a unique gameplay experience. Additionally, the ambience and art of this game is phenomenal, absolutely stunning. Very chill and soothing game that, believe it or not, is actually FUN and EXCITING to play; this is unfortunately rare with today's gaming industry. Do give this game consideration if you're willing to branch out to something new.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game. You can blow through it in a few hours if you want, but once I got the hang of it, I savored every minute and nook & cranny. The movement is great, the story is barebones but surpisingly good, and . It's kinda like Breath of the Wild and Journey had a kid. 9/10 will replay, hopefully after I've forgotten most of it
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless envelops you in a mythical atmosphere, where every step flows like a dance, effortlessly guiding you through a world of boundless wonder. The fluidity of movement transforms exploration into a satisfying journey, where puzzles and boss battles unfold gracefully, never punishing, but rather inviting you to uncover their secrets. The game's ethereal music and minimalist visuals weave together, creating an enchanting tapestry that lures you into a captivating embrace. Each moment feels like a poem, a harmonious blend of adventure and serenity. These elements combine to craft an experience that is as mesmerizing as it is unforgettable, making The Pathless a truly exceptional game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The whole game is a quiet dunk on the modern open world genre. No map, No markers, No miserably dull traversal to get to the next thing. Raw gameplay flow takes you between activities and everything is on the same level of being worthwhile to do. The art is incredible. The story and mechanics embody the themes immaculately. Its the kinda game you don't forget
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The game has breath taking visuals when traversing around the map, great soundtrack by Austin Wintory, Interesting puzzles which gel well with the movement mechanic and moving around the world feels satisfying with the arrow mechanics. Overall, it is an excellent game to experience for those seeking for Adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous visuals especially in HDR (using Special K). Hauntingly beautiful soundtrack. Very zen-like experience.If you like exploration, gliding, speed-boosting movement, solving (mostly basic but still rewarding) Zelda-like shrines and interesting yet simple boss fights then you should give this a try. This is one to experience for the journey and the soundtrack, not for any particular challenging game play.  8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I would like to state that I do not think this game is worth 40 dollars in terms of game-play after experiencing it.. Only get this one if it's on sale if at all, it's asking too much for what you get in engagement.What you're mostly paying for here is Annapurna and what they are known for, that being the overall art-style and unique experience, which are always lovely in their own way don't get me wrong, I have enjoyed a few of Annapurna's games before this one. But if you are not familiar with Annapurna's style and are expecting something a bit more substantial or fulfilling, your appetite will not be met here.What will draw you in is a female protag archer in a feudal era-esque time period theme, running around and fighting bosses. Which is true, that is what it is.. But maybe not what you think at first in meeting expectations.Before the criticism let me give the positives:The main enjoyments that I got from this game are the aforementioned art-style and animation; very nice and whimsical and as a fan of ninjas/shinobi and dragon fantasy type stuff it looked cool and got me into it. You will traverse through heavily wooded areas and mountains where there is plenty of space to explore looking for the puzzles you need to complete in the form of castle-like ruins and towers. The movement is incredibly fun because you get to zoom and rush forward with leaps and bounds with every arrow you nail on the talismans that are laid out almost everywhere; smooooth and satisfying. The boss fights pair really well with that, having a really cinematic feel and the way it always has you on the move taking advantage of your everlasting speed boosts. The puzzles laid out across the map leading up to the boss fights are simple enough, pleasant and the whole experience is.. relaxing!Negatives and Criticism:To clarify what I said earlier about appetite, if you are an avid gamer looking for a challenge or an in depth story or even a somewhat lengthy game to keep you occupied then this game is not for you. While it does take a few minutes to get the hang of finding your way around due to not having a map at all, everything about this game is easy. Which is why I say it's more relaxing than anything. It's basically a huge lump of simple-and-straight-forwardness churned up and slathered onto an extra long slice of bread.. but the extra bread doesn't add to the flavor which is mid at best.The puzzles are too straight forward, the boss fights are too simple and end too quickly and there are only 4 of them plus the end bit. There are no health bars on the bosses which was surprising but it's because you literally don't need them with the fight ending so fast. You don't even take damage as a player.. Did I mention that? You do not have hearts, there are no enemies in the map other than the bosses and you cannot die from what I can tell, you just kinda start the last sequence over with no consequence whatsoever and there really isn't much else to do in between those fights other than zip around everywhere which feels empty. The only collection action is the little golden bits you get from the smaller puzzles that make your eagle carrier you a bit higher, which is alright and makes traveling to higher areas easier but there isn't anything else to do or find except for the plentiful and exaggerated "lore" if you want to call it that, scattered around every puzzle that all really say the same thing in the form of woes from warriors who passed trying to fight this great and TERRIBLE "challenging" evil. Which made me laugh honestly after experiencing the fights. So yeah, lore isn't even great, not much story at all, minimal dialogue from the bird mother... Everything is pretty linear and lackluster imo and it get's repetitive and boring really quick.End note:I will say this game is worth it if you are looking for that sort of easy, relaxing, whimsical-natured game to play after work or if you are stressed. Also would recommend for a kid; pretty family friendly other than the very mild looking armored skeletons left around where the "lore" can be found. Would recommend if you are an inexperienced player in general. It's definitely got all that going for it. Simple, aesthetically pleasing, fun. Worth a try.. ..But NOT at the full price, absolutely not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Great art direction as usual from these developers, and this game is more mechanically involved than Abzu. Traversal is fun, yet simple, though it takes some upgrades to get really good. If I had one gripe, it'd be that getting caught by the corruption dome isn't really that scary, and is more annoying to get out of with a very slow stealth section. It's not that hard to evade, though, so it's a minor gripe.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with well-thought-out bossfights, fast paced action and Mongol-inspired mythology. Gameplay contains exploration, zipping around the landscape and discovering lore and puzzles. Some timing-based puzzles can be somewhat challenging and the boss-fights are very satistfying, but mostly this is a game to chill out with and enjoy the care and love that went into the world and mythos.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, Pathless is an absolutely beautiful game with a stunning landscape and a really solid story for a game that might not see much more than 25 hours worth of play. It is very much worth the $40, and I would totally recommend it to anyone.I'd say my favorite part about the game has to be that you can pet your eagle whenever, a feature which I used like 5% of the time because I had to do it because I died to the storm, but the other 95% of the time I used it was because its such a cool, unique and downright adorable feature that the devs did not have to add but they DID add it and I am very glad they did. The connections to Abzu are also cool, but the birb gets first place by far.The primary gameplay loop of the Pathless, after you clear the tutorial, is to explore the big area in front of you while avoiding a certain hazard that I have personally nicknamed "the death storm". The death storm is a stationary hazard that teleports around the map every now and then, but if you get too close to it, it will start to chase you, which when I saw it for the first time, was one of the most riveting and jolting experiences I have had in a videogame, but it can be easily avoided if you know how. As you explore the area you are in, you will find these little sigil things which you use to activate 3 towers.Once you activate the 3rd tower, the death storm homes in on your location and once you enter it, you are prompted to an absolutely amazing first phase of a bossfight I have seen, and thankfully, you get to experience that first phase a total of 4 times throughout the game and it never gets old. After you clear the boss, you can fully explore the area you are currently in without the death storm hunting you down, or you can climb up to the next area and repeat the process again until you have done this a total of 4 times.When I played through the game for the first time, I waited until I fully explored each area before starting the next, and the game does reward you for this, by granting you extra movement abilities which are WELL worth it, though meeting the requirements for these extra abilities can be annoying since you have to scour almost every nook and cranny of the game, but once you figure out the rhythm, it becomes much less annoying.I only have two complaints about the game, the first of which are the puzzles. They are rather simple, which makes them easy to understand, but they are also repetitive since rarely are new elements and mechanics introduced. Once you understand how all the puzzle mechanics the game has work, it only takes a minute or so of exploring the area around the puzzle to figure out what you have to do to solve it.My other complaint is about the 3rd phase of the 3rd boss, which is stupid hard. It throws a lot of challenges at you all at once that it is really difficult to overcome without getting yeeted out of the boss arena. This might be less of a problem if the game placed more emphasis on combat, but it doesn't. There are only 5 times you actually fight in the game, all of which are bossfights. So having the 3rd combat encounter in the entire game be the hardest of the lot is annoying. The trick I found to beating it is to try to move only when needed to dodge an attack and to hold down the attack button. Doing so will only hinder your movement when the boss exposes one of its weakpoints, so when it does, just wait a second, let go of the attack button, and then press and hold it again until it exposes its next weakpoint, rinse and repeat until you defeat the boss.Overall opinion: 9/10. Great game, stunning visuals, captivating story, but the puzzles are simplistic and Nimue is hard af, would totally recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Great thanks to Apple Games for giving a chance to try it out the first time around, but this game is definitely meant for big screen. 10/10 would recomment for anyone who likes roaming around big, beautiful world full of nature and little critters. The puzzles are amazing, and every time you think you've got it all down, the game gives you a new challenge to figure out. And the little secrets? Honestly both happy and disappointed there's no achievement for collecting ALL of them, because I'm pretty sure it'd drive most people crazy. Nothing like thinging you've gotten at least most of them at the location, then coming back for one reason or another only to find out that you missed, in fact, a couple more secrets along the way. The way those secrets are woven into the story, though... From cozy, atmospheric places of worship where you won't mind to stay a bit, to chests hidden among ruined camps surrounded by long since dead guards. Opening them almost feels like a bad omen...Of course, all of it leads to the action-packed moments of glory when the hunted at last becomes the hunter, relentlessly pursuing the prey. The switch feels so stark compared to the usual mode of the game, it only adds to the adrenaline of the boss fights. All in all, cannot recomment it enough: for the story, the worldbuilding, the secrets, and, of course, amazing action. The ending is absolutely worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This is my new favorite game. It's got everything I love- open world, fun movement, interesting lore, fun puzzles, lots of secrets, beautiful graphics, gorgeous music, and of course, a bird friend. As a lifelong birdwatcher I'm super impressed with the animations on the eagle- probably the most lifelike of any bird I've ever seen in a video game. I ended up loving it so much I bought it again on the Switch so I could play it more often- I'm on my third playthrough now. 10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about The Pathless?Well, the first thing I can say is that The Pathless has the greatest movement system I've found in any open-world game, period. Not because it plays like a precision platformer or anything. No, far from it. The game is incredibly forgiving, with no death states and a hilariously easy-to-use aim system. The Pathless knows exactly how to keep a player engaged in moving about the world, in the rush of speed that comes from good timing, without actually being that mentally taxing or difficult. The Pathless has an open area design, but said areas are not packed to the brim with Zelda levels of content. There are only really three types of collectibles, after all. There isn't even a map. The entire game is about the Path you take between those points of interest, the Journey, if you will. I'm sorry, I should probably stop. But it is the first open-area game where I've genuinely had a tone of fun just moving around the world. When people say they enjoy exploring an open world, they usually mean they enjoyed the points of interest, they found unique secrets, they were intrigued by the level design. That's not the case with the Pathless. It's just a joy to move, not even do anything, just move. Oh, sure, there are points of interest, light pressure-platey archery type things. And there are boss fights, and lore dumps, and all of that. But it really is about moving.Also, if you can't tell from the trailers, the game is absolutely gorgeous. It's not a hard game. Like I said, there's no death states. The puzzles aren't exactly head scratchers and the aim system is ridiculously forgiving. If you came here for a hardcore gaming experience, you will not find it. But if you want an interesting, artsy, and very enjoyable experience, well, you are in the right place.I've noted that there are a lot of complaints about repetition. Yes, the game is quite repetitive, and you will get bored after a while. In my experience, the best thing to do is to stop playing the game for a bit. Come back to it later. Not everything has to be played in four hour sessions.Obviously, this is all just my opinion. But The Pathless has one of the greatest responses to the open-world boom I've seen. The Pathless is a gorgeous, incredibly fun, and dare I say atmospheric experience. It's not the most challenging thing out there, but it never needed to be. Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy exploring for exploration's sake, reading snippets of lore about a dead society, that sort of thing, you'll probably like this game. Puzzles are pretty basic, but you wouldn't want brain-busters in this kind of game anyway. Would mess with the vibe. Same deal with the story; simple but evocative. You're here to soak in the visuals and the music, and to pet your pet bird. This game succeeds on the "games as art" axis more than anything.There might be enough content here to justify the price, but for me it's a "wait for sale" type of recommendation. I gave up on 100%ing each area halfway through. There's a lot of open ground to cover and re-cover in between points of interest, which becomes increasingly tedious as you're trying to find the last couple collectibles. I enjoyed myself a lot more by focusing on just getting to the end, but the playtime to cost ratio suffered accordingly if you care about that sort of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and fun game with enjoyable mechanics and clever puzzles. Boss fights rather easy but that seems to "fit" this game. Loved the final form of the Godslayer! Enjoyed the world so much that I went back in after the denouement to achieve 100% completion. If you loved The Pathless, check out Abzu and Journey too!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a wonderful flow game designed to provide a relaxing experience where you wander around with occasional bursts of action at the end of each section. It boasts an amazing atmosphere with a simple yet enthralling story and scenes. Movement in this game is incredibly addictive, making traversing the open world feel fun rather than tedious. The puzzles are very simple, offering a nice break between moving around and staying in the flow of things. Boss fights are definitely an experience, featuring intense changes in music and atmosphere that really get you going. Overall, it’s a pretty fun experience if you are looking for a fast but relaxing flow game in a beautiful world.Recommendations:- Play with a controller. Since you will be moving around a lot, using a stick instead of mashing WASD keys will make the game more relaxing and fun.- If you tend to 100% games, play through the story first and then go back to complete the game later. Progressing through The Pathless will unlock more features that help you traverse the world. This keeps the game from becoming stale, as by the time things start feeling repetitive, the game will introduce new features to keep it interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Note: this review has light gameplay spoilers for Journey. If you haven't played it, I'd recommend you don't read this because it will spoil the ending. Go buy Journey and play it instead - it's one of the best game experiences ever made.The Pathless has a lot of overlap with Journey, but if someone had forced the devs to put in more of the usual videogame tropes. There are boss fights, in-your-face lore, and grindy collectibles, etc. But the flip-side of this is that this game can kinda stretch out and relax a bit. There's a bit of roughness in many of Annapurna Interactive's published titles, and it's definitely in The Pathless - but it adds something I can only describe as the "Indie/AA cozy factor." You've probably come across it before if you're considering buying this game. It's not that the gameplay is the same, but the world feels - despite the very different tone of the story - like it's got traces of things like A Short Hike or Sable in it. The vibes and the simple story are great.The two most successful gameplay-centric additions are the freedom of exploration and the thrill of movement. Journey has glimpses of speed, but - compared to this game - they're rare, not tied to exploration, and you don't get much sense of freedom or power out of it due to the game's linearity and how tightly choreographed the gameplay and narrative progression are in Journey. In The Pathless, you either walk (which feels horrible) or sprint - which drains your energy bar. However, as you move you can autotarget these floating icons in the world with your bow. Shooting them refills your energy (solving the problem of Journey, which in many areas was very stingy with the energy that let you fly) and adding a small element of skill, as you have to release when your bow is fully drawn or the (auto-aimed) shot will miss. In this way, The Pathless is more like The Valley, in that it wants to make you feel - especially as you progress - fast and powerful. Unlike The Valley or Journey, however, this game is effectively open world, and it's a fantastic combination.The puzzles are short and satisfying to complete. For the most part, you won't find yourself having to look up how to do anything (or having to leave a puzzle and come back to it), which is good because this would have really hurt the game's flow. I only remember two puzzles I disliked - one because it was simple but added an element of tight timing that felt really out of place (no other puzzles do this), and another that was basically a "find the hidden switch" - again, there had been no precedent for this being what the puzzles were doing, so it just felt disappointing when I gave up and looked this one up and that was the answer. (Both of these were in the final stage, which is by far the weakest in the puzzle department.) For me, the puzzles were still short enough and simple enough to be satisfying up until about the 75% mark, and I went for 100% completion. The problem is that within each major area of the world, there's no reason to go for any completion of extra content unless you complete 100% of it, which is a major issue because it creates a high incentive to commit to the least fun part of the game (grinding puzzle completion for extra powers). But even then, if it had just been like 20% less grind, I wouldn't be making this criticism.Finally: bosses. I was worried going in that I wouldn't like this part of the game, and that's pretty much true. I am just not into mechanical challenge (fast reactions, learning when to press a button in response to a telegraphed attack, etc.)  in games (see above re: fast puzzle). Because the game is effectively auto-aimed (this is necessary because the majority of the game you are moving far too fast to manually aim at the targets that propel you), boss battles are basically "quick time events" in the exact sense that most players hate - the difference is that you have to hit the mouse button in the context of jumping and/or gliding. I think for players like me, the boss battles aren't fun because what to do is very poorly telegraphed, and the twitch reaction gameplay doesn't fit well with the rest of the game. Conversely, for players who LIKE a mechanical challenge, these will almost certainly feel too easy to be satisfying to beat.What makes up for all these quibbles I have with the game is something that many people wouldn't care about, so I can understand the reviews which give all the caveats above and then rate it negatively. But the art direction and sound design of this game are unbelievably good. The environment design is amazing. The eagle is very cute. I love the look of all the temples and the armor of the fallen soldiers. On the sound side: The voice acting is perfect. The sound of the bosses is the only thing I liked about them other than their look. The ambient sounds of the environment and the rush of movement are incredible. The final battle has the best sound design of anything I can remember in a videogame.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 starsbeautiful game! Great music, awesome art direction & environments, extremely snappy & fluid animation. Story is fine, nothing amzaing. Core gameplay loop can sometimes get a little stale but overall the game evolves *enough* in both difficulty and ability progression to keep me engaged. Traversal is the fun mechanic that you keep coming back, it's just so fun to zip and fly around in this game. This is mostly an exploration & puzzle game but the boss fights are very fun and well designed, and sometimes quite challenging to your reflexes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from some of the same developers who have worked on Journey and Abzu, The Pathless is an action-adventure that is a mix between Breath of the Wild and Shadow of the Colossus. You, a master archer with your trusty bow and your eagle companion, are to liberate an island from the antagonist and his darkness. The Pathless is a crazy fast-paced game where your movement speed is focused around shooting these targets dotted around the map to move faster and faster throughout the map. There are a metric ton of these, so there will not be many interruptions to your speed as you traverse the wide open spaces in the game. The Pathless' combat consists of fighting the boss in each area to cleanse the corruption within. To summon each into combat, you have to light up a beacon tower with tokens around the area. These tokens are often in small places that require a bit of puzzle solving and creative thinking. There's enough variation in this to make it not be boring. As a treat, it is often in this locations that you can learn more about the lore in the form of letters and environmental storytelling. The boss fights are also filled with variety with different ways of offense and defense needed depending on the boss being fought. They are easily the highlight of the game as you inch closer and closer to the end. Lastly, The Pathless has that typical nice indie art style that's found in games such as Journey or Abzu, leading to a memorable visual experience. It's also pretty cool to see some of the Mongolian influences in the game, such as the architecture, the focus on archery, and especially the throat singing found in the soundtrack. Austin Wintory knocks it out of the park in the soundtrack with memorable moments being elevated by his music.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most immersive gaming experiences I've had in a long time - no map, no inventory management, barely any HUD, aiming is pretty much automatic. This is an easy game, which was really refreshing. It's liberating to explore a really beautiful landscape without real fear of death or worrying about health/healing. The puzzles are simple, but engaging - very similar to hunting for korok seeds in Legend of Zelda, and traversal is similar with gliding over the world. The platforming can be irritating at times, but for the most part zooming around the landscape is so satisfying. Definitely a big fan of Giant Squid now, having played Abzu and The Pathless, both games you get to be mindfully present in a beautiful environment. Excited for their next game!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely phenomenal game that may take a lot of patience at first. Between not knowing where to go at first, and exactly what you're doing, its going to take an hour or so get what exactly this game has in store for you. Its a puzzle game with action sequences thrown into the mix, but the majority of it is exploration. I absolutely loved the developers previous game, "Abzu," so I knew it'd be made in a similar vein. The story and world will engage you the further you pursue it, and the puzzles will challenge you.  There are many similarities to BOTW, whether intentional or not. It runs on its own two feet, and that is a good thing. If your'e looking for a beautiful world to explore, with amazing mechanics, challenging puzzles, great soundtrack and an interesting story, give this a try.  Youll dig.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It's fast, fun and simple. The overarching game loop is between a flow-esque game where you fire arrows at floating targets to run faster, and a puzzler where you have to collect certain tokens to progress the story. It's a decent mix of genre and works most of the time, even though both parts of the offering can feel a bit underbaked at times. Puzzles are simple and the running-and-shooting is uninteresting quite quickly. That said, its a short game, clocking in somewhere around 6 hours so it doesn't really wear out its welcome. But I'd love for it to have explored its systems further, its a worthwhile experience, but it often feels a bit surface level.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Time well spent. I loved the gameplay - the smooth running and jumping coupled with arrow shots was so nice and smoothe - so pleasing to the brain. I enjoyed that there were really only main fights and the rest was just exploration at your own pace. I felt so free to do what I wanted. The bird was really cute. Loved the soundtrack. Loved the story. Very much enjoyed the ending. Great game, I'm glad I found it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: incredibly relaxing, beautiful and entertaining.great for people that enjoy exploring a scenery and finding lore bits here and here, which reminded me a bit of zelda64.graphics are gorgeous, art style is really well done.its a short game, and not a challenge. the puzzles and bosses are all easy. this is more about the aesthetics and lore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good, relaxing game. It has a fun movement system, like Abzu and Journey.It has mildly challenging puzzles.It has some visually stunning, mechanically entertaining and fairly easy bossfights.The open world is stunning, it is just big enough to be satisfying but has enough to do that it doesn't get boring.The story is sweet and the lore/backstory you can find around the world enhances it and makes the main villain feel less evil and more misguided.i'd say if you take your time with the game and 100% it, it will give you around 10-15 hours of gameplay.Also you can pet the birb and it even cuddles with you. 37€ well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Such a nothing of a game. It's got the Abzu art style but the gameplay is just exceptionally unengaging. I don't get the rave reviews. You just run around holding left trigger at all times to run and then hold right trigger periodically to shoot something with auto aim. Why not just let you run fast all the time?The puzzles aren't even puzzles. It's just find the box and make the eagle put it on a button.Pretty sure it also bugged and I didn't get music or voice over.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually beautiful, satisfying and smooth to play, with amazing boss fight spectacles that are some of the best I've ever seen in all my gaming years.The star of the show is your movement in the world. It is incredibly smooth and refined. Stringing together shooting talismans scattered across the landscape will accelerate you faster and help maintain momentum. The developers nailed the feeling of this, and gliding across the beautiful landscapes is immensely satisfying. The boss fights in this game a unique, and unlike anything I've seen done before. They take the aforementioned satisfying movement and crank is up a notch, making it faster and more intense as you fight epic, visually awe-inspiring battles of epic-proportions. The story takes a more exploration-driven direction, where you get the basic framework but can expand upon it through discovering old texts, plaques, and fallen warriors. Ultimately the story isn't terribly deep and I wish there was a bit more meat to it, but I can't say I'm unsatisfied given then short overall length of this game. It took me roughly 7 hours to beat while finding all major collectibles and unlocking a secret, extended ending.For $39.99 I think this game is a pretty tough sell. This is an amazing the game, but that's a steep price for only 7 hours of gameplay with a shallow story. I recommend waiting for a sale and picking it up for 50% off or more (which I did), and at that price it's a fantastic experience that anybody who is intrigued should pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: A regret that I will carry with me is that I will never be able to experience this title for the first time again. This work of art was amazing to experience when I first played it through and it is something I will still love to come back to once every few years. A beautiful story that brought tears to my eyes
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible game, stunning on all aspects. The OST is amazing, I'll definitely be listening to it.Relaxing but also engaging, the little puzzles are not difficult but quite satisfying, made so that you can go from one to the next smoothly as you explore. The message of this game is very sweet and well introduced.You can (and have to) pet the eagle.

The fast running and the gliding is really nice. 10/10, beautiful, difficult, enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little adventure for a weekend+ 1. you can clean the bird (run straight to the storm a couple times just to clean the bird, yeah feels good)2. quite facinating hunt like bossfights3. some tricky puzzles-1. you can't choose difficalty, i prefer games to be a little bit more challanging than this.2. little use of combat (just 5 bosses, no trash mobs or sidequest combat encounters ), for openworldy expiriance i'd prefere some guard to the pazzles just to diversify the experienceoverall nice little adventure chase part of the fight is perfect, running through the wild, chasing fantastic creatures, nice
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I played The Pathless! A very beautiful and pleasant game with a satisfying movement system, which does such a great job marrying game-play with storytelling, messaging, and themes. This was clearly intentional and I appreciate it a lot.Most of The Pathless is exploring a beautiful open world and solving simple puzzles, with a few boss fights. This is not a challenging game in the slightest once you get the hang of moving around and shooting talismans with your bow and arrow. Oh! And you have a sweet eagle companion that lets you glide and basically fly as you accrue more flaps.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The game succeeds with an astonishing visual style with many natural 'wow' moments throughout its story. The music and sheer grandness of the landscapes often times had me sucked in and feel the adventure and excitement to discover this world. I was always very intrigued to read the various little lore pieces scattered everywhere, which rarely ever happens in any game I play. While semi-open, it doesn't bring useless fetch quests or sidequests, which I very much enjoyed. Therefore you can focus on the main task at hand and actually feel like a lot has happened in your session. And it does offer itself to be played in several sessions as it's easy to pick up again.But it isn't perfect by any means: The little puzzles you have to do to progress rarely got me invested and repeat their core objective too many times despite always putting a little twist on them. I want to forget the many times I had to wait for my bird to drop a heavy block on a pressure plate for a puzzle I had figured out 5 minutes ago.Furthermore, the movement, while being very enjoyable throughout the first couple of hours, never feels like it has reached its full potential. Flaps slow you down too much, transitions from ground to air and vv. are a bit choppy and never contribute to 'the ideal way' to reach maximum speed to get where you want faster. The bosses also rarely profit from the very good core movement aside from their first phase - which is always the same.This should not be a deterrend from keeping you to play this game. While relatively short, it is well worth your time and my criticism is more as feedback for the developer to hopefully improve on their mechanics and variety in a potential successor.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: one of the most beautiful and awe-inspiring games ive played in a long time. ironically the last one that comes to mind is ABZU, made by the same people and whose soundtrack was composed by the same legendary composer, Austin Wintory. I have a lot of respect for both Austin and Giant Squid, they've made some seriously great things that have filled me with inspiration to make my own seriously great things.everything about The Pathless hits the nail on the head. it's a sublime experience that doesn't forget that it's a video game, and FEELS good to play. since your movement is tied to hitting your mark on floating talismans, you feel like an acrobat precisely taking opportunities through small windows to soar through the air with your eagle companion. 100%ing the game (minus the flight crystals i got 10 flaps and thats all i needed lol) took a very satisfying amount of time without external help, and no challenge was so hard that it would genuinely make me angry, instead any frustration i felt would just fuel the satisfaction i would get once i completed whatever challenge i was doing.I cant find enough good things to say about this game, it's beautifully made, fun, the story is simple enough to follow but still manages to be grand and really make you feel like you're doing something amazing.pick this up if you think you'd enjoy it, show these guys some love
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning. I remember playing Journey when it came out and if you loved that game then you'll love this one. Simple yet satisfying experience. A truly chill game for those times when you need to feel better. You can pet your little bird buddy when he's down on his luck! 10/10Doing everything and just taking your time took me about 12 hours. I recommend dropping it in your wishlist and waiting for a sale as $40 is definitely a bit much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Much like Journey or Abzu, it has a certain calming atmosphere, which matches its gameplay. This game - while having more traditional action than the aforementioned games - is very relaxing and does not require nor force you to grind for collectibles or play a certain way. You can take everything at your own pace while exploring a huge world with charming graphics. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a simple yet satisfying game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, but in no way, shape, or form, is it even worth 20 dollars, let alone 40. I understand that a lot of love and care went into this game, but you have to actually water your plants for them to bear good fruit. The large open world of the game did the exact opposite of what it intended to do for me. Instead of giving me an open world to explore and enjoy, it felt like a massive amount of nothing with multiple points of interest around the area. There's almost nothing to do outside of the points of interest. Once the big red circle starts moving around, it becomes even more problematic, as stealth sections that were involuntary and not tied to progression are forced on the player. It also doesn't help that areas meant to be used as final-boss stages with no puzzles, or areas meant for after defeating that areas boss are outlined in the exact same way as places with puzzles yet to be solved. The scanner that you get to find these places is nice, but the pulsating scan it has is irritating at times, and after completing an area, the constant bright light at the edge of the screen is irritating. Why does that get a constant bit of annoyance and the areas you need to go to otherwise get short pulses. It doesn't help, that again, the massive expanses of nothing somehow add to this problem, because cliffs and trees will block your vision, so you don't really know if you've fully completed an area or not without going high up. It feels like it's trying to not be ABZU, but it fails in that aspect.Story-wise, the game did a good job of presenting itself. It wasn't "story rich" at all though. It's very much a background element of the game. Even if you speedrun through the game, there's not much that's given in a short amount of time. There's really nothing here. Again, this feels like it's trying to break out of it's shell from ABZU.The combat system is fine. You hit points on a target on the boss and they die. It's not what I expected, but then I remembered this game has the tagline "From the creators of ABZU". That made it click. I was expecting something more traditional, maybe with healthbars or actual failure/death, but that never came. I'm happy to have a relaxing experience, but the combat did get very boring at times, and stakes were minimal, at least in my experience.The puzzles themselves were great. However, I feel like they took up a minimal amount of gameplay. This game really is ABZU 1.5. Traversing through the world took up most of the time I spent playing. It sucks, because I enjoyed the puzzles, but rarely were they intricate or clever enough to be worth the minute or several minute long trek to them. Again, the big red storm cloud that moves around and sometimes chases the player did not help here, as these puzzles would get covered up by them, forcing players to do things in a usually much slower order. I love the idea of the movement. I like the auto-aim hitting the targets and moving faster. What I hated was the implementation. Sprinting was awful. Toggle or no toggle, it was terrible and felt like ice-skates were on me. You don't auto-sprint after landing from flying, which is fine, but you can't change it, and you can't choose to sprint once you land by pressing the sprint button while in the air. God forbid you do press it before you land, because you'll have to press it after you land in order for it to detect that you're sprinting. It's really fun on the boss fights where speed matters most.Speaking of the bosses, they were fine. I really enjoyed the arkham-asylum scarecrow sort-of sequence. That puzzles was fun. The bossfights overall were actually fun, but the chasing them down and shooting them was boring as hell. It was extremely tedious, and they lacked any difficulty or content in general. It was as fun as running through the nothing sandwich that the world is in this game.On to designs, every single design is amazing, except for 2. The evil version of the bird is lame as hell. It just has 2 heads. This was an amazing opportunity to turn it into a dragon or a phoenix, and it wasn't taken. The Godslayer's final phase was also really boring. It felt cheap and uninspired. Every other boss was amazing too, so I was really looking forward to fighting these guys. That made it especially hard to watch the last two bosses get thrown down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The message of the game is one I really like. If you care, I'm gonna spoil it here. The message of, "No path is the right path for everyone." is honestly a great message. An ancient phrase of "one man's trash is another man's treasure" is basically what the game tells us. What is going to work for you might not work for me, and vice versa, and that's okay.On to the tags that this game has. This is something I have a gripe with. Calling this an "archery game" is like calling Terraria a shooter because it has guns. There's no exploring in this game either. It's a massive walking sim, with no beauty that ABZU had to warrant it. There's a story, but it's not the focal point. The message is the only focal point that's given. You can't call your game story rich just because lore is scattered around your world. Firewatch is story rich, and it costs half of the price of The Pathless. And congrats on having a 3d game. Lethal Company is 3d as well, and it's a quarter of the price, and I already have more hours on it. Finally, I have a 1 dollar per hour rule, where I believe a game is worth it if it can provide content equal to its price point in hours. This game should have 40 hours of content. It doesn't even have 20. I nearly have this game at 100% and I have just under 9 and a half hours on it. What's around 6 achievements really going to do to change that playtime? In a game like this. it'll do jack all. This game is barely worth it on sale under my criteria. Even breaking my criteria, this game is not worth 40 bucks, and I'd say it's not worth 20. This game felt like it was trying to not be another ABZU, and it really shows. The game feels like it's taking steps in that direction, but it feels like half ABZU and half what it wants to be. It's like a crossbreed of any dog with a corgi. Its body is going to end up being a corgi's almost no matter what. I hope that the devs make something like this in the future, but separate it from ABZU more, or instead go all in on what made ABZU great. This half and half mix is a slog to play through, and it didn't have to be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: What happens when a very competent team switches from making scenic exploration walking simulators to something more action focused?You get  a scenic exploration walking simulator... with bosses!A lone archer finds herself in a struggle to purify the spirits of the land from the Godslayer’s influence before the world is no more. A very simple hook that feels like a passed-down fairytale.There is not much besides a message on environment and destiny or lack thereof of one, still the story is not forced on you as you’ll be mostly engaged with the gameplay.Jump, shoot arrows, run and glide at the speed of the wind.Controls are very minimalistic, but in no way shape or form this makes them bad, on the contrary, they’re easy to grasp and always do what you want them to.You’ll be exploring the various plateaus and in points of interest some puzzle-solving to access the boss of each zone.The momentum of this game is incredible, looks good and feels big enough to accommodate it and make it shine.One great inclusion is one of talismans, little targets that when shot will refill your stamina for your running, and while shot on the run will give you a further burst of speed, this way both giving you something to do while going from place to place while silently guiding you towards secrets and landmarks.Bossfights are incredibly cinematic experiences, having no hut plus and incredibly stylized look along with many phases the fight become something you wish more games did.Music, scene composition, design, and visuals aren’t to be slept on either, all aspects that help elevate the game even more.Frame drops...Heavy frame drops.This game runs silky smooth most of the time, but at random times when you have in view too many elements of the overworld your frames will tank hard.On a side note, while the sense of speed is what really sells this game, the few times you need to do some precision platforming it works against you as having too much momentum and no tools to halt it immediately will make you overshoot some platforms.Story is so easy to grasp that searching for spirits and tablets to understand the tale of this world won’t say much as the lore is very simple.There isn’t much else to say, a very good game that is a great addition to any library.Now, 40 bucks isn't exactly a bargain for its duration but it's quality time, and sales certainly help in this aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. Petting the bird (WHENEVER YOU WANT) is one of the best things about it tbh. It's also very pretty to look at, satisfying to complete with smooth and satisfying mechanics. It does get a bit repetitive as the puzzles feel quite samey and easy to complete but I enjoyed being a little bit of a completionist. The bosses are pretty nifty and unique but the difficulty scaling is a bit out of wack which can be a little off-putting considering general gameplay is easy peasy lemon squeezy. That being said, I eagerly completed it and did a bunch of extras so take that as you will! I definitely recommend picking this game up and trying it if it's on sale. It's a fabulous candidate for those 100% achievement folks, too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game I have played in 4 years.The Pathless is the only game I have played in 4 years that actually compelled me enough to not have a podcast in the background or just speed through the game. I am not a huge puzzle guy, kinda hate em', but The Pathless has such fun puzzles that aren't too difficult but also not annoyingly just there for the sake of it, that I have replayed it and spent hours just because I wanted to 100% it and find all the secrets and solve all puzzles. The lore and overall story is not era changing but its really, really good and I would watch a movie of it. The graphics are beautiful, although not groundbreaking. The audio is genius and lovely, once again, didn't even have to have a podcast or music in the background to enjoy it, I even have some of the songs on spotify now.Should you buy? Yes, absolutely.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: decided to play the game after finishing ABZU by the same developers, and it was absolutely worth it!the environments are beautiful, and are only made better by the phenomenal soundtrack. whether it was navigating the world with the movement mechanics, solving puzzles, or simply soaring through the sky and admiring the view, the game allows you to take your time to soak it in.the puzzles in the game are fairly simple but fun. sometimes the bossfights can be a bit frustrating and the movements a tad clunky, but overall it didnt affect my enjoyment of the gamei finished the game with 100% achievements. if youve enjoyed Journey or ABZU, youll probably enjoy this one as well! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Giant Squid already showed with Abzu that they mastered the way of creating games with a zen like flow and atmosphere. The Pathless follows the same path, and throughout my roughly 13 hours of gameplay,I experienced nothing but tranquility and a sense of inner peace.If you're a fan of Studio Ghibli's Princess Mononoke, you'll discover numerous similarities in The Pathless. While playing, I found myself recalling the movie frequently, making it perhaps the closest we'll come to a Mononoke video game.It probably has the most helpful and charming companion out of any game I've played recently. Every time I could pet the eagle, my heart jumped with joy; his animations and demeanor felt so lifelike. he is also very well integrated into the puzzles and traversal aspects. At the end of our journey, i really felt melancholic when it was time to say goodbye.The puzzle design may become repetitive over time, and, with a few exceptions, the lore bits are quite basic. The initial three areas seemed somewhat monotonous and perhaps less spectacular, especially when compared to the final area. Despite this, the boss fights were expertly telegraphed, delivering a cinematic and epic experience. Even though you are practically invincible, there's still a rush of adrenaline in each one, creating a compelling contrast to the otherwise calm and peaceful nature of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The art direction is next level stuff, and the story, while short and lean on dialogue, is surprisingly profound. The gameplay is fairly simple and very easy. The majority of your time is spent traversing (by running and gliding, and arrowing floating talismans that give you stamina and a boost in speed) and solving very simple puzzles. Solving puzzles gives you currency to light a tower. Lighting three towers in an area (there are three areas) allows you to fight the area boss. these sections are a real spectacle, but the gameplay is very limited. The game's traversal is the funnest part, and the rest is more of an interactive fantasy adventure. I don't think there are any failstates in the game, just inconveniences during a fight, dragging it on until you finally learn the cadence of the fight. It was beginning to overstay it's welcome, but then the story wrapped up and I was very pleased. I think to 100% this game would be a chore, and probably not worth it.Side note: I purchased this game for $17 on sale and it's absolutely worth it for that. Some people might think this game isn't worth the full asking price of $40. I'm on the fence about it, but this game has some incredible moments, and it's basically flawless in it's execution, at least where spectacle and art direction are concerned. this game runs on the steam deck OLED at 40fps beautifully, with some tweaks. I also played this on a PC on an OLED tv. If at all possible, play it on an OLED. There are many scenes and areas that have incredible contrast that an OLED screen really showcases.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Cruise around the wasteland with your bird (and petting them uncontrollably). Travel with extreme speed and grace. Solve puzzles and find out that you don't need to overthink it. Battle against corrupted gods and a poser to essentially make everyone pathless. All using a bow, assist of our friend(s), and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ solid determination.Firstly, this game's artstyle is beautiful. I love almost everything about it. Every sections are very well put together, and flows seamlessly. Everything is just simply gorgeous.Traversal is so fun. I think it is subjective, because I can see how it can be boring for people. But me personally I loved it. The only thing that hinders the movement flows is water. I think if theyd make that she could run across water it would be so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. but oh well.I think the whole sections is a little bit too empty (which makes sense) but there should at least one psycopath homeless man residing in the evil god's territory. That's just how humans usually are, they adapt to every situations. But you dont get to meet any other humans. As only corpses leave lores and it's kinda unfortunate. Also the main character really is just one dimensional. But her interactions with the birdo is cute so I still give her a passAnyways great game(9+/10)
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I played Praey for the Gods recently, which was a game that was trying to do a spin on Shadow of the Colossus that just did not work. Everything that made that game not work absolutely works in this game. It's like playing a Ghibli movie, especially the high production value monster fight scenes.Not a difficult game at all because the focus is very much on the story and the vibe, makes good use of the movement mechanics and the whole thing is very cinematic. It's pricey for a nine hour experience though, so I'd get it on sale. Worth whatever you pay though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: In general it's fun, but the storms are atrocious,Each new area they spawn on top of you until you get caught once, which is incredibly frustrating; you are punished no matter how well you play.  And then when you get caught, 50% of the time the spirit just appears on top of you near the end and you lose with no recourse. Very not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Picked it up on a whim, and glad I did. It's poignant, fun, and unique. Just when I thought the main mechanic was starting to get dull, I discovered the skillshot and got right back in.Only real complaint is that the puzzles get a bit repetitive, though the final area does introduce at least one new component to them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games I've played. BotW level exploration and discovery, but dense with content rather than requiring countless hours to complete. The only game I've played to make the raw act of moving around a giant landscape fun.And it's a Giant Squid game and has Austin Wintory on the music, so you know that it's absolutely beautiful.Story could be a bit better though. But damn if those boss fights didn't feel intense, even if they weren't actually difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone has a movie/song/game/book that they admit maybe isn't all that great but they love it. I'll admit The Pathless has some really really big flaws but I love it.Basically every level is the same, the puzzles are taken from a garbage can after a Tomb Raider meeting, it's dumb to make Souls-like bossfights where you can't die, etc.But it feels so good to play! It's a joy! Smash an arrow into a golden target for a boost and hit another for a vertical lift just before a cliff it rocks. Sorry. Love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review for a game before but THIS GAME i have to. Honestly its perfect to me. I usually play all sorts of games and this one is in the top 10 I think. The music is so fitting for the game and the puzzles are a decent challenge. They aren't too hard to where you want to give up and not play anymore. I found myself getting lost to how much time I played it in one day. The art is so beautiful as well. The boss fights are so mesmerizing to look at that you almost forget you're fighting a boss. Overall this was such an amazing game to play and i'm glad I gave it a chance!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Cool platformer with some puzzle solving elements. Great environments and the music is phenomenal. Storytelling is quite good, too. Some of the platforming can get repetitive/clunky, and I had a bear of a time keeping the Unreal engine from crashing like crazy (especially during the final boss sequence. That took me 8-9 times to figure how how to keep it from crashing.)Good for a playthrough, though I'm glad I waited for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, pretty fun game. Get ALL the collectibles, the puzzles are fun and the upgrades abilities are cool, and without them you can't see the extended ending. Very atmospheric, good music. The only two voice actors in the game are Laura Bailey and Troy Baker which I think is funny because despite this game's unique identity it still hired the most prolific and AAA voice actors ever. It is a little distracting, lol. The stealth sections are also annoying, and very hard. I beat the entire game and didn't get the achievement for beating them three times. I only ever succeeded twice. Probably the only part of the game that isn't at least good, I think they are genuinely kinda bad. But not enough to bring down the experience.It has a cute eagle in it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful experience. There is a very thin line between having an interactive story and a game with a good story. I think they had a great balance here. You can't "die" in the game, at all. Basically, you'll finish the game, no matter what, lol... But It still challenges you in its forgiving gameplay. The puzzles are nice, not too complicated, but make your brain work a little bit. The art style is fantastic, and frankly, reminds me a little bit of shadow of the colossus. It has a GIGANTIC gorgeous map with stuff to do IN it, but the only bad guys are the bosses in the game. Each of which are unique, and are fun to fight. There's only a few, but the game doesn't outstay its welcome. You could probably finish it a few hours faster than I did, but I went around and messed about in the world, enjoying the movement and the scenery. There's pretty much no replay value, but the time I did spend with it, I enjoyed. Good job.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals, big fan of the dynamic music system, interesting movement mechanic with the lock on to the talismans across the plains, and a lot of little platformer puzzles to do between boss fights. Very forgiving boss fights too.Sometimes the puzzles took away from the fast flowy movement portion, but i kind of assume you're supposed to do the bare minimum number of puzzles to speed run and the rest are for replayability.worst bug i saw was the random animal companions would go slow motion and burst into sparkles if they ran into ruins.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning and the music could not be better! If you are looking for a nice video game with puzzles and an original way of getting around (i.e. shooting talismans with the bow to increase speed), you will love this. The completion of the main story is not very challenging and if you want to do all the puzzles (which is not necessary to complete the story) you will probably find them repetitive, but overall a very beautiful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very beautiful game with interesting plot and scenery. But, I feel like it was confused between wanting to be an RPG or a "calm game about exploration (like the previous games of the studio like "ABZU" or "journey")" and because of that, it kinda failed in both. It had boss fights and other events that made you feel urgency but there were no consequences.  It had way too many colectibles but the game helped you find them. You learned the lore from exploration but it was soo much scattered thet some parts of it was not clear. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The game is far too in love with its movement system and doesn't consider that it's incredibly cumbersome to make precise actions which are required for multiple puzzles that get super annoying. There's also many places where they strip half your moves and expect you to hobble into solving some puzzles. There's also tons of minor annoyances like how much time it takes to pet your eagle, having to aim at every single talisman all the time (which probably single handedly used up the lifetime of my RT switch), the massive environments that don't really have much going for them, how time slows when you use detective vision, the completely unnecessary stealth sections and so on. The puzzles also really aren't particularly challenging or complex. One boss battle in particular is also incredibly irritating to get through and requires that you know that you don't always have to fill the arrow bar to shoot and hit the target. The story is also nothing to write home about and is bog standard, tropey, hero's journey through and through.That said, it's a beautiful, well scored and fairly engaging open world puzzle platformer that's mostly pretty good. None of my complaints are offensively bad and I was invested enough to keep going. If you're just looking for a relatively short, open world, checklist type adventure game then this might be for you
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: - At this point, I'd be more surprised if a game published by Annapurna weren't pretty to look at. Even by that standard, The Pathless is often a very pretty game- It's a marked improvement from Giant Squid's previous game, Abzû. It's not that Abzû was unpleasant to look at (on the contrary, it was also quite scenic), but now the spacious environments this team apparently likes to create aren't so barren and featureless. Level designs are peppered with ruins, caves, and forests that often contain puzzles or offer a good viewpoint for getting the lay of the land- The character and boss designs are also interesting. I like the little motifs like the extra eyeballs and forked tails that unify the way they look- The music was fairly somber and relaxing. Appropriate for the overall mood of the game, but it's not the type of soundtrack you'll find yourself thinking about days later- Speaking of mood, The Pathless is a pensive, philosophical game that gives you plenty of time to absorb its peaceful settings- The narrative is dropped progressively as you find and read the last thoughts of the spirits that scatter the almost entirely unpopulated land you explore- The central thesis of the game's message is essentially summed up in a memorable line towards the end of the game, "The truth is a pathless land." The game's plot mostly serves as an allegorical vehicle to drive that point home- Beyond that, there's not much meat on the bones, narratively or rhetorically speaking- As you traverse each of the game's large environments, you're accompanied by your trusty bow and your eagle buddy who helps you solve puzzles, access higher locations, and glide from place to place. Your bow is primarily used for shooting small boost icons that scatter the maps, which cause you to run faster and jump higher. In tandem, these two mechanics can help you navigate swiftly from place to place despite each level's verticality- Your eagle's flap ability works as an extra jump and is the only upgradeable ability in the game. You obtain experience for it by solving puzzles- Puzzles can be easily located with a spirit vision ability that highlights points of interest in a glowing fog. In addition to experience, you might also be rewarded with a special crest- Collecting these crests is important for unlocking the boss sequence in each level. When using your spirit vision to look for puzzles, you'll encounter large towers. You'll have to ascend a certain number of these in each level, insert 1 or 2 crests, and move to the next one- After lighting all the towers in a level, you'll initiate a chase sequence that requires chasing the boss down and shooting its weak spots while on the run. Succeeding here will take you to the boss fight, where you'll have to dodge and shoot your way to victory- The boss fights begin to feel repetitive by the end. The chase sequences are all basically identical, and their attacks during the fights also feel fairly similar- Beyond what I've already mentioned, there's poorly-designed stealth sequences that are fortunatley brief. These are only triggered if you try to enter the roving boss area before lighting each tower (or otherwise find yourself caught in its path as it moves around the map)- Given the repetition and shallow mechanical depth for every system besides movement, I'm not feeling motivated to replay this anytime soon- I found myself wanting a little more of everything out of the game. It's pretty and moving around is kinda fun, but more variety in puzzles, bosses, weapons, abilities, or combat would have gone a long way to improve the experience- Minimalism in game design can be done well when a single idea or mechanic is explored and used creatively, but a game having multiple shallow systems tacked onto one good one just feels unsatisfying- The game ran flawlessley, but then again, it's not a program that'll work your setup too hard- . The game isn't without its charm and the overall message is nice, but like the developer's previous game, it winds up feeling like a pretty experience that lacks substance. Worth a playthrough on a sale if you want a chill action-adventure game that's heavy on the adventure bit, but don't go in expecting too much
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite aspect of this game is how it makes the experience of speed accessible. I don't think this is a difficult game, and it's not trying to be either, you're mostly just solving environmental puzzles after all (which I found pretty engaging, surprisingly so) and the traversal between said environmental puzzles in the massive landscape is just pretty damn fun. The "boss fights" if you can call them that, are the icing on the cake, and really make the game a lovely little casual adrenaline rush, which I don't think any other casual game manages to achieve. Usually, if you want adrenaline from your game, it requires quick reflexes, lots of dexterity, practice, high stakes, etc. This game manages to feel intense without any of those, and I think even my grandma could play it. That's a good thing! <3

_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Giant Squid is in a league of their own; they continue to make visual master pieces that have a soundtrack that partner so well it never fails to astonish me. These games re-define narratives and continue to make truly emotional stories that everyone can relate to. The Pathless moved me to tears and just like their previous works Abzu and Journey; this game should be experienced by everyone at least once. These games have the ability to emotionally connect with the player and use that connection to build more and more investment into the story and its charters. Not to mention the buttery smooth movement mechanics and the perfectly balanced arc in difficulty meeting the expertise and skill of the player with the progression and time in game. Truly, I cannot say enough about how much this studio takes care in their games and more importantly their stories; all I can say is I am eager to play there next work of art Sword of the Sea.

_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game that doesn't reach it's full potential.The Pathless is a wonderful experience. It's contemplative, breathtakingly beautiful and has a nice story. If you enjoyed games like Abzu (go check it out!), then this one may be for you.Compared to Abzu, the movement added here can make the game incredibly fun to play and makes it enjoyable to travel over the huge (but still unique and detailed) map. There is a clear progression and storyline even though the game really feels open. Special mention for the final boss which I found super fun. Sadly, a few things prevent this game from being one of my very favorites:- It takes a long time to get started. Be patient for the first hour or two. I initially abandoned the game and am glad I picked it back up in the end.- It is quite repetitive. Once the main story is started you'll basically do the same thing over and over again with small variations. This isn't a problem in itself, you just have to know it.- Movement has issues: The combination of dashing and gliding can be incredibly fun. But the controls have issues and the hero doesn't always do what I expect. This is in contrast to the moments of pure joy doing huge chains of glides and dashes.- The game is missing a way to visit the world after the story. Find all the last secrets and enjoy the land. Maybe see the animals you freed roaming the world.All in all, I think the game would have needed some more refinement, and Giant Squid being a small studio, it is very much possible they didn't get the chance. Still, thank you for making this wonderful little game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece from Giant Squid but this time with more gameplay elements. The Pathless is an open world puzzle adventure game, but don't let the open world trick you into thinking this is some sort of Elden Ring or a Ubisoft game, the Open World is really just there  so you have the freedom to tackle all of the puzzles in any order and of course, so you can marinate in the beautiful world in peace without being forced to move in a straight line. And I cannot emphasize how beautiful the world is enough. Puzzle solving is really really good. They can range from simple one step puzzles into complex multi layered ones, I'm not good with puzzles so the puzzles here really had me racking my smooth brain and that gets me engaged. Boss fights are very well designed, each one of them are unique but they are all incredibly bonkers and intense. And of course, the beautiful art style and soundtrack, pretty much a Giant Squid signature at this point, one of the best if not the best out there. And I'm not gonna talk about the story, but if you played Abzu you know what you're getting into. Lots of environmental story telling, though we have more dialogues and lines of lore here, and of course all the symbolisms.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is an absolute masterpiece of a game! From its stunning graphics to its mesmerizing gameplay, this title truly has it all. The game's unique combination of puzzle-solving, exploration, and action makes for an incredibly engaging and enjoyable experience.One of the standout features of The Pathless is its breathtaking visuals. The game's art style is simply gorgeous, with a vibrant color palette and beautifully detailed environments that truly transport you to another world. The game's sound design is also top-notch, with an immersive soundtrack that perfectly complements the gameplay.Speaking of gameplay, The Pathless is truly a joy to play. The game's open-world setting allows for plenty of exploration, and the puzzles and challenges you encounter along the way are both challenging and satisfying to solve. The game's main mechanic, the ability to shoot arrows to gain speed and glide through the air, is incredibly fun and intuitive to use.But what really sets The Pathless apart is its story. The game's narrative is both emotional and compelling, and the relationship between the player and their animal companion is truly touching. The game's themes of redemption and forgiveness are explored in a way that feels both authentic and impactful, making for a truly memorable gaming experience.Overall, The Pathless is an absolute must-play for any fan of action-adventure games. With its stunning visuals, engaging gameplay, and powerful storytelling, this title is a true masterpiece that is sure to stay with you long after the credits roll.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is quite simple, though that's not to discredit it in any way. I think it's well-written and it certainly captivated me. I also enjoyed exploring the world and finding bits of lore scattered across, gaining more of an insight into what was actually happening.The visuals are great. From the stunning world, to the boss fights and even the movement of the Hunter, it all looks really nice. Great choice of art style too.The soundtrack is fantastic. It quickly became one of my favourite video game soundtracks.The gameplay is good, but kind of repetitive. Basically, you arrive in a new area, you get a very quick introduction of the boss you'll have to fight, then you run around solving some puzzles and collecting lightstones which will let you initiate the fight. Now, despite the repetitiveness, I still very much enjoyed the boss fights - I think they're great.The puzzles are nice and fairly simple, but even they end up becoming a bit samey after some time. Maybe you won't feel this as much if you only do the bare minimum that's necessary for progressing the story, but if you decide to go the "completionist route" be prepared to do a lot of the same things.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game with spectacular boss fights and scenery. The majority of the game you'll be running around exploring an island.
