_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game, that went unfairly unnoticed because of Epic Game Store exclusivity. I had zero expectations for it and anticipated something similiar to Giant Squid's previous game - Abzu. What I got instead was the freshest take on open world I experienced in years.To state the obivious - The Pathless is a beautiful game, both visually and musically. Colors are vibrant and contrast each other nicely. Each area you visit has very different look and theme, from green plains through red autumn forest to snowy mountain peaks. You get to experience each zone with at least 4 variations too. At first you explore the land in its corrupted state, with giant creatures of darkness and flame roaming the place, hunting you. Once you trap the area's boss by cleansing three towers in the area, weather changes to dark and stormy, drastically changing the atmosphere in anticipation of coming boss fight. Once you challenge the boss the chase begins and you have to keep up with the beast and shoot it  while the area gets covered in roaring flames. After defeating the boss you cleanse the land of darkness and corruption, giving it a sunshine covered, almost idyllic look.All these transformations and events are accompanied by music, setting a perfect tone to the goings-on. Overall sound design is spot on, nothing feels out of place and music often changes to match the speed of your traversal. Rarely does a game feel so inseparable from its sound and music, in The Pathless they are in perfect harmony.Fortunately outside of audio-visual feast The Pathless has a gameplay to match. While the only combat you will experience is with game's bosses, each fight is different and exciting. The mechanics are simple, but polished to shine and keep evolving through entire game. Outside of combat you will explore a lot and solve many enjoyable puzzles, that while not especially challenging keep things varied and satisfying.Most enjoyable aspect of gameplay for me was exploring this world. It is so fascinating and rewarding, that you want to visit every nook and cranny. There is no map in The Pathless and while you can use Spirit Vision to highlight unexplored areas in the world, you need to actually see them for them to highlight. That requires you to climb tall buildings and mountains and really look at this world and take note of points of interest. This is no Ubisoft slog, there is no tedious checklist or map filled with overwhelming amount of icons, in The Pathless you really feel like you are exploring this island and it feel amazing.I can easily recommend The Pathless to anyone, its accessible and finishing it in 100% takes a solid 12 hours. It doesn't really have a replay value, but what you experience during these 12 hours is rare in gaming. It made me fully immerse myself in its world and story. I really hope Giant Squid expands on this game's concept and create more worlds for us to visit.

_childDocuments_.review: So, the main game with mostly complete exploring took about 10 hours for me to finish and I'd say that alone made this worth the buy. I'll begin this review by saying this is genuinely one of my favorite games after finish, easily in my top 10 list. I will admit, this game is simple and repetitive, but I do not see that as a problem, I liked combo-ing the talismans and zooming across the land to my next target and solving puzzles ( some of which were quite tricky although I am rather daft lol). For those who do not want any spoilers, this game was totally worth the money and time IF you like lore and relaxing exploring. Art direction and story was amazingly executed. Looks: 9/10Gameplay: 10/10Sound: 10/10Story: 8.5/10Let me say it again, this game is for people who like exploration and story, if you're one of the people who want to rush through to get to the boss battles and hates the puzzles and everything about the game other than the combat then this game simply was NOT made for you. That's not an excuse but a definite fact, just as how a horse game is made for horse people and would most likely not be fun for people who do not like horses, so if you do not like finding lore or the long travel in games without fast travel why are you here? This applies to all games, CoD is probably a good game, but I dislike it because I do not enjoy shooters, does not make it a bad game overall. This games main gameplay is exploring and finding the islands story with breaks of action inbetween and not the other way around. If you're a puzzle/exploring enjoyer and still didn't like this game.. Valid, your opinion is valid. Not everyone will like all games and I'm not mad, I hope you find another game you like more.In the end, I'm really satisfied with this game for what it was. And I want to share it with my friends and let them experience this story as well. Definitely will replay this game soon. PET THE BIRD 10/10 JUST BECAUSE YOU PET THE BIRDNow for the spoilers: You have been WarnedSome may have wanted more varied sneak sections or chase scenes but I liked it just as they were, The over-world 'threat' was more of an annoyance by the end of it constantly being where I want to go but that was sort of the point, it was supposed to be an obstacle to force you to either face it or go elsewhere while it cleared. The chasing was super fun to me, dodging and weaving through the fire and building speed to get to the tall ones side to shoot the eyes. It reminded me very much of the shrine quest in BoTW where you clean the dragon Naydra of her curse. It was a good intro to the following boss fight. And speaking of, the boss battles in my opinion were incredible. Similar enough for you to gain skill from a previous battle but different enough to keep you on your toes, and the cursed designs were so innovative and freaky they really worked well. Godslayers final battle was definitely living up to the hype in my opinion.Speaking of, Godslayer was incredible. IMO a God-Tier villain in design and story with an obviously incredible voice performance by TROY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BAKER?? His voice worked so well together with Godslayers appearance and it did not feel out of place at all. Also props to Laura Bailey for being everywhere I look, she did a phenomenal job bringing Hunter to life. And whoever did the voice for Eagle Mother, very soothing.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is an open world adventure game from the Giant Squid studio – the creators of magnificent ABZU. Back in the day when I firstly saw the game on E3 I honestly thought it would be some sort of a platformer because making a full-fledged open world 3D indie game is quite difficult, and making a good one is much harder. Nonetheless, the studio managed to succeed despite all the odds but not without certain problems that I will specify lower.First things first, graphics are wonderful. The game keeps a great balance between quality and style: the sceneries look majestic and traversing the locations is a pleasure. The developers, though, could have created more textures to make the sites look more diverse but I guess it’s a sort of a price they had to pay for the open world. The only thing I can really nitpick to is collisions of objects in boss fights and cutscenes: again, I understand that is an indie game but when in a pre-rendered cutscene up-close you see how the character’s bandana is fluttering through the bow it kind of breaks the atmosphere and perception of the world.Speaking about the soundtrack, it was composed by Austin Wintory and this already means that the music just cannot be bad. The tracks are great, fit the game and make your journey very atmospheric. Though objectively there are not that many memorable compositions that you will relisten afterwards it does not cancel the fact that the music itself is gorgeous and soundtrack is worth a separate purchase. The story of The Pathless, unlike ABZU, is much less obscure at least because you get direct text describing the characters and events. The lore and plot themselves are quite simple and will hardly provide any revelation for the player but it is certainly entertaining to unravel them via gameplay which we will talk about in a moment. In addition, the fans of ABZU will get their share of easter eggs and potentially may find deeper connections between the two games.Now, let’s talk about the gameplay, which is a bit controversial. On the one hand it is interesting to travel through the lands and discover various sites, nonetheless, on the other hand that is basically everything you’re gonna do 95% of the time. Sure, all of the landmarks have some sort of a puzzle to solve, however, in reality, it is hard to call those spatial problems puzzles as they mostly require not your wits but your attention (and rarely reaction time), so looking for a solution also becomes an exploration. Of course, The Pathless was never advertised as a puzzle game but the developers could include a bunch of harder ones for the dedicated players: I don’t think this would make the game worse. There is also no map of any kind in the game. Though eventually you climb the high ground and can look over the level to see the sites you missed, it would be really useful to have at least a basic one. However, despite all of the gameplay drawbacks it is very addictive. You are eager to travel from site to site, find every little detail, and by thinking “one more landmark and that’s all” you may eventually find yourself discovering all of the notable locations around. Another 5% of the gameplay is boss encounters and battles. The first ones will definitely happen several times during the game and if the first 2-3 ones are interesting to play, later they become quite irritating. Good thing that the developers knew about the problem, so these encounters can be avoided relatively easily later in the game and once you clear a certain area they vanish completely. As for the boss battles, they are, just like the core gameplay, controversial. They are not bad in itself but it seems that the developers were too focused on making a relaxing game, so the battles are unlosable. You will never see a “game over” screen and there is no real punishment for bad fighting. Last but not least, the bow-shooting gameplay. I cannot say it is great but the final solution is solid. Instead of need to aim and calculate the bowstring tension you can either hold the button for long and definitely hit the target or you can try to release it at a certain moment and hit the target fast but miss if you don’t hit the timing. In conclusion, The Pathless is a good indie game and an interesting experience. I would gladly want to say that only real problem is repetitive gameplay which will bore you if you try to finish the game in one go but, unfortunately, there is a 40$ price tag. Though I respect Giant Squid and Annapurna Interactive, it is just way too high! You can buy a 2-3 year old AAA game for this price and get much more diverse gameplay and longer playtime. So, I would recommend buying The Pathless only with a 50% discount unless you really want to support the developers and play the game. All in all, if you are looking for a relaxing experience with a bit of boss fights The Pathless will certainly be enjoyable for you, however, if you want something challenging and gameplay-deep I would advise skipping this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended if on a  sale.Like 60% - 90% steep.The visuals, movement and music are absolutely enjoyable, but that's really all the meat there is to it - and really rather lean at that.Exploration can be fun, but it's really all rather generic fantasy meadows, monuments & forests - it's desperately lacking that exotic uniqueness that the ABZÛ setting could leverage. Equally, the movement  fun, but it's exactly , which struggles to carry this game all the way. There's really no reason at all to tie the sprint to a meter - except to give players something to arbitrarily level up.Then by the end, if you are diligent with your puzzles, you have so much sprint- & air-time, that you likely needn't engage with the movement mechanic basically  for the last quarter of the game. Just boost up into the sky and hang-glide everywhere...The puzzles are all very formulaic - light all the torches, shoot through all the rings, weigh down all switches, etc.Not difficult in the slightest. If you can't solve one, it's 100% because you've not yet looked around & into every corner to find the missing interactive piece.What's especially galling is that all the puzzles, all the upgrades to your flight-ability you're getting, are . You could only do the utter minimum necessary to reach the bosses and the bossfights would  be more difficult.On top, quite frankly, the asking price is  for this kind of  - I hurt to say this - generic content. 40 bucks is incredibly stiff.It's a game to spend two, maybe three afternoons on and then probably not ever think about again - not a spellbinding journey through interesting lore, not an intoxicating challenge, or even that much of a visual design spectacle.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun for people who like good puzzle games, it also has breathtaking imagery and the bird is cute and the soundtrack slaps.  However, the movement mechanic altho simple, is very repetitive so after 2 hours you get bored, this is very noticable if you're going for the 100% achievements like I did. _childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless feels like Breath of the Wild, the ease with which you can get lost just running through the world is almost identical. The simple loop of run, arrow shot into a glide off a cliff, and then serenely gliding over a portion of the map to your next destination in the distance is addictive. The narrative is a good one its not anything you haven't heard or seen before, but the emotional beats all hit their mark and don't feel forced, I found myself very concerned for my pet eagles well being. I highly recommend this title to anyone who enjoys open world games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always down for a good puzzle game. The Pathless gave me exactly that: bite-sized, well contained puzzles built around an extremely simple tool set. It's a great experience traversing the land and crack the ancient locks with my birdie. And about traversal, the game features a unique parkour system. Figuring out an optimal path and executing it out smoothly gave me so much joy and excitement every time I wander away from one puzzle to another.Some complaints and spoilers:Overall though, I think the game achieved what they want with the stunning visual effects and flawless use of music/sound. It's the best looking and sounding game I've played in quite a while. The Pathless look and sound like what one can possibly expect a visualized mythology story can be - at least for now since Giant Squid is surely working on their next project.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and generally fast paced with puzzles dispersed throughout, my main frustration was with how doing bonus objectives was pointless due to you losing all those points any time you get caught during the stealth bits (which is usually). Still, one hell of a dramatic ending worth putting up with a minor gripe or two.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. There are long sections where you must solve puzzle after puzzle in order to collect items in order to get to the boss of each section (there are four area bosses and one final boss). I thought the high puzzle to combat ratio would get old, but the puzzles are intuitive enough to keep things moving and traversal is so much fun that it breaks up any monotony. I think that the length of the game is perfect. I think it could get too repetitive if it were much longer. The environment and art style is beautiful and the story is simple but good. The boss fights are fun and visually impressive. I picked this up on sale for $20 and I think it was worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Movement is extremely fun in this game and rewards precise timing and positioning. I never felt that it was a chore to get from point A to point B. Your strikes in the boss battles feel like they have so much power behind them with the great sound and visual effects which makes it really satisfying to pull off and left me looking forward to the next one. At the same time the bosses don't feel weak and the "storms" that happen that lead up to the fights make the enemies feel like an ever-present threat.My only gripe is that I wish the "storms" had different mechanics for each zone instead of always being a game of red light green light. And I wish there was a way to replay the boss battles without restarting the story.Oh, you can also pet the eagle which obviously puts this game at a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is an absolutely stunning game. The world is beautifully decorated and presented to you as soon as you start the game. The art style is unique, and although it took me a while to get used to the art style and the game’s mechanics, I had a blast. The game is filled with unique puzzles that get gradually difficult as you discover new areas. Each puzzle uses environmental cues to help you understand what you’re supposed to do, and even though many puzzles use the same type of environmental cues throughout the game, each puzzle has its own unique layout and solution. Giant Squid did a great job of making a game that was alluring, beautiful, and engaging. I love how there’s no overview map so you have to learn the map, which is half of the fun. I also very much enjoyed petting the eagle any chance I got. 10/10, very good game. I got the platinum trophy in about 13 hours, but that’s not enough for me, and I’ll definitely be doing another playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Bass-Man recommended, 8/10This game is a mixed bag for me, but it definitely has its benefits. I'll start on a high point.1 - Visuals. The game looks gorgeous and balances art and world extremely well.2 - Sound. The music is amazing (Austin Wintory pulled out all the stops for this game as well as a great main motif), and the sound design feel warm and comforting in a way I can't quite describe. It's more akin to the warm sounds of Ori versus the cold harshness of something like GOW4. 3 - Gameplay. Outside of the bosses (which I'll get to), the gameplay is for the most part fleshed out. The arrow-talisman mechanic feel like it should grow old quickly, but it remains fun and engaging for the whole story. And I will defend the eagle friend (her name is Zenith and I will give no other).Now, for the cringe.1 - Story. I normally love story and lore in games but The Pathless just doesn't need it, and when it does have it, it is not the story we need fleshed out. SPOILERS AHEAD: The motif of 'there is no one path to truth' just doesn't work in a game like this. We don't have characters to reflect the themes, we don't have any reason to say the philosophy is supported other than 'good character good' and 'bad character bad'. This game either needed more or less, not some odd in between. They did get Troy Baker tho, so I can't fault that.2 - Bosses, Obvious Spoilers Incoming. They feel very same-y, and are often annoyingly designed. I don't mean visually, all of them rock, but the actual bosses seem very clunky at times. The book ends of the main bosses (Kumo and Cernos) are fun and engaging for what they're worth, but the middle two suffer in terms of being interesting. I think a more proactive shooting mechanic would make the bosses more challenging and engaging rather than 'move, wait, repeat'. And the last boss follows in the BOTW tradition of having an awesome finale first phase and then just bombing hard.Overall, it has its own fair share of problems like any game, but the design, sound, and gameplay is engaging and fun enough to have my support.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly thrilling game,  is a boss rush with collect-a-thon elements that on paper sounds a lot worse than it is. It’s a bit difficult to describe what makes it good though the individual pieces are evident. Visually it boasts an attractive world with suitable vistas and varied designs. To start, things may seem pretty enough on their face but the game does leave you with a sense of, “That’s it?” from the opening scene. The controls are initially clunky, the objectives a bit unclear, and the gameplay loop nonobvious. Thankfully this feeling doesn’t stick around.What  does remarkably well is tying its various pieces into fantastic setpieces that are a pure joy to run through. The game is a puzzler at its core, and it has a variety of the typical environment manipulation type, but the real fun comes from the puzzle of navigating the world. This is a game where you run, but your running is slow and cumbersome. To speed it up, you need to gain speed by attacking floating talismans with your bow. This requires both good decision making in terms of which to shoot as well as good timing, as if you hit the talisman with the proper charge on your bow you gain a massive burst in speed. If you’re good, you can quickly parkour through the environment, navigating over hazards and structures with a great deal of grace.My description fails to do it justice. There’s something about the sound design and visuals that makes hitting these talismans incredible fun, and frankly epic when doing so during the boss chases. You feel fast, you feel powerful, and you feel skilled. It’s oddly cinematic despite starting off so poorly.Besides the gameplay loop, the character designs and background lore are enticing enough.  takes place in a broken land and while not incredibly creative, it’s story is serviceable and provides enough carrot to see it through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game. I like the traversal and exploration, it's fun just to move around the world. The lack of combat is certainly a choice, you have tension only by being chased around by the big baddie of each region, then you have the boss fight which you really can't lose. It's more of a relaxing game.I'd say it's worth the experience, there is a bit of a predictable story, but I like how it was told. I'd love a sequel!

_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the best art direction I've seen for any game in quite a while. This is easily the prettiest game that I have played so far in 2022. It's got a simple story to follow but the whole package everything comes in feels exuberant but at the same time, relaxed and meditative at times. I'm not usually one to like puzzles but they were simple enough to solve that they didn't make me feel like I got really stuck at any point, further adding to it being a relaxing game for me to play. It felt so incredibly nice to play a game where I felt like I could explore wherever I wanted and be rewarded with that exploration. The game never told me where to go yet it gave me an entire open world to explore, and I can't really ask much more from an open-world game like this. I love how all the different plateaus in the game have their own unique look and feel to them, you get to see a wide pallet of design and it's marvelous to experience. There's not much I can say about this game that I didn't enjoy. Even though the music didn't stand out to me a lot, it still was a nice compliment to everything that was going on. The music never felt out of place, I just wish there were a couple tracks or parts in the music that got stuck in my head. I will admit, the loop of lighting the 3 towers and then fighting the boss did start to feel a little stale after the 2nd one, but I'm okay with that considering even doing that loop still felt pretty relaxing with me getting to explore more new places. I appreciate that the game was short enough for me to really dive into while also not feeling like it dragged on for too long. While this didn't quite evoke the same emotions in me that Journey did a decade ago, there were a handful of heartwarming moments that made me smile uncontrollably (and yes, tear up a little too).For as simple and beautiful and short as a game this is, I'm glad I played it. It's one of those games that feels like you can heal from playing it. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: PROSIt's not AAA game but super polished for what it is.The controls and gameplay are really flowy and tight and make moving and shooting arrows around the world's natural environments feel really fun.The environments are really engaging and are sort of characters in and of themselves, which is good considering there aren't many characters.It's a joy to play through and stops before overstaying it's welcome.CONSThe game is pretty short The story is mostly alluded to but not fleshed out so it's hard to feel a stronger connection to the world.The (enjoyable) game loop doesn't really change from start to finish besides the awesome new biomes.The price point I feel like it should be 25 or 30 USD for what it is, so wait for a sale and then go soar! _childDocuments_.review: A stylish and fun game focused on exploration and movement. You are an archer, yes, but aiming is automatic.The open world is split into four sections, which keeps it from feeling overwhelming. Traversing the world is a joy from the beginning, and never gets old. Some of the puzzles were a bit tedious, but solving them is always satisfying. The story is bare-bones, but what is there is well done.My only complaint is that there wasn't much development of your abilities, so in the end there wasn't much of a feeling of mastery. This is exacerbated by the difficulty. I have no patience for games that constantly kill you, but you can't even die in the Pathless - making mistakes is too inconsequential.Overall though I really recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: after playing this game on my iPhone from Apple Arcade, I had a really positive experience. I was excited to play this once I heard that it out was out on Steam, where I could achieve greater graphics, framerate, and steam achievements.The Pathless is a beautifully crafted adventure-exploration game set on a mystical island that houses the gods and their respective tribes of this world. The story is that someone named "The Godslayer" had cursed and taken each god as a slave to become powerful. In the game you venture the four plateaus to purify and challenge the cursed gods. The game has a system of progression where you, the Huntress, get more powerful with each plateau cleared. The pacing in this game is AWESOME. The game focuses heavily on movement mechanics, where you shoot these talismans floating across the land that give you a boost of speed and also refill your "sprint" bar. You can chain shot these talismans while holding sprint to race across the fields and mountains of the game, and its a really thrilling experience. You can use your eagle pal to get up to higher spaces and see the world from above. I've never seen a game with such entertaining movement mechanics as this. Granted, if you are ever in a spot lacking on talismans, you will find yourself walking very slowly until you can finally shoot at one of them. That is the only qualm I have, but overall it is a fantastic system.While exploring and advancing in these plateaus, you must avoid these large red smoke bubbles that are actually the cursed gods trying to corner and find you during your progress of the game. This keeps the player engaged and also has restricted me from accessing a few places, which comes to be very entertaining and flexible. However, it seems that the times that the cloud actually "chases" you is completely random and can be frustrating. Regardless, it is a very cool system to play around with.The boss fights are what I have the heaviest opinion about. At certain stages of the fights the camera will lock onto a forced perspective, whether it be at a weak point of the boss or on a projectile coming your way that the boss sends towards you.  While the forced perspective does go hand in hand with the fast paced, swerving action on screen, it is not the most friendly system to work with.  However, overall, I have found the boss fights to be incredibly unique and fun to play.My last point is to cover the difficulty of the game, or lack thereof. This game has a lot of content and places to explore, which balances well with the ease of advancing through the story. There are no deaths, simply the loss of your points (which allow you to have more "flaps" with your eagle pal). The boss fights proceed through your chance of going through unscathed, where getting hit out of the arena simply resets your progress on beating the boss down. It's a really smooth system that doesn't make you rage quit or frustrated for having to restart each time some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ move lands on your head. So while this game may not be very difficult to understand and get the hang of, the absolute marathon that is traversing each plateau makes up for it. The Huntress' legs must be absolutely JACKED.probably my favorite game, 10/10 lol
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a good game - if you know what you want from it, namely a game that has similar vibes as Abzu and Journey. Like those games, it's better at achieving a certain mood and tone than at being a varied game, and after Journey both Abzu and The Pathless have felt too close to that game without quite reaching its heights. Having said that, there aren't that many games around that feel like this - so again, if you loved Journey and Abzu, do check this one out. If those games didn't do anything for you or if you've never heard of them, chances are that The Pathless won't be a new favourite.All of this sounds pretty negative probably, but The Pathless is done with care and love and artistry. For me, it felt too much like diminishing returns, but if you want a second or third album by this band whose first album you loved, and you're okay with getting something that's 70% or 80% as good, do go for this. You might actually enjoy it better than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless was one of those strange games that manages to make the simple act of movement fun, and yet it doesn't quite stick the landing the whole way through. Particularly in the ending, there are moments that are just tedious which are clearly meant to be epic or awe-inspiring. Getting caught by the corrupted gods is boring, not frightening or exciting. The bosses themselves are little more than glorified quicktime events, despite their impressive visuals. And, even though this is putting me firmly in the contrarian camp: I'm glad you *can* pet the bird, but *having* to pet the bird is not fun.But, I'd recommend it overall. It has this wonderful sense of exploration that is hard to find, and the movement is amazing. The visuals are stunning, and the puzzles, while simple, are fun. It's not a masterpiece, but it's certainly worth the time put in!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely an amazing game in art direction, music, performance, boss fights and overall atmosphere. Where the game falls short for me was the repetition of the actual gameplay loop. Go there, glide here, do a basic puzzle, go to the next one, all of the game. Coming from the same people that made ABZU and Journey, I kinda hoped for a more relaxing experience, but "The Pathless" still manages to deliver breathtaking moments even though playing the game started to feel like a chore after the first area. Some people will like the gameplay loop more than I did, but I'm still going for a positive review because this game has so much to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a beautiful game with a unique twist on the open world exploration genre.Everywhere in the world are strewn about talismans you may shoot with your bow, which will give you a short burst of speed and charge up your stamina bar, which in turn you can use to sprint.This makes traversing the world quick and engaging.For another layer on that system, there's also 2 options you have when shooting talismans - either you fully draw back your bow, for a guaranteed hit or you try to charge it up to exactly half before shooting.This lets you hit talismans even quicker, for quicker traversal in turn, but requires very precice timing, because otherwise your arrow will miss it's mark.For me personally though, the timing this required was a little too tight to reliably pull off, so towards the end of the game i usually opted to simply go for the guaranteed hits.On top of that you get the help of your trusted eagle, which let's you glide around and gain vertical mobility.Together, this makes traversing the huge areas fun and keeps you engaged.The gameloop mainly consists of having to solve puzzles that are strewn about each of the 5 planes to gain enough seals to cleanse three towers in each area.That will let you challenge the local boss, upon who's defeat you may ascend to the next plane or stay and keep solving the remaining puzzles if you so wish.Most of the puzzles are rather simple, with a few more elaborate ones here and there.I mostly focused on only getting enough puzzles solved to move on personally, because i didn't find them to be fun enough to seek out afterwards.Though they still give you other rewards, like being able to fly higher for example.In general i found the game to drag on a bit, the gameplay loop becoming a little stale after a while.I'd still recommend checking this out, just for the traversal, visual presentation and the grand soundtrack though.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent visuals and music with engaging puzzles throughout. The boss fights are well-executed, with interesting mechanics. The biggest thing this game has going for it is definitely the movement. Landing shot after shot on talismans (the funny glowing squares with eyes on them) and practically (or literally sometimes) flying across the landscape. The world itself is also teeming with secrets and most puzzles are either unique in how they are solved or are quick enough that it's not a bother to solve a few of them as you run around. The only (minor) gripe I have with this game is the stealth sections, as they don't really change much from area to area, but you only  to do them each once, unless you run into  Overall, still a great experience, with tons of exploration and challenges throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good casual exploration game. You spend most of the time cruising around a fairly large open world solving simple puzzles to acquire tokens to unlock new areas and increase the strength of your movement abilities. There is a stamina bar that is pretty restrictive, but you replenish stamina by shooting the talismans that are floating around all over the place, which also give you a minor speed boost. There is a bit of a skill shot you can pull off by firing your arrow at the correct time, which doesn't have much of a benefit other than that it reduces the time it takes to aim and also feels pretty satisfying to pull off with consecutive shots. There are a couple of boss fights that don't offer much in the way of challenge, but they tie the game together with a nice little narrative about gods and individuality and stuff. The visuals are great but the camera is a bit wonky and took a while to get used to. I also have to criticise the "box" art, which depicts the protagonist doing a ground slide while aiming her bow towards the viewer. It's a very action-style pose that implies the game will be a combat-oriented action game, but that's not what this game is at all. There was a lot of this in the promotional material as well; lots of screenshots of the protagonist in these over-the-top action poses pointing her bow and arrow at something off-screen. I was a little annoyed about this at first because it felt misleading to me. I was expecting a different kind of game.Play The Pathless if you just want something easy to relax or get stoned with, or maybe if you just had major dental surgery. Or just for fun, its shortcomings are minor and I think it does a pretty good job of what it was trying to do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a great experience, the story is told through the environment and writings. The gameplay is crafted by carefully mixing the puzzle elements with action and platforming resulting in a unique experience. The boss fights are phenomenal and the ending is simply marvellous. Overall it is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die hard fan of BOTW I get irritated to no end when people say "it looks like botw" just because it is cell shaded with lots of bright colors. This however fits the bill very nicely while also being a hybrid of shadow of the colossus (not in the spirit of climbing on giant beasts but in the spirit of giant creatures being the main challenge for the entire game in an otherwise not dangerous world) This game is so open ended in its exploration and progression and as a person who uses maps in games way too heavily I really enjoyed the mapless interface that shows unexplored points of interest from a birds eye view insteadexcellent story and visuals with some great music on top I highly recommend to anyone looking for a botw style open world mixed with shadow of the colossus and some light puzzle solving in a game that I would say strikes the perfect balance in length. Not too short and not overstaying it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting too much when I got this game, but it exceeded quite a few of my expectations. The movement was great, as was the ability to actually bypass a boss and come back to it later, which I found quite fitting for the game. Most surprisingly to me though, was the sheer amount of meaning and gravitas this game can bring when it feels the need. So I vehemently recommend this game to anyone looking to both relax, and sometimes really engage with the world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the devs behind Abzu were working on a new game I got excited and I was no let down here. The momentum of this game is just plain fun, hitting targets with the bow to go faster and faster to explore a world that actually has quite a bit packed into it. All the little secrets kind of remind me of the Korok seed puzzles in Breath of the Wild, but in this game you can zero in on the area that they are in, meaning youre coming across them a lot more frequently. A few of the boss battles are pretty memorable and fun as well. The story is cliche but its there enough to justify the exploration. My main gripe with the game is the price, I don't know that 40 bucks worth of content is in here, but getting this game on sale is a no brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: A very aesthetically pleasing puzzle game with a classic storyline about good vs evil. The game mechanics for getting around (speed boosts from hitting targets with your bow and arrow) was a nice creative touch, but I personally found the learning curve a bit too steep. After getting the hang of it, it was fun and the mix between fast paced ground movement and slow gliding through the air created a dynamic gameplay. The puzzles gradually introduced more complex interactions while not being overly difficult. (Especially since you don't need to solve all of them to progress to the next level). The boss fights were very epic visually, but sometimes dragged on too long (quite possibly because I suck at fighting!).I liked that you could generally not screw up too bad in the game, not even in boss fights. Overall I found this to be a very enjoyable game and I would definitely recommend it! Almost everything fits together perfectly (visuals, music, gameplay).  8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Best way I can describe it is it's got a sorta BOTW aesthetic open world with Zelda style puzzles (including the korok variety) and you move super fast. It's like if Zelda, Sonic, and Legolas all somehow had a baby. Your only weapon is a bow, but you have infinite arrows and you can go nuts with it.but there are no enemies except for the bosses, of which there are only like six, but the bosses are big, flashy, complex fights, so in that way it's kinda like SOTC. The boss fights will make you feel VERY Legolas.It has a unique movement mechanic where your character runs at a slow plod by default, but there are little red eye "talismans" all over the map, and if you shoot one, it gives you a sudden burst of speed and then fills up a sprint meter that allows you to move faster as long as it lasts. If you shoot one while you are in the air, the boost will launch you further upward, sustaining your hangtime. So you get around quickly by dashing and shooting these talismans and trying to chain together these sonic-the-hedgehog sorta movement combos, only it's a much more Legolas flavor.You also have an eagle that is your constant companion. Helps you solve certain puzzles and can be used as a glider. Powering it up with collectibles can let you fly faster or flap to increase height etc.I don't know if it would be everyone's cup of tea. Some might get bored with the lack of enemies to fight, and some of the puzzle ideas do repeat with just a little variation (similar to koroks), but I just love open world "zelda-ish" games, and especially cartoony and vibrant aesthetics.I only really have two complaints with it. One is that, even if you are very skillful at avoiding the boss enemies in certain situations, the game on multiple occasions will force you into situations where you basically have to "take a hit" from the boss, presumably so that the game can "demonstrate their might" to you, but it does feel kind of annoying when it happens. The second is that there are parts where you have to kind of "stealth" to avoid the bosses, which is okay for the most part, but the bosses will vanish/teleport around while you are trying to avoid their gaze. However, this means that no matter how well you stealth, the boss can randomly teleport directly on top of you and cause you to fail, which exacts a sort of "loss of experience" penalty upon you, which feels like some serious bullsh-t when it happens.But these are minor and rare complaints on the whole. I found the game to be much bigger and of a much higher quality than I was expecting. Full of surprises. Do recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a so-so rating, but that isn't an option. This game is like a distilled Breath of the Wild; there's an open world and you're given all the tools you need for puzzles right off the bat. The puzzles are pretty straight-forwards and never require additional upgrades or items, just clever thinking and spatial awareness. Core movement is handled really well, and you can chain together 'dashes' by hitting talismans floating around the world. Animations are super detailed, especially when you can pet the eagle. Character designs are pretty good; the main character is almost always easily visible, enemies have inventive designs, and the main villain is easily identifiable. That's about it, though. There's some really interesting ideas with the boss battles, but the game really shows its flaws there too. This isn't a game with a combat system. Battling monsters doesn't really work because they attack pretty quickly, and you don't have a dodge button. You can't really run to avoid attacks because your Stamina regenerates at a laughable pace - but only if you find an OPTIONAL upgrade. Also strange are segments during boss battles where you need to sneak around the enemy (it only happens twice), since it isn't difficult and completely halts the pacing. Stealth segments sprinkled in the overworld via storms is pretty cool, but also frustrating when the only penalty for getting caught is PERMANENTLY LOSING UPGRADES. This, combined with the scarcity of upgrades, makes the game frustrating. You can also just hard save and load if you lose upgrade points, which undermines that whole penalty mechanic. There's really obscure collectibles that do nothing, and the core upgrades don't really do anything after the stamina regen other than 'go faster when doing X'. The developers have previously made artsy games, and it shows - ABZU's aesthetic bleeds into this game, as does Journey. However, this game can't seem to decide if it wants to be a soothing aesthetic quest, or a more fast-paced game at times. While the puzzles are good and reflect the game's bow mechanics well, as does traversing large flat spaces, the boss battles are designed for a character with greater mobility than the one we're given. Giving bosses a health bar or visual cue you're making progress would bring this game up a notch - which I know Giant Squid is capable of doing, because the final boss displays physical damage as you win the fight. The lack of a player health bar also makes these battles weird, since the stakes are never the threat of dying, but watching your character get tossed around like a rag doll and potentially losing upgrade points. The narrative also weighs this game down a LOT. While cutscenes are animated wonderfully, the story is basically about an evil guy who shows up and wants to destroy the world, and you show up to stop him. Obligatory lore across the world establishes the villain as single-minded and that he's powerful, but that's about it. There's a handful of interesting logs near the end where his followers doubt their mission, but you only get a handful of these - most other logs are either "Oh no we're being murdered by the bad guy/bad guy's minions" or "Haha I follow bad guy he is so cool I die for him now". While there's some logs giving insight into the bosses and their role in nature, there isn't any mythos or context really given to them. They exist almost solely to give the player boss battles. If anything, I'd call the story 'safe' in terms of avoiding going anywhere that might make people uncomfortable. Kids might be okay with this game if they can tolerate the scariness of the monsters. I really like certain aspects of this game, but it also shows that despite having extremely talented artists behind it, including Austin Wintory once again saving the day with an outstanting soundtrack that gives the world a sense of majesty and foreboding. A lot of good sound design exists here, especially when the player is using their mask (definitely not detective vision). It compliments the visuals really nicely, and is almost always going in step with giving the player perfect feedback to their actions.So we've got really good visuals, animation, and sound, gameplay that works really well most of the time but falls short at key moments, and a narrative that feels almost obnoxiously simple and doesn't feature any depth or growth for anyone involved (unless you count 'get stronger to defeat bad guy' growth, which isn't reflected in the narrative, and in gameplay you mostly just get faster). It's worth picking up on sale or trying out; after the first few cutscenes you've pretty much experienced the entire game, and can decide at that point if the rest of the experience is worth your time. TL;DR:G O T T A   G O   F A S T

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous game with a pretty enjoyable gameplay loop of exploration, puzzles, and light platforming, with really fluid ground and air movement, an easy-to-use but satisfying bow-and-arrow mechanic, and some really fun and intense boss segments. It's not too hard and maybe a bit more variety in the puzzles could've helped, and there's these forced stealth sections that are a bit wonky, but the vast majority of the experience is really enjoyable and chill.None of that matters though because you can both pet -and- hug a bird in this game. So it's functionally perfect.

_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: It's like they realised they made their game world bigger than was enjoyable, and so utterly littered it with things to help you move through the empty majority of it faster.Each puzzle you find is devoid of challenge, and there's only about 4 different puzzles, just slightly rearranged each time.The "boss" battles are a bit more interesting, but still underwhelming.And, having just done 3 of the areas, thinking I was nearing the end of the game, it reveals a 4th area, and i can barely muster the effort to bother...Judging by the global achievement stats, few others bothered to even finish the 1st area.Getting caught up in a "hide and seek" with the boss can result in permanently losing some yellow crystals that build up to the only worthwhile "upgrade" in the game, more flaps from the bird to get higher.edit: persisted to the end. final boss was visually immense, but also devoid of challenge, and the ending was completely lacking in payoff.LOL the end credits negates the ending, wtf.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a very polished and well-executed game. This is a short semi-open world adventure with fun and engaging movement mechanics. In line with the philosophy of Giant Squid's previous game Abzu, The Pathless takes a minimalist approach to design that pares the game back to its essentials. Due to this approach, the developers are able to polish each gameplay system to a mirror shine.In the Pathless, you move through large open spaces solving bow and switch puzzles. Solve enough of these puzzles and you fight a boss (the boss fights are multi-phase and of a very high quality). Moving through the world is unconventional (shooting strange floating targets to gain speed), but it's so polished that it feel like second nature. There is no mini-map to speak of, nor any unnecessary UI clutter, allowing the player to remain present within the compelling world Giant Squid have conjured up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: There is something to say about simplicity. Purity of form and function. This game does not ask too much of the player, but if they are curious they will be awash in wind-whistling speed, immaculate scenery, and a deep mysticism that makes my inner worldbuilder replete. Visually - the color scheme may be simple, but that does little to diminish the beauty of this game.  The Unreal Engine really puts in work to make this a fluid masterpiece of a time if you're flying, running at lightning speeds, or just staring at the scenery from a great vantage. Have I mentioned it's stunning? Because it is.Gameplay - Although it is quite simple, it doesn't require much time to understand what the game asks of you, and generally you are able to go through it with very few hiccups. There are only one or two gripes I have with the game, and they are both related to the "big clouds" you'll notice at certain points.1. Occasionally, the creatures in those clouds just spawn or path poorly and you can be instantly caught while being a deer in the headlights. You'll understand.2. Though the clouds themselves move, sometimes it's not immediately apparent what their tells are.The bulk of the game is focused on puzzles though and I'm glad to say I didn't really encounter any that stumped me for long, though quite a few are tricky! But many are extremely satisfying to solve and the musical/visual cues just add to that sense of accomplishment.Also, you can pet your eagle. That's just great!Narrative - No spoilers, I promise. If you like to put together the story, the core narrative can do that just fine by itself. However, I do extremely recommend seeking out any tablets or memories as much as you can. They are the details that give this picture the accents to show you how deep the struggle is. And some of the lessons are quite poignant.Music and Sound. Anything by Austin Wintory is worth a listen. You will be transported to this magical place by the power of orchestration, throat-singing, and traditional instrumentation. It's a masterpiece. The creature and ambient sounds are quite memorable too, and when everything comes together it's a very cinematic work and frankly, I should play it again someday just to relive the big beats.Anyone who enjoys exploration, narrative, eastern mysticism,the power of flight, and some unexpected guidance in life will probably enjoy this game to pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If you've loved Abzû, you will love the Pathless. The pathless continues to be a representation of Giant Squid's vision, on what makes a good game. The Pathless is a continuation. It actually broadens and at the same time specifies what Giant Squid is about. And I'm all for it.Just like Abzû, The Pathless presents you with gameplay centered around exploration and fluid movement, added with a great atmosphere. Now, the atmosphere in The Pathless is not always as calming as in Abzû. It's because The Pathless actually becomes more action-centered, but it retains its simplicity. Which is good, because that's what made their games so charming and calming to play. It's just fun, and you don't need to think to much about it. There are some boss battles, but they are fun rather than hard. The story is interesting as well. But the best part is after you have cleared an area of the boss: you run and glide around, gather collectibles, enjoy the amazing view. If you liked Abzû because you were swimming among the fishes, you might enjoy The Pathless because you will be running among the forest animals. The game is lovely.Oh and the soundtrack? Damn, Austin Wintory did it AGAIN. Abzû had an amazing OST, that I often listen to outside of the game. And with The Pathless, he hid it out of the park again. It fits well but also adds a lot to the game. Great work.I spent quite a lot of time playing this game, 'cause I was interested in getting all the lanterns in every area. If you want to get the most out of this game, it is recommended to check every green lit area for a lantern icon on top of it. If the lantern icon can not be found, or the area is red, it means that there is more to explore/more collectibles to find. But if you skip all of that, the game can be finished quite quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: this is like Breath of the Wild - LITE. Lots of mini puzzles. LOTS. And epic boss fights that happen in 4-stages each, VERY similar to Shadow of the Colossus. The game is simple. no map. no items. the same bow and arrow the entire game. you do get some mini-buffs if you find all Animal Medallions, but other than that, its just a fun, beautiful, fast, entertaining game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I may have completed this game around 10-13 hours, however the time I spent on it was magical. The way the music changes with each situation, i.e: Hitting different targets which evokes different sounds/music, varying as you continue stacking up the hits. It complements the landscape which is beautiful and crammed full of secrets and objectives that requires a keen eye and usage of an inner sense of sorts.     Each different locations is distinct with the weather and colour palette varying, making it unique. The boss fights are very entertaining and mildly annoying at times, but they are very different in that it infuses the mechanics from the puzzles found in the open world with dealing with the bosses themselves.     Which leads to the story, in my opinion is paced well and ties each area together to create a cohesive conclusion that hits the sweet spot of vanquishing the enemy/saving the world archetype.    Overall, its a great game that is beautiful story/music wise. A masterpieces no doubt.    10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game! This is "open" world done right. Tight mechanics, smooth controls, good pace, good rewards for going beyond the minimum required to make progress. And of course, the incredible graphic aesthetic and soundtrack you would expect from these developers. Some might say this game is lacking in variety, but the way I see it, it respects my time by not meandering pointlessly or cramming unnecessary mechanics down my throat. I appreciated the visual storytelling in all of the many ruined buildings you can find and visit, each of them unique. The fights against the various corrupted gods felt epic and satisfying. Note: This is not an incredibly challenging game. The puzzles range from obvious to medium-easy, and the punishments for failure are always mild. If you're looking for a test of skill, this might not be the game for you. But if you want an experience that is both enjoyable and largely devoid of frustration, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If you love games like Journey, Abzu, Inner Space, and Lost Ember, you will love this game.Beautifully crafted, wonderful lore and story, and fun game mechanics.For some people the puzzles may feel too easy, any many of them did feel a little easy, but I feel it suited the relatively relaxed game play. If they had been more difficult and what they are, I think it would have been a point of frustration for many players.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is more about asthetics than challenge. Most of the puzzles and races are fairly easy (but I did't mind). The game loop is roughly this: collect lightstones > unlock towers > hunt/fight boss > get reward > find all lighstones > get extra reward > repeat in next area.This can get a little monotonous, but the boss fights are quite fun - not too difficult but always different.You can save anytime. So in the end, I recommend this for casual players.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful through and through with a great emotional ending. If anyone likes Abzu, Journey, Gris, or Ori then I'd easily recommend this one. Played smoothly, sounds great, lots to explore, and even a completion playthrough would easily be under 20ish hours with a casual run being like 8 or so that should leave you plenty satisfied whether you decide to 100% it or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: I really didn't know what to expect from this game but saw a positive review, noticed it was in a Steam sale and decided to give it a go.The game is broken into several large areas all of which are non-linear and essential open world. You can travel between these areas whenever you want although I chose to more or less complete each area one at a time. Without spoiling it game play involves some character/ability progression combined with well done but mainly easy puzzle solving, exploration and boss combat. Outside of combat your bow is used to get around using those floating markers you can see in screenshots.Really enjoyed the game. Solid story line which you can ignore if you want. Strongly recommended especially at the lower price.It took me 12 hours to complete including finding most, but not all, of the "artifacts"
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, minimalistic game, graphics don't really matter, gameplay is non-linear, relaxing, and most of the time calm (with the exception of the 'storm' scenes), because it is impossible to die, or lose 'lives'. Aiming is automatic, you don't have to be an aim genius with a perfect score on Aim Lab. There is no fast travel mechanic, nor is there any sense of direction, except for the spirit mask guiding you to the "corrupted" places to purify them. While I do think it has taken some inspiration from Breath of the Wild, It is not a blatant copy of it, even though many people think differently. Truly an 'open-world' game. 10/10. Edit: (P.S. You can pet the eagle)

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful exploration game. The world is large and beautiful, the movement is fun,and there's a lot to discover - lore, interesting locations and gameplay benefits.The boss fights can be a little fiddly, but that's about everything negative there is to say about the game.Overall, the best game I've played in 2021 (and 2022, so far).
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely is for you if you like open world games, but it also does something what other open worlds don't do. It makes travelling and running around fun and satisfying. It keeps you engaged while moving by having to shoot your arrows at the runes to keep your momentum. Along with a great soundtrack that fits the overall vibe and beautiful visuals the game is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a short but sweet adventure game. The main focuses of the game, exploration and movement, are done very well. I never felt lost or unsure of where to go, even without using the "eye" ability that allows you to see points of interest. There is all kinds of lore and small secrets to uncover around the map. Moving around uses a quite novel system of shooting objects with your bow and arrow in order to move at a faster pace, as well as gliding using your eagle. It never got boring and always felt satisfying to do well, especially with the upgrades you receive after defeating the bosses. The game also looks great, and has a wonderful atmosphere in its nature-reclaimed landscapes full of ancient ruins and long-dead citizens. The story, while not groundbreaking, certainly isn't bad and the music is phenomenal.That is not to say the game is perfect. The main complaint I had was the lack of variety in environments. The first three areas are all essentially the same biome of mixed forest and open plains. That is not to say they can't be told apart, but I do wish they were more distinctive, especially when compared to Giant Squid's previous game ABZU, and even their spiritual predecessor Journey. The game is also quite short and is not especially challenging. The latter I would consider a boon as an overly difficult section would upset the game's pacing in my opinion, but I understand that some desire more of a challenge. Overall, this is a good game, though I would not consider it a great one, and I don't think I would recommend it over titles like Shadow of the Colossus, the previously mentioned ABZU and Journey, or maybe even Breath of the Wild if you are interested in this sort of aesthetic (though I am personally not a huge fan of BoTW). But, if you have already played those or they do not interest you, I would give this game a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stunning game. It has a large open world with many hidden puzzled all around to discover, amazing movement controls to start that only get better the more you play, stunning visuals and sound design, and a simple, but lovely story that gets expanded on the more you seek out the lore of the land.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: The Pathless is a genuine breath of fresh air in the collectathon genre.Pros:The music is smooth.Low entry, high ceiling.Amazing companion mechanic that forces you to care for your companion animal.Controls super simple to the point you could technically play with with just your mouse.Puzzles are super solid.Cons:For how good the music is, it gets rather boring when trying to fully complete the game.The camera on some bosses are really bad and stand in the way of execution.Totally a game worth getting if collecting items, puzzles and simplicity is your vibe!
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: Personally really loved the game. The game is very good at using its limited amount of controls very effectively. I got a lot more out of this game than I expected going in. The boss fights feel very good, though the chase sequences take some time to get into the groove of. The exploration is great! They give you a tool to help you find the secrets, instead of it just being a never-ending game of running into walls hoping you find something. There is so much to find in this game, from lore to mini-games. The achievements are very attainable, and you can get most of them without ever looking at the list. I personally liked the story a lot, and got very emotionally attached to the eagle.If you are someone who loved Journey, and are looking to find a game that will scratch that kind of artistic, story driven, exploration game well this is it. The only draw back I had was the second to last area crashed repeatedly for a couple of days. After that though the game ran smoothly, and I'd say was worth persisting through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a puzzle platformer with a fantastic movement system, stunning visuals, fun-but-not-too-complicated puzzles and interesting boss fights, look no further, for you have just found it.The Pathless is all of the above, and more. It is not endlessly long, but feels like it is juuuust the right length, especially if you're not intending on 100%-ing it. However, if you DO intend on 100%-ing it, it does outstay its welcome by and hour or two. If you can live with that, it is well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I am speechless, that's why I am writing a review :-PI finished the game a few minutes ago.What are the keywords coming to my mind thinking about this game.- Great villan. His design, his voice and the end fight are amazing.- Beautiful art direction and graphics- Smooth framerate (UE4) are in my opinion often bad optimized. Offering good graphics quality for okay framerate and having often reloading stutters. Nothing here, this is a perfectly smooth experience for me.- Amazing music- Deep lore- Movement that feels increadibly smooth once you get into it.I especially want to highlight the cutscenes. The duo, the huntress and the eagle are so cute together. They really touched me emotionally. For me it's a masterpiece.But, if you only search for action non stop. It could be a troublesome game for you. Between each boss fight, every single one of the is amazing, there are repeating enviromental puzzles and jump'n run challenges. _childDocuments_.review: The pathless is a pretty cool game. It's beautiful with phenomenal music, the game world is fun to move around especially as you unlock more mobility options. The game is fairly engaging even though it's super easy and there is not a fail state. There are a lot of extremely basic puzzles you do to progress, they will never stop you for more than a couple minutes at most, and the boss design is engaging and fun. The bosses are also the only combat encounters in the game. The stealth/storm mechanic however got old after the first time and is a slog every time you get caught in one after that. I found the world to be too large for such a focused linear game is, and the only way to interact with the world besides moving through it is too solve puzzles and find secrets. I think the areas could have used a bit more visual variety as well, since three out of four of the major areas are variations on forests with minor differences. There is an alternate ending after the credits if you collect all the extra keys and secrets if you enjoy that kind of thing. These gripes aside I can easily recommend The Pathless if you are looking for a relaxing "journey" through a desolate world with kino presentation and simple but mostly entertaining gameplay. I think the game should have been 25 dollars instead of 40 but that's just my opinion, you may want to get it on sale if the asking price seems a little steep for whats on offer, but thats up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Pathless

_childDocuments_.review: While I personally preferred the linearity and lack of puzzles in Giant Squid's previous title , and its "spiritual predecessor" ,  still delivers a unique and impactful experience. Retaining their outstanding visual style and presentation,  is truly a sight to behold. Minimal UI puts the focus on the breathtaking environments and highlights character movement and speed. Even on keyboard and mouse, controls are smooth and satisfying, though they may take you a minute to get used to. Certainly recommend this one!

_childDocuments_.review: A very gorgeous game with lots of zen like exploration and some light combat.  Its chasing those Shadow of the Colossus vibes but with fun and fast motion and controls. _childDocuments_.review: Obligatory: You can pet the birb, 10/10!For real though, above all else, this game FELT good. I just finished the ending and it was a wonderful experience through and through. Audio is ambient, beautiful, heart wrenching, and stirring when it needs to be, the final sequences has me amped up! The graphics are simple, clean and beautiful, exploring the world was enjoyable. The gameplay mechanics are simple and intuitive to the point where when I entered the final challenges of the game I knew exactly what to do but still had a blast doing it! Remember how you felt at the end of SotC? Like you personally underwent every trial and tribulation yourself and came out at the end for better or worse? This made me feel like that again. Plus, I was as attached to my eagle as I was to Agro. <3Amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, charming, cute little game.Not terribly long, I beat it in just under 7 hours leisurely going through the game just trying to progress consistently but occasionally detouring for things that peaked my interest.It's not revolutionary, but it's self-contained and well designed.The game is not difficult, however that's not a bad thing, as the game's spectacle is greatly entertaining. Don't expect to be challenged, as this game is more of an interactive experience than anything else.If you're weird like me and enjoy skill-based optional mechanics that speed up gameplay efficiency, this game has one that is perfect for you, and I seriously enjoyed trying to get those perfectly consistent half-draws.The only things I dislike are the very incremental and barebones settings, and one particular area on the multi-headed boss By the way, you can hold jump to jump a little higher than usual.Overall, 9/10. Fantastic for what it is. Also you can pet the bird.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game is well done. Reviewers talk a lot about the movement mechanics, but there is so much more to love about this game: the storytelling, the soundtrack, the characters, I mean they nailed everything. Even on a anim tech/prog level, it's fabulous. I love petting the eagle, the hand glides flawlessly through the feathers and the hand never jitters, the blending between the poses are perfect, and trust me, it takes a lot of work to do a thing like that so well. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing game for those who are a fan of BOTW-likes. May not have the visual style of something like Sable, but the puzzle and movement mechanics are polished. _childDocuments_.review: The pathless is a short 3D puzzle-platformer (yes I know its listed as actiion adventure but let's be real).It's main tool is a story that is neither layered nor complicated, but rather a simple beauty. The game plays fluid and never puts you under stressful pressure, tho some movements can be frustrating until you figure them out (might also just be that I'm not good at platformers).The the main selling points tho are the stunning graphics and most of all, the absolutely incredible soundtrack. Even if you never pick up this game, at least do yourself a favor and give the music a listen. If you are looking to escape for a few hours into a mystical world of forests, mountains and spirits, The Pathless could be the right choice for you.Sincerely, Chris

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked games like Journey, RiME, Abzu or Flower you should feel right at home. Over my 13 hours playthrough where I got every single achievement there wasn't a single time where I would be bored or exhausted. Game length feels on point - not too long to get burned out and just enough to still want a little bit more.I would describe this game as a next step in evolution of formula presented by games I listed above. You get big open map, divined in regions that you "cleanse" one by one. There are plenty locations to explore and uncover more information about the world with different, rather easy puzzles or challenges. Both gameplay and story are simple but really enjoyable and satisfying. I had fun running and flying through the areas, trying to maintain my speed by shooting arrows around or just slowly taking it all in, appreciating everything around me. Pathless artstyle looks gorgeous and minimalistic hud cooperates with it well. Each area looked different and there was always something that would make me stop and admire the view. Final act of the game deserves a special mention - it looked absolutely stunning.Last but not least - soundtrack. Throughout the years I discovered more and more of a fantastic works made by Austin Wintory - Journey, Banner Saga, Assassin's Creed Syndicate, Abzu and now Pathless. Once again he creates something unique and memorable, music that will elevate your experience by a wide margin. This man and people he works with are truly genius.Just pet the bird.

_childDocuments_.review: The pathless is a great game akin to Journey or its sister game ABZU. The game doesn't have any fail states, so its not going to be testing your skills, but its not meant to. Even so some of the boss fights can feel exciting just from the spectacle of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of ABZÛ, The Pathless is a mythic adventure game about an archer and an eagle in a vast forest. Become the Hunter, a master of archery who travels to a mystical island to dispel a curse of darkness that grips the world. Forge a connection with your eagle companion as you hunt corrupted spirits, but be careful not to become the hunted yourself. Explore misty forests full of secrets, solve puzzles in ancient ruins, and test your skill in epic battles. The bond with your eagle and the fate of the world hang in the balance. [Giant Squid]

name: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden
detailed_description: SCORES Join our Discord About the Game In New Eden, 1695, communities of settlers are plagued by a dreadful curse. As Banishers, step into their lives, investigate the source of evil, unravel chilling mysteries, explore diverse landscapes, and interact with unforgettable characters whose fate lies in your hands. Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is an all-new title crafted by renowned studio DON'T NOD, known for their acclaimed titles such as Life is Strange and Vampyr. Immerse yourself in an intimate narrative Action-RPG, taking you on an exhilarating journey between life, death, love and sacrifices. Play as a couple of Banishers, Red and Antea, experienced spirit hunters entrusted with the daunting task of dispelling a malevolent curse through powerful rituals. Protect the living from the threat of lingering ghosts and specters, and become a beacon of hope in a world consumed by darkness. Experience a heart-wrenching love story between Antea Duarte and Red mac Raith. When Antea is killed and turned into a spirit, you find yourself facing a choice. Will you uphold your oath and ascend her soul, or will you sacrifice the living in the hope of bringing her back? Your decisions will shape the fate of New Eden’s inhabitants - may they be living or dead, and determine the end of your journey. BLAME the living and sacrifice their lives, holding them responsible for their actions BANISH souls of the departed, condemning them to eternal suffering ASCEND souls, liberating them from eternal sorrow and granting them serenity Banishers are specialized in combat against undead creatures, such as specters or ghosts. Combine Red's physical arsenal with Antea's supernatural powers in a dynamic combat system. Find your own style by mixing weapon attacks and spiritual abilities. Powerful synergies will lead you to defeat New Eden’s most dangerous enemies and bosses. Unleash the full power of the Banishers by unlocking new gear and supernatural abilities. By exploring New Eden, you will find ancient artifacts, trinkets and valuable resources to enhance your equipment in preparation of future fights. In addition to your arsenal, progress in Antea’s skill trees to upgrade her devastating spectral powers and unseal new combos. Investigate haunting cases in a mystical world full of dark secrets. Discover New Eden, a North America settlement marked by terrible stories and secrets of its tormented inhabitants. Understanding each resident’s motivations will be essential to guide your decisions throughout the game.
