_childDocuments_.review: A shining example of what a AA game should be. The story and atmosphere are great, each quest and character is unique. Which really surprised me. Every character has their own story, and some of the dramatic moments are truly heart-wrenching. Take, for example, the side quest where we have to help a soldier who accidentally shot his best friend in the heat of battle and is now consumed by guilt. Overall, it's a very mature drama that raises important and sometimes existential questions. But the game is magnificent not only in terms of its story but also as a complete work of art. The graphics and music are beyond praise. What's especially surprising is that, despite being built on Unreal Engine 5, the game not only looks fantastic but also runs flawlessly. There are absolutely no complaints about the performance. And as far as I can recall, this is the first game on this engine that runs so impeccably. Because everything else released on Unreal Engine 5 so far has performed terribly. For example, the recent "Nobody Wants to Die" doesn't even achieve 60fps at native resolution on a 4090, despite its graphics not being outstanding. Of course, if you're looking for flaws, you can find them in Banishers. The somewhat uninteresting bosses are a bit disappointing, as they act too predictably in many, though not all, cases. In addition, some story missions feel drawn out and disrupt the pacing. The rather limited bestiary is also a letdown. There are simply too few enemy types for a game of this length.Nevertheless, it's an excellent game with a mature storyline, serious themes, and dramatic choices that force you to constantly check in with your own conscience. It's a unique game about banishing not ghosts, but your own inner demons.
_childDocuments_.name: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden

_childDocuments_.review: DONT NOD better not ever make another game like this because they totally suck at it.  The setting is great, the story is great, the characters are great.  ButCombat sucks.  Not much variety.   Mostly meaningless stats making most weapon alternatives meaningless.  Little enemy variety and very little variation on enemy combat tactics.  Basic ghost attack is a...punch?   Who teh hell makes a ghost character playable and has them punching things?  So stupid.  Also, really dumb equipment buffs like : using this makes your next (insert attack type here) do extra damage.  God it's awful.  Also, lots of enemies are so damage spongy it's ridiculous.  Also, later in the game there are section that take away your ghost part in combat and a lot of combat is based around switching between the two for bonus damage or effects and that's stupid because it can take away your most effect attacks.Navigation sucks.  You can only fast travel from resting fires and they are far and few between making backtracking excessive.  Also, every path to everywhere else is a long twisting path that full of climbing up and down and shimmying along cliffs and squeezing through narrow rocks.  You'll come to a spot and be all "Hey, that what I need!" and it will be 30 feet away but on the other side of a small crevice so to get there you'll spend 20 minutes taking a scenic rout of all the features listed above with probably 6 combat encounters along the way with at least 1 or 2 of the real spongy enemy types.  Traveling around is really a pain in the butt and probably the worst part of the game.  Especially these voidwalk areas which are basically enemy filled zones with a boss battle at the end for some equipment.  They are overly long, yield rewards you're not likely to ever use, and they have a GREAT chance of dropping you out of the void far away from where you entered (once on the opposite side of the world map).   Talk about not respecting you time.The worst part about combat though is target lock.  There is not changing target lock automatically. To lock to a different target you have to unlock from your current target an dthen lock on to the new target.  This really messes up the flow of combat and really goes against how we learn from most other games with similar combat.  It basically goes completely against what we develop as an instinct.  Such a common gaming standard to be overlooked is inexcusable and if don't on purpose it's an egregious FU to players.Also, there are "nests" that you can clear out and they are the more challenging enemies you'll face in the game, but some of them are ridiculously hard.  You'll fight 3 or 4 waves of multiple enemies that you'll barely damage so each wave takes about 10 minutes to beat.  The way the enemies fight isn't new or special, they;re just damage sponges that take 10 times longer to kill that normal.   The laziest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you can have is just increasing health and not making the fights more interesting.You collect materials that are used to enact various little rituals (mostly to summon an enemy or listen  in on  a past event) or to upgrade your equipment and they seem more like an afterthought to check a gameplay feature box than be any kind of fun.  At least you can sell most of it, but all you can really buy is other materials for those mostly useless upgrades.It's a shame, this is a great ghost story game (thought the frights are few and far between, not a horror game to be sure), but combat and travel feel like a chore.  It's feels artificially extended to just add filler to how long it takes to finish and it really hurts the flow of what ever task is at hand.  Several times you expect to finish a task real quick, but the  you have to spend 30 minutes going to some spot way from where you expect just because the character you are looking for has, for some reason, gone there.And then there's the addition of the stupidest kind of achievements to ever exists.  Achievements that are tied to doing some particular feat in combat like "Defeat 3 enemies with a post parry attack in a single encounter".  What the hell for?  Who effing cares?  Why in god's name ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like this exists I don't know but developers are morons for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like it.  There are other dumb achievements too, but combat ones for a game which combat is uninteresting and pretty sucky?  *SIGH* I don't know if the great story is even strong enough for me to want to finish the game, let alone actually finish it.Please DONT NOD.  Stick to Life is Strange and the like.  You are really, REALLY bad at this kind of game.  You should have switched combat and climbing for more investigative skill and reputation systems or something.  Your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat really ruins the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with an excellent story and believable characters.PRO:- great story, plot and writing- long game, lots of content (80h one full playthrough)- excellent world/map - this game can act as a case study on how to get great value out of a world map/level design.- excellent voice acting- excellent sound effects and especially good and subtle environmental sounds- good graphics with only medium hardware requirements, very stable framerate- atmospheric music- zero bugs encounteredCON:- parrying mechanic is clunky and unrewarding and not worth the trouble- music can get a bit old - it is very atmospheric, but a bit of a tune sometimes would be appreciatedThis game delivers a LOT of value even at full priceStrongly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: perfectly optimized unreal game on day 1?!? super cool setting. amazing visuals and dialog. serviceable combat and animation. highly recommended if you are okay with a little AA jankUpdate: damn near 50 hours later. I love this game. The simple one sentence description is God of War level design and combat meets The Witcher 2 world design, mission structure, and story telling. It is a stellar story about loss and it weaves an intricate web of characters with what is essentially a collection if interconnected ghost stories where each one tells a compelling moral tale that peels away at the onion of the main story.My only criticism is that fast travel becomes damn near essential as the back half of the game trades perfectly paced exploration with map wide fetch quests that literally send you back and forth (sometimes several times over). The game is at it's best when either (a) you are questing and traversing a never before seen section of the map or (b) when you are solving ghost stories that keep you in or around one location. When it eventually veers to (c) running all over the damn map to do one small objective at a time it really hurts the otherwise perfect pacing.Small spoiler: I think the void would have been better utilized as an immersive fast travel akin to the god of war world tree instead of a gameplay experience that shoots you out at random places on the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden

_childDocuments_.review: BEST GAME EVER!!!!!Without spoiling too much, the game incorporates a mechanic that allows you to switch between the 2 main characters for 2 reasons, 1 a different perspective and secondly different abilities. It's hard to explain how brilliantly this is done without giving away a huge part of the beginning of the story.The 2 main characters have a unique relationship that complement each other well forming some light comical humour in their banter throughout this dark tale. Switching between the 2 in battle grants you with a variety of ways to fight your combatants, while the quests allow for chilled spiritual investigative work. The story, lore and world itself, left me wanting to read EVERYTHING, and I generally tend to get overwhelmed trying to read it all.

_childDocuments_.review: The game boasts amazing controller support and haptics, with a polished and optimized launch day experience, featuring zero crashes. Its price point is better than a $70 title. The combat, starting slow, becomes engaging, but encounters feel repetitive. Clue-finding lacks excitement, serving its purpose for later moral choices. Overall, a 7/10.Update: Finished the game. Combat became monotonous, prompting a difficulty reduction. The same enemy types made exploration predictable. The combat system very shines in the end but requires a lengthy buildup. 16 hours? Why? The story is mediocre, with forced woke lines and characters out of place. While the developers and studio show talent, the writing includes unnecessary propaganda. The historical accuracy and timeline alignment feel off, impacting the immersion. The game could have been more enjoyable with a faster-paced combat introduction and a more thought-out narrative. Mixed 5/10 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Another modern game ruined by modern ideology. Men bad. Men stupid. Men weak. Women good. Women smart. Women strong. It takes place in an interesting time period but the immersion is completely broken. You play as Red who is basically told what to do by Antea the whole game like he is stupid and useless without her. He barely ever disagrees with her or speaks up for himself. People also often disrespect him and talk to him like a child. It is ridiculous. Also, a lot of the hauntings which are probably the most interesting part of the game also inject the men are inferior to women mindset. Completely ruined the game for me honestly. While the performance is decent, even on lower end hardware, there is often frame drops while traversing the world. The less powerful your processor, the worse they are. I tested this game with 4 different computers ranging from old low end to newer high end and experienced this issue. It isn't bad but it definitely the game could use better optimization which unfortunately isn't something Don't Nod tends to be good about.The world is beautiful but it is like a maze. You are constantly forced to take obscure ways to get where you need to go. There is fast travel but the bonfires are so far apart that you often just have to spend a lot of time just running where you need to go. Plus if you get caught in a fight, the game will prevent you from running past it. You will have to kill all the enemies before you can proceed. If you decide to complete all the hauntings, after awhile you will get tired of dealing with the maze world over and over. Especially because the hauntings will have your character running back and forth over long distances.The combat is decent but the lock on is pretty much useless. There is a good variety of "builds" you can do with your character but you will find that focusing on a certain build can make the challenge areas difficult because you will have to fight enemies a certain way to do real damage. Otherwise, you will be stuck doing trash damage until the enemies die. The game had potential to be something good but the developers decided to inject modern ideologies into it. I even made myself do a lot of the side stuff and finish all the hauntings to see if it would change my mind about the game but it didn't. At the end, I was just ready for it to be over.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers is basically what you would get if you took God of War and gave it a little bit of the Sherlock Holmes treatment. It’s an interesting combo that has both its pros and cons.Overall, the combat is pretty good. Hits have weight behind them, there’s a few different weapon types to mix and match mid-fight, the movement feels fluid, dodging, parrying, and blocking are responsive, and there’s an entire skill tree with new moves and such to add even more flavor. For not being the focus of the experience, the studio did a pretty good job making the combat fun to play.That said, it really suffers with its enemy variety. It gets kinda boring fighting the same type of ghosts over and over throughout the game, especially since the only visual difference between most of them is their color. The boss fights are cool, but there aren’t enough of them to break up the otherwise monotonous enemies.Exploration is also a big part of the experience and something Banishers does well. The level design in particular is solid. You have this large map to explore complete with branching paths, plenty of side objectives, towns with people to get to know, beautiful scenery, and I am just kinda a sucker for medieval/fantasy infused aesthetics and the world here in Banishers absolutely nails that.One thing I really was not a fan of was the whole crafting/upgrading element. It reminded me of games like A Plague Tale or even God of War, where it’s just kinda tacked on to the experience and there to give you an excuse to wander around more to find more grass, stone, and other random material to collect for future upgrades. That aspect was not really fleshed out and came across as tedious as a result.I liked the overarching plot. Two banishers - basically ghost hunters or paranormal investigators - traveling around solving cases and ultimately trying to decide the fate of Antea, your partner who herself is a ghost. It’s a great set up to tie together the rest of the game, which ultimately comes across as episodic.That can be good or bad depending on the person. You have this goal of reaching New Eden - the town where your partner died - but must stop along the way to assist with cases that ultimately have no relation to the rest of the plot. Some of these cases are genuinely interesting, some are bad, but most are just okay. You’ll get one that dives into a couple characters and raises some great questions about topics like death, relationships, and what it takes to survive in the world, and then one that has a very predictable and boring twist with surface-level characters.I would say for the most part, the cases are interesting, but there are quite a lot that just aren’t and you’re forced to go through them to progress anyways. Oftentimes the only relation they have to the main story is the decision you make at the very end when deciding who is to blame in a specific case. Your choices there ultimately decide the fate of your ghost partner, but I feel like the game could have done a bit more in making the rest of the story feel more than just episodic mini-stories.The entire thing takes about 20-25 hours to clear, so it is rather lengthy, but I can’t say I see myself replaying this one to make different choices purely because the individual cases themselves - given I already know the outcome - would just be a slog. Character designs are solid, the environments are detailed, the lighting is well-done, and the soundtrack is alright too. Performance-wise, I was unable to run the game natively at 4k 144fps medium-high settings on my 3080 Ti and ended up having to enable DLSS to compensate. After that though, no issues aside from the occasional funky animation bug.I would give Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden a light recommendation. It does many things well, such as the combat, the exploration, and the narrative too, but I can’t say that any single one of these is anything more than just “good”. The combat has issues with how repetitive it can be, the narrative is hit or miss due to the episodic nature of the game loop, and the whole crafting/upgrading system just felt shallow. That said, you do get some really interesting cases, characters, and the boss fights are really cool too. I’m glad I played it, but would only recommend it on sale or in a bundle.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unlike any other i have played in quite a while. I'm a huge fan of games with story and where the choices actually matter. This is that game. In a world where we are filled to the brim with remakes, re-releases, or the same game every year with a new cover, it's a breath of fresh air to get a unique entry into our catalogs. PROS:Unique, immersive, emotional story.Hauntings give a fresh perspective on the human condition and how sometimes evil can be hidden behind a bonnet or a bowtie.The interactions between Red and Antea are top notch, the dialogue, the voice acting, it's like a full-fledged movieThe graphics are some of the best you'll see. Whether it be slicing through specters to a lonely tear streaming down a character's face.CONS:The combat is by far the weakest aspect of the game. It's solid, it works, it's reactive but it just doesn't do anything new and exciting and for me personally it was a bit of a let down and repetitive. This has been a hidden gem of a game. Everytime i tell anyone about it, they claim to have never heard of it before and that's a shame. If you are a story fan, an RPG fan, a Souls fan, or even a horror fan, this game is definitely a must play. And it's not even going to cost you $70 like most AAA games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I am very impressed with this game. It is a massive step up from Vampyr in my opinion. The writing is super solid so far, the world and setting are cool and interesting, and, most importantly they don't punish you for not being a psychopath like they did in that game. The moral conundrum of deciding whether or not to kill is sooo much more compelling as it is actually  relevant to the game's story, and it also helps that you aren't forced into making the "bad" choices by the game's difficulty. A few cons worth noting though: the map is super hard to navigate; as hard as or harder than in Vampyr and it is downright infuriating sometimes. The camera is as much of an enemy in combat as any ghost. When you lock on it only tracks in one dimension, so if may pan towards the enemy, but still may point directly at the ground or sky unless you correct it manually. It is also just hard to control even outside of combat, at least on a controller. Another small thing is that the lip sync is really bad on the dialogue, but that's a minor complaint.I don't normally buy games on day one, but Vampyr had me intrigued enough that I wanted to give this one a go, and I definitely don't regret it so far.Edit: Additional note: it's sad that this is worth noting, but the game is pretty stable at launch. It crashed once when I first started and has had no issues since, which is what I had read in another review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great story-driven action game. I was sad to hear that it didn't sold as well as DON'T NOD expected and that they have to re-size the scope of their future projects. I would love to see another chapter of Banishers, whether it's a sequel, a prequel or a completely different story taking place in the same universe. I really enjoyed the 50+ hours I spent on this game. The combat is fun, nothing revolutionary but it has interesting mechanics, i.e. switching mid-combat between the two protagonists. The feeling of the fight is also great, your blows have weight and so the ones from your opponents. Speaking of opponents, variety isn't great but it's enough to never become boring. The graphics are nice, you can see it's not a triple A project and that there are some budget limits but the environment, backgrounds and characters all look inspired and overall the game looks very good. Where Banishers really shines though, it's the story. Narration is compelling and stays interesting from the beginning to the end. Side quests are also very intriguing, you get to investigate into the lives of many secondary characters you meet along the way. and lot's of them will reveal themselves quite different from what you thought at first glance. Player's decisions also have a big impact on the story, as you can choose which characters to save and which to condemn. You also have at least two different finales, but I don't want to lean too much into spoilers. Bottom line, if you enjoy a good looking, action-packed. story-driven action game, look no further. Banishers got everything you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This was quite an experience. The story is so well done and deeply emotional. Very few of the relationships are black and white, but rather very gray. Collecting information and solving haunting cases was always fun and intriguing. I still haven’t finished them all, (will come back. I get open world fatigue usually after 30-40hrs in a game) despite finishing the game. Everyone’s stories easily pull you in and get you invested. This game stands on its story above all. The combat is not setting the world on fire, but neither is it boring, IMO. I found it serviceable and by the second half of the game and getting close to the end, it was engaging. Just don’t expect deeply dynamic God of War level combat and in my opinion, you’ll be fine. The visuals are excellent. There are small things that point to it being a AA game but that is nothing negative. It’s a well crafted game and beautiful. The performance is solid and my 4070/7800X3D ran it like a dream. There doesn’t seem to be a way to turn off upscaling, which I found odd. Not an issue though. The game is well optimized and stable. I would add one note: although everyone is different, if you’re dealing with any kind of loss and the grief is still near, best keep this in your wishlist until the wound has had time to scab. It’s very emotional and I found myself frequently choked up. I hope many people try and enjoy this game. Huge thank you to Don’t Nod for this experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I'm a big Don't Nod! Vampyr is hands down one of the best games they ever made. Now when I had my first playthrough of this game I was absolutely exhausted n skipped 80% of dialogue just to get through the quest. I own a decent rig, but somehow this game had huge issues running smoothly. The fps drops were so high around third act of the game it was barely playable. Even with settings toned down, game still had huge fps drop and stutters and one crash. Let's talk about the story, they have/had amazing concept! The character design n enemy models in this game are absolutely gorgeous. Around the final act all pieces fit together and you get the full picture of how it all began and it's very well crafted. No issues with the story other than pacing. My biggest issue, and their biggest fumble with this game was optimization and gameplay. Gameplay is super bland, it's just sad. The upgrades, new weapons barely made a difference to the gameplay. Only thing different was how spongy enemies get with highest difficulty. After finishing the story I went to go for full 100% achs n I cannot put it into words what a rough time I had backtracking in this game. They could've implemented a mode of transport like horse or something to make moving around faster. The only way you move around apart from sprinting is fast travel which is strictly limited to safe houses. Which are never near the check point or location you're trying to get to. This game has the most saddest traversal I have ever experienced. It's clunky, it's ultra-slow, it's just not efficient. Sometimes you need to reach somewhere and the game will literally fool you around some pathetic obstacles while the objective just above your head..like climb ten rock walls, cross across a big wooden log with as slow movement as possible and so on. When you're trying to collect all collectibles it shouldn't be a chore, I beleive the traversal and sloggy movement took a heavy toll on backtracking. By the end of this games 100% completion, I was just done. I beleive this game had potential and could've been way better than what they dished out.

_childDocuments_.review: I want so badly to like this game, but for something toted as being all about "Difficult choices", it's maddening to have one choice shoved down your throat consistently throughout the game. In order to get the "good" endings, you must make the same exact choice every time for the entirety of the game, which takes every bit of the enjoyment of a role-playing game out of the game. The game even goes so far as to restrict your movement in places with invisible walls just in the middle of the road to block your progress. It feels very constrained.The combat is bland and flavorless. Punch things or stab things. Occasionally shoot things. Easy, cut and dried, with very little variance, and the same mobs springing up every couple of minutes.And the worst bit is the script / writing. The story has so much promise - it's INTERESTING - and it's just gutted by having the same tired conversations over and over again (Red and Antea are flat as characters; twenty hours in and it feels like all they ever talk about is their commitment to each other, which is nice, but we don't need constant dialogue about it to remind us its' there). Some of the dialogue with the NPCs is so obtuse you don't know what your actual goal is until it pops up on your map. And there are points where the game just jumps from talking to someone to "and now we're in the next spot to start the next quest". There are even moments where the soundtrack cuts out abruptly to silence because you've passed a marker where it should transition to the next track.It feels lazy. It feels hastily made and not well composed. Partly unfinished, and partly "we did just enough that we shouldn't have to deliver anything more".

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: After finishing it, i keep a clear thumbs up, but there are some issues. You can tell the Vampyr DNA. Partly from the weird engine that actually looks very good but has a infuriating (non-)movement system from the late stoneage.  But also a very intriguing story, characters, quests (hauntings), voice acting and all.  Which they then (/as in Vampyr!) sabotage!"   (check the super lazy short endings videos on youtube instead)  Movement and control wise it's not great. You can't jump even of minor ledges unless they are marked. Think Witcher 2 movement. Some (marked) barrels and stuff are destructable but most are not.  Making the world and your way though it feel rather scripted and pre-planned, despite the good size. .  So techncially apart from the very good graphics (with good performance) , it's not horrible but it feels somewhat outdated.  Ultrawide works fine, only cutscenes letterbox switch to 16:9. There is no FOV slider.----It is an absolute shame, the main plot forces all your choices in one direction for the "right" ending.  The game TELLS you you have to make THIS choice for this ending and THIS choice for the other. Giving you interesting  moral choices and then completely sabotaging that by telling you can't make these choices! What a waste!They did something similar in Vampyr. It's such a waste of all these great quests. ---There is  more depth and variety to the gameplay, quests and story telling than in Vampyr, which was mostly dialogues. This feels more like a bigger RPG. And the world is vastly bigger.  Sadly skills are exclusively combat focussed. Missed chance.There is some location recycling going on later (the mines...) and in the back and forth, the combat (for me!) somewhat overstays it's welcome. ---Story issue #2:I don't mind that they tried to check every PC box they could possibly reach. I guess devs have today (no, not really,it's history, you have very excuse).  But it causes massive problems with the world and story. There seems to be complete gender and racial equality in this 17th century. Except in a  few specific quests where it's suddenly not. It's world is full of strong independent woman and there is NO slavery to be seen anywhere in the world except in said quests...  These quests raise issues that don't seem to exist in that world (very, VERY much unlike the real 1600's) .But as a consequence these serious topics, that the protagonists approach like time travelled 21st century people btw (which they are NOT, they are meant to be contemporary) , feel completely out of touch with the games world. Beyond any political debate, there is a REAL plot logic problem. I don't care too much about this, but i get the anger over this point.  If you want modern rules, just set it in the modern world.  After all, your characters seem to come straight out of the 21st century. They do not act or think like 1600's people!Also there is a another crowbared in crafting/looting system. Will this crap ever stop?  Quite dramatic story moments and haunting(!) journeys instantly and utterly trivialised by picking up 3 leather and 2 flowers 2 seconds later. ... It feels SO unncessary. You could easily tie that to skill points without he resources loop. Maybe that's just me.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is going to be a bit of a Hidden Gem that has seemed to have flown under the radar of the "mainstream" . _childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is an interesting one. The gameplay is best described as God of War (2018)'s combat and inventory mechanics, plus some light conversation additions (like a "choose what you'll say next" kind of thing). What it certainly "lifts" from God of War, it adds its own little style and nuance to it just enough to not make it feel like a blatant copy. Banishers by trade, Antea Duarte and Red mac Raith live a nomadic lifestyle and find hauntings to solve. The hauntings are a neat type of quest as some of them are quite varied and have some interesting twists and turns. You'll spend time investigating secrets, lies, and even horrific wrongs that have been done to others and you do fulfil the role of judge, jury, and sometimes executioner.Nothing is ever black and white in this game (aside from Antea and Red 😅) and you will be in for a story that will show how flawed mankind is. Short sighted, scared, judgemental, stubborn, and scarred are just some of the many traits shared by the numerous NPC characters in a world that has a lot of stories to tell.But the real stars of the game are Antea and Red. Although not married, it is clear that they have the love of a couple that have been married for a while. It is not a perfect romantic love, but rather a more pragmatic and "matured" love. They have long since moved past the "whispering sweet nothings" stage and sometimes do argue. But the chemistry is there, both in the writing and in the excellent voice acting. Antea dies early in the game and becomes the very thing that they banish by trade, a ghost. There's a consistent in-world reason for her to remain with Red throughout the game, and as the story progresses they do have to come to terms with what they need to do. Will Red banish her? Or will he find a way to bring her back to life? And at what cost? While they work towards their goal, Antea does help Red with her new supernatural abilities.Banishers is also a fairly good game gameplay-wise. It's not all hack and slash, and you won't spend hours and hours in cutscenes. The gameplay does mix it up a little bit, even if only in pacing (some quests being hauntings and other being more traditional fetch or "clear out a bunch of enemies" types). It was incredibly refreshing to see that in the end they did not present a "choose your ending" type of selection and just went with the choice I made dozens of hours in advance (supported by the way I resolved the hauntings). It is possible that this might be different based on your play, but if you play the game with the "goal" in mind, then the ending just goes on naturally.I actually felt like I was going to add a lot more to both lists above, but somehow I am hard pressed to add much more. It's not the best game I have ever played, but also far from the worst. It does not have huge set pieces, and yet I won't easily forget the main story. I will play this again in the future to see the other ending, and how what I have to do to achieve that affects the world.At around 50 hours for a fairly complete run through the campaign (I did not collect all of the collectibles, but I did all of the side quests), I would say this is a worthwhile purchase. I picked it up on a sale, and I would recommend you do the same if you are uncertain.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, I'm about 2 hours into the game and this far I can say, it's amazing. I might update my review when I'm further in or if I have finished it. We'll see.What I can say about it so far?The game picks up the pace rather slowly. It's a story driven game and is more about talking to the people and listening to what they have to say. The investigation part is not specifically mention worth, you get guided a lot to the next clue one by one. You don't have to put any effort in solving a riddle or something like that. You enter an area of investigation and then look around, but mostly the quest markers guide you, to where you find the next clue. That's a little disappointing so far, but since those were only the first cases and they still seem to be a part of the tutorial, I hope they will become more of a challenge.The fighting is simple, but fun. You can dodge, parry and riposte, but it's not like a souls game. You can heal by flasks mid fight and it's mostly about avoiding damage and choosing the right kind of attack at the right timing, but it's pretty forgiving. When there are enough enemies around you, you get indications when an attack is about to hit. If you are in the middle of a combo, it's hard to deal with an attack. So again, it's all about timing and best not to let the enemies circle you.The levels are rather narrow but you can explore a little bit and gather ressources. It's not an open world game so far and I'm glad about that. But there is a quick travel system and a little bit of metroidvanian, since some paths will open up later, when you gained some new abilties. There is a skill tree that opens up when you keep playing and by levelling up you can decide where to spend your skill points. Currently it's mostly about improving your combat abilties.The resources you gather are for rituals and improving your gear. No crafting involved yet, but that might also be coming into play.What the game really excels in is the story and atmosphere. It's dark and mysterious, the story is intruiging. I'm really curious how the story will play out and what impact my choices will have. But there are choices you have to make that seem very impactful forced upon you very early in the game. I'm wondering if I can go against my choices later or not. Even if the choices do result in different stories, I probably won't see this as a game that I will be replaying.So should you buy the game? If you're in for a story driven game in a dark setting full of despair and some emotional plot points, mixed with a little bit of fighting, then the game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden emerges as a distinctive addition to the action-RPG genre, blending supernatural elements with a rich narrative that delves deeply into themes of love, loss, and redemption. This title continues the tradition of narrative-driven experiences but with a fresh twist: the hauntingly beautiful, yet perilous setting of New Eden, a fictional colonial America filled with ghosts and ethereal mysteries.Gameplay in Banishers is a compelling mix of combat, exploration, and narrative choices that significantly impact the storyline. Players take on the roles of Antea Duarte and Red mac Raith, ghost hunters and lovers, navigating through a world where the living and the dead are intricately intertwined. The combat system is robust, offering a variety of spectral weapons and abilities that are as satisfying to use as they are strategic. The game's graphics are visually striking, with environments that beautifully capture the eerie and somber atmosphere of New Eden. However, it's not without its faults; some players might find the pacing a bit slow, and certain gameplay mechanics, like the ghost-binding sequences, can feel repetitive over time.Overall, Banishers is a notable achievement. It successfully marries a poignant, character-driven story with engaging gameplay mechanics. While it may not reinvent the wheel in terms of action or RPG mechanics, it offers enough innovation in its narrative approach and setting to stand out in a crowded market. For fans of story-rich games and supernatural narratives, Banishers is a journey worth taking, though some may crave a bit more polish in gameplay to match the excellence of its storytelling.I'd rate Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden an 80 out of 100.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers truly embodies Dontnod's reputation for crafting captivating stories. However, while the game excels in storytelling for the most part, there are instances where it feels like the writers are forcing character motivations and personal agendas, resulting in some amateurish writing at times, particularly with the central relationship between Antea and Red. The lack of substantial motivation for players to invest in their bond is disappointing, as it undermines many pivotal choices throughout the game. there are times where its almost a surprise the game marketed them as a couple considering how little the writing of these characters supports this fact.Additionally, the combat system proves to be more of a hindrance than a compelling gameplay element, often feeling like a cumbersome obstacle standing in the way of the game's more engaging aspects.Despite these shortcomings, Banishers still manages to shine through its remarkable character side stories and overall gripping plot. While there may be eye-rolling moments along the way, the journey is ultimately worth experiencing, making it a recommendation despite its flaws

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Cons:As interesting as the story and world is, I feel that it falls short of its potential as an enticing game. Maybe it's the hassle of walking around the world in circular motion, a lack of early investment in the main characters, or too heavy an emphasis on world-building and not enough on player-character interaction. Or more likely it's a whole bunch of things from UI to writing. There's a lot to collect & go back to after exploring, but doing so might be really annoying depending on how much patience you have. A lot of people seem to dislike Antea's character, but I find her more developed than Red. Antea has strong (sometimes conflicting and nonsensical tho) opinions and reasons for them, where Red doesn't appear to. Some voice lines repeat far too much in areas such as world exploration and combat, so Antea's 'lemme fight' lines do get irritating. Just feels like it falls short of 'better than average' in every area besides story & graphics. But I'm 5" so who am I to complain?

Because of this, the game can absolutely feel too long especially if you spend too much time doing the optional objectives.Conclusion: I liked the game and the story was very well written and presented. _childDocuments_.review: I've played a LOT of great games in my lifetime. EASILY thousands of games. Thing is, this game here has to be one of the best written, best voiced games I've ever experienced. It's full of actual heartfelt motives, emotions and events that really make you think. It doesn't hurt that it's beautiful to look at and play, that the sound is amazingly well done and that combat is actually really well done the more you get on with it. I enjoyed Vampyr a LOT. Now, after having played this game for a bit, I REALLY wish that Don't Nod would, at some point, give it a hi-def redux. A face-lift per se. Anyway, just rambling. However, Don't Nod's games are easily worth the price of admission and give you dozens of hours to get lost in their narratives and action. I will say this though. DO NOT GO ONLINE AND LOOK UP "ANSWERS" TO QUESTION ABOUT THE GAME. Just don't. PLAY THE GAME LIKE YOU'RE LIVING IT. Like you're the ONLY person playing it and YOU will make the outcome happen. Don't watch Youtube videos. Don't watch Let's Play vids. Don't ask your friends what they did or will do. Do what YOU WOULD DO. Make the game YOURS and whatever outcome you get it will be truly be UNIQUE to YOUR choices. Fantastic game in all regards. The writing staff are, easily, some of the best writers in the business now and it shows in all their games. If you're on the fence and you enjoy a more action heavy approach to a fantastic narrative, then, well, get the game and enjoy it.Oh, and LOOK UP.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely beautiful game - an absolutely stunning follow up to Vampyr (which I liked as well).If you enjoy beautifully written (and acted) characters, Banishers is for you. The developers did an incredible job creating New Eden and in Red and Antea, two highly compelling and sympathetic leads.  The world is unrelentingly bleak and the story line centre on themes of prejudice, violence and, trauma and grief. Your moral choices are a core part of this game and you face the consequences of them right through to the end, of which there are several conclusions. This is all complemented by a haunting soundtrack.  The game is not a technical marvel but it is beautifully presented (especially the characters) asnd ran bug free on my 4080-based system with DLSS 3 active. A highly polished game in my experience.The only shortcoming that many point to is the combat. While I do agree that it is the weak link in that it can be a bit clunky at times - I mostly enjoyed it! There weren't any annoying difficulty spikes and I found there was enough variety to keep me engaged - both in terms of abilities and enemies. This is to its credit given that I spent close to 30 hours playing this game (I did not complete all the side quests). Definitely a contender for one my games of the year in the single player action/adventure category. Well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Could have been a fun and spooky game, but the writers chose racism and no atmosphere.Colonial Americans would not have accepted Antea. At all. Some would call her a devil. Some would kill her on sight. 100%, without exception, would respond to her with hostility or contempt, as to a lesser being. Many would have Red arrested for consorting with her. Remember, these are the people who fled England because they were TOO EXTREME in their zealotry.This is set in 1695. Starting in the 1640s, the colonies started passing laws involving people from African descent. In 1695, not only was slavery legal, but in much of Colonial America at this time, it was *against the law* for people of African descent NOT to be enslaved.The devs wanted a woman of color as a main character, and that's awesome. But to do it in Colonial America, they needed to whitewash history. They needed to make monstrously abusive people seem like normal decent folks. They needed to make real suffering and abuse seem negligible. And any sane person would have realized, this is an either/or. To have the WoC co-protagonist meant they would have to brazenly rewrite history in favor of the most hideous monsters this side of the Nazis. And that's what they chose to do.This whitewashing is so offensive. It’s a grievous insult to the untold thousands of people who suffered through race-based slavery, trading off the reality of human oppression for an easy fix of simplistic woo-woo empowerment. It is far too forgiving of the evils of the early colonists, and it makes light of the suffering of historical African Americans.This game is racist. It gives depth and dignity to some of the most bigoted people imaginable, and robs the dignity and reality of those who were exploited. There is no upside to this whitewashing of extreme racism and downplaying of the historical realities of oppression.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start with the positives.  The voice acting and detailed, life-like characters are simply put, superb. The story is a novel idea and very well executed.  Interesting game play with the switch between Antea and Red....and of course the beautifully crafted world.What I, however, felt was leaning a bit too far out of the window, was the very clear 'feminist' push.  I am myself a female gamer, but a crucial fact, is that if one is to balance an unequal state, one must do just that.  Balance it.  Not tip it in the other direction.  It seemed subtle at first, but over time made me sigh and roll my eyes a bit.  How all the women, or comments about them (barring maybe one or two), were so courageous and so strong and so remarkable and so intelligent and..and ...and.... It was so over stated that it became 'desperate'.  To add, the only snivelling cowardly types were men. Along with that, take the underlying, almost constant nip of condescendance in Antea's manner towards Red.  Keep the script exactly the same....but change the sexes.  Impossible.   Now these situations can be a reality in any given sample of people, but it was too predictable not to be deliberate.  The icing on the cake was using sentences describing the male character Lammy as having an over eager manner of a 'constantly yapping pup' in his Haunting description.  Would that have been used to describe any of the female characters?  Absolutely not.  Balance the scale!  Don't tip it.

_childDocuments_.review: +A well-written story with likable characters +Amazing voice acting of the lead characters+A slew of quality side missions+A continuous Meteroidvania-esque landmass to explore +Rich with content-The lip animations are atrocious-Melee combat feels underwhelming-Lackluster enemy variety and repetitive encounter design-Getting 100% completion is tiresome Seemingly set in the same universe as Vampyr, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden tells the story of Red mac Raith and Antea Duarte, lovers and professional Banishers — ghost detectives and all-around paranormal problem solvers. Set in 1695, the duo travels to the North American frontier, to a fictional New England town called New Eden, tasked with investigating a curse that has befallen the once-booming community. Things do not go as planned and the duo is defeated by an evil force way beyond their banishing capabilities. Antea is brutally murdered and Red is thrown into the ocean, only to be saved by a mysterious stranger. Antea also returns, but as a ghost, something Banishers are trained to get rid of. Torn between their duty as Banishers and vows as lovers, the tragic couple is left with a moral dilemma — do they sacrifice the hapless denizens to bring Antea back to life, or will Red muster up the willpower to elevate Antea from eternal sorrow? The narrative of Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is made more memorable by the excellent performances of the main actors. Red and Antea are compelling and highly likable characters possessing unique traits, emotions, and attitudes. While Amaka Okafor does a great job as the stern and emotionally stoic Antea, Rus Bain's portrayal of Red steals the show. Bain delivers an award-worthy performance as the guilt-driven Scottsman. Torn between his vows and his beloved, Bain delivers each line with such conviction and emotion that I was in awe. Moreover, the main characters share such good chemistry that makes even the most mundane and trope-y moments feel entertaining. There's a lot of character development, back and forth, and moments of revelations with the main actors nailing the script they're given. Voice acting for the rest of the cast is pretty good as well, and a big step up from Don't Nod's previous ventures. What's not great is the lip-syncing or the lack-there-of. The lip animations do not sync at all with what's being spoken, and they do not do justice to the excellent voice acting. Seriously, a big letdown.Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a game full of choices and consequences. The frontier is filled with characters afflicted by the spirits of those who have departed. On their quest, the grief-stricken Red and ghastly Antea have to solve cases of hauntings and decide the fate of the former townsfolk of New Eden. The game features more than twenty well-written and varied cases for Red and Antea to take on, each presenting the duo with conflicting and difficult choices that affect their lives as those of those involved. While all the cases are similar structurally (find a haunting, investigate, find clues, confront the ghost, make a decision), each one is distinct in terms of its story, motivations, and themes. While one case may have the duo assisting a spirit solve its murder, another might be about helping a ghost say goodbye to a loved one. There's even a case where you help a time-traveling ghost trying to prevent its past self from taking her life. These are not stand-alone side missions, either. Almost all the cases connect the inhabitants of New Eden in one way or another and tie into the main story beautifully while exploring the socio-political undertones of the 17th-century American frontier.  The gameplay department is where Don't Nod's games typically stumble a bit. While Banishers has its share of problems, the game offers a far more cohesive gameplay loop than the developers' previous ventures. While Banishers takes a cue from Vampyr for its narrative design, its God of War (2018) inspirations are clear as day. Traversal, exploration, and combat closely resemble that of Santa Monica's blockbuster game. But rather than coming across as a cheap imitation, Banishers take the GoW formula and reshape it into its own style.As mentioned above, the exploration and traversal of Banishers closely resemble that of GoW due to having the same level design philosophy. The whole game takes place in a huge, continuous landmass (with one minor exception) and hardly takes away the focus from the main characters. The levels are designed akin to a 3D Metroidvania with plenty of ability-gated sections and secret areas. There are 4 large biomes with their own visual style and activities. They are all interconnected (except dimensional rifts) and loop back to one another thanks to a slew of shortcuts. This type of design gives the whole game a great sense of scale and gives the feeling that you're going on a single, large adventure. The downside to this is that there is a lot of tedious backtracking if you decide to engage in side activities. Thankfully, the map screen and HUD compass are pretty accurate. There are lots of traversal animations like jumping down, scaling walls, jumping across platforms, rappelling down, etc. and these get old fast. Thus, I wish there were some end-game abilities that made backtracking easier.Exploration in Banishers is an extremely rewarding experience. The game is filled with enemy clusters to destroy, loot to find, collectibles to collect, treasures to hunt, puzzles to solve, and side missions to uncover. It feels as if there is something new waiting to be discovered in each corner of the map. That being said, there are a bit too many checklist activities in the game for completionists. I played Banishers for a whopping 45+ hours and still couldn't finish all the side content. Hunting for the ungodly amount of collectibles made me give up on getting the platinum. The lack of a NG+ means that you'll have to get all items in a single playthrough, which is just too much tedium. The combat system in Banishers is not up to par with the rest of the game. Sure, it's way better than the combat systems in Remember Me and Vampyr, but at the same time, it makes the production value of the game stick out. The melee combat, in particular, is kind of bland. The animations are decent and chaining combos feel fluid, but it just doesn't have the "oomph". Moreover, the camera and lock-on system seem to have a mind of their own and are wildly inconsistent. Ranged combat fares better in comparison, thanks to excellent haptic trigger support and the beefy sound of a musket firing. You can also switch to Antea at any given time (provided you have enough spirit points) and she has her own combo system, and you're drip-fed with powerful abilities as the story progresses. The combat does get better after you've unlocked lots of skills and found better gear. However, much like GoW, Banishers suffer from the problem of lackluster enemy variety and encounter design. What little enemy types there are, all look and act more or less the same and the arena type of encounter design gets stale fast.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - 5 out of 5 StarsI saw this game advertised at the Game Awards in 2022 and I immediately knew I was going to play it day 1. Supernatural RPG with horror elements and based on the colonies/witch trials in America? Sign me up - the witch trials are my Roman Empire.With 108 hours under my belt, I just finished the game and all side-quests/haunting cases and it was INCREDIBLE, the whole game. I took my time and really savored this game and enjoyed all my time in New Eden with Red and Antea. I took so many screenshots (the game is STUNNING), I felt like a tourist.The ending - I chose the  ending and I have no regrets. If I feel up to it (the ending was VERY emotional), I may go back and play the other main ending, but I'm satisfied with my choice for now. This game feels very much like the newer God of Wars, so if you like those games, this could be right up your alley.Red Mac Raith is up there with Arthur Morgan as one of the best written male characters ever. The very definition of masculinity done right, I loved him right away. Nit-picks - Devs, PLEASE, for all that is holy, PLEASE stop Antea from saying stuff during battles so much. We get it, she wants to participate. It's fine the first couple times, but OMG, I could repeat her lines in my sleep. "Hogging all the fun?" "Can I join in?" "I'm here, you know." GIRL. She even said it when SHE was the one fighting! Other than that, my only other dislike was the music, which seemed to be put together in FL Studio with some random generators. The budget for this game definitely wasn't spent on music or marketing (I've barely seen any advertising for this game, and half of my friends don't even know about it - I'm trying to spread the word).Honestly, this is probably my Game of the Year. I will definitely go back and play it again in the future, once my ADHD addled brain has forgotten most of the plot. One last thing - I swore to myself when I started the game that not one yellow barrel or crate would survive in New Eden by the time I was finished. I meant it. Those wily b*st*rds tried to hide from me, but I found them all and banished every single one. They deserved it.They know what they did.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the mid-2000s, there were many God of War clones, and that trend continues with the 2018 reboot. Banishers is essentially a God of War clone, almost to a T, barrowing many elements such as combat, exploration, storytelling, and the upgrade system. However, there’s a hint of “Eurojank” present that I just can’t shake. While the story, setting, and lore are interesting enough (the key word is “enough”), the game never excels to the heights of the game it’s trying to become.You play Red Mac, Raith, and Antea Duarte. Lovers who are now separated by the plane of the dead. Banishers are people who go around removing hauntings from people, places, and objects, but they can also pass judgment and execute the living for doing wrong to those who previously lived. It’s an interesting concept, but sadly, the game never goes into more detail about it. How can these people just kill the living based on what the dead say? What are the laws and rules surrounding this? The game also doesn’t go into the background or history of the Banishers. This is something that God of War did well. We need a lot of backstory if we’re going to spend 25+ hours in a game like this. The entire game is just pretty “good,”  but never memorable or amazing. It always just falls below that mark. While I found the world and atmosphere of New Eden fascinating, the way the story and world are unfolded to the player are boring, mundane, or just not interesting. Reading material is pointless and doesn’t add to anything. Let’s just start with the combat. Heavy and light attacks make up the basis of combos, but you can switch to Antea in the ghost plane, who has more powerful attacks. Her bar isn’t HP, but an energy meter. Hit decrease this as well as using your attack powers. You can refill this bar by fighting as Red in the real world, but he doesn’t have any special attacks, and this really kept me from creating a strategy or learning how to beat enemies. Red just light and heavy attacks enemies (with a heavy charge attack), and the game tells you Red does more damage to ghosts and Antea does more damage to possessed bodies, but it never really seemed to be effective. You can parry attacks, which the game heavily relies on for more damage, and Red has a gun that you get about 1/4th through the game; it’s a one-shot rifle that requires a reload. This can sometimes do a lot of damage, but the enemies are so boring and uninteresting that there’s no distinguishable feature or stat to build strategies in your head. Ghosts are pretty easy, while anything else can damage sponges. I just couldn’t combo or create a meaningful pattern for defeating enemies, and it made combat one of the least enjoyable parts of the game. It also just feels slightly clunky and sluggish.The upgrade system feels almost as useless. You get experience for Red and Antea by completing side quests (called hauntings), which grant you additional damage for certain attacks, but I never really got to unlock any new combos or powers. Antea’s three powers are found during the story, so the upgrade tree is just boring, and I never felt powerful enough and couldn’t even use skills to become more powerful. This also bleeds over into the equipment system. Red can equip rifles, blades, outfits, and potion bottles, which increase attributes, but no matter how high they were, I always felt just too weak to really get an edge over the enemies. Antea can equip various accessories to help her attributes, but nothing felt powerful or meaningful.This leads to the exploration and hunting gameplay loop that’s identical to God of War, but without the enjoyment. Why do I want to hunt chests and haunted objects, fast travel back, and open new paths with new powers if all this equipment feels useless and haunting cases only give me a single esence for the skill tree when it also feels pointless? They are fun at first, and the haunting cases are like mini-murder mysteries you can solve, but they also play out the same way. Some lead to small boss fights, some are just item gathering quests, and they all add to the main story choice (I won’t spoil it) for the ending, but they are all optional. There is a lot of side content here, but I gave up about halfway through because I just didn’t feel any of the rewards were worth it. With that said, the game looks pretty good for an Unreal Engine 4 game. There is a lot of detail in the environments; they are varied, and the atmosphere is thick and heavy, but everything just teeters on not quite being enough on every front. The ability to even upgrade equipment doesn’t help make you feel like you’re growing as a player or character. I felt just as weak from the beginning of the game to the end and wound up dying quite a bit. Some side content, like the void walking dungeons, is tedious and boring, and the only redeeming value is exploring the world and picking up all these items and chests. I just wish the rewards were better.Overall, Banishers has a lot of interesting concepts going for it, and the voice acting is good (the facial animations are very dated). I wanted to know more about this world, but the game just doesn’t give it up. The side content is questionable, the combat is too clunky, and there’s no strategy or really good combo system implemented to make it stand out from the crowd. There aren’t really any puzzles, and the story is predictable towards the end, making you feel like your choices are almost meaningless. I feel like if DONTNOD had another go, they could get a lot more right. As it stands, this feels like a “Eurojank” God of War.

_childDocuments_.review: An [Okay] RPG game with choices and a pretend-to-be detective vibe, with great graphics that are on par with 2024 yet the visual landscapes are too realistic and ordinal, nothing rememberable or special. Has a good story but non-lasting gameplay and gameplay/flow is really slow in all aspects.The prolog is long af, and the first starter mission is also quite long, like solid 2-3 hours long. This becomes really slow and probably is where the majority would fall off because it does not ramp up, it remains slow.The main story is good but there's an issue with it. And the side story flow is terrible, while the majority of the quests have the same plot -> someone has done something objectively horrible -> is haunted for it -> forgive or kill them, that's around 70% of all quests, including the main one. The exploration and traveling are not interesting enough to spent so much time running from A to B to A to C to A.The side quest and story have the biggest flaw of all detective games where you are not actually a detective, you follow a linear discovery of clues and are fed with the whole plot through it, not having to think or deduce or wonder if you about to murder or forgive a lying murderer is not that fun.The exploration has the biggest issue, it is treated as it is fun to run around while it aint, it is for the first quarter of the game, but then falls off as it's just the same, in fact, all of the game stays the same after around a quarter of it, you do get new skills but that doesn't really shake things up. One of the main issues with exploration is that random "Metroidvania" elements, which does not fit the style/gameplay; this pass is blocked, come back later after you unlock the game. The first major unlock is about at 33% of the game, and the third is around 60%, so you are either faced with rushing the main story to get those unlocks and explore freely or face the disappointment of realizing you cannot go there now, come back later when you have no more reason to be here as you have completed the side quest that sent you here, which is simply disappointing.Combat variety is lackluster, with not much variety in enemies or enemy types, it gets boring after a few hours, and if you start doing quite long sidequests you are just repeating the same combat and same exploration patterns for hours, with non-impactful rewards. The one good part of it was the random affixes on "activity" that had a basic melee/lunge/parry/range or one of the abilities does more damage, so you change your playstyle for it.Gearing is somewhat okay but is very simple and lacks any complexity, you pick the gear with the stats you want, you gather the resource on your way to a mission, you upgrade to increase stats, and that's it. Skill upgrade choices felt unimpactful as well.Overall, it's way too slow, way way too slow, nothing is captivating, neither the gameplay nor exploration, story choices are the only good part yet they have no consequence on you, and 90% of side quests are not worth it. If you pick this up, I'd recommend focusing on the main story only, forgetting about everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game! It's a very solid 8.5/10, but only for two reasons I cannot give it a 10. First, the combat, which is heavily inspired by God of War, is just not as good. The other is too much combat and exploration. Where this game shines is in the narrative, the story, and the characters. Every side character is well-written and well-acted. The VO is one of the best in games. The Haunting cases are very interesting, and more often, you are brought to a heavy choice. The story is about the two main characters, a married couple, Red and Antea. At the beginning of the game, Antea dies from a Nightmare ghost, the big baddy of the game. And later, she rejoins you as a ghost. In this universe, the dead linger if they have unfinished business to do, and you, as a Banisher, are the one who should cut their ties to the living by either Banishing them or Ascending them. There is also a Third option, to Blame the living for the ghost's return by killing them and taking their life force, cutting the tie. For these options, you need the object that ties the ghost to this world; in this case, it is your wife's body, which is held hostage by the Nightmare, so basically, you need to recover Antea's body, no matter your choice. If you do like me and Blame most people, you will have the option to resurrect your dead wife, but you must Blame a lot of people, and not everyone will deserve it.Secondly, the main story uncovers what happened and why the whole county of New Eden is cursed. Why is the Nightmare here? And honestly, in some places, it broke my heart. The final boss is an undead, floating corpse full of hatred toward everything alive, yet you can feel sympathy toward them and wonder if there is a way that you could help her...It's a must-play for people who enjoy a good story.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Beat it and the ending mostly delivers. Definitely feels like a game where it's more about the journey than the destination.Overall, it's a good game with a few flaws that hold it back. First, this game lives and dies by it's story and the two leads. If you don't connect with them, then the game won't work for you. Second, the combat isn't good. I didn't like God of War 2018 or Ragnarok's combat much at all, and this is a less polished version of it. And holy moly are enemies spongey. Like, why? Don't Nod. Hire an actual combat director and figure it out PLEASE. You're so close, but not quite there. Third, padded side content. The game is open world, but really doesn't feel as though it needs to be. Fourth, performance is all over the place. Fifth, enemy variety is lacking and the enemies aren't very fun to fight. Again, combat is serviceable but not good enough to warrant how often the game forces you into combat scenarios. In spite of all that, the game's narrative is excellent, voice acting is mostly great across the board, choices feel meaningful, and it presents some interesting moral dilemmas. _childDocuments_.review: [Normal difficulty]+ I really loved the setting, late 1600s settler America with ghosts makes for really interesting, atmospheric storytelling, a great sense of place for all the locations; all of these together form the game's biggest strength and what carried it hard for me, in spite of its deficiencies. + It's well written, with an interesting story revolving around a deeply-rooted mystery and a beautifully written relationship between the two main characters. The haunting side-quests also have good writing across the board with great (and mournful, they are hauntings after all) little side-plots that I had fun uncovering. The lore is also well done, featuring an interesting world in which banishers, witches and demonologists all have their own philosophies and ways of dealing with the supernatural.+ While it's not the most advanced use of Unreal Engine (the character and facial animation and ghost VFX could have been better), the environments are gorgeous and an integral part in building the setting. Overall, the game is a looker and makes the most of a AA budget.+ The combat system, in isolation, is actually pretty great, it has depth. It's snappy when switching between light and hard attacks, the rifle, Antea's powers, when parrying and blocking. There are various perks, granted by either pieces of equipment or a skill-tree where you can make some choices, which make this back-and-forth feel powerful and fun to use and the two archetypes of enemies (ghosts and possessed) are weak to the two different main characters. There is some fun to be had with these systems and the juggling of abilities and cooldown management and I found it pretty fun to fight overall. - What lets the combat system down is the small variety of enemies and the fact they kind of fight the same way. Other than being either ghosts or possessed, they don't really force you to strategize differently so you keep switching between the same systems and managing the same cooldowns all the time. It's repetitive, but saved by the fact that the combat itself is fortunately fun and feels good.* The music definitely fits the setting and builds up the atmosphere, but it doesn't really stand out besides that.+ Voice acting is generally strong and, coupled with good writing, it makes for believable characters.- Each haunting case has an additional activity at the end, required to mark it as closed, but all of them bar a couple are the most tedious kind of padding sadly.- Speaking of padding, the game unfortunately has a lot of it. There are a lot of hidden places to be found and a lot of question marks dotting the world map, but very few of those have actually meaningful rewards sadly. Some do, but it will take a bit to intuit which ones are worth searching for and which ones are just endless amounts of crafting materials. I wish the world was smaller and more concentrated with better rewards, so it could free budget for other things. The game is needlessly too big.* On normal difficulty, if you close all the haunting cases and explore around a bit as well, you'll be overleveled enough that it trivialises the final boss fight, which may rob the ending of some its impact. Boss fights overall are pretty fun though.+ Siridean has one of the more eerie character designs for a witch I've seen recently. Really cool character, both from a visual and narrative standpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: My first session took 50 hrs and that was with about 90% map completion. The story revolves around you blaming or ascending/banishing the npcs or their ghost according to which oath you want to fulfill. The things I liked most about the game were the story, narrative and voice acting. It was very fun doing the side quest and meeting new npcs in New Eden. Each person felt like they had different personalities and had a sense of belonging in the world. That is what mainly kept me hooked to keep playing. The things I greatly disliked were the combat and traveling in the game. My god this should have just been titled rock climbing simulator because you will be climbing, ducking, and squeezing your way around New Eden every other minute. The combat is fun at first and there are modifiers that make you want to experiment with different builds, but that is about as far as the combat goes. The transitioning between Red and Antea to do combo moves works, but I would rather of mabye idk gave her orders or so she could fight while Red could do his own thing at the same time. The combat modifiers in some sections can really drag out the combat if you don't do some experimentation with builds due to how bad all other damage is reduced because of forced modifiers. New Eden has some pretty big sections and the only way to fast travel is by BONFIRES. There are wayyyyyy to many side quest where most of my time was just spent running back and fourth and climbing. I really would have appreciated just being able to teleport as soon as a quest was done since some quest have steps that require you to go to multiple places for completion. One thing I wanted to mention was it gets annoying to hear Antea and Red converse EVERY time he/she use their powers and whatnot to break walls and kill roots and shoot things. _childDocuments_.review: It's an okey game. More of a 6.5/10, with some decent storytelling, decent core combat, not enough variety, and ALOT of padding. By 30 hours it outstays it's welcome, let alone the 50 it took me to beat it.If you need more detail, read on.- The story is good, except a few issues (see "The Ugly" section). The characters feel real, well fleshed out, and the central romance at the heart of the story will hook you and compel you to keep playing. If it does not, then the game is not worth it.- The magical lore of the world is interesting. I found the way they use ghosts, spirits and magic to be a fresh take on lower magic fantasy.- The core combat mechanics of the game are good, except one big issue (again see "The Ugly" section). By core combat mechanics I mean how you character moves, fights and combos moves.- The itemisation and ability tree gave me fun options to play with and create a cool build (see "The Bad" section for a caveat though).- Good metrovenia puzzles (although hampered by a big issue see "The Bad").- The game looks good, and the environmental details are awesome, the areas are creative and different too.- It has excellent choices, and consequences, and puts a lot of other RPG's to shame in that area. Even for minor quests, which will give you different follow up quests, depending on your choices.- The game takes the time to really let you get to know the NPC's and fleshes them out in good detail. - It weaves different stories into each other, and really makes it feel like a consistent world.- The stance switching in combat, is actually quite fun as are the powers.- The locations weave into themselves in a cool way. - Enemy variety is very low. Let me break down the enemy variety for you, because this the main reason not to play the game. There are 5 spirit enemies, which can posses 5 corpse types, and there are 5 boss types. In a 30 to 50 hour game! The developers though they were clever by allowing 4 different spirit types to posses the same corpse type, thereby giving it "different" mechanics to and create more variety. But in reality they are all kind of the same, you will barley notice the difference. Compare this with an old game like Dark Souls 3. In just the starting area you will encounter 13 different enemy types.- Loot in this game is bad 19/20 times. You will solve puzzles (which are very good) to get to a chest, and most of the time its just some money (you don't need) and some materials (you have plenty of). And then as your reward the game spawns spirits for you to fight which you are already tired of fighting.- Because there are so few enemies, and they are not that hard to fight, creating cool builds feels like a waste of time. Despite the fact that the build system is very creative.- Weapon variety does not exist. You have a sword, a gun, ghost fists and 3 active powers. You will use all of these because you have to. They unlock slowly as well. No single option is good enough to carry the game, and would also be boring.- The game encourages you to grind (via special areas) for materials and attribute bonuses. So you can upgrade your gear, and character. You do this by fighting enemies you are bored of fighting, so you could get better at fighting those same enemies again (sound fun?)- The story has a lot political messaging. It starts of small, but by the end of the game I was getting sick of it. Luckily their writing team was good enough (which is rare) to wrap their political message in a good story. In fact sometimes it feels like there are two writing philosophies fighting with each other in the game. One that wants to shove modern American politics down your throat, and another that just wants to tell a tragic love story between two people. The second one won, but not by much. If you are curious about the message, it goes something like this: men are bad, religion is bad, white people are bad (I'm sure you've heard it before).- The game has no way for you to switch your enemy lock in. In many combat games you can press the right thumbstick to lock onto a enemy (this game has that). Then in those games you can more the thumbstick left and right to switch who you are locked onto (this game does not have that). It may sound minor, but it will ruin you combat experience 9/10 times, the frustration level with this is high.- The game is too damn long. If you take into account the problems under "The Bad" section, you can see how it gets boring. The game should have been half as long and set in a smaller area. They should have build less levels and areas, and made more enemies and weapon types.
