_childDocuments_.review: A Mostly Positive ReviewBanishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a game that captivates players with its beautiful graphics and intriguing storylines. The visuals are stunning, creating an immersive experience that draws you into the haunting world of New Eden. The game's dialogue and main storyline are well-crafted, keeping you engaged and invested in the unfolding narrative.One of the standout features of Banishers is the "Hauntings" — mini-stories that are scattered throughout the game. These Hauntings are enticing, motivating you to unravel the mysteries and resolve the issues plaguing the spirits. You genuinely care about discovering what lies at the end of their dramas, adding a layer of emotional depth to the game.The music in Banishers is fine, though not particularly memorable. It blends seamlessly with the game, enhancing the atmosphere of each zone. The ambiance is fitting and contributes to the overall immersive experience.The game offers multiple difficulty levels, including a "Story" mode that makes the game almost too easy, perfect for players who are more interested in the narrative than the challenge. For those seeking a tougher experience, the Hard and Very Hard modes provide a significant increase in difficulty. However, there are no achievements tied to these harder modes, so it's purely for those who crave a challenge.The map in Banishers is large, requiring a lot of walking, which can become a bit frustrating towards the end. While there is a fast travel system, it only allows you to travel between camps, which can be limiting. Allowing fast travel from any location would have greatly improved the experience. It took me about 25 hours to beat the game, mostly because I kept getting lost, and I probably only did about half of the Hauntings.Choices in the game have a real impact, with options to BLAME, BANISH, or ASCEND. Each choice affects the story and the world, adding replayability and depth. Without delving into spoilers, these choices create a sense of consequence and significance in your actions.The game's RPG elements are solid, featuring skill trees, gear upgrades, and various equipment slots (chest, gun, blade, etc.). Upgrading and swapping out gear changes your appearance, adding a satisfying layer of customization. The game is quite long, especially if you enjoy side quests and exploration. There are plenty of collectibles, cursed chests, and treasure maps to find, and helpful icons on the map show the locations of these items, which is a welcome feature.The combat in Banishers feels reminiscent of God of War, with an average level of complexity and some flashy moves. While this isn't necessarily a bad thing, it doesn't stand out as particularly great either. The combat is serviceable and fits well within the game's structure, providing moments of excitement without overshadowing the narrative.However, one major complaint is the lack of enemy variety. You'll encounter the same few monsters throughout the game, with only a few truly unique and cool-looking ones. This can make combat feel repetitive after a while. There's also a particularly silly-looking boss that seems out of place in the otherwise dark and serious game world.Overall, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a good game if you enjoy heavy story-driven experiences with average combat and impressive graphics. The game could have attracted more attention with a better name and more fitting cover art, as the current presentation doesn't quite capture the game's darker tone. Despite its flaws, Banishers offers a captivating journey through a beautifully haunted world. At 25% off, making it $37.49, it's worth the money for those looking for an engaging, story-rich game.

Do we not see the human of tomorrow when contemplating the cow?" - Vilém Flusser, ~1979.Short version: Playing Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden thankfully only resembles the life of a cow temporarily and is not unsatisfactory most of the time. Is it the next big thing that I must tell everyone about? No, there's too much "rumination", too many limitations, small annoying design quirks, and time-consuming ways to trot from A to B, just to name a few reasons why this game (for me personally) doesn't surpass a ~7.944/10 rating. However, it's better than above average; not brilliant, but often very very good. For now, let's just give a clear recommendation: If you enjoy adventures, mystery elements, predominantly mature storytelling (in a historically reimagined world of the 17th century, dealing with themes of religion, existential homelessness, morality, guilt, atonement, racism, intolerance, violence, witch hunts, etc.), surprising ghost and detective stories where you're guided more through cases without actively having to investigate, and a gameplay loop that falls somewhere between conversations and battles, somewhere between Witcher and God of War, then you can confidently dive in: this is fun, this is worth your time, now off to leisure, off to death.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Vampyr, this review is for you. Slight spoilers I guess.I'm a huge huge fan of vampyr. I would like to try and review this game on its own but it's really hard to do that without comparing it to companies previous game. I think this is a good game if Vampyr did not exist. However it does, so this is really just going to be a comparison review.Combat - a lot of people said Vampyrs combat was clunky, I personally think they just were not very good because I happened to love it. However, if you think Vampyr had clunky combat Wow! Are you in for a treat in this game. The clunkiness of this game would make Vampyr look like a from software game. The camera is way too close, your characters make crazy swing animations, the parry is off, the shooting feels bad and the enemies feel literally the same as each other.Character Upgrades - This game has a skill tree but it feels so bare bones. I never get excited looking at the new things to unlock and also they don't feel very impactful. New skills feel just as clunky as the other skills. I felt the complete opposite in Vampyr, I always was working towards a new skill and the new skills also made combat feel significantly better. There is also something Vampyr had with leveling up, that this game is very much missing. It's crucial to what made Vampyr a phenomenal game. Morality system - In Vampyr you could murder someone and drink their blood. Doing so would give you tons of XP to help you get stronger. However, It would also change the world in the game. All characters in Vampyr felt connected, they felt like real people with personalities. So killing someone would always have a weight to it. Also more importantly, it would change quests, areas you go in, the story ECT. All that and you still had different endings depending on how many people you killed. Now I like to get immersed in my games and a morality/choice system is a good way to do that. I personally would feel bad anytime I would kill someone a vampyr. Honestly besides good or bad endings, It always felt a little selfish because guess what, it is. Now here comes my biggest issue with Banishers. Banishers messes up the best part of vampyr. The morality system. For some lore, banishers are basically Ghostbusters. They go around solving haunts. Then they decide to either banish the ghost, ascend the ghost (to heaven or something) or blame (execute) the person that the ghost is attached to. That sounds really cool on paper and it's why I was very excited for this game. However, it's missing all the pieces that made Vampyr work. You do not get more XP if you kill someone. So already there is a huge gameplay difference. The characters don't feel as connected to the world. I don't really feel any changes when I go around killing people. Maybe the world changes but I have not felt it. Also, My characters don't seem to feel it, maybe they will later but I have a feeling I won't play this game again to find out. All that is much worse in this game but the worst part is the morality feeling of this game. See like I said in Vampyr It feel selfish to kill and wrong because I'm immersed. In this game your wife is dead and the people you blame (execute) can bring her back. Now again on paper that sounds fine. From an immersion perspective it's not great. Unless you're playing solely to get a good ending, there are very few people in the world that would not kill people to bring their spouse back. That's morally wrong but it's also how people are. So I really don't feel the weight of my decision because if I'm immersed in it yeah I'm bringing my wife back duh! Now maybe I could feel bad for blaming / murdering these people if they weren't all terrible. However, a majority of the hauntings end with you finding out that the person being haunted murdered the ghost. So now really the immersive decision is, would I kill a murderer to bring my wife back. Yeah and 90% of the world would probably do the same (not saying it's right, but definitely a easy decision in a game.) Now add the fact that banishers can find all motive, intent, info about the haunting. They are literally givin godly powers and given the power to blame people for their crimes. Really it's not even a moral issue anymore. They 100% are judge, jury, and executioner. They get to find out all facts of the crime that cause the haunt, they find out all intent of the person affected by the haunt and the ghost itself. So there is no need for a trial. So really I think they have the right to be executioner. Just like in today there are many places that have the death penalty. So really blaming someone in banishers feels morally and legally fine. At least in the world that these devs built.World/Adventure- I feel like this review is becoming a roast, so I'll try to keep this section quick. I just don't feel as connected to the world in this game as it did in Vampyr. I already went over how the morality system doesn't feel as impactful. This game is also way more linear. It really feels like a budget PlayStation exclusive. You have the moving of objects to get to higher terrain. You have the moving through tight spaces to get to a new area. It literally has everything that a PlayStation exclusive has now. The areas are much smaller to explore and not very exciting to explore. Vampyr might have been a smaller map but it felt more open. It felt like I could go explore areas and it felt grander. It felt like a soul's type exploration game where as this game feels like a PlayStation exploration game. Not saying it's worse in this game but definitely saying it's not as exciting for me.Story - I think both games are very well written. The only reason I'm even debating on beating this game is because I'm interested to see how the story will end. Now having said that, again I just feel like the characters and NPCs are written better in Vampyr. So it really tied into the morality system. I feel like I was killing real people in the world that the devs created. I don't feel the same in this game. Having said that, I do think the main characters in this game are pretty well written. Length - this game has way too much padding. This game could be like a 13-hour game if there wasn't so much walking around and boring combat in between story sections. I felt like vampyr was perfectly paced. I could spend hours getting to know people in a new area and then go spend some time killing stuff. This game has way more hours walking around and way fewer hours talking to people. I feel like they got their priorities backwards. This game should have been dialogue first and combat second.If you read all this, thanks. I don't think this is a bad game, I think it's really good for the price point. It's sadly just nowhere near Vampyrs level. Also it is way too long. Stop making games with so much padding! Ps. To those saying this is better than Vampyr. I want whatever you are smoking.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8/10Story:Genuinely one of the best narrative experiences I've played so far in 2024. Don't Nod are notorious for making very high quality AA games, and Banishers is definitely a prime example of this. From the beginning of the game I was captivated by the story, ghost hunting side quests/activities, and the general setting/world design of 1695 New England. The voice acting is also especially impressive and passionate, not only between the two main characters, Antea and Red, but also the settlers you talk to within the world. Visuals: Despite being an AA game, the graphics and visuals are extremely cinematic. This is most prevalent in the main story, but even the side cases have some visually stunning moments that had me pleasantly surprised.The various designs of the different gear were also very welcomed. It felt bracing to find a new outfit or sword that had a different look than your current selection, but was just as stunning to look at and came with a new buff.Music/Sound Design:The music in Banishers is stellar. Throughout the main story, the music choice was perfectly emotional and seamless at setting the tone of the scenes. there was never a point that I questioned the music's quality, rather I often found myself admiring the composition of each track, from the combat, all the way to general tracks that play depending on the region you're in. The sound design is no exception either. All of it from the sound of Red running across gravel, to doors creaking when being opened, to the sound of Antea's manifestation explosion all sound perfectly selected. I have no complaints! Gameplay: In my opinion the gameplay, however, is where the game has more noticeable shortcomings. Combat felt stiff for the first few hours of playing as Red. As I unlocked more skills and got more of a feel for the game, the combat smoothed out, but still felt like it was lacking some fluidity. This felt exceptionally true with Antea's combat throughout the entire game. Even as I mastered parrying, dodging, and perfect switches, I still felt like the pacing was off with Antea's combat sometimes. All this to say that by the end of the game, I did however find the combat to be more refined than the combat in Vampyr.The puzzles also felt like more of a hassle than anything. Now, I'm not the biggest fan of puzzles in third person action role-playing games in the first place, but some of the puzzles, like the roots, felt unnecessarily convoluted for where they were located and what specifically they were blocking.World:While I will admit I'm a big fan of the world design, I definitely got tired of running everywhere. If you are someone who likes doing all side activities, getting all the gear, obtaining all collectibles, etc. then be prepared to run. A LOT. You are only able to fast travel from one of the predesignated campfires/safe houses to another, of which there are only 30 throughout the entire game. This led to some moments where the closest fast travel point to a specific side activity objective could be as far as 400m ONE WAY. This specific feature was mildly annoying at best, and immensely draining at worst, during longer gaming sessions when you're just trying to run to an objective that is 350 meters away from your closest safe house, and will potentially have to fight through two different groups of specters standing around in the woods to get there.All in All:Everything considered, I feel that I got my money's worth out of Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden and have to say I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who is into the "God of War (2018)" genre of games, open world RPG's, or is just looking for their next amazing single player experience!

_childDocuments_.review: After spending about 60 hours in this game and finishing the main story I would like to share my thoughts.> Antea (gorgeous and brilliant woman)> Music (atmospheric, but not overwhelming)> Environmental visuals (all locations are precisely detailed, which adds to the immersion)> Story (cohesive and down-to-earth)> Combat system (variety of enemies and their behaviour)> Boss fights (pleasant dynamic)> Voice acting (gave me goosebumps)> Map (not having a mini map on the screen and having to constantly pause and open it)> Sequence of map discovery (even with my full attention I feel like I missed some content because of the misleading order)> Gear system (lack of comparison menu in buying mode)> Attributions system (one turns on another or the opposite; multiple attribution trees)> Occasional ghosts in places with ghost-wardsIn conclusion, this was very nice entertaining experience. _childDocuments_.review: A really REALLY good game, with a few irritating flaws. Overall I really enjoyed this game, but by the end I was glad when I finally finished it. I really enjoyed the story. The voice acting is well done and the protagonists and are quite likable. I actually enjoyed the combat, although sometimes it did get quite repetitive. There's plenty of exploration in the semi-open world and quite a lot of hauntings and side quests to keep you busy as the game moves forward. There is no crafting, but plenty of upgrading to be done for equipment. The game seems to be pretty much bug-free and runs quite well at 4K without DLSS. (Bear in mind I'm running this on a 4090 and 12700K and 32GB DDR5 RAM so take it with a grain of salt).The choices you make do affect the story as it progresses and in-game things can also change (people may or may not talk to you based on choices, merchant prices can become higher, the fates of settlements, etc.). Exploration is pretty straightforward with the compass, map, painted areas to jump/climb/skip.Now for the things I didn't care for:The map in this game is atrocious in my opinion. Not so much how to read it for direction, but for going up and down levels and figuring out where things are. There are arrows that will make where you need to go up and down, but the game fails to tell you a lot of times you'll have to take a long way around first, then drop a rope to open access to the way up/down. Places of interest can also be a pain at times because you can't always figure out what level it's on, even if there's an arrow pointing to go up or down.Fast traveling could be better. Often times you'll have to backtrack quite a bit to get to a campsite. You have to be at a campsite to fast travel. Most times you'll have to scale walls and go through tons and tons of crevices to get back to a campsite, which really slows the game down. While that's not the worst thing in the world, it gets tiresome after awhile. You also cannot skip the resting scene at campsites or the scene where Antea helps Red up. This gets old after watching it so many times. It's a huge time waster.Relatively early on you'll be given the choice to swear one of two oaths. Later on you'll be given a chance to change it if you wish. Regardless of which path you pick, you can deviate if you want. The part I don't like about this is one of the oaths will pigeon hole you into a "darker path" and a certain criteria must be met for it to work, and this can actually add quite a few hours to the game. Other than those few things, I highly enjoyed the game. Bugs were very minimal and nothing game breaking. Definitely worth the full price. I don't think I'll bother playing again to get the other ending since there's no NG+, but I could see people easily playing this at least twice.

_childDocuments_.review: I played it twice, i definitely recommend this game. It has very few flaws, thus my score is 9/10.I played Vampyr before, which this game is kind a spiritual successor, and had mixed feeling about it. Banishers, however, left a very good impression on me. It is a masterpiece.A summary of the game's aspects:Visuals: Realistic, perfect animations.Performance: Reasonable, runs at 1440p max on my rtx 3070 + ryzen 5700xSmoothness: Very smooth, stutter are barely noticiable, very few and far.Narrative: impeccableStory: Good, nothing mind blowing, but very well written and presented.Exploration: you will be wanting to explore every inch of the map.Level design: Large areas very well connected, feels very believable. Secrets hidden everywhere, and sort metroidvania like.World: All main areas are very well crafted, very distinct visually, compelling to explore.Combat: It is ok, after getting all skills it can become more satisfying, overall it gets the job done. Don't come mainly for the combat, it is not the strongest aspect of this game.Side content: Lots of side quests and errands, worth doing.Progression: Well paced, new skill trees open up as you progress, points are hard to earn, some skills are useful others not so much.Customization: There is a lot of gear to play with, but for the most part they are not so impactful, you can get by with starting gear without too much trouble.Upgrades: Yes, you can upgrade weapon and gear, and some material must be earned.Now some nit-pickings:Not being able to open map, select a destination and fast travel is very bad decision, even if you could only travel to fixed places, that would be tremendously helpful. It could also use more bonfires, you will be walking a lot in this game, and sometimes if feels tedious to backtrack.Most conversations can be skipped, but there are some which you cannot and this is annoying when playing for the second time.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game. Great story, some cool new mechanics, etc. But I *despise* games that go out of their way to trap players. Multiple times already I've been progressing along the (pretty narrow) prescribed path on a quest, health potions ("decoctions") have been whittled down by earlier encounters. Now I have no healing, no way to rest and get any until I get through a mandatory fight, and suddenly there are *several* enemies significantly more powerful than any I've encountered before. Death, death, death. I can usually figure out the exact sequence of moves to survive, but if that were the gameplay I wanted I'd play Dark Souls. Or a platformer. I want to *explore* and be able to handle enemies with skill instead of memory. This game ain't that. It's "open" only in a way that doesn't matter. Moving on.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic game by Don't Nod- it's just so good. I played the whole thing and I'm sure I'll play it again in a few years. So much work and love has gone into the character development and the stories exploring human relationships, both romantic and platonic. Great respect is shown for all types of relationships and the characters are fleshed out just the right amount with enough information to understand but not over explain. It also looks beautiful, the characters look so clean and the details are delicate and perfect. They never enter the uncanny valley, which is truly impressive. The combat was difficult at first but once I understood it, it was a lot of fun. Upgrading weapons is in proportion to the play, you're not suddenly winning each encounter but you can see the difference. The only thing that they need to update is the point system, I was fighting with Antea and she would ask if she could join in. Join in? You're doing everything right now haha. And I also wasn't able to finish the haunting case Prudence in all things but that may be because of the decision I made in another haunting case. The game play is a good mix of conversations and combat. You can also skip through the dialog, if you're a quick reader. The side missions left me wanting more, rather than and endless boring list of chores they have punchy, meaty side quests that are possible to finish. I also found the decisions to be enough to satisfy me and I didn't feel that more were required. That being said, I did choose to save Chloe at the end of Life is Strange, so do with that information what you will!100% recommend this game. I paid full price and I don't regret it one bit. If you're a reader and you enjoy novels and complex stories I highly recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story, graphics and voice acting. The narrative is expertly crafted. Sadly the game play just isn't there for me.Combat, while better than Vampyr, falls short of satisfying and uses all too familiar patterns very quickly. Traversal seems hollow as there are no environmental hazards and no risk of falling amidst all the climbing and clinging, so there is no real sense of struggling through the elements. The loot is entirely lack luster and crafting very routine. None of the rewards really made me excited about my build. Rituals could have been more complicated and engaging. The esoteric work of a Banisher could have better been implemented within combat and in exploration. Really all you need is items, and solving cases becomes rote mechanically speaking, which doesn't do the narrative justice.The story and dialog really draw you in. The setting is strong as it maintains a good sense of mystery through the play through. The variety of choices may justify more than one play through as well as the difficulty options, though the combat isn't so much fun you get excited for the concept of challenge runs.I consider worth the price tag, but I can't really recommend it unless you're a big fan of ghost stories, no matter how contrived they seem at times.

_childDocuments_.review: This is 2024's sleeper hit for sure. A lot of high-profile games have come out at this time of year, and it's damn shame this game isn't making the waves it deserves. Even now as I write this, only 2% of players have the ending achievement I have just acquired.A wonderful narrative held together by perhaps one of the most well-made couples I've seen in a game -- and the backdrop of a melancholy world filled with intrigue and misery. And yet, some hope still remains.While not perfect by any means, if you're searching for a story-driven game with acceptable gameplay and Witcher 3 styled side quests, this is a definite buy. Not a single fetch quest in sight, however the map can be a little difficult to traverse when the location isn't spelled out for you. This may lead to some pacing issues in terms of gameplay, but if you want quality story, it's here and in spades.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like pain simulators. And I know one when I see them.While not as hurtful as for example TLOU2, it falls good in line with the Plague Tale games.Storywise, it adresses and handles the themes given within that time period like the assumption of witchcraft, god's fear, political and personal intrigues, the standing of women and people of colour very good.And of course the acceptance of loss."You always think you have more time.And suddenly, you don't".We know from the trailers and promo material that Antea dies.What then happened to me, though I am not shure if only because of this, that her death left me completely cold.Something because of the staging even made me think she brought that upon herself. In her defense, the move she makes more or less also appears in the gameplay. When it comes to the haunting cases, the game gets really dark and depressing. After a couple of main quests, the game "opens up" to choose between the main story and optional haunting cases. This confused me at first because they suddenly just appeared on the map.While not as deep or complex as the main cases, they still tell their stories well.While at first sometimes simpler, most of the cases twist quite a bit, wich often leads to rethinking the already made decisions. Though when ascending ghosts, they often make a 180 turn on their believes due to the case ending in "a good way". This is fine but sometimes feels a bit weird because the turn is so sudden.At one point you have to choose between ascending Anteas ghost in the end or resurrecting her.I chose the former but the game and its stories work with the help of a gameplay feature heavily against it. This is very well executed. Two other problems I have with this game are that when you enter a new area or one of the random fights, it cuts of dialogue, wich is especially painfull when it is character or story related. The other is quite similar, especially in the last third when the tension between the two main characters rise it is sadly broken a couple of times trough random spawning enemies. Not being able to select the dialogue options with the arrow keys also was a bit weired to me.Luckily, exept from that and that I sadly couldn't bring my self to finish the last to optional haunting cases because it was a bit to much for me, this is an absolutely worthy experience. Live to the living, death to the dead!-The owls approve.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm not normally one to leave a review for a game, but I feel a duty, self imposed and maybe unwanted as it may be.Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a solid idea, but, game-play that just had me feeling like it could be better.The story revolves around two Banishers called Antea Duarte and Red mac Raith, through the course of their adventures through New Eden, you will decide the fate of living and dead. Sadly most of these cases where not thought provoking (at least for me) a few did have me go well what is the right thing to do here, but mostly I picked the Ascended option as my first play through was trying to show compassion to both the living and dead, further more it felt like most if not all the npcs where about as deep as a paper plate, the main cast do talk about past, Red mac Raith for example talks about his time in the war and a couple other bits and bobs but it doesn't feel like anything it has any bearing on who he is currently and sadly this is the case for most character you will meet it all means nothing, on another note their are points in the story despite some of them making sense and some not that had me riled up a little bit, the sensible is Antea gets aggressive toward Red at points and while some of it I can shake of as ghosts getting less them selfs as time goes on (the lore reasoning) theirs clearly some distatful politics going on that I'll cover a bit later in this reviewCombat is fine for the most part its simple enough that within 10-20 hours I suspect most people will have mastered the basics, block, parry, light attack, heavy attack, rifle body/weak point (head-shots mostly) shots, banishing and manifestations (essentially magic). That may sound like a lot when I type it out like that but its really not and its fine as I said before. Sadly 60 hours in enemy's for whatever reason start acting strange, you may go to block/parry an attack and either will ignore the attack and not hit you, ignore it and hit you, or change the parry timing and you block or get hit and you will have fought most of the enemy's enough by this point to have an idea of those timings. You will be using both a combination of melee and ranged and depending on your play style (aka if you add Antea to your attacks) you will be using the manifestations you gain through out the story.Build craft is also quite full, theirs a large enough selection of gear that id wager all players will have a load out unique to them, the stat distribution can be a little lacklustre for example I found roughly only 3 pieces of armour with strengths and dexterity on the stat list as I was playing a build where I was up close trying to parry and counter attack as often as possible while using a rifle when and where I needed to. Finally each piece of gear along side their stats has a unique buff for example a sword and torch that when you parry the next light or heavy attack does a bonus 75% damage so late game my heavy attacks after a parry where doing 500-1k dmg roughly depending on the encounter.Collectables and oh boy is their a lot of them are scattered through out the world and while I've been able to collect most of them in this play-through I've reached the point where its hunting for the last few before i go to the final area, while theirs resources out their that mark locations of soul catchers and lore notes for example theirs no official resource that does this, so as much as id like to grab these remaining collectables that i missed its feeling a little disheartening to not see in game map markers to help late game grind like this. Upgrades yes upgrades before all your equipment can be upgrade seven times, yes you will have to hunt down these soul catchers if you want to do that, you will have to repeat nests, elites, scourge and void dungeons to do these soul catchers, you will need to harvest world resources for these repeatable events so don't skimp out on any you see unless you stock up a lot of cash from quests, side quests and treasure hunts, for the shop resources, pray you also have good favour with the vendors also as they will bump up or down their prices by a coin or so.As I said earlier theirs distasteful politics for me it boils down to the men week, woman strong and smart thing that has been going around for awhile now. Theirs some woman that are clearly really confrontational toward men for no seemingly good reason than what i listed above. I want to be clear that while I say all this stuff I support equal rights and while people will enjoy what they enjoy I think unless you execute your ideas in a tasteful way they should be kept out of gaming entirely. I'll say no more as I don't think I'm in a good position to say more beyond that.Extra little notes here that don't fit anywhere else in the review, Antea talks way to much in and out of combat, if its not nagging you to dodge something you can clearly see coming toward you, or telling you to let here have some action, its point out the painfully obvious thing that you know is there and locking you out of using her manifestations for a solid couple seconds. Crashes sooooo many of them never figured out what caused them but i muse have had 20-50+ crashes in my play-through they where less as I progressed but still cropped up occasionally.To wrap it all up it a neat ball, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a Flawed game, that really needs a patch to address the issues it has, for now unless this game goes on a 50%+ sale do not buy it, I sincerely hope the developers are hard at work fixing the issues that are present within the game but I cant in good faith recommend this in its current state.To all those that read through this sorry for the wall of text mega review tried to consolidate it but not great at this but thanks for reading and hopefully helps make an informed decision. Also 2 hours is not enough in my opinion to know if you will like it.

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful story, at least going the "good" path.Writing and acting are top notch and elevate this game above so many others. Gameplay itself is satisfactory. Nothing incredibly complex, but entertaining enough to do stuff and progress while the different stories of New Eden are told. The relationship between the two protagonists is both loving and true. It feels true. It feels like two persons truly talking, with the playful banter and unashamed love gestures and words. The story itself is not too complex, but the relation between the characters is well written. With grace and elegance. You get to know many characters intimately, and you get to care for them. The setting is also an interesting one to explore.Although by the end (39h) I was somewhat rushing to the end of the story, because what remained for me was starting to become a little bit repetitive, I enjoyed the journey greatly and the ending did not disappoint. I don´t care that much about gameplay, so take that into account for my review. In fact, I played it in easy mode. I was here for the story and the game clearly delivered.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like being lost in the woods? This is definitely the game for you. If you love games with well-written stories about human existence, with or without great voice-acting (which this certainly has), you should definitely play this. If you want to experience one of the finest and most realistically portrayed love stories in a video game, I highly recommend this.DON'T NOD consistently push narrative boundaries in games, and I am happy that I supported their amazing efforts by buying and playing this. It took me 3 months to get through it - it isn't short (especially if you want to wring as much story from this experience as you can) - but I was compelled to see it through and get all those story icons off my map. The two main characters and their relationship will last in my memory as it is more intimate than you usually get in a game. The highest praise I can offer is that it was a delight to spend all this time in Red and Antea's company and that's a tribute to the voice actors as well (I experienced the English ones).Graphically it is great. Sound design is fantastic. Voice acting as I said is superlative. Story-telling and writing perhaps good enough to support a TV series, with each episode one of the character sub-stories. The setting was original and intriguing for me; being from the UK, I have little knowledge of stories from the newly-founded puritan colony beyond plays such as The Crucible.A few comments about other aspects of the game. It reminded me of God of War, mechanically. I started the game on normal difficulty, and engaged in the upgrade systems, but as I spent more time failing specific combat encounters and it dawned on me how many of them I would be engaged with, I dropped the difficulty once, and then again later, playing the last third on Easy. Combat just became a road-block to exploration and story-telling. However I applaud the developer for what they achieved with their budget as it has weight and is fluid and feels great. The monster variety just is not there to sustain my 70hr playthrough, and though you get more powers it's still the basic whacking and occasional shooting. There are environmental puzzles, and they are reasonably enjoyable, but variety is limited.Collectables - you will find crafting upgrades everywhere but the economy around them is not really there. I had so much of everything and just sold it for the rare upgrade stuff gated behind combat - that I could do that is nice. They do a decent job of giving you lots of different item types with different trade-offs, but really I don't like trade-offs; I just want items that will make the combat easier. In the end I used the difficulty slider so full thanks to the devs for giving me that, as I just wanted to end each fight ASAP so I could get on.There's no mini-map - and there's no fast-travel except to/from bonfires. Those decisions are no-doubt informed by trying to not have technology that doesn't fit the narrative world of the game, but it just means you spend far too much time flicking to your map (which has dynamic mission markers on it btw, like that's technology from the 17th century). Especially in the first half of the game you will get lost a lot as everywhere looks the same. As for fast-travel, it's there but you can't do it except from certain locations and this is super-annoying when you have to do so much constant back-tracking. Maybe there are times when it could sequence break something, but just stop me doing it for that bit, or give me an upgrade that gives it to me late-game. At that point, when I am trying to clean up the stories before heading to the end-game any kind of friction sucks a bit of the fun out. Also the 2D map doesn't help you find your way to certain spots easily. Antea is already a kind of 'detective vision' so I think a bread-crumb trail ability for her late game, if only to help me get back to a bonfire as quickly as possible so I could then teleport to the next mission marker, would have been very welcome.So some downsides, all of them understandable when you compare budget/team-size to something like God of War, but also highly impressive for what they did achieve on those terms. Strongly recommended though for people with a desire for a well-told interesting story, who can put up with some every-present competently executed combat. Oh and some moments just felt beautiful. I may have shed the odd tear.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is an action-packed narrative adventure set in 1695 New England, where you play as ghost hunters Antea and Red. Developed by Dontnod and published by Focus Entertainment, the game offers a blend of familiar elements from titles like The Witcher 3, God of War, and New World MMO, creating a unique experience within a double-A budget./* Minor Spoiler happening in the Prologue */The story begins with Antea and Red arriving in New Eden to confront a powerful ghost called a Nightmare, leading to . As Red, players must choose between . This choice drives the narrative, exploring themes like religious extremism, mental illness, and morality in a Puritan colony./* Spoiler end */Gameplay revolves around solving haunting cases, making decisions that affect the world and characters. The quest system includes main story missions, haunting cases, and activities, offering replayability and depth. Exploration is encouraged, with hidden treasures, specter nests, and optional activities scattered throughout the semi-open world.Combat, leveling, and gear mechanics allow for strategic gameplay, with Red and Antea's complementary abilities enhancing combat dynamics. The game's graphics, while not flawless, offer immersive landscapes and character designs, supported by subtle sound design and impressive voice acting.Despite minor flaws and limited enemy variety, Banishers offers a compelling experience with over 100 hours of content for completionists. Its strengths lie in its setting, atmosphere, and thought-provoking choices, making it a worthwhile investment for narrative-driven gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're an "only play the main story" player like me, avoid this game.A fantastic 8 hour game stretched threadbare over 20+ hours. The story and combat are fantastic but they're really held back by distracting exploration, horrible loot and time wasting interactions. So many tense moments undercut by the compulsion to pick up garbage, backtracking made eye-rollingly monotonous by slow, interactionless traversal animations and progression hindered by poorly conveyed interactions leaving me feeling like I have to consult a guide. If this had been cut down to get rid of all the crafting and "RPG" equipment progression down to some simple perk systems to tune your playstyle alongside the combat progression and some nice item skins with no impact on gameplay, this'd be an easy recommend. But as it is, exploration feels like a waste of time since all you get is crafting materials and the upgrades are so cookie-cutter by-the-numbers stat buffs I just wish there were flat stat increases alongside my levels. I almost love this game, and I would have if I felt like it respected my time. But so much was wasted doing nothing that the good parts just weren't enough for me to recommend this.SPOILERS AHEAD:So I finished the game and further felt like this game has no respect for the player's time. I finished the game at level 19 so all the enemies at the end were 6 levels higher than me, making me feel like the game was punishing me for not doing enough "optional" content. I Blamed every person along the required path and two to three optional hauntings and was rewarded with the Broken Oath ending. So being loyal to your oath and killing everyone on the main path is not enough. This means not only is optional content not optional, but you also have ZERO indication that this is the case. I like bad endings, but that's not what I got. I got a "go fill the invisible bar more and come back later" notification. A real crown of crap on what was an otherwise awesome story that I felt like I had to drag myself through the ending of due to how much of a slog the open world is, only to have my face spat on for not playing enough.

_childDocuments_.review: 2024 has a great handful of games I look forward to playing, including the remakes of , , , , and so many more. One game that has been on my radar for some time is this one, which I’m thrilled I played.Set in the New World in 1695, an evil curse has swept and engulfed the communities of New Eden and its settlers. Crops and cattle are dying, and specters roam the land. People have left New Eden Town in search of safety. It feels like the end is upon them. That is, until two banishers, Antea Duarte and Ruaidhrigh ‘Red’ mac Raith, receive a letter from their good friend, Charles Davenport, insisting on their assistance in dispelling the curse. The task takes a turn when Antea is killed by the Nightmare plaguing New Eden and turned into a spirit. This leaves Red with a difficult choice: will he let her ascend, staying to his oath as a banisher, or bring her back from the dead? Throughout the game, players will make choices that will affect the outcome. What choice will you make in this action RPG game?After playing , I want to say, first and foremost, that this is a game I don’t think anyone should sleep on. This was such an awesome experience that I thoroughly loved. I was engaged with everything from the story and its settings to its characters. The true heart of this game is its story and main characters, Antea and Red. As I played, I became increasingly attached to them, so much so that there were times when this game made me feel for them. Especially the ending, where I was a sobbing mess. The game features two different endings, and I chose the one where Red gives Antea her Ascent (the best ending, in my opinion). Another thing I loved about this game was the beautiful world rich in lore and the open-world aspect. It made the game a long experience as I wanted to see everything, but it was worth it.The combat can sometimes seem repetitive, and some would say boring, but I really liked it for what it is. You can switch between Antea and Red, each with their own sets of skills and gear. There is an upgrade system for items found along the way and a skills tree system, giving new abilities. In addition, with the game being open-world, there is so much to do and explore, like side quests (haunting cases), locked chests to open, scourges, nests, elites for fighting enemies and farming XP, and so much more. This was such a fantastic and fun game that I can’t forget!

_childDocuments_.review: in a world where micro transactions and poorly made mmos have taken over the gaming world. Banishers is a breath of fresh air, you have the freedom to go where you want, when you want. Get lost in a world that is frightening, entertaining, and funny. The combat is great, feels great. The quests are fun, and make you think at times. The choices you make change the outcome of the world you play in. The only two things I don't quite like are the targeting in combat, and the gps when trying to guide yourself to a quest or something specific. The gps can confuse you at first till you get used to it. Then the quest gps, like when following trails, is very.....annoying. It'll leave you making wrong turns because you can't see this super light green aura in a light green/white background. the combat targeting is just meh, it's not terrible, but it's not great either. I normally just don't target anything. When you do that, you just have to make sure you're facing your enemy. Otherwise you'll be laying down some armageddon on a fly, or some grass. Other than that, the game is great. I really enjoy it and everything that comes with it. I'm not finished with my first playthrough yet. But I already intend on making another run after this. The ways you can play this game and spec out, develop a loadout, even the decisions you make in quests. It makes it so there's not one way of playing the game, and I think that's the best part. 5 outta 5 stars for me. I would recommend it to anyone wanting a break from mmos, or fps.

_childDocuments_.review: I am as torn about this game as I have not been in a long time. I do not want to drag it down, because all together Banishers is a very-very well made game. The story is great, the characters are well written, the world is aesthetic and engaging, the gameplay is enjoyable, I haven't experienced bugs, other than one crash due to Unreal and a boss fight bug that dissapeared after reloading the save. So all together this is a great game. Why am I torn then? Well... How I would summarise, is that at the beginning, when the game presents the first big decision for you and you realize that there are two, very different ways to approach the story which will definitely lead to different endings, I was like "I am 100% replaying this game again"... By the time I got to the half of the game I was absolutely sure I won't be replaying this game again and will be completely satisified with watching the other endings on YouTube. This game is the very definition of overstaying it's welcome. I spent 48 hours in this game, around 15 to 20 of this was pointless walking around on the map for meaningless loot in corners of the map. The game operates with what I call a semi-open world. It is a huuuuuuuuuuuuuuge map, but you can't freely traverse it, as it is more like a convoluted web of paths, rather than true open world, just as it was with Greedfall and Vampyr (although with 0 loading screens which was a bane on Greedfall and at least in Vampyr it was reasonable, because it is all played within London). Here, you have a vast wilderness streched out in front of you, but you need to go through B-C-D-E-F to get from A to G. And most of the time, exploring the map does not pay out and you will get easily overwhelmed by how massive it is, which was unnecessary. Half the size would have been more than enough. On the positive side, the navigation system is top notch. At first I didn't understand why can't you place your own marker on the map, but then I realized, that when you are tracking a highlighted objective or important location, the compass on the top leads you corner to corner, like the magical string in the Minotaurs lair, so getting lost in the game is virtually impossible which gets a big thumbs up from me. The main story is not that long but well written as I said. I felt a connection with the characters, cared about them, was interested to get familiar with the situation. The story beats are well paced, the boss fights are exciting and interesting even if not that challenging. The game tries to have some tiny bits of soulslike elements, but it never turns up the heat enough. I died maybe 5 or 6 time the whole game, maybe it is worth turning up the difficulty, on medium it was nothing for a seasoned gamer like myself. But all and all I was invested into playing the story. Just like with Vampyr your decisions effects the NPCs around you, but here doing questionable stuff is separated from character progression. While in Vampyr if you did not kill anybody the game was unfairly hard and if you did, you were hard locked into a bad ending, here your decisions only effect the ending which is fair and shout out to the devs for doing it this way this time. But then I immediately have to take some of these praises back, because the skill tree is all kinds of stupid and the equipments does not help the case either. There are effects that only an idiot would pick and that makes leveling up straight forward and not fun and rewarding. Why would you pick a skill that raises your damage against full health enemies? They are full health until the first hit is landed so after that the skill is pointless. The same mechanics come up with equipment pieces. I would say the ability points doesn't have any meaning either, you will never equip something for the ability point benefits, you will read the effects it has and be done with it. But that is enough about that...What buffs up the gameplay time is the Haunting Cases (which is good, it is story content which is always welcome). They are fairly interesting, offer enough fun to chase them down and you need them for the main story as well. So all and all, I enjoyed them and was happy when a new one popped up on the map. But then, after every solved Haunting Case, you get a meaningless fetch quest attached to the citizen it came from, which does not add much. It doesn't lead you to new places, it doesn't give you further insight into the lives of these people, they are literally there to generate playtime and give you a reason to dive back into the map maze they created. It would have been nice to highlight the aftercare part of a Banishers job, helping the grieving with their experience and nudging them back towards normalcy. Same goes for treasure maps, cursed chests and such. Meaningless run arounds which murders any joy you felt when dove into the game at first. Hunting for loot, other then the cursed chests and the orange symbols covered chests is pointless. You only get resources that you harvest by walking around anyway and money which is worthless, because 99% of the time you can only buy resources at merchants in which as I said, you already swimming in. They could have left the whole trading mechanics out, nobody would have noticed. Then comes the obvious time wasters, the Endless Nests/Elites/Scourges and Void Gates. The word endless should sound alarm bells. These are made for farming special resources and XP instead of giving it to you in meaningful ways, they throw you into repetitive chore like situations, which they try to spice up with whacky fighting rule modifications, but if you get a bad one, the thing will turn into a nightmare and not the fun kind you would expect in a horroristic setup like that. So, I talked a lot of sh*t of this game, would I recommend it? Yes, I would, but only for the patient ones. Wait for a sale and get it on a discount. You will get content for your money even if maybe not the bestest of the best kind on every level. This game will try your patience and as much as I wanted to see the end of it, I wanted to see it finally end, if you know what I mean. If it would had a smaller map, less pointless walk arounds, less "clear out ivy to reveal a chest with worthless loot", less meaningless fetch quest, less pointless equipment... just all around less, it would have been more. I have to say, the teams working on this already came a long way from Vampyr and the direction is good. Bit more course correction and they will produce legendary games, I know it. This one will be a memorable stepping stone on that path.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Play as a romantic duo in a superb action RPG with quick gameplay, simple mechanics, and an intriguing story that unfolds mysterious hauntings in late 1600s North America.Play as a wizen ghost hunter and a war-veteran appreciate traipse across the America east coast in 1695 to banish a nightmare. The pair is easily recognized as a romantic couple with jests and secrets. The voice acting from the entire cast is great, and the dialogue is extremely well-written. The banter between the duo fills the expansive wilderness as the story slowly unfolds. The story is more expansive with plenty of sorrowful sidequests that build towards the ending.Banishers sets up a cold, eerie atmosphere with instrumentals and the theme of a cursed land. The character models are great, each unique. The world is a maze between each settlement and offers much exploration. How the world connects and unlocks quick routes is fantastic. Some environments are too dark; an option to raise the offhand weapon as a torch would have helped. Visual effects like water, rain, fire, and smoke were done very well. Backtrack will be required to collect and see everything. However, you can fast travel, and the compass and map make navigation easy.Combat is simple and quick, with a few tricks thrown in, and smooth animations as you swap between the banishers, although there are only a handful of enemies. At camp, you can enhance gear and rest to restore potions and respawn enemies. Levels and sidequests can provide points to buy perks that can be redistributed freely anytime to fit the play style. A few callouts. The stills between load screens are gorgeous, the evolving story after decisions are made, and tons of collectibles, notes, and letters that expand the world. The investigation is more story-driven; turning objects to discover clues or an examination would have made it feel more like a hunt instead of along for a ride. Once you complete a void, it should be a one-way teleport. A solid price point for a game with a ton of value. DON’T NOD has created something special, and I would gladly return to this universe. Cheers to the team!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 6/10 for me, will probably not immediately buy next installments from this publisher:My pro's: - Combat, even though repetetive, is rather fun because of the decent skill trees and options.- Gear looks nice and does provide usefull bonusses/ interesting combinations.- Decent lore and concepts.My cons:- Traversal options such as climbing, lifts etc take excruciatingly long and this got more and more annoying over time. - Side-quests give little to no reward especially considering the time and travelling they require.- Sad to say, but had some annoyingly 'modern audience'-oriented writing which also hurt the story.Overall I should start by saying that at 4 hours in I regretted no longer being able to refund the game. After this time it became clear that the game was going to consistently push a narrative which I personally find extremely off-putting and especially unfitting for a game that requires you to make so many 'hard' choices. In my opinion the game started showing a horribly predictable pattern in which male characters are usually oppressive, plain dumb, annoyingly dependant/incompetent or at the very best misguided, females on the other hand are clearly justifieable in their behavior or are clearly/objectively the victim in most situations. While being rather condencending to male players (I feel so good about spending money on this game now...), you also have to know that this game is all about the moral dillemma's! Who do you save, who do you damn and who might you even sacrifice? This could be the essence of a truly compelling story, making the player hesitate between different and understandable options, instead we get mostly dumbed down options such as 'hmmmm, should I banish this clearly one-dimensional oppressive white guy or side with the woman who got tormented by him'... The tediousness of travelling combined with the uninteresting side-quests with flat and horribly predictable characters made me rush towards the ending after completing the 3 pillars questlines. I'd seen enough of the game, no longer cared about any side-quests or the fact that I didn't get all the gear or skills, which is rare for me. I simply felt like a bought the game, wasn't quite getting my moneys worth because of the poor writing and just wanted to finish it. Worst of all, I found the game got heavier and heavier on it's agenda the closer to the end, making me barely care by the time I reached the ending cutscene. I went from liking Antea to finding her rather arrogant and condenscending. I did like Red's character design and overall Irish theme, but he got very little backstory and was, aside from his design, an overall flat character. Gameplay was nice, concept was good, writing was bad, choices felt too guided. I will check reviews before buying new games from this publisher because I'm getting kinda sick of buying goods that push certain agenda's. I want to buy games for my enjoyment lol.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: good creative work, repetitive and uninteresting combat mechanics that don't let you really enjoy the one great combat feature they put in.Interesting and enjoyable story. Early on you have to make a difficult decision without knowing the full ramifications of it, and the consequences haunt you throughout the gameplay as they should, without either punishing you too much for it or making it inconsequential. The villains you deal with feel like real people, rather than caricatures of evil. They've had hard lives, they're hurt and broken, and while they hurt other people, it's generally out of fear and ignorance and all of the other motivations that have always driven people to depraved and vile behavior. The way you go about investigating the source of hauntings doesn't break any new ground, but it makes the cases interesting and it's satisfying to complete a case.The voice acting is good. The English version has enough awkward phrasing and grammatical errors that I assume it was written in some other language and translated by a non-native speaker, but it's not too distracting. It's mostly written in modern English, but they occasionally throw in some more archaic speech and that feels very awkward, especially when they misuse it. Writers: pick a linguistic setting and stick with it; it doesn't have to fit the story setting, but be consistent.There's a large world, but it's not open; you're limited to a few paths through the world and your character can't even jump. The map design is a little frustrating at times, with limitations like branches lying on the ground that you have to walk 10 feet to get around because your character can't step over anything larger than a pebble. That's annoying when you're walking around, but it's infuriating when it gets you killed in combat. The environment looks good and is enjoyable to explore, other than the frustrations about having to walk a mile to get to a location twenty feet away even though there's an obviously climbable direct path between them.Unfortunately, all of the good is wrapped up in a package with typical console action combat mechanics. You essentially need to figure out and then memorize the attacks and required dodges to defeat various enemies. The game does a fairly lousy job helping you figure it out. There's not enough variety in the enemies you fight. You can't control the direction your character attacks; you always attack camera-forward, and the camera rotates way too slowly for combat. If you dodge past someone attacking you, you can't turn around to attack them before they've recovered and hit you. The solution they provide for this is to lock your attacks to a single enemy, which makes the camera track them as you dodge. This helps a lot, but the locking system is finicky and some enemy types constantly break lock by warping to other locations.At times you'll get mobbed by a half dozen different enemies at once, and (particularly in the void) when long, unblockable attack sequences overlap sometimes you have to do nothing but dodge for a minute or more until there's some sort of opening to attack. The game allows you to turn the difficulty of the game down to the point that it's not a challenge, but then you have to spend a lot of time in very boring combat. Either way, it's tedious, incredibly repetitive, and--at least for me--more of a job than a game.That's a shame, because the one great aspect of the combat system--rapid switching and cooperative fighting between your living and ghost characters--would really shine if you could use it more creatively. You can respec your skills at any time, allowing you to experment with a variety of ways the two charcters can work together. There are automatic two-character combos, manually triggered two-character combos, abilities that allow one character to charge up the attacks of the other for later use, etc. Many of the skills improve one aspect of your combat abilities while worsening another. I really like how parts of this were designed.With all of those options, it should be a lot of fun, but unfortunately 95% of what you end up doing is just dodge, dodge, fast attack, dodge, dodge, dodge, slow attack, repeat... over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over again. Adding a "switch character" here in there in the repeated action sequence isn't enough to make that kind of combat fun. Now and then you have to fight bosses, which work exactly the same except that you have to endure a good 5-10 minutes of it without making more than a few mistakes. Those mistakes are easy, because some actions--particularly healing, dodging, and switching characters--can be difficult to trigger at the right time without either having them ignored or interrupted or interrupting other combat actions, making the combat feel a little clunky.That said, I know that this sort of combat system is incredibly popular with other gamers. You know whether or not you like it. I was intrigued enough by the story to give it a shot, and I'm slogging through the combat to get to the parts I like, although I've quit to go play something else quite a few times because I don't want to face the same boring fight yet again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a recognition that is much more MASSIVE than what it currently has. I went into this filled with scepticism, and I was pleasantly surprised FAR beyond expectations. This game is a masterpiece - the main heroes Red and Antea are extremely charming and lovable and their dynamic is more unique than what I have ever seen in video games. Truly, the personalities of the main protagonists, as well as most NPCs and even antagonists, are Baldur's Gate 3 level. I loved the story from the very start to the bittersweet end. This is the only game that has ever made me shed a tear at the end. Like I literally cried. Additionally, if you loved Vampyr (which I did very much), you will not be disappointed. This game is similar in terms of mechanics, and so much better! It is also PACKED with occult and mysterious, so if you are into that kind of stuff, expect a delightful experience. Now some specifics (positives first):COMBAT - addictive and highly satisfying, tries to mimic God of War with the addition of its many own unique elements and I think it does it with great success. I played on the highest difficulty setting and it felt rewarding and bosses pleasantly challenging. The combination of different perks and equipment allows making builds that are actually very different from each other and everyone will find their own style - including the variety of melee and ranged builds for both Red and Antea, with focus on both or either.GAMEPLAY - the combination of alternating story telling, combat, and deep world exploration creates a highly satisfying gameplay loop. This is not an open world game, but it almost feels like one at times, with a rather huge world with areas that are nicely interconnected, much like what we know and love from Souls games. The side quests (haunting cases and optional activities here) are interesting and everything clicks together so beautifully it feels like the producers prepared a highly complex and beautiful puzzle to assemble. Add a plethora of underground and otherworldly locations and you have a massive world that will take many hours to explore fully. I also found collecting materials and upgrading equipment very enjoyable.GRAPHICS - beautiful, the sceneries and views are gorgeous with the variety of different biomes like forests, swamps and fields.There are some negatives, but compared to everything else this game has to offer, they feel completely negligible:The enemy variety kicks off OK from the start until around halfway through the game, but after that it gets repetitive. There is fast travel in this game, but often you still have to walk around a lot (often through the same locations) and enemies will ambush you A LOT, and you MUST fight them given that individual world areas are separated by geographical obstacles that can be traversed only outside of combat. In other words, there is no fleeing from combat here and this can become annoying for some people.There was only a couple of very minor bugs I experienced, nothing major that would take away from fun experience.Also, this game TOTALLY needs a New Game +, which it unfortunately does not have as of the time of this review.Overall, this is an amazing game with beautiful story, satisfying combat, and stunning world to explore that is full of life (and also death). I give it 9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers : Ghosts of New Eden is a 3rd person Action RPG set in New Eden (New England) in 1695. You play as two Banishers, Red & Antea (some ghosts linger and haunt people, banishers get rid of them). You are invited by your mentor Charles Davenport to New Eden to help lift a curse. Prologue : Upon arrival you walk around and talk to people and find out about the curse and more importantly find out that Charles Davenport is dead. New Eden is haunted by a Nightmare (a very powerful Ghost basically). Antea gets killed in the prologue and Red is dropped from a cliff by the Nightmare and he is rescued and survives. Antea's ghost is soon united with Red and they both go around trying to learn more about the curse of New Eden and slowly solving the cases of haunting and learning more about the settlers and why this place is haunted by such a powerful Nightmare. Gameplay is combat with melee & ranged weapons  (Red) and melee & supernatural weapons (Antea). You also have a lot of "haunting cases" (main & side quests) which are basically detective style cases where someone is haunted by a ghost and you have to figure out why and then confront and deal with the ghost. Game is not open world but has several areas with paths you can take with a lot of side stuff and fast travel points.You can upgrade skills and weapons/armors for both charcters. You play as both Red & Antea. In combat you simply switch between them with a button and skills are complimentary as well. Such as getting gun reloading automatically for Red when Antea does some damage for example.Pros+ Great voice acting and graphics.+ Performance is great (no stutters, crashes even in the pre-release build)+ Quest design is excellent especially with the Haunting Cases and the number of ways it can be solved.+ Game difficulty is very flexible with 5 Difficulty settings ranging from Story which is for those you want to just enjoy the story to Very Hard for those who want challenging combat.+ Great Protagonists (Always fun to hear the Scottish accent).+ Relationship of the two protagonists was also done well. Very subtle, like an older couple who know each other well.Cons- No minimap.- While fast travel is available, it can only be done from camps. You can also only upgrade weapons and stats from camp as well.- Certain areas can be blocked off if you go exploring too early. Not a big deal but I went exploring a certain windmill and no matter what I did couldn't get in to the top floor only for the door to magically be open after I had reached a point later in the story. Again not a big issue but at the time the game suggested that it could have been opened when it couldn't have been.- Limited number of saves. This was a bit strange as this is a bigger game. I rarely come across a game with a limit on number of saves.Overall I really enjoyed the game. Spent 30 hours to finish the main campaign and still nowhere near to completing everything. Lot of side cases and activities left.If you are looking for a decent well made AA quality game this might be one of the best I have come across. Little to no jank, great voice acting, interesting combat and best of all the "haunting cases" which are a sort of detective style missions and reminded me a little of Witcher 3 as they have multiple choices and outcomes and some don't even finish when you solve the case as the outcome affects things in the area.Priced reasonably as well and I did not have a single issue performance wise or any crashes in well over 20 hours of playing (for a pre-release build, Day 1 patch is coming to iron out any minor problems).I have made a detailed Spoiler-free Review and also done a sample 'Haunting Case' from the beginning of the game to give you a taste of the game (pun intended, you will get it after you watch the video :)Thanks and have a nice day.Review : Sample Gameplay (A Haunting Case) :

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a recommend from me if you like narrative focused single player games.THAT SAID, this recommend comes with a pretty big caveat: DO NOT try to 100% this game. This is Don't Nod's first attempt at a big open world and the rookie mistakes are fairly glaring. There is so much padding you will burn out long before you get close to finishing which kind of ruins the experience. A lot of the rewards are useless, as I think I ended up with my preferred loadout about 30 hours in and every bit of equipment I unlocked after that was worse than what I had. Grinding for upgrade materials is beyond tedious and with all the backtracking you'll do once you unlock new abilities the combat really begins to drag.The combat *is* decent, and reminds me of the newer God of War games a lot. The problem is that there isn't a whole lot of enemy variety and they mostly ambush from nowhere, making me feel like I was playing a late '90's JRPG with random battles and dreading entering a new area when I just wanted to advance the story. Also, I would STRONGLY recommend playing this on Normal difficulty. I played about 75% of the game on Hard, and while it wasn't overly challenging, the enemies are such massive hit sponges every encounter takes far too long. I dropped it down to Normal and this mostly fixed that issue.I realise all of this must make it sound like I hated it but I absolutely didn't. The writing and characters were fantastic and I loved every part of the story and side quests. I just wish the world had have been cut down to half the size and 2/3 of the open world bloat had have been cut out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a terrible shame that something with such good bones ended up so ugly.There was a great game here, somewhere, in the idea. However, the execution of the idea left a lot to be desire.Things I like: The story. The voice acting and overall sound design. Exploration. The premise behind the combat system (not the execution).Things I don't like: Being told the main protagonists are "in love", a notion which drives the narrative, but there is no history and Antea just nags the s*** out of you constantly during gameplay. The game outside of the story. There is a lot of running around and retreading old ground. The map traversal system is... just. not. good. Fast travel to a spot, run to another spot, killing the same enemies over and over, find a clue, run back to the fast travel spot, travel to a new location, fight the same enemies over and over, find a clue, travel back to the original fast travel spot. Progressions: Gear/Talents. It seems the devs just didn't have any ideas here how to balance the game and give you a sense of progression. Every piece of gear or talent after the first few hours has both a positive and negative stat. I.E You can do extra damage with a specific ability, but every time you use it someone comes to your home and kicks you in the balls. Combat: Repetitious. Enemies don't change over time, they just absorb more damage... alot more. Parry system (which quite a few talents support) is non-existent. It seems that combat is designed to be played with the idea that you will be constantly switching between characters, but the timing of the attacks are janky, they should be an afterthought, but you feel surprised when they work as intended. Finally; the game it about some pretty terrifying ideas, possession, hauntings, scourges, and an entire colony besieged by malignant supernatural entities, yet there is not ONE SINGLE scary moment. The game is not spooky, scary or even mildly upsetting.  This game could've been so much more, and maybe the sequel will be... I hope so.

The combat so far is simple and nothing complex. There isn't much of a wow factor with the combat, but I think the focus here is the story, setting, and tone. For a AA game, solid. Very good start. I may update this after more hours of play, by the first impression is good enough to justify grabbing this while on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this may be the first game I've ever written a review for. Solid 9/10 for me. Game was really pretty. Music was good. Character animations weren't groundbreaking in a new standard, but the characters look real damn good. For an RPG, it was really solid. It had solid dialogue choices and a different insight to a potential look at puritan New England. The combat was really solid. It wasn't a very difficult combat at it's base (there is a modifier option to certain encounters that can really adjust how you tackle it, which was refreshing) but the play style of combat was fun. The switch between characters felt really natural, and added a deeper step to the combat to really make it feel different. You could tackle different fights with different tactics. There's a solid talent system which can be adjusted on the fly, unless you're in combat, so it really allowed you to modify based on gear acquired. My only complaint about the game, is rather small, and that's the modifier system on certain encounters. As an example. Let's say when doing this combat, you get told that your light attack (LA) damage is increased. I would normally think that LAs would do an extra....10-15% damage and everything else would be where it is. But what they adjust is LAs do an extra 100% damage and everything else does 90% less damage. This isn't game breaking, and the talent system really allows you to make adjustments before hand if you pay attention. But it was an oddity to feel like you'd make a small adjustment where you have to use very specific attacks/chains to do the proper damage. I would love if those modifier systems could make it to bosses later on, it would add more flair to the game.Finally, to really laud the strength of the game is it's paranormal investigation system. It felt closer to the Batman Arkham games with the crime scene investigations, just you didn't have the ability to rewind/fastforward time for the game. But, as the player, you really got a solid choice on how you wanted to adjust, and there were multiple side missions that had "extra" information that would give you insight if you read, but weren't actually tied with the mission as required. I loved this ♥♥♥♥. There were multiple times where I'd guess the case ending about half way through, and felt rewarded by the game for finding the trails they left. And then the other half I'd make a guess and be off (in a good way) with how the case ending, finding a last piece of information just at the bottom of the 9th and it adjusted the entirety of how I viewed it.I *really* hope Don't Nod makes another one. It's such a great game that I had to write something, so others would see this and give it a shot. I've played a handful of games in 2024, some big, some small. This was one of my top 3's of this year. As a player, I really felt like I was making choices that matter and really enjoyed the ride.Give it a shot!
