_childDocuments_.review: First of all, here’s a link to a video with my early impressions about Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden:Being a DON’T NOD game, we can expect to find superb writing, engaging stories, emotional moments and difficult choices.After Antea’s death, right at the beginning of the game, you will have to decide if you will honor your oath to the living, protecting them from the dead, or if you will sacrifice them to save your departed partner.We can alternate between the two player characters at the touch of a key, easily choosing the one that is best suited for each occasion.While exploring, you will meet characters that are haunted by ghosts. Through detective work, you will solve these hauntings, finding the reasons why those ghosts are haunting the living. When solved, you will have to decide the fate of the living and of the ghosts. Making these choices won’t be easy, because generally there’s a lot of moral ambiguity involved, no one is completely innocent. This is a very compelling part of the game, one that keeps you invested in every decision you make, knowing that there are always repercussions.Generally speaking, combat feels good. Attacks feel like they have weight and are impactful. You can block/parry attacks and you can dodge and roll out of harm’s way. Normally, in other games, when you do these actions, you consume some kind of resource like stamina or endurance. Banishers doesn’t have a system like that implemented, which means you can perform dodge and rolls whenever you want. I think that this makes combat too easy.You can customize both characters attack skills. Each ability as a skill tree, where you can unlock skills using skill points that you receive when you level up. This way, you can select skills that best fit your playing style, adding a level of strategy to the gameplay. Another way you can customize your characters is by unlocking new gear and upgrading it.Another thing I like a lot about the game is its character design. The characters are very well modelled and have unique facial features. The animations are well done and voice acting is very good.The game does have some technical problems. I experienced several game freezes and crashes. I found out that the problem was caused by DLSS, Nvidia’s AI frame generation technology. After disabling it, I never experienced those problems again.

_childDocuments_.review: All men bad.Women suffer, men make suffer.Synopsis of the whole game main plot, 80% of sidequests, and, I guess, some kind of misguided viewpoint the developers wanted to shove down our throats.This game had a solid potential to be 8/10, but instead it should be banished.Gameplay-wise mechanics are quite interesting when you get to the full arsenal of banishers. Combat can be repetitive, but if you experiment with builds, you will sometimes feel rewarded. There are some usual open world loot scavenging and challenges. Nothing really groundbreaking, but It's ok.Leveling up is somewhat fun, but disappointing at the same time. There are builds, yes, but it's all completely pointless due to enemy scaling. Felt like wasted potential.A lot of pointless wondering (due to how lazily some sidequests are organized) with enemies respawning and no way to escape combat - this is the biggest drawback in terms of gameplay.But all-in-all, gameplay-wise it's good. I suppose you could say it's 7/10.But then there is plot and all sidequest content. And this is where the game could have been great, but alas!The protagonists are pleasant, their love is palpable, and the potential the game presented for exploring human drama and making difficult choices via sidequests felt really inspired!And that is where the developers, for some unexplainable reason, decided to mix it all with stinking ♥♥♥♥ in such proportions I had never experienced before. At first all seems fine. There are some obvious nods to modern woke culture, but they are nicely balanced (for example Antea is great and complex character, and sister-leaders of the first major location are themselves nuanced, conflicted and interesting). Strong, capable, independent and smart female leaders start to feel a bit tired lately, but I'll take it, no problem. The stench of the real problem manifests as early as the end of the first major locations (if you go through all the haunting quests you will feel it). And the problem feels like someone's gender hate. Oh, boy, the men are disgusting in this game (except for the gay men - they are the only one decent enough; and except for the Red, but I guess this is mainly due to the fact that he has the stongest, capabelest and smartest black woman to guide him).Evil, weasel, scheming, corrupted or weak, in 4/5 sidequests men are either at fault or really unpleasant.Husbands, fathers and brothers - all these roles are gruesomely failed by men in this game.Time and time again characters will remind you that this or that gal is better at her business than any man. Times and times again characters will discover, that this or that gal would be fine if not for those damned men. Even marriage was ♥♥♥♥ on: all straight marriages in this game are a disaster, and even Antea and Red discuss how they are not married cause it's ♥♥♥♥.At first this slightly annoys, than takes you out of the stories, then really frustrates. After 10th or so haunting you more or less know how it will end in 4/5 times (gay couple are exception, but of course!).And this, ladies and gentlemen, I find unacceptable. Rebalancing gender roles is one thing, but hating is too much. Pushing radical political agenda through a screen is a new low for AA gaming. Damn you, Don't Nod, for bringing this ♥♥♥♥ into gaming.This game could have been: 8/10It plays like: 6-7/10For bringing politics into gaming it's -10

Dialogs are slow and long from the get go, when you're most likely  to want to actually play rather than listen passively to long conversations, and the loot is not very exciting and contains a lot of info dumps.Combat wise : the game is too punishing early on, which feels unfair. You don't have much to fight with, are always outnumbered by ennemies whose patterns are barely recognizable and often hidden by the body and movements of your own character, making it even harder to try and use the pary/counter system. Once your three potions are consumed, because fires and few and far betweens, you can get stuck very fast in areas with multiple combats and not enough health to hope for a win.Overall, after a few hours, I'm interested to see where the game goes story-wise, but the combat and the exploration are already frustrating and I'm not certain I'll keep engaging itht them. Oh but since you get locked in combat without the ability to run away from minor fights, I guess I won't have much of a choice...I want to point out that the souls-like infection of the gaming industry is getting on my nerves. update : this game is decidedly too chatty. I've only done a few haunting cases yet, but these stories are gripping, and at the end of each haunting case you have to bring closure, you have to make a decision how to end it. Dontnod is good at writing stories and it shows in these cases.Don't go in looking for a souls-clone, the combat isn't the hook of this game. It's the atmosphere, haunting cases and the relationship between Red and Antea. After the game opened up a little I feel I can recommend this game for people who like these types of games with interesting stories and quality writing.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, Banishers is like The Witcher meets Horizon meets A Plague Tale meets Shadow Of The Tomb Raider. And while it does not go as far as outshining any of these masterpieces, it manages to build the identity of its own and deliver about 80 hours of mostly excellent gameplay if you go the completionist route.Great combat is among the definite highlights of the game. Heavily centered around constant switching of the characters, it's fast, enjoyable and at some points delivers almost physical feeling. And then there's enough different gear and skills to experiment with various types of builds for different playstyles. One cool feature is that many encounters (especially elites & scourges) have modifiers for some types of damage, forcing the player to go for a different approach each time. Limited number of enemy types is a bit of a downside. While dispatching them is truly fun, at some point you realize that you're dealing with the same ghosts & skeletons over and over, again and again.The dark world of Banishers looks stunning and feels hauntingly atmospheric. Exploring every nook and cranny is a rewarding experience. There are lots of different activities and - for the most part - they are enjoyable (though I wish there were a few less ivy puzzles). The game does not feel like truly open-world, but this is somewhat compensated by lots of vertical exploration on a rather compact maps.  The plot is not very complex, but unveiling it is truly engaging thanks to many lesser details and twists. The main protagonists and pretty-much all NPCs are well-written and this makes solving the haunting cases (Banishers' name for a side-quests) worth the extra 15 hours of time. There are a few side-stories that I found disappointing, but that might be a matter of personal perception.Last but not least, I did not notice any quality issues (we're 9 months into release now). The game ran smooth on 4070 with highest graphics settings and I only experienced a single random crashing during my 70+ hours.As a final verdict, Banishers is a decent action/rpg that deserves way more attention than it's been getting so far. In my book, this is a very real candidate for a GOTY shortlist in 2024. Fingers crossed for a DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Spooky and fun, great theme, great stories. It's disappointing not to be able to finish this game due to lack of accessibility options that should be standard. Motion sickness is not new, and the solutions are pretty well known these days, so I don't really appreciate paying for a game I can't play because these options were left out.If you are prone to motion sickness, I recommend against buying this game. Otherwise, play away, it's well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird. It's really weird. I can't say I recommend the game, but I can't say that I don't recommend it either. Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden feels pretty shallow in most of the components. Tech part:Visuals and graphics looks OK, but generic; I didn't experience any major problems with framerate and stutters, but some framedrops occure from time to time; facial animation is not really impressive and up-to-date but I can't say it's really that bad - it doesn't ruin the game, it's just OK. The combat mechanics are pretty dull and also generic - light attack, charge heavy, dodge, block, rinse&repeat. The combat isn't like "snappy", there is no weight in your hits, you can't really feel the hits that you land on the enemies or hits they land on you. Animations here are also pretty generic, and, one major flaw - the developer didn't add a button to WALK for keyboard users. It exists in the engine, and you can active it. probably, with Y/Z buttons, but you can't remap it. Maybe they added this already, but at the moment I played the game it wasn't there, and it ruined my immersion and experience a lot, because there is no style in running like an ape. Story part:One part that ruined my experience the most was the certain part of the story. It really decided the refund. The game starts really grim and intriguing, until we discover who our enemy really is. The detective part is great, it's interesting, it's fun, even in the prologue, but it's impressive how easy ONE dumb plot move destroyes it all. You really feel like a MASTER of your job, almost like witcher, investigating the curse, but ...SPOILERS AHEAD (It's prologue of the game, and you know it from trailers, but, just in case).the way two main characters, MASTER-BANISHERS, completely ignore their experience and knowledge about tricky nature of ghosts when working with Nightmare (who is known to be very dangerous = requires extra caution) and just go full-suicide into it's lair - it's lame way to start the game. I don't even want to continue after that. It's lazy, lame and full of cliche. It' dirty, you can't do us that way - they are professionals, and the plot builds up around it, and when things like THAT happen, personally I can't believe in their whole story after those lame tricks. Maybe it gets better, and I am sure it does, but I got my punch I don't want to go on from this point.DON'TNOD do some really interersting stuff with the story, but the gameplay is always lacking. A good example - Vampyr was horrible on the gameplay and tech sides, but very interesting as a concept and idea, and pretty decent in terms of story. Maybe this game is the same, but I don't want to check it out. I've fallen for it once with Vampyr, but this time I am aware of how this developer works, and suffering through the gameplay-loop this game provides for some chunks of story and dialog is not my cup.My verdict: It would be a great game to buy on sale, a great game for those value the story over everything, not so good for just a casual player.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinkin about getting this, I think you'd prefer play Beyond: two souls.. the story is better, the game play is a little basic but it's also far more innovative playing as the ghost in that game then this one. In this game the ghost is just a toggle for powers youve seen like a magic shield, if you're in ghost form, your normal guy doesn't take damage.. in the ghost form you can see hidden items.. in the ghost form you can unlock pathways forward.. one is a giant leap mechanic to cross large gaps or get up high cliffs but it's only available on the specific spot you're meant to do it from.. one allows you to explode things which block your path.. There isn't really any morality to this, you make a choice at the start to either ascend\banish every ghost or to "blame" which just means kill every person possible.. Ascending and banishing hasn't been properly explained to me so far, i think even the main characters don't really know what the difference is other then the ghosts reaction to it, they just have theories but it's pretty clear that ascending is always the right option unless you just want to punish a ghost you see as bad.There are no grey choices here unless you chose to blame everyone at the start, this is a selfish route that allows you to resurrect your ghost character.. but you won't have much issue choosing blame, in my opinion, since you know that's the only way to get the right ending, it will tell you that as you're choosing at the start and remind you every time you make a choice, you must blame everyone possible to do this. It might have been a harder choice if it wasn't telling you it has to be every single one.. and you were left trying to balance it out so that you try to get the correct number of souls needed to resurrect.. while not knowing if the next person you could 'blame' was going to be a worse person or not, so you have to really think about if that person is worth blaming and has faults they should die for or is he worth sparing an hoping someone worse comes along.. and if you let the wrong person go, maybe you would have to sacrifice someone far nicer to make up for it later.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game!!Edit: Having spent three hours playing the game, I believe I can provide a more detailed review.Firstly, the game runs exceptionally well and is highly efficient. There's no stuttering, and the shader compilation is swiftly completed upon initial start-up. The game performs admirably overall. Moreover, it already supports DLSS, FSR, and even DLSS3 with Framegeneration.I'm playing the game on my system with 4K DLAA, and the graphics are impressive. My 4080 Super easily delivers more than 60 fps, which is where I've capped the frame rate.Currently, there's no option to remove the film grain and chromatic aberration. Although these effects don't bother me as much in this game as they do in others, I would still prefer an option in the settings to disable these two effects.In terms of visuals, the game didn't impress me in the first hour. You start in the dark at night, and I initially found it underwhelming, even questioning if it was an UE4 game. However, as you play longer and venture into brighter areas, the game's visuals improve significantly. The VFX is also nicely done.Overall, I would rate the visuals a 7/10. The game could certainly benefit from some Lumen and Nanite. I was disappointed that these features weren't included in the game, and I hope they will be added later with a patch.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers is a game that you can tell doesn't quite have the budget of modern heavy hitters, but what it absolutely does not lack is heart. The story is great, the Hauntings are largely well fleshed out moral dilemmas that examine life in the time of the puritans, the world is just expansive enough and lovely to go through outside of the occasional muddy texture and sometimes a bit too extensive walking to get back to an npc or town. _childDocuments_.review: With a ghostly undercurrent, moral conundrums, and an endearing story, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is definitely worth possessing. _childDocuments_.review: Look, i wont sit here and knock a AA company for this kind of game but i will be critical. The story, characters, voice acting, visuals and choice's are very well immersive. The game reaches to test your humanity. Each character is very well done and with great effort all around making this immersive choice impacting game feel more consequential than most I have played in the past resulting in different outcomes when it comes to the ending of the game.That being said. Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden, is very lacking when it comes to what matters most in a video game and that is of course the game-play. Constantly running back and forth for 'hidden or rare items' was quite tedious and unrewarding, most items are basically materials you find around the world or from fighting world enemies, most rare weapons are basically skin copies of the starter weapon but with different stats. I used the starting sword for most of the game-play and upgraded it which makes it relatively as strong as the rest.Combat in lack of a better term is, unappealing, inconsistent and flat out just not very fun. Switching between Antea and Red for combo execution did not feel proper. Antea consistently telling you how to fight or to switch over in every battle up until the end of each fight gets annoying after awhile. It feels slow and delayed due to the fact the game leaves you with wanting to throw combos together bwteen the two of them and adjust to enemies more fluently with aggression. The best example I can give for this feeling of game-play is 'God of War'. It almost seemed like they were going for a 'God of War' type combat but didn't execute it properly. All in all i would give this game a solid 6/10 as the story is very well executed and managed. Choices are hard to make and the outcomes to each investigation leave you intrigued. Is it worth the full price? No. Wait for it to go on sale, it most definitely will. Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this 10 hours in. While I really enjoy the game and think that it has a great story so far, I have one pretty significant gripe with the map design. In several places you can get yourself trapped in front of a boss with no heals remaining and no way to return to a campfire to rest.  There are only two ways to resolve this: One is to roll back to a previous save from before you entered the area, but that only works if you basically fill your save slots with separate saves to make sure you have one from far back enough. The only other way is to lower the difficulty far enough that you can get through the fight without dying, which completely takes away from the overall soulslike experience of learning to win against difficult bosses.There should *never* be a boss fight that you can't rest before, even if it means you have to back track a bunch.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending considerable time immersed in "Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden," I've found it to be an exemplary piece of interactive storytelling. The narrative is exceptional and is both engaging and profound. The attention to world-building is remarkable, providing a depth that captivates from the onset.My primary critique centers around the game's combat mechanics, which feel somewhat disjointed and in need of further polishing. Specifically, the timing for parries is challenging to master, and there appears to be inconsistency with the activation of certain combo inputs, leading to moments of frustration. Additionally, I would have favored a gameplay design that focused on controlling a single protagonist, with the other character serving as an AI companion, reminiscent of the dynamic seen in "God of War." This, I believe, would have offered a more streamlined and focused gameplay experience.Visually, the game ranges from satisfactory to stunning. The developers have clearly dedicated a great deal of effort into the presentation of cutscenes, which are both immersive and beautifully crafted, drawing the player deeper into the game's narrative. However, the sound design presents a mixed bag. While it can be exceptionally immersive, particularly in environmental storytelling and key narrative moments, it falls short in combat scenarios. This inconsistency occasionally detracts from the overall experience, leaving engagements feeling somewhat underwhelming. Additionally, the game's musical score shines brilliantly during certain scenes, such as the poignant moment the protagonist finds themselves awakening on a beach. Yet, outside these highlights, the soundtrack tends to fade into the background, marred further by a noticeable looping issue post-release, where at least one track abruptly stops and restarts at inappropriate times.The Foley work, especially in terms of character movement and during cutscenes, stands out as a highlight for me, showcasing a meticulous attention to detail. Voice acting within the game is varied, with the majority delivering exceptional performances that enhance the narrative's impact.It's evident that the development team drew inspiration from the "Witcher" series, as seen in the game's animations, user interface, and overall feel of the game. Despite these similarities, "Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden" secures its place among my favorite games, primarily due to its superb writing and atmospheric depth. I am eagerly looking forward to a sequel, hopeful that it will continue to build upon this strong foundation.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to be writing a very critical review because I liked this game a lot and think some changes from the beginning of planning and development could have made it as good as if not a better game than the Witcher 3, which has been the best-to-date RPG IMO.Firstly, no one has ever once said, "you know what, I wish this game had backtracking." The amount of backtracking in this game stole so much away from my enjoyment. It annoyed the absolute hell out of me. The game is quasi-open world, in the since it is possible to manually travel from region/location, but the world and areas are designed linearly such that there is an obvious start and finish. If you want to send me back to an old location, you cannot combine that with linear level design. Second, the ambient dialogue needs to go. Either you have to record 500 more lines to use or just eliminate it altogether. If I ever hear "Remind me not to make you angry" or "Aye but you cannae cook" again I may go on a watchlist. There is PLENTY of ABSOLUTELY engaging dialogue that is part of the story, investigations, readable material, and game stage transitions - having 3 recycling stupid catch phrases for ambient gameplay got on my nerves very quickly. Third, the skill system in this game is bad. It is over-thought and generally irrelevant with few exceptions. The plus I will give it is being able to re-spec at any time at no cost - that is a good feature. But the majority of the skills are just too annoying to deal with. It's a skill tree, not a coin - it shouldn't be a conglomeration of "X becomes better in B way but Y now sucks" which is what most of the skills are. Just present additional features or bonuses to things. The whole skill tree is just "what trade off do you want". The exceptions to this, without spoiling anything (although I assume most people would identify these on their own quickly) is there are a handful of skills that simply make no sense in any use case at all. The tree is designed that you can only take 1 of 2 skills in a slot, which is fine, but some of the options are just awful - they'd never be taken over the alternative. Why have them there at all?1 play through of the game with no DLC is short, 50 hours. I bought this game on sale for less than $50 and I would pay $70 for it knowing the experience I had. The design and atmosphere is fantastic. I would say it is a mix of Witcher and Bloodborne, and the gameplay/combat is GoW/baby Souls. I had an immense amount of fun playing this game. I only ran into a bug/glitch twice, where I got stuck in terrain, but thanks to the excessive auto save feature neither of these instances cost me more than 30 seconds. The story from start to finish is amazingly well done, and the set up from at least 1 of the endings for a sequel left me very excited. I know there are a lot of variables that determine if that gets made, but here's 1 hoping it does.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming off of DontNods previous game Vampyr, Banishers takes a lot of the concepts and improves them into a new and unique story but also stumbles on some unnecessary fluff. Story-wise, following the tale of the banishers Red and Antea is excellent, DontNod kill it with telling an emotional main story as always that lets you choose along the way how to get invested with the community of new Eden and the things that haunt them. Even the optional haunting cases are all great and I recommend doing them to get additional background flavor on supporting characters which make the ending much more impactful. The missteps are mostly in the combat and the open world. Combat, while initially cool because of the skill tree that Red and Antea share, lacks some depth and towards the end of the game starts feeling button mashy due to a lack of combos. And the open world is beautiful to look at but a lot of double backing and not always the easiest to navigate, sometimes leaving me frustrated that I just wanted to get to the next fast travel point. Vampyr had a controversial morality system making you choose between killing NPCs for growth but obviously locking yourself out of their quests and effecting which ending you got but not always being clear about the impact. Banishers has its own version of this with letting you act as judge, jury, and even executioner for haunting cases by sacrificing the victims if you so choose, which will impact the ending. I dug this system but can see some people being annoyed with some of the vagueness in consequences and how it might effect which ending you get. I still appreciate the effort that DontNod took to do their unique form of emotional storytelling and enjoyed the hell out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying... MAKING GAMES IS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HARD!With that being said, let's rip DONTNOD a new one.Banishers is really ambitious in some ways and utterly deplorable in others. The story and writing are nothing short of spectacular with engaging characters, some nail-biting twists and turns not just in the main story but also the side missions. It's rather the gameplay that fails to borrow what it so strongly attempts borrowing from. I've reached what you'd assume is the second area that slowly moves into two sub areas divided up north and south (light spoiler but not really). There's a few great things about how the world works and is designed. The limited but rich crawlspaces that are the levels although same-y bring some amount of charm through traversal. Capturing what a small set of woods and marshes outside of say New England in the 1700-1800s would look like, at least in my head.Back to gameplay now and oh my god where do I begin. I want to love this game for the game, but no... I instead love it for the story. It's an unusual concept done with a bit of panache and it works. What doesn't work is -  A. Climbing and B - Enemy Variety Climbing being the only consistent annoyance as its too frequent and very sluggish.Enemy variety however is abysmal - In 11 hours I've fought a handful of enemy types not counting the bosses and I believe I've seen everything that a 30 hour game has to offer.Onto the positives however; the powers and abilities and even the combat, yes the same combat people have been hating, is actually quite nice. I like it, it serves it's purpose, you unlock new things and moves you can combo up and execute enemies. I must say that the lock on and camera system could've been better. Heck! Even an FOV slider would fix a lot of the problems here. And that's what i feel is making the crowd go into a tizzy about the combat. On top of that Enemies are sometimes just hit sponges, taking upwards of 20 to 25 hits to simply get rid of an enemy just a couple levels above mine. Needless to say i switched the difficulty to story because I just couldn't take anymore of the enemies being so repetitive and invincible.There's pretty cool equipment that really makes you think about stats and balancing your physical abilities vs your manifestation (ghost) powers and that makes it interesting. The skill tree is pretty damn dynamic. Good enough to keep you switching your moves on the fly and trying new "builds" If i can say that but there's never really a stark difference across builds. The choice system seems reasonably detailed, something Dontnod have established themselves as being more than capable at. So if that's something you enjoy, go for it. It will not disappoint.It's an 8/10 game disguised as a 6/10 game. But hey, it's a damn good 6/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers is an ambitious action/adventure game that combines the mechanics of God of War with the morally ambiguous narrative choices of The Witcher. This is spiced up by the fact that you can switch between two characters at any point, each with their own attacks and abilities. This is used to great extent when it comes to exploration, puzzle-solving and combat and helps keep things interesting. I typically get burned out doing all the side-content in open-world games but I never got bored of it in Banishers. Exploring the world and doing side-quests was consistently engaging throughout my 60+ hour playthrough. Enemy variety is a bit limited, though it can be dynamic because of how the specters work. Basically, different specters have different abilities and can possess different corpses, resulting in a good mix of enemy behaviors. For example, a specter that can teleport might possess the corpse of a sniper, resulting in a sniper that can teleport. This keeps you on your toes and prevents you from getting too complacent. I recommend playing on the highest difficulty for the most engaging experience, as your characters get pretty overpowered if you do all the side content.Banisher's presentation is great and in many ways rivals that of AAA games. The graphics are very nice, the music, sfx and VO are great and the game just feels really polished. This is easily Don't Nod's biggest and slickest game yet. The writing is good too, with a lot of poignant, believable dialogue and meaningful character development. I think the writing's biggest flaw is that the "right" decision in any given situation is usually pretty obvious. I would have preferred more moral ambiguity.Overall, I enjoyed Banishers a lot. The setting wasn't all that interesting to me but the game's writing, presentation and gameplay kept me hooked. Don't Nod clearly put a ton of work into this and it's well worth a playthrough if you enjoyed God of War and The Witcher.

_childDocuments_.review: Great RPG with lots of exploration and interesting (though very bleak) world. The combat system starts out very simple and limited; you only have light and heavy sword attack and banishing that you can only use after charging the banishing meter. But slowly you build up skills for both Red and Antea and eventually you have Antea dropkicking ghosts from beyond after critical, supercharged rifle headshots...The game rewards exploring secrets, deciphering treasure maps and resolving environmental puzzles with all kinds of gear that gives additional effects to your combat skills or survivability, and you can upgrade them with resources you find by defeating ghosts.The story has the main characters pondering the morality of their actions and the fates of a cast of increasingly horrible human beings, while they solve haunting cases on their way to confront the big bad. Some tough choices along the way (and some very easy ones...).Overall, a lovely adventure, especially if you like the New World setting with magic and ghosts!

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden started off quite strong for me and for the first ten hours or so I was loving the game despite the flaws you notice early on but the longer I kept playing the less I enjoyed it. Beating the game took me roughly 37 hours on very hard difficulty with around 65% map completion and by the end of it I didn't have any motivation to do more side content as I was bored not only by the shallow gameplay loop but by the narrative as well - in fact it had me thinking of the saying that sometimes less is more and how the game would have benefited from a much smaller scope.In many ways B:GoNE feels inspired by God of War (2018) with more emphasis placed on the narrative aspects and world building even if there is still a whole lot of combat which unfortunately is one of the weakest aspects of the game. Combat could be described as "serviceable" and while it improves a little as you unlock more things throughout the main story it never really progresses past being not only janky and shallow but also incredibly repetitive: After roughly 5 hours of gameplay you have already seen most if not all of the basic enemy types you face in 90% of the combat encounters and the remaining 10% don't really change the combat loop in any meaningful way.As mentioned above you unlock more combat options as you progress throughout the game which happens in form of multiple small skill trees, in addition to that you have the usual equipment with stats/bonuses that you can upgrade for bigger numbers. These allow you to focus on specific aspects of the combat by boosting the power of specific things such as light, heavy attacks or switch skills etc. but at the end of the day gear and skill bonuses (outside of ones that actually add new moves) feel very surface level and don't really act as playstyle changing or as "builds" but instead they make parts of your arsenal a bit more effective - as you are still encouraged to utilize most of it rather than just focusing on say spamming heavy attacks only.Narrative and world building are a huge focus and I would say they are what carry the game to some degree, even with some minor flaws and a main story that blatantly telegraphs its major plot points very early on to the point where the player doesn't exactly need to be Sherlock Holmes to piece things together which takes away the mystery aspect of figuring out what has happened but still leaves you focused on the stories of the colonists. As you progress through haunting investigations you uncover reasons why the various inhabitants are haunted and you are presented with a choice on how to solve the haunting. Which brings me to another issue as the game establishes a major decision early on and depending on what you want to do, you need to solve the cases in a specific way: This unfortunately makes the choices feel completely binary and their consequences feel largely irrelevant - on the path I chose it was absolutely irrelevant what sort of sob stories I might hear or if there were harsh words after my choice, after all they were simply obstacles on the way to the ending I wanted to get.That being said there are things that the game does well: Atmosphere is great, voice acting for almost entire cast is great and M/KB controls actually work well. Aside from some traversal stutters the PC port seems alright as well and avoids some of the usual issues that have been plaguing unreal engine ports as of late.For me this ended up being a title that lands somewhere in the ballpark of 6 or 7 out of 10, a decent but flawed game and one that can be recommended to the fans of story heavy adventures but only if you have tolerance for good amount of jank and repetition.

_childDocuments_.review: The Banishers game is very good and in my opinion meets all the expectations of its genre. It's definitely worth people trying it out. I would personally rate the game as 8/10. The game was good, even very good, but there were elements that needed a little fine-tuning.We play as Red, who as a Banisher faces decisions that are morally very difficult,  he fights ghosts, demons, specters and tries together with Antea (his partner) to solve the case that darkens the city of New Eden in the new world.Speaking of the new world.The game takes place during the great colonization of America, from the 1500s to the late 1600s. The world that the developers have built is beautiful, filled with breathtaking scenarios in nature, well-integrated puzzles in the terrain. Interacting with objects feels  very natural and fit well into the world and gameplay. Its not entirely an open world game, since it is divided into many regions. Each region is unique with its own town, biome, people, stories and even enemies. But I assure you, the world is BIG, the regions are BIG, so if you worry about how huge the map is....you dont have to. Trust me. The world, the characters and even the enemies seem very realistic, which is very important in this game and I think that this "factor" holds the game on its high spot. At least for me. The story is interesting, although slow at times. However, towards the end, it can pleasantly (or unpleasantly) surprise you with its twists and turns that Red and Antea have to face. The main idea of the story keeps the pace of the game going. As Red, we meet many characters who have their own stories and side quests. All of them are part of the climax of the overall endgame. Red and Antea decide their fate and how the game will end. Your decisions shape the gameplay, the story and even the world around you. I noticed that a lot of people complained about the combat in this game. But in my opinion, most of them are overly negative complaints. The combat in this game is solid, and it even gets better as Red´s and Antea's abilities develop. You just have to grind a little. You can fight at close range with your sword, at a distance with your musket or you can combine it for some cool combos. Red and Antea can change forms and each form has its own abilities. Also each form has its own pros and cons, depending on how you develop your skill tree. ALTHOUGH...What did I miss from this game ? COMBAT - ...one thing I have to agree with the other reviews concerning combat is that it gets pretty repetitive after some time. It would require more enemy types, not always the same specters and ghosts. They are fun to defeat at the beginning but gets boring after you spend 50+ hours in the game. Also (this is just my opinion) they could have added more weapons...and by weapons I mean more weapon TYPEs, like spears, axes, crossbows etc. It would give more freedom to the combat. MUSIC/SOUNDTRACKS - oh god...the music...lets forget about the combat for a sec....This GAME is seriously lacking in soundtracks and music. I think this is one is a great game, and music should be part of every great game. Its a missed opportunity...the developers were either not aware of this or maybe it didnt fit in their budget for the game...but the music is something that is MISSING from this game. There are so many scenes and moments in the game that with the right MUSIC could hit the spot and have been way more epic. Please developers...next time, dont underestimate the power of soundtracks and music for your game.These two factors are the NEGATIVES for me. FINAL WORDS Other than that, it's a great game and anyone who likes this genre should definitely give it a chance. The end of the story has a moral lesson, it reveals the true nature of people and points out what happens when people lie and act without reason...and a game with a lesson and "good" ending is always worth to play. (If you like RPG, story telling games like me)

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED Vampyr. I was really looking forward to this game. But unfortunately it can not compare to Vampyr. In area of combat, "open" world and graphics, the game is not worth mentioning compared to other games of that kind in the market, so I'll stick to commenting the story and setting - what was the strong point of Vampyr too.If Vampyr had a great setting and you could "feel" the dark, gothic surroundings, I can not immerse into this game and setting. A game aims for a story set in 17th century New England haunted by ghosts. What it actually delivers are very predictable (and very not scary) ghost/haunting cases, which require zero brains and just running from A to B to pick up clues - again, more than 1 clue is redundant, since one figures out the "who did it/what is happening" really fast.Dialogues are fit for a College Campus in 2024, not 17th century New England. For instance, you ask a random female settler of a settlement you've just arrived in how the settlement is faring (remember, the place is haunted) and she will tell you straight off the bat she doesn't need a man, because she is a strong, independent woman. Exactly how a 17th century settler of a cursed village would respond. Other dialogues are (mostly) less "into your face" but it seems the ghost haunting the town of New Eden is 21st century feminism.Protagonist is strangely "happy" and positive (despite him, just recently, going through some terrible stuff) and a companion who is plain boring (and annoying). Further ruins immersion. The chemistry between MC and his companion is non existent. One should feel the urge to save his beloved (companion), thus making decisions about life and death tough. But there is really nothing that would make you care about them. A game which aims at making moral decisions tough should make you care about the characters. It's a mix of poor to average writing and poor to average voice acting.I would say this game is a wasted opportunity, but unfortunately it was doomed from the start, when the story was written.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fun enough, the premise is great, character design, locations, dialogues - beautiful. BUT DEAR GOD IS THE GAMEPLAY ATROCIOUS. You get one of these LITERALLY EVERY 15 SECONDS. Quests? Go there, on your way have 15 combat encounters and watch 40 animations, pick something up then backtrack through all of that again to finish the mission.  It's the second time in my life that I got so pissed off at a video game that I ragequit and uninstalled it instantly. Right before I quit I started a quest and decided to count it, I sat through 19 animations and had 8 combat encounters on my way to a quest that was 500 meters away and I didn't even get halfway there before I decided that I've had enough of this. I feel like out of my 13 hours of gameplay 80% was watching these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying ass animations or fighting weak enemies that respawn for several waves. Maybe someday I'll finish this game but the story would honestly have to be the eighth wonder of the world to make it something more than a complete waste of life

_childDocuments_.review: Right away: the story and characters are really cool. The cases can be very interesting and you will face some hard and unique choices. _childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game, it feels like a unique story, but to summarize you're basically old school Ghostbusters in the late 1600s. Your choice matter in this game, and there is a lot of side quests and exploration you can do. There is diverse gear to obtain with differing effects. _childDocuments_.review: A murky yet rich take on regret, love and guilt. Despite its flaws Banishers will be a game I will remember for many years through it's thoughtful, measured approach toward heart-wrenching loss and fathomless grief, although this story offers some respite through its journey it is profound sadness that guides this game, personally I found that it provides great comfort to the thoughts that circle my mind when reflecting loss.I am hopeful looking forward to what this IP could bring, though I struggle to imagine it being able to explore a grief more exhaustive than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations after so many years apart from the masterpiece that was Vampyr. Everything was perfect there, classic DONTNOD storytelling with a simple, but well-fitted RPG component. That was the balance I was expecting from Banishers. I was sorely mistaken.This game comes with Unreal Engine and its well-know optimization problems, but I was ready to face this issue... If I had a fun time playing this game.I will now give you a better description, that perfectly fits the game intention and design. It is a dialogue simulator, with bad voice actors, and a wannabe God of War inspired experience. It misses every point it can miss, just to result in an obnoxious experience. A walking simulator with the same terrain patterns; it makes you feel you are playing through mediocre designed environments, where the same 3 spawning enemies are perfunctorily thrown at you over and over and over again, but with scaled level. They are not even re-skinned; at least, that would have given you the mere illusion that you were facing something different, even if superficially made. It is simply a copy paste, and don't even get me started on the combat system, "boss fights" and the actual combat gameplay. The feeling is awful. As I was making my way through any dialogue, every environments, battling my way through every boring combat sequence, I felt the urge to stand up and just do something that would have helped me to stay awake and not fall asleep on the chair I was sitting. I just couldn't go on like that, and I didn't even finish the game. I was feeling overwhelmed and completely let down, at the same time. I was not having fun, and this is definitely messed up when it comes to videogames.This is a disgraceful, squandered piece of art, and it feels like a waste of time and money. The price tag of 50 (€-$) is a pretty bitter pill to swallow, for what the game has to offer. And coming from DONTNOD, it feels kind of sad.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR summary; don't explore unless you just absolutely love that kind of stuff. Great story! "Open world" is too big and boring.First off, I wish Steam offered a neutral option because that's what I'd go with. If I could re-do my time with B:GoNE, I would stick to the main/side quests like white on rice. World is too big, too slow to navigate and not interesting enough to waste as much time as I did exploring.With that being said, what initially piqued my interest in Banishers was its concept and seemingly strong focus on narrative. I was not disappointed there. I genuinely had a hard time deciding how to resolve most of the ghost Hauntings. It was especially difficult justifying my end goal in my first play through. Only a few of the cases had a "right" way of going about them. Overall high remarks for the story presentation.Lastly the combat. It honestly wasn't as bad as I thought it'd be. Nothing game-defining but there is enough depth and mechanics there to have fun. As always this category is largely subjective as a lot of people disliked Witcher 3's combat which I didn't mind at all. Gear also plays big role and you can build around some interesting synergies.It's just yet another case of a game that has no business being as big as it is. A tighter focus would've been greatly appreciated ... or maybe I'm just getting old.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden, is a narrative action game from the devs behind Life is Strange.You play as a couple of lovers and Banishers, Red and Antea, who have been tasked with uncovering the mystery behind a paranormal curse that plagues the land of New Eden. The situation is worse than they thought, and Antea loses her life as a result, coming back as a ghost, the thing she swore to banish from the land of the living.The strongest aspect of the game for me, was its narrative. As Banishers, you continue to solve hauntings throughout the land, piecing together clues found at the scene of the crime, talking to culprits, ghosts, and watching moments from the past. For the most part, solving a mystery is a linear experience. It isn't like LA Noire where you can piece it together wrong, and accuse someone innocent, but that wasn't a problem for me, as every case was super interesting, and presents a tough choice at the end.Solving hauntings for other people also has an effect on Antea's fate. You see, at the end of a typical case, you can for example, help a possessed villager by violently banishing the ghost that haunted them. However, by digging through their history, you might understand why the ghost did what it did, and choose to peacefully help it ascend from the realm of the living. There is also a third option though...You can cast a "blame" ritual that kills and absorbs the life essence from the living target, with the aim of bringing Antea back to life eventually.The choice isn't easy, as cases are usually quite complicated without a clear victim. That is the main problem you have to juggle throughout the game, which I found very intriguing. I even thoroughly enjoyed the side-quests in the game, and found them to be worth my time for the most part. All of this is heightened by the fantastic voice actors, and likeable personalities of the cast.Banishers isn't purely a narrative game though, so let's talk about the gameplay too.Combat is really fun. Red uses a sword with a light and heavy attack. It can also parry, and he has a rifle for longer range combat. Antea can utilize powerful spells, and avoid permanent health damage. You are encouraged to switch back and forth during combat, as they each have their own strengths and weaknesses. For example, Antea deals more damage to possessed bodies. However, when she attacks, her spirit bar drains. In order to refill that, Red needs to deal damage. The constant juggle back and forth feels super fun, especially when you pair it with interesting talents and equipment that further reward certain playstyles. It's great that your talents aren't locked in, and you can freely move your selections around on the go to try new playstyles. Unfortunately, upgrading gear doesn't have that same freedom, so I found myself a bit scared to commit to upgrading certain items in fear that I'd just find something else I liked and wasted my materials. Another minor gripe I had, was that many of the attributes attached to equipment, and what they do are not explained.Navigating the environment is quite restricted, however through enough exploration you can unlock shortcuts. The maps have a metroidvania-esque feeling to them, as you retread a lot of your steps after obtaining new abilities in order to access new places with hidden loot.I'm normally someone who likes to fully explore and collect everything, which I did here too, and enjoyed for the most part, however there were times where I found the backtracking to be a bit tedious. You can only fast travel from one camp to another, you might not always have the materials you need to start a side-task, and so on. But for the most part, I had fun with it.Overall though, I really loved playing through the game, as I enjoyed the characters and world. In my opinion, it's biggest strength by far is the interesting narrative. The combat is really fun, but I would only recommend the game to someone that is intrigued by the premise of ghost-mystery solving and dealing with moral dilemmas, which in my opinion, Banishers does incredibly well!(BONUS: The game looks beautiful, and I've had no bugs or performance issues.)

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the chance to play and buy [Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden] and I have to say, it's one of the best games I've played in a long time. The story is rich and captivating, drawing you in from the very beginning. I found myself invested in the characters and their journey, which is a testament to the excellent writing and world-building.The graphics and sound design also deserve praise. The game has a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere, with stunning visuals and a haunting soundtrack that adds to the overall immersion.If I had to compare Banishers to another game, I would say it's a blend of God of War and Vampyr. The combat feels similar to God of War, while the supernatural elements and mysterious setting are reminiscent of Vampyr.But don't let the comparisons fool you, Banishers stands on its own as a unique and captivating experience. It offers a refreshing take on the supernatural genre and keeps you engaged from start to finish.In conclusion, I highly recommend Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden to anyone looking for a well-crafted and engaging game. It's definitely worth buying and will provide hours of entertainment. So if you're a fan of action games with a rich story, do yourself a favor and give Banishers a try. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I do recommend. The game has all the traits of a good open world RPG so anyone looking for a longer story based time sink will likely be happy with it. I will say though it is far from perfect. While playing this I couldn't help but compare with God of War, it was basically just them copying the homework but not completely understanding the source material. All the good elements are there but not put together amazingly well. Just quickly - This is not a souls-like. I saw some people claiming it is on forums and wanted to stab them. This is a souls-like in the same way chess is an RTS.Some spoilers below.The Good.- Story outcomes. By this I mean the "closures". Players can often not predict what the actual outcomes of any closure decision will lead to. This is both good and bad in how the player wants the story to play out but at the same time it can make each choice matter more and seem more, and sometimes less, organic to the player that way and thus better storytelling. The only catch / benefit of this is the player can never truly tell what the main characters are actually thinking so somewhat innovative idea but feels odd. The game also doesn't quite tell the player what "good" and "evil" really are. E.g Banishing a ghost that is truly malignant and has intent to kill isn't forced nor is sparing a sister for the accidental death of her brother. In this way there is a bit more "freedom" for the player but it does still feel kind of odd due to the unpredictable element. E.g Does blaming an innocent mean the real perpetrator will now go on to harms others etc.The Meh- Combat, fairly free-flow. It begins being very clunky and restrictive but opens up a decent amount with options as you move through the story. But it gets stale pretty quickly. This is made especially apparent when there are less than 10 enemy types and they are not very unique nor do they encourage combat versatility. You can basically play the entire game just using the rifle and almost never using Antea. - Real Life Political Influence (WOKE). I call this meh because I've seen a lot of comments on forums stating this game is "woke" or at least influenced, however at least not enough in my opinion to be a problem. It does highroad a little bit but in understandable ways. My only issue was a few of the Haunting missions SPECIFICALLY used minority victims a few too many times. Apparently, along with all the witches that came to America in 1680 at least I think 3 gay couples decided to all settle in this VERY SMALL community. Doubt. However, I didn't entirely mind that their hauntings usually centered on their orientation because at this time in history and surrounded by Puritan Christians they would be in a VERY dangerous situation.- Main story. Very weird scale. The game surrounds ghosts and their unfinished business / how they were wronged. However, I cannot, with the exception of the "illmouth" which would likely be in similar places elsewhere, see how the root of the curse is in any way special or be as powerful as it is. Similar tragedies happened all over the world during this time and on much larger scales and somehow a "nightmare" is a nigh unheard of entity and is in retrospect caused by an event that is, again for the time, fairly mundane. This same argument could be made for 90% of the haunting cases. If New Eden were a benchmark there would be no one alive not haunted, again illmouth not withstanding. Banishers would be a staple industry in every town like a Priest of cobbler.- Choppy Dialogue. Both visually and screenplay. Some of the conversations seeme poorly edited. Red / Antea would at times change emotional states every other second. This can happen with dialogue trees but it also happens in the banter between the two. There was a scene where Red bid farewell to a ghost twice, in dialogue and then again in Ascension (a little odd). Animations were weird. This is more a pet peeve of mine. But if your going to the effort of trying to make the characters faces actually mouth / shape the words their saying either do it properly or not at all. Came off as a really weird dub. Ofc I could forgive it if the default language is not English, devs I think are French / Canadian. - Gear. Very simple system. After looking through all the gear (I found it all) I probably only used 2-3 of each type of gear. Some of them are very generic. Once you start doing the endless voids / fight pits stats are obsolete so you only want their special effects and most of them are garbage. All but 2 of the potions were useless as they were the only ones that increased damage and the golden rule is always damage > defense. A bit more effort would have been appreciated. Either by adding more versatility to the items or adding actual effects not just buffs / stat changes. E.g an amulet that makes all manifestations apply Weaving but do no damage. Players could combo this with rifle damage or punches etc. The current system is pretty much just min/maxing for the damage type you want which encourages players to stick to the playstyle they use and not grow or adapt. Especially apparent when you see that most of the same effects can be found in the skill tree in weaker forms.The Bad- Travel. The areas are big enough that travel is a chore. Once your into the free roam part of the game there are soooo many fetch / bad chain quests that demand long travel. This ofc would be fixed by adding more campsites / fast travel spots or they could have given Antea some kind of dash along the ground like casting Leap. At least they could have made an effort to make it enjoyable. Also the CONSTANT specter ambushes are soooo tedious. Especially when running some errand or scanning an area for collectibles.- Replayability. Low. The game honestly wore me out. I had to force myself to do some of the hauntings / post haunting activities as I have really bad OCD and even then I doubt I'm gonna try and 100% it. Only a couple of elements are replayable, namely endings and some closures which were more interesting. However, endings are affected, not sure how much, by all the closures / choices made prior so changing endings likely requires starting nearly from the beginning. So, no ty.- Ambient Sound / Music. Specifically, SOUL SHARDS. As a collectible they shouldn't be so stupidly hard to notice. You can't hear them unless your literally on top of them. Finding them once you knew one was in the area should be the challenge / puzzle not hoping to find them in a small country. Some are stashed sneakily but if you actually search you will SEE them as they are hidden in nooks / around other loot. Their sound however is easily mistaken for the weird ambient screech heard in the harrows / dark forest which is a big middle finger to players searching. This should have been much more unique.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially my DREAM GAME made manifest. I'm a Dungeon Master for multiple TTRPGS like D&D, Vampire the Masquerade, Call of Cthulhu and such. Over the years I have created this massive leather bound ghost hunting journal as a prop for my players to use as most of the stories are about ghosts or the paranormal in some extent. I have always dreamed of a game that mix real-world occultism inspiration with paranormal monsters such ghosts. Especially one that is story-based and all about Gothic horror (the horror of the self). THIS IS THAT GAME.This game has even taught me some major real world things and how completely complex people are. In this game, you have a lot of side missions that are about helping people dealing with haunting. These hauntings aren't just simple 'find evidence and banish the ghost'. The ghosts are as complex at the individuals they haunt. There's always a reason and story to be told in each haunting. No haunting case ever feels the same and each one is incredibly different. When I first started up this game, the main menu was one of the two characters sitting infront of a fire. A deep beautiful melancholy song played as snow fell around him as he stares in the fire. As the game was prompting me to "press any key to continue". I knew immediately that this game was going to hit me with all the emotions. It does not disappoint. You have to make heavy choices that have huge implications on not only yourself morally but also on the journey of the game.  It also has some very emotional moments that doesn't have me in tears but it's gotten close a few times and it's hard to get me to cry.I'm not even done with the game at the time of writing this. I think I'm near the end but I really don't want this game to end lol. I adore every little amazing thing of this game. If you like ghosts, if you like gothic horror, if you like the trailers. Get the damn game. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Story and writing are good, with some occasional hiccups, but mostly smooth sailing. The story and the various hauntings (side quests) cover some deeply emotional topics and themes, covering people's grief and pain and mortality. The game is almost reminiscent of the Witcher 3 in a sense, but instead of monsters, you're dealing with ghosts. The gameplay is simplistic but fun and satisfying, and takes some inspiration from the newer God of War games.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Awesome game that's not the same old same old.  Definite recommend.I've been a gamer since I got an Atari 2600 as a kid.  So yeah, I'm old & I've played a ton of games.  After all these years you start feeling like you've played many "new" titles already because they are just like X game you've played before, reskinned and rebranded.  This one is stands out as being delightfully different, but not in a weird way.  It has a great and unique setting, subject matter and story.  The voice acting is phenomenal with very nice music and visuals.   The few downsides are that the combat feels just ok and the rank and file enemies start to feel a bit same'ish.  The first big boss fight I've cleared was different and enjoyable.  Try this if you're looking for something to play that stands out from the crowd.  I think you'll really enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like story driven games this is a good one. Its like playing a 50 hour movie. That being said it does play like any action game with lots of fights, light/heavy attack combo's. Switching between characters one of which is alive the other dead allows for different views of the world as you explore. The world is not an open world. The exploration is map based and many of the pathways are blocked and you have to solve environmental puzzles to continue. By the end of my 50 hour play through I was a little tired of all the running in this game. Red even makes a joke about it at one point. The story is excellent and the exploring is better than I had originally thought. My hope is that if they ever make a sequel it will be open world with less travel time between quests.  8/10Edit after completion: This was a solid game, I did all of the haunting quests and and finished about 50% of the map. This took me 50 hours. If you were to 100% this you would be looking at about 65 hours probably.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden tells an incredibly intriguing and moving story while offering some really good gameplay and exploration for you to experience. The side quests (Hauntings) are nearly Witcher 3 levels of quality, and the combat really settles into a nice rhythm as you unlock key abilities. It may not be a technical showpiece, but the art design and environments do look quite good, and the voice acting, writing, storyline, and decisions you have to make are phenomenal. If you enjoyed games like God of War (2018), Plague Tale, The Witcher 3, or really ANY Don't Nod game... get this one. It's worthy of your money and your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game although I had to dig for videos about what outcome I wanted or how to find certain locations. The game felt like I was in on all of the town gossip which was super fun to unravel and find out the lore of New Eden. If I were to play the game again I want to try to help Antea Duarte ascend. The way the towns people judge you based off of your actions did remind me of Red Dead Redemption. I loved the dialogue the most, and progressively the gameplay got more challenging but also more fun especially toward the final boss fight. Throughout the game, the atmosphere is very eerie and gloomy but the banter between Antea and Red make you feel more prepared for the worst. Super fun game all in all and I would highly recommend it if you like solving cases because the fate of New Eden is essentially up to what you prioritize.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the latest GOW games, then this may be right up your ally. The gameplay loop is very similar to the GOW games and offers a variety of content in similar ways, such as platforming, puzzle solving, and combat. The story is quite interesting, and while it does take a lot of inspiration from a bygone time in its setting, many liberties have also been taken, but don't let that dissuade you from playing. It's a video game about malevolent supernatural forces overtaking a community, so some things aren't going to be 100% historically accurate. You will be doing a lot of walking and a lot of backtracking and a lot of exploring, but it's worth it for that sweet sweet loot.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible new IP that marries God of War with The Witcher into something truly its own. A fantastic story that is, unfortunately, marred by a few bad choices. If you're on the fence about this I would say that it's absolutely worth it. I easily got almost 50 hours out of this and can say, for the vast majority of that, I enjoyed it. The writing, acting, animations, environments, combat, and overall gameplay are truly fantastic. This, in my opinion, easily rises to 'AAA' game quality standards from what is probably a 'AA' game (though Dont Nod and Focus are both incredible in their own right). For all the good it has, it unfortunately does, however, have some truly sour notes.The tick marks in the 'con' column for me are small but immensely impactful and if a dev does read this, I truly hope they take the following 3 bits of feedback to heart when they (hopefully) make Banishers 2.1- The fast travel system is awful. Out of 50 hours I wager I spent 35 of that just...traversing the map. Repeatedly running from point A to point B over and over again, tracing and retracing steps dozens of times. Walking the same cliffs, shimmying through the same crevices, climbing the same ropes. Why cant I simply open my map and fast travel to a hearth? Why must I be at a hearth to travel to a hearth? Or hell, give me a horse or something. This simple change would elevate this game to top tier but as it currently stands you will spend a LOT of time just playing colonial running simulator as it, like the games antagonist, slowly sucks away your soul.2- The game does get incredibly grindy after a certain point in the game (around act 2). For the most part, you will repeat the same activities, perform the same tricks, do the same puzzles, and fight the same monsters over and over. The entire games set of enemies is basically just 4 ghosts + wolves. A white ghost, blue ghost, green ghost, big red ghost (then all of those in 'armor') plus wolves. Oh..and 'wisps' that are just light balls. From hour 1 to hour 50, that's it. The boss battles are fantastic, particularly act 2's but it isnt enough to carry the game when you're still fighting white specters 15 minutes before the end of the game, the same as in hour 1. Likewise, the same tricks get played on you and after a time they all wear thin. The "Oh look a house with a blocked door - ill go around the back and shoot the door jam" is so overplayed and if I have to do another creeping ivy puzzle I'll lose my mind. It's just not fun, it's tedium, it's work, it's a roadblock TO fun. After about the 3 dozenth creeping ivy and 10th void mirror I was just...spent. The rewards werent worth it and I stopped caring and just wanted it to be over. 3- The endings in the game are obfuscated, to a degree, and that really frustrated me. I was going for a specific ending. I was counting the number of decisions I made to ensure I was putting more emphasis on one over another. In the end, I got the worst possible ending regardless. After the monotony of running simulator and the grind mentioned above, I sort of just wanted it to be over towards the end. Only to realize that this entire time, I was unable to get the ending I wanted and would have to play the entire game again if I wanted to change that. This should be far more obvious to the player and trackable so they truly know what they're working toward rather than getting an unwelcome surprise after 50 hours of gameplay. Thankfully, YouTube exists...All that being said, I do strongly recommend it, it's a wonderful new IP and I do hope to see a sequel perhaps set in a different timeline (though I very much enjoyed colonial America). Bravo to the team, this is a masterpiece that flew under the radar but deserves its time in the light. Life to the living, death to the dead.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, I’m playing Banishers Ghosts of New Eden, and I’m really enjoying it. This game was very low on my radar—I had seen some footage and read a few articles online—but I wasn’t sure if I wanted to play it. I decided to buy it anyway, and from the first mission, it’s been incredibly compelling.The game has a rich story, presented in a cinematic way that feels unique and immersive. The voice acting is top-notch, AAA quality. The actors bring so much to their roles that you feel connected to the characters right from the start. You play as Red and Antea, two ghost hunters who bring peace to those stuck between the living and the dead, and this story really resonates with me.The gameplay is linear, set in a semi-open world. Well, actually, it’s not an open world at all. It’s a linear experience, but there are plenty of opportunities for exploration—looting chests, searching for resources, and upgrading equipment. That’s all I needed, honestly. I didn’t expect or need this to be a vast open-world game. The world they’ve created fits perfectly with the early settlement setting which complements the story really well.The combat is very satisfying, especially when switching between Red and Antea to perform certain moves—not really combos, but they feel satisfying enough to be considered that. I’ve played a few hours and done some main quests, and the enemy variety is decent. I’ve seen games with less variety and others with more, but for a game of this caliber, it’s good so far.What sets this game apart are its unique gameplay elements, like performing rituals and completing ghost-hunting side quests. These side quests are well-executed and often provide choices with moral consequences that affect both the main characters and the overall story. It’s been a while since I’ve played a game that offers real choices with real consequences. Many recent games offer the illusion of choice, but I feel like this game gives me meaningful options, which is fantastic.For me, Banishers Ghosts of New Eden is one of the biggest surprises of 2024. It came out a few months ago, and I’ve been hooked ever since playing it. If you enjoy ghost-hunting games or stories about the occult, life after death or if you’re looking for a game with an engaging story, this is the game for you. It also offers a good balance of varied gameplay elements and meaningful choices that impact the narrative.Don’t Nod Games has done something magical here, and Focus Entertainment has done an excellent job bringing this to the masses. A big thank you to the developers and everyone involved in bringing this game to life. It’s truly one hell of a game, so be sure to check it out!

Not going into detail, in case you want to see, but I KNEW she would not only skip apologizing to the husband, but she never apologized to Red for snapping at him either. You get bread crumbs, not much. Bits a pieces of the details. You fight the boss......... Thats it. She never fills it in. Which is funny because the entity dogs Red because Antea won't tell him.. So she doesn't tell him even after facing it with her? Another? Antea bashes Christians and marriage quite a bit. Denying Red her hand because a "piece of paper doesn't define their love".... Not to speak for Red, but maybe he doesn't care about paper or the government. Maybe he wants your hand under God and the symbolic gesture that it serves for not only you two, but the world. BUT BUT BUT! She doesn't believe in God... In a game where she has to confront ghosts, admits there are demons, who CAN posses mortals and lore tells of souls. WHO WROTE THIS!Another? (SIDE NOTE: Some details below are story driven. Nothing serious. First mission stuff.)At one point she openly states she blames Red for her death, right to his face. By the end, would you think there will be character development? Welp, NOPE! She NEVER forgives him. She never actually grows to be honest. The writers probably hide behind Antea stating, and actually believing, people do not change. Again, in my opinion, not compelling. What blows me away is Antea basically sees the enemy that kills her at one point AND the attack the enemy uses to kill her with. Still, when the time comes, Antea falls right into it. Red only misfortune was having a teacher that did not forewarn him of the type of trickery that could befall them with the type of enemy they were facing. Still, a massive question pops up. WHERE WAS ANTEA? Basically, Red falls into a trap solo, without Antea. Truthfully he only goes because Red thought Antea went without him because he is a newb and Antea is strong willed and would face the threat alone to spare him. So he goes in search for his love to fight beside her. Sadly this IS the trap and Red gets himself in a pickle. Honorable as he is, he does fall into a trap. My issue though is Antea, and to the extent the writers at Dont Nod who forgot to mention WHERE Antea went? You play as Red at this point in time, Antea really was not around. Was Red sleep walking? Did Antea go to the bathroom? Don't know. But I do know she blames Red. TRUE ConclusionLook, I tried for a refund, to just walk away. _childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden has one of the best stories I've experienced in a while. Banishers mixes a bunch of influences into a delicious little stew. It's got a big world, not really open world, but a lot to explore. There's snappy third-person combat with dodging and parrying and big skills on cooldowns. You can find resources and upgrade your weapons and unlock skills in a skill tree. A lot of the surface stuff is familiar but it's in service of telling a truly great story.Banishers follows two banishers, Antea and Red, who travel to New Eden, a fictionalized settlement in New England, during the end of the 17th century to investigate a curse on the region. Banishers investigate hauntings and get rid of the ghosts causing them. When Antea and Red arrive in New Eden, a bunch of stuff happens and the rest of the game you're trying to fix things in New Eden. An important aspect of the story is that while Antea and Red are mentor and apprentice, respectively, in the banishing profession, they are also lovers. As you progress, their history and relationship opens up and evolves and you see these are two people with their own pasts, personalities, and priorities. It ends up being maybe the most authentic and compelling example of a romantic relationship in a video I've played, supported by excellent writing and great voice acting across the board, especially from the two leads. The game can drag from time to time in the combat or backtracking across the map, but the story is always compelling, even in small moments of banter between Antea and Red.Beyond Antea and Red's relationship, the main story is also very compelling with a lot of complicated choices to make that don't have easy answers. As you unravel why New Eden is cursed, it makes decisions even tougher. As a bonus to the main story, you'll be able to complete several haunting cases where you find out that someone is haunted and have to figure out why and then decide how to resolve things. While these are smaller stories, they're great, and a perfect example of how thoughtful writing can elevate a side quest from a simple fetch quest to something that feels indispensable from the rest of the game. If you've played the Witcher 3, they remind me a lot of the monster contracts from that game which always seemed simple on the surface but inevitably provided some twist or surprise you weren't expecting.You can spend a lot of time with Banishers, but even if you just choose to tackle the main story, you'll be left with a moving and thoughtful tale. It's a story I didn't really want to end, but still feel incredibly satisfied to have seen.
