_childDocuments_.review: Banishers is excellent, if you love God of War and The Witcher 3, or other cinematic action RPGs, this game is a MUST PLAY!This game starts out slow and kind of boring. But, it then starts drawing you in with the excellent voiceacting, cinematic presentation, and interesting world. After that, it starts introducing the RPG and loot mechanics, which are all quite damn solid and fun, with a skill tree featuring branching choices that you can respec on the fly. I like this trend of offering choices instead of just allowing you to get every single skill in the skill tree, in Banishers you have to choose one upgrade over the other in a path.I know we are all tired of color coded loot and whatnot, but Banishers makes it fun and rewarding again... well, just like any GOOD action RPG not trying to be a live service nightmare. You can upgrade your equipment with various items you scavenge, and I like how there is a lore reason for why you do it: Because Banishers are also alchemists, survivalists, wanderers, and herbalists who use plants in rituals or fur/leather/metal/thread to reinforce equipment.The combat is standard, but it's challenging and starts growing on you, there is a real sense of weight to the sword swings and the game steadily introduces new abilities for you to use in combat or while exploring. Combat starts getting more fresh and fun.The world is semi-open, with just enough branching paths to explore and find secrets.Then, after all of that awesomeness, the game introduces the central story-driven choice mechanics. You are going to make some DIFFICULT choices, and it's up to you to decide whether or not it's right or wrong.In summary, Banishers is a game that gets better the more you play it, just be patient with the slow start and you'll love it IF you loved God of War.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very interested in this game after it's reveal at the game awards in 2022 but forgot about it shortly after. When it got close to release I remembered how good it looked. I was originally waiting to buy it until clearing some of my backlog, but decided to jump in anyways after seeing all the good reviews. I believe I'm about 3/4 of the way through the game and wanted to express how great I feel it is. The combat feels most similar to the newer God of War games and that isn't a bad thing. There is a large amount of gear items and skill tree options (later in the game) to choose from that allow you to pick how you want to play. Maybe you want to be centered around doing the most damage from range, or maybe you want to use a certain skill or power as often as possible. It gives you lots of freedom to choose your play style.I do have to say that my favorite part of the game and probably its strongest part is the dialogue and story telling. I love meeting people and getting to the bottom of the games side quests called "hauntings". They work exactly as they sound, someone is haunted, find out why. You then are allowed to choose how you handle the case after you finish investigating. Is the person haunted to blame, or the ghost? It's a lot of fun and your choices may not always affect the main story line, but you can see its affect on the communities they're in. In regards to the dialogue, I just love the little chats between the two main characters, their strong connection to each other really helps build your attachment to them and their relationship. It feels very real, and not cringey.I will admit that the game isn't perfect. I have encountered a few different bugs while playing, but nothing game breaking. It usually occurs while initiating or in the middle of a conversation with an NPC. Occasionally I will speak to an NPC and be teleported inside their house for the duration of their conversation, but return outside after it concludes. Another, is when initiating a conversation with an NPC the time of day and weather completely changes during the conversation, and returns to normal once concluding. Aside from those two things I can't say I've experienced much else and it's only happened during side content.If you're on the fence about the game, I strongly recommend it. If you like story driven games where you are put in a position to make some VERY HARD choices, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: People that say the AA game genre is dead are ignoring brilliant games like Banishers, It is an emotional and heartfelt story with combat that on its surface seems shallow but has a good amount of depth to it.Beyond the great storytelling, voice acting and such that other reviewers have mentioned, my favorite part of the game is its unique approach to the skill tree. You have many skill tree, each unlocking when you unlock a new ghostly ability for Antea to use. The best part of it though is instead of unlocking a single "abiliuty" with your point, you instead unlock a "branch" of abilities for 1 skill point, and then are able to freely swap from any of the abilities on that branch to have active without needing to spend another point. But you can only have one ability on that branch active at a time. This is a minor downside if you want to have both abilities on the branch, but the abilities in each branch are also widely varied for example one will give you a health regen for 10 seconds if you make a perfect parry, while the other will boost your attack after you have Antea do one of her abilities. So the branches do not overlap and you do not tend to feel any sort of "missing out" by having one abilitiy in the branch over another.The boss fights are incredible and cinematic.and while some say the game drags on a bit too long I havent experienced that myself, though I have only completed chapter 4 at the time of writing.Dont Nod as a developer may have gotten their name primarily from the acclaimed Life Is Strange series. but this game along with their previous similar title Vampyr, shows they can make a decent AA RPG as well. and I am looking forward to seeing what this tream at Don't Nod cook up in the future. Despite the flaws of this game is it extremely fun and got really good reviews. I have hope and belief that this team can and will make something even better in the future. Don't pass on this game, it may not be an Assassin's Creed, Dragon Age or Elden Ring, but it is still an experience you will not forget

_childDocuments_.review: I am very divided. The character writing and narrative are good, but there is really little to no mystery whatsoever. Left offset 3rd person open world action game is one of my most despised types of game. In my 30 hours, very little of that is meaningful gameplay. Cutscenes, traversal animations, running around, spamming interact, waiting for dialogue to end, and menuing will make up most of your playtime. Combat can be passable if you are intentional about using your unlocked abilities, although the difficulty is not sufficient to force you to do so. If you care about enemy variety, this game will piss you off because you fight the same 4 guys the whole game. The main questline is good but there's no shot in hell I'm doing anymore side content. I enjoyed this game's plot but was eager for it to end from hour 1 when I picked up 4 leather and realized what type of game this was about to be. For a AA team, this is a commendable effort; and even though I didn't find it very fun, it was cool. Unfortunately I feel this game might be best experienced as a 3 hour long youtube video. I was just playing Ninja Gaiden before this which may have colored my experience as the contrast is significant.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave a review, before finishing a game, but this is such an exceptional title. What a unique premise for a story - a pair of ghost hunters in the colonial period North America (1695) perform rites to help people with ghost problems. This is an rpg with plenty of dialogue and tough choices, coupled with detective mechanics where you question both the living & the dead, and then search your surroundings in order to solve hauntings in a semi-open world. There are also plenty of accessibility settings and difficulty options (inc. easy) if you just want to focus on the narrative and kill everything in a few hits. The main characters - Antea and Red have such amazing chemistry and dialogues are fantastic! People are missing out on this gem - this should be a massive seller and deserve every bit of attention! Might be the most unique and one of my favorite AA games I've ever played. Also check out Vampyr, their previous rpg, where you're a Vampire Doctor in 1910s England struggling between your thirst for blood & the desire to help patients.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't Nod polished the formula they used for Vampyr and created another beautiful AA+ game where you play God and judge people based on their actions .Despite the investigative nature of this game there isn't much text to read at all. I personally struggle with reading text and I appreciate this A LOT.Unlike most games with a "karma" mechanic, in Banishers your choices will not affect you directly but the person you care about the most (I won't spoil). For this reason I decided to tank the guilt of exploiting innocents and i went for a selfish/genocide/evil/whatever run as my first and only playthrough instead of my usual good karma/pacifist gameplay.The "district/town/settlement citizen health" system is not as invasive as it was on Vampyr and won't kill the entire zone if you fail to keep up with it.-Exploration follows a pretty scripted model but level design benefits a lot from it and the whole map is very well made.-Combat feels weird and clunky at first but starts to make sense once you unlock more skills. Building doesn't go too deep and this makes build variety pretty vast and can be changed at any time. Rebinding some keys can help.-Technically the game is well polished and optimized. Haven't had any problems typical of modern games in the first months after launch.CONS:

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth a play if you enjoy a good story. The voice acting and dialogue and choices in this game are excellent and actually seem meaningful (you want to be the bad guy, characters are going to make you feel like it). The graphics are very well done and the devs do a good job of pulling off realism, though the teeth are unsettling for some reason to me. I miss karma systems in games so it's nice to see some semblance of one appearing here with the mechanic of 'relationships' with NPCs.Unfortunately, the combat is extremely dull and the progression of combat abilities is slow. Most combat boils down to button mashing while trying to appear souls-like. Sure, you have a fixed number of heals, but they'll replenish after the encounter. Sure, you have camps (bonfires), but if you die, you'll just start at the start of the encounter. The combat is good looking and fluid enough, but just boring. The movement feels weirdly blocky and don't stray too far from the path when exploring (because you literally can't walk into the bushes). The environmental puzzles are less GoW/Prince of Persia and more 'did you fall the path?'. The game seems to have some frame issues too. I'm able to run LotF at 120 on my rig, but Banishers struggles to maintain 45 and will sometimes bottom out for no apparent reason.All in all, I'd recommend this game, but not at full price. I haven't finished it yet, but outside of the story, it's not doing anything unique and some of the stuff it tries to emulate, it doesn't do well. I'd recommend others wait until it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a third person Role Playing Game about Red MacRaith and Antea Duarte, a married couple who hunt ghosts in late 1600s North America.When Antea is killed by a powerful nightmare which haunts an entire town, Red must find a way to banish the nightmare with the help of Antea’s ghost. But this also gives Red a difficult choice to make. Will he help Antea ascend to the afterlife, or will he consume the souls of living people in order to resurrect his wife?•	The player can control both characters, and you’re able to switch between them at any time. While both characters can use melee attacks, Red has a rifle for ranged attacks, and Antea can use three magic abilities. Dash lets you instantly jump across long distances towards an enemy, outburst damages all enemies around you, while ensnare roots an enemy in place for a few seconds. These attacks and skills can be upgraded with bonus effects when levelling up.•	Combat feels slightly repetitive because there’s not much enemy variety, with just a few different ghosts who have melee or ranged attacks, the occasional pack of wolves, and a couple of unique bosses.•	While normal difficulty isn’t too challenging, at times I felt like some of the enemies have too much health, which makes the fights drag on a bit too long. Ghosts can possess dead bodies, which means you often have to defeat them twice to finish them off properly, and of course many fights will spawn extra waves of additional enemies.•	You can equip new weapons, armour, and other items which provide boosts to different stats, and can be improved further by crafting upgrades. While you can compare items in your inventory to see which is better, I couldn’t see how to compare items in shops to see if a new item is better than what I already own. This makes buying new items more difficult than it should be.•	Your journey will take you through small villages, forests, snowy mountains, and underground caves. Some areas have been corrupted by the nightmare, with ruined buildings covered in strange plant growths, and large areas shrouded in fog.•	The world map has a similar design to Metroidvania games, as some paths are blocked until you acquire the relevant skill to remove or bypass the barrier. Its worth exploring to find hidden items, passive upgrades, and elite enemies who reward you with rare crafting materials. Antea can see hidden objects in the spirit realm, which is also used in light puzzle solving.•	Story is well written and features many interesting characters, some of whom are hiding dark secrets. It takes place in roughly the same location and time period as the Salem witch trials, and the dialogue has an appropriately old timey feeling.•	Side quests feature detailed, unique stories involving ghosts haunting the citizens of New Eden. Talk to the living and the dead, search the area for clues, discover the cause of the ghost’s death, and learn what unfinished business is preventing them from moving on. Then you’ll need to decide whether to banish or ascend the ghost, or blame the living, which kills them. These moral choices are further complicated by the fact that your decisions will determine Antea’s fate.•	Voice acting is excellent, especially for Red and Antea.•	It took me 43 hours to complete the main story and all of the side quests.•	I didn’t have any problems with framerate, with most settings maxed at 1440p. (RTX 3080, i7-12700K, 32GB DDR4).•	The game crashed twice, but I think this is acceptable stability for the number of hours played.•	Controls are fully rebindable and work well with mouse and keyboard.•	I would advise disabling film grain, because its very distracting during cutscenes, and everything looks significantly better without it. However, there’s no option in the game menu, so you’ll need to search the forum for instructions.Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden is a very enjoyable RPG. While the combat feels a bit repetitive, the story is excellent. This is easily Dontnod’s best game since the original Life is Strange, and you should consider buying it on a small sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Like everything in this world, there are some good things about this game, and some bad ones. This game has a good main story and narrative in its quests. I like how the destinies of many side characters are intertwined with the main plot. It also has a pleasant soundtrack however, sometimes melodies are mismatched with the mood of the scene where they are played.  Let's stress out some negative things, such as boring exploration and combat systems. This game should not be that long. It makes you walk and run distances far too long and almost without a purpose or meaningful reward. I can't remember any other game that made me use fast travel to avoid its traversal mechanics so often as this one. Developers surely were inspired by the God of War, however, their lack of experience and/or resources doesn't allow them to make exploration fun. It looks like they had to make this game as long as possible, and pacing has been a victim of this. The combat system doesn't evolve much during the game, and I think Antea's animations are done far better than Red.And of course, there is plenty of left-wing discourse here. The game takes place in 1690s in New England and we can find here lesbian couples, gay love stories, and the fight against racism and crimes of the first colonists. That's apart from criticism of religion where people of faith are shown like a bunch of uneducated bloodthirsty lunatics where people of magic and sorcery look like some sort of misunderstood and oppressed scientists. In short words:An interesting region, a good main love story, very mediocre gameplay, and misplaced modern left-wing discourse in a historical setting. You may play it for the sake of the story, but it will cost you many boring hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with a question: What is art? No, really, what is it? It's subjective, right? Nothing is objectively good or bad, so-called "masterpieces" are nothing more than common consensus, love is just a chemical reaction, God is dead. Right? *Right?*Wrong, and you're a fool for ever suggesting otherwise. *I* decide what art is, *I* am the arbiter of quality, and like a child expectantly awaits the will of the father, *you* are the audience to my judgment. Overall, 13 hours in, I give Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden a 8.5/10. I've seen a lot of people hedging and giving very safe, lukewarm assessments: 7/10s, 6.5/10s, "great writing but bad combat", etc.The reality is, despite its imperfections, it is simply *incorrect* to place this game in the same tier as other 7/10s. What is on offer here, what the game does well, what it brings to the table far and away exceeds its "slightly better than mediocre" brethren. I want to set the record straight. The world-building, the narrative, the pacing, the prose, the voice performances--all of the *non-gameplay-specific elements* are, unbelievably, best-in-class. We're not talking Greedfall or Elex (no shade on either of these--i love eurojank) or Dying Light (still not throwing shade, just giving examples of 7/10s). We're talking The Witcher 3, God of War, A Plague Tale (Innocence or Requiem). No exaggeration. The story that is being told here and the panache and proficiency and heart with which it is told is The Real Deal^tm. Okay, so what about the gameplay? What about the mediocre combat? Sure, it has good talky-talky word bits, but how are we expected to care about things like "plot" and "characters" without that sweet vidya dopamine? Good questions. Combat IS a 7/10. It's good. It's serviceable. It's better than Nu-Assassin's Creed, it's worse than Sekiro and God of War. That's really all you have to know. It's good. It has decent animations, decent hitboxes, and overall doesn't commit any major sins. You'll be fine. But maybe you can see how the maths aren't mathing? The game executes SO many things at SUCH a high-level, and then its greatest flaw is that its combat isn't as good as some of the most genre-defining, most universally GOATed titles, and yet somehow that is enough to bring the sum of its parts down to a 7/10? That makes no sense. If Plague Tale was an 8/10, then this was an 8/10. If Plague Tale was an 8.5/10, then this was an 8.5/10. This is absolutely on the same level as that--whatever that level was.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I recommend this game only if you're a fan of "investigation missions". Do not approach this game if your main interests are its combats or its open world mechanics.Review in short:"Gameplay-wise and animation-wise, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden feels like playing an average game from the late PS2/early PS3 era. The game gets carried by the narrative, although that is lacking as well at times. With no innovations, this game is just a set of The Witcher 3-style investigation missions with not enough personality."Info on how I played:* Played on PC with controller* Played at Normal DifficultyPros:+ Good graphics+ Good voice acting+ Settings menu can be opened at any time+ Difficulty settings that can be changed at any time+ Photo mode, although very simple+ Possibility to remap controls+ Cannot enter other people's houses without their permission+ Changing equipment, visually changes it+ Important documents for quests have the most relevant information highlighted+ High amount of optional content+ Good endingsCons:- Clunky combat system, which feels pretty old- Very simple combat animations- Camera too close to the character and not very good- The character attacks in the direction of the camera and not that of the directional stick- No minimap- Map is not very good- Very invasive tutorials- The premise and initial world building of the game is pretty weak- Useless resources gathering mechanic- Poor skill tree system - Investigation system and mechanics are very classic and not innovative at all, feeling very repetitive not only in this game alone, but across similar games- Choices and Consequences system is very limited- The protagonist has a clear writing, and the choices throughout the game can often go in the opposite direction of it without that being addressed- Cannot compare items in shop with those currently equipped- Optional content is extremely repetitive gameplay-wiseMiscellaneous:* The game is mostly structured around self-contained investigative missions

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is surprisingly HUGE!!! It's as AAA as AA can get without actually being AAA. The day 1 experience is perfect. No bugs. Great performance. Looks great. It has DLSS 3 + HDD support + Frame Generation + Nvidia Boost.  No HDR but apart from that, all AAA features you can expect.I can recommend for the originality factor of the premise and setting although the setting lacks heavily in identity. For example you know how in God of War you pass though some linear dungeons to get to the next landmark? Well the world here mostly looks like these landmarkless dungeons but without the nordic motif. It's not bad, it's just unremarkable. But it's not a deadly sin.Also of special note is its Dark Souls quality of having a huge connected map in which usually if you can see something in the distance, you can reach it at some point. Altough it's a bit stingy with landmarks. It has enough freshness and heart to be easily recommendable especially for the asking price. Now... Is it better than its predecessor "Vampyr"? Yes, in some regards. Is it worse in some regards? Yes. I would say the most important aspect is the world and the setting of Vampyr was a bit more unique as both context and looks.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - If you want a good spooky love story wrapped around a solid game, you should absolutely give Banishers a shot.Review:Banishers was pretty much made with me in mind, oddly. Likeable protagonists a supportive, friendship-rich romance? Check. Ghosts and spookiness? Check. Investigation and mystery? Check. Incredibly solid writing and voice acting? Check. Good engine and graphics without anything remotely approaching high-end tech requirements? Check. Love to see it.As I played more, it seemed to me that one of the core themes in Banishers is this: "How selfish is love, and if you go too far to preserve it, are you still the same people who fell in love in the first place?" I'm here for it. It's not the sort of question that I've seen explored in games a lot, and I think it's a question that has a TON of room for good exploration. Add to that the fact that some of the choices made are BRUTAL (but never in a way that I found too cheap-shot-y), and it really gets on thinking about just how much love it worth, especially when set against trauma, guilt, and horror.Game-play wise, it's fun and solid, but not in any particularly ground-breaking ways. It's smooth and gets the job done, and there's a good amount of room for customization of builds in both equipment and power sets. But, at the end of the day, I would guess that people are going to be talking about the story of Banishers a LOT more than they will about game play.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to start... Don't Nod is a studio that I really like and I've always supported their games. I've played all of their games since Remember Me, but this time things are a little different. My favorite Don't Nod game is undoubtedly the Life is Strange series (especially the first game, Before the Storm and True Colors).The story and concept of the game had intrigued me since its first introduction and I couldn't wait to play it. I started the game on the first day and everything was very enjoyable, but as the time went on and I wanted to complete all the content, the game started to become more and more mediocre. Very bad fighting mechanics, a terrible maze-like map, a very bad guidance system (really, where is the minimap?), a lot of completely unnecessary game mechanics, and a game structure that becomes a complete loop after the first few hours... In fact, many mechanics are completely thrash. Why would someone add things to their game that players hate the most? Why am I always crawling between two walls? Why do I just watch for seconds during every door opening, why do I examine one object and then can't examine another object immediately while listening to the characters tell me what I have already seen? I can list many more of these...I don't want to elaborate on the subject too much, but even Vampyr was a much better game than Banishers. It seems that a situation similar to Remember Me, which caused the collapse of Don't Nod years ago, has occurred again. Unfortunately, Don't Nod aimed for a AAA-like game without considering the AA level production, budget and team, and the result is truly mediocre. However, the fact that this game is AA cannot be a defense. It should not be forgotten that the games we have seen recently, such as Alan Wake II and Assassin's Creed: Mirage, are also AA productions, but the difference is incredible... This game is mediocre in every aspect and unfortunately, unless you like the studio very much, I would never recommend you to play it (at least unless it drops to at least around $5 or $10). Please stop trying to make such games, it means the team you have is not suitable for such things. Give us more Life is Strange, and let the studios that can make these kinds of games keep making them.

_childDocuments_.review: I am utterly baffled at how anyone can give this game a good review.  This is an exceedingly bad game that is incompetently made.  It is a waste of both your time and money.  It is as if these developers not only are bad at their job…but they also must never have played a videogame before as they seem to have no concept of what bad game design is.  Thank god Deck Nine now makes the Life is Strange games, it literally feels like Life is Strange was some absurd stroke of luck for DontNod as every single game they made after Life is Strange 1 has been abysmal.Before going into why this game is an utter train wreck I guess I’ll quickly go through what is good.  You got some pretty great voice acting between the two main leads and their love story which is the central theme of the game is very well done.   The game has quite a few side quests dealing with a variety of ghost stories and they are all handled equally well…and that’s it…Sure wish those things were in a better game .To get it out of the way the first massive problem with this game, like Vampyr, is the combat is atrocious.  DontNod needs to stop making games with combat because they simply don’t know how to do it.  You know what isn’t fun?  Fighting the exact same enemy model thousands of times, having enemy hordes randomly spawn to block your path, forcing you to kill these enemy hordes to move forward, having enemies that once you kill them have a 2nd phase that you then have to kill again, after killing all those enemies having more random enemies spawn on top of those.  Jesus Christ, why would you make a game like this it’s both frustrating and boring.  It’s so bogged down in this tedious combat that after 5hrs I set it on the easiest difficulty…even then it takes forever to get passed these mobs.  DontNod needs to face reality and accept they have no idea how to do combat so take it out, you don’t have to put combat in your games.  I think it’s even worse than the combat in Vampyr.Next, don’t make an open world game when you don’t know how to design a map.  The amount of times that getting to a point on this map bordered on impossible because you put up roadblocks that required me to backtrack 20 minutes or more to then find like a secret path around a mountain or forest was beyond frustrating.  When you design an open world map…here’s a tip…don’t make it a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ maze.  It’s not fun wandering around what amounts to a giant maze where literally only one path is the correct path to the destination and everything else goes to a dead end.  Also…I don’t know…maybe if you are going to do this make instant fast travel a thing?  So you know I don’t have a find a stupid campfire to fast travel that is still miles away from where I want to be requiring me to spend 20min wandering a maze.  Similarly why in God’s name does every single quest require you to backtrack through this stupid maze every single time.  I’m not sure their was one quest where I wouldn’t have to backtrack through all of this world fighting tedious monsters to get back to where I wanted to be.  This quest design is horrendous.  This is easily the worst open world design I have encountered in all of videogames.The overall story dealing with the mystery of what caused this haunting is just not good.  While the love story is great…the rest of the plot is just bad. While the side quests tell fun little ghost stories they aren’t really mysteries.  I would describe these as quick snacks and not a full meal.  Each of these quests feels like the outline of a ghost story instead of a real story in it’s own right.  The best story is the Bligh Manor story near the end of the game…but like all others not enough time is spent on this.  Most of these stories from step 1 you know exactly what the twist is going to be and then find out about 5min later…well 5min if you discount walking 90min across a map that is a maze being bogged down in constant horde mode enemy fights.This game is also extremely linear as far as choices go.  Your choices only are useful to determine the 3 main endings you can get at the end of the game and that’s it.  When you solve a haunting you can either sacrifice the person the ghost is haunting, ascend the ghost, or banish the ghost.  To complete these quests you are just on a linear journey picking up the exact items the game directs you to pick to then confront the ghost.  It would have been massively better if instead each quest involved you talking to people finding items and making your own deductions like in one of the Sherlock Holmes games.  Then based on your deductions and the clues you found you should only get one of those options.This entire game was just poorly designed from the start.  The game should take place in just one very large town, “New Eden.”  The open world should just be one city with maybe a small amount of outskirts.  They probably should have just set it in colonial Boston.  They should have removed all combat and had it be more of an adventure game where you a searching for clues to solve these mysteries and each one should have been an actual mystery involving you talking to a variety of people in town.  The way you deal with each haunting should have immediate effects on the overall story creating branching narratives in the main story that cause different plot beats to occur.  Maybe one branching path could have been Antea doesn’t even die at the start of the game and maybe Red dies instead.  If you want to have combat like game play you could do quick time events or something for “boss” fights.   Maybe if more time had been spent on story crafting instead of this horrendous combat mechanics and bland open world this would have been a much richer game.This game is such a waste of the players time, no one should spend their time on it.  You want a great ghost haunting game play “Murdered: Soul Suspect.”  That game came out like 10 years ago and is basically this same game but a million times better.  There is also Vampire Swansong.  Another game that is far superior…that isn’t technically a ghost haunting game…but it’s a spooky game with a decent murder mystery and player choice actually having consequences.  Better yet just play Scarlet Hollow a ghost haunting visual novel with massive amounts of player choice.  Don’t waste your time on this…your life is worth more than spending countless hours backtracking through a maze to complete a quest to solve a mystery you will know the solution to from the first conversation.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn to this game due to its open world, story-telling aspects, and what seemed to be lore-rich "choices matter" content. Its combat is linear and the same throughout the game with few options to customize gameplay; I would not recommend from a gaming perspective. From a narrative standpoint, it has potential in portraying a variety of different people and moral dilemmas that arise when acting as a . That said, it is not worth the price, despite the lovely graphics. The 'open world' is a fairly linear map that guides you from one location to the next with some cartographic loops and hidden loot. It is never explained to the player what your loot from treasure boxes and stashes is. You can talk to merchants and upgrade gear, though you never have a sense of if something is useful when you discover it. The gun has infinite ammo but there is a limited amount of leather for crafting -- suspend your belief for not only ghost banishing but also for any other random aspect as it appears in the game via Deus ex Machina. I sincerely wanted to enjoy this game, but I have felt it more of a chore to get through a novel rather than a decent game that interests me. Perhaps this review will inform your decision moving forward. c:Prior to purchasing, I read the positive and negative reviews; I'd suggest reading more thorough negative reviews for more info -- I do regret getting this game and I would not recommend this game at its price at $50 USD. I would wait for a sale approximately ~ $15 to $20. Best of luck and godspeed, gamer. o7

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of this game is great. It's got occult case-solving aspects reminiscent of The Witcher, combo-laden combat reminiscent of God of War, and the morally grey variety of community-pillar NPCs we've come to know from Vampyr. The voice acting and dialogue are solid, and Red and Antea's story is an absolute beautiful tragedy. As it stands though, this might've been a better concept for a TV series.The world is too big for the story, the combat and puzzles are ridiculously repetitive, there are too many  collectibles, and the bulk of the side quests feel unrewarding I could've finished this 20 hours earlier if I weren't so invested in loot-hunting. Eventually I ran out of side-quests to lace in-between and I gave up after finding 90% of the collectibles. If they make a New Game Plus or a post-game DLC I'll happily go snatch the rest of it and watch a different ending; but there's NO way I'm replaying the first half of the game without a decent gear setup again, I'm not interested in redoing the root-shooting puzzles, and I want an option to kill every NPC the minute they open their mouths. "Oh your loved one / neighbor was upset and now they're a ghost and moving your stuff around?"*stabs all of New Eden*  Also? The difficulty level should be WITH or WITHOUT Antea. She does ALL the DPS. Story thru Very Hard just means more punches to enemies that are already way too resilient for ghosts. If Vampyr let you drink blood or not drink blood, why wasn't there a design to be possessed or  be possessed? Overall, some really solid RPG elements here that were watered down by a bland open world, lack of combat variety, and lazy side-quest writing. It looks, sounds, and acts like a AAA-game; if you do the main quests and ignore everything else. If you spend an extra day running around searching for more, it'll be hollow and lifeless - like a ghost.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eagerly anticipating a game like this for quite some time, and I must say, it doesn't disappoint. From its captivating gameplay to its immersive storytelling, Banishers offers an experience reminiscent of some of my favorite titles like Tomb Raider, Vampyr, and the new Jedi series.Venturing through its semi-open world, unlocking new areas as you progress, provides a sense of discovery that keeps you engaged from start to finish. While the combat may not pose a significant challenge, even on the hardest difficulty setting, it remains satisfying, especially with the strategic depth offered by the skill tree system.Speaking of the skill tree, it's a joy to experiment with different abilities and tailor them to suit your playstyle, fostering a sense of personalization and strategic synergy. And let's not forget the gripping narrative, which delves deep into the human condition, unveiling dark truths and moral dilemmas that leave a lasting impact.The inclusion of moral choices further enhances the narrative depth, forcing players to question their decisions and grapple with shades of gray. Plus, the dynamic world, shaped by your choices, ensures that each playthrough feels unique, with different side quests and outcomes awaiting depending on your actions.For completionists, there's no shortage of collectibles to hunt down, offering hours of additional gameplay for those who enjoy exploring every nook and cranny. And on the technical side, smooth performance and stability ensure a seamless experience, allowing you to fully immerse yourself in the game world.However, despite its many strengths, there's a glaring issue that prevents me from wholeheartedly recommending it. A frustrating bug halts progression entirely during a critical side quest, effectively blocking access to the rest of the area and essential collectibles. Despite reports from the community, the lack of response or acknowledgment from the developers is disappointing and leaves a bitter taste.Until this issue is addressed, I can't in good conscience recommend Banishers to others, especially considering its premium price point.Nevertheless, if you're willing to overlook this setback or aren't fussed about completing every aspect of the game, there's still plenty to enjoy here. Just be aware of the potential roadblock ahead.PS:The bug was reported on reddit a week ago.And on steam there is a post too, though not that old:

_childDocuments_.review: All in it's a good game. Worth playing if you enjoy story driven adventures with combat thrown in along the way.It is rough around the edges, and several of the systems don't feel all that well thought through. It is VERY slow to start. But after a few hours, it will begin to grow on you. You'll learn that you can essentially ignore the shop dynamic, and you'll be overstocked with resources soon enough. You won't really need to go too far out of your way for decent gear, so you won't be so heavily invested in the sidequest required to unbound the witch chests.You'll find the enemies pretty repetitive, frankly. And after the 100th wave fighting the exact same enemies with essentially the same combination of moves (don't worry the game gives you interesting new ways to fight over time) you'll realize the combat isn't why you're playing.Nor are the "haunting cases." Or the exploration. It eventually becomes a matter of progressing the story, and making incremental progress along the way. Sure, you could grind out some elites, or poke into every corner and try to 100% every chest. But none of that is really all that compelling, or worth it.I assume I'll finish the game, but after nearly 30 hours I can say it's an interesting game that gets you invested enough in the story that you'll keep going, despite the incomplete feeling that many of its mechanics give off.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a lovely game, with a very well written story. The main characters are both likeable and interesting, and the premise itself is a breath of fresh air, personally. Even the overarching villain is sympathetic, and the side characters are distinct and memorable.The combat isn't going to stack up to God of War, but it has enough nuance that there are multiple different builds that can be made, only suffering from a lack of enemy diversity. It's perfectly acceptable, however, especially for a story-driven game, and in that department, it delivers.I would definitely recommend, it was easy to put near thirty hours into one run, and I by no means did anywhere near everything. I'd hazard a 100% run would go 50-60 hours, which justifies the price of 50 dollars. Of course, if it is on sale, grab it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a tremendous story line, and great side-stories. If that's what you're looking for in a game, this is it. It also has interesting combat, particular in its "arenas" of sorts, where quirky rules apply (for example, you do more damage the less health you have).Saying that, however, be aware that this is a Don't Nod game, so expect 21st century issues to crop up in 17th century America, particularly LGBTQ+ characters that simply would not have existed in that era, since the consequences of discovery would have been a capital offense.Make sure, by the way, that you buff up ranged combat, since many boss fights, particularly the last one, are very difficult via melee.Also, make sure you do all these "arenas" such as nests, elites and even scourges, since they significantly add buffs to your attributes. I initially avoided doing them, so a couple of the initial bosses were harder than they needed to be.By the way, take your time and upgrade your character and your equipment before advancing the main quest line. I found the first boss after leaving the initial town to be too challenging, since I rushed into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Jusant and I was hoping this was another surprise from Don't Nod.- First things first, lip sync, voice acting and motion capture: if you don't have these 3 things is better to hide it somehow, without making a dialogue heavy game, Banishers is often gorgeous to look at it but unfortunately the expressions of the characters are super bland and the voice acting of the protagonists is off.- Combat feel rushed, enemies attacks are difficult to telegraph and most of the time is just spam attack to stun lock anything, maybe in the late game you have enough abilities to make combat fun but in the first hours is really really boring to fight 2 types of enemies and spam "RB/RT".Give the players more abilities from the start!- Movement feel unpolished, you have a walk animation but as soon you tilt the analog stick the protagonist make a really weird move like from completely still to full running. The animation should pass from still to walk to run, at least in the houses.-/? The "investigation areas" are just like "find the only right thing to go on", there's really nothing to investigate but ok, even Witcher 3 make it so boring and everybody like it, so maybe I'm the problem.- If you have only few animations of climbing don't make so many climbing moments, it feels cheap to see it again and again with just a change of camera perspective when you climb down. More little single button climb, less walls climb.+ Moral choices are super interesting and they will be a core part of the ending I think, I was hoping to see this even for the first quest not after 2-3h of gameplay.+ Graphics and settings are super good, especially the texture of the models and the dresses.+ The core idea of splitting the protagonists is original and I loved it, just change the initial combat possibilities of Altea, spamming RB endlessly is so boring that I avoided using her.

_childDocuments_.review: The demo felt like an entirely different game from the actual game itself- if you like a detective based game, this is more for you. However, for a game that preaches multiple choices and endings, it really feels like they are forcing one narrative, and it's not as open world as it may seem. _childDocuments_.review: DON'T NOD never fails to deliver. I also played Vampyr back on PS4 which was a very good game aswell.I needed somewhat like 36 hours to finish the game however I stopped collecting everything the game has to offer when I was half way through it because I just wanted to enjoy the stories new eden without the feeling of "work" as some of you may know from Ubisoft open world titles.- Graphics are good, I really like the art style they choose for new eden and the game as a whole. Atmospheric and immersive.- Performance is good. Maxed out everything and had constant 120 FPS in most regions however some are not that good optimized  and fps dropped to 70 in rare cases which is still fine for me. Played the game on 2K with DLSS activated.- Audio Design is good.I like the music and the sound FX in general. However they could have used more diverse music and maybe more emotional music at some scenes to make them even more dramatic/atmospheric.- Gameplay feels good.The game has a somewhat similar approach like the newer god of war titles have. Which is not bad. It works good even if not as good as in god of war but when it comes to fights you can still work on a build you create in your head and once you try to play that specific build and it works it feels really satisfying. Maybe I should have raised the difficulty because I was already giga strong. Even Boss fights were easy but after Malenia from Elden Ring every Boss fight is easy anyway lol.Puzzles for loot or interesting stuff were also included and were fun most of the time.There are however some gameplay mechanics I didn't like. BACKTRACKING. As much as I can understand the reason behind such a decision I just don't like to be forced to go back in areas that are partly locked because you don't have the mechanic you need to progress at this time. Additionally enemies spawn over and over again when you revisit these places which mostly have the same level as they had before. Not sure if they scaled but even if they did these fights felt like artificially lengthen the game. I also wanted to skip these fights but you simply can't most of the time because these enemies chase you to the moon if you could go there. You are basically forced to fight them.Questmarkers were confusing aswell sometimes and I ended up at places I didn't want to go because I thought it was the correct path to my destiny.- Story telling was insanely goodThe stories from new eden are dark, gritty, everyone has secrets and there is no black and white. You always feel being in a struggle when it comes to decision making. Especially because of the main narrative but I don't want to spoil things. The dialogues are plausible most of the time and german synch was really good aswell as most of the facial animations. Some NPCs must have been on a metal festival cuz of their head shaking but overall it was fine. I loved how they handled the dialogues. A lot of different camera perspectives, changing constantly while in a dialogue which have it a really nice atmosphere.Also: Your decisions have consequences. And I mean CONSEQUENCES. If you end up being in disgrace for some NPCs you even have to pay more for goods. But there is more..Without spoiling: I was really satisfied with the ending I got and it feld good. However it felt a little bit rushed. When I reflect on all the dialogues and preparation for the ending it feels like they could have used more time for the ending. Being able to meet some NPCs afterwards for example. My ending screamed like "OKAY WHEN COMES BANISHERS 2?". I doubt we will ever see one but I would be down for a new adventure with Red and...Would give a solid 8/10Very good game and I hope DON'T NOD keeps being an amazing developer studio.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and voice acting was excellent in this game, as expected from Don’t Nod however the game falls short in every other way. Skill tree is mostly just passive abilities around a small set of combat skills, many of them have trade offs which makes it feel like a linear progression rather than actually becoming more powerful as you progress. That said there are a handful of new moves you get throughout the game, but they were not enough to keep the combat feeling fresh, at least for me. Puzzles are not challenging and don’t add to the game, they are just tedious and time consuming. The story and its side missions could’ve been told just as effectively in half the time. The game strives to be like other open world games which just want you to spend as much time in game completing arbitrary activities and checking off question marks on the map. Unfortunately my grievances with these issues even made me feel rather apathetic towards the story even though that was the one high point for the game. Maybe others will enjoy the combat and exploration more than I did. I wouldn’t even recommend this game on deep sale. It’s just altogether way too tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and most of the side content.  The story, voice acting and motion capture are excellent.  Many NPC side storylines branch in interesting ways.The combat is middling, and not as good as  Jedi Survivor, which seems to be the main inspiration for both traversal and combat/progression, but not as polished.  There seem to be major performance issues in the engine with the open world being hidden by many more arbitrary and annoying “slow down” barriers (where Jedi Survivor might have one every five minutes, this would have one every 20 seconds of traversal)  - twisty narrow passageways, logs to jump over, gaps to jump over, line of sight blocking hills etc.The world/monster design is mediocre because of it.  No grand vistas. Can’t see mobs until they spawn on top of you in obvious mini arenas.  The same mobs over and over despite the interesting corpse possession riffs (there’s only one animal, wolf), and traversal is horrendous.  It has no stakes, no real platforming (all jumps are perfect when prompted, you cannot otherwise scale a low fence) and simply wastes your time.  Exploration is not rewarding at all.As a smaller, linear game without side content and traversal it would have been an easy recommend but this has been bloated into Assassin Creed Valhalla levels of pointlessness, but without anything nice to look at while you’re running around or meaningful side activity like base building.A tight sequel would be great without all the nonsense sprint/ slow /sprint/ slow traversal.As it is, for the same money Jedi Survivor is a much better game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 6 hours into the story and it feels like I have a lot to do still, you do get your moneys worth I would say.The story is amazing, you get to know the two characters early on and also their main objective while you follow them on their journey. It is emotional and does a really good job dragging you into the story. Playing as the two banishers is fun, you have some side quests to complete outside of the main story. For me, it is some of the best side quests I've played, they're long and the investigations are always fun and you become interested in the characters you help.The environment is beautiful and eye catching, there is a lot of exploring while you're on the quests and usually it could become boring but not in this game. This game does an excellent job at keeping you interested with the help of the environment around you, the different obstacles, the scenery and different elements around you.Overall I give this game a 8.5/10, which is rare these days by my standards. I searched long and hard on Steam for a story driven game that captures everything that I mentioned above, and I haven't had this much fun since the Assassin's Creed days. The price could be better but honestly, with the pricing nowadays I would say it is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Narrative game, very well done lore and engaging side stories with well written quests and their conclusions. It is also quite hard to make choices, and will simply depend on your personality or the outcome you wish to achieve. But the combat, OH GOD the combat. It is absolutely dreadful. It is just one step away from the combat of the Gothic Games. Not similar to them, just almost as bad. For example blocking an attack gives no marker, meaning you can not judge when you have blocked an attack. Enemies have no stagger stat, so you can not stagger them long enough to feel meaningful, just push them slightly with heavy attacks. Parrying an attack only parries the first attack hit, so if more enemies surround you, you will still get hit. Combat feels like you are hitting wind, there are only 6 types of enemies the whole game and you fight constantly.Last but not least although the writing in quests is great, the quest mechanic is pathetic. You talk to an NPC, select all blue lines in chatbox. enter their home go through their stuff, find out one more thing is missing, go to the world map to one place where that thing is located, find a ghost, talk to them and you make a decision. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. No diviation, no investigation, no nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Incredible game for those who enjoy storytelling, immersion, and ambiance. Combat leaves some to be desired but not bad. Highly recommend picking this up, especially if you're a fan of Horizon, God of War, Plague Tale, etc. If you're looking for constant action, this probably isn't it. Ignore the negative reviews talking about "wokeness", they just don't like that Antea isn't a helpless damsel and is her own character. Overall I had high hopes for this game from when it was announced. I'm glad to say Don't Nod absolutely delivered on my hopes. I love story-rich games and Banishers really shines in its storytelling. The main story is great and really interesting. Ghost stories in colonial New England is a setting we haven't really had and it lends itself really well to the story the devs want to tell. Each individual haunting you investigate has it's own great writing you discover by finding clues to piece together to find out what is causing the haunting before deciding how to bring closure to the haunted/ghost. It's pretty simple "find object, press A to investigate" but the writing really makes up for it once you start finding clues. I appreciate that by the end of each haunting, the decision on how to bring closure (banish a violent/cruel ghost, give peace to a ghost that's been trapped in the mortal realm, or blame the living and sacrifice them) actually has nuance and I can absolutely see that each choice has a legitimate argument The art style, environments, and writing just perfectly blend to create an atmosphere where you're really living in this haunted colony. Few games have really drawn me into the setting the way Banishers has. Combat feels similar to God of War/Ragnarok while missing a little bit of the fluidity and polish. I do enjoy the mechanic of switching between Red and Antea to tackle different encounters. Certain enemies take more damage from Red vs. Antea so you're switching on the fly and the buildcrafting can synergize with that. Overall not bad, but could use some work to string the animation a bit smoother. There's a bit of buildcrafting/upgrades to try and tweak the combat to fit your preferred style. I'm enjoying it in the early-ish game so I imagine it will only get better as I level up.

_childDocuments_.review: Banishers is an absolute disaster in every aspect. Do not recommend buying even with a generous discount.The map is a pseudo-open GoW-like world with a lot of grind. Oh boy, grinding in this game provides more joy than the actual story/side quest completion.There are no decisions which "carry dramatic consequences". There is a lack of choices instead. Existing banish/spare decisions have zero consequences except for the last cut-scene. And there are no other types of choices, even in side quests. You wander through a static world with a static scripted story with only an illusion of choice.Moreover, there are no "dramatic consequences" at all. All the decisions (i.e. those are only banishing or sparing) affect the final cut scene and nothing more. The individuals you banish or spare trigger no events even in the village they were/are living in, not speaking of the overall game world. That said, no one in this game gives a single solid reaction if a good half of a village is banished or stopped being haunted. Any changes in the world are strictly scripted and bound to the storyline triggers.Again, Banishers pretends to be a story-driven RPG despite explicitly mocking the player when a "bad" or "incorrect" choice is made in the scope of "social justice" problems. There are no depictions of the actual consequences but only boo-hoo dialogues when everyone tells Red how bad he is because of acting wrong. This is a perfect example of a game where DEI made the characters, story progression, and quests way beyond miserable.Banishers runs on Unreal 5. It is a disgrace to ship such visuals with Unreal 5.It's not a story-driven action RPG. It's not even an RPG at all.

_childDocuments_.review: After sleeping on it after beating the game - Yes I would recommend the game.I will echo a lot of positive and negative reviews that the weakest parts are:- The combat.- The poor fast travel system.  After about 20-30 hours you will get upset by the lack of fast travel points.  You can only travel to and from campfires - I wish that changed even if only at the end game where you can fast travel from anywhere- The economy, I found no reason to use a store for anything outside of buying a new weapon or armor for the underlying achievement.However I will stress just like most if not all positive reviews say that the lore, story and voiced dialogue to name a few are complete standouts.  You get a lot but you will wish there were more which is a sign of good writing and delivery.I personally would have structured the story a little different.  More quiet times like you're getting to the end.  More dread for one or both of the main characters when you're almost finished.  Also, I would have changed the power game where Antea would start out very strong and she gets weaker if you choose the ascension path and weaker and gets stronger if you choose the ressurection path - it would add more depth to the storytelling.The game does suffer a lot from mechanics from yesteryear; slow unskippable or speed-up-able elevator sequences (similar to OG Mass Effect 1), tunnels and cliff sides and the like you need to go in and out of all the time that slow down your progress.  Yes!  It's realistic or normal in real life but doing it many many many times over when combined with the above mentioned poor (over time) fast travel really eats up your time.  Most of the time spent is just trying to get from Point A to Point B, going through obstacles and non-escapable battles slow you down.The game also asks you to make choices that punish you if you actually role play correctly or make grey decisions.  You almost have to go full evil or full good on every playthrough else you will potentially ruin your ending.  Its VERY similar to Mass Effect 1 again where making neutral decisions punished you in gameplay; you had to go full or near full Paragon or Renegade to get the abilities/skills and armor.  Not going full paragon or renegade would lock you out of decisions or endings as well.However the good overwhelming outshines these issues - I was extreamly engrossed in the storytelling, the lore and the actors performances to forgive all of this.  It also has a theme that absolutely resonates me because I do believe I have thanatophobia and seeing how Red goes through his emotions with the concept of loss and grief was very compelling for me.Narratively it is a 5 out of 5 for me but overall it's a 4 out of 5 due to the above negative blemishes.  If you enjoy story driven games I absolutely would recommend this; if it helps put the game on story/easy and breeze through the combat and just enjoy one of the best, well told stories in years.4 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: I was really surprised by this game!This game has that God of War 2018 feeling where you have this open world and you can explore various areas, do side missions, fight some bosses, take out collectible just like Odin's ravens and more. The gameplay is really fun with it mostly being meele but at a later point you get a rifle which really helps. You also play as the female character who later on gets a variety of abilities that is really awesome to use and at points are OP. It does suffer the same issues that God of War 2018 did which is fighting the same kind of enemies over and over. You also fight some mini bosses which are basically the same enemies you fought earlier with higher health bar and who take less damage. So that can get annoying at times especially when you are just exploring and from out of nowhere 4 enemies spawn who are the exact same as the last 4 fights you had.The story is really gripping and it has been made better with stellar performances by the main characters, that being Red Mac Raith and Antea. Their relationship is really strong and you see that throughout the game. Everyone you interact with has their own stories, especially if you do the side missions. Their stories are really fun to explore. _childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games where I wish there was a neutral or mixed option, but there's not. So I'll go with "not recommended" because I would literally not recommend it, though I would not try to dissuade you either if you're interested.The game is mediocre in a lot of ways, there's a great many aspects that work just fine, but it's missing that final point to push it over the line into good or great territory. I'll give a few examples of what I mean.Enemy variety - There's not a lot of enemy types, even if you include bosses and they are only 3 types really change up your gameplay. Every battle outside of big boss fights feel exactly the same because of this.Combat controls - It works fine, but doesn't really flow well. Like dodging and attacking will result in a special dodge-attack, that doesn't chain into your regular attack chain, so you get an awkward half second where your character has to "reset" before beginning the new attack chain.Fast travel - If you're a completionist like me, you'll be doing a lot of running back and forth, lots of climbing, shimmying and crawling. There are fast travel-points but you have to run back to them every time you want to use one and that makes for a lot of running back and forth, broken up by meaningless ambushes by specters.Haunting cases - It really is the selling point of the game, solving the haunting cases and they are fine and good. They even change based on your choices in the main storyline. But the conclusions are not very satisfying, there's not much ambiguity to them. You essentially get 3 choices when you solve a case, ascend the ghost (good afterlife, heaven), banish the ghost (bad afterlife, hell) or blame the haunted person (rip out their soul and banish them). In the VAST majority of cases, there's really only one correct choice because the choice is so obvious and it's almost always Ascend, because how bloody cruel do you have to be to warrant an eternity in hell?The main characters - Red I quite like, he's a good relatable man and his voice actor does an excellent job. But I really dislike Antea, she's arrogant and constantly doubts and belittle Reds ability. Not like she's overtly doing so, but it's a lot of small comments and the way she acts. Like "I can't manifest, will you be fine on your own?", "I would've used a different ritual" (after telling me there were specters, so i used a specter summoning ritual, but I needed to use a Scourge summoning ritual), "Stop hogging all the fun" the list goes on. It's even more grating when she speaks to Red during conversations, like Red will be speaking to Jacob and Antea will pause the conversation and comment to Red and you're just sitting there imagining the conversation from Jacobs perspective, because he can't see Antea. He's having a conversation and Red just occasionally spaces out for several seconds. And when an NPC can see ghosts, Antea takes center stage constantly, pushing Red to the back. I get that she's the master banisher and he's the apprentice, but they are also a couple and it really doesn't seem like she respects him in the field. It also doesn't help that her voice actor is flat as a board, no doubt she was instructed to be calm, cool and stoic, but she sounds very bland because of it. The polar opposite of Red who injects a lot of character and flavor into his delivery.Themes - The game will occasionally tell you that racism was rife and prevalent at the time, being black was a horrible existence at the time. But there's only really 2 out and out racists, nobody hassle Red for being with a black woman and nobody who can see Antea seems to mind her being black. There is a disconnect between what the game is telling me and what it's showing me. I recognize that it'd be deeply annoying if racism was a constant throughout. The same holds true for misogyny, you'll be told that women aren't respected but see plenty of female leaders, shopkeepers and barely a soul actually bringing up gender.It's not a bad game by any stretch and there certainly are plenty of positives. The setting is interesting, the equipment is very meaningful to your playstyle, the skill tree is quite good, the game looks and feels good, no loading screens outside of fast travel, a good variety of locations, the haunting cases are interesting (even if the moral choice at the end isn't really a choice), Red's voice acting.There's just a lot of small things holding me back from recommending it. If you're in it for the story and don't mind the repetitive combat, you'll probably get your moneys worth from Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden.

_childDocuments_.review:
New Eden, 1695. Antea Duarte and Red mac Raith are lovers and Banishers, ghost-hunters who vowed to protect the living from the threat of lingering ghosts and specters. Following a disastrous last mission, Antea is fatally wounded, becoming one of the spirits she loathes. In the haunted wilds of North America, the couple desperately searches for a way to liberate Antea from her new plight.

Immerse yourself in a beautiful, intimate and powerful story between two fated lovers. As Banishers, enter the lives of New Eden's communities and solve haunting cases in a mystical, lore-rich world plagued with supernatural creatures and ancient secrets. Use your wits or combine Antea's spiritual powers and Red's arsenal to defeat and banish the souls tormenting the living.

detailed_description: Evil Dead: The Game - GOTY Edition The Game of the Year Edition of Evil Dead: The Game includes content from 6 DLC packs, including the new “Ash vs Evil Dead” “Who’s Your Daddy” DLC, and more at a discounted rate: • Survivors: David, Mia, The Blacksmith, Ruby, and Brock • Demon: Schemer - Featuring the notorious Baal as the demon boss • Ash S-Mart Uniform Outfit • Ash Gallant Knight Outfit • Ash Savini Alternate Outfit • Ash Williams College Outfit • Ash Williams Hunter Outfit • Ash S-Mart Halloween Outfit • Ash Sellsword Outfit • Ash Party Animal Outfit • Ash Ashy Slashy Outfit • Amanda Duty Calls Outfit • Annie Knowby Explorer Outfit • Cheryl Williams Browntown Outfit • Ed Getley Explorer Outfit • Gilded Attire costume pack for the Necromancer Demon army • Henry The Red’s Scottish Vibe Outfit • Henry the Red: Red Pikeman Outfit • Henry the Red: Berserker Cosplay Outfit • Kelly Scourge of Evil Outfit • Lord Arthur Battle Prep Outfit • Lord Arthur Rightful King Outfit • Mia Demon Slayer Outfit • Pablo Fish and Chips Outfit • Pablo El Brujo Outfit • Puppeteer Demon King of the White Frost Costume Pack • Scotty College Outfit • Warlord Demon Firefighter-Themed Costume Pack About the Game The ultimate Evil Dead multiplayer experience is here… and it’s groovy! Step into the shoes of Ash Williams or his friends from the iconic Evil Dead franchise and work together in a game loaded with over-the-top co-op and PVP multiplayer action! Play as a team of four survivors, exploring, looting, managing your fear, and finding key items to seal the breach between worlds in a game inspired by all three original Evil Dead films as well as the STARZ original Ash vs Evil Dead television series. Iconic Characters - Play as characters from throughout the Evil Dead universe, including Ash, Scotty, Lord Arthur, Kelly Maxwell, & more, with new dialogue performed by Bruce Campbell & others! Play As Good or Evil - Fight for the forces of good or take control of the Kandarian Demon to hunt Ash & others while possessing Deadites, the environmental objects & more as you seek to swallow their souls! Off-the-Wall Visuals - Whether you’re tearing a Deadite in 2 with Ash's chainsaw hand or flying across the map as the Kandarian Demon, realistic visuals & physics-based gore brings the horror to life! This...Is My Boomstick - Brandish your double barrel shotgun, chainsaw, cleavers and more to do some delightfully gruesome violence against the armies of darkness. Splatter Royale - Choose Deadite versions of any Survivors and Demons from the game in this battle royale–style game mode. Use your wits and weapons to duke it out to the last person standing in fast-paced, cutthroat action for up to 40 players!

_childDocuments_.review: This may not be the dream game I've been looking for but it's a nice love letter to all things Evil Dead. Someday we'll get a full drop in drop out style co-op game against dozens of deadites but until then this is the best we have outside playing fully modded L4D2. What we have is decent enough but true co-op from the ground up would be nice. We already have all the ingredients we need from Saber's WWZ and Insurgency: Sandstorm. I am a huge fan of this series so it makes sense I would have this in my library. This is the greatest gift I've ever received and am thankful to own the whole GOTY package will all the content. This is still being updated and the playerbase is pretty hardcore at the moment coming off the one year Epig exclusivity. I love all the visuals and the shot for shot remakes of all my fav characters and locations. The singleplayer content is actually pretty fun covering different moments through the films and show. I can stretch something like this to hundreds of hours no doubt and I am looking forward to the future of this title or any future titles. We have all the ultraviolence as well as the dark humor. A masterpiece in so many ways. Playing versus with randoms is also pretty damn entertaining and with all the content around there is a high replayability rate. I highly recommend this now that it is on Steam and if you are a die hard fan of Evil Dead. The servers are a little sketchy though and you may disconnect a lot.This is the best thing to ever happen in a long time. Been waiting since 2013 for a game like this. Easily 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so badly to give this game a positive review. It is a great homage to the Evil Dead franchise. It has the dark humor, fully voiced characters with the original actors providing the voices, iconic locations, and it has (or rather, had) the potential to really be something amazing. I am a huge fan of the series, which is why I bought this in the first place. But then Saber Interactive abandoned development for it, only a year and four months after launching it. And since it is one of those always online / needs official servers and a connection to play type deals, it is on borrowed time and life support until they inevitably pull the plug on that, too. I found this game's take on asymmetrical play to be a refreshing change from stale Dead by Daylight, as it feels something like a blend of DbD, Overwatch, and L4D2. There are objectives and points to find and hold, a map to explore and loot, you can fight back instead of just passively running, and there's an ever present demon hounding your steps, gaining strength over time. That being said, it suffers from the same issues almost all asymmetrical games have, those being balance issues, toxic sweaty players, grinds, people who don't understand team play (run off by themselves and die), and being very rough for those just starting. As a consequence of little to no communication or support from the developer, queue times and exploits have become an issue as well.  Saber never should have gotten this IP, since they did the absolute bare minimum for advertising and updates and are dumping it once they got their cash. Being an Epic exclusive for a year didn't help things either. With some TLC this could have been, and still could be, a really great game. Its rough around the edges and it has its issues, but there's potential. I had a lot of fun with it, and Evil Dead deserved so much better than this. I wish another studio would pick it up. But alas, it seems destined for the same early grave that so many of these IP-based asymmetrical horror games end up in. If only this had been made into a proper single player game, or at least have a single player mode. Even allowing for unofficial servers to keep it alive longer would be -something-, but Saber has clearly washed their hands of it. Disappointing as hell. The wheels have fallen off. I'm so sick of this happening.If you are a big Evil Dead fan, I.. want to tell you to give it a try, because you'll probably really like it, but you'd be throwing your money at an abandoned game. As such, I cannot recommend this, as much as I want to. Feels bad, man. A lot of people worked hard to make this happen. I hope Saber goes bankrupt like its garbage parent company so it can never inflict this on another IP and player base.

_childDocuments_.review: Stupid decisions made by the developers caused this game to die.The combat mechanics resemble what I had hoped for in Dead Island: you can dodge, use melee weapons, and shoot with guns. (You'll need to employ all these skills when facing hordes of enemies on your own or dealing with sub-bosses.)However, I find the finishing moves broken: you don't take any damage during the animations, which can be abused. (Implementing finishers after a certain number of kills would have been a better choice.)I particularly enjoy how the game encourages survivors to stay together through the fear mechanic.The addition of missions made me wish for something similar in Dead by Daylight.Unfortunately, I couldn't play online due to the game's dead player base, which is a shame. I noticed there are three game modes available, including the missions. You can also play against AI  either solo or with friends, but it can get repetitive once you become too skilled for the AI.In its current state, I can't recommend this game due to its dead player base, as I mentioned earlier.
