_childDocuments_.review: Evil Dead. It’s one of the most beloved franchises in cinematic history. Nearly every Evil Dead related production becomes an instant classic that receives a widely positive reception, and Evil Dead: The Game is no bloody exception. If my playtime doesn’t make it obvious, I’m a  fan of the franchise and I know the lore better than I know my own father (I’ll find you one day, pops).I can proudly say that the original development team absolutely nailed their research, and the passion really shows. This game was made by Evil Dead fans, chainsaws down. The atmosphere, appearance, behavior, and personality of Evil Dead is flourishing with its diverse cast of playable characters, brilliant maps, and deadites alike. Characters also have their backgrounds expanded through audio recordings, texts, and playable scenarios. Seeing icons like Scotty & Henry The Red return to get even with the Kandarian Demon is an absolute joy. The reasoning behind the Survivors’ returns makes sense within the Evil Dead universe. Having been resurrected by Professor Knowby in this timeline, as their past and future battles with the dead are foretold in the Necronomicon. The world itself is  with film, TV, and even comic-accurate locations, and the attention to detail is quite impressive. While there is a complete lack of a campaign, what’s there is still incredibly well done. The only question I have is, “Where is Chet?”.Time to discuss the big mother, The Gameplay. The meat & potatoes of any game. Evil Dead: The Game is one of those titles that can be very challenging to get into, especially when you’re up against a more experienced player(s). However, once you’ve mastered the art of kicking ass – it’s extremely rewarding both as a Survivor or a Demon. The intended mode to play is 4 Survivor Players versus 1 Demon Player, that is where my focus will be. There’s a lot of ground to cover here, considering Survivors have four classes to choose from and every individual Survivor & Demon has their own unique abilities. Survivors can play as a Leader (balanced), Warrior (melee), Hunter (ranged), and Support (healing). They all play very differently and a successful team will usually have a player from each class. Playing as the Demon is more cut-and-dry as you’re flying solo, so choosing the Demon that suits your playstyle is pretty straightforward.Matches begin with a scramble for recovery items, weapons, upgrade points (Pink F), and supply chests. After gearing up, Survivors search for map pieces to locate two key items that need to be collected in order to battle the Dark Ones and vanquish the Evil, all while the Demon player hunts them down between setting traps, spawning deadites, and even possessing vulnerable Survivors. It’s a loop that surprisingly doesn’t get old, not in my case at least. The combat itself is a bloody good time, it’s the root of my addiction. Melee battles have a rock-paper-scissors feel with light/heavy attacks, dodges, stuns, combos, and brutal finishers. It’s buttery smooth and just so much fun slaughtering an army of deadites while listening to that chainsaw ripping & tearing. Popping off the Boomstick or a revolver to dish out some major damage never stops being satisfying. Even playing as a support and keeping your team in the fight with area healing and useful abilities is a great time. Taking on any Demon-possessed deadite or boss unit by yourself is generally a feat that only the most veteran players can possibly achieve. You really do need your team in this game, although it’s not  to pull off some impressive victories on your own or as a duo. Granted, it’s not perfect. Stun-locking can be a prevalent issue and there’s a handful of bugs & exploits that never got fixed. Not to mention, hackers. Yeah, there’s sadly  of them. Some of which, I have been recording & reporting consistently for 2 years and no action has been taken to ban them from ruining the game – forcing me to keep a ‘blacklist’ of names to not play with. Apart from that, the gameplay itself feels great and its endless fun when you’ve got good players on both sides. The vehicles are garbage though, they’ll flip over from a windy fart.I can’t give enough props to the original development team for being so faithful to Evil Dead. Everything from the weapon sound effects, to the deadites, to the music, and of course the voice acting is superb. The fact that they brought back  original actor they could to perform their respective characters is amazing. Hearing Hal Delrich back as Scotty, and my ex-girlfriend Lucy Lawless back as Ruby just gets me all giddy. Even the substitutes for the actors that couldn’t reprise their roles do a great job of portraying the characters. And of course, Bruce Campbell reprising different versions of Ash from the past 40 years. Apart from that – the deadites sound like deadites, the guns go boom, and the chainsaw goes ‘groovy’. The soundtrack deserves its own shoutout. It’s perfectly crafted, gives every situation more intensity and by God, it’s as Evil Dead as it gets. My only criticism is that there’s a  amount of dialogue that is locked & doesn’t play in-game because there’s cursing, which I thought was a very childish move on the developer’s end. Excuse me while I cut off this gas station clerk’s head with a chainsaw but thank goodness he didn’t say the F-word. Grow a pair, Saber.I had modest expectations in terms of the graphics, but hot diggity dog! It’s strange to say, but Evil Dead: The Game is one of the most visually impressive games that I’ve played. The attention to detail is outstanding. From the incredible sunset vistas to the over-the-top gore effects, down to the fabric of your character’s shirt flapping in the wind – it’s hauntingly beautiful. Character models are faithful to the actors’ appearances (mostly), deadites look exactly as they should (although they do lack variety), and the world itself is so detailed, it’s like the developers were on set during filming. There’s also randomized times of day/night and weather events for each match. It’s not perfect – there’s some mucky textures, a near total lack of facial animations, and blood/gore/corpses disappear in seconds, nullifying much of the carnage. I could nitpick but overall, it’s a dashingly handsome game. Hail to the Chin.Right off the bat, the learning curve is steep now since the majority of the playerbase are now seasoned veterans that have been playing since release. This can be a  challenging game to pickup as a new player but you will get better each time you play as you learn how to time your dodges, predict the opposing players actions, and prioritize more important goals. Contrary to what people say, this is a pretty well-balanced game, with the exception of OP Baal. There’s a lot more I want to say, but Steam has a character limit of 8,000 and I’m about to hit it.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔸  Evil Dead: The Game also addresses the problem people have with these types of games where the survivors are often helpless against the bad guys. As Tommy Jarvis is no match for Jason Voorhees' machete, and victims can only pray that Sadako doesn't crawl out of the well behind the static of the TV, your only real option is to run away from your pursuer on Friday the 13th and be dead by day. But Ash Williams, ably voiced by lead actor Bruce Campbell in Evil Dead: The Game, doesn't have a freaky chainsaw arm for anything. You can, and should, give absolute hell when you see the dead. You'll find axes, hammers, pistols, shotguns, and rifles around the map, and here they don't just stun the enemy, they kill them outright.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER:As you can see I've made the review and played the game for few additional hours. It is because the game is very fun and I was wrong - it just has a terrible first impression moment. I'm planning on making a simple video explaining basic confusing mechanisms this game has to offer because I believe tutorials are not doing a good job. Once I do this I'll delete this review.I've made this review before learning about leveling with spirit points. It indeed makes leveling process much, much faster. There's no hint or tutorial telling you about this though, wish devs did a better job explaining in game systems with their tutorials. It is true what more experienced players are saying - the vertical progression is NOT as big of a deal as you may think by the first impression. I highly recommend giving this game a try yourself and remember to spend your spirit points for your favorite character, you will have a strong option in no time.There's a reason why PVP games lean more towards horizontal progression, or if they have vertical progression it's either very subtle or very fast to get through. This game is none hf that, the progression system is heavily punishing newer players. Combine it with lack of matchmaking system and you have a perfect mixture of not wanting to play this game after your first two matches as any of the roles.Leveling in this game is a huge grind and it gives you a huge, objective benefit in power, which is such an insanely bad game design I'm baffled someone came out with this idea.Each level gives you a power to do something better, your damage will be higher, your strikes will be faster, your cooldowns will be shorter and so on and so forth. And unfortunately it is not in values which are negligible, these are values like 20/30% per level, which is insane.What it means is that this game is basically an online RPG with no level restrictions, so if you are a brand new player and you run into 100h player - too bad, you can both do literally the same actions and he will win 100% of the time because he's just objectively stronger.Because of this hostility against newer players this game will never have a heavily needed casual playerbase, a steady new player income, because they will play two matches, realize the enemy pressing the left mouse button is 10 times stronger not because he's more skillful but because he already grinded the game for 500h,  and they will leave because they don't want to get through this lengthy unfun process just to get into an even field. At one point only old fans will remain, until they won't because every now and then some of them will drop as well and noone will play this game anymore.Shame, I barely noticed this gem has came out. How about instead of turning off the matchmaking system you'd actually throw some money for balancing & marketing so you wouldn't need to disable the matchmaking in the first place?

_childDocuments_.review: The levelling system makes the game garbage for new players, there are 25 level to grind for survivors and 45 for demons each granting a skill point that increase the damage and the defenses of your characters and also talents that give you new passives abilities at lvl 10/25 for survivors and 15/25/45 for demons + 5 prestige levels granting five more skill points and even more improvements to your passives.You can earn levels by playing and spending spirit points that you earn after a match or after your account level increase but it can take quite a while and it can be very frustrating since you'll be constantly matched against high level players that will just destroy you, if you play survivor and get matched with high level players the demon will focus on you to gain easy points, if you play demon and end up against high level survivors your unit will get destroyed in 2 seconds and you won't be able to do anything.If you decide to stick with the game and grind a character to max level you'll also need to grind again for every other character you may want to use so i hope you enjoy using the character you levelled since you'll need a lot more games to get the spirit points to level more, if you bought the GOTY and want to try them all with their unique passives unlocked there are 18 survivors and 5 demons to grind, enjoy.

I can't praise the game enough; it definitely has the edge over it's competitors in the genre. However, the implementation of most online features, along with a very anti-casual vibe both dance hand-in-hand as they drag everything down to the depths of the underworld (Reduced xp gain when playing against AI, no bots in private matches, NO xp/currency gain when playing solo, iffy matchmaking, wonky balancing, etc.). Of course, a lot of these issues are solved by having a group of friends purchase the game with you; however, in my opinion, this shouldn't be a requirement. Perhaps I am eternally afflicted with the curse of despising the always-online style of video game, but sometimes, I'd like to just sit down and play one without it causing me a headache, or leaving me feeling like I'm missing out on a core aspect of the game. Definitely a tad disappointing, but hey, maybe the team can make some much-needed changes. _childDocuments_.review: They actually managed to create a very cool 1 vs 4 multiplayer experience. The survivors don't hide/flee for the entire game, they're actively searching for weapons and resources so they can fight through the match and eventually banish the last boss. Meanwhile, the demon player tries to prevent it by possessing evil units, survivors, cars and trees. It's loads of fun on either survivors or demon side, and the game is full of small techniques that you can enjoy learning.The problem is that at higher rating, the demons are barely playable and the game has a few issues like bugs, exploits and bizarre balance decisions. With a decent survivor team composition and the right strategy the demon chances of winning are virtually zero. Beginner players might also have quite a rough time. I just wish someone else was handling the balance because the game feels like it has a lot of potential.TLDR: if you treat it as a party/light competitive game and endure through initial leveling (about 10 matches worth of exp), you'll have a blast.Also packs a lot of fanservice for an Evil Dead fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for a couple hundred hours on Epic before making the swap to Steam.First, this game is not very friendly to newcomers. That isn't to say that nobody new can or will enjoy this game, but like Dead by Daylight (an obvious comparison as a fellow 4v1 asymmetrical horror game,) people who have leveled more will have access to things you don't know how to counter yet.Additionally, unlike Dead by Daylight, the "demon" side is more of an RTS-type mode wherein you fly around in first person gathering "energy" and placing traps/possessing items and people. You are not generally a being with a form. If you've seen any of the Evil Dead series, you're familiar with "demon cam," and this is demon cam as a game.Meanwhile, for survivors, I find the gameplay of this more similar to Friday the 13th: The Game than I do to Dead by Daylight. First, you loot up for weapons (melee & ranged,) healing (in the form of Shemps Cola,) shields (in the form of blessed amulets,) and in-match skill tree upgrades (in the form of Pink F, found in chests.) Then, you traverse the map (on foot or by car, but the car alerts the demon to your location and is generally used late-game instead,) to find three Map Pieces. After all three are collected, you play a mini-tower-defense game wherein you stand in a circle and fight AI enemies (or enemies possessed by the demon player) to capture the Kandarian Dagger & the Lost Pages of the Necronomicon. Following this, you have a "boss battle" type scenario to fight the Dark Ones, and then a two-minute period wherein survivors try to defend the Necronomicon and the demon tries to destroy it. You can fight back, unlike Dead by Daylight, and unlike any other game of its genre, you can respawn your teammates at altars (like vans in Fortnite or beacons in Apex.)Prior to the Steam release, fans who'd been playing for a while (on Epic and consoles) noticed that something went a lil funny with the MMR and it seems as if the MMR was reset. This means that people who have much higher leveled characters than you do were going against you, and demons levels 46+ were going against survivors on their first game. This has started to level out, but isn't 100% accurate yet.Generally, I find this game to be engaging and a lot of fun. There's characters for every possible playstyle (Warriors if you prefer extra melee damage, Hunters if you're good at headshots, Supports if you wish to heal, and Leaders if you wish to apply a variety of buffs to your team,) and all of them have their own unique abilities and skill trees you can level into to build around what you specifically enjoy doing. These are NOT just skins, these are actually different characters... and if you're worried? Every single class has an Ash, so even though characters cannot appear multiple times in the same lobby, you can always play Ash if you'd like to.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real shame that this game is going the way of the dodo.  It had real promise, but the developers just bungled everything that could've been bungled. They dragged their feet on releasing new content. Balance was virtually non-existant and they made the mistake of taking money from Epic to put it on their game store where no one plays.  So, right off the bat, this game had almost no audience on PC.  Despite this and the lack of balance, I had a lot of fun playing the game when it first came out (though I largely played on console where there were players to actually play with).  The survivor game play was legitimately fun (much more involved  than just holding R1 for the majority of the game like in Dead by Daylight) and the deadite gameplay was pretty innovative, I think, despite the lack of balance I mentioned earlier.  The music to the game was also a real highlight for me as well.  It legitimately pains me to have to give this game a downvote because I legitimately had fun before it crapped the bed.Such a waste for such a beloved franchise and almost all of it could have been avoided.  The developer (Saber Interactive) ought to be ashamed of themselves...or at least never try to make another asymmetric multiplayer horror game again.  So, some advice for horror franchises out there that are thinking about hiring a developer to make a video game....avoid this company like you would an STD.

_childDocuments_.review: IGNORE NEGATIVE REVIEWS SAYING YOU CANT CATCH UP NOW: Its completely wrong and not how the game works, its a cop-out excuse and a wrong belief. You can get competitive in short time, and all games require learning to become better. Importantly you dont need even need to win to make good progress.Full Review. About me: I have over 2000 hours playing this on epic. I started playing as a gamer first, and evil dead fan second (though Im even more of an evil dead fan now), and Im familar with competitive online gaming. You dont need to know evil dead to enjoy this game.TLDR: This game is absolutely amazing.This game deserves so much more attention and acclaim. If you enjoyed Left4Dead pvp and still havent had that itch scratched (Back4Blood only partly did for me) - this fulfills that but further on a whole next level of gaming innovation, truely. There is nothing like it.Rather than set levels/courses, each match is a fairly large map with choices on how to tackle it. I guess you could think something like Fortnite or Hunt Showdown maps in that regard and it has a rarity looting system too (it doesnt play anything like Fortnite though). The demon player doesnt just control set enemies, rather choose what and when to control, spawn, set traps (designated possible spots however), flip cars and one of the best things - possessing the survivors and messing with them. For me this is one of the best games ever created and has a gameplay that so perfectly suits evil dead. It also does very well at capturing the annoying but hilarious style of humour the deadites have in the horror-comedy movies - this can be somewhat of frustration for new players however especially if they arent familiar with evil dead or competitive gaming.And thats probably the biggest weakness - as hilarious as it can be, it can be just as frustrating at times too especially for new players who have yet to discover all the ins and outs and techniques and tricks that can be done (for both sides). More experienced players that get really into can also get frustrated sometimes, but thats part of it being so engaging, and most who understand the game just enjoy it. Its just so much fun, and the hilarious moments are worth.The new player experience is also double whammy made harder by no points for skill trees when they start out (NOTE TO SABER: Please give new players 1m spirit points for completing tutorial). There is a leveling system and skill trees (which you can freely allocate/deallocate as you wish btw, they do get quite a few things right like that). There is also a prestige system which has a well designed reset-but-no-skill-loss system (something else they get right), the challenges for it are kinda generic and long but hey cant have everything.That said - if a new player just sticks with about 20 matches or so they can easily have a character fully levelled, thats all thats really needed for strong play. You can then use that character to earn points to level up other characters/demons, and so forth, is just getting that first character up thats the thing. The lengthy prestige system is only a small bonus so dont worry about that. So yeah: new players have to face learning the game AND being gimped at the same time, but only for a short while. Its common new players will often disconnect and leave matches early though (mistake on their part) and forfeit earned xp. The game is more about the matches and attempting to win, rather than having to win. You still progress and earn decent xp for all the actions you do (shows tallies at end) as long as you stay until the match is finished.So: absolutely amazing game, rough new player experience (I see almost every negative review is from this, rather than whether the actual game is good or not). Just stick with it for a bit maybe watch some youtubes guides/videos, and welcome to having some great memorable times with this game!

But at least that has a semblance of an MMR system, so even if you only have 1-2 decent builds you're still likely to be on an even playing field for a little while.♥♥♥♥ me man this is so infuriating. I'm pissed I wasted money on this ♥♥♥♥.Like. Who looked at PvP in MMOs where one player is max level, and the other one only has half his first skill tree leveled up. And thought "Y'know, what if we based an entire game around this system of progression. But there's no way for them to ♥♥♥♥ off back to PvE until they're also max level. So they can actually have a chance of enjoying the game?"This game REALLY didn't need to be this bad.On the subject of the game itself. The melee combat is really questionable. If you're on the defensive, you dodge over and over while other survivors take their guns out and shoot the killer. And if you're on the offensive, but get into a bad spot. Just "Execute" a low health monster to give yourself invincible frames for the next 3 or so seconds. But the killer has no way of telling when survivors start their i-frames on executes, unless you know all of the different execute animations (To be fair they'd be pretty cool in a PvE game).There's a lot of tech the survivors can do to ♥♥♥♥ with the killer and make them waste their resources. _childDocuments_.review: Horribly balanced, and revolved around abuse of mechanics that will likely never be removed. If you are looking to buy this game to play demon, look elsewhere. As with most of these asymmetrical games, the game is heavily skewed within the favor of the survivors, with such design flaws deeply ingrained into the system rather that being something that's easily "patchable". Furthermore, the game is very much at the end of its lifecycle, and highly unlikely to receive any new meaningful DLC. The only thing preventing it from hitting the cemetary is crossplay.The horrible character perk progression has already been expounded upon by numerous other reviewers, and won't be commented on in detail here.For a tl;dr, the demon is forced to be "reactive" and to play a game of attrition, and can only ever succeed if the survivors make some grave error. RNG, horrid game progression, and the game heavily leaning in favor of survivor movement makes the game generally unfun to play as demon, though horrible RNG can screw over survivors as well.The maps are often far too large for the demons to find survivors within a reasonable time frame, in which it is highly possible for them to simply complete the first objective without being found. As demon leveling and progression is revolved around activity against the survivors, the ability of the demon to win is completely hampered if they are unable to find the survivors within this timeframe, for which the first objective is heavily within their favor.Also, depending on the loot gained by the survivors, which depends on RNG, games can simply become unwinnable against certain teams. Legendary weapons found by characters that coincidentally specialize in that weapon are capable of wiping the floor with the demon, who has a more linear progression. If survivor progression was not heavily RNG dependent and instead followed a linear progression like with the demon's leveling, such as picking up scrap to upgrade a weapon from common to legendary rather than finding a wide array of rarities in a chest, it would make for more consistent and fair games.Lastly, the issue with cars and splitpushing. Experienced players are consistently capable of outrunning the demon through the usage of cars, and it is through this that they are able to tackle multiple objectives at the same time. Unlike games such as Dead by Daylight, when survivors complete objectives in the second stage *all teammates are revived and the demon is teleported to a random spot a large distance away*. This puts an unreasonable amount of pressure on the demon to play hyper-aggressively and to tunnel survivors in order to regain leverage against strategies such as splitpushing, both of which are generally unfun for both sides to deal with.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely. I was hesitant to get this game thanks to Epic store nonsense and effectively slept on it up until now. With both PvP and PvE elements and game types to try out it has something for everyone interested in the asymmetric genre of gaming. With four classes and a bunch of different characters in each category, you'll have no shortage of play style to hone in on as you cooperate with your team. Decent variety in demon types too to fight or play as if you're into just going against the survivors. This game got the attention I long hopped Friday the 13th was to get, but never got. With cross platform compatibility there is no shortage of matches to be had as they pair you with anyone on PC, Xbox, or Playstation. Only negatives I can say are nitpicks really, some disconnection issues in some parties (likely from the host), long loading screens for character upgrading and that abysmally long intro screen you can't seem to skip, and some very fortnite-like elements like a closing storm and supply box/rarities which does reward some exploration but still feels a bit out of place in game.Most of my random matches have been a blast, and with friends you can host private games too if thats what you're looking for as well. A definite buy for anyone looking to play a solid movie to game adaptation.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally on Steam and it seems a little to late personally due to player base but I hope Steam can revive it.Graphics: So the graphics are pretty decent to look at, some of the nicest visual styles around and if anything. Some very pretty effects going on in this game.Audio: Spooky, dark and great! In love with this audio on this game!Controls: Some keybind issues which I managed to fix which is good and the characters do feel great to handle.Game-play and everything else after: So the game was originally an EGS and now on Steam and I completely understand and agree, I refuse and never buy a game on EGS but when the money stops and players stop, only then they come to the biggest platform to get the rewards which I do not support, sadly it's the market from scummy devs which is sad because they made a great game originally.Anyway, if you know the Evil Dead universe, you will understand this game.You can play as the survivors or killers in this game. It's a tactical game which involves thinking and working as a team (As for the team part, not everyone does help and thinks of this game as a solo game, which are the brain dead people and it's quiet a bit here so I would recommend using your MIC or joining friends and not randoms)The survivors have to complete tasks in order to vanquish the evil on the land, this involves multiple trips around from driving and running to do them, all the same time the killer(s) are hunting you and trying to slow you down, while they get stronger to push you.If you do not have a team working together, the killer(s) can VERY quickly put a stop to you and wipe the floor in minutes of the match. You NEED to work as a team and NEED to use a mic and chat, not think it's a solo shooter.There are some great things to do and find in the game, you also have some skills, XP and customisation to make you better in the matches.The sad thing is, the player base while on EGS was low which I believe why they've come over to Steam and most likely what might happen is the Steam community will play for a few weeks and then drop off, but thankfully there is a PvE only area in this game with bots which you might find ends up being your main area once the above happens.I would say though, keep your eyes on the horizon for Killer Klowns from Out Space: The Game:  The Texas Chain Saw Massacre:  - Both of these games look like some great alternatives and are launching on Steam day one so should have the best start to the community.It's fun to run around as a group, get killed by a haunted car, bum rushed by a hag and then watch the randoms not work as a team, so you quit and do a private just to play for fun!The game IS a grind to get levels and anywhere though. _childDocuments_.review: Grab your chainsaws and get ready to battle the deadites in Evil Dead: The Game! As a longtime fan of the Evil Dead franchise, I was excited to dive into this game, and I was not disappointed. The game perfectly captures the over-the-top gore and humor that the movies are known for, while also delivering a fun and engaging multiplayer experience.Playing as Ash or one of the other iconic characters from the series, you'll team up with other players to explore creepy cabins and battle hordes of demons. The gameplay is a mix of survival horror and action, with plenty of weapons and upgrades to unlock as you progress. The graphics are also impressive, with detailed environments and character models that really bring the world of Evil Dead to life.One of the highlights of the game is the inclusion of Bruce Campbell as the voice of Ash. His hilarious one-liners and trademark snarky attitude are a perfect fit for the game's tone, and his presence really adds to the overall experience.Overall, Evil Dead: The Game is a must-play for fans of the franchise and anyone who loves a good horror game. It's a bloody good time that will keep you coming back for more!

_childDocuments_.review: Hail to the King, baby.Despite an 'end of life' from development, this game is far from dead -- it is EVIL DEAD!This 4v1 action/horror asymmetrical title also sports a 4vAI teamplay option; alternate 40-player 'Splatter Royale' & single-player open-world exploration modes; as well as 6 character-based story 'Chapters' to complete...Standard matches have a baseline 30 minute timer, so lobby rotations run accordingly -- with games picking up every 5, 10, or 15 minutes.  Wait times will vary by this metric, but the public lobbies always pop with a full team & demon ready to go.Your success will ultimately rely on knowing how to play your role/class/character -- so read the fine print regarding your abilities.  After you've indulged in all the wonderful fan service that this game delivers, your pack will expect you to start pulling your weight.So mark those crates -- and remember...Ghostbeaters never leave a man behind.

_childDocuments_.review: - Highly Recommended (8.5/10)The Evil Dead: The Game is a great adaptation of the horror franchise, merging intense survival gameplay with the original films' charm and style. - Intense and Engaging (8/10): The Evil Dead: The Game presents a thrilling blend of cooperative and competitive gameplay elements that will keep players on the edge of their seats. The combat is challenging and satisfying, featuring both melee and ranged combat mechanics that are easy to grasp but difficult to master. The game does an excellent job incorporating elements from the Evil Dead universe, which enhances the overall experience for the fans. However, beginners might find the difficulty curve steep initially. - Dark and Atmospheric (8.5/10): The game delivers a visually impressive horror aesthetic, effectively recreating the eerie atmosphere of the Evil Dead series.  - Immersive and Chilling (8/10):  The audio enhances the world of Evil Dead with unsettling sounds and iconic voice lines. - High (9/10): The game offers plenty of re-playability with different characters to play as, each with unique abilities and play styles. The varied map layouts and the combination of cooperative and competitive gameplay modes ensure that no two matches are the same. - Approachable with Practice (7.5/10): While the game may initially seem intimidating because of its challenging combat mechanics and intense atmosphere, it becomes more approachable as players learn the systems. The tutorial and many online resources available can significantly help newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from very game of this genre's issue, where everyone is more concerned about the "us versus them" argument rather than playing the actual game, most content created will be heavily biased towards demon or survivor, and has created a toxic stew even rougher than DBD.The game part, i find very fun. Survivor is extremely interesting and varied, allowing players to tweak and cater to their own playstyle with characters, and skill points, which for me personally creates a lot of longevity and fun experimenting.Demon, is the same way, though the starting curve for the game is akin to a brick wall rather than a steady curve, it took me a while to get the hang of it but demon is very fun and satisfying to play correctly, and allows for a lot of player expression as well, being an entity rather than being "man who walk fast with machete" i find much more engaging.There are frustrating things in the game for sure, Hunter dodges are pretty obnoxious, some vaults cant be vaulted by your demon units creating silly situations, and some characters are defintely more annoying to deal with than others, hunter ash being a big example. My advice, if you are really interested in the game, just buy it, play it, experience it for yourself until you get a max character, then go hunting for builds/information/other things after you have your own feelings and thoughts, rather than 100% bandwagoning everything the community says for either side, and i really wish the "Us versus them" was less encompassing for asym's overall but it simply takes over everything the community has to talk about.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, Evil Dead is one of the most legendary properties of modern media, so much so that films and gaming still pull from it’s influence to this day, and the game perfectly reflects it’s unique balance of horror and triumphant action here.Do you want to experience what it's like to make a stand as a bloodied knight against demon spawn, with sweeping orchestras and the shouts of your teammates to feel like God is on your side as you stand alone? Would you like to make it a Doomguy rampage with bloodshed and heavy metal playing as you kill endless foes, with one-liners being thrown out left and right as you use a chainshaw and a double-barreled shotgun? Or would you like to be the enemy, and strategize the action as the dungeon master while being able to jumpscare them anytime you want? Evil Dead has all of that magic and more, but really, the soundtrack has no right to be this good. It feels like you're fighting for your life at the end of existence. The game also has crossplay so there's not a complete reliance on Steam, and even the option for offline bots. Totally worth the purchase. There’s something about the properties of this era that glow with its passion, and on that note, I have only one thing left to say:Hail to the king baby.

The game may not be perfect as no asymm really is, specifically with matchmaking/tutorial...but once you learn the basics and truly get into learning your favorite class and abilities it is so much fun!

_childDocuments_.review: The game can be fun and offers a unique experience, but the glaring balance issues is to hard to overlook. Fresh players are forced to played with any level of skill, including those maxed prestiged who can soak in hits as if I was hitting them with a wet noodle. I chased a survivor for a good solid 5-10 minutes, but he just healed whatever damage I did do or dodged out of the way completely with seemingly no drain on their stamina. Other times survivors just vaulted a window over and over and I couldn't do the same completely wasting a possession.Much of the bosses play long winded animations that can just let survivor burst you down as they line up their shots. I had one boss last only about 30 seconds before being obliterated by headshots. Against a well grouped team possessing a survivor becomes impossible as they either stun lock you or burst you down all the same as they quickly line up their shots while you are animation locked.Other times you can just be ruined by bad rng, survivors finding the map within minutes or finding legendary weaponry for the entire team and being stocked to the brim with ammo and heals. The demon all the while has to hope he find the survivors before then as only they knows where the first objectives are.The game is just stacked way to much in one favor to ignore, a common sight in these asymmetrical games sadly. I really like the concept and did find myself having fun against players of equal skill level, but it can be just like bashing your head against a brick wall. They really need to do a balance overhaul as well as some skill based matchmaking.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of the Evil Dead franchise, diving into Evil Dead: The Game was a thrill. The nostalgia hits hard with the accurately portrayed characters that fans have come to love. It’s clear that a lot of care went into capturing their personalities, which adds an authentic touch that makes the game feel like an extension of the films.The gameplay itself is both unique and enjoyable. The asymmetrical multiplayer format, where you can either take on the role of the survivors or the demon, offers a fresh twist on the typical horror game. It’s a blast strategizing with friends and switching the fifth player spot to try out the demon role, bringing an extra layer of fun to each match. The chaos of hunting or being hunted in the dark, creepy environments is exhilarating, and the game does a great job of maintaining that classic horror vibe.However, there are some downsides. The game feels a bit lifeless at times due to the dwindling player base. Long loading times for matches can really detract from the experience, making it frustrating when you're eager to jump back into the action. It’s a shame, as this could be a fantastic experience with a more active community.Overall, Evil Dead: The Game is definitely worth playing, especially with a group of friends who appreciate the franchise. Just be prepared for some potential downtime while waiting for matches. If you love the movies and are looking for a fun way to relive those horror moments, gather your friends and dive in!

_childDocuments_.review: is a co-operative survival horror monster masher, not unlike your  or : one player controls a Demon with an army of minions to spawn and derail 4 player survivors gaining the items required to successfully close the Necronomicon.Where it varies from those other titles is the survivors have access to weapons/skills to fight back. It is actually extremely satisfying to monster mash as a survivor, with access to more tricks than pallet jumps.+💗I am not a lifelong  fan. I still have yet to see the first 2 (I did see ), and only had my interest piqued because of Lucy Lawless being in it. Then I saw Jill Marie Jones was, too, and I was all in.I was expecting Ruby to be a character, but was extremely surprised when I saw Amanda was, too! Though not voiced by Jill Marie Jones herself, the model/artwork are excellent representations, and I definitely  playing as her.The show is really good. I might watch the first 2 movies someday.+Even though I am not a stark fan of the franchise, I  Ash Williams is THE MAN when it comes to mastering demon ass. This game captures the over-the-top heroics of slapping a chainsaw on your wrist and digging in pretty well.You gotta keep your Fear level in check to avoid being possessed, and you get more points for more damage/headshots/finishers. If  is a sociopath's dream for being able to stalk literal helpless victims, this is the antithesis of that. Dancing around palettes is for simps - pick up a meat mallet and bash evil in it's fugly face.+I wonder if this is the level of gore they wanted in the game, or if they had to scale it back, but gosh, there is a lotta gore in this game.  Finishers look painful with dismemberment and insertions into orifices, enemies rip their limbs off and use it as a weapon, you will get biled on and muddied up from blood as you slice into elite units.The characters, too, get appropriately bloodied the more bedlam they unleash during fights.+One thing I sincerely wished F13 did was provide a solo mode. Well, they did, but you only play as Jason.  kicks Vorhees right in the nards while giving him the finger as it serves up individual solo missions to play to unlock lorebits/costumes.Further - there is an  solo mode of the online offering complete with AI for demon and teammates. Is it end-all, be-all best solo experience? Naw. . And it just being there is positive enough to warrant a mention. You do not gain points to level your character, but I do appreciate and enjoy being able to play it this way when chosen to.+Being able to upgrade characters is pretty dope, and let's you truly carve out what you enjoy most about each. Additionally, they have character-specific perks that level up gradually, and recent Prestige additions means you can take 'em further.+You are not weighed down by your team. You could, potentially, manage a map yourself if you know what you are doing. You are only as great as your strongest player here, and not necessarily as weak as the weakest. I appreciate this, as it means most matches (even if a loss) offer a fair chance to win if you try.+I appreciate the inclusion of different weather and time cycles for the maps. Don't expect them to change dynamically - what you start with, you finish with. But it's still pretty dope and each genuinely create a different atmosphere!+You can tell A LOT of care was put into making this  for it's subject. I was initially unsure, as these types of games aren't totally my bag and I am not a super fan, but it all hits the mark, and the audio/visual quality of what it captures is made with tender lovin' chainsaw. Most of the major stars reprise their character roles.-As , itself, is a niche franchise, so too shall the audience for this game be. I have never had issues finding a game, against AI or IRL demons across my time since release on EGS and now here on Steam.But I do wonder about the sustainability. Crossplay goes a long way to helping, no doubt, and most of my games have PS/XB players in it.-It's great that you can play the stuff solo, HOWEVER - you cannot even access the game without an internet connection. I took this for granted and initially thought you could, but a quick try shows you can't even get past "Press A" on the title screen without it slapping you with an internet connection error.Quizzical to make decent solo modes and lock them behind online connectivity. -Could use more maps. Was hoping there would be more by now, and was super excited just seeing the Castle Kandar map drop. But I def wouldn't knock anyone for knocking this game for limited maps.They are, at least, expansive maps filled mostly with spots from the series. But we just need a few more.-For the love of Baal, let me jump! Not "Press Y - Vault". An actual dedicated jump button.Evil Dead: The Game

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, as someone who's invested a good amount of time and 100% in this game, it really infuriates me to my core to see Saber Interactive discontinue this game. There's so much content they could have added, especially Evil Dead Rise, which was my most anticipated release. It is sad to see a game like this getting treated like garbage by the developers, and for that reason, I will no longer buy a single product from Saber Interactive ever again for the lies to their fan base and broken promises, so I can only hope they revert their decision and go by their promises again and try to bring this game to life, which I highly doubt they will do that because Saber doesn't care enough since they are working on other projects, ignoring their fans.     Also I think what really killed this game was the lack of advertising, updates, and releasing on the Epic Games store. There have also been some balancing issues with the game and the astronomical grinding with the prestige system, also the game for new players has a huge learning curve. Trying to win as a demon is almost impossible against good survivors. The sad thing is that I really wanted to play this game on Steam, but when I found out that it was only on Epic, I was filled with so much disappointment because the Epic Games launcher is just trash later on I forgot about this game till I found out it was being released on Steam after a year, and Dear God, why is every asymmetrical horror game always getting treated poorly and not lasting for a long time? First, we had Friday the 13th, and VHS. What's next? Will the Texas Chainsaw Massacre game get the same treatment, including killer clowns from outer space? I'm getting fed up with these asymmetrical multiplayer horror games being treated this way and not lasting a long time because of poor developer decisions. As of now, you can still play this game, and the servers will be up for the foreseeable future, but there will be no more updates or content added in the meantime. I'll just play Taxes Chainsaw Massacre until then, and I pray it doesn't receive the same treatment in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fun experience. Whether you're a fan of Evil Dead or just love slashing through zombies, you gotta try this game. You can play as famous characters like Ash Williams, Pablo or Ruby. Each character has their own cool weapon specialisation and abilities. Majority of the characters are voiced by the original cast. Plenty of flying limbs and witty quips from the characters as you cut up deadites.The story mode missions are also really cool. You have to solve puzzles and fight enemies. There are scary moments that keep you on your toes.Playing as the Demon offers a fresh perspective, allowing you to see the game from the other side. Demon playstyle has an almost RTS style of gameplay. You get to observe the fear and panic in the eyes of the survivors as you relentlessly pursue them. It's a thrilling change of pace and adds an extra layer of excitement to the gameplay.Overall, Evil Dead: The Game is a gory and fun adventure. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an a-symmetrical battle royale like game which combines the two elements in a way which makes every game feel immersive and different from the last, tho it has one of the worst if not the worst toturials i've ever done. i've been dealing alot with the "fatal error" crash which i simply fixed by putting -dx11 and -fullscreen in launch options so please do that:)!The a-sym part of this games seems rather unbalanced, it's 4 survivors vs 1 demon and it can feel like the demon is overpowered at times, but on the other side i've also heard that a coordinated survivor team should be superior so idk. How does these two types of playstyles operate?Demon: Playstyle: The demon acts like an overseer who most of the time dont actually interact with the survivors in person, the demon traps chests making you gain fear, he sends evil units at you and scares you to make you gain fear but what is fear and does it even matter? Well yes very much so as when your fear goes above a certain treshold showed on your screen the demon WILL be able to posses you making him wipe your whole team if you aren't carefull. Tho if you are good at keeping your fear down then the demon will probably choose to posses his own units instead giving him the control over them and making them much stronger, this can be a real danger so watch out.Survivor: Survivors starts off the match split up in a little area so still close, their objective is to find 3 parts of a map but i would very much recommend looting atleast till you have both a gun and a melee weapon before going for the maps. The maps is spread out, tho you can see which place it's located in in the top-right of your screen aswell as the game marking the map for you with a red mark when you get close enough.General tips and info:Probably the best tip you will ever get in this game is to STAY WITH YOUR TEAMMATES, this is so important for the survivors as there are a reason why you are 4 vs 1, the demon can totally destroy you without the healp of your teammates so please just stay with them. Another great tip is to spam finisher whenever possible if your character is low level as the finishers give you i-frames (invinsibility frames) while still dealing damage. Also please use your dodge ability as it's very great at dealing with high damage output units such as elites or even the demon itself. The spirit points under your level can be used to level up characters if you hold down "F" while on the collection screen. I recommend: I recommend to start out playing survivor as mechanics are way easier to learn and you have a team to back you up if you make mistakes along the way, also i would start out playing a warrior or a leader as they are mechanically way easier to use and learn.How the game goes on: After the survivors have gotten all 3 maps they now have two objectives: going after the book pages and the kandarian dagger (Note: the kandarian dagger isn't an item and DOESN'T help you slay enemies, it's just an objective which needs to be completed) after the survivors have done these missions they will be rewarded with a chest at each location and it's now time to take down the dark ones, it's a very simple and weird fight as you just have to look at it and hold down "control" on your keyboard, when that's done you have to defend a book as your final objective, in this fight you CANNOT be revived so if you're downed during this fight you are dead.Conclusion:-Toturial is very bad-Unbalanced -Use spirit points to gain character level-Abuse dodge ability as survivor-Finisher can be great to gain i-frames-PUT -dx11 AND -fullscreen IN LAUNCH OPTION TO NOT CRASH!!!!-Play survivor to learn the game-Easiest survivors is leaders and warriors-Stay with mates as it reduces fear and helps kill evil units9/10 game, this is probably a very high rating for a game like this but after almost 1000 hours of dbd my opinion is probably biased because it's an a-sym but i would defenately give the game a try:)!

_childDocuments_.review: I really really really wish steam had a neutral option. but it doesn't, so right now i cant recommend this one.This review will only cover my limited experience of 8 hours that being just playing demon: Tutorial- The tutorial is REALLY bad to the point where it exists solely as a testing ground for controls. you're a lot better off watching a couple of Youtube tutorials to really figure out whats going on here.Que Experience- The Que times are bad. Like really bad, i'm not even kidding i waited so long that I thought my game was corrupted,  apparently this is normal. Expect a 5-10 minute Que as demon. worst of all if someone leaves the lobby its right back to the 10 minute Que- this isn't much fun.Balance-The balancing on this one is off the walls absurd, in 8 hours of playing demon i have won 3 games one of them because a survivor disconnected partway through. Yes I know- skill issue. No. I don't know why but the devs decided to power play the survivors in what really feels like a complete role reversal where as the demon player you're fighting for your life to survive against these literal demigods. its insane how strong these guys are, and theres really not a ton you can do to level the playing field. I cant overstate how strong the survivors are, a fully maxed out demon is going to lose to survivors almost every time. and man the dodge that they have is a HUGE pain to deal with as all of your attacks are very easily telegraphed and they can all dodge 3-5 times which is usually enough to dodge your entire attack chain. This almost always results in you trying to hit someone who immediately dodges 4 times while the rest bludgeon you to death with a rusty pipe.General issues-WHY ON EARTH DO I HAVE TO WAIT ANOTHER 145 SECONDS TO SCREAM AT PEOPLE BECAUSE I HIT A HILL AND FLEW OVER EVERYONE. The amount of times that this has single handedly completely ruined an offensive is well above 10. you shouldn't be punished this badly for a buggy feature especially when its so vital to playing demon. speaking of buggy features there's a lot. in my 8 hours I've seen the camera go completely sideways, consistent rubber-banding, and getting stuck repeating a spell animation multiple times (this usually leads to the survivors again bludgeoning you to death). Also this seems like a huge oversight but you cant harm someone who's mid kill animation (all of these are 4-10 seconds); I've seen multiple people use this to chain I-frames to bleed out the demon timer. Separately there's a lot of downtime, when you've used all of your spells/summons both you and the survivors are left sitting there for up to 30 seconds doing nothing just waiting for everything to come back up.All in all Im sure the survivor experience is bit better but as demon right now its not even close to rewarding and it just feels  genuinely brutal and unfair. Im not sure if they're going to work on balancing/Bugs as this games been out for a year over on epic and if this is the state the games in I don't really have high hopes for it, but hey maybe im wrong. its fun but it needs more going for it and there's a LOT of work that can be done in terms of balance, if that happens id say go for it but in its current state i just can't recommend itTLDR: Might be fun to play as survivor, but if you're looking to play demon maybe go somewhere else for now

damage against them, since they couldn't evade this.Now they went overkill in traps not triggering on freshly unpossessed survivors.Take this change back Saber, implement instead a Baal-specific your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to play this game once I got it, because there is very very few games that let you play as an undead character of any kind. Especially in an action based type game. most are RTG or turn based....However I was very quickly disappointed in the the mechanisms in Evil Dead The Game... I quickly learned that when you play the Demon side you spend most of your time running around collecting these red smokey orbs that are "Infernal Energy" to replenish my Infernal energy meter, and this infernal energy is used to arm traps and spawn my sides characters. The most disappointing part of the game is that my infernal energy started depleting more quickly or less quickly depending on how far I was able to up grade my "Threat Level", while I was controlling one of my units/characters/"Deadites I was only able to control them a few minutes at a time, and then I would lose control of them once my infernal energy ran out. As, I was booted from controlling my own unit my unit would automatically die upon my exit from controlling him/her. I was stuck running around in "spirit mode" again unable to attack or stop the "survivor side" from grabbing all the goals, while I had to play "Infernal Pacman" again, even if I up graded my threat level and was supposed to be generating infernal energy it is still WAY to slow to help stop the Pacman phenomenon. Even fully up graded Threat level equaled only a few second longer controlling my guys. I could not place my guys/units in strategic locations, because once I control them and leave their control, they die automatically. Upgrading my Demon/armies level only did little to improve my ability to really get in the game and to some action. No matter if I even got to the top level with a Demon/undead army, my controlling units was only extended a few more lousy seconds. MORE than just a few times when I was able to fight a survivor and knock his/her health really low, and I was getting ready to deliver my killing shot/hit, I suddenly was kicked from my units/deadites control and my guy died instead by default, because "I ran out of infernal energy" AGAIN, and you can't collect it while you are controlling one of your units, so I die instead, and the survivor that should have died, has now time to heal him/her self and grab the oblective, I get exorcised, and I can start doing Infernal Pacman again and hurry to the next falling objective, if the survivors have split up, which I don't fault them for doing, it's just good strategy, but by the time I'm done playing Infernal Pacman" my next objective is practically over, I spawn some units take control of one to join the fight, and because my energy is down form spawning units I get even less time to enjoy the action with the survivors, and agian I ALMOST win a fight only to be booted for the lack of this dam Infernal Energy, and my guy dies by default again survivor heals and grabs objective, and on to the next objective, and rinse and repeat....... Till I lose that match as well.I fully understand that the Demon side should not be allowed to control a survivors character forever/for the whole match unlimited, but the Demon side should be able to control their units without loss of infernal energy or any other energy other than the will to continue to play this disappointing game as long as it takes, any energy to control your own units! My solution is to make it not take infernal energy to control your own units, and you can grab infernal energy while controlling your units and it also heals them. The Demons unit have no way of healing, unless you have one of the demons who has the vampiric attack to replenish health. Survivors can heal. Of course as I said when the Demon side "possesses" a survivor that SHOULD only be a few seconds because that player needs to get back into the fight with their character.Controlling your own units should NOT cost energy of any type, AND your units should NOT die automatically once you relinquish control of them, now if the Demon side is setting traps, and spawning units, then that should cost infernal energy, and a significant amount to limit units spawned and prevent spamming units like crazy, I get that part. The Demon should generate infernal energy a little faster if it is fully up graded. This is the first game I saw that controlling your own units is timed, and your control is lethal to your own units.... THIS SUCKS!  I only won 3 out of 250 matches so far.The reason for that is the bad mechanics, and controlling loss of infernal energy, and the inevitable fact that you have to kill your own units with your control.There is also a MAJOR problem with cheating, or maybe the survivors upgrades are too powerful. I one match I saw piles of ammo on the floor, and more matches than I can remember that survivors were one shotting my deadites as I spawned them, and stood around waiting for me to spawn the next batch and repeat. Again if I managed to fight back a little the infernal energy loss of controlling would defeat me fast than the over powering survivors....I can only hope that the Devs read the comments, and at least eliminate that part of this game that cause the Demon side to lose infernal energy while controlling its own sides units, and that controlling kills...Resident Evils Resistance doesn't even make you lose energy to control your units when your the bad guy(Evil Scientist side). I am and OLD gamer and I recognize a bad design when I see it. I might even ask for a refund...

_childDocuments_.review: Evil dead is a wedding between Dead by Daylight and a Battle royale, 4 survivors vs 1 demon-18 survivors : each survivor have 4 unique differences for example 1 start with a weapon, 2 can see chests through walls, 3 have a bonus on a specific weapon 4 an unique ability where you can expel the demon from a possessed body.-4 main classes for survivors : (There are no restrictions, you can have 4 of the same in the same match)-5 demons, with a different roster of units, from zombies, to demons, to squeletons, each one have a different approach to killing survivors. Each action cost energy, summoning units, settings traps, possessing an unit, a survivor, taking a car, etc-3 huge maps with different weather each time (Snow, sun, rain, blood rain, foggy, etc)-A lot of different weapons with 4 tiers ranging from pistols, smg, shotgun, double barrel, sawed-off, crossbow, grenade launcher, blunderbuss / machete, two handed hammer, chicken hammer (where you beat the meat, no pun intended), stick, pickaxe, one handed axe, two handed axe, scythe, baseball bat, knife, etc)-A skill tree for each survivor and demons that you keep between games, unlocking new mecanics or boosting stats-You can also boosts stats in match with drug-You can play vs demon AI in coop, vs demon AI with survivors bots---------------------------------The game is quite fun, dead survivors can be resurrected at any time, the demon is original and very fun to play too. (10/10 would possess a survivor and throw him into a river again)---------------------------------As of 27/09/2024 most of the time you find games faster than on Dead by Daylight, don't ask me why

_childDocuments_.review: Asymmetrical Horror 4 v 1 PvP games are rare and difficult to balance. Communities are usually in one camp or the other. One side complaining how OP the other side of the fence. Grass is always greener right? I understand this because I am a Dead by Daylight player with over 700 hours invested in DBD. I am killer main, although I do play survivor occasionally, I find this helpful insight into the mind of a Survivor. DBD has an incredibly high skill cap, easy to learn, hard to master. I'm giving context to my opinion, I am reviewing this game through the eyes of a player who enjoys a challenge and has played Evolve (I miss that game), DBD, Darkest Dungeon, and other games that can be frustrating experiences. I also don't write reviews for games very often, you should decide for yourself what is fun and how you want to play your games, so take my opinion with a grain of salt. That being said. Whew. Ok, here it comes. Evil Dead the Game, from the Demon camp, is incredibly hard to enjoy. It is very, very, very Survivor sided at this stage of development. I won't go into detail as to the mechanics and why it is imbalanced, no spoilers, however I will say at 7 hours in Demons feel bad. Really bad. The skill tree improvements are a heavy grind. I would guess it's about an 80 grind to start feeling the buffs received from Perks. That is for one Demon, they do not share skill trees. That means you could invest a lot of hours into a Demon in hopes it pays off, only to be potentially disappointed with ones choice of Camp/Demon/Purchase of the game. This is a recipe for Salty communities, toxic player base, and hours misery with no guarantee that it's worth grinding out a character. With so many games out there all competing for your money, and more notably, your Time it may be wise to look elsewhere for feelings of satisfaction. Diablo IV releases soon, I played the Server Smash and it was very fun. DBD is still here, it has its issues, but it's more fun. Playing a match of Killer and getting a few kills feels good, satisfying. Plus there is A Lot of content. Elden Ring is the best video game experience I have Ever had the pleasure of experiencing. There are dozens of other games I would recommend playing before paying for this game. Perhaps it just needs time to balance, I would recommend waiting until the Player Reviews indicate it's ready to be enjoyed. Wait and see if the developers give a **** about their player base. Save yourself from that feeling of wasting your time and money. I do not recommend this game. Official Review - 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: New statistics show that there are few games with Polish localization on Steam. Fortunately, the situation is improving, because after all, that's what players need.Yes, I'm looking at you. company, despite the crazy popularity of the game series in our country, did not make our games Polish. And it's good, but on the other hand a bit bizarre that the game doesn't even have subtitles in our language. And unfortunately, this applies to many other items of Games in Polish on SteamNew research appeared on Gamesensor, where researchers checked how many titles available on Steam offer the Polish language version. Polish audiences are a distinct but quite small part of the Valve platform community – they make up a group of about 1.35% (people who play, comment and communicate in Polish). Interestingly, this is a clear decrease of 0.58% compared to the previous month (Valve data). After all, there are not many games in our language when it comes to the total catalog of titles available on Steam. The chart above clearly shows that out of over 14,000 of paid games available on Steam, only 6-7% offer a Polish localization. It's hard to be surprised though. The largest part of the platform's catalog are independent, low-budget games. No wonder indie studios can't afford localization to languages ​​other than English (or even the native language of the studio itself). Therefore, it is more interesting to read a chart showing similar statistics, but only for games sold in at least 10,000. copies Here it is much better, although a bit "bumpy". Over the years, the number of games with Polish localization has been increasing, but the "breakdown" has occurred. Fortunately, the situation has improved, up to a historical record of 26.65%. The trend is up and I'm very happy about it. Interestingly, there are currently about 951 games in Polish on Steam. The question remains - is it not enough? _childDocuments_.review: 500 Hours on Epic because I don't let something like which market I buy from affect the games I play... That's dumb. I love the game. It has a fair share of balance issues and new players are going to have a hard time against the veterans (they will not chill, don't even try) but it has it's own thing going for it. It's NOT DBD so don't compare, comparisons stop at 4 v 1. Secondly, you can't balance a game that is already unbalanced to begin with (4 v 1) and that's true for every asymm. Third point? The game is just a lot of fun. You explore a map, gear up, fight deadites by the handful or harass survivors for like 20 minutes. There's a lot of goofy glitches, memey demons and survivors, just a lot of good fun to be had in what's essentially an Evil Dead theme park. The character you play as actually matters which is a big one, and being able to fight back makes getting trashed not feel quite as bad. Customs from the get go with a lot of AI modes is useful for learning the game, of course, and having fun with your friends. Is it a masterpiece? No. Is it better than DBD? It's a different game, don't compare them. Will I have fun playing it? Yeah, I think you will if you give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a acceptable Pro-Survivor game, that allows you to a 4 man group to find complete some objectives and "destroy evil" while also using ranged and melee weapons to stylishly kill minions. However, it is severely unbalanced in terms of Survivor vs Killer (or Demon in this case) and favours the survivor outright (unless you have maxed out perks on a killer, then maybe you stand a chance). Waste of money on my part.Survivor gameplay can be amusing. The pathfinding is terrible, but the action is cool and fun. Survivor gameplay seems to relate more to what gear you pick up, rather than your perks or personal ability, but those do count for something as well. Each character has a unique ability, along with a perk tree and they each feel unique and somewhat interesting.Demon gameplay is severely weaker, especially as a new player. You lack the perks to be effective at all, which means your Infernal Energy drain is laughably ridiculous. Your units are weak and pathetic (despite maxing their levels) and possessing units (and survivors) is about the only thing you can do to stand a chance of actually dealing damage. And then of course, if they haven't already got the best-tier weapons, they can still wipe the floor with you. You are certainly no threat to survivors at low levels, just a play thing to make their progression more enjoyable. It's pathetic.Conclusion: If you like playing a Survivor and smashing through the "killer" to save the day, without much challenge. This is the game for you. But if your looking for challenge or to enjoy time being a "killer". Better off staying in Dead By Daylight.

_childDocuments_.review:
Step into the shoes of Ash Williams or his friends from the iconic Evil Dead franchise and work together in a game loaded with over-the-top co-op and PVP multiplayer action! Play as a team of four survivors, exploring, looting, crafting, managing your fear, and finding key items to seal the breach between worlds in a game inspired by all three original Evil Dead films as well as the Starz original Ash vs Evil Dead television series.

ICONIC CHARACTERS
Play as characters from throughout the Evil Dead universe, including Ash, Scotty, Lord Arthur, Kelly Maxwell, Pablo Simon Bolivar, and more, with new dialogue performed by Bruce Campbell and others!

PLAY AS GOOD OR EVIL...
Fight for the forces of good or take control of the powerful Kandarian Demon to hunt Ash and other players while possessing Deadites, the environment, and even the survivors themselves as you seek to swallow their souls!

OVER THE TOP VISUALS
Whether you're tearing a Deadite in two with Ash's famous chainsaw hand or flying through the map as the Kandarian Demon in spirit form, the game captures the look and feel of the Evil Dead franchise in all its glory, with realistic visuals and a physics-based gore system that brings the horror to life! 

THIS...IS MY BROOMSTICK!
Brandish your short barrel shotgun, chainsaw, cleavers and more to do some delightfully gruesome violence against the armies of darkness.

Evil Dead: The Game features multiplayer co-op and PvP for PC, Xbox One, Xbox X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch.

name: QV
detailed_description: Start a dimension-jumping adventure with Quby! In a universe, dimensions are connected to each other. In the center of the passages lies Dimensional Core, keeping the balance between dimensions. This balance began to collapse when the Core stopped working. Unless someone gives a helping hand, soon the universe will follow. The Gate doesn't let anyone into the Dimensional Core. But Quby, as the last descendant of Chosen Ones, can access the Gate. To restore the balance between dimensions, Quby opens a portal to the Gate. With Varon, the talking penguin, she must explore the long-forgotten ruins of her ancestors and find a way to reactivate the Core. Let the journey begin! Gameplay Features ⦁ Unique Inter-dimensional Adventure - Use Quby's brush to create an ink bridge over the water and draw portals for inter-dimensional travel. ⦁ Colorful Companions - Embark on a grand adventure with companions from other worlds! Meet Varon the Penguin, mysterious shadow, Golems guarding the fire, and many more. ⦁ Various Costumes - Discover and collect hidden fairies in the stage to unlock fancy costumes and hairstyles! ⦁ Multi-language Support - QV supports a total of 7 languages: English, German, French, Korean, Japanese, and Chinese(Simplified and Traditional) ⦁ The Game for Everyone - Having 4 difficulty levels in each stage, QV features a total of 172 different gameplay experience. QV is made for both beginners and challenge-lovers. ⦁ Controller Support - Gameplay experience becomes more mesmerizing with controllers. ⦁ Beautiful Music - Enjoy the merry adventure with soundtracks that match with the ruins.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute, it has a nice soundtrack, and the puzzles are decent, even if simple, at least in the beginning. Sadly, the implementation is lackluster: there is no mouse support except for the top level menus, no way to rebind controls and the gameplay feels clunky because of poorly aligned interaction triggers (You often can interact with puzzle elements only in a very narrow area or from a particular angle.) , the ultra-wide resolutions seem broken.All in all, "QV" needs lots of QoL improvements to become enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: QV

_childDocuments_.review: Quby's magic wand paint brush will swish swoosh its way into your heart. If you want to see gameplay and my first impressions as they happened, watch my video above. QV is a simple puzzle game that puts you into the many hairstyles of Quby, a carefree paintress ready to save the world. The soundtrack is the true star of the game, and QV as a whole is aimed at anyone who wants to relax while solving simple puzzles. It's an almost zen-like game. Normal difficulty has very straightforward solutions, and Hard is there to provide a modest challenge. Personally, I wish the QV difficulty (Very Hard) was unlocked from the beginning, and it's also strange that Easy isn't unlocked from the start either.And... that's really all there is to it. QV is one of those games that you'll quickly know is or isn't for you. Its simplicity will turn off some people (such as myself), but others will enjoy the charm of its art and music. Which are you?

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and lots of fun!Firstly, I want to state that I played this with a controller, and it was a lot easier than a keyboard, so keep that in mind before you buy.I really enjoyed playing this game, and even after I finished I felt like I'd happily play it all over again.Don't let the cute art style fool you, this game can be quite challenging to figure out at times, particularly on the harder levels. I personally really liked that. If you like the game play and figuring out all the puzzles, I would recommend playing the levels on ALL difficulties. Many of the levels can seem quite different when you do so!Pros:- Beautiful art style. I love all the little outfits and colour combinations.- Lovely, non-intrusive music (I fully recommend the soundtrack as well as the game itself)- Challenging. But has different game modes for the people who want a harder or a more relaxed experience.- Nice bonus bit of story (though I definitely wouldn't play it only for the story as there's not much of it)Cons:- Controls work best with a controller- Controls can be a little annoying to line up at times (to me that just added to the challenge)- Checkpoints work in a really annoying way that can sometimes cause you to save after making a mistake, forcing you to restart the level (my biggest gripe)- Some of the longer last levels felt like they could do with a few more checkpoints to be less frustrating, particularly in the easier modesAll in all, I did really enjoy this game and would recommend it for people of any age!9/10
