_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of the rogue-like genre, especially dead cells, so this game feels right at home for me with many weapons of varying levels, two random spells on every weapon that make each one feel unique, factors like these make the randomness of the game very good.A big complaint of mine though would have to be problems with the moveable, platforms which are quite literally everywhere. Some enemy attacks, weapon skills, and spells like leap will trap me inside the platforms of different elevation. When going form high to low elevations, I sometimes get stuck on the high part. Another instance of elevated platform shenanigans would be enemies on different elevation platforms basically flying above, following me, though I've only encountered this once. I know this seems like a lot, but I don't say it with the intent of demeaning the game, only with the hopes that the devs will see this and fix these issues to make the game better.Then there's hit boxes, they are really accurate, sometimes not for their own good. Short weapons like the ax have a really tiny hit box although visually it seems to hit. Enemy attacks seem to not affect you if you are positioned correctly near the enemy, but others times they hit you if you stand the same way. I don't know if this can be fixed or if its intentional, but it's just something I felt like bringing up.Now although I brought up many problems with the game I still do enjoy it very much. The platform movement and the puzzles that arise from it are something I enjoy very much and have never seen before. Also, the high risk high reward system of giving up potions for a single section to double them on the next one is something I've never seen. The uniqueness of each run is also very, very good, and in my opinion only monotonous in the sunken village.

_childDocuments_.review: Really novel idea with some interesting mechanics that mostly engrossed me for the short runtime. However, there are some serious balancing issues with the game. Firstly, this game promotes itself as being very challenging, but frankly the game more often felt janky rather than hard, especially when it comes to different elevations and bossfights. The combat itself can range from being very engaging when you are using platforms to your advantage in large puzzle-like encounters to mindless attack mashing, which I think is a sign the gameplay loop wasn't fully explored.Secondly, there are a couple of items that pretty much trivialise the whole progression system. There is a really neat mechanic where you can get rid of some of your healing potions when going into an area in order to double their amount if you manage to finish that area. This whole dynamic can be entirely bypassed if you manage to acquire the parry heal charm, which is so extremely overpowered because of how easy it is to parry enemies in this game. That's not even mentioning you can make the parry window even larger if you choose so. But an even bigger offender is the flayer weapon. Its unique attribute is that it gives knowledge whenever you kill an enemy with a charged attack, knowledge being the resource you collect to unlock new items. With how many oneshot fodder enemies can spawn sometimes, you can practically unlock the entire arsenal in a single area run-through. Now, I don't know if this was intentional or not, but to me it felt like a cheap way to hide the lack of variety in encounters between runs by shortening the time it takes to unlock everything.I have other nitpicks like the camera feeling wonky, especially in the hub area, as well as the generally uninteresting story. The artwork and atmosphere are fantastic though, and it's worth at least trying this game out for the vibe and novelty of the mechanics. This game is definitely not for everyone, but I still enjoyed it for what it was quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Loot River

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a fan of games that combine unique mechanics together in interesting ways. Loot River is a rogue-lite, dungeon crawler with Souls-lite combat and spatial block puzzles and...it works, but is still being improved.Let's get down to the nitty gritty: there are negative reviews on here because, upon release, the game had some issues with, mainly, the early-game: the dash/dodge felt weird, movement in general was a little bit stilted, combat takes some getting used to, the difficulty outweighed the reward of runs, and there wasn't much worthwhile LOOT until multiple weapons, spells and armors were unlocked over the course of several runs.These issues are all being fixed, though, very quickly, and now the game feels so much better already, just a week after release. It's a passion project from a very small indie team and they really should have had much more internal testing before release, but it is what it is. I'm confident that they'll make all the improvements the game deserves. Just consider it to be in early access still, I'd say, since major improvements are happening on an almost-daily basis.Why the positive review? I believe in this game. It's got SO much potential. But, most importantly, after playing it for 15 hours so far: it's fun to play right now. I've enjoyed it that entire time (my initial jaunt through the First City notwithstanding, lol.) Just understand that it's a difficult game that was released with more in common with rogueLIKES than rogueLITES, though that is changing with the introduction of partially-spendable meta currency (unlocking new items a little bit at a time, like how Dead Cells does it.)I'll update this review as more game updates happen. For now, I recommend it wholeheartedly for fans of dark fantasy dungeon crawlers and action roguelikes, with the caveat that they should have gone early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fire, but it definitely is one of the harder roguelikes on the market. Playing this game gives me the same feeling Elden Ring does, where opening the game takes a little bit of effort. I need to put myself in the mindset that I'm about to really go through a difficult run.The whole "You lose knowledge (the meta resource) when you die" complaints are really... stupid. When you complete an area you can use the knowledge that you have to buy. If you have an upgrade pending worth 20, and you finish a level with 22, you can buy that upgrade. You arent forced to beat the game just to spend them.People may ask "Why can't you just invest your knowledge?" Well, Dead Cells does that and you see what is wrong with it. Dead Cells has upgrades that literally take runs upon runs upon runs just to unlock. People can beat the game multiple times just to unlock one upgrade because they're so artificially increased. Players at the 2BC level often have to spend time "grinding" the meta resource just to progress. This game is not perfect, but it is definitely worth the purchase. If you like Soulslike games, and you like Roguelikes, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Loot River is a tough roguelike but can be very rewarding if taken the time to master its mechanics. I'm not just talking about the obvious features like attacking, dodging, and even leveling up. I'm specifically talking about knowledge of enemy types, weapons, and the pretty unique mechanic of moving platforms.It doesn't hold your hand much, and the meta currency you earn are lost unless you reach the next biome which really increases the tension during runs and can alter your play style and state of mind. Left stick to move your character and Right stick to move the platform you're currently standing on. This sliding puzzle-esque mechanic is good change of pace in this genre and you can use it for many different advantages.Obviously moving platforms are used to traverse and solve puzzles, but for combat it opens up more strategy. You can segment waves of enemies by luring them and moving away, charge up attacks then move in for the kill, and even skillfully run past them. Loot River is not without its flaws though and I might be nitpicking here, but I the amount of camera shack after EVERY hit on an enemy is disorienting, you whiff and enemy whiff attacks, the elevation combat can be misleading, and the dodge roll is a sort of teleport but with how claustrophobic things can get it makes sense you'd need it that way to maneuver around.Check out my full gameplay review video for Loot River. _childDocuments_.review: What is Loot River? It is an action rogue-like game with soulslike vibes. The game has a very dark world, hometown area with NPCs like in Dark Souls 2 (Majula) and quite unique gameplay. The gameplay is very tricky - it requires you to use your "tetris skills" (connecting block on which you stand to other blocks in order to advance) during combat alongside your fighting skills (dodging, parrying and timing attacks).Pros- Very strong Dark Souls Vibes (it even has NPC like patches)- Good, innovative fighting system. Everything works smooth. - Gameplay is fast and enjoyable. I didnt experience any bugs. - Items are different from each other and you can only bring two weapons. If you find one more you have to chose which one of the current ones to abandon. The same with armor but you can only carry one. There is no vast inventory/magic  bottomless backpack - it is good this way feels more realistic. I like it.Cons- Maps are very boring. You just jump from one tetris block to another which are placed on map resembling a river - seldomly anything looks memorable or interesting. - The aim is to finish the level and get to the boss/defeat him as fast as you can. If you do it in under few minutes you are rewarded vastly. I do not like games that are with timers especially soulslike.- When you start mission you have to finish it. You cannot retreat to home town to regain health or level up. Upon death you lose everything - both currencies and even your level and skills! You start completely anew except for your 2 weapons. And it is very easy to die - the healing is very scarce. It is my main problem with the game - it is too unrewarding and difficult in a wrong way. I like difficult games but hate when I am being robbed of everything I acquired during gameplay every time the character dies.   - The fighting even tho it works great it gets old very quickly due to similar levels and enemies - Loot river uses pixel art, which I am not fan of. It just looks dated and like an old game.The game has good concepts and is definitely something you should try if you like rogue-likes. I would not pay the full price - this indie game definitaly isnt worth 20GBP or even 10  - for under 5 maybe. It did not work for me but I am not saying it is a bad game - for sure some people will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Loot River is yet another of literally hundreds of lazy amateur 2D retro top-down shooter/brawlers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  This is a weak and badly made top down brawler with trash tier graphics and worse gameplay.  And no content to speak of, it's all procgen. There's a gimmick where you have to move platforms that you stand on, so it's like one of those annoying block puzzle games.  Yeah, that is not what the old, dead top down brawler genre needed to keep it on life support.  Ugh. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.To make matters worse, while lazy, low quality pixel "art" has been used, making the game look bad, many elements of the game aren't done with pixelcrap... which accomplishes a couple of things.  First, it shows the developers perhaps could have done better and they knew it, so that's a major screwup.Secondly, it destroys any hopes the developer had of creating a "retro aesthetic" as their excuse for the lazy pixelart compromise... It looks completely inauthentic from a retro gaming perspective.  Visually, this is a hamfisted mess, a dogs breakfast of bad visuals, and this kind of laziness and poor quality should never be foisted on gamers.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls and game handling are notably very clunky and unsmooth here.  It's janky and unsatisfying to play... and any experienced gamer will tell you, the handling, responsiveness and general gameplay feel of the control scheme must be well polished for this kind of game to succeed.  Unfortunately, this is something the developer seems to have phoned in, with little to no apparent gameplay testing.  They dropped the ball on this one.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Loot River has the almost unethical price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Hogwarts Legacy", "Dark Souls III" or "Day-Z".  No pixelcrap is worth $25. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly.

But they're janky in a fairly predictable way so it's fine. There are also some minor glitchy issues with the AI and platforms that don't  really impact the gameplay but are clearly buggy.There does seem to be a potential issue where you can get a lot of knowledge early and unlock everything super quickly. You just use the knowledge gathering sword, it gives way to much. But after playing some more I'm thinking it may actually be intentional. It doesn't seem overpowered to have everything unlocked early and the unlock tree seems to be at least partially intended to be used to tune the drop pool on new playthroughs, so the knowledge sword is more of a tool for doing that. But IDK maybe they'll patch it, I unlocked everything from clearing about 4 floors with it.The structure is kind of weird, it's a sort of a roguelite like Hades where you get stronger between runs, and like Hades you dying a bunch is part of the story. The map is mostly always the same, but the arrangement of platforms varies. So you can always navigate easily but the details change, it's really smart. You also go back to home base between floors (walk to the head to heal), and there seems to be a bunch of different paths that you can unlock.It also has this sweet potion mechanic where you invest potions at the start of a floor to get twice that many back at the end. This is a great idea and the game seems balanced to make it worth using. You can choose which bosses and how strong you want to get, to some extent - just getting to the end is quite fast once you know the fights you need to do, and you can skip most enemies, but if you do you won't level up. And the platform fighting is sick, it's really well thought out and adds a bunch of unique tactics to have fun with. There's some puzzle parts too, I like them, they're fun and well designed. But they're clearly a secondary feature, you can even turn on a guide mode that tells you how to solve them. Sometimes you have to solve puzzles while fighting enemies which is great.On top of all that the story is very intriguing. I haven't finished it yet but I really want to, they've done a great job integrating you dying into the story and the worldbuilding is very compelling.Overall a really fun and unique game, it's kind of weird at first but once things start to click it's great. It's definitely an indie title, it could use some polish but it's still worth playing IMO. Maybe wait for it to be on sale though. Go find the Houndmaster guy, 10/10 boss design and fight.

_childDocuments_.review: I did a few runs and the mechanic with the platforms on the river itself is very interesting but it didn't really feel like there is much more to the game. you can pretty much make your own path through out the dungeon with the platforms, avoid enemies or lure them on your own platform to not get overwhelmed which is very cool but everything else seems very bare bones. most of the weapons from the start felt quite bad and not really fun to fight with and the enemies felt very weird, especialy when i was using stuff with electric properties which sometimes did stunlock the enemies, making the fight a piece of cake, but it also sometimes just skipped their attack animations so i could not even react to anything they did.Overall if it wasn't that expensive i wouldn't mind it, but i really did not feel anything around the first two areas and in the first hour of gameplay would warrant that kind of pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked loot river a decent bit but with some caveats.- gorgeous pixel art everywhere from the different equipment and level environments; in particular the water ripples look stellar. Was nice to see equipment actually shows up on character too.- interesting run modifiers equip some of them positive. For example spear enemies kicking your ass? Equip a run modifier so spears were never invented and those enemies' attack range is way smaller. There are some really cool ones ranging from making a particular boss easier, enemies hit harder but drop better gear etc. The true run ending requires equipping a set of these to ensure can fight all bosses in a run which was really fun to do.- some nice variation in equipment. This is stuff like really cool weapons ranging from a chakram thing can huck at distant enemies to big slow axes. Spells are a lot of fun too with traps, shields invisibility etc. Lots of variety and all feel pretty good. Armor as well gives unique abilities like being able to dash through enemies or more mana regeneration- once got used to it the combat. On normal (different for easy) you cannot dodge out of attack animations which heavily punishes spamming. The platform moving is incorporated really well letting you setup arenas isolating tough enemies or can do drive-by heavy attacks to do hit and run attacks. - how often you get new gear is glacially slow and early runs feel incredibly samey before start unlocking more weapon and spell variations. In particular if you miss how to get the spell vendor can be a long while before can mix up the combat- Even after getting all vendors a completed run can not give you enough currency to unlock something new which feels awful- There is one sword in the game which gives you the meta currency on kills with charge heavy attack. This completely breaks the unlocks; in one area killing every enemy with charge attacks I got enough currency to buy every single weapon.spell/armor etc. I actually enjoyed the game a lot more after getting the run variety from having everything but still felt kinda bad having unlocking new stuff speed be so slow then all of a sudden got everything- parry timing feels incredibly off. You have to hit the parry button well before the enemy attacks and basically looks like you are back in a neutral stance when the parry can go off. It is an incredibly generous timing window but just feels a bit out a whack of where it should be. Parry window is tied to a stat so that might be part of it- Some really awful bosses in particular the matron. The second phase of this fight the boss spins in a half circle doing a stabbing attack and repeats; there is no pause, they just do this over and over. I found I could only hit their non weapon arm as it went by and not their body etc. The stab attack is trivial to dodge (can just stand in a corner) but the window to attack them is so small the fight ends up taking for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ever. It was kind of miserable how long this took each runOverall I liked the ~10 hours I put into this but after getting the all boss clear run I think I'm done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:  Decent enough little rogue-like that gets by mostly on its novelty. It's not going to be the first, second, or third rogue-like I recommend, but you could do a lot worse. Long version:  It's a Tetris-themed hack-and-slash. Where else are you going to get that?I've put a little over 5 hours into the game at this point, and I've already seen the default ending and the extra ending that forces you to jump through some hoops. (Granted, I only knew what steps to take because I read the Achievements guide explaining all of the steps, but it is doable.) It's not particularly challenging as rogue-likes go, though the RNG can screw you a tiny bit. On my most recent run, I wasn't getting any gear drops for the longest time, forcing me fight through about 2/3 of the game with my crappy starter weapons. With my DPS so low, the boss fights were pretty dicey. I couldn't blow through them with some chunky weapon, forcing me to "git gud" in real time. To the game's credit, breaking up enemy parties and pulling them into one-on-ones when they were about to jump you feels satisfying and is easily the highlight of the Tetris effect meshing with the combat. By the same token, you can also pull off hit-and-run tactics, slamming your platform into an occupied area just long enough to run in, do some damage, and float your platform away again before they can chase you down. In fact, the biggest mark against the Tetris side of the game is the fact that the game's developers did not do more with it. It might have been nice to give the platforms some extra wrinkle to really spice up the combat, like combining platforms of two different colors to produce special effects. Low friction? Higher or lower defense for anything standing on it? Increased chance for item drops if you kill an enemy on a certain type of ground? What could have been. So what does the game really offer beyond the Tetris and the swordplay? There's actually not much else to write home about, but I'll write more words anyway.Yeah, there's a parry mechanic, but I find the game a bit muddy on the visual side of things. The game has its unique art style at a glance, but it an be hard to focus in on your tiny character and what the nearest enemy is doing. Landing a parry in this game feels great, but it was never consistently great. (Then again, I've always sucked at parrying attacks in action games, so consider the source.) I eventually fell back on my Dark Souls instincts and spent most of my time dodging through enemies to stab them in the back. The dodge is usually reliable, but it can be kind of janky with how it lurches your character across the screen. So can inputs altogether. Once in a while, the game would not pick up the fact that I had tapped the attack button. It did not get me killed, but it is annoying to see it happen.The weapons could also afford to be a little more balanced. I suppose there is something to be said for unlockable weapons doing more and being more, but there is really no reason I will ever pass up the rapier (which pierces shields), a weapon with an elemental affinity like lightning or poison (the damage-over-time effect is crazy), or a greatsword (which is just stupidly powerful as a weapon class). The other weapons have their niches and their gimmicks, like the spear that can double in size or the ring blade that can be tossed like a frisbee for ranged attacks, but they all tend to lose out to those three categories of the rapier, elemental additions, and greatswords. Fortunately, you can carry two weapons at a time, and the game is entirely beatable even with the mediocre weapons. (There are also charms and helmets to be unlocked, but they have a much smaller impact on the overall flow of the game. Weapons are what's really going to change up each run.) I was really charmed by the NPC who gives you the opportunity to trade away a health potion at the start of each major level/dungeon in exchange for giving you back twice as much at the start of the next. Do you want to gamble and give away three of your starting potions in the hope that you won't need them and be rewarded with a whopping six potions a little further down the line? You can do that. Or you can play it safe, giving up no potions but getting no more as you progress. It's usually wiser to bet on yourself and give away a potion or two at the start of every area. In fact, the high-risk, high-reward strategy of giving away all of my potions at the start of the game usually worked out in my favor, as it got me started with a nice little stockpile when I went to pick up my deposit from the NPC. All in all, Loot River is a fairly tame rogue-like with one or two really cool ideas sprinkled in between some blandly inoffensive combat. I doubt it will be anyone's favorite game, but it was a fun afternoon. And it's probably one of those rogue-likes I will fire up for a few runs every now and then when I don't have anything else on my plate. It did its job by entertaining me, and there's just enough here that it makes me want to see what straka,studio does with their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of, if not the, best dungeon crawlers out there, especially for a 2D pixel one. Not to mention the pixel art is stunning and very smooth, almost like its just a pixel filter over animated models. Quite a challenging game, and yet, once you get used to the controls and the way its played, the combat feels so smooth and satisfying. Just now finding Emmet I can see there is so much more content than I had originally thought there would be for the player to find and unlock, and I'm excited to do just that. 10/10 across the board, would highly reccomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loot River

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely title! Keeps the right amount of gameplay complexity to not overwhelm you but also doesn't dish out a crazy amount of uncontrollable random generation. In fact, it feels pleasantly benevolent in challenge compared to e.g. Dead Cells by allowing you to plan what gear you get across the game and thus model the mechanics and approaches you want to utilize. Especially when given the platform sliding mechanic and its shenanigans even with the simplest abilities/weapons, there's tons of ways to play around with/invest time in that I have yet to explore all them.There's a few oddities to the unlock system involved (you get a copy of an item right after unlock and then only as monster drops) but none of them water the core experience but actually became more interesting the more you progress in the game. Overall, I'd give a sparkling 8/10 if Steam had a rating system but will give it ye olde thumbs up instead. Highly recommend if you like action roguelikes but don't wanna waste all your time acquiring crazy skill to beat it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loot River

_childDocuments_.review: A nice roguelike with a stunning pixel look and an epic soundtrack creating a poetical atmosphere with a really interesting playstyle somewhere between a topdown Dark Souls and shifting 'tetris' platforms. Although there's a small plot don't expect it to be lavish but anyway the main focus is the combat. With every run you can unlock new weapons, spells, hats and robes with different buffs.Most of the time there are just two or three enemies on a platform which can be beaten easily but it gets really tricky when you have platforms with dozens of different enemies where you need to find a good mix of attacks, dashes and parries but another interesting strategy is to use the platforms to your advantage by separating an enemy from the rest and fighting one after another. This makes combat dynamic while still leaving room for creativity in decisions instead of just 'waiting' for the next damage window.Once you managed to complete the game don't expect the next run to be easy. Addictively fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Loot River

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun roguelite with interesting mechanics. The ability to time your attacks by moving platforms as you attack is cool at first but I started to use it less and less as it slows you down. You can do other things however, like separating the enemies or moving them out of range of the enemy that creates a field of shielding. My biggest issue so far is the parrying system which is about the worst one you can make. As you pretty much cannot react to enemy attacks in time, you have to press the parry button before the enemy even starts attacking. As a result you are rewarded for spamming the button without thinking. I guess If the goal was meant to make it dependant on endurance, which increases the parry window as you level it up, then it works well in that regard.If you don't have a controller don't even think about buying. With how the game works the devs might have as well given  a disclaimer that mouse and keyboard is not supported.  If you do, it's pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming into this, a souls-like roguelite with puzzle exploration, it seemed like this game was made for me. After 10 hours, the time I needed to reach the true ending, my verdict is: pretty cool. Let's break it down.In this game, you control a humanoid character, but also the platform they are on. To navigate the dungeons, you have to maneuver both in order to clear obstacles that are in your way. This gives exploration a puzzle component, which really helps the game have a nice rhythm. Alternating combat and puzzling very quickly like this almost melds the two together, and in some cases you can reach a flow state where you just speed through both combat and puzzling and you satisfyingly move through the level very quickly. However, due to the procedural nature of the puzzles, after a while you start to see patterns and repeated puzzle ideas which you already know how to solve, and at that point the puzzles start becoming a bit of a hassle. Fortunately, most puzzles are very quick if you know how to solve them. Another issue with the procedural puzzle generation is that, though rarely, some areas of the map are completely impossible to access because of unsolvable puzzles. Fortunately, it never gated my way towards the exit of the dungeon, thanks to alternate routes or the inaccessible sections just being dead ends. All that being said, the moving platforms add to the game, rather than take away from it.The combat is the other pillar of the game. You have a dodge and a parry, as well as a very large roster of weapons with unique traits, animations, damage scaling and heavy attacks. The combat is satisfying enough, though at some points it's a bit unfair. Several enemies have very wide attacks, to where actually avoiding attacks laterally is not feasible, and most enemies have extremely quick attack startups, to where parrying on reaction is almost impossible. However, once you learn the enemies' AI, you start to parry by predicting when they will attack: combined with a very generous parry window, this leads to most one on one fights being completely trivial. Group fights, however, are another story entirely, and that is when the combat is most enjoyable: since trying to fight large amounts of enemies is basically suicide, you have to use every tool at your disposal to come out on top, such as using spells or manipulating the platforms advantageously. The bosses are not abundant, but they are distict and come with interesting gimmicks and challenges, for the most part, but they take the unfairness of the combat up to eleven.Let's move on to what is probably my favorite part of the game: run progression and meta-progression. Leveling up, allocating stat points, finding better weapons and spells, swapping charms, getting stronger throughout the run is great, with perhaps the exception of gold and vendors, which feel useless on most runs. Meta-progression, though, is even better. Run after run you accumulate knowledge, which you can spend to unlock new equipment to find on your journey. Slowly expanding the stuff, especially spells and weapons, mean that you can learn how to use them effectively bit by bit, rather than getting overwhelmed by strange weapons at the start of the game. The part I liked least about this side of the game is that you unlock the vendors by finding them in the dungeons, and I feel like some of them were a bit too hard to find. The next form of meta-progression comes in the form of run modifiers, which you unlock by finding them during your runs. They make your life easier at first, as you get your grips with the game, but as you get better and better, perhaps after having successfully completed your first run, you will start swapping them out for modifiers that unlock extra bosses and areas in order to reach the alternate, "true" ending. There is some jank, with enemies occasionally being unresponsive or getting stuck on staircases, but it didn't impact my enjoyment of the game meaningfully.Overall, if the game looks cool to you, I think you will likely have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: is a fantastically stylized rougelike with an inventive movement system, that is not without its flaws. Primarily, it suffers from a difficulty curve that I find too steep to be enjoyable. Had it not been for the saving grace of "Easy mode",  would've sat unfinished in my library -- which is a shame for an otherwise great experience.That is not to say the game is impossible, but instead that it lacks any recompense for that sudden difficulty. For example, there is no major story progression between runs like there is in . Nor is there any choice, before runs, in the equipment you gradually unlock. Instead, unlocked items simply have a chance to spawn in the world, meaning your fate is quickly in the hands of the RNG gods. Some players may enjoy this, but I found it sadly tedious and frustrating.All that being said, "Easy mode" (which truly needs a better name), allows one to experience the excitement and satisfaction of this game's wholly unique movement system, satisfying and punchy combat, and jaw-dropping pixel art. I definitely recommend , even if you have to put your pride aside and join Weeine Hut Jr's like myself. Have fun!P.S. If you are struggling or simply confused, I highly recommend the following guide:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great base. I think I may have been a moment away from winning my first run, sooner than I expected (lost track of my health at the boss though). I'm hoping there is more content to keep me coming back, but with how active and passionate the developer is, I expect there to be something down the line, if not already here. Too soon to say if it has lasting power, but I really like what is here and see myself playing some runs before work for at least the next week or two.The game plays like a souls-like, but top-down and 2d, which I wouldn't expect to play very well, but the gameplay actually feels pretty smooth and enjoyable, and it's still easy enough to keep track of what's going on. I was expecting more emphasis on the "puzzle" part of the game,  but the raft movement is an enjoyable mechanic nonetheless. It allows for basic tactics like luring single enemies to fight when you first start off for practice, and fun speedrunning challenges.I also enjoy the fact that this game actually veers closer to roguelike territory, rather than roguelite, As much as i suck at them, I do enjoy punishing games like Spelunky, games that let you play for 30, 60, 120 minutes at a time, and throws all that progress into the fireplace if you have the audacity to die, and yet somehow makes you hit the retry button for "just one more" run of punishment. That said, this game could be harder for my tastes. Parrying is maybe a little too easy, and when you couple that with the badge that heals you for successful parries... well, I think that's going to be in the inventory of everyone's first win, is all I'm saying.I have a lot of hope for this game, what is here is great, and the developer seems passionate and very involved with community feedback. I hope the game takes off and can fund future updates, I want to see this game get as bloated as The Binding of Issac :P I plan on buying the soundtrack when I get some spare funds just to chip in a little more, I appreciate developers that sort through the feedback and reviews for ways to improve their product.SUGGESTIONS: Maybe a tighter parry window? May need to rework the animation or something to make it work, shrug.  Maybe options to make the game harder, and tossing the shorter parry window in there? Moar levels and bosses :D Hopefully figure out a vacation plan soon too, y'all seem like you could use it. Keep up the awesome work :D
_childDocuments_.name: Loot River

_childDocuments_.review: this game is absolutely overflowing with fresh ideas and stunning art. the slow and deliberate attacking brings me back to Dark Souls 1 nostalgia - and DS1's chunky, satisfying pace - while the moving rafts introduce a sort of mobility that just doesn't exist in any other game. Loot River feels like nothing else, and will feel like home to people who enjoyed older soulslikes. If that's not your cup of tea, though, stick it out until you unlock some spells and weapons! it won't take long, and in time you'll have loads of options for pace and playstyle. and if somehow you don't think you'll love this game, I *insist* - it's worth it just to encounter some game design ideas that i've scarcely seen elsewhere, and that really ought to get more attention. PS THE MUSIC SLAPS

_childDocuments_.review: I got 100% on this game. I would say this game is ALMOST pretty good. The game needs a lot of polish, between timing on parries, platform smoothness, and overall balance. Really, the game needs a serious once over for balance, there are so many garbage weapons, rings, and spells, while the strong items can make the game feel really playable and decent. The enemies are decent, but the main strategy of the game just comes down to slow combat, then parry parry parry, riposte with your strongest weapon. I really think there is room for improvement, a lot of room honestly. The style is something akin to Hyper Light Drifter and Blighttown from Dark Souls 1, it's honestly pretty cool. The substance however, is disappointing.8/10 Style3/10 Gameplay It's worth grabbing if it gets cheap, definitely a worth a 10 dollar or less sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very intrigued by the gameplay mechanics when I first saw this game, and after purchasing it I'm happy to say I enjoy the puzzle style of moving the platforms beneath you. Now, after reaching my first Victory, here's what I have to say:- I agree with other reviews that the combat feels a bit...off. At times you can cheese it but if you go for a parry, sometimes it doesn't connect. Maybe it's my inexperience with these kind of souls-like combat games.- There were times where I felt lost regarding what I was supposed to do. After the initial playthrough, I don't think that'll be an issue anymore. - Looking at the run modifiers, I'm interested on what else there is to explore in this game. - There are a few bugs I found when moving from the "first level" platforms to the stairs of the "second level" ones.I will recommend this game with the hope that the devs are able to continue fleshing out the game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Dev team changed my opinion. I'm leaving my original review for transparency though.I'm actually really moved by the developer's response to the opinions of players. As a professional who works in art, I know how hard it is when feedback don't go as planned. It's really common to see people dropping their projects even if they took years, some people will try to "learn" of the failure and move on. I've done so myself. The team behind this game actually went ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane and in a very short time fixed a lot of stuff that made this game really hard to play and turned it into a really fun roguelike that I'm personally looking forward to keep playing. There's still some polish to do, but as of today, I can confidently say that if you like roguelikes, there's a big chance you will like this one.ORIGINAL REVIEW:I'm eager to change my recommendation and looking forward to some patches! I believe this game needs two things: To fix the absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dash animation, and fix the loot. How is it possible that you don't loot anything interesting in several runs in a game named LOOT River? Also, this doesn't really feel like a roguelike, as there is little to no evolution from run to run. I want to like it very bad, but I can't enjoy it in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: Loot River

_childDocuments_.review: Look River is a pixel art, top down, action RPG Roguelite where walkable terrain is moveable by the player. Think of the slide puzzles you used to do as a kid.Everything you step on looks like a puzzle piece. Think tetris pieces. The right stick moves the pieces in any direction. To progress, sometimes pieces will be in the way, and you'll have to move them around in order to continue on. You can also move the pieces while in combat, separating packs of enemies into 1v1 situations, or use it to just run from everything if you wish.I think it's a lot of fun. It adds a light puzzle element to the game, as well as some strategy. How should I move the pieces during combat to help?The combat is on the slower/more methodical side. You have your dodge roll, parry, basic combos, and charge attacks. Most enemies do a good amount of damage before you upgrade your HP so you want to be careful. You can also use the ground to your advantage, moving the sliding sections to take more favorable fights.The parry window feels good to me, and can be increased by leveling up Endurance. (I like this a lot)Overall it follows what you'd expect from a roguelike, progress, collect currency, spend it for permanent buffs, die, repeat while you get stronger each run. Loot river also features a level up system with stats, you can upgrade strength, dexterity, vitality, endurance, all to increase things like HP, Damage, Parry Window, etc. each run. These stat points reset when you die. (You always start at level 1, but you can start with better weapons/passives) You also have equipment (armor and ring slots) plus two weapon slots. There's also two spell slots and a mana bar!I'm enjoying the game a lot so far. The art style is nice, I enjoy the theme of the game, the combat is fun, and the level up/build choices generally feel meaningful. I enjoy how it incentivizes you to fight all the enemies because they give EXP for levels as well as currency for upgrades.However, I do have a few issues:1. The "dodge roll" is more like a "teleport then do a weird roll". I'm not sure if the animation is incorrect, but it feels extremely weird and disjointed.2. Enemy attack hit boxes. Sometimes an attack "hits" you, but you just don't take damage. It's not really an issue... But it just feels weird.3. The game does feel a bit like it's still in early access. Just not 100% there.I'd recommend this game if you're a fan of rogulites with combat more on the harder side. At least early on don't expect to be able to just mash light attack to victory. Hopefully it gets some patches to fix some of the minor issues.Otherwise, if you're hesitant adding this to wishlist and waiting for a few patches could also be a good idea.

_childDocuments_.review: Explore procedurally generated labyrinths in a dungeon crawling action roguelike that combines tense, real-time combat with spatial block-shifting - slide blocks of ancient ruins, fight bestial abominations, loot, explore, level-up, strategize, cast powerful spells, die and wake up anew.

name: BUSTAFELLOWS
detailed_description: STORY Arrive in New Sieg, a beautiful fictional town. Step into the shoes of a strong, smart and gifted journalist in this romantic adventure. You play the part of a young woman with the ability to leap in the past for a very short period in the bodies of others, which you use for data collection and helping people. After witnessing the murder of a crooked lawyer – she goes back in time in an attempt to save him. Thus, the journey begins as our protagonist goes back in time in the body of another person and tries to warn Limbo. It's up to you to figure out how to save him! FEATURES Unravel mysteries and solve puzzles Take the lead and choose your destiny Romance 5 dangerous fellows, each with an unlockable side story Unlock different endings Experience a unique interactive gameplay Meet guests characters from Side Kicks! Navigate through gorgeous visuals and polished animations Listen to a complete Japanese voice cast, including KENN, Yoshimasa Hosoya & more Will all routes lead to romance? Which happy ending awaits you? Play to find out! CHARACTERS Teuta - the protagonist (the name can be changed) A 21 years-old freelance journalist working in New Sieg. She witnessed the murder of her brother when she was younger and became a reporter for her to serve justice. She has a mysterious ability that allows her to leap in the past for a very short period in the bodies of others, and uses it to help people and collect data. She is a bright and cheerful woman with a positive personality. Although she is a reporter, she is not skilled at taking pictures. Limbo Fitzgerald - A Crooked Lawyer A 27 years-old Lawyer. Limbo is known for advocating in court for even the toughest criminals. Although he is called a crooked lawyer, he is extremely skilled, and he is popular in the city and is seen as a hero. He abides by the law in his own standards and serves justice. Born into an extremely wealthy family, Limbo is soft-hearted. Shu - A hitman that silently eliminates hitmen He is 28 years old. Shu is a heavy smoker who makes a living as a bounty killer by eliminating other hitmen. He is a top-class martial artist and specialised in long-range sniping. The best sniper in town, he has no other goals in life apart from executing those on the list left behind by his foster parents and mentor. Helvetica - A professional in changing people's appearance A 26 years-old plastic surgeon. Popular in New Sieg, he loves beautiful things and constantly rates passer-by women based on their looks. Highly confident in his skills, he believes that people can be reborn by changing their natural features. Mozu - An autopsy Specialist At only 25 years old, Mozu is the chief of the autopsy department and work with the police forces. He is often misunderstood as apathetic and indifferent towards others. His way of thinking is usually from a medical point of view, which sometimes creates unexpectedly fun situations. Mozu talks to corpses and it is rumoured that he dissects animals as a hobby. He likes riding bicycles. Scarecrow - A Self-proclaimed Underground Boss A 22 years-old cyber-geek and computer hacker who is famous on the internet for hacking, money laundering, stealing, etc. Thanks to his abilities and connections, he is a self-proclaimed underground boss.

_childDocuments_.review: While there are problems with PC port not being the most intuitive or accessible, the writing is charming and humorous, the characters are endearing in their own ways, and the backgrounds of the game is simply gorgeous. There's also animation in both backgrounds and cut scenes, making the game livelier than your average visual novel. Definitely recommended <3EDIT with problems for PC port since I was asked to clarify: Basically PC port has a problem with not being able to change between full screen and windowed, at least not anywhere accessible enough to be seen easily since I have been searching and there weren't any in the settings. The full screen is also not up to scale with the monitor resolution so the art ended up looking low-quality with the edges bleeding. You can see problems like this for games like Steam Prison which look fine windowed but poor quality full screen.The PC port basically took a copy-pasta of a handheld game but without the necessity optimization to play on a computer. The controls are just not immediately obvious to a player, I said this as someone who played a lot of visual novels in the past. I had to do a bunch of tests before I found which buttons do what. Home = Quick Menu, Page Up/Down = Auto/Skip. Even with a controller, the game's binding is really weird and makes it inconvenient to navigate.These are not usual keys used in visual novel on PC and there is no instruction for it the moment you open the game. Also, nitpicking but I'm a player who don't really like voices because I read really fast but even when you mute voices, some lines still bleed in. While I had the voices enabled, there are lines spoken without translated subtitles on screen to help players who don't understand Japanese.
_childDocuments_.name: BUSTAFELLOWS

_childDocuments_.review: Visually-speaking, this is possibly the highest quality otome I've ever played. Characters blink, their mouths move when they speak, and even backgrounds have some animated aspects, such as water movement, crackling fires and other neat little touches. The art is top-notch and, in my opinion, the game's strongest point.Another aspect that makes Bustafellows a standout is the heroine. Teuta has much more presence than a lot of other protagonists in the genre because she has a face, voice and strong personality. She's her own character and not one of those 'we're going to make MC as bland as humanly possible for self-insertion purposes' heroines, which I very much appreciated.The Steam version is a bit clunky compared to the console release, and at times it suffered from some pacing issues, but all the characters and their interactions were enjoyable. The main story was great; I really loved the group dynamic they established in the common route, and while Shu and Crow were definitely my favorites, there was nobody I really disliked as a love interest. They each had an interesting story behind them and unique dynamic with Teuta.The final stories that attempt to wrap everything up were the only part of the game that just really didn't do it for me. I can't go into much detail without spoilers, but the best I can describe it is everything comes at you too fast, parts of it felt out of nowhere, and for me it was a downer. Not awful enough to ruin the game, and some of the ideas were good, but I feel like they were executed poorly.All in all, Bustafellows is one of the better otome games out there. It's not perfect, but its strengths shine brighter than its flaws, and I'm dearly hoping Bustafelllows Season 2 gets localized so I can see more of its wonderful art and characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I find this important to a lot of people I am putting this here so it is easy to find. BUSTAFELLOWS has an ESRB rating of Mature 17+ with content warnings of blood, drug references, partial nudity, strong language, suggestive themes, use of alcohol and tobacco, and violence. Several potentially upsetting and/or triggering topics are mentioned in the game to varying degrees, including but not limited to body image/ appearance, death, explosions, firearms, kidnapping, loss of loved ones, mental illnesses and disorders, murder, needles, self-harm, sexual violence, suicide, surgeries, terminal illnesses, and viruses. Visual-wise, there are infrequent camera flashes, flashing lights, and some RGB glitch and blur effects used.  As far as my review I find the game is quite good but there are some annoying things. One to open up the menu you have to press home. I should not have to look up how to get even to the basic menu after starting the game.  The keybindings suck! There are quite a few talking parts that do not have translations. I did not find out until too late that you can bring up the log to find out what was said. But unfortunately that is not the case for the ending video after Auld Lang Syne. I still don't know what was said. Overall I would recommend be be aware it is dark and does have a lot of triggers.

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say that I'm grateful that Pqube decided to pick an otome game, and I really do hope they're willing to bring us more! Unfortunately, I'm not a fan of this game... I know there's another one coming out, but I'll definitely not get it.This game is really good at the first chapter (and grabbing you to stay), 2nd is okay too, then at the 3rd you start wondering when the otome part is going to start, at the 4th you're poking your eyes! I mean, there's no need for 10 hours of just little somethings happening, the rest is just people getting together drinking and eating, that could be sum in 30 minutes, and superpowers stuff that are never explained, nor doubt it.The inconsistances in this game are HUGE! The romance and built up is just not there! Our protagonist is okay but sooo dense!You know, people come into these games with different interests, some just want the slice-of-life, others just want the gansta feeling, some even just come for the VAs.... I don't want a game that drags on nothing for hours (like Cafe Enchante where I was already mutilating my wrists after 20 hours of common route); and I also don't want that cliche type of otome where, I see you, you're mine!All I ask in an otome game is a good built up... and lately I can't find that (I really miss the old games), but 12 hours of common route, then getting into LIs route and still no build up in there, just kills me...Sorry, I cannot even recommend it for myself, much less for others....Forgot to mention:- Sprites are blurry as hell in this game;- Skip feature is really annoying, you take like 30-40 minutes just skipping to get to next route;- You absolutely cannot play this game between PC and Steam Deck! Your memorabilia is not retained from one to another, then you miss SIde B and other extras;- Can't seem to find a window mode, only fullscreen- Can't seem to find a quit game button option

_childDocuments_.review: I've yet to finish this game, but I've cleared chapters to the point I've reached Helvetica's exclusive chapter, and I can honestly say this is one of the best otome games I've ever played. I heard the people who worked on it didn't even think of it as an otome, only giving it the label after the fact, and I can see why they did, and I think that's why I love it so much. Although Bustafellows showers you with male love interests from the beginning, it does not do the same with affection, nor does it provide a love meter for any character (don't worry, as I implied above, each character has an entire chapter dedicated to them based on your choices). Instead, you are left to enjoy fascinating mysteries all while teaming up with fleshed-out characters. I seriously have never laughed more while playing an "otome" game, the main group of guys is sincerely funny and built upon excellent chemistry. It isn't just the love interests either, the side characters are also fantastic, each one so unique and interesting on their own that the entire world feels bigger. You have characters in positions of power, characters from low places, even an enthusiastic and respected trans woman (it feels weird that I have to congratulate a game for having a fun trans character, but you really don't see one that not only has their pronouns respected, but that they're seen and treated as other women are, it just really drew my attention). And let's not forget our main girl! I seriously love how she's written so much, I can always sort of get myself into the mindset of a timid and helpless MC for the sake of the sexy love interest to show concern or protective instincts, but it's so much more fun to have an MC who's not only capable on her own, but has sense and abilities that genuinely help and impress the other characters, it's so, so refreshing!! Overall, I'd absolutely give this game an 11/10, not only for spooking me with it's tense atmosphere, but with how maturely it handles difficult topics such as social class and cosmetic surgery. If you're having a tough time deciding on which game you're going to buy next, then please consider this one, it became my favorite in the genre overnight (literally, I'm typing this at 1:00 in the morning).

_childDocuments_.review: BUSTAFELLOWS easily takes the top spot on my list of favourite otome games. I have absolutely no regrets about buying this at full price, even if there are some minor technical issues in this port.I didn't expect to experience so much emotional damage while playing this, but I very much enjoyed every bit of the story this game provided. Everything about this game is just perfect: the story, the characters and their personalities, the voice acting, the artwork - all of it is simply top notch. Speaking of the artwork, it is stunning, especially considering the fact that plenty of things in the background are actually animated and give more life to the environments. I'm really hoping BUSTAFELLOWS Season 2 will also come to Steam!Separate thank you for giving us the main character who actually has a personality, and a consistent one at that. As someone who doesn't self-insert in this kind of games, I greatly appreciate having a great main character like Teuta. All of the love interests were different and likeable as well; there's none of them that I heavily disliked for once. Every love interest has their own story that doesn't make you re-read the same things many times since their stories are set before or after something happened in a different route. Even the side characters were enjoyable, no matter good or evil, which is also a plus.Technical problems didn't ruin my experience personally. Some text that doesn't show up during screen transitions can be easily accessed through the text log; there was never anything important to the story that was missed. A couple of times I saw text go out of the text box, so that's probably the only annoyance I might have been taken aback by. Generally, the translation was really good, even though I noticed a few typos, but nothing really that would hinder the reading experience. My only complaint would be the odd choice of control buttons, but once you remember the buttons, it stops being an issue.Summary:- Interesting story, especially if you like crime stories and drama.- A few short side stories in the extras.- Set in the fictional town of New Sieg, USA.- A very good cast of characters, both main and side.- Great voice acting.- Very detailed artwork with minor animations in the background. - 5 love interests, with multiple different endings for each. I got completely destroyed by Limbo's second bad ending. :(- MC and main cast have a good group dynamic outside of the romance routes, but it's also present within the romance routes, so that's pretty neat.I can't recommend this game enough. I've had a very enjoyable time with it, so if you like otome games, you definitely should give this game a look!

_childDocuments_.review: In Bustafellows you play as a 21 year old freelance journalist named Teuta, which you can rename her to another five-letter name if you wish, working in New Seig. She even has her own newspaper column in the local newspaper, New Seig Today, which it seems is loved by those that read it as she aims to look into perspectives that aren’t normally thought of and it’s often described as not pushing an opinion on readers. Though, she has an interesting secret. Teuta has the ability to go back in time. Granted, she can’t control how far she can go back (and at most she can only go back a couple hours) and she gets put into a random person… but still.This very power pretty much caused her to run into the five love interests. Limbo, nicknamed as the crooked lawyer by the public, was actually someone Teuta was looking into interviewing. But when she runs into him again, he was shot right in front of her and died. Teuta decides to save Limbo and thankfully Limbo heeded her warning despite not being too convinced. Limbo, who brings one of his friends Shu along, isn’t convinced no matter the proof Teuta has, but he decides to keep her close after she mentions certain names. Which also turned out to be perfect timing as she was looking for another place to stay anyway due to the apartment she lives in is basically falling apart. This also pretty much has her caught up in their various schemes as well, which she helps out in as it might help her with writing a juicy story.And from here, Teuta gets to officially meet all of the five love interests. We already know Limbo, the confident crooked lawyer that can seemingly get anyone an innocent verdict, but he does have his own set of morals and want justice to be dealt to those that deserve it. Next is Shu who is the group’s hitman and smokes way too much, even trying in places where it’s not allowed or doing it in spite of others that don't like smoke in their face. Shu has his own kill list for personal reasons, but he does take up other hits whether it’s for the group or for another. There’s Helvetica who’s a popular plastic surgeon that’s a master of disguise and changing his own voice and is way too focused on looks based on how he rates other women and comes off as narcissistic as he knows that he’s attractive. Next up is Mozu, a coroner who works closely with the police as he often is requested to do autopsies due to his proficiency, but he will often fake corpses and reports for the group if needed. At first, you really think he’d be the one that isn’t too sociable or detached, but he has his own sense of humor, he cares about his friends, and he is often more in tune with knowing how other people are thinking or feeling than others. And lastly, there’s Scarecrow who gives off a mysterious serious vibe as he’s a self-proclaimed “Boss of the Underworld” and is the group’s computer geek that has master hacking skills, but he’s actually an awkward cute dork that gets dunked on so much he implemented a “Respect” jar… which the others will often put money in in advance to insult him.I was actually quite surprised with how much I loved the love interests. It’s really easy not having the best impression on most of them when they first appear, but as Teuta hangs out with them more and you get to know them, they really do grow on you. Really, the only one I didn’t like as much was Helvetica, but that was mostly due to his Side B and extra episode. They all give off a “found family” vibe, despite how much they say they’re totally not, and they have a really good dynamic with each other (which Teuta easily slides in). I loved every scene where they were interacting as it really elevates it and made the funny moments even funnier (even causing some surprised “he did not just say that” reactions where I couldn’t stop laughing) as you can realistically see these characters doing what they did. Bustafellows does a really great job in establishing these characters so much in so little time.After you complete the first four chapters, you’ll be able to go down the love interest routes. The route you’ll be going down are based on some of your choices and the game confirms which route you’re going down twice. You’ll go down the route right after the end of Chapter 4 and their route mostly deals with their past and their trauma, though there is room made for them to get with Teuta. I do recommend doing your first playthrough blind just to see who you get first (I personally got Scarecrow first). Once you finish, a “Side B” will unlock, which is basically an epilogue that may also have some cute or angsty scenes with their relationship, and an extra episode revolving around either Teuta, them, or both of them cooking something.Though, throughout the game and when going through the last two ending chapters that unlock after doing all of the routes, I really had a feeling that this would have benefited from being longer and maybe even having the love interest routes being the last chapters of the story. There are plot points that pop up but are forgotten about as the game moves on and a lot is often packed in a short timeframe. There are stories that do work with a fast pacing, but not here. Not to mention the two chapters meant to close everything out had little to no build up at all and were surprisingly short. To the point where it felt like it was a last minute addition to have a couple more twists and shocking reveals. The last two chapters do have aspects that I loved and thought worked really well for the story, but it could have been better if there was actual build up to it and longer.However, Bustafellows also other problems which I’m surprised most of them are in a $40 otome visual novel. There are little things like misspellings or using the wrong word here and there, flip flopping between Teuta’s brother’s name being Zora or Zola (most notably after Chapter 4), and suddenly shifting perspectives for one text box. But then you’ll encounter text that will go past the text boxes and the backlog (which shows up more towards the end) making you miss the rest of the sentence, there were a few sentences that didn’t make sense, there’s no option to change your resolution/go into windowed mode (which can make the videos and art look bad in places) and there’s no way to exit the game through the main menu. The controls for the most part also don’t follow the standard control scheme that many other visual novels have (I haven’t played any games that used the “Home” and “End” buttons). Not to mention that there are spoken lines that don’t get subtitled. It’s fine when it happens in scenes, as it is translated and in the backlog and in retrospect most of it isn’t necessary, but there’s a whole ending video that isn’t subtitled and there are six other extra videos (that are focused on two characters talking) that aren’t either.While Bustafellows has disappointing problems both with how the story was handled and on the technical side, I would still recommend it (though maybe not for full price). It was an enjoyable experience that I honestly couldn’t put it down, despite my original plan of spreading it out, where the only thing that got me away from it was when I had to eat or sleep; and the artwork and voice acting was great. I wouldn’t get this if you were expecting a great crime mystery, as it turned out to be the weakest part of Bustafellows, but if you want great character dynamics and a “found family” feel this will satisfy your desires.

_childDocuments_.review: This became one of my favorite otome, with Code: Realize and Our Life. And I think it's deeply unfair so many people focus on the minor technical flaws to say the localization is bad.Those flaws include very few instances of text going outside the box (iirc I counted three or four instances of this), untranslated background lines (you can check those in the log), resolution issues (I didn't notice these as I'm playing on my laptop, I thus advise you to also play on a laptop or computer with a small screen) and unintuitive controls. And I will insist, these are VERY MINOR. It didn't stain my experience in any way: going into the log to check unstranslated background lines becomes a reflex (and most of those are literal flavor background noise) and come on, it's a visual novel, once you learn the controls that's that.To be honest, I vastly prefer an otome with minor technical flaws and a good localization than a game which is technically perfect with a mediocre or even bad localization (that's for you Aksys). I truly hope those who've bashed the game over those small details are at least as much critical toward Aksys.Anyway, the game is great, it's more romantic than 90% of otome I've played, there's a LOT of content, all the LIs are great, and it's very entertaining. If you love otome or romance, don't hesitate !
_childDocuments_.name: BUSTAFELLOWS

_childDocuments_.review: Controls were unclear and not made for all keyboard types. As for the game itself it honestly drags along at some points. You don't need to have a "Wait for the next chapter' animation pop up in between every chapter, especially when they're fully released. While I understand not having captions for every VA line (Some being more background flavor I assume) there's an entire scene late into the game that would absolutely be better with them. At times the POV changes characters, which would be very intriguing, but the lack of telegraphing when it was going to happen left it jarring in some places.I won't spoil the story but I will say the writers aren't very subtle in certain ways the female characters are portrayed. ||There's only so many times you can play off comparing MC to a child.||A huge negative as well was that there isn't an exit button in game. I could (with some difficulty) find the menu and main menu, but as far as I could tell there was no exit game in either the main or in game menu options. Every time I closed it I had to windows out and close it from the task bar. Also this game covers multiple triggering topics that aren't all assumed to be covered by a mystery or murder mystery label. I completed it because I tend to be a completionist on games like these, but do not take my time spent playing as an endorsement to play yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: The individual romance stories are great, but the ending to the main story was so bad, not a single hint was dropped the entire game about anything, they just drop bombshell after bombshell on you and it was very forced and made no sense. Honestly ruined the entire game for me. The character you play as is also very childish and annoying. I will say the art is stunning and again, the characters you can romance have interesting stories. The mystery part of this game was not very well done like the romance. There was also some confusing dialog throughout the game which I attributed to translation errors, it wasn't a big deal to me, just thought I would mention it for people who have trouble reading in between the lines. I go back and fourth on yes or no to recommend it so I'll say yes if you like romance, and no if you like mystery.

_childDocuments_.review: An ultimately, personally disappointing game. _childDocuments_.review: I played Bustafellows, it's not a bad game, but it's not extraordinary either. It has its strong points and weak points but for my part it is a fake Otoge. And it's clearly a game that I do not recommend to everyone. It's more a kind of adventure game with "feel good" atmospheres and from time to time we put “crime scenes” to put a little action in the game but there is so much inconsistency on the crime scenes, which I think could have been better if the game was longer in length, on some scenes.The highlights of the game:- dubbing + feel good scenes = ASMR- humor = the game is very fun to play- if you like restaurant scenes where we talk about everything and nothing between friends (I really like that, especially when it's mixed with feel good)- uses all the technology of the latest VNs (the jump/skin jump to the next choice = this is the first time I've seen this in a VN)The weak points of the game:- crime scenes have too much inconsistency- scenes that are sometimes too short which undermines the depth of the game- the game is too short and this is felt with certain rush scenes which impoverishes the game (especially the end of the game)Romance:- the first part of the game (about 10h) has no romance. We are really on pure visual novel with "feel good + some crime scenes". This part is +16.- the second part contains the romance always with crimes but I found some scenes hard and the rating is +18. All stories from each guy are not bad and honestly some scenes are cute. But I found the romances very short with barely 2h30 of romance per ways. A major problem is that since there was no romance in part 1, the way the heroine or the guy falls in love together is sometimes implausible or too fast.- part three is the spoiler part. It all takes part 1 without taking part 2 into account, so we just come back to "feel good + some crime scenes", so no romance. The game is +16.Honestly, I saw that it was one of the first games of the team. It's not all bad, but there are some areas for improvement. I think one of the problems is that the game is too short, and the team is not made to do "black crimes" scenes but rather "feel good X romance" scenes. But the team has tried some points to create originality compared to most Otoge and I can only encourage the team to try to do better next time.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the very last story chapter after the individual routes. I'm speechless. I got goosebumps. Crying. Chest hurts. As someone who has been in the Otome game scene since 2015, I must say this is one of the best visual novels I have ever played. This is my first ever actual game review, BUSTAFELLOWS deserves it. The writing is insane. This game manages to have a story that cleanly comes back in a full circle(pun not intended.) Just, wow. If this is your first Otome game, this will set your standards so high. The interface, vocal performances, plot writing, illustration, soundtracks, and many other things are just so amazing. The characters are not what I expected, they broke off the character archetypes I had set in my head. I ended up loving characters that are not my type in other games (Limbo Fitzgerald.) This game is so good I found myself recommending it before I even finished playing all of the main routes. Please play this game. You'll be doing yourself a favor. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: A bad port but a very good game. If you can get past the following issues, the game is worth it. In any case (and despite the problems linked to the port), it would be a shame to skip on this game if you like the Otome genre. It's really one of the best Otome games I've ever played. - The game itself  is very well done. There are animated cutscenes and backgrounds, lots of CGs, sound and visual effects that complement the story well. Each chapter is built as if it were an episode of a series, with an introduction that puts us right away in the action and a credit sequence. Each chapter ending is followed by a short video teaser of the next chapter. - The main cast is very likeable and funny. I really liked the bond between the heroine and the guys. Their relationship felt very natural. - One of the few Otome games where the secondary characters are not bland and feel like characters of their own. They are as engaging as the main cast and they are not there just to highlight the heroine. - I loved the heroine. She's not your typical clueless and passive protagonist and she has goals of her own. She actively participates in every chapter, in every case. She is also voiced. Usually, I don't like voiced heroines in Otome games because their voices are often very high pitched, but this is not the case there. - The story is engaging and quite funny at times. Each route introduces a mystery to be solved. In this aspect, some routes were definitely better than others but I really liked the game's overall plot. - The introduction is quite long (4 chapters in total, each chapter with a specific case/mystery to solve). Usually, I don't like long introductions but it was very well done and helped flesh out the character's personalities, motivations and relationships. The game does a good job of balancing serious, action-oriented moments with fun, slice-of-life moments.- The controls are awful and don't make any sense. It's a pain just to save or access the log. - You cannot use the CTRL key in this game (which, in most PC visual novels, allows you to skip text faster) so you have to use the game's skip feature which is way too slow. It's espcially annoying when you have to replay 4 chapters just to access another route. It took me more than 30min just to skip the introduction. - You cannot save during choices. - It was already mentionned but video previews for each chapter (and videos in general) are not translated. This is espcially frustrating because  is :  - Similarly, sometimes characters will speak and it won't be translated on screen (you have to access the log, which is a pain, to see the translation). I know it was meant to be a stylistic choice but it doesn't make any sense.- There is an annoying problem with sound balancing (even if you try to change it yourself through the option menu). Sometimes characters will speak very loudly and in the next line speak very quietly. It was especially noticeable with the character Crow.- The individual routes felt a bit short. The romance part was a bit rushed in my opinion. - I noticed quite a lot of typos and some text that would not fit on the screen.
