_childDocuments_.review: I finished chapter 1 and the anime boys are very pretty so far. Scarecrow best boiEDIT: Finally finished this game!!The art in this game is fantastic. The CGs are excellently done and a delight to look at. The sprites are all very well done and the facial expressions show the characters' emotions very clearly. There's a large variety too, including back sprites, which is especially cool since I've never seen those in an otome. The backgrounds are even animated!The music is wonderful and sets the tone well. My favorite tracks were Come and Get Me and The Yellow Rose of Texas -unplugged-. I wish there was a Spotify or YouTube playlist of the tracks.The UI is great to look at and simple to read. My only problem is the odd controls (seriously, look at that controls guide on the community tab for this game before you pick it up) and lack of a proper quit button. The skip is also quite slow, but since there's a jump to the next choice button I wasn't too fussed about it. Some text spilled out of the text box once (IIRC it was on Limbo's route) but I could still make out the sentence.The localization is very well done. The only issue I had was some inconsistent naming of side characters (is it Zora or Zola? Pick one and stick with it lmao).The story is very captivating and kept me clicking through. I enjoy the episodic storytelling for the common route. The only route that I feel had any narrative issues was Limbo's, the pacing was strange and there were some plotholes. His bad ending #2 was the one that freaked me out the most though, so he has his strong points :pThe Joker and Full Circle episodes have some controversial story decisions, but I still enjoyed them. The story threads that are brought up in them leave some nice room for the sequel at least.My favorite route is Shu, with Mozu as a very close second. I enjoyed Crow, but not as much as I thought I would. Similar case for Limbo. Helvetica is trash man. Each of the major themes of each route is executed well (kinda iffy on Limbo but it wasn't the worst). I particularly enjoyed the theme of grief and death in Mozu's, and how it links to his profession.Tier list for quality of plot:Mozu > Crow > Helvetica > Shu > LimboTier list for level of romance:Shu > Limbo > Crow > Helvetica > Mozu

_childDocuments_.review: Bustafellows serves as an enthralling experience for crime genre enthusiasts, delivering an intriguing story complemented by appealing character designs and artwork. It explores the murky waters of morality, prompting players to examine what constitutes right and wrong, thus adding a philosophical dimension to the game. Each character's unique and engaging backstory ensures a rich and diverse narrative, catering to a wide range of player interests.The story unfolds at a comfortable pace. While player choices may not significantly alter the narrative, they contribute to a more immersive experience by allowing players to feel integrally involved in the story's progression. Nevertheless, the otome elements in the game seem slightly underdeveloped. The focus leans more towards constructing the characters' backstories and the overarching narrative, leaving the romantic elements slightly overshadowed until later parts of the game.The PC adaptation of Bustafellows poses certain technical difficulties, primarily due to its original design not being suitably optimized for PC platforms. This has resulted in several minor yet rectifiable problems that remain unresolved, such as the requisite usage of the 'alt+F4' command to terminate the game. Prospective buyers are advised to consider purchasing the PC version only if absolutely necessary. Furthermore, it's important to note the lack of Steam Cloud support. Consequently, save files will not seamlessly synchronize across different devices - including, but not limited to, a Steam Deck and your primary PC - without manual intervention.In conclusion, Bustafellows provides an ideal starting point for those venturing into the otome genre and a compelling treat for crime drama enthusiasts. For a refreshing blend of intricate storylines and fascinating characters, this visual novel is well worth your consideration.

_childDocuments_.review: So yea…this game is abysmal.  I mean just literally unbelievably bad.  It fails on a narrative level, it fails on a game design level, and it even fails on a technical level (at least as a PC port, maybe the non-port original Japanese version is fine).  It is incomprehensible to me how this game has such rave reviews.  On a game design level this is an utter failure.  So the game elements of a visual novel normally at least allow you to make decisions to affect the story.  This game has no actual decisions that affect the story in any meaningful way.  In 35hrs maybe there are 6-12 decisions you make.  I want to be clear I’m not saying the game has 6-12 decisions that matter…it has 6-12 decisions as in except for those exceedingly few times all you are doing in this visual novel is just reading text.  The decisions also do not affect the narrative except for who you end up romancing…but the decisions that lead to your romance options are so spectacularly stupid I needed a walkthrough to do it.  The main decision that chooses your romance option is a personality test you take near the beginning of the game…no competent narrative would ever base who you romance on a personality test.  The whole point of a romance visual novel game is choosing who you want to romance and the game literally takes this one and only decision away from you.  It’s even more baffling because the game literally has scenes that so easily could create decisions to allow you to actually have narrative involvement in picking your romance option.  One point the romance options all offer names for a cat you adopted, the game could have had this be a decision where whoever’s name you pick gives you points to become closer to that person.  Another instance you are picking out a bathing suit.  Why are these not choices?The game design issues even go further than that though.  In order to actually progress in the game you have to play through the game 5 times and romance each person.  Oh also the game doesn’t tell you this it just rolls the credits after your first play through, I had to look online to find out the only way to progress the story to the end was to romance all the people.  There are skip options so the repeating dialogue can all immediately be skipped, which was a great design feature…but still…even this absurdly minor decision you make of taking a personality test is completely nullified, because you have to romance all of them to progress to the final 2 chapters in the story.  Narratively this doesn’t even make any sense because the true ending of the game shows you actually didn’t romance any of these people…the romance stories are basically side stories that never even happened.  It’s so baffling.  So again the one decision you have in this game is a personality test to pick who you will romance…which has no narrative impact on the game because narratively you don’t actually romance any of these people.  As a narrative beat it’s revealed your character has the ability to time travel.   A competent narrative could have EASILY wrapped this into these options and could have done something like every time you romance someone the game results in your death and then you could be “thrown back” in time to the start of the game until you realize you can’t romance any of these people if you want to avoid dying and repeating this loop.  Because the writers of this game are incompetent they just have the game end and make you replay it without it actually being part of the narrative.Finally, the game fails as a narrative.  The story of this game is just terrible.  It’s billed as a romance and murder mystery game.  Again…the romances are not actually part of the main narrative…nor do you have choices who to romance so that’s a failure.  However, I would also say none of the 5 characters you can romance are characters I found any attraction to.  They are all horrifically emotionally damaged individuals and the main character can’t even hold their hands without apparently feeling like she is doing some kind of extreme sexual act.  The main character is 21 years old who is a major news reporter in what is clearly New York City and yet thinks about sex like she was a child and the other characters also seem to treat her like a child.  It’s disturbing how emotionally and mentally childish she comes across.  The game also massively fails as a murder mystery though.  For starters this is not a puzzle mystery, meaning there are no clues or dialogue that can lead you to figuring out the mystery.  This is a thriller, so already I dislike that.  Still as a thriller it really doesn’t work either.  The game is broken into “chapters” and each one tells it’s own separate story, but none of those stories are particularly interesting as they have no room to breathe.  They have to be wrapped up so fast they can’t even tell much of a story.  In the first instance you find out a lawyer has been murdered so I assumed this would be the central mystery…nope about 2mins after you find out about his murder you then figure out who did it.  Which is then wrapped up within another 2hrs and you never talk about it again.  Each chapter is similar.  The overarching plot involves a shadowy organization that runs the city and you trying to figure out whose behind it…the ultimate twist of this is incomprehensibly stupid.  Besides the facts no clues could have ever led you to this conclusion it’s just so random and laughable This is a travesty of a game that no one should play.  Please for the love of god give some visual novels your money that deserve it.  Go play Lady Killer in a Bind a fantastic erotic romance game, or how about Seeds of Chaos easily the best visual novel I’ve played with a ludicrous amount of decisions that drastically change the plot of the game and who you can romance and where characters don’t act like children.  If you want a great visual novel murder mystery instead of a romance game then go play Zero Escape (1, not the others, 2 and 3 are unplayable) or AI Somnium.  I beg you do not waste your time on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the highest quality otome game that's been localised into English so far. I have yet to play a game with this many immersive elements, I'm shocked that this isn't the standard. There's animated CGs, dynamic voice work, characters with multiple outfit changes and poses. Their eyes even move to the speaking character if they happen to be on the same screen. This game has THE smoothest intro to main menu transition I have ever seen in my damn life.So let's look at our lovable cast:- Limbo is the confident and suave type who always seems like he's in control. He's funny, and supportive, but he's actually a lot more childish than one would think. He's a really good poster boy.- Shu is a kuu-leaning hitman who spends the most of the game coming off as a nonchalant, blunt, laidback, 'I don't give a hoot' type. But in actuality, he really cares for his found family deep down, and although he comes off as objective about things, he's an emotional guy.- Helvetica is this game's flirt and makes a move on you the first scene he's in. He's a bit superficial and places a huge emphasis on people's appearances. He cares for the others but doesn't like to rely on them.- Mozu is a coroner who has a very unique, more analytical approach to life. He's a bit eccentric, but he is considerate and tries to understand things around him.- Scarecrow is the cheery, friendly type who is also the comedic relief of the game. He's more empathetic than most people and encourages everyone in the group to get along, but he often gets made fun of by the others.Everyone has their own serious problems that you have to help them overcome. There's plenty of angst, pain, and plenty of fluff too.Pros: - This is one of those games where even if there was no romance, it would still be just as good. The dateable characters are all lovable as hell and have a found family situation going on. The banter is the funniest stuff I've ever read. Every other otome I've played, there's always at least one guy I don't really like. Not this game though, even the guy I rank last eventually grew on me. These characters are all really hard to hate. Some of the side characters are just as memorable and fun. Valerie and Carmen are girlbosses.- The heroine, Teuta, is a solid character in her own right. She has some hallmark traits of what main characters are like, but none of them are written out in obnoxious annoying ways. She's funny, she's relatable, she's proactive, she takes action to change things in the story.- Shu exists.- The plot is fairly interesting. It's set up to feel like a crime TV show, and it covers many incidents that are connected by an overarching story. I'm not a crime noir type of person, so I don't know how this compares, but the story is engaging enough. The common route is about 1-4 chapters long, and the 5th chapter will be your man's story. It's shorter than most games, maybe 2-3 hours each depending on your reading speed, and his means that the romance doesn't kick in until way into the story, but I personally liked that each relationship builds up on friendship and the care they have for each other as a found family. The themes in this game were good, like a better version of Collar x Malice, if you've played that.- The translation is amazing. I've spotted a few errors here and there, but nothing that's taken me out of the game. Many of localisation choices are literally perfect, modern, and not clunky.- Whoever does the background art is a god. They're also animated and atmospheric.- Gap moe king Shu.----Cons: (I've seen these come up a lot in other reviews but honestly, it's not a big deal.)- The controls are a little funky, but since this game has been out for a few days, it shouldn't be too hard to find a guide somewhere. To sum it up: Home key for the menu to save and load and skip. End key to get to the backlog.- Volume can be weird, you will need to fiddle with the sound setting to find what works best for you.- Can't save during choices, but it's no big deal because you'll be using the skip function a lot anyway. Just skip back a dialogue.- You need to keep going back into the backlog in order to see what some characters say. The game has this thing where voices will sound when the dialogue box hasn't come up yet, which will lead into the conversation. I like it, it's a really nice and immersive design choice but it sucks for translators. This is pretty much fine until the last chapter, because it ends with a scene where you can't pop up the backlog to see what the character said.- Animation resolution is not good, but not super poor.- Story wise: I can't say much without spoiling, but while the bulk of the story is fine, there are a lot of loose ends. I personally was very disappointed by the ending chapters. This game direly needs a sequel, and I'm glad that one's been announced! Here's to hoping PQube will pick that up too.Thank you so much PQube for picking up this game! And thanks for the new boyfriend. Anyway, stan Shu.

_childDocuments_.review: It was okaish, but I doubt I will be back to play and I definitely won't recommend buying for the full priceI purchased this game with intention to spend my weekends with a new interesting story, interact with it and with a possibility of some romance. Keep my intentions in mind , cause it will be important understanding my points. Also please keep in mind that I fully played only 2 routes - Mozu and Shu (just began Limbo).Before starting, wanted to address the most common complain among "not recommended" reviews regarding "not translated dialogues". But, to be fair, it were just chunks of convo during scene transitions. Meaning, when MC moved from one scene to another - there was animation and while we, from MC perspective, were focusing on the next set - there were minor conversations not translated on the background. I think it has plenty to do with convenience (must have been just technically complex to do ) rather than intention. Never bothered me, never was important. So, yeah...Back to review, generally in the game I found this to be GREAT:- Visuals.   Background arts, animation and in general CGs were well spread, nicely done.- The plot.    The plot for the 'otome' genre was approached differently. There were multiple serious issues addressed  such as human trafficking, corruption, poverty, the gap between poor and rich and etc. I loved it. Developers did their homework, and I generally found their approach interesting. Also some scenes were def set for more mature audience (not steamy tho - shame), as a adult player I appreciated it.- Characters.   I genuinely liked how some characters were opening before MC though the story. Once I played more - picking one person and interacting with them, I enjoyed how each character's personality just unwrapped before me - their fears, secrets, motivations. That was interesting.- How routes different from one another.   As we talked about diversity in characters, we shall also talk about how much work has been put into each story line (of course I played only 2, but I am amazed). Starting from side characters for each route, different background sets and endings with twits.Now, the things that made me ROLL my EYES :- Lack of personalisation + obvious otome traits.     One of the major factors for purchase was that this game was"non-otome but just tagged as one" I was greatly disappointed.Yes, in this game MC did not blush easily or jumped to conclusions if someone smiled at her, but it is so far from "doing my own thing". The choices were spread widely among the story and influenced very little outside of 'i am going for this dude'. It was not very obvious(thanks for it), but still choices had a very small weight to them and didn't shape experience for me.MC was girly-girl (if this makes sense) - young, naive, who changed the world with a touch of her finger, made people fall for her and at the same time appear strong. Even with these girly-girl trait I would be okay if only developers dropped some small details that basically make a person - individual. They were not subtle about this. They throw away any chance for me to resonate with MC. She would say, act and do very specific things that I was not sure I can resonate with as a reader. Yes, I am aware I am buying a story, but I am also buying experience and play as the MC, not along the MC. I would prefer if they gave us a meaningfulness choice what to do/say or not to do/say, or just cut out all of these small details, which would've had absolutely no changer for a plot.  Sometimes I had to just pause and roll my eyes at how stupid MC acted and I had no choice but tag alone with it, cause, again, they DON'T give you a choice. - World building.   some details were not relevant, at all. We were introduced to people, events and details which at the end played no role whatsoever. I did finished only 2 characters, but  some story lines so heavily introduced to me in the prologue and chapter 1,2 (and we are talking hours here) - were not necessary and did not resolve themselves at the very end. It felt like the developers did tons of work , spent way too much time of exploring different side stories and slowly introducing them to us, but suddenly Big Boss came and told them they had to finish it ASAP, so they rushed things over, did not explain some details and just pretended to forget about some side characters (computer, monitor, blood, encryption, organisation... if u know what I am talking about...)Overall, it was okay to play for a weekend, but I doubt I will be back to play other routes.  I can not recommend to buy for a full price or to those who are not into-Otome genre because it is one, just a bit more subtle.PS. just corrected some spelling mistakes

_childDocuments_.review: Of course, both my opinions and the metrics from which I form my opinions are subjective.  Simply top-notch- need I say more?  Their faces are very well designed but I have a couple of qualms about their clothing; for a 5/5 character design please see Dramatical Murder  Very good voice actors. Shu is Reiner from Attack on Titan! Shu, is Reiner, from Attack on Titan!   I have a short attention span: the story isn’t extremely enthralling but it wasn’t at all boring. The story is meaningful and I played it because I enjoyed playing it and not because I needed to kill time. I weighed the logic of the story more lightly than the other three factors. Also the story is SO funny.  Vulnerable, healthy and mature. Therapists would probably recommend this game for healthy relationships and healthy communication. Little to none toxic masculinity.  Unique personalities, three-dimensional human beings with realistic emotions. No strong character development but honestly not complaining because they showed vulnerability so well.  Doesn’t feel well-researched. Heavy topics used as means to evoke emotions but doesn’t try to properly represent.  It’s not good. Time-travel loopholes. LIs and MC’s friends are either OP or have professions that’s convenient to the plot. Conflicts not suspenseful and resolutions don't feel earned.  Also, just for fun,  (oh boy will probably be controversial) (very light spoilers- descriptions about LIs' personalities):  He’s like the sun: warm, confident and energetic. He’s like the default ideal of an attractive American guy who’s well-adjusted. I think he is the best match for Teuta- they think in similar ways.  I think he’s really hot. Probably the hottest out of everyone. He’s aloof but also he’s really nice. He’s assertive without being mean or patronizing.  Sigh, his character won’t age well at all. But his story is genuinely such a good one. The writer did him dirty.  Intellectual, gentle and kind. He is actually everything I want in a partner. He has to be my favourite, and by a large margin too. I like him so much that I literally fall for him in the other LIs’ routes. Just like, ahhhh he’s so knowledgeable AND he’s good at cooking AND he likes animals AND he’s so nice and caring and would notice you being upset when no one else would ahhhhh I think I’m gonna pass out  He feels like a younger brother. He’s sincere and strives to be a better person and I want to be by his side all the time. You know how Teuta calls him Crow-chan? Yeah that’s what I’d call him too. ________________________________________Full review:  Not only is everything well-drawn, but also the composition of the CGs is so satisfying.  (for a 5/5 character design please see Dramatical Murder) Can you tell the personalities of each character based on their character design? From their faces and bodies, yes; from their clothing, Mozu and Crow yes, Limbo, Shu and Helvetica no. For a more in-depth look at character design please see the last section of my review.  They're just good actors. Like they're just good. Brings the experience to a whole new level. Also, Shu is Reiner from Attack on Titan!!! I’m about to open my window and scream!  Helvetica uses honorifics all the time. His speech should have been translated to be more formal than everyone else's, but I don’t really feel that they’ve done that.   I have a very short attention span. Nonetheless, at no point in the game was I bored. I wasn’t exactly addicted, nor did I stay up late eager to read more, but the story isn’t boring at all and I feel that time playing this game is time well-spent.  Characters are so healthy for each other and are able to have mature conversations about difficult topics- therapists would probably recommend this game as an example of healthy relationships and healthy communications. They take care of each other emotionally. Also, NO TOXIC MASCULINITY AT ALL (except for Helvetica, but only slightly to moderately so.)  LIs have their unique personalities- everyone's route feels different. But they are all developed fully as humans with realistic emotions and are thus not one-dimensional. You bond with the characters because you will have seen them in their most vulnerable state- they feel sad, they feel hurt, they show you all of themselves. Teuta is really awesome too! She has her own voice and is a strong person. There are not many romantic scenes but you do feel that the characters like each other. I didn’t feel like the characters had major character development though. We only get to see a fuller picture of the characters but they don’t really change, but honestly, I’m not even complaining because they do the vulnerability part so well. Also, having character quirks for the sake of having character quirks really bugs me- like how Helvetica uses honorifics all the time and Mozu with his medical terminologies. Also the fact that MC only barely made the “half-your-age-plus-seven” rule for the oldest LI.  The game touches on many sensitive topics and focuses on minorities. However, it seems like the game uses heavy topics for shock value, but doesn’t research what it’s actually like to be in those situations because of the sheer lack of detail they give. (Light spoilers about the themes of this game)  (Major spoiler) Also,  is whitewashed. That’s really really problematic.   Time-travelling creates so many logical loopholes, which the game doesn’t make any attempt to close. Plot twists are very predictable. Conflicts are often resolved by the LIs and Teuta’s friends being too overpowering or by luck, which makes the conflicts not at all suspenseful and makes their resolutions feel unearned. Shu’s route is the best-written imo; it avoids the problems above AND is really funny. I honestly played everyone else’s route solely for the characters and not the plot though.    Their hairstyle, eyes, expression, build and poses tell us a lot about who they are. Limbo has big, welcoming eyes and hair typical to bois with sunny personalities. Shu has mature, smaller eyes and bangs that cover half of his face to show his cool reservedness. Helvetica has eyes that are tilted down almost to a biologically unrealistic extent, which fits well with his popularity. Mozu has  Also men in this game have really broad shoulders. Don't know if that's good or bad.  Crow and Mozu's clothing designs are ok. Mozu's over-sized off-the-shoulder jumper reflects his shy, off-beat personality. Crow's outfit is quite otaku. Limbo, Shu and Helvetica's clothing is really disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is worth playing, it's just it doesn't have what it takes to become my absolute favourite and I can't in good conscience wax euphoric about it. It doesn't really leave a lasting impression, as the story, instead of focusing on the genuine, becomes too contrived.  However, the story isn't bad by any means and does offer a few heart-rending and heart-warming moments. This is a good  visual novel with otome elements…but it lacks heart, it doesn’t feel genuine and leaves me with pretty mixed feelings because the story, while good in concept,  feels overthought, instead of being more simple, straightforward and genuine.  The gameplay is not really unique, that's an overstatement in the game description. The game offers otome, but goes beyond it and the storyline is good, though some elements are a bit weird and thrown in without much of an exploration  even for a game where the MC leaps back in time when she conveniently needs it.STORY: Mc is a reporter that comes across a weird bunch of people by a weird stroke of fate and stumbles into an thrilling story about a mysterious organisation. We get to know the characters while exploring their routes in the otome parts, and then the storyline concludes in two extra episodes. The stories are about choices, about becoming strong, about what that strength is, about  facing  up to things. The characters are varied and interesting. Limbo – a crooked detective but has a sense of justice. His feelings of fear, caused by a past event and encounter, feel the most genuine and this route is the most satisfying in terms of the build-up and the bond formed with the MC. His feelings run deep and I felt his route establishes the strongest, most palpable bond. and a sense of yearning. It's a route with the strongest mutuality for me. Shu – the strong silent type, an assassin but his side B ending is touching. He knows his feelings Helvetica – a man remade, he’s the flirtatious trope, his story is tragic but overdone in a way that put me off. Mozu – the silent scientific type. I felt sorry for him. I didn’t feel his bond with Mc was very strong though Crow – an overzealous person, he’s not my favourite but his story does have an interesting twist that makes him more than he seems. What makes his story for me is the father. I like father-son storylines The problem is only Limbo’s route made me feel strongly enough, though Shu's ending in Side B was pretty nice and Crow's too. The otome part is satisfying enough – albeit I hated how the routes seemed to poke fun at proposals. It put me off and was a mood killer.  In terms of romantic fulfilment, Limbo is my favourite. The feelings there run deep and the story creates a very convincing bond between him and the MC. Shu’s ending in side B is touching, he wants to talk to MC's parents and in general he is more open and confident about his feelings – I liked that.   I liked the father-son storyline for Crow, though he’s not my favourite. His ending in B is cute .  Mozu was ok, Helvetica was my least favourite, though his story was fairly interesting, albeit overdone.  I just feel the author tried too hard to make it striking but the stories end up being over the top, too melodramatic and not in a good way. But the characters find strength in each other and  what's also important is that there's a strong sense of mutual support - the MC supports them but they do too.Like in similar games, the otome routes served to explore the backgrounds of characters and they end before the main plotline is solved. The plotline is then solved in an extra episode / ending that does not in any way invalidate any of the obtained otome endings - this is very important for a satisfying otome experience. At the same time, I'm not particularly fond of these type of solutions. If you want to make it an otome, I feel it's better if you split the end into five routes too. But, the extra episodes really  solve the story and tie loose ends about Teuta's friendship with Adam and Luka and about the mystery of  a criminal organistion Ryu Lopez, both of which form the core of the plot and both felt overdone and contrived in places. I found the otome part of the game satisfying and was glad the extra episodes didn't touch the romantic choices any more.  There are some unexpected twists and some side characters do surprise too. Liked+ Gorgeous CGs + characters, otome routes and extra episodes with some added warmth told from the guys' POV.  + extra episodes with other characters+ the plot ending does not invalidate otome endings + story concepts and ideas+ japanese voice over+i mmersion+ not vulgar+ MC is kind+ Adam Favourite routes in terms of who I like: and romantic fulfillment Limbo > Shu > Crow > Mozu > Helvetica Favourite routes in terms of story: Limbo > Crow > Mozu > Helvetica and ShuDisliked + the UI, while very neat, is a littlle complicated  - it took me a few tries to find the hotkey to bring up menu during the gameplay (Home button)+ Subtitles don't always appear - there are parts at the beginning of chapters that lack them and it's annoying+ overall storyline lacks heart, but is not devoid of warmth + poked fun at proposals in otome – that was annoying and mood killer. I like proposals. + some typos - but they don't ruin the immersion + some  weird ideas - Alexy and his changing body idea, I found it weird and not thought-out enough.   +Carmen+ Zora part was overdone, overly tragic and melodramatic+Magda + there is no need to make the names so weird. While Scarecrow, Mozu and Shu are fine, Limbo and Helvetica are just silly. + I don't particularly enjoy the comment Limbo makes about Valerie (his sister) in a swimsuit, it's off-putting. And there are a few scenes of similar off-putting kind. It’s worth playing, however. The game is interesting, has a few ideas that do speak to the heart, Limbo's route is fulfilling,  but at the same time the game does not feel heartfelt enough for me – and “noir” has nothing to do with it. It's hard to find a truly satisfying otome nowadays, perhaps because I have outgrown the genre. This is one of the more interesting ones all in all.

_childDocuments_.review: No spoilers review:Positives:- Engaging storyline, to the point where you can't sleep til you know what happens next at times- Very fleshed-out characters; you WILL have favorites, whether they're one of the boys or not- Just the right amount of silly and serious- You may actually learn some things from this; they did their research before discussing almost everything in-game, and I am impressed- It's depressingly real to a lot of what goes on in New York City...because we all know it's New York City- Outside of the main character's skill, you WILL learn about the entire universe of the game- One of the bad ends made me legitimately cry, it hit so personally. It made me afraid to do the rest, but because the story was so well-done- The voice acting is BRILLIANT. Not a single complaint. The faces line up quite well almost all the time, too- I, at the beginning, couldn't stand 2 of the boys. At the end, 1 is one of my two favorites, and the second is, well...look, he's not a bad guy. Just not my type. I think the voice acting saved one, and the story saved the otherNegatives:- Cutscene subtitles don't exist, though some can be seen if you press 'End' and scroll through- The controls, outside of mouse controls, are not intuitive for PC users, and you'll have to find the picture guide on one of their twitter handles (it's not hard to find at least)- Some subtitles (about 3 total in the game) roll off-screen and you'll just have to guess, but they're not majorly plot-important- Gratuitous English. "NEXT EP-SODE" - It completely knocks you out of the zone. Fortunately you can Enter through it after the first time, but it'll occur when choosing different boys.- Though there were some very cute scenes, I never truly fell for any of the boys. But this could just be meTl;dr - Amazing voice acting, animations, and world. Educational and real to some very dark things that happen in very big cities. Whether or not you fall for any of the boys hard enough to write fan fiction, the story makes the game worth what I paid. I 100%ed it.And my favorite character in the game was, of course...Carmen.

_childDocuments_.review: A really well-done high-production-value otome game, a must-play for any fan of the genre. Lackluster mystery aspects, weird after-ending after you complete all routes, and 1 love interest that many people feel is annoying (although the rest are pretty cute), so it's not perfect but it is very very good. Key binding is weird but you get used to it. Home to access Menu; page up to turn on/off auto read. People always post about playing the LIs in a certain order but for better or worse each LI reveals a separate piece of the underlying story but the plot doesn't really build on these pieces, so seriously play them in whatever order you want. No guide is necessary if you pay attention - the colors give you hints about who likes what you're saying.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so I'm half and half with this review, story wise i loved it, characters, plots, art was amazing but its the damn controls and game itself that lets it down. First off the good: As said above the characters and their stories are really cool and unique, the art and even the generic music wasn't bad, it set the moods as they needed to be set. The animated backgrounds were really cool (moving cars, signs, flashing lights) The blinking was a cool touch, and if you play with VAs on you get moving mouths (I didn't was too confusing) but it added life to the characters that some games don't do. Getting other POVs is really cool, it's not just the FMC you get the boys occasionally. The different coloured ‘read’ text is a real nice touch, with the 4 chapters being somewhat identical it's really nice to skim read and know you're not missing anything new. It took three playthroughs but the skip button is a life changer, it will skip to the next choice or a new section of text that's been unread. It is a really nice feature in a game like this.I liked that there is a chance to get a bad ending and the bad endings are actually that it's not a ‘they-dont-get-together’ so that i found is a nice change. The translations felt natural, the conversations followed pretty well and nothing felt too out of place. The Not So Good…First off there is no variation for the first 4 chapters, you may get a different line, cat name and bikini but that's about it, so on a replay factor it made it very tedious because you have to go back and do that damn questionnaire to get the character you want (thank you walkthroughs because i wouldn't have had the patience)A big one was translations, now it doesn't make it that unplayable, the background voice lines aren't that important with my very minimal Japanese even i could tell it was just people saying excuse me and ordering things. BUT the ending of ‘Auld Lang Syne’ was a sh!t show. No subtitles for us poor English peeps and no real hints into what is actually being said so i had to go google hunting for a translation and that was a mission. I'm still confusedHonestly story wise those last two Chapters you get ‘Full Circle’ and ‘Auld Lang Syne’ felt cheap, its like they decided ‘sh!t we need to tie up loose ends’ and just came up with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ endings, everyone felt like a villain by the end of it and I was left more confused than not. (in my opinion to keep the game good, don't touch these leave the loose ends open it's better that way honestly) The controls are horrible, i can't say for any other platform but on pc they are bad, it took me half the game to figure out how to pull up the damn menu (my two year old fluked that with button mashing the keyboard) and then even finding what you wanted to find was a mission the menus took a bit to figure out. I never found a quit button on the main page so I had to use steam to shut the game down constantly but that could have just been me.I want to go back to the story and characters themselves and answer the real question: what order do I rate them in??This was hard, by the end of almost everyone's story I actually loved their characters and stories i liked each one for different reasons which made rating them kinda hard, I actually don't think I can rate them.. I've been sitting here for 5 mins trying to figure it out.. Ill go in order i played them. **potential spoilers ill try not too**-When i first played this game i played it based off my personality and how i would answer and pick questions and i ended up landing Scarecrows story (managed to get the good ending too) in Scarecrows story it felt the most natural, the bond with him felt real and genuine, but also the bond he had with the other boys was strong in this story. I loved his story in general. It fascinated me and well who could hate that geek, his personality matches mine and i was laughing so much through his play through. -My next One was Limbo, look those blue eyes had me. Limbo was an interesting one, when first introduced i put him in the ‘a$$hole’ box and figured i would chase him as i have a weakness for that, but as you play through the chapters you start to see he isn't one, he isn't the crooked lawyer and is actually a really nice guy, and i was a nice surprise, his confession and that whole moment is still on replay in my head and out of them all this one was high up on the list. His story was kinda boring but i feel his character made up for that. -Shu was my next one, now this man caught my heart instantly in SC story. How angry he got over that certain necklace (IYKYK) i knew in that story that i was gonna be a simp for this man and well i'm glad my stubbornness argued that. (one thing that bugs me is the 180 he does from SC story about death to his story) I went in wanting to win this man over but decided no, if you don't like my sharp tongue then f you. Well that was the right answer! His story was one of the more entertaining ones action wise, it was interesting to follow along, it was obvious where it was going but it was still entertaining to follow along with. I think the fact that I loved this man was the reason i enjoyed his story. -Mozu was the next, this man had me at “I just think you have a very good skeletal structure. Your skeletal framework is Caucasian, but your eye sockets are smooth. The cavities are quite fair” nothing wins me over more than commenting on my bones (im joking but it entertains me this seems to be a compliment in dating sims) Now to tell you i was not prepared for the emotional trauma i was going to face in this story… I have not cried over a character so much, I was in his story refusing to move forward because I couldn't deal with what he would go through. I had to sit there and process, amp myself up and try to continue on only to start crying again. To have hope built up and crushed constantly just killed me and his bad ending was just soul crushing. Out of all the stories this one was the most emotional out of them all and i still haven't gotten over it (Scarecrows is up there too)Lastly was Helvetica, I had no interest in him whatsoever. He came off as a creep and I just hated him, his personality clashes with my actual one and everything he said made me hate him more. His story for me was the most boring and confusing, at one point I was convinced 'he' wasn't a 'he'. I just felt detached from this character compared to the rest. So when it comes to picking a fav I just can't, Scarecrow's relationships are what drew me to him, Limbos Personality to him, Shu’s mystery and then Mozus emotional trauma i just can't decide. I can tell you who i really didn't like if it wasn't obvious. Overall the stories of this game were amazing, if you can ignore the repetitive first 4 chapters i really enjoyed it the only thing that lets it down are those controls and the odd translation error. But if you can get past that then this game is a really fun play.

_childDocuments_.review: Why yeah, thumbs up.The main story isn't boring, I wouldn't ask more than that. It's interesting. Character stories are somewhat meh, and because of that I mostly skipped them. Even Shu's story appeared to be boring to me, although I loved him.  The main heroine is not stupid. This is something new. However, I thought hard about giving her the Worst Otome C**kblocker Award, but it was already given to Cyrus from Steam Prison. She is soooo much annoying in any of the romance scenes. When you read them, she struggles so hard that you start feeling like she's being sexually harassed. Drawing is cool compared to the most otome games. Sprites, CGs, backgrounds look great. And the short videos make you feel like you're watching anime. A fresh decision. This game has one big problem: CONTROLS. I had to google up how to go to menu. I saw some comment saying something like "Seems like the developers never played any game on PC". I 100% agree. Man, nobody use HOME and END buttons. Some laptops need Fn to activate them. I know developers will never read my review, but I'll say this thing: any visual novel should need a single mouse to play them. NO KEYBOARDS. No numpad, no F-keys, no number keys, no Ctrl&Alt&Shift&anything else. Space, Enter, Esc, arrow keys, but no HOME or END. And daaaamn, this scroll bar is insane. The strange thing is that I didn't see any warnings or age ratings anywhere. I'm an old hag compared to the most otome players, but here's my personal warning: if you don't want to read/see VIOLENCE, S**CIDE, MURDER and BLOOD, and just wanna play some generic peaceful childish otome, do not buy this game. I enjoyed it a lot, really noirish. But children, stand back!I'm gonna buy the upcoming sequel. As long as this game isn't boring, I love it, and have some trust in developers. But please, onegai, do better controls next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished chapter 3 so far so my review may change in the future but so far...Nothing particularly bad to say for the story and characters as of now. I like all of the characters and their amusing interactions, although admittedly some parts feel less impactful than it could've been (for me, anyway). As a protagonist, Teuta is charming - she can carry herself quite well throughout the story and is well-rooted even if she basically gets dragged into the mess in the first place. All of the boys and the side characters have their own quirks while still contributing to the story cohesively. In short, story-wise, the game is a hard-recommend for me.However, in terms of technicality, this is where things get clunky. As some others pointed out, the technical side of the port has problems. Some stuffs I noticed so far:* Quality of movie assets... leaves a lot to be desired. Not sure how to put it properly, but I keep noticing pixelated stuffs here and there.* I noticed there are voice-only dialogues in the game - probably deliberately left without text as means to heighten the immersion to the story's world with the "background voice" and such. However, while I can still decipher the voice-only dialogues just fine, I think they really should be translated and have their subtitles properly inserted into the game one way or another, especially to help those who have trouble following voice-only dialogues.* No way to remap controls. I am personally using controller instead of my keyboard and mouse because of my hand problems, and the assigned controls for the controller doesn't bother me, but it really would be nice to be able to remap.* (Edit) Also, there REALLY should be help screen or something related to the controls in the beginning. Even if the help screen is there in the in-game menu, I still had to figure some things out by myself because there are no pointers on what should I press even for accessing menu at first.* No way to switch between windowed and full-screen mode, or change the resolution.* No option to quit the game from the title screen and in-game menu - or at least, I haven't found any. This may sound silly, but I simply dislike having to press Alt-F4 every time to close the game.For reference, I'm running the game in my laptop's built-in monitor, which has 1920x1080 resolution and running at 150% scale.As for me, the technical problems doesn't quite break the game. However, I still hope they can be fixed/improved somehow. Until that happens, for those who want to try the game, they need to be on the lookout for said problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just say: aside from Amnesia (an absolute classic Japanese otome), Bustafellows is probably the highest quality otome game available on Steam. The art and the voice acting are top-tier! I absolutely recommend this game to fans of the genre. That being said, Bustafellows is not by any means without flaws. I'll leave my pros and cons below before breaking down each character's route.Pros: The art is stunning. Every character sprite, CG, and background was clearly drawn with great care and consistency. The voice acting is done by an incredibly talented cast of veteran seiyuus, which only enhances the already strong characterization of both the main and side characters. Seriously, just about every character in Bustafellows is incredibly likable, including Teuta, the MC. The overall world building was, in my opinion, strong, and I found the premise quite interesting. To their credit, the writers were very good at balancing humor and serious subject matters, which is definitely something they should be commended for. Cons: The common route was too long! It got rather tedious force skipping through it, especially because the actual love interests' routes felt fairly short in comparison. Because of this setup, Bustafellows focused heavily on plot, and in most of the routes, there was not much romance until the end. This point brings me to probably my biggest complaint: Bustafellows literally described on the Steam page as being a "steamy noir visual novel," but steamy it most certainly is not. Each LI certainly had the potential to get there based on their characterization, but it felt like just about every opportunity for steaminess was subverted by Teuta saying it was "embarassing," or the LIs just responding platonically instead. I live in Japan, and I know that romance/dating culture is different here than in the West, but I can't say I don't find it a tiresome trope to have in escapist romance games. For the M rating, I was expecting SOMETHING a little more, but it never gets steamier than a kiss. Sadly, the M rating seems to only be in place for violence and drug use.As I implied above, the characters are the real draw of Bustafellows, and for what it's worth, I actually enjoyed all of them for different reasons.Limbo - The "crooked lawyer" and poster boy for Bustafellows, i.e. Teuta's primary love interest. I'll be honest; even though Limbo is charismatic, confident, and considerate, I found his route pretty bland. So bland, in fact, that I can barely remember the plot. It wasn't very memorable outside of Limbo's moments with Teuta, which is why it was great that these characters had so many enjoyable scenes together. The progression of their relationship from trusted friends to lovers felt very natural; the characters are compatible and seem to just plain like each other. I expected a little more sizzle, danger, and excitement from the "main" route, but ultimately, I was able to enjoy Limbo's story for what it was. To be fair, his "genki guy" character is not a type I favor; I suspect that lots of people will love Limbo and enjoy his *slightly* spicy after-story. Helvetica - Helvetica's route surprised me. Though he engages in some rather problematic behavior (giving women points based on appearance, wtf???), I am absolutely weak to flirts, and he is unquestionably the most forward of Teuta's love interests. Props to the writers for subverting the typical stoic, reserved megane trope; Helvetica is portrayed as quite a playboy! His story itself is probably the angstiest of the bunch, but in a way that actually made perfect sense for his character. Helvetica showed a great deal of development from the beginning to the end of his route, all while remaining very much true to his (admittedly complex) character. Though I certainly didn't expect it going in, Helvetica's route ended up being my absolute favorite of the game!Shu - While Helvetica's route was my favorite, Shu definitely ended up being my favorite love interest. His characterization was, in my opinion, the best developed and the most consistent. Shu is a calm, cool-headed assassin with a soft spot and a strong sense of loyalty. As much as I adore Shu and love his type of character, my biggest issue was that his relationship with Teuta was, at times, not super believable. He's clearly the most mature of her love interests and, given his experience level and tendency to make dirty jokes, it didn't seem plausible that he would pursue someone so innocent and immature. If the writers had actually let Shu and Teuta get some action in this route, it would absolutely have been more believable, and may have been my favorite. Believability aside, I loved playing Shu's route, and I thought his epilogue was very sweet and enjoyable.Mozu - Mozu's route is the most emotional one in the game, and is by far the best written. Rather than following the game's overarching criminal investigation, Mozu's story focuses on his search for clues regarding the disappearance of his younger sister. I loved this about his route, because it gave us every opportunity to get to know him. For me, Mozu was incredibly relatable and likable, even for him being written as "the eccentric." His relationship with Teuta was my favorite; it made perfect sense that they would develop a connection through the shared trauma of having a sibling disappear. It was clear throughout they story how much they cared for and respected one anothers' feelings. As much as I adored Mozu's route, it was HEAVY. There were definitely points at which I couldn't hold back tears; this is just a testament to how beautifully written Mozu's route was. Make sure you have tissues nearby while playing it!Scarecrow - Two words: cinnamon roll! Scarecrow is a sweet, awkward nerd who refers to himself as an "underworld boss." He instantly develops a crush on Teuta, making for some adorable moments throughout both his route and the common route. Scarecrow is the closest in age and maturity to Teuta, so their relationship progression feels very natural and true to both characters. Though he wasn't my favorite love interest by any means, I still thoroughly enjoyed playing Scarecrow's route! It was surprisingly dark- prior to choosing him, you're given almost no indication the amount of trauma that Scarecrow is coping with. Poor boy; you can't help but love his character, even if you don't care for him as a love interest. Scarecrow's epilogue was so, so adorable and satisfying.I'll be honest - Bustafellows' true ending gave me mixed feelings. Some parts of it I saw coming from almost the beginning, while other plot twists truly surprised me. I wish that there had been more of a payoff for the reveal of Teuta's brother's fate; I was rather perplexed and blindsided by the end reveal of this plot point, and I didn't find it wholly satisfying. Otherwise, though, I felt that many elements of the true ending were fitting, even for many of them being expected.Some have complained about PC port issues, but I personally had no problems with any of the controls. The big thing that may bother some players is the abundance of untranslated transition comments. As a Japanese speaker, I wouldn't say that any of these untranslated bits were integral enough to the plot detract from the overall story or game experience, but I can understand why this would be annoying to some. Is Bustafellows a perfect game? No, not by any means. But it is one of the best available to the Western market, and I would wholeheartedly recommend it to any otome fan. Whether it be the plot, the characters, the art, or the voice acting, there are so many wonderful parts that make up Bustafellows that I genuinely believe that there's something for everyone to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VNs yet. Controls are cumbersome and you'll need to use alt+F4 to log out of the game, but it's worth the trouble for this VN. Great cast of characters, high quality voice overs and art work, and the overall design makes it seem like you're watching an anime rather than playing a VN. I really like VNs that require you to play through multiple times in order to get the full story (like Amnesia or Cinderella Phenomenon), and that's what Bustafellows does. Once you finish all LI routes you'll finally get to see the end of the main story, and it's pretty surprising. There's even some bonus material that has more WTF endings to tie up all loose ends. My only complaint is how childish everyone treats the MC, who is a pretty accomplished and capable journalist and young woman who gets far too many hair ruffles for my liking.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to come out since 2 years ago.  I specifically used 3 days of vacation time to play it :v (not something to be proud of). I almost burst into tears because it's been forever since I've played such a high quality Otome game! There are things which could be improved, sure. However, I prefer focusing on what is already there. Should I mention the art? YES. CGs and BGs are so freaking beautiful! Lots of effort could be seen from just looking at them. The words in my dictionary are not enough to describe how pleased I am with the art. What about UI? Quite user friendly once you know how to get there. I personally appreciate it because it's very cool.Port? I honestly have no problem with it because I used both controller and keyboard. Gameplay? Hmm...this is where some improvement could be used. I understand the intention behind some monologues during plot development, but not knowing japanese limit the fun I could have had out of it. Plot? I only have one thing to say. If you don't like the plot, you're either not fan of mystery and thriller genre or you're not a fan of visual novel.Overall opinion:  It is a high quality game made with care and effort. The mystery element is very thick and arouses interests, definitely a must-not-missed game for mystery genre fans. On the contrary, the otome element is thin, if you're a fan of mushy romance novel, you'll do better to reel the mush in and enjoy cute scenes more. In any case, I enjoyed the game a lot and the it left behind a satisfactory feeling afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished most of the routes now, and I love this game. The stories are really good, the art is good, the guys are interesting, and I really like this heroine. There are 3 relatively minor issues I had:1. The keyboard controls were different from any otome game I've played before. In case anyone else is in the same situation, the HOME key will bring up the menu, and the rest of the controls can be found under Help. The only other key I used much was END, to review or roll back dialogue.2. You can't save the game when there's a choice to be made. The very easy workaround for this is to go back a step in the dialogue (the END key), save, then go on from there. 3. Some of the dialogue was not translated. This was mainly at the start of an episode or a cutscene. Again, the END key was my friend--even if it wasn't translated on screen, it still showed up in the dialogue.I felt like these were minor inconveniences at most, and they didn't hinder my enjoyment of the game at all. I thought the game was well done, one of the most fun otome games I've played yet.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, I like reading Bustafellows. Although it has many places where it underwhelms me.The stories in this game are kind of all over the place. It seems there are too many topics the game wants to tackle on, but fails to do so in depth.A lot of the settings are far-fetched and unrealistic, like Crow being a super genius all-powerful hacker.  The existence of magical plastic surgeries. Our 5 fixers, who are supposed to do things hidden, expose all of themselves to the enemy, or even worse, to the internet. Villains who conveniently put everything that would prove them guilty in a nice  for us to read.  I know I shouldn't expect realism in this kind of games, but not doing so would require me to lower expectations.The mysteries in each episode are pretty predictable. They usually all end up in a stereotypical "bad guy goes crazy and commits crime" situation. They leave me with little to ponder on. The main storyline in the end is an exception, though, and I enjoyed it much more.One gimmick of Bustafellows is that our protagonist can travel back in time. Time travel! How many cool stories can be written with that? It's going be an interesting key feature -- or so I though. In this game, this superpower just feels unnecessary, it is detached from the rest of stories, as most of them can still happen without.Limbo was supposed to be the "crooked" lawyer, but apart from the beginning, he just end up being "a lawyer", the crooked part is never explored. The 5 fixers are all cool in their own ways, but they are mostly pretty shallow.The game has many instances of having dialog during scene transitions (without showing a text box), while this would make a nice immersive effect for those who understands Japanese speech. Those who don't are left completely in the dark until when we can call out the history screen again to read the translation. This totally backfired on creating the immersion. Not to mention if an ending is reached after such a transition, we don't get the chance to see translations at all.Those things said, I did enjoy the game, spending whole 50 hours on it and felt good. Miraculously, it kept me hooked throughout all those 50 hours, while I was complaining about the things said above, which I think is quite a difficult feat. The main storyline at the end is quite unexpected, if not a little abrupt. You might like it even if you are bored by the first 4 episodes of common route. The more calm parts of the game are also enjoyable, they made me smile often.One good thing to point out is the art style. It really effectively gave the promised "steam noire" vibe. The animated backgrounds are stunning. And the characters are well drawn.A solid 7/10.My favourite character route is Helvetica's for , despite of him having a difficult personality to like and has the name of a font. And the least favourite route is Scarecrow's for being boring.On a funny note, the story is set in the US, right? But in the pause menu, it clearly shows the temperature of "New Sieg, USA" in degrees Celsius!

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this writing, I've completed 51% of the game after successfully completing all five guys’ routes  . There’s a lot I wanted to say so I’ll organize them into sections:Each guy’s route is divided into two parts: Side A (which focuses on the crime and thriller of each guy’s story) and Side B (the after-story romance aspect). Although some characters have more romance content than the others, overall, I think the game has managed to balance out the action and romance in which there’s just enough romance without it getting in the way of the murder mystery and vice versa. The game managed to put me on edge with the mystery and it kept me squealing at times with the romance.Least to most truth revelation: Least to most romance-heavy route: Weakest to strongest Side A story: The thing that stood out most to me in this game is definitely the characters. The characters have strong colorful personalities and I am very much in love with all of them- especially our heroine Teuta. Teuta is a wonderful heroine; she’s playful, witty, sticks to her principle and is a woman of action. That aside, I also love the relationship between all characters, I can just read their conversations and not get bored. For me, I think the characters have managed to stay consistent throughout the story in which their actions are aligned to their personality.The art is easily very gorgeous- the characters’ sprites, the CGs, realia and background art are all very spectacular. I’m amazed at the amount of background art and each character’s sprites that this game has. There’s a number of animations too which adds flare to the game. The music isn’t to my taste but they sound good and fit the scenes they were in.Since this version is the PC port of a Switch game, I believe this section is where most of the bad reviews nitpicked on. Personally, while the technicality issues bothered me a bit, it wasn’t much that it takes away my experience from playing the game. Just in case, I’m listing down the issues that might need some improvements:1.  You can easily counter this issue by checking the backlog to read the missing dialogues but for players who don’t understand Japanese or use the “Auto-Read” function, this issue hinders the momentum since they will have to stop to check the backlog every time it happens.2.  I’m not sure if this was meant to be this way (since Japanese players could understand the language so the lack of text dialogue is for comedic/ realistic experience purpose) but similar as above, it hinders the momentum of players using “Auto-Read” and players with no basic knowledge in Japanese.3.  When I play VN, the first thing I’ll do is check the key/button mapping but it took me about 5 minutes pressing random keys on my keyboard just to locate the in-game menu. The choice of key mapping is pretty odd compared to other VN. For those using a controller, there’s no [Quick Save] or [Quick Load] button assigned which is an issue.For reference, here are the key mapping for keyboard control:[Home] In-game menu[End] Backlog[Pg Up] Auto Read[Pg Dn] Fast Forward[F1] Quick Load[F2] Quick Save[Enter] Select/ Proceed[Esc/ Backspace] Back/ Cancel/ Close dialogue box4.  Since this was originally a Switch game, the lack of [Quit Game] menu made sense since you close the software from the Switch home screen. However, the lack of [Quit Game] menu or the [Are you sure you want to exit the game?] command for a PC port feels quite awkward. You have to change the game to window mode [Alt] + [Enter] and close it via the close [X] button or use the command prompt to close the game.5.  So far, I’ve noticed several minor text issues which are:-Less than five minor typos.-In Limbo’s route, there was one line from Limbo’s POV where Teuta’s name was accidentally replaced with Limbo’s.-Wrong line in Mozu’s Side B story. There’s a line where Mozu said the coroner’s office has sufficient facilities like the TV, etc. but the line displayed was the line Teuta previously said to him.-About 3 lines of text went over the dialogue box in Scarecrow’s route. The texts were too long and instead of the rest of the words going to the line under, they went straight over the dialogue box in one straight line. 6.  This issue doesn’t really happen to me but I’ve seen other players who complained that the BGM and characters’ voices had inconsistent volume (the BGM being too loud at times or the voices were too soft)My Japanese is so-so but so far, the translations were accurate. The dialogues were localized and flowed nicely. Some terms were Westernized for the Western audience’s understanding without changing the original meaning.  If you have a Switch, I’d say go buy the Switch version. But if you don’t have a Switch or simply enjoy playing on the PC like me, I’d still say yes, I recommend it! Despite the technical issues mentioned above, I did not encounter any bugs or glitches in the game. The game runs smoothly on my laptop without any issues. This game has wonderful story, characters, voice actors, art and romance so if you love otome game, it’s a miss for you to not try this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Played with a controller, much easier than using a keyboard. Anyway, this is actually one of the best otome games you can play on PC. Two icky things about the game though, 1st of all; last two chapters you can unlock by finishing all ML route side A and B's feel like they come out of nowhere. As in, it just all unravels. I didn't like how it all went down much I would prefer it to have a better build up but despite that I must say the last two chapters were an absolute delight. Now this one wasn't really an ick but a preference. My second problem with this game however is that it sadly has the womaniser, overly flirty to the point where it gets uncomfortable type of character. Don't get me wrong he was way better than almost all LI's with the same troupes ive seen in otoge's but I believe it should be noted nonetheless. On the plus side other characters do acknowledge his behaviour comes across as creepy so there is at least that. He also has a pretty amazing backstory! Thankfully the other 4 LI's were pretty chill in my opinion.The game also has a lot of triggering content, character death, abuse and much more that I would love to get into but the Spoiler Warning starting from chapter 2 are pretty strict and I would like to be in the safe :,)TL;DR Amazing Otoge, raised my standarts in both otoge's and men. Fun cast, amazing character dynamics. I definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Chapter 2 but some details in the story bugged me so I'm gonna let it out here.So far the game seemed mostly fine to me. The characters are adorable and charming. I like how hilarious Scarecrow is. It seemed to me that the narrative tried to mimic the style of American sitcoms and that's good. The characters interacted in the ways that made them look like a funny gang. I think Chapter 1 worked out well to tell an interesting story. The protagonist encountered some mysterious crime incident and used her superpower to save the man whose death she witnessed. And the gang gathered together to work with her. They solved the incident and dragged the protagonist to join their gang. That's a good start and is appealing to me.However,  the case in Chapter 2 is less satisfying. The reason why the heroine used her superpower does not make sense to me. I mean, you can say she's so kind that she felt bad for the little boy and wanted to help him, and I get that the story needs her to show her superpower. But I don't understand why she found it necessary to use her superpower to go back in time. It's not her responsibility and that's too naive and childish. When I read that story, I almost forgot the protagonist is a 21-year-old adult. It makes more sense if it's a kid show and the protagonist couldn't stand that bad things happen to other so she tried to stop all of them. It's not like that I'm the policewoman who rushed to the crime scene in the first place and failed to stop the kid from shooting so that I felt awful and couldn't sleep at night cuz the nightmare haunted me and I couldn't stop thinking about it so I had to do whatever I could to fix it. It's tragic, but definitely not something that horrible. It's an unfortunate accident that happens every now and then. If "I" try to go back in time to stop it every time it happens, it just cheapens the meaning of... justice. It just doesn't seem fair to other "murderers" like that little boy in the story. I mean, "I" am not even close to that little boy. Is it so serious that I have to use the superpower which might or might not interrupt the whole timeline? Some teenagers committed crime out of impulse. That's almost all the cases are. The protagonist shouldn't make excuses like "he doesn't know what killing means","he's a victim". Yeah. There are laws set for these reasons. That's why they wouldn't experience cruel penalty like adults who did it on purpose. Is she really trying to stop it from happening just because of these reasons? Then congrats! No more youth crimes for NYC.

(still no spoilers): Utter hot tier burning garbage. I thought it was also very predictable.It gets even worse from there. After you "finish" the main story you get an "extra"-part "connected" to the main story which basically fills you in and explains what you might be curious about. That episode is EVEN WORSE. It provides such a cliche reason and the way it's told is so unfair and doesn't even tie anything up. It ends OPEN ENDED. It's painfully frustrating and felt really rushed.  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Thirdly, there are obvious issues which may deter people: I didn't find them hard to use or finicky. But for those of you with a 60% keyboard gg. Unless you're willing to rebind them in your keyboard engine. The main button you'll be pressing is the HOME button. There you'll find how to save, load, skip and go to main menu (which is called TOP) etc.I don't have an issue with the keybindings because the game itself requires such minimal effort. There's a few. Not a lot. I'm currently studying Japanese so I can basically understand it without subtitles. However this may irk some people. But honestly, you are not missing on VITAL information. They don't say anything interesting. And honestly you can surmise what they're saying from context and tone so you don't really need to be able to understand in my opinion. But, it's a deal breaker for most.Do they? To a degree. If you're expecting some in depth changes don't bother. It doesn't change the main story at all.Getting into every characters route can be very hard. Chapter's 1-4 and the answers you choose determine who you'll be in a relationship with or whose path you unlock. After your first route you basically have to play the chapters again and again and again. I found it easy to get all the characters paths but, I understand it can be frustrating and hard for some. The way to tell on your first play who've you romanced is who chose the cat's name and your swimsuit.I really cannot overstate how much I hate female MC's. Even in anime. However, the MC in this story I quite liked and didn't have any issues with. She wasn't clueless nor frustrating. Many reviews state that she's childish. One said that she thinks about sex?!?! (LOL(she doesn't imo)). She has a strong character, down to earth, honest, playful (I suppose in a childish way sometimes) wholesome, and caring. Character development. I super duper loved, even though I don't like Helvetica's story or him as a person the connection all characters had with each and the MC. I loved the banter and jokes with all existing characters. I thought they developed the characters fairly well. Except for 3 side characters.Overall,  I recommend playing for the characters, main story is garbage. I loved their stories. Each of them were different, fun and immersive. The connections built with the MC didn't feel too forced. The keyboard settings are so easy to get over. I haven't had a major game breaking graphic issue that some people have mentioned. If it's below 20 bucks I don't see the harm in buying it. But as it is, the price is outrageously bad and it's obviously a quick port for some quick cash.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a bit torn on this one. I will give it a positive review for the sheer amount of content and overall quality, but some things are... weird. Borderline distasteful.The positives: its the highest production value for an otome game I have ever seen. Visuals are great, sprites are really well drawn despite being a bit blurry, CGs are top quality, VA work is amazing. Music is decent, with outros being above average.The protagonist is the typical bubbly airhead who eats a lot seen in many other Japanese productions. However, the peculiar nature of her power - being able to go back in time, but in someone else's body - made the premise pretty damn interesting. The plot is (initially) well written, with three solid chapters and a reasonable buildup to the mystery.Then... the tiresome switching between routes happen, and the story just stops. To switch in between characters' routes, one has to go through the same questionnaire four times, and is forced to rewatch one chapter and a half every time a new LI is picked. Truly an inconvenience, which I wished the developers had handled better. I spent several hours just reloading saves for that purpose rather than actual playtime, which is unfortunate.During the individual character routes, as mentioned, the plot just freezes to give you time to appreciate character development and the actual "otome" part of the content, which up until that point was quite lacking. While most routes do a good job in that regard, the sub-chapters are very short and the buildup is poor. One has to wonder why is that, considering the game takes its sweet time making people sit in a room and talk about nothing for 30 minutes to an hour at any given opportunity in the common route, happily wasting the player's time with trivialities, not to mention the endless text message exchanges through phone which could have been summed up in 10 seconds instead of showing every little passage.Let's not forget this product is advertised as a noir adventure first, and in hindsight the "otome" aspect of it felt totally secondary. On one hand, the characters are well flashed out and their involvement in the plot, camaraderie and personal attachment to the protagonist is endearing and sufficiently explained. On the other though, the story never truly picks up until after every route has been cleared, and two more chapters are unlocked. These two chapters are suppsed to be the climax, and they certainly are... for all the wrong reasons.The plot is wrapped up in a hurry, with plenty of reveals and truth bombs just casually dropped on the player's head one after another, the central organization which is at the core of the whole game is explained away with scooby-doo level writing and final villains. Of course the big bad is the one person with 5 seconds screen time, considering everyone else has been already revealed to be connected in some way. At the very least, while it is poorly written and laughably bad in its final chapter, the main story arc closes on a positive note.And then Auld Lang Syne happened. And ♥♥♥♥ that closure I hate it with every fiber of my being. I wish I didnt read it, more still, I wish it didnt exist. The game just switches genres out of nowhere, gut-wrenching reveals one after the other blatantly added for shock value, absolutely not fair. It left an awful taste in my mouth, didnt have to go that far, there was no reason for what was being described, and a throwaway line to handwave one of the sub-characters' behaviors in the plot which had not been stated up until then, just... no. My stomach is still hurting.Would I recommend this novel? Yes, provided that you read it for the journey not for the conclusion. Characters are overall well written and their interactions funny, charming and acted greatly. Do stop before the very last chapter if you wish to keep a good memory of the whole ordeal though, which in my honest opinion brings the quality down a full point. Moreover, some speeches have not been translated, namely when characters speak in a video, therefore you'd have to go hunt for a translation on the internet.

_childDocuments_.review: Would you go back in time to save a local celebrity?Click on my video to see gameplay and watch my first impressions as they happened. Bustafellows puts you into the shoes of Teuta, a reporter looking to get to the bottom of mysteries in New Sieg. The twist is that she can travel back in time, and you goal is to save the life of the crooked lawyer Limbo. (Yes, Limbo is his name.) Oh, and of course you get to romance Limbo and four others: Shu, the Seto Kaiba jacket-wearing hitman; Helvetica, the effeminate master of master of disguise; Mozu, a socially awkward genius and chief of the autopsy department; and Scarecrow, a computer geek and self-proclaimed "underground boss" who definitely doesn't live in his parents' basement.If you've been asking for more Japan-exclusive titles, Bustafellows needs to be on your radar. Characters from the Japan-only "Side Kicks!" game on PS Vita will make an appearance, and we've been lucky enough to get a passable localization of Bustafellows. Otome games rarely make it to English with this level of production value and voice acting, and that's the kind of thing we all should try to support.Sadly, controls are awkwardly mapped, and sound adjustments don't seem to work right. Cutscene volume is too loud, and voices are often quiet. The story is also the awkward fare you might expect from over-the-top anime style writing, along with the hilarity of Japanese writers portraying American characters.If you needed to read this review, chances are that Bustafellows isn't for you. But if you want an interactive anime, or if you want to support this kind of game making it to the west, then pick up Bustafellows.
