_childDocuments_.review: This visual novel has a ton going for it, likable characters, gorgeous art, interesting plot (each branching route was interesting as well! Lots of great character development!) The UI is gorgeous, and there's a great skip option between choices so you don't have to wait for the text to skip through... however, the controls are a bit clunky -- home and end keys are your friends. I think the only thing I truly disliked about this story was the very end, it kind of felt like barely scratching the surface of the main overarching or hinted plot. Maybe that's due to part two existing? (Not in English... yet.) Now, that isn't to say that it isn't still enjoyable because there is still a lot of shocking or touching moments to be found within, but the ending could've been fleshed out a bit more. OTHERWISE, let it be noted that the character routes themselves and side stories offer plenty of meat to sink your teeth into. I personally 100% <30 hours, but depending on reading pace you might do it in less/more time. I did skip common route between character routes, and I didn't "autoplay" all dialogue, sometimes I would manually read because certain scenes have you on the edge of your seat, dying to know what's happening next. If you enjoy interesting, wonderfully voiced (can we say all-star cast???) characters (attractive anime men???) with traumatic backstories and plots that enrapture your attention... this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game 45% off but I think for fullprice it still would've been completely worth it. It does take a bit to get into it since the first chapters of the story are a bit confusing and boring. I found the story to be mildly interesting. i did (and still do) struggle with understanding what was happening. Luckily once you get to the parts where the main story splits to continue 1 romance path it gets a lot more interesting.The MC is fairly relatable. I usually self-insert and at least she's not a dimwitted idiot who can't even tie her own shoes. She has a job (journalist), good friends, a goal in life and she seems pretty smart. Having said that, I do think sometimes she was naive and in some individual stories I did not like her responses. I also thought thinks like touching, hugging, swimming and thus wearing a bikini or kissing were made into very big embarrassing things. That could just be a culture difference though. I'm from the Netherlands so we're pretty open about those things here.I would strongly recommend looking up a guide for opening each route. The choices are few and far apart and don't really make a lot of sense on which character you end up with. So to spare yourself some frustration, follow a guide.I did notice the story to get the MC and the rest of the guys together is pretty thin and, as with a lot of games like this, doesn't really follow that much logic. Her powers to travel back in time are not believed but despite that the guys still want to keep an eye on her. She fully agrees to live with them and when she hears what they do she immediately decides she wants in on it. The guys are happy with this, despite her not really adding anything useful to the group.I played 3 routes so far.Scarecrow:This was the one I liked least. There's minimal romance and Crow is very awkward. Often having his hands in front of his eyes or saying things out loud he doesn't mean to. He was funny though and I did like his story in itself. He and the MC are very sweet together, I'll give them that.His bad ending is quite sad but to be fair, most of them are.Shu:This story I liked a lot better. Shu is often misunderstood and he has a hard time opening up about things. He does have a sweet side to him though and sometimes I was surprised with the depth of things he said. He also quits smoking for the MC (okay, tries to, but still) and his number 1 priority becomes protecting her.I didn't like the MC as much in this story though. Shu is a hitman which means he kills people. Now, I understand when someone is against that. But in this case no one of the group had issues asking Shu for help. But everyone at the same time judged him for killing and the MC had a hard time accepting those sides of him.Nozu:Yeah, buckle up for this one since this really gets emotional. Even the good ending ends on a sad note and it really is bad what poor Nozu has to go through. I liked his character a lot. He's honest, very sweet and straightforward. Not to mention he analyses things which I appreciate. Which is why it made me extra sad that he had to go through all that sadness. The MC often doesn't understand him and I didn't think they really fitted together.All in all though, the stories are all engaging and the characters really have a depth to them. I also love the idea of the group living together as friends. The art is pretty well done although the videos in between are very low quality.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... this is complicatedI have very, VERY mixed feelings about this VN, somewhere because of localisation, somewhere - because of porting to PC, and... well, I guess, some of the controversary happens because of the original pacingThe thing I probably liked the most - is about the general settings, which are presented by the common routes and second to last chapter. It truly unfolds the world in front of player, makes it feel real and puts you into the questioning "What would I say or do in place of these characters?", and I enjoy it really muchThen... the character routesThey are really uneven in pacing - some feel really forced by both the character and their surroundings, making you think "when the interesting stuff finally happens, huh?" Probably, the most "natural" route out of all belongs to Shu, as it has intrigue, action, dynamics balanced pretty well. It may be my personal taste, though, but no other story could stick out to me as much, and there was more potential to what could be written insteadAnother issue is the omittion of the videos in translations. Why. I would really like to watch the conversations for the characters in my video library, but instead I should search for them somewhere else, and this is not something that has to be happening. Especially when it comes to the final - okay, well, extras are extras, but the ending? Really?And, of course, the controls and other technical stuff. I did not have much issues, thankfully, but still. It is the port to PC - so, it should have been adapted to the needs of computers. Overall - I claim this game as good, but expected a lot more from itIt could have been better, it could show more opportunities to captivate me for full walkthrough, including bad endings (and I usually hate it), but, due to the all the reasons mentioned, its potential is wasted for disappointment over simple detailsI would still recommend others to play it, but more for the plot and while being aware about its imperfectionsMy only hope is that the game will be reviewed again and patched with all the missing stuff, but... well, only time tells whether it becomes true

_childDocuments_.review: Bustafellows! (At the time of this review I am on Chapter 4 of the common route, will edit when fully completed :) )The moral boundaries the game pushes - the ability to make its players think amaze me. This game reminds me a lot of Tears of Themis (with Bustafellows coming out before) in terms of the action and quality but follows the more traditional “Choices matter” while still being limited in choices. But compared to other games I have played the thing that stands out the most is having Teuta (the MC) voiced - it makes such a difference, adding to her personality, the game experience, and so much more. While marketed as an otome - the romance is more of a side plot after the main story. If you are looking solely for the romance aspect, I would not recommend it. I would consider this game more like a high-action/drama show that you can play through at your own pace with the added bonus of having routes for each lead. The writing is AMAZING. Mixed in with the voice acting, you really get a feel of each character while also feeling both the tension and the excitement. The ability of this game to touch upon these “darker” subjects while also mixing in both comedic and tension-building moments elevates it above other otomes. In addition, the animation of each character when talking and the careful detail in changing the placements of sprites, and the beautiful CG’s ? add to the money's worth !! I think the only thing I dislike about the game is the lack of clarity about the controls. Would it be worth 40 dollars? No. Personally, I think buying the game on sale is when it's worth the best bang for your buck. But if you have excess money to spend it is 100% worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, I do recommend this game. It's a very polished game oozing with style, and does some wonderful things with the sounds, sprites and animation. Designed to be like some kind of TV series, this is a fun game to set to Auto and just eat food while watching.That said, this is not a perfect game.First, the things I liked - and even loved - about the game: Scarecrow, lol. Great characters in general, actually. One of my favourite parts about this game is the dialogue between the characters in general. They all play roles in each other's stories, they all good-naturedly tease the heroine with whoever she gets with, and the script is just so darn funny sometimes. I enjoyed their chemistry a lot. The art in this game is gorgeous, of course. The sofa bed by the pool and the sofa in the living room both had separate sets of sprites and it looked so good, and added to the whole 'we are at home, being a chill and cosy family' dynamic a ton. I loved how they all had 'at-home and relaxing' sprites next to their 'I'm out and working' (in Crow's case, in and working) sprites. Having the backs of their heads also drawn and placed to create the illusion of space and distance, as well as set up dramatic shots was pretty good. Sound design is also pretty great in this game - it REALLY needs an English dub because checking the log to get the full translation of what we just heard is kind of annoying, plus you have a lot of fun and fairly innovative overlapping sound design here that just isn't as cool when you can't understand it (like you can hear characters order coffees in the background while other character are talking, or hear people's conversations just trail off in the distance while they're walking away, etc.). The audio levels were controlled really well so none of it is intrusive. If it was in English it would be so much more appreciated by non-Japanese speakers. (The Engrish did tickle me, though.)The not-so-great parts of this game are sort of a huge letdown for me personally because story is really important for me. There are odd dangling threads with a lot of the characters' stories. Some points in some stories got cringe-inducingly tropey (I'm looking at you, Troy) and Limbo's bad endings were comically melodramatic to the point I couldn't help a smile twitching on my lips as his second bad ending trailed away. Auld Sang Lyne could have been, in my humble opinion, completely omitted. WTF, lol. It threw some characters under the bus and soured a lot of things, and required even more suspension of disbelief than all of the other plot points (yes, even the bit about nanomachines) combined. The way they tried to write this thing like some poetic tragedy was... uh... I just wasn't feeling any of it. Frankly after playing the extra episode I wished I hadn't. In a word, it was unnecessary. As a more minor quibble, I also wish they'd found a better way to integrate Full Circle. It was a very necessary episode but feels so detached because of the way they did it. I personally feel that they should have carried each separate route through with Full Circle, and had each route handle the crisis slightly differently. This would have resulted in a lot more writing they probably didn't have time for, so I'm just speaking for what I would have *ideally* wanted to see.Overall, BUSTAFELLOWS is worth playing because it's a dazzling experience, but I would absolutely recommend skipping Auld Sang Lyne when unlocked because it detracts rather than adds to the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone familiar with otome games (dating sims aimed at female audiences) probably already has a general idea of what they're getting themselves into. In all likelihood, if you're considering purchasing this game you won't be disappointed.The story is "fun" (not quite the right word in some cases) and the characters are a lively bunch that play very well off of each other. I'd highly recommend playing through blind for the first time even if you think you already have an idea of which love interest will be your favourite. There's no recommended route order so you won't be missing anything if you play through one guy's route before another's. The writers have a good job of giving you a reason to care about each character, even if you initially think they're boring/annoying for whatever reason. I'd also add that there's not really anything "creepy" or dangerously toeing the line of consent like in some other games *cough cough*.The time-travel gimmick isn't really played up too much. You're not really ever faced with a choice of whether you do or don't at a particular point, however, you are confronted with the consequences of the choices you make during 'reruns', which is a nice touch instead of just assuming that whatever the protagonist does is okay. I do have mixed feelings about how/why it was used a couple times but that's likely just my background in Ethics refusing to turn off.The setting of not!New York (they call it New Sieg but it's literally just an inaccurate version of New York) will probably be a little more disorientating for people actually from New York but you kind of just get used to it after a few hours. Even the weird names just start feeling super natural after a while, perhaps because they're paired up with much more normal names elsewhere (surnames, other characters, etc.). My personal highlight has to be the regular trips to 'Trader Joneses' and listening to the dumb shop music :)There's not much to write here, given that it's a visual novel but there's still something.The protagonist's name is player chosen but a default name (Teuta) is offered, which is a plus for players like me who don't like to play as themselves or just aren't very good at coming up with names. I noticed that Hiragana input is also accepted, if that's a plus for anyone else.I liked that once you selected a choice, it briefly changes colour to indicate the love interest it 'aligns' with (if there is one - not all options have any alignment). It made it a lot easier to tell where I had messed up :). The game also gives a 'rewind' option allowing you to replay or undo a choice if the immediate aftermath is truly too horrifying to continue or you're just trying to 100% and accidentally chose the wrong option, which is handy since some of the choices are timed ('rewind' can only go back so far so you still need to make saves for good/bad endings).I'm a little bit sad that the game didn't have any 'point and click' elements (à la Ace Attorney) as I was really getting into the mystery elements of the game but at that point, I think I'm asking too much from a game that wasn't advertised as such.It's pretty clear as soon as you boot the game up that it's just a direct port from the Switch version so don't expect 4K @ 144 FPS lol. I haven't had any performance issues or weird glitches, however, it's worth nothing that the keyboard controls are a tad strange (e.g. it's HOME for the menu, not ESC for some reason) but usable once you find out what they are. Personally, I just played with a controller for the most part. The only thing I mapped was the D-pad  (to work as left analogue) so it could be used for navigation and then some of the menus because I have bad habits from other games :)There are no achievements on Steam but there is a progress tracker in game which serves my purposes well enough. The only thing I couldn't get to work was Steam's cloud sync thingy so I was stuck to only playing on my laptop, which isn't a deal breaker for me but it may be for someone else, I suppose.The translation's good. There is the odd typo here and there and there are a few cases where certain words and phrases maybe weren't the best choice (at least, based off of my understanding of the voice over) but there was certainly nothing glaringly awful that detracted from my enjoyment of the game. In fact, they did a very good job of transforming the characters' different styles of speech and each has a distinct 'voice' in the text.But yeah, overall a good game. Probably worth the money if you've read this far.

_childDocuments_.review: Bustafellows is a good game. Subtle details in the sound (characters arguing in background, characters speaking over each other, etc) make the game-play experience immersive. The dialogue is well-written, and the translation is great with the exception of a few misspellings and the occasional cheesy line ("本当ですか?" is translated as "For realsies?"). The game takes place in the slums and art deco buildings of New Sieg—  a welcomed change from the usual fantasy castles and feudal villages so common in this genre. Routes differ in quality, and a few feel more rushed than others, but in general, each has an interesting story to offer.Something I've also particularly enjoyed about the game was heroine, Teuta. She contributes to the plot in meaningful ways and displays much more agency than the conventional otome heroine. She also develops an especially fun chemistry () with the love interests.However, the game is not without flaws. The PC port is terrible, and if you are unlucky, you will end up with a grainy, partially cut version of the game (both reviews and discussions testify to the frequency of this issue). Experimenting with display resolution will remediate the problem— but it doesn't change the fact that this company is demanding over 40 CAD for a game with a bug that makes game play impossible while offering no technical support.There are also several parts of the game that are left untranslated, including the dialogue in transitions between chapters and an important video near the end of the game. Most of what is untranslated can be understood with weeb-level Japanese, but again, for over 40 CAD, this is unacceptable.Pros:- Immersive storytelling- Engaging dialogue and smooth translation- Fresh plot- Convenient skip & jump function- Heroine of character and agency- Great artCons:- Terrible port - Some dialogue untranslated

_childDocuments_.review: this otome game is so interesting!!Merits:1. Reality-based settingDifferent from lots of this kind of game, it takes place in a modern city so it makes itself easier for me to relate. The city is glamourous on the surface yet crimes that includes drug selling and human trafficking happen everyday in the darkness. And the immigrant issues. Basically, pretty like USA. The realistic setting engages me so much that I can't help to think about the plot during my lunch breaks.2. Relatable personalities as a woman who is trying to be independent. Also, as the female protagonist is working as an ambitious journalist, I can feel the same way that she and I are both striving for a place to rely on in the big city. Though I know it is a tradition that the female protagonist always will say something brave and impress the male characters, the words which come from her mouth do surprise me from time to time. I kinda even start to fall in luv with her.3. Good visual performanceWhen I was randomly scrolling my Steam page, the thing that caught my eyes first was BUSTAFELLOWS's excellent preview video. It is well-drawn and well-animated not only about the characters but also the background pictures. You can even see smokes rising from the factories when it comes to a period of time in the New Sieg (the setting). Those lovely CGs are my favourites, especially Scarecrow's cute blushes and smiles.4. A pretty impressive way to chose your dating mateAs I mentioned before, Scarecrow is really sweet, cute, a bit childish maybe? I like all of those anyway. He's the first one I developed a romantic relationship with. Was it a surprise? Yes and no. Yes bcz  I didn't see it coming until the cat responses to his choice of name and I didn't realise I would like him that much even though he's probably not the most popular one. No bcz I did like him more before I got into his part of the story later. He is so fresh and young in terms of romance (he even watches teen movies to imagine what a date should be like, so naive and cute). But when it comes to technology, he, a talented genius for it, is professional and confident. Tho when he's got something wrong, he becomes suddenly embarrassed and starts to stammer lolCorrect me if I'm wrong, the way that decides your date seems rather uncommon in those mountains of otome games. But it's actually a good way to see your preferences and how well you and your date is gonna match.(Spoiler alert: the test Mr. Sauli gives you will determine who is your next one among the five fela)Demerits:1. Quite dragging when the parts of solving cases together ends since the personal story is, well, 'personal'.What you'll see later in the story is mostly about solving individual issues. Though you could consider this as a way to know more about the person you want to date (this is hundred percent right), to be honest, I got bored in the personal stories. I have only played Scarecrow's and Helvetica's. so maybe I'll change my opinion later.2. Overusing and lack of development of the female protagonist's special skill and backgroundI do think that there should've been deeper discussion on her side. The going-back-in-time talent. Her family. This game, however, uses them as merely a tool to work out almost all the problems. Also, I don't see the point of foreshadowing that there might be risks of time travelling since the plot later just goes to saving your date and then sweet romance. _childDocuments_.review: Bustafellows is a game about a young reporter with limited time traveling powers who, by going back in time to save the leader, joins a gang of men who bring justice through their own means from within and outside the lines of the law. That being said: this game is a lot deeper than I had expected. Firstly, the love interests, there is variety in stereotypes. The princely leader (Limbo), the broody older man (Shu), the picky pretty boy (Helvetica), the quiet smart one (Mozu), and the young prodigy (Scarecrow). Each has their own route that is distinct and separate from the common route and from the routes of the others. They are all paced differently with a fun adventure that ends up having everyone work together for the greater good. As characters, while I loved "loving" them, honestly feel a little predicable. While I could tell how they'd think and feel in their stories, the writing was done so well that I had felt like they were fleshed out people with their own genuine emotions. So kudos to the writers for their hard work. Second, the art. I don't know much about art as a whole, or about a pictures composition or color theory or whatever, but everything was drawn consistently. The artists where clearly together to make sure that the characters, no matter the angle or lighting, were always identifiable and distinct. While I wish I could say more for the variety in character design, the boys aren't exact copies with different color pallets. All light skinned men aged 20+, although it's supposed to be taking place in a fictional city around New York City, USA. Third: Main/Player character. The MC is very pretty and generally likable. While this is the aim otome games try to take not all can execute it as gracefully as bustafellows was able to. While my ideas don't match up with the ideals of the MC, I can completely understand her hard points and stubbornness. And while I think that she is occasionally over dramatic in expressing herself, I must also acknowledge that I am a more reserved person. She isn't a pushover or a doormat, nor overly nice. She explicitly will explain that some characters are just acquaintances or that some are being annoying. She is honest and passionate in her job and life. Fourth: Supporting cast. MC has two childhood friends. Luka, a female police officer, and Adam, a male news broadcaster. Their friendship is established as a no secrets, tell all, friendship. While it does show the realities of real life, with schedules butting heads and being late to designated meetings, it also shows the difficulties of maintaining such a friendship.  We also meet Limbos older sister, Valarie, an established prosecutor and independent woman. I find her to be graceful while also being overly stern with how those around her interact with her. She is controlling and demanding in that she be treated with the upmost respect at all times, but to an extreme extent becoming threatening at even the slightest unintentional "girl". Over all, I'm aware that my dislike for her is surface level because she does care for Limbo and his friends, helping them when possible and even fighting on their behalf. Next you meet Helvetica's caretaker and legal guardian, Professor Sauli, a professor at the nearby academy for privileged students. He is calm and collected, but still a relaxed man.  Carmen, a restaurant owner and best friend to Valarie. She, while annoying me at first, had become one of my favorite characters over the game. Carmen is an outgoing charismatic woman who often hosts the gang at her restaurant and joins them in their highjinks. She is brightly dressed and has an equally as bright personality. The  plot.  I cannot explain the entirety of the plot because, while it makes sense, is a little complicated to explain. However the plot is worth playing through all the routes to get to, as it wraps up so many plot holes that I had noticed throughout the individual romantic interests routes.  Overall the boys are both attractive and distinct, no two being the same in looks or personality. The art is consistent and smooth. The NPCs are charming and definitely grow on you. And the individual routes and overarching story line are interesting and have replay value. I'd say 8/10, beautiful art, characters, and writing. Only downsides were personal opinions about character diversity, and certain routes that should have considered adding trigger warnings.

_childDocuments_.review: BUSTAFELLOWS is a very good VN. Detective / adventure part of the story gets here more attention than romance. But the story is interesting, sometimes funny, sometimes thought-provoking.Pros:1. Story is very entertaining. It is a detective adventure, where a team of very talented different people solve crimes or expose criminals, guided by their own sense of justice. It also touches complicated social questions.2. MC is not dumb. OMG it is a useful, independent and smart main character in Otome game! Who would have thought. She actively participates in all adventures, sometimes playing the one of most important parts of the mission (she also has some quests that she solves on her own without help of anyone else). She reacts on dangerous or emotional situations like a decent and sane person. She still has some common Otome features though: she is cute, shy and naive. But it's fine, I liked her.3. Boys are cool and interesting. In the game you'll have 4 common route chapters, and then you'll unlock 'Side A' chapter for the man you've showed the most interest in. What route will be unlocked depends on your non-plot related choices. Game actually hints you which choice favours which character: after making a choice dialog button will flash in a specific colour .There is no "recommended order" for this game, as all Side A stories are different. For my taste, the best love interest would be Adam, but he has no route, so from those who left the order be: Shu > Mozu > Crow > Helvetica > Limbo. Ye, in my opinion Limbo's story was the weakest one . All their stories worth reading IMO.4. Side characters are also good and interesting.5. Art is good, especially backgrounds and character's sprites. This game is fully voiced and voice acting is a quality one. CGs and music are alright, not too bright, but not bad either.Cons:1. rare for VNs, but this one have bugs: it shows no subtitles on chapter start/end or some transition scenes (it has only Japanese voice). A workaround that I used: open log and read from there everything you missed. Log can be opened from 'End' or 'Home' buttons on PC, yes, the ones above your arrow-keys, weird controls indeed.2. 'Side B' stories are weak. Side B stories are opened when you finish Side A chapter with a good ending. Side B includes a very short episode after characters started dating, and they are behaving like teenagers there, which is kind of dumb.So the conclusion, I would recommend BUSTAFELLOWS, it's a good story, it's a good read, it worth it's time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty solid! To preface, I have played Shu and Scarecrow's route but won't include any spoilers.First, I have to give a big round of applause for the  in this game. Not a lot of otome games pay attention to these types of details like moving the character's eyes to face different characters that are also speaking in the same frame. It gives life and a certain realness to the world they live.Then I have to talk about the . How often do we have MC's friends who just jump in from time to time to say things and then leave? No, here our MC has an effective support system where friends respond to to the trouble she is in. They also hang out in a trio without the MLs.Which leads me to the . They all bounce off of each other in a playful and hilarious way. They aren't just there to further the plot but they also banter about different things like who's better at a game, their personal habits and tease each other about their personal pet peeves. The MC herself is also pretty funny, cheeky and sarcastic. It's all around a fun crew that accepts the MC into their lives, not a world specifically formed around her which makes them shine as individuals.The genre of this game was really interesting with them as a rag tag crew solving different mysteries. Although Limbo (the himbo) is the poster boy, he doesn't stand out as the leader because , even the MC. What I can appreciate is how the MC actively helps the MLs in their route  especially in the two routes I've played.Yes, I will admit the game mechanics were clunky (I hooked up my PS4 controller) and the game was in lower res because I played it on PC but you won't usually notice it unless you are watching the OP. Overall, a game I would highly recommend anyone to pick up and play~

name: What The Dub?!
detailed_description: Remote Play - Quick Start In What the Dub?! players use any browser enabled device to enter text and vote. However, when playing with remote players, they'll need a way to see the host's screen in order to view the video clips. Luckily, playing on PC/Mac is fairly simple. We recommend these two methods. Zoom Download Zoom Open Zoom and start a new meeting. Invite players to your meeting. Click Share Screen. Select your desktop and make sure 'Share Sound' and 'Optimize for Video Clip' (in the lower left corner) are selected. Open What The Dub?! and start a game! If you run into any issues, don't hesitate to reach out in the discussion forums! About the Game What The Dub?! is a multiplayer party game where each player overdubs missing dialogue from hilariously awful B-movies, woefully outdated PSAs, and bizarre industrial films, with their own witty (or just plain stupid ) dubs. Players watch the dubs and vote on the best one. The player with the highest score at the end of the game wins! It's just that easy! Over 600 so-bad-they're-good clips to dub! Play head to head with 1 to 6 players (6 players enter dubs and an additional 12 audience members can vote). Expand your clip library with hundreds of community created clip packs! What the Dub?! comes loaded with a host of Streamer-friendly features. Twitch chat voting allow your entire audience to get in on the fun! Our moderation and content tools ensure your game remains troll-free. Enter text using your phone, tablet, or computer. You write the dub, we do the talking! Your dubs are played back via text-to-speech. Supports over 29 different languages! NOTE: Players are required to use web enabled devices (such as smartphones, tablets, computers, etc.) to input text into the game. TTS Language Support is available in the following languages: Arabic Bahasa Indonesia Dansk Deutsch (German) English Español - España (Spanish - Spain) Español - Estados Unidos (Spanish - US) Filipino Français (French) Italiano (Italian) Nederlands Norsk bokmål (Norwegian Bokmål) Polski (Polish) Português (Portuguese) Tiếng Việt (Vietnamese) Türkçe (Turkish) Русский (Russian) हिन्दी (Hindi) বাংলা (Bengali) ગુજરાતી (Gujarati) தமிழ் (Tamil) తెలుగు (Telugu) ಕನ್ನಡ (Kannada) മലയാളം (Malayalam) 國語 - 台灣 (Mandarin - Taiwan) 普通话 - 中国大陆 (Mandarin - Mainland) 廣東話 (Cantonese) 日本語 (Japanese) 한국어 (Korean)

_childDocuments_.review: As an English teacher during this seemingly never-ending pandemic, thank you for this game! It's so simple to set up and incorporate What the Dub into online lessons via Zoom, Microsoft Teams etc that I'd recommend it to any and all ESL teachers. The included video clips manage to be both humorous in their dubbing potential whilst also being relatively simple in terms of their language that it allows students who are A2 level and above to reliably produce clever, funny or appropriately wacky sentences. Moreover, the simplicity of the game makes it suitable for everyone over the age of 10 and the price is very fair for what's offered. Highly recommended to any online English teacher in need of adding some fun activities into their online lessons!!!PS. I reckon the game would be pretty fun with a group of adult friends too.Update - Most of my qualms with the first release have since been addressed with various patches. Kudos to the devs for listening to everyone's feedback. I guess all that's left now is to hope for some new and maybe even premium expansions to drop with more clips to dub. I'd pay for that!

_childDocuments_.review: You write over lines from old public domain movies. That's it. It does one thing and it does it well. You know exactly what you're getting into if you've ever enjoyed a Jackbox game. As always, it's as fun as the people you bring into the mix. Luckily I always seem to have lots of fun! If you think your friend group might like it, they probably will. There seem to be a lot of clips (haven't seen any repeats yet!) and I think the robot voice really adds a lot and brings out the deadpan humor. The set up is nice and easy. Lots of options to play with (and the devs seem really fast and receptive to adding new ones). And at the end of the day it's 8 bucks!
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun to play, it takes a little bit for first-time players to get used to the general gist of the game, but once everybody finds their rhythm it's an incredibly hilarious and fun game!Some quick suggestions for the developer -1. Add more TTS voices. Although the current voice is funny, it would be a lot more versatile to add different voices, and would give players a sea of creative opportunities.2. Allow the player to change the pacing of the clip to fit their dub. Sometimes, when we would submit longer dubs, the clip would just run in its entirety, or if they were short dubs, wouldn't last long enough to fit the scene. I think it would be super helpful if the player could actually fit their dubs better with the scenes by adjusting the speed of the narration/clip to match their dub.3, Create a robust dev toolkit to allow players to create mods/add their own clips to the game. This is where this game would stand out compared to Jackbox etc - Allowing players to mess around with the game and add their own clips and game modifications!Overall, incredibly fun game that is absolutely now a part of my party game rotation!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: NEW REVIEWThe developer has fixed all of my issues, so I'm happy to alter the review to a positive and repurchase the game :)Thank you, Dev!I only hope now that the number of players or audience members is increased.OLD REVIEWNeeds a lot of polish.If someone is disconnected, the game doesn't realise, and forces you to sit through the entire timer each time. It should kick them if they don't post anything twice in a row.The extended timers are DOUBLE timers, essentially. It should either be 30 seconds, or allow a custom timer.Finally, it says the game is for 12 players, but it's actually just 6. Anyone over 6 becomes an audience member.We had fun with it, but it was very short lived because of these short comings.

Largely the same type of concept as Jackbox games, this game sees you placing your own imaginative lines over scenes of cheesy old films, using TTS to read out your responses.Some hilarious and crude responses and something the viewers will love. It sat well with my community who were all racing to get a spot in each game session. At a reasonable price, it's not one to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! Love this game. If you like Jackbox, you may love this. It is basically a game where you watch clips and then write captions for it. Your captions will go head to head against everyone else's. The more people you have to play this, the better diversity of answers. I would recommend having at least 4 players. The game says it allows a lot more players than it does, however I think the maximum for actual caption entries is 6. Any additional players become audience members. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes party games. You only need one copy to play with friends and the rest of the players can just use their browsers and discord to play along.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: This is like a game out of a Jackbox pack, where you make a room and can provide a code to anyone else that can participate using their phones or a browser to submit the answers.  Out of the box without mods, it may take a couple games to get into the swing of things in What The Dub but after that it turns into great fun if you play with people who go all out with their answers and not restrain themselves.  Clips can be modded in as well, so there is some possible variety where you can add your own spice to the game or if you have great ideas for random scenes in movies to add.Playtime showing is lower than my actual playtime since you only need one copy of the game to play the game with others similarly to the way Jackbox does it with their party packs.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what happens when Quiplash and Mystery Science Theater 3000 have a baby.A squishy, forgotten footage baby with text-to-speech and a diaper full of sound effects.All in all, it's a great, quick moving game that doesn't require players to have anything special (just need a browser and a room code). If you've worn out your Jackbox collection, swap this in to freshen things up.I'd like to see a smoother, snappier flow when clip responses have a lot of TTS and effects blended together and an option to turn off the Loser announcement (or make it a little more tongue in cheek).EDIT - 2021.04.20: A recent patch tightened up the TTS and added the option to remove negative commentary. That was fast!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty great and funny game. Me and my friends had a blast playing it yesterday, creating those silly prompts for the videos and I still remember some. And now that videos can be played twice it's even better. Be sure to disable negative announcer quips if you have a friend that is not as creative as your other friends. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game to play with a group. I enjoy stream hopping on twitch, hearing new answers and approaches to questions. This game gets the creative juices flowing. Adding sound effects, Text to speech, being able to kick players mid game, are a few of the areas where this game has excelled by similar "user interaction games" in my opinion.Dubbing over videos is a lot of fun. 10/10(splash)
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, my gaming group loves it as an addition to the Jackbox stuff. It is very well done and fun! You can make it as clean or as dirty as you like which means everyone can play. The clips are weird and esoteric enough that most people won't know where they're from and that is perfect. I hope they add more. I do have some minor suggestions, though. Something more for the audience to do. Maybe they could throw out suggestions on screen or something. Just a thought. Being in the audience can be boring at times. I know more players would mean more repeating clips, but maybe have the game know when there are more than 6 and only use short clips for that game so it doesn't get too monotonous. The game takes a little getting used to and the timer is set way too quick for first timers. Maybe set it higher as the default. I find 45 seconds to be about right. Then the players can tweak it later. Also, the negative comments on the lowest scorer are not great. They're just unnecessary.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: What the dub is a really great game. It's similar to jackbox games where players use their controllers to play and then try to come up with funny quips and vote for the best one.In this game (and it's sequel rifftrax) you watch a video clip typically from an old movie, and the clip has a space with missing dialogue. Your job is to add dialogue to the scene by typing it out on your phone. You can also add music or sound effects. You then get to watch the clip with everyone's dialogue read off using text to speech. It's a very fun game for a party.It's also much better than it's sequel "rifftrax the game" here's a quick breakdown of what's better in each game:Rifftrax: More sound effectsAllows you to use premade jokes instead of writing your own (but they're never as good)What the Dub:Workshop support (allows you to download hundreds of clip packs to expand the game infinitely) Which the sequel does not have!And the sequel seems to add an unfunny prewritten response to every prompt which adds nothing to the game and stands out like a sore thumb.Buy this one!
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game and always have a great time when I'm playing it. The sound effects are hilarious (although I miss a "Crowd: awhhh" sound) and the prompts are often very useable. Like many others, I'd love a function that enables you to easily add your own clips, but also a function that lets you save the filled in clips to your device because we often get hilarious results and would love to watch them back without having to set up an external recording
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun to play with lots of friends! It's like Jackbox. You enter the text you see fit (or not) and the game will do the dubbing for you. . On the text-entering screen, you can change the TTS to any language available. I chose Thai, my native tongue, and the game read the text in those AI voices. Imagine Siri. Yeah. Darn hilarious. Totally recommended. 10 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: I knew this game would be the perfect party game as soon as I discovered it.You could use your imagination with your friends.But realistically it all comes down to d*cks & sh*t!Bring out your best insults & cash in on those inside jokes. Hilarious game well worth it, I'll be playing many hours in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun. Playing it in our virtual group almost every week. Only one person needs to own the game. Rules are extremely simple, so it is always easy to introduce new players. There are a lot of clips included, so it is hard to get tired of this game. If you are looking for a fun game for a virtual or local party — it is an excellent choice. And, yes, while developers can't include clips from commercial movies for the obvious legal reasons, let's say, it is not so hard to include them into the game by yourself. So we, for example, had What the dub Star Trek-themed play sessions, it was so much fun!
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the following:-Mystery Science Theater 3000-Rifftrax-Cinematic Titanic-Jackbox Party games-Classic movies or Vintage TVYOU WILL LOVE THIS GAME.This game works just like Jackbox and it also works like MST3K. It is set up like Jackbox but it is its own thing at  It has Twitch integration and everything just like Jackbox. Basically, you are given B movie or TV show clips from the really old days of movies or television (1930's through the 1970's)  These video clips are short with closed caption audio. The video clips have dialogue followed by missing audio dialogue. Your job is to make up the missing audio dialogue with your own caption. after the caption is written and typed out on the website. The clips are played back with your caption and read by text to speech robot voices. You then vote for the best caption for that clip and then go on to the next round and do it again. I highly recommend this to anyone looking for a good party game.If you want gameplay footage, I submit to you My first gameplay from this stream highlight from YouTube. (it is NSFW. you have been warned!) see for yourself..

For a bit, I couldn't figure out what it was, but I think another reviewer put it well - the clips lack context. _childDocuments_.review: A favorite of ours for game night playing with family across the country.  Even though the newer RiffTrax is also fun, I feel like What the Dub?! is easier to come up with funny lines.  RiffTrax is more for funny commentary, while WTD is better for swapping in dialogue.  Adding in Steam Workshop for community clips gives this added life.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a better party game than any Jackbox game, by far.I really recommend this game if your group of friends likes party games. It's absolutely worth the price, even more considering that if you split the price with your friends it might cost very little.Theoretically it has infinite longevity, since the base clips are more than 300, and then you can add more custom clips from the workshop, or you could add your custom clips, and most importantly in the language you prefer, so that if your friends can't understand english, like in my case, you can make them enjoy the game in a better way.Said that, it's important that the game doesn't rely that much to language, since it depends on clips language, so it has a lot of potential.You can even select the speech synthesis voice from your smartphone, changing the language your dub will be read in, making it easier to pronounce the phrases in your own language, or making it funnier by making it being pronounced with a different language voice.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: What the Dub is essentially a beefed-up version of a Jackbox Party Pack minigame. It revolves around you and your friends being shown a randomized selection of clips from public domain shows, or films, with a piece of dialogue removed. Players then submit their own interpretation of what the lines would be in the gaps, with an endearingly janky TTS voice (along with plenty of sounds) reading them out. Whoever's funniest wins.This is good enough on it's own, but the game recentley entered a whole new level with the addition of it gaining workshop support. The public domain clips wear thin after a while, but now you practically have an unlimited amount of clips, modern and old, to choose from. It's like hand-crafting a YTP, one scene at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: -Edit- The dev added workshop support now too, what a LEGEND!Absolutely hilarious and brilliant concept, a complete riot with some funny, open minded friends too naturally. I've seen some hilarious videos/streams of this with Admiral Bulldog and some other streamers too.Only 1 of you needs the game and up to 5 friends and 6 voters can participate, they just need a device with internet browser access, so a phone, tablet, a games console, laptop or whatever should be fine.Its best with 4 more or people at least but it can even be played solo or with just 2 or 3. The developer is very thoughtful and nice and even created a successor to this  called Rifftrax too.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral review button for steam, this would be under that category. _childDocuments_.review: Of all the Jackbox-likes out there, this and its RIfftrax-based successor are probably my favourites. But that's probably more a signifier of how much I've played this game, and they did do a better job in that regard with the Rifftrax game. If you want a wider selection of video clips (and a funnier text-to-speech option, in my opinion), then give this a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game for the price. Being able to play from the phone and across Discord is an amazing feature also, which I've only ever seen in the Jackbox series. Unlike those games however, which sometimes have a learning curve and can be more challenging for the uninitiated, What the Dub?! is much more straightforward in gameplay and can be geared toward a wider audience. The optional profanity filter is nice for playing with the whole family. Obviously take it off when the kids go to bed though, because this game is pretty hilarious when you cut loose. Lastly, I think it's neat that you can still play if you only have two people. There's no scoring or audience, it's just fun. Good game. Buyer's remorse-free. Big smiles.
_childDocuments_.name: What The Dub?!

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Use Your Word's "Sub the Title", this is basically just "Sub the Title: The Game". And it's GREAT. The one thing I love "What the Dub!?" does compared to "Sub the Title" is it actually allows you to add sound effects and reads your responses in a Microsoft Sam-style voice instead of just putting your reply over the actual audio clip. Hearing some the absolutely INSANE things coming out of Microsoft Sam's voice is just hilarious. I do wish some of the sound effects weren't obnoxious (I use only a handful of them reliably - the others I avoid because they are just grating), but they can be fun to use. The game does mock you for having the lowest scores a round or losing - as much as I love how the game talks **** about you, it also gets old real quick and overstays it's welcome, so I appreciate the fact you can disable it.If you like "Use Your Words" or "Jack Box", this is a great addition to your party game library. It may not have as much variety as other party games, but it does it well and it's a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: What The Dub?! is a simple game, with a simple premise, and for a party game, that's absolutely okay. It's not going to hold a group's attention longer than a Jackbox, but it doesn't need to for you to get your money's worth. It isn't a Jackbox night replacement, it's a Jackbox night supplement. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty entertaining way to pass the time with friends. If you've played Jackbox games and want something in the same style, but different, this is solid and enjoyable. There are some downsides though, which you should be aware of before purchasing. The player limit is eight players. While sometimes in Jackbox the player limit is smaller than I'd like, it usually makes sense given the constraints of the game, whereas this seems like it would work with 8 people without any real changes. Six is pretty close to right though.  At the end of each round the host picks someone who didn't get a vote and makes a joke or comment about it. At the end of the game the loser is called out. Maybe some groups will enjoy this but in my group it felt weird and mean-spirited. There is an option to turn it off, but it's on by default, my group didn't notice the option before starting, and you can't change it (or even show it) in the middle of a round.Other than that... some of the clips are duds, but that's kind of a given with a game like this, and most of them are pretty good. One request for the devs: show the clip's script on screen while the timer counts down for reference.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of those wisecracking robots on MST3K, or maybe you think you can write a script better than those screenwriters from the golden age of cinema.  What The Dub?! might be the game you’ve been waiting for, especially after a year-long drought on parties and general get-togethers of any kind.  This multiplayer game presents you with over 300 retro clips from all sorts of B-movies and other random sources – basically anything in the public domain is fair game –  and then play a short section of content with a bit of the dialogue removed.  You then get to fill in the gap with your own dialogue and everyone votes on the responses as they are played back with some adequate text-to-speech software.The clips are hysterically bad in most cases, and while some are pretty easy setups for witty ADR other had me drawing a complete blank.  Thankfully, there is a fun Foley menu that lets you insert amusing sound effects either to enhance your contribution or even serve as your response when you start to experience writers’ block.  What The Dub?! supports 29+ languages making this fun pastime accessible to much of the world.  The actual text-to-speech is surprisingly good with male and female voices that still come off a bit robotic and have trouble with some pronunciations, but everyone gets the idea.  There are some great achievements to be unlocked and random fun stuff like having all the players listed in the credits with fun character names/titles.Full review at

name: Mary Skelter 2
detailed_description: What must you sacrifice to escape fate? Find out in this nightmarish dungeon-crawling RPG! The Nightmare continues in Mary Skelter 2! In this first-person dungeon crawler, play as fairy tale-inspired characters called Blood Maidens, each with deeply customizable character-specific classes. Balance between power and madness in turn-based battles with a blood-fueled transformation system, and escape a living prison while indestructible Nightmares give chase in real time. The Jail - a living prison that feeds on the humans trapped within its confines. The Jail appeared a number of years ago with the caving of the city around it. Now twisted creatures known as Marchens and treacherous Nightmares roam its halls. Otsuu and Little Mermaid are a part of a group of humans known as 'Dawn' attempting to survive these horrors. They succeed in saving Alice and a young man named Jack on one mission. However, on their return back to base, Alice goes mad and begins attacking those around her. Alice strikes Jack, who was trying to protect Otsuu and Little Mermaid, knocking them down a chasm. Later, Otsuu and Little Mermaid awaken from the fall only to find Jack on the verge of death... And so begins the tale of escaping from fate, led by a group of girls seeking sanctuary in this mad world, and of the young man who would transform into madness itself - a Nightmare. Mary Skelter 2 revisits the previous game by including the remake of Mary Skelter: Nightmares. Improvements made in the remake have been reflected in Mary Skelter 2, for an even more intense experience. (Of course, you can enjoy Mary Skelter 2 on its own.)

_childDocuments_.review: I had a hard time writing this, as after years, this is the first time this game is available on any other platform than the Switch in English. I had hopes this new PC release would fix the issues with that release and make it more accessible to those who don’t have one or want to deal with the mediocre performance, and that Ghostlight would break the curse of mediocre (or borderline awful) PC ports from IdeaFactory. This port is a downgrade from their previous ports, and even PC ports outsourced to PreApp Partners using the same engine to a degree. There’s definitely other things that you can criticize them for, such as their odd practices of region locking Japanese players from their PC releases (Although this is apparently due to licensing reasons). I am revising some points in this review, since an uncensored patch has been released off-site, and they were on pushing updates every few days to fix some port issues. So far, three or four patches have been pushed so far, but none of the major issues have really been fixed yet, alongside some further graphical regressions (Such as the wireframe effect on enemies in dungeons when fading), and game breaking bugs with sidequests.I’ll preface this by saying I nearly 100%’d the game to completion on Switch, I spent ~80-90hrs in the 2nd game, and ~40hrs or so in the 1st (Which includes a new ending which retcons the original’s, has balance changes, and is abridged, which made the final dungeon digestible). The game is fantastic, and I came into this series blind, as my takes on “blobbers” was ruined by how mind-numbing Persona Q was. I didn’t want this game to end like how Sakura Wars and strategy JRPGs (after Fire Emblem and Valkyria Chronicles put me off on trying them). Most of the characters are likable (except Rapunzel), and the game has downtime (this game’s equivalent of Persona’s social links) between dungeons that you unlock by using the gift exchange feature to max out character’s affections. The difficulty can be rather unforgiving at higher difficulties, which forced me to save often on several occasions, so there’s definitely some challenge for those interested in it. Otsuu and Ningyo-hime are probably the most wholesome lesbian representation I’ve seen in gaming.The good news that I can say about this port: GL fixed the hardcoded resolution on post-processing effects that the PreApp ports on the same engine have (Which results in 4K looking identical to 1080p). Despite some resolution issues being fixed however, there are some notable issues still worth mentioning. On a 3440x1440 monitor, the resolution is listed as “3440x1935”, and that runs the internal resolution at 3440x1440 before it’s crunched to a 2560x1440 space resulting in extra GPU strain. At 2560x1440, the image doesn’t have filtering when it’s being scaled, resulting in a nearest filtering effect or chunky pixels based on your monitor. Borderless and windowed modes are still using Copy to GPU GDI composition rather than Flip Discard (Which would result in latency being equivalent to running in exclusive fullscreen). There is also a bug with stutter and MSAA somehow being enabled on 2D elements, which results in performance and rendering related problems when running through Proton (And is why the game wasn't verified for Steam Deck support) as well. Some of these issues may be moot as updates happen, but ymmv.There are no graphics options (Such as to disable the forced TAA (Which was an issue in PreApp’s PC ports), enabling/disabling motion blur, disabling DoF and Chromatic Aberration (Which are used quite liberally in most of Compile’s games to the point where it get’s obnoxious). The engine has these options in the game executables (and I’ve even managed to force override them in previous ports), so I have no clue why these options are not provided. There isn’t even a custom FOV option (Which would help in the case of sitting close to a monitor, to prevent motion sickness), let alone ultrawide support during gameplay (Nobody would really care if stuff outside of gameplay was pillarboxed to a 16:9 aspect ratio). This port is as bare as you’re gonna get when it comes to scalability. Even No More Heroes and Ninja Gaiden offer more options. VIIR, another CH game on PC even has more options.KB/M support in the port is not there yet. The game refused to pick up on inputs on anything other than my mouse, until I turned on my controller and went to the settings in-game to switch it to KB/M. The game doesn’t swap between them based on the last input like in the first game. As for bindings, several things have hardcoded bindings which are joined with other actions, such as activating blood abilities being tied to the same button that hiding dialogue text and going back in a menu, which by default is backspace or left shift, which is clunky. A and B are reversed during dungeon exploration due to the swapped buttons, which is odd coming from the Switch release, so A is now for interacting and B is for blood abilities. Mouse navigation (including the left mouse button) is missing when using healing items or the blood licking ability in battle, resulting to using WASD and Space to navigate. Mouse buttons and scroll wheel are absent from bindings. Full rebinding with categories for gameplay, battles, and VN/Dialogue segments would’ve been appreciated.The Switch version has double buffered Vsync (The game will dip 20-30 FPS if it can’t hit 60FPS), which when tied with the game logic being on a fixed 60FPS timestep, often results in slowdown, especially in the Temple or Aquatic ruins. Due to this, I hoped the PC release would support uncapped framerates (alongside fixing the speed issue), which the first game did on PC. However, the game uses the same busted limiter which has a rounding error to 63-64FPS (Which makes the game speed faster if you use a refresh rate over 60Hz) like every previous IFI port using Orochi 4. This is bad. Not everyone has a FreeSync display or hardware that can handle a locked 60FPS. When you remove the limit in this port (note, Vsync is always on), only dialogue segments with characters run at the full refresh rate, while game menus, gameplay, and combat are capped at 92-93FPS. This is similar to running 2 and Finale in Yuzu/Ryujinx, where the framerate is higher during dialogue segments, but cap at ~96FPS outside of those (I have narrowed down what is causing this). I appreciated that the first game gave the option of that, and there were no game speed related issues outside of some character portrait animations updating faster.As updates were being pushed, and the purification minigame can be added again using an off-site uncensored patch, It’s becoming a little easier for me to recommend the PC port of the game. While there’s still plenty of issues to note, and I’m a little less disappointed with the current state of the PC release (make sure to send Ghostlight’s technical support with issues with the port). While I can say they did a far better job at handling post-launch updates for a small portion of time than PreApp Partners’ PC ports, and that already is worth commending. Between this and possibly looking into doing the same with their previous ports (if they can), I’m likely going to buy a few copies for some friends of mine as a way of voting with my wallet.It's really hard for me to recommend *any* version of this game due to technical issues, which is a shame. I'm incredibly burned out from rushed IF ports and releases that never get patched. I'm also leaving my modding efforts on the backburner for now, as the lack of debug symbols makes finding functions and variables for certain things that need to be fixed a pain.EDIT: It's been two months, and still no update to fix the game speed/framerate issues. It's safe to say the port has been abandoned, judging by a recent interview with the Ghostlight CM on a Twitch stream. Also, this port is based on the Switch release, which was downgraded

_childDocuments_.review: Good dungeon-crawlers (or blobbers, which this isn't technically the definition of) are hard to come by. I put 160+ hours into this, so I feel I'm qualified to review. Mary Skelter 2 is full of strong ideas and isn't afraid to take risks. Most of the risks pay off; some of them don't.I played both games; for those of you that don't know, upon beating this game you get the first game (Mary Skelter: Nightmares) for FREE. So don't buy the first game; it's bundled in here. Anyway, I enjoyed both games and I liked 2 more than 1, mostly due to quality of life issues. The games have similar strengths and weaknesses, but not always, so consider what I'm about to say covering both games.Alright, so any RPG review really only needs to touch on two things the story/plot, and the combat. I'll touch on both.First off, the characterization and story here gets a solid B+. All the characters were MOSTLY distinctive in combat, with a few copies, but all good as far as writing goes. A couple characters are annoying, a couple are okay but boring, I'm sure everyone will have 2 or 3 favorites. There is enough variety that you'll find some you like, although some characters are VERY plot-unimportant so they don't get much time to shine (and I'm talking about 'in party' characters, not just NPCs). The games story has some pretty interesting gimmicks going on that I wont spoil, but the characters and story were strong enough to carry me through to the Final Ending. Both games start strong and end strong which are the most important parts. Both games have parts in the mid-game that drag but there are always important plot reviews being doled out, which is good because dungeon crawling can be tedious (still fun, but tedious) so you NEED a decent story and characters to make for a good break/reward from completing a dungeon or hard floor. Mostly the pacing is okay, although the final dungeon of both games outstayed the welcome (although again, they both nail the endings I'd say).Okay, the combat/gameplay. We got some cool mechanics here; doing critical damage or hitting weakness charges a characters blood meter. When maxed they get attacks they cost very little mana for good return. This is important because almost all attacks are VERY mana intensive. The flipside is your party builds up corruption as they take damage and if they buiild up to much, they may go into the super mode but a version of it that is berserk and will attack randomly, potentially wiping out your own party with these super powerful attacks. Often the threat isn't so much the enemies as it is the corruption buildup from your own party. This creates interesting swings in combat where things can be going smoothly but you slowly start to lose control. The fights can turn into damage control over your corruption just trying to stablilize so you can finish the fight. All good stuff. The itemization/gearing is also decent; your inventory sometimes has too much junk in it that you have to sell, but in general the gear offers more than just NUMBERS GO UP so there are interesting choices to be made there. Stats have a big impact too so getting gear upgraded is impactful and you actually gear when you get a solid upgrade. Some gear is restricted by class, so that forces choices, also good. Unfortunately some of the gear balancing is out of wack; some weapon types are GARBAGE (heavy swords and hammers? Why would I take -100 agility for like +25 attack? Guns and Cards and Reg. Swords are all way too good!). The classes have the same issues; you'll have them all eventually and you don't mix them up in very interesting ways. Unlock them all, get all the skills, pick the best final class and that's it. The costume changes ARE nice though. Not TERRIBLY executed but there's wasted potential in this area.In general I'm glad I played through it for sure, but the encounter rate was too high throughout most of it. I played on Hard for 90% of the series but I swapped to Easy at the very end because I just wanted to be done with all the fighting. I regret playing on Hard; I loved the challenge in some parts, very well balanced. Other parts (some bosses in both games, some random forced encounters in 1) were ridiculously unbalanced. Random encounters were one shotting me and I was NOT under-leveled; I was fairly optimized. The best way to play the game became stack agility, go first, one shot everything. If you can't do that, grind-grind-grind or die instantly in combat. Do yourself a favor, play on Normal.Thanks for the fun time game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, little thing, this game includes a remake of the first game, you just need to enable it from the DLC menu. make a file in the game's directory called "Minigame.dat" to remove censorship, and if you use a controller you're gonna need to set it as active EVERY startup. I thought locking the config file would help but it doesn't.The PC port's kinda rough, but well I don't have a physical Switch, and this port does still run better than the Switch version in Yuzu, even if it has some ODD framerate issues on occasion if you're running the game at a really high resolution, like I am. Resolution's no longer just rescaled 720p, that much has been patched, so no matter what you do it will still actually LOOK better than the Switch version. The game does run at 4K even on a 1060 6GB, so I suspect those framerate issues are something to do with weird VSync buffers more than actual performance.BUT, what I will say, is the gameplay itself is SOLID, and I'm willing to put up with a slightly jank port in favor of better visuals, for a really good game like this. Big Wizardry vibes, if you enjoy Experience Inc games, or the PS2 Wizardry games, Labyrinth of Lost Souls, the Elminage series, or hell just DRPGs in general, do yourself a favor and pick this game up. The game should be pretty self explanatory compared to the cryptic hell that is Elminage ORIGINAL, which is a game I still love, despite it's deeply cryptic nature.The sequel's closer to an alternate campaign with new maps, compared to a direct sequel, like Mary Skelter Final, which is still sadly not on PC yet. Also that game includes story stuff from the first two games, so if you want to start there, that's ALSO fine.It's your usual dungeon crawler fare, but with a lot more field interaction than most games, and a mechanic that each of your party members is capable of doing different things on the field. You also get alternate jobs that you can share activated skills from, although each job has it's own unique passives. You can down-level to get more skill points, as opposed to the usual Japanese Wizardry spin-off/Team Muramasa mechanic of reincarnating characters into a new class and taking a few skills with you.There's also dating sim elements, and there are 5 different class setups, each with two characters who share them, and they each have individual character skills, that are amped up by their dating sim mechanics. The main character is also not actually a fighter, but he can protect your allies and later in the game, prevent them from hitting a berserk mode that they have a change of going into, called Blood Skelter.In short, this game is a very good take on a niche subgenre, and it's certainly one of the more accessible DRPGs out there. Even if you haven't played one before, this isn't a bad place to start, although I will confess Etrian Odyssey Untold is the BEST place to start, and that game actually runs beautifully in Citra, and the touch screen mechanics actually translate quite nicely to the mouse.Oh yeah and also, if you happen to already own it, the original Mary Skelter 1 on PC and Vita does actually also has totally different maps than the remake in this game, and if you really enjoy this game, it is practically an "arrange version" or "B-side" to the remake of the first. If you enjoy DRPGs that's ALSO worth playing. It's a LOT, and I mean a LOT, more labyrinthine than this version's remake, and the maps get absolutely ridiculously long, and it's WAY harder. Can anyone else say THREE 100x100 bonus dungeon maps? In this version they're 30x30 lol.Now THAT, is an experience for the hardcore DRPG fans, but Mary Skelter 2 and the remake of 1/Nightmares included with this are more easily accessible for newbies to DRPGs.EDIT: I was asked to elaborate on why I think both versions are worth playing, and so I shall, this mostly is copied off my reply in my profile. The main thing I'm addressing is the different changes other than the maps.Outside of the maps, there's also a bunch of battle system differences, as the remake outright uses the battle system from 2 with the old magic system, and TBH, I actually prefer the changes the remake made to the battle system. For example, in the original, Gimmicks didn't damage in battle, and dodging was significantly more powerful. BUT, I personally am more of a fan of old-school disorienting large dungeons, which I why I mentioned that originally. Also Mary Skelter 2 adds a new true ending to the remake, and there is an associated map with that that's only in this version.In short, the game is significantly altered to match Mary Sketler 2's mechanics. Which isn't a bad thing, it's just different, and that's why I say the original is worth playing, because it's less like a DQ11 vs DQ11 S situation, where one version has straight up more content, and more of a situation like the Resident Evil 1 remake, where the changes are enough to make each version a different experience, even if overall the remake is preferable.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, hate the port. I know I'm late to the party but I'm back on a DRPG spree so I have to scream at the void about this one.There was a perfect opportunity to make a proper definitive version on PC, using the original PS4 version's code and polishing the translation up. Instead, we got a port of the downgraded Switch version (with broken lighting and all), except somehow buggier and prone to crashes. Barely anything was fixed since launch; last I checked the game still crashed at random, and even the text was still riddled with typos and mistranslations. Mary Skelter Finale is on the same boat even though the PS4 version was released in the West.I'm genuinely beyond disappointed and downright angry regarding this situation, especially knowing that we'll probably never get good native (and future-proof) versions of these games on PC. Idea Factory and Ghostlight had two absolutely brilliant games then proceeded to make quick and dirty ports and leave them to rot.It pains me to say it, but unless you know Japanese or really don't care about the broken graphics, you're better off skipping the entire series at this point. Mary Skelter 2 is cursed with a broken and censored PS4 SEA release, a downgraded English Switch version (compared to the original PS4 one), and a broken and downgraded English PC port. And it's supposed to be the best entry point. Same story on Switch and PC for Finale, but at least it's available in English on PS4, albeit with a dubious localisation from what I've heard. Only the PC port of the original Mary Skelter: Nightmares is apparently decent, somehow.TL;DR: The game is excellent, but for your own sake don't buy this port.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter 2 holds an interesting premise, has great character design, and is a fun dungeon crawler to enjoy. Unkillable monsters follow you through the maps, battles require some careful thinking and the massacre mode is a double edge mechanic that gives the player a boost but also can have consequences in the story. Sadly, it crashes like crazy when using its mechanics. Open this door-crash, use this skill to progress-crash, watch this scene-crash. If there is one thing I hate in games is the loss of progress. It kills the game for me to have to redo that 30 minutes apart again. During my 1.4 hours with the game, the title crashed 4 times. That is WAY too much in that time. It doesn't help that Mary Skelter 2 also has what is called "fixed save points" which means you can only save in certain areas every 30-60 minutes unless you love backtracking every 10 minutes to save again and again. It saddens me to see the port in this poor state because the game is honestly good and enjoyable but the poor code ruins the experience completely. Stay away from it unless you love redoing your last hour constantly because this is an utter mess. I cannot get immerse in the game because every 20 minutes I am asking myself "when will this crash?".
