_childDocuments_.review: around 65h 4/10 1 Yes, there is  and I wrote  No No, as long as you use a few different save slots No No No No No No, you can play on the easiest difficulty NoMary Skelter 2 is an amazing game and it also included Mary Skelter: Nightmares which unlocks after beating the main game. This is done that way because you kinda should play them in that order: First MS2, then MS:N and after that Mary Skelter Finale, which hopefully will get a Steam release. Mary Skelter 2 is a Dungeon Crawler with a lot of story moments. You can skip those story moments if you don't want to go through a lot of endless talks, but I would recommend at least going through the one that happen in the dungeon and when you return to your base to keep up with the story. Personally, I skipped the ones around the rooms of the girls and in the base after a while as they can keep going for a while. The main gameplay is going through the dungeons. They will have multiple floors, but you'll unlock shortcuts to new floors after you have reached them and found those. The game can be a bit challenging as you try to keep the mood of everybody stable... they might be more powerful when they go crazy, but also have a higher chance to die, so most of the time it isn't worth the risk. There is an auto move feature if you want to go back to a certain point in the dungeon when you already have been. With the standard settings, it will stop working when coming close to a threat, but you can change this in the settings. The game also has an auto-battle function, which you can activate and stop while being in a battle. I have used this a lot when encountering easier monsters, but you will want to fight manually when encountering a boss fight. I love that Mary Skelter 2 has those 2 quality of life features.Before the release and in the first week after the release on steam, there was some controversy around the "purge" mechanic being removed from this version. This is a feature with some mature content. I didn't mind that it was removed as I skipped through it in MS:N as soon as I could. By now there has been a patch where it has been added to the game, but it is optional, which is the best of both worlds, this way the people who want it can turn it on and those who don't like it can have it turned off. I have encountered a few bugs while playing through the game. At one point the story just stopped after a boss battle and I had to reload my save and beat the boss again for it to continue. That wasn't too bad as I always just save before story points in the dungeon (as you can see them before encountering them). What was worse is that I have had a few crashes, which made me lose progress. This seems to have to be something to do with playing MS2 on an ultrawide monitor, but it is kinda annoying. I would suggest saving a lot and on different save slots, this will also help out with the achievements and when you screw up during a boss fight. Speaking about the achievements, it has the kinds you expect in an RPG/Dungeon Crawler. There are a lot story related, using a skill X amount of times, completing side quests, and more stuff like that. The game has 2 different endings, but after you complete one you can go back to your previous save and get the other one. As long as you save often and before each story point, you will have no problem at all.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have an appropriate level of tolerance for Idea Factory games, and you like dungeon crawlers, then you'll probably like this too.Mechanically the Mary Skelter series are probably the best games that IF has developed, ie. the mechanics basically make sense and aren't completely insane garbage like Death End Re;Quest. At the same time though, it's poorly balanced; there are a few good classes and weapon types that you will use and many that are worthless. The battle system doesn't have much depth and dungeons, while visually appealing, don't have much in the way of puzzles or any kind of meaningful level design beyond being a series of corridors and rooms.That said, it's just about on the right side of 'good enough', which is a 10/10 by Idea Factory standards. You get two games, here, essentially, and it should be noted that the remake of the first game has original level designs and plays more like the sequel, so it can be enjoyed even if you already played the original.e: to add one thing, the port is fairly decent. Performance is fine. Keyboard and mouse support isn't perfect, but playing on a controller is good. The character portraits (a prominent feature during the VN sections) are very low resolution though, and some contain compression artefacts (which, to be fair, I believe are present in the Switch version too)

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Persona or Disgaea games, you'll probably like the gameplay of Mary Skelter. It's a grid-based Dungeon Crawler RPG with turn-based battles.Your characters can learn new skills from various classes, you can customise each move-set and you can level down your characters to level them up again, gaining more points to unlock skills.There are different types of attacks, like physical/magic, elemental or buffs/debuffs.There are also other features like farming to get items/equipment, increasing relationships by giving gifts, but those aren't as fleshed out as in other games, yet still fun.While cutscenes are usually presented by the usual "sprites of characters talking" like in visual novels, they have some animations to them and are fun to watch.The battles and dungeon-exploring are in 3D, but there aren't overly many animations besides enemies attacking.The design of the game is something I specifically like. Enemies, clothing, dungeons and the atmosphere are great.The story might not be as deep or intense as other RPG stories, but it's entertaining and interesting. Again, it feels similar to Disgaea: there's a lot of comedy, but it also gets serious and dark.I personally really like the music, design and gameplay in this. At first, I was unsure about getting this because of it seeming to be full of fan-service, which isn't something I'm keen on, but it's not that bad and it doesn't feel like the game relies on it.If you buy this, it actually comes with the remake of the first Mary Skelter game, which is a nice bonus, even if it has been changed in story to fit Mary Skelter 2's story better.Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Streamed this for about 3 hours on release day and here's my take.First off, that opening scene right? Very anime. Good job there.Overall graphics and style? I like the visuals. The battle graphics are in-line with this type of game. I enjoy the first-person grid-style dungeons (I used to play the OG Wizardry series and they were all built like this).Music & sounds? Solid. Some of the random voice lines in combat made me look at the screen funny (nani?!) but overall nothing done detracted from the game.My biggest gripe by far .... BY FAR is the unbalanced amount of dialogue scenes versus actual game play.3 hours and I think I spent maybe 30-40 minutes actually playing the game? It felt like a glorified visual novel, which is a huge disappointment based on the description of the game. The first hour of the game is 90% dialogue, which is a huge turn-off. Even games made by both smaller and larger studios don't make this cardinal sin of RPG by overusing dialogue to death. The only good thing is the turbo skip (which isn't really much of a turbo skip but it helps).The English voice acting is nice, so points there... but again, too much dialogue.Maybe it gets better the later in the game you go, but I expected more actual game play than what I saw in the first 3 hours.The game also has random bugs that just cause it to crash, forcing you to replay scenes through limited save points. I had the game crash 3-4 times just in the first 45 minutes. Don't know if it is a bad port issue (I know this was on Switch initially) but it is infuriating.Recommend? Yes, only because nothing is too broken, and I do like the theme, and when I do actually get gameplay it is interesting especially with the blood mechanics involved. The $34.99 tag is a tough sell though for not delivering on gameplay in the crucial hours of the Steam Refund window though.Check out the Youtube VOD I made, see what you think. Maybe you'll like the package the game provides.

_childDocuments_.review: The textures clip. Nothing too serious.Also, the items found in the chests all over the levels are, besides some of the consumables, completely useless. The game allows you to *grow* your own items, easily in +99 variations while the ones you find on the map are their basic variants that only clutter the team’s pouches until the next merchant.  The side quests are absolutely pointless and infuriating. There are only several, very basic types of them: kill x number of enemies, get an x number of certain item (mostly from killing enemies) and go to an x spot on the map. They take a lot of time and the rewards are meaningless. In fact, most of the time I had to go to the inventory and drop a certain amount of items or the game would not let me accept the reward due to the party's holding limit. The worst yet, said quests are given AT THE END of a chapter. This means that instead of completing your quests while you're discovering a new dungeon, you will be forced to return to the floors you've already completed and crawl for another hour or two, hoping for the required enemy to spawn. Just skip the side quests entirely unless you have some form of OCD. In that case, you may consider skipping Mary2 altogether before you fall in love with it and avoiding those completely unnecessary 30 hours or so of running back and forth is no longer an option.Mary keeps crashing. Quite a lot in some locations, and with seemingly no particular action to trigger it. Just walking the maze of corridors and next thing you know, you're watching the desktop. Hopefully, not after you've been hunting that one rare enemy for that one pointless quest for the last hour. Luckily, the ability to save nearly everywhere somewhat remedies this particular issue if you manage to muster up the patience.Finally, the pacing is awful. All the relationship - building events are made available by the end of each chapter just like the quests. Consequently, instead of having a balanced experience of dungeoning alternated with character building, you will have to crawl for approximately 10 hours and then read for an hour or two. Unless, of course you are an intelligent person who can time those events and not ingest them all at once. I, obviously, was not.     Having said that, Mary2 was my game of the year 2022. And then close second to Outer Wilds in 2023, which is still a soul-shakingly astounding ♥♥♥♥♥ of a compliment since nothing comes close to Outer Wilds. Except little lady Mary here. And, look at me still playing it in 2024. I am starting to suspect there might be a pattern somewhere here. I knew this series was going to be somewhat unique the moment I saw a Nightmare in the trailer of the first game some years ago, but I’ve never expected how much this game was going to captivate me in the long run. In retrospect, I believe this might have happened because  The game's entire world is this living, feeling, extremely alien, hostile organism with the sole purpose of containing the protagonists, tormenting them and keeping them caged. There is a good explanation for that buried in the game’s lore and I'd absolutely love to discuss it here but my spoiler policy prevents me. Henceforth, accept the fact that the Mary's world is a miraculously dark place, wonderful to witness from a safe distance of the other side of a screen. Places done, humans now.  Let me dwell on them for a little while. Theirs dreams, hopes, those things. Their autonomy becauseCan you believe they've actually written a fascinating, complex character just with nodding and snoring?Yep... yep...And quite an exceptional bosom, but that's beside the point.The way Mary twists and bends the fable archetypes to create believable characters is insane-good. Red Riding who feels incomplete without her hood. Cinderella saying she is not beautiful and people only think she is because she's hiding behind her extravagant clothes. Snow White with her soul-crushing phobia of mirrors. Everyone being drawn to Little Mermaid's singing.Don't even get me started on Otsuu and Little Mermaid. The maturity and complexity of their relationship is extraordinary. And full of lovely little details. Just go to Otsuu's inventory and idle for a while. The first thing the Crane'd say is "I wonder what Little Mermaid is doing." Switch to the Mermaid's equipment and wait.And finally, there's Gretel. Took me approximately 150 hours and two and a half games to grow fond of her. And Hansel. Just like any other family. Strawberries finishing this paragraph off for no reason at all because I absolutely love the skelter mechanic. Long story short, it's the thing that unconditionally makes the protagonists lose their minds to that all-consuming, overwhelming bloodlust. The discrepancy is fascinating. Watching the quietest, shyest girls of your team screaming in pure euphoria as they harm and mutilate and mangle and murder. And maim. Did I ever tell you my definition of beauty?Malleability is a big thing. The game's systems let you modify basically everything. The party's skills, equipment, even the dungeons. Mary can be an unbearable slog if you choose poorly. It can be a breeze and a power fantasy if you do it right. It's a roulette if you go in blind since the respec comes at a price and is not available on a whim.There's also a superb, customizable autopilot feature. Just open the map, select any spot in the dungeon you've already discovered and pour another drink as the party gets there on their own, across several floors if you wish. Terms and conditions may apply.Then there are the Marchens and Nightmares, the team's enemies. I love the way they look because I absolutely hate it. Honey, sugarcone, sweet pastries and waffles, giant maggots, malformed tissue, blisters and parasites just underneath the skin. Lopsided. Crooked. Very, very pleasant to the eye if you enjoy hurting yourself.Music is gorgeous, but enough about that because      You don't need to have played the first game to enjoy Mary2.In fact, a minor spoiler: the entire 70 hours plus long first game is available from the main menu when you finish Mary2. With a bonus, approximately 10 hours long chapter that links the two games together. For free. In times of paid swimsuit DLCs.What you need is the love for crawling miles upon miles of sprawling dungeons and turning pages upon pages of visual novels. If that's okay with you, dig in. Just bear in mind that this game is an absolute master of unhinged mood swings, from comedy to agony and back, overriding the good ending with a sudden and bitter downer just to set a tiny, fragile, sparkle of hope in waiting.There is something absolutely wondrous about this fragility. A marvelous spiral of ups and downs, hatred and forgiveness. Misunderstanding, overthinking, second guessing yourself and everyone around, jumping to conclusions, lying with the purest of intentions at heart becauseDo with this knowledge whatever you wish, and, as always,

_childDocuments_.review: Well, since the publisher got rid of the censorship (you have to patch it yourself but its pretty easy to do anyway) we can now enjoy the game as intended and thats really nice.The dungeon crawling has a lot of quality of life stuff, the auto-pilot alone is a great welcome, and the game has a lot of mechanics regarding both combat and exploring to always keep you in your toes, the exploration rewards curiosity, attentiveness and creative use of characters skills to unlock paths or get loot.The game also offers a lot of ways to make grinding interesting and more worth while, accompanied with a lot of reasons to keep going back to already explored dungeons.As far as combat is concerned, the whole thing of having unstable party members who can go nuts if you dont pay attention make it interesting and if you are unlucky the game gets to enjoy kicking you while you are down, but it isnt that hard anyway (this is no smt).Some complains i have:- How long winded the characters tend to be, if they can say it in 10 words, they will say it in a 100 and they will take at least 20 minutes  to get to the point.- The early game does take a while to get rolling and there is a serious lack of save points (this does get somewhat resolved when a certain party member who can make save points joins).- A lot of menu navigation when you are at base (this one is nitpicking tbh).Overall id say to give the game a go, its an interesting concept engaged with fun gameplay, the story its very anime so that can be a turn off to some people, and finally its uncensored now so its a better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've decided to change my stance on this game after some recent updates fixing some glaring issues like the crazy and audio. Although I will still keep my original review under as more or less a legacy thing. But, I still recommend reading KingKrouch's review. With that out of the way.Mary Skelter 2 is one of my favourites game Idea Factory has made. It fixes the issues of the first game and hands a what if scenario surprisingly well, on top of having 2 games in one and a remastered as well ending up being a better game overall. I will say there will be spoilers in the story department so fair warning.GameplayIts a rather simplistic Dungeon Crawler with 3 settings of difficulty for the more Casual Dream/Easy will be fine but if you want to have a true reality of the hellscape you're thrown into choose Fear/Hard it can be unfair with surprise encounters but if you mid man your units you should be fine for the most part. Every character has their own classes with only a few matching.Otsuu is her own Demon being able to be any class with enough time and effort.Little Mermaid and Thumbelina and Hamlen (MSN) are the Mage/Healing ClassSleeping Beauty and Kagua are the Archer ClassSnow White and Gretel are a unique class of support and mimic depending on how you use themAlice, Hamlen (MS2) and Cinderella are Fighter/Tank ClassRapunzel and Red Ridding Hood are an All-Arounder ClassWith 6 characters to choose from (5 in the first game) you will have fun mix and matching to make the most effective parties to survive.CharactersIf you've played the first game or really any Idea Factory game for that fact the cast is mostly what you'd expect except I wanted to talk mainly about the important 2 being Otsuu and Little Mermaid. They're easily the best written characters Idea Factory have made playing off each other hand to hand and although Otsuu might seem like a simp she is a simp that won. They're really good couple and enhances the game especially the outcome of it all.Story [Spoilers Ahead]The story is rather slow and build up faster and faster until it hits the climax and gives you 50 doses of depression.The bad ending is masked as a good and happy ending because the true ending we're hit with the sad truth that in the original and right world Little Mermaid needed to die and it all comes together with everyone except for Otsuu and Mermaid dying. With this tough choice Otsuu reveals her true nature being the original nightmare of the underground dungeon and tries to use witchcraft to reset the world again (something that the opening hints at). Only being stopped by Little Mermaid who tells Otsuu that everyone else was happy without her and with the wishes of the one she loved she resets the world to normal creating an infinite paradox which only Jack can save in the remaster.The saddest part of it all is the fact how Little Mermaid death impacted everything. I'll list the main things:-Since Little Mermaid body wasn't procured they couldn't learn from her body and had to abuse and experiment on the live ones scaring both Cinderella and Kaguya into being obedient.-Cinderella turning Blood Skelter prematurely and running away. Which not only keep her young and not let her become an adult but also due to mimicry killed Chiaki which split the Dawn and the the order of the sun. This also took Snow White, Sleeping Beauty and Thumbelina away with Thumbelina wanting her dead.-Alice becoming a Nightmare and killing all of Dawn (Also killing Snark in the process)-Jack Becoming a Nightmare as well-Otsuu being allowed to have a second life if not a hard one. This makes it sadder because not only will resetting everything wipe her memory but will go back to living alone in the Underground Cavern as a nightmare for decades only to be found and marked for death by the people she once called friends.OverallI love this game I have alot of passion in this franchise which is why I originally discarded the official release on steam due to how botched it was but now I can say for the most part I would recommend this game if not on a discount. I would love more people to understand why I love this franchise. [Outdated Review]I'll say this before anything, KingKrouch's review is the best one when it comes to talking about how shocking of a port this game sadly is. This isn't a review this is to inform you that the game as it currently stands is a buggy mess and a overall horrid port of one of my favourite Series of all time. If you have the money and the console please buy it on Switch it's completely uncensored and in its full glory. It comes with two games and runs pretty smoothly.I honestly don't understand why Idea Factory never ported them personally it feels like International would rather see the game crash and burn.

_childDocuments_.review: The translation is rough, there are a bunch of possible crashes, but if you manage to get past those issues, you end up with an interesting dungeon crawler. I was especially surprised by the story, which was pretty bold so far and has some good ideas writing-wise. I don't know a lot about dungeon crawlers, but this one has enough ideas when it comes to dungeon puzzles and hazards to keep me entertained for now. The RPG system is robust, you can play around with a good number of systems, be they gear and skills and their upgrades, classes, party formations or the partner system. The combat system is made interesting by threats not only coming from enemies, but your own party as well via the Massacre and Blood Skelter system. Personally, I also like the art design a lot, but that's more of a question of taste. Be wary that this is a Switch port, which means the art assets are made for a 720p resolution (the PC release could've really used a proper in-game upscale!). I recommend using the external program Magpie to upscale the game. Especially the character images will look blurry otherwise (see Graciaus' review for details). You might also want to create a file called Minigame.dat in your game directory to re-add a minigame that was censored from the original PC release (see iriyap's review for details). And as others have pointed out, this game contains Mary Skelter: Nightmares (the first game), which you unlock after finishing the game (or via the DLC menu, if I understood correctly). So buy this one if you wanna play both.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: UNCENSORED PATCH IS NOW AVAILABLE OFFICIALLY ON GHOSTLIGHT'S BLOG SITE. YOU CAN DOWNLOAD IT HERE: Original write-up below.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------(This is not a review, this write-up will primarily focus on the censorship + the PC port quality)Mary Skelter 2 is a promising Dungeon-Crawler. Think the POV and grid-movement mechanics of Wizardry or Legend of Grimrock mixed with turn-based JRPG battles. It's really fun. It's got a good soundtrack, some great voice acting (English or Japanese) and an interesting, dark premise for the story. Despite feeling familiar, there's a uniqueness to it. Mary Skelter 2 also includes a remaster of Mary Skelter: Nightmares - the first game in the series. The anime aesthetic might put some people off but it's a really fun, dark, mature game from the little I've played.  I think there's a great game here and I'm excited to play it more and the fact that we might not get a third game if this doesn't sell well is a crying shame. The PC port is fairly barebones but it has options where it counts. Its locked to 63fps but otherwise the game can go to 4k resolution, it has rebindable buttons for both your controller AND keyboard as well as alternate keys. It has full mouse support, and it runs great even at 4k on a RX 580. There are no graphics options so bare that in mind if you're running a potato. There's also no Anti-Aliasing option which is just baffling as the game is using some rather scratchy assets from the vita version that look a bit grainy.If you want to know about the censorship issue. There's more info in the video but essentially, there's a "purification" minigame where you need to remove pink liquid from girls by "rubbing them" until it disappears. You can consequently rub off their clothes as well (but only down to their underwear). It's been removed entirely from both games in this package (Mary Skelter 2 includes Mary Skelter Nightmares: Remastered), despite the fact that the minigame is on the 2018 pc version of Mary Skelter Nightmares WHICH IS ON STEAM RIGHT NOW. And this sequel/remake game combo was also released first on Nintendo's Switch which didn't have censorship either. So either the censored PS4 version of the game was ported and it was cheaper/easier to do that than the Switch version (for some reason), or Valve is going full puritan again.Personally, I don't see this as a deal breaker for myself and I think I'll enjoy the game for what it is. But I can see why people are frustrated. This is a game company whose fanbase knows exactly what they want and they know that company is going to deliver. But when that company (Ghostlight, Compile Hearts, Ideafactory int) can't or doesn't want to deliver on something PEOPLE GO TO THE COMPANY SPECIFICALLY FOR! I can see that being absolutely frustrating and a downright betrayal of trust, especially when its clear the artist's original vision is being trampled on.Thanks for reading. I have more critiques of games that will disappoint your parents here: (also some non-anime stuff too, lol)Update:The GoG version seems to be censored as well as indicated by the reviewers, meaning it's unlikely that Valve's policies had anything to do with the game being censored on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, I wanted to try to write a review on how I felt, but then I saw that KingKrouch wrote a review that basically said what I wanted to say. I was super excited for this game to come to PC, I was lucky enough to be a tester from Mary Skelter 1 and despite that port not being great (for PC options and that crash that occurs during the final dungeon) I didn't care because I really liked the game and its' premise. It hooked me and had me excited for Mary Skelter 2 to come to PC once that game was announced. I didn't know about GL's previous ports that had censored some entries but honestly, I didn't care that Mugen Souls or Mugen Souls Z was censored because Chou Chou looks too much like a Loli for me to want to see her in the bath. I feel the same way about MS2 getting the censorship treatment because I don't care much about rubbing the blood of the characters off their body. I was just excited to play MS 2 on my PC since I played the Switch version and I really liked it but I don't really play my switch a lot so I figured I would just double-dip and get it on PC instead where I tend to do 99% of my gaming. Though, after years of seeing the ports that IFI, Preapp, and Ghostlight put out, I really can't recommend this version.To start all 3 of those companies ports have 1 thing in common, barebones PC ports, missing a lot of options, and having some issues with fullscreen and Ultrawide Monitors to the point where some users have to tweak the INI files just to start up the game and disable the game launching in fullscreen and leaving the game with a black screen. So disregarding the censored release (Which as I mentioned earlier I don't really care that they did so) but the issues with the port and the lack of effort on display from Ghostlight make it so this game is not worth your money, the one thing I'm upset that was removed (But wasn't done by Ghostlight unless they did the Switch port too) was the fog that was present whenever you encountered a nightmare in the JP PS4 version, it really looked great and it was removed when it came over which upsets me because it could've been a great addition to the Nightmare Hunts and make them tenser.  Not to mention the audio mixing is really bad, some sound effects don't play, some sounds are extremely muted and during my playtime of 1 hour, I've had 3 random spikes in the volume where the music plays normally and then all of a second it's blaring in my ears and it's super aggravating. I love the series but with how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ IFI treats their games on PC you're better off waiting for a great sale for any of their games or playing them on another platform unless you want 60 FPS because both versions will have the same amount of graphical options (none) In conclusion, I really was excited for this and I'm sad to see this come in a buggy/half-hearted release. It makes it so I'm probably not going to wait for Finale on PC (which will probably happen in another 3 years) and just buy it on Switch or something because the experience will probably be the sameEDIT: Looks like most of the problems I had with the port have been fixed. Also looks as though the cleansing minigame works a lot better (according to my sources) now that the minigame is able to be patched back in.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter trilogy (after first game was remade and released with second as Nightmares version) is probably my favourite "blobber" dungeon crawler there is. Character builds are interesting, giving a lot of options and allowing for player expression. Special skills usable during exploration add a lot variety to typical dungeon design, especially when paired with special "nemesis-like" system of mega monster that will sometimes spawn and follow player making for mad dashes to safety. All this makes gameplay rather fresh and good.Characters and story, while nowhere near great, have charm to them and are still miles ahead of most dungeon crawler games of that type, which often don't even have defined characters.This release includes both second game and remake of first one, making for great value purchase – and third final game is also available on Steam now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it a lot! In the past I was worried about tech issues/a bad port mentioned in other reviews, but I've experienced no issues at all and the game has been absolutely wonderful to me.The gameplay is really solid in my experience, individual turns aren't ultra complicated but it has unique mechanics that add a solid amount of engagement to the battles overall.After about ~8 hours I can say the game is more narrative-focused than others in its genre but does it really well so far and makes you interested in figuring it out more. It's brimming with personality and stands out in a great way.It's anime-ish enough in that some aspects lean lightly sexual, but it's *usually* kept tame enough that it adds to the game's tone and aesthetic in a way that's interesting and adds to it moreso than detracts from it. There may be suggestive scenes but so far they don't seem to be significantly sexual. The main exception is an overly-sexualized minigame that was removed from this version - there's ways to re-enable it but I would honestly recommend pretending it doesn't exist. Treating it as a fanservice game honestly downplays a lot of what this has to offer.If you're interested in the genre and can tolerate some light anime weirdness, or if anything about this catches your eye in some way, this is an easy recommendation to make. Etrian Odyssey will probably always be the best entry point to the genre but this is a close second. Goes on sale for $20 or less and I can say it's easily worth at least that much.If you're hesitant, I say jump in and give it a shot - personally, chances are you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I'll say is that i really wish Steam gave us the opportunity to give a Mixed review,since in cases like this game there's some things to consider before outright giving it a full thumbs up or down. The game itself (Story,characters,atmosphere,music etc) were all great just like the first game, and here you get sequel and prequel bundled together so it's a good deal. The technical aspect and how the release was handled though.... that was pretty rough. The game came out with a purging minigame robbed of its manual way of completing it,and it took days of protest and fighting against this in the discussions. Luckily in the end this part was restored through an official patch made available some time down the line, but the fact alone that this was done is just appalling; this age of political correctness and hypocrisy surrounding games,anime,tv shows and whatever needs to completely die already. It's not about what is censored or altered,it's about the fact that it was done when no one in their right minds gets offended over something like this (no,rainbow haired mentally ill people never will and never should be a concern,since they're not part of the audience,they never buy these games or anime,and they rarely buy any game or anime at all,so STOP CARING about their useless whining). Imagine paying for a game and wanting to experience exactly what the authors/creators wanted to make, and then get treated with a "no you can't decide for yourself what you can/cannot see, we'll choose for you and force you"; this is pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and doesn't deserve any kind of support,be it moral or especially economic. If there's violence in the game and it's part of the story i want it to be there,if there are (really slightly in this case) erotic parts same thing, i want the game to be EXACTLY how the creators envisioned it,period. Now that i explained this I'll explain the other reason why this game was handled badly: it's a poor port from the Nintendo Switch version, which means lower resolution for 2d elements and lower graphical fidelity in general, and it also crashes pretty often and randomly, if you check the discussions it seems like they did patch the game for a while,but then abandoned it with people still crashing, and the reasons seem to be random and different between users, for example i crashed 8 times in this title (you can see that from the crash dumps the game creates in its main folder) and also froze at least a couple times and didn't create logs probably, the only thing that seemed to mitigate it for me was completely closing MSI Afterburner,no idea why or how effective was this really,but that's the only thing that seemed to work.Point is that this series is really good but deserves better from both original developers and teams handling the port, i want to see it treated better.Plus there is a third game, Mary Skelter Finale, (still not on steam,no idea when or if it will come) which seems to be self-censored at the development stage,so the average person won't even know they're supporting Sony's censorship policy when spending their money on it; unless they restore that to non-dumb standards it's a hard buy for me, I might rather watch how the story ends on youtube than support these choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter 2(MS2) is the prequel to Mary Skelter Nightmares(MSN). The latter is also included with the purchase, but has no achievements are tied to it. As someone who played Nightmares a while back, I feel like I spent way too much time to learn the truth of MS2. The reason for this is because it felt like I was going through MSN a second time until very late in the story. The overall story, the tweaks and the new mechanics implemented were not enough to deliver a fresh experience. For this reason, I was not able to enjoy the game as much as I enjoyed the original MSN when it was still fresh. As for the version of Mary Skelter Nightmares included, it seems that some tweaks have been made. I started a game real quick and looked at the inventory. The cap is set at 9999, which I believe was previously 99 in the original standalone game. I did not check anything else, as I did not want to waste my time on it as I previously beat the original version and I am kind of burnt out on MS now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time coming into the Mary Skelter series. Personally, I wish they would port the final game so I could see the end of this story. However, my time with this game wasn't without problem. Personally I've been experiencing constant crashing of the game which caused me to lose hours of progress, just like what a few of the review before me had stated.For MS2, it often occurs when I enter new dungeons/new nightmares.For MS:N, it was fine for the first half of the game but it started crashing at the later half.Sure, you can get around these issues by saving often, but when the game gives you an option to disarm the save feature, you'd figure the only risk you have by doing so is dying to mobs/bosses rather than the unpredictable risk of having your game crash on you.That said, it was still a enjoyable run for me up until the end. So, if you're the type to save often, perhaps you won't be turned off by the crashes it'll spring on you, since it did serve as a reminder for me to get off the game and start my work.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter 2 is honestly one of my new favourite games I've played in a long time. The start of the game is a little slow and it does take a bit to properly start getting to do stuff but once the game opens up and you have free reign to go to the different Jails and explore the game really hits it stride. The game play is one of those first person dungeon crawlers with multiple floors to a dungeon and you explore the place looking for items, treasure chests, and stairs that lead you up or down to each floor. In the Jails you'll also be met with these Invincible opponents named "Nightmares" which can vary in its looks in each area and eventually you'll  get to fight and defeat these foes which is always satisfying after running from them for the whole area. In the story you'll also meet these characters who will help you on your journey  and party members called "Blood Maidens" who will assist in battle. They each have their own unique personalities and are enjoyable to meet and interact with in their own rights and are what carry the game in my opinion. Mary Skelter 2 is honestly a game I could recommend to most if not all people as it's a great game to experience and it even comes with the remake of the first game.Completing the remake for Mary Skelter Nightmares was a slight chore as you basically start from level one and like the first game, it can seem a little slow but Nightmares does pick up steam a lot quicker than the second game and like the sequel, I enjoyed the Remake immensely. There are slight differences and mechanics which are not in the Remake from the sequel which makes it a bit difficult when jumping between the games but its similar enough where you'll have a much easier time getting started. Nightmares is a Plot driven story while MS2 is a Character driven story and both have their strengths and weaknesses with how they are approached. Nightmares though I enjoyed just a bit more and without going into spoilers had a great true ending

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the first Mary Skelter, and now this new version of the game, I'm surprised at the changes in the game's details and tone. Compared to the first Mary Skelter, this new version has, in my mind, a somewhat darker tone than the first. And the first one already had a dark tone in itself. The play mechanics are also a bit more complicated, but at the same time more innovative and interesting. The Blood Garden is a great addition, but i haven't decided yet if it's an unneccesary additional complexity or not. For now, it's an intruiging ans stimulating addition. The overall graphic uality is better than the first, One major complaint is the confusing nature of the Mini Map during actual gameplay in the Aq ... m site. I find it neccesary to keep switching between the game view and the map in detail view for better clarity and understanding. Whether this is a bug of the game itself, of due to the fact that my laptop's specs are only a bit better than the minimum required specs to run the game, i have no idea. One complexity that i like is the multi floor nature of the map areas, with a greater variety of traps to catch the unwary. It favors a slow methodical pace when exploring; something which i personally favor. So, so far, so good. I give the game overall high marks in spite oh my nit picks. I highly reccomend the game for those with the patience and tenacity to tackle it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter 2 :Good points:-Good characters design and personalities.-The story is dark and interresting and the ending is worth it.-Good gameplay, its simple to understand and building your characters isnt that hard to comprehend. The level design is ok for a dungeon crawler, you have some easy puzzles and you'll need to use some characters specific skills to build a path toprogress through dungeons.-Two games in one with a good price, you can expect close to 100 hours if you want to complete both of themBad points:-Become repetitive after the mid-game : close to no characters progression "RPG-wise", a lot of skills are bad imo and the story is slow paced.-Exploration rewards and quest rewards are terrible :  the equipment are always bad upgrades specially if you use the bloodfarm system. I suggest to completly skip the quests uneless you're doing the achievements, they're not worth your time and some of them are time consuming because of the RNG involves in them. Dont be like me and explore everything, its not worth it. Near the end of the game i looked for the dungeons maps online and just rush through the levels.-Some dungeons are confusing and too large.-Devolution is useless and not necessary, you dont need it to finish the game on normal and the xp gain are so low that its not worth it. The amount of grinding seems insane to make it worth.-Like every IFI games there is a ton of "slice of life" VN parts, its not for everyone, the problem i have with them is there are too much of them at the same time unless you bactrack during your dungeon exploration to put a "break" between them.-Low effort port : the resolution is low since they didnt upscale it from the switch version and unless you played it in "windows mode/low resolution + Reshade for example" it's very blurry. I have only one crash in 70hours so no problem for me.Overall score : 6/10Mary Skelter Nightmares "remake" :Good points:Overall the same points as the second game. Some comparaisons between the games :-Story was better paced than the second game imo, the "slice of life" dialogues are shorter too.-The maps layout was better and shorter too and less like a labyrinth.-The game have better balance job-wise overall (magic feels better on this game). I did a team with one of each archetype and finish it just fine. Devolution is a "must do" in the endgame dungeon compared to 2, it's fast to re-lvl-up.Bad points :-Only 5 people in a team instead of 6 and we dont have the new skills/class from the second game.-The game is way harder compared to 2 in Normal for the first 4 chapters, Nightmares hits like a truck. There is something wrong with the difficulty curve.-Lots of weapons types are quite bad. Every weapon with a malus on AGI is a hard pass in this game because AGI is one of the best stat in the game, it makes your turn come faster and you can finish most random battles in 1 turn thanks to this stat. -The "Order" sidequests aren't rewarding and are boring to do.-The port isnt that great, same reasons as the second game.Overall score : 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't able to play the 1st Mary Skelter because the port was horrible and the game just straight-up crashed in the 2nd dungeon. Turn out that was somewhat a blessing in disguise cause you will want to play Mary Skelter 2 before the 1st one (which is bundled in with this game)Haven't got the time to play the 1st one next but this one is definitely fun. Good story and characters, I like the whole blood mechanic. The dungeon design can be confusing at times but nothing too outrageous. There is also the censorship controversy on release, which was patched, I didn't touch the minigame the entire time though. Here hoping we can get the full trilogy on Steam (sales numbers don't look good unfortunately)Played and got all achievements in 40 hours in 5 days.

_childDocuments_.review: The Nightmare continues in Mary Skelter 2! In this first-person dungeon crawler, play as fairy tale-inspired characters called Blood Maidens, each with deeply customizable character-specific classes. Balance between power and madness in turn-based battles with a blood-fueled transformation system, and escape a living prison while indestructible Nightmares give chase in real time. This game also includes the first installment of the series, Mary Skelter: Nightmares.

name: Tchia
detailed_description: Special Edition The Tchia: Oléti Edition comes with the Tchia base game and the Kepler Customization Pack, which includes four costume sets for Tchia and four boat customization packs, inspired by fellow titles from the Kepler game catalogue. All costume sets include hair, make-up, outfit, and backpack. All boat packs include flag, sail, and base. About the Game Join Tchia on her tropical open-world adventure as she sets off to rescue her father from the cruel tyrant, Meavora, ruler of the archipelago. Climb, glide, swim, and sail your boat around beautiful islands as you explore a physics-driven sandbox. Face the fabric soldiers created by Meavora in open encounters where your creativity gives you the edge. Take control of any animal or object you can find, make new friends and jam on your fully playable Ukulele. A poetic coming-of-age story inspired by New Caledonia. SOUL JUMPING Tchia's special gift lets you take control of any animal or object you can find. With over 30 animals and hundreds of objects to choose from, fly around as a bird, explore the ocean as a fish or dig for treasures as a dog! Use your unique soul-jumping abilities to explore solve puzzles, and uncover secrets. EXPLORATION & TRAVERSAL Jump and glide your way across a vast archipelago and use the Tricks system to perform cool stunts and dives. The free climbing mechanic lets you ascend anything in the world without restriction including any physics-driven tree. Take to the ocean waves, and sail your customizable boat across turquoise lagoons and dive around coral reefs and shipwrecks. COMBAT & ENCOUNTERS Face the Maano: mysterious enemies spawned from pieces of wood and fabric. Keep moving, improvise, and use all of Tchia’s abilities to come out on top of those intense encounters. You can also put your skills to the test by tackling mystical challenges in the Totem Shrines. UKULELE Just jamming by yourself or playing alongside other inhabitants of the archipelago, your fully playable ukulele will be a trusty companion throughout the game. Use it at key story moments during rhythm sections, or play unlockable melodies at any point in the open world to trigger special events such as attracting animals, triggering rainfall… STORY & MUSIC Take Tchia on a heartfelt adventure and meet a diverse cast of characters inspired by New Caledonian cultures. Fully animated cutscenes voiced in traditional language will punctuate your journey while an original orchestral score infused with local sounds creates a unique and immersive world. CUSTOMIZATION & ITEMS Stylize Tchia’s clothing and boat with hundreds of unlockable cosmetic items ranging from a traditional look to the most over the top options. You will also unlock useful and fun tools along the way such as a flashlight, slingshot, compass, camera... NEW CALEDONIA The world of Tchia was inspired by New Caledonia, A tiny island in the Pacific Ocean, homeland of Awaceb's co-founders. Inspiration was taken from the rich and varied local landscapes, cultures, music, languages, folklores and traditions and was used to create a fictional world and to tell a universal story for all to understand and enjoy. The characters are voiced by local talent in traditional languages, and subtitled in many languages including English, French, Russian, Chinese, German, and more. Looking to spend more chill time in Tchia's archipelago ? Tchia's free update include 8 new soul melodies to have even more fun during your exploration, such as acrobat mode, human torch or the super boat ! You'll also be able to equip a variety of new outfits, and all cosmetic items will now give you additional perks in your journey, such as more stamina or special abilities. If you've ever wanted to lead a crab gang or attract sharks, suit up!

_childDocuments_.review: I really hoped Tchia would be fun, because it’s such a great game on paper, but some poor gameplay design decisions made this game extremely frustrating and dull to play from nearly the first hour onwards. I want to make very clear that there are a lot of things I really do appreciate about this game—Tchia is beautiful, from a graphical perspective, a musical perspective, and also from a cultural perspective. It’s great to see the success of a small indie team making a game about a place they love and sharing its unique culture with the world. More games like this absolutely should exist.Unfortunately, however, Tchia suffers from a bit of an identity crisis when it comes to the scope of the world, which leads to major gaps in traversal mechanics. Tchia’s map includes two relatively large islands, Ija Nöj and Madra Nöj, as well as a handful of other small archipelagos and shipwrecks. The game’s main storyline leads you on quests across these islands, and there are tons of different collectibles to be found on the islands and all over the ocean. All of this (in addition to the game’s own marketing) suggests that Tchia is a big open-world game. And yet, Tchia wants to be a small, easygoing, cozy game at the same time, so it purposely avoids traversal mechanics that are necessary to make an open-world game work. For example:For some reason, you can’t see your own position on the map. If you push the left stick (which I frequently did by accident, due to it being the sprint button in 99% of other games—with no option to rebind it in Tchia), your map will recenter to an unhelpfully large circle saying you are “somewhere near here,” which is frequently half the size of one of the major islands. You have a boat you can travel with, but it’s slow, clunky, and difficult to steer—I almost never used it. There are certain docks you can fast-travel to with the boat, but they are also largely unhelpful given that a) there are very few of them, b) they are not close to major areas/villages on the islands, and c) you have to be at one dock to fast-travel to another one, so the time to get there is often not even worth the benefit of fast-traveling.What I found to be the most effective means of locomotion was soul-jumping, which allows you to inhabit other objects or animals and move as them. Soul-jumping into birds is useful for traversing land, and dolphins for traversing the ocean. There is a limit to how long you can soul-jump for, but you can max this out early on, at which point it’s not a major concern. When you reach a certain point in the game, you unlock the ability to summon some of these animals, which you can then soul-jump into (assuming the summon actually works, which only happened about half of the time for me). This helps tremendously to explore the open world, but there are still issues with it. Any time you exit a soul-jump in order to interact with a collectible or view a cutscene, the animal will likely leave (birds and dolphins can get away quickly), and you will be stuck waiting on a cooldown before you can summon one again. Even after completing the main story, when the game grants you several “overpowered” abilities, there are still long cooldowns for these summons, making them very impractical for large-scale exploration of Tchia’s world. I do generally enjoy “collect-a-thons,” and I’ve 100%ed some much longer and larger than Tchia, but exploration in this game is downright tedious due to the fact that the only remotely efficient means of getting around disappears every time you exit it and you have to wait to summon it again.I should also mention that Tchia took 6 minutes to boot up every single time I launched it, and around once per hour I encountered a “UE4 fatal error” that crashed the game while I was in the middle of playing. I haven’t experienced anything anywhere close to this bad playing any other game, so I believe Tchia is rather poorly optimized.I wish I had more fun playing this game, because there are a lot of things it absolutely nails that I hope to see other games take note of, but sadly the gameplay and traversal in Tchia was painfully tedious for me the entire way through, so I can’t recommend playing it. Devs—you’re on the right track. There’s clearly a ton of love put into this game, which is great, and if you can figure out how to improve your gameplay systems, I have no doubt your future games will be fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: TCHIA, is quite simply, one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences in my almost 40 years of gaming. TCHIA begins as a very typical RPG, and ends up as a game of vast scope, with literally hundreds of items and locations to find, numerous races to be won, flying, swimming and sailing to be done (and even sailing long distances is simply beautiful, and never tedious), all while meeting special people. (My favorite game is the search for chests in secret locations! It just seems to go on for EVAH!) If you don’t want to tackle all the challenges…then don’t! (My bum left hand makes racing, high diving, and slingshot shooting in Tchia very difficult. So, I just never bothered after I discovered the difficulty, and it really didn’t matter much to the game at all! In fact, even though I finish few games, TCHIA is a game that I did finish, and wanted more!)There are numerous battles in Tchia, but few of them are more than just fun with little risk of harm. (And if you lose, you just wake up on your raft, or from a nap beside a relaxing campfire.) Not to say there aren’t dark places in the game, but also a “family friendly” mode to lighten things up a bit.The titular character (curious to see how Steam handles a completely appropriate word), has the special skill to transform into just about any creature she encounters, whether they live on land, or in air or water. Also, she has a ukulele with magical powers, so that’s pretty handy.Tchia is not perfect, with the unfortunate propensity for clipping to allow travel through walls (where it should not happen.) But the minor issues are counterbalanced by the total immersion in the beautiful world representing the island nation of New Caledonia. If you see it, you can most likely pick it up and carry or throw it. If it lives, it’s likely you can pet it. And if it’s a tree, hill, building or mountain…you can climb it!!! And the POV is exactly as encompassing as any player might wish.Tchia starts pretty easy, but with some platforming and racing that can be challenging. But considering the entire world is open as HUNDREDS of challenges, it’s always a simple matter to find something easier, or more difficult, than your current challenge if you should so wish.And BTW…NONE of the achievements are quick or easy! The most common challenge is currently only obtained by 20.2% of all players.If you want fun with just the right amount of challenge to keep you happy, Tchia may be as perfect a game for you as it was for me.I played much of TCHIA offline, so my hours are understated by more than half. Also, please be aware that "woke assaults" have skewed ratings data significantly, and TCHIA would otherwise have (and should have, in this player's opinion) a substantially higher rating.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: An indie project that puts principles over funPros:* Unique setting and an interesting way of looking at things.* Good music.* Sailing is fun.* Kitty/doggo petting! (careful to use the correct button tho, or you instead grab and huck 'em)* Treasure maps are fun.Cons:* Mini-map doesn't follow you, so you have to manually refresh it as you travel.* Game can't decide if it wants to fish or cut bait - it tries too hard to be & do everything.  See below section.* Freaking tons of collectibles.Meh:* Gear has stat bonuses.* Ubisoft-style "climb tall things to fill your map with stuff that's around you" mechanic.Fish or cut bait:* It doesn't give you a GPS dot on the map - unless you're on a boat.  It makes it tough to locate things on the map - unless you drop a pin on the map, then you can zero in on it with ease.* Combat is a rare, but when it happens it's a joke - enemies typically kill themselves by walking over fire, before they get to me.* Collectibles aren't required - except when they are.  Mostly they're for cosmetics, but some quests require them.* Mana is limited, and you have to eat to regain it - but early on you can unlock an ability to spawn food from thin air.* The graphics are simple - but it frequently made my (albeit ancient) GPU chug hard.* On the "guitar hero" minigames, you can either play the song, or turn on auto-play and then you can read the (amusing) lyrics.  You can't go back and play the song again, though, as far as I can tell.* You can't fast travel - except when you're at a dock.  Which are liberally scattered around the islands.TL;DR: Game may be fun, but after ~8 hrs I found myself dreading playing it more - so I'm out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was crafted with a lot of love, but by people who spend their time outside and not playing games. This was marketed as a BOTW clone, and the beginning of the game spent far too long trapped in cutscenes / music minigames. The 45 minute intro is somehow too long AND too short. I get that these campfire songs are of cultural relevance to the creator, and experiencing them in person is probably quite magical. They do not translate well to gameplay, nor to cutscenes. 4+ rounds of the same verse is entirely too long. The setup for the classic hero's journey trope is here, but I feel no connection to the characters and so separating from them to adventure off on my own feels... flat.  Every open world game that tries some new gimic for a map that isn't updated or revealed in real time always fails to deliver the... realism? Immersion? Whatever they were going for with the map system, it didn't land. The premise seems cool, but the writing and execution feel very lacking. I'm sure a lot of people will love this game. I did not.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing Tchia and I definitely recommend it. The graphics are beautiful and music plays a big role in this game. You get to play different instruments from time to time and the songs are mostly in Drehu which makes them even more unique and nice to listen to. If you want to fully enjoy the music and the visuals, you can turn on autoplay and Tchia will play her instruments automatically. The voice-overs are primarily in Drehu as well which is great for immersion. In general I learnt a lot about a culture and language that I didn't know before and you could see right from the start that the devs have put a lot of love into this game. I also enjoyed the story, it was touching and honestly not what I expected, but I was surprised in a positive way. Being able to explore the world as an animal (mostly birds, deer and dolphins in my case) or different objects such as oil lamps or coconuts is an amazing feature, I love this idea, but unfortunately it doesn't always work perfectly fine. I'll elaborate on this a bit later.Despite all the positive aspects, there are some issues that have also been mentioned by other people. First of all, the game always took more than five minutes to start. It's not a huge problem, but pretty annoying when you don't have a lot of time to play. Some people complained about the game being too brutal and I cannot fully agree. It's probably not the right game for an 8-year-old, but you can actually turn on "Family Mode" in the settings which should "reduce the intensity of some specific scenes", although I haven't tested it because imo there are some scenes in Ghibli movies or even Spongebob that are way more disturbing. You shouldn't give a game a negative review for something that you are able to turn off in your settings, it's not really fair. While soul-jumping is the most convenient way to travel and in the settings there is actually an option to be able to soul-jump without limits, it can also be quite annoying. Sometimes you have to jump out, for example to pick up objects, but by the time you're ready to soul-jump back into the animal that you used before, it will have run away. This kind of ruined the feature because the world is big but empty at the same time, so sometimes you have to run around for like five minutes to find a new animal for travelling. This brings me to another issue, the biggest one for me. It took me 8.5 hours to complete the story and there's no incentive to further explore the world (unless you really wanna go for that 100%) which is sad because the game has a lot of potential. Probably some more side quests would have done the trick. For these reasons, I strongly recommend getting the game in a sale. It's definitely worth playing but probably not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a truly outstanding game and I highly recommend it.Story: This game shines in its storytelling elements. It's deeply moving, both through very dark storytelling at some points and powerfully heartwarming in others. I was very moved playing this game. The game is also pro-LGTQIA+ both in story and in design elements, which is nice to see.Design: As a game that is largely exploration and item collection, the design elements of the game stood out with it being a love letter to New Caledonia. It gives the game such a unique look (to myself in North America anyway), and is filled with Indigneous culture and language (though also with colonizer elements as it is a French territory). The game is very rich visually and is so much fun to explore and move through. Additionally, it also has a wonderful soundtrack (though I did get sick of all the music mini games, even with auto play options, there were just too many and they were quite long for such repetitive songs).Game play: As noted, the game is mostly exploration and item collection. There is also a range of mini games that go into the "collection" aspect such as racing and combat. The game takes place on a series of islands and you are constantly moving between them. At times this can get a little tedious, but the visuals of the game mostly make it okay.The only downsides of this game for me are that there are some places where the game is a little too platformer heavy. I thought I was purchasing a nice, relaxing game, but there's certainly a few points where it most certainly is not. The game does allow you to skip over such areas, though, as I didn't use that feature, I can't speak to how much you skip over and lose. As someone who is generally not great at platformers games, I was able to complete all platformer parts of the game, even the more challenging ones that are not required to complete the game. Took a few (or several) tries for some, but none to the point where I got too frustrated with the game, so I wouldn't let that stop you from playing).Overall: a true gem of a game. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Friends,Today I will review the game TCHIA. Originally the game was a exclusive for EPIC GAME STORE. Now it is available on steam. Also, this game may look cutesy, but it is not really for very young children. There are death, enslavement, demons, and other dark aspects of people in the game. Although the game looks and starts out very child friendly, the deep messages in the game are somewhat dark. Avoid this game if very young child.This game takes place on a actual island based on a real life location near Australia called New Caledonia. Although the game is fictional and probably based on some kind of legend from there, the people and the locations in the islands all use fake names and fake people names. The storyline is ok, and is a interesting legend about the island. Also the music is awesome and great. There are many collectibles in the game you can also find. The ability to soul jump into animals is pretty neat too. One really good point is you can pet any animal in the game, which is awesome. Anyways, here is my Pros and Cons list:PROS:- The world is quite beautiful in this game.- The game can be considered relaxing while not doing the main quest.- Lots of places to explore on several different islands.- A young lady with special powers to fight evil.- A storyline that could be considered possibly myth from the country.- Ability to soul jump into any animal and control them.- Abilty to pet almost every animal in the game, including dugongs and many other animals.- Players can find clothing that lets the player upgrade different skills depending on what they wear.- Minigames and awesome music scores.- Easy to get all achievements. Although players must complete the whole game to get them all.- Supports controllers. I used a ZEN PRO switch controller. - Works on Windows 11 OS.CONS:- Some people may take offense about what they would define as "WOKE" stuff in the game. This personally did not bother me, but these range from one same sex kissing scene to some flags that show gay pride colours and other sexual orientation flags. If this bothers you, please avoid this game.- Some bugs are in the game. One such bug is that i found it rains underwater and inside buildings.- The diving minigame is quite difficult. If you do combos, which is basically doing one move to back to back moves, it makes it easier. Out of all the mini games, the diving one is the most difficult.- This game is not for children. It is more appropriate for ages 12 and up. There are also things about death, slavery, violence, and other dark things.- Some people complained of stuttering in the game. I have not personally run into this issue. I did have slowdown only on one part.- No steam cloud saves and no Steam cards. They may add these in the future, but at the current time of the writing of this review, they have not been implemented.Recommended game. The fact this was a epic game store exclusive game, and the woke stuff in the game make many people turn off this game. If you are interested, i suggest buying on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 25 hours 3/10 1 Yes,  No No, there is a chapter selection for the 2 that can be missed while playing through and finishing the game. No No No No No Unsure, I just noticed the "never-failing" and "infinite soul bar" in the options when writing this, but I hadn't seen them before. I don't think they influence the achievements.  NoWhat a lovely game is Tchia. I expected a chill adventure game that just looks awesome... but Tchia was so much more than that! What a beautiful game! what a heartwarming but emotional story! What a lovely gameplay! And what is there a lot to do! I'm blown away and totally in love with Tchia. The story starts with you and your father living on a desolate island. A family friend comes over to visit. However.. somebody followed that friend and that is when things escalate very quickly (and this will not be the only time things escalate). Your father gets kidnapped and you'll start your journey to rescue him. On your journey you'll meet wonderful people, who will help you on your quest. I love that this game is based on the culture of an island in the real world. It is a fantasy story but it also isn't in a lot of ways. Including the spoken language used in-game (it is subtitled to be able to understand it). You can feel how much love and passion went into this project ad that shrines through the whole game. The music added through Tchia is also wonderful. I'm so glad the songs where you play along have the opinion of auto-play, as I just wanted to vibe on the music and read the translation without the worry of hitting the buttons. Next to playing through the story, there are a lot of things to do in this beautiful world. There are tons of collectibles, gladly all highlighted on the map. There are 3 kinds of mini-games (Racing, Making loops while diving, and a shooting range), there is a treasure hunt questline to solve 21 puzzles and there are a lot of nature and animals to discover. This all is tracked in the menu so you know what you're missing. What really makes Tchia a gem of a game is that you have the ability to jump into the body of animals for a short while. This allows you to fly, dig, or run very fast. Things like that. You'll also have a ukulele to play songs to change the time of day, summon animals, and make your raft faster. Think Ocarina of Time style music melodies to unlock something for a short amount of time. This all allows for a relaxing gameplay loop where there are so many different things to do. I encountered a few bugs and crashes. The developer is working on them. Gladly the game saves very regularly, so even with around 8 crashes through my total game time of 27 hours, I didn't lose any progress. None of the achievements in Tchia are missable. There are 2 achievements you can miss out on when playing through the story, but gladly there is chapter selection, so you can go back to a specific part and still unlock it. Most of the achievements are just for completing all the different objectives and mini-games. For those mini-games, you have to unlock the gold trophy to let them count. I found the shooting challenges the most difficult while playing with a gamepad, but since I'm playing on PC I could switch to playing those with my mouse to make them so much easier. I give Tchia 4,5 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Really delightful.  Beautiful and just plain fun, with moments of poignancy and humor, this is a really special game.  I've tried to write a review for Tchia several times, but always end up going on for too long- I scrapped my last attempt after it had reached 870 words.  So, I'll just transcribe the text I wrote my brother when I was trying to get him and his friends to play the game:Lovely heartfelt indie cozy action adventure game, made by people from the Pacific island of New Caledonia, it's as much of a "Hey check out our culture, our food, our music, our traditions" as it is "defeat the evil baby-eating god of the sea coming-of-age adventure."  It's as good an argument for the "games are a form of cultural expression" statement as I've ever seen, made entirely in the native Drehu as well as French, with lots of musical breaks (with little Ukelele Hero mini games, natch.  There is of course also lots of good fun running and jumping and sailing from isle to isle exploring, and some pretty light, low stakes combat against evil spirits. _childDocuments_.review: Beat it in about 20h doing a lot of sidequests but not all of them. Overall the game is solid and very impressive for the cost. The challenge areas are unique.  There are games with stuff that's similar, but there isn't a single game that does everything this game does. One thing I liked a lot about this game is, I'd have random thoughts of something that could be better about it. 15 to 20 minutes later that upgrade would appear. There was only 1 that I had to wait until after the game was beat. But it's worth it. Unlike some triple A titles, this game doesn't force you to learn how to do certain things. Figuring out how to launch and get back into things is nice. Once you figure out the certain things to keep in your backpack the game gets even better. I didn't start keeping a soccer ball until late in the game. But a bird and a crab are musts. Certain cut scenes really irritated me. There's 2 cut scenes where you're falling. The entire game falling isn't an issue. Yet those cut scenes pretend like the Glider doesn't exist. You use it every 10 seconds!The character and boat customization is a nice touch. Mixing and matching to get the power ups you want to focus on in the beginning helps. By the end You can wear what you want and not notice any set backs. The combinations of items to Attract certain animals is a bonus. The food system is just where it needs to be. Almost none existent. Being able to spawn food is nice. Especially when you dont HAVE to eat.One setting I'd have liked to see is to have more animals and NPCs if your gpu/cpu can handle it. Sometimes swimming in the water and there's NOTHING in it was weird. I would have loved it if dolphins would have swam behind the boat if you crossed their path going full speed. Overall, I dont have any real complaints about the game. The Treasure Maps get more and more vague but as you go around the map more and more it works out. Good game. If youre thinking about buying it, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest testament to this game is that the fake review bombers (apparently afraid of a flag?) seem to have all played 10-15 hrs in the first 2 days, despite their disapproval.Tchia is a visually stunning, relaxing, coming of age adventure of a young girl who's father is taken away from her. Throughout the game she discovers her unique powers which allow her to change the environment and even briefly turn into the creatures around her, helping to solve puzzles or reach hard to get to places. The game is light on combat and more about casually exploring and furthering the story at your own pace, sailing around the island or hunting for collectables. It's a labour of love from the developers, and their portrayal of New Caledonia along with the stellar soundtrack was a breath of fresh air.The tutorial does go on for a little while, but there's a fair bit of story told (Not necessarily with words) and 4-5 game play mechanics introduced, once complete you're let completely loose on the environment and can explore as you choose.This game is definitely one for when you need to decompress after a long/stressful day.
_childDocuments_.name: Tchia

_childDocuments_.review: the core divide i see in responses to this game is between those who mainly view video games as museums for art and stories, and those who see video games as vehicles for progression, usually via combat. tchia mechanically draws heavily from a huge list of inspirations, mostly many 3d zelda game and mario games, to build a world directly related to a real place, its peoples, and its history. but theres little focus on progression mechanics, combat development, or advancing tchia's stats or power.tchia uses VERY common, clearly inspired mechanics for lots of unique locations, characters, interactables, animals, puzzles, treasure maps, races, diving spots, carving challenges, music activities, combat, and parkour tests. this game is remarkably far from empty. its telling that only one negative review makes this claim. these parts of the game are built well, but can feel empty if you don't care about them. i think this is because if you're used to those mechanics, you never feel much friction in 'learning' the game.tchia is easy to learn. some people may find this boring.for the rest of us, tchia is a beautiful and relaxing escape. the music especially is divine.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:  The rain issue mentioned below has been patched.  Prior to the patch, it also appeared to only affect my PC with an Nvidia GPU (3070), the AMD one (7900GRE) did not have any performance or frame rate degredation when it rained.  This makes me think it was a VRAM issue, or some strange driver related difference between Nvidia and AMD.This is a solid exploration/adventure game with some really interesting mechanics.Graphically, there's a bit of cartoon-iness with the look of the characters that contrasts a bit with the slightly more realistic environment.  It handles light and reflection well as well.  The only problem I had with the graphics was that when it rained, the whole game turned into a stuttery mess with highly inconsistent frametimes and framerates.  I never could figure out what setting controlled that, and none of my Linux/Vulkan workarounds could get it to be stable.  Eventually I just learned a soul melody to turn off rain and used that whenever it started.  I'm not sure if it was specifically a Linux and vkd3d (DX12->Vulkan conversion layer) issue, or if it affects Windows users as well.Movement feels pretty good, Tchia moves fairly slow but there are a lot of ways to obtain momentum and fling yourself along.  Your main power is to possess animals and objects and to obtain their abilities.  Possessing a bird lets you fly and travel quicker, most fish let you dash underwater and not have to worry about breath for stamina, and deer have fast overland movement.  You can also obtain momentum by using trees to propel you, and one soul melody lets you jump higher and longer.Like most adventure games that are inspired by Zelda, there are minigames, but most of them can be avoided if you don't want to deal with them.  There are required musical numbers, but the game gives you the option to autoplay the rhythm game portion and just listen.Combat is frustrating until you gain an ability later on, you need to possess flammable or explosive objects and fling them at foes.  You can carry some of these with you if there aren't enough around.  Some large combat camps can be a bit frustrating to clear, one in particular has over 30 individual soldiers you have to find and take out, it can sometimes take a while to find that one last one hiding.  Later on you .Most loot are two forms of currencies, or clothing/cosmetics for Tchia or her boat.  Once you complete the story, there's not a lot of incentive to finish exploring the map.  You do get a huge amount of customization options though, so if you like changing your look there's a payoff.The story is heavily themed on New Caledonian culture, has some LGBT elements, and involves child death and a pretty vile pair of villains .  Viewer discretion is advised if you are uncomfortable with any of those topics.Overall, good exploration game with fun powers and abilities, but without a lot of incentive besides cosmetics to complete the world.
