_childDocuments_.review: it's perfectly alright. I guess I didn't expect a game centred around animism to feel so inorganic in its execution.You can possess anything! You can fling yourself as a rock, dive to the ocean floor as a dolphin, or fly through the skies as a gull, but the main gameplay loop is tied to finding viewpoints that then mark a bunch of icons on your map for you to go to. By the time I got pulled into the loop, I wasn't paying attention to the world, anymore, I was just ticking checkboxes, and that's a shame because the world is gorgeous, and the traversal mechanics are fluid. There're some iffy design decisions, like animals immediately fleeing when you unpossess them, but I got around this by filling my inventory with birds! I think this game could've been a masterpiece if it'd leaned harder into Breath of the Wild, and other open-world games with organic designs like Fallout: New Vegas and Ghost of Tsushima. Instead of peppering your map with icons, the viewpoint could've simply given you a view of intriguing destinations that you'd mark yourself. This would've kept me invested, because the journey would've been of my own making. It's still a lovely gem, but it also makes me want to just play Breath of the Wild again.

_childDocuments_.review: Tchia is just a beautiful game. It's all about exploration and immersion in the culture of New Caledonia, and it is done with such evident passion and care. The world is a collection of islands that you sail between on a raft boat. The sailing is far from tedious and in fact, is relaxing as beautiful music plays while you're in the open ocean. The music is absolutely one of the biggest highlights of the game. It is tranquil, lively, and filled with the stylings of music from the culture. You even get a ukulele with which you can play at any time and there are musical segments where you play along (but can be skipped if that's not your thing). The end credits even include pictures of the staff on the actual island learning about the culture, and I absolutely loved that.The gameplay is all about exploring these islands, finding collectables, completing an optional treasure hunt, and completing trials to power up your soul gauge. The soul gauge is basically a timer that determines how long you can possess animals and objects. As you complete the tiki trials, that timer increases. Much of the exploration is done by taking control of animals of the islands, sea animals, and objects. It is a brilliant mechanic that is fun and inventive. I do think it could have been expanded upon further with puzzles or combat. Combat is very one note where you possess explosives to blow up the enemies. It's fun for a bit but with that being the only way to deal with them, it can get old. Now, enemies only reside in camps so many combat encounters are optional, but it would have been neat to be able to use animals in some way in those encounters. With this being a smaller indie game though, I understand that expanding all of those things would have been difficult. Maybe for a sequel or other future title though! If you are only progressing through the story, it takes about 7 hours to finish.I cannot recommend this game enough, and it is a stunning gem due to its immersion in its beautiful culture and environment. The developers should be very proud of what they have created, and it is absolutely worth your time and money!

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't so impressed by this game, but once I got into it and discovered the special abilities and their possibility for emergent gameplay, the exploration quests, the temples, and the later storyline, I was convinced. Travel is fun, too, since the game only allows fast travel between 8 or so locations, you get to do a lot of flying (as a bird) or swimming (as a dolphin). Strangely this game managed to make me feel immersed in its open world where Tears of the Kingdom failed for the most part, so given its much smaller size and budget, that's about the highest praise I can give the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully charming open-world adventure. Take a refreshing swim in the sights and sounds of a fictionalized New Caledonia. Delight in its language and music, learn about its folklore and diversity, and enjoy relatively easy, slow-moving gameplay. The game is clearly influenced by  in mood, look, and play-style.  doesn't quite rise to the heights of Nintendo, but it has a lot to offer.There is a main quest and you can play it and only it. Actually, that might the best path for most players, because once you open yourself to finding all the collectibles and completing all the optional challenges then you're in for a repetitive slog. The world is lovely, but there's just not a lot of kinds of things to do in it. Alas, 's open world scheme is Ubisoft-like: find a vantage spot, highlight all the points of interest on the map, and then go clean 'em up. You can also do this after finishing the game.That sounds boring, and indeed it might be for you. There's just too much of this filler content in . That said, the world is vibrant enough to keep the game loop enjoyable even when doing the same things over and over again. As the game progresses you get access to more traversal methods, and some of them are truly delightful. But even slowly sailing your raft from island to island has a certain beauty to it. The lapping of waves, the cries of seagulls, a small village in the distance. You can almost feel the warmth of the sun and smell the Pacific sea salt.While most of the game is about slow traversal, there are some more things to do. Specifically, your powers provide opportunities for emergent gameplay. There's not a lot of combat, but it can be made interesting if you approach it creatively. There are also several mini-games and challenge areas, which work as a change of pace. They are mostly easy, but some can be frustrating if you're going for 100% achievements. could have used more polish before release. Controls are wonky during climbing, and you might get trapped in the scenery and have to reload a save. For me, these were relatively small annoyances that did not keep me from enjoying the game as a whole.Affection for New Caledonia is present in every nook and cranny of this passion project. If that sounds compelling to you, and you're not entirely put off by some repetitive grind, then  is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tchia

_childDocuments_.review: The setting and the culture was worth experiencing, and the game looks generally very lovely (shout-out to the water), so I would generally recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: If I had to use only one word to describe this game it would be "charming", but that feels like almost too reductive of a word, too small for what this game is doing. I'm not even done, not sure I'm even halfway done, but I love it. Theres a whole lot of genuine humanity to every interaction, and all the mechanics are enjoyable. Getting good at launching a rock and then riding it across the whole island is supremely satisfying, and somehow the music portions don't feel like a rhythm game, they feel like I'm just actually playing music along with everyone else. I've never had a game replicate the feeling of a jam session before.Ive had a couple graphical bugs, one time a button wasn't accessible except during transition animation, but restarting fixed thatMy biggest criticism is that I wish there was a way to scroll back through conversation history, and to replay the music sections. I really like the game committing to being in it's own languages, but I can't read the subtitles AND play the music at the same time, and I'd like to know what that parrot song was about, and sometimes I get distracted and don't remember I need to be reading subtitles during conversations.Overall, superb game in both how fun it is to play and how much heart clearly went into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely Loved this game, it has a lot of really fun and unique elements that really make it special. I'll make a list of some of the aspects that I enjoyed most:1) There are lots of varied cosmetic options you can find, I love when a game let's me play dress up.2) The Movement is unique and fun. You're a bit slow just running around on foot, but between possessing animals, sliding down slopes, catapulting possessed objects and recapturing them mid flight, and gliding, there are lots of ways to get where you're going faster and keep Traveling fun.3) The Story is compelling and unique, I don't know if it's fully made up just for the game, or based in the folklore of the island that inspired the game, but either way, props to the writers.4) There is a great sense of humor in this game, but it also isn't afraid to get sad or a bit dark at times, where appropriate. A lot of games lean too much into being cute and silly, but I always feel like that makes the story feel less significant, and that is Not something that this game struggles with. Every beat was a hit for me here.Now, all that said, it isn't Perfect. There are a few things that, to me at least, would really bring this game to the next level. So, my biggest complaints are as follows:1) The game lacks any sort of side quests. There are a few mini games, specifically several timed challenges, a few target practice games, and diving boards, but the Main story is the Only story. A few more interactions with other characters and completing jobs that Aren't directly related to the main quest would really help flesh out the world.2) The combat system is fairly simple, consisting of "Find something that burns/explodes and chuck it at an enemy", and the hardest part of combat is often just tracking down where the last enemy is hiding (Mostly just an issue in one of the three big factories). I love that there IS some form of combat, and I don't know exactly what could be added to improve it, but it does feel like it's missing Something to me.3) Although the music system is pretty deep, the Rhythm Game that pops up fairly frequently in the story is Only available during the story, and as far as I know, there is no way to Replay a sequence in game other than just starting a new one and playing up to that point. Not a Huge issue, but there is an Achievement linked to getting 100% in one of these sections, so if you don't get it Before beating the game, you'll have to start a new game to get it.If the game was just a touch longer/bigger and had more minigames and some side adventures to do, it would absolutely be my new favorite game, but as it is, it's still a great game with fun gameplay, cute graphics, compelling story, and banger music, Well worth the price.

I pretty much only did the main missions so after a few missions i were behind in level compared to what the main mission recommended me to be in. I would recommend to probably wait a little before buying the game, for them to fix the low frames and the crashes.If i had played with better frames i am sure i would have enjoyed the game way more, and if the missions didn't have a level system.

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I'm a comic book fan & would've bought  this game if it wasn't Arkham adjacent.  For me that it was co-op and story driven was enough of a lure.  Sadly, nobody really plays.Pros-- The story campaign is fantastic.  It allows you to switch between characters as you play and follow their stories without issue.  I've played the campaign twice already.-- Customization of costumes: Could it be more? Sure, but I appreciate what we have.-- Heroic Assault Mode: Definitely endgame content that is hard and while repetative it is dynamic and allows for 4 players.-- Collectables - all the little side moments and collectibles flesh out the story and Gotham itself nicely.-- Photo Mode:  Undeniably cool.  -- LGBT Inclusive.  Cons-- Co op isn't as easy to engage as you'd imagine.  Dropping in and out of games esp. random games doesn't work well.-- Gear system: Nonsense.  -- Skills locked behind challenges.  -- Not enough enemies.  Beef up the city.-- Hard mode is cake once you level to a certain point-- $20 for 4 Jim Lee Iconic costumes is rough.  -- Batcycle.  Why?  There is no instance where gliding isn't faster than using your bike so why use it at all?**  My concern - what now?  Beyond the Heroic Assault modes have you heard about any Year 2 DLC?  New playable characters? New chapters? Villains?  Exactly.  The potential is there but how can they expect players who have abandoned the game without something and someone NEW to bring them back.  Lastly, $60 for this game is a crime.  I would drop it to $29.99 permanently to pull new players in while announcing new DLC content for returning players.  The MOD community still keeps this game alive for me. Gameplay 8/10Story 9/10Graphics & Art 9/10Performance 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you expect something from the Arkham Games, don't buy. This has nothing to do with those games story wise, and is an alternate adaption of Batman. It does take some inspiration from the Arkham Games in some of its mechanics, but with a twist to reach its own style. I feel like a lot of the mechanics in this game are misunderstood, like the hero-specific traversal. You may think it's the best traversal method, but I actually find it more useful for when I'm in combat, and I feel like this is the true idea behind it. Then I use the bike for long distance and grapple for medium distance to get around in the open-world. Overall, I'm having a blast with combat as well. Should you be concerned about combat, I suggest reading up on the "timed strikes" mechanic, this is inspired by the Arkham Games and both increases speed, damage and the resource gain used for special abilities. Nail this mechanic, and you can do some cool ass ♥♥♥♥. No easy-parry mechanic like Arkham, instead you have a 2x combo for a counter-attack = perfect-dodge + perfect-attack. The progression system is cool, I'm having a hard time choosing between the four heroes, but favorites are Nightwing and Red-Hood. The skill-trees makes you think of what abilites to chose, since you can't get enough AP for all three trees, which I think is great. Lot's of things to do in Gotham as well, I personally feel like the city is alive filled with crimes and mysteries. Needs optimization like a lot of people are mentioning though, not unplayable I think, still I would recommend staying away from ray-tracing unless you want to play the console-version of the game. :) My settings are set to max at 1440p with DLSS at balanced and no RT, average FPS 80-100. I do experience drops down to 50, during traversal with the bike so it is clear to see some update(s) are needed here because this is not okay. But still, I'm enjoying the game a lot. _childDocuments_.review: Got this game on sale thinking I would still at least enjoy it enough if I bought it so long after release (now a year ago that it came out) so that the issues could be fixed and that I could enjoy it at a discounted priceBut alas even at a discounted price the game is just not fun, the frustrations just add up the longer you play the game and even today there are a lot of bugsNot to mention I cringe everytime they call Ra's al Ghul as instead Race All Ghoul like wtf people how can you make a game so lazily you didn't bother to check the correct pronunciation before doing the voice recordings. It is from Arabic as demon's head and the correct pronunciation is heard in the Nolan films as "Raz Al Ghul" you can also hear this same pronunciation in Arabic and the same one in interviews with Neal AdamsCrappy pronunciations aside the game just isn't fun. The combat, movement and even vehicle movement is stiff, slow and boring. Melee combat lacks impact and doesn't flow well, the timing of perfect strikes, perfect dodges just feels off and the special attacks are perhaps the lamest I've seen in any game. It doesn't help either that counters are linked to dodging which just feels strangeThe game just plays like a poor man's Arkham gameNow the only positive is, yes there is co-op but there is no one playing anymore and I have no friends that have this game so couldn't test it and I honestly wouldn't recommend this game to any friends either so yeah. Presuming the co-op works then perhaps this game is more fun on co-op but if that is the case then why did the devs not add AI so that you can at least have an AI ally helping you so it feels like a form of co-op even when playing soloBeyond gameplay issues, the game while having 4 characters to play as just doesn't offer as much variety as you'd hope especially since in the end you just try the 4 different ones and end up sticking to your favourite one for your playstyle or based on their personalityIt is nice it has a transmog system but yet manages to mess that up. On normal outfits you can pick from different masks, boots and colour sets but then if you transmog to another outfit design you are locked in on the preset design you can't change the colours or individual parts of the outfit even though those are in the game and the UI already exists to let you do that they've simply intentionally disabled that feature for unknown reasons. Apparently their logic is less features for the players to have is a good thingThe game has skill trees one for each of the 4 Gotham Knights but here again you will only find disappointment. While there are useful skills sown about the skill trees the bulk of the trees are just stat upgrades which seems a bit pointless when you already have gear that achieves stat upgrades as well, most games with have a lot of upgrades to pick from so that you really are spoiled for choice in what skill tree you go for first. Here you just target the ones that give you an actual new skill/ability be it passive or active and then after that you just focus on the stat upgrades. Each skill tree only has a few active and passive unlocks all the rest are stat upgradesThe gear system is nice and I like the crafting system, mod system and such. Not a fan of the pointless power rating though. Basically the stats are what you need to look at the power rating is an arbitrary number that doesn't actually mean anything and often in this game gear with a lower power rating are better than one with a higher power rating but much lower stats but if that was the only issue this game had it would be of minimal impact the problem is just there are so many issues on issues on design flaws on top of other design flaws that you just think at a certain point ugh and press alt-f4.....Talking about design flaws, there is a training room you can enter to learn how to use all the skills and stuff in the game and you kind of have to do them as the first time on each character they unlock bonus XP. The training room is nice but what really gets on your nerves is every time you enter it for the first time when you come back to the Belfry again after a night of fighting crime. Batman gives the same speech EVERY FREAKING TIME!!!!!! and this is unskippable!!!!!! Really gets on your nerves lol!So yeah after playing it for 4 hours I was just like no, enough of this, I am not having fun I am really having to force myself to keep play this why bother? And I am a massive massive fan of the Arkham games. Arkham Asylum I've played 3 times, Arkham City I've played out twice. Arkham Origins I've finished once and Arkham Knight I've not played yet due to the launch performance issues but I do intend to play that tooBut Gotham Knights just is a bad game in almost all aspects

_childDocuments_.review: The game has been out for 4 days and I have near 40 hours on it at the time of this review. I have beaten the main story and i have indulged in the side quest, but have yet to 100% the game. As a die hard batman fan i was intrigued when the game was announced and counted the days until release. My opinion on the game may differ from the 'norm'- but this is just my take. - The elephant in the room is how does the game preform, and my answer is just meh. I have a 3080ti and a ryzen 9 5900x - and I was still going below 60fps when riding the bat-cycle, grappling long distances, or using the heroic traversals. With time this will obviously be a resolved issue so I wont hold it against the game, but it can be annoying. - The open world is great, Gotham looks good and its super fun to free roam around using any transportation available to you at the time. Unlocking the heroic traversals can be a little tedious but from the 3 that i have used they all been awesome. Red Hoods mystic jump I'm still not a fan of, simply for the fact i don't think it fits his character, but using it in game is very helpful for moving quickly. Batgirl's cape glide feels nice as it feels much like Batman from the Arkham series. And Nightwing's glider is actually very fun to use - even if it looks like hes in Fortnite the whole time.- The combat feels very nice and its a good change I personally think. The game isn't much on stealth for certain but its there still. Generally, I'd compare the combat to Spider-Man because of the fluid combat and the dodge mechanic, but also compare it to Elden Ring in the sense that you need to learn each enemies attack patters so you and dodge effectively - dodge to early and the enemies readjust to hit/shoot you - dodge to late and you don't move in time. The combat is good but needs a little fine tuning. There are times were I would be caught in an animation preventing me from dodging, and then I would take damage. Not a deal breaker but I would like to this this changed.- The game can be a little bit difficult at times, I started on 'Hard' mode but near the end of the story I had to bring it back down. The damage done to you was fine and manageable, but the bosses and some of the bigger enemies are just damage sponges. You couldn't deal enough damage at times for how much you were taking, and moving it down to 'medium' difficulty fixed this issue. - The characters are portrayed very nicely, from how they sound to how they act/talk - each character feels right. Especially Nightwing, I think his actor did the best both with the motions and the talking, but each character manages to shine at different parts of the story. No complaints here- The story .... feels like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spit in the face to all Batman fans. I don't know what WB was thinking allowing it to happen. It was captivating and half decent all the way up until the end cut-scene. This one moment damn near ruins the whole game for me. Without going into spoilers, yes Batman is dead. opening cut-scene he dies and they find the body, but this is not my issue with the game. My issue is only with the end, and its possible with a DLC they can potentially fix this but I've no hope for that.- Do I recommend this game? If you are a comic book nerd like myself and you love the 4 playable characters, and everything I listed (other than the story point) sounds appealing then sure. It's very fun to go on patrol each night and rid the city of crime either solo or with a friend. However, you will not find an amazing story experience in Gotham Knights. the ending really is that bad. The story deserves a 2/10 at best. The other aspects of the game deserves a 9/10. Over all, I'd give the game a solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Over 40 hours played. Still not done. Collected every collectable before even trying to tackle the main game. I play on Hard for a challenge as can be a little easy at times. _childDocuments_.review: Gotham Knights on PC left me thoroughly disappointed and frustrated with its execution. From the moment I started playing, it was clear that the developers had dropped the ball on multiple fronts. The dialogue, for instance, was cringe-worthy at best, with characters spouting lines that felt forced and inauthentic. It's as if the writers were more focused on trying to be witty and edgy rather than creating engaging and believable interactions.To make matters worse, the game attempted to incorporate what I can only describe as "dumb woke themes." It felt like a blatant attempt to pander to a specific audience, rather than focusing on delivering a compelling narrative. The themes came across as forced and out of place, detracting from the overall experience and leaving a sour taste in my mouth.But the issues didn't end there. The PC version of the game suffered from a plethora of technical problems, from performance hiccups to game-breaking bugs. It's clear that the game was released without proper optimization, making it nearly unplayable at times. The frustration of dealing with these technical issues overshadowed any potential enjoyment I could have had.All in all, Gotham Knights on PC is a prime example of a game that had potential but ultimately fell flat due to its lackluster dialogue, questionable themes, and numerous technical shortcomings. It's a shame to see a beloved franchise treated in such a careless manner, and I can't recommend this game to anyone looking for a satisfying gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Game is decent but it doesn't compare to the Arkham series.The story is interesting, with a decent mix of familiar characters and legacy villains. The user experience is designed well for the hero-leveling system, gear selection, crafting, modding, and ability trees. Graphics, all-around, were excellent, as were the highly customizable suits for each hero. Regarding the technical quality and expectations, the game has some significant issues that hold it back from being a standout. Some side missions can feel repetitive, the music was also meh. Additionally, there are a few hiccups that can be frustrating. Compared to the legacy Arkham games, the combat mechanics have regressed rather than progressed. Striking and evading in combat feels unpolished, nowhere close to the Arkham series quality. If you're into stealth, you will be disappointed. The silent take-down animation takes an eternity to complete, it often gives the enemy enough time to detect you just by their usual patrols. There's also a lack of grapple points in most areas.Why am I comparing this game to the Arkham series? Because the same people who built Arkham Origins also developed this game, the typical expectation is that you'll take something already good and evolve it, not diminish it.Overall, Gotham Knights is a decent game for fans of Batman and Co., but it falls just short of being a must-play. If you're a die-hard Batman fan or just looking for a fun action game, it's worth checking out. Just be aware that it has its flaws and does not compare to the Arkham series.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a terrible shame that this game should be the quality that it is. In concept, it's fantastic - play as the smaller heroes of Gotham City in a remarkably large open world, following your own dynamically generated leads and crimes whilst gradually discovering more about an overarching story and all topped off with the promise of co-op.Sadly, there are multiple flaws. For a start, the narrative leaves a lot to be desired. Broadly speaking, the death of batman seems to have had little effect on Gotham. A lot of the old faces are still around, the GCPD have regressed in terms of technology and capability, and barely any dialogue from civilians or criminals mentions Batman in any depth after the first few nights. This was an opportunity to let the smaller villains shine as the new kingpins of Gotham, contested by your take on your favourite Gotham side hero, but instead it's a bunch of badly written one-note parodies of the bat family against the usual line-up of villains.Technically, this game is an absolute mess. I have been trapped in rooms to fallen through the map, but the worst are the constant crashes - especially during co-op play. I actually bought this game to play with a fellow DC fan, as a concept that both of us were very excited for, but left us miserable and disappointed.Perhaps some day in the future, this game will be fixed, but not at the time of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: Overhated and an absolute unexpected joy. Absolutely fun to play and the variety of characters to choose from spruces up the gameplay. The missions make for visually stimulating and engaging gameplay and its repetition never came off as boring, rather mindless fun to fill up your time if you're not looking for anything story or cutscene heavy. You can divide your progress between nights and the game offers you a lot of leeway before proceeding to the next story beat, if you want to explore Gotham and beat lower stakes crime or power through in the mainline story. Narratively, there are optional cutscenes that add to the dynamics of the Batfamily post-Batman's passing, and it makes for tasteful character work. The main story, I will admit, isn't as engaging as any of the Arkham games but in my opinion still holds its own. Overall, this is really cool and I wish it got more love.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a blast in this game. The combat is pretty basic at first, but as you progress it gets more interesting as better enemies show up and you unlock more skills. It can be a bit grindy.I play on hard mode, and Ihave friends who chose to play on normal difficulty. It seems there's a pretty big difference between the two, most notably that enemies have either greater defense or greater health pools. Their attacks also do a lot more damage. As far as community goes, it seems like this game is being treated poorly by critics and some salty Arkham fans. Don't let them discourage you! This game is like playing a comic book. The characters play off each other really well, and the city feels alive. The patrol system, in spite of some drawbacks, is really immersive. Lastly, it's been a few days since release and I've noticed a huge graphics improvement. Performance was pretty mid day 1, but has gotten steadily better and better to the point that I have very little lag. My co-OP partner is using an old laptop to play and he's doing fine.

_childDocuments_.review: after now finishing the game, I felt the need to add my thoughts.to start with, the combat. it's no arkham knight.the combat can be shallow, but the more I played, the less "right" this statement felt. the combat can be simple, just button mashing, or you can take special care to pull off combos and find the best mix of light, heavy and ranged. this was an eye opener for me and since that point the combat felt more much more engaging, and I didn't particularly have an issue with it before.bottom line, the more you put into it, the more you will get out of it.graphics wise, the game is no red dead 2, but it isn't ugly either. no good no negative. artstyle is very reminiscent of arkham games so if you enjoy that style you'll have no issue.the basic gameplay loop of crime-fighting (traversing the world and fighting small time crime, interogating to find large scale crime, etc) feels fun and I easily lost myself in it for hours on end, and that's not including co-op.boss fights were relatively fun, apart (sadly) from the last 2 in the story as they kind of threw out all the standards of combat you'd been learning for the entire game.the story was interesting and I enjoyed playing through it, and twist felt satisfying because it subverted the trope it was based on well.characters felt different from each other and enjoyable, but most importantly they all work for co-op. no combo of characters felt like a "bad combo" each could compliment the other well, or even work on their own perfectly fine, and I feel that's a difficult balance to find.finally, the main reason I wanted to make this review, the credits scene.my god.that was cool!I genuinely believe games need to take note here.the entire credits sequence shows off key moments in story missions...WITH THE CHARACTER, CUSTOMISATION AND EQUIPMENT THEY HAD AT THE TIME!maybe I'm weird, but THIS WAS SO COOL! I got to see cool moments from the story again, remember then and the fun I had, while seeing the character I had played at the time, and the eventual progression of outfit and weapons I went through, it was really cool! and helped show me the progress I made throughout my time.all in all, a really cool idea, and I really hope other games take this idea and run with it because I think it was a wonderful way to make me, the player, feel important.all in all. I know this game isn't perfect. however, I think it's an actual diamond in the rough, and I think more people should give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: So i have very mixed feelings to an extreme over this game.On one hand i can see what people mean about the fighting getting repetitive with the button mashing and damage sponge enemies. I also get mildly irritated at fps drops but that comes with launches ( no excuse though but im not gonna be anal about it ). the stats in the trees dont provide too much to really notice but ive only been playing for a bit so i can imagine that equipment and gear stats buff those stats up ( such as crit, defense, damage, etc ) finishing off people in combat isnt as satisfying as the arkham games where finishing blows sounded like thunder but it does give u a slow motion view in your finishers which is cool. the story is actually pretty good though, comic fans might be able to guess the plot easily but even then from a comic reader's view this story does well in showing you interactions between red hood, nightwing, robin, and batgirl pretty well. The game even gives different social interactions in story cutscenes which is kinda rare nowadays. The character designs are great, i only have some slight issues with the face models when masks are off but thats more of a personal preference. the costumes are sick ( Robin hands down has the best costumes imo ) and it is always nice to hop in a random lobby admiring your partner's costume and color scheme. And speaking of coop it is pretty laggy for me but i have been enjoying my time so far joining random lobbies and helping people fight crime literally all over gotham, it is actually crazy how long you can be out at night just kicking ass and solving crimes. The game also does a decent job at letting you feel your partner's capabilities. Nightwing dropping his nest to provide some cc and buffs in case you are getting overwhelmed ( which you will be, the enemies aren't pushovers and can mess you up fairly quick if you aren't careful ), Red hood has a bullet for everyone and if not he is going to beat you mercilessly, Tim pops in and out with his plethora of gadgets and stealth capabilities, Batgirl is surprisingly just an unkillable single target dps machine. There really hasn't been a time where i was in coop and i thought to myself " hmm, that character kinda sucks compared to mine " and if anything it makes me super excited to see the 4 player coop mode and being able to have all 4 characters teaming up.So in the end...it all depends on how high your bar is set. If you compare this to the arkham games you may have a bit of fun before getting bored. If you're like me though and want something casual to play with your friend/partner this is definitely something id recommend as its fun, simple, and the story is engaging when its moving forward. Currently playing this with my gf and we are having a blast with Red Hood and Nightwing. 7.5-8/10Pros: satisfying combat theatrics, coop in gotham, classic yet good comic story, overall cool in a cinematic way.Cons: cheap stealth, traversal on foot/grapple could be better, Repetitive combat mechanics, slow paced in between story missions

_childDocuments_.review: So the game does have some crashing issues that I've had to work through and some poor performance when in windowed full screen and full screen mode. But running the game in its windowed setting clears up a lot of those performance issues even while keeping the graphics on the maximum setting.I did get one weird bug one time changing a setting all i adjusted was brightness and it crashed the game and PC, then on relaunch kept trying full screen and crashing. Had to use the steam launch command -windowed to force it to launch in windowed modeAs for the usual crashes, hopefully they will patch those soon, but in the mean time best I've found are a few work arounds ill put below.1)Verify the game files on a fresh install somehow a game file became corrupted and caused a crash in the during an early game cutscene with  2) verify drivers are up to date.3) This is the unfortunate one if the above isn't the issue and its a continual crash at the same spot skip the cutscene. But the story you might ask well YouTube is your friend, there are several channels with videos of every cutscene with each of the characters. Pause, watch the relevant cutscene, and move on. There are a few hit or miss launch options you can find online that may or may not help your performance or crashing.Now lets get down to game play.Quick Summary: If you mixed the Batman Arkham games with the Spiderman Games added in a loot and level system you'd end up here.Overall Score 6.5/10 -  The game does somethings well, others it could have and probably should have done better. It like Arkham Asylum compared to Arkham Knight, there's things that might take a game or two to figure out but it had to start somewhere. Nothing feels like it shouldn't be in the game but some things feel like they could have used more time to mature and develop. However nothing (besides the crashes) have stopped me from enjoying the game.Story 9/10 - Great story, encase you didn't know this is not part of the Arkham series storylineCombat 7/10 - If you've played a Arkham Batman game you'll understand quickly how to play.Repetitiveness 6/10 - There can be some degree of doing the same or similar minor crimes over and over but that's a failure of the superhero game type not the game itself. But enemies levels and elemental effects add enough variety to keep it interesting.Movement Traversal 5/10 - On foot its just like every other game nice simple clean makes sense, fluid in combat. Batcycle seems slow but given affects to seem fast, kinda clunky to control, also beyond strait A to B not much utility. Arkhma Knight did vehicle movement/utility better with the Batmobile. Grappling hook and other means like gliding feel verify similar to the Arkham games.Customization 5/10 - Weird category for a Batman game i know. But i do like there are several suit styles for each hero. Also each style has a few customization options for it Color Pallet 15 options, Cowl 3 options each suit, Symbol 3 options each suit, Arms 3 options each suit, Legs 3 options each suit. I would have like to be able to mix and match some of the pieces between the suits. In my opinion some suits look great but have terrible cowls which ruins the look or annoys me when there are other cowls that might look better.Loot System 7/10 -  Interesting take on this for this type of game reminds me of Avengers loot system but done much better. I'm always getting better schematics to craft better gear with decent options for how to spread stats.Leveling System  6/10 - This one is tied very closely to the combat in the game. As you level your gear really has the most impact on your combat level. The skills you can unlock for the characters are more minor changes to your character but somehow still important. Like not having one at a certain time might make the difference in winning a fight or staying undetected ect.AI Intelligence 5/10 - Now this might be more related to playing on less then the hardest setting. But the AI can sometimes be kinda stupid. Like could happen in the Arkham series, you might be stealth  knocking out a guy and not even arms length his buddy is completely unaware. Or even with them looking at you being more then like 15 ft away they might not see you choking out a guy in front of car headlights. But the Arkham series had these flaws to and so to most stealth games.Stealth 6/10 - Simple Easy to do and maintain, they probably could and should have added more detail here like using shadows vs well lit areas.Game Scenery 10/10 - Beautiful game love the Gotham Vista, nice pastel colors, glowing lights, and foggy atmosphere. It's very much what you would expect a rainy Gotham to look like from the comics and movies.Character Art 9/10 - The characters all looks great, some places here and there i would prefer different choices but not bad by any means. But all well designed and looks visually interesting and unique.

_childDocuments_.review: Character: Barbara Gordon (Batgirl)Difficulty: HardEquipment: Dell G15 Ryzen Edition- Controller I need to start this by saying that this was my first experience with the franchise, as I have not played the Arkham trilogy. Although I consider myself a seasoned gamer, I am more of an RPG person, yet my significant other is committed to Batman lore and all the games that are even remotely associated with “Bats” so he was excited when the game launched and we both bought it to play together. Here is exactly where the problem starts… Co-op was problematic, as more often than not it was impossible to connect together, progress was not saved on both sides, and regularly one of us would be disconnected mid-game and would be ridiculously difficult to come back. That being said, the experience of playing with someone else was very satisfying, as no matter that one of the two characters has a secondary role, in combats the game remains thrilling, and combined assaults are very pleasing. Moreover, you get to see the cinematics for both characters, which are well scripted and tell you more about the background of each individual hero and their relationship with Bru…, I mean with Batman. Now turning to the game as such, at least at the beginning of the game as well as in some more difficult quests strategy is important, as well as how well you are prepared. Playing around with your equipment is fun, and you can create a couple of weapons and apparels that are customized and useful. The scenery of Gotham is amazing and does create a great atmosphere for the game. Moreover, I LOVED flying around, collecting batarangs and landmarks of the city. (I know the motorcycle is also fun, but dude…you can fly around like BATMAN!)Other than issues with the co-op, the story, although satisfying, it left a lot to be desired. Additionally, the combats and the quests soon became repetitive, and the combination of movements was rather poor. After a certain level there was almost no challenging opponent and stealth was almost never something you could keep to the end, nor something you actually needed. Moreover, the game was much shorter than I expected. Just when I started really enjoying it and longing for more…it was over!…and the biggest problem of all was that the trilogy-nerd next to me could not stop saying “OMG this was so much better done in the older games…!” He said it so many times that I had to check for myself and…he kinda was right. Verdict: Very fun to playVery amusing Too shortSome times repetitive …FLYING AROUND GOTHAM CITY <3 PS: Really good for controller

_childDocuments_.review: (this is from the POV of a primarily solo player). I think Gotham Knights is a very solid game. Nothing too special, but nothing too bad either. The combat is simple but is satisfying on every character, though in my opinion robin is the least entertaining to play as. Each character has enough depth to keep interest and their "niches" don't stop you from being able to play any of them in any scenario. The story is solid, nothing too exciting either but it's certainly not a bad story. It's really intriguing to see the world of Gotham and it's characters without Batman. Each of the main cast is cool enough to follow through their backstory as well. The U.I for the game is simple and clean as well, easy to navigate through and find all you need. I also like how fast travel and other things are locked at the beginning, incentivising exploration. That being said though, my biggest complaint is how fast the novelty of it all wears off. The crimes and everything you're expected to do each patrol get really boring after sometime, even though there's a lot of variety (it truly doesn't feel that way). Most likely because all missions feel the same structurally -- which is why a lot of it falls flat after a couple hours in my opinion. Overall, I'd give Gotham Knights a 6/10. Not worth full price at all, but definitely worth checking out on a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, by its nature, invites comparison with two other games: Arkham Knight, and Marvel's Avengers. Since it has so many (bad) things in common with the Avengers game and so few (good ones) with Arkham Knight from which it really should have drawn inspiration, I am going to be very critical of it, perhaps even harshly so.Playing Gotham Knights is such a frustrating experience. The controls are floaty and unresponsive. The gameplay is severely unpolished. Movement is weird, it takes ~0.5s to start moving, and you can forget about precision turning. Combos are weird. Perfect attacks? Good luck, every combo is different. Predator mode is a far cry from what the game has to look up to, it reminds me of a mobile game in terms of how simplified and stupid it is.And the collectibles are some of the stupidest I've ever seen in any game. Find batarangs in a huge-ass city with zero hints? Find barely visible symbols on random walls? Scan tiny plaques on humongous buildings? Arkham Asylum, Wayne Tower, the GCPD building, Gotham General Hospital aren't Gotham landmarks???Remember how fluid and powerful traversal in Arkham City, Origins, and Knight felt? If you do, Gotham Knights says ♥♥♥♥ you.Here are some more stupid things in this game:- The 15 (!!) different types of "crafting" currency.- Red Hood's traversal is double-jumping, although that's nowhere nearly as stupid as Robin's traversal, which is just... moving the cursor.- The Knights arrange to go to a pride parade via e-mail; there is also a pride flag in the belfry for some unknown reason.- The Knights, the freaking Batman's successors, accidentally let Harley out of prison, and then when a certain Dr Q shows up, THEY DON'T KNOW WHO IT IS???- You go to the Penguin for info, he tells you to ♥♥♥♥ off, and indeed you ♥♥♥♥ OFF IN SHAME, this was hilarious.- The same cinematic for each of the 4 characters where Alfred tells you "It's certainly brighter than the Batcave".- Accessing the Social menu crashes the game every single time :)- "Crafting different gear unlocks new style components to customize your Suit." Yeah, no it doesn't.- The trap gauntlet.- Crime scene investigations with the same pieces of evidence occurring in the same way in multiple crime scenes (unrelated, ofc).- Also the stupid simplicity of the crime scene investigations.- Occasionally you get challenges that are just impossible to do, like Perfect Attack 3 enemies, which requires you to evade a melee attack, and you get all ranged enemies.- There are several motorbike models, but you need to have 1) preordered, and 2) bought a comic book to unlock them??- There are also outfits and weapons only unlockable via comic book??- There are traversal challenges and motorbike "races". I'm sure you can imagine what that looks like in a game of such shoddy craftsmanship.- The twist at the end was beautiful and wholesome and hopeful, and then of course that also had to be ruined. Luckily, it was the very end of the main story.- Good luck hitting your ranged attacks where you aim them.The art team is the only element here that's actually pulling its weight - the outfits, the animations, the environments, Gotham itself, it all looks wonderful. The Court of Owls reveal was sick as well. Too bad that's where the quality stops.

_childDocuments_.review: [TL;DR] This game is a victim of a hate band wagon caused by Console players who think they're gonna get 60fps on every game and Lets-Players who don't even enjoy these types of games. I have been a huge fan of pretty much anything in the Batman world and DC universe for a long time, and this game I am definitely a fan of. The story is on familiar ground and gets you invested to the characters, The open world is pretty big and rewarding to explore, the combat is fun, similar to that of the Arkham games but without spamming the dodge button making it more challenging. All the different enemies actually feel different and not just reskins of a few different combat classes like in most games like this. Building different kits to apply to the stats of different gangs or bosses you'll go against makes gadgets all that much more useful and important. My personal favorite thing is that we finally have a game where you can play through this known universe as these side characters through the whole game and not just 2-3 levels like in the Arkham games (being able to do it in coop is just a cherry on top).The performance that everyone seems to be talking about, the main thing that isn't even that bad (for me at least). I run this game at 4k, with all graphics maxed out and I get a solid 60-80fps, I RARELY dip below 60fps. I use a 3090Ti but I see people that are getting less frames with similar overall specs as me. So yes, for some people I am sure performance is really bad, but theyre yelling nonsensical blasphemy because they can't run a good game. This happens a lot with games, like Arkham Knight and Cyberpunk 2077, two games that everyone hopped on a bandwagon calling it bad but once people forgot about it, suddenly the games are now GOATed and the people that hated on them act like they always loved them. That is exactly what is going to happen with this game. What's my biggest issue with the game? Well, it's that the GRAPPLING IS AWFUL! It's bad, worse then The Avengers games spider-man swinging bad. It never will go where you're trying to aim and often times just launch you in a spot you weren't even looking. It more works like a "you wana just be flung straight at this ledge?" and you're launched. Another thing that does not make sense to me is the eventual unlock of Red Hood's powers...the sky hopping...it makes no sense for him to have those powers and they kinda brush over it. In the comics Red Hood actually has these swords or wing things that let him do the exact same thing so I am not sure why they didnt go with those, coulda been the same animation and everything. After 22.2 hours in this game, right now the game is a 7/10 for me. It is a really fun, captivating, and very enjoyable game. If you are not sure on this game cause of all the mixed reviews, wait for a performance patch that is likely soon to come, or wait for it to go on sale. If you have a good PC, buy it and try it.Update: The devs have been very active in releasing performance patches and updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game.  From a gameplay perspective, if one considers GK purely on its own, it's mediocre at best.  If one considers this game in the shadow of the Arkham series, it's utter ♥♥♥♥♥.  Which really annoys me because the gameplay footage made it look like the combat was really similar to the Arkham games.  Gone are the days of the incredibly fun free flow combat system from Arkham.  There's no "counter" button anymore, now you're only allowed to evade.And on evasion, think back to every game you've played the last 20 years that had sandbox exploration with melee combat.  If your character had the ability to jump and the ability to evade (aka "jump out of the way"), then dollars-to-donuts you used the same key to perform both of those maneuvers. Not the case here; you now use two separate keys for that.  Not only did some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius come up with the idea to split those two commands up, but said idea managed to get all the way through QAQC to get approved.  Like, every step of the way, people thought this was a *good idea*.The Devs also managed to ♥♥♥♥ up one of the most defining iconic aspects about the Bat Family - their tech, aka "gadgets".  Think back to all of Batman's most BadAss Moments (tm) - spoiler alert, I'm sure they all involved a gadget.  I sure hope none of you were hoping to be able to use gadgets in this game, because... well, they kind of don't exist.  Yeah, there's the grapple hook you can use to move through the city, but you're not gonna be grappling onto an enemy to initiate combat ever again.  No more explosive gel traps, freeze/glue grenades, guided batarang, etc; they're all gone.But the Devs were true to at least one aspect of the Arkham games: vehicles.  The introduction of the Batmobile into the Arkham Series was the worst ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mistake ever.  I'm guessing WB Montreal really wanted to hammer home how much they hate their customers by giving us a Batcycle that handles a lot like a speeding bobsled on an open field of really, really slick ice.  There were only so many accidental complete 180* turns I could take before completely ditching that piece of ♥♥♥♥ and never using it ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: I could not uninstall this game fast enough after I finished it.  I basically hate played it from chapter 2 onward just because I wanted to see if it got any better.  It did not.  You don't need to believe me, buy it for yourself and play it.  Just make sure you keep and eye on that refund timer.The first issue: It runs poorly.  It's a Batman game so that is to be expected. It would almost be more surprising if it ran well before a patch, but this isn't anything new with 3D Batman games, and they normally do get patched and play smoother after being out for awhile so I am not even that upset about that.Second(and probably biggest) issues: The game doesn't know what it wants to be.  Is it an RPG?  Is it an action adventure?  Is it a walking simulator?  I played 18 hours of it and I still don't know!  There are elements that feel like they were just tacked on for the sake of it, such as the crafting system.  You get just generic materials and blueprints and use it to make gear that has no real stats besides level and elemental damage.  It does have things such as health and power, but basically boils down to "higher level = better."There are simple things that should be expected in a 3D action game that are completely missing.  Such as a lock on system.  There would be times I was fighting a group of enemies, and when I would want to use my momentum move on the enemy I was beating up to finish him off, my character would just decide to jump across the screen and attack something else entirely with it.  The grapple system would do similar things where you would have the target grapple point highlighted, and when you push the button he would just grapple straight overhead and drop down.The last issue worth mentioning: It was slow.  Combat felt like your character was in molasses the entire time.  They give you a batcycle to navigate the city, but it is only slightly faster than running, and SLOWER than just grappling around where you want to go.  But it's not just the physics that feel slow.  The game play itself feels slow as you will randomly just not be able to progress the story until you go around and fight random crimes in the streets of Gotham.  At one point I spent 30+ minutes looking for a crime being committed by a specific faction so I could learn what to do next only to find out that I needed to clear out a side mission I had activated to spawn the ones I needed because it changed the ones to specific factions for the side quest.The only redeeming thing I have to say about it is: It's short.  Not short enough to beat inside the return window.  But short.

_childDocuments_.review: : Arbitrary 6 /10.  recommend. Wait for >40% sale and for performance fixes and reviews. Very frequent  are my main issue (during fast travel, combat, open-world traversal, cases. . .) Launch day Cyberpunk crashed way less than this game. All heroes feel good late game but all feel janky and awkward early on. Enjoyable enough narrative and writing to stick with the janky gameplay to see it through. If you enjoy action RPG-lites, typical Ubisoft-like open-world elements, and replayability, then Gotham Knights will be enjoyable.Despite all the issues, I actually enjoy the game when everything is working fine. While most of the criticism you'll read is true, outside of the performance issues Gotham Knights isn't the worst of its genre. The  is pretty interesting. I enjoy the direction the characters are taken: their individual moments are intimate and I'm satisfied with their visual designs and stories but the overall main plot is a bit meh -- predictable and slightly-too-fast pacing. It doesn't feel like enough time in the story is spent per faction nor villain.  can also be a bit cringe but it isn't obnoxiously present throughout the entirety of the game. Per hero, not a lot of the dialogue is unique in side content. can be decent fun on medium. The heroes are actually unique and I can see the different roles they would play in co-op but this is something you might not explore enough in singleplayer as switching heroes is interruptive to the flow. _childDocuments_.review: Combat is... not good. The dodge notifications are easy to miss, and the gun ones are super easy to mis-time. If you play too long as red hood for example, skill points do get transffered, but all of your other characters will have absolutely garbage gear and no option to craft more because you would actually have to go into the city and find schematics. Having to unlock the Knighthood skill tree is honestly just tedious, especially since it locks the character's unique traversal mechanics behind it (for reference, it's a tutorial on each character and 10 premeditated crimes with that character as well, forcing you to play without an entire tree for at least 1.5 hours). It is definitely not at the caliber of an arkham game in terms of storytelling but overall if you are a fan of batman there is lots here that they do right by these characters. Combat was more fun than I expected, it can feel a little slow sometimes but you can pull off some really cool combos and when you take out a batch of enemies within seconds it feels very rewarding. At the time of writing, having just completed the main story I'm 38 hours in with lots more to unlock and discover. It wasn't the smoothest technical journey i've played but to fellow batman nerds and rpg fans like me, I think this one is worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The enjoyment of any video game depends heavily on what you value most in the art form. If you most value high performance, little to no bugs, and visually stunning action, you're probably not going to like it. If you value hours worth of  character specific dialogue, huge amounts of character customization, emphasis on character interactions, and cutscenes... you may or may not like it.  When going in to this game you need to realize that this is not an Arkham game, and NOT a Batman game. The Batfamily in and out of official comics are not stoic, nihilistic, depressed, or by the books. They banter, tell puns, say wholesome comments, and have a much more sunny disposition... even Jason. They are purposefully opposite of Batman in many ways. and that stretches even in to the environment. Gotham is much less intense and gloomy, there's many normal citizens who aren't murder clowns, the city is bright with neon lights that illuminate the smog, and it doesn't take place in a prison city. The major characters, their voice acting, dialogue, and the story are what they spent most of their energy on. If from game play videos these don't resonate with you then you might either want to skip it or wait for a sale. I personally love these aspects of the game, and it feels like it was lovingly catered to what I value most in games, and has close to nothing that I find abrasive. I highly recommend it to people who are looking for a feel good story that is made for comic readers, who can forgive some technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just painfully muddled about what it wants to be. Gotham Knights is stuck in Rocksteady’s shadow and never really pushes beyond being a mediocre beat-em-up that doesn't seem to learn from any of the other titles in its genre. The story has its moments but never truly settles into any one theme. The narrative is disjointed and feels overtly episodic, never giving any theme enough room to breathe or be explored properly and leaving its best moments always falling short of truly resonating with the player. It’s an open world game with abysmal clunky traversal, even after you unlock the motorcycle and character-exclusive mobility options. The city itself is bland and pretty forgettable, the story is held back by PG-13 language and tonal restrictions but the gameplay has criminals detonating thermal explosives strapped to civilians, a mass grave, public executions and cutscenes show characters bleeding or getting stabbed. There’s no reason for the dissonance, either make the game kid friendly or lean into the darker sides of Batman’s coterie but this half and half decision just leaves all aspects unsatisfying and incomplete. The core gameplay loop is just the random events from Spiderman PS4 but without any of the movement. Criminals don’t run away in vehicles and the city doesn’t feel alive during combat, it’s just a series of miniature arenas that all feel empty. Core experience is you grapple, land, mash buttons, grapple away. There’s no predator encounters, no option to bail out of a silent takedown (something Arkham City introduced in 2011), an incredibly slow trickle of new enemy types and a complete absence of a counter button. The massive dodge window and I-frames on the dodge makes it even less challenging. PS3 era beat-em-ups have better core gameplay than this.If it was a stand-alone game it would be decent but knowing that this is coming after the Arkham Trilogy makes it not worth it. Boss fights are alright, but the core gameplay and narrative are so lackluster I walked away feeling like it was just a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like DC/Batman content, you'll find something to enjoy with this game. I can say however, if you're not, this might just be a really bog standard gaming experience. I personally love DC/Batman, so I can look pass the flaws, which the game has quite a bit of, unfortunately. Other than FPS drops and muddy graphics here and there, the game-play loop can get very repetitive. While the story is generally good and the villains are handled extremely well, if you don't like the IP, I feel like it'll be a struggle for you to get through the repetitiveness  to see those story beats and villain encounters. The combat is not Arkham, it's also not trying to be Arkham. However, that does not excuse the stickyness of the controls and awkward button choices with no option to remap, at least if you're using a controller. I often feel a few seconds ahead of what my character is actually doing. With that out of the way though, the combat is serviceable, but don't go in expecting Arkham or for the combat to be overly smooth. My BIGGEST pet peeve though, is how your character controls when it comes to find platforming, sneaking. From jumping 60 feet off a rallying, to getting stuck on boxes, to refusing to grab a ledge, your character controls like a shopping cart with a busted wheel. The delay in movement from controller input is a bit ridiculous, and the boxyness of your character movement makes stealth a fools errand. Imagine an Assassins Creed characters movement, but slower and more awkward. Sounds like a lot of negatives right? Well, that's because there is a lot to be improved here. However, as I said at the beginning, if you like DC/Batman games and you're starving for that content, you'll be able to push through like I did. But if you do not like the IP, please skip this or wait for a sale. My Yes recommendation purely comes down to the above. If I could give the so-so hand, I would. Happy Gaming everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow. I have read that this game has performance issues on PC (alongside consoles, on which the game fails to maintain even abysmal 30 FPS and drops into 20s). I haven’t imagined it to be that bad though. So, on RTX 4090, which carried any game I’ve thrown at it so far on 4K ultra settings at 120 FPS, this game can’t even lock to 60 (with RT enabled). I’ve played around some settings, and the results are still far from having a locked FPS. The main party-pooper is RT in this game, with it disabled, a lot of frames are regained and 120 becomes possible, although still not stable. Surprisingly, visually, RT does not change that much in this game. What makes it especially bad is the fact that the game looks very unimpressive even on all settings set to highest (including RT). It’s not the case of some future-proofed experience either. For instance, I was mind-blown by visuals served at max settings and with RT doing its magic in WD: Legion and Cyberpunk 2077, and was able to understand why my GPU at the time couldn’t serve high frame rates. Here I understand one thing: poor coding/optimization. You don’t even need to glide above Gotham to see staggering frame fluctuation. The very beginning of the game is set in pretty enclosed spaces and even then the performance is bad.  Furthermore, even when I managed to get the game running close to 120 FPS, I was disappointed (once again) to see that all the cutscenes rendered real-time (not a pre-rendered movie, like the intro, which sports 30 FPS) are locked to 60 FPS.On the game itself, performance aside. I found it hard to keep on playing because of the poor performance, but from what I’ve seen so far, the game is designed as poorly as it is optimized. It starts with a very lengthy pre-rendered cutscene, and then drops you into a pretty dull location. It doesn’t feature the beautiful design of, say, Arkham Asylum or any of the Uncharted games, where you immersed into the game almost immediately and see the story unfold through gameplay (most of the time), not some long and boring cutscene. Furthermore, the voice acting, which was stellar in Arkham games, is so bland here. Batgirl's voice sounded so annoying to me in the intro, I've had no desire to play the character, although prior to hearing that voice, I was interested in playing that character the most. Red Hood's voice was the only one I found more or less pleasant. Stephen Oyoung is behind that and it's a familiar voice, too, as I'v recently played the long-awaited Spider-Man port (which easily runs at max settings, including RT, and looks great on my hardware, unlike this game), and the same actor gave his voice to Martin Li.I see no reason to pay full price or even half price for this game at its current state. There are so many incredible games launched around the same time: Persona 5, Uncharted 4, A Plague Tale: Requiem, and so many others. Some of the costume designs are really incredible, although i wish the transmog system was better implemented, and it didn't take me until the end of the game to unlock most of them.All in all i'd say the game is a 5/10 and recommend buying it when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanted to like this game, I simply could not in the end. This is a huge step back after the Arkham series, and I'm not just talking about poor optimization because, as most of you know, Arkham Knight didn't always run smoothly on PC to say the least, but it was a great videogame in all aspects (except for Batmobile).The combat system gets boring really quick, especially when the game forces you to fight the same enemies to complete the same tasks in the very same locations to level up your character. What's worse, the very same enemies you fight in the beginning become exceptionally strong all of a sudden in the later stages of the campaign. Just pointless grinding to extend your playthrough by ~10-15 hours. The stealth system is even WORSE; it's an absolute joke compared to the Arkham games. Enemies are both blind and deaf - take one guard down while standing two meters away from another and no one will notice. I refuse to believe actual human beings tested that and thought it was alright.But to be fair, the game is fun at times. I liked the side quests with Quinn, Clayface, and Dr. Freeze, and the boss fights. The main plot is cool too, but I think it should have been used in an Arkham game. The level of threat is too great to be handled by Batman's protégé, it's something that the Dark Knight himself should be facing off against.In the end of the day, I can see you enjoying this game in a way if you are a DC fan, but as for the rest - it's just not worth it. TL;DR combat and stealth are horrible and get boring quickly, optimization is bad, crashes occur constantly, you have to grind a lot. The story is the only thing worthy of your attention, but, IMHO, is predictable and falls short at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I'm the one complaining about performance issues, but my RTX 3060 Ti is running the game on Ultra1080 with RTX and DLSS Quality at 120-144 FPS throughout. Not a single framedrop or crash in the 4 hours I've played so far.Gotham Knights is not a narrative-heavy Arkham game, but a free-roam game with a similar formula put on top of it. You don't have the same repertoire of gadgets as Batman did, but four different characters with different skills you can unlock. Combat feels a bit more slow-paced and clunky, unfortunately, but I've primarily played it solo despite it clearly being targeted at 2 player coop. The open world with its diverse side quests (probably prodecurally generated?) might get grindy after a while, but so far I'm enjoying the pacing between stealth, combat, and investigation. I'm just a bit overwhelmed by the crafting mechanics and the ton of different equipment the game throws at me.Pedestrians have random conversations and comment on your actions, which adds a lot to the atmosphere and attention to detail. I'm not far into the game yet, but I'm surprised by how good it feels all around and can barely comprehend the many negative ratings. I'll update when I played it for a bit longer.UPDATE:Alright, 4 hours later, I need to add some things.First of all, I can't believe how atrocious the controls actually are. Coming from the Arkham games, it is ridiculous how broken and imprecise these controls are. You get constantly stuck on ledges, you can almost never grapple to the position you are actually aiming at, and in combat you keep attacking enemies in a completely different direction from the one you are actually looking and pressing to. This will regularly to extremely frustration situations where you die because you cannot attack the enemy you need to attack, you fail time trials because you cannot move towards the next target, you will blow your cover and lose stealth bonuses because you cannot move or because "stealth takedown" and "loud ranged attack" are mapped to the same button.I still stick to my previous points: While regular frustration is unavoidable, the gameplay is generally fun. It just takes some work. And this is where my main criticism comes in:The main story makes it absolutely clear that the game isn't meant to be played alone. I continued the game in singleplayer mode because my friend walked out on me and never has time for a coop session, and I just finished a main mission where I was fighting enemy waves for 10 minutes straight. I failed stealth sections because I couldn't take out two enemies at once. While the open world grind is easily doable without a partner, the main missions don't scale down at all, and you will have to do twice as much work. And I'm using the word "work" on purpose, because combat can become repetitive and tedious. In cutscenes, all of the main characters will talk about the events as if all of them took part in the mission, even if you went in on your own.I'm assuming this is where the many negative reviews come from: The game gives you the illusion that you can play it solo, and you kinda can. Hell, you don't even unlock coop mode until you're 90 minutes into the game. But if you don't have anyone you actually plays the game with you, you likely won't get much enjoyment out of it after the tutorial. You can team up with randoms, but I haven't tried that yet.So, do I still recommend the game? Yes, I do. But only, really ONLY, if you're going to play it in multiplayer mode.

_childDocuments_.review: To get this out of the way, Gotham Knights is NOT an Arkham Game, and does have many deviations from the previous installments that make it better and worse in many ways. Understand that I am reviewing the game from the perspective that I understood this well going in, and was not expecting a fifth Arkham game. Also know that I played through the game with an RTX 3070 and did not have even close to perfect performance running it with this. Just be warned that this game is terribly optimized and you should not attempt to run this on anything less than the minimum recommended specs. Anyways, I recommend Gotham Knights with a large amount of hesitance because its core mechanics in many ways just make me pissed rather than giving me enjoyment. It's auto-lock is absolutely terrible and barely works, the grinding that you'll experience is generally a pain in the ass, most enemies when you reach close to endgame are annoying bullet sponges, and I've found (from getting nearly all momentum abilities with all heroes) that only Red Hood will make it partially tolerable. I will say though that even with all of the negative aspects that I've experienced, and how much this game can piss me off, I had a large amount of fun with this game and continue to recommend it. The story, while honestly not being the most engaging, is still fun to play though, and I enjoyed spending the time to play through it. The fact that all members of the Batman family are humanized and you get to spend time with them in their daily lives, it gives a level of depth to each member that is nice to see. The Heroes all do feel unique and make the experience feel drastically different depending on who you're playing. For instance, if you're playing with Red Hood, you'll be much more in the fray using your dual pistols to gun down the enemy. This, in stark contrast with how you could be playing Nightwing and his timing based melee gameplay, and so on and so Forth. Also, when the combat works, it can be very engaging and fun, and gives you a concrete system to hone your skills with. The city of Gotham feels lived in and, for the most part, is well designed with its size is being large enough to feel vast, but still allows you to remember the map easily. Overall it's clear that the devs did care a large amount for the game they were producing and it shows through. Obviously do your own research and watch reviews on Youtube to come to a decision, however know that the game is worth it to play through and experience. It has its flaws and issues that inhibit a perfect experience, but there are a large amount of positive aspects to the game that make it worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I want to like this game, but theres a serious crashing issue, like not even a crash it just shuts down with no warning and theres no crash report to submit. At first it was every 20~ mins, i do make the effort with games to find out why and how to rectify so i can play on, theres general reasons like corrupt files you need to verify integrity that can help which it did for me with marvels avengers to a good extent, this game had no corrupt files to repair. The one thing that helped alot was giving it the option to force run with dx11, prolonging my game to a couple hrs before crash, today it decided to hit some kind of graphical stutter during combat against 4 enemies with nothing to strain a gpu, i fled the combat and the stutter stopped and i went back in to finish the fight no issue. i dont even have the game on high graphics which i can do on practically any other game i play, so its a bad performance game to me.Other than the above i hate the traversal system, you try grapple something and the points it chooses arent what youre looking at half the time, sometimes it will grapple directly above when theres a perfectly good grapple edge right in front of you, you can grapple like 100m away at times but other times it wont even do 10m unless you look at it on a funny angle.The movement sucks hard, if you walk into some edge like a chair or rock, your movement gets like a hard reset and you have to try navigate away from the object at a slow acceleration type movement, this could probably be fixed with better movement reactions.The combat.... its part good, the high impact finishing knock outs and stealth KOs have good graphical action, but the weapon play is queer to the point that it doesnt even look applicable to the fights at times.Another problem i had with fights, i got stuck on an open corner edge where i shouldve just fallen off, but one of the big bruiser enemies popped a slam AoE that has a duration element on the ground and instead of letting me dodge off the edge it just held me in place taking damage with no ability to get out, so another issue is edges having a barrier when you dodge into it, even walking off an edge its hit and miss if it will grab and hang, but if you want to jump off the edge you have to hold sprint so you cant play with 'sprint toggle' since each time you press it you either slow to jogging pace or sprint and its not easy to keep track of with all these little steps you jump.There are good points in the game like vehicle summon and the ability to swap characters when you return to the belfry at nearly any time, but there arent enough good things to drown out the issues.Also if youre wondering the set up im playing on, its a GeForce RTX 3070 with an i7 13700KF CPU, game is installed on a 1TB SSD.
