_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Just save yourself if the money, If you're a Batman fan just go watch someone stream it. I'm just gonna request a refund.How do I describe this game? Well on the one hand I feel trapped because this a Batman game and I a fan of Batman. However, on the other hand I feel like Warner Bros. is counting on people like me to just carry them through a poorly optimized game that doesn't seem completed yet with regards to mechanics.PROS:1. Side character focus: one of the best things that I saw about this game was the focus on side characters that I felt was lacking in other Arkham games. With this I felt better about more combat focus.2. Detective mode: This replaced by an AR sonar system. It's refreshing not having to spend significant portions of the game in detective mode with the awful colors.CONS:1. Poorly optimized: Even on my RTX 3090 and i9-10850k w/ 64 GB RAM on an SSD, which I imagine is above average specs, the game had moments where it stuttered. I'm not talking about long loading times either. This happened while grappling from one location to another or driving the batcycle. I thought Arkham Knight was bad, but how is it possible that the graphics didn't get better and the end result of the newer version was worse. 2. Story: This seemed a little boring. I was expecting a more aging Batman in his last stand "death". I won't go further than that for spoiler reasons.3. Combat: Here is the double edged sword that is combat. While I am glad that we've got combat focusing on side characters and actually developing them, it seems that this was just not fully fleshed out. I can't tell you just how disappointed it was to see potential in the fact that we we're moving forward from the freestyle combat system in the Arkham games, only to find it incomplete. I feel like the devs wanted to flesh this out but weren't able to in time.In short Warner is expecting the fans to carry this unfinished game and just buying whatever trash they throw at us. However, I just can't keep giving them my money while ignoring the bad. I feel like a WoW player at this point complaining about the company not listening to the player and still giving them money.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is showing improvements over time. Compared to prior, I no longer need DLSS to enjoy ray tracing at playable frame rates. It still dips every now and then, but it is no doubt an improvement.I still won't recommend it on the basis of rusty movement. It takes half a second for the character to start moving after holding a direction. The characters jump a meter to the next ledge past an L shape instead of the floor when aiming for the latter. Bumping into walls, NPCs, or other players causes one to stop instead of side-step like other games, including DCUO, which is about a decade older.The game is a lot of fun with friends, but half the time, we both encounter unfair situations that just cause anger. Seriously, the game makes returning the Marvel's Avengers feel like I'm dipping my feet into the smooth, warm sands of Boracay. It is shameful for a modern "AAA" game. I'm not putting the devs' skills into question. Ii'm only targeting their frankly awful decision to make movement so rusty.They really looked at Arkham and said, "Hey, you know what it could have done better? When you hit a corner in a vent, you should stop. Yeah, all gameplay should halt, instead of smoothly going to the next objective!" It is aggravating.This next part has no effect on my recommendation. It puzzles me why transmogs can't be edited on a case-by-case basis. I'm not asking them to make new meshes for Knightwatch, Talon, and Knighthood, but for suits that already have modular meshes attached to crafted variants, I don't see why we shouldn't be able to modify 'em. New Guard, Titan, Eternal, Year One, Neon Noir, Demon, Privateer, Metal, Beyond, Knight Ops, and Shinobi should be modifiable as transmogs in my humble opinion. Again, this part has no effect on whether or not I recommend the title.Thanks for reading. If you end up loving this game despite the issues I mentioned, then there's no harm nor shame in that. I also enjoy the game's story, characters, world, etc... Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: There are few positives to this.The game looks good; the characters are all well acted. The story is totally fine, well foreshadowed so it all comes across as fairly non-shocking. The small details, especially in the emails, are great. But fundamentally this game is Broken. A large beautiful Gotham city with no reason to go to any of it. It's shamefully soulless; which is a shame because you can tell the devs put a lot of time and heart into it. Whoever thought of the idea of having the credits show scenes from the story, but include the character and suit you were using at the time? A wonderful touch.It is a shame such passion is wasted on a game with a core concept so poor.The combat is clunkier than it needs to be, for no reason. I understand these 4 are not Batman, but this isn't their first rodeo either. And they feel terrible. What made Batman Batman was not his level 23 Pauldrons of Exceptional Strength, it was his dexterity and strength. In Gotham Knights, you WILL upgrade your suit to the next highest number, or you will not finish this game. You WILL ensure you carefully apply Frost Damage to your enemies in order to win. You WILL socket the best quality gem (Jesus H) into your weapon's gem slot to up the Critical Hit %.Enemies do not require intelligent navigation of the correct combination of dodging, stunning, or countering -- no. Specific enemies require specific special abilities. I hope you enjoy slowly building up your Special meter to get rid of them (and you had the aforemention gear to output the damage so it's not a half an hour slog). This and the Gear Rating locks you into some of the worst, most tedious combat imaginable. If you're not spec'd for the right battle, it's all over before it's begun. Additionally, it means that different enemy types in combination with one another are basically useless because you just have to use your Special Meter to make them go away. Not consider that that enemy requires this sort of combat before the next one.I fully appreciate that the Arkham games have a One Button approach, but the complexity was the way in which you used the 4 different buttons in combination with one another. How many enemies you had to remember the moves of. This is replaced now with: Enemies have dodgeable moves that you can punish, Enemies are weak to certain Elemental attacks, Enemies occasionally need you to do a Heavy Attack to break their guard. On paper this might come across as very similar, and fundamentally this game is about flying around a room at high speed to kick goons in the face, but to be clear: All enemies are dodged the same. All enemies are guard broken the same. No enemies are chosen to punish you for needing to perform a particular action in a particular manner. But they do need you have that Correct Gear on! I see it as a step down across the board.Boss battles follow on -- they are all terrible. They are long and uninteresting. You dodge the same combo, you put hits in, you find the boss has hyper armour, you wait for your next chance. You use a special ability and waste a bar because *that* power doesn't work on *this* boss (hint: they basically all don't). I especially detest the Mr Freeze battle(s) & Clayface battle. (Remember when the greatest boss battle was Mr Freeze in Arkham City?!) I am stunned that they exist in this game. You do not feel the weight of your attacks to them. But you do get to see "413" show up when you land the hit because this is foremost an RPG about getting your numbers higher. There's no thought to "The combat system works like This. So the boss battle requires This." Think of Mr Freeze in City, or Deathstroke in Origins. They would require you to master a particular gameplay style. These bosses do no such thing. They are not a challenge to your skill, or your planning, they are a challenge to your patience if you don't have the right damage output.A giant open city to crawl around in and you will spend that time fast travelling to a section and then travelling as quickly as possible to the next randomly generated Activity as quickly as possible. There is nothing to see in Gotham City. Are there collectables? Sure. You can scan large art murals. You can scan tiny plaques. Or you can touch one of approx. 4 dozen glowing batarangs that sit on empty building, next to empty alleyways. Oh. Excuse me. There are small caches left around by the Court of Owls, that require noticing symbols. What's your reward? A smattering of crafting mats. Oh joy. This game is 100% focused on "Show up and punch a criminal and then get out of there." You will not remember the minute details of Gotham City. Just the arenas you waltz around in again and again.There is a "Detective System" which is used a small handful of times for story related puzzles and then offers an extremely watered down version for the "randomly generated" stuff where you literally just scan a crime scene and select the clue with the answer. It's a bit like watching Blue's Clues. Except you need to have noticed everything before you can leave.The Batcycle feels slow. The fact there is no boost button is quite funny, what's the point if not to feel good? It feels like they had no faith in the vehicle. A fact that is backed up by the fact there's zero encouragement to replay any of the races. You do them, you get your XP, it disappears from your mind and the game forever. Once you get the power to fast travel, aside from a few Side Quests, you will basically spend zero time riding it.I see people talking about the Side Quests a lot. I've mentioned them here. In the world there are a number of set invisible nodes, on which a crime may occur. That comes in one of several flavours, most of which are basically surface-level differences (prevent the break in, prevent the hack, and prevent the robbery are all the SAME crime but with different flavour-text). Once you've done one crime in that location, you've basically done them all. I just don't see the desire to fill the game with an ever replenishing set of "Show up to this courtyard and kill these dudes who are now doing This" style. I am stunned that the spiritual successor to the Arkham games (and let's not pretend this is not what this game is) could mess all of the factors that make that game good, and just surface level copy the notes of those games (press Square to fly across room and hit in face. large city. batman is in game. villains appear) and produce this one.The "Heroic Assault" mode is not out by time of writing, and perhaps that will magically turn around the core of the game being unmitigated bread; but I doubt it. The only way this game could have been fixed is it was thrown out.I totally appreciate that it might be unfair to compare it to the Arkham games, but this company owns that IP; and clearly used it at a surface level to inject an RPG system; and the result is a game that feels worse to play, with ironically less replayability than it's predecessors.Gotham Knights is not now, nor will ever be, worthy of your attention.

_childDocuments_.review: It's better than, "Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League", but not nearly as good as the Arkham series. Steam only gives you a binary choice of Yes or No to rate a game, so I have to choose "no", but if you're like me, that's a "no" in terms of quality UNLESS the price is right, which for me, it was. There are a few redeeming qualities about this game: I happen to LOVE all four of these characters and have spent 40 years of my life (and countless dollars) reading about them in comics, so seeing them have a game together where the main premise puts them in the driver's seat was too much to pass up, even though the reviews have been terrible. I got it on a DEEP sale, and that's the only time I'd recommend buying it. Aside from loving the characters, there's a fun "Barbie Dress Up" system of customizing your heroes and their gear that can be really, really fun to mess around with. There are some fantastic costume and weapon designs for each character, and for many of the gear sets, you can adjust between multiple versions of gloves, masks, boots, color palates, etc. That was one thing I truly enjoyed about this game was decking out my heroes in very swanky looking costumes and taking them out to fight the criminals in Gotham, dressed to impress! And for the villains, I have to say that Mr. Freeze has one of the BEST designs I've ever seen for the character. Also as a redeeming quality in the game is a positive message about moving on from loss. There is also very strong emphasis in the story about family, and what it means to move on from tragedy to become both the person you're meant to be as well as a better-functioning family unit. But that said, this game is way too grindy, and inexplicably does everything worse than the Arkham series. The combat is worse, the stealth is worse, the mini-games and sidequesting is ungodly repetitive, and the game had some SERIOUSLY bad glitches.  I had characters become invisible in post-Boss fight cutscenes and some incredibly difficult boss fights not end properly, forcing me to either restart the fight or restart the game.. The Kelvin Incident final boss fight uses a mash-up of three different bosses, plus henchman, and in my game, this fight glitched over and over and over again until I finally stuck to killing the bosses in a certain order and making sure I didn't bring their health all the way to zero so that the 'plot' of the fight would kill them. Bugs like this combined with an a god-awful decision about how the characters get geared up was beyond frustrating. There is a pool of modifications shared between all four characters, but you only get blueprints for better armor and weapons for the hero you are currently playing as; if I'm playing as Red Hood and I get some spiffy new crafting blueprint, it's ONLY for Red Hood; this puts a nasty gear cap on the characters you aren't playing as and forces you to do a lot of tedium if you want to play as the other characters and make sure they have good gear. I came out of the mulitplayer floors so overpowered for the final Main Story Quest final boss fight that I was able to kill the final boss in each phase in three hits or less, and that made THAT fight glitch because their health would drop so far, so fast that it would skip a quick-time event. I put about 60 hours into the game and the good doesn't outweigh the bad or the comparisons to the Arkham series. This game, with some better graphics, combat, stealth, and less grind, could have been an awesome spiritual successor to Arkham Knight. As it is, it feels like a pale shadow. At that heart of that shadow was at least an attempt to make a decent super hero video game, and I respected that. But the parts that don't work just REALLY don't work, some of which of is totally unforgivable. If you're a huge fan of these characters and can get this on a big sale like I did, then yes, buy this game. If you're on the fence, I'd say just play Arkham Knight again or any of the games in the Arkham series. I loved being able to play as these characters, but the game world around them made almost tiring and aggravating at points, and made me sad that such great characters were trapped in a game that somehow is worse than a set of games from almost 10 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotham Knights is an Arkham-esque “open city” action game from Arkham Origins developer, WB Games Montréal.I had just assumed it was another Arkham spin-off, following on from Knight for all the fuss it makes about Batman being dead. But apparently not. It does seem to be performing a similar job to Origins though, being a stand in while Rocksteady continue to (struggle to?) get the next “proper one” ready.In Gotham Knights, Batman is dead. No, really! So the protection of Gotham (no nicer a place to live than it ever has been) falls to his proteges, specifically Nightwing, Batgirl, Robin (Tim Drake) and Red Hood.All 4 Batkids are playable, and you can switch between them as inclined. They each have some unique attributes, with Nightwing having his acrobatics, Batgirl's skill with tech/hacking, Robin is best at stealth, while Red Hood shoots and smashes stuff + is a jerk.I found Red Hood just too slow to be any use at all. Batgirl and Robin a bit on the weak side. So mostly stuck with Nightwing as a good allrounder.The main story concerns the League of Shadows and (recent-ish addition) Court of Owls going at it on your turf, with other more well-trod faces like Mr. Freeze, Clayface and Harley Quinn putting in another turn to pad it out with their own side stories.Gotham Knights retains the “open city” setup introduced in Arkham City, with more of a hub this time in the Belfry, a HQ you return to at the end of each night (where the out-of-suit story progressing cutscenes play out, like an episode of Power Rangers).Gotham Knights is a “follow the objective marker” kind of game. You’ve got your superhero grapple hook for scaling and zipping between buildings but not the “cape glide” you’re used to from the Arkham games, which caused me some difficulty throughout.Possibly it was muscle memory from the Arkham games? But I kept finding myself in the enemy database screen when trying to get around the city, since (for whatever reason?!) holding down the A button here is some kind of context sensitive shortcut to menus.There is a bit of a glider unlocked quite far in (unless it was just late for me, since it felt like I should have had it earlier?). It reminded me of the one from Breath of the Wild, but less useful.It does some other daft things too, like on-screen text tutorials when introducing new enemy types which can only be beat in a specific way, throwing it up right at the same time as they start attacking you! You can’t really defend against that whilst also reading the text! Surely you’d think to pause it so you can read the instructions?!The last open city superhero game I played like this was Insomniac’s Spider-Man. That game gave you a real sense of awe and exhilaration as you swung your way through the city that was completely lacking here.The game still looks/plays very much like an Arkham game, with a similar mix of combat, open city traversal, crime scene investigation, more combat…You can travel at street level on a motorbike which is instantly summonable. And there is a fast travel system unlocked (Assassins Creed tower-like) to quickly jump between the different city districts.You swoop around the city breaking up an infinite number of crimes, and as with all these open environment superhero games, there’s a limited number of different “types” which you quickly become familiar with.Combat is also very similar to Arkham but feels more “streamlined”, to put it nicely.You take on groups at a time, enemies telegraphing their attacks with big colour-coded glowing fists, which you evade with the press of a button, countering if you time it just right.Enemy groups are a familiar mix of melee, gun-toting, heavies and new/annoying types like these ones who control drones. To survive, you need to manage each encounter, landing the requisite attacks which work well against the individual enemy types you’re facing, between constantly evading their attacks.Doing well in combat (chaining together hits without also taking damage) earns Momentum Points used to perform character-specific special attacks.Again like Arkham, enemies get tougher/better equipped over the course of the game. By the end, when it’s all Court Talon’s and League ninjas, it’s all quite annoying and drawn out.Compared to Arkham, there is more of a “levelling” system and more variables to balance due to the (questionable) introduction of a loot/crafting system, where you find crates around the city containing materials you can make more powerful suits/weapons from.It’s something other “open” games dabble with, to varying levels of success. As a result, some of the encounters in Gotham Knights did feel much more difficult than others. I never had to do any grinding, and you’re given a large supply to “health packs” to keep you going.Another factor is co-op play, seemingly a big focus for the development team, wanting to do an Arkham game for two. I had a couple of random people drop in (literally 2 over 30 hours of play, so not sure how active the servers are) and it was mostly fun.I was really struggling with the Man-Bat mini-bosses near to the end until an over-powered Robin joined the game and took them out quicker than I could regular enemies! Solo, the boss fights felt really very drawn out.Four player open city co-op was apparently too big of a challenge. There is a separate 4-player horde type mode, if that counts?Arkham Knights is marked as “Playable” on Steam Deck, citing small text as a potential issue. I didn’t have a problem with the text size, it was more the terrible frame rate and that it kept crashing!Clearly, this is more game than the hardware can really handle. Turning all the settings down as far as they’d go did improve stability (it did still crash semi-often) and made it playable, if very ugly. Character models looked especially bad, like everyone has candyfloss for hair and eyebrows.The Steam Deck was definitely struggling, but it might also be a pretty buggy port in general? The game was panned on release for extreme instability, mainly referencing the frame rate. Since then it has been improved with patches.I couldn’t say for sure how much of the jankiness I encountered was the hardware and how much the software. The PS5 version is no doubt a better experience.I still enjoyed Gotham Knights, quite a bit, just not as much as the Arkham games. Which seems to be how everyone has summed it up. It scratches the itch for a bit.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Preface that every review should inlcude: THIS IS NOT NOT ARKHAM GAME. There are similarities that resemble Arkham (3d brawler, combos, stealth and grapples) but at its core, its very different.Gotham Knights is pretty good when getting past the above. The gameplay is the biggest focus, and its pretty fluid once you get past the missing combo meter and focus more on racking up charge for your abilities and a more arcade-y feel. Gear and mods are alright, they provide a little bit of player builds to how you play, but at least in my experience were mostly passive changes. Otherwise the grind to get new gear is kinda boring when there are so little actual side missions, instead forcing you to replay the same infinite crimes around Gotham. But I was never "bored" playing this game. I played mainly as Red Hood as I liked his character story combined with the gameplay aspects. I played solo, but I'll probably try Nightwing next if I play through co-op at any point to add some replayability. I wish travelling Gotham was a bit faster, as the best way to get around I found was just grappling point to point and utilizing your special movement (for Red Hood, midair jumping??). The Batbike is outright worse. It needs a solid buff in speed to be even worth it. It's only mildly faster than your movement ability, but combined with grapple speed and being able to go across buildings, it's never worth it. But once you're either in the action or doing a special mission, the game is solid and fighting criminals in this 3d brawler style is still really fun.The story is pretty meh in my opinion. It's a lot more akin to a CW show vs a gritty Arkham feel. It feels especially bizarre to me the mood changes between scenes. At one point, its a grim moment, its everyone's dark (k)night of their soul, and there's no hope but they have to try. Then next scene, everyone's joking about making a mess of tomato sauce while making dinner in their Friends-esque headquarters. It's nothing offensive and there are some nice touches. Harley is really unique, I love what they do with her and make her the most developed villain in the game (she's only a side character sadly). A lot of the twists were too obvious, and I wished they stuck to things without spoiling things. I have a theory this game was originally a TMNT game that turned into a Batman game (or at least super heavy inspiration). "A teen-oriented story of 4 martial artist family members (the blue leader, purple tech savvy, yellow/orange underdog, and red violent edgelord) who were trained by a father-figure in a dark urban city fights groups of criminals who utilize goo to try to take over the world." If the story was a bit better written, I could see this be a much more well put-together game. The gameplay was always the thing that led me back, but I wish the gameplay was backed up by good characters/story.Overall I still recommend Gotham Knights cautiously. If you're a diehard Arkham fan and do not want to experiment with different gameplay styles, I really would not get this game. I love the Arkham games but accepting it isn't Arkham is mandatory to like this game lmao. Totally get it if you absolutely love comics or this style of superhero game then totally get it, but otherwise this is a solid game to get on sale or try for a free weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotham Knights is far from perfect, but is it fun playing this with my friend? Yes, even if it is filled with flaws.Between forced mouse acceleration, horrible movement, and combat controls that don’t often do what I want, I am constantly fighting with the controls. That is probably my biggest issue with the game. Things like jumping, dodging, stealth attacking, grapple hooking, and even just walking from A to B do not feel good and often do not do what the game tells you they should. The grapple hook is the worst offender. You get a marker showing you where you will grapple onto, but it only works 75% of the time. Quite often I will see a marker when I want to go, click the grapple hook button only for my character to shoot the hook somewhere that is both off-screen and behind me. A lot of things also share a keybinding, as if my keyboard is short on keys. For example, stealth attack and ranged attack are the same button. Often I will be sneaking behind an enemy, the game will prompt me to stealth attack, and then my character chooses to use the ranged attack and alert everyone.My second biggest issue is the speed. Everything is so slow. Your attacks take so long to animate that if an enemy starts an attack after you have clicked, you are pretty much getting hit and there's nothing you can do until you get farther in the game and get some upgrades. Their attack will happen before your animation can finish and it will take priority, sometimes leading to you being stun locked and dying. They can even cancel your ultimate attacks, which take extra long to animate. There are some perks you can get that somewhat alleviate this problem, but it never completely goes away. Your bat cycle is also super slow to the point that using your grapple hook would be faster if it wasn’t so buggy.I’m also not a fan of the map. It consists of 3 land masses separated by bridges. In lore this may be what Gotham looks like, but it does not make for fun gameplay, at least not without some better traversal. Anytime you want to switch parts without fast travelling, you need to slowly go to the far edges of the map to get a bridge, slowly cross it, and then slowly get to wherever you wanted to go. The map is also filled with bad objectives. For example, there is one where you need to run and grapple hook between blue lights in a certain amount of time. Sounds easy, but you’re going to need to fight with the grapple hook the whole way, so you’ll probably fail a few times, which is just frustrating.In terms of enemy design, there's only a handful of enemy types and the rest are just variants on them. Towards the end of the game you start having to fight these ninjas that teleport around and can disappear for 10s of seconds at a time, while also having a very high dodge chance. I don’t know who thought that was a good idea, but they are extremely annoying.The story is pretty good. You get to see several Batman villains, which is cool, and some of the levels and set pieces are pretty interesting, but I did find it hard to follow at times. Unfortunately, the game’s map sucks and it is never clear what you are supposed to be doing next to continue the story, but once you get into a story area, it is usually pretty fun.The game would be significantly better if it was not open world. Get rid of the open world. Get rid of the open world style quests. Just have you go directly from the hub area to the mission level areas like a linear game. The actual main story levels are usually pretty good. Nothing amazing, but they do have some cool locations.The performance is fine to bad. It’s not horrible, but it runs much worse than I would think it should be based on how it looks and performance gets worse the longer you play, but for the first bit after you open the game, it does run pretty decent.If you get this for cheap or in a bundle and have a friend to play with, go ahead, give it a try, it can be pretty fun and it definitely has a lot of potential. You can ignore most of the open world stuff and the controls are probably fixable if the developers want to spend time on that. I’m just not going to recommend anyone buy a game that is this flawed. Hopefully they can fix it because a lot of the issues sound like things that should be fixable to me. The core game isn’t bad.

I am purely going to talk about the gameplay and not the story or dialogue (you can judge that yourself everyone has different opinions on everything especially when it comes to narrative and story.)lets talk about the worst part of gameplay. Traversal. When they first showed it, it looked fun. Playing it is a different matter entirely.Parkour system is bassically.. just a few vaults and climbing and weird leaping that stops your character after landing.and you can't even vault over obstacles like, anything other than gates, railings it really stops the flow when you think you can vault over a trash can or a bench or even just a ventilation shaftsony's spiderman game did it right. Everything you saw that looked like an obstacle could be vaulted over. And it was smooth. Here.. not so much..EDIT: Tried it again after a few months, still as terrible as i remember, not to mention the performance is still just as bad.Overall the movement is clunky, buggy, and just feels not fun to jump around on rooftops. I am not even going to talk about grappling because that's how bad it feels. Again. Games like Arkham Knight had one of the best traversal systems, i know i should not compare the two, but its very clear that this game is inspired by arkham games.So that's how i feel about the movement and traversal.Now lets talk about the combat, i think its fine. nothing to write home about but sadly its the game's strongest point out of everything.It works, animations are fantastic especially for robin's moveset. The combat system could have used an actual counter mechanic like even ubisoft's recent AC games have good parry mechanics sure it would make the game easier but also that much more satisfying to deflect attacks using actual weapons. And it's only logical that a melee focused game should have some sort of a deflect mechanic, yes you can perfect dodge but it breaks the flow of combat completely and its a bit goofy to see superheroes dodge out of the way of the smallest attacks.Stealth:- it has stealth, it sort of works but the AI is very bad like skyrim bad.- there are smoke bombs, but you are limited to only use it if you want to escape while grappling away. You cannot throw it its an escape mechanism sort of like what amazing spider-man 1,2 did. Its bad.-silent takedowns are silent yes, but they take a long time so its very risky to use even when the other enemy isnt near you because by time the takedown is finnished he will walk towards you and immediately alert everyone.- absolutely zero versatility compared to Arkham. Not even a freaking corner takedown.- heroic takedowns are super nicely done in terms of animation and function but only Robin can takedown big goons- sometimes clunky with the mechanics but that's gotham knights for you.Some side notes:- Graphics are pretty good nothing to be hyped about- Map is huge, a bit too huge for your character's movement speed and it feels very dead at times. it doesnt feel like gotham at all because you don't hear gunfire in the distance, or police sirens or anything that would resemble the crime infested city we all know and love. Even Arkham Knight had more life to the city and the game starts with everyone leaving the city but the criminals.- OST is fine-ish, nothing compares to Arkham's ambient music while free-roaming. Here its a lot more.. marvel like? Its a lot less moody is what im saying. And the bike's theme should never have been added that ♥♥♥♥ needs to go im serious WB! no i am serious, worst part is that the bike is slow and you have to hear the theme everytime you ride it. It feels like the start of a mobile game ad.- Performance has improved a lot. Like a lot. But its still very much DENUVO stuttery like. If they'd remove that, we'd get stable frames im sure. Techland removed denuvo after a year, WB better remove it too. (performance definetly improved since last review 2024)TLDR:- If you never played Arkham games you might like this game- If you enjoy sekiro like mechanics this game isnt for you.- If you love stealth this game is not for you.- If you enjoyed arkham games this game will dissapoint you because you won't be able to NOT compare the two.- If you like the batfamily this game isnt for you. it doesnt feel like that at all.- game is 5/10 because main elements that you use are broken, and not fun and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bike's theme song drives me nuts but i still finnished it without crying myself to sleep.Aight, buy or don't I could not care less and it seems like neither does WB.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally 8/10, writing this as I've just completed all achievements overall i think this game is worth especially if you love Batman/Gotham. I caution that its biggest hindrance is optimization/crashes. if you have low tolerance to these problems avoid till patched.simply put this isn't the typical superhero game we all know from the past decade, its closer to that of condensed Assassins Creed game with drop in co-op play. optimization is all over the place, I've had great luck with a medium-high end machine maybe 5-7 crashes in my total playtime frames drop when moving quickly either on the bat-cycle or using traversal skills. While others i know are crashing frequently.-Story honestly pretty predicable and a little shallow overall. Huge potential diving into the court of owls with all the families that we could've investigated, but instead we immediately find the voice/leader. Overall even with its pacing flaws the story is quite enjoyable. The ending however is rough honestly it feels like a full circle of what we started with at the beginning definitely wish it was handled different. Paves the way for DLC which I hope  they can pull off and we get proper investigations into the court of owls, and the rise of other villains thinking Gotham is free game with the Bat dead. -CombatQuite good, it takes a moment to get used to combat. Its honestly closer to what you would find in the newer Assassins creed games. I believe the idea of this game being clunky is because of how dodge seems to have no invincibility frames and getting into the groove of timed attacks since it helps pick up your attack speed. Panic dodging has a tendency to get people killed as tracking isn't always lost on the dodge animation. It actually takes correct timing to dodge especially on with chain attacks/multi-hits. One of the biggest things I've enjoyed is that with a semi-good build even on hard no one is an actual bullet sponge. Each character feels different and potential for multiple builds on each character. I do hope we get some QoL updates dealing with the amount of crafting recipes, mods fusing and hopefully dismantling some mods. As it gets tedious in NG+ with the amount of stuff we acquire trying to find our god rolled gear.-Co-opA big selling point for this game, and its quite good. The fact we can be on the complete opposite ends of the map doing separate things is awesome. Missions are synced so you can keep progress when you decide to go solo. -MusicNot bad, not the most memorable, outside the time trial and the lounge music enjoyable-Gotham/Atmosphere City looks great I find the change in design to be a good direction. the different architectural design is by far my favorite version of Gotham yet. The enclosed spaces are immaculately designed, some serious creepy vibes.

_childDocuments_.review: ### **Title: Gotham Knights: A Disappointing Dive into Gotham's Shadows****Rating: ★★☆☆☆ (2/5)****Review:***Gotham Knights*, developed by WB Games Montreal, promised an exciting new chapter in the Batman universe, focusing on the next generation of heroes after the apparent death of Bruce Wayne. However, while the game introduces intriguing concepts and a rich environment, it ultimately falls short due to numerous gameplay issues, lackluster storytelling, and technical shortcomings. This review will delve into the game’s mechanics, narrative, visuals, and overall experience.### **Gameplay Mechanics****Combat System:**The combat in *Gotham Knights* is one of its most significant letdowns. While it attempts to replicate the fluidity of the previous *Arkham* games, it feels clunky and uninspired.- **Repetitive Combat:** Players engage in button-mashing combat that lacks depth. Each character has unique abilities, but the overall feel is monotonous, with enemies showing little variety in their attack patterns.- **Character Switching:** While the ability to switch between characters like Nightwing, Batgirl, Red Hood, and Robin is a promising feature, it is poorly executed. The transition feels more like a gimmick than a meaningful addition to the gameplay. Each character doesn’t feel distinct enough, making it hard to develop a connection with any of them.**Leveling and Progression:**The RPG elements feel tacked on rather than integrated into the core gameplay.- **Skill Trees and Gear:** The skill trees are overly simplistic and don’t provide a satisfying sense of progression. Gear upgrades are often tedious, requiring players to grind for materials in repetitive missions that feel uninspired.- **Difficulty Scaling:** The game employs an open-world structure with a leveling system that often feels unbalanced. Players may find themselves over-leveled or under-leveled for certain missions, leading to frustrating encounters that disrupt the flow of gameplay.### **Storytelling and Characterization****Weak Narrative:***Gotham Knights* suffers from a lack of a compelling story. The premise, which revolves around the aftermath of Batman’s death and the rise of new heroes, feels underdeveloped.- **Generic Plot:** The narrative follows a predictable path with little to no surprises. The antagonists lack depth, and the overarching plot does not provide enough motivation for players to remain engaged.- **Character Development:** While the game attempts to flesh out its main characters, the writing falls flat. Dialogue often feels forced, and character arcs lack the nuance needed to create genuine emotional investment. The heroes’ relationships feel superficial, diminishing their potential impact on the story.### **Visual Design and Technical Issues****Mixed Visuals:**While the game features some beautiful environments, they are often marred by inconsistent graphics and character models.- **Performance Problems:** Many players report technical issues, including frame rate drops, glitches, and bugs that disrupt the experience. These issues can be particularly frustrating in a game that requires precise timing in combat.- **Inconsistent Art Style:** The artistic direction lacks cohesion, with character designs that feel disjointed from the overall aesthetic of Gotham. Environments are richly detailed, but character models often look bland and unpolished.### **Sound Design and Voice Acting****Lackluster Audio:**The sound design is another area where *Gotham Knights* fails to impress.- **Generic Soundtrack:** The music score lacks the intensity and memorability of previous entries in the *Batman* franchise. It often fades into the background, failing to enhance key moments.- **Voice Acting:** While the voice cast includes talented actors, the delivery feels inconsistent. Character interactions can come off as wooden, further detracting from the emotional weight of the story.### **Co-op Features and Online Play****Co-op Experience:**The game introduces a co-op mode, allowing players to team up with friends, but this feature feels underutilized.- **Limited Cooperative Mechanics:** While the concept is appealing, the execution is flawed. There are few meaningful cooperative gameplay elements, which can make the experience feel like a missed opportunity.- **Connection Issues:** Players have reported connectivity problems when trying to engage in online play, leading to frustrations that detract from the overall enjoyment.### **Conclusion***Gotham Knights* had the potential to be a standout title in the DC universe, but it ultimately stumbles in key areas. The repetitive gameplay, lack of a compelling narrative, and technical issues overshadow its positive aspects. While the concept of exploring Gotham with a new generation of heroes is intriguing, the execution leaves much to be desired.For fans of the Batman franchise, this game may feel like a disappointing entry in an otherwise stellar series. While there are moments of fun to be had, they are often overshadowed by the game’s shortcomings. *Gotham Knights* is best approached with tempered expectations, as it struggles to live up to the legacy of its predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's get this part out of the way; **The Stability Issues that people are complaining about are 100% Valid! If you want to have a good experience with this game, my advice, run it in Medium res. It is still beautiful and you will have no where the issues that others do.**Also, No, this is Not an Arkham game, do not expect that style of combat. This is a different Team of Devs, a different universe and a very different style of game play. This is an Action RPG. Some mechanics do work better then others. I wasn't expecting combat to be as good as it is to be honest. Stealth works very well, but the auto lock tends to get weird at times, at the last second, example "Tap Y to Stealth Take Down" you do it, and all of the sudden the character does a ranged attack instead of the button prompt. Movement and traversing the environment with the grappling hook is very clunky, however. You can't just aim the grappling hook at a ledge, you have to swivel the camera until the abysmal auto target finds a place to highlight. This may or may not be the location you wanted. Getting stuck on the environment is also a thing, if the characters foot hits a rock or anything really, it will halt movement. Trying to do grab take downs can become a chore if there any boxes or walls near you. The prompt will display but nothing will happen regardless how much you spam 'X'. So, you need to relocate the enemy to a more open area.I bought the game, thought I would put in an hour or so, and more then likely just refund it. From the Opening cut scene on, I was hooked. Unfortunately, the story (which starts out very strong) turns rather cliche and boring by Chapter 6. A lot of the story revolves around the Bat Family and how they are trying to deal with the lose of Batman, at times it can be very hard hitting, I think even more so now because of the recent lose of the real Batman, Kevin Conroy (R.I.P). The End Game and Final Chapters feel... lazy. Very uninspired, and even though the game offers a New Game Plus, I refuse to run threw all those endless monologues and the ridiculous ending again. Just no lol, once was enough. The SIDE Stories though, they involve Clayface, Harley Quinn and Mr Freeze, and are absolutely wonderful, just far more enjoyable then the main questline. The Clayface fight is nothing short of epic.Each member of the team plays very different and you can switch when ever you like, just go back to base, switch then hit the streets. The combo system for everyone is different and feels right for that character. It is very nice, once you get it down, I do recommend taking advantage of the different training scenarios as they become available. They help a lot. Stealth take downs and final hit animations, grapple strikes all look so clean. It's just very pleasing to look at... when it works.One feature they show very early and probably one of my most favorite, is the side quest system. Once you step out of the base to start doing missions, you have the Main Mission then a list of just randomly generated crimes, gangs to take down, robberies, hostages all kinds of stuff. Now lets say you do alll the side missions and you still just do not feel like doing the main mission yet. Go back to base. Step in, then back out and Presto! A New List of randomly generated crimes to take on. It is endless, you never run out of things to do, which is a good way to take a break in between Chapters.Customization takes a moment to get into, you can unlock skins that are not customizable, and versions of those skins that improve stats and can be customized. Crafting gear is 'meh', always looking to improve those stats, as you would in any rpg, but the mechanic is bland and you eventually just get an inventory full of garbage schematics that you can't get ride of. Can't even destroy them. They just pill up and there are Zero options for inventory management.The map of Gotham is massive! It's all of Gotham, not just a large chunk, but the whole city, like in DC Universe Online. There is so much to explore and interact with. Lore from the universe to just get lost in, especially if you are a fan of the comics. Historical locals, audio logs, there is a lot of love and attention to detail in this game. The things that work are awesome, but the stuff that doesn't is actually abysmal. There doesn't seem to be much middle ground.I know I may get some clown awards for all of this because there are aggressive haters and defenders of this game right now. I can't help but to stand in the middle. What works, works very well, what doesn't, made me hate the time I had to spend dealing with it. I do think it is a good superhero game, but frankly there are a lot better ones out there. I would give this game a Neutral rating if Steam allowed such, but since they don't, I'll say that FOR ME the game is a 6/10, and that's only because of the side stories and the combat. I would, however, recommend waiting on a sale. The game is by no means worth full price.My recommendation. You know Steam will refund you if the game has been played less then 2 hours, so if you are a fan of the universe, give it a go. Set you an alarm on your phone for an hour and forty five minutes. If the game doesn't drag you in, uninstall and get a refund. If you get into the combat and the portrayal of the characters, you may want to keep it to scratch that superhero itch. Either way, you can't loose by giving it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I got through the main story, did plenty of side activities, but I still can't come away recommending this game in its current state. Maybe if it gets fixed down the line it'll be worth a recommendation, but this game is barely held together.The story in this game doesn't have much going on. It starts off on the right foot by killing Batman, but nothing else in the story really sticks its landing or has a lasting impact. There are villain side stories that all fall short and aren't interesting. The random crimes that the villains' factions are tied to don't have any effect on the story outside of adding a few grindy activities you have to do to access those story missions. None of what's going on is interesting, and nothing you do feels like it matters, because the same batch of predetermined crimes pop right back up with the same exact factions. I get Gotham is literally supposed to be a place with more monthly crimes than human population, but it makes the game feel like progression goes nowhere and it doesn't matter what do you, which hurts the story.I played Batgirl because she's the least obnoxious of the four playable characters, and while her dialogue typically wasn't terrible, her voice actor really didn't sound like she was giving an A+ effort. While her voice actor has limited video game work experience, she has done plenty of work before, so it's disappointing to have almost all of Batgirl's dialogue come through in the same tone of voice. It also draws attention to the mediocre writing when the delivery isn't great.The gameplay itself works, but for as padded as this game is, it gets repetitive after a while. Having a counter system instead of a dodge would have made everything flow and feel better, but outside of some enemies that are way too spongy, the combat works well enough. You punch bad guys and bad guys eventually get knocked out. Pretty standard stuff.The gliding is horrendous though. I don't know if the person in charge of the gliding was on a GTA kick and decided that flying needs to feel as awkward and annoying as possible, but they succeeded if that was the goal. The Batcycle works much better, and the time challenges for that are even fun (if a bit easy), but I always found it way more efficient to just use my grappling hook to move where I needed to.Honestly, the game at its core isn't nearly as bad as people make it out to be. It's a live service game without the financial exploitation, which is weird, but there are games that are a lot worse at their cores. The gameplay does its job, the costume variety is cool, enemy variety is decent enough, and I felt that I used every ability I had pretty regularly.But no matter how fun the game can be at times, I can't recommend a game with this many performance issues. If it wasn't dropping to a 2-4 FPS range randomly in the middle of a fight, it was crashing when I was navigating Gotham. In 30 hours of gameplay, I crashed at least 20 times, often in the middle of one of those AWFUL organ harvesting crimes. With a 3070 Ti laptop GPU, i7-12700H processor, and 32GB of RAM, these kinds of performance issues and crashes just aren't acceptable. Reducing my settings down to medium or lower didn't help in the slightest.If the game gets fixed down the line, it could be worth a recommendation at a discount, but Gotham Knights absolutely needed more time in the oven before launching.

_childDocuments_.review: "Gotham Knights" needs a hotfix / major patch ASAP. That won't surprise you if you've played... well, any game within the first week of it's launch in the last decade. Frame rate issues, stuttering, crashing - I've experienced all of this on every quality preset / resolution. Right now, the game can't go above 30 FPS without stuttering. There's a major optimization issue here. Not surprising, as Batman: Arkham Knight had a disastrous PC launch (but the issues were eventually fixed).Technical issues aside, I've enjoyed my time with Gotham Knights so far. I honestly wasn't having fun with it at first, but after trying out all of the available characters - I settled on Red Hood and I've been having a good time playing as him. I definitely recommend trying out each individual character before writing the game off completely, because they are vastly different and cater to different play-styles. I also had to stop myself from comparing the game to the Arkham series, and other superhero games. This game is not as polished as something like "Spider-Man" by Insomniac, which is literally the gold standard of superhero action-adventure games (to me, at least). But take this with a grain of salt, because I'm an idiot who likes pretty much every open world game (I even enjoyed Crackdown 3). I can't recommend purchasing it for it's launch price, wait until the game hits $30. By that point, the issues will (hopefully) be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing on a 2070 Super at 1440p for reference:I feel like all the reviews out there are for lower end rigs or highest end rigs so I wanted to offer my experience playing the game so far- Tweaking some of the settings after looking up an article, I'm achieving between 60-90 frames in the open world and 144fps in enclosed environments. I know that sounds like it is insane dips (because it is), but that honestly hasn't diminished my fun factor. The game has some very slight stutters in the streets but nowhere near the level I have seen from PS5 and YT'bers reviewing the game. The game is also super nice looking and I am probably the only person that thinks this, but I'm glad they went with a less gritty art style than the arkham games because for the 100th time, this is NOT that game. Crafting is another point of contention, but its literally equipping the highest number stats.... just like any other RPG but even simpler lol. It doesn't NEED to be there but it breaks up the gameplay a little and I like that!I haven't even finished the main campaign (I think I'm almost to chapter 3 of 8), but I have been having fun running around the city fighting crime and leveling each of the 4 heroes between story beats and side cases. As far as combat and open world crimes being reported as redundant, I would kind of argue some of the biggest open world games are full of repetition (looking at AC, specifically Valhalla) but I still logged 100+ hours on those because they were still fun!Is this game perfect? No. Is it worth $60? mmmm probably not. Is it fun and enjoyable on my hardware? Absolutely! I do want the game to be better optimized before people start jumping in to play it though... I'm soloing the game for my first playthrough but hoping to get friends to join for the next round! So I recommend this to any Batfan that has the ability to run it and on sale (or until optimized for all to enjoy)

_childDocuments_.review: Gotham Knights is a very solid Batman game. It introduces some cool new mechanics that differ from the Arkham Series and lets you play as the four key members of the bat-family. Each characters abilities are fun to use and they all bring something new to the table. Also, the customisation really is something special. There is a large variety of cosmetics to equip as well as slick looking gear to mix and match. The story is quite good, introducing the Court Of Owls who haven't been seen before in a Batman game. The inclusion of old foes is also a bonus. Each boss fight is generally quite awesome. There's some great background music and each boss improves upon the one before. While the boss fights are quite simple, they really go all out and big scale as they were trying to make up for the lack of bosses in Batman Arkham Knight. However, Gotham Knights can improve upon a lot of things. The combat is very bland and basic being a step down from the Arkham games which is quite upsetting considering the legendary mechanics of those games. Each character has the exact same move-sets. All you do is press the attack button, dodge and then occasionally do a special move which really isn't that special. The combat is a lot slower which makes the game have less enemies. The grappling is honestly atrocious, it feels so delayed. The momentum abilities for each character could've been done a lot better. Gotham Knights does have some good elements, but it certainly doesn't live up to the Arkham Games standards. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to state that this is my first ever review I've written simply because this game could have been so good but lacks in important departments. The concept of the game is great. It really has that Gotham hero feel that mentioned. Crafting is simple and easy to understand. Co-op is an amazing feature in this game. Truly amazing. Now for the cons. My main problems with this game is the mechanics and graphics. I have everything at low and still can't manage to have a consistent 60 frames. Even without graphical problems, the mechanics are extremely bothersome. It seems as though there is an input lag regards of the settings. V-Sync off, Low Latency on, Graphics Low, and yet still can't seem to get a good response for my controls. Perfect dodges are weird because if I time it, what I would assume to be perfect, I get no dodge. However if I'm early, I get a mixture of a normal dodge or perfect dodge. Additionally, the random moments of when it just does not read my controls for a split second. For instance, walking into vents are hard when my character walks past it half the time. I think if mechanics, alone, were to be fixed, this game would be better. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------For people with ADHD or who simply wants a quick read: Pros:-  Co-op is amazing and feels unlimiting.-  Crafting is easy to understand. Cons:-  Mechanics have input lag.    ( Regardless if you're on controller or keyboard ) -  Random moments of not reading your inputsEdit: Taking damage while doing takedowns feels very unfair. Getting stealth takedowns feel impossible, even with the prompt, my character ends up chucking a batarang to their face instead which is annoying. Glitches - random cars that think that they're Barry Allen as they speed across your screen. Regardless of area ( Inside, Outside, In the Sky, Underground) Graphics - Getting a smooth 60 frames feels impossible. ( I do want to say that I have a 1660. However, on any other game, the lowest settings has always been a guaranteed 60 - 165 frames. )In my opinion, I feel like it's just poorly optimized. I tried as much as I can not to talk about aspects of the game that seems as though it could have been the intention of the game. ( but getting hit while doing a takedown is still crazy to me ) If these were to be fixed, I feel like this game would be a 5 star game. _childDocuments_.review: Very surprising indeed! When this game released I took a gander at the reviews and decided that the game was not worth my time or money. However, I recently acquired this game in the WB100 humble bundle and wow, it is so much better than everyone else said! You should buy this game! It's not groundbreaking but it's good fun and the multiplayer co-op is even better. Here are my big takeaways:Pros+Decent story.+Fast gameplay.+Non complicated puzzles and stages.+Incredible looking outfits for the characters.+Beautiful graphics for Gotham City.+You can play as Nightwing.+You can play as Red Hood.+You can play as Batgirl.+You can play as Red Robin.Cons-Story is overall kind of disjointed. I said it was decent but there are some moments that really make you feel like there was so much missed potential. We get emails from Superman and Wonder Woman but they never show up. I would have liked for them to have made an appearance. -Gameplay can be monotonous. Attack, attack, attack, heavy attack. Ranged attack combo. Etc. The momentum moves do break up the monotony but overall it's like pokemon with different inputs. -Stealth is lame. There's no point to doing a stealth run unless you are challenging yourself. Personally this doesn't bother me because I hate stealth (takes too long), but the options for sneaking around are very limited. -Side quests are lame. I wish they added world bosses to the map or some other dynamic event instead of goons raiding a truck or robbing a bank every single time. -Batcycle is quickly made irrelevant thanks to individual character traversal abilities. Nightwing can fly, Robin can teleport, Red Hood can skip through the sky, and Batgirl glides. These are way better means of getting around Gotham than riding the batcycle. -Crafting is truly pointless. You get better gear as you play so it doesn't make sense to craft anything. Just delete for materials and move on. Overall, it's not a perfect game, but it is a ton of fun - especially in Co-Op! I've experienced crashes on the Steam Deck, but none on PC. The story had some funny, cringe, and sad moments. I love the Bat Family and this game made my day. I'll probably play it again after beating it to unlock the other endings. I'd give it a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: When this game first launched, it received a fair amount of criticism, some of which was warranted. However, I have genuinely enjoyed my experience with it. I've played the game on PS5, Steam, and even the SteamDeck, where, despite lower graphics quality, it still performs well. The game also runs smoothly on PC. Fans of Batman and the characters he associates with will likely appreciate the engaging storyline.One of the standout features of the game is the ability to play as various characters, such as Robin, whom I favor. Each character offers a distinct playing experience, so I encourage you to try them all and find the one that best suits your playstyle. The gameplay loop is enjoyable, albeit not groundbreaking. There is a continuous stream of crime to combat and random encounters that offer enough variety to keep things fresh for quite some time. Additionally, Gotham City is filled with hidden treasures to discover, and the city itself is visually stunning, especially when played on a good graphics card.While I wish the story had more depth, I still found it to be a lot of fun. In fact, I enjoyed it so much that I achieved a platinum trophy on PS5. I initially purchased the PC version to play on my SteamDeck while bedridden, but my experience with the game has shown me that it's better than critics initially made it out to be. As a self-proclaimed comics nerd with a soft spot for Robin and Nightwing, I would even go as far as to say that this was my favorite game of 2022, if I am allowed to embrace the nostalgia bias.Comparisons to the Arkham games are inevitable, but one of the key differences between the two (aside from gameplay, as this game doesn't attempt to mimic the Arkham series) is how this game captures the relentless "grind" that Gotham's vigilantes endure. Crime is incessant, and the game does an excellent job of conveying that reality. Arkham games were all on "one night" and so it was a different feel. This game can have unlimited nights. In conclusion, I would highly recommend this game to fans of action RPGs or Batman and the Batfamily. Give it a chance, and you might find that it's far more enjoyable than many YouTube reviews would lead you to believe.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels more like a product than a game. It has no redeeming qualities. The live service-ness is on full display, from mission design to progression to EULAs and privacy policies.The first thing you get in this game is a privacy policy. You cannot decline it and play offline. (Blocking with firewall works to be clear) There's a button for it, but it just redirects to an empty website. I have read that it is only functional in U.S.. Idiocy.The next ridiculous thing you will see is the plot hole ridden story. There's so much stupid stuff that has to happen for the story to happen. Voice acting sometimes sounds like the actors are trying too hard to act, sounds fake at times.The gameplay is no better. My biggest critique here are the controls and movement. Movement feels surprisingly unresponsive, in many cases your character just refuses to move at all despite mashing buttons. This is most noticeable near walls/obstacles, you get stuck on them, and when hanging off of ledges as well as sitting on posts, the character just refuses to go anywhere at all a lot of the time.The open world feels quite dead, besides some random activities to fight some guys and pointless collectibles, there is no other exploration. No puzzles, no unique loot hidden somewhere, nothing like that, nothing to explore really.Controls are quite bad as well, as is common for console ports, specifically keys for dodge/crouch/climb up ledge, etc. There are also a few cases of buttons sharing different actions, so you end up activating what you did not intend, specifically ranged attacks and stealth takedown having the same button.The graphics are good, despite what some people might say, but I do not consider graphics a good reason to play this.Finally there's the live service-ish progression. It feels gutted, like the entire loot system was an afterthought. All of the loot feels extremely pointless, all the icons look extremely similar to the point of making it literally impossible to tell what you are getting. and when getting items for other characters, there's absolutely no indication which character the loot was for. There are basically 2 unique variations of items you get: elemental bonus or crit bonus. Similar thing for "mods". That's it. That's all the "build variety" you get. Funniest thing is that you mostly get elemental buildup mods, and weapons with elemental effects are rare.The crafting system feels like its there just to be there, and to stretch out the "end-game" grind. Oh and the end-game is also quite "amazing", it's basically just rooms of enemies with maybe 3 objective variations. It feels very hollow and pointless, especially because of the aforementioned crappy loot system.There is some amount of customization, and thankfully it is free, requiring in-game time to unlock. If I remember correctly its 14 costumes per character plus some color customization.This is just a fundamentally flawed game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are expecting the Arkham experience here, you will be disappointed. This isn't it. A better comparison will be for eg. Marvel's Spiderman Remastered (on Steam) or The Division 2. Gotham Knights is an open world action RPG. It has serviceable skill trees for each hero. All 4 play differently and are unique in their own way. There is crime everywhere and it encourages exploration via collectibles and discovering more enemies to beat up for better loot.The story : Engaging, has a mystery to it as you dig into Batman's last case. Plenty of cutscenes and objects/clues to interact with in the world that are easter eggs to the DC franchise. Each Knight has their own unique cutscenes, interaction and this experience is better in co-op when the knights talk to one another as well. Gameplay : After finishing the main story, there are several sidequests. A bike minigame is available to unlock skins. But more importantly, Gotham Knights offers a New Game Plus (NG+) mode, pushing the level cap from 30 to 40. The skill tree can be maxed out as well by completing collectibles, and allowing you to unlock suit transmogs, giving insentive to do these challenges.Seamless drop in drop out coop is also available. The endgame gameplay loop involves you doing high level crimes, collecting clues, then calling it a night back at base before heading out the next day to grind tougher missions that give a higher chance for legendary gears. Since there is no tethering in coop, the world feels alive with another player gliding as batgirl or roaming the streets in a batcycle as you hear red hoods gunfire echo nearby. Cookie points for :1) Cops showing up at the crime scene after it has been cleared out. Staying at the scene will lead to cops attacking you and attempting to take you down.2) Team takedowns and cooperative stealth action Drawbacks : Game is not well optimized. Framerates dip. Gear is a bit lacklustre especially mods. Needs fine tuning. Tldr, Gotham Knights is an engaging open world action rpg. If the devs can pull a Division 2 with this by introducing seasonal manhunt targets, more content, more gear sets, and expand upon the world they have built, this will easily be a highly recommended game from me. November will see the introduction of a new 4 player coop mode (30 floors with enemies to beat up) but only time will tell if the devs can step it up and polish this gem in the rough.

In order to grapple where you want, you have to carefully adjust the camera and pay close attention to where the grapple target is, which ruins the flow of movement.- The batcycle is INCREDIBLY slow. it's somewhere around 35 mph... I guess entire Gotham is a school zone now?**Combat:**Combat is very basic and sluggish. There's just no combat flow, you just bash on enemies until they're knocked out, and dodge when there's a clear indication to dodge. All of it happening at a very slow pace. You can also perform finisher-style moves, where your character performs a special animation on an enemy - however other enemies will still walk up and attack during those animations, and you're stuck in the animation unable to dodge. Normally in these kind of games, those moves should be safe to perform.Fighting is neither fun, satisfying, nor challenging.**Objective:**I've only played little over 2 hours, but during that time the game has felt rather directionless. It's been "go out and find random goons and fight them", which then triggered the story to progress. Most of my playtime so far has been aimlessly driving through the city on a granny-bike at 35 MPH and fighting generic thugs, and watching some cutscenes when I'm told to go back to the headquarters. There were times when I wasn't sure what I was supposed to be doing, and had to take time to go through menus and read what I had to do to progress. It's not a big problem, but unexpected from a modern game to not receive a clear objective.**Graphics and performance:**Graphics look nice, but performance is terrible. While I managed to get a solid 60 FPS most of the time, I could tell that the game was poorly optimized when moving through the city. I don't think they've optimized loading, so when the game tries to dynamically load and unload areas, it starts stuttering. This results in frame drops and audio stuttering. (this happened with the game installed on an SSD)My guess is that this is why the batcycle drives so slow - driving faster would mean more loading/unloading, which the game just can't handle.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotham Knights is definitely a good game. Well written story,the four playable characters are neat and well fleshed out with their own stories and very different play styles. Graphics, effects and music are all very decent and the game is generally fun to play. The game has a lot of potential if developed further and gets some good DLC. However its lacking in many ways. First its way too short. Main story finished with all other case files done, all collectables done. Started NG+, level up to 40, done all side quests again, finished main story again, done all characters story quests, unlocked all momentum abilities on all chars and maxed out all skilltrees. All done in my first 40 hours of game play. Only looking for a handful of Gotham's most wanted and that's it.Huge difference between first playthrough and NG+ as well. On first playthrough your characters are low level and dont have decent enough gear. So particularly the boss fights can be very annoying and test your patience. Particularly Clayface and Freeze took forever cause i was barely able to damage them at my level and with my gear. On NG+ at Level 40 with legendary gear the same bosses require little more than just clicking your mouse buttons a few times.Another downside is the open world. Gotham looks beautiful. By the the best Gotham ever in any game so far. So much details. Just no reason to travel around much. You travel to a fast travel point and from there traverse to the next crime scene. rinse and repeat. Yes there are around 120 different collectables in the game but you stumble across them randomly and without guides some of them are almost impossible to find. There is just nothing else to do in this beautifully designed game world. Seems a waste that the devs put so much effort effort into designing Gotham when there is no real reason to spend any time looking around.Unfortunately there are many other gamebreaking issues as well. Frequent CTD's. Completely random. Walk down a road. Crash, Attack an enemy. Crash. Use a fast travel point. Crash. Do nothing. Crash. Sometimes no crash in 6 or 7 hours. Sometimes crash after 3 mins in the game. Still the case after latest patch today (07/11) even tho patch note says many crash issues have been addressed. And at least for me the Baterang Collectable issue (and therefore the associated achievement) is buggy. Have them all collected but the game did not unlock the suit that comes with it and neither did i get the achievement.Also the game lacks many basic QOL features. Cant customise transmog suits? Why? Whats the point of unlocking transmog suits when the all look the same in game? And how about mass deconstruction of unused armours/weapons etc? Its super tedious to deconstruct every unused item in your inventory individually. Same goes for armour and weapon mods. Once you reached endgame you only go for FOXmods anyway. Let us deconstruct anything we don't need. Or at least let us fuse mods beyond epic rarity. List of blueprints grows and grows and grows... Even tho most of them are complete trash and obsolete. Very tedious to scroll through them after every night to check out whats new and if there is anything thats better than current gear. We need an option to delete obsolete blueprints.Upgradeable traversals would also be epic. Like investing crafting mats to improve batgirl's glide speed, robins teleport timer etc. same for the batcycle. increaseable speed, manoeuvrability and acceleration etc. Would also be awesome if you could change characters "on the fly" rather than only in the belfry.Would still recommend the game. Its mega fun to play and has huge potential for future DLC's and hopefully the upcoming 4 player MP but in its current state it's not worth the money. Too short, too many bugs and crashes and the UI is probably the worst I seen in a £60 game.

_childDocuments_.review: An okay-ish game that got pushed out of the bird's nest way too soon. I've beaten the main story along with the side cases and despite what fun I did manage to have the issues with this game were still very persistent. To leave this review simple and clean here's a pros and cons list of Gotham Knights.TL;DRDon't waste your $60 or more on this game like I did. Wait for a major price drop, sale or go buy any of the batman related games on steam cause you're not missing out with this title.Pros:- Decent story, despite being predictable from the beginning and until the very end- Portrays the bat family as an actually family which just gives off good vibes- The unique skills and abilities are pretty fun to mess around with for each character- Gotham looks fantastic and is a treat to explore, especially for DC fans- Cutscenes and some sequences are pretty well done- Most craftable and transmog outfits and styles look greatCons:- Certain enemies completely ignore grabs which can ruin the point of certain skill (Particularly for Red Hood as he's the only one I've played so far).- The game struggles to load different sections of Gotham and will freeze you in place-The game has a pretty decent chance of crashing several times when travelling to the Belfry or other parts of Gotham whether on foot or with the glider-Multiplayer is almost unplayable because it puts massive strain on the host which double the amount of loading lag and chances of crashing- Other players have collisions so you can easily get blocked into places-Bosses are kind of generic and don't really feel fun to fight against-The boss' story conclusions are lackluster and unsatisfying leaving you with more questions then answers-The driving is horrible. Avoid it as much as possible because the faster you go the more frames you lose.-The story plot is decent, but it does have cringe-worthy parts to it-There's no freedom to the customization. You'll end up most likely going with gear that has higher stats rather than enjoying experimenting with different gear mods that can mix up your playstyle and builds.-The transmog system is okay, but also very bad. You can equip a transmog style over any of your suits, however these transmogs themselves cannot be customized. You're only allowed to customize the suits that offer you stats so if you don't have that particular suit in your inventory or haven't unlocked by finding it's blueprint and crafting it, you won't be able to use that specific style let alone change its default colors.-The npc's have really repetitive voice lines and tend to get annoying-Some missions are a slog to play through. For example, to unlock fast travels you need to go scan survey drones up close. The thing is some of them have a shield that you can't scan through so you have to sit and wait up to a couple minutes for it decide to dock and recharge its shields. Just one of these has a chance to keep you there for around 10 minutes.-The ending of this game has tons of plot holes and quite frankly doesn't make sense.-In the trailer for the game, they've showed off what looks like team synchronized combos, but there really isn't anything of the sort in here. Me and my pal were mostly fending for ourselves and there's no options to sync our attacks to make a cool combo.-This game doesn't know whether it wants to be a singleplayer or multiplayer game. All the cutscenes will take the point of view of whatever bat kid you play as even in multiplayer. The other bat kids are simply not there, on other patrols or back at the Belfry. This only adds more plot holes to the story and makes the experience seem more lonely then what was originally advertised.-The base price of this game is overpriced, especially for the $80 I put into it being the gullible fanboy I am. This game should honestly be around $40 and as for the deluxe maybe around $50. They tease somewhat of a cliffhanger to open the path to a future expansion, but they have no right to do so since we're going on day 4 still awaiting a launch patch.-New game plus isn't worth the time and adds nothing to the game except making the enemies even more tankier.Conclusion:Believe it or not, I did enjoy this game somewhat and the time I spent on it, but the deeper I got the more of a chore the game became. I didn't even get to experience my first playthrough how I originally wanted to. Was really pumped about playing Gotham Knights with my pal, but didn't get to do so until the third day where me and him had already individually beaten the game. Talk about a serious let down and for that reason all of the ones above I cannot recommend this game to anyone.
