_childDocuments_.review: This is the worst game out of the entire Batman series. I have now played the game as entirely as I could before giving this review to be as accurate and unemotional as possible. Stay far away from this game if you hate games that revolve around loot grinding, have very poor game controls, poorly implemented game mechanics, and force you to fight the same 6 enemies over and over the entire game - just with different skins and different looking attack colors. 1. Loot grinding & hero skills grinding: Till your eyeballs bleed - thats all the game is about and all end game is2. The batman games have historically had very frustrating controls and poorly implemented action button design. This is the same here only worse. Your action buttons will change what you do on the fly and often change if a target moves even slightly. Additionally the game uses the tried and failed mechanic of "if 1 enemy is alerted, every single enemy on the entire map is also instantly alerted, even if the 1st enemy didn't have a change to verbally alert anyone or make any noises before taken down."3. During your first 1 hour of game play, you will have fought every single enemy in the rest of the game. The only difference will be the enemy appearance. They use the same moves, the same weapons, the same tactics, and even say the same things. The only thing different (which was most likely implemented to hide the lack of enemy variety) is to justify the same characters having slightly different graphics - they implemented different elemental effects. This doesn't change much for the enemies but means you will have to grind out every single set of armor, melee weapons, and ranged weapons in the different elements to do damage. ALL OPEN WORLD LOCATIONS SPAWN AT THE EXACT SAME LOCATIONS WITH THE ENEMIES IN THE EXACT SAME LOCATION - Once you've completed an open world spawnable mission you'll just be replaying the same 12 open world missions over and over and over. The only thing that changes sometimes is the location - but the EXACT positioning of enemies is the same always. ZERO fresh fights.4. Poor controls: I've mentioned some issues above, but in addition the game often becomes unresponsive with inputs, causing you to not attack when directed, not move when directed, and not do special moves when directed. It appears that this is more prevalent the larger the group of enemies in the area there are.5. Constantly getting stuck in the environment and having to fail missions & events. There are 3 very specific building assets that (if you're unlucky enough to grappling hook to) instantly stick you INSIDE of the asset, with no way of getting out of it. You either die, falling through the game, or have to teleport to a different location from the map selection screen.6. The character design very obviously revolves around making Batgirl the strongest character in the game, and most like batman - while the other characters are much much weaker. At end game (what most youtubers demo for views) none of this matters because your damage is so overpowered, everything dies in seconds. Just an example though: Batgirl gets every single batman technique (Beatdown, Batswarm, Ground pound, etc) and also gets ignored (permanently) by all cameras & security devices. You also get to hack everything like Batman. All the other characters don't. Buy this for 60% off sale - its not worth even half its cost at the current state of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S ALRIGHT 6/10 I got the game at a good deal through the WB humble sale and it kept me entertained enough. Would not recommend at full price.Best part of the game is of course, the characters - the lovable Bat Family. The four featured Batman proteges have their own distinct personalities and quirks. It's a story about growth and dealing with loss, as each of them struggle to find their place as Gotham's protector while dealing with the death of their mentor and father figure, and the camaraderie in the group having only each other to rely on.Gameplay is hindered by terrible controls causing clunky movements. The fight animations look good and feel powerful! However they are so slow, your character is forced to complete the entire animation regardless, which as a result can make their actions feel sluggish. Especially as you get towards the higher level enemies who seem to have infinite dodges and need a specific special attack to counter them. You can do nothing but watch helplessly as your character is unable to react to an incoming attack because they are still mid-animation doing the stupidly slow special attack you are required to use. There is also no lock on to enemies so if your camera is just a smidge off sometimes you randomly fly off to punch a distant enemy???Despite having access to four unique characters that you can swap between, you can only do so in the tower. I found myself wishing numerous times that I was playing as a different character because their skillset would have been better suited for a particular mission. I understand that yeah realistically you can't prepare for every crime! But nevertheless it feels like a shame I cannot utilize each character's skillset to its max potential. Which brings up another minor peeve - if your system does not allow respec, I think the skilltree should be able to be maxxed out at max level! (barring NG+)Unnecessarily complicated gear systemWhat is the difference between Power vs Damage, Defense vs Health? What are these mechanics? Hidden stats on equipment you have to tab into to see what the modifier is. Look at all these modchips. Who knows. The UI is a mess, none of it makes sense and the game doesn't tell you. Just slap on the gear with higher numbers you silly goose. All the armor designs look really good and cool though, transmog is a nice touch. You can't fight crime if you ain't cute.

_childDocuments_.review: This game cost me 2 quid. And I still say no. However, if you love Batman or love this kind of game, maybe for 10-15 quid it's worth a punt.The graphics are great, they run smoothly for me and look very decent and occasionally fantastic (The clay man was awesome). A lot of time was clearly spent on the presentation, and it's "Batman" so it's cool already, but as is often the way the gameplay guys were on holiday for the whole production period. Good job engine guys, good job textures artists, good job level designers though.So, forgetting this is a coop game which no one asked for, and playing it Solo...Combat:I've never felt so powerless in a Batman game. You have a single melee attack, or you can hold the button for a "heavy" attack. That's it. No real combos to speak of, a "special" piercing attack for certain enemies and a few other "momentum" attacks, but you can only use them after banging away with the default boring melee attack to build your meter. There's no flow, it all feels janky. On the hardest level (which I played on) you *constantly* get ranged attacks interrupting you every 1s which is not fun. (The drone guys are massively OP) There's also enemies which will dodge 100% of your attacks unless you attack them with a certain move. It's dumb to see someone dodge ALL your attacks especially when any attack that requires you to hold a button down takes AGES to register. Let's not also forget when I perform a special move (I was Batgirl) I would leap into the air in a canned animation and the whole time I was vulnerable to attacks. Yes, no invincibility for anything and considering how slow and unresponsive and lumpy it all feels it's a nightmare to start a move and then see an enemy attack knowing you are now not only powerless to dodge but will also take damage because you can't cancel what you're doing. Who signed off on that?Stealth is annoying. You drop down to attack someone but you don't move back to cover auto. So you're waving your camera back up at the perch you came from hoping at some point it will recognise it and let you grapple to safety. But yeah, a lot of the time you can point at a grapple point and it won't register - you need to aim at a very certain angle, from a certain distance, while having perfect line of sight... it's just, annoying. That pretty much sums up the grappling entirely. You can't just aim at any edge like you'd expect, it has to be a certain one, at a certain angle, at a certain distance. Often you will press grapple and end up shooting 100ft up in the air backwards. I'm not even joking. The same can be said of the ranged attacks. There have been times I am pointing the camera AND the character at a target and I've pressed fire and my player has turned around and shot an explodable barrel BEHIND me. Aiming any ranged attack in general is a nightmare with your player attacking everything except who you're probably aiming at. Who signed off on that?Player movement is also weird, it has an odd delay/stutter before you start moving and I can't help but feel they were trying to add a realistic momentum-based approach that failed. Even the act of just moving around feels unresponsive and it suffers from "Assassin's Creed" syndrome - it won't just let you jump when you want to, you can only jump when the game lets you, which leads to stupid moments where you want to jump over a 2ft barrier and are denied or a brilliant moment I was trying to avoid a pressure plate but couldn't jump 30cm over it. You also get stuck on everything with the game just not letting you drop off geometry when you want to, it feels so sticky and frustrating. Who signed off on that?Map traversal is also horrible. You have a bike but the handling is abysmal... actually, it's not the handling, it's the weird camera movement. It's delayed, with heavy momentum, and just makes driving awful. You can also grapple and "glide" but it feels slow and cumbersome.You know how in Just Cause 4 you can use your wingsuit and grapple to skim the ground with an exhilarating risk/reward high speed movement? Well in GK when you grapple you stop gliding and just get dragged to your destination in a straight line. It's dreadful. There is the promise of a glider of some sort, but apparently I have to scan some "drones" before I can use it, and I have a feeling it just unlocks fast travel and won't let me actually use the glider (not played enough to find out yet) Edit: Yup, just fast travel and the drone scanning thing is dull. Who signed off on that?The UI is absolute trash. Like Starfield levels of trash. Everything is primary coloured, low res, non-descript childish icons you're just supposed to "know". Apparently I pick up blueprints and gear but I have no idea what icon each is (and still don't after 30hrs), along with all the other "materials" that are horrible low-res jumbled messes. There is a fine line between minimalist, and childish. Windows 10 was childish. Starfield was childish. This, is childish. Words work, icons don't.I also had my legendary blueprints destroyed for some reason. Is it a bug or were they auto-scrapped because they were 3 levels lower? (Dumb, as they can be levelled up) so I find myself in the position where I finally have the resources to build legendary gear but the game scrapped all my blueprints automatically. Who signed off on that?As always my mind boggles how so much time and money can be spent on a game and it comes out like this. No QA? No public testing? Who is working at these companies to release games like this? Yes men? Do yourself a favour, play the original Batman games instead.The painful thing is, there's some great art direction, some great boss fights (and some bad ones) and the combat shows potential if it had more complexity. This could've been an amazing game, but it shoots itself in the foot over and over and over with things that really are minor to fix compared to all the major things they got right, but they still manage to ruin the game.Who signed off on this?

_childDocuments_.review: New Review 12/21/2023  New score: 7/10 and only get when the game is on sale.After a long while some patches and updates have been implemented that improved the performance of this game. Which was one of my biggest gripes initially.  With the addition of Heroic Assaults 1 & 2 you have some post game content to do. Although the content itself can be very repetitive, if you're looking for a co-operative loot based experience revolving around super heroes, then this content can be really fun. A cooperative super hero game to this degree has a lot of potential and Gotham Knights has proven that. And given that we don't have many options for that even now your choices are going to be slim but this can be enjoyable with friends. -- Below is my previous review when I initially DID NOT recommend the game --Note: Do not compare or look at this game in any way as a successor to the Arkham games. It wasn't meant to be. I'm going to tldr/preface this by saying that despite all of the technical difficulties, and repetitive nature of the game I still enjoyed my time spent playing this, in and out of co-op.  I just cannot justify purchasing this game at the current price point because of the sheer amount of performance issues, bugs, lack of polish, and just lack luster story.- The main cast, and their interactions with one another is really charming and consistent and adds a really nice flare to the game.  Despite the story being pretty much predictable, especially if you're an avid comic book reader or at least familiar with Batman. These characters made it all the more worth it to progress through the story that was otherwise forgettable and not all that interesting.- The playable characters all feel really different to play, each with their own unique abilities and play style while still adhering to the basic controls across all characters, makes switching between them easy enough to adjust to. You get points for leveling up or completing certain challenges and quests you spend on selecting skills/passives for your characters.  The combat itself is easy to learn and offers a decent range of depth despite it's simplistic nature. Different combinations of light and heavy attacks both melee and ranged, with a mix of your skills/abilities will net you some nicely animated attacks and finishers. Unfortunately this is severely hindered by the clunky transition in between attacks, and the poor optimization of the game, making combat sometimes feel jarring,weird or too slow.- The open world is massive and pretty to look at with pretty accurate comic book references across the map. But traversing it is a mixed bag. You could be enjoying your character's unique movement ability, grappling from building to building, or speeding down the road on the batcycle. And you can freely explore the map without being tethered to your co-op partner. But yet again poor performance is going to hinder that experience with constant FPS drops, stuttering, random cars spawning in front of you and even the game crashing. And no matter where you shift your graphical settings to, from highest to lowest it doesn't seem to make even the slightest bit of difference. Missions that take place inside will give you a smoother gameplay experience with consistent frames. But teasing smooth gameplay before throwing you back into an FPS mess just makes it all the more Frustrating. -Questing/Missions are overall average at best. The story would be better off without the side missions you're forced to do in between just to progress.  Side missions in general can become really repetitive, not to say they can't be fun. Between stepping in and out of the main hub I did every single side mission available on the map before returning, and I did enjoy myself playing through them with a co-op partner. What's there is fun, but the lack of variety can be mind numbing at times. - The gear system is simplistic and easy to understand and the same goes for customization. You can craft suits with different aesthetics, change the colors, the cowl, the gloves, and the boots. Allowing a decent enough amount of personalization. You can even transmog over equipment you don't like the appearance of, unfortunately you can't customize an item you transmogged, but you can always revert it back whenever you want to. Getting gear isn't really a problem so long as you're doing side quests and opening chests. And equipping the next highest level item you have, or an elemental weapon that doesn't match the enemy you're going against seems good enough to progress without any issues. The UI/Menus are an overcrowded mess and navigating them can be annoying. - The game definitely should have not been released with it's current state of performance. The frame rate drops, stuttering, and crashing are truly unacceptable. Anyone could say they've seen and experienced worse, but at the end of the day each game should be graded individually and objectively. If you can push past all the annoying technicalities you might be able to find a fun co-op experience as I have. Otherwise:6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is getting so much unjustified hate.Performances aren't great, but the game is alright! Gotham Knights seems to get a lot of hate for very little reasons. Sure, the framerate isn't good, but Arkham Knight was a total disaster on that front when it came out. Remember Steam issueing refunds after the 2hrs/2weeks period because the game was running so terribly bad? I do, cause I got a refund back them. I won't be asking one for GK though, it doesn't run perfectly, but it runs and it's playable, and I don't even have a high end PC.Before we talk about the game, let's talk about the other elephant in the room: this is not and Arkham game. I feel a lot of people are just disgruntled because they didn't get another Arkham game, but WB never lied about the fact that this WASN'T gonna be an Arkham game. A lot of people also seem disgruntled because they get bored of superheroes. I totally get that, but why would you subject yourself to anything superhero related when you don't enjoy it?In any case, let's be clear, THIS IS NOT AN ARKHAM GAME. And it's fine that way.If you want to play Arkham, you have 4 other titles to play or replay. And I'd like to point out, as much as Arkham Asylum is one of my all time favorites and Arkham City is also pretty much up there, that Origins wasn't bad but wasn't brilliant either, and Arkham Knight wasn't all that good nor fresh. And since a lot people complain about the plot of GK and how predictable it is, the plot of Arkham Knight was so damn predictable that everyone had it guessed BEFORE the game launched, to the point that Rocksteady had to make statements about the fact that folks got it all wrong, and that Arkham Knight (wait for it) was totally not Red Hood. Plot twist, he totally was.Anyway, let's talk about Gotham Knights. It isn't perfect of a game, it's got a few bugs, some aspects need tweaking, a lot of annoyances could be fixed with a patch or two, but it's still fun.First of all, you can play coop and coop makes everything better. No friends to play with? Well, the game might feel a bit more repetitive and a bit less lively, but it's still alright. Combat is nice, it's got more to it than what originally seems. You can tweak out the difficulty to better fit what you're looking for, and you'll have enough content to keep you busy for at least 20-30 hours if you're not a completionist.The game clearly has its moments here and there (although not as much as the Arkham games, I'll give you that), and feels pretty good once you start getting the hang of your travel power, perfect dodges and timed attacks. There are the usual side activities which, to be honest, I could have had a little bit more of, but a least no one will complain that travel power challenges or bike races will overstay their welcome. On a sidenote, the batcycle feels so much better than Arkham Knight's overused batmobile.The playable characters are enjoyable, they each have their own fields of expertise and their own feel. Treat them as protagonists, though. Don't go barging into the game thinking they're just sidekicks. These characters have been around for a while now, they're pretty fleshed out and have a solid background.You have somewhat "RPG" element to it, as in there's experience, levels, talent trees, loot and gear crafting. I've seen a lot of complaints about the game being too grindy and requiring too much min/maxing (hey, there, IGN). It simply isn't true. I went through the normal campaign (in coop, which makes enemies "stronger") on normal difficulty and never felt the need to grind or min/max. My gear got better overtime naturally because I was just paying attention to it. I'm going through NG+ on max difficulty now, and so far, I just feel the need to be more careful in combat, which is exactly what I would expect from a higher difficulty setting. True, however, that the whole crafting UI isn't very well explained and is pretty confusing at first (especially for mod fusion).Animations are dope and varied. You'll get your fair share of silent takedowns and beatdowns, cinematic victories over the thugs of Gotham, interrogations, and even a few investigations (although they're obviously not the game's strongpoint). Exploration is great, there's a lot of collectibles to find if that's your thing. You won't have to get them if you don't like that sort of thing, but, I mean, this is pretty much your average AAA Ubi-style open-world game, keep that in mind.Overall, this is not a masterpiece, far from it, but it's still pretty enjoyable. If you desperately want some Arkham, this is NOT it. It sometimes feels like it, it sometimes looks like it, but Gotham Knights is its own game, just as much as the 4 main characters are not Batman but are related to him, and that's exactly the point. GK feels a bit more like Assassin's Creed Odyssey on a smaller scale with a Batman setting. If you're ok with that, give it a try. If you're not, look somewhere else, and that's all there is to it. Try to enjoy this game for what it is, don't hold it up to standards that belong to another, different game. Don't painfully wait or demand for it to be something it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my only reviews I've ever written on here, and it's to warn others. Don't buy this game. I finished the main story and all the side missions and feel completely exhausted. The combat is really the biggest issue I have with this game as it makes playing feel so boring. The animations for finishers are top notch and very entertaining, but the entire fight up to that point is mashing X, even more so than any of the Batman games. It's like they looked at all the superhero games in the last decade with fun and engaging combat and thought they knew better. They thought they could reinvent the critically praised and player enjoyed systems of the past and make something better. In the end, they made Avengers 2.0.Maybe you can look past the combat and try to engage with the story, like I did. Not worth it. The main story is surpassed by even the side missions in this game. There's 3 optional "case files" dealing with 3 iconic Batman villains, and then there's the main story. I kept thinking eventually more side missions will unlock, but they never do. I kept waiting for the actual villain of the main story to reveal themselves, and they do... right before the game ends. The story of this game is honestly average at best, and it's far worse than what Batman fans deserve.A final point I want to make is with the open world aspect. It's as bland as they come with "live-service" style activities popping up around you all the time. My system is pretty good, and I got tons of framerate drops every time I drove the Batcycle. Exploration is also terrible as there's really nothing unique or noteworthy about any of the buildings in this game. Looking at how detailed and beautiful the world was in Arkham Knight puts most games to shame, but especially this one that supposedly takes place in the same location. Aside from visuals, there are no secrets or riddler trophies hidden around the map. Instead, there's 4 types of "collectibles," and they're all so boring to find. Batarangs are stuck to the sides of buildings and laying on rooftops. Murals that need to be scanned coat the sides of buildings. Historic landmarks have plaques you walk up to and hold A. Side note: these "landmarks" are so haphazard with what is and isn't a landmark. The final and worst collectible is the "Court of Owl" notes. Someone scattered the pages of their journal on the Court around Gotham. We get a symbol painted on a wall "nearby" that's supposed to guide us to the collectible. This is stupid and lead to me wasting way too much time looking for the pages. "Nearby" could be across the road, on the roof, on another building, in another castle. These are the least fun collectibles to search for, because I would run in circles for about 10 minutes constantly scanning the environment.If none of the issues I described above are enough to put you off, maybe you'll like the game. However, I would encourage you to thing about it before purchasing. You can do what you want with your money. I obviously chose to not wait for reviews and preorder the game. I just recommend you think about weather this is a game you "need" to play. I loved the Arkham series, and this game severely let me down. I still have hope Rocksteady can bring back the glory days with Suicide Squad, but I will not be preordering that game, or any others that come from WB games.

_childDocuments_.review: I was given the game as a gift, and that's about the price I would pay for it.  TLDR: 5/10Imagine someone took Arkham Knights, removed the cool story and added in some (lite) looter shooter equipment elements and trigger warnings. While actual gameplay feels like the developers tried to overlay a 'live-service' or 'mobile' game model, but gave up on it half way through. That's pretty much Gotham Knights, its not terrible, just not good.The story isn't terrible its just not 'good'.The sound isn't terrible its just not 'good'.The graphics... the game play.... not terrible, just not 'good'.That's pretty much Gotham Knights.I played the game to completion and did much of the optional content, some of it is decent, but overall the game just falls short of the mark in too many ways for me to recommend it. About the nicest thing I can say is that the 4 characters are significantly different from each other, which does allow for some change in gameplay.My biggest gripe is that the tone of the game seems to be more towards younger teens as opposed to mature players. It's a personal gripe, and my own opinion, but after playing the excellent dark, moody and gritty stories of Arkham Asylum, Arkham City and Arkham Knight.... this just seems like it was childish in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy refund. I'm going to leave aside the performance issues because that will probably be patched. This game is rough. The character movement is janky and feels like it was designed for a D-pad. The investigation "puzzles" are...a point and click adventure? You get a screen where you click every combination of items until you get the right answer. Who designed this? Dialog and writing is sub-par hackery. Some of the lines characters deliver are downright atrocious. The combat is average. There's no enemy lock-on so your character kind of looks like they're running around and flipping aimlessly. Riding the Batcycle feels more like the ground moves under you while you sit stationary on a floating bike. There's little sense of velocity at all.  The character designs and outfits are the best thing about the game. Batgirl's figure looks really good. But that's not enough to salvage this trash. Better to replay to the Arkham series. They're all orders of magnitude better than Gotham Knights.

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally Arkham Origins all over again. Right up to a unique multiplayer aspect (in this case the 4 player coop) and absolutely abysmal performance and bugs at launch.Once you stop expecting a Arkham sequel and expect more a different take on the same formula, additionally set more in the future timeline wise than usual Batman games, well this is it exactly.The open world minutae are not too annoying as long as you don't take them seriously. The storyline missions, both main and side story wise, are set pieces across multiple "arenas", though Knights does not have Predator encounters per say (though stealth will still be at least somewhat required for some of the rng missions) with lots of cut-scenes, exposition Arkham style dialogue.Narrative wise its a fairly well executed comic book one-shot style adventure with an ensemble cast which... Honestly can be a tough sell sometimes just due to how fragmented it feels. Pretty sure that when you want to emulate comic books in video games you're supposed to emulate the positive aspect. Anyway I can't say I'm a terrible discerning fan, but I liked the story beats well enough. Its good to get now, especially since it pops up on sale everywhere but...Man that launch, just... It's not something that's enjoyably replayable like the Arkham series, there's no part of it that stands out like, wow that was pretty cool. This would of had more potential as a service game with frequent content drops and new things to do, or, the open world needs some kind of procedurally generated system to add something more than just the same handful of crimes going around, replayable mini missions and boss fights with a variety of changing modifiers/variations or something. They give you gear options and multiple characters but no reason to want to explore any of it once you've done everything once.It feels like they had a vision of mixing the Arkham games with Marvel Avengers but kinda fell short on both aspects. The game masterfully blends thrilling action, deep storytelling, and impressive visuals, making it a must-play for both fans and newcomers alike.The character development is phenomenal. Playing as Batgirl, Nightwing, Red Hood, and Robin offers a fresh and diverse gameplay experience. Each hero has a unique set of abilities and combat styles, allowing players to explore different strategies and find their favorite vigilante. The dynamic combat system keeps encounters exciting and engaging, with fluid animations and satisfying mechanics.The story is captivating, pulling players into a gripping narrative filled with twists and turns. The writing is top-notch, and the voice acting brings each character to life, adding depth and emotion to the unfolding drama. Gotham itself feels alive and vibrant, with a stunning open-world design that encourages exploration and discovery.Co-op mode is a standout feature, providing a seamless and enjoyable multiplayer experience. Teaming up with a friend to tackle Gotham's criminal underworld adds a layer of strategy and fun, making every mission an adventure.Visually, the game is a treat. The atmospheric graphics and detailed environments create an authentic Gotham City, full of dark alleys, towering skyscrapers, and hidden secrets. With its engaging gameplay, compelling story, and stunning visuals, it stands out as one of the best superhero games in recent years. Suit up and dive into the shadowy streets of Gotham—you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game much later than most so I'm not sure how bad things were at launch. However, my experience with Gotham Knights has been great, it's one of the best co-op games I've played in a long time. I picked it up on sale for $30 and played through the campaign and the heroic assault as Nightwing in co-op on keyboard & mouse on hard difficulty so most of my experience will be coming from that perspective. I also got my traversal ability and unlocked all the fast travel points early so I never really had any issues with getting around the map. I never really used The Interceptor once I had The Flying Trapeze(glider) and fast travel but I appreciate it immensely for crossing bridges early on.It performed well at 60 fps on my own, although sometimes got random 1 fps frame drops that would go back to normal after using a smokebomb grapple to lose aggro, so not sure what that was about. There was also crashing but the only times it occured often was after completing a story mission and heading back to the belfry on foot (teleporting to belfry completely avoided this) and sometimes when grappling or gliding . The game is really fast for me to launch and load into so although annoying it was quick to get back to where I was at, never really losing progress whenever I did crash. In the start of multiplayer I had some frame drops to around 20-30 frames, but over time the game ran smooth.I liked the story. Batman's death means Batgirl, Nightwing, Red Hood and Robin have to work together along with Alfred to protect Gotham and solve the last case Batman was working on before his death. There's the main story aswell as 3 storylines you can follow to take on additional villains  Each playable character is likable and does make a difference to cutscenes and some parts of the game.   There's also scenes you can interact with in the belfry and sometimes in Gotham to see characters interact with each other, outside of the immediate story.   It was something they didn't have to do but I greatly appreciate that they did as it made me like the characters even more. There's also plenty of dialogue the game's characters will say to to each other to add to your immersion or at the very least humor you. Combat is fun, beat em up style similar to Arkham with an evade instead of a counter and momentum abilities (abilities unique to each character that you gain charges by attacking and performing perfect evades) to use in a variety of situations and to deal with trickier enemies. They also have an ultimate they can use that's powerful but has a cooldown tied to it.  Momentum abilities have challenges to unlock them appear as you progress the story, they're worth doing and usually can be done as you play the game normally.  There's light and heavy attack combos for melee and ranged attacks along with precision aiming you can do to aim for weak spots, and you can use both during a combo and switch targets in case you need to stop someone from getting a shot on you or perfect evade attacks from behind. Stealth is an option as well, with silent takedowns and working in sync with your co op partner to remain undetected can be extremely satisfying. Robin seems to be the stealth guy(Stealth/perch takedowns) with batgirl (hacking) afterwards followed by Nightwing and Redhood. A gripe I have though is that the ranged attack and silent takedown button are the same and can't be binded separately, so if you hit the takedown key just an inch too far you end up blowing your cover pretty easily.There's 5 factions to fight in total, technically 6 (Freeze aligned Regulators). Each faction has a nice variety of enemies to fight along with specific threats to each of them (freaks can be buffed and revived, regulators have a drone operators, mob with grenade launchers, etc) and after a certain point upgraded versions of them show up to amp the difficulty (more armored attacks, brawlers requiring guard breaking, evasion on ranged opponents,etc). These changes are mostly positive to the fun, needing a change up of tactics and/or teamwork to overcome them (although evasion can be a bit annoying when the only way to break it without using momentum is to land a heavy ranged attack). All factions have an element they can apply and elements they are resistant/immune too. I personally really like how they all look too, especially champion tier enemies. The leveling system was fine, progression seemed just right for me. Skill trees are cool to level into, my favorites being things like Nest (Nightwing's ultimate ability) cooldown lowered by 15% each time he defeats an enemy, shoot 3 darts instead of 1, the evade chain ability w/ knock down and hopping back into the air after doing an aerial. Made Nightwing a real spectacle to play as and fight with, on top of him already doing jumps and flips when running off platforms. All characters get the levels as well so you can switch and not have to worry about grinding individually (although knighthood tree and momentum abilities will still be locked till you do the requirements)Gear is the way you up your power rating even being able to make a sort of build depending on what traits your gear has. You get blueprints and resources from chests you can loot and completing objectives so you can craft new gear, each faction also gives a different type of resource as well. They can have elemental effects on them that gives a status affect after you build up enough on your opponent if its a weapon or give resistance to a specific type like ice or stun. There's also mod chips you can obtain that improve the power rating of your character, these will be where most of your power rating comes from later on. They affect things like elemental buildup on your weapons, crit chance, crit damage, hp, etc. All of the blueprints are random though so you kind of just hope a good weapon with an interesting effect shows up with as many sockets as possible. Would've been nice to manually switch up the element type on your weapons or their traits. I did like that some non elemental weapons were viable with special traits as the trade off like momentum gain on crit. All of the gear has different looks too, although you can only directly customize suits. There's 12 suit styles (+2 if you get the dlc) in total, 10 of which you can change how different pieces look like the cowl, arms, boots, symbol as well as the colorway.  You can't transmog a suit to look like another style and still customize it unfortunately, would be nice to see in the future. It's a co-op game made with co-op in mind which makes the experience so much better. Characters have plenty to talk about with each other, emotes(all the dances are incredible), team take downs and it's really just fun fighting as a duo. Photo mode as well to take all the cool pic you want. There's also Heroic Assault which lets you fight with up to 4 people in 30 floors, completing objectives along the way till you reach the end, they really pour on the enemies you face too. Great to spend time in after the main game with your level 30-40 character. Great gameplay and fun story to play through with great characters throughout the way. Especially worth with a friend to play with. Would definitely recommend picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could score this game higher, but at this point I'm just a bit fed up with it. - The boss fights (I'm looking at you Clayface) are poorly designed and damage-spongy. - The traversal is ALMOST fun, but just a bit too weak to fully grip you, not to mention the fact that you have to earn each character's traversal ability first before getting to use them. - It feels like the animation team and the combat designers didn't realise they were working on the same project, because sure, you look pretty cool in fights, but your attack wind-ups and ability triggers take so long that it's hard to not get constantly hit or shot at.  What's the point of letting me dodge gunfire if enemies can just MOVE THEIR GUNS to follow your dodge ?  - I'm not look for the 42 Glory-holes in Gotham so I can find all the History book pages. If the traversal was better, I might have bothered with the collectables. - My ADHD ass actually likes repetitive patrol-like missions and collect-a-thons, but even I have limits. I can only stop SO many crimes before I start justifying ignoring the calls for aid, sirens and gunfire constantly going off in the distance.  - Your inventory looks like the inside of a Leprachaun's butthole. I'm tired of RPG game mechanics haphazardly being jammed into every game to pad out runtime and feign complexity. 'Punch do low damage because enemy have big number on head' gets tiring, and I don't want to spend hours grinding different rainbow colours of nth tier materials  and mods so my punches do more damage than a sack of feathers.      tl;drIt's a Watered down Batman Arkham game that does all the same things, slightly worse, and without Batman. A corporate-feeling slog that misses the mark and suffers from modern gaming tropes and what I like to call 'Ubisoft-destiny disorder'. Gotham Knights is ultimately a game that fails to step out of the shadow of it's far superior predecessors from multiple console generations ago, despite a serviceable plot, interesting characters and detailed game world. A tough recommendation for even this die-hard Batfan, that could have done with a bit of extra development time and a rework or two.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal game. In the DC/Batman gaming world, we now have a modern RPG version in the mix. We got Injustice in the fighting game genre, Arkham in the Action adventure genre and now Gotham Knights is spear-heading the Open world RPG genre. Set your expectations right and you will experience what I think is the most underrated game on the market today.Things to know - This is not an Arkham Game, nor is it Injustice. Those games are in their own little niche and are played and enjoyed differently. Gotham Knights is radically different.Story -I rate this a 7/10 - Its hard to tell a super hero story that will wow your audience. So, its simply a game of guessing story plots based on your pre-existing knowledge of the Batman Universe. The story is paced out in a methodical way that complements the type of game this. Expect some story breaks that might seem unnatural. However, it stays good and keeps you somewhat interested.Combat -  I rate this a solid 8/10 Again, you are playing a different game. The combat is a melee-special ability system. It takes some notes from the Arkham games, but is much more similar to the love child of Spider-Man (2018) and Assassin's Creed Odyssey. To get the best out of it, don't mash. Master the attacks, combos, perfect strikes and momentum abilities. When you have done this, you can create new recipes for combat which will yield maximum satisfaction when dished out properly to bad guys.Traversal - I rate this 8/10Each character has a distinct traversal method that has a story beat to it. They are altogether distinct, yet share similarities.you can grapple your way across the city in a seamless chain and move rapidly across the world with all characters. The distinction comes in when each character has to use their special heroic traversal. This is where you have some major variety like nothing ever seen in any video game with super heroes. I like it.Bat cycle is the same for everyone, but it is somewhat slow and is one of the main sources of frame drops since you are streaming the world faster. If the Batcycle was faster and had much more solid physics, I'd give it a 10/10. But frame issues make it somewhat weird.Crafting and Gear - I rate this 8/10They did enough for a Super Hero game. Its not too deep and one could call it shallow. If you want a solid gear game, play The Division. You'll min max to your heart's content. I think the devs want the focus to be on content overall.Co-op - I rate this 9/10  This is such a fun aspect that you can;t explain until you actually play it. You and someone else just running around whacking and beating bosses. There aren't many limits to playing in another person's session other than you can't swap your knight on the fly unless the host goes back to Belfry.End Game and DLC - 9/10They already announced a 4 player mode called Heroic Assault. This mode will be available in Nov. That's a big deal since they prioritized their end game to come immediately after release.There's also a new game + mode to hold you over.Open World -  8/10The worl looks well crafted. Its simple and elegant. The lighting really does take it to a different level. Its not Hyper-Realistic like other games, but it is not at all as bereft as many lead you to believe.Cosmetics and Suits -  This is a 10/10The drip is real. All the characters have a plethora of skins to choose from and they are free. In fact there was a glitch for console where everyone has them all now, including the Jim Lee skins. LolFun Factor -  10/10 It appears that the most important metric in a video game has gotten lost in today's very strange internet world. Reviewers who have to play a game for a job don't remember what having fun is like anymore. Sad.Overall, this is a good game. The reviewers exposed their laziness when they didn't properly research, categorize or understand this game and spouted Arkham! Arkham !! Arkham!!! for their entire reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. If you like Batman stuff in general, you'll probably like this game. If you're looking for a great game a la Arkham, go replay one of those. It has substantial changes form that formula that make zero sense. Stealth is basically out the window because it's easiest to just rush in and destroy enemies. The combat is way more paired down than Arkham Knight for some reason. You can dodge, light attack, and heavy attack. Varying the speeds of your button mashing allows for combos, which means that they get activated at dreadful times and are extremely unsatisfying. I got used to the combat after a while, but it's more mind-numbing / easy than truly engaging. The four different characters are fun to play around with and I enjoyed switching characters every so often to experience different play styles. Jason is abysmally bad, so that was frustrating, but at the very least, it is a fun mechanic to be able to switch. The story is fine, it does take an interesting approach, but the interchangable nature of the main characters leaves a lot to be desired from what ends up being a sort of neutral / meh story. It's not bad, just not stellar either. There were a few performance problems I had; it would not let me play on high settings without immediately crashing, but the problems largely went away after a while. Overall, it's a decent game. It certainly isn't great and it doesn't live up to the Arkham games, but I played it all the way through just the same.

name: Open Roads
detailed_description: One fine fall day, Tess Devine and her mother, Opal, discover a cache of old notes and letters carefully stashed away in the attic of their house. Hints of deep-rooted family secrets, decades-old burglaries, a lost treasure somewhere near the Canadian border... What they uncover suggests a much darker mystery, best left well enough alone. But that’s not going to happen. In Open Roads, Tess and Opal embark on a road trip adventure to explore a series of long-abandoned family properties, unearthing the past. They’ll search the ruins of these places that hold buried memories, things Opal has tried for years to forget. And in this search, they'll discover not just the truth they've been seeking, but each other. Featuring star performances by Keri Russell (The Americans, Star Wars: Rise of Skywalker) and Kaitlyn Dever (Booksmart, Uncharted 4). Features: • Experience the story of Open Roads as 16-year-old Tess Devine, on a road trip with her mother to discover what has been left behind in evocative places forgotten to time. • Bask in classic road trip vibes as you chill in the car en route to your next destination, fiddling with the radio and chatting with your mom. • A groundbreaking art style melds detailed first-person environments with beautifully hand-animated characters, bringing the adventure to life. • A unique and engaging interactive dialogue system moves the narrative along, exposing character flaws, secrets, and buried truths.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard not to have high expectations for this since this has been teased for such a long time (it's been seven years(!) since the release of Tacoma) and I found it did not live up to my hopes. This game plays like a much more linear and restrictive version of Gone Home, with each room separated off into different chapters, removing the real exploration & discovery element of the game-play. Other than that, this plays exactly like Gone Home in that it's essentially a take on narrative through environmental storytelling, centred on a young woman and with a strong millennial-nostalgia vibe and soundtrack.It's fun enough while it lasts, but it's short (about 2 hours start-to-finish) and doesn't compare well with similar games by the same developers. Also I found it technically lacking with a lot of juddering visuals as I moved around (full disclosure: I played this on launch day so this may have been patched by the time you read this).
_childDocuments_.name: Open Roads

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, much like I've enjoyed Gone Home and Tacoma. I think it does a great job showing perspectives of people, and how it's difficult to really know someone if you're struggling with emotions and aren't willing to talk. I thought the voice acting was fantastic, and I liked a lot of the dialog. I wish the game was a bit longer- and in some ways it feels like it was meant to be longer. I know this game had some turmoil during development, and kudos to those who kept working on it and fighting for this game. It is a beautiful game, but it also feels like there's things unsaid. I wish Tess had talked to her father at least one more time. I think there was a lot unresolved between Opal and August. I found August to be a really intriguing character that might have had a different perception of what family life was like growing up, but it felt like she was unexplored and kind of ragged on. I think it was missing one more location... one more longer scene that would have given it the robustness of Gone Home that I so enjoyed. But overall a great game, and I think most will enjoy playing it and contemplating the family relationships in their lives.

_childDocuments_.review: The game gave me what I consider the most important when I buy an Annapurna game - a good slice of life story. With that said I will recommend it to people looking for that,It is however not a game without flaws. If you put something into the game it should be meaningful. Running around watching 3D models of various junk while looking for the important bits is a time sink and doesn't help the pacing of the story, The music was to me handled poorly, both with radios and at the end. It just sort of drowns into nothing. The lack of save games quickly becomes a source of frustration when you have fiddled through a lot of junk and accidentally clicks past something that might have had more inspection options but now you will never know what it is unless you restart the game. There are also story elements that feels unsatisfying as they are introduced but then sort of left hanging. If you dwindle down the story to the meaningful parts, there isn't a lot of content,In short it's an Annapurna game. Not one of the strongest. It feels like an unpolished diamond that with a few more iterations of both story and gameplay could have been great. It still entertained me though.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, that was kinda disappointing. I don't know, maybe my expectations were a bit too high for this one since I had been following its development ever since they announced it.It's so short, and feels like it's unfinished. The way they chose to do the animation for the characters feels very off. If the game world was 2D as well, it would have fit better, but when you're surrounded by 3D objects and watching 2D characters talk, it just doesn't fit exactly right. After awhile, I got more used to it, but it still felt more like a development build to me personally, like this was more of an idea rather than a finished product.That's kind of how I felt about the game as a whole: an unfinished project. The story, albeit simple, is somewhat interesting in certain parts, but does not really feel fleshed out, it feels more surface level. It felt very "after school special", a lesson with vague details.The environments are really nice, however. The lighting and detailing is honestly pretty spectacular. I enjoyed seeing different objects scattered about and figuring out which items were pertinent to the story or not. I didn't mind that certain items couldn't be held up.One of the mechanics that felt very bogged down to the experience was the "Hey, Mom!" interactives. I totally get why these are there, but there were certain times where I just wanted to discover things on my own, piece together certain things, and THEN talk to the Mom. But instead, each item that has this interactive, you have to go ahead and start dialogue which yes, furthers the story, but interrupts the player portion of the game too often. It could be that I am so used to games like Gone Home, Tacoma, and Life is Strange to allow the player more freedom in their interactions, but I just felt like this only hindered exploration of the environments. Overally, I'd give this game a 6/10. It was somewhat enjoyable. I did like the hotel portion for whatever reason. The graphics for the environments were highly detailed and quite stunning, but the character animations in this environment just felt odd to me. Hopefully Fullbright gets more freedom in their next game, with less stressors in the workplace.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so bad. I was excited for the release for months. The experience came and went and I'm left feeling so little. Ultimately, this game has so few environments I can't help but feel disappointed. I love the this genre of game, but so few choices mattered. The dialogue was amusing at times, but the constant tension between the characters usually led to fights that were neither entertaining, nor engrossing.  I did enjoy exploring the few very detailed scenes, easily the best parts of the game. I was hoping the premise for this game would lead to something profound, but it's ultimately a brief story with a few clever twists, and then its over. _childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, ex Fullbright, but this game missed the mark for me. It's the first game from the studio that I can't say I enjoyed.The premise of a mother-daughter road trip to uncover a hidden family secret was very intriguing to me and fits perfectly with Fullbright's style of storytelling through letters and environmental cues. With the back-and-forth between the two characters, some of the magic of discovering things for yourself is lost. About 80% of their conversations are just exposition dumps. While the voice acting is great and there's chemistry between Tess and Opal, some of the dialogue just doesn't feel right and is honestly sometimes even poorly written.The flute ambient soundtrack is annoyingly lifeless and lacks emotion. They even missed playing the essential radio songs during the car rides, which is a must-have for a road trip experience, why not add some nice early 2000 indie track? totally missed opportunity there.The 2D character design against 3D backgrounds kind of works, but the lack of animations during dialogue is very noticeable. As Dusk Falls handled this much better, where scenes naturally flowed into one another. Here, it's just a monotonous sequence of the same three animations that sometimes don't even match what the character is saying or feeling.Story-wise, it's somewhat okay. I see what they're trying to tell, and the message isn't lost; it subtly develops into something substantial by the end, and I could connect with it to some extent. It's even more frustrating because there seems to be a great script, but everything around it just feels off. I sincerely hope they get another chance to make a game without the development turmoil, as I really appreciate the way they use this medium.

_childDocuments_.review: "Open Roads" is a short (5h for a VERY thorough playthrough), decent, slice-of-life narrative game that focuses on the relationships within a small family and their past. It also features exploration of detailed environments, but no puzzles. The story never really grabbed me, but I still enjoyed my time with it.You play a 16-year old teenager whose grandmother has died. While clearing the lady's house (which will be sold) together with your mother, you discover mysterious postcards and diary entries that pull into question what you know about your family. Traces lead to the family's former "Summer Home" (which you'll also explore) and one other location after that.I found the story interesting and decently written. Given that the game plays in the 2000s and focuses on events that took place in 1968, a lot of the conversations revolve around "how things were" back at that time, and how the things that you find out about your family fit into that. Those conversations are pretty mundane and the writers didn't really manage to make them interesting, but they weren't boring either. The writing in this game felt like a meal that lacks spice, but is still nourishing.Unfortunately, I found parts of the story very predictable. If you connect two seemingly random, but suspiciously well-fitting details (presented to you very early on), then you've already revealed half of the story's "big twist", and it's only a short logical jump to the full picture. While the details remained mysterious enough to keep me engaged, I spent a lot of time waiting for the characters to realize the obvious.There is an obvious loose end that may make the story feel unfinished, but I think it actually explained very well why the characters have grown beyond caring about this thread - this actually sends a strong message.This game started out as the next title from Fullbright Studios after Gone Home and Tacoma (but it's more complicated than that, see my comment for details). Compared to those two games, I found the story of "Open Roads" the weakest. The premise of exploring dilapidated buildings in a rural US setting already elicited less interest from me than exploring a space station or a seemingly spooky house, and the writing did not manage to change that.Gameplay mostly consists of exploring 3 mid-sized (about half a dozen connected rooms) environments and picking up everything you can. Most of the items aren't particularly interesting and you'll just put them back immediately - you can rotate them to get a closer look if you want, but there isn't a point in doing so. Some items are notes or newspaper articles that provide background information. Several items in each location give you a "Hey, Mom" prompt - you then press a certain key to trigger a conversation with your mom. Due to this, I never felt like I was actually exploring environments together with my mother. Instead, it was always very clear that I was a player supposed to do the exploration, whereas the mother was a passive NPC supposed to provide commentary. That made the situation feel pretty unnatural to me. While I do value player agency highly, it would have been better for my immersion if the mother had taken a more active role.The game does not feature any puzzles apart from "find the key to the lock".Apart from the exploration, the only other gameplay element are dialog choices. As far as I can tell from just one playthrough, these don't affect the story, but just give you an opportunity to roleplay your character a little.Progress through the story is very linear, there are no decisions to make and no alternative paths. If an action would cause you to leave the area, you have to click-and-hold the mouse button instead of just clicking, which is nice for people who like to explore thoroughly and don't want to leave locations early.The game uses a two-pronged approach to graphics. The environments that you explore in full 3D are rendered in a fairly realistic style, though the textures aren't particularly high in fidelity. The conversations with your mother are shown as cinematic, hand-drawn cutscenes. Those mostly just show the face of the person, and the same animations are re-used frequently throughout the game. I don't think this mix of styles did anything positive for the game, but it's probably a good compromise between graphical fidelity and manageable production costs.Unfortunately, the lips of the characters often stay closed while they are talking, which breaks immersion and feels frankly unfinished. In a game with a more abstract style, foregoing lip-synching would have worked for me - but for the cinematic style that was chosen here, it felt very odd. The fact that some scenes are lip-synched while others aren't, only accentuates the problem.Sound effects and music are appropriate, they are used sparingly but fit the occasion when they are present.The publisher used their connections to the movie industry to attract big(ger) Hollywood actors to an indie project with otherwise limited production values. Unfortunately, I don't think it worked very well. While the delivery is certainly competent (if very subdued, but that was probably intended), I just don't find 27-year-old Kaitlyn Dever convincing as a 16-year-old teenager, no matter how popular the actress might currently be. Her voice is too dark and her mannerisms feel too "adult".The bigger problem, however, is that the actresses seem to have recorded their lines separately. This is a narrative game in which the conversations between the two main characters form a huge part of the experience. It would have been imperative to make them sound as natural as possible. Yet, they feel very much like actors (competently) reading lines. They never fall into each other's words or briefly talk over each other, which would naturally happen in such situations. Due to this very noticeable separation, I also felt practically no chemistry between the actors. I think getting less popular but equally competent talent that could find room in their schedules to record together, would have produced better results while also being more cost-effective.The game provides the expected resolution selector and fullscreen toggle, three pre-set graphics settings (with no way to go into details), and a framerate limiter. Five separate volume sliders let you finetune your acoustic experience. Subtitles can be toggled on or off and their speed can be adjusted. There are also separate sensitivity sliders for mouse and controller and an option to invert the Y axis, but no way to rebind keys.Movement is fixed to WASD. Arrow keys work as an alternative, which is very welcome for people with left-handed mice, but the lack of proper rebinding still leaves players with French keyboards, Dvorak layouts, certain disabilities, or just different preferences out in the cold. Considering that ready-made key rebinding solutions exist for every popular game engine out there, I don't appreciate the omission of such a basic PC feature. That said, the game does not require fast reactions or precise movement, so if you just have a way to operate the mouse and the W key (or "Arrow Up"), it should work.The game does not provide any accessibility options. It does provide a "chapter select" function after finishing the story, which is nice if you're going for achievements or want to explore some other dialog options.While most of this review focuses on the details that I found problematic (as each of those might be a dealbreaker for potential players), I'd like to repeat that I did enjoy the story and the way how present and past relationships within the family developed. It's not a great story, but a decent one, and I feel I can recommend it to fans of narrative games. Perhaps get it on a sale, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the most important part to review is the story. Even though I think it has some great moments, they are buried in a sea of:1) teen protagonist trope2) trope of mom-daughter fighting3) trope of eventually kissing-up with a "mom's always right" kind of theme4) melancholic, dramatic monologue/dialogue *a la* the Pacific Northwest (I don't know a good name for this), except the game takes place in Michigan in 2003Still, this game has some nice bonuses, i.e. hidden achievements and some nice callbacks from 2003 (i.e. certain toys I knew I owned back then).For other games that IMO make better points, I'd recommend Hindsight or Coffee Talk.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option instead of positive/negative on steam. I didn't like this game, but that doesn't mean this is necessarily a bad game. Gone Home and Tacoma both felt like they brought something novel to the already saturated genre of exploratory, story-rich "walking simulators". I've played those 2 games multiple times! And ravaged through their respective commentaries. Open Roads didn't make me fall in love like that. I think this game is a miss, not just technically (feels unfinished in some parts with the animations for example), but also in terms of soul. I was not as invested in these characters as much as the ones from Gone Home or Tacoma. _childDocuments_.review: 7'5/10. I waited for this for years. Was so excited when it first got announced, and then I went into doom mode thinking, with all the issues that arose in Fullbright, that his would never see the light of day. But I'm so glad I was wrong!It's exactly what I wanted it and expected it to be. It scratches the same kind of itches Gone Home did (And I LOVED Gone Home, AND Tacoma), but the voice acting in this one definitely made the experience different enough, but still exactly as sweet.I guess it's not a game for everyone. You just go around, pick up stuff, read notes, talk to your mom about the history of your small family, and the end is just... It just ends, and you don't really know what happens to the characters. But as I always say, isn't that exactly how life is?I think it's a really good game, short, full of charm, and if you're into walking simulators I totally recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Open Roads is a short, sweet experience, the kind of walking sim worth spending an evening on to get through in one sitting. The story is paced very well, the puzzle elements are simple but engaging enough to hold your attention, and the juxtaposition between the 3D environments and the 2D character sprites creates a unique visual identity that feels like it'll stick in my memory for a while. The voice acting is crisp and enhances the script, really selling the complex relationship between Tess and her mother, and the way they circle around each other as the story picks up is very well-done. I think that, ultimately, my only real complaint is that I wish the character sprites actually visually spoke - there are a number of animations that play for voice lines, but once the animation stops, the voice lines will just keep going past the animation because they're not specifically coded to each voice line. Not really a big deal, but it was a little jarring at first. Ultimately, though, if you like walking sims, if you like one-night game experiences, give Open Roads a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this one. I loved both of Fullbright's (now the Open Roads Team) previous two games - Gone Home and Tacoma. Both of these games rely heavily on environmental storytelling, augmented by additional narration. In Gone Home, finding cassette tapes triggered voice-over by the player character's sister. In Tacoma, triggering hologram recordings allowed you glimpses into the past. In Open Roads, the core gameplay remains true to form with optional commentary from player character Tess's mother when you interact with objects. It's a solid formula, so why did this game pack less of a punch?Gone Home was about queer identity and (angsty) teen love in a time (the 90s) when being gay was much more stigmatized. Under its sci-fi dressing, Tacoma has fun exploration of strong AI and more serious commentary on labor rights. Open Roads seems to be split between tackling single motherhood (and navigating how to talk to one's kid about a less-than-stellar ex). It also looks at the question of .The protagonist is a 2003 high school senior, but for the most part, the game doesn't lean into the period setting the way Gone Home embraced the 90s. There is a flip phone and crappy texting, an old-timey iMac (in giant colorful cube form), and some gone-by-the-wayside ephemera, but most of the locations are not rooted in the time. Instead you spend most of the game exploring locations that have been uninhabited since the late 60s. This is fine, but dilutes past games' ability to embrace the environmental storytelling with a consistent time period and feel to the environments.In contrast to previous games (perhaps due to development hell), the environments are less interactive. There are many times I tried to open cabinets or drawers, only to find them non-interactive. There also seem to be fewer unique objects in the world. A minor gripe, but it made the world feel more superficial and less lived-in.I was put off by the art style as well. The world is rendered in a more realistic style (as with previous games), but interactions between Tess and Opal are in a hand-drawn cartoon format. The latter is layered over the former, and it is a bit jarring (see the promotional screenshots, above). Also, the characters seem to only have a few alternating frames, so they're mouths/faces don't sync with dialog, which is odd to see.The mother-daughter relationship is messy, which is the strength of the game's storytelling. They are dealing with the recent loss of Tess's grandmother, the repossession of the grandmother's house (and theirs) due to outstanding debts, and mother Opal's pride (). On top of this, Tess .This is why the ending of the story was so disappointing for me. In the aftermath of the grandmother's death, Tess and Opal , leading to an  in search of clues. The game builds up the idea that . After building suspense and dropping clues, the ending feels like a cop-out: . I was hoping to see how Opal (and by extension, Tess) tackle a revised understanding of their pasts , but the conclusion is much more of a shrug ().I'd say grab it on sale if you want a short (2-3 hours) game in the vein of past offerings. But know that it's not quite as polished (or narratively coherent) as past games from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Open Roads

_childDocuments_.review: Open Roads is a 2024 game, and I thought it was a fun game overall. The game is short, but enthralling for its story. It features two women, Opal (Keri Russell) and her daughter Tess, are packing up their house, and getting ready to move on after the death of Tess’s grandmother. They discover a secret that could change their view on grandma. They suddenly feel the urge to drive to Michigan and find secrets. It turns out Opal’s father is a person who has depth but no cheating was involved and they get the closure they wanted. Overall, it is a short game that can be played in two hours, and it is enthralling with the banter between two people who suddenly are rocked and shocked out of their comfortable and cushy life. It just is an overall good time for fun.A few things I had noticed about it. The voice acting is spot on and now I can’t separate the voice from the character, all suited well. Art is beautiful and well done Finally, the game took roughly 3 years to develop from 2020 when the first teaser came to its March 2024 release date. Solid amount of time to cook and brew the game. Verdict: Recommended. Doesn’t matter if you pay money for this game or on Gamepass. Just do it. Play the game and enjoy the great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Open Roads

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable and well written Gone-Home-esque walking sim/visual novel all about family relationships, nostalgia and loss in the mid-Western US.The opening chapters are about a recent bereavement, something you might want to know, but it’s dealt with very kindly and there aren’t big content warnings beyond this.A few downsides:* There aren't quite enough character animations for me, making the dialogue scenes, which are central to the story, janky and hard to watch. This is a shame because the art style is beautiful and works well for what it's trying to do.* You will pick up a lot of cups, examine them, and find that they do nothing.* Spent about 40 minutes trying to find a single key which was a little annoying but didn't detract from it too much.* Music is missable.Racked up about 3 hours to complete for me. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Open Roads

_childDocuments_.review: "It's just a walking sim", we hear sometimes from gamers community about new releases, and they always get it wrong. Best games ever that I've witnessed in my life weren't high budget projects, but passionate works with independent spirit and great storytelling made by small studios. Gone Home was pretty important in that genre, The Vanishing of Ethan Carter made the experience gorgeous and exciting, and What Remains of Edith Finch gave brilliant poignance to the exploration part of the gameplay. The level of immersion in these worlds was outstanding. Open Roads is a worthy successor in that sense.It took the best from its predecessors: > attention to the details (interiors design of 2000s era; bits and pieces of a family in a lived-in places; the nuances in how different generations interacted between their peers - through postcards, letters, sms; telling about various personalities through their personal belongings)> letting players to dissolve in a simple beauty of a sunny day when you packing things for moving out, in a bittersweet melancholy of a time-worn buildings and rooms full with sentimental meaning, in a pride and sorrow for the late loved ones which left a great deal of broken memories about their life decisions, and in a colorful cautiousness of road journey where mother and daughter relationship depends on our own ability to be curious, honest and vulnerable about many issues> telling the story without judging its characters; there's no "sides", only humanity - the point is not being right about something, but trying to understand that each person has his own justified reality; people has their own fair share of illusions and stubborness, in the end they deal with the consequences of their decisions. The further we go into the spirals of the past, the better we get the picture that our relatives are stronger or weaker than they seemed to us in the past. And suddenly realisation comes: there's no divide between generations in terms of universal approach to life. People were falling in love and made stupid choices in the 1960s and 2000s the same, and any other decades. It just a matter of final choice: how certain families/individuals decide to deal with it - to bury their emotions (sometimes quite literally) or to let it in the open and trust your companions to answer with empathy and kindness in returnOpen Roads is relatively short game, but it was a genuinely great few hours which I was glad to spend in the company of two interesting female characters with their own conviction and compassion towards each other in their casual talk. It was a fun, engaging and memorable exploration of human bonds between mother and daughter, and awesome voice performances from Keri Russell and Kaitlyn Dever made the immersion flawless. I continue to be impressed by how much publisher Annapurna Interactive supports their developers no matter what obstacles these independent studios have on their shoulders to make really unique art works. I hope that you will enjoy Open Roads too!My only criticism probably is about the discrepancy between characters animation and voice acting. Not a big deal, but it's obvious and at first a bit distracting. Also it's too easy to find things in the game, even Gone Home (made years ago) was more sneaky in that regard (you could miss stuff if you didn't search the location enough). But it's really nitpicking, don't hesitate to buy the game, especially if you're a fan of games I mentioned in this review earlier.

_childDocuments_.review: Impactful, touching, and intimate, I was captivated enough by Open Roads to finish it in one sitting, though I won't say it was a long experience by any means. It is much closer, however, to capturing the sensation I felt playing Gone Home some years ago for the first time than Tacoma, which is what I was hoping for. That's not to say I didn't appreciate Tacoma, but I found myself yearning for the melancholic, personal storytelling grounded in the real world that Gone Home tackled so elegantly.Part of what makes a game like this feel like an interactive extension of cinema for me is undoubtedly the way it uses implicit and explicit strategies to communicate its narrative. Much of it is filling in the gaps, whether it's imagining the intangible, unseen aspects of characters, or recognizing what parts of the story reflect the real world, which is often inconclusive or lacking in clarity. It was exceedingly engaging to see how Opal and Tess would pour over small environmental details in connection to larger, more meaningful ideas, events, and people. Unlike Gone Home or Tacoma, however, Open Roads has an endearing character in the way it amplifies emotions through conversation, and more specifically, a juxtaposition of hand drawn animations that are far more expressive than 3D characters can be at times.All of those compliments aside, I do have to admit the animations might be the only disappointment in an otherwise complete package. For a three and a half hour experience, the variety of 2D animations, which rarely synchronize with the wonderful voice acting of Keri Russell and Kaitlyn Dever, are slightly barebones. The transitions between expressions can be slightly jagged at times, and while the 3D environments are well executed, I feel as though more time spent crafting individual animations for each chapter might have been more effective. It wasn't enough of an issue to distract me longer than the beginning hour, but nonetheless, after playing games like The Night is Grey I have to admit it would have enhanced this story quite a bit, in my opinion. If you're comfortable with visual novels that are less kinetic assuredly this won't be all that significant, but after years of development I suppose I was hoping for more diverse animated interactions between the hand drawn characters as well as the world around them. I think this team has made yet another captivating emotional experience and after all the struggles they went through to release this game, I hope they are proud to have arrived at the finish line. Definitely give the game a look and support them if you can; especially at what is a surprisingly reasonable price point, and if you enjoy the walking simulators this team did at Fullbright prior to this project.
_childDocuments_.name: Open Roads

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly short.  6.1 hours of play time.  I really believe the developers could have added so much more to this story and just didn't. While the calm atmosphere is really nice and chill, it's frustrating to have paid even the discounted price (it was on sale for $15) for something that was so short and brief.  Definitely a game for when you want just enjoy the ride and search but not at all worth the money.
