_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and atmospheric game reminiscent of old-style puzzle games.Aggressively linear though, the game actively prevents you from having options that would confuse you or lead to any emergent sequence breaking. A pleasant way to spend a couple hours of your life, think of it as purchasing an interactive movie.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: very beautiful little puzzle game. probably took about 3-4 hours of playtime to see the credits but i enjoyed the whole journey. the puzzles got pretty mind bending at the end and there isn't any tutorializing from the game to tell you what you're expected to do, but it was all reasonable and within the realm of possibility.a+ do recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game, a beautiful example of less is more...the world, environment and the unique rules of it somehow make sense very quickly.without tutorials or any text to read you'll manage to figure out every obstacle, the game progress perfectly and manage to not be repetitive because it keeps evolving as you keep learning it,there's a great sense of satisfaction when solving puzzles and winning against bosses.----with that said, this game is not for everyone, but i mean just check the videos and see if it speaks to you...if you like this kind of genre i definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out as a somewhat interesting puzzle game, but as it progresses it becomes more and more tedious to juggle the orbs, backtrack repeatedly, and slowly align everything in place to solve puzzles. The puzzles are conceptually pretty easy to figure out, but then have minutes of padding to actually reach the solution. I got to the point where I had all 4 orbs and I think my next objective was to find all the "Moon Ancestors" and it was all just so tedious and uninteresting at that point that I didn't have the drive to continue.It might be impressive if you don't play a lot of indie games or puzzle games, but there are plenty of things I'd rather play and I will honestly likely forget that this even exists in a month.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game with great level and puzzle design that stimulate rather than challange the player. The world is beautiful, intriguing and little scary, the world feels great to move around in. Most importantly, it's a game that a player like me who is generally bad at puzzle games, can complete and feel smart about it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lot of fun. Honestly, I don't really like puzzle games. I'm bad at them, and in general, they feel a bit pointless. However, I really liked The Swapper, Limbo, and Inside. This game is by the designer of the last two games, so I figured I'd give it a try. It's hard to explain how the game works, but there's a lot of fun exploration, and the puzzles are intuitive. The game's designed so that you don't spend a lot of time wandering around, and I really appreciated that. The overall world-building is great, and I'm having a lot of fun.Edit: at around 6.5 hours, there's a gameplay shift that I absolutely hated. It's basically a new gameplay style that's completely unrelated to the adventure/puzzle bits. This new gameplay feels out of place and also makes the game a frustrating and joyless slog.  You also can't skip or use a walkthrough to get past these sections.[Vague spoiler alert ahead]: I might keep playing, but from walkthroughs, I've seen that there are even more "shoot the triangles" later, and they're so tedious and unpleasant. Ugh. I really liked the parts of this game that they featured on the commercials: neat worlds to explore, fun mind-bending orb puzzles. Not a tedious shooting gallery. Disappointed is an understatement. Limbo and Inside didn't have crap like this.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but a great experience. Puzzles are often really clever and especially near the end take great advantage of the mind-bending core premise, but some are a bit too linear. Felt sometimes like I was watching an (admittedly cool) cutscene instead of doing a puzzle. The mood and visuals make the whole experience a breeze to get through even on the occasions that the puzzles aren't hitting, very fun overall.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little and wonderful journey with some puzzles. And at some points i really got stuck a while. And man... the graphics and the atmospere was fantastic. If you like a small game (I played it in 7 hours but i saw many guys solve the game in the half of the time) with great atmosphere and some good puzzles, cocoon is a must have for you.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Recursion heaven. Played the whole thing on stream (bought the game myself and was never sponsored/paid to talk about it or play it) and had a great time.I loved the game, best way to describe it was that it played like butter. Puzzles weren't too easy or hard, just satisfying. Combat was interesting each time. I felt that the mechanics all felt a bit new to me rather than being rehashes of mechanics I've seen everywhere else, and that feeling of "this is innovative" was there pretty consistently. Game was nicely segmented in ways where you constantly learn new mechanics that compound rather than having a ton of new challenges dumped on you at once. Loved the visuals, although the purple area definitely had some phallic bits that had me laughing rather than in awe. Still great though. Shoutout to the audio designer(s) as well, I loved the feeling the game had with all of that combined.I appreciated that it was playable with so few controls, the accessibility there is massive.I wish it were a bit longer and a tiny bit more difficult.  This game is ripe for DLC, I hope you guys look into adding more content or continuing with it somehow!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This great puzzle game will make you seriously get confused at some points. I can easily recommend it. My only complaint is the boss fights, I feel like it makes it less accessible to new players than it would've otherwise. Instead of having it be a bullet time style fight, it should've been a puzzle-based fight.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic experience. The sound and music and environment design were wonderful. I felt immersed and interested in the universe the whole time. The puzzles were some of the most satisfying and unique I have ever experienced. I recommend this game to literally anyone who enjoys puzzle games. It will definitely be one of the best games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is one of those games that, makes a clear case for the potential for video games to be a form of high art.The design of the worlds are all unique and clearly meticulously crafted. It is wildly unique how well the art tied in with all of the puzzles and how clear effort was taken to get the atmosphere of each segment and step of the game right.The game gives you one action button and a d-pad. There is no text in this game, and it clearly doesn't need any.  It is up to you, via trial and error and intuition, to figure the rest out. The game does a fantastic job teaching the player what to do and helps keep the player on the rails at nearly all times, by cutting off needless back-trackable area.The puzzle designs seemed so unique and well thought out, by the end of the game, I could figure out what buttons to press, but I would have a hard time explaining to you how I knew.If you enjoy puzzlers and you have 8 hours to kill, do yourself a favor and play this game.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet but a very good time. Clever mechanics that blew me away multiple times and made for some puzzles that while not always the most challenging, always felt super satisfying. Every little mechanic this game has is utilized for a puzzle in some way. Only possible criticism is that I would have liked more, but with how carefully designed a game like this would need to be I can't really say it's fair to expect. Absolutely worth the play, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best games I have ever played. It's a puzzle game that is very simple yet surprisingly complicated. Each puzzle offers a delightful experience. There are no unnecessary key bindings; the entire game is played with just five buttons: up, down, left, right, and action. I would definitely recommend it. I wish there were more games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? Excellent puzzle design, nice graphic, attractive universe. This is a great game.It is simple but fun. There is no complicated system, just move around and press a button for interaction.Also, the 'cocoon' concept is a way to explain our lives, reminding me with Matrix and simulation theory.It is quite short, so I really hope the studio could make more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great, short, but satisfying puzzle game with a good dimensional twist that, at some point, blows your mind with the "inception" feel. Each puzzle element gives depth to previously established mechanics. Boss fights—yes, they are here—are a great guide for fellow developers on creating not challenging but deep encounters with the sole use of player movement mechanics. The art style is gorgeous and provides the necessary variety and sense of progression, compensating for the low use of puzzle quantity variety in the traditional sense but working in tandem with puzzle identity.There is nothing to add here, the game is just a solid experience!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great little puzzler with unique gimmick. If you enjoy puzzlers in general and don't mind them being somewhat abstract, you will not be disappointed with this title. A bit too easy. Could have been few more puzzles at the end. Nothing that will keep me from recommending though. Play it for the novelty or because it's a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: puzzles are really really easy. lets be real, you play this for the aesthetic. still enjoyable. pretty short.honestly, im surprised this won a game award, there's nothing super unique about this one.im on the fence on recommending this one. i'll say thumbs up solely because it isn't bad and its polished, but its nothing super special that really stands out here.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are fun, but not too challenging. Visuals are great and lots of cool synth music and sound effects. Main game mechanic is implemented well and fun to use. Hard to glean much about the true nature of the story much like their other games.  Completed in roughly 5 hours, but I didn't find all the secrets or achievements. Worth it IMO; especially if on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game was not what I expected but in a good way. And it would be a shame to spoil it. I will just say the balance between positional boss fights (which were just the right difficulty for me) and Inception-inspired puzzle solving was perfect. The overall ambience and sound design is also very impressive and adds to the game. You can aim for the Platinum in 6 hours, so maybe wait for a -20 to -40% off if it bothers you. Definitely would recommend. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: easily one of the best puzzle games ive ever played. constantly reminded me just how brilliantly these levels and mechanics are designed so i never got lost or felt frustrated. also just a rlly beautiful game with amazing animations and a world that is wholly unique to itself. tldr you are bug, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pure art. From the mysterious alien setting, to the atmospheric sound effects and music; both work hand in hand to create the perfect backdrop for this amazing game.Playing in 1080p felt like I was playing in 4K and the fluid animation further enforces how great this game looks. Being able to carry around these orbs and travel between them creates such a cool dynamic with some cool paradox moments. Before collecting each orb, you're faced with a boss to defeat. I was genuinely blown away by how unique and engaging each one was for a puzzle game. The fidelity in this game is insane.I was surprised to find myself never getting stuck exploring in this game which just goes to show how great the level design is. It's a great balance of leading you where to go but never holding your hand. Solving puzzles just flows so naturally and using music queues to let you know you're on the right path was a great treat.Once again, my only complaint with these games are how short they are. But this game is all killer no filler, which I can appreciate. This year has been pretty generous with the amount of puzzle games but this is without a doubt my favourite in terms of overall package.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. But a first a small thing to get out of the way:This was the first game I really, really wanted to play on my TV. As I started to play on my steamdeck, I was overwhelmed by the Graphics and sounds (headphones), so I wanted to experience this on 65” with surround sound. I have bought my steamdeck with an original dock, so attached that to my TV. I was all set and ready for this treat. I don’t get it to work on my tv though and I read I’m not alone. Tried every tip on Reddit and all, but don’t get the deck to work. So a warm and genuine wish for people responsible at steam / Valve to go find another job. You’ve really screwed me over getting the original dock, for way too much money, that doesn’t do what it should. I will buy the game on PlayStation then. You are welcome to give a refund for the useless dock. Back to the game:It’s lovely. Colorado and graphics look a bit like Tunic, and the puzzle elements give me a Journey feel.Getting teleported through the little spheres looks wonderful. It is like getting warped through a wormhole in hyperspeed with impressive sounds.It’s a linear game. Not very complicated, but having to find out all of it by yourself makes me feel smart and I don’t like games that make me grind puzzles for hours.This game contained boss fights, that aren’t hard, and you can die as often as you like. I’d recommend this. Thanks developers for this lovely game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A mind bending, brain melting puzzle game where you hop between the fabric of the universe.Quite simple and not extremely long. Yet deeply fascinating and interesting. Reeks of Inside in the best ways. Yet also stands on it's own as a wonderful, weird sci-fi adventure. 10/10 Actually made my brain hurt.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like playing Portal for the first time, more than most of the games that actually try to imitate Portal. Cocoon is very much its own thing, but the design and feel of the puzzles, the a-ha moments and moments of insight are very similar (and extremely good).  It's also weird and beautiful in an eerie kind of way — an awe-inspiring tour of an ancient and inscrutable alien world (or series of worlds). Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is an impeccably designed puzzle game with excellent art direction, but the narrative and the world felt lacking.I had a great time blasting through the whole thing in one sitting, but I don't think this will be lingering with me for long -- certainly not in the way INSIDE did.A worthwhile four-hour snack of a game, if nothing else.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only game I would sell on its visuals alone. The graphics are outstanding and present an alien reality that is so captivating you'll want to explore it forever. When people dream about space games with strange worlds, this is the ♥♥♥♥ they are thinking of. The puzzles drive progression and are genuinely simple but require you to delve deep into the mechanics at work and exploit pocket dimension physics in fun ways. Your reward is not only the mind-bending transition between dimensions but also getting to explore more of the worlds within.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely creative. All the puzzle-solving is so pure and precise. There’s no text, no dialogue, and one ‘interact’ button. New mechanics intuitively unfold in these perplexing layers of alien realms. It’s continually intriguing to see what sort of visuals these worlds will present you with. Cocoon is expertly crafted and certainly has the most captivating and original premises for puzzles I've experienced in a long while.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a decent challenge. Working with nested worlds and intermingled puzzles with hidden collectibles brings a fun focus to how these kinds of mechanics can work.A couple of puzzles were particularly challenging for me, though, retrospectively, they shouldn't have been so difficult. One of these took me almost forty minutes by itself, a significant portion of my playthrough.I don't know that there's significant replay value in Cocoon, but I enjoyed the five or six hours I put into the game and would welcome DLC, or a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a delicious puzzler that utilizes the concept of multiple worlds treated like Matryoshka dolls exceedingly well!The organic and alien-like atmosphere in each world's design and music provides a sense of wonder and mystery to the game as a whole. After spending a considerable amount of time solving puzzles, I noted a sense of meditative enjoyment by simply watching gates opening, bridges unfolding, and story set pieces revealing themselves (cutscenes after solving a puzzle, essentially).The bosses were quite enjoyable, but I do wish that there was one more in order to evenly space out the time between the puzzles and bosses. In addition, the various mechanics used to defeat bosses are seldom reused to solve puzzles. It truly would've brought it all together to see what the player learned from solving puzzles be presented against the bosses, or revisiting a new mechanic after defeating a boss being used for a puzzle.That, and I find some of the timing puzzles to be my least favorite to solve, too much backtracking!Nonetheless, I had a wonderful experience! For the amount of time spent to completing this game, I would highly recommend it when it's on sale :)
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Gets better and better the further in you are. When it's over it leaves you craving more, which is a good thing I guess, but I also hope there is a DLC at some point. The game systems feel well explored by the end but not all systems do. Purple ball was very intersting but only had a fairly short section dedicated to it. Would have loved to have a section with all balls that also utilizes the purple one. All in all super memorable. A must for all puzzle lovers. The puzzles feel incredibly fair and the game actively prevents you from trying out pointless things by blocking off paths that are not relevant to the current puzzle. Sound and atmosphere are 10 / 10. I will buy DLC if there is one even if its short. (Make one pls! :D)
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The game is crazy good and smart! Loved every minute playing it. It's very simple at the beginning but it's getting harder by the end. The pacing is perfect, though. Don't wait for the sale. Buy this game now and enjoy this masterpiece.I know it's not going to happen for quite a while but man... I can't wait for the sequel already.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Very imaginative game with a gorgeous art style. The puzzles are really intricate. I was consistently blown away by what was actually possible. Yet the game is so well paced and designed that there is rarely any need for trial and error, you’ve always gathered the necessary info on your current capabilities before facing a big or more lengthy challenge, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you practically need a guide for.Best puzzle game I’ve played, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Super slick and mysterious puzzle game. The mystery is dense and wordless, to the degree that this reminds me of Hyper Light Drifter, minus the combat. The world has a freshness to it that reminds me of watching the first Avatar for the first time. While puzzle games typically fail to hold my interest, this is beautiful and captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Positives+ Ambience+ SFX / Music+ Interesting Puzzles+ Nice little encouragement sounds when you are heading in the right direction+ Fascinating WorldNegatives- No official ultrawide support (had to make do with a normal resolution)- Could have done with possibly another world to make the game a little longer- Some of the puzzles were confusing to figure out such as getting the last little machine thingy at 97% (the one where the symbols reflect in the water)Overall this game is truly fantastic and worth every penny. I would recommend anyone who enjoys puzzle games to buy this and give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've played. Everything about the design is perfect, including the visual design, sound design, and most of all, the level design. The puzzles are intuitive and rewarding, and it's pretty much impossible to badly stuff anything up or break the game because of how well everything is laid out; it's linear enough that you can't get stuck, but it still feels open enough to make full use of its unique game mechanic, which is travelling in and out of each "sphere's" dimension. Give it a shot. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, compact, gorgeous little puzzle game. Its strengths are in its pacing and presentation. Each mechanic has enough focus to feel interesting without ever outstaying its welcome, and the design of each area is consistent and excellent. The buttons, platforms, mechanisms, and occasional creature all share a strange, not quite organic, not quite mechanical aesthetic. It creates an immaculate vibe of strange sci-fi that keeps things feeling 3 parts mysterious, 1 part vaguely hostile. Its *great*.The flip side is, that this being a short game with an emphasis on efficient design, the puzzles themselves are never more than moderately complex, and there is little in terms of narrative or other gameplay to speak of (there are a few boss fights, but they play more like puzzles than anything else). Put another way, this game is roughly 4 hours of relatively fun, well paced, beautifully dressed puzzles, and little else. Up to you if that's worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool puzzle platformer! The developers succeeded in making a game where some pretty complicated mechanics are seamlessly explained through the environment, without a single word. I especially like how the puzzles flow from each other and build upon each other, reaching precisely the right level of complexity. One could make harder puzzles to prolong the game but that would probably make their solutions quite tedious, and Cocoon does not overstep these bounds (as many other games, alas, do). Kudos to the devs and a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great games with good really good graphics ! The puzzles are original but not that hard. The game however is short ( 5-6h and even faster if you rush) and i would have loved to see more "Boss figh" mechanics throughout the game. Its worth getting but with a discount because it's a bit pricey for the time it takes to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice puzzle game with intriguing world design and great graphics style. The puzzles are not too difficult, so if you are a veteran in this regard, then it may almost become a walking simulator. Still, with this world, it will be a great journey (especially if you like fractals and/or insect themes).
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Ehhhhh... I tried to like it, I really did try. I quite like the art style.This is framed as a puzzle game, and it kind of is I suppose, but it's also mostly a case of just grabbing whatever the game gives you (or doesn't give you) and running in the only direction available. It feels like you're just following a set of steps towards the inevitable solution (which I suppose is what a puzzle game IS, but it feels very restricted here). I got maybe about 3/4 through it and then the linear trail seems to disappear. This resulted in me having to trial and error all the available routes I had, which felt like a lot of random legwork due to a lack direction.As I wasn't really having that much fun in the first place, I decided to call it a day there.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous and inviting. I’m not good at puzzle games nor am I particularly drawn to them in any way but I have been getting into cozy games with impeccable art style like Sable and Journey.  It’s a very forgiving game and as long as you are experimenting, you will move forward. It will bend your mind in fun and friendly ways but it doesn’t want to punish you or stop you from having experiences. Seriously incredible animations and use of disparate visual styles. Lovely and very effective minimal sound design with restrained amounts of tasteful synth music. All together there’s an uncanny feeling of TEXTURE such that I have never experienced in a video game before. Short game. Art.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable puzzle game wrapped in a biomechanical skin that looks incredible, and an amazing soundtrack as well. None of the puzzles have been too challenging so far, but some of them do make you stop and think for just a moment, not a frustrating amount of time by any means. Lack of tutorial but purposefully so, and introduces new concepts organically.The only real con to the game I notice so far is that it's a short game, but sometimes that's all it takes. I haven't beaten it yet but judging from the reviews of others and the rate I'm gathering achievements, seems to be a 3-5 hr experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Since the game has no text or audio dialogues, there is a universe where I understood everything about it. Within that is another universe where I didn't understand anything. Within that is another universe where I think I understood it. Within that is another universe where I understood everything about it...
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but it gets dragged down by many tedious and confusing elements. In mid to end game, there is a ton of backtracking during puzzles to the point of boredom and frustration. The levels are linear in design with only one solution to the puzzles. The only thing that carries these areas are the scenery and ambiance, filling the space/ alien setting in a way. But the most unfortunate downside is the story, or the lack of one. Its a story where even looking up "Cocoon lore explained" videos still will leave you confused with a wtf feeling. Everything is in the background and implied, hinting towards a greater purpose for your little bug guy but never shown beyond subtlety. I would not recommend this game to most people due to my experience, but others may feel different so ♥♥♥♥ it, give it a try. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: the game literally tells you nothing not even how to play and was great wouldnt be surprised if aliens made this one so bizarre in some pretty specific ways it would make more sense genuinely funky for human tastes though with some perception bending puzzles that really made you think in different ways edit for those who wany easier 100% completion theres a pretty wide percentage where you can load just about anywhere to get to what you need pretty quick
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Can we please stop calling walking simulators puzzles?"Find a code of 6 symbols as world objects", "walk through a labyrinth of 2 actual paths and other dead ends, and maybe turn one junction in it on the way" and "find this glowing orb to kill a boss" are not puzzles. Puzzles are what makes you think, if you didn't know. In a way this game is indeed a lot like Limbo and Inside - they are not puzzles, they are just walking simulators with "bring this object here" fillers and "cool" aestheticsI played for an hour, completed about half of the game and already super bored. Yes, the game is kinda pretty, but *yawn*Calling this a puzzle is an insult to the genre. Why GMTK's Mark recommended the game is beyond me. Go grab Mosa Lina instead
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon has beautiful artistic design but is weighed down by its price and lack of gameplay. It's a walking simulator without a story or challenging puzzle. The most challenging piece of this game are "timing" puzzles. At no point during the entire playthrough of this game did I once scratch my head and have to work a problem out. It's a shame too, because the concepts behind the puzzles, had they been fleshed out, could've created a brilliant game. Unfortunately the creators seemed to prioritize spectacle over puzzle. I never want to disparage anyone's hard work and this game is clearly a labor of love, with the world design and concepts being both breathtaking and alien, but as a fan of puzzle games this game was a major disappointment. In short if you purchase this game, expect incrediblly rich art but expect no substance in game design.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It wasn't "bad" but I wouldn't recommend it to my friends. It didn't click for me, made the effort to finish it and it took me 4 hours to finish it with all successes.There is definitly high quality work here, environment, music and visuals effects (and probably programming too for making this work flawlessly)But the main things I was expecting were good puzzles and I am disappointed to say the least. The first 3 hours of the game were pretty boring and I forced myself to go through it, I felt no challenge at all as the solutions were almost always straightforward.The last hour was ok but I didn't enjoy this game overall
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is an above average puzzle game, with a major focus on minimalism, atmosphere, and visuals. You're simply a little bug out in a large universe, trying to find your way. There is no dialogue or text on screen, and cut-scenes are rather frequent and transition smoothly with gameplay, which add to create a very atmospheric experience.The puzzles range in difficulty but never really get very difficult. Most of my time playing Cocoon was spent walking where I need to go to complete the puzzle rather than actually thinking about how to solve it. This added to the atmosphere, but also meant I frequently wished there was a run button or that the walking speed would at least be faster.Overall, if you're looking for a relaxed, atmospheric experience with light puzzle themes, Cocoon is a fantastic pick. While I personally preferred Limbo and Inside, Cocoon feels like a great spin-off with more focus on beauty over dark fantasies.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle game with a unique setting and amazing art visualsThis is overwhelmingly positive so it is worth a look on steam, but for me it was a miss - I would give it neutral if this was an optionThe puzzles are very samey and require a lot of backtracking - normally this is fine but each time its a complete guess on which path to go and I didnt get any enjoyment from that - felt like being lost in the desert with no clear way to go and path finding was a complete chore - im very easy to please with games so this was totally surprising for an Overwhelmingly Positive oneThe boss battles are great, this is a real ++ for the game - the sound music and visuals are also really pretty to listen to and see.This game just falls short for me, this could just be personal preference but I expected more - id give it a 6/10 overall but wouldnt recommend unless its on sale or you watch a brief youtube video to get an idea of the game
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I've played enough puzzle games to never be surprised again, but this game proved me wrong. The puzzles are very simple when broken down, but they're presented in such a way that will have you in awe. There were so many points where you'd think 'Surely I can't?' - but yes, in this world you can! The game presents you with couple of rules that you can always rely on to explore the solutions. They get progressively more complex as you're given more toys to play around with, but never to a point where you'll actually get stuck. The environment is laid out in a way that always gently pushes the player in the right direction. Makes the gameplay shorter but also smoother, so you get to enjoy the world building more (and oh boy there's plenty to enjoy). Genuinely a stellar experience. Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting idea at first. Get's incredibly repetitive very very quickly until the end when some more interesting puzzles are added. Basic loop is: move forward, drop key item, backtrack, pick up key item, move forward, drop key item, backtrack, pick up key item, backtrack again. _childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: For a "simple" game with basically one control, this packs a huge punch! I was blown away by how visually stunning everything is and the sound design is on another level. I love media that blends mechanical and biological life forms. There's a perfect balance between challenging puzzles and bosses without being too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I was in a puzzling mood after Thanksgiving dinner, when suddenly I found myself changed into a bug & thrust into a strange world with no explanation. _childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's just like Pathless or Journey, I don't seriously understand the hype even though I force myself through it. The art is marvelous, but that's about it. Puzzles aren't hard, just inconvenient most of the time. I didn't truly understand the story, maybe it's good but I won't pretend I understand by looking up some nobody's interpretation on YouTube unlike Elden Ring, this is just "another game".If I could, I would give this game on Steam a 6/10. An "okay", a "You won't regret beating it but I wouldn't pay full price".My TL;DR would be: "You aren't really wasting your time because the game is extremely easy and short". 3.7h, despite people on HLTB saying it's a 4.9h game. Maybe I've just played way too many puzzle games and I'm spoiled though.Unsure how DREDGE and Pizza Tower were considered worse than Cocoon other than the presentation and maybe the tech. _childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a masterclass in level and puzzle design.Moment to moment gameplay is engaging, with well layered and mind-bending puzzles, though I never felt out of my depth. The way they introduce the player to new mechanics is always very clear and beautifully done, so I always knew had the tools to hand, I just had to work out how to utilise them. The puzzles towards then end are a particular highlight, but I won't spoil them here.Also want to pay compliments to the visuals, which are sharp and clean with some gorgeous animations woven throughout. This all makes for some intriguing world based story-telling, raising questions about what exactly we are working towards here, and why a wee bug is carrying worlds on his back. No spoilers here.My only criticism is the price is perhaps a little steep for a game that lasts between 3-5 hours, but what is here is of the highest quality so it's personal preference.Genuinely incredible game, and the definition of an indie gem.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I am immensely satisfied with my time playing this game. It is first and foremost a puzzle platformer, and it excels as such. As portrayed in the promotional material, you control a small character on the screen which you can use to jump in and out of a variety of worlds. I absolutely love the visual aesthetic of each world and of the game overall, very much retaining that INSIDE DNA we've all come to know.There is absolutely no hand-holding (unless you count a small companion you meet at certain points in the game), and yet the puzzles are presented to you in a way that makes them almost instantly understandable. Some of them require quite a bit of pondering to figure out, while others will come to you almost as if by second nature. The main mechanic of this game is brilliant, with extremely smooth animations of jumping in and out of each world. The subsequent mechanics contained within each world only seek to elevate the complexity of each puzzle, while still remaining just understandable enough to make you feel like a genius after figuring out the solution. There was never really a point in the game where I had to look up the solution only to go "oh come on, seriously? *that's* how you do it?" Every puzzle was entirely intuitive and fun to figure out. I actually burst out with laughter in sheer disbelief once I saw how certain puzzles in this game played out (you'll know which ones I'm talking about when you get to them).The worlds are gorgeous and fun to explore. My only disappointment with this game lies within its short runtime, taking me only about 5 hrs to complete, and only another hour or so to find every  (achievement). However, due to the nature of how the puzzles expand in complexity with each world's new mechanic, it's easy to see why this game had to be limited so. And this disappointment in the game's length is only because I enjoyed every second of it. I simply wanted more. It's been years since I thoroughly enjoyed a game from start to finish as much as this one, and I can't wait to see what Geometric Interactive do next.I should also add: there were 0 bugs, technical issues, or performance issues throughout my entire playthrough. It ran as smooth as butter without a single stutter, despite never once presenting me with a loading screen after initially starting the game (discounting the necessary loading screens for selecting different save points).BUY THIS GAME NOW!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game to other players? No. Is it a bad game? Definitely not. The game is extremely short, linear, and frankly easy. It feels like baby's first puzzle game. If you had not played the bigger puzzle games in the genre before this then I can see how this game would blow your mind, but as it is it's not even better than it's predecessors of LIMBO and INSIDE, not to mention the dozens of other far superior puzzle games.This is one of the most overrated games I've ever played. If you want a good puzzle game series try Talos Principle 1+2.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Beautiful style and artistic design. This has some of the most innovative game and puzzle design I have seen in several years. All puzzles are pretty reasonable to follow, even when the game overlaps its mechanics into very intricate puzzles. Exceptional game, superb design, and all around great package.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give a positive review, but... it feels rather basic, especially if you've played LIMBO and INSIDE. _childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Just 100% completed it with 3-4 hours. I really liked it! Honestly want more and tougher puzzles (think they could've done a few more big ones at the end), these are pretty easy, but for a chill puzzle game with cool mechanics and honestly some REALLY good animation and art direction, a great time, it has a short, interesting story, not much of it I guess, which is fine, usually puzzle games struggle with that, although the end intrigues me for sure, hopefully a cocoon 2 eventually! _childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This puzzle game is absolutely fantastic. It does very little handholding, or explanation as to what is going on, but gives you just enough to make your next move. The mechanics are fantastic, and layer upon themselves brilliantly. As you keep playing, the game layers in more and more complexity and interactions in ways that feel natural and not contrived. There are so many WOW and AHA moments in this game. Highly, HIGHLY recommend you play Cocoon.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This puzzle game is truly extraordinary, featuring mind-blowing mechanics that leave a lasting impression. Solving puzzles in this game is immensely satisfying, especially as you delve deeper and encounter increasingly complex environments. The game's duration is perfectly balanced, offering just the right amount of content for an unforgettable experience. Once I started playing, I found it impossible to tear myself away.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. The visuals are great. The puzzles got a bit too complex for me towards the end of the game but overall it's very good. I like that this is a very "safe" puzzle game: everything on a level has a purpose, it's not possible to soft-lock yourself, and the moment some part of the puzzle is not needed anymore, it's removed. Some might think this makes puzzles too easy but it was really helpful to me. The game has its internal logic and follows it but sometimes the Orbs' interaction between each other was a bit confusing. Fortunately, as I said before, it's a very "safe" puzzle game and there's only one way you can do things, so a little (or a lot of) trial-and-error helps even if you don't completely understand how everything works.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is that one puzzle game I was waiting for. Take the the beautiful art style of an isometric adventure game and instead of holding the hand of players, let curiosity guide you through the world while challenging them on the way. I am about 3 worlds in so far, but this game is fantastic all around. Killer soundtrack, gorgeously appealing visuals, and probably one of the most amazing direction in puzzle design where juggling whole worlds is how you achieve your goals. I can't recommend this game enough, whether full price or not.I came here to add that after beating the game, everything still stands. THIS IS HOW YOU MAKE A GAME. No amount of bad dialogue can flesh out a story like one that simply tells it via music and the world while delivering insanely well developed puzzle mechanics that feel fresh at every stage of the game. It is like starting the game with a fork but finding out how to use it 15 different ways to make something happen. This is a must play game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have anything interesting to say, so here's a recipe on how to create chicken stew.   1) Roughly chop chicken thighs into chunks that are easy to manage with a fork.   2) Toss chicken in the flour mixed with the dried Italian or mixed herbs.   3) Preheat the oven to 150C regular bake, not fan.   4) Heat avocado or olive oil in a frying pan. Add chopped onion, crushed garlic, 2 x 410g seasoned tomatoes, sliced mushrooms and rindless, chopped bacon (middle). 5) Place into casserole dish when onion is translucent and mushrooms are lightly cooked. Add a little oil and in batches cook the chicken till just lightly golden and no more. Place in casserole dish with all the other ingredients except the wine.   6)Pour the wine into the pan that has been cooking the chicken. With all the "bits" left over in the pan from cooking the chicken, swirl the wine around. Pour that wine mix over the chicken in the casserole. Sprinkle with a little sea salt and any leftover herb flour.   7)Cover and cook for 2-3 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Artistic aesthetics. Beautiful, minimalistic 3d graphics with nice color palette and atmospheric lighting conditions.- Well designed sci-fi world full of peculiar places. Its mysterious atmosphere has something dreamy and dark simultaneously like a dull fairytale. Some sceneries are imposing too.- Amazing, smooth animations with flying things, moving mechanicals parts and floating particles. Protagonist's movement also feels fluid and pleasant.- Simple but effective controls. Every single of your various actions essentially uses the same single button. Yet, it never gets confusing.- Nicely designed puzzles that gradually introduce more gameplay mechanics so it never gets boring or repetitive. It has some tricky moments and some clever ideas, especially this with the interconnected worlds. Yet, it reaches its fully potential only during its very last part. Before that most of its puzzles are pretty unchallenging.- Through your journey you'll meet some unique, weird creatures designed with lots of imagination.-  Fantastic ambient music that manages to enhance the atmosphere without aiming to impress or become the protagonist.- Simple, yet cool audio design with some pleasant, convincing mechanical and environmental sounds.- It's so relaxing as you wonder solving puzzles and traveling from one world to another.The bad- Puzzles' mechanics are interesting, but it takes them too long  to become really creative. For the biggest part you mainly walk in a single path with only a few actions available so the solutions get pretty obvious. The core idea of interconnected worlds is used really imaginative only through the very last past of the game, but its too late. A missed opportunity for a great puzzle game.- The story is so abstract and full of cryptic symbolisms that fails to immerse the player. Also it doesn't feel organically connected to your actions and the puzzles. You solve puzzles just because they're there without really knowing why. Without giving you a specific purpose it soon gets less interesting.- There are boss fight that combine puzzle logic with some king of platforming sessions. They're too simplistic and easy though, with generic ideas that lack imagination.- Flat main character. He's cute visually for sure, but lacks any kind of personality that would allow the player to bond emotionally with him.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent puzzler/explorer w/ a handful of moderately-tough mini-bossesPros:* Good music* Intuitive map design - bonus points, won't let you lock yourself out by leaving items behind.* Fun puzzlesCons:* Nothing huge - only had one bug (got stuck - the quadrupedal miniboss kept punting me into a wall, I'd helplessly rebound back, controls locked, and he'd punt me again - ad infinitum)Meh:* I'm not a huge fan of action in my puzzle games, but you can repeat the minibosses w/o penalty.Colorblind folks: Might be challenging, some levels use shades of red/pink to delineate paths.TL;DR: If you like puzzles and don't mind occasional "combat", 9/10; if you just like puzzles, 7.5; else, avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played and enjoyed 'LIMBO' or 'INSIDE', 'COCOON' will be right up your alley. The visual art, world design, and soundscapes are immaculate. Though the puzzles aren't very difficult, they are excellently constructed in a 'Braid' / 'Portal' level of simplicity. It only took me a handful of hours to finish, but there are still a few achievements left to 100%. One caveat: the ending may be disappointing if you enjoy rich and detailed stories in your games. It's all non-verbal and non-textual (sort of like 'Little Nightmares' or 'YNGLET'), though the visuals and sound do pull off some cool reveals. The game is definitely atmospheric and immersive, just not much plot.EDIT: if you want to 100% the game, the bonus ending is ridiculously obscure and has such baffling design decisions, that I couldn't believe it was intended to be solved at all. I would recommend looking up a guide instead of trying to stumble into this unsatisfying gauntlet. Fortunately, the achievements themselves are not too hard and can probably all be found in your second run. Aside from the horrendous bonus ending secret, I still give this game the thumbs up overall.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful piece of art. Shorter than one might expect, at about 4-5 hours depending on whether you figure stuff out quickly, might take a tad longer if you take more time. To some, it may be a tad expensive, but as good games are too cheap anyhow, it is definitely worth the purchase on or off sale. Puzzles are simple, though a couple can be challenging for some. All puzzles remain elegant, never feeling scuffed or gimmicky. Only a few concepts are ever at play, and there isn't much variety in terms of mechanics, but the devs have done a fantastic job of diversifying the application of the mechanics. And that's none of that considers the aesthetics. This is a GORGEOUS game. There are a number of environments, meticulously designed and each unique. Effects are beautiful, gameplay feels smooth. And the sound design? gahdamn! Soundtrack is excellent, as befitting a game that excels so greatly in all other categories. Overall, at least 9-10/10 in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: i liked it.  short and sweet, took me about 5 hours of non-rushed gameplay. it tricked me into feeling clever.  lot's of puzzles, but you shouldn't get too hung up if you pay attention to the rules the game establishes.you do need to use your brain, but at the same time it feels like it rides on rails and you can't mess up.  i was wondering if I was just more clever than the average bear, but looking at game times most of us had the same experience.wouldn't recommend if you want long gameplay, replayability, AAA graphics or strong narrative.  would recommend if you want to feel engaged in a cool concept for a number of hours with great feel and scope working at a consistent and pleasing pace with a good sense of accomplishment and progression.i could see game design either being praised or lambasted, i never felt at a loss as to what to do, i only felt like i needed a little time to figure it out.  if you easily see through their tricks you'll realize this game isn't hard at all, if you are willing buy into the illusion it is a very pleasing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The game design itself is as good as flawless (except that it's a pure puzzle game, more about that below). I'm impressed by the simple controls, only using five buttons. Any other kind of input device, like analog sticks, are objects inside the game world. I think that's cool.The lack of humans however, or some kind of human language (in text or spoken), makes me feel alienated and unable to relate to anything that's going on in the game. There's also no story. You are just some alien bug doing stuff in an abstract world.Also, pure puzzle games are not really my thing, as they enforce a certain solution to a problem. That's actually, in my opinion, a bad design choice. But it's the entire genre that I don't like. I enjoy puzzles as secondary mechanics, second to exploration.So to balance the overwhelmingly positive reviews, I'll give this a no.

_childDocuments_.review: The king of the world would not be the same. A few people laughed, a few people cried, but most remained silent. I recalled a passage from the Hindu scripture, the Bhagavad-Gita, where Vishnu attempts to convince the prince to fulfill his duty. To impress him, Vishnu assumes his multi-armed form and declares, "Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds." I suppose, in one way or another, we all harbored similar thoughts.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A small bug-like creature emerges from an alien cocoon, stuck on a desert cliffside. Foreign technology scatters around the wasteland, and somehow you know how to operate some of the moving parts. Soon, a launchpad-like device catapults you outside of the desert and into another dimension. The desert you just inhabited is an orb you can carry with you. You move forward, deeper into the strange machinations presented by Inside's lead game designer Jeppe Carlsen in his new game Cocoon.The lineage of Cocoon's developers is very clear in the design. Retaining Inside and Limbo's one-button control setup, the complexities of the puzzles are not restricted by controls or minute decisions, but rather a pure understanding of recursive thinking and testing the limits of the unknown elements you find along the way. Various buttons and switches to a little guiding drone can clear the path ahead. While the puzzles get more and more layered, the game is generally approachable and walks an excellent balance of a-ha moments and temporary roadblocks. There were only 1 or 2 moments that truly stumped me, but time away from the game for a few minutes cleared my thoughts.Cocoon succeeds in almost every way at providing players with a steady sense of wonder and discovery, while not blowing the game's length out of proportion. While I think some more late game puzzles could have taken some of the large ideas further, Cocoon wants you to see its conclusion rather than be stumped at some point in the journey. Within the 4-5 hour adventure, you may happen upon secrets, but generally the path is linear, and expertly so, removing completed and irrelevant elements to focus players on the current task at hand. On my first playthrough, achievements were bugged, but that issue has since been fixed and it is now easy to tell what you have missed.In a year with so many massive titles, both in spectacle and in length, Cocoon manages to stand out through its simple, but precise gameplay loop filled with excellent solves and odd worlds to dive in and out of. It is one of the year's best titles and can easily be played in a weekend. Don't skip the newest great puzzle phenomenon.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: "Dünya İçinde Dünya" kavramını tam anlamıyla bize yaşatan ve Inception kadar kafa karıştıran bir oyun. Uzun zamandır oynadığım en kendine has, özel oyunlardan biriydi. Oyun bittiği için üzüldüm. Bölüm tasarımları dahiyane bir şekilde hazırlanmış. Bazı bölümlerde ciddi manada kafa yoruyorsunuz. Bazen bölümü geçmenin bir yolu yok diye düşünüyorsunuz ama nasıl geçeceğinizi çözdüğünüz anda bölüm tasarımcılarının önünde saygıyla eğiliyorsunuz. Boss fightlar çok iyiydi. Farklı mekanikler ve farklı ortamlar ile oyun daha keyifli hale geliyor. Oyunu daha fazla övmek istiyorum ama ne kadar översem öveyim yetersiz gelecekmiş gibi geliyor. Ödülleri boşuna toplamamış. O yüzden sadece alıp oynayın diyorum.The game literally gives us the concept of "World Within a World" and confuses us as much as Inception. It's one of those special games that's totally different. I felt bummed when I finished it. The levels are super cleverly designed. Some of them really make you think hard. Sometimes you're stuck and think there's no way out, but when you figure it out, you gotta give props to the level designers. The boss fights were awesome too. Different tricks and places make the game more fun. I want to hype this game up more, but no matter how much I say, it doesn't feel like enough. It totally deserves all the awards it got. So, just go get it and play it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a really great premise, but is ultimately let down a bit in execution. In short: this feels like half of a game. While the mechanics are cool, they remain pretty easy until the final puzzle, after which the game ends. I feel like this concept could have been taken further, but the game stops just as it gets going.Same thing goes for the story. Everything is so indistinct that it’s hard to get emotionally invested in anything that’s happening like in Inside or Limbo. I know this game isn't going for the same thing those ones are, but the story is just kind of uninteresting. Again, there’s a sort of cool development at the end, but the game just stops after that.I would still recommend it based on the unique mechanics and solid (if easy) puzzle design, but I just wish it was taken further.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A tightly woven gem of a puzzle game. No UI, no words, but it never needs any. A nice variety of puzzles that challenge the brain in different ways, while all being relatively similar difficulty. The sound design is TIGHT and the visuals and themes are super creative. Story was satisfying, and it didn't overstay its welcome!The only knock against this game is there is no vibration intensity slider, and sometimes the rumble gets VERY intense. Also, you will want a controller to play it. Annapurna and fmod continue to put out some really solid stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The jaw dropping aesthetic, incredibly unique biomes, and the fantastic dynamic of puzzle solving with all the different orbs kept me on the edge of my seat the entire time. There wan't a single moment that I wasn't absolutely awed by what I was seeing and desperate to find out what came next. The buildup and payoff of the ending wraps up a magnificent game with an equally impressive finale. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I consider myself a beginner in the world of video-games as I started gaming 1.5 years ago at the age of 59. During this time I have experierinced different entertaining game-genres. However, those of problem-solving charachter appeals most to me.
