_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A very impressive game. If you liked Limbo and inside, you' certainly love this one. My only regret about this game is the complete absence of storytelling or scenario, I mean there isn't even environmental storytelling like in Inside : the synopsis is really just 'you're an abstract hero in an imaginary abstract world purposelessly trying to reach the next room'. So it's purely a game design thing, but what a game design masterpiece! As a game developer myself, I can tell this game is really a textbook example of how to create a complex game design just with a few simple features. It starts very easy, then it progressively add new features and combines them in more and more complex and intricate ways, without ever repeating the same resolution logic twice. The game also manages to be challenging enough without ever being frustrating or resorting to a 'hints' system (I was just blocked once in the entire game, for like 20 minutes).The game also enforces (very strictly) that you can never get soft-locked or waste time in a previous zone where you don't have anything to do anymore, and I really appreciated that. (without some of the strategically positioned no-return points, I probably would have go back and wander for 30 minutes in the search of non-existent solutions, so thanks for that)
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with amazing visuals and a stellar soundtrack.   Has some interesting interpretations to the story, but does not shove it in your face either.  Puzzles are really fun and engaging, but my only complaint is how long some can take making it difficult to remember what you are trying to achieve.  Juggling the orbs is a bit of a headache overtime also, but that could be from playing a puzzle game for over 4 hours straight.  Definitely worth a play through, but maybe do it across two gaming sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best puzzle games I've ever played. Its concept is simple yet unique, layering its mechanics on top of each other like different, flavorful stacks of cake. The soundtrack and sound design is incredible from start to finish. Although the puzzles aren't too perplexing, it strikes a great balance of simplistic and challenging gameplay. The team has created an immensely satisfying experience and enough to provide drops of dopamine as you explore COCOON's colorful and immersive worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter than I expected, but a very nice concept that results in some really mind-bending puzzles that will leave you feeling dumb once you figure them out, but never feel cheap. The visuals are really nice, and there's some good immersive storytelling going on, with each world having a distinct feel.My main gripe is the price, I picked it up on sale and still paid almost £20 for 5 hours of game play, which feels a  little too pricey.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of value for game play and puzzle from just two input controls is staggering and mind boggling. The design is air tight and cannot be overstated of how good it is. Cocoon takes a simple concept and controls and makes its puzzle warp the player's mind without breaking it. New puzzle mechanics are introduced organically so that the immersion is never broken by new puzzle types. This game is an example to those who want to learn game design with as little to no direct intervention from the games creators (ex: no need for tutorials if everything is intuitive).tldr: Awesome, simple, complex and well design. If you can afford it and like puzzle games, get this game!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzle/level design here is superb, head-scratching but not bruising. There's an almost nonstop variety of ideas; some conventional, many unlike anything else I've seen in a game before. I'd say it falters only the slightest bit when you're doing the sections that require you to activate symbols in the correct order, but even those aren't carbon copies of each other. Immersion has been polished to basically perfection, with zero loading screens after the first boot-up, unintrusive controls, and incredible sounding atmosphere and music. I would've loved a standout challenging final boss after how cool the previous ones were, though I was very satisfied with how the game wrapped up regardless. Any game that has excellent artistic merit while refusing to deprive us of creative and interesting gameplay should be praised.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon has gorgeous presentation and a slick premise that never delivers on its potential. The biggest detractor for this game is the puzzles. They only really get engaging at the very end. Throughout the first 3/4 of the game, Cocoon essentially plays itself. It looks amazing, has excellent environment design and a killer soundtrack but in the end I think this is an example of a game that is less than the sum of its parts.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little game. You have no idea what to do or where to go while simultaneously knowing where to go and what to do. The game is very well designed and looks AMAZING. It's nothing like any other game I've played. The puzzles are easy to understand but sometimes makes you stop and think about it as near the end they get a little perplexing but not overwhelmingly so. If there is a sequel I would buy it in a heartbeat. I love this game. It is small as I completed it in 7 hours but I'm ok with it since it was an awesome journey into a surreal world.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's challenging enough to be interesting, but not enough for you to get stuck for more than a few minutes on any given puzzle. It also does a great job of locking backward movement to constrain the possibility space of your puzzle solution and keep you from veering off in some totally wrong direction. That perfect difficulty keeps you engaged while you absorb the incredible visual and audio design, which match the game design in quality.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most inventive puzzle games I've played in a good while. I just wish that there were a few more hard puzzles. The game doesn't seem like the sorta thing to get a sequel, but a DLC adding 'challenge levels' would be amazing. Anyway, don't let the difficulty or the length of the game deter you, it's worth every penny :D
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I feel a bit weird giving COCOON a "do not recommend" because it isn't offensively bad.It has some genuinely excellent boss fights, and the biomechanical artstyle reminds me of Scavengers Reign (which I loved). Unfortunately, the game's high moments are heavily diluted by unusual but droll traversal and by-the-numbers why-even-bother "puzzles".The main gimmick of the game (you gain traversal abilities depending on which orb you're carrying) also isn't a winner. It just turns what would ordinarily be seamless and automatic into "*sigh* I need the light bridge ability, so I guess I have to swap around orbs again." The traversal options aren't even all that interesting. The light bridge ability allows you to cross very specific gaps in a visually interesting way and that's it. The pillar ability allows you to toggle/ascend pillars in a visually interesting way and that's it. The abilities can't even interact with each other because - again - you can only have one ability at a time and switching abilities is an involved process.All of this over the course of about 5 hours  if COCOON was a budget title somewhere around 10-15 USD, but it's on the expensive side for an indie game at a whopping 25 USD. That's more expensive than LIMBO and INSIDE - either of which I'd consider superior - combined!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: So many amazing things to say about this game! Beautiful visual style, nice music, super cool and challenging puzzles. Fantastic character and world design! It's mysterious story is really fun to unfold. If you like Death's Door, Tunic, or other games like that then you'll probably love it! Give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely unique and enjoyable game, refreshingly abstract in its sounds, visuals and structure and with some of the most creative puzzle creations I've engaged with without being so complex as to stump the player for longer than a few minutes.   Narrative and lore are very vague in a way that befits the prophetic, tone-shifting, sci-fi style.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Coming off The Game Awards 2023 and this title winning GOTY in the indie category I had my hopes up upon trying it out. So, did it meet the hype?For starters, this puzzle game has a really alien, eerie and sometimes borderline creepy but mysteriously intriguing atmosphere that is portrayed in an isometric perspective and a variety of ecosystems with various life forms. Most of them are bugs, as the one you control is, and the soundtrack certainly delivers on that unsettling feeling of arriving to a place you don't really know but can tell it's alive or persisting on the ruins of a previous civilization. But why put so much on the setting for a cinematic puzzle game?Well, much like Limbo and Inside, this one conveys the logic of how to overcome its obstacles by not giving you a single line of dialogue nor instructions but instead relying on the background and the player to figure it out with what they have. Some indicators make some assumptions pretty straight forward while others rely a bit more on thinking outside the box or maybe changing your perspective. Indeed, the latter plays a major part in the way you interact with orbs you find along your journey, ending in some trippy yet not so mind bending transitions that may give you a brain scratch with a satisfying conclusion.Nonetheless, even with how intuitive some of the solutions were I didn't feel too challenged up until some of the last puzzles which were coincidentally the most clever ones. This doesn't make the game bad necessarily but at points it felt a bit stale despite having some boss fights here and there which switched up the gameplay for more time focused confrontations.Even with that, I can't really say understate that my overall experience left me wanting to know more about the world and eager for more puzzles to be solved. As to the question of whether the award is deserved I'd say that I'm not too confident on that personally but can respect it either way.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with nice atmosphere, beautiful sceneries and details.As for the puzzle part, it's not that hard, yet they are clever and use all the original mechanics very well without overusing them. A bit of Patrick Parabox's feeling, without the crazy difficulty.A bit on the short side, though, and for that it's a 9.5/10 recommendation, if you like clever puzzling it's a must try
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This puzzler is super unique. If you've games with inventory management, prepare for a puzzle game with world management. The atmosphere and world design is good. It takes a bit of time before the puzzles pick up. Once the puzzles start getting really interesting the game ends soon after which is kind of a bummer, but it's a neat experience. There doesn't seem to be an alternate ending for reaching all secret areas unless I'm blind.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a debut game of Geometric Interactive which is co-founded by expirienced game designer Jeppe Carlsen who was one of the main developers of Playdead's Limbo and Inside (and left it after release of Inside), programmer/composer Jakob Schmid who previously helped Carlsen in making of 2 indie games (140 and THOTH) and art director Erwin Kho.I personally wasn't amazed with this game, but I believe that it's because of other puzzle games with similar mechanics and art. In addition to previously named Limbo and Inside that also were the games narrated without a single word being said, it's Portal, The Swapper and Patrick's Parabox in terms of spatial, dimenional puzzles and recursion, it's Tunic with its epic lore, majestic setting and also the same perspective. And many more titles can come to mind, but Cocoon is definitely not copying any of those, so that partial similarities are not it's flaws. Frankly, I can't come up with any faults or weaknesses of Cocoon for people who are into puzzle games.It's perfectly thought through, very well made, the art of Erwin Kho felt fresh for me. Soundtrack doesn't stand out much, but feels in place, consisting mostly of electronic synth ambient, sometimes interspersed with monumental synthesizers like from PS1 start up sound or synths that are not that grand. For me it stood out only at times when it should - when sounds like they came from Oneohtrix Point Never's tracks told me that I'm going in right direction or doing proper actions. Its puzzles are not plain and not hardcore like, for example, some Patrick's Parabox riddles. To find all 11 collectibles you don't have to be genius and it's definitely possible to do without youtube, but if you miss it, you can freely load a moment in game where it was, grab it and go back to the place where you left off, and it's rather pleasant. Also huge thanks for devs for unobtrusively closing paths that shouldn't be used any more.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, finished it under a day but it was a good day because this game made me feel good and smart. I wonder how much play-testing this game went through because it really teaches you without using any typical guidance, no text, no dialogue, just play randomly with what you find and you'll discover how everything works eventually. Very solid gameplay loop.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A platformer with a simplified style, featuring an incredible surrealist atmosphere of the insect world, filled with peculiar puzzles and interesting adventures.Despite the change in genre, there are strong references to the game 'Inside' (controlling a strange slug remotely xD).However, the story is not as captivating as the original. Nevertheless, I highly recommend it for a few hours of great fun.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what you'd expect from the makers of Limbo and Inside. Really beautiful and eerie art style and soundtrack. Puzzles were just the right level of intensity for a chill play through (though the  gets a little tedious towards the end). It's a pretty short game (5-7 hours incl. hunting for the handful of secrets), so I'd suggest waiting for a sale, since the $25 sticker price is a tad steep.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept of entering, exiting tiny worlds of puzzles, I had a great time, thanks!I had some trouble playing in on Mac M2 Max, I tried installing it on Whisky.app (on which I installed Steam) which always led to a black screen.I ended up installing it in a Parallels Desktop virtual Machine and it ran very smoothly ! (the entering/exiting of world were stuttering, and some heavy animations would freeze the screen for 3-6s, despite that, the game is completely playable)
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are great. The game doesn't really reward exploration very much.It's a linear walking simulator with some very light puzzle elements and a couple of simple boss fights sprinkled in. The puzzle solutions are all really easy, which is a bit of a let down. You'll figure out the solution instantly, but then it usually takes a couple minutes to physically walk around and move the marbles to the spots to progress, which can be more frustrating than fun.It's not clear when the game creates new save states, and they seem to be fairly infrequent. This means when you quit and come back you'll have to go through a bunch of areas you have already been through and re-do the tedious part of solving them all over again which isn't that much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game which does a great job of playing around with it's core mechanic which is carrying around different orbs which have different effects on the environment. It starts to get a bit mind bending when you start going inside different orbs and bringing other orbs in with you. It's got a really great art style and the puzzle are really satisfying to complete but do yourself a favour and try to play this is a fairly short period of time. If you take a break and/or play other games in between, it can be really easy to forget what you were doing and how things work and end up feeling completely lost!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The game is perfectly designed. The gameplay, the graphics, the programming, and sounds are top-notch. Follows the Playdead heritage well. The plot may be dull (the protagonist goes through a linear journey). The puzzles are well designed, maybe the first few minutes are too basic, but everything is perfectly balanced throughout the game. Things never get too repetitive. The last few percent of the game felt like it was designed with Charlie Kafuman's mindset.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give Cocoon a nice review, it's a nice little artsy indie puzzle game.There are no glaring issues! It's a fine game. But it's not really worth playing.Only in the final puzzle of the game is the core mechanic actually used to its fullest. The rest of the game is barely more than "walk forward, click button".That is except the boss fights, which are a fleeting distraction at best and annoying at worst.Some games can get by on looks alone and Cocoon has that high-polish indie artsy-fartsy style that will win them a bunch of awards. But it didn't do anything for me.It's abstract surrealist cosmic... bug. I've seen it before.It made no attempt to intrigue me or pull me into a story or the world, it's just pretty visuals over a middling puzzle game. Pretty wallpaper on a boring house.There's a lot of small, almost dev, details that I appreciate. Cocoon is by all means a very well made game: solid art style, QoL save system, puzzle design that avoids backtracking, and even a unique concept. It is just unfortunately... boring.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The prime example of how an extremely "simple" gameplay (you use one button throughout the whole game) can be used to craft one of the deepest, most complex experiences you can find.Everything is spot on, level and environment design, art style, animations, effects... the soundtrack is amazing as well.An absolute masterclass in game design.Absolutely a must-play, provided you like environmental puzzles, because that's what this game is, literally one giant, mesmerizing, truly amazing puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a really fantastic puzzle game.7/10The art style is beautiful.Each world has its own theme and each are just as captivating as the last.Minor eye candies around the levels really help to pull the the environments together.Animations are quick and satisfying.One of my favorite things about this game is the way this game does not TELL you anything. Not once does the game TELL you what to do.Cocoon does an incredible job SHOWING the player how they are able to use the tools they've been given, and leaving the rest up to the player to figure it out.The puzzles start simple and they build on previous mechanics expertly well.(The later puzzles might have you scratching your head, but just remember to try stuff even if you think it wont lead anywhere.)There are a few boss fights, but the combat is not super exhilarating. (The boss fights are more like fast-paced puzzles.)I beat the entire game in about 4 hours, though I haven't unlocked all of the steam achievements. (Some of the Moon Ancestors are pretty well hidden, and there doesn't seem to be any option for backtracking. If you intend to 100% the game- it looks like you'll need to be sure to find each Moon Ancestor as soon as you have the option.)I bought the game for $25, and I'd say that it isn't quite worth that price.Cocoon is a VERY Well put together game, but I would probably only recommend picking it up if it goes on sale to bring it under $15-$20.I didn't encounter any bugs on my play-through.Wish the game was longer. (I also wish backtracking to pick up missed Moon Ancestors was an option.)There is definitely TONS of rooms for more complex puzzles in an expansion or sequel of some sort.Solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: not satisfying enough for experienced puzzle fans, or people who've played through one too many low-poly indie bite sized personal voyage stories.I mostly enjoyed my time with it, but I think it's overhyped and not worth the $20 I paid so I want to put in a contrarian view. It doesn't fully explore the mechanics it introduces, and recursion has been done better. There's more looking for the next path than thinking about what to do, and the environmental art doesn't always cooperate. Does inspire that hey-neato feeling in a couple of spots and worth picking up sometime when it's sub-$10.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon Review (In-Progress)Cocoon immediately captivates with its art style—simple yet stunning, creating a visually compelling world. The sound design is equally enchanting, delivering sparkly and ethereal tones that complement the atmosphere beautifully. The music also ramps up in intensity during battles, which I really enjoy.The puzzles start off light and not too difficult, though some do become trickier. Still, they remain manageable, avoiding frustration while keeping things engaging. There’s also a bit of combat, though it’s not your typical action-heavy fare—more of a “hit the boss three times and move forward” approach.Overall, I’m really enjoying the experience so far. I haven’t completed the game yet, but I’d definitely recommend it based on what I’ve played.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It might have head and body of "Limbo" and "Inside" (Jeppe Carlsen), but it doesn't have its soul (Arnt Jensen). It's disingenuous to ride on the hype of the Playdead games because "Cocoon" is nothing to compare with them. There's no story, no emotion. You just do stuff because you can or because it blocks you from doing other stuff without any point or explanation. There's no satisfaction in resolving puzzles. Every puzzle had me like: "Oh, it's like this. Ok, I guess, whatever". It's Inception-like traversals don't bring anything to the gameplay, but it's just a gimmick which looks "cool" in the trailer. I think I'll try "Somerville" instead despite its negative reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a fantastic puzzle game and it is easily one of the best games of 2023.It immerses you extremely well into its world without saying a line of text. The music is great and it makes each world you visit feel unique. The art direction is memorable and it keeps you curious about where you will go next.I don't usually play puzzle games but Cocoon flowed so well that before I realized, I was at the end of the game. It makes you, literally, think outside of the box and the feeling of completing a more complex puzzle is awesome!So, even if you are not fond of puzzle games, Cocoon is absolutely recommended! Make sure you turn off the lights, put some headphones on, grab a controller and you will be in for a fantastic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I loved LIMBO and INSIDE, but somehow I missed this one until now. What a gorgeous and brilliant little puzzle game! COCOON is one of those near perfect games like Portal that manages to make the player feel clever by gradually and intuitively introducing new mechanics, with a healthy sense of wonder sprinkled in for good measure. It's amazing how many ways they found to use a single button, and to mask the gameplay that is essentially linear. While there is some backtracking required, there are many thoughtful nudges to keep you from going too far down the wrong path.I only have a few nitpicks that would make this an even better game:1) Several of the boss battles and action sequences were frustrating, since you have to start over from the beginning if you mess up. In a game that is otherwise strictly a puzzle game, these action sequences seem out of place. Perhaps a checkpoint system or more lenient difficulty ramp would feel more balanced.2) Given the short playtime and no real replay value, the regular price of $24.99 USD feels very steep. I picked it up for 40% off, which is still a bit of a stretch but I think that is fair for a game this good.3) The game would benefit from an on-screen icon when it is autosaving, since there is no manual save function. Several times I quit and loaded back in, only to realize my most recent progress hadn't been saved...I guess I hadn't made as much progress as I thought!All that to say, I highly recommend this, and it is one of the best games I've played in recent memory.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real tricky head F*ck of a game. I don't know how they thought this one up.Butt if you like PUZZLES, playing with your BALLS and trying about a Billion combinations then this game is for you.REAL BRAIN TEASER.TRICKY TRICKY TRICKY.Each stage/level will test your BRAIN.It will make you say that is IMPOSSIBLE. BUT THERE IS A SOLUTION.SOMETIMES YOU HAVE TO THINK OUTSIDE OF THE COLORED BALLS
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, although it has the same problem as many mainstream puzzle games: it doesn't explore its mechanics nearly as much as it could have.While I think this game could easily have been better, I still like it for what it is. The puzzles on offer are good, if a tad easy for my tastes, and the visuals and sound design are excellent, as to be expected from one of the guys who made Limbo and Inside, they're great at that stuff.Expect around 4-6 hours to beat the game and maybe a little bit more for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just blown away by how someone managed to think some of these puzzles up. That's some 4-dimensional creativity! In some cases to solve a puzzle in one universe you have to go to a path not taken in a different universe... It's mind boggling.Great game! I get that it's short but after playing a couple of hours I was already saying - that's money well spent. I honestly don't like long games, so this is perfect.This is the game that tries something new and different, just like Viewfinder, which I just recently completed as well. What a great year for little gaming gems!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely masterful game design.  The puzzles are conveyed in a way that challenges you but never frustrates and the subtle visual and audio cues along the path reinforce good decisions in a reassuring and motivating way.  The graphics are engrossing and to get so much variable gameplay out of a joystick and one button is commendable and all too rare in modern gaming.  Sublime.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a visual and auditory experience. The puzzles started fairly simple, but as you get deeper in they get more and more complex and creative, until eventually it blows your mind with some of the things it makes you do to find solutions. This bends the mind the way portal did when I first played it, but on a whole new level. Couldn't even begin to guess what the 'plot' is, or what's going on. But I thoroughly enjoyed it.Cocoon is a shorter game. It took me about 4 hours to play through it, and I didn't manage to %100 it. I missed some of the hidden objectives, but I felt the whole experience was well worth full price. Solid thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant puzzle game without any spoken or written word.You will have to figure out how everything works on this alien world.The unique concept in this game are the 'world orbs' -- orbs that can be CARRIED (at which point they are granting you a special ability), they can be placed into 'button sockets' (at which point they activate a nearby mechanism), or they can be placed into 'world sockets' -- at which point you (or other objects) can ENTER the worlds and explore them.You can only carry one world orb at a time, but there are (at least) 4 of them, so you will be switching between them, placing orbs within orbs (or even orbs within orbs within orbs), to be able to carry all of them to a new location.Around the ~3 hour mark of the game, you then start seeing puzzles in which an energy projectile hits a world orb placed in a world socket -- which means the energy projectile enters the embedded world and does something inside.The game is very linear -- the designers tightly control where you can go, even blocking your path back once you have successfully solved a particular milestone puzzle, so that you don't wander aimlessly.At the end of each 'world', there is a puzzle boss, where you have to outsmart a big boss to steal its power. These boss battles are very nicely designed and while you are probably going to fail them a few times, it's never frustrating.The graphics is truly amazing - the flat shaded / low poly alien biospheres you explore build the atmosphere of exploring an alien world.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: oh.. my.. god.. that was absolutely amazing!all of the environments feel so alive, with an attention to detail that very few titles can compete with. on top of that, each of the 4 different sphere "domains" feel incredibly unique, which just brings a whole new level of depth to the game's puzzles.speaking of which, the puzzles are so well crafted.. I don't think I've had so much fun looking for patterns in the chaos since playing "Castle of Dr Brain" as a kid back in the 90's... the whole concept of using "portals" to jump in and out of the spheres, often multiple levels deep, and sometimes even recursively, is nothing short of incredible. I also greatly appreciate the way that none of them seemed to have any way to "soft lock" the player, very cleverly done.the one and only downside I can think to highlight is the 3rd "boss fight" (spinning blade boss, with the 6 compartments in a ring where you switch sides), which was unexpectedly difficult... all others took me no more than 2 attempts, while this one took me 5.but in the end, for a game with a mere 5 inputs and absolutely no spoken or written language, this interactive graphical novel spoke utter volumes... I'm already looking forward to playing through it again!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Half-way in: This game really ticks all the boxes within the genre and sucked me in for a chill and amazing problem solving/puzzle experience.Game completed: Best 20 bucks spent in a long time, would easily payed the double for the same experience, what a well put together and beautiful looking game with a great soundtrack. Holding thumbs for a follow up game in the near future.Overall: 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Short well-polished puzzle-like game with unique visuals, sound and play style and very easy controls. Progress is linear with most puzzles being combinatorial in nature including the occasional easy timed run, unfortunately also punctuate often enough by required reflex-based boss fights that, while beautifully done, feels aggravating and out of place compared to the serene and zen-like puzzle solving game play. The puzzles drew me in, while the boss fights drew me out, but at least I did manage to get all puzzles done. Your mileage may vary.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.user: a u t o m a t i c
_childDocuments_.review: If you liked 'INSIDE' and you enjoy mind-bending alien worlds and puzzle games, then just buy this game and play it already!... and DON'T LOOK UP ANY GAMEPLAY VIDEOS (unless you get stuck).You can thank me later.After beating the game, I will say that I wasn't thrilled with how many of the puzzles that I have come across in the back half of the game that seemed like "busy work" to me as opposed to puzzles that actually make you use the game mechanics in new ways.  IMO, this was quite disappointing.  Still... good game though.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I played this at the recommendation from a few people that this was "mind-blowingly good." I guess my expectations were a bit high. I did really enjoy the puzzles, and easily give it a thumbs up, but there's no story, no twists, and the main mechanic while well done, also seemed to never reach its full potential to me.Expectations have a lot to do with a game, and I think mine were too high going in, so I didn't enjoy it as much as I could have. I still enjoyed it and recommend it to puzzle lovers. But I guess gauge your expectations?
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game while it was on sale and tried it out recently after finishing STRAY on the Steam Deck. Overall, I did not like it. _childDocuments_.review: It's a charming little game. Doesn't take the "world within worlds" concept as far as Recursed did but it has a lot else going for it. Great art design, sound and music for example. Some people aren't liking the boss fights but I think they're quite fun. Just think of them as timed puzzles. Overall it exceeded my expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why people may like this, I mean the aesthetic alone is worth it BUT....The puzzles are so bland and annoying with their backtracking and pretty much unoriginality that I can't force myself to keep pushing.The game is extremely linear and it's clear it's made for a wider audience, which is good to be honest but I need captivating original puzzle games, and it seems like the developers  didn't want  or couldn't push what the main puzzle mechanic of the game should be (which is interesting by the way) and make more use of it.Overall, to puzzle gamers I can't recomend it
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: If I got a penny every time I played a good game about a space beetle, I'd have two pennies. Which isn't a lot, but it's still weird that it's happened twice.'s design is very neat. Imagine that you have a puzzle with several abilities, but each ability is also a level with an internal structure that you can use other abilities in. This allows the game to be extremely simple with controls — you only have movement and one button (that you don't even get a prompt for — the game is completely wordless!). Complexity arises from combining abilities and sometimes using them inside each other.Such a design can get mindboggling very quickly, and not necessarity in a good way. (My brain did kind of break when I placed an ability sphere within itself at a later stage of the game.) All the more impressive, then, that  doesn't become insanely complicated. If anything, it errs on the side of being easier and choosing spectacle over very complex puzzles — most of them don't have too many elements, and the game pays careful attention to lock unnecessary backtracking to make sure the player isn't confused.I liked the game's take on bosses — they challenge your logical thinking rather than twitch skills. And the overall presentation is lovely.I wish the game was longer and harder without becoming more complex. But even as is, it's a lovely brainteaser for one big gaming session. And the spectacle is indeed lovely.

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a simplistic puzzle game with very vague stakes. You play as some sort of humanoid insect person, and you are solving puzzles. The central conceit of the game is that you are jumping between worlds, with each world contained in an orb. Place these orbs on certain places, and you can jump into the world inside of them; there are bouncy platforms in each world which will launch you out of the world back to the main world.This is a one-button game; you have directional controls, and you have an action button, which lets you pick up a sphere, place it on a designated position (you can’t drop them wherever you want, you have to put them on stands), activate things in the environment, and activate your currently carried sphere’s special power once you unlock it.While this seems very simple – and it is – the game manages to do a number of quite clever things with it, leading to increasingly clever puzzles as you unlock more and more of the spheres. As you get more of them, you have to do ever more elaborate puzzles involving jumping between spheres and manipulating them to get across obstacles, and by the end of it, it has added some additional ways of getting between spheres that further increases the game’s ability to use these simple mechanics and push them to their limit.The game’s puzzles are actually quite clever overall, and I think that the game did some interesting things with them – this is one of the best games that involves nothing more complicated than moving things around, and the visuals of jumping between worlds are quite cool.However, while the game’s puzzles are pretty clever overall, it’s not Portal; this is a pretty mechanically simple game, and while it ends up making the puzzles work pretty well, I honestly don’t know why this game is so hyped up. It’s definitely a decent puzzle game, but I didn’t feel like the puzzles were as clever as they were in, say, The Talos Principle 2; the game’s puzzles are all pretty simple and straightforward, and while there are some clever bits in there, you’re unlikely to ever get stuck, as the game is very deliberate in limiting the number of options, which helps you to find the solution as there’s only a small possibility space.That said, if you do like puzzles, it’s certainly clever enough.The game, rather unexpectedly, has boss fights as well; there’s not a huge number of them, but they work well enough, and they help mix things up and add a bit of action-based excitement. If you get caught by the boss, you get chucked up out of the sphere you’re inside, allowing you to go back in and go fight the boss again, and none of them are overly difficult or long. It works pretty well, and once you figure out that there are bosses, you have something to look forward to, as beating them is what unlocks the sphere’s special powers, leading to some new puzzles.Overall, the gameplay works well enough, and I thought it was quite decent; the game also knew it didn’t have TOO many ideas, so it kept things short, with a 100% play time of under 6 hours – in fact, it was likely under 5 hours, as I spent some time chatting to friends while playing.On the other hand, story wise, this game is very, very weak indeed. You are some sort of humanoid insect, but what your agenda is – what your purpose in doing the things you’re doing – is never really made clear, and this isn’t the kind of game that has audio logs or any sort of text descriptions in it. There’s honestly very little if any story to speak of, and while I think that the creators had some ideas in this regard, the game does a poor job of communicating them. As such, if you are a more narrative-focused player, you will find literally nothing here – go play Portal or The Talos Principle.Overall, this is a very decent puzzle game, and worth playing if you like the genre – but I feel like the 88 metacritic score makes this seem like a really amazing game, but I thought it was merely quite decent for what it was, but nothing that I think you’re missing out if you never play it. I liked my time with this game well enough, and if you like puzzle games, you probably will too – but it’s a good game, not a great one. Go in with that expectation in mind, and you’ll probably come away satisfied; go in expecting this to be the puzzle game of the year, though, and you probably won’t find it to quite reach those heights.

_childDocuments_.review: "Cocoon" - a game so simple, yet so complex. Wow!The world of "Cocoon" is visually stunning, fascinating, - a place where structures mix with nature, where machinery meet biology. The feeling of mystery, uncertainty, weirdness is only heightened by the incredibly unique soundtrack and sound design. But wait, did I say world? I mean worlds, of course. Over time, you will collect orbs. When held, each orb grants a different capability, necessary to solve puzzles and continue on with the adventure. But each orb is also an actual pocket world, a world that you can both travel into and out of, a world with its own puzzles and progression. And so it happens that things get more and more crazy as you realize that orbs can be carried into other orbs, worlds can live inside other worlds ... And all that with a single button for any interaction. Despite these super-simplified controls, the occasional boss fights do actually work surprisingly well.Two additional remarks. For one, the story is pretty slim and open for interpretation, so it's the puzzles and environments that shine here. Second, and more importantly, this game is very linear. Not an issue per se, but maybe unexpected. My guess is that the puzzle mechanics, especially towards the end, already felt pretty mindbending. Moving these concepts into a more open world / metroidvania style would've probably been a tad too complex for many players and rather challenging for the developers to pull off properly (especially for the first game of this kind). "Cocoon" is already pretty clever in guiding you, both by its level design and audio cues. Maybe a successor could be able to bring these brilliant ideas to the next level.I do highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for you.  Its visuals are stunning, and the animations, even better.  It is an absolute masterpiece.  I can promise that you will think the same. I myself haven't yet complete it, so I couldn't quite tell you what the end goal is, because there are no cutscenses, hints, UI, or even worse other than the menu, so you are left to figure it out yourself.  This makes it feel a bit lacking in story, but it makes up for it in the satisfaction of completing a puzzle.  One of the reasons I love this game so much, is that it makes you feel lonely, yet relaxed due to lack of npcs or dialogue.  It's art style makes me so happy. I would have finished it all in one sitting had it not been for My PC.  All in all, this game is insanely amazing and I would recommend it to anyone and I am also looking forward geometric interactives new games that they will release in the future, so please buy this game in order to support them.

I would say that the game solves them for you, but not in a condescending way. Instead, you are left with the feeling of awe at how cleverly the puzzle is designed and are rewarded with an angelic chime for correctly guessing what to do. So my advice would be to trust the game and let it lead you. A couple of puzzles were so mind-boggling that I thought to myself "No way this is what's going to happen" and then it did and played the chimes.Lastly, if you enjoyed the wordless storytelling and world-building of "Sky: Children of the Light" or "Hyper Light Drifter", I think you should check out this game.

I'm already familiar with the idea of "worlds are items and can be taken into other worlds" from Recursed, which takes the idea much further, with mechanics such as duplicating worlds, or worlds being able to contain themselves. No regular enemies, no story being told, just puzzles and bosses. Very tight design on the puzzles and worlds, the developers intentionally constrained things to ensure you never feel too lost. Doesn't even have an inventory, you just pick things up one at a time and control it all with a single button.There's also some sidepath stuff for 100% collection, if you want some replay value. It doesn't seem to change the ending at all. However, THIS IS NOT AN OPEN WORLD EXPLORATION GAME. You are locked into linear paths in a level-based fashion.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

Light to moderate difficulty in puzzle solving, creative and interesting boss fights, and a good amount of exploring around to find extra stuff. The real feast here is for your eyes. The art design here is just incredible. There's constantly a full screen of amazing things to see, and watch as they move around and interact with the world. All of the beauty of this game mixes perfectly with the gameplay itself to really make something unique and special.

_childDocuments_.review: better than somerville-- a fraction of limbo and inside's fun.the puzzles are better than somerville, but they're a chore compared to limbo and inside. i found the puzzles satisfying at first, if not Too Easy, even though they require you to think outside of the box. it quickly becomes a time-consuming inventory management puzzle. the boss fights are an interesting idea, but they're just.. kind of lame. you can't jump or grab things-- the whole thing feels like you're on a rail and everything is too clearly defined, even without a single world being shown or spoken. the game never developed into what i wanted or expected. perhaps it does at some point, but i can't justify the price spent if i'm not enjoying the majority of the experience.the game setting can't hold a candle to its spiritual predecessors. limbo and inside build their worlds so well. there's an actual sense of progression and that you're getting deeper into something. each puzzle room provides a unique setting that is interesting and makes you think about the game-world. even in my brief experience with somerville, i found the settings more interesting. in cocoon, everywhere is just a place. each place might be pretty and neat, but they lack any sort of importance or true identity. -- granted, each world has a theme and may function differently in accordance with which puzzle is being solved, but they're all too samey.and finally, the tonal departure is insane. it's way too light. you can't freaking die in this game. one of my favorite things about the predecessors is that your character ( a young boy )can die horribly. in limbo's opening scene you're being chased through a forest by grown-ups and dogs. they'll suffocate you or maul you to death if you're caught, and that's only part of it. the shockwave puzzle will completely obliterate the player, slamming their ripped apart flesh against the surroundings. in limbo, there are bear traps, buzz saws, machine guys and a giant spider trying to kill you. pair the gruesome deaths with the ambient and beautiful soundtracks and it makes for a memorable experience. the only thing you have to lose in cocoon is time. that is the only stake.if you want an experience like limbo or inside, this is NOT it. i don't think there's anything else quite like those titles and it breaks my heart. the disappointment of somerville was immeasurable. this game is cool in a vacuum, but i can't really recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a top-down puzzle adventure that does a great job easing you into it's world jumping mechanics. The high-level mechanic of the game is jumping between worlds that also double as powers when in their "minified" state. However, the more interesting puzzles and new mechanics come into play just as the game is wrapping up, leaving you wanting more. The audio and visual design helps carry the game through it's downtime moments in between puzzles. As the game went on I found myself slowing down more, taking in the art more as it is really impressive. The game starts to chug on Steam Deck at the tail-end of the game with a certain new mechanic, hitting sub 40 frames. While not game ruining, it is worth noting for future purchases since at first glance this game seems perfect for the Deck. Ending up finishing the game on my main PC.Looking forward to following this studio and seeing what comes next. Well worth the price as long as you are okay with it's ~6 hour runtime.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a beautiful, well-polished but short puzzle game.  All actions are done through movement and a single interaction button. The game does a great job of getting the player to understand the mechanics without ever explicitly telling or showing what they are. The puzzles were challenging without being too difficult and the designers somehow managed to ensure that the player never got into a situation where they were blocked from progress.  Played on Steam Deck, worked flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this because I was a big fan of Limbo and Inside. While Cocoon is a very pretty game, it's just not very fun. The puzzles are simple and there's only ever one solution. It reminds me a lot of Monument Valley, which was made to play in short burst and very cheap. Another detraction, there is only ever one path to follow. As far as I can tell there's not even hidden collectibles. I had to stop myself from exploring because there was never anything else to find. Story is very abstract/nonexistent. The whole game feels like just solve these puzzles to see the next environment. I finished the first "combat" section and realized this game wasn't worth my time. Better luck next time.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't find this game particularly difficult. I didn't get stuck very often, and when I did, it only took a bit of thought for me to figure out what I was supposed to do. _childDocuments_.review: If Inception was a video game.I find it very difficult to highlight any individual aspect of this game, as the entire package is simply excellent. _childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game a lot (and I usually hate puzzle games) so they must have done something right! (Only other puzzle game I remember actually enjoying was Portal 2). The idea to use orbs that contain worlds within them and have you jump in between them to solve increasingly complex puzzles was an absolute trip at first! I love the weird abstract world of these alien bug people that just does not look like anything in our own world and this feeling you were somewhere truly alien. The game does a good job at making you feel like you're in a strange alien place full of uncertainty while solving puzzles. Also gotta praise the art style/animation and sound design/music. It's all TOP NOTCH and really gives this game a ton of atmosphere and intrigue! Although for how well designed and interesting many of the puzzles are, I still got stuck near the end and had to watch YouTube guides to figure out the last ones (They get REALLY confusing near the end) but that may just be me, cause like I said, I usually suck at puzzle games. But yeah I definitely recommend COCOON! It's also made by some of the people who did Limbo and Inside and they formed a new studio. Annapurna seems amazing at finding these indie gems and helping them get made and published. Another W for them! It's also really short, but sweet. Took me like 5-7 hours to beat, but that's only cause I suck at puzzle games. If you are good at puzzle games and enjoy them, probably will take you less than half the time it took me to beat the game. I am starting to appreciate shorter but amazingly well designed games more, as this game has all killer and no filler. Every corner is made with love and care and high attention to detail (which I definitely prefer over a 100+ hour long slog type of game with some good moments sprinkled in between a bunch of filler. So yeah, COCOON is a great game. I give it an 8/10 and highly recommend if you like puzzle games, and maybe even if you don't usually like puzzle games!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed traversing the different worlds, I like these clean aesthetics and it felt very much like a game made for me. _childDocuments_.review: A Masterpiece of Visual and Mechanical DesignFrom the moment you step into the world of Cocoon, it's clear that this game is a triumph of visual and mechanical design. Every aspect of its aesthetics and gameplay mechanics is meticulously crafted to create a harmonious experience that both captivates the senses and challenges the mind.Visual Design: A Living Work of ArtCocoon’s visual presentation is nothing short of breathtaking. The art style seamlessly blends organic and surreal elements, bringing to life a world that feels simultaneously alien and familiar. The environments are richly detailed, with each world offering its own distinct palette and atmosphere. From luminescent caves that pulse with bioluminescent light to vast, sprawling landscapes filled with mysterious structures, the visual design invites players to pause and appreciate every meticulously drawn texture and subtle color gradient.The use of lighting and shadows is particularly noteworthy. Soft glows and contrasting silhouettes create a mood that evokes both wonder and intrigue. This attention to detail extends to the game’s environmental storytelling, where every shape, object, and pattern feels purposefully placed. The worlds themselves appear to be living organisms, and navigating through them feels like exploring a living, breathing entity.Mechanical Design: Elegance in ComplexityThe gameplay mechanics of Cocoon are just as thoughtfully designed as its appearance. The core concept revolves around using orbs, each representing a distinct world, to manipulate space and solve puzzles. This mechanic is ingeniously simple yet opens up a vast array of possibilities, allowing players to interact with the environment in surprising and delightful ways. Transitioning between these orbs, players can dive deeper into nested worlds, seamlessly folding layers of reality into one another.The elegance of the game’s mechanics lies in its ability to convey complexity through simplicity. Every puzzle is designed with a clarity that encourages experimentation and exploration without ever feeling obtuse or overwhelming. The mechanics are introduced gradually and intuitively, with each puzzle building on the last to create a satisfying progression. There is no need for hand-holding tutorials—the game’s design speaks for itself, guiding the player through its intricacies with perfect pacing.The interaction between these different worlds isn’t merely a gimmick; it’s the beating heart of the game. Each orb-world has unique properties that change how players perceive and interact with the environment. Whether it’s using an orb to reflect light and reveal hidden paths or transporting it through a series of portals to unlock new areas, every interaction feels purposeful and rewarding. The result is a series of puzzles that feel organic, as though they are part of the world’s natural order rather than arbitrary challenges.A Perfect Marriage of Form and FunctionCocoon excels in balancing its aesthetic and mechanical elements, ensuring that neither outshines the other. The visual design enhances the player’s understanding of the game’s mechanics, while the mechanics serve to highlight the beauty of the environments. Each new discovery, whether visual or mechanical, feels like uncovering a new piece of the puzzle that is the world of Cocoon itself.The synergy between the game’s appearance and mechanics is most apparent in its transitions. Moving between different worlds through the use of orbs is a visual and mechanical marvel. The fluidity of these transitions is mesmerizing, blurring the line between where one world ends and another begins. It’s an experience that’s as much about navigating physical space as it is about traversing abstract concepts like layers of reality and perception.Conclusion: A Design MasterpieceCocoon stands out as a brilliant example of how game design can achieve a perfect equilibrium between form and function. Its visual design is mesmerizing, drawing players into a world that feels alien yet natural, while its mechanical design is a masterclass in intuitive complexity. Together, these elements create a game that is not just played but experienced—every puzzle solved, every transition made, is a testament to the meticulous craftsmanship and vision behind the game.For those who appreciate games that push the boundaries of visual and mechanical design, Cocoon is a must-play. It’s a journey that mesmerizes the eyes, challenges the mind, and lingers in the memory long after the screen fades to black.

_childDocuments_.review: At only 3.5 hours, COCOON is still one of the most striking puzzle games I've played this year. The puzzles are linear, which is a nice break from games with lots of open-ended backtracking - you focus on one thing at a time. Difficulty doesn't ramp up until an hour or two in, but when it does it really starts bringing in some mind-breaking mechanics. The game explores its various mechanics pretty thoroughly, which was super refreshing compared to a lot of recent puzzlers. The simple control scheme also made for great focus. Aesthetic is novel and the sound design lent a lot to the whole experience. Definitely worth a playthrough, especially if you like non-euclidean / recursive puzzling!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful yet short puzzle game by brilliant Jeppe Carlsen (of INSIDE fame). Every aspect of the game is polished and satisfying:- The music elevates tension, guides the player and rewards when taking the right path/solving puzzles. - The art style is a mesmerizing bio-mechanical and at times Escher-esque, all the while sneaking peeks of a vast unobtainable world. - The puzzle design is simple and ramps up in complexity as the game progresses, I was was stumped for a while on one or two puzzles but on the whole felt it was mostly straightforward and easily understandable. I guess I would have liked some harder or more mind bending puzzles (though I am a fan of puzzle games and played quite a lot of them)- As I've mentioned, the game is pretty short - finished it completely (including all achievements) in under 5 hours. On the one hand I fell like I would've liked more, yet on the other hand it was a very concentrated and curated experience. This is the only part where if you are not a fanatic of Carlsen's or of puzzle games might want to consider if the price to game to time ratio is enough for you. In my opinion it is very much worth my money.A uniquely gorgeous experience, one that at least on the puzzle side is very close to portal, and transports you to an artfully imaginative world. _childDocuments_.review: Whether you like this game or not depends on what you want from a game. The tag says "exploration" and it kinda is, and kinda isn't. The game is pretty much on rails. You often go in blindly, and soon you'll stop wondering if you're going the right direction. If the direction is open, then it's the right one. If it's closed, then it means it will open up later.This is refreshing for me, because it was what I was looking for (something calm and alien-like) so I recommend it, but it might not be for everyone. The puzzles are quite simple, though the game offers a unique mechanic of jumping through worlds, and you soon find yourself acquainted with this mechanic, which is really different to how we are programmed to think. Like, you can even put a world inside a world to retrieve it later which sounds so weird and innovative.However, if that sounded crazy (it would, to me) it's not as crazy within the game since, like I said above, it's on rails. When you have to do something like that, it's the only thing you *can* do to progress, so it comes to you naturally rather than having to think about it.The tags also say "Adventure" and it is if we take the literal meaning of the word, but it isn't if we take into account "adventure games". There are no items that you would have to take from one world and use in another, it's pretty much just solving a puzzle, progressing, solving another puzzle, etc. Like I said, it's pretty calm.Graphics and Sound-wise, I loved it. It's also not memory-hungry so low-end pcs might handle it as well as high-end ones.Anyway, I recommend it, but remember, it's pretty much on rails, and despite what the description might make you think, the puzzles are quite simple. Which I loved, but it might not be for everyone.Imho, buy it on a sale, pick a very calm day, after work, where you have nothing else to do and just want to switch off, and play it then. You'll love it.EDIT: Ok, later on it gets really trippy lol, I had to come back and edit this. I don't wanna say why but you will go "what" a couple of times lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man Cocoon is so good!  Cocoon is a gorgeous top down (with a slight angle) exploration/puzzle game with pretty simple systems.  There are various orbs you acquire, that give you different powers when you hold them, but you can only hold one at a time, additionally, there are stations where you can put these orbs, and then dive into the world inside them (Like Disgaea, except its nothing like that at all).  I was blown away by Cocoon, and loved every minute I spent playing it.The game looks stunning, the amount of creativity in the art direction is astonishing.  Each biome has its own look and feel, everything is strange, colored a little flat, but detailed at the same time.  the world is odd and alive, and organic, it is super creative and interesting.  The animation is also superb, especially on the little guy that you control.The gameplay is fantastic.  The mechanics or using and diving into the orbs is so interesting, it is unlike anything I have ever played.  On top of that, the puzzles are so perfectly created, unlike some other environmental exploration/puzzle games I never had that feeling where I felt like I only barely understood a puzzle, and am just flailing on whatever they let me interact with to try and brute force it.  I have had issues with that in games like the Witness, and others, but never in Cocoon.  I felt like I totally grok'd how they wanted me to nest the orb, etc and etc.  And it felt great and I felt smart, what a cool game.Cocoon took me like seven hours or so and it is an easy 10/10. _childDocuments_.review: Score w/o Context: 2 * pi * r / 10, r = 1.5The Context:Balancing flavors for someone can be a tough task. I, for example, fall somewhere between 'mayo is too spicy' and 'this white bread is very flavorful'. Others who are not perpetually 5 years old have more refined palettes, and making something tasty can involve a lot of trial and error. Puzzle games are a similar 'big ask' in that you have one mechanic to work with, and it has to toe the line between difficult and doable at all times. Cocoon does this as well as any I've played in the last few years, and was a thoroughly enjoyable experience in its 10 or so hour playtime.In essence, you use different universes to affect others. But in practice it ends up being a lot simpler. Each world is contained in a sphere, and bequeaths a power to influence aspects of the environment in others. You can hop in and out of each world, bring other spheres in and out, and experiment freely. It's a very intuitive system that works even when complexity ramps up.This journey is mostly textless, leaving it up to the interpretation of the player, and it mostly works. The highlights for me came in the conflicts between your character and the boss monsters, merging the puzzle design and a more frantic solution sleuthing section. There are a few additional hints and extras scattered throughout, but it really is a mostly linear adventure (for the better, in my mind) bumping up against various environs and seeing how they affect each other.The only issue I had, and this may sound crazy coming from a man who has selective blindness for both puzzle solutions and things in my pantry, is I wish the puzzles had actually gone just a bit further in complexity. It was only near the very end of the game that I felt very challenged, which surprised me. But as with flavors, difficulties also can be loved by some and reviled by others. You may find it hits that perfect spot, but even if it doesn't, it is well worth the brain power.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Geometric Interactive's  is a wonderful first time effort from a studio of incredibly accomplished game devs, and this feels truly, like the culmination of all their work. It is an intelligent, tightly designed environmental puzzler with a more hands off approach, opting to give players subtle visual and audio clues and rich mechanics to exercise at will. And rather than a strict level to level structure, the game creates an illusion of freedom with an intrinsic feeling of discovery despite never letting you that far off the leash. And so even if those worlds themselves are linear and relatively small, the intertwining of these through the "switching" opens them up in a way I could not have expected. The worlds themselves, hostile and yet intriguing landscapes, some dull and some full of life. They're all very distinctive, not just because of their looks but the unique ability granted to each "ball" the world resides in. Abilities that transcend the barriers of this universe, one seemingly without rules of any discernible nature. It is one of the best puzzlers I've played, which, admittedly is a small sample size, but that doesn't take away the strength of this experience. It is a blaringly bold and unique take that I would recommend to anyone, fans of the genre or not.
