_childDocuments_.review: The game is certainly pretty, and I enjoyed the world design, but the game play is just not that satisfying.  The main line of puzzles in the games are never very hard, and it basically just linear, even if you are jumping between worlds and revisiting worlds as the game progresses.It isn't a bad game, but I don't feel it was quite worth the money for me.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly not recommending it to get more nuance among the reviews but let's hear me out:While it's a beautiful and interesting game I  didn't find it engaging, challenging, or memorable.There is no storytelling, or mysteries to unravel except for the themes in each zones and possibly the ending.The puzzles are too easy. Playing the game felt like walking from A to B flicking a few switches are along the way. Nothing "minding bending" like many other reviews said.A handful of bosses are the only the real enemies and boss fights are easy. Though  this isn't to the game's detriment as I think this is the the kind of game that shouldn't require too much motor skills.Did I enjoy the game? Yes, it was worthwhile to play. I'm just thinking I will put up the game on the virtual shelf and never think about it again. I won't be recommending the game unless it's on a considerable sale.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I unequivocally enjoyed my time with Cocoon, but I think any recommendations would have to come with some caveats. It is a beautiful experience with some really clever puzzle design, but I don't know if it is for everyone. This is a puzzle game, played in third person where your character moves around in order to solve the puzzles. There are some very occasional sequences where timing is required (you have to do something fast enough to solve a puzzle), and some boss sequences that require some action reflexes (there is no death, but if you fail one of these sequences you have to do it again until you succeed).The puzzles are truly clever and well-designed, and yet I couldn't help but feel like there was room for improvement. One of the issues had nothing to do with the puzzles themselves, but rather with the chosen genre: It sometimes felt annoying to engage with the mechanics of the puzzle because it required running around to manipulate different parts. The other issue is that it felt like the brilliance of the concept didn't quite get explored as fully as I would have liked. There is a strong theme of what I think of as recursion, where there are different levels (in the sense of nested hierarchical levels, not traditional video game "levels") that you have to pop between, and it's a really cool premise. There were 2 or 3 legitimately amazing "whoa" moments I had (kind of like in Portal or Braid where I could feel my mind expanding), but otherwise it didn't feel like this really paid off. For me it almost felt like the game was too accessible and polished to remove frustration, which meant that I sometimes didn't even have to fully understand the cool recursive rules of the game because there weren't really any alternatives. Don't get me wrong, I appreciated the lack of frustration and the forethought given to making the experience smooth, but for me personally it felt like there were mind-blowing elements that didn't quite translate into a mind-blowing experience. It makes me feel a bit guilty to say this, but as I was playing I kept realizing that I loved that the game existed, but I didn't actually love the game itself.Visually the game is stunning. The game was clearly made with a priority to make everything as high quality as possible, and all of the nice dithering and antialiasing makes for an experience that feels very soft (in a good way) and natural. Artistically the design is also endlessly creative, although sometimes felt that I was appreciating it more than loving it emotionally. Even with relatively limited art sets (for lack of a better word), there is always something new to see, and none of it ever becomes at all predictable. Even by the end when the pattern of how the game works is established there are still lots of surprises to discover visually.There are subtle music cues whenever you finally get a puzzle right that kind of builds anticipation. I love when games do that :-DI think if you played and liked Limbo or Inside then the chances are high that you will also like Cocoon. If you don't like puzzles there probably isn't enough here for you to enjoy unless you really love the art. If you only play puzzle games but don't like action there is a reasonable chance you will like this, although some of the boss encounters might be frustrating (if you play action games, however, then you have nothing to worry about with these bosses). If you like mind-expanding puzzles (like the aforementioned Portal or Brain) then I think you can give Cocoon a bonus multiplier, and I think it would be worth checking out for you.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not an expert on puzzle games by any means, but this game has a 'simplicity' that suggests a great deal of intention and thought behind it's decisions. The puzzles are approachable and intuitive to an extent i haven't seen before in a puzzle game - even when I got stuck for a bit, I never felt annoyed! The world is beautiful and strange, and the atmosphere is enthralling. A couple of miniboss sections helped break things up a bit. Just a very good experience!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked/loved Somerville and feel you didn't have enough of it, then go ahead and play Cocoon. You'll probably get a very similar taste. With beautiful visuals, nicely laid puzzles and great atmospheric soundtrack, Cocoon has easily become one of my favorite puzzle games. Obviously, Playdead was/is a great school, it really shows with these games from their "sibling" companies.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: COCOON is both one of the most creative and original puzzle games I've experienced and offers some of the most engrossing, enjoyable boss fights.An incredibly polished game, it deftly guides you forward with its invisible hand while giving the impression its world (within worlds) is impossibly large and expansive. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous, innovative and meditative puzzle game.The core mechanics revolve around jumping in and out of different worlds to advance and feel portalesque, but in a unique way.The difficulty curve is very well done and the game never lingers to long on a single mechanic. It introduces a surpising amount of possibilities, while staying simplistic at its core.Despite it's low poly artstyle the game looks amazing and often manages to suprise with creative levels, shaders and effects.Recommended for pretty much all fans of puzzles and creative visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a marvel. Perhaps one of the most clever puzzle games ever devised. No other game on the market is doing anything like this. All the puzzles revolve around the concept of worlds within worlds, and every minute of this game is impressively mind-bending. The art direction is superb, with environments that manage to both give off an alien, fleshy aesthetic and a dystopian, mechanical atmosphere. It's simply otherworldly.You're looking at one of the best games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: After watching some gameplays and witnessing the players' enthusiasm for Cocoon, I couldn't resist and got myself the game (especially since it was created by the developers of Inside... nothing more needs to be said there). And I wasn't disappointed ! Simple but great gameplay with well-crafted puzzles, distinctive graphics, mysterious sound design, everything is tailored for you to savor the game. It's a favorite and the first game I've completed at the beginning of this year. Definitely worth a try if you get the chance
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good, really tight little puzzle game. The puzzles are solid but the visuals and the atmosphere are the main attraction. I think I would've liked a tiny bit more of a narrative but the game gets by very well on vibes alone. The gameplay also didn't go quite as crazy with the core concept as I was expecting, but maybe that's for the best - it would have been very easy for the puzzles to get too confusing to be fun.So overall this gets a recommend from me, but I would also recommend not getting carried away with the hype.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I can see how the game designer came from limbo and Inside.  This is yet another unique game with fresh gameplay elements  that I could have never imagined.  The visuals are unique and so beautiful in every one of the multiple worlds you end up exploring.  I won't lie and pretend I understood the story and ending of the game - I have an idea but I'm sure I'm far from understanding it fully...But seeing the worlds, the unique "enemies", and figuring out the worlds within worlds concept was great.  The sound and background music are also really great.  This is one of those games that shines especially on an OLED display with pure blacks and great contrast, and a good sound system or headset.  Although basically nothing has textures and each object is mainly a flat color, the art style combined with unique animations, glows and effects give the game such depth and beauty.  It's definitely a visual feast and I recommend it to anyone who enjoys short puzzle games!I look forward to more amazing games from this developer as well as PlayDead.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning game with amazing sound design. The difficulty is OK, the game introduces mechanics clearly enough to not get stuck because of incorrect game design/storytelling. If you get stuck, it’s you, not the game 😉. Difficulty was also well balanced, not frustratingly difficult, but not easy as well.Overall, really nicely though out game that is just a joy to chill with.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: COCOON is a great puzzle game. There's a good sense of exploration and experimentation. Similar to INSIDE, the story is solely told through visuals. The game is full of those satisfying 'a-ha!' moments. I admit that some puzzles were too much for my pea-sized brain and my entitled-millennial-instant-gratification desires. So yeah, I looked up the solution to a few puzzles that really stumped me. But I did play most of the game legitimately and I really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a peaceful puzzle game. You explore the game's world to unlock new spheres, and each sphere contains its own world. They unlock special abilities if held. What sets the game apart is the ability to navigate between different worlds, creating a truly unique experience, and having you think in novelty ways. I didn't find the game particularly challenging, but it was very enjoyable. Also the game is exceptionally beautiful, featuring phenomenal creatures and landscapes.I would rate the game 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon!A puzzle game with worlds, within worlds. Visually beautiful with a calming atmosphere, making this a joyful and meditative puzzle game. The core mechanics revolve around jumping in and out of different worlds to advance. The difficulty curve is well done and Cocoon doesn't linger too long on a single mechanic. It introduces a surprising amount of possibilities, while staying simplistic at its core. Cocoon is an innovative masterpiece and defiantly what I have been looking for, in terms of platform puzzles. It succeeds entirely at what it sets out to do. Visuals and sound design are top tier and something to admire truly. A few boss fights, and they're all super fun and unique!I loved the fluidity of the mechanics and all the environmental sounds and details that were put into COCOON. A solid 8/10, could have been a little longer in my opinion. Nonetheless, a great experience! I highly recommend to anyone that enjoys puzzles, creative visuals, quirky boss fights and originality.    Big tip! Make sure you bounce/leap between worlds. It will help immensely especially towards the end puzzles/worlds :)P.S. Compatible with my Steam Deck & runs incredibly smooth. Highly recommended for any Steam Deck!Edit: The negative reviews for Cocoon are absolutely hilarious, clearly the type of people to stand in the corner of a party and hold that one drink all night XD
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I beating this game made my day off relaxing and entertaining. The puzzles and boss fights aren't the hardest, but some of the puzzle took me a few minutes, and most of the boss fights took a few tries. The art was amazing. I love that the simple controls and intuitive mechanics allowed for full immersion without reading rules/instructions. I would recommend this game to anyone that enjoys a simple, but fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles will get you stuck but not for too long. When you do solve them you get an a ha! moment which feels amazing. Also, its way of teaching you the world's rules is incredible. By the time you are tasked with a puzzle requiring intimate knowledge of the rules of the world you feel you know them without fully understanding how.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I heard so many good things about COCOON, but I found it quite underwhelming.There is a lot to like here. COCOON has simple, elegant mechanics, a unique setting, and some clever puzzles. But the game never really went anywhere; there was no sense of progression, no reward, nothing drastically new or different to spice up the gameplay. Ultimately it became samey, bland, and unsatisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Mesmerizing, psychedelic, gorgeous, delightful , brilliant....these are just some of the words that I'd use to describe this game. Puzzle games are my favorite genre, and this one does not disappoint! This is one of those games where you you know right from the beginning, it's gonna be a lot of fun. There were so many  "that's so cool!" moments...and the game & puzzle design is top notch.The puzzles themselves I would rate as easy to medium. There was one at the end that required a lookup...it's a mechanic I had not seen before...but it was totally fair. A couple suggestions on how this could even be better....a bit more difficulty in the puzzles as you progress, a longer game (I didn't want this to end) , and maybe a bit more of a story elements.  Overall, highly recommend, what an awesome game!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely outstanding game! Don't let the short play time turn you off from this game. If you are a fan of the adventure-puzzle genre then this game is a must-buy! The puzzles are amazing and, in my opinion, are the perfect difficulty: not too easy, but not mind nummingly hard. On top of that, the soundtrack and sound design are super immersive. I could not recommend this game more.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful game with very clever puzzles. Very good case for interesting storytelling without any cutscenes. The core puzzles about travelling through worlds are very interesting and well executed but I felt like some of the other ones were a bit easy and not as interesting. Overall not disappointed having played Limbo/Inside and having somewhat high expectations.Score: Am I high?/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very well designed* short, but full of content puzzle game. It plays very smooth, puts you into the flow. Puzzles are clever so they are interesting, but not hard, so you're never stuck. However there is a big asterisk on the well designed part. I even contemplated leaving a negative review because of it. There is a section towards the end of the game that drastically differs from the rest of it. This section is unskippable, so to progress you don't have a choice but to suffer through it. It is a timed reflex-based level, despite the rest of the game being a chill classic puzzle. People with disabilities are screwed. I don't understand who the hell thought it was a good idea to change the gameplay so drastically just for this one part. It does not fit in with the rest of the game and it spoiled my enjoyment of it quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing this game's trailer and immediately playing it at release. There's like two sides of me on this game. On one side, this game is crazy with incredible atmosphere and puzzles, and it builds ideas on top of each other as you progress, going into this crazy insanity. On the other side, it's so painfully easy to see the level design doing its thing, to the point where immersion is broken, depending on how used to you are with solving puzzles in games. It's good that they funnel you into the right solution, but doing stuff like closing gates kinda feels like the game is forcefully telling you not to do certain things you want to try and fail, and instead only try the only solution you can really do. A lot of puzzles feel like a checklist of ideas you have and just solving them, which is cool in its own right, but there's only a few puzzles in this game where I truly felt like I had to think of a good solution. Don't expect super crazy story or lore, even though the game's atmosphere is really nice. I still enjoyed it tho. Really great game, and doesn't waste a lot of time
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone should play Cocoon.This is a roughly 6 hour experience wherein you will glide through worlds within worlds within worlds. You likely won't struggle for long with any single puzzle. The design encourages you along in many considerate and thoughtful ways, all without a single spoken word.I must stress that controlling the character is effortless, and interacting with the world is reduced to a single simple button - often  either asking you to press it or to hold it.This is an easy game to play, which carefully balances your pace and somehow manages to elicit a state of flow in so short an amount of time, as if it's always been your job to journey through surreal nested alien worlds.Again, everyone should play Cocoon.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A darn-near perfect game. If you enjoy puzzle games or experiencing novel, alien settings, snag this one. Just be aware that it’s not terribly long.An absolutely brilliant little self-contained gem. This game manages to walk the tightrope of always being puzzling enough to make you feel like the goodest, smartest kid while avoiding being so hard as to frustrate you. If you find it too easy, which probably won’t be an issue, there’s even a deeper secret to uncover that is so cryptic I didn’t even realize I was missing anything while playing.I don’t want to overexplain Cocoon, as it’s best gone into somewhat blind. Without giving too much away, you’ll be hopping into and out of worlds that are themselves contained in spheres that can be transported, even into one-another. It’s one of those wordless games that expects you to figure things out as you go through trial-and error. Unlike with some other titles that have attempted this, I never had that “What the heck am I supposed to do?!” moment. The rules are introduced in ways that make them feel natural, and progression typically sees you combining tactics in new ways.I really enjoyed the art direction on this title; it does a great job of evoking alien worlds, critters, and machines whose functions are only hinted at. Each world has a unique look and feel, and there are enough secrets to make exploring every inch feel rewarding. You won’t see amazing set pieces, but Cocoon establishes a great atmosphere and lets you soak up the vibes, delivering a story whose meaning is only suggested.Typically I like to list anything that detracts from the experience, but there are only a few nit-picks here. The boss battles are a little arcade-y and somewhat out of character for the rest of the game, which could be a little frustrating to people who aren’t into action games and are here for the puzzling. For my own tastes, I also wish Cocoon had lasted a little longer, perhaps introducing one more mechanic. I beat it in one (admittedly pretty long) sitting, and it left me wanting more, but I’d rather that than overstaying its welcome.There are no perfect games, but this one comes really close. Exploration / puzzle is a fairly niche genre, but Cocoon is easily one of the best I’ve ever played. If you enjoy the dopamine hit from overcoming challenging conundrums, this game is a no-brainer recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Up front? If you don't like backtracking as part of your puzzle games, probably best to skip this one. The backtracking isn't "go back to the start" punishment like a bad Metroidvania, but you'll be making extensive short loops back to previous locations as the game gets towards the back end and leans heavily on its "worlds within worlds" portal mechanic.The inscrutable, biomechanic alien aesthetic is an awesome choice, giving wonder and discomfort in equal measure. Soundtrack matches the visual aesthetic perfectly. Puzzles felt rewarding as hell, and had what felt like a comfortable difficulty curve across almost every challenge.$25 USD feels maybe a bit pricey for its length, but definitely snap this up if it's part of a Steam Sale.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Orbino's QuestI ended up liking this game. The puzzles in the latter half were fun. I think if I played on a big tv sized screen, I would have appreciated running around the world more, there's just a lot of little environmental stuff that the game runs of vibes more than a thought out world. By that, I mean the puzzles only make sense as puzzles and don't fulfill a real world logic. But perhaps I am wrong, and they would make sense to a little bug.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game! Was so intuitive to play, and most of the puzzles, while mind-numbing at times, were reasonable and adhered to the logic that the game presented. It looks lovely, and each section of the world has its own definitive look.Note if you have older hardware (like I do) this game may potentially freeze up, but that might just be because I need a new comp.Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The best puzzle game I've played in a while. During the second half the puzzles get especially interesting and the game knows how to limit the available actions perfectly so that you're not fiddling with items that don't have anything to do with the solution.There is no dialogue or text in the game so you're left with trying to interpret the story based on your surroundings and events that transpire during the game. I personally would've preferred something less mysterious, but I was still interested in finding out where the game takes me next.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect puzzle game. The levels design keeps iterating on itself in such fun ways. The progression and game mechanics feel so organic to the locations within the game. It's easy to immerse yourself in this beautiful world thanks to impeccably creative visuals and sound design. I love the goopy robotic insect themes of all the locations and creatures, and the sound effects and ambience absolutely suck you in to each area. Puzzles are very satisfying and it feels like they explore most mechanics extensively. The last few puzzles are so cool and the ending was amazing. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game is maybe the best puzzle game I have ever played.The puzzles are simple, but hard enough that you have to stop and think, and they never get too hard, they are always satisfyingly hard.and on top of nice puzzles, the visuals are so so good and enjoyable to look at!The only puzzle that I had to look up was the last one unfortunately.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The recursive, pastel dreamscape of  is an absolute delight to experience from start to finish. The puzzles are inventive and challenging, yet never frustrating, and the tremendous stylistic design makes exploring every level immensely satisfying. Annapurna continues to publish gems left and right -- I highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It is a pretty game, but it is essentially a Tower of Hanoi puzzle. You move objects from one place to a holding place and then to where they need to go. It isn't new or innovative or challenging. In this game you put rings inside of other rings, but really that's the only difference. You'll see the solution instantly and then be able to execute it after seeing the same jumping in and out or orb animations a dozen times. Also, while I have enjoyed games that utilize visual or explicitly non-verbal story telling this game just gives you so little that I'm not genuinely certain there is a story. Rather it seems as though the game implies there is story or meaning, hints at it, without ever having to explicitly develop one. Ultimately there was nothing about it that compelled me to keep playing, so I refunded it. There are much better stories, and puzzles, and visual designs out there... I had heard so much about Cocoon that I was willing to try it out, but at least to me the hype isn't particularly well deserved. It's fine I guess, I just didn't like it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a puzzle-driven game with a worlds-within-worlds mechanism. The worlds are orbs and you can carry these orbs to power devices. The most notable being the one that allows you to enter the orb's world. Each world has its own alien feeling to it. For a game that allows worlds-within-worlds, I actually expected the puzzles to be a lot more brain-burning than they actually were. I think this is partly a testament to the designers of the game as it's pretty good cutting off a lot of backtracking. That said, this kind of made the game feel a little more linear than one might expect.I think people have described the game as elegant. I agree with this. They managed to have no tutorial and everything just flows and makes sense. Additionally, they managed all the puzzles and boss battles with just movement and one "interact" button. It's hard not to think of Limbo and Inside when thinking of this game. I think Limbo had the hardest puzzles or at least was the hardest of the three. Inside had the best atmosphere of almost any single game I've ever played. So, that would make Cocoon the worst? I wouldn't say so. There is just something and compelling about it. Maybe because this worlds-within-worlds was completely novel to me.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The amazing art and sound design come together to make a well crafted world, however the puzzles were just too easy. Every puzzle you can figure out in 5 seconds but then are forced to run around for 5 min to get the correct setup. I don't think this is a bad game, I just went into it expecting some more challenging puzzles. The bosses are beautiful and unique but were also too easy. TLDR knowing the solution to the puzzle instantly and yet taking 5 mins to solve it feels bad.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is the strangest and most alien metroidvania I've ever seen. Original puzzles, interesting art style, fun to discover new mechanics. I believe we've got a winner.I highly recommend.Edit: After playing a bit more I think I made a mistake and it's not actually a metroidvania since I haven't seen a need to or possibility of backtracking across the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely concept, but very frustrating that there’s no difficulty settings. After a promising start, and lovely set of discoveries of the various mechanics you are faced with the first ‘boss’. This is an unwelcome change of style from the intellectual challenge of the game until this point. It’s too hard and there’s no way to puzzle your way to solving it except to brute force it. The boss mechanic feels very Mario-esque and derivative, which is a real shame in an otherwise novel game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this, took me around 6 hours and it was fun for all of that time. I don't think 6hrs is at all short for this sort of game and it never outstayed its welcome. The puzzles were on the whole fox/grain/chicken puzzles but with a beautiful aesthetic execution. It reminded me visually of abzu or even astroneer. I only really had to think hard in the last 30mins or so, but that again is no real complaint. I suppose you could be critical that it follows the abstract-alien-puzzle-wordless setting thats is fairly common for these sort of games.. But it does it so well that I can forgive it! If you fancy a slightly metroidvania 3rd person puzzler give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: , but not because of genius complex challenges or a huge everlasting game; it is the best because absolutely everything is unique.The art style, the soundtrack and audio design, the atmosphere and world-building, the pacing and even the puzzles in themselves - Cocoon has managed to solidify itself as a reference in the genre.I found myself mesmerized how a game this majestic and magnificent could be so fast-paced. There isn't a single second you are doing nothing, never got stuck on puzzles, and even if, there is a hint system that works so subtly to not break your immersion and I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Do not go into this game expecting hard puzzles. The game is beautiful and creative with multiple worlds in which you can get lost in. However the puzzles are, as already said, not very hard so do not go in expecting to be stuck at a puzzle for 30 minutes unil you have an eureka moment like in other puzzle games. Instead go in expecting a very atmospheric game. The game is only between 3 and 4 hours long but I would say that the experience is worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle game with great atmosphere, music, and distinctive mechanics. Would recommend to anyone that likes to get lost in another world (or 5) and solve puzzles.My only issue is that it holds onto the "tutorial" phase of each of the individual orbs for too long, which are all rather straight forward puzzle solutions. The game is as its greatest when you lose access to the orbs after the tutorial and you really get to layer in the mechanics together. Would had love to have seen more puzzles using all the orbs like towards the end which I felt was too short of a section. Boss fights were also great showcase of each individual orb. Was expecting some more Boss fights using multiple orbs, but the boss boss was kind of lackluster timed shooting sections that didn't feel like it thematically fit with the rest of the game. Would still recommend and would 100% play more if there were more available in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Very great puzzle design, more so puzzle design that leads on the stretching the limits of the mechanics rather than focusing on pushing the limits of the player. This kind of puzzle solving lends itself well to calm atmosphere this game is going for, as a lot of the fun I had was making sense of all of the functionality of the different robotics of the worlds that you navigate through. Though the game took 3.7 hrs to beat, I think the value of the experience you get in that short run time is incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience. The game has such a beautiful art style that mixes organic and mechanical designs with basic shapes.The puzzle system is simple yet develops into a mind bending system where I often would solve a puzzle and feel like I had left my own mind. A mark of a truly thought out game mechanic taking to such a height which was a joy to experience. Everything about this game felt well crafted and considered with great care.I highly recommend this game to gamers and non-alike.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5 years in the making, Jeppe Carlsen is back with the game of the year. As you can tell from the trailer the art direction is some of the best out there, the use of color in particular is really stellar and the game only works because of it. The game design is a masterclass in intuitive puzzle design, the world-bending puzzle mechanic is really satisfying and clever.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I played and beat Cocoon on another platform, but purchased on Steam to support the team and be able to leave this review. My thoughts:I don't want to hyperbolize Cocoon, but it was awe-inspiring for me personally. The animations, puzzle design, world environment, sounds, music, mechanics, climaxes, and game length are both perfectly cohesive and as close to immaculate as I've ever found.If you're someone who doesn't *hate* puzzle games, I'd say you have to play Cocoon at least on Game Pass. If you even remotely *like* puzzle games, it deserves a purchase; it starts slow and smooth and the puzzle cleverness never ceases to grow throughout the short experience. At the end, I was swearing like a sailor as *individual puzzle interactions blew my mind*, not just puzzle conclusions (this is not an exaggeration; the last 45 minutes was ecstasy for me).Its grasp and execution on the concept of "alien" is the best I've ever seen, bar none. It thrashes other games' attempts at feeling otherworldly; only Outer Wilds' best moments even come close, as Cocoon marries foreign art and animations with alien mechanics and even  *concepts of thinking*.This game is an unequivocal masterpiece. And it's only ~4-5 hours long.I have some final takeaways from me on Cocoon's vision and why I think the game is bloody brilliant; I can go into crazy depth on these, but these were the notes I took along the way of what Cocoon's goals seem to be:- Abstract and repurpose; never completely repeat- Art IS function; delight both sides of the brain simultaneously- Remove unintended backtracking and traps; but keep options- Every path is a choice; even to the same destination- Respect the player's time- Force intrinsic learning- Challenge the brain and thumbs- Distinguish palettes to contextualize the area's expectations, mechanics, and limitations- Contrast repeated patterns and ideas with novel interruptions- Celebrate player success while remaining internally consistent- Test the player; don't punish them- Inundate the player with feedback and clues; let the player win the first timeAdditional fun notes:- Coocon succeeds in every area Cyan failed in Obduction.- There is no UI- There is only one button for the entire game's mechanics- I did not encounter a single bug- Performance is incredible- Zero visible loadtimes, only phenomenal in-game transitions
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's pretty amazing that this game guides players into learning the rules without any dialogue. I enjoyed the puzzles, and the sound and art direction were beautiful. I highly recommend playing with headphones. The only thing I didn't like was the third boss fight, but that's mostly because I am impatient.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: TL DR: Yes, this is a great game, but the final 20% were unpleasant.Cocoon was a really beautiful experience, but for me, the final 20 % of the game did not deliver. After the character gets the silver ball, the puzzles that were once intuitive and fun became unintuitive and challenging in a way that felt unfair to the players. Most people who have finished this game would also probably agree that the sequence with the diamond shapes (not a spoiler) was very different from the previously encountered gameplay and was, for me, the most frustrating part of the whole game.Overall, I really enjoyed Cocoon, it's just a shame that the last 20% were the unpleasant ones.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing experience.COCOON is a relatively small but incredibly well crafted puzzle game with great level & sound design, smart puzzles, beautiful art style, and clear attention to detail. The "worlds" all feel distinct from one another, and the world-hopping mechanism / world powers are really interesting, especially when you get to the second half of the game and you need to go down multiple levels to solve a puzzle.Performance is stellar, and puzzle difficulty is fair enough that you'll have to think about it, but not so impossible that you have to look them all up. Also easy to get 100% completion just by playing through normally and exploring the environment. Would absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a superb game that runs perfectly on the steam deck. I found it consistently engaging, delivering satisfying puzzles which are challenging but not so much that I ever felt hopelessly stuck. Overall it's a very chill experience with a number of shining moments where the game's mechanics come together in a truly delightful way.The length of  the game feels pretty good. The world juggling mechanics are very cool but I can feel there is a limit of complexity beyond which it would be rather cumbersome and more of a hassle than a really fun and interesting mechanic. Cocoon does a good job walking up to that line and ending in a timely manner. That said, in my opinion a price of over $20 USD is on the high end for a game that is only several hours in length. People on a budget should be aware of what they are paying for before buying this game. Regardless, Cocoon is an easy recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this on my Steam Deck, runs smooth and very easy to play in the train because of the seprate puzzles you can do!It's a very cryptic but good to follow game!Multple times I struggle with the puzzle, going to sleep just to wake up by understanding the solution. I finished the last level around 3 hours in.For an indie game, fair price but I MUST BUY in the sale!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: These low-poly games often have a strange, colorful beauty on them.There is not really a story here, it is more or less the journey to experience.To travel through a world with stunning and a little bit of disturbing art design. This is completet by an equally excelent sound design wich best workes with headphones.The puzzles get quite complex and I had to look up the solution a couple of times.They are still very clever designed.-The owls approve.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: is a masterpiece with its beautifully designed environments, splendid sound design and perfectly crafted puzzles. With its simple control design (movement and one interaction button), the player simply focuses on the puzzle themselves which are both imaginative and intuitive. Each new world you discover unlocks a new ability that you can activate while carrying the world. Complexity of these puzzles come from combining abilities and sometimes using them inside each other. There are several bosses throughout the game you will encounter which will challenge you logically. Hidden "Moon Ancestors" are also scattered throughout the levels and adds an incentive for exploring. From its cleverly crafted puzzles to the polished presentation,  is a must-play for all puzzle enthusiasts. [100/10]
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I like the concept, the music is beautiful, and it's fun to play a game that requires a bit of brain activity.  I am not crazy about the limited combat, and some of the later puzzles get more abstract, with a lot of back tracking and puzzles within puzzles.  I'll recommend it if you want to play something different, but otherwise meh.  I would give it a so-so rating if possible, but it didn't hold my interest enough for me to even finish it and can't ever see myself going back to it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful atmospheric puzzle game. There is no exposition or dialog, only a variety of alien landscapes to explore and immerse yourself into- and some quite unique puzzle concepts. None of the puzzles seemed obtuse, though some of the later ones did require a bit of backtracking and tedious orb-shuffling, however I don't think this detracted from the experience too much. Spoilers for the ending: A great experience overall, and I  I understand the gist of the plot, but I don't think it's really necessary to understand what's happening to enjoy it. Looking at the achievements, I missed six secrets on my first playthrough, so there is some replayability to find where those are if you missed them.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game started out really great.  Fun main character, great graphics, interesting puzzles and a really exciting journey.  But the main puzzle concept of using colored orbs to travel between locations got so complex that I had to use a utube gameplay cheat to get through most of the last 1/3 of the game.  What started out as a really fun and challenging experience, turned out to be a game I couldn't wait to be done with.  Too bad. I was really sold on the game in the beginning.  This game is very complex and i would recommend it only for advanced puzzle gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, when you play a puzzle game, you might already know some patterns from previously playing similar puzzle games. However, COCOON feels like an entirely new experience where you learn everything from scratch, and you feel very satisfied when you're able to solve the puzzle and move on to the next area.I really like the layering element of the puzzles in the game; it makes you think outside the box and provides a very satisfying backtrack. The art style and storytelling are quite unique, with additional dramatic sound design accompanying your battles against godly creatures. Oh, I forgot to mention that there are also boss fights in this game, which require you to be witty and fast. Now that I realize it, this game not only trains your senses to solve puzzles but also to be witty and agile. Personally, I enjoy both of this combinations.A gem and surprising entry for a game released this year.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Just not very interesting. Very much of the Monument Valley type where you are walking through a landscape and have gentle puzzles to solve. The whole thing is so tightly on rails that I found no room for mystery - either you do what the game wants you to (which admittedly is well signposted) or you become stuck.I'd forgive this if it was just not my thing puzzle-structure-wise - it's beautiful visually, runs butter-smooth, and the recursive conceit is at least interesting - but there's also no FLAVOUR. Compare again to Monument Valley. In Monument Valley the levels have NAMES. You get scraps of DIALOGUE. It's pretty sparse but there's something to spark the imagination. There is NOTHING here, no indication of who you are or why you are doing what you are doing. What are these worlds you are moving in and out of? Who are the bosses you are fighting? Who cares? You are a beetle but you may as well be a gelatinous cube for all that it affects anything. I did not finish the game but I discussed it with some who did and I apparently didn't miss anything that would've changed my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Overrated and the textbook definition of style over substance. The game is basically an atmospheric ' 3D puzzle' game . There are no real / actual puzzles, it is just sequences that you do and most of these 'puzzles' are so straightforward that you can complete them without even thinking. Boss fights in the game are out of place and do not mesh well with the rest of the segments; the battles are frustrating and not difficult which results in a feeling of boredom. There's a sense of wonder only in the few segments of the puzzles that depend on the 'world within a world' mechanic. Controls are awful where the character continues moving and drifting after the input commands have ended. This further exasperates the awful boss battles. Absolutely no sense of story for the most part of the game, there is no environmental story telling either. There is one game breaking bug that occurs too often where if you move too fast or too unexpectedly, the orange hidden paths won't load just in time to catch you and you will fall into the abyss of nothingness forcing you to reload and repeat the puzzle. The game just looks pretty and can make some cool wall papers, but other than that it is just a downright waste of money and time.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is every bit the brain workout. How the developers managed to bring an inception type of concept into an indie effort like this is truly the sign of masterful level and puzzle design. The game is fun and beautiful, and brilliantly put together.Speaking of which, I recommend giving this game your undivided attention. Putting a game like this down and then coming back later might leave you trying to remember how these worlds work together. It's difficult to explain, but there are worlds within worlds in this game, and the way you navigate each affects the other. Simply put, it's brilliant but you have to pay attention to what you're doing or you'll be stuck for a while. Don't let that scare you off, however. The game is a masterpiece IMO and I very HIGHLY recommend it!Thank you for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with a written path that you have to take. There are no sandbox solutions whatsoever. Also, it is a game that you can easily finish within 4 hours. However, because it's breathtaking audiovisual, satisfying puzzle solutions, and great gameplay optimization (you play with move buttons and one action button), I can recommend every bit of it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Though the game wraps up quickly, no moment is wasted. This is a pure game which does not cater to pillars of modern gaming like online-ness or micro-transactions, standing solely on solid game design. You'll feel butterflies at each new mechanic's inception, and ride the flow state as you hatch plans to overcome obstacles. Engaging puzzles combined with beautiful, clean graphics to draw you like a moth to an orb make for an experience to metamorphose you into a fresh new gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent graphics but the puzzles are too trivial. If you are a hardcore puzzle gamer or played games like recursed, completing this game wouldn't take more than 4 hours.To be honest this is barely a recommendation. There are just so many ways to introduce extra mechanics and to make the game harder.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: really good, kinda short if you're good at it (hehe) but not in a way that feels frustrating or anything.visually stunning, there's no compromise on all the work that the devs wanted to put in, that's clear.the puzzles are interesting, never too obtuse or open that you'd be stuck without understanding what to do and get stuck. It's pretty good at rewarding you when you understand the solution and execute it, but also at not giving you too many options so that if you don't know what to do, you can exhaust all options before finding the right thing to do.it has its "mind blowing" moments, where it breaks a rule that you thought was in place, and has a nice little story open to interpretation but also not too fuzzy either. really good
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing. Very few games achieve the feat of defining a new universe with its own rules totally different from the real world, yet totally consistent. It's very satisfying to find yourself thinking in terms of its rules and seeing that things work out. Just a work of art. Do yourself a favor and try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really sure what I just experienced, but it was beautiful, unique, and fascinating to explore.Game-play is an adventure/puzzle style with a few light combat sequences. If you have ever played this game designers previous games (Limbo or Inside) it has a very similar feel. But all the puzzles and environments have taken a HUGE step up in quality. The story, like the designer's previous games, is minimal with no dialog and all story elements delivered via context clues in the environment. While that kind of storytelling can be super engaging, it makes for a vague ending that is left up to your interpretation. This can be mildly irksome for people like me who enjoy a story with a solid resolution, but didn't impact my overall enjoyment very much.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A well-made, beautiful puzzle game that finishes just before it overstays its welcome.  Puzzles have a good difficulty curve, quickly showing you the techniques and tricks you'll use with each new tool without fully taking you by the hand and rubbing your face in every solution, nor leaving you feeling under-equipped to solve the later puzzles.  I did find that, on a couple of occasions that I felt stumped, stepping away and coming back the next day fresh and distanced from my previous solution attempts allowed me to overcome the few progress blocks I seemed to hit, with only one very late game puzzle requiring a guide simply because I'd gone a few days without playing it and had simply forgotten which steps I'd already taken prior to it and which direction I needed to move in order to progress.  There are no fail states that I encountered and every puzzle can be completed regardless of how much prodding you've put into it.  All in all, this is an excellent package for exercising the mind and a good palate cleanser between larger or more intense games.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a great little puzzle game. I found it visually quite beautiful, and mechanically it was incredibly well crafted. The puzzles were interesting and creative; they led well into one another, and it always felt like things were moving forward. About 8 hours is the most I think you're likely to get out of this game, but I do enjoy puzzle games which deliver a tight, concentrated experience without unnecessary padding or losing momentum.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of 2023. A true gem of atmospheric puzzling with some uniquely ingenious mechanics, amazing score, and art design that made me wish this game was 3x longer. Played this with a big smile on my face the entire time and some solutions actually astounded me. It's not exactly Talos Principle 2 in terms of difficulty, but it'll stretch your brain in the best way. Highly recommend.If you're stuck in the game or need some mechanical help, here's some non-spoiler tips:- You can trade the orb on a pedestal with the one you are carrying, without needing a second pedestal.- There are some rare, scripted instances where you can drop or place an orb mid-movement.- You can nest worlds within worlds to move multiple orbs at once. The orb you are carrying is the ability you can use.- Pay attention to where an exit pad will teleport you. It is always consistent.- You will always have the tools you need to complete a puzzle. It's very hard to softlock yourself.- Things traveling into a world orb will continue in the same direction they entered. They don't stop until they hit an obstacle.- The special musical cue will tell you that you've got the correct solution.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: - Would you like to solve some smart-but-not-smug puzzles?- Would you like to navigate a beautiful, cohesive set of environments?- Would you, and this is important, like to be slightly grossed out the entire time?If you answered yes to all of these, then Cocoon is for you. If you're not quite sure, here's the skinny: Cocoon is a 3rd person puzzler where you control a lil' bug-man guy who can pick up and put down orbs. You solve puzzles with the orbs. The orbs also contain entire worlds, which you dive in and out of. Sometimes you put a world  a world, and then maybe need a cigarette.The graphics are great. The story is wordless and oblique but told well, and also not the main draw (although the mystique is nice). But really, you're here for the puzzles - and that's just dandy. They're good puzzles. They're not the toughest, mind. It's not unfair to observe the game is a little on-rails at times. But, given the inception-like quantum possibilities that would otherwise strangle your brain in the counterfactual, there's no real harm in this.If you liked INSIDE, Little Nightmares, Braid, or Brothers:AToTS then this should be well worth your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great puzzle game. I absolutely love the puzzle and level designs; not so much the boss fights, but they weren't enough of an impediment to kill my joy. The sound effects and grotesque art were fun, and some of the "wow" moments were pretty epic.I think some of the action sequences would have been better with a controller rather than a keyboard, and I wish there would have been better remap options (like being able to use my mouse as the action button).I'll almost certainly play again to pick up more of the secrets now that I understand what I'm doing better, and can take my time to explore a little more. It'd be great if I could access the full content of the game at the ending, instead of having to get all the secrets in order. But, that's a me problem. ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game where carrying things doesn't make you slower. Humor aside, this game is amazing. Simply put, I haven't played another puzzle game as of recently which has felt both as fair and rewarding in each of it's solves in a while. It felt like if Patrick's Parabox was both amazingly pleasing on the eyes and also comprehendable. I mean in the way of like, things make sense, while also being completely mind boggling. Towards the end of the game I had some jaw drop WTF moments where things truly felt unbelievable. If you have 25 bucks you should buy this game, plain and simple. If it goes on sale, like, this is an obligatory purchase. It's beautiful, it's fulfilling, it has a little guy with 4 legs who coos at you and carries your things around like a little puppy dog (don't know the name of it, but do I want a plushie of it? Yes? Do I understand why I do? No?), so go play this game. It's really good, and deserving of your time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant showcase of an intriguing world where it's never quite clear what's going on but it keeps you hooked in until the very end. The game is filled with the perfect amount of puzzles, combining few mechanics in ingenious ways, gradually increasing in difficulty and becoming more involved but never too challenging. Wholly satisfying from beginning to end in presentation, design, and atmosphere.There is some welcome guidance - usually in the form of temporarily being cut off from areas - that eliminates experimentation that would have resulted in a lot of time wasted.The inner logic of the game however encourages experimentation and figuring out solutions feels very satisfying.An easy recommendation to puzzle enthusiasts. I would not be making comparisons to either Limbo or Inside as those two are very different games.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting atmospheric indie puzzler with a really uniquely memorable art style and a great soundscape.Not too hard or too long so doesn't out stay its welcome but does manage to explore its own mechanics in a satisfying way along with some rather mind-bending moments.Liked it enough to play it to completion and find 100% of the secrets.While I managed to 100% the game in 5 hours I really enjoyed all 5 of those hours and didn't find myself bored or overly frustrated at any point. The weirdness of the world left me constantly eager to see what was around the corner in an attempt to try and understand the bizarre setting I'd been dropped into.Can't wait to see what the devs do in future.What a great little Christmas present
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: offers a great time, there is a story but the focus is in the moment-to-moment experience. This is a very relaxing and satisfying game, with mostly tame puzzles and boss fights. It's also absolutely gorgeous, the levels are intricately designed and the top-down view really sells the idea of looking into a smaller contained world. The soundtrack complements the gameplay excellently, staying in the background for the most part but sometimes coming forth in a very atmospheric way. The central mechanic stays fresh as new twists are incorporated, adding complexity to the puzzles. However, if you're looking for difficulty, you won't find any head-scratchers until perhaps the last quarter of the game.I highly recommend this game and I can't wait to see what else this studio comes out with.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really like this game. I played it exclusively on deck, and laying in bed exploring the world of COCOON, I found it above all else to be cosy. The environments are visually interesting and small non-gameplay related props make it feel stunningly alive. The sci-fi elements feel unique and I was always excited to complete a puzzle to get to watch some  strange alien-bug-tech do it's fancy activation animations. COCOON's environment and technology designs are simultaneously futuristic but also derelict. Familiar, yet unknowably alien. One room will be satisfying to watch it complete an intricate power on sequence, the next a horrifying display of something almost-but-not-quite visceral. The scale slips between feeling like you are a microbe in a drop of water, to an interstellar traveller throwing around planets in your hands.COCOON, overall, is quite laid back and forgiving. There is no long lasting punishment for failure; most of the time it costs you only 30 seconds to return to exactly where you were. That lends itself nicely to the cosiness but, after beating and 100%ing, I actually found myself wanting a more difficult challenge mode.Although, like many, I was surprised by the length, COCOON does a good job of introducing new ideas consistently but without overwhelming the player. Many other developer would have locked features behind DLCs, or milked a novel mechanic for hours with small variations. The puzzle and level design are extremely well executed, I think they struck a masterful balance between railroading and open environments that are a good size without being too big. I can't think of any times I was upset or disappointed with a "boring" section, I can't remember the last game before this when I didn't find at least something boring. They present interesting mechanics with rules about how they work, and then let you figure out how to break them in very satisfying ways later on.The storytelling is exclusively show not tell, which is refreshing, it leaves a decent amount up for interpretation. I remember immediately thinking after watching the final cut scene, "THAT'S IT? But what about <spoiler> and <spoiler>! What did <spoiler> mean?! Although frustrated that I lacked the answers I craved, reflecting I think that goes to show how interesting and captivating the story was to demand my attention in that way.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I'd always been a bit wary of puzzle focused games. The small puzzles in games from the The Legend of Zelda games to the Uncharted games being as complex as I had played. However, after reading so much about Cocoon, from podcasts to a feature, and subsequently, a review in Edge Magazine, I decided to take the plunge.Having now finished the game, I am so glad that I did, and also, proud of the fact that I was able to make it until the end.Cocoon delights in the way it's puzzles require some thought, but are never too complex as to be impossible. As long as I kept in mind each spheres' mechanics, I was able to eventually figure out the path forward.Cocoon is more than a puzzler, with beautiful graphics, and a captivating score that helps pull you in. Furthermore, the audio design also adds to the atmosphere. The sound that plays once the solution to a puzzle has been found being a particular highlight.Boss fights do feature, and serve as a break between the puzzles. Each adding a different layer of complexity. None too difficult, however one featured an element that I had a bit of difficulty getting right.In conclusion, I would highly recommend this game, even if puzzlers are not normally a genre you play. The time spent in Cocoon's worlds will be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I can absolutely 100% recommend. The puzzles, atmosphere, colors, graphics, sound, music, game play. It all comes together to like a click. Never before seen or played, but feels familiar. I enjoyed every moment, even the moments of total confusion. No words are spoken, yet the totality of this game speaks for itself. Great job.Thank you for an awesome experience!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my radar since it was shown off in (I think) Day of the Devs last year or so. I finally got around to beating it, and it did not disappoint. Maybe I've grown too cynical but a lot of games nowadays seem to be disappointing or have too many drawbacks to be truly enjoyable. Not Cocoon, however.From the soundtrack, to visual design, to puzzles, everything connected in such a fun and satisfying way. The game was intuitive enough in its design that I could put the game down for any length of time and pick it up and still understand what I'm doing and where I'm at. It was a great experience with plenty of "ah ha" moments and lovely musical fanfare to accompany that.I'm really happy to see this game win awards across multiple award shows. As meaningless as some people say they are, it's nice to see it getting the recognition it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a complex puzzle game where you transcend worlds and carry them around with you to navigate through the game. While the game does test your intellect countless times, I went from start to finish in just under 5 hours for full completion, so don't expect anything too overwhelming.Many see this game as the one that sniped TGA's "Best Debut Indie" title from Pizza Tower, but having played through it, I now understand why it won the award. With an outstanding visual style and level design that made my jaw drop on countless occasions, Cocoon is an absolute must-play title.It runs relatively well on my Steam Deck, where I carried out my playthrough from start to finish. On High settings, it struggled to reach the native 90Hz, but it performed very well at 60Hz. For a complete world-ception experience, Cocoon is sure to blow your mind; it certainly did for me!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Puzzle mechanics are gracefully introduced and never overstay their welcome. The game is so simple to drop in and out of, making it perfect for people who don't have the most time on their hands. Genuinely one of my favorites in a while, the visuals and sound design had me hooked from the start.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Very entertaining. Puzzles are just the right amount of difficult so that you need to think about it but not so hard that you have to look up a walk-through.Only gripe is some bosses are really difficult to beat on keyboard controls. I'm specifically referencing the bosses you fight using flight as it uses tank controls. If you have a controller, I highly recommend using it at over keyboard--at least for those bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome “audiovisual journey”, the Limbo and Inside DNA is there. Less awesome as a puzzle game but worth getting. The puzzles are simple for the most part. There is nothing that should seriously stump you, but many are satisfying to figure out. On the other hand, the main gameplay loop of moving orbs around and getting in and out of them involves a bit too much juggling and becomes a bit of a chore. At the same time, the puzzle design doesn’t do too much mind-bending with the conceit. Going a bit deeper would have been nice. I would have appreciated a fast roll or similar “cutting-grass-in-a-Zelda-game” mechanic to make moving around more engaging when walking from orb to orb for the hundredth time. Maybe most importantly, it’s the perfect length - the good stuff doesn’t get old and the annoying stuff doesn’t get too annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Can't help but feel underwhelmed with this. The concept has potential, but it wasn't really explored to its fullest. The level design is very restrictive, and the controls literally only use one button, so the puzzle solutions can be very easily figured out through trial and error. There aren't any enemies outside of a few bosses, and there isn't any platforming or movement tech, so there isn't any other form of engagement.The game ending is also very abrupt, and it doesn't even have a final boss.  While COCOON is clearly much more ambitious than LIMBO and INSIDE, it unfortunately falls flat on the execution aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and bittersweet.It is a very interesting concept. The game starts a bit boring and tedious but gets interesting over time, especially near the end where you can nest a ball into itself. The sad part is that this is kind of a wasted potential because at the moment when the game starts to be really enjoyable, it just ends. They did not explore the possibility of recursive nesting further which I think was the point of the whole thing.Apart from the puzzle aspect, the boss fights were just annoying. Did not enjoy that part. Graphics are nice and the different worlds are distinct enough. Music was pretty meh.Overall, not a bad game to kill a few hours with. Not a great one either though.

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon feels different than other puzzle games! _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Strong recommend for art, but weaker recommend on gameplay. 3.5/5 on Backloggd (Note, took me ~6 hours, played offline on my Steam Deck, very good game to jump into on a flight.)Easily one of the most beautiful works of visual media I've ever experienced. It's not just the alien beauty of the environments, it's the immense attention to detail in every facet of how those things move and interact. There's a fascinating interplay of organic, inorganic, and abstract visual concepts that are all flawlessly employed into an interactive space with so many moments of sublime and wondrous environmental motion offered as a reward for solving puzzles and interacting with the world.The gameplay, on the other hand, is only pretty good. There are some solid puzzles on offer here, but it rides a really weird line between the simplicity of Limbo and Inside and a much more abstract puzzle design space that begs for a more fully realized and longer puzzle game. For me, that causes it to land in an unsatisfying spot. Some people don't like Inside for being too easy or simplistic, but if something is going to be mostly about atmosphere and art, I'd personally prefer the gameplay to be a bit more straightforward. Similarly, if a puzzle is going to make me think, I want it to make me think in a way where resetting the state of the puzzle is fast and most of the complexity lies in figuring things out top-down rather than just carrying objects slowly around large levels to figure out where to slot something for the next (usually simple) step.It's not braindead easy, but the most difficult moments just feel obtuse not because the conceptual tissue is lacking but because the layouts of the level obfuscate how things connect often due to requiring the player to travel unsatisfyingly large distances between the pieces of the puzzle. The most complex world layering puzzles at the end also have some really annoying setups in terms of how much space has to be traversed to reset elements of the puzzle when the player makes mistakes, and every case of this is implemented in an unnecessary way (the distances could all easily be halved in terms of level design).There are also weirdly some bosses, they're... Fine? A little bit too long on waiting on behavior cycles in some cases, but not frustrating or boring. Not a lot to say there. Also a bit annoyed I missed 2 of 12 collectibles, but there's no backtracking whatsoever, so it happens.Overall worth the play experience for the art alone, but the gameplay offered an itch that it never fully scratched.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I found this to be a very enjoyable game.Simple controls, nice art and good sound.The game doesn't allow you to miss steps, so you won't be "Oh no...I didn't do that 400 steps ago and now I have to go back!" - which is a bonus.So when you get 'stuck' you just have to breathe and realise that everything you need to solve the puzzle, is available to you.  If it isn't, it's not part of the solution.I played for 14 hours.  Even if I take 4 hours off for me getting stuck somewhere, that still leaves 10 hours.So if you've read other reviews about it only being 5 hours long, those players are either full time exceptional players....or full of crapola.  I/m not judging.  But I think the majority will spend more than 5 hours on it.Due to the lack of info sometimes you'll be faced with trial and error, where the 'error' will send you back a bit.   I'm not a fan of this, I like puzzle games to be puzzles only not 'try to get through a door, fail three times and I'm thrown back over the wall and have to start again'  - (this is an example only, not related to the game).   However, that was far from a deal breaker.Anyway...I liked it and recommend Cocoon.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals in Cocoon are absolutely stunning. They are easily the biggest draw to this game. They remind me a lot of Scavenger's Reign in the sense that the different biomes, creatures, and technologies are all very foreign but still very coherentThe gameplay is nothing crazy. It's good, but the puzzles are not too difficult so as not to get in the way of the real draw of the game, which is traversing through the setting and just seeing everything. I was told this was a puzzle game so I was a tiny bit disappointed when I realized they don't throw anything at you that makes you think very hard I also think it's really impressive how this game guides you without making you feel like it guides you. You constantly feel like you're figuring everything out organically, but the game does as much as it possibly can to make sure you figure out what you need to, and that you don't ever get stuckOverall, Cocoon is definitely worth picking up. Only ~5 hours long but worth the $25 anyway just to see the beautiful world they've sculpted for this game

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Cocoon is a gorgeous, mind bending puzzle platformer that was one of my most anticipated games of 2023.  This game is very unique in every conceivable way.  Not only is this game one of the most beautiful games ever made but it has a top notch soundtrack that fits the game perfectly.  Unfortunately, I was disappointed w/ the gameplay and puzzles.  I never found the puzzles to be all that challenging, but I did find them to be very tedious.  This is a game that has so much potential, but I'm not sure it really met those lofty heights.  Having said that, I still think this is a game that every game lover should experience at least once, but I'd probably recommend to wait until there's a sale before snagging it.Consensus:-Middle of the Road Game (Tier 4 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  Obviously, this is a deeply beloved game, and the team behind this is incredibly talented.  I wanted to love this game so much but unfortunately, I don't think this game stands up to any of the top puzzlers or logic puzzle games on the market right now.  This game feels more like an experience than a true puzzle platformer.  I think that's ok, but I think it's important that ppl know that going in.  Maybe I'm the minority here, but far too many of the puzzles just felt like juggling different colored universes as opposed to thought provoking puzzles that would give the "eureka moment".  It's an incredibly cool concept.  I'm glad I got to experience this unique game, but I don't see myself ever returning to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally my GOTY 2023. This game was a light that I really needed this year as I faced multiple disappointments with the games I was hoping to like.So up front, this game doesn't really explain anything to you. The story is told like the stories in LIMBO and INSIDE: It's not. The story and how you interpret it is entirely based on your perception of a story and your willingness to try to understand it. And with that said: It's present, I guess? It's not much to write home about.But the gameplay? The presentation of this game as a whole? You'll be hard pressed finding a game on this level. The gameplay revolves around world puzzles - not just puzzles in the world, but puzzles involving the worlds themselves. Each reality of the game is represented as a glass marble (which, btw, the way this game uses spheres as visual language for interaction is great!) that you can carry around and enter/exit like portals, seamlessly at that. The puzzles get especially mind-bending when you're traversing worlds inside worlds, and eventually even looping between worlds.All the while that's going on, the game's visuals are INCREDIBLE and selling the truly alien nature of the environments. There's familiarity, of course, but the difference in how these worlds work and look are truly alien. The audio going along with that visual presentation helps sell the alien feeling - because it's not real audio. Every sound in the game is entirely synthesized. So even things that sound familiar sound *off*, but without feeling like it's wrong or improper.Now here's the bad: The gameplay parts that aren't puzzles. The game features a handful of boss fights and a "shooting" sequence. These suck. The boss fights are unforgiving, which would be fine if they didn't reset you back to the beginning. I went into the game wanting to puzzle, not deal with increasingly frustrating boss fights. The "shooting" segment also just felt out of place and weirdly difficult. And while it's not as bad, I do think the game could've kept better accessibility in mind with differentiating color. The world balls are fairly difficult to tell apart if you can't perceive their colors and that carries over into the coloration of a lot of things. I played the game on Steam Deck and the small screen made any existing differentiating factors vanish. I can see all color just fine, but it still stood out to me.This game is a perfect example of a modern puzzle game, and shows that it's possible to create deep, intriguing puzzles without just doing the same puzzle over and over as with games like Superliminal or Viewfinder. One of my favorite puzzle games ever, and probably one of my favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - a very clean, captivating few hours, that'll draw you in and capture your mind both artistically and mentally.+ Very clean and cool aesthetic+ Moody soundtrack+ Very polished, completely bug free+ Unique boss fights and compelling, unique puzzle mechanics* Very linear* Zero dialogue* Fairly incoherent "story"- Little replayability- Very short (~3 hours)Cocoon is a unique, passionately imaginative puzzle game, both artistically, and puzzle-wise. It's set in a completely alien environment, where your surroundings constantly shift between unsettling melds of geological, technological, biological, and everything in between. The game has zero dialogue, or any spoken or written language of any kind. In fact, the only non-diagetic text you'll find anywhere at all is in the main and pause menu of the game. There are no explicit, written tutorials anywhere; the game teaches every mechanic entirely via player interaction.In addition to the psychedelic visual design, the puzzle mechanics leave little to be desired either. The unique "cocoons" you find throughout the game, and the interesting ways they can interact with one another, make for a surprisingly large variety of potential puzzle designs. Many have unexpected, clever solutions that don't just feel like gimmicks, but natural consequences of the way the mechanics work. The puzzles have just as much thought put into them as the complex and alien world they inhabit.Cocoon is a very well designed game, but it's also a very short game. A typical playthrough might only last 4-5 hours, and an experience puzzle game player may be able to beat it in as few as 2 or 3. For the price it's offered at, that's a hard sell. But the game itself is polished to a mirror shine in every other capacity.In addition, much of the "story" (if you can call it that) is largely mood driven. There isn't really a coherent story of any sort that the player can follow along with. For the most part, progression consists of: find a new cocoon, defeat the boss inside it, then use the ability you get to locate the next cocoon, and repeat. Most often, you're just figuring out how to manipulate your environment to continue moving forward, without really knowing why. That might not be a problem, but it does make the game feel somewhat aimless at times.If you're craving something unique that you can play for a bit to escape, and don't mind the price, cocoon is a very high quality experience.
