_childDocuments_.review: COCOON is a fantastic game that I have been looking forward to since the minute it was announced and I am happy to let you know that my expectations were met and exceeded and if you don't want to read any further, I can not recommend this game enough!I have always been a huge fan of Jeppe Carlsen's work. LIMBO and INSIDE by Playdead are both excellent games, but also his lesser known solo work, 140 and THOTH are terrific in their own right. If you have played the latter, you might remember my name from one of the achievements. I even had the honor of meeting Jeppe Carlsen, Jakob Schmid and some other (ex-)Playdead folk and I still cherish the memories of that night.When I heard that Carlsen had left Playdead to start his own studio, I was sad on one hand, because I had valued his puzzle design of their games as feeling integral to the world. But on the other hand, I felt excited for what was to come.Knowing Carlsen's work well, I expected this game to put a huge emphasis on game feel and intuitive player guidance with excellent sound design and music integration. And this is pretty much what I got, but I did not, even after watching the trailers, expect this game to look so absolutely gorgeous all of the time on screen.The game controls nice and fluid, everything can be done with eight directions and a single button. If you play on controller, you have analog movement controls but your character's idle animation can only appear in said eight directions. The music is more calm and atmospheric but there are occasional intense sections in the soundtrack, fitting the action on screen.What really boggles my mind is the puzzle design. Knowing Carlsen, I did not expect any less, but the way in which mechanics are introduced to the player, consecutively in didactically designed challenges to the point where it feels completely natural to come up with the solution for the next puzzle made me speechless. There was never a time in the game where I felt lost or stuck, I always had the drive forward but at the same time, the puzzles always provided the right amount of challenge to me and did not seem trivial to solve.There are very few very, very minor nitpicks that I still feel obliged to state here. The game starts with a "cold start" opening which is always cool, but from the player perspective, specifically on PC not always the best, since it prevents players from checking the game’s settings. As a result, the game started, at least for me, in 1080p and 60fps despite my monitor supporting 1440p 144fps and these gorgeous graphics deserve the crispest resolution you can offer them. The other slight issue I found was that some more frequent actions needed a held button press which felt just a tiny tad too long for my taste, to the point where I felt a slight bit of annoyance when I needed to do them often in succession. But as I said, these are absolute minor nitpicks, and the graphics options in the cold start can hopefully be fixed in a future patch. (Edit: The two issues with native resolution and frame rate have been fixed with the first hotfix.)Other than that, I have absolutely nothing negative to say about this game. Its length and dramaturgical development with environmental storytelling combined with gameplay make for definitely the most compelling experience, by far, I've had with any game I played this year.Very highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is an incredible game. Anyone that has played Limbo and/or Inside before is familiar with the designer's worlds already, and Cocoon is no different: It is a highly abstracted puzzle game in a stunning world, with very engaging gameplay that keeps the player interested by introducing layer upon layer of mechanics to scratch their heads at. The puzzles are brilliant. They start out simple but they gradually become incredibly complex without becoming irritatingly difficult or relying on cheap tricks for difficulty. Here's a list of benefits that I now enjoy after having partaken in the puzzles of Cocoon:-My brain size has increased by approximately 1.5 centimetre.-My spatial awareness has expanded massively. I now know the relative position of every object in my apartment at any given moment.-I feel more comfortable holding big balls in my hands. In fact, I feel confident in my ability to handle multiple pairs of balls at once.-I have a better understanding of Christopher Nolan's Inception.-I appreciate insects more and want to see them succeed.Thank you for listening.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me feel like a genius.I could actually feel the smoothness of my brain wrinkling away as I played through the game.In fact, merely having it in my library raises my IQ to double digits!Cocoon has some of the most mind-blowing puzzles l've ever solved in a game, and somehow none of them pissed me off. That's an incredible achievement in my book.It almost broke me 1-2 times but I kept telling myself "not losing to a children's videogame puzzle tonight" and managed to finish without cheating. Also nothing gets the adrenaline pumping like beating a game for ages 6 and up!This game is such a mind bending experience! I was simply BLOWN AWAY by how simplistic yet incredibly engaging this game is. Not just that but making you feel like you're learning a language in the process, with the way it builds upon itself. The stuff I was pulling off towards the end felt pretty incredible, and the puzzles weren't hard but they felt like they would be hard to explain what I was doing, which makes for a great puzzle game to me. Like I mentioned, the puzzles aren't super difficult but it does stuff that you're just like godd*mn, I had no idea you could do that, while still remaining intuitive.Cocoon does an excellent job of giving you enough tools to figure everything out without explaining anything. All of the mechanics - and how they build on and interrelate to one another - are discovered organically and without tutorial. But at the same time, the environments are thoughtfully designed with an economy of options, so there's no real threat of being led down the wrong path by a red herring solution. Even the controls are simply a movement stick and a single action button, leaving little to be guessed at other than how to progress with the limited and well-defined tools at your disposal. It certainly doesn't hurt that the game is gorgeous from beginning to end, with some lovely animations and attention to detail.It's an exceptional game with crazy art direction and superb puzzle design. A must for gamers looking for something as solid as it is different. I also saw some Hyper Light Drifter influences in terms of music and color palettes. The music is soothing, the puzzles are fun and become challenging as you go along with creative/clever ways to solve them, furthermore, the colors are vibrant and the animations are well-made. The whole game was for me very surreal. Cocoon and Inside are for me the highest level of gameplay design, where player's every action is absolutely natural within the game world. And it is achieved without a single word. The sound design is just— chef’s kiss. I was also equally impressed with boss monster/creature design, both visually and functionally. Loved the alien landscapes and insect-themed characters. Very cool and creative.Most of the time I found myself in awe at how well designed and intricate some of the later puzzles were. Especially how it seemed to carefully make sure you never softlocked yourself by detracting bridges at the right time etc. Whatever they used to map out how the puzzles would link together must have been so complex I was constantly wondering how they came up with them. For some reason the bits with the green orb and having to create circuits with further and further nesting to get timings right to automatically switch the green plaftorms really stood out to me. I think it’s cause they used that concept a few times but each time made it cleverer.The way the complexity of the puzzles ramps up gradually in this game is masterful. When I think back to some of the last few puzzles, they are incredibly intricate, yet the game leads you to understanding the mechanics so well that you will fully form the solution in your mind before enacting it. For me that's the sign of a brilliant puzzle game, there was no trial and error involved at all. Every time I got stuck, the solution would hit me like a freight train after a bit of pondering.While the game is easy, the ease is not down to poor design or underbaked ideas by any stretch. Many of the puzzles are only easy to solve because of how seamlessly and perfectly the game builds upon itself and teaches the player what is possible with the mechanics in small increments. A lot of the puzzles in the game would have been complete head-scratchers had they given you a sequence ending puzzle up front. What I enjoyed most with this game was the level of sophistication it was able to achieve with some of the puzzle solutions with what appears as such a simple barrier/obstacle on the surface. A snappy enjoyable little game.The less you know about this game the better, I recommend diving in with no knowledge. I beat it in a couple hours in two sittings, but your mileage may vary! It's short, but you know what, I prefer short and sweet to too long or dull. If you liked Limbo, Inside, Tunic, and Planet of Lana, you are going to have a blast with this one as well short, sweet, weird, and delightful. One of the best indie games last year. Highly recommended.Finally, HOW DARE YOU DISRESPECT ON PIZZA TOWER? THATS IT! YOURE GROUNDED GROUNDED GROUNDED GROUNDED GROUNDED GROUNDED GROUNDED GROUNDED FOR 1093847482299394577447745757382829294940202049494 YEARS! GO TO YOUR ROOM NOW!PIZZA TOWER SHOULD’VE WON!10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some really clever mechanics and a nice difficulty curve. The graphics and music are fitting, but not overly innovative. Some of the puzzles involve a lot of back-and-forth travel, which makes them a bit tedious. Last, to my taste, the game could have used more of a story. You solve a puzzle, traverse to the next area, solve another puzzle, traverse.. and that is all, except for the boss fights.Overall, I still recommend the game for its innovative core mechanic, despite its lack in some other areas.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: + AMAZING concept. As someone obsessed with fractals and infinity, this game was a dream come true.+ Vibrant and strange alien worlds with a beautiful polygon aesthetic. Exploring these dense yet lonely lands reminded me of sci-fi movies like Alien and Blade Runner.+ Killer soundtrack and immersive ambience that truly made you feel like you are undertaking an immense and mysterious journey.+ Masterfully crafted puzzles that made great use of the 'worlds within worlds' mechanic. As the game progresses, the puzzles get trippier, but never too challenging or obtuse. The game's linearity was one of its biggest strengths, making you focus on the puzzle in front of you rather than make you backtrack to some other faraway corner of the world to retrieve some stupid key to complete it.+ Very creative boss fightsCocoon manages to successfully weave a difficult concept into its game structure, standing proudly head to head with other indie masterpieces. Even if you are a veteran at puzzle games and may find this on the easier side, the game is more than worth it for the sensory experience and brilliant concept alone. What an experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games since Portal 2 that has grabbed my attention. It's a beautiful game with equally beautiful animations, etc. Those are just some nice extras because the gameplay stands on its own. It subtly tips its hat to Portal. You'll know what I mean when you play it.I've only played a bit over 3 hours and nothing has felt repetitive or boring. Quite the opposite in fact, which is unusual, especially for me, as I tend to get bored extremely easily and don't finish games too often. So far this has not been even close to a 'one trick pony'. The variety of items and their unique uses keeps expanding keeping the puzzles fresh and entertaining.I feel I've said enough without having to resort to spoilers. Bottom line, if you like puzzle games with a touch of some other game styles then you'll love this one. This is also one of the few games I'd pay retail price for. I would almost feel guilty if I got it for too cheap. I looked at the Credits page and was surprised to see that it was made by only a handful of people. Literally 5 or 6. I give this a 4.9/5 on every detail.Get it when you can and don't start playing until you have plenty of time because you won't want to quit.Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful puzzle game. It blew my mind several times. The style is minimal and beautiful, and the game-play reflects that. There are no tutorials or text in the game, and yet it's intuitive to play. The difficulty is perfect. I never got stuck, but never felt that the solutions were too obvious.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun puzzler with a very relaxing soundtrack. I do recommend to play it straight to the end over the course of a few days if you don't want to complete it at once. I left some months between plays, so for me it was a bit confusing at times due to the 'Inception' vibe. But that is also part of the fun.It even has replay value if you miss some Moon Ancestors, like me :)
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Spectacular. Such a distinct vision from the moment you start the game: from the gorgeous art direction and satisfying puzzles to the well-designed levels and bosses - I can easily say COCOON has been one of my favorite gaming experiences in awhile. I HIGHLY recommend this game - it's a must-play for anybody that appreciates a great puzzle game. This game rules.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely enjoyed COCOON. While the game is not long at all, clocking around 4 hours for me for 100% completion, I really liked the puzzles, the music and atmosphere. The idea of jumping between worlds is used nicely and doesn't feel bad. The game cleverly reduces the parts of the world you're allowed to travel to so that one doesn't get lost. In several circumstances I was surprised by a new mechanic I didn't expect.I just wish that the game would be a bit longer (like 1-2h) so that some concepts can get more time to shine. Even optional (hard) puzzles would be nice.All in all, this game is great if you want to spend a few hours, get all achievements and be done with it afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: brilliant stuff. i really stretched out the gameplay in terms of time spent but it's a great experience for how short it is. the puzzle design is so well done for the amount of aha moments it gives you, and the amount it lets you learn without (direct) guidance, save for the encouragement of swelling music (really stellar sound design). i never felt too frustrated to continue, only like i was exploring more. love a jeppe carlsen game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A bit too overhyped - really good atmosphere, although the visual design did not really fit me. Interesting blend of 140 and Inside, but in those elements does not reach highs of its predecessors. Puzzles are a bit obvious and do not feel like part of the bigger world... Overall good experience though.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game made my head hurt in the best way. I admittedly had to turn to youtube for help on a few later puzzles, but just having something telling me where to go next, or show me what little clue I was missing let me put the guide away and figure most of it out myself.TL;DR if you like the concepts presented in the movie Inception and enjoy puzzle games with really rich environments and GORGEOUS artwork, this is for you.This is NOT for you if you like prefer linear thinking, want dialogue, a combat system, gear, etc, or don't have the patience to walk a lil bug who can't even jump back and forth along the same path 4 times ferrying lil orbs back and forth. It's a puzzle game. If you don't like being confused and challenged, don't play it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The clever mechanics and ingenious style are more than enough to compensate for the lack of challenge and quick play through. The way the game holds your hand is beautiful, but I didn't want my hand held. If this game was mind bendingly difficult in addition to mind bendingly creative, it would be a perfect 10.Don't pick this game up if you're only looking for a challenge. If you want to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ inspired, then give this dude your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ money!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and unique game. No HUD and no text yet still the game has no problem showing you how the different game mechanics work. That's the definition of master class game design. I highly recommend this unique experience with its' well-balanced puzzles, great art style and useful - as well as atmospheric - soundscape.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's a puzzle game with a very good art style. These games live and die on the puzzle design and I think they kind of nailed it here. The puzzles here are simplistic but interesting which makes the experience fun and not frustrating.  Also, the general concept of the world is pretty intriguing with some neat secrets to find.All in all a very good experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely Not worth 25 bucks.It's mostly just a set of very basic back and forth puzzles that only serve to add padding to the game so that it'd last about 6 hours... assuming that the puzzles aren't immediately obvious to the player.Which then it becomes more like 3-4 hours.The visuals are great, but nothing special... and the soundtrack is... There, at most.I'll say, the game is pretty relaxing... since nothing really happens throughout 90% of it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience. The music, the visuals, the control; everything feels right. If I had to say one less positive thing is that, even if the controls can be remapped, there is no secondary button, only one can be set for each action. I would have liked mapping WASD to the arrows as secondary, for better ergonomics in the boss fights. But it doesn't actually detract from the gameplay one bit.In terms of running under Linux, it runs perfectly as is, you only need to enable Proton. It runs under XWayland on Wayland DEs, so be sure to have it available. A workaround would be to run it under Gamescope, but it's not needed.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Good game! As a few others have said, the puzzles are challenging but not brutally hard, often the kind where I kick myself immediately upon realizing the answer. Also as a few others have said, I would say its best mechanic is only used in one segment right near the end, which is a shame, as is the abrupt end. Also, if you're the type who views the price of games as important to how long you play them, uh, this is a little short for 20 dollars. Still, I am not one of those people. The game's strongest point is its atmosphere, which I really enjoy. It complements the puzzles extremely well. If you like wheels within wheels, this is a good game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting basic mechanic is cleverly built upon during the course of a concise game that is well executed in practically every regard.Whether you're on the right track is clearly communicated throughout by audiovisual cues and dynamic obstacles which eliminates senseless backtracking but might make the game feel a bit too easy at times depending on how well and how quickly you pick up the mechanics and the difficulty level you enjoy seeing in "puzzles".For me personally it hit a sweet spot combining just-right difficulty with a feeling of meaningful and varied progression in a world that was a joy to explore and difficult to leave between sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This game probably has over a hundred different doors and every single one is animated differently.I know that sounds random, but that should give you an idea of just how much attention to detail is in this game. Every second oozes with uncontrollable uniqueness and creativity. It's honestly an artistic achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game.  What can I say about it that others haven't already?Not as dark and brutal as Inside or limbo.  So kids can watch and play this one, nothing to worry about that might scar a young mind.Some of these puzzles are tough.  I had to think in new directions.  At least one of these solutions involved using a paradox.  I'm good with that.Very happy that the controls are so simple, Atari-2600 simple.  It really helps you fall into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle game. Very polished. Took me 5 hours with all collectibles, felt just right, not too short, didn't overstay its welcome either.Boss fights were the right amount of challenging, but once you learn their patters, wasn't too hard.The games has just 1 stick 1 button control scheme with an added accessibility setting that turns it into any stick + any button, which was a nice touch. Overall a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant. I feel bad that I didn't buy this last year when it released, it absolutely was GotY material. Although the debut work of this new studio, the devs have previous experience and the head of the studio has worked on another classic with Inside already. The design, a term which applies to both the visual and game design, is just a perfect crystalization of its underlying concept. Worlds within worlds. I also loved Patrick's Parabox, which features a similar core idea, but this is much more accessible and beautiful and can be recommended to anyone really.While rendered in 3D, the fixed top down perspective makes this a 2D scrolling game in terms of gameplay. So breaking it out of its frame, which is possible with Raicuparta's early UUVR mod, is not recommended. It does look stunning on a cinematic screen in Virtual Desktop though.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles, level, and map design are all great.However, the rhythm makes me lack motivation and flow when playing the game. The rhythm has been flat. Although it gives me a sense of calm, clarity, and reason, it lacks surprise and mood swings.Another issue is the boss fights. The connection between boss battle mechanics and the core gameplay is weak. These encounters seem to be included merely as a standard element typical in games, rather than being meaningfully integrated into the unique mechanics of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually very appealing, the puzzles are often simple, but yet they require some good thinking.Cocoon is really well-designed and fun to play, the only thing I think could be better is the playtime. I'm not saying 4h is bad for an indie game, I really REALLY enjoyed and loved it, I think that some mechanics could be developed a little more in depth for that extra “ah-ha!” moment.Solid game, 100% recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the worlds within worlds puzzles, and that I didn't need to look up any guides but it was still a challenge, and that no words were used to tell me either what to do or how the game works. I also really enjoyed the strange insecty otherworldly art. It was very fun and very satisfying! Also, I only needed the arrow keys and the spacebar for the whole game, no memorizing what button does what. Great puzzle game! I finished it in 5 hours over a whole bunch of sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I won't say that I understood the plot , but the gameplay here is incredibly captivating. Fantastic visual style and an intriguing setting, accompanied by pleasant and relaxing music. It's an excellent puzzle game for a couple of evenings.I can't claim to be a fan of puzzles and riddles; usually, when I encounter them, I'm searching the internet for solutions within a minute. However, this game was an exception, and I completed it without any guides . It's not that the puzzles are childishly easy here, but it truly engrossed and hooked me.A masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, stunning visuals, great audio, engaging puzzles. Doesn't hold your hand and tells you absolutely nothing. You are forced to try, experiment, and think for yourself. I like that very much.Only minor issue I have with the game, is that it's a bit on the short side. It can be beat in roughly 2 hrs. (Don't let my play time fool you, I leave my games paused and get off my PC to do other things, rather than closing the game).All in all, definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great little puzzle game. There's basically nothing I didn't like in this game. It has really strong visuals. The puzzles are all great. It's paced really well. It's really good and introducing mechanics that are simple to understand but are innately complex, and making you come up with lots of new ways to use them. It doesn't overstay its welcome but it's also not too short. Highly recommend to anybody that likes puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: 1. the game process is pretty linear, and for each level, the balls that can be used are limited2. in each level, the return path will be closed, reducing the puzzle's complexity3. the art style and colour scheme are very unique4. you can directly select the level to replay after completing the game, very friendly to finishing achievements
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is another game to add to the list of short art experiences that are well worth the price of admission. Think Artful Escape, Gris, and of course Limbo and Inside. Annapurna Interactive sure knows how to pick who and what to publish because this game deserves all of the love that its getting. There is legitimately not a single part of this game that I can knock. I don't dislike any part of it and thats coming from someone that DESPISES puzzles and puzzle games. The puzzle design and general gameplay felt very good, forcing me to think outside the box a good bit but still very much playing within its own ruleset. The best part of this game though is not the gameplay but the presentation, art direction and music all working in harmony. If you are a little wary that the trailers are just showing the good parts of the game? Yeah, those are the boring parts in the trailer, actually. There is a visual feast on display that absolutely blows you away when it gets paired with the atmospheric sound design and a fantastic soundtrack that really does a good job pacing the game out and setting the tone as you move through it. It's hard for a puzzle game to increase in complexity without getting overly complex, but Cocoon managed to not only increase the loose narrative stakes throughout the game, but it also gradually increased the complexity of puzzles in an impressive way that kept surprising me. I love how they used the mechanics like building blocks ending with some genuine brain tickling tests that force you to use all of the tools available to you and show that you were in fact not getting lucky up to that point, but understanding EXACTLY how the puzzle mechanics worked. That being said, it was again, very fair and unfrustrating to work through. For completionists, there is a function after you beat the game that allows you to go back to any specific point in the game to acquire all of the things you were missing so don't focus too hard on the extra stuff your first playthrough if you wanna get all achievements, just have a good time and enjoy yourself and you can go back later to find what you need. (It also has a statue that shows you where and what you are missing for the extra goodies so no need to guess where stuff is)I wish I had more to say beyond, "Hey, this kicks ass", but I don't. This is precisely what is advertised on the outside of the box and does a great job at providing surprises the whole way through that keeps you intrigued and engaged. This is one of those sleeper games that won't get mentioned come GOTY time but absolutely deserves a nod for being fantastic in 2023, a year that is jam PACKED with great games.Easily recommended. Follow my steam curator page for more reviews on indies like this, which helps.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is like the exclamation point at the end of the sentence "Games are art!"The world and character design are beautiful, the puzzle designs are clever, the audio design is excellent.It's not overly long, but I don't need that from a game like this, it would just either get way too complex or overly repetative.  The length feels just right.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Inside and Limbo were thematically interesting games but mechanically very underwhelming and rarely helped to enhance the overall package.Cocoon on the other hand keeps a ambiguous but striking, eerie theme going on while delivering one of THE most impressive puzzles games I either seen or played. Just when i thought i had figured it all out this game throws in such a tremendous curveball in complexity that caused me to overthink once it winded down. Dont get me wrong the pacing is excellent and so was the difficulty curve, but it really can play on your ego once you start making progress.Its what turns this game from a great time to something exceptional.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an amazing lesson on good puzzle game design. Its attention to detail (like with Carlsen's previous games) is just incredible, from the art to the music (Omg the way it beautifully plays a little melody when you've progressed) to the carefully planned out gameplay. However, what impressed me the most about this game was its ability to steadily increase the difficulty with its mind-wrangling puzzles, while still managing to keep me engaged and curious. I will say the worlds and characters are a bit "abstract" for my taste, which made the overall story a bit hard to follow, or maybe harder to connect with, especially since I completed it in more than one sitting. Still, the game is like a 9/10. Big congrats to Carlsen for leaving such a praised studio and moving on in a new direction while keeping the quality so so high.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it, wouldn't even say that it's short, for a puzzle game it was just about right. Most of the puzzles were fairly simple to challenging, can't say I really got stuck on anything, more so just trying to wrap my head around what I need to do. Also the fact that the thing that I thought was gonna bug out the game  was actually a real mechanic was an awesome feeling.Amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I wish the game was longer, but it is so well designed that I'm more than satisfied. The ramp up of difficulty is butter-smooth, the challenges are original and satisfying, ambience is spot on. The game could be use as a case study on how to communicate new mechanics to a player without needing a tutorial (or text for that matter). Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's short, it's unusual, and it's relatively mind-bending. I'd say that it's a puzzle game done very right =)The main pro of COCOON is that it successfully creates an air of truly alien world, a friendly mostly but still very different from what we're used to. The soundtrack and visuals are great but they are mostly to add to the feel and don't distract from it.Novelty wears off at about the same moment you finish the game, which is a good thing. Also, after I completed the game and wanted to load a checkpoint to collect all achievements I was told that the progress will be partially lost but it wasn't lost.Other than that this is an interesting experience albeit maybe a bit too expensive for 5 hours full completion time.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Beautiful. Cerebral. Worth every penny. The puzzles and mind-blowing and fun. Once I kind of understood what was going on it reminded me of the brain-spinng parts in Portal games. The art is colorful and eye-catching. The music and ambience are submersive. I couldn't stop playing, and even though it's kind of slow the short side, the experience of Cocoon will stick with me for years.I'm already looking forward to Jeppe Carlsen's next project.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: i haven't finished the game yet, but so far it seems like the reviews made its "world swapping" mechanic sound much more "deep" than it actually is. you can basically have a single "ability" at a time that allows you certain world interactions (all pretty standard puzzle game stuff), and you can swap those abilities by holding different spheres. each sphere is also a world you can jump into when it's placed in a certain area. there are games that utilize the recursion idea much, much better - recursed, patrick's parabox. the puzzles in this game barely had me pause so far (which is maybe 40% of the game?), but the reason for a premature review is the thing that roadblocks me for long - absolutely infuriating boss battles. they are completely unimaginative and formulaic - you basically have to evade boss attacks while traversing a "moving minefield", waiting for a randomly spawned "ammo" you can hit the boss with. a single mistake resets your progress, and it looks like each boss has more stages than the last. until they add a "skip battle" option, the game's definitely much more frustrating than it's fun.update after completion: well, in the end i pushed through and finished it. i'd say, feel free to try the game if you are confident about your reflexes, but if you are a puzzle game aficionado, you might as well skip it without losing much. it doesn't break any new ground; puzzles are logical and moderately clever, but not particularly memorable. "worlds within worlds" mechanic is mostly used to carry two spheres instead of one at a time, since it lacks recursion mechanic. later you can shoot a missile into a world. it adds some looping at the very end, by allowing to move from one world to another without leaving the world sphere, but it looks underexplored and i have a feeling the developer got confused himself about how to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles: very easy, but entertaining. Art: great. The game world is beautiful to look at.Gameplay is very simple and the mechanisms for interacting with the game world are introduced organically through the level design, there is no tutorial, nor is there a need for one.Replay value: very little. The game is very linear, following a strict path and a set story. There are some secrets that I missed, but going through the entire story again is too tedious for me.Overall I see this as an adventure game more than a puzzle game. A nice story to enjoy watching, with just enough gameplay to provide immersion.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I loved watching Limbo and Inside on youtube and this was my chance to play one of those games for myself, and I learned that these games are best experienced watching someone else play so you don't have to deal with the tedious chore of playing it yourself.If the character had twice the walking speed the game would be half as long. I had to stop and think about a solution exactly twice (Although one of the puzzles was actually good). The entire rest of the game isn't puzzles, it's opening doors with extra steps.Every now and then you come across some bars that you can't carry your orb through, but there's a pipe a few seconds away that will carry it to the other side for you. So you walk over, deposit your orb, pass through the bars, collect your orb. and then that's it, 10/15 seconds running around to deal with something that took you 1 second to solve mentally, and this game design is a constant. It makes every single action feel painfully tedious. It doesn't matter how many cool and unique mechanics you have in your game, if it's the only interactive object in the room the solution is obvious.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I guess it's kinda alright overall? About five hours long, though I've been mostly bored throughout the first half. There's no plot, other than solving puzzles and enjoying the visuals. Really had to question my life choices in the first half when the puzzles were pretty easy, but it kept building on top of existing mechanics and had some "thinking with portals" moments towards the end. Worth checking it out, but maybe consider waiting for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is a pretty and surreal experience but felt lacking as a game. Few of the puzzles required much deduction as the connections between the elements became clear as soon as all of the elements were spotted. Some of the puzzles were just about hitting the timing of a series of shots and the section would reset if you took too long. These would take a few tries while you got the timing down, but none of the shots could be designed as puzzles since the designers gave themselves no space because of the time constraints. The bosses were also rudimentary as puzzles since you could fail the section and needed to be able to complete all of the sections in a row. These boss fights were still frustrating due to the hit boxes feeling larger than they looked. Not a bad experience, but mostly bland to mildly annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: In a word, weird. In a second, nice casual puzzle game. The puzzles aren't particularly hard but do require some forethought and slightly out-of-the-box thinking, definitely nothing most people will be banging their heads against the wall over. The good:1. Nice puzzler. The limited control options kinda help with this. You only have directional movement and an interact button. I'd recommend a game controller, I used keyboard and it felt cumbersome. The puzzles themselves get more complicated once you have to take into account the layers of the orbs and boy did that get complicated. At one point the game  Though in hindsight its unexpectedness was ingenious.2. Length. The game was deceptively long. Just long enough to be enjoyable and not soo long that it felt like a slog. The puzzles also didn't get stale like they usually do. Whenever they were it was when a secret or a new mechanic or new curveball puzzle would hit you, simply put it was well paced.3. Silent story. I would normally say this is bad. Depends on the story and how it is portrayed to the player. But this was told entirely through subtext and minute detail in the environment. If it weren't for the ending giving "some" clarity I feel like each player could take something very different away from this. Considering it's length leaving the player guessing "WTH is going on?!?! is surprisingly not a bad choice. The bad:1. Level design. This is actually not bad per se. But the levels do this kinda "dickish" move where they make a LOT of nooks and crannies merely to distract or disorient the player. Considering the "secrets" hidden throughout and the lack of backtracking this just felt kinda cheap. Only consolation is that while looking around for these secrets its more likely for the player to notice the environment design / story elements so pros and cons.2. Replay value. Low to very low. Outside of getting any secrets you've missed I don't see any reason to replay sadly. Story was interesting sort of but without the surprise / wow factor it has low appeal. The only chance it'd have is the sheer number of puzzles so likely between runs you will have forgotten most if not all the solutions.In the end a good game. If you got 4-5 hrs to burn this'll do that quite well. Unless you get stuck :P
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cocoon is fantastic. Its an insanely polished and dense game. The principle of the game is that your puzzle mechanics are also worlds that you carry with you, at the start this feels like a fun gimmick. But as you make your way across the game you start blowing your own mind while constantly figuring out what you are capable off. The beauty of it is that you wouldn't be able to recreate the experience of cocoon in any other medium, its a game that REALLY makes use of the medium.That being said don't be worried if you are new or bad at puzzles, Cocoon is a super accessible game and you generally won't get stuck. You only have your movement and 1 action button. Yet the game really pushes that simplicity to its limits. It is a master at teaching you stuff without using text. It constantly throws new mechanics at you and yet it does so in a super digestible and fun manner.All of that is packaged with a game that feels insane to the senses. The sound, visuals and world concepts all feel so alien and intense. It can at times be a bit much, but it never really outstays its welcome due to its short length. All in all the only real complaint I had is that the game can feel slow at times, in the physical sense. Your main character doesn't move very fast, and a lot of the mechanics require you to walk or wait for stuff. So there were quite a lot of moments where I knew exactly what the answer of the puzzle was, but I still had to wait quite a lot to solve it.But that is just a minor complaint in a sea of compliments. The game is a master piece that doesn't waste your time, and for its cheap price I highly recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The start seems a bit too simple for me, but it does pick up in complexity. I had hoped, it would be more like a pure puzzle game (somewhat like Patrick's Parabox maybe), but it's more of an adventure/exploration game with puzzles.What bothers me is that the game won't let you experiment much. After solving a puzzle, you can't interact with the elements anymore, because they straight up dissolve or bridges and gates get closed. It feels a bit too guided for me because of this.I'm not sure if it's too short, or if it's just right in length for what it is. The art and sound direction and the whole atmosphere of the game in general are absolutely phenomenal, though. Very very alien, with shapes, nobody could have ever imagined.Overall pretty decent game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I can fully recommend COCOON if you want a pretty, simple, short, relaxing puzzle game that activates your almonds but doesn't make you want to look up a guide every 5 minutes. Not much of a story or a theme when compared to INSIDE or LIMBO, but I still greatly enjoyed the presentation and the boss battles were very creative surprises in a game with no combat and one interact button. At the later stages of the game some puzzles can seem confusing since you have to do a lot of sphere juggling but solving them is very satisfying (I really like the "puzzle solved" sound) and I never felt stuck.While I feel it's worth the money, I bought it during a sale and you might wait for a better one. I did take my sweet time and the game took me about 7 hours to complete, it's definitely on the short side.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Challenging puzzle design and boss fights yet not to the point of ever making you feel like giving up. The puzzle mechanics work very well and the art style is gorgeous. Audio design makes the world feel very immersive.If you have thalassophobia and/or megalophobia, be warned that the game does contain these themes.It's like Portal (design) and Journey (art) had a unique lovechild. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: At long last, HERE is the missing puzzle design component of the PlayDead Studios creative schism!If Jumpship's Somerville in particular left you cold, I think Cocoon will restore your faith in wordless, vibes-based puzzle adventures. I know takes like this must be frustrating for those at PlayDead, and I'm sure their followup to Inside will be amazing, but it's been a very long time...The fact that we don't get much high quality iteration on Limbo-adjacent formulas is a shame,  so it's very natural to be tracking experienced developers and hungrily picking apart the creation of the few games in this style we get.Assuming a sentient extraterrestrial sees/hears in similar light/sound spectrums we do, and they can handle a single directional input and one button, THIS is the game we should expose aliens to as a demonstration of human creativity and intelligence...In fact, much about Cocoon is so refreshingly otherworldly and smartly designed that it frequently feels like Geometric Interactive might have had access to documents or inspirations from an advanced civilization.Coming from someone that wolfed the whole experience down in a couple of days; slow down and savor this one for as many little play sessions as you can!From the communicative and evocative synths, to the beautiful and attractive take on organic technology,  this is a rare and brilliant little treat that respects your time and expands your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- The different worlds are well designed and visually appealing.- Puzzles are incorporated in a straightforward way, mostly to open blocked paths. There's no big fanfare to congratulate you, you just move on and feel good about solving puzzles as more and more worlds and mechanics are introduced.Neutral:- The game is completely linear with very little exploration. Some paths are even blocked off after you've crossed them so you don't even begin to think about backtracking.- It feels like they didn't even try to put in complex puzzles. Recursion and paradoxes, which should be a core part of this world-inside-world theme, are only briefly introduced at the very end. There are some "aha moments", but not a lot to keep up the constant progression. I often wished for some complex puzzle to test my understanding of a mechanic, but instead there are action-focused boss battles.Negatives:- Random dead ends, everywhere, on every pathway. Very annoying and completely unnecessary.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A unique, mind-bending, horizon-expanding experience. Incredible sights, sounds, and style. Short - yes, but somehow exactly the right length for it to convey everything it wants to. Quite simply a masterclass in game design. We may be living in 2023 but the these devs are living in ... well, a different dimension, I would assume.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Unique art style and game mechanics. I kind of wish there was more of a story line and I was also a bit disappointed with the little amount of play time. Especially for the price. $25 for not even a full day's worth of game-play? I get that it's a pretty game and took a lot of design work, but it's overpriced for what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 perfect puzzle game - Each puzzle is a total mindf***. Somehow the levels keep getting crazier and crazier, the game constantly building upon itself while never feeling convoluted or confusing. I didn't want the experience to end! I believe there is much more untapped potential to this concept, however when finishing the game, I didn't feel unsatisfied. The game didn't leave any threads dangling, and it adequately explored all of its core mechanics in new and interesting ways. I appreciate that they didn't try to make the game longer than they were ready for, at the risk of some mechanics feeling repetitive. This is a truly remarkable puzzle game and I congratulate the team on a 10/10 execution. The entire experience is so seamless- no unnecessary UI clutter, the controls are simple, the game has 0 bugs and runs effortlessly on my PC. Artistically beautiful on the visuals and audio. You can tell every single department brought their "A game" to this one. Game is 4-5 hours long. Any DLC or sequel to this game will be an insta-buy for me. Really, really strong start for this company. Excited to see what they do next!!!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I gave up writing reviews of games a long time ago, I mean what is the point, who really reads them?Once in a while however there comes along a game that stands out that you want to shout from the rooftops.."WHAT A GREAT GAME...BUY IT!" Cocoon is one such game.To tag it a puzzler/exploration would be doing it a disservice.Puzzles are not difficult, there is a learning curve but it is beautifully judged and organic that I never felt like I was"solving" anything.Most of all, this game conveys a sense of wonder and awe, transporting the gamer to a truly Alien World, where the only way of navigating through is by "reading" the signs and following your intuition.Sublime .
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Annapurna blessing us with another GEM of an indie game.  The puzzles are very unique and fresh, requiring some in-depth thought without being too punishing. The game is consistently implementing new tools/tactics and only expands upon them with each passing moment.  No techniques that you learn will be tossed to the side; everything keeps compounding together in a very rewarding way.  Highly recommended for the price. Extremely smooth experience with no bugs at all. Gave me a drastically better experience than all the $70 AAA titles that are riddled with issues nowadays.  Great job, Geometric Interactive.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and design in this game are amazing. Not needing load times between worlds is truly a testament to how far we've come in creating games. The puzzles feel challenging, but also fair. The difficulty ramps up as you play, so although you might burn through the first couple of puzzles, you'll be trying to wrap your brain around the last one. Not entirely sure about the story, but what was there was pretty engaging.Pretty fun, very short. Needs DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles were incredibly easy, so if you're in to solving things then this isn't the game for you.The most difficult part of this game, when I had to turn off my autopilot and /sort of/ think for a moment, was when I lost the green orb. After not-so-meticulously scanning the worlds that I had available in search of the green orb, I learned that you may access the green world through the purple world, but the purple sphere does not reflect the accessibility that would then allow you to reclaim the green orb. Should one play without autopilot, they may simply remember that the last time they had the green orb was shortly after play within the purple orb. Me not being capable of playing this without my psyche as numb as possible, I not-so-frantically searched through each of these worlds which had then consumed approximately 30-60 minutes of my life that I will never get back.To be honest, this seems like a developer oversight to me.Aside from that, I would describe a bulk of the game to be waiting for incredibly slow mechanics to eventually, E.V.E.N.T.U.A.L.L.Y., make its way through its animations to then allow you to further your progress.That's the game. You're waiting. You're waiting for what may feel like seconds, minutes, even hours. You're waiting for your crawler to catch up to you. You're waiting to get back where you were when you fall through a platform due to your crawler being unable to catch up to you. You're waiting for the unskippable credit sequence to end so that you may claim the achievement for completing the game. You're waiting. Waiting. Waiting. Forever waiting. Never a moment spent not waiting. Because that's what you're doing. That's how you're choosing to spend your life, and your time, that you will never get back. Waiting. Waiting for more? Less? I don't know. I waited for so long that I had forgotten why I started waiting in the first place. I waited until my face turned purple, because I forgot to breath as I was focusing on what I believe the developers wanted you to most experience throughout this game. The wait. I put every fiber of my being into experiencing this wait. Making sure to salaciously, almost in a perverted sense, FEEL the wait that they tried so hard, within every passing moment of this experience, to force you to endure.So, yeah. Should you purchase the game, enjoy the wait. It certainly isn't one of those more quick games with mechanics designed to keep you playing. Some people are in to that, though. If you are, enjoy. If you aren't, you'll be bald by the time you finish because you've had the time to continue pulling out each and every single one of your hairs in sequence due to the never-ending wait.Okay, I think we covered it. Later. Have a good one. Enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving it a positive review because creativity like this should always be encouraged, the world building and environments are excellent. The puzzles seem to be many of the same type of regurgitated mechanic that these type of games contain. Not bad but not great. It took me just over 7 hours to compete the game, which is on the edge of value for money.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with a unique mechanic. The game never lets you feel lost, but I wish there was more of a struggle. There were a handful of puzzles I found challenging, but sometimes just experimenting with the mechanics will allow you to run into the solution without fulling understanding the puzzle. The plus side to this is the game has a very nice flow with slight difficulty, but constantly making progress.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an impressive game this is. Stunning artstyle, the sound design is STUPID good, puzzles can be very intresting and creative, as the boss battles can be as well. Quite the challenge at times, and for the most part it was a challenge I was happy with! But near the end bit of the game, it was getting to be just a bit too much and frustrating. I was hoping there'd be a final big boss at the end but there wasn't which was a lil disappointing, I feel like that could've really wrapped this game up together better but who knows maybe my thoughts will change on this game. Overall, I rate it an 8/10. Was gonna be a 9, but the last 3rd or less of the game's puzzles really brought it down lower though but still, really wonderful game! If you like yourself some puzzles, I'd say try it out! See watchu think! If you're new to puzzle games, this may be a bit more challenging, maybe not but feel free to try it out anyways if you'd like to try something new!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Checked it out because it got awards in 2023. My complaints come from the end of the game, so spoilers abound.The casual run through is great, the most memorable bit for me: there is one puzzle in particular that required placing worlds within worlds -- and launch the orbs that represent them to catch a laser beam so you can trigger an effect and move on. Very clever.I dunno what it is with Indie Games lately and true endings but there's a cryptic secret ending and seemingly no indicators for the collectibles (moon ancestor) after you've cleared the game.I found just over half of em and won't be turning the dial manually, just fished em out. Its a short and tight experience, why make these so cryptid?
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: You start by getting plopped into a world, with no text, no dialogue, and no instructions everything you do you must figure out on your own. Things start simple but gradually build to more and more complexity, but never feel too farfetched or out of reach, and that’s the genius of the design here.As this weird little bug explores stunning vistas and mind-bending worlds, more layers are added. There were several puzzles as the game progressed I had to sit there and think about the full mechanics of how it would work, usually just a minute or so, and then I’d spring into action invoking my plan, for the most part, these plans worked well and the satisfaction from doing so was immense. It’s all relatively simple, just movement and an action button but it can lead to stunning complexity.The ease of the controls and what you can do isn’t all great though as many of the puzzles, especially later on get a bit repetitive, you’ll constantly be switching out orbs and running back and forth and if you mess up it’ll be even longer doing this, at points it could feel tedious.Boss fights are more like puzzles with a sort of fail state(although the game is very forgiving and you’ll never get a game over the screen) as you try to figure out how to best them you’ll be chased down, these are some of the best parts of the game as it adds a bit of tension to an otherwise relaxed game. Despite this, however, failure can feel a bit tedious.It also helps that the world our creature inhabits is so beautifully realized, it evokes a truly alien landscape as you ponder just how this world works and what exactly is going on, and since there is no dialogue or text in the game the visuals, as well as the sound, is all you have to understand the world. Things will catch your eye as you walk past or even fly past them seemingly so much bigger than what you can see on the screen and begging for more explanation. It is this alienation that makes the game feel so unique. Both the soundtrack and the sound in general add to this alien feeling, weird bug-like noises and melodic beats pump out that feel just a bit off evoking wonder and mystery as well as unfamiliarity. All three of those elements blend in a way many games can only dream of achieving.In terms of story as with the lack of dialogue and text it leaves a lot for interpretation, making it best to experience on your own, though each orb you best seems to be leading up to something. Managing to succeed at telling a sort of story and having a visually and audibly stunning game is an impressive feat, while the gameplay sometimes feels a bit tedious it is overall a great experience and a good contrast to some more text and dialogue-heavy games.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little puzzle game that will delight anyone looking for a mysterious adventure.Puzzle enthusiasts looking for a brain challenge might get a bit disappointed, though.If you're one of the latter, I'd recommend checking out Recursed for a real challenge involving worlds that can be carried into/out from other worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect puzzle game.Really. I don't just say these things.Geometric Interactive has tuned this work of art to a fine point. It completely absorbed me and I already want to experience it again.The control scheme is deceptively simple (movement plus one button), and yet the mechanics develop depth that continued to surprise me until the end of the game. When you think you have it all figured out, something comes up and you realize your tools can do more and more.All of this woven into one of the most beautiful minimal tapestries I have seen in a game of this budget level.Just buy it and play it. Don't look it up. Don't use a guide.It isn't very long (took me less than five hours), nor is it very hard, but you have never played a game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: One of the coolest and most memorable puzzle games I’ve ever played. My favorite thing about it was that the difficulty level felt absolutely perfect. The game has ways of gently guiding you in the right direction without making things too easy. Great if you’re like me and can start to get impatient when you get stuck in one spot for too long. Would highly recommend to anyone who likes other games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: fun flow to the puzzles, good art direction + music and lots of nicely polished details in animations, scene transitions, etc.the similarity in motif to a certain other fav -  - isn't a bad thing and is overall done well but it doesn't quite reach the same heights. that's the GOAT though so it's an achievement to be in the same ballpark.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Don't come into this game expecting Limbo or Inside. This doesn't have the same creepy industrial atmosphere, but is much more alien, which is interesting. This one is heavy on puzzles if you're into that. Overall great game. Only thing I didn't like is its very PG. I hate to keep comparing, but in Limbo and Inside, part of the fun was seeing all the different ways you could die.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a 50/50 score but I have to lean a bit negative due to the legacy of Inside which is a superior game. Cocoon is a good puzzle game with a nice art style and passable music/ambiance. The game suffers from a few issues however, There is a consistent aspect where paths needlessly branch to service the aesthetic at the expense of flow. I find myself checking branching paths constantly to see they are in fact dead ends that are there simply to add texture to the map. This is a mistake on the part of the designer. Also, the game suffers from periodic stutters whenever it is loading in data for the next area as you traverse. This is a unity bug which exists in almost every game using the engine. It can be obfuscated but this developer hasn’t done that. Minor but irritating on such a low demand game. Finally, the previous game inside was not only a masterpiece of design but it felt like something large was at stake. What you were moving towards felt dire , grim and important. Cocoon on the other hand feels simply like a puzzle game. I don’t really care what’s happening in this world. I’m just solving puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game where you simply and only press meaninglessly distinct buttons in bloomfoggy locales.As far as I know from fully beating one 'orb dimension' and boss; your powers, capabilities, and movement never permanently increase. And the manner in which your 'interact' button conditionally changes are nonsensically disconnected, boring, and meaningless.For example, early on in the game, you need to get down from a higher location. You press a button and a stone staircase appears heading downwards.  Later on, you need to get from a lower to a higher location.Here, instead you pull a sticky switch orb that tugs its gooey tether across a groove in the ground that appears fleshy and perhaps living. After pulling it across this arced groove, totally disconnected from it a few feet away a giant wafer thin beetle looking creature nearly the size of the room you are in unearths it self and stands stock still. There exists a giant button on its back, and since it is flush with the ground you walk on to it and press it. The behemoth creature then minutely adjusts its posture, forming a 25 degree slant and allowing you to walk slightly upwards to your implied destination. How 'cool'. End of room.Every puzzle is like this.There is no connection between form, function, and meaning in this game. This combined with the fact that nothing changes the status quo of the game, means I can't recommend it.For a second I thought otherwise when I acquired a little drone buddy that could remotely activate things in the overworld, but roughly a minute and thirty seconds after I received him he was permanently removed from my character. Why? well because inside the desert dimension there is a randomly crashed ship from who knows where considering how dimensions and the outer space contained in these worlds works.And the little drone buddy decided this particular activatable was his fated final destination. What did the ship that ate the only buff in the game do exactly? Open a big door.The game merely functions, and looks fine in the way nearly every other textureless polygon indie game looks fine. All other possible aspects you might wish to find are either weak or nonexistent.The thought would be this game might just be for true blue puzzlefans, but the puzzles were not particularly challenging unless they became briefly unintuitive. To the games credit, that was relatively rare, but present.Regardless, with the game being virtually nonexistent otherwise, it instead might only tickle the fancy of some walking-sim enjoying video game tourists. Those who are for some reason so stilted even in that sub-genre's bad tastes they are excited to walk by all those aforementioned, textureless, purposelessly arranged polygons.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Quality atmospheric puzzle exploration game. The graphics and style are very pretty, though I wasn't entirely fond of some of the areas. The puzzles aren't extremely hard, though I sometimes had to look up a guide to figure out what I missed. I really struggled with some of the bosses and timing this one sequence in the latter portion of the game, but it was otherwise an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: While it doesn't have the impactful and more straightforward story of Inside, Cocoon really makes up for it with extremely interesting and unique puzzles. The world of this game is alien in a way most games aren't when it comes to intergalactic beings; their forms are inhuman and obtuse and abstract, they move in discomforting ways and gurgle perplexing noises. The art style makes the creatures and all the things you interact with so visually stimulating, and open to interpretation as to what they are attempting to resemble. The environments in which these worlds inside of worlds take place is always so interesting and finding a new globe to dive into was never not exciting. The ending was also way more interesting than expected and put all of my actions into a much more galactic perspective. Overall, it's a really fun puzzle game with amazing art that's worth the price
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game with mechanics that feel new. The visuals are beautiful, original, and clean, and so is the music. Had me scratching my head a few times but nothing too hard which is good since you don't feel stuck for too long. I felt like the more interesting recursion puzzles only really showed their face towards the end, I think it could have been cool to have a few more mind benders. Highly recommend for those who like puzzle games and want to sink their teeth into something novel.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle game with even greater visual design, relaxing to play and a feast for the eyes. The game has unique puzzle mechanics. The puzzles start easy but get more complex as the game progresses and more mechanics and interactions are unlocked. The last puzzles are more challenging, but really rewarding when solved.While the concept of the puzzles already makes the game worth playing, the graphics make it outstanding. Games where you are happy when you can't play because you are stuck in an animation are rare. This game certainly achieves it. Instead of using a loading screen, this game transports you from one puzzle to the next by using animations that transform the game world. The different regions are all beautifully designed and small details like rippling water or plants the react to your movement are included. Solutions to puzzles are sometimes hinted by details in the level design. They do not spoil the fun as they are often equally hard to notice as solving the puzzle would be.Now I did not mention sound design earlier, but not cause it is lacking anything. The game has a relaxing atmospheric music that fits well to the mood of the game. It is more riveting in a boss fight and reacts when you solve a puzzle.A feature worth mentioning is the load function. When you solve a puzzle, the game closes the way back and takes options away that are not needed anymore or that would break future puzzles. When this happens, you normally get a new checkpoint. If you ever want to replay a puzzle or feel like you have missed something, you can load a checkpoint and continue from there. I highlight this here because I overlooked that feature at first. While I believe this game was developed for Windows only, it worked quite well with Proton on Linux. The only issues I had were noise errors that seem to be an issue of Proton and over-steering when using the keyboard. When I walked in a direction for some time, the player movement did not stop right away when I released the key. If you have this issue, a restart might already help. Or you can use a controller. I never had the issue there, (Or you play the first boss by tiptoeing because you did not try either xd)
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very beautiful experience. Not as hard as it may seem, the game gives a lot of guidance to avoid going into areas that do not assist in the current puzzle. Sounds are very soothing, animations are always different, visuals are weird but lovely, puzzles are fun, and story is kind of non-existent. I definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful little game with puzzles that don't get old. There's new gimmicks everywhere and the art enraptures you and pulls you into the world the developers have created, much like the orbs you carry on your back. It's a shorter game but nowadays my time is limited and it's games like these I enjoy the most.Definitely get it if you're debating it, the price is a lot but this is not just a game - it's art. Games like these are few and far between. Despite the short playtime you'll be thinking about it for a while and there's plenty of secret optional puzzles to uncover, but they're not so hidden it's frustrating to find them.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: A game primarily about a little bug creature hurriedly transporting pearls to and fro. The twist is, however, that each pearl contains an entire world to explore. Worlds, within worlds, within worlds - our little bug creature's journey will involve making use of the mystical, recursive nature of these portable wormholes, solving many puzzles as they slowly work their way out of their dimensional chrysalis. What awaits them at the outermost layer? In and out an in again, the process of their grand metamorphosis growing ever-more complicated. But perhaps a creature like this little one can't grow without experiencing adversity... And developing an understanding of the many worlds they both explore the vast expanses of... and cradle on their sturdy back. A marvelous  (if short!) atmospheric puzzler. Inputs are so simple, they're bound to only four keys. Wonderful vistas ranging from the serene to the grotesquely alien are yours to explore and puzzle through. Despite the brevity, the puzzles really do get pretty head-twisting! But, despite it all, the game does a marvelous job offering encouraging little nudges in the right direction. And rumor has it there's a big secret lurking very deep within this wordless world...
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Took me 6 hours to Finish because I am stupid. Good - Graphics, ambience, animations, physics, first 4 bosses, gameplay, transitions, sound design, music Bad - back tracking, easy solutions that made me feel like an idiot, no story, no characters to emotionally invest in, Ugly - no gruesome deathsthe game has some really enjoyable bosses I wish the entire game was just bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Astonishing game. Short, beautiful, nice soundtrack and awesome transition animations. This game requires only one analog stick and A(or X on dualsense) button on gamepad, yet gameplay somehow in many places ahead of some AAA games. Really love that game utilize soundtrack very well, especially I love moments when game hints me I am on the right way making neat sound progress.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. Too bad for me it was ruined by unnecessarry boss levels that just make gameplay frustrating.  Why oh why are devs still stuck on including these things in what otherwise would be a great experience. Im so done with this game and any other that feels the need to include it.  As the saying goes... Repeat Repeat Repeat Delete.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful little gem!If you enjoyed LIMBO and INSIDE, then this is a no-brainer (though you'll need to bring your brains along for the ride :P).There are some recurring perspective-based puzzles, which can get a little stale, and an arcade-y "shooting" sequence involving flying rhombuses that feels out of place in such an inventive, pitch-perfect puzzle game.However, these two slight missteps are not nearly enough to diminish the experience, which is elevated further by the lovely visuals, flawless controls/interface, and alien sound design. Don't miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: It's visually nice but you can get the full experience by watching a video. I really don't know why anyone would choose the "puzzle" tag for this game. There are only a few situations where you have to mind the order of operations, but that's like saying going to the toilet is a puzzle because you have to remember to pull your pants down -> sit down -> relax. If you're not looking for a game but an interactive experience, a world to explore, I still couldn't recommend the game because the bosses require you to actually play a video game. They're not difficult but it's in stark contrast to the walking around that makes up the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Exceedingly clever game.(++) Core concept/execution of that concept was done superbly, it was a fascinating and unique type of puzzle game. Plenty of 'aha' moments throughout, as any good puzzle game has(+) Difficult curve was perfect-- nothing was too trivial, and the game ended just as the puzzles of nested worlds was reaching a breaking point(+) Level design was really well done, it kind of organically/quietly kept you to small sections so the game focused on solving problems rather than exploration or 'where do I go again?'. Adds to the zen flowstate nature of the game, since it's not discretized like Portal(+) Sound design was impeccable(+) There were at least a few major 'wow' moments for me in my playthrough(+) Its very short, ~5 hrs or so(=) World was very alien; visually interesting but a bit abstract/sterile. I thought it was cool(=) Ultimately not that difficult. Most of the puzzles are relatively easy, and even the harder ones aren't too bad. There are no frustrations/true struggle in the game, which makes it more of a meditative/flowstate puzzler than a brain bender(=) There are boss 'fights' in the game, which felt slightly out of place and where more of the difficulty lies(-) No major narrative elements, it is truly a 'vibey' puzzle game. If you don't like puzzles, stay away, that's mostly what this has to offer
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for so long, after being massive fans of 140 and THOTH by Jeppe Carlsen and Jakob Schmid. This game is above and beyond what the trailers made me think. Every puzzle makes you go "whoa, I never thought that mechanic could be used in that way." The game's visuals are stellar; art style is impeccable. Sound design and music are ALWAYS on point in a Schmid game. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun! The end was totally worth it. I think the biggest thing I learned was to trust the developers and the puzzles. There were multiple times where I got frustrated and felt like a situation was impossible. But if it's possible to break these puzzles, I never did. SO, if you feel stuck, keep looking around and exploring. The game is really good about making sure that your path forward is always available, though not always straightforward. It's also a nice touch that the music corroborates your actions when you are on the right path. Keep an eye out for the moon ancestors!
_childDocuments_.name: COCOON

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give this a middle thumb, but I'm leaning more towards yes, so that's what I'm giving it. Some advice for newcomers to get maximum enjoyment, I would recommend doing two play sessions for your first playthrough. For the first one, play up until you get to the purple zone, take a break or come back the next day, then finish the game. If you want to know why, keep reading, but you're better off stopping here and just playing the game instead.Spoiler's Ahead:I didn't love this game, but there are a couple points that are pretty neat. Although I think you're time (and money) is better spent on games that have more focus, I think Cocoon at least sticks its ending, even if most of the process leading up to it wasn't very interesting. What I mean by that is Cocoon has a sort of half and half split of looking at symbolic imagery and solving puzzles. It leans more on the latter, but none of the puzzles were very challenging because (I'm pretty sure) the intended experience was supposed to get you thinking about how the main mechanic relates to the theme of creation. It worked for me, but only in isolation of actually playing the game. It's hard to put into words, but what I mean is that because 95% of the puzzles weren't hard to figure out, my mind was checked out for a vast majority of the game since I wasn't being asked to do much. It's weird but I think if Cocoon was shorter and had WAY harder puzzles, or if it was a walking sim focused on its theme with no puzzles, this would have been a slam dunk like Limbo and Inside. Instead I'm mixed, since most peoples' playthroughs won't be interesting until they're already half way done.I don't regret my time with Cocoon, but I probably won't ever play it again.
