_childDocuments_.review: Worth 60$? I absolutely think so. For newcomers, this is a great place to start as well. The game makes a lot of great QOL changes to the formula that Sandlot should absolutely adopt.However, it can fall into the same trap as all other EDF games once you try to get to higher difficulties at times.You either have to grind a mind numbingly large amount of time to get better weapons and armor. (In this game mostly armor since Yukes sees the obviously stupid flaws of Weapon pickup crates in Sandlot's games. And reduces that grind a ton. Thank you yukes.)Or.You have the best weapons the game will give to you (IE: Level 3 weapons on Hardest in this game), but then the game throws at you enemies (IE: Mission 55) that make the game mechanics completely fall apart.If you've been playing normally up to this point, your average Brother has probably 2-5000 armor points.That means nothing as the game will throw waves of enemies that either can kill you in 1-3 hits.Use those same moves but essentially aimbotting across the entire map (Queen Ant, King Spider).Or all of the above,  the enemies attacks can clip through any and all geometry at random so you can't hide at all from the majority of the attacks and you are stuck with pure luck being able to survive. (You are limited by normal working collision detection. Not Ant and Spider attacks. Sometimes they are blocked by geometry. But rarely. And if you think you can out speed them, good luck. Even using a boost from something like Jet Trooper or a Jet Lifter will still get you instantly wall hack killed easily)Meanwhile the weapons you have available barely put a dent in said enemies. But you can't get anything better because you are locked out by difficulty. (You can't get level 4 weapons unless you play Inferno. Can't unlock Inferno unless you beat Hardest. The one change I don't like that that Sandlot actually got right)Normally this isn't a problem as you can kite around long enough to kill them. But in missions like 55 (Can you guess i'm salty about it?), that's nearly impossible due to the above problems.Well you stop and say, well doesn't Royal Brother have a Shield you can deploy? Why yes, and it's extremely helpful against flying enemies and bees (And their stingers) and energy weapons. But Ants and Spiders? Lol, we are back to the typical Wall hack jankiness of those enemies like in Sandlot's games. Almost like it's some kind of feature, not a bug. That only leaves the awful option of the grind for Armor.  While Yukes made some great choices here like in previous spin offs and the amount you can get per mission can be decent comparatively  it's still an extremely dumb way to pad out the game as you hit extreme difficulty spikes requiring you to farm for more HP.  At best if you are lucky Wing Diver/Pale Rider type Sisters/Brothers will get less than 100 armor points per level.I feel like I could talk about this too long.  (And Yukes actually does a decent job of patching what minor issues there are. Unlike Sandlot. For many, EDF 4/5 are nearly unplayable on PC with numerous technical problems)You don't have to hunt for armor, and Weapon crates. (You just need to win and pick up the Brothers and Sisters in each map. From 2-4) The huge number of playable characters is a huge plus as every one of them feels unique with their own special abilities, pros and cons. Being able to use 4 different characters a ton of fun that adds a lot of variety to how you approach missions.The characters are a blast and the writing/characters is immensely entertaining. The banter between them is hysterical at times and the 4th wall breaking along with references to each previous game are a great touch. It's akin to Red vs Blue level of fun banter occasionally even!  You can listen in English, Chinese, Korean or Japanese.The soundtrack as usual is A+++ with tons of songs from past EDF games included along with another fun feature many may not notice! Certain songs when playing will add a double of the lead melody with an instrument that changes depending on what Brother or Sister you are using at the moment! It's a lot of fun to stop and listen to the instrument choices! They aren't super advanced or realistic samples, sometimes humorously along the lines of a Korg M1, Roland SC-55 or your average SNES game. But it's a great touch that shows how much love went into this game. I wonder how they implemented this in the game considering the quality of the samples. It almost makes me think it's running a MIDI sequencer in the background just for these instruments! :P

_childDocuments_.review: Aggressively mediocre, but my expectations left me feeling disappointed. Given the silly nature of ordinary edf I thought this was going to be an over the top cartoonish remake of the game. Instead this is sort of like diet EDF.There are fewer enemies per map and the weapons are less crazy. Given the voxel graphics I thought they were freeing up resources for greater environmental destruction with even more and crazier enemies, but no, Playing this game feels like driving with the emergency brake on - They went for grounded extremely balanced combat. To me that seems like a really odd decision. The cartoonish nature of the game, gave the devs a chance to go nuts with the weapons and abilities. I expected my characters to be unreasonably powerful with the counter balance to this being an endless hoard of monsters, with the voxel based destruction leaving the map a scarred, utterly destroyed battlefield by the end of every round. Instead they gave me pretty basic weapons from the original edf games but in most cases theyre even weaker than the originals. Each map basically consists of a few waves of couple handfuls of enemies each, and the gamplay loop almost never varies from the standard -rescue the new characters from the ground then kill all remaining enemies. And thats it over and over and over and over. Each new character has a new weapon and new ability but all the abilities are pretty unremarkable, some jump higher than other, some can fly, some can slide, some can double jump, some can do a droidecka roll, some get items, (quick tangent - the pirate's ability uses a claymore as its sign but he actually drops barrels - these barrels do not act as mines they are instead just emplaced bombs that have to be shot by the player to detonate.... the pirates primary weapon is a cannon with a similar splash radius. why would I bother setting up this trap, if I can just shoot them with my primary weapon, its so pointless, claymore mines would have actually been a useful ability) all of them are very bland. It kind of seems like this was made for very young children. The story is supremely stupid, normally EDF is just kind of silly, but in this one the edf crew mount like 5 full blown military operations looking for soup ingredients. IF this was made for children - why? Your IP is rated M most of the time.I dunno.... this whole thing was weird and disappointing. I'm going back to the mainline games. EDF 6 should be coming to the USA soon, so thats pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I love "Earth Defense Force". Unfortunately, "World Brothers" lacks the better qualities of the original: there is little tactical variety, too many classes and lots of mostly passive enemies. This game is more about collecting and mindless shooting than about strategy and situation awareness. It can be fun, I guess, but I personally got bored fast.P.s. The biggest launch day issue, namely the mouse control, is partially fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: People often cite Earth Defense Force as being Dynasty Warriors with guns. I don't think that's true, but for this game in particular it is more true than usual. World Brothers is faster and more streamlined. Where Iron Rain was the most tactical and had the gear with the harshest downsides, World Brothers is the least tactical and everything you can bring is simple, convenient.None of this is a point against it, I find the game pretty fun. It's shorter, faster, and more lighthearted than the mainline, and sometimes it's nice to fly in with a wing diver, drop an air strike, then back out with your fencer covering your retreat with a gatling. When it works, it works well, although the difficult missions seems to force you into playing multiple fencers and kiting for the whole mission, which isn't really my preferred playstyle.It's good that missions are short, because I would often encounter crashes, glitching through the terrain into places you can't get back out from, or enemies crawling off under the map where you can't finish them off.

_childDocuments_.review: One hell of a blast playing this game. A ton of playable characters, with a 4 character/ player system that allows many weapons to be brought alongside many abilities: ranging from support to movement to devestation! And the SP or super absolutely elevate each character. Destructable buildings as well as free vechicles provided for some missions, so no tank spam but they will feel impactful when you get them. Would love to play it more in multiplayer.All in all, its great! It can offer a ton of fun!Go defend the Earth! EDF! EDF!

_childDocuments_.review: Yuke's finally made a good EDF game. Sadly there are issues with the mouse control. But otherwise the port quality is pretty good.The mainline games are still better but this is a pretty good game that is worth experiencing. Its a smaller scale with a larger focus on comedy with occasional 4th wall breaks and the like. There are only 60 levels and you can complete it all in roughly 10 hours. Much shorter experience than EDF 5. Might want to wait for a sale if you only plan on playing it once.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that this is hands down the best spinoff EDF game there is. Not quite better than say 4.1 or 5 but it's up there. It does do some things better like it has actual characters and a better sense of humor. It's self aware and breaks the 4th wall more than once. There are things from many if not all the other EDF games in here even if it's just minor.Gameplay-wise at it's heart it's an EDF game and that's how it plays though a bit simpler, like no energy management for wing divers thanks to weapons not sharing energy with flight. It is the shortest EDF with only 60 missions. And even in those missions the maps are smaller so you feel the repetition more than the main EDF games.I could see some people being bothered the stereotypes that are in the game with the brothers and sisters as some are very blatant and stupid. This is not a sensitive game in that regard.NEGATIVE: The multiplayer is essentially partly broken. You can play together but only way I've gotten it to work is by inviting to an open public lobby. The game won't let you make private lobbys. And I've never seen a public game open to join so I'm not sure the public lobbys even work how they're supposed to. But as long as you're steam friends you can get it to work.Changes from other EDFs:-The entire class system and being able to swap between 4 different ones anytime. Means you can always have a wing diver.-Because of the simplification there aren't large differences in how different classes play for the most part so they can feel samey and unimportant. But there is a lot of variety in ultimate powers at least.-Shooting different parts do different damage amounts. IE: Headshots matter-You don't have to pickup weapons!-You have to "rescue" teammates to unlock new things like weapons. Limited at 3 per mission for most difficulties. -Pulls things in from all other EDFs including enemy types and weapons.-No real underground missions. There is only one underground mission and it's still part of map with a sky.-No civilians-You can damage buildings without destroying them-Small maps-More character driven than talking solely about the war effort-You have to beat EVERY mission on hard then hardest to unlock the higher difficulties.-Shortest EDF at 60 missions-No credit for doing easy or normal when beating hard.-DLC adds difficulty higher than InfernoThat's what comes to mind I'm sure there are more.I've played EDF 2017, 2025, 4.1, 5, and Insect Armageddon. I averaged about an hour play time per 1% completion at around 70% complete with not having unlocked Inferno yet.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: A weird game in the EDF Series to pin down. It's easier than other EDF Titles, which should attract newer players. It's simple art style and colorful aesthetics is inviting to most people. It's content is shorter than most EDF games. It's full of references that EDF fans should understand and like. But due to it being easier, a lot of fans didn't bother with it. But I'm having a blast, so far. It sort of is "baby's first EDF" But it's still fun. Mixing up your brothers and sisters to make interesting play styles, is a lot of fun. The story is good. It runs good, even on my older hardware. Lots of bugs to smash, shoot, blast, slice, and punch. The AI is less aggressive, so far (I've started Hard and it is warming up) than other EDF games. Full price is a bit much compared to other EDF titles, but I think the main detraction is that nobody plays it online. That is were the main draw of the other EDFs are, hoping into rooms with randoms and having fun. So far, it's been worth the sale price I got it for, even single player. Some common gripes form others, I just don't have. The controls are perfectly responsive, for me. Maybe they don't know how to adjust settings? The weapons feel good.  A lot of special moves are meh, but others are great. It plays into the "mixing it up and see what works" aspect. (Use the genocide gun while getting damage buffed , etc) Some weapons don't seem to feel good, but it's mostly situational weapons or a few weird ones. "the sister dressed as a clown has a joke weapon, who would have guessed?" it actually does good damage but slows her down. I also think a lot of them just use what ever the brother or sister start with. Which can work but mixing it up and experimenting is what must be don't to see WHO can use a particular weapon the best. If you love EDF, I think you will like it and enjoy it. If you are unsure of EDF, as a series, this is a great jumping in point. It's simple and easy to jump into. Most of the negatives seem to be about price and content. which i get. But we are kinda lucky that newer games only cost 60 USD. While inflation has everything else up to insane levels.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like the first spinoff EDF that did it right. Whereas Iron Rain and Insect Armageddon both seem like poor attempts at replicating previous EDF titles, World Brothers is its own game that takes place in the EDF universe. It's a very different tone and feel but it's very well polished and fun to play. It's like EDF and Gotcha Force had a child.

_childDocuments_.review: Its basically a parody EDF game made for EDF fans... _childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: It's a different kind of EDF experience than the mainline EDF games and even the other spinoffs. That's not necessarily a bad thing, and while the near constant 4th wall breaking dialogue can get a little annoying (though, sometimes it's funny, but not in the normal EDF way), the game can be fun if you can figure out how to have fun with it. That being said, I can't recommend this game, because the PC version lacks splitscreen. Instead of basing this version in the superior PS4 code, which has splitscreen, they based it on the inferior Switch version, which doesn't. Also the settings are tied to the cloud save, which is IMMENSELY annoying and can actually prevent you from playing the game on other PCs if you go from high end machine to a lower end one like a laptop or handheld.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: It's a stopgap between other EDF games, but it's missing two key things for me. NO SPLITSCREEN for local coop. I play this series together with my gf and it was disappointing that they only support splitscreen on PS4, which they don't specify in their marketing. The other element is a little less tangible, it's missing the EDF soul. It's a fine game and better voice acting than the main series, but it's missing that element that makes it feel like an EDF title rather than just another hoard based shooter. It's less frantic and quirky as the main series. It lacks that little something to make you want to be a glutton for punishment and grind through the levels like 4.1.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on a 4-Player full campaign on Hard.Getting right to it- The game lacks variety in weapon choices that actually feel fun, not dissimilar to Iron Rain's problem but exasperated by the fact that the levels are too small and we're far too mobile- making all the slower weapon choices completely irrelevant. There aren't even that many weapons to begin with, some being direct upgrades to others. Multiple classes just feel completely pointless because their skills just aren't needed in any capacity whatsoever. By the end of the Story Mode on Hard, you will have some characters up to level 3 or 4, which  allows them to equip a third type of weapon category. They can't even do that on Hard because the Level Limit is 2, so they will never have access to using those weapons. There are no other benefits to leveling up characters.Vehicles are THE WORST they have ever been. They cannot even be called in. They have inconsistent aiming (not sluggish like the other low-level EDF vehicles are), unusable mobility, and the levels are so small they feel utterly pointless when characters can blitz across them in seconds.Not to even mention that the mission count is abysmally small compared to what you'd normally expect from EDF. The game is also extremely buggy with multiple times where the mission would start with no UI whatsoever until a player performs an SP move (super), cutscenes would just outright softlock the lobby, and there were several instances of players just losing connection during a loading screen.The contents of the story are absolutely ridiculous and yet the writing can't decide whether it's joking or if it's serious. The entire thing reads like an infomercial for offensive stereotypes around the world. It's so painful to listen to. Usually the story for EDF is one that's genuinely somewhat interesting with layers of B-Movie cheese on top of it, but I spent a lot of time thinking in World Brothers that it's just... downright stupid, insulting even. The voice cast did their best, though, it isn't their fault the writing is awful., but prepare to be disappointed. Start up a fresh run on a harder difficulty of EDF4.1, EDF5, or even Iron Rain if you have to. This spin-off is thoroughly a spin-off in the worst way.---Few other smaller things: The menus are obtuse, you can't see what other people have equipped, Accessories literally only give bonuses of 0.01-0.10 increases to things like movement speed/cooldown, enemy variety is lacking despite being a crossover game, the game advertises World Brothers like there'll be a lot of variety in characters but duplicates are almost exactly the same, and the AI in this game is a straight downgrade from all the other games and are often found wandering around or standing there doing nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the ability to switch between 4 characters, I like how each character has their own gun, special move, and ultimate. Each can also equip an accessory. I like the music. The characters constantly yapping didn't bother me, but then I only played 90 minutes. They did finally fix the mouse controls and it felt fine; guess they didn't learn their lesson from their previous releases.I hate how to level up your characters you have to rescue them again, which given the amount of characters I imagine isn't going to happen very often for the ones you want. I hate how armor earned after the mission only applies to the characters you brought with you. Considering you are constantly getting new characters and swapping them out, and you know you're not going to stick with any of them long term until the end game and hardest difficulties, it feels frustrating and like a waste. Shooting bugs isn't as satisfying as the other EDFs.I could perhaps have forgiven these, but the game loves to stutter at various points including when you use an ultimate. Very annoying. First EDF game I didn't like, refunded. Buy EDF5 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: In an attempt to create an EDF mash-up and present itself in a fun way, World Brothers fails to recognize what makes Sandlot's EDF work and falls flat in every regard. I genuinely cannot find any redeeming qualities. The enemies are passive, the humour is forced, and the classes, while many and varied, are uninteresting and lack usefulness. Technical problems, visuals, and temporary issues aside (including the audio spam), the foundation of World Brothers is flawed. They missed the point, fell short of the mark, and somehow folks still love it. I can only assume some wild paid marketing campaign is running amok and I cannot, for the love of EDF, recommend this atrocity.---I played a mix of normal and hard difficulties and most missions involving species beta turns into an alleyway bughunt because they refuse to engage. Flying enemies circle the skies but wait their turn to attack like a terrible martial arts film. A few missions have a swarm appear and they charge your position only to stand around and wait to die. I feel no panic or pressure. My allies are stuck on walls, running in place, dashing into nothing, and firing into the air. They do very little damage and take very little damage. I don't know why they're there, but I miss other soldiers and civilians trying to hold their own among the chaos. No wave of reinforcements, no day-saving artillery rolling in, and no grim reapers here to save the day.A majority of the classes lack a dodge or any mobility while a good portion lack an impactful ultimate. Grinding in World Brothers will involve searching for a tolerable class and re-finding them to unlock your favourite weapon compatibility. At the end of the day, most folks will likely be using the same few classes. The splendor of classes seems to serve as an oversaturating time-kill to elongate the grind. Folks you rescue come with a weapon, but the weapons don't need upgrading. You'll accumulate plenty of armour as you progress, but those wanting to play on the hardest difficulty will need to farm for that as well. Nothing really new there, I suppose, but it would be nice for the grind to involve something more than "I need a useful character. All of these characters are genuinely bad."EDF has a unique way of passively showing and acknowledging its absurdity, but World Brothers is the type of game to use a red arrow and circle to highlight the joke and hammer away until you laugh. The jokes go on too long and lack subtlety. EDF 4.1 started by acting serious and turning into a laugh. EDF 5 starts a bit ridiculous and slowly becomes serious. World Brothers just feels like a child's game for simple people and it rubs me the wrong way. Iron Rain was like this, too, but was overshadowed by the "realism" and awkwardly contrasted well-enough that it kind of worked.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly a pretty fun spin-off to the overarching series. I wouldn't recommend it to someone who's totally uninitiated to EDF in general, but if you've got a few of the titles under your belt already then this is a decently entertaining, lighthearted love letter referencing all of the entries and then some. Still retains the addictive and shooty horde-based genocidal gameplay EDF's renowned for albeit in voxel form, but I'm not a vain grafixwhore so I don't mind. Surprisingly, the quick-swap character system and simplified customization makes the game a ton more bearable in solo mode compared to the other games, so it's great for a fast romp if you're looking to kill time.

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️Acceptable graphics options if somewhat anemic✔️Properly uncapped framerate✔️Runs well even in combat❌No built-in FOV Adjustments❌The graphical options are a good step up from the horror show that was Iron Rain (which had an 83.33% default resolution scale and was locked to 60 fps and required a community patch to fix). Those issues  present here. However, the mouse aim in this game is among the worst I've ever experienced.It is simply mapping the mouse to joystick inputs and using joystick style acceleration. It feels terrible and I pretty much have to say the game is not playable with a mouse in this state.One of the key reasons PC gamers like to play shooters on PC is because we get to use a mouse. This has been a solved problem since Quake. Until this is fixed I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Many EDF fans took one look at Earth Defense Force: World Brothers' voxel-style graphics and dismissed this game as a Minecraft-esque, sub-par, shameless cash grab. It is unfortunate that so many fell into the folly of "judging a book by it's cover" because Earth Defense Force: World Brothers is not only a great EDF game in its own right, but also an unabashed love letter to the EDF franchise as a whole. After the polarizing release of EDF: Iron Rain, many fans openly wondered if YUKE'S really had any idea what makes EDF games so special. World Brothers seems to be their response, and the answer is yes, they do.

_childDocuments_.review: A colorful take on the classic EDF formula. It's a bit easier than the previous entries - I managed to beat it on hard on my first playthrough and died about 3 times total. But every EDF soldier knows the fun begins at hardest and inferno difficulties!You can bring up to 4 characters to each mission and all of them will level up after completing it (at different rates, roughly by class), so no more collecting armor boxes. Each character has unique abilities and you can switch on the fly during the mission. Using a character with a sky leap ability, then switching to a character with flight while in the air to rain hell on your enemies with the air strike ability felt awesome.The only downsides are the price point and the awful humor #omgsofunny! I get it, it's aimed at younger players, but the constant references to previous entries and some other jokes makes it feel like EDF WB has an identity crisis. I muted the voice lines for subsequent playthroughs and I didn't miss a thing. Overall recommended at a sale, while I'd love to see the formula with different characters/abilities in a main EDF entry.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not gonna lie, I only played the first 4 missions, but after the disappointment I felt from it I went to Youtube to watch Lets Plays so I would not pass the 2 hour mark as I already wanted a refund but was holding out hope that it would get better.Spoilers: It only gets more annoying. The controls are rough and awkward, and the art-style taqkes getting used to, but the worst part is the one-liners. EDF 4.1 and 5 had a radiant chatter from the NPCs that could get annoying but I found it comical. EDF: WB on the other hand takes that all away and replaces the grunts soldiers used to make when they got hurt or rolled with one liners that are not just words but can be full sentences that yhou will just be spammed with. Worse yet they cap how much you can lower voiced dialogue so it is always there and you can't mute it without muting the whole game. _childDocuments_.review: It's fun, the switch to casual block graphics really let them do a lot of experimentation here that wouldn't be feasible in mainstream EDF. Environments are varied, it's silly, there are lots of character classes. I could best describe this as an EDF Musou game - it plays just like the main EDF games except you're swapping between four characters to charge up and unleash their Musou attacks. It even has that Warriors Orochi style universe-bending ruleset where characters, classes, enemies, etc. from all of the games in the series make an appearance.The only downside is that there are only 60 missions and they tend to be short compared to normal EDF missions - but they've cut out most of the filler and every mission is fun, straight to the point, and action packed.Your progress is shared between Online/Offline. I play with Mouse/Keyboard and it feels great (for example, there's no mouse acceleration) - they either already fixed it or adjusting the mouse sensitivity in the in-game options menu was all that was needed.

_childDocuments_.review: "Love letter" describes this one pretty well. A good game that ties together parts of other EDF titles in a cute little package, and makes its own way on top of that.Where Iron Rain is still clearly an EDF game but failed to keep the core of EDF (vast swarms of enemies that you blow up with satisfying guns), World Brothers understood the mission statement far better. When you play, it becomes very clear that the devs looked back and learned (or just knew) how the various enemies and weapons of the EDF titles worked to port them in properly. The descriptions and mission dialogue make this pretty obvious even if the gameplay doesn't. When the Assault Beetle mentions how it's "no longer a god-awful liability to your efforts" (paraphrasing) it's actually true, and does the job it was intended to do but failed in before.The gameplay is pretty solid overall, really. The biggest flaw is definitely the vehicles, which you can't call in and aren't always present. Even when they're present, they're usually a bit weak and awkward to use, especially when trying to aim. It could also be said that the earlier missions are too easy, especially in multiplayer, and giving the player access to higher difficulties right off the bat instead of unlocking them would solve that. The characters aren't all unique, that's for damn sure - I don't think there's even one skill that doesn't have a similar copy elsewhere - but that's not just a time-saver for the devs, it makes getting the "perfect loadout" a little more possible. A bunch of characters can lay mines as their "at will" power, but each one has a different weapon progression and their special moves are all different. There are enough for you to get the chance to have the toolkit you want. Sure, Iron Rain has the more flexible loadouts, but aside from that EDF generally doesn't let you have this kind of freedom, especially since you carry four characters into battle per player.The guns are fairly similar. Again like Iron Rain, the selection is less all-over-the-damn-place than mainline EDF, but here I can safely say every gun is quite usable, and they each do something a little different. Do we have the Fencer's Blood Storm missile launcher? Not really, only some vaguely similar solutions. Air Raider's classic Bulge Laser or Caesar Wire? No. However, the weapons here are just fine.Also, despite how it looks, this game is... actually the EDF with the most complex characters and things you could actually call story arcs for said characters. Most of it is still cutesy and silly, that's for damn sure; don't expect a steady, dark, and cohesive story. No, the characters are a separate thing from the setting and story, that's for sure.When the game sends you right from the Pyramids to the Eiffel Tower to a farm in Kansas without any rhyme or reason, you just have to roll with it. They don't even bother to try and explain how the hell this cube world works, and time-traveling ninjas and grown men in koala suits casually join the EDF wielding their own miniguns and laser katanas. It's silly and stupid, and the game knows that. It tries to make sure you know it knows, too.However, within that framework, they do pretty well for themselves.A character later into the game (callsign Calm Leader) insists he can't go see his son until he's succeeded in his mission, and denies anyone who suggests he should just do it while he has the chance. He, in turn, hypocritically tells someone else to go visit their family despite their present obligations, and there is a *reason* for that, which you can catch if you pay attention. There are actually a lot of subtle character interactions in here similar to this, stories and traits buried under silly cube graphics and goofy jokes. Plus, when they set out their goofy concepts - like the ancient Egyptian worshiping the cat-girl-maid - they stick with it and don't contradict.I get the distinct feeling that someone new to EDF might not understand what the heck else is going on in this one, though. Descriptions, missions, enemies, and so on will pretty much rely on your knowing what you're looking at from previous games; jokes and story beats won't land unless you've played the appropriate game (when Storm 1 shows up and saves the day, you don't get any explanation on who or how - they're the protagonist in previous games), and some classes have mobility options that you won't know to look for unless you remember them from back when, like the Jet Lifter's sprint and the Air Raider's roll.I also want to make a mention of how one of the "most helpful" negative reviews states that "there is no point to leveling up characters, because on Hard their skill above 2 doesn't apply." This is outright false; the level limitation isn't on characters. Character level lets you equip different weapon types and still works as normal be it on Hard or Easy. It's odd that they said otherwise. Even if it were the case, armor still increases the more you use a character and, just like in previous EDF titles, armor is pretty much crucial in surviving difficult missions.

_childDocuments_.review: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS (in short EDF:WB) Is based on like every EDF game and basicly created for actual fans of the EDF-Series.I duno if i should count it as "Main title" or actual "Spin-off"  since, unlike spin-offs like Iron Rain, It actually makes a lot more fun to play and is pretty similar to the original series - even with a fun story, at least "somewhat".EDF is already a "known" series -  - for shooting stuff which is at least 4 times bigger than you. Ants, Spiders, Robots, "aliens" and like. This stuff does, of course, return in EDF:WB as well and  - Still, thats what this game is actually build for: Yes, EDF:WB has a "own story" but all stuff -  - are all based "somewhat" of already older EDF titles, As sample, the very first character you "get" to play is the normal Ranger from EDF 5 with a base rifle.With that said there comes some problems with the changes it also has from the main series.Normaly, EDF players are used to, if they are not IRON RAIN players, collect boxes after each kill which the enemies drop to get XY items. This is actually Yes, EDF:WB  and "tried" to make everything a bit easier, gameplay wise, but made it feel a biiiiiiit more..."grindy".To begin with, as i said,  AND Hitpoints/armor will now automaticly go up after each mission.So yes, it makes the "farm" for armor at least easier but the actual grind for new weapons or better characters  - But again, if you think about it, its more now of a "guaranteed" system behind it than luck coz sometimes, you couldnt even find ONE weapon back in other EDF games - also you basicly had to run around like an idiot to find and get ALL the boxes -  So i duno how to say but i would say the system behind is kinda a 50% or "win/lose" situation - In EDF:WB, you play with a Team of 1-4 people and yes, even in soloplayer AND yes, EVEN in Multiplayer which basicly means you can play a game in which you play with 4 players Coz of this odd design choice, it feels like the actual "teamplay" suffers a bit since why should you go "air diver" and call an ambulance car  RARELY you see people which create different kind of teams since the system change that only the characters you actively play get the Hitpoint/armor boost actually get said boost makes it feel like you have to choose which characters you wanna play really fast like nearly from the beginning of the game or the character "might" be to weak, hitpoint/armor wise, in the later missions.I mean i made myself 2 different teams which also use 2 characters which i didnt change so that 2 of the characters will basicly always get stronger no matter which of my 2 teams i use. As i said, the grind/farm system is a bit of a oddball...Next to the changes i said and the somewhat still fitting voxel style, i still do recommend it. Yes, its a bit grindy, yes its kinda more of the same but hey, its EDF, its pur fun and in multiplayer its again just great to blast away with your team(s) and enjoy exploding stuff around you. The areas are big enough, the enemies are nice to look it, the weapons are typical EDF-crazyness and the story is so odd and fun that i wanna ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ eat meso-soup now.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore 99.9% of the negative reviews. most people are salty about the price of the game but i will tell you, If you have liked any of the past EDF games this game promises more of that good old B-rate comedy and all the Insect blasting action we know and love. People are upset that each character only get to carry 1 weapon BUT, you get to control not 1 but 4 characters each mission YES thats 4 weapons rather than the 2 all the other games limited us to. AND you can pick and choose which classes you want to bring. Want to use a wing diver to speed into the action and then switch over to a ranger or fencer to do some serious damage and then switch back to wing diver to speed off again? Then THIS game is for you! I hear you can also cross class your weapons later in the game but i have not progressed that far yet. Sure the weapon drops dont exist per se BUT you do gather 3 new characters each mission and they come with a new weapon or a copy of one of your old weapons if you get a copy you can merge them to upgrade the old one so all the same systems from EDF 5 still exist but have just been implemented a little bit differently! this game is 5/5 stars for me and it should be for you as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game, but with a big asterisk next to it regarding the decision to make the game voxel based. Firstly, on gameplay, they did a few things different from other EDF games which I can respect and still enjoy despite the differences, only allowing one weapon per character, using teams of four ala a warriors game and giving some playable characters personalities. I like it, I appreciate it for being a new take on a standing series.On Story, I definitely enjoy the multiverse crossover aspect of the game between the different "branches" of the EDF series, the main numbered series, Insect Armageddon, and Iron Rain.And finally, on the graphics, I don't mind the Voxels, I actually really like the how the buildings look in this game, when getting chucks blown out of them. But do I think this game *needs* to be in Voxels? I'm not sure. But then, I'm not really sure what alternative would have been better either. So all in all, I enjoy  the game, but I'm still torn on the graphics. And to people who do like the graphics, I can respect their decision.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and pays homage to the EDF series in a very good way. It's one of the most fun EDF games for sure.Originally I could not recommend this game because of region lock but it has since been removed.Although EDF 5 remains my favourite EDF game, World Brothers easily earned a high place near the top of my list.In this game you play a “simplified” version of the different characters that have appeared through the series, in addition to new characters with a theme based on their country of origin. While you can’t change the abilities a character has, which include what used to be special weapons like spritefall, you still run around with 4 of them and can use “cross-class” weapons. This enables you to make teams where each character can focus on a specific type of combat.The game pulls off the “dumb ridiculous fun” that characterizes EDF games very well while using a diferent formula when it comes to the player’s selection of weapons and skills.I’m definitely going to be playing World Brothers in conjunction with EDF 5 while we wait for EDF6.

_childDocuments_.review: EDF World Brothers is a hectic third person shooter with a focus on hot swapping characters and positioning. Setting it apart from the other entries is a lack of depth and difficulty all while seemingly being more obtuse to new players. The game is certainly cute, but it feels torn between trying to please EDF veterans, newcomers, and some kids too. It’s still EDF, but there are a lot of things that just hold it back, and to that end, it’s hard to recommend.EDF is a third person shooter where you fight enemies many times your size. What this means is that aim isn’t a big deal, and this being the EDF, neither is damage. The EDF asks the all important question of “How well does a giant bug hold up against a 120mm howitzer?”. “Not very well”. Most enemies drop like flies when you shoot them, having an advantage in numbers and stopping power. If a spider gets you with all its web, you’re probably dead. And so the real focus is in staying on the move to avoid being surrounded, and using buildings to block the worst of enemy attacks.Historically, there are four character classes: Wing Diver, Ranger, Fencer, and Air Raider. Wing divers fly across the map with a jetpack, often complementing their high movement with powerful close range weapons. Rangers are standard infantry with a combat roll and reliable weapons. Fencers trade mobility and reliability for durability and power. Lastly, air raiders can’t really defend themselves, but can wipe the battlefield with artillery and airstrikes if they’re positioned well. Since fencers and air raiders can have trouble on their own, they typically require support to reach their full potential. To this end, each class plays very differently because of the way they move and the reliability of their equipment.If you ask me, EDF world brothers missed the mark. The player can swap between four characters at any point in time, with each character carrying one gun and having one ability. Abilities include movement like the fencer’s dash, attacks like the air raider’s fire support, and several others. What this means is that you’ve effectively got air raiders with jet packs and fencers who fly for longer. Every character has great movement since they can be swapped once a second. Further, each character has their own weapon with arbitrary restrictions, meaning that you can have the ranger’s reliable shotgun, a fencer’s minigun, and a wing driver's guided weapon all without compromising on movement.In my eyes, the game sabotages any need for carefully considered loadouts by allowing the player to just have everything. With a squad of four characters, movement’s almost never an issue. That said, I took a squad of four air raiders and nothing could stop me. That’s balance. Anyhow, it’s not terrible, but it doesn’t live up to what EDF can be.Progression in this game is pretty bad. In effect, you collect three random characters per mission, with duplicates increasing that character’s “skill”. Characters with higher levels of skill can equip more types of weapons. For instance, the rangers with an assault rifle, but can later equip any weapon with enough duplicate finds. While that’s fine on paper, there are a whopping 62 characters, each with three variants, resulting in 186 total. It is cluttered at best and a grindy mess the rest of the time. To top that off,  gets armor independently, with only the four characters brought into a mission gaining armor.There are 60 missions meaning this game’s just over half the length of the mainline EDF games and  longer than Iron Rain. The first missions are standard with enemies running about, later introducing tunnel entrances and drop ships. That said, the game really leans on its giants for many of the missions. For those unfamiliar, it’s basically just shoot the big thing until it dies or leaves. It’s a different kind of challenge, but it's always short, and it’s troubling that they make upwards of 15% of them.Further setting the game apart from entries like EDF 4.1 and 5 is a lack of map variety. There are probably more maps in this game than the others, but where this game has many maps, most are tiny in comparison. EDF 4.1 could completely recontextualize a map by shifting the borders slightly and starting the player eight blocks down the road. The maps of World Brothers are used in their entirety each mission due to their small size, making reuse glaringly obvious. Previous games have also employed squads of friendly armor and soldiers to fine tune the intensity of the missions and shift their focus. The friendlies in EDF World Brothers cannot be injured, and would be nigh invisible if not for the spoken dialogue during the missions.To top it all off, mission descriptions are a thing of the past, leaving players with a single image for the missions. What this means is that the player cannot account for the missions that are actually unique, such as the cave mission. All in all, the missions are just lacking.EDF World Brothers feels like it’s split between trying to appeal to some group of kids out there while also appealing to the usual EDF crowd, and it’s to the detriment of both groups.This game is easy. My friend and I just waltzed through all the levels on hard, and nothing could stop us. The enemies can’t hold ground, and have a rough time pinning the player down. Heck, the bugs barely attack. Past that, the player is just handed the raw damage needed to plow through everything, and the mobility to employ it no matter how unwieldy. While we never lost a mission, there were two or three of the missions that gave us trouble, usually due to the enemies killing us in one or two hits. It’s not bad, but part of the joy I took in playing the previous games was in the struggle to find the right tools and strategies to beat new levels. When compared to levels like “Brute Force”, this game has no challenge, and is lacking in depth.That said, it's loyal to EDF. Fencer has the janky dash slide and rangers can only roll to the side. Most skills carry over just fine, and you’ll probably get most of the one liners.It’s EDF, and as such, it’s pretty hard if you’re not familiar with the series. This one’s kinder than the other entries, but it doesn’t teach you anything about map positioning or how to counter different enemies until it’s too late. It’s not until later in the game that the difficulty starts to increase, and without the aforementioned skills, you just die. You’re going to have trouble learning when the map’s covered in mechs. Past that, they don’t do a great job teaching the player which weapons counter different enemies. While a veteran might reach for a rapier or autocannon to handle a hector, new players might be tricked into using a sniper due to the way equipment is limited.Past some more obtuse gameplay, the game is littered with references you probably won’t get. If you like it though, the other games are vaguely similar, and a fair bit better.I’m running out of characters so I have to be brief. The voice acting is really good, and so is some of the dialogue. The writing itself has some painful educational stuff shoehorned in, and the degree that it leans into stereotypes bothers me. What cripples it is the lack of reinforcement in gameplay. If they say it’s hopeless, you just have to take their word for it.For those familiar with the series, I am pleased to report that it is still EDF, albeit markedly less so than the other entries. Whether or not it’s better than Iron Rain is a topic for some debate. It’s short and grindy, and manages to cut out the decision making that makes EDF special. For newcomers, might I recommend EDF 4.1 or EDF 5? Let this be the entry you reach for last.

_childDocuments_.review: EDF World Bros is a really fun more casual take on EDF. However do make sure you have a gamepad to play with, the mouse support is really bad.EDIT: The mouse support has been fixed with an update!!The gameplay is quite different from mainline entries thanks to the character system where you get to pick 4 brothers/sisters each with their own abilities and weapons and you switch between them on the fly. The system works very well in practice and has a fair amount of depth when you build your team. The graphics are voxel-like, it looks fine, not as nice as the mainline entries. The positive thing is that enemies and items are easy to see and the game runs smooth as butter on my old graphics card.The sound and music are great, no complaints at all. Lots of real bangers in the soundtrack, both old and new songs.Writing is more like a silly saturday morning cartoon full of 4th wall breaks and just wacky and silly stuff happening. A little bit cringe at times but overall entertaining. Not really comparable at all to the great writing in EDF5 for example. The missions are very creative with the goals though, which is quite fun.The PC port overall is good,  (FIXED). The menus are also much easier to navigate with a gamepad. Other than that the game runs great and I have not encountered any bugs in my first 6 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game with fun characters and a silly story, tons of content and progression/unlocks to be had.However thanks to severe region locking, chances are you won't be able to play online with random people much.Yup, game's online has tons of people playing, but is dead.This game is a great buy if you like playing Single Player EDF, or you have a group.This game is a complete waste of money if you like playing with random people online, depending on your region.Chose to not recommend for my general opinion, as I feel this has a huge chance of making people feel like they were cheated when they buy it for the online co-op with random people.However if that isn't a problem for you, I recommend it. This game is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: EDF World Brothers is a third-person co-op or singleplayer shooter title where you control a full squad of 4 Brothers/Sisters from different EDF branches. Seems like people have the wrong idea of what the game is, and are spreading outright lies about it, so I'll explain briefly what it is.Its a spin-off game mixing enemies from every single EDF game in the series, as well as EDF classes, including a big amount of newcomers made for this title. Made by Yuke, the ones who did Iron Rain, I was hesitant at first, but this game just screams "EDF!" the more you play it. The story is silly, but its as it needs to be. Its a spin-off crossover game in vein of G Gundam, expect silly designs for the heroes as they're based on nationalities and stereotypes from all around the world. It's also very self aware that it is a videogame, so keep that in mind.Each character, unlike the mainline games, can only carry 1 gun, and has a fixed active skill and a SP Skill. However, you can change that gun to any other one of the category you have unlocked. Example: You can equip a Blasthole Spear + Shield on a Wing Diver/Pale Diver who has the Close Range weapon unlocked. You have complete freedom on what weapon to bring, so long as your character knows how to use it. This system is great, straight outta Iron Rain, if it wasn't for the only downside it has, if it can be called as such. Each Brother will only have 1 weapon category unlocked, rescuing said Brother multiple times will increase their proficiency, meaning they'll be allowed to use different weapon types. Theres around 100 characters, with 3 variants for each, except DLC. Each time you play a map they're randomized, getting dupes is a bit hard sometimes.To unlock guns, you just need to rescue the characters, and the gun will be unlocked for everyone to use. They also added an accesory slot, similar to EDF5. You can equip different accesories that will upgrade the performance of the character you give them to.You can make a big variety or teams, or stick to making teams of the same game, or whatever you wish. You'll have different teams loadout slots, that will let you switch between different ones easily before a mission starts.One gripe I had was the overall lenght and difficulty on my first playthrough, however. It was never hard on normal, played the whole thing on co-op with a friend. And on EDF5 and 4, they're pretty hard games as the levels come by. But this one was a breeze on normal, even on singleplayer. I'd say start with Hard and turn it down if things get too heated.On technical issues, I've only found the issue of the mouse sensitivity not being good at all. Turned it up to 100 and works just fine though.  The game runs great, looks great and plays great as you'd expect from EDF.People say the graphics suck but, I fail to see that anywhere. They couldn't have done this with any of the games artstyle as they're quite different from eachother, and the silly nationality based characters would not look silly and fun either. Its a japanese game, made with a loooot of love for fans of the series.If you like it, go grab it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a damn good, EDF time. It's different in some ways, and it may be a better solo game than a multiplayer one. As a solo game, I'm having an absolute blast with it. It has plenty of fun weapons and special abilities, and tweaking your team is an even bigger part of it than in the main EDF games.

_childDocuments_.review: Earth Defense Force World Brothers is a game built for EDF fans. Developer Yukes pulls from every era of the series, with the game featuring characters, weapons and locations from the PS2 originals, the handheld re-releases and even the various spin offs. As a fan of the oft-derided Insect Armageddon it was cool to see that game represented here. Players new to the series won't get as much out of the fanservice elements, but the core gameplay is still enjoyable enough whether this is you first EDF game or not. From the games available on Steam, I would probably recommend one of the Sandlot titles (Earth Defense Force 4.1 or 5) over this, but World Brothers is still enjoyable in its own right. Though I did appreciate the brief pace of World Brothers compared to the more recent titles. In my review of EDF5 I mentioned that the game started to drag due to the high mission count, but World Brothers clocks in at around sixty levels, putting it around the same length as EDF3 Portable (my personal favourite in the series). As for the PC port itself, this is one of the better EDF titles in that regard. World Brothers uses UE4, and while the graphic options aren't as granular as one would like there are more options here than in the Sandlot titles, and the general performance itself is good. There's also subtitles for most dialogue now as opposed to EDF5 which lacked any form of subtitling. Overall, World Brothers isn't the best in the series, but a good entry nonetheless. I hope some of the improvements from this release, such as subtitling, can make their way over for EDF6; but while we wait for that game to release, World Brothers isn't a bad way to kill time.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: A flawed, but overall very well designed alternate take on the EDF formula. Progression is quite different to main games, meaning you get new playstyles and weaponry much faster (but there is still plenty to grind out if you're one of the people that like the absurd grind of the main series for some reason). Rather than having a class with a bunch of unique weaponry and loadouts, you create a squad of 4 characters with 1 weapon and 2 unique abilities each, making the game a bit faster paced and more aggressive overall than the mainline games. On paper this would make it easier, but the smaller maps and still pretty dense enemy counts means the game gets quite a bit more difficult than EDF 5 does. World Brothers uses a wide variety of enemies from each EDF title (including spinoffs) making what is possibly the most varied and interesting roster of enemies in the entire franchise which is arguably this game's biggest strength. Absolutely worth playing if you like EDF, especially if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: While it has crashed and bugged out a few times, and I have not yet tested the multiplayer, after getting a feel for it I'm honestly disappointed I did not play this sooner - it is a very genuine loveletter to seventeen years of EDF. I've just matched up a Pale Wing and an Air Raider, and a unique using a prowl-rider moveset takes my third slot. Fill in the last with a Fencer or the unbelievable Dragon Sister, I'm ready to facetank some hectors.Grab this on sale. Right now! Humble Bundle, EDF UNITED!

_childDocuments_.review: Is it EDF 5?  No.  But it's something to tide you over until EDF 6 arrives, especially if it's on sale.  And if you crave more detail, boy howdy are you in luck.The simplest description comes from my wife: "It's like somebody crossed EDF with G Gundam".  That didn't mean a whole lot to me but other people found it funny, so I laughed too just to fit in.But down to the tangibles:  The world and all monsters are all made from voxels.  Think "Cube World", and if that doesn't mean much, it's clumsily like 2d retro graphics, but in 3D.  I'm sort of flailing to describe "voxels" without an essay or a slideshow with annotations.  But if you're finding yourself bored now, there's coop.  Go play it with a few friends.The music is cheerful, the characters are largely cheerful, the weapons are as absurd as ever, but instead of playing the same character and collecting a big fistful of different weapons, you wind up collecting different characters instead, and you run four at a time and can switch between them as you see fit.Themeatically, the game's much more light-hearted.  There's some effing of the fourth wall which I'm not a fan of, and there's a lot of morality plays which I'm also not a fan of, being that I'm a grown-ass adult and I understand the virtues of honesty, friendliness, courage and compassion, but I wanted some fresh EDF experiences and this will do for now.Gameplay-wise, if you've played EDF then nothing will surprise you greatly, except there's no armour/weapon crates.  New weapons come as a function of "recruiting" new characters.  Three of them will be laying around on each map, so go rescue them.  If it's a duplicate of a character you already have, they level up and can equip a wider variety of weapons.  Likewise, the four characters you take along with you will gain a small boost in hitpoints.  (So far, 0.2 to 0.5% of their maximum, a tiny trickle.)You'll control one character, the AI will control the other three, and they'll shoot occasionally at things and, thankfully, not blow themselves up if they drop a 20m burst-radius grenade at their own feet.  And you can't really ask for more than that.  They won't do special moves or anywhere near the level of damage you will, though, but you can switch characters dynamically.  Give 'em each different weapons, pick the right character for the moment.And those characters range from dreadfully earnest (all the old EDFs have characters present), the self-awarely weird (such as "Panda Brother" who will tell you he's just a guy in a suit) to the just vaguely uncomfortably weird, which involves characters embodying national stereotypes.  The American does wear a cowboy hat, packs a six-shooter and is obsessed with cattle.  Because of course he is.I presume there's a Canadian, since we have a Dane and a character from Holland, but I haven't found 'em yet.  I'm getting ready to cringe.Anyway, while the maps are notably smaller, it's not like most EDF rounds used up all that terrain anyway, so this winds up being a more efficient use of space.  That makes for less searching for your collectible dudes, and it makes each experience much more compact.  And I'm fine with that.In fact, if I had to summarize all this ramble into one sentence, then it's this: "EDF World Brothers:  I'm fine with that."
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: It's EDF alright, just with the silliness cranked to 11.Overall it's standard EDF gameplay, but in a voxel world, and instead of having 4 classes, you gather teammates that you save during missions.  Each teammates come with variants Alpha, Beta, Theta, etc and have different stats (more Armor, slower/faster, etc) Teammates also act as "weapon drops", get a duplicate and it will level up the teammate which will allow them to equip a more varied selection of weapons (usually each teammates can only equip 1 class of weapon)Along with a weapon, sometimes they'll come with an accessory which gives various effects (positive or negative), like Boosting your armor, but making you much slower, etcIn single player you select a team of 4 teammate that you can switch from on the fly, even if you're midflight with an Wing Diver, you can switch to a Ranger, etc. Let's you prepare for different scenarios and also serves as some kind of "lives stock" as if one dies, you can switch to another, and revive them.Overall you can think of this as a "Best of" of EDF, as it includes characters and monsters from almost every EDF games made (Except I believe Insect Armageddon).I'm up to stage 26 now, and I think the mission progression is showing 8% completion, so there's a lot of content.Unfortunately I can't say anything about online yet, as I only played the Single Player campaign so far, but loving it.Lastly, the game seems to run very well on lower end computer, as mine is getting pretty old, and I'm getting a pretty stable 60FPS in 1080p with all setting on high (which are the default) on my old i5-4670 + GTX960

_childDocuments_.review: I actually got upset with this title after first two missions and uninstalled.  Back to proper EDF games.  Get ready for refund.However, next day I ended up re-installing and playing even more.  It is not EDF, and definitely not the best EDF ever.  Come on!!!  However, it is a great game with a lot of similar game mechanics and some great new ways to approach this type of game play.After giving myself a second chance at this game, I found myself pretty much addicted to it.  I will admit that at first the design threw me into confusion and my ingrained expectations of an EDF like game.  Suspending that need for EDF 6, I found myself really enjoying this game as it is.  A parody of EDF in a manner of presentation and a very good shooter with humongous amounts of variety.  If you are thorough like myself, you will try every character and every special ability they have.  I found myself switching characters constantly to pick up yellow boxes to get everyone up to 100% because they all had to have their moment to shine.The game play is the first time I have enjoyed character switches.  I have never enjoyed this kind of thing.  For this game, it is very well done.  I have to bow down to the "TEAM", it is awesome.  You can do it alone, but why?Every new character rescued I play.  I have to try them all out, making a true motivator to replay.  So no, this is not EDF that I still play, from 3, 4.1, to 5 (and please 6 don't be too much longer), but it is EDF flavor served up in humongous servings, both gratifying and a thrill to experience.  No, not the best EDF ever, give me a break.  But an outstanding implementation of a fun stand alone game with its own merits and dripping in EDF homage.Did I mention refund?  What was I thinking!!!  Don't be too quick, keep playing, try all the characters.  You'll be glad you did.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a first impressions review since I haven't had time to play a huge amount of the game yet but so far I think this game is pretty solid and I appreciate some of the new concepts this game introduces into the EDF formula.Before each mission you can now select a team of up to 4 squadmates that you can swap between at any time during the mission and instead of just collecting new weapons and armor like in the other games, you instead find and rescue new characters you can take into battle, and armor is earned based on performance instead of collecting it.Each character has their own standard and ultimate abilities and also different stats and such so there is some strategy involved for picking the right squadmates for the mission and using the right ones at the right times. I think this new system is great for single player but could be a bit too powerful for multiplayer since everyone will have 4 squadmates each and cooperation becomes less important. Other than that the gameplay is standard EDF stuff and it plays pretty well.Online play is a little laggy for me but does work at least, although I'm not a fan of how the game pauses every time anyone uses their ultimate ability.Enjoying the game overall so far, and enjoy some of the new ideas it has.

_childDocuments_.review: World brothers is a more cartoonish take on EDF as well as a giant fan service piece for long-time EDF fans. Overall, it does it quite well. I should warn people to avoid this game for a few days if you want to play on mouse and keyboard, the mouse controls are broken and the devs acknowledge it. It feels like you're mouse is emulating a joystick.The good:- There's a large amount of characters each with their own abilities allowing for a lot of variety in playstyle. They even allow for any character to use any weapon class if you upgrade their skill enough so you can eventually roll with any set up. For a normal EDF game I wouldn't be too keen on this, but for a game that offers as many options as this without pre-defined classes I'm more than fine.- The attention to detail in places is very much appreciated, especially when they are going for fan service like this. Things like air raiders airstrikes being the only normal ability that uses an ability call out, EDF4 fencer getting dash cancels, the Iron Rain Trooper's PA overdrive ult increasing the speed of the music, making jokes about how the ranger was never taught to roll forwards, etc. - Humor is there and I've enjoyed it... mostly. There's some decent jokes and almost every character is a massive stereotype from the tequilla and nap loving mexican to the german officer who sounds way too evil and talks too much about efficiency. Overall it's more corny jokes over cheesy but serious acting.- Enemy variety is solid. They take enemies from every EDF game so there's a lot to choose from.The bad:- As I mentioned the mouse controls are awful for aiming but I also hope their fix also addresses the abysmal UI controls as well. Only a few things are controlled with mouse and it's a bit messy.- While there is a ton of extra variety, it has a few issues that comes with it. First, every characters HP has to be leveled separately with use. This won't be too bad for a single playthrough on normal, but if you intend to stick with the game a bit longer as EDF games do offer a lot more past the base difficulty, then finding a new character or having a bunch of characters that have 800-1600 HP while your main team has over 6k is a kick in the teeth. Second, as a single team unit you have too many options for this game to challenge you anywhere near as much as normal EDF games do. You have 4 separate health bars as well as healers, you can cover any range and situation with all the weapons you have available, and escape abilities/nukes are pretty plentiful so being a little more tactical like in main-line EDF games isn't as much of a thing. I accidentally loaded a mission on hard and it really wasn't that much worse aside from taking more damage, which didn't matter too much given I just swapped characters until I found a med pack.- There's less sheer amount of enemies at once, it does get kind of close in places, but most importantly enemies just aren't very aggressive it feels. Normally in EDF when you trigger a cloud of bees you can expect heavy showers within seconds as they all get together to set the world record for "largest concentration of iron inside of a single person". But no, in this game you can trigger a horde and still have to chase a few down because they are just hopping around or are agrod onto your invincible party member whos kind of far away. I remember playing the mission where you take out a hive. I just shot the hive from very far away and not a single enemy came to me. Normally the second a hive is hit EVERYTHING knows where you are.So in the end I'd say it's still a solid EDF-game, pretty good for a spin off considering the history of this series, but it's definitely not an EDF game for people who want the standard EDF experience. While I'm waiting for them to fix the mouse issues, by the time I stopped I'll admit this game was wearing on me a little. I was having a lot of fun, but when compared to the main series, it's a lot more brain dead. Still, a good time overall.

_childDocuments_.review: The game so far has been a blast, managing to change up the formula without completely abandoning what makes the franchise enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: Great tribute to the franchise. Has references and cameos from all of the entire series from Monster Attack to Iron Rain. Plays slightly different to your traditional EDF with 4 party members all with unique weapons and abilities, but it's fun to switch out from a Wingdiver midair to a sword wielding Spartan and demolish swarms of Wasps. Genuinely far better than Iron Rain was, I enjoyed Iron Rain but it had plenty of issues, Yukes shows they know how to handle EDF with changes and I am glad to see that. Combat is smooth and handles as decently as you'd expect from EDF shooting, Dialogue and characters are more involved and funny, they even poke jabs at how OTT Insect Armageddon is and how people thought IR was a sequel. Overall a fun ass entry in the franchise and worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the EDF series. That being said, I had completely missed this title. The Humble Bundle recently had these games in a set and I picked it up. _childDocuments_.review: Mother Earth is once again being invaded by mysterious alien forces and the EDF has deployed once more to stop them. Only this time, the invading alien force is the biggest it has been, being comprised of a combination of all previous aliens the EDF have fought against up to now. The aliens have torn Earth asunder with such a brutal opening strike and the EDF has dwindled greatly in number, so now it's up to YOU, the newly appointed commander of the (remains of the) EDF, to gather up who has survived the catastrophe and valiantly drive back those alien bastards and save Mother Earth.... Oh yeah and everything's in voxel graphics.Now, since it's an EDF game you should definitely expect to experience mindless horde-shooting, mass destruction, terribly ridiculous writing, and intensive yelling and singing. But also keep in mind this is a spin-off, so expect deviation from the usual EDF formula. The horde shooting is there... or slashing or bashing or whatever depending on what weapons you choose to wield against the aliens.  As far as mass destruction goes, there aren't any weapons that really do a good job leveling whole city blocks in record time. At least, no where near as efficiently in comparison to the main-series EDF games. Sure, you can recruit characters that have abilities and SP moves that can wreak havoc but so few have only come rather close to capturing the glory of a main-series Air Raider bombing.Oh yeah speaking of recruiting characters, instead of playing as the legendary lone soldier like in any other EDF game you now assemble a team of up to 4 soldiers, each of which can have abilities different to one another depending on who you choose to deploy. Characters gain more armor (level up their max health) when you complete missions with them. New characters, equipment and upgrades are unlocked by finding and rescuing unconscious people lying around somewhere on the field in each mission. As you'd guess, the new recruits you get have different stats and abilities. All new recruits start out only being able to use weapons from one weapon class (i.e. assault rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, rocket launchers, etc.) Finding the same recruits again on the battlefield after you've already recruited them will raise their skill level which will give them access to more of the weapon classes depending on how high the skill level gets. Equipment upgrades do not work the same; either you get a higher level weapon/accessory from rescuing or you don't. From what it seems, only 3-5 people that need rescuing spawn at a time per mission. So if your looking to upgrade (aside from armor), you have only 3-5 chances per mission for rng to give you more powerful versions of whatever weapons you want and more of the same character(s) you want to raise the skill level of.With the writing, it's much different to that of any other EDF game, I'd say. The writing to any other EDF game that I've experienced (namely EDF 5) is taken completely seriously in-universe. The writers themselves are well aware of just how ridiculous the writing is and revel in it, but the characters in those universe take the events seriously. In EDF: World Brothers, the writing is blatantly playful and meta. Characters in World Brothers break the fourth wall every now and then straight up acknowledging that this is a game whilst spewing out jokes here and there. The tone feels like a saturday morning cartoon compared to all other EDF games feeling like Starship Troopers. I may enjoy the writing from time to time, but when the story has been nothing but meeting a new buddy in a mission that the people in your team (in the story) fawn over, the buddy gets to a low point, and then they make a comeback that redeems themselves and makes a huge push towards victory in the mission (or so the writing keeps whacking you senseless with that statement) I can't help but see it as being forced. It also really didn't help when I've come across some characters whom I've thoroughly despised but just because they did one certain thing that was good all the other characters start exclaiming "Wow! They actually did something! They totally redeemed themselves and I trust them with my life now!" even though I, the player, am still the one doing all the work because the AI is especially useless in gameplay in this game only aside from taking some aggro.Now, when it comes to EDF games the voice commands are a must. Voice line usage has simply become integral to EDF's identity at this point to where I cannot in good conscience imagine an EDF game where you can't keep chanting "EDF!!" every second mixed with "To save our Mother Earth from any alien attack~... (From vicious flying insects who have once again comback~...)" or "Oh~ we are the valiant infantry. We are the alpha team with passion and comraderie~..." all the while slaughtering giant insects. The voice lines are very limited in this game; some lines aren't voiced and the one's that are (namely the shouting lines like as "EDF! EDF!" or "Wooaaaahh!!") don't have the level of conviction EDF 4.1 shouting lines have and therefore they come off as rather pathetic. The new EDF song is good, I liked it. The way how singing works, however, is unengaging. Entire verses are bound to a single command so you can't really do a call-and-response deal like  EDF 4.1's singing. The big charm in singing is being able to nail those singing responses in rhythm with the possibility of being  by going off rhythm and screwing with the whole choir all during combat mind you.Doesn't look like a positive review, now does it? Well, beyond all of the points I've made I'm still having some good fun with it. I still get those dopamine hits from clearing hordes and the bright and upbeat aesthetics help stave off my inevitable depression. I enjoy the gameplay mechanics and the team-building; it doesn't seem dull to me. While I've become apathetic towards the story's writing, I do love some of the personalities given to the characters based on the main-series EDF classes. For instance, the EDF 5 Air Raider is portrayed as some crazed military tactics enthusiast and the EDF 4 Ranger is overconfident but also panics when taking damage (also his "DODGE!" voiceline never gets old to me when I hear it.) Now, I cannot in good conscience say EDF: WB is a good EDF game, but much like how I look at Insect Armageddon and Iron Rain it is a good game on its own nonetheless. However, I would say it's not worth $60 US. Get it on sale perhaps... Hm? It's $40 US now? Well... still a bit steep in my opinion, so I'd maybe still wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the second best EDF entry out right now with 5 still being the leader. When you buy this and you inevitably enjoy it, make sure to pick up 5 on PS4 or PC. No but really, this is a horde shooter with randomized character and weapon drops that are dependent on what level and difficulty you're playing. You're killing giant insects, robots, aliens and kaijus to protect planet Earth from total destruction. You bring a team of 4 characters of your choice to each mission. Each character has their own unique ability with some being exponentially better than others. Characters also have weapon preferences, but with enough play time any character can use any gun. This can make for some broken combos. It also can lead to hilarious models too as your dainty Wingdiver is flying like a bee with a chaingun twice her size in her hand. You can increase character health by just playing missions with the EDF members that you want to level up.If you're experienced with this series or just prefer a general challenge I definitely recommend playing through the story on Hard the first time, taking a hiatus and then picking it up on the next highest difficulty. Otherwise use a trainer or something to unlock all difficulties. This game suffers from being too easy on Hard even with low armor. I understand this is a spinoff and all but no mainline EDF game is this much of a cake walk on hard, especially if is your first run through and your characters are still gaining armor.
