_childDocuments_.review: This game is way more charming than it has any right to be. I can't help but think of it as a sequel to Iron Rain, which is not, in fact, a sequel to Insect Armageddon. It's a fun take on the franchise, and feels like it was made by fans of previous games who have put their own fun spin on the formula.Pros: It's EDF.Dumb banter.Cons: Not enough group singing.Dumb banter.The menus are somehow more awful than other EDF games....some possibly offensive cultural stereotypes (don't look too closely at Amigo Bro)To be honest, my expectations were pretty low. I'm not a big fan of the voxellated style, and from the trailers I expected it to be nothing more than a skin-deep attempt to attract some younger gamers to the franchise, but to my surprise there is a mechanical addition it makes in the form of partial building destruction, allowing you to take cover inside buildings after blowing a chunk out of them. I also scoffed at the character swapping, but in practice it's totally fine and works great.Besides that, the enemy AI seems mostly identical to other games. It's chaotic and straightforward as well it should be. The bones of the game are EDF through and through. This is very much a game made for fans of the franchise, and I feel a little bad for taking so long to give it a chance. If you're new to EDF, I'd still recommend starting with one of Sandlot's mainline games like 4.1 or 5. But you wouldn't be too bad off if this was your first introduction to the series, even if some of the references won't make any sense. World Brothers is a pretty fun third-party addition to the collection, and it's getting me amply pumped for EDF 6.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the easiest starting point for being introduced to the Earth Defense Force series. The skill bar is low enough for newcomers, but certain characters still have their trademark movement to make fans happy (wing divers and prowl riders).  Weapons/Characters are still randomized, but a LOT LESS of a grind than the mainline series.  Also, now with enough unlocks, you can equip any soldier with any weapon (similar Iron Rain). The best plus is that each player can now take up to 4 chosen soldiers in to battle and switch them out on the fly, with the ones not in direct control actually still helping out (probably the most helpful NPCs of EDF series).  This also means if you down all but 1 of your 4, you still can be in the fight and even go back to revive your 3 downed NPC teammates without having to require help from your online friends (though they can still revive your guys too).The humor is wonderfully stereotyped on nationalities (no political correctness here), and has the lightest tone of the series with quips from your operator and your chosen soldiers galore.  Heck, there's even a spaceman soldier who does a Shatner like log narration when he is your main for missions.  For the long time fans there are lots of references to previous games (shout out to Insect Armageddon!), and quite a few pixelated models of the foes you fought before (no dragons this time, sorry).   Speaking of existing fans, don't let the cutesy aesthetic keep you from enjoying this one.  It is probably one of the better in the series and may end up being your favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: May genuinely be the best EDF game in my opinion.What I enjoy+Almost everything+True EDF experience+Less grind+Fun and fairly varied characters+Enjoyable maps, enemies, and charactersWhat I don't enjoy-Awful meta-humor-Maps feel a slight small which leads to literally falling out of maps-Hitting deep water deals considerable damage-Seemingly less weapons-Game seems to have less missions, but considering the sheer length of EDF games, this is basically a non-issueIf you like EDF, get it! _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It is a very good game (and EDF) game with very lackluster dialogue and story.I really like the game and have been having a blast with it. There are alot of characters and weapon variety which expands as you go into higher difficulties. Mission Structure is pretty similar however, this EDF does an amazing job at throwing as much as it can at you starting pretty early. First 10 levels or so are pretty easy and straightforward, and the battles get much larger going forward. It isn't that hard on normal, but you might run into some stressful missions. That being said, there are FOUR difficulties above normal and playing around on hard you can certainly see how insane the battles could get. If you want an edf game with good combat with lots of things to upgrade, unlock and experiment with than this is a great game. If you want an EDF game that has the charm of edf5 and 4.1 than stay away cause the dialogue is likely worth turning off entirely.Sidenote: I would recommend turning the voice volume of the characters lower than any other option of the game, because it is almost best read as subtitles with some chatter than actually hearing what is said. It's pretty bad and in no way entertaining unlike EDF5. However unlike EDF5, the dialogue is a bit less repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the EDF games. I love the EDF spin-offs also and while I personally think Iron Rain is the best of the spin-off games I would say World Brothers is a very close second place because it is just an excellent game that perfectly captures the essence of the series in a cute voxel shooter full of unique characters with fun abilities. It is still a great EDF game and in general a great shooter despite what the spin-off detractors keep trying to tell you and is a very different flavour that no other EDF game has thus making it very unique in the series.Pros:- Classic EDF gameplay- Cute, bouncy and pretty visuals and aesthetic- Tons of characters to play as- Loads of abilities, combined with character switching allows for fun and creative synergies- Pure EDF fanservice with weapons, enemies and more from past games- Huge variety of locations from around the world- Lighthearted story with characters that don't take anything seriously- Tons of improvements, changes and QOL additions also found in Iron Rain that I wish the mainline series would adoptCons:- Not as child friendly as it may seem as characters frequently use curse words (just a word of warning for the parents out there)- No creative modes at all, the game looks like it was made for this- A little too easy for my liking despite some enemies getting notable buffs- Unskippable special ability animations- Some enemies deal crazy damage even on normal difficulty, leaving you in a revive loop from time to time- A bit too pricey with too much DLCWhether you're an EDF fan and enjoy the fact that these spin offs are different from the mainline games or just a fan of shooters and wants to try something a lot different to what you usually play then World Brothers is a great choice. While I feel the game is a bit too expensive at full price and the complete lack of creative modes is a disappointment; what you have here is a great shooter and a great if somewhat different EDF experience.Well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into EDF: World Brothers knowing it wasn't a typical EDF game, and that it was the Iron Rain team going with a different approach to EDF. While they definitely had some good ideas, a lot of them just.. don't work well, and the end result (along with the sound design and voiceacting being trash) is that it's just not a good game.EDF has always been a game that rode on the strength of customization and its incredibly bad-on-purpose writing.  That's all gone. Instead of having one character that can equip multiple weapons, you have four characters at a time, each of which can equip exactly one weapon, along with an ability and a special attack that charges as you do damage. The problem is that this eliminates any kind of depth the characters have: each one only has around five voice lines and a lot of them are so samey that there's not really a reason to use one over the others.. and others are purely non-viable.As an example, early on you get a Spartan hoplite who is purely a melee character, but doesn't have any of the special abilities or movement tech you got with melee Fencers in EDF 4 and EDF 5. As a result, the hoplite is going to spend most of the game dead in the water because you simply can't move fast enough to kill anything - especially when you have any number of characters with guns. On the other end, you have a bunch of different characters that all use sniper rifles, which are nearly identical except that some do more damage. Sure, some of them have different abilities, but those don't really make enough of an impact to matter.The biggest crime, however, is what Yukes did to the Air Raider. The Air Raider was the best class in EDF 4 and EDF 5 complete with an entire voiceacting cast that only showed up for their support abilities. All of that is gone. There is an Air Raider, they do not get any support voicelines (even though I believe one of the trailers showed one that gets the Spritefall operator from EDF 5, but I did not see that) and their abilities are nigh-unusable due to the lack of the overhead zoomed-out camera that the Air Raider had in the older games. This somehow doesn't surprise me given that the Air Raider wasn't in Iron Rain at all.The one good decision Yukes made with this game is to have it so that you no longer need to pick up armor - a lot of people in EDF 4 and EDF 5 would use hacks to automatically pick it up because of how crates disappeared over time, so that's kind of an understandable advancement in game design... even if it takes a lot of the gameplay value away because you're no longer scrambling to grab crates.Anyway, this game isn't worth full price. Wait for a steep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best EDF games so far happens to be a game most people would consider a parody.  Instead of switching equipment and limited ammo supplies you have infinite ammo with reload cooldowns and each of your four characters has only one weapon they can bring. The hilarious cultural stereotype outfits for characters all have their own EDF style aesthetics to them as well. While the mission plotlines vary from hilarious to fourth wall breaking to clutch and intense.  It's been a long time since a game actually had me cracking up with laughter from both the story and the action on screen. Who would've thought i'd be learning about the soybean supplies of japan while firing rockets  from a chinese man in a purple panda costume. It's an absolute must have. A fantastic experience solo and multiplayer just intensifies it even more. Since each character has their own gameplay mechanics, well thought out friend groups can wind up with 16 characters that not only look unique, but bring their own useful spins to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: It's EDF with a twist and rng is still awful.Has the same b-movie feel as the rest and a decent story.For pro/cons:+Weapon drops have fixed stats so you don't have to farm the same weapon for it to be usable.-Weapons are tied to characters and it's fine enough on the earlier difficulties but the last 3 tiers are pretty much tied together so makes it hard to collect them all purely due to rng.+/- The way Rng was implemented is annoying, you no longer have to pick up crates as you get armor from mission+difficulty but the scaling is fairly bad for inferno+ so takes ages to get enough for 100k achievement, weapons being tied to characters means you can go after a specific type if you like them but missions have to big a pool of them and with only 3-5 drops per mission you can take longer than the mainlines to get what you want as rng still screws you over.Each character levels up individually from each other, levels unlock weapon types they can take into missions so a wingdiver can use fencer miniguns, air raider can use laser rifles etc, they gain armor from participating in missions but that makes using any other character than your main 4 annoying as you need to grind up armor from them or they die to fast.Each character has a special ability and an ultimate, some are borderline useless and others gamebreaking (combo of viking and vampire can oneshot any boss)Last character (there are 3 "unique" subtypes of everyone (alpha/beta/gamma)) took longer to find than doing all 60 missions on all 5 difficulties, Koala Gamma just wouldn't show up even after the other 2 were maxed out so had to go for it when grinding armor for several hours after the rest of the game was "done".+ You don't run the same risk to get one shot here, as you have 4 characters of your choice when entering missions each with their own weapon and hp bar, they take and deal reduced damage when not actively being controlled -> if you get hit with a big attack most of the time only one dies so have 3 extra "lifes" to win + can revive downed characters to get back that "life"-collision is still bad, enemies gets stuck in the ground, sometimes far enough down that you can't reach them and have to start over, other times you can with a big weapon stick it through and hit them or use explosives, same problem with spiders as the mainlines, attacks go through walls/floors to hit and on inferno can be lethal.In the end it's still a fun game but could do with some more balancing and reduced pool for droprates in missions (would be nice with a list of potential drops as well but that might be asking too much)

_childDocuments_.review: This spinoff of the EDF series trades the PS3-esque graphics and single-character gameplay of the mainline games for a bright voxel LEGO aesthetic and a party system that lets you bring  up to 4 characters from a roster of dozens, each with different weapons and abilities. _childDocuments_.review: EDF World Brothers stands out as a fantastic spin-off within the Earth Defense Force series. While maintaining the classic chaos and mayhem characteristic of EDF, it introduces unique mechanics that distinguish it from the mainline series. In contrast to the original EDF, World Brothers departs from the four-class system with hundreds of weapons; instead, players collect distinct characters known as brothers or sisters. Each character comes with their own unique weapon, special ability, and ultimate ability.World Brothers features a diverse roster of characters, some exclusive to the game, while others are familiar faces from previous EDF titles such as Insect Armageddon, Iron Rain, and EDF 1. The game serves as a grand EDF festival, appealing to devoted fans of the series. Despite the voxel art style, don't be deceived – this is unquestionably an authentic EDF experience. While it may initially seem easier than the mainline games, World Brothers gradually intensifies, delivering truly epic battles.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't outright say it is a bad game, so I can't "Not Recommend" it. It is inconvenient at times, and just odd in aspects.If one wants to compare it to the proper EDF games, it isn't that. It has a lot of references and characters and weapons and such from all of them, but it goes in a different direction for gameplay. I've only played solo, and the game really wants multiplayer.The AI companions you can use, are about useless. Their only purpose is to give an option to switch to when grabbed by an ant. This was the first major difference that struck me, in that you can't shoot your way out of being grabbed, so one must switch or wait (if all of the characters are grabbed). The AI companion's weapons don't work well. Their damage is useless, and their "homing" weapons, don't. I think the knockback stat still works properly, if that mattered.The weapons are what I'd compare to the un-upgraded versions. They don't do enough damage, so for the weapons that do, you'll wait for reloads or waiting on the slow fire rate, which is the second reason to have AI companions to switch to, just swap to a different character to keep attacking while that other character reloads. Weapon ranges aren't where they need to be either. In a ways (30 missions, so not far, as I think it has hundreds) into the game, and I still don't have a useful anti-air weapon. Best so far is a sniper rifle.The characters one can play as are something else. Their running speed is abysmal. They use a lot of national stereotypes (some are quite... something, like the mexican is constantly hungover), and the one for India just slowly shuffles about. His step doesn't even take his moving foot beyond the toes of the stationary foot. A lot of annoyances, but I still can't say it is a bad game, just /different/.Well, unto what really makes it odd. The game obviously has voxel based graphics. It is nice to be able to blow off chunks of buildings and such. I blew up London Bridge, because it had ants on it. Anyways, because of the voxel art style, I think they wanted to go for a more "kid friendly" comedy style. So, instead of B & C sci-fi movie types of humor, it is more like Saturday Morning Cartoon humor. This makes the fact that the game loves referencing things from previous EDF games, which doesn't have a large over lap with people younger than 12 years old. I'm wondering if it is a translation issue in the script. At least the voice actors seemed to be having fun, and they did a good job.Gameplay feels like an early to middle PS2 or Dreamcast Capcom game, in how simple overall it is. Does likely have the best menu feel in any of the EDF games though. Was surprised to find a nice looking, easy to use menu.Either way, it comes down to the fact that I'm only playing it, because it has EDF things. It is alright at the end of the day, but not "for me."

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the classic EDF series so I was genuinely surprised that World Brothers ended up being such a strong entry despite it's more kid friendly approach. Sure there's an inundation of novelty characters but they still pay homage to all of the older games with tongue-in-cheek jokes about the series.If you're new to the series then expect non-stop waves of giant insects, robots, and UFOs to blast to smithereens with your crew of EDF heroes and their ridiculous arsenal - this time in a minecraft style. The action is fast, frantic, and satisfying while also being surprisingly nuanced as you hose down the invaders with bullets and lasers while carefully dodging and reloading.This entry has tons of voxel character skins that unlock with each level and every skin has it's own weapon which means you're collecting your arsenal at a quicker pace than usual. Since you can bring multiple characters to each mission (even in single player) if you get downed you can swap to another character to keep playing which makes levels a little too easy, but this one is clearly built around accessibility.If you're new to the series and want a gentle introduction or if you're an experienced player with kids or family you want to play with this will be a good buy since the voxel bugs are easier on the eyes and less intensive on the CPU. For older troopers maybe stick to 5 until 6 comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: Ill be honest, at first i thought I wasn't going to enjoy this game but after beating it, EDF World brothers is the normal cheese you'd expect from the main line games but pushed to 100Very entertaining dialogue that makes EDF 4.1 look serious in comparison. Few differences from this title compared to the rest other than the obvious cube graphics. The one I personally enjoy the best is that instead of using one class you get to control a team of 4 comprised of various whackey international stereotypes (e.g. canadian guy is in a bear suit and says eh? every 5 nanosecond), EDF soldiers from all franchises, and even aliens.This is the top tier game to shut off your brain and blast things while listening to a podcast or music, with occational pauses to catch the absurd dialogue. ofc this wouldn't be EDF without a plethora of missions 60 + DLC(still have yet to go through DLC), weapons and brothers/sister characters to unlock and level up. Leveling up a character occurs when you find a second copy of that character during a mission and upon increasing a character's skill level they are able to equip a new weapon. Default EDF brothers/sisters can only use one weapon type ranging from Assault rifles, Assault Rifles Type 2, Melee, Mortars, Rocket Launcher, Special, Shotgun, Close Range, and Sniper.So on a given mission you basically have 4 guns that you can make use of switching on the fly to your squad of characters controlled by AI. As you're reloading on one character you can quickly jump to another, if one of them is being chomped by an ant you can switch to another to free them. Pretty fun new way of playing that allows you to experiment.Moreover every brother/sister has a special skill and an ulitimate e.g. ninja brother has a quick dash as a skill that goes on cool down after 4 uses and and ultimate of throwing explosive kunai. So far I think Im close to having unlocked all characters but I've only beaten the game on normal, there is hard difficulty and hardest (that u unlock after normal) with a potentially hinted inferno to unlock but unconfirmed so perhaps there are other yet to be discovered characters but so far I have about 60 ish characters although some are repeats but I'd say 80% are unique. This really is a game for all ages! Anyone can enjoy the whacky mindless fun of this game, well worth the pick up full price or on sale.Now get out there and repair cube earth and stomp on sum bugs!EDIT: Still havent unlocked acquiring all the characters achievement, definately a lot more unique characters than I thought

_childDocuments_.review: This is an odd game as the crowd it caters to a tiny audience. The mainline EDF games are niche as is and this game is meant as fanservice for those fans. A niche of a niche.This game allows you to use a diverse team of 4 characters that can be swapped back and forth at any time, the problem in my opinion is that each character has very limited use, aren't very customizable, and the game expects you to constantly swap back and forth and a lot of classes don't feel like their main counterpart. Air Raiders aren't constantly air raiding and can use normal guns, Rangers are kind of rangers but act more like party healers. Wing Divers are just the class you use to quickly reposition and are swapped out practically right away after you get to where you need to be. All of this makes gameplay basically always feel the same. That isn't to say it's a bad game, I just prefer how highly specialized classes were in the mainline games were which made it a lot more fun for me in coop. You don't really need other players in World Brothers and each player can basically act fully independently with 0 teamwork required. Still a lot of good EDF fun is to be had here with silly, albeit TOO on-the-nose humor sometimes.I honestly don't recommend this game if you haven't already played EDF4 and EDF5 first, since they have better story, humor, and gameplay imo, but if you've played both before and want more while waiting for EDF6, and you can get over how the game looks, this is a good option.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of EDF since 2017(the game, not the year) and have played it, 2025/4.1, 5, Insect Armageddon, and Iron Rain. I put this game off for too long, partly due to the design, partly because I wanted a sale. I regret waiting.Style/Graphics: As you likely saw, this spin off takes a minecraft/roblox/lego style approach. It lends an air of goofiness, but given the game is about killing hordes of bugs and robots with over the top weaponry, it actually works.Gameplay: This is where the game really stands apart from its predecessors. Instead of playing one soldier/class with two, maybe three or four, weapons, you pick out a team of four for each mission. Each soldier can only carry one weapon, however, you can switch between them at your leisure. The dozens of soldiers(not including what are essentially reskins) have their own special features. These typically involve an ability to dodge, an extra attack of some sort, flying, grenades, turrets, or some combination of the above. Each one also starts with one specific weapon category unlocked, though you can level up each one individually to unlock different weapon types. They also added in these accessories that boost various attributes of each soldier. You'll have to experiment alot to find your ideal playstyles, but generally you will want a versatile team unless you know exactly what you are fighting. Farming is also changed for better or worse, To get armor you finish the mission with whoever you want boosted, the amount varies by difficulty. Weapons, soldiers, and accessories however, require you to find three "fallen" allies on the battlefield, who upon winning will give you the mentioned prizes with some rng. No more grinding one mission for hours, instead grind it several times over hours.Music: Now EDF never had bad music, but it never really stuck out to me. While this could be due to the overwhelming explosions and chaos, none really stick out save for the small radio bits in loading cutscenes in Iron Rain(which make a return on mission accomplished screens, neat). In this game, when you do get to hear it over the carnage, it's amazing. It actually pumps you up and drives you to fight on. I noticed it heavily in the last few missions which helped any tiredness of marathon running the game.Story: This is, without a doubt, the cheesiest story in a video game to date. Without giving too much away, Earth is broken up as "Dark Tyrant" (actual name) brings together the aliens and their alternate versions from across the games. You, along with numerous characters both old and new, join forces to take Earth back, piece by piece. The culturally diverse team, using feel good messages and meta humor, look past each others differences to become Brothers and Sisters in arms and save their fellow Earthlings. Most of the time the mood is silly, with bits of seriousness and occasional worry as characters may seem dead, but give them two minutes and they reveal tis but a scratch. Nothing new or revolutionary, but EDF has always been the same "We're screwed, but we fight on and win because we can!" and it will never not work.TLDR: The cheesiest installment ever, and I loved every bit of it.EDF! EDF! EDF!

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike Iron Rain and EDF:IA, EDF:WB is a little spin off of the original series with cartoony block graphics and a twist in game play. With its classic "drop you off shoot everything in sight game play", this time around you take a squad of 4 characters with their own unique weapon type that you can switch to on the fly within the mission. As you progress, you unlock/find new characters throughout missions you can take with later in the game. It's a fun casual title to the series if you're a big EDF fan like me. But if you're looking for something similar to the mainline games, you may be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Y'all might be thinking this is something of a downgrade to the visual standards of EDF in the past, but one must realise this game recognises EDF for its true worth: An almost self aware campy parody of any xenomorphic slaughter-fest B-movie that has ever existed.It's taken up to eleven in this entry with a voxel style to help facilitate unique character and environmental design to better emphasise its sense of parody but also to demonstrate its flavour of being a love letter to previous EDF games. The somewhat cringeworthy dialogue and memetic characters are also fit perfectly into what's becoming a tradition for the series, helping you to laugh with it rather than at it. If you can't find it in your heart to love a game such as this, you should probably visit a priest because you clearly lack SOUL.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: If you are an EDF fan, don't think, just buy it. If you are not a fan, I'd say the game is worth the money when on sale.It includes every classic enemy bosses of all EDF games, along with their corresponding background music when fighting them, really brings me back to the time when I played EDF4.1, Iron Rain and Insect Armageddon (EDF5 is still fresh in my memory), and that feeling tells me my money was well spent.However this game has different combat from EDF4.1 and 5. So if you are purely looking for EDF gameplay and don't have any emotional attachment to the EDF series then you probably want to watch a few game video before deciding buying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: If you like EDF, and Lego adventure games, you will probably like this. It is a huge departure from EDF's tone as a series. So if you do not like the Lego adventure tone in games, definitely pass on this one. It is juvenile, and if you are okay with that you could enjoy it a lot. If you want a more serious EDF look at EDF 4.1 or wait for 6.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is what an EDF spinoff should be.Insect Armageddon and Iron Rain are fine games but they lack the core elements of an EDF game. Those elements being loads of weapons to collect and a freaking million enemies on screen. World Brothers has both of those. The only important difference (besides the graphics obviously) is that instead of guns you find 3ish characters in each mission that you can switch out with your team of 4. Each levels up like in EDF 5. Each character starts with one weapon type but can unlock other types as they level up. The characters get unique abilites and supers that are locked to that character type and makes them play completely different from one another. Characters come with weapons and like in EDF 5 if you get a duplicate the weapon levels up.Another welcome change is the level variety. The visual difference is SO much greater than in the mainline games where it's basically city/mountains/underground. In World Brothers we get city and mountains for sure as well as paris, japan, egypt and a super cool jungle looking area with rainbows you can walk on.Only real negative right now is that the story and characters just aren't as campy. It's clearly just a bunch of silliness aimed at children which is perfectly okay but not quite the amazingness found in 2017, 2025 and 5. Also the enemy count IS lower than the mainline games (but WAY higher than IA or IR) but the smaller levels make sure it's utter chaos at all times. Your radar WILL be covered completely in red.So yeah, if you're a huge fan of the mainline games but don't really like the spinoffs this is the spinoff for you. Plays FAR more closely to the mainline games than the other spinoffs. Is it on par with the mainline games? No. This just makes me REALLY want EDF 6. But this game is a fantastic hold over until that comes out and worth sinking dozens or even hundreds of hours into.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a ball playing this game! I enjoyed a lot of the other EDF games and have been a fan for a bit. This one is very different and has some uniquity to it that's very appealing. The core of the game is similar to most EDF's but it's got it's differences. I enjoy the Team aspect and I like the humorous dialog between the characters. It's a very fun game and i'd recommend getting it during a sale. Only thing that sucks is it seems online is dead already. I only ever see one foreign lobby and it's password locked. :(

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Edf 5 and 4.1 I liked this one a lot. Don't go in thinking this is going to be Edf 6 or anything but imo this is a spinoff done right.  My only two real problems is that its pretty easy until you beat the game and unlock the harder difficulties by beating the game, And the 60 dollar price tag on a somewhat short game. Not worth that price tag at all. But if you see it drop to 20 bucks and like Edf 4.1/5 I would say its worth checking out as a spinoff game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The Combat feels similar while changing things up a lot with addition of numerous characters. Each Brother or Sister Comes with their own weapon and accessory which can be swapped out for another one in that weapons class or more when you level them up. They also have a unique ability (shift) like the ranger's dodge roll or the Wing Diver's flight. They also have their own Special Move which can vary from buff circles that heal, or increase atk and def, to massive Air Drops like the old games that will wreck everything in its path. Not every character its equal to every other and some are more unique compare to the standard EDF forces you know and love. The inclusion of so many variations of every EDF and they all feel different, for example The Rangers from EDF 4.1, 5, & 1...yes 1. all have the dodge roll, but they each have a different starter weapon and a different Special Move, making each feel unique while maintaining the fun of a Ranger. The Grind of old has been replaced...kinda. Instead of farming levels for Weapons and Armor. Armor and weapon boxes are gone in replace of healing and SP boxes. The "Grind" come from saving Brothers and Sisters. Each Mission has Characters that need to be saved. If you save them and win you either Unlock that new Character or it will Level up that existing character, allowing them to use a new class of weapon. That change has made me love the EDF series all over again, and honestly I would love if this replaced the "Side Series" and continued this along side the Main Franchise. The Voxel Look maybe a turn off for some but if you are a fan of EDF, this is a game for you and your friends to squad up and just have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't exactly gotten too far in due to many events in other games, but I've seen enough to know exactly what I've experienced.So this is basically a voxel version of an EDF game with boundaries being "replaced" by end-of-world falls. This actually stems from the story of the game explaining that the world was...basically broken up by mothership attacks. It's still an EDF game, and it mostly plays like one. The biggest factor of this game is that it combines ALL of the EDF universes into one, meaning that enemies and classes from all games are present here.As far as classes go, it was mostly replaced by character selections from a wide variety which expands as you rescue them during missions; these classes also have variants to differentiate them (alpha, beta, gamma, etc.). Players familiar with previous games will know the class characters with the difference being that most movement has been moved to a skill button. Heavy Infantry classes (Fencer, Striker, etc.) will see that they will not being able to dual wield their weapons anymore due to a different weapon system; weapons are instead initially tied to individual characters classes and can only used if the class allows that weapon category to be used. This can be increased by rescuing dupes of a character class.For how the game plays during missions, it still follows the same rules of destroy all enemies to complete the mission. One thing players will notice is a sort of squad system. You can create a team of up to 4 characters to use in missions, provided they're not duplicates of the same character. While it does seem powerful, it's balanced out by the game significantly reducing the damage of the characters you're not currently controlling. Another thing is the SP Skill system. Kills generate SP which is obtained at different rates depending on the enemy killed, the character class (which has an SP speed stat), as well as equipment. These generally have powerful effects from widespread attacks to support. All characters have different SP Skills, but characters under the same category (EDF4 Ranger, Jet Lifter, Soldier, etc.) (Alpha, Beta, Gamma) will have the same SP Skill, meaning you can use the same SP Skill multiple times in succession.As for the story characters themselves...they really like breaking the 4th wall. Was there a 4th wall in this game to begin with? Probably not. They also like setting up flags.Good game if you're familiar to the series. For those new to the EDF series, I'd recommend starting with previous games first.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get deep into a review, I just want to give a shoutout to the wonderful Devs behind this for listening to player feedback and doing the work to improve their game based on it. With the new update now allowing people to play with people in other regions, the online multiplayer has truly opened up. They have also been working on the mouse acceleration issue, and for their commitment alone, I am happy with my purchase.That being said? Would I recommend this game? Eh, it REAAALLLY depends. If you are like me, and are an avid EDF fan who appreciates every EDF game faults and all, and are looking for a game that is 110% a love letter to everything EDF and then some? I can absolutely recommend this game. This game is a nostalgia overload, and as an EDF fan, I was grinning like an idiot at all the references to past games. I say yes.But if you are somebody who loved the slow grind and challenging gameplay approach featured in EDF 4.1/5 and want to go in guns blazing on harder difficulties with little to your name... this is definitely not for you. For starters, the only difficulties you have unlocked initially are Easy, Normal, and Hard. Hardest require a game clear, and Inferno requires an additional game clear on top of that. So if you miss the rush of doing Inferno with underleveled gear... sorry to say, but you have to put a lot of work in for it. Which can be difficult for a lot of reasons, not just including gameplay.Since this is not a mainline game and is a spinoff, it plays entirely different than mainline EDF games. If I had to give an analogy? It's basically what Warriors Orochi is to the Dynasty Warriors and Samurai Warriors series. The most obvious examples are this are in the introduction of the 4 Party System and SP Moves, which are basically just Ultimate abilities. Rather than having two different guns, you have four characters that use a single gun. This is essentially just having four lives, and it makes the game feel incredibly easier as a result. Although the enemies are balanced around this idea, the same challenge you faced as a Ranger in EDF4.1 is completely absent, since you can just simply switch to a Wing Diver and fly, and then switch to ANOTHER wing diver when the flying runs out. Surrounded by enemies and you need to retreat? Just turn into a Fencer and stab your away out of there. The game truly doesn't get challenging till the last stretch of the game, which some might find a turn off, and I wouldn't necessarily blame them.In addition, there are NO weapon or armor crates to pick up in the game. No more end of mission rolling-to-the-crate rush, no more "keep one enemy alive to gather stuff" rush, and more over, no more grinding to get better leveled gear. Instead, armor is given based on performance in the match, and you are given three random (sometimes, only one) teammates to rescue every mission. Each teammate has a different weapon, with higher difficulties giving them a chance to carry upgraded gear. Duplicate team members level up the skill level for the original unit, which allows them to use different classes of weapons the further they go. With the weapons being divided into classes, this means that you can create some incredibly fun builds, like a Wing Diver using a Fencer's Blasthole spear. Or a Ranger using a Rapier or Idunn. While this seems exciting at first, it quickly becomes a problem the further through the campaign, as, simply put, there are so many unlockable characters, with most characters having three variations that  have their own stat variations. You will very quickly run into the problem where you just will not be able to upgrade a specific unit  because you simply just...don't find them again. This is made even worse with DLC, if you could believe it.And that's to say nothing of balance, because, boy howdy, this game has some pretty weird balancing at times. DLC weapons and characters, which I will say is definitely worth their value with the Season Pass Bundle, are just flatout busted in a lot of areas, with Mian, her laser cannon, and her Shooting Star ultimate in particular just absolutely trivializing a lot of encounters. Give her weapon to an Air Raider, and Air Raiders just terrorize the battlefield. The Grim Reaper Unit EDF5 Fencer's weapon thrusts him forward with every press of the button, providing an extremely reliable and fast option out of encounters in conjunction with the dash. Outside of the DLC, though? There are just some characters and weapons that are flatout objectively better than others. One that comes to mind is the EDF3P Infantry with the Backpack, as his heavy assault rifle has absurd range and damage output, and his Genocide Gun Ultimate literally just dealing 99999 damage. His walkspeed and reloading being the only drawback, which is again mitigated by the fact that you can change to another character, to say nothing of just giving other characters his same weapon. On the other side, EDF5 Ranger has a lousy Ultimate where he just fires an incredibly short timed burst of extremely potent healing, but is outclassed by the Maid Class who has a healing bubble that does the same thing but lasts far longer. If you put the Cowboy Brother's upgraded weapon, which does more damage the closer you are to a target, on a Wing Diver, your wing diver will be able to consistently do 9000+ damage per shot as she circles around a large enemy and unload. Meanwhile, the Limpet Gun has to be reloaded in order to detonate the grenades and deal any real damage, which just places your Air Raider in danger. And that's just the tip of the iceberg. The list goes on, and you very quickly realize that not every character is treated equally.And finally, there's just the issue of going through the writing. Which is...hoh boy. EDF games have always been self aware, but they also didn't rely on shattering the fourth wall. It took itself seriously, and was equal parts goofy and serious, with a lot of moments in 4.1 being genuinely emotional. This game, however, does this with less finesse and is very confusing in its tone. It feels as though it has an identity crisis, being unable to decide whether to be kid friendly and a serious EDF game, as there are several moments where characters just flatout tell you that this is a "showing off a tough monster" mission and that you need to "trigger the escape event." And then turns around and tries to talk about the horrors of warfare with the aliens.  This is saying nothing about the honestly cringe inducing characters revolving around annoying country stereotypes and literally one character trait. Kotaro, who is a time travelling ninja, is either complaining about honor, or miso soup, and often ends his sentences with "NINJAAAA." Joe is cowboy who talks about his cows getting abducted and acts like an ignorant git with a southern accent most times, and Lazenby is just a British soldier that screams "FOR THE QUEEN!" To say nothing about the Maid Cafe Cat Girl with two personalities or the Korean Live Streamer that has a frustratingly large pull in the plot. However, all that said though? Even with everything above, I personally loved this game.Buried beneath all the frustrating plotlines, writing, and gameplay decisions, however, is a genuine love for everything EDF, and in my opinion, a fun game overall. Having Lightning Alpha from Insect Armageddon was awesome, and I got a goofy grin on my face when the characters started talking about the "legendary soldier" from EDF1 and Storm-1 from EDF3/4.1. I personally loved that you can hide out in destroyed buildings and regroup your soldiers, as it often gave you a moment to breathe and collect yourself for a battle. I liked many characters had different mechanics to them, and that the ultimates weren't all just attacks. Many are healing and stat raising, too. It isn't a mainline EDF game, but I'm okay with that.Ultimately, YMMV, but something I'd say is worth checking, when on a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: You can be a Prowl Rider, Wing Diver, and Fencer all at once. What's not to like?This is the second game done by Yuke's for EDF, their first being Iron Rain (which I actually like for the movement mechanics and melee weapons). If you've played Iron Rain, you know that there's a few issues with it. It doesn't have the scale of prior EDF titles (which just have absurdly large maps, to be honest), vehicles are pretty much an after thought that feel like garbage to use, and guns, for the most part, have zero audio or visual impact and feel terrible to use.World Brothers still doesn't have the scale of previous EDF titles, and the are vehicles are sparse (they're placed on certain maps rather than called in) but handle mostly fine. Most importantly though, the guns actually feel pretty good now. At least roughly on par with the rest of the EDF series. As I mentioned in the open of this recommendation, this game allows you to use multiple characters at once. Rather than have a single character with a couple weapons you take into a mission, you now select 4 characters, each with one weapon, an ability, and a special move. The abilities can be any number of things, including but not limited to: dodge rolling, flight, attack buffs, air strikes, tackles, and the e-needle. Specials tend to be hard-hitting attacks that vary from character to character, but they can also be things like healing for the team (which the ranger has), and an invincibility mode with an attack buff (Saki from OneeChanbara has this special, specifically).All 4 of your selected characters are always active on the field. The ones you're not in control of take greatly reduced damage and deal greatly reduced damage. When you swap to a character, they'll instantly teleport to where you are, unless the character you're using has been downed or grabbed, in which case your camera will move to the location of the character you swap to. When a character is downed, you can revive them much like you would revive a co-op teammate in other EDF titles.It's notable that the new character mechanics somewhat simplified and changed the characters as well, however. For example, Wing Divers no longer run on an energy meter, and their jets don't recharge while you're in the air, even when not in use. None of the jetpack characters recharge boost while in the air, to be clear. On the other hand, all weapons now run on ammo, so weapons that used to be terrible due to the energy drain they caused now actually may be pretty strong (or at least usable).Also, you can have 4 Wing Divers or Pale Wings, or Jet Lifters, or  whatever, and you can swap active characters while mid-air, so you can get a pretty good amount of flight this way. That said, if you use up all of their flight, then that means that all of them will have to recharge when you hit the ground, which could leave you pretty vulnerable, to say the least. The ability to switch midair also allows you to fly up to a large enemy, and then swap to a melee character to perform aerial attacks rather than swiping at its ankles.Rather than  weapon boxes dropped around levels, there's now simply 3 characters (on the vast majority of stages) spread around that you can revive and recruit. They come with a weapon and an accessory. Each character starts only being able to use one type of weapon, but as you pick up duplicates in stages, they have a progress meter that increases, and each level they gain allows them to use another category of weapons. Want a Wing Diver flying around with a minigun? You can do that, provided you've got enough duplicates of that Wing Diver to unlock the ability for her to equip one.There's also no more armor boxes you have to pick up. You just gain armor for killing things and completing missions.The game's humor style, rather than the traditional self-aware but serious-toned B-movie cliche romp that is normal EDF humor, is an occasionally 4th-wall breaking totally silly style that pokes fun at some anime tropes and cliches. Just how silly is it? One of the early characters you get is a cowboy that's annoyed that the aliens stole his cows, and it only gets more wild and outlandish from there. Anyway, much like Iron Rain, World Brothers is EDF, but different, but it manages to feel much more like proper EDF thanks to the guns feeling like they have proper weight to them. I recommended Iron Rain specifically for the movement and melee weapon mechanics while saying that the guns were kind of garbage. In this case, I can recommend World Brothers as a normal EDF title, so long as the graphical and humor style departures from the norm don't bother you. The game plays like proper EDF (minus calling in vehicles as Air Raiders, if that was your thing) this time around, and it brings interesting ideas (particularly using a team of characters rather than just one character) to the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: In true EDF fashion World Brothers is a colossal sidestep. It’s a lot different than anything that came before, some stuff better and some worse, but still feeling like Earth Defense Force.The best way to sum this up is “Lego Earth Defense Force”. Instead of a B-Movie theme, it’s a parody of the series filled with love and clever references. There’s some plot about the voxel world being shattered but that “Plot” also includes several missions dedicated to gathering ingredients for Miso Soup. At the end of the day, this is all an excuse to blow up swarms of giant bugs and chuckle at the references to past games. The core gameplay is surprisingly true to the past game despite massive evolution. You still fight hordes of the classic EDF monsters (Literally all of them) while collecting bigger and more ridiculously overpowered weapons and grinding for armor bonuses. The new touch is that you can switch between 4 characters at will. You can use your wing diver to fly onto a rooftop… swap to your air raider to nuke the city below… only to dive off the side of the building dressed in a panda suit to punch your way to victory. This opens up new tactical options, but more importantly, means that you can rescue your fallen teammate in single player. One mistake no longer leads to a game over.This does make for an easier game, especially when you have 4 players, each with 4 EDF soldiers, each with stupidly overpowered guns, and special moves. There is some challenge late game and I assume inferno will be a pain, but it feels more friendly and casual. If that isn’t what you wanted, you’ll probably hate the voxel art style and silly dialogue anyways. -- Characters and Progression --One place that really deserves review attention is the characters. It’s both my favorite part of this game and the place they dropped the ball.There are loads of unique characters that each have their own statistics, secondary action, special attack and even controls. Wingdivers fly, Air Raiders call in strikes, Vampire’s sparkle jump, Amigo Bros toss molotovs, Yodel sisters sing to distract the enemies, and so on. Picking your squad is as important as picking out their weapons and accessories and can massively depend on your play style. It’s downright fantastic. But the sales pitch “There are over 100 characters to build your team” isn’t quite accurate. Nearly every “World Brother” class can be found in 3-4 colors which are near identical.  EDF 1 Infantry is a genuinely different character EDF 5 character complete with its classic inability to forward roll and unique dialogs and different abilities.But Blue Koala vs. Gray Koala on the other hand have the same lines, weapons, abilities, and a one-point stat difference. It only serves to pad the character count for and actively hurts the experience. Character skill growth is tied to random gacha  drops. The more clones they have, the harder it is for me to level up the characters that I actually use. So the developers were smart and made “Skill Level” only determine the number of weapon types they’ve mastered. Lower-level characters aren’t weaker, but are simply locked into a single class of weapons. This allows you to switch between characters throughout the game and enjoy the wide variety that they throw at you. And this makes the next Design so baffling to me. To mimic classic EDF you increase your armor after each mission. No need to collect boxes or kite the enemies while you clear the field of drops. You can focus on the action and it was passively make the characters on your team more powerful. But only the characters on your team.If you use a variety of characters you won’t collect the armor you need for the harder difficulties. The most fun I had in this game was swapping characters around and trying crazy new teams, but I'm actively penalized for doing so.The very same developers that had shared armor in iron rain for 5 classes, decided to make you grind 100 characters separately.- Final Opinion –Despite the visual change this was a relatively safe design that stays true to the core series. I loved this game in the same way I did the Core series, Iron Rain, Wing Diver, Tactics and everything in between.But playing it safe meant that it falls somewhere in the middle. The low points in World Brothers are nowhere near the tedium of other games in the series, but the high points are nowhere near the excitement and joy from other games either. I can easily recommend it, but it’ll also be one that game I’ll probably forget about sooner than later.

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT REVIEW:  Do you like EDF games?  Well this is an EDF game and so you'll probably like it as well.I reckon roughly 7-10 hours for a playthough depending on skill & difficulty.Slightly longer and rambling review:EDF World Brothers is a surprising entry into the EDF games and in general if you enjoy EDF for what it is then you'll enjoy this one even if you are put off by the different art style.Additionally this game makes a number of other changes to the EDF formula which imo are actually really great Quality of Life improvements that help the game flow quickly and well:- No more random drops for weapons (whilst this is a bit of an EDF staple it does mean that unless you're a completionist you'll probably only ever see half of the weapons in the game- Smaller maps - this keeps each mission down to 5-15 minutes in length and much more pick up and play- no more scooping up armour pickups- unexpected critical mission updates to inform you about miso soup and tofu- the levels have a lot more character to them than the nondescript cities of previous gamesThe bad:- Feels overpriced- all of the characters are fun, but EDF fans will probably wish they could unlock weapons for specific classes instead of hoping you pick up a character which fits your playstyle

_childDocuments_.review: A more-so-than-usual lighthearted EDF game with Voxel graphics, allows partial building destruction for foot soldiers to take cover in.Play 4 characters at a time to balance movement firepower or tankiness, or pick whatever hilarious combination of weirdos and caricatures you want.The grind revolves around collecting characters & weapons, so you're almost ensured something new each map. Raising  armor points necessitates playing with a character, so don't sweat it and pick the ones you like.Lots of potential for gameplay variety. Only downside is vehicles being locked to maps.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of EDF? You will *love* this game. This is everything about EDF but better than ever. The tone is less serious and the graphics are different... but the gameplay is better, more fun, and more in depth than ever. It's not a very difficult entry in the series, but it deserves your attention as a fan of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game alot. its an interesting take on EDF and I feel like added abilities to characters is a really cool Idea wouldnt mind seeing that hit standard EDF eventually. but when they said all the past enemies were coming back I was expecting ALL of the enemies not just 1-2 enemies from each of the series.the story is fantastic, all the characters were pretty silly and I enjoyed most of the dialogue. the characters you play as are pretty fun some of them are a little terrible but I can see most of them are pretty useful for one reason or another.Regarding the Mothership's its a shame we never get to fight one. I would say that is the worst part of this game because the Mothership's fights was my favorite part of every game. I was hoping for a Mothership marathon of back to back Mothership fights. Its the only part that I find disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the EDF series. The game is silly and lighthearted fun, and as an EDF fan, I thoroughly enjoyed myself. I felt it was a nice departure from the far more bleak tone of EDF 5 (which it seems likely will be continued in 6), simply for variety's sake. I've only played 4.1 and 5 before, but instead of feeling like I was missing out on something when other games were being referenced, or characters and classes I was unfamiliar with showed up, I found myself wanting to try those games out too. While World Brothers is a slight departure in mechanics, and a significant change of visual style, it's still a great addition to the series, and overall a ton of fun. I would love to see another game of the sort somewhere down the line, to include content from whatever EDF games are released in the coming years.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: having never played an EDF game before i was blown away by the quality of this game.the voxel based art style blends perfectly with the gameplay and humour.the gun play feels great for the most part, maybe one or two weapons out of the absolute plethora i have unlocked feel a little jank. theres so many different characters which is both a huge positive and a negative. there's infinite replay ability but its extremely hard to level up the characters you like the most.story wise its heckin long, i have 7 hrs and only reached the 10%  mark and theres been a steady stream of updates

(wanted my space bar to use wing divers jets)when you alt tab it can cause glitches with the ui making your mouse out of place.cool parts about this game - over 100 playable characters -special abilities- you're no longer solo as you get a team of 4 people to use and they follow you as you can also switch between them.Great art style kid friendly this game is good for 1st timers. or couch parties EXPECT STORY TO BE TACKY ITS A TRADEMARK FEATUREall'n all probs best price at 50% or less. 10/10 would rec EDF 5 again.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly the best EDF i ever played (played 4.1, 5 and IR).Why ?They fixed all time gating stuff. Hope alle Future EDF Releases learn from that.- No "let one Monster live to run around and collect every loot boxes at the other side of the map". Its just play the missions and get your stuff.- No single player instant death. Switch on other teammates and revive yourself.- No waiting game. Reload ? Just switch teammate with the same weapon and continue firing !Its just so more fun. Sure the voxels are not the coolest stuff, but if you can get used to it, greatness awaits.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Much easier to get into than other EDFs. Teambuilding mechanics make loadout customization truly diverse and able to fit a wider variety of play styles. Progress is much easier than previous games and encourages replaying with friends, even if online is a little buggy. Hard is the equivalent of previous EDF Normal modes. Once you understand the basic mechanics just play everything on Hard.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who hated Iron Rain I can gladly say Yuke's seriously stepped their game up with this one. World Brothers is filled to the brim with personality and fun characters. The new team mechanic is also incredibly fun as swapping brothers around allows for great synergy between classes such as using a wing diver to fly to the top of a building then swapping to air raider in order to get a better drop for your air strikes. Only downsides are some minor bugs with the PC port and bad mouse acceleration but hopefully those can get patched out.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally an EDF: Greatest Hits game, with great gameplay changes to streamline the experience and make for a new combat experience, centered around switching between different characters, rather than specific classes. For everyone unhappy with it not being like another mainline game, I'd argue it's a nice change of pace, and I've been having a ton of fun with friends playing the game.The dialog is retched though, so uh, prepare for REALLY bad fourth-wall humor.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: One playthrough on easy isn't enough for a full review, so bear that in mind. That said, this one is for EDF fans, not newcomers.  This game is at its best when it does its own thing, which it is reluctant to do until the last 6 missions. Nevertheless, I enjoyed it and I hope it gets support as new games come out.

_childDocuments_.review: Well after going through the game once, I can safely say that this is a good EDF game.  But it does have issues compared to the main series and a tone shift that cause my friend dislike the game who normally enjoys the series.Let's just quickly go over the gameplay, it's pretty much EDF but if you can only equip one weapon for your character.  However you got 4 characters who all got different moves and special moves.  So this firstly opens up the gameplay in that you got more characters to play as and different styles of movement to control between characters, additionally allowing the base gameplay to not get pale as you can now just switch to the character which has the moveset you like the most in that moment.  The only difference in this game between the main series is the smaller maps and there being almost no NPC allies, smaller maps aren't a bad thing and I do like the different locations in this game.  They help to spice up the environments nonstop, now with there being no npcs.  Yeah that's a shame but it makes sense due to smaller maps, the fact your characters in your team are npcs when you don't control them.  So only adding 1-3 allies as pure npcs who aren't in your team is fine.So yeah the gameplay is good and my only real complain with the gameplay in the end is the game is very easy, even on hard I only struggled with HP forwards the end and even if you do die as one character.  You got 3 more characters who you can just take control over and heal the downed character back up.Up next is visuals and well they fix the game perfectly, I think this is one of the only voxel based games that I enjoy the visuals of and that's due to how consistent the style is.  The enemies look great and the detail on the environment is top notch, all the different playable characters look great too and can be easily told apart even if some of them look similar.  Honestly feels like some the EDF enemies originally came from a voxel game due to their looks here.Finally the story/tone, what is a EDF without it's story/tone and well here.... it's different.  This is mostly due to the game's change of tone, the game still has that B-movie vibe but its been mixed in with some ridiculous nonsense and self awareness humour.  Well it isn't nonsense but more like references with layers stacked upon each other and all those references are from different media.  This isn't a bad thing but the change of tone is very noticeable.  Like in the main series everyone acts completely 100% seriously to the situation they are in, sometimes referencing but still sticking to the serious tone despite the ridiculous of it.  Here they fully embrace the ridiculousness and even the characters know that they are in a video game, so the serious tone that we are used is thrown out the window and is now replaced with humour that people might see as childish.Now I'm not too bother by this and is instead happy that the game has alot of humour, on top of that this game has tons of characters that just talk and interact with each other.  They got clear names and goals, they all got different personalities and I love that.  But for my friend, they missed how the main series handle it and even how Iron Rain handle it.  The serious tone blended in with the b-movie vibe without embracing the madness.  This game might turn off people just due to it's tone and I won't fault them for it, it is more childish and that isn't a bad thing in the end.  For me I don't mind it but for my friend it heavily impacted their enjoyment of the game.So in the end is this game good, HELL YEAH.  EDF EDF EDF.  But if you think the game's tone and visuals will impact your enjoyment of the game, it probably will hurt your enjoyment and I won't fault you.  It's childish, has some random lol moments and internet humour thrown in.  If you don't mind that then you probably will enjoy this game.For me this game gets an 8/10 and is above most of the series due to it's uniqueness alone, I would happy play this alongside EDF 5 and potentially EDF 6 soon.  An issue I have with the series is how hard it is to play earlier games due to them lacking features and quality of live improvements from the newer games, this game can easily be played without feeling that due to it's different approach and tone among it's gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely comical spin off of the edf series that feels like playing a normal edf game with 60 levels of fun to be had. Normally edf games are b-movie esque with strategic shooting versus hordes, but this one takes it into the comical realm with strategic shooting versus hordes.It takes all the previous edf games and stuffs them together in a fun package with comedy like the lego games.Normally in edf one gathers weapons and armor by farming for them, but this game one gathers them by finding duplicates of playable characters to unlock using other weapons on them and on higher difficulties or level a higher version of their standard gun.This game also differs that each character can only field one weapon, but one has up to 4 characters in ones team and can freely switch between them to use the other weapons and special skills, a well balanced team is needed to have an easy time getting further along in the game.Each character one uses in a level also gets more armor after a level and the higher the level, the more armor they will get, so switching around between favorite characters to get them more armor will be needed.The makers of this game truly made a fun game worthy of belonging to the edf franchise imho and I am truly enjoying this game.Please note that I played it so far in single player mode and not tried out their multiplayer, nor did I run into the problems other people had with their mouse and keyboard controls (except sometimes a mouseclick not registering for a charge weapon or somesuch). Should I play multiplayer I will add it to this review.If one orders the dlc characters, one can find duplicates in the levels to up their lvl and probably also their weapons on higher levels.The real problem is to min/max certain weapons as with so many characters to find and unlock and level, targeted levelling or working for a certain weapon is impossible and just playing for fun and seeing what drops is your best bet to get better weapons and characters. Do note that for most sub characters finding a weapon upgrade for them even for a different colored version (unless a special one) will still allow one to use that weapon on the main class, the lvl of the class only allows one to use different weapons of other classes of characters.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning for those looking for split screen EDF this version doesn't have it (at least not yet. hopefully later). it has it on the other ports though.TL;DR Im enjoying this game as a EDF fan. My favorite so far. Better than Iron Rain.Honestly this has become my favorite EDF game so far. Where Iron Rain was trying to be too serious this is the exact opposite of that. what It lacks in that classic tongue-in-cheek B tier Horror movie vibe from the main series this replaces it with charm, self reference to the series, and meta humor. This is basically a EDF All-Stars game that brings back enemies from all previous games.The gameplay is like any other EDF games with some differences. The main difference is the, for a lack of better term, gacha style character system minus the micro-transactions. The cast is a mixture of new characters and characters from past EDF games with their own personalities. Even the silent old EDF player characters now talk.Each character comes with their own weapons, stats, and abilities. Each character has an active ability and a "ultimate" you build up by grabbing certain boxes or racking up kills. You can rescue (which are sudo rolls) three random characters per level and are different depending on level and difficulty (at least from what i can tell). Each character has a few variations to them in stats and color schemes. If you get a copy, the character will level up allowing for use of more types of weapons on that character.Where in the other games you had to grind from drops in World Brothers you passively gain armor on characters you play as and weapons come with characters you collect. I kinda prefer this as i don't have to stop and look for weapon and armor boxes. Something new to the grind is some characters come with accessories which work as stat boosts. There's an actual story and cut-scenes? Yeah kinda weird in a EDF game. Even more than Iron Rain had.  Though it is simple and I haven't felt it detracted from the game at all.The only thing I've found objectively wrong is they didn't put split screen in this version at least at this time, Hopefully it will come in a patch. Everything else just comes down to how much of a EDF purest you are. Like the levels are typically smaller like in Iron Rain and in the beginning it feels like the enemy count is smaller and the game feels a little too easy at the start. But i only got up to the 6th or 7th level so it may change later down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Same EDF Gameplay but with "Gotcha" Mechanics.Best way to describe this game is "EDF: Heroes" as the game no longer revolves around traditional EDF Mechanics but these new "Gotcha" mechanics where instead of finding weapon crates and armor crates scattered around the map, you're locating and rescuing "fallen Brothers/Sisters" scattered around each map. Each map has a number of Brothers & Sisters you can rescue, each one with with their own weapons, skills, special abilities and in some cases accessories. This is where the "Gotcha Mechanics" come into play as each character you rescue is a character you can add to a 4 man team. each team you play with allows you to switch between characters at will and use their abilites as needed. an Example of this would be if you are using the Starting Ranger from EDF 5, you can use his automatic G&M Sniper Rifle to take out large groups of targets, his sprint ability to get around faster, his traditional dodge role to dodge incoming attacks and his SP ability (The Reverser Gun) to heal yourself and the Team. But let's say you want to get on a more elevated position that you can't access with your ranger. At any time you can switch to your EDF 4 Wing Diver and use her Jump Pack to fly to a higher position and what ever other weapons and special abilities she comes equip with. As stated before, weapons unlock when you rescue specific characters, most of them are from other games that were made by the same development team/producers, others are completely new characters made specifically for this game with completely new weapons. once you unlock a character with a specific weapon you can mix and match weapons with other characters as long as they have the specific skills to use said weapon type, for example Rangers can't use Plasma Weapons but can use shotguns, assault rifles and explosives, wing divers can't use ballistic weapons like sniper rifles and assault rifles but can use laser and plasma weaponry, etc. Weapons and characters can be leveled up when you rescue similar characters from the field and if they have the same weapons. Example: rescuing another EDF 5 ranger will level up my EDF 5 Ranger and if he has the same Sniper rifle that too will be leveled up as well. and gaining armor for your characters seems to be automatic as you're no longer collecting Armor crates from the field and based on performance? it's hard to tell at the moment but at the end of each stage your team receives armor bonuses with the "MVP" seemingly gaining the most of the 4. lastly the gameplay feels fine with a combination of traditional EDF controls mixed with newer features like SP attacks that recharge the more enemies you kill or energy crates you collect when dropped. dialog and story are all still very much cheezey, but in a more Meta style, where characters are commenting on the craziness of what's happening and breaking the fourth wall with comments like "oh this is one of those 'see how tough the enemy is' battles where the creature can't be killed." and "Judging by the music playing in the background I'd say this is a proper boss battle so you should be able to take it down!" and other hilarious character quips like the wingdiver actually commenting how she's afraid of heights while using her jet pack and rangers from EDF 5 talking about how valient the infantry is and how they're ready to put down thier lives to defend mother earth from alien attacks...get it?All in all, fun game, don't care too much for the graphical redesign but it's not all bad considering it was first released on the Switch so it was kinda targeted at a more younger audience while still retaining that "all-ages" gameplay, and the fact that they mix content for all other EDF games in the franchise, including the Global Defense Force Games we never got in America is pretty cool. EDF Fans will like it, new comers to the Franchise might enjoy it as a run n' gunner.

_childDocuments_.review: World Brothers is a really fun and interesting entry into the EDF franchise. If you think this is just a voxel based re-skin, think again! This game features unique gameplay elements that sets it apart from other games in the franchise. The ability to bring in 4 fully customizable characters into a match is a very welcome addition as it allows you to come up with some awesome combos. And to be clear, each player does in fact bring in 4 characters, regardless if they are playing solo or multiplayer!That means that everyone can enjoy this feature at any given time. With that said, it's not all sunshine and roses. If you are planning on playing with KB+M, be warned. There is a very terrible and borderline broken mouse acceleration present in the game. It's so bad in fact that I have to wonder if it was even intended to function the way that it does to begin with.To help remedy this, be sure to turn down your mouse sensitivity in-game and raise your camera speed instead. Try playing with the two to find something that truly works for you. Aside for that, from the little time that I've played so far, I'm having a blast and truly do recommend this game to fans of the franchise and new players alike. The price is a little steep, but at least it's on sale for -20% for the time being. So pick it up while it's discounted, either now or in the future.Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions are very good. Game runs fine with no need to change graphics options on my PC. Combat feels good. Lots of weapons and accessories. Wide variety of skills. Lots of characters from the various EDF games. Characters level up by rescuing duplicates. Which unlocks their ability to use other weapons. This also adds replay value and may make a character you initially don't like work a little better. It seems pretty random though so it may be a while before you get the character you want. The story is silly and the characters lean heavily into their stereotypes like an old Saturday morning cartoon. Online play is pretty good if you can find a lobby. Didn't experience any lag but did disconnect a few times. I did not get any of the DLC.  The game is better than I expected. Might even be the most fun I have had with an EDF game. Warning: Use a controller. Mouse aim is busted.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Great game at its core, like a tribute to the EDF series, playing like a mashup of every game. Loads of characters and weapons to swap between in real time, still insanely fun if you already like the series.Main issues at launch are repetitive battle chants (switch to foreign VA, or mute voices altogether), and the flatout unacceptable mouse input. You may want to play with a controller if you dislike heavy acceleration with ini edits seemingly not working.
_childDocuments_.name: EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy casual racism? Killing bugs? Do you wish that when you play an Air Raider in EDF that you could also fly like a Wing Diver? Then this game is for you! There's a lot here that the game does right:-armor system is much better than mainline EDF; just use who you want and get kills-accessories are fun and add a nice way to really customize your guy-speaking of customizing, each of your 4 units can use 1 weapon. As you level them, they will unlock more and more weapon categories to use. -with 4 units, you can really adapt to any situation the game throws at you with good loadoutsall in all, the game is a pretty fun way to kill time until EDF 6.

_childDocuments_.review:
A new battlefield appears in the "EDF" series. This time, the world becomes the square Earth. The name of this game is "EARTH DEFENSE FORCE: WORLD BROTHERS". 

This game takes place in the 3D voxel world, which everything is made up of square pieces. In this world, the Earth is not round but square. And now, this voxel Earth is fallen apart into square pieces, breaking its blocky peace. But whether round or square, the Earth must be the Earth. So now, the player and the "EARTH DEFENSE FORCE" must rise to the occasion and save the day to restore a shattered Voxel Earth to one peace.
