_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fighting game fan? Instantly buy this because it respects your time, is fun, and has amazing onlineAre you new to fighting games? Well here it becomes a harder sale. This game stays mostly faithful to the series with 3v3 team building, complex inputs, and a buffer system that is a little less lenient than newer fighting games. Single player is severely lacking and the tutorial bits here are very bare bones. The game teaches you mechanics, gives you very basic missions, and then you're left to fend for yourself. Just keep this in mind if you are completely new. If you can overcome these barriers, then the game does a good job at rewarding your time and it feels very satisfying when you do.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I have yet to play online yet. Once I have done that, I will edit this review with my thoughts.The fifteenth entry of the King of Fighters series is finally here and my GOD it's excellent!First thing first, let's talk about game play: I love it! It's like they took the mechanics of KoF XIV, added the overall speed of KoF '03 & XI, made EX Specials use meter like in XIII, and added Street Fighter IV's Focus Attack in the form of Shatter Strike. One thing I should mention: People who play on keyboard... as Wrathra pointed out, the arrow keys, tab, and space bar can not be bound for some reason. This is rather annoying, but that's just a minor annoyance, and won't stop me from playing the game. 'Story Mode' was a bit misleading as I would expect... you know an actual story mode. But if that's what they want to call Arcade Mode, then whatever.Next thing I want to talk about is the fan service: SNK knows their audience well. The fact that they brought CYS and Ash Crimson back is astounding, but they also brought every single song from KoF's history into the game (Although, you have to beat 'Story Mode' with a specific set of characters in order to unlock one of them). On top of that, they also added songs from Fatal Fury, Samurai Shodown, Metal Slug, and other games within the Neo Geo library and SNK's earlier games. The fact that I can put some of my favorite KoF songs onto the stages is outstanding!Thirdly, graphic: Looks way better than KoF XIV. I can tell that SNK finally mastered making 3D models of their characters. I can look at Andy Bogard and recognize that it is him rather than seeing what he looks like in XIV (Where he looked tired or looked like an addict). Another thing: the flame and hit effects... honestly, the effects in general. I love the flair and flashiness of everything. I don't know what else to say. It looks cool.In my opinion, I'd say this game is just as good as The King of Fighters 2002 Unlimited Match, if not better. It's smooth, fast, responsive, and most importantly... FUN! It's not perfect, but I'm sure SNK will fix these issues that everyone else is having. Well, what are you waiting for? Buy the game man!!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to overstate how much the team dynamic has added to my enjoyment of KOFXV as a fighting game. There are dozens of characters and you get three mains. The gameplay reminds my uneducated self most of Street Fighter, though that could be because my team of Sakura-likes (Team New High School) can spam projectiles and panic with dragon punches all day long, and that's the extent of my capabilities in SNK's storied rival as well.A common complaint about KOFXV is the matchmaking, but the game decided I was rank 12, I did a ranked match for any connection, similar rank and similar region, and narrowly (when the third round ended, I wasn't sure who knocked out who because we both had slivers) bested a rank 11. The match was found quickly, and I don't think a more even match is theoretically possible. He narrowly beat me round one. I finished his first character off and narrowly lost round two, then finished off his second character and had a stroke of luck in round three for a virtual draw that erred in my favor. It's probably the best online experience I've had in a fighting game. Most of the time, I just log in and get annihilated. I think the connection quality was fine - I saw rollback 2 at one point, but that was about it. I've no complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely my favorite fighting game and the only thing close to it is under night.Yes, this game has been stuck in matchmaking hell for the longest time, crossplay has fixed that. Not only that, this meta is insane with how healthy it is right now. Nobody is in C tier and even the characters at the bottom of the ladder can still stand a chance against top tiers. The Bnbs of this game has been the most satisfying to me as well. Just the overall team building is satisfying as you have to decide who you want to put on point, mid, and anchor, especially with meter being the biggest factor in your damage output.~~~~~~BIG SPOILERS AREA BELOW~~~~~~Learning about the history and struggles of the series has been a huge journey and I would like to share what XV did right for the franchise. A big point is how XV was able to bring back characters originally dead. Team orochi being brought back since 97 (canon wise) is insane. Since orochi needed to be brought back, both yashiro and shermie needed to die while chris had to be the host for the evil god and he had to be killed be as well. It wasn't until the events of kof 14 that they were able to be brought back, making it more than two decades since their appearance. Team Khronen being a huge one as well since many fans thought he couldn't come back because of his heave inspiration from Akira. Originally being named as K9999, khronen's last appearance was in 2001 with him showing up in the 2002 dream match (which was later replaced by Nameless in the UM version.) Like team orochi, he's been missing from the franchise for around 2 decades.Lastly, bosses being brought back and ACTUALLY BEING LEGAL TO PLAY. Insane! The DLC as well has been a blast since they're bringing in goated characters like Dio Yubaki and Mr. Fist of the North Star (Yes these are actually their voice actors.) I could go on longer, but you get the idea.The soundtrack? The soundtrack is peak, sf6 wishes it had that level of rawness. As well as the new ost, xv brings back past songs as well. You can also customize your jukebox to play these songs during matches online.Is this game perfect? No. There are many reasons as to why people wouldn't buy this game But despite its shortcomings, I think everyone should try this game, especially on sale (15 dollars for peak!?)

_childDocuments_.review: The first fighting game that is finished and with full features and game modes in literally years. Please hold other big name fighting game developers to this standard in the future and purchase this game to support devs who actually care about delivering you a finished, quality product.The game play is also very good, with a variety of single and multiplayer modes to choose from. It keeps core KoF game play intact while spicing it up, but not going overboard with seemingly random mechanics that disrupt the pacing of the match like a lot of other games. Netplay is also very solid. Only really experience heavy disruption when playing against people from halfway across the world, or someone very obviously on WiFi.The roster is good as well with a solid representation of character types and play styles, the devs are constantly patching and improving on the minor bugs, and are releasing DLC teams regularly. SNK supports their titles for a long time, even if they don't do so well. With that being said, you can expect good things from the future regarding their newest flagship title, from their most well known IP.All in all I am very pleased with the overall package and my purchase of this video game, and I haven't felt that way about a new game, much less a fighting game in quite some time. New to fighting games or no, I would give this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember the days of playing Fatal Fury in the arcades. It wasn't easy to find like Street Fighter II, but the arcade cabinets where here and there. And seeing Samurai Shodown for the first time in the burger place about a 5 minute ride from my house...I was blown away.I remember going to a school buddy's house to see and experience his Neo Geo System when they were considered rare and super elite.I remember the first time seeing Fatal Fury 2. While watching the person playing choosing their character on the select screen..I already knew who I would be. And I remember getting laughed at for choosing that character: Mai. I remember going to the donut shop with my buddy every weekend because it had Mortal Kombat and Fatal Fury 2 side by side. He would play Mortal Kombat non-stop, and I was always on the Fatal Fury 2 machine. Just two doors down was Street Fighter II Rainbow Edition, and he and I would pop in there when the donut shop closed.And I remember picking up a Dreamcast and two games shortly after it came out: Soul Calibur and King of Fighters 98 (It was labeled as 99 then). I poured so many hours into that version.......and then my memories stop. After that there wasn't much in the KOF scene that could hold my attention.....or any fighting game scene for that matter. I think Capcom vs SNK really killed a lot of the magic for me. I tried a few more in the KOF series, but could never get into them.Until now....I am just amazed at the version of KOF. It really has an old school feel that just moves so smoothly. Back in the day it always felt like this series was weighed down with so much technical knowledge needed to really do well. This thought feels different. I am not saying that it isn't a technical fighter....but it feels like it caters to both the casual player and the veteran much better. When I jumped in I was already piecing out combos and what cancels well pretty quickly...almost second nature.And it has a great roster as well. Now I do miss few of my characters like Mature, Vice, and Kim Kaphwan....but seeing B. Jenet included made it an easy purchase for me. And Hoahmaru will be fun as well to fiddle with.There is one thing that bothers me a little about it. I also got thsi game because I read it has both 3v3 and 1v1. I like the idea of 1v1...however I have only found one way to play that way: through versus (which makes sense since the boss is set up for a 3 person party). The problem with versus is that you have to randomly select the next fighter for the computer each time. But in the end I can live with that. Also training works a little odd. i have yet to figure out how to get into it without a second controller or keyboard.All together I am really happy with the feel of this fighter and glad I added it to my library. I might not have a lot of time in it just yet...but I can already see myself playing this over Street Fighter easily. I should point out that I am an offline player only. That is more the old school style that I enjoy..just in case that may change how you see everything I said.So now, if you don't mind, it is time for me to make some new SNK memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of KOF94-2000. I played KOF98 every day for around 3 years. Hated KOF2001-2002. 2003 was okay-ish. I liked KOF14 somewhat. Kinda regret buying this. I thought I could deal with the parts I don't like, but they are pretty painful. Better than the new Samurai Spirits/Shodown, though.- Loads impressively fast, even without SSD. Samurai Shodown is the opposite.- Visuals are pretty nice, although somehow still feels a little ugly somehow. I've seen other people complain about the visuals.- One of the very few recent games with female characters who are not repulsively hideous. No exaggeration. This was honestly one of my first thoughts of this game.- Huge cast with lots of returning characters. Free character updates, too. Some have free alt outfits thrown in, which is VERY NICE.Not memorable at all. Some tracks are downright painful, especially the last boss theme. Probably the first KOF with a BAD boss theme. I used to listen to KOF94-2000 music all the time. Still do, occasionally. Sometimes I listen to 14. Never felt like listening to 15. None of the tracks even stuck in my head.The bosses were one of the big attraction points of classic KOF for me. I'm sure I'm not the only one, because I know lots of people love how cool classic KOF bosses are. Current SNK keeps screwing that up. Their recent bosses feel like lazy afterthoughts with minimal effort. To be fair, it's still better than other recent fighting games that often don't even have bosses (or arcade mode) anymore.I'm talking about in-combat, not the mocapped poses and super moves. I played lots of KOF14 on PS4 and I was always impressed by how they managed to faithfully capture the feel of the original 2d animation. This game feels like they broke most of those animations. For example, IIRC, Kula's jump animation has her finish her entire flip animation from the moment she starts a jump, before she's even reached the peak of the jump.This is actually a common problem in a lot of recent fighting games. I wouldn't be surprised if SF4/5/6 animation staff worked on this game. Modern 3d animators often fail at aerial animation, ie. animation with gravity applied. In many recent fighting games, this is especially obvious when jumping or falling. Characters often flip too early or too late.Falling animations are sometimes animated with unintended movement built-into the animation (as a result of bad axes for each frame of animation), on top of the in-game falling gravity. This makes characters look like they are moving in multiple directions when falling, which is objectively terrible.Special moves like the iconic Dragon Punch often look strange because they are timed to spin around too early or too late. In SF6, Luke's jumping uppercut has a lengthy landing animation as if he's floating to the ground and smoothly transitioning from air-to-ground, instead of heavily landing from a jump. Normally, you would cut from falling anim to landing anim, not animate a smooth landing transition from air-to-ground.This game takes the jumping uppercut problem to another level. When doing jumping uppercuts in this game, they suddenly get a huge speed-up on the way down. It looks ridiculously bad. It's like someone on the dev team wanted to make dragon punch whiffs unpunishable, or something. It's really painful to look at.Maybe this problem stands out to me because I'm an animator, or because I played almost every fighting game from the past 30 years, or grew up playing 2d games.I've been wondering for a while, why do modern game animators keep failing at basic aerial animation? My current theory goes like this: In the past, most games were 2d (X/Y axis), and so jumping/gravity was super important, and developers got GOOD at it. Nowadays, most games are 3d (X/Y/Z axis, primarily X/Z) and often don't even have jumping (Y axis).Indeed, if you talk to modern gamers, many hate platformers because they have trouble timing jumps. This probably carries over to modern developers - they simply don't have a feel for good aerial gravity.Another possible factor is how fighting games gradually trended towards floaty air juggles over the years. Many fighting games also became more simplified in animation timing and velocity calculation, because that's easier to balance, and the end-user often can't tell the difference.You know that problem with 3d animation tweening, where it's hard to tell which frame has what attributes? This game has that problem. KOF14 didn't, as far as I can recall. Again, I'm pretty sure I'm not the only one saying this.AI has a dumb exploit where you trick them into doing a dodge and then punish. KOF14 has the same problem. You can beat the last boss in this with a similar trick. Kinda reminds me of beating Kintaro in MK2 by spamming punch until time ran out. Except they patched that later. I know not many people care about the AI, but still. To be fair, it's still better than the AI in most other fighting games, which tend to be extremely bare minimum.I don't like what they did to Rugal. His Dark Genocide Cutter is based on KOF2002, where he moves forward for the 2nd kick, and that feels/looks awful to me. He also does not have his regular God Press or Kaiser Wave (my favorite moves), and has a stupid-looking eye beam attack that is way too useful. Player Rugal also does not seem to have his grab and pummel super.I don't like what they did to Orochi Yashiro. His throws used to feel AMAZING in KOF97 and 98. They feel awful here. You know it's bad animation when it consistently fails to convey a satisfying feeling of weight. Especially fatal for a grappler. They significantly changed his commands, too. I don't get why/how his throws can/can't grab/combo. I shouldn't have to look it up, that's not intuitive. I'm guessing it's because one version is used in combos, and the other cannot. Dumb design, if true.I don't like the GUI/presentation/announcer, etc. I also keep hearing that the online is broken. I haven't tried it yet.Again, as someone who was a big fan of classic KOF (being a fan doesn't mean blindly supporting everything), I really can't stand how this game feels. I tried to like it, many times. Almost every recent 2d fighter fails at capturing the feel of basic movement, jumping/falling gravity and combat/feedback. If you don't notice any of these issues, then feel free to play this game and enjoy it. I can't, because I have decades of memories of classic KOF/other 2d fighters. It's easier to enjoy stuff if you have no memories or experience of better times.When I complain about modern fighters feeling bad, people like to talk E-sports viability and balance. I personally don't care if a game has good balance if it feels like crap to play. It's like people saying a game "gets better later". What's the point if the start is terrible? Or there are fundamental problems that never go away?Not to promote Melty Blood: Type Lumina, but it's the only recent fighter I've played that feels like a classic 2d fighter, with satisfying weighty combat and movement. But it has its own problems (eg. freezing/crashing lobbies, default filtering anyone outside of your bathroom, and actively alienating their fanbase).I don't understand why some developers go 99% of the way making a good game, and then drop the ball hard on the last fundamental 1% and forever refuse to fix those issues.Oh, and TO BE FAIR, it is kinda hard to go back to a classic clunky fighter after playing a speedy fluid mobile one like Melty. But that doesn't explain why KOF94-2000 feel far better than this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Latest entry in the King of Fighters series. I mostly play Street Fighter, so my perspective will come from that of a SF player.The game can be intimidating at first, especially for newcomers. Learning a single character is already hard enough, let along learning three different characters to fill a team. Not to mention dealing with the dynamics of 6 different characters in a single match. 4 different jumps??It's natural that these may seem like a tall task, and it is. But there are a bunch of guides online from passionate players that will help ease these starting pains, from channels such as Maximilian Dood, Rooflemonger, as well as the various KOF communities on social media are all eager to help you learn. And boy, one the game clicks, it clicks.Rollback netcode. Crossplay. Matchmaking (allegedly) fixed. What are you even waiting for?   - Game is visually underwhelming, especially coming from something like SF6, T8 or MK1. Up to personal taste   - Standard FG single player, and I mean standard as in pre-SF6. You get an arcade mode (with admittedly nice cutscenes), but if you're not invested in the lore or characters then you're out of luck.   - Relatively low active player base, the lowest out of the big FGs. Although crossplay and rollback does mitigate this, it's something to think about.

_childDocuments_.review: This latest King of Fighters is pretty much more of the same, which I mean as a compliment. The series has the core of what it's about down so well by this point that it can ♥♥♥♥ around the margins with combo mechanics and weird character designs as much as it wants and still have a rock-solid game at the end of the day. And KoF XV is especially rock-solid, having more or less resolved the aesthetic issues of the last game and the meter-balancing issues of the last two to produce a game that's both attractive and fun to make combos in. The roster is also pretty good this time around, although the series leans more heavily now on characters based around mixups and setplay than twists on the series' idiosyncratic neutral game than I personally would like. In fact, the game overall is objectively very good but just something I'm not subjectively interested in; the characters are a bit too anime for me, the combos are a bit too long and central to the meta, and the input detection just doesn't agree with me at all for some reason, despite being much more forgiving this time around. However, even if I don't care for it that much as far as KoF games go, it's still a great product, and definitely worth giving a shot if you're at all interested in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fantastic, really well produced and a lot of fun. The netcode is great when you connect with opponents -- obviously it works perfectly when both players are using ethernet, but even on the worst connections (known as Level 1 connections) the rollback works fantastically to keep things running. Lots of great characters, the 3 on 3 format is fun, and it's generally got a lot for all kinds of players. However, the matchmaking itself is borked -- on a good day you'll be able to connect with only one or two opponents, can only fight them, and otherwise are left queuing for a match for minutes on end. On a bad day, you're simply left waiting infinitely for an opponent to be matched. As a newbie to KOF, I only desire playing against others, and the best way to get matches against a number of opponents in fighting games is to play Ranked Mode to match up with others at your skill level -- with KOF XV's broken matchmaking, I am very lucky to even have one opponent when I look for a match, and whomever I get is simply the only person the game will pit me against until I quit out of the game and reload, forced to spin the "will I even find an opponent" roulette once more. The broken matchmaking is the only thing making this review a Thumbs Down, and it's really so bad that it changes an otherwise positive experience into a poor one. Definitely pick the game up if you have other friends playing, since you can easily get into private matches with them, but fighting randoms is broken.

_childDocuments_.review: KAY OH EFF FIFTEEN is finally here! And with a tagline like "Shatter All Expectations" you'd think that this game has to be pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good for the devs to confidently rock a tagline like this. Well it's been over a month now and does it "Shatter All Expectations"? The game is a huge step up over KOFXIV especially when it comes to the graphics while it doesn't reach the level of KOFXIII ( and it probably never will) It's still great nonetheless and not the PS2 graphics everyone alot say it is with the exception of the effects of the special moves. Most of them are decent while others are downright terrible. Dolores was a character I was very excited to play but upon watching her gameplay trailer and the effects on the mudlike thingy or whatever, I was instantly turned off. Don't know what went wrong there.The roster aside from the inclusion of CYS, Chizuru & Krohnen is hella boring and a step down from KOFXIV which I already thought was kinda disappointing both in quality and quantity. Minor nitpick but even the team compositions which the devs said would be shaken up quite a bit aren't really all that different. The DLC roster of season 1 which is 13 characters is way more interesting & "Expectation Shattering" than most of the 39 included in the base roster. Props on them for giving away Rugal for free though, I'll give them that.The gameplay is where I'm most positive about. It is interesting, fun and overall a good time. And all they did was not lock EX moves behind Max Mode and added another mechanic called Shatter Strike which I honestly don't see used that much but will probably catch on as the meta develops. Max Mode also costs 2 bars to activate now which I'm not really a fan of as I would've loved to see the degenerate ♥♥♥♥ people could come up with coupled with the EX changes but was probably done for balancing purposes my tiny brain could not comprehend.Story mode is there and it's nothing too special. Quite forgettable infact not as good as the last 3 Sagas imo. Tutorial is decent, gets the job done and training mode is also great but could use some qol improvements which I'm sure will be added over time. And finally fan of DJ Station bringing back countless SNK soundtracks but not a fan of unlocking them which in all honesty is a chore and probably could've been handled better.And finally the online. Nowadays could possibly make or break the game. The reason why SamSho died and it still hurts me to this date. So what of KOFXV? The netcode is actaully pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. played plenty of matches in rooms, casual and a few in ranked and it was great. But.. the matchmaking is pretty bad.. it's horrible infact. Can't find poeple to play with despite many being online and have to wait from 30 minutes to an hour to get games especially in ranked . SNK did say they are adressing this issue but have yet to do anything about it and honestly it worries me. Hopefully they will not share the same fate as SamSho.Despite me being pretty harsh about the game. I do love this game. I enjoy playing it when it works, discovering crazy ♥♥♥♥ and playing with other people. But until and unless they fix the matchmaking issues and the various other PC issues I cannot in good faith recommend this to anyone. And I really hope they do so soon cause I for one am looking forward to Rugal, Team Southtown and what more this game has to offer.- Game does not shatter expectations but game is fun nonetheless. Needs to fix the various issues plaguing it before it can be recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing The King of Fighters since 1995, starting with KOF94, when I was a kid in the arcades in Mexico, and at the local corner marts. I've seen this game evolve over several years and improve with each iteration, sometimes taking steps forward and sometimes taking steps back. As time has passed and I've gotten older, I find that the fighting game series that I will always truly love is KOF. Games like Capcom VS SNK 2 or Tekken 7 may individually be some of my favorite games, but my heart is always with KOF.That said, my interest in the series as a whole simply waned quite a bit in recent years. KOF XIV, while a fun entry early on, simply didn't manage to hold my attention through its full competitive lifespan. KOF 2002 UM was a fun diversion, but the style of its gameplay was never my scene. KOF 98, my previous absolute favorite, felt a little too different in ways I didn't like when it became KOF 98 UM. Ultimately, I waited for the release of KOF XV with some trepidation. That said, the betas for XV really did help alleviate many of my fears: the characters moved well! The netcode was a little strange but was basically fixed entirely during the second beta. The gameplay was simply exactly what I expected out of KOF, and my excitement began to swell.Upon release, I can say this with absolute certainty, in a way that I am sure will get me the derision of some of my peers, but I have to shout it from the rooftops: KOF XV is my favorite KOF game of all time.It certainly is my favorite aesthetically, even despite its shortcomings (the VFX can go from "pretty OK", such as Iori's fireballs, Kyo's Orochinagi flare, and the effects on Isla's hands... to "this is the ugliest thing I've ever seen"—the block sparks are super ugly and several fireballs just look hideous, like Ryo's and Robert's). The UI is incredible to look at. All the features, like being able to select oldschool KOF tracks to listen to while you play, feel awesome. The soundtrack fits the theme of the game very well. I will never REALLY be that into Max Powers as an announcer, but he's growing on me (much to my chagrin, not gonna lie; he's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ extra). The character models are such a huge improvement over XIV and the game has sort of established its own visual style that I just really do find appealing. Just... it's a good-looking game, hell. It's definitely a PS4-era game in terms of looks, sure. But it looks great within that context, and that's what I love.As for how it functions? Let's break it down.- You will hear this a lot: the game plays as though they took the good lessons from KOF XIV and applied them, while fixing all of the pitfalls from that game. Gone is 2B 2B 2B into MAX activate for every situation.- The game moves like you expect KOF to; if you're a veteran, it will be a tiny adjustment.- The lobby system is incredible, with rotating lines, automatic spectating, and the ability to change a bunch of settings mid-spectating.- The matchmaking is a little suspect, but it works well enough and is a few fixes away from being perfect; it may need some automatic firewall assistance though!- The online play feels amazing, although some matches feel a little rough if people are playing on older PCs and don't use mods to fix the issues (I suggest a "Potato" mod if your computer isn't too hot).- This is the easiest KOF has ever been to get into, without feeling like it's surrendering too much of its own style to accomodate newer players. - The UI is fairly responsive, but they kinda went overboard with the animations of everything adding a bunch of friction to what should be a fast few button presses to get somewhere. Closing the pause menu shouldn't take as long as it does, for instance.- The move list could stand to have more information (like super cancel information), but it is rather informative.- The tutorial could stand to have some improvements: KOF plays a very specific way and it would be a lot better to be able to direct people to a good, functional tutorial instead of relying on, say, Dandy J to bear the brunt of educating newer players. Still, it's pretty solid for what it is and covers the very bare necessities to learn KOF.- The training UI features, such as the Frame ++/+/=/-/-- indicators in training are excellent, as is the frame-counted input system.- The auto-recorded match replays are an awesome feature and will be helpful to players leveling up, and for people looking to create game content.Some nerdier nitty gritty stuff:- The PC version has the least input lag of all the versions at an average of 2.5 frames of input delay, if you care. The next best would be the Series X version, followed by the PS4 version played on a PS5.- The PC version doesn't have an option to disable VSync. Look up online how to turn it off! It involves a settings file. This honestly is best if you have a 144hz monitor with low input delay.- The matchmaking in ranked works best if you're sitting in a training lobby. The regionality indicator is less important than the connection quality setting. Leaving it at 3+ but letting any region or any rank fly is the best if you're trying to play ranked to get better faster.- Depending on your connection, you are probably fine playing against people with up to 150ms ping so long as they're wired. Experiment with room lobbies to find your favorite.This is the easiest fighting game recommend I have ever made in my life. KOF 2002 UM is perhaps the best of the classic remade versions of KOF. This is perhaps the best version of KOF, over all. I cannot recommend it highly enough. See you online!

_childDocuments_.review: so I fee l like I should preface this with the fact that KoF02UM is literally the game that got me into fighting games in any meaningful way, which means the bar was really high from the get-go, and that when I say this is the best KoF since 02UM it means a lot. I'm not gonna go into an essay on the various games since then in here since that doesn't tell you anything about XV but this is the first one that has captured (for me) 02UM's sense of depth to everything.They managed to preserve the accessibility that 14 offered by way of Rush combos and simplified inputs without feeling like cheapening the experience. And while 14 still felt like a KoF because the movement mechanics were in-tact, a lot of movesets felt pared back or unfinished; that isn't the case here. In fact that's one of this game's biggest strengths, the newer mechanics (EX moves, shatter strike) coupled with more fleshed out movesets allow for a whole range of expression in fighting style that I think hasn't been around in the past several entries. Everyone's moveset feels really well thought out, with moves kind of moving logically to their followup specials and supers. Each character feels like they clearly have a function they were designed with, but all but the most extreme specialists have enough in their kits to avoid being too predictable, and allow them to fight on other terms if they need to. The movement mechanics that define KoF are still here and still feel good to use, despite the switch to 3D the characters still move with the pace and tempo that players would come to expect.On the subject of 3D: the game looks really really good. The character models in the backgrounds don't, but everything else is genuinely visually pleasing in a way that 14 most definitely wasn't. With that said, I got a not-insignificant amount of screen tearing during cutscenes and climax moves, which I assume is because there's really not a ton of visual/graphics options in the game right now. I'm hoping that's because this is a day one review that they'll eventually add some more options on that front, primarily V-Sync. The only other main issue I have with the game is that the tutorial just, misses stuff. Like KoF has a lot of series-specific mechanics that aren't really covered by it, and I seriously recommend checking out some of those youtube videos about tips or combo mechanics for the game because they're not really spelled out for you otherwise. You can sort of gleam some from the trial challenges (they actually have a few this time around that you could use in a real game!) but close Heavies aren't really explained, nor are the way some moves become cancellable inside of a combo.Anyway, I wanted to also mention that the game has the feel of a celebration of the franchise and of SNK's history (furthered by the DLC outfits for Terry and Leona, as well as the Garou Team DLC). This roster has several really popular characters, a few of which have absent for literal decades from the franchise (the last time Chizuru was in a game, I wasn't born yet). They also have the soundtracks to every previous KoF game, as well as Metal Slug, Samsho, Fatal Fury, etc. in the gallery to really drive home that this is like, a capstone piece, and I'm really glad that the game itself is good enough to hold up all that historical heft. If you like KoF, I super recommend it. If you like fighting games, I super recommend it. If you just wanted a jukebox to play weirdly specific video game music, I guess I recommend it as well. Oh also the bosses are a lot cooler than they've been recently.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun fighting game with its mobility, offensive and defensive options as the highlights of its gameplay. Sure it's not as pretty compared to other current gen fighting games like Guilty Gear Strive, but it looks fine during actual play; the characters move smooth and fluid in action. Newcomers might be intimidated by legacy skills, having to learn three characters, or KOF's inputs, but like most fighting games, matches become rewarding or just plain fun once you get the hang of it. Not to mention KOF got some banger ost's, adding a whole vibe to each match.However, the biggest con at the moment is the matchmaking. Honestly, it's an absolute disappointment and letdown for a $60 game. It takes forever to find a match, if not just won't. SNK announced plans to implement crossplay in the near future which should help by enlarging the overall pool of players, but who knows...we can only cross our fingers for now. The plus side though is online connections have been great and performed without much issues so far.Despite its flaws and looks, KOF is still a fun, fast paced fighting game. Give it a shot.Now go get wrapped around by Shermie's thighs.
_childDocuments_.name: THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV

_childDocuments_.review: It's good! By golly, it's good. It's certainly true to KoF, with a great roster (sorry if your favorite didn't make it in, I'm missing some as well), great visuals (no, it's not MK11 and it never will be, SNK doesn't have WB money), and great music (new and old)!No issues playing on stick or pad, some keyboard folks might be bothered and not being able to bind space bar as of right now. 1440p is missing for some reason, not sure why - game looks good without it just run in 1080 or downscale 4k.Netcode is nice and playable, you wil feel it on poor and/or distant connections that but will always be true. For regular matchmaking it's very nice and infinitely better than what they put out in the recent Samurai Shodown. Lots of story endings and secret team endings to unlock, combo trials, unlockable soundtracks and... well, fighting. Nothing too fabulous beyond the excellent fighting package but if you're familiar with KoF you know what to expect.For newcomers, I can't tell you this game is *easy*, but it is fairly simple to pick up at the starting level and start having fun, it is definitely the most accesible KoF package so far without sacrificing the higher level of play.Just watch the gameplay - you should know if you're going to like it or not already.

_childDocuments_.review: As a primarily 3D fighting game player, I can say I really enjoy this take on the 2D genre. Many recent 2D games kind of funnel you into one playstyle or archetype that is good at higher levels of competition. Where KOFXV is different is the viability of styles: zoning, control, grappler, rushdown etc. If you are someone who can't get into 2D games or Anime games due to the heavier rushdown or the "limitations" the game can sometimes put on the player, I suggest giving this one a look as it is a very diverse cast and a very free-form and expressive style of fighting game, even more than its competitors.As a closing note, I will say the execution is harder than what you may be used to, but easier than the older versions, so don't get discouraged at the potential combo difficulty you may face, it isn't the be-all-end-all in the game and pokes are more than strong enough to win full matches!

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm just old now, but KOF seems to have lost some of its charm since it went 2.5D. There's nothing major going wrong, but designs for new characters are becoming increasingly overwrought, and I'm not a fan of the "mash LP to instacombo" mechanic that carried over from KOF XIV. Nor am I a fan of forking over extra cash to complete a character roster, even if that roster is really good. Despite these unwelcome and continuing breaches of convention, our Saudi overlords have seen fit to resume gracing us with one of the most fundamentally sound fighting franchises available. Yes, KOF XV is a good game, one that doesn't let its new touches overshadow the elements that gave it the staying power to keep it quasi-relevant for 30 years. The series in 2022 still requires the skills that it required in 1998, and that most fighting games used to require. While most see this game as a diversion to be played when you need a rest from games with a larger playerbase, KOF XV is actually better than some of those games. It requires a better grasp of fundamentals, it has better balance, and matches have an undeniable flow that comes from forcing players to build up to and wind down from their most damaging attacks rather than forcing a constant contest to be the first to get them to connect. KOF XV doesn't offer a whole lot that KOF XIV didn't, but the series has always been about incremental progress, and this installment still gets an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best modern fighting game on the market in my opinion. It has the best mechanics, very solid netplay with both rollback and crossplay and a great selection of fighters (Athena and Mai, my beloved queens...). My only complaint is that its single player content is quite lacking unfortunately, featuring only an arcade mode, combo trials (5 per character and they're honestly not very hard compared to the torture chambers of XIII for example) and a boss fight mode where you can get stomped once again by Omega Rugal and Goenitz. Highly recommend to fighting game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best KOF games since 98UM and 02UM. Great roster of characters with a lot of variety. Easiest KOF to get into and play casually, but still has that depth for the people who want to take the dive. Single player content is lacking, but that is common with most fighting games. DJ Station is a really nice feature with a lot of custom options, but still doesn't have the Mark of the Wolves soundtrack.The matchmaking and player count is a hot topic about this game, but I find this to be quite common with KOF. Every one that I have played has had low player counts and very hard to find anyone through the game's matchmaking. There are a lot of good discord communities that still very actively play this game across all platforms.I would recommend this game highly if you are into KOF gameplay or the characters. If you are looking to just play a fighting game and not specifically looking for what KOF offers... I say just wait for Street Fighter 6 or something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent fighter, and possibly one of my favorite KOFs. Easily in my top 5, and possibly even in my top 3. I already put more time into this one in a day than I have other new fighters that I've tried that have come out in the past year and I'm making time to play it every night. The game feels better balanced at launch than a lot of fighters; it feels more like a 2.0 or even 2.5+ patch in terms of that. Roster is wide and varied with a lot of fan favorites(it's not perfect, but it's really strong), and promises to grow. Graphics are vibrant. Netcode is rather excellent as well. The game has enough stuff to unlock for a casual player(it's not the most robust story mode, but every team has an ending and there are other special edit team cards to unlock as well), and the usual KOF meat for veterans who like the competitive angle will find a lot of what they like here. Highly recommended for anyone looking to pick up a fighting game with a large roster, vibrant look and fast playstyle.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tight. It leaves room for emergent gameplay and personal expression, and doesn't treat the player with kid gloves: unnecessary restrictions and over-engineered gameplay begone. KOFXV has a ton of interesting universal mechanics, a rich roster of complex and diverse characters, and – perhaps most important of all – is obviously crafted by a team of people who dearly love the franchise and its legacy. If SNK is able to carry this momentum by continuing to support this game and its playerbase in the years to come, this might just become one of the all-time great KOFs.

_childDocuments_.review: It does have season passes (well, "team passes"), but this is one of the few fighting games that is not openly going straight for you wallet, having 90% of its content as DLC, or doing shameless things like putting ADS (let alone ads on SINGLE PLAYER content) between matches.Also, SNK is one of the few japanese developers that is not trying to pander to "western sensibilities", so the fanservice this franchise always had, its all there.Also, the game is incredible well optimized.On the cons side, there arent that many people playing online, and it when it comes to single player content, it has the minimum; a ladder, some combo missions, and that's it, because the "boss challenge" was just Rugal, they never added any other boss...you can tell by some aspects that this was a budget title (still no excuse to not include some art galleries), but as I said above, it doesnt go for all the shameless tactics most fighting games are going for these days.
_childDocuments_.name: THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay feels right, and the online experience has never been better. My favorite edition up to this point was XIII but now I see the difference a decent online mode makes.Visually the game is goofy, most characters look good but the VFX is so over the top. The only real improvement besides prettier characters is the purge of cinematic camera, now exclusive to Climax moves. Still some visual aspects are a downgrade from XIV, which is kinda unforgivable. I guess they really wanted the game to feel "epic" huh. It didn't work for me.I see a lot of articles complaining about story mode or the lack of tag system. ♥♥♥♥♥ this is KoF. They've done it all before and in the end stuck with what works for the series. XV is quite successful in this sense, it's fresh entry for the new gaming generation. It doesn't need ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tag teaming, or an exclusive, cinematic story mode. It isn't that deep.The XV cast could've included more new or redesigned characters, given that they had 6 years to work on this, and still how much has been copy/pasted from XIV. The roster is solid but it feels like another dream match with a couple new characters, as if SNK had gone indie and this is what the dev team had resources to make. Unfortunately most DLCs are going to be cash grabs so I doubt we're gonna see anything fresh or exciting from them.
_childDocuments_.name: THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV

_childDocuments_.review: As a casual gamer, fighting games are unique. While it is true I just pick up and play most fighting games, with friends and family just to have fun. Each franchise has something to offer and The King of Fighters franchise has done a great job for the loyal fan base and new comers a like. This latest entry and proven that SNK is doing a great job with visuals, controls, and a solid online experience. To start off, this game looks great and feels amazing. To be honest, if you're looking to just jump in and be competitive be sure to practice. Yes I'm talking about practice, choose your three and practice to get good. It can be a bit intimidating with all the joystick/D-pad input and timing. Rest assured its a great feeling when you understand the fundamentals of this fighting game. Translates so well when playing online, played several matches no "lag" or other issue so far. So playing online was a solid experience for myself. I just wish we got animated endings with movement, not just still shots. Oh well other than that, this chapter of KoF is closed. Lets see where they go from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone online uses auto combos. This is as of writing this my first experience with KOF. I absolutely love the mechanics in this game. They require skill and good execution to really master. But personally, I think auto combos kinda ruin it for me. Why do a special move after a command normal when you can just spam the X button and get a combo. Yes I know that the damage is lowered with auto combos, but does it really matter when they can be easily spammed? But either way I still recommend this game to anyone willing to learn the game's mechanics rather than just hit one button over and over again. I encourage you to give your feedback in the comments as I would love to hear others opinions on this.

_childDocuments_.review: After the new Fatal Fury trailer's hype, I wanted to try out SNK's previous games. I already played KoF XIV before and loved it, though I was never really good at it, and thought this game would be a huge upgrade over it but I was left disappointed.The game finally allows EX moves outside of Max mode but I felt like that was the only pro. There isn't much of a visual improvement, some characters/maps look better in XIV and some characters/maps look better here and the gameplay overall doesn't feel that much different. The roster was greatly improved even though it's much smaller, a lot of the weirdos from XIV have been removed to nobody's surprise.What really killed it for me was the lack of offline/singleplayer modes. Where's survival? Time trial? We get a 'Boss rush' mode as an alternative that has.. two bosses. This game really wants you to play online, which in my opinion is a huge detriment to the game. I get that fighting games need to build a player base that's consistently playing online to find matches but having no other option than online-play isn't the way to do this.This wasn't the way to go for XV, even at a discount of 12eur I felt I wasn't getting my money's worth. Thankfully Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves is going in a different direction with its RPG mode and character customization.

_childDocuments_.review: Has "almost" everything you'd want in a fighting game:- Rewarding Combos- Large starting roster- Customizable online lobbies with spectate modes and rotations.- Online Training Mode- Replay archive- Legacy Soundtracks and able to customize per stage- Good netcode using rollback (Trash internet will stay trash)- Matchmaking filters and allows you to see connections before going into matches.- Devs care about the longevity of the game by providing somewhat frequent updates. (So far)What it lacks/struggles with:- Story mode is somewhat disappointing, its becomes a repeat of the previous game with less plot. - Trails although teaches you essentials of what a character can do it is not very hard and I want there to be more. But this game encourages you to lab which I don't mind.- Matchmaking has issues with some people taking extended periods of time and getting errors (I don't have that problem. You have to be glued to the opponent to start them with your close standing punch and since you're probably used to start with light crouches or close heavies it's not super easy to start them by mistake. Since most characters have close heavies with around four frames of startup (yes, far heavies are super slow and unsafe, but close heavies start superfast are good hit confirms and can be linked to command normals for safety, apparently) and anyways you can always link your close standing light punch to a command normal and manually input a combo that does more damage with the same amount of resources, I wouldn't say that this game is autocombo hell like dragonball fighterz. There's a single autocombo (with four possible endings), it's not optimal (I think the damage is severely scaled), it's just there to help ease people into the games when they are already worried about learning everything else and sometimes just need a button to mash.

_childDocuments_.review: Not for the faint of heart, KOF XV is a great 3v3 fighter filled with 90s design sensibilities. If you don't have previous experience with the series it will be *grinding.* Crossover skills from other 2D fighting games will be rare to come by here.Execution and movement leave little room for error (although SNK have been much more lenient with this iteration than previous games), but thanks to the universality of those mechanics among the cast, once they're gotten down everyone in the game becomes exponentially easier to play.That being said, that grind is extremely rewarding, and you will see tangible improvement every time you play. Add in great netcode, fun character designs and a fantastic soundtrack and you have a recipe for a fighting game that will give you years of playing time if you stick with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe a 2 out of 5 if you like fighting games, 3 out of 5 if you're a longtime fan. Everyone else, this ain't the one. As a full-price game, this is a major let-down.Pros+ Online netcode works well in matches (rollback with ping on the screen? nice)+ Solid launch roster (39 characters with at least 14+ more coming)+ Core game has seen some good additions, like EX moves out of max mode and shatter strikesCons- Bare-bones tutorials (the same low-effort garbage you've seen from most fighting games for 10+ years) and combo trials (literally nothing new or expanded upon since kof 14, which was less than 13 had)- Graphics and presentation are 2 gens behind the industry standard (remember when fighting games used to be cutting edge? This isn't like that at all)- Graphical problems (some exclusive to PC, including crazy tears in character models when moving)- Matchmaking often pairs you up with people well below your connection standards*Edit: Halfway through the first season of content (though a second season is confirmed) and the devs have come out and said "well we can't fix it, so is it really even broken?" (not kidding). Finding a match has gotten nearly impossible. When I did get matched up, it was usually with someone in Central America playing in NA server region so the netcode couldn't save it.- Nonsensical story that barely even appeals to longtime fans, even after taking time to catch myself up via youtube and fan pages (i did that for GG Strive and had a good time, this... this is just not entertaining)-Input precision is far too demanding for a modern fighting game (i don't mind strict combo timing, but miss one direction in a move that requires you hit a quarter circle and then a full half circle in just a few frames and you're not getting that move, ever. especially frustrating when paired up with someone playing with over 100ms ping over their wifi)Honestly, this just feels like KOF 14.5. How SNK took such a giant step back in design compared to Samurai Showdown (the 2019 one) is beyond me. I almost wish they had just added rollback netcode like this game has into SS and left this in development for another year (Edit: Okay they announced rollback for Samsho, but so far they haven't gotten it to work there either). It seems like no matter what, these guys just can't ship a solid overall product. My sincere advice to the SNK team is to just let Gaurd Crush Games (of Streets of Rage 4 fame) make the Garou sequel like they asked to and just try Samurai Showdown again with this quality of online while in-match. (Edit: They did announce a Garou sequel a few months after launch, look at me manifesting)For fighting games, this level of quality and effort isn't acceptable for 60 dollars anymore. They get extra points off for bundling the DLC characters in teams and charging 15 bucks for all 3 with no option to just get one or two of them. I would've called this an "okay" fighting game if it had come out in 2010 or if the base price was around 30 bucks. In 2022 for 60 dollars, it's just a bad product.You are going to see a LOT of people standing up for this game online, but the fact is there's no one playing it. They're also going to say a lot of racist things to you if you're not from Latin America or Japan, so be ready for that. SteamCharts says there's less than 1k people online for it daily, but I'm personally surprised when I seem more than 600. Crossplay was added too long after launch, and the releases of Street Fight and Tekken put the final nails in this coffin for all but the most hardcore fans. I have no idea why you would choose to play this over any other fighting game unless you're just absolutely obsessed with this franchise. If you are, have fun with the gooner fans, because that's all that's left.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to register here my review about this game, for those who are interested in my opinion about this version of the King of Fighters XV. Take a drink, it may take you some time.I've been playing king of fighters since the Neo Geo era, where I got to know the game, so I feel confident enough to give my honest opinion, which may displease those who think differently. So be prepared to maybe feel displeased with this review. ______________________________________________________________________Prós: Good character and scenario design, plus a wide variety of fighters to play with. Except for the design of the special moves, which were so horrible and very amateurishly designed, to the point that it looks like the fighters are shooting jets of orange and grape soda.Beginner players who have never played previous versions of The King of Fighters can easily play and win in this game.Cons:Bad Ultimate Moves system. In this game, you have 05 special movement bars, which fast and easily fill up every atack you land, making the game unbalanced. There is no need to be skilled in game, just hit any blow and do in sequence the specials that can all be linked together  with blows EX, ending the fight in seconds. Best part, you can do it all just smashing auto combo button.There is no solid system to break the opponent's guard, just a useless guard break bar. each blow you deliver causes damage to the guard bar, however, if the opponent dodges or runs away from you, this bar recovers very quickly. Practically a useless bar that does not fulfill the purpose it have, motivating turtling strategy untill feel confortable to take an action against the enemy.There is no effective counter system to prevent skill spam pressure. Despite having 05 bar of specials, none of them give you the option of sacrificing them to deliver a special counterattack in case of suffering pressure in the defense of characters with very fast recovery inputs like Vanessa for example. An "Alpha Counter" like in Street Fighter Alpha, would solve this problem right here. The least you can do is cancel roll sacrificing one bar, but depending on the character you are facing, the roll is useless, as the opponent still manages to counterattacking and killing you with all their super bars.The characters' hitboxes are, in most cases, broken, large characters that should be easily hit, often leave unharmed when receiving aerial attacks, the case only gets worse when it comes to skinny, feminine and small characters.All games have a system of pushing the opponent for a short time, when he receives a blow in defense, some are even imperceptible by amateur players, but in KOF XV, this system really is a headache! Each blow pushes far away, locking any action of your char for some time (Hitlock) and characters that benefit from hit spam with low skill CD time,, are free to massacre your defense, together with the system I mentioned before, the lack of a Counter EX. You just get stuck and just can sacrifice a special bar to use the advanced dodge, which is terrible , and risk yourself taking a special counterattack from fast recovery characters.Special and EX moves are mostly weak, being easily disarmed by a simple punch or strong kick, taking away the whole point of sacrificing a special bar for its use.It seems that moves that use Especial Bras to amplify them are totally useless and only work in combos, not as a pressure or escape plan.Terrible online system, never manages to get players to meet up to play.DJ Station is a mode where you can listen to music from KOF series games, but many songs are not remastered, and with horrible audio. Story Mode is weak and uninteresting, it doesn't bring any of the rich plot of the series that you find on the internet in the manga and in previous games, which brought the series to fame.Finally, in my opinion this KOF along with all the others that came after King of Fighters 98, could easily be thrown in the trash, they are nothing more than lazy and poorly done work, which are not worth 01 cent of invested currency. I would like that one day SNK returned to make King of Fighters like the ones from the 94,95,96,97,98 era, where this game was really interesting and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the best entries in the entire franchise and one of the best fighting games to come out in 2022At the beginning of launch the popularity of the game was kneecapped due to the fact that the matchmaking was bugged for about 8 months into the first year of the game's lifespan, but now the game features cross-play support and the SNK has worked hard in order for the matchmaking to work as well as possible, don't let people misinform you that the matchmaking is broken, IT WORKS NOWyou get 41 characters for the base roster and find the game on sale for 15 dollars on steam, that alone is a steal due to other modern fighting game releases not featuring such a large roster, you can easily find a character that you may like!the king of fighters is a legacy game which rewards the player for being able to play within the engine well rather than it being a character driven game, it doesn't matter if the character you pick is broken, if you're not good at KOF, you're not going to win any setsdespite KOF being 3 on 3 team game, it may seem overwhelming to have to learn and play 3 different characters, but I promise you that a lot of the characters follow the same rule when it comes to creating combos and strings so once you learn how to play one character, learning multiple other characters becomes a lot easier since the combo recipe is universalKOF XV also features a large song library and you can customize your own music playlists so you can personally curate your own background music rather than listen to the default soundtrack, music is an important aspect to fighting games that people don't talk about, but hearing the same song over and over can be tiringunfortunately the game does not have a lot of single player options, the only thing you get is the story mode, which is just a glorified arcade ladder with cut scenes sprinkled in between to help with the variety, the mission mode is bland and doesn't offer much outside of giving you information on how certain special moves link together, but you have to find out optimal combos on the internet or on your own if you want a game you can play with your friends, it does offer 1v1 VS, Team VS, and Party battles, where you can play with 5 other people and pick your own characters and make your own teams, its a fun casual experience where you can round up your friends to play!this is easily one of my favorite fighting games to currently play and I encourage anyone to pick up this game, especially when its on sale, its a steal

_childDocuments_.review: SNK IS FINALLY BACK.SNK has been floundering for so long. We've had the trash that was released in the PS2/Xbox era, and that lead into KOF XIII and XIV which in my opinion were very stale and lifeless compared to the originals. Finally entering the current era of games like Heroines which can only be described as crimes against an IP. Going in, despite the nice trailers, I was very apprehensive. It's been a long time since I've seen SNK really shine. Well, if you're on the fence, get off of it, because this puts Capcom and frankly every other current fighting franchise dev to shame. If you're worried about 3D graphics vs the classic 2D sprites, worry not. Unlike the 3D in XIV, everything has soul and life. Animations are fluid and polished, the color palette is bright and vibrant, and humorous and skimpy outfits are offered off the bat without the need of expensive DLC to unlock them (COUGH: Capcom). Speaking of DLC, most of us are sick and tired of the crud Capcom is pulling with their Arcade/Champion/Super/Turbo crap piled onto endless DLC for literally everything under the sun. SFV Champion Edition is rated Mixed for a reason. KOF has never had this problem with multiple different versions for one game, and I don't see that starting here. DLC will be for characters, and clothes will be included with those packs, as they should. The first DLC character pack is already astounding taking the already high amount of fighters (39) to 45 with an additional 6 characters, including fan favorites like Geese and long-gone stars like B. Jennet.But how's the fighting? Basically perfect! Control is spot on, characters are extremely varied and don't feel like cheap model swaps like many fighting games (Smash Bros for example). Counters are well executed and feel so good to pull off, while special moves are allowed to be used at any power meter level, not forcing you to only use it once 100% full. Games are quick, fun, and old school laugh out loud/punch the guy on the sofa next to you, level of fun. I played with a buddy online tonight for over 3 hours. I legit have played every main fighting game release for the last decade, and this is the first time I've had as much fun as I did when I was a teen back in the PS1/Saturn era. This game is a serious competition title, but is jovial and lighthearted enough to not take itself too seriously. Music, character designs, move sets, backgrounds all keep you entertained and keep the convo and trash talk flowing to the point where it's always "just one more game". My wife in the master bedroom a hallway down was surprised to hear me screaming and hollering so loud with the fun we had, as she's never heard me so animated over a video game before.Long story short, it's incredibly fun and refreshing. I feel rewarded for playing the game. This isn't a comprehensive review, and I recognize that. Netcode is great btw, story mode is good enough ... it's a story mode, and you have all the usual options. The new characters look kinda stupid but the girl with ghost hands and a spray painted getup is so freakin fun to use, that it keeps the game fresh. The guy named Dinosaur is our new "wtf" character, and his ability to produce some truly surprising move sets is great and keeps even seasoned vets on their toes.All in all, it's a truly great time. I honestly thought of SNK as the "life support" company, producing crappy arcade 1UP like machines and games like Heroines to keep the lights on, with zero respect for the characters they own or the IPs they reside in. But this game truly gives me not only hope, but genuine excitement for the future of SNK. It's honestly like there's an entirely new dev team at the helm here, and if that was true I really wouldn't be surprised. It feels like a seasoned team of industry vets who were also huge fanboys of the originals were hired to make this game. That passion and soul comes off it's practically dripping off the screen at every moment. So, much to my surprise, I'd like to humbly thank SNK for this game, and the efforts done to not only do this well mechanically, but unlike the Samurai Shodown game that came out a couple years ago, to do this in a way that refreshes what was becoming a stale IP. I'm so glad to finally be proud again of SNK, and I wish them all the best in the near future. Please buy the game, it deserves it. I NEVER say this in my reviews, in fact most are negative, but seriously 10/10 for me, here. I have no complaints.PS: If you have a nice rig like me (3090 and 5950X Ryzen 9) this has RTX support. Yeah, would NEVER have expected that lol, and it looks fantastic. Again, the little things that make this game really feel like it went the extra mile.

_childDocuments_.review: The good things: A lot to learn and practice if you're new to KoF, especially if new to fighting games as a whole. Will require a bit more dedication to get into as opposed to GG Strive, for example. Large and varied roster. Fun and rewarding gameplay - like I said, there is A LOT you can improve on. There's a bit more of an emphasis on movement options and mechanical skill compared to other fighters (i.e. three different types of jumps you'll use).The rest: As many other modern fighting games, the game lacks singleplayer content. This would be forgiven if the online was acceptable, yet that is the glaring issue. Playing offline at a tournament, I'm sure it's a blast. The matchmaking, however, is complete dog and continues to be that way. Every time I log onto this game, it ends up where I'm just sitting in training mode for 15 minutes,  to then closing the game in disappointment. Sometimes I'll find a match after 10 minutes or so, yet often, they'll have a faulty connection.The netcode- to me, is a disappointment as well. They improved it slightly with a recent update. It is rollback, sure, but it is not implemented well. The way it handles high ping and or low quality connections are where it shows its bad implementation. Even if I have an average connection to someone else, it will occasionally hiccup, desync audio or rollback an animation quite randomly. We see in something such as Guilty Gear Strive, bad connections/high ping are typically put on 'slow-mo' to at least make a somewhat playable environment, so your inputs can be registered. 200 ping on Strive is playable. 200 ping on KoF XV will drop my inputs left and right. This severity should highlight the fact that the experience online still has occasional annoyances with even the above average connections. It just feels inconsistent.

_childDocuments_.review: A MUCH needed upgrade to the foundation that was KOFXIVThe game features 39 characters, most of which are returning faces from the previous game. Adjustments made to the system of the game made it much more approachable for beginners to pick up while veterans (and especially those who played KOFXIV) will feel right at home. EX moves are now accessible outside of MAX mode and costs only half a bar of meter, MAX mode adjustments made it more expensive to use (2 bars now) while toned down in general compared to the previous game.Graphically, the game also builds upon the foundation of its predecessor. Characters look a ton better than in XIV, the colors are vibrant, special effects look good in motion and they added new animations to almost all the cast. Voice actors reprise their roles from the previous games too with new lines recorded that far surpass their previous work, adding more life to their respective characters. Terry's VA did an exceptional job shouting "BUSTER IGNITION" for example. That delivery...Online has been working great for me so far considering that I live in Kuwait (Middle East), I have had some great matches with neighboring friends from Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates and Bahrain for example, thanks to the implementation of rollback netcode. I've had matches with players with pings as high as 230ms yet they played incredibly and shockingly smooth! I don't know how they pulled this off but I am guessing Code Mystics might have helped them achieve that. My only problem with the game's current state (as of the date of publishing this review) is that the matchmaking requires a rework, it takes a long time to match me with someone and I get a lot of failed connections when I find a match.I haven't delved into any single player since I rarely play fighting games and enjoy them alone so I cannot give a fair opinion with regards to their single player content, but the game does have some form of story mode and a combo challenge mode (albeit seemingly watered down). They included a DJ Mode which allows you to pick music from previous games in the KOF franchise or other NeoGeo games but that requires you to beat the game with secret team combinations to unlock (which is nice if you want single player content).Overall, I am very happy with this game. Great online, looks and moves fantastic, music is nice and the overall gameplay feels fantastic. I hope SNK continues to support the game with DLC and keep interest high.My only request from the devs at this point is to hopefully add crossplay. Maybe some day!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 5/15/2022: The below review still stands but I have changed my overall review to negative. I got on to check and see how the game had changed since I last played and the experience made me change my review. The matchmaking is still awful as it takes forever to find a match. On top of the length in matchmaking once you finally get a match the opponent you are playing is of a vastly different skill bracket. I played a few games and all of them had a rank differential of over 10. One opponent was even a champion with over 300 stars. Do not buy this game unless matchmaking is fixed.Disclaimer: I am not good at this game  nor other fighting games. My opinion is based on my experience against other crappy players so take that as you will. I do recommend this game. It can be a ton a ton of fun. The characters are great and the combos are very satisfying to pull off. However there are some on going issues I have with the game that I think are important to know before you buy it. 1. Check the player count.This game has very little single player content and thusly requires a decent player count to be playable. Make sure to check the steam charts (as there is no crossplay) before you get it. 2. Input difficulty. KOF is known for being a difficult fighting game and XV definitely tones it down, but I find the cancel windows and timing to be a bit too strict unless you know some legacy tricks that the game doesn’t teach you. If you don’t want to invest the time to learn the KOF combo structure and cancel timing the. Give this a pass. If you are ok with the difficulty you will have a blast! 3. Matchmaking.As of writing this review there is a problem with matchmaking outside of training mode. It seems like half the time you get an error or the match times out. I  personally have been able to get plenty of games, but the issue exists and may affect you more so than it did me. 4. Contradictory gameplay KOF is naturally a very aggressive game with jumps/super jumps, hops/hyper hops, and a heavy combo focus style. This is great fun and gives a feel different than most fighting games. The neutral is more mobile and fast paced which I consider a plus. The problem comes at when you do get an opening. You get a hit and confirm into combo and now your opponent is knocked down. Typically in fighting games the aggressor has advantage on knockdown, but in my experience in KOF XV the defender is in advantage. On top of the typical invincible reversals and other normal wake up options you have grabs and rolls. Grabs are frame 1 and strike invincible. They also don’t have a typical whiff animation since they are performed with f./b. HP or f./b. HK. Rolls are strike invincible from frame one and must normal thrown on a read. However if you mistime the throw input you get HP/HK which gives the opponent a punish. I’ve found myself more often than not being defensive after a knockdown rather than applying pressure. I find this quite annoying considering how the rest of the game seems to be hyper aggressive. I’m sure if I kept playing I’d figure out this game’s style of oki, i just don’t find it fun. If this isn’t a negative to you, than by all means go and enjoy some great fighting game fun. The game is great fun. I just don’t think it’s the game for me. Though it might be for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you've never really gotten into fighting games, this KOFXV feels very rewarding to get into. The team-based structure makes losses more bearable as there's something for you to learn from every interaction between the different characters. There's a right amount of motivation gained from every new round. Whether you're trying to play through the story on the hardest difficulty or learn stuff from the trials, there's going to be inevitable roadblocks if you're no pro player. But as you get comfortable with more and more characters, as you try to get better with your favorite, you will improve. Whether it be your ability to do the inputs or understanding risk/reward or just blocking attacks better. Even if you don't purchase any DLC, there's so much depth to the roster. It may not be wholly polished graphic-wise and content-wise, but it is certainly a return to the higher standards of KoF.

_childDocuments_.review: Unquestionably one of the best KOF titles SNK have produced.  While not perfect, KOF15 provides an experience that few fighting games have, with features that appeal to newcomers without completely alienating the veterans.  The artstyle is gorgeous to look at, building on the style introduced in SamSho 2019 with beautiful, life-filled stages, artfully rendered character models, and hit/super effects that make everything feel explosive and impactful.   The music, as expected of an SNK fighting game, is top-notch, exploring a wide variety of styles while allowing the player to fully customize their soundtrack experience down to the menu theme.  Additionally, the games rollback netcode, while not perfect, is a massive step up from the atrocious delay-based netcode of previous offerings, providing a mostly smooth online experience.However, as mentioned earlier, this game isn't perfect.  The matchmaking for this game leaves a lot to be desired, particularly for a relative newcomer like myself.  While this isn't my first KOF, it is the first KOF I've played online, and it's not at all a good impression for a low-level player like myself to be matched constantly with Rank 10 or higher players who 3-0 me every time I dare to boot up the game's online mode.  This issue is worsened by the wait times between matches, wherein I'll sit for 15-30 minutes at a stretch in training mode waiting to be matched with someone, often only to be matched up with someone who already 3-0'd me.  For this reason, I wouldn't advise a newcomer to hop straight into online mode.  While I've heard rumors that the forthcoming Crossplay Update will potentially fix this, until this is confirmed, I will be assuming that the matchmaking will remain in its current state for the foreseeable future.Overall, KOF15, while not perfect, is a fantastic fighting game and a massive improvement over its predecessor, which itself was no slouch.  I look forward to whatever SNK has in store for this game and hope to see it in a better state down the line.
