_childDocuments_.review: KOF is back baybeee! If you haven’t played KOF before here’s how I like to describe it. KOF is for people that LOVE Street Fighter. And also offense is much stronger than in SF. If that did anything for you, do yourself a favor and check out KOF. The combos in the game are easier than KOFXIII, mainly because Max Mode is a lot simpler to use and shorter than Dust. The game is a little more accessible but still strongly appeals to KOF lovers. SNK didn’t totally throw away much of the legacy and legacy skill of the game like other fighting game series are doing right now The way the auto combo works is great, you spam light punch 3 times and depending on the 4th button you press a different super comes out. It doesn't affect seasoned players at all and gives new players a little taste of doing KOF combos.There’s no comeback mechanic in this game which is really welcome, just your meter and max mode. The pace of the game is so much more natural if you don’t have to stop your offense to bait Rage Arts/Ultras when you get your opponent down to 30%. The game has just as much tech as you expect it to if you’ve played KOF before. There’s always going to be something you can practice. Trust me on this, that’s a lot better than running out of things to practice in your fighting game. Having ways to improve your game is a major carrot on a stick to keep you playing. It keeps your mind interested in the game and the possibilities of the game. The roster is generally more balanced than XIII, in XIII some characters like EX Iori and Mr. Karate really towered over the roster. There’s still high and low tiers but I think the disparity isn’t as bad in XV. I was a little worried about the graphics but they do look noticeably better in person than on Twitch/YouTube. I would say the visuals are about on par with SF4, the colors are a lot more vibrant and it's got that classic SNK stylizing. The tutorials are about average for the genre, meaning they could be a lot better but the community always steps up with resources for new players. Story mode is about average for the genre as well. You can customize the music that plays on different menus and stages which is a really nice feature. You can also unlock extra music by playing the story mode with specific teams, I wish there were more arranged tracks but there’s plenty of music to choose from. (Side note: KOF 96’ arranged tracks are ridiculously good)Conclusion: I really like this game and what KOF represents in general. KOF is for people that love Street Fighter and I love Street Fighter. I am overjoyed that SNK not only made another great KOF game, but that they also didn't throw the legacy of KOF out the window in order to pander to consumers who will play this game 15 minutes and give up. I hope SNK continues to stick to their guns because KOF is a badass game. And because if SNK keeps putting out games of this quality against the Strives and the Fives, KOF will continue to grow with an identity that sets itself apart from the other current 2D fighting games on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: With every single iteration of KOF, comes the time that when you start the game :) the KOF tournament is about to begin! :)What makes KOF special in all graces are that you don't attack people that you down. This game lets you focus enemies into the map edge/corners and keep them suspended in mid air as they take your beatings! This allows a lot more fair play, and the elemental attacks from everyone are also pretty fair, in the sense that your HP bar feels larger and lets you take a more faithful fight in all aspects.Singleplayer 39 characters to create, the odds are endless, DLC has 12 characters to far, and both season passes = equate more than the total price of this base game. Only get it on sale, I feel spoilt that i got it for 75% off, but that is also something that flows well with r/patientgamersThis is a remarkable package and truly shows the game's evolution over time! I put some extra time into KOF 13, and 14 this weekend too, and especially to compare, because i sat aside reading reviews on Steam over and over, till i was sure, this is it. My own valentine's day gift to myself. It's actually big in size, and you still get the Leona skin with the standard base game purchase , vs deluxe. The time to put into every character is going to develop, and I'm sure they will beef up the game modes to include Survival, Missions, and Time attack to this beautiful game.Performance wise, It's running incredibly fast on a USB3 HDD, and it loads competently fast, in games in no loading screens, just a scoreboard of what's up next, and boom the stage is there. You can do better with Steam Overlay, OFF _ and Windows Game bar also never popping up. All overlays are forbidden in new releases... ESPECIALLY if you're going to record, or stream your games. Enjoy Unreal Engine 4 at its finest.When you search online, you can choose how many frames to consider in your rollbacks, etc. BUT< 450ms ping fights are pretty possible, IF nothing interferes during the fight, which it does get, even on LAN connection. So it's going to be up and down. Embrace it if you want, it's pretty fun and laughable at the same time. Cannot take any rank seriously. Also punishes you for skipping tutorials to just play the game, and warns you about it. It's a strict no knows bounds attack at you, but it keeps it pretty fair.You can be a single good button or two spammer with a game like this. You can bait people out, or you can get completely eaten depending on who you face, and what they know. Never underestimate anyone you meet in this game. The trios of fighting make it pretty fun, because it's like a life, when one character is down, you have 2/3 remaining. At the start of each fight, you determine their order of lives, depending on who you're facing. As you get better, your first character usually cleans up house on all 3 of the others, and the more HP your team has, the better your scoring at the end.The japanese and subtitles really do it for me. It feels like an organic Japanese experience, and native tongues are telling their stories. It sounds good and keeps persistent tone in all different areas of the game.Loving it so far, tested with PS5 and Xbox Wolverine V2, and they're both wonderful.Will update for more if anything catches my eye or something i feel is important to let you know of.If you cannot get this game yet, definitely feel free to test 13, and 14 or even the older ones for a healthy dose of a great fighting game platform. Lots of love is in each and every title.The fact that they hid certain characters behind DLC in a game that is this expensive already, is disappointing, in contrast to all characters and more being in the previous games without DLC requirement.The engine usage of Unreal Engine should have made this game universally cheaper due to the royalties of this grand engine. I feel some details were lost between 14 and 15. The characters in XV are wider/fatter/broader than the very same people in XIV. The characters look all around more stocky in this title, compared to how agile and thin 90% of the fighters are in 14.Anyway, that's the minor differences, underneath it all, if you can remember combos from previous games, find your characters and repeat them here :) with more fluidity, and in a state of learning what is different here.Max Form mode is a type of adrenaline release during fights where you activate your beast mode, and the damage done during this time is meant to be a bit extra to boost your position in  a fight. You also get a good speed burst to  use during this time. The length of time this activates for, is based on whether you save it during your fight, or release it as you need [minimum 1 bar required to activate]Practicing in-game with the above will help you get used to it.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a primarily story-centric review as that is the main reason I was personally most intrigued to play this, having a lot of interest in the story of previous games, especially XIII. King of Fighters XV is a game I had been looking forward to for a very long time and I am very glad it is finally released!Firstly, as someone who is fairly new to the series, it was helpful to have tutorials included here (although I feel as if these should have definitely been more in depth as they were rather basic.) The game seems to play easier than the previous instalments however, CPU is adjustable so beginners and experts can satisfy to their skill level and the command list is available on pause as well as services after losing on Story mode.On a positive, the game definitely feels like it's taken account of beginners to experts with its various levels of challenge that can be customised to your preferences. The graphics are very nice and particularly the stages look of a wonderful quality.Unfortunately I had a lot of issues with screen tearing, Enabling V-sync does indeed fix this but sadly adds a lot of lag. This seems like a common problem so I am hoping it is fixed. Otherwise, I have not encountered any bugs or glitches, everything seems to be very well coded and work together gameplay-wise. And its also nice to have various modes of play online and bonus features such as the DJ Station and gallery. The soundtrack is very good and in my opinion one of the best so far in the series. However, my main concern is with the story mode. Compared to previous KOF games, there is no way to say it other than the story is very disappointing.The previous titles had a very engaging and interesting story however I feel as if this time around it just falls flat.I found particularly the protagonist and rival this time around to be very boring and generic, especially in comparison to the previous 3 protags and rivals. Also, many story-centric characters had very little involvement with the plot if any at all. Which was definitely a let down due to characters such as Team Orochi, Ash Crimson and others being dead for a very long time and their comebacks felt anticlimactic.Ash in particular, as the main events of this story were a consequence of his doing in XIII. The bosses felt very shoehorned in and there was little explanation of them. There seemed to be very few interactions between the characters and when they did interact in the (lack of) animated cutscenes it felt incredibly awkward and stiff as if they were reading off a script. The ending was very cliché and predictable and lacked the emotion the previous instalments had.The individual endings also didn't add much, if anything at all, however the art was very pretty. I feel as if the focus this time around is definitely on gameplay rather than story, which would be fine if this were a new series or a standalone game however I feel this is unfortunate because past titles had very in-depth and engaging storylines which gave the player a reason to care about the backstories of the characters. In comparison to those, this time around it was very vague and nondescript which is especially disappointing considering from promotional material it seemed as if there would be a big story this time around.I'm hoping that the story will be expanded more in the next release or with a manga like XIV, however it's disappointing to have waited this long for very little development at all. Overall, this is a fun to play title and a solid fighting game with many characters to choose from and I have personally not had too many problems with gameplay, but if you are looking for any development to the long running story unfortunately this falls very short.I feel neutral overall, but unfortunately you can only give positive or negative. I'm really hoping that in the future there will be more story and character development added, like previous titles.And also many of the bugs are fixed so that both players interested in story and gameplay will be satisfied!~

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I would like to mention that I have played some of the previous original KOF games (when they were still flash games at the time) and have to say they were sick af. It's like developers, in general, have specific assets they all just copy-paste and really only change the menu and colours a little bit. As an example, I remember the old hexagonal character selection screen for which I was really fond of and found it unique and characteristic to the series, in contrast to the square one every arcade fighting game has nowadays, including this one now.Additionally, the game feels so slow, for some reason. There is no effect like a motion blur or any additional visual effect to suggest a fast-paced arena match happening. Even the movement's kind of janky and retracts from the "fast" feeling of the game and it is really disappointing seeing that occurring in this title. There are some animations that do not feel right to me, like they are disconnected with what's happening but that's it. And lastly, I feel like the power meter fills too slowly during matches.What I like; Most other things, to be honest.Graphics are good, nothing impressive or new to the genre, though. Characters are still as cool as I remember them to be with unique moves and techniques I still very much enjoy and some of the new ones I tried have their own charm and attraction. Another plus regarding characters, the majority of the effects are pretty amazing and highly detailed, graphically speaking. Music is standard hard/power rock OST that pumps up the action and gets you more invested in the game itself. Button mapping is pretty much fine. Some of the arena scenes are really beautiful and all of them are of high quality as well.I honestly do not feel entitled enough to rate the game, since I have not played it much but the reason I am not going to keep playing it is because it feels pretty generic overall and other ones do generally better overall. Hopefully, this review might help you decide for yourself.Thanks for reading! Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks and feels like the most premium, contemporary fighter.I really dig the music and the overall positive vibe of the game. That Metal Slug scenario, that latest version of Soy Sauce for Geese...To me the most important factors are the look and feel, beginner-friendliness and good graphical optimisation.My use case is originally offline: bringing this game on a laptop, on a trip. Most importantly, being able to play with friends with just one extra gamepad without neither of us knowing any character. For that to work, the game needs to be reasonably beginner friendly, and have a high enough number of characters, to play random 3v3 and still find new characters after 1 hour. It also should be possible to play at least 2 hours on battery: for that I have to set the laptop power limit to a pretty low number (35W/40W), at which most of the current top fighting games just don't work. And that's the thing: find me a modern fighter that can comply with that.The game is very straightforward to you: you get frame info in the challenges, and you really get to see why/when your moves hit. This has encouraged me to keep learning and playing online as well (and the music is cool, the characters are cool, etc).Despite SNK being a known company, it's a small company. It's incredible how much content this game has to offer. With so many teams and 3 characters per team, intros and endings+special endings for each team, it really reminds one of successful MOBAs with not nearly as much reach nor (probably) budget.The online matching worked pretty well for me. As a sample of one person so far, I've played 25 matches:- I got my matches in less than 1 minute, with the exception of the error ("An error occurred" message)(see * below).- Nearly half of the opponents have asked for rematch (12 out of 25).- So far I have not been disconnected from a match.I want to draw attention to a bunch of things here.First of all, this technology is incredible. The fact that a fighting game is even playable (and winnable) against somebody with more than 250ms ping is crazy to me.Second, at the time of writing 367 players on Steam and I can find a game in less than a minute. Personally I play what I like, as long as I can find people to play with. I have plenty of <1000-player games in my library, I have an idea of how hard it is to find a game.What is sorely lacking in this game is more tools to learn in general. There is a lot to learn, because well, it is KoF freaking 15, isn't it. Other games have more comprehensive tutorials. Getting your first win won't be as straightforward as with Mortal Kombat or Guilty Gear Strive. There is an achievement for "first victory online", and 30.8% players have it.(*) "An error occurred" seems to be  main matchmaking issue. After getting such message in "Begin Search", one can get through and possibly retry and find a match. However, this message  on "Training Standby" so you may as well wait forever. My advice is that, if you don't get a match in 1 minute, just exit "Training Standby".

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy playing this game. It's probably the most fun I've had with KOF since 13. Unfortunately, it would be a disservice to recommend the game in its current state.Kaiserwave has posted on the discussion board what SNK is investigating. If you guys run into any issues and need to report them or give feedback, join the official SNK discord server and post under the #kofxv-feedback section.I would be happy to change this review when the issues get addressed. (This review will be updated to reflect the current state of the game)EDIT (04/19/22): Most of the issues surrounding this game have still not been fixed. The netcode still suffers from one-sided rollback, matchmaking (both ranked & casual) is nonfunctional leaving room matches as the default way to play, the game seems to frequently crash, some people who have bought Team Garou after their release are not able to play as them, some users have reported not being able to play online since release. There was that whole issue with Steam being locked out of Team Garou for about 16 hours, whereas Epic had no issues with accessing the characters at the time the patch came out (basically all versions could use the characters except for Steam during that period). I understand game development is a complex process and the devs on the Steam forums have been communicating with us regarding new issues that arise, but it gets a little problematic when almost every other thread is someone asking what's wrong with the matchmaking. There's allegedly not enough clarity for these issues & I am editing this to ensure that someone may be informed of the current state of the game before making their purchase.I have not played online since a month ago and will not do so until SNK fixes the most egregious issues with this game.EDIT (05/22/22): After the major update involving Team South Town, I can say that the optimization of the PC port has improved immensely. The weird nuances involving my friend who lives on the same coast's ping, being double what it should have been, has been reduced to where it should be. Any instances of one-sided rollback has been removed based on my experience playing with him & the game now gives you the option to run the CGI videos in game using your software or hardware on the computer. There may be some minor bugs that need to be ironed out, but I would say this patch has improved a lot of the game.The next major step is matchmaking. If SNK is willing to address this by either discussing it or fixing it outright, I will happily change this to a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: This product was returned after only the tutorials and a few test games. To the people looking to buy this game. Don't, to most of you I cannot recommend this. If however you think all games need auto combos to be accessible and you're tired of DBFZ maybe look into it.This game has auto combos that cannot be disabled for yourself or as a whole. The animation and sound design make hits feel nonimpactful. And the new roster shows that fighting games as a whole are still behind on trends by 30 years.To SNKPlease leave rush out of your next title SNK. I am the beginner you are trying to ease into the game, but it is one of the most disrespectful and harmful things I've seen done in a fighting game to try to help new players. If you had an option to turn rush off at least on your own side that would be somewhat better, but they discourage learning the actual game and get in the way of trying to. Why can I not just keep jabbing someone in the corner if they keep their defense down without losing meter, position, and time? What would actually help new players is a way to practice inputs for specific moves with feedback. The input log on the side could show all the correct motions without a move coming out, so a timing tutor would be very helpful. An auto combo system that you have to intentionally try to avoid using if you want to learn the game on a fundamental level, much much less so. I never even had the rush combos used against me by ai this isn't something I'm saying I don't want to play against, as the trolls who will vehemently defend this game on public forums about disabling rush will tell you, I don't want to use it myself and if I'm jumping between your own games (samurai showdown, snk heroines, KOF13, and this) it will get lost along the way that I'm not allowed to jab too many times in this game without burning meter. Yes I own a number of fighting games, no that does not make me any less of a beginner. Stop trying to cater to us and just give us the tools we need to improve. P.S. thank you for making those other games listed, they are all rather fun even if I think they could use the same style of feedback on input moves. it would be especially helpful on charge characters to try to learn the timing of when charge is built up.

(I understand he is in the Fighter pass 2 with Billy and Ryuji, but it's just weird not having him in an SNK fighting game right off the bat)Another more minor complaint I have is Sylvie and Mian not being including as fighters despite being introduced in the previous title. Feels a bit off since Kukri and Dinosaur are, and being left to be eye candy for SNK Heroine Tag Battle is eh?One could argue the South American Invite Team wasn't included either, but they were more just another team compared to Sylvie and Mian who formally worked for NEST which is a relatively more connected party to the KOF story line overall. I know they're in Team G.A.W's ending but it just feels off to me. That's just a me thing tho, and doesn't really affect the rating of the game. I made the mistake of getting hyped because my favorite Team had been resurrected, so that was my fault and not the games'. It's not the worst entry in KOF, but there are better ones, and it is hard to live up to KOF 03. It was a bold move to make KOF go from 2D to 3D with KOF14, but in my opinion, KOF14 did it far better than than than KOF15. It feels too shiny, and the arenas feel empty. In KOF14, the arenas were full of life and really added atmosphere to the fight, like an actual tournament was being watched by fans. In KOF15, they just don't feel alive at all with barely any spectators, even in the more populous ones. It is a bit disappointing that we waited nearly 6 years for an atmospheric downgrade to give character models a modest upgrade, and a shorter campaign than its predecessor.On the plus side MY GIRL SHERMIE IS BACK!I know my review seems to come off as a more negative one, but the game itself is good. Terry got Power Dunk back and King can use Venom Strike in the air again, so that's a huge plus. The fighters do feel like they have more toolkit use out of their moves than previously, except maybe Luong and Vanessa (however they are one trick pony fighters so it makes sense). Also, despite the arenas themselves being empty, they look absolutely stunning. The game looks good, plays solid, and while the story is very brief, it does push the climax a healthy dose forward even if it is a bit out there. Also, hope we get Alice and Oswald back as DLC fighters.Overall, KOF 14 is the better game of this current arc, but KOF15 is still good.  7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna make something very clear, I love this game. It's my first REAL step into a KoF game on release and I will be mentioning why I love it later. But I first wanna get the reason out of the way as to why I am not recommending it at the moment:The Matchmaking is broken, it has been broken since release and SNK has not been communicative on their progress besides a small "We are looking into it" in a Twitch Chat of all places. This is not a problem with small player numbers or being part of a low rank past release. This has been a problem on all platforms. If you want further info, I recommend checking out SNK, this game could be way bigger than it is, but atm players struggle to play ladder and it makes for a really bad experience. Having Discords that allow for matchmaking should not be the excuse for a feature that has been essentially solved since 2009.With that out of the way I wanna talk about what I love concerning the game.I only played a minimal amount of KoFXIII and KoFXIV when they came to Steam, I have however played a lot of other Fighting Games for a bunch of years now, including old retro titles and newer titles.KoFXV makes for one of the most fun experiences yet, it gives me chills to play and is almost antithetical to the modern fighting game experiences. I love most modern FGs, but it's unavoidable how every franchise tries to reinvent itself, leading to some awkward feelings by old fans and even new fans.KoFXV doesn't reinvent, it doesn't even really innovate, it instead focuses on iterating on previous titles and it's obvious with so many of its choices. It builds on previous titles and adds simply more unto the already pretty fun XIV system. A small change like making EX Moves always accessible just gives this game so much new expression, characters almost feel new to me.The game feels like a formula that has been perfected through trial and error over multiple decades, the only real new addition is Shatter Strike, a sort of Focus Attack and the simplification of all Climax moves being the same motion, which I welcome.The roster is filled with some of the most fun and stylish character designs I have ever seen in a fighting game. It doesn't quite hit the crazy metal/hard rock inspired designs of Guilty Gear or the iconicity of some Street Fighters, yet all of the characters feel fully realized with extra cutscenes and quotes if they meet certain other characters in this games Arcade Mode. Stages are full of life, but there are some stage concepts I really wish would come back, like the train from XIV/Garou (My favorite stage out of any FG).The Arcade Mode really is just what it always has been. If you've ever played a KoF or even any FG it won't be a big surprise. The story only really focuses on two teams, but what little interaction is there is still really fun to see. SNK does a really good job of letting these characters bounce off of eachother, referencing past events and in some cases even playing unique music that adds a ton of weight to an encounter. Shoutout to Way to The Horizon, the theme of Rock vs. Geese and the always wonderful to hear Good Bye Esaka that plays during Iori vs. Kyo. But besides Arcade there is nothing really, there are trials and Special Endings based on your teams, but that is it. Recently we got the extra Boss mode which was incredibly awesome, please do more of that.I also put a lot of importance on good netcode and sure enough KoFXV brings that. Rollback is working wonderful with most of my games feeling great as long as both players use a wired connection. When testing between continents it was expected to feel not great, but it still worked better than some other games (Nothing on the level of Skullgirls though, that game's netcode runs on some sort of witchcraft).The lack of content sucks, but at the same time I believe a good roster can make for good content in its own way. I often find myself replaying MvC2 and just picking up a different character to see what sort of combos I can do with them and KoFXV is the first time a modern game had me feel the same way over again. If that isn't your cup of tea, then I warn you that this game will not blow you away with its content.What makes the content sting even more is the awful matchmaking, which leads to almost hours on end with no matches found when the player numbers are clearly high enough to support it. So far the best option to play online is finding people on Discords, which I haven't had a bad experience with so far. The KoF community in europe has been extremely welcoming and fun to be around.Congrats SNK, I am now a fan of your properties, especially KoF.

_childDocuments_.review: KoF 15 was one of my most anticipated fighting games of the year, so let’s go ahead and get right into it.King of Fighters XV is by no means an easy fighting game to get into. The attacks, moves, and overall aesthetic may appear on the simplistic side, but there is a mountain of depth beneath it all. My friend and I played for hours and still were unable to figure out the most basic of combos and it was not until we went through all the training missions, a few character challenges, and dabbled in the training mode that the mechanics really unlocked.And even then, it’s like a multi-hour thing just to get the hang of the basics of ONE character - and there are 39 total to play around with. Basically what I’m trying to say here is that this is not really a beginner-friendly game. On one hand, yeah this does make the beginning a bit of a struggle, but then again on the other, it is cool to see a fighting game embrace tradition and just have so much cool stuff to learn and master that I can’t not appreciate it. Will I ever get to the point where I can claim to be good at the game? Debatable. But will it be fun along the way? For sure.The actual fighting is absolutely solid. Hits with impact, quick and fluid movement, decent buffer size - it’s got pretty much all the basics down. I may not be busting out mega combos yet, but I did quickly grow to appreciate how everything just “flows”. It’s not jittery, it’s not slow, it doesn’t feel like my inputs are being misread - it just plays well and goes to show the experience of the developers here.Character-wise, there is a good bit of variety here. Brawlers, zoners, grapplers, rushdown, defensive, mixups - all the archetypes are checked off here multiple times over. I love me a good zoner, so my personal favorite ended up being Athena Asamiya, but given the 3 on 3 nature of the game, I was also able to have a basic brawler and a grappler on my team to cover my other bases and it was a lot of fun to mixup with these different styles within the same match.You get your basic versus mode, multiplayer modes, tutorial modes, mission mode, and story - but nothing beyond that. There is no traditional “arcade” mode and the “story” mode takes up that role instead. As usual though with the genre, the story itself is some hot garbage and the cutscenes aren’t all that great so really you’re just playing it for the “arcade mode” gameplay but with extra steps.Training mode is fine, but the mission mode where you get to learn character combos is a bit lacking too. You get just five combos per character, which considering the depth behind this game, feels like a weak offering. The only notable “unique” mode is boss challenge, which simply pits you against a beefed up boss character with rewards given upon completion.Compared to what I’ve seen in some other recent fighters, the offering across the board here is nothing special. It really is just the bare minimum to get by and this is definitely NOT a game you would want to pick up if you are not interested in playing it online or competitively offline. Maybe not an issue for some, but worth noting regardless.For some unknown reason, despite there being over 1000 players online at any given moment, finding matches just straight-up does not work for many. It’s not like a home connection issue either - it’s a legitimate bug that the developers themselves have acknowledged but have not appeared to address.I don’t have it so bad that I never find a match, but I have had situations where I would be sitting there for a while waiting for a match (or never, in the case of casual and room matches). When I did get into ranked matches though - the rollback connection was fine. I didn’t have any stutters, disconnects, or the like - that part was relatively smooth, it’s just the finding of matches that may prove difficult. Again, I don’t seem to have it as bad as others - but I felt it was important to mention regardless.Aesthetically, I’d say the game is fine. It’s obviously trying to go for that Street Fighter look and while I kinda miss the style of KoF 13, I’m not opposed to the new style either. Just be sure not to pay close attention to the stage backgrounds - those definitely took a backseat to the character models. The music, on the other hand, is some good stuff all around and par for the course for this series.When KoF 15 launched, the 1440p resolution option was missing, but that has since been fixed and I can’t say I have any complaints. Looks good, runs well without any technical hiccups, and has a handful of graphical options to change on top of that. Not the most advanced I have seen, but good enough.The King of Fighters XV is a fun fighting game all around. Solid gameplay base, complex mechanics, a massive roster - it may take a while to get into, but it’s a fun journey along the way. Still, I was a bit disappointed by the singleplayer content offering and the game could have done a better job with its character missions and overall tutorial options. It might not be a constant on my fighting game rotation, but I’ll likely come back from time to time to mess around with friends.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is heavily spam oriented.I've dropped it! I like it, i like the characters, i like the team-concept, but the game is broken in too many ways, especially in hitboxes, and i don't have much time, nor desire to "git gud" with broken mechanics, especially when you need to put extra effort comparing to SF 6, GG, Tekken 7, MK 11, MK 1.ONLINE:- There is no “1 vs 1” mode in casual or ranked mode, only “3 vs 3”, although there is such mode in single. There is "1 vs 1" mode in lobby mode, but lobby mode is dead.- You can’t fill all three slots with same character, so you have to learn three different characters simultaneously.- There are few totally imbalanced characters that everyone chooses.- I saw players who has rank 2, but they were not rank 2. They were much higher.- You can't quit match if your opponent is spammer.PRACTICE:- There is no hitbox, hurtbox, collisionbox views.- There is no frame data chart like in SF6. It would be very helpful during combo challenges, because I can’t figure out when to input next step of the combo.MECHANICS:- You want to make a grab? He! Good luck! You will make a punch or a kick instead.- Poor keyboard support. It’s hard to perform double quarter-circle or quarter-circle and half-circle.- Hitboxes and timings are definitely f*ucked. I can't figure out how hitboxes work in this game. There are times when opponent counter yours EX moves, but when you do the same you can't counter them.P.S. Getting good, getting accustomed to broken hitboxes, mechanics and characters doesn't make them unbroken. It makes you only masochists.

_childDocuments_.review: KOF XV is a fun game that's worth it when on sale.  It's not as beginner-friendly as some, but it's also not super-intimidating, either, especially if you are not trying to be the best and simply want to have fun.  In the USA, I can quickly find online matches even at lower levels as of late August, 2023.Although my general experience with SNK games goes back to Fatal Fury on the Genesis, I believe that I've only owned one KOF game before this (which I believe was KOF 98 - "Dream Match 1999" on the Dreamcast).  So I'm not a diehard by any means.  I have SF6 and have been into that series more, and also love Granblue Fantasy Versus.  Now, KOF XV is my most recently-bought fighting game as of this writing, and I like it!KOF XV is definitely a worthy fighting game that can be a lot of fun.  I'm in the lower levels (around Rank 12 after 12 hours of gameplay, including story mode and training, and 44 online fights so far).  I live in the eastern US, and ranked matches pop up pretty constantly in the evenings when I've been playing online.  As of August 2023, I have not run into any matchmaking issues (that apparently were prevalent previously).If you are a diehard KOF fan, you already have this game.  For others, there are some things that do make it a bit more difficult to get into than some other fighting games.  It's improved from previous versions, but a lot of the inputs for specials and supers are more than one might expect if coming from Street Fighter.  (One hope for a future installment is that there can be something along the lines of the SF6 Modern mode or Granblue Fantasy Versus (Rising)'s simplified special inputs, which make me want to actually play as more characters because I don't have to re-learn a specific move list and remember sometimes unintuitive inputs, but can rather pick up and play any character and know how to perform moves without any glancing at command lists again and again.)  Even so, there are autocombos that can be used that can lead into supers, and a really cool thing is that lower-level supers can often be linked into higher-level supers, so if you have the bar and are okay with the inputs, you can pull off some impressive feats.  That said, this is not the most combo-heavy game (like DBZ FighterZ, for example), and I think that's a good thing.  And the good thing is that you have three characters, so even if one is taken out soon, there are two others remaining.  Also, if you are relatively capable at fighting games in general, then a lot of that learning can be used here.  You might not be the best unless you really practice a lot and focus on this game's own systems (and each character's differing inputs and combos), but you don't have to get really good, as there are moderate-level players online as well.Although I haven't spent much time with KOF, I have been familiarized with the older games to some extent through online videos, and I do believe that this is the best KOF ever.  It's a worthy fighting game, and can be a good deal if you can buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike other recent fighting games, a lot of time must be spent just labbing/practicing before you can actually have fun.It appears to be fun, but I don't recommend it for those new to KOF or fighting games in general unless you are willing to put in a ridiculous amount of hours just labbing in the beginning.The execution barrier is just too high for me, personally. I see people saying that this one is easier than the older ones and it's probably true (I've tried 2002um), but if you're like me and just want to enjoy a game after work without stressing out too much, it's not for you. As an example, I love Tekken and enjoyed GG Strive. For both games, you can practice a little bit and start having fun right away. They at least try to let you match you with someone around your skill level. In those games, you can get rewarded with good damage if you manage to create a whiff or cause your opponent to make a mistake, because the execution barrier is not that high. In KOF, even if you manage to get a hit stun animation or create a whiff, it's ridiculously difficult to get good damage out or  punish your opponent for it. The execution is what stops you from doing any damage. It's like:1) I hit someone with a close normal and I see the hit stun animation2) I better do a combo now3) I drop the combo because I cannot execute4) repeatKOF players must be on adderall or cocaine or something, because I just don't understand how they can execute all of these combos in the moment.So far, for me, the overall experience has been:-Hours just practicing characters-Get on casual and lose about 12+ games in a row to people who seem exponentially better than me-Back to lab-Lose a bunch in a row in casual mode-back in practice mode I'll keep playing because it is fresh at the moment, but I just wanted to warn newer players: you will need to be very patient and lab for a long time.Also for those who care, the largest shareholder of SNK is MBS (Mohammed bin Salman).

_childDocuments_.review: I think most notable about this game is that it's one of the few fighting games released in recent years that hasn't changed or compromised its design very much to appeal to new audiences. If you want a game that does not pointedly "cater" to casual players, this might be for you. I'd say it is still fun for the casual audience, just as something like Guilty Gear XXAC+R can be, but its mechanics do few favors to that. Many completely new people want a game like that.For the veterans, KoF is mostly still KoF. They stuck to their guns. Besides that, if you're into game music and having choices of what to listen to, DJ Station is a *huge* improvement over something like how SF6 does it (or rather, doesn't do it). KoF XV's music setup is more similar to Smash Ultimate's, there's just that much, and it's free to unlock.There is NOT a lot to do with single-player. You can run through arcade and unlock endings and music, do some boss challenges and missions etc, but there is not an extensive story or single player mode of any sort. I believe that will be coming with SNK's next game, Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.Either way, this is a tight, exemplary and well-balanced fighting game with lots of variety and things to improve at over a long period of time. Nothing else much is much like KoF. If the characters look cool and/or the fighting looks fun, please give it a shot. And yes, the matchmaking has been improved now.

I can now recommend this game if you plan to play it online, though I am still a bit sour it took so long to get to this point. If you've not picked it up yet get it on sale and it's a pretty good deal and be thankful you dodged the worst era of KoF15.

I hope this gets changed next season where we get a universal buff or character movement speed also reduce the clunky frames.Conclusion (updated)I would change this games rating from 8/10 to 6/10 as of December 2022, its been 10 month since it came out and I feel like the change in movement speed as well as simplification of inputs is a major let down to long term KOF fans.SNK PLEASE STOP CHANGING THE GAME TO COPY STREET FIGHTER. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR If you are somebody that doesnt like the way KOF games played in the SNKP era, or are not fan of combo heavy fighters, you should still give XV a try, and take a bit of time to learn it. It strikes a good overall balance between combo heavy and neutral heavy IMO, and is a fun game overall, but it takes getting used to. I would say that its a sort of "alternate take" of 2002(UM), where its again the balance of neutral and combo heavy, but done in a different way. Good KOF game, not the best, but definitely in the higher echelon.REVIEW:KOF XV is a fighting game that made me change some of my habbits, and it took some time to get used to it.As somebody who likes and plays KOF 98 the most (both OG and FE), I was never a fan of the series going intentionally toward more combo heavy route ( with games from the Ash saga being the worst offenders in that regard).It feels like KOF XV is a game that is trying to find middle ground between something like say 98 (which is mostly neutral heavy) and something like XIII (pull HD combos out of ass - the game).  XV felt so much better gameplay wise compared to something like KOF XIII, since normals in XV feel like they are actually strong, and there is more emphasis on neutral play. That said, jump felt nerfed overall, but even that is a better alternative than having a braindead jump fiesta like XIII.  I was never a fan of QuickMax mechanics and EX moves in KOF. This game made me actually want to learn how to do those QM combos. And the way they made the system work, is that once you activate QuickMax, you get a small pause before starting a combo, which makes them easier to do. At the same time, most of the combos are not the "loop 2 -3 moves to infinity and beyond" like in XIII, but feel more to the point overall.All of that makes me recommend XV as a good game to play. Its not perfect, and its definietly not my most favorite KOF, but the fact it was the game that made me want to get out of my shell and learn things that i hated before speaks volumes IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with the negative, because people reading reviews just want to know whats broken. Only downside to this game is the online matchmaking. Outside of prime playing time, it takes minutes to find matches. If you're on during good hours and have your settings on same region and a connection rating of 3+, have fun playing the same 2 people. It's sad because the online netcode is rock solid, virtually no lag or stutters. Matchmaking just sucks.Other than that, the game is great! Don't listen to the people complaining about auto combos. Yes they are there, but put in the time and no noob can out damage a manual combo. Strategy and timing will out play a guy spamming the auto combo button. Story CPU is pretty weak, on max difficulty a decent player can beat it without losing a match. Overall, buy. Even if you aren't a big KOF fan, showing support leads to more good fighting games and helps promote the community.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from only playing old KOF games when I was younger (especially 2002), I never wanted to try 14 because I thought it looked very yanky and...not so aesthetically great, however I was excited to see what 15 had in stock once the trailers started coming out, and I gotta say I'm very pleased.Gameplay is great, it is still a bit technical but nothing too complicated and very welcoming for new players (I had a friend who this was his first KOF and he did very good), and it just feels nice to play.I very much like the new models and the overall style they choose for 15, a huge improvement compared to the 3D models they had in 14. The character designs are incredible, I like the new renditions of some old ones or just how well they look now with their old style translated to the new game, plus the new characters are very nice too, my personal favorite being Isla by far.Multiplayer is a little weird, because so far, private room matches are great, the netcode is very good, it has little to no delay....the only problem being that if you don't have friends to play with and hop on Casual or Ranked, from some time on to now, it is a little difficult to find a match. I've been sitting for nearly 30 minutes without any success. I surely hope this is solved, because MP is very good, however there is that one issue.If you play with friends (either local or through Steam), or by yourself either with bots or the Story Mode, there is no issue whatsoever.Overall, a very good and fun fighting game. If you love the KOF franchise or any SNK games, you will very much like this one, and if you are a newcomer, it is a very welcoming game to just pick up and get some matches going.Definitely would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this at the moment.The Good: - Varied roster. - Almost all chars are fun to play from what i've tried. - Rollback Netcode. - Some good music and stagesThe Bad:PC issues - - The game soft-locks from time to time - specifically during matches. Worst in ranked since you lose points and get a leaving penalty for force quitting the game because it's stopped functioning. - the matchmaking is bugged on casual and ranked. - Room search is bugged.General Game issues - - Training needs a way to reset to left/right/centre instead of just centre round-start position. - Training needs a toggle for recorded actions to play on resetting training position. At the moment every time you reset position, you also have to activate the recorded actions (This is pretty annoying when doing reversal practice) - Trials are pretty weak. Some trials don't even go over some moves/aspects of moves. - Tutorial is very very basic. Some legacy knowledge is needed to understand what properties some moves have (Shermie whip is hit inv, armoured moves for Dino, Clark, Maxima one hit vs armoured moves for multi hits etc) - Personally feel the leniency for inputs is sometimes HUGE and sometimes quite strict depending on character.there are some other PC related issues that have yet to be resolved. Will change review once patch hits that actually fixes the PC issues.It definitely feels like an afterthought port, unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favorite fighting game since Central Fiction. I will likely put 100 hours into it before 2022 is through - assuming they fix the weird technical issues and matchmaking. Across just 24 hours i have had 5 mid-match or post-match disconnects that caused me to take a loss and a "fair play" penalty over a match I either won or was winning until 20000 rollback frames showed up out of the blue and caused both my opponent and myself to play the waiting game for upwards of 10 minutes. Constant matchmaking errors, one-sided rollback, and frequent disconnects make it impossible to recommend this game for 60 dollars. The ranking and netcode - when the matchmaking and rollback DO work - feel phenomenal and will guarantee that I keep coming back for more. However, until they address the technical issues present, this game is not worth 60 bucks to anyone but the hardcore KOF fans as the single player content is virtually non-existent and the accessibility for newbies to the series is simply not there.

_childDocuments_.review: looks great, plays great, lots of content, solid selection of modes including online training mode and both ranked and unranked matchmaking queues. Really big roster. Also supports raytracing if your PC can handle it. Rollback netcode. Arcade mode has been turned into a repeatable story mode with many alternate endings based on your team composition, following up on the attempt at a more fleshed out story in XIV. I'll be honest, what's on offer here is one of the most impressive launch packages I've seen from a full priced fighting game release in ages. If you're at all interested in fighting games, this should be on your radar. Other fighting game developers should take note, this is what a modern fighting game should offer as a full priced product at the absolute minimum.I'll be updating this review if anything changes, as fighting games evolve over time both in terms of metagame and content, but overall from both my own experience and the experiences shared by others, there doesn't seem to be any major glaring issues with design or balance found so far.

_childDocuments_.review: There probably are plenty of reviews for this game written by fighting game pros discussing all there is to this game. This is supposed to be a polar perspective to that. I've owned this game since launch, at the time I'm writing this 1 1/4 years, and I've only played nine hours. The way I play this game is occasionally remembering it exists, try out new characters, herp derp around pressing random buttons and having fun.I'll be brutally honest here: Not a whole lot. Most game modes are online only, but obviously it makes no sense to play them if you're playing like an hour every other month and can't remember what your character was supposed to do. It would be impossible to find someone on my "skill" level online, which leaves offline play.And let's just say the offline game modes are very basic:There is story mode, which lets you play trough a series of encounters against teams as it makes sense lore wise I guess. They don't mix team members up is what I mean. In the end you get a boss fight. Then there is Versus mode, which I usually play, where you pick a character or a team of three characters and go up against opponents of your chosing (or the chosing of the random button). It's fun but you have to pick again after each fight. So the game is missing a truely randomized Arcade mode. I don't understand how any fighting game can not have an Arcade mode but that's how it is.Then there is practise mode. But the devs seem to hate people getting practise because you need to confirm player 2 to enter it. And you can't confirm with your player 1 gamepad. So you need to either use your keyboard or plug in a second controller. The reason for this is beyond me, only the devs may know.As for variety in your gameplay session: There are just sooo many characters it's amazing! And they are all so well designed to have their own persona, play and look truely different. I love this and it's one of the main selling points of this game for me. I also love their modern interpretations of classic KoF characters, I feel like they did a good job there. And before you ask: Yes, I also was a total scrub in KoF 13 and 14.As far as stage variety goes this is one of the worst I've ever seen. There are so brutally few to call it boring would be an understatement. I mean what there is looks good, but there just isn't enough. People been asking on the forum pretty much nonstop for new stages. People would be willing to buy stages as expensive DLC just like they buy them many characters. But so far the devs did not hear their pleas. In fact it seems at least a decade behind. Graphics wise, the last gen of famous fighting games such as Tekken 7, Dead or Alive 6, Street Fighter V, Soul Calibur 6, Grandblue Fantasy Versus - they all had a higher quality style when it comes to character models. Once the new gen fighters hit KoF XV might even be called visually offensive by some. I don't know why but they added an option for Ray Tracing to this most basic graphics design, and if you're owning an AMD card you can see it must be working as the FPS go whoops. The irony of how inconsequential this is makes me chuckle every time I go through the settings.There is another side of the coin to this though: KoF has always been graphically vintage. And I do acknowledge the visual improvements made from 13 to 14 to 15. I assume it's a team size and money issue here. This game is probably too niché to spend more on the graphics engine. And if I'm being totally honest when you've played for a few minutes you don't even care anymore if characters got weird armpits or their faces look like dolls in your daughter's room.I don't dislike KoFXV. It's fine for what it is. But I can see how it is very hard to find a target audience other than people who have always played KoF, which is why I don't recommend the game. For casuals like myself there just isn't enough content in it. People coming from other fighting game series will probably be disappointed by the lack of care for the product and low production value. I'd say only buy this game if you either belong to the really highly skilled fighting gamers who care more about mechanics than anything else, or buy if you come in with zero expectations so you won't feel disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to King of Fighters XIV, it is a step forward, and a step back. For starters, the roster is not as big as it was in the King of Fighters XIV base game. Don't get me wrong though, this roster is still stacked, but they could have added a few more teams to keep in line XIV. As a result of this though, they omitted some series regulars such as Kim Kaphwan, Vice, Mature, and others. Kim probably being the biggest loss for me personally. That said though, 39 characters off the bat is nothing to frown at, considering in this day and age when most fighting games launch with rosters in the teens. Hell, some not even breaking double digits. Visually the game is a step in the right direction. To the untrained eye it might look similar to XIV, but there are some nice subtle changes to the character models such as improved physics affecting cloth movement, hair movement and more. There also appears to be much better animations for characters, and some changes to the way some faces look making characters seem more lively compared to their XIV counterparts. There is also now RTX support for reflections for cards that support it. that said though the graphics don't come without some odd drawbacks. There is no VSync option built into the game, and the resolution options are limited when playing in fullscreen or windowed. You have to force your resolution by playing borderless windowed if your resolution is not listed. Only with borderless windowed mode was my 3440x1440 monitor able to display correctly. Of course being on an ultrawide monitor, there are pillarboxes, with the game displaying at 16:9 correctly. I'm a huge UW supporter, and I can safely say to all the other UW games out there, don't get mad. This is a fighting game. Full UW support without without pillarboxes would never make sense in this type of game. As for the the lack of vsync options, this has caused screen tearing for some players, which is never a good thing for a fighting game. This is something that could be fixed with the right monitor by forcing freesync/gsync, or enabling vsync in your GPU options. But not everyone is computer savvy, so this is a problem. Vsync should really be a built in option. I'll discuss the actual gameplay some more once I get more time with it, but so far it is very solid as expected. KoF has rarely let me down in this department. The only downside I'm seeing so far in terms of gameplay is that auto combos can not be disabled. It's not a deal breaker mind you since auto combos do not mean you are actually going to be a better player. Quite the opposite in fact. So the question is, is it worth dropping $60usd on? If you're a KoF fan, the answer is undoubtedly yes. For general fighting game fans I'd still say yes for the sheer variety the roster gives you. For the casual gamer who is interested in getting into fighting games? Maybe wait for a sale. But definitely check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game,even more than the previous game of the series.It takes all the good things of KOF XIV and adds more stuff to make it better:-A very diverse roster, featuring characters from diferent eras of the franchise, including some characters that have been absent from mainline KOF games for a long time.-Better visuals than the previous game, is not KOF XIII levels of good, but this is better than what we got in KOF XIV and is probably the best looking SNK game with 3D models.-Changes to the EX moves: Just like in KOF XIII you can use EX moves without needing to be on Max mode, and unlike KOF XIII EX moves cost half bar now instead of a full bar.-Changes to Max mode: now your character will automatically run when you activate max mode, wich makes things easier for beginners who want to start playing a KOF game. And if you activate Max mode during neutral, you get a damage buff and you can do very damaging combos, even touch of death combos.-New mechanic: Shatter Strike:This mechanic reminds me of the Focus attack of SF IV, is an armored attack that puts the oponent in a crumbling state on hit, and can be used in the middle of a combo to extend it. If the move connects it uses half bar, if it misses it uses a full bar.-Game has Rollback netcode, wich makes online matches much more playable compared to matches in a lot of other fighting games released in this past generation of consoles.-You can Unlock songs from previous games of the franchise, and also songs from other SNK games(including Fatal fury, Art of Fighting, Samurai Shodown, Metal Slug and many more), you can use these songs during your online matches thanks to DJ Station.-Autocombos are still present in this game and can't be turned off(however they don't do too much damage)-For a fighting game released in 2022, it has very little single player content, besides Story mode(wich is actually the arcade mode of this game) you only have mission mode and training.-The menus are kinda blandOver all I will recomend the game to every KOF fan and to people who like fighting games, especially for those who want to play a fighting game online.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game and an excellent entry in this great series, I really love all the work they put into this game. The story is okay, it's not as good as the Orochi Saga but it's still fine. The gameplay has been improved over XIV and I like that they brought back some older mechanics, and even though I'm not good at combos I do think that auto combos should be able to be toggled on or off. I've been playing KOF since I started with 98, but I've never been the best at the game (especially with combos, my execution is pretty good though), but this time around I'm looking to get very deep into the gameplay.The graphics are a pretty big step up from XIV, even though I thought the last game looked good after they finalized the 3D models. I really like the art style they used this time around, especially the shading, animations, and effects in this game are excellent. In terms of fighters, hopefully they add more fan-favourites (Kim, Mature, Vice, etc.) back into this game. The roster is pretty good so far but there are many more fighters I'd like to see return in this art style.The soundtrack is very good and very enjoyable, as usual SNK is known for their great soundtracks, and they haven't disappointed with this soundtrack. Also the fact that they have the DJ mode is a pretty big plus, and the inclusion of all the older KOF soundtracks as unlockables is like the cherry on top. That was very respectable of SNK to give the fans such a treat.Now onto the netcode, overall the rollback code has been working great for me and my friend, and we haven't had much lag or slowdown. Occasionally there will be some random slowdown or ping spikes during gameplay, and they should probably they a look into it, and maybe make some adjustments to fix this (I'm not too sure how this works).Edit: It seems they've fixed the screen resolution and keyboard mapping issues since I last reviewed this game. There still is the weird lag during gameplay when sometimes doing special or climax moves for the first time, and then after that it doesn't do it again, until I restart my PC (I don't understand why). The game seems to be getting a lot of support from SNK, and we got our first two sets of DLC characters, but I'm still waiting for alternate costumes for all the characters, especially some older costumes from previous entries would be very much appreciated.Overall I've upgraded my rating of this game to 8.7/10, and I would very much recommend any fighting game fans to give this game a try, it is very enjoyable and once they fix the matchmaking problem some people are having, the weird startup lag when using climax moves, and I still think you should be able to toggle auto combos on/off, then I will increase it's rating, other than that this game may very well be one of the best fighting game in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: I like a lot about this game. Characters are fun, game is pretty balanced, easily my favorite fighting game right now while I wait for SF6.With that said, I can't leave a positive review for it with matchmaking in its current state. I look forward to changing this review, but right now it takes me 40+ minute queues to find anyone, of any skill, of any connection online. Casual or Ranked. Matchmaking isn't broken, its non-existent. I wait half an hour to find a single game and when I finally get one its 200-300 ping with 6-8 rollback frames. Shockingly, the netcode and rollback is some of the best I've played in so somehow those matches are actually playable, but its just miserable. They're supposed to come out with crossplay soon. The crossplay beta was nice, I was actually able to find matches. Some is certainly more than none. They cannot roll out that beta fast enough -- matchmaking has been completely broken since this game released and its the only thing holding it back on Steam. To play the game I need to request room matches in a discord server, but half the days Room matches are even bugged so we can't connect to eachother. I mean it when I say matchmaking truly could not be worse, such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: KOF XV is a really good game and possibly the best KOF game in the franchise. It's tied with XI for me at least. The gameplay feels really smooth, the character roster is great, and it's gotten some really good updates along the way. The game itself is amazing.Unfortunately, this game has one major problem. The online functionality. The online matchmaking was broken for at least the entire first year this game released. The que times commonly took up to 10 minutes despite there being thousands of people in game. This was somehow never fixed. I also think the game places too much emphasis on its online capabilities. Online functionality takes up almost half of the main menu, and like I said before, it doesn't really work. Placing so much emphasis on the online functionality is detrimental to the replay-ability of the game in the long run, and KOF was never known for being an esport-esque game. I think it's a horrible decision.The other issue with the online mode is the player-base. This is more of a subjective thing, but do any of you really think it's fun to repeatedly have to deal with King fireball spam over and over and over again? Even if there's counter-play, does it sound fun on the receiving end? No. It doesn't and it's not. I'm using King as an example (because she's the most prominent and worst offender) but the reality is that there's a handful of gimmicky ass characters that too many players abuse an annoying ass loop with. It's a very small cast of characters that somehow make up a majority of the players I saw online. Honorable mention is clark/dino grab spam. These gimmicky loops are not fun to play against, regardless if I'm able to counter it or not. It ruins the experience.I also don't really like the UI and the overall presentation of the system. It's relies on being minimalist, which while being the current meta in design language, is void of any creativity and simply boring. It makes me feel like it was engineered to get you to the online matches and nothing else.Despite all the negative things that I've said about this game, it truly is a great game and extremely fun. Sadly, the game's online dependence, emphasis, and infrastructure are all things that work to destroy its potential. There is still room for offline play, but a game like KOF should have a lot more options than it currently does. So this is a great game that I'd recommend only playing alone or with friends, unless you planned on waiting in a 10 minute que to watch King players sit in a corner, fireball spam, flying kick to the opposite corner, do it again, and have "fun"

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea what to expect from this game because I haven't played a kof in at least two decades. Thank goodness I was pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoy the combat and characters here. Everyone looks wonderful, and has flashy fun combos that are fun to do. The online matchmaking has worked really well for me personally and the story mode is pretty decent for a fighting game, which is a high bar since the last one I did was mk11. I will say, I find the $15.99 price point for a new team a little pricey, but that's more of a personal preference thing since most people seem cool with it. Overall easy call for me, if you already play fighting games then there is no reason not to check this one out. HUGE Warning: This game is hard! If you do not play fighting games, don't start with this one!!! I cannot stress that enough. There is an insane amount of legacy skill required here, and many combos require extreme movements that controller players will likely struggle with (if two half circles sounds hard to you, or half circle back to forward does, or you don't know what those mean you are in trouble).

_childDocuments_.review: KOF XV > SF VISLA!! we have got a Chilean fighter girl in the tournament!!! I'm not so good at 1vs1 fighting games (actually... I suck LoL xD), but simply KOF took over of my heart with Isla, LoL xDIt's the KOF we fans were expecting for so long. The trailers hyped us to the max, they weren't for nothing, and now the game totally demonstrates that SNK really "shattered" all our expectations, like the slogan says.A decent roster, 39 characters at launch + 6 coming in March and May, plus other six later. In my case I own the Deluxe Edition, is not so expensive. There are some unexpected teams, like the Rival team: Isla, Heidern and Dolores, also the Super Heroine team (Athena is super cute!!), and other returns like the Art of Fighting team.A really good job, beautiful! technically greatly improved, and even though is not a big deal, KOF XV has Ray Tracing!! Nice surprise. RTX is not a feature specially required in a fighting game (even unnecessary, we might say) but, hey, given is offered I gladly appreciate it, It's nice to have it! Good nice surprise.As always, it's incredibly fun. Story mode is super interesting. Good cutscenes, interesting dialogues. I think KOF has a well deserved good reputation within fans because its rich history. Classic KOFs are great, we love them, but KOF XV really takes the things one step further. Online mode so far goes ok, good netcode, I was playing some online matches and was fun, but I like to focus on other aspects, like gameplay: exquisite controls, well balanced, they kept the rush mode so people like us, who suck in fighting games, we can make combos easily, LoL xD pros hates this, I know, but all people deserve to enjoy every game, and SNK kept that in mind for us, really thank you SNK!!Also, the soundtrack, marvelous!! Adds intensity to every fight. Each song is exciting, and it's nice to hear outside the game too! But which also really surprised me, it's that you can configure stages with old KOF music!!! woah, you need to unlock by playing, but this really blew my ears!! Great idea for the old school fans!!Downsides?.... maybe. I noticed there are too few resolution options, just 1080p and 4K. To me, 4K runs perfect, the game also has the option of Ray Tracing, barely is a dealbreaker, but on my system runs great. Maybe some people are going to complain because there is no 2K resolution (1440p), and it's totally understandable. I hope SNK adds 1440p resolution so all those people can enjoy the game however they want.In other hand, other people say they can't set up the keyboard bindings.... I don't know what they mean, because I could change all the keyboard configuration to my preference. But maybe some people are experiencing this. Is not my case.Anyway, it's a great game.Totally recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game solely from the perspective of the single-player content as a beginner to the fighting game genre. This game has a lot of great things to offer, especially if you're a fighting game veteran -- but if you're new to the genre there are better places to start.Fighting game devs: please start including more robust ways for new fighting game players to learn your games... it's too overwhelming. I'm not asking to make the game simpler or easier -- I love the variety and options this game seems to have; but for goodness sake just include content that assists you in learning instead of leaving it to the player to figuring out and practicing everything on their own (like allow me to display and cycle thru special moves instead of having to constantly open and close command list). Basically game-ify practice and training modes. Mini-games, katas, more trials (not just for combos but practicing scenarios)... Help user pick their characters and teach what each character is about at the same time.$80 for content basically more akin to an arcade port in 2022 is kind of unacceptable especially for a game with as much legacy as KoF.

_childDocuments_.review: The core of the game, with it's fast paced 3v3 fighting game play is a ton of fun. It's got a great large (not giant) roster of characters (although not that many surprises for returning players if you know that dead characters are returning) It's got a great soundtrack with previous entries soundtracks being unlockable, and decent rollback netcode, Also they've added a little bit of free DLC which is nice.The game does suffer from 2 possibly giant issues depending on what kind of player you are. The biggest issue is that the matchmaking is broken and has been for quite some time. Sometimes you just won't find a match or it will take ten minutes to find a really laggy match. The game also doesn't have that much content. You only have story mode, training mode, tutorial, Missions (trails and a boss mode which currently incluides a single boss), online matchmaking, and online rooms with four different game modes.  The story mode is a decent arcade experience but doesn't really have any replayability (other then seeing new endings and unlocking music which requires playing through storymode with different teams). If you have friends to play this with or are fine going through discord to find matches, I'd highly recommend it. If you want to rely on online matchmaking or you're looking for single player content, this probably isn't the game for you.(WE GOT CROSSPLAY BABY!)

_childDocuments_.review: It's KOF and an improvement from 14, not an easy thing considering that today's fighting games prefer to go in another direction instead of improving the old systems.Movements are more powerful than those in many other games and offer more freedom of expression. Strong universal mechanics in general.In addition to the Story/Arcade mode, the game offers a variety of online modes, including Ranked Match, Casual Match, Room Match and Tournament,etc.. the basic stuff, a boss mode has been added but it will take a while for it to fill up properly, and there are trial combos, these were created trying to teach the special move cancellation structures, KOFXIII have become a meme at this point, however an update with something more difficult would be fun.For those who have never played the saga there are 4 buttons (ABCD) plus CD, proximity moves, and the basic rule for combo structure in general (and if you have the meter) is normals ➨comand normal➨EX version special moves ➨special moves ➨super (level1,2,3).One of my favorite things was the addition of the DJ station, music from throughout the saga that continues to be fed into the game, fully customizable from the menus to the stages, to be unlocked in some cases via the story mode along with some secret endings.The base game has 41 characters and eight colors (some have alternate costumes such as Rugal).The game has had issues with matchmaking, and I waited to publish to make sure they are resolved. While testing the game at different times (morning, afternoon, and evening), I didn't have any problems finding matches as of the publication date of this review.It is one of the series that defines this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: KOF XV builds upon the foundations set by its predecessor to deliver a fun and rewarding gameplay experience. Sure, it's not as rich as KOF XIV when it comes to single-player content, but this game's online experience is something else entirely. Not only is its utilisation of rollback netcode solid for the most part; there are a whole variety of ways to play against opponents online, and the online settings are presented in a way which is easy to navigate through. In terms of the game itself, the overall presentation is brilliant, with characters looking more vibrant than ever and game mechanics being on the looser end of the fighting game spectrum (i.e. it allows for plenty of player freedom in approaching different styles and tactics). It also helps that there's a whole variety of characters to choose from (even though the overall character count is lower than that of its predecessor) as well as a dedicated jukebox function which allows for custom stage music with soundtracks from throughout SNK's storied history.At the end of the day, KOF XV is a fighting game which does shatter some expectations (but not all of it), and it is worth taking a shot at, especially for newcomers to the KOF franchise.

It's worth a buy for anyone that enjoys the genre, and easily is the most value for your dollar out of any fighting game I've played for the past few years.

_childDocuments_.review: The King of Fighters XV follows up on XIV, but in true KOF fashion, it doesn't change too much. The most immediately obvious change are the improved visuals, showing that SNK is starting to get the hang of 3D characters and environments. Gameplay, it's mostly the same but with two notable tweaks for new players. First, backwards DP motions are gone entirely, although any situation where the player faces left still technically allows for practice. Perhaps more notable is the tweaked rush combos, which will result in a super or climax move if you press any attack button after pressing light punch three times in a row. While I'm all for accessibility, it does force me as a slightly more experienced player to rethink how I press buttons in order to not use my meter by accident, and there's currently no way to disable this feature.Otherwise, I find myself enjoying this game about as much as I enjoyed KOF XIV. Even as someone who doesn't usually play online, I expect to come back quite a bit to unlock the edit team endings and mess around with upcoming dlc characters. If you're familiar with The King of Fighters, you know exactly what you're getting with this game, and if you don't, you'll find this to be a very fun and very deep fighting game.
